english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: Esi wòkpɔ be, medo ɣli sesĩe la, egblẽ eƒe avɔ ɖe gbɔnye, eye wòsi do go le aƒea me.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ eƒe avɔ ta da ɖe eɖokui gbɔ, vaseɖe esime eƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: Then she said, “That Hebrew slave of yours tried to rape me!
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nya mawo ke na eya hã bena: Kpɔ ɖa, Hebri-kluvi, si nekplɔ vɛ na mi la, va gbɔnye, be yeado ŋukpem.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: Ke esi medo ɣli sesĩe la, egblẽ eƒe avɔ ɖe gbɔnye, eye wòsi do go le aƒea me. Wode Yosef gaxɔ me.

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: Eye Yosef ƒe aƒetɔ lée de gaxɔ, si me fia ƒe gatɔwo nɔna la me, eye wònɔ afima le gaxɔa me.

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa nɔ kple Yosef, eye wòna gaxɔdzikpɔla ƒe dzime kɔ ɖe eŋu, eye wòve enu.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Eye gaxɔdzikpɔla tsɔ gatɔ, siwo katã le gaxɔa me la, de Yosef si, eye nusianu, si wowɔna le afima la, eyae ɖonɛ na wo.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Eye gaxɔdzikpɔla metsɔ ɖeke le nusi wòwɔna la me o, elabena Yehowa li kplii, eye nusianu, si wòwɔ na la Yehowa na wòdzea edzi nɛ.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ wo de gaxɔ, si le fia ŋuti mewo ƒe amegã ƒe xɔ, si me wode Yosef hãe la me.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Fia ŋuti mewo ƒe amegã la tsɔ wo de Yosef si, bena wòakpɔ wo dzi, eye wonɔ gaxɔ me ɣeyiɣi didia ɖe.

english_verse: One night each of the two men had a dream, but their dreams had different meanings.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka ƒe zã Egipte-fia ƒe ahakula kple aboloƒola, siwo le gaxɔ me la, woku drɔ̃e wo tɔ wo tɔwoe, eye drɔ̃eawo gɔme le vovovo.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Esi Yosef va wo gbɔ le ŋdi la, ekpɔ wo bena, woli kpoo.

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu nɛ bena: Míeku drɔ̃e, gake amesi aɖe egɔme, meli o. Tete Yosef gblɔ na wo bena: Alo drɔ̃e gɔmeɖeɖe la menye Mawu fɔe oa? Gake milii nam ko! Ahakula la ƒe drɔ̃ekuku.

english_verse: The king's personal servant told Joseph, “In my dream I saw a vine
translation_verse: Tete ahakulawo ƒe amegã lĩ eƒe drɔ̃e la na Yosef, eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Meku drɔ̃e kpɔ weinkaa ɖe le ŋkunye me.

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: Alɔ etɔ̃ le weinka sia ŋu, eye esi wode asi dzedze me la, seƒoƒo ɖo wo dzi, eye woƒe tsetsewo de asi ɖiɖi me.

english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: Ke Farao ƒe kplu la le asinye; tete megbe weinkpoawo, eye mefiã wo ɖe Farao ƒe kplu la me, emegbe metsɔ kplu la de asi na Farao.

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Yosef ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Drɔ̃e la gɔme enye si: Alɔ etɔ̃awo nye ŋkeke etɔ̃.

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke etɔ̃agbe la Farao ado wò ɖe dzi, eye wòagatsɔ wò aɖo wò dɔ nu. Eye nagatsɔ kplu ade Farao si, abe alesi nèwɔna tsã, esi nenye eƒe ahakula ene.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Ke ɖo ŋku dzinye, ne eva nyo na wò! Meɖe kuku, ve nunye, eye naɖo ŋku dzinye na Farao, bena wòaɖem le xɔ sia me.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Elabena yakatsyɔe wofim le Hebritɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, eye afi sia hã nyemewɔ naneke, hafi wolém de ga o. Aboloƒola ƒe drɔ̃ekuku.

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Esi aboloƒolawo ƒe amegã kpɔ bena, drɔ̃e la gɔme nyo la, egblɔ na Yosef bena: Nye hã meku drɔ̃e, eye metsɔ abolo kusi etɔ̃ ɖe ta.

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: Ke kusi etametɔ me la abolo vivi vovovowo li na Farao, eye xeviwo va le wo ɖum de kusia me le tanye.

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Yosef ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Drɔ̃e la gɔme enye si: Kusi etɔ̃awo nye ŋkeke etɔ̃.

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke etɔ̃agbe la Farao atso ta le nuwo, eye woahe wò ɖe ati ŋu, eye xeviwo ava ɖu wò ŋutilã. Alesi drɔ̃ewo va ve me.

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke etɔ̃agbe la Farao ɖu eƒe dzigbe, eye wòɖo kplɔ̃ na eƒe dɔlawo katã, eye wòɖe ahakulawo ƒe amegã kple aboloƒolawo ƒe amegã le gaxɔa me le eƒe dɔlawo katã ƒe ŋku me.

english_verse: He put the personal servant back in his old job
translation_verse: Egatsɔ ahakulawo ƒe amegã la ɖo eƒe ahakudɔ nu, bena wòagatsɔ kplu anɔ asi ɖem na Farao.

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: Ke ena wohe aboloƒolawo ƒe amegã ya ɖe ati ŋu, abe alesi Yosef ɖe egɔme na wo ene.

english_verse: but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_verse: Ahakulawo ƒe amegã megaɖo ŋku Yosef dzi o, ke boŋ eŋlɔe be.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Le ƒe eve megbe la Farao ku drɔ̃e. Ele tsitre ɖe Nil to.

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: Eye wòkpɔ nyinɔ adre, siwo nyo, eye woda ami la, do go tso tɔsisi la me, eye wole gbe ɖum le tagba.

english_verse: ate the fat, healthy cows. When this happened, the king woke up.
translation_verse: Eye nyinɔ, siwo vlo, eye woɖi ku nyatsã la, lé nyinɔ adre, siwo nyo, eye woda ami la mi. Tete Farao nyo.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: Esi wògayi alo me la, egaku drɔ̃e, eye wòkpɔ liŋɔ adre, siwo ʋã, eye wodo ku la, do ɖe luti ɖeka ŋu.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Wo yome la liŋɔ adre, siwo pepi lé, eye wòlé bu la do.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Eye liŋɔ, siwo lé bu la, mi liŋɔ adre, siwo ʋã, eye wodo ku la. Esi Farao nyo la, edze sii bena, drɔ̃e yeku.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Le ŋdi la Farao mekpɔ gbɔdzɔea ɖeke o, eye wòdo woyi ɖayɔ Egipte-fakalawo kple nunyalawo va ƒo ƒu, eye Farao li drɔ̃eawo na wo; ke wo dometɔa ɖeke mete ŋu ɖe egɔme na Farao o.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Tete ahakulawo ƒe amegã ƒo nu kple Farao gblɔ bena: Egbe la meɖo ŋku nye vodada dzi.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: Esi Farao bi dzi ɖe eƒe dɔlawo ŋuti, eye wòna wòlé mía kple aboloƒolawo ƒe amegã de gaxɔ me le fia ŋuti mewo ƒe amegã ƒe me la,

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: mía kple eve míeku drɔ̃e le zã ɖeka me mia ta míatɔe, eye drɔ̃eawo gɔme hã le vovovo.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Eye Hebri-ɖekakpuia ɖe, si enye fia ŋuti mewo ƒe amegã ƒe kluvi la, nɔ mía gbɔ le afima. Mieli míaƒe drɔ̃eawo nɛ, eye wòɖe wo gɔme na mi mia to mía tɔe pɛpɛpɛ.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Alesi wòɖe egɔme na mi la, nenema wòva mee; nye la wogatsɔm ɖo nye ɖa nu, ke eya la woɖee ɖe ati ŋu. Yosef ɖe drɔ̃ewo gɔme na Farao.

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Tete Farao do woyi ɖayɔ Yosef vɛ. Enumake woɖee le gaxɔa me, eye wòko ta ɖɔ li eƒe awuwo hafi yi Farao gbɔ.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Eye Farao gblɔ na Yosef bena: Meku drɔ̃e, eye amea ɖeke mete ŋu ɖe egɔme nam o. Ke mese le ŋuwò bena, ne ese drɔ̃e ko la, eɖea egɔme.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Tete Yosef ɖo ŋu na Farao bena: Gbeɖe, menye nyee o; ke Mawu agblɔ nusi enyo la na Farao.

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Eye Farao gblɔ na Yosef bena: Meku drɔ̃e, eye mele tsitre ɖe Nil to.

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: Kasiaa mekpɔ nyinɔ adre, siwo da ami, eye wonyo la, do tso tɔsisi la me, eye wole gbe ɖum le tagba.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Wo yome la nyinɔ kudɔe adre, siwo vlo ŋuta, eye woɖi ku nyatsã la, hã do, nyemekpɔ nyinɔ vlo siawo tɔgbe le Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi kpɔ o!

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: Gake esi womi wo hã la, ɖeko wole abe ɖe womemi wo o ene, eye woƒe nɔnɔme gavlo abe tsã ene. Tete menya.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: Emegbe megaku drɔ̃e kpɔ liŋɔ adre, siwo ʋã, eye wodo ku la, le luti ɖeka ŋu.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Wo yome la liŋɔ adre, siwo pepi lé wo wòlé bu, eye wotsi to nu la do.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: Eye liŋɔ, siwo lé bu la, mi esiwo do ku la. Esia meli na afakalawo, ke wo dometɔa ɖeke mete ŋu ɖe egɔme nam o.

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Tete Yosef gblɔ na Farao bena: Farao ƒe drɔ̃eawo gɔme le ɖeka. Nusi wɔ ge Mawu gbɔna la, eyae wòɖe fia Farao.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Nyinɔ dami adreawo nye ƒe adre, eye liŋɔ ʋaʋã adreawo hã nye ƒe adre, drɔ̃eawo kple eve gɔme le ɖeka.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Nyinɔ kudɔe adre, siwo vlo, eye wodo ɖe wo yome la, wonye ƒe adre, eye liŋɔ adre, siwo pepi lé wotsi to nu la, wonye ɖɔŋɔliƒe adre.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Eyatae megblɔ na Farao gbã bena: Nusi wɔ ge Mawu ala la, eya wòɖe fia Farao.

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Fe adre gbɔna, si me nuɖuɖu ado agbogbo ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: when the king made him governor, and he went everywhere for the king.
translation_verse: Eyome la dɔŋɔliƒe adre ava, eye woaŋlɔ alesi nuɖuɖu do agbogbo ɖe Egipte-nyigba dzi la be; eve dɔwuame agblẽ anyigba la.

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Ale bena womaganye naneke le alesi nuɖuɖu do agbogbo ɖe anyigba dzi la ŋuti o, le dɔ, si ava to la ta: elabena enu asẽ ŋutɔ.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Ke nusi ta Farao ku drɔ̃ea zi eve ɖo la enye: Mawu ɖoe kplikpa, eye Mawu le ewo ge kaba.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: Azɔ Farao nedi ame, si dze aɖaŋu, eye tagbɔ li nɛ ta, ɖo Egipte-nyigba la nu.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Eyata Farao nadi dzikpɔlawo aɖo anyigba la dzi kaba, bena ne nuɖuɖu do agbogbo ɖe anyigba dzi le ƒe adreawo me la, woadzɔ nuawo ƒe atɔ̃lia,

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: eye woaƒo nuɖuɖuwo nu ƒu le ƒe nyui, siwo gbɔna la me, eye woadzra bliawo ɖo ɖe avawo me le duwo me na Farao.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: Eye nuɖuɖuawo anye nusi wotu ɖo na anyigba la ɖe dɔŋɔliƒe adre, siwo ava Egipte-nyigba dzi la ŋu, bena ne dɔwuame nagagblẽ anyigba la o. Wodo Yosef ɖe dzi.

english_verse: The king and his officials liked this plan.
translation_verse: Nya sia dze Farao kple eŋuti mewo katã ŋu.

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Tete Farao gblɔ na eŋuti meawo bena: Ɖe míate ŋu akpɔ amea ɖe, si me Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ la le abe eya ene mahã?

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Eye Farao gblɔ na Yosef bena: Esi Mawu ɖe nu, siawo katã fia wò la, amea ɖeke meli, si dze aɖaŋu, eye wònya nu abe wò ene o.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Eyata wòe anɔ nye aƒe nu, eye nye dukɔ la katã aɖo to wò nyawo; negbe fiazikpui la ko matsɔ awu wò.

english_verse: You are now governor of all Egypt!”
translation_verse: Eye Farao gblɔ na Yosef bena: Kpɔ ɖa, meɖo wò Egipte-nyigba blibo la nu.

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Eye Farao ɖe eƒe ŋkɔsigɛ le asi hetsɔ do na Yosef, eye wòdo aklalabiɖibiɖiwu nɛ, eyome wòtsɔ sikakɔsɔkɔsɔ de kɔ nɛ.

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: Emegbe la ena wòɖo tasiaɖam evelia, si kplɔ fia tɔ ɖo la, eye kpodolawo le eŋgɔ le gbɔgblɔm bena: Midze klo, midze klo! Ale wòɖoe Egipte-nyigba la katã nu.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Eye Farao gblɔ na Yosef bena: Nye enye Farao, ke ne wòa melɔ̃ o la, amea ɖeke mate ŋu akɔ eƒe asi alo afɔ dzi le Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi o.

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Eye Farao na ŋkɔ Yosef bena Zafnat Paneax , eye wòtsɔ On-nunɔla Potifera ƒe vinyɔnu Asnat nɛ wòɖe. Emegbe la Yosef tsa le Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Eye anyigba la wɔ nu ŋutɔ le ƒe adreawo me.

english_verse: Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested.
translation_verse: Eye wòƒo agblemenu siwo katã wɔ le ƒe adreawo me, le esime nuɖuɖu do agbogbo ɖe Egipte-nyigba dzi la, nu ƒu, eye wòdzra du sia du ƒe agblemetiwo ɖo ɖe ɖu la ŋutɔ me.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Eye Yosef tu bliawo ɖo wòsɔ gbɔ ŋutɔ abe ƒutake ene, ale bena womagate ŋu adzidzee o, eye wodzudzɔ edzidzedzidze.

english_verse: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
translation_verse: Hafi dɔŋɔlia nava la, On-nunɔla Potifera ƒe vinyɔnu Asnat dzi ŋutsuvi eve na Yosef.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Eye Yosef na ŋkɔ eƒe ŋgɔgbevia bena Manase, elabena egblɔ be Mawu na meŋlɔ nye fukpekpewo kple nye ƒometɔwo be.

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: Eye wòna ŋkɔ evelia be Efrayim; elabena egblɔ be: Mawu na medzi ɖe dzi le afisi mekpe fu le la.

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Esi nuʋãƒe adre, siwo va Egipte-nyigba dzi nu yi vɔ la,

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: tete dɔŋɔliƒe adreawo dze gɔme, abe alesi Yosef gblɔ ene. Eye dɔ to ɖe anyigbawo katã dzi, ke nuɖuɖu le Egipte-nyigba ya dzi.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Ke esi dɔ va Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi la, dukɔ la ƒo zi va bia nuɖuɖu Farao. Eye Farao gblɔ na Egiptetɔwo bena: Miyi Yosef gbɔ, eye nusi wòagblɔ na mi la, miawɔe.

english_verse: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Eye esi ɖɔ to le afiawo katã la, Yosef ʋu blivawo katã, eye wòdzra blia na Egiptetɔwo. Eye dɔ la nu le sesẽm ɖe dzi le Egipte-nyigba la dzi.

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Eye amewo tso afiawo katã va Egipte, be woaƒle bli le Yosef gbɔ, elabena dɔ la nu sẽ ŋutɔ le afisiafi.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Esi Yakob se bena, bli le Egipte la, Yakob gblɔna viawo bena: Nukaŋuti miele mia nɔewo ƒe mo kpɔm ale?

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Mesee vavã bena, bli le Egipte; miyi ne míaƒle bli le afima na mí, bena míatsi agbe, eye miagaku o!

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Tete Yosef nɔvi ewo dze mɔ, be woayi aɖaƒle bli le Egipte.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Ke Yakob meɖe mɔ na Yosef nɔvi Benyamin, be wòayi kple nɔviawo o, elabena ele vɔvɔ̃m be, dzɔgbevɔ̃ea ɖe ava dzɔ ɖe edzi.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Tete Israel ƒe viwo kple ame bubuwo va bli ƒle ge, elabena dɔ to le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Eye Yosef, si enye anyigba dzi ɖula la, dzra bli na anyigbadzitɔwo katã. Esi Yosef nɔviwo va, eye wodze klo de ta agu nɛ la.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Tete Yosef ɖo ŋku drɔ̃e, si wòku le wo ŋu la dzi, eye wògblɔ na wo bena: Ŋkutsalawo míenye! Ɖe mieva, be miadi mɔnu le anyigba la ŋu.

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu ne bena: Gbeɖe, amegã, wò dɔlawo va nuɖuɖu ƒle ge boŋ.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Mí katã ŋutsu ɖeka viwo míenye, eye nyateƒetɔwo míenye: wò dɔlawo menye ŋkutsalawo o.

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu na wo bena: Kpao, mɔnu ɖi ge mieva le anyigba la ŋu!

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu bena: Nɔvi wuieve wò dɔlawo nye, eye ŋutsu ɖeka viwo míenye le Kanaan-nyigba dzi. Ɖevitɔ la tsi fofoa gbɔ, ke ɖeka megali o.

english_verse: Joseph replied: It's like I said. You're spies,
translation_verse: Eye Yosef xɔ dzi na wo bena: Ele me kokoko bena, ŋkutsalawo míenye!

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Esia matsɔ ado mi akpɔe: Mefa Farao be, miadzo le afisia akpɔ o, negbe mia nɔvi ɖevitɔ la koe ava hafi!

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Mido mia dometɔ ɖeka ɖa, be wòakplɔ mia nɔvi la vɛ, ke malé mi ame mamleawo ade ga. Esia me mado mi akpɔ le be, ɖe mietoa nyateƒe loo; ke ne mele nenem o la, meta Farao bena, ŋkutsalawo míenye.

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Tete wòlé wo de ga ŋkeke etɔ sɔŋ.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke etɔ̃agbe la Yosef gblɔ na wo bena: Miwɔ esia, ne míatsi agbe, elabena mevɔ̃a Mawu.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Ne mietoa nyateƒe la, ekema mina mia nɔvi ɖeka natsi ga me, ke mi mamleawo mitsɔ blia yi na mia ƒometɔwo, bena woatsɔ atsi dɔwuamea nui.

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: Mikplɔ mia nɔvi ɖevitɔ vɛ nam, ekema miaƒe nyawo anye nyateƒe, eye miagaku o. Tete wowɔ nenema.

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ na wo nɔewo bena: Nyateƒe, mia nɔvi lae nu sia va mía dzi ɖo, elabena esi miekpɔ, alesi dzidzi ƒoe, eye wòƒo koko nam: la, mieɖo tokui! Eyata mieɖo xaxa sia me ɖo.

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Ruben xɔ dzi na wo bena: Ɖe nyemegblɔ na mi bena, migada vo ɖe ɖevi la ŋu oa? Ke miesee o, azɔ wole eƒe ʋuhlɔ̃ biam mí.

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Ke womenyae bena, Yosef le esem o, elabena gbesevi le wo dome.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Tete wòtrɔ dzo le wo gbɔ ɖade asi avifafa me, emegbe egatrɔ va wo gbɔ heƒo nu kple wo, eye wòlé Simeon le wo dome hebla le wo katã ŋku me.

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Eyome Yosef de se bena, woade bli woƒe kotokuawo me taŋ, atsɔ amesiame ƒe ga ade eƒe kotokua me, eye woana mɔ dzi nuɖuɖu hã wo. Eye wowɔ na wo nenema.

english_verse: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
translation_verse: Tete wotsɔ bliawo ɖo woƒe tedziwo dzi, eye wodze mɔ tso afima.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Ke esi woɖo dɔƒe, eye wo dometɔ ɖeka tu eƒe kotoku, be yeana nu yeƒe tedzi la, tete wòkpɔ be, yeƒe ga le blia dzi le kotokua me.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na nɔviawo bena: Kpɔ ɖa, wogagbugbɔ nye ga nam, eya enye si le nye kotokua me! Tete wolulu, eye wodzo nyanyanya kpo wo nɔewo hegblɔ bena: Nuka enye si Mawu wo ɖe mia ŋu? Yakob viŋutsuwo ƒe tɔtrɔgbɔ.

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Esi wogbɔ va wo fofo Yakob gbã le Kanaan-nyigba dzi la, wogblɔ nya, siwo katã dzo ɖe wo dzi la, nɛ bena:

english_verse: The governor of Egypt was rude and treated us like spies.
translation_verse: Ŋutsu, si enye anyigba dzi ɖula la, he nya sesẽ kple mí, eye wobu mí ŋkutsalawoe.

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Ke míegblɔ nɛ bena, nyateƒetɔwo míenye, eye míenye ŋkutsalawo o.

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Nɔvi wuieve míenye, eye fofo ɖekae dzi mí. Ke ame ɖeka megali o, eye miaƒe ɖevitɔ tsi fofoa gbɔ le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu, si enye anyigba dzi ɖula la, gblɔ na mí bena: Esia me madze sii ale bena, nyateƒetɔwo míenye: Migblẽ mia nɔvi ɖeka ɖe gbɔnye, ke mi ame mamleawo mitso bli yi na mia ƒomeawo, bena woatsi dɔwuame nui.

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: Mikplɔ mia nɔvi ɖevitɔ la vɛ nam, ne manyae bena, menye ŋkutsalawo mienye o, ke boŋ nyateƒetɔwo míenye. Emegbe maɖe asi le mia nɔvi la ŋu na mi, eye miatsa le anyigba la dzi faa.

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Ke esi wotrɔ blia le kotokuawo me la, wo dome ɖesiaɖe gakpɔ eƒe gale kotokua me. Eye esi woa kple wo fofo wokpɔ ga la la, wovɔ̃ ŋutɔ.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Tete wo fofo Yakob gblɔ na wo bena: Vinyewo ko ɖem miele le ŋunye! Yosef meli o, eye Simeon hã meli o, eye miele didim be, miagaxɔ Benyamin hã! Dzinye koe nu siawo katã le dzɔdzɔm ɖo!

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Ruben gblɔ na fofoa bena. Ne nyemegakplɔe vɛ na wò o la, ekema nawu nye ŋutsuvi eveawo! Tsɔe de asi nam ko, eye magakplɔe vɛ na wò!

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Vinye la mayi kple mi o, elabena nɔvia ku, eye eya ɖeka koe susɔ ɖi. Ne dzɔgbevɔ̃ea ɖe adzɔ ɖe edzi le mɔ dzi la, ekema miawoe na nye amegã wɔtamee sia metsɔ konyifafa yi tsiẽƒee.

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,
translation_verse: Ke dɔwuame la nu sẽ ŋutɔ le anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Eye esi woɖu bli, siwo wotsɔ tso Egipte vɛ, vɔ la, wo fofo gblɔ na wo bena: Miyi, ne miagaƒle bli vɛ nam!

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: Ke ne mèlɔ̃ ɖe asi le eŋu na mí o la, ekema míayi o. Elabena ŋutsu la gblɔ na mí bena: ne miekplɔ mia nɔvi ɖe asi vɛ o la, ekema migava ye ŋku me o.

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Israel ɖo ŋu bena: Nukaŋuti miewɔ vɔ̃ ɖe ŋunye ale, eye mieʋu me na ŋutsu la be, nɔvi gale yewo si?

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu bena: Ŋutsu la bia mía ŋutɔwo kple míaƒe ƒome ta se kolokolo bena: Ɖe mia fofo gale agbea? Ɖe nɔvi gale mia sia? Eye mieʋu me ne, abe alesi wòle ene. Ɖe míenyae bena, agblɔ na mí be, míkplɔ mía nɔvi vɛ mahã?

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Yuda gblɔ na fofoa Israel bena: Ɖe asi le ɖevi la ŋuti nam, bene míadze mɔ ayi, ne míatsi agbe, eye mía ŋutɔwo, wò ŋutɔ kple mía nɔviwo míagaku o.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Manɔ enu, eye nabiae atso asinye. Ne nyemegakplɔe va ɖo ŋkuwò me o la, ekema nabum vodalae le nye agbe me ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Ɖe menye hehem míele ɖe megbe o la, anye ne miede zi eve gbɔ xoxo.

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Tete wo fofo Israel gblɔ na wo bena: Ne ele alea la, ekema miwɔ ale: Mitsɔ anyigba dzi nu vevia ɖewo de miaƒe kotokuwo me yi ɖana ŋutsu la: lifi kple anyitsi via ɖe, ami ʋeʋẽ, kotoklobo, ayedee kple newo.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Migatsɔ ga bubu ɖe asi hekpe ɖe ga, siwo miekpɔ le blia dzi le kotokuawo me la ŋuti. Ɖewohi ɖe woɖe ŋu ɖi.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Emegbe miakplɔ mia nɔvi la, eye miadze mɔ ayi ŋutsu la gbɔ.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Mawu ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ana bena, ŋutsu la nave mia nu, eye woaɖe asi le mia nɔvi la kple Benyamin ŋuti na mi. Ke ne vinyewo le bubum hã, ne wònɔ bubum ko dzro. Yosef xɔ nɔviawo nyuie.

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsuawo tsɔ nunanaawo kple ga bubu ɖe asi, eye wokplɔ Benyamin hã hedze mo yi Egipte, eye wova Yosef gbɔ.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Esi Yosef kpɔ bena, Benyamin le wo dome la, egblɔ na eƒe aƒedzikpɔla bena: Kplɔ ŋutsu siawo yi aƒe mee, eye nawu lã aɖa nu, elabena ŋutsuawo le nu ɖu ge kplim egbe ŋdɔ.

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsu la wo, abe alesi Yosef gblɔ nɛ ene, eye wòkplɔ ŋutsuawo yi Yosef ƒe mee.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsuawo vɔ̃, le esi wokplɔ wo yi Yosef ƒe mee la ta, eye wogblɔ bena: Ga, si miekpɔ le míaƒe kotokuawo me le míaƒe vava gbãtɔ me, tae wokplɔ mi vɛ ɖo, bena woanye zi atsyɔ mía dzi, eye woalé mí kple míaƒe tedziwo awɔ kluviwoe.

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Eye wote ɖe Yosef ƒe aƒedzikpɔla ŋu le xɔa ƒe mo nu, eye woƒo nu kplii gblɔ bena:

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: Taflatse, mia aƒetɔ, mieva afi sia zi gbãtɔ va ƒle bli.

english_verse: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
translation_verse: Ke esi mieɖo dzeƒe, eye mietu míaƒe kotokuawo la, amesiame gakpɔ eƒe ga blibo la le eƒe bli dzi le kotokua me; kpɔ ɖa, míegatsɔe ɖe asi vɛ.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Míegatsɔ ga bubu ɖe asi vɛ, be míaƒle bli lae, ke mienyã amesi tso ga la ɖe míaƒe kotokuawo me o.

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu na wo bena: Miaƒe dzi nedze eme, migavɔ̃ o. Miaƒe Mawu kple mia fofo ƒe Mawu la tsɔ kesinɔnu ɖe miaƒe kotokuawo mele adza me. Miaƒe ga la su asinye. Tete wòkplɔ Simeon do go va wo gbɔ.

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Emegbe la ekplɔ ŋutsuawo va Yosef ƒe me, ku tsi na wo woklɔ afɔe, eye wòtsɔ gbe na woƒe tedziwo. Yosef ɖo kplɔ na nɔviawo.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Eye wotsa nunanaawo da ɖi, vaseɖe esime Yosef gbɔ le ŋdɔ me, elabena wose bena, yewole nu ɖu ge le afima.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Esi Yosef va aƒea me la, wotsɔ nunana, si wotsɔ vɛ la, yi ne, eye wodze klo de ta agu nɛ.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Eye wòdo gbe na wo nyuie bia wo bena: Mia fofo tsitsi, si ŋu mieƒo nu le nam la, li sesĩe, eye ele agbe mahã?

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu bena: Wò dɔla, mía fofo le sesĩe, eye wogale agbe, Tete wodze klo tsyo mo anyi nɛ.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Esi wòfɔ kɔ dzi kpɔ dadavia Benyamin la, ebia bena: Esia nye mia nɔvi ɖevitɔ, si ŋu mieƒo nu le nam mahã? Eye wõgblɔ be: Mawu nayra wò, vinye!

english_verse: Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried.
translation_verse: Enumake Yosef tso nuƒoƒo la, eye eƒe dɔme trɔ ɖe nɔvia ŋu, eye wòdi be, yeafa avi; eyata wòyi ɖe eƒe xɔgã me ɖafa avi le afima.

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: Emegbe etutu mo, eye wògado go hezi eɖokui dzi gblɔ bena: Mido kplɔ̃!

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Tete woɖo kplɔ nɛ ɖe vovo, eye woɖoe na woawo hã ɖe vovo, nenema ke woɖoe ɖe vovo na Egiptetɔ, siwo ɖua nu kplii la hã. Egiptetɔwo meɖua nu kple Hebritɔwo o, elabena enye ŋunyɔnuwɔwɔ le woƒe ŋku me.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: Eye wobɔbɔ nɔ anyi dze ŋgɔe le kplɔ̃a ŋu, eye wòɖo wo tso tsitsitsɔ dzi vaseɖe ɖevitɔ dzi ɖe woƒe tsitsime nu; ke ŋutsuawo ƒe nu ku, eye wode asi wo nɔewo kpɔkpɔ me.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Eye wòna womã nuɖuɖu, si le egbɔ la, na wo, ke Benyamin tɔ sɔ gbɔ wu wo katã tɔ zi atɔ̃. Emegbe la wono nu kplii, eye wokpɔ dzidzɔ.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: Eye natsɔ nye klosalokplu ade ɖevitɔ ƒe kotoku me hekpe ɖe ga, si wòtsɔ va blia ƒle gee la ŋu. Tete wòwɔe, abe alesi Yosef gblɔ nɛ ene.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Le ŋdi kanya la wodo mɔ ŋutsuawo woyi kple woƒe tedziwo.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Eye esi wodo go le dua me, eye wo yome mebu haɖe o la, Yosef gblɔ na eƒe aƒedzikpɔla bena: Tso, nati ŋutsuawo yome, eye ne etu wo la, nagblɔ na wo bena. Nukaŋuti mietsɔ vɔ̃ ɖo nyui teƒe mahã?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Alo menye eya me nye aƒetɔ noa nu lena, eye eya me wokpɔa nu lena dzea sii o mahã? Miewɔ busunu!

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Esi wòva tu wo la, eƒo nu kpli wo alea tututu.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: Wodo ŋu nɛ bena: Ao, aƒetɔ, nukaŋuti nèle nu ƒom ale? Nu sia wɔwɔ nede megbe xaa tso wò dɔlawo gbɔ!

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Ga, si miekpɔ le miaƒe kotokuawo mele blia dzi la, míegatsɔ wo tso Kanaan-nyigba dzi vɛ na wò, aleke awɔ míafi klosalo alo sika le wò aƒetɔ ƒe me mahã?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Wo dɔla, si gbɔ nakpɔe le la, naku; ke mí ame mamleawo miazu mia aƒetɔ ƒe kluviwo.

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Enyo, woawɔ nenema, abe alesi miegblɔ ene. Amesi gbɔ woakpɔe ale la, nazu nye kluvi: ke mi ame mamleawo miadzo ayi faa.

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Enumake wo dome ɖesiaɖe ɖiɖi eƒe kotokua ɖe anyigba, eye amesiame tu eƒe kotoku la.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Eye wòde asi edidi me, dze egɔme tso xoxoetɔ dzi va wu enu ɖe ɖevitɔ dzi, eye wòkpɔ kplu la le Benyamin ƒe kotoku me.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Tete wodze woƒe awuwo, eye wo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe gado agba na eƒe tedzi, eye wogatrɔ va du la me.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Eye esi Yuda kple nɔviawo va Yosef ƒe me la, Yosef gale afima ko — tete wodze klo ɖe ta agu nɛ.

english_verse: who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
translation_verse: Yosef gblɔ na wo bena: Nuka enye si miewɔ? Ɖe mienyae bena, amegã menye, eye mekaa nu o mahã?

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Eye Yuda ɖo ŋu bena: Nuka miagblɔ na nye aƒetɔ, eye nu ka míaƒo, alo aleke miaɖe mia ɖokui nuí, esi Mawu kpɔ wò dɔlawo ƒe vodada la? Kpɔ ɖa, miawo kple amesi gbɔ wokpɔ kplua le la, miazu nye aƒetɔ ƒe kluviwo.

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Esia wɔwɔ neɖe megbe xaa tso gbɔnye! Amesi gbɔ wokpɔ kplua le la, eya anye nye kluvi: ke miawo miagbugbɔ ayi mia fofo gbɔ faa.

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Tete Yuda te ɖe eŋu gblɔ be: Taflatse, nye aƒetɔ! Na wò dɔla naƒo nu kple nye aƒetɔ, eye megabi dzi ɖe wò dɔla ŋu o; elabena èle abe Farao ene.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Nye aƒetɔ bia eƒe dɔlawo bena: Ɖe fofo alo nɔviŋutsu gale mia siá?

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Míegblɔ na nye aƒetɔ bena: fofo gale mia si, si ku amegã ɖeɖi, eye wodzi dɔmlɔea nɛ le eƒe amegãkuku me. Ke dadavia ku, eye eya ɖeka koe susɔ na dada, eye fofoa lɔ̃nɛ.

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: Eye nègblɔ na wò dɔlawo bena: mikplɔe vɛ nam, ne makpɔ.

english_verse: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
translation_verse: Mieɖo ŋu na nye aƒetɔ bena: Ɖevi la mate ŋu agblẽ fofoa ɖi o, ne egblẽe ɖi la, ekema fofoa aku.

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Tete nègblɔ na wò dɔlawo bena: ne miekplɔ mia nɔvi ɖevitɔ vɛ o la, ekema migava do ɖe nye ŋku me o.

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: Esi mietrɔ va wò dɔla, fofonye gbɔ la, miegblɔ nye aƒetɔ ƒe nyawo nɛ.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: Emegbe mía fofo gblɔ bena: Migayi ɖa ƒle bli vɛ.

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: Ke mieɖo ŋu bena: Míate ŋui o! Ne mia nɔvi ɖevitɔ le eme la, eya ko míayi. Elabena miate ŋu ado ɖe ŋutsu la ƒe ŋku me o, ne mia nɔvi ɖevitɔ mele mía me o.

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Tete wò dɔla, fofonye gblɔ na mi bena: Mienyae bena, vi eve siawo ko srɔ̃nye dzi nam.

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: Ɖeka gblẽm ɖi, eye mesusu be, lãa ɖe vuvui, eye va ɖo egbee nyemegakpɔe kpɔ o.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Ne miekplɔ eya hã le gbɔnye yii, eye dzɔgbevɔ̃ea ɖe adzɔ ɖe edzi la, ekema etso mia gbɔ, ne nye amegã wɔtamee sia matsɔ konyifafa ayi tsiẽƒee.

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: Azɔ ne mava ɖo wò dɔla fofonye gbɔ, eye ɖevi, si gbɔ melɔ̃a nu le o la, megale mia dome o la,

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Elabena wò dɔlae nɔ ɖevia nu le fofonye gbɔ, eye medo ŋugbe ne be: ne nyemegakplɔ ɖevi la vɛ na wo o la, ekema manye fɔɖila le fofonye gbɔ le nye agbe me ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Eyata meɖe kuku na wò, wò dɔla nazu kluvi na nye aƒetɔ ɖe ɖevi la teƒe, ne ɖevia nayi aƒe kple nɔviawo.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Aleke wɔ mayi fofonye gbɔ, ne ɖevi la mele ŋunye oa? Nyemagate ŋu akpɔ fofonye ƒe konyifaƒe o.

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Ke Yosef megate ŋu zi eɖokui dzi, abe alesi wòwɔ vaseɖe fifi, esime amewo le egbɔ la ene o; eye wògblɔ bena: Amesiame nado go le gbɔnye! Eye amea ɖeke menɔ Yosef gbɔ, hafi wòɖe eɖokui fia nɔviawo o.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Tete wògbã avi doo, ale bena Egiptetɔwo kple Farao-ƒemetɔwo hã see.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: Eye Yosef gblɔ na nɔviawo bena: Nye enye Yosef! Fofonye gale agbea? Ke nɔviawo lulu le eƒe ŋku me, eye womete ŋu ɖo nyaa ɖeke ŋu nɛ o.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Eye Yosef gblɔ na nɔviawo bena: Mite ɖe ŋunye dzro! Esi wole ɖe eŋu la, egblɔ bena: Nye enye mia nɔvi Yosef, si mietsɔ dzra ɖe Egipte la.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Migana woazu nuxaxa na mi o, eye megave mi be, mietsɔm ƒle ɖe afisia o; elabena Mawue dɔm ɖe mia ŋgɔ, bena maɖe miaƒe agbe.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Fe eve enye si dɔwuame le anyigba dzi, eye wògasusɔ ƒe atɔ̃, siwo me womaŋlɔ nu, eye womaŋe nu o.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Ke Mawu dɔm ɖe mia ŋgɔ, bena mia ŋutɔwo kple mia viwo míatsi agbe, eye ame geɖewo nakpɔ ɖeɖe.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Menye miawoe dɔm ɖe afisia o, ke boŋ Mawue, eye wòtsɔm wɔ adaŋudela vevi na Farao, eye wòɖom amegãe ɖe eƒe aƒe dzi kple dziɖulae ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: Eyata netsɔ, ne miayi fofonye gbɔ, eye miagblɔ nɛ bena: Ale viwò Yosef gblɔ esi: Mawu ɖom amegãe ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi; va gbɔnye, megahe ɖe megbe o!

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Eye nanɔ Gosen-nyigba dzi, ate ɖe ŋunye, wò ŋutɔ, viwòŋutsuwo kple wò tɔgbuiyɔviwo, wò alẽwo kple nyiwo kpakple nusiwo katã le asiwò.

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Makpɔ dziwò le afima, elabena esusɔ ƒe atɔ̃ dɔwuame naganɔ anyi, bena hiã nagatu wò ŋutɔ, viwòwo kple aƒewòmetɔwo katã o.

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: Mia ŋutɔwo kple nɔvinye Benyamin hã miekpɔe kple miaƒe ŋkuwo bena, nye ŋutɔe ƒo nu kpli mi.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Migblɔ bubu, si katã mekpɔ le Egipte-nyigba dzi, kple nusiwo katã miekpɔ la, fia fofonye, eye netsɔ, miakplɔ fofonye ava afisiae.

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Eyome la eɖuɖɔ nu na nɔviawo katã, eye wòfa avi ɖe woƒe kɔ dzi, emegbe la nɔviawo ƒo nu kplii. Yosef na wokplɔ fofoa va Egipte.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Eye Farao kple eƒemetɔwo se bena, Yosef nɔviwo va. Eye wòdze Farao ŋuti mewo katã ŋu.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Tete Farao gblɔ na Yosef bena: Gblɔ na nɔviwòawo be, mido agba na miaƒe lãwo, eye míayi Kanaan-nyigba dzi

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: aɖakplɔ mia fofo kple mia ƒomeawo ava gbɔnye, eye mana anyigba nyuitɔ mi le Egipte, ne miaɖu nu ʋaʋãawo le anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Ke wò la, gblɔ nusi woawɔ la na wo! Mitsɔ tasiaɖamwo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi ɖe asi hena mia viwo kple mia srɔ̃wo, eye mina mia fofo hã naɖoe ava.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Eye migana miaƒe ŋkuwo nanɔ miaƒe xɔmenuwo ŋu, eye woƒe nu nave mi o, elabena Egipte-nyigba dzi nu nyuiwo katã lanye mia tɔ.

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Eye Israel viwo wɔ nenema, eye Yosef tsɔ tasiaɖamwo na wo le Farao ƒe nya la nu, eye wòna mɔ dzi nuɖuɖu hã wo.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: Eye wòna atsyɔɖowu wo dome amesiame: ke ena klosalo sekel alafa etɔ kple atsyɔɖowu atɔ Benyamin ya.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Eye wòɖo tedzi ewo, siwo tsɔ Egipte-nu veviwo kple tedzinɔ ewo, siwo tsɔ bli kple abolo kple mɔ dzi nuɖuɖu, ɖe fofoa.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Emegbe edo mɔ nɔviawo, eye hafi wòadze mɔ la, exlɔ̃ nu wo bena: Migawɔ dzre le mɔ dzi o!

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Ale wotso le Egipte, eye wova ɖo wo fofo Yakob gbɔ le Kanɔan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ nɛ bena: Yosef gale agbe, eye wònye dziɖula le Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi. Ke nya la ka ɖe Yakob, eye mexɔe se o.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Ke esi wogblɔ nya, siwo katã Yosef gblɔ na wo la, nɛ, eye wòkpɔ tasiaɖam, siwo Yosef ɖo ɖee, be woaɖo ava la, wo fofo Yakob ƒe dzi gaɖo me.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Eye Israel gblɔ bena: Esɔ gbɔ be, vinye Yosef gale agbe! Mayi aɖakpɔe ɖa hafi aku!

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Eye Israel dze mo kple eƒemetɔwo katã, eye esi wòɖo Berseba la, esa vɔ na fofoa Isak ƒe Mawu la.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Tete Mawu ɖe eɖokui fia Israel le drɔ̃eƒe gblɔ bena: Yakob, Yakob! Eɖo ŋu bena: Nye enye si!

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Nye enye Mawu, fofowò ƒe Mawu la. Megavɔ̃ Egipte yiyi o, elabena mana nazu dukɔ gãa ɖe le afima.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: Nye ŋutɔ mayi Egipte kple wò, eye ye ŋutɔ magakplɔ wò agbɔe; ke Yosef ahe wò ŋkuyiwo akpe.

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
translation_verse: Esiawo nye Lea ƒe viŋutsu, siwo wòdzi na Yakob le Mesopotamia hekpe ɖe vianyɔnu Dina ŋu: viaŋutsuwo kple vianyɔnuwo katã le ame blaetɔ̃ vɔ etɔ̃.

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Ne Farao ayɔ mi, eye woabia mi bena, dɔ ka wɔlawo míenye mahã la,

english_verse: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
translation_verse: Esiawo nye Silpa, amesi Laban tsɔ na vianyɔnu Lea la ƒe viŋutsu, siwo wòdzi na Yakob; wo katã le ame wuiade.

english_verse: Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren. Their son Dan took his son Hushim. Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
translation_verse: Esiawo nye Bilha, amesi Laban tso na vianyɔnu Raxel la, ƒe viŋutsu, siwo wòdzi na: Yakob; wo katã le ame adre.

english_verse: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
translation_verse: Yakob vi, siwo katã nu kplii yi Egipte, ne woɖe viaŋutsuwo srɔ̃wo le eme la, wole ame blaade vɔ ade.

english_verse: Jacob's two grandsons who were born there made it a total of
translation_verse: Ŋutsuvi, siwo wodzi na Yosef le Egipte la, wole ame eve. Yakob vi, siwo katã va Egipte la, wole ame blaadre. Yosef xɔ fofoa.

english_verse: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
translation_verse: Ke edɔ Yuda ɖe eŋgɔ ɖo ɖe Yosef gbɔ, bena wòaɖe ame aɖo ŋgɔ nɛ, ne wòayi Gosen. Eye esi woɖo Gosen-nyigba dzi la,

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Yosef na woɖo eƒe tasiaɖam ɖo, eye wòɖoe yi fofoa Israel kpe ge le Gosen. Esi wòkpɔe la, ekpla asi kɔ ne, eye wòfa avi ɖe eƒe ko dzi ʋuu.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Eye Israel gblɔ na Yosef bena: Azɔ maku faa, elabena megakpɔ wò agbagbee.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Eye Yosef gblɔ na nɔvia wo kple fofoa ƒemetɔwo bena: Meyi maɖagblɔe na Farao bena: nɔvinyewo kple fofonyeƒemetɔ, siwo le Kanaan-nyigba dzi la, wova gbɔnye.

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Lãhawo le ŋutsuawo si, elabena lãnyilawo wonye, eye wova kple woƒe alẽwo, nyiwo kple woƒe kesinɔnuwo katã.

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: ekema miaɖo ŋu bena: lãnyilawo wò dɔlawo nye tso ɖevime vaseɖe fifi abe mía tɔgbuiwo ke ene, bena wòaɖe mɔ na mi mianɔ Gosen-nyigba la dzi. Elabena Egiptetɔwo nyoa ŋu lãnyilawo.

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Eye Farao bia nɔviawo bena: Dɔ ka wɔlawo míenye? Woɖo ŋu na Farao bena: Lãnyilawo wò dɔlawo nye abe mia tɔgbuiwo ke ene.

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ na Farao bena: Amedzrowo míenye va afisia na ge; elabena gbe megali na wò dɔlawo ƒe lãwo o, eye dɔwuame nu sẽ ŋutɔ le Kanaan-nyigba dzi. Eyata miede kuku, na wò dolawo nano Gosen-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Tete Farao gblɔ na Yosef bena: Fofowò kple nɔviwòwo va gbɔwò.

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Egipte-nyigba la enye si, na bena woano teƒe nyuitɔ, na fofowò kple nɔviwòwo nanɔ Gosen-nyigba la dzi Eye ne ekpa bena, ame zãzɛwo le wo dome la, ekema natsɔ nye lãhawo ade wo si. Yakob le Farao ŋku me.

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Emegbe la Yosef kplɔ fofoa Yakob va fia Farao gbɔ, tete Yakob yra Farao.

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: Eye Farao bia Yakob bena: Ƒe nenie nèxɔ?

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Emegbe la Yakob yayra Farao, eye wòdzo le Farao gbɔ.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Eye Yosef fia nɔƒe fofoa kple nɔviawo, eye wòna anyigba wo le Egipte le Ramses, afisi anyigba nyuitɔ le, abe alesi Farao de se nɛ ene.

english_verse: Joseph also provided food for their families. A Famine in Egypt
translation_verse: Eye Yosef tsɔ nuɖuɖu kpɔ fofoa, nɔviawo kple fofoa ƒemetɔwo katã dzi, amesiame kple evia. Dɔwuame va Egipte.

english_verse: The famine was bad everywhere in Egypt and Canaan, and the people were suffering terribly.
translation_verse: Ke nuɖuɖua ɖeke megale anyigba blibo la dzi o, elabena dɔ la nu sẽ ŋutɔ, eye dɔwuame na Egipte kple Kanaan-nyigba dzi ƒu.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Mlɔeba la Yosef ƒo ga, siwo Egiptetɔwo kple Kanaantɔwo tsɔ ƒle bli le esi la, nu ƒu, eye wòtsɔ ga la yi Farao ƒe mee.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Ke esi ga megale Egipte kple Kanaan-nyigba dzi o la, Egiptetɔwo katã va Yosef gbɔ, eye wogblɔ bena. Na nuɖuɖu mi, nukaŋuti míaku ɖe gbɔwò? Elabena ga vɔ!

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Yosef ɖo ŋu bena: Ne ga vɔ le mia si la, ekema mikplɔ miaƒe lãhawo ve, eye mana nuɖuɖu mi ɖe wo teƒe!

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Ƒe sia va yi. Le ƒe bubu me la wogava egbɔ, eye wogblɔ nɛ bena: Aƒetɔ, míate ŋu aɣla nyaa ɖeke ɖe wò o. Míaƒe ga vɔ, eye míaƒe lãhawo ge ɖe mía aƒetɔ si me. Naneke megali miatsɔ na mía aƒetɔ o, negbe mía ŋutɔwo kple miaƒe agblenyigbawo koe susɔ.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti miaku ɖe gbɔwò? Tsɔ bli ƒle mia kple míaƒe agblenyigbawo, bena mía ŋutɔwo kple miaƒe agblenyigbawo nanye Farao tɔ! Na bli mí, bena míatsi agbe, eye miagaku, ne míaƒe agblenyigbawo nagazu afuti o.

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: Tete Yosef ƒle Egiptetɔwo ƒe agblewo katã na Farao. Eye Egiptetɔwo dome amesiame tsɔ eƒe agblenyigba dzra, elabena dɔwuamea nu sẽ ŋutɔ; ale anyigba la katã zu Farao tɔ.

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: Ke meƒle nunɔlawo ƒe agblenyigbawo o, elabena nunɔlawo kpɔ wo tɔ gome le Farao gbɔ, eye woɖu gome, si wòxɔ tso Farao gbɔ la; eyata womedzra woƒe anyigbawo o.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Tete Yosef gblɔ na dukɔ la bena: Kpɔ ɖa, egbe meƒle mia kple miaƒe anyigbawo na Farao. Mixɔ nuku, ne miaƒã ɖe miaƒe agblewo me.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: Eye ne nuŋeɣi ɖo la, ekema miatsɔ agblemenuawo ƒe atɔ̃liawo ɖeka na Farao; ke atɔ̃liawo ene nanye mia ŋutɔwo mia tɔ, bena miatsɔ ɖe aƒa ɖe agbleawo me, eye ɖe nanye nuɖuɖu na mia ŋutɔwo, mia ƒemetɔwo kple mia viwo.

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Tete wogblɔ bena: Wòe xɔ mí ɖe agbe! Aƒetɔ, ne ànya ve mia nu ko, ekema mianye Farao ƒe awɔbamewo faa.

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Eye Yosef tsɔe wɔ see na Egiptetɔwo vaseɖe egbegbe bena, woatsɔ woƒe agblemenuwo ƒe atɔ̃liawo ɖeka ana Farao; negbe nunɔlawo ƒe anyigbawo koe menye Farao tɔ o. Yakob ƒe nuwuwu gogo.

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Ke Israel nɔ Egipte le Gosen-nyigba dzi, eye wotsi edzi, eye wodzi viwo hedzi ɖe dzi ŋutɔ.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: Esi Israel kpɔ be, yeƒe kuɣi le ɖoɖom la, ena woyɔ via Yosef vɛ, eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Ne mele vevie na wò la, ekema tsɔ wò asi ɖo nye ali me, eye nave nunye, aɖi anukware nam bena, màɖim ɖe Egipte o;

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: ke boŋ naɖim ɖe tɔgbuinyewo gbɔ, eye natsɔm atso Egipte aɖaɖi ɖe woƒe yɔdo me. Tete wòɖo ŋu bena: Mawɔe, abe alesi nèdi ene.

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Ka atam! Eye wòka atam nɛ. Tete Yakob gadze ŋe ɖe eƒe abati la dzi.

english_verse: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Le nusiawo megbe la wogblɔ na Yosef bena: Fofowò le dɔ lém. Tete wòkplɔ viaŋutsu eveawo, Efrayim kple Manase, ɖe asi.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ na Yakob bena: Kpɔ ɖa, viwò Yosef va gbɔwò. Tete Israel do ŋusẽ eɖokui hefɔ ɖe ali nu.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: Eye Yakob gblɔ na Yosef bena: Mawu ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ɖe eɖokui fiãm le Lus le Kanaan-nyigba dzi, eye wòyram

english_verse: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
translation_verse: gblɔ nam bena: Mana nadzi, eye wò dzidzimeviwo nasɔ gbɔ ɖe dzi; mana nazu dukɔha, eye matsɔ anyigba sia ana megbewò viwo, be wòanye wo tɔ tegbee.

english_verse: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
translation_verse: Ke viwòŋutsu eveawo, Efrayim kple Manase, siwo wodzi na wò le Egipte, hafi meva gbɔwò le Egipte la, nazu vinyewo abe Ruben kple Simeon ene.

english_verse: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ke vi, siwo nèdzi ɖe wo yome la, nanye tɔwo; eye woayɔ woƒe ŋkɔwo ɖe wo nɔviwo ƒe domenyinyi ŋu.

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: Esi metrɔ tso Mesopotamia gbɔna va Kanaan la, Raxel ku le gbɔnye le mɔ dzi, esi mele tu Efrat, eye meɖii ɖe afima le Efrat, si enye Betlexem, mɔ to.

english_verse: Jacob was very old and almost blind. He did not recognize the two boys, and so he asked Joseph, “Who are these boys?” Joseph answered, “They are my sons. God has given them to me here in Egypt.” “Bring them to me,” Jacob said. “I want to give them my blessing.” Joseph brought the boys to him, and he hugged and kissed them.
translation_verse: Ke Israel tsi, eye eƒe ŋkuwo dzi tsyɔ, ale bena megate ŋu le nu kpɔm o. Eye esi wòkplɔ wo te ɖe eŋu la, ekpla asi kɔ na wo heɖuɖɔ nu na wo.

english_verse: Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.”
translation_verse: Tete Israel gblɔ na Yosef bena: Nyemesusu be, magakpɔ wo ŋku me o, ke azɔ Mawu na mekpɔ viwò wo gɔ̃ hã.

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
translation_verse: Emegbe Yosef ɖe wo ɖa le eƒe ata dzi, eye wòdze klo de ta agu.

english_verse: After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right.
translation_verse: Eyome la Yosef le via eveawo ɖe asi Efrayim ɖe ɖusi, be woatrɔ ɖe Israel ƒe miã me, eye Manase ɖe miã, be wòatrɔ ɖe Israel ƒe ɖusi me, eye wokplɔ wo te ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ke Israel da eƒe nuɖusi ɖe Efrayim ƒe ta dzi, wònye eyae nye ɖevia hafi, eye wòda eƒe mia ɖe Manase ƒe ta dzi, ale wotso ga eƒe asiwò, evɔ wonye Manase enye tsitsia hafi.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: Eye woyra Yosef gblɔ bena: Mawu, si ƒe ŋku me fofonye Abraham kple Isak zɔ le, Mawu, si nye kplɔlanye le nye agbe me ŋkekewo katã me va do egbee,

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: mawudɔla, si ɖem tso nye hiãwo katã me la, ayra ɖeviawo eye woayɔ nye ŋkɔ kple fofonye Abraham kple Isak ƒe ŋkɔ ɖe wo ŋu, wòadzi ɖe dzi, eye woasɔ gbɔ le anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
translation_verse: Esi Yosef kpɔ bena, fofoa da eƒe nuɖusi ɖe Efrayim ƒe ta dzi la, menyo eŋu o; eyata wòlé fofoa ƒe asi, be yeaɖee ɖa le Efrayim ƒe ta dzi ahada ɖe Manase ƒe ta dzi.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: Eye Yosef gblɔ na fofoa bena: Fofonye, menye nenema o; esia nye ŋgɔgbetɔ, tsɔ wò nuɖusi da ɖe eƒe ta dzi!

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: Ke fofoa gbe, eye wògblɔ bena: Menyae, vinye, menyae! Eya hã ava nye dukɔ, eye wòasẽ ŋu. Gake nɔvia ɖevitɔa asẽ ŋu awui, eye eƒe dzidzimeviwo anye dukɔ gã.

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: Eye wòyra wo gbemagbe gblɔ bena: Wò ŋkɔ Israel-viwo atsɔ ayra amewo agblɔ bena: Mawu naɖi na wò abe Efrayim kple Manase ene! Ale wotsɔ Efrayim ɖo tsitsii na Manase.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Emegbe Israel gblɔ na Yosef bena: Mele kuku ge kaba, ke Mawu anɔ anyi kpli mi, eye woakplɔ mi ayi mia togbɛwo ƒe anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: Meanwhile, I'm giving you the hillside I captured from the Amorites.”
translation_verse: Ke metsɔ anyigbaa ɖe, si mexɔ le Amoritɔwo si kple nye yi kple da la na wò, si natsɔ awu nɔviwòwo.

english_verse: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
translation_verse: Eye Yakob ya viawo gblɔ bena: Miƒo ƒu, ne magblɔ nusi le dzɔdzɔ ge ɖe mia dzi le ɣeyiɣi, siwo gbɔna me la afia mi!

english_verse: Come, gather around, as I tell your future.
translation_verse: Miƒo ƒu, eye mike to, nu Yakob viwo, miɖo to mia fofo Israel!

english_verse: Reuben, you are my oldest, born at the peak of my powers; you were an honored leader.
translation_verse: Ruben! wòe nye nye ŋgɔgbevi, nye ŋusẽ kple nye ali me vi gbãtɔ, gbãtɔ le bubu me kple gãtɔ le ŋusẽ me.

english_verse: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
translation_verse: Ele fiefiẽm abe tsi ene, maganye gbãtɔ akpɔ o, elabena ede fofowò ƒe aba dzi, eye nedo ŋunyɔe gbemagbe, ẽ, nye aba dzie nede!

english_verse: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
translation_verse: Simeon kple Lewi la, nɔviwoe, wotsɔ woƒe lãnuwo do biae.

english_verse: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
translation_verse: Nye luʋɔ made woƒe adaŋu me o, eye nye dzi mabɔ ha kple wo o, elabena de dziku me wowu ŋutsuwo eye le dzidzɔ teƒe wòŋe ata na nyitsuwo.

english_verse: Now I place a curse on you because of your fierce anger. Your descendants will be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Aɖi woƒe nyanyrã ŋu, elabena enu sẽ, kple woƒe dziku ŋu, elabena eteƒe meka o! Mamã wo de Yakob viwo dome, eye makaka wo ɖe Israel.

english_verse: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
translation_verse: Yuda! wòe nɔviwòwo akatu, wò asi axe wò funɔwo ƒe ve, eye fofowoviwo adze klo na wò.

english_verse: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
translation_verse: Dzatavi enye Yuda. Le nuléle ta, vinye, anɔ to dzi. Emlɔ anyi tsyɔ akɔ abe dzatatsu ene, eye abe dzatanɔ ene; ameka ate ŋu aʋuʋui?

english_verse: You will have power and rule until nations obey you and come bringing gifts.
translation_verse: Atamkayi magbe Yuda si nanɔ o, eye womede fiatikplɔ da le ekɔme o, vaseɖe esime amesi tɔ wònye nava; amesi dukɔwo ana tae.

english_verse: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
translation_verse: Ede ka eƒe tedzivi de weinka ŋuti, kple eƒe tedzinɔvi ɖe weinka nyui ƒe abɔwo ŋui! Enyã eƒe avɔ le wein me, kple eƒe avu le weintsetse me tsi me.

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: Wein na eƒe ŋku bia, eye notsi na eƒe aƒu fu.

english_verse: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
translation_verse: Zebulon anɔ ƒutanyigbawo dzi le ʋudzeƒewo, eye eƒe liƒo ade Zidon ke.

english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: Isaxar enye tedzi, si ƒu tsi de lãme na, eye wotsyɔ akɔ de lãkpɔwo domee.

english_verse: You found them so pleasant that you worked too hard and became a slave.
translation_verse: Esi wòkpɔ be, dzudzɔ vivina, eye eƒe anyigba dze ani la, ebi eƒe abɔ ta, be wòatsɔ agba, eye wòzu agbatetsɔla.

english_verse: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
translation_verse: Dan aʋli eƒe dukɔ ta abe Israel to bubuwo ke ene.

english_verse: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
translation_verse: Dan enye da tsomɔ, dakpui le afɔmɔe dzi; eɖu sɔ ƒe afɔʋume, eye sɔdola dze anyi megbe megbee.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: Yehowa, wò ɖeɖe la ko lalam mele!

english_verse: Gad, you will be attacked, then attack your attackers.
translation_verse: Gad la, adzohawo ava dze edzi; ke eya ayɔ wo de nu.

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: Aser la, nu ado agbogbo de esi, eye woadzra nuɖuɖu veviwo na fiawo.

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: Naftali enye zinɔ, si ʋlãna, eye wògblɔa nu me vivi nyawo.

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: Ati fẽ enye Yosef, ali fe le vudo to, eye wòɖe ala ɖe gli dzi.

english_verse: Enemies attacked with arrows, refusing to show mercy.
translation_verse: Wole fui, eye wotee kple ɖa, eye aŋutrɔdalawo ɖee ɖe nu.

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: Ke eva eƒe dati goŋgoŋ, eye eƒe asiwò le tsatsam; elabena exɔ ŋusẽ tso Yakob ƒe ŋusẽtɔ kple Israel ƒe kplɔla kple kpe la gbɔ,

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: tso fofowò ƒe Mawu la gbɔ, eya akpe ɖe ŋuwò! tso ŋusẽkatãtɔ la gbɔ, eya ayra wò! Atsɔ dziƒo nu nyuiwo ayra wò, atsɔ tɔ gɔme nu nyuiwo ayra wò, eye atsɔ notsi kple vidzidɔ geɖe ayra wò!

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: Fofowò ƒe yayra, si gbɔ tonyigba xoxo wɔnuwo kple togbe dzeani, siwo li tegbee ŋu la, ava Yosef ƒe ta dzi kple nɔviawo ƒe amegã ƒe dzodome.

english_verse: Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf, destroying your enemies morning and evening.
translation_verse: Benyamin enye amegãxi lénu. Ŋdi la eɖua eƒe nuléle, eye fiẽ la emãa eƒe adzonu la.

english_verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings. Jacob's Death
translation_verse: Esiawo nye Israel ƒe to wuieveawo; eye esiawo nye nya, siwo wo fofo gblɔ na wo. Eyra wo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe wo tɔ wo tɔe.

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: ɖe kpeto, si le agble la me, si wòƒle le Xitiviwo si la me.
