english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Esi Yakob wu nyawo nu na viawo vɔ la, eƒo ata ƒu ɖe aba dzi, eye wòmia nu, eye wòyi ɖe tɔgbuiawo gbɔ.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Tete Yosef dze fofoa dzi, fa avi ɖe edzi, eye wòɖuɖɔ nu nɛ.

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Ke esi konyifaɣiawo va yi vɔ la, Yosef gblɔ na Farao ŋuti mewo bena: Meɖe kuku, ne miave nunye la, ekema migblɔ na Farao bena:

english_verse: Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
translation_verse: Fofonye na meka atam ne bena, ne yeku la, ekema maɖi ye ɖe yɔdo, si yeɖe ɖe Kanaan-nyigba dzi la me. Eyata meɖe kuku, mayi aɖaɖi fofonye, emegbe magatrɔ agbɔ.

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Farao ɖo ŋu nɛ bena; Yi naɖaɖi fofowò, abe alesi nèka atam nɛ ene!

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Esi wova ɖo Gorenhatad, si le Yordan godo la, wofa konyi ŋutɔŋutɔ le afima, eye wowɔ yɔƒe na wo fofoa ŋkeke adre.

english_verse: The Canaanites saw this and said, “The Egyptians are in great sorrow.” Then they named the place “Egypt in Sorrow.”
translation_verse: Esi Kanaantɔ, siwo nye anyigba dzi nɔlawo, kpɔ yɔƒewɔwɔ la le Gorenhatad la, wogblɔ bena: Afisia Egiptetɔwo wɔ yɔƒe gãa ɖe le. Eyata woyɔa teƒe ma bena Abel-Mizraim, si le Yordan godo.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Eye viaŋutsuwo wo nɛ, abe alesi wòde se na wo ene.

english_verse: They took him to Mamre in Canaan and buried him in Machpelah Cave, the burial place Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite.
translation_verse: Eye viawo tsoe yi Kanaan, eye woɖii ɖe kpeto, si le Maxpela gble me, le Mamre kasa la me; agble, si Abraham ƒle le Efron Xititɔa si, be wòanye ameɖiƒe nɛ.

english_verse: After the funeral, Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else returned to Egypt. Joseph's Promise to His Brothers
translation_verse: Esi wòɖi fofoa va la, Yosef kple nɔviawo kple amesiwo katã kpe ɖe eŋu woɖaɖi fofoa la, wogatrɔ va Egipte. Yosef de dzi ƒo na nɔviwo; eƒe ku.

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Le wo fofo ƒe ku megbe la Yosef nɔviwo le vɔvɔ̃m gblɔ bena: Ɖewohĩ Yosef alé fu mi, eye wòaɖo vɔ̃, siwo katã miewɔ ɖe eŋu la, teƒe na mí.

english_verse: So they sent this message to Joseph: Before our father died,
translation_verse: Eye wodɔ ame ɖo ɖe Yosef gbɔ gblɔ bena: Hafi fofowò naku la, ede se gblɔ bena:

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: Ale miagblɔ na Yosef enye si: Meɖe kuku, tsɔ nɔviwòwo ƒe nuvɔ̃ kple woƒe vodada ke wo; elabena wowɔ vɔ ɖe ŋuwò. Eyata míeɖe kuku, tsɔ míaƒe nuvɔ̃wo ke mí, elabena miawo hã míesubɔa fofowò ƒe Mawu la. Tete Yosef fa avi le nya sia ŋuti.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Emegbe la nɔviawo ŋutɔ yi, eye wodze klo de ta agu nɛ gblɔ bena: Miawo nye si, tsɔ mi wɔ wò kluviwoe!

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Eye Yosef ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Migavɔ̃ o! Alo Mawu teƒe melea?

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Miawo miesusu vɔ̃ ɖe ŋunye, ke Mawu trae wòzu nyuie, be yeawɔe axɔ ame geɖe ɖe agbe, abe alesi miele ekpɔmi egbegbe ene.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Eyata migavɔ̃ o, manyi mia kple mia viwo siaa! Ale wòfa ako na wo, eye wòde dzi ƒo na wo.

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Eye Yosef kple fofoa ƒemetɔwo tsi Egipte-nyigba dzi, eye Yosef xɔ ƒe alafa ɖeka kple ewo.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: Eye Yosef nɔ agbe tso Efrayim ƒe tɔgbuiyɔviwo ɖo, eye Maxir Manase vi hã dzi viwo le Yosef ƒe agbenɔɣi me.

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Eye Yosef gblɔ na nɔviawo bena: Nye la mele kuku ge; ke Mawu aɖo ŋku mia dzi, eye wòakplɔ mi atso anyigba sia dzi ayi ɖe anyigba, si ŋugbe wodo na Abraham, Isak kple Yakob la dzi.

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Tete Yosef na Israel ƒe viwo ka atam, eye wògblɔ bena: Ne Mawu aɖo ŋku mia dzi la, ekema mitso nye ƒuwo hã tso afisia yii!

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Emegbe Yosef kple nɔviawo kple wo viwo katã ku.

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo dzi hele agbɔ sɔm ɖe dzi ŋutɔŋutɔ, wokeke ta, eye woxɔ anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Eye fia yeyea ɖe ɖu fia le! Egipte, amesi menya naneke le Yosef ŋuti o.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na eƒe dukɔ la bena: Mikpɔ ɖa, Israel-dukɔ la sɔ gbɔ, eye wosẽ ŋu wu mi.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Enyo, mina miadze aye ɖe wo ŋuti, bena womagasɔ gbɔ ɖe edzi o, eye ne aʋa dzɔ la, womagade míaƒe futɔwo dzi awɔ aʋa kpli mí ahaʋu le anyigba la dzi o.

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Tete wotsɔ dzikpɔlawo ɖo wo nu, bena woate wo ɖe anyi, ne woawɔ dɔ sesẽwo; eye wotu nudzraɖoƒewo na Farao, siwo nye Pitom kple Ramses.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Gake esi wole wo tem ɖe anyi hã la, dzidzim ko wole ɖe dzi, eye wole ta kekem, ale be wòde asi Israel-viwo vɔvɔ̃ me.

english_verse: and made them work so hard
translation_verse: Eye Egipte-tɔwo zi Israel-viwo dzi nublanuitɔe, be woawɔ dɔ sesẽ.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Eye dɔ sesẽ wowɔ na agbenɔnɔ ti wo; wonyã anyi, me anyikpe, eye wowɔ agbledɔ ƒomevi vovo vo, siwo wozi wo dzi nublanuitɔe de asi na wo la.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Eye Egipte-fia de se na Hebritɔwo ƒe vixela, siwo dometɔ ɖeka ŋkɔ nye Sifra, eye evelia ŋkɔ nye Pua la bena;

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: Ne miele vi xem na Hebri-nyɔnua ɖe, eye miekpɔ le viadziƒe bena, ŋutsuvie la, ekema miawui, ke nenye nyɔnuvi la, ekema mina wòanɔ agbe!

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Ke vixelawo vɔ̃ Mawu, eye womewɔ se, si Egipte-fia de na wo la dzi o, boŋ wona ŋutsuviawo nɔ agbe.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Tete Egipte-fia ya vixelawo vɛ, eye wòbia wo bena: Nukaŋuti miewɔ alea, eye miena ŋutsuviawo tsi agbe?

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Vixelawo ɖo ŋu na Farao bena: Hebri-nyɔnuwo mele abe Egipte-nyɔnuwo ene o, ke boŋ wosesẽ; kasiaa vixela nava wo gbɔ la, woawɔ ŋutɔ dzia vi la xoxo.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Emegbe Farao de se na eƒe dukɔ la katã bena: Ne Hebritɔwo dzi ŋutsuvi la, ekema mitsɔe ƒu gbe ɖe Nil-tɔsisi la me, ke mina nyɔnuviwo katã nanɔ agbe.

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Ŋutsua ɖe tso Lewito la me ɖe Lewi-nyɔnua ɖe.

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Eye nyɔnu la fɔ fu dzi ŋutsuvi. Esi wòkpɔ bena, edze ɖeka la, eɣlae ɣleti etɔ̃.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ke esi megate ŋu le eɣlam o la, etsɔ kusi, si wotso aɖa lɔ̃e, eye wòtree kple aŋɔ keŋ, emegbe la etsɔ ɖevi la mlɔ me, eye wòkɔe ɖada ɖe Nil-tɔsisi to le aƒlawo me.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Eye nɔvianyɔnu le adzɔge, bena yeakpɔ nusi ava dzo ɖe edzi. Mose ƒe agbetsitsi le nukumɔa ɖe dzi kple enyinyi.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Tete Farao vinyɔnu va tsi le ge le Nil me. Ke egbɔ nyɔnuviwo le tsa ɖim le tɔa to. Kasiaa wòkpɔ kusia ɖe le aƒlawo dome ɖa, eye wòdo eƒe dɔlanyɔnu ɖa, be wòaɖatsɔe vɛ.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Esi wòʋui la, ekpa ŋutsuvia ɖe le avi fam le ame. Eye eƒe nu wo nublanui ne wògblɔ bena: Ɖewo Hebri-ŋutsuviwo dometɔa ɖee!

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Tete nɔvianyɔnu gblɔ na Farao ƒe vinyɔnua bena: Nyemayi aɖayɔ Hebri-nyɔnua ɖe vɛ, bena wòana no ɖevi la na wò oa?

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Farao vinyɔnu la ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Heyi! Tete nyɔnuvi la yi ɖayɔ ɖevi la ɖada vɛ.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Eye Farao vinyɔnu la gblɔ nɛ bena: Xɔ ɖevi sia, eye nana noe nam, ekema mana adzɔ wò! Tete nyɔnu la xɔ ɖevi la, eye wòna noe.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Esi ŋutsuvia tsi la, ekplɔe ve na Farao vinyɔnu la, eye wòxɔe wɔ viae hetsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ bena Mose: elabena egblɔ be: To mee meɖee tsoe.

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Esi Mose va tsi la, gbe ɖeka eyi nɔviawo gbɔ, eye wòkpɔ, alesi wole woƒe dɔ sesẽ la wɔmi. Tete wòkpɔ Egiptetɔa ɖe le nɔvia Hebritɔa ɖe ƒom.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Eye esi wotsa ŋu mlamlamla mekpɔ amea ɖeke o la, eƒo Egiptetɔ la wu, eye wòlɔ ke ɖe edzi.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, egayi, eye wòkpɔ Hebritɔ ɖeɖe eve le avu wɔm. Tete wògblɔ na amesi le ge dim la bena: Nukaŋuti nele nɔviwò ƒom?

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Ke eya ɖo ŋu bena: Amekae ɖo wò amegã kple ʋɔnudrɔ̃la ɖe mía nu? Ɖe nèbe, yeawu nye hã, abe alesi nèwu Egiptetɔ la enea? Tete Mose ɖe asi vɔvɔ̃ me, elabena ekpɔ bena, nya la ɖi wose. Mose ti dzo le Egipte, eye woɖe srɔ̃.

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Farao hã se nya la, eye wòle didim be, yeawu Mose. Ke Mose si le Farao nu heyi ɖe Midian-tɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, eye wòva bɔbɔ no vudoa ɖe to.

english_verse: the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Eye vinyɔnu adre le Midian-nunɔla si, amesiwo va tsi du ge ɖe lãwo ƒe towo me, bena woana tsi wo fofo ƒe alẽwo.

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Eye alẽkplɔlawo va tutu wo ɖe megbe. Ke Mose tsi tre xɔ na wo, eye wòna woƒe alẽwo no tsi.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Esi wogbɔ va wo fofo Reguel gbɔ la, ebia wo bena: Nukaŋuti miegbã egbe kaba ale?

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu bena: Egipte-ŋutsua ɖe xɔ mí le alẽkplɔlawo si, eye wòdu tsi gɔ̃ hã na miaƒe alẽwo wono.

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ na vianyɔnuawo bena: Afika wòle? Nukaŋuti miegblẽ ŋutsu la ɖe afima? Miyi ɖayɔe vɛ, ne woaɖu nu!

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Eye Mose lɔ̃ bena, yeatsi ŋutsu la gbɔ, eye wotsɔ vianyɔnu Zipora na Mose wòɖe.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Eye wòdzi ŋutsuvi ne, eye wòyɔ eƒe ŋkɔ bena Gersom; elabena egblɔ bena: Amedzro menye le dzronyigba dzi.

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Esi eteƒe va didi la, Egipte-fia ku Eye Israel-viwo fa konyi le woƒe dɔ sesẽ la ŋu, eye wodo ɣli. Eye woƒe ɣli, si wodo, be woavo tso woƒe dɔ sesẽa me la, de Mawu gbɔ.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Eye Mawu se woƒe konyifafa, eye wòɖo ŋku nu, si wòbia kple Abraham, Isak kple Yakob la dzi.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Eye Mawu kpɔ Israel-viwo ƒe nublanui, eye wòve wo nu.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Eye Mose kpɔ toa Midian-nunɔla Yetro ƒe alẽwo dzi. Gbe ɖeka esi wòkolɔ alẽawo yi gbedzi la, eva Mawu ƒe to Xoreb gbɔ.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe dɔla ɖe eɖokui fiae le dzobibi me le ŋuvea ɖe me. Esi wòlé ŋku ɖe eŋu la, ekpɔ bena, ŋuve la le bibim, gake mele fiafiãm o.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Tete Mose gblɔ bena: Mate ɖe eŋu, ne makpɔ nukpekpe gã sia ɖa, nusi ŋuti ŋuve la mele fiefiẽm o ɖo.

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Ke esi Yehowa kpɔ bena, ele tetem ta, be yeakpɔe ɖa la, Mawu yɔe tso ŋuve la me bena: Mose, Mose! Eɖo ŋu bena: Nyee nye si!

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Megale va afisia o, ɖe wò atokotawo le afɔ; elabena anyigba, si dzi nèle la, teƒe kɔkɔee!

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Eyome egblɔ be: Nyee nye fofowò ƒe Mawu, Abraham ƒe Mawu, Isak ƒe Mawu kple Yakob ƒe Mawu. Tete Mose tsɔ nu tsyɔ mo, elabena ele Mawu kpɔkpɔ yɔm.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ bena: Mekpɔ alesi wole nye dukɔ tem ɖe anyi le Egipte keŋ, eye mese woƒe ɣli, si wodo, be yewoavo atso yewo dzikpɔlawo si me la; ẽ, menya woƒe fukpekpewo.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Eye meɖi va, be maɖe wo le Egiptetɔwo si me, eye makplɔ wo atso anyigba sia dzi ayi ɖe, anyigba, si nyo, eye wòlólo la dzi, anyigba, si dzi notsi kple anyitsi bɔ do, afisi Kanaanitɔwo. Xititɔwo, Amoritɔwo, Perizitɔwo, Xiwitɔwo kple Yebusitɔwo le.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Eye esi Israel-viwo ƒe ɣli ɖi mese, eye mekpɔ, alesi Egiptetɔwo le fu wɔm wo la,

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: eyata mele dɔwòm ɖe Farao gbɔ, be nakplɔ nye dukɔ Israel-viwo adzoe tso Egipte.

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Ke Mose gblɔ na Mawu bena: Ameka menye, be mayi Farao gbɔ, eye makplɔ Israel-viwo adzoe atso Egipte?

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Manɔ anyi kpli wò! Eye esia anye dzesi na wo bena, nyee dɔ wò: Ne èkplɔ dukɔ la dzoe tso Egipte la, ekema miasubɔ Mawu le to sia dzi.

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ na Mawu bena: Ne meva Israel-viwo gbɔ, eve megblɔ na wo be: mia fofowo ƒe Mawu dɔm do de mia gbɔ, eve woabiam bena eŋkɔ ɖee hã la, aleke maɖo ŋu na wòe?

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Heyi, ne naƒo Israel-viwo ƒe ame tsitsiwo nu fu, eye nagblɔ na wo bena: Yehowa, mia fofowo ƒe Mawu, Abraham ƒe Mawu, Isak ƒe Mawu kple Yakob ƒe Mawu la, de eɖokui liam gblɔ bena: Medo ŋku mia dzi, eye mekpɔ nusi dzɔ de mia dzi le Egipte.

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Eyata medo bena, made mi atso Egiptetɔwo ƒe teteɖanyi la me akplɔ mi ayi Kanaanitɔwo, Xititɔwo, Amoritɔwo, Perizitɔwo, Xiwitɔwo kple Yebusitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, afisi notsi kple anyitsi bɔ ɖo.

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: Eye ne woɖo to wò gbe la, ekema mia kple Israel-viwo ƒe ame tsitsiwo miayi Egipte-fia gbɔ, eye miagblɔ nɛ bena: Yehowa, Hebritɔwo ƒe Mawu la, ɖe eɖokui fia mí; eyata na miazɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃ ƒe mɔ ayi gbedzi, aɖamè nu na Yehowa mia Mawu la.

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Gake menyae bena, Egipte-fia maɖe mɔ na mi miadzo o, negbe ɖeko woazi edzi hafi.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Mado nye asi da, eye matsɔ nye nukunuwo katã, siwo mawɔ le wo dome la, aɖee le mo na Egiptetɔwo: emegbe hafi woana miayi.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: ke nyɔnu sia nyɔnu nabia klosalo kple sikanuwo kpakple avɔwo le eƒe aƒelika kple eƒe me medzrowo si, eye miatsɔ wo aɖo atsyɔ̃ na mia viŋutsuwo kple mia vinyɔnuwo. Ale miaha Egiptetɔwo enye si!

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Mose do ŋu gblɔ bena: Ne womexɔ nye nya dzi se o, eye womeɖo to nye gbe o, ke boŋ wogblɔ bena: Yehowa mede eɖokui fia wò o ɖe?

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Yehowa gblɔ nɛ bena: Nukae ma le asiwò? Eɖo ŋu bena: Atizɔtie.

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ bena: Tsoe ƒu gbe ɖe anyigba! Esi wòtsɔe ƒu gbe ɖe anyigba la, etrɔ zu da, eye Mose si le enu.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Do wò asi ɖa nalé eƒe asike! Eye wodo eƒe asi ɖa lee; tete wògatrɔ zu atizɔti de esi.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Ekema woaxɔe ase bena, Yehowa, wo fofowo ƒe Mawu, Abraham ƒe Mawu, Isak ƒe Mawu kple Yakob fe Mawu lae de eɖokui fia wò.

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gagblɔ nɛ bena: Tsa wò asi ƒo ɖe wò axatome! Eye wòtsɔ eƒe asi ƒo de eƒe axatome. Esi wògaɖee ɖa la, anyi ƒo ɖe eƒe asi ŋuti fu tii.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Gagbugbɔ wò asi ƒo de wò axatome! Eye esi wògagbugbɔ eƒe asi ƒo de axatome, eye wògaɖee da la, kpɔ ɖa, eƒe asi gazu abe eƒe ŋutilã susɔea ene.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Ke ne womexɔ dzesi eve siawo hã dzi se o, eye womese wo gbe o la, ekema naku tsi le Nil-tɔsisi me akɔ de anyigba, eye tsi, si nèku le Nil-tɔsisia me la, atrɔ zu ʋu ɖe anyigba.

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Tete Mose gblɔ na Yehowa bena: Taflatse, Aƒetɔ, nyemenya nuƒoƒo o, eye esia metso etsɔ kple nyitsɔ alo tso esime nède asi nuƒoƒo me kple wò dɔla o, elabena nye aɖe metrɔna ɖe nya ŋuti o.

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Yehowa ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Ameka wo nu na ame? Ameka wo aɖetututɔ alo tokunɔ alo nukpɔla alo ŋkuagbãtɔ? Alo menye nye Yehowa oa?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Heyi ko, makpe ɖe ŋuwò naƒo nu, eye mafia nusi nagblɔ la wò.

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Taflatse, Aƒetɔ, ɖi amea ɖe do boŋ.

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa, do dɔmedzoe ɖe Mose ŋu gblɔ bena: Alo nyemenyae bena, nɔ viwò Aron, Lewitɔ la, nya nuƒoƒo nyuie oa? Kpɔ ɖa, egbɔna kpe; wò ge, eye ne ekpɔ wò la, dzi adzoe ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Eye natsɔ atizɔti sia ɖe asi, eya natsɔ awɔ dzesiawoe! Mose gatrɔ yi Egipte.

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Eye Mose trɔ gbã va toa Yetro gbɔ, eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Mele didim be, magbugbɔ aɖakpɔ nɔvinyewo ɖa le Egipte be, wogale agbe mahã? Yetro ɖo ŋu; na Mose bena. Heyi faa!

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose le Midian bena: Tso, gbugbɔ yi ɖe Egipte, elabena amesiwo katã le didim be, yewoatsrɔ̃ wò agbe la, woku.

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Tete Mose tsɔ srɔ̃a kple viawo ɖo tedzi dzi, eye wòdze mɔ heyi Egipte-nyigba dzi; eye Mose tso Mawu ƒe atikplɔ la ɖe asi.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Ne ede Egipte la, ekema naɖo ŋku nukunu, siwo katã mede asi na wò la dzi awɔ le Farao ƒe ŋku me; ke nye la mana eƒe dzime nasẽ, bena maɖe asi le dukɔ la ŋu wòayi o.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Gblɔ na Farao bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Israel la nye ŋgɔgbevie!

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: Eyata mele gbɔgblɔm na wò bena: Ɖe asi le vinye ŋuti, ne wòava subɔm, ke ne ègbe asiɖeɖe le eŋu la, ekema mawu wò ŋgɔgbevi!

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Le ma dzi, esi wova ɖo dzeƒe la, Yehowa va, eye wòdi be, yeawui.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Tete Zipora tsɔ kpe ɖaɖɛa ɖe lã viaŋutsu ƒe aʋanuyi ɖa, eye wòtsɔe da ɖe eƒe afɔ nu gblɔ bena: Ʋuŋugbetɔsrɔ̃ nènye nam.

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Tete wòɖe asi le eŋu. Gbemagbe wògblɔ bena ʋuŋugbetɔsrɔ̃ le aʋatsotso la ta.

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Aron bena: Yi ɖakpe Mose le gbea dzi! Tete wòyi ɖakpee le Mawu ƒe to la gbɔ, eye wògbugbɔ nu nɛ.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ Yehowa ƒe nya, siwo katã ta wòdɔe ɖo kple dzesi, siwo katã wòde esi la nɛ.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Esia megbe Mose kple Aron woyi, eye woyɔ Israel-viwo ƒe ame tsitsiwo katã ƒo ƒu.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Eye Aron gblɔ nya, siwo katã Yehowa de asi na Mose la; ke eya wo dzesiawo le dukɔ la ƒe ŋku me.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Esi dukɔ la se bena: Yehowa ɖo ŋku Israel-viwo dzi, eye wòkpɔ woƒe teteɖanyi la, woxɔe se, eye wode ta agu hedo gbe ɖa.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Emegbe Mose kple Aron woyi dagblɔ na Farao bena: Ale Yehowa. Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi. Ɖe asi le nye dukɔ la ŋuti, bena wòayi aɖaɖu ŋkekenyuie nam le gbedzi!

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Farao ɖo ŋu bena: Ameka nye Yehowa, ne maɖo to eƒe gbe aɖe asi le Israel-viwo ŋuti wòayi? Nyemenya Yehowa la o, eye nyemaɖe asi le Israel ŋuti wòayi hã o!

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ bena: Hebritɔwo ƒe Mawu la ɖe eɖokui fia mí. Na míazɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃ ƒe azɔli ayi gbeɖzi, ne miasa vɔ na Yehowa, mía Mawu la: ne menye nenem o la, adze mia dzi kple dɔvɔ̃ alo yi.

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Eye Farao gagblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, dukɔ la so gbɔ le anyigba la dzi tso, eye miedi be, wòadzudzɔ woƒe dɔ la mahã? Farao gate Israel-viwo ɖe anyi wu.

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: Migana gbe dukɔ la, bena woade anyi me, amè anyikpewoe, abe alesi miewɔe vaseɖe fifi ene o; ke boŋ woawo ŋuta nayi aɖadi gbe na wo ɖokui!

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Gake kpe alesi nu womèna vaseɖe fifi la, mina woamèe, eye migaɖe ɖeke le edzi na wo o! Elabena kuvia wɔm wole; eyata wole ɣli dom le gbɔgblɔm bena: Míayi aɖasa vɔ na miaƒe Mawu.

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Dɔ la nu nasẽ na wo, ale be dɔ geɖe nanɔ wo si, ne womagaɖo to ameblenyawo o!

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Tete nuka la ƒe dɔdzikpɔlawo kple dɔnunɔlawo yi, eve wogblɔ na dukɔ, la bena: Ale Farao ɖo enye si. Nyemegale gbe na ge mi azɔ o.

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: Mia ŋutɔwo miyi, ne miadi gbe na mia ɖokui, afisi míakpɔe ale, ke womaɖe miaƒe dɔ la dzi na mi o.

english_verse: The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw.
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la kaka ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi, bena woadi gbe.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Eye dɔdzikpɔlawo ƒo du de wo nu gblɔ bena: Ele na mi be, mia wu miaƒe goesiagbe dɔ nu blibo, abe alesi miewɔna tsã, esime gbe no mia si la ene.

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Eye woƒo Israel-vi, siwo Farao ƒe dɔdzikpɔlawo tsa do dɔnunɔlawoe la, gblɔ na wo bena: Nukaŋuti mieme miaƒe anyikpe, siwo woɖo na mi la, wu nu blibo etsɔ kple egbe, abe tsã ene o mana?

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Tete Israel-viwo ƒe dɔnunɔlawo yi ɖafa konyi na Farao gblɔ bena: Nukaŋuti nele wò dɔlawo wɔm alea?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Womegale gbe nam wò dɔlawo azɔ o, gake wole gbɔgblɔm na mí bena: mimè anyikpe! Azɔ wole mia ƒom gɔ̃ hã, eye wobu wò dukɔ la vodalawoe.

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Ke eya ɖo ŋu gblɔ bena: Kuviatɔwo, kuviatɔwo míenye! Eyata miele gbɔgblɔm bena: Míayi aɖasa vo na Yehowa.

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Miheyi miaƒe dɔ dzi; womana gbe mi o, gake ele na mi be, miame anyikpe, abe alesi wodo na mi ene.

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Eye wosesẽ na Israel-viwo ƒe dɔnunɔlawo be, woaɖagblɔ be, womeɖe woƒe gbesiagbe kpemème la dzi na wo o.

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Esi wodzo le Farao gbɔ la, wokpe Mose kple Aron, amesiwo tsi tre ɖi, be woaɖo go wo

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ na wo bena: Yehowa adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu mi, eye wòakpɔ me na mi. Elabena miena miede asi ʋeʋẽ me ɖe Farao kple eŋuti mewo, gɔ̃ la miede yi asi na wo, be woatso awu mí.

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Tete Mose trɔ ɖe Yehowa; ŋu gblɔ bena: Aƒetɔ! Nukaŋuti nèhe vɔ̃ sia va dukɔ la dzi? Nukata gɔ̃ nedɔm ɖo?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Elabena tso esime meva Farao gbɔ, eye meƒo nu le wo ŋkɔa me la, azɔ gɔ̃ wòle ŋuta sẽm le dukɔ la ŋu; ke wò la meɖe dukɔ la kpɔ o.

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Azɔ akpɔ nusi mele Farao wɔ ge. Alɔ sesẽ ana wòaɖe asi le wo ŋu, eye alɔ sesẽ ana wòanya wo atso eƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: Nyee ɖe ɖokuinye fia Abraham, Isak kple Yakob abe Mawu ŋusẽkatãtɔ ene, ke nyemeɖe nye ŋkɔ Yehowa fia wo o.

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: Mebia nu kpli wo be, matsɔ Kanaan-nyigba, si dzi wonye amedzrowo le la, ana wo wòanye wo tɔ.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Eye azɔ mese Israel-viwo ƒe konyi, si wòta le Egiptetɔwo ƒe wo teteɖanyi la ŋuti, eye meɖo ŋku nye nubabla la dzi.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: Eyata gblɔ na Israel-viwo bena: Nyee nye Yehowa! Makplɔ mí le dɔ sesẽ, si wɔm miele na Egiptetɔwo la nu, eye mana miavo atso miaƒe kluvidɔ la me, eye mado nye alɔ ɖa atsɔ ŋusẽ gã aɖe mi.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Mawɔ mi mianye nye dukɔ, eye manye miaƒe Mawu, eye miadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa, miaƒe Mawu, amesi kplɔ mi le dɔ sesẽ la nu tso Egipte.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: Eye makplɔ mi ayi anyigba, si ŋu meka atam ɖo be, matsɔ na Abraham, Isak kple Yakob la dzi. Nye Yehowa matsɔe na mi wòanye mia tɔ.

english_verse: When Moses told this to the Israelites, they were too discouraged and mistreated to believe him.
translation_verse: Eye Mose va gblɔ nyawo na Israel-viwo, ke woawo meɖo to Mose o, elabena womegale dzi ɖom ɖe amea ɖeke ŋu o, le dɔ sesẽ la ta.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Emegbe Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena:

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: Yi ɖaƒo nu kple Farao, Egipte-fia bena: Ɖe asi le Israel-viwo ŋuti woadzo le wo anyigba dzi.

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Eye Mose ɖo ŋu na Yehowa bena: Esi Israel-viwo mele to ɖomem o la, aleke Farao aɖo to nye amesi nu menya ƒona na o la!

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose kple Aron, eye wòdo wo de Israel-viwo kple Farao, Egipte-fia gbɔ, bena woakplɔ Israel-viwo atso Egipte-nyigba dzi. Dzidzimegbalẽ.

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Esiawo nye aƒehanuawo le woƒe ƒome la me. Ruben, Israel ƒe ŋgɔgbevi, ƒe viwo nye: Henox, Palu, Xezron kple Karmi; esiawo nye Ruben-hawo.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Simeon viwo nye: Yemuel, Yamin, Ohad, Yaxin kple Zoxar kpakple Saul, si nye Kanaan-nyɔnu ƒe vi; esiawo nye Simeon-hawo.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Gerson viwo nye Libni kple Simei le woƒe dzidzime nu.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Merari viwo nye: Maxeli kple Musi; esiawo nye Lewi-hawo le woƒe dzidzime nu.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Yizhar viwo nye: Korax, Nefeg kple Sixri.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Uziel viwo nye: Misael, Elzafan kple Sitri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Eye Aron ɖe Eliseba, Aminadab vinyɔnu, amesi nye Naxason nɔvinyɔnu, eye wòdzi Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar kple Itamar nɛ.

english_verse: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph.
translation_verse: Korax viwo nye: Asir, Elkana kple Abiasaf; esiawo nye Korax-hawo.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Eye Eleazar, Aron vi ɖe Putiel vinyɔnuwo dometɔ ɖeka, amesi dzi Pinexas nɛ. Ame siawo nye Lewi viwo ƒe aƒehánuawo le woƒe ƒome la nu.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Esiawo nye Aron kple Mose, amesiwo Yehowa gblɔ na bena: Mikplɔ Israel-viwo ƒe hawo dzo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi!

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Amesiwo yi ɖagblɔ na Farao, Egipte-fia bena, yewoakplɔ Israel-viwo atso Egipte, wonye Mose kple Aron.

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Esi Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose le Egipte la,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Nyee nye Yehowa! Yi ɖagblɔ nya, siwo katã magblɔ na wò la, na Farao, Egipte-fia.

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Ke Mose gblɔ na Yehowa bena: Nu menya ƒona nam o; aleke awɔ Farao aɖo to nye gbe?

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Yehowa ɖo ŋu na Mose bena: Mana nanye Mawu ɖe Farao nu, eye nɔviwò Aron nanye wò nyanuɖela.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Gblɔ nya, siwo katã magblɔ na wò la, eye nɔviwò Aron nagblɔe na Farao be, wòaɖe asi le Israel-viwo ŋu woadzo le eƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: Ke Farao maɖo to mi o, eye mado nye asi ɖe Egiptetɔwo gbɔ, eye matsɔ ŋusẽ gã akplɔ nye amehawo, nye dukɔ Israel-viwo atso Egipte.

english_verse: When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ekema Egiptetɔwo adze sii bena, nyee nye Yehowa, ne medo nye asi ɖe Egipte dzi, eye mekplɔ Israel-viwo dzoe le wo dome.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord
translation_verse: Alesi Yehowa ɖe se na Mose kple Aron la, nenema wowɔ.

english_verse: and spoke to the king. At the time, Moses was
translation_verse: Mose xɔ ƒe blanyi, eye Aron xɔ ƒe blanyi vɔ etɔ̃, esime woƒo nu kple Farao.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: Ne Farao abia nukunua ɖe tso mia si la, ekema gblɔ na Aron bena: Tsɔ wò atikplɔ da ɖe Farao ƒe ŋku me! eye wòatrɔ zu da gãa ɖe.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Tete Mose kple Aron woyi Farao gbɔ, eye wowɔ, abe alesi Yehowa de se na wo ene. Aron tsɔ eƒe atikplɔ da ɖe Farao kple eŋuti mewo ƒe ŋku me, eye wòtrɔ zu da gãa ɖe.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Ke Farao hã yɔ nunyalawo kple afakalawo vɛ, eye Egiptetɔwo ƒe akunyawɔlawo tsɔ woƒe aye me nuwɔwɔwo wɔe nenemake.

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: Wo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe tsɔ eƒe atikplɔ ɖa ɖe anyi, tete wotrɔ zu da gãwo; ke Aron ƒe atikplɔ lé woƒe atikplɔwo mi.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Gake Farao ƒe dzime sẽ, eye meɖo to wo o, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ ene. Fukpekpe gbãtɔ: Tsi trɔ zu nu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Emegbe Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Farao ƒe dzime sẽ, eye wogbe asiɖeɖe le dukɔ la ŋuti.

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Yi Farao gbɔ ŋdi kanya: kpɔ ɖa, ayi to la nu, eye natsɔ atikplɔ, si zu da la, ɖe asi aɖado goe le Nil-tɔsisi la to.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: Eye nagblɔ nɛ bena: Yehowa, Hebritɔwo ƒe Mawu la, dom ɖo ɖe gbɔwò, be yeagblɔ na wò bena: Ɖe asi le nye dukɔa ŋuti, ne wòaɖasubɔm le gbedzi! Ke meɖo to vaseɖe fifi o.

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esia natsɔ anyae bena, nyee nye Yehowa. Matsɔ atikplɔ, si le asinye la, aƒo Nil-tɔsisi me tsia dzi, eye wòatrɔ zu ʋu.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Eye lã, siwo le Nil me la, laku, eye tɔ la aɖe asi ʋeʋẽ me, ale be Egiptetɔwo anyɔ ŋu tɔa me tsi nono.

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Gblɔ na Aron bena: Tsɔ wò atikplɔ, eye nado wò asi ɖe Egiptetɔwo ƒe tsiwo dzi, ɖe woƒe tɔsisiwo, tɔʋuwo, tawo kple tsiteƒewo katã dzi, bena woatrɔ zu ʋu, eye ʋu nanɔ Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi le goewo kple zewo me.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Eye Mose kple Aron wɔ, abe alesi Yehowa de se na wo ene. Eye wotsɔ eƒe atikplɔ ƒo Nil me tsi la dzi le Farao kple eŋuti mewo ƒe ŋku me, tete tsi, siwo katã le Nil me la, trɔ zu ʋu.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Eye lã, siwo katã le Nil me la, ku, eye lɔ la de asi ʋeʋẽ me, ale be Egiptetɔwo megate ŋu no Nil me tsi o. Eye ʋu le Egipte-nyigba dzi afisiafi.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Ke Egipte-tɔwo ƒe akunyawɔlawo tsɔ woƒe ave me nuwɔwɔwo wɔe nenema ke. Eye Farao ƒe dzime sẽ, eye meɖo to wo o abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ ene.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Tete Farao trɔ yi aƒe me, eye meɖo toe na wo o.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Eye Egiptetɔwo ɖe vudowo ɖe Nil ŋu, bena woakpɔ tsi ano, elabena womete ŋu no tɔa me tsi la o.

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: Esi Yehowa gblẽ Nil me tsia la, etsi nenema ŋkeke adre sɔŋ. Etsɔ fukpekpe evelia do ŋɔdzi nɛ.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Gblɔ na Aron be: Do wo asi kple atikplɔ ɖe tɔsisiwo, tɔʋuwo kple tawo dzi, eye nahe akpɔkplɔwo ava Egipte-nyigba la dzi!

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Tete Aron do eƒe asi ɖe Egiptetɔwo ƒe tɔwo dzi, eye akpɔkplɔwo do hexɔ Egipte-nyigba la dzi.

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Mose ɖo ŋu na Farao bena: Ele asiwò me! Ɣekaɣie maɖe kuku la ɖe wò ŋutɔ, ŋuwò mewo kple wò dukɔ la ta, bena akpɔkplɔawo nadzo le ŋuwo kple aƒewò me, eye woasusɔ ɖe Nil ko me?

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Wò ŋuta kple wò aƒe, ŋuwò mewo kple wo dukɔ la miakpɔ gbɔdzɔe tso akpɔkplɔwo si me, negbe Nil me ko woasusɔ ɖo

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Esi Mose kple Aron wodzo le Farao gbɔ la, Mose do gbe ɖa na Yehowa le akpɔkplɔ, siwo wokplɔ ƒu Farao la ŋuti.

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa wɔ Mose ƒe nya la dzi, eye akpɔkplɔ, siwo le aƒewo me, xɔxɔnuwo kple agblewo me la, ku.

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Eye wolɔ wo li kɔ gagãwoe, eye anyigba la katã dzi va ʋeʋẽ ge kũ.

english_verse: and frogs will no longer be found anywhere, except in the Nile.”
translation_verse: Ke esi Farao kpɔ bena, yekpɔ gbɔdzɔe la, esẽ eƒe dzime, eye meɖo to wo o, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ ene. Fukpekpe etɔ̃lia: mũwo.

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Gblɔ na Aron be: Tsɔ wo atikplɔ, eye naƒo ke me le anyigba dzi, ekema atrɔ zu mũwo ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Eye afakalawo hã tsɔ woƒe aye me nuwɔwɔwo wɔe nenema, be woahe mũwo vɛ, ke womete ŋui o. Eye mũawo nɔ amewo kple lãwo ŋu.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Eye afakalawo gblɔ na Farao bena: Esia la Mawu ƒe asibidee! Ke Farao ƒe dzime sẽ, eye meɖo to wo o, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ ene. Fukpekpe enelia: togbatowo.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Emegbe Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Yi Farao gbɔ ŋdi kanya, ne eyi tɔa nu la, eye nagblɔ nɛ bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Ɖe asi le nye dukɔ la ŋuti, bena wòaɖasubɔm!

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Ke ne ègbe asiɖeɖe le nye dukɔa ŋu la, ekema mana togbatowo nava ɖo wò ŋutɔ, ŋuwò mewo kple dukɔ la dome, eye woava aƒewò me; Egipte-tɔwo ƒe xɔwo me kple anyigba, si dzi wotsi tre ɖo gɔ̃ hã ayɔ fũ kple togbatowo.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Gbemagbe maɖe Gosen-nyigba, si dzi nye dukɔ le la, le eme, eye togbatoawo made afima o, bena nanyae be, nyee nye Yehowa le anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Eye made vovo nye dukɔ kple wò dukɔ dome; etsɔe dzesi sia ava me!

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa wo nenema; tete togbato geɖe fũ va Farao ƒe aƒe kple eŋu mewo ƒe xɔwo me kpakple Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi, eye togbatoawo gblẽ anyigba la.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Eye Farao yɔ Mose kple Aron vɛ, eye wògblɔ na wo be: Enyo, miɖasa vɔ na mia Mawu la le anyigba sia dzi!

english_verse: “The Lord's people in Goshen won't be bothered by flies, but your people in the rest of the country will be tormented by them. That's how you will know that the Lord is here in Egypt. This miracle will happen tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Míazɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃ ƒe mo ayi gbeɖzi, ne míasa vɔ na Yehowa, mía Mawu la le afima, abe alesi wòɖe se na mí ene.

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Farao gblɔ bena: Maɖe asi le mia ŋu, be miaɖasa vɔ na Yehowa, mia Mawu la le gbedzi, ke ɖeko migayi didiƒe akpa o. Eye miaɖe kuku ɖe nye hã tanye.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Mose ɖo ŋu bena: Ne menya dzo le gbɔwò ko, maɖe; kuku na Yehowa, bena wòana togbatoawo nadzo le Farao kple eŋu mewo kpakple dukɔ la dome etsɔ; ɖeko Farao megablem agbe asiɖeɖe le dukɔ la ŋu, be womagayi aɖasa vɔ na Yehowa o!

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa wɔ, Mose ƒe nyawo dzi, eye wòɖe togbatoawo ɖa le Farao kple eŋu mewo kpakple dukɔ la dome, ale be ɖeka hã hã megasusɔ ɖi o.

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Ke Farao sẽ eƒe dzime fifia hã, eye meɖe asi le dukɔ la ŋu woyi o.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Yi Farao gbɔ, eye nagblɔ ne bena: Ale Yehowa, Hebritɔwo ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Ɖe asi le nye dukɔ la ŋu, bena wòaɖasubɔm!

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: ekema Yehowa ƒe asi alé wò lãha, siwo le gbedzi, eye adza sesẽa ɖe aƒo sɔwo, tedziwo, kposɔwo, nyiwo kple alẽwo.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa ade vovo Israel-viwo ƒe lãwo kple Egiptetɔwo to dome, eye lã, siwo nye Israel-viwo to la, dome ɖeke maku o.

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ɖo ŋkeke gblɔ bena: Etsɔ Yehowa ana nu sia ava anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, Yehowa na wòva me. Eye Egipte-tɔwo ƒe lãwo katã ku; ke Israel-viwo ƒe lãwo dome ɖeka hã meku o.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Emegbe Yehowa gblɔ na Mose kple Aron bena: Miɖe kpo me dzɔble ɖe miaƒe asiʋlowo me, eye Mose nahlẽe ɖe ya me le Farao ƒe ŋku me;

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: ekema azu ʋuʋu akaka ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi, eye wòatrɔ zu ƒoƒoe, siwo me dɔvɔ̃ aɖo, ɖe amewo kple lãwo siaa ŋu, le Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi.

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Eye woɖe kpo me dzɔble la heva tsi tre ɖe Farao ƒe ŋku me, eye Mose tsɔe hlẽ ɖe ya me; tete wòtrɔ zu ƒoƒoe, siwo me dɔvɔ̃ ɖo, ɖe amewo kple lãwo siaa ŋu.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Ke afakalawo mete ŋu no te ɖe Mose nu o, le ƒoƒoeawo ta, elabena ƒoƒoeawo te afakalawo hã abe Egiptetɔwo katã ene.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa na Farao ƒe dzime sẽ, eye meɖo to wo o, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ na Mose ene. Fukpekpe adrelia: tsikpe.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Eyome Yehowa gblɔ na Mese bena: Yi Farao gbɔ ŋdi kanya, eye nagblɔ ne be: Ale Yehowa, Hebritɔwo ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Ɖe asi le nye dukɔ la ŋuti, bena wòaɖasubɔm!

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: Ne menye nenem o la, mala nye fuwɔamewo katã atrɔ ɖe wò ŋutɔ, ŋuwò mewo kple dukɔ la dzi, bena nanyae be, amea ɖeke mede nunye le anyigba blibo la katã dzi o.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Elabena mate ŋu ado nye asi ɖa atsɔ dɔvɔ̃ agblẽ wò ŋutɔ kple wò dukɔ, ale be natsrɔ̃ le anyigba la dzi xoxoxo hafi,

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: gake megblẽ wò ɖi vaseɖe fifi, bena maɖe nye ŋusẽ afia wò, eye woakafu nye ŋkɔ le anyigba blibo la katã dzi.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Ke ne egagbe asiɖeɖe le nye dukɔa ŋu la,

english_verse: All right. At this time tomorrow, he will bring on Egypt the worst hailstorm in its history.
translation_verse: ekema mana kpetsi gãwo nadza etsɔ wɔale siawo, esiwo tɔgbe medza ɖe Egipte-nyigba dzi kpɔ o vaseɖe fifi, tso esime woɖo egɔme anyi.

english_verse: You had better give orders for every person and every animal in Egypt to take shelter. If they don't, they will die.
translation_verse: Eyata dɔ woadzra wò lãha kple wò nusianu, si le gbedzi la ɖo, elabena ame kple lã, siwo katã gale gbedzi, eye womeyi xɔ me o la, kpetsi la adza ɖe wo dzi, eye wòawu wo.

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Eye Farao ŋuti mewo dometɔ, si ke Yehowa ƒe nya la tso dzika ƒo na la, na wokplɔ eƒe dɔlawo kple lãhawo si yi xɔ mee.

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: Ke amesi ke mebu Yehowa ƒe nya la o la, gblẽ eƒe dɔlawo kple lãhawo ɖe gbedzi.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Do wò asi ɖe dziƒo, bena kpetsi nadza ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi, ɖe amewo kple lãwo siaa kpakple agblemenuwo katã dzi le Egipte-nyigba la dzi!

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: Kpetsia le dzadzam, eye dzi le dzo kem ɖe eme edziedzi; kpetsia nu sẽ ŋutɔ, eye etɔgbe medza ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi kpɔ o, tso esime amewo va edzi.

english_verse: People, animals, and crops were pounded by the hailstones, and bark was stripped from trees.
translation_verse: Eye kpetsia gblẽ nusianu, si le gbedzi, le Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi hewu amewo kple lãwo siaa, eye kpetsia gblẽ agblemenuwo katã, eye wòle gbemetiwo katã.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Negbe Gosen-nyigba, si dzi Israel-viwo le ko, dzi kpetsia ɖeke mede o.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Tete Farao do woɖayɔ Mose kple Aron vɛ, eye wògblɔ na wo bena: Meda vo! Yehowa tɔ dzɔ, ke mía kple nye dukɔ la to medzo o.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Miɖaɖe kuku na Yehowa, bena wòana dziɖegbe kple kpetsi la nu natso; ekema maɖe asi le mia ŋu, eye miaganɔ afisia o.

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Mose ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Ne menya do le dua me ko la, make nye abɔwo me na Yehowa, bena dziɖegbe la nu natso, eye kpetsia nadzudzɔ dzadza, ne nanyae be, Yehowa ta enye anyigba la.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Ke menyae be, wò ŋutɔ kple ŋuwò mewo miele Yehowa Mawu vɔ̃m haɖe o.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Eye ɖeti kple mɔli gblẽ, elabena mɔli ɖi, eye ɖeti ƒo se.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Ke lu kple bli ya megblẽ o, elabena womekpɔ mie haɖe o.

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Emegbe Mese dzo le Farao gbɔ, eye esi wòdo le dua me la, eke eƒe abɔwo me na Yehowa, tete dziɖegbe kple kpetsi la nu tso, eye tsi dzudzɔ dzadza ɖe anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Ke esi Farao kpɔ bena, tsidzadza, kpetsi kple dziɖegbe la nu tso la, egayi nu vɔ̃ wɔwɔ dzi, eye eva kple eŋu mewo sẽ woƒe dzime.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Eye Farao ƒe dzime sẽ, eye meɖe asi le Israel-viwo ŋu o, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ to Mose dzi ene.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Emegbe Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Yi Farao gbɔ, elabena nyee na eya ŋutɔ kple eŋu mewo ƒe dzime sẽ, bena mawɔ nye dzesi siawo le wo dome;

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: eye bene nava xlẽ nusiwo mewɔ Egiptetɔwo kple dzesi, siwo mewɔ le wo dome la, afia viwòwo kple wò tɔgbuiyɔviwo, bena miadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Tete Mose kple Aron woyi Farao gbɔ, eye wogblɔ nɛ bena: Ale Yehowa, Hebritɔwo ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi. Zi nenie gɔ̃ nagbe be, yemabɔbɔ ɖokuiwò nam oa? Ɖe asi le nye dukɔ la ŋuti, bena wòaɖasubɔm!

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: Ke ne egbe asiɖeɖe le nye dukɔ ŋu la, ekema mana ʋetsuviwo nava wò anyigba dzi etsɔ.

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: Eye woanye atsyɔ anyigba blibo la katã dzi, ale bena anyigba magadze o; woaɖu nu mamlea, siwo kpetsia tso ɖi na mi la, eye woaɖu miaƒe ati, siwo gadze le gbe me la.

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: Eye wòayi ɖe wò xɔwo, ŋuwò mewo ƒe xɔwo kple Egiptetɔwo katã ƒe xɔwo me taŋ, nusi teƒe fofowòwo kple tɔgbuiwòwo mekpɔ kpɔ vaseɖe fifi, tso esime wova anyigba la dzi o. Tete wòtrɔ dzo le Farao gbɔ.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Eye Farao ŋu mewo gblɔ nɛ bena: Zi nenie gɔ̃ ame sia anye mɔ̃ anɔ mía ɖem? Ɖe asi le ameawo ŋu, be woaɖasubɔ Yehowa, woƒe Mawu! Mèle ekpɔm haɖe be, Egipte le gbagbãm oa?

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: Tete wogagbugbɔ Mose kple Aron va Farao gbɔ, eye wògblɔ na wo bena: Miheyi ɖasubɔ Yehowa, mia Mawu la! Ameka kple amekawoe le yiyi ge?

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Mose ɖo ŋu bena: Miele mía viwo kple míaƒe amegã ɖeɖiwo kplɔ ge ɖe asi; miele mía viŋutsuwo kple mía vinyɔnuwo, miaƒe alẽwo kple míaƒe nyiwo kplɔ ge ɖe asi; elabena ŋkekenyuie ɖu ge míeyina na Yehowa.

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu na wo bena: Yehowa naɖi na mi! Maɖe asi le mia kple mia viwo siaa ŋua? Nyateƒee, mieɖo vɔ̃ ɖe tame.

english_verse: Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
translation_verse: Gbeɖe! Ŋutsuwo ko nayi aɖasubɔ Yehowa, elabena alea míeɖi! Eye wonyã wo dzo le Farao gbɔe.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward Egypt. Swarms of locusts will come and eat everything left by the hail.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Do wò asi ɖe Egipte-nyigba dzi, be nakplɔ ʋetsuviwo vɛ, ne woava Egipte-nyigba dzi aɖu gbe, siwo katã le anyigba dzi kpakple nusianu, si kpetsia tso ɖi la.

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Tete Mose do eƒe atikplɔ ɖe Egipte-nyigba dzi, eye Yehowa na ɣedzeƒeya ƒo ɖe anyigba la dzi ŋkeke blibo la katã kple zã blibo la katã, eye esi ŋu ke la, ɣedzeƒeya la kplɔ ʋetsuviwo vɛ.

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Eye ʋetsuviawo ƒo ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi, eye wodze ɖe anyigba la ƒe afisiafi taŋtaŋ; wo tɔgbe meva kpɔ o, eye magava alea hã akpɔ o.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: Eye wonye tsyo anyigba blibo la katã dzi, ale bena anyigba megale dzedzem o; woɖu gbe me nu miemiewo katã kple kutsetse, siwo kpetsia tso ɖi, eye aŋgba mumũa ɖeke megale atiwo kple gbe me nu miemiewo dzi le Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi o.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Tete Farao na woyɔ Mose kple Aron ve kaba eye wògblɔ bena: Meda vo ɖe Yehowa, mia Mawu la, kple mia ŋuti.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: Eyata mitso nye vodada la kem fifia hã, eye miɖe kuku na Yehowa, mia Mawu la, ɖe tanye, bena wòaɖe ku sia ɖa le dzinye!

english_verse: Moses left the palace and prayed.
translation_verse: Tete wòdzo le Farao gbɔ, eye wòdo gbe ɖa na Yehowa.

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa na ɣetoɖoƒeya sesẽa ɖe ƒo, eye wòlɔ ʋetsuviawo ɖe nu ɖakɔ ɖe Avaƒu la me, ale be ʋetsuviawo dometɔa ɖeke megatsi Egipte-nyigba la ƒe afia ɖeke o.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa na Farao ƒe dzime sẽ, eye meɖe asi le Israel-viwo ŋuti woyi o. Fukpekpe asiekelia: viviti.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Do wò asi ɖe dziƒo, bena viviti nado ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi, ale bena woate ŋu ali asi viviti la ŋu.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Tete Mose do eƒe asi ɖe dziƒo, eye viviti tsiɖitsiɖia ɖe do ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi ŋkeke etɔ̃ sɔŋ.

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
translation_verse: Amea ɖeke mete ŋu kpɔ nɔvia o, eye amea ɖeke mete ŋu dzo le enɔƒe o ŋkeke etɔ̃ sɔŋ. Ke kekeli le Israel-viwo katã ƒe nɔƒewo.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Eye Farao yɔ Mose vɛ gblɔ bena: Miheyi ɖasubɔ Yehowa la! Miaƒe alẽwo kple nyiwo natsi anyi, ke mia vi suewo nayi kpli mi.

english_verse: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
translation_verse: Mose ɖo ŋu bena: Ele be, wò ŋuta hã natsɔ vɔsalã kple numelã na mí, bena míatsɔ wo ana Yehowa, mía Mawu la!

english_verse: and we won't know which animals we will need until we get there. That's why we can't leave even one of them here.”
translation_verse: Ke míakplɔ míaƒe lãwo hã ɖe asi, afɔkli gɔ̃ hã matsi anyi o; elabena woawo ƒe ɖe tsa ge míala asubɔ Yehowa, mia Mawu lae. Mienyã nusi tso ge míala asubɔ Yehowa haɖe o, vaseɖe esime míaɖo afima hafi.

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Gake Yehowa na Farao ƒe dzime sẽ, eye melɔ̃ be, yeaɖe asi le wo ŋu o.

english_verse: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
translation_verse: Eye Farao gblɔ nɛ bena: Te ɖa le gbɔnye! Kpɔ nyuie, bena nagava nye ŋku ta azɔ o, elabena gbesigbe nagava nye ŋku ta la, ku ke naku!

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Mose ɖo ŋu bena: Yoo, wòe ƒo nu loo! Nyemegale wò ŋku ta va ge azɔ o.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Esusɔ fuwɔame ɖeka mahe ava Farao kple Egiptetɔwo dzii; emegbe la aɖe asi le mia ŋu miadzo le afisia. Ke menye asi ko wòaɖe le mia ŋu o; boŋ anyẽ mi atso afisia.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Eyata gblɔ na dukɔ la bena: Ŋutsu sia ŋutsu kple nyɔnu sia nyɔnu nabia klosalo kple sikanuwo le eƒe aƒelika si!

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa na Egipte-tɔwo ve dukɔ la nu, eye Farao ŋu mewo kple eƒe dukɔ la bu Mese ŋuta le Egipte-nyigba dzi. Ŋɔdzidodo na Egiptetɔwo kple fukpekpe ewolia.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ be: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi. Le zã titina la mele Egipte-nyigba me to ge ayi,

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: eye ŋgɔgbeviwo katã aku le Egipte-nyigba dzi, tso Farao ƒe ŋgɔgbevi, si ava no eƒe zi dzi la dzi vaseɖe kosi, si le teƒo, ƒe ŋgɔgbevi kpakple lãwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo katã dzi.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Eye nublanuiɣli aɖi le Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi, esi tɔgbe meva kpɔ o, eye magava hã akpa o.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Ke avũ mawo ɖe ame alo lã ŋu le Israel-viwo katã dome o, bena mianyae be, Yehowa de vovo Egiptetɔwo kple Israel-viwo dome.

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: Emegbe ŋutiwò me siawo katã ava gbɔnye, eye woade ta agu nam agblɔ bena: Wò ŋutɔ kple amesiwo katã le ŋuwò la, miyi! Emegbe hafi madzo Eye wòdzo le Farao gbɔ kple dziku gã ŋutɔ.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena Farao maɖo to mi o, bena nye nukunuwo nasɔ gbe le Egipte-nyigba la dzi.

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Eye Mose kple Aron wowɔ nukunu siawo katã le Farao ƒe ŋku me; ke Yehowa na Farao ƒe dzime sẽ, eye meɖe asi le Israel-viwo ŋu wodzo le eƒe anyigba dzi o.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose kple Aron le Egipte-nyigba dzi bena:

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: Ɣleti sia nanye vevietɔ na mi, eya nanye ɣleti gbãtɔ na mi le ƒe la me.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Migblɔ na Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la katã bena: Le ɣleti sia ƒe ŋkeke ewolia dzi la ŋutsu sia ŋutsu nalé alẽvi ɖeka; aƒe sia aƒe, si me aƒehánua le la, nalé alẽvi ɖeka.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Eye miadzrae ɖo vaseɖe ɣleti sia ƒe ŋkeke wuienelia dzi, eye Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la nawui le fiẽ me.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Eye woatsɔ nu la ƒe ɖe asisi ɖe xɔ, siwo me wole eɖu ge le la, ƒe ʋɔtrutiawo kple eve kpakple etametɔ ŋuti.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Woame lã la aɖu le zã ma me, eye woatsɔ abolo maʋamaʋã kple ama veve adoe.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Migaɖui mumũ alo aɖae hafi o; ke boŋ miamee ɖo nogo, eye la kple afɔwo nanɔ enu.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: Migagblẽ ɖeke ɖi ŋu nake ɖe edzi o, eye esi tsi anyi ŋu ke de dzi la, mitɔ dzoe.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Ale mianɔ hafi aɖui enye si. Mibla miaƒe aliwo dzi, eye mido atokotawo de afɔ; milé atizɔtiwo ɖe asi, eye miɖui abe sisilawo ene, elabena Yehowa ƒe ŋutilotoŋkekenyuie ve.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: Elabena mele Egipte-nyigba dzi to ge le zã ma me, eye mawu amewo kple lãwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo le Egipte-nyigba la dzi, eye made nye ŋusẽ afia Egipte-trɔ̃wo katã hã, nye Yehowa!

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Eye ʋu, si anɔ xɔ, siwo me miele la ŋu la, ade dzesi mi; elabena ne mekpɔ ʋua la, mato mia ŋuti, eye tuwɔamea ɖeke magblẽ mi, ne meyina Egiptetɔwo wu ge o.

english_verse: Remember this day and celebrate it each year as a festival in my honor.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke sia nanye ŋkuɖodzigbe na mi, eye mianɔ eɖum na Yehowa, wòanye ɖoɖo na miaƒe dzidzimeviwo, be miaɖui tegbee.

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
