translation_verse: Ŋkeke adre sɔŋ mianɔ abolo maʋamaʋã ɖum; tso ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi ke miaɖe amɔwɔ ʋaʋã ɖa tso miaƒe xɔwo me, elabena amesi ke agaɖu abolo ʋaʋã tso ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi vaseɖe ŋkeke adrelia dzi la, woaɖee ɖa le Israel-viwo dome.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi miawɔ takpekpe kɔkɔea de, eye le ŋkeke adrelia dzi hã miawɔ takpekpe kɔkɔea ɖe. Migawɔ dɔa ɖeke le wo dzi o, negbe nusi amesiame aɖu la, eya ko miaɖa.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: Miɖo ŋku abolo maʋamaʋã la dzi, elabena gbemagbe mekplɔ miaƒe amehawo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi. Eyata mido ŋku ŋkeke sia dzi, be wòanye ɖoɖo na miaƒe dzidzimeviwo tegbee!

english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti gbãtɔ me, tso ɣleti la ƒe ŋkeke wuienelia ƒe fiẽ miadze abolo maʋamaʋã ɖuɖu gɔme vaseɖe ɣleti la ƒe ŋkeke blave vɔ ɖekɛlia ƒe fiẽ.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke adre sɔŋ womakpɔ amɔwɔ ʋaʋã le miaƒe xɔwo me o, elabena amesiame, si aɖu abolo ʋaʋã la, woaɖee ɖa le Israel-viwo ƒe ha me, eɖanye amedzro alo dumevi o.

english_verse: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
translation_verse: Migade nu abolo ʋaʋãa ɖeke ŋu o, eye afisiafi, si miele la, miaɖu abolo maʋamaʋã sɔŋ.

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
translation_verse: Eye Mose yɔ Israel-viwo ƒe ame tsitsiwo katã vɛ, eye wògblɔ na wo be: Miyi ɖalé alẽ ɖe miaƒe aƒewo nu, eye miawui hena ŋutitotoŋkekenyuie la!

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Eye mitsɔ isop babla nyrɔ̃ ɖe ʋu, si le ze me la me, eye miatsɔ ʋu, si le zea me la, asisi ɖe ʋɔtruti eveawo kple etametɔ ŋuti. Ke mia dometɔa ɖeke megado go le xɔ me ɖe ʋɔtru nu, vaseɖe ŋu nake o!

english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
translation_verse: Elabena ne Yehowa yina Egiptetɔwo gblẽ ge, eye wòkpɔ ʋu, si le ʋɔtruti eveawo kple etametɔ ŋuti la, Yehowa ato ʋɔtru la ŋu, eye mana nugblẽla la nage ɖe miaƒe xɔwo me awu mi o.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Ne mieva anyigba, si Yehowa le mia na ge la dzi, abe alesi wògblɔ na mi ene la, ekema miɖo ŋku subɔsubɔ sia dzi.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Eye ne mia viwo abia mi be: miaƒe subɔsubɔ sia gɔme ɖe mahã la,

english_verse: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: ekema migblɔ na wo bena: Esia enye ŋutitotovɔsa na Yehowa, amesi tso míaƒe aƒewo ɖi le Egipte-nyigba dzi, eye wowu Egiptetɔwo; ke ekpɔ miaƒe aƒewo ta. Tete dukɔ la de ta agu, eye wodo gbe ɖa.

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo wɔ, abe alesi Yehowa de se na Mose kple Aron ene; nenema wowɔ. Ŋgɔgbeviwo wuwu.

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Le zã titina la Yehowa wu ŋgɔgbeviwo katã le Egipte-nyigba dzi, tso Farao ƒe ŋgɔgbevi, si le eƒe zi dzi la dzi vaseɖe gatɔ, si le gaxɔ me la, ƒe ŋgɔgbevi kpakple lãwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo katã dzi.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Tete Farao kple eŋu mewo kpakple Egiptetɔwo katã fɔ le zã titina, eye avifafa de dzi le Egipte-nyigba dzi hoo, elabena aƒea ɖeke meli, si me ame meku le o.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Eye wòyɔ Mose kple Aron vɛ le zã me gblɔ bena: Netsɔ, midzo le nye dukɔ la dome, mia ŋutɔwo kple Israel-viwo; miyi ɖasubɔ Yehowa, abe alesi miegblɔ ene.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Mikplɔ miaƒe alẽwo kple nyiwo hã ɖe asi yii, abe alesi miegblɔ ene, eye miɖayra nye hã!

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Eye Egiptetɔwo ƒo ɖu ɖe dukɔ la nu, be woadzo le anyigba la dzi kaba, elabena wogblɔ be: Mí katã miele kuku ge! Gododo tso Egipte dze gɔme.

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Eye dukɔ la tsɔ woƒe amɔwo, si mekpɔ ʋã haɖe o la, kpakple woƒe amɔwɔkpakuwo bia ɖe woƒe avɔwo me helé ɖe abɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo wɔe ɖe Mose ƒe nya la nu, eye wobia klosalo kple sikanuwo kpakple avɔwo le Egiptetɔwo si.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa na Egiptetɔwo ve dukɔ la nu, eye wolɔ̃ edzi na wo. Ale woha Egiptetɔwo enye si.

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ʋu tso Ramses va Sukot; ŋutsu, siwo katã zɔ afɔ, anɔ ame akpe alafa ade, ɖeviwo mele eme o.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Amedzro geɖewo hã kpe ɖe wo ŋuti, eye wokplɔ alẽwo kple nyiwo, lãha gã ŋuta, ɖe asi.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ amɔwɔ, si wotsɔ tso Egipte la, ƒo akaklãe, ke meʋã o, elabena esi wonyã wo tso Egipte la, womete ŋu ta ɖi, ne woaɖa nu aɖo asi o.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Eyata wodɔa ŋu na Yehowa le zã ma me, elabena ekplɔ wo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi. Esia enye zã, si me Israel-viwo kple woƒe dzidzimeviwo katã anɔ ŋu dom na Yehowa le. Sedede le ŋutitotolẽvia ɖuɖu ŋuti.

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose kple Aron bena: Esia enye ŋutitotoŋkekenyuie la ŋu ɖoɖowo: Amedzroa ɖeke mekpɔ mɔ aɖui o.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Ke ne amea ɖe ƒle ŋutsua ɖe kple ga la, wòatso aʋa ne, hafi wòakpɔ mɔ aɖui.

english_verse: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
translation_verse: Amedzro kple agbatedɔwɔla mekpe mo aɖui o.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: Xɔ ɖeka me woaɖui ale; migatsɔ lã la ƒe ɖeke do go le xɔ me ɖe xexe o, eye migagbã eƒe ƒua ɖeke o.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Eye Israel ha blibo la nawɔ alea.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Ke ne amedzroa ɖe le gbɔwò, le didim be, yeaɖu ŋutitotoŋkekenyuie na Yehowa la, ekema wo dome ŋutsu sia ŋutsu natso aʋa, hafi woate va aɖui, eye woabui abe dumevi ene; ke bolobolotɔa ɖeke mekpɔ mɔ aɖui o.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Se ɖeka ano eŋu na dumevi kple amedzro, si le mia dome la siaa.

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo katã wɔ, abe alesi Yehowa de se na Mose kple Aron ene; nenema wowɔ.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Gbemagbe Yehowa kplɔ Israel-viwo ƒe amehawo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena:

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: Kɔ ŋgɔgbeviwo katã ŋuti nam, nusianu, si aʋu dɔ nu na dada le Israel-viwo dome, eɖanye ame alo lã o, tɔnyee. Abolo maʋamaʋã ŋu se.

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Ne Yehowa akplɔ wò ava Kanaanitɔwo, Xititɔwo, Amoritɔwo, Xiwitɔwo kple Yebusitɔwo ƒe anyigba, si ŋu wòka atam ɖo na fofowòwo be, yeatsɔe na wò, anyigba, si dzi notsi kple anyitsi bɔ ɖo la dzi la, ekema naɖo ŋku subɔsubɔ sia dzi.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Abolo maʋamaʋã miaɖu ŋkeke adre sɔŋ, eye womekpɔ abolo ʋaʋã alo amɔwɔ ʋaʋã le wò anyigba katã dzi o.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Gbemagbe naxlẽe afia viwòŋutsuwo bena: Ale Yehowa wɔ nam, esime meʋu tso Egipte.

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Eye wòanye dzesi na wò anɔ wò asi ŋu kple ŋkuɖodzinu anɔ wò ŋgonu, bena Yehowa ƒe se la nanɔ wò nu me, elabena asi sesẽ Yehowa tsɔ kplɔ wò tso Egipte.

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Ne Yehowa akplɔ wò ava Kanaanitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, abe alesi wòka atam mia kple fofowòwo ene, eye wòatsɔe na wò la,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: ekema natsɔ nusianu, si ʋu dɔ nu na dada la, ana Yehowa, eye natsɔ wò lãwo ƒe ŋgɔgbevi, siwo nye atsu la, na Yehowa.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Eye natsɔ alẽ aɖɔ li tedzi ƒe ŋgɔgbevi; hafi ne mèɖɔ lii o la, ekema naŋe kɔ nɛ; ke naɖɔ li amewo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviŋutsuwo katã ta.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Eye ne viwòŋutsu ava bia wò bena: esia gɔme ɖe mahã la, ekema gblɔ ne bena: Asi sesẽ Yehowa tsɔ kplɔ mí tso Egipte, afisi míenye kluviwo le.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Esi Farao sẽ tame be, yemaɖe asi le mia ŋu o la, Yehowa wu ŋgɔgbeviwo katã le Egipte-nyigba dzi, tso amewo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo dzi vaseɖe lãwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo dzi; eyata metsɔa atsu sia atsu, si ʋu ɖo nu na dada la, sa vɔe na Yehowa; ke vinyeŋutsuwo la, meɖɔa li wo ta.

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Eye wòanye dzesi anɔ wò asi ŋu kple ŋgoblanu anɔ wò ŋgonu, elabena alɔ sesẽ Yehowa tsɔ kplɔ mi tso Egipte. Gododo tso Egipte ƒe dziyiyi.

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Esi Farao ɖe asi le dukɔa ŋu la, Mawu mekplɔ wo to Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi mɔ o, wònye eya tsɔ kpuie hafi. Elabena Mawu gblɔ be: Ne dukɔ la do go aʋli la, ave wo, eye woagbugbɔ ayi Egipte.

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: Eyata Mawu kplɔ dukɔ la to gbedzimɔ heyi Avaƒu la nu; eye Israel-viwo bia akpa hafi ʋu tso Egipte.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Eye Mose ho Yosef ƒe ƒuwo ɖe asi; elabena eka atam na Israel-viwo gblɔ bena: Ne Mawu va ɖo ŋku mia dzi la, ekema miɖo nye ƒuwo ɖe asi tso afisia yii.

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Eye woho tso Sukot heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Etam le gbedzi la me. Alilikpo kple dzobabla.

english_verse: During the day the Lord went ahead of his people in a thick cloud, and during the night he went ahead of them in a flaming fire. That way the Lord could lead them at all times, whether day or night.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke me la alilikpo dodo la medzona le dukɔ la gbɔ o, eye le zã me la dzobibi la nɔa wo ŋgɔ.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena:

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na Israel-viwo bena, woatrɔ ava ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Pi-Haxirot gbɔ le Migdol kple ƒu la dome; miƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Baal-Zefon kasa le ƒu la nu.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Elabena Farao agblɔ le Israel-viwo ŋu be: Wotre mɔ le anyigba la dzi, eye wotsi gbedadaƒo.

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Eye mana Farao ƒe dzime nasẽ, ale be wòati wo yome, eye maɖe nye ŋusẽ afia ɖe Farao kple eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la ŋuti; bena Egiptetɔwo nadze su be, nyee nye Yehowa. Eye wowɔ nenema.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Esi wogblɔ na Egipte-fia bena, dukɔa si la, Farao kple eŋu mewo ƒe dzi trɔ ɖe dukɔ la ŋuti; elabena wogblɔ bena: Nukaŋuti míewɔ alea, eye míeɖe asi le Israel-viwo ŋuti, be womagasubɔ mí o?

english_verse: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
translation_verse: Tete wòna wodzra eƒe tasiaɖamwo ɖo, eye wòkplɔ eƒe aʋakɔwo ɖe asi.

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa na Egipte-fia Farao ƒe dzime sẽ, ale bena wòti Israel-viwo yome; ke asi sesẽ kplɔ Israel-viwo dzoe.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Eye Egiptetɔwo kple Farao ƒe sɔwo, tasiaɖamwo, sɔdolawo kpakple aʋakɔ bubuawo katã ti wo yome heva tu wo, esime woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe ƒu la nu le Pi-Haxirot gbɔ le Baal-Zefon kasa.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Esi Farao gogo wo, eye Israel-viwo fɔ ka dzi kpɔ Egiptetɔwo le wo megbe gbɔna la, wovɔ̃ ŋutɔ. Tete Israel-viwo do ɣli ya Yehowa,

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: eye wogblɔ na Mose bena: Esi yɔdo mele Egipte o ta, nèkplɔ mi dzoe, bena miava ku ɖe gbedzia? Nukaŋuti nèwɔ esia ɖe mía ŋuti, eye nèkplɔ mi tso Egipte?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Menye esia mienɔa gbɔgblɔm na wò le Egipte bena: ɖe asi le mía ŋu míasubɔ Egiptetɔwo ko, elabena ne míesubɔ Egiptetɔwo la, enyo wu esi míaɖaku ɖe gbedzi oa?

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Ke Mose gblɔ na dukɔ la bena: Migavɔ̃ o, milé dzi ɖe ƒo, eye miakpɔ, alesi Yehowa le mia ɖe gee egbe; elabena Egiptetɔ, siwo kpam miele egbea la, miegale wo kpɔ ge alea gbeɖegbeɖe akpɔ o.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: Yehowa le aʋa wo ge ɖe mia nu, ke miawo la mizi kpi ko!

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Nukaŋuti nèle ɣli dom le yɔyem? Gblɔ na Israel-viwo bena, woaho adzo.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Ke wò la tsɔ wò atikplɔ, eye nadoe ɖe ƒu la dzi, bena wòamã ɖe eve, eye Israel-viwo nazɔ ƒuƒuiƒe ato ƒu la me.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Nye la mana Egiptetɔwo ƒe dzime nasẽ, eye woakplɔ wo ɖo, be maɖe nye ŋusẽ afia ɖe Farao kple eƒe aʋakɔ la katã, eƒe tasiaɖamwo kpakple eƒe sɔɖolawo ŋuti.

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Tete mawudɔla, si le Israel ƒe aʋakɔa ŋgɔ la, dzo yi ɖe wo megbe; eye alilikpo dodo la dzo le wo ŋgɔ yi wo megbe.

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: Eye wònɔ Egiptetɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ kple Israel ƒe aʋakɔ la dome, eye alilikpo la do viviti ɖe Egiptetɔwo, eye wòklẽ na Israel-viwo le zã la me, ale bena wo dometɔa ɖeke mete ɖe nɔvia ŋu zã blibo la katã o.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Eye Mose ɖo eƒe asi ɖe ƒu la dzi. Tete Yehowa na ɣedzeƒeya nyama ƒu la zã blibo la katã, ale bena ƒu la mie keŋ, eye tsi la ma ɖe akpa eve me.

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo zɔ ƒuƒuiƒe to ƒu la me, eye tsi la zu abe gli ene na wo ɖe woƒe nuɖusi me kple woƒe miã me.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Le fɔŋli la Yehowa le dzobibi kple alilikpo dodo me kpɔ Egiptetɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ dzi ɖa, eye wòtɔtɔ Egiptetɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ la.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: Eye wòna woƒe tasiaɖamfɔwo gli, ale be ŋgɔyiyi zu dɔ na wo. Tete Egiptetɔwo gblɔ bena: Mina miasi le Israel nu, elabena Yehowa le aʋa wɔm na wo ɖe Egiptetɔwo ŋuti.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Do wò asi ɖe ƒu la dzi, bena tsi la nagbugbɔ aŋe ɖe Egiptetɔwo, woƒe tasiaɖamwo kple woƒe sɔdolawo dzi.

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Tete Mose do eƒe asi ɖe ƒua dzi, eye esi ŋu ke ɖe le eme la, tɔa gaɖo eƒe nɔnɔme, eye Egiptetɔwo si yi ɖakpee. Ale Yehowa nyã Egiptetɔwo de ƒu la me.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Eye tsi la nyẽ zi va kpe, eye wòŋe ɖe tasiaɖamwo, sɔdolawo kple Farao ƒe aʋakɔ blibo, siwo ti wo yome va ƒua me la dzi. Wo dometɔ ɖeka hɔ̃ hã mesusɔ o.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Ke Israel-viwo ya zɔ ƒuƒuiƒe to ƒu la me, eye tsi la zu abe gli ene ɖe woƒe nuɖusi me kple woƒe mia me.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Gbemagbe Yehowa ɖe Israel tso Egiptetɔwo si me, eye Israel kpɔ Egiptetɔwo ƒe kukuwo le ƒutsia nu.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Eye Israel kpɔ ŋusẽ gã, si Yehowa ɖe fia ɖe Egiptetɔwo ŋuti la. Eye dukɔ la vɔ Yehowa, eye wòxɔ Yehowa kple eƒe dɔla Mose dzi se.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi Mose kple Israel-viwo dzi ha sia na Yehowa bena: Madzi ha na Yehowa, elabena ewo nu tsuwo, ede sɔ kple sɔdola ƒu.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: Nye ŋusẽ kple kafukafuha enye Yehowa, elabe eya gbɔ ɖeɖe tso va nam. Nye Mawue, eyata makafui, fofonye ƒe Mawue, eyata madoe ɖe dzi!

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: Yehowa enye aʋawɔla, eŋkɔe nye Yehowa.

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: Ede Farao ƒe tasiaɖam kple eƒe aʋakɔ la ƒu, eye eƒe aʋawɔla veviwo nyrã ɖe Avaƒu la me.

english_verse: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
translation_verse: Ƒuɖɔɖɔ gbagba ɖe wo dzi, eye wodze to abe kpe ene.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: Yehowa, wò nuɖusi netsɔ de bubu ɖokuiwò ŋu le ŋusẽ me, Yehowa, wò nuɖusi kaka futɔwo hlẽ.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: Ewo nu tsu geɖe, eye neƒo wò ketɔwo ƒu anyi. Wò dɔmedzoe bi ɖe wo ŋu, eye wòfiã wo abe gbe ene.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Wò ŋɔti me gbɔgbɔ na tsiawo ƒo kɔ, tsi sistawo dzɔ abe gli ene; ƒuɖɔɖɔ la dzi lɔ̃ agba, abe ɖe wòɖo alɔ̃ ene.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: Futɔ la gblɔ be: Mati wo yome, matu wo; mamã aboyonuwo me, hafi nye dzi nagbɔ ɖe me; maɖi nye yi, eye nye asi atsrɔ̃ wo!

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Eɖo ƒuƒu, tete ƒu la gbagba ɖe wo dzi, wodze to abe tsumi ene le tsi kpakawo nu.

english_verse: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
translation_verse: Yehowa, ameka de nuwo le mawuwo dome? Ameka de nuwo, kpɔ ŋusẽ, eye ŋutikɔkɔe le eŋu; amesi ŋu vɔvɔ̃ le, eye wòwɔ nu gãwo kple nukunuwo?

english_verse: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
translation_verse: Edo wo nuɖusi ɖa, tete anyigba mi wo.

english_verse: The people you rescued were led by your powerful love to your holy place.
translation_verse: Eve wò dukɔ la nu hekplɔ wo, eye nèɖe wo. Ekplɔ wo kple wò ŋusẽ heva wò teƒe kɔkɔe la.

english_verse: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
translation_verse: Esi dukɔwo see la, dzidzi ƒo wo, vovɔ̃ ɖo Filistitɔwo.

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi la Edom-fiawo ɖi vo, Moab-megãwo dzo nyanyanya, eye dzika tso Kanaanitɔwo katã ƒo.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Vɔvɔ̃ kple ŋɔdzi lé wo, wò alɔ sesẽ na wodze ti zu abe kpe ene, vaseɖe esime wò dukɔ la to wo dome yi, Yehowa, vaseɖe esime wò dukɔ, si nèɖe la, to wo dome yi.

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Ekplɔ wo yii, eye netsɔ wo ɖo to, si nye tɔwò la dzi, teƒe, si nèdzra ɖo be, yeanɔ, Yehowa, kɔkɔeƒe, si nèdzra ɖo kple wò asi, Aƒetɔ!

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: Yehowa aɖu fia ɖaa tegbetegbe.

english_verse: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Elabena esi Farao ƒe sɔwo, eƒe tasiaɖamwo kple eƒe sɔɖolawo ge ɖe ƒua me la, Yehowa na ƒu la ŋe tsyɔ wo dzi; ke Israel-viwo zɔ ƒuƒuiƒe to ƒu la me.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Eye nyɔnu nyagblɔla Miryam. Aron nɔvinyɔnu, tsɔ axatse ɖe asi, eye nyɔnuwo katã tsɔ axatsewo ɖe asi le ɣe ɖum kplɔe ɖo.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Eye Miryam ɖo ha la ɖa bena: Midzi ha na Yehowa, elabena ewo nu tsuwo, ede so kple sɔdola ƒu. Tsi veve trɔ zu tsi nyui.

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Emegbe Mose na Israel-viwo ho tso Avaƒu la nu heva Surgbedzi. Eye wozɔ gbea dzi ŋkeke etɔ̃, womekpɔ tsia ɖeke o.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Eye wovɔ Mara, ke womete ŋu no Mara-tsi la o, elabena ele vevem. Esiata woyɔ afima be Mara ɖo.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Eye dukɔ la li Mose ŋu gblɔ bena: Nuka no ge míala?

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ke eya do ɣli yɔ Yehowa, eye Yehowa fia aba ɖee, si wotsɔ ɖa ɖe tsi la me, tete wòtrɔ zu tsi nyui. Afima wòna se kple ɖoɖo wo le, eye afima wòɖo wo kpɔ le

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: gblɔ bena: Ne eɖo to Yehowa, wò Mawu la ƒe gbe pɛpɛpɛ, eye nèwɔ nusi nyoa eŋu, lé to ɖe eƒe seawo ŋu, eye nèwɔ eƒe ɖoɖowo katã dzi la, ekema nyemate fukpekpe, siwo katã mena wova Egiptetɔwo dzi la, ava dziwò o; elabena nye Yehowa enye wò dɔyɔla.

english_verse: Later the Israelites came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and
translation_verse: Eyome wova Elim. Afima vudo wuieve kple deti blaadre le; eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe afima le tsia gbɔ.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Emegbe woho tso Elim, eye Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la va Sin-gbedzi, le Elim kple Sinai dome, le woƒe ʋuʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi ɣleti evelia ƒe ŋkeke wuiatɔ̃lia dzi.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la li Mose kple Aron ŋu le gbea dzi,

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: eye Israel-viwo gblɔ na wo bena: Ɖe Yehowa na míeku le Egipte-nyigba dzi, afisi míebɔbɔ nɔ miaƒe lãzewo dome, eye míeɖua abolo ɖia ƒo la, ne nyo wu esi miekplɔ mí va gbe sia dzi, bena dɔ nawɔ ameha blibo sia woaku!

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Kpɔ ɖa, mana abolo nadza atso dziƒo na mi, eye dukɔ la nado gbesiagbe aɖafɔe ɖe ŋkeke ɖeka ƒe ɖuɖu nu, bena mado wo akpɔ be, woazɔ de nye seawo nu loo, alo womazɔ ɖe enu o.

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Eye ne woada nusi wofɔ va aƒe me le ŋkeke adeagbe la, ekema; adzi ɖe dzi agaɖe nusi wofɔna gbesiagbe la nu.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Eye Mose kple Aron gblɔ na Israel-viwo katã bena: Fiẽ la miadze sii bena, Yehowae kplɔ mi tso Egipte-nyigba dzi,

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: eye ŋdi la míakpɔ Yehowa, ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe, elabena ese miaƒe, liʋĩliʋĩlilĩ ɖe Yehowa ŋu; ke míawo la amehawo míenye, be miele; mia ŋu lim?

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ bena: Fiẽ la Yehowa ana lã mi miaɖu, eye ŋdi la ana abolo nu miedu aɖi ƒo, elabena Yehowa se liʋĩliʋĩ, si mieli ɖe eŋu la, ke miawo la amekawo míenye? Menye mía ŋu mieli o, ke boŋ Yehowa ŋue mieli.

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ na Aron bena: Gblɔ na Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la bena: Mite va Yehowa ƒe ŋku me, elabena ese miaƒe liʋĩliʋĩlilĩ la.

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Esi Aron ƒo nu kple Israel-viwo ƒe ha bliboa la, wòtrɔ ŋgɔ dze gbedzi lɔƒo, eye kpɔ ɖa, Yehowa ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe ɖe eɖokui fia le alilikpoa ɖe me.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: Mese Israel-viwo ƒe liʋĩliʋĩlilĩ la. Gblɔ na wo be: Fiẽ la miaɖu lã, eye ŋdi la miaɖu abolo aɖi ƒo, bena miadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa, miaƒe Mawu la.

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Le fiẽ la tegliwo dzo va nyẽ tsyɔ asaɖa la, eye le ŋdi la afu dza ƒo xlã asaɖa la.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Esi afu la kɔ ɖa la, tete nu sue nogonogoewo le anyigba le gbe la dzi abe ketsi ene.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Eye esi Israel-viwo kpɔe la, wogblɔ na wo nɔewo bena: Nuka nye esi? Elabena Womenya nusi wònye o. Tete Mose gblɔ na wo bena: Esia enye abolo, si Yehowa na mi, be miaɖu la.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Se, si Yehowa de, enye si: Amesiame nafɔe ɖe eƒe ɖuɖu nu; miafɔe ɖe amesiwo le miaƒe agbadɔ me la ƒe xexlẽme nu, ame ɖeka gomer ɖeka.

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo wɔ nenema; amea ɖewo fɔe fũ, eye amea ɖewo fɔe ʋee.

english_verse: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ na wo bena: Amea ɖeke megagblẽ ɖeke ɖiŋu nake ɖe edzi o!

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Ke womeɖo to Mose o, eye amea ɖewo gblẽe ɖi ŋu ke ɖe edzi; gake wòdze nyẽ, eye wòƒaƒã. Tete Mose do dɔmedzoe ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Ale wofɔnɛ ŋdi sia ŋdi; amesiame ɖe eƒe ɖuɖu nu, ke ne ŋdɔ ʋu ko la, elólona.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Ke le ŋkeke adeagbe la wolɔa nuɖuɖu la teƒe eve, ame ɖeka gomer eve. Eye ha la ƒe amegãwo katã va gblɔe na Mose.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na wo bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Etsɔ nye dzudzɔgbe, ŋkeke kɔkɔe na Yehowa. Nusi miatsɔ aƒo aboloe la, mitsɔe ƒoe, eye nusi miatsɔ aɖa la, miɖae; ke esi susɔ la, midzrae ɖo hena etsɔ.

english_verse: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
translation_verse: Eye wodae ɖi ŋu ke ɖe edzi, abe alesi Mose gblɔ ene, ke meƒaƒã o, eye medze nyẽ hã o

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ bena: Miɖu eya egbea, elabena egbe enye dzudzɔgbe na Yehowa, egbe la miegale ekpɔ ge le gbe me o.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Ŋkeke ade miafɔe; ke ŋkeke adrelia enye dzudzɔgbe, eya dzi miele ɖeke kpɔ ge o.

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Eye le ŋkeke adreagbe la amea ɖewo tso dukɔ la me yi efɔ ge, ke womekpɔ ɖeke o.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Zi nenie miagbe toɖoɖo nye sewo kple nye ɖoɖowo mahã?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Mikpɔ ɖa Yehowa na dzudzɔgbe mi, eyata wòna nuɖuɖu mi le ŋkeke adelia dzi ɖe ŋkeke eve nu. Amesiame natsi aƒe, eye amea ɖeke nagado go le aƒe me le ŋkeke adrelia dzi o!

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ale dukɔ la dzudzɔ eɖokui le ŋkeke adrelia dzi.

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Eye Israeltɔwo na ŋkɔe be man; ele abe xetsetse ene hele ɣie; eye wòvivina abe tatali, si me wode anyitsii ene.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ bena: Se, si Yehowa de, enye si: Midzra gomer ɖeka ɖo hena miaƒe dzidzimeviwo, bena woakpɔ abolo, si mena mieɖu le gbedzi, esime mekplɔ mi tso Egipte-nyigba dzi la.

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ na Aron bena: Tsɔ zevia ɖe, eye nade man gomer ɖeka eme fũ, eye natsɔe ada ɖe Yehowa ŋku me, bena wòanɔ anyi hena miaƒe dzidzimeviwo.

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Eye Aron tsɔe dzra ɖo ɖe seawo gbɔ, abe alesi Yehowa de se na Mose ene.

english_verse: The Israelites ate manna for
translation_verse: Gomer ɖeka enye eta ƒe mamã ewolia ɖeka.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la ho tso Sin-gbedzi hele teƒeleƒewo tom, abe alesi Yehowa de se ene, eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Refidim. Ke tsia ɖeke meli be, dukɔ la nano o.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la wɔ dzre kple Mose, eye wogblɔ bena: Mina tsi mi miano! Mose ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Nukaŋuti miele dzre wum kplim? Nukaŋuti miele Yehowa tem kpɔ?

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Eye tsikɔ wu dukɔ la le afima. Eye dukɔ la ti Mose ŋu gblɔ bena: Nukaŋuti nèkplɔ mí tso Egipte, bena tsikɔ nawu mia ŋutɔwo, mía viwo kple míaƒe lãwo míaku mahã?

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: Tete Mose do ɣli yɔ Yehowa bena: Nuka mawɔ na dukɔ sia? Esusɔ vie ko woafɔ kpe aƒum!

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Dze dukɔ la ŋgɔ, eye naɖe ame tsitsia ɖewo le Israel dome akpe ɖe ɖokuiwò ŋu, eye natsɔ atikplɔ, si netsɔ ƒo Nil dzi la, ɖe asi yii.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, matsi tre ɖe ŋkuwò me ɖe Horeb-kpe la dzi, eye naƒo kpe la, ekema tsi ado atso me, be dukɔ la nano. Eye Mose wɔ nenema le Israel-me tsitsiawo ƒe ŋku me.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: Eye wona ŋkɔ teƒe la bena: Masa kple Meriba. Elabena Israel-viwo wɔ dzre, eye wote Yehowa kpɔ gblɔ bena: Ɖe Yehowa le mía dome loo, alo meli o? Israel-viwo ɖu Amalekitɔwo dzi.

english_verse: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Esia megbe Amalekitɔwo va wɔ aʋa kple Israel le Refidim.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Tete Mose gblɔ na Yosua bena: Tia ŋutsuwo kpe ɖe ŋuwò, eye nayi aɖawɔ aʋa kple Amalek etsɔ; ke nye la maɖatsi tre ɖe togbe la tame, eye male Mawu ƒe atikplɔ la ɖe asi.

english_verse: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
translation_verse: Eye Yosua wɔ, abe alesi Mose gblɔ nɛ ene be, wòaɖawɔ aʋa kple Amalek. Ke Mose, Aron kple Xur woyi togbe la tame.

english_verse: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
translation_verse: Eye ne Mose kɔ eƒe asi dzi la, ekema Israel ƒe alɔ ɖea dzi; ke ne eɖiɖi asi ɖe anyi la, ekema Amalek ƒe alɔ ɖea dzi.

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: Ke esi alɔ ku ɖe Mose ŋu la, wotsɔ kpe ɖe ete wòbɔbɔ nɔ edzi. Eye Aron kple Xur lé eƒe asiwò ɖe dzi; ame ɖeka le axa ɖeka, eye ame evelia le axa bubu dzi Ale wole eƒe asiwò de te, vaseɖe esime ɣe ɖo to.

english_verse: That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Eye Yosua ɖu Amalek kple eƒe aʋakɔ dzi kple yi.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Eve Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Ŋlɔ nusia ɖe agbalẽ me hena ŋkuɖoɖo dzi, eye nakui ɖe Yosua ƒe to me, elabena matsrɔ̃ Amalek ƒe ŋkɔ ɖa le dziƒoa te keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Eye Mose ɖi vɔsamlekpui, eye wòna ŋkɔe be: Yehowa nye aflaga.

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ bena: Meta Yehowa ƒe zikpui Yehowa ewo aʋa kple Amalek tegbetegbe.

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: Eye wòda ame ɖo ɖe Mose gbɔ be: Nye towo Yetro kple srɔ̃wò kpakple viaŋutsu eveawo míegbɔna gbɔwò.

english_verse: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
translation_verse: Tete Mose yi ɖakpe toa, eye wòde ta agu, eye wòɖuɖɔ nu nɛ; emegbe wòbia wo nɔewo ƒe dɔdɔ ta se, eye woyi agbadɔ la me.

english_verse: where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
translation_verse: Eyome Mose xlẽ nusiwo katã Yehowa wɔ Farao kple Egiptetɔwo le Israel ta, kple fu, siwo katã dzɔ ɖe wo dzi le mɔ ta, kpakple alesi Yehowa ɖe wo la, na toa.

english_verse: Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.”
translation_verse: Fifi ko menyae bena, Yehowa kpe wu mawuwo katã; elabena etsɔ woawo ŋutɔ ƒe nu vlo wɔwɔ he toe na wo.

english_verse: Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship. Judges Are Appointed (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Eyome Mose to, Yetro, tsɔ numevɔsawo kple akpedavɔsawo ve na Mawu, eye Aron kple Israeltɔ tsitsiwo katã va, be woaɖu nu kple Mose to le Mawu ƒe ŋku me. Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ɖoɖo.

english_verse: You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone.
translation_verse: Ɖeɖi ate wò ŋutɔ kple dukɔ, si le gbɔwò la ŋu. Elabena dɔ la sesẽ na wò akpa; wò ɖeka màte ŋu awɔe o.

english_verse: The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, Mose bɔbɔ nɔ anyi, be yeadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na dukɔ la, eye dukɔ la tsi tre ɖe Mose gbɔ vaseɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
translation_verse: Ke esi Mose to kpɔ dɔ, siwo katã le esi le dukɔa ŋuti la, egblɔ bena: Nuka nèle wɔwɔm na dukɔ la alea? Nukaŋuti wò ɖeka nèbɔbɔ na anyi, eye dukɔ blibo la le tsitre ɖe gbɔwò tso ŋdi vaseɖe fiẽ?

english_verse: Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do.
translation_verse: Mose ɖo ŋu na toa bena: Dukɔ la va gbɔnye, be woabia nu Mawu.

english_verse: They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
translation_verse: Ne nyaa ɖe le wo si la, wotsɔnɛ vaa gbɔnyee, eye medrɔ̃a amesiame kple nɔvia dome nya na wo, eye megblɔa Mawu ƒe sewo kple ɖoɖowo na wo.

english_verse: Jethro replied: That isn't the best way to do it.
translation_verse: Tete Mose to gblɔ ne bena: Menyo be, nanɔ wɔwɔm alea o.

english_verse: God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people,
translation_verse: Eyata ɖo to nye gbe, ne maɖo aɖaŋu na wò, eye Mawu akpe ɖe ŋuwò. Na dukɔ la nu le Mawu gbɔ, eye natso woƒe nyawo aɖo Mawu ŋku me.

english_verse: and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
translation_verse: Ɖe seawo kple ɖoɖoawo me na wo, eye nafia mɔ, si woato kple nusi woawo la wo.

english_verse: These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier.
translation_verse: bena woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na dukɔ la ɣesiaɣi, negbe nya veviwo ko woatso va gbɔwò; ke nya kpotokpotoewo la woa ŋutɔwo nadrɔ̃e. Ale naɖe agba le ɖokuiwò dzi, eye woaxɔ na wò.

english_verse: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
translation_verse: Ne èwɔ alea, eye Mawu lɔ̃ ɖe dzi na wò la, ekema àkpɔ gbɔdzɔe, eye dukɔ blibo la hã ayi aƒe me le ŋutifafa me.

english_verse: They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
translation_verse: Eye wodrɔ̃a ʋɔnu na dukɔ la ɣesiaɣi, negbe nya veviwo ko wotsɔna vaa Mose gbɔe, ke nya kpotokpotoewo katã la woawo ŋutɔ drɔ̃nɛ.

english_verse: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_verse: Emegbe Mose ɖo toa ɖa, wòyi wo denyigba dzi.

english_verse: The Israelites left Rephidim and arrived at the desert. Then two months after leaving Egypt, they arrived at the desert near Mount Sinai, where they set up camp at the foot of the mountain. This was two months after they had left Egypt.
translation_verse: Esi woho tso Refidim la, wova Sinai-gbedzi, eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe gbea dzi; afima Israel ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖo le to la kasa.

english_verse: Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
translation_verse: Ke Mose yi Mawu gbɔ le to la dzi. Eye Yehowa yɔe tso to la dzi gblɔ bena: Ale nagblɔ na Yakob-ƒomeawo, eye ale naɖe gbe ƒãe na Israel-viwo enye si:

english_verse: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
translation_verse: Mia ŋutɔwo miekpɔ nusi mewo Egiptetɔwo, kple alesi metsɔ mi ɖe hɔ̃ ƒe aʋala wo dzi, eye mekplɔ mi va gbɔnyee.

english_verse: Now if you will faithfully obey me, you will be my very own people. The whole world is mine,
translation_verse: Azɔ ne míaɖo to nye gbe, eye mialé nye nubabla me ɖe asi la, ekema mianye tanye koŋ le dukɔwo katã dome, elabena anyigba blibo la tɔnyee.

english_verse: but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests. Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
translation_verse: Eye mianye; nunɔlawo ƒe fiaduƒe kple dukɔ kɔkɔe nam! Esiawo nye nya, siwo nagblɔ na Israel-viwo.

english_verse: After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said,
translation_verse: Eye Mose yi ɖayɔ dukɔ la ƒe ame tsitsiawo hegblɔ nya, siwo katã Yehowa de esi la, na wo.

english_verse: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ blibo la ɖo ŋu yoo bena: Nya, siwo katã Yehowa gblɔ la, míawɔe. Eye Mose tsɔ dukɔ la ƒe nyawo va Mawu gbɔe.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Mava gbɔwò le alilikpo dodoa ɖe me, be ne mele nu ƒom kpli wò la, dukɔ la nasee, eye woaxɔ dziwò ase tegbee. Eye Mose gblɔ dukɔ la ƒe nyawo na Yehowa. Dukɔ la dzra eɖokui do hena sexɔxɔ tso Mawu gbɔ.

english_verse: Once more the Lord spoke to Moses: Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Yi dukɔ la gbɔ, eye nana be, woadzra wo ɖokui ɖo dzadzɛ egbe kple etsɔ, eye wòanya woƒe avɔwo,

english_verse: and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
translation_verse: ne wòasu te le ŋkeke etɔ̃agbe; elabena le ŋkeke etɔ̃agbe Yehowa aɖi va Sinai-to la dzi le dukɔ blibo la ƒe ŋku me.

english_verse: Warn the people that they are forbidden to touch any part of the mountain. Anyone who does will be put to death,
translation_verse: Ɖo liƒo na dukɔ la godoo, eye nagblɔ na wo bena: Mikpɔ nyuie, be amea ɖeke nagalia to la alo ade enu akɔ asi eŋu o. Amesiame, si aka asi toa ŋu la, ku ke wòaku!

english_verse: either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Ne asia ɖe aka eŋu la, woaƒu kpee, alo woatee kple da; eɖanye ame alo lã o, maganɔ agbe o. Ke ne woku lãdzokpẽ la, ekema woaha to la.

english_verse: After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God.
translation_verse: Tete Mose ɖi tso toa dzi va dukɔ la gbɔ, eye wòna dukɔ la wɔ wo ɖokui dzadzɛ, eye wonyã woƒe avɔwo.

english_verse: He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime. The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na dukɔ la bena: Misu te vaseɖe ŋkeke etɔ̃lia dzi; amea ɖeke megado nyɔnu gbɔ o. Mawu ɖe eɖokui fia le Sinai-to dzi.

english_verse: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear.
translation_verse: Eye le ŋkeke etɔ̃lia ƒe ŋdi kanya la dzi de asi gbeɖeɖe me, eye wòle dzo kem; alilikpo dodoa ɖe va tsyɔ to la dzi, eye kpẽwo le ɖiɖim sesĩe ŋutɔ. Tete dukɔ blibo, si le asaɖa me la, de asi dzodzo me nyanyanya.

english_verse: Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Eye Mose kplɔ dukɔ la tso asaɖa la me yi Mawu kpe ge, eye wotsi tre ɖe to la te.

english_verse: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook.
translation_verse: Eye dzudzɔ bia Sinai-to blibo la, elabena Yehowa ɖi va edzi le dzo me; eye dzudzɔ la ɖe dzi abe aŋɔɖaƒe dzudzɔ ene, eye to blibo la le ʋuʋum ŋutɔ.

english_verse: The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
translation_verse: Eye kpẽawo nu le sesẽm ɖe dzi. Mose ƒo nu, eye Mawu ɖo ŋu nɛ kple gbe sesẽ.

english_verse: The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ɖi va Sinai-to la tame, eye Yehowa yɔ Mose, be wòava Sinai-toa tame, eye Mose ha to la.

english_verse: Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Ɖi yi ɖaxlɔ̃ nu dukɔ la bena, womegagbɔ liƒo la me, ava Yehowa gbɔ, nu kpo ge o, elabena wo dometɔ geɖewo ava ku.

english_verse: Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
translation_verse: Eye nunɔla, siwo ate ɖe Yehowa ŋu hã, nawɔ wo ɖokui dzadzɛ, bena Yehowa magaɖe gbe ɖe wo dzi.

english_verse: Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
translation_verse: Mose ɖo ŋu na Yehowa bena: Dukɔ la mate ŋu aha Sinai-to la o, elabena wò ŋutɔ èxlɔ̃ nu mi bena: Miɖe liƒo ɖe to la ŋu, eye mibui kɔkɔe!

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Ɖi yi, ne mia kple Aron miava; ke nunɔlawo kple dukɔ la megagbɔ liƒo la me, ava Yehowa gbã le toa dzi, bena Yehowa nagaɖe gbe ɖe wo dzi o.

english_verse: After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Tete Mose ɖi yi dukɔ la gbɔ, eye wògblɔe na wo.

english_verse: God said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Eye Mawu to nya siawo katã bena:

english_verse: But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off. Idols and Altars
translation_verse: Ale dukɔ la tsi tre ɖe adzɔge ke; ke Mose te ɖe alilikpo dodo, si me Mawu le la ŋu. Vɔsamlekpui ɖiɖi.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
translation_verse: Nyee nye Yehowa wò Mawu, si kplɔ wò tso kluvinyenyeƒe me le Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Do not worship any god except me.
translation_verse: Mawu bubua ɖeke megunɔ asiwò kpe ɖe ŋunye o.

english_verse: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
translation_verse: Megawɔ legbaa ɖeke na ɖokuiwò o. Megawɔ nusiwo le dziƒo, alo nusiwo le anyigba dzi, alo nusiwo le tsi me le anyigba te la, ƒe nɔnɔme o.

english_verse: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
translation_verse: ke mevea ame akpe nane, siwo lɔ̃am, eye wowɔa nye seawo dzi la nu.

english_verse: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
translation_verse: Megayɔ Yehowa, wo Mawu, ƒe ŋkɔ yakayaka o, elabena Yehowa magbe tohehe na amesi yɔa eƒe ŋkɔ dzodzro la o.

english_verse: Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me.
translation_verse: Ɖo ŋku dzudzɔgbe la dzi, ne nawɔe kɔkɔe.

english_verse: You have six days when you can do your work,
translation_verse: Ŋkeke ade nawɔ dɔ, eye nawɔ ŋuwò dowo katã.

english_verse: but the seventh day of each week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your slaves, your animals, or the foreigners who live in your towns.
translation_verse: Ke ŋkeke adrelia enye dzudzɔgbe na Yehowa, wò Mawu la; megawɔ dɔa ɖeke le edzi o, eɖanye wò ŋutɔ, viwòŋutsu alo viwònyɔnu o, eɖanye wò dɔlaŋutsu, wò dɔlanyɔnu, wò lã, alo wò amedzro, si dzewo du me la o.

english_verse: In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
translation_verse: Elabena ŋkeke ade mee Yehowa wɔ dzi kple anyigba, atsiaƒu kple nusiwo katã le eme, eye wòdzudzɔ eɖokui le ŋkeke adreagbe. Eyata Yehowa yra dzudzɔgbe la, eye wòwɔe kɔkɔe.

english_verse: Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
translation_verse: Bu fofowò kple dawo, bena nanɔ agbe didie le anyigba, si Yehowa, wò Mawu, ana wò la dzi.

english_verse: Do not murder.
translation_verse: Megawu ame o.

english_verse: Be faithful in marriage.
translation_verse: Megawɔ ahasi o.

english_verse: Do not steal.
translation_verse: Megafi fi o.

english_verse: Do not tell lies about others.
translation_verse: Megaɖi aʋatsoɖase le hawòvi ŋuti o.

english_verse: Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else. The People Are Afraid (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Megabiã ŋu ɖe hawòvi ƒe aƒe dzi o. Megabiã ŋu ɖe hawòvi srɔ̃, eƒe dɔlaŋutsu alo eƒe dɔlanyɔnu, eƒe nyi alo eƒe tedzi, alo nusianu, si nye hawòvi to la ƒe ɖeke dzi o.

english_verse: So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
translation_verse: Migawɔ mawu bubua ɖeke kpe ɖe ŋunye o; migawɔ ɖeke o, eɖanye klosalolegba alo sikalegba o.

english_verse: The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off
translation_verse: Esi dukɔ blibo la se dziɖegbe kple kpẽawo ƒe ɖiɖi, eye wokpɔ dzikedzo kple alesi toa le dzudzɔ tumi la, dukɔ la dzo nyanyanya, eye wotsi tre ɖe adzɔge ke.

english_verse: and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ na Mose bena: Wò la ƒo nu kpli mí, eye míaɖo to asee, ke Mawu megaƒo nu kpli mí, bena míagaku o.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.”
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ na dukɔ la bena: Migavɔ̃ o, elabena Mawu ɖe wòva mia do ge akpɔ, bena vɔvɔ̃ nanɔ eŋu le mia dome, ne miagawɔ nuvɔ̃ o.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel: With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Ale nagblɔ na Israel-viwo enye si: Mia ŋutɔwo miekpɔ bena, meƒo nu kpli mi tso dziƒo.

english_verse: Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you.
translation_verse: Tso anyi ɖi vɔsamlekpui nam, eya dzi natsɔ wò alẽwo kple wò nyiwo ame numevɔsa le, eye nasa, akpedavɔwo le Mava afisiafi, si meɖo be, woaɖo ŋku nye ŋkɔ dzi le la, eye mayra wò.

english_verse: If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship.
translation_verse: Ne ebe, yeatsɔ kpe aɖi vɔsamlekpui nam la, megatsɔ esi wotu o; elabena ne etso ga fu kpee la, ekema ègblẽ ka ɖo nɛ.

english_verse: And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
translation_verse: Megaflɔ atrakpui de nye vɔsamlekpui dzi o, bena wò ama nagadze le edzi o.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
translation_verse: Amesi ke aƒo fofoa alo dada la, woawui.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for murder.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe ƒo ame woku la, ekema woawu eya hã.

english_verse: Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed,
translation_verse: Ne ŋutsuwo le dzre wɔm, eye ɖeka tsɔ kpe alo kodzi ƒo nɔvia meku o, gake wòtsi aba dzi,

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses the following laws for his people:
translation_verse: Esiawo nye ɖoɖo, siwo nagblɔ na wo.

english_verse: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him.
translation_verse: Ne èƒle Hebriŋutsua ɖe kluvii la, ekema woawo do ƒe ade, eye le ƒe adrelia me la wòadzo fea ɖeke maxemaxee.

english_verse: If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom.
translation_verse: Nenye eya ɖekae va la, eya ɖeɖe nadzo; ne ekplɔ srɔ̃a vɛ la, ekema eya kple srɔ̃a nadzo.

english_verse: If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
translation_verse: Nenye eƒe aƒetɔe ɖe srɔ̃ ne, eye wòdzi ŋutsuviwo alo nyɔnuviwo nɛ la, ekema nyɔnu la kple viawo nanye eƒe aƒetɔ tɔ, eye eya ɖeɖe nadzo.

english_verse: But suppose the slave loves his wife and children and his owner so much that he won't leave them.
translation_verse: Ke ne kluvi la gblɔ be: Melɔ̃ nye aƒetɔ, srɔ̃nye kple vinyewo, nyemadzo anɔ ɖokuinye si o la,

english_verse: Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
translation_verse: ekema eƒe aƒetɔ nakplɔe ava Mawu ƒe ŋku me, atsɔe aɖo ʋɔtru nu alo ʋɔtrutiwo gbɔ, eye eƒe aƒetɔ naŋɔ to nɛ kple nuŋɔnui, be wòasubɔe tegbee.

english_verse: A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe dzra vianyɔnu kosii la, eya madzo abe ŋutsuwo ene o.

english_verse: If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her.
translation_verse: Ne eƒe nu menyo eƒe aƒetɔ ŋu o, eye megadi be, yeaɖee o la, ekema wòana woava xɔe kple ga. Mekpe ŋusẽ adzrae ɖe dukɔ bubuwo dome, le esi wògbee la ta o.

english_verse: If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
translation_verse: Ne etsɔe na viaŋutsu la, ekema wòawɔ nɛ abe eya ŋuta vianyɔnue ene.

english_verse: If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife.
translation_verse: Ke ne eya ŋutɔ gaɖe nyɔnu bubu kpe ɖe eŋu la, ekema megale nuɖuɖu kple avɔtatae o, eye megagbe egbɔ dɔdɔ, hã o.

english_verse: If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it. Murder and Other Violent Crimes The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ne mewo nu etɔ̃ siawo nɛ o la, ekema wòadzo taa fea ɖeke maxemaxee. Se le amewuwu ŋuti.

english_verse: But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe mebua o, gake Mawu to eƒe asi dzi wɔe la, ekema maɖo teƒea ɖe na wò, afisi wòasi ayi.

english_verse: If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
translation_verse: Gake ne amea ɖe bua wu nɔvia ƒe aye me la, ekema woahee atso nye vɔsamlekpui gɔ̃ hã gbɔ aɖawu.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
translation_verse: Amesi ke aƒo fi ade fofoa alo dada la, woawui. Se le abidede ame ŋu ŋuti.

english_verse: and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
translation_verse: emegbe wògafɔ do go le tɔtɔm ɖe ati ŋu la, ekema amesi ƒoe la, megaɖi fɔ o, negbe eƒe afiɖekanɔfewo kple dɔyɔfewo ko wòaxe.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for beating to death any of your slaves.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe ƒo eƒe kluvi alo kosivi kple kpo, woku ɖe esi me la, ekema woabia hlɔ̃e.

english_verse: However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
translation_verse: Ke ne eganɔ agbe ŋkeke ɖeka alo eve hafi la, ekema womagabia hlɔ̃e o; elabena eya ŋutɔ ƒe gãe.

english_verse: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
translation_verse: Ne ŋutsuwo le dzre wɔm, eye wotutu nyɔnu funɔa ɖe ƒu anyi, ke vɔ̃a ɖeke mewɔe o, negbe fua koe ge le eƒo la, ekema nyɔnua srɔ̃ naxa fe le esi, abe alesi ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ɖo ene.

english_verse: But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life,
translation_verse: Ke ne vɔ̃a ɖe dze eme la, ekema woabia agbe ɖe agbe teƒe,

english_verse: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
translation_verse: ŋku ɖe ŋku teƒe, aɖu ɖe aɖu teƒe, asi ɖe asi teƒe, afɔ ɖe afɔ teƒe,

english_verse: burn for burn, cut for cut, and bruise for bruise.
translation_verse: dzobi ɖe dzobi teƒe, abi ɖe abi teƒe, dodro ɖe dodro teƒe.

english_verse: If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe ƒo ŋku na eƒe kluvi alo eƒe kosivi wògbã la, ekema wòaɖe asi le eŋu, ne wòana eɖokui si ɖe eƒe ŋku la ta.

english_verse: The same law applies if you knock out a slave's tooth—the slave goes free.
translation_verse: Eye ne amea ɖe ŋe aɖu na eƒe kluvi alo eƒe kosivi la, ekema wòaɖe asi le eŋu, ne wòano eɖokui si ɖe eƒe aɖu la ta.

english_verse: A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
translation_verse: Ne nyia ɖe tu dzo ŋutsu alo nyɔnu woku la, ekema woaƒu kpe nyi la, eye womagaɖu eƒe lã o; ke womabu fɔ nyia tɔ o.

english_verse: Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning.
translation_verse: Ke ne nyi la dia dzotutu ame, eye wogblɔe na nyia to, gake mekpɔ edzi o, eye wòwu ŋutsu alo nyɔnu la, ekema woaƒu kpe nyi la, eye woawu nyia to hã.

english_verse: pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
translation_verse: Ke ne wodo hlɔ̃le nɛ la, ekema woaxee pɛpɛpɛ, abe alesi woɖoe nɛ ene, ɖe eƒe agbe ta.

english_verse: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
translation_verse: Ne etu dzo ŋutsuvi alo nyɔnuvia ɖe la, ekema woawo nɛ ɖe ɖoɖo sia nu.

english_verse: If the bull kills a slave, you must pay the slave owner
translation_verse: Ne nyi la tu dzo kluvi alo kosivi la, ekema nyia tɔ naxe klosalo sekel blaetɔ̃ na eƒe aƒetɔ.

english_verse: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe ʋu doa ɖe nu da ɖi, alo amea de ɖe vudo metu nu enu o, eye nyi alo tedzia ɖe ge ɖe me la,

english_verse: You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
translation_verse: ekema vudoa tɔ, naxe te ɖe eta na lã la so; eye; lã kukua nazu etɔ.

english_verse: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe ƒe nyi tu dzo nɔvia ƒe nyi wòku la, ekema woatsɔ nyi gbagbe la adzra, eye woamã ga la, emegbe woamã lã kuku la hã.

english_verse: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_verse: Ke ne wonyae bena nyi la dia dzotutu ame, gake nyia tɔ mekpɔ edzi o la, ekema wòatsɔ nyi gbagbe ado eteƒe, eve kukua nazu etɔ.

english_verse: If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep.
translation_verse: Ne wole fiafitɔa ɖe le fi dzi, eye wo ƒoe woku la, ekema hlɔ̃a ɖeke mele me o.

english_verse: But if you cannot afford to replace the animals, you must be sold as a slave to pay for what you have stolen. If you steal an ox, donkey, or sheep, and are caught with it still alive, you must pay the owner double. If you happen to kill a burglar who breaks into your home after dark, you are not guilty. But if you kill someone who breaks in during the day, you are guilty of murder.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe kplɔ lãwo yi eƒe boƒo alo weingble me, eye wòɖe asi le wo nu woɖagblẽ ame bubu ƒe agble la ekema wòatsɔ eƒe agblemenuwo aɖo nusi wogblẽ la teƒe; ke nenye agble blibo la wogblẽ la, ekema wòatsɔ eƒe boƒonu nyuitɔ alo weingblemenu nyuitɔ aɖo eteƒe.

english_verse: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
translation_verse: Ne dzo dze gbe, eye wòlé ho, siwo le liƒo dzi, hefiã ava alo bli, siwo le bo dzi, alo agble blibo la katã la, ekema amesi tɔ dzo gbea ta, naɖo eteƒe.

english_verse: If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe dzra ga alo nuwo ɖo de nɔvia gbɔ, eye wofii le amea ƒe me, ne wokpɔ fiafitɔa la, ekema wòaɖo eteƒe zi eve.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
translation_verse: Gake ne womekpɔ fiafi la o la, ekema woakplɔ aƒeatɔ ava Mawu ƒe ŋku me, be eya ŋutɔe ɖo asi nɔvia ƒe nua dzi loo, alo menye eya ŋutɔe o.

english_verse: Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe tsɔ tedzi, nyi, alẽ alo lãa ɖe na nɔvia, be woakpɔ edzi, eve wòku, alo nane wɔe, alo woda adzoe, eye ame bubua ɖeke mekpɔ teƒe o la,

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking.
translation_verse: ekema woata Yehowa na nɔvia be, menye eya ŋutɔe ɖo asi nɔvia ƒe nu la dzi o, eye lã la tɔ naxɔ nya la nɛ, ekema fea ɖeke mele eme o.

english_verse: If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough.
translation_verse: Nenye ɖe wofii le egbɔ la, ekema woaɖo eteƒe na lã la tɔ.

english_verse: But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it.
translation_verse: Nenye lãa ɖee vuvui la ekema wòatsɔ kukua ava fia abe ɖase ene, eye fea ɖeke manɔ me o.

english_verse: If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe ɣe lã le nɔvia si, eye nane wɔe, alo wòku, eye lã la tɔ mele eteƒe o la, ekema wòaɖo eteƒe.

english_verse: Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it.
translation_verse: Ke ne lã la tɔ le eteƒe la, ekema maɖo eteƒe o, elabena esi wòɣee la, ele fe xam ɖe eta.

english_verse: Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
translation_verse: Ke ne fofoa gbe be, yematsɔe nɛ o la, ekema wòa ve srɔ̃ɖenu, siwo wowɔna na ɖetugbiwo la ƒe fe.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
translation_verse: Amesiame, si adɔ lãa ɖe gbɔ la, woawui.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for offering sacrifices to any god except me.
translation_verse: Megate amedzro ɖe anyi o eye megasẽ ŋuta le eŋu o; elabena miawo hã míenye amedzrowo kpɔ le Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue.
translation_verse: eye nye dɔmedzoe abi ɖe mia ŋu, eye mawu mi kple yi, ale be mia srɔ̃wo atrɔ zu ahosiwo, eye mia viwo azu tsyɔ̃eviwo.

english_verse: In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
translation_verse: Ne edo ga na nye dukɔ la dome ame dahea ɖe si le gbɔwò la, megaɖi kasae o, eye megabia deme hã le esi o.

english_verse: Don't charge interest when you lend money to any of my people who are in need.
translation_verse: Ne exɔ hawòvi ƒe avɔ awɔbae la, ekema gatsɔe nɛ, hafi ɣe naɖo to,

english_verse: Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan,
translation_verse: elabena eyae koe nye avɔ le esi, eya wòtana; nuka tsyɔ ge wòala amlɔ anyii mahã? Ne edo ɣli yɔm la, maɖo toe, elabena amenuvela menye.

english_verse: Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
translation_verse: Megamiã asi ɖe wò agblemenu ʋaʋãwo kple wò ami dzi o, eye natsɔ wò ŋgɔgbeviŋutsuwo nam.

english_verse: Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me. Dedicate to me your first-born sons
translation_verse: Nenema ke nawɔ wò nyiwo kple alẽwo hãe; ŋkeke adre wòanɔ dada gbɔ, eye le ŋkeke enyilia dzi natsɔe nam.

english_verse: and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
translation_verse: Ame kɔkɔewo míenye nam. Eyata migaɖu lã, si nu lé le gbe me la o; ke boŋ mitsɔe ƒu gbe na avũwo.

english_verse: Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice.
translation_verse: Meganɔ ha yome le nu vlo wɔwɔ me o, eye megade ame geɖewo dzi le dzrenya me ate nya dzɔdzɔe la ɖe to o.

english_verse: And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
translation_verse: Megaɖe ami ɖe ame dahe ƒe nya o.

english_verse: If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
translation_verse: Ne èkpɔ wò ketɔ ƒe nyi alo tedzi tre mɔ la, gakplɔe vɛ ne.

english_verse: If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
translation_verse: Ne agba nɔ wò futɔ ƒe tedzi dzi nèkpɔ la, megato eŋu yi o; ke boŋ kpe ɖe eŋu, ne miatui le edzi.

english_verse: Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court.
translation_verse: Megatrɔ ame dahe ƒe nya bu anyi le ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe o.

english_verse: Don't bring false charges against anyone or sentence an innocent person to death. I won't forgive you if you do.
translation_verse: Ɖe nu le aʋatsonyawo me; megawu amesi ƒe nya dzɔ, eye meɖi fɔa ɖeke o la o, elabena nyematso afia na ame vɔ̃ɖi o.

english_verse: Don't accept bribes. Judges are blinded and justice is twisted by bribes.
translation_verse: Megaxɔ zãnu o, elabena zãnunana gbãa ŋku na nukpɔlawo, eye wòtrɔa ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe nya bua anyi.

english_verse: Don't mistreat foreigners. You were foreigners in Egypt, and you know what it is like. Laws for the Sabbath The Lord said:
translation_verse: Migase ŋuta le amedzrowo ŋu o, elabena mia ŋutɔwo mienyã, alesi wònɔna na amedzrowo, elabena míenye amedzrowo le Egipte-nyigba dzi kpɔ?

english_verse: Plant and harvest your crops for six years,
translation_verse: Ƒe ade naƒã nu ɖewo anyigba dzi, eye naƒo wò agblemenuwo nu ƒu.

english_verse: but let the land rest during the seventh year. The poor are to eat what they want from your fields, vineyards, and olive trees during that year, and when they have all they want from your fields, leave the rest for wild animals.
translation_verse: Ke le ƒe adrelia me la na wòagbɔ ɖe eme, eye woazu flu, bena wò dukɔ la me ame dahewo nakpɔ nu aɖu, eye nusi susɔ la, gbemelãwo naɖui. Nenema ke nawɔ wò weingblewo kple wò devewo hãe.

english_verse: Work the first six days of the week, but rest and relax on the seventh day. This law is not only for you, but for your oxen, donkeys, and slaves, as well as for any foreigners among you.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke aɖe nawɔ wò dɔwo, ke naƒo ŋkeke adrelia ade eme, bena wò nyi kple wò tedzi nadzudzɔ, eye wò kosi ƒe ŋutsuvi kple amedzro nagbɔ ɖe eme.

english_verse: Make certain that you obey everything I have said. Don't pray to other gods or even mention their names. Three Annual Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: Midzra nya sia nya, si megblɔ na mi la ɖo. Migaɖu mawu bubuwo ƒe tame o, eye womagase woƒe ŋkɔ hã le nua nu o.

english_verse: Do not offer bread made with yeast when you sacrifice an animal to me. And make sure that the fat of the animal is burned that same day.
translation_verse: Megatsɔ nye vɔsalã ƒe ʋu sa vɔe le afisi amɔwɔ ʋaʋã le o, eye megadzra nye ŋkekenyuievɔsalã ƒe ami ɖi ŋu nake ɖe edzi o.

english_verse: Your women will give birth to healthy children, and everyone will live a long life.
translation_verse: Fu mage le nyɔnuwo ƒo, alo woatsi ko le wò anyigba dzi o; eye mana nanɔ agbe wòaɖe edeƒe.
