english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had said, and they celebrated Passover there in the desert in the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ɖu ŋutitotoŋkekenyuie la le Sinai-gbedzi le ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke wuienelia dzi le tiẽ; alesi Yehowa ɖe se na Mose la, nenema Israel-viwo wɔ. Alesi ame makɔmakɔwo kple mɔzɔlawo naɖu ŋutitotoŋkekenyuie la.

english_verse: Some people in Israel's camp had touched a dead body and had become unfit to worship the Lord, and they could not celebrate Passover. But they asked Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Ke ŋutsua ɖewo gblẽ kɔ ɖo ɖe ame kukuwo ŋu, eye womete ŋu ɖu ŋutitotoŋkekenyuie la gbemagbe o. Ŋutsu siawo va Mose kple Aron gbɔ le ŋkeke ma dzi,

english_verse: “Even though we have touched a dead body, why can't we celebrate Passover and offer sacrifices to the Lord at the same time as everyone else?”
translation_verse: eye wogblɔ nɛ bena: Miegblẽ kɔ ɖo ɖe ame kuku ŋu. Nukaŋuti miekpɔ mɔ atsɔ vɔsa vɛ na Yehowa akpe ɖe Israel-viwo ŋu le ɣeyiɣi la dzi o?

english_verse: Moses said, “Wait here while I go into the sacred tent and find out what the Lord says about this.”
translation_verse: Mose ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Milala, ne mase se, si Yehowa ade nam.

english_verse: The Lord then told Moses
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you or your descendants touch a dead body and become unfit to worship me, or if you are away on a long journey, you may still celebrate Passover.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na Israel-viwo be: Ne mia ŋutɔwo alo miaƒe dzidzimeviwo dometɔa de gblẽ kɔ ɖo ɖe ame kuku ŋu alo yi nugbe la, ekpɔ mɔ aɖu ŋutitotoŋkekenyuie la na Yehowa.

english_verse: But it must be done in the second month, in the evening of the fourteenth day. Eat the Passover lamb with thin bread and bitter herbs,
translation_verse: Woawo naɖui le ɣleti evelia ƒe ŋkeke wuienelia dzi le fiẽ, eye woatsɔ abolo maʋamaʋã ado ama veve.

english_verse: and don't leave any of it until morning or break any of the animal's bones. Be sure to follow these regulations.
translation_verse: Womagblẽ ɖeke ɖi ŋu nake ɖe edzi o, eye womagbã ƒua ɖeke hã o. Woaɖu ŋutitotoŋkekenyuie la ɖe ɖoɖo, siwo katã le eŋu la nu.

english_verse: But if any of you are fit to worship me, and yet refuse to celebrate Passover when you are not away on a journey, you will no longer belong to my people. You will be punished because you did not offer sacrifices to me at the proper time.
translation_verse: Ne amea de megblẽ kɔ ɖo o, eye meyi nugbe hã o, gake wògbe ŋutitotoŋkekenyuie la ɖuɖu la, ekema woatsrɔ̃ ame la ɖa le eƒe dukɔ me viwo dome, elabena mesa vɔ na Yehowa ɖe ɣeyiɣi la dzi o; ame la ŋutɔ ƒe nuvɔ̃ le edzi.

english_verse: Anyone, including foreigners who live among you, can celebrate Passover, if they follow all the regulations. The Cloud over the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Ne amedzro, si le mia dome be, yeaɖu ŋutitotoŋkekenyuie na Yehowa la, ekema wòaɖui ɖe ɖoɖo kple se, siwo le ŋutitotoŋkekenyuiea ŋu la nu. Ɖoɖo ɖeka nanɔ eŋu na amedzrovi kple duamevi siaa. Alilikpo kple dzo le asaɖa la tame.

english_verse: whether it was only one night, a few days, a month, or even a year. As long as the cloud remained over the tent, the Israelites stayed where they were. But when the cloud moved, so did the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ɖewo etsia anyi ŋkeke eve, ɣleti ɖeka alo wu nenema. Ne alilikpo la tsi nɔƒea dzi la, ekema Israel-viwo hã tsia asaɖa la me, eye womehona o; ke ne eho le edzi ta, ekema wohona.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: Have someone make two trumpets out of hammered silver. These will be used to call the people together and to give the signal for moving your camp.
translation_verse: Tso klosalo wo kpẽ eve, woawo natsɔ ayɔ ameha lae, eye woawo natsɔ ana asaɖawo nahoe.

english_verse: If both trumpets are blown, everyone is to meet with you at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ne woku kpẽawo wòtso tatata la, ekema ha blibo la naƒo ƒu ɖe gbɔwò le Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la nu

english_verse: But if just one is blown, only the twelve tribal leaders need to come together.
translation_verse: Ke ne woku kpẽ ɖeka ko tatata la, ekema Israel ƒe ame akpeawo ƒe amegãwo naƒo ƒu ɖe gbɔwo.

english_verse: Give a signal on a trumpet when it is time to break camp. The first blast will be the signal for the tribes camped on the east side, and the second blast will be the signal for those on the south.
translation_verse: Eye ne wogaku wo zi evelia tsiã ɖe nu la, ekema asaɖa, si le dziehe gome la, naho. Ne woku kpẽawo tsiã ɖe nu la, ekema woaho.

english_verse: But when you want everyone to come together, sound a different signal on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Ne wobe, ha la nava kpe ta la, ekema woaku kpẽawo tatata ko, gake womaku wo atsiã ɖe nu o.

english_verse: The priests of Aaron's family will be the ones to blow the trumpets, and this law will never change.
translation_verse: Aron viŋutsu, siwo nye nunɔlawo, naku kpẽawo; ɖoɖo mavɔ wòanye na miaƒe dzidzimeviwo.

english_verse: Whenever you go into battle against an enemy attacking your land, give a warning signal on the trumpets. Then I, the Lord, will hear it and rescue you.
translation_verse: Ne mieho aʋa le miaƒe anyigba dzi ɖe miaƒe futɔ, siwo le fu ɖem na mi la ŋu, eye mieku kpẽ tsiã ɖe nu la, ekema Yehowa, mia Mawu, aɖo ŋku mia dzi, eye wòaɖe mi atso miaƒe futɔwo si me.

english_verse: During the celebration of the New Moon Festival and other religious festivals, sound the trumpets while you offer sacrifices. This will be a reminder that I am the Lord your God. The Israelites Begin Their Journey
translation_verse: Gbesigbe miele dzidzɔ kpɔm, alo miele ŋkekenyuie ɖum, alo ɣleti yeye dze dzi, eye miesa numevɔ kple akpedavɔ la, ekema miaku kpẽ, eye wòana mia Mawu naɖo ŋku mia dzi. Nyee nye Yehowa, mia Mawu! Dukɔ la ho tso le Sinai-gbedzi.

english_verse: On the twentieth day of the second month of that same year, the cloud over the sacred tent moved on.
translation_verse: Le ƒe evelia me, le ɣleti evelia ƒe ŋkeke blavelia dzi la alilikpo la ho le nɔƒe, si sea le la dzi.

english_verse: So the Israelites broke camp and left the Sinai Desert. And some time later, the cloud stopped in the Paran Desert.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ho tso Sinai-gbedzi hamehame, eye alilikpo la va tɔ ɖe Paran-gbedzi.

english_verse: This was the first time the Lord had told Moses to command the people of Israel to move on.
translation_verse: Esia nye zi gbãtɔ woho ɖe se, si Yehowa de na Mose la nu.

english_verse: Judah and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out first, carrying their banner. Nahshon son of Amminadab was the leader of the Judah tribe,
translation_verse: Yuda-viwo ƒe asaɖa la ho gbã kple woƒe aflaga hamehame, eye woƒe aʋakɔ la fe tatɔ enye Naheson, Aminadab vi.

english_verse: Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the Issachar tribe,
translation_verse: Amesi le Isaxar-viwo to la ƒe aʋakɔ nu, enye Netaneel, Zuar vi,

english_verse: and Eliab son of Helon was the leader of the Zebulun tribe.
translation_verse: eye Eliab, Xelon vi, le Zebulon-viwo to la ƒe aʋakɔ nu.

english_verse: The sacred tent had been taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites carried it, marching behind the Judah camp.
translation_verse: Emegbe wokaka nɔƒe la, eye Gerson viwo kple Merari-viwo, amesiwo nye nɔƒe la tsɔlawo la ho.

english_verse: Reuben and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out second, carrying their banner. Elizur son of Shedeur was the leader of the Reuben tribe,
translation_verse: Eyome Ruben ƒe asaɖa la ho kple woƒe aflaga hamehame; woƒe aʋakɔ la ƒe tatɔ enye Elizur, Sedeur vi.

english_verse: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was the leader of the Simeon tribe,
translation_verse: Amesi le Simeon-viwo to la ƒe aʋakɔ nu, enye Selumiel, Zurisadai vi,

english_verse: and Eliasaph son of Deuel was the leader of the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: eye Elyasaf, Deguel vi, le Gad-viwo to la ƒe aʋakɔ nu.

english_verse: Next were the Kohathites, carrying the objects for the sacred tent, which was to be set up before they arrived at the new camp.
translation_verse: Emegbe Kehat-viwo, amesiwo nye nu kɔkɔeawo tsɔlawo la ho; wotua nɔƒe la, hafi woawo va ɖona

english_verse: Ephraim and the tribes that camped alongside it marched next, carrying their banner. Elishama son of Ammihud was the leader of the Ephraim tribe,
translation_verse: Eyome Efrayim-viwo ƒe asaɖa la ho kple woƒe aflaga hamehame; woƒe aʋakɔ la ƒe tatɔ enye Elisama, Amihud vi.

english_verse: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was the leader of the Manasseh tribe,
translation_verse: Amesi le Manase-viwo to la ƒe aʋakɔ nu, enye Gamliel, Pedazur vi,

english_verse: and Abidan son of Gideoni was the leader of the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: eye Abidan, Gideoni vi, le Benyamin-to la ƒe aʋakɔ nu.

english_verse: Dan and the tribes that camped alongside it were to protect the Israelites against an attack from behind, and so they marched last, carrying their banner. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was the leader of the tribe of Dan,
translation_verse: Emegbe Dan-viwo ƒe asaɖa la ho kple woƒe aflaga hamehame, woawo nye aʋakɔwo katã ƒe megbexeawo, eye woƒe aʋakɔ ƒe tatɔ enye Axieser, Amisadai vi.

english_verse: Pagiel son of Ochran was the leader of the Asher tribe,
translation_verse: Amesi le Aser-viwo ƒe to la ƒe aʋakɔ nu, enye Pagiel, Oxran vi,

english_verse: and Ahira son of Enan was the leader of the Naphtali tribe.
translation_verse: eye Axira, Enan vi, le Naftali-viwo to la ƒe aʋakɔ nu.

english_verse: Hobab the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses, was there. And Moses said to him, “We're leaving for the place the Lord has promised us. He has said that all will go well for us. So come along, and we will make sure that all goes well for you.”
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ na Hobab toa, Midiantɔ Reguel ƒe viŋutsu, bena: Miele hoho ge ayi teƒe, si Yehowa gblɔ be, yeatsɔ na mí la; wò hã yi kpli mí, eye míawɔ nyuie na wò, elabena Yehowa ɖo nyuie ɖe Israel ŋu.

english_verse: “No, I won't go,” Hobab answered. “I'm returning home to be with my own people.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Nyemayi kpli mi o, boŋ magbugbɔ ayi nye anyigba dzi kple ƒonyemeawo gbɔ.

english_verse: “Please go with us!” Moses said. “You can be our guide because you know the places to camp in the desert.
translation_verse: Egblɔ nɛ bena: Megagblẽ mí ɖi o dzro, elabena enya teƒe, siwo míaƒu asaɖa anyi ɖo le gbeadzi, eyata nanye ŋku na mí;

english_verse: Besides that, if you go, we will give you a share of the good things the Lord gives us.”
translation_verse: ne èyi kpli mí la, ekema miawo nyuie, si Yehowa awɔ na mí la na wò.

english_verse: The people of Israel began their journey from Mount Sinai. They traveled three days, and the Levites who carried the sacred chest led the way, so the Lord could show them where to camp.
translation_verse: Eye woho tso Yehowa to la gbɔ hezɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃ ƒe mɔ, eye Yehowa ƒe nubablaɖaka la dze wo ŋgɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃, be woadi dzudzɔƒe na wo.

english_verse: And the cloud always stayed with them.
translation_verse: Ne woho la, Yehowa ƒe alilikpo la nɔa wo ŋgɔ.

english_verse: Each day as the Israelites began their journey, Moses would pray, “Our Lord, defeat your enemies and make them run!”
translation_verse: Ne aɖaka la ho la, Mose gblɔna be: Yehowa, tsi tre, ne wò fofowo naka hlẽ, eye amesiwo le fu wò la, nasi le nuwò!

english_verse: And when they stopped to set up camp, he would pray, “Our Lord, stay close to Israel's thousands and thousands of people.”
translation_verse: Eye ne edro la, egblɔna be: Yehowa, gagbugbɔ va Israel ƒe ame akpeawo gbɔ!

english_verse: One day the Israelites started complaining about their troubles. The Lord heard them and became so angry that he destroyed the outer edges of their camp with fire.
translation_verse: Eye dukɔ la li liʋĩliʋi le Yehowa ŋu le fuwɔame ta Yehowa see; eye wòdo dɔmedzoe eye Yehowa na dzo dze aƒe le wo dome, eye asaɖa ƒe mlɔenu bi dzo.

english_verse: When the people begged Moses to help, he prayed, and the fire went out.
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la do ɣli na Mose, eye Mose ɖe kuku na Yehowa, enumake dzo la tsi.

english_verse: They named the place “Burning,” because in his anger the Lord had set their camp on fire. The People Grumble about Being Hungry
translation_verse: Eye wona ŋkɔ afima be „dzobiƒe“, elabena Yehowa na dzo dze aƒe le wo dome. Dukɔ la ƒe nudzodzro.

english_verse: One day some foreigners among the Israelites became greedy for food, and even the Israelites themselves began moaning, “We don't have any meat!
translation_verse: Eye yakame, siwo le wo do me la, de asi nudzodzro me, tete Israel-viwo gafa avi gblɔ bena: Ameka gɔ̃e le lã na ge mi miaɖu hã?

english_verse: In Egypt we could eat all the fish we wanted, and there were cucumbers, melons, all kinds of onions, and garlic.
translation_verse: Mieɖo ŋku tɔmelã, siwo míeɖuna le Egipte dzodzro, kpakple adzamatre, aɖiba, agumetaku, sabala kple gbegãdziwo dzi.

english_verse: But we're starving out here, and the only food we have is this manna.”
translation_verse: Azɔ miaƒe veme ƒu; naneke mele afisia o, negbe mana sia ko kpɔm miele.

english_verse: The manna was like small whitish seeds
translation_verse: Mana la lolo abe xetsetsee ene, eye wòdzena abe Bedolion ene.

english_verse: He prayed: I am your servant, Lord, so why are you doing this to me? What have I done to deserve this? You've made me responsible for all these people,
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ na Yehowa bena: Nukaŋuti nèwɔ vɔ ɖe wò dɔla ŋu, eye nukaŋuti méve nunye o, eye netsɔ dukɔ blibo sia ƒe agba ɖo dzinye?

english_verse: but they're not my children. You told me to nurse them along and to carry them to the land you promised their ancestors.
translation_verse: Alo nyee fɔ dukɔ blibo sia ƒe fua? Eye nyee dzi wo, hafi nèle gbɔgblɔm nam be, matsɔ wo ɖe akɔ nu, abe alesi vitsɔla tsɔa vidzie ene, ayi anyigba, si ŋu nèka atam ɖo na wo fofowo la dzia?

english_verse: They keep whining for meat, but where can I get meat for them?
translation_verse: Afika makpɔ lã atsoe na dukɔ blibo sia? Elabena wole avi fam nam le gbɔgblɔm be: Na lã mí miaɖu!

english_verse: This job is too much for me. How can I take care of all these people by myself?
translation_verse: Nye ɖeka nyemate ŋu atsɔ dukɔ blibo sia o, elabena wole kpeyem akpa.

english_verse: If this is the way you're going to treat me, just kill me now and end my miserable life! Seventy Leaders Are Chosen To Help Moses
translation_verse: Nenye alea nèle wɔ ye gee la, ekema wum zi ɖeka boŋ, nenye be, eve nunye; bena magakpɔ nye dzɔgbevɔ̃e teƒe o. Amegã blaadre gblɔ nya ɖi.

english_verse: While I am talking with you there, I will give them some of your authority, so they can share responsibility for my people. You will no longer have to care for them by yourself.
translation_verse: Maɖi ava ƒo nu kpli wò le afima, eye maɖe gbɔgbɔ, si le dziwò la, ƒe ɖe ada ɖe wo dzi, bena woatso dukɔ la ƒe agba na wò ti, eye wò ɖeka matsɔe o.

english_verse: As for the Israelites, I have heard them complaining about not having meat and about being better off in Egypt. So tell them to make themselves acceptable to me, because tomorrow they will have meat.
translation_verse: Ke gblɔ na dukɔ la bena: Mikɔ mia ɖokui ŋu hena etsɔ; miakpɔ lã aɖu, elabena mieta avi ɖe Yehowa ƒe to me gblɔ bena: Ameka ana lã mi miaɖu? Eme nyo na mí le Egipte! Eyata Yehowa le lã na ge mi miaɖu.

english_verse: . They turned against me and wanted to go back to Egypt. Now they will eat meat until they get sick of it.
translation_verse: boŋ ɣleti ɖeka sɔŋ, vaseɖe esime wòado alo ŋɔti me na mi, eye woazu ŋunyɔnu na mi; elabena mieɖo vlo Yehowa, si le mia dome, eye miefa avi nɛ bena; Nukata gɔ̃ míedzo le Egipte ɖo?

english_verse: Even if we butchered all our sheep and cattle, or caught every fish in the sea, we wouldn't have enough to feed them.”
translation_verse: Alẽ alo nyie wole wuwu ge, hafi wòaɖe wo nu loo, alo ƒumelãwo katãe woaƒo ƒu, hafi wòaɖe wo nua?

english_verse: The Lord answered, “I can do anything! Watch and you'll see my words come true.”
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Ɖe Yehowa ƒe asi to ɖe emea? Azɔ àkpɔe be, nye nya la le eme loo, alo mele eme o.

english_verse: Eldad and Medad were two leaders who had not gone to the tent. But when the Spirit took control of them, they began shouting like prophets right there in camp.
translation_verse: Ke ŋutsu eve tsi asaɖa la me, amesiwo dometɔ ɖeka ŋkɔ enye Eldad, eye evelia ŋkɔ nye Medad. Eye gbɔgbɔ la va woawo hã dzi, wode asi nyagbɔgblɔ me ɖi le asaɖa la me; elabena woŋlɔ wo ŋkɔwo, gake womeva agbadɔ la gbɔ o.

english_verse: A boy ran to Moses and told him about Eldad and Medad.
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsuvia ɖe ƒu du ɖagblɔ na Mose bena: Eldad kple Medad wode asi nyagbɔgblɔ me ɖi le asaɖa la me.

english_verse: Joshua was there helping Moses, as he had done since he was young. And he said to Moses, “Sir, you must stop them!”
translation_verse: Eye Yosua, Nun vi, amesi nye Mose ƒe dɔla tso ɖekakpuime ke la, do ŋu be: Nye aƒetɔ Mose, gbe na wo!

english_verse: But Moses replied, “Are you concerned what this might do to me? I wish the Lord would give his Spirit to all his people so everyone could be a prophet.”
translation_verse: Ke Mose ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Wòe le ŋu ʋã ge ɖe nunyea? Oo, Yehowa mana eƒe gbagba nava dukɔ blibo la dzi, eye wòatrɔ zu Yehowa ƒe nyagblɔɖilawo dzro oa? Tegliwo kple „nudzrolawo ɖiƒe“.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord sent a strong wind that blew quails in from the sea until Israel's camp was completely surrounded with birds, piled up about a meter high for many kilometers in every direction.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa na yaa ɖe ƒo, eye wòlɔ tegliwo tso ƒu gome kɔ ɖe wo nɔewo dzi ƒo xlã asaɖa la godoo va kpe; wozɔ wo ŋu le go si me ŋkeke ɖeka, eye wozɔ wo ŋu le go keme me hã ŋkeke ɖeka, eye wokɔ tso anyigba ano abɔklugui eve.

english_verse: The people picked up quails for two days—each person filled at least ten large baskets. Then they spread them out to dry.
translation_verse: Eye dukɔ la tso yi ɖafɔ tegliawo ŋkeke blibo la kple zã blibo la kpakple ŋkeke, si dze eyome hã; amesi fɔe ʋee ko la tɔ ade gomer ewo, eye wosia wo ƒo xlã asaɖa la godoo va kpe.

english_verse: But before the meat could be eaten, the Lord became angry and sent a deadly disease through the camp.
translation_verse: Lã la mekpɔ do le aɖu tame na wo wòahayi wo katã ɖu ge avɔ o, tete Yehowa do dɔmedzoe ɖe dukɔ la ŋu, eye Yehowa na do vɔ̃ɖia ɖe ɖo dukɔ la dome.

english_verse: After they had buried the people who had been so greedy for meat, they called the place “Graves for the Greedy.”
translation_verse: Eye wona ŋkɔ teƒe la bena „nudzrolawo ɖiƒe“, elabena afima woɖi dukɔ, si dzro nu la ɖo.

english_verse: Israel then broke camp and traveled to Hazeroth.
translation_verse: Emegbe dukɔ la ho tso „nudzrolawo ɖiƒe“ heva Xazerot, eye wotsi Xazerot.

english_verse: and told Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to come to the entrance of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose kple Aron kpakple Miryam bena: Mia kple etɔ̃ la mido va Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la gbɔ, eye woa kple etɔ̃ la wodo va.

english_verse: There the Lord appeared in a cloud and told Aaron and Miriam to come closer.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ɖi va agbadɔ la nu le alilikpo dodoa ɖe me, eye wòyɔ Aron kple Miryam, eye woa kple eve la woyi.

english_verse: Then after commanding them to listen carefully, he said: “I, the Lord, speak to prophets in visions and dreams.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Mise gbenye! Ne amea ɖe nye Yehowa ƒe nyagblɔɖila le mia dome la, ekema meɖea ɖokuinye fianɛ le ŋutega me, eye meƒoa nu kplii le drɔ̃e me.

english_verse: But my servant Moses is the leader of my people.
translation_verse: Ke menye alea mewɔna na nye dɔla Mose, amesi nye anukwaretɔ le nye aƒe blibo la nu o;

english_verse: He sees me face to face, and everything I say to him is perfectly clear. You have no right to criticize my servant Moses.”
translation_verse: boŋ nye ŋutɔ meƒoa nu kplii ŋku me kple ŋku me, nyemetoa adzo nɛ o, ke boŋ meɖea nuawo ŋutɔ fia nɛ, eye wòkpɔ Yehowa ƒe dzedzeme. Nukaŋuti mieva nye dɔla o, eye mieƒo nu le Mose ŋua?

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Aaron and Miriam. And after the Lord left
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa do dɔmedzoe ɖe wo ŋu hedzo.

english_verse: and the cloud disappeared from over the sacred tent, Miriam's skin turned white with leprosy. When Aaron saw what had happened to her,
translation_verse: Esi alilikpo la ho tso agbadɔa dzi la, kasia Miryam dze anyi, eye wòfu ɣie abe agbelimɔwɔtsi ene; eye esi Aron trɔ ɖe Miryam ŋu la, kpo ɖa, edze anyi.

english_verse: he said to Moses, “Sir, please don't punish us for doing such a foolish thing.
translation_verse: Tete Aron gblɔ na Mose bena: Ao, nye aƒetɔ, megana woahe to na mí le nuvɔ̃, si míetsi bome wo la ta o.

english_verse: Don't let Miriam's flesh rot away like a child born dead!”
translation_verse: Megana wòano abe ɖevi, si ku ɖe dɔ me na dada, eye eƒe akpa ɖeka vo, hafi wodzii la ene o!

english_verse: Moses prayed, “Lord God, please heal her.”
translation_verse: Tete Mose ɖo ɣli na Yehowa bena: Ao, yɔ dɔe dzro!

english_verse: But the Lord replied, “Miriam would be disgraced for seven days if her father had punished her by spitting in her face. So make her stay outside the camp for seven days, before coming back.”
translation_verse: Yehowa ɖo ŋu na Mose bena; Ɖe wònye fofoa ye ɖe ta ɖe mo nɛ la, ne ŋu makpee ŋkeke adre oa? Eyata woatui ɖe xɔ me le asaɖa godo ŋkeke adre, emegbe hafi woagaxɔe.

english_verse: The people of Israel did not move their camp until Miriam returned seven days later.
translation_verse: Ale woɖe Miryam xa ɖe asaɖa godo ŋkeke adre; ke dukɔ la meho o, vaseɖe esime wogaxɔ Miryam hafi.

english_verse: Then they left Hazeroth and set up camp in the Paran Desert.
translation_verse: Emegbe dukɔ la ho tso Xazerot, eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Paran-gbedzi.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: In fact, we saw the Nephilim who are the ancestors of the Anakim. They were so big that we felt as small as grasshoppers.”
translation_verse: Miekpɔ Enak viwo, amesiwo nye ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe dzidzimeviwo, hã le afima, eye miawo ɖeko míedze abe ʋetsuviwo ene, eye nenema woawo hã kpɔ míi.

english_verse: “Choose a leader from each tribe and send them into Canaan to explore the land I am giving you.”
translation_verse: Dɔ ŋutsuwo ɖa, bena woaɖatsa ŋku le Kanaan-nyigba, si tsɔ ge mala ana Israel-viwo la dzi. Midɔ ŋutsu ɖekaɖeka tso wo fofowo ƒe toawo me; ame ŋkutawo sɔŋ woanye.

english_verse: So Moses sent twelve tribal leaders from Israel's camp in the Paran Desert
translation_verse: Eye Mose ɖɔ wo ɖa tso Paran-gbedzi le Yehowa ƒe se la nu; ŋutsuawo, katã nye ame ŋkutawo le Israel-viwo dome.

english_verse: Before Moses sent them into Canaan, he said: After you go through the Southern Desert of Canaan, continue north into the hill country
translation_verse: Eye Mose dɔ wo, bena woaɖatsa ŋku le Kanaan-nyigba dzi hegblɔ na wo bena: Miyi ɖe anyigba la ƒe dziehe gome, eye miaha toawo.

english_verse: and find out what those regions are like. Be sure to remember how many people live there, how strong they are,
translation_verse: Milé ŋku ɖe alesi anyigba la le kple dukɔ, si le edzi la ŋu, abe wo kako alo wo beli, wole ʋee alo wosɔ gbɔ ene;

english_verse: and if they live in open towns or walled cities. See if the land is good for growing crops and find out what kinds of trees grow there. It's time for grapes to ripen, so try to bring back some of the fruit that grows there.
translation_verse: alesi anyigba la le, ewɔa nu alo mewɔa nu o, atiwo le edzi alo womelé edzi o. Milé dzi ɖe ƒo, no miatsɔ anyigba dzi kutsetsea ɖewo agbɔe, ɣemaɣi weintsetsewo dze ɖiɖi gɔme.

english_verse: The twelve men left to explore Canaan from the Zin Desert in the south all the way to the town of Rehob near Lebo-Hamath in the north.
translation_verse: Eye woyi ɖatsa ŋku le anyigba la dzi tso Zin-gbedzi vaseɖe Rexob heɖo ta Xamat.

english_verse: As they went through the Southern Desert, they came to the town of Hebron, which was seven years older than the Egyptian town of Zoan. In Hebron, they saw the three Anakim clans of Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai.
translation_verse: Woɖo ta dziehe vaseɖe Xebron, afisi Aximan, Sesai kple Talmai, amesiwo nye Enak viwo nɔ. Ke wotso Xebron ƒe adre megbe, hafi wova tso Zoan le Egipte.

english_verse: the twelve men returned to Kadesh in the Paran Desert and told Moses, Aaron, and the people what they had seen. They showed them the fruit
translation_verse: Eye wogbɔ va Mose kple Aron kpakple Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la gbɔ, le Kades le Paran-gbedzi, hegblɔ dɔgbedenyawo na woa kple ha blibo la, eye wotia anyigba dzi kutsetseawo hã wo.

english_verse: and said: Look at this fruit! The land we explored is rich with milk and honey.
translation_verse: Eye wòto woƒe numegbe la nɛ bena: Miede anyigba, si dzi nedɔ mí ɖo la dzi; notsi kple anyitsi bɔ ɖe edzi vava, eye edzi kutsetsewo hã enye si;

english_verse: But the people who live there are strong, and their cities are large and walled. We even saw the three Anakim clans.
translation_verse: negbe dukɔ, si le anyigba la dzi, koe kako, woƒe duwo sesẽ, eye wololo, eye míekpɔ Enak viwo hã le afima.

english_verse: Besides that, the Amalekites live in the Southern Desert; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites are in the hill country; and the Canaanites live along the Mediterranean Sea and the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Amalekitɔwo le dziehe gome, Xititɔwo, Yebusitɔwo kple Amoritɔwo le towo dzi, eye Kanaanitɔwo le ƒu ŋu kple Yordan ƒe go ɖeka

english_verse: Caleb calmed down the crowd and said, “Let's go and take the land. I know we can do it!”
translation_verse: Ke Kaleb tsi nya ɖe dukɔ la nu hexɔ ɖe Mose dzi bena: Míate ŋu ade, eye míaxɔe, m ate ŋui kokoko tsã!

english_verse: But the other men replied, “Those people are much too strong for us.”
translation_verse: Ke ŋutsu, siwo hã ɖe la, gblɔ bena: Míate ŋu ade dukɔ mawo gbɔ o, elabena wosesẽ wu mi.

english_verse: Then they started spreading rumors and saying, “We won't be able to grow anything in that soil. And the people are like giants.
translation_verse: Eye wode vɔvɔ̃ anyigba, si dzi wotsa ŋku le la, ŋu na Israel-viwo be: Anyigba, si dzi miede ɖatsa ŋku le la, le edzinɔlawo mim, eye dukɔ, siwo katã le edzi la, nye ame kplalawo sɔŋ.

english_verse: and complained to Moses and Aaron, “We wish we had died in Egypt or somewhere out here in the desert!
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo katã li Mose kple Aron ŋu, eye ha blibo la gblɔ na wo bena: Oo, ɖe mieku le Egipte-nyigba dzi boŋ, ɖe mieku le gbe sia dzi boŋ la, ne nyo wu!

english_verse: Is the Lord leading us into Canaan, just to have us killed and our women and children captured? We'd be better off in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Nukata gɔ̃ Yehowa kplɔ mí va anyigba sia dzi, bena míatsi yi nu, eye mia srɔ̃wo kple mia viwo nazu aboyonu? Ne míagbugbɔ ayi Egipte la, ɖe manyo na mí awu oa?

english_verse: Then they said to one another, “Let's choose our own leader and go back.”
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ na wo nɔewo bena: Mina míaɖo tatɔ na mía ɖokui, eye míagbugbɔ ayi Egipte!

english_verse: Moses and Aaron bowed down to pray in front of the crowd.
translation_verse: Tete Mose kple Aron tsyɔ mo anyi ɖe Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la katã ŋku me.

english_verse: and said: We saw the land ourselves, and it's very good.
translation_verse: eye wogblɔ na Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la bena: Anyigba, si dzi miede ɖatsa ŋku le la, nyo ʋuu keke tso me.

english_verse: If we obey the Lord, he will surely give us that land rich with milk and honey.
translation_verse: Ne miaƒe nu dze Yehowa ŋu ko la, ekema akplɔ mí ayi anyigba sia dzii, eye wòatsɔ anyigba, si dzi notsi kple anyitsi bɔ ɖo la, na mi.

english_verse: So don't rebel. We have no reason to be afraid of the people who live there. The Lord is on our side, and they won't stand a chance against us!
translation_verse: Ɖeko migadze aglã ɖe Yehowa ŋu o, eye migavɔ̃ anyigbadzitɔwo o, elabena wole na mi abe abolo ene. Luʋɔ dzo le wo ta, ke Yehowa li kpli miawo ya, eyata migavɔ̃ wo o!

english_verse: The crowd threatened to stone Moses and Aaron to death. But just then, the Lord appeared in a cloud at the sacred tent. Moses Prays for the People
translation_verse: Ke ha blibo la be, yewoaƒu kpe wo woaku, tete Yehowa ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe do ɖe Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la gbɔ le Israel-viwo katã ŋku me.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I have done great things for these people, and they still reject me by refusing to believe in my power.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Zi nenie gɔ̃ dukɔ sia ado vlom, eye zi nenie woagbe dzinye xɔxɔ ase? Evɔ wonye mewo dzesi geɖewo le wo dome hafi?

english_verse: So they will no longer be my people. I will destroy them, but I will make you the ancestor of a nation even stronger than theirs.”
translation_verse: Eyata matsɔ dɔvɔ̃ atsrɔ̃ wo, eye mana dukɔ gãa ɖe, si asẽ ŋu wu wo la, nadzo tso mewo

english_verse: Show us your great power, Lord. You promised
translation_verse: Eyata Aƒetɔ, ɖe wo ŋusẽ fia, abe alesi negblɔ ene be:

english_verse: that you love to show mercy and kindness. And you said that you are very patient, but that you will punish everyone guilty of doing wrong—not only them but their children and grandchildren as well.
translation_verse: Yehowa gbɔa dzi blewu, eye eƒe amenuveve sɔ gbɔ, etsɔa vodada kple dzidada kena, ke megbea tohehe o, boŋ etua fofowo ƒe vodadawo ŋuti fe na viwo vaseɖe dzidzime etɔ̃lia kple enelia dzi.

english_verse: You are merciful, and you treat people better than they deserve. So please forgive these people, just as you have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Eyata tsɔ dukɔ sia ƒe vodada ke wo le wò amenuveve gã la nu, abe alesi nẽtsɔe ke dukɔ sia tso Egipte ke vaseɖe afisia ene.

english_verse: But as surely as I live and my power has no limit,
translation_verse: Gake zi alesi mele agbe, eye Yehowa ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe ayɔ anyigba blibo la dzi la, ayɔ anyigba blibo la dzi

english_verse: But my servant Caleb isn't like the others. So because he has faith in me, I will allow him to cross into Canaan, and his descendants will settle there.
translation_verse: Ke makplɔ nye dɔla Kaleb ayi anyigba, si dzi wògbɔ tso la dzi, eye wòazu eƒe dzidzimeviwo to, elabena gbɔgbɔ bubu le eme, eye wodze yonyeme blibo.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose kpakple Aron bena:

english_verse: to give this message to the people of Israel: You sinful people have complained against me too many times! Now I swear by my own life that I will give you exactly what you wanted.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na wo be, Yehowa ƒe numegbe enye si: Meta nye agbe be, mawo mi, abe alesi miegblɔ ɖe nye to me ene!

english_verse: You will die right here in the desert, and your dead bodies will cover the ground. You have insulted me, and none of you men who are over
translation_verse: Mia dometɔ, siwo wotia xlẽ amesiwo xɔ ƒe blave kple vo la, woaku ɖe gbe sia dzi keŋkeŋ, le esi mieli ŋunye la ta.

english_verse: will enter the land that I solemnly promised to give you as your own—only Caleb and Joshua will go in.
translation_verse: Miade anyigba, si ŋu meka atam ɖo na mi be, mianɔ edzi la dzi o, negbe Kaleb, Yefune vi, kple Yosua, Nun vi ko.

english_verse: You were worried that your own children would be captured. But I, the Lord, will let them enter the land you have rejected.
translation_verse: Ke makplɔ mia vi, siwo ŋu miegblɔ le be, woazu aboyonu la, ayi edzi, bena woakpɔ anyigba, si miedo vloe la.

english_verse: You will die here in the desert!
translation_verse: Gake miawo miaku ɖe gbe sia dzi kokoko.

english_verse: So they got up early the next morning and got ready to head toward the hill country of Canaan. They said, “We were wrong to complain about the Lord. Let's go into the land that he promised us.”
translation_verse: Wotso ŋdi kanya, eye wolia to la hegblɔ bena: Ɖe mieva afisia, be míayi teƒe, si ŋu Yehowa ƒo nu le la; elabena miewo nuvɔ̃.

english_verse: You sinful people who ganged up against me will die here in the desert.
translation_verse: Nye Yehowae gblɔe, eye alea mawɔ ha vɔ̃ɖi sia, si dze aglã ɖe ŋunye lae; gbe sia dzi woatsrɔ̃ ɖo, eye afisia woaku ɖo!

english_verse: Ten of the men sent to explore the land had brought back bad news and had made the people complain against the Lord.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa na ɖɔ vɔ̃ɖia ɖe ɖo amesiwo Mose dɔ be, woaɖatsa ŋku le anyigba dzi, amesiwo trɔ gbɔ, eye wode ŋɔdzi anyigba la ŋu hena ha blibo la li eŋu la dome,

english_verse: So he sent a deadly disease that killed those men,
translation_verse: eye woku, le esi wode ŋɔdzi anyigbaa ŋu la ta.

english_verse: but he let Joshua and Caleb live. The Israelites Fail To Enter Canaan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ke Yosua, Nun vi, kple Kaleb, Yefune vi, koe tsi agbe le ŋutsu, siwo ɖe ɖatsa ŋku le anyigbae dzi la dome.

english_verse: But Moses replied, “You're disobeying the Lord! Your plan won't work,
translation_verse: Ke Mose gblɔ bena: Nukaŋuti miele Yehowa ƒe se la dzi dam? Mehele edzi dze ge o!

english_verse: The Amalekites and the Canaanites came down from the hill country, defeated the Israelites, and chased them as far as the town of Hormah.
translation_verse: Tete Amalekitɔwo kple Kanaanitɔwo, amesiwo le to sia dzi la, va si wo, eye woka wo hlẽ vaseɖe Xorma ke.

english_verse: The people of Israel were very sad after Moses gave them the Lord's message.
translation_verse: Esi Mose gblɔ nya siawo na Israel-viwo katã la, dukɔ la xa nu ŋutɔ.

english_verse: so don't even try it. The Lord refuses to help you, because you turned your backs on him. The Amalekites and the Canaanites are your enemies, and they will attack and defeat you.”
translation_verse: Amalekitɔwo kple Kanaanitɔwo le mia ŋgɔ le afima, eye míatsi yi nu. Esi mietrɔ le Yehowa yome la, eyata Yehowa manɔ kpli mi o.

english_verse: But the Israelites ignored Moses and marched toward the hill country, even though the sacred chest and Moses did not go with them.
translation_verse: Ke wosẽ tame helia to la, gake Yehowa ƒe nubablaɖaka la kple Mose wotsi asaɖa la me.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: to give the Israelites the following laws about offering sacrifices:
translation_verse: Ƒo nu kple Israel-viwo, eye nagblɔ na wo bena: Ne miava anyigba, si matsɔ na mi mianɔ edzi la dzi,

english_verse: Bulls or rams or goats are the animals that you may burn on the altar as sacrifices to please me. You may also offer sacrifices voluntarily or because you made a promise, or because they are part of your regular religious ceremonies. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices is pleasing to me.
translation_verse: eye mieɖe adzɔgbe alo na nu le mia ɖokui si alo le ŋkekenyuie ɖum hehe, yewoatsɔ nyi alo alé asa dzovɔ na Yehowa, eɖanye numevɔ alo akpedavɔ o, bena wòaʋẽ lilili ɖe Yehowa la,

english_verse: If you sacrifice a young ram or goat, you must also offer a kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil as a grain sacrifice. A liter of wine must also be poured on the altar.
translation_verse: Eye natsɔ wein awɔ nunovɔsa akpe ɖe numevɔsa kple akpedavɔsa la ŋu; hin ƒe eneliawo ɖeka nanɔ alẽvi ɖeka ŋu.

english_verse: If a bull is offered as a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing,
translation_verse: Ke ne èbe, yeatsɔ nyivi asa numevɔ, adzɔgbeɖevɔ alo akpedavɔ na Yehowa la,

english_verse: you must offer three kilograms of flour mixed with two liters of olive oil.
translation_verse: ekema natsɔ wɔ memee efa ƒe ewoliawo etɔ̃, si wotsɔ ami hin afã dzabae la, akpe ɖe nyivi la ŋu,

english_verse: Two liters of wine must also be poured on the altar. The smell of this smoke is pleasing to me.
translation_verse: eye natsɔ wein hin afã, awɔ nunovɔsa akpe ɖe eŋu. Esiawo natsɔ asa vɔe, bena wòaʋẽ lilili ɖe Yehowa.

english_verse: If you are a native Israelite, you must obey these rules each time you offer a bull, a ram, or a goat as a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Ne duamevi sia duamevi sa dzovɔ, be wòaʋẽ lilili ɖe Yehowa la, wòawɔe alea.

english_verse: This law will never change. I am the Lord, and I consider all people the same, whether they are Israelites or foreigners living among you.
translation_verse: Se ɖeka kple ɖoɖo ɖeka nanɔ eŋu na mia kple amedzro, si le mia dome la siaa. Amɔwɔ ƒe gbɔ̃tɔ.

english_verse: When you eat food in the land that I am giving you, remember to set aside some of it as an offering to me.
translation_verse: eye miekpɔ abolo ɖu le anyigba dzi la, ekema miana adzɔ Yehowa.

english_verse: From the first batch of bread dough that you make after each new grain harvest, make a loaf of bread and offer it to me, just as you offer grain.
translation_verse: Mitsɔ miaƒe wɔ gbãtɔwo tɔ tatali ahana; eya nanye adzɔ tso miaƒe lu, siwo mieƒo la me.

english_verse: All your descendants must follow this law and offer part of the first batch of bread dough.
translation_verse: Mia kple miaƒe dzidzimeviwo miatsɔ miaƒe wɔ gbãtɔwo ƒe ɖe ana adzɔ Yehowa. Gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔ nuvɔ̃ kple tameɖotɔ.

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses to tell the people what must be done if they ever disobey his laws:
translation_verse: miewɔ se, siwo katã Yehowa na Mose de na mi, tso gbesigbe Yehowa de asi sedede me na mi hena miaƒe dzidzimeviwo dzi la, dzi o;

english_verse: If all of you disobey one of my laws without knowing it, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice, a wine offering, and a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: ne ha blibo la ɖe ŋu ɖi da ƒu la, ekema ha blibo la nana nyitsuvi ɖeka, bena woasa numevɔ, si aʋẽ lilili ɖe Yehowa lae, eye woawɔ nuɖuvɔsa kple nunovɔsa ɖe ɖoɖo la nu; eye woana gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka, woawɔ nuvɔ̃vɔsae.

english_verse: Then the priest will pray and ask me to forgive you. And since you did not mean to do wrong, and you offered sacrifices,
translation_verse: Eye nunɔla nalé avu na Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la, eye woatsɔe ake wo; elabena ɖe woɖe ŋu ɖi da ƒu, eyata wona nu, be woatsɔ sa dzovɔ na Yehowa, eye wosa nuvɔ̃vɔ le Yehowa ŋku me, le esi woɖe ŋu ɖi da ƒu la ta.

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong without knowing it, you must sacrifice a year-old female goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Ke nenye ame ɖeka koe ɖe ŋu ɖi da ƒu la, ekema wòana gbɔ̃nɔ, si xɔ ƒe ɖeka, woawɔ nuvɔ̃vɔsae.

english_verse: The priest will then ask me to forgive you, and your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Eye nunɔla nawɔ avulenuwo na amesi ɖe ŋu ɖi da ƒu la, le Yehowa ŋku me ahale avu nɛ, eye woatsɔe akee.

english_verse: The law will be the same for anyone who does wrong without meaning to, whether an Israelite or a foreigner living among you.
translation_verse: Se ɖeka nanɔ mia si na amesiwo ɖe ŋu ɖi da ƒu la, eɖanye Israel-viwo ŋutɔ alo amedzro, si le mia dome la o.

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong on purpose, whether Israelite or foreigner, you have sinned against me by disobeying my laws. You will no longer belong to my people. A Man Put to Death for Gathering Firewood on the Sabbath
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe nya wodo vloe, eve eƒe se dzi wòda, eyata ele be, woatsrɔ̃ ame la ɖa kokoko, eya ŋutɔ ƒe fɔɖiɖi le edzi. Tohehe na amesi gblẽ kɔ ɖo na Sabat.

english_verse: Once, while the Israelites were traveling through the desert, a man was caught gathering firewood on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Esi Israel-viwo nɔ gbedzi la, wokpɔ ŋutsua ɖe le nake tɔm le dzudzɔgbeŋkeke la dzi.

english_verse: He was taken to Moses, Aaron, and the rest of the community.
translation_verse: Eye amesiwo kpɔe wole nakea fɔm la, kplɔe va Mose kple Aron kpakple ha blibo la gbɔ.

english_verse: But no one knew what to do with him, so he was not allowed to leave.
translation_verse: Eye wolée da ɖi, elabena womenya nusi woawɔe la gobi o.

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Tell the people to take that man outside the camp and stone him to death!”
translation_verse: Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Ele be, woawu ŋutsu la; ha blibo la naƒu kpee le asaɖa la godo, woaku.

english_verse: So he was killed, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Tassels on the People's Clothes
translation_verse: Tete ha blibo la kplɔe yi ɖe asaɖa la godo, eye woƒu kpee wòku, abe alesi Yehowa de se na Mose ene. Dzesinu le awuwo ŋu.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena:

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel, “Sew tassels onto the bottom edge of your clothes and tie a blue string to each tassel.
translation_verse: Ƒo nu kple Israel-viwo, eye nagblɔ na wo be: Mia kple miaƒe dzidzimeviwo miade gbo miaƒe avɔwo to, eye woatsi gboa ɖe aɖabɛ blɔtɔ lɔ̃ka ŋu.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God who led you out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Nyee nye Yehowa, mia Mawu, si kplɔ mi tso Egipte-nyigba dzi, be manye miaƒe Mawu. Nye Yehowa, mia Mawu!

english_verse: Korah son of Izhar was a Levite from the Kohathite clan. One day he called together Dathan, Abiram, and On from the Reuben tribe, and the four of them decided to rebel against Moses. So they asked
translation_verse: dze aglã ɖe Mose ŋuti, eye Israel-viwo dome ŋutsu alafa eve blaatɔ̃, amesiwo nye ŋkutatɔwo le ha la dome, eye wonye adaŋudelawo le takpekpewo me kple ame ŋkɔŋuwo la, kpe ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: and Aaron and said, “Why do you think you're so much better than everyone else? We're part of the Lord's holy people, and he's with all of us. What makes you think you're the only ones in charge?”
translation_verse: Eye wokpe ta ɖe Mose kple Aron ŋu hegblɔ na wo bena: Mia tɔ do ɖoɖo akpa! Ha blibo la le kokoe, eye Yehowa le wo dome tso, nukaŋuti miawo miele mia ɖokui dom ɖe dzi le Yehowa ƒe dukɔ la dome ale?

english_verse: When Moses heard this, he knelt down to pray.
translation_verse: Esi Mose see la, etsyɔ mo anyi.

english_verse: Then he said to Korah and his followers: Tomorrow morning the Lord will show us the person he has chosen to be his priest, and that man will faithfully serve him.
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ na Korax kple eƒe ha blibo la bena: Etsɔ la Yehowa aɖe amesi nye etɔ, amesi le kɔkɔe, be wòate ɖe eŋu kple amesi wòaha, be woate ɖe eŋu la, afia.

english_verse: Korah, here is what you and your followers must do: Get some fire pans, fill them with coals and incense, and place them near the sacred tent. And the man the Lord chooses will be his priest. Korah, this time you Levites have gone too far!
translation_verse: eye miaɖe dzo ɖe wo me atsɔ dzudzɔdonu ada ɖe dzi le Yehowa ŋku me etsɔ, eye amesi ke Yehowa atia la, eya nanye ame kɔkɔe. Mi Lewi-viwo, mia tɔ ɖi kpi gbɔ me akpa!

english_verse: You know that the God of Israel has chosen you Levites from all Israel to serve him by being in charge of the sacred tent and by helping the community to worship in the proper way. What more do you want?
translation_verse: Mesɔ gbɔ na mi haɖe be, Israel ƒe Mawu la tia mi tso Israel ƒe ha la me, be miate ɖe eŋu, eye miawɔ dɔ le Yehowa ƒe nɔƒe la ŋu, mianɔ ha la nu, eve miasubɔ wo oa?

english_verse: The Lord has given you a special responsibility, and now, Korah, you think you should also be his priest.
translation_verse: Ena mia kple nɔviwò Lewi viwo katã miegogoe tso, azɔ miegale nunɔladɔ hã dima?

english_verse: You and your followers have rebelled against the Lord, not against Aaron.
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa ŋue mia kple wò ha blibo la mietsi tre ɖo; ameka nye Aron, hafi miele eŋu lĩm?

english_verse: Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, but they sent back this message: “We won't come!
translation_verse: Eye Mose dɔ be, wonɖayɔ Datan kple Abiram, Eliab viwo ve; ke woɖo ŋu bena: Míegbɔna o.

english_verse: It's bad enough that you took us from our rich farmland in Egypt to let us die here in the desert. Now you also want to boss us around!
translation_verse: Mesɔ gbɔ na wò be, nekplɔ mí tso anyigba, si dzi notsi kple anyitsi bɔ ɖo la dzi, be nava wu le gbedzi oa? Azɔ nele amegã hã ɖu ge ɖe mía dzia?

english_verse: Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Don't listen to these men! I haven't done anything wrong to them. I haven't taken as much as a donkey.”
translation_verse: Tete dɔme ve Mose ŋutɔ, eye wògblɔ na Yehowa bena: Megatrɔ ɖe woƒe vɔsa la ŋu o! Nyemexɔ tedzi ɖeka hã le wo si o, eye nyemewɔ vɔ ɖe wo dometɔa ɖeke ŋu hã o.

english_verse: Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ na Korax bena: Mia kple wò ha blibo la miakpe ɖe Aron ŋu ava Yehowa ŋku me etsɔ.

english_verse: Each of you take along your fire pan with incense in it and offer the incense to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Amesiame natsɔ eƒe dzudzɔdosonu, eye woada dzudzɔdonu ɖe eme ava Yehowa ŋku me; dzudzɔdosonu alafa eve blaatɔ̃ wòanye, amesiame kple etɔ, eye mía kple Aron hã miatsɔ míaƒe dzudzɔdosonuwo vɛ.

english_verse: The next day the men placed incense and coals in their fire pans and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Tete amesiame tsɔ eƒe dzudzɔdosonu ɖe dzo ɖe eme, eye wotsɔ dzudzɔdonu da ɖe edzi heva Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la nu; Mose kple Aron hã le eme.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders. When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory
translation_verse: Eye Korax ƒo ha blibo la nu ƒu ɖe wo ŋu heva Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la nu. Tete Yehowa ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe ɖe eɖokui fia ha blibo la.

english_verse: and said to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose kple Aron bena:

english_verse: “Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
translation_verse: Mite ɖe aga le ha sia ŋu, ne matsrɔ̃ wo zi ɖeka. Korax ŋuti mewu yi to.

english_verse: But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
translation_verse: Ke woawo tsyɔ mo anyi hegblɔ bena: Oo, Mawu, si nye agbegbɔgbɔ, si le ŋutilãwo katã me la, ƒe Mawu! Esi ame ɖeka wɔ nuvɔ̃ la, eye nèle dɔmedzoe dom ɖe ha blibo la ŋua?

english_verse: The Lord answered Moses,
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: “Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
translation_verse: Gblɔ na ha la bena: Miɖe megbe le Korax, Datan kple Abiram ƒe aƒewo ŋu!

english_verse: Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed.
translation_verse: Eye Mose tso yi Datan kple Abiram gbɔ, eye Israel-ame tsitsiwo kplɔe ɖo.

english_verse: Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na ha la bena: Mite ɖa le ame mavɔ̃mawu siawo ƒe agbadɔwo gbɔ, eye migaka asi woƒe nua ɖeke ŋu, bena miawo hã míagatsrɔ̃ le woƒe nuvɔ̃wo ta o.

english_verse: Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know:
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ bena: Esia miatsɔ adze sii bena, Yehowae dɔm, be mawɔ dɔ siawo katã, eye menye nye ŋutɔ nye dzimee wotso o.

english_verse: But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ke ne Yehowa awɔ nu masekpɔa ɖe, eye anyigba ake nu ami wo kple woƒe nuwo katã, eye wòayi tsiẽ agbagbe la, ekema mianyae bena, ame siawoe do vlo Yehowa!

english_verse: As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up
translation_verse: Esi wowu nya siawo nu vɔ la, tete anyigba wo le wo te,

english_verse: and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
translation_verse: Ale woamawo kple woƒe nuwo katã yi tsiẽ agbagbe; anyigba tu ɖe wo nu, eye wobu le ha la dome.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
translation_verse: Eye Israel blibo la katã, amesiwo ɖe to ɖe wo la, si le woƒe ɣlidodo la ta; elabena wobu be, anyigba le yewo hã mi ge.

english_verse: Suddenly the Lord sent a fire that burned up the
translation_verse: Eye dzo tso Yehowa gbɔ fiã ŋutsu alafa eve blaatɔ̃, siwo tsɔ dzudzɔdonu ve la.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: Call together the twelve tribes of Israel and tell the leader of each tribe to write his name on the walking stick he carries as a symbol of his authority. Make sure Aaron's name is written on the one from the Levi tribe, then collect all the sticks.
translation_verse: Elabena nuvɔ̃wɔla mawo ƒe ku na dzudzɔdosonuawo ŋu kɔ, woaƒo wo gbadzaa atsɔ fa ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ŋu, elabena wotsɔ wo va Yehowa ŋku mee, eyata wo ŋu kɔ, eye woanye ŋkuɖodzinu na Israel-viwo.

english_verse: Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you.
translation_verse: Tete nunɔla Eleazar fɔ akɔbli-dzudzɔdosonu, siwo amesiwo dzo fiã tsɔ vɛ la, eye woƒo wo gbadzaa tsɔ fa ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ŋu,

english_verse: I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
translation_verse: hena ŋkuɖoɖodzi na Israel-viwo, bena ame tutɔa ɖeke, amesi metso Aron ƒe dzidzimeviwo dome o la, magate va, be yeatɔ dzo dzudzɔdonu le Yehowa ŋku me, eye wòava me nɛ abe Korax kple eƒe ha la ene o; abe alesi Yehowa de se nɛ to Mose dzi ene.

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Ke esi ŋu ke la, Israel ƒe ha blibo la lì Mose kple Aron ŋu gblɔ bena: Miawoe wu Yehowa ƒe dukɔ la.

english_verse: The next day when Moses went into the tent, flowers and almonds were already growing on Aaron's stick.
translation_verse: Eye esi Mose kple Aron wova Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la ŋgɔ la,

english_verse: and doomed if we even go near the sacred tent!”
translation_verse: Eye esi wotsi tre ɖe ame kukuawo kple agbagbeawo dome la, dɔvɔ̃ la nu tso.

english_verse: The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent.
translation_verse: Na nɔviwowo, amesiwo tso fofowò Lewi ƒe toa me la, nava kpli wò, eye woanɔ ŋuwò awɔ subɔsubɔdɔ, ne mia kple viwòŋutsuawo miele agbadɔ, si me sea le la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die.
translation_verse: Eye woawɔ dɔ, siwo katã le ŋuwo kple agbadɔ blibo la ŋu; ke womagate ɖe nu kɔkɔeawo kple vɔsamlekpui la ŋu, be mia kpli wo miagaku o.

english_verse: No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it.
translation_verse: Woanɔ ŋuwò awɔ dɔ, siwo katã le Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la ŋu, ke ame tutɔa ɖeke mate va mia gbɔ o.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: Eye miawo miawo do, siwo le kɔkɔeƒe la kple vɔsamlekpuia ŋuti, bena dɔmedzoe magava Israel-viwo dzi o.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Elabena nye ŋutɔe ɖe mia nɔvi Lewitɔwo, amesi wo wona Yehowa la, le Israel-viwo dome ma mi, bena woawɔ Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la ŋu dɔwo.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ke mia kple viwòwo miawo nunɔladɔ la le vɔsamlekpui la gbɔ kple xɔmetsovɔ la godo. Ɖe metsɔ nunɔladɔ la na mi: ke ne ame tutɔa ɖe te va la, woawui. Nunɔlawo ƒe nuɖuɖu.

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Gake woƒe lã nanye tɔwò, abe alesi akɔ, si wonyè kple ɖusita nye tɔwoe ene.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Teƒe kɔkɔetɔ naɖui le, ŋutsu sia ŋutsu kpɔ mɔ aɖui; nu kɔkɔe wòanye na wò. Metsɔ nunana bubu, siwo katã Israel-viwo ana,

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: bena woanyè la, na wò, wò ŋutɔ, viwòŋutsuwo kple viwònyɔnuwo tɔ woanye; amesiame, si ŋu ko le aƒewò me la kpɔ mɔ aɖui, ɖoɖo mavɔ wòanye.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: Metsɔ ami nyuitɔ, wein matsimatsi nyuitɔ kple agblemenu gbãtɔ, siwo woatsɔ vɛ na Yehowa la, na wò.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Woƒe anyigbadzinu gbãtɔwo katã dometɔ, siwo woatsɔ vɛ na Yehowa la, nye tɔwo; amesiame, si ŋu kɔ le aƒewò me la, kpɔ mɔ aɖui.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: Nusianu, si Israel-viwo tsɔ ɖe adzɔgbe ɖika la, nanye tɔwo!

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: Nusianu, si aʋu ɖɔ nu na dada, eɖanye ame alo lã o, eye wotsɔe na Yehowa la, nye tɔwò; ke woatsɔ ga axɔ amewo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo kple lã makɔmakɔwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeawoe.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Ne woxɔ ɣleti ɖeka la, ekema woatsɔ ga sekel kɔkɔe atɔ̃ axɔ wòe, abe alesi nado asi lae ene. Gera blave nanye sekel ɖeka.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: Ke womatsɔ ga axɔ nyiwo, alẽwo kple gbɔ̃wo ƒe ŋgɔgbeawoe o, elabena wo ŋu kɔ; nawu woƒe ʋu ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ŋu, eye natɔ dzo woƒe amiwo, bena woanye dzovɔsa, si aʋẽ lilili ɖe Yehowa.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: Metsɔ adzɔ, siwo katã woɖena le Israel-viwo ƒe nunana kɔkɔe, siwo wona Yehowa, ŋu la na mia kple viwòŋutsuwo kple viwònyɔnuwo; ɖoɖo mavɔ wòanye. Dzenubabla wònye le Yehowa ŋku me tegbee na mia kple wò dzidzimeviwo. Lewitɔwo ƒe nuɖuɖu.

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Aron bena: Naneke manye tɔwo le woƒe anyigba dzi o, eye makpɔ gomea ɖeka le wo dome o, elabena nyee nye wò gome kple wò domenyinu le Israel-viwo dome:

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Eye metsɔ nuwo katã ƒe ewoliawo ɖeka na Lewi-viwo, bena wòanye wo tɔ le Israel, ɖe woƒe ɖɔ, si wole wɔwɔm le Mawu ƒe agbadɔ ŋu la ta.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: boŋ Lewitɔwo nawɔ dɔ le Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la ŋu, eye woaxɔ woƒe vodadawo atsɔ; ɖoɖo mavɔ wòanye na miaƒe dzidzimeviwo. Ke domenyinu manɔ wo si le Israel-viwo dome o,

english_verse: they will be given the crops and newborn animals that the Israelites offer to me. What the Levites Must Give
translation_verse: elabena metsɔ Israel-viwo ƒe nuwo ƒe ewoliawo ɖeka, siwo wotsɔ na Yehowa la, na Lewitɔwo abe domenyinu ene; eyata megblɔ na wo be, domenyinu manɔ wo si le Israel-viwo dome o.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na Lewitɔwo be: Ne miexɔ nuwo ƒe ewoliawo ɖeka, si mexɔ le Israel-viwo si na mi, be wòanye miaƒe domenyinu le wo si la, ekema miɖe ewoliawo ɖeka le eŋu na Yehowa

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Wòabu adzɔ, si miana la, abe mia ŋutɔwoe xa agblemenu, eye mieha wein ene.

english_verse: so the best of what you receive will be mine.
translation_verse: Miɖe nusiwo katã woana mi la, ƒe nyuitɔwo wɔ adzɔ na Yehowa abe nunana kɔkɔe ene.

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na wo be: Ne mieɖe nyuitɔwo na adzoe la, ekema woabui na Lewitɔwo abe woawo ŋutɔe xa nu, eye wòfiã wein ene.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mia kple miaƒe ƒometɔwo miekpɔ mɔ aɖui le afisiafi, elabena dɔ, si wɔm miele le Mawu ƒe agbadɔ ŋu la, ƒe fetu wònye.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Ne miede nyuitɔ le wo ŋu na adzɔe la, ekema nuvɔ̃ manɔ mia dzi o; miagblẽ kɔ ɖo na Israel-viwo ƒe nunana kɔkɔewo o, eye miaku o.

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa de se gblɔ enye si: Gblɔ na Israel-viwo be, wòalé nyinɔ dzẽ, si sɔ blibo, nu mewɔ afia ɖeke nɛ o, eye womede kɔkuti kɔ nɛ kpɔ o la, vɛ na wò.

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: Miatsɔe na nunɔla Eleazar, eye wòana woakplɔe ayi asaɖa la godo, eye woawui le eŋku me.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Eye nunɔla Eleazar nade eƒe asi nu la me ahlẽ zi adre ɖe go, si me Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la dze ŋgɔe.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: Eye woatɔ dzo nyinɔ la ƒe agbalẽ, eƒe lã, eƒe ʋu kple dɔmemiwo.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Eye nunɔla natsɔ sederti, isop kple ka dze ade nyinɔ ƒe dzo la me.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Nunɔla nanyã eƒe avɔwo, eye wòale tsi, emegbe hafi wòkpɔ mɔ ava asaɖa la me: gake nunɔla ŋu mekɔ o vaseɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Amesi tɔ dzo nyinɔa la, nanyã eƒe avɔwo, eye wòale tsi, eye eŋu mekɔ o vaseɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsu, si gu ka la, nalɔ nyinɔ ƒe afi la ada ɖe teƒe kɔkɔea ɖe le asaɖa godo, eye wòadzrae ɖo na Israel-viwo ƒe ha la hena ameŋukɔtsi la, nuvɔ̃vɔsae wònye.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Amesi la nyinɔ ƒe afia la, nanyã eƒe avɔwo, eye eŋu mekɔ o vaseɖe fiẽ. Ɖoɖo mavɔ wòanye na Israel-viwo kple amedzro, si le wo dome la.

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe de asi ame kuku ŋu la, eŋu mekɔ o ŋkeke adre.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: Eye wòatsɔe aɖe nuvɔ̃ ɖa le eɖokui ŋu le ŋkeke etɔ̃lia kple ŋkeke adrelia dzi, ekema eŋu ko; gake ne meɖe nuvɔ̃ ɖa le eɖokui ŋu le ŋkeke etɔ̃lia kple ŋkeke adrelia dzi o la, ekema eŋu meka o.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe ɖe asi ame kuku ŋu, eye meɖe nuvɔ̃ ɖa le eɖokui ŋu o la, ekema edo ŋunyɔ Yehowa ƒe nɔƒe la; ele be, woatsrɔ̃ ame sia ɖa le Israel, elabena womewu ameŋukɔtsi la ɖe eŋu o, eyata eŋu mekɔ o, eye eya ŋutɔ de busu eɖokui ŋu.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: Se la enye si: Ne ame ku le agbadɔa ɖe me la, ekema amesi va agbadɔa me kple nusiwo katã le agbadɔa me la, ŋu mekɔ o ŋkeke adre.

english_verse: Any open jar in the tent is unclean.
translation_verse: Nusianu, si le nuvo, eye wometu nu enu o la, ŋu mekɔ o.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe de asi amesi wowu kple yi alo ame kuku, ameƒu alo yɔdo ŋu le gbe me la, eŋu mekɔ o ŋkeke adre.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsu, si ŋu kɔ la, natsɔ isop ade tsi la me awu ɖe agbadɔ la, eme nuwo katã kple amesiwo katã de afima la ŋu; alea woawui ɖe amesi de asi ameƒu alo amesi wowu, ame kuku alo yɔdo ŋu la hã ŋui.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Amesi ŋu kɔ la, nawui ɖe amesi ŋu mekɔ o la ŋu le ŋkeke etɔ̃lia kple ŋkeke adrelia dzi, emegbe wòanyã eƒe avɔwo, eye wòalé tsi, ekema eŋu kɔ le fiẽ.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ke ne amea ɖe ŋu mekɔ o, eye womeɖe nuvɔ̃ le eŋu o la, ekema woatsrɔ̃e ɖa le ha la dome, elabena edo ŋunye Yehowa ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la; womewu ameŋukɔtsi ɖe eŋu o, eyata eŋu mekɔ o.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Ɖoɖo mavɔ wòanye na mi. Amesi wu ameŋukɔtsia la, nanyã eƒe avɔwo, eye ne amea ɖe de asi ameŋukɔtsia ŋu la, eŋu mekɔ o vaseɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Ne amesi ŋu mekɔ o, de asi nua ɖe ŋu la, eŋu mekɔ o, eye ne amea ɖe ɖe asi amea ŋu la, eŋu mekɔ o vaseɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti gbãtɔ me la Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la va Zin-gbedzi, eye dukɔ la ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Kades. Miryam ku le afima, eye woɖii ɖe afima.

english_verse: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Ke tsi mele afima na ha la o. Tete wokpe ta ɖe Mose kple Aron ŋu.

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Eye dukɔ la wɔ dzre kple Mose bena: Oo, ɖe miawo hã míeku, esi mia nɔviwo ku le Yehowa ŋku me boŋ la, ne nyo wu!

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Nukata gɔ̃ miekplɔ Yehowa ƒe ha la va gbe sia dzi, bena mia kple míaƒe lãwo miaku ɖe afisia?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti miekplɔ mí tso Egipte va teƒe baɖa sia, afisi womate ŋu aƒa nu ɖo o, eye gbotiwo, weinkawo kple yevuboɖatiwo mele o, eye tsi hã mele, be woano o.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Ke Mose kple Aron dzo le ha la gbɔ yi ɖe Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la nu, eye wotsyɔ mo anyi; tete Yehowa ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe ɖe eɖokui fia wo.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: Tsɔ wò atikplɔ, eye mia kple nɔviwò Aron miaƒo ha la nu ƒu, eye naƒo nu kple agakpe la le woƒe ŋku me, ekema ana tsi. Ale nana tsi nado le agakpe la me, bena ha la kple woƒe lãwo nano.

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Tete Mose tso atikplɔ la le Yehowa ŋku me, abe alesi wòde se nɛ ene.

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: Eye Mose kple Aron ƒo ha la nu ƒu ɖe agakpe la ŋgɔ, eye wògblɔ na wo bena: Misee, mi tosẽlawo! Ɖe míate ŋu ana tsi naɖo tso agakpe sia mena mia?

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Eye Mose ko eƒe asi dzi tsɔ eƒe atikplɔ ƒo agakpe la zi eve, tete tsi do bababa, eye ha la kple woƒe lãwo no.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ na Mose kple Aron bena: Esi mieɖo ŋu ɖe ŋunye o, eye miekɔ ŋunye le Israel-viwo ŋku me o ŋuti la, eyata makplɔ ha sia aɖe anyigba, si matso na wo la dzi o.

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Esia nye dzrewɔtsi, si ta Israel-viwo wo dzre kple Yehowa ɖo, eye wòna eɖokui ŋu kɔ le wo dome la.

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Eye Mose dɔ dɔlawo le Kades ɖo ɖe Edom-fia gbã bena: Ale nɔviwò Israel gblɔ esi: Wò ŋutɔ ènya fu, siwo katã dzo ɖe mia dzi.

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: Mía fofowo ʋu va Egipte, eye míenɔ Egipte eteƒe didi; ke Egiptetɔwo sẽ ŋuta le mía kple mía fofowo ŋu.

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: Eye mieɖo ɣli na Yehowa, eye wose míaƒe gbe hedɔ mawudɔlaa ɖe ɖa wòkplɔ mi tso Egipte; azɔ miele Kades, du, si le wò liƒo ŋu la me.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Na míato wò anyigba dzi ayi! Miele agble alo weinbɔwo me to ge o, eye míele vudo me tsi hã no ge o, negbe mɔ gã dzi ko míato, eye míadze ɖe ɖusi alo mia me o, vaseɖe esime míato wò anyigba dzi ayi.

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Edom ɖo ŋu bena: Mato gbɔnye avi o, ne menye nenem o la, mava kpe mi kple yi.

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Tete Israel-viwo gblɔ nɛ bena: Dumɔ gã dzi ko miehe, míato ayi, eye ne mia kple miaƒe lãwo mieno wò tsi la, ekema míaxe fe ɖe eta. Afɔ pɛ ko miehe, míatsɔ azɔ edzi ayi, eye miele naneke dim wu esia o.

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Ke eɖo ŋu be: Mèle eme tso ge ayi o! Eye Edom tsɔ aʋakɔ gã, si sesẽ la, yi ɖakpee.

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Esi Edom gbe be: Israel mato yeƒe anyigba dzi: ayi o la, eyata Israel godo mo to eŋu. Aron ƒe ku.

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Eye Israel ƒe ha blibo la ho tso Kades heva Hor-to la gbɔ.

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: Aron nayi tɔgbuiawo gbɔ; elabena mele anyigba, si matsɔ na Israel-viwo la, dzi de ge o, le esi miesẽ to ɖe nye sea ŋu le dzrewɔtsia gbo la ta.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Kplɔ Aron kple viaŋutsu Eleazar yi Hor-to la dzi,

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: eye naɖe awuawo le Aron ŋu ado na viaŋutsu Eleazar; ke Aron naku le afima.

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Mose wo, abe alesi Yehowa de se nɛ ene. Eye wolia Hor-to la le ha blibo la ŋku me.

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: Eye Mose ɖe awuawo le Aron ŋu heɖo na viaŋutsu Eleazar. Eye Aron ku le to la tame, eye Mose kple Eleazar ɖi tso to la dzi

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Eye esi ha blibo la kpo bena, Aron megali o la, Israel ƒe aƒe blibo la fa Aron ŋkeke blaetɔ̃ sɔŋ.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Eye woho tso Hor-to la gbɔ heɖo ta Avaƒu la nu, bena woatrɔ Edom-nyigba ta. Ke dukɔ la tsi dzi le mɔ ta,

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: eye dukɔ la ƒo nu le Mawu kple Mose ŋu bena: Nukata miekplɔ mí tso Egipte, be míaku le gbedzi? Elabena abolo kple tsia ɖeke mele afisia o, eye nuɖuɖu vlo sia le ŋu nyɔm na mí.

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ɖo da vɔ̃ɖiwo ɖe dukɔ la dome, eye woɖu dukɔ la, eye ame geɖe ku le Israel.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la va Mose gbɔ gblɔ bena: Míewɔ nuvɔ̃ be, mieƒo nu le mia kple Yehowa ŋu. Ɖe kuku na Yehowa, bena wòaɖe dawo ɖa le mía dome. Eye Mose ɖe kuku ɖe dukɔ la ta.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Wɔ da vɔ̃ɖi la ƒe nɔnɔme, eye nakui ɖe ati ŋu, bena ne ɖa du amea ɖe, eye wòkpɔe ɖa la, wòatsi agbe.

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Eye Mose tsa akɔbli wɔ ɖaa ɖe heku ɖe ati ŋu, eye ne dawo ɖu amea ɖe wokpe akɔblida la ɖa ko la, etsia agbe. Israel-viwo ƒe asaɖabɔƒewo.

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ho heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Obot.

english_verse: and then in the Zered Gorge.
translation_verse: Woho tso afima heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Zered-tɔʋu la nu.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Eye woho tso afima heva gbedzi le Arnon, si dzɔ tso Amoritɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi la nu. Arnon enye liƒo le Moabitɔwo kple Amoritɔwo dome.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Eyata woŋlɔ ɖe Yehowa ƒe aʋawɔwɔwo ƒe agbalẽ me bena: „Waheb le Sufa kple Arnon-toʋu la,

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: tɔʋu la me tsi, si si ɖo ta Ar-nutowo me, eye wòɖo liƒo na Moab.“

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Emegbe wotso le afima va vudo la gbɔ. Esia nye vudo, si ŋu Yehowa gblɔ le na Mose be: Ƒo dukɔ la nu ƒu, bena mana tsi wo.

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi Israel-viwo dzi ha sia bena: „Vudo, dzi! Midzi ha ɖe eŋu!

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Esia nye vudo, si amegãwo ɖe, eye dukɔ la ƒe bubumewo tsɔ woƒe atikplɔ kple woƒe atizɔti ɖee la.“ Eye wotso gbe sia dzi heva Matana.

english_verse: then at Nahaliel, and then at Bamoth.
translation_verse: Tso Matana wova Naxaliel, eye tso Naxaliel wova Bamot.

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Tso Bamot wova bali la me le Moab-nyigba dzi, le Pisga, si dze ŋgɔ gbegbe la gbɔ. Woɖu Sixon dzi.

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: Elabena Xesbon enye Amoritɔwo ƒe fia Sixon ƒe du; eya nye amesi wɔ ana kple Moab-fia tsãtɔ, eye wòxɔ eƒe anyigba katã le esi vaseɖe Arnon nu.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Eye Israel dɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Sixon, Amori-fia gbɔ bena:

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: Na mato wò anyigba dzi yi! Miadze ato agblewo alo weinbɔwo me o, eye miele vudo me tsi hã no ge o, boŋ mɔ gã ko míalé tẽ, vaseɖe esime miatso wò anyigba me ayi.

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Ke Sixon meɖe mɔ na Israel be, wòato eƒe anyigba dzi ayi o; boŋ Sixon ƒo eƒe dukɔ blibo la nu ƒu, eye woho va kpe Israel le gbedzi. Esi wòɖo Yaza ta, ewɔ aʋa kple Israel.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Ke Israel wu wo kple yi, eye wòxɔ woƒe anyigba la tso Arnon gbɔ vaseɖe Yabok nu heva ke ɖe Amon-viwo ŋu, elabena Yaezer enye Amon-viwo ƒe liƒo.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Eye Israel xɔ du siawo katã, eye Israel nɔ Amoritɔwo ƒe du Xesbon kple eŋu duwo katã me.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Eyata ahamasilawo gblɔna be: Miva Xesbon, eye mitu Sixon ƒe du la sesĩe!

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Elabena dzo do tso Xesbon, eye dzoƒaɖe tso Sixon ƒe du la me hefiã Moabitɔwo ƒe Ar kpakple Arnon-ŋu nɔlawo.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Baba na wo, Moab! Wo, Kemos-dukɔ, ebu! Ena viaŋutsuwo si, eye wona Amoritɔwo ƒe fia Sixon ɖe aboyo vianyɔnuwo.
