english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: Míeda wo, eye Xesbon bu vaseɖe Dibon. Mietsrɔ̃ wo vaseɖe Nofa, eye dzo la bi vaseɖe Medeba.

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Ale Israel-viwo nɔ Amoritɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi. Woɖu Og dzi.

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Eye Mose da be, woaɖatsa ŋku le Yaezer, eye woxɔ eŋu duwo, eye woɖu Amoritɔ, siwo le afima la dzi.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Emegbe wotrɔ dze Basan-mɔ dzi. Tete Og, Basan-fia, kple eƒe dukɔ blibo la ho aʋa va kpe wo le Edrei.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Megavɔ̃e o, elabena metsɔ eya ŋutɔ kple eƒe dukɔ blibo la kpakple eƒe anyigba de asi na wò, eye nawɔe, abe alesi nèwɔ Sixon, Amoritɔwo ƒe fia, si nɔ Xesbon la ene.

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Eye wowu eya ŋutɔ kple viaŋutsuwo kpakple eƒe dukɔ blibo la, ale bena amea ɖeke metsi agbe ahayi sisi ge o.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ho heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Moab-tagba, le Yordan godo le Yerixo kasa.

english_verse: When King Balak of Moab and his people heard how many Israelites there were and what they had done to the Amorites, he and the Moabites were terrified and panicked.
translation_verse: vɔvɔ̃ le Moab ŋutɔ le dukɔ la ŋu, elabena esɔ gbɔ akpa, eye dzidzi ƒo Moab le Israel-viwo ŋu.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Eye Moab gblɔ na Midian-ame tsitsiwo bena: Ameha, si ɖe to ɖe mí la, le mía ɖu ge, abe alesi nyi ɖua gbe le gbe mee ene. Balak, Zipor vi, enye Moab-fia le ɣemaɣi me.

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: Eye wòdɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Bileam, Beor vi gbɔ, le Petor le tɔsisi la nu le edetɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, bena woayɔe vɛ hegblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, dukɔa ɖe nye si ʋu tso Egipte, eye wònyẽ tsyɔ anyigba ŋku me, eye wòƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe mia kasa.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Eyata va naƒo fi ade dukɔ sia nam, elabena ekpe dzinye! Ɖewohi mate ŋu aɖu edzi, eye manyãe ɖa le anyigba la dzi. Elabena menyae bena, amesi neyra la, eya ŋu yayra nɔna, eye amesi ne ƒo fi de la, eya ŋu fiƒode nɔna.

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Esi Moab-ame tsitsiwo kple Midian-ame tsitsiwo xɔ afãkaho la, wodze mɔ, eye wova Bileam gbɔ hegblɔ Balak ƒe nyawo nɛ.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu na wo bena: Mitsi afisia dɔ, emegbe magblɔ, alesi Yehowa ato nam la na mi. Eye Moab-amegãwo tsi Bileam gbɔ.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Eye Mawu va Bileam gbɔ gblɔ bena: Ŋutsu kawo nye siawo le gbɔwò?

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Bileam ɖo ŋu na Mawu bena: Balak, Zipor vi, Moab-fiae, dɔ ame ɖe gbɔnye bena:

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, dukɔa ɖe ʋu tso Egipte, eye wònyẽ tsyɔ anyigba ŋku me, eyata va naƒo fi aɖee nam. Ɖewohi mate ŋu awɔ aʋa kplii, eye manyãe ɖa.

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Tete Mawu gblɔ na Bileam bena: Megayi kpli wo o, eye megaƒo fi ɖe dukɔ la o, elabena woyrae xoxo!

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Eye esi Bileam fɔ ŋdi la, egblɔ na Balak ŋu megãwo bena: Migbugbɔ yi mia ɖe, elabena Yehowa gbe be, nyemagayi kpli mi o.

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Eye Moab-amegãwo dze mɔ va Balak gbɔ gblɔ bena: Bileam gbe be, yemayi kpli mí o.

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Ke Balak gadɔ amegã geɖewo, amesiwo ŋu bubu le wu gbãtɔwo la ɖa.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Eye wova Bileam gbɔ hegblɔ nɛ bena: Ale Balak, Zipor vi, gblɔ esi: Megana woaxe mɔ na wò be, magava gbɔnye o.

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: Elabena made bubu ŋuwò ŋutɔ, eye nusianu, si nagblɔ nam la, mawɔe. Eyata va naƒo fi ade dukɔ sia nam dzro!

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Bileam ɖo ŋu, eye wògblɔ na Balak ƒe dɔlawo bena: Ne Balak atsɔ klosalo kple sika xɔ taŋ nam hã la, nyemate ŋu aɖa Yehowa, nye Mawu, ƒe se dzi ahayi nu sue alo nu gãa ɖeke wɔ ge o.

english_verse: That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
translation_verse: Eye Mawu va Bileam gbɔ le zã me gblɔ nɛ bena: Nenye yɔ wò ge ŋutsu siawo va la, ekema fɔ, ne nayi kpli wo; gake alesi magblɔ nawò la, nenema ko nawɔ. Bileam ƒe tedzinɔ ƒo nu.

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Tete Bileam fɔ ŋdi, bia akpa na eƒe tedzinɔ, eye wòyi kple Moab-amegãwo.

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Ke esi wòyi la, Mawu do dɔmedzoe, eye Yehowa ƒe dɔla va tso mɔ nɛ, bena woatsi tre ɖe eŋu. Eya ŋutɔ do tedzinɔ, eye eƒe subɔla eve kpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Eye tedzinɔ la kpɔ alesi Yehowa ƒe ɖɔla tsi tre ɖe mɔ dzi di yi ɖe asii, eyata wòdze le mɔ dzi ɖe gbe me. Ke Bileam ƒo tedzi la, be wòagatrɔe va mɔ dzi.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Emegbe Yehowa ƒe dɔla va tsi tre ɖe weinbɔwo ƒe kpɔdomee mɔ, si ƒe akpawo kple eve gli le la dzi.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Esi tedzinɔa kpɔ Yehowa ƒe dɔla la, edze ɖe gli ŋu, eye wòmimi Bileam ƒe afɔ ɖe gli ŋu; eyata wògaƒoe ke.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe ɖɔla la gayi ŋgɔ va tsi tre ɖe teƒe xaxɛa ɖe, afisi mɔa ɖeke mele be, wòadze ɖe ɖusi alo mia me o.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Esi tedzinɔ la kpɔ Yehowa ƒe dɔlaa la, etsyɔ akɔ anyi ɖe Bileam te. Tete Bileam do dɔmedzoe, eye wòƒo tedzinɔ la kple ati.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ʋu nu na tedzinɔ la wògblɔ na Bileam bena. Nuka mewo wò, hafi nèƒom zi etɔ̃ sɔŋ?

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Bileam ɖo ŋu na tedzinɔ la bena: Esi nedo tsukunɔm ta! Ɖe wònye yie le asinye la, ne mewu wò gɔ̃!

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Tedzinɔ la gblɔ na Bileam bena: Menye nyee nye wò tedzinɔ, si nèdo le wò agbe me ŋkekewo katã me va do egbee oa? Alo mewɔ ale nu ɖe ŋuwò kpɔa? Eɖo ŋu be: Kpao!

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ʋu Bileam ƒe ŋkuwo wòkpɔ, alesi Yehowa ƒe dɔla tsi tre ɖe mɔ dzi ɖi yi ɖe asi. Tete wòde ta agu hetsyɔ mo anyi.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe dɔla gblɔ ne bena: Nukaŋuti nèƒo wò tedzinɔ la zi etɔ̃ sɔŋ? Evɔ wònye nyee tsi tre ɖe ŋuwò hafi; elabena afɔ, si dzi nèle la, evlo le ŋkunye me.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Tedzinɔ la kpɔm, eyata wòdze ɖe aga le ŋkunye me zi etɔ̃ sɔŋ. Ɖe menye eyae dze ɖe aga o la, anye ne mewu wò kokoko ahagblẽ eya ɖe agbe.

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Bileam ɖo ŋu na Yehowa ƒe ɖɔla la bena: Mewɔ nuvɔ̃, elabena nyemenyae be, wòe tsi tre ɖe ŋunye le mɔ dzi o. Eyata ne medze ŋuwò o la, ekema magbugbɔ.

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe dɔla la gblɔ na Bileam bena: Yi kple ŋutsuawo; gake nya, si mato na wò la, eya ko nagblɔ! Ale Bileam yi kple Balak-ŋu megãwo.

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Esi Balak se bena, Bileam gbɔna la, eyi ɖakpee le Ir-Moab, du, si le Arnon nu le liƒo dzi kekeake la me.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: Eye Balak gblɔ na Bileam bena: Ɖe nyemedɔ ame ɖa, be woayɔ wò ve oa? Nukaŋuti metso hiã va gbɔnye oa? Ɖe nèsusu be, nyemate ŋu ade bubu ŋuwò oa?

english_verse: “I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
translation_verse: Bileam ɖo ŋu na Balak bena: Menya va gbɔwò la hafi, gake ɖe mate ŋu agblɔ nyaa ɖea? Negbe nya, si Mawu aɖe nunye la, eya ko magblɔ.

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Eye Bileam yi kple Balak, eye wova Kiryat-Xuzot.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Eye Balak wu nyiwo kple alẽwo sa vɔe, eye wòɖo ɖe ɖe Bileam kple amegã, siwo le egbɔ.

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, Balak kplɔ Bileam yi Bamot-Baal, afisi wòkpɔ dukɔ la ƒe mlɔenu le.

english_verse: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Eye Bileam gblɔ na Balak bena: Na woaɖi vɔsamlekpui adre ɖe afisia nam, eye woakplɔ nyitsu adre kple agbo adre vɛ nam.

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Eye Balak wɔ, abe alesi Bileam gblɔ ene, eye Balak kple Bileam tso nyitsu ɖekaɖeka kple agbo ɖekaɖeka sa vɔ le vɔsamlekpuia ɖesiaɖe dzi.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
translation_verse: Emegbe Bileam gblɔ na Balak bena: Va tsi tre ɖe wò numevɔsa gbɔ, eye maɖe kpo; ɖewohĩ Yehowa aɖe eɖokui afiam, eye nusi wòna mekpɔ la, eya magblɔ na wò. Eye wòyi togbɛ ƒeƒlea ɖe dzi.

english_verse: When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
translation_verse: Tete Mawu ɖe eɖokui tia Bileam, eye eya gblɔ bena: Meɖi vɔsamlekpui adre, eve metsɔ nyitsu ɖekaɖeka kple agbo ɖekaɖeka sa vɔ le vɔsamlekpuia ɖesiaɖe dzi.

english_verse: The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa de nya nu na Bileam, eye wogblɔ bena: Gbugbɔ yi Balak gbɔ, eye alea naƒo nui!

english_verse: When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
translation_verse: Tete wogbugbɔ va egbɔ, eye kpo ɖa, eya kple Moab-amegãwo le tsitre ɖe eƒe numevɔsa la gbɔ.

english_verse: Balaam said: “King Balak of Moab brought me from the hills of Syria to curse Israel and announce its doom.
translation_verse: Eye wòdo eƒe numegbe la hegblɔ bena: Balak kplɔm tso Aram, ɣedzeƒetɔwo dzi Moab-fia kplɔm tsoe be: Va naƒo fi de Yakob nam, eye va nado ɖiŋu na Israel nam!

english_verse: But I can't go against God! He did not curse or condemn Israel. *
translation_verse: Aleke maƒo fi de amesi Mawu meƒo fi de o, eye mado ɖiŋu na amesi Yehowa medo ɖiŋu na o?

english_verse: “From the mountain peaks, I look down and see Israel, the obedient people of God.
translation_verse: Agakpewo tame mele kpɔ wo ɖa, eye togbɛwo dzi mele kpɔ wo. Kpɔ ɖa, dukɔ la ɖe ɖe aga, eye mebua eɖokui ɖe dukɔ bu bu wo do me o.

english_verse: They are living alone in peace. And though they are many, they don't bother the other nations. “I hope to obey God for as long as I live and to die in such peace.”
translation_verse: Ameka ate ŋu axlẽ Yakob ƒe ke, eye ameka axlẽ Israel ƒe akpa enelia? Maku abe ame dzɔdzɔewo ene, eye nye nuwuwu nanɔ abe wo tɔ ene!

english_verse: Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
translation_verse: Tete Balak gblɔ na Bileam bena: Nuka nye esia nèwɔ ɖe ŋunye? Meyɔ wo vɛ, be naƒo fi ade nye futɔwo nam loo, ɖeko nètsɔ wo yra!

english_verse: Balaam answered, “I can say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Second Message
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu gblɔ be: Ɖe mele nam be, magblɔ nya, si Yehowa de nunye la pɛpɛpɛ oa?

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.”
translation_verse: Eye Balak gblɔ nɛ bena: Va miyi teƒe bubu, afisi nakpɔ wo le, ke mèle wo kpɔ ge blibo o, negbe woƒe mlɔenu ko nakpɔ; afima naƒo fi ade wo nam le.

english_verse: So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
translation_verse: Eye wòkplɔe yi ɖe Pisga-to tame, afisi gbetasrãlawo nɔna, eye wòɖi vɔsamlekpui adre hetsɔ nyitsu ɖekaɖeka kple agbo ɖekaɖeka sa vo le vɔsamlekpuia ɖesiaɖe dzi.

english_verse: “Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ na Balak bena: Tsi tre ɖe wo numevɔsa gbɔ afi, eye mayi aɖado go ame le afime.

english_verse: The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ɖe eɖokui fia Bileam, eye wòde nya enu, eye wògblɔ bena: Gbugbɔ yi Balak gbɔ, eye alea naƒo nu.

english_verse: Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings. Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
translation_verse: Esi wòva egbɔ la, kpo ɖa, ele tsitre ɖe eƒe numevɔsa la gbɔ, eye Moab-amegãwo le egbɔ. Eye Balak gblɔ nɛ bena: Aleke Yehowa gblɔ?

english_verse: God is no mere human! He doesn't tell lies or change his mind. God always keeps his promises.
translation_verse: Mawu menye amegbetɔ wonye, ne wòaka aʋatso o eye menye amegbetɔwo ƒe vi wònye, ne wòatrɔ nya o. Ɖe woagblɔ nya, eye mawo edzi oa? Ɖe woaƒo nu, eye mawɔe oa?

english_verse: “My command from God was to bless these people, and there's nothing I can do to change what he has done.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa yayra mexɔ vɛ: eye ne eya yra la, nyea nyemate ŋu atrɔe o.

english_verse: Israel's king is the Lord God. He lives there with them and intends them no harm.
translation_verse: Womekpɔ dzɔgbevɔ̃e le Yakob ŋu o, eye womekpɔ fuwɔamea ɖeke le Israel ŋu o. Yehowa, eƒe Mawu la, li kplii, eye ayibopɛ le ɖiɖim le wo dome.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led Israel out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Mawu, si kplɔe tso Egipte la, le nɛ abe to ƒe dzo ene.

english_verse: No magic charms can work against them— just look what God has done for his people.
translation_verse: Dzo mate Yakob ŋu o, eye afã aŋe vo ɖe Israel ŋu. Azɔ ko woagblɔ le Yakob kple Israel ŋu be: Nu gã ka nye esi Yehowa wɔa?

english_verse: They are like angry lions ready to attack; and they won't rest until their victim is gobbled up.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, dukɔ la tso abe dzatanɔ ene, eye wòto abe dzatatsu ene. Mele akɔ tsyɔ ge anyi o, negbe ɖeko wòaɖu eƒe nuléle, eye wòano amesiwo wowu ƒe ʋu hafi.

english_verse: Balak shouted, “If you're not going to curse Israel, then at least don't bless them.”
translation_verse: Tete Balak gblɔ na Bileam bena: Megaƒo fi de wo o, eye megayra wo hã o!

english_verse: “I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Third Message
translation_verse: Bileam ɖo ŋu, eye wògblɔ na Balak bena: Nyemegblɔ na wò be: Nya sia nya, si Yehowa agblɔ la, eya mawɔ oa?

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.”
translation_verse: Emegbe Balak gblɔ na Bileam bena: Va, makplɔ wò yi teƒe bubu, ɖewohĩ adze Mawu ŋu, bena naƒo fi ade wo nam tso afima.

english_verse: So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Eye Balak kplɔ Bileam yi Peor-to, si dze ŋgɔ gbegbe la tame.

english_verse: Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Eye Bileam gblɔ na Balak bena: Ɖi vɔsamlekpui adre ɖe afisia nam, eye nakplɔ nyitsu adre kple agbo adre vɛ nam.

english_verse: After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Balak wɔ, abe alesi Bileam gblɔ ene, eye wòtsɔ nyitsu ɖekaɖeka kple agbo ɖekaɖeka sa vɔ le vɔsamlekpuia ɖesiaɖe dzi.

english_verse: Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
translation_verse: Esi Bileam kpo bena, edze Yehowa ŋu be, wòayra Israel la, megayi afã ka ge abe tsã ene o, boŋ etrɔ mo ɖe gbedzi gome.

english_verse: and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him,
translation_verse: Eye Bileam fɔ kɔ dzi, kpɔ alesi Israel ƒu asaɖa anyi tototoe. Tete Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ va edzi,

english_verse: and Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: eye wòdo eƒe numegbe la hegblɔ bena: Ale Bileam, Beor vi, gblɔ esi, eye ale ŋutsu, si ƒe ŋku ʋu la, gblɔ esi:

english_verse: It comes from the Lord, the God All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Amesi sea Mawu ƒe nyawo, ƒe gbe enye si, amesi ŋusẽkatãtɔ ɖea nuwo fiana, amesi tsyɔ mo anyi, ke eƒe ŋkuwo le te:

english_verse: “People of Israel, your camp is lovely.
translation_verse: Oo, Yakob, wò agbadɔwo dze ani loo! Israel, wò nɔƒewo nyo loo!

english_verse: It's like a grove of palm trees or a garden beside a river. You are like tall aloe trees that the Lord has planted, or like cedars growing near water.
translation_verse: Ele abe alesi tɔʋu mlo ɖe nu le bali me ene; eye wòɖi aba le tɔsisi to, ele abe aloeti, siwo Yehowa do ene, eye wòɖi seder le to to.

english_verse: You and your descendants will prosper like an orchard beside a stream. Your king will rule with power and be a greater king than Agag the Amalekite.
translation_verse: Tsi gbagba eƒe tɔkpowo, eye wòƒã nu ɖe tɔ geɖewo to. Eƒe fia xɔ ŋkɔ wu Agag, eye eƒe fiaɖuƒe keke ɖe nu.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led you out of Egypt. You will defeat your enemies, shooting them with arrows and crushing their bones.
translation_verse: Mawu, si kplɔe tso Egipte la, le nɛ abe to ƒe dzowo ene; aɖu dukɔ, siwo nye eƒe futɔwo, eye woagbã woƒe ƒuwo, eye wòatsɔ eƒe da atsrɔ̃ wo.

english_verse: Like a lion you lie down, resting after an attack. Who would dare disturb you? “Anyone who blesses you will be blessed; anyone who curses you will be cursed.”
translation_verse: Etsyɔ akɔ anyi abe dzatatsu kple dzatanɔ ene, ameka le eʋuʋu ge? Ne amea ɖe yra wò la, woayrae; eye ne amea ɖe ƒo fi de wò la, woaƒo fi aɖee. Ɣletivi tso Yakob.

english_verse: When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
translation_verse: Tete Balak do dɔmedzoe ɖe Bileam ŋu, eye Balak si akpe hegblɔ na Bileam bena: Meyɔ wò vɛ, bena naƒo fi ade nye futɔwo nam loa, ɖeko nètsɔ wo yra zi etɔ sɔŋ.

english_verse: Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
translation_verse: Eyata netsɔ nayi mia de! Ɖe mebe, made bubu ŋuwò pete hafi, gake Yehowa te bubu la wò.

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: Ne Balak atsɔ klosalo kple sika xɔ taŋ nam hã la, nyemate ŋu ada Yehowa ƒe se la dzi awɔ nyui alo vɔ̃ le ɖokuinye si o, negbe nya, si Yehowa alo la, eya ko magblɔ oa?

english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: Azɔ mele mía detɔwo gbɔ yi ge; eyata magblɔ nusi dukɔ sia le wò dukɔ wɔ ge le ɣeyiɣi, siwo gbɔna me la, fia wò.

english_verse: Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Eye wòdo eƒe numegbe la gblɔ bena: Ale Bileam, Beor vi, gblɔ esi, ale ŋutsu, si ƒe ŋku ʋu la, gblɔ esi.

english_verse: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the Lord All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Amesi sea Mawu ƒe nyawo la, ƒe gbe enye si, amesi dzea si dziƒoʋitɔ ƒe susuwo, amesi ŋusẽkatãtɔ ɖea nuwo fiana, amesi tsyɔ mo anyi, ke eƒe ŋkuwo le te.

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.
translation_verse: Mele ekpɔm, gake menye fifiae o; mekpɔnɛ, gake mele kpuiƒe o. Ɣletivi ado tso Yakob me, eye fiatikplɔ ado tso Israel me; aŋe tonuƒuiwo na Moab, eye wòakaka la le amesiwo nye zi la nu.

english_verse: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
translation_verse: Woaxɔ Edom ƒe anyigba, eye woaxɔ eƒe futɔ Seir hã ƒe anyigba; ke Israel ya akpɔ ŋusẽ.

english_verse: The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.
translation_verse: Ame atso Yakob me aɖu dzi, eye wòawu amesiwo kpɔtɔ ɖe duwo me.

english_verse: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.
translation_verse: Esi wòkpɔ Amalekitɔwo la, edo eƒe numegbe la gblɔ bena: Amalek enye gbãtɔ le dukɔwo dome; ke mlɔeba la ava tsrɔ̃ tsã!

english_verse: “And this is what I saw about the Kenites: They think they're safe, living among the rocks,
translation_verse: Eye esi wòkpɔ Kemtɔwo la, edo eƒe numegbe la gblɔ bena: Wò nɔƒe sesẽ, eye nèwɔ alɔ ɖe agakpewo dzi.

english_verse: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.
translation_verse: Ke woatsrɔ̃ wò Kain ya, eye ekpɔtɔ vie, Asur naɖe aboyo wò.

english_verse: “No one can survive if God plans destruction.
translation_verse: Eye wògado eƒe numegbe la gblɔ bena: Alele! ameka anɔ agbe, ne Mawu awɔ nusia?

english_verse: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
translation_verse: Ʋuwo atso Kitim, ava bɔbɔ Asur kple Eber ɖe anyi, eye woatsrɔ̃ eya hã.

english_verse: After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_verse: Emegbe Bileam dze mɔ, eye wògbugbɔ va wo ɖe, eye Balak hã lé eƒe mɔ.

english_verse: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men had sex with Moabite women.
translation_verse: Esi Israel le Sitim la, dukɔ la de asi ahasiwɔwɔ me kple Moab-nyɔnuwo.

english_verse: These women then invited the men to ceremonies where sacrifices were offered to their gods. The men ate the meat from the sacrifices and worshiped the Moabite gods.
translation_verse: Wokpe dukɔ la va woƒe mawuwo ƒe vɔsanu wo ɖuƒe, eye dukɔ la du nu, eye wòde ta agu na woƒe mawuwo.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel because they had worshiped the god Baal Peor.
translation_verse: Eye Israel ku de Baal-Peor ŋu; eyata Yehowa do dɔmedzoe ɖe Israel ŋu.

english_verse: So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: Yɔ dukɔ la ƒe amegãwo katã ƒo ƒu, eye wòatrɔ ati vodalawo ɖe ŋdɔgbe na Yehowa, ne Yehowa nadzudzɔ dɔmedzoedodo ɖe Israel ŋu!

english_verse: Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ na Israel ƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo bena: Amesiame nawu nɔvia, si ku ɖe Baal-Peor ŋu la!

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Esi wole avi fam le Mawu ƒe agbadɔa nu la, Israel-ŋutsua ɖe kplɔ Midian-nyɔnua ɖe va wo tɔwo gbɔe le Mose kple Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la ŋku me.

english_verse: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear
translation_verse: Eye esi Pinehas, nunɔla Aron vi Eleazar ƒe viŋutsu, kpɔe la, etsi tre le ha la dome, eye wòtsɔ akplɔ ɖe asi

english_verse: and followed the man into his tent, where he ran the spear through the man and into the woman's stomach. The Lord immediately stopped punishing Israel with a deadly disease,
translation_verse: heti Israel-ŋutsu la yome yi xogã me, eye wòƒo nu ɖe Israel-ŋutsu la kple nyɔnu la siaa ƒe dome floi. Tete dɔvɔ̃ la nu tso le Israel-viwo dome.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: “In my anger, I would have wiped out the Israelites if Phinehas had not been faithful to me.
translation_verse: Pinehas, nunɔla Aron vi Eleazar ƒe viŋutsu, enye amesi na nye dɔmedzoe nu fa ɖe Israel-viwo ŋu, elabena eʋã ŋu ɖe nunye le wo dome; eyaŋuti nyemevã nu tsrɔ̃ Israel-viwo o.

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
translation_verse: eye metso nunɔladɔ la de asi na eya ŋutɔ kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo tegbee, elabena ena ŋu ɖe eƒe Mawu nu, eye wòlé avu na Israel-viwo.

english_verse: The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe.
translation_verse: Israel-ŋutsu, si wowu hekpe ɖe Midian-nyɔnua ŋu la ŋkɔ nye Simri, amesi nye amegã Salu, si le Simeon viwo fofo ƒe aƒe nu la, ƒe viŋutsu

english_verse: And the Midianite woman killed with him was Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite clan leader named Zur.
translation_verse: Eye Midian-nyɔnu, si wowu la, ŋkɔ nye Kosbi, amegã Zur, amesi nye Midian-tɔwo ƒe to ɖeka ƒe amegã la, ƒe vinyɔnu.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: “The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_verse: elabena wòlé fu mi, eye wòto aye me tsɔ Peor kple wo de nyɔnu Kosbi, si nye Midian-amegã ɖeka ƒe vinyɔnu, amesi wowu le gbesigbe dɔvɔ̃ va le Peor ta la, tre mɔ̃ na mi.

english_verse: After the Lord had stopped the deadly disease from killing the Israelites, he said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron,
translation_verse: Esi dɔvɔ̃ la nu tso la, Yehowa gblɔ na Mose kple Eleazar, nunɔla Aron vi bena:

english_verse: “I want you to find out how many Israelites are in each family. Then make a list of every man
translation_verse: Mixlẽ amesiwo xɔ ƒe blave kple vɔ le Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la me, le wo fofowo ƒe aƒewo nu: amesiwo katã ate ŋu ade aʋa le Israel.

english_verse: years and older, just as Moses and their ancestors had done when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Yuda viwo nye si le woƒe ƒomewo nu Sela, amesi dzi Sela-ƒome la; Perez, amesi dzi Perez-ƒome la; Sera, amesi dzi Sera-ƒome la;

english_verse: Israel was now camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. Moses and Eleazar told them
translation_verse: Eye Mose kple nunɔla Eleazar fia wo xlẽ le Moab-tagba le Yordan nu le Yerixo kasa;

english_verse: Pallu was the father of Eliab
translation_verse: Palu vi enye Eliab.

english_verse: and the grandfather of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram who had been chosen by the people, but who followed Korah and rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord.
translation_verse: Eye Eliab viwo nye Nemuel, Datan kple Abiram. Woawo nye Datan kple Abiram mawo, siwo nye adaŋudelawo le ha la dome, eye wowɔ dzre kple Mose kple Aron, le esime Korax ƒe ha la wo dzre kple Yehowa,

english_verse: That's when the Lord made the earth open up and swallow Dathan, Abiram, and Korah. At the same time, fire destroyed
translation_verse: eye anyigba ke nu mi wo kpe ɖe Korax ŋu, eye ha la ku, eye dzo fiã ŋutsu alafa eve blaatɔ̃awo, eye wòzu ŋkuɖodzinu la.

english_verse: But the Korahite clan wasn't destroyed.
translation_verse: Ke Korax viwo ya meku o.

english_verse: None of the people that Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai Desert were still alive,
translation_verse: Ke Israel-vi, siwo Mose kple nunɔla Aron tia xlẽ le Sinai-gbedzi la, dometɔa ɖeke mele ame siawo dome o.

english_verse: Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Eye wodzi Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar kple Itamar na Aron.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: “Divide the land of Canaan among these tribes, according to the number of people in each one,
translation_verse: Ame siawoe woamã anyigba la na wòazu woƒe domenyinu le ŋkɔwo ƒe agbɔsɔsɔ nu.

english_verse: I will show you what land to give each tribe, and they will receive as much land as they need, according to the number of people in it.”
translation_verse: Woadzidze nu hafi amã domenyinu la na amesiwo sɔ gbɔ kple amesiwo le ʋee.

english_verse: as well as the clans of Libni, Hebron, Mahli, Mushi, and Korah. Kohath the Levite was the father of Amram,
translation_verse: Lewi-ƒomeawo nye si: Libni-ƒome la, Xebron-ƒome la, Maxeli-ƒome la, Musi-ƒome kple Kora-ƒome la, Kehat enye amesi dzi Amram.

english_verse: the husband of Levi's daughter Jochebed, who was born in Egypt. Amram and Jochebed's three children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
translation_verse: Amram srɔ̃ ŋkɔ nye Yoxebed, nyɔnuvi, si wodzi na Lewi le Egipte, eye wòdzi Aron, Mose kple wo nɔvinyɔnu Miryam na Amram.

english_verse: But Nadab and Abihu had died when they offered fire that was unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke Nadab kple Abihu ku, elabena wotsɔ dzo bubu va Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar counted the Israelites while they were camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Esiawo nye Israel-vi, siwo Mose kple nunɔla Eleazar tia xlẽ le Moab-tagba, le Yordan nu le Yerixo kasa.

english_verse: except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. The Lord had said that everyone else would die there in the desert.
translation_verse: Elabena Yehowa gblɔ na wo bena. Woaku le gbeadzi, eye wo dometɔa ɖeke masusɔ o, negbe Kaleb, Yefune vi, kple Yosua, Nun vi ko.

english_verse: One day his daughters went to the sacred tent, where they met with Moses, Eleazar, and some other leaders of Israel, as well as a large crowd of Israelites. The young women said:
translation_verse: Eye wotsi tre ɖe Mose kple nunɔla Eleazar, amegãwo kpakple ha blibo la ŋku me le, Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la nu hegblɔ bena:

english_verse: You know that our father died in the desert. But it was for something he did wrong, not for joining with Korah in rebelling against the Lord. Our father left no sons
translation_verse: Mía fofo ku le gbeadzi, ke menɔ Korax ƒe ha, si dze aglã ɖe Yehowa ŋu la dome o, ke boŋ eya ŋutɔ ƒe nuvɔ̃ tae woku ɖo, eye viŋutsua ɖeke mele esi o

english_verse: to carry on his family name. But why should his name die out for that reason? Give us some land like the rest of his relatives in our clan, so our father's name can live on.
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti mía fofo ŋkɔ atsrɔ̃ le eƒe ƒome la me, le esi viŋutsu mele esi o ta? Eyata na anyigba mi ɖe mia fofo nɔviwo dome.

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord what should be done,
translation_verse: Eye Mose tsɔ woƒe nya la va Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: and the Lord answered:
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena:

english_verse: Zelophehad's daughters are right. They should each be given part of the land their father would have received.
translation_verse: Zelofxad-vinyɔnuawo gblɔe ɖe teƒe; eyata na domenyinu wo ɖe wo fofo nɔviwo dome, eye nana wo fofo ƒe, domenyinu nayi ɖe wo si me.

english_verse: If he has no daughter, his brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Ke ne vinyɔnua ɖeke mele esi o la, ekema mitsɔ eƒe domenyinu na nɔviaŋutsuwo.

english_verse: But if he has no brothers, his father's brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Ne nɔviŋutsua ɖeke mele esi o la, ekema mitsɔ eƒe domenyinu na fofoa nɔviŋutsuwo.

english_verse: And if his father has no brothers, the land must be given to his nearest relative in the clan. This is my law, and the Israelites must obey it. Joshua Is Appointed Israel's Leader (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ke ne nɔviŋutsua ɖeke mele fofoa si o la, ekema mitsɔ eƒe domenyinu na eƒe ƒometɔ kekeake, amesi te ɖe eŋu le eƒe ƒome la me, eya nanyi doame. Wòanye se kple ɖoɖo na Israel-viwo, abe alesi Yehowa de se na Mose ene. Yosua zu Mose vomedzela.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “One day you will go up into the Abarim Mountains, and from there you will see the land I am giving the Israelites.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena: De Abarim-to dzi, eye nakpɔ anyigba, si mele Israel-viwo na ge la ɖa!

english_verse: After you have seen it, you will die, just like your brother Aaron,
translation_verse: Eye ne ekpɔe vɔ la, wò hã nayi tɔgbuiwowo goɔ, abe alesi nɔviwò Aron yii ene.

english_verse: because both of you disobeyed me at Meribah near the town of Kadesh in the Zin Desert. When the Israelites insulted me there, you didn't believe in my holy power.”
translation_verse: Elabena miesẽ to ɖe nye nya ŋu le Zin-gbedzi, le esime ha la wɔ dzre, eye miena ŋunye kɔ le tsi la gbɔ le woƒe ŋku me o. Esia nye dzrewɔtsi la le Kades le Zin-gbedzi.

english_verse: “You are the Lord God, and you know what is in everyone's heart. So I ask you to appoint a leader for Israel.
translation_verse: Yehowa, si nye gbɔgbɔ, si le ŋutilãwo katã me, ƒe Mawu la, natia ŋutsua ɖe aɖo ha la nu,

english_verse: Your people need someone to lead them into battle, or else they will be like sheep wandering around without a shepherd.”
translation_verse: amesi ado kpli wo, eye wòagagbɔ kpli wo, amesi akplɔ wo adoe, eye wòagakplɔ wo agbɔe, bena Yehowa ƒe ha la maganɔ abe alé, siwo nu kplɔla mele o la, ene o.

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Joshua son of Nun can do the job. Place your hands on him to show that he is the one to take your place.
translation_verse: Yehowa ɖo ŋu na Mose bena: Yɔ Yosua, Nun vi, ŋutsu, si me gbɔgbɔ la le la, eye natsɔ wò asi aɖo edzi,

english_verse: Then go with him and tell him to stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the Israelites. Appoint Joshua as their new leader
translation_verse: eye nakplɔe ava nunɔla Eleazar kple ha blibo la gbɔ, eye nade se nɛ le wo ŋku me,

english_verse: and tell them they must now obey him, just as they obey you.
translation_verse: eye naɖe bubu, si le ŋuwò la, ɖe aɖa ɖe edzi, bena Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la naɖo toe.

english_verse: But Joshua must depend on Eleazar to find out from me what I want him to do as he leads Israel into battle.”
translation_verse: Ele nɛ be, wòava nunɔla Eleazar gbɔ, bena wòatsɔ Urim abia nu nɛ le Yehowa ŋku me; eye alesi wògblɔ la, eya nu woa kple Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la katã naho, eye woagatrɔ agbɔ ɖo.

english_verse: Moses followed the Lord's instructions and took Joshua to Eleazar and the people,
translation_verse: Eye Mose wɔ, abe alesi Yehowa de se nɛ ene; èkplɔ Yosua ɖo nunɔla Eleazar kple ha blibo la ŋku me,

english_verse: then he placed his hands on Joshua and appointed him Israel's leader.
translation_verse: eye wotsɔ eƒe asiwò ɖo edzi, eye wòde se nɛ, abe alesi Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose ene.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: eye efa ƒe ewoliawo ɖeka akpe de alẽviawo dome ɖesiaɖe ŋu.

english_verse: This sacrifice to please me was first offered at Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Esia nye numevɔ, si wosa gbesiagbe le Sinai-to la gbɔ, ne wòanye dzovɔsa, si aʋẽ lilili ɖe Yehowa.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices will please me.
translation_verse: eye miatsɔ wɔ memee efa ƒe ewoliawo ɖeka, si wodzaba kple ami la, awɔ nuɖuvɔsa akpe ɖe alẽvia ɖesiaɖe ŋu. Numevɔsa, si aʋẽ lilili, kple dzovɔsa wònye na Yehowa.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Offer sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, so that I will smell the smoke and be pleased.
translation_verse: De se na Israel-viwo, eye nagblɔ na wo bena: Milé ŋku ɖe nye dzovɔsa ƒe vɔsanu, si nye nye nuɖuɖu, eye wòʋẽna ɖem lilili la ŋu, eye miatsɔe asa vɔ nam le ɣeyiɣi, si woɖo la dzi.

english_verse: Each day offer two rams a year old as sacrifices to please me. The animals must have nothing wrong with them;
translation_verse: Gblɔ na wo bena: Dzovɔ, si miasa na Yehowa la, enye si: Miatsɔ alẽvi eve, siwo sɔ blibo, eye woxɔ ƒe ɖekaɖeka la, asa numevɔe gbesiagbe.

english_verse: Along with each of them, one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice.
translation_verse: Eye natsɔ wo memee efa ƒe ewoliawo ɖeka, si wodzaba kple dzomi hin eneliawo ɖeka la, awɔ nuɖuvɔsae.

english_verse: Finally, along with each of these two sacrifices, a liter of wine must be poured on the altar as a drink offering.
translation_verse: Eye woatsɔ nunovɔsa hin eneliawo ɖeka akpe ɖe alẽvia ɖesiaɖe ŋu. Woatsɔ wein, si nye nunovɔsa la, asa vɔe le kɔkɔeƒe la le Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: On the first day of each month, bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Gbesigbe ɣleti dze dzi la, miatsɔ nyitsuvi eve, agbo ɖeka kple alẽvi adre, siwo sɔ blibo, eye woxɔ ƒe ɖekaɖeka la, asa numevɔ na Yehowa.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Eye miatsɔ wɔ memee eta ƒe ewoliawo etɔ, si wodzaba kple ami la, awɔ nuɖuvɔsa akpe ɖe nyitsua ɖesiaɖe ŋu; miatsɔ wɔ memee efa ƒe ewoliawo eve, si wodzaba kple ami la, awɔ nuɖuvɔsa akpe ɖe agbo ɖeka la ŋu,

english_verse: Celebrate Passover in honor of me on the fourteenth day of the first month of each year.
translation_verse: Ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke wuienelia enye ŋutitotoŋkekenyuie na Yehowa.

english_verse: On the first day of this festival, you must rest from your work and come together for worship.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke gbãtɔ enye takpegbe kɔkɔe, eye wòmã wɔ asinudɔa ɖeke o.

english_verse: Bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. And then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Miatsɔ nyitsuvi eve, agbo ɖeka kple alẽvi adre, siwo xɔ ƒe ɖekaɖeka, eye wòsɔ blibo la, asa dzovɔ, si enye numevɔsa na Yehowa;

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: eye miatsɔ wɔ memee efa ƒe ewoliawo etɔ̃, si wodzaba kple ami la, awɔ nuɖuvɔsa akpe ɖe nyitsua ɖesiaɖe ŋu; efa ƒe ewoliawo eve akpe ɖe agbo ɖeka la ŋu,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: eye eta ƒe ewoliawo ɖeka akpe ɖe alẽviawo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe ŋu.

english_verse: All of these are to be offered each day of the festival in additional to the regular sacrifices, and the smoke from them will please me.
translation_verse: Alea miasa vɔe gbesiagbe ŋkeke adre sɔŋ, ne wòanye nuɖuvɔsa kple dzovɔsa, si aʋẽ lilili ɖe Yehowa, akpe ɖe gbesiagbe numevɔsa kple nunovɔsa ŋuti.

english_verse: Then on the last day of the festival, you must once again rest from work and come together for worship. The Sacrifices during the Harvest Festival (Leviticus
translation_verse: Eye ŋkeke adreagbe enye takpegbe kɔkɔe na mi, miawɔ asinudɔa ɖeke o. Pentekosteŋkeke vɔsawo.

english_verse: On the first day of the Harvest Festival, you must rest from your work, come together for worship, and bring a sacrifice of new grain.
translation_verse: Gbesigbe mieŋe nu gbãtɔwo, eye mietsɔ nuɖuɖu yeyewo sa vɔ na Yehowa le miaƒe kwasiɖawo ƒe ŋkekenyuie dzi la, enye takpegbe kɔkɔe na mi, miawɔ asinudɔa ɖeke o.

english_verse: Offer two young bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Eye miatsɔ nyitsuvi eve, agbo ɖeka kple alẽvi adre, siwo xɔ ƒe ɖekaɖeka asa numevɔ, ne wòaʋẽ lilili ɖe Yehowa.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,

english_verse: Also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Emegbe woatsɔ gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka alé avu na mi.

english_verse: The animals must have nothing wrong with them and are to be sacrificed along with the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: Esiawo miatsɔ asa vɔe akpe ɖe gbesiagbe numevɔsa kple nuɖuvɔsa kple nunovɔsa ŋuti; lãwo nasɔ blibo.

english_verse: On the first day of the seventh month, you must rest from your work and come together to celebrate at the sound of the trumpets.
translation_verse: Ɣleti adrelia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ enye takpegbe kɔkɔe na mi eve miawɔ asinudɔa ɖeke o; kpẽkugbe wòanye na mi.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with the bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Eve miatsɔ wɔ memee efa ƒe ewoliawo etɔ, si wodzaba kple ami la, awɔ nuɖuvɔsa akpe ɖe nyitsu ɖeka la ŋu eta ƒe ewoliawo eve akpe ɖe agbo la ŋu,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: eye efa ƒe ewoliawo ɖeka akpe ɖe alẽvi adreawo dome ɖesiaɖe ŋu.

english_verse: You must also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Eye woatsɔ gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka asa nuvɔ̃vɔe ahatsɔ le avu na mi,

english_verse: These sacrifices will be made in addition to the regular daily sacrifices and the sacrifices for the first day of the month. The smoke from these sacrifices will please me. The Sacrifices on the Great Day of Forgiveness (Leviticus
translation_verse: hekpe ɖe ɣleti yeye dzi numevɔsa kple eŋu nuɖuvɔsa kpakple gbesiagbe numevɔsa kple, eŋu nuɖuvɔsa ŋuti; eye woawɔ wo ŋu nunovɔsawo ɖe ɖoɖo la nu, ne wòanye dzovɔsa, si aʋẽ lilili ɖe Yehowa. Avuleŋkeke-vɔsawo.

english_verse: The tenth day of the seventh month is the Great Day of Forgiveness. On that day you must rest from all work and come together for worship. Show sorrow for your sins by going without food,
translation_verse: Ɣleti adrelia sia ƒe ŋkeke ewolia enye takpegbe kɔkɔe na mi, míatsi nu adɔ, eye miawɔ dɔa ɖeke o.

english_verse: and bring to the altar one young bull, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Eye miatsɔ nyitsuvi ɖeka, agbo ɖeka kple alẽvi adre, siwo xɔ ƒe ɖekaɖeka la, asa numevɔ, ne wòaʋẽ lilili ɖe Yehowa; lãwo nasɔ blibo.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with the bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Eye miatsɔ wɔ memee eta ƒe ewoliawo etɔ̃, si wodzaba kple ami la, awɔ nuɖuvɔsa akpe ɖe nyitsu la ŋu, efa ƒe ewoliawo eve akpe ɖe agbo ɖeka la ŋu,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: eye efa; ƒe ewoliawo ɖeka akpe ɖe alẽvi adreawo dome ɖesiaɖe ŋu.

english_verse: A goat must also be sacrificed for the sins of the people. You will offer these sacrifices in addition to the sacrifice to ask forgiveness and the regular daily sacrifices. The Sacrifices during the Festival of Shelters (Leviticus
translation_verse: Emegbe miatsɔ gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka asa nuvɔ̃vɔe vɔ akpe ɖe nuvɔ̃vɔsa, si wotsɔ lé avui kple gbesiagbe numevɔsa kpakple eŋu nuɖuvɔsa kple nunovɔsa ŋuti. Agbadɔ me nanɔ ŋkekenyuie-vɔsawo.

english_verse: Beginning on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and continuing for seven days, everyone must celebrate the Festival of Shelters in honor of me.
translation_verse: Ɣleti adrelia te ŋkeke wuiatɔ̃lia enye takpegbe kɔkɔe na mi miawɔ asinudɔa ɖeke o, eye miaɖu ŋkekenyuie na Yehowa ŋkeke adre sɔŋ.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the rams,
translation_verse: Eye miatsɔ wɔ memee efa ƒe ewoliawo etɔ̃, si wodzaba kple ami la, awɔ nuɖuvɔsa akpe ɖe nyitsu wuietɔ̃awo dome ɖesiaɖe ŋu; efa ƒe ewoliawo eve akpe ɖe agbo eveawo dome ɖesiaɖe ŋu,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: eye efa ƒe ewolia wo ɖeka akpe ɖe alẽvi wuieneawo dome ɖesiaɖe ŋuti.

english_verse: You must also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These are to be offered in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: Emegbe miatsɔ gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka asa nuvɔ̃vɔe akpe ɖe gbesiagbe numevɔsa kpakple eŋu nuɖuvɔsa kple nunovɔsa ŋuti.

english_verse: On the eighth day, you must once again rest from your work and come together for worship.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke enyilia enye takpegbe na mi, eye miawo asinudɔa ɖeke o.

english_verse: Bring to the altar one bull, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Eye miatsɔ nyitsu ɖeka, agbo ɖeka kple alẽvi adre, siwo sɔ blibo, eye woxɔ ƒe ɖekaɖeka la, asa numevɔ, si nye dzovɔsa, ne wòaʋẽ lilili ɖe Yehowa.

english_verse: You must also offer the proper grain sacrifices and drink offerings of wine with each animal.
translation_verse: Eye miawɔ nuɖuvɔsa kple nunovɔsa ɖe nyitsu la, agbo la kple alẽviawo ƒe agbɔsɔsɔme ŋu ɖe ɖoɖo la nu.

english_verse: And offer a goat as the sacrifice to ask forgiveness for the people. These sacrifices are made in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: Emegbe miatsɔ gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka asa nuvɔ̃vɔe akpe ɖe gbesiagbe numevɔsa kpakple eŋu nuɖuvɔsa kple nunovɔsa ŋuti.

english_verse: You must offer all these sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, together with any offerings that are voluntarily given or given because of a promise.
translation_verse: Esiawo miatsɔ asa vɔ na Yehowa le miaƒe ŋkekenyuiewo dzi hekpe ɖe numevɔsa, nuɖuvɔsa, nunovɔsa kple akpedavɔsa, siwo mieɖe adzɔgbe alo na le mia ɖokui si la ŋuti.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to Israel's tribal leaders:
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ se, siwo katã Yehowa ɖe nɛ la, na Israel-viwo.

english_verse: When one of you men makes a promise to the Lord, you must keep your word.
translation_verse: Eye Mose ƒo nu kple Israel-viwo ƒe toawo ƒe amegãwo bena: Ale Yehowa ɖe se enye si:

english_verse: Suppose a young woman who is still living with her parents makes a promise to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe ɖe adzɔgbe na Yehowa, alo wòka atam hetsri nu na eɖokui la, ekema megada eƒe nya la dzi o, boŋ wòawɔ nya, siwo katã do le enu la dzi.

english_verse: If her father hears about it and says nothing, she must keep her promise.
translation_verse: Ne nyɔnua ɖe nye ɖetugbi le fofoa ƒe me, eye wòɖe adzɔgbe na Yehowa alo tsri nu na eɖokui,

english_verse: But if he hears about it and objects, then she no longer has to keep her promise. The Lord will forgive her, because her father did not agree with the promise.
translation_verse: eye fofoa se adzɔgbe, si wòɖe, alo nusi wòtsri na eɖokui, gake fofoa zi kpi kpɔe la, ekema wòawɔ adzɔgbe, si wòɖe, alo nusi wòtsri na eɖokui la dzi.

english_verse: But if her husband hears about the promise and objects, she no longer has to keep it, and the Lord will forgive her.
translation_verse: eye srɔ̃a zi kpi kpɔe le gbesigbe wòsee la, ekema wòawɔ eƒe adzɔgbe, si wòɖe, alo nusi wòtsri la dzi.

english_verse: Suppose a married woman makes a promise to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke ahosiwo kple nyɔnu, siwo wogbe la, nawɔ woƒe adzɔgbeɖeɖewo kple nusiwo wotsri na wo ɖokui la dzi.

english_verse: If her husband hears about the promise and says nothing, she must do what she said.
translation_verse: Nenye srɔ̃ ƒe me wòɖe adzɔgbe le, alo wòka atam hetsri nu na eɖokui la,

english_verse: But if he hears about the promise and does object, she no longer has to keep it. The Lord will forgive her, because her husband would not allow her to keep the promise.
translation_verse: eye srɔ̃a see, gake wozi kpi kpɔe, eye megbe nɛ o la, ekema wòawɔ eƒe adzɔgbe, siwo katã wòɖe, alo nusiwo wòtsri na eɖokui la dzi.

english_verse: If her husband hears about a promise and says nothing about it for a whole day, she must do what she said—since he did not object, the promise must be kept.
translation_verse: Ne nyɔnua ɖe ɖe adzɔgbe sia adzɔgbe alo ka atam sia atam hetsri nu bena, yeatsi nu adɔ la, srɔ̃a ate ŋu ana be, wòawɔ edzi alo agblẽ eme nɛ.

english_verse: But if he waits until the next day to stop her from keeping her promise, he is the one who must be punished.
translation_verse: Ke ne srɔ̃a zi kpi egbe kple etsɔ la, ekema wòawɔ adzɔgbe, siwo katã wòɖe, alo nusi wòtsri la dzi, elabena ezi kpi kpɔe le gbesigbe wòsee.

english_verse: These are the laws that the Lord gave Moses about husbands and wives, and about young daughters who still live at home.
translation_verse: Gake ne esee eteƒe didi, hafi wogblẽ eme nɛ la, ekema eƒe vodada le ŋutsu la dzi.

english_verse: “Before you die, make sure that the Midianites are punished for what they did to Israel.”
translation_verse: Bia hlɔ̃ Midiantɔwo na Israel-viwo; emegbe nayi tɔgbuiwòwo gbɔ.

english_verse: Then Moses told the people, “The Lord wants to punish the Midianites. So tell our men to prepare for battle.
translation_verse: Tete Mose gblɔ na dukɔ la bena: Mina ŋutsuwo nabia akpa le mia dome, bena woaho aʋa ɖe Midian ŋu, ne woabia hlɔ̃ Midian na Yehowa.

english_verse: Twelve thousand men were picked from the tribes of Israel, and after they were prepared for battle,
translation_verse: Eye to sia to na ame akpe ɖeka tso Israel ƒe ame akpe akpeawo dome; amesiwo bia akpa hena aʋayiyi la, le ame akpe wuieve.

english_verse: Moses sent them off to war. Phinehas the son of Eleazar went with them and took along some things from the sacred tent and the trumpets for sounding the battle signal.
translation_verse: Eye Mose ɖɔ ame akpe ɖeka tso to sia to me ɖo ɖe aʋa la, eye Pinehas, nunɔla Eleazar vi, he nu kɔkɔeawo kple kpẽ, siwo woaku atsiã ɖe nu la, ɖe asi.

english_verse: The Israelites fought against the Midianites, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. They killed all the men,
translation_verse: Woho aʋa ɖe Midian ŋu, abe alesi Yehowa de se na Mose ene, eye wowu ŋutsuwo katã.

english_verse: including Balaam son of Beor and the five Midianite kings, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
translation_verse: Eye wowu Midian-fia atɔ̃awo, siwo nye: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Xur kple Reba la, kpe ɖe ame bubuawo ŋu; eye wowu Bileam, Beor vi, hã kple via.

english_verse: The Israelites captured every woman and child, then led away the Midianites' cattle and sheep, and took everything else that belonged to them.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ɖe aboyo Midiantɔwo srɔ̃wo kple wo viwo, eye woha woƒe agbatsɔlãwo katã, lãhawo katã kple woƒe kesinɔnuwo katã:

english_verse: They also burned down the Midianite towns and villages.
translation_verse: eye wòto dzo du, siwo katã me wònɔ, kple woƒe agbadɔwo katã.

english_verse: and said, “I can't believe you let the women live!
translation_verse: Eye Mose gblɔ na wo bena: A, miena nyɔnuwo katã tsi agbea?

english_verse: You must put to death every boy and all the women who have ever had sex.
translation_verse: Eyata miwu ŋutsuvi, siwo katã le ɖeviawo dome, eye miwu nyɔnuvi, siwo katã ɖo ŋutsu gbɔ kpɔ;

english_verse: But do not kill the young women who have never had sex. You may keep them for yourselves.”
translation_verse: gake mina nyɔnuvi, siwo katã medo ŋutsu gbo kpo o te ɖeviawo dome la, natsi agbe na mi.

english_verse: Then Moses said to the soldiers, “If you killed anyone or touched a dead body, you are unclean and have to stay outside the camp for seven days. On the third and seventh days, you must go through a ceremony to make yourselves and your captives clean.
translation_verse: Ke miawo mitsi asaɖa godo ŋkeke adre sɔŋ, eye amesiwo wu ame kple amesiwo ka asi ame tsiaʋawo ŋu la, naɖe nuvɔ̃ ɖa le wo ɖokui kple amesiwo wòlé la ŋu, le ŋkeke etɔ̃lia kple ŋkeke adrelia dzi.

english_verse: Then wash your clothes and anything made from animal skin, goat's hair, or wood.”
translation_verse: Eye miaɖe nuvɔ̃ ɖa le avɔwo katã kple nusiwo katã wotsɔ lãgbalẽ kple gbɔ̃fuwo wɔe, kpakple atinuwo katã ŋuti.

english_verse: Eleazar then explained, “If you need to purify something that won't burn, such as gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, or lead, you must first place it in a hot fire. After you take it out, sprinkle it with the water that purifies. Everything else should only be sprinkled with the water. Do all of this, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
translation_verse: kpakple nusianu, si ate ŋu aɖe dzo me la, haha dzoe, ekema wo ŋu akɔ; gake ele be, woatsɔ ameŋukɔtsi aɖe nuvɔ̃ ɖa le wo ŋu. Ke woatsɔ tsi aklɔ nusiwo katã mate ŋu ade dzo me o lae.

english_verse: Wash your clothes on the seventh day, and after that, you will be clean and may return to the camp.” Everything Taken from the Midianites Is Divided
translation_verse: Eye ne mienyã miaƒe avɔwo le ŋkeke adreagbe la, ekema mia ŋu akɔ, emegbe miekpɔ mɔ ayi asaɖa la me. Aboyo me mamã.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Mose bena:

english_verse: From the half that belongs to the soldiers, set aside for the Lord one out of every
translation_verse: Naɖee le wo tɔ ŋu awɔ adzɔe na Yehowa ahatsɔ na nunɔla Eleazar.

english_verse: So we want to give the Lord all the gold jewelry we took from the Midianites. It's our gift to him for watching over us and our troops.”
translation_verse: Eyata mietsɔ sikanu, siwo amesiame ha la vɛ, be miana Yehowa, woawo nye: abɔkpowo, alonugɛwo, asigɛwo, togɛwo kple kɔdzonuwo, ne míalé avu na mía ɖokui le Yehowa gbɔ.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar followed the Lord's instructions
translation_verse: Eye Mose kple nunɔla Eleazar wɔ, abe alesi Yehowa de se na Mose ene.

english_verse: women and gave them to Eleazar to be dedicated to the Lord. Then from the half that belonged to the people, Moses set aside one out of every
translation_verse: Eye aboyonu, siwo aʋawɔlawo ha la, ƒe kpɔtɔea le alé akpe alafa ade blaadre vɔ atɔ̃,

english_verse: and listed everything that had been taken from the Midianites. The list included
translation_verse: eye nyɔnuvi, siwo medo ŋutsu gbɔ kpɔ o la, le ame akpe blaetɔ̃ vɔ eve.

english_verse: and said, “Sir, we have counted our troops, and not one soldier is missing.
translation_verse: eye wogblɔ na Mose bena: Wò dolawo xlẽ aʋawɔla, siwo wode asi na mí la, eye wo dometɔa ɖeke meto le eme o.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar accepted the jewelry from the commanders,
translation_verse: Tete Mose kple nunɔla Eleazar xɔ sikatsyɔ̃ɖonu vovovoawo le wo si.

english_verse: This did not include the things that the soldiers had kept for themselves.
translation_verse: Ke aʋawɔviawo dome ɖesiaɖe ha nu na eɖokui.

english_verse: So Moses and Eleazar placed the gold in the Lord's sacred tent to remind Israel of what had happened.
translation_verse: Eye Mose kple nunɔla Eleazar xɔ sikawo le amesiwo woɖo ame akpewo kple ame alafawo nu la si, eye wotso wo va Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la me, ne woanye ŋkuɖodzinu na Israel-viwo le Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: except Caleb and Joshua. They remained faithful to the Lord,
translation_verse: negbe Kaleb, Yefune vi, Kenesitɔ la, kple Yosua, Nun vi ko, elabena woawo dze Yehowa yome blibo.

english_verse: then after the Lord helps Israel capture the land, you can return to your own land. You will no longer have to stay with the others.
translation_verse: eye anyigba la na ta le Yehowa ŋku me, emegbe hafi mietrɔ la, ekema miaɖi fɔ le Yehowa kple Israel ŋku me o, eye anyigba sia azu mia tɔ le Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben and Gad owned a lot of cattle and sheep, and they saw that the regions of Jazer and Gilead had good pastureland.
translation_verse: Eye lã geɖewo le Ruben-viwo kple Gad-viwo si. Eye wokpɔ Yaezer kple Gilead-nyigba bena, enye afisi nyo na lãnyinyi.

english_verse: So they went to Moses, Eleazar, and the other leaders of Israel and said,
translation_verse: Eyata Gad-viwo kple Ruben-viwo va gblɔ na Mose kple nunɔla Eleazar kpakple ha la ƒe amegãwo bena:

english_verse: “The Lord has helped us capture the land around the towns of Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon. That's good pastureland, and since we own cattle and sheep,
translation_verse: anyigba, siwo Yehowa xɔ le Israel ƒe ŋku me la, enyo na lãnyinyi, eye lãwo le wò dɔlawo si.

english_verse: would you let us stay here east of the Jordan River and have this land as our own?”
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ bena: Ne eve mía nu la, ekema tso anyigba sia na wò dɔlawo, ne wòanye wo to, eye megakpɔ mí yi Yordan godo o.

english_verse: Moses answered: You mean you'd stay here while the rest of the Israelites go into battle?
translation_verse: Tete Mose gblɔ na Gad-viwo kple Ruben-viwo bena: A, mia nɔviwo le aʋa yi ge, eye miawo miedi be, miatsi afisia?

english_verse: If you did that, it would discourage the others from crossing over into the land the Lord promised them.
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti miele didim be, miaɖe dzi le Israel-viwo ƒo, bena womagayi toa godo le anyigba, si Yehowa na wo la dzi oa?

english_verse: This is exactly what happened when I sent your ancestors from Kadesh-Barnea to explore the land.
translation_verse: Alea pɛ mia fofowo wɔ, esi medo wo tso Kades-Barnea, bena woaɖakpɔ anyigba la ɖa.

english_verse: They went as far as Eshcol Valley, then returned and told the people that we should not enter it.
translation_verse: Wova Eskol-tɔʋu la nu hekpɔ anyigba la ɖa, eye woɖe dzi le Israel-viwo ƒo, ale bena wobe, yewomegale anyigba, si Yehowa na wo la, dzi yi ge o.

english_verse: The Lord became very angry.
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa do dɔmedzoe gbemagbe heka atam bena:

english_verse: Moses said: You promised that you would be ready to fight for the Lord.
translation_verse: Tete Mose gblɔ na wo bena: Ne miawɔ alea, eye miabla akpa le Yehowa ŋku me hena aʋayiyi:

english_verse: but he was so angry with the others that he forced them to wander around in the desert for
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa do dɔmedzoe ɖe Israel ŋu, eye wòna wotsa le gbedzi ƒe blane sɔŋ, vaseɖe esime ƒome, siwo katã wɔ nuvɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me la, tsrɔ̃ keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: So Moses gave the Machirites the region of Gilead, and they settled there.
translation_verse: Eye Mose tsɔ Gilead na Manase vi Maxir, eye wònɔ eme.

english_verse: Now you people of Reuben and Gad are doing the same thing and making the Lord even angrier.
translation_verse: Azɔ mi nuvɔ̃wɔlawo ƒe dzidzimeviwo, miexɔ ɖe mia fofowo teƒe, be Yehowa nagado dɔmedzoe ɖe Israel ŋu awu.

english_verse: If you reject the Lord, he will once again abandon his people and leave them here in the desert. And you will be to blame!
translation_verse: Ne mietrɔ le eyome la, ekema ana woagatsi gbeadzi eteƒe nadidi, eye miahe gbegblẽ ava dukɔ blibo la dzi.

english_verse: The men from Reuben and Gad replied: Let us build places to keep our sheep and goats, and towns for our wives and children,
translation_verse: Tete wova egbɔ gblɔ bena: Miato kpɔ na míaƒe lãwo ɖe afisia, eye míatso duwo na mía viwo;

english_verse: where they can stay and be safe. Then we'll prepare to fight and lead the other tribes into battle.
translation_verse: ke mía ŋutɔwo míabla akpa anɔ Israel-viwo ŋgɔ, vaseɖe esime míakplɔ wo ava wo teƒee; gake mía viwo nanɔ du sesẽwo me le anyigbadzinɔlawo ta.

english_verse: We will stay with them until they have settled in their own tribal lands.
translation_verse: Míatrɔ va míaƒe xɔwo nu o, vaseɖe esime Israel-viwo dome amesiame naxɔ eƒe domenyinu wòanye etɔ hafi.

english_verse: The land on this side of the Jordan River will be ours, so we won't expect to receive any on the other side.
translation_verse: Míaxɔ domenyinu ɖe wo ti le Yordan godo o, elabena míaƒe domenyinu le Yordan ƒe go si dzi, le ɣedzeƒe gome.

english_verse: You also agreed to cross the Jordan and stay with the rest of the Israelites, until the Lord forces our enemies out of the land. If you do these things,
translation_verse: eye mia dometɔ, siwo katã bia akpa atso Yordan le Yehowa ŋku me, vaseɖe esime wòanya eƒe futɔwo ɖa le eŋgɔ,

english_verse: But if you don't keep your promise, you will sin against the Lord and be punished.
translation_verse: Ke ne miewɔ alea o la, ekema miewɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Yehowa ŋu, eye míakpɔ miaƒe nuvɔ̃wo tɔ nua.

english_verse: Go ahead and build towns for your wives and children, and places for your sheep and goats. Just be sure to do what you have promised.
translation_verse: Mitso duwo na mia viwo, eye mitɔ kpɔ na miaƒe lãwo; nuwo, abe alesi do le mia nu ene.

english_verse: The men from Reuben and Gad answered: Sir, we will do just what you have said.
translation_verse: Eye Gad-viwo kple Ruben-viwo ɖo ŋu na Mose bena; Wò dɔlawo awɔ, abe alesi miaƒe aƒetɔ de se ene.

english_verse: Our wives and children and sheep and cattle will stay here in the towns in Gilead.
translation_verse: Mia viwo kple nua srɔ̃wo, miaƒe lãwo kple míaƒe agbatsɔlãwo katã natsi Gilead-duwo me.

english_verse: But those of us who are prepared for battle will cross the Jordan and fight for the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke wò dɔlawo katã abla akpa le Yehowa ŋku me ayi aʋa le tɔa godo, abe alesi miaƒe aƒetɔ gblɔ ene.

english_verse: Then Moses said to Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders,
translation_verse: Tete Mose de se le wo ta na nunɔla Eleazar kple; Yosua, Nun vi, kpakple Israel-viwo ƒe toawo ƒe amegãwo,

english_verse: “Make sure that the tribes of Gad and Reuben prepare for battle and cross the Jordan River with you. If they do, then after the land is in your control, give them the region of Gilead as their tribal land.
translation_verse: eye Mose gblɔ na wo bena: Ne Gad-viwo kple Ruben-viwo katã abla akpa le Yehowa ŋku me ayi aʋa kpli mi le Yordan godo, eye anyigba: la ana ta mi la, ekema mitsɔ Gilead-nyigba na wo, ne wòanye wo tɔ.

english_verse: But if they break their promise, they will receive land on the other side of the Jordan, like the rest of the tribes.”
translation_verse: Ke ne womebla akpa yi tɔa godo kpli mi o la, ekema woaxɔ anyigba ɖe mia dome le Kanaan-nyigba dzi

english_verse: The tribes of Gad and Reuben replied, “We are your servants and will do whatever the Lord has commanded.
translation_verse: Tete Gad-viwo kple Ruben-viwo do ŋu bena: Alesi Yehowa gblɔ na wò dɔlawo la, nenema miawɔ

english_verse: We will cross the Jordan River, ready to fight for the Lord in Canaan. But the land we will inherit as our own will be on this side of the river.”
translation_verse: Míabla akpa le Yehowa ŋku me ayi Kanaan-nyigba dzi, bena miaƒe domenyinu nanɔ Yordan ƒe go si dzi.

english_verse: So Moses gave the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh the territory and towns that King Sihon the Amorite had ruled, as well as the territory and towns that King Og of Bashan had ruled.
translation_verse: Eye Mose tsɔ Sixon, Amori-fia ƒe fiaduƒe kple Og, Basan-fia ƒe fiaduƒe, anyigba la kple edzi duwo kpakple eŋu liƒowo na Gad-viwo kple Ruben-viwo kpakple Yosef vi, Manase ƒe to afã.

english_verse: The tribe of Gad rebuilt the towns of Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
translation_verse: Eye Gad-viwo tso Dibon, Atarot kple Aroer,

english_verse: Atroth-Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
translation_verse: Aterot-Sofan, Yaezer kple Yogbeha,

english_verse: Beth-Nimrah, and Beth-Haran. They built walls around them and also built places to keep their sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Bet-Nimra kple Bet-Haran, siwo nye du sesẽwo, afisi wòtɔ alẽkpɔwo ɖo.

english_verse: The tribe of Reuben rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
translation_verse: Eye Ruben-viwo tso Xesbon, Eleale kple Kiryatayim,

english_verse: Sibmah, as well as the towns that used to be known as Nebo and Baal-Meon. They renamed all those places.
translation_verse: Neho, Baal-Meon kple Sibma, eye wotrɔ ŋkɔ na wo hetsɔ ŋkɔ yeye na du, siwo wotso la.

english_verse: The clan of Machir from the tribe of East Manasseh went to the region of Gilead, captured its towns, and forced out the Amorites.
translation_verse: Eye Manase vi Maxir ƒe viwo yi ɖaxɔ Gilead, eye wonyã Amoritɔ, siwo le eme la ɖa.

english_verse: Jair from the Manasseh tribe captured villages and renamed them “Villages of Jair.”
translation_verse: Eye Manase vi Yair yi ɖaxɔ woƒe kɔƒewo, eye wòna ŋkɔ wo be Yair-kɔƒewo.

english_verse: Nobah captured the town of Kenath with its villages and renamed it Nobah.
translation_verse: Eye Nobax yi ɖaxɔ Kenat kple eŋu kɔƒewo, eye wòna ŋkɔe le eƒe ŋkɔ nu be Nobax.

english_verse: As Israel traveled from Egypt under the command of Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Esiawo nye Israel-viwo ƒe toƒewo, lé esime woʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi hamehame, eye Mose kple Aron le wo nu la.

english_verse: Moses kept a list of the places they camped, just as the Lord had instructed. Here is the record of their journey:
translation_verse: Eye Mose ŋlɔ woƒe mɔzɔzɔ la le woƒe toƒewo nu, abe alesi Yehowa de se ene. Esia nye woƒe mɔzɔzɔ la le woƒe toƒewo nu.

english_verse: After the Israelites left Rameses, they camped at Succoth,
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ho tso Ramses heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Sukot.

english_verse: and from there, they moved their camp to Etham on the edge of the desert.
translation_verse: Woho tso Sukot heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Etam le gbegbe la nu,

english_verse: Then they turned back toward Pi-Hahiroth, east of Baal-Zephon, and camped near Migdol.
translation_verse: eya woho tso Etam hetrɔ ɖo ta Pihaxirot le Baal-Zefon ŋgɔ, eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Migdol ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome.

english_verse: They left Pi-Hahiroth, crossed the Red Sea, then walked three days into the Etham Desert and camped at Marah.
translation_verse: Woho tso Pihaxirot, eye wotso ƒu la heva gbedzi, eye wozɔ Etam-gbedzi ŋkeke etɔ̃ heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Mara,

english_verse: They left Elim and camped near the Red Sea,
translation_verse: Woho tso Elim heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Avaƒu la nu,

english_verse: then turned east and camped along the western edge of the Sinai Desert.
translation_verse: eye woho tso Avaƒu la nu heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Sin-gbedzi.

english_verse: From there they went to Dophkah, Alush, and Rephidim, where they had no water.
translation_verse: Woho tso Alus heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Refidim, afisi tsia ɖeke mele, be dukɔ la nano o;

english_verse: They left Rephidim and finally reached the Sinai Desert.
translation_verse: eye woho tso Refidim heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Sinai-gbedzi.

english_verse: When they left Kadesh, they came to Mount Hor, on the border of Edom.
translation_verse: eye woho tso Kades heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Hor-to la gbɔ, le Edom ƒe liƒo dzi.

english_verse: That's where the Lord commanded Aaron the priest to go to the top of the mountain. Aaron died there on the first day of the fifth month,
translation_verse: Eye nunɔla Aron ɖe Hor-to la dzi, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ ene, eye woku le afima, le esime Israel-viwo ʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi ƒe blane megbe le ɣleti atɔ̃lia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi.

english_verse: It was then that the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Southern Desert of Canaan, heard that Israel was headed that way.
translation_verse: Eye Kanaanitɔ, Arad-fia, si nɔ Kanaan-nyigba ƒe dziehe gome la, se bena, Israel-viwo gbɔna.

english_verse: and finally in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: eye woho tso Abarim-to la gbɔ heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Moab-tagba le Yordan nu le Yerixo kasa.

english_verse: Their camp stretched from Beth-Jeshimoth to Acacia. The Lord's Command To Conquer Canaan
translation_verse: Woƒu asaɖa la anyi ɖe Yordan nu tso Bet-Yesimot vaseɖe Abel-Sitim le Moab-tagba. Se le Kanaanitɔwo tsɔtsrɔ̃ ŋuti.

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose le Moab-tagba, le Yordan nu, le Yerixo kasa bena:

english_verse: to give the people of Israel this message: When you cross the Jordan River and enter Canaan,
translation_verse: Ƒo nu kple Israel-viwo, eye nagblɔ na wo bena: Ne mietso Yordan va Kanaan-nyigba dzi la,

english_verse: you must force out the people living there. Destroy their idols and tear down their altars.
translation_verse: ekema mianya anyigbadzinɔlawo katã le mia ŋgɔ, eye miagbã woƒe aklama kpakpɛwo katã kple woƒe legbawo katã kpakple woƒe vɔsamlekpuiwo katã.

english_verse: Then settle in the land—I have given it to you as your own.
translation_verse: Eye miaxɔ anyigba la wòanye mia to miano edzi; elabena miawoe metsɔ anyigba la na, be wòanye mia to.

english_verse: I will show you how to divide the land among the tribes, according to the number of clans in each one, so that the larger tribes will have more land than the smaller ones.
translation_verse: Miadzidze nu ɖe anyigba la dzi amãe ɖe miaƒe ƒomeawo nu; miana domenyinu la amesiwo sɔ gbɔ la, wòalolo, eye amesiwo le ʋee la, ƒe domenyinu nanɔ ʋee. Teƒe, si dzi nudzidze la dze nɛ la, afima woaxɔ; mianye ɖe mia fofowo ƒe toawo nu.

english_verse: If you don't force out all the people there, they will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your back. They will always be trouble for you,
translation_verse: Ke ne mienyã anyigbadzinɔlawo le mia ŋgɔ o la, ekema amesiwo miegblẽ ɖi la, atro zu ŋu ano miaƒe ŋku ta kple aŋɔka anɔ mia xa, eye woaxaxa mi ɖo le anyigba, si dzi miele la dzi.

english_verse: and I will treat you as severely as I planned on treating them.
translation_verse: Eye matsɔ nusi meɖi be, mawɔ wo la, awɔ mi.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: to tell the people of Israel that their land in Canaan would have the following borders:
translation_verse: De se na Israel-viwo, eye nagblɔ na wo bena: Ne mieva Kanaan-nyigba dzi la, ekema anyigba, si anye miaƒe domenyinu la, enye si: Kanaan-nyigba kple eŋu liƒowo.

english_verse: The southern border will be the Zin Desert and the northwest part of Edom. This border will begin at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Miaƒe dziehekpa natso Zin-gbedzi amlo ato Edom ŋu. Ale miaƒe dzieheliƒo natso Dzeƒu la ƒe mlɔenu le ɣedzeƒe gome,

english_verse: It will go west from there, but will turn southward to include Scorpion Pass, the village of Zin, and the town of Kadesh-Barnea. From there, the border will continue to Hazar-Addar and on to Azmon.
translation_verse: eye liƒo la naɖo ta Akrabim-to dzi mo ƒe dziehe gome ato Zin ŋu ayi ɖe Kades-Barnea ƒe dziehe gome, eye wòaɖo ta Xazar-Adar ava ke ɖe Azmon.

english_verse: It will run along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Eye liƒo la nanyè kpo tso Azmon ɖe Egipte-tɔʋu la ŋu ava wu nu ɖe ƒu la nu.

english_verse: The western border will be the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Miaƒe ɣetoɖoƒeliƒo nanye ƒu gã la; eya nado liƒo na mi le ɣetoɖoƒe gome.

english_verse: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean, then continue eastward to Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Miaɖe anyieheliƒo la tso ƒu gã la nu ato Hor-to la ŋu.

english_verse: After that, it will run to Lebo-Hamath and across to Zedad, which is the northern edge of your land.
translation_verse: Miaɖee tso Hor-to la gbɔ aɖo ta Xamat, eye liƒo la naɖe Zedad.

english_verse: From Zedad, the border will continue east to Ziphron and end at Hazar-Enan.
translation_verse: Liƒo la nato Zifron ava wu nu ɖe Xazar-Enan. Esia nanye anyieheliƒo na mi.

english_verse: and on down to Riblah on the east side of Ain. From there, it will go south to the eastern hills of Lake Galilee,
translation_verse: Eye liƒo la natso Sefam ato Ribla le Ain ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome, eye liƒo la nazɔ Kineret-ta ƒe ɣedzeƒekpa ŋu.

english_verse: then follow the Jordan River down to the north end of the Dead Sea. The land within those four borders will belong to you.
translation_verse: Eye liƒo la nazɔ Yordan ŋu axa wu nu ɖe Dzeƒu la nu.

english_verse: Then Moses told the people, “You will receive the land inside these borders. It will be yours, but the Lord has commanded you to divide it among the nine and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Eve Mose de se na Israel-viwo bena Esia nye anyigba, si dzi woadzidze nu ɖo amã na mi la; anyigba si ŋu Yehowa ɖe se le be, woatsɔ na to asieke kple afã la.

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh have already been given their land
translation_verse: Elabena Ruben-viwo ƒe to kple Gad-viwo ƒe to kpakple Manase ƒe to atã la xɔ woƒe domenyinu ɖe wo tofowo ƒe aƒewo nu xoxo.

english_verse: across from Jericho, east of the Jordan River.” The Leaders Who Will Divide the Land
translation_verse: To eve kple afã xɔ woƒe domenyinu ɖe Yordan ƒe go keme dzi le Yerixo kasa le ɣedzeƒe gome. Alesi woama anyigba la mee.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu kple Mose bena:

english_verse: “Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun will divide the land for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ŋutsu, siwo amã anyigba la na mi, ƒe ŋkɔwo nye si: Nunɔla Eleazar kple Yosua, Nun vi.

english_verse: One leader from each tribe will help them,
translation_verse: Eye miade amegã ɖekaɖeka le to sia to me, bena woamã anyigba la.

english_verse: These are the men the Lord commanded to help Eleazar and Joshua divide the land for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Esiawo nye amesiwo Yehowa de se na bena, woamã domenyinu la na Israel-viwo le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: to say to them: When you receive your tribal lands, you must give towns and pastures to the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: De se na Israel-viwo bena, woana duwo Lewitɔwo ɖe woƒe anyigba dzi, ne woanɔ eme; eye miana lãnyiƒe Lewitɔwo aƒo xlã dua wo akpe ɖo.

english_verse: That way, the Levites will have towns to live in and pastures for their animals.
translation_verse: Woawo ŋutɔ nanɔ duawo me, eye woƒe agbatsɔlãwo kple lãhawo kpakple lã bubuwo nanɔ lãnyiƒeawo.

english_verse: The pasture around each of these towns must be in the shape of a square, with the town itself in the center. The pasture is to measure
translation_verse: Eye miadzidze du la ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome woakeke abɔklugui akpe eve, dziehe gome abɔklugui akpe eve, ɣetoɖoƒe gome abɔklugui akpe eve kple anyiehe gome abɔklugui akpe eve, eye du la nanɔ titina Esia anye lãnyiƒe na wo anɔ duawo ŋu.

english_verse: Six of the towns you give them will be Safe Towns where a person who has accidentally killed someone can run for protection. But you will also give the Levites
translation_verse: Eye du, siwo miatsɔ na Lewitɔwo la, dometɔ ade nanye sitsoƒeduwo, siwo me hlɔ̃dolawo nasi ayi ɖo, eye miatsɔ du blane vɔ eve akpe ɖe ŋu na wo.

english_verse: Since the towns for the Levites must come from Israel's own tribal lands, the larger tribes will give more towns than the smaller ones. The Safe Towns (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Eye mina Israel-vi, siwo ƒe anyigba lolo la, nana du geɖe, ke amesiwo tɔ le sue la, nana ʋee alesi miava xɔ anyigba lae la, nenema ŋu miana duawo Lewitɔwo ɖo. Sitsoƒewo ŋu nya.

english_verse: by one of the victim's relatives. He will take revengefor his relative's death as soon as he finds you.
translation_verse: Hlɔ̃tɔ kpɔ mɔ be, wòawu hlɔ̃dola, eye ne edo goe la, ekpɔ mɔ awui.
