english_verse: “Achan,” Joshua said, “the Lord God of Israel has decided that you are guilty. So tell me what you did, and don't try to hide anything.”
translation_verse: Tete Yosua gblɔ na Axan bena: Vinye, de bubu Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋu, eye na woakafui! Gblɔe nam dzro, nuka gɔ̃ nèwɔ? Megada alakpa nam o!

english_verse: “It's true,” Achan answered. “I sinned and disobeyed the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Axan ɖo ŋu na Yosua gblɔ bena: Nyateƒe, mewɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋu, eye ale kple ale mewɔ enye si:

english_verse: They brought them back and put them in front of the sacred chest, so Joshua and the rest of the Israelites could see them.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ wo tso agbadɔ la me va Yosua kple Israel-viwo katã ŋku me, eye wotrɔ wo kɔ de Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: Then everyone took Achan and the things he had stolen to Trouble Valley. They also took along his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and everything else that belonged to him.
translation_verse: Tete Yosua kple Israel blibo la kplɔ Axan, Zerax vi, hekpe de klosalo la, awu ʋlaya la kple sikakpɔti la kpakple viaŋutsuwo kple vinyɔnuwo, eƒe nyi, tedzi kple alẽwo, eƒe agbadɔ kpakple nusiwo katã le esi la ŋu, yi Axor-bali la me.

english_verse: Joshua said, “Achan, you caused us a lot of trouble. Now the Lord is paying you back with the same kind of trouble.” The people of Israel then stoned to death Achan and his family. They made a fire and burned the bodies, together with what Achan had stolen, and all his possessions.
translation_verse: Eye Yosua gblɔ bena: Esi nèhe dzɔgbevɔ̃e va mía dzi la, eyata Yehowa ahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ava dziwò egbea! Tete Israel blibo la ƒu kpe wo, eye wòtɔ dzo wo. Esi woƒu kpe wo vɔ la,

english_verse: They covered the remains with a big pile of rocks, which is still there. Then the Lord stopped being angry with Israel. That's how the place came to be called Trouble Valley.
translation_verse: wofɔ kpewo li kɔ gãa ɖe ɖe wo dzi, eye wòli vaseɖe egbe. Tete Yehowa ƒe dziku nu fa. Eyata wona ŋkɔ teƒe la bena Axor-balime, vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: The rest of the army will come with me and attack near the gate. When the people of Ai come out to fight, we'll run away and let them chase us. They will think we are running from them just like the first time. But when we've let them chase us far enough away,
translation_verse: bena woati mía yome, vaseɖe esime miaɖe wo atso dua mee; elabena wòabu be, ɖe míegale sisim le yewo nu abe tsã ene. Eye ne miele sisim le wo nu la,

english_verse: you come out of hiding. The Lord our God will help you capture the town.
translation_verse: ekema miawo miado te xa me aɖaxɔ du la, eye Yehowa, mia Mawu, atsɔe ade asi na mi.

english_verse: Then set it on fire, as the Lord has told us to do. Those are your orders,
translation_verse: Eye ne miexɔ dua vɔ la, ekema mitɔ dzo du la; miwɔ, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ na mi ene, kpɔ ɖa, nyee ɖe se na mi.

english_verse: Early the next morning he got his troops ready to move out, and he and the other leaders of Israel led them to Ai.
translation_verse: Tete Yosua fɔ ŋdi kanya, eye wòɖo aʋawɔlawo, eye eya kple Israel-ame tsitsiwo dze aʋawɔlawo ŋgɔ yi Ai.

english_verse: They set up camp in full view of the town, across the valley to the north.
translation_verse: Eye aʋawɔla, siwo katã le eŋu la, ho heva du la kasa, woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Ai ƒe anyiehe gome, eye ʋea ɖe tso woawo kple Ai dome.

english_verse: Now all his troops were in place. Part of the army was in the camp to the north of Ai, and the others were hiding to the west, ready to make a surprise attack. That night, Joshua went into the valley.
translation_verse: eye woɖo asaɖa blibo la ƒe aʋawɔla, siwo nɔ du la ƒe anyiehe gome, ale be eƒe mlɔenu de du la ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome Eye Yosua yi ɖe bali la me le zã ma me.

english_verse: Finally, the Lord told Joshua, “Point your sword at the town of Ai, because now I am going to help you defeat it!” As soon as Joshua pointed his sword at the town,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Yosua bena: Do akplɔ, si le asiwò la, ɖe Ai dzi, elabena matsɔe ade asi na wò! Tete Yosua do akplɔ, si le esi la, ɖe du la dzi.

english_verse: the soldiers who had been hiding jumped up and ran into the town. They captured it and set it on fire.
translation_verse: Esi wòdo eƒe asi ɖa la, xadelawo wɔ kaba tso le wo nɔƒe hege ɖe du la me, eye woxɔe, eye wòtɔ dzo du la.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the other Israelite soldiers had come from the town and attacked the men of Ai from the rear. The Israelites captured the king of Ai and brought him to Joshua. They also chased the rest of the men of Ai into the desert and killed them. The Israelite army went back to Ai and killed everyone there.
translation_verse: Esi Israel wu Aitɔwo katã le tagba le gbedzi, eye amesiwo katã ti wo yome tsi yi nu hetsrɔ̃ vɔ keŋkeŋ la, Israel blibo la trɔ ɖo ta Ai, eye wotsrɔ̃ wo kple yi.

english_verse: Joshua made sure every building in Ai was burned to the ground. He told his men to kill the king of Ai and hang his body on a tree. Then at sunset he told the Israelites to take down the body, throw it in the gateway of the town, and cover it with a big pile of rocks. Those rocks are still there, and the town itself has never been rebuilt. Joshua Reads the Blessings and Curses (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Eye wòde ka ve na Ai-fia ɖe atia ɖe ŋu vaseɖe fiẽ; eye esi ɣe ɖo to la, Yosua ɖe se be, woade eƒe kukua atsɔ ƒu gbe ɖe dua ƒe agbo nu, eye wofɔ kpewo li ko gãa ɖe ɖe edzi wòtsi anyi vaseɖe egbe. Wode gbe ƒã yayra kple fiƒode le Gerizim kple Ebal-towo dzi.

english_verse: The people of Gibeon had also heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
translation_verse: Ke esi Gibeon-tɔwo se nusi Yosua wo Yerixo kple Ai la,

english_verse: So they decided that some of their men should pretend to be messengers to Israel from a faraway country. The men put worn-out bags on their donkeys and found some old wineskins that had cracked and had been sewn back together.
translation_verse: woawo hã wɔ ayenu, eye wodzra mo dzi nuɖuɖu ɖo, wotsɔ kotoku xoxowo ɖo woƒe tedziwo dzi, eye wotso weingolo xoxo vuvu, siwo woka,

english_verse: Their sandals were old and patched, and their clothes were worn out. They even took along some dry and crumbly bread.
translation_verse: wodo atokota xoxo, siwo woka la de afɔ, woƒe awuwo do xoxo, eye abolo, siwo katã woɖo asi la, ƒu hefli keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: Then they went to the Israelite camp at Gilgal, where they said to Joshua and the men of Israel, “We have come from a country that is far from here. Please make a peace treaty with us.”
translation_verse: Eye wova Yosua gbɔ le asaɖa me le Gilgal gblɔ na eya kple Israel-ŋutsuwo bena: Anyigba didia ɖe dzi míetso va, eye miedi be, miabla nu kpli mi!

english_verse: We are your servants, and we live far from here. We came because the Lord your God is so famous. We heard what the Lord did in Egypt
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Wò dolawo tso anyigba didi booa ɖe dzi va le Yehowa, wò Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ la ta, elabena miese eŋkɔ kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ le Egipte,

english_verse: and what he did to those two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan: King Og of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, and King Sihon of Heshbon.
translation_verse: kpakple nusiwo katã wòwɔ Amoritɔwo ƒe fia eveawo le Yordan godo, siwo nye Sixon, Xesbon-fia, kple Og, Basan-fia, sina Astarot.

english_verse: Our leaders and everyone who lives in our country told us to meet with you and tell you that all of us are your servants. They said to ask you to make a peace treaty with our people. They told us to be sure and take along enough food for our journey.
translation_verse: Eyata miaƒe ame tsitsiwo kple anyigbadzitɔwo katã gblɔ na mi bena: Mido mo dzi nuɖuɖu asi, miyi ɖakpe wo, eye migblɔ na wo bena: Miaƒe dolawo míenye, eyata mibla nu kpli mí!

english_verse: See this dry, crumbly bread of ours? It was hot out of the oven when we packed the food on the day we left our homes.
translation_verse: Esi miele mo dzi dze ge ava mia gbɔ la, eya mietsɔ abolo siawo dzodzo le míaƒe xɔwo me ɖo asi, ke azɔ la woƒu hefli keŋkeŋ:

english_verse: These cracked wineskins were new when we filled them, and our clothes and sandals are worn out because we have traveled so far.
translation_verse: míaƒe weingolo siawo la yeye wole, hafi míeku wein ɖe wo me, ke azɔ la wovuvu, eye míaƒe avɔ kple atokota siawo do xoxo, le esi mɔa didi akpa ta.

english_verse: The Israelites tried some of the food, but they did not ask the Lord if he wanted them to make a treaty.
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsuawo xɔ woƒe mɔ dzi nuɖuɖuawo, gake womebia gbe Yehowa se o.

english_verse: So Joshua made a peace treaty with the messengers and promised that Israel would not kill their people. Israel's leaders swore that Israel would keep this promise.
translation_verse: Eye Yosua wo xɔlɔ̃ kpli wo hebla nu kpli wo be, yeana woatsi agbe, eye ameha la ƒe amegãwo ka atam na wo.

english_verse: But they did not attack the towns, because the Israelite leaders had sworn in the name of the Lord that they would let these people live. The Israelites complained about their leaders' decision not to attack,
translation_verse: Ke Israel-viwo mesi wo o, elabena ameha la ƒe amegãwo la Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, na wo. Esi ameha blibo la li amegãwo ŋu la,

english_verse: Joshua told some of his soldiers, “I want to meet with the Gibeonite leaders. Bring them here.” When the Gibeonites came, Joshua said, “You live close to us. Why did you lie by claiming you lived far away?
translation_verse: Tete Yosua yɔ wo gblɔ na wo bena: Nukaŋuti mieble mí gblɔ bena, didiƒe ke yewotso, evɔ wònye mietsɔ ɖe mia gbɔ hafi?

english_verse: So now you are under a curse, and from now on your people will have to send workers to cut wood and carry water for the place of worship.”
translation_verse: Eyata aɖi mia ŋu, eye dɔlawo, naketɔlawo kple tɔmedelawo na nye Mawu ƒe aƒe la mavɔ le mia dome akpɔ o!

english_verse: The Gibeonites answered, “The Lord your God told his servant Moses that you were to kill everyone who lives here and take their land for yourselves. We were afraid you would kill us, and so we tricked you into making a peace treaty. But we agreed to be your servants,
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu na Yosua bena: Ɖe wogblɔ na wò dɔlawo bena, Yehowa, wò Mawu, de se na eƒe dɔla Mose be, yeatsɔ anyigba blibo la na mi, eye yeatsrɔ̃ anyigbadzitɔwo katã le mia ŋgɔ, eye mieva be, miava wu mí, eyata miewɔ alea ɖo.

english_verse: and you are strong enough to do anything to us that you want. We just ask you to do what seems right.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, miele asiwò me, alesi dzɔ, eye wònyo ŋuwò nebe, yeawɔ mí ko la, wɔ mí!

english_verse: Joshua did not let the Israelites kill the Gibeonites,
translation_verse: Eye wòwɔ wo nenema heɖe wo tso Israel-viwo si me, ale be womewu wo o.

english_verse: King Adonizedek of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured and destroyed the town of Ai, and then killed its king as he had done at Jericho. He also learned that the Gibeonites had signed a peace treaty with Israel.
translation_verse: Esi Yerusalem-fia Adonizedek se bena, Yosua xɔ Ai, eye wòtsrɔ̃e gbidigbidi, ewɔ Ai kple eme fia, abe alesi wòwɔ Yerixo kple eme fia ene, eye Gibeontɔwo wɔ xɔlɔ̃ kple Israel, eye wole wo dome la,

english_verse: So Adonizedek sent messages to the kings of four other towns: King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon. The messages said,
translation_verse: Tete Yerusalem-fia Adonizedek dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Xebron-fia Hoham, Yarmut-fia Piram, Laxis-fia Yafia kpakple Eglon-fia Debir gbɔ gblɔ bena:

english_verse: “The Gibeonites have signed a peace treaty with Joshua and the Israelites. Come and help me attack Gibeon!”
translation_verse: Miho va kpe ɖe ŋunye, ne miasi Gibeon, elabena ewɔ xɔlɔ̃ kple Yosua kpakple Israel-viwo.

english_verse: the Gibeonites sent a message to the Israelite camp at Gilgal: “Joshua, please come and rescue us! The Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together and are attacking us. We are your servants, so don't let us down. Please hurry!”
translation_verse: Tete Gibeontɔwo ɖo ame ɖo ɖe Yosua le Gilgal le asaɖa me gblɔ bena: Megaɖe asi le wò dɔlawo ŋu o, va mía gbɔ kaba naxɔ na mi, eye nakpe ɖe mía ŋu, elabena Amoritɔwo ƒe fia, siwo katã le towo dzi la, ƒo ta kpli ɖe mía ŋu.

english_verse: Joshua and his army, including his best warriors, left Gilgal.
translation_verse: Enumake Yosua kple eƒe aʋakɔ la katã kpakple kalẽtɔwo katã ho tso Gilgal.

english_verse: “Joshua,” the Lord said, “don't be afraid of the Amorites. They will run away when you attack, and I will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Yosua bena. Megavɔ̃ o, elabena matsɔ wo ade asi na wò, eye wo dometɔa ɖeke manɔ te ɖe ŋuwò o.

english_verse: Joshua marched all night from Gilgal to Gibeon and made a surprise attack on the Amorite camp.
translation_verse: Tete Yosua va ƒo ɖe wo dzi kpoyi, elabena ezɔ zã blibo la tso Gilgal.

english_verse: The Lord made the enemy panic, and the Israelites started killing them right and left. They chased the Amorite troops up the road to Beth-Horon and kept on killing them, until they reached the towns of Azekah and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa na wolulu le Israel ŋku me, eye wòsi wo le Gibeon gbɔ tɔtɔtɔ, eye woli wo yome vaseɖe Bet-Xoron-mɔ dzi, eye wòsi wo vaseɖe Aseka kple Makeda ke.

english_verse: And while these troops were going down through Beth-Horon Pass, the Lord made huge hailstones fall on them all the way to Azekah. More of the enemy soldiers died from the hail than from the Israelite weapons.
translation_verse: Esi wosi le Israel nu hele Bet-Xoron-to ƒe abu ɖim la, Yehowa hlẽ kpe gãwo ɖe wo dzi tso dziƒo vaseɖe Aseka, eye woku; amesiwo kpetsiawo wu la sɔ gbɔ wu esiwo Israel-viwo wu kple yi.

english_verse: Never before and never since has the Lord done anything like that for someone who prayed. The Lord was really fighting for Israel.
translation_verse: Eye ŋkekea ɖeke meɖo ŋgɔ nɛ alo va le emegbe de esia nu, esi Yehowa ɖo to amegbetɔ ƒe gbe o; elabena Yehowa wɔ aʋa na Israel.

english_verse: After the battle, Joshua and the Israelites went back to their camp at Gilgal. Joshua Kills the Five Enemy Kings
translation_verse: Eye Yosua kple Israel blibo la gbugbɔ va asaɖa la me le Gilgal.

english_verse: While the enemy soldiers were running from the Israelites, the five enemy kings ran away and hid in a cave near Makkedah.
translation_verse: Ke fia atɔ mawo si yi ɖaɣla ɖe do me le Makeda.

english_verse: Joshua's soldiers told him, “The five kings have been found in a cave near Makkedah.”
translation_verse: Eye wova gblɔ na Yosua bena, wokpɔ fia atɔ̃awo woɣla ɖe do me le Makeda.

english_verse: Joshua answered, “Roll some big stones over the mouth of the cave and leave a few soldiers to guard it.
translation_verse: Yosua ɖo ŋu be: Mimli kpe gãwo tu do la nu, eye miɖe ŋutsuwo ɖo enu, bena woadzɔ wo ŋu.

english_verse: But you and everyone else must keep going after the enemy troops, because they will be safe if they reach their walled towns. Don't let them get away! The Lord our God is helping us get rid of them.”
translation_verse: Ke miawo migatɔ o, hafi boŋ miti miaƒe futɔwo yome, mitsrɔ woƒe megbexeawo, eye migana woage ɖe woƒe duwo me o, elabena Yehowa, mia Mawu, tsɔ wo ɖe asi na mi.

english_verse: So Joshua and the Israelites almost wiped out the enemy soldiers. Only a few safely reached their walled towns.
translation_verse: Eye esi Yosua kple Israel-viwo si wo vɔ hetsrɔ̃ wo, eye ame mlɔeawo si yi ɖe ɖu sesẽwo me la,

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp at Makkedah, where Joshua was waiting for them. No one around there dared say anything bad about the Israelites.
translation_verse: dukɔ blibo la gbugbɔ va Yosua gbɔ le Makeda le asaɖa me dedie, eye amea ɖeke medo dzi ke fi ɖe Israel-viwo ŋu o.

english_verse: Joshua told his soldiers, “Now, move the rocks from the entrance to the cave and bring those five kings to me.”
translation_verse: Eye Yosua gblɔ bena: Miɖe nu le doa nu, eye mikplɔ fia atɔ̃awo tso doa me va gbɔnye!

english_verse: The soldiers opened the entrance to the cave and brought out the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
translation_verse: Tete wowɔ nenema, eye wokplɔ fia atɔ̃awo tso ɖoa me va egbɔe; woawo nye: Yerusalem-fia, Xebron-fia, Yarmut-fia, Laxis-fia kple Eglon-fia.

english_verse: After Joshua had called the army together, he forced the five kings to lie down on the ground. Then he called his officers forward and told them, “You fought these kings along with me, so put your feet on their necks.” The officers did this,
translation_verse: Esi wokplɔ fia atɔ̃ siawo va Yosua gbɔ la, Yosua yɔ Israel-ŋutsuwo katã, eye wògblɔ na aʋakɔ la kplɔlawo, amesiwo ɖe aʋa la kplii bena: Mile va, eye miɖo afɔ ve dzi na fia siawo! Tete wote va, eye woɖo afɔ ve dzi na wo.

english_verse: and Joshua continued, “Don't ever be afraid or discouraged. Be brave and strong. This is what the Lord will do to all your enemies.”
translation_verse: Eye Yosua gblɔ na wo bena: Migavɔ̃ o, eye dzika megatso mia ƒo o, milé dzi ɖe ƒo, eye mise ŋu! Elabena alea Yehowa awɔ miaƒe futɔ, siwo katã mia kple wo miele aʋa wo ge lae.

english_verse: Joshua killed the five kings and told his men to hang each body on a tree. Then at sunset
translation_verse: Emegbe Yosua wu wo, eye wòde ka ve na wo ɖe ati alɔ̃ ŋu; eye wotsi atiawo ŋu vaseɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: he told some of his troops, “Take the bodies down and throw them into the cave where the kings were found. Cover the entrance to the cave with big rocks.” Joshua's troops obeyed his orders, and those rocks are still there. Joshua Continues the Fighting
translation_verse: Eye esi ɣe yina to ɖo ge la, Yosua ɖe se bena, woaɖe wo le atiawo ŋu atsɔ aƒu gbe ɖe do, si me woyia ɖo la me, eye wòfɔ kpe gãwo ɖo do la nu wotsi anyi vaseɖe egbe. Yosua gaɖu du bubuwo dzi.

english_verse: Later that day, Joshua captured Makkedah and killed its king and everyone else in the town, just as he had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Eye Yosua xɔ Makeda le ŋkeke ma ke dzi; ewu wo kple yi, eye wotsrɔ̃ eme fia kple amesiwo katã le eme la gbidigbidi, eye mena amea ɖeke si o, eye wòwɔ Makeda-fia, abe alesi wòwɔ Yerixo-fia ene.

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Makkedah and attacked the town of Libnah.
translation_verse: Eye Yosua, kple Israel blibo la ho tso Makeda heyi Libna, eye wòwɔ aʋa kple Libna.

english_verse: The Lord let them capture the town and its king, and they killed the king and everyone else, just as they had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa tsɔ eya hã kple eme fia ɖe asi na Israel, eye wotsrɔ̃e kple eme nɔlawo katã kple yi; womèna amea ɖeke si o, eye wowɔ eme fia, abe alesi wowɔ Yerixo-fia ene.

english_verse: Joshua then led his army to Lachish, and they set up camp around the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Eyome Yosua kple Israel blibo la ho tso Libna yi Laxis, eye woɖe to ɖee hewɔ aʋa kplii.

english_verse: and the next day the Lord let them capture the town. They killed everyone, as they had done at Libnah.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa tso Laxis de asi na Israel, eye woxɔe le ŋkeke eveagbe, eye wotsrɔ̃e kple eme nɔlawo kple yi, abe alesi wowɔ Libna ke ene.

english_verse: King Horam of Gezer arrived to help Lachish, but Joshua and his troops attacked and destroyed him and his army.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi Horam, Gezer-fia ho, be yeava xɔ na Laxis, ke Yosua si eya hã kple eƒe dukɔ la, vaseɖe esime amea ɖeke mekpɔtɔ o.

english_verse: From Lachish, Joshua took his troops to Eglon, where they set up camp surrounding the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Emegbe Yosua kple Israel blibo la ho tso Laxis yi Eglon, eye woɖe to ɖee hewɔ aʋa kplii,

english_verse: captured it that same day, then killed everyone, as they had done at Lachish.
translation_verse: eye woxɔe le ŋkeke ma dzi hetsrɔ̃e kple yi, eye wotsrɔ̃ amesiwo katã le eme la gbemagbe gbidigbidi, abe alesi wowɔ Laxis ke ene.

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Eglon and attacked Hebron.
translation_verse: Tete Yosua kple Israel blibo la ho tso Eglon heyi Xebron, eye wowɔ aʋa kplii,

english_verse: They captured the town and the nearby villages, then killed everyone, including the king. They destroyed Hebron in the same way they had destroyed Eglon.
translation_verse: eye woxɔe hetsrɔ̃e kple eme fia, eƒe duwo katã kple wo me nɔlawo kple yi; mena amea ɖeke si o, abe alesi wowɔ Eglon ene, eye wotsɔe kple eme nɔlawo gbidigbidi.

english_verse: Joshua and the Israelite army turned and attacked Debir.
translation_verse: Eyome Yosua kple Israel blibo la trɔ yi Debir ɖawɔ aʋa kplii,

english_verse: They captured the town, and its nearby villages. Then they destroyed Debir and killed its king, together with everyone else, just as they had done with Hebron and Libnah.
translation_verse: eye woɖu eya hã kple eme fia kpakple eƒe duwo katã dzi, eye wowu wo kple yi hetsrɔ̃ amesiwo katã le eme lã gbidigbidi, eye mena amea ɖeke si o, alesi wowɔ Xebron la, nenema wowɔ Debir kple eme fia hãe, abe alesi wowɔ Libna kple eme fia ene.

english_verse: Joshua captured towns everywhere in the land: In the central hill country and the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert and the region that slopes down toward the Dead Sea. Whenever he captured a town, he would kill the king and everyone else, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
translation_verse: Ale Yosua du anyigba blibo la kple fia, siwo katã le towo dzi, dziehe, gbadzaƒe kple towo ŋu la dzi; mena amea ɖeke si o, eye wòtsrɔ̃ nu gbagbewo katã gbidigbidi, abe alesi Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, de se ene.

english_verse: Joshua wiped out towns from Kadesh-Barnea to Gaza, everywhere in the region of Goshen, and as far north as Gibeon.
translation_verse: Eye Yosua ɖu wo dzi tso Kades-Barnea vaseɖe Gaza, tso Gosen-nyigba blibo la dzi vaseɖe Gibeon.

english_verse: the kings in the northern hill country and in the Jordan River valley south of Lake Galilee, and the kings in the foothills and in Naphath-Dor to the west.
translation_verse: kple fia, siwo le anyiehe gome le towo dzi, tagba, si le Kinerot ƒe dziehe gome, gbadzaƒe kple Nafot-Dor le ɣetoɖoƒe

english_verse: He sent messages to the Canaanite kings in the east and the west, to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite kings in the hill country, and to the Hivite kings in the region of Mizpah, near the foot of Mount Hermon.
translation_verse: kpakple Kanaanitɔ, siwo le ɣedzeƒe kple ɣetoɖoƒe. Amoritɔwo, Xititɔwo, Perizitɔwo kple Yebusitɔwo, siwo le towo dzi, kpakple Xiwitɔwo, siwo le Xermon te le Mizpa-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua: Don't let them frighten you! I'll help you defeat them, and by this time tomorrow they will be dead. When you attack, the first thing you have to do is to cripple their horses. Then after the battle is over, burn their chariots.
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa gblɔ na Yosua bena Megavɔ̃ wo o, elabena mana wo katã natsrɔ̃ le Israel ŋgɔ etsɔ wɔle siawo; natu ata na woƒe sɔwo, eye natɔ dzo woƒe tasiaɖamwo.

english_verse: Joshua and his army made a surprise attack against the enemy camp at Merom Pond
translation_verse: Tete Yosua kple aʋawɔlawo katã va ƒo ɖe wo dzi le Merom-tɔ la nu kpoyi, eye wodze wo dzi.

english_verse: Up to this time, the king of Hazor had controlled the kingdoms that had joined together to attack Israel, so Joshua led his army back and captured Hazor. They killed its king
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi ke Yosua trɔ va xɔ Xazor, eye wowu eme fia kple yi, elabena tsã la Xazor enye ta na fiaɖuƒe siawo katã.

english_verse: Joshua and his army took control of the northern and southern hill country, the foothills to the west, the Southern Desert, the whole region of Goshen, and the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Ale Yosua xɔ anyigba blibo la, toawo kple dziehe gome katã, Gosen-nyigba blibo la kple gbadzaƒe la, tagba la kple Israel-toawo kpakple wo ŋu balimewo,

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he wanted the towns in this region destroyed and their people killed without mercy. That's why the Lord made the people in the towns stubborn and determined to fight Israel. The only town that signed a peace treaty with Israel was the Hivite town of Gibeon. The Israelite army captured the rest of the towns in battle.
translation_verse: Elabena Yehowa gbɔ wòtso be, woƒe dzime sẽ, eye woho aʋa ɖe Israel ŋu, ne woatsrɔ̃ wo gbidigbidi, womave wo nu o, ke boŋ woatsrɔ̃ wo, abe alesi Yehowa de se na Mose ene.

english_verse: During this same time, Joshua and his army killed the Anakim from the northern and southern hill country. They also destroyed the towns where the Anakim had lived, including Hebron, Debir, and Anab.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi Yosua va tsrɔ̃ Enakitɔwo ɖa le toawo dzi le Xebron, Debir, Anab kple Yuda-towo kpakple Israel-towo katã dzi, eye Yosua tsrɔ̃ wo kple woƒe duwo gbidigbidi.

english_verse: There were not any Anakim left in the regions where the Israelites lived, although there were still some in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
translation_verse: Enakitɔa ɖeke mekpɔtɔ ɖe Israel-viwo ƒe anyigba dzi o, negbe Gaza, Gad kple Asdod ko ɖewo susɔ ɖo.

english_verse: That's how Joshua captured the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua divided it up among the tribes. Finally, there was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Ale Yosua xɔ anyigba blibo la, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ na Mose pɛpɛpɛ ene, eye Yosua mãe na Israel, to sia to kple etɔ, eye anyigba la kpɔ gbɔdzɔe tso aʋawɔwɔ me.

english_verse: Before Moses died, he and the people of Israel had defeated two kings east of the Jordan River. These kings had ruled the region from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, including the eastern side of the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Esiawo nye anyigba dzi fia, siwo dzi Israel-viwo ɖu, amesiwo ƒe anyigba woxɔ le Yordan godo le ɣedzeƒe gome, tso Arnon-tɔʋu la nu vaseɖe Xermon-to la gbɔ kple gbadzaƒe blibo, si le ɣedzeƒe:

english_verse: Sihon also controlled the eastern side of the Jordan River valley from Lake Galilee south to Beth-Jeshimoth and the Dead Sea. In addition to these regions, he ruled the town called Slopes of Mount Pisgah and the land south of there at the foot of the hill.
translation_verse: tso gbadzaƒe heyi Kinerot-ƒu la nu le ɣedzeƒe heva tagbaƒu, si nye Dzeƒu la nu, le ɣedzeƒe heɖo ta Bet-Yesimot, vaseɖe Pisga ƒe aga nu le dziehe.

english_verse: His kingdom stretched north to Mount Hermon, east to the town of Salecah, and included the land of Bashan as far west as the borders of the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. He also ruled the northern half of Gilead.
translation_verse: amesi ƒe dziɖuƒe nye Xermon-to, Salxa kple Basan blibo la, vaseɖe Gesuritɔwo kple Maaxati-tɔwo ƒe liƒo ŋu kple Gilead afã heva ke ɖe Sixon, Xesbon-fia, ƒe anyigba ŋu.

english_verse: Moses, the Lord's servant, had led the people of Israel in defeating Sihon and Og. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe dɔla Mose kple Israel-viwo ɖu wo dzi, eye Yehowa ƒe dɔla Mose tsɔe na Ruben-viwo, Gad-viwo kple Manase ƒe to afã wònye wo tɔ.

english_verse: Many years later, the Lord told Joshua: Now you are very old, but there is still a lot of land that Israel has not yet taken.
translation_verse: Esi Yosua tsi xɔ ƒe geɖe la, Yehowa gblɔ nɛ bena: Etsi, eye nèxɔ ƒe geɖe; anyigba geɖe kpɔtɔ womexɔ haɖe o.

english_verse: Moses had already given land east of the Jordan River to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Elabena Manase ƒe afã, Ruben-viwo kple Gad-viwo xa woƒe anyigba, si Mose tsɔ na wo le Yordan godo le ɣedzeƒe, abe alesi Yehowa ƒe dɔla Mose tsɔe na wo ene:

english_verse: This region stretched north from the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, and included the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley. It covered the flatlands of Medeba north of Dibon,
translation_verse: tso Aroer, si le Arnon-tɔʋu la nu kple du, si le bali lãme gbɔ kpakple Medeba-tagba blibo la vaseɖe Dibon;

english_verse: and took in the towns that had belonged to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon. Some of these towns were as far east as the Ammonite border.
translation_verse: Sixon, Amoritɔwo ƒe fia, si ɖu fia le Xesbon la, ƒe duwo katã vaseɖe Amon-viwo ƒe liƒo ŋu;

english_verse: However, the Israelites did not force the people of Geshur and Maacah to leave, and they still live there among the Israelites. Why Moses Did Not Give Land to the Levi Tribe
translation_verse: Ke Israel-viwo menyã Gesuritɔwo kple Maaxatitɔwo o, eyata Gesur kple Maaxat tsi Israel dome vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.” The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
translation_verse: Negbe Lewi-to la ko metsɔ anyigba ɖeke na o, elabena Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, ƒe dzovɔsa nye eƒe domenyinu, abe alesi wògblɔ nɛ ene. To eve kple afi ƒe domenyinu le Yordan godo.

english_verse: Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Eye Mose na anyigba Ruben-viwo ƒe to la ɖe woƒe ƒomewo nu,

english_verse: The Amorite King Sihon had lived in Heshbon and had ruled the towns in the flatlands. Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth. Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
translation_verse: tagba duwo katã kple Sixon, Amoritɔwo ƒe fia, si ɖu fia le Xesbon ƒe fiaɖuƒe blibo la; Mose ɖu dzi hekpe ɖe Midian amegãwo ŋu, siwo nye: Ewi, Rekem, Zur, Xur kple Reba, amesiwo nye Sixon ƒe amegãwo, siwo nɔ anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo wu bokɔ Bileam, Beor vi, kple yi hekpe ɖe ame bubu, siwo wowu la ŋu.

english_verse: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
translation_verse: Ale Yordan kple eŋu nyigba ɖo liƒo na Ruben-viwo. Esia nye Ruben-viwo ƒe anyigba, duwo kple kɔƒewo le woƒe ƒomewo nu.

english_verse: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Eye Mose na anyigba Gad-viwo ƒe to la de woƒe ƒomeawo nu.

english_verse: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
translation_verse: tso Xesbon vaseɖe Ramat-Mizpa kple Betonim, eye tso Maxanayim vaseɖe Debir ƒe liƒo ŋu;

english_verse: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
translation_verse: Bel-Haram, Bet-Nimra, Sukot kple Zafon, siwo le bali la me, woawo nye Sixon, Xesbon-fia, ƒe fiaɖuƒe kpɔtɔea, Yordan kple eŋu nyigba, vaseɖe Kineret-ta ƒe mlɔenu, le Yordan ƒe go keme dzi le ɣedzeƒe gome.

english_verse: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
translation_verse: Esia nye Gad-viwo ƒe anyigba, duwo kple kɔƒewo le woƒe ƒomewo nu.

english_verse: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Eye Mose na anyigba Manase-viwo ƒe to afã le woƒe ƒomeawo nu:

english_verse: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
translation_verse: Ke Mose mena anyigbaa ɖeke Lewi-to la o, elabena Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, ŋutɔ nye woƒe domenyinu, abe alesi wògblɔ na wo ene.

english_verse: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
translation_verse: Tete Yuda-viwo va Yosua gbɔ le Gilgal, eye Kaleb, Yefune vi, si nye Kenizitɔ la, gblɔ nɛ bena: Enya nya, si Yehowa gblɔ na Mose, Mawu ƒe ame la, le mía kpli wo ŋuti le Kades-Barnea.

english_verse: The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God.
translation_verse: Ke nɔvinye, siwo ɖe kplim la, ɖe dzi le dukɔ la ƒo; gake nye la medze Yehowa, nye Mawu la yome blibo.

english_verse: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
translation_verse: Tete Mose ka atam gbemagbe gblɔ bena; Anyigba, si dzi neɖo afɔe la, anye mia kple viwòwo ƒe domenyinu tegbee, elabena edze Yehowa, nye Mawu la yome blibo.

english_verse: So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Eyata tsɔ tonyigba sia, si ŋu Yehowa ƒo nu le gbemagbe la nam; elabena wò ŋutɔ èsee gbemagbe bena, Enakitɔwo le afima, eye duawo lolo hesesẽ. Ɖewohĩ Yehowa anɔ kplim, be manyã wo, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ ene.

english_verse: Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants.
translation_verse: Tete Yosua yrae, eye wòtsɔ Xebron na Kaleb, Yefune vi la, ne wòanye eƒe domenyinu.

english_verse: And Hebron still belongs to Caleb's descendants, because he was faithful to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Eyata Xebron zu Kaleb, Yefune vi, si nye Kenizitɔ la, ƒe domenyinu vaseɖe egbe, elabena edze Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la yome blibo.

english_verse: Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim. There was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Woyɔ Xebron tsã bena Araba ƒe du, amesi nye ame gãtɔ le Enakitɔwo dome. Eye anyigba la kpɔ gbɔdzɔe tso aʋawɔwɔ me.

english_verse: Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Woƒe dzieheliƒo tso Dzeƒu la ƒe mlɔenu, afisi ƒu la wɔ adɔ̃ nyẽ kpo ɖe dziehe gome le,

english_verse: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
translation_verse: eye wòva to Akrabim-to ƒe dziehe gome vaseɖe Zin, eye wòmlo va zɔ Kades-Barnea ƒe dziehe vaseɖe Xezron, eto Adar hegɔdɔ̃ mɔ to Karka

english_verse: and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
translation_verse: vaseɖe Azmon, eye wòzɔ Egipte-tɔʋu la ŋu va wu nu ɖe ƒu nu. Esia nye miaƒe dzieheliƒo.

english_verse: Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea. The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ɣedzeƒeliƒo tso Dzeƒu la nu vaseɖe Yordan nu, eye anyieheliƒo tso adɔ̃, si le Yordan ƒe mlɔenu la nu

english_verse: From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: vaseɖe Bet-Xogla, eye wòmlo zã Bet-Araba ƒe anyiehe to Bohan, Ruben vi, ƒe kpe la gbɔ

english_verse: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
translation_verse: hezɔ Axor-bali la me vaseɖe Debir, eye wònyè kpo to Gilgal, si le Adumim-to dzi mo kasa la, ƒe anyiehe le tonu la ƒe dziehe gome; emegbe liƒo la va to En-Semes-tɔ la ŋu va ke ɖe Rogel ƒe vudo la gbɔ.

english_verse: and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites. Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Eye liƒo la zɔ Ben-Hinom-bali la me va to Yebusitɔwo ƒe to la ŋu le dziehe, esia nye Yerusalem; eyome liƒo la zɔ to, si le Hinom-bali la nu le ɣetoɖoƒe gome la tame le Refaim-bali la ƒe mlɔenu le anyiehe gome,

english_verse: At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
translation_verse: eye wòtso to sia tame va to Neftoax ƒe tsivudo la gbɔ heɖo ta ɖu, siwo le Efron-to dzi la gbɔ vaseɖe Baala, esia nye Kiryat-Yearim.

english_verse: From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah.
translation_verse: Eye liƒo la tro tso Baala ɖo ta Seir-to gbɔ le ɣetoɖoƒe heva zɔ Har-Yearim-to la ŋu le anyiehe, esia nye Kesalon, eye wòmlo to Bet-Semes vaseɖe Timna.

english_verse: It continued along to the hillside north of Ekron, curved around to Shikkeron, and then went to Mount Baalah. After going to Jabneel, the border finally ended at the Mediterranean Sea,
translation_verse: Emegbe liƒo la zɔ Ekron-to la ŋu le anyiehe vaseɖe Sikron, eye wòmlo to Baala-to la tame ɖo ta Yabneel va wu nu ɖe ƒu nu.

english_verse: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Emegbe woho aʋa ɖe Debirtɔwo ŋu; tsã la woyia Debir bena Kiryat-Sefer.

english_verse: Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
translation_verse: Eye Yosua tso Arba, Enakitɔwo fofo, ƒe du, si nye Xebron la na Kaleb, Yefune vi, ɖe Yuda viwo dome, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ ne ene.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
translation_verse: Eye Kaleb nyã Enakitɔ etɔ̃ Sesai, Aximan kple Talmai, amesiwo Enak ŋutɔ dzi la ɖa tso afima.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Eye Kaleb gblɔ bena: Amesi ke aɖu Kiryat-Sefer dzi, eye wòaxɔe la, matsɔ vinyenyɔnu Axsa nɛ wòaɖe.

english_verse: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, and Caleb let him marry Achsah.
translation_verse: Esi Otniel, Kaleb nɔvi Kenas ƒe viŋutsu, xɔe la, etsɔ vianyɔnu Axsa nɛ wòɖe.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Eye esi wòkplɔe la, nyɔnu la ɖo dali nɛ be, yeaɖabia agble ye fofo, eye wòɖi tso tedzi la dzi; tete Kaleb biae bena: Nya kae le asiwò?

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond. Towns in Judah's Land
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu be: Yram, elabena ètsɔ dziehenyigba nam xoxo, eyata tso tsivudoawo hã nam! Tete Kaleb tso vudo, siwo le to dzi kple bali me la nɛ.

english_verse: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
translation_verse: Esia nye Yuda-viwo ƒe to la ƒe anyigba le woƒe ƒomeawo nu.

english_verse: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
translation_verse: Lebaot, Silxim, Ain kple Rimon. Wo katã le du blaetɔ̃ vɔ asieke hekpe ɖe woƒe koƒewo ŋu.

english_verse: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: Saarayim, Aditayim, Gedera kple Gederotayim. Wole du wuiene hekpe ɖe woƒe koƒewo ŋu.

english_verse: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: Gederot, Bet-Dagon, Naama kple Makeda. Wole du wuiade hekpe ɖe woƒe koƒewo ŋu.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_verse: Ke Yuda-viwo mete ŋu nyã Yebusitɔ, siwo le Yerusalem la ɖa o, eyata Yebusitɔwo tsi Yerusalem le Yuda-viwo dome vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon
translation_verse: Efrayim-viwo ƒe anyigba enye si le woƒe ƒomeawo nu. Woƒe anyigba la ƒe ɣedzeƒeliƒo tso Aterot-Adar vaseɖe Bet-Xoron ƒe dzigbe gome

english_verse: Ephraim also had some towns and villages that were inside Manasseh's tribal land.
translation_verse: hekpe ɖe du, siwo katã wotia le Manase-viwo ƒe anyigba dzi na Efrayim-viwo la ŋuti.

english_verse: Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ke Womenya Kanaanitɔ, siwo nɔ Geser la ɖa o, eyata Kanaanitɔwo tsi Efrayim dome vaseɖe egbe, eye wona wowɔ dɔ na wo yaka.

english_verse: The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
translation_verse: Tapuax-nyigba enye Manase tɔ, ke Tapuax, si le Manase ƒe liƒo dzi la, enye Efrayim-viwo tɔ.

english_verse: Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands: Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
translation_verse: Du, siwo nye Manase tɔ, le Isaxar kple Aser gbɔ, wonye: Bet-Sean kple eƒe duwo, Yibleam kple eƒe duwo hekpe ɖe Dortɔwo kple woƒe duwo ŋu; En-Dortɔwo kple woƒe duwo, Tanaxtɔwo kple woƒe duwo kpakple Megidotɔwo kple woƒe duwo, woawo nye togbɛ etɔ̃awo.

english_verse: But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them.
translation_verse: Ke Manase mete ŋu xɔ ɖu siawo o, ale Kanaanitɔwo do dzi nɔ anyigba sia dzi bɛ.

english_verse: When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave. Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
translation_verse: Gake esi ŋusẽ va ɖo Israel-viwo ŋu la, wona Kanaanitɔwo wɔ dɔ na wo yaka; ke ɖeko womenya wo o.

english_verse: One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
translation_verse: Eye Yosef-viwo gblɔ na Yosua bena: Nukaŋuti nèna anyigba kple gome ɖeka pɛ ko mi, evɔ míesɔ gbɔ, eye Yehowa yra mí vaseɖe fifi hafi?

english_verse: Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
translation_verse: Yosua ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Ne míesɔ gbɔ la, ekema miyi Filistitɔwo kple Refaitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, eye miƒo aveawo ɖa le afima; elabena Efrayim-to la xaxa na mi akpa.

english_verse: “Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
translation_verse: Tete Yosef-viwo gblɔ bena: To la menya de mia nu-o, evɔ galasiaɖamwo hã le Kanaanitɔ, siwo katã le bali la me kple esiwo le Bet-Sean kple eƒe duwo me kpakple esiwo le Yezreel gbadzaƒe la si.

english_verse: “Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful,
translation_verse: Yosua gblɔ na Yosef ƒe aƒe, si nye Efrayim kple Manase bena: Miesɔ gbɔ, eye ŋusẽ geɖe le mia ŋu; menye gome ɖeka koe anɔ mia si o;

english_verse: so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_verse: ke boŋ mixɔ tonyigba la, eye miƒo aveawo ɖa le edzi, eye wòanye mia tɔ vaseɖe eƒe mlɔenu. Elabena mianyã Kanaanitɔ, siwo si gatasiaɖamwo le, eye ŋusẽ le wo ŋu la ɖa.

english_verse: After Israel had captured the land, they met at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Esi anyigba la na ta wo vɔ la, Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la va kpe ta ɖe Silo, eye wotu Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la ɖe afima.

english_verse: There were still seven tribes without any land,
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ƒe to adre susɔ, siwo womemã anyigba na haɖe o.

english_verse: Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsuawo dze mɔ heyi, eye Yosua de se na amesiwo yina anyigba la de ge agbalẽ me la bena: Miyi ɖatsa le anyigba la dzi, eye miŋlɔe tsɔ ve nam, ekema madzidze nu ɖe dzi na mi le Yehowa ŋku me le Silo.

english_verse: The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Ale ŋutsuawo yi ɖatsa le anyigba la dzi, eye womãe ɖe akpa adre me le woƒe duwo nu heŋlɔe tsɔ vɛ na Yosua le asaɖa me le Silo.

english_verse: Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided. Benjamin's Land
translation_verse: Tete Yosua dzidze nu ɖe dzi na wo le Yehowa ŋku me le Silo, eye wòmã anyigba la na Israel-viwo wo tɔ wo tɔe. Benyamin ƒe domenyinu.

english_verse: Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north.
translation_verse: Wodzidze nu ɖe Benyamin-viwo ƒe to la dzi le woƒe ƒomewo nu, eye anyigba, si ge ɖe wo si me la, le Yuda-viwo kple Yosef-viwo dome.

english_verse: Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert.
translation_verse: Woƒe anyieheliƒo tso Yordan nu zɔ Yerixo-to la ƒe anyiehe heto toawo dzi le ɣetoɖoƒe gome, eye wòva ke ɖe Bet-Awen-gbedzi;

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town. These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ɣetoɖoƒeliƒo la nyẽ kpo ɖo ta dziehe tso to, siwo le Bet-Xoron kasa la ƒe dziehe heva wu nu ɖe Kiryat-Baal, eya nye Kiryat-Yearim, si nye Yuda-viwo ƒe ɖu; esia nye ɣetoɖoƒekpa.

english_verse: Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring.
translation_verse: Dziehekpa tso Kirvat-Yearim ƒe mlɔenu ɖo ta ɣetoɖoƒe gome heva se Neftoax ƒe tsivudo la gbɔ;

english_verse: From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
translation_verse: eye liƒo la trɔ va zɔ to, si le Efrayim-tagba ƒe anyiehe le Ben-Hinom-bali la kasa la ƒe mlɔenu, eye wòzɔ Hinom-bali la me heto Yebusitɔwo ƒe to la ŋu vaseɖe Rogel ƒe vudo la gbɔ,

english_verse: At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: eye wòtrɔ ɖo ta anyiehe gome va to En-Semes heto Gelilot ŋu le Adumim-to dzi mɔ kasa, eye wòva to Bohan, Ruben vi ƒe kpe la gbɔ

english_verse: The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: hezɔ to la ŋu le gbadzaƒe la ƒe anyiehe vaseɖe Araba.

english_verse: Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Eye liƒo la va to Bet-Xogla-to da ŋu le anyiehe heva wu nu ɖe adɔ la nu le Dzeƒu la ƒe anyiehe, le Yordan ƒe dziehe mlɔeanu; esia nye dzieheliƒo la.

english_verse: The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border. These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
translation_verse: Eye Yordan nye liƒo le ɣedzeƒe gome. Esia nye Benyamin-viwo ƒe anyigbe ƒe liƒowo godoo va kpe le woƒe ƒomeawo nu.

english_verse: Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders.
translation_verse: Dzidze evelia dze Simeon-viwo ƒe to la dzi le woƒe ƒomeawo nu, eye woxɔ woƒe anyigba ɖe Yuda-viwo ƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following
translation_verse: Bet-Lebaot kple Saruxen. Wole du wuietɔ̃ kple woƒe kɔƒewo.

english_verse: and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah
translation_verse: eye wòtso afisia ɖo ta ɣedzeƒe gome va to Gat-Xefer kple Et-Kazin hemlo to Rimon va ke ɖe Nea;

english_verse: In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages: Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
translation_verse: Ayin, Rimon, Eter kple Asan. Wole du ene kple woƒe kɔƒewo,

english_verse: Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
translation_verse: hekpe ɖe kɔƒe, siwo katã le du, siawo gbɔ vaseɖe Baalat-Beer la ŋuti, eya nye Ramat le dziehe. Esia nye Simeon-viwo ƒe to la ƒe anyigba le woƒe ƒomeawo nu.

english_verse: Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon. Zebulun's Land
translation_verse: Yuda-viwo ƒe gome ŋu woɖe anyigba le na Simeon-viwo, elabena Yuda-viwo tɔ lolo na wo akpa, eyata Simeon-viwo xɔ woƒe anyigba ɖe wo dome.

english_verse: and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
translation_verse: eye liƒo la gɔdɔ̃ zɔ Xanaton ƒe anyiehe gome heva to Yiftax-El-bali la me.

english_verse: Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Katat, Nahalal, Simron, Yidala kple Betlexem. Wole du wuieve hekpe ɖe woƒe kɔƒewo ŋu.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh. Asher's Land
translation_verse: Esia nye Zebulon-viwo ƒe anyigba, woƒe duwo kple kɔƒewo le woƒe ƒomeawo nu.

english_verse: Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following
translation_verse: Esia nye Isaxar-viwo ƒe to la ƒe anyigba, woƒe duwo kple kɔƒewo le woƒe ƒomeawo nu.

english_verse: then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel,
translation_verse: eye wònyè kpo to ɣedzeƒe gome va ke ɖe Bet-Dagon, eye wòmlo to Zebulon, Yiftax-El-bali la ƒe anyiehe, Bet-Haemek kple Negiel, eye wòzɔ Kabul ƒe mia me gome

english_verse: Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon.
translation_verse: va to Ebron, Rexob, Xamon kple Kana vaseɖe Zidon, ɖu gã la gbɔ.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages, including Mahalab, Achzib, Acco, Aphek, and Rehob. Naphtali's Land
translation_verse: Eye liƒo la va ke ɖe Tabor, Saxazima kple Bet-Semes ŋu heva wu nu ɖe Yordan nu. Wole du wuiade hekpe ɖe woƒe kɔƒewo ŋu.

english_verse: The Naphtali clans received this region as their tribal land, and it included
translation_verse: Esia nye Naftali-viwo ƒe anyigba, woƒe duwo kple kɔƒewo le woƒe ƒomeawo nu.

english_verse: The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
translation_verse: Esia nye anyigba, siwo nunɔla Eleazar kple Yosua, Nun vi, kpakple Israel-viwo ƒe ƒomewo ƒe amegãwo dzidze nu ma le Silo le Yehowa ŋku me, le Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la nu. Ale wowu anyigba la mamã nu.

english_verse: These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_verse: Esiawo nye ɖu, siwo woɖo na Israel-viwo katã kple amedzro, si le wo dome bena, ne amea ɖe mebua wu nɔvia o la, wòasi ayi afima, ne magaku ɖe hlɔ̃tɔ si me, hafi woahe eƒe nya ava ameha la ŋku mee o.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Joshua:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Yosua bena;

english_verse: When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na Israel-viwo be, woatia sitsoƒedu, siwo ŋu meƒo nu le na mi to Mose dzi la;

english_verse: One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies.
translation_verse: Ke ne hlɔ̃tɔ ti eyome la, womegatsɔ amewula la de asi nɛ o; elabena mebua hafi wu nɔvia o, eye menye ɖe wòlé fui tsã hafi o.

english_verse: The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder. Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
translation_verse: Eye wòana du ma me, vaseɖe esime woakplɔe ava ameha la ŋku me, eye woadzro nya la me; eye ne nunɔla gã, si fi ɣemaɣi ku la, ekema amewula la kpɔ mɔ agbugbɔ ayi du, si me wòsi tso kple eya ŋutɔ ƒe xɔ nu.

english_verse: The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns: Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
translation_verse: Tete woɖo Kedes le Galilea le Naftali-to dzi kple Sixera le Efrayim-to dzi kpakple Kiryat-Arba, si nye Xebron le Yuda-to dzi.

english_verse: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
translation_verse: Eye woɖo Bezer, si le gbedzi kple tagba la, ɖe Ruben-to la me le Yordan ƒe go keme dzi le Yerixo ƒe ɣedzeƒe, kple Ramot le Gilead ɖe Gad-to la me, kpakple Golan le Basan ɖe Manase-to la me.

english_verse: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
translation_verse: Tete Israel-viwo ɖe du siawo kple wo ŋu nyigba wole woƒe anyigbawo ŋu tsɔ na Lewitɔwo, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ ene.

english_verse: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
translation_verse: Tete dzidze dze Kehat-viwo ƒe ƒomewo dzi, eye wodzidze nu tsɔ du wuietɔ̃ na nunɔla Aron-viwo, siwo nye Lewitɔwo la, ɖe Yuda-to, Simeon-to kple Benyamin-to me;

english_verse: towns from the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and West Manasseh.
translation_verse: Du, siwo wona Aron-viwo, siwo nye Kehat-ƒomeawo tso Lewi-viwo dome la, wonye — elabena eya dzi dzidze; gbãtɔ dze —

english_verse: The clans that were descendants of Merari received
translation_verse: eye wona du wuieve Merari-viwo le woƒe ƒomewo nu ɖe Ruben-to, Gad-to kple Zebulon-to la me.

english_verse: towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Ke wotsɔ, agble, si le dua ŋuti, kple eƒe kɔƒewo na Kaleb, Yefune vi, wònye etɔ.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did. Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo dzidze nu tsɔ du siawo kple wo ŋu nyigbawo na Lewitɔwo, abe alesi Yehowa de se to Mose dzi ene.

english_verse: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
translation_verse: Nunɔla Aron-viwo ƒe duwo katã le du wuietɔ̃ kple wo ŋu lãnyiƒewo.

english_verse: The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received
translation_verse: Gerson-ƒomeawo ƒe duwo katã le du wuietɔ̃ kple wo ŋu lãnyiƒewo.

english_verse: The people of the Levi tribe had a total of
translation_verse: Du siawo katã nye du ɖekaɖekawo, eye lãnyiƒewo le wo ŋu godoo va kpe. Ŋugbedodo la va me.

english_verse: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa tsɔ anyigba blibo la na Israel, abe alesi wòka atam na wo fofowo ene, eye woxɔe hetso aƒe ɖe edzi.

english_verse: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa na wokpɔ gbɔdzɔe le afisiafi, abe alesi wòka atam na wo fofowo pɛpɛpɛ ene; woƒe futɔwo katã dometɔa ɖeke menɔ te ɖe wo nu o, ke boŋ Yehowa tsɔ woƒe futɔwo katã de asi na wo.

english_verse: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_verse: Nyaa ɖeke meto le nya nyui, siwo katã Yehowa gblɔ na Israel ƒe aƒe la me o, wo katã va me pɛpɛpɛ.

english_verse: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi Yosua ya Ruben-viwo kple Gad-viwo kpakple Manase-to afã la,

english_verse: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
translation_verse: Miegblẽ mia nɔviwo ɖi le ɣeyiɣi didi siawo me vaseɖe egbe sia o, eye miewɔ Yehowa, mia Mawu ƒe se la dzi.

english_verse: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ Yehowa, mia Mawu, na mia nɔviwò kpɔ gbɔdzɔe, abe alesi wòdo ŋugbe na wo ene; eyata migbugbɔ yi miaƒe agbadɔwo me le miaƒe anyigba, si Yehowa ƒe dɔla Mose na mi le Yordan godo la dzi.

english_verse: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
translation_verse: Ɖeko mikpɔ nyuie, be miawɔ ɖoɖo kple se, siwo Yehowa ƒe dɔla Mose gblɔ na mi la dzi; milɔ̃ Yehowa, mia Mawu la, eye mizɔ eƒe mowo katã dzi, midzra eƒe seawo ɖo, miku ɖe eŋu, eye misubɔe tso dzi blibo kple luʋɔ blibo me!

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo se bena, Ruben-viwo, Gad-viwo kple Manase ƒe to afã la ɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe Yordan-nuto me dze ŋgɔ Kanaan-nyigba le Israel-viwo ƒe go keme dzi.

english_verse: the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Esi Israel-viwo see la, tete Israel-viwo ƒe ha blibo la kpe ta ɖe Silo, be yewoaho aʋa ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ɖɔ Pinehas, si nye nunɔla Eleazar vi, ɖo ɖe Ruben-viwo, Gad-viwo kple Manase-to afã la gbɔ le Gilead-nyigba dzi,

english_verse: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
translation_verse: eye amegã ewo, siwo nye amegãwo le Israel-viwo ƒe toawo katã me la, kpe ɖe eŋu; woawo enye amegã ɖekaɖekawo le wo fofowo ƒe aƒewo nu le Israel ƒe ame akpeawo dome.

english_verse: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
translation_verse: Esi wova Ruben-viwo, Gad-viwo kple Manase-to afã la gbɔ le Gilead-nyigba dzi la, wogblɔ na wo bena:

english_verse: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa ƒe ha blibo la gblɔ esi: Nukaŋuti mieda vo ɖe Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋu, mietrɔ le Yehowa yome egbe, eye mieɖi vɔsamlekpui na mia ɖokui hedze aglã ɖe Yehowa ŋu egbe?

english_verse: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
translation_verse: Ɖe vo, si woda le Peor ta, eye mía ŋu mekɔ vaseɖe egbe haɖe o, eye dɔvɔ̃ va Yehowa ƒe ameha dzi la, mesɔ gbɔ na mí oa?

english_verse: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
translation_verse: Eye miawo mietrɔ le Yehowa yome egbe hedze aglã ɖe Yehowa ŋu, ne Yehowa nayi dɔmedzoe do ge ɖe Israel-ha blibo la ŋu etsɔa?

english_verse: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
translation_verse: Ke ne miaƒe anyigba ŋu mekɔ o la, ekema miva Yehowa ƒe anyigba dzi, afisi Yehowa ƒe nɔƒe la le, ne miatso aƒe ɖe mía dome; ɖeko migaɖi vɔsamlekpuia ɖeke kpe ɖe Yehowa, mía Mawu ƒe vɔsamlekpui la ŋuti ahadze aglã ɖe Yehowa kple mía ŋu o!

english_verse: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
translation_verse: Ɖe Axan, Serax vi, megbe anukwareɖiɖi le busunuawo me, eye dɔmedzoe va Israel-ha blibo la dzi, eye menye eya ɖeka kolia koe ku ɖe eƒe vodada la ta oa?

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh answered:
translation_verse: Tete Ruben-viwo kple Gad-viwo kpakple Manase-to afã la ɖo ŋu na Israel ƒe ame akpeawo tatɔwo bena:

english_verse: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
translation_verse: Mawu, Mawu Yehowa, Mawu, Mawu Yehowa ŋutɔe nyae, eye Israel hã nanyae: Nenye aglãe miehe, miadze, alo voe míebe, míada ɖe Yehowa ŋu la, ekema megaxɔ mi ɖe agbe egbe sia o!

english_verse: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Nenye vɔsamlekpui míeɖi, be míatrɔ le Yehowa yome, eye nenye ɖe míebe, míasa numevɔ kple nuɖuvɔ alo akpedavɔ le edzi la, ekema Yehowa ŋutɔ nekpɔ eme!

english_verse: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Eyata mieɖo be, míaɖi vɔsamlekpui, menye hena numevɔsa alo akpedavɔsa o,

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
translation_verse: Eye Pinehas, nunɔla Eleazar vi, gblɔ na Ruben-viwo, Gad-viwo kple Manase-vi wo bena: Egbe míedze sii bena, Yehowa le mía dome, elabena esi mieda vo ɖe Yehowa ŋu o la, eyata mieɖe Israel-viwo tso Yehowa si me.

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
translation_verse: Tete Pinehas, nunɔla Eleazar vi, kple amegãwo gbugbɔ tso Ruben-viwo kple Gad-viwo gbɔ le Gilead-nyigba dzi va Israel-viwo gbɔ le Kanaan-nyigba dzi, eye wohe dɔgbedenya vɛ na wo.

english_verse: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
translation_verse: Eye nya la dze Israel-viwo ŋu, eye Israel-viwo kafu Mawu, eye womegadi be, yewoaho aʋa ɖe wo ŋu ahagblẽ anyigba, si dzi Ruben-viwo kple Gad-viwo le la o.

english_verse: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_verse: Eye Ruben-viwo kple Gad-viwo na ŋkɔ vɔsamlekpui la bena: „Eya nye ɖase le mía dome be, Yehowae nye Mawu.“

english_verse: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
translation_verse: Esi Yehowa na Israel kpɔ gbɔdzɔe tso eƒe futɔ, siwo katã ƒo xlãe godoo, si me eteƒe didi, eye Yosua tsi xɔ ƒe geɖe la,

english_verse: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
translation_verse: Yosua yɔ Israel blibo la, woƒe ame tsitsiwo kple tatɔwo, ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo kple dzikpɔlawo gblɔ na wo bena: Metsi, eye mexɔ ƒe geɖe.

english_verse: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
translation_verse: Mia ŋutɔwo miekpɔ nusiwo Yehowa, mia Mawu la, wɔ dukɔ siawo katã le mia ŋgɔ, elabena Yehowa, mia Mawue, wɔ aʋa na mi.

english_verse: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Yehowa, mia Mawu la, ŋutɔ ate wo ɖa le mia ŋgɔ, eye wòanya wo da le mia ŋgɔ, be miaxɔ woƒe anyigba, abe alesi Yehowa, mia Mawu la, do ŋugbe na mi ene.

english_verse: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
translation_verse: Eyata milé dzi ɖe ƒo vevie, ne mialé nusiwo katã woŋlɔ ɖe Mose ƒe segbalẽa me la me ɖe asi, eye miawɔ wo dzi, eye migadze ɖe ɖusi alo mia me o.

english_verse: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
translation_verse: Migatra ɖe dukɔ, siwo kpɔtɔ ɖi la, dome o, eye woƒe mawuwo ŋkɔ megava mia nu, alo miatsɔ wo aka atam o, migasubɔ wo, eye migade ta agu na wo o,

english_verse: Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
translation_verse: ke boŋ nuku ɖe Yehowa, mia Mawu la ŋu, abe alesi miewɔ vaseɖe egbe ene.

english_verse: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
translation_verse: Yehowa nyã dukɔ gã kple dukɔ sesẽwo ɖa le nua ŋgɔ, ke miawo la amea ɖeke mete ŋu nɔ te ɖe mia nu vaseɖe fifi o.

english_verse: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Mia dome ŋutsu ɖeka te ŋu nyã ame akpe, elabena Yehowa, mia Mawue, wɔ ana na mi, abe alesi wòdo ŋugbe na mi ene.

english_verse: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Eyata mikpɔ nyuie le miaƒe agbe ŋu, ne míala Yehowa, mia Mawu la.

english_verse: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
translation_verse: ekema minyae bena, Yehowa, mia Mawu la, maganyã dukɔ siawo ɖa le mia ŋgɔ akpɔ o, eye woatrɔ zu adoboli kple mɔ na mi, woanye atam anɔ miaƒe axada me, eye woanye gu anɔ ŋku dzi na mi, vaseɖe esime miatsrɔ̃ avɔ keŋkeŋ le anyigba nyui, si Yehowa, mia Mawu, na mi la dzi.

english_verse: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
translation_verse: Mikpɔ ɖa, mele demagbɔnugbe yi ge, ke miawo mienyae tso dzi blibo kple luʋɔ blibo me bena, nyaa ɖeke meto le nya nyui, siwo katã Yehowa, mia Mawu la, gblɔ na mi la me o, wo katã va me na mi, eye nya ku ɖeka hɔ̃ hã meto le eme o.

english_verse: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Tete Yosua na Israel-toawo katã va kpe ta ɖe Sixem, eye wòyɔ ame tsitsiwo kple tatɔwo, ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo kple dzikpɔlawo, eye wova tsi tre ɖe Mawu ŋku me.

english_verse: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
translation_verse: Eye Yosua gblɔ na dukɔ blibo la bena: Ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Tsãtsãtsã la mia fofowo nɔ tɔsisi la ƒe go keme dzi, Tarax, Abraham kple Naxor fofo, eye wosubɔ mawu bubuwo.

english_verse: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
translation_verse: Tete mekplɔ mia fofo Abraham tso tɔsisi la ƒe go keme dzi, eye mena wotsa le Kanaan-nyigba blibo la dzi — mena viawo dzi ɖe dzi — eye metsɔ Isak nɛ.

english_verse: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
translation_verse: Metsɔ Yakob kple Esau na Isak, eye metsɔ Seir-to na Esau, be wòanye etɔ, ke Yakob kple viawo ya ʋu yi Egipte.

english_verse: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
translation_verse: Eye wodo ɣli yɔ Yehowa, tete wòde viviti mia kple Egiptetɔwo dome, eye wòna ƒu la ŋe gbagba ɖe wo dzi. Miekpɔ nusiwo mewo Egiptetɔwo la kple ŋku, eye mietsi gbedzi eteƒe didi.

english_verse: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
translation_verse: Emegbe mekplɔ mi va Amoritɔwo, siwo no Yordan ƒe go keme dzi la, ƒe anyigba dzi, eye wowɔ aʋa kpli mi; ke metsɔ wo de asi na mi, miexɔ woƒe anyigba, eye metsrɔ̃ wo le mia ŋgɔ.

english_verse: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
translation_verse: Tete Moab-fia Balak, Zipor vi, ho va wo aʋa kple Israel, eye wòdo woyi ɖayɔ Bileam, Beor vi vɛ, be wòaƒo fi ade mi;

english_verse: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
translation_verse: ke megbe toɖoɖo Bileam, eye wotso mi yra boŋ, eye meɖe mi tso esi me.

english_verse: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
translation_verse: Eyome mietso Yordan va Yerixo; tete Yerixotɔwo, Amoritɔwo, Perizitɔwo, Kanaanitɔwo, Xititɔwo, Girgasitɔwo, Xiwitɔwo kple Yebusitɔwo va wo aʋa kpli mi, eye metso wo ɖe asi na mi.

english_verse: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Medɔ teamekplɔɖoewo ɖe mia ŋgɔ, eye wonyã Amoritɔwo ƒe fia eveawo le mia ŋgɔ; menye wò yi kple wò dae wɔe o.

english_verse: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
translation_verse: Metso anyigba, si ŋu miedze agbagba le o la, na mi kple ɖu, siwo mietso o la, be mianɔ wo me, eye metsɔ weinbɔ kple amitibɔ, siwo mietso o la, na mi, be miaɖu wo me nuwo.

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
translation_verse: Eyata mivɔ̃ Yehowa, eye misubɔe blibo le nyateƒe me, miɖe mawu, siwo mia fofowo subɔ le tɔsisi la godo kple Egipte la ɖa, eye misubɔ Yehowa!

english_verse: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
translation_verse: Ke ne Yehowa subɔsubɔ medze mia ŋu o la, ekema mitia, amesi subɔ ge míala, egbea: eɖanye mawu, siwo mia fofowo subɔ le tɔsisi la godo, alo Amoritɔ, siwo ƒe anyigba dzi miele la, ƒe mawuwo o. Ke mía kple nye aƒe ya miasubɔ Yehowa!

english_verse: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la ɖo ŋu gblɔ bena: Nede megbe xaa tso mía gbɔ be, miagblẽ Yehowa ɖi asubɔ mawu bubuwo!

english_verse: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
translation_verse: Ke boŋ Yehowa enye mía Mawu, eyae kplɔ mía kple mia fofowo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi le kluvinyenyeƒe me, eye wòwɔ dzesi gã siawo le mía ŋku me, eye wòkpɔ mia ta le mɔ blibo, si miezɔ heto dukɔ geɖewo dome la dzi.

english_verse: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
translation_verse: Yehowa nyã dukɔwo katã kple Amoritɔ, siwo nɔ anyigba dzi la, ɖa le mía ŋgɔ. Miawo hã miasubɔ Yehowa, elabena eyae nye mía Mawu!

english_verse: Joshua said: The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it.
translation_verse: Yosua ɖo ŋu na dukɔ la bena: Miate ŋu asubɔ Yehowa o, elabena Mawu kɔkɔe kple Mawu hã ŋu wònye, matsɔ miaƒe vodadawo kple nuvɔ̃wo ake mi o.

english_verse: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
translation_verse: Ne miegblẽ Yehowa ɖi, eye miesubɔ mawu bubuwo la, ekema ahe vɔ̃ ava mia dzi, eye woatsrɔ̃ mi ɖa, evɔ wònye ewɔ nyuie na mi va yi hafi.

english_verse: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la ɖo ŋu na Yosua bena: Gbeɖe, Yehowa ko miasubɔ!

english_verse: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
translation_verse: Yosua gblɔ na dukɔ la bena: Mia ŋutɔwoe nye ɖasefo na mia ɖokui be, mietia Yehowa, be miasubɔ. Woɖo ŋu be: Ẽ, mia ŋu tɔwoe nye ɖasefo.

english_verse: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
translation_verse: Ekema miɖe mawu bubuwo ɖa le mia dome, eye mitrɔ miaƒe dzi ɖe Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋu!

english_verse: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
translation_verse: Eye dukɔ la ɖo ŋu na Yosua bena: Yehowa, mia Mawu ta, miasubɔ, eye eƒe gbe ko miase!

english_verse: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
translation_verse: Ale Yosua bia nu kple dukɔ la gbemagbe, eye wòtsɔ seawo kple ɖoɖoawo ɖo woƒe ŋku me le Sixem.

english_verse: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
translation_verse: Eye Yosua ŋlɔ nya siawo ɖe Mawu ƒe segbalẽ la me, eye wotsɔ kpe gãa ɖe ɖi ɖe afima le logoti, si le Yehowa ƒe kɔkɔeƒea gbɔ la te.
