english_verse: and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
translation_verse: Tete Yosua gblɔ na dukɔ blibo la bena: Kpɔ ɖa, kpe sia nye ɖase na mi, elabena ese nya, siwo katã Yehowa gblɔ na mi la, eye wòanye ɖase na mi, ne miagasẽ nu le mia Mawu la ŋu o.

english_verse: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
translation_verse: Emegbe Yosua de asi le dukɔ la ŋu, eye amesiame yi eƒe anyigba dzi. Yosua kple Eleazar ƒe ku. Woɖi Yosef ƒe fuwo.

english_verse: Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Nya siawo megbe la Yehowa ƒe dɔla Yosua. Nun vi, amesi xɔ ƒe alafa ɖeka kple ewo la ku,

english_verse: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: eye woɖu ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi le Timnat-Serax, si le Efrayim-to dzi, le Gaas-to ƒe anyiehe gome.

english_verse: As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Eye Israel subɔ Yehowa, ŋkeke alesi Yosua nɔ agbe kple ŋkeke alesi ame tsitsi, siwo nɔ agbe le Yosua megbe eteƒe didi, eye wokpɔ nusiwo katã Yehowa wɔ na Israel teƒe la, le agbe.

english_verse: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ɖi Yosef ƒe ƒu, siwo wotsɔ tso Egipte vɛ la, ɖe Sixem, ɖe anyigba, si Yakob ƒle kesita alafa ɖeka le Sixem fofo Xamor ƒe viwo si la dzi, eye wòtrɔ zu Yosef-viwo ƒe domenyinu.

english_verse: When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_verse: Eye Eleazar, Aron vi, hã ku, eye woɖii ɖe Gibea, si wotsɔ na via Pinehas ɖe Efrayim-to dzi la.

english_verse: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the Lord, “Which of our tribes should attack the Canaanites first?”
translation_verse: Le Yosua ƒe ku megbe la Israel-viwo bia Yehowa bena: Mia dometɔ kae atre hoho ayi aɖawɔ aʋa kple Kanaanitɔwo?

english_verse: “Judah!” the Lord answered. “I'll help them take the land.”
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ bena: Yuda neho yi; kpɔ ɖa, metsɔ anyigba la de asi nɛ!

english_verse: The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.” Troops from Simeon came to help Judah.
translation_verse: Eye Yuda gblɔ na nɔvia Simeon bena: Ho kplim, míayi nye anyigba dzi aɖawɔ aʋa kple Kanaanitɔwo, ekema nye hã makpe ɖe ŋuwò, míayi tɔwo dzi! Tete Simeon yi kplii.

english_verse: After that, they attacked the Canaanites who lived at Hebron, defeating the three clans called Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. At that time, Hebron was called Kiriath-Arba.
translation_verse: Eye Yuda ho aʋa ɖe Kanaanitɔ, siwo nɔ Xebron la ŋu, — tsã la woyɔ Xebron bena Kiryat-Arba — eye woɖu Sesai, Aximan kple Talmai dzi.

english_verse: The king tried to escape, but soldiers from Judah caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes,
translation_verse: Ke Adoni-Bezek si, eye woti eyome ɖalée, eye wolã eƒe asidegblefetsuwo kple afɔdegblefetsuwo.

english_verse: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
translation_verse: Eye Yuda-viwo wɔ aʋa kple Yerusalem, woxɔe, eye wowu wo kple yi hetɔ dzo du lã.

english_verse: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.
translation_verse: Emegbe Yuda-viwo ho yi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Kanaanitɔ, siwo le towo dzi kple dziehe kpakple gbadzaƒe.

english_verse: From Hebron, Judah's army went to attack Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Eyome woho aʋa tso afisia ɖe Debirtɔwo ŋu; tsã la woyɔ Debir bena Kiryat-Sefer.

english_verse: Caleb told his troops, “The man who captures Kiriath-Sepher can marry my daughter Achsah.”
translation_verse: Tete Kaleb gblɔ bena. Amesi aɖu Kiryat-Sefer dzi, eye wòaxɔe la, matsɔ vinyenyɔnu Axsa ne wòaɖee.

english_verse: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, so Caleb let him marry Achsah. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Eye esi Otniel, Kaleb ƒe tsɛ, Kenas ƒe vi, xɔe la, etso via Axsa nɛ woɖee.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Eye esi wokplɔe la, nyɔnu la ɖo dalĩ nɛ be, yeabia agble ye fofo, eye wòɖi tso tedzi la dzi, Tete Kaleb biae bena: Nya kae le asiwò?

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so please give me some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Yram, etsɔ dziehenyigba nam xoxo, eyata tsɔ tsivudoawo hã nam! Tete Kaleb tsɔ vudo, siwo le to dzi kple bali me la nɛ.

english_verse: The people who belonged to the Kenite clan were the descendants of the father-in-law of Moses. They left Jericho with the people of Judah and settled near Arad in the Southern Desert of Judah not far from the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Eye Mose nyo, Keni ƒe viwo kpakple Yuda-viwo, ʋu tso devedu la me yi Yuda-gbedzi, si le Arad ƒe dziehe gome, eye wova no dukɔ la dome.

english_verse: Judah's army helped Simeon's army attack the Canaanites who lived at Zephath. They completely destroyed the town and renamed it Hormah.
translation_verse: Eye Yuda ho kpe ɖe nɔvia Simeon ŋu wova ɖu Kanaanitɔ, siwo no Zefat la dzi, eye wotsrɔ̃ wo gbidigbidi hena ŋkɔ ɖu la bena Xorma.

english_verse: The Lord helped the army of Judah capture Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the land near those towns. They also took the hill country. But the people who lived in the valleys had iron chariots, so Judah was not able to make them leave or to take their land.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa nɔ kple Yuda, ale be wòte ŋu xɔ to la, ke mete ŋu nyã amesiwo nɔ bali me la ɖa o, elabena gatasiaɖamwo le wo si.

english_verse: The tribe of Judah gave the town of Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had told them to do. Caleb defeated the three Anakim clans and took over the town. The Benjamin Tribe Does Not Capture Jerusalem
translation_verse: Wotsɔ Xebron na Kaleb, abe alesi Mose gblɔ ene, eye wònyã Enak vi elɔ̃awo le afima. Womenya Kanaanitɔwo katã o.

english_verse: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
translation_verse: Ke Benyamin-viwo menya Yebusitɔ, siwo nɔ Yerusalem la ɖa o; eyata Yebusitɔwo kple Benyamin-viwo tsaka le Yerusalem vaseɖe egbe?

english_verse: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
translation_verse: Tete ŋkutsalawo kpɔ ŋutsua ɖe ɖo tso dua me, eye wogblɔ ne bena: Fia mɔnu, si míato age ɖe dua me la mí, ekema míave nuwò.

english_verse: The man showed them, and the two Israelite tribes attacked Bethel, killing everyone except the man and his family. The two tribes made the man and his family leave,
translation_verse: Tete wòfiã dua me mɔnu wo, eye wowu duametɔwo kple yi; ke woɖe asi le ŋutsu la kple eƒe ƒometɔwo katã ŋu.

english_verse: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsu la yi ɖatso du ɖe Xititɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, eye wòna ŋkɔe be Luz; ŋkɔ sia tsi eŋu vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
translation_verse: Eye Efrayim hã menya Kanaanitɔ, siwo nɔ Gezer la ɖa o; eyata Kanaanitɔwo tsi wo dome le Gezer.

english_verse: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
translation_verse: Eye Naftali menya Bet-Semestɔwo kple Bet-Anattɔwo ɖa o, eye wònɔ anyigbadzitɔ, siwo nye Kanaanitɔwo la dome; ke Bet-Semestɔwo kple Bet-Anattɔwo wɔ dɔ na wo yaka.

english_verse: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
translation_verse: Amoritɔwo nyã Dan-viwo ɖo ɖe towo dzi, eye womèna be, woava bali me o.

english_verse: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
translation_verse: Eye Amoritɔwo do dzi nɔ Xeres-towo dzi kple Ayalon kpakple Saalbim bɛ. Ke esi Yosef-viwo ƒe alɔ va kpe wo dzi la, wowɔ dɔ na wo yaka.

english_verse: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
translation_verse: Amoritɔwo ƒe liƒo tso Akrabim-to dzi mɔ gbɔ kple Sela hemlo ɖe nu yii.

english_verse: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe dɔla tso Gilgal va Boxim gblɔ bena: Mekplɔ mi tso Egipte va anyigba, si ŋu meka atam ɖo na mia fofowo gblɔ be, nyematu nye nu, si mebia kpli mi, akpɔ gbeɖe o la dzi;

english_verse: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
translation_verse: migabia nu kple anyigba sia dzitɔwo o, eye migbã woƒe vɔsamlekpuiwo! Gake mieɖo to nye gbe o. Nukaŋuti miewɔ alea ɖo?

english_verse: And so, I'll stop helping you defeat your enemies. Instead, they will be there to trap you into worshiping their idols.
translation_verse: Eyata nye hã mele egblɔm na mi bena: nyemanyã wo le mia ŋgɔ o, ne woanye fuɖenametɔwo anɔ mia ŋu, eye woƒe mawuwo nanye mɔ̃ aɖe mi.

english_verse: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
translation_verse: eye wona ŋkɔ teƒe ma bena Boxim, eye wosa vɔ le afima na Yehowa.

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: eye woɖu ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi le Timnat-Xeres, si le Efrayim-to dzi le Gaas-to ƒe anyiehe gome.

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Esi dzidzime mawo katã yi wo tɔgbuiwo gbɔ vɔ la, dzidzime bubu va dzɔ le wo megbe, amesiwo medze si Yehowa o, eye womenya naneke le nusiwo katã wòwɔ na Israel la ŋu o.

english_verse: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe asi nye dzɔgbevɔ̃e le wo ŋu le afisiafi, si woyi ɖo, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ na wo kple alesi Yehowa ka atam na wo ene, ale be woɖo xaxa me ŋutɔ.

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: Ke womeɖo to woƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo o, eye wodze mawu bubuwo yome de ta agu na wo, wote ɖa le mɔ, si dzi wo fofowo zɔ heɖo to Yehowa ƒe seawo la dzi, eye womewɔ nenema o.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Ne Yehowa ɖo ʋɔnudrɔ̃la na wo la, Yehowa nɔa anyi kple ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la, eye wòɖea wo tsoa woƒe futɔwo si me, ŋkeke alesi ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la le agbe, elabena woƒe hũɖeɖe le fuɖenametɔwo kple ŋutasẽlawo ŋuti na be, Yehowa ƒe dɔme trɔ ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
translation_verse: Ke ne ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la ku la, ekema wotrɔna, eye wogblẽna de dzi wua wo fofowo, wodzea mawu bubuwo yome, subɔa wo hedea ta agu na wo, eye womedea asi le woƒe nuwɔwɔ kple tamesesẽ ŋu o.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa do dɔmedzoe ɖe Israel ŋu gblɔ bena: Esi dukɔ sia tu nye nu, si mebia kple wo fofowo, eye meɖo to nye gbe o la,

english_verse: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
translation_verse: eyata nye hã nyemaganyã dukɔ, siwo Yosua kpɔtɔ ɖi hafi ku la ɖa le wo ŋgɔ o;

english_verse: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: ne matsɔ wo ado Israel akpɔ be, wòalé ŋku ɖe Yehowa ƒe mɔ ŋu, eye woazɔ edzi abe wo fofowo ene loo, alo womalé ŋku ɖe eŋu o.

english_verse: That's why the Lord had not let Joshua get rid of those enemy nations all at once.
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa kpɔtɔ dukɔ siawo ɖi, menya wo enumake o, eye metsɔ wo de asi na Yosua o.

english_verse: the Philistines and their five rulers, as well as the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived in the Lebanon Mountains from Mount Baal-Hermon to Hamath Pass.
translation_verse: Woawo nye. Filistitɔwo ƒe amegã atɔ̃awo, Kanaanitɔwo katã, Zidontɔwo kple Xiwitɔwo, siwo nɔ Libanon-towo dzi tso Baal-Xermon vaseɖe Xamat.

english_verse: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
translation_verse: Wotsi anyi, ne wòatsɔ aɖo Israel akpɔ, be woaɖo to Yehowa ƒe se, siwo wòde na wo fofowo to Mose dzi loo?

english_verse: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
translation_verse: Woɖe woƒe vinyɔnuwo, eye woawo hã tsɔ woƒe vinyɔnuwo na woƒe viŋutsuwo, eye wosubɔ woƒe mawuwo.

english_verse: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo wɔ nusi medze Yehowa ŋu o, woŋlɔ Yehowa, woƒe Mawu la be, eye wosubɔ Baalwo kple Aserawo.

english_verse: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa do dɔmedzoe ɖe Israel ŋu, eye wotsɔ wo dzra na Mesopotamia-fia Kusan-Risatayim, eye Israel-viwo subɔ Kusan-Risatayim ƒe enyi sɔŋ.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ɖo ɣli yɔ Yehowa, tete Yehowa ɖo xɔnametɔ na Israel-viwo, Otniel, Kaleb ƒe tsɛ, Kenas ƒe vi, eye wòɖe wo.

english_verse: and Israel was at peace until Othniel died about
translation_verse: Eye anyigba la dzi fa ƒe blane, vaseɖe esime Otniel, Kenas vi la ku.

english_verse: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
translation_verse: Ke esi Israel-viwo gade asi nusi medze Yehowa ŋu o wowɔ me la, Yehowa do ŋusẽ Moab-fia Eglon ɖe Israel-viwo ŋu, elabena wowɔ nusi medze Yehowa ŋu o.

english_verse: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
translation_verse: Eye wòda Amon-viwo kple Amalekitɔwo kpe ɖe eɖokui ŋu, eye woho aʋa va si Israel, eye woxɔ devedu la.

english_verse: Then he ruled Israel for
translation_verse: Israel-viwo subɔ Moab-fia Eglon ƒe wuienyi sɔŋ.

english_verse: Ehud went with the other Israelites as far as the statues at Gilgal. Then he turned back and went upstairs to the room where Eglon had his throne. Ehud said, “Your Majesty, I need to talk with you in private.” Eglon replied, “Don't say anything yet!” His officials left the room, and Eglon stood up as Ehud came closer. “Yes,” Ehud said, “I have a message for you from God!”
translation_verse: Eye Ehud yi egbɔ, esime wòle dziƒoxɔ, si me eya ɖeka nɔna xɔa ya la me. Ehud gblɔ ne bena: Mehe Mawu ƒe gbe vɛ na wò! Tete wòtsi tre tso eƒe zikpui la dzi.

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: Enumake Ehud do mia ɖa di adekpui la le ɖusiklito heƒo ɖe dɔme nɛ,

english_verse: that even the handle was buried in his fat. Ehud left the dagger there. Then after closing and locking the doors to the room, he climbed through a window onto the porch
translation_verse: Emegbe Ehud do go ɖe akpata me, eye woɖe ga dziƒoxɔ la ƒe ʋɔtru me ɖe enu.

english_verse: and left. When the king's officials came back and saw that the doors were locked, they said, “The king is probably inside relieving himself.”
translation_verse: Esi wòdo go la, eƒe dolawo va, eye wokpɔ bena, dziƒoxɔ la ƒe ʋɔtruwo le dodo; eyata wobu be, afɔdzi ɖem wòanya le le yaxɔƒe la.

english_verse: They stood there waiting until they felt foolish, but Eglon still didn't open the doors. Finally, they unlocked the doors and found King Eglon lying dead on the floor.
translation_verse: Ke esi wolala ʋuu ɖokpoe meʋu ʋɔa o la, wotso safui va ʋu ʋɔ lae, eye kpɔ ɖa, woƒe amegã ku ɖe anyigba.

english_verse: But by that time, Ehud had already escaped past the statues. Ehud went to the town of Seirah
translation_verse: Ke esi wole lalam nenema la, Ehud gbɔ legbawo ŋu, eye wòsi va Seira.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na wo bena: Mikplɔm ɖo kaba, elabena Yehowa tso miaƒe futɔ Moabitɔwo de asi na mi! Enumake wodze eyome heva xe Yordan-tsoƒemɔ na Moabitɔwo, eye womena amea ɖeke tso tɔ la o.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Ale Moabitɔwo ge ɖe Israel ƒe asi te ɣemaɣi, eye anyigba dzi la ƒe blanyi sɔŋ.

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Eye Samgar, Anat vi, dze eyome, amesi tsɔ nyikplɔti wu Filistitɔ ame alafa ade, eye eya hã ɖe Israel.

english_verse: After the death of Ehud, the Israelites again started disobeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke esi Ehud ku la, Israel viwo gade asi nusi medze Yehowa ŋu o la wɔwɔ me.

english_verse: So the Lord let the Canaanite King Jabin of Hazor conquer Israel. Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-Ha-Goiim.
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa tso wo dzra na Kanaan-fia Yabin, amesi ɖu dzi le Xazor; eƒe aʋafia nye Sisera, amesi nɔ Xaroset-Goyim.

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Eyome wògblɔ nɛ bena: Yi, natsi tre ɖe agbadɔ la ƒe mɔnu, eye ne amea ɖe va bia wò bena: amea ɖe le afisia hã la, ekema gblɔ bena: O!

english_verse: Deborah the wife of Lappidoth was a prophet and a leader of Israel during those days.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi la nyɔnu-nyagblɔɖila Debora, Lapidot srɔ̃e, drɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel.

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: Ena Debora ƒe ɖeti te le Rama kple Betel dome le Efrayim-to dzi, eye Israel-viwo yia egbɔ ɖadrɔ̃a ʋɔnu.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: Eye wòdɔ ame woyi ɖayɔ Barak, Abinoam vi, tso Kedes-Naftali vɛ, eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, ɖe se na wò be: Ho, yi Tabor-to la dzi, naɖe ame akpe ewo tso Naftali-viwo kple Zebulon-viwo dome kpe ɖe ɖokuiwò ŋu;

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: makplɔ Sisera, Yabin ƒe aʋafia kple eƒe tasiaɖamwo kpakple eƒe aʋakɔ ava gbɔwò le Kison-toʋu la nu, eye matsɔe ade asi na wò!

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Mele yiyi ge kpli wò tso; ke bubu, si le mɔ, si dzi dze ge nala me la, manye tɔwò o, elabena Yehowa atsɔ Sisera ade asi na nyɔnua ɖe! Eye Debora tso yi Kedes kple Barak.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Ke Xeber. Kenitɔ la, ʋu tso Mose ƒe nyo Xobab viwo, siwo nye Kenitɔwo la gbɔ, eye wòva tu eƒe agbadɔwo ɖe logotiwo gbɔ le Zaanayim le Kedes gbɔ.

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Eye esi wogblɔ na Sisera bena, Barak, Abinoam vi, ho va Tabor-to ŋu la,

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Eye Debora gblɔ na Barak bena: Tso! Elabena egbe sia Yehowa le Sisera tso ge aɖe asi na wò. Alo ɖe Yehowa medze ŋgɔwò oa? Tete Barak ɖi tso Tabor-to la dzi, eye ame akpe ewo dze eyome.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa tsɔ yi de zi Sisera kple eƒe tasiaɖamwo katã kple eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la me le Barak ŋgɔ, eye Sisera ɖi le eƒe tasiaɖam me heto afɔ si.

english_verse: Barak's forces went after Sisera's chariots and army as far as Harosheth-Ha-Goiim. Sisera's entire army was wiped out.
translation_verse: Ke Barak ti tasiaɖamwo kple aʋakɔ la yome vaseɖe Xaroset-Goyim; eye Sisera ƒe aʋakɔ blibo la tsi yi nu, ame ɖeka hɔ̃ hã mekpɔtɔ o. Yael wu Sisera.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: Ke Sisera to afɔ si va Yael, Kenitɔ Xeber srɔ̃ ƒe agbadɔ gbɔ, elabena ŋutifafa le Xazor-fia, Yabin kple Kenitɔ Xeber ƒe aƒe la dome.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Tete Yael yi ɖakpe Sisera gblɔ ne bena: Va, nye amegã, va dze gbɔnye, eye megavɔ̃ o! Enumake wòyi egbɔ le eƒe agbadɔ me, eye nyɔnu la tsɔ avɔ tsyɔ nɛ.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ nɛ bena: Taflatse, na tsi via ɖem mano, elabena tsikɔ le wuyem. Enumake wòʋu notsilãgbalẽgolo la, eye wonae wòno, emegbe wògatsyɔ avɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Sisera was exhausted and soon fell fast asleep. Jael took a hammer and drove a tent-peg through his head into the ground, and he died.
translation_verse: Tete Xeber srɔ̃ Yael tsɔ agbadɔtsyɔti, eye wotsɔ zu ɖe asi yi egbɔ dzaa, eye wòƒu tsyoti la ɖe tonu nɛ mimi ɖe anyigba. Ke edɔ alɔ yi me ʋĩ, elabena ɖeɖi le eŋu, eye woku.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Esi Barak ti Sisera yome la, Yael do go va kpee, eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Va, ne mafia amesi ɖim nèle la wò! Esi wòyi la, ekpa Sisera ku ɖi, eye tsyoti ƒo ɖe tonu nɛ.

english_verse: That same day God defeated the Canaanite King Jabin while the Israelites looked on, and his army was no longer powerful enough to attack the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ale Mawu baba Kanaan-fia Yabin ɖe anyi le ŋkeke ma dzi le Israel-viwo ŋku me enye si.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ƒe asi kpe Kanaan-fia Yabin dzi, vaseɖe esime wotsɔe vo keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: After the battle was over that day, Deborah and Barak sang this song:
translation_verse: Tete Debora kple Barak, Abinoam vi, wodzi ha gbemagbe bena:

english_verse: We praise you, Lord! Our soldiers volunteered, ready to follow you.
translation_verse: Esi aʋafiawo dze Israel ŋgɔ, eye dukɔ la lɔ̃ faa ŋuti la, mikafu Yehowa!

english_verse: Listen, kings and rulers, while I sing for the Lord, the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Mi fiawo, misee; mi amegãwo, miƒu to anyi! Mele ha dzi ge, Yehowae mele ha dzi ge na, Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu lae mele saŋku ƒo ge na!

english_verse: Our Lord, God of Israel, when you came from Seir, where the Edomites live,
translation_verse: Yehowa, esi neho tso Seir, eye netsa to Edom-tagba la, anyigba ʋuʋu, dziŋgɔ ɖuɖu tsi, eye alilikpowo hã dza tsi;

english_verse: rain poured from the sky, the earth trembled, and mountains shook.
translation_verse: towo dzo kpekpekpe le Yehowa ŋku me, eye Sinai sia ʋuʋu le Yehowa. Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe ŋku me.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: Le Samgar, Anat vi, ŋɔli kple Yael ŋɔli la mɔwo to gbe, eye amesiwo zɔa mɔ tatawo dzi la, to gbedzemɔwo.

english_verse: and villagers couldn't work in their fields. Then Deborah took command, protecting Israel as a mother protects her children.
translation_verse: Aʋafiawo nu tso le Israel, wo nu tso, vaseɖe esime nye Debora medo, medo abe Israel dada ene!

english_verse: The Israelites worshiped other gods, and the gates of their towns were then attacked. But they had no shields or spears to fight with.
translation_verse: Wotia mawu yeyewo; eyata aʋa va ke ɖe woƒe duwo ŋu. Womegakpɔ akpoxɔnu kple akplɔa ɖeke le Israel ƒe ame akpe blaneawo dome o.

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: Nye dzi enye Israel ƒe tatɔwo kple amesiwo lã faa le dukɔa dome la to. Mikafu Yehowa!

english_verse: Listen, everyone! Whether you ride a donkey with a padded saddle or have to walk.
translation_verse: Mi amesiwo do tedzinɔ ɣiwo, kple mi amesiwo no kuntruwo dzi, kpakple mi amesiwo le mo la, midzi ha!

english_verse: Even those who carry water to the animals will tell you, “The Lord has won victories, and so has Israel.” Then the Lord's people marched down to the town gates
translation_verse: Esi aŋutrɔdalawo tso aseye le lãtoawo gbɔ la, wokafu Yehowa ƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔwo kple Israel ƒe aʋafiawo ƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔwo le afima Emegbe Yehowa ƒe dukɔ la gbugbɔ yi duwo me.

english_verse: and said, “Deborah, let's go! Let's sing as we march. Barak, capture our enemies.”
translation_verse: Nyɔ, nyɔ, Debora! nyɔ, nyɔ, nadzi ha! Tsi tre. Barak! Abinoam vi, kplɔ wò aboyomewo!

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la ƒe bubume mamleawo va, eye Yehowa ɖi va gbɔnye le kalẽtɔwo dome.

english_verse: Troops came from Ephraim, where Amalekites once lived. Others came from Benjamin; officers and leaders came from Machir and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Wotso Efrayim, amesi ƒe agunu le Amalek, eye Benyamin to wo megbe va ge ɖe woƒe amehawo dome. Tatɔwo ɖi abu tso Maxir kple Zebulon, amesiwo si tsiameti la le.

english_verse: The rulers of Issachar came along with Deborah, and Issachar followed Barak into the valley. But the tribe of Reuben was no help at all!
translation_verse: Isaxar-amegãwo le Debora ŋu, eye Isaxar kpe ɖe Barak ŋu hedze eyome kpledu-kpledu yi bali la me. Ruben-tɔʋuwo nu wode adaŋu gãwo le.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti nètsi lãhawo gbɔ, be nalé to ɖe lãhawo ƒe xɔxlɔ̃ ŋu? Ruben-tɔʋuwo nu wode adaŋu gãwo le.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Gilead tsi Yordan ƒe go keme dzi bɔkɔɔ. Nukaŋuti Dan nye amedzro le nuwo me? Aser baba nɔ ƒuta, eye wòtsyɔ akɔ anyi ɖe eƒe adɔ̃wo nu.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Zebulon enye dukɔa ɖe, si ku kutsikpe, hekpe ɖe Naftali ŋu le gbadzaƒeto la dzi.

english_verse: Canaanite kings fought us at Taanach by the stream near Megiddo— but they couldn't rob us of our silver.
translation_verse: Fiawo va wɔ aʋa, Kanaan-fiawo va wɔ aʋa ɣemaɣi le Tanax le Megido-tɔ la nu; ke womekpɔ klosaloa ɖeke xɔ o!

english_verse: From their pathways in the sky the stars fought Sisera,
translation_verse: Dziƒo wotso wɔ aʋa la, ɣletiviwo nɔ woƒe mɔwo dzi wɔ aʋa kple Sisera.

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Kison-tɔʋu la kplɔ wo yii, blematɔʋu Kison. Nye luʋɔ, do kple ŋusẽ!

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: Kalẽtɔ, siwo si la, ƒe sɔwo ƒe afɔzi le ɖiɖim.

english_verse: The Lord's angel said, “Put a curse on Meroz Town! Its people refused to help the Lord fight his powerful enemies.”
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe dɔla be; Aɖi Meros ŋu! Aɖi eme nɔlawo ŋu kpekpekpe; elabena womeva xɔ na Yehowa o, womeva xɔ na Yehowa le kalẽtɔwo dome o!

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Tsi wòbia, ke notsie wònae, bubumewo ƒe tre me woku notsi kpekẽ ɖo vɛ.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: Eɖo asi ɖa tsɔ tsyoti, eye wòlé gbeɖe ƒe zũ ɖe ɖusi; eda zũ ɖe Sisera ƒe ta dzi, eye wòfe eƒe tonu ŋɔe wòɖi go ɖe egodo.

english_verse: Sisera sank to his knees and fell dead at her feet.
translation_verse: Etsra ɖe eƒe afɔ nu wɔɔ, eƒe afɔ nu wòtsra ɖo, eye afisi wòtsra ɖo la, afima woku ɖo.

english_verse: Sisera's mother looked out through her window. “Why is he taking so long?” she asked. “Why haven't we heard his chariots coming?”
translation_verse: Sisera dada do mo ɖe fesre nu, eye wòdo ɣli to adzralawo me gblɔ bena: Nukaŋuti eƒe tasiaɖamwo gbe vava, eye nukaŋuti eƒe sɔwo ƒe afɔzi tsi megbe ale?

english_verse: She and her wisest women gave the same answer:
translation_verse: Nyɔnu bubume, siwo le egbɔ la, ɖo eŋu nɛ; ke egale biabia dzi ko be:

english_verse: “Sisera and his troops are finding treasures to bring back— a woman, or maybe two, for each man, and beautiful dresses for those women to wear.”
translation_verse: Ɖe womekpɔ aboyonu ma oa? Nyɔnuvi ɖeka alo eve na ŋutsu ɖeka, Sisera ƒe aboyonu nanye awu ŋɔŋɔewo, akɔgbavɔ ɖeka alo eve, siwo le ŋɔŋɔe, nanye fiasrɔ̃ ɖeka tɔ!

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
translation_verse: Yehowa, alea wò futɔwo katã atsrɔ̃ enye si! Ke amesiwo lɔ̃nɛ la le, abe alesi ɣe dzena kple ŋusẽ ene. Eye anyigba la ŋu fa ƒe blane sɔŋ.

english_verse: Then once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord, so he let the nation of Midian control Israel for seven years.
translation_verse: Esi Israel-viwo wɔ nusi medze Yehowa ŋu o la, Yehowa tsɔ wo ɖe asi na Midiantɔwo ƒe adre sɔŋ.

english_verse: The Midianites were so cruel that many Israelites ran to the mountains and hid in caves.
translation_verse: Midiantɔwo ƒe asi kpe Israel dzi, eye Israel-viwo wɔ bebeƒewo ɖe towo dzi kple agadowo me kpakple nɔƒe sesẽwo le Midiantɔwo la.

english_verse: Every time the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites invaded Israel together with the Amalekites and other eastern nations.
translation_verse: Godoo ne Israel ƒã nu la, Midiantɔwo kple Amalekitɔwo kpakple ɣedzeƒeviwo hona ɖe wo ŋu,

english_verse: They rode in on their camels, set up their tents, and then let their livestock eat the crops as far as the town of Gaza. The Midianites stole food, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. Like a swarm of locusts, they could not be counted, and they ruined the land wherever they went.
translation_verse: elabena ɖe wohona vana kple woƒe lãwo kpakple agbadɔwo, eye woawo kple woƒe kposɔ naneawo ƒona ɖi bibibi abe ʋetsuviwo ene; ale wovana, be woagblẽ anyigba la.

english_verse: The Midianites took almost everything that belonged to the Israelites, and the Israelites begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Esi Israel-viwo do ɣli yɔ Yehowa le Midiantɔwo ta la,

english_verse: I am your God, and I told you not to worship Amorite gods, even though you are living in the land of the Amorites. But you refused to listen. The Lord Chooses Gideon
translation_verse: Eye megblɔ na mi bena: Nyee nye Yehowa, mia Mawu, migasubɔ Amoritɔ, siwo ƒe anyigba dzi miele la, ƒe mawuwo o; ke miegbe toɖoɖo nye gbe.

english_verse: One day an angel from the Lord went to the town of Ophrah and sat down under the big tree that belonged to Joash, a member of the Abiezer clan. Joash's son Gideon was nearby, threshing grain in a shallow pit, where he could not be seen by the Midianites.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe ɖɔla va bɔbɔ nɔ logoti te le Ofra, si nye Abiesritɔ Yoas tɔ, eye via Gideon le lu ƒom le lugbɔƒe, be wòatsɔ asii le Midiantɔwo nu.

english_verse: The angel appeared and spoke to Gideon, “The Lord is helping you, and you are a strong warrior.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe ɖɔla ɖo ɖe edzi gblɔ nɛ bena: Yehowa li kpli wò, wò ŋutsu kalẽtɔ!

english_verse: Gideon answered, “Please don't take this wrong, but if the Lord is helping us, then why have all of these awful things happened? We've heard how the Lord performed miracles and rescued our ancestors from Egypt. But those things happened long ago. Now the Lord has abandoned us to the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Gideon ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Tsoo, nye aƒetɔ! Ne Yehowa li kpli mi ɖe, nukaŋuti nusiawo katã dzɔ ɖe mia dzi? Eye afika eƒe nukunu, siwo katã ŋu mía fofowo nɔa dze ɖom le na mí be, Yehowa kplɔ mí tso Egipte la le? Azɔ Yehowa tutu mí ƒu gbe, eye wòtsɔ mí ɖe asi na Midiantɔwo.

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa trɔ ɖe eŋu gblɔ bena: Yi le wò ŋusẽ sia nu, eye naɖe Israel tso Midiantɔwo si me, nye ŋutɔe le dɔwòm!

english_verse: Gideon replied, “But how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in Manasseh, and everyone else in my family is more important than I am.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Taflatse, nye aƒetɔ! Nuka tsɔ ge mala ade Israel? Kpɔ ɖa, nye ƒome enye suetɔ le Manase, eye nyee nye dɔmlɔea le tofonye ƒe me!

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord answered, “you can rescue Israel because I am going to help you! Defeating the Midianites will be as easy as beating up one man.”
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ nɛ bena: Manɔ anyi kpli wò kokoko, eye asi Midiantɔwo abe ŋutsu ɖeka ene.

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Edo ŋu nɛ bena: Ne eve nunye la, ekema na dzesim be, wòe le nu ƒom kplim!

english_verse: And wait here until I bring you an offering.” “All right, I'll wait,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Megadzo le afisia o, vaseɖe esime matsɔ nye vɔsanu aɖo akɔwòme hafi! Eɖo ŋu be: Manɔ anyi, vaseɖe esime natrɔ agbɔ.

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: Tete Gideon yi ɖawu gbɔ̃tsuvi ɖeka, eye wotsɔ wɔ eta ɖeka tɔ tatali maʋamaʋã; efɔ lã la ɖe golo me, eye woku detsitsi la de kutu me hetsɔ va egbɔ le logoti la te, eye wòtsɔe ɖo ekɔme.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Ke Mawu ƒe dɔla la gblɔ ne bena: Tsɔ lã kple tatali maʋamaʋã la da ɖe agakpe sia dzi, eye natsɔ detsitsi la akɔ ɖe anyi. Tete wòwɔ nenema

english_verse: The angel was holding a walking stick, and he touched the meat and the bread with the end of the stick. Flames jumped from the rock and burned up the meat and the bread. When Gideon looked, the angel was gone.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe dɔla la tsɔ atikplɔ, si le esi la nu tɔ lã kple tatali maʋamaʋã la dzi, enumake dzo do tso agakpe la me hefiã lã kple tatali maʋamaʋã la, eye Yehowa ƒe dɔla la bu vi le eƒe ŋku me.

english_verse: Gideon realized that he had seen one of the Lord's angels. “Oh!” he moaned. “Now I'm going to die.”
translation_verse: Esi Gideon kpɔ bena, Yehowa ƒe dɔlae la, egblɔ bena: Alele, Aƒetɔ Yehowa! Elabena mekpɔ Yehowa ƒe dɔla ŋku me kple ŋku me.

english_verse: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa gblɔ nɛ bena: Ŋuwo nafa, megavɔ̃ o, mele kuku ge o!

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Eye Gideon ɖi vɔsamlekpui na Yehowa ɖe afima, eye wòna ŋkɔe bena: Yehowae nye ŋutifafa. Ele Abiesritɔwo ƒe Ofra vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: That night the Lord spoke to Gideon again: Get your father's second-best bull, the one that's seven years old. Use it to pull down the altar where your father worships Baal and cut down the sacred pole next to the altar.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ nɛ le zã ma me bena: Lé fofowò ƒe nyitsu ɖeka kpe ɖe nyitsu bubu, si xɔ ƒe adre la ŋu; gbã Baal ƒe vɔsamlekpui, si nye fofowò tɔ, eye nalã Asera, si le eŋu la ɖa!

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: Tete Gideon ɖe ŋutsu ewo le eƒe dɔlawo dome, eye wòwɔ, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ nɛ ene; mewɔe le keli o, ke boŋ ewɔe le zã, elabena ele fofoa ƒemetɔwo kple dua me ŋutsuwo vɔ̃m.

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Esi dua me ŋutsuwo fɔ ŋdi kanya la, kpɔ ɖa, wogbã Baal ƒe vɔsamlekpui la, lã Asera, si le eŋu la ɖa, eye wotsɔ nyitsu sa vɔ le vɔsamlekpui, si woɖi la dzi.

english_verse: “Who could have done such a thing?” they asked. And they kept on asking, until finally someone told them, “Gideon the son of Joash did it.”
translation_verse: Tete wode asi gbɔgblɔ me na wo nɔewo bena: Ameka wɔ nusia? Eye wodzro me hebia eta se, eye wose bena, Gideon, Yoas vi, wɔ nusia.

english_verse: The men of the town went to Joash and said, “Your son Gideon knocked over Baal's altar and cut down the sacred pole next to it. Hand him over, so we can kill him!”
translation_verse: Enumake dua me ŋutsuwo gblɔ na Yoas bena: Kplɔ viwò la doe, ne wòaku, elabena egbã Baal ƒe vɔsamlekpui, eye wòlã Asera, si le eŋu la ɖa.

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Tete Yoas gblɔ na amesiwo katã tsi tre ɖe egbɔ bena: Dzree miehe, yewoawɔ ɖe Baal nua? Alo ɖe miebe, yewoaxɔ nya ɖe enua? Ne amea ɖe be, yeawɔ dzre ɖe enu la, aku ŋdi sia! Nenye Mawue wonye la, ekema newɔ dzre ɖe eɖokui nu, le esi wogbã eƒe vɔsamlekpui la ta!

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: Eye wona ŋkɔe tso gbemagbe be Yerub-Baal hegblɔ bena: Baal newɔ dzre kplii, elabena eyae gbã eƒe vɔsamlekpui.

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Eye Midiantɔwo katã kple Amalekitɔwo kpakple ɣedzeƒeviwo kpe la heho va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Yezreel-bali me.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ yɔ Gideon me fũ; tete woku kpẽ yɔ Abiesritɔwo bena, wòadze eyome.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Edɔ lãme ɖo ɖe Manase blibo la yɔ wo be, wòadze eyome, eye wòdo ame ɖo ɖe Aser, Zebulon kple Naftali, eye wova kpe wo.

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: ekema matsɔ alẽgbalẽ da ɖe lugbɔƒe, eye ne zãmu ƒo alẽgbalẽ la ɖeɖeko, eye anyigba blibo la le ƒuƒuie la, ekema madze sii be, dzinye to ge nala aɖe Israel, abe alesi nègblɔ ene.

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me nenema. Esi wòfɔ ŋdi la, efiã zãmu le alẽgbalẽa me wòyɔ tre bana.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Eye Gideon gblɔ na Mawu bena: Taflatse, megado dɔmedzoe ɖe ŋunye be, megale nu ƒo ge fifia o! Na magatsɔ alẽgbalẽ la atee akpɔ zi ɖeka! Alẽgbalẽ la ɖeɖeko nanɔ ƒuƒuie, ke zãmu naƒo anyigba blibo la dzi!

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Eye Mawu wɔ nenema le zã ma me Alẽgbalẽ la ɖeɖeko dzi le ƒuƒuie, ke zãmu ƒo anyigba la: dzi.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Gideon and his army got up and moved their camp to Fear Spring. The Midianite camp was to the north, in the valley at the foot of Moreh Hill.
translation_verse: Tete Yerub-Baal, si nye Gideon, kple dukɔ blibo, si le eŋu la, fɔ ŋdi kanya va ƒu asaɖa anyi de Xarod-vudo la gbɔ, eye Midiantɔwo ƒe asaɖa le woƒe anyiehe gome, tso More-togbɛ la gbɔ ɖo ta bali la me.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Gideon bena: Amesiwo le ŋuwò la, sɔ gbɔ akpa be, matsɔ Midiantɔwo ade asi na wo; ne Israel magaƒu asi akɔ ɖe ŋunye agblɔ bena: nye ŋutɔ nye asi metsɔ xɔ na ɖokuinye o!

english_verse: So call your troops together and tell them that anyone who is really afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home.” Twenty-two thousand men returned home, leaving Gideon with only
translation_verse: Eyata ɖe gbe ƒã ɖe amea wo ƒe to me bena: Amesi ke le vɔvɔ̃m, eye dzi mele eƒo o la, netrɔ, eye wòagbugbɔ tso Gilead-to la gbɔ! Tete ameawo dome ame akpe blave vɔ eve trɔ dzo, eye ame akpe ewo susɔ.

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Ke ne èle yiyi vɔ̃m la, ekema mia kple wò dɔla Pura miyi asaɖa la me,

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord said, “you still have too many soldiers. Take them down to the spring and I'll test them. I'll tell you which ones can go along with you and which ones must go back home.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Gideon bena: Ameawo: gasɔ gbɔ akpa ko. Kplɔ wo yi tɔ la nu, ne mado wo akpɔ na wò le afima, eye amesi ke magblɔ na wò be, neyi kpli wò la, eya nayi kpli wò; ke amesi ke magblɔ na wò be, megayi kpli wò o la, mayi kpli wò o!

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Esi wòkplɔ ameawo va tɔa nu la, Yehowa gblɔ na Gideon bena: Tia amesiwo ɖuɖɔ tsi la abe avu ene kple amesiwo dze klo kpe nu ɖe; me noe la, ɖe vovo!

english_verse: Three hundred men scooped up water in their hands and lapped it, and the rest knelt to get a drink.
translation_verse: Eye amesiwo kui kple asi kplɔ la, le ame alafa etɔ̃, ke ame mamleawo katã dze klo kpe nu ɖe tsia me noe.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army will be made up of everyone who lapped the water from their hands. Send the others home. I'm going to rescue Israel by helping you and your army of
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Gideon bena: Ame alafa etɔ̃, siwo kui kplɔ la, tsɔ ge mala aɖe mi, eye matsɔ Midiantɔwo aɖe asi na wò; ke ame mamleawo katã negbugbɔ yi aƒe.

english_verse: That night, the Lord said to Gideon. “Get up! Attack the Midianite camp. I am going to let you defeat them,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ nɛ le zã ma me bena: Tso, naɖi yi asaɖa la me, elabena metsɔe ɖe asi na wò!

english_verse: When you hear what the Midianites are saying, you'll be brave enough to attack.” Gideon and Purah worked their way to the edge of the enemy camp, where soldiers were on guard duty.
translation_verse: eye nase nya, si gblɔ ge wòala. Emegbe dzi aɖo ƒowò, eye naho ɖe asaɖa la ŋu. Tete eya kple eƒe dɔla Pura wova asaɖa la me le aʋawɔlawo ƒe dodo nu.

english_verse: The camp was huge. The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. And it would be easier to count the grains of sand on a beach than to count their camels.
translation_verse: Eye Midiantɔwo kple Amalekitɔwo kpakple ɣedzeƒeviwo ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe bali la me kpaŋkpaŋ abe ʋetsuviwo ene, eye woƒe kposɔ naneawo sɔ gbɔ abe ƒutake ene.

english_verse: Gideon overheard one enemy guard telling another, “I had a dream about a flat loaf of barley bread that came tumbling into our camp. It hit the headquarters tent, and the tent flipped over and fell to the ground.”
translation_verse: Esi Gideon va la, kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsua ɖe le drɔ̃e lim na nɔvia bena: Meku drɔ̃e kpɔ luboloa ɖe mli togotogo va Midiantɔwo ƒe asaɖa me, eye wòlɔ aʋafia ƒe agbadɔ wòmã dze anyi hetrɔ gbo, eye agbadɔla tsi nenema.

english_verse: The other soldier answered, “Your dream must have been about Gideon, the Israelite commander. It means God will let him and his army defeat the Midianite army and everyone else in our camp.”
translation_verse: Tete nɔvia ɖo ŋu ne bena: Menye nu bubua ɖekee o, ke boŋ Israeltɔ Gideon, Yoas vi la, ƒe yie. Mawu tsɔ Midiantɔwo kple woƒe asaɖa blibo la ɖe asi nɛ.

english_verse: As soon as Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to praise God. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, “Let's go! The Lord is going to let us defeat the Midianite army.”
translation_verse: Esi Gideon se drɔ̃e la kple egɔme la, edo gbe ɖa; emegbe wògbugbɔ va Israel ƒe asaɖa la me gblɔ bena: Mitso, elabena Yehowa tsɔ Midiantɔwo ƒe asaɖa la de asi na mí!

english_verse: Gideon said, “When we get to the enemy camp, spread out and surround it. Then wait for me to blow a signal on my trumpet. As soon as you hear it, blow your trumpets and shout, ‘Fight for the Lord! Fight for Gideon!’ ”
translation_verse: Ne mía kple amesiwo katã le gbɔnye míeku kpẽawo la, ekema mi amesiwo katã ƒo xlã asaɖa blibo la godoo la, miaku kpẽawo ahagblɔ bena: Yehowa kple Gideon tɔe!

english_verse: Gideon and his group reached the edge of the enemy camp a few hours after dark, just after the new guards had come on duty. Gideon and his soldiers blew their trumpets and smashed the clay jars that were hiding the torches.
translation_verse: Eye Gideon kple ame alafa ɖeka, siwo le eŋu la, va asaɖa la ƒe mlɔeanu le zãtiƒe, esime woɖe ŋudzɔnɔlawo ɖo anyi tetee; eye woku kpẽawo hegbà ze, siwo le wo si.

english_verse: The rest of Gideon's soldiers blew the trumpets they were holding in their right hands. Then they smashed the jars and held the burning torches in their left hands. Everyone shouted, “Fight with your swords for the Lord and for Gideon!”
translation_verse: Eye aʋalɔgo etɔ̃awo ku kpẽawo hegbã zeawo; wole akakatiawo ɖe mia, eye wòlé kpẽawo ɖe ɖusi le kukum hele ɣli dom bena: Yehowa kple Gideon tɔe nye yi la!

english_verse: The enemy soldiers started yelling and tried to run away. Gideon's troops stayed in their positions surrounding the camp
translation_verse: Amesiame tɔ ɖe eteƒe le asaɖa la ŋu godoo, tete zi ƒo ɖe asaɖa blibo la me, eye wole ɣli dom hele sisim.

english_verse: and blew their trumpets again. As they did, the Lord made the enemy soldiers pull out their swords and start fighting each other. The enemy army tried to escape from the camp. They ran to Acacia Tree Town, toward Zeredah, and as far as the edge of the land that belonged to the town of Abel-Meholah near Tabbath.
translation_verse: Esime ame alafa etɔ̃awo le kpẽawo kum la, Yehowa na amesiame trɔ yi nu ɖe nɔvia ŋu le asaɖa blibo la me, eye aʋakɔ la si, vaseɖe Bet-Sita ɖo ta Zereda va ke ɖe Abel-Mexola ƒe liƒo ŋu hegbɔ Tabat ŋu yi.

english_verse: Gideon sent word for more Israelite soldiers to come from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher, and both halves of Manasseh to help fight the Midianites.
translation_verse: Eye woyɔ Israel-ŋutsuwo tso Naftali kple Aser kpakple Manase blibo la, eye wonyã Midiantɔwo ɖe nu.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to tell all the men who lived in the hill country of Ephraim, “Come and help us fight the Midianites! Put guards at every spring, stream, and well, as far as Beth-Barah before the Midianites can get to them. And guard the Jordan River.” Troops from Ephraim did exactly what Gideon had asked,
translation_verse: Eye! Gideon do ame ɖo ɖe Efrayim-to blibo la dzi gblɔ bena: Miyi ɖaxe towo kple Yordan nu na Midiantɔwo vaseɖe Bet-Bara! Tete woyɔ Efrayim-ŋutsuwo katã, eye woxe tɔawo kple Yordan nu vaseɖe Bet-Bara.

english_verse: and they even helped chase the Midianites on the east side of the Jordan River. These troops captured Raven and Wolf, the two Midianite leaders. They killed Raven at a large rock that has come to be known as Raven Rock, and they killed Wolf near a wine-pit that has come to be called Wolf Wine-Pit. The men of Ephraim brought the heads of the two Midianite leaders to Gideon.
translation_verse: Eye wòlé Midiantɔwo ƒe amegã eveawo, Oreb kple Zeeb; wowu Oreb ɖe Oreb-kpe la gbã, eye wowu Zeeb ɖe Zeeb ƒe weinfiãƒe. Emegbe woti Midiantɔwo yome, eye wotsɔ Oreb kple Zeeb ƒe ta vɛ na Gideon le Yordan ƒe go keme dzi.

english_verse: But the men were really upset with Gideon and complained, “When you went to war with Midian, you didn't ask us to help! Why did you treat us like that?”
translation_verse: Tete Efrayim-ŋutsuwo gblɔ nɛ bena: Nuka nye esi nèwɔ ɖe mía ŋu, eye esi neho aʋa ɖe Midiantɔwo ŋu la, negbe mia yɔyɔ? Eye wohe dzre kplii vevie.

english_verse: Gideon answered: Don't be upset! Even though you came later, you were able to do much more than I did. It's just like the grape harvest: The grapes your tribe doesn't even bother to pick are better than the best grapes my family can grow.
translation_verse: Ke eɖo ŋu na wo bena: Ɖe miawo miewɔ wum oa? Ɖe Efrayim ƒe weinxaxa mlɔetɔ menyo wu Abieser ƒe weinxaxa blibo la oa?

english_verse: Besides, God chose you to capture Raven and Wolf. I didn't do a thing compared to you. By the time Gideon had finished talking, the men of Ephraim had calmed down and were no longer angry with him. Gideon Finishes Destroying the Midianite Army
translation_verse: Mawu tso Midian-amegãwo, Oreb kple Zeeb, de asi na mi, eye nuka mewo tso wu mi? Esi wògblɔ nya sia la, woƒe dziku la nu fa.

english_verse: The town of Succoth was nearby, so he went there and asked, “Please give my troops some food. They are worn out, but we have to keep chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the two Midianite kings.”
translation_verse: egblɔ na Sukottɔwo bena: Midi aboloa ɖewo na amesiwo le yonyeme la, elabena ɖeɖi te wo ŋu belibeli, eva mele Zebax kple Zalmuna, Midtan-fiawo, yome tim.

english_verse: The town leaders of Succoth answered, “Why should we feed your army? We don't know if you really will defeat Zebah and Zalmunna.”
translation_verse: Sukot-amegãwo ɖo ŋu bena: Ɖe wò asi tu Zebax kple Zalmuna, hafi miatso abolo na wò aʋakɔ la?

english_verse: “Just wait!” Gideon said. “After the Lord helps me defeat them, I'm coming back here. I'll make a whip out of thorns and rip the flesh from your bones.”
translation_verse: Eye Gideon gblɔ bena: Enyo! Ne Yehowa tsɔ Zebax kple Zalmuna de asi nam la, ekema matsɔ gbedadaƒoŋɔka kple ŋuwo adze mia ŋutii.

english_verse: After leaving Succoth, Gideon went to Penuel and asked the leaders there for some food. But he got the same answer as he did at Succoth.
translation_verse: Eye woho tso afima yi Penuel, eye wògblɔ na woawo hã alea ke, ke Penueltɔwo ɖo ŋu nɛ abe Sukottɔwo ke ene.

english_verse: “I'll come back safe and sound,” Gideon said, “but when I do, I'm going to tear down your tower!”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ na Penueltɔwo bena: Ne metrɔ gbɔ le ŋutifafa me la, magbã mɔ̃ sia aƒu anyi!

english_verse: Gideon went to the town officials and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. Remember how you made fun of me? You said, ‘We don't know if you really will defeat those two Midianite kings. So why should we feed your worn-out army?’ ”
translation_verse: Eye esi wòva Sukottɔwo gbɔ la, egblɔ bena: Zebax kple Zalmuna enye si, amesiwo mietsɔ ɖu fewu le ŋunye gblɔ bena: Ɖe wò asi tu Zebax kple Zalmuna, hafi miana abolo wò ame, siwo ŋu ɖeɖi te belibeli la mahã?

english_verse: Gideon reached the enemy camp by going east along Nomad Road past Nobah and Jogbehah. He made a surprise attack,
translation_verse: Eye Gideon to asimɔ gã dzi le Nobax kple Yogbeha ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome, eye wòsi aʋakɔ la, le esime woli bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: and the enemy panicked. Zebah and Zalmunna tried to escape, but Gideon chased and captured them.
translation_verse: Tete Zebax kple Zalmuna wòsi, eye woti wo yome helé Midian-fia eveawo, Zebax kple Zalmuna, eye wòde zi asaɖa blibo la me.

english_verse: After the battle, Gideon set out for home. As he was going through Heres Pass,
translation_verse: Esi Gideon, Yoas vi, trɔ tso aʋa la tso Xeres-to dzi mo nu la,

english_verse: he caught a young man who lived in Succoth. Gideon asked him who the town officials of Succoth were, and the young man wrote down
translation_verse: ele Sukot-ɖekakpuia ɖe, eyewòbiae wòŋlɔ Sukot-amegãwo kple ame tsitsiwo ŋkɔ nɛ, wole ame blaadre va adre.

english_verse: Gideon made a whip from thorn plants and used it to beat the town officials.
translation_verse: Emegbe wòlé dua me tsitsiawo, eye wòna Sukottɔwo ʋẽ gbedadaƒoŋɔka kple ŋuwo se.

english_verse: Afterwards he went to Penuel, where he tore down the tower and killed all the town officials.
translation_verse: Egbã Penuel mɔ̃ la ƒu anyi, eye wowu duametɔwo.

english_verse: Then Gideon said, “Zebah and Zalmunna, tell me about the men you killed at Tabor.” “They were a lot like you,” the two kings answered. “They were dignified, almost like royalty.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na Zebax kple Zalmuna bena: Ŋutsu ka ƒomeviwoe miewu le Tabor gbɔ? Woɖo ŋu bena: Wole abe wò ene, eye wo dome ɖesiaɖe ɖi fiavi.

english_verse: “They were my very own brothers!” Gideon said. “I swear by the living Lord that if you had let them live, I would let you live.”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ bena: Nɔvinyeŋutsuwoe, danyeviwo wonye. Meta si Yehowa ƒe agbe! Ɖe wònye ɖe miena wotsi agbe la, anye ne nyemele mia wu ge o.

english_verse: kilograms. In addition, there was the gold from the camels' ornaments and from the beautiful jewelry worn by the Midianite kings. Gideon also took their purple robes.
translation_verse: Enumake wògblɔ na eƒe ŋgɔgbevi Yeter bena: Tso, nawu wo! Ke ele vɔvɔ̃m, eye meɖi eƒe yi o, elabena ɖevi wònye.

english_verse: “What's the matter, Gideon?” Zebah and Zalmunna asked. “Do it yourself, if you're not too much of a coward!” Gideon jumped up and killed them both. Then he took the gold ornaments from the necks of their camels. The Israelites Ask Gideon To Be Their King
translation_verse: Tete Zebax kple Zalmuna gblɔ bena: Wò ŋutɔ tso, nadza mí, elabena ŋutsu kple eƒe ŋusẽe sɔ! Tete Gideon tsi tre, eye wowu Zebax kple Zalmuna; eye wòɖe kogɛ, siwo le kɔ na woƒe kposɔwo. Gideon ɖo trɔ̃subɔsubɔ anyi.

english_verse: After the battle with the Midianites, the Israelites said, “Gideon, you rescued us! Now we want you to be our king. Then after your death, your son and then your grandson will rule.”
translation_verse: Tete Israeltɔwo gblɔ na Gideon bena: Wò ŋutɔ kple viwòŋutsu kpakple viwòŋutsu ƒe vi miɖu fia ɖe mía dzi, elabena wòe ɖe mí tso Midiantɔwo si me!

english_verse: “No,” Gideon replied, “I won't be your king, and my son won't be king either. Only the Lord is your ruler.
translation_verse: Gideon ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Nye ŋutɔ alo vinyeŋutsu míaɖu fia ɖe mia dzi o, ke boŋ Yehowa neɖu fía ɖe mia dzi!

english_verse: But I will ask you to do one thing: Give me all the earrings you took from the enemy.” The enemy soldiers had been Ishmaelites, and they wore gold earrings.
translation_verse: Gideon gblɔ na wo bena: Nu ɖeka biam mele tso mia si, mia dome amesiame netsɔ togɛ, siwo woha la nam. Ismaeltɔwo wonye, eyata woɖo sikatogɛ.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers replied, “Of course we will give you the earrings.” Then they spread out a robe on the ground and tossed the earrings on it.
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu bena: Miana wò baa! Tete wokeke avɔ ɖe anyi, eye amesiame fɔ togɛ, si woha la, va ɖa ɖe eme.

english_verse: He even had a wife who lived at Shechem. They had a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
translation_verse: Eye eƒe ahiã, si le Sixem la, dzi ŋutsuvi nɛ, eye wòtsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ bena Abimelex.

english_verse: Gideon lived to be an old man. And when he died, he was buried in the family tomb in his hometown of Ophrah, which belonged to the Abiezer clan.
translation_verse: Gideon, Yoas vi la, tsi ŋutɔ hafi ku, eye woɖii ɖe fofoa Yoas ƒe yɔɖo me le Abiesritɔwo ƒe Ofra.

english_verse: Soon after Gideon's death, the Israelites turned their backs on God again. They set up idols of Baal and worshiped Baal Berith as their god.
translation_verse: Esi Gideon nya ku ko la, Israel-viwo trɔ hesubɔ Baalwo, eye wotsɔ Baal-Berit wɔ woƒe mawui.

english_verse: The Israelites forgot that the Lord was their God, and that he had rescued them from the enemies who lived around them.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ƒe ŋku dzo le Yehowa, woƒe Mawu la dzi, amesi ɖe wo tso woƒe futɔwo katã, siwo ƒo xlã wo godoo la si me.

english_verse: Besides all that, the Israelites were unkind to Gideon's family, even though Gideon had done so much for Israel.
translation_verse: Eye womeve Yerub-Baal, amesi nye Gideon la ƒe ƒomeawo nu o, evɔ wònye ewo nyui geɖe na Israel hafi.

english_verse: and told them to say to the leaders of Shechem, “Do you think it would be good to have all
translation_verse: Miƒo nu ɖe Sixemtɔwo ƒe to me bena: Kae nyo na mi wu; Yerub-Baal vi blaadreawo katã naɖu fia ɖe mia dzi loo, alo ame ɖeka naɖu fia ɖe mia dzia? Minyae bena, nyee nye mia ƒu kple mia ŋutilã!

english_verse: Abimelech's uncles talked it over with the leaders of Shechem who agreed, “Yes, it would be better for one of our relatives to be king.”
translation_verse: Tete dadaa nɔviwo gblɔ nya siawo katã ɖe Sixemtɔwo katã ƒe to me, eye woƒe dzi trɔ ɖe Abimelex ŋu, elabena wobui wo nɔvii.

english_verse: Abimelech and his soldiers went to his father's home in Ophrah and brought out Gideon's other sons to a large rock, where they murdered all
translation_verse: Eye wòva fofoa ƒe me le Ofra, eye wowu nɔviawo, siwo nye Yerub-Baal vi blaadreawo, ɖe kpe ɖeka dzi; ke Yotam, si nye Yerub-Baal ƒe dɔmlɔea, tsi agbe, elabena eɣla eɖokui.

english_verse: The leaders of Shechem, including the priests and the military officers, met at the tree next to the sacred rock in Shechem to crown Abimelech king.
translation_verse: Eye Sixemtɔwo katã kple Milo-nɔlawo katã va kpe ta, eye woɖo fia Abimelex le logoti, si nye ŋkuɖodziti le Sixem la gbɔ. Yotam ƒe glinya la.

english_verse: Jotham heard what they were doing. So he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted down to the people who were there at the meeting: Leaders of Shechem, listen to me, and maybe God will listen to you.
translation_verse: Esi wogblɔ nya sia na Yotam la, eyi ɖatsi tre ɖe Gerizim-to la dzi, eye wòdo ɣli sesĩe gblɔ na wo bena: Mi Sixemtɔwo, miɖo tom, ne Mawu naɖo to mi!

english_verse: Once the trees searched for someone to be king; they asked the olive tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka atiwo be, yewoaɖo fia ɖe yewo ɖokui nu, eye wogblɔ na amiti bena: Ɖu fia ɖe mía dzi!

english_verse: But the olive tree replied, “My oil brings honor to people and gods. I won't stop making oil, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Tete amiti gblɔ na wo bena: Magblẽ nye ami, si mawuwo kple amegbetɔwo kafuna nam la ɖi, ne mayi aɖanɔ agba sam ɖe atiwo dzia?

english_verse: Then they asked the fig tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Atiawo gblɔ na gboti bena: Wòava ɖu fia ɖe mía dzi!

english_verse: But the fig tree replied, “I won't stop growing my delicious fruit, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Tete gboti gblɔ na wo bena: Magblẽ nye tsi vivi kple nye kutsetse xɔasiwo ɖi, ne mayi aɖanɔ agba sam ɖe atiwo dzia?

english_verse: Next they asked the grape vine, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Atiawo gblɔ na weinka bena Wòa va naɖu fia ɖe mía dzi!

english_verse: But the grape vine replied, “My wine brings cheer to people and gods. I won't stop making wine, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Tete weinka ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Magblẽ nye tsetse me tsi, si doa dzidzɔ na mawuwo kple amegbetɔwo la ɖi, ne mayi aɖanɔ agba sam ɖe atiwo dzia?

english_verse: Finally, they went to the thornbush and asked, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Eye atiawo katã gblɔ na ŋuve bena: Wòa va ɖu fia ɖe mía dzi!

english_verse: The thornbush replied, “If you really want me to be your king, then come into my shade and I will protect you. But if you're deceiving me, I'll start a fire that will spread out and destroy the cedars of Lebanon.” After Jotham had finished telling this story, he said:
translation_verse: Tete ŋuve gblɔ na atiawo bena: Nenye nyateƒe to gblɔm miele be, miasi ami nam manye fia ɖe mia dzi la, ekema miva bè ɖe nye vɔvɔli te! Ne menye nenem o la, ekema dzo ado tso ŋuve la me, eye wòafiã Libanon ƒe sedertiwo!

english_verse: My father Gideon risked his life for you when he fought to rescue you from the Midianites. Did you reward Gideon by being kind to his family? No, you did not! You attacked his family and killed all
translation_verse: hafi miawo miedze aglã ɖe fofonye ƒe aƒe ŋu egbea, eye miewu via blaadreawo ɖe kpe ɖeka dzi hetsɔ eƒe ahiã ƒe vi Abimelex ɖo fia ɖe Sixemtɔwo nu, le esi wònye mia nɔvi ta.

english_verse: So, you leaders of Shechem, if you treated Gideon and his family the way you should have, then I hope you and Abimelech will make each other very happy.
translation_verse: Nenye nuteƒe kple nu dzɔdzɔe wònye miewɔ na Yerub-Baal ƒe aƒe egbe la, ekema mikpɔ dzidzɔ le Abimelex ŋu, eye eya hã nakpɔ dzidzɔ le mia ŋu!

english_verse: But if it was wrong to treat Gideon and his family the way you did, then I pray that Abimelech will destroy you with fire, and I pray that you will do the same to him.
translation_verse: Ne menye nenem o la, ekema dzo nedo tso Abimelex me, ne wòafiã Sixemtɔwo kple Milo-nɔlawo, eye dzo nedo tso Sixemtɔwo kple Milo-nɔlawo me, ne wòafiã Abimelex!

english_verse: Jotham ran off and went to live in the town of Beer, where he could be safe from his brother Abimelech. Abimelech Destroys Shechem
translation_verse: Tete Yotam si le nɔvia Abimelex nu yi Beer, eye, wònɔ afima. Abimelex ƒe nuwuwu.

english_verse: Abimelech had been a military commander of Israel for three years,
translation_verse: Esi Abimelex ɖu Israel dzi ƒe etɔ̃ la,

english_verse: Then they sent some men to hide on the hilltops and watch for Abimelech and his troops, while they sent others to rob everyone that went by on the road. But Abimelech found out what they were doing.
translation_verse: Eye Sixemtɔwo ɖe amewo wode xa ɖe towo dzi ɖe eŋuti, eye woda adzo amesiwo to mɔ dzi yi. Tete wova gblɔe na Abimelex.

english_verse: One day, Gaal son of Ebed went to live in Shechem. His brothers moved there too, and soon the leaders of Shechem started trusting him.
translation_verse: Ekema me Gaal, Ebed vi, kple nɔviawo va Sixem. Eye esi! Sixemtɔwo ɖo ŋu ɖe eŋu la,

english_verse: Gaal said: Hamor was the founder of Shechem, and one of his descendants should be our ruler. But Abimelech's father was Gideon, so Abimelech isn't really one of us. He shouldn't be our king, and we shouldn't have to obey him or Zebul, who rules Shechem for him.
translation_verse: Eye Gaal, Ebed vi, gblɔ bena: Ameka nye Abimelex, eye ameka nye Sixemtɔ ma ƒe vi, ne míasubɔe? Ɖe menye eyae nye Yerub-Baal ƒe vi, eye wòtsɔ Zebul ɖo dumegã oa? Misubɔ Sixem fofo Hemor ƒe viwo boŋ! Nuka la gɔ̃ miasubɔ eya ɖo?

english_verse: If I were the ruler of Shechem, I'd get rid of that Abimelech. I'd tell him, “Get yourself an even bigger army, and we will still defeat you.”
translation_verse: Ɖe wònye dukɔ sia asinye mee wòle la, ne manyã Abimelex, eye magblɔ na Abimelex bena: Dzi wò aʋakɔ ɖe dzi, eye naho aʋa!

english_verse: Zebul was angry when he found out what Gaal had said.
translation_verse: Esi dumegã Zebul se Gaal, Ebed vi ƒe nyawo la, eve dome nɛ,

english_verse: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
translation_verse: Eyata mia kple wò amewo mifɔ zã, ne miava de xa ɖe gbe me!

english_verse: Get up the next morning at sunrise and rush out of your hiding places to attack the town. Gaal and his followers will come out to fight you, but you will easily defeat them.
translation_verse: Ne ŋu ke, eye ɣe dze la, nava dze ɖu la dzi; ekema eya kple eƒe amewo aho ɖe ŋuwò, eye nawɔe, abe alesi nakpɔ mɔnu le eŋu ene.

english_verse: So one night, Abimelech led his soldiers to Shechem. He divided them into four groups, and they all hid near the town.
translation_verse: Tete Abimelex kple aʋakɔ blibo, si le eŋu la, fɔ zã heva de xa ɖe Sixem ŋu le atidzedze ene me.

english_verse: The next morning, Gaal went out and stood in the opening of the town gate. Abimelech and his soldiers left their hiding places,
translation_verse: Esi Gaal, Ebed vi, do yi ɖatsi tre ɖe dua ƒe agbo nu la, tete Abimelex kple aʋakɔ, si le eŋu la, do tso xa me.

english_verse: and Gaal saw them. Zebul was standing there with Gaal, and Gaal remarked, “Zebul, that looks like a crowd of people coming down from the mountaintops.” “No,” Zebul answered, “it's just the shadows of the mountains. It only looks like people moving.”
translation_verse: Eye esi Gaal kpɔ aʋakɔa la, egblɔ na Zebul bena: Kpɔ ɖa, aʋakɔa ɖe nye kem le ɖiɖim tso to la dzi! Ke Zebul ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Towo ƒe vɔvɔli kpɔm nèle be, amewoe.

english_verse: “But Zebul, look over there,” Gaal said. “There's a crowd coming down from the sacred mountain, and another group is coming along the road from the tree where people talk with the spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Ke Gaal gagblɔ ne bena: Kpɔ ɖa, amewo le ɖiɖim tso anyigba ƒe kɔkɔƒe, eye aʋalɔgo ɖeka to dzotɔwo ƒe logoti gbɔ mɔ!

english_verse: Then Zebul replied, “What good is all of your bragging now? You were the one who said Abimelech shouldn't be the ruler of Shechem. Out there is the army that you made fun of. So go out and fight them!”
translation_verse: Tete Zebul gblɔ nɛ bena: Menye wòe le nu me ɖim le gbɔgblɔm bena: ameka nye Abimelex, ne míasubɔe oa? Esia nye aʋakɔ, si ŋu nèle alɔme ɖem le. Azɔ ho, nayi aɖawɔ aʋa kplii!

english_verse: Gaal and the leaders of Shechem went out and fought Abimelech.
translation_verse: Tete Gaal ho dze Sixemtɔwo ŋgɔ, eye wòwɔ aʋa kple Abimelex.

english_verse: Soon the people of Shechem turned and ran back into the town. However, Abimelech and his troops were close behind and killed many of them along the way.
translation_verse: Ke Abimelex nyãe, eye wòsi le enu vaseɖe agbo nu, eye ame geɖewo tsi aʋa.

english_verse: Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
translation_verse: Abimelex tsi Aruma, ke Zebul nyã Gaal kple nɔviawo, ale be womekpɔ mɔ anɔ Sixem o.

english_verse: The next morning, the people of Shechem were getting ready to work in their fields as usual, but someone told Abimelech about it.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke, eye amewo yi agble la, wova gblɔe na Abimelex.

english_verse: Abimelech divided his army into three groups and set up an ambush in the fields near Shechem. When the people came out of the town, he and his army rushed out from their hiding places and attacked.
translation_verse: Tete wòmã aʋakɔ la ɖe aʋalɔgo etɔ̃ me, eye wòyi ɖade xa ɖe gbe me. Eye esi wòkpɔ be, amewo do tso dua me gbɔna la, edo ɖewo ŋu, eye wòwu wo.

english_verse: Abimelech and the troops with him ran to the town gate and took control of it, while two other groups attacked and killed the people who were in the fields.
translation_verse: Abimelex kple aʋalɔgo, si le eŋu la, va xe du la ƒe agbo nu, ke aʋalɔgo eve yi ɖadze amesiwo katã le agble la dzi, eye wowu wo.

english_verse: He and his troops fought in Shechem all day, until they had killed everyone in town. Then he and his men tore down the houses and buildings and scattered salt everywhere.
translation_verse: Emegbe Abimelex wɔ aʋa kple ɖu la ŋkeke blibo la katã, eye wòxɔ du la hewu eme nɔlawo, eye wògbã du la hewu dze ɖe edzi.

english_verse: Earlier that day, the leaders of the temple of El Berith at Shechem had heard about the attack. So they went into the temple fortress,
translation_verse: Esi Sixem-mɔ̃metɔwo see la, woyi ɖe mɔ̃, si le mawu Berit ƒe me la me.

english_verse: but Abimelech found out where they were.
translation_verse: Eye wova gblɔe na Abimelex bena, Sixem-mɔ̃metɔwo katã ƒo ƒu.

english_verse: He led his troops to Mount Zalmon, where he took an ax and chopped off a tree branch. He lifted the branch onto his shoulder and shouted, “Hurry! Cut off a branch just as I did.”
translation_verse: Tete Abimelex kple aʋakɔ, siwo katã le eŋu la, yi Zalmon-to la dzi, eye Abimelex tsɔ fia lã atilɔ hetsɔ ɖe abɔta, eye wògblɔ na eƒe amewo bena: Netsɔ, miawɔ abe alesi mewɔ miekpɔ ene!

english_verse: When they all had branches, they followed Abimelech back to Shechem. They piled the branches against the fortress and set them on fire, burning down the fortress and killing about
translation_verse: Tete ana ka blibo la lã atilɔwo hedze Abimelex yome, eye wotsɔ wo va kɔ ɖe mɔ̃ la ŋu hetɔ dzo mɔ̃ la. Ale Sixem-mɔ̃metɔwo katã hã ku woanɔ ŋutsu akpe ɖeka hekpe ɖe nyɔnuwo ŋu.

english_verse: After destroying Shechem, Abimelech went to Thebez. He surrounded the town and captured it.
translation_verse: Emegbe Abimelex ho ɖe Tebez ŋu, eye wòɖe to ɖe Tebez hexɔe.

english_verse: But there was a tall fortress in the middle of the town, and the town leaders and everyone else went inside. Then they barred the gates and went up to the flat roof.
translation_verse: Mɔ̃ sesẽa ɖe le dua titina, eye duametɔwo katã, ŋutsuwo kple nyɔnuwo, si yi ɖe afi ma hedo ʋɔ ɖe wo ɖokui nu, eye wode mɔ̃ la tame.

english_verse: Abimelech and his army rushed to the fortress and tried to force their way inside. Abimelech himself was about to set the heavy wooden doors on fire,
translation_verse: Eye Abimelex te ɖe mɔ̃ la ŋu hewɔ aʋa kplii, eye wòva kekeke mɔ̃ la ƒe agbo nu, be yeatɔ dzoe.

english_verse: when a woman on the roof dropped a large rock on his head and cracked his skull.
translation_verse: Tete nyɔnua ɖe tsɔ tevi xlã ɖe la na Abimelex, eye wògbã ta le enu.

english_verse: The soldier who carried his weapons was nearby, and Abimelech told him, “Take out your sword and kill me. I don't want people to say that I was killed by a woman!” So the soldier ran his sword through Abimelech.
translation_verse: Enumake wòyɔ eƒe adekplɔvi gblɔ ne bena: Di wò yi, ne natrɔm ɖo, ne womagagblɔ ɖe ŋunye be, nyɔnue wui o! Tete eƒe adekplɔvi da nui wòku.

english_verse: And when the Israelite soldiers saw that their leader was dead, they went back home.
translation_verse: Esi Israeltɔwo kpɔ bena, Abimelex ku la, amesiame gbugbɔ yi aƒe.

english_verse: That's how God punished Abimelech for killing his brothers and bringing shame on his father's family.
translation_verse: Ale Mawu ɖo Abimelex ƒe nu vlo, si wòwɔ ɖe fofoa ŋu hewu nɔvia blaadreawo la, teƒe nɛ.

english_verse: God also punished the people of Shechem for helping Abimelech. Everything happened just as Jotham's curse said it would.
translation_verse: Eye Mawu he nu vlo, siwo katã Sixemtɔwo wo la, va wo dzi. Ale Yotam, Yerub-Baal vi, ƒe fiƒode la ɖi wo ŋu.

english_verse: Tola was the next person to rescue Israel. He belonged to the Issachar tribe, but he lived in Shamir, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His father was Puah, and his grandfather was Dodo.
translation_verse: Le Abimelex megbe la Isaxartɔ Tola, si nye Pua, Dodo vi ƒe vi ɖo, be yeaxɔ na Israel, eye wònɔ Samir le Efrayim-to la dzi.

english_verse: The next leader of Israel was Jair, who lived in Gilead. He was a leader for
translation_verse: Eya megbe Gilead-tɔ Yair do, eye wòdrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel ƒe blave vɔ eve sɔŋ.

english_verse: When he died, he was buried in the town of Kamon. Israel Is Unfaithful to God
translation_verse: Eye Yair ku woɖii ɖe Kamon. Filistitɔwo kple Amon-viwo ɖe fu na Israel-viwo.

english_verse: Before long, the Israelites began disobeying the Lord by worshiping Baal, Astarte, and gods from Syria, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, and Philistia.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo yi dzi wɔ nusi medze Yehowa ŋu o, eye wosubɔ Baalwo kple Astarot, Aramtɔwo ƒe mawuwo, Zidontɔwo ƒe mawuwo, Moabtɔwo ƒe mawuwo, Amon-viwo ƒe mawuwo kple Filistitɔwo ƒe mawuwo, ke wogblẽ Yehowa ɖi, eye womesubɔe o.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and decided to let Philistia and Ammon conquer them.
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa do dɔmedzoe ɖe Israel ŋu, eye wotsɔ wo dzra na Filistitɔwo kple Amon-viwo.

english_verse: The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Tete Gileadtɔwo ƒe amegãwo gblɔ na wo bena: Amesi ayi aɖakpe aʋa kple Amon-viwo gbã la, eya anye natɔ ɖe Gileadtɔwo nu!

english_verse: Then the Ammonites began crossing the Jordan and attacking the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Life was miserable for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Eye Amon-viwo tso Yordan, be woawɔ ana kple Yuda kple Benyamin kpakple Efrayim-viwo, eye Israel ɖo xaxa me.

english_verse: They begged the Lord for help and confessed, “We were unfaithful to you, our Lord. We stopped worshiping you and started worshiping idols of Baal.”
translation_verse: Eyata Israel-viwo ɖo ɣli yɔ Yehowa bena: Miewɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò, elabena miegblẽ miaƒe Mawu ɖi hesubɔ Baalwo.

english_verse: “We have been unfaithful to you,” the Israelites admitted. “If we must be punished, do it yourself, but please rescue us from the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Ke Israel-viwo gblɔ na Yehowa bena: Miewɔ nuvɔ̃, eyata wɔ mí, alesi dze ŋuwò; ke ɖe mí fifia ko!

english_verse: Then the Israelites got rid of the idols of the foreign gods, and they began worshiping only the Lord. Finally, there came a time when the Lord could no longer stand to see them suffer. The Ammonites Invade Gilead
translation_verse: Tete woɖe mawu bubuawo ɖa le wo ɖokui dome hesubɔ Yehowa; eyata Israel ƒe fukpekpe la mena wòɖe dzi ɖi o.

english_verse: The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp. The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there.
