translation_verse: Eye Amon-viwo kpe ta heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Gilead, eye Israel-viwo hã kpe ta va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Mizpa.

english_verse: “Please come back to Gilead! If you lead our army, we will be able to fight off the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na Yefta bena: Va nanye míaƒe aʋafia, ne miawo aʋa kple Amon-viwo!

english_verse: “Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
translation_verse: Tete Yefta ɖo ŋu na Gilead-ame tsitsiwo bena: Menye miawoe le fum, eye mienyãm tso fofonye ƒe me oa? Azã esi mieɖo xaxa me la, mieva gbɔnye!

english_verse: “But we do want you to come back,” the leaders said. “And if you lead us in battle against the Ammonites, we will make you the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Gilead-ame tsitsiwo gblɔ na Yefta bena: Esia ta pɛ mieva gbɔwo ɖo, be nayi kpli mi, ne miawo aʋa kple Amon-viwo, eye natre zu nato ɖe Gileadtɔwo katã nu!

english_verse: “All right,” Jephthah said. “If I go back with you and the Lord lets me defeat the Ammonites, will you really make me your ruler?”
translation_verse: Eye Yefta gblɔ na Gilead-ame tsitsiwo bena: Ne miekplɔm meyi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Amon-viwo, eye Yehowa tso wo ɖe asi nam la, ekema manye miaƒe tatɔ.

english_verse: “You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
translation_verse: Gilead-ame tsitsiwo gblɔ na Yefta bena: Yehowa enye ɖasefo le mía dome! Miawo, abe alesi nègblɔ ene kokoko.

english_verse: So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
translation_verse: Tete Yefta yi kple Gilead-ame tsitsiawo, eye Yefta gblɔ nya siawo katã le Yehowa ŋku me le Mizpa.

english_verse: After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
translation_verse: Eye Yefta do amewo ɖo ɖe Amon-viwo ƒe fia gbɔ gblɔ bena: Nya ka le mía dome, hafi nèho ɖe ŋunye, be nawɔ aʋa kple nye anyigba?

english_verse: The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
translation_verse: Amon-viwo ƒe fia gblɔ na Yefta ƒe dolawo bena: Elabena Israel xɔ nye anyigba, esime wotso Egipte va, tso Arnon nu vaseɖe Yabok kple Yordan nu; eyata gagbugbɔe nam kpoo!

english_verse: Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon,
translation_verse: Tete Yefta gadɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Amon-viwo ƒe fia eho,

english_verse: and they told him that Jephthah had said: Israel hasn't taken any territory from Moab or Ammon.
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Yefta ƒe gbe enye si: Israel mexɔ anyigbaa ɖeke le Moabtɔwo kple Amon-viwo si o.

english_verse: When the Israelites came from Egypt, they traveled across the desert to the Red Sea and then to Kadesh.
translation_verse: Elabena esi Israel tso Egipte, eye wòto gbedzi va Avaƒu la nu heva ɖo Kades la,

english_verse: They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
translation_verse: edo ame ɖo ɖe Edom-fia be, woagblɔ nɛ bena: Na mato wò anyigba dzi ayi! Ke Edom-fia melɔ̃ edzi nɛ o. Eda ame ɖo ɖe Moab-fia gbã, ke eya hã gbe; eyata Israel tsi Kades.

english_verse: A little later, the Israelites set out into the desert, going east of Edom and Moab, and camping on the eastern side of the Arnon River gorge. The Arnon is the eastern border of Moab, and since the Israelites didn't cross it, they didn't even set foot in Moab.
translation_verse: Eye wòto gbedzi hetrɔ Edom-nyigba kple Moab-nyigba ta, eye wova ɖo Moab-nyigba ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome heƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Arnon ƒe go keme dzi, ke womeva Moab-nyigba dzi o, elabena Arnon ye do liƒo na Moab.

english_verse: The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
translation_verse: Tete Israel do amewo ɖo ɖe Amoritɔwo ƒe fia Sixon, si no Xesbon la gbo be, woagblɔ nɛ bena: Na mato wò anyigba dzi ayi, vaseɖe esime made denyeƒe!

english_verse: towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more. Jephthah's Daughter
translation_verse: Ke Sixon meɖo ŋu ɖe Israel ŋu, ne wòana wòato eƒe anyigba dzi ayi o, eye Sixon ƒo eƒe dukɔ blibo la nu ƒu heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Yaza, eye wòwɔ ana kple Israel.

english_verse: But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived,
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, tso Sixon kple eƒe dukɔ blibo la de asi na Israel, eye wòsi wo. Ale Israel xɔ Amoritɔ, siwo nye anyigba dzi towo la, ƒe anyigba blibo la wòzu wo to.

english_verse: from the Arnon River in the south to the Jabbok River in the north, and from the desert in the east to the Jordan River in the west.
translation_verse: Eye woxɔ Amoritɔwo ƒe anyigba blibo la tso Arnon nu vaseɖe Yabok nu, tso gbedzi vaseɖe Yordan nu.

english_verse: The messengers also told the king of Ammon that Jephthah had said: The Lord God of Israel helped his nation get rid of the Amorites and take their land. Now do you think you're going to take over that same territory?
translation_verse: Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, nyã Amoritɔwo ɖa le eƒe dukɔ Israel ŋgɔ tso, hafi wòa nèbe, yeaxɔe wòanye tɔ wòa?

english_verse: If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
translation_verse: Me wò mawu Kemos xɔ nane na wò la, eya nye tewò, ke amesiwo katã Yehowa, mía Mawu, nyã le mía ŋgɔ la ƒe anyigba enye mía tɔ.

english_verse: Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
translation_verse: Wòe nye ame wu Moab-fia Balak, Zipor vi la? Ɖe wòwɔ dzre kple Israel alo wɔ aʋa kplii kpɔa?

english_verse: I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
translation_verse: Nyemeda voa ɖeke ɖe ŋuwò, hafi wòa nèwɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi sia ɖe ŋunye hehe, yeawɔ aʋa kplim o. Yehowa, nye ʋɔnudrɔ̃la, nadrɔ̃e na Israel-viwo kple Amon-viwo egbea!

english_verse: But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
translation_verse: Ke Amon-viwo ƒe fia meɖo to Yefta ƒe nya, siwo wògblɔ ɖo ɖee la o. Yefta ɖu Amon-viwo dzi, eye wòɖe adzɔgbe.

english_verse: Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ dze Yefta dzi, eye wòto Gilead kple Manase heva Mizpe-Gilead; eye woho tso Mizpe-Gilead ɖe Amon-viwo ŋu.

english_verse: he promised the Lord, “If you will let me defeat the Ammonites
translation_verse: Eye Yefta ɖe adzɔgbe na Yehowa gblɔ bena: Ne ètsɔ Amon-viwo ɖe asi nam vava,

english_verse: and come home safely, I will sacrifice to you whoever comes out to meet me first.”
translation_verse: eye megbɔ tso Amon-viwo gbɔ le ŋutifafa me la, ekema nusianu, si ke ado tso aƒenye me ava kpena la, anye Yehowa tɔ, eye matsɔe asa numevɔe.

english_verse: From Mizpah, Jephthah attacked the Ammonites, and the Lord helped him defeat them.
translation_verse: Tete Yefta ho aʋa ɖe Amon-viwo ŋu, eye Yehowa tsɔ wo ɖe asi nɛ.

english_verse: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
translation_verse: Eye esi Yefta gbɔ va aƒe le Mizpa la, kpɔ ɖa, vianyɔnu tsɔ axatsɛ le ɣe ɖum va kpee; ŋutsuvi alo nyɔnuvia ɖeke megale esi o, eyae nye eƒe tesi.

english_verse: “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
translation_verse: Esi wòkpɔe la, edze eƒe awuwo gblɔ bena: Oo, vinye, èdo nublanuitɔm, eye nèhe dzɔgbevɔ̃e va dzinyea? Meke nu na Yehowa, eye nyemagate ŋu atrɔe o!

english_verse: “Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die.
translation_verse: Tete wòɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Fofonye, ne èke nu na Yehowa la, ekema wɔm, abe alesi do tso wò nu me ene, elabena Yehowa bia hlɔ̃ wò futɔ, siwo nye Amon-viwo, na wò!

english_verse: But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na fofoa bena: Wɔ esia ko nam: Ɖe mɔ nam dzinu eve, ne mia kple xɔ̃nyewo míayi towo dzi aɖafa nye ɖetugbinyenye!

english_verse: “Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said. She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Heyi! Ale wòɖe mɔ nɛ dzinu eve, eye eya kple xɔlɔ̃wo yi ɖafa eƒe ɖetugbinyenye le towo dzi.

english_verse: Then she went back to her father. He did what he had promised, and she never got married. That's why
translation_verse: Esi dzinu evea nu yi la, egbugbɔ va fofoa gbɔ, eye wòwɔ nyɔnuvi la, abe alesi wòɖe adzɔgbee ene. Ke ŋutsua ɖeke mede asi eŋu kpɔ o. Eye wòtrɔ zu kɔnu le Israel ƒe sia ƒe

english_verse: every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_verse: be, Israel-nyɔnuviwo yina ɖafaa Gileadtɔ Yefta ƒe vinyɔnu ŋkeke ene le ƒe ɖeka me.

english_verse: The men of the Ephraim tribe got together an army and went across the Jordan River to Zaphon to meet with Jephthah. They said, “Why did you go to war with the Ammonites without asking us to help? Just for that, we're going to burn down your house with you inside!”
translation_verse: Tete Efrayimtɔwo ƒo ƒu ho va anyiehe, eye wogblɔ na Yefta bena: Nukaŋuti nèho ana ɖe Amon-viwo ŋu, eye mèyɔ mí, be míayi kpli wò oa? Miatɔ dzo wò xɔ ɖe dziwò!

english_verse: “But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us.
translation_verse: Yefta ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Mía kple nye dukɔ míekpe aʋa vɔ kple Amon-viwo, eye meyɔ mi, gake mieva xɔm le wo si o.

english_verse: So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
translation_verse: Esi mekpɔ be, miele xɔxɔm nam o la, metsɔ nye agbe ke ku, eye meho aʋa ɖe Amon-viwo ŋu, eye Yehowa tsɔ wo de asi nam. Nukaŋuti mieho ɖe ŋunye fifia, be miawɔ aʋa kplim?

english_verse: But the men from Ephraim said, “You people of Gilead are nothing more than refugees from Ephraim. You even live on land that belongs to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.” So Jephthah called together the army of Gilead, then they attacked and defeated the army from Ephraim.
translation_verse: Tete Yefta ƒo Gileadtɔwo katã nu ƒu yi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Efrayim, eye Gileadtɔwo si Efrayim; elabena wogblɔ bena: Gileadtɔwo nye Efrayim ƒe ame dzegowo: Gilead le Efrayim kple Manase dome.

english_verse: The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.” If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether,
translation_verse: Wogblɔna nɛ be: Gblɔ be Sibolet! Tete wogblɔna be Zibolet; elabena meɖo ŋu ɖo be, wòagblɔe nyuie o. Enumake wolénɛ, eye wowunɛ ɖe Yordan-tsoƒe la. Ale Efrayimtɔ ame akpe blane vɔ eve kũ ɣemaɣi.

english_verse: Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead. Ibzan
translation_verse: Eye Yefta drɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel ƒe ade, emegbe Yefta, Gileadtɔ la ku, eye woɖu ɖe Gilead-duwo dometɔ ɖeka me. Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo Ibzan, Elon kple Abdon ŋu nya.

english_verse: Ibzan, the next leader of Israel, came from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Eyome Ibzan, amesi tso Betlexem la, drɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Bethlehem. Elon
translation_verse: Emegbe Ibzan ku, eye woɖii ɖe Betlexem.

english_verse: Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years,
translation_verse: Elon, Zebulontɔ la, drɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel ɖe eyome ƒe ewo.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe. Abdon
translation_verse: Eye Elon, Zebulontɔ la ku, woɖi ɖe Ayalon le Zebulon-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Abdon the son of Hillel was the next leader of Israel. He had
translation_verse: Eye Piratonitɔ Abdon ku woɖi ɖe Piraton le Efrayim-nyigba dzi le Amalekitɔwo ƒe to dzi.

english_verse: Once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let the Philistines take control of Israel for
translation_verse: Ke esi Israel-viwo gawɔ nusi medze Yehowa ŋu o la. Yehowa tsɔ wo de asi na Filistitɔwo ƒe blane sɔŋ.

english_verse: Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children,
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi ŋutsua ɖe tso Zora le Dan-ƒome la me, amesi ŋkɔe nye Manoax, eye srɔ̃ tsi ko, medzi vi o.

english_verse: She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name,
translation_verse: Tete nyɔnu la yi ɖagblɔ na srɔ̃a bena: Mawu ƒe amea ɖe va gbɔnye, ele abe mawudɔla ene, eye ŋɔdzi le eŋu ŋutɔ, ke nyemebia afisi wòtso o, eye meyɔ eƒe ŋkɔ hã nam o.

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nam bena: Kpɔ ɖa, ele fu fɔ ge adzi ŋutsuvi, eyata megano wein alo aha muamea ɖeke o, eye megaɖu nu makɔmakɔa ɖeke o; elabena ŋutsuvi la anye Mawu ƒe klu tso dada ƒe dome vaseɖe eƒe kugbe.

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Tete Manoax ɖe kuku na Yehowa gblɔ bena: Oo Aƒetɔ, na Mawu ƒe ame, si nedɔ ɖa la, nagava mia gbɔ zi ɖeka, ne wòafia nusi míawɔ na ɖevi, si woadzi la mí!

english_verse: God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time,
translation_verse: Eye Mawu se Manoax ƒe gbe, eye mawudɔla la gava nyɔnu la gbɔ, esime wòle agble me, eye srɔ̃a Manoax mele egbɔ o.

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Tete nyɔnu la ƒu du kaba yi ɖagblɔe na srɔ̃a bena: Kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsu, si va gbɔnye tsã la, gava!

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Enumake Manoax tsi tre dze nyɔnu la yome heva ŋutsua gbɔ, eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Wòe nye amesi ƒo nu kple nyɔnu la tsãa? Eɖo ŋu bena: Nyee!

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Manoax gblɔ bena Ne wò nya la va me la, ekema kɔ ka woanyi na ɖevi la, eye nuka woawo nɛ?

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ƒe dɔla la gblɔ na Manoax bena: Nusi megblɔ na nyɔnua la, eya nye vevitɔ, si wòalé be na.

english_verse: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
translation_verse: Maɖu nusi tso weinka ŋu o, mano wein alo aha muamea ɖeke o, eye maɖu nu makɔmakɔa ɖeke o; ke boŋ woawo nusiwo katã ŋu meɖe se nɛ le la dzi.

english_verse: “Please,” Manoah said, “stay here with us for just a little while, and we'll fix a young goat for you to eat.”
translation_verse: Tete Manoax gblɔ na Yehowa ƒe dɔla la bena: Na míasika wò ɖi, ne miaɖa gbɔ̃via de aɖo akɔwò me.

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe dɔla la ɖo ŋu na Manoax bena: Ne èsikam ɖi hã la, nyemele wò abolo ɖu ge o; ke nenye numevɔ nèbe, yeasa la, ekema sae na Yehowa! Ke Manoax medze sii bena, Yehowa ƒe dɔla wònye o.

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Eye Manoax gblɔ na Yehowa ƒe dɔla la bena: Ŋkɔwò ɖe? Bena ne wò nya la va me la, ne miaɖe bubu ŋuwò.

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe dɔla la gblɔ nɛ bena: Nukaŋuti nèle nye ŋkɔ, si nye nukunu la, ta biam?

english_verse: So Manoah took a young goat over to a large rock he had chosen for an altar, and he built a fire on the rock. Then he killed the goat, and offered it with some grain as a sacrifice to the Lord. But then an amazing thing happened.
translation_verse: Tete Manoax lé gbɔ̃vi hekpe ɖe nuɖuvɔsa ŋu, eye wosa vɔ le agakpea ɖe dzi na Yehowa. Eye wòwɔ nukunu Manoax kple srɔ̃a wokpɔ.

english_verse: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
translation_verse: Esi dzo ƒe aɖewo de dzi le vɔsamlekpuia dzi la, Yehowa ƒe dɔla to vɔsamlekpui la ƒe dzo ƒe aɖeawo me yi dzi Manoax kple srɔ̃ wokpɔ. Tete wotsyɔ mo anyi.

english_verse: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa ƒe dɔla megaɖe eɖokui fia Manoax kple srɔ̃a kpɔ o Azɔ Manoax dze sii bena, Yehowa ƒe dɔla wònye.

english_verse: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
translation_verse: Manoax gblɔ na srɔ̃a bena: Miele kuku ge, elabena miekpɔ Mawu!

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: Ke srɔ̃a gblɔ nɛ bena: Ɖe wònye Yehowa ɖe wòdi be, yeawu mí la, anye ne mexɔ numevɔsa kple nuɖuvɔsa tso mía si o, eye anye ne mena míekpɔ nusiawo katã, eye míese nusiawo fifia o.

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Eye nyɔnu la dzi ŋutsuvi hena ŋkɔe bena Simson. Ɖevi la va tsi, eye Yehowa yrae.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ ɖe asi edzi dzedze me le Dan ƒe asaɖa, si le Zora kple Estaol dome la me.

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Simson yi Timnat, eye wòkpɔ nyɔnuvia ɖe le Filistitɔwo ƒe nyɔnuwo dome le Timnat.

english_verse: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Esi wògbɔ la, eka ta na fofoa kple dadaa bena: Mekpɔ nyɔnuvia ɖe le Filistitɔwo ƒe nyɔnuwo dome le Timnat, eyata midee nam!

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Fofoa kple dadaa gblɔ nɛ bena: Ɖe nyɔnua ɖeke mele nɔviwòwo ƒe vinyɔnuwo kple nye dukɔ blibo la dome o, eyata nayi aɖade srɔ̃ tso Filistitɔwo, siwo nye bolotɔwo la domea? Simson gblɔ na fofoa bena: Ɖee nam, elabena eƒe nu nyo ŋunye!

english_verse: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
translation_verse: Ke fofoa kple dadaa medze sii be, Yehowa gbɔ wotso o; elabena mɔnu dim wòle le Filistitɔwo ŋu. Ɣemaɣi la Filistitɔwoe le Israel-viwo dzi ɖum.

english_verse: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
translation_verse: Esi Simson kple fofoa kpakple dadaa woyina ɖe Timnat, eye wova ɖo Timnat-tɔwo ƒe weingblewo gbɔ la, kpɔ ɖa, dzatavia ɖe le gbe tem va do goe.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ dze edzi, eye wòvuvui, abe alesi wovuvua gbɔ̃vi ene, evɔ wònye metsɔ naneke ɖe asi o hafi. Ke megblɔ nusi wòwɔ la na fofoa kple dadaa o.

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: Eye wòyi ɖaƒo nu kple nyɔnu la, eye eƒe nu nyo Simson ŋu.

english_verse: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
translation_verse: Eye esi eteƒe didi ʋee, wòyina, be yeakplɔ nyɔnua la, edze gbe, be yeakpɔ dzata kuku la ɖa, eye kpo ɖa, anyi ɖa ɖe dɔ me na dzata la.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: Tete woɖee ɖe asi le nyinyim heva fofoa kple dadaa gbã, eye wòna ɖe woawo hã wonyi; ke megblɔe na wo be, dzata ƒe dɔ me yeɖe anyitsi la le o. Simson ɖe srɔ̃, eye woto adzo.

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: Eye fofoa va nyɔnua gbɔ. Tete Simson tu aglo le afima, elabena nenema ɖekakpuiviwo wɔna.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Eye esi wokpɔe la, woɖe hafi blaetɔ̃ kpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: Ke ne miete ŋu ɖe egɔme nam o la, ekema miawo miatso awutewui blaetɔ̃ kple atsyɔ̃ɖowu blaetɔ̃ nam! Tete wogblɔ ne bena: To wò adzo la míase!

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na wo bena: Nuɖuɖu tso nutsuɖula me, eye nu vivi tso ŋusẽtɔ me. Ke ŋkeke etɔ̃ sɔŋ womete ŋu ɖe adzo la gɔme o.

english_verse: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke eneagbe la wogblɔ na Simson srɔ̃ bena: Ƒoe ɖe srɔ̃wò nu, ne wòaɖe adzo la gɔme na mí! Ne menye nenem o la, míatɔ dzo mia kple fofowò ƒe aƒe! Alo ɖe miekpe mí, be miawɔ mi ame dahewoea?

english_verse: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
translation_verse: Tete Simson srɔ̃ la avi nɛ gblɔ bena: Fu ko nèlém, eye mele lɔ̃yem o; eto adzo na mia ɖe viwo, gake megblɔe nam o! Eɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, nyemegblɔe na fofonye kple danye gɔ̃ hã o, eye mayi egblɔ ge na wòa?

english_verse: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
translation_verse: Eye wòfa avi ne le ŋkeke adre, siwo wotu aglo la me; eye wòɖe egɔme nɛ le ŋkeke adreagbe, elabena eɖe fu nɛ akpa. Eye nyɔnu la yi ɖaɖe adzo la na wo de viwo.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Tete duameviwo va gblɔ nɛ le ŋkeke aɖreagbe, hafi ɣe naɖo to bena: Nuka vivina wu anyitsi? Eye nuka sesẽ wu dzata? Eye wògblɔ na wo bena: Ɖe menye nye nyivi lae mietsɔ ŋlɔ agblee o la, anye ne miele nye adzo la gɔme ɖe ge tututu o.

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Eye wotso Simson srɔ̃ na ehati, si wòɖe kpe ɖe eɖokui ŋu la, wòɖe.

english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ bena: Mebu be, ɖe nèlé fui keŋ, eyata metsɔe na hawòti. De eƒe tsɛ medze tugbe wui oa? Xɔ eya ɖe eteƒe!

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Ke Simson gblɔ na wo bena: Ne mehe dzɔgbevɔ̃e va Filistitɔwo dzi fifia la, nyemeɖi fɔ o.

english_verse: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
translation_verse: Emegbe wòdra akakatiawo heɖe asi le wo ŋu ɖo ɖe Filistitowo ƒe agblewo me; eye ale wòto dzo lu, siwo woxa, kple esiwo le tsitre nu kpakple amitibɔwo.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo gblɔ bena: Ameka wo nusia? Eye wogblɔ bena: Simson, Timnattɔ ƒe toe wòe, elabena woxɔ srɔ̃a tso na eƒe hati. Tete Filistitowo va tɔ dzo nyɔnu la kple fofoa.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Eye Simson gblɔ na wo bena: Ne miewɔ alea hã la, mabia hiã mi kokoko hafi adzudzɔ!

english_verse: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
translation_verse: Eye wòdza sobo kple ali na wo nyamanyama. Tete wòdzo yi ɖanɔ agato me le Elam.

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Eye Filistitɔwo ho va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Yuda, eye wokaka ɖe Lexi.

english_verse: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?” The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
translation_verse: Tete Yuda-ŋutsuwo gblɔ bena: Nukaŋuti mieho ɖe mía ŋu? Woɖo ŋu bena: Simson lé ge mieva, ne míawɔe, abe alesi wòwɔ mí ene.

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Eye Yuda-ŋutsu akpe etɔ̃ yi agato la me le Elam gblɔ na Simson bena: Menyae be, Filistitɔwoe le mia dzi ɖum oa? Eɖo ŋu na wo bena: Alesi wowɔm la, nenema mewo wo.

english_verse: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
translation_verse: Tete wogblɔ nɛ bena: Lé wò ge mieva, ne miatsɔ wò ade asi na Filistitɔwo! Simson ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Mika atam nam be, menye mia ŋutɔwoe le dza ye ge o!

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: Esi wòƒo nu vo la, eɖe asi le tedziglã la ŋu ƒu gbe; eyata wona ŋkɔ teƒe ma be glãtogbɛ.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Tete tsikɔ wui ŋuta, eye wòdo ɣli yɔ Yehowa gblɔ bena: Ete wò dɔla ƒe asi dzi ɖu dzi gã sia, eye azɔ tsikɔ nawum maku, eye mage ɖe bolotɔ siawo si mea?

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Tete Mawu fe kpea ɖe le Lexi, eye tsi do le eme wono, ale be agbe gaɖo eme, eye eƒe lãme kɔ. Eyata wona ŋkɔ vudo la be ameyɔlavudo; ele Lexi vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_verse: Eye wòdrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel le Filistitowo ŋɔli ƒe blave sɔŋ.

english_verse: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
translation_verse: Esi wofi tofi na Gazatɔwo bena, Simson va afisia la, woɖe to ɖee, eye wode xa ɖe du la ƒe agbo nu nɛ le zã blibo la katã me; wozi ɖoɖoe le zã blibo la katã me be, ne ŋu ke la, yewoawui.

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: Esia megbe la elɔ̃ nyɔnua ɖe le Sorek-tɔʋu la nu, si ŋkɔ nye Delila.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
translation_verse: Eye Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo va egbɔ gblɔ nɛ bena: Ble enu, ne nadze si nusi me eƒe ŋusẽ gã la le, kple nusi míatsɔ aɖu edzi, kpakple nusi míatsɔ ablae, be míabɔbɔe ɖe anyi; ekema mía dome amesiame ana klosalo akpe kple alafa ɖeka wò!

english_verse: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
translation_verse: Tete Delila gblɔ na Simson bena: Taflatse, ɖe nusi me wò ŋusẽ gã la le la fiãm kple nusi woatsɔ abla wò abɔbɔ wò ɖe anyi!

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Simson ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Ne wotsɔ atagbi mumu adre, siwo meƒu haɖe o la, biam la, ekema magbɔdzɔ, eye mazu abe ame bubuwo ke ene.

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Eye Delila gblɔ na Simson bena: Kpɔ ɖa, èblem, eye nèka aʋatso nam! Gblɔ nusi woatsɔ abla wòe la nam dzro!

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu ne bena: Ne wotsɔ ka yeye, si mede naneke ŋu haɖe o la, biam la, ekema magbɔdzɔ, eye mazu abe ame bubuwo ke ene.

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Tete Delila tsɔ ka yeyewo biae, eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Simson, Filistitowo ƒo ɖe dziwò loo! Ke amewo de xa ɖe xogã me. Tete wòtso kawo le aba abe ɖeti ŋuɖekɛ ene.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Delila gblɔ na Simson bena: Ɖeko neblem vaseɖe fifi, ye nèka aʋatso nam; gblɔ nusi woatsɔ abla wòe la nam! Eɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Ne elɔ̃ ɖakɔ adre, siwo le nye ta la, ɖe avɔ tsitsi me.

english_verse: “Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ ne bena: Aleke nègblɔ be, yele lɔ̃yem, gake wò dzi meku ɖe ŋunye o? Zi etɔ̃ enye si nèblem, eye mègblɔ nusi me wò ŋusẽ gã la le la nam o.

english_verse: Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
translation_verse: Esi wòle dzi gbãm ne gbawotsyogbe kple eƒe nyawo, eye wòle fu ɖem nɛ la, eva gloe, eye ku ɖo mo nɛ.

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ eƒe dzime-nyawo katã nɛ bena: Talũhɛa ɖeke ɖeke medea nye ta ŋu o, elabena Mawu ƒe klue menye tso danye ƒe da me ke. Ne wolũ ta nam la, ekema nye ŋusẽ ado le ŋunye, eye magbɔdzɔ azu abe ame bubuwo katã ene.

english_verse: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
translation_verse: Esi Delila kpɔ bena, egblɔ eƒe dzimenyawo katã nɛ la, edo ame ɖo ɖa, be woayɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo vɛ gblɔ bena: Miva azɔ, elabena egblɔ eƒe dzimenyawo katã nam! Tete Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo va, eye wohe klosalo la ɖe asi.

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: Eye wòna wòdɔ alɔ̃ ɖe eƒe ata dzi; tete wòyɔ ŋutsua ɖe vɛ wòlũ ɖakɔ adreawo le eta. Ale wòna wòde asi gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔ me, eye eƒe ŋusẽ do le eŋu.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Eye Filistitowo lee heŋɔ eƒe ŋkuwo, eye wokplɔe yi Gaza: wode akɔbli kɔsɔkɔsɔe, eye ele ne be, wòanɔ wɔ tum le gaxɔ me.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Esi wolũ ta nɛ megbe la, eƒe ɖa gade asi toto me.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: Eye Filistitowo ƒe amegãwo va kpe ta, be woasa vɔ na woƒe mawu Dagon, eye wotu aglo gãa ɖe hegblɔ bena: Mia mawu tsɔ míaƒe futɔ Simson de asi na mí!

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: Eye Simson gblɔ na ŋutsuvi, si le ekplɔm la bena: Ɖe asi le ŋunye, ne malé sɔti, siwo dzi xɔa nɔ, eye maziɔ ɖe wo ŋu!

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Tete Simson yɔ Yehowa gblɔ bena: Aƒetɔ Yehowa, ɖo ŋku dzinye, eye do ŋusẽm fifia ko, oo Mawu, ne mabia hlɔ̃ Filistitɔwo ɖe nye ŋku eveawo nu!

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Eye Simson va titinasɔti eveawo, siwo dzi xɔa nɔ, ɖeka ɖe ɖusi, eye evelia ɖe mia, eye wòtutu wo.

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: Eye Simson gblɔ be: Maku kple Filistitɔwo! Eye wòbi eɖokui kple ŋusẽ, tete xɔ la mũ dze amegãwo kple dukɔ blibo la dzi. Ale amesiwo wowu le eƒe kuɣi la, sɔ gbɔ wu amesiwo wòwu le eƒe agbe me.

english_verse: His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Tete nɔviawo kple fofoa ƒemetɔwo katã va tsɔe yi ɖaɖi ɖe fofoa Manoax ƒe yɔdo me le Zora kple Estaol dome? Edrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel ƒe blave sɔŋ.

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: Eye wòtsɔ klosalo la na dadaa Ke dadaa ɖe klosalo alafa eve na sikanutula, amesi tsɔe wɔ aklama kpakpɛ kple legbae, eye wotsɔe va Mixa ƒe me.

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi la fíaa ɖeke mena Israel o, eye amesiaame wɔ nusi dze eŋu.

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: Eye woʋu tso Betlexem-Yuda-du la me, be wòaɖanɔ afisi wòkpɔ; eye wòva Efrayim-to la dzi heyi ɖe Mixa ƒe me, be wòagayi eƒe azɔli dzi emegbe.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Tete Mixa gblɔ nɛ bena: Afika nètso? Eɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Lewito menye tso Betlexem-Yuda, eye meyina, be manɔ afisi makpɔ.

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Mixa gblɔ nɛ bena: Tsi gbɔnye, eye nanye fofo kple nunɔla nam, ekema mana klosalo ewo wò ƒe sia ƒe hekpe ɖe avɔtata kple nuɖuɖu ŋu. Ale wozi Lewito la dzi.

english_verse: then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons.
translation_verse: Eye Mixa ɖo Lewitɔ la. Ale ɖekakpui la trɔ zu nunɔla nɛ, eye wòtsi Mixa ƒe me.

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Tete Mixa gblɔ bena: Azɔ menyae bena, Yehowa le nyui wɔ ge nam, elabena Lewitɔe nye nunɔla nam.

english_verse: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi la fiaa ɖeke menɔ Israel o. Eye Dan-viwo ƒe to la ɖi anyigba, be woanɔ edzi ɣemaɣi, elabena anyigbaa ɖeke mesu wo si le Israel ƒe toawo dome vaseɖe ɣemaɣi o.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Eye Dan-viwo dɔ ŋutsu kalẽtɔ atɔ̃ le woƒe ƒome blibo la me tso Zora kple Estaol ɖo ɖa, be woaɖatsa ŋku le anyigba la dzi, eye woadzra eme hegblɔ na wo bena: Miyi ɖadzro anyigba la me! Esi wova Efrayim-to dzi la, woyi ɖe Mixa ƒe me hetsi afima dɔ.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Esi woɖo Mixa ƒe aƒe gbɔ la, wodze si Lewi-ɖekakpui la ƒe gbe; tete woge ɖe me hebiae bena: Ameka kplɔ wò va afisia? Nuka wɔm nèle le afisia? Eye dɔ ka le ŋuwò le afisia?

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu na wo bena: Ale kple ale Mixa wɔ nam, eye wòdɔm be, manye nunɔla ne.

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ nɛ bena: Bia Mawu na mí kpɔ be, azɔli, si dzi miele la, adze edzi na mí hã?

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Nunɔla la ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Miyi le ŋutifafa me! Miaƒe mɔ, si dzi miele la, dze Yehowa ŋu.

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu atɔ̃awo dze mɔ heva Lais, eye wokpɔ bena, dukɔ, si le eme la, ti kpoo bɔkɔɔ, eye woɖe dzi ɖi abe Zidontɔwo ene, amea ɖeke mewɔ vɔ̃ wo o, eye nu bɔ ɖe wo si, wole didiƒe tso Zidontɔwo gbɔ, eye womebɔa ha kple amea ɖeke o.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Esi wogbɔ va wo nɔviwo gbɔ le Zora kple Estaol la, wo nɔviwo bia wo bena: Aleke miedee?

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Ne mieyi la, miage ɖe dukɔa ɖe, si li bɔkɔɔ la dome, eye anyigba la keke ta; elabena Mawu tsɔ anyigba, si dzi hiã metua ame le naneke me o la, de asi na mi.

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu alafa ade, siwo bia akpa la, ho le Dan-viwo ƒe ƒome la me tso Zora kple Estaol.

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: Eye woho va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Kiryat-Yearim le Yuda; eyata woyɔa teƒe ma vaseɖe egbe be Dan ƒe asaɖa; kpɔ ɖa, ele Kiryat-Yearim godo.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Woho tso afima heyi Efrayim-to la dzi, eye wova Mixa ƒe aƒe gbɔ.

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu atɔ, siwo yi ɖatsa ŋku le Lais-nyigba dzi la, gblɔ na wo nɔviwo bena: Miawo hã mienyae bena, kɔmewu, aƒeli, aklama kpakpɛ kple legba le aƒe sia mea? Eyata mibu nusi miawɔ!

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ ne bena: Zi ɖoɖoe! Tsɔ asi bu nu, eye yi kpli mí, ne nanye mia fofo kple míaƒe nunɔla! Esi nènye nunɔla ɖe ame ɖeka kolia ƒe aƒe nu la, eyae nyo wu esi nanye nunɔla ɖe to kple ƒome nu le Israel mahã?

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Tete wòdze nunɔla la ŋu, eye wotsɔ kɔmewu la, aƒeli kple aklama kpakpɛ la, eye woge ɖe dukɔ la dome.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Emegbe wòtrɔ hedzo, eye wotsɔ ɖeviwo kple lãwo kpakple nu veviwo ɖo ŋgɔ.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Esi wode megbe le Mixa ƒe aƒe gbɔ la, woyɔ ŋutsu, siwo ƒe aƒe te ɖe Mixa ƒe aƒe ŋu la, eye wodze Dan-viwo yome.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Eye esi woyɔ Dan-viwo ɖa la, wonyè kɔ gblɔ na Mixa bena: Nya ka dzɔ, hafi nèyɔ amewo ƒo ƒu ale?

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu na wo bena: Mietsɔ nye mawu, si mewɔ la, eye miekplɔ nunɔla hã dzoe. Nuka gakpɔtɔ nam, hafi miele biayem be, nya ka dzɔ?

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Ke Dan-viwo gblɔ ne bena: Ɖe nu le mía ŋu, ne dɔmedzoetɔwo magadze mia dzi, eye woatsrɔ̃ mia kple aƒewòmetɔwo ƒe agbe o!

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Tete Dan-viwo lé woƒe mɔ, eye esi Mixa kpɔ bena, wosesẽ wu ye la, etrɔ gbɔ va eƒe xɔ nu.

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ ŋkɔ na du la bena Dan ɖe wo fofo Dan, amesi wodzi na Israel la, ƒe ŋkɔ nu; ke tsã la du la ŋkɔ nye Lais.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: Le ɣemaɣi la fiaa ɖeke menɔ Israel o. Eye Lewi-ŋutsua ɖe yi ɖanye amedzro le Efrayim-to la ƒe mlɔenu, eye wòdze ahiã tso Betlexem-Yuda.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: Eye eƒe ahiã la wo ahasi le emegbe, eye wodzo yi fofoa ƒe me le Betlexem-Yuda hetsi afima dzinu ene.

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu la kplu ɖekakpui ɖeka kple tedzi eve ɖe asi, eye wòtso dze eyome, be yeaƒo nu kplii fafɛ, ne yeakplɔe agbɔe. Eye nyɔnu la kplɔe yi fofoa ƒe me, eye esi ɖetugbi la fofo kpɔe la, exɔe kple dzidzɔ.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: Ɖetugbi la fofo, si nye toa, lée ɖi, eye wòtsi egbɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃; woɖu nu no nu, eye wotsi afima do.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Esi wofɔ le ŋkeke eneagbe, be yewoadze mɔ la, ɖetugbi la fofo gblɔ na toa bena: Di nuɖuɖu via ɖe ɖe dɔ me, hafi miadze mo!

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Tete wobɔbɔ nɔ anyi, eye woa kple eve la woɖu nu no nu, eye ɖetugbi la fofo gblɔ na ŋutsu la bena: Tsi anyi dɔ, eye wò dzi nagbɔ ɖe me!

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Esi ŋutsu la tso, be yeadze mo la, toa ƒoe ɖe enu, eye wòtsi anyi dɔ.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Esi wòfɔ le ŋkeke atɔ̃lia ƒe ŋdi, be yeadze mo la, ɖetugbi la fofo gblɔ nɛ bena: De nane do me, eye milala, vaseɖe esime ɣe natrɔ hafi! Tete woa kple eve la woɖu nu.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Ke esi ŋutsu la kple eƒe ahiã kpakple ɖekakpui la wotso, be yewoadze mo la, ɖetugbi la fofo, si nye toa, gblɔ nɛ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, ɣe la yina lɔ̃, eye anyinu le fafam, eyata mitsi do! Ye la trɔ xoxo, eyata tsi dɔ, eye wò dzi nagbɔ ɖe me! Etsɔ ŋdi la miafa kaba alé miaƒe mo ayi wò agbadɔ nu!

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Gake ŋutsu la melɔ̃ be, yeatsi adɔ o, eye wòdze mɔ heva Yebus, si nye Yerusalem la kasa, eye tedzi eve, siwo wòbia akpa na, kple eƒe ahiã la kpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Esi woɖo Yebus gbo la, ɣe la yi lɔ̃ xoxo; tete ɖekakpui la gblɔ na eƒe aƒetɔ bena: Na miayi aɖadze Yebusitɔwo ƒe du sia me, eye míatsi eme aɖa!

english_verse: “No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah,
translation_verse: Ke eƒe aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ bena: Miayi aɖadze ame tutɔwo ƒe ɖu, si me Israel-via ɖeke mele o la me o; ke boŋ míayi ŋgɔ vaseɖe Gibea.

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Esi woyi azɔlia dzi la, ɣe va ɖo to ɖe wo le Gibea, si nye Benyamin to la gbo.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: Tete woge ɖe Gibea, be woatsi afima adɔ, eye wodro ɖe du la ƒe ablɔ me, elabena amea ɖeke mena dzeƒe wo ɖe eƒe me o.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Eye kpɔ ɖa, ame tsi tsia ɖe gbɔ so agbledɔwɔƒe le fiẽ; ŋutsu la tso Efrayim-to dzi va nye amedzro le Gibea, ke afimatɔwo nye Benyamin-viwo.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Tete wòfɔ ko dzi kpo amedzro la le dua ƒe ablɔ me, eye ame tsitsi la gblɔ bena: Afika nèyina, eye afika nètso?

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Míetso Betlexem-Yuda heyina ɖe Efrayim-to la ƒe mlɔenu; afima metso va yi Betlexem-Yuda, eye meyina Yehowa ƒe me, ke amea ɖeke mexɔm ɖe eƒe me o.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Evɔ wònye aƒla kple nuɖuɖu hena míaƒe tedziwo, eye abolo kple wein hã hena mia kple wò dɔlanyɔnu kpakple ɖekakpui la le wò dɔla si, eye naneke mele ehiãm o hafi.

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Tete ame tsitsi la gblɔ nɛ bena: Ŋutifafa na wò! Ne nane le hiãwòm la, ekpo ɖe asinye; ɖeko mele ablɔ me ya tsi ge adɔ o!

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Eye wòkplɔe yi eƒe me hena nuɖuɖu eƒe tedziwo, eye woklɔ afɔ, eye woɖu nu wono nu.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Ke esi woƒe dzi gbo ɖe me la, tete duametɔwo, siwo nye ame vlowo la, va ɖe to ɖe aƒe la hele agbo la ƒom, eye wogblɔ na ame tsitsi, si nye aƒeatɔ, bena: Kplɔ ŋutsu, si va dze aƒewò me la ɖoe, ne míanyãe!

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu, si nye aƒeatɔ la, ɖo yi wo gbɔ gblɔ na wo bena: Oo, nɔvinyewo, migawɔ nu vlo sia o! Esi wònye aƒenye me ŋutsu sia va dze la, eyata migawɔ nu baɖa sia o!

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, makplɔ vinyenyɔnu kple ŋutsu la ƒe ahiã ɖoe, ne miade asi wo ŋu, eye miawɔ nusianu, si dze mia ŋu la, ɖe wo ŋu; ke migawɔ nu baɖa ɖe ŋutsu sia ŋu o!

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Ke ŋutsuawo gbe toɖoɖoe. Tete ŋutsu la kplɔ eƒe ahiã yi wo gbɔ le xexe, eye wode asi eŋu hewɔ funyafunyae zã blibo la, vaseɖe esime ŋu ke; eye esi agu dze la, woɖe asi le eŋu.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Esi ŋua mekpɔ ke ɖe le eme keŋ o la, nyɔnu la va dze anyi ɖe ŋutsua ƒe xɔ, si me eƒe aƒetɔ le la, ƒe ʋɔtru nu, vaseɖe esime ŋua ke ɖe le eme.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Eye esi eƒe aƒetɔ fɔ ŋdi, eye woʋu nɔa do, be yeayi eƒe azɔli dzi la, tete nyɔnu, si nye eƒe ahiã la, tsra ɖe xɔa ƒe ʋɔtru nu, eye eƒe asiwo le kpuia dzi.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ ne bena: Tsi tre, ne miadzo! Ke meɖo ŋu nɛ o. Tete wòkɔe ɖo tedzi la dzi, eye ŋutsua dze mɔ yi enɔƒe.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: Esi wògbɔ va aƒe la, etsɔ hɛ, eye wòlé eƒe ahiã la heflii kɔ wuieve ɖe eƒe ƒunuɖeƒeewo, eye wòɖo wo ɖe Israel-nyigba blibo la katã dzi.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Eye amesiame, si kpɔe la, gblɔ bena: Esia tɔgbe medzɔ kpɔ o, eye womekpɔ eteƒe kpɔ, tso esime Israel-viwo ʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi vaseɖe egbe o. Mibu eŋu, miɖo aɖaŋu, eye miƒo nu le eŋu!

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Tete Lewitɔ, si nye nyɔnu kuku la srɔ̃, xɔ edzi gblɔ bena. Mía kple nye ahiã mieva Gibea, si nye Benyamin tɔ la, be míatsi adɔ.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Tete melé nye ahiã la, eye meflu heɖo ɖe Israel-nyigba ƒe nutowo katã me, elabena wowɔ ŋukpenanu kple nu vlo le Israel.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, mi Israel-viwo katã nye esi! Miƒo nu, eye miɖo aɖaŋu fifia!

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ blibo la xɔ edzi nu ɖekɛ gblɔ bena: Mía dome amea ɖeke mayi eƒe agbadɔ me o, eye amea ɖeke mayi eƒe xɔ nu o;

english_verse: Everyone agreed that Gibeah had to be punished.
translation_verse: Tete Israel-ŋutsuwo katã ƒo ƒu, eye wòbia ɖekae ɖe du la ŋu.

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Eye Israel-toawo ɖɔ ame ɖo ɖe Benyamin-ƒomeawo katã gbɔ bia wo bena: Nu vlo ka enye si wowɔ le mia dome?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: Eyata miɖe Gibeatɔ vloawo na, ne miawui wo, eye miaɖe vɔ la ɖa tso Israel! Ke Benyamin-viwo meɖo to wo nɔvi Israel-viwo ƒe gbe o.

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: Tete Benyamin-viwo tso duwo me va ƒo ƒu ɖe Gibea, ne woakpe ana kple Israel-viwo.

english_verse: The other Israelite tribes organized their army and found they had
translation_verse: Eye woxlẽ Israel-ŋutsuwo: amesiwo katã ta yi, eye wonye aʋamewo la, le ame akpe alafa ene, ke Benyamin-viwo mele eme o.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Israel-viwo fɔ ŋdi va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Gibea gbɔ.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Eye Israel-ŋutsuwo ho aʋa ɖe Benyamin ŋu, eye wodze aʋa ɖe wo ŋu le Gibea gbɔ.

english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Tete Benyamin-viwo ɖo tso Gibea, eye wotsrɔ̃ ame akpe blave vɔ eve le Israel ŋu gbemagbe ƒo ɖe anyi.

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo ɖe xadelawo ɖo Gibea ŋu va kpe.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Eye wòsi le Israel-ŋutsuwo nu heto gbedzimɔ; ke aʋa la yɔ wo ɖe nu, eye amewo ɖo tso duwo me, eye wotsɔ wo ɖe to me hetsrɔ̃ wo.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: Woɖe to ɖe Benyamin, eye wonyae ɖe nu, eye wotsrɔ̃ wo tso droƒe vaseɖe Gibea kasa le ɣedzeƒe gome.

english_verse: Some other warriors of Benjamin turned and ran down the road toward Rimmon Rock in the desert. The Israelites killed
translation_verse: Tete wòtrɔ hesi ɖo ta gbedzi vaseɖe Rimon-kpe la gbɔ; wowu ame akpe atɔ̃ le woƒe megbexeawo ŋu le mɔ dzi, eye woti wo yome vaseɖe Gideom, eye wogawu ame akpe eve le wo ŋu.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Ŋutsu kalẽtɔ, siwo katã ta yi, eye wotsi aʋa le Benyamin ŋu gbemagbe la, le ame akpe blave vɔ atɔ̃.

english_verse: The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-ŋutsuwo trɔ ɖe Benyamin-viwo ŋu, eye wowu nusianu, si wokpɔ le dua me la, kple yi, amewo kple lãwo siaa, eye wòta dzo du, siwo katã wokpɔ la.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Eye Israel-ŋutsuwo ka atam le Mizpa gblɔ bena: Mía dometɔa ɖeke matsɔ vianyɔnu na Benyamin-viwo woaɖe akpɔ o!

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Eye esi dukɔ la va Betel la, wotsi Mawu ŋku me le afima vaseɖe fiẽ, eye wofa avi sesĩe

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: gblɔ bena: Oo, Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, nukaŋuti nusia dzɔ le Israel, eye to ɖeka bu le Israel egbe sia?

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Eye dukɔ la fɔ ŋdi kanya le ŋkeke eveagbe heɖi vɔsamlekpui, eye wosa numevɔ kple akpedavɔ.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo gblɔ bena: Ameka le Israel-toawo katã dome, si meva takpeƒe le Yehowa gbɔ le Mizpa o? Elabena ɖe woka atam ɖe amesi mava Yehowa gbɔ le Mizpa o la ŋu bena, ele be, woawui kokoko!

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Eye wòve Israel-viwo na wo nɔvi Benyamin, eye wogblɔ bena: To ɖeka tsrɔ̃ ɖa le Israel egbe sia!

english_verse: The warriors attacked Jabesh in Gilead, and returned to their camp at Shiloh in Canaan with
translation_verse: Eye wokpɔ ɖetugbi alafa ene, siwo medɔ ŋutsu gbɔ kpɔ o, le Yabes-Gileadtɔwo dome, eye wokplɔ wo va asaɖa la me le Silo le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Eye ameha blibo la dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Benyamin-viwo gbɔ le Rimon-kpe la gbɔ, eye wodo ŋutifafa ŋugbe na wo.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Tete Benyamin-viwo trɔ gbɔ ɣemaɣi, eye wotsɔ nyɔnu, siwo woxɔ ɖe agbe tso Yabes-Gilead-nyɔnuwo dome la na wo; ke womede wo nu o.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Eye Benyamin ƒe nu ve dukɔ la, elabena Yehowa na Israel-toawo tsi ŋuzã.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Tete ameha la ƒe amegãwo gblɔ bena: Aleke míawɔ hafi ana nyɔnu ame kpɔtɔeawo? Elabena nyɔnuwo tsrɔ̃ le Benyamin.

english_verse: If they don't have children, one of the Israelite tribes will die out.
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ bena: Benyamin ƒe anyigba enye woƒe amesiwo kpɔtɔ la tɔ, eye toa ɖeke nu matsi le Israel o!

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Ke miawo la míate ŋu atsɔ mia vinyɔnuwo na wo woade o; elabena Israel-viwo ka atam bena: Aɖi amesi ana nyɔnu Benyamin la ŋu!

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, woɖua Yehowa ƒe ŋkekenyuie la ƒe sia ƒe le Silo, si le Betel ƒe anyiehe kple mɔ, si tso Betel ɖo ta Sixem la, ƒe ɣedzeƒe kpakple Lebona ƒe dziehe.

english_verse: The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives: Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival.
translation_verse: Eye wode se na Benyamin-viwo bena: Miyi ɖade xa de weingblewo me,

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: eye ne miekpɔ be, Silo-nyɔnuviwo do va ɣe du ge la, ekema mido tso weingbledelawo me, eye mia dome amesiame nelé nyɔnu le Silo-nyɔnuviwo dome na eɖokui, eye mido yi Benyamin-nyigba dzi!

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Ke ne wo fofowo kple wo nɔviŋutsuwo va dzre wɔ ge kpli mí la, ekema miagblɔ na wo bena: Miele asi le wo ŋu na mi, elabena miekpɔ nyɔnu le aʋa me na amesiame o; ɖe wònye mia ŋutɔwoe tsɔ wo na wo la, eya ko wòanye ɖe míeɖi fɔ.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Tete Benyamin-viwo wɔ nenema, eye wokpɔ nyɔnu wòde wo nu tso ɣeɖula, siwo woha la dome. Emegbe wotrɔ yi woƒe anyigba dzi, eye wogbugbɔ duawo tso hena wo me.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo dome amesiame dzo ɣemaɣi tso afima yi eƒe to me kple eƒe ƒomeawo gbɔ, eye amesiame dzo tso afima yi eƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi la fiaa ɖeke menɔ Israel o, eye amesiame wɔ nusi dze eŋu.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Ŋutsu la ŋkɔ nye Elimelex, eye srɔ̃a ŋkɔ nye Naomi, viaŋutsu eveawo ŋkɔ-wo nye Maxlon kple Xilion. Wonye Efrayimtɔwo tso Betlexem-Yuda, eye woʋu va Moab-nyigba dzi henɔ afima.

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: Esi Naomi srɔ̃ Elimelex ku, eye eya kple viaŋutsu eveawo kpɔtɔ la,

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: woɖe Moab-nyɔnuwo, siwo dome ɖeka ŋkɔ nye Orpa, eye evelia ŋkɔ nye Rut; eye wonɔ afima anɔ ƒe ewo.

english_verse: Mahlon and Chilion also died. Now Naomi had no husband or sons.
translation_verse: Ke wo ame eve la Maxlon kple Xilion hã ku; ale nyɔnu laƒeviwo kple eve kpakple srɔ̃a wogblẽe ɖi.

english_verse: When Naomi heard that the Lord had given his people a good harvest, she and her two daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go to Judah. As they were on their way there,
translation_verse: Ale wòʋu tso afisi wònɔ la, eye lɔ̃xoa eveawo kplɔe ɖo; eye wodze mɔ, be yewoagbugbɔ ayi Yuda-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Tete Naomi gblɔ na lɔ̃xoa eveawo bena: Mitrɔ, eye mia dome amesiame negbugbɔ yi dadaa ƒe me! Yehowa ave mia nu, abe alesi mieve mía kple ame kukuawo nui ene!

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: Yehowa ana miakpɔ dzudzɔ le mia srɔ̃wo ƒe me! Eye wòɖuɖɔ nu na wo; tete wofa avisesĩe

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: hegblɔ nɛ bena: Míayi wò dukɔ gbɔ kpli wò boŋ!

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Ke Naomi gblɔ bena: Vinyewo, migbugbɔ! Nukaŋuti miebe, yewoayi kplim? Alo ŋutsuvie gale dɔ menam miava ɖea?

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Vinyewo, migbugbɔ yi; elabena metsi akpa, ne mayi srɔ̃ ɖe ge. Eye ne megblɔ be, mele srɔ̃ ɖe ge le zã sia meadzi ŋutsuviwo la,

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: ɖe mialala, vaseɖe esime woatsia? Alo ɖe miatsi anyi srɔ̃maɖemaɖea? Gbeɖe, vinyewo! Mia tɔ koe le veyem, elabena Yehowa do asi ɖe gbɔnye!

english_verse: They cried again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
translation_verse: Tete wogafa avi sesĩe. Eye Orpa ɖuɖɔ nu na lɔ̃xoa, ke Rut ya ku ɖe eŋu,

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, atsuwòsi gbugbɔ yina eƒe ɖukɔ kple eƒe mawu gbɔ; gbugbɔ dze atsuwòsi yome!

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Ke Rut gblɔ bena: Megaƒoe ɖe nunye be, magblẽ wò ɖi agbugbɔ le yowòme o! Ke boŋ afisi nayi la, afima mayi; afisi natsi la, afima matsi; wò dukɔ anye nye dukɔ, eye wò Mawu anye nye Mawu;

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: afisi naku ɖo la, afima maku ɖo, eye afima woaɖim ɖo! Yehowa nefiam, ne wòagafiam ɖe dzi; negbe ku koe aklã mía dome!

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Esi wòkpɔ be, eɖoe kplikpaa be, yeayi kplii la, edzudzɔ nyaƒoƒo ɖe enu.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Ale woa kple eve la wodze mɔ heva Betlexem. Eye esi woɖo Betlexem la, du blibo la ƒo zi ɖe wo ŋu le gbɔgblɔm bena. Naomi enye sia?

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Ke egblɔ na wo bena: Migayɔm be Naomi o, hafi boŋ miyɔ Mara nam: elabena ŋusẽkatãtɔ la do nublanuitɔm!

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: Metsɔ nu geɖe yii, ke Yehowa kplɔm gbɔe asi gbɔloe; nukaŋuti miele yɔyem be Naomi, evɔ wònye Yehowa do nublanuitɔm ɖe?

english_verse: The barley harvest was just beginning when Naomi and Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law, arrived in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ale Naomi gbɔ va aƒe, eye lɔ̃xoa Rut, Moab-nyɔnu la, kpe ɖe eŋu tso Moab-nyigba dzi; eye wova Betlexem, esime wodze nuŋeŋe gɔme.

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Eye kpɔ ɖa, Boas tso Betlexem va, eye wògblɔ na nuŋelawo bena: Yehowa anɔ anyi kpli mi! Woɖo ŋu ne bena: Yehowa ayra wò!

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Tete Boas bia eƒe dɔla, si le nuxalawo dzi kpɔm bena: Ameka ƒe nyɔnuvie nye ekem?

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Dɔla, si nye nuxalawo dzikpɔla, ɖo ŋu bena: Moab-nyɔnu, si kple Naomi wotso Moab-nyigba dzi vae.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ nam bena: Na mafɔ nusiwo dzɔ ɖe nubablawo domee le nuxalawo yome la, aƒo ƒu na ɖokuinye. Ŋdi ke wòva hetsi anyi vaseɖe fifia, eye azɔ ko wòle gbɔgblɔm ɖe eme vie.

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Tete Boas gblɔ na Rut bena: Vinye, see! Megayi ɖafɔe le agble bubua ɖeke me o, eye megadzo le afisia hã o; ke boŋ lé ɖokuiwò ɖe nye dɔlanyɔnuwo ŋu!

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Afisiafi, si wole nu xam le agblea me le nèkpɔ la, ɖze wo yome, elabena mede se na dɔlawo bena, womegaɖe fu na wò o; eye ne tsikɔ le wuwòm la, yi ɖe zeawo gbɔ nano tsi, si dɔlawo du ɖi!

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Tete wòɖe ta agu hegblɔ nɛ bena: Aleke nève nunye, eye nèbu nye amesi nye amedzro la ale gbegbe?

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Boas ɖo ŋu gblɔ nɛ bena: Wogblɔ nusiwo katã nèwɔ na lɔ̃xowò, le srɔ̃wò ƒe ku megbe kple alesi nègblẽ fofowò kple dawò kpakple mia de ɖi heʋu va ɖukɔi, si mènya tsã o gbɔ la nam

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Yehowa naɖo wò nuwɔwɔ teƒe na wò, eye fetu dedie le Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, si ƒe aʋala te nèva sisi ge tso la, gbɔ na wò!

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ bena: Nye aƒetɔ, ne ènya ve nunye ko, elabena èfa akɔ nam, eye nèƒo nu kple wò, dɔlanyɔnu xɔlɔ̃tɔe, evɔ wònye nyemeɖe wò dɔlanyɔnuwo dometɔa ɖeke nu o hafi!

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Eye Boas gblɔ nɛ bena: Nuɖuɣi ɖo, eyata te va natsɔ abolo asisi ataditsi aɖu! Tete wòbɔbo nɔ nuxalawo kasa, eye wòtsɔ bliti memee nɛ, eye, wòɖui ɖi ƒo ɖe kpɔtɔ.

english_verse: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
translation_verse: Emegbe wòtsi tre gayi efɔ ge. Tete Boas de se na eƒe dɔlawo bena: Mina wòafɔe le bablawo hã domee, eye migaka mo nɛ o;

english_verse: Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
translation_verse: milũ ɖewo le bablawo ŋu da ɖe anyi nɛ, be wòafɔ, eye migahe nya ɖe eŋu o!

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Ale wòfɔe le agble la me vaseɖe ɣetrɔ, eye wòƒo nusiwo wòfɔ la, anɔ lu efa ɖeka.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: Eye wòtsɔe va du la me, eye lɔ̃xoa kpɔ nusi wòfɔ. Tete wòɖe nusi wòɖu ɖi ƒo kpɔtɔ la, ɖe go hetsɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Eye lɔ̃xoa biae bena: Afika nèyi ɖafɔe le egbea? Eye afika nèwɔ do le? Woayra amesi bu wò ale! Tete wòto amesi gbɔ wòwɔ dɔ le la, na lɔ̃xoa gblɔ bena: Ŋutsu, si gbɔ mewɔ dɔ le la, ŋkɔ nye Boas.

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Tete Naomi gblɔ na lɔ̃xoa bena: Yehowa, si mete eƒe amenuveve agbagbeawo kple kukuawo o la, ayrae! Eye Naomi gblɔ nɛ bena: Ŋutsu la míaƒe ƒometɔe, eye mía srɔ̃ɖia wònye.

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Rut, Moab-nyɔnu la, ɖo ŋu bena: Egblɔ nam hã bena, malé ɖokuinye ɖe yeƒe dɔlawo ŋu, vaseɖe esime yeƒe nuŋeŋe blibo la nawu enu.

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Tete Naomi gblɔ na lɔ̃xoa Rut bena: Enyo, vinye, be nèle dedem kple eƒe dɔlanyɔnuwo, ne amea ɖeke magawɔ naneke wò le agble bubu me o!
