english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Ale wòlé eɖokui ɖe Boas ƒe dɔlanyɔnuwo ŋu hele efɔfɔ dzi, vaseɖe esime lu kple ƒo ŋeŋe la wu enu, eye wònɔ lɔ̃xoa gbɔ.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Tete lɔ̃xoa Naomi gblɔ nɛ bena: Vinye, nyemadi dzudzɔƒe na wò, be wòanyo na wò oa?

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Boas, amesi ƒe dɔlanyɔnuwo gbɔ nènɔ la, enye míaƒe ƒometɔ. Kpɔ ɖa, ele lu gbɔ ge egbe Zã le lugbɔƒe.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Eyata le tsi nasi ami, eye naɖe avɔ ata ahayi lugbɔƒe la; ke megana ŋutsu la nadze si wò o, vaseɖe esime wòaɖu nu, eye wòano nu vɔ hafi!

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: Eye ne eyi ɖamlɔ anyi la, ekema lé ŋku ɖe afisi wòmlɔ la ŋu; emegbe nayí aklo avɔ le afɔgbɔ nɛ ahamlɔ anyi, ekema afia nusi nawɔ la wò.

english_verse: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Tete wòɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Nusiwo katã nègblɔ la, mawɔe!

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Eye wòyi lugbɔƒe la hewɔ, abe alesi lɔ̃xoa gblɔ nɛ pɛpɛpɛ ene.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Esi Boas ɖu nu no nu, eye eƒe dzi gbɔ ɖe eme la, eyi be, wòamlɔ anyi ɖe lu, siwo woƒo ƒu la, ƒe mlɔenu. Ke eva dzaa, eye wòklo avɔ le afɔgbɔ nɛ hemlɔ anyi.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Le zãtiƒe la ŋutsu la ɖi vo, eye wòbi kɔ, eye kpɔ ɖa, nyɔnua ɖe mlɔ eƒe afɔde.

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ bena: Wò amekae? Eɖo ŋu bena: Nye Rut, wò dolanyɔnue; keke wò avɔ ɖe wò dɔlanyɔnu dzi, elabena srɔ̃ɖia nènye!

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Yehowa ayra wò, vinye! Eɖe wò lɔlɔ̃ fia fifia wu tsã; elabena mèdze ɖekakpuiwo, ame dahe alo hotɔwo yome o.

english_verse: Don't worry, I'll do what you have asked. You are respected by everyone in town.
translation_verse: Eyata, vinye, megavɔ̃ o! Mawɔ nusiwo katã nègblɔ la na wò; elabena nye dukɔ ƒe du blibo la nyae bena, nyɔnu zãzɛ nènye.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Nyateƒe, nyee nye srɔ̃ɖia hafi; ke srɔ̃ɖia bubu li, esi tsɔ ɖe gbɔwò wum.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Tsi afisia dɔ, eye ne ŋu ke wòbe, yeaxɔ wò la, enyo nexɔ wò; ke ne egbe be, yemaxo wò o la, ekema meta Yehowa ƒe agbe be, maxɔ wò. Mlɔ anyi vaseɖe ŋu nake!

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Tete wòmlɔ eƒe afɔde vaseɖe ŋu ke, eye wòfɔ, hafi asiƒome nava kɔ; elabena egblɔ be, amea ɖeke megadze sii be, nyɔnu va lugbɔƒe o!

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Ɖo taɖedzi, si le ŋuwò! Tete wòɖoe, eye wòku lu dzidzenu ade ɖe eme, eye wòlée nɛ, wòtsɔ yi dua me.

english_verse: Naomi asked her what had happened, and Ruth told her everything.
translation_verse: Eye esi wògbɔ va lɔ̃xoa gbɔ la, ebiae bena: Aleke nèɖee, vinye? Tete wòto nusiwo katã ŋutsua wɔ nɛ la nɛ

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: hegblɔ bena: Lu dzidzenu ade sia wòtsɔ nam, elabena egblɔ be, megagbugbɔ yi lɔ̃xowò gbɔ asi gbɔlo o!

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Gbɔ dzi ɖi ko, vinye, vaseɖe esime nanya, alesi nya la ava nɔ! Elabena ŋutsu la maɖe dzi ɖi o, vaseɖe esime wòano ta na nya la egbea hafi.

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Eye Boas yi agbo nu hebɔbɔ nɔ afima. Eye kpɔ ɖa, srɔ̃ɖia, si ŋu Boas ƒo nu, le la, va yina, eye wògblɔ bena: Xɔ̃, va bɔbɔ nɔ afi! Eye wòyi ɖabɔbɔ nɔ anyi.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Eye wòɖe dumegã ewo hegblɔ bena: Mibɔbɔ nɔ afi! Tete wobɔbɔ nɔ anyi.

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na srɔ̃ɖia la bena: Naomi, amesi gbɔ tso Moab-nyigba dzi la, le mía nɔvi Elimelex ƒe agble dzram.

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: Eyata meɖo be, maka eta na wò bena: Xɔe ƒle le nyaselawo kple nye dukɔ la ƒe ame tsitsiwo ŋku me! Ne èbe, yeaxɔe la, xɔe; ke ne èbe, yemaxɔe o la, gblɔe nam, ne mase! Elabena srɔ̃ɖia bubua ɖeke megali kpe ɖe ŋuwò o, negbe nye koe gale yowòme. Eɖo ŋu bena: Maxɔe!

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Eye Boas gblɔ bena: Gbesigbe naxɔ agblea aƒle le Naomi si la, gbemagbe naxɔ Moab-nyɔnu Rut, si nye ame kuku la srɔ̃ hã, ne ame kuku la ŋkɔ natsi eƒe domenyinu ŋu!

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Tete srɔ̃ɖia la gblɔ bena: Nyemate ŋu axɔe na ɖokuinye o, ne nye domenyinu nagagblẽ o; ke boŋ wòa xɔ nusi maxɔ hafi la, na ɖokuiwò, elabena nyemate ŋu axɔe o!

english_verse: To make a sale legal in those days, one person would take off a sandal and give it to the other.
translation_verse: Tsã la, ne wole nane xɔ ge le Israel, alo wole li ɖɔ gee, eye wobe, woaɖo kpe edzi la, ekema ame ɖeka ɖea afɔkpa tsɔna na nɔvia; esia nye ɖase le Israel.

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: Eyata esi srɔ̃ɖia la gblɔ na Boas bena: xɔe ƒle la, eɖe eƒe afɔkpa.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Tete Boas gblɔ na ame tsitsiawo kple duametɔwo katã bena: Miawoe nye ɖasefo egbea be, mexɔ Elimelex ƒe nuwo katã kpakple Xilion kple Maxlon ƒe nuwo katã ƒle le Naomi si.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: Eye mexɔ Moab-nyɔnu Rut, Maxlon srɔ̃, hã wòzu srɔ̃nye, be ame kuku la ƒe ŋkɔ natsi eƒe domenyinu ŋu, ne ame kuku la ŋkɔ magatsrɔ̃ le noviawo kple wo dedu me o! Miawoe nye ɖasefowo egbe!

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Tete duametɔ, siwo katã le agboa nu kple ame tsitsiawo gblɔ bena: Míawoe nye ɖasefo! Yehowa nawɔ na nyɔnu, si le aƒewò me va ge la, abe Raxel kple Lea, nyɔnu, siwo kple eve ɖo Israel ƒe aƒe la tè dzi la ene! Wò alɔ nede dzi le Efrata, eye wò ŋkɔ nenyɔ le Betlexem!

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: Eye vi, si Yehowa ana ɖetugbi sia nadzi na wò la, nana wò aƒe nanɔ abe Perez, amesi Tamar ɖzi na Yuda la ƒe aƒe ene!

english_verse: Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son.
translation_verse: Ale Boas ɖe Rut wòzu srɔ̃a, eye esi wòdɔ egbɔ la, Yehowa na wòfɔ fu dzi ŋutsuvi.

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Tete nyɔnuwo gblɔ na Naomi bena: Woakafu Yehowa, si mete xɔnametɔ wò o, eye woanyɔ eƒe ŋkɔ le Israel!

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: Afa akɔ na wò, eye wòakpɔ dziwò le wò nyagãkuku me; elabena lɔ̃xowò, si wò, eye wòde ŋutsuvi adre nu na wò gbɔ edzi lae, dzii na wò!

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Eye Naomi xɔ ɖevi la ɖe akɔ, eye wòzu enyila.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Eye aƒelikawo tsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ hegblɔ bena: Wodzi ŋutsuvi na Naomi! eye wona ŋkɔe be Obed; eyae dzi Dawid fofo Isai.

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Ŋutsua ɖe tso Ramatayim-Zofim le Efrayim-to la dzi, eŋkɔ nye Elkana, amesi nye Yeroxam vi, amesi nye Elihu vi, amesi nye Toxu vi, amesi nye Zuf vi, eye wònye Efrayimtɔ.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: Eɖe srɔ̃ eve, ɖeka ŋkɔ nye Xana, eye evelia ŋkɔ nye Penina; Penina dzi vi, ke Xana medzi via ɖeke o.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsu sia tsoa eƒe ɖu me ƒe sia ƒe yina ɖadoa gbe ɖa, eye wòasa vɔ na Yehowa Zebaot le Silo, afisi Eli ƒe viŋutsu eveawo Xofni kple Pinexas wonye nunɔla na Yehowa le.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Gbesigbe Elkana sa vo la, emãa lã na srɔ̃ Penina kple viaŋutsuwo kpakple vianyɔnuwo.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: Ke ena lã Xana ɖe ame eve nu, elabena elɔ̃ Xana, evɔ wònye Yehowa tsi eƒe dɔ nu hafi.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: Eye atsusia tsɔ dzikunyawo gbã dzi nɛ, le esi Yehowa tsi eƒe dɔ nu ta.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Alea wòwɔna ƒe sia ƒe, eye godogodo, ne wova Yehowa ƒe me la, edoa dziku nɛ, ale be wòlea avi me, eye wòdoa kpo nuɖuɖu.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: Tete srɔ̃a Elkana gblɔ nɛ bena: Xana, nuka le wowòm nele avi fam, eye nukaŋuti nègbe nuɖuɖu, eye wò dzi le nu xam? Ɖe nyemede ŋutsuvi ewo nu na wò oa?

english_verse: When the sacrifice had been offered, and they had eaten the meal, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli was sitting in his chair near the door to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Eye esi Xana du nu no nu le Silo vɔ la, etsi tre yi Yehowa ŋku me. Eye nunɔla Eli bɔbɔ nɔ atiklã dzi le Yehowa ƒe gbedoxɔ la ƒe ʋɔtru nu.

english_verse: Hannah was heartbroken and was crying as she prayed,
translation_verse: Eye wòle nu xam vevie, eye wòdo gbe ɖa na Yehowa hele avi fam hehehe.

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: Eye wòɖe adzɔgbe gblɔ bena: Yehowa Zebaot, ne ekpɔ wò dɔlanyɔnu ƒe hiã ɖa, eye nèɖo ŋku wò dɔlanyɔnu dzi, mèŋlɔe be o, eye nena ŋutsuvi wò dɔlanyɔnu la, ekema matsɔe na Yehowa le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me, eye talũhɛ made ta ŋu nɛ o!

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Ke Xana le nu ƒom le dzi me, negbe eƒe nuyiwo koe le ʋaʋãm butubutu, eye eƒe gbe mele dzi dem o: eyata Eli bui ahamulae.

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: Eye Eli gblɔ nɛ bena: Ɣekaɣi namu aha ase do? Na wein la nakɔ le mo na wò!

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Tete Eli gblɔ bena: Yi le ŋutifafa me, Israel ƒe Mawu la awɔ nusi nèbiae la na wò!

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Ne ève wò dɔlanyɔnu nu ko! Emegbe nyɔnu la lé eƒe mɔ, eye woɖu nu, eye megato mo azɔ o.

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Eye wòfɔ ŋdi kanya ɖado gbe ɖa le Yehowa ŋku me, emegbe wotrɔ yi woƒe xɔ nu le Rama. Eye Elkana do srɔ̃ Xana gbɔ, eye Yehowa ɖo ŋku edzi. Samuel dzidzi kple etsɔtsɔ yi Mawu ƒe aƒe me.

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: Esi ƒe trɔ la, Xana fɔ fu dzi ŋutsuvi, eye wòna ŋkɔe bena Samuel, elabena egblɔ be: Yehowa si me mebiae le.

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Eye Elkana kple eƒemetɔwo katã yi, bena wòasa ƒevɔ, eye wòawɔ eƒe adzɔgbeɖeɖewo dzi na Yehowa.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Ke Xana ya meyi o, elabena egblɔ na srɔ̃ bena: Ne ɖevi la ɖi no la, ekema makplɔe ayii, be wòado ɖe Yehowa ŋku me, eye woatsi afima ɖaa.

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Tete srɔ̃a Elkana gblɔ nɛ bena: Wɔ alesi dze ŋuwò, tsi anyi, vaseɖe esime naɖee le no nu! Yehowa nena wò nya nava me ko! Ale nyɔnu la tsi aƒe, eye wòna no via, vaseɖe esime woɖee le no nu.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Nye aƒetɔ, taflatse! Nye aƒetɔ, meta wò siaa! Nyee nye nyɔnu, si tsi tre ɖe gbɔwò le teƒe sia ɖo gbe ɖa na Yehowa.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: Ɖevi sia tae medo gbe ɖa le, eye Yehowa na nusi mebiae la, va me nam.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Eyata mekplɔe ve na Yehowa le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me, elabena Yehowa si me wobiae le. Eye wòdo gbe ɖa na Yehowa le afima.

english_verse: Hannah prayed: You make me strong and happy, Lord. You rescued me. Now I can be glad and laugh at my enemies.
translation_verse: Eye Xana do gbe ɖa gblɔ bena: Nye dzi le aseye tsom le Yehowa me, eye nye dzo do lɔƒuu le Yehowa me, nye nu ké baa ɖe nye futɔwo ŋu, elabena wò ɖeɖe ladzɔ dzi nam!

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: Amea ɖeke mele kɔkɔe abe Yehowa ene o, ɖeke mekpe ɖe ŋuwò o, eye agakpea ɖeke meli abe mía Mawu la ene o!

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Miganɔ adegbe ƒom atraɖii o, eye nya vlo meganɔ dodom le mia nu o! Elabena nunyawo ƒe Mawu enye Yehowa, amesi ɖaa nuwɔwɔwo kpɔ na.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: Kalẽtɔwo ƒe dati ŋe kliklikli eye ame benɔwo tsɔ ŋusẽ bia ali dzi;

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: Yehowa wua ame, eye eya ke gbɔa agbe ame, edea ame tsiẽ, eye wògahea ame ɖoa goe.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: Yehowa wɔa ahetɔ kple kesinɔtɔ, eyae ƒua ame anyi, eye wògafɔa ame ɖe dzii.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: Eya ɖea hiãtɔwo tso ké me, eye wòhea ame dahewo tso bafifi me, ne wòana woawo kple amegãwo nanɔ kasɔsɔ me, eye wòaɖe bubumewo ƒe zi asi na wo; elabena anyigbatu me sɔtiwo nye Yehowa tɔ, eye woawo dzi wòtu xexeame godoo ɖo.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: Ekpɔa eƒe ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe afɔ dzi, ke ame vlowo atsrɔ̃ ɖe viviti me; elabena ame ƒe ŋusẽ mena wòzua dziɖula o.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: Yehowa atsrɔ̃ eƒe futɔwo, eye wòaɖe gbe ɖe wo dzi tso dziƒo; Yehowa adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu anyigba ƒe mlɔenuwo. Ana ŋusẽ eƒe fia, eye wòana eƒe amesiamina la ƒe dzo nado lɔƒuu!

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Emegbe Elkana dzo yi eƒe xɔ nu le Rama; ke ɖevi la zu subɔla na Yehowa le nunɔla Eli gbɔ. Eli-viwo ƒe nu tovo wɔwɔ.

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: kple kɔnu, si le nunɔlawo si ɖe dukɔa ŋu la me o. Ne amea ɖe sa vɔ, eye wòle lã ɖam la, ekema nunɔla ƒe dɔla léa gaflo nuetɔ̃e ɖe asi vɛ,

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: eye wòtɔ lãwo le gaze alo ze, kutu alo agba me, eye nunɔla la tsɔa nusianu, si gaflo la he ɖi goe la, na eɖokui. Alea wowɔna ɖe Israel blibo, si va Silo la ŋu.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Ɖewo la nunɔla ƒe dɔla vana, hafi woava lɔ dzo amiawo, eye wogblɔna na amesi tsɔ vɔsa vɛ bena: Tsɔ lã vɛ, ne woatɔ na nunɔla, elabena mele lã bibi dim tso asiwò o, ke boŋ mumua.

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Ne ame la do ŋu be: Na woatɔ dzo amiawo gbɔ, emegbe hã axɔ nusianu, si dze ŋuwò la, ekema egblɔna be: Gbeɖe, ke boŋ nae tititi, ne menye nenem o la, maxɔe kple sesẽ!

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Eye dɔlawo ƒe vodada sɔ gbɔ le Yehowa ŋku me, elabena woɖi gbɔ Yehowa ƒe vɔsa le ameawo ŋku me.

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment
translation_verse: Ke Samuel subɔna le Yehowa ŋku me, enye ɖevi, eye wòdoa aklala kɔmewu

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Gake dadaa tɔa dziwui ɖagbia ɖe vana nɛ ƒe sia ƒe, ne eya kple srɔ̃a wova ƒevɔ sa ge.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Emegbe Eli yra Elkana kple srɔ̃a gblɔ bena: Yehowa ana nyɔnu sia nadzi vu na wò natsɔ ɖo amesi nèbia Yehowa la teƒe! Eye wogbugbɔ yi wo nɔƒe.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Yehowa ɖo ŋku Xana dzi, eye wòfɔ fu dzi ŋutsuvi etɔ kple nyɔnuvi eve. Ke Samuel ɖevi la tsi le Yehowa gbɔ.

english_verse: Eli was now very old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ke Eli ku amegã ɖeɖi, eye wose nusiwo katã viawo nɔa wɔwɔm ɖe Israel blibo la ŋu kple alesi wonɔa nyɔnu, siwo le dɔ wɔm le Mawu ƒe agbadɔ nu la gbɔ dɔmee.

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Menyo o hee, vinyewo! Elabena nya, si Yehowa ƒe dukɔ la le gbɔgblɔm mese la, menye nya nyui wònye o!

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Ne amegbetɔ da vo ɖe nɔvia amegbetɔ ŋu la, ekema ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo tsoa eme; ke ne amegbetɔ da vo ɖe Yehowa ŋu la, ameka aɖe kuku ɖe eta? Ke womese wo fofo ƒe gbe o, elabena Yehowa ɖo be, yeawu wo.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Ke Samuel ɖevi la tsi ɖe dzi, eye eƒe nu nyo Yehowa kple amegbetɔwo ŋu. Eli ƒe aƒe ƒe gbegblẽ gbɔgblɔɖi.

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Eye Mawu ƒe amea ɖe va Eli gbɔ gblɔ nɛ bena: Yehowa ƒe gbe enye si: Meɖe ɖokuinye fia fofowò ƒe aƒe, le esime wonye kluviwo le Farao ƒe me le Egipte.

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, ƒe gbe nye si: Megblɔ tsã be, mana mia kple fofowò ƒe aƒe nanɔ ŋkunye me tegbee; ke azɔ la ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Nede megbe xaa tso gbɔnye, elabena amesi buam la, mabui, eye amesi doa vlom la, mado vloe.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ŋua ɖe le keke ge, eye mala wò alɔ kple fofowò ƒe alo ɖa, ale be ame tsitsia ɖeke maganɔ aƒewò me o.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: Eye nu nyui, siwo katã mawɔ na Israel la, abia ŋu na wò, si nye nye nɔƒe la ƒe futɔ; ke ame tsitsia ɖeke manɔ aƒewò me akpɔ o.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Gake wò ƒometɔ ɖeka ko nyematsrɔ̃ ɖa le nye vɔsamlekpui la gbɔ o, ne mana eƒe ŋkuwo nalé ayi, eye agbe nanye hiã nɛ; ke aƒewòmeviwo aku le ɖekakpui dzodzo me.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: Nusi ava viwòwo kple eve Xofni kple Pinexas dzi la, anye dzesi na wò: Woa kple eve la woaku gbe ɖeka!

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Eye maɖo nunɔla nuteƒetɔ na ɖokuinye, amesi awɔ nu ɖe nye dzi dzi, eye wòawɔ nusi adze ŋunye; mana eƒe aƒe nali ke, eye wòadze nye amesiamina la ŋgɔ ɖaa

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Eye amesiwo akpɔtɔ ɖe aƒewò me la, dome ɖesiaɖe ava dze klo ɖe eŋku me, eye woabia ga kple aboloe agblɔ bena. Tsɔm kpe ɖe wò amesiwo le nunɔladɔ wɔm la ŋuti, ne makpɔ abolo aɖu!

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: womekpɔ tsi Mawu ƒe akaɖiawo haɖe o, eye Samuel mlɔ Yehowa ƒe gbedoxɔ me, afisi Mawu ƒe aɖaka la le.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa yɔ Samuel, eye wòtɔ gblɔ bena Nyee nye si!

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: Enumake wòƒu du yi Eli gbɔ gblɔ bena; Nyee nye si, elabena eyɔm. Ke eɖo ŋu bena: Nyemeyɔ wò o, gbugbɔ yi ɖamlɔ anyi! Eye wòyi ɖamlɔ anyi.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa gayɔ Samuel. Tete Samuel fɔ yi Eli gbɔ gblɔ bena: Nyee nye si, elabena eyɔm. Eɖo ŋu bena: Vinye, nyemeyɔ wò o, gbugbɔ yi ɖamlɔ anyi!

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: Samuel menya Yehowa haɖe o, eye Yehowa meɖe eƒe nya fiae haɖe o.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Yehowa gayɔ Samuel zi etɔ̃lia, enumake wòfɔ yi Eli gbɔ gblɔ bena: Nyee nye si, elabena eyɔm. Tete Eli dze sii bena, Yehowae le ɖevi la yɔm.

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: Eye Eli gblɔ na Samuel bena: Yi ɖamlɔ anyi, ne wogayɔ wò la, ekema gblɔ bena: Ƒo nu, Yehowa! Wò dɔla ke to ɖi. Eye Samuel yi ɖamlɔ emlɔƒe.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa va tsi tre ɖi, eye wòyɔe abe tsã ene bena: Samuel! Samuel! Eye Samuel gblɔ bena: Ƒo nu, wò dɔla ke to ɖi!

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ na Samuel bena: Kpɔ ɖa, mele nane wɔ ge le Israel, eye amesiame, si asee la, ƒe toawo kple eve me aɖi yeŋ!

english_verse: I will punish Eli and his family, just as I promised.
translation_verse: Gbemagbe mana nusiwo katã megblɔ ɖe Eli ƒe aƒe ŋu la, nava me; madze egɔme, eye mawu enu.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: Megblɔ nɛ be, mahe to na eƒe aƒe la kokoko le eƒe vodada ta, elabena enyae bena, viawo wo busunu gake megbe na wo o.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: Eyata meka atam ɖe Eli ƒe aƒe la ŋu bena: Womatsɔ vɔsalã alo nuɖuvɔsa alé avu ɖe Eli ƒe aƒe la ƒe vodada nu akpɔ o!

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Eye Samuel mlɔ anyi, vaseɖe esi ŋu ke, eye woʋu Yehowa ƒe xɔ la ƒe ʋɔtru. Ke Samuel le ŋutega la gbɔgblɔ na Eli vɔ̃m.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Tete Eli yɔ Samuel bena: Vinye Samuel! Etɔ bena: Nyee nye si!

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Nya ka wogblɔ na wò? Megaɣla naneke ɖem o! Ne èɣla nusi wògblɔ na wò la ɖe ɖem la, ekema Mawu afia wò agafia wò ɖe edzi!

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Tete Samuel gblɔ wo katã ne, eye meɣla ɖeke ɖee o. Eye wòɖo ŋu bena: Yehowae, newɔ nusi dze eŋu ko!

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Samuel va tsi, eye Yehowa nɔ kplii, eye mena nyaa ɖeke to le nya, siwo wògblɔ la me o.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Eye Israel blibo la tso Dan vaseɖe Beerseba nyae bena, Yehowa bu Samuel nyateƒetɔe, eye wòɖoe nyagblɔɖilae.

english_verse: The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gade asi eɖokuiɖeɖefia me le Silo, elabena Yehowa ɖe eɖokui fia Samuel le Silo to Yehowa ƒe nya la me.

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: Eye Samuel ƒe nya de Israel blibo gbɔ. Eye Israel ho aʋa ɖe Filistitɔwo ŋu; woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Eben-Ezer gbɔ, eye Filistitɔwo ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Afek.

english_verse: The Philistines made a fierce attack. They defeated the Israelites and killed about
translation_verse: Eye Filistitɔwo ho ɖatɔ Israel, eye aʋa la keke ta. Ke Filistitɔwo si Israel, eye wowu ame akpe ene ɖe aʋagbe dzi.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Eye dukɔ la ɖɔ ame ɖo ɖe Silo woyi ɖatsɔ Yehowa Zebaot, si le Kerubiwo ta me la ƒe nubablaɖaka tso afima ve, eye Eli vi eveawo Xofni kple Pinexas kpe ɖe Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la ŋu.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Esi dukɔ la va asaɖa me la, Israel-ame tsitsiwo gblɔ bena: Nukaŋuti Yehowa si mí egbea le Filistitɔwo nu? Mina míayi aɖatsɔ Yehowa ƒe nubablaɖaka la tso Silo va mia gbɔ, ne wòava mía dome aɖe mi tso míaƒe futɔwo si me!

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Eye esi Yehowa ƒe nubablaɖaka la va asaɖa me la, Israel blibo la tso aseye hoo, ale be anyigba ʋuʋu.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Ke esi Filistitɔwo se aseye la ƒe ɖiɖi la, wogblɔ bena: Aseye gã ka enye si le ɖiɖim le Hebritɔwo ƒe asaɖa me? Eye wose bena, Yehowa ƒe nubablaɖakae va asaɖa la me.

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: Tete Filistitɔwo vɔ, elabena wogblɔ bena: Mawu va asaɖa lãme. Eye wogblɔ bena: Nane wɔ mí, elabena esia tɔgbe medzɔ etsɔ kple nyitsɔ o!

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: Nane wɔ mí tututu! Ameka aɖe mí atso mawu ŋusẽtɔ siawo si me? Woawo nye mawu, siwo tsɔ dɔvɔ̃ geɖewo wu Egiptetɔwo le gbeɖzi!

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Milé dzi ɖe ƒo, eye miwɔ ŋutsu, mi Filistitɔwo, ne miaganye kluvi na Hebritɔwo, abe alesi wonye kluvi na mi tsã ene o! Eyata miwɔ ŋutsu, eye miwɔ aʋa!

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Woxɔ Mawu ƒe aɖaka la, eye Eli vi eveawo Xofni kple Pinexas tsi aʋa.

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Eye Benyamintɔa ɖe ƒu du tso aʋagbe dzi va ɖo Silo gbemagbe; awu vuvu le eŋu, eye anyi le ta me nɛ.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Esi wòva la, kpɔ ɖa, Eli bɔbɔ nɔ zikpui dzi le agbo nu hele mɔ ta kpɔm, elabena Mawu ƒe aɖaka la na meɖe dzi ɖi o. Eye esi ŋutsu la va gblɔe le dua me la, tete du blibo la do ɣli.

english_verse: “I escaped from the fighting today and ran here.” “Young man, what happened?” Eli asked.
translation_verse: Ŋutsu la gblɔ na Eli bena: Aʋagbe dzi metso, egbea mesi tso aʋagbe dzi! Eye wòbiae bena: Aleke nya la le, vinye?

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Dɔla la ɖo ŋu gblɔ bena: Israel si le Filistitɔwo nu, eye wòsi dukɔ la tɔlɔtɔ; viwò eveawo Xofni kple Pinexas hã ku, eye woxɔ Mawu ƒe aɖaka la!

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Esi wose Mawu ƒe aɖaka ŋkɔ la, emũ tso eƒe zikpui dzi ŋedze ɖe agbo la nu, eye wòtɔ kɔ heku; elabena ame tsitsi wònye, eye kpekpe le eŋu. Edrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel ƒe blane sɔŋ.

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: Ke fu tsi ɖe lɔ̃xoa, Pinexas srɔ̃ ƒo. Eye esi wose be, woxɔ Mawu ƒe aɖaka la, eye toa kple srɔ̃ woku la, ena klo dzi, eye wòdzi vi, elabena fua le eɖum vevie.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: Eye esi wòle kudɔ ƒom la, amesiwo le tsitre ɖe egbɔ la, gblɔ nɛ bena: Megavɔ̃ o, elabena ŋutsuvie nèdzi! Ke meɖo ŋu na wo o, eye medo toe o.

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Ke Filistitɔwo xɔ Mawu ƒe aɖaka la, eye wotsɔe tso Eben-Ezer va Asdod.

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: Esi Filistitɔwo xɔ Mawu ƒe aɖaka la, wotsɔe va Dagon ƒe me, eye wodae ɖe Dagon gbɔ.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Ke esi Asdodtɔwo fɔ ŋdi kanya la, kpɔ ɖa, Dagon tsɔ mo bu anyi ɖe Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la ŋgɔ, eye wòfɔ Dagon gatsɔ ɖo eteƒe.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: Esi wogafɔ ŋdi kanya la, kpɔ ɖa, Dagon tsɔ mo bu anyi ɖe Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la ŋgɔ, eye ta kpakple asibayawo kple eve dudu le Dagon ŋu, eye wòƒo kponogo ɖi.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: Eyata Dagon ƒe nunɔlawo kple amesiwo katã dea Dagon ƒe me la, megaɖoa afɔ Dagon ƒe kpui nu le Asdod vaseɖe egbe o.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe asi sẽ ɖe Asdodtɔwo dzi, egblẽ wo, eye wòna ƒoƒoe te Asdodtɔwo kple amesiwo le woƒe nutowo me.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Esi Asdodtɔwo kpɔ bena, ale nɔ ge wòala la, wogblɔ bena: Israel ƒe Mawu la ƒe aɖaka la meganɔ mía gbɔ o, elabena eƒe asi sẽ ɖe mía kple miaƒe mawu Dagon dzi.

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Eye wodɔ ame woɖaƒo Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo katã nu ƒu va wo gbɔ, eye wogblɔ bena: Aleke miele Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe aɖaka la wɔ gee? Woɖo ŋu be: Mitsɔ Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe aɖaka la ɖo ɖe Gat! Tete woɖo Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe aɖaka la ɖa.

english_verse: the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened,
translation_verse: Ke esi aɖaka la va afima la, Yehowa ƒe asi he ŋɔdzi gãa ɖe va ɖu la dzi, eye wòna ƒoƒoe te duametɔwo, ɖeviwo kple ame tsitsiwo siaa.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Eye woɖo Mawu ƒe aɖaka la ɖe Ekron; ke esi Mawu ƒe aɖaka la va Ekron la, Ekrontɔwo do ɣli gblɔ bena: Woɖo Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe aɖaka la ɖe mía gbɔ, be woawu mia kple míaƒe dukɔ la!

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Tete wodɔ ame woyi ɖaƒo Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo katã nu ƒu, eye wogblɔ bena: Migbugbɔ Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe aɖaka la ɖada ɖe eteƒe, bena magawu mia kple mía dukɔ la o! Elabena dzidzi ƒo du blibo la kutɔkutɔe, eye Mawu ƒe asi sẽ le afima.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Amesiwo meku o la, ƒoƒoe te wo, eye du la ƒe ɣli de dzi.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: Esi Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la tsi Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi ɣleti adre la,

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo yɔ nunɔlawo kple afakalawo gblɔ bena: Aleke miele Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la wɔ gee? Migblɔ alesi miawɔ, hafi aɖoe ɖe eteƒe la na mí!

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Tete woɖo ŋu bena: Ne miehe, yewoaɖo Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe aɖaka la ɖa la, ekema migaɖoe ɖa ƒuƒlu o; ke boŋ mitsɔ avulénu kpe ɖe eŋu! Ekema miaƒe lãme asẽ, eye ne eƒe asi madzo le mia ŋu o hã, mianya.

english_verse: “What should we send?” the Philistines asked. The priests and fortunetellers answered: There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have.
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ bena: Avulénu ka miatsɔ akpe ɖe eŋu? Woɖo ŋu bena: Miwɔ sikaƒoƒoe atɔ̃ kple sikafi atɔ̃ ɖe Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo ƒe xexlẽme nu, elabena dɔvɔ̃ ɖeka ŋugbe va mi katã kple miaƒe amegãwo dzi!

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: Miwɔ miaƒe ƒoƒoeawo kple afi, siwo le miaƒe anyigba gblẽm la, ƒe nɔnɔme, eye miɖe bubu Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋu! Ɖewohĩ ana eƒe asi, si va mia ŋutɔwo kple miaƒe mawuwo kpakple miaƒe anyigba dzi la, dzi naka aɖe.

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti miehe, yewoasè dzime, abe alesi Egiptetɔwo kple Farao sẽ dzinye enea? Alo esi wòɖee le eme na wo ɖe, womeɖe asi le wo ŋu wodzo oa?

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: Eyata mifɔ nuwo vɛ, ne miawɔ tasiaɖam yeye ɖeka, eye mikplɔ nyivinɔ eve, siwo womeku kɔkuti kɔ na wo kpɔ o la, kpe ɖe eŋu: mitsi nyinɔawo ɖe tasiaɖam la ŋu, eye milé wo viwo le wo ŋu va aƒee!

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: Mikɔ Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la da ɖe tasiaɖam la me, eye mifɔ sikanu, siwo nye avulénu mietsɔ koe ɖe eŋu la, ɖe aɖakavi me da ɖe exa, eye miɖoe ɖa wòayi.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Eye ne miekpɔ bena, ele aƒemɔ ɖo ta Bet-Semes la, ekema eyae he dzɔgbevɔ̃e gã sia va mía dzi; ke ne mele alea o la, ekema míanyae bena, menye eƒe asie va mia dzi o, ke boŋ nua ɖe ƒomevie wɔ mí.

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsuawo wɔ alea; wòlé nyivinɔ eve, eye wotsi wo ɖe tasiaɖam la ŋu, ke wotsi ka wo viwo ɖe aƒe.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: Emegbe wotsɔ Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la kple aɖakavi, si me sikafiawo kple woƒe ƒoƒoe, siwo wowɔ le la, da ɖe tasiaɖam la me.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Eye nyinɔwo lé mɔ kɔ ɖo ta Bet-Semes, wòlé mɔ ɖeka hele xɔxlɔ̃m, eye womedze ɖe ɖusi alo mia me o. Eye Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo le wo yome vaseɖe Bet-Semes ƒe liƒo dzi.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Ke Bet-Semestɔwo le lu ŋem le bali la me, eye wòfɔ kɔ dzi kpɔ aɖaka la; eye esi wokpɔe la, wokpɔ dzidzɔ.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo ƒe amegã atɔ̃awo kpɔ eteƒe, eye wogbugbɔ yi Ekron gbemagbe ke.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Sikaƒoƒoe, siwo Filistitɔwo tsɔ lé avu Yehowa, wonye si: Asdodtɔ ɖeka, Gazatɔ ɖeka, Askalontɔ ɖeka, Gattɔ ɖeka kple Ekrontɔ ɖeka.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Eye sikafiawo le amegã atɔ̃awo ƒe xexlẽme nu, amesiwo le Filistitɔwo ƒe duwo katã nu, tso du, siwo ŋu woɖo gli ɖo gbɔ vaseɖe agblekɔƒewo gbɔ. Kpe gã, si dzi woda Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la ɖo la, le Bet-Semestɔ Yosua ƒe agble me vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Eye Bet-Semestɔwo gblɔ bena: Ameka ate ŋu anɔ te ɖe Yehowa, Mawu kɔkɔe sia nu? Eye ameka gbɔ woatso mía gbɔ ayi?

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Tete wodɔ ame ɖo ɖe Kiryat-Yearimtɔwo gblɔ bena: Filistitɔwo gbugbɔ Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la vɛ, miva, ne miakɔe ayi mia gbɔe!

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Tete Kiryat-Yearimtɔwo va kɔ Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la yi ɖada ɖe togbɛ dzi le Abinadab ƒe me, eye wokɔ via Eleazar ŋu, ne wòakpɔ Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la dzi.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Tete Samuel gblɔ na Israel ƒe aƒe blibo la bena. Ne mietrɔ ɖe Yehowa ŋu kple miaƒe dzi blibo la, ekema miɖe mawu bubuwo kple Astartewo ɖa le mia dome; mitsɔ miaƒe tame ɖo Yehowa ŋu, eye misubɔ eya ɖeɖeko, ne wòaɖe mi tso Filistitɔwo si me!

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Tete Israel-viwo ɖe Baalwo kple Astartewo ɖa, eye wosubɔ Yehowa ɖeɖeko.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Eye Samuel gblɔ bena: Miƒo Israel blibo la nu ƒu va Mizpa, ne maɖe kuku na Yehowa ɖe mia ta!

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Tete wova kpe ta ɖe Mizpa, eye woku tsi ƒo ɖe anyi le Yehowa ŋku me hetsi nu dɔ gbemagbe, eye wogblɔ le afima bena: Miewɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Yehowa ŋu. Eye Samuel drɔ̃ ʋɔnu Israel le Mizpa.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Esi Filistitɔwo se bena, Israel-viwo kpe ta ɖe Mizpa la, Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo ho ɖe Israel ŋu; ke esi Israel-viwo see la, vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo le Filistitɔwo ŋu

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: Tete Israel-viwo gblɔ na Samuel bena: Megadzudzɔ kukuɖeɖe na Yehowa, mía Mawu la, ɖe mía ta o, ne wòaɖe mi tso Filistitɔwo si me!

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Esi Samuel le numevɔa sam la, Filistitɔwo ho aʋa va gogo Israel Tete Yehowa ɖe gbe sesĩe ɖe Filistitɔwo dzi gbemagbe, eye wòtɔtɔ wo, ale be Israel si wo.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Israel-ŋutsuwo do tso Mizpa heti Filistitowo yome, eye wowu wo vaseɖe Bet-Kar ƒe anyigbe.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Eye du, siwo Filistitɔwo xɔ le Israel si la gasu Israel si. Ale Israel xɔ Ekron vaseɖe Gat kple woƒe anyigbawo le Filistitɔwo si. Eye ŋutifafa ɖo Israel kple Amoritɔwo dome.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Samuel drɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel le ele agbe me ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Etsana ƒe sia ƒe dea Betel, Gilgal kple Mizpa, eye wòdrɔ̃a ʋɔnu na Israel le du siawo katã me.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: Emegbe wòtrɔna va Rama, elabena afima eƒe xɔnu le, eye wodrɔ̃a ʋɔnu na Israel le afima, eye woɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afima na Yehowa.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: Viaŋutsu ŋgɔgbea ŋkɔ nye Yoel, evelia ŋkɔ nye Abia, woawoe nye ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo le Beerseba.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Ke viaŋutsuwo meto eƒe ʋe me o, eye wodi viɖe yome, woxɔ zãnu, eye wòtrɔ gbɔ ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Tete Israel-ame tsitsiwo katã va kpe ta ɖe Samuel gbɔ le Rama,

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: eye wogblɔ nɛ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, ètsi, eye viwowo mele wo ʋe me tom o; eyata ɖo fia na mí, amesi adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na mí abe alesi wòle le dukɔwo katã dome ene!

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Ke nya la medze Samuel ŋu o, esi wogblɔ be: Ɖo fia na mi, ne woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na mi! Eye Samuel ɖo gbe ɖa na Yehowa.

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Samuel bena: Ɖo to dukɔ la ƒe gbe le nusianu, si woagblɔ na wo la me, elabena menye wòe wogbe o, ke boŋ nyee wogbe be, nyemagaɖu fia ɖe yewo dzi o.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Alesi wole wɔwɔm tso gbesigbe mekplɔ wo tso Egipte vaseɖe egbe, eye wogblẽm ɖi subɔ mawu bubuwo la, nenema pɛpɛpɛ wole wɔwɔm de wò hã ŋuwò.

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Tete Samuel gblɔ Yehowa ƒe nyawo katã na dukɔ, si le fia biam le egbɔ,

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: hegblɔ bena: Fia, si le mia dzi ɖu ge la, ƒe kɔnuwo enye si: Axɔ mia viŋutsuwo, eye wòatsɔ wo aɖo eƒe tasiaɖam kple eƒe sɔɖolawo nu, ne woanɔ du ƒum le eƒe tasiaɖam ŋgɔ.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: Atsɔ mia vinyɔnuwo awɔ amitɔlawo, nuɖalawo kple aboloƒolawoe.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: Eye woaxɔ agble, weingble kple amitibɔ nyuitɔwo le mia si atsɔ na eƒe dɔlawo.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: Axɔ agblemenu kple weingblemenu fe ewolia le mia si na eƒe aƒe dzikpɔlawo kple dɔlawo.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: Axɔ miaƒe dɔlaŋutsuwo kple dɔlanyɔnuwo kple miaƒe ɖekakpui zãzɛwo kpakple miaƒe tedziwo, ne woawɔ dɔ nɛ.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Axɔ miaƒe alẽwo ƒe ewolia, eye mianye dɔlawo nɛ.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Gbemagbe míado ɣli le fia, si mieha la ta; ke Yehowa mado to mi o.

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: ne miawo hã mianɔ abe dukɔwo katã ene! Míaƒe fia nadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na mí, eye wòadze mía ŋgɔ awɔ aʋa na mí!

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Eye Samuel se dukɔ la ƒe nyawo katã, eye wogblɔ wo ɖe Yehowa ƒe to me.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Samuel bena: Ɖo to woƒe gbe, eye nado fia ɖe wo nu! Tete Samuel gblɔ na Israel-ŋutsuwo bena: Mia dome amesiame negbugbɔ yi eƒe du me!

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Ŋutsua ɖe le Benyamin, eŋkɔ nye Kis, amesi nye Abiel vi, amesi nye Zeror vi, amesi nye Bexorat vi, amesi nye Afia vi; enye Benyamintɔa ɖe ƒe vi, eye alɔme le esi.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsuvia de le esi, si ŋkɔ nye Saul, enye ɖekakpui, eye wòdze ɖeka ŋutɔ, amea ɖeke medze ɖeka wui le Israel-viwo dome o, eye wòkɔ, ale be dukɔ blibo la se abɔta nɛ.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Eye Saul fofo Kis ƒe tedzinɔwo bu, eye Kis gblɔ na via Saul bena: Kplɔ ame ɖeka le dɔlawo dome ɖe asi, eye tso, nayi aɖadi tedzinɔawo!

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Eye wotsa le Efrayim-to kple Salisa-nyigba dzi womekpɔ wo o; wotsa le Saalim-nyigba dzi, ke womelé afima o, eye wotsa le Benyamin-nyigba dzi, gake womekpɔ wo o.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Esi wova Zuf-nyigba dzi la, Saul gblɔ na dɔla, si le eŋu bena: Na miatrɔ, ne fofonye magaɖe ŋku le tedzinɔawo ŋu, eye wòanɔ nu xam le mia ŋu o!

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, Mawu ƒe amea ɖe le du keme me, eƒe ŋkɔ nya, eye nusianu, si wogblɔna la, vaa me. Eyata na miayi afima, ɖewohĩ afia mɔ, si míato la mí.

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ na eƒe dɔla bena: Ne míeyi ɖe, nuka miatsɔ ayi na ame la? Elabena abolo vɔ le akplɔ me na mi, eye nunanaa ɖeke hã meli miatsɔ ayi na Mawu ƒe ame la o. Nukae heli ma?

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Tete dɔla la gaɖo ŋu na Saul gblɔ bena. Kpɔ ɖa, klosalo sekel eneliawo ɖeka le asinye, eya matsɔ na Mawu ƒe ame la, ne wòafia mɔ mi.

english_verse: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ na eƒe dɔla la bena: Wò nya la le eme, va miyi! Tete woyi du, si me Mawu ƒe ame la le la me.

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Esi wole to liam yina dua me la, wokpe nyɔnuviwo woyina tsi du ge, eye wobia wo bena: Nukpɔla le afisia?

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu na wo bena. Ẽ, ele afisia, afɔ netsɔ na mi, eva dua me egbea, elabena dukɔ la le vɔ sa ge le to dzi egbea.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Ne miede dua me la, miatui, hafi wòava yi nuɖuƒe le to la dzi; elabena dukɔ la meɖua nu o, vaseɖe esime wòvana va yra vɔsanu la, hafi amesiwo wokpe vɛ la ɖua nu. Eyata miyi, elabena miele etu ge egbea kokoko!

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Tete woyi dua me. Eye esi woɖo dua me la, wokpe Samuel wòyina ɖe to la dzi.

english_verse: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa de gbe to me na Samuel ŋkeke ɖeka va yi, hafi Saul nava ɖo, gblɔ bena:

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: Etsɔ wɔle siawo la mele ŋutsua ɖe ɖo ge ɖe wò tso Benyamin-nyigba dzi, nasi ami nɛ, wòanye amegã ɖe nye dukɔ Israel nu, eya naɖe nye dukɔ tso Filistitɔwo si me; elabena mekpɔ nye dukɔ ɖa, eye eƒe ɣli ɖi va gbɔnye.

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Esi Samuel kpɔ Saul la, Yehowa gblɔ ne bena: Kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsu, si ŋu nya megblɔ na wò la, enye si; eyae aɖu fia ɖe nye dukɔ nu.

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Tete Saul te ɖe Samuel ŋu le agbo la nu gblɔ bena: Taflatse, gblɔe nam, afika nukpɔla ƒe aƒe le?

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Samuel ɖo ŋu na Saul gblɔ bena: Nyee nye nukpɔla la. Dze ŋgɔnye yi to la dzi, eye miaɖu nu kplim egbea! Etsɔ ŋdi la mado mɔ wò, eye maɖe nusiwo katã le wò dzi me la afia wò.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Megatsi dzi le tedzinɔ, siwo bu na wò ŋkeke etɔ̃ enye egbe la ŋu o, elabena wokpɔ wo! Eye ameka tɔ enye Israel ƒe nu veviwo katã? Ɖe menye mia kple fofowò ƒe aƒe blibo la tɔa oa?

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Saul ɖo ŋu gblɔ bena: Ɖe menye Benyamintɔ menye tso Israel ƒe to suetɔ me, eye nye ƒome enye gblɔetɔ le Benyamin-to la ƒe ƒomeawo me oa? Nya ka enye si gblɔm nèle nam?

english_verse: Samuel took Saul and his servant into the dining room at the place of worship. About
translation_verse: Tete Samuel kplɔ Saul kple eƒe ɖɔla yi xɔa me, eye wòna wobɔbɔ nɔ taɖenɔƒe le amesiwo wokpe la dome; woanɔ ame blaetɔ̃.

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Tete nuɖala yi ɖatsɔ ata kple nusiwo le eŋu la, va ɖo Saul kɔ me. Eye wògblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, esia wotsɔ le megbe kpɔm na wò, hee ɖe akɔ me naɖu, elabena esi mekpe dukɔa la, eya medzrae ɖo na wò vaseɖe fifi. Eye Saul kple Samuel woɖu nu gbemagbe.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Emegbe woɖi tso toa dzi yi dua me, eye wòƒo nu kple Saul le xɔta.

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Eye wolɔ ŋdi kanya; esi agu dze la, Samuel yɔ Saul le xɔta gblɔ bena: Fɔ, ne mado mɔ wò! Eye Saul fɔ, eye woa kple eve, eya kple Samuel, wodo ɖe mɔ dzi.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Esi woɖo ɖua ƒe mlɔenu la, Samuel gblɔ na Saul bena: Gblɔ na ɖɔla la be, wòadze mía ŋgɔ; — eye wòdze ŋgɔ — ke wò la tɔ ɖe tsitre, ne mato Mawu ƒe gbe na wò!

english_verse: Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him: The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people.
translation_verse: Tete Samuel tsɔ amigoe la kɔ ɖe la me ne, eye wòɖuɖɔ nu nɛ gblɔ bena: Ɖe Yehowa mesi ami na wò be, naɖu fia ɖe eƒe domenyinu dzi oa?

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: Ne edzo le gbɔnye egbea la, ado go ŋutsu eve le Raxel ƒe yɔdo gbɔ le Benyamin-nyigba dzi le Zelzax, eye woagblɔ na wò bena: Wokpɔ tedzinɔ, siwo di ge neyi la, eye fofowò tasi tedzinɔwo ƒe nya hele nu xam le mia ŋu gblɔ bena: Nuka mawɔ le vinye ta?

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: Ne eyi azɔlia dzi tso afima va ɖo logotiwo gbɔ le Tabor la, ekema akpe ŋutsu etɔ̃ le afima, siwo yina ɖe Mawu gbɔ le Betel; ɖeka lé gbɔvi etɔ̃ ɖe ta, evelia tsɔ abolo bɔbɔ etɔ̃, eye etɔ̃lia kpla wein lãgbalẽgolo ɖeka.

english_verse: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
translation_verse: Woana ɖoaƒe wò, eye ne wotsɔ abolo eve na wò la, naxɔe!

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: Emegbe ava Mawu ƒe Gibea, afisi Filistitɔwo ɖo dzɔlawoe. Eye avɔ me be, ne èɖo dua me afima la, akpe nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe haa ɖe, siwo tso to dzi, eye saŋku, axatsɛ, dze kple kasaŋku le ɖiɖim le wo ŋgɔ, ke woawo ŋutɔwo le nya gblɔm ɖi.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ adze dziwò, eye ade asi nyagbɔgblɔ me ɖi akpe ɖe wo ŋu, eye atro zu ame bubu sa.

english_verse: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
translation_verse: Ne dzesi siawo va me na wò la, ekema wo nusi tsɔ ɖe asi gbɔ na wò, elabena Mawu li kpli wò!

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: Dze ŋgɔnye yi Gilgal, eye kpɔ ɖa, megbɔna gbɔwo, be masa numevɔ kple akpedavɔ. Lala ŋkeke adre, vaseɖe esime mava gbɔwò, eye magblɔ nusi na wo la na wò!

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Eye esi wòtrɔ be, yeadzo le Samuel gbɔ la tete Mawu trɔ eƒe dzi bubui, eye dzesiawo katã va me gbemagbe.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Esi wòva ɖo Gibea la, kpɔ ɖa, nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe haa ɖe va do goe, eye Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ dze edzi wògblɔ nya ɖi le wo dome.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Esi amesiwo katã nyae tsã, kpo be, ele nya gblɔm ɖi kpe ɖe nyagblɔɖilawo ŋu la, amewo bia wo nɔewo bena: Nuka le Kis ƒe vi la wɔm? A, Saul hãe le nyagblɔɖilawo ɖomea?

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Tete amea ɖe ɖo ŋu le afima bena: Ameka nye woawo ya fofo? Eyata wòtrɔ zu lodonya be: A, Saul hãe le nyagblɔɖilawo domea?

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Esi wowu nyagbɔgblɔɖi nu la, eva to la dzi.

english_verse: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
translation_verse: Eye Saul nyuri gblɔ na eya kple dɔla la bena: Afika mietso? Eɖo ŋu bena: Tedzinɔwo di ge mietso, eye esi miekpɔ wo le afia ɖeke o la, mieyi Samuel gbɔ.

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Tete Saul nyuri gblɔ bena: Taflatse, gblɔe nam, aleke Samuel gblɔ na mi?

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Saul ɖo ŋu na nyuria bena: Egblɔ na mi be, wokpɔ tedzinɔwo xoxo. Ke meto fiaɖuɖu ŋu nya, si Samuel gblɔ la nɛ o. Woɖo na Saul to nudzidze me.

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Eye Samuel yɔ dukɔ la va Yehowa ŋku me le Mizpa.

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ na Israel-viwo bena: Ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Mekplɔ Israel tso Egipte, eye meɖe mi tso Egiptetɔwo kple fiaɖuƒe, siwo te mi ɖe anyi la si me.

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: Ke miawo miegbe Mawu, si ɖe nu tso miaƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃ewo kple hiãwo katã me, eye miegblɔ nɛ bena: Ɖo fia ɖe mia nu! Azɔ miɖo le Yehowa ŋku me ɖe miaƒe towo kple ame akpeakpeawo nu!

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Eye Samuel na Israel-toawo te va, eye nudzidze lé Benyamin-to la.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Benyamin-to la te va le woƒe ƒomeawo nu, eye nudzidze lé Matri-ƒome la hedze Kis vi Saul dzi: eye wòdu, gake womekpɔe o.

english_verse: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
translation_verse: Eye wogabia nu Yehowa bena: Ɖe ame la hã va afisia? Yehowa ɖo ŋu bena: Kpɔ ɖa, eɣla ɖe agbawo totro me.

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Tete woƒu du ɖahee tso afima vɛ, eye esi wòva dukɔa dome la, ekɔ, ale be dukɔ la se abɔta nɛ.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Eye Samuel gblɔ na dukɔ blibo la bena: Miele amesi Yehowa tia na mi la kpɔma? Amea ɖeke mede enu le dukɔ blibo la dome o! Tete dukɔ blibo la tso aseye gblɔ bena: Fia nenɔ agbe!

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Azɔ Samuel gblɔ fiaɖuɖu ƒe kɔnuwo na dukɔ la, eye woŋlɔ wo ɖe agbalẽ me hetsɔ da ɖe Yehowa ŋku me. Emegbe Samuel ɖe asi le dukɔ blibo la ŋu, amesiame yi aƒe.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Eye Saul hã yi aƒe le Gibea, eye kalẽtɔ, siwo ƒe dzi Mawu ʋã la, yi kplii.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Ke ame vloa ɖewo gblɔ bena: Amesia hãe aɖe mía? Wodo vloe, eye wometsɔ nunanaa ɖeke vɛ nɛ o. Gake esee, abe ɖe mesee o ene.

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Ke Amonitɔ Nahas ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Hafi mabia nu kpli mi la, ele be, maŋɔ ɖusi me ŋku na mia dome amesiame, ne mado ŋukpe Israel blibo la!

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Tete Yabes-ame tsitsiwo gblɔ nɛ bena: Na asinu mí ŋkeke adre, ne miadɔ ame aɖo ɖe Israel-nyigba blibo la dzi, eye ne amea ɖeke meva xɔ na mí o la, ekema míado ava gbɔwò.

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Eye ame dɔdɔwo va Saul ƒe Gibea hegblɔ nyawo ɖe dukɔ la ƒe to me; tete dukɔ blibo la fa avi kple ɣli.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Ke Saul le nyiwo yome tso agble gbɔ. Tete Saul gblɔ bena: Nuka le dukɔ la wɔm wòle avi fam? Eye wòto Yabes-ŋutsuawo ƒe nyawo nɛ.

english_verse: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
translation_verse: Esi Saul se nya siawo la, Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ dze edzi, eye dzi kui vevie ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: Enumake wòlé nyi eve heɖi, eye wòtsɔ wo ɖe amewo si ɖo ɖe Israel-nyigba blibo la dzi gblɔ bena: Ale woawɔ amesi metso dze Saul kple Samuel yome o la, ƒe nyiwo enye si! Tete Yehowa ƒe ŋɔdzi lé dukɔ la, eye woho zi ɖeka.

english_verse: at Bezek. Saul had them organized and counted. There were
translation_verse: Eye woxlẽ wo le Besek: Israel-viwo le ame akpe alafa etɔ̃, eye Yuda-ŋutsuwo le ame akpe blaetɔ̃.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Azɔ wògblɔ na ame dɔdɔ, siwo va la bena: Miyi ɖagblɔ na Yabes-Gileadtɔwo bena: Etsɔ ŋdɔ la woaxɔ na mi! Eye esi ame dɔdɔwo va gblɔe na Yabestɔwo la, dzi dzɔ wo.

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: Eye Yabestɔwo gblɔ bena: Etsɔ la míado ava mia gbɔ, ne miawo nusianu, si dze mia ŋu la, ɖe mía ŋu.

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, Saul mã dukɔ la ɖe aʋalɔgo etɔ me, eye wova dze asaɖa la dzi le ŋdi ŋudzɔɣi hewu Amonitɔwo vaseɖe ŋdɔ. Ke amesiwo kpɔtɔ la, ka hlẽ, ale be wo dome ame eve metsi afi ɖeka o.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Emegbe dukɔ la gblɔ na Samuel bena: Amekawo gblɔ be: Saul hãe aɖu fia ɖe mía dzia? Mikplɔ ameawo de asi, ne míawu!

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Ke Saul gblɔ bena: Womawu amea ɖeke le egbe ŋkeke sia dzi o, elabena egbe Yehowa na dziɖuɖu le Israel!

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Eye Samuel gblɔ na dukɔ la bena: Miva míayi Gilgal, ne míakɔ fiaɖuɖu la ŋu le afima!

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Ale dukɔ blibo la yi Gilgal, woɖo fia Saul le afima le Yehowa ŋku me le Gilgal, eye wosa akpedavɔ le afima le Yehowa ŋku me. Eye Saul kple Israel-ŋutsuwo katã kpɔ dzidzɔ ŋutɔ le afima.

english_verse: Samuel told the Israelites: I have given you a king, just as you asked.
translation_verse: Eye Samuel gblɔ na Israel blibo la bena: Kpɔ ɖa, meɖo to miaƒe gbe le nusiwo katã miegblɔ nam la me, eye meɖo fia ɖe mia nu.

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: Azɔ fia la adze mia ŋgɔ. Ke nye la metsi, meƒo wɔ, eye vinyewo le mia dome; gake mezɔ mia ŋgɔ tso nye ɖekakpuime vaseɖe egbe.
