english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: Nyee nye si, miɖi ɖase le ŋunye le Yehowa kple eƒe amesiamina la ŋku me! Ameka ƒe nyitsu mexɔ, eye ameka ƒe tedzi mexɔ? Ameka ŋu mese ŋuta le, ameka mete ɖe anyi, eye ameka si mexɔ zãnu le hemiã ŋku ɖe edzi? Ne maɖo teƒe na mi!?

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord and his chosen king are witnesses to what you have said.” “That's true,” they replied.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na wo bena: Yehowa kple eƒe amesiamina la wonye ɖasefo na mi egbe sia be, miekpɔ miaƒe naneke le asinye o. Woɖo ŋu bena: Eya nye ɖasefo!

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Tete Samuel gblɔ na dukɔ la bena: Eya nye Yehowa, si wɔ Mose kple Aron, eye wòkplɔ mia fofowo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: Eyata miva ɖo, ne maɖe dɔmenyo, siwo katã Yehowa wɔ na mia kple mia fofowo la me na mi le Yehowa ŋku me!

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: Esi Yakob va Egipte la, mia fofowo ɖo ɣli na Yehowa, eye Yehowa ɖɔ Mose kple Aron ɖa wokplɔ mia fofowo tso Egipte, eye wona nɔƒe wo ɖe teƒe sia.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: Ke woŋlɔ Yehowa, woƒe Mawu la be; eyata wotsɔ wo dzra na Xazortɔwo ƒe aʋafia Sisera kple Filistitɔwo kpakple Moab-fia, eye wowɔ aʋa kpli wo.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Eye wodo ɣli yɔ Yehowa gblɔ bena: Miewɔ nuvɔ̃, elabena miegblẽ Yehowa ɖi hesubɔ Baalwo kple Astartewo; azɔ ɖe mí tso míaƒe futɔwo si me, ekema miasubɔ wò!

english_verse: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ɖɔ Yerub-Baal, Bedan, Yefta kple Samuel ɖa, eye woɖe mi tso miaƒe futɔ, siwo li godoo va kpe la si me, eye miele ablɔɖenyi.

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Ke esi miekpɔ be, Amon-viwo ƒe fia Nabas ho ɖe nua ŋu la, miegblɔ nam bena: Ɖabi, fia boŋ neɖu mia dzi! Evɔ wònye Yehowae nye mia Mawu kple miaƒe fia hafi

english_verse: You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king.
translation_verse: Azɔ miaƒe fia, si mietia, eye miebia la, enye si! Kpɔ ɖa. Yehowa ɖo haɖe mia nu.

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Ne mieva Yehowa, eye míesubɔe, mieɖo to eƒe gbe, eye miesẽ to ɖe Yehowa ƒe se ŋu o, eve mia kple miaƒe tia, si le mia dzi ɖu ge, miadze Yehowa, mia Mawu la yome la, ekema aɖe mi.

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Ke ne mieɖo to Yehowa ƒe gbe o, eye miesẽ to ɖe Yehowa ƒe se ŋu la, ekema Yehowa ƒe asi ava mia dzi, abe alesi wòva mia fofowo dzi ene.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: Ke mite va fifia hã, ne míakpɔ nu gã, si wɔ ge Yehowa ala le nua ŋku me!

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: Alo menye fifi enye luŋeɣi oa? Ke mele Yehowa yɔ ge, eye wòana dzi naɖe gbe, eye tsi nadza, ne miadze sii, eye míakpɔe bena, miaƒe nu vlo, si miewɔ le Yehowa ŋku me hebia fia la, tri akɔ.

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Eye Samuel yɔ Yehowa, tete Yehowa na dzi ɖe gbe, eye tsi dza gbemagbe. Eye dukɔ blibo la vɔ Yehowa kple Samuel ŋutɔ.

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: Eye dukɔ blibo la gblɔ na Samuel bena: Ɖe kuku na Yehowa, wò Mawu la, ɖe wò dɔlawo ta, ne míagaku o! Elabena miewɔ nu vlo hetsɔ ƒu míaƒe nuvowo katã dzi be, miebia fia.

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Eye Samuel gblɔ na dukɔ la bena: Migavɔ̃ o! Mienyã wɔ nu vlo siawo katã hafi, gake ɖeko migate ɖa le Yehowa ŋu o, eye misubɔ Yehowa tso miaƒe dzi blibo me!

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Migate ɖa, ne miadze nu dzodzro, siwo me viɖe mele o, eye womate ŋu aɖe mi o la yome o; elabena nu dzodzrowo wonye!

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Elabena Yehowa maɖe asi le eƒe dukɔ ŋu o le eƒe ŋkɔ gã la ta; elabena edze egɔme, be wòawɔ mi mianye dukɔ nɛ.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: Ke nede megbe xaa tso nye hã gbɔnye, be matasi kukuɖeɖe ɖe mia ta, eye magbe mɔ nyui kple mɔ dzɔdzɔe fiafia mi ahawɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Yehowa ŋu!

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Ɖeko mivɔ̃ Yehowa, eye misubɔe nyateƒetɔe tso miaƒe dzi blibo me, elabena miekpɔ nu gã, si wòwɔ na mi!

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Ke ne miewɔ nu vlo la, ekema atsrɔ̃ mia kple miaƒe fia siaa ɖa.

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Eye Israel blibo la se bena, Saul si Filistitɔwo ƒe dzɔlawo, eye Israel-viwo ƒe nya gblẽ le Filistitɔwo gbɔ. Tete woyɔ dukɔ la ƒo ƒu ɖe Saul ŋu le Gilgal.

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: Eye Hebritɔwo tso Yordan yi Gad-nyigba kple Gilead-nyigba dzi; ke Saul gale Gilgal ke, eye dukɔ blibo la le dzodzom nyanyanya le eyome.

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: Eye wolala ŋkeke adre, si Samuel ɖo; ke Samuel meva Gilgal o. Tete dukɔ la kaka le eŋu.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: Esi wosa numevɔ vɔ la, tete Samuel do, eye Saul yi ɖakpee, be yeado gbe nɛ.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Ke Samuel gblɔ bena: Nuka nèwɔ? Saul ɖo ŋu bena: Esi mekpɔ be, dukɔ la kaka le ŋunye, wò hã mèva le ɣeyiɣi la dzi o, eye Filistitɔwo va kpe ta ɖe Mixmas la,

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: tete mebu be, Filistitɔwo le gbɔnye va ge le Gilgal, evɔ nyemekpɔ ƒo koko na Yehowa haɖe o; eyata mezi ɖokuinye dzi hesa numevɔ.

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ na Saul bena: Ewo bometsinu! Ɖe wònye ɖe nèlé Yehowa, wò Mawu ƒe se, si wòde na wò me ɖe asi la, anye ne Yehowa ana wò fiaɖuɖu nali ke ɖe Israel tegbee.

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: Ke azɔ wò fiaɖuɖu mali ke o. Yehowa ɖi ŋutsu bubu, si dze eŋu, na eɖokui, eye Yehowa tsɔe ɖo fia ɖe eƒe dukɔ nu; elabena melé se, si Yehowa de na wò la me ɖe asi o. Aʋa yeye.

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Tete Samuel dze mo tso Gilgal yi Gibea-Benyamin. Ke Saul xlẽ dukɔ, si tsi eŋu la, wole ame alafa ade.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Eye Saul kple via Yonatan kpakple dukɔ, si tsi eŋu la, ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Geba-Benyamin, eye Filistitɔwo ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Mixmas.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Eye aʋalɔgo etɔ̃ tso Filistitowo ƒe asaɖa me, be woaɖanyi afu. Aʋalɔgo ɖeka trɔ to Ofra-mɔ dzi ɖo ta Saul-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: Aʋalɔgo evelia trɔ to Bet-Xoron-mɔ, eye aʋalɔgo etɔ̃lia trɔ to liƒo, si ho gɔ̃ ɖe Zeboim-bali me ɖo ta gbedzi la gbɔ mɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Ke nutulaa ɖeke mele Israel-nyigba blibo la dzi o; elabena Filistitɔwo bu be, Hebritɔwo ava tu yi kple akplɔ na wo ɖokui.

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Esi aʋakpegbe ɖo la, womekpɔ yi alo akplɔ le dukɔ blibo, si le Saul kple Yonatan ŋu la si o, negbe Saul kple via Yonatan si ko wole.

english_verse: The Philistines moved their camp to the pass at Michmash,
translation_verse: Eye Filistitɔwo ƒe dzɔlaa ɖewo to Mixmas ƒe to dzi mɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
translation_verse: Agakpe ɖeka dzɔ kã ɖe anyiehekpa dzi ɖo ta Mixmas, eye evelia le dziehekpa dzi ɖo ta Geba.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Eye Yonatan gblɔ na ɖekakpui, si nye eƒe adekplɔvi la bena: Va miyi bolotɔ siawo ƒe dzɔlawo gbɔ! Ɖewohĩ Yehowa awɔ nane ɖe mía nu, elabena mesesẽ na Yehowa be, wòatsɔ ame geɖe alo ame ʋee axɔ na ame o!

english_verse: “Do whatever you want,” the soldier answered. “I'll be right there with you.”
translation_verse: Tete eƒe adekplɔvi ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Wɔ nusianu, si le wò dzi me; yi, kpɔ ɖa, mele ŋuwò, abe alesi nedi ene!

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Eye Yonatan gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, míeyina ameawo gbɔ, eye wole mía kpɔ ge.

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: Ne wogblɔ na mi bena: mitɔ, vaseɖe esime míava mia gbɔ la, ekema miatɔ ɖe mía teƒe, eye miaɖe zɔ ayi wo gbɔ o.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Ke ne wogblɔ na mí bena: Miva mía gbɔ la, ekema míayi; elabena Yehowa tsɔ wo de asi na mí! Esia anye míaƒe dzesi!

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier stood at the bottom of the hill where the Philistines could see them. The Philistines said, “Look! Those worthless Israelites have crawled out of the holes where they've been hiding.” Then they yelled down to Jonathan and the soldier, “Come up here, and we will teach you a thing or two!” Jonathan turned to the soldier and said, “Follow me! The Lord is going to let us win.”
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsu, siwo nye dzɔlawo, ɖo gbe Yonatan kple eƒe adekplɔvi bena: Miva mía gbɔ, ne miagblɔ nyaa ɖe na mi! Tete Yonatan gblɔ na eƒe adekplɔvi bena: Dze yonyeme, elabena Yehowa tsɔ wo ɖe asi na Israel!

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Yonatan ta asi kple afɔ, eye eƒe adekplɔvi la le eyome; Yonatan ƒo wo ƒu anyi, eye eƒe adekplɔvi wu wo le eyome.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: De wònye aʋakɔ la ɖe woɖu aboyonu, si wòxɔ le eƒe futɔwo si la, anye ne wometsrɔ̃ Filistitowo geɖe oa?

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Eye Saul kple aʋakɔ blibo, si le eŋu la, kpe ta heyi aʋa la nu, eye kpɔ ɖa, wotɔtɔ nyamanyama, eye amesiame ɖi yi ɖe nɔvia ŋu.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Eye ŋɔdzi ɖo asaɖa la kple gbeadzi kpakple aʋakɔ blibo la; dzidzi ƒo dzɔlawo kple afunyilawo, eye anyigba ʋuʋu, elabe ŋɔdzi la tso Mawu gbɔ.

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Eye Saul ƒe gbetasrãla, siwo le Gibea-Benyamin la, kpɔ bena, amehaa ɖewo le du ƒum tso afi yi afi.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Tete Saul gblɔ na aʋakɔ, si le eŋu la bena: Mixlẽ ameawo, ne míakpɔ amesi dzo le mía dome! Eye esi woxlẽ wo la, kpɔ ɖa, Yonatan kple eƒe adekplɔvi meli o.

english_verse: At that time, Ahijah was serving as priest for the army of Israel, and Saul told him, “Come over here! Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ na Axiya bena: Tsɔ Mawu ƒe aɖaka la vɛ! Elabena Mawu ƒe aɖaka la le Israel-viwo gbɔ ɣemaɣi.

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: Esi Saul le nu ƒom kple nunɔla, eye ɣli, si le ɖiɖim le Filistitɔwo ƒe asaɖa me, nu le sesẽm ɖe dzi la, Saul gblɔ na nunɔla la bena Nenɔ anyi ko!

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Hebritɔ, siwo nɔ Filistitɔwo gbɔ tsã, eye woho va asaɖa me kpli wo la, hã dzo va ɖe Israel, si le Saul kple Yonatan ŋu la dzi.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-ŋutsu, siwo katã ɣla wo ɖokui ɖe Efrayim-to dzi la, se be, Filistitɔwo si, eye woawo hã ti wo yome va aʋa la nu.

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Ke ɖeɖi te Israel-ŋutsuwo ŋu gbemagbe, eye Saul ka atam na dukɔ la bena: Aɖi amesi aɖu nu, hafi fiẽ naɖo la ŋu, vaseɖe esime mabia hlɔ̃ nye futɔwo hafi! Eye aʋakɔ blibo la mede naneke nu me o.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Eye esi dukɔ la va avee me la, kpɔ ɖa, anyitsi le sisim; gake amea ɖeke metɔ asi eme de nu me o, elabena dukɔ la le atam la vɔ̃m.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Ke Yonatan mese be, fofoa ka atam na dukɔ la o, eye wòdo atikplɔ, si le esi la, ɖa tso enu to anyiɖaɖa la me hede nu me, enumake eƒe mo ko.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Tete amea ɖe gblɔ le dukɔa dome ɖa bena: Fofowò ka atam na dukɔ la be: Aɖi amesi aɖu nu egbea la ŋu! Eva ɖeɖi te dukɔ la ŋu hafi.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Yonatan gblɔ bena: Fofonye he dzɔgbevɔ̃e va anyigba la dzi; kpo ɖa esi meɖe anyitsi ʋee sia nu me la, nye mo kɔ.

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Eye wòsi Filistitɔwo gbemagbe tso Mixmas vaseɖe Ayalon, eye nu te dukɔ la ŋu ŋutɔ.

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Eye aʋakɔ la dze aboyonuawo dzi, wòlé alẽwo, nyiwo kple nyiviwo hetso ʋu wo ɖe anyigba, eye aʋakɔ la ɖu lã, si ƒo ʋu.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Eye wova gblɔe na Saul bena: Kpɔ ɖa, aʋakɔ la wɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Yehowa ŋu heɖu lã, si ƒo ʋu! Tete wogblɔ bena: Mieda ƒu; numli kpe gãa ɖe vɛ nam fififi!

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: Eye Saul gagblɔ bena: Mikaka ɖe aʋakɔ la dome, ne miagblɔ na wo bena: Mia dome amesiame nekplɔ eƒe nyi kple eƒe alẽ vɛ, miwu wo ɖe afisia, ne miaɖu, eye migawɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Yehowa ŋu ahaɖu lã, si ƒo ʋu o! Tete aʋakɔ blibo la dome amesiame kplɔ eƒe nyi ɖe asi yi le zã ma me, eye wowu wo le afima.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Eye Saul ɖi vɔsamlekpui na Yehowa; esia nye vɔsamlekpui gbãtɔ, si wòɖi na Yehowa.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ bena: Mina míaho ati Filistitɔwo yome le zã me, ne miaha wo vaseɖe ŋu ƒe keke me, eye miana wo dometɔa ɖeke nakpɔtɔ o! Tete woɖo ŋu bena: Wɔ nusianu, si dze ŋuwò! Eye nunɔla gblɔ bena: Mina míate ɖe Mawu ŋu afi!

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Eye Saul bia nu Mawu se bena: Maho dze Filistitɔwo yomea? Atsɔ wo ade asi na Israel mahã? Ke meɖo nyaa ɖeke ŋu nɛ gbemagbe o.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Tete Saul gblɔ bena: Mi dukɔ la ƒe tatɔwo katã, mite va afi, ne miadze sii egbe, eye míakpɔ amesi wɔ nuvɔ̃ sia!

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: Mefa Yehowa, si xɔ na Israel, ƒe agbe be, ne anye vinye Yonatan ye hã, ele be, woaku! Gake amea ɖeke meɖo ŋu nɛ le dukɔ la dome o.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na Israel blibo la bena: Miɖo ɖe akpa ɖeka, eye mía kple vinye Yonatan mianɔ akpa evelia! Dukɔ la ɖo ŋu na Saul bena: Wɔ nusianu, si dze ŋuwò!

english_verse: Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?” The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army.
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ na Yehowa bena: Israel ƒe Mawu, ɖe nyateƒe ɖe go! Tete nudzidze la lé Yonatan kple Saul; ke dukɔ la to le eme.

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ be: Midzidze nu ɖe mia kple vinye Yonatan dzi! Tete nudzidze la lé Yonatan.

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ na Yonatan bena: Gblɔe nam, nuka nèwɔ? Yonatan gblɔ ne bena: Metsɔ atikplɔ, si le asinye la nu ɖɔ anyitsi viaɖe kpɔ. Nyee nye si, maku!

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ be: Yehowa nefiam, ne wòagafiam ɖe dzi. Yonatan, ele be, naku!

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Gake dukɔ la gblɔ na Saul bena: Ɖe Yonatan, amesi du dzi gã sia le Israel la, akua? Esia nede megbe xaa! Mieta Yehowa ƒe agbe be, taɖaa ɖeke mage tso eƒe ta ɖe anyigba o; elabena Mawue na be, wowu nusia egbea! Ale dukɔ la xɔ nya ɖe Yonatan nu, be meku o.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Eye Saul gbugbɔ le Filistitowo yome, eye Filistitowo yi wo nɔƒe. Saul ƒe mawo kpakple eƒe aƒe.

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Eye Saul wo aʋa kple Filistitowo vevie le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me. Ne Saul nya kpo ŋutsu kakoa ɖe alo kalẽtɔa ɖe ko la, ekplɔnɛ ɖe eɖokui ŋu.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Eye Samuel gblɔ na Saul bena: Yehowae dom, be masi ami na wò, ne naɖu fia ɖe eƒe dukɔ Israel dzi. Eyata ɖo to Yehowa ƒe gbe!

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: Ate Yehowa Zebaot gblɔ esi: Meɖo ŋku nusi Amalek wo Israel la dzi, esi wode xa ɖe mo dzi nɛ, le esime woʋu tso Egipte.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Eyata yi, nasi Amalek, eye natsrɔ̃ eƒe nuwo katã gbidigbidi, megave enu o; ke boŋ wu ŋutsuwo kple nyɔnuwo, ɖeviwo kple vidzĩewo, nyiwo kple alẽwo, kposɔwo kple tedziwo siaa!

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: Tete Saul na woɖe gbe ƒã na dukɔ la, eye wòxlẽ wo le Telaim, afɔzɔlawo le ame akpe alafa eve, eye Yuda-ŋutsuwo le ame akpe ewo.

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Samuel bena:

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Eye Saul va! Amalekitɔwo ƒe du gbɔ, eye wòde xa de bali la me.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ na Kenitɔwo bena: Midzo, mite da, eye miho tso Amalekitɔwo dome, ne magatsrɔ̃ mi akpe ɖewo ŋuo; elabena mieve Israel-viwo katã nu, esi woʋu tso Egipte! Tete Kenitɔwo te ɖa tso Amalekitɔwo dome.

english_verse: and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt.
translation_verse: Eye Saul si Amalekitɔwo tso Xawila vaseɖe Sur, si le Egipte kasa.

english_verse: Every Amalekite was killed except King Agag.
translation_verse: Ele Amalekitɔwo ƒe fia Agag agbagbe, eye wòtsɔ yi tsrɔ̃ dukɔ blibo la gbidigbidi.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Eye Saul kple dukɔ la kpɔ Agag kple alẽ nyuiwo, nyi damiwo kple alẽviwo kpakple nu nyuiwo katã ta, eye wometsrɔ̃ wo gbidigbidi o; ke wotsrɔ̃ nu ɖigbɔwo kple nu, siwo ŋu viɖea ɖeke mele o la gbidigbidi.

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: Evem be, meɖo fia Saul, elabena etrɔ megbe ɖem, eye mewo nye gbe dzi o. Tete dzi ku Samuel, eye wòdo ɣli na Yehowa zã blibo la.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Eye Samuel fɔ ŋdi kanya, be yeayi aɖakpe Saul. Eye wogblɔ na Samuel bena: Saul va Karmel, eye wòli ŋkuɖodzinu ɖe afima, emegbe wòtrɔ yi Gilgal.

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Esi Samuel va Saul gbɔ la, Saul gblɔ nɛ bena: Yehowa ayra wò! Mewo Yehowa ƒe gbe dzi.

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Ke Samuel gblɔ bena: Alẽwo kple nyiwo ƒe xɔxlɔ̃ ka nye esi le ɖiɖim ɖe to me nam mele sesem?

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Saul ɖo ŋu bena: Amalekitɔwo gbɔ wokplɔ wo tsoe, elabena dukɔ la kpo alé kple nyi nyuiwo ta, be woatsɔ asa vo na Yehowa, wò Mawu la, ke mietsrɔ̃ kpɔtɔeawo gbidigbidi.

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Tete Samuel gblɔ na Saul bena: Ɖo to gbɔ, ne magblɔ nya, si Yehowa to nam eto ƒe zã la na wò! Egblɔ be: Ƒo nu!

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ be: Mele eme oa? Esi mèbu ɖokuiwò naneke o hã, mèzu Israel-toawo ƒe tatɔ oa? Eye Yehowa si ami na wò heɖo fia ɖe Israel nu.

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa dɔ wò ɖe nugbe gblɔ bena: Yi naɖatsrɔ̃ nuvɔ̃wɔla, siwo nye Amalekitɔwo la gbidigbidi, eye nawɔ aʋa kpli wo, vaseɖe esime natsrɔ̃ wo!

english_verse: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti meɖo to Yehowa ƒe gbe o; edze aboyonuwo dzi, eye nèwɔ nu vlo le Yehowa ŋku me?

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Saul ɖo ŋu na Samuel bena: Meɖo to Yehowa ƒe gbe tso, eye mede nusi gbe Yehowa dɔm ɖo la, nakplɔ Amalek-fia Agag ve, ke metsrɔ̃ Amalekitɔwo gbidigbidi.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Negbe dukɔ la koe ha alẽwo kple nyiwo, siwo nye busunuawo ƒe nyuitɔwo, be woatso asa va na Yehowa, wò Mawu la, le Gilgal.

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Tete Samuel gblɔ bena: A, numevɔsawo kple akpedavɔsawoe dzea Yehowa ŋu wu toɖoɖo Yehowa ƒe gbea? Kpɔ ɖa, toɖoɖo nyo wu vɔsa, eye nusese nyo wu agbo ƒe ami

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: Elabena tosesẽ enye afakaka ƒe nuvɔ̃, eye tamesesẽ enye legbawo kple aklama kpakpɛwo subɔsubɔ. Esi negbe Yehowa ƒe gbe la, eyata eya hã gbe wò be, magaɖu fia o.

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ na Samuel bena: Mewɔ nuvɔ̃ be, meda Yehowa ƒe se kple wò nyawo dzi; elabena ɖe mevɔ̃ dukɔ la, eyata mese woƒe gbe ɖo.

english_verse: Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
translation_verse: Eyata tso nye nuvɔ̃wo kem, eye nagbugbɔ kplim, ne made ta agu ɖe Yehowa ŋku me!

english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ na Saul bena; Nyemagbugbɔ kpli wò o; elabena ègbe Yehowa ƒe gbe, eye Yehowa hã gbe wò be, magaɖu fia ɖe Israel nu o.

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Ke esi Samuel trɔ be, yeadzo la, ele eƒe awu ʋlaya toga, eye wòdze.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
translation_verse: Tete Samuel gblɔ nɛ bena: Yehowa dze Israel-fiaɖuƒe la le asiwò egbe, eye wòtsɔe na hawòvi, si nyo wu wò.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Israel ƒe ŋusẽtɔ mekaa aʋatso o, eye metrɔa nya o, elabena menye ame wònye, ne wòatrɔ nya o.

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Mewɔ nuvɔ̃; gake de bubu ŋunye fifia le nye dukɔ la ƒe ame tsitsiwo kple Israel ŋku me dzro, eye nagbugbɔ kplim, ne mayi aɖade ta agu de Yehowa, wò Mawu la ŋku me!

english_verse: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Tete Samuel gbugbɔ kple Saul ɖo, eye Saul de ta agu ɖe Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Eye Samuel gblɔ bena: Mikplɔ Amalek-fia Agag vɛ nam! Agag zɔ yi egbɔ kakaka, eye Agag gblɔ bena: Ku ƒe vevesese gɔ̃ hã bu!

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ bena: Alesi wò yi ɖe viwo le nyɔnuwo ŋu la, nenema ke woaɖe viwo le dawò ŋu le nyɔnuwo dome! Eye Samuel dza Agag le Yehowa ŋku me le Gilgal.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Samuel dzo yi Rama, eye Saul yi eƒe xa nu le Saul ƒe Gibea.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Eye Samuel megakpɔ Saul kpɔ o vaseɖe eƒe kugbe; elabena Samuel xa nu le Saul ŋu, eye wòve Yehowa be, wòɖo fia Saul ɖe Israel nu.

english_verse: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Samuel bena: Ŋkeke nenie nanɔ konyi fam le Saul, amesi megbe be, megaɖu fia ɖe Israel dzi o la ŋu? De ami wò lãdzo la me, eye nayi; kpo ɖa, mele dɔwòm ɖe Isai gbɔ le Betlexem, elabena mekpɔ fia ɖi na ɖokuinye le viawo dome.

english_verse: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
translation_verse: Samuel do ŋu bena: Aleke mawɔ ate ŋui? Ne Saul see la, awum. Yehowa gblɔ bena: Kplɔ nyivi ɖeka ɖe asi, eye nagblɔ be: Vɔ sa ge meva na Yehowa.

english_verse: then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Kpe Isai va vɔsa la gbɔ, eye mana nanya nusi nawɔ asi ami na amesi magblɔ na wò la nam!

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Samuel wɔ, alesi Yehowa gblɔ nɛ la, eye wòva Betlexem. Tete dumegãwo ɖi vo, eye woyi ɖakpee gblɔ be: Ŋutifafa nèhe vɛa?

english_verse: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Ŋutifafae! Vɔ sa ge meva na Yehowa. Mikɔ mia ɖokui ŋu, ne miava vɔsa la gbɔ kplim! Eye wòkɔ Isai kple viawo ŋu hekpe wo va vɔsa la gbɔe.

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: Esi wova, eye wòkpɔ Eliab la, ebu bena: Eƒe amesiamina la enye si do ɖe Yehowa ŋku me vava!

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa gblɔ na Samuel bena: Megakpɔ eƒe dzedzeme kple eƒe atsudzɔdzɔ o, elabena megbee. Menye alesi amegbetɔ kpɔa nui o; elabena amegbetɔ kpɔa ŋku nu, ke.

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Yehowa kpɔa keke dzi me ke. Tete Isai yɔ Abinadab, eye wòkplɔe to Samuel ŋku me, ke egblɔ be: Yehowa metia eya hã o.

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: Isai kplɔ Sama to eŋku me, ke egblɔ be: Yehowa metia eya hã o.

english_verse: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
translation_verse: Ale Isai kplɔ via adreawo to Samuel ŋku me, gake Samuel gblɔ na Isai be: Yehowa metia woawo o.

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: Eye Samuel bia Isai bena: Ɖekakpuiawo vɔa? Eɖo ŋu bena: Ekpɔtɔ ɖevitɔ, kpɔ ɖa, eyi alẽkplɔƒe! Tete Samuel gblɔ na Isai bena: Dɔ ame woaɖakplɔe vɛ; elabena míayi nuɖugba nu o, vaseɖe esime wòava afisia hafi!

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Tete wòdɔ ame woɖakplɔe vɛ; ebiã, eƒe ŋkuwo le hɔ̃e, eve wònye ame kpokploe. Eye Yehowa gblɔ be: Tso, nasi ami nɛ, elabena eyae!

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Tete Samuel tsɔ lãdzo, si me ami le, eye wòsi ami nɛ le nɔviawo dome. Eye Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ va Dawid dzi tso gbemagbe dzi. Eye Samuel dze mo yi Rama. Dawid ƒe kasaŋkuƒoƒo fa akɔ na Saul.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ dzo le Saul dzi, eye gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃e ɖe tso Yehowa gbɔ va noa fu ɖem ne.

english_verse: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
translation_verse: Eye Saul ƒe dolawo gblɔ nɛ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ tso Mawu gbɔ le fu ɖem na wò.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Mía aƒetɔ ɖi nyaa ɖe gblɔ, wò dɔlawo nye si le ŋkuwò me, ne woaɖadi ŋutsua ɖe, si nya saŋkuƒoƒo, eye ne gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ tso Mawu gbɔ va dziwò la, woatsɔ eƒe asi aƒo saŋkui, ne wòaka ɖe me na wò!

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Saul ɖo ŋu na eƒe dolawo bena: Miyi ɖadi ŋutsu, si nya saŋkuƒoƒo nyuie la nam, eye mikplɔe va gbɔnye!

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Tete ɖekakpuiawo dometɔ ɖeka gblɔ bena: Kpo ɖa, mekpɔ Betlexemtɔ Isai ƒe viŋutsua ɖe, si nya saŋkuƒoƒo; enye kalẽtɔ, eye wònye aʋame, enya nuƒoƒo, eye wòdze ɖeka, eye Yehowa li kplii.

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: Eye Saul do ame ɖo ɖe Isai gbɔ, be wòagblɔ nɛ bena: Ɖo viwò Dawid, si le alẽkplɔƒe la ɖem!

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Tete Isai kple tedzi ɖeka, eye wòtsɔ abolo kple wein lãgbalẽgolo ɖeka kpa kple gbɔ̃vi ɖeka de via Dawid si ɖo ɖe Saul.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: Ale Dawid va Saul gbɔ, eye wòtsi tre ɖe eŋku me, eƒe nu lé dzi nɛ ŋutɔ, eye wòtrɔ zu eƒe adekplɔvi.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Eye Saul ɖo ame ɖo ɖe Isai bena: Na Dawid nanɔ gbɔnye, elabena eƒe nu nyo ŋunye!

english_verse: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_verse: Eye ne Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ la dze Saul dzi la, Dawid tsoa eƒe asi ƒoa kasaŋku, eye edzi kana ɖena na Saul, ekana ɖe eme nɛ, eye gbagba vɔ̃ la dzona le edzi.

english_verse: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
translation_verse: Eye Filistitowo ƒo woƒe aʋakɔwo nu ƒu, be yewoawɔ aʋa. Wova kpe ta ɖe Soxo le Yuda, eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Soxo kple Azeka dome le Efes-Damim.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Filistitowo tsi tre ɖe to ŋu le go si me, eye Israel tsi tre ɖe to ŋu le go keme, eye bali tso wo dome.

english_verse: The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall.
translation_verse: Tete ame dzɔtsua ɖe ɖo tso Filistitɔwo ƒe asaɖa la me, eŋkɔ nye Goliat, amesi tso Gat; ekɔ abɔklugui ade kple asi ɖeka.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: Esi Dawid gbɔ tso Filistitɔ la wuƒe la, Abner kplɔe yi Saul ŋku me, eye wòlé Filistitɔ la ƒe ta ɖe asi.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: Eƒe akplɔ ƒe ati le abe abaladoti ene, eye akplɔ la ŋuta kpe gayibɔ sekel alafa ade, eye akpoxɔnutsɔla zɔ eŋgɔ.

english_verse: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
translation_verse: Eye wòtsi tre yɔ Israel ƒe aʋalɔgoawo ɖa gblɔ na wo bena: Nukaŋuti mieho va dze aʋa? Alo menye Filistitɔ menye, eye miawo míenye Saul ƒe dolawo oa? Miɖe ŋutsu ɖeka le mia dome, ne wòava gbɔnye!

english_verse: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
translation_verse: Ne ete ŋu wɔ aʋa kplim, eye wòwum la, ekema mianye dɔlawo na mi; ke ne nye alɔ sẽ wu etɔ, eye mewui la, ekema mianye dɔlawo na mí, eye miasubɔ mi.

english_verse: Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
translation_verse: Eye Filistitɔ la gblɔ bena: Meɖe alɔme le Israel ƒe aʋalɔgoawo ŋu egbe. Miɖe ŋutsu ɖeka nam, ne mía kplii míawɔ aʋa!

english_verse: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
translation_verse: Esi Saul kple Israel blibo la se Filistitɔa ƒe nyawo la, dzi ɖe le wo ƒo, eye wovɔ̃ ŋutɔ.

english_verse: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
translation_verse: Dawid enye Efrattɔ ma, si tso Betlexem le Yuda, amesi ŋkɔ nye Isai la, ƒe vi; viŋutsu enyi le esi, eye wònye amegã ɖeɖi le ŋutsuwo dome le Saul ŋɔli.

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid dzona le Saul gbɔ enuenu ɖakplɔa fofoa ƒe alẽwo le Betlexem.

english_verse: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
translation_verse: Ke Filistitɔ la tena vana ŋdi kple fiẽ va tsia tre ɖi ŋkeke blane sɔŋ.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: Etsɔ eƒe atizɔti ɖe asi, eye wòdi kpe zɔzrɔ̃e atɔ̃ le tɔʋu la me hetsɔ wo de alẽkplɔnu, si nye akplɔ la me, eye wòlé eƒe akafo ɖe asi hezɔ ɖe Filistitɔ la dzi.

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Eye Isai gblɔ na via Dawid bena: Tsɔ bli tɔtɔe efa ɖeka sia kple abolo bɔbɔ ewo siawo ƒu du yi na nɔviwòwo le asaɖa la me!

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: Tsɔ notsi babla lalã ewo siawo yi na ame akpe ƒe amegã, eye bia nɔviwòwo be, woli sesĩe mahã? Eye xɔ dzesi tso wo gbɔ vɛ!

english_verse: They're with Saul's army, fighting the Philistines in Elah Valley.”
translation_verse: Woawo kple Saul kpakple Israel-ŋutsuwo katã le aʋa wɔm kple Filistitɔwo le logobali la me.

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid fɔ ŋdi kanya hetsɔ alẽawo de asi na alẽkplɔla, eye wòdo agba heyi, abe alesi Isai de se ne ene; eye wòva tasiaɖamwo ƒe takpeƒe, esime aʋakɔ la dze aʋa ɖe asi aseyetsotso me.

english_verse: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
translation_verse: Eye Israel kple Filistitowo ƒe aʋalɔgoawo dze aʋa hedze ŋgɔ wo nɔewo.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid tsa nusiwo wotso vɛ la, de asi na aʋawɔnuwo ŋu dzɔla, eye wòƒu du yi aʋadzedze la nu. Esi wòva la, ebia nɔviawo be, woli sesĩe mahã?

english_verse: While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
translation_verse: Esi wòle nu ƒom kpli wo la, kpo da, ame dzɔtsu, si ŋkɔ nye Goliat, amesi nye Filistitɔ tso Gat la, do tso Filistitowo ƒe aʋadzedze la me va gblɔ nya mawo ke, eye Dawid see.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Ke esi Israel-ŋutsuwo katã kpɔ ŋutsua la, wòsi le enu, eye wovɔ̃ ŋutɔ.

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: Eye Israel-ŋutsuwo gblɔ bena: Miele ŋutsu sia, si do va la, kpɔma? Alɔme de ge wòva le Israel ŋu. Ne amea de wui la, fia ana kesinɔnu geɖe, atsɔ vianyɔnu nɛ wòaɖe, eye wòana fofoa ƒe aƒe magadze nu le Israel o.

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
translation_verse: Tete Dawid bia ŋutsu, siwo le tsitre ɖe egbɔ bena: Nuka woawɔ na amesi awu Filistitɔ ma, eye wòaɖe ŋukpe ɖa le Israel ŋu la? Elabena ameka nye Filistitɔ bolotɔ sia, be wòanɔ alɔme ɖem le Mawu gbagbe la ƒe aʋalɔgoawo ŋu?

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Ameawo ɖo ŋu ne abe tsã ene be: Ale kple ale woawɔ na amesi wui la, enye si.

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: Esi nɔvia xoxoetɔ Eliab se, alesi wòle nu ƒom kple ameawo la, dzi ku Eliab ɖe Dawid ŋu wògblɔ bena: Nuka wɔ ge nèva, eye ameka si netsɔ alẽ ʋee mawo ɖee le gbeadzi? Menya dàda kple vovlo, si le wò dzi me, elabena aʋa teƒe kpɔ ge nèva!

english_verse: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
translation_verse: Dawid ɖo ŋu bena: Nuka mehewɔ fifia? Menye nya ta koe mebia oa?

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: Eye wòtrɔ le egbɔ te ɖe ame bubu ŋu hebia nya mawo ke, eye ameawo ɖo ŋu ne abe tsã ene.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: Wose nya, siwo Dawid gblɔ, eye wova gblɔe na Saul, eye wòna wokplɔe vɛ.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ na Saul bena: Dzika megatso amea ɖeke ƒo o! Wò dɔla ayi aɖawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔ ma.

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ na Dawid bena: Màte ŋu ayi aɖawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔ sia o, elabena ɖevi nènye, ke eya la aʋawɔla wònye tso ɖevime ke!

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ na Saul bena: Ne wò ɖɔla le fofoa ƒe alẽwo kplɔm, eye dzata alo sisiblisi va lé alẽ ɖeka le lãha ŋu la,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: metia eyome, eye meƒonɛ heɖenɛ le eƒe nu me; ke ne ebe, yeawɔ nu kplim la, meléa eƒe ge, eye meƒonɛ wuna.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: Alesi wò ɖɔla ƒoa dzata kple sisiblisi la, nenema ke wòava me na Filistitɔ bolotɔ sia abe wo dometɔ ɖeka ene, elabena Mawu gbagbe la ƒe aʋalɔgowo ŋu wòɖe alɔme le.

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: Dawid gagblɔ bena: Yehowa, si ɖem tso dzata kple sisiblisi si me la, eya ke aɖem tso Filistitɔ sia si me. Tete Saul gblɔ na Dawid bena: Heyi, Yehowa nanɔ kpli wò!

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Eye Saul na Dawid do eƒe awu, edɔ akɔblikuku ɖe ta nɛ, eye wòna wodo gawu nɛ.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: Eye Dawid ta eƒe yi ɖe awu la dzi, eye wòde asi zɔɖeɖe me, elabena mete edodo kpɔ o. Tete Dawid gblɔ na Saul bena: Nyemate ŋu anɔ alea ayi o, elabena nyemedoe kpɔ o. Eye Dawid ɖe wo ɖi.

english_verse: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
translation_verse: Eye Filistitɔ la le tetem ɖe Dawid ŋu, eye eƒe akpoxɔnutsɔla dze eŋgɔ.

english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: Eye Filistitɔ la fɔ kɔ dzi kpɔ Dawid, eye wòdo vloe, elabena ɖevi ko wònye, ebia, eye wòdze ɖeka.

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: Tete Filistitɔ la gblɔ na Dawid bena: Avũe menye, hafi nèfɔ kpowo gbɔna gbɔnyea? Eye Filistitɔ la yɔ eƒe mawuwo ƒo fi de Dawid.

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: Eye Filistitɔ la gblɔ na Dawid bena: Va gbɔnye, ne matsɔ wò dã na dziƒoxewo kple gbemelãwo!

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ na, Filistitɔ la bena: Wòa ètsɔ yi, tunuhlo kple akplɔ gbɔna gbɔnyee; ke nye la megbɔna gbɔwò le Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe aʋalɔgo, siwo ŋu nède alɔme le la ƒe Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ me.

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Yehowa atsɔ wò ade asi nam egbea, eye mawu wò atso ta le nuwò, eye matsɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ la ƒe kukuwo ana dziƒoxewo kple anyigba dzi lãwo egbe sia, ne anyigba blibo la nadze sii bena, Mawua de li na Israel;

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: eye ameha blibo sia nadze sii bena, Yehowa metsɔa yi alo akplɔ ɖea ame o; elabena aʋa enye Yehowa tɔ, eye eyae atsɔ mi ade asi na mí.

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid ƒo asi ɖe akplɔ me ɖe kpe ɖeka da kple akafo heƒo Filistitɔ la ƒe ŋgonu, eye kpe la ŋɔ eƒe ŋgonu, wòmũ tsyɔ mo anyi.

english_verse: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
translation_verse: Ale Dawid tsɔ akafo kple kpe la kpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe Filistitɔ la dzi, eye wòƒo Filistitɔ la hewui; ke yi mele Dawid si o.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid ƒu du te ɖe Filistitɔ la ŋu, eye wò ɖi eƒe yi le aku me hewui, eye wòtsɔe tso ta le enu. Esi Filistitɔwo kpɔ bena, woƒe kalẽtɔ ku la, wòsi.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-ŋutsuwo kple Yuda-ŋutsuwo ho, eye wotso aseye heti Filistitɔwo yome vaseɖe bali la me kple Ekron ƒe agbo nu, eye Filistitɔwo tsi aʋa ɖe Saarayim-mɔ dzi vaseɖe Gat kple Ekron.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-viwo trɔ tso Filistitɔwo yometiti me heva ha woƒe asaɖawo.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: Eye Dawid tsɔ Filistitɔ la ƒe ta va Yerusalem, eye wotsɔ eƒe aʋawɔnuwo da ɖe eƒe agbadɔ me.

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Esi Saul kpɔ Dawid wòyina Filistitɔa kpe ge la, ebia aʋafia Abner bena: Abner, ameka vi enye sia? Abner ɖo ŋu bena: Fiã, mefa wò siaa, nyemenyae o!

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Eye Saul biae bena: Ɖekakpui, ameka vi nènye? Dawid ɖo ŋu bena: Wò dɔla Betlexemtɔ Isai ƒe vi menye.

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Eye Saul xɔe gbemagbe, eye meɖe mɔ nɛ be, wòagbugbɔ ayi fofoa ƒe me o.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Eye Yonatan kple Dawid wòbia nu, elabena elɔ̃e abe eya ŋutɔ ɖokui ene.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Eye Yonatan ɖe awu ʋlaya, si le eŋu la, tsɔ na Dawid hekpe ɖe eƒe aʋawu kple yi, dati kple alidziblanu ŋu.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: Eye Dawid yia afisiafi, si Saul ɖoe ɖo, eye wòdze adaŋu; Saul tsɔe do aʋawɔlawo katã nu, eye eƒe nu nyo dukɔ blibo la kple Saul ƒe dɔlawo ŋu.

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Esi wogbɔ tso Dawid ƒe Filistitɔa wuƒe la, nyɔnuwo tso Israel-duwo katã me le ha dzim hele ɣe ɖum va kpe fia Saul; wole axatsɛ ƒom, le aseye tsom, eye wole gakogoe ƒom.

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: Eye nyɔnuawo le ʋu ƒom hedo ha ɖa bena: Saul wu akpe, Dawid wu akpe nane!

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Tete dzi ku Saul ŋutɔ, eye nya la medze eŋu o, eye wògblɔ bena: Wotsɔ akpe nane na Dawid, ke nye la wotsɔ akpe nam; fiaɖuƒe la koe kpɔtɔ ne!

english_verse: Saul never again trusted David.
translation_verse: Tso gbemagbe dzi Saul va Dawid kpɔ ge ɖe ƒomevii.

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ tso Mawu gbɔ va dze Saul dzi, eye wòdze agbo le aƒea me; ke Dawid tsɔ eƒe asi ƒo saŋku abe tsã ene, eye Saul lé akplɔ ɖe asi.

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: Eye Saul da akplɔ la, be yeatɔ Dawid amimi ɖe gli ŋu; ke Dawid de axa zi eve.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Azɔ Saul de asi Dawid vɔvɔ̃ me, elabena Yehowa li kplii; ke edzo le Saul ya gbɔ.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: Dawid ƒe mɔwo katã dzea edzi, elabena Yehowa li kplii.

english_verse: This made Saul even more afraid of David.
translation_verse: Esi Saul kpɔ be, nuwo dzea dzi nɛ ŋutɔ la, ede asi evɔvɔ̃ me.

english_verse: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
translation_verse: Ke Israel blibo la kple Yuda lɔ̃a Dawid ƒe nya, elabena edona dzea wo ŋgɔ, eye wògagbɔna kpli wo.

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ na Dawid bena: Kpɔ ɖa, matsɔ vinyenyɔnu xoxoetɔ Merab na wò naɖe; nye kalẽtɔ nam ko, eye wɔ Yehowa ƒe aʋa wo! Ke Saul gblɔ be: Matsi ye si me o, boŋ netsi Filistitɔwo si me!

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ na Saul bena: Ameka menye, ameka nɔvinyewo nye, eye nuka fofonye ƒe ƒome nye le Israel, ne mahayi fia ƒe to nye ge?

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Ke esi ɣeyiɣi, si Saul le vianyɔnu Merab tsɔ ge na Dawid wòaɖe, ɖo dzi la, etsɔe na Mexolatɔ Adriel wòɖe. Dawid ɖe Mixal.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Gake Saul ƒe vinyɔnu Mixal lɔ̃ Dawid ƒe nya; esi wova gblɔe na Saul la, ma la dze eŋu.

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: Tete Saul gblɔ bena: Matsɔe nɛ, ne wòatrɔ zu mɔ nɛ, eye Filistitɔwo ƒe asi natui! Eye Saul gblɔ na Dawid bena: Xɔ evelia, ne nanye nye to egbe!

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Saul ƒe dɔlawo gblɔ nya siawo ɖe Dawid ƒe to me, eye Dawid gblɔ bena: Nu tsɛ wònye le mia ŋku me be, woazu fia ƒe toa? Ke nye la ame dahe menye, eye nyemele ɖeke me o.

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Tete Saul ƒe dɔlawo va gblɔe ne bena: Ale kple ale Dawid gblɔ esi.

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ be: Ale miagblɔ na Dawid enye si: Fia mele srɔ̃ɖenua ɖeke dim o, negbe Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋanuyi alafa ɖeka ko, ne woabia hlɔ̃ fia ƒe futɔwo. Ke Saul bu be, yeana Dawid natsi Filistitɔwo si me.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Dɔlawo va to nya la na Dawid, eye nya la dze Dawid ŋu be, woazu fia ƒe to. Esi ŋkekeawo mekpɔ de haɖe o la,

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Esi Saul kpɔ dze sii be, Yehowa li kple Dawid, eye Saul vinyɔnu Mixal lɔ̃a eƒe nya la,

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, ne Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo ho, eye zi geɖe alesi woho la, edzea dzi na Dawid wu Saul ƒe dɔlawo katã, eye eƒe ŋkɔ de du ŋutɔ.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ na via Yonatan kple eƒe dɔlawo katã bena, woawu Dawid; ke Dawid ƒe nu lé dzi na Saul vi Yonatan.

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: Ke nye la mayi adatsi tre ɖe fofonye gbɔ le gbedzi, afisi nèle, eye maƒo nu le ŋuwò na fofonye, eye ne mekpɔ, alesi wòle la, mava gblɔe na wò.

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: Etsɔ eƒe agbe ɖo asiƒo me hewu Filistitɔ la, eye Yehowa ɖu dzi gãa ɖe na Israel blibo la. Wo ŋutɔ èkpɔe, eye dzi dzɔ wò; nukaŋuti nèbe, yeada vo ɖe ʋu maɖifɔ ŋu ahawu Dawid dzodzro?

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Tete Saul ɖo to Yonatan ƒe gbe, eye Saul ka atam bena: Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe, ne woawui fi!

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Tete Yonatan yɔ Dawid hegblɔ nyawo katã nɛ, eye Yonatan kplɔ Dawid vɛ na Saul wònɔ egbɔ abe tsã ene.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Eye aʋa gadzɔ, eye Dawid yi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo, eye wowu wo dometɔ geɖewo ŋutɔ, ale be wòsi le wo nu.

english_verse: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
translation_verse: Eye Saul di be, yeatɔ akplɔ Dawid amimi ɖe gli ŋu, ke ede axa na Saul, eye akplɔ la yi ɖatɔ gli. Eye Dawid si dzo le zã ma me.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Tete Saul dɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Dawid ƒe me, be woadzɔ eŋu, eye ne ŋu ke la, woawui. Eye Dawid srɔ̃ Mixal gblɔ nɛ bena: Ne mèɖe wò agbe le zã sia me o la, ekema ne ŋu ke la, àku!

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: Eye Mixal ɖiɖi Dawid to fesre nu, eye wòsi dzo heyi.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Eye Mixal tsɔ aklama kpakpɛ da de aba dzi, etsɔ gbɔ̃fuvɔ ɖo eƒe tade, eye wotsyɔ avɔ nɛ.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Tete Saul ɖɔ amewo ɖo ɖa, be woaɖakplɔ Dawid ve; ke egblɔ be, ele dɔ lém.

english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: Eye Saul dɔ amewo ɖo ɖa, ne woaɖakpɔ Dawid ɖa gblɔ bena: Miyi ɖakɔ eya kple abati la vɛ nam, ne mawui!

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Esi dɔlawo va la, kpɔ ɖa, aklama kpakpɛ le aba dzi, eye gbɔ̃fuvɔ le eƒe tade.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Tete Saul gblɔ na Mixal bena: Nukaŋuti nèflum, eye neɖe asi le nye futɔ ŋu wòsii? Mixal ɖo ŋu na Saul bena: Egblɔ nam be, ɖe asi le ŋunye mayi, ne menye nenem o la, mawu wò!

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: Ke Dawid si dzo, eye wòva Samuel gbɔ le Rama hegblɔ nusiwo katã Saul wɔe la, na Samuel, eye eya kple Samuel wònɔ Nayot. Saul hã le nyagblɔlawo dome.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Tete wova gblɔe na Saul be: Kpɔ ɖa, Dawid le Nayot le Rama.

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: Enumake Saul dɔ amewo ɖo ɖa, be woaɖakplɔ Dawid va; ke esi wokpɔ nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe ha le nya gblɔm ɖi, eye Samuel nye tatɔ le wo nu la, Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ va Saul ƒe dɔlawo dzi, ale be woawo hã gblɔ nya ɖi.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Eye wova gblɔe na Saul, tete wòda dɔla bubuwo ɖo ɖa, eye woa wo hã gblɔ nya ɖi.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Tete eya ŋutɔ yi Rama, eye esi wòva ɖo ʋe gã, si le Sexu gbɔ la, ebia bena: Afika Samuel kple Dawid wole? Woɖo ŋu be: Kpɔ ɖa, wole Nayot le Rama.

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Eye wòyi Nayot le Rama. Tete Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ la va eya hã dzi, eye wòde asi nyagbɔgblɔ me ɖi le yiyim, vaseɖe esime wòva Nayot le Rama.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: Eye eya hã ɖe eƒe awuwo ɖi hede asi nyagbɔgblɔ me ɖi le Samuel ŋku me, eye wòɖe ama ɖi ŋkeke blibo ma kple zã blibo la. Eyata wogblɔna be: Saul hãe le nyagblɔɖilawo domea?

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid si tso Nayot le Rama heva ƒo nu kple Yonatan gblɔ bena: Nuka mewo, vo ka meda, eye nuvɔ̃ ka mewo ɖe fofowò ŋu, hafi wòle nye ku dim?

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Esia nede megbe xaa, mèle kuku ge o! Kpɔ ɖa, fofonye mewɔa nu gã alo nu suea ɖeke, ne meɖee fiãm hafi o; nukaŋuti fofonye aɣla nusia ɖem? Mele alea o.

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: Ke Dawid gaka atam gblɔ bena: Fofowò nyae be, mèlɔ̃a nu le gbɔnye o, eyata wobu be, Yonatan meganyae, ne wòavee o! Ke meta Yehowa ƒe agbe kple wò siaa: Ne afɔɖeɖe ɖeka le mía kple ku dome fi!

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Tete Yonatan gblɔ na Dawid bena: Gblɔ nusi mawɔ na wò!

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ na Yonatan bena: Kpɔ da, etsɔ enye dzinu yeye, eye wòle nam be, mayi nuɖuƒe kple fia hafi; eyata na mayi ɖaɣla ɖokuinye de gbe me vaseɖe ŋkeke etɔ̃lia ƒe fiẽ!

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Ne fofowò bia tanye la, ekema gblɔ be: Dawid bia gbem be, yeade abla ayi yewo de Betlexem, elabena ƒome blibo la le ƒevɔ sa ge le afima.

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: Ne egblɔ be, enyo la, ekema wò dɔla ŋu fa; ke ne edo dɔmedzoe la, ekema nyae be, eɖo vɔ̃ ɖe tame.

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: Eyata ve wò dɔla nu, elabena mía kple wò dɔla míeɖo Yehowa ƒe nubabla me. Ne meda vo la, ekema wum, nukaŋuti nakplɔm ayi fofowò gbɔe?

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Yonatan gblɔ bena: Esia nede megbe xaa tso gbɔwò, ne menyae be, fofonye do vɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò, eye nyemeva gblɔe na wò o!

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: Tete Yonatan gblɔ na Dawid bena: Va miyi gbe me! Eye woa kple eve la woyi gbe me.

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Eye Yonatan gblɔ na Dawid bena: Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu! Ne medi nya le fofonye nu nyitsɔ wɔale siawo, eye kpɔ ɖa, eƒe dome kɔ ɖe Dawid ŋu, eye nyemedɔ wova gblɔe ɖe to me na wò o la,

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: ekema Yehowa nafia Yonatan agafiae ɖe dzi! Ne fofonye ɖo vɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò kplikpaa la, ekema mava gblɔe ɖe to me na wò, eye mado mɔ wò nayi le ŋutifafa me. Yehowa anɔ kpli wò, abe alesi wònɔ kple fofonye tsã ene!

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: Eye ne Yehowa tsrɔ̃ Dawid ƒe futɔwo dome ɖesiade ɖa le anyigba dzi la, megana wò lɔlɔ̃ la nu natsɔ le aƒenye me o tegbee!

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Eye Yonatan gaka atam na Dawid de dɔla, si wotsɔ lɔ̃e la dzi; elabena elɔ̃e abe eya ŋutɔ dokui ene.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Eye Yonatan gblɔ nɛ bena: Etsɔe nye dzinu yeye, eye wole tawo bia ge, elabena wò nɔƒe aɖi gbɔlo.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Eye nyitsɔ la nade abla ayi afisi nèɣla ɖokuiwò do le gbedzrogbe, eye nabɔbɔ nɔ Asel-kpe la gbɔ!

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: Mele aŋutrɔ etɔ da ge de exa, abe nanee medzidze ene.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: Eye madɔ ɖekakpuia ɖe ɖa agblɔ be: Yi ɖadi aŋutrɔwo! Ne megblɔ na ɖekakpui la be: Kpɔ ɖa, aŋutrɔwo le megbewò afi, fɔ wo vɛ la, ekema gbugbɔ, elabena ŋuwò fa, eye nyaa ɖeke meli o; mefa Yehowa ƒe agbe!

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Ke ne megblɔ na ɖekakpui la bena: Kpɔ ɖa, aŋutrɔwo le ŋgɔwò afime la, ekema yi, elabena Yehowa do mo wò!

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, nya, si mía kpli wò miegblɔ egbe la, Yehowa ano mia kpli wò dome tegbee!

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: Eye Dawid ɣla eɖokui ɖe gbea me. Esi dzinu yeye do la, fia la bɔbɔ nɔ kplɔ̃ ŋu, be yeaɖu nu.

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: Eye fia la bɔbɔ nɔ eteƒe xoxoa le gli ŋu, eye Yonatan tsi tre hena Abner bɔbɔ nɔ Saul ŋu, ke Dawid nɔƒe ɖi gbɔlo.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Ke Saul megblɔ nyaa ɖeke gbemagbe o, elabena ebu be, nanee dzɔ ɖe edzi, ale be eŋu manya kɔ o; eŋutie mekɔ o kokoko.

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: Esi Dawid nɔƒe ɖi gbɔlo le dzinu yeye ƒe ŋkeke evelia dzi la, Saul bia via Yonatan bena: Nukaŋuti Isai vi la meva nuɖuƒe etsɔ kple egbe oa?

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: Na mayi, elabena míaƒe ƒome le vɔ sa ge le dua me, eye nɔvinye ɖo du ɖem: ne ève nunye la, ekema ɖe mɔ nam, ne mayi aɖakpɔ nɔvinyewo ɖa. Eyata meva fia ƒe kplɔ̃ ŋu o ɖo.

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Tete Saul do dɔmedzoe ɖe Yonatan ŋu, eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Wò nyɔnu tsigbe ƒe vi! Menyae be, ètia Isai vi la, be natsɔ ado ŋukpe ɖokuiwò kple dawo ƒe ama.

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Elabena ŋkeke alesi Isai vi la le agbe le anyigba dzi la, mia kple wò fiaɖuƒe mali ke o; eyata ɖo, ne woakplɔe vɛ nam, elabena kuvi wònye!

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Yonatan ɖo ŋu na fofoa Saul gblɔ ne bena: Nukata woaku ɖo, eye nuka wòwɔ?

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Enumake Saul da akplɔe, be yeatɔe. Tete Yonatan dze sii, be ye fofoa ɖo be, yeawu Dawid.
