english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Eye dzi ku Yonatan vevie, wòtsi tre le kplɔ̃a ŋu, eye meɖu nu le dzinu yeye ƒe ŋkeke evelia dzi o; elabena ele nu xam le Dawid ta, elabena fofoa do ŋukpee.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, Yonatan yi gbe me, afisi eya kple Dawid woɖo ɖi, eye ŋutsuvi suea ɖe kpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na ŋutsuvi la bena: Ƒu du, nadi aŋutrɔ, siwo da ge mala! Tete ŋutsuvi la ƒu du, eye wòda aŋutrɔ to eta.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Esi ŋutsuvi la va, afisi Yonatan da aŋutrɔ wòdze la, Yonatan do ɣli ɖe ŋutsuvi la yome gblɔ bena: Aŋutrɔ la nye kem le ŋgɔwò afime!

english_verse: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
translation_verse: Yonatan gado ɣli ɖe ŋutsuvi la yome bena: Ɖe abla, nètso, megate o! Eye Yonatan ƒe ŋutsuvi la fɔ aŋutrɔawo va eƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Ke ŋutsuvi la menya naneke me o, negbe Yonatan kple Dawid koe nya nya la.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Yonatan tsɔ eƒe nuawo na ŋutsuvi, si kpe ɖe eŋu la, eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Tsɔ wo yi dua me!

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Esi ŋutsuvia dzo la, tete Dawid tsi tre tso dziehe gome, eye wòde ta agu hebɔbɔ zi etɔ̃, eye woɖuɖɔ nu na wo nɔewo heta avi kple wo nɔewo, vaseɖe esime Dawid ƒe gbe sẽ wu.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Eye Yonatan gblɔ na Dawid bena: Yi le ŋutifafa me; nusi dzi mía ame eve míeka atam ɖo le Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ dzi bena, Yehowa nanɔ mía kple wò, nye dzidzimeviwo kple wò dzidzimeviwo dome la, nanɔ anyi tegbee!

english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid va nunɔla Aximelex gbɔ le Nob; tete Aximelex ɖe abla va kpe Dawid, eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Nukaŋuti wò ɖeka neva, eye amea ɖeke mekpe de ŋuwò o?

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Eyata nuka le asiwò? Na abolo atɔ ato nusi nya le asiwò lam!

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: Nunɔla la gblɔ na Dawid bena: Abolo dzodzroa ɖeke mele asinye o, negbe abolo kɔkɔe koe li; ne ɖekakpuiawo nya kpɔ wo ɖokui dzi le nyɔnu gome ko.

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: Dawid ɖo ŋu na nunɔla la gblɔ nɛ bena: Wotsri nyɔnu na mi etsɔ kple nyitsɔ, hafi medze mɔ, eye ɖekakpuiawo ŋutinuwo ŋuti kɔ, evɔ wonye afɔ vɔ̃ dzi mele hafi; aleke abolo la ŋu makɔ le wo ŋutinuwo me egbea oa?

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Eye nunɔla la tsɔ nu kɔkɔe la nɛ, elabena aboloa ɖeke meli o, negbe ŋkumeɖobolo, si woɖe ɖa le Yehowa ŋku me, be woatsɔ abolo dzodzoe ada di le gbesigbe woɖee ɖa la koe.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: Ke Saul ƒe dɔlawo dometɔ ɖeka le afima, amesi wosika ɖe Yehowa ŋku me gbemagbe; eŋkɔ nye Doeg, Edom-tɔ, si nye Saul ƒe lãkplɔlawo ƒe amegã.

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ na Aximelex bena: Akplɔ alo yia ɖeke mele asiwò le afisia oa? Nyemetsɔ nye yi alo aʋawɔnua ɖeke ɖe asi o, elabena fia ƒe nya la le kplakplakpla dzi.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: Tete wòdo tsu eɖokui le woƒe ŋku me, eye wòle aɖaʋanu wɔm le wo si me, ele agbo la kukom, eye ade le tsyɔtsyɔm ɖe gè me nɛ.

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: Eye Axis gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo bena: Miekpɔ be, aɖaʋatɔ enye amesia, nukaŋuti miekplɔe va gbɔnyee?

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid dzo le afima hesi yi Adulam-gado la me, eye esi nɔviawo kple fofoaƒemetɔwo katã see la, woyi egbɔ le afima.

english_verse: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
translation_verse: Eye hiãtɔwo, fenyilawo kple amesiwo katã dome le vevem la, va kpe ta ɖe eŋu, eye wòzu woƒe tatɔ; amesiwo le eŋu la, woanɔ ame alafa ene.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid dzo tso afima heyi Mizpe le Moab, eye wògblɔ na Moab-fia bena: Taflatse, na fofonye kple danye naʋu ava mia gbɔ, vaseɖe esime manya, alesi Yehowa awɔ nam!

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: Eye wòkplɔ wo va Moab-fia gbɔe, eye wotsi egbɔ ŋkeke, siwo katã Dawid nɔ mɔ̃ me le to dzi.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Ke nyagblɔɖila Gad gblɔ na Dawid bena: Megatsi mɔ̃ me le to la dzi o, ke boŋ yi Yuda-nyigba dzi! Eye Dawid dzo heva ave me le Xarel. Saul na wowu nunɔla

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Eye Saul se Dawid kple amesiwo le eŋu la ŋkɔ. Ke Saul bɔbɔ nɔ to dzi le baniti te le Gibea; ele eƒe akplɔ ɖe asi, eye eƒe dɔlawo tsi tre ƒo xlãe.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: Tete Saul gblɔ na eƒe dɔla, siwo tsi tre ƒo xlãe la bena: Mi Benyamin-viwo, misee! Ɖe Isai vi la atsɔ agblewo kple weinbɔwo na mi katã? Eye ɖe wòaɖo mi katã amegãwoe ɖe ame akpe kple ame alafa nu,

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: hafi mi katã miebla ɖe ŋunye, eye amea ɖeke meli tofi nam be, vinye bia nu kple Isai vi la o, eye nye nya meɖi amea ɖeke, ne wòafi tofi nam be, vinye na nye futɔ de xa ɖe ŋunye, abe alesi wòle egbe sia ene oa?

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Tete Edomtɔ Doeg, amesi tsi tre ɖe Saul ƒe dɔlawo gbɔ, ɖo ŋu gblɔ bena: Mekpɔ Isai vi la, esime wòva Axitub vi Aximelex gbɔ le Nob.

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: Ebia nu Yehowa nɛ, etsɔ mɔ dzi nuɖuɖu ne, eye wotso Filistitɔ Goliat ƒe yi ne.

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Tete fia la da be, wòayi aɖayɔ nunɔla Aximelex, Axitub vi, kple fofoa ƒemetɔwo katã, siwo nye nunɔlawo le Nob la vɛ, eye wo katã wova fia la gbɔ.

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ bena: Axitub vi, se gbe! Eɖo ŋu bena: Nyee nye si, aƒetɔ!

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ nɛ bena: Nukaŋuti mia kple Isai vi la miebla ɖe ŋunye? Etso abolo kple yi ne, eye nèbia nu Mawu nɛ, ne wòaɖe xa ɖe ŋunye, abe alesi wòle egbe sia enea?

english_verse: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
translation_verse: Tete Aximelex ɖo ŋu na fia la gblɔ bena: Ameka le wò dɔlawo katã dome, si woa nuteƒe abe Dawid ene, amesi nye fia ƒe to, eye wònye amegã ɖe ŋuwò mewo nu, eye bubu le eŋu le aƒewò me?

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: Egbee mede asi nubiabia me Mawu nɛa? Esia nede megbe xaa tso gbɔnye! Fia megada nya ɖe eƒe dɔla kple fofonye ƒe aƒe blibo la dzi o, elabena wò dɔla mese nya suetɔ alo geɖe le nusiawo katã ŋu o.

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ bena: Wò Aximelex kple fofowò ƒe aƒemetɔwo katã miaku!

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Eye fia la gblɔ na blafo, siwo le tsitre ɖe egbɔ bena: Mile yi, ne miawu Yehowa ƒe nunɔlawo, elabena woawo hã ƒe asi le Dawid ƒe nya me, eye wonyae bena, ɖe wòsi, gake womeva fi tofi nam o! Ke fia ƒe dɔlawo melɔ̃ be, yewoado yewoƒe asi ɖa ada nu Yehowa ƒe nusiawo o.

english_verse: Saul turned to Doeg, who was from Edom, and said, “Kill the priests!” On that same day, Doeg killed
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ na Doeg bena: Wòa te yi, ne nada nu nunɔlawo! Enumake Edomtɔ Doeg te yi heda nu nunɔlawo, eye wowu ŋutsu blanyi va atɔ, siwo do aklalakɔmewuwo la gbemagbe.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: Etsɔ yi tsrɔ̃ Nob, si nye nunɔlawo ƒe du la, eye wotsɔ yi wu ŋutsuwo kple nyɔnuwo, ɖeviwo kple vidzĩewo, nyiwo kple tedziwo kpakple alẽwo.

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Eye Axitub vi, Aximelex ƒe vi ɖeka, si ŋkɔ nye Abyatar la, si dze Dawid yome.

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: Eye Abyatar gblɔ na Dawid bena: Saul wu Yehowa ƒe nunɔlawo!

english_verse: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid gblɔ na Abyatar bena: Gbemagbe, esi Edomtɔ Doeg le afima la, menyae bena, eyina egblɔ ge na Saul. Nyee ɖi fɔ le fofowò ƒemetɔwo katã ƒe ku me.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: Tsi gbɔnye, megavɔ̃ o, elabena amesi le nye ku dim la, eya aɖi wò hã wò ku; èkpɔ sitsoƒe le gbɔnye.

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: Eye wova gblɔ na Dawid bena: Kpɔ ɖa, Filistitɔwo le aʋa wɔm kple Kegila, eye wole lugbɔƒewo ham.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
translation_verse: Tete Dawid bia Yehowa bena: Mayi ɖasi Filistitɔ siawoa? Yehowa gblɔ na Dawid bena: Yi, ele Filistitɔwo si ge, eye èle Kegila ɖe ge.

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Tete Dawid ƒe amewo gblɔ nɛ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, miele vɔvɔ̃m le Yuda afisia tso, hafi míaho ayi Kegila aɖakpe kple Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋalɔgoawoa?

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Dawid gabia nu Yehowa, eye Yehowa ɖo ŋu gblɔ ne bena: Tso nayi Kegila, elabena matso Filistitɔwo aɖe asi na wò!

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid kple eƒe amewo yi Kegila, wowɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo, eye wokplɔ woƒe lãhawo dzoe, eye wowu wo dome ame geɖewo. Ale Dawid ɖe Kegilatɔwo.

english_verse: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Esi Dawid dze sii be, Saul ɖo vɔ̃ ɖe ye ŋu le adza me la, egblɔ na nunɔla Abyatar bena: Tsɔ kɔmewu la vɛ!

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ be: Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, wò dɔla se be, Saul le didim be, yeava Kegila, eye yeagblẽ du la le tanye.

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Ɖe Kegilatɔwo atsɔm ade asi nɛa? Eye ɖe Saul le vava ge, abe alesi wò dɔla se enea? Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, ɖee fia wò dɔla dzro! Yehowa gblɔ bena: Ele vava ge.

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ bena: Ɖe Kegilatɔwo atsɔ mía kple nye amewo ade asi na Saul mahã? Yehowa ɖo ŋu bena: Woatsɔ mi ade asi.

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid nɔ bebeƒewo le gbedzi kple towo dzi; eye Saul du ŋkekeawo katã, gake Mawu metsɔe de asi nɛ o.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid kpɔ bena, Saul ho be, yeadi eƒe ku. Ke Dawid le ave me le Sif-gbedzi.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Eye Saul vi Yonatan dze ma yi Dawid gbɔ le ave la me, eye wotso Mawu de dzi ƒo nɛ.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ ne bena: Megavɔ̃ o, elabena fofonye Saul ƒe asi matu wò o, eye wòe le fia ɖu ge ɖe Israel dzi, ke nye la manye evelia anɔ ŋuwò, eye fofonye hã nyae alea.

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: Eye woa kple eve la wobla nu le Yehowa ŋku me; Dawid tsi ave la me, ke Yonatan yi aƒe.

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Eye Siftɔwo va Saul gbɔ le Gibea gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, Dawid ɣla eɖokui ɖe mía gbɔ le bebeƒe ɖe ave me le Xaxila-togbɛ, si le gbegbe ƒe dziehe la dzi.

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ bena: Yehowa ayra mi, elabena mieve nunye!

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Miyi ɖadi eme tsitotsito, ne mianya, eye miakpɔ teƒe, si eƒe alo le, kpa kple amesi kpɔe le afima; ela bena wogblɔ nam bena, edze adaŋu ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Eyata miyi ɖadii le bebeƒe, siwo katã wòɣla ɖo la, eye ne mienyae vavã la, ekema migbugbɔ va gbɔnye, ne mayi kpli mi! Nenye be, ele anyigba la dzi la, ekema madii le Yuda ƒe ame akpeawo katã dome.

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Eye wotso dze Saul ŋgɔ heyi Sif; ke Dawid kple eƒe amewo le Maon-gbedzi le gbadzaƒe, si le gbegbe la ƒe dziehe gome.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Esi Saul kple eƒe amewo yi edi ge, eye wova gblɔe na Dawid la, eɖi abu yi agakpe la gbɔ ɖanɔ Maon-gbedzi. Ke esi Saul see la, eti Dawid yome va Maon-gbedzi.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Saul le to la ƒe go si me, ke Dawid kple eƒe amewo le to la ƒe go keme me; eye Dawid wɔ kaba, be yeasi le Saul nu, ke Saul kple eƒe amewo ɖe to ɖe Dawid kple eƒe amewo, be yewoalé wo.

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: Tete ame dɔdɔa ɖe va Saul gbɔ gblɔ bena: Nètsɔ nava, elabena Filistitɔwo va ƒo ɖe anyigba la dzi!

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Eye Saul gbugbɔ tso Dawid yometiƒe heyi ɖakpe Filistitɔwo. Eyata wona ŋkɔ teƒe ma bena kaklãgakpe.

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid tso afima yi ɖanɔ totamemɔ̃ me le En-Gedi.

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: Tete Saul ɖe ŋutsu tiatia akpe etɔ le Israel blibo la me heyi, be woaɖi Dawid kple eƒe amewo le agamegbɔ̃gakpe la dzi.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: Eye wova alẽkpɔwo gbɔ le mɔ to, afisi agadoa ɖe le, eye Saul yi ɖe eme, be yeade afɔdzi; ke Dawid kple eƒe amewo le agado la ƒe agɔ me gbɔ.

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na eƒe amewo bena: Neɖe megbe xaa tso gbɔnye le Yehowa ta be, mawo nusia ɖe nye aƒetɔ, si nye Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la ŋu ahade asi eŋu, elabena Yehowa ƒe amesiamina wònye.

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: Ke Dawid gbe nya na eƒe amewo, eye mena ma be, wòadze Saul dzi o; eye Saul tsi tre tso agado la me helé eƒe mo.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: Emegbe Dawid tso hedo le agado la me, eye wòdo ɣli ɖe Saul yome gblɔ bena: Nye aƒetɔ fia! Eye Saul nyẽ kɔ, tete Dawid de ta agu, eye wòbɔbɔ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, wò ŋkuwo kpɔe egbe sia be, Yehowa tsɔ wò ɖe asi nam egbea le agado la me; eye wogblɔ be, mawu wò, ke meve nuwò, eye megblɔ bena: Nyemaɖe asi nye aƒetɔ ŋu o, elabena Yehowa ƒe amesiamina wònye.

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: Fofonye, kpɔ ɖa, wò awu ʋlaya nu enye si le asinye; esi melã wò awu ʋlaya nu, eye nyemewu wò o la, nadze sii bena, vɔ̃ alo tame vɔ̃a ɖeke mele menye o, eye nyemewɔ nuvɔ̃a ɖeke ɖe ŋuwò o; ke wò la èle nye agbe ɖim be, yeaɖe ɖa.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Yehowa nadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu le mía kpli wò dome, eye Yehowa nabia hlɔ̃ wò nam, ke nye asi made ŋuwò o!

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Abe alesi blematɔwo doa lo ene be: Ame vɔ̃ɖiwo gbɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi tsona! Ke nye asi made ŋuwò o!

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
translation_verse: Ameka gɔ̃ yome Israel-fia la dze, eye ameka yome nètí? Avũ kuku alo dosu ɖeka kolia?

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: Esi Dawid wu nuƒoƒo na Saul nu vɔ la, Saul gblɔ bena: Vinye Dawid, wò gbee nye esia? Eye Saul fa avi kple ɣli

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: hegblɔ na Dawid bena: Enye ame dzɔdzɔe wum, elabena èwɔ nyui nam, ke nye la mewo vɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò!

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Ede nyui, si nèwɔ nam la, fia egbe be, esi Yehowa tsɔm de asi na wò la, mèwum o.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: Ɖe amea ɖe atu eƒe futɔ, eye wòana wòalé eƒe mo kɔ̃a? Eyata Yehowa natsɔ nyui aɖo eteƒe na wò le nusi nèwɔ nam egbe la ta!

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: Ke kpɔ ɖa, menyae be, èle fia zu ge, eye Israel-fiaɖuƒe la ali ke ɖe asiwò.

english_verse: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_verse: Eyata ta Yehowa nam be, matsrɔ̃ megbenye viwo o, eye màtsrɔ̃ nye ŋkɔ ɖa le fofonye ƒe me o!

english_verse: One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it.
translation_verse: Esi Dawid se le gbeadzi bena, Nabal va fu ko ge na eƒe alẽwo la,

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: Mese be, èva fu ko ge na alẽwo; wò lãkplɔlawo nɔ mia gbɔ, gake míede fu na wo o, eye woƒe naneke mebu le ŋkeke, siwo katã me wole Karmel o.

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: Bia wò ɖekakpuiawo, ne woagblɔe na wò! Eyata ve wò ɖekakpuiwo nu, elabena ŋkeke nyui dzi mieva. Na nusi le asiwò la wò dɔlawo kple viwò Dawid!

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid ƒe ɖekakpuiawo va gblɔ nya siawo katã na Nabal le Dawid ƒe ŋkɔ me, eye wole esinu kpɔm.

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Ke Nabal ɖo ŋu na Dawid ƒe dɔlawo gblɔ bena: Ameka nye Dawid, eye ameka nye Isai vi? Egbe siawo la dɔla geɖewo ɖe wole go dzem le woƒe aƒetɔwo gbɔ.

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Ɖe matsɔ nye nuɖuɖu kple nye nunono kpakple lã, si mewu na nye fukolawo la, na amesiwo nyemenya afisi wotso oa?

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid ƒe ɖekakpuiawo gbugbɔ lé woƒe mɔ heva gblɔ nyawo katã nɛ.

english_verse: “Everybody get your swords!” David ordered. They all strapped on their swords. Two hundred men stayed behind to guard the camp, but the other
translation_verse: Tete Dawid gblɔ na eƒe amewo bena: Mia dome amesiame nefa yi! Eye wo dome amesiame ta yi, eye wotso dze Dawid yome, woanɔ ame alafa ene; ke ame alafa eve tsi nuawo gbɔ.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Eyata bu ta me nadi nusi nawɔ, elabena woɖo vɔ̃ ɖe míaƒe aƒetɔ kple eƒe aƒe blibo la ŋu; ke eyama la ame vɔ̃ɖi wònye, eye amea ɖeke mekpɔ mɔ aƒo nu de egbɔ o

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na eƒe ɖekakpuiwo bena: Midze ŋgɔnye; kpɔ ɖa, mele mia yome dze ge! Ke megblɔ nyaa ɖeke na srɔ̃ Nabal o.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: Esi wòdo tedzi ɖi abu hebu ɖe toa xa la, tete Dawid kple eƒe amewo do ɖe edzi, eye wòƒo go wo.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: Ke Dawid gblɔ tsã bena: Yakatsyɔ mekpɔ amesia ƒe nuwo katã dzi le gbeadzi, be eƒe nuwo katã dome suetɔ hã mebu o, eye wòtsɔ vɔ̃ ɖo nyui teƒe nam.

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: Mawu afia Dawid ƒe futɔwo agafia wo ɖe dzi, ne makpɔtɔ eƒe ŋutsuwo katã dometɔa de ɖi, hafi ŋu nake fi!

english_verse: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Esi Abigail kpɔ Dawid la, ewɔ kaba ɖi le tedzi la dzi, eye wòde ta agu ɖe Dawid ŋku me hebɔbɔ ɖe anyigba.

english_verse: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
translation_verse: Nye aƒetɔ megaɖii na Nabal, ŋutsu vɔ̃ɖi sia o: elabena eya kple eƒe ŋkɔe sɔ: eŋkɔ nye Nabal, eye movitɔ wònye; ke wò dɔlanyɔnu mekpɔ nye aƒetɔ ƒe ɖekakpui, siwo wòdo ɖa la o.

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: Tsɔ wò dɔlanyɔnu ƒe vodadawo kee! Yehowa ana nye aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe nali ke, elabena Yehowa ƒe aʋawo wɔm nye aƒetɔ la le, eye dzɔgbevɔ̃ea ɖeke madzɔ ɖe dziwò le wò agbe me ŋkekewo katã me o!

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe tso ti yowòme, eye wòle wò ku dim la, ekema woabia wò agbe ɖe agbagbeawo ƒe nu me ɖe Yehowa, wò Mawu gbɔ; ke woatsɔ wò futɔwo ƒe agbe ade akafo me aɖa!

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: Eye nenye be, Yehowa na nu nyui, siwo ŋugbe wòdo na wò, nye aƒetɔ, va me nɛ pɛpɛpɛ, eye wotsɔ wò ɖo amegã ɖe Israel nu la,

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: ne nusia maganɔ mɔ me na wò, nye aƒetɔ, eye woaɖu dzi na wò, be wò, nye aƒetɔ, nèkɔ ʋu maɖifɔ ɖi, eye nèxɔ na ɖokuiwò o! Ne Yehowa na wònyo na wò, nye aƒetɔ la, ekema naɖo ŋku wò dɔlanyɔnu dzi!

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid gblɔ na Abigail bena: Woakafu Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, amesi dɔ wò ɖa nèva kpem egbe!

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: Woakafu wò nunya, eye woakafu wò, amesi xe mɔ nam egbe be, nyemagaɖe hlɔ̃fe, eye nyematsɔ nye asi axɔ na ɖokuinye o!

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Ɖeko meta Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, si xe mɔ nam be, nyemagawɔ vɔ̃ wò o la ƒe agbe, ɖe menye ɖe nèɖe abla va kpem o la, anye ne ŋutsua ɖeke makpɔtɔ na Nabal, hafi ŋu nake o.

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid xɔ nusiwo wòtsɔ vɛ la le esi, eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Yi aƒe le ŋutifafa me! Kpɔ ɖa, mese wò gbe, eye meve nuwò!

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Esi Abigail va Nabal gbɔ la, kpɔ ɖa, etu aglo ɖe eƒe me, abe alesi fia tua agloe ene, eye Nabal kpɔ dzidzɔ hemu aha wòtso me; ke megblɔ nya sue alo geɖe nɛ, vaseɖe esime ŋu ke o.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Ke esi ŋu ke, eye wein la kɔ le mo na Nabal la, srɔ̃a to nya siawo nɛ; tete dzi fa ɖe dɔ me ne, eye eyama zu kpe ɖi.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke ewo megbe la Yehowa ƒe asi va Nabal dzi, eye woku.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: Tete wòtsi tre, eye wotsyɔ mo anyi gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, wò dɔlanyɔnu aklɔ eƒe aƒetɔ ƒe dɔlawo ƒe afɔ ŋu abe kosi ene.

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Enumake Abigail wɔ kaba dze mɔ, edo tedzi, eye egbɔ nyɔnu atɔ̃ kpe ɖe eŋu, eye wòdze Dawid ƒe dɔlawo yome, eye wòzu srɔ̃a.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: Dawid ɖe Axinoam tso Yezreel hã, eye woa kple eve wòzu srɔ̃awo.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Ke Saul tsɔ vianyɔnu Mixal, si nye Dawid srɔ̃ la, na Lais vi Palti, tso Galim.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Eye Siftɔwo va Saul gbɔ le Gibea gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, Dawid yia eɖokui ɖe Xaxila-togbɛ la dzi le gbegbe la kasa.

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Eye Saul ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Xaxila-togbɛ, si le gbegbe la kasa le mɔ to la dzi; ke Dawid le gbeadzi. Esi Dawid kpɔ be, Saul ti eyome va gbea dzi la,

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: edɔ ŋkutsalawo ɖa, eye wose be, Saul va vavã.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid tso heva afisi Saul ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖo, eye Dawid kpɔ afisi Saul kple eƒe aʋafia Abner, Ner vi la mlɔ; Saul mlɔ tasiaɖamwo ƒe takpeƒe, eye aʋakɔ la ɖe to ɖee godoo.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid xɔ edzi gblɔ na Xititɔ Aximelex kple Abisai, Yoab nɔvi, Zeruya vi bena: Amekae ayi Saul gbɔ le asaɖa me kplim? Abisai ɖo ŋu bena: Mayi kpli wò!

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid kple Abisai wova aʋakɔ la gbɔ le zã me; kpo ɖa, Saul mlɔ anyi le alɔ̃ dam le tasiaɖamwo ƒe takpeƒe, eye wòtsɔ eƒe akplɔ tu anyi ɖe eƒe tade, eye Abner kple aʋakɔ la ɖe to ɖee godoo.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Tete Abisai gblɔ na Dawid bena: Mawu tso wò futɔ de asi na wo egbe, eyata na matu akplɔ edzi zi ɖeka pɛ amimi ɖe anyigba, nyemele eda ge zi eve o!

english_verse: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
translation_verse: Ke Dawid gblɔ na Abisai bena: Megawui o: elabena ameka ade eƒe asi Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la ŋu, eye woagbe tohehe nɛa?

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: Dawid gagblɔ bena: Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe: Ne menye Yehowae awui, alo eƒe ŋkeke aɖe woaku, alo wòayi aʋa woawui o fi!

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: Nede megbe xaa tso gbɔnye le Yehowa ta be, made nye asi Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la ŋu! Eyata tsɔ akplɔ, si le eƒe tade, kple tsize la, ne miadzo!

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid tso akplɔa kple tsize la le Saul ƒe tade eye wodzo: ke amea ɖeke mekpɔe o, amea ɖeke menyae o, eye amea ɖeke menyɔ o; ke boŋ wo katã wodɔ alɔ̃, elabena Yehowae na wodo alɔ̃ ku bliblibli.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid yi go keme hetsi tre ɖe to la tame le adzɔge, eye wo dome didi.

english_verse: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
translation_verse: Tete Dawid yɔ aʋakɔ la kple Abner, Ner vi ɖa bena: Abner, mèle tɔtɔ ge oa? Abner ɖo ŋu bena: Ameka nye ekema le ɣli dom ɖe fia la ta?

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ na Abner bena: Menye ŋutsue nènye oa? Ameka de nuwò le Israel? Nukaŋuti mèdzɔ wò aƒetɔ fia la ŋu oa? Elabena amea ɖe tso dukɔ la dome va, be yeawu wò aƒetɔ fia la.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: Menye nu nyui nye esia nèwɔ o. Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe be: Mi amesiwo medza miaƒe aƒetɔ, si nye Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la ŋu o la, miedze ku! Azɔ kpɔe ɖa be, afika fia ƒe akplɔ kple tsize, si le eƒe tade la le hã?

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Saul dze si Dawid ƒe gbe, eye wògblɔ bena: Wò gbeea, vinye Dawid? Dawid ɖo ŋu bena: Nye gbee, nye aƒetɔ fia!

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Nukaŋuti nye aƒetɔ le eƒe dɔla yome tim? Nuka mewo, eye vɔ̃ ka le ŋunye?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Azɔ nye aƒetɔ nese eƒe dɔla ƒe nyawo dzro: Nenye Yehowae do wò ɖe ŋunye la, ekema axɔ vɔsa aʋẽ ase, ke nenye amegbetɔviwoe la, ekema aɖi wo ŋu le Yehowa ŋku me, elabena wonyãm egbe, be nyemagakpɔ gome le Yehowa ƒe anyigba dzi o hegblɔ bena: Yi ɖasubɔ mawu bubuwo!

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Eyata nye ʋu megage ɖe anyigba ɖe adzɔge tso Yehowa ƒe ŋku ta o, elabena Israel-fia do be, wòadi dosu ɖeka, abe alesi wotia tegli yome le towo dzi ene.

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Tete Saul gblɔ bena: Mewɔ nuvɔ̃, gbugbɔ, vinye Dawid, nyemagawɔ vɔ̃a ɖeke wò azɔ o, elabena nye agbe xɔ asi le ŋkuwò me egbe, kpɔ ɖa, mewo lãnu, eye meda ƒu ŋutɔ.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: Dawid ɖo ŋu gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, fia ƒe akplɔ enye si, ɖekakpuiawo dometɔ ɖeka neva afi, ne woaxɔe!

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Yehowa aɖo amesiame ƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ kple nuteƒewɔwɔ teƒe nɛ, elabena Yehowa tsɔ wò de asi nam egbe, eye nyemeɖe asi Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la ŋu o.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, alesi wò agbe nye nu gã le ŋkunye me egbe la, nenema ke nye agbe anye nu gã le Yehowa ŋku me, eye wòaɖem tso hiãwo katã me.

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ na Dawid bena: Woayra wò, vinye Dawid; àdze egɔme, eye awu enu! Tete Dawid lé eƒe mɔ, eye Saul gbugbɔ yi enɔƒe.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: Ke Dawid gblɔ le eƒe dzi me bena: Gbe ɖeka ko mele Saul si me tsi ge; anyo nam wu, ne mesi yi ɖe Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, ekema Saul atasi nye nya, eye magadim le Israel-nyigba blibo la dzi azɔ o, eye mage le esi me.

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Esi wova gblɔ na Saul bena, Dawid si yi Gat la, megadii azɔ o.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ na Axis bena: Ne ève nunye la, ekema na nɔƒem ɖe anyigba dzi duawo dometɔ ɖeka me, ne manɔ afima; nukaŋuti wò dɔla anɔ fiadua me kpli wò?

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Tete Axis tso Ziklag nɛ gbemagbe; eyata Ziklag zu Yuda-fiawo to vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke, siwo Dawid no Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi la, le ƒe ɖeka kple dzinu ene.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid kple eƒe amewo yi ɖadze Gesuritɔwo, Girzitɔwo kple Amalekitɔwo dzi; elabena woawo na anyigba la dzi tso tititi yi ɖake de Sur kple Egipte-nyigba ŋu.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: Tete Dawid si anyigba la, eye mena ŋutsu alo nyɔnua ɖeke tsi agbe o, eye wotso alẽwo kple nyiwo, tedziwo kple kposɔwo kple avɔwo gbɔe va Axis gbɔ.

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: Dawid mena ŋutsu alo nyɔnu tsi agbe o, elabena ebu be, ne yekplɔ wo va Gat la, woava ƒo nu le yewo ŋu agblɔ be: Ale kple ale Dawid wo enye si. Alea wòwɔ le ŋkeke, siwo katã wònɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi la me.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: Axis ɖo ŋu ɖe Dawid ŋu hebu bena, anya wɔ nu baɖaa ɖe le eƒe dukɔ Israel gbɔ, eye wòanye yeƒe dɔla ɖaa.

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Esi Filistitɔwo kpe ta va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Sunem la, Saul hã ƒo Israel blibo la nu ƒu, eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Gilboa.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Ke esi Saul kpɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakɔa la, evɔ̃, eye dzika tso eƒo ŋuta.

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
translation_verse: Eye Saul bia nu Yehowa, ke Yehowa meɖo ŋu nɛ le drɔ̃e me loo alo to Urim alo nyagblɔɖilawo dzi o.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Tete Saul gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo bena: Midi nyɔnua ɖe, si me ŋɔliyɔgbɔgbɔ le la nam, ne mayi egbɔ aɖabia nui ase. Eƒe dɔlawo gblɔ nɛ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, nyɔnu ŋɔliyɔlaa ɖe le En-Dor.

english_verse: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
translation_verse: Tete Saul trɔ eƒe nɔnɔme hedo awu bubuwo, eye eya kple ŋutsu eve woyi heva nyɔnu la gbɔ le zã me. Eye wògblɔ bena: Ka nu, ne nayɔ ŋɔli nam, eye nakplɔ amesi mayɔ na wò la vɛ nam!

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Nyɔnu la gblɔ nɛ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, wò ŋuta ènya nusi Saul wo, eye wotsrɔ̃ ŋɔliyɔlawo kple afakalawo ɖa le anyigba la dzi. Nukaŋuti nèle mɔ trem na nye agbe, be nawum?

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Tete Saul ta Yehowa nɛ bena: Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe, ne fɔɖiɖi anɔ dziwò le nya sia me fi!

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Nyɔnu la gblɔ bena: Ameka yɔ ge mala na wò? Eɖo ŋu bena: Yɔ Samuel nam!

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Esi nyɔnua kpɔ Samuel la, edo ɣli sesĩe. Eye nyɔnu la gblɔ na Saul bena: Nukaŋuti nèblem? Evɔ wònye wòe nye Saul hafi!

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Ke fia la gblɔ nɛ bena: Megavɔ̃ o, nuka nèhekpɔ ma? Nyɔnu la ɖo ŋu na Saul bena: Mekpɔ mawua ɖe le dodom tso anyigba tu me.

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
translation_verse: Eye wòbiae bena: Aleke eƒe nɔnɔme le? Eɖo nu bena: Ame tsitsia ɖe le dodom, eye wòɖo awu ʋlaya. Esi Saul dze sii bena, Samuel ye la, ede ta agu, eye wobɔbɔ.

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Eye Samuel gblɔ na Saul bena: Nukaŋuti neɖe fu nam, eye nèna wokplɔm vɛ? Saul ɖo ŋu bena: Meɖo xaxa me ŋutɔ: Filistitɔwo le aʋa wɔm kplim, ke Mawu trɔ ʋu le yonyeme, eye megale nya ŋu ɖom nam azɔ to nyagblɔɖilawo dzi loo alo to drɔ̃e me o; eyata mena woyɔ wò vɛ, ne nagblɔ nusi mawɔ la nam!

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ be: Yehowa trɔ ʋu le yowòme hezu wò futɔ; evɔ nukaŋuti nèle nu biamem?

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Yehowa wɔ, abe alesi wògblɔ to dzinye ene, eye Yehowa xɔ fiaɖuƒe la le asiwò hetsɔ na hawòvi Dawid.

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: Esi meɖo to Yehowa ƒe gbe o, eye mèwɔ eƒe dɔmedzoe, si wòdo ɖe Amalek ŋu dzi o la, eyata Yehowa le nusia wɔm wò egbea ɖo.

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Yehowa atsɔ Israel hã ade asi na Filistitɔwo akpe ɖe ŋuwò, eye etsɔ la mía kple viwòŋutsuwo miava gbɔnye, Yehowa atsɔ Israel ƒe aʋakɔ la hã ade asi na Filistitɔwo.

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Enumake Saul tsra ɖe anyigba dremu, eye wòvɔ̃ ŋutɔ le Samuel ƒe nyawo ta. Ŋusẽ gɔ̃ hã megale eŋu o, elabena meɖu naneke ŋkeke blibo kple zã blibo la o.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Eye nyɔnu la va Saul gbɔ, eye wòkpɔ bena, dzidzi ƒoe ŋutɔ. Tete wògblɔ nɛ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, wò dɔlanyɔnu sewo gbe; metsɔ nye agbe ɖo asi ƒo me, eye meɖo to wò nya, siwo negblɔ nam.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: Eyata wò hã ɖo to wò dɔlanyɔnu ƒe gbe, eye na matsɔ abolo via ɖe aɖo akɔwòme, ne naɖu, be ŋusẽ naɖo ŋuwò, hafi nalé wò mɔ!

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: Ke egbe gblɔ bena: Nyemele nu ɖu ge o. Tete eƒe dɔlawo kple nyɔnu la ƒoe ɖe enu, eye wòɖo to woƒe gbe, eye wòtsi tre tso anyigba hebɔbɔ nɔ aba dzi.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Nyivi damia ɖe le nyɔnu la si le aƒea me, eye wòɖe abla hetsoe, eye woku wɔ blu hetɔ tatali maʋamaʋã.

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: Eye wòtsɔe va ɖo Saul kple eƒe dɔlawo kɔme, eye woɖui; emegbe; wotso hedzo le zã ma me.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Tete Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo do dɔmedzoe ɖe eŋu, eye Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo gblɔ ne bena: Na ame sia nagbugbɔ ayi teƒe, si netsɔ nɛ, ne magayi aʋa la kpli mí, eye wòanye miaƒe futɔ le aʋa me o! Elabena nuka ame sia awɔ atsɔ dze eƒe aƒetɔ ŋu, ne menye ame siawo ƒe ta oa?

english_verse: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
translation_verse: Ɖe menye eyae nye Dawid, amesi nu wodzi ha le heɖu ɣe bena: Saul wu akpe, Dawid wu akpe nane oa?

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Tete Axis yɔ Dawid gblɔ nɛ bena: Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe, ame dzɔdzɔe nènye, eye wò aʋahoho kple gbɔgbɔ kplim dze ŋunye; elabena nyemekpɔ vɔ̃a ɖeke le ŋuwò tso gbesigbe nèva gbɔnye vaseɖe egbe o; ke wò nya metrɔ na amegãwo o.

english_verse: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
translation_verse: Eyata gbugbɔ yi le ŋutifafa me, eye megawɔ nusi medze Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo ŋu o!

english_verse: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ na Axis bena: Nuka mehewɔ, eye nuka nèkpɔ le wò dɔla ŋu, tso gbesigbe meva gbɔwò vaseɖe egbe, esi ta nyemekpɔ mɔ aɖawɔ aʋa kple nye aƒetɔ fia ƒe futɔwo o?

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Axis ɖo ŋu gblɔ na Dawid bena: Nye la menyae bena, ame nyui nènye abe mawudɔla ene, ke Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo gblɔ bena, megayi aʋa la kpli mí o!

english_verse: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
translation_verse: Eyata mia kple wò aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla, siwo va kpli wò la, mifɔ ŋdi kanya, hafi ŋu nake ade le eme, eye midzo!

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid kple eƒe amewo fɔ ŋdi kanya, eye wodze mɔ le ŋdi hegbugbɔ yi Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi; ke Filistitɔwo ho yi Yezreel.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: Esi Dawid kple eƒe amewo gbɔ va Ziklag le ŋkeke etɔ̃agbe la, kpɔ ɖa, Amalekitɔwo va dze dziehenyigba kple Ziklag dzi, eye wòsi Ziklag hetɔ dzoe.

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: Esi Dawid kple eƒe amewo va dua me la, kpɔ ɖa, wòtɔ dzoe, eye wòlé woƒe viŋutsuwo kple vinyɔnuwo.

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid kple aʋakɔ, si le eŋu la, fa avi kple ɣli, vaseɖe esime avi meganya le fafam na wo o.

english_verse: David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
translation_verse: Wòlé Dawid srɔ̃ eveawo, siwo nye Yezreeltɔ Axinoam kple Karmeltɔ Nabal srɔ̃ Abigail hã.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: Eye Dawid xaxa ŋutɔ, elabena aʋakɔ la be, yeaƒu kpee, elabena dzi ku aʋakɔ blibo la dome amesiame le viaŋutsuwo kple vianyɔnuwo ta; ke Dawid tsɔ eƒe Mawu, Yehowa, do ŋusẽ eɖokui.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ na nunɔla Abyatar, Aximelex vi bena: Tsɔ kɔmewu la vɛ! Tete Abyatar tsɔ kɔmewu la yi na Dawid.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid bia nu Yehowa bena: Mati adzoha sia yomea? Eye matu woa? Eɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Ti wo yome, elabena èle wo tu ge, eye axɔ ameawo!

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: Wokpɔ Egipte-ŋutsua ɖe le gbe me, eye wokplɔe va Dawid gbɔe, eye wona aboloe woɖu kpakple tsii wono.

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: Woka gbotsetsebolo hetsɔ weintsetse ƒuƒu kpe ɖe eŋu nɛ woɖu, eye agbe gaɖo eme, elabena ŋkeke etɔ̃ kple zã etɔ̃ sɔŋ meɖu abolo o, eye meno tsi o.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: Dawid biae bena: Ameka ƒe ame nènye? Eye afika nètso? Eɖo ŋu be: Egipte-ɖekakpui menye, eye menye Amalekitɔa ɖe ƒe dɔla; ke nye aƒetɔ gblẽm ɖi, elabena dɔ dze dzinye ŋkeke etɔ̃agbe enye egbe.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: Míeyi ɖadze Kretitɔwo ƒe dziehe kple Yuda-nyigba kpakple Kaleb ƒe dziehe gome dzi, eye mieta dzo Ziklag.

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ nɛ bena: Màkplɔm ayi adzoha siawo gbɔe oa? Eɖo ŋu bena: Ta Mawu nam be, màwum o, eye màtsɔm ade asi na nye aƒetɔ o, ekema makplɔ wò ayi adzoha siawo gbɔe!

english_verse: He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah.
translation_verse: Esi wòkplɔe yii la, kpɔ ɖa, wokaka ɖe anyigba blibo la dzi, eye wole nu ɖum le nu nom hele ɣe ɖum le aboyonu geɖe, siwo katã woha tso Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba kple Yuda-nyigba dzi la ta.

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid si wo tso ɣetrɔ vaseɖe fiẽ, eye wo dometɔa ɖeke mesi o, negbe ɖekakpuivi alafa ene, siwo do kposɔ si la koe.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid xɔ nusiwo katã Amalekitɔwo ha la, eve Dawid xɔ srɔ̃a eveawo hã.

english_verse: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
translation_verse: Woƒe nusiwo katã woɖe aboyo la, dometɔa ɖe ke mekpɔtɔ o, eɖanye ɖevi alo ame tsitsi, ŋutsuviwo alo nyɔnuviwo o, Dawid xɔ wo katã gbɔe.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid xɔ alẽwo kple nyiwo katã hã, eye wokplɔ wo dze lãha bubuawo ŋgɔ, eye wole gbɔgblɔm bena: Dawid ƒe aboyonu enye si!

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Tete ame vlo kple yakame, siwo katã le ŋutsu, siwo de kple Dawid dome la gblɔ bena: Esi woawo mede kpli mí o la, eyata miana aboyonu, siwo míexɔ la, ƒe ɖeke wo o; ke boŋ wo dome amesiame nekplɔ srɔ̃a kple viawo ko, ne wòayi!

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Ke Dawid gblɔ bena: Nɔvinyewo, migawɔ alea o! Yehowae tsɔ nu siawo na mi, ekpɔ mia ta, eye wotsɔ adzoha, siwo va dze mía dzi la, de asi na mí.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Ameka aɖo to mi le nya sia me? Ke boŋ amesiwo de aʋa la kple amesiwo tsi nuawo gbɔ la, namãe sɔsɔe; woamã wo hayooe!

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔe wɔ se kple kɔnu na Israel tso gbemagbe dzi vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Esi Dawid gbɔ va Ziklag la, eɖo aboyonuawo ƒe ɖewo ɖe Yuda-ame tsitsiwo, siwo nye xɔlɔ̃awo la bena: Kpɔ ɖa, mixɔ nunana tso Yehowa ƒe futɔwo ƒe aboyonuwo me!

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Eye Filistitɔwo wɔ aʋa kple Israel, eye Israel-ŋutsuwo si le Filistitɔwo nu, eye amewo tsi aʋa le Gilboa-to la dzi.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo ɖe Saul kple viaŋutsuwo ɖe nu, eye wowu Saul viŋutsuwo, siwo nye Yonatan, Abinadab kple Malkisua.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Aʋa la nu sẽ ŋutɔ ɖe Saul dzi, eye esi aŋutrɔdalawo va tui la, vɔvɔ̃ ɖoe ŋutɔ le aŋutrɔdalawo ŋu.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Eye Saul gblɔ na eƒe adekplɔvi la bena: Di wò yi naƒo ɖem, ne bolotɔ siawo magava ƒo nu ɖem awɔ funyafunyam o! Ke eƒe adekplɔvi la melɔ̃ o, elabena ele vɔvɔ̃m ŋutɔ. Tete Saul tsɔ eƒe yi, eye wòdze enu.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Ke esi Saul ƒe adekplɔvi la kpɔ be, eku la, eya hã tso eƒe yi dze enu, eye woku kplii.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Ale Saul kple viaŋutsu etɔ̃awo kple eƒe adekplɔvi la kpakple eƒe amewo katã ku gbe ɖeka enye si.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Esi Israel-ŋutsu, siwo le bali la ƒe go keme kple Yordan ƒe go keme dzi, kpɔ bena, Israel-ŋutsuwo si, eye Saul kple viaŋutsuwo ku la, wogblẽ woƒe duwo ɖi hesi, eye Filistitɔwo va nɔ wo me.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la. Filistitɔwo va nu ɖe ge le ame tsiaʋawo ŋu, eye wokpɔ Saul kple viaŋutsu etɔ̃awo le Gilboa-to la dzi.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Ke esi: Yabes-Gileadtɔwo se nusi Filistitɔwo wɔ Saul la,

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: tete ŋutsu kalẽtɔwo dze mɔ zɔ zã blibo la ɖaɖe Saul kple viaŋutsuwo ƒe kukuawo le gli ŋu le Bet-San, eye wova Yabes hetɔ dzo wo le afima.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ woƒe ƒuwo ɖi ɖe baniti te le Yabes, eye wotsi nu dɔ ŋkeke adre.

english_verse: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me le Saul ƒe ku megbe, esime Dawid gbɔ tso Amalek-ʋa, eye Dawid nɔ Ziklag ŋkeke eve megbe la,

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsua ɖe tso Saul ƒe asaɖa me va le ŋkeke etɔ̃agbe, awu vuvu le eŋu, eye ke le ta me nɛ. Eye esi wòva Dawid gbɔ la, ede ta agu, eye wòbɔbɔ.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid biae bena: Afika netso? Eɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Israel ƒe asaɖa mee mesi tso!

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ nɛ bena: Aleke nya la le? Taflatse, gblɔe nam! Eye wòɖo ŋu bena: Dukɔ la si le aʋa la nu, eye ame geɖewo tsi aʋa le dukɔ la dome, eye Saul kple via Yonatan hã ku.

english_verse: David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
translation_verse: Tete Dawid bia ɖekakpui, si to nya la nɛ bena: Aleke newɔ, hafi nyae be, Saul kple via Yonatan ku?

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Ɖekakpui, si to nya la nɛ la, ɖo ŋu bena: Nanetɔe meva Gilboa-to la dzi, eye kpo ɖa. Saul ziɔ ɖe eƒe akplɔ ŋu, eye tasiaɖam kple sɔdolawo ɖee ɖe enu.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: Esi wònyè ka kpam la, eyɔm, eye metɔ bena: Nyee nye si!

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: Eye wòbiam bena: Ameka nenye? Meɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Amalekitɔ menye.

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nam bena: Te ɖe ŋunye, ne nawum, elabena ŋuzi le tsɔyem, eye agbe gale menye ko.

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: Tete mete ɖe eŋu hewui, elabena menyae be, anyi, si wòdze la, menye agbenɔtɔe o; eye meɖe ŋgoblanu la le eta kple abɔga le eƒe abɔ hetsɔ va afi na nye aƒetɔ.

english_verse: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid kple ŋutsu, siwo katã le eŋu la, dze woƒe awuwo.

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: Eye wofa konyi, fa avi hetsi nu dɔ vaseɖe fiẽ le Saul kple via Yonatan kple Yehowa ƒe dukɔ la kpakple Israel ƒe aƒe la ŋuti, le esi wotsi yi nu la ta.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid bia ɖekakpui, si to nya la nɛ bena: Afikatɔ nènye? Eɖo ŋu bena: Amalekitɔa ɖe, si nye amedzro la ƒe vi menye.

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ nɛ bena: Wò ʋu anɔ wò ta dzi! Elabena wò ŋutɔ wò nue ɖi ɖase le ɖokuiwò ŋu gblɔ bena: Mewu Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la. Dawid ƒe konyifaha le Saul kple via Yonatan ƒe ku ŋuti.

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: Tete Dawid kpa konyifaha sia le Saul kple via Yonatan ŋu,

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: Oo Israel, wowu wò atsyɔ̃ɖoɖo le wò togbɛwo dzi! Aleke kalẽtɔwo hetsi aʋa ale!

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Migaɖe gbe ƒãe le Gat o, eye migado kpoe le Askalon ƒe ablɔwo me o, ne Filistitɔwo ƒe vinyɔnuwo nagadzɔ dzi, eye bolotɔwo ƒe vinyɔnuwo nagatso aseye o!

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: Mi Gilboa-towo, zãmu alo tsi magadza ɖe mia dzi o, eye agble wɔnuwo maganɔ mia dzi o; elabena afima wotsɔ kalẽtɔwo ƒe akpoxɔnu ƒu gbe ɖo. Saul ƒe akpoxɔnu le abe ɖe womesi ami nɛ o ene.

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Yonatan ƒe aŋutrɔ medea megbe le ame tsiaʋawo ƒe ʋu kple kalẽtɔwo ƒe ami me o, eye Saul ƒe yi megbɔna ƒuƒlu o.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: Saul kple Yonatan, amesiwo wolɔ̃na le woƒe agbe me, eye tsi metoa wo dome o, wo dome memã le ku me hã o; woɖe abla wu hɔ̃, eye wosesẽ wu dzata.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: Israel-nyɔnuviwo, mifa avi na Saul, amesi la aɖabɛ na mi heɖo atsyɔ̃ na mi, eye wòɖo sikatsyɔ̃ɖonu ɖe awu: dzi na mi!

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: Aleke kalẽtɔwo tsi aʋa ale, eye wowu wò, Yonatan, ɖe wò togbɛwo dzi!

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: Tɔwo le veyem, nɔvinye Yonatan! Wò nu vivi nunye ŋutɔ, eye wò hlɔ̃ nam ƒo nyɔnuwo ƒe lɔlɔ̃ ta!

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: Aleke kalẽtɔwo tsi aʋa, eye aʋawɔlawo tɔ aka ale!

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Le nya sia megbe la Dawid bia Yehowa bena: Mayi Yuda-duawo dometɔ ɖeka mea? Yehowa ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Yi! Eye Dawid gblɔ be: Afika yi ge mala? Yehowa ɖo ŋu bena: Yi Xebron!

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid yi afima, eye srɔ̃ eveawo, Yezreeltɔ Axinoam kple Karmeltɔ Abigail, kpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid kplɔ ŋutsu, siwo le eŋu, hã yii amesiame kple eƒemetɔwo, eve wonɔ Xebron-duwo me.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Tete Yuda-ŋutsuwo va, eye wosi ami na Dawid le afima, ne woaɖu fia ɖe Yuda ƒe aƒe la dzi. Eye wova gblɔ na Dawid bena: Yabes-Gileadtɔwoe nye amesiwo ɖi Saul.

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: Tete Dawid ɖɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Yabes-Gileadtɔwo gblɔ na wo bena: Yehowa ayra mi, elabena mieve miaƒe aƒetɔ Saul nu, eye mieɖii!

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa ave mia nu, eye wòaɖi anukware na mi, eye nye hã mawɔ nyui sia tɔgbe na mi, le esi miewɔ nusia la.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Ke migana miaƒe asi nado agblɔ o, eye miwɔ ŋutsu, elabena miaƒe aƒetɔ Saul ku, eye Yuda ƒe aƒe la si ami nam, be maɖu fia ɖe wo dzi.

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Ke Saul ƒe aʋafia Abner, Ner vi, kplɔ Saul vi Is-Boset yi Maxanayim,

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: eye wòɖoe fia ɖe Gilead kple Asertɔwo, Yezreel, Efrayim, Benyamin kple Israel blibo la dzi.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: Ŋkeke, siwo Dawid ɖu fia le Xebron de Yuda ƒe aƒea dzi la, le ƒe adre kple dzinu ade.

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Eye Abner, Ner vi, kple Saul vi Is-Boset ƒe dɔlawo ho tso Maxanayim yi Gibeon.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Eye Zeruya vi Yoab kple Dawid ƒe dɔlawo hã ho, eye wova ƒo go wo nɔewo le Gibeon-tato; woawo le ta la ƒe go si me, eye ame meawo le ta la ƒe go keme.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Tete Abner gblɔ na Yoab bena: Na ɖekakpuiawo natsi tre; ne woate wo ɖokui akpɔ le mía ŋku me! Eye Yoab gblɔ bena: Ne wotsi tre!

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Eye wotsi tre yi le woƒe xexlẽme nu; ame wuieve nye Saul vi Is-Boset lɔ tso Benyamin, eye wo ame wuieve tso Dawid ƒe dɔlawo dome.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Wòlé ta na wo nɔewo heƒo yi ɖe wo nɔewo ƒe abla me, eye wodze anyi zi ɖeka. Eye wona ŋkɔ teƒe sia be nudaƒe; ele Gibeon. Abner wu Asahel.

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Aʋa la nu sẽ ŋutɔ gbemagbe, eye Dawid ƒe dɔlawo si Abner kple Israel-ŋutsuwo.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Eye Zeruya viŋutsu etɔ̃ le afima: Yoab, Abisai kple Asahel; eye Asahel ƒe afɔ tsɔna abe zi le gbe me ene.

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Tete Abner nyẽ kɔ gblɔ bena: Wòe nye Asahel mahã? Eɖo ŋu bena: Nyee.

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Abner gblɔ nɛ bena: Dze ɖe ɖusi alo mia me, eye nalé ɖekakpuiawo dometɔ ɖeka aɖe eŋutinu na ɖokuiwò! Ke Asahel gbe be, yematrɔ le eyome o.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Abner gagblɔ na Asahel bena: Trɔ le yonyeme dzro! Nukata mada nu wò aƒu anyi? Aleke mawɔ agate gu akpɔ nɔviwò Yoab ŋku mea?

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Ke egbe tɔtrɔ, eye Abner tso akplɔnu ƒo ɖe do me nɛ, eye akplɔ la ɖi go ɖe egodo, eye wòdze anyi ɖe afima heku ɖe eteƒe. Eye wòva me, ne amesiame va teƒe, si Asahel dze anyi ku ɖo la, etɔna ɖi.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Eye Yoab kple Abisai woti Abner yome, eye esi ɣe ɖo to la, wova Ama-togbɛ, si le Giax kasa le Gibeon-gbegbe-mɔ dzi la gbɔ.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Tete Benyamin-viwo ƒo wo ɖokui nu ƒu ɖe Abner yome hewɔ asafokɔ ɖeka, eye wotsi tre ɖe togbɛa ɖe ta me.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Eye Abner yɔ Yoab gblɔ bena: Ɖe yi anɔ nuɖuɖu dzi koa? Menyae be, ava vɔ̃ɖi ɖe dzi emegbe oa? Ɣekaɣi nagblɔ na dukɔ la be, woatrɔ le wo nɔviwo yomea?

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Yoab ɖo ŋu bena: Meta Mawu ƒe agbe, ɖe menye wòe ƒo nu o la, anye ne dukɔ la gbugbɔ le wo nɔewo yome tso egbe ŋdi ke.

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Eye Yoab ku kpẽ, tete aʋakɔ blibo la tɔ, womegati Israel yome o, eye wodzudzɔ aʋawɔwɔ.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Eye Abner kple eƒe amewo to tagba le zã blibo la me hetso Yordan, eye woto ʋe blibo la me va Maxanayim.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Eye esi Yoab gbugbɔ tso Abner yometiƒe la, eƒo aʋakɔ blibo la nu ƒu, eye ame wuiasieke hekpe ɖe Asahel ŋu to le Dawid ƒe dɔlawo dome.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Eye wokɔ Asahel ɖaɖi de fofoa ɖiƒe le Betlexem; eye Yoab kple eƒe amewo zɔ zã blibo la, eye ŋu ke de wo le Xebron.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Esi aʋa nɔ Saul ƒe aƒe kple Dawid ƒe aƒe dome la, Abner ku de Saul ƒe aƒe ŋu vevie.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Ahiãa ɖe nɔ Saul si, eŋkɔ nye Rizpa, Aya vinyɔnu. Eye Is-Boset gblɔ na Abner bena: Nukaŋuti nède fofonye ƒe ahiã gbɔ?

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
