translation_verse: Tete Abner do dɔmedzoe le Is-Boset ƒe nyawo ta gblɔ bena: Avũ ta menye tso Yuda? Meve fofowò ƒe aƒe kple nɔviawo kpakple xɔlɔ̃awo nu egbea, eye nyemetsɔ wò de asi na Dawid o; eye wòa nèle nya hem de ŋunye le nyɔnu ta fifia?

english_verse: I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him!
translation_verse: Mawu nefia Abner, ne wòagafiae de dzi, ne nyemewɔ, abe alesi Yehowa ka atam na Dawid be:

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: yeaxɔ fiaduƒe la le Saul ƒe aƒe si, eye yeana Dawid ƒe fiazikpui nali ke ɖe Israel kple Yuda dzi tso Dan vaseɖe Beer-Seba o fi!

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Ke mete ŋu ɖo nyaa ɖeke ŋu na Abner o, elabena ele evɔ̃m.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Enumake Abner dɔ amewo do de Dawid, ne woagblɔ nɛ bena: Ameka tɔe nye anyigba la? Eye wògagblɔ be: Bia nu kplim, eye kpɔ da, nye asi akpe de ŋuwò, be matrɔ Israel blibo la de ŋuwò!

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Enyo, mabia nu kpli wò: ke nu ɖeka dim mele tso asiwò; makpɔ nye ŋku me o, negbe ɖeko nakplɔ Saul vinyɔnu Mixal vɛ, hafi ava kpɔ nye ŋku me!

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: Tete Dawid dɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Saul vi Is-Boset, ne woagblɔ nɛ be: Kplɔ srɔ̃nye Mixal, si metsɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋanuyi alafa ɖeka ɖe la, vɛ nam!

english_verse: Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
translation_verse: Eve Is-Boset dɔ woɖaxɔe le srɔ̃a Lais vi Paltiel si vɛ.

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Eye srɔ̃a dze eyome le avi fam ʋuu kekeke vaseɖe Baxurim; eye Abner gblɔ nɛ bena: Gbugbɔ yi! Tete wògbugbɔ.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Ke Abner ƒo nu kple Israel-amegãwo bena: Menye egbe o, menye etsɔ o, miele Dawid dim, be wòaɖu fia de mia dzi.

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Miwɔe azɔ! Elabena Yehowa gblɔ le Dawid ŋu be: Nye dɔla Dawid ƒe asi dzi to ge mala ade nye dukɔ Israel tso Filistitɔwo kple woƒe futɔwo katã si me.

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Eye Abner ƒo nu ɖe Benyamin hã ƒe to me: emegbe Abner yi Xebron, be yeagblɔ nusiwo katã dze Israel kple Benyamin ƒe aƒe blibo la ŋu la, na Dawid.

english_verse: soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
translation_verse: Esi Abner kple ŋutsu blave, siwo kpe ɖe eŋu, va Dawid gbɔ le Xebron la, Dawid wɔ amedzro na Abner kple ŋutsu, siwo kpe ɖe eŋu la.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Eye Abner gblɔ na Dawid bena: Na matso ayi aɖaƒo Israel blibo la nu ƒu ɖe nye aƒetɔ fia ŋu, ne woabia nu kpli wò, eye, naɖu fia, alesi dze ŋuwò! Tete Dawid ɖo Abner ɖa wòyi le ŋutifafa me.

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: Eye kpɔ ɖa, Dawid ƒe dɔlawo kple Yoab gbɔ tso adzoʋa, eye wohe aboyonu geɖe gbɔe; ke Abner megale Dawid gbã le Xebron o, elabena eɖoe ɖa wòyi le ŋutifafa me.

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Esi Yoab kple aʋakɔ blibo, si le eŋu, gbã la, wogblɔ na Yoab bena: Abner, Ner vi, va fia la gbã, eye wòɖoe ɖa wòyi le ŋutifafa me.

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Tete Yoab va fia la gbɔ gblɔ bena: Nuka nye esi nèwu? Kpɔ ɖa, Abner va gbɔwò; nukaŋuti nèɖoe ɖa wodzo?

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: Mènya Abner, Ner vi la oa? Elabena nuwò ble ge wòva, ne wòanya wò dodo kple wò gbɔgbɔ kpakple nusiwo katã nèwɔna.

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Tete Yoab do le Dawid gbɔ hedɔ ame ɖo ɖe Abner yome, eye wotrɔe tso Sira-vudo la gbɔ gbee, ke Dawid menyae o.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Esi Abner trɔ gbɔ va Xebron la, Yoab kplɔe yi agbo la te, be woa kplii woaɖe kpɔ; eye wòda nu do me nɛ le afima wòku ɖe nɔvia Asahel ƒe ʋu ta.

english_verse: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
translation_verse: Ke esi Dawid va see la, egblɔ bena: Mia kple nye fiaɖuƒe la míeɖi fa le Abner, Ner vi ƒe ʋu me o le Yehowa ŋku me tegbee.

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: Neva Yoab ƒe ta kple fofoa ƒe aƒe blibo la dzi, eye afuɖɔla kple anyidzela, amesi tɔna ɖe ati ŋu kple amesi tsia yi nu kpakple amesi abolokoe wona, nu matso le Yoab ƒe me o!

english_verse: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Yoab kple nɔvia Abisai wowu Abner, le esi wòwu wo nɔvi Asahel le aʋa me le Gibeon la ta.

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid gblɔ na Yoab kple ameha, siwo katã le eŋu, bena: Midze miaƒe awuwo, mita akpanya, eye mifa konyi le Abner ŋgɔ! Eye fia Dawid dze amekukugba la yome.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Eye woɖi Abner ɖe Xebron; fia la fa avi kple ɣli le Abner ƒe yɔdo to, eye ameha blibo la hã fa avi.

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: Eye fia la fa na Abner gblɔ bena: Ɖe Abner aku abe yakame enea?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: Womebla asi na wò o, eye womede akɔbliga afɔ na wò o; èku, abe alesi wokuna ɖe ame vlowo si me ene! Tete ameha blibo la gafa avi ɖe dzi wu.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Esi ɣe gale dzi ko, eye ameha blibo la va nuɖuɖu na ge fiaa la, Dawid ka atam bena: Mawu nefiam ne wòagafiam ɖe dzi, ne made nu nuɖuɖu alo nu bubua ɖe ŋu, hafi ɣe naɖo to fi!

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Eye esi ameha blibo la dze sii la, edze wo ŋu; nusianu, si fia la wɔ la, dze ameha blibo la ŋu.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: Eye ameha la katã kple Israel blibo la dze sii gbemagbe bena: Abner, Ner vi la ƒe ku metso fia la gbɔ o.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: Eye fia la gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo bena: Mienyae be, amegãa ɖe kple ame ŋkɔŋua ɖee ku egbea le Israel oa?

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Ke nye la ɖevi dzaa menye, hafi wòsi ami nam menye fia. Ke Zeruya vi siawo tri akɔ wum. Yehowa naɖo vɔ̃ eteƒe na nuawɔla ɖe eƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wowɔ la nu!

english_verse: Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
translation_verse: Esi Saul vi se bena, Abner ku le Xebron la, eƒe asiwò gbɔdzɔ, eye dzidzi ƒo Israel blibo la.

english_verse: Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsu eve, siwo nye adzohawo kplɔlawo, le Saul vi la si; ɖeka ŋkɔ nye Baana, eye evelia ŋkɔ nye Rexab, amesiwo nye Beerottɔ Rimon viwo tso Benyamin-viwo dome, elabena wobua Beerot hã kpe ɖe Benyamin ŋu;

english_verse: The people who used to live in Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they still live there.
translation_verse: ke Beerottɔwo si yi Gitaim, eye wonye amedzrowo le afima vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsuvia ɖe le Saul vi Yonatan si, amesi ƒe ata tu. Exɔ ƒe atɔ̃, esime du tso Yezreel va le Saul kple Yonatan ŋuti; tete enyila tsɔe kpa hesii, eye esi wòle kplakplakpla dzi le sisim la, ege, eye wòtu; eŋkɔ nye Mefiboset.

english_verse: One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting
translation_verse: Azã Beerottɔ Rimon viwo, Rexab kple Baana, tso yi, eye wova Is-Boset ƒe me le ŋdɔkutsu, esime wòle ŋdɔlɔ̃ dɔm.

english_verse: in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them. Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long.
translation_verse: Esi wova aƒea me la, emlɔ eƒe aba dzi le xɔgã me, tete woda nui wu, eye wotso ta te enu hetsɔ eƒe ta dze mɔ to tagba le zã blibo la me.

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ Is-Boset ƒe ta vɛ na Dawid le Xebron gblɔ na fia la bena: Kpɔ ɖa, wò futɔ Saul vi Is-Boset, amesi le wò ku dim la, ƒe ta enye si; ale Yehowa bia hlɔ̃ Saul kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo na nye aƒetɔ fia egbe sia!

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: Melé ame ma, si va gblɔ nam be, Saul ku la, eye mewui le Ziklag, evɔ wònye eya ŋutɔ bu be, gbe nyui yehe vɛ, eye mana dɔtsɔho ye hafi.

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: Azɔ esi ame vlowo wu ame dzɔdzɔe ɖe eƒe aba dzi le eƒe xɔ me la, ɖe nyemabia eƒe nu tso mia si, eye matsrɔ̃ mi ɖa tso anyigba dzi oa?

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid de se na ɖekakpuiawo, eye wowu wo helã woƒe asiwò kple afɔwo ɖaku ɖe ta to le Xebron; ke wotso Is-Boset ƒe ta ɖi ɖe Abner ƒe yɔdo me le Xebron.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
translation_verse: Eye Tiro-fia Xiram ɖo amewo kple sedertiwo ɖe Dawid hekpe ɖe atikpalawo kple kpefulawo ŋu, ne woatu xɔ na Dawid.

english_verse: He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for
translation_verse: Eɖu fia ɖe Yuda dzi le Xebron ƒe adre kple dzinu ade, eye wòɖu fia ɖe Israel blibo la kple Yuda dzi le Yerusalem ƒe blaetɔ̃ va etɔ̃. Dawid xɔ Yerusalem.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
translation_verse: Eye fia la kple eƒe amewo ho yi Yerusalem ɖe Yebusitɔ, siwo nye anyigbadzitɔwo la ŋu; ke woawo gblɔ na Dawid bena: Màte ŋu ava afisia o, ŋkuagbãtɔwo kple xodrɔ̃wo koe anyẽ wò! Egɔme enye be, Dawid mate ŋu ava afisia o.

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid le ŋusẽ kpɔm ɖe dzi, eye Yehowa, aʋakɔwo ƒe Mawu la, li kplii. Dawid ƒe aƒe kple eƒe dziɖuɖuwo.

english_verse: David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people. David's Sons Born in Jerusalem (
translation_verse: Azɔ Dawid dze sii bena, Yehowae ɖo ye, ne yeaɖu fia ɖe Israel dzi, eye wòna eƒe fiaɖuƒe de dzi le eƒe dukɔ Israel ta.

english_verse: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children.
translation_verse: Esi Dawid tso Xebron va la, egadze ahiãwo, eye wòɖe srɔ̃wo le Yerusalem, eye wogadzi ŋutsuviwo kple nyɔnuviwo na Dawid.

english_verse: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
translation_verse: Yibxar, Elisua, Nefeg kple Yafia,

english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Tete Filistitowo se bena, wosi ami na Dawid heɖo fiae ɖe Israel dzi, eye Filistitɔwo katã ho, bena woadi Dawid. Eye esi Dawid see la, eyi mɔ̃ la me.

english_verse: So the Philistines camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Eye Filistitɔwo va kaka ɖe Refaim-bali la me.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?” The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid bia nu Yehowa bena: Mahe ɖe Filistitɔwo ŋua, eye ɖe atsɔ wo ade asi nama? Yehowa ɖo ŋu na Dawid bena: Ho yi, elabena matsɔ Filistitɔwo ade asi na wò!

english_verse: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Tete Dawid va Baal-Perazim, eye Dawid si wo le afima, eye wògblɔ bena: Yehowa dze nye futɔwo le ŋgɔnye, abe alesi tɔsisi ŋɔa go ene. Eyata wona ŋkɔ teƒe ma bena Baal-Perazim.

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Ke wogblẽ woƒe legbawo ɖe afima, eye Dawid kple eƒe amewo fɔ wo.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Eye Filistitɔwo gaho heva kaka ɖe Refaim-bali la me

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid bia nu Yehowa, eye wòɖo ŋu nɛ be: Megaho yi o, ke boŋ to wo megbe, ne nava tu wo le klẽtiawo kasa!

english_verse: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
translation_verse: Eye ne eva me be, zi ɖi va to klẽtiawo dome nèse la, ekema wɔ kaba, elabena Yehowa dze ŋgɔwò, be wòasi Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ la!

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid wɔ, abe alesi Yehowa de se nɛ ene, eye wòsi Filistitɔwo tso Geba vaseɖe Gezer.

english_verse: The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, ne Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la tsɔlawo ɖe afɔ zi ade la, etsɔa nyitsu ɖeka kple nyivi dami ɖeka sa vɔe.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
translation_verse: Dawid ɖu ɣe kple ŋusẽ katã le Yehowa ŋku me, eye Dawid do aklala-kɔmewu.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid kple Israel ƒe aƒe blibo la te aseye tsom le kpẽ kum hetsɔ Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la yii.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Esi Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la va Dawid ƒe dua me la, Saul vinyɔnu Mixal le fesre nu kpɔ Dawid le kpo tim hele ɣe ɖum le Yehowa ŋku me, eye woɖu fewu le eŋu le eƒe dzi me.

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
translation_verse: Woɖa Mawu ƒe aɖaka la ɖe tasiaɖam yeyea ɖe me, eye wotsɔe tso Abinadab ƒe aƒe, si le togbɛ dzi la me, eye Abinadab viwo Usa kple Axio kplɔ tasiaɖam yeye la.

english_verse: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid kple dukɔ blibo, si le eŋu la, dze mɔ yi Baal-Yuda, ne woatsɔ Mawu ƒe aɖaka, si ŋu woyɔa Yehowa Zebaot, amesi le Kerubiwo ta me ƒe ŋkɔ ɖo la, atso afima.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid kple Israel ƒe aƒe blibo la le ɣe ɖum kple ŋusẽ katã hele ha dzim ɖe saŋku kple kasaŋku, axatsɛ, nyawowoe kple gakogoe ŋu le Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Esi wova Naxon ƒe lugbɔƒe la, Usa do asi ɖa lé Mawu ƒe aɖaka la, elabena nyiawo dze ɖe aga.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa do dɔmedzoe ɖe Usa ŋu, eye Mawu ƒoe ƒu afima ɖe Mawu ƒe aɖaka la xa.

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: Tete wòve Dawid be, Yehowa ɖe Usa ɖa, eye wòna ŋkɔ teƒe ma be Perez-Usa vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid vɔ̃ Yehowa gbemagbe hegblɔ be: Aleke Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la ava gbɔnye?

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid melɔ̃ be, woatsɔ Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la ava ye gbɔe le Dawid ƒe ɖu la me o; eye Dawid na be, woaɖadroe ɖe Gattɔ Obed-Edom ƒe me.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Eve wova gblɔna fia Dawid bena: Yehowa yra Obed-Edom ƒe aƒe kple eƒe nuwo katã le Mawu ƒe aɖaka la ta. Tete Dawid yi ɖakɔ Mawu ƒe aɖaka la tso Obed-Edom ƒe me va Dawid ƒe ɖu la me kple dzidzɔ.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ Yehowa ƒe aɖaka la va da ɖe enɔƒe le agbadɔ, si Dawid tu nɛ la me, eye Dawid sa numevɔ kple akpedavɔ le Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Esi Dawid sa numevɔ kple akpedavɔ vɔ la, eyra dukɔ la le Yehowa Zebaot ƒe ŋkɔ me.

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: Eye Dawid ma abolo bɔbɔ, lãkɔ kple weintsetse ƒuƒu abolo ɖekaɖeka na dukɔ la katã, si nye Israel ƒe ameha blibo la dome amesiame, eye dukɔ blibo la dome amesiame yi eƒe xɔ nu.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: Esi Dawid yi gbe do ge na eƒemetɔwo la, tete Saul vinyɔnu Mixal va kpe Dawid gblɔ bena: Aleke gbegbe Israel-fia de bubu eɖokui ŋu heɖe ama le eteviwo ƒe dɔlanyɔnuwo ŋku me egbe, abe alesi yakamewo ɖea amae ene!

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid gblɔ na Mixal bena: Yehowa, amesi ŋu nye nu nyo wu fofowò kple eƒe aƒe blibo la, eye wòtsɔm ɖo amegã ɖe Yehowa ƒe dukɔ Israel nu la, ŋku mee meɖu ɣe le!

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: Ne meɖi gbɔ, eye medo yakame ɖokuinye ʋuu hã la, ɖe mebe, made bubu ɖokuinye ŋu le dɔlanyɔnu, siwo ŋu nèƒo nu le la ŋku me.

english_verse: Michal never had any children.
translation_verse: Ke Saul vinyɔnu Mixal tsi ko vaseɖe eƒe kugbe.

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Gake nye amenuveve madzo le egbo, abe alesi mena wodzo le Saul, amesi meɖe ɖa le ŋkuwò me la gbɔ ene o.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: fia la gblɔ na nyagblɔɖila Natan bena: Kpɔ ɖa, nyea mele sedertixɔ me, ke Mawu ƒe aɖaka la le kuntruwo te.

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Natan do ŋu na fia la bena: Yi nawɔ nusianu, si le wò dzi me; elabena Yehowa li kpli wò!

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ƒe gbe va Natan gbɔ le zã ma me bena:

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: Yi nagblɔ na nye dɔla Dawid bena: Ale Yehowa to enye si: Wòe atu xɔ nam manɔ emea?

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Elabena tso gbesigbe mekplɔ Israel-viwo tso Egipte la, nyemenɔ xɔa ɖeke me vaseɖe egbe o, ke boŋ menɔ agbadɔ kple nɔƒe la me henɔa tsatsam.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Ŋkeke alesi menɔ Israel-viwo katã dome tsã la, ɖe megblɔ na Israel ƒe toawo dometɔa ɖe, si meɖo be, wòanyi nye dukɔ Israel la bena: Nukaŋuti mietu sedertixɔ nam oa?

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: Azɔ ale nagblɔ na nye dɔla Dawid enye si: Gbe, si Yehowa Zebaot do enye si: Mekplɔ wò tso lãnyiƒe le alẽwo yome, be naɖu amegã ɖe nye dukɔ Israel nu!

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Menɔ anyi kpli wò le afisiafi, si nèto, metsrɔ̃ wò futɔwo katã ɖa le ŋgɔwò, eye mede ŋkɔ gã ŋuwò abe ame ŋkɔŋu, siwo le anyigba dzi ƒe ŋkɔ ene.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: Mana nɔƒe nye dukɔ Israel, eye mana wòaɖo zunu anyi, ne wòanɔ eteƒe, eye dzika magatso eƒo azɔ o, eye ame vlowo magatee ɖe anyi azɔ abe tsã ene

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: tso gbesigbe meɖo ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ɖe nye dukɔ Israel nu la o. Mana gbɔdzɔe wò tso wò futɔwo katã si me, eye Yehowa le gbɔgblɔm na wò be: Yehowa le xa tu ge na wò!

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Ne wò azã de, eye nèmlɔ fofowòwo gbɔ la, ekema maɖo viwò, si ɖo tso wò ali me la, ɖe yowòme, eye mana eƒe fiaɖuƒe nali ke.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Eya natu xɔ na nye ŋkɔ, eye maɖo eƒe fiaɖuƒe ƒe fiazikpui te dzi ɖaa.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Manye fofoa, eye eya anye vinye, eye ne eda vo la, mahe to nɛ kple ameƒoti, eye maƒoe, abe alesi woƒoa amegbetɔviwo ene.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Elabena wò Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔe ɖe wò dɔla ƒe to me bena: matu xɔ na wò; eyata dzi ɖo wò dɔla ƒo wòle gbe sia dom ɖa na wò.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Eye fia Dawid yi ɖabɔbɔ nɔ Yehowa ŋku me hegblɔ bena: Aƒetɔ Yehowa, ameka menye, eye nuka nye aƒe nye be, nèkplɔm vaseɖe fifi?

english_verse: and yet you have promised to do even more. Is this the way you usually treat people?
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Yehowa, ɖe esia nye nu tse le ŋkuwò me, hafi nègado nusi ava gbaɖegbe la ŋugbe ɖe wò dɔla ƒe aƒe la ŋua? Esia nye nusi nèɖo ɖe amegbetɔvi ŋua, Aƒetɔ Yehowa!

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Eye nukata Dawid aganɔ nu ƒom kpli wò, elabena ènya wò dɔla, Aƒetɔ Yehowa!

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: Le wò nya kple wò tamesusu ta nèwɔ nu gã siawo katã, bena nana wò dɔla nanyae.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Eyata ètri akɔ, Yehowa Mawu, elabena amea ɖeke mede nuwò o, eye mawu bubua ɖeke mexe ɖe ŋuwò o, abe alesi míesee kple to pɛpɛpɛ ene.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Dukɔ ka le anyigba dzi de wò dukɔ Israel nu, anyigba dzi dukɔ, si ɖeɖe ko mawua ɖe va ɖe, be wòatsɔ awɔ eƒe dukɔ, ne wòaɖe ŋkɔ eɖokui ŋu, eye wòawɔ nu gã kple ŋɔdzinuwo, be wòanya dukɔwo kple woƒe mawuwo le wò dukɔ, si nèɖe tso Egipte na ɖokuiwò la ŋgɔa?

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Eye nèɖo wò dukɔ Israel tè dzi, be wòanye wò dukɔ tegbee, eye wò Yehowa nèzu eƒe Mawu.

english_verse: And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants.
translation_verse: Eyata, Yehowa Mawu, nɔ nya, si nègblɔ ɖe wò dɔla kple eƒe aƒe ŋu la dzi tegbee, eye nawɔ, abe alesi nègblɔ ene!

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: Ekema wò ŋkɔ ade du tegbee, eye woagblɔ be: Yehowa Zebaot enye Mawu ɖe Israel nu, eye wò dɔla Dawid ƒe aƒe nali ke le ŋkuwò me!

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ Yehowa, wòe nye Mawu, eye wò nyawo nye nyateƒe, eye nègblɔ nya nyui sia na wò dɔla.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: Eyata lɔ̃ nayra wò dɔla ƒe aƒe la, ne wòano ŋkuwò me tegbee; elabena wò Aƒetɔ Yehowae gblɔe, eye wò yayra ana yayra nanɔ wò dɔla ƒe aƒe dzi tegbee.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Benaya, Yehoyada vi, le Kretitɔwo kple Pletitɔwo nu, eye Dawid viŋutsuwo nye aɖaŋuɖolawo.

english_verse: David fought the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed
translation_verse: Eye Dawid ƒe ŋkɔ nyɔ. Esi wògbɔ tso Aramtɔwo siƒe la, ewu Edomtɔ akpe wuienyi le dzeʋe la mea.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: Emegbe wòsi Moabitɔwo, eye wòna womlɔ anyigba, eye wòdzidze wo kple ka; edzidze ka eve be, woawu, eye wòdzidze ka ɖeka be, woanɔ agbe. Ale Moabitɔwo zu Dawid ƒe dɔlawo, siwo dzɔ nu nɛ.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid si Zoba-fia Hadadezer, Rexob vi, esi wòva be, yeaɖo yeƒe fiaɖuƒe anyi ɖe Frat-tɔsisi la nu.

english_verse: When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
translation_verse: Eye esi Aramtɔwo tso Damasko, be woava xɔ na Zoba-fia Hadadezer la, Dawid wu ame akpe blave vɔ eve le Aramtɔwo dome.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid ɖe amewo ɖo Aramtɔwo ƒe Damasko, eye Aramtɔwo zu Dawid ƒe dolawo, siwo dza nu nɛ. Eye Yehowa kpe ɖe Dawid ŋu le afisiafi, si wòyi.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid xɔ sikakpoxɔnu, siwo le Hadadezer ŋu mewo si la, hetsɔ va Yerusalem.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: Eye fia Dawid xɔ akɔbli geɖe fũ le Beta kple Berotai, siwo nye Hadadezer ƒe duwo me.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: Toi do via Yoram ɖe fia Dawid, ne wòado gbe nɛ, woadi dzɔgbenyuie ne, eye wõayrae le esi wòwɔ aʋa kple Hadadezer, eye wòsii la ta, elabena Toi kple Hadadezer wole kè me; eye wòhe klosalonuwo, sikanuwo kple akɔblinuwo ɖe asi vɛ.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: Eye fia Dawid ka woawo hã ŋu na Yehowa hekpe ɖe klosalo kple sika, siwo wòxɔ le dukɔ, siwo katã dzi woɖu la si, eye wòkɔ wo ŋu la ŋuti.

english_verse: Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, Amalek, and from King Hadadezer of Zobah.
translation_verse: Exɔ wo le Aramtɔwo, Moabitɔwo, Amon-viwo, Filistitɔwo kple Amalekitɔwo si hekpe ɖe nusiwo woha le Zoba-fia Hadadezer, Rexob vi si la ŋuti.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: Zadok, Axitub vi, kple Aximelex, Abyatar vi, wonye nunɔlawo, eye Seraya nye agbalẽŋlɔla;

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Yoab, Zeruya vi, le aʋakɔ la nu, eye Yosafat, Axilud vi, nye fia ƒe tsiami;

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid bia bena: Ɖe amea ɖeke mekpɔtɔ ɖe Saul ƒe me, ne mave enu le Yonatan ta oa?

english_verse: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
translation_verse: Dɔlaa ɖe le Saul ƒe me, si ŋkɔ nye Ziba; eye woyɔe va Dawid gbã, eye fia la gblɔ ne bena: Wòe nye Ziba? Eɖo ŋu bena: Wò dɔlae.

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Fia la bia bena: Ɖe amea ɖeke megale Saul ƒe me, ne mave enu abe Mawu ene oa? Ziba ɖo ŋu na fia la bena: Yonatan viŋutsu ɖeka li, amesi ƒe ata tu.

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ nɛ bena: Afika wòle? Ziba ɖo ŋu na fia la bena: Kpɔ ɖa, ele Amiel vi Maxir ƒe me le Lo-Debar.

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Eye esi Saul vi Yonatan ƒe vi Mefiboset va Dawid gbɔ la, etsyɔ mo anyi, eye wobɔbɔ. Tete Dawid gblɔ bena: Mefiboset! Etɔ bena: Wò dɔla enye si.

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ nɛ bena: Megavɔ̃ o, elabena mave nuwò le fofowò Yonatan ta: magagbugbɔ fofowò Saul ƒe agblewo katã na wò, eye naɖu nu le nye agba nu ɖaa.

english_verse: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
translation_verse: Ke eya de ta agu gblɔ bena: Ameka nye wò dɔla, be nètrɔ ɖokuiwò ɖe nye, amesi nye avũ kuku la ŋu?

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Tete fia la ya Saul ƒe ɖekakpui Ziba gblɔ nɛ bena: Metsɔ nusiwo katã nye Saul kple eƒe aƒe blibo la to la, de asi na wò aƒetɔ ƒe vi.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_verse: Esi fia, siwo katã nye Hadadezer teviwo, kpɔ bena, Israel-viwo si wo la, wowɔ ŋutifafa kple Israel, eye wosubɔ wo, eye Aramtɔwo de asi vovɔ̃ me azɔ na kpekpe ɖe Amon-viwo ŋu.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid gblɔ bena: Mave Naxas vi Xanun nu, abe alesi fofoa ve nunye ene. Eye Dawid do eƒe dɔlawo, be woaɖafa akɔ ne le fofoa ta. Ke esi Dawid ƒe dɔlawo va Amon-viwo ƒe anyigba dzi la,

english_verse: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
translation_verse: Amon-viwo ƒe amegãwo gblɔ na woƒe aƒetɔ Xanun bena: Ɖe Dawid dɔ akɔfalawo ɖa, be woaɖe bubu fofowò ŋu na wò loo? Alo menye ɖe Dawid da eƒe dolawo ɖe gbɔwò, be woadzro dua me, eye woatsa ŋku le eme ahagblẽe oa?

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Tete Xanun lé Dawid ƒe dɔlawo, eye wona wolũ gè afãafã na wo, eye wòlã woƒe awu ɖe domedomee ɖe agɔnu, emegbe wòdo mɔ wo.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Esi wova gblɔe na Dawid la, edo ame woyi ɖakpe wo, elabena wodo ŋukpe ŋutsuawo ŋuta; eye fia la na wogblɔ na wo bena: Musi Yerixo, vaseɖe esime miaƒe gè nato, hafi miagbɔ!

english_verse: The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah,
translation_verse: Ke esi Amon-viwo kpo be, yewozu Dawid ƒe ketɔwo la, Amon-viwo dɔ woɖatsɔ aʋa Aramtɔwo le Bet-Rexob kple Aramtɔwo le Zoba, wole afɔzɔla akpe blave, kple Maaxa-fia ame akpe ɖeka kpakple Istobtɔwo ame akpe wuieve.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Lé dzi de ƒo, eye na míasẽ ŋu na míaƒe dukɔ kple mía Mawu ƒe du la; eye Yehowa awɔ nusi dze eŋu!

english_verse: David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
translation_verse: Esi Dawid see la, edɔ Yoab kple kalẽtɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ blibo la ɖo ɖa.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
translation_verse: Tete Amon-viwo ho va dze aʋa ɖe agbo la nu, eve Aramtɔwo tso Zoba kple Rexob kple Istobtɔwo kple Maaxatɔwo le aʋagbe dzi la wo tɔ wo tɔe.

english_verse: Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans.
translation_verse: Esi Yoab kpɔ be, wodze aʋa ɖe ye ŋu le ŋgɔ kple megbe la, eɖe amewo le Israel ƒe ame tiatiawo katã me, eye wòdze aʋa ɖe Aramtɔwo ŋu.

english_verse: He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Ke etsɔ aʋakɔ la ƒe kpɔtɔea de asi na nɔvia Abisai, ne wòadze aʋa de Amon-viwo ŋu.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Ne Aramtɔwo sesẽ wum la, ekema nava xɔ nam; eye ne Amon-viwo sesẽ wu wò la, ekema mava xɔ na wò.

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them.
translation_verse: Tete Yoab kple aʋakɔ, si le eŋu la, ho yi ɖatɔ Aramtɔwo, eye wòsi le wo nu.

english_verse: When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Eye esi Amon-viwo kpo be, Aramtɔwo si la, wòsi le Abisai nu yi dua me, eye Yoab trɔ le Amon-viwo yome heva Yerusalem.

english_verse: The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again.
translation_verse: Esi Aramtɔwo kpɔ bena, Israel-viwo si yewo la, woƒo wo ɖokui nu ƒu.

english_verse: Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
translation_verse: Eye Hadadezer do be, woana Aramtɔ, siwo le tɔsisi la fe go keme dzi, naho; eye wova Xelam, eye Hadadezer ƒe aʋafia Sobax le wo nu.

english_verse: David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them.
translation_verse: Esi wova gblɔe na Dawid la, eƒo Israel blibo la nu ƒu, eye wotso Yordan heva Xelam. Eye Aramtɔwo dze aʋa ɖe Dawid ŋu hewɔ aʋa kplii.

english_verse: It was now spring, the time when kings go to war. David sent out the whole Israelite army under the command of Joab and his officers. They destroyed the Ammonite army and surrounded the capital city of Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Esi ƒe trɔ, eye fiawo ƒe aʋahoɣi do edzi la, Dawid dɔ Yoab kple eƒe dɔlawo kpakple Israel blibo la, eye wotsrɔ̃ Amon-viwo heɖe to ɖe Raba; ke Dawid tsi Yerusalem.

english_verse: he may get angry and ask, “Why did you go so near the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall?
translation_verse: eye fia la do dɔmedzoe gblɔ na wò bena: Nukaŋuti miegogo dua, be miawo aʋa? Mienyae bena, woanɔ glia dzi ate mi oa?

english_verse: But later, when she found out that she was going to have a baby, she sent someone to David with this message: “I'm pregnant!”
translation_verse: Eye nyɔnu la fɔ fu, eye wòdo woyi ɖagblɔ na Dawid bena: Mefɔ fu.

english_verse: David sent a message to Joab: “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.” Joab sent Uriah
translation_verse: Tete Dawid do ame do de Yoab bena: Ɖo Uriya, Xititɔ la dem! Eye Yoab ɖo Uriya de Dawid.

english_verse: to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?”
translation_verse: Eye esi Uriya va egbo la, Dawid bia bena. Yoab doa, aʋakɔ la doa, aleke aʋa la le edzi yimi?

english_verse: Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house.
translation_verse: Dawid gagblɔ na Uriya bena: Yi aƒewò me, ne naklɔ afɔ! Tete Uriya do le fia ƒe me, eye fia ƒe nunana dze eyome.

english_verse: But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside the entrance to the royal palace, where the king's guards slept.
translation_verse: Ke Uriya tsi eƒe aƒetɔ ƒe dɔlawo katã gbɔ dɔ le fia ƒe agbo nu, eye meyi eƒe me o.

english_verse: Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
translation_verse: Eye wova gblɔ na Dawid bena: Uriya meyi eƒe me o. Tete Dawid gblɔ na Uriya bena: Alo menye mɔ dzi nètso gbɔ oa? Nukaŋuti meyi aƒewò me o?

english_verse: Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
translation_verse: Uriya ɖo ŋu na Dawid bena: Aɖaka la kple Israel kpakple Yuda wole agbadɔ me, nye aƒetɔ Yoab kple nye aƒetɔ ƒe dolawo ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe tagba, eye nyea mayi aƒenye me, aɖu nu, ano nu ahadɔ srɔ̃nye gbɔa? Meta wò amea kple wò agbe siaa, ne mawɔ nusia fi!

english_verse: Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.” Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day,
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ na Uriya bena: Tsi afisia egbea hã, etsɔ la mado mɔ wò! Eye Uriya tsi Yerusalem gbemagbe kple ŋu, si ke ɖe eyome hã.

english_verse: David invited him for dinner. Uriah ate with David, who gave him so much to drink that he got drunk. But Uriah still did not go home. He went out and slept on his mat near the palace guards.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid kpee wòva ɖu nu no nu le egbɔ, eye wòna ahae wòno mu. Le fiẽ la edo yi ɖamlɔ eƒe aba dzi le eƒe aƒetɔ ƒe dɔlawo gbɔ; ke meyi eƒe me o.

english_verse: Early the next morning, David wrote a letter and told Uriah to deliver it to Joab.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, Dawid ŋlɔ agbalẽ ɖe Uriya si ɖo ɖe Yoab.

english_verse: The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
translation_verse: Ale wòŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽa me enye si: Miɖe Uriya ɖo ŋgɔ, afisi aʋa la nu sẽ le, eye miɖe megbe le eŋu, ne wòatsi aʋa!

english_verse: Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, esi Yoab ɖe to ɖe dua la, eɖe Uriya ɖo afisi wonyã be, enye kalẽtɔwo ƒe akpa dzi.

english_verse: When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
translation_verse: Tete duametɔwo do va wɔ aʋa kple Yoab, eye amewo tsi le aʋakɔ, si nye Dawid ƒe dɔlawo la dome, eye Uriya, Xititɔ la, hã ku.

english_verse: Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war.
translation_verse: Enumake Yoab do ame be, woaɖagblɔ aʋanyawo katã na Dawid.

english_verse: He gave the messenger these orders: When you finish telling the king everything that has happened,
translation_verse: Eye Yoab de se na dɔla la bena: Ne ègblɔ aʋanyawo katã na fia la vɔ,

english_verse: Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?” Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Ameka wu Abimelex, Yerubeset vi la? Ɖe menye nyɔnua ɖee le gli dzi xlã tevi ɖee woku le Tebez oa? Nukaŋuti miegogo glia hã la, ekema gblɔ be: Wò dɔla Uriya, Xititɔ la, hã ku.

english_verse: The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him.
translation_verse: Eye dɔla la yi ɖagblɔ nya, siwo katã gbe Yoab dɔe ɖo la, na Dawid.

english_verse: He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate.
translation_verse: Dɔla la ɖo ŋu na Dawid bena: Ŋutsuawo sesẽ wu mí, eye esi woɖo ɖe mia ŋu va tagba la, mieno te ɖe wo nu vaseɖe agboa nu ke.

english_verse: Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Tete aŋutrɔdalawo le gli dzi tewò dɔlawo, eye fia ƒe dɔlawo dometɔa ɖewo ku, eye wò dɔla Uriya, Xititɔ la, hã ku.

english_verse: David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ na dɔla la bena: Ale nagblɔ na Yoab enye si: Megana nusia nave wò o, elabena yi ɖua nu le afi kple afi! Do dzi wo aʋa kple dua, eye nagbãe! Ale naɖe dzi ƒo nɛ enye si!

english_verse: When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
translation_verse: Esi Uriya srɔ̃ se bena, srɔ̃a Uriya ku la, efa na srɔ̃a.

english_verse: Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son. The Lord's Message for David The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
translation_verse: Eye esi wòwɔ aho vɔ la, Dawid dɔ woɖakplɔe va eƒe me wòzu srɔ̃a, eye wòdzi ŋutsuvi nɛ. Ke nusi Dawid wo la, medze Yehowa ŋu o.

english_verse: The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle,
translation_verse: Alẽ kple nyiwo le kesinɔtɔ la si fũ.

english_verse: One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
translation_verse: Ke esi mɔzɔlaa ɖe va dze kesinɔtɔa la, eƒe alẽwo kple nyiwo dometɔ ɖeka lelé ɖa na amedzro, si va dze egbɔ la vee, eye wòlé ame dahe la ƒe alẽvia heɖa na ŋutsu, si va dzee.

english_verse: David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die!
translation_verse: Tete dzi ku Dawid vevie ɖe ŋutsu la ŋu, eye wògblɔ na Natan hena: Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe, ŋutsu, si wo nusia la, dze ku;

english_verse: And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
translation_verse: eye wòaɖo alẽvi la teƒe zi ene, le esi wòwɔ nusia, eye ame ƒe nu mevee o ta.

english_verse: Then Nathan told David: You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul
translation_verse: Tete Natan gblɔ na Dawid bena: Wòe nye ŋutsu la! Ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Mesi ami na wò heɖo fia wò ɖe Israel nu, eye meɖe wò tso Saul si me;

english_verse: and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.
translation_verse: mede wò aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe asi na wò, eye metsɔ wò aƒetɔ srɔ̃wo ɖo wò akɔ nu; metso Israel kple Yuda ƒe aƒe la na wò, eye ne esia mesɔ gbɔ o la, mate ŋu atsɔ nu bubu akpee na wò le mɔ vovovowo dzi hafi.

english_verse: Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti nèdo vlo Yehowa ƒe gbe hewɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi sia le eƒe ŋku me? Ewu Uriya, Xititɔ la, kple yi, eye nèxɔ srɔ̃a ɖe; ke ètsɔ Amon-viwo ƒe yi wu eya ŋu tɔe.

english_verse: “Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace.
translation_verse: Eyata yi madzo le aƒewò me gbeɖe o, le esi nèɖo vlom, eye nèxɔ Uriya Xititɔ la srɔ̃ ɖe ta.

english_verse: Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, mana dzɔgbevɔ̃e natso aƒewò me ava dziwò, eye maxɔ srɔ̃wòwo le ŋkuwò me atsɔ na xɔ̃wòvi, eye wòadɔ srɔ̃wòwo gbɔ le ŋdɔkutsu dzatsɛ.

english_verse: What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
translation_verse: Wòa èwɔe le bebe me, ke nye la mawɔ nusia le Israel blibo la ŋku me le ŋdɔ. Dawid nu eƒe nuvɔ̃ me, eye wotsɔe kee. Salomo dzidzi.

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Ke esi newɔ nusia, eye nena Yehowa ƒe futɔwo kpɔ fewuɖunu la, eyata ŋutsuvi, si wodzi na wò la, aku.

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Emegbe Natan yi aƒe me. Eye Yehowa ɖe fu na ɖevi, si Uriya srɔ̃ dzi na Dawid la, eye wòle ɖa lém vevie.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: Ke Dawid ƒo koko na Mawu le ɖevi la ta, eye Dawid tsi nu da, eye wòtsi anyigba da.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: Eye eƒe me amegãwo va egbɔ, be ye woa fɔe le anyigba; ke melɔ̃ o, eye meɖu nu kpli wo o.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke adreagbe la ɖevi la ku. Eye Dawid ƒe dɔlawo le vɔvɔ̃m be, woagblɔ nɛ be, ɖevi la ku; elabena wogblɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, esi ɖevi la gale agbe, eye míeƒo nu kplii la, egbe toɖoɖo míaƒe gbe; ɖe mawɔ nu vevia ɖe eɖokui, ne míegblɔ nɛ be, ɖevi la ku oa?

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: Esi Dawid kpɔ be, eƒe dɔlawo le dalĩ dom la, Dawid dze sii bena, ɖevi la ku. Eye Dawid bia eƒe dɔlawo bena: Ɖe ɖevi la kua? Woɖo ŋu bena: Eku.

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: Eƒe dolawo gblɔ nɛ bena: Nuka nye si newɔ? Esi ɖevi la gale agbe la, etsi nu do, eye nefa avi; ke esi ɖevia ku la, ètsi tre, eye nèɖu nua?

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Esi ɖevi la le agbe la, metsi nu dɔ, eye mefa avi; elabena mebu be, ɖewohĩ Yehowa ave nunye, be ɖevi la natsi agbe.

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: Ke azɔ esi wòku la, nukata matsi nu adɔa? Ɖe mate ŋu agagbugbɔe agbɔea? Nye koe ayi egbɔ, ke eya magatrɔ ava gbɔnye o.

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: Eye Dawid fa aka na srɔ̃a Bat-Seba; eye wòyi ɖadɔ egbɔ, eye wòdzi ŋutsuvi, si wòna ŋkɔe be Salomo; eye Yehowa lɔ̃ eƒe nya.

english_verse: and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.” The End of the War with Ammon (
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔe ɖe asi na nyagblɔɖila Natan, amesi na ŋkɔe le Yehowa ta be Yedidya. Raba-du xɔxɔ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress
translation_verse: Eye Yoab wo aʋa kple Amon-viwo ƒe Raba, eye wòxɔ fiadu la.

english_verse: and sent a messenger to tell David: I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply.
translation_verse: Tete Yoab da amewo ɖo ɖe Dawid gblɔ bena: Mewɔ aʋa kple Raba, eye mexɔ tɔ ŋu du la hã.

english_verse: Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
translation_verse: Eyata ƒo aʋakɔ, si kpɔtɔ la, nu ƒu, eye naɖe to ɖe dua axɔe, ne nyea magaxɔe, eye woayɔ nye ŋkɔ ɖe eŋu o!

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: Tete Dawid ƒo aʋakɔ blibo la nu ƒu yi Raba, eye wòwɔ aʋa kplii hexɔe.

english_verse: and took the crown from the statue of their god Milcom. The crown was made of about
translation_verse: Eye wòɖe fiakuku la le woƒe fia ta; eƒe kpekpeme le sika talento ɖeka, eye kpe xɔasi le eŋu, eye Dawid tsɔe ɖɔ. Aboyonu, siwo wotsɔ tso dua me gbɔe la, sɔ gbɔ ŋutɔ.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: Eye wòkplɔ dukɔ, si le eme la, ɖaɖo laxalaxadɔwo kple tasiaɖam, siwo wotsɔna ƒoa lui ƒe dowo, fíadɔwo kple kpememedɔwo nu. Alea wòwɔ Amon-viwo ƒe duwo katã me tɔwoe. Eye Dawid kple aʋakɔ blibo la gbugbɔ va Yerusalem.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: Esia megbe la Dawid vi Absalom nɔvinyɔnu Tamar, si dze tugbe la, ƒe nu lé dzi na Dawid vi Amnon.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Eye wòve Amnon, vaseɖe esime wòzu da dze edzi le nɔvianyɔnu Tamar ta, elabena ɖetugbi wònye, eye Amnon menya alesi gɔ̃ woawɔ awɔ nane kplii o.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Xɔlɔ̃a ɖe le Amnon si, eŋkɔ nye Yonadab, Dawid nɔvi Simea vi; eye Yonadab dze aɖaŋu ŋutɔ.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Fia vi, nukaŋuti nèle ku ɖim gbesiagbe ale? Màgblɔe nam oa? Tete Amnon gblɔ nɛ bena: Absalom nɔvinyɔnu Tamar ƒe nue lé dzi nam.

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Eye Yonadab gblɔ ne bena: Yi ɖamlɔ wò aba dzi, eye nalé kpɔ̃dɔ; eye ne fofowò va kpɔ wò ge ɖa la, ekema gblɔ ne bena: Na nɔvinye Tamar nava na nuɖuɖum! Ne eva ɖa nua le ŋkunye me mekpɔ la, ekema maɖu nua le esi me.

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Eye Amnon mlɔ anyi le kpɔ̃dɔ lém, eye esi fia la va ekpɔ ge ɖa la, Amnon gblɔ na fia la bena: Na nɔvinyenyɔnu Tamar nava to tatali eve te ŋkunye me, ne wòalé ɖe asi maɖu!

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: Tete Dawid ɖo ame ɖe Tamar ƒe me be, woagblɔ nɛ be: Yi nɔviwò Amnon ƒe me, eye naɖa nu ne!

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Eye Tamar yi nɔvia Amnon ƒe me, esime wòmia anyi. Eye wòka amɔwɔ, blui, eye wòmlii heta tataliawo le eŋku me.

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: Eye wòtree le nutɔgba me le eŋku me: ke egbe be, yemaɖu nua o. Eye Amnon gblɔ bena: Na amesiame nado le gbɔnye! Tete amesiame do le egbɔ.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Azɔ Amnon gblɔ na Tamar bena: Tsɔ nuɖuɖua va xogã me, ne nalée ɖe asi maɖu! Eye Tamar tsɔ tatali, si wòtɔ la, yi na nɔvia Amnon le xɔgã me.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Esi wòtsɔe nɛ, be woaɖu la, elée gblɔ nɛ bena: Nɔvinyenyɔnu, va mlɔ gbɔnye!

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Ke eɖo ŋu bena: Kpao, nɔvinye! Megagblẽm o, elabena womewɔna alea le Israel o! Megawɔ ŋukpenanu sia o!

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Ke nye ɖe, afika mayi kple nye ŋukpe la? Eye wòabu wò ɖe ŋukpenanuwɔlawo dome le Israel. Ƒo nu kple fia la, elabena matem wò o!

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Ke azɔ Amnon lé fui vevie ŋuta, ele fui wu alesi wòlɔ̃e tsã gɔ̃ hã. Eye Amnon gblɔ ne bena: Tsi tre, nadzo!

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu ne bena: Megawɔe o, elabena esi nèle nyãyem la, eya vɔ̃ɖi ɖe dzi wu nusi ne wo ɖe ŋunye gbã! Ke egbe toɖoɖoe.

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: Eye wòyɔ ɖekakpui, si le esubɔm la ɖa, gblɔ bena: Mihe amesia do goe le gbɔnye do ɖe mɔ dzi, eye mido nɔa ɖe emegbe!

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Edo awu ʋlayaa ɖe; elabena alea fia vinyɔnu, siwo nye ɖetugbiwo la, doa awui tso blema ke. Eye eƒe dɔla hee do goe do ɖe ma dzi hedo oa ɖe emegbe.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Eye Tamar ku afi kɔ ɖe ta me, eye wòdze awu ʋlaya, si wòdo la, eye wòkpla asi ta le boboe dom le yiyim.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Tete nɔvia Absalom gblɔ nɛ bena: Ɖe nɔviwò Amnon va gbɔwòa? Nɔvinye, zi ɖoɖoe; elabena nɔviwòe! Megana nya sia natɔ dzi na wò o! Eye Tamar nɔ aga le nɔvia Absalom ƒe me.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Ke Absalom megblɔ nya vɔ̃ alo nyuia ɖeke na Amnon o; elabena Absalom lé fu Amnon, le esi wogblẽ nɔvianyɔnu Tamar ta.

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me le ƒe eve megbe, esime Absalom le fu kom na alẽwo le Baal-Xazor, si le Efrayim gbɔ la, Absalom kpe fia viŋutsuwo katã.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Eye Absalom va fia la gbɔ gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, wò ɖɔla le fu kom na alẽwo, taflatse, fia la kple eƒe dɔlawo neyi kple eƒe dɔla!

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ na Absalom bena: Gbeɖe, vinye! Megana mí katã míayi o, ne míaganye agba na wò o! Eye wòƒoe ɖe enu; ke egbe be, yemayi o, eye wòyrae.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Eye Absalom gblɔ bena: Ne mèlɔ̃ o la, ekema na nɔvinye Amnon nayi kpli mi dzro! Fia la ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Nukata wòayi kpli wòa?

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Ke Absalom ƒoe ɖe enu, eye wòdɔ Amnon kple fia viŋutsuawo katã kpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Eye Absalom de se na eƒe ɖekakpuiwo bena: Miɖo ŋku anyi; ne wein na Amnon le dzidzɔ kpɔm, eye megblɔ na mi be: miwu Amnon la, ekema miwui, eye migavɔ̃ o; esi wònye nyee de se na mi ɖe! Milé dzi ɖe ƒo, eye miwɔ ŋutsu!

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Eye Absalom ƒe ɖekakpuiawo wɔ Amnon, abe alesi Absalom de se ene. Tete fia viŋutsuawo katã tsi tre, eye wo dome amesiame do eƒe tedzi hesi.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Esi wole mɔ dzi la, nya la ɖi Dawid se be: Absalom wu fia viŋutsuawo katã, eye wo dometɔ ɖeka hɔ̃ hã mekpɔtɔ o!

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Tete fia la tsi tre dze eƒe awuwo, eye wòmia anyigba, eye eƒe dɔlawo katã le tsitre le awu vuvuwo me.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Ke Yonadab, Dawid nɔvi, Simea ƒe vi, xɔ dzi gblɔ bena: Nye aƒetɔ megabu be, wowu ɖekakpuiviawo katã, siwo nye fia viwo la o, ke boŋ Amnon ɖeɖe koe ku; elabena Absalom ƒe nu me nya la tso, wòɖoe tso gbesigbe wògblẽ nɔvianyɔnu Tamar.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Eyata nye aƒetɔ fia megana nya sia naɖu dzi nɛ be, fiaviŋutsuawo katãe ku o, ke boŋ Amnon ɖeɖe koe ku. Absalom ƒe sisi.

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Ke Absalom si. Eye ɖekakpui, si nye dzɔla la, fi ka dzi, eye wòkpɔ bena, ameha gãa ɖe le mɔ dzi to emegbe tso to la ƒe axa dzi gbɔna.

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Tete Yonadab gblɔ na fia la bena: Kpɔ ɖa, fia viŋutsuawo gbɔna; alesi wò dɔla gblɔ la, nenema wòle.

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: Esi wòɖe nu le nyaa me la, tete fia viŋutsuawo do, eye wofa avi kple ɣli, eye fia la kple eƒe dɔlawo katã hã gba avi doo.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Ke ele fia Dawid dzrom vevie be, yeatsɔe ake Absalom; elabena eƒe akɔ fa le Amnon, si ku la ta.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Eye Zeruya vi Yoab dze sii bena, fia la ƒe dzi ku ɖe Absalom ŋu.

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Eye Tekoa-nyɔnu la va fia la gbɔ, eye wòbɔbɔ hede ta agu gblɔ bena: Fia, xɔ nam!

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ ne bena: Nya ka dzo ɖe dziwò? Eɖo ŋu bena: Ahosi menye, eye srɔ̃nye ku.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: Ŋutsuvi eve le wò dɔlanyɔnu si, eye woa kple eve wole dzre wɔm le gbe me; ke amea ɖeke meli alé avu wo o, eye ɖeka ƒo nɔvia woku.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Azɔ kpɔ ɖa, ƒome blibo la tso ɖe wò dɔlanyɔnu ŋu gblɔ bena: Ɖe amesi wu nɔvia la de asi, ne míawu ɖe nɔvia, si wòwu la, ƒe agbe teƒe, eye míatsrɔ̃ domeɖula hã ɖa! Eye wole didim be, yewoatsi nye dzoka, si kpɔtɔ ɖi la, ne ŋkɔ kple dzidzimevia ɖeke maganɔ srɔ̃nye si le anyigba dzi o.

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ na nyɔnu la bena: Yi aƒewò me, eye made se le tawo!

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Eye Tekoa-nyɔnu la gblɔ na fia la bena: Nye aƒetɔ fia, mía kple fofonye ƒe aƒe dzi vodada la le, ke fia kple eƒe fiazikpui meɖi faa ɖeke o.

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ bena: Ne amea ɖe ƒo nu ɖe gbɔwò la, ekema kplɔe vɛ nam, eye magaka asi ŋuwò azɔ o!

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Nyɔnu la gblɔ be: Taflatse, fia la neɖo ŋku Yehowa, eƒe Mawu dzi, ne hlɔ̃biala magagblẽ nu ɖe dzi, eye wòatsrɔ̃ vinyeŋutsu ɖa o! Tete wògblɔ be: Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe: Ne viwò ƒe ɖa ɖeka age ɖe anyigba fi!

english_verse: Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?” “Yes,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ke nyɔnu la gblɔ bena: Taflatse, na wò dɔlanyɔnu nagblɔ nya ɖeka na aƒetɔ, nye fia. Eɖo ŋu bena: Ƒo nu!

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Nyɔnu la gblɔ bena: Nukaŋuti nèle esia bum ɖe Mawu ƒe dukɔ la ŋu? Esi fia la gblɔ nya sia, gake fia la mena wokplɔ eƒe amesi wonyã la gbɔe o la, eyata ele abe ame ɖifɔ ene.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Elabena ele be, míaku, eye míele abe tsi, si wokɔ ɖe anyigba, eye womagate ŋu aklui o ene; eye Mawu medea amea ɖeke ɖa o, ke boŋ ebua eme kpɔna be, ne maganyã amesi wonyã la ɖa le eɖokui gbɔ o.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Esi dukɔ la le ŋɔdzi dom nam la, eyata meva nye aƒetɔ fia la gbɔ fifia, be magblɔ nya sia; elabena wò dɔlanyɔnu bu be: Maƒo nu kple fia la kpɔ, ɖewohĩ awɔ eƒe dɔlanyɔnu ƒe nya la dzi.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Elabena fiã la aɖo to eƒe dɔlanyɔnu, eye wòaɖem tso ŋutsu, si be, yeatsrɔ̃ mía kple vinye ɖa le Mawu ƒe domenyinu nu la si me.

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: Eye wò dɔlanyɔnu bu be: Nye aƒetɔ fia la ƒe nya ana ɖoɖoe nazi: elabena nye aƒetɔ fia la le abe Mawu ƒe dɔla ene, amesi wòase nyuia kple vɔ̃a; eye Yehowa, wò Mawu, anɔ kpli wò.

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Tete fia la xɔ dzi gblɔ na nyɔnu la bena: Megaɣla nya, si mabia wò la, ɖem o! Nyɔnu la ɖo ŋu be: Nye aƒetɔ fia neƒo nu ko!

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Eye fia la gblɔ bena: Menye Yoab ƒe asie li kpli wò le nya siawo katã me oa? Nyɔnu la ɖo ŋu gblɔ bena: Meta wò agbe, nye aƒetɔ fia, womate ŋu adze ɖe ɖusi alo mia me le nya, siwo katã nye aƒetɔ fia gblɔ la me o; elabena wò dɔla Yoab ye dɔm, eye wòde nya siawo katã wò dɔlanyɔnu la nu.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: Wò dɔla Yoab wɔ nusia, ne wòatsɔ ablu nya la ƒe afɔ; ke nye aƒetɔ ƒe nunya le abe mawudɔla ƒe nunya ene, ne wòanya nusianu, si dzɔna le anyigba dzi.

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Emegbe fia la gblɔ na Yoab bena; Kpɔ ɖa, mawɔ nusia; eyata yi ɖakplɔ ɖekakpui Absalom la gbɔe!

english_verse: Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
translation_verse: Tete Yoab bɔbɔ heɖe ta agu, eye wòyra fia la. Eye Yoab gblɔ bena: Nye aƒetɔ fia, egbe wò dɔla dze sii bene, ève wò dɔla nu, esi fia ta wɔ eƒe dɔla ƒe nya dzi ta.

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Tete Yoab dze mɔ yi Gesur, eye wòkplɔ Absalom va Yerusalem.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Eye fia la gblɔ be: Netrɔ yi eƒe me, eye megava kpɔ nye ŋku me o! Tete Absalom trɔ yi eƒe me, eye mekpɔ fia la ŋku me o.

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: Eye ne eko eƒe taɖa la, eƒe ɖa ɖaa sekel alafa eve le fia ƒe nudanu dzi. Ne ƒe sia ƒe trɔ la, ekoa ta; elabena ekpe ne akpa, eyata wòkonɛ.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Wodzi ŋutsuvi etɔ̃ kple nyɔnuvi ɖeka, si ŋkɔ nye Tamar, eye wòdze tugbe la, na Absalom.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Esi Absalom nɔ Yerusalem ƒe eve, eye mekpɔ fia la ŋku me kpɔ o la,

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Absalom dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Yoab be, yeaɖoe ɖe fia la gbɔ; ke egbe be, yemayi egbɔ o. Egadɔ ame ɖee zi evelia, ke egbe vava.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo bena: Mikpɔ ɖa, Yoab ƒe agble le axanye, eye lu le afima ne; miyi, ne miatɔ dzoe! Eye Absalom ƒe dɔlawo yi ɖatɔ dzo agble la.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Eye Yoab tso yi Absalom gbɔ le aƒea me gblɔ ne bena: Nukaŋuti wò dɔlawo tɔ dzo agble, si nye tanye?

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Absalom ɖo ŋu na Yoab bena: Kpɔ ɖa, medo ame ɖe wò be: va, ne made gbe asi na wò aɖo ɖe fia la bena: Nukaŋuti metso Gesur va? Ɖe metsi afima la, ne nyo nam wu! Azɔ meɖi be, makpɔ fia la ŋku me; eye ne vodadaa ɖe le ŋunye la, ekema newum!

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Tete Yoab yi fia la gbɔ ɖagblɔe ne; eye wòyɔ Absalom. Esi wòva fia la gbɔ la, ede ta agu ɖe fia la ŋku me, eye fia la gbugbɔ nu na Absalom.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: Esia megbe la Absalom di tasiaɖam kple sɔwo na eɖokui hekpe ɖe ŋutsu blaatɔ̃, siwo anɔ du ƒum le eŋgɔ la ŋu.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Eye Absalom fɔna ŋdi kanya ɖatsia tre ɖe agbo la ƒe mɔ to; eye wòva me, ne amesiame tsɔ dzrenyaa ɖe yina ɖe fia gbɔ, be woadrɔ̃ la, Absalom yɔne hebianɛ be: Du ka me nètso? Ne ame la ɖo ŋu be: Wò dɔla tso Israel-toawo dometɔ ɖeka me la,

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: Absalom gblɔna nɛ bena: Wò nya le eme, eye wodzo, ke fiahawo dometɔa ɖeke mele to do ge wò o.

english_verse: I wish someone would make me the judge around here! I would be fair to everyone.”
translation_verse: Eye Absalom gblɔ bena: Ɖe wònye amea ɖee atsɔm aɖo ʋɔnudrɔ̃la ɖe anyigba la dzi, eye amesiame ahe dzrenya kple ʋɔnudrɔ̃nya ava gbɔnyee la, ne matso afia ne!

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, ne amea ɖe te ɖe eŋu be, yeabɔbɔ ne la, edoa eƒe asi ɖa lénɛ, eye wògbugbɔa nu nɛ.
