english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Alea Absalom wɔ na Israel blibo, si va ʋɔnu drɔ̃ ge le fia la gbɔ, eye Absalom fi Israel-ŋutsuwo ƒe dzi.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Le ƒe ene megbe la Absalom gblɔ na fia la bena: Taflatse, na mayi adawɔ nye adzɔgbe, si meɖe na Yehowa la dzi le Xebron.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Elabena esi menɔ Gesur le Aram la, wò dɔla ɖe adzɔgbe bena: Ne Yehowa gakplɔm yi Yerusalem la, ekema miasubɔ Yehowa.

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Fia gblɔ nɛ bena: Yi le ŋutifafa me! Tete wòdze mɔ heyi Xebron.

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Eye amea de va toe na Dawid gblɔ bena: Israel-ŋutsuwo ƒe dzi trɔ ɖe Absalom ŋu.

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Tete Dawid gblɔ na eƒe dɔla, siwo katã le eŋu le Yerusalem la bebena: Mitso, ne miasi; elabena mía dometɔa ɖeke makpɔtɔ le Absalom ŋku me o! Netsɔ, mídzo, ne eƒe afɔ nagatsɔ wòabi mi, eye wòahe dzogbevɔ̃e ava mia dzi, eye woatsrɔ̃ du la kple yi o!

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: Eƒe dɔlawo katã le exa le yiyim, eye Kretitɔwo kple Pletitɔwo katã kpakple Gatitɔ alafa ade, siwo katã dze eyome tso Gat la, zɔ fia la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Eye fia la gblɔ na Gatitɔ Itai bena: Nukaŋuti wò hã nèbe, yeayi kpli mí? Trɔ, yi ɖanɔ fia la gbɔ; elabena du bubu me tɔ nènye, eyata gbugbɔ yi nɔwòƒe!

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Etsɔ nèva, eye egbe ko mana nana tsaglalã tsam kpli mia? Nye la meyina, afisi menya kpɔ ko; mia kple nɔviwòwo migbubɔ, eye amenuveve kple nyateƒe anɔ kpli wò!

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Ke Itai ɖo ŋu na fia la gblɔ bena: Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe kple nye aƒetɔ fia ƒe agbe: Afisi nye aƒetɔ fia ano la, afima eƒe dɔla anɔ, eɖanye ku me alo agbe me o!

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ na Itai bena: Yi kpli mí! Ale Gatitɔ Itai kple eƒe amewo katã kpakple ɖevi, siwo katã le eŋu la, yi kplii.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Eye anyigba blibo la fa avi hoo, esi ameha blibo la tso me yi. Esi fia la tso Kidron-tɔʋua la, ameha blibo la dze ŋgɔ to mo, si ɖo ta gbedzi.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Eye kpɔ ɖa, Zadok hã kple Lewito, siwo katã le eŋu la, tsɔ Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la, eye wodro Mawu ƒe aɖaka la ɖi, vaseɖe esime ameha blibo la tso dua me va to eŋu yi vɔ; eye Abyatar hã yi

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Ke fia la gblɔ na Zadok bena: Gbugbɔ Mawu ƒe aɖaka la yi dua mee! Ne Yehowa ve nunye la, ekema akplɔm agbɔe, eye wòana makpɔe kple afisi wòle

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Gake ne egblɔ be, nye nu menyo ye ŋu o la, nyee nye esi, newɔm, alesi dze eŋu!

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Eye fia la gblɔ na nunɔla Zadok bena: Wòe nye nukpɔla, gbugbɔ yi dua me le ŋutifafa me, eye mia viwo kple eve nakpe ɖe mia ŋu: viwò Aximaaz kple Yonatan, Abyatar vi.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Mikpɔ ɖa, manɔ totsoƒewo le gbedzi, vaseɖe esime gbea ɖe atso mia gbɔ ava nam.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Tete Zadok kple Abyatar wogbugbɔ Mawu ƒe aɖaka la va Yerusalem, eye wonɔ afima.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid lia amiti-togbɛ la, eye wòle avi fam le yiyim; etsyɔ nu ta, eye wòzɔ afɔ ƒuƒlu; ameha blibo, si le eŋu la, dometɔ ɖesiaɖe tsyo nu ta, eye wolia to la hele avi fam le yiyim.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Eye wova gblɔ na Dawid bena: Axitofel le nugbeɖolawo dome kpe ɖe Absalom ŋu! Tete Dawid gblɔ bena: Yehowa, meɖe kuku, na Axitofel ƒe adaŋudede nazu lãnya!

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Esi Dawid va ɖo toa ta me, afisi woɖoa gbe ɖa na Mawu le la, kpɔ ɖa, Xusai, Arkitɔ la, le awu vuvu me, eye ke le ta me nɛ wòva kpee.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ nɛ bena: Ne ayi azɔlia dzi kplim la, ekema ava zu agba nam;

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: ke ne ègbugbɔ yi dua me, eye negblɔ na Absalom be: Fia, medi be, mazu wò dɔla; fofowò ƒe dɔla menye tsã, ke azɔ mebe, mazu wò dɔla la, ekema àte ŋu agblẽ Axitofel ƒe adaŋudede me nɛ nam.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Nunɔla Zadok kple Abyatar hã le afima kpe ɖe ŋuwò; eyata ne èse nya sia nya le fia ƒe me ko la, nadagblɔe na nunɔla Zadok kple Abyatar.

english_verse: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, wo vi eveawo le wo gbɔ le afima: Aximaaz, Zadok ta, kple Yonatan, Abyatar ta; eye miɖe nya sia nya, si miese la, wo si ɖo ɖem!

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid xɔlɔ̃ Xusai va dua me, esime Absalom hã va Yerusalem.

english_verse: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
translation_verse: Esi Dawid to toa ta me yi ʋee la, kpo ɖa, Mefiboset ƒe dɔla Ziba va kpee, eye tedzi eve, siwo wòbia akpa na, eye wotsɔ abolo bɔbɔ alafa eve, weintsetse ƒuƒu bolo alafa ɖeka kple wein lãgbalẽgolo ɖeka do agba ɖe wo dzi la, kpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Fia la bia Ziba bena: Nuka nèbe, yeawɔ nu siawoe? Ziba ɖo ŋu be: Tedziawo nye fia la ƒe aƒea to, ne woaɖo; aboloawo kple kutsetse kpoawo nye ɖekakpuiawo tɔ, ne woaɖu; eye wein la nye amesiwo ŋu ɖeɖi te le gbedzi la to, ne woano.

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ be: Afika wò aƒetɔ ƒe vi la le? Ziba ɖo ŋu na fia la bena: Kpɔ ɖa, etsi Yerusalem, elabena egblɔ be: Azɔ la Israel ƒe aƒe la agagbugbɔ fofonye ƒe fiaɖuƒe la nam!

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ na Ziba bena: Kpɔ ɖa, Mefiboset ƒe nuwo katã nye tɔwò! Eye Ziba gblɔ be: Mede ta agu na wò! Ne nye aƒetɔ nya ve nunye ko! Simei do ɖiŋu na Dawid.

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Esi fia Dawid va Baxurim la, kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsua ɖe, si tso Saul ƒe aƒe ƒe ƒome la me, si ŋkɔ nye Simei, Gera vi la, do tso afima va le ɖiŋu dom.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Eye wòfɔ kpe le Dawid kple fia Dawid ƒe dɔlawo katã kple ameha blibo la kpakple kalẽtɔ, siwo katã le eƒe ɖusi kple mia me la dam.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Eye Simei le ɖiŋu dom le gbɔgblɔm be: Dzo, dzo, wò hlɔ̃me kple ame vɔ̃ɖi!

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: Yehowa gbugbɔ Saul, amesi teƒe nèzu fia ɖo la, ƒe aƒe ƒe ʋu katã va dziwò, eye Yehowa tsɔ fiaɖuƒe la de asi na viwò Absalom; kpɔ ɖa, azɔ ège ɖe dzɔgbevɔ̃e me, elabena hlɔme nènye!

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Zeruya vi Abisai gblɔ na fia la bena: Nukaŋuti avũ kuku sia anɔ ɖiŋu dom na nye aƒetɔ fia la? Na mayi aɖatso ta le enu!

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Ke fia la gblɔ be: Nya ka me mele kple mi Zeruya viwo? Nedo ɖiŋu faa! Elabena nenye Yehowae gblɔ nɛ be: do ɖiŋu na Dawid la! ameka kpɔ mɔ agblɔ be: nukaŋuti nèle wɔwɔm alea?

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ na Abisai kple eƒe dɔlawo katã bena: Kpɔ ɖa, vinye, si do tso nye ali me la, le nye ku dim; aleke wɔ Benyamintɔ mahadii oa? Mina, ne wòado ɖiŋu ko, elabena Yehowae gblɔe nɛ!

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Ɖewohĩ Yehowa akpɔ nye hiã la nam, eye Yehowa atsɔ nyui aɖo ɖiŋu, si wòɖo nam egbe la teƒe.

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid kple eƒe amewo lé mɔ, ke Simei zɔ to la xa le ekasa, eye wòle ɖiŋu dom le yiyim, eye wòtɔ kpe le edam hele ke hlẽm ɖe ya me.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Eye fia la kple ameha blibo, si le eŋu la, va Ayefim, eye wogbɔ ɖe me le afima.

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ke Absalom kple ameha blibo, si nye Israel-ŋutsuwo la, va Yerusalem, eye Axitofel kpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Esime Dawid xɔlɔ̃ Xusai, Arkitɔ la, va Absalom gbɔ la, Xusai gblɔ na Absalom bena: Fia nenɔ agbe! Fia nena agbe!

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Tete Absalom gblɔ na Xusai bena: Xɔ̃wò lae nye esia lɔ̃m nèlea? Nukaŋuti mèyi kple xɔwo la oa?

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Xusai ɖo ŋu na Absalom bena: Kpao, ke boŋ amesi Yehowa kple dukɔ sia kpakple Israel-ŋutsuwo katã da la, tɔ menye, eye eya gbɔ manɔ!

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: Eye evevea ke: Ameka masubɔ, ne menye via oa? Alesi mesubɔ fofowòe la, nenema manɔ wò hã gbɔwòe.

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Eye Absalom gblɔ na Axitofel bena: Miɖe adaŋu, nusi míawɔ!

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Axitofel gblɔ na Absalom bena: Yi fofowò ƒe ahiã, tsiwo wogblẽ ɖe megbe, be woakpɔ aƒea dzi la gbɔ; eye ne Israel blibo la se be, mia kple fofowò dome gblẽ la, ekema ŋusẽ aɖo alɔ me na amesiwo katã le ŋuwò!

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Eye wowɔ agbadɔ ɖe xɔta na Absalom, eye Absalom de asi fofoa ƒe ahiãwo ŋu le Israel blibo la ŋku me.

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Wobua Axitofel ƒe aɖaŋu, si wòɖona ɣemaɣi la, abe Mawue wòbia gbee ene: alea Axitofel ƒe aɖaŋuɖoɖo nɔ na Dawid kple Absalom siaa.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: Míado ɖe edzi le teƒeawo dome oa ɖe, afisi wòle, eye míaƒe ɖe edzi, abe alesi zãmu dzana ɖe anyigba dzi ene; eye eya ŋutɔ kple amesiwo katã le eŋu la, dometɔ ɖeka hɔ̃ hã makpɔtɔ o.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: eye mado ɖe edzi, esime ɖeɖi te eŋu, eye eƒe alɔwo gbɔdzɔ; eye mado voɖi nɛ, ale be ameha blibo, si le eŋu la nasi, eye mawu fia la ɖeɖe,

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: eye makplɔ ameha blibo la vɛ na wò! Ne wo katã gbugbɔ va, eye amesi dim nèle to le eme la, ekema dukɔ blibo la anɔ anyi le ŋutifafa me.

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Nya la dze Absalom kple Israel-ame tsitsiwo katã ŋu.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Tete Absalom gblɔ bena: Miɖayɔ Xusai, Arkitɔ la, hã ve, ne míase gbe, si le eya hã nu!

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Esi Xusai va Absalom gbɔ la, Absalom gblɔ nɛ bena: Ale Axitofel ƒo gbe lae enye si; ɖe míawɔ eƒe gbe dzi loo? Ne míawɔe o la, ekema ƒo nu!

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Xusai gblɔ na Absalom bena: Adaŋu, si Axitofel ɖe fifia la, menyo o.

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Eye Xusai gblɔ bena: Enya fofowò kple eƒe amewo be, kalẽtɔwo wonye, eye aɖa le mo na wo abe sisiblisi, si ŋu wole viwo la le gbedzi ene. Aʋame hãe fofowò nye, eye mana ameha la natsi adɔ o.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, eɣla ɖe doa wo dometɔa ɖe me alo ɖe teƒea wo dometɔa ɖe, eye ava me, ne amewo de asi aʋatsitsi me le gɔmedzedzea me la, ekema woasee agblɔ be: wosi aʋakɔ, si kplɔ Absalom ɖo:

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: eye dzi aɖe le kalẽtɔ kekeake, amesi ƒe dzi le abe dzata ƒe dzi ene la, hã ƒo; elabena Israel blibo la nyae be, fofowò nye kalẽtɔ, eye amesiwo katã le eŋu, nye ŋutsuwɔlawo.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Ke nye aɖaŋu enye si: Na Israel blibo la nakpe la ɖe ŋuwò tso Dan vaseɖe Beer-Seba, abe alesi ƒutake sɔ gbɔe ene, eye wò ŋutɔ naho kpli wo!

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: Eye ne ede megbe yi dua ɖe me la, ekema Israel blibo la nado ka atsɔ du ma ɖe eme, eye míahee aɖakɔ ɖe, abu me, vaseɖe esime kpekula ɖeke matsi afima o!

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Tete Absalom kple Israel-ŋutsuwo katã gblɔ bena: Xusai, Arkitɔ la ƒe aɖaŋu nyo wu Axitofel ƒe aɖaŋu! Ke Yehowae ɖoe, be yeagblẽ Axitofel ƒe aɖaŋu nyui la me; elabena Yehowa be, yeahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ava Absalom dzi.

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Eye Xusai gblɔ na nunɔla Zadok kple Abyatar bena: Ale kple ala Axitofel ɖo aɖaŋu na Absalom kple Israel-ame tsitsiwo enye si, eye ale kple ale meɖo aɖaŋu enye si.

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Eyata nètsɔ, mido ame ɖo ɖa, ne woaɖagblɔ na Dawid bena: Megatsi tɔtsoƒe da le gbea dzi o, ke boŋ yi taa godo, ne womagatsrɔ̃ fia lã kple ameha, siwo katã le eŋu la o!

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Eye Yonatan kple Aximaaz wonɔ Rogel-vudo la gbɔ. Eye dɔlanyɔnua ɖe hea gbe yinae na wo woɖagblɔna na fia Dawid be: womekpɔ mɔ ayi dua me o, elabena woava kpɔ wo.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Ke ŋutsuvia ɖe kpɔ wo, eye wòva gblɔe na Absalom. Tete woa kple eve la ƒu du kaba yi ŋutsua ɖe ƒe me le Baxurim, amesi ɖe vudo ɖe eƒe xɔxɔnu, eye woyi ɖe eme.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: Ke nyɔnua ɖe tsɔ avɔ keke ɖe vudo la nu, eye wòsia bli gbagbã ɖe edzi, be womagadze sii o.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Eye Absalom ƒe dɔlawo va nyɔnu la gbɔ le aƒea me hebia bena: Afika Aximaaz kple Yonatan wole? Nyɔnu la ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Woyi to la godo. Eye esi wodi wo, eye womekpɔ wo o la, wogbugbɔ va Yerusalem.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Eye esi wodzo la, wodo le vudoa me yi ɖagblɔe na fia Dawid. Eye wogblɔ na Dawid bena: Mitso, ne miatso toa kaba: elabena ale Axitofel de adaŋu ɖe nua ŋu enye si!

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Tete Dawid kple ameha, siwo katã le eŋu la, tsi tre, eye wotso Yordan; ame ɖeka hã hã mekpɔtɔ, si metso Yordan hafi ŋu ke o.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Esi Axitofel kpɔ be, womewɔ yeƒe adaŋudede dzi na ve o la, ebla akpa na tedzi, eye wodze mɔ yi eƒe me le wo de. Eye esi wòɖo eƒe me la, ede ka ve na eɖokui, eye wòku, eye woɖii ɖe fofoa ƒe yɔdo me.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Ke Dawid va Maxanayim, esime Absalom kple Israel-ŋutsu, siwo katã le eŋu la, tso Yordan.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Eye Absalom tsɔ Amasa ɖo aʋakɔ la nu ɖe Yoab teƒe; Amasa enye Ismael-ŋutsu, si ŋkɔ nye Yitra, amesi ɖɔ Nahas vinyɔnu Abigal, si nye Yoab dada, Zeruya nɔvinyɔnu gbɔ la ƒe vi.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Eye Israel kple Absalom ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Gilead-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, esime Dawid va Maxanayim la, tete Nahas vi Sobi tso Amon-viwo ƒe Raba, kple Amiel vi Maxir tso Lo-Debar kpakple Gileadtɔ Barzilai tso Roglim

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: anyitsi, notsi kpẽke, alẽwo kple nyinɔkesuwo vɛ na Dawid kple ameha, si le eŋu, be woaɖu; elabena wogblɔ be: Dɔ wu ameha la, ɖeɖi te eŋu, eye tsikɔ wui le gbea dzi.

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid tsɔ aʋakɔ ta ƒe etɔ̃liawo ɖeka de Yoab si, etsɔ etɔ̃liawo ɖeka de Zeruya vi Abisai, si nye Yoab nɔvi la si, eye wòtsɔ etɔ̃liawo ɖeka ɖe Gititɔ Itai si. Eye fia la gblɔ na aʋakɔ la bena: Nye hã mayi kpli mi.

english_verse: But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth
translation_verse: Ke aʋakɔ la ɖo ŋu bena: Megayi o; elabena ne míesi la, womabui na mí o, eye ne miaƒe akpa afã ku hã la, womabui na mi o; elabena ele abe mía dome ame akpe ewo ene. Eyata ne axɔ na mi tso dua me la, anyo wu.

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsua ɖe kpɔe va gblɔ na Yoab bena: Kpɔ ɖa, mekpɔ Absalom wòtsi klẽtia ɖe ŋu.

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Eye aʋa la kaka tso afima ɖe anyigba blibo la dzi, eye amesiwo tsi ave si la sa gbɔ wu esiwo tsi yi nu gbemagbe.

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Eye Absalom va ƒo go Dawid ƒe dolawo Absalom do tedzisɔ, eye tedzisɔ la va to klẽti gãa ɖe, si vu alo dranyi la te, eye eƒe ta tsi klẽti la ŋu, eye wòle nyenyem le anyigba kple dziƒo dome; ke tedzisɔ la do le ete dzo.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Tete Yoab gblɔ na ŋutsu, si va gblɔe ne, bena: Kpɔ ɖa, esi nèkpɔe la, nukaŋuti mèda nui ƒu anyi ɖe afima oa? Anye ne mana klosalo ewo kple alidziblanu ɖeka wò!

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Ɖe wònye ɖe mewo nane ɖe eŋu le adza me la, anye ne atro ʋu le yonyeme, elabena naneke meɣlana ɖe fia la o.

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Tete Yoab gblɔ bena: Nyematɔ ɖe gbɔwò didie o! Eye wòtsɔ akplɔ etɔ̃ ɖe asi ɖatɔ Absalom ƒe dzinu; ke esi wogale agbe le klẽtia ŋu ko la,

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: ɖekakpui ewo, siwo nye Yoab ƒe adekplɔviwo la, va ɖe to ɖee, eye woda nui woku

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Tete Yoab ku kpẽ, eye aʋakɔ la trɔ le Israel yome; elabena Yoab na aʋakɔ la to te.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ Absalom ƒu gbe ɖe do gãa ɖe me le avea me, eye wofa kpe li ko gãa ɖe ɖe edzi, eye Israel blibo ta dome amesiame si yi eƒe agbadɔ me.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Ke esi Absalom le agbe la, eɖo kpea ɖe ɖe fia ƒe bali la me; elabena egblɔ be: Viŋutsua ɖeke mele asinye, ne wòalé nye ŋkɔ ɖe te o. Etsɔ eƒe ŋkɔ na kpe la, eye woyɔnɛ vaseɖe egbe be Absalom ƒe ŋkuɖodzikpe. Kusi ƒe ami dɔdɔwo.

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Eye Zadok vi Aximaaz gblɔ bena: Maƒu du ahe du ayi na fia la bena, Yehowa tso afia nɛ le eƒe futɔwo si me.

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Tete Yoab gblɔ nɛ bena: Mèle du nyuia ɖeke he ge ayii egbea o, ɣebubuɣi hã ahe du ayii xoxo; ke megahe dua ɖeke yii egbea o, elabena fiavi la ku!

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Eye Yoab gblɔ na Kusitɔ la bena: Yi ɖagblɔ nusi nekpɔ la, na fia la! Tete Kusitɔ la bɔbɔ de Yoab ŋku me, eye wòƒu du yi.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Ke Zadok vi Aximaaz gaxɔ edzi gblɔ na Yoab bena: Ne edze agbodo ʋuu hã, maƒu du adze Kusitɔ la yome! Yoab gblɔ bena: Vinye, nukaŋuti nèbe, yeaƒu du ayi, esi amea ɖeke mele dɔtsɔho xe ge na wò oa?

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Ne edze agbodo ʋuu hã la, mele yiyi ge! Eye wògblɔ ne bena Heyi! Tete Aximaaz to tagbamɔ tre dede na Kusitɔ la.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Dawid bɔbɔ nɔ agbo eve dome, eye dzɔla de agbo, si le glia ŋu la ta me. Eye esi wòfɔ kɔ dzi la, ekpɔ ŋutsu ɖeka koliaa ɖe le ɖu dzi gbɔna ɖa.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Tete dzɔla la gblɔe na fia la. Eye fia la gblɔ bena: Nenye eya ɖekae la, ekema gbe nyuia ɖe le eŋu. Eye esi wòle ɖu dzi le aƒe tum la,

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
translation_verse: agbonudzɔla la gakpɔ ŋutsu bubu le du ƒum, eye agbonudzɔla la do ɣli ɖo ɖe agbo la me bena: Kpɔ da, ŋutsu ɖeka koliaa ɖe le du dzi gbɔna! Tete fia la gblɔ be: Eya hã he gbe nyuia ɖe ɖe asi.

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Eye dzɔla la gblɔ bena: Ame gbãtɔ ƒe duƒuƒume ɖi Zadok vi Aximaaz tɔ. Tete fia la gblɔ bena: Ame nyui wònye, eye gbe nyui wòbe gbɔnae.

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Eve Aximaaz do ɣli gblɔ na ba la bena: Ŋutifafa! Eye wobɔbɔ de ta agu ɖe fia la ŋku me gblɔ bena: Woayra Yehowa, wò Mawu, si tsɔ ŋutsu, siwo do woƒe asi ɖe dzi ɖe nye aƒetɔ fia ŋu la, de asi!

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ be: Ɖekakpui Absalom li sesiea? Aximaaz ɖo ŋu bena: Mekpɔ zitɔtɔ gãa ɖe, esime Yoab dɔ fia ƒe dɔla kple wò dɔla, ke nyemenya nusi dzɔ o.

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ be: Te ɖe aga, eye natsi tre ɖe afi! Tete wòle ɖe aga, eye wòtsi tre ɖi.

english_verse: The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
translation_verse: Eye kpɔ ɖa, Kusitɔ la va, eye Kusitɔ la gblɔ bena: Mehe gbe nyui vɛ na nye aƒetɔ fía, elabena Yehowa tso afia na wò tso amesiwo katã tsi tre ɖe ŋuwò la si me egbe

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ na Kusitɔ la bena: Ɖekakpui Absalom li sesiea? Kusitɔ la ɖo ŋu bena: Ava me na nye aƒetɔ fía ƒe futɔwo kple amesiwo katã tsi, tre ɖe ŋuwò, be woawɔ vɔ̃ wò la, abe alesi wova me na ɖekakpui la ene!

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: Eye wova gblɔ na Yoab bena: Kpɔ ɖa, fia la le avi fam, eye wòle konyi tam le Absalom ŋuti.

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Ale dziɖuɖu la trɔ zu konyifafa na dukɔ blibo la gbemagbe, elabena dukɔ la se gbemagbe be, fia la le nu xam le via ŋuti.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Eve aʋakɔ la zɔ minyaminya va yi ɖe du la me, abe alesi aʋakɔ, si ɖu ŋukpe, zɔna nunya nunya, ne esi le aʋa nu la ene.

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Fia la tsyɔ nu ŋku me, eye fia la do ɣli kple gbe sesi bena: Vinye Absalom, vinye Absalom, vinye!

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: Tete Yoab yi ɖe fia la gbɔ le xɔa me gblɔ bena: Ede ŋukpe mo na wò dɔlawo katã, amesiwo xɔ mia kple viwòŋutsuwo kple viwònyɔnuwo, srɔ̃wòwo kple wò ahiãwo ɖe agbe egbea:

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: elɔ̃ amesiwo lé fu wò, eye nele fu amesiwo lɔ wò; elabena eɖee fia egbea bena, amegã kple dɔlaa ɖeke mele asiwò o; elabena medze sii egbea bena, ɖe wònye Absalom ye tsi agbe, eye mi katã míeku la, ne enyo ŋuwò wu.

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Eyata tsi tre, nado ayi, eye naƒo nu kple wò dɔlawo fafɛ; elabena meta Yehowa: ne medo yi o la, amea ɖeke makpɔtɔ ɖe gbɔwò le zã sia me o; eye esia avɔ̃ɖi na wò awu vɔ̃, siwo katã dzɔ ɖe dziwò tso wò ɖekakpuime vaseɖe fifi!

english_verse: everyone in Israel started arguing. They were saying to each other, “King David rescued us from the Philistines and from our other enemies. But then we chose Absalom to be our new leader, and David had to leave the country to get away. Absalom died in battle, so why hasn't something been done to bring David back?”
translation_verse: Eye dukɔ blibo la he dzre le Israel-toawo katã me gblɔ bena: Fia la ɖe mí tso míaƒe futɔwo si me, eye wòxɔ mí tso Filistitɔwo si; azɔ esi tso anyigba la dzi le Absalom nu.

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Ke Absalom, amesi míesi ami na heɖo fiae ɖe mía nu la, tsi aʋa. Azɔ nukaŋuti miele hehem ɖe megbe le fia la kpɔkplɔ gbɔe me?

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Nɔvinyewo míenye, nye ƒu kple nye ŋutilã míenye; nukaŋuti miehe, yewoanye ame mlɔetɔ, siwo ava kplɔ fia la?

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Eye migblɔ na Amasa bena: Alo menye nye ƒu kple nye ŋutilã nenye oa? Mawu nafiam agafiam ɖe dzi, ne menye wòe anye aʋafia le ŋkunye me ɖaa ɖe Yoab teƒe o fi!

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Eye fia la gbugbɔ heva Yordan nu; ke Yuda va Gilgal, be woakpe fia la, eye wòaɖe tsii ato Yordan dzi. Dawid ƒe kalẽwɔwɔ kple akpedada.

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na fia la bena: Nye aƒetɔ megabu vodada nam o, eye megado ŋku vo, si eƒe dɔla dã le gbesigbe nye aƒetɔ fia la tso Yerusalem la o, eye fia la megabui o!

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Eye Benyamin-ŋutsu akpe ɖeka kple dɔla Ziba, si le Saul ƒe me, kple via wuiatɔ̃awo kple eƒe dɔla blave wokpe ɖe eŋu, eye wotre Yordan nu vava na fia la.

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: Emegbe duwo yi, be woaɖe tsi fiaƒe me tɔwo, eye woawo, abe alesi wòdi ene. Tete Simei, Gera vi, de ta agu ɖe fia la ŋku me, esime wotso Yordan.

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Tete Abisai, Zeruya tu la, gblɔ bena: Alo womele Simei, amesi do ɖiŋu na Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la, wu ge oa?

english_verse: Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came to meet David. He had missed David so much that he had not taken a bath or trimmed his beard or washed his clothes the whole time David was gone. David asked him, “Why didn't you go with me?”
translation_verse: Eye Saul vi Mefiboset va kpe fia la; ke meɖo eƒe afɔ kple ge ɖo o, eye menya eƒe avɔ o tso gbesigbe fia la dzo, vaseɖe gbesigbe wògbɔ le ŋutifafa me.

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: Esi wòva Yerusalem fia la kpe ge la, fia la biae be: Mefiboset, nukaŋuti meyi kplim o?

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Nye aƒetɔ fia, nye dɔlae blem; elabena wò dɔla gblɔ be: Bla akpa na tedzi nam, ne mado ayi kple fia la, elabena xɔdrɔ̃e wò dɔla nye.

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: Eye wòva zɔ wò dɔla gɔme na nye aƒetɔ fia la; ke nye aƒetɔ fia la le abe Mawu ƒe ɖɔla ene, eyata wɔ nusi dze ŋuwò!

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ nɛ bena: Nukaŋuti nègale nu ƒom ɖe edzi? Megblɔ be, mia kple Ziba miamã agble lɔ!

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Tete Mefiboset ɖo ŋu na fia la bena: Esi nye aƒetɔ fia la trɔ gbɔ va aƒe le ŋutifafa me ko la, nexɔ wo katã gɔ̃!

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Barsilai ku amegã ɖeɖi xɔ ƒe blanyi; eya kpɔ fia la dzi, esime wònɔ Maxanayim, elabena alɔme le esi ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Eye fia la gblɔ na Barsilai bena: Yi kplim, eye nanɔ gbɔnye, makpɔ dziwò le Yerusalem!

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: Ƒe blanyi mexɔ egbe siawo. Ɖe mate ŋu ade vovo nu nyui kple nu manyomanyo domea? Ɖe nusi wò dɔla ɖuna, eye wònona la, gavivia enua? Alo ɖe maganɔ hadzilaŋutsuwo kple hadzilanyɔnuwo ƒe gbe sema? Nukaŋuti wò dɔla anye agba na nye aƒetɔ fia?

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Ɖeko wò dɔla be, yeakplɔ fia la atso Yordan ʋee. Nukaŋuti fia la be, yeaɖo eteƒe nam ale?

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Na wò dɔla nagbugbɔ, eye maku ɖe mia de kple fofonye kpakple danye ɖiƒe! Kpɔ ɖa, wò dɔla Kimham neyi kple nye aƒetɔ fia la, eye nawɔ nusi nyo ŋuwò la na!

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ be: Kimham neyi kplim, eye mawo nusi nyo ŋuwò la nɛ, eye nusianu, si nèdi tso asinye la, mawɔe na wò.

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Eye aʋakɔ blibo la tso Yordan, emegbe fia la hã tsoe. Eye fia la ɖuɖɔ nu na Barsilai heyrae, eye wògbugbɔ yi enɔƒe.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Emegbe fia la yi azɔli la dzi heva Gilgal, eye Kimham kpe ɖe eŋu. Yuda ƒe ameha blibo la kplɔ fia la yi, eye Israel-ameha la ƒe afã hã le eme.

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Eye kpɔ ɖa, Israel-ŋutsuwo katã va fia la gbɔ, eye wogblɔ na fia la bena: Nukaŋuti ma nɔvi Yuda-ŋutsuwo fi wò dzoe, eye wokplɔ fia la kple eƒemetɔwo yi Yordan godo, eye Dawid ƒe ŋutsuwo katã kpe ɖe eŋu?

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Tete Yuda-ŋutsuwo katã ɖo ŋu na Israel-ŋutsuwo bena: Le esi fia la tsɔ mía gbɔ la tae! Nukaŋuti miele dɔmedzoe dom le nya sia ŋuti? Ɖe mieɖu fia la ƒe nanea? Alo ɖe míexɔ nunana le esia?

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: Eye yakamea ɖe le afima, si ŋkɔ nye Seba, Bixri vi, eye wònye Benyamintɔ; eku kpẽ gblɔ bena: Gomea ɖeke mele Dawid gbɔ na mi o, eye domenyinu ɖeke mele Isai vi la si na mi o. Israel lee, mia dome amesiame neyi eƒe agbadɔ me!

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Tete Israel-ŋutsuwo katã tu le Dawid ŋu hedze Seba, Bixri vi la yome. Ke Yuda-ŋutsuwo ku ɖe woƒe fia la ŋu tso Yordan nu vaseɖe Yerusalem.

english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: Esi Dawid va eƒe me le Yerusalem la, fia la tsɔ nyɔnu ewo, siwo nye eƒe ahiãwo, amesiwo wogblẽ ɖi, be woanɔ aƒea dzi kpɔm la, de xɔ me, eye wòkpɔ wo dzi, ke medɔ wo gbɔ o; eye wotsi xɔa me, abe alesi ahosiwo nɔa agbee ene, vaseɖe woƒe kugbe.

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Eye na la gblɔ na Amasa bena: Yɔ Yuda-ŋutsuwo nam le ŋkeke etɔ me, emegbe nagava afi!

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Eye Amasa yi Yuda yɔ ge; ke esi wòtsi anyi ɣeyiɣi, si woɖo nɛ, de gbɔ edzi la,

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: tete Dawid gblɔ na Abisai bena: Azɔ Seba, Bixri vi la, le vɔ wɔ ge mi awu Absalom. Eyata ɖe wò aƒetɔ ƒe dɔlawo, eye nati eyome, ne magaxɔ du sesẽwo, eye wòasi le mia ŋku me o!

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Eye Yoab ƒe amewo ho dze eyome hekpe ɖe Kretitɔwo kple Pletitɔwo kpakple kalẽtɔwo katã ŋu, eye woho tso Yerusalem ti Seba, Bixri vi la yome.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: Esi woɖo kpe gã, si le Gibeon gbɔ la, tete Amasa va ɖo go wo. Ke yi le Yoab si le eƒe aʋawu, si wòɖo la te, eye wòta yi, si le aku me la, ɖe edzi le aklito, eya ɖo le eme hege ɖe anyigba.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Yoab gblɔ na Amasa bena: Nɔvinye, èli sesĩea? Tete Yoab tsɔ ɖusi lé Amasa ƒe ge, be yeaɖuɖɔ nu nɛ.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Ke Amasa melé ŋku ɖe yi, si le Yoab si la ŋu o; eye wòtsɔe ɖa nu dɔ me nɛ, eye eƒe, dɔmenuwo dudu ɖe anyigba, ke megadae zi evelia o. Esi Yoab kple nɔvia Abisai woti Seba, Bixri vi la yome la,

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Yoab ƒe ɖekakpuiwo dometɔ ɖeka tsi egbɔ le gbɔgblɔm bena Amesi ke lɔ̃a Yoab ƒe nya kple amesi ke nye Dawid lɔ la, nedze Yoab yome!

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Ke Amasa le mimlim le eƒe nu me le maƒo me. Esi ŋutsu la kpɔ be, aʋakɔ blibo la tɔ la, èhe Amasa ɖa tso mɔa dzi yi gbe me, eye wotsɔ avɔ tsyɔ edzi; elabena ekpɔ be, amesiame, si va la, tɔna ɖi.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: Esi wòtee ɖa le mɔa dzi la, amesiame to eŋuli dze Yoab yome, be woati Seba, Bixri vi la yome.

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Ke eya tsa to Israel-toawo katã me vaseɖe Abel-Bet-Maaxa, eye Bixritɔwo katã hã ƒo ƒu hedze eyome.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Azɔ wova ɖe to ɖe wo le Abel-Bet-Maaxa, eye woƒu kpo ɖe du la ŋu vaseɖe glia dzi. Eye aʋakɔ blibo, si le Yoab ŋu la, lu ɖe eme, be woamũ gli la.

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: Tete nyɔnu dzeaɖaŋua ɖe do ɣli tso dua me bena: Ago gbɔ! Ago gbɔ! Taflatse, migblɔ na Yoab be, nete va ati, ne maƒo nu kplii!

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Tete wote ɖe eŋu, eye nyɔnu la gblɔ be: Wòe nye Yoab la? Eɖo ŋu be: Nyee! Eye wògblɔ nɛ be: Se wò dɔlanyɔnu ƒe nya! Eɖo ŋu be: Mele esem.

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Nyee nye ame fafa kple anukwaretɔwo dometɔ ɖeka le Israel; èbe, yeatsrɔ̃ du kple dada le Israel; nukaŋuti nèbe, yeagblẽ Yehowa ƒe domenyinu?

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Tete Yoab xɔ edzi gblɔ bena: Nyemebe, matsrɔ̃ naneke o, eye nyemebe, magblẽ naneke o.

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Nya la mele alea o, ke boŋ ŋutsua ɖe, si tso Efrayim-to la dzi, amesi ŋkɔ nye Seba, Bixri vi lae, do eƒe asi ɖe dzi ɖe fia Dawid ŋu. Ne mieɖe eya ɖeɖe na la, ekema madzo le dua ŋu. Eye nyɔnu la gblɔ na Yoab bena: Kpɔ ɖa, woatsɔ eƒe ta aƒu gbe ato glia dzi aɖo de wò.

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Eye nyɔnu la va dukɔ blibo la gbɔ kple eƒe aɖaŋudzedze la, eye wotso ta le Seba, Bixri vi la nu tsɔ ƒu gbe ɖe Yoab. Tete woku kpẽ, eye woka le du la ŋu, eye amesiame yi ɖe eƒe agbadɔ me. Emegbe Yoab gbugbɔ va fia la gbɔ le Yerusalem. Dawid subɔlawo.

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Yoab le Israel ƒe aʋakɔ blibo la nu, eye Benaya, Yehoyada vi, le Kretitɔwo kple Pletitɔwo nu;

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: Adoram kpɔa dɔwɔwɔ dzi, eye Yosafat, Axilud vi, enye fia ƒe tsiami;

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: Seya enye agbalẽŋlɔla, eye Zadok kple Abyatar wonye nunɔlawo;

english_verse: Ira from Jair was David's priest.
translation_verse: eye Ira, Yairitɔ, hã enye nunɔla le Dawid gbɔ.

english_verse: The Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were descendants of the Amorites. The people of Israel had promised not to kill them, but Saul had tried to kill them because he wanted Israel and Judah to control all the land. David had the Gibeonites come, and he talked with them.
translation_verse: Eye fia la ya Gibeontɔwo ƒo nu kpli wo. Gibeontɔwo metso Israel-viwo dome o, ke boŋ wonye Amoritɔwo ƒe kpɔtɔe, siwo Israel-viwo ka atam na; eye Saul di be, yeawu wo, elabena eʋã ŋu ɖe Israel-viwo kple Yuda nu

english_verse: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ na Gibeontɔwo bena: Nuka mawo na mi, eye nuka matsɔ alé avu mi, be miayra Yehowa ƒe domenyinu la?

english_verse: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu na fia la bena: Ŋutsu, si wu mi, eye wòɖo lãme be, yeatsrɔ̃ mi ɖa, ne míaganɔ Israel-nyigba blibo la dzi o lae!

english_verse: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
translation_verse: Ne woɖe ame adre na le viaŋutsuwo dome, ne míahe wo ɖe ati ŋu na Yehowa le Saul, amesi nye Yehowa ƒe ame tiatia la ƒe Gibea. Eye fia la gblɔ be: Maɖe wo ana

english_verse: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
translation_verse: Ke fia la ve Mefiboset, Saul vi Yonatan ƒe viŋutsu la nu le Yehowa ƒe atam, si le Dawid kple Yonatan, Saul vi dome la ta.

english_verse: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
translation_verse: eye wotsɔ wo de asi na Gibeontɔwo, eye wohe wo ɖe ati ŋu le to la dzi le Yehowa ŋku me, eye wo ame adre la ku zi ɖeka. Wowu wo le nuŋeɣi ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi, esime wodze luŋeŋe gɔme.

english_verse: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
translation_verse: Tete Aya vinyɔnu Rizpa tsɔ akpanya keke ɖe agakpe la dzi tso nuŋeɣi ƒe gɔmedzedze, vaseɖe esime tsi dza tso dziƒo ɖe wodzi; eye mena dziƒoxewo dze ɖe wo dzi le ŋkeke me, alo gbemelãwo va wo gbɔ le zã me o.

english_verse: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Dawid yi ɖaxɔ Saul kple via Yonatan ƒe ƒuwo, siwo Yabes-Gileadtɔwo yi ɖafi le Bet-San ƒe ablɔ me, afisi Filistitɔwo tsɔ wo va ku ɖo, le gbesigbe Filistitɔwo wu Saul le Gilboa la, le wo si.

english_verse: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: Eye woɖi Saul kple via Yonatan ƒe ƒuwo ɖe Zela le Benyamin-nyigba dzi ɖe fofoa Kis ƒe yɔdo me, eye wowɔ nusiwo katã ŋu fia la ɖe se le la. Esia megbe Mawu gase gbe, si wodo ɖa ɖe anyigba la ta. Dawid ɖu Filistitɔwo dzi.

english_verse: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
translation_verse: Wogawɔ aʋa le Gat, eye ame dzɔtsua de to asi ade kple afɔ ade; wo katã le blave vɔ ene; eye eya hã tso ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe dzidzime.

english_verse: One time David got very tired when he and his soldiers were fighting the Philistines.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo gãwo aʋa kple Israel, eye Dawid kple eƒe dɔlawo ho ɖawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo, eye ɖeɖi te Dawid ŋu.

english_verse: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
translation_verse: Eye Yisbi tso Nob, amesi nye ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe dzidzimeviwo dometɔ ɖeka, di be, yeawu Dawid. Eƒe akplɔ ƒe kpekpeme le akɔbli sekel alafa etɔ̃, eye wòkpla aʋawɔnu yeye.

english_verse: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
translation_verse: Ke Zeruya vi Abisai xɔ nɛ, eye wòwu Filistitɔ la. Ɣemaɣi Dawid ƒe ŋutsuwo ka atam nɛ bena: Magade aʋa kpli mi azɔ o, ne nagatsi Israel ƒe akaɖi la o!

english_verse: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me emegbe be, wowɔ aʋa kple Filistitowo le Gob. Ɣemaɣi Xusatilɔ Sipai wu Saf, si tso ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe dzidzimeviwo dome.

english_verse: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Wogawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo le Gob, eye Elxanan, Yaare-Orgim vi, tso Betlexem wu Gatitɔ Goliat, amesi ƒe akplɔti le abe abaladoti ene.

english_verse: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
translation_verse: Eɖu fewu le Israel ŋu, tete Yonatan, Dawid nɔvi Simea vi wui.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_verse: Ame ene siawo tso ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe dzidzime le Gat, eye wotsi Dawid kple eƒe dɔlawo si me.

english_verse: You rescued me from enemies who were hateful and too powerful for me.
translation_verse: Eɖem tso nye futɔ sesẽ la kple nye ketɔwo si me, elabena wosesẽ wum.

english_verse: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
translation_verse: Tete Dawid gblɔ ha sia ƒe nyawo na Yehowa le gbesigbe Yehowa ɖee tso eƒe futɔwo katã kple Saul si me,

english_verse: I will praise you, Lord, and I will honor you among the nations.
translation_verse: Eyata mele kafuwòm, Yehowa, le dukɔwo dome, eye mele kafukafuha dzim na wò ŋkɔ.

english_verse: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ be: Yehowa enye nye agakpe, nye mɔ̃ kple nye ɖela.

english_verse: You are the rock where I am safe. You are my shield, my powerful weapon, and my place of shelter. You rescue me and keep me safe from violence.
translation_verse: Mawu enye nye ɣaɣlaƒe, amesi gbɔ mebe ɖo nye akpoxɔnu kple nye xoxo ƒe lãdzo, nye mɔ̃ sesẽ kple nye sitsoƒe kpakple nye xɔla, amesi ɖem tso ŋutasẽlawo si me.

english_verse: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
translation_verse: Meyɔ Yehowa, amesi dze bubu, eye medo tso nye futɔwo si me.

english_verse: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
translation_verse: Elabena ku ƒe tsitsotsoewo ɖe to ɖem eve gbegblẽ ƒe tɔsisiwo do ŋɔdzi nam.

english_verse: Ropes from the world of the dead had coiled around me, and death had set a trap in my path.
translation_verse: Tsiẽƒe ƒe kawo ƒo xlãm eve ku ƒe adoboliwo ɖem

english_verse: I was in terrible trouble when I called out to you, but from your temple you heard me and answered my prayer.
translation_verse: Meyɔ Yehowa le nye xaxa me eye meɖo ɣli na nye Mawu, ese nye gbe tso eƒe fiasã me, eye nye kokoƒoƒo de eƒe to me.

english_verse: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
translation_verse: Anyigba ʋã, eye wòʋuʋu, eye dziƒo ƒe anyinɔwo dzo kpekpekpe: woʋã elabena edo dɔmedzoe.

english_verse: and breathed out smoke. Scorching heat and fiery flames spewed from your mouth.
translation_verse: Dzudzɔ de dzi tso eƒe ŋɔti me, dzo tso eƒe nu me fiã nu, eye aka lé dzo tso egbɔ.

english_verse: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
translation_verse: Eviã dziƒo heɖi ɖe anyi, eye alilikpo dodo le eƒe afɔ te.

english_verse: You rode on the backs of flying creatures. You appeared with the wind as wings.
translation_verse: Ena Kerubi dzi hedzo, eye woɖo agba ɖe ya ƒe aʋalawo dzi.

english_verse: Darkness was your tent! Thunderclouds filled the sky, hiding you from sight.
translation_verse: Ewo viviti no me abe agbadɔ ene, eye tsiɖɔɖɔ tso alilikpo dodo me.

english_verse: Fiery coals lit up the sky in front of you.
translation_verse: Dzoka xɔxɔwo do tso keklẽ me le eŋgɔ.

english_verse: Lord Most High, your voice thundered from the heavens.
translation_verse: Yehowa ɖe gbe tso dziƒo, eye dziƒoʋitɔ la na eƒe gbe ɖi.

english_verse: You scattered your enemies with arrows of lightning.
translation_verse: Eda aŋutrɔ wòkaka wo hlẽ, eye wòɖo dzikedzo ɖa wòtafa wo.

english_verse: You roared at the sea, and its deepest channels could be seen. You snorted, and the earth shook to its foundations.
translation_verse: Tete atsiaƒu gɔme dze, eye anyigba ƒe anyinɔwo tsi go to Yehowa ƒe ŋɔdzidodo kple eƒe ŋɔti me gbɔgbɔ me.

english_verse: You reached down from heaven, and you lifted me from deep in the ocean.
translation_verse: Edo alɔ ɖa tso dzi lém, eye wòhem tso tɔ gãwo me

english_verse: On the day disaster struck, they came and attacked, but you defended me.
translation_verse: Wodze dzinye le gbesigbe meɖo dzɔgbevɔ̃e me, ke Yehowa enye nye ziɔɖeŋu.

english_verse: When I was fenced in, you freed and rescued me because you love me.
translation_verse: Ekplɔm va dogba dzi, eye wòɖem, elabena nye nu nyo eŋu.

english_verse: You are good to me, Lord, because I do right, and you reward me because I am innocent.
translation_verse: Yehowa wɔ nam ɖe nye dzɔdzɔenyenye nu, eye wòɖo teƒe nam le esi nye asi dza ta.

english_verse: I do what you want and never turn to do evil.
translation_verse: Elabena melé ŋku ɖe Yehowa ƒe mɔwo ŋu, eye nyemewɔ nu vloa ɖeke ɖe nye Mawu ŋu o.

english_verse: I keep your laws in mind and never turn away from your teachings.
translation_verse: Elabena eƒe sewo katã le ŋkunye me, eye nyemeɖe eƒe ɖoɖowo ɖa le gbɔnye o.

english_verse: I obey you completely and guard against sin.
translation_verse: Mede blibo le eƒe ŋku me, eye mekpɔ ɖokuinye dzi le nye vodada ŋuti.

english_verse: You have been good to me because I do right; you have rewarded me for being innocent by your standards.
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa ɖo eteƒe nam le nye dzɔdzɔenyenye ta, le esi nye asi dza le eŋku me ta.

english_verse: You are always loyal to your loyal people, and you are faithful to the faithful.
translation_verse: Wò dɔme nyona ɖe dɔmenyotɔ ŋu, eye èdea blibo le amesi dea blibo la gbɔ.

english_verse: With all who are sincere you are sincere, but you treat the unfaithful as their deeds deserve.
translation_verse: Edzana le amesi dzana gbɔ, ke èvlona ɖe amesi vlona ŋu.

english_verse: You rescue the humble, but you look for ways to put down the proud.
translation_verse: Exɔna na dukɔ, si wolena ɖe anyi, eye wò ŋku nɔa dadalawo ŋu, be nabɔbɔ wo ɖe anyi.

english_verse: Our Lord and God, you are my lamp. You turn darkness to light.
translation_verse: Elabena wò Yehowa ènye nye akaɖi, eye Yehowa na nye viviti me kɔ.

english_verse: Your way is perfect, Lord, and your word is correct. You are a shield for those who run to you for help.
translation_verse: Mawu ƒe mɔ de blibo, Yehowa ƒe nya me kɔ, akpoxɔnu wònye na amesiwo katã sii tso.

english_verse: You alone are God! Only you are a mighty rock.
translation_verse: Elabena ameka nye mawu kpe ɖe Yehowa ŋu? Eye ameka nye agakpe kpe ɖe mía Mawu la ŋu?

english_verse: You are my strong fortress, and you set me free.
translation_verse: Mawu enye nye mɔ̃ sesẽ, eye wòna nye mɔ zu gbadzaa.

english_verse: You make my feet run as fast as those of a deer, and you help me stand on the mountains.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nye afɔ abe zinɔwo tɔ ene, eye wòɖom togbɛwo dzi.

english_verse: You teach my hands to fight and my arms to use a bow of bronze.
translation_verse: Efia aʋawɔwɔ nye asiwò, ale be nye alɔwo vu akɔblidati me.

english_verse: You alone are my shield, and by coming to help me, you have made me famous.
translation_verse: Etsɔ wò xɔxɔ ƒe akpoxɔnu la nam, eye wò gbesese wɔm mezu gã.

english_verse: You clear the way for me, and now I won't stumble.
translation_verse: Ena nye afɔɖeɖe keke le tenye, eye nye afɔkɔewo mebotsona o.

english_verse: I kept chasing my enemies until I caught them and destroyed them.
translation_verse: Meɖe nye futɔwo ɖe nu, eye mewu wo, eye nyemetrɔ o, vaseɖe esime metsrɔ̃ wo vɔ.

english_verse: I destroyed them! I stuck my sword through my enemies, and they were crushed under my feet.
translation_verse: Metsrɔ̃ wo, eye meto wo nyanyanya, ale be womegafɔ o, eye wodze anyi ɖe nye afɔ te.

english_verse: You helped me win victories and forced my attackers to fall victim to me.
translation_verse: Etsɔ ŋusẽ bla ali dzi nam ɖe aʋawɔwɔ ŋu, eye nèbɔbɔ nye futɔwo ɖe tenye.

english_verse: You made my enemies run, and I killed them.
translation_verse: Ena nye futɔwo trɔ ʋume dem, eye metsrɔ̃ nye futɔwo gbidigbidi.

english_verse: They cried out for help, but no one saved them; they called out to you, but there was no answer.
translation_verse: Wodo ɣli na Yehowa, ke xɔnametɔa ɖeke meli o, eye meɖo ŋu na wo o.

english_verse: I ground them to dust, and I squashed them like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: Metu wo abe anyigba ʋuʋudedi ene, eye metu afɔ wodzi hefanya wo abe kpɔdomeeba ene.

english_verse: You rescued me from my stubborn people and made me the leader of foreign nations, who are now my slaves.
translation_verse: Eɖem tso nye dukɔ ƒe dzrewɔwɔwo me, èdzram ɖo hetsɔm ɖo dukɔwo ƒe lae, eye dukɔ, si nyemenya o la, subɔm.

english_verse: They have lost all courage and from their fortresses they come trembling.
translation_verse: Dzidzi ƒo amedzroviawo, eye woƒe lãme tu, wodo tso woƒe mɔwo me.

english_verse: You are the living Lord! I will praise you! You are a mighty rock. I will honor you for keeping me safe.
translation_verse: Yehowa le agbe; woakafu nye agakpe, eye wòado Mawu, nye xoxo ƒe agakpe la, ɖe dzi.

english_verse: You took revenge for me, and you put nations in my power.
translation_verse: Mawu, amesi bia hlɔ̃ nam, eye wòtsɔ dukɔwo ɖe tenye.

english_verse: You protected me from violent enemies, and you made me much greater than all of them.
translation_verse: Ekplɔm tso nye futɔwo dome, eye wòtsɔm ɖo nye futɔwo dzi, eye wòɖem tso ŋutasẽla si me.

english_verse: You give glorious victories to your chosen king. Your faithful love for David and for his descendants will never end.
translation_verse: Eɖe xɔxɔ gã fia eƒe fia, eye wòve Dawid, eƒe amesiamina la, kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo nu tegbee.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord has told me what to say.
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe Gbɔgbɔ ƒo nu to dzinye, eye eƒe nya le nye aɖe dzi.

english_verse: Our Mighty Rock, the God of Jacob, told me, “A ruler who obeys God and does right
translation_verse: Israel ƒe Mawu la ƒo nu, Israel ƒe agakpe la gblɔ nam bena: Amesi ɖu amegbetɔwo dzi dzɔdzɔe kple amesi ɖu dzi le mawuvɔvɔ̃ me la,

english_verse: I have ruled this way, and God will never break his promise to me. God's promise is complete and unchanging; he will always help me and give me what I hope for.
translation_verse: Ɖe nye aƒe mele alea le Mawu ŋku me oa? Elabena ebia nu mava kplim, si woɖo pɛpɛpɛ, eye wodzrae ɖo. Elabena ɖe mana nye xɔxɔwo katã kple nye nudidiwo katã natsi ɖe dzi oa?

english_verse: But evil people are pulled up like thornbushes. They are not dug up by hand,
translation_verse: Ke yakamewo katã le abe ŋu, siwo wotsɔna ƒua gbe, eye womeɖea asi wo ŋu o la ene;

english_verse: but with a sharp spear and are burned on the spot. The Three Warriors (
translation_verse: ke boŋ amesi be, yeade asi wo ŋu la, ele be, woatso ga kple akplɔti ɖe asi, eye wòatɔ dzo wo ɖe wo teƒe. Dawid ƒe kalẽtɔwo kple woƒe nuwɔwɔwo.

english_verse: except Eleazar. He killed Philistines until his hand was cramped, and he couldn't let go of his sword. When Eleazar finished, all the Israelite troops had to do was come back and take the enemies' weapons and armor. The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
translation_verse: eya tsi tre, eye wòdza amewo le Filistitɔwo dome, vaseɖe esime ɖeɖi te eƒe asi ŋu, eye yi la lé ɖe asi me nɛ. Yehowa na woɖu dzi gãa ɖe gbemagbe, eye dukɔ blibo la gbugbɔ dze eyome, be woaɖaha nu.

english_verse: and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was the commander of the Thirty Warriors, but he still did not become one of the Three Warriors.
translation_verse: Wode bubu eŋu le ame blaetɔ̃awo dome, eye eya nye woƒe amegã; gake mede ame etɔawo nu o.

english_verse: These are the names of David's warriors: Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed
translation_verse: Dawid ƒe kalẽtɔwo ŋkɔwo nye esi: Isbaal, Xaxmoni vi, amesi nye fia ŋu asrafowo ƒe amegã, eya da eƒe akplɔ zi ɖeka to ame tsiaʋa alafa enyi dzi.

english_verse: The next one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. One time when the Philistines were at war with Israel, he and David dared the Philistines to fight them. Every one of the Israelite soldiers turned and ran,
translation_verse: Eyometɔ nye Eleazar, Axoxi vi, Dodo ƒe vi, amesi le kalẽtɔ etɔ̃awo dome le Dawid gbɔ. Esi woɖu fewu le Filistitɔwo ŋu, eye woƒo ƒu ho aʋa va afima, eye Israel-ŋutsuwo ho yi la,

english_verse: but Shammah stood in the middle of the field and killed the Philistines. The crops were saved, and the Lord gave Israel a great victory.
translation_verse: etsi tre ɖe agble la titina, eye wòxɔe, eye wòsi Filistitɔwo, eye Yehowa na woɖu dzi gãa ɖe.

english_verse: One year at harvest time, the Three Warriors went to meet David at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
translation_verse: Eye amegã blaetɔ̃awo dometɔ etɔ̃ tso yi Dawid gbɔ le Adulam-do la me le nuŋeŋɔli. Esime Filistitɔwo ƒe adzohawo ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Refaim-bali la me la,

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress,
translation_verse: Dawid le mɔ̃ me le to dzi, eye Filistitɔwo ɖe aʋakɔ ɖo Betlexem ɣemaɣi.

english_verse: and he was very thirsty. He said, “I wish I had a drink from the well by the gate at Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Eye nu de asi Dawid dzodzro me, wògblɔ bena: Ameka aku tsi tso vudɔ, si le agbo me le Betlexem la me ve mano?

english_verse: The Three Warriors sneaked into the Philistine camp and got some water from the well near Bethlehem's gate. But after they brought the water back to David, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as a sacrifice
translation_verse: Tete kalẽtɔ etɔ̃awo yi ɖage ɖe Filistitɔwo ƒe asaɖa me, eye woku tsi le vudo, si le agboa me le Betlexem la me hetsɔ ve na Dawid; ke egbe be, yemanoe o, eye wòtsɔe ƒo ɖe anyi na Yehowa.

english_verse: and said to the Lord, “I can't drink this water! It's like the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ be: Yehowa, esia wɔwɔ nede megbe xaa tso gbɔnye! Esia nye ŋutsu, siwo tsɔ woƒe agbe ke yi la, ƒe ʋu. Eye wogbe be, yemanoe o. Kalẽtɔ etɔ̃awoe wɔ esia.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
translation_verse: Benaya, Yehoyada vi, enye ŋutsu kalẽtɔa ɖe, si wɔ nu tsuwo la ƒe vi tso Kabzeel. Eya wu Moabitɔwo ƒe kalẽtɔ eveawo, eye wowu dzata le vudo la me le gbesigbe sno dza.

english_verse: Joab's brother Abishai was the leader of the Thirty Warriors, and in one battle he killed
translation_verse: Abisai, Zeruya vi, Yoab nɔvi, enye ame blaetɔ̃awo ƒe tatɔ; eya da eƒe akplɔ to ame tsiaʋa alafa etɔ̃awo dzi, eye wòxɔ ŋkɔ le ame blaetɔ̃awo dome.

english_verse: Another time, he killed an Egyptian, as big as a giant. The Egyptian was armed with a spear, but Benaiah only had a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
translation_verse: Eya wu Egipte-ŋutsu kakoa ɖe; akplɔ le Egiptetɔ la si, gake eyi egbɔ kple atizɔti, eye wòxɔ akplɔ la le Egiptetɔ la si hetsɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe akplɔ wui.

english_verse: Benaiah did these things. He never became one of the Three Warriors, but he was just as famous as they were and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. David made him the leader of his bodyguard.
translation_verse: Wode bubu eŋu le ame blaetɔ̃awo dome, ke mede ame etɔ̃awo nu o, eye Dawid tsɔe ɖo fia ŋu asrafowo nu.

english_verse: and said, “Your Majesty! Why have you come to see me?” David answered, “I've come to buy your threshing place. I have to build the Lord an altar here, so this disease will stop killing the people.”
translation_verse: Eye Arawna gblɔ bena: Nukata nye aƒetɔ fia va eƒe dɔla gbɔ ɖo? Dawid ɖo eŋu bena: Ɖe mebe, maƒle lugbɔƒe la, ne maɖi vɔsamlekpui na Yehowa, ne dɔvɔ̃ la nu natso le dukɔa dome.

english_verse: They went to Gilead and to Kadesh in Syria. Then they went to Dan, Ijon, and on toward Sidon.
translation_verse: Wòto Gilead heva Kades le Xititɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, eye wova Dan hetrɔ ɖo ta Zidon.

english_verse: So David told Joab and the army officers, “Go to every tribe in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north all the way south to Beersheba, and count everyone who can serve in the army. I want to know how many there are.”
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ na aʋakɔ la ƒe tatɔ Yoab bena: Yi ɖatsa le Israel-toawo katã me tso Dan vaseɖe Beer-Seba eye naxlẽ dukɔ la, ne manya dukɔ la ƒe xexlẽme!

english_verse: But when David refused to change his mind, Joab and the army officers went out and started counting the people.
translation_verse: Ke esi fia ta tsi eƒe nya la dzi na Yoab kple aʋakplɔlawo la. Yoab kple aʋakplɔlawo dzo le fia la gbɔ, be woaɖaxlẽ Israel-dukɔ la.

english_verse: They crossed the Jordan River and began with Aroer and the town in the middle of the river valley. From there they went toward Gad and on as far as Jazer.
translation_verse: Eye wotso Yordan heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Aroer, ɖe du, si le bali la me ƒe ɖusi me, ɖo la Gad kple Yaezer lɔƒo.

english_verse: After they had gone through the whole land, they went back to Jerusalem. It had taken them
translation_verse: Eye wotsa to anyigba blibo la dzi, eye wogbugbɔ va Yerusalem le dzinu asieke kple ŋkeke blave megbe.

english_verse: Araunah looked and saw David and his soldiers coming up toward him. He went over to David, bowed down low,
translation_verse: Esi Arawna fɔ kɔ te la, ekpɔ fia la kple eƒe dɔlawo gbɔna ɖe egbɔ; tete Arawna yi hebɔbɔ, eye wòde ta agu na fía la.

english_verse: David saw the angel killing everyone and told the Lord, “These people are like sheep with me as their shepherd. I have sinned terribly, but they have done nothing wrong. Please, punish me and my family instead of them!” David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place (
translation_verse: Esi Dawid kpɔ mawudɔla, si la ame wum le dukɔa dome la, egblɔ na Yehowa bena: Kpɔ ɖa, nyee wɔ nuvɔ̃, eye meda vo; ke alẽ siawo la, nuka wowɔ? Wò asi neva mia kple fofonye ƒe aƒe dzi boŋ!

english_verse: After everyone had been counted, David realized he had done wrong. He told the Lord, “What I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Lord, please forgive me.”
translation_verse: Tete Dawid ƒe dzi lã kpo, esime wòxlẽ dukɔ la vɔ megbe, eye Dawid gblɔ na Yehowa bena: Mewɔ nuvɔ̃ ŋutɔ be, mewɔ nusia; eyata Yehowa, ɖe wò dɔla ƒe vodada ɖa, elabena mewɔ lãnu ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Before David even got up the next morning, the Lord had told David's prophet Gad
translation_verse: Esi Dawid fɔ ŋdi kanya la, Yehowa ƒe gbe va nyagblɔɖila Gad, amesi nye Dawid ƒe nukpɔla, gbɔ bena:

english_verse: to take a message to David. Gad went to David and told him: You must choose one of three ways for the Lord to punish you: Will there be seven years when the land won't grow enough food for your people? Or will your enemies chase you and make you run from them for three months? Or will there be three days of horrible disease in your land? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God, who sent me.
translation_verse: Tete Gad va Dawid gbɔ, eye wòto nya la nɛ gblɔ bena: Dɔwuame neva wò anyigba dzi ƒe adre loo, alo asi le wò futɔwo nu, eye woaɖe wò ɖe nu dzinu etɔ̃ loo, alo dɔvɔ̃ neva wò anyigba dzi ŋkeke etɔ̃a? Azɔ bu eŋu, ne nakpɔ nyaa ɖe maɖagblɔ na amesi dɔm ɖa!

english_verse: David was really frightened and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ na Gad bena: Mexaxa ŋutɔ! Na miadze Yehowa si me, elabena eƒe amenuveve sɔ gbɔ, ke nyemele amegbetɔwo si me dze ge o!

english_verse: So that morning, the Lord sent an angel to spread a horrible disease everywhere in Israel, from Dan to Beersheba. And before it was over,
translation_verse: Esi mawudɔla la do eƒe asi ɖe Yerusalem dzi, be yeagblẽe la, vɔ̃ la ve Yehowa, eye wògblɔ na mawudɔla, si le nu gblẽm le dukɔa dome la bena: Esɔ gbɔ! Azɔ ɖiɖi wò asi ɖe anyi! Eve Yehowa ƒe dɔla la le Yebusitɔ Arawna ƒe lugbɔƒe gbɔ.

english_verse: Araunah said, “Take whatever you want and offer your sacrifice. Here are some oxen for the sacrifice. You can use the threshing-boards and the wooden yokes for the fire.
translation_verse: Arawna gblɔ na Dawid bena: Nye aƒetɔ fia nexɔe, eye wòasa vɔ, alesi dze eŋu! Kpɔ ɖa, nyiwo nye esi hena numevɔsa, eye luƒotasiaɖam kple nyiawo ŋutinuwo nanye nake!

english_verse: That same day the prophet Gad came and told David, “Go to the threshing place that belongs to Araunah and build an altar there for the Lord.” So David went.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid yi le Gad ƒe nya la nu, abe alesi Yehowa de se ene.

english_verse: Take them—they're yours! I hope the Lord your God will be pleased with you.”
translation_verse: Nusiawo katã wò dɔla Arawna tsɔ na eƒe aƒetɔ fia la. Eye Arawna gblɔ na fia la bena: Yehowa, wò Mawu, axɔe na wò nyuie!

english_verse: But David answered, “No! I have to pay you what they're worth. I can't offer the Lord my God a sacrifice that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing place and the oxen for
translation_verse: Ke fia la gblɔ na Arawna bena: Kpao, ke boŋ maƒlee le asiwò kple ga, eye nyemasa numevɔ na Yehowa, nye Mawu la, dzodzro o. Ale Dawid ƒle lugbɔƒe kple nyiawo klosalo sekel blaatɔ̃.

english_verse: Then he built an altar for the Lord. He offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. The Lord answered the prayers of the people, and no one else died from the terrible disease.
