He will take them out of the land he gave to their ancestors, then scatter them as far away as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Yehowa asi Israel, eye woaʋuʋu, abe alesi aƒla ʋuʋuna le tɔ me ene, eve woaɖe Israel ɖa le anyigba nyui sia, si wotsɔ na wo fofowo la dzi, eye wòaka wo ahlẽ ɖe tɔsisi la godo, elabena wowɔ Aserawo hetsɔ do dziku na Yehowa.

english_verse: years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon.
translation_verse: Tete Yerobeam srɔ̃ tso hedze mɔ yi Tirza. Eye esi wòɖo xɔ la ƒe kpui nu la, ŋutsuvi la ku.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel came and mourned at his funeral, just as the Lord's servant Ahijah had said. Jeroboam Dies
translation_verse: Eye woɖii, eye Israel blibo la fa nɛ, le Yehowa ƒe nya, si wògblɔ to eƒe dɔla nyagblɔɖila Axiya dzi la nu.

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including the battles he won, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Yerobeam ŋutinya susɔea, aʋa, siwo wòwɔ kple alesi woɖu fiae la, kpɔ ɖa, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: The people of Judah disobeyed the Lord and made him even angrier than their ancestors had.
translation_verse: Eye Yuda wɔ nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me, eye wotsɔ woƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wowɔ la, ɖo dziku nɛ wu nusiwo katã wo fofowo wɔ.

english_verse: They also built their own local shrines and stone images of foreign gods, and they set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Elabena woawo hã wɔ nuxeƒewo, aƒeliwo kple Aserawo ɖe togbɛ kɔkɔwo katã dzi kple ati damawo katã te.

english_verse: Even worse, they allowed prostitutes at the shrines, and followed the disgusting customs of the foreign nations that the Lord had forced out of Canaan.
translation_verse: Matrewɔlawo hã le anyigba la dzi, eye wokpɔ dukɔ, siwo Yehowa nyã le Israel-viwo ŋku me la, ƒe ŋunyɔnuwo katã wɔ.

english_verse: After Rehoboam had been king for four years, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me le Rexabeam ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒe atɔ̃lia me bena: Egipte-fia Sisak ho va ɖe Yerusalem ŋu,

english_verse: He took everything of value from the temple and the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
translation_verse: eye wòlɔ Yehowa ƒe aƒe ƒe kesinɔnuwo kple fia ƒe aƒe ƒe kesinɔnuwo dzoe, wo katãe wòlɔ dzoe hekpe ɖe sikakpoxɔnu, siwo katã Salomo wɔ la ŋu.

english_verse: Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe.
translation_verse: Ke fia Rexabeam wɔ akɔblikpoxɔnuwo ɖe wo teƒe, eye wotsɔ wo de fia ŋu asrafo, siwo dzɔa fia ƒe aƒe ƒe ʋɔtru nu la, ƒe amegãwo si.

english_verse: Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he was finished.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, ne fia la yina ɖe Yehowa ƒe aƒe me la, fia ŋu asrafoawo tsɔa wo, eye wogagbugbɔa wo va dana ɖe fia ŋu asrafoawo ƒe xɔ me.

english_verse: Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Rexabeam ŋutinya susɔea kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Yuda-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: He and Jeroboam were constantly at war.
translation_verse: Eye aʋa nɔ Rexabeam kple Yerobeam dome ŋkekeawo katã.

english_verse: Rehoboam's mother Naamah was from Ammon, but when Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Abijam then became king.
translation_verse: Eye Rexabeam mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ, eye woɖu ɖe fofoawo gbɔ le Dawid ƒe du la me. Dadaa ŋkɔ nye Naama, Amoni-nyɔnu, eye via Abiyam ɖu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: His own grandmother Maacah had made an idol of Asherah, and Asa took it and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
translation_verse: Eɖe dadaa Maaxa hã ɖa, be magaɖu dzi o, elabena ewo legba na Asera, eye Asa mũ legba la ɖatɔ dzoe ɖe Kidron-bali la me.

english_verse: Abijam became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel,
translation_verse: Le Yerobeam, Nebat vi, ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒe wuienyilia me la Abiyam zu fia ɖe Yuda dzi.

english_verse: Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to strengthen the town of Ramah. Then he used these same stones and wood to fortify the town of Geba in the territory of Benjamin and the town of Mizpah.
translation_verse: Eye fia Asa na woyɔ Yuda blibo la, wo dometɔa ɖeke meto le eme o, eye woyi ɖafɔ kpe kple ati, siwo Baesa tso le Rama tsomi la, eye fia Asa tso wo tso Geba le Benyamin kple Mizpa.

english_verse: Abijam did not truly obey the Lord his God as his ancestor David had done. Instead, he was sinful just like his father Rehoboam.
translation_verse: Eye wòzɔ le fofoa ƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo katã wòwɔ le eŋgɔ la me, eye eƒe dzi menɔ Yehowa, eƒe Mawu la ŋu blibo abe fofoa Dawid ƒe dzi ene o.

english_verse: David had always obeyed the Lord's commands by doing right, except in the case of Uriah. And since Abijam was David's great-grandson, the Lord kept Jerusalem safe and let Abijam have a son who would be the next king.
translation_verse: elabena Dawid wɔ nusi nyo le Yehowa ŋku me, eye mete ɖa le se, siwo katã wòɖe nɛ la me le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me o, negbe ɖe Uriya, Xititɔ la ƒe nya me koe.

english_verse: The war that had broken out between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continued during the time that Abijam was king. Everything else Abijam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Abiyam ŋutinya susɔeawo kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Yuda-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me. Eye aʋa nɔ Abiyam kple Yerobeam dome.

english_verse: Abijam died and was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Asa became king. King Asa of Judah (
translation_verse: Eye Abiyam mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ, eye woɖii ɖe Dawid ƒe du la me, eye via Asa zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Asa

english_verse: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Eye wòtsɔ fofoa ƒe nu kɔkɔewo kple eya ŋutɔ ƒe nu kɔkɔewo, siwo nye klosalo, sika kple ŋudɔwɔnuawo, yi Yehowa ƒe mee.

english_verse: Asa was always at war with King Baasha of Israel.
translation_verse: Eye aʋa no Asa kple Israel-fia Baesa dome le woƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: Asa obeyed the Lord, as David had done.
translation_verse: Asa wɔ nusi nyo le Yehowa ŋku me abe fofoa Dawid ene.

english_verse: Asa became king of Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's rule in Israel,
translation_verse: Le Israel-fia Yerobeam ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒe blavelia me la Asa zu fia ɖe Yuda dzi.

english_verse: He forced the prostitutes at the shrines to leave the country, and he got rid of the idols his ancestors had made.
translation_verse: Enyã matrewɔlawo ɖa le anyigba la dzi, eye wòɖe legba, siwo fofoa wɔ la ɖa.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was completely faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines.
translation_verse: Ke womeɖe nuxeƒewo ɖa o; gake Asa ƒe dzi nɔ Yehowa ŋu blibo le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
translation_verse: Esi Israel-fia Baesa ho ɖe Yuda ŋu la, etso Rama, ne wòaxe mɔ, be Yuda-fia Asa ƒe amea ɖeke magaɖo alo agbɔ o.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Tete Asa tsɔ klosalo kple sika, siwo katã kpɔtɔ ɖe Yehowa ƒe aƒe ƒe nudzraɖoƒe kple fia ƒe aƒe ƒe nudzraɖoƒe la, de eƒe dɔlawo si; eye fia Asa dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Aram-fia Ben-Hadad, si enye Xesion vi Tabrimon ƒe vi, amesi le Damasko la gbɔ be, woagblɔ nɛ bena:

english_verse: “Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
translation_verse: Nubabla le mía kpli wò dome, le fofonye kple fofowò dome, kpɔ ɖa, mele nunana, si enye klosalo kple sika la, ɖom ɖe wò. Ne ètu nubabla, si le mia kple Israel-fia Baesa dome la, ekema aho adzo le gbɔnye.

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, and Abel-Bethmaacah, and the territories of Chinneroth and Naphtali.
translation_verse: Tete Ben-Hadad ɖo to fia Asa ƒe gbe, eye wòdo eƒe aʋafia ɖo ɖe Israel-duwo me, eye wòsi Iyon, Dan, Abel-Bet-Maaxa kple Kinerot blibo la hekpe ɖe Naftali-nyigba blibo la ŋu.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, esime Baesa see la, edzudzɔ Rama tsotso, eye woɖana Tirza.

english_verse: Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease.
translation_verse: Ke Asa ŋutinya susɔeawo katã kple eƒe kalẽwɔwɔwo katã, nusiwo katã wòwɔ kple du, siwo wotso la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Yuda-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me; negbe le eƒe amegãkuku me ko wòdze dɔ ɖe afɔ.

english_verse: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years.
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Asa ƒe ƒe evelia me la Yerobeam vi Nadab zu fia ɖe Israel dzi, eye woɖu fia ɖe Israel dzi ƒe eve.

english_verse: Nadab disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of his father, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nusi nye vɔ le Yehowa ŋku me, eye wòto fofoa ƒe ʋe me hewɔ eƒe nuvɔ̃, si wòtsɔ ble Israel ɖe nuvɔ̃ me la.

english_verse: The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family,
translation_verse: Esi wòle fia ɖum la, etsrɔ̃ Yerobeam ƒe aƒe blibo la, eye mena nu gbagbea ɖeke kpɔtɔ na Yerobeam o, ke boŋ etsrɔ̃ wo keŋ le Yehowa ƒe nya, si wògblɔ to eƒe dɔla Axiya, Silotɔ dzi la nu;

english_verse: because Jeroboam had made the Lord God of Israel angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: le Yerobeam ƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wòwɔ hetsɔ ble Israel ɖe nuvɔ̃ me, kple nusiwo wòwɔ hetsɔ do dziku na Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la ta.

english_verse: Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Nadab ŋutinya susɔeawo kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war. King Baasha of Israel
translation_verse: Eye aʋa nɔ Asa kple Israel-fia Baesa dome le woƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Asa ƒe ƒe etɔ̃lia me la Axiya vi Baesa zu fia ɖe Israel blibo la dzi le Tirza ƒe blave vɔ ene.

english_verse: Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Eye wòwɔ nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me, eto Yerobeam ƒe ʋe me, eye wòwɔ eƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wòtsɔ ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me.

english_verse: The Lord sent Jehu son of Hanani to say to Baasha:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va Xanani vi Yehu gbɔ na Baesa bena:

english_verse: Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry
translation_verse: Esi meɖe wò le ke me, eye metsɔ wò ɖo fia ɖe nye dukɔ Israel nu, gake nèto Yerobeam ƒe ʋe me, eve nèble nye dukɔ Israel ɖe nuvɔ̃ me, be wotsɔ woƒe nuvɔ̃wo do dziku nam la,

english_verse: that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam.
translation_verse: eyata kpɔ ɖa, matsɔ xa akplɔ Baesa kple eƒe aƒe, eye mawo eƒe aƒe abe Yerobeam, Nebat vi ƒe aƒe ene.

english_verse: Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Baesa ƒe ame, si ke ku ɖe du me la, avũwo aɖui, eye eƒe amesi ke ku ɖe gbe me la, dziƒoxewo aɖui.

english_verse: Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family! Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king. King Elah of Israel
translation_verse: Eve Yehowa ƒe nya gava Xanani vi nyagblɔɖila Yehu gbɔ na Baesa kple eƒe aƒe le nu vɔ̃ɖi, siwo katã wòwɔ le Yehowa ŋku me kple eƒe asinudɔwɔwɔ, siwo wòtsɔ do dziku ne la ta, ne woazu abe Yerobeam ƒe aƒe ene, elabena eya tsrɔ̃e. Ela kple Zimri.

english_verse: Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel after Asa had been king of Judah for
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Asa ƒe ƒe blave vɔ adelia me la Baesa vi Ela zu fia ɖe Israel dzi le Tirza ƒe eve.

english_verse: Omri did more evil things than any king before him.
translation_verse: Eye Omri wo nusi nye vɔ le Yehowa ŋku me, ewɔ nu gbegblẽ wu amesiwo katã nɔ ŋgɔ nɛ la.

english_verse: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah. One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister,
translation_verse: Tete eƒe ɖɔla Zimri, si nye tasiaɖamwo ƒe afã ƒe amegã la, ɖo gbe ɖi ɖe eŋu, esime wono aha mũ le Arza, si nye aƒedzikpɔla le Tirza la ƒe me

english_verse: when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Eye Zimri va ƒoe wu le Yuda-fia Asa ƒe ƒe blave vɔ adrelia me, eye wòzu ba ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed.
translation_verse: Esime wòle fia ɖum, eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ fiazikpuia dzi la, etsrɔ̃ Baesa ƒe aƒe blibo la, eye mena eƒe ŋutsuwo, ƒometɔwo kple xɔlɔ̃wo dometɔa ɖeke kpɔtɔ o.

english_verse: Baasha's family was completely wiped out, just as the Lord's prophet Jehu had warned.
translation_verse: Eye Zimri tsrɔ̃ Baesa ƒe aƒe blibo la le Yehowa ƒe nya, si wògblɔ ɖe Baesa ŋu to nyagblɔɖila Yehu dzi la nu;

english_verse: Baasha and Elah sinned and caused the Israelites to sin, and they made the Lord angry by worshiping idols.
translation_verse: le Baesa kple via Ela ƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo katã wowɔ hetsɔ ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me, eye wotsɔ woƒe yakanuwo do dziku na Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la ta.

english_verse: Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Zimri of Israel
translation_verse: Ela ŋutinya susɔea kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah. Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day.
translation_verse: Esi dukɔ la se le asaɖa me be, Zimri ɖo gbe ɖi, eye wowu fia la hã la, Israel blibo la tsɔ aʋafia Omri ɖo fia ɖe Israel dzi gbemagbe le asaɖa la me.

english_verse: At once, Omri and his army marched to Tirzah and attacked.
translation_verse: Tete Omri kple Israel blibo la dzo le Gibeton ŋu, eye wova ɖe to ɖe Tirza.

english_verse: When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire.
translation_verse: Esi Zimri kpɔ bena, woxɔ dua la, eyi ɖe fia ƒe aƒe ƒe mɔ̃ me, eye wòtɔ dzo fia ƒe xɔ la ɖe eɖokui dzi, eye woku

english_verse: Zimri had disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: le eƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wòwɔ la ta; elabena ewɔ nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me, eye wòto Yerobeam ƒe ʋe me wɔ eƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wòwɔ hetsɔ ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me la.

english_verse: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
translation_verse: Zimri ŋutinya susɔea kple nugbe, siwo wòɖo la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi Israel-dukɔ la ma ɖe akpa eve me; dukɔ la ƒe akpa ɖeka ku ɖe Tibni, Ginat vi ŋu, be woatsɔe aɖo fiae, eye akpa evelia ku ɖe Omri ŋu.

english_verse: in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah. Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah,
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Asa ƒe ƒe blaetɔ̃ ɖekɛlia me la Omri zu fia, eye woɖu Israel dzi ƒe wuieve; eɖu fia le Tirza ƒe ade.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
translation_verse: Eto Yerobeam, Nebat vi la ƒe ʋe me pɛpɛpɛ, eye wòwɔ eƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wotsɔ ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me, be wotsɔ woƒe yakanuwo do dziku na Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la.

english_verse: Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Omri ŋutinya susɔea, nusiwo wòwɔ kple eƒe katã, si wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king. King Ahab of Israel
translation_verse: Eye Omri mia fofoawo gbɔ, eye woɖii ɖe Samaria, eye via Axab zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Asa ƒe ƒe blaetɔ̃ vɔ enyilia me la Axab, Omri vi, zu fia ɖe Israel dzi, eye Axab. Omri vi, du fia ɖe Israel dzi le Samaria ƒe blave vɔ eve.

english_verse: Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him.
translation_verse: Eye Axab, Omri vi, wɔ nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me wu amesiwo katã nɔ ŋgɔ nɛ.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Esi wòwɔ Yerobeam, Nebat vi ƒe nuvɔ̃wo la, nu tsɛ ko wònye ne; eye wòɖe Zidon-fia Etbaal ƒe vinyonu Izebed, eye wòyi ɖasubɔ Baal hede ta agu nɛ.

english_verse: Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria
translation_verse: Eye wòɖi vɔsamlekpui na Baal ɖe Baal ƒe xɔ, si wòtu ɖe Samaria la me.

english_verse: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
translation_verse: Axab wɔ Asera hã. Eye Axab wɔ nu geɖe hetso do dziku na Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, wu Israel-fia, siwo katã nɔ ŋgɔ nɛ.

english_verse: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_verse: Eŋɔli Beteltɔ Xiel tso Yerixo; eƒe ŋgɔgbevi Abiram ƒe ku wotso ɖo egɔme anyi, eye eƒe dɔmlɔea Segub ƒe ku wotso de agbowo enu, le Yehowa ƒe nya, si wògblɔ to Yosua, Nun vi la dzi la nu.

english_verse: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
translation_verse: Eye Eliya, Tisbitɔ, si tso Gilead ƒe amedzrowo dome, gblɔ na Axab bena: Meta Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, amesi ŋku me mele tsitre ɖo la ƒe agbe. Zãmu kple tsi madza le ƒe siawo me o, negbe nye koe agblɔe hafi!

english_verse: Later, the Lord said to Elijah,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va egbɔ bena:

english_verse: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: Dzo le afisia, eye natrɔ ayi ɣedzeƒe gome aɖaɣla ɖokuiwò ɖe Krit-tɔʋu, si dze ŋgɔ Yordan la to.

english_verse: You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
translation_verse: Nano tɔʋu la me tsi, eye mede se na akpaviãwo be, woanyi wò le afima.

english_verse: Elijah obeyed the Lord and went to live near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: Tete wòyi dawo, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ ene; eyi ɖanɔ Krit-tɔʋu, si dze ŋgɔ Yordan la to.

english_verse: Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek.
translation_verse: Akpaviãwo tsoa abolo kple lã vanae nɛ le ŋdi, eye wotsoa abolo kple lã vanae ne le fiẽ, eye wonoa tɔʋu la me tsi.

english_verse: But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain. Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
translation_verse: Ke le ŋkekea ɖewo megbe la tɔʋu la mie, elabena tsia ɖeke megale dzadzam le anyigba la dzi o.

english_verse: The Lord told Elijah,
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ƒe gbe va egbɔ bena:

english_verse: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
translation_verse: Tso, nayi Zarpat, si nye Zidontɔwo tɔ, eye natsi afima; kpo ɖa, meɖe se na ahosia ɖe le afima, be wòanyi wò.

english_verse: When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked.
translation_verse: Eye wòdze mo heyi Zarpat. Esi wòva dua ƒe agbo nu la, ahosia ɖe le afima le nake fɔm, eye wòyɔe gblɔ bena: Taflatse, ku tsi ɖe nane me vɛ nam mano.

english_verse: As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
translation_verse: Esi wòyina eku ge la, eyɔe ɖagblɔ bena: Taflatse, ɖi abolo kakɛa ɖe ɖe asi vɛ nam.

english_verse: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Meta Yehowa, wò Mawu ƒe agbe: Ne aboloa ɖe le asinye fĩ! Negbe wɔ asiʋlo ɖeka koe le ze me kple ami via ɖe le goe me, eye kpɔ ɖa, meva nake wuwlui fɔ ge, be mayi aɖaɖae, ne mía kple vinyeŋutsu miaɖu, hafi míaku.

english_verse: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
translation_verse: Tele Eliya ɖo ŋu na bena: Megavɔ̃ o! Yi nawɔ, abe alesi negblɔ ene; ke tsɔ ɖe tɔ tatali via ɖe nam gbɔ, eye natsɔe vɛ nam, emegbe hafi nawɔ mia kple viwò lɔ.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
translation_verse: Elabena ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Wɔze la maɖi gbolo o, eye ami, si le goea me la, mavɔ o, vaseɖe esime Yehowa nana tsi nagadza ɖe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
translation_verse: Eye wòyi ɖawɔ, abe alesi Eliya gblɔ ene, eye woa kplii kpakple viaŋutsu woɖui eteƒe didi.

english_verse: The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil. Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
translation_verse: Wɔze la meɖi gbɔlo o, eye ami, si le goea me la, meva o, la Yehowa ƒe nya, si wògblɔ to Eliya dzi la nu.

english_verse: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me le nya siawo megbe bena, aƒeanɔ ƒe vi dze dɔ, eye eƒe dɔ la nu sẽ ɖe dzi, ale be megate ŋu le gbɔgbɔm o.

english_verse: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ na Eliya bena: Mawu ƒe ame! Nya ka le mia kpli wò dome? Ɖe nèva gbɔnye, be naɖo ŋku nye nuvɔ̃wo dzi, eye nawu vinyea?

english_verse: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu ne bena: Tsa viwò la nam! Eye wòxɔe le eƒe akɔnu tso yi xɔtaxɔe, si me wòle la me, eye wòtsɔe mlɔ eƒe aba dzi.

english_verse: and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.”
translation_verse: Eye wòyɔ Yehowa gblɔ bena: Yehowa, nye Mawu, ahosi, si gbɔ menye amedzro le, hã ŋue nèbe, yeawo vɔ̃ do, eye nawu via?

english_verse: Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
translation_verse: Tete wòdra ɖe ɖevi la dzi zi etɔ̃ heyɔ Yehowa gblɔ bena: Yehowa, nye Mawu, gbugbɔ ɖevi sia ƒe luʋɔ gava emee dzro!

english_verse: The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again.
translation_verse: Yehowa se Eliya ƒe gbe, eye ɖevi la ƒe luʋɔ gagbugbɔ va eme, eye wògbɔ agbe.

english_verse: Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
translation_verse: Eye Eliya tsɔ ɖevi la ɖi tso xɔtaxɔ la me va xɔa me, eye wòtsɔe na dadaa. Eye Eliya gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, viwò la tsi agbe.

english_verse: “You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_verse: Tete nyɔnu la gblɔ na Eliya bena: Azɔ medze sii bena, Mawu ƒe amee nènye, eye Yehowa ƒe gbe, si le nuwò la, nye nyateƒe.

english_verse: At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid
translation_verse: Esi Izebel tsrɔ̃ Yehowa ƒe nyagblɔɖilawo la, Obadya kplɔ nyagblɔɖila alafa ɖeka ɖaɣla ɖe agado me blaatɔ̃blaatɔ̃, eye wòtsɔ abolo kple tsi nyi wòe.

english_verse: and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass.
translation_verse: Eye Axab gblɔ na Obadya bena: Yi ɖatsa le anyigba dzi le tsidzɔƒewo katã kple tɔʋuwo katã ŋu, ɖewohĩ míakpɔ gbe axɔ sɔwo kple tedzisɔwo ɖe agbe, be lãwo magatsrɔ̃ na mi o.

english_verse: You go one way, and I'll go the other.” Then they left in separate directions.
translation_verse: Tete wòmã anyigba la, be woatsa le edzi; Axab ɖeɖe lé mɔ, eye Obadya hã ɖeɖe lé mɔ.

english_verse: As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”
translation_verse: Esi Obadya le mɔ dzi la, kpɔ ɖa, Eliya va do goe, eye esi wòdze sii la, etsyɔ mo anyi gblɔ bena: Wòea, nye aƒetɔ Eliya?

english_verse: Obadiah replied: King Ahab would kill me if I told him that. And I haven't even done anything wrong.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Nuvɔ̃ ka mewɔ, hafi nèbe, yeatsɔ wò dɔla ade asi na Axab, ne wòawu?

english_verse: I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country.
translation_verse: Meta Yehowa, wò Mawu ƒe agbe. Dukɔ alo fiaɖuƒea ɖeke meli, afisi nye aƒetɔ medɔ ame ɖo, be woadi wò le o; eye ne wogblɔ be, mele afi o la, ekema enana fiaɖuƒe la kple dukɔ la ka atam nɛ be, womekpɔ wò o.

english_verse: Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
translation_verse: Eye azɔ nele gbɔgblɔm be: Yi ɖagblɔe na wò aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, Eliya le afia?

english_verse: What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me. I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy.
translation_verse: Eye wòava me be, ne medzo le gbɔwò la, Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ akplɔ wò adzoe ayi afisi nyemenya o. Eye ne meva gblɔe na Axab, eye mekpɔ wò o la, ekema awum; evɔ wònye wò dɔla vɔ̃a Yehowa tso eƒe ɖevime ke hafi.

english_verse: Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”
translation_verse: Eliya ɖo ŋu bena: Meta Yehowa Zebaot, amesi ŋku me mele tsitre ɖo ƒe agbe. Ne nyematsɔ ɖokuinye afiae egbea o fi!

english_verse: Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah. Ahab went to meet Elijah,
translation_verse: Tete Obadya yi ɖakpe Axab, eye wògblɔe nɛ; eye Axab yi ɖakpe Eliya.

english_verse: and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
translation_verse: Esi Axab kpo Eliya la, Axab gblɔ nɛ bena: Wò, amesi he gbegblẽ va Israel dzi la, enye esia?

english_verse: Elijah answered: You're the troublemaker—not me! You and your family have disobeyed the Lord's commands by worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Menye nyee he gbegblẽ va Israel dzi o, ke boŋ mia kple fofowò ƒe aƒee, elabena mieɖe asi le Yehowa ƒe seawo ŋu, eye mèdze Baalwo yome.

english_verse: Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel.
translation_verse: Eye Axab do ame ɖo ɖe Israel-viwo katã, eye wòƒo nyagblɔɖilawo nu ƒu ɖe Karmel-to la gbɔ. Eliya kple Baal ƒe nunɔlawo.

english_verse: Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!” The people did not say a word.
translation_verse: Tete Eliya te ɖe dukɔ la ŋku me gblɔ bena: Vaseɖe ɣekaɣi miaɖu adza evee ase ɖo? Nenye Yehowae nye Mawu la, midze eyome, eye nenye Baal ye la, midze eyome! Ke dukɔ la meɖo nyaa ɖeke ŋu nɛ o.

english_verse: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
translation_verse: Eyata ne woatso nyitsu eve na mí, eye woawo natsɔ nyitsu ɖeka aflii ahaɖo nake dzi, ke womaɖe dzo ade ete o; eye nye hã maɖi nyitsu ɖeka atsa aɖo nake dzi, eye nyemaɖe dzo ade ete o.

english_verse: The prophets of Baal will pray to their god, and I will pray to the Lord. The one who answers by starting the fire is God. “That's a good idea,” everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Emegbe miayɔ miaƒe mawu ŋkɔ, eye nye hã mayɔ Yehowa ŋku, eye wòava me be, mawu, si atso dzo atɔe la, eyae nye Mawu. Tete dukɔ blibo la do ɣli gblɔ bena: Gbe la medze vɔ o.

english_verse: Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”
translation_verse: Eye Eliya gblɔ na Baal ƒe nyagblɔɖilawo bena: Mitia nyitsu ɖeka, eye mitre ewɔwɔ, elabena miesɔ gbɔ, eye miyɔ miaƒe mawu ŋkɔ, ke migaɖe dzo de ete o.

english_verse: They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
translation_verse: Eye wòlé nyitsu, si wotsɔ na wo la, hewɔe, eye woyɔ Baal ŋkɔ vaseɖe ɣeɖota le gbɔgblɔm bena: Baal, tɔ na mi! Ke gbea ɖeke meɖi o, eye amea ɖeke metɔ o. Eye wole kpo tim le xlã ƒom vɔsamlekpui, si wowɔ la.

english_verse: At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
translation_verse: Eye wòva me le ɣeɖota be, Eliya ɖe alɔme le wo ŋu gblɔ bena: Miɖo ɣli sesĩe ko, elabena mawue, ɖewohĩ ele ŋugble dem, eɖe kpɔ, alo eyi nugbe, alo ele alɔ dɔm, ne wòanya.

english_verse: The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped,
translation_verse: Tete wodo ɣli sesĩe, eye wotsɔ yi kple akplɔ de abi wo ɖokuiwò ŋu le woƒe kɔnu la nu, vaseɖe esime ʋu do le wo ŋu.

english_verse: and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
translation_verse: Eye esi ɣetrɔ ɖo la, wode asi nugbenugbee wɔwɔ me vaseɖe ɣeyiɣi, si wosaa nuɖuvɔ; ke gbea ɖeke meɖi o, amea ɖeke metɔ o, eye amea ɖeke meɖo to o.

english_verse: Elijah told everyone to gather around him while he repaired the Lord's altar.
translation_verse: Azɔ Eliya gblɔna dukɔ blibo la bena: Mile va gbɔnye. Esi dukɔ blibo la te ɖe eŋu la, eɖɔ Yehowa ƒe vɔsamlekpui, si wogbã la ɖo.

english_verse: Then he used twelve stones to build an altar in honor of the Lord. Each stone stood for one of the tribes of Israel, which was the name the Lord had given to their ancestor Jacob. Elijah dug a ditch around the altar, large enough to hold about
translation_verse: Etsɔ kpeawo ɖi vɔsamlekpui le Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ me, eye wòɖe ne ƒo xlã vɔsamlekpui la kpe ɖo, ale be woate ŋu aƒa lu dzidzenu eve ɖe wo domee.

english_verse: until finally, the water ran down the altar and filled the ditch.
translation_verse: Eye tsi la gbagba ɖe vɔsamlekpui la dzi, eye woɖu tsi ɖe ʋe la hã me wòyɔ taŋ.

english_verse: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah prayed: Our Lord, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Now, prove that you are the God of this nation, and that I, your servant, have done this at your command.
translation_verse: Esime nuɖuvɔsaɣi ɖo la, nyagblɔɖila Eliya te va hegblɔ bena: Yehowa, Abraham kple Isak kpakple Israel ƒe Mawu, egbe nana woanyae be, wòe nye Mawu le Israel, eye menye wò dɔla, eye be mewo nusiawo katã le wò nya nu.

english_verse: Please answer me, so these people will know that you are the Lord God, and that you will turn their hearts back to you.
translation_verse: Tɔ nam, Yehowa, tɔ nam, ne dukɔ sia nadze sii be, wò Yehowa enye Mawu, eye wòe agatrɔ woƒe dziwo!

english_verse: The Lord immediately sent fire, and it burned up the sacrifice, the wood, and the stones. It scorched the ground everywhere around the altar and dried up every drop of water in the ditch.
translation_verse: Tete dzo tso Yehowa gbɔ va fiã vɔsalã la, nakeawo, kpeawo kple anyigba, eye wòɖuɖɔ tsi, si le ʋea me hã keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: When the crowd saw what had happened, they all bowed down and shouted, “The Lord is God! The Lord is God!”
translation_verse: Eye esi dukɔ blibo la kpɔe la, wotsyɔ mo anyi hedo ɣli gblɔ bena: Yehowae nye Mawu, Yehowae nye Mawu!

english_verse: Just then, Elijah said, “Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let any of them get away.” So the people captured the prophets and took them to Kishon River, where Elijah killed every one of them. It Starts To Rain
translation_verse: Eye Eliya gblɔ na wo bena: Milé Baal ƒe nyagblɔɖilawo, wo dometɔa ɖeke megasi o! Eye wòlé wo. Tete Eliya kplɔ wo yi Kison-tɔʋu la nu, eye wowu wo ɖe afima.

english_verse: Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
translation_verse: Emegbe Eliya gblɔ na Axab bena: Yi naɖu nu, eye nano nu, elabena mese tsidzadza ƒe nuwɔwɔ.

english_verse: Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground
translation_verse: Tete Axab yi, be yeaɖu, eye yeano nu. Ke Eliya yi Karmel-to la ta me, eye wonɔ klotinu ɖe anyigba hetsɔ mo de ata me.

english_verse: and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.” The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na eƒe ɖekakpui bena: Lia to la, eye nakpɔ ƒu gome ɖa! Eye wòyi ɖakpɔe ɖa hegblɔ bena: Naneke meli o. Eɖo ŋu bena: Yi zi gbɔ zi adre.

english_verse: After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.” Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
translation_verse: Esi wòyi zi adrelia la, egblɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, alilikpovia ɖe le abe ame ƒe asi ene, tso ƒu gome gbɔna. Eye wògblɔ be: Yi ɖagblɔ na Axab bena: Tsi lãwo ɖe tasiaɖam ŋu, eye nadzo, ne tsi megasika wò ɖi o.

english_verse: Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done and that he had killed the prophets.
translation_verse: Axab va to nusiwo katã Eliya wo kple alesi wòtsɔ yi wu nyagblɔɖilawo katãe la, na Izebel.

english_verse: She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Tete Izebel da ame ɖo ɖe Eliya be, wòagblɔ nɛ bena: Mawuwo afiam agafiam ɖe dzi, ne nyemewɔ wò agbe etsɔ wɔle siawo abe wo dometɔ ɖeka ƒe agbe ene o fi!

english_verse: Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there,
translation_verse: Tete wòvɔ̃, eye wòtso dze mo yi Beer-Seba, si nye Yuda to la, le eƒe agbe ta, eye wògblẽ eƒe ɖekakpui ɖe afima.

english_verse: then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.”
translation_verse: Eye wòzɔ ŋkeke ɖeka ƒe azɔli yi gbedzi heva bɔbɔ nɔ dzoŋgbalẽtia ɖe te, eye wòdi ku be, yeaku gblɔ bena: Esɔ gbɔ! Azɔ, Yehowa, xɔ nye luʋɔ, elabena nyemenye wu fofonyewo o.

english_verse: Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.”
translation_verse: Eye esi wòmlɔ anyi dɔ alɔ̃ ɖe dzoŋgbalẽtia te la, kpɔ ɖa, mawudɔlaa ɖe va ʋuʋui gblɔ ne bena: Fɔ naɖu nu!

english_verse: Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
translation_verse: Esi wòfɔ kɔ la, kpɔ ɖa, tatali tɔtɔe kple tsigoe le eƒe tade, eye woɖu nu no nu gamlɔ anyi.

english_verse: So Elijah sat up and ate and drank. The food and water made him strong enough to walk
translation_verse: Tete wòtsi tre ɖu nu no nu, eye nuɖuɖu sia do ŋusẽe wòzɔ ŋkeke blane kple zã blane vaseɖe Mawu ƒe to Xoreb gbɔ. Mawu ɖe eɖokui na Eliya le Xoreb to dzi.

english_verse: and he spent the night there in a cave. The Lord Appears to Elijah While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Afima wòyi ɖe agadoa ɖe me le ɖatsi afima dɔ. Eye kpɔ ɖa, Yehowa ƒe gbe va egbɔ hegblɔ nɛ bena: Eliya, nuka wɔm nèle le afisia?

english_verse: He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena. Ɖe meʋã ŋu ɖe Yehowa, aʋakɔwo ƒe Mawu la, nu, elabena Israel-viwo gblẽ wò nubabla ɖi, wogbã wò vɔsamlekpuiwo ƒu anyi, eye wowu wò nyagblɔɖilawo kple yi; ke nye ɖeka koe kpɔtɔ, eye wole nye agbe dim, be yewoaɖe ɖa.

english_verse: “Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.” All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Do go, nava tsi tre ɖe to la dzi le Yehowa ŋku me! Eye kpɔ ɖa, Yehowa va tso me yi; eye ya gã ʋuɖuʋuɖua ɖe ƒo, towo wo, eve agakpewo tu wɔ le Yehowa ŋku me, ke Yehowa mele ya la me o. Le va yome la anyigba ʋuʋu, ke Yehowa mele anyigbaʋuʋu la me o.

english_verse: Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. Finally, there was a gentle breeze,
translation_verse: Le anyigbaʋuʋu yome la dzo va, ke Yehowa mele dzo la me o. Le dzo yome la ya bɔbɔea ɖe ƒo miaa.

english_verse: and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave. A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Esime Eliya see la, etsɔ eƒe mo de eƒe awu ʋlaya me, eye wòdo go va tsi tre ɖe agado la nu, eye kpɔ ɖa, gbea ɖe va egbɔ gblɔ bena: Eliya, nuka wɔm nèle le afisia?

english_verse: Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Ɖe meʋã ŋu ɖe Yehowa, aʋakɔwo ƒe Mawu la nu, elabena Israel-viwo gblẽ wò nubabla ɖi, wogbã wò vɔsamlekpuiwo ƒu anyi, eye wowu wò nyagblɔɖilawo kple yi, ke nye ɖeka koe kpɔtɔ, eye wole nye agbe dim, be yewoaɖe ɖa.

english_verse: The Lord said: Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ nɛ bena: Trɔ gbugbɔ dze wò mo dzi ɖo ta Damasko-tagba, eye nayi aɖasi ami na Xazael, ne wòanye fia ɖe Aram dzi.

english_verse: Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
translation_verse: Si ami na Yehu, Nimsi vi, ne wòanye fia ɖe Israel dzi, eve si ami na Elisa, Safat vi, tso Abel-Mexola, ne wòanye nyagblɔɖila ɖe tewòƒe.

english_verse: Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
translation_verse: Eye wòava me be, amesi ke asi le Xazael ƒe yi nu la, Yehu nawui, eye amesi ke asi le Yehu ƒe yi nu la, Elisa nawui.

english_verse: Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
translation_verse: Esi wodzo le afima la, ekpa Elisa, Safat vi, tsa nyi eveve teƒe wuieve le agble ŋlɔmee, eye eva ŋuta le wuieveliawo ŋu; tete Eliya yi egbɔ, eve wòtsɔ eƒe awu ʋlaya ƒu gbe ɖee.

english_verse: Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said. “You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblẽ nyiawo ɖi fu du kplu Eliya ɖo gblɔ bena: Taflatse, na maɖagbugbɔ nu na fofonye kple danye, emegbe madze yowòme. Eɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Yi nagatrɔ agbɔ, elabena nuka mewɔ na wòa?

english_verse: Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_verse: Tete wò trɔ tso egbɔ ɖalé nyi eve hewu, eye wòtsɔ nyiawo ƒe ŋutinuwo heɖa lã lae na wo, eye wòtsɔe na ameawo woɖu. Emegbe wòtso dze Eliya yome, eye wòsubɔe.

english_verse: They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.” “Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”
translation_verse: Tete wosa akpanya ɖe ali, eye wosa ka ɖe ta heva fia la gbɔ gblɔ bena: Ale wò dɔla Ben-Hadad gblɔ esi: Taflatse, na matsi agbe! Eɖo ŋu bena: Egale agbea? Nɔvinyee wònye.

english_verse: Benhadad sent a messenger to tell King Ahab of Israel,
translation_verse: Eye wòdo amewo ɖo ɖe Israel-fia Axab gbɔ le dua me,

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Ahab replied, “everything I have is yours, including me.”
translation_verse: Israel-fia ɖo ŋu bena: Nye aƒetɔ fia, wòe ƒo nu! Mia kple nusianu, si le asinye la, tɔwo míenye.

english_verse: Later, Benhadad sent another messenger to say to Ahab, “I already told you to give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your children.
translation_verse: Tete dɔlawo gatrɔ gbɔ va gblɔ bena: Ale Ben-Hadad be, woagblɔ na wo enye si: Menya dɔ ame ɖo ɖe gbɔwò, ne woagblɔ na wò be, natsɔ wò klosalo kple sika, srɔwòwo kple viwòwo nam.

english_verse: But tomorrow at this time, I will send my officials into your city to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take everything else that you own.”
translation_verse: Ke etsɔ wole siawo la madɔ nye dɔlawo ɖe gbɔwò, ne woadzro wò aƒe kple wò dɔlawo ƒe aƒewo me, eye woatsɔ nusiwo katã dze wo ŋu la adzoe.

english_verse: “Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Ke amegãwo katã kple dukɔ blibo la ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Megaɖo toe o, eye megalɔ̃ edzi o!

english_verse: So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.” When Benhadad got his answer,
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na Ben-Hadad ƒe dɔlawo bena: Migblɔ na nye aƒetɔ fia be: Mawɔ nusiwo katã ŋuti nèdɔ ame ɖo ɖe wò dɔla gbɔ gbã la, ke nyemate ŋu awɔ nusia ya dzi o. Eye dɔlawo tsɔ ŋuɖoɖo la yi nɛ.

english_verse: he replied, “I'll completely destroy Samaria! There won't even be enough of it left for my soldiers to carry back in their hands. If I don't do it, I pray that the gods will punish me terribly.”
translation_verse: Tete Ben-Hadad dɔ ame ɖo ɖee, ne woagblɔ nɛ bena: Mawuwo afiam agafiam ɖe dzi, ne Samaria ƒe ke asɔ gbɔ ayɔ aʋakɔ, siwo katã kplɔm ɖo ƒe asiʋlo me fi!

english_verse: Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
translation_verse: Ke Israel-fia ɖo ŋu gblɔ bena: Miɖagblɔ be: Amesi ke bia ali dzi la, meƒoa adegbe o, negbe amesi ke tu ali dzi la ko!

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, esime eya kple fiawo le aha nom le agbadɔ me, eye wòse nya siawo la, egblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo bena: Midze aʋa! Tete wodze aʋa ɖe du la ŋu.

english_verse: At that very moment, a prophet ran up to Ahab and said, “You can see that Benhadad's army is very strong. But the Lord has promised to help you defeat them today. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Eye kpo ɖa, nyagblɔɖila ɖe va Israel-fia Axab gbɔ gblɔ bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Ele ameha gã geɖe sia kpɔma? Kpɔ ɖa, matsɔe ade asi na wò egbe, ne nadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa.

english_verse: “Who will fight the battle?” Ahab asked. The prophet answered, “The young bodyguards who serve the district officials.” “But who will lead them into battle?” Ahab asked. “You will!” the prophet replied.
translation_verse: Axab gblɔ be: Ameka dzi wòato? Eɖo ŋu be: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Ato anyigba dzikpɔlawo ƒe ɖeka kpuiwo dzi. Eye wògblɔ be: Ameka le aʋa la gɔme dze ge? Eɖo ŋu be: Wòe!

english_verse: At noon, King Ahab and his Israelite army marched out of Samaria, with the young soldiers in front. King Benhadad of Syria and the
translation_verse: Anyigba dzikpɔlawo ƒe ɖekakpuiawo tre hoho. Eye Ben-Hadad da ame ɖa, eye wòtrɔ va gblɔ nɛ bena: Samaria-ŋutsuwo ho aʋa.

english_verse: “Take them alive!” Benhadad ordered. “I don't care if they have come out to fight or to surrender.”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ bena: Nenye ŋutifafa ta woho ɖo la, milé wo agbagbe, eye nenye aʋa ta woho ɖo la, milé wo agbagbe!

english_verse: The young soldiers led Israel's troops into battle,
translation_verse: Ke esi anyigba dzikpɔlawo ƒe ɖekakpuiawo do le dua me la, aʋakɔ la dze wo yome;

english_verse: and each of them attacked and killed an enemy soldier. The rest of the Syrian army turned and ran, and the Israelites went after them. Benhadad and some others escaped on horses,
translation_verse: eye wo dome amesiame wu ame etɔxɛ. Tete Aramtɔwo si, eye Israel ti wo yome; ke Aram-fia Ben-Hadad do so hesi kple sɔdolawo.

english_verse: but Ahab and his soldiers followed them and captured their horses and chariots. Ahab and Israel's army crushed the Syrians.
translation_verse: Azɔ Israel-fia ho hetsrɔ̃ sɔwo kple tasiaɖamwo, eye wòsi Aramtɔwo ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Later, the prophet went back and warned Ahab, “Benhadad will attack you again next spring. Build up your troops and make sure you have some good plans.” Syria Attacks Israel Again
translation_verse: Tete nyagblɔɖila va Israel-fia gbɔ gblɔ nɛ bena: Yi nadzra ɖo, eye nabu ta me le nusi na wo ŋu; elabena ne ƒe trɔ la, Aram-fia gale hoho ge ɖe ŋuwò.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad's officials went to him and explained: Israel's gods are mountain gods. We fought Israel's army in the hills, and that's why they defeated us. But if we fight them on flat land, there's no way we can lose.
translation_verse: Eye Aram-fia ƒe dɔlawo gblɔ nɛ bena: Woƒe mawuwo la to dome mawuwo wonye, eyata wosẽ ŋu wu mí ɖo. Ke na míawɔ aʋa kpli wo le gbadzaƒe, abe míasẽ ŋu awu wo o ene.

english_verse: Here's what you should do. First, get rid of those
translation_verse: Ale nawɔ enye si: Ɖe fiawo ɖa le wo nɔƒe, eye natsɔ ɖu dzikpɔlawo aɖo wo teƒe.

english_verse: Then get more soldiers, horses, and chariots, so your army will be as strong as it was before. We'll fight Israel's army on flat land and wipe them out. Benhadad agreed and did what they suggested.
translation_verse: Eye ɖe aʋakɔ abe wò aʋakɔ, si tsrɔ̃ ene kple sɔwo abe sɔ kemeawo ene kpakple tasiaɖamwo abe tasiaɖam kemeawo ene, eye miawɔ aʋa kpli wo le gbadzaƒe, abe míasẽ ŋu awu wo o ene. Tete wòɖo to woƒe gbe hewɔ nenema.

english_verse: In the spring, Benhadad got his army together, and they marched to the town of Aphek to attack Israel.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, esi ƒe trɔ la, Ben-Hadad tia Aram xlẽ, eye woho va Afek, be yeawɔ aʋa kple Israel.

english_verse: The prophet went to Ahab and said, “The Syrians think the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys. So he has promised to help you defeat their powerful army. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Tete Mawu ƒe ame va gblɔ na Israel-fia bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esi Aramtɔwo be Yehowa enye to dome mawu, eye menye gbadzaƒe-mawu o la, eyata matsɔ ameha gã geɖe sia ade asi na wò, ne miadze su be, nyee nye Yehowa.

english_verse: For seven days the two armies stayed in their camps, facing each other. Then on the seventh day the fighting broke out, and before sunset the Israelites had killed
translation_verse: Eye woƒu asaɖa anyi dze ŋgɔ wo nɔewo ŋkeke adre. Le ŋkeke adreagbe la aʋa la fe ati, eye Israel-viwo wu ŋutsu afɔzɔla akpe alafa ɖeka le Aramtɔwo dome le ŋkeke ɖeka dzi.

english_verse: The rest of the Syrian army ran back to Aphek, but the town wall fell and crushed
translation_verse: Ke esi ame mlɔeawo si yi Afek-dua me la, gli mũ dze ame akpe blave vɔ adre, siwo kpɔtɔ la dzi; eye Ben-Hadad si yi dua me tso xɔ me yi xɔ me.

english_verse: His officials said, “Your Majesty, we've heard that Israel's kings keep their agreements. We will wrap sackcloth around our waists, put ropes around our heads, and ask Ahab to let you live.”
translation_verse: Tete eƒe dɔlawo gblɔ nɛ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, míese bena, Israel ƒe aƒe la ƒe fiawo la, fia veamenuwo wonye, eyata na míasa akpanya ɖe ali, eye míasa ka ɖe ta ahayi Israel-fia gbɔ; ɖewohĩ ana natsi agbe.

english_verse: Benhadad's officials were trying to figure out what Ahab was thinking, and when he said “brother,” they quickly replied, “You're right! You and Benhadad are like brothers.” “Go get him,” Ahab said. When Benhadad came out, Ahab had him climb up into his chariot.
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsuawo dze sii enumake be, nya nyuia ɖe le eme, eye wotso nya le enu kaba gblɔ bena: Nɔviwòe nye Ben-Hadad. Eɖo ŋu bena: Miyi ɖakplɔe vɛ! Eye esi wòdo va egbɔ la, ena wòɖo tasiaɖam me kplii.

english_verse: Benhadad said, “I'll give back the towns my father took from your father. And you can have shops in Damascus, just as my father had in Samaria.” Ahab replied, “If you do these things, I'll let you go free.” Then they signed a peace treaty, and Ahab let Benhadad go. A Prophet Condemns Ahab
translation_verse: Tete Ben-Hadad gblɔ nɛ bena: Magbugbɔ du, siwo fofonye xɔ le fofowò si la, na wò, eye nado mɔwo ɖe Damasko, abe alesi fofonye do wo ɖe Samaria ene; ke mía kpli wò míabla nu, hafi naɖe asi le ŋunye. Tete wòbia nu kplii heɖe asi le eŋu.

english_verse: About this time the Lord commanded a prophet to say to a friend, “Hit me!” But the friend refused,
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsua ɖe tso nyagblɔɖilaviwo dome gblɔ na ehavi le Yehowa ƒe nya nu bena: Taflatse, ƒom! Ke ŋutsu la gbe eƒoƒo.

english_verse: and the prophet told him, “You disobeyed the Lord, and as soon as you walk away, a lion will kill you.” The friend left, and suddenly a lion killed him.
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ ne bena: Esi meɖo to Yehowa ƒe gbe o la, eyata ne edzo le gbɔnye la, dzata awu wò. Eye esi wodzo le egbɔ la, dzata va do goe hewui.

english_verse: The prophet found someone else and said, “Hit me!” So this man beat him up.
translation_verse: Eye wòkpɔ ŋutsu bubu gblɔ bena: Taflatse, ƒom! Eye ŋutsu la ƒoe de abi eŋu.

english_verse: The prophet left and put a bandage over his face to disguise himself. Then he went and stood beside the road, waiting for Ahab to pass by.
translation_verse: Tete nyagblɔɖila la yi ɖatso mɔ na fia la, eye wòtsɔ nu bla ŋku, be amea ɖeke magadze si ye o.

english_verse: When Ahab went by, the prophet shouted, “Your Majesty, right in the heat of battle, someone brought a prisoner to me and told me to guard him. He said if the prisoner got away, I would either be killed or forced to pay
translation_verse: Esime fia la va yina la, edo ɣli gblɔ na fia la bena: Wò dɔla yi ana la me, eye kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsua ɖe va hekplɔ amea ɖe vɛ nam gblɔ nam bena: Dzɔ ŋutsu sia ŋu, ke ne ebu la, woatsɔ wò agbe aɖo eƒe agbe teƒe, alo nada klosalo talento ɖeka aɖo eteƒe.

english_verse: But I got busy doing other things, and the prisoner escaped.” Ahab answered, “You will be punished just as you have said.”
translation_verse: Ke esi wò dɔla le nu wɔm le afi kple afime la, ame la bu Eye Israel-fia gblɔ nɛ bena: Wò ŋutɔe dze se me.

english_verse: The man quickly tore the bandage off his face, and Ahab saw that he was one of the prophets.
translation_verse: Tete wòɖe nu le ŋku dzi kaba, eye Israel-fia la dze sii be, nyagblɔɖilawo dome wotso.

english_verse: The prophet said, “The Lord told you to kill Benhadad, but you let him go. Now you will die in his place, and your people will die in place of his people.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esi nèɖo asi le ŋutsu, si medo busui ŋu la, eyata wò agbe anɔ eƒe agbe teƒe, eye wò dukɔ anɔ eƒe dukɔ teƒe.

english_verse: Ahab went back to Samaria, angry and depressed.
translation_verse: Tete Israel-fia la ɖo aɖa, eye dzi kui wòyi aƒe, eye wòva Samaria.

english_verse: One day, Ahab said, “Naboth, your vineyard is near my palace. Give it to me so I can turn it into a vegetable garden. I'll give you a better vineyard or pay whatever you want for yours.”
translation_verse: Tete Axab ƒo nu kple Nabot gblɔ bena: Tsɔ wò weingble la nam, ne matsɔ wɔ amabɔe, elabena ete ɖe nye aƒe ŋu, eye matsɔ weingble nyui bubu aɖo eteƒe na wò; ke ne edze ŋuwò la, maxe eƒe xɔxɔme ƒe fe na wò

english_verse: Naboth answered, “This vineyard has always been in my family. I won't let you have it.”
translation_verse: Nabot ɖo ŋu na Axab bena: Yehowa nena wòaɖe megbe xaa tso gbɔnye be, matsɔ fofonyewo ƒe domenyinu na wò.

english_verse: So Ahab went home, angry and depressed because of what Naboth had told him. He lay on his bed, just staring at the wall and refusing to eat a thing.
translation_verse: Tete Axab yi eƒe me, eɖo aɖa, eye dzi kui le nya, si Yezreeltɔ Nabot gblɔ nɛ be: nyemetsɔ fofonyewo ƒe domenyinu na wò o la ta. Eye wòmia eƒe aba dzi hetrɔ mo ɖe aga, eye wogbe nuɖuɖu.

english_verse: Jezebel his wife came in and asked, “What's wrong? Why won't you eat?”
translation_verse: Tete srɔ̃a Izebel yi egbɔ gblɔ nɛ bena: Nukaŋuti dzi le kuwòm, eye nègbe nuɖuɖu?

english_verse: “I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard or to let me give him a better one,” Ahab replied. “And he told me I couldn't have it.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ nɛ bena: Elabena meƒo nu kple Yezreeltɔ Nabot gblɔ nɛ bena: Tsɔ wò weingble nam, ne maƒle, alo ne èlɔ̃ la, matsɔ weingble bubu aɖo eteƒe na wò; ke eɖo ŋu bena: Nyematsɔ nye weingble na wò o.

english_verse: “Aren't you the king of Israel?” Jezebel asked. “Get out of bed and eat something! Don't worry, I'll get Naboth's vineyard for you.”
translation_verse: Tete srɔ̃a Izebel gblɔ nɛ bena: Fianue nye esia wɔm nele le Israel? Fɔ, naɖu nu, eye wò dzi nagbɔ ɖe eme! Matsɔ Yezreeltɔ Nabot ƒe weingble la na wò.

english_verse: They told the people that it was a day to go without eating, and when they all came together, they seated Naboth at the front.
translation_verse: Woɖe gbe ƒã be, woatsi nu adɔ, eye wokplɔ Nabot ɖo dukɔ la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: The two liars came in and sat across from Naboth. Then they accused him of cursing God and the king, so the people dragged Naboth outside and stoned him to death.
translation_verse: Emegbe yakame eve wova nɔ ekasa, eye yakameawo le ɖase ɖim le Nabot ŋu le dukɔ la ŋku me le gbɔgblɔm bena: Nabot do ɖiŋu na Mawu kple fia la! Eye wokplɔe do go yi dua godo ɖaƒu kpee wòku.

english_verse: The leaders of Jezreel sent a message back to Jezebel that said, “Naboth is dead.”
translation_verse: Eyome wodɔ ame ɖo ɖe Izebel, be woagblɔ nɛ bena: Woƒu kpe Nabot wòku.

english_verse: As soon as Jezebel got their message, she told Ahab, “Now you can have the vineyard Naboth refused to sell. He's dead.”
translation_verse: Esi Izebel se be, woƒu kpe Nabot wòku la, Izebel gblɔ na Axab bena: Tso, ne naxɔ Yezreeltɔ Nabot ƒe weingble, si wogbe be, màƒle o la, wòanye tɔwo, elabena Nabot megale agbe o, ke boŋ eku.

english_verse: The Lord said to Elijah the prophet,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va Eliya, Tisbitɔ gbɔ bena:

english_verse: “King Ahab of Israel is in Naboth's vineyard right now, taking it over.
translation_verse: Tso, nayi aɖakpe Israel-fia Axab, si le Samaria: kpɔ ɖa, ele Nabot ƒe weingble me, afisi wòva, be yeaxɔ wòanye ye tɔ.

english_verse: Go tell him that I say, ‘Ahab, you murdered Naboth and took his property. And so, in the very spot where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they will lick up your blood.’ ” When Elijah found him,
translation_verse: Ƒo nu kplii gblɔ bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Ewu ame tso gaxɔ eƒe nu wɔ tɔwòea? Eye ƒo nu kplii gblɔ bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Afisi avũwo ɖuɖɔ Nabot fe ʋu le la, afima avũwo aɖuɖɔ wo hã wò ʋu le.

english_verse: Ahab said, “So, my enemy, you found me at last.” Elijah answered: Yes, I did! Ahab, you have managed to do everything the Lord hates.
translation_verse: Tete Axab gblɔ na Eliya bena: Nye keto, èkpɔma? Eɖo ŋu bena: Mekpɔ wò; elabena ètsɔ ɖokuiwò ƒle na nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ le Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: Now you will be punished. You and every man and boy in your family will die, whether slave or free.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ava dziwo, eye makplɔ wò kple xa; eye matsrɔ̃ Axab ƒe ŋutsuwo katã, ɖeviwo kple ame tsitsiwo siaa, ɖa le Israel.

english_verse: Your whole family will be wiped out, just like the families of King Jeroboam and King Baasha. You've made the Lord very angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Eye mawɔ wò aƒe abe Yerobeam, Nebat vi ƒe aƒe kple Baesa, Axiya vi ƒe aƒe ene, le dziku, si nèɖo nam kple alesi nèble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me la ta.

english_verse: And as for Jezebel, dogs will eat her body there in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Eye ale Yehowa gblɔ le Izebel hã ŋu enye si: Avũwo aɖu Izebel le Yezreel ƒe gli gbɔ.

english_verse: Dogs will also eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Axab ƒe ame, si ke ku ɖe du me la, avũwo aɖui, eye eƒe ame, si ke ku ɖe gbe me la, dziƒoxewo aɖui.

english_verse: Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
translation_verse: eye migblɔ bena: Ale fia la gblɔ esi: Mitsɔ amesia de gaxɔ me, eye mina abolo viaɖe koe wòaɖu kple tsi viaɖe koe, vaseɖe esime magbɔ le ŋutifafa me.

english_verse: Ahab asked his officials, “Why haven't we tried to get Ramoth in Gilead back from the Syrians? It belongs to us.”
translation_verse: Eye Israel-fia gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo bena: Mienyae be, Ramot le Gilead nye mía tɔ oa? Ke míezi kpi gbe exɔxɔ le Aram-fia si.

english_verse: Then he asked Jehoshaphat, “Would you go to Ramoth with me and attack the Syrians?” “Just tell me what to do,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na Yosafat bena: Avi aʋa kplim le Ramot le Gilead a? Yosafat ɖo ŋu na Israel-fia bena: Mele abe wò ene, nye dukɔ le abe wò dukɔ ene, eye nye sɔwo le abe wò sɔwo ene.

english_verse: But first, let's ask the Lord.”
translation_verse: Yosafat gagblɔ na Israel-fia bena: Bia gbe Yehowa se egbe.

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Eye Yosafat gblɔ bena: Yehowa ƒe nyagblɔɖila bubua ɖeke mele afisia, ne miaɖabia nu le egbɔ oa?

english_verse: “We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.” “Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied.
translation_verse: Israel-fia ɖo eŋu na Yosafat bena: Ame ɖeka li, amesi gbɔ wobiaa nu Yehowa le, ke melé fui, elabena metoa nya nyuia ɖeke nam o, negbe vɔ̃a ko, eya nye Mixa, Yimla vi. Ke Yosafat gblɔ bena: Fia meganɔ nu ƒom alea o.

english_verse: Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
translation_verse: Tete Israel-fia yɔ aƒedzikpɔlaa ɖe gblɔ bena: Yi ɖayɔ Mixa, Yimla vi, ve kaba!

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria. They were listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Israel-fia kple Yuda-fia Yosafat, wo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe do fiawu bɔbɔ nɔ eƒe fiazikpui dzi le teƒea ɖe le Samaria ƒe agbo nu, eye nyagblɔɖilawo katã le nya gblɔm ɖi le wo ŋku me.

english_verse: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
translation_verse: Tete Zedekiya, Kenaana vi, tsɔ ga wɔ lãdzowo gblɔ bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esiawo natsɔ atu Aramtɔwo, vaseɖe esime natsrɔ̃ wo avɔ.

english_verse: All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth, and they promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
translation_verse: Eye nyagblɔɖilawo katã gblɔ nya ɖi alea gblɔ bena: Ho yi Ramot le Gilead, eye aɖu dzi! Elabena Yehowa atso wo ade asi na fia

english_verse: Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
translation_verse: Eye dɔla, si yi Mixa yɔ ge la, ƒo nu kplii gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe gbe sɔ, wogblɔ nya nyui na fia la; eyata wò hã wò nya nenɔ abe wo dometɔ ɖeka ƒe nya ene, eye ƒo nu nyuie.

english_verse: “I'll say whatever the living Lord tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
translation_verse: Mixa ɖo ŋu bena: Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe. Ne menye nya, si Yehowa alo nam la, magblɔ o fi! Nyagblɔɖila Mixa gblɔ aʋasisi ɖi.

english_verse: Then Micaiah went to Ahab, and Ahab asked, “Micaiah, should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?” “Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Esi wòva fia la gbɔ la, fia la gblɔ nɛ bena: Mixa, mího aʋa yi Ramot le Gilead loo, alo mitasia? Eɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Ho yi, eye aɖu dzi! Elabena Yehowa atsɔe ade asi na fia.

english_verse: “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth!” Ahab shouted. “What does the Lord really say?”
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ nɛ bena: Zi nenie mata wò be, gblɔ nyateƒe sɔŋ ko nam le Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ mea?

english_verse: He answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers walking around in the hills like sheep without a shepherd to guide them. The Lord said, ‘This army has no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
translation_verse: Egblɔ bena: Mekpɔ Israel blibo la wòka hlẽ ɖe towo dzi abe ale, siwo nu kplɔla mele o ene. Eye Yehowa gblɔ be: Aƒetɔa ɖeke mele amesiawo nu o, wo dome amesiame negbugbɔ yi eƒe me le ŋutifafa me.

english_verse: Micaiah replied: Listen to this! I also saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Azɔ se Yehowa ƒe gbe: Mekpɔ Yehowa wòbɔbɔ nɔ anyi ɖe eƒe fiazikpui dzi, eye dziƒoʋakɔ blibo la le tsitre ƒo xlãe le eƒe ɖusi kple mia me.

english_verse: “I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.” “Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Mayi aɖanye aʋatsogbɔgbɔ anɔ eƒe nyagblɔɖilawo katã ƒe nu me Egblɔ bena: Àte ŋu aflui, heyi ɖawɔ nenema. Axab ku.

english_verse: This is exactly what has happened, Ahab. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, Yehowae tsɔ aʋatsogbɔgbɔ ɖe wò nyagblɔɖila siawo katã nu; elabena Yehowa ɖo dzɔgbevɔ̃e ɖe ŋuwò.

english_verse: Zedekiah walked up to Micaiah and slapped him on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
translation_verse: Tete Zedekiya, Kenaana vi, te va ƒo to me na Mixa gblɔ bena: Afika Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ dzo le gbɔnye yi hafi ƒo nu kpli wò?

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-fia gblɔ bena: Milé Mixa, ne miakplɔe yi dumegã Amon kple fiavi Yoas gbɔ,

english_verse: However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab where two pieces of his armor joined. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
translation_verse: Ke ŋutsua ɖe vu eƒe ɖa me heda ɖe ya me, eye wote Israel-fia le gawua kpeƒe; tete wògblɔ na eƒe tasiaɖam-kplɔla bena: Trɔ, ne nakplɔm tso aʋa la nu, elabena mexɔ abi.

english_verse: Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Tete Israel-fia kple Yuda-fia Yosafat woho yi Ramot le Gilead.

english_verse: Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Then Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
translation_verse: Eye Israel-fia gblɔ na Yosafat bena: Maɖɔ li nye awuwo, eye mayi aʋa la nu, ke wò la, wò awuwo nenɔ ŋuwò. Eye Israel-fia ɖɔ li eƒe awuwo heyi aʋa la nu.

english_verse: So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But when Jehoshaphat shouted out to them,
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, esime tasiaɖam-amegãwo kpɔ Yosafat la, wogblɔ bena: Israel-fia tututu enye sia! Tete wòtrɔ ɖe eŋu, be yewoakpe kplii; ke Yosafat de asi ɣlidodo me.

english_verse: they realized he wasn't Ahab, and they left him alone.
translation_verse: Esime tasiaɖam-amegãwo kpɔ bena, menye Israel-fiae o la, wodzo le eŋu.

english_verse: As the sun was going down, someone in Israel's army shouted to the others, “Retreat! Go back home!”
translation_verse: Esi ɣe ɖo to la, ɣli ɖi le asaɖa la me bena: Amesiame neyi eƒe du me, eye amesiame neye eƒe anyigba dzi,

english_verse: Ahab's body was taken to Samaria and buried there.
translation_verse: elabena fia la ku! Eye wotsɔ fia la va Samaria heɖii ɖe Samaria.

english_verse: Some workers washed his chariot near a spring in Samaria, and prostitutes washed themselves in his blood. Dogs licked Ahab's blood off the ground, just as the Lord had warned.
translation_verse: Wova klɔ tasiaɖam la le Samaria-ta to, eye avũwo ɖuɖɔ eƒe ʋu, eye gbolowo va le tsi le eme, le Yehowa ƒe nya, si wògblɔ la nu.

english_verse: Everything else Ahab did while he was king, including the towns he strengthened and the palace he built and furnished with ivory, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Axab ŋutinya susɔea kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ, nyiɖuxɔ, si wòtu kple ɖu, siwo katã wotso la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Ahab died, and his son Ahaziah became king. King Jehoshaphat of Judah (
translation_verse: Eye Axab mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ, eye via Axazya zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Yuda-fiaɖuƒe. Yosafat.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in Ahab's fourth year as king of Israel.
translation_verse: Yosafat, Asa vi, zu fia ɖe Yuda dzi le Israel-fia Axab ƒe ƒe enelia me.

english_verse: The country of Edom had no king at the time, so a lower official ruled the land.
translation_verse: Eye wònyã matrewɔla, siwo kpɔtɔ le fofoa Asa ŋɔli la ɖa le anyigba dzi.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat had seagoing ships built to sail to Ophir for gold. But they were wrecked at Ezion-Geber and never sailed.
translation_verse: Fiãa ɖeke menɔ Edom o, ke boŋ du dzikpɔlaa ɖee nye fia.

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab offered to let his sailors go with Jehoshaphat's sailors, but Jehoshaphat refused.
translation_verse: Eye Yosafat wɔ Tarsis-ʋuwo, be wòaɖatsɔ sika tso Ofir vɛ; ke womede o, elabena ʋuawo gbã le Ezeon-Geber.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king. King Ahaziah of Israel
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi Axab vi Axazya gblɔ na Yosafat bena: Na nye dɔlawo kple wò dɔlawo nanɔ miwo me; ke Yosafat melɔ̃ o.

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Eye Yosafat mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ, eye woɖii ɖe fofoawo gbɔ le fofoa Dawid ƒe du la me, eye via Yoram zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Israel-fiaɖuƒe. Axazya.

english_verse: Ahaziah disobeyed the Lord, just as his father, his mother, and Jeroboam had done. They all led Israel to sin.
translation_verse: Axazya, Axab vi, zu fia ɖe Israel dzi le Samaria le Yuda-fia Yosafat ƒe ƒe wuiadrelia me, eye woɖu fia ɖe Israel dzi ƒe eve.

english_verse: Ahaziah worshiped Baal and made the Lord God of Israel very angry, just as his father had done.
translation_verse: Ewo nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me, eye wòto fofoa kple dadaa ƒe ʋe me kpakple Yerobeam, Nebat vi, amesi ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me la ƒe ʋe me.

english_verse: Soon after King Ahab of Israel died, the country of Moab rebelled against his son King Ahaziah. One day, Ahaziah fell through the wooden slats around the porch on the flat roof of his palace in Samaria, and he was badly injured. So he sent some messengers to the town of Ekron with orders to ask the god Baalzebub if he would get well.
translation_verse: Eye Axazya ge tso eƒe xɔtaxɔ ƒe fesre nu le Samaria, eye do dze eɖzi. Tete wòdo amewo gblɔ na wo bena: Miyi Mabia nu Ekrontɔwo ƒe mawu Baal-Zebub be, ɖe mahaya tso nye dɔléle sia mea?

english_verse: About the same time, an angel from the Lord sent Elijah the prophet from Tishbe to say to the king's messengers, “Ahaziah has rejected Israel's own God by sending you to ask Baalzebub about his injury.
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa ƒe dɔla ƒo nu kple Eliya, Tisbitɔ la bena: Tso, naɖakpe Samaria-fia ƒe dɔlawo, eye gblɔ na wo bena: Esi Mawua ɖeke mele Israel o ta, mieyina ɖe nu bia ge Ekrontɔwo ƒe mawu Baal-Zebub a?

english_verse: Tell him that because he has done this, he's on his deathbed!” And Elijah did what he was told.
translation_verse: Eyata ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Aba, si dzi nède la, màgaɖi le edzi akpɔ o, ke boŋ àku. Tete Eliya yi.

english_verse: When the messengers returned to Ahaziah, he asked, “Why are you back so soon?”
translation_verse: Eye esi dɔlawo gbugbɔ yi egbɔ la, ebia wo bena: Nukaŋuti mietrɔ gbɔ?

english_verse: “A man met us along the road with a message for you from the Lord,” they answered. “The Lord wants to know why you sent us to ask Baalzebub about your injury and why you don't believe there's a God in Israel. The man also told us that the Lord says you're going to die.”
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Ŋutsua ɖe va kpe mí, eye wògblɔ na mí bena: Mitrɔ gbugbɔ yi fia, si dɔ mi ɖa la gbɔ, eye migblɔ nɛ bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esi Mawua ɖeke mele Israel o ta, nèdɔ ame ɖo ɖa, be woaɖabia nu Ekrontɔwo ƒe mawu Baal-Zebub a? Eyata aba, si dzi nède la, màgaɖi le edzi akpɔ o, ke boŋ àku.

english_verse: “He was hairy and had a leather belt around his waist,” they answered. “It must be Elijah!” replied Ahaziah.
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Ŋutsu la nye fume, eye wòtsɔ lãgbalẽ bla ali dzi. Tete wògblɔ be: Eliya, Tisbitɔe. Eliya nɔ dzo ge tso dziƒo.

english_verse: Fire has already wiped out the other officers and their soldiers. Please don't let it happen to me.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, dzo tso dziƒo, eye wòfiã ame blaatɔ̃wo ƒe amegã gbãtɔ eveawo kple woƒe ame blaatɔ̃awo; eyata na nye agbe naxɔ asi le ŋkuwò me.

english_verse: The angel from the Lord said to Elijah, “Go with him and don't be afraid.” So Elijah got up and went with the officer.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe dɔlaa ɖe ƒo nu kple Eliya bena: Yi kplii, megavɔ̃ o. Tete wòtso, eye eya kplii woyi fia la gbɔ. Axazya ku.

english_verse: When Elijah arrived, he told Ahaziah, “The Lord wants to know why you sent messengers to Ekron to ask Baalzebub about your injury. Don't you believe there's a God in Israel? Ahaziah, because you did that, the Lord says you will die.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ ne bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esi Mawua ɖeke mele Israel, ne woabia gbee ase o ta, nèdɔ ame, be woaɖabia nu Ekrontɔwo ƒe mawu Baal-Zebub a? Eyata aba, si dzi nède la, màgaɖi le edzi akpɔ o, ke boŋ àku.

english_verse: Ahaziah died, just as the Lord had said. But since Ahaziah had no sons, Joram his brother then became king. This happened in the second year that Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
translation_verse: Ale woku le Yehowa ƒe nya, si Eliya gblɔ la nu. Eye Yoram zu fia ɖe eteƒe le Yuda-fia Yoram, Yosafat vi ƒe ƒe evelia me, elabena ŋutsuvia ɖeke mele esi o.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Axazya ŋutinya susɔea kple nusi wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Not long before the Lord took Elijah up into heaven in a strong wind, Elijah and Elisha were leaving Gilgal.
translation_verse: Esime Yehowa le Eliya kɔ ge ato ahom me ayi dziƒoe la, Eliya kple Elisa wotso le Gilgal.

english_verse: Elijah said to Elisha, “The Lord wants me to go to Bethel, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Bethel.
translation_verse: Ke Eliya gblɔ na Elisa bena: Tsi afisia, elabena Yehowa le dɔyem ɖo ɖe Betel. Elisa ɖo ŋu bena: Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe kple wò agbe: Ne magblẽ wò ɖi fi! Eye woyi Betel.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Tete nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nusrɔ̃vi, siwo le Betel la, va Elisa gbɔ gblɔ nɛ bena: Enyae be, Yehowa le wò aƒetɔ kɔ ge agbɔ tawo ayii egbea? Eɖo ŋu bena: Nye hã menyae, mizi ɖoɖoe.

english_verse: Elijah then said, “Elisha, now the Lord wants me to go to Jericho, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life, that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Jericho.
translation_verse: Eye Eliya gblɔ nɛ bena: Elisa, taflatse, tsi afisia, elabena Yehowa le dɔyem ɖe Yerixo Eɖo ŋu bena: Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe kple wò agbe. Ne magblẽ wò ɖi fi! Eye wova Yerixo.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Tete nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nusrɔ̃vi, siwo le Yerixo la, te ɖe Elisa ŋu gblɔ nɛ bena: Enyae be. Yehowa le wò aƒetɔ kɔ ge agbɔ tawò ayii egbea? Eɖo ŋu bena Nye hã menyae, mizi ɖoɖoe.

english_verse: Elijah then said to Elisha, “Now the Lord wants me to go to the Jordan River, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will never leave you!” So the two of them walked on together.
translation_verse: Eye Eliya gblɔ nɛ bena: Taflatse, tsi afisia, elabena Yehowa le dɔyem ɖe Yordan nu. Eɖo ŋu bena: Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe kple wò agbe: Ne magblẽ wò ɖi fĩ! Eye woa kple eve la woyi.

english_verse: Fifty prophets followed Elijah and Elisha from Jericho, then stood at a distance and watched as the two men walked toward the river.
translation_verse: Eye nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nusrɔ̃viwo dome ame blaatɔ̃ yi ɖatsi tre ɖe wo kasa le adzɔge; ke wo kple eve la wovi Yordan nu.

english_verse: When they got there, Elijah took off his coat, then he rolled it up and struck the water with it. At once a path opened up through the river, and the two of them walked across on dry ground.
translation_verse: Tete Eliya ɖe eƒe awu ʋlaya, eye wòŋlɔe tsɔ ƒo tsi la dzi wòmã ɖe akpa eve, eye woa kple eve la woto ƒuƒuiƒe ɖi go.

english_verse: After they had reached the other side, Elijah said, “Elisha, the Lord will soon take me away. What can I do for you before that happens?” Elisha answered, “Please give me twice as much of your power as you give the other prophets, so I can be the one who takes your place as their leader.”
translation_verse: Esime woɖi go la, Eliya gblɔ na Elisa bena: Bia nusi mawɔ na wò, hafi woatsɔm adzoe le gbɔwò. Elisa gblɔ bena: Taflatse, maxɔ wò gbɔgbɔ ƒe akpa eve nu.

english_verse: “It won't be easy,” Elijah answered. “It can happen only if you see me as I am being taken away.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena Ebia nu sesẽ. Ne èkpɔ be, wotsɔm dzoe le gbɔwò la, ekema ava me na wò; ke ne mele alea o la, ekema mava me o.

english_verse: Elijah and Elisha were walking along and talking, when suddenly there appeared between them a flaming chariot pulled by fiery horses. At once, a strong wind took Elijah up into heaven.
translation_verse: Esime wogale nu ƒom le yiyim la, kpɔ ɖa, dzotasiaɖam kple dzosɔwo va klã woa kple eve la dome, eye Eliya to ahom me yi dziƒo.

english_verse: Elisha saw this and shouted, “Israel's cavalry and chariots have taken my master away!” After Elijah had gone, Elisha tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ke esi Elisa kpɔe la, edo ɣli be: Fofonye, fofonye! Israel ƒe tasiaɖam kple eƒe sɔdolawo! Eye megakpɔe o. Tete wòlé eƒe awuwo hedze wo ɖe akpa eve me.

english_verse: Elijah's coat had fallen off, so Elisha picked it up and walked back to the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Eye wòtsɔ Eliya ƒe awu ʋlaya, si ge le eŋu la, eye wògbugbɔ va Yordan nu.

english_verse: He struck the water with the coat and wondered, “Will the Lord perform miracles for me as he did for Elijah?” As soon as Elisha did this, a dry path opened up through the water, and he walked across.
translation_verse: Tete wòtsɔ Eliya ƒe awu ʋlaya, si ge le eŋu la, ƒo tsi la dzi hegblɔ bena: Afika Yehowa, Eliya ƒe Mawu la le? Eya hã ƒo tsi la dzi, eye wòmã ɖe akpa eve; eye Elisa ɖi go ɖe egodo.
