english_verse: When the prophets from Jericho saw what happened, they said to each other, “Elisha now has Elijah's power.” They walked over to him, bowed down,
translation_verse: Esi nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nusrɔ̃vi, siwo le Yerixo, kpoe le adzɔge la, wogblɔ be: Eliya ƒe gbɔgbɔ le Elisa dzi. Eye woyi ɖakpee hede ta agu nɛ.

english_verse: They kept begging until he was embarrassed to say no. He finally agreed, and the prophets sent the men out. They looked three days for Elijah but never found him.
translation_verse: Eye woƒoe ɖe enu, vaseɖe esime nya la wui, eye wògblɔ bena: Midɔ ame ɖa! Tete wodɔ ŋutsu blaatɔ̃ ɖa woɖadii ŋkeke etɔ̃, ke womekpɔe o.

english_verse: They returned to Jericho, and Elisha said, “I told you that you wouldn't find him.” Elisha Makes the Water Pure at Jericho
translation_verse: Eye wogbugbɔ va egbɔ, esime wòle Yerixo; ke egblɔ na wo bena: Nyemegblɔ na mi bena, migayi oa? Elisa na tsi manyomanyo trɔ zu tsi nyui le Yerixo, eye woƒo fi de ŋutsuviwo le Betel.

english_verse: One day the people of Jericho said, “Elisha, you can see that our city is in a good spot. But the water from our spring is so bad that it even keeps our crops from growing.”
translation_verse: Eye duametɔwo gblɔ na Elisa bena: Kpɔ ɖa, du la le teƒe nyui, abe alesi nye aƒetɔ le ekpɔmee ene; ke tsi la menyo o, eye anyigba la na be, fu le gegem le ame ŋu.

english_verse: He replied, “Put some salt in a new bowl and bring it to me.” They brought him the bowl of salt,
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ be: Mitsɔ agba yeye vɛ nam, eye miɖe dze kɔ ɖe eme! Eye wotsɔe vɛ nɛ.

english_verse: and he carried it to the spring. He threw the salt into the water and said, “The Lord has made this water pure again. From now on you'll be able to grow crops, and no one will starve.”
translation_verse: Tete wòdo yi tsi la dzɔ ƒe hetsɔ dze la kɔ de eme gblɔ bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Meyɔ dɔ tsi sia, eye magahe ku kple fugege vɛ azɔ o.

english_verse: The water has been fine ever since, just as Elisha said. Some Boys Make Fun of Elisha
translation_verse: Eye tsi la trɔ vaseɖe egbe le Elisa ƒe nya, si wògblɔ la nu.

english_verse: Elisha left and headed toward Bethel. Along the way some boys started making fun of him by shouting, “Go away, baldy! Get out of here!”
translation_verse: Eye wòdzo tso afima heyi Betel. Esi wòle mɔ dzi le to liam la, ŋutsuvi suea ɖewo ɖo tso dua me, eye wole alɔme ɖem le eŋu le gbɔgblɔm bena: Tabebetɔ, lia va, tabebetɔ, lia va!

english_verse: Elisha turned around and stared at the boys. Then he cursed them in the name of the Lord. At once two bears ran out of the woods and ripped to pieces
translation_verse: Eye esi wònyè kɔ kpɔ wo la, eƒo fi de wo le Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ me; tete sisiblisi eve do tso ave me va vuvu ɖevi blane vɔ eve le wo dome.

english_verse: Elisha went up to Mount Carmel, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Eye wòdzo tso afima yi Karmel-to la dzi, eye wòtrɔ tso afima heva Samaria.

english_verse: Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year as king of Judah. Joram ruled twelve years from Samaria
translation_verse: Yoram, Axab vi, zu fia ɖe Israel dzi le Samaria le Yuda-fia Yosafat ƒe ƒe wuienyilia me, eye woɖu fia ƒe wuieve.

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He tore down the stone image his father had made to honor Baal, and so he wasn't as sinful as his parents.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me, ke mede fofoa kple dadaa nu o, eye wòɖe Baal ƒe legba, si fofoa wɔ la ɖa.

english_verse: But he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel to do. The Country of Moab Rebels against Israel
translation_verse: Negbe Yerobeam, Nebat vi, amesi ble Israel ɖe nuvɔ̃ me la ƒe nuvɔ̃wo ŋu ko woku ɖo, eye meɖe asi le wo ŋu o.

english_verse: For many years the country of Moab had been controlled by Israel and was forced to pay taxes to the kings of Israel. King Mesha of Moab raised sheep, so he paid the king of Israel
translation_verse: Moab-fia Mesa enye lãnyila, eye wòdzɔa alẽvi akpe alafa ɖeka kple agbo akpe alafa ɖeka ƒe fu na Israel-fia.

english_verse: But soon after the death of Ahab, Mesha rebelled against Israel.
translation_verse: Ke esi Axab ku la, Moab-fia dze aglã ɖe Israel-fia ŋu.

english_verse: One day, Joram left Samaria and called together Israel's army.
translation_verse: Tete fia Yoram ho tso Samaria gbemagbe, eye wòtia Israel blibo la xlẽ.

english_verse: He sent this message to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “The king of Moab has rebelled. Will you go with me to attack him?” “Yes, I will,” Jehoshaphat answered. “I'm on your side, and my soldiers and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Eye wòyi ɖada ame ɖo ɖe Yuda-fia Yosafat, be wòagblɔ nɛ be: Moab-fia dze aglã ɖe ŋunye; àho aʋa kplim ɖe Moab ŋua? Eɖo ŋu bena: Mayi kpli wò, mele abe wò ene, nye dukɔ le abe wò dukɔ ene, eye nye sɔwo le abe wò sɔwo ene!

english_verse: But which way should we go?” “We will march through Edom Desert,” Joram replied.
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: Mɔ ka to ge míala ayi? Eɖo ŋu bena: Míato Edom-gbedzimɔ.

english_verse: So Joram, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom led their troops out. But seven days later, there was no drinking water left for them or their animals.
translation_verse: Ale Israel-fia kple Yuda-fia kpakple Edom-fia woyi, eye wozɔ mɔ ŋkeke adre sɔŋ; ke tsia ɖeke meli na aʋakɔ la kple lã, siwo le wo ŋu la o.

english_verse: Joram cried out, “This is terrible! The Lord must have led us out here to be captured by Moab's army.”
translation_verse: Tete Israel-fia gblɔ bena: Alele, Yehowa yɔ fia etɔ̃ siawo, be wòatsɔ wo ade asi na Moabitɔwo.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.” One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
translation_verse: Eye Yosafat gblɔ bena: Ɖe Yehowa ƒe nyagblɔɖilaa ɖeke mele afisia, ne míabia gbe Yehowa ase oa? Tete Israel-fia ƒe dɔlawo dometɔ ɖeka ɖo ŋu gblɔ bena: Elisa, Safat vi, amesi de tsi asi na Eliya la, le afi.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.” The three kings went over to Elisha,
translation_verse: Yosafat gblɔ bena: Yehowa ƒe gbe le esi. Eye Israel-fia kple Yosafat kpakple Edom-fia woyi.

english_verse: and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.” “No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
translation_verse: Eye Elisa gblɔ na Israel-fia bena: Nya ka le mía kpli wò dome? Yi fofowò ƒe nyagblɔɖilawo kple dawo ƒe nyagblɔɖilawo gbɔ! Israel-fia ɖo ŋu bena: Kpao, elabena Yehowa yɔ fia etɔ̃ siawo, be wòatsɔ wo ade asi na Moabitɔwo.

english_verse: Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.”
translation_verse: Elisa gblɔ be: Meta Yehowa Zebaot, amesi ŋku me mele tsitre ɖo la ƒe agbe. Ɖe menye Yuda-fia Yosafat ŋku mee mesi ɖa o la, anye ne nyemanyẽ kɔ ayi kpɔ wò ge gɔ̃ hã o.

english_verse: Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.” The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
translation_verse: Azɔ miyɔ kasaŋkuƒolaa ɖe ɖem! Esime kasaŋkuƒola le saŋkua ƒom la, tete Yehowa ƒe asi va edzi,

english_verse: The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water.
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Miɖe ʋewo ɖe wo nɔewo xa le bali sia me!

english_verse: You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
translation_verse: Elabena ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Miele yaa ɖeke ŋkɔ se ge o, eye miele tsidzadzaa ɖeke kpɔ ge o, gake tsi ayɔ bali sia me fũ, eye miawo ŋutɔ kple miaƒe aʋakɔwo kpakple miaƒe lãwo miano.

english_verse: That simple thing isn't all the Lord is going to do. He will also help you defeat Moab's army.
translation_verse: Ke esia mesɔ gbɔ le Yehowa ŋku me o, ke boŋ atsɔ Moabitɔwo ade asi na mi,

english_verse: You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
translation_verse: eye miasi du sesẽwo katã kple du veviwo katã, mialã ati nyuiwo katã, miaxe tsidzɔƒewo katã, eye miatsɔ kpe agblẽ agble nyuiwo katãe.

english_verse: The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, esime ŋu ke, eye nuɖuvɔsaɣi ɖo la, tsi tso Edom-mɔ dzi va yɔ anyigba la dzi fũ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle.
translation_verse: Eye esi Moab blibo la se be, fiawo ho, be woawɔ aʋa kple yewo la, woƒo amewo katã nu ƒu, amesiwo bla akpa kple bubuwo siaa, eye wodze aʋa ɖe liƒo dzi.

english_verse: When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look
translation_verse: Esi wòfɔ ŋdi kanya, eye ɣe klẽ ɖe tsia dzi la, Moabitɔwo kpɔ tsi la tso adzɔge wòbiã abe ʋu ene.

english_verse: and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
translation_verse: Tete wogblɔ be: ŋue! Fiawo tsrɔ̃, elabena wowu wo nɔewo. Eyata Moab, yi ɖaha nu!

english_verse: But when they arrived at Israel's camp, the Israelite soldiers came out and attacked them, until they turned and ran away. Israel's army chased them all the way back to Moab, and even there they kept up the attack.
translation_verse: Eye esi wova Israel ƒe asaɖa me la, Israel tso, eye wowu Moabitɔwo, eye wòsi le wo nu; ke wolũ ɖe me hewu Moabitɔwo.

english_verse: The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks. Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it.
translation_verse: Wogbã duwo, eye wo dome amesiame fɔ kpewo ƒu gbe ɖe agble nyuiwo katã me taŋtaŋ, woxe tsidzɔƒewo katã, eye wolã ali nyuiwo katã, negbe Xareset ƒe glimekpewo koe kpɔtɔ. Tete akafodalawo ɖe to ɖee, eye woda wo.

english_verse: He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_verse: Tete wòlé eya ŋutɔ ƒe ŋgɔgbeviŋutsu, si le fia du ge ɖe eyome la, sa vɔe le glia dzi. Tete dɔmedzoe gãa ɖe va Israel dzi, eye wodzo le egbɔ hetrɔ yi woƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
translation_verse: Eye nyɔnua ɖe tso nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nusrɔ̃viwo ƒe srɔ̃wo dome va gblɔ na Elisa bena: Srɔ̃nye, wo dɔla ku, eye ènyae bena, wò dɔla vɔ̃a Yehowa. Azɔ fetɔ va, be yealé vinyewo kple eve awɔ kluviwoe.

english_verse: “Maybe there's something I can do to help,” Elisha said. “What do you have in your house?” “Sir, I have nothing but a small bottle of olive oil.”
translation_verse: Elisa gblɔ ne be: Nuka mawɔ na wòa? Gblɔe nam, nuka le asiwò le aƒe me? Edo ŋu be: Naneke mele wò dɔla si le aƒe me o, negbe amigoe ɖeka ko.

english_verse: Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can,
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ be: Yi gbɔdome naɖaɣe goewo le wò aƒelikawo katã si; goe gbɔlowo woanye, eye wòasɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: go home and shut the door behind you and your sons. Then begin filling the jars with oil and set each one aside as you fill it.”
translation_verse: Emegbe nayi xɔ me ado ʋɔ ɖe mia kple viwòŋutsuwo nu, eye naku ami la de goeawo katã me; ne ɖeka yɔ la, natee ɖe axa dzi.

english_verse: The woman left. Later, when she and her sons were back inside their house, the two sons brought her the jars, and she began filling them.
translation_verse: Eye wodzo le egbɔ ɖado nɔ de eya kple viaŋutsuwo nu, woawo le goeawo tsɔm nɛ, eye wòle ekum ɖe wo me.

english_verse: At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.” “We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
translation_verse: Esime goeawo yɔ vɔ la, egblɔ na viaŋutsu be: Gatsɔ goe ɖeka ɖo dem. Eɖo ŋu nɛ be: Goea ɖeke megali o. Tete ami la nu tso.

english_verse: After she told Elisha what had happened, he said, “Sell the oil and use part of the money to pay what you owe the man. You and your sons can live on what is left.” Elisha Brings a Rich Woman's Son Back to Life
translation_verse: Tete woɖagblɔe na Mawu ƒe ame la. Eɖo ŋu nɛ be: Yi ɖadzra ami la, ne natsɔ axe ŋuwò fewoe, eve natsɔ susɔea anyi mia kple viwowoe.

english_verse: Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
translation_verse: Eva me gbe ɖeka be, Elisa yi Sunem, eye nyɔnu hotɔa ɖe le afima, amesi ƒoe ɖe enu be, wòaɖu nu kplii. Eye ne eva yina godoo la, edzea afima heɖua nu.

english_verse: Some time later the woman said to her husband, “I'm sure the man who comes here so often is a prophet of God.
translation_verse: Eye nyɔnu la gblɔ na srɔ̃a bena: Kpɔ ɖa, medze sii be, Mawu ƒe ame kɔkɔea ɖe nye esia va nɔa mía gbɔ tom godoo.

english_verse: Why don't we build him a small room on the flat roof of our house? We can put a bed, a table and chair, and an oil lamp in it. Then whenever he comes, he can stay with us.”
translation_verse: Na míatu xɔvia de de xɔta, míatre eŋu, eye miatsɔ abati, kplɔ̃ kple ablegɔ kpakple akaɖiti ada de eme nɛ, eye ne eva mia gbɔ la, ne wòadze afima.

english_verse: The next time Elisha was in Shunem, he stopped at their house and went up to his room to rest.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la eva afima, eye wòdze xɔtaxɔ la me hetsi afima dɔ.

english_verse: He said to his servant Gehazi, “This woman has been very helpful. Have her come up here to the roof for a moment.” She came, and Elisha told Gehazi to say to her, “You've gone to a lot of trouble for us, and we want to help you. Is there something we can request the king or army commander to do?” The woman answered, “With my relatives nearby, I have everything I need.”
translation_verse: Eve wògblɔ nɛ bena: Gblɔ na nyɔnu la be: Kpɔ da, edze agbagba siawo katã le mia ta, nuka woawɔ na wò? Nyaa de le mia kple fia la alo aʋafia domea? Edo ŋu bena: Mía detɔwo dome mele.

english_verse: “Then what can we do for her?” Elisha asked Gehazi. Gehazi replied, “I do know that her husband is old, and that she doesn't have a son.”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ be: Nuka gɔ̃ woawɔ ne? Gexazi ɖo ŋu be: Vi mehele esi o ɖe, eye srɔ̃a ku amegã.

english_verse: “Ask her to come here again,” Elisha told his servant. He called for her, and she came and stood in the doorway of Elisha's room.
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ be: Yi ɖayɔe ɖa! Esi wòyɔe ɖa wòva tsitre ɖe ʋɔtrua nu la,

english_verse: Elisha said to her, “Next year at this time, you'll be holding your own baby son in your arms.” “You're a man of God,” the woman replied. “Please don't lie to me.”
translation_verse: egblɔ bena. Le ƒe, si gbɔna ƒe wɔale siawo ɣi la, ŋutsuvi anɔ alɔto na wò. Egblɔ bena: Kpao, nye aƒetɔ, Mawu ƒe ame, megaflu wò dɔlanyɔnu o!

english_verse: But a few months later, the woman got pregnant. She gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.
translation_verse: Eye nyɔnu la fɔ fu, eye wòdzi ŋutsuvi le ɣeyiɣi, si Elisa gblɔ nɛ la dzi.

english_verse: One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops.
translation_verse: Esi ɖevia tsi la, eva me gbe ɖeka be, eyi fofoa gbɔ le nuŋelawo gbɔ.

english_verse: Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!” “Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant.
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ na fofoa be: Nye ta, nye ta! Eye wògblɔ na ɖekakpuia de be: Kɔe yi na dadaa!

english_verse: loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
translation_verse: Tete wòkɔe yi na dadaa, eye wòlée ɖe akɔ, vaseɖe esime woku le ŋdɔ me.

english_verse: She carried him upstairs to Elisha's room and laid him across the bed. Then she walked out and shut the door behind her.
translation_verse: Eye wòyi ɖatsɔe mlɔ Mawu ƒe ame la ƒe aba dzi, eye wòdo go hedo nɔa de enu.

english_verse: The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
translation_verse: Eye wòyɔ srɔ̃a gblɔ be: Taflatse, ɖo ɖekakpuiawo dometɔ ɖeka kple tedzinɔwo dometɔ ɖeka ɖem, ne maɖe abla ayi Mawu ƒe ame la gbɔ magbɔ.

english_verse: “Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.” “That's all right,” she answered.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Nukata nèbe, yeayi ɖo, egbe mehenye dzinu yeye alo dzudzɔgbe oa? Eɖo ŋu bena: Enyo!

english_verse: She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Let's go. And don't slow down unless I tell you to.”
translation_verse: Eye wòbia akpa na tedzinɔ la hegblɔ na eƒe ɖekakpui be: Nɔ ekpɔkplɔ dzi, eye megatɔm de afia ɖeke o, negbe ɖeko magblɔe na wò hafi.

english_verse: She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha. When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem.
translation_verse: Ale wòyi heva Mawu ƒe ame la gbɔ ɖe Karmel-to la dzi. Eye wòva me, esi Mawu ƒe ame kpɔe le adzɔge la, egblɔ na eƒe ɖekakpui Gexazi bena: Kpɔ Sunami-nyɔnu la enye keme ɖa.

english_verse: Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.” “Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi.
translation_verse: Eyata ƒu du yi ɖakpee, eye gblɔ nɛ bena: Edɔa, srɔ̃wò dɔa, viwo dɔa? Edo ŋu be: Wodɔ!

english_verse: But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet. Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
translation_verse: Eye wòyi Mawu ƒe ame la gbɔ le toa dzi helé eƒe afɔwo. Tete Gexazi va, be yeafee da; ke Mawu ƒe ame la gblɔ bena: Ɖe, asi le eŋu, elabena eƒe dzi le nu xam, gake Yehowa ɣlae ɖem, eye meɖee fiãm o.

english_verse: The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
translation_verse: Eye nyɔnu la gblɔ be: Ɖe mebia vi nye aƒetɔa? Nyemegblɔ be, megaflum oa?

english_verse: “Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ na Gexazi bena: Bla wò ali dzi, eye natsɔ nye atikplɔ ɖe asi ayi. Ne èdo go amea ɖe la, megado gbe nɛ o, eye ne amea ɖe do gbe na wò la, megalɔ̃ nɛ o, eye natsɔ nye atikplɔ la ada ɖe ŋutsuvi la ƒe mo.

english_verse: But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsuvi la dada gblɔ bena: Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe kple wò amea siaa: Ne magblẽ wò ɖi fĩ! Ale wòtso hedze eyome.

english_verse: Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
translation_verse: Ke Gexazi dze wo ŋgɔ va tsɔ atikplɔ la da ɖe ŋutsuvi la ƒe mo, gake gbea ɖeke meɖi o, eye mese naneke o. Tete wògbugbɔ va kpee hetoe nɛ gblɔ bena: Ŋutsuvi la menyɔ o.

english_verse: Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed.
translation_verse: Eye esi Elisa va xɔa me la, kpɔ ɖa, ɖevi la ku wotsɔ mlɔ eƒe aba dzi.

english_verse: He walked in, shut the door, and prayed to the Lord.
translation_verse: Eye woge ɖe eme hedo ʋɔa ɖe woa kple eve la nu, eye wòdo gbe ɖa na Yehowa.

english_verse: Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm.
translation_verse: Emegbe wòde aba la dzi hetsyɔ akɔ ɖe ɖevi la dzi; etsɔ yeƒe nu ɖo eƒe nu, yeƒe ŋku ɖo eƒe ŋku dzi, eye wotsɔ yeƒe asi do eƒe asiwò me, eye wòdra ɖe edzi, vaseɖe esime dzo ɖo lã me na ɖevi la.

english_verse: Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room, then he went back and leaned over the boy's body. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
translation_verse: Emegbe wòtrɔ hezɔ le xɔa me yi afi zi ɖeka kple afime zi ɖeka; eye wòde aba la dzi hetsyɔ akɔ ɖe edzi. Tete ŋutsuvi la nyẽ zi adre, eye ŋutsuvi la ʋu ŋku.

english_verse: Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
translation_verse: Eye wòyɔ Gexazi gblɔ bena: Yɔ Sunami-nyɔnu sia vɛ. Esi wòɖayɔe wòva egbɔ la, egblɔ be: Kɔ viwò la.

english_verse: She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left. Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
translation_verse: Tete wòyi ɖabɔbɔ ɖe eƒe afɔ nu heɖe ta agu, eye wòkɔ via heɖo go dzo. Elisa wɔ nu maɖumaɖua wòtrɔ zu nu ɖuɖua, eye ame geɖewo ɖui.

english_verse: Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed. One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
translation_verse: Emegbe Elisa gbugbɔ va Gilgal. Eye dɔ to le anyigba dzi, eye nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nusrɔ̃viwo bɔbɔ nɔ eŋku me. Tete wògblɔ na eƒe ɖekakpui bena: Ɖo ze gã dzoe, ne naɖa nu na nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nusrɔ̃viawo.

english_verse: One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
translation_verse: Tete wo dometɔ ɖeka yi gbe me, be yeada ama, eye wòkpɔ gbemekaa ɖe, eye wogbe treklɔnuwo le edzi lɔ ɖe avɔ me fũ, eye wògbɔ va flii ɖe zea me, ke womedze sii o.

english_verse: The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
translation_verse: Eye wotrɔe tsɔ ɖo ameawo kɔ me, be woaɖu. Ke esi woɖu nua ɖe la, wodo ɣli be: Mawu ƒe ame, ku le zea me! Eye womete ŋu ɖui o.

english_verse: “Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine. Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ be: Ekema miku wɔ vɛ. Eye wòtsɔe kɔ ɖe zea me gblɔ be: Mitrɔe ɖo ameawo kɔ me, ne woaɖu. Eye nu vɔ̃ɖia ɖeke meganɔ zea me o.

english_verse: So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Eye wòtsɔe ɖo wo ko me, eye woɖui wòkpɔtɔ le Yehowa ƒe nya la nu.

english_verse: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
translation_verse: Naeman enye Aram-fia ƒe aʋafia, exɔ ŋkɔ le eƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ, eye bubu le eŋu, elabena eya dzi Yehowa to na dziɖuɖu Aram; enye kalẽtɔ, gake edze anyi.

english_verse: One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife.
translation_verse: Eye Aramtɔwo ƒe adzohawo ho, eye woɖe aboyo nyɔnuvi suea ɖe tso Israel-nyigba dzi, eye wònɔ Naeman srɔ̃ gbɔ.

english_verse: When Naaman told the king what the girl had said,
translation_verse: Eye wòyi ɖagblɔe na eƒe aƒetɔ bena: Ale kple ale nyɔnuvi, si tso Israel-nyigba dzi la, gblɔ esi.

english_verse: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
translation_verse: Tete Aram-fia gblɔ bena: Yi, eye maɖo agbalẽ ɖe Israel-fia. Eye wòyi hetsɔ klosalo talento ewo kple sika sekel akpe ade kpakple atsyɔ̃ɖowu ewo de asi.

english_verse: He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
translation_verse: Eye wòtsɔ agbalẽ la vɛ na Israel-fia; eme nya enye: Ne agbalẽ sia su asiwò la, ekema nanyae be, nyee dɔ nye dɔla Naeman ɖe gbɔwò, be nayɔ dɔ eƒe anyi la nɛ.

english_verse: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
translation_verse: Eye Elisa do ame ɖo ɖee, ne woagblɔ nɛ be: Yi ɖale tsi zi adre le Yordan me, ekema wò ŋutigbalẽ aɖɔ ɖo, eye wò ŋuti aka.

english_verse: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
translation_verse: Esi Israel-fia xlẽ agbalẽa la, edze eƒe awuwo gblɔ bena: Mawue menye, ne mawu ame agagbɔ agbee, hafi amesia dɔ ame ɖo ɖe gbɔnye, be mayɔ dɔ anyi na ŋutsu sia? Midze sii kokoko be, mɔnu dim wòle le ŋunye.

english_verse: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
translation_verse: Ke esi Elisa, Mawu ƒe ame la se be, Israel-fia dze eƒe awuwo la, edo ame ɖo ɖe fia la gbɔ, ne woagblɔ nɛ bena: Nukaŋuti nèdze wò awuwo? Ɖoe ɖe gbɔnye, ne wòadze sii be, nyagblɔɖilaa ɖe le Israel.

english_verse: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
translation_verse: Ale Naeman kple eƒe sɔwo kple eƒe tasiaɖam va tɔ ɖe Elisa ƒe aƒe nu.

english_verse: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
translation_verse: Tete Naeman bi dzi hedzo gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, nyea mebu be, ɖe wòle dodo ge ava gbɔnye, eye wòate ɖe ŋunye ayɔ Yehowa, eƒe Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ, eye woatso eƒe asi alili de teƒeawo, eye wòayɔ dɔ anyia hĩ!

english_verse: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
translation_verse: Ɖe Damasko-tɔsisiwo, Amana kple Farfar, menyo wu Israel-tosisiwo katã oa? Ɖe nyemale tsi le wo me, eye ŋunye nakɔ oa? Eye wòdo dzo kple dziku.

english_verse: His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
translation_verse: Tete eƒe dɔlawo va egbɔ ƒo nu kplii gblɔ bena: Mía fofo, ne nyagblɔɖila gblɔ nu sesẽa ɖe na wò la, màwɔe oa? Kakaka wògblɔ na wò be: Ɖale tsi, ne ŋuwò nakɔ!

english_verse: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
translation_verse: Tete wòɖi abu yi ɖado ɖi ɖe Yordan me zi adre le Mawu ƒe ame ƒe nya la nu, eye eƒe ŋutigbalẽ zu abe ŋutsuvi dzaa ɖe ƒe ŋutigbalẽ ene, eye eŋuti kɔ.

english_verse: Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
translation_verse: Tete eya kple eƒe ameha blibo la wogbugbɔ va Mawu ƒe ame la gbɔ, eye wòva egbɔ gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, azɔ medze sii bena, mawu ɖeke mele anyigba blibo la dzi o, negbe le Israel ko. Eyata xɔ nunanaa ɖe tso wò dɔla si!

english_verse: “I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.” Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing.
translation_verse: Ke egblɔ be Meta Yehowa, amesi ŋku me mele tsitre ɖo la ƒe agbe: Ne maxɔ nane fĩ! Eye wòƒoe ɖe enu, be wòaxɔe, ke egbe.

english_verse: Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Naeman gblɔ bena: Ne ele alea la, ekema na woaku anyi tedzisɔ eve ƒe tsɔtsɔ nu na wò dɔla, elabena wò dɔla magasa numevɔ kple akpedavɔ na mawu bubuwo azɔ o, negbe Yehowa ko.

english_verse: “Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left. Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi After Naaman had gone only a short distance,
translation_verse: Egblɔ nɛ bena: Heyi le ŋutifafa me! Eye esi wòdzo le egbɔ eyome bu vie la,

english_verse: Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.”
translation_verse: Mawu ƒe ame Elisa ƒe ɖekakpui Gexazi gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, nye aƒetɔ gbe nusi Aramtɔ Naeman tso vɛ la, xoxo le esi. Meta Yehowa ƒe agbe: Ne nyemaƒu ɖu adze eyome aɖaxo nane le esi o fi!

english_verse: So he hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
translation_verse: Tete Gexazi dze Naeman yome. Esi Naeman kpɔ be, amea ɖe ƒu du kplɔe ɖo la, eɖi go le eƒe tasiaɖam la meyi ɖakpee gblɔ bena: Wo katã doa?

english_verse: “Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Wodɔ! Nye aƒetɔe ɖom ɖa be, magblɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, fifi laa ɖekakpui eve tso Efrayim-to dzi le nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nusrɔ̃viwo dome va dze gbɔnye; taflatse, tso klosalo talento ɖeka kple atsyɔ̃ɖowu eve na wo.

english_verse: “Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
translation_verse: Naeman ɖo ŋu be: Ne enyo ŋuwò la, xa talento eve. Eye wòƒoe ɖe enu, eye wòbia klosalo talento eve ɖe kotoku eve me hekpe ɖe atsyɔ̃ɖowu eve ŋu, eye wòtsɔ wo de eƒe ɖekakpui eve si wotsɔ dze eŋgɔe.

english_verse: When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone,
translation_verse: Esi wova ɖo togbɛa gbɔ la, exɔ wo le wo si hetsɔ dzra ɖo ɖe eƒe me, eye wòɖo mɔ ŋutsuawo wodzo.

english_verse: Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
translation_verse: Ke eya va tsi tre ɖe eƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ. Tete Elisa biae bena: Afika netso, Gexazi? Eɖo ŋu bena: Wò dɔla medo de afi alo afime o!

english_verse: Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nɛ bena: Nye dzi de kpli wò tso, esime ŋutsua ɖe tre heɖi go le eƒe tasiaɖam me va kpe wò. Alo klosalo kple awuwo, amitiwo kple weingblewo, alẽwo kple nyiwo, dɔlaŋutsuwo kple dɔlanyɔnuwo xɔɣienye esia?

english_verse: Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!” Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
translation_verse: Eyata Naeman ƒe anyi la ade ɖe mia kple wò dzidzimeviwo ŋu tegbee! Tete wodzo le eŋku me, eye anyi ƒo ɖe eŋu fu kpii.

english_verse: One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small.
translation_verse: Eye nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nusrɔ̃viwo gblɔ na Elisa bena: Kpɔ ɖa, teƒe, si míele le gbɔwò la, xaxa na mí akpa.

english_verse: Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.” “That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
translation_verse: Na, ne miayi Yordan nu, eye mía dome amesiame natsɔ ati tso afima vɛ, ne míawɔ nɔƒe ɖe afima, afisi míanɔ. Eɖo ŋu na wo bena: Miheyi!

english_verse: “Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked. “Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered,
translation_verse: Eye wo dometɔ ɖeka gblɔ bena: Ne edze ŋuwò la, ekema yi kpli mí. Eɖo ŋu bena: Mayi!

english_verse: and he left with them. They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees.
translation_verse: Tete wòyi kpli wo, eye wova Yordan nu hede asi atilalã me.

english_verse: “Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
translation_verse: Eye Mawu ƒe ame la gblɔ bena: Afika woge dze? Efia teƒe lae, eye wòlã ati tsɔ ƒu gbe ɖi, tete fía la ho ɖe dzi.

english_verse: “Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it. Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ be: Lée! Tete wòɖo asi ɖa lée. Woƒo Aramtɔwo kple ŋkuagbã.

english_verse: Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
translation_verse: Eye Aram-fia ho aʋa ɖe Israel ŋu, eye wòde adaŋu kple eƒe dɔlawo gblɔ bena: Afi kple afime maƒu nye asaɖa ɖo.

english_verse: Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.”
translation_verse: Ke Mawu ƒe ame la dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Israel-fia, ne woagblɔ nɛ bena: Kpɔ nyuie, ne màgato teƒe sia ŋu ayi o, elabena Aramtɔwo ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe afima.

english_verse: The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
translation_verse: Tete Aram-fia ƒe dzi de asi dzodzo me nyanyanya le nya sia ŋuti, eye wòyɔ eƒe dɔlawo gblɔ na wo bena: Miate ŋu agblɔe nam mia dometɔ, si le Israel-fia la dzi dem oa?

english_verse: “None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
translation_verse: Tete eƒe dɔlawo dometɔ ɖeka gblɔ bena: Kpao, nye aƒetɔ fia, ke boŋ nyagblɔɖila Elisa, si le Israel lae, nɔa wò nya, siwo nègblɔna le wò xogã me la, gblɔm na Israel-fia.

english_verse: “Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.” They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king.
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: Miyi ɖakpɔ afisi wòle, ne mado ame dɔ, ne woalée vɛ. Eye wova gblɔ nɛ be: Kpɔ ɖa, ele Dotan.

english_verse: He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
translation_verse: Tete wòdo sɔwo kple tasiaɖamwo kple aʋakɔ gãa de ɖo ɖe afima, eye wova le zã me heɖe to ɖe dua.

english_verse: When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
translation_verse: Esi Mawu ƒe ame la ƒe dɔla fɔ ŋdi kanya, eye wòdo go la, kpɔ ɖa, aʋakɔa ɖe kple sɔwo kpakple tasiaɖamwo de to de dua. Eye eƒe ɖekakpui la gblɔ bena: Oo, nye aƒetɔ, nuka wo ge míala?

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.”
translation_verse: Edo ŋu bena: Megavɔ̃ o, elabena amesiwo le mía dzi la, sɔ gbɔ wu amesiwo le wo dzi.

english_verse: Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
translation_verse: Eye Elisa do gbe ɖa gblɔ bena: Yehowa, ʋu eƒe ŋkuwo, ne woakpe nu! Tete Yehowa ʋu ɖekakpui la ƒe ŋkuwo, eye wòkpɔ nu, eye kpɔ ɖa dzosɔwo kple dzotasiaɖamwo le to la ŋu kpaŋkpaŋ ƒo xlã Elisa.

english_verse: As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
translation_verse: Esi woɖi abu va egbɔ la, Elisa do gbe ɖa na Yehowa gblɔ bena: Na ameha sia ƒe ŋku nagbã! Eye wòna woƒe ŋkuwo gbã le Elisa ƒe nya la nu.

english_verse: Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Eye Elisa gblɔ na wo bena: Menye mo lae nye esia o, eye menye du lae nye esia o; mikplɔm ɖo, ne makplɔ mi yi ŋutsu, si dim miele la gbɔe. Eye wòkplɔ woyi Samaria.

english_verse: When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
translation_verse: Esime wova Samaria la, Elisa gblɔ be: Yehowa, ʋu amesiawo ƒe ŋkuwo, ne woakpɔ nu! Tete Yehowa ʋu woƒe ŋkuwo, eye wokpɔ be, yewole Samaria titina.

english_verse: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
translation_verse: Esi Israel-fia kpɔ wo la, egblɔ na Elisa bena: Fofonye, madza woa? Madza woa, fofonye?

english_verse: “No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
translation_verse: Edo ŋu bena: Magadza wo o! Ɖe nèbe, yeadza amesiwo metsɔ wò yi kple wò dati de aboyoe o la? Tsɔ abolo kple tsi ɖo wo kɔ me, ne woaɖu nu ano nu, eye wòayi woƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go. For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory. King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
translation_verse: Tete wòwɔ amedzro gãa de na wo, woɖu nu no nu, eye wòdo mɔ wo woyi woƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ. Eye Aramtɔwo ƒe adzohawo megava Israel-nyigba dzi kpɔ o. Dɔwuame va Samaria.

english_verse: Some time later, King Benhadad of Syria called his entire army together, then they marched to Samaria and attacked.
translation_verse: Esia megbe la Aram-fia Ben-Hadad ƒo eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la nu ƒu, eye woho va ɖe to ɖe Samaria.

english_verse: They kept up the attack until there was nothing to eat in the city. In fact, a donkey's head cost
translation_verse: Eye dɔ gãa ɖe to le Samaria; kpɔ da, wode to ɖee, vaseɖe esime tedzita ɖeka xɔ klosalo sekel blanyi, eye ahɔnemi kab eneliawo ɖeka xɔ klosalo sekel atɔ̃.

english_verse: One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
translation_verse: Esime Israel-fia le tsa ɖim le gli dzi la, nyɔnua ɖe do ɣli yɔe gblɔ bena: Nye aƒetɔ fia, xɔ nam!

english_verse: “Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu bena: Esi Yehowa mele xɔxɔm na wò o la, afika nyea mato axɔ na wò? Lugbɔƒe loo alo weinfiãƒea?

english_verse: Then he asked, “What's the matter anyway?” The woman answered, “Another woman and I were so hungry that we agreed to eat our sons. She said if we ate my son one day, we could eat hers the next day.
translation_verse: Fia la gagblɔ nɛ bena: Nya ka le asiwò? Eɖo ŋu bena: Nyɔnu sia gblɔ nam be: Tsɔ viwòŋutsu miaɖu egbea, eye miaɖu vinyeŋutsu etsɔ.

english_verse: So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
translation_verse: Eye míeɖa vinye heɖu. Ke esi ŋu ke, eye megblɔ ne be: tsɔ viwò míaɖu la, kpɔ ɖa, etsɔ via ɣla.

english_verse: The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath.
translation_verse: Esime fia la se nyɔnua ƒe nyawo la, edze eƒe awuwo hele tsa ɖim le glia dzi; eye dukɔ la kpɔe be, eta akpanya de eƒe awuwo te.

english_verse: He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Mawu afiam agafiam ɖe dzi, ne Elisa, Safat vi ƒe ta aganɔ eŋu fi!

english_verse: Then he sent a messenger to Elisha. Elisha was home at the time, and the important leaders of Israel were meeting with him. Even before the king's messenger arrived, Elisha told the leaders, “That murderer is sending someone to cut off my head. When you see him coming, shut the door and don't let him in. I'm sure the king himself will be right behind him.”
translation_verse: Esi Elisa bɔbɔ nɔ eƒe me, eye ame tsitsiwo bɔbɔ nɔ egbɔ la, fia la ɖɔ ame ɖo ɖe eŋgɔ. Ke hafi ɖɔla la nava egbɔ la, egblɔ na ame tsitsiawo bena: Miele ekpɔm be, hlɔ̃mevi sia ɖɔ ɖo ɖa, be woatso ta le nunyea? Miɖo ŋku anyi, ne dɔla la va la, ekema mitutui kple ʋɔtru, eye mido nɔa! Ɖe menye eƒe aƒetɔ ƒe afɔzi le eyome gbɔna oa?

english_verse: Before Elisha finished talking, the messenger came up and said, “The Lord has made all these terrible things happen to us. Why should I think he will help us now?”
translation_verse: Ke esi wogale nu ƒom kpli wo la, kpo ɖa, fia la do ɖe egbɔ gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, dzɔgbevɔ̃e sia tso Yehowa gbɔ, nukata maganɔ mɔ kpɔm na Yehowa?

english_verse: Elisha answered, “I have a message for you. The Lord promises that tomorrow here in Samaria, you will be able to buy a large sack of flour or two large sacks of barley for almost nothing.”
translation_verse: Tete Elisa gblɔ bena: Se Yehowa ƒe gbe! Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Etsɔ wɔale siawo la wɔ memee dzidzenu ɖeka axɔ sekel ɖeka, eye lu dzidzenu eve axɔ sekel ɖeka le Samaria ƒe agbo nu.

english_verse: The chief officer there with the king replied, “I don't believe it! Even if the Lord sent a rainstorm, it couldn't produce that much grain by tomorrow.” “You will see it happen, but you won't eat any of the food,” Elisha warned him. The Syrian Army Stops Its Attack
translation_verse: Ke fia ŋu me, si ƒe alɔ ŋu fia la ziɔ ɖo la, ɖo ŋu na Mawu ƒe ame gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, ne Yehowa aɖe fesre ɖe dziƒo ŋu hã la, ɖe esia ava mea? Eɖo ŋu nɛ be: Kpɔ ɖa, akpɔe kple wò ŋkuwo, ke maɖu ɖeke o!

english_verse: About the same time, four men with leprosy were just outside the gate of Samaria. They said to each other, “Why should we sit here, waiting to die?
translation_verse: Eye anyidzela ene le agboa nu, amesiwo gblɔ na wo nɔewo bena: Nukaŋuti mianɔ afisia, vaseɖe esime míaku?

english_verse: There's nothing to eat in the city, so we would starve if we went inside. But if we stay out here, we will die for sure. Let's sneak over to the Syrian army camp and surrender. They might kill us, but they might not.”
translation_verse: Ne miehe, miayi dua me la ekema miaku ɖe afima, elabena dɔwuame le dua me; eye ne míetsi afisia hã, kuku ge míala. Eyata mina miayi Aramtɔwo ƒe asaɖa me aɖabu aka na wo! Ne wona míetsi agbe la, ekema míetsi agbe; ne wowu mí la, ekema ɖe mieku.

english_verse: They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
translation_verse: Tete wogblɔ na wo nɔewo bena: Menye nu nyui enye esia wɔm miele o, elabena egbe enye du nyui xɔgbe. Ne míelala, vaseɖe ŋu ke la, ekema míaɖi fɔ; eyata mina míayi aɖagblɔe le fia fe me.

english_verse: They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
translation_verse: Eye woyi ɖayɔ dua ƒe agbonudzɔlawo gblɔ na wo bena: Miede Aramtɔwo ƒe asaɖa me, eye kpɔ ɖa, amea ɖeke meli o, eye amegbetɔ ƒe gbe meɖi o, ke boŋ wode ka sɔwo kple tedziwo ɖi, eye agbadɔwo li, abe alesi wole ene.

english_verse: The guards reported the news to the king's palace.
translation_verse: Woyɔ agbonudzɔlawo, eye woawo ɖagblɔe le fia ƒe me.

english_verse: The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
translation_verse: Tete fia la fɔ le zã gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo bena: Magblɔe na mi, nusi Aramtɔwo be, yewoawɔ mí. Wonyae bena, dɔ le mia wum, eyata wodzo le asaɖa la me yi ɖaɣla ɖe gbe me gblɔ bena: Ne wodo tso dua me la, ekema míalé wo agbagbe, eye míage ɖe dua me.

english_verse: One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.”
translation_verse: Eye eƒe dɔlawo dometɔ ɖeka xɔ edzi gblɔ bena: Na woaɖe sɔ alɔ̃ tso sɔ, siwo kpɔtɔ ɖe dua me la me, ɖewohĩ ava me na wo abe Israel ƒe ameha blibo, si kpɔtɔ la ene, alo ava me na wo abe Israel ƒe ameha blibo, si ku la ene; eye na míadɔ ame woaɖakpɔe ɖa.

english_verse: They found two chariots, and the king commanded the men to find out what had happened to the Syrian troops.
translation_verse: Tete woɖe tasiaɖam eve kple sɔwo, eye fia la dɔ wo ɖe Aramtɔwo ƒe asaɖa me gblɔ bena: Miyi ɖakpɔe ɖa!

english_verse: The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
translation_verse: Eye wodze wo yome vaseɖe kekeke Yordan nu, eye kpɔ ɖa, mɔ blibo la dziya fũ kple awuwo kple aʋawɔnuwo, siwo Aramtɔwo tsɔ ƒu gbe, esime wole sisim. Eye dɔlawo gbugbɔ va gblɔe na fia la.

english_verse: At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la do go ɖaha Aramtɔwo ƒe asaɖa la, eye wɔ memee dzidzenu ɖeka xɔ sekel ɖeka ɖe Yehowa ƒe nya la nu.

english_verse: The king of Israel had put his chief officer in charge of the gate, but he died when the people trampled him as they rushed out of the city.
translation_verse: Ke fia la ɖe fia ŋu me, si ƒe alɔ ŋu wòziɔna ɖo la, ɖo agbo la nu, eye dukɔ la fanyae ɖe agbo la nu woku, abe alesi Mawu ƒe ame la gblɔ, esime fia la va egbɔ ene!

english_verse: Earlier, when the king was at Elisha's house, Elisha had told him that flour or barley would sell for almost nothing.
translation_verse: Elabena esi Mawu ƒe ame la gblɔ na fia la bena, lu dzidzenu eve axɔ sekel ɖeka, eye wɔ memee dzidzenu ɖeka axɔ sekel ɖeka le Samaria ƒe agbo nu etsɔ wɔale siawo la,

english_verse: But the officer refused to believe that even the Lord could do that. So Elisha warned him that he would see it happen, but would not eat any of the food.
translation_verse: fia ŋu me la ɖo ŋu na Mawu fe ame la gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, ne Yehowa ɖe fesre ɖe dziƒo ŋu hã la, ɖe nusia ava mea? Eye wògblɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, àkpɔe kple wò ŋkuwo, gake màɖu ɖeke o.

english_verse: And that's exactly what happened—the officer was trampled to death.
translation_verse: Eva me nɛ nenema, eye dukɔ la fanyae ɖe agbo la nu woku.

english_verse: Then she returned to Israel and immediately begged the king to give back her house and property.
translation_verse: Esi ƒe adrea nu yi vɔ la, nyɔnua gbugbɔ tso Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, eye wòyi, be yeaɖe kuku na fia la le eƒe aƒe kple eƒe agble ta.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king was asking Gehazi the servant of Elisha about the amazing things Elisha had been doing.
translation_verse: Eye fia la le nu ƒom kple Mawu ƒe ame ƒe ɖekakpui Gexazi bena: Taflatse, gblɔ nu gã nu gã, siwo katã Elisa wɔ la nam.

english_verse: While Gehazi was telling him that Elisha had brought a dead boy back to life, the woman and her son arrived. “Here's the boy, Your Majesty,” Gehazi said. “And this is his mother.”
translation_verse: Esi wògblɔ na fia la be, egbɔ agbe ame kuku la, kpɔ ɖa, nyɔnu, si ƒe vi wògbɔ agbee la, va ɖe kuku na fia la le eƒe aƒe kple eƒe agble ta. Tete Gexazi gblɔ bena: Nye aƒetɔ fia, nyɔnu la nye esia, eye esia nye via, si Elisa gbɔ agbee la.

english_verse: Some time later Elisha went to the capital city of Damascus to visit King Benhadad of Syria, who was sick. And when Benhadad was told he was there,
translation_verse: Elisa va Damasko, esime Aram-fia Ben-Hadad le dɔ lém. Eye wova gblɔ nɛ be: Mawu ƒe ame va afisia!

english_verse: Hazael left with forty camel loads of the best things made in Damascus as a gift for Elisha. He found the prophet and said, “Your servant, King Benhadad, wants to know if he will get well.”
translation_verse: Eye Xazael yi ɖakpee, eye wòtsɔ nunanawo kple Damasko ƒe nu veviwo ɖe asi; wole kposɔ blane ƒe agbatsɔtsɔ. Eye wòva egbɔ gblɔ bena: Viwò, Aram-fia Ben-Hadad dɔm ɖe gbɔwò gblɔ bena: Mahaya le dɔ sia mea?

english_verse: “Tell him he will,” Elisha said to Hazael. “But the Lord has already told me that Benhadad will definitely die.”
translation_verse: Elisa ɖo ŋu bena: Yi ɖagblɔ ne bena: Àhaya! Gake Yehowa ɖee fiãm bena, ele kuku ge.

english_verse: Elisha stared at him until Hazael was embarrassed, then Elisha began crying.
translation_verse: Eye wòlé ŋku ɖe edzi gã eteƒe didi, eye Mawu ƒe ame la de asi avifafa me.

english_verse: “Sir, why are you crying?” Hazael asked. Elisha answered, “Because I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn down their walled cities and slaughter their young men. You will even crush the heads of their babies and rip open their pregnant women.”
translation_verse: Tete Xazael gblɔ bena: Nukaŋuti nye aƒetɔ le avi fam? Eɖo ŋu bena: Menya nu vɔ̃ɖi, si wɔ ge nala ɖe Israel-viwo ŋu; àtɔ dzo woƒe du sesẽwo, eye atsɔ yi awu woƒe ɖekakpuiwo, àxlã woƒe vidzĩewo ɖe nu, eye adze ƒo le woƒe funɔwo nu.

english_verse: “How could I ever do anything like that?” Hazael replied. “I'm only a servant and don't have that kind of power.” “Hazael, the Lord has told me that you will be the next king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Xazael gblɔ be: Nuka wò dɔla, avũ, nye be, wòawɔ nu gã sia? Elisa gblɔ bena: Yehowa ɖee fiãm be, wòe le fia ɖu ge ɖe Aram dzi.

english_verse: Hazael went back to Benhadad and told him, “Elisha said that you will get well.”
translation_verse: Tete wodzo le Elisa gbɔ heyi eƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ, eye wòbiae bena: Nya ka Elisa gblɔ na wò? Eɖo ŋu bena: Egblɔ nam bena, èle hayahaya ge.

english_verse: But the very next day, Hazael got a thick blanket; he soaked it in water and held it over Benhadad's face until he died. Hazael then became king. King Jehoram of Judah (
translation_verse: Ke esi ŋu ke la, etsɔ avɔ de tsi me hetsyɔ mo nɛ, tete woku. Eye Xazael zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Yuda-fiaɖuƒe. Yoram.

english_verse: So Jehoram and his cavalry marched to Zair, where the Edomite army surrounded him and his commanders. During the night he attacked the Edomites, but he was defeated, and his troops escaped to their homes.
translation_verse: Tete Yoram ho yi Zair, eye tasiaɖamwo katã kpe ɖe eŋu. Esi wòfa le zã me la, edze Edomtɔ, siwo ɖe to ɖe eya kple tasiaɖam-amegãwo la, eye dukɔ la si yi eƒe agbadɔ me.

english_verse: While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king.
translation_verse: Le eŋɔli Edom dze aglã ɖe Yuda ƒe dziɖuɖu ŋu, eye woɖo fia ɖe wo ɖokui nu.

english_verse: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah in Joram's fifth year as king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was still king of Judah.
translation_verse: Eye Yoram, Yuda-fia Yosafat ƒe vi, zu fia le Israel-fia Axab ƒe vi Yoram ƒe ƒe atɔ̃lia me, le Yuda-fia Yosafat ŋɔli.

english_verse: Jehoram disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He married Ahab's daughter and was as sinful as Ahab's family and the kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Eye wòto Israel-fia wo ƒe ʋe me, abe alesi Axab ƒe aƒe la wo ene, elabena eɖe Axab ƒe vinyɔnu, eye wòwɔ nusi enye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: But the Lord refused to destroy Judah, because he had promised his servant David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa mebe, yeagblẽ Yuda o, le eƒe dɔla Dawid ta, abe alesi wògblɔ nɛ be, yeana akaɖia ɖe eya kple viawo ɖaa ene.

english_verse: years old when he became king, and he ruled from Jerusalem for only one year. His mother was Athaliah, a granddaughter of King Omri of Israel.
translation_verse: Ale Edom dze aglã ɖe Yuda ƒe dziɖuɖu ŋu vaseɖe egbe; eye Libna hã dze aglã le ɣemaɣi.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoram did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Yoram ŋutinya susɔea kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Yuda-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Jehoram died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Ahaziah then became king. King Ahaziah of Judah (
translation_verse: Eye Yoram mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ, eye woɖii ɖe fofoawo gbɔ le Dawid ƒe du la me, eye via Axazya zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Axazya.

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah in the twelfth year of Joram's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Axazya, Yuda-fia, Yoram ƒe vi, zu fia le Israel-fia Axab ƒe vi Yoram ƒe ƒe wuievelia me.

english_verse: Since Ahaziah was related to Ahab's family, he acted just like them and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong.
translation_verse: Eto Axab ƒe aƒe la ʋe me, eye wòwɔ nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me, abe Axab fe aƒe la ene; elabena to wònye na Axab ƒe aƒe la.

english_verse: Ahaziah went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
translation_verse: Eye Axab vi Yoram ho aʋa yi Ramot-Gilead ɖe Aram-fia Xazael ŋu; ke Aramtɔwo si Yoram.

english_verse: One day, Elisha called for one of the other prophets and said: Take this bottle of olive oil and get ready to go to the town of Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Eye nyagblɔɖila Elisa yɔ nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nusrɔ̃viwo dometɔ ɖeka gblɔ nɛ bena: Bla wò ali dzi, eye natsɔ amigoe sia ɖe asi ayi Ramot-Gilead.

english_verse: When you get there, find Jehu son of Jehoshaphat and grandson of Nimshi. Take him to a place where the two of you can be alone,
translation_verse: Ne eɖo afima la akpɔ Yehu, Nimsi vi Yosafat ƒe vi, ge ɖe eme, eye nana wòatsi tre tso nɔviawo dome, eye kplɔe yi xogã me.

english_verse: then pour olive oil on his head to show that he is the new king. Say to him, “The Lord has chosen you to be king of Israel.” Then leave quickly—don't wait around for anything!
translation_verse: Eye natsɔ amigoe la akɔ ɖe ta me nɛ agblɔ bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Mesi ami na wò heɖo fia ɖe Israel dzi. Emegbe naʋu ʋɔa, eye nasi, megalala o.

english_verse: The young prophet left for Ramoth.
translation_verse: Tete nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nusrɔ̃vi la yi Ramot-Gilead.

english_verse: When he arrived, the army officers were meeting together. “Sir, I have a message for you,” he said. “For which one of us?” Jehu asked. “You, sir,” the prophet answered.
translation_verse: Esi woge ɖe eme la, kpɔ ɖa, aʋakɔ la ƒe amegãwo ɖi anyi. Eye wògblɔ bena: Amegã, mehe gbea ɖe vɛ na wò! Yehu ɖo ŋu bena: Mí katã dometɔ kae? Eɖo ŋu bena: Amegã wòe!

english_verse: So Jehu got up and went inside. The prophet poured olive oil on Jehu's head and told him: The Lord God of Israel has this message for you: “I am the Lord, and I have chosen you to be king of my people Israel.
translation_verse: Tete wòtsi tre heyi xɔa me, eye wòka ami la ɖe eƒe ta me gblɔ nɛ bena: Ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Mesi ami na wò heɖo fia wò ɖe Yehowa ƒe aƒe Israel dzi.

english_verse: I want you to wipe out the family of Ahab, so Jezebel will be punished for killing the prophets and my other servants.
translation_verse: Eye tsrɔ̃ wò aƒetɔ Axab ƒe aƒe la, ne mabia hlɔ̃ Izebel ɖe nye dɔla nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe ʋu kple Yehowa ƒe dɔlawo katã ƒe ʋu nu.

english_verse: Every man and boy in Ahab's family must die, whether slave or free.
translation_verse: Axab ƒe aƒe blibo la atsrɔ̃ gbidigbidi, eye matsrɔ̃ Axab ƒe ŋutsuwo, ɖeviwo kple ame tsitsiwo siaa.

english_verse: His whole family must be destroyed, just like the families of Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah.
translation_verse: Mawo Axab ƒe aƒe la abe Yerobeam. Nebat vi ƒe aƒe kple Baesa, Axiya vi ƒe aƒe ene.

english_verse: Jehu went back to his officers, and one of them asked, “What did that crazy prophet want? Is everything all right?” “You know him and how he talks,” Jehu answered.
translation_verse: Eye esi Yehu do va eƒe aƒetɔ ƒe dɔlawo gbɔ la, wobiae bena: Eme nyoa? Nya ka ta aɖaʋatɔ sia va gbɔwò ɖo? Eɖo ŋu na wo bena: Mienya ŋutsu la kple eƒe nuwɔwɔ tso!

english_verse: “No, we don't. What did he say?” they asked. “He had a message from the Lord,” Jehu replied. “He said that the Lord has chosen me to be the next king of Israel.”
translation_verse: Ke wogblɔ bena: Aʋa tsoe, gblɔe na mí dzro! Tete wògblɔ bena: Ale kple ale wògblɔ nam enye si be: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Mesi ami na wò heɖo fia wò ɖe Israel dzi.

english_verse: They quickly grabbed their coats and spread them out on the steps where Jehu was standing. Someone blew a trumpet, and everyone shouted, “Jehu is king!” Jehu Kills Joram and Ahaziah
translation_verse: Tete wowɔ kaba, eye wo dome amesiame tsɔ eƒe avɔ ɖo ete le atrakpuifɔflɔ la dzi, eye woku kpẽ gblɔ bena: Yehu zu ha!

english_verse: When the guard in the watchtower at Jezreel saw Jehu and his men riding up, he shouted to the king, “I see a large group of men coming this way.” Joram ordered, “Send someone out to ask them if this is a friendly visit.”
translation_verse: Eye esi dzɔla le mɔ̃ ta me le Yezreel kpɔ Yehu ƒe amehawo gbɔna la, egblɔ be: Mekpɔ amehaa ɖe! Tete Yoram gblɔ bena: Ɖe sɔdola ɖeka ɖo ɖa, ne wòaɖakpe wo abia bena: Ŋutifafaea?

english_verse: One of the soldiers rode out and said to Jehu, “King Joram wants to know if this is a friendly visit.” “What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just stay behind me with the rest of my troops!” About the same time the guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back.”
translation_verse: Eye sɔdola la do sɔ yi ɖakpee gblɔ bena: Ale fía la gblɔ esi: Ŋutifafaea? Yehu gblɔ bena: Ŋutifafanya kae tsɔ gbɔwò? Trɔ va yi megbenye! Eye dzɔla la yi ɖagblɔ bena: Dɔla la yi ɖaɖo wo gbɔ, ke megatrɔ gbɔ o.

english_verse: So Joram sent out another rider, who rode up to Jehu and said, “The king wants to know if this is a friendly visit.” “What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just get behind me with the rest of my troops!”
translation_verse: Eye wòdɔ sɔdola evelia wòdo sɔ yi wo gbɔ gblɔ bena: Ale fia la gblɔ esi: Ŋutifafaea? Yehu gblɔ be: Ŋutifafanya kae tsɔ gbɔwò? Trɔ va yi megbenye!

english_verse: The guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back either. Wait a minute! That one man is a reckless chariot driver—it must be Jehu!”
translation_verse: Eye dzɔla la yi ɖagblɔ bena: Eyi ɖaɖo wo gbɔ, gake megatrɔ gbɔ o. Nuwɔwɔ la le abe Yehu, Nimsi vi ƒe nuwɔwɔ ene, elabena ele nu wɔm abe aɖaʋatɔ ene.

english_verse: Joram commanded, “Get my chariot ready.” Then he and Ahaziah got in their chariots and rode out to meet Jehu. They all met on the land that had belonged to Naboth.
translation_verse: Tete Yoram gblɔ bena: Tsi sɔ ɖe tasiaɖam ŋu! Eye wotsii ɖe tasiaɖam ŋu, eye Israel-fia Yoram kple Yuda-fia Axazya dome amesiame ɖe eƒe tasiaɖam me, eye woyi Yehu kpe ge: eve wokpɔe Yezreeltɔ Nabot ƒe agble me.

english_verse: Joram asked, “Jehu, is this a peaceful visit?” “How can there be peace?” Jehu asked. “Your mother Jezebel has caused everyone to worship idols and practice witchcraft.”
translation_verse: Esi Yoram kpɔ Yehu la, egblɔ bena: Yehu, ŋutifafaea? Eɖo ŋu bena: Ŋutifafa ka? Esi dawo Izebel ƒe ahasiwɔwɔ kple dzosasa ta le agbɔ sɔm ɖaa ko laa?

english_verse: “Ahaziah, let's get out of here!” Joram yelled. “It's a trap!” As Joram tried to escape,
translation_verse: Tete Yoram trɔ hesi, eye wogblɔ na Axazya bena: Axazya, nugbeɖoɖoe!

english_verse: Jehu shot an arrow. It hit Joram between his shoulders, then it went through his heart and came out his chest. He fell over dead in his chariot.
translation_verse: Ke Yehu vu ete da me, eye wote megbe na Yoram, eye aŋutrɔ la ŋɔ eƒe dzi ɖi go, eye wòmũ dze eƒe tasiaɖam me.

english_verse: Jehu commanded his assistant Bidkar, “Get Joram's body and throw it in the field that Naboth once owned. Do you remember when you and I used to ride side by side behind Joram's father Ahab? It was then that the Lord swore to Ahab that he would be punished in the same field where he had killed Naboth and his sons. So throw Joram's body there, just as the Lord said.”
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi Mekpɔ Nabot kple viawo ƒe ʋu etso tso! Yehowa ƒe gbe enye si; Maɖo eteƒe na wò le agble sia me. Eyata kɔe ƒu gbe ɖe agble la me le Yehowa ƒe nya la nu!

english_verse: Ahaziah saw all of this happen and tried to escape to the town of Beth-Haggan, but Jehu caught up with him and shouted, “Kill him too!” So his troops shot Ahaziah with an arrow while he was on the road to Gur near Ibleam. He went as far as Megiddo, where he died.
translation_verse: Ke esi Yuda-fia Axazya kpɔe la, esi to abɔ me xɔ ƒe mɔ, eye Yehu ti eyome gblɔ bena: Mité eya hã! Eye wotée ɖe tasiaɖam la me le Gur-togbɛ, si le Yibleam gbɔ la dzi, eye wòsi yi Megido heku ɖe afima.

english_verse: Ahaziah's officers put his body in a chariot and took it back to Jerusalem, where they buried him beside his ancestors.
translation_verse: Eye eƒe dɔlawo kɔe yi Yerusalem, eye woɖii ɖe eƒe yɔdo me ɖe fofoawo gbɔ le Dawid ƒe du la me.

english_verse: Ahaziah had become king of Judah in the eleventh year of the rule of Ahab's son Joram. Jehu Kills Jezebel
translation_verse: Axazya zu fia ɖe Yuda dzi le Axab vi Yoram ƒe ƒe wuiɖekɛlia me.

english_verse: Jehu headed toward Jezreel, and when Jezebel heard he was coming, she put on eye shadow and brushed her hair. Then she stood at the window, waiting for him to arrive.
translation_verse: Emegbe Yehu va Yezreel. Esi Izebel see la, eɖo tu ɖe ŋku, eye wòwɔ leke na eƒe ta, eye wòdo mo ɖe fesre nu.

english_verse: As he walked through the city gate, she shouted down to him, “Why did you come here, you murderer? To kill the king? You're no better than Zimri!”
translation_verse: Eye esi Yehu va agboa me la, tete wògblɔ be: Zimri, eƒe aƒetɔ wula doa?

english_verse: He looked up toward the window and asked, “Is anyone up there on my side?” A few palace workers stuck their heads out of a window,
translation_verse: Wòfɔ ka dzi kpo fesre nu gblɔ bena: Ameka le dzinye, amekae? Tete aƒemenuwo dzikpɔla eve alo etɔ̃ do mo ɖe fesre nu.

english_verse: and Jehu shouted, “Throw her out the window!” They threw her down, and her blood splattered on the walls and on the horses that trampled her body.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Mitu asii ƒu anyi! Tete wotu asii ƒu anyi, eye eƒe ʋu hlẽ ɖe gli kple sɔwo ŋu, eye wofanyae.

english_verse: Jehu left to get something to eat and drink. Then he told some workers, “Even though she was evil, she was a king's daughter, so make sure she has a proper burial.”
translation_verse: Eye esi woge ɖe eme ɖu nu no nu la, egblɔ bena: Miyi ɖakpɔ fiƒodeme sia ɖa, ne miaɖii, elabena fia vinyɔnue.

english_verse: But when they went out to bury her body, they found only her skull, her hands, and her feet.
translation_verse: Ke esi woyi, be yewoaɖii la, womekpɔ eƒe afia ɖeke o, negbe eƒe takoli, afɔbaya kple asibayawo ko.

english_verse: They reported this to Jehu, and he said, “The Lord told Elijah the prophet that Jezebel's body would be eaten by dogs right here in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Eye wogbugbɔ va gblɔ̃e nɛ; tete wògblɔ be: Esia nye nya, si Yehowa gblɔ to eƒe dɔla Eliya, Tisbitɔ la dzi bena: Avũwo aɖu Izebel ƒe lã le Yezreel-gble me.

english_verse: And he warned that her bones would be spread all over the ground like manure, so that no one could tell who it was.”
translation_verse: Eye Izebel ƒe kukua ano abe mi ene anɔ gbe me le Yezreel-gble me, ale be amea ɖeke mate ŋu agble be: Izebel enye si o.

english_verse: Your town is strong, and you're protected by chariots and an armed cavalry. And I know that King Ahab's descendants live there with you. So as soon as you read this letter,
translation_verse: Azɔ, ne agbalẽ sia ɖo mia gbɔ̃ la, — miaƒe aƒetɔ ƒe viŋutsuwo, tasiaɖamwo kple sɔwo, du sesẽwo kple aʋawɔnuwo le mia gbɔ tso —

english_verse: choose the best person for the job and make him the next king. Then be prepared to defend Ahab's family.
translation_verse: ekema mitia miaƒe aƒetɔ ƒe viŋutsuwo dome nyuitɔ kple zãzɛtɔ ɖo fofoa ƒe fiazikpui dzi, eye miwo aʋa ɖe miaƒe aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la nu.

english_verse: The officials and leaders read the letters and were very frightened. They said to each other, “Jehu has already killed King Joram and King Ahaziah! We have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Tete vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo vevie ŋutɔ wogblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, fia eve mete ŋu na te ɖe enu o, aleke miawo míate ŋu ana te?

english_verse: The prime minister, the mayor of the city, as well as the other leaders and Ahab's supporters, sent this answer to Jehu, “We are your servants, Your Majesty, and we will do whatever you tell us. But it's not our place to choose someone to be king. You do what you think is best.”
translation_verse: Tete amesi le aƒea nu kple amesi le dua nu kple ame tsitsiwo kpakple ɖeviawo dzikpɔlawo ɖo ame ɖo ɖe Yehu, ne woagblɔ nɛ bena: Wò dolawo míenye, eye nusianu, si nagblɔ na mi la, míawɔe; miele amea ɖeke tso ge aɖo fiae o; wo nusianu, si dze ŋuwò!

english_verse: Jehu then wrote another letter which said, “If you are on my side and will obey me, then prove it. Bring me the heads of the descendants of Ahab! And be here in Jezreel by this time tomorrow.” The
translation_verse: Eye wòŋlɔ agbalẽ ɖo ɖe wo zi evelia bena: Ne míenye tanye, eye miebe, yewoaɖo to nye gbe la, ekema mitsɔ miaƒe aƒetɔ ƒe viŋutsuwo ƒe tawo va gbɔnye le Yezreel etsɔ wòalé siawo! Fia viŋutsuawo le ame blaadre, eye wonyi wo le dua me bubumewo gbɔ.

english_verse: And when these people read Jehu's second letter, they called together all
translation_verse: Esime agbalẽ la ɖo wo gbɔ la, wolé fiavi blaadreawo wu, eye wotsɔ woƒe tawo de kusiwo me ɖo ɖee le Yezreel.

english_verse: When Jehu was told what had happened, he said, “Put the heads in two piles at the city gate, and leave them there until morning.”
translation_verse: Eye dɔlaa ɖe va toe nɛ gblɔ bena: Wotsɔ fiaviawo ƒe tawo vɛ. Egblɔ bena: Mitsɔ wo li kɔ eve ɖe agboa nu, vaseɖe ŋu nake!

english_verse: The next morning, Jehu went out and stood where everyone could hear him, and he said, “You people are not guilty of anything. I'm the one who plotted against Joram and had him killed. But who killed all these men?
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, edo yi ɖatsi tre hegblɔ na dukɔ blibo la bena: Míenye ame dzɔdzɔewo! Kpɔ ɖa, mebia nu ɖe nye aƒetɔ ŋu, eye mewui; ke ameka wu amesiawo katã?

english_verse: Then Jehu killed the rest of Ahab's relatives living in Jezreel, as well as his highest officials, his priests, and his closest friends. No one in Ahab's family was left alive in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Eye Yehu wu amesiwo katã kpɔtɔ ɖe Axab ƒe me le Yezreel, eƒe amegãwo katã, xɔlɔ̃awo kple eƒe nunɔlawo, vaseɖe esime amea ɖeke mekpɔtɔ si o.

english_verse: Jehu left for Samaria, and along the way, he met some relatives of King Ahaziah of Judah at a place where shepherds meet. He asked, “Who are you?” “We are relatives of Ahaziah,” they answered. “We're going to visit his family.”
translation_verse: eɖo go Yuda-fia Axazya nɔviŋutsuwo, eye wòbia bena: Amehawo míenye? Woɖo ŋu bena: Axazya nɔviŋutsuwo mienye, eye mieyina, be míado gbe na fia viŋutsuwo kple fiasrɔ̃ ƒe viŋutsuwo.

english_verse: “Take them alive!” Jehu said to his officers. So they grabbed them and led them to the well near the shepherds' meeting place, where they killed all
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ be: Milé wo agbagbe! Eye wòlé wo agbagbe hewu wo ɖe takpexɔ la ƒe do me; wole ŋutsu blane vɔ eve, eye mena wo dometɔa ɖeke si o.

english_verse: As Jehu went on, he saw Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. Jehu greeted him, then said, “Jehonadab, I'm on your side. Are you on mine?” “Yes, I am.” “Then give me your hand,” Jehu answered. He helped Jehonadab into his chariot
translation_verse: Eye wodzo tso afima heva ɖo go Rexab vi Yonadab, amesi va ekpe ge. Tete wòdo gbe nɛ biae bena: Wò dzi me kɔ, abe alesi nye dzi le ɖe wo dzi ŋu enea? Yonadab ɖo ŋu bena: Ele nenema! Yehu be: Ne ele nenema la, ekema na asim kpɔ! Eye wòna asii. Tete wòna wòɖo egbɔ le tasiaɖam la me,

english_verse: and said, “Come with me and see how faithful I am to the Lord.” They rode together in Jehu's chariot
translation_verse: eye wogblɔ bena: Va miyi, ne nakpɔ, alesi mele ŋu nam ɖe Yehowa nui eye wòna woɖo eƒe tasiaɖam la.

english_verse: to Samaria. Jehu killed everyone there who belonged to Ahab's family, as well as all his officials. Everyone in his family was now dead, just as the Lord had promised Elijah. Jehu Kills All the Worshipers of Baal
translation_verse: Eye wòyi Samaria ɖawu Axab ƒe amesiwo katã kpɔtɔ ɖe Samaria la, vaseɖe esime wotsrɔ̃ wo vɔ, le Yehowa ƒe nya, si wògblɔ na Eliya la nu. Yehu tsrɔ̃ Baal-subɔsubɔ; gake meɖe legba subɔsubɔ ŋutɔ ɖa o.

english_verse: Jehu called together the people in Samaria and said: King Ahab sometimes worshiped Baal, but I will be completely faithful to Baal.
translation_verse: Tete Yehu ƒo dukɔ blibo la nu ƒu gblɔ na wo bena. Axab mesubɔ Baal wòde edeƒe o, Yehu asubɔe ɖe edzi awu.

english_verse: I'm going to offer a huge sacrifice to him. So invite his prophets and priests, and be sure everyone who worships him is there. Anyone who doesn't come will be killed. But this was a trick—Jehu was really planning to kill the worshipers of Baal.
translation_verse: Eyata miyɔ Baal fe nyagblɔɖilawo katã kple esubɔlawo katã kpakple eƒe nunɔlawo katã ɖem, amea ɖeke megatsi anyi o, elabena mele vɔsaŋkeke gãa ɖe ɖu ge na Baal. Amesi ke tsi anyi la, maganɔ agbe o! Ke ŋɔdzomenue Yehu wɔ, be woatsrɔ̃ Baal-subɔlawo.

english_verse: He said, “Announce a day of worship for Baal!” After the day had been announced,
translation_verse: Eye Yehu gblɔ bena: Miwo ŋkekenyuie ƒe takpekpe la kokoe na Baal! Tete woɖe gbe ƒã.

english_verse: Jehu sent an invitation to everyone in Israel. All the worshipers of Baal came, and the temple was filled from one end to the other.
translation_verse: Eye Yehu dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Israel blibo la, eye Baal-subɔlawo katã wova, amea ɖeke metsi anyi si meva o; woyi ɖe Baal ƒe xɔ la me, eye Baal ƒe xɔ la yɔ tratratra tso go ɖeka me vaseɖe go keme me.

english_verse: Jehu told the official in charge of the sacred robes to make sure that everyone had a robe to wear.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na awudzikpɔla bena: Ɖe awuwo do goe na Baal-subɔlawo katã! Tete woɖe awuawo do goe na wo.

english_verse: Jehu and Jehonadab went into the temple, and Jehu said to the crowd, “Look around and make sure that only the worshipers of Baal are here. No one who worships the Lord is allowed in.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Yehu kple Yonadab, Rexab vi, wova Baal ƒe xɔ la mɔ, eye wògblɔ na Baal-subɔlawo bena: Midzro eme, ne míakpɔ be. Yehowa ƒe subɔlawo dometɔa ɖeke maganɔ mia dome afisia o, negbe Baal-subɔlawo ɖeɖeko.

english_verse: As soon as Jehu finished offering the sacrifice, he told the guards and soldiers, “Come in and kill them! Don't let anyone escape.” They slaughtered everyone in the crowd and threw the bodies outside. Then they went back into the temple
translation_verse: Esime wowu numevɔsa nu la, Yehu gblɔ na fia ŋu asrafowo kple fia ŋu amewo bena: Mige ɖe me, ne miawu wo, eye amea ɖeke megasi o! Tete wowu wo kple yi. Ke esi fia ŋu asrafowo kple fia ŋuti amewo tsɔ woƒe kukuawo ƒu gbe la, woge ɖe Baal ƒe xɔ kɔkɔetɔ me,

english_verse: and carried out the image of Baal. They burned it
translation_verse: eye woɖe legbawo tso Baal ƒe xɔa me heta dzo wo.

english_verse: and broke it into pieces, then they completely destroyed Baal's temple. And since that time, it's been nothing but a public toilet.
translation_verse: Wogbã Baal ƒe legba la, eye wogbã Baal ƒe xɔ la hetsɔe ɖo kpɔxadeƒee vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: But he did not stop the worship of the gold statues of calves at Dan and Bethel that Jeroboam had made for the people to worship.
translation_verse: Negbe Yerobeam, Nebat vi ƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo nye sikanyivi le Betel kple Dan, siwo wòtsɔ ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me la, ŋu ko Yehu meɖe asi le o.

english_verse: Later the Lord said, “Jehu, you have done right by destroying Ahab's entire family, just as I had planned. So I will make sure that the next four kings of Israel will come from your own family.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Yehu bena: Esi nèwɔ nusi dze ŋunye pɛpɛpɛ, eye nèwɔ Axab ƒe aƒe la, abe alesi le nye dzi me tututu ene la, eyata viwòwo anɔ Israel-fiazikpui la dzi vaseɖe dzidzime enelia dzi.

english_verse: But Jehu did not completely obey the commands of the Lord God of Israel. Instead, he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam had caused the Israelites to do. Jehu Dies
translation_verse: Ke Yehu melé ŋku ɖe Yehowa ƒe seawo ŋu, ne woazɔ ɖe wo nu kple eƒe dzi blibo o; eye meɖe, asi le Yerobeam ƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wotsɔ ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me la nu o.

english_verse: In those days the Lord began to reduce the size of Israel's territory. King Hazael of Syria defeated the Israelites and took control
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi Yehowa de asi Israel nu tsitsi me, eye Xazael si wo le Israel ƒe liƒowo katã dzi,

english_verse: of the regions of Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan River and north of the town of Aroer near the Arnon River. This was the land where the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh had once lived.
translation_verse: tso Yordan nu ɖota ɣedzeƒe. Gilead-nyigba blibo la, si nye Gad, Ruben kple Manase tɔ, tso Aroer, si le Arnon-tɔʋu la nu vaseɖe Gilead kple Basan.

english_verse: Everything else Jehu did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Yehu ŋutinya susɔeawo, nusiwo katã wòwɔ kple eƒe kalẽwɔwɔwo katã da, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Jehu died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoahaz became king.
translation_verse: Eye Yehu mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ, eye woɖii ɖe Samaria, eye via Yoaxaz zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Jehoiada brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David and gave them to the commanders.
translation_verse: Eye nunɔla la tsɔ fia Dawid ƒe akplɔ kple akpoxɔnu, siwo le Yehowa ƒe me la, na ame alafa ƒe amegãwo.

english_verse: Jehoiada brought Joash outside, where he placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, while the crowd clapped and shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Tete wòkplɔ fiavi la do goe hetsɔ fiakuku la ɖɔ ne, eye wotsɔ se la de asi nɛ, eye wòɖoe fia hesi ami nɛ; tete woƒu akpe hedo ɣli bena: Fia nenɔ agbe!

english_verse: Joash hid in the temple with Jehosheba for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah. Jehoiada Makes Joash King of Judah (
translation_verse: Eɣla ɖe egbɔ le Yehowa ƒe me ƒe ade. Eye Atalya ɖu anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: Joash son of Ahaziah had hidden in the Lord's temple six years. Then in the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest sent for the commanders of the king's special bodyguards and the commanders of the palace guards. They met him at the temple, and he asked them to make a promise in the name of the Lord. Then he brought out Joash
translation_verse: Ke le ƒe adrelia me la Yehoyada do woɖayɔ bia towo kple fia ŋu asrafowo ƒe ame alafawo ƒe amegãwo vɛ, eye wòkplɔ wo yi Yehowa ƒe me hebla nu kpli wo, eye wòna woka atam nɛ le Yehowa ƒe me, eye wòfiã fiavi la wo.

english_verse: and said to them: Here's what I want you to do. Three of your guard units will be on duty on the Sabbath. I want one unit to guard the palace.
translation_verse: Eye wòde se na wo gblɔ bena: Nusi miawɔ enye si: Mi amesiwo le dɔ me do ge le dzudzɔgbe dzi la ƒe akpa etɔ̃liawo ɖeka nadzɔ fia ƒe aƒe la ŋu;

english_verse: Another unit will guard Sur Gate, and the third unit will guard the palace gate and relieve the palace guards.
translation_verse: akpa etɔ̃liawo ɖeka nanɔ agbo Sur me, eye akpa etɔ̃liawo ɖeka nanɔ fia ŋu asrafowo yome le agbo la me, eye midzɔ aƒe la ŋu le ɖoɖo me.

english_verse: The other two guard units are supposed to be off duty on the Sabbath. But I want both of them to stay here at the temple and protect King Joash.
translation_verse: Eye mia dometɔ, siwo katã do le dɔ me le dzudzɔgbe dzi la, ƒe akpa eve nadzɔ Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ŋu le fia la ta.

english_verse: Make sure they follow him wherever he goes, and tell them to keep their swords ready to kill anyone who tries to get near him.
translation_verse: Miƒo xlã fia la godoo va kpe, eye amesiame nalé aʋawɔnu ɖe asi; amesi be, yeadze mi la, naku; eye minɔ fia la gbɔ, ne eɖo, alo wògbɔ.

english_verse: Then they gave the weapons to their guards, who took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect Joash on every side.
translation_verse: Eye fia ŋu asrafowo dome amesiame lé eƒe aʋawɔnu ɖe asi tso xɔ la ƒe ɖusi me gome vaseɖe xɔ la ƒe mia me gome kpakple vɔsamlekpui kple xɔ la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns, which was the usual place for the king. The singers and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the people were celebrating and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
translation_verse: Esi wòkpɔ bena, fia la tsi tre ɖe kɔkɔƒe, abe alesi wònye kɔnu ene, amegãwo kple kpẽkulawo ƒo xlã fia la, esi dukɔ hahoo la le dzidzɔ kpɔm hele kpẽ kum la, Atalya dze eƒe awuwo gblɔ bena: Nugbeɖoɖoe! Nugbeɖoɖoe!

english_verse: At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Kill her! But don't do it anywhere near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops and kill anyone who is with her!”
translation_verse: Tete nunɔla Yehoyada de se na ame alafawo ƒe amegãwo, siwo nye aʋakɔ la ƒe kplɔlawo gblɔ na wo bena: Mikplɔe to amea wo dome, eye ne amea ɖe dze eyome la, mi wui kple yi! Elabena nunɔla la gblɔ be, womawui ɖe Yehowa ƒe aƒe la me o.

english_verse: So the commanders dragged her to the gate where horses are led into the palace, and they killed her there.
translation_verse: Esi wolée, eye wova ɖo afisi sɔwo tona yia fia ƒe me la, wowui ɖe afima.

english_verse: Jehoiada the priest asked King Joash and the people to promise that they would be faithful to each other and to the Lord.
translation_verse: Eye Yehoyada ɖo nubabla Yehowa, fia la kple dukɔ la kpakple fia la kple dukɔ la dome, be woanye Yehowa ƒe dukɔ.
