english_verse: Then the crowd went to the temple built to honor Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal right in front of the altars. After Jehoiada had placed guards around the Lord's temple,
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ hahoo la katã ge ɖe Baal ƒe me, womũ eƒe vɔsamlekpuiwo, eye wogbã eƒe legbawo gudugudu, eye wowu Baal ƒe nunɔla Matan ɖe vɔsamlekpuiawo ŋgɔ. Eye nunɔla la ɖe dzɔlawo ɖo Yehowa ƒe aƒea ŋu.

english_verse: he called together all the commanders, the king's special bodyguards, the palace guards, and the people. They led Joash from the temple, through the Guards' Gate, and into the palace. He took his place on the throne and became king of Judah.
translation_verse: Eye wòɖe ame alafawo ƒe amegãwo, blafowo kple fia ŋu asrafowo kpakple dukɔ hahoo la katã, eye wokplɔ fia la tso Yehowa ƒe me heto fia ŋu asrafowo ƒe agbonumɔ yi ɖe fia ƒe me, eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ fiawo ƒe fiazikpui la dzi.

english_verse: Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_verse: Dukɔ hahoo la katã kpɔ dzidzɔ, eye du la me fa. Ke woatsɔ yi wu Atalya ɖe fia ƒe aƒe me.

english_verse: Jehoiada the priest taught Joash what was right, and so for the rest of his life Joash obeyed the Lord.
translation_verse: Le Yehu ƒe ƒe adrelia me Yoas zu fia, eye woɖu fia le Yerusalem ƒe blane. Dadaa ŋkɔ nye Zibya tso Beer-Seba.

english_verse: The fines that had to be paid along with the sacrifices to make things right and the sacrifices for sin did not go to the temple. This money belonged only to the priests.
translation_verse: Eye womebu akɔnta kple amesiwo si wode ga lae, be woatsɔ na dɔnunɔlawo o, elabena wo wɔe le anukware me.

english_verse: But even Joash did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Eye Yoas wɔ nusi nyo le Yehowa ŋku me le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me, elabena nunɔla Yehoyada fia nui.

english_verse: One day, Joash said to the priests, “Collect all the money that has been given to the Lord's temple, whether from taxes or gifts,
translation_verse: Negbe nuxeƒewo ko womeɖe ɖa o, eye dukɔ la gasa vɔ hedo dzudzɔ le nuxeƒewo.

english_verse: But the priests never started repairing the temple. So in the twenty-third year of his rule,
translation_verse: nunɔlawo naxɔe, amesiame naxɔe le ehavi si, ne woatsɔe aɖɔ xɔ la ƒe gbagbãƒewo ɖo afisiafi, si wonyã kpɔ wògbã ko.

english_verse: Joash called for Jehoiada and the other priests and said, “Why aren't you using the money to repair the temple? Don't take any more money for yourselves. It is only to be used to pay for the repairs.”
translation_verse: Ke le fia Yoas ƒe ƒe blave vɔ etɔ̃lia me la nunɔlawo mekpɔ ɖɔ xɔ la ƒe gbagbãƒewo ɖo haɖe o.

english_verse: Then they would give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. Some of the money was used to pay the builders, the woodworkers,
translation_verse: Ne wokpɔ be, ga, si le aɖaka la me, sɔ gbɔ la, ekema fia la ƒe agbalẽŋlɔla kple nunɔlagã vana, eye woblaa ga, si le Yehowa ƒe me la, hexlẽna.

english_verse: the stonecutters, and the men who built the walls. And some was used to buy wood and stone and to pay any other costs for repairing the temple.
translation_verse: Emegbe wotsɔ ga, si woxlẽ la, na Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ƒe dɔ nunɔlawo, eye wotsɔe na atikpalawo kple xɔtulawo, amesiwo le dɔ wɔm le Yehowa ƒe aƒe la nu

english_verse: While the repairs were being made, the money that was given to the temple was not used to make silver bowls, lamp snuffers, small sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or anything gold or silver for the temple.
translation_verse: kple gliɖolawo kple kpefulawo, eye wotsɔe ƒle atiwo kple kpewo, ne woatsɔ aɖɔ Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ƒe gbagbãƒewo ɖo, kple nusiwo katã wohiã le xɔ la ɖɔɖɔɖo me.

english_verse: The men in charge were honest, so no one had to keep track of the money.
translation_verse: ke boŋ wotsɔ wo na dɔnunɔlawo be woatsɔ aɖɔ Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ɖoe.

english_verse: About the same time, King Hazael of Syria attacked the town of Gath and captured it. Next, he decided to attack Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ke wometsɔ ga, si woxe ɖe dzidada kple nuvɔ̃wo ta la, va Yehowa ƒe me o; nunɔla wo tɔ wònye. Xazael ho aʋa yi Yerusalem. Wowu Yoas.

english_verse: Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king of Israel in the twenty-third year of Joash's rule in Judah. Jehoahaz ruled
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Axazya ƒe vi Yoas ƒe ƒe blave vɔ etɔ̃lia me la Yehu ƒe vi Yoaxaz zu fia de Israel dzi le Samaria ƒe wuiadre.

english_verse: and said, “Open the window facing east.” When it was open, Elisha shouted, “Now shoot!” Jehoash shot an arrow and Elisha said, “That arrow is a sign that the Lord will help you completely defeat the Syrian army at Aphek.”
translation_verse: gblɔ bena: ʋu fesre, si ɖo ta ɣedzeƒe gome! Eye wòʋui. Eye Elisa gblɔ be: Da aŋutrɔ la! Tete wòdae. Eye wògblɔ bena: Dziɖuɖu ƒe aŋutrɔ tso Yehowa gbɔ kple Aram-tɔwo dziɖuɖu ƒe aŋutrɔ! Asi Aramtɔwo le Afek, vaseɖe esime woatsrɔ̃.

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He never stopped following the example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nusi nye vɔ le Yehowa ŋku me, eye wòwɔ Yerobeam, Nebat vi ƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wòtsɔ ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me, eye meɖe asi le eŋu o.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with the Israelites, so he let King Hazael of Syria and his son Benhadad rule over them for a long time.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa do dɔmedzoe ɖe Israel ŋu, eye wotsɔ wo de asi na Aram-fia Xazael kple Xazael vi Ben-Hadad ŋkekeawo katã.

english_verse: Jehoahaz prayed to the Lord for help, and the Lord saw how terribly Hazael was treating the Israelites. He answered Jehoahaz
translation_verse: Eye Yoaxaz ƒo koko na Yehowa, eye Yehowa ɖo toe, elabena ekpɔ alesi Aram-fia te Israel ɖe anyii.

english_verse: by sending Israel a leader who rescued them from the Syrians, and the Israelites lived in peace as they had before.
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ɖo xɔnametɔa ɖe na Israel, eye woge le Aramtɔwo si me, eye Israel-viwo nɔ woƒe agbadɔwo me abe tsã ene.

english_verse: Jehoash became king of Israel in the thirty-seventh year of Joash's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Yoas ƒe ƒe blaetɔ̃ vɔ adrelia me la Yoaxaz ƒe vi Yoas zu fia ɖe Israel dzi le Samaria ƒe wuiade.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoahaz did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Yoaxaz ŋutinya susɔeawo, nusiwo katã wòwɔ kple eƒe kalẽwɔwɔwo la, woŋlɔ wo de Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Jehoahaz died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoash became king. King Jehoash of Israel
translation_verse: Eye Yoaxaz mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ, eye wodi ɖe Samaria, eye via Yoas zu fia de eteƒe. Yoas

english_verse: “Grab a bow and some arrows,” Elisha told him, “and hold them in your hand.” Jehoash grabbed the bow and arrows and held them. Elisha placed his hand on the king's hand
translation_verse: egblɔ na Israel-fia bena: Tso wò asi ɖo dati la dzi! Esi wòɖo eƒe asi edzi la, Elisa tso eƒe asi ɖo fia la ƒe asi dzi

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord by doing just like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ewo nusi nye vɔ le Yehowa ŋku me, eye meɖe asi le Yerobeam. Nebat vi ƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo katã wòtsɔ ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me la ŋu o, ke boŋ ewɔ wo.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his war against King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Yoas ŋutinya susɔeawo, nusiwo katã wòwɔ kple eƒe kalẽwɔwɔwo kpakple aʋa, si wòwɔ kple Yuda-fia Amazya la, woŋlɔ wo de Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria beside the other Israelite kings. His son Jeroboam then became king. Elisha the Prophet Dies
translation_verse: Eye Yoas mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ, eye Yerobeam bɔbɔ nɔ eƒe fiazikpui la dzi, eye woɖi Yoas ɖe Israel-fiawo gbɔ le Samaria. Elisa gblɔ nya ɖi kuha dzi. Eƒe kukua fɔ ame kukua ɖe ɖe tsitre.

english_verse: Some time before the death of King Jehoash, Elisha the prophet was very sick and about to die. Jehoash went in and stood beside him, crying. He said, “Master, what will Israel's chariots and cavalry be able to do without you?”
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi do, si me Elisa alo aku la, dze edzi. Tete Israel-fia Yoas yi egbɔ, eye wòfa avi le egbɔ gblɔ bena: Fofonye, fofonye! Israel ƒe tasiaɖam kple eƒe sɔdolawo!

english_verse: Elisha said, “Pick up the arrows and hit the ground with them.” Jehoash grabbed the arrows and hit the ground three times, then stopped.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Fɔ aŋutrɔawo! Esi wòfɔe la, egblɔ na Israel-fia la bena: Tsɔ wo ƒo anyigbae! Eye wòƒoe zi etɔ̃ ko tasi.

english_verse: Elisha became angry with the king and exclaimed, “If you had struck it five or six times, you would completely wipe out the Syrians. Now you will defeat them only three times.”
translation_verse: Tete Mawu ƒe ame do dɔmedzoe ɖe eŋu gblɔ bena: Ɖe wònye zi atɔ̃ alo zi aɖe nèƒoe la, eya ko hafi nasi Aramtɔwo, vaseɖe esime woatsrɔ̃; ke azɔ la zi etɔ̃ ko nasi Aramtɔwo.

english_verse: Elisha died and was buried. Every year in the spring, Moab's leaders sent raiding parties into Israel.
translation_verse: Emegbe Elisa ku, eye woɖii. Esi ƒe trɔ la, Moabitɔwo ƒe adzohawo va anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: Once, while some Israelites were burying a man's body, they saw a group of Moabites. The Israelites quickly threw the body into Elisha's tomb and ran away. As soon as the man's body touched the bones of Elisha, the man came back to life and stood up. Israel Defeats Syria
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, esime wole ŋutsua ɖe ɖim, eye wokpɔ adzohawo la, wotsɔ ŋutsu la ƒu gbe ɖe Elisa ƒe yɔdo me. Ke esi ŋutsu la ka Elisa ƒe ƒuwo ŋu la, egbɔ agbe, eye wòtso ɖe eƒe afɔwo dzi.

english_verse: Israel was under the power of King Hazael of Syria during the entire rule of Jehoahaz.
translation_verse: Ke Aram-fia Xazael te Israel ɖe anyi le Yoaxaz ƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: But the Lord was kind to the Israelites and showed them mercy because of his solemn agreement with their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. In fact, he has never turned his back on them or let them be completely destroyed.
translation_verse: Gake Yehowa ve wo nu, ekpɔ woƒe nublanui, eye wòtrɔ ɖe wo ŋu le nu, si wòbia kple Abraham, Isak kple Yakob la ta, eye meɖi be, yeagblẽ wo o, eye meɖe woɖa le eƒe ŋkuta o vaseɖe fifi.

english_verse: Hazael died, and his son Benhadad then became king of Syria.
translation_verse: Esi Aram-fia Xazael ku, eye via Ben-Hadad zu fia ɖe eteƒe la,

english_verse: King Jehoash of Israel attacked and defeated the Syrian army three times. He took back from Benhadad all the towns Hazael had captured in battle from his father Jehoahaz.
translation_verse: tete Yoaxaz vi Yoas gaxɔ du, siwo Xazael xɔ le fofoa Yoaxaz si le aʋa me la, le via Ben-Hadad si. Zi etɔ̃ Yoas sii, eye wògaxɔ Israel-duwo.

english_verse: Jeroboam extended the boundaries of Israel from Lebo-Hamath in the north to the Dead Sea in the south, just as the Lord had promised his servant Jonah son of Amittai, who was a prophet from Gath-Hepher.
translation_verse: Egbugbɔ Israel ƒe liƒowo xɔ tso Xamat nutowo me vaseɖe tagbaƒu la nu, abe alesi Yehowa. Israel ƒe Mawu la gblɔ to eƒe dɔla, nyagblɔɖila Yona, Amitai vi, tso Gat-Xefer dzi la ene.

english_verse: Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah in the second year of Jehoash's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Le Israel-fia Yoaxaz ƒe vi Yoas ƒe ƒe evelia me la Amazya, Yuda-fia Yoas ƒe vi, zu fia.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nusi nye vɔ le Yehowa ŋku me, eye meɖe asi le Yerobeam, Nebat vi ƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo katã wòtsɔ ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me la ŋu o.

english_verse: Jeroboam died and was buried, and his son Zechariah became king.
translation_verse: Eye Yerobeam mlɔ fofoa, Israel-fiawo gbɔ, eye via Zaxarya zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Amaziah followed the example of his father Joash by obeying the Lord and doing right. But he was not as faithful as his ancestor David.
translation_verse: Ewo nusi dze Yehowa ŋu, ɖeko meɖe fofoa Dawid nu o, eye wòwɔ pɛpɛpɛ, abe alesi fofoa Yoas wɔ ene.

english_verse: Amaziah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Negbe nuxeƒewo ko womede ɖa o, eye dukɔ la gasa vo hedo dzudzɔ le nuxeƒewo.

english_verse: As soon as Amaziah had control of Judah, he arrested and killed the officers who had murdered his father.
translation_verse: Esime fiaɖuɖu la li ke ɖe esi me la, ewu eƒe dɔla, siwo wu fofoa fia.

english_verse: But the children of those officers were not killed. The Lord had commanded in the Law of Moses that only the people who sinned were to be punished, not their parents or children.
translation_verse: Ke mewu hlɔ̃dolawo ƒe viwo o, abe alesi Yehowa ɖe se gblɔ woŋlɔ ɖe Mose ƒe segbalẽa me ene bena: Womagawu fofowo ɖe viwo nu o, ke boŋ amesiame nèku ɖe eƒe nuvɔ̃ ta.

english_verse: Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. Go ahead and celebrate—but stay at home. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Esi Edomtɔwo, eyata dzi ɖo ƒowò. Wò bubu la nenɔ ŋuwò, ne natsi aƒe; nukaŋuti nèbe, yeade ɖokuiwò dzɔgbevɔ̃e me, eye mia kple Yuda siaa míatsi?

english_verse: One day, Amaziah sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi Amazya do ame ɖo ɖe Israel-fia Yoas, Yehu vi Yoaxaz ƒe vi gbã, ne woagblɔ nɛ bena: Va, ne miakpe akɔ kple mía nɔewo kpɔ!

english_verse: Jehoash sent back this reply: Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon announced that his son was going to marry the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
translation_verse: Tete Israel-fia Yoas da ame ɖo ɖe Yuda-fia Amazya gbã, ne woagblɔ nɛ bena: Ŋuvegoe, si le Libanon dzi la, dɔ ame ɖo ɖe sederti, si le Libanon dzi, gblɔ bena: Tsɔ viwònyɔnu na vinyeŋutsu, ne wòaɖe. Tete gbemelã, siwo le Libanon dzi, va nyã avuzi le ŋuvegoe la dzi.

english_verse: But Amaziah refused to listen. So Jehoash and his troops marched to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops.
translation_verse: Ke Amazya meɖo toe o. Tete Israel-fia Yoas ho va, eye eya kple Yuda-fia Amazya wokpe akɔ le Bet-Semes, si nye Yuda to la.

english_verse: During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home,
translation_verse: Ke Israel si Yuda, eye wo dome amesiame si yi eƒe agbadɔ me.

english_verse: and Jehoash captured Amaziah. Jehoash then marched to Jerusalem and broke down the city wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a section nearly
translation_verse: Israel-fia Yoas lé Yuda-fia Amazya, Axazya vi Yoas ƒe vi, le Bet-Semes, eye wòkplɔe va Yerusalem. Eye wògbã Yerusalem ƒe gli tso Efrayim-gbo la nu vaseɖe dzogoedzigbo la gbɔ, ele abɔklugui alafa ene.

english_verse: He took the gold and silver, as well as everything of value from the Lord's temple and the king's treasury. He took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Eve wòlɔ sika kple klosalowo katã kple nusiwo katã le Yehowa ƒe aƒe kple fia ƒe aƒe ƒe nudzraɖoƒe hekpe ɖe awɔbamewo ŋu, eye wògbugbɔ yi Samaria.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he defeated King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Yoas ŋutinya susɔea, nusiwo wòwɔ kple eƒe kalẽwɔwɔwo kpakple alesi wòwɔ aʋa kple Yuda-fia Amazya la, woŋlɔ woɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: After his death the people of Judah made his son Azariah king, even though he was only
translation_verse: Tete Yuda-dukɔ blibo la tsɔ Azarya, amesi nye ƒe wuiade vi la, ɖo fia ɖe fofoa Amazya teƒe.

english_verse: Azariah was the one who later recaptured and rebuilt the town of Elath. King Jeroboam the Second of Israel
translation_verse: Eyae tso Elat, eye wògaxɔe na Yuda, le esi fia la mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ megbe. Israel-fiaɖuƒe. Yerobeam fia evelia.

english_verse: Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel in the fifteenth year of Amaziah's rule in Judah. Jeroboam ruled
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Amazya, Yoas vi ƒe ƒe wuiatɔ̃lia me la Yerobeam, Israel-fia Yoas ƒe vi, zu fia le Samaria ƒe blane vɔ ɖeke.

english_verse: The Lord helped Jeroboam do this because he had seen how terribly the Israelites were suffering, whether slave or free, and no one was left to help them.
translation_verse: Elabena Yehowa kpɔ Israel ƒe hiã be, enu sẽ ŋutɔ, eye be, ɖeviwo kple ame tsitsiwo siaa nu yi, eye xɔnametɔa ɖeke meli na Israel o.

english_verse: And since the Lord had promised that he would not let Israel be completely destroyed, he helped Jeroboam rescue them.
translation_verse: Elabena Yehowa megblɔ be, yeatutu Israel ƒe ŋkɔ ɖa le dziƒoa te o, eyata wòɖe wo to Yerobeam, Yoas vi la dzi.

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he recaptured the towns of Damascus and Hamath, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Yerobeam ŋutinya susɔea kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ, eƒe kalẽwɔwɔwo kple aʋa, si wòwɔ kpakple alesi wògbugbɔ Damasko kple Xamat, siwo nye Yuda tɔ tsã, na Israel la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Everything else Pekahiah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Pekah of Israel
translation_verse: Pekaxya ŋutinya susɔea kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ la, kpɔ ɖa, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me. Pekax. Asiria-boyo me nɔnɔ dze gɔme.

english_verse: Pekahiah became king of Israel in the fiftieth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Azarya ƒe ƒe blaatɔ̃lia me la Pekaxya, Menaxem vi, zu fia ɖu Israel dzi ƒe eve le Samaria.

english_verse: Azariah obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nusi dze Yehowa ŋu, abe alesi fofoa Amazya wɔ pɛpɛpɛ ene.

english_verse: But Azariah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Negbe nuxeƒewo ko womeɖe ɖa o, eye dukɔ la gasa vɔ hedo dzudzɔ le nuxeƒewo.

english_verse: The Lord punished Azariah with leprosy for the rest of his life. He wasn't allowed to live in the royal palace, so his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
translation_verse: Ke Yehowa ɖe fu na fia la, eye wòdze anyi vaseɖe eƒe kugbe, eye wònɔ xɔa ɖe me le aga. Eye fia ƒe vi Yotam no aƒe la nu hedrɔ̃ ʋɔnu dukɔ hahoo la.

english_verse: Everything else Azariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Azarya ŋutinya susɔea kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Yuda-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Azariah died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Jotham then became king. King Zechariah of Israel
translation_verse: Eye Azarya mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ, eye woɖu ɖe fofoawo gbɔ le Dawid ƒe du la me, eve via Yotam zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Israel fiaɖuƒe. Zaxarya.

english_verse: Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, but he ruled only six months from Samaria.
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Azarya ƒe ƒe blaetɔ̃ vɔ enyilia me la Zaxarya, Yerobeam vi, zu fia ɖe Israel dzi le Samaria dzinu ade.

english_verse: Shallum son of Jabesh plotted against Zechariah and killed him in public. Shallum then became king.
translation_verse: Tete Salum, Yabes vi, ɖo nugbe ɖe eŋu, eye wòwui le Yibleam hezu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: So the Lord had kept his promise to Jehu that the next four kings of Israel would come from his family. Everything else Zechariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Shallum of Israel
translation_verse: Esia nye nya, si Yehowa gblɔ na Yehu bena: Viwòwo anɔ Israel-fiazikpui la dzi vaseɖe dzidzime enelia dzi: eye nenema wòva mee. Salum.

english_verse: Shallum became king of Israel in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's rule in Judah. But only one month after Shallum became king,
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Uziya ƒe ƒe blaetɔ̃ vɔ asiekelia me la Salum, Yabes vi, zu fia, eye woɖu fia le Samaria dzinu ɖeka.

english_verse: Menahem became king of Israel in Azariah's thirty-ninth year as king of Judah, and he ruled Israel ten years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Azarya ƒe ƒe blaetɔ̃ vɔ asiekelia me la Menaxem, Gad vi, zu fia ɖe Israel dzi ƒe ewo le Samaria.

english_verse: He constantly disobeyed the Lord by following the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ewo nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me, eye meɖe asi le Yerobeam, Nebat vi ƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wòtsɔ ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me la ŋu o.

english_verse: During Menahem's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria invaded Israel. He agreed to help Menahem keep control of his kingdom, if Menahem would pay him over
translation_verse: Eŋɔli Asur-fia Pul va dze anyigba la dzi, eye Menaxem tsa klosalo talento akpe ɖeka na Pul, be woakpe ɖe ye ŋu, ne fiaɖuɖu la nali ke ɖe ye si me.

english_verse: Jotham followed the example of his father by obeying the Lord and doing right.
translation_verse: Ewo nusi dze Yehowa ŋu; alesi fofoa Uziya wɔ la, nenema pɛpɛpɛ wòwɔ.

english_verse: Everything else Menahem did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Menaxem ŋutinya susɔea kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king. King Pekahiah of Israel
translation_verse: Eye Menaxem mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ, eye via Pekaxya zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Pekaxya.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and caused the Israelites to sin, just as Jeroboam son of Nebat had done.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nusi nye vɔ le Yehowa ŋku me, eye meɖe asi le Yerobeam, Nebat vi ƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wòtsɔ ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me la ŋu o.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and followed the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me, eye meɖe asi le Yerobeam, Nebat vi ƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wotso ble Israel de nuvɔ̃ me la ŋu o.

english_verse: During Pekah's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria marched into Israel. He captured the territories of Gilead and Galilee, including the towns of Ijon, Abel-Bethmaacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, as well as the entire territory of Naphtali. Then he took Israelites from those regions to Assyria as prisoners.
translation_verse: Le Israel-fia Pekax ŋɔli la Asur-fia Tiglat-Pileser va, eye wòxɔ Yion, Abel-Bet-Maaxa, Yanoax, Kedes, Xazor, Gilead kple Galilea, si nye Naftali-nyigba blibo la, eye wòkplɔ wo yi Asur.

english_verse: In the twentieth year of Jotham's rule in Judah, Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah and murdered him. Hoshea then became king of Israel.
translation_verse: Tete Xosea, Ela vi, ɖo nugbe ɖe Pekax, Remalya vi la ŋu, eye wòwui hezu fia ɖe eteƒe le Yotam, Uziya vi ƒe ƒe blavelia me.

english_verse: Everything else Pekah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Jotham of Judah (
translation_verse: Pekax ŋutinya susɔea kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ la, kpɔ ɖa, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me. Yuda-fiaɖuƒe. Fia Yotam.

english_verse: Jotham son of Azariah became king of Judah in the second year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Le Israel-fia Pekax, Remalya vi ƒe ƒe evelia me la Yotam, Yuda-fia Uziya ƒe vi, zu fia.

english_verse: It was Jotham who rebuilt the Upper Gate that led into the court around the Lord's temple. But the local shrines were not destroyed, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Negbe nuxeƒewo ko womeɖe ɖa o, eye dukɔ la gasa vɔ hedo dzudzɔ le nuxeƒewo. Eyae de dzigbegbo le Yehowa ƒe aƒe la nu.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Yotam ŋutinya susɔea kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Yuda-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: During his rule, the Lord let King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel start attacking Judah.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi Yehowa de asi Aram-fia Rezin kple Pekax, Remalya vi dɔdɔ me ɖe Yuda ŋu.

english_verse: Jotham died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Eye Yotam mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ, eye woɖu ɖe fofoawo gbɔ ɖe fofoa Dawid ƒe du la me, eye via Axaz zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah in the seventeenth year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Le Pekax, Remalya vi ƒe ƒe wuiadrelia me la Axaz, Yuda-fia Yotam ƒe vi, zu fia.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Hezekiah became king.
translation_verse: Eye Axaz mia fofoawo gbɔ, eye woɖii ɖe fofoawo gbɔ ɖe Dawid ƒe du la me, eye via Xizkiya zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Uriah did everything Ahaz told him.
translation_verse: Eye nunɔla Uriya wo pɛpɛpɛ, abe alesi fia la de se ene.

english_verse: and was even more sinful than the kings of Israel. He sacrificed his own son, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
translation_verse: ke boŋ eto Israel-fiawo ƒe ʋe me; gɔglɔ̃gɔ la ena viawo to dzo me le dukɔ, siwo Yehowa nyã le Israel-viwo ŋgɔ la ƒe ŋunyɔnuwo nu.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Esa vɔ, eye wòdo dzudzɔ le nuxeƒewo, togbɛwo dzi kple ati damawo katã te.

english_verse: Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria that said, “Your Majesty, King Rezin and King Pekah are attacking me, your loyal servant. Please come and rescue me.”
translation_verse: Tete Axaz dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Asur-fia Tiglat-Pileser, ne woagblɔ nɛ bena: Wò dɔla kple viwò menye, va, ne naɖem tso Aram-fia kple Israel-fia, amesiwo tso ɖe ŋunye la si me.

english_verse: Along with the message, Ahaz sent silver and gold from the Lord's temple and from the palace treasury as a gift for the Assyrian king.
translation_verse: Eye Axaz tso klosalo kple sika, si le Yehowa ƒe aƒe kple fia ƒe aƒe fe nudzraɖoƒe la, wo nunanae ɖo ɖe Asur-fia.

english_verse: Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one.
translation_verse: Tete fia Axaz yi, be yeakpe Asur-fia Tiglat-Pileser le Damasko. Esi fia Axaz kpo vɔsamlekpui, si le Damasko la, eɖo eƒe nɔnɔme ɖe nunɔla Uriya, eye wotae, abe alesi wowɔe pɛpɛpɛ ene.

english_verse: Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
translation_verse: Eye nunɔla Uriya ɖi vɔsamlekpui la; alesi fia Axaz ɖoe ɖa tso Damasko la, nenema pɛpɛpɛ nunɔla Uriya wɔe, hafi fia Axaz gbɔ tso Damasko.

english_verse: When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar
translation_verse: Esi ha la gbɔ tso Damasko, eye wòkpɔ vɔsamlekpuia la, ede vɔsamlekpui la dzi, eye wòsa vɔ le edzi.

english_verse: and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings.
translation_verse: Etɔ dzo eƒe numevɔsa kple nuɖuvɔsawo le edzi, eye wòkɔ eƒe nunovɔsawo ɖe edzi, eye wohlẽ eƒe akpedavɔsa ƒe ʋu ɖe vɔsamlekpui la dzi.

english_verse: After that, he had the bronze altar moved aside, so his new altar would be right in front of the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Ke ete akɔblivɔsamlekpui, si le Yehowa ŋku me le xɔa ŋgɔdze la ɖa, be maganɔ vɔsamlekpui; la kple Yehowa ƒe xɔ la domee o, eye wòtsɔe ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ƒe axa dzi le anyiehe gome.

english_verse: He told Uriah the priest: From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
translation_verse: Eye fia Axaz de se na nunɔla Uriya gblɔ bena: Sa ŋdinumevɔ kple fiẽnuɖuvɔ kple fia ƒe numevɔ kple eƒe nuɖuvɔ kpakple dukɔ hahoo la katã ƒe numevɔ kple nuɖuvɔ kpakple woƒe nunovɔwo le vɔsamlekpui gã la dzi, eye hlẽ woƒe numevɔsa kple akpedavɔsa ƒe nuwo katã ɖe edzi. Ke akɔblivɔsamlekpui la nena anyi, mana eŋuti bum kpɔ.

english_verse: Ahaz also had the side panels and the small bowls taken off the movable stands in the Lord's temple. He had the large bronze bowl, called the Sea, removed from the bronze bulls on which it rested and had it placed on a stand made of stone.
translation_verse: Fia Axaz gbã anyinɔawo kɔgo, eye wòɖe zeawo ɖa le wo dzi, eɖe gazɔ, si le akɔblinyiawo dzi la, ɖe anyi hetsɔe ɖo kpewo dzi.

english_verse: He took down the special tent that was used for worship on the Sabbath and closed up the private entrance that the kings of Judah used for going into the temple. He did all these things to please Tiglath Pileser.
translation_verse: Eye wòɖe dzudzɔgbekpata, si wotu ɖe xɔ la ŋu, kple fia ƒe toƒe, si le gota gome la ɖa le Yehowa ƒe xɔ la ŋu le Asur-fia ta.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Axaz ŋutinya susɔea kple nusiwo wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Yuda-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz's rule in Judah, and he ruled nine years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Axaz ƒe ƒe wuievelia me la Hosea, Ela vi, zu fia ɖu Israel dzi ƒe asieke le Samaria.

english_verse: Hoshea disobeyed the Lord and sinned, but not as much as the earlier Israelite kings had done.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me, ke menye abe Israel-fia, siwo nɔ ŋgɔ nɛ la ene o.

english_verse: During Hoshea's rule, King Shalmaneser of Assyria invaded Israel; he took control of the country and made Hoshea pay taxes.
translation_verse: Eye Asur-fia Salmanaser ho ɖe eŋu, eye Hosea zu eƒe dɔla hedzo nu nɛ.

english_verse: But later, Hoshea refused to pay the taxes and asked King So of Egypt to help him rebel. When Shalmaneser found out, he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison. Samaria Is Destroyed and the Israelites Are Taken to Assyria
translation_verse: Ke Asur-fia kpɔ be, Hosea ɖo nugbe ɖe eŋu, elabena edo ame ɖo ɖe Egipte-fia So, eye megatsɔ nunana vɛ na Asur-fia abe ƒe sia ƒe ene o; tete Asur-fia lée, eye wòblae tso de gaxɔ me.

english_verse: Shalmaneser invaded Israel and attacked the city of Samaria for three years,
translation_verse: Eye Asur-fia ho va anyigba blibo la dzi, eye woho ɖe Samaria ŋu heɖe to ɖee ƒe etɔ̃.

english_verse: before capturing it in the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. The Assyrian king took the Israelites away to Assyria as prisoners. He forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
translation_verse: Le Hosea ƒe ƒe asiekelia me la Asur-fia xɔ Samaria, eye wòkplɔ Israel yi Asur hetsɔ wo ɖo Xalax kple Xabor le Gozan-tɔsisi la nu kpakple Media-duwo me. Asiriatɔwo ɖe aboyo Israel le eƒe megbedede ta.

english_verse: All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods,
translation_verse: Elabena Israel-viwo wɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Yehowa, woƒe Mawu, si kplɔ wo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi tso Egipte-fia Farao ƒe ŋusẽ nu la ŋu, eye wovɔ̃ mawu bubuwo.

english_verse: followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel, and were just as sinful as the Israelite kings.
translation_verse: Wozɔ de dukɔ, siwo Yehowa nyã le Israel-viwo ŋgɔ la ƒe ɖoɖowo kple Israel-fiawo ƒe ɖoɖowo nu.

english_verse: Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Israel-viwo wɔ nusi menyo Yehowa, woƒe Mawu ŋu o la, le adza me, eye wotu nuxeƒewo ɖe woƒe duwo katã me, ɖe dzɔlawo ƒe miwo kple du sesẽwo siaa gbɔ.

english_verse: They also built stone images of foreign gods and set up sacred poles for the worship of Asherah on every hill and under every shady tree.
translation_verse: Woli aƒeliwo kple Aserawo ɖe togbɛ kɔkɔwo katã dzi kple ati damawo katã te;

english_verse: They offered sacrifices at the shrines, just as the foreign nations had done before the Lord forced them out of Israel. They did sinful things that made the Lord very angry.
translation_verse: eye wodo dzudzɔ le afima le nuxeƒewo katã abe dukɔ, siwo Yehowa nyã le wo ŋgɔ ene, eye wowɔ nu vɔ̃ɖiwo, be woatsɔ ado dziku na Yehowa.

english_verse: Even though the Lord had commanded the Israelites not to worship idols, they did it anyway.
translation_verse: Wosubɔ legbawo, evɔ wònye Yehowa gblɔ na wo be, migawɔe o hafi!

english_verse: So the Lord made sure that every prophet warned Israel and Judah with these words: “I, the Lord, command you to stop doing sinful things and start obeying my laws and teachings! I gave them to your ancestors, and I told my servants the prophets to repeat them to you.”
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa xlɔ̃ nu Israel kple Yuda to eƒe nyagblɔɖilawo katã, siwo nye nukpɔlawo la dzi gblɔ bena: Mitrɔ tso miaƒe mɔ vɔwo dzi, eye milé nye sewo kple nye dodowo me ɖe asi, abe alesi mede se na mia fofowo kple alesi mede nye dɔla nyagblɔɖilawo si ɖo ɖe mi la ene.

english_verse: But the Israelites would not listen; they were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to worship the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Ke womeɖo to o, hafi boŋ wosẽ ta me abe wo fofo, siwo mexɔ Yehowa, woƒe Mawu dzi se o la ene

english_verse: They ignored the Lord's warnings and commands, and they rejected the solemn agreement he had made with their ancestors. They worshiped worthless idols and became worthless themselves. The Lord had told the Israelites not to do the things that the foreign nations around them were doing, but Israel became just like them.
translation_verse: Wodo vlo eƒe ɖoɖowo kple nu, si wobla kple wo fofowo kpakple eƒe se, si wòde na wo la, eye wowɔ yakanuwo hezu ame ɖigbɔwo, eye wodze dukɔ, siwo ƒo xlã wo la yome, eva wònye Yehowa de se na wo be, womegawɔ abe woawo ene o hafi.

english_verse: The people of Israel disobeyed all the commands of the Lord their God. They made two gold statues of calves and set up a sacred pole for Asherah; they also worshiped the stars and the god Baal.
translation_verse: Woɖe asi le Yehowa, woƒe Mawu ƒe sewo katã ŋu, eye wokɔ legbawo, siwo nye nyivi eve, wowɔ Aserawo, eye wode ta agu na dziƒonuwo katã, eye wosubɔ Baal.

english_verse: They used magic and witchcraft and even sacrificed their own children. The Israelites were determined to do whatever the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Wona wo viŋutsuwo kple wo vinyɔnuwo to dzo me, woka afã hesa dzo, eye wotsɔ wo ɖokui ƒle na nu vɔ̃ɖi wowɔ le Yehowa ŋku me, ne woatsɔ aɖo dɔmedzoe nɛ.

english_verse: The Lord became so furious with the people of Israel that he allowed them to be carried away as prisoners. Only the people living in Judah were left,
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa do dɔmedzoe ɖe Israel ŋuti ŋutɔ, eye wòɖe wo ɖa le eƒe ŋku ta; wo dometɔa ɖeke mekpɔtɔ o, negbe Yuda-to la ko.

english_verse: but they also disobeyed the Lord's commands and acted like the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ke Yuda hã melé Yehowa, eƒe Mawu ƒe seawo me ɖe asi o, eye wozɔ le ɖoɖo, siwo Israel ɖo la nu.

english_verse: So the Lord turned his back on everyone in Israel and let them be punished and defeated until no one was left.
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa gbe Israel ƒe dzidzimeviwo katã, eye wote wo de anyi, etso wo de asi na adzodalawo vaseɖe esime wòɖe wo ɖa le eƒe ŋku ta.

english_verse: Earlier, when the Lord took the northern tribes away from David's family, the people living in northern Israel chose Jeroboam son of Nebat as their king. Jeroboam caused the Israelites to sin and to stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Elabena Israel fe eɖokui da le Dawid ƒe aƒe la ŋu, eye wotsɔ Yerobeam, Nebat vi la, ɖo fiae, eye Yerobeam ɖe Israel ɖa tso Yehowa ŋu heble wo de nuvɔ̃ gã me.

english_verse: until the Lord got rid of them, just as he had warned his servants the prophets. That's why the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners to Assyria, and that's where they remained. Foreigners Are Resettled in Israel
translation_verse: vaseɖe esime Yehowa ɖe Israel ɖa le eƒe ŋku ta, abe alesi wògblɔ to eƒe dɔla, nyagblɔɖilawo katã dzi ene, eye wòkplɔ Israel tso eƒe anyigba dzi yi Asur vaseɖe egbe. Samariatɔwo ƒe gɔmedze ŋu nyawo.

english_verse: The king of Assyria took people who were living in the cities of Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and forced them to move to Israel. They took over the towns where the Israelites had lived, including the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Eye Asur-fia kplɔ amewo tso Babel, Kuta, Awa, Xamat kple Sefarwayim, eye wòna wonɔ Samaria-duwo me ɖe Israel-viwo teƒe, eye woxɔ Samaria henɔ eƒe duwo me.

english_verse: At first these people did not worship the Lord, so he sent lions to attack them, and the lions killed some of them.
translation_verse: Ke esime wova afima tete la, womeyɔ Yehowa o, eyata Yehowa kplɔ dzatawo de wo, eye wowu amewo le wo dome.

english_verse: A messenger told the king of Assyria, “The people you moved to Israel don't know how to worship the god of that country. So he sent lions that have attacked and killed some of them.”
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ na Asur-fia bena: Dukɔ, siwo nèkplɔ yii, be woadanɔ Samaria-duwo me la, menya anyigba dzi mawu la ƒe kɔnuwo o, eyata wòkplɔ dzatawo de wo wowu wo, elabena womenya anyigba dzi mawu la ƒe kɔnu wo o.

english_verse: The king replied, “Get one of the Israelite priests we brought here and send him back to Israel. He can live there and teach them about the god of that country.”
translation_verse: Tete Asur-fia de se gblɔ bena: Miɖo nunɔla, siwo mieɖakplɔ tso afima la, dome ɖeka ɖa, ne wòayi aɖanɔ afima, eye wòafia anyigba dzi mawu la ƒe kɔnuwo wo.

english_verse: One of the Israelite priests was chosen to go back to Israel. He lived in Bethel and taught the people how to worship the Lord.
translation_verse: Ale nunɔla, siwo wokplɔ dzoe tso Samaria la, dometɔ ɖeka va nɔ Betel, eye wòfia, alesi woavɔ̃ Yehowae la wo.

english_verse: But in towns all over Israel, the different groups of people made statues of their own gods, then they placed these idols in local Israelite shrines.
translation_verse: Ke dukɔ sia dukɔ wɔ mawuwo na eɖokui, eye wotsɔ wo ɖo nuxeƒexɔ, siwo Samariatɔwo wɔ la me; dukɔ sia dukɔ wɔe ɖe du, si me wòle la me.

english_verse: The people from Babylonia made the god Succoth-Benoth; those from Cuthah made the god Nergal; those from Hamath made Ashima;
translation_verse: Babeltɔwo wɔ Sukot-Benot; Kuttɔwo wɔ Nergal, eye Xamattɔwo wɔ Asima;

english_verse: those from Avva made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the people from Sepharvaim sacrificed their children to their own gods Adrammelech and Anammelech.
translation_verse: Awitɔwo wɔ Nibxaz kple Tartak, eye Sefarwayimtɔwo tɔ dzo wo viwo na Adramelex kple Anamelex, siwo nye Sefarwayimtɔwo ƒe mawuwo.

english_verse: They worshiped their own gods, just as they had before they were taken away to Israel. They also worshiped the Lord, but they chose their own people to be priests at the shrines.
translation_verse: Wova Yehowa, eye wogasubɔ woƒe mawuwo le dukɔ, siwo dome wokplɔ wo tsoe la ƒe kɔnuwo nu.

english_verse: Everyone followed their old customs. None of them worshiped only the Lord, and they refused to obey the laws and commands that the Lord had given to the descendants of Jacob, the man he named Israel.
translation_verse: Vaseɖe egbegbe wogale woƒe kɔnu xoxoawo dzi; womevɔ̃a Yehowa ɖeɖe o, eye womewɔna le woƒe dodowo kple woƒe kɔnuwo ɖeɖe nu loo, alo wona le nufiafia kple se, siwo Yehowa de na Yakob, amesi wotsɔ ŋkɔ na be Israel ƒe viwo la nu o.

english_verse: At the time when the Lord had made his solemn agreement with the people of Israel, he told them: Do not worship any other gods! Do not bow down to them or offer them a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Elabena Yehowa bia nu kpli wo, eye wòde se na wo gblɔ bena: Migavɔ̃ mawu bubuwo o, migade ta agu na wo o, migasubɔ wo o, eye migasa vɔ na wo o!

english_verse: Worship only me! I am the one who rescued you from Egypt with my mighty power. Bow down to me and offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ke boŋ mivɔ̃ Yehowa, amesi tsɔ ŋusẽ gã kple abɔ, si wodo de dzi, kplɔ mi tso Egipte-nyigba dzi la; eya miade ta agu na, eye eya miasa vɔ na!

english_verse: and remember the solemn agreement between us. I will say it again: Do not worship any god
translation_verse: Migayɔ nu, si mebia kpli mi la be o, eye migavɔ̃ mawu bubuwo o,

english_verse: except me. I am the Lord your God, and I will rescue you from all your enemies.
translation_verse: ke boŋ mivɔ̃ Yehowa, mia Mawu la, ne wòaɖe miatso miaƒe futɔwo katã si me.

english_verse: But the people living in Israel ignored that command and kept on following their old customs.
translation_verse: Ke womeɖo to o, hafi boŋ wowɔ woƒe kɔnu xoxoawo.

english_verse: They did worship the Lord, but they also worshiped their own idols. Their descendants did the same thing.
translation_verse: Ale dukɔ siawo vɔ̃ Yehowa, eye wosubɔ woƒe legbawo hã; wo viwo kple wo tɔgbuiyɔviwo le alea wɔm vaseɖe egbe abe wo fofowo ene.

english_verse: Stop listening to Hezekiah! Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns
translation_verse: Migado to Xizkiya o! Elabena ale Asur-fia gblɔ esi: Mibla nu kplim, eye mido va gbɔnye, ekema mia dome amesiame aɖu eƒe weintsetse, amesiame aɖu eƒe gbotitsetse, eye amesiame ano eƒe vudo me tsi,

english_verse: Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
translation_verse: Azɔ ɖe Yehowa megbe meto ho ɖe teƒe sia ŋu, be magblẽea? Yehowae gblɔ nam be: Ho ɖe anyigba sia ŋu, eye nagblẽe!

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done.
translation_verse: Eye wòwɔ nusi dze Yehowa ŋu, abe alesi fofoa Dawid wɔ pɛpɛpɛ ene.

english_verse: He destroyed the local shrines, then tore down the images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. He also smashed the bronze snake Moses had made. The people had named it Nehushtan and had been offering sacrifices to it.
translation_verse: Eɖe nuxeƒewo ɖa, eye wògbã aƒeliwo, elã Aserawo, eye wògbã akɔblida, si Mose wɔ la; elabena Israel-viwo do dzudzɔ nɛ vaseɖe ɣemaɣi, eve wòna ŋkɔe be Nexustan.

english_verse: Hezekiah trusted the Lord God of Israel. No other king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before or after him.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu ɖe Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋu, eye etɔgbea ɖeke mena Yuda-fia, siwo katã dze eyome alo do ŋgɔ nɛ la dome o.

english_verse: He was completely faithful to the Lord and obeyed the laws the Lord had given to Moses for the people.
translation_verse: Eku ɖe Yehowa ŋu, eye mele ɖa le eŋu o, eye wòle Yehowa ƒe se, siwo wòde na Mose la me ɖe asi.

english_verse: The Lord helped Hezekiah, so he was successful in everything he did. He even rebelled against the king of Assyria, refusing to be his servant.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa nɔ kplu, afisiafi, si wòyi la, edzea edzi nɛ Eye wòdze aglã ɖe Asur-fia ŋu, eye megasubɔe o.

english_verse: Hezekiah defeated the Philistine towns as far away as Gaza—from the smallest towns to the large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Esi Filistitɔwo vaseɖe Gaza kple eƒe liƒowo gbɔ, tso dzɔlawo ƒe xɔ tsralawo gbɔ vaseɖe du sesẽwo gbɔ.

english_verse: During the fourth year of Hezekiah's rule, which was the seventh year of Hoshea's rule in Israel, King Shalmaneser of Assyria led his troops to Samaria, the capital city of Israel. They attacked
translation_verse: Le fia Xizkiya ƒe ƒe enelia, si nye Israel-fia Hosea, Ela vi ƒe ƒe adrelia me la, Asur-fia Salmanaser ho ɖe Samaria ŋu, eye woɖe to ɖee.

english_verse: and captured it three years later, in the sixth year of Hezekiah's rule and the ninth year of Hoshea's rule.
translation_verse: Exɔe le ƒe etɔ̃ megbe. Woxɔ Samaria le Xizkiya ƒe ƒe adelia me, eya nye Israel-fia Hosea ƒe ƒe asiekelia.

english_verse: All of that happened because the people of Israel had not obeyed the Lord their God. They rejected the solemn agreement he had made with them, and they ignored everything that the Lord's servant Moses had told them. King Sennacherib of Assyria Invades Judah (
translation_verse: Elabena womeɖo to Yehowa, woƒe Mawu ƒe gbe o, eye woda eƒe nubabla kple se, siwo katã Yehowa de na eƒe dɔla Mose la dzi, womeɖo to o, eye womewɔ edzi o. Sanxerib ɖe to ɖe Yerusalem ŋuti.

english_verse: for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards, raise your own grain, and have plenty of olive oil and honey. Believe me, you won't starve there. Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him.
translation_verse: vaseɖe esime mava, eye makplɔ mi ayi anyigba, si le abe mía ta ene la dzi, anyigba, si dzi bli, wein kple abolo, weingblewo, amitiwo kple anyitsi le, ne miano agbe, eye miaku o. Migado to Xizkiya o! Mia blem wòle le gbɔgblɔm be: Yehowa aɖe mí!

english_verse: One of the Assyrian commanders told them: I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself.
translation_verse: Eye Rabsake gblɔ na wo be: Migblɔ na Xizkiya bena: Ale fia gã, Asur-fia, gblɔ esi: Nuka ŋu gɔ̃ nele dzi ɖom ɖo?

english_verse: Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
translation_verse: Ke ne miegblɔ nam be: Yehowa, mia Mawu la ŋu miele dzi ɖom ɖo la, ekema ɖe menye eya ƒe nuxeƒewo kple vɔsamlekpuiwo Xizkiya ɖe ɖa, eye wògblɔ na Yuda kple Yerusalem bena: Miɖe ta agu ɖe vɔsamlekpui sia ŋgɔ le Yerusalem oa?

english_verse: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's rule in Judah, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city, except Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Le Xizkiya ƒe ƒe wuienelia me la Asur-fia Sanxerib ho ɖe Yuda-du sesẽwo katã ŋu, eye wòxɔ wo.

english_verse: Hezekiah sent this message to Sennacherib, who was in the town of Lachish: “I know I am guilty of rebellion. But I will pay you whatever you want, if you stop your attack.” Sennacherib told Hezekiah to pay ten tons of silver and one ton of gold.
translation_verse: Tete Yuda-fia Xizkiya da ame ɖo ɖe Asur-fia le Laxis, ne woagblɔ nɛ bena: Mewɔ nuvɔ̃! Ho dzo le gbɔnye, eye maxɔ nusi natsɔ aɖo dzinye la atso. Eye Asur-fia ɖo klosalo talento alafa etɔ̃ kple sika talento blaetɔ̃ na Yuda fia Xizkiya, be wòaxe.

english_verse: So Hezekiah collected all the silver from the Lord's temple and the royal treasury.
translation_verse: Eye Xizkiya tsa klosalo, siwo katã wòkpɔ le Yehowa ƒe aƒe me kple fia ƒe aƒe ƒe nudzraɖoƒe la hena.

english_verse: He even stripped the gold that he had used to cover the doors and doorposts in the temple. He gave it all to Sennacherib.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi Xizkiya flo sika, siwo Yuda-fia Xizkiya fa ɖe Yehowa ƒe xa ƒe ʋɔtruwo kple sɔtiwo ŋu la, eye wòtsɔ wo na Asur-fia.

english_verse: The king of Assyria ordered his three highest military officers to leave Lachish and take a large army to Jerusalem. When they arrived, the officers stood on the road near the cloth makers' shops along the canal from the upper pool.
translation_verse: Ke Asur-fia do Tartan, Rabsaris kple Rabsake kpakple aʋakɔ gãa ɖe tso Laxis ɖo ɖe Yerusalem ɖe fia Xizkiya ŋu, eye woho heva Yerusalem. Esi woho va la, wotɔ ɖe dzigbeta, si le avɔnyãla ƒe agblenu dzi la, ƒe tɔʋu nu,

english_verse: They called out to Hezekiah, and three of his highest officials came out to meet them. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
translation_verse: eye woyɔ fia la ɖa. Tete Elyakim, Xilkiya vi, amesi le aƒe la nu kple Sebna, agbalẽŋlɔla kpakple Yoax, Asaf vi, ha ƒe tsiami la, wodo yi wo gbɔ.

english_verse: Does he think he can plan and win a war with nothing but words? Who is going to help him, now that he has turned against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Ɖe nèle bubum be, numenya ƒuƒlu enye aɖaŋuɖoɖo kple ŋusẽ hena aʋawɔwɔa? Azɔ tso, ameka ŋu nèle dzi ɖom ɖo, be nedze aglã ɖe ŋunye?

english_verse: Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
translation_verse: Azɔ èle dzi ɖom ɖe aƒla ŋeŋe ma, si nye Egipte la ŋu, esi ne amea ɖe ziɔ ɖe eŋu la, wòŋɔa asi nɛ flo la; alea Egipte-fia le na amesiwo katã le dzi ɖom ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: The king of Assyria wants to make a bet with you people. He will give you
translation_verse: Eyata mia kple nye aƒetɔ, Asur-fia, mitso gbe kpɔ, eye matsɔ sɔ akpe eve na wò, be ate ŋu akpɔ sɔdolawo aɖo wo dzi mahã?

english_verse: How could you even defeat our lowest ranking officer, when you have to depend on Egypt for chariots and cavalry?
translation_verse: Mate ŋu asi aʋafia ɖeka, si nye nye aƒetɔ ƒe dɔlawo dome suetɔ hã o, eye wòa nele dzi ɖom ɖe Egipte gu le sɔwo kple sɔdolawo taa?

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Sir, we don't want the people listening from the city wall to understand what you are saying. So please speak to us in Aramaic instead of Hebrew.”
translation_verse: Tete Elyakim, Xilkiya vi, kple Sebna kpakple Yoax wogblɔ na Rabsake bena: Taflatse, ƒo nu kple wò dɔlawo ɖe Aram-gbe me, elabena míawo míesenɛ, eye megaƒo nu kpli mí ɖe Yuda-gbe me ɖe dukɔ, si le glia dzi la, ƒe to me o.

english_verse: The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you.”
translation_verse: Rabsake ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Ɖe wobe, mia kple wò aƒetɔ gbɔe nye aƒetɔ la dom ɖo, be magblɔ nya siawoa? Ɖe menye ŋutsu siawo, siwo na klotinu le glia dzi, be woaɖu woawo ŋutɔwo ƒe mi, eye woano woƒe aɖuɖɔ kple mi la, gbɔe oa?

english_verse: Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted in Hebrew: Listen to what the great king of Assyria says!
translation_verse: Tete Rabsake le va do ɣli sesĩe le Yuda-gbe me ƒo nu gblɔ bena: Mise fia gã, Asur-fia ƒe gbe!

english_verse: Don't trust him when he tells you that the Lord will protect you from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Eye migana Xizkiya natsɔ Yehowa ade dzi ƒo na mi agblɔ be: Yehowa aɖe mi, eye womatsɔ du sia ade asi na Asur-fia o.

english_verse: Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Ɖe dukɔwo ƒe mawuwo te ŋu ɖe woƒe anyigbawo tso Asur-fia si mea?

english_verse: What happened to the gods of Hamath and Arpad? What about the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces?
translation_verse: Afika Xamat kple Arpad ƒe mawuwo le? Afika Sefarwayim, Hena kple Iwa ƒe mawuwo le? Ɖe wote ŋu ɖe Samaria tso asinye mea?

english_verse: None of these gods kept their people safe from the king of Assyria. Do you think the Lord your God can do any better?
translation_verse: Ɖe anyigbawo ƒe mawuwo katã dometɔa ɖe ɖe eƒe anyigba tso asinye me, ne Yehowa naɖe Yerusalem atso asinye mea?

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.
translation_verse: Eye Elyakim, Xilkiya vi, amesi le aƒea nu, kple Sebna, agbalẽŋlɔla, kpakple Yoax, Asaf vi, fia ƒe tsiami, wole awu vuvuwo me va Xizkiya gbɔ, eye woto Rabsake ƒe nyawo nɛ.

english_verse: One day he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, when his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with their swords. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me, esime wòle gbe dom ɖa le eƒe mawu Nisrox ƒe me la, evia Adramelex kple Sarezer wowui kple yi, eye wòsi yi Ararat-nyigba dzi, eye via Esar-Xadon zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah heard the news, he tore off his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he went into the temple of the Lord.
translation_verse: Esime fia Xizkiya see la, edze eƒe awuwo, eye wòta akpanya heyi Yehowa ƒe aƒe la me.

english_verse: The kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah have all disappeared. Hezekiah Prays (Isaiah
translation_verse: Afika Xamat-fia, Arpad-fia kple du Sefarwayim, Hena kple Iwa ƒe fia le?

english_verse: He told Prime Minister Eliakim, Assistant Prime Minister Shebna, and the senior priests to dress in sackcloth and tell the prophet Isaiah:
translation_verse: Eye wòdo Elyakim, amesi le aƒea nu, kple Sebna, agbalẽŋlɔla, kpakple nunɔlawo ƒe ame tsitsiwo, amesiwo ta akpanya la, ɖo ɖe nyagblɔɖila Yesaya, Amoz vi gbɔ,

english_verse: These are difficult and disgraceful times. Our nation is like a woman too weak to give birth, when it's time for her baby to be born.
translation_verse: ne woagblɔ nɛ bena: Ale Xizkiya gblɔ esi: Egbe enye xaxa-, tohehe-kple vlodogbe; elabena viwo ɖo dzidzi me, gake ŋusẽ meli, ne wòadzi wo o.

english_verse: Please pray for those of us who are left alive. The king of Assyria sent his army commander to insult the living God. Perhaps the Lord heard what he said and will do something, if you will pray.
translation_verse: Ɖewohi Yehowa, wò Mawu, se Rabsake, amesi eƒe aƒetɔ Asur-fia dɔ ɖo ɖa, be wòaɖe alɔme le Mawu gbagbe la ŋu la ƒe nyawo katã, eye woahe to nɛ le nya, siwo Yehowa, wò Mawu, se la ta; eyata ɖo gbe ɖa ɖe ame susɔe, siwo li la ta!

english_verse: When these leaders went to Isaiah,
translation_verse: Eye Xizkiya ƒe dɔlawo va Yesaya gbɔ.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had this message for Hezekiah: I am the Lord. Don't worry about the insulting things that have been said about me by these messengers from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Tete Yesaya gblɔ na wo bena: Ale miagblɔ na miaƒe aƒetɔ enye si: Yehowa ƒe gbe enye si: Megavɔ̃ nya, siwo Asur-fia ƒe ɖekakpuiwo tso ɖe alɔme le ŋunye nèse la o!

english_verse: I will upset him with rumors about what's happening in his own country. He will go back, and there I will make him die a violent death.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, made gbɔgbɔa ɖe eme, eye wòase nyaa ɖe ahagbugbɔ avi eƒe anyigba dzi, eye mana woatsi yi nu le eƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.
translation_verse: Esi Rabsake gbugbɔ yi la, ekpɔ Asur-fia wòle aʋa wɔm kple Libna, elabena ese be, eho tso Laxis.

english_verse: About this same time the king of Assyria learned that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia was on his way to attack him. Then the king of Assyria sent some messengers with this note for Hezekiah:
translation_verse: Ke esi wose le Kus-fia Tirhaka ŋu be: Kpɔ ɖa, eho, be yeawɔ aʋa kpli wò la, egadɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Xizkiya, ne woagblɔ nɛ bena:

english_verse: Don't trust your God or be fooled by his promise to defend Jerusalem against me.
translation_verse: Ale miagblɔ na Xizkiya enye si: Megana wò Mawu, si ŋu nèle dzi ɖom ɖo la, naɖu wò nagblɔ be: womatsɔ Yerusalem ade asi na Asur-fia o.

english_verse: You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe?
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, wò ŋutɔ èse nusi Asur-fia wo anyigbawo katã, vaseɖe esime wotsrɔ̃ wo, eye woaɖe wò ya?

english_verse: The Assyrian kings before me destroyed the towns of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and everyone from Eden who lived in Telassar. What good did their gods do them?
translation_verse: Ɖe dukɔ, siwo fofonyewo tsrɔ̃: Gozan, Xaran, Rezef kple Eden-viwo, siwo le Telasar la ƒe mawuwo ɖe woa?

english_verse: After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see.
translation_verse: Esi Xizkiya xa agbalẽa le dɔlawo si xlẽe la, eyi Yehowa ƒe aƒe la me, eye Xizkiya kekee ɖe Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: Isaiah went to Hezekiah and told him that the Lord God of Israel had said: Hezekiah, I heard your prayer about King Sennacherib of Assyria.
translation_verse: Tete Yesaya, Amoz vi, dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Xizkiya gblɔ bena: Ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Gbe, si nèdo ɖa nam le Asur-fia Sanxerib ŋuti la, mesee.

english_verse: He prayed: Lord God of Israel, your throne is above the winged creatures. You created the heavens and the earth, and you alone rule the kingdoms of this world.
translation_verse: Eye Xizkiya do gbe ɖa le Yehowa ŋku me gblɔ bena: Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, asi nɔa Kerubiwo dzi, wò ɖeka koe nye Mawu ɖe anyigba dzi fiaɖuƒewo katã dzi, wòe wo dziƒo kple anyigba.

english_verse: It is true, our Lord, that Assyrian kings have turned nations into deserts.
translation_verse: Yehowa, Asur-fiawo nya tsrɔ̃ dukɔwo kple woƒe anyigbawo vava.

english_verse: They destroyed the idols of wood and stone that the people of those nations had made and worshiped.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ woƒe mawuwo de dzo me, elabena menye mawuwo wonye o, ke boŋ amegbetɔwo ƒe asinu dɔwɔwɔwoe, ati kple kpewo wonye, eyata wo srɔ̃ wo.

english_verse: But you are our Lord and our God! We ask you to keep us safe from the Assyrian king. Then everyone in every kingdom on earth will know that you are the only God. The Lord's Answer to Hezekiah (Isaiah
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa, mia Mawu, ɖe mi tso esi me dzro, ne anyigba dzi tiaɖuƒewo katã nadze sii bena, wò ɖeka koe nye Yehowa Mawu!

english_verse: Now this is what I say to that king: The people of Jerusalem hate and make fun of you; they laugh behind your back.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ ɖe eŋu enye si: Ɖetugbi, Zion vinyɔnu, ɖe alɔme le ŋuwo, eye wòke wò, Yerusalem vinyɔnu ʋuʋu ta ɖe yowòme.

english_verse: Sennacherib, you cursed, shouted, and sneered at me, the holy God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ameka nedo vloe, eye ameka ŋu neɖu fewu le, ameka ta nèɖo ɣli ɖo, eve ameka ŋu nèfɔ mo dzi ɖo? Israel ƒe kɔkɔetɔ lae loo!

english_verse: You let your officials insult me, the Lord. And this is how you bragged about yourself: “I led my chariots to the highest heights of Lebanon's mountains. I went deep into its forest, cutting down the best cedar and cypress trees.
translation_verse: Edo vlo Aƒetɔ la to wò dɔlawo dzi gblɔ bena: Metsɔ nye tasiaɖam gbogboawo va toawo ta me kple Libanon ƒe tsutsuẽ aƒe, eye melã eƒe sederti kɔkɔwo kple eƒe sesewu nyuitɔwo, azɔ mege ɖe eƒe nɔƒe kɔkɔwo kple eƒe abɔmeti dodowo gbɔ;

english_verse: I dried up every stream in the land of Egypt, and I drank water from wells I had dug.”
translation_verse: meɖe vudo, eye meno du bubu me tɔwo ƒe tsi, eye metsɔ nye afɔƒome na Egipte tɔsisiwo katã mie.

english_verse: Sennacherib, now listen to me, the Lord. I planned all this long ago. And you don't even realize that I alone am the one who decided that you would do these things. I let you make ruins of fortified cities.
translation_verse: Mesee kpɔ be, metre ewɔwɔ tso tititi ke, eye meɖoe tso gbaɖegbe ke oa? Azɔ mena wòva me, be wogblẽ du sesẽwo wòzu glikpo.

english_verse: Their people became weak, terribly confused. They were like wild flowers or tender young grass growing on a flat roof, scorched before it matures.
translation_verse: Wo me nɔlawo ƒe lãme tu, dzi ɖe le wo ƒo, eye ŋu kpe wo; woɖi agblemenu kple gbe mumu, xɔtagbe kple bli, si tsi tonu hafi va ƒu.

english_verse: I know all about you, even how fiercely angry you are with me.
translation_verse: Menya wò anyinɔnɔ, wo dodo kple wò gbɔgbɔ kpakple wò agbodzedze ɖe ŋunye.

english_verse: I have seen your pride and the tremendous hatred you have for me. Now I will put a hook in your nose, a bit in your mouth, then I will send you back to where you came from.
translation_verse: Esi wò agbodzedze ɖe ŋunye kple wò dada va nye to me ŋuti la, eyata made nye ga wò ŋɔti, eye made nye numega nu na wò akplɔ wò agbugbɔ ato mɔ, si neto va la.

english_verse: Hezekiah, I will tell you what's going to happen. This year you will eat crops that grow on their own, and the next year you will eat whatever springs up where those crops grew. But the third year you will plant grain and vineyards, and you will eat what you harvest.
translation_verse: Eye esia anye dzesi na wò. Le ƒe sia me la miaɖu nusiwo mie le wo ɖokui si, eye le ƒe evelia me la miaɖu flu me nuwo, eye le ƒe etɔ̃lia me la miaƒã nu aŋe nu, eye miade weingblewo aɖu wo me kutsetsewo.

english_verse: Those who survive in Judah will be like a vine that puts down deep roots and bears fruit.
translation_verse: Yuda ƒe aƒe la ƒe amesiwo woɖe, eye wòkpɔtɔ la, aɖe ke aɖo ta to me, eye woatse ku ɖe dzi me.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will see to it that some who live in Jerusalem will survive.
translation_verse: Elabena ame susɔeawo ado tso Yerusalem, eye amesiwo woɖe la, atso Zion-to la dzi; Yehowa Zebaot ƒe ŋuʋaʋã la le esia wo ge.

english_verse: I promise that the king of Assyria won't get into Jerusalem, or shoot an arrow into the city, or even surround it and prepare to attack.
translation_verse: Eyata ale Yehowa gblɔ ɖe Asur-fia ŋu enye si; Mava du sia me o, eye mada aŋutrɔ ɖe eme o, mate ɖe eŋu kple akpoxɔnu o, eye maƒu kpo ɖe eŋu o.

english_verse: As surely as I am the Lord, he will return by the way he came and will never enter Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Agbugbɔ ato mo, si dzi wòto va, eye mava du sia me o Yehowa ƒe gbee nye esia!

english_verse: I will protect it for myself and for my servant David. The Death of King Sennacherib (Isaiah
translation_verse: Makpɔ du sia ta, eye maɖee, le nye ŋutɔ kple nye dɔla Dawid ta. Asurtɔwo le toyiyi le nukumɔa ɖe dzi. Sanxerib ku.

english_verse: After this King Sennacherib went back to Assyria and lived in the city of Nineveh.
translation_verse: Tete Asur-fia Sanxerib ho dzo gbugbɔ yi aƒe, eye woɖanɔ Niniwe.

english_verse: Hezekiah died, and his son Manasseh became king.
translation_verse: Eye Xizkiya mlɔ fofoawo gbɔ, eye via Manase zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: “Don't forget that I have been faithful to you, Lord. I have obeyed you with all my heart, and I do whatever you say is right.” After this, he cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Oo Yehowa, ɖo ŋu, alesi mezɔ le ŋkuwò me le nyateƒe kple dzi blibo me, kple alesi mewo nusi nyo le ŋkuwò me la. Eye Xizkiya fa avi kple ɣli.

english_verse: Before Isaiah got to the middle court of the palace,
translation_verse: Esi Yesaya mekpɔ do le dua titina o la, Yehowa ƒe gbe va egbɔ bena:

english_verse: the Lord sent him back to Hezekiah with this message: Hezekiah, you are the ruler of my people, and I am the Lord God, who was worshiped by your ancestor David. I heard you pray, and I saw you cry. I will heal you, so that three days from now you will be able to worship in my temple.
translation_verse: Gbugbɔ yi ɖagblɔ na nye dukɔ ƒe amegã Xizkiya bena: Ale Yehowa, fofowò Dawid ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Mese wò gbedodoɖa, eye mekpɔ wò aɖatsiwo, kpɔ ɖa, mayɔ dɔ wò, eye le ŋkeke etɔ̃agbe la ayi Yehowa ƒe me.

english_verse: “What did you show them?” Isaiah asked. Hezekiah answered, “I showed them everything in my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ be: Nuka wokpɔ le aƒewò me? Xizkiya ɖo ŋu be: Wokpɔ nusiwo katã le aƒenye me la, naneke mele nye ke sinɔnuwo me, si nyemetsɔ fia wo o.

english_verse: Then Isaiah said to the king's servants, “Bring some mashed figs and place them on the king's open sore. He will then get well.”
translation_verse: Eye Yesaya gblɔ bena: Mitso gbotsetsebolo vɛ! Eye wotsɔe va do ƒoƒoeawo dzi, tete wòhaya.

english_verse: Isaiah replied, “The Lord will prove to you that he will keep his promise. Will the shadow made by the setting sun on the stairway go forward ten steps or back ten steps?”
translation_verse: Yesaya ɖo ŋu be: Esia nye dzesi tso Yehowa gbɔ be, Yehowa le nusi wògblɔ la wɔ ge. Ɖe vɔvɔli la nayi ŋgɔ ɖoƒe ewo loo, alo negbugbɔ ɖe megbe ɖoƒe ewoa?

english_verse: “It's normal for the sun to go forward,” Hezekiah answered. “But how can it go back?”
translation_verse: Xizkiya gblɔ bena: Mesesẽ be, vɔvɔli nayi ŋgɔ ɖoƒe ewo o, ke boŋ vɔvɔli la negbugbɔ ɖe megbe ɖoƒe ewo.

english_verse: Isaiah prayed, and the Lord made the shadow go back ten steps on the stairway built for King Ahaz. The Lord Is Still with Hezekiah (Isaiah
translation_verse: Tete nyagblɔɖila Yesaya yɔ Yehowa, eye wòna vɔvɔli, si yi ŋgɔ la, gbugbɔ yi ɖoƒe la dzi; egbugbɔ ɖe megbe le Axaz ƒe ɣega la dzi ɖoƒe ewo. Xizkiya wɔ bometsinu le Hebritɔwo ƒe ame dɔdɔwo ŋku me, eye woku.

english_verse: Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, was now king of Babylonia. And when he learned that Hezekiah had been sick, he sent messengers with letters and a gift for him.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi Babel-fia Berodax-Baladan, Baladan vi, ɖo agbalẽ kple nunanawo ɖe Xizkiya, elabena ese be, Xizkiya lé dɔ.

english_verse: Hezekiah welcomed the messengers and showed them all the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oils that were in his storehouse. He even showed them where he kept his weapons. Nothing in his palace or in his entire kingdom was kept hidden from them.
translation_verse: Eye Xizkiya ɖo to wo, eye wòfia eƒe kesinɔnuxɔwo katã, klosalo kple sika, atike ʋeʋẽe kple ami xɔasi kple aʋawɔnuxɔ kpakple nusiwo katã le eƒe kesinɔnuwo me la wo, naneke meli, si Xizkiya metsɔ fia wo le eƒe aƒe kple eƒe fiaɖuƒe blibo la me o.

english_verse: Isaiah asked Hezekiah, “Where did these men come from? What did they want?” “They came all the way from Babylonia,” Hezekiah answered.
translation_verse: Tete nyagblɔɖila Yesaya va fia Xizkiya gbɔ gblɔ ne bena: Nya ka ŋutsu siawo gblɔ, eye afika wotso va gbɔwò? Xizkiya ɖo ŋu bena: Wotso kekeke Babel ke.

english_verse: Then Isaiah told Hezekiah: I have a message for you from the Lord.
translation_verse: Tete Yesaya gblɔ na Xizkiya bena: Se Yehowa ƒe gbe!

english_verse: One day everything you and your ancestors have stored up will be taken to Babylonia. The Lord has promised that nothing will be left.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ŋkekewo gbɔna, esime wòala nusiwo katã le aƒewò me kple nusiwo fofowòwo tu ɖo vaseɖe egbe la, ayi Babel, naneke makpɔtɔ o; Yehowa gblɔe!

english_verse: Some of your own sons will be taken to Babylonia, where they will be disgraced and made to serve in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Eye woakplɔ viwòŋutsu, siwo dzɔ tso mewò, amesiwo nèdzi la, dometɔa ɖewo woaɖanye aƒemenu dzikpɔlawo le Babel-fia ƒe me.

english_verse: Hezekiah thought, “At least our nation will be at peace for a while.” So he told Isaiah, “The message you brought me from the Lord is good.” Hezekiah Dies (
translation_verse: Xizkiya ɖo ŋu na Yesaya bena: Yehowa ƒe gbe, si nègblɔ la, enyo. Eye wògagblɔ tomefafa kple nuteƒewɔwɔ nya le nye ŋkekewo me ko evɔ.

english_verse: Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he made the upper pool and tunnel bring water into Jerusalem, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Xizkiya ŋutinya susɔea kple eƒe kalẽwɔwɔwo katã, alesi wòɖe ta kple tɔʋui, eye wòhe tsi va dua mee la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Yuda-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: years. His mother Meshullemeth was the daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.
translation_verse: Eye wòwɔ nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me, le dukɔ, siwo Yehowa nyã le Israel-viwo ŋgɔ la ƒe ŋunyɔnuwo nu.

english_verse: Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done.
translation_verse: Eye wòwɔ nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me, abe alesi fofoa Manase wo ene.

english_verse: Now I, the Lord God of Israel, will destroy both Jerusalem and Judah! People will hear about it but won't believe it.
translation_verse: eyata ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ava Yerusalem kple Yuda dzi, ale be amesiwo katã asee la, ƒe towo kple eve me laɖi yeŋ.

english_verse: He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah, just as King Ahab of Israel had done. And he faithfully worshiped the stars in heaven.
translation_verse: Egagbugbɔ nuxeƒe, siwo fofoa Xizkiya gbã la tu, eɖi vɔsamlekpuiwo na Baal, eye wòwɔ Asera, abe alesi Israel-fia Axab wɔ ene, eye wòde ta agu na dziƒonuwo katã hesubɔ wo.

english_verse: In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods
translation_verse: Eɖi vɔsamlekpuiwo ɖe Yehowa ƒe aƒe, si ŋu Yehowa gblɔ le be, yeatsɔ yeƒe ŋkɔ aɖo Yerusalem la me.

english_verse: and the stars. He placed these altars in both courts of the temple,
translation_verse: Eye wòɖi vɔsamlekpuiwo na dziƒonuwo katã ɖe Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ƒe xɔxɔnuwo kple eve.

english_verse: and even set up the pole for Asherah there. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own son. He did many sinful things and made the Lord very angry. Years ago the Lord had told David and his son Solomon: Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there I will be worshiped forever.
translation_verse: Eye wòtsɔ Asera ƒe legba, si wòwɔ la, ɖo aƒe la me, aƒe, si ŋu Yehowa gblɔ le na Dawid kple via Salomo be: Matsɔ nye ŋkɔ aɖo aƒe sia me kple Yerusalem, si metia le Israel-toawo katã me la tegbee.

english_verse: If my people will faithfully obey all the commands in the Law of my servant Moses, I will never make them leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
translation_verse: Eye nyemena Israel ƒe afɔ nage le anyigba, si metsɔ na wo fofowo la dzi o, nenye be, wòlé se, siwo katã mede na wo kple se, siwo katã nye dɔla Mose de na wo la me ɖe asi, eye wowɔ wo dzi ko

english_verse: But the people of Judah disobeyed the Lord. They listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
translation_verse: Ke womeɖo to o, eye Manase ble wo wowɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi wu dukɔ, siwo Yehowa tsrɔ̃ ɖa le Israel-viwo ŋgɔ

english_verse: One day the Lord said to some of his prophets:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒo nu to eƒe dɔla, nyagblɔɖilawo dzi gblɔ bena:

english_verse: King Manasseh has done more disgusting things than the Amorites, and he has led my people to sin by forcing them to worship his idols.
translation_verse: Esi Yuda-fia Manase wɔ ŋunyɔnu sia, eye wòwɔ nu gbegblẽ wu nusiwo katã Amoritɔwo wɔ le eŋgɔ, eye wòtsɔ eƒe legbawo ble Yuda hã de nuvɔ̃ me la,

english_verse: Jerusalem is as sinful as Ahab and the people of Samaria were. So I will wipe out Jerusalem and be done with it, just as someone wipes water off a plate and turns it over to dry.
translation_verse: Matsi Samaria ƒe ka kple Axab ƒe aƒe la ƒe kpe ɖe Yerusalem dzi, eye matutu Yerusalem, abe alesi wotutua agba me tsɔna tsyɔ anyi ene.

english_verse: I will even get rid of my people who survive. They will be defeated and robbed by their enemies.
translation_verse: Mate nye domenyinu ƒe susɔea ɖa, eye matsɔ wo ade asi na woƒe futɔwo woanye aboyonu kple nuxaxa na woƒe futɔwo katã.

english_verse: My people have done what I hate and have not stopped making me angry since their ancestors left Egypt.
translation_verse: Elabena wowɔ nusi nye vɔ̃ le ŋkunye me, eye wodo dziku nam tso gbesigbe wo fofowo ʋu tso Egipte vaseɖe egbe.

english_verse: Manasseh was guilty of causing the people of Judah to sin and disobey the Lord. He also refused to protect innocent people—he even let so many of them be killed that their blood filled the streets of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Manase kɔ ʋu maɖifɔ geɖe ŋutɔ hã ɖi, vaseɖe esime wona Yerusalem yɔ tso go ɖeka me vaseɖe go keme me hekpe ɖe eƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wotsɔ ble Yuda wòwɔ nusi nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋku me la ŋuti.

english_verse: Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his terrible sins, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Manase ŋutinya susɔea kple nusiwo katã wòwɔ kpakple eƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Yuda-fiawo ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: He died and was buried in Uzza Garden near his palace, and his son Amon became king. King Amon of Judah (
translation_verse: Eye Manase mia fofoawo gbɔ, eye woɖii ɖe eƒe aƒe ƒe abɔ, si nye Uza ƒe abɔ la me, eye via Amon zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Fia Amon.

english_verse: refused to be faithful to the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: Egblẽ Yehowa, fofoawo ƒe Mawu la ɖi, eye meto Yehowa ƒe mɔwo o.

english_verse: Some of Amon's officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace.
translation_verse: Eye Amon ƒe dɔlawo ɖo nugbe ɖe eŋu, eye wowu fia la le eƒe xɔ me.

english_verse: While Shaphan was at the temple, Hilkiah handed him a book and said, “Look what I found here in the temple—The Book of God's Law.” Shaphan read it,
translation_verse: Tete nunɔlagã Xilkiya gblɔ na agbalẽŋlɔla Safan bena: Mefɔ segbalẽa ɖe le Yehowa ƒe aƒe lãme. Eye Xilkiya tsa agbalẽ la na Safan wòxlẽ.

english_verse: and ask Hilkiah the high priest to collect from the guards all the money that the people have donated.
translation_verse: Yi nunɔlagã Xilkiya gbɔ, ne wòaxlẽ ga, siwo katã wotsɔ va Yehowa ƒe aƒe la me, siwo kpuinudzɔlawo dzɔ le dukɔ la si la.

english_verse: Tell Hilkiah to give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. They can use some of the money to pay

translation_verse: Eye fia ŋu asrafowo ƒe amegã la tsɔ sonuawo kple ʋutreawo, sikatɔwo kple klosalotɔwo siaa dzoe,

english_verse: The pile of bronze from the columns, the stands, and the large bowl that Solomon had made for the temple was too large to be weighed.
translation_verse: sɔti eve kple gazɔ ɖeka kpakple anyinɔawo, siwo fia Salomo wɔ bena Yehowa ƒe aƒe la; nusiawo katã ƒe akɔbli mele dada me o.

english_verse: Next, Nebuzaradan arrested Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah his assistant, and three temple officials.
translation_verse: Eye fia ŋu asrafowo ƒe amegã lé nunɔlagã Seraya kple nunɔlagã yometɔ Zefanya kpakple kpuinudzɔla etɔ̃;

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam to rule the few people still living in Judah.
translation_verse: Eye Babel-fia Nebukadnezar tso Gedalya, Safan vi Axikam ƒe vi, ɖo dukɔ, si wogblẽ de Yuda-nyigba dzi la dzikpɔlae.

english_verse: When the army officers and troops heard that Gedaliah was their ruler, the officers met with him at Mizpah. These men were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth from Netophah, and Jaazaniah from Maacah.
translation_verse: Esi aʋakɔ la ƒe amegãwo katã kple woƒe amewo se be, Babel-fia tso Gedalya do dzikpɔlae la, wova Gedalya gbɔ le Mizpa; eye Ismael, Netanya vi, Yoxanan, Kareax vi, kple Seraya, Tanxumet vi, tso Netofat kpakple Yaazanya, Maaxati vi, kple woƒe amewo hã le eme.

english_verse: Gedaliah said to them, “Everything will be fine, I promise. We don't need to be afraid of the Babylonian rulers, if we live here peacefully and do what Nebuchadnezzar says.”
translation_verse: Tete Gedalya ka atam na woawo kple woƒe amewo gblɔ na wo bena: Migavɔ̃ Kaldeatɔwo ƒe dɔlawo o! Mina anyigba la dzi, eye misubɔ Babel-fia, ekema anyo na mi.

english_verse: Ishmael was from the royal family. And about two months after Gedaliah began his rule, Ishmael and ten other men went to Mizpah. They killed Gedaliah and his officials, including those from Judah and those from Babylonia.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me le dzinu adrelia me be, Ismael, Elisama vi Netanya ƒe vi, amesi tso fiaƒome la me kple ŋutsu ewo, siwo kpe de eŋu la, wova wu Gedalya kple Yudatɔ kpakple Kaldeatɔ, siwo le eŋu le Mizpa.

english_verse: After that, the army officers and all the people in Mizpah, whether important or not, were afraid of what the Babylonians might do. So they left Judah and went to Egypt. Jehoiachin Is Set Free (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Eye dukɔ blibo la, ɖeviwo kple tsitsiawo siaa, kple aʋakɔ la ƒe amegãwo dzo yi Egipte, elabena wole Kaldeatɔwo vɔ̃m. Babel-fia ve Yoyaxin nu.

english_verse: Evil-Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
translation_verse: Eƒo nu kplii fafɛ, eye wòtsɔ eƒe zikpui ɖo fia, siwo le eŋu le Babel la ƒe zikpuiwo ŋgɔ.

english_verse: Jehoiachin was even allowed to wear regular clothes, and he ate at the king's table every day.
translation_verse: Ena wodo li eƒe gaxɔ me awuwo, eye wòdu nu le egbɔ ɣesiaɣi le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: Abraham and his slave woman Keturah had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan.
translation_verse: Abraham ƒe ahiã Ketura ƒe viwo nye esi: eya dzi Zimran, Yoksan, Medan, Midian, Yisbak kple Suax. Yoksan viwo nye: Seba kple Dedan.

english_verse: Ethiopia was also the father of Nimrod, the world's first mighty warrior.
translation_verse: Kus dzi Nimrod; eya de asi kalẽwɔwɔ me le anyigba dzi.

english_verse: Egypt was the ancestor of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
translation_verse: Mizrayim dzi Luditɔwo, Anamitɔwo, Lehabitɔwo, Naftuxitɔwo,

english_verse: Gomer was the ancestor of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
translation_verse: Gomer viwo nye Askenaz, Rifat kple Togarma.

english_verse: Javan was the ancestor of Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
translation_verse: Yawan viwo nye: Elisa, Tarsisa, Kititɔwo kple Rodantɔwo.

english_verse: Ethiopia was the ancestor of Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah was the ancestor of Sheba and Dedan.
translation_verse: Kus viwo nye: Seba, Xawila, Sabta, Raama kple Sablexa. Eye Raama viwo nye Seba kple Dedan.

english_verse: Canaan's oldest son was Sidon; his other son was Heth.
translation_verse: Kanaan dzi Zidon, amesi nye ŋgɔgbea kple Xet,

english_verse: Shem was the ancestor of Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech; they were the ancestors of the kingdoms named after them.
translation_verse: Sem viwo nye: Elam, Asur, Arpaxsad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Xul, Geter kple Mesex.

english_verse: Arpachshad was Shelah's father and Eber's grandfather.
translation_verse: Arpaxsad dzi Selax, eye Selax dzi Eber.

english_verse: Eber named his first son Peleg, because in his time the earth was divided into tribal regions. Eber's second son was Joktan,
translation_verse: Wodzi ŋutsuvi eve na Eber; ɖeka ŋkɔ nye Peleg, le esi wòmã anyigba lé eŋɔli la, eye nɔvia ŋkɔ nye Yoktan.

english_verse: the ancestor of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Ebal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab.
translation_verse: Ofir, Xawila kple Yobab; amesiawo katã nye Yoktan viwo.

english_verse: Abraham was the father of Isaac and Ishmael.
translation_verse: Abraham viwo nye Isak kple Ismael.

english_verse: Midian was the father of Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. Esau's Family (Genesis
