translation_verse: Mido akpe na Yehowa, elabena eƒe dome nyo, eye eƒe amenuveve li tegbee!

english_verse: Say to him, “Save us, Lord God! Bring us back from among the nations. Let us celebrate and shout in praise of your holy name.
translation_verse: Eye migblɔ be: Wò Mawu, miaƒe xɔla, xɔ na mi, ƒo nua nu ƒu, eye ɖe mi tso dukɔwo si me, ne míada akpe na wò ŋkɔ kɔkɔe la, eye miatsɔ wò kafukafu aƒo adegbee!

english_verse: Lord God of Israel, you deserve to be praised forever and ever.” After David finished, the people shouted, “Amen! Praise the Lord!” David Appoints Worship Leaders at Jerusalem and Gibeon
translation_verse: Woakafu Yehowa Israel ƒe Mawu la, tso mavɔ me yi mavɔ me! Tete dukɔ blibo la gblɔ be: Nenɔ alea! Eye wokafu Yehowa.

english_verse: David chose Asaph and the Levites in his clan to be in charge of the daily worship at the place where the sacred chest was kept.
translation_verse: Eye wòɖe Asat kple nɔviawo ɖo afima le Yehowa ƒe nubablaɖaka la ŋgɔ, ne woasubɔ gbesiagbe le aɖaka la ŋgɔ de ŋkeke sia ŋkeke ƒe ɖoɖo nu;

english_verse: David also chose Zadok the priest and his relatives who were priests to serve at the Lord's sacred tent at Gibeon.
translation_verse: eye wòɖo nunɔla Zadok kple nɔvia, siwo nye nunɔlawo la, Yehowa ƒe nɔƒe la ŋgɔ le vɔsaƒe le Gibeon,

english_verse: They were to offer sacrifices on the altar every morning and evening, just as the Lord had commanded in the Law he gave Israel.
translation_verse: ne woasa numevɔ na Yehowa le numevɔsamlekpui la dzi ɖaa, ŋdi kple fiẽ, abe alesi woŋlɔ ɖe Yehowa ƒe se la me na Israel ene;

english_verse: Heman and Jeduthun were their assistants, as well as the other men who had been chosen to praise the Lord for his never-ending love.
translation_verse: eye Heman kple Yedutun kpakple ame tiatia susɔeawo, siwo ŋkɔ woŋlɔ la, kpe ɖe wo ŋu, ne wòadzi: „Mida akpe na Yehowa, elabena eƒe amenuveve li tegbee!“

english_verse: After that, everyone went home, and David went home to his family.
translation_verse: Esi dukɔ blibo la dome amesiame yi eƒe xɔnu la, Dawid trɔ, be yeaɖado gbe na eƒemetɔwo.

english_verse: Soon after David moved into his new palace, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest is kept in a tent.”
translation_verse: Esime Dawid le eƒe fiasã me la, Dawid gblɔ na nyagblɔɖila Natan bena: Kpɔ ɖa, nye la mele sedertixɔ me, ke Yehowa ƒe nubablaɖaka ya le kuntruwo le.

english_verse: and yet you have promised to do even more for my descendants. You are treating me as if I am a very important person.
translation_verse: Oo Mawu, esia nye nu tsɛ le ŋkuwò me, hafi nègado nusi ava gbaɖegbe la ŋugbe ɖe wò dɔla ƒe aƒe ŋu, eye nèkpɔm, abe alesi amegbetɔ kpɔa nui enea? Yehowa Mawu, wò, amesi kɔm ɖe dzi!

english_verse: to go to David and tell him: David, you are my servant, so listen carefully: You are not the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Yi, nagblɔ na nye dɔla Dawid be: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Menye wòe atu xɔ nam manɔ me o;

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: elabena tso gbesigbe mekplɔ Israel la, nyemenɔ xɔa ɖeke me vaseɖe egbe o, ke boŋ metsa tso agbadɔ me yi agbadɔ me, eye tso nɔƒe yi nɔƒe.

english_verse: I chose special leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Afisiafi, si menɔ Israel blibo la dome to la, de megblɔ na Israel ƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃la, siwo medo, be woanyi nye dukɔ la dometɔa ɖe kpɔ be, nukaŋuti mietu sedertixɔa ɖeke nam oa?

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Menɔ anyi kpli wò le afisiafi, si neyi, eye metsrɔ̃ wò tutɔwo katã da le ŋgɔwò; eye mede ŋkɔ ŋuwò abe amegã, siwo le anyigba dzi la ƒe ŋkɔwo ene.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace. They will no longer have to tremble with fear—evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: Mana nɔƒe nye dukɔ Israel, eye mana wòaɖo zunu anyi, be wòanɔ enɔƒe, eye magatsi dzi azɔ o, eye ame vɔ̃ɖiwo míagatsrɔ̃ wo abe tsã ene o,

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people, and I will keep your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that like you, your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: eye abe le ɣeyiɣi, si me meɖo ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ɖe nye dukɔ Israel dzi la ene o. Mabɔbɔ wò futɔwo katã de anyi, eye mele gbe ƒã dem na wò be, Yehowa atso aƒe na wò.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried beside your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Ne wò ŋkekewo de, nèyi fofowòwo gbɔ la, ekema mado wò dzidzimevi, si tso viwòwo dome la, yowòme, eye mali ke eƒe fiaduƒe.

english_verse: I will be like a father to him, and he will be like a son to me. I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Manye fofoa, eye eya anye vinye, eye nyemana nye amenuveve nadzo le egbɔ, abe alesi mena wòdzo le ŋgɔwònɔla gbɔ ene o;

english_verse: I will make sure that your son and his descendants will rule my people and my kingdom forever.
translation_verse: ke boŋ matsɔe ado nye aƒe kple nye fiaɖuƒe me tegbee, eye eƒe fiazikpui ali ke tegbee. Dawid do gbe ɖa.

english_verse: Nathan told David exactly what the Lord had said. David Gives Thanks to the Lord (
translation_verse: Eye Natan ƒo nu kple Dawid le nyã siawo katã kple ŋutega blibo la nu pɛpɛpɛ.

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts. What else can I say, except that you have honored me?
translation_verse: Nya ka Dawid agagblɔ na wò akpe ɖe wò dɔla ƒe bubu la ŋu, elabena ènya wò dɔla.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. He sat there and prayed: Lord God, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Tete fia Dawid va bɔbɔ nɔ Yehowa ŋku me, eye wògblɔ bena: Yehowa Mawu, ameka menye, eye nuka nye aƒenye be, nèkplɔm vaseɖe fifi!

english_verse: It was your choice to do these wonderful things for me and to make these promises.
translation_verse: Yehowa, le wò dɔla kple wò tamebubu la la nèwɔ nu gã siawo katã, be naɖe wò nutsuwɔwɔwo katã afia.

english_verse: No other god is like you, Lord—you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Yehowa, le nusiwo katã míese kple miaƒe towo nu la, amea ɖeke mede nuwò o, eye mawua ɖeke meli kpe ɖe ŋuwò o.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so that your people could live here.
translation_verse: Dukɔ ka de wò dukɔ Israel nu, anyigba dzi dukɔ, si ɖeɖe ko mawua ɖe yi, be yeaɖee awɔ dukɔ na eɖokui, ne yeawɔ nu gã dziŋɔwo ahade ŋkɔ eɖokui ŋu, abe alesi nènyã dukɔwo le wò dukɔ, si neɖe tso Egipte la ŋgɔ ene?

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Etsɔ wò dukɔ Israel wɔ dukɔe na ɖokuiwò tegbee, eye wò, Yehowa, nèzu woƒe Mawu!

english_verse: Lord God, please do what you promised me and my descendants.
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa, nɔ nya, si nègblɔ ɖe wò dɔla kple eƒe aƒe ŋu la dzi tegbee, eye nawɔ, abe alesi nègblɔ ene!

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord All-Powerful rules Israel and is their God.” My kingdom will be strong,
translation_verse: Woaɖo ŋu ɖe wò ŋkɔ ŋu, eye woade du woahagblɔ be: Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, enye Mawu na Israel, eye wò dɔla Dawid ƒe aƒe li ke le ŋkuwò me!

english_verse: because you are my God, and you have promised that my descendants will be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Elabena wò, nye Mawue, gblɔe ɖe wò dɔla ƒe to me be, yele xɔ tu ge nɛ; eyata dzi ɖo wò dɔla ƒo wòle gbe sia dom ɖa le ŋkuwò me.

english_verse: You are the Lord God, and you have made this good promise to me.
translation_verse: Azɔ Yehowa, wòe nye Mawu, eye nègblɔ nya nyui sia na wò dɔla;

english_verse: Now please bless my descendants forever, and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already blessed my family, and I know you will bless us forever.
translation_verse: eyata lɔ̃, ne nayra wò dɔla ƒe aƒe, ne wòanɔ ŋkuwò me tegbee, elabena ne wò Yehowa nèyra la, yayra la nɔa anyi tegbee!

english_verse: While King Hadadezer of Zobah was trying to gain control of the territory near the Euphrates River, David met him in battle at Hamath and defeated him.
translation_verse: Dawid si Zoba-fia Hadadezer le Xamat, esime wòva, be yeado eƒe fiaɖuƒe anyi ɖe Frat-tɔsisi la nu.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried gold shields, but David took these shields and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Dawid xɔ sikakpoxɔnu, siwo le Hadadezer ŋu mewo si hetsɔ va Yerusalem.

english_verse: When troops from the Syrian kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
translation_verse: Esi Aramtɔwo tso Damasko, be yewoaxɔ na Zoba-fia Hadadezer la, Dawid wu ame akpe blave vɔ eve le Aramtɔwo dome.

english_verse: Then David stationed some of his troops in Damascus, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid ɖe amewo ɖo Aramtɔwo ƒe Damasko, eye Aramtɔwo zu Dawid teviwo hedzɔ nu nɛ. Ale Yehowa kpe ɖe Dawid ŋu le afisiafi, si wòyi.

english_verse: King Tou of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Tou heard that David had defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Hadoram to congratulate David on his victory. Hadoram also brought him gifts made of gold, silver, and bronze.
translation_verse: etsɔ sika kple klosalo kpakple akɔblinu vovovowo de via Hadoram si ɖo ɖe fia Dawid, ne yeado gbe ne, eye yeadi dzɔgbenyuie nɛ, le esi wòwɔ aʋa kple Hadadezer, eye wòsii ta; elabena Tou kple Hadadezer wole ke me.

english_verse: David gave these gifts to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold he had captured from Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, and Amalek.
translation_verse: Eye fia Dawid kɔ woawo hã ŋu na Yehowa hekpe ɖe klosalo kple sika, siwo wòxɔ le dukɔwo katã si la ŋuti; exɔ wo le Edomtɔwo, Moabitɔwo, Amon-viwo, Filistitɔwo kple Amalekitɔwo si.

english_verse: Abishai the son of Zeruiah defeated the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed
translation_verse: Abisai, Zeruya vi, wu Edomtɔ ame akpe wuienyi le dzeʋe la me,

english_verse: Then he stationed troops in Edom, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler. Everywhere David went, the Lord gave him victory in war. A List of David's Officials (
translation_verse: eye wòɖe amewo ɖo Edom. Ale Edomtɔwo katã zu Dawid teviwo, eye Yehowa kpe ɖe Dawid ŋu afisiafi, si wòyi.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Yoab, Zeruya vi, le aʋakɔ la nu, eye Yosafat, Axilud vi, nye fia ƒe tsiami;

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were the priests. Shavsha was the secretary.
translation_verse: Zadok, Axitub vi, kple Abimelex, Abyatar vi, wonye nunɔlawo, eye Sawsa enye agbalẽŋlɔla;

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were his highest-ranking officials.
translation_verse: Benaya, Yehoyada vi, le Kretitɔwo kple Pletitɔwo nu, eye Dawid viŋutsuwo nye ame gbãtɔwo le fia ŋu.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, so I will be kind to his son.” He sent some officials to Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died. But when David's officials arrived at Ammon,
translation_verse: Tete Dawid gblɔ bena: Mawɔ dɔmenyo na Naxas vi Xanun, elabena fofoa ve nunye. Eye Dawid dɔ amewo, be woaɖafa akɔ nɛ le fofoa ta. Ke esi Dawid ƒe dɔlawo va Xanun gbɔ le Amon-viwo ƒe anyigba dzi, be woafa akɔ nɛ la.

english_verse: Joab saw that the enemy troops were lined up on both sides of him. So he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Syrians.
translation_verse: Ke esi Yoab kpɔ be, wodze aʋa ɖe ye ŋu le ŋgɔ kple megbe la, eɖe amewo le Israel ƒe ame baliawo katã dome, eye wòdze aʋa ɖe Aramtɔwo ŋu.

english_verse: Some time later, King Nahash of Ammon died, and his son Hanun became king.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me le nusiawo megbe be, Amon-viwo ƒe fia Naxas ku, eye via zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and accepted him as their new ruler. The Syrians never helped the Ammonites again.
translation_verse: Esi Hadadezer ƒe dɔlawo kpɔ be, Israel si yewo la, wowɔ ŋutifafa kple Dawid, trɔ zu eteviwo, eye Aramtɔwo gbe be, yewomagakpe ɖe Amon-viwo ŋu azɔ o.

english_verse: the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, “Do you really believe King David is honoring your father by sending these men to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our country, so he can come and destroy it.”
translation_verse: Amon-viwo ƒe amegãwo gblɔ na Xanun bena: Ɖe Dawid dɔ akɔfa-lawo ɖa, be woaɖe bubu fofowò ŋu na wò loo? Ke boŋ ɖe eƒe dɔlawo va, be woadzro anyigba la me, woatsa ŋku le edzi, ne woagblẽ.

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off and their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Tete Xanun na wòlé Dawid ƒe dɔlawo, wolũ ge na wo, eye wolã woƒe awu ɖe domedo-mee ɖe agɔnu, eve wodo mɔ wo

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message that told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Ke esi wova gblɔ ŋutsuawo ŋu nya na Dawid la edɔ ame woɖa-kpe wo, elabena wodo ŋukpe ŋutsuawo ŋutɔ, eye fia la gblɔ be; Mitsi Yerixo, vaseɖe esime miaƒe ge nato, hafi miegbɔ!

english_verse: David heard what was happening, and he sent out Joab with his army.
translation_verse: Esi Dawid see la, edɔ Yoab kple kalẽtɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ blibo la ɖa.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops marched to the entrance of the city and prepared for battle, while the Syrian troops took their positions in the open fields.
translation_verse: Tete Amon-viwo ho va dze aʋa ɖe du la ƒe agbo nu, eye fia, siwo va la, le aʋagbe dzi wo tɔ wo tɔe.

english_verse: Then he put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and told them to fight against the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ aʋakɔ la ƒe susɔea de asi na nɔvia Abisai, ne woawo nadze aʋa ɖe Amon-viwo ŋu.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Syrians are too much for me to handle, come and help me. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Ne Aramtɔwo sesẽ wum la, ekema nava xɔ nam, eye ne Amon-viwo sesẽ wu wò la, ekema mava xɔ na wò!

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the towns of our Lord God. I pray he will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Lé dzi ɖe ƒo, eye na míasẽ ŋu na míaƒe dukɔ kple mía Mawu ƒe du la, eye Yehowa awɔ nusi dze eya ŋutɔ ŋu.

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Syrians, and the Syrians ran from them.
translation_verse: Ke esi Yoab kple aʋakɔ, si le eŋu la, yi ɖatɔ Aramtɔwo la, wòsi le wo nu;

english_verse: When the Ammonite troops saw that the Syrians had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab then returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: eye esi Amon-viwo kpɔ be, Aramtɔwo si la, woawo hã si le nɔvia Abisai nu yi ɖage ɖe dua me, Ke Yoab trɔ gbɔ va Yerusalem.

english_verse: As soon as the Syrians realized they had been defeated, they sent for their troops that were stationed on the other side of the Euphrates River. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led these troops to Ammon.
translation_verse: Esi Aramtɔwo kpɔ be, Israel si yewo la, wodɔ ame woɖakplɔ Aramtɔ, siwo le tɔsisi la ƒe go keme dzi la vɛ, eye Hadadezer ƒe aʋafia Sofax enye wo kplɔla.

english_verse: David found out what the Syrians were doing, and he brought Israel's entire army together. They crossed the Jordan River, and he commanded them to take their positions facing the Syrian troops. Soon after the fighting began,
translation_verse: Eye wova gblɔe na Dawid, tete wòƒo Israel blibo la nu ƒu, eye woho tso Yordan hedze aʋa ɖe wo ŋu. Esi Dawid dze aʋa ɖe Aramtɔwo ŋu la, wowɔ aʋa kplii.

english_verse: The next spring, the time when kings go to war, Joab marched out in command of the Israelite army and destroyed towns all over the country of Ammon. He attacked the capital city of Rabbah and left it in ruins. But David stayed in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Esi ƒe trɔ, eye fiawo ƒe aʋahoɣi do edzi la. Yoab kplɔ aʋakɔ la, eye woɖagblẽ Amon-viwo ƒe anyigba, eye wòva ɖe to ɖe Raba; ke Dawid tsi Yerusalem. Eye Yoab si Raba, eye wògbãe.

english_verse: He forced the people of Rabbah to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. He also did the same thing with the people in all the other Ammonite towns. David then led Israel's army back to Jerusalem. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: Ekplɔ dukɔ, si le eme la, ɖaɖo laxalaxadɔwo, luƒotasiadamdɔwo kple fíadɔwo nu. Alea Dawid wɔ Amon-viwo ƒe duwo katãe, eye Dawid kple aʋakɔ blibo la gbugbɔ va Yerusalem. Woɖu Filistitɔwo dzi zi etɔ̃.

english_verse: Some time later, Israel fought a battle against the Philistines at Gezer. During this battle, Sibbecai from Hushah killed Sippai, a descendant of the Rephaim, and the Philistines were defeated.
translation_verse: Eye wogawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo le Gezer. Ɣemaɣi Xusatitɔ Sibexai wu Sipai, amesi tso ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe dzidzimeviwo dome, eye wobɔbɔ wo ɖe anyi.

english_verse: In another battle against the Philistines, Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.
translation_verse: Emegbe wogawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo, eye Elxanan, Yair-vi, wu Goliat nɔvi Lami tso Gat, amesi ƒe akplɔti le abe abaladoti ene.

english_verse: Another one of the Philistine soldiers who was a descendant of the Rephaim was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. During a battle at Gath,
translation_verse: Eye wogawɔ aʋa le Gat. Ame dzɔtsua ɖe to asi ade kple afɔ ade, wo katã le blave vɔ ene; eya hã tso ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe ƒome me.

english_verse: he made fun of Israel, so David's nephew Jonathan killed him.
translation_verse: Eye wòdu fewu le Israel ŋu, tete Dawid nɔvi, Simea vi Yonatan, wui.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these three men from Gath who were descendants of the Rephaim.
translation_verse: Amesiawo tso ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe ƒome le Gat, eye wotsi Dawid kple eƒe dɔlawo si me.

english_verse: But David replied, “No! I want to pay you what they're worth. I can't just take something from you and then offer the Lord a sacrifice that cost me nothing.”
translation_verse: Fia Dawid gblɔ na Ornan bena: Kpao, ke boŋ maƒlee ho dedie; elabena nyemaxɔ wò nu ana Yehowa o, eye nyemasa numevɔ fe maxemaxee o.

english_verse: The Lord said to Gad, one of David's prophets,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Dawid ƒe nukpɔla Gad bena:

english_verse: Joab answered, “Your Majesty, even if the Lord made your kingdom a hundred times larger, you would still rule everyone in it. Why do you need to know how many soldiers there are? Don't you think that would make the whole nation angry?”
translation_verse: Yoab ɖo ŋu bena: Nye aƒetɔ fia, ne Yehowa na eƒe dukɔ la dzi ɖe dzi zi alafa wu alesi wòle hã la, ɖe menye nye aƒetɔ ƒe dɔlawo ko wo katã wonye oa? Nukaŋuti nye aƒetɔ le nusia tugbe dim, eye nukaŋuti wòatrɔ zu fɔɖiɖi na Israel?

english_verse: But David would not change his mind. And so Joab went everywhere in Israel and Judah and counted the people. He returned to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ke esi fia la tsi eƒe nya la dzi na Yoab la, Yoab yi ɖatsa le Israel blibo la, eye wògbɔ va Yerusalem.

english_verse: Joab refused to include anyone from the tribes of Levi and Benjamin, because he still disagreed with David's orders. God Punishes Israel (
translation_verse: Gake metia Lewi kple Benyamin xlẽ ɖe wo dome o, elabena fiaƒe nya la nyo ŋu na Yoab.

english_verse: “Tell David that I will punish him in one of three ways. But he will have to choose which one it will be.”
translation_verse: Yi ɖagblɔ na Dawid be: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Nu elɔ̃ metso le ŋkuwò me ɖom, tia wo dometɔ ɖeka, ne mawo wò.

english_verse: and David prayed, “It's my fault! I sinned by ordering the people to be counted. They have done nothing wrong—they are innocent sheep. Lord God, please punish me and my family. Don't let the disease wipe out your people.” David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place (
translation_verse: Tete Dawid gblɔ na Mawu bena: Alo menye nyee de se be, woaxlẽ dukɔ la oa, eye menye nyee da vo hewɔ nuvɔ̃ gã sia oa? Ke alẽ siawo la, nuka wowɔ? Yehowa, nye Mawu, wò asi neva mía kple fofonye ƒe aƒe dzi, ke megava dukɔ sia dzi, ne wòawu wo o!

english_verse: David's order to count the people made God angry, and he punished Israel.
translation_verse: Ke nusia medze Mawu ŋu o, eye wowu Israel.

english_verse: David prayed, “I am your servant. But what I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Please forgive me.”
translation_verse: Tete Dawid gblɔ na Mawu bena: Mewo nuvɔ̃, be mewo nusia, eyata tsɔ wò dɔla ƒe vodada kee, elabena mewo lãnu ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Gad went to David and told him: You must choose how the Lord will punish you:
translation_verse: Tete Gad va Dawid gbɔ gblɔ nɛ bena: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ wo dome, natsɔ:

english_verse: Will there be three years when the land won't grow enough food for its people? Or will your enemies constantly defeat you for three months? Or will the Lord send a horrible disease to strike your land for three days? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God who sent me.
translation_verse: dɔwuame ƒe etɔ̃ loo, alo nasi le wò ketɔwo nu dzinu etɔ̃, eye wò futɔwo ƒe yi naɖe wò ɖe nu loo, alo Yehowa ƒe yi kple dɔvɔ̃ nanɔ anyigba dzi ŋkeke etɔ̃, eye Yehowa ƒe dɔla nawu ame le Israel-nyigba blibo la dzia? Azɔ bu eŋu, alesi maɖaɖo eŋu na amesi dom ɖa!

english_verse: David was miserable and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
translation_verse: Dawid gblɔ na Gad bena: Mexaxa ŋuta! Na madze Yehowa si me, elabena eƒe amenuveve so gbɔ ŋutɔ; ke nyemele amegbetɔwo si me dze ge o!

english_verse: So the Lord sent a horrible disease on Israel, and
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa na dɔvɔ̃ va Israel, eye ame akpe blaadre ku le Israel. Dawid mè nu le Ornan ƒe luƒoƒe.

english_verse: Then he sent an angel to destroy the city of Jerusalem. But just as the angel was about to do that, the Lord felt sorry for all the suffering he had caused the people, and he told the angel, “Stop! They have suffered enough.” This happened at the threshing place that belonged to Araunah the Jebusite.
translation_verse: Eye Mawu dɔ dɔlaa ɖe ɖo ɖe Yerusalem, be wòaɖagblẽe. Ke esi wòde asi nugbegblẽ me la, Yehowa kpoe, eye vɔ̃ la vee, eye wògblɔ na dɔla, si le nu gblẽm la bena: Esɔ gbɔ azɔ, ɖiɖi wò asi ɖe anyi! Yehowa ƒe dɔla la tsi tre ɖe Yebusitɔ Ornan ƒe lugbɔ ƒe gbɔ.

english_verse: David saw the Lord's angel in the air, holding a sword over Jerusalem. He and the leaders of Israel, who were all wearing sackcloth, bowed with their faces to the ground,
translation_verse: Ke esi Dawid fa ko dzi, eye wòkpɔ Yehowa ƒe dɔla la le dziƒo kple anyigba dome, eye wòdi eƒe yi do ɖe Yerusalem dzi la, Dawid kple ame tsilsiwo ta akpanya, eye wode ta agu.

english_verse: The Lord's angel told the prophet Gad to tell David that he must go to Araunah's threshing place and build an altar in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe dɔla gblɔ na Gad be, wòaɖagblɔ na Dawid bena, neyi ɖaɖi vɔsamlekpui na Yehowa ɖe Yebusitɔ Ornan ƒe lugbɔƒe.

english_verse: Araunah and his four sons were threshing wheat at the time, and when they saw the angel, the four sons ran to hide.
translation_verse: Eye esi Ornan trɔ kɔ la, ekpɔ dɔla la, esime Ornan le lu ƒom, eye eya kple viaŋutsu eneawo si ɣla.

english_verse: Just then, David arrived, and when Araunah saw him, he stopped his work and bowed down.
translation_verse: Esi Dawid va Ornan gbɔ, eye Ornan fɔ kɔ dzi kpɔ Dawid la, edo tso lugbɔƒe la ɖade ta agu de Dawid ŋku me.

english_verse: David said, “Would you sell me your threshing place, so I can build an altar on it to the Lord? Then this disease will stop killing the people. I'm willing to pay whatever you say it's worth.”
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ na Ornan bena: Tsɔ lugbɔƒe la nam, ne maɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖi na Yehowa; tsoe nam le eƒe asixɔxɔ blibo la nu, ne dɔvɔ̃ la nu natso le dukɔ la dome.

english_verse: Araunah answered, “Take it, Your Majesty, and do whatever you want with it. I'll even give you the oxen for the sacrifice and the wheat for the grain sacrifice. And you can use the threshing-boards for the fire. It's all yours!”
translation_verse: Tete Ornan ɖo ŋu na Dawid bena: Xɔe, eye nye aƒetɔ fia nèwu alesi dze eŋu; kpɔ ɖa, mana nyiwo woasa numevɔe, luƒotasiaɖamwo nanye nake kple lu woasa nuɖuvɔe; mana wo katã.

english_verse: David built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. David prayed, and the Lord answered him by sending fire down on the altar.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid ɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afima na Yehowa hesa numevɔ kple akpedavɔ. Eye esi wòyɔ Yehowa la, etɔ ne, eye wòna dzo tso dziƒo va numevɔsamlekpui la dzi.

english_verse: Then the Lord commanded the angel to put the sword away.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa de se na dɔla la be, wòatsɔ eƒe yi ade aku.

english_verse: When David saw that the Lord had answered his prayer, he offered more sacrifices there at the threshing place,
translation_verse: Esi Dawid kpo le ɣemaɣi be, Yehowa to nɛ le Yebusitɔ Ornan ƒe lugbɔƒe la, ede asi vɔsasa me le afima.

english_verse: David said, “The temple of the Lord God must be built right here at this threshing place. And the altar for offering sacrifices will also be here.” David Prepares To Build the Temple
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ be: Esia nye Yehowa Mawu ƒe aƒe, eye esia nye vɔsamlekpui ɖe Israel ƒe numevɔsa ŋu.

english_verse: David ordered the foreigners living in Israel to come to Jerusalem. Then he assigned some to cut blocks of stone for building the temple.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid de se be, woaƒo amedzro, siwo le Israel-nyigba dzi la nu ƒu, eye woɖo kpefulawo, be woafu kpewo, ne woatso atu Mawu ƒe xɔ lae.

english_verse: He also brought an endless supply of cedar logs from the cities of Sidon and Tyre.
translation_verse: eye sedertiawo mele xexlẽ me o, elabena Sidontɔwo kple Tiro-tɔwo tsa sedertiwo vɛ na Dawid taŋtaŋ.

english_verse: He said, “The temple for the Lord must be great, so that everyone in the world will know about it. But since my son Solomon is young and has no experience, I will make sure that everything is ready for the temple to be built.” That's why David did all these things before he died. David Instructs Solomon To Build the Temple
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ bena: Vinye Salomo enye ɖekakpui dzaa ko, eye xɔ, si wole tutu ge na Yehowa la, ele be, wòalolo ŋutɔ, ne eƒe ŋkɔ kple bubu nade anyigbawo katã dzi, eyata maƒo nuwo nu ƒu ɖi nɛ! Ale Dawid ƒo nuwo nu ƒu taŋtaŋ hafi va ku.

english_verse: David sent for his son Solomon and told him to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Eye wòyɔ via Salomo hede se ne be, wòatu xa na Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la.

english_verse: He said: My son, I wanted to build a temple where the Lord my God would be worshiped.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ na Salomo bena: Vinye, meɖo ɖe ta me be, matu xa na Yehowa, nye Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ,

english_verse: But some time ago, he told me, “David, you have killed too many people and have fought too many battles. That's why you are not the one to build my temple.
translation_verse: ke Yehowa ƒe gbe va gbɔnye be: Ekɔ ʋu ɖe anyi akpa, eye nèwɔ aʋa geɖe, eyata matu xɔ na nye ŋkɔ o, elabena ekɔ ʋu geɖe ɖe anyi le ŋkunye me.

english_verse: But when your son becomes king, I will give him peace throughout his kingdom. His name will be Solomon, because during his rule I will keep Israel safe and peaceful.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, wole ŋutsuvia ɖe dzi ge na wò, amesi anye ŋutifafame, eye mana gbɔdzɔe le eƒe futɔwo katã si me godoo, elabena Salomo anye eƒe ŋkɔ, eye mana ŋutifafa kple gbɔɖeme Israel le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: Solomon will build my temple. He will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him. In fact, one of his descendants will always rule in Israel.”
translation_verse: Eya atu xɔ na nye ŋkɔ; azu vinye, eye nyea mazu fofoa, eye mana eƒe fiaɖuƒe ƒe fiazikpui nati ke ɖe Israel dzi tegbee.

english_verse: Solomon, my son, I now pray that the Lord your God will be with you and keep his promise to help you build a temple for him.
translation_verse: Eyata vinye, Yehowa ana kpli wò, natu Yehowa, wò Mawu ƒe xɔ la aɖe goe dedie, abe alesi wògblɔ ɖe ŋuwò ene.

english_verse: May he give you wisdom and knowledge, so that you can rule Israel according to his Law.
translation_verse: Yehowa ana gɔmesese kple nunya wò, eye woaɖo wò Israel nu, ne na é Yehowa, wò Mawu ƒe se la me ɖe asi.

english_verse: If you obey the laws and teachings that the Lord gave Moses, you will be successful. Be strong and brave and don't get discouraged or be afraid of anything.
translation_verse: Ne èlé ɖoɖo kple kɔnu, siwo Yehowa ɖo na Mose hena Israel-viwo la me ɖe asi, eye nèwɔ wo dzi la, ekema akpɔ dzagbenyuie. Sẽ ŋu, eye nalé dzi ɖe ƒo, megavɔ̃ o, eye dzika megatso ƒowò o!

english_verse: gold, silver, bronze, and iron. You have plenty of workers to do the job. Now get started, and I pray that the Lord will be with you in your work.
translation_verse: Sika kple klosalo, akɔbli kple gayibɔ mele xexlẽ me o; eyata tso de do la ŋu, eye Yehowa ano kpli wò!

english_verse: David then gave orders for the leaders of Israel to help Solomon.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid de se na Israel-amegãwo katã be, woakpe de via Salomo ŋu gblɔ bena:

english_verse: David said: The Lord our God has helped me defeat all the people who lived here before us, and he has given you peace from all your enemies. Now this land belongs to the Lord and his people.
translation_verse: Yehowa, mia Mawu la, li kpli mi tso, eye wòna gbɔdzɔe mi godoo va kpe, elabena etsɔ anyigba la de asi nam, eye anyigbadzitɔwo na ta le Yehowa kple eƒe dukɔ la ŋku me.

english_verse: Obey the Lord your God with your heart and soul. Begin work on the temple to honor him, so that the sacred chest and the things used for worship can be kept there.
translation_verse: Eyata midi Yehowa, mia Mawu la, kple miaƒe dzi kpakple miaƒe luʋɔ, eye mitso, ne miatu Yehowa Mawu ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la, ne woatsɔ Yehowa ƒe nubablaɖaka la kple Mawu ƒe nu kɔkɔeawo ada ɖe xɔ, si tu ge woala na Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ la me.

english_verse: David was old when he chose his son Solomon to be king of Israel.
translation_verse: Esi Dawid tsi, eye agbe tii la, etsɔ via Salomo ɖo fia ɖe Israel nu?

english_verse: Some time later, David called together all of Israel's leaders, priests, and Levites.
translation_verse: Eye wòƒo Israel-amegãwo katã, nunɔlawo kple Lewi-viwo nu ƒu.

english_verse: He then counted the Levite men who were at least
translation_verse: Eye woxlẽ Lewi-vi, siwo xɔ ƒe blaetɔ̃ kple edzivɔwo, ŋutsu ɖekaɖekawo ƒe xexlẽme de akpe blaetɔ̃ vo enyi.

english_verse: Every morning and evening, the Levites are to give thanks to the Lord and sing praises to him.
translation_verse: eye ele na wo be, woatsi tre ɖi ŋdi sia ŋdi, ne woada akpe na Yehowa, eye woakafui; alea woawo le fiẽ hã.

english_verse: David then divided the Levites into three groups according to the clans of Levi's sons, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid ma wo haha ɖe Lewi viwo Gerson, Kehat kple Merari nu.

english_verse: Gershon had two sons: Ladan and Shimei.
translation_verse: Gerson viwo nye: Laedan kple Simei.

english_verse: Ladan was the father of Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel.
translation_verse: Laedan vi wo nye: Yexiel, amesi nye toto, Zetam kple Yoel, wole wo ame etɔ̃.

english_verse: They were all family leaders among their father's descendants. Shimei was the father of Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran.
translation_verse: Simei viwo nye: Selomit, Xaziel kple Haran, wole wo ame etɔ̃. Woawo nye Laedan ƒe aƒekɔwo ƒe tatɔwo.

english_verse: Later, Shimei had four more sons, in the following order: Jahath, Ziza, Jeush, and Beriah. But Jeush and Beriah didn't have many children, so their descendants were counted as one family.
translation_verse: Yaxat enye tatɔ, eye Ziza enye evelia; ke Yeus kple Beria medzi vi geɖe o, eye woxlẽ wo wo aƒekɔ ɖekae.

english_verse: Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
translation_verse: Kehat viwo nye; Amram, Yizhar, Xebron kple Uziel, wole wo ame ene.

english_verse: Amram was the father of Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were chosen to be in charge of all the sacred things. They served the Lord by offering sacrifices to him and by blessing the people in his name.
translation_verse: Aram viwo nye: Aron kple Mose, ewolia Aron, be wòakɔ eya kple viaŋutsuwo ŋu ne woanye ame kɔkɔetɔwo tegbee ne woaɖo dzudzɔ le Yehowa ŋku me, woasubɔe, eye woayra ame ɖe eƒe ŋkɔ dzi tegbee.

english_verse: Gershom's oldest son was Shebuel.
translation_verse: Gersom vi nye Sebuel, amesi nye tatɔ.

english_verse: The second son born to Kohath was Izhar, and his oldest son was Shelomith.
translation_verse: Yizhar vi nye: Selomit, amesi nye tatɔ.

english_verse: Hebron, the third son of Kohath, was the father of Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
translation_verse: Xebron vi nye: Yeriya, amesi nye tatɔ, evelia nye Amarya, etɔ̃lia nye Yaxaziel, eye enelia nye Yekamam.

english_verse: Merari had two sons: Mahli and Mushi. Mahli was the father of Eleazar and Kish.
translation_verse: Merari viwo nye: Maxli kple Musi Maxli viwo nye: Eleazar kple Kis.

english_verse: Eleazar had no sons, only daughters, and they married their uncle's sons.
translation_verse: Eleazar medzi ŋutsuvia ɖeke hafi ku o, negbe nyɔnuviwo ko, eye woɖe Kis ƒe ŋutsuviwo, siwo nye wo nɔviwo.

english_verse: Mushi the second son of Merari, was the father of Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.
translation_verse: Musi viwo nye: Maxli, Eder kple Yeremot, wole wo ame etɔ̃.

english_verse: David said: The Lord God of Israel has given his people peace, and he will live in Jerusalem forever.
translation_verse: Elabena Dawid gblɔ be: Esi Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, na gbɔdzɔe eƒe dukɔ, eye wole Yerusalem no ge tegbee la,

english_verse: And so, the Levites won't need to move the sacred tent and the things used for worship from place to place.
translation_verse: eyata Lewi-viwo hã megale nɔƒe la kple eƒe nuwo katã tso ge azɔ o; —

english_verse: will serve the Lord by helping Aaron's descendants do their work at the temple, by keeping the courtyards and rooms of the temple clean, and by making sure that everything used in worship stays pure.
translation_verse: ke boŋ wo nɔƒe nanɔ Aron viwo xa, ne woawɔ Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ŋu dɔwo, woakpɔ xɔxɔnuawo kple xɔawo dzi, woaklɔ nu kɔkɔeawo katã, eye woawɔ Mawu ƒe aƒe la ŋu dɔwo;

english_verse: They will also be in charge of the sacred loaves of bread, the flour for the grain sacrifices, the thin wafers, any offerings to be baked, and the flour mixed with olive oil. These Levites will weigh and measure these offerings.
translation_verse: woakpe ŋkumeɖobolo la, wɔ memee hena nuɖuvɔsa, tatali maʋamaʋãwo, nusiwo wotɔna le nutɔgba me, nu bakabakawo kple nudotree kpakple dzidzenuawo dzi;

english_verse: They must also give thanks and sing praises when sacrifices are offered on each Sabbath, as well as during New Moon Festivals and other religious feasts. There must always be enough Levites on duty at the temple to do everything that needs to be done.
translation_verse: Woava tasɔsɔe, ne wole numevɔwo katã sa ge le dzudzɔgbe, dzinu yeye kple ŋkekenyuiewo dzi le woƒe ɖoɖo la nu le Yehowa ŋku me tegbee;

english_verse: They were once in charge of taking care of the sacred tent; now they are responsible for the temple and for helping Aaron's descendants.
translation_verse: ne woawo Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la ŋu dɔwo, kɔkɔeƒe la ŋu dɔwo kple wo nɔvi Aron viwo ƒe dɔwo, eye woasubɔ le Yehowa ƒe aƒe la me.

english_verse: Aaron's descendants were then divided into work groups. Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Aron viwo ƒe hawo nye esi: Aron viwo nye: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar kple Itamar.

english_verse: But Nadab and Abihu died long before their father, without having any sons. That's why Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
translation_verse: Ke Nadab kple Abihu wotre kuku na wo fofo, eye viŋutsua ɖeke menɔ wo si o, eyata Eleazar kple Itamar wòzu nunɔlawo.

english_verse: David divided Aaron's descendants into groups, according to their assigned work. Zadok, one of Eleazar's descendants, and Ahimelech, one of Ithamar's descendants, helped David.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid kple Zadok, amesi tso Eleazar viwo dome, kpakple Aximelex tso Itamar viwo dome mã wo ɖe woƒe dɔ me haha.

english_verse: groups, and Ithamar's were divided into eight groups, because Eleazar's family included more family leaders.
translation_verse: wuiasiekelia dze Petaxya dzi, blavelia dze Yexezkel dzi,

english_verse: However, both families included temple officials and priests, and so to make sure the work was divided fairly, David asked God what to do.
translation_verse: Edzidze nu hafi ma woa kple eve la, elabena woawoe nye kɔkɔeƒe la nu amegãwo kple Mawu ƒe amegãwo tso Eleazar viwo kple Itamar viwo dome.

english_verse: As each group was assigned their duties, Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the Levite wrote down the name of the family leader in charge of that group. The witnesses were David and his officials, as well as Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the family leaders from the clans of the priests and the Levites.
translation_verse: Eye agbalẽŋlɔla Semaya, Netaneel vi tso Lewi-viwo dome, ŋlɔ wo ɖi le fia la kple amegãwo, nunɔla Zadok kple Aximelex, Abyatar vi, kpakple nunɔlawo kple Lewi-viwo ƒe aƒekɔwo ƒe tatɔwo ŋku me; ne wodzidze nu ɖe Eleazar ƒe aƒekɔ ɖeka dzi la, ekema wodzidzea nu ɖe Itamar to ɖeka dzi.

english_verse: These men were assigned their duties at the temple, just as the Lord God of Israel had commanded their ancestor Aaron. The Rest of the Levites Are Assigned Their Duties
translation_verse: Esia nye woƒe ɖoɖomewo hena woƒe dɔwɔwɔ, ne woayi Yehowa ƒe aƒe la me le ɖoɖo, si wo fofo Aron do na wo la nu, abe alesi Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, de se nɛ ene. Lewitɔwo ƒe tatɔwo.

english_verse: Here is a list of the other descendants of Levi: Amram was the ancestor of Shubael and Jehdeiah.
translation_verse: Lewi-vi susɔeawo nye esi: Subael tso Amram viwo dome, Yexdeya tso Subael viwo dome,

english_verse: Rehabiah was the ancestor of Isshiah, the oldest son in his family.
translation_verse: Yisiya enye tatɔ le Rexabya viwo dome,

english_verse: Izhar was the father of Shelomoth and the grandfather of Jahath.
translation_verse: Selomot tso Yizhar viwo dome, Yaxat tso Selomot viwo dome.

english_verse: Hebron had four sons, in the following order: Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
translation_verse: Xebron viwo nye: Yeriya, amesi nye tatɔ, evelia nye Amarya, etɔ̃lia nye Yaxaziel, enelia nye Yekamam.

english_verse: Uzziel was the father of Micah and the grandfather of Shamir.
translation_verse: Uziel viwo nye: Mixa, Samir tso Mixa viwo dome.

english_verse: Isshiah, Micah's brother, was the father of Zechariah.
translation_verse: Mixa nɔvi nye Yisiya; Zaxarya tso Yisiya viwo dome.

english_verse: Merari was the father of Mahli, Mushi, and Jaaziah.
translation_verse: Merari viwo nye Maxli kple Musi kpakple via Yaazya viwo.

english_verse: Jaaziah had three sons: Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
translation_verse: Merari vi, siwo via Yaazya dzi, wonye Soham, Zakur kple Ibri.

english_verse: Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the descendants of Levi, according to their clans.
translation_verse: Musi viwo nye: Maxli, Eder kple Yerimot. Esiawo nye Lewi-viwo ƒe viwo le woƒe aƒekɔwo nu.

english_verse: Each one was assigned his duties in the same way that their relatives the priests had been assigned their duties. David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the family leaders of the priests and Levites were the witnesses.
translation_verse: Eye woawo hã dzidze nu abe wo nɔvi Aron viwo ke ene, le fia Dawid, Zadok kple Aximelex kpakple nunɔlawo kple Lewi-viwo ƒe aƒekɔwo ƒe tatɔwo ŋku me; aƒekɔwo ƒe ame tsitsiwo kple woƒe tsɛwo siaa.

english_verse: David and the temple officials chose the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to be in charge of music. They were to praise the Lord by playing cymbals, harps and other stringed instruments. Here is a list of the musicians and their duties:
translation_verse: Eye Dawid kple aʋakɔ la ƒe amegãwo ɖa Asaf viwo, Heman viwo kple Yedutun viwo, amesiwo ƒoa kasaŋku, saŋku kple gakogoe la, hena woƒe subɔsubɔdɔ. Dɔwɔla, siwo asubɔ la ƒe xexlẽme enye si:

english_verse: Asaph's four sons, Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, were under the direction of their father and played music whenever the king told them to.
translation_verse: Asaf viwo nye: Sakur, Yosef, Netanya kple Asarela Asaf viwo nɔ Asaf, si ƒoa saŋku le fia ƒe ɖoɖo nu la gbɔ.

english_verse: Heman was one of the king's prophets, and God honored Heman by giving him
translation_verse: Amesiawo katã nye fia ƒe nukpɔla, Heman ƒe viwo, ne eƒe dzo nadidi le Mawu ƒe nya nu; elabena Mawu na ŋutsuvi wuiene kple nyɔnuvi etɔ̃ Heman.

english_verse: His sons were under his direction and played cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments during times of worship at the temple. Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman took their orders directly from the king.
translation_verse: Amesiawo katã tsoa gakogoe, saŋku kple kasaŋku ƒoa hãe le Yehowa ƒe aƒe la me le wo fofo Asaf, Heman kple Yedutun ƒe kpɔkplɔ te, abe alesi fia la ɖo ene.

english_verse: David assigned them their duties by asking the Lord what he wanted. Everyone was responsible for something, whether young or old, teacher or student.
translation_verse: Eye wodzidze nu ɖe woƒe dɔ ƒe ɖoɖome dzi hena ɖeviwo kple ame tsitsiwo, nufialawo kple nusrɔ̃viwo siaa.

english_verse: Obed-Edom had been blessed with eight sons: Shemaiah, Jehozabad, Joah, Sachar, Nethanel, Ammiel, Issachar, and Peullethai.
translation_verse: adelia nye Amiel, adrelia nye Isaxar, eye enyilia nye Peultai: elabena Mawu yrae.

english_verse: Shemaiah was the father of Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad, Elihu, and Semachiah. They were all respected leaders in their clan.
translation_verse: Semaya viwo nye: Otni, Rafael, Obed kple Elzabad, amesi nɔviwo Elihu kple Semaxya wonye kalẽtɔwo.

english_verse: Eighteen descendants of Meshelemiah were chosen for this work.
translation_verse: Meselemya viwo kple nɔviawo le wo ame wuienyi, eye wonye kalẽtɔwo.

english_verse: The guards were divided into groups, according to their family leaders, and they were assigned duties at the temple, just like the other Levites.
translation_verse: Agbonudzɔlawo ƒe ha siawo, siwo nye ŋutsuawo ƒe tatɔwo la ƒe dɔ enye ŋudzɔdzɔ, ne woasubɔ le Yehowa ƒe aƒe la me abe wo nɔviwo ke ene.

english_verse: Each group, no matter how large or small, was assigned a gate to guard, and they let the Lord show them what he wanted done.
translation_verse: Eye wodzidze nu le woƒe aƒekɔwo nu, woɖale sue alo wololo o, hena agbo sia agbo.

english_verse: Shelemiah was chosen to guard the East Gate. Zechariah his son was a wise man and was chosen to guard the North Gate.
translation_verse: Dzidze la dze Selemya dzi ɖe ɣedzeƒe gome; eye wodzidze nu de via Zaxarya, amesi nye adaŋudela nyanu la dzi, eye eƒe dzidze dze anyiehe gome.

english_verse: Obed-Edom was then chosen to guard the South Gate, and his sons were chosen to guard the storerooms.
translation_verse: Obed-Edom tɔ nye dziehe gome, eye viawo tɔ nye nudzraɖoƒe la.

english_verse: Shuppim and Hosah were chosen to guard the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the upper road. The guards were assigned the following work schedule:
translation_verse: Supim kple Xosa tɔ nye ɣetoɖoƒe gome le Salexet-gbo la nu le mɔ, si lia to la to, dzɔƒe le dzɔƒe xa.

english_verse: Each day six guards were on duty on the east side of the temple, four were on duty on the north side, and four were on duty on the south side. Two guards were stationed at each of the two storerooms,
translation_verse: Lewi-vi ade le ɣedzeƒe gome, wo ame ene le anyiehe gbesiagbe, wo ame ene le dziehe gbesiagbe, eye wo ame eve le nudzraɖoƒe la nu;

english_verse: four were stationed along the road leading to the west courtyard, and two guards stayed in the court itself.
translation_verse: esiwo le Parbar le ɣetoɖoƒe gome, wonye: wo ame ene le mɔ to, eye wo ame eve le Parbar.

english_verse: These were the guard duties assigned to the men from the clans of Korah and Merari. Guards Are Assigned to the Treasury
translation_verse: Esia nye agbonudzɔlawo ƒe hawo tso Korax viwo kple Merari viwo dome. Kesinɔnuwo dzikpɔlawo ɖoɖo.

english_verse: The Levites who were relatives of the Korahites and the Merarites were in charge of guarding the temple treasury and the gifts that had been dedicated to God.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ wo nɔvi Lewi-viwo ɖo Mawu ƒe aƒe la ƒe kesinɔnuwo kple nu kɔkɔeawo nu.

english_verse: Ladan was from the Gershon clan and was the father of Jehieli. Many of his other descendants were family leaders in the clan.
translation_verse: Laedan, amesi tso Gerson viwo dome ƒe viwo, siwo nye Gerson vi Laedan ƒe aƒekɔwo ƒe tatɔwo, wonye Yexiel viwo.

english_verse: Jehieli was the father of Zetham and Joel, and they were responsible for guarding the treasury.
translation_verse: Yexiel viwo nye: Zetam kple nɔvia Yoel; woawoe le Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ƒe kesinɔnuwo nu.

english_verse: Other guards at the treasury were from the Kohathite clans of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
translation_verse: Amesiwo tso Amram-hawo, Yizhar-hawo, Xebron-hawo kple Uziel-hawo dome, wonye.

english_verse: Shebuel was a descendant of Gershom the son of Moses. He was the chief official in charge of the temple treasury.
translation_verse: Sebuel, amesi nye Mose vi Gersom ƒe vi, eya le kesinɔnuawo nu.

english_verse: The descendants of Gershom's brother Eliezer included Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, and Shelomoth.
translation_verse: Eye nɔvia Eliezer viwo nye Rexabya, eya ƒe vi nye Yesaya, eya ƒe vi nye Yoram, eya ƒe vi nye Zixri, eya ƒe vi nye Selomot.

english_verse: Shelomoth and his relatives were in charge of all the gifts that were dedicated to the Lord. These included the gifts that King David had dedicated, as well as those dedicated by the family leaders, army officers, and army commanders.
translation_verse: Selomot sia kple nɔviawo wotsɔ ɖo kesinɔnu kɔkɔeawo katã, siwo ŋu ba Dawid kple aƒekɔwo ƒe tatɔwo, ame akpe kple ame alafawo ƒe amegãwo kpakple aʋafiawo kɔ la nu;

english_verse: And whenever valuable things were captured in battle, these men brought back some of them to make repairs to the temple.
translation_verse: aboyonu, siwo wokpɔ tso aʋa me la dome, woɖe wo tsoe heka wo ŋu, ne woatsɔ akpe ɖe Yehowa ƒe aƒe ta tutu ŋui;

english_verse: Shelomoth and his relatives were responsible for any gifts that had been given to the temple, including those from Samuel the prophet, King Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah. Other Officers Are Assigned Their Duties
translation_verse: hekpe ɖe nusiwo katã ŋu nukpɔla Samuel, Saul, Kis vi, Abner, Ner vi, kpakple Yoab, Zeruya vi, woka la ŋuti. Ne amesiame kɔ nane ŋu la, wotsɔnɛ dea asi na Selomot kple nɔviawo. Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ɖoɖo.

english_verse: Chenaniah from the Izhar clan and his sons were government officials and judges. They did not work at the temple.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ Kenanya, amesi tso Yizhar viwo dome la, kple viawo ɖo dɔwɔwɔ nu le Israel, wonye dɔdzikpɔlawo kple ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah had begun to count the people, but he stopped when the Lord began punishing Israel. So the total number was never included in David's official records. Officials in Charge of the King's Property
translation_verse: Yoab, Zeruya vi, de asi wo xexlẽ me, ke mewu enu o, elabena eyatae dɔmedzoe va Israel dzi ɖo; eya ŋuti womede xexlẽme la fia Dawid ŋutinya me o. Dawid ƒe subɔlawo kple dɔwɔlawo.

english_verse: who was the leader of the Thirty Warriors, and whose son Ammizabad was also an army commander;
translation_verse: Benaya sia enye kalẽtɔ le ame blaetɔ̃awo dome, eye wòle ame blaetɔ̃awo nu; evia Amizabad le eƒe ha la me.

english_verse: in the fourth month, Asahel the brother of Joab, whose son Zebadiah took over command after him;
translation_verse: Enelia, le dzinu enelia me, enye Asahel. Yoab nɔvi, eye via Zebadya dze eyome; eƒe ha la le ame akpe blave vo ene.

english_verse: in the sixth month, Ira the son of Ikkesh from Tekoa;
translation_verse: Adelia, le dzinu adelia me, enye Ira, Ikes vi, tso Tekoa; eƒe ha la le ame akpe blave vɔ ene.

english_verse: in the seventh month, Helez from Pelon in the territory of Ephraim;
translation_verse: Adrelia, le dzinu adrelia me, enye Pelonitɔ Xelez tso Efrayim-viwo dome; eƒe ha la le ame akpe blave vo ene.

english_verse: in the eighth month, Sibbecai from Hushah of the Zerah clan;
translation_verse: Enyilia, le dzinu enyilia me, enye Xusatitɔ Sibexai tso Zarxi viwo dome; eƒe ha la le ame akpe blave vɔ ene.

english_verse: in the ninth month, Abiezer from Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin;
translation_verse: Asiekelia, le dzinu asiekelia me, enye Anatotitɔ Abiezer tso Benyamin-viwo dome; eƒe ha la le ame akpe blave vɔ ene.

english_verse: in the tenth month, Maharai from Netophah of the Zerah clan;
translation_verse: Ewolia, le dzinu ewolia me, enye Netofatitɔ Maharai tso Zarxi viwo dome; eƒe ha la le ame akpe blave vɔ ene.

english_verse: in the eleventh month, Benaiah from Pirathon in the territory of Ephraim;
translation_verse: Wuiɖekɛlia, le dzinu wuiɖekɛlia me, enye Piratonitɔ Benaya tso Efrayim-viwo dome; eƒe ha la le ame akpe blave vɔ ene.

english_verse: in the twelfth month, Heldai from Netophah, who was a descendant of Othniel. David Assigns Tribal Leaders
translation_verse: Wuievelia, le dzinu wuievelia me, enye Netofatitɔ Xeldai tso Otniel viwo dome, eƒe ha la le ame akpe blave vɔ ene. Ƒomeawo ƒe amegãwo

english_verse: When David decided to count the people of Israel, he gave orders not to count anyone under
translation_verse: Ke Dawid mexlẽ amesiwo xɔ ƒe blave kple amesiwo mekpɔ xɔ nenema haɖe o la, ɖe eme o, elabena Yehowa do ŋugbe be, yeawɔ Israel wòasɔ gbɔ abe dziƒoɣletiviwo ene.

english_verse: years of age, because the Lord had promised long ago that Israel would have as many people as there are stars in the sky.
translation_verse: Efrayim-viwo tɔ enye Hosea, Azazya vi; Manase-to afã la tɔ enye Yoel, Pedaya vi;

english_verse: Azmaveth the son of Adiel was in charge of the king's personal storage rooms. Jonathan the son of Uzziah was in charge of the king's other storerooms that were in the towns, the villages, and the defense towers in Israel.
translation_verse: Azmawet, Adiel vi, le fia la ƒe kesinɔnuwo nu, eye Yonatan, Uziya vi, le nusiwo wodzra ɖo ɖe agblewo, duwo, kɔƒewo kple mɔwo me la nu;

english_verse: Ezri the son of Chelub was in charge of the workers who farmed the king's land.
translation_verse: Ezri, Kelub vi, le agbledela, siwo ŋlɔa agble la nu;

english_verse: Shimei from Ramah was in charge of the vineyards, and Zabdi from Shepham was in charge of storing the wine.
translation_verse: Simei, Ramatitɔ, le weingblewo nu; eye Zabdi, Sifmitɔ, le wein, siwo wotsɔ tso weingblewo me dzra ɖo la nu.

english_verse: Baal Hanan from Geder was in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the western foothills, and Joash was in charge of storing the olive oil.
translation_verse: Baal-Xanan, Gederitɔ, le amiti kple gboti, siwo wodo ɖe tagba la nu; eye Yoas le ami, siwo wodzra ɖo la nu:

english_verse: Shitrai from Sharon was responsible for the cattle that were kept in Sharon Plain, and Shaphat son of Adlai was responsible for those kept in the valleys.
translation_verse: Sitrai, Saronitɔ, le nyi, siwo ɖua gbe le Saron la nu; eye Safat, Adlai vi, le nyi, siwo le bali me la nu;

english_verse: These were the men in charge of David's royal property. David's Personal Advisors
translation_verse: Yaziz, Hagritɔ, le alẽwo nu. Amesiawo katãe nɔ fia Dawid ƒe kesinɔnuwo nu.

english_verse: David's uncle Jonathan was a wise and intelligent advisor. He and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni taught David's sons.
translation_verse: Dawid tɔdia Yonatan enye adaŋudela, gɔmesese le esi, eye wonya agbalẽ me; Yexiel, Xaxmoni vi, le fiaviwo gbɔ;

english_verse: Ahithophel and Hushai the Archite were two of David's advisors.
translation_verse: Axitofel enye fia ƒe adaŋudela; Xusai, Arkitɔ, enye fia xɔlɔ̃.

english_verse: Jehoiada the son of Benaiah was the king's advisor after Ahithophel, and later, Abiathar was his advisor. Joab was commander of Israel's army.
translation_verse: Amesiwo kplɔ Axitofel ɖo, wonye Yoyada, Benaya vi, kple Abyatar; eye fia la ƒe aʋafia enye Yoab.

english_verse: David called a meeting in Jerusalem for all of Israel's leaders, including the tribal leaders, the government officials, the army commanders, the officials in charge of the royal property and livestock, the palace officials, and the brave warriors.
translation_verse: Tele Dawid ƒo Israel ƒe amegãwo katã, toawo ƒe amegãwo, hawo ƒe amegã, siwo subɔa fia la, ame akpewo ƒe amegãwo kple ame alafawo ƒe amegãwo kpakple amesiwo kpɔa fia la kple viawo ƒe kesinɔnuwo kple lãhawo dzi la nu ƒu ɖe Yerusalem hekpe ɖe aƒedzikpɔlawo, kalẽtɔwo kple ŋutsu ŋkumesesẽtɔwo katã ŋu.

english_verse: After everyone was there, David stood up and said: Listen to me, my people. I wanted to build a place where the sacred chest would be kept, so we could go there and worship the Lord our God. I have prepared all the supplies for building a temple,
translation_verse: Eye fia la tso ɖe tsitrenu gblɔ bena; Nɔvinyewo kple nye dukɔ, miɖo tom! Meɖo ɖe la me be, matu gbɔɖemeƒe na Yehowa ƒe nubablaɖaka la kple mía Mawu ƒe afɔɖodzinu, eye medzra ɖo ɖe elutu ŋu.

english_verse: but the Lord has refused to let me build it, because he said I have killed too many people in battle.
translation_verse: Ke Mawu gblɔ nam be: Matu xɔa ɖeke na nye ŋkɔ o, elabena aʋame nenye, eye nekɔ ʋu ɖe anyi.

english_verse: The Lord God chose Judah to be the leading tribe in Israel. Then from Judah, he chose my father's family, and from that family, he chose me to be the king of Israel, and he promised that my descendants will also rule as kings.
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, dam le fofonye ƒe aƒe blibo la me, be maɖu fia ɖe Israel dzi tegbee, elabena etia Yuda, ne wòanye amegã, eye nye nu nyo eŋu le fofonye Yuda ƒe aƒe me kple fofonye viwo dome, eye wòtsɔm ɖo fia ɖe Israel blibo la nu.

english_verse: The Lord has blessed me with many sons, but he chose my son Solomon to be the next king of Israel.
translation_verse: Etia vinye Salomo le vinyewo katã dome, elabena Yehowa na vi geɖem, ne woabɔbɔ nɔ Yehowa ƒe Israel-fiaɖuƒe la ƒe fiazikpui dzi.

english_verse: The Lord said to me, “Your son Solomon will build my temple, and it will honor me. Solomon will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nam be: Viwò Salomo netu nye xɔ, eye wòatɔ nye kpɔwo, elabena metia eya, ne wòanye vinye, eye nyea manye fofoa.

english_verse: If he continues to obey my laws and commands, his kingdom will never end.”
translation_verse: Mali ke eƒe fiaɖuƒe la tegbee, nenye be, elé nye sewo kple kɔnuwo me ɖe asi sesĩe, eye wòwɔ wo dzi, abe alesi wòle egbe siawo ene.

english_verse: My friends, you are the Lord's people. And now, with God as your witness, I want you to promise that you will do your best to obey everything the Lord God has commanded us. Then this land will always belong to you and your descendants.
translation_verse: Eyata mele nu xlɔ̃m mi le Israel blibo la kple Yehowa ƒe ha la ŋku me kpakple ɖe mía Mawu ƒe to me be: Milé Yehowa, mia Mawu ƒe seawo katã me ɖe asi, eye midi eyome, ne miaxɔ anyigba nyui la, eye mia megbeviwo natsɔe anyi dome tegbee.

english_verse: Solomon, my son, worship God and obey him with all your heart and mind, just as I have done. He knows all your thoughts and your reasons for doing things, and so if you turn to him, he will hear your prayers. But if you ignore him, he will reject you forever.
translation_verse: Eye wò, vinye Salomo, dze si fofowò ƒe Mawu la, eye nasubɔe kple dzi blibo kpakple luʋɔ blibo, elabena Yehowa dzroa dziwo katã me kpɔna, eye wonya tamesusuwo katã! Ne èdii la, ana be, nakpɔe; ke ne ègblẽe ɖi la, atsɔ wò aƒu gbe tegbee.

english_verse: The Lord has chosen you to build a temple for worshiping him. Be confident and do the work you have been assigned.
translation_verse: Eyata nyae be, Yehowa ɖa wò, be natu xɔ, si anye kɔkɔeƒe; lé dzi ɖe ƒo, eye na wɔe ade goe! Dawid tsɔ gbedoxɔ ƒe nɔnɔme de asi na Salomo, eye wòtsɔ nusiwo wodzra ɖo hã nɛ.

english_verse: After David finished speaking, he gave Solomon the plans for building the main rooms of the temple, including the porch, the storerooms, the rooms upstairs and downstairs, as well as the most holy place.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid tsɔ xɔ la ƒe akpata, eŋu xɔwo, nudzraɖoƒewo, dzisasrãwo kple xɔ emetɔwo kpakple nutsyɔnu la xɔ ƒe nɔnɔme de asi na via Salomo.

english_verse: He gave Solomon his plans for the courtyards and the open areas around the temple, and for the rooms to store the temple treasures and gifts that had been dedicated to God.
translation_verse: Etsɔ nusiwo katã wobu ɖe ta me la ƒe nɔnɔme de asi nɛ, siwo nye Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ƒe kpɔwo kple eŋu xɔwo katã godoo, Mawu ƒe aƒe la ƒe nudzraɖoƒewo kple nu kɔkɔeawo dzraɖoƒewo;

english_verse: David also gave Solomon his plans for dividing the priests and the Levites into groups, as well as for the work that needed to be done at the temple and for taking care of the objects used for worship.
translation_verse: nunɔlawo kple Lewi-viwo ƒe hawo, Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ƒe subɔsubɔdɔwo katã kple Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ƒe subɔsubɔnuawo katã;

english_verse: He told Solomon how much gold and silver was to be used in making the sacred objects,
translation_verse: sika ɖe sikanuawo ŋu, alesi atu subɔsubɔnuawo dome ɖesiaɖe nu,

english_verse: the gold table which held the sacred loaves of bread, the tables made of silver,
translation_verse: sika alesi nu atu ŋkumeɖobolo ƒe kplɔ̃wo dome ɖe siaɖe nu, kple klosalo ɖe klosalokplɔ̃awo ŋu;

english_verse: the gold incense altar, and the gold statue of a chariot for the winged creatures which were on the lid of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: kple sika nyuitɔ alesi atu dzudzɔdovɔsamlekpui la nu hekpe ɖe sika Kerubiawo, siwo keke aʋala hetsyɔ Yehowa ƒe nubablaɖaka dzi la ƒe tasiaɖam la ŋuti.

english_verse: David then said to Solomon: The Lord showed me how his temple is to be built.
translation_verse: Nusiawo katã Yehowa, amesi fia do siawo katã ƒe nɔnɔmem la ƒe asi ŋlɔ nam.

english_verse: But you must see that everything is done according to these plans. Be confident, and never be afraid of anything or get discouraged. The Lord my God will help you do everything needed to finish the temple, so it can be used for worshiping him.
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ na via Salomo bena: Sẽ ŋu, eye lé dzi ɖe ƒo, eye na wòe aɖe goe; megavɔ̃ o, eye dzika megatso ƒowò o; elabena Yehowa Mawu, nye Mawu, li kpli wo, maɖe asi le ŋuwò o, eye magblẽ wò ɖi o, vaseɖe esime na wu Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ƒe dɔwo katã nu!

english_verse: The priests and Levites have been assigned their duties, and all the skilled workers are prepared to do their work. The people and their leaders will do anything you tell them.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, nunɔlawo kple Lewi-viwo ƒe hawo nye esi ɖe Mawu ƒe aƒe la ƒe subɔsubɔdɔwo katã ŋu, eye aɖaŋuwɔla, siwo lɔ̃ le wo ɖokui si hena do vovovowo wɔwɔ kple amegãwo kpakple du ko blibo la, le asiwò me.

english_verse: That's why I have done my best to get everything Solomon will need to build it—gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, onyx, turquoise, colored gems, all kinds of precious stones, and marble.
translation_verse: Metso nye ŋusẽ katã dzra ɖo ɖe nye Mawu ƒe aƒe la ŋu; sika ɖe sikanuawo ŋu, klosalo ɖe klosalonuawo ŋu, akɔbli ɖe akɔblinuawo ŋu, gayibɔ ɖe gayibɔ miawo gu, ati ɖe atinuawo ŋu, soham-kpe, kpe, siwo woatsɔ aɖo awuawo ŋu, kpe yibɔwo, kpe ŋɔŋɔewo, kpe xɔasi vovovowo kpakple kpe ɣiwo wosɔ gbɔ taŋtaŋ.

english_verse: and to make the gold and silver objects. Now, who else will show their dedication to the Lord by giving gifts for building his temple?
translation_verse: eye woatsɔ wo awɔ sikanuawo katã kple klosalonuawo katã kpakple aɖaŋuwɔlawo ƒe do vovovoawoe. Azɔ, amekae lɔ̃ le eɖokui si be, yeana nu Yehowa egbea?

english_verse: After David finished speaking, the family leaders, the tribal leaders, the army commanders, and the government officials voluntarily gave gifts
translation_verse: Tete aƒekɔwo ƒe amegãwo, Israel-toawo ƒe amegãwo, ame akpewo kple ame alafawo ƒe amegãwo kpakple fia ƒe dɔwɔlawo ƒe amegãwo lã faa,

english_verse: Everyone who owned precious stones also donated them to the temple treasury, where Jehiel from the Levite clan of Gershon guarded them.
translation_verse: Eye amesi ke si kpe xɔasi le la, etsɔnɛ na Gerson vi Yexiel, ne woatso awɔ Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ƒe kesinɔnui. Dawid da akpe na Mawu.

english_verse: David and the people were very happy that so much had been given to the Lord, and they all celebrated. David Praises the Lord
translation_verse: Eye dukɔ la kpɔ dzidzɔ le esi wolɔ̃ faa la la, elabena wona nu Yehowa tso dzi blibo me faa; eye fia Dawid hã kpɔ dzidzɔ eteƒe mekɔ o.

english_verse: Then, in front of everyone, David sang praises to the Lord: I praise you forever, Lord! You are the God our ancestor Jacob worshiped.
translation_verse: Tete Dawid kafu Mawu le ameha blibo la ŋku me gblɔ bena: Woakafu wò Yehowa, mía fofo Israel ƒe Mawu, tso mavɔ me yi mavɔ me!

english_verse: Your power is great, and your glory is seen everywhere in heaven and on earth. You are king of the entire world,
translation_verse: Yehowa, tɔwòe nye gãnyenye kple ŋusẽ, ŋutikɔkɔe, bubu kple kafukafu, elabena nusianu, si le dziƒo kple anyigba la, tɔwòe. Yehowa, tɔwòe nye fiaɖuƒe, eye wòe ɖo kpo ɖe nusiwo katã ƒe ŋkɔ de dzi la dzi.

english_verse: and you rule with strength and power. You make people rich and powerful and famous.
translation_verse: Kesinɔnu kple bubu tso gbɔwò, eye nèɖu fia ɖe nusianu dzi; gãnyenye kple ŋusẽ le asiwò me, eye gbɔwò wòtsona be, amea ɖe nazu gã, eye woakpe ŋusẽ.

english_verse: We thank you, our God, and praise you.
translation_verse: Eyata, mia Mawu, míele akpe dam na wo, eye miele wò ŋutikɔkɔe ƒe ŋkɔ la kafum;

english_verse: But why should we be happy that we have given you these gifts? They belong to you, and we have only given back what is already yours.
translation_verse: elabena ameka menye, eye ameka nye dukɔ la nye, be, miekpɔ ŋusẽ hena nu faa alea? Elabena nuwo katã tso gbɔwò, eye asiwò me miexɔ wo le hetsɔ na wò.

english_verse: We are only foreigners living here on earth for a while, just as our ancestors were. And we will soon be gone, like a shadow that suddenly disappears.
translation_verse: Elabena amedzrowo míenye le ŋkuwò me, eye amegbɔmewo míenye abe mía fofowo katã ene; míaƒe ŋkeke le abe vɔvɔli ene le anyigba dzi, eye mɔkpɔkpɔ mele eŋu o.

english_verse: Our Lord God, we have brought all these things for building a temple to honor you. They belong to you, and you gave them to us.
translation_verse: Yehowa, mía Mawu, nu gbogbo siawo, siwo mieƒo ƒu, be míatsɔ atu xɔ na wò hena wò ŋkɔ kɔkɔea la, tso asiwò me, eye tɔwòe nye wo katã.

english_verse: But we are happy, because everyone has voluntarily given you these things. You know what is in everyone's heart, and you are pleased when people are honest.
translation_verse: Nye Mawu, menyae be, wòe dzroa dziwo me kpɔna, eye dzimekɔkɔ nyoa ŋuwò. Nye dzime ko mena nusiawo katã faa; eye azɔ mekpe wò dukɔ, si le afisia kple dzidzɔ, be wona nu wò faa.

english_verse: Always make us eager to give, and help us be faithful to you, just as our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob faithfully worshiped you.
translation_verse: Yehowa, mía fofowo Abraham, Isak kple Israel ƒe Mawu, dzra susu kple tameɖoɖo sia ɖo ɖe wò dukɔ ƒe dzi me tegbee, eye natrɔ woƒe dziwo ɖe ŋuwò!

english_verse: And give Solomon the desire to completely obey your laws and teachings, and the desire to build the temple for which I have provided these gifts.
translation_verse: Eye na dzi blibo vinye Salomo, ne wòalé wò sewo, nufiafiawo kple ɖoɖowo me ɖe asi wòawɔ nuawo katã aɖe goe, eye woatu fiasã, si ŋu medzra nuawo ɖo ɖo la! Amisisi na Salomo.

english_verse: David then said to the people, “Now it's your turn to praise the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped!” So everyone praised the Lord, and they bowed down to honor him and David their king. Solomon Is Crowned King
translation_verse: Eye Dawid gblɔ na ameha blibo la bena: Mikafu Yehowa, mia Mawu la! Tete ameha blibo la kafu Yehowa, wo fofowo ƒe Mawu la, eye wobɔbɔ hede ta agu ɖe Yehowa kple fia la ŋku me.

english_verse: The people were very happy, and they ate and drank there at the Lord's altar. That same day, Solomon was again crowned king. The people celebrated and poured olive oil on Solomon's head to show that he would be their next king. They also poured oil on Zadok's head to show that he was their priest.
translation_verse: Woɖu nu no nu le Yehowa ŋku me gbemagbe kple dzidzɔ geɖe, eye woɖo fia Salomo, Dawid vi, zi evelia, wosi ami nɛ heɖo amegãe na Yehowa, eye wòsi ami na Zadok heɖo nunɔlae.

english_verse: So Solomon became king after David his father. Solomon was successful, and everyone in Israel obeyed him.
translation_verse: Eye Salomo bɔbɔ nɔ Yehowa ƒe fiazikpui la dzi hezu fia ɖe fofoa Dawid teƒe, eye dzɔgbenyuie le eŋu. Israel blibo la ɖo toe,

english_verse: Every official and every soldier, as well as all of David's other sons, were loyal to him.
translation_verse: eye amegãwo katã kple kalẽawo kpakple fia Dawid ƒe viwo katã hã de ta fia Salomo le.

english_verse: The Lord made Solomon a great king, and the whole nation was amazed at how famous he was. In fact, no other king of Israel was as great as Solomon. David Dies
translation_verse: Yehowa wo Salomo gã ŋutɔŋutɔ le Israel blibo la ŋku me, eye wòtso fiaɖuɖu, si ŋu kafukafu le la nɛ, esi tɔgbe menɔ fia, siwo ɖu Israel dzi do ŋgɔ nɛ la si o. Dawid ku.

english_verse: David the son of Jesse was king of Israel
translation_verse: Dawid, Isai vi la, ɖu fia ɖe Israel blibo la dzi.

english_verse: David was rich and respected and lived to be an old man. Then he died, and his son Solomon became king.
translation_verse: Eku amegã belibeli hafi ku, eye agbenɔnɔ, kesinɔnu kple bubu ti kɔ nɛ, eye via Salomo zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Everything David did while he was king is included in the history written by the prophets Samuel, Nathan, and Gad.
translation_verse: Fia Dawid ŋutinyawo, tsãtɔwo kple megbetɔwo la, kpɔ ɖa, woŋlɔ wo ɖe nukpɔla Samuel ŋutinyawo, nyagblɔɖila Natan ŋutinyawo kple nukpɔla Gad ŋutinyawo me

english_verse: They wrote about his powerful rule and about the things that happened not only to him, but also to Israel and the other nations.
translation_verse: hekpe ɖe eƒe dziɖuɖuwo katã, eƒe nu tsu wɔwɔwo kple nya, siwo dzɔ ɖe eya ŋutɔ kple Israel kpakple anyigba dzi fiaɖuƒewo katã dzi la ŋuti.

english_verse: While Solomon was king of Israel, there was silver and gold everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as ordinary sycamore trees in the foothills.
translation_verse: Fia la na klosalo kple sika sɔ gbɔ abe kpewo ene le Yerusalem, eye sedertiwo sɔ gbɔ abe gboti, siwo le tagba ene.

english_verse: and there at the bronze altar, Solomon offered a thousand animals as sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Eye Salomo sa numevɔ akpe ɖeka le afima le akɔblivɔsamlekpui, si le Yehowa ŋku me le Mawu ƒe agbadɔa gbɔ la dzi. Salomo ƒe gbedodoɖa, eƒe nunya kple kesinɔnuwo.

english_verse: God appeared to Solomon that night in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
translation_verse: Eye Mawu ɖe eɖokui fia Salomo le zã ma me gblɔ nɛ bena: Bia nusi mana wo!

english_verse: Solomon answered: Lord God, you were always loyal to my father David, and now you have made me king of Israel.
translation_verse: Salomo ɖo ŋu na Mawu bena: Eve fofonye Dawid nu ŋutɔ, eye netsɔm ɖo fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: I am supposed to rule these people, but there are as many of them as there are specks of dust on the ground. So keep the promise you made to my father
translation_verse: Azɔ Yehowa Mawu, nɔ wò nya, si negblɔ na fofonye Dawid la dzi, elabena wòe tsɔm ɖo fia ɖe dukɔ, si sɔ gbɔ abe anyigbake ene la dzi.

english_verse: God replied: Solomon, you could have asked me to make you rich or famous or to let you live a long time. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom and knowledge to rule my people.
translation_verse: Eye Mawu gblɔ na Salomo bena: Esi nusia le dzi me na wò, eye mebia ho kple kesinɔnu, bubu kple wò futɔwo ƒe ku kpakple wò agbenɔnɔ didi o, ke boŋ nebia nunya kple sidzedze, be ate ŋu aɖu fia ɖe nye dukɔ, si nu metsɔ wò ɖo fia ɖo dzi la,

english_verse: Solomon then left Gibeon and returned to Jerusalem, the capital city of Israel. Solomon's Wealth (
translation_verse: Eye Salomo gbɔ tso vɔsaƒe le Gibeon kple Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la gbɔ va Yerusalem, eye wòdze fiaɖuɖu gɔme ɖe Israel dzi.

english_verse: Solomon decided to build a temple where the Lord would be worshiped, and also to build a palace for himself.
translation_verse: Eye Salomo xlẽ agbatsɔla akpe blaadre kple kpefula akpe blanyi le towo dzi; wo dzikpɔlawo le ame akpe etɔ kple alafa ade.

english_verse: No one can ever build a temple large enough for God—even the heavens are too small a place for him to live in! All I can do is build a place where we can offer sacrifices to him.
translation_verse: Eyata do ŋutsu aɖaŋutɔa ɖe ɖem, amesi nya sika kple klosalo, akɔbli kple gayibɔ, aɖabɛ dzĩtɔ, ka dzẽ kple aɖabɛ blɔtɔ ŋu dɔwɔwɔ, eye wonyã aliŋɔŋlɔ la, wòava akpe ɖe aɖaŋutɔ, siwo le gbɔnye le Yuda kple Yerusalem, amesiwo fofonye Dawid do la ŋuti.

english_verse: Send me a worker who can not only carve, but who can work with gold, silver, bronze, and iron, as well as make brightly colored cloth. The person you send will work here in Judah and Jerusalem with the skilled workers that my father has already hired.
translation_verse: Eye do sedertiwo, sesewutiwo kple papawutiwo dem tso Libanon, elabena menyae bena, wò amewo nya Libanontiwo lalã, eye nye amewo akpe ɖe wò amewo ŋu,

english_verse: I know that you have workers who are experts at cutting lumber in Lebanon. So would you please send me some cedar, pine, and juniper logs? My workers will be there to help them,
translation_verse: ne woaƒo atiwo nu ƒu nam taŋtaŋ, elabena xɔ, si tu ge mala la, alolo eteƒe makɔ o.

english_verse: Hiram sent his answer back to Solomon: I know that the Lord must love his people, because he has chosen you to be their king.
translation_verse: Eye Xuram gblɔ bena: Woakafu Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, si wɔ dziƒo kple anyigba, eye wòna vi nyanu fia Dawid, amesi si gɔmesese kple nunya le, ne wòatu xɔ na Yehowa, eye wòatu xɔ na eƒe fiaɖuƒe.

english_verse: Go ahead and send the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine you promised to pay my workers.
translation_verse: ekema miatso atiawo le Libanon-to dzi, alesi nu nèhiã, eye míabla wo tatata ato ƒu dzi ava Yafo na wò, eye nava afɔ wo ayi Yerusalem.

english_verse: I will tell them to start cutting down trees in Lebanon. They will cut as many as you need, then tie them together into rafts, and float them down along the coast to Joppa. Your workers can take them to Jerusalem from there. Solomon's Work Force
translation_verse: Eye Salomo xlẽ amedzro, siwo katã le Israel-nyigba dzi, le alesi fofoa Dawid xlẽ wo la nu, wole ŋutsu akpe alafa ɖeka blaatɔ̃ vɔ etɔ̃ kple alafa ade.

english_verse: Solomon counted all the foreigners who were living in Israel, just as his father David had done when he was king, and the total was
translation_verse: Etso wo dometɔ akpe blaadre wo agbatsɔlawoe, etsɔ ame akpe blanyi wɔ kpefulawoe le towo dzi, eye ame akpe etɔ̃ kple alafa ade nye dzikpɔlawo, amesiwo kpɔ dukɔ la dzi le dɔwɔwɔ me.

english_verse: He used precious stones to decorate the temple, and he used gold imported from Parvaim
translation_verse: Eɖo kpe xɔasi xɔ la me, ne wòanye atsyɔ, eye sika la nye Parwayim-sika.

english_verse: Five hundred and seventy grams of gold was used to cover the heads of the nails. The walls of the small storage rooms were also covered with gold.
translation_verse: Gatagbadzɛawo ƒe kpekpeme le sika sekel blaatɔ̃, eye wòfa sika ɖe xɔ etametɔwo me.

english_verse: Solomon had the inside walls of the temple's main room paneled first with pine and then with a layer of gold, and he had them decorated with carvings of palm trees and designs that looked like chains.
translation_verse: Eklã sesewuʋuƒowo ɖe xɔ lolotɔ me, eye wòfa sika nyuitɔ ɖe wo ŋu, eye wòɖe detiwo kple kɔsɔkɔsɔwo ɖe wo me.

english_verse: Solomon had two statues of winged creatures made to put in the most holy place, and he covered them with gold.
translation_verse: Ekpa Kerubi eve ɖe kɔkɔeƒewo ƒe kɔkɔeƒe ƒe xɔ la me, eye wòfa sika ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: A curtain was made of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with designs of winged creatures. The Two Columns (
translation_verse: Eye wòtsɔ aɖabɛ blɔtɔ kple dzĩtɔ ƒe ka, ka dze kple ka ɣi lɔ̃ xɔmetsovɔ la, eye wòlɔ̃ Kerubiwo ɖe eme.

english_verse: Two columns were made for the entrance to the temple. Each one was
translation_verse: Ewɔ sɔti eve ɖe xɔ la nu, wokɔ abɔklugui blaetɔ̃ vɔ atɔ̃, eye wòɖo ta na wo wòkɔ abɔklugui atɔ̃.

english_verse: The top of each column was decorated with designs that looked like chains and with
translation_verse: Ewɔ kɔsɔkɔsɔwo ɖe gaɖɔwo ŋu hetsɔ ɖo sɔtiawo ta me, eye wòwɔ yevuboɖa alafa ɖeka hetsɔ de kɔsɔkɔsɔawo ŋu.

english_verse: Solomon had one of the columns placed on the south side of the temple's entrance; it was called Jachin. The other one was placed on the north side of the entrance; it was called Boaz.
translation_verse: Eye wòtu sɔtiawo ɖe akpata la nu, ɖeka le ɖusi me, eye evelia le mia me; ena ŋkɔ ɖusimetɔ be Yaxin, eye wòna ŋkɔ miametɔ be Boaz.

english_verse: Solomon had a bronze altar made that was nine meters square and four and a half meters high.
translation_verse: Eye wòwɔ akɔblivɔsamlekpui la, edidi abɔklugui blave, eye wòkɔ abɔklugui ewo.

english_verse: Ten gold lampstands were also made according to the plans. Solomon placed these lampstands inside the temple, five on each side of the main room.
translation_verse: Ewɔ sikakaɖi; ewo ɖe woƒe ɖoɖo la nu eye wòtsɔ wo ɖa ɖe dodonuxɔ la me, wo ame atɔ̃ le ɖusi me, eye wo ame atɔ̃ le mia me.

english_verse: He also gave orders to make a large metal bowl called the Sea. It was
translation_verse: Eye wòkɔ gazɔ la wòle tegblẽ, tso etoga ɖeka vaseɖe toga keme le abɔklugui ewo, ekɔ abɔklugui atɔ̃, eye ka abɔklugui blaetɔ̃ atui akpe ɖo.

english_verse: Its outer edge was decorated with two rows of carvings of bulls, ten bulls to about every
translation_verse: Wowɔ treklɔnutsetsewo ɖe eto godoo va kpe, wo ame ewo le abɔklugui ɖeka; treklɔnutsetsea wo le agbaka eve me ƒo xlã gazɔ la, eye wokɔ wo kplii ɖekae.

english_verse: He also made ten small bowls and put five on each side of the large bowl. The small bowls were used to wash the animals that were burned on the altar as sacrifices, and the priests used the water in the large bowl to wash their hands.
translation_verse: Eye wòwɔ gagba ewo; etsɔ wo ame atɔ̃ ɖo ɖusi me, eye wòtsɔ wo ame atɔ̃ ɖo mia me, esiwo me woaklɔ nuwo ɖo; woawo me woakpala numevɔsa ƒe lãwo ɖo, ke gazɔ la li, bena nunɔlawo nale tsi ɖe eme.

english_verse: He also made ten tables and placed them in the main room, five on each side. And he made
translation_verse: Ewɔ kplɔ̃ ewo hetsɔ da ɖe dodonuxɔ la me, wo ame atɔ̃ le ɖusi me, eye wo ame atɔ̃ le mia me; eye wòwɔ sikatre alafa ɖeka.

english_verse: Solomon gave orders to build two courtyards: a smaller one that only priests could use and a larger one. The doors to these courtyards were covered with bronze.
translation_verse: Eye wòtɔ nunɔlawo ƒe kpɔ kple kpɔ gãtɔ, ekpa kpɔ la ƒe agbowo, eye wofa akɔbli ɖe agboa wo ŋu.

english_verse: The large bowl called the Sea was placed near the southeast corner of the temple.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ gazɔ la ɖo ɖusi me kpa dzi le ɣedzeƒe gome ʋã ɖe dziehe.

english_verse: Huram made shovels, sprinkling bowls, and pans for hot ashes. Here is a list of the other furnishings he made for God's temple:
translation_verse: Eye Xuram wɔ zewo, sofiwo kple trewo. Ale Xuram wu Mawu ƒe xɔ ŋu ɖɔ la nu na fia Salomo,

english_verse: two columns, two bowl-shaped caps for the tops of these columns, two chain designs on the caps,
translation_verse: sɔti eveawo kple woƒe ta mligo, siwo le sɔti eveawo dzi,

english_verse: the stands and the small bowls,
translation_verse: ewɔ anyinɔwo kple gagbawo ɖe anyinɔawo ŋu;

english_verse: the large bowl and the twelve bulls that held it up,
translation_verse: gazɔ ɖeka kple nyi wuieve, siwo le ete;

english_verse: pans for hot ashes, as well as shovels and meat forks. Huram made all these things out of polished bronze
translation_verse: zewo, sofiwo kple gaflowo. Eye Xuram-Abi tsɔ akɔbli, si ŋu wozrɔ̃, wɔ nusiwo katã kpe ɖe wo ŋu la, na fia Salomo hena Yehowa ƒe aƒe la.

english_verse: by pouring melted bronze into the clay molds he had set up near the Jordan River, between Succoth and Zeredah.
translation_verse: Eye fia la na wokɔ wo ɖe nɔnɔme, sii wotsɔ anyi wɔe la me le Yordan-nutowo me le Sukot kple Zeredata dome.

english_verse: There were so many bronze furnishings that no one ever knew how much bronze it took to make them.
translation_verse: Salomo wɔ nusiawo katã taŋtaŋ, elabena akɔbliawo mele dada me o.

english_verse: Solomon also gave orders to make the following temple furnishings out of gold: the altar, the tables that held the sacred loaves of bread,
translation_verse: Eye Salomo tsɔ sika nyuitɔ wɔ Mawu ƒe aƒe la me nuwo katã: sikavɔsamlekpui la kple kplɔ̃, siwo dzi woada ŋkumeɖobolo ɖo,

english_verse: the lampstands and the lamps that burned in front of the most holy place,
translation_verse: akaɖitiawo kple woƒe akaɖigbɛ, siwo anɔ bibim le megbexɔ la ŋgɔ ɖe ɖoɖo la nu.

english_verse: whose wings covered both the chest and the poles used for carrying it.
translation_verse: Kerubiawo keke aʋala ɖe aɖaka la nɔƒe, ale be Kerubiawo tsyɔ aɖaka la kple eŋu kpoawo dzi tso dzi gome.
