translation_verse: eye fia la neɖo dzikpɔlawo ɖe eƒe fiaɖuƒe ƒe anyigbawo katã dzi, ne woaƒo ɖetugbi dzetugbewo katã nu ƒu ɖe nyɔnuwo ƒe aƒe me le Susa-mɔ̃ me, eye woatsɔ wo ade fia ƒe aƒe dzikpɔla Hegai, amesi nye nyɔnuwo ŋudzɔla si me, eye wòasi atike na wo,

english_verse: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
translation_verse: eye nyɔnuvi, si adze fia ŋu la, eya nanye fiasrɔ̃ ɖe Wasti teƒe! Tete nya la dze fia la ŋu, eye wòwɔ nenema.

english_verse: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Yuda-ŋutsua ɖe nɔ Susa-mɔ̃ me, amesi ŋkɔ nye Marɖoxai, Yair vi, amesi nye Simei vi, amesi nye Kis vi, enye Benyamintɔ

english_verse: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
translation_verse: eye woɖe aboyo eya kple aboyomeawo tso Yerusalem hekpe ɖe Yuda-fia Yexonya, amesi Babel-fia Nebukaɖnezar ɖe aboyoe la ŋuti.

english_verse: Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died.
translation_verse: Eya nyi etɔɖia ƒe nyɔnuvi Hadasa, si nye Ester la wòtsi, elabena tɔ kple nɔ megale esi o. Nyɔnuvi la nyo, eye wòdze tugbe. Eye esi fofoa kple dadaa woku la. Mardoxai xɔe wòzu vianyɔnu.

english_verse: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
translation_verse: Esime fia ƒe nya kple eƒe se ɖi wose, eye woƒo nyɔnuvi geɖewo nu ƒu ɖe Susa-mɔ̃ me hetsɔ wo de asi na Hegai la, wokplɔ Ester hã va fiasã la me hetsɔ de asi na nyɔnuwo ŋudzɔla Hegai.

english_verse: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
translation_verse: Nyɔnuvi la dze eŋu, eye wòve enu. Tete wòwɔ kaba, be wòasi atike nɛ, wòana eƒe nuduɖui, eye woatsɔ nyɔnuvi adre, siwo wotia tso fiaƒe me la, akpe ɖe eŋu, eye wòna nɔƒe nyuitɔ eya kple eƒe nyɔnuviwo le nyɔnuwo ƒe aƒe la me.

english_verse: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
translation_verse: Ke Ester meyɔ eƒe dukɔ kple wo de o, elabena Mardoxai de se nɛ be, megagblɔe o.

english_verse: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
translation_verse: Eye Mardoxai ɖia tsa gbesiagbe le nyɔnuwo ƒe aƒe la ƒe xɔxɔnu la nu, be yeanya, alesi Ester le kple nusi dzɔ ɖe edzi.

english_verse: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
translation_verse: Eye ne fia Axasweros gbɔ yiyi ɖo nyɔnuviawo dome ɖesiaɖe dzi, esime wowɔ nɛ le nyɔnuwo ƒe kɔnu la nu dzinu wuieve sɔŋ megbe vo la, — elabena ɣeyiɣi geɖe siawo wogblẽna ɖe woƒe atikesisi ŋu; wosia miremi dzinu ade, eye wosia atike ʋeʋẽe kple nyɔnuwo ƒe ami ʋeʋẽe dzinu ade —

english_verse: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
translation_verse: ekema nyɔnuvi la yia fia gbɔ, eye wotsɔa nusianu, si wòbia, be yeatsɔ tso nyɔnuwo ƒe me ayi fia ƒe me la nɛ.

english_verse: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
translation_verse: Ne eyi le fiẽ, eye wòtrɔ gbɔ va nyɔnuwo ƒe aƒe evelia me le ŋdi le fia ƒe aƒe dzikpɔla Saasgaz, amesi nye ahiãwo ŋudzɔla ƒe dzikpɔkpɔ te la, ekema mekpɔ mɔ agayi fia la gbɔ o, negbe ne eƒe nu nyo fia ŋu, eye wòyɔe hafi.

english_verse: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
translation_verse: Eye fia la lɔ̃a Ester wu nyɔnuwo katã, eƒe nu nyo eŋu, eye wòve enu wu ɖetugbiawo katã, etsɔ fiakuku la dɔ nɛ, eye wòtsɔe ɖo fiasrɔ̃e ɖe Wasti teƒe.

english_verse: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
translation_verse: Eye fia la tu aglo gãa ɖe na eƒe amegãwo katã kple eƒe dɔlawo, si nye Ester ƒe aglo; ena anyigbawo dzinɔlawo dzudzɔ dɔwɔwɔ, eye wòna nu, abe alesi dze fia ene.

english_verse: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
translation_verse: Esi woƒo ɖetugbiwo nu ƒu zi evelia la, Mardoxai bɔbɔ nɔ fia ƒe agbo nu.

english_verse: He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
translation_verse: Ke Ester meyɔ wo de kple eƒe dukɔ o, abe alesi Mardoxai de se nɛ ene, eye Ester ɖo to Mardoxai ƒe gbe, abe alesi wònɔ egbɔ wònyii wòtsi ke ene. Mardoxai ka atam ɖe fia ŋu.

english_verse: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Le ɣemaɣi, esi Mardoxai bɔbɔ nɔ fia ƒe agbo nu la, fia ƒe aƒe dzikpɔla eve, Bigtan kple Teres, amesiwo tso, agbonudzɔlawo dome la, do dɔmedzoe, eye wodi be, yewoawu fia Axasweros.

english_verse: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
translation_verse: Tete Mardoxai se nya la, eye wògblɔe na fiasrɔ̃ Ester, eye Ester gblɔe na fia la le Mardoxai ƒe ŋkɔ me.

english_verse: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_verse: Esi wodzro nya la me kpɔ be, ele me la, wohe wo ame eve la ɖe ati ŋu, eye woŋlɔe ɖe nyadzɔdzɔgbalẽ me na fia la.

english_verse: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
translation_verse: Le nya siawo megbe la fia Axasweros do gã Haman, Hamedata vi, si nye Agagitɔ la, gãe edoe ɖe dzi, eye wotsɔ eƒe zikpui ɖo amegã, siwo katã le eŋu la tɔwo ŋgɔ.

english_verse: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
translation_verse: Fia ƒe ɖɔla, siwo katã le fia ƒe agbo me la, bɔbɔna dea la agu na Haman, elabena alea fia la de se le, eŋu; ke Mardoxai mebɔnɔna nɛ o, eye mede ta agu hã o.

english_verse: When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command,
translation_verse: Tete fia ƒe dɔla, siwo le na ƒe agbo me la, gblɔna na Mardoxai bena. Nukaŋuti nele fia ƒe se dzi dam?

english_verse: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
translation_verse: Esime wole alea gblɔm nɛ gbesiagbe, ke medo toe na wo o la, woɖagblɔe na Haman be, yewoakpo be, woalɔ̃ ɖe Mardoxai ƒe nuwɔwɔ dzi loo; elabena egblɔ be, Yuɖatɔ yenye.

english_verse: Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him.
translation_verse: Eye esi Haman kpɔ be, Mardoxai mebɔbɔ hede ta agu na ye o la, dzi ku Haman vevie.

english_verse: And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
translation_verse: Ke ebu Mardoxai ɖeɖeko wuwu numaɖinui; elabena woyɔ Mardoxai ƒe dukɔ nɛ. Eyata Haman di be, yeatsrɔ̃ Yudatɔ, siwo katã le Axasweros ƒe fiaɖuƒe blibo la me, siwo nye Mardoxai ƒe dukɔ la.

english_verse: It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
translation_verse: Le dzinu gbãtɔ, si nye dzinu Nisan me, le fia Axasweros ƒe ƒe wuievelia me la, woda pur, si nye nudzidzernu le Haman ŋku me le ŋkeke sia ŋkeke dzi kple dzinu sia dzinu me vaseɖe dzinu wuievelia, si nye dzinu Adar me.

english_verse: Then Haman went to the king and said: Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them!
translation_verse: Tete Haman gblɔ na fia Axasweros bena: Dukɔ ɖekaa ɖe li, si kaka, eye, wòmã ɖe dukɔwo dome le wò fiaduƒe ƒe anyigbawo katã dzi; woƒe sewo to vovo tso dukɔ sia dukɔ tɔ gbɔ, eye womewɔa fia ƒe sewo dzi o; eyata medze fia be, wòazi kpi akpɔ wo alea o.

english_verse: Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
translation_verse: Ne edze fia ŋu la, ekema nena woaŋlɔ agbalẽ, ne woawu wo, eye mada klosalo talento akpe ewo na dzikpɔla wo woatsɔ ade fia ƒe kesinɔnuwo me.

english_verse: The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him,
translation_verse: Tete fia la ɖe eƒe ŋkosigɛ le asi hetsɔ na Haman, Hamedata vi, Agagitɔ, si nye Yudatɔwo ƒe ketɔ la.

english_verse: “Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ na Haman bena: Klosalo la nenɔ anyi ko; gake woawɔ dukɔ: la, alesi dze ŋuwò!

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
translation_verse: Tete woyɔ fia ƒe agbalẽŋlɔlawo le dzinu gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke wutetɔ̃lia dzi, eye woŋlɔ agbalẽ, abe alesi Haman de see ene, ɖe anyigba sia anyigba ƒe nuŋɔŋlɔ kple dukɔ sia dukɔ ƒe gbegbɔgblɔ nu heɖo ɖe fia ƒe amegãwo kple anyigba dzikpɔla, siwo le anyigba sia anyigba nu kpakple dukɔ sia dukɔ ƒe tatɔwo; woŋlɔe le fia Axasweros ƒe ŋkɔ me, eye wotsɔ fia ƒe ŋkɔsigɛ ɖo ŋkɔ ete.

english_verse: The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
translation_verse: Tete wode agbalẽ la duxɔlawo si ɖo ɖe fia ƒe anyigbawo katã dzi, be woatsrɔ̃ Yudatɔwo katã, woawu wo, eye woagblẽ wo, ɖeviwo kple tsitsiawo, vidzĩewo kple nyɔnuwo siaa le ŋkeke ɖeka dzi le dzinu wuievelia, si nye dzinu Adar ƒe ŋkeke wuietɔ̃lia dzi, eye woaha woƒe nuwo.

english_verse: King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_verse: Tete duxɔlawo yi kaba le fia ƒe nya la nu, eye wode se la le Susa-mɔ̃ me. Eye fia la kple Haman wobɔbɔ nɔ anyi le aha nom; ke ʋunyaʋunya ɖo Susa-du la me.

english_verse: When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping.
translation_verse: Esi Mardoxai se nya, siwo katã dzɔ la, Mardoxai dze eƒe awuwo, ta akpanya, si afi, eye wòto dua titina le ɣli dom sesĩe nublanuitɔe

english_verse: But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace.
translation_verse: heva fia ƒe agbo nu; elabena amea ɖeke mekpɔ mɔ anɔ akpanya me age ɖe fia ƒe agbo me o.

english_verse: In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
translation_verse: Eye nuxaxa gãa ɖe ɖo Yudatɔwo dome le anyigba, siwo katã dzi fia ƒe nya kple eƒe se la de la dzi, wotsi nu dɔ, wofa avi, eye wofa konyi, eye wo dometɔ geɖewo ta akpanya hesi afi.

english_verse: When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
translation_verse: Esi Ester ƒe nyɔnudɔlawo kple eƒe aƒe dzikpɔlawo va toe nɛ la, dzika tso fiasrɔ̃ la ƒo ŋutɔ, eye wòɖo awuwo ɖa, be woatsɔ ado na Mardoxai, ne woaɖe akpanya la le eŋu; ke egbe wo xɔxɔ.

english_verse: Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
translation_verse: Tete Ester yɔ Hatax tso fia ƒe aƒe dzikpɔla, siwo wòɖe, be woasubɔe la dome, eye wòdɔe ɖo ɖe Mardoxai gbɔ, be yeanya nusi dzɔ kple nusi ta wòwɔ alea ɖo.

english_verse: Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate,
translation_verse: Eye Hatax yi Mardoxai gbɔ le dua ƒe ablɔ, si le fia ƒe agbo nu la me.

english_verse: and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
translation_verse: Tete Mardoxai gblɔ nusiwo katã dzɔ ɖe eɖzi, kple klosalo, si ŋugbe Haman ɖo be, yeada atsɔ de fia ƒe kesinɔnuwo me ɖe Yudatɔwo ta, ne yeatsrɔ̃ wo la ƒe xexlẽme nɛ.

english_verse: Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
translation_verse: Etsɔ se, si wode le Susa, be woatsrɔ̃ wo la ƒe ŋɔŋlɔ ɖe asi nɛ, ne wòaɖatsɔ afia Ester, eye wòagblɔ wo nɛ; eye wòdɔe, be wòayi fia la gbɔ, ne wòaƒo koko nɛ, eye wòaɖe kuku nɛ ɖe eƒe ɖukɔ la ta. Mardoxai di kpekpeɖeŋu tso Ester gbɔ.

english_verse: Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said.
translation_verse: Eye esi Hatax va gblɔ Mardoxai ƒe nyawo na Ester la,

english_verse: there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
translation_verse: Fia ƒe dɔlawo katã kple fia ƒe anyigbawo dzitɔwo nyae bena, ne ŋutsu alo nyɔnua ɖe yi fia gbɔ le xɔxɔnu emetɔ, eye womeyɔe hafi o la, se ɖeka koe li, be woawui, negbe amesi ke fia la do sikafiatikplo ɖo la, eya koe tsia agbe; ke womeyɔm, be mayi fia la gbɔ o ŋkeke blaetɔ̃ enye si.

english_verse: When Mordecai was told what Esther had said,
translation_verse: Eye woɖagblɔ Ester ƒe nyawo na Mardoxai.

english_verse: he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Tete Mardoxai be, woaɖo ŋu na Ester be: Megasusu be, wòa akpɔ ɖeɖe le fia ƒe me tso Yudatɔwo katã dome o;

english_verse: If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
translation_verse: elabena ne àzi kpi le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, ekema ablɔɖe kple ɖeɖe atso afi bubua ɖe ava na Yudatɔwo, ke mia kple fofowò ƒe aƒe ya miatsrɔ̃ amea ɖe menya nu o, ɖewohĩ ɣeyiɣi sia tae fianyenye la su asiwò ɖo.

english_verse: Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying,
translation_verse: Tete Ester be, woaɖagblɔ na Mardoxai be:

english_verse: “Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
translation_verse: Yi ɖaƒo Yudatɔ, siwo katã le Susa la nu ƒu, eye mitsi nu dɔ le tanye, migaɖu nu o, eye migano nu o zã kple keli ŋkeke etɔ̃ sɔŋ; mía kple nye nyɔnudɔlawo hã míatsi nu adɔ alea, eye manɔ alea ayi fia la gbɔ menye le sekɔ la nu o, eye ne meku la, ɖe meku!

english_verse: Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_verse: Eye Mardoxai yi ɖawɔ pɛpɛpɛ, abe alesi Ester de se nɛ ene.

english_verse: Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke etɔ̃agbe la Ester do fiawu, eye wòyi fiasã ƒe xɔxɔnu emetɔ, si le fia ƒe xɔ ŋgɔ la. Fia la bɔbɔ nɔ eƒe fiazikpui dzi le fiasã me dze ŋgɔ aƒe la ƒe ʋɔtru.

english_verse: He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her. When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter,
translation_verse: Ke esi fia la kpɔ fiasrɔ̃ Ester wòtsi tre ɖe xoxɔnua la, eve enu; eye fia la lé sikafiatikplɔ ɖe asi do ɖe Ester; tete Ester te va heka asi fiatikplɔ la ta me.

english_verse: the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ nɛ bena: Fiasrɔ̃ Ester, nya ka dzɔ ɖe dziwò, eye nuka dim nèle? Nenye fiaɖuƒe la ƒe afã gɔ̃e hã la, woatsɔe ana wò!

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
translation_verse: Ester ɖo ŋu bena: Ne edze fia ŋu la, ekema fia kple Haman neva kplɔ̃, si meɖo nɛ egbe la ŋu.

english_verse: The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.” The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner,
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ be: Miɖayɔ Haman vɛ kaba, be míawɔ Ester ƒe nya la dzi! Eye fia la kple Haman wova kplɔ̃, si Ester ɖo la ŋu.

english_verse: and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Esime wole wein nom la, fia la gblɔ na Ester bena: Nuka dim nèle? Woana wò! Eye nuka biam nèle? Nenye fiaɖuƒe ƒe afã gɔ̃e hã la, woawɔ edzi!

english_verse: Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.” Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
translation_verse: Ne fia la ve nunye, eye ne edze fia la ŋu be, wòana nye nubiabiam, eye wòawɔ nye didi dzi la, ekema, ne fia kple Haman wova kplɔ̃, si magaɖo na wo ŋu la, mawɔ fia ƒe nya la dzi etsɔ. Haman di Mardoxai ƒe ku.

english_verse: Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry,
translation_verse: Tete Haman do go gbemagbe kple dzidzɔ, eye eƒe dzi gbɔ ɖe eme. Ke esi Haman kpɔ Mardoxai le fia ƒe agbo me metsi tre, ne wòahayi eɖokui ʋã ge le eŋku me o la, dzi ku Haman vevie ŋutɔ ɖe Mardoxai nu;

english_verse: but he did not say a thing. When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh
translation_verse: ke Haman zi eɖokui dzi. Esi wòva eƒe me la, edɔ woɖayɔ exɔlɔ̃wo kple srɔ̃a Zeres vɛ.

english_verse: and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him.
translation_verse: Eye Haman xlẽ eƒe kesinɔnu nyuiawo, via gbogboawo kple nusiwo katã fia la tso ɖoe gãe, kpakple alesi wòtsɔe ɖo amegãwo kple fia ƒe dɔlawo dzi la na wo.

english_verse: Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow.
translation_verse: Eye Haman gagblɔ bena: Fiasrɔ̃ Ester hã mekpe amea ɖeke kpe ɖe fia ŋu ɖe kplɔ̃, si wòɖo la ŋu o, negbe nye ko; etsɔ hã egakpem kpe ɖe fia la ŋu.

english_verse: But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
translation_verse: Ke nusiawo katã meɖi ve nam o, ŋkeke alesi megale Yudatɔ Mardoxai kpɔm wobɔbɔ nɔ fia ƒe agbo me.

english_verse: That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king.
translation_verse: Le zã ma me la fia la tsi zãdomadɔlɔ̃e, eye wògblɔ be, woatsɔ ŋkuɖoɖo nyadzɔdzɔwo dzi ƒe agbalẽ vɛ, eye woxlẽe na fia la

english_verse: When the servant read how Mordecai had kept Bigthana and Teresh from killing the king,
translation_verse: Tete wokpɔ woŋlɔ ɖi be Mardoxai ɖe fia ƒe aƒe dzikpɔla eveawo Bigtana kple Zeres, amesiwo tso agbonudzɔlawo dome la gɔme ɖe go be, wodi be, yewoawu fia Axasweros.

english_verse: the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?” “Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
translation_verse: Tete fia la bia bena: Nuka wowɔ tsɔ de bubu Mardoxai ŋui, eye aleke wodoe ɖe dzii le esia ta? Fia ƒe dɔlawo, siwo le esubɔm la, ɖo ŋu bena: Womewɔ naneke nɛ o.

english_verse: About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
translation_verse: Eye fia la gblɔ be Amekae le xɔxɔnua? — Haman ye va fiasã ƒe xɔxɔnu gbãtɔ be, yeagblɔ na fia la be woahe. Mardoxai ɖe ati, si wòtu nɛ la ŋu. —

english_verse: The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.” “Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
translation_verse: Tete fia ƒe dɔlawo gblɔ nɛ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, Haman ye tsi tre ɖe xɔxɔnu la! Eye fia la gblɔ be Neva me

english_verse: When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?” Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor.
translation_verse: Esi Haman ge ɖe eme la, fia, la biae bena: Nuka woawɔ na ŋutsu, si ŋu fia le didim be, yeade bubui? Tete Haman bu le eƒe ta me be Ameka gɔ̃ ŋu fia la ade bubui, ne menye nye ko oa?

english_verse: So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man,
translation_verse: Tete Haman ɖo ŋu na fia la bena: Ne fia la di be, yeade bubu amea ɖe ŋu la,

english_verse: get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress.
translation_verse: ekema woaɖe fiawu, si fia dona kple sɔ, si fia dona, si ƒe ta fiakuku le la, ɖe go;

english_verse: Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
translation_verse: emegbe woatsɔ awua kple sɔ Ia ade asi na bubumeawo, siwo nye fia: ƒe amegãwo dometɔ ɖeka la, ne wòado na ŋutsu, si ŋu fia di be, yeade bubui la, wòana wòado sɔ ato dua ƒe ablɔ me, eye wòanɔ ɣli dom le eŋgɔ be: Ale woawɔ na ŋutsu, si ŋu fia di be yeade bubui enye si!

english_verse: The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ na Haman bena: Netsɔ, natsɔ awua kple sɔ la, eye nawɔ na Yudatɔ Mardoxai, amesi bɔbɔ nɔ fia ƒe agbonu la, abe alesi negblɔ ene; eye megana naneke nato le nya, siwo katã negblɔ la me o!

english_verse: Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
translation_verse: Eye Haman tso awu kple sɔ la, edo awua na Mardoxai, eye wòna wòdo sɔ la to dua ƒe ablɔ me, eye wòle ɣli dom le eŋgɔ be: Ale woawɔ na ŋutsu, si ŋu fia di be, yeade bubui la enye si!

english_verse: Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame.
translation_verse: Azɔ Mardoxai trɔ va fia ƒe agbo me; ke Haman ɖe abla yi eƒe me, eye wòle nu xam hetsɔ nu tsyɔ ta.

english_verse: Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.”
translation_verse: Eye Haman xlẽ nusiwo katã dzɔ ɖe edzi la, fia srɔ̃a Zeres kple exɔlɔ̃awo katã. Tete eƒe nunyalawo kple srɔ̃a Zeres wogblɔ nɛ bena. Nenye Yudatɔwo ƒe dzidzimeviwo dome Mardoxai, amesi ŋku me nede asi toyiyi me le tso la, ekema màte ŋu awɔ nanekee o, ke boŋ to kokoko nayi agayi le eŋku me!

english_verse: They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_verse: Esime wogale nu ƒom kplii la, fia ƒe aƒe dzikpɔlawo va kplɔ Haman enumake yi kplɔ̃, si Ester ɖo la ŋu.

english_verse: The king and Haman were dining with Esther
translation_verse: Tete fia la kple Haman wova kplɔ̃ ŋu le fiasrɔ̃ Ester gbɔ.

english_verse: and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
translation_verse: Eye esi wole wein nom la, fia la gabia Ester le ŋkeke evelia dzi be: Fiasrɔ̃ Ester, nuka biam nèle? Woana wò Eye nuka dim nèle? Nenye fiaɖuƒe ƒe afã gɔ̃e hã la, woawɔ edzi na wo!

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want,
translation_verse: Fiasrɔ̃ Ester ɖo ŋu gblɔ bena: Fia, ne eve nunye, eye ne edze fia ŋu la, ekema woatsɔ nye agbe kem le nye biabia nu, eye woatsɔ nye dukɔ nam le nye didi nu!

english_verse: because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
translation_verse: Elabena wotsɔ mía kple nye dukɔ dzra, be woatsrɔ̃ mí, woawu mí, eye woagblẽ mía dome. Ɖe wònye ɖe wotsɔ mí dzra míenye kluviwo kple kosiviwo la, anye ne mezi kpi, elabena anye ne ketɔ la mana gbegblẽ nava fia dzi o.

english_verse: Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!” Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
translation_verse: Ester ɖo ŋu bena: Ketɔ kple futɔ lae nye Haman vɔ̃ɖi sia! Tete Haman ɖi vo le fia kple fiasrɔ̃ ŋku me.

english_verse: The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden. Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
translation_verse: Ke fia la tsɔ dziku tsi tre le wein la gbɔ heyi fiasã ƒe abɔ me; eye Haman tsi afima, be yeabia eƒe agbe tso fiasrɔ̃ Ester si, elabena ekpɔ be, fia la ɖo dzɔgbevɔ̃e ɖe ye ŋu kplikpaa.

english_verse: Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!” As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head.
translation_verse: Eye esi fia la trɔ tso fiasã ƒe abɔ me va xɔ, si me wono, wein le me la, kpɔ ɖa, Haman tsra ɖe kuntrunu, si dzi Ester nɔ anyi ɖo la dzi, fia la gblɔ be: Fiasrɔ̃ hãe wòbe, yealé sesẽ le aƒe me le gbɔnyea? Esi nya sia nya do le fia nu ko la, wotsyɔ nu mo na Haman xoxo.

english_verse: At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_verse: Eye wohe Haman ɖe ati, si wotu ɖe Mardoxai ŋu la ŋuti Azɔ fia ƒe dziku la nu fa.

english_verse: Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials
translation_verse: Gbemagbe fia Axasweros tso Yudatɔwo ƒe ketɔ Haman ƒe aƒe na fiasrɔ̃ Ester. Eye Mardoxai va fia la ŋku me, elabena Ester gblɔ amesi wònye la nɛ.

english_verse: and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
translation_verse: Eye fia la ɖe eƒe ŋkɔsigɛ, si wòxɔ le Haman si la, na Mardoxai. Eye Ester tsɔ Mardoxai ɖo Haman ƒe aƒe nu.

english_verse: Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!”
translation_verse: Ester gaƒo nu le fia la ŋku me, ede ta agu ɖe eƒe afɔ nu, eye wòfa avi heƒo koko nɛ be, wòagblẽ Agagitɔ Haman ƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃e kple eƒe ta me, si wòɖo ɖe Yudatɔwo ŋu la me.

english_verse: and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed,
translation_verse: gblɔ bena: Ne edze fia la ŋu, eye wòve nunye, ne nya sia nyo fia ŋu, eye nye nu nyo fia ŋu la, ekema nena woaŋlɔ agbalẽ, ne woagblẽ agbalẽ, si Hamedata vi Haman, Agagitɔ, ŋlɔ heɖo ta me be, yeatsrɔ̃ Yudatɔwo le fia ƒe anyigbawo katã dzi la me.

english_verse: King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews.
translation_verse: Tete fia Axasweros gblɔ na fiasrɔ̃ Ester kple Yudatɔ Mardoxai bena: Kpɔ ɖa, metsɔ Haman ƒe aƒe na Ester, eye wohe eya ŋutɔ ɖe ati ŋu, le esi wòɖo eƒe asi dzi ɖe Yudatɔwo ŋu la ta.

english_verse: I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
translation_verse: Ke miawo miŋlɔ agbalẽ ɖo ɖe Yudatɔwo le fia ƒe ŋkɔ me, alesi dze mia ŋu, eye mitsɔ fia ƒe ŋkɔsigɛ ɖo ŋkɔ ete; elabena agbalẽ, si woŋlɔ le fia ƒe ŋkɔ me, eye wotsɔ fia ƒe ŋkɔsigɛ ɖo ŋkɔ ete la, womate ŋu atrɔe o.

english_verse: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
translation_verse: Woŋlɔ agbalẽ la le fia Axasweros ƒe ŋkɔ me, eye wotsɔ fia ƒe ŋkɔsigɛ ɖo ŋkɔ ete, eye wòde agbalẽawo duxɔlawo, siwo nye sɔɖolawo, eye wodo fia ƒe sɔ ɖiduwo la, si ɖo ɖa

english_verse: Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth. After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered,
translation_verse: Eye Mardoxai le fiawu, si nye aɖabɛ blɔtɔ kple aklala me, eɖo sikafiakuku gãa ɖe, eye wòle awu ʋlaya, si nye aklala kple aɖabɛ dzĩto me hedo le fia la gbɔ; eye Susa-du la tso aseye hekpɔ dzidzɔ.

english_verse: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_verse: Yudatɔwo kpɔ dzidzɔ, wotso aseye, wotu aglo, eye woɖu ŋkekenyuie le anyigbawo katã dzi kple du, siwo katã, me, fia ƒe nya kple eƒe se la de; eye anyigba dzi dukɔwo dometɔ geɖewo trɔ zu Yudatɔwo, elabena Yudatɔwo ƒe ŋɔdzi lé wo.

english_verse: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,
translation_verse: Le dzinu wuievelia, si nye dzinu Adar la ƒe ŋkeke wutetɔ̃lia, si dzi woawɔ fia ƒe nya kple eƒe sea dzi la dzi, gbesigbe Yudatɔwo ƒe futɔwo le mɔ kpɔm be, yewoakpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe wo dzi la, nya la trɔ be, Yudatɔwo kpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe woƒe ketɔwo dzi.

english_verse: and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
translation_verse: Tete Yudatɔwo ƒo wo dokui nu ƒu ɖe woƒe duwo me le fia Axasweros ƒe anyigbawo katã dzi, be yewoawu amesiwo katã di yewoƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃e la. Amea ɖeke menɔ te ɖe wo nu o, elabena woƒe ŋɔdzi lé dukɔwo katã.

english_verse: The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews.
translation_verse: Anyigbawo ƒe tatɔwo katã, amegãwo kple anyigba dzikpɔlawo kpakple fia ƒe dziɖulawo xɔ na Yudatɔwo, elabena Mardoxai ƒe ŋɔdzi le wo

english_verse: Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
translation_verse: Elabena Mardoxai zu gã le na ƒe me, eye eƒe ŋkɔ de anyigbawo katã dzi; elabena ŋutsu Mardoxai le gã zum ɖe dzi ɖaa.

english_verse: The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy.
translation_verse: Eye Yudatɔwo tsɔ yi dza woƒe futɔwo katã, wowu wo, eye wotsrɔ̃ wo, eye wowɔ woƒe ketɔwo alesi dze wo ŋu.

english_verse: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
translation_verse: Gbemagbe wohe amesiwo wowu la ƒe xexlẽme va fia la ŋku me le Susa-mɔ̃ me,

english_verse: Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ na fiasrɔ̃ Ester bena, Ne Yudatɔwo wu ŋutsu alafa atɔ̃ le Susa-mɔ̃ me, eye wotsrɔ̃ wo hekpe ɖe Haman vi ewoawo ŋu la, aleke womahawɔ le fia ƒe anyigba mamleawo dzi oa? Azɔ nuka biam nele? Woana wò. Eye nuka dim nègale? Woawɔ edzi.

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
translation_verse: Ester ɖo ŋu bena: Ne edze fia ŋu la, ekema woaɖe mɔ na Yudatɔ, siwo le Susa etsɔ hã, ne woawɔ ɖe egbe ƒe se la nu, eye woahe Haman vi ewoawo ɖe ati ŋu.

english_verse: King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa.
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ be, woawɔ nenema. Wode se le Susa, eye wohe Haman vi ewoawo ɖe ati ŋu

english_verse: Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed
translation_verse: Eye Yudatɔ, siwo le Susa la, ƒo wo ɖokui nu ƒu le dzinu Adar ƒe ŋkeke wuienelia hã dzi, eye wowu ŋutsu alafa etɔ̃ le Susa; ke womede asi aboyonuawo ŋu o.

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed
translation_verse: Esia va me le dzinu Adar ƒe ŋkeke wuietɔ̃lia dzi, eye wogbɔ ɖe eme le eƒe ŋkeke wuienelia; si wotsɔ wo aglotugbe kple dzidzɔkpɔgbe la dzi.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
translation_verse: Ke Yudatɔ, siwo le Susa la, ƒo wo ɖokui nu ƒu le ŋkeke wuietɔ̃lia kple wuienelia dzi, eye wogbɔ ɖe eme le ŋkeke wuiatɔ̃lia, si wotso wo aglotugbe kple dzidzɔkpɔgbe la dzi.

english_verse: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Eyata Yudatɔ, siwo le kɔƒewo kple du nuvowo me la, tso dzinu Adar ƒe ŋkeke wuienelia wo dzidzɔkpɔgbe, aglotugbe kple ŋkekenyuie, si dzi woɖoa nuɖuɖu ɖe wo nɔewo le. Yudatɔwo ɖo ŋkekenyuie ɖe anyi hena ŋkuɖoɖo woƒe ɖeɖe dzi.

english_verse: Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces
translation_verse: Mardoxai ŋlɔ nya siawo ɖi, eye wòɖo agbalẽ ɖe Yudatɔ, siwo katã le kpuiƒe kple didiƒe le fia Axasweros ƒe anyigbawo katã dzi la

english_verse: and told them: Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,
translation_verse: hele ɖoɖom na wo be, woaɖu dzinu Adar ƒe ŋkeke wuienelia kple wuiatɔ̃lia ɖaa ƒe sia ƒe,

english_verse: the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
translation_verse: abe ŋkeke, siwo dzi Yudatɔwo kpɔ gbɔdzɔe tso woƒe futɔwo si me, kple dzinu, si dzi woƒe vevewo trɔ zu dzidzɔ, eye nuxaxa trɔ zu ŋkekenyuie ene; ne woatsɔ wo awɔ aglotugbe kple dzidzɔkpɔgbewoe, esiwo dzi woaɖo nuɖuɖu ɖe wo nɔewo, eye woana nu ame dahewo le.

english_verse: They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration. The Reason for the Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Eye Yudatɔwo tsɔ nusi wɔwɔ gɔme wodze kple nusi Mardoxai ŋlɔ na wo la, wo kɔnui.

english_verse: Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
translation_verse: Elabena Hamedata vi Haman, Agagitɔ la, si nye Yudatɔwo katã ƒe ketɔ ɖo ɖe ta me be, yeatsrɔ̃ wo, eye wòda pur, si nye nudzidzenu la, ne yeade ʋunyaʋunya wo me, eye yeatsrɔ̃ wo.

english_verse: Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged.
translation_verse: Ke esi Ester va fia la ŋku me la, ede se woŋlɔ agbalẽ, be eƒe tame vɔ̃, si wòɖo de Yudatɔwo ŋu la, natrɔ va eya ŋutɔ ƒe ta dzi, eye wohe eya kple viawo de ati ŋu.

english_verse: Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast.
translation_verse: Eyata wona ŋkɔ ŋkeke siawo be Purim le pur ƒe ŋkɔ nu. Le agbalẽ sia me nyawo katã kple nusi teƒe wokpɔ, kpakple nusi dzɔ ɖe wo dzi la nu,

english_verse: Now every year the Jews set aside these two days for having parties and celebrating, just as they were told to do.
translation_verse: Yudatɔwo ɖoe, eye wotsɔe wɔ kɔnu na woawo ŋutɔ kple woƒe dzidzimeviwo kpakple amesiwo katã aku ɖe wo ŋu la be, woaɖu ŋkeke eve siawo le agbalẽ, si woŋlɔ na wo, kple ŋkeke ɖoɖo la nu, eye womada edzi o;

english_verse: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast.
translation_verse: Eye fiasrɔ̃ Ester, Abixayil ƒe nyɔnuvi, kple Yudatɔ Mardoxai woŋlɔ agbalẽ zi evelia le Purim ŋuti heté gbe ɖe dzi be, woaɖo kpe eɖzi wòanye kɔnu.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
translation_verse: be woaɖo kpe Purim-ŋkekeawo dzi ɖe woƒe ɣeyiɣi dzi, abe alesi Yudatɔ Mardoxai kple fiasrɔ̃ Ester woɖo na wo, kpakple alesi woawo ŋutɔ woɖo nutsitsiɖɔ kple konyifafa na woawo kple woƒe dzidzimeviwo ene.

english_verse: These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_verse: Ester ƒe se la ɖo kpe Purim ƒe ɖoɖowo dzi, eye woŋlɔe ɖe agbalẽ me.

english_verse: King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea.
translation_verse: Fia Axasweros ɖo nuɖzɔɖzɔ na anyigba la kple atsiaƒu me ƒukpowo.

english_verse: All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai.
translation_verse: Eƒe nu gã wɔwɔwo kple nu klitsu wɔwɔwo katã kpakple Mardoxai ƒe ŋkɔxɔxɔ, alesi fia la ɖo gãe la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Media kple Persia-fiawo ŋɔli ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_verse: Elabena Yudatɔ Mardoxai enye evelia kplɔ fia Axasweros ɖo, exɔ ŋkɔ le Yudatɔwo dome, eye nɔvia gbogboawo lɔ̃ eƒe nya; edi nyui na eƒe dukɔ, eye wòƒo nu na edeviwo katã ƒe nyonyo.

english_verse: Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
translation_verse: Ŋutsua ɖe nɔ Uz-nyigba dzi, si ŋkɔ nye Hiob. Ŋutsu sia nye ame maɖifɔ, ame dzɔdzɔe kple mawuvɔ̃la, eye wòtsri nu vɔ̃ɖi.

english_verse: the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa bia Satana be: Afika nètso? Satana ɖo ŋu na Yehowa gblɔ bena: Metso tsatsa ge le anyigba dzi kple tsa ɖi ge le edzi.

english_verse: Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Eye viaŋutsuwo tua aglo ɖe woƒe aƒewo me, wo dome ɖesiaɖe le ŋkeke, si dze edzi la dzi, eye wodɔa ame da woɖakpea wo nɔvinyɔnu etɔ̃awo, be woaɖu nu, eye woana nu kple yewo.

english_verse: After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God. Angels, the Lord, and Satan
translation_verse: Eye ne aglotuɣiawo trɔ va kpe la, Hiob dɔa ame da woɖakɔa wo ŋu. Efɔna ŋdi kanya, eye wòsa numevɔ ɖe wo katã ƒe xexlẽme nu; elabena Hiob gblɔ be: Misela vinyewo wɔ nuvɔ̃, eye wofe Mawu ɖe aga le woƒe dziwo me hĩ. Alea Hiob wona ɣesiaɣi. Hiob ge ɖe do tokpɔ sesẽa ɖe me.

english_verse: One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Eye wòva me gbe ɖeka be, esi mawuviwo va tsi tre ɖe Yehowa ŋku me la, Satana hã le wo dome va.

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
translation_verse: Yehowa gblɔ na Satana be: Elé ŋku ɖe nye dɔla Hiob ŋua? Elabena enye ame maɖifɔ, ame dzɔdzɔe kple mawuvɔ̃la, eye wòtsri nu vɔ̃ɖi, eye amea ɖeke mede enu le anyigba dzi ti.

english_verse: “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked.
translation_verse: Tete Satana ɖo ŋu na Yehowa gblɔ bena: Dzodzroe Hiob vɔ̃a Mawua?

english_verse: “You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere.
translation_verse: Ɖe menye wòe tɔ kpɔ ɖe eya ŋutɔ kple eƒe nuwo katã ŋu godoo oa? Eyra eƒe aƒe kpakple eƒe asinudɔwɔwɔwo, eye eƒe lãhawo gbagba ɖe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Ke do asi da, ne nade asi nusiwo katã le esi la ŋu kpɔ, be magbe wò nya ɖe ŋkuwo me keŋ oa?

english_verse: The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.” Then Satan left. Job Loses Everything
translation_verse: Yehowa gblɔ na Satana be: Kpɔ ɖa, eƒe nuwo katã le asiwò me, ɖeko megade asi eya ŋutɔ ŋu o. Tete Satana dzo le Yehowa ŋku me.

english_verse: Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son,
translation_verse: Eye wòva me gbe ɖeka be, esi viaŋutsuwo kple vianyɔnuwo le nu ɖum, eye wole wein nom le wo nɔvi xoxoetɔ ƒe me la,

english_verse: when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass,
translation_verse: tete ame dɔdɔa de va Hiob gbɔ gblɔ bena: Nyiawo le agble ŋlɔm, eye ledzinɔawo le gbe ɖum le wo xa,

english_verse: a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: kasia Sabatɔwo va dze wo dzi, wole wo, eye wowu dɔlaawo kple yi, eye nye ɖeka koe kpɔtɔ, be mava gblɔe na wò.

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Esi amesia gale nuƒoƒo dzi la, ame bubu va gblɔ bena: Mawu ƒe dzo ge tso dziƒo dze alẽawo kple dɔlaawo dzi hefiã wo, eye nye ɖeka koe kpɔtɔ, be meva gblɔe na wò.

english_verse: Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Esi mekpɔ ɖe nu le eme o le ame bubu va gblɔ bena: Kalɖeatɔwo dze aʋalɔgo etɔ̃ va dze kposɔawo dzi, wole wo, eye wowu ɖɔlaawo kple yi, eye nye ɖeka koe kpɔtɔ, be mava gblɔe na wò.

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son,
translation_verse: Esi amesia gale nuƒoƒo dzi le ame bubu va gblɔ bena: Esi viwòŋutsuwo kple viwònyɔnuwo le nu ɖum, eye wole wein nom le wo nɔvi xoxoetɔ ƒe me la,

english_verse: when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: kpɔ ɖa, ya ʋuɖua ɖe tso gbe dzi va lɔ xɔ la ƒe dzogoe eneawo ɖe eme wòmũ dze ɖekakpuiawo dzi woku, eye nye ɖeka koe kpɔtɔ, be meva gblɔe na wò.

english_verse: When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God
translation_verse: Tete Hiob tso hedze eƒe awu, elũ eƒe ta, eye wòde ta agu hedo gbe ɖa

english_verse: and said: “We bring nothing at birth; we take nothing with us at death. The Lord alone gives and takes. Praise the name of the Lord!”
translation_verse: gblɔ bena: Amama mele tso ɖanye ƒe ɖɔ me, eye ama ma manɔ agayi Yehowae na, Yehowae gaxɔe, woakafu Yehowa ŋkɔ!

english_verse: In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_verse: Le nusiawo katã me la Hiob mewɔ nuvɔ̃ o, eye mebu vɔ̃a ɖeke ɖe Mawu ŋu o.

english_verse: and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa bia Satana bena: A ika nètso? Satana ɖo ŋu na Yehowa gblɔ bena: Metso tsatsa ge le anyigba dzi kple tsa ɖi ge le edzi.

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
translation_verse: Yehowa gblɔ na Satana be: Ele ŋku ɖe nye dɔla Hiob ŋua? Elabena enye ame maɖifɔ, ame dzɔdzɔe kple mawuvɔ̃la, eye wòtsri nu vɔ̃ɖi, ye amea ɖeke mede enu le anyigba dzi o. Egale eƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye me ɖe asi ko, ke woa ède adã ta me nam, be magblẽ edome naneke mawɔmawɔe.

english_verse: Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive.
translation_verse: Tete Satana ɖo ŋu na Yehowa gblɔ bena: Ŋutigbalẽ ɖe ŋutigbalẽe teƒe, eye amegbetɔ atsɔ nusiwo katã te esi la, ana be eƒe agbe ta.

english_verse: Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Ke ɖo wò abɔ ɖa, ne nade asi eƒe ʋu kple eƒe ŋutilã ŋu kpoa, be magbe wo nya me ŋkuwo me keŋ ene oa?

english_verse: “All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.”
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa gblɔ na Satana bena: Kpa ɖa, ele asiwò me, ɖeko kpɔ eƒe agbe ta!

english_verse: Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
translation_verse: Tete Satana dzo le Yehowa ŋku me hekplɔ ƒoƒoe vɔ̃ɖi ƒu Hiob tso eƒe afɔƒome vaseɖe eƒe dzodome.

english_verse: his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
translation_verse: Tete srɔ̃a gblɔ nɛ bena: Egale wo blibonyenye me ɖe asi koa? Gbe Mawu, ne naku!

english_verse: Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God. Job's Three Friends
translation_verse: Ke eya ɖo ŋu nɛ bena: Eƒo nu, abe alesi nyɔnu abunetɔwo ƒoa nui ene. Miexɔ nu nyuiwo tso Mawu si, ɖe miaxɔ vɔ̃ hã oa? Le nusiawo katã me la Hiob mewɔ nuvɔ̃ kple eƒe nuyiwo o.

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him.
translation_verse: Esi Hiob ƒe xɔlɔ̃ etɔ̃awo se dzɔgbevɔe, siwo katã dzɔ ɖe edzi la, wo dome amesiame tso wo de: Elifaz tso Teman, Bildad tso Suax, eye Zofar tso Naama; woɖo gbe ɖi kple wo nɔewo be, yewoayi aɖafa nɛ, eye yewoafa akɔ nɛ.

english_verse: When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Ke esi wota mo te le adzɔge la, womedze sii o: tete wofa avi kple ɣli, wo dome amesiame dze eƒe awu, eye wohlẽ ke ɖe ya me wòʋuʋu ɖe woƒe ta me.

english_verse: For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_verse: Eye wobɔbɔ nɔ anyi ɖe anyigba ɖe egbɔ ŋkeke adre kple zã adre; ke wo dometɔa ɖeke meƒo nu kplii o, elabena wokpɔ be, veve la nu sẽ ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Finally, Job cursed the day of his birth
translation_verse: Emegbe Hiob ke nu heƒo fi de eƒe dzigbe.

english_verse: by saying to God:
translation_verse: Eye Hiob xɔ edzi gblɔ bena:

english_verse: Blot out the day of my birth and the night when my parents created a son.
translation_verse: Gbesigbe wodzim kple zã, si gblɔ be, wodzi ŋutsuvi la, nebu!

english_verse: Forget about that day, cover it with darkness,
translation_verse: Ŋkeke ma nedo viviti, Mawu megabia eta tso dziƒo o, eye keklẽ megaklẽ ɖe edzi o!

english_verse: and send thick, gloomy shadows to fill it with dread.
translation_verse: Viviti kple blukɔ negbugbɔe yii, alilikpo dodo netsyɔe edzi, eye zãdokeli neɖo dzikatsoƒoe nɛ!

english_verse: Erase that night from the calendar and conceal it with darkness.
translation_verse: Viviti nekplɔ zã ma yii, dzi megadzɔe le ƒe me ŋkekewo dome o, eye megana dzinuwo ƒe xexlẽ me o!

english_verse: Don't let children be created or joyful shouts be heard ever again in that night.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, zã ma neɖi ƒuƒlu, eye aseye megaɖi le eme o!

english_verse: Let those with magic powers place a curse on that day.
translation_verse: Amesiwo ɖoa golo ŋkeke, eye wotea ŋu ɖee adã ta me na ʋɔ driba la, nedo ɖiŋu nɛ!

english_verse: Darken its morning stars and remove all hope of light,
translation_verse: Eƒe ŋukeɣleti neɖo viviti; nelala keklẽ, ke ɖeke megado o, eye megakpɔ agudzedze ƒe aɖaba o!

english_verse: because it let me be born into a world of trouble. Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
translation_verse: Elabena mexa danye ƒe vidzidɔ nu o, eye meɣla fuwɔame ɖe nye ŋkuwo o.

english_verse: Why was I accepted and allowed to nurse at my mother's breast?
translation_verse: Nukata wotsɔm do akɔ eye nukata meno no ɖo?

english_verse: Now I would be at peace in the silent world below
translation_verse: Anye ne memlɔ anyi, eye megbɔ de eme, anye ne medɔ alɔ̃, eye medzudzɔ

english_verse: with kings and their advisors whose palaces lie in ruins,
translation_verse: kple anyigba dzi fiawo kple adaŋumegãwo, amesiwo tu; ameɖiƒewo na wo ɖokui,

english_verse: and with rulers once rich with silver and gold.
translation_verse: alo kple amegã, siwo si sika bɔ ɖo, amesiwo ƒe yɔdo yɔ kple klosalo

english_verse: I wish I had been born dead and then buried, never to see the light of day.
translation_verse: Ɖe mele ahe la gege, si woɖe do ene la, anye ne nyemegali o; eye anye, ne mele abe vidzie, siwo mekpɔ kekeli kpɔ o la ene.

english_verse: In the world of the dead, the wicked and the weary rest without a worry. *
translation_verse: Afima ame nyanyrãwo dzudzɔ agbodzedze le, afima eme gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔwo gbɔ ɖe eme le.

english_verse: where captives and slaves are free at last. Why Does God Let Me Live?
translation_verse: Ɖeviwo kple tsitsiawo siaa sɔ le afima, eye kluvi vo tso eƒe aƒetɔ si me.

english_verse: Why does God let me live when life is miserable and so bitter?
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti wòna kekeli ayaɖulawo? Eye wòtsɔ agbe na nuxalawo?

english_verse: I keep longing for death more than I would seek a valuable treasure.
translation_verse: Amesiwo le ku dzɔm, ke meva o, eye wole ŋu tsom nɛ wu kesinɔnuwo;

english_verse: Nothing could make me happier than to be in the grave.
translation_verse: amesiwo akpɔ dzidzɔ atso aseye, ati kpo, nenyo be, woakpɔ yɔɖo:

english_verse: Why do I go on living when God has me surrounded, and I can't see the road?
translation_verse: ŋutsu, si ƒe mɔ bu ɖee, amesi ŋgɔ Mawu tɔ kpɔ ɖo.

english_verse: Moaning and groaning are my food and drink,
translation_verse: Elabena nye tseɖuɖu xɔ ɖe nuɖuɖu teƒe nam, eye nye hũɖeɖe le dodom abe tsi ene.

english_verse: I have no peace or rest— only troubles and worries.
translation_verse: Nyemekpɔ; ŋutilafa, dzudzɔ kple gbɔɖemea ɖeke o tso, hafi veveawo le ga: dom ɖe dzi.

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman said:
translation_verse: Tete Temanitɔ Elifaz xɔ edzi gblɔ bena:

english_verse: Please be patient and listen to what I have to say. *
translation_verse: Ne wodo nya ɖe gbɔwò la, ɖe woaɖu dzi na woa? Ke ameka ale ŋu ami nye ɖe dɔ me?

english_verse: have guided and encouraged many in need.
translation_verse: Wo nya fɔ ame kudɔewo ɖe te, eye nèdo ŋusẽ klo benɔwo.

english_verse: You respect God and live right, so don't lose hope!
translation_verse: Ɖe menye wò mawuvɔvɔ̃ enye wò dziɖeƒo oa? Eye wò zɔzɔ meɖitɔ la enye wò mɔkpɔkpɔ oa?

english_verse: No truly innocent person has ever died young.
translation_verse: Bu eme kpɔ! Ameka dome gblẽ fɔmaɖimaɖii kpɔa? Eye afika wotsrɔ̃ ame dzɔdzɔewo le kpɔa?

english_verse: In my experience, only those who plant seeds of evil harvest trouble,
translation_verse: Le nye nukpɔkpɔ nu la amesiwo ŋlɔa dzɔgbevɔ̃e hetsɔa agbagbadzedze ƒãna la, woawoe xanɛ ha.

english_verse: and then they are swept away by the angry breath of God.
translation_verse: Mawu ƒe ƒuƒu gblẽ wo dome, eye eƒe dɔmedzoe gbɔgbɔ na wo nu yi.

english_verse: They may roar and growl like powerful lions. But when God breaks their teeth,
translation_verse: Dzata le xɔxlɔ̃m, dzata le gbe ɖem, ke woŋe aɖu na dzataviwo.

english_verse: they starve, and their children are scattered. A Secret Was Told to Me
translation_verse: Dzata tsrɔ̃, le esi nuléle meli o la, eye dzatãnɔ ƒe viwo ka hlẽ.

english_verse: A secret was told to me in a faint whisper—
translation_verse: Gbea ɖe ɖi va gbɔnye dzaa, eye nye to se dalidodo

english_verse: I was overcome by sleep, but disturbed by dreams;
translation_verse: le zã me ŋutega ƒe tameyiyi me, esime amewo yi alɔ̃ me ʋĩ.

english_verse: and my hair stood on end, as a wind blew past my face.
translation_verse: Yea ɖe ƒo va to ŋunye, ɖadoe ɖo to ɖe ŋunye.

english_verse: It stopped and stood still. Then a form appeared— a shapeless form. And from the silence, I heard a voice say,
translation_verse: Nɔnɔmea ɖe tsi tre ɖe ŋkunye me, ke nyemedze sii o, eye mese gbe bɔlɔea ɖe be:

english_verse: “No humans are innocent in the eyes of God their Creator.
translation_verse: De ame kodzogbea nye dzɔdzɔetɔ le Mawu ŋku mea? Alo ɖe ŋutsua ɖe dza le ewɔla ŋku mea?

english_verse: He finds fault with his servants and even with his angels.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, meɖoa dzi ɖe eƒe subɔlawo ŋu o, eye wòbua tatra ɖe eƒe dɔlawo ke hã ŋu

english_verse: Humans are formed from clay and are fragile as moths, so what chance do you have?
translation_verse: ʋuu kekeke wòahayi anyixɔ me nɔlawo nye ge, amesiwo dzɔ tso anyi me, eye wolilia afɔ wo dzi abe agbagblaʋuiwo ene.

english_verse: Born after daybreak, you die before nightfall and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Woatugu wo tso ŋdi vaseɖe fiẽ, eye woabu nigbi, amea ɖeke madze sii o.

english_verse: Your tent pegs are pulled up, and you leave this life, having gained no wisdom.”
translation_verse: Ɖe mele eme oa? Ne wotso woƒe agbadɔka le wo ŋu la, ekema wokuna le numanyamanya me.

english_verse: Job, call out for help and see if an angel comes!
translation_verse: Yɔ ame kpɔ, ɖe amea ɖe atɔ na wò hã? Eye kɔkɔetɔawo dometɔ ka ŋu nèbe, yeatrɔ ɖo?

english_verse: Envy and jealousy will kill a stupid fool.
translation_verse: Ke boŋ dziku wua bometsila, eye abunetɔ kuna ɖe ŋuʋaʋã me.

english_verse: I have seen fools take root. But God sends a curse, suddenly uprooting them
translation_verse: Mekpɔ bometsilaa ɖe do ke; tete wònyunyɔ ɖe enɔƒe enumake.

english_verse: Then hungry and greedy people gobble up their crops and grab their wealth.
translation_verse: Dɔwuitɔwo mi eƒe agblemenuwo, eye woɖahe wo tso keke ŋuvegoewo me ke, eye tsikɔwuitɔwo ɖa tsyo ɖe eƒe kesinɔnuwo ŋu.

english_verse: Our suffering isn't caused by the failure of crops;
translation_verse: Elabena dzɔgbevɔ̃e medona tsoa ke me o, eye hiãtuame metsoa anyigbatu me o,

english_verse: it's all part of life, like sparks shooting skyward.
translation_verse: ke boŋ wodzi amegbetɔ ɖe hiãtuame ŋu, abe alesi dzoxi dzena yia dzii ene.

english_verse: Job, if I were you, I would ask God for help.
translation_verse: Nyee wònyea, anye ne matrɔ ɖe Mawu ŋu, eye matsɔ nye nya ade asi na Mawu,

english_verse: His miracles are marvelous, more than we can count.
translation_verse: amesi wɔa nu gã, siwo me dzodzro meli o, kple nukunu, siwo mele xexlẽ me o,

english_verse: God sends showers on earth and waters the fields.
translation_verse: amesi naa tsidzadza anyigba, eye woɖoa tsi ɖe lãnyiƒewo.

english_verse: He protects the sorrowful and lifts up those who have been disgraced. *
translation_verse: Edoa ame bɔbɔɖokuiwo de dzi, eye wòkplɔa dzɔgbenyuie ƒua nuxalawo.

english_verse: in their own evil schemes, and their wisdom fails.
translation_verse: Eléa nunyalawo le woƒe ayenuwɔwɔ me, eye wònana ayedzelawo tsi klokloklo le woƒe adaŋudede me.

english_verse: Darkness is their only companion, hiding their path at noon.
translation_verse: Viviti kpea wo le ŋkeke me, eye wonoa asi tsam le ŋdɔkutsu abe zã me ene.

english_verse: God rescues the needy from the words of the wicked and the fist of the mighty.
translation_verse: Ke eɖea ame dahe tsoa yi nu, tsoa woƒe nu me, eye tsoa ŋusẽtɔ si me.

english_verse: The poor are filled with hope, and injustice is silenced. Consider Yourself Fortunate
translation_verse: Mɔkpɔkpɔ li na hiãtɔ, eye nu vlo wɔwɔ amia nu.

english_verse: Consider yourself fortunate if God All-Powerful chooses to correct you.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, woayra amegbetɔ, si Mawu hea to na, eyata megado vlo ŋusẽkatãtɔ ƒe tohename o.

english_verse: He may cause injury and pain, but he will bandage and heal your cuts and bruises.
translation_verse: Elabena edea abi eme ŋu, eye wògablanɛ, eƒoa ame, eye eƒe asi daa gbe le eŋu.

english_verse: God will protect you from harm, no matter how often trouble may strike.
translation_verse: Aɖe wò le fukpekpe ade me, eye le adadrelia me la vɔ̃a ɖeke maka esi ŋuwò o.

english_verse: In times of war and famine, God will keep you safe.
translation_verse: Le dɔŋɔli la aɖe wò tso ku me, eye le, aʋa me la aɖe wòtso yi nu.

english_verse: You will be sheltered, without fear of hurtful words or any other weapon.
translation_verse: Aɣla de adeɖiƒoame, eye ne gbegblẽ va la, mãvɔ o.

english_verse: You will laugh at the threat of destruction and famine. And you won't be afraid of wild animals—
translation_verse: Àko gbegblẽ kple dɔwuame, eye mavɔ̃ anyigba dzi gbemelãwo o.

english_verse: they will no longer be fierce, and your rocky fields will become friendly.
translation_verse: Elabena mia kple agble me kpewo miabla nu, eye gbemelãwo adze xɔlɔ̃ kpli wò.

english_verse: Your home will be secure, and your sheep will be safe.
translation_verse: Ekema adze sii be, wò agbadɔ ŋu fa, eye ne èɖe ŋku de nɔwòƒe la, naneke mahiã wò o.

english_verse: You will have more descendants than there are blades of grass on the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Adze sii be, viwòwo sɔ gbɔ, eye wò dzidzimeviwo le abe gbe le anyigbã dzi ene.

english_verse: You will live a very long life, and your body will be strong until the day you die.
translation_verse: Atsi aƒu ga, hafi ayi yɔ me, abe alesi wotsɔa lu bablawo va aƒee le woƒe ɣeyiɣi dzi ene.

english_verse: Our experience has proven these things to be true, so listen and learn.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, nusia me míedzro, eye ele eme alea; see eye nadzrae ɖo!

english_verse: It's impossible to weigh my misery and grief!
translation_verse: Ne woaxada nye dziku, eye woatsɔ nye fukpekpe ade nudanu me kpakplii ɖe!

english_verse: They outweigh the sand along the beach, and that's why I have spoken without thinking first.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la ele kpekpem wu ƒutake, eyata nye nyawo le mɔ tram ɖo.

english_verse: The fearsome arrows of God All-Powerful have filled my soul with their poison.
translation_verse: Elabena ŋusẽkatãtɔ ƒe aŋutrɔ le nye lã me, eye nye gbɔgbɔ no eƒe aɖi; eye Mawu ƒe ŋɔdzidodowo kpe aʋa kplim.

english_verse: Do oxen and wild donkeys cry out in distress unless they are hungry?
translation_verse: Ɖe gbetedzi xlɔ̃na le gbe mumu gbɔa? Alo de nyitsu ɖea gbe le eƒe nuɖuɖu gbɔa?

english_verse: What is food without salt? What is more tasteless than the white of an egg?
translation_verse: Ɖe nu vɔvɔ nya ɖuna, ne womekpɔ dze oa? Alo ɖe vivi le azi ƒe ɣia mea?

english_verse: That's how my food tastes, and my appetite is gone. *
translation_verse: Nye luʋɔ gbe asiɖeɖe eŋu: nuɖuɖu nyɔŋu wònye nam.

english_verse: How I wish that God would answer my prayer
translation_verse: Oo, ɖe nye didi nava me, eye Mawu nawɔ nye mɔkpɔkpɔ dzi nam!

english_verse: Then I would be comforted, knowing that in all of my pain I have never disobeyed God.
translation_verse: Anye ne nye akɔ afa tso, be nyemesẽ nu le kɔkɔetɔ ƒe nyawo ŋu o, eye mati kpo le veve heliheli la me.

english_verse: Why should I patiently hope when my strength is gone?
translation_verse: Nukae nye nye ŋusẽ, be maɖo dzi, eye nukae nye nye nuwuwu, be magbɔ dzi ɖi?

english_verse: I am not strong as stone or bronze,
translation_verse: Nye ŋusẽ la, kpe ƒe ŋusẽ wònyea? Eye nye ŋutilã la, akɔbli wònyea?

english_verse: and I have finally reached the end of my rope. My Friends, I Am Desperate
translation_verse: Metsi ya me, eye woɖe nu ziɔɖeŋua ɖa le ŋunye.

english_verse: My friends, I am desperate, and you should help me, even if I no longer respect God All-Powerful. *
translation_verse: Ne dzi ɖe le amea ɖe ƒo la, ele be, xɔlɔ̃wo nafa tu nɛ, nenye be, edzudzɔ ŋusẽkatãtɔ la vɔvɔ hã.

english_verse: like streams that swell with melting snow,
translation_verse: siwo tsi babla na woblu, eye sno ɣla ɖe wo me.

english_verse: I am like a caravan, lost in the desert while searching for water.
translation_verse: Asihawo dze gbe to tagba, eye wotsrɔ̃.

english_verse: thought they would find water. But they were disappointed,
translation_verse: ke woƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ zu ŋukpe, eye esi wova afima la, woƒe mo tsi dã.

english_verse: just as I am with you. Only one look at my suffering, and you run away scared. What Have I Done Wrong?
translation_verse: Alea miawo hã miele ɖeke mee o; miekpɔ ŋɔdzi, eye vɔvɔ̃ ɖo mi.

english_verse: Have I ever asked any of you to give me a gift
translation_verse: Ɖe megblɔ be: Mina num, eye mitsɔ miaƒe kesinɔnuwo wɔ nunanae nam,

english_verse: or to purchase my freedom from brutal enemies?
translation_verse: miɖem tso ketɔ la si me, eye mixɔm le ŋlɔmitɔ si me loo?

english_verse: What have I done wrong? Show me, and I will keep quiet.
translation_verse: Mifia num, eye mazi kpoo; eye mlɖe nusi me metra le la, me nam!

english_verse: The truth is always painful, but your arguments prove nothing.
translation_verse: Aleke gbegbe ŋusẽ mehele nyateƒe ƒe nyawo mee o! Ke aleke miaƒe nya heɖeameŋuawo le?

english_verse: Here I am desperate, and you consider my words as worthless as wind.
translation_verse: Nya tɔe miebe, yewoaɖia? Amesi ɖo ɖikeke me nyawo la, yae wonye.

english_verse: Why, you would sell an orphan or your own neighbor!
translation_verse: Nu ko wònye miele dzidzem ɖe tsyɔ̃eviwo dzi, eye mietsɔ mia xɔlɔ̃ le dzadzram.

english_verse: Look me straight in the eye; I won't lie to you.
translation_verse: Azɔ, ne mielɔ̃ la, mitrɔ ɖe ŋunye, nyemaka aʋatso le mia ŋku me akpɔ o.

english_verse: Stop accusing me falsely; my reputation is at stake.
translation_verse: Mitrɔ dzro, alakpa megana me o, mitrɔ, tɔnyee nye dzɔdzɔea kokoko!

english_verse: I know right from wrong, and I am not telling lies.
translation_verse: Ɖe alakpa le nye aɖe dzia? Eye ɖe nye veme madze si nu vlo oa?

english_verse: We are slaves in search of shade; we are laborers longing for our wages.
translation_verse: Alesi kluvi ƒe ŋku blãna ɖe vɔvɔli ŋu, eye alesi agbaledɔwɔla nɔa eƒe fetu dzɔmee la,

english_verse: God has made my days drag on and my nights miserable.
translation_verse: nenema nyea mexɔ hiãɣletiwoe, eye wotso fuzãwo nam.

english_verse: I pray for night to end, but it stretches out while I toss and turn.
translation_verse: Ne memlɔ anyi la, ekema mebuna be: Ɣekaɣi mele fɔfɔ ge? Fiẽ gbɔ hã metsɔ o; eye meƒoa togogoe wòtiam, vaseɖe esime ŋu ɖena le eme.

english_verse: My parched skin is covered with worms, dirt, and sores,
translation_verse: Nye ŋutilã dze nyẽ, eye wòƒo anyi; nye ŋutigbalẽ lé akpɔ, eye wògagbã tsi,

english_verse: and my days are running out quicker than the thread of a fast-moving needle. Don't Forget!
translation_verse: Nye ŋkekewo ɖia ɖu wu avɔlɔ̃ʋu, eye wo nu yina mɔkpɔkpɔ manɔmee.

english_verse: I beg you, God, don't forget! My life is just a breath, and trouble lies ahead.
translation_verse: Mibu eme kpɔ, ƒuƒu enye nye agbe, eye nye ŋku magakpɔ dzɔgbenyule o.

english_verse: I will vanish from sight, and no one, including you, will ever see me again.
translation_verse: Amesiwo ƒe ŋku le ŋunye la, womagakpɔm o; eye ne wò ŋkuwo dim la, nyemaganɔ anyi o.

english_verse: I will disappear in the grave or vanish from sight like a passing cloud.
translation_verse: Alilikpo buna, eye enu yina; nenema ke, ne amea ɖe yi tsiẽ la, megagbɔna o,

english_verse: Never will I return home; soon I will be forgotten.
translation_verse: megatrɔna va eƒe me o, eye enɔƒe megadzea si eyama o.

english_verse: Am I the sea or a sea monster? Is that why you imprison me?
translation_verse: Atsiaƒue menyea, alo bosoe menye, be nèɖe ŋudzɔlawo ɖo ŋunyea?

english_verse: but you torture me with terrible dreams. *
translation_verse: ekema ètsɔa drɔ̃e doa vɔvɔ̃ nam, eye nètsɔa ŋutega ɖoa ŋɔdzi nam,

english_verse: I'd rather choke to death than live in this body.
translation_verse: ale be nye luʋɔ di be, gbɔgbɔtsixe natsi ye ƒo, eye wòlɔ̃ ku wu ƒuɖiɖi glaŋglaŋ sia.

english_verse: Leave me alone and let me die; my life has no meaning.
translation_verse: Etim azɔ, nyemebe, manɔ agbe tegbee o. Ɖe asi le ŋunye, elabena ƒuƒu enye nye ŋkekewo.

english_verse: What makes you so concerned about us humans?
translation_verse: Nuka nye amegbelɔ be, nèɖo kɔkɔe, eye be, nétsɔ wò tame ɖo eŋu?

english_verse: Why do you test us from sunrise to sunset?
translation_verse: Eɖoa teƒe nɛ ŋdi sia ŋdi, eye nèdonɛ kpɔna aɖabaƒoƒo sia aɖabaƒoƒo.

english_verse: Won't you look away just long enough for me to swallow?
translation_verse: Ɣekaɣi naɖe kɔ ɖa le ŋunye, eye naɖe asi le ŋunye, be mami ta tetee?

english_verse: Why do you watch us so closely? What's it to you, if I sin? Why am I your target and such a heavy burden?
translation_verse: Ne mewɔ nuvɔ̃ la, nuka wonye mewɔ wò, wò amegbetɔwo ŋn dzɔla? Nukaŋuti nètsɔm ɖo nu dzidzea na ɖokuiwò, be metrɔ zu agba na ɖokuinye?

english_verse: Why do you refuse to forgive? Soon you won't find me, because I'll be dead.
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti mẽtsɔ nye dzidadawo ke o, eye mèna nye vodadawo nu yi o? Elabena azɔ mele ke me mlɔ ge, eye ne èdim la, nyemaganɔ anyi o.

english_verse: Bildad from Shuah said:
translation_verse: Tete Suaxtɔ Bildad xɔ edzi gblɔ bena:

english_verse: How long will you talk and keep saying nothing?
translation_verse: Zi nenie nanɔ nu ƒom alea, eye wò nu me nya nanye ya ʋuduʋudu?

english_verse: Does God All-Powerful stand in the way of justice?
translation_verse: Ɖe Mawu atrɔ gbo nya dzɔdzɔea? Eye ɖe ŋusẽkatãtɔ atrɔ gbo dzɔdzɔenyenyea?

english_verse: So why don't you turn to him
translation_verse: Ke ne èdi Mawu vevie, eye nèƒo koko na ŋusẽkatãtɔ la,

english_verse: and start living right? Then he will decide to rescue and restore you to your place of honor.
translation_verse: ne èdza, eye nèwɔ nu dzɔdzɔe la, ekema adzɔ ŋuwò, eye wòagaɖɔ wò dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe nɔƒe la ɖo.

english_verse: Your future will be brighter by far than your past. Our Ancestors Were Wise
translation_verse: Eye ne ele nyaŋui gbã la, ekema àdzi ɖe edzi emegbe.

english_verse: Our own time has been short, like a fading shadow, and we know very little.
translation_verse: Elabena míatvo la etsɔviwo míenye, eye ame makpɔnuteƒewo míenye; elabena míaƒe ŋkekewo le ahe vɔvɔli ene le anyigba dzi.

english_verse: Papyrus reeds grow healthy only in a swamp,
translation_verse: Ɖe nyɔnufɛgbe miena ɖe afisi sii mele oa? Eye ɖe aƒla miena tsi makpɔmakpɔea?

english_verse: and if the water dries up, they die sooner than grass.
translation_verse: Egale mumu ko, eye meɖo sisi me o, ke etrea ƒuƒu na gbewo katã.

english_verse: Such is the hopeless future of all who turn from God
translation_verse: Alea wonona na amesiwo kalã ŋlɔ Mawu be la, eye ame vlowo ƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ ɖoa agu.

english_verse: and trust in something as frail as a spider's web—
translation_verse: Eƒe dziɖoɖo ɖe nu ŋu mele naneke me o, eye eƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ le abe yiyiɖɔ ene.

english_verse: they take hold and fall because it's so flimsy.
translation_verse: Eziɔna ɖe eƒe xɔ ŋu, ke menɔa tsitrenu o, ekuna ɖe eŋu, ke melina ɖe te o.

english_verse: Sinful people are like plants with spreading roots and plenty of sun and water.
translation_verse: Ewɔna mlɔmlɔmlɔ le ɣetotoe nu, eye wòɖea ka ɖe eƒe abɔ me.

english_verse: They wrap their roots tightly around rocks.
translation_verse: Edoa ke ɖe kpewo dzi, eye wòtoa kpewo me.

english_verse: But once they are pulled up, they have no more place;
translation_verse: Ne eɖee da le eteƒe la, ekema teƒe la sẽa nu le eŋu be: Nyemekpɔ wò kpɔ o.

english_verse: their life slips away, and other plants grow there.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ale eƒe mɔ ƒe dzidzɔ le enye si eve bubu miena tso ke me.

english_verse: We know God doesn't reject an innocent person or help a sinner.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, Mawu medoa vlo mawuvɔ̃lawo o, eye meléa nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔlawo ƒe asi o.

english_verse: And so, he will make you happy and give you something to smile about.
translation_verse: Agana nu koko nayɔ wò nume, eye aseyetsotso nano wò nuyi nu.

english_verse: But your evil enemies will be put to shame and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Ŋukpe ale wò ketɔwo, eye nu tovo wɔlawo ƒe agbadɔ maganɔ anyi o.

english_verse: What you say is true. No human is innocent in the sight of God.
translation_verse: Nyateƒe, menyae be, ele alea; eye aleke amegbetɔ ƒe nya adzɔ le Mawu gbɔa?

english_verse: Not once in a thousand times could we win our case if we took him to court.
translation_verse: Ne edze eŋu wòbe, yeahe nya kplii la, mate ŋu aɖo akpe ƒe ɖeka ŋu o.

english_verse: God is wise and powerful— who could possibly oppose him and win?
translation_verse: Dzi nyanu le esi, eye eƒe ŋusẽ kako. Ameka tsi tre ɖe eŋu, eye megbe kpɔdodoe o?

english_verse: When God becomes angry, he can move mountains before they even know it.
translation_verse: Emli towo ɖa, ke womenyae o; etrɔ wo bu anyi le eƒe dɔmedzoe me.

english_verse: God can shake the earth loose from its foundations
translation_verse: Eʋuʋu anyigba le enɔƒe, ale be eƒe sɔtiwo na.

english_verse: or command the sun and stars to hold back their light.
translation_verse: Ede se na ɣe, eye medze o, eye wòtu nu ɖe ɣletiviwo nu.

english_verse: God alone stretched out the sky, stepped on the sea,
translation_verse: Eya ɖeka keke dziŋgɔli me, eye wòzɔ ƒu dzeagbo dzi.

english_verse: Of all the miracles God works, we cannot understand a one.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nu gã, si me dzodzro meli o, kple nukunu, siwo melexexlẽ me o.

english_verse: God walks right past me, without making a sound.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, eto ŋunye yi, eye nyiemekpɔe o; esa agbe va yi, eye nyemedze sii o.

english_verse: And if he grabs something, who can stop him or raise a question?
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ehoa nu kple ke, ameka axe mɔ na? Ameka agblɔ nɛ be: Nuka wɔm nèle?

english_verse: When God showed his anger, the servants of the sea monster fell at his feet.
translation_verse: Mawu mefaa eƒe dziku nu o, eye Raxab ƒe xɔnametɔwo abɔbɔ ɖe ete.

english_verse: How, then, could I possibly argue my case with God? Though I Am Innocent
translation_verse: Aleke nyea mahe nya kplii, eye afika makpɔ ava dzɔdzɔe le le eƒe ŋkume?

english_verse: Even though I am innocent, I can only beg for mercy.
translation_verse: Ne tɔnye dza ʋuu keke hã la, nyemate ŋu aɖo ŋu nɛ o, koko boŋ maƒo na nyia ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la.

english_verse: And if God came into court when I called him, he would not hear my case.
translation_verse: Ne meyɔe, eye wòtɔ nam hã, nyemaxɔe ase be, ele to ɖe nye gbe ŋu o.

english_verse: He would strike me with a storm and increase my injuries for no reason at all.
translation_verse: Edze dzinye le ahom me, eye wòdzi nye abiwo ɖe dzi naneke mawɔmawɔe.

english_verse: Before I could get my breath, my miseries would multiply.
translation_verse: Mede mɔ nam be, magbɔ o, ke boŋ ena vevesesewo ɖi ƒo nam.

english_verse: God is much stronger than I am, and who would call me into court to give me justice?
translation_verse: Ne eɖi ŋusẽ nu la, kpɔ ɖa, ŋusẽtɔ enye si; eye nenye ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ la, ameka akplɔm ayii?

english_verse: Even if I were innocent, God would prove me wrong.
translation_verse: Ne tanye dzɔ la, nye nu abu fɔm, eye ne nyemeɖi fɔ o hã la, abum bubui.

english_verse: I am not guilty, but I no longer care what happens to me.
translation_verse: Nyemeɖi fɔ o! Nyemedze si ɖokuinye o, eye megbe nye agbe!

english_verse: What difference does it make? God destroys the innocent along with the guilty.
translation_verse: Wo katã le ɖeka! Eyata mebe: Ame maɖifɔ kple fɔɖila siaa wotsrɔ̃na.

english_verse: When a good person dies a sudden death, God sits back and laughs.
translation_verse: Ne atam de asi amewuwu me ɖe vo me ta, ekema eɖea alɔme te ame maɖifɔwo ƒe vevesese ŋu.

english_verse: And who else but God blindfolds the judges, then lets the wicked take over the earth? My Life Is Speeding By
translation_verse: Wotsɔ anyigba de asi na nu vlo wɔlawo, eye wòtsyɔ nu mo na woƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo. Ne menye eyae o la, ekema amekae wɔe?

english_verse: My life is speeding by, without a hope of happiness.
translation_verse: Nye ŋkekewo le abla dem wu duƒula; wosi, eye womekpɔ dzɔgbenyuiea ɖeke o.

english_verse: Each day passes swifter than a sailing ship or an eagle swooping down.
translation_verse: Woyi mii abe aƒlaʋu ene, eye abe alesi hɔ̃ dea agba anyi ɖe nuɖuɖu dzi ene.

english_verse: Sometimes I try to be cheerful and to stop complaining,
translation_verse: Ne mebu be: maŋlɔ nye konyifafa be, madzudzɔ adãɖoɖo, eye makɔ mo la,

english_verse: but my sufferings frighten me, because I know that God still considers me guilty.
translation_verse: ekema nye veveseseawo katã doa vɔvɔ̃ nam, elabena menyae be, mèle tsotso ge nam o.

english_verse: So what's the use of trying to prove my innocence?
translation_verse: Fɔɖila menye tso, nukata manɔ agbagba dzem dzodzro ɖo?

english_verse: Even if I washed myself with the strongest soap,
translation_verse: Ne mele snotsi, eye meklɔ nye asi de adzalẽtsi me la,

english_verse: God would throw me into a pit of stinking slime, leaving me disgusting to my clothes.
translation_verse: ekema anyrɔm ɖe ba me, eye manyɔ ŋu na nye awuwo.

english_verse: God isn't a mere human like me. I can't put him on trial.
translation_verse: Elabena menye ame wònye abe nye ene, ne maɖo ŋu nɛ be: na míayi ʋɔnu o.

english_verse: Who could possibly judge between the two of us?
translation_verse: Nyametsolaa ɖeke mele mía dome, ne wòado asi mí ame eve la dzi o.

english_verse: Can someone snatch away the stick God carries to frighten me?
translation_verse: Ne eɖe eƒe ameƒoti la ɖa le ŋunye, eve eƒe ŋɔdzi megaɖo vɔvɔ̃ nam o la,

english_verse: Then I could speak up without fear of him, but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_verse: ekema maƒo nu, eye nyemavɔ̃e o; elabena menye alea mele o.

english_verse: I am sick of life! And from my deep despair, I complain to you, my God.
translation_verse: Nye agbe le ŋu nyɔm na nye luʋɔ, eyata mana konyifafa naɖo bababa, eye maƒo nu le nye luʋɔ ƒe vevesesewo me.

english_verse: Don't just condemn me! Point out my sin.
translation_verse: Megblɔ na Mawu be: Megabu fam o; na manya nusi la nele avu wɔm kplim ɖo!

english_verse: Why do you take such delight in destroying those you created and in smiling on sinners?
translation_verse: Ɖe wòle nuwò vivim be, nète ame ɖe anyi, eye nètsɔ nye, wò asinudɔwɔwɔ la, ƒu gbe, eye nèklẽ ɖe ame vlo ƒe adaŋudede dzia?

english_verse: Do you look at things the way we humans do?
translation_verse: Ŋutilãŋkue le tawòa? alo ɖe nèkpɔa nu, abe alesi amegbetɔ kpɔa nui enea?

english_verse: Is that why you are so quick to find fault with me?
translation_verse: Hafi nèle nye vodadawo gɔme dim, eye nèle nye nuvɔ̃wo ta biam le sesem,

english_verse: You know I am innocent, but who can defend me against you?
translation_verse: eya wònye ènyae be, nyemeɖi fɔ o hafi, eye amea ɖeke mate ŋu axɔ ame le asiwò me o.

english_verse: Will you now destroy someone you created?
translation_verse: Wò asie mem, eye néwɔ nye afisiafi pɛpɛpɛ tso, hafi natsrɔ̃m mahã?

english_verse: Remember that you molded me like a piece of clay. So don't turn me back into dust once again.
translation_verse: Ɖo ŋui be, tsue nètsɔ wɔm, eye ɖe nèbe, magatrɔ zu anyia?

english_verse: As cheese is made from milk, you created my body from a tiny drop.
translation_verse: Ɖe mèkɔm ɖe anyi abe notsi ene, eye nèna mebla abe notsi kpekẽ ene oa?

english_verse: Then you tied my bones together with muscles and covered them with flesh and skin.
translation_verse: Efa ŋutigbalẽ kple lã ɖe ŋunye, eye nède ƒu kple lãmeka menye.

english_verse: You, the source of my life, showered me with kindness and watched over me. You Have Not Explained
translation_verse: Ena agbe kple amenuvevem, eye wò ametakpɔkpɔ dzra nye gbɔgbɔ ɖo.

english_verse: You have not explained all of your mysteries,
translation_verse: Nusia nèɣla ɖe wò dzi me, menyae be, èɖo esia ɖe tame.

english_verse: but you catch and punish me each time I sin.
translation_verse: Ne mewɔ nuvɔ̃ la, èle ŋudzɔ nam hã, eye mètso nam le vodada me o.
