translation_verse: Nuwo kalã le agbagbadzedze dzi, emegbelɔ mele ŋu aƒo nu le wo ŋu avɔe o; nukpɔkpɔ meɖia ƒo na ŋku o, eye nusese meyɔa to o.

english_verse: Someone might say, “Here is something new!” But it happened before, long before we were born.
translation_verse: Ne nane to, eye amewo be: „Mikpɔ ɖa, nu yeyea ɖe to“ la, edzɔ do ŋgɔ na mi gbaɖegbe ke.

english_verse: No one who lived in the past is remembered anymore, and everyone yet to be born will be forgotten too. It Is Senseless To Be Wise
translation_verse: Ŋku dzo le blematɔwo dzi, nenema ke amesi gbɔna dzadza ge hã, wo yometɔwo maɖo ŋku wo dzi o.

english_verse: I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel.
translation_verse: Nye, nyagblɔla, meɖu fia ɖe Israel dzi le Yerusalem.

english_verse: With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do.
translation_verse: Meɖo nye ta me anyi, be matsɔ nunya adzro nusiwo kalã dzɔna le dziƒoa te la me akpa, eye makpɔ wo ta ɖa. Agbagbadzedze vɔ̃e wònye Mawu tsa na amegbetɔviwo, ne woatsɔ ana kutri kumi.

english_verse: I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Mele ŋku ɖe nusiwo katã wowɔna le ɣea te la ŋu, eye kpa ɖa, wo katã tofloko kple dagbadagba ɖe ya me wonye.

english_verse: If something is crooked, it can't be made straight; if something isn't there, it can't be counted.
translation_verse: Womete ŋu adzɔ nu gɔglɔ̃ o, eye nusi kpɔtɔ la, womate ŋu axlẽe akpe ɖe nu ŋu o.

english_verse: I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.”
translation_verse: Megblɔ le nye dzi me be: Vavãe, nye asi tu nunya ga geɖewo wu amesiwo katã bɔ Yerusalem nu ɖo ŋgɔ num la, eye nye dzi kpɔ nunya kple gɔmesese fũ.

english_verse: Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Eye esi meɖo ta me enyi, be medze si nunya, eye medze si aɖaʋadzedze kple bometsitsi la, medze sii be, esia hã dagbadagba de ya me wònye.

english_verse: The more you know, the more you hurt; the more you understand, the more you suffer.
translation_verse: Elabena dziku geɖe kpe ɖe nunya geɖe ŋu, eye amesi li kɔ sidzedze la, eli kɔ vevesese.

english_verse: I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense.
translation_verse: Megblɔ le nye dzi me be: Mãtsɔ dzidzɔ mee akpɔ, eye maɖu agbe! Ke esia hã toflokoe.

english_verse: Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do?
translation_verse: Megblɔ na nukoko be: adaʋae! eye na dzidzɔ be: nuka esia ya awɔ?

english_verse: I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
translation_verse: Mehe le nye dzi me be: Matsɔ wein anyro nye ŋutilã, ke nye dzi natsɔ nunya akplɔm, ne meva bometsitsi goŋgoŋ, eye makpa nusi nyo na amegbefɔviwo be, woawɔ le dziƒoa te le woƒe agbenɔɣi me la.

english_verse: I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards.
translation_verse: Mewɔ dɔ klitsuwo: metu xɔwo, mede weingblewo,

english_verse: I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees.
translation_verse: melɔ ahɔwo, eye mewɔ tsaɖiƒevewo hedo afi tseku ɖuɖua vovovowo ɖi;

english_verse: And I had pools where I could get water for the trees.
translation_verse: medo tsitawo, ne matsɔ ade tsi avemeti damawo.

english_verse: I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Meƒle kluvliwo kple kosiviwo, eye esiwo wodzi le aƒe me hã nɔ asinye. Nyihawo kple alẽhawo nɔ asinye taŋ wu amesiwo katã nɔ Yerusalem do ŋgɔ nam.

english_verse: Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
translation_verse: Meƒo klosalo kple sika, fiawo kple anyigbawo ƒe kesinɔnuwo nu ƒu; medo ŋutsu hadzilawo kple nyɔnu hadzilawo ne ɖokuinye; mese amegbetɔviwo ƒe vivisese, eye nyɔnu hɔ ɖe asinye kpaŋ.

english_verse: I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise.
translation_verse: Ade meɖo kpo gaɖo kpo ɖe dzi wu amesiwo katã nɔ Yerusalem ɖo ŋgɔ nam; eye nye nunya hã tsi ŋunye.

english_verse: I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work.
translation_verse: Nusianu, si nye ŋkuwo di la, nyemete wo o; nyemetsri dzidzɔa ɖeke na nye dzi o, ke boŋ nye dzi kpa dzidzɔ ɖe nye agbagbadzedzewo katã ŋu, eye esia nye tanye gome tso nye agbagbadzedzewo katã me.

english_verse: Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble. Wisdom Comes from God
translation_verse: Ke esi metrɔ kɔ ɖe ɖɔ, siwo katã nye asi wɔ, kple agbagba, siwo medze ɖe wo ŋu ŋutl la, kpɔ ɖa, tofloko kple dagbadagba ɖe ya me wonye, eye viɖea ɖeke mele ɣe la te o.

english_verse: I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity.
translation_verse: Eye metrɔ, be makpɔ nunya, aɖaʋadzedze kple bometsitsi ɖa, elabena nuka amesi ava dze fia yome la awɔ? Nusi wowɔ xoxo va yi la koe!

english_verse: And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.
translation_verse: Tete mekpɔ be, nunya ƒo bometsitsi ta, ahe alesi kekeli ƒo viviti tae ene.

english_verse: Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
translation_verse: Nu nyala to ŋku ɖe ta, ke bometsila zɔa viviti me. Ke medze sii be, nye ɖeka tɔgbe koe dzɔna ɖe wo katã dzi.

english_verse: Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense.
translation_verse: Tete megblɔ le nye dzi me be: Nya, si adzɔ ɖe bometsila dzi la kee le dzɔdzɔ ge ɖe nye hã dzinye tso, nukata gɔ̃e nyea medze nunya alea gbegbe ɖo? Eye megblɔ le nye dzi me be: Esia hã toflokoe.

english_verse: This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Tete melé fu agbenɔnɔ, elabena nusiwo wowɔna le ɣea te la, medze ŋunye o, elabena wo katã tofloko kple dagbadagba ɖe ya me wonye.

english_verse: Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all.
translation_verse: Eye melé fu agbagba, siwo katã medze le ɣea le la, le esi mele wo gblẽ ge ɖi na yonyemedzela ta.

english_verse: Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
translation_verse: Eye amekae nyae be, nunyala loo, alo bometsila nye ge wògbɔna? Hafi eyae le ŋusẽ kpɔ ge ɖe nye agbagba, siwo katã metso kutrikuku kple nunya dze le ɣea te la dzi. Esia hã toflokoe!

english_verse: I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed.
translation_verse: Tete metrɔ, eye ɖikeke do nye dzi me ɖe agbagba, siwo katã medze le ɣea te la ŋu.

english_verse: When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong.
translation_verse: Elabena ne amea ɖe tsa nunya, gɔmesese kple aɖaŋu wɔ eƒe ɖɔe la, ele na be, wòagblẽe ɖi na ame bubu, si medze agbagba le eŋu o la, woa zu etɔ. Esia hã tofloko kple vɔ gã wònye.

english_verse: What do we really gain from all of our hard work?
translation_verse: Elabena nuka amegbefɔ kpɔna tsoa eƒe dɔwo kalã kple agbagba, siwoeƒe dzi dzena le ɣea te la mea?

english_verse: Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
translation_verse: Elabena eƒe ŋkekewo katã nye vevesese, eye nuxaxa nye eƒe dɔwɔwɔwo, le zã me gɔ̃ hã eƒe dzi mekpɔa gbɔdzɔe o. Esia hã toflokoe!

english_verse: The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us,
translation_verse: Ɖe menyo na amegbetɔ wu be, wòaɖu nu ana nu, eye eƒe luʋɔ naɖu agbe akpe ɖe eƒe agbagbadzedzewo ŋu oa? Ke esia la, Mawu si me ko wòtsona, abe alesi mekpɔe ene.

english_verse: and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do.
translation_verse: Elabena ameka ato exa aɖu nu, eye wòase vivi?

english_verse: If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Elabena etsɔ nunya, sidzedze kple dzidzɔ na amesi ƒe nu dze eŋu la; ke nuvɔ̃wɔla la, etsɔ dɔwɔwɔ nɛ, be wòaƒo nu nu ƒu, eye wòali kɔ nu, ne Mawu natsɔ na amesi ƒe nu dze eŋu la. Esia hã tofloko kple dagbadagba ɖe ya me wònye.

english_verse: Everything on earth has its own time and its own season.
translation_verse: Ɣeyiɣi li na nusianu, eye azã li na lameɖoɖowo katã le dzi ƒoa te.

english_verse: There is a time for birth and death, planting and reaping,
translation_verse: Amedziɣi li, eye kuɣi li; nuɖoɣi li, eye nu dodoawo hoɣi li;

english_verse: for killing and healing, destroying and building,
translation_verse: amewuɣi li, eye gbeɖaɣi li; xɔgbãɣi li, eye etuɣi li;

english_verse: for crying and laughing, weeping and dancing,
translation_verse: avifaɣi li, eye nukoɣi li; konyifaɣi li, eye ɣeɖuɣi li;

english_verse: for throwing stones and gathering stones, embracing and parting.
translation_verse: kpekakaɣi li, eyekpeƒoƒoƒuɣi li; asikplakɔɣi li, eye adzɔgenɔnɔ na asikplakɔɣi li;

english_verse: There is a time for finding and losing, keeping and giving,
translation_verse: nuɖiɣi li, eye nubuɣi li; nudzraɖoɣi li, eye nuƒugbeɣi li;

english_verse: for tearing and sewing, listening and speaking.
translation_verse: nuvuvuɣi li, nye nutɔɣi li; ɖoɖoeziɣi li, eye nuƒoɣi li;

english_verse: There is also a time for love and hate, for war and peace. What God Has Given Us To Do
translation_verse: lɔlɔ̃ɣi li, eye fuléɣi li; aʋawɔɣi li, eye ŋutifafaɣi li.

english_verse: What do we gain by all our hard work?
translation_verse: Viɖe ka ame kpɔna tsoa dɔ, si ŋu wòdzea agbagba lena la me?

english_verse: I have seen what difficult things God demands of us.
translation_verse: Mekpe dɔ, siwo Mawu tsɔ de asi na amegbetɔviwo, ne woatsɔ aku kutrii la ɖa.

english_verse: God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nuwo katã nyuie ɖe wo wɔɣi, eye wòde: mavɔmavɔ dzi me na wo, negbe ɖeko amegbetɔ menya mɔnu le nusiwo Mawu wɔ la ƒe agɔmegbɔ, kple tagbɔ ŋu ne

english_verse: I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life,
translation_verse: Medze sii bena, nu nyuia ɖeke meli na wo wu be, woakpɔ dzidzɔ, eye woaɖu agbe le woƒe agbenɔɣi o.

english_verse: because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do.
translation_verse: Ke be amea ɖe naɖu nu ano nu, eye wòanyo nɛ le eƒe agbagbadzedzewo katã me la, Mawu ƒe nunanae.

english_verse: Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
translation_verse: Medze sii be, nusiwo kam Mawu wɔ la, anɔ anyi ɖaa, womatsɔ naneke akpee o, eye womaɖe naneke le eme o. Mawu ɖe wòwɔe, alea, be woavɔ̃ ye.

english_verse: Everything that happens has happened before, and all that will be has already been— God does everything over and over again. The Future Is Known Only to God
translation_verse: Nusi li la, nɔ anyi tsã va yi, eye nusi gbɔna anyi nɔ ge la, nɔ anyi gbaɖegbe ke; eye Mawu gaɖia nusi nu va yi la. Vɔ̃ Mawu, eye na wɔ gome nadze ŋuwo.

english_verse: Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice.
translation_verse: Eye megakpɔ le ɣea te be, nu madzɔmadzɔ le ʋɔnuɖrɔ̃ƒe, eye nu madzɔmadzɔ le dzɔdzɔenyenye nɔƒe.

english_verse: So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good.
translation_verse: Tete megblɔ le nye dzi: me be: Mawu le ʋɔnu drɔ̃ ge ame dzɔdzɔewo kple ame vɔ̃diwo, elabena eɖo azã na tameɖoɖowo katã kple nuwɔwɔwo katã.

english_verse: I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals.
translation_verse: Megblɔ le nye dzi me bena. Amegbetɔviwo ta esia va me do, ne Mawu naɖo wo akpa, eye ne woadze sii be, lãwo yewonye.

english_verse: Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense.
translation_verse: Elabena nya ɖeka tɔgbe dzɔna de amegbetɔviwo kple lãwo siaa dzi; alesi esiawo kunae la, nenema ke ekemeawo hã kunae, gbɔgbɔ ɖekae le wo katã si, eye amegbetɔ mexɔ asi wu lã o; elabena wo katã tofloko wonye.

english_verse: All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth.
translation_verse: Wo katã woyina teƒe ɖeka; anyi me wo katã wotso, eye anyi wo katã woagazu.

english_verse: Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth?
translation_verse: De amea de nyae be, amegbetɔviwo ƒe gbɔgbɔ yia dzi, eye lãwo ƒe gbɔgbɔ yia anyi me loo?

english_verse: We were meant to enjoy our work, and that's the best thing we can do. We can never know the future.
translation_verse: Eyata mekpɔ be, enye wu na amegbetɔ be, wòakpɔ dzidzɔ le eƒe dɔwɔwɔwo ŋu, elabena esia nye eƒe gome. Elabena amekae akplɔe ayi afisi wòakpɔ nusiadzɔ le emegbe la le?

english_verse: I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful.
translation_verse: Eye megade ŋku de ameteteɖeanyi, siwo katã dzɔna le ɣea te la, eye kpa da, amesiwo woto de anyi la ƒe aɖatsiwo le tsyɔtsyɔm, ke akɔfalaa ɖeke meli na wo o; amesiwo te wo de anyi la, se ŋuta le wo ŋu, ke akɔfalaa ɖeke meli na wo o.

english_verse: I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living.
translation_verse: Tete mekafu amesiwo ku gbaɖegbe ke la, wu agbagbeawo, siwo gale agbe;

english_verse: But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
translation_verse: eye amesi medzɔ gɔ̃, ne wòayi nuwɔwɔ vɔ̃di, siwo dzɔna le ɣea te, kpɔ ge o la tɔ me nyo wu wo ame eve la tɔ.

english_verse: Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Eye mekpɔ agbagbadzedzewo katã kple aɖaŋudzedzewo katã de dɔwɔwɔ ŋu be, ŋuʋaʋã wonye de amehavi ŋu. Esia hã tofloko kple dagbadagba de ya me wonye.

english_verse: Fools will fold their hands and starve to death.
translation_verse: Bometsila ɖe asi asitɛ me hele eya ŋutɔ ƒe ŋutilã ɖum.

english_verse: Yet a very little food eaten in peace is better than twice as much earned from overwork and chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Gbɔɖeme asiʋlo ɖeka nyo wu agbagbadzedze kple dagbadagba ɖe ya me asiʋlo eve taŋ.

english_verse: Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense.
translation_verse: Eye megakpɔ tofloko le ɣea te;

english_verse: For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life! It Is Better To Have a Friend
translation_verse: Amea de eya ɖeka kolia li, eye evelia mekpe de eŋu o, ŋutsuvi alo nɔviŋutsu hã mele esi o, gake eƒe agbagbadzedzewo mewua enu o, eye kesinɔnuwo meɖia ƒo na eƒe ŋkuwo o. Ke ameka la gɔ̃e mehele agbagba dzem, eye mele nu nyui tsrim na ɖokuinye do? Esia hã tofloko kple agbagbadzedze vɔ̃di wònye!

english_verse: You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn.
translation_verse: Ne ame le eve la, enye wu ame ɖeka, elabena woakpɔ fam nyui de woƒe agbagbadzedzewo la.

english_verse: If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble.
translation_verse: Elabena ne wo ɖometɔ ɖka dze anyi la, nana ame de tsitre; ke haha na amesi tsi akogo, elabena ne edze anyi la, evelia meli afɔe de tsitre o.

english_verse: If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night.
translation_verse: Nenema ke ne ame eve womlɔ wo nɔewo gbɔ la, woléa dzo de wo nɔewo ŋu; aleke ame ɖeka alé dzo de eɖokui ŋui?

english_verse: Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
translation_verse: Eye ne ame ɖeka kpɔ ŋusẽ de amesi tsi akogo dzi hã la, ame eveawo ya anɔ te ɖe enu, eye ka ŋukplaba eta mateŋu alã bɔbɔeo.

english_verse: You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice.
translation_verse: Ɖekakpui dahe nyanu nyo wu fia tsitsi tsibome, si menana woxlɔ̃a nui o.

english_verse: Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king.
translation_verse: Eya la gaxɔ mee wotso, ne woava ɖu fia, eye ahedada me wodzii ɖo ɖe fiaɖuƒe la me.

english_verse: I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone.
translation_verse: Mekpe be, agbagbeawo katã, siwo le zɔzɔm le ɣea te la, xa ɖe ɖekakpui, si ana ame kemea teƒe la dzi.

english_verse: His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Dukɔ, siwo katã nu wole la seƒeɖo meli na wo o; ke wo megbeviwo meva kpɔ dzidzɔ de eŋu o. Esia hã tofloko kple dagbadagba ɖe ya me wònye.

english_verse: Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship.
translation_verse: Wò nu megatsɔ blablabla o, eye wò dzi megatsɔ, ne wòaƒo nu le Mawu ŋku me o; elabena Mawu le dziƒo, eye wòa nèle anyigba, eyata wò nyawo nenɔ ʋee.

english_verse: Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much.
translation_verse: Afisi kutrikuku geɖe le la, drɔ̃ekuku noa anyi, eye nu kpoloe ƒoƒo ɖea ha bometsilawo.

english_verse: If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
translation_verse: Ne èɖe adzagba na Mawu la, megahe edziwɔwɔ ɖe megbe o, elabena bometsilawo ƒe nu medzea eŋuo; alesi nèɖe adzɔgbe la, wɔe.

english_verse: God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God.
translation_verse: Ne méɖe adzɔgbe kura o la, enye wu esi naɖe adzɔgbe, eye mãwɔ edzi o.

english_verse: Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
translation_verse: Elabena tofloko geɖe le ɖrɔ̃ekuku kple nu kpoloe ƒoƒo geɖe me. Ke wò la vɔ̃ Mawu boŋ! Kesinɔnuwo ƒe dzodzronyenye.

english_verse: And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
translation_verse: Amesi lɔ̃a ga la, ga maɖi ƒo na o, eye amesi lɔ̃a kesinɔnu la, viɖea ɖeke metso eme nɛ o. Esia hã toflokoe.

english_verse: If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense.
translation_verse: Ne kesinɔnu dzi ɖe dzi la, eɖulawo hã dzinu ɖe edzi, eye nuãtɔ mekpɔa viɖeã ɖeke tsoe eme o, negbe ekpɔkpɔ kple ŋku ko.

english_verse: The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you.
translation_verse: Dɔwɔla ɖaɖu nu ʋee o, eɖaɖu nu geɖe o, alɔ̃ vivina nɛ; ke kesinɔtɔƒe nu gbogboawo menana wòɖɔa alɔ̃ o.

english_verse: If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
translation_verse: Vɔ̃ gã, si mekpe le ɣen le la, enye be, kesinɔtɔ le eƒe nuwo ŋu dzɔm hena eya ŋutɔ ƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃e.

english_verse: I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good.
translation_verse: Ne nya vɔ̃a ɖe na kesinɔnu siawo bu, eye wòdzi ŋutsuvi le ekema naneke metsia esi me o.

english_verse: Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children.
translation_verse: Alesi wòle tso dadaa ƒe mi me la, nenema ke wòaganɔ amama ayii, abe alesi wole va ene, eye matsɔ naneke aɖo asi tso eƒe agbagbadzedzewo me o.

english_verse: They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work.
translation_verse: Esia hã vɔ̃ gã wònye be, alesi wònɔ va la, nenema ke wòaganɔ ayi, eye viɖe kawòkpɔ, be wòdze agbagba ɖe ya me?

english_verse: That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind.
translation_verse: Eɖu eƒe ŋkekewo kalã le viviti, dzibibi geɖe, fukpekpe kple dziku me. Ɖokuinudede.

english_verse: What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do.
translation_verse: Eye ne Mawu na kesinɔnu kple nu xɔesiwo amea de, eye wòna misee be, wòaɖui, wòaxɔ elɔ gome, eye wòakpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe eƒe dɔwɔwɔ ŋu la, Mawu ƒe nunana nye esia.

english_verse: Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you.
translation_verse: Elabena mebua ta me le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo ŋu boo o, le esi Mawu do dzidzɔ na eƒe dzi ta.

english_verse: There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth.
translation_verse: Dzɔgbevɔ̃ea ɖe li mekpe le ɣea te, eye wòɖo agbe ɖe amegbetɔwo dzi fu;

english_verse: God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
translation_verse: Ne Mawu na kesinɔnu, nu xɔasiwo kple bubu amea ɖe, ale be nusiwo katã wòdina la, mehiãnɛ o, gake Mawu mene ŋusẽe, be wòaɖui o, ke boŋ ame tutɔ naɖul la, tofloko kple vɔ̃ gã wònye.

english_verse: You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial.
translation_verse: Ne amea ɖe dzi vi alafa, enɔ agbe ƒe geɖe, eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo sɔgbɔ, gake meɖi ƒo ɖe nu nyuiawo ŋu o, eye ameɖiƒea ɖeke mesu esi o la, mele gbɔgblɔm be, fu gege nyo wu eyama.

english_verse: even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
translation_verse: Eye nenye ƒe akpe eve wona agbe, ke meɖu agbe o la, ɖe menye teƒe ɖeka wo kam woyi oa?

english_verse: We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied.
translation_verse: Amegbetɔ ƒe dɔwɔwɔwb katã la, nue wòwɔnɛ, ke womefaa nudzodzro nu gbeɖe o.

english_verse: We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right.
translation_verse: Elabena nuka nunyala tsɔ wu bometsila, eye viɖe ka ame dahe, si nya zɔzɔ le agbagbeawo ŋku me la, kpɔna?

english_verse: It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Nukpɔkpɔ kple ŋku nyo wu nudzodzro ƒe tsa glalã tsatsa. Esia hã tofloko kple dagbadagba ɖe ya me wonye.

english_verse: Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us.
translation_verse: Nusi dza la, woyɔ eƒe ŋkɔ ɖi tsa, eye nusi ame ava zu la, woɖoeɖa ɖi, eye mate ŋu ahe nya kple amesi sẽ wui o.

english_verse: The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk?
translation_verse: Elabena nya geɖe li, si dzia toflokonyenye ɖe edzi, ke viɖe ka amegbelɔ kpɔna tsoe eme?

english_verse: Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
translation_verse: Elabena ameka nya nusi nyo na amegbelɔ le agbe me, le eƒe agbe ƒuƒlu, si wònɔ abe vɔvɔli ene la ƒe ŋkekewo katã me? Elabena ameka agblɔ nusi adzɔ le amegbetɔ megbe le ɣea te la nɛ?

english_verse: A good reputation at the time of death is better than loving care at the time of birth.
translation_verse: Ŋkɔ nyui nyo wu ami xɔasi, eye kugbe nyo wu dzigbe.

english_verse: It's better to go to a funeral than to attend a feast; funerals remind us that we all must die.
translation_verse: Kuteƒeyiyi nyo wu agloluƒeyiyi; elabena afi kemea nye emegbetɔwo katã ƒe nuwuƒe, eye wòdea dzigbɔ na agbagbeawo.

english_verse: Choose sorrow over laughter because a sad face may hide a happy heart.
translation_verse: Nuxaxa nyo wu nukoko, elabena ne mo ɖo adã la, esɔnɛ na dzi.

english_verse: A sensible person mourns, but fools always laugh.
translation_verse: Nunyalawo ƒe dzi le kuleƒe, ke bometsilawo ƒe dzi le dzidzɔleƒe.

english_verse: Correction from someone wise is better by far than praise from fools.
translation_verse: Nunyalawo ƒe dzusese nyo wu, ne woase bometsilawo ƒe ha.

english_verse: Foolish laughter is stupid. It sounds like thorns crackling in a fire.
translation_verse: Elabena alesi aŋɔka wona kpotokpoto le ze gome la, nenema nye bometsilawo ƒe nukoko. Esia ha toflokoe.

english_verse: Corruption makes fools of sensible people, and bribes can ruin you.
translation_verse: Elabena sesẽnuɖuɖu doa bometsila nunyalawo, eye zãnunana gblẽa dzi.

english_verse: Something completed is better than something just begun; patience is better than too much pride.
translation_verse: Nu ƒe nuwuwu nyo wu eƒe gɔmedzedze; dzigbɔɖitɔ nyo wu ɖaɖala.

english_verse: Only fools get angry quickly and hold a grudge.
translation_verse: Wò gbɔgbɔ megayɔ ɖe dzikudodo ŋu o, elabena bometsilawo ƒe akɔtae dziku nana.

english_verse: It isn't wise to ask, “Why is everything worse than it used to be?”
translation_verse: Megagblɔ be, nukata tsa ŋkekewo nyo wu fifitɔwo hã o, elabena mèle biabiam ɖe nunya me o.

english_verse: Having wisdom is better than an inheritance.
translation_verse: Nunya nyo kpe ɖe domenyinu ŋu, eye wònye viɖe na amesiwo le ɣe kpɔm.

english_verse: Wisdom will protect you just like money; knowledge with good sense will lead you to life.
translation_verse: Elabena nunya doa vɔvɔli, eye ga hã doa vɔvɔli; eye sidzedze ƒe viɖe enye; Nunya léa amesi si wole la ƒe agbe ɖe te.

english_verse: Think of what God has done! If God makes something crooked, can you make it straight?
translation_verse: Ɖe ŋku ɖe Mawu ƒe ɖɔwo; elabena ameka hadzɔ nusi wòglɔ̃ la?

english_verse: When times are good, you should be cheerful; when times are bad, think about what it means. God makes them both to keep us from knowing what will happen next. Some of Life's Questions
translation_verse: Kpɔ dzidzɔ le gbe nyui gbe, eye le dzɔgbevɔ̃egbe la ɖo ŋui be, Mawu ye wɔe abe ekeme ke ene, ne amegbelɔ maganya nusi adzɔ le emegbe o.

english_verse: I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper.
translation_verse: Nusiwo katã mekpɔ le nye agbe me ŋkeke ƒuƒluawo me la, enye esi: Ame dzɔdzɔea ɖewo tsrɔ̃na ɖe woƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye me, eye ame vɔɖia ɖewo nɔa agbe ɖiɖie ɖe woƒe vɔ̃ɖiwɔwɔ me.

english_verse: So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart!
translation_verse: Megawɔ nu dzɔdzɔe vivivo o, eye meganya nu tso eme akpa o; nukaŋuti nébe, yeaɖe ye ɖokui tsɔtsrɔ̃ me ɖo?

english_verse: Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool.
translation_verse: Megawu nu vɔ̃ɖi wòagbɔ eme o, eye meganye bometsila o; nukaŋuti nẽbe, yeaku, hafi azã nava de?

english_verse: Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
translation_verse: Enyo, ne ele esia ɖe asi sesie, eye ekemea hã niege le asiwò o; elabena amesi vɔ̃a Mawu la, ƒoa asa na wo katã.

english_verse: Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
translation_verse: Nunya naa ŋusẽ nunyalawo wu ŋusẽtɔ ewo, siwo le du me.

english_verse: No one in this world always does right.
translation_verse: Elabena ame dzɔdzɔea ɖeke mele anyigba dzi, si wɔa nu nyui sɔŋ, eye mewɔa nuyɔ o.

english_verse: Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you.
translation_verse: Megalé to hã ɖe amewo ƒe nusiwo katã woƒona la ŋu o, ne mãgasee, ne wò dɔla le ɖiŋu dom na wò ti.

english_verse: I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me.
translation_verse: Nusiwo katã metso nunya te kpɔ la, wonye si: Mebu be, madze nunya; ke etsi adzɔgedzɔgee nam.

english_verse: The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep.
translation_verse: Nusi li la, adzɔge wòle; ele to me, ẽ, to me wòle; ameka ƒe asi atui?

english_verse: So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
translation_verse: Eye metrɔ hetsɔ tame ɖo anyi, be madze si nunya kple tamebubu, madzro eme, eye madii, ne manyae be, nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ la bometsitsi wònye, eye lãnyenye la aɖaʋadzedze wònye.

english_verse: Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for.
translation_verse: Eye mekpɔ be, nusi vena wu ku, enye nyɔnu, si nye ɖɔ vena kaɖikaɖi wu ku ɖeɖe sɔŋ, ete dzi nye mɔ̃ka, eye eƒe asiwo nye kunyowu. Amesi ƒe nu nyo Mawu ŋu la, sina le enu, ke eɖea nuvɔ̃wɔlawo.

english_verse: With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together,
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, nyagblɔla be: Esiawoe nye asi tu ɖekaɖeka, ne makpɔ sidzedze.

english_verse: but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman.
translation_verse: Nusi dim mele atraɖi nyemekpɔe o la, enye si Mekpe ŋutsu ɖeka le wo ame akpe ɖome, ke nyemekpɔ nyɔnu le esiawo katã ɖome o.

english_verse: I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_verse: Negbe esia ko mekpɔ be, Mawu wɔ amegbetɔwo woto mɔ ɖeka, ke woawo dia ayedzedze geɖe.

english_verse: Who is smart enough to explain everything? Wisdom makes you cheerful and gives you a smile. Obey the King
translation_verse: Amekae le ahe nunyala ene? Eye ameka se nuwo gɔmeɖeɖe me? Nunya nana amegbetɔ ƒe mo kɔna, eye eƒe mo kplala la trɔna.

english_verse: If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise.
translation_verse: Mebe: Dzra fia ƒe sedede ɖo le Mawu ƒe atam la te.

english_verse: Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind.
translation_verse: Wò afa megatsɔ nadzo le esia gbɔ o; megaɖo nya vɔ̃ me o; elabena nusianu, si dze eŋu la, awɔe.

english_verse: The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?”
translation_verse: Esi wònye ŋusẽ le fia ƒe nya ŋu ta la, ameka agblɔ nɛ be: Nuka wɔm nele?

english_verse: If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it.
translation_verse: Amesi dzra sedede ɖo la, vɔa ɖeke mava edzi o, eye nunyala ƒe dzi nyaa azãgbe kple ʋɔnudɔdrɔ.

english_verse: Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything,
translation_verse: Elabena azãgbe kple ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ li na nuwɔwɔ ɖesiaɖe, elabena amegbetɔ ƒe vɔ̃wɔwɔ do agba ɖe edzi.

english_verse: We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil.
translation_verse: Amegbetɔa ɖeke mekpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe ya dzi be, wòaxe ma na ya o; amea ɖeke mekpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe kugbe dzi o, eye asiɖeɖe le ame ŋu meli le aba me o; nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ mexɔna na ewɔla o.

english_verse: I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another? Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
translation_verse: Nusiawo katã mekpɔ, eye melsɔ nye tame ɖo nuwɔwɔ, siwo katã dzɔna le ɣea te, le ɣeyiɣi, si me amegbetɔ ɖua fia ɖe ame bubuwo dzi bena woƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃e la ŋuti.

english_verse: I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense.
translation_verse: Emegbe mekpɔ woɖe ame vɔ̃ɖiwo yɔ me, eye woyi gbɔɖemeƒe; ke ele na amesiwo wɔa nu dzɔdzɔe la be, woaʋu adzo le teƒe kɔkɔe la, eye woŋlɔ wo be le dua me. Esia hã tofloko wònye.

english_verse: When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime.
translation_verse: Esi afia menye tsona le nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ŋu kaba o ŋuti la, eyata dzi doa amegbetɔviwo ƒo ŋutɔ de nu vɔɖi wɔwɔ ŋu.

english_verse: They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying: Everyone who lives right and respects God will prosper,
translation_verse: Ne nuvɔwɔla wɔa vɔ̃ zi alafa, gake nɔa agbe didie hã la, nyee menyae be, eme anye na mawuvɔ̃la, siwo sia eƒe ŋku me.

english_verse: but no one who sins and rejects God will prosper or live very long.
translation_verse: Ke eme menye na ame vɔ̃ɖiwo o, eye abe vɔvɔli ene womanɔ agbe didie o, elabena womevɔ̃a Mawu o.

english_verse: There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens.
translation_verse: Nu dzodzroa wònye dzɔna le anyigba dzi be: Ame dzɔdzɔea ɖewo li nya dzɔna ɖe wo dzi le eme vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe nuwɔwɔ nu, eye ame vɔ̃ɖia ɖewo li nya dzɔna ɖe wo dzi le ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe nuwɔwɔ nu. Mebe: Esia hã toflokoe!

english_verse: So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
translation_verse: Eyata mekafu dzidzɔkpɔkpɔ be: Nu nyuia ɖeke mele ɣea te na amegbetɔ wu esia be, wòaɖu nu ana nu akpɔ dzidzɔ o. Eye esia akplɔe alo eƒe agbe me ŋkeke, siwo Mawu nae le ɣea le la ƒe agbagbadzedzewo me.

english_verse: Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world.
translation_verse: Esi meɖo nye tame anyi, be madze si nunya, eye makpɔ nuwɔwɔ, siwo dzɔna le anyigba dzi ɖa la, — elabena ŋkeke kple zã amegbetɔ ƒe ŋku mekpɔa alɔ o —

english_verse: I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_verse: mekpɔ Mawu ƒe dɔwo katã be, amegbetɔ menya ta le nusiwo le ɣea te la nu o, eye ne amegbetɔ le kutri kum le edim hã, menya ta le enu o, eye ne nunyala be, yedze sii hã la, manya ta le enu akpɔ o.

english_verse: I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad.
translation_verse: Nusiawo katã ŋu metsɔ nye tame ɖo, eye medzro wokɔtã me kpɔ be: Ame dzɔdzɔewo kple nunyalawo kpakple woƒe nuwɔwɔwo le Mawu si me; amegbetɔ medze si lɔlɔ̃ kple fuléle tsã o; wo katã wodo ŋgɔ na wo.

english_verse: But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
translation_verse: Nu ɖeka ƒomevie kpea amewo katã: Nya ɖeka tɔgbe dzɔna ɖe ame dzɔdzɔe kple ame vɔ̃ɖi, ame nyui, eme dzadzɛ kple eme madzamadza, vɔsala kple eme masavɔ, ame nyui kple nuvɔwɔlm atamkala kple amesi atam dzia ŋɔ na la dzi.

english_verse: It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die.
translation_verse: Esia nye vɔ̃ gã le nusiwo katã dzɔna le ɣea te la dome be, nye ɖeka tɔgbe dzɔna ɖe amewo katã dzi; eyata vɔ̃ɖiwɔwɔ yɔa amegbetɔviwoƒe dzi me, eye aɖaʋadzedze le woƒe dzi me le woƒe agbenɔɣi katã; ke emegbe la woayi kukuawo gbɔ.

english_verse: As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion.
translation_verse: Elabena amesi gale ha dem kple agbagbeawo ko le mɔkpɔkpɔ le esi; elabena avu gbagbe nyo wu dzata kuku.

english_verse: We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten.
translation_verse: Elabena agbagbeawo nyae be, yewogbɔna kuku ge, ke kukuawo menye naneke o, fetua ɖeke megali na wo o, eye woŋlɔ woƒe ŋkɔ be.

english_verse: Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
translation_verse: Woƒe emelɔlɔ kple fuléle kpakple ŋuʋaʋã nu yi gbaɖegbe ke, eye womagakpɔ gome le nusiwo katã dzɔna le ɣea te la me akpɔ o. Ɖu Mawu ƒe nunanawo kple dzidzɔ, eye nawɔ nusi ƒe se wode na wo.

english_verse: So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do.
translation_verse: Eyata yi naɖu wò abolo kple dzidzɔ, eye nano wò wein le dzidzeme me, elabena gbaɖegbe ke Mawu tso na wò nuwɔwɔ sia.

english_verse: Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best.
translation_verse: Wò avɔwo nefu ɣeawokatãɣi, eye ami megagbe wò tamenɔnɔ o.

english_verse: Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth.
translation_verse: Mia kple nyɔnu, si nèlɔ̃na la, miɖu agbe le wò agbenɔnɔ ƒuƒlu ƒe ŋkekewo katã, si wotsɔ na wò le ɣea le la me, ŋkeke ƒuƒlu, siwo katã nele agbe; elabena esia nye wò agbe kple wò agbagba, si nèdze le ɣea te la ƒe gome.

english_verse: Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
translation_verse: Nusianu, si wò asi ate ŋu awɔ la, wɔe kple wò ŋusẽ; elabena nuwɔwɔ alo tamebubu, sidzedze alo nunya mele tsieƒe, afisi yi ge nala o.

english_verse: Here is something else I have learned: The fastest runners and the greatest heroes don't always win races and battles. Wisdom, intelligence, and skill don't always make you healthy, rich, or popular. We each have our own share of misfortune.
translation_verse: Eye megakpɔ le ɣea te be, duƒuƒu mele alo ɖablae me o, aʋawɔwɔ mele kalẽ me o, nuɖudukpɔkpɔ mele nunya me o, kesinɔnu mele ayedzedze me o, eye ŋudzedzekpɔbpɔ mele nugɔmesese me o, ke boŋ azãgbe kple nudiɖeame li na wo katã.

english_verse: None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap. Better To Be Wise than Foolish
translation_verse: Amegbetɔ menya eƒe azãgbe o, ke boŋ abe alesi wotsɔa dɔ vɔ̃ɖi ɖea tɔmelãwo, eye wotsɔa mɔ̃ ɖea xewoe la, nenema woɖea amegbetɔviwo abe woawo ene le dzɔgbevɔ̃eɣi, ne eƒo ɖe wo dzi kpoyi. Nunya tsoa aseye.

english_verse: Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me.
translation_verse: Mekpɔ nunya sia hã le ɣea te, eye wòdze gã nam:

english_verse: It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls.
translation_verse: Du suea ɖe li, ŋutsu ʋeea ɖewo koe le eme; tete fia gãa ɖe ho ɖe eŋu, eɖe to ɖee, eye wòƒo kpo gãwo ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten.
translation_verse: Ŋutsu ɖahe nyanua ɖe le eme; eyae tsɔ eƒe nunya xɔ du lae; ke amea ɖeke medo ŋku ŋutsu dahe ma dzi o.

english_verse: So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
translation_verse: Tete megblɔ be: Nunya nyo wu ŋusẽ, ke wodoe vlo ame dahe ƒe nunya, eye womeléa to de eƒe nyawo ŋu o.

english_verse: Words of wisdom spoken softly make much more sense than the shouts of a ruler to a crowd of fools.
translation_verse: Wosea nunyala ƒe nyawo le dziɖeɖi me wu dziɖula ƒe ɣli le bometsilawo dome.

english_verse: Wisdom is more powerful than weapons, yet one mistake can destroy all the good you have done.
translation_verse: Nunya nyo wu aʋawɔnuwo; ke nuvɔ̃wɔla ɖe ka gblẽa nu nyui geɖe dome.

english_verse: A few dead flies in perfume make all of it stink, and a little foolishness outweighs a lot of wisdom.
translation_verse: Nudzodzoe wuamewo nana amiɖala ƒe ami mina ku heƒaƒãna; bometsitsi ʋeea ɖe kpena wua nunya kple bubu.

english_verse: Sensible thoughts lead you to do right; foolish thoughts lead you to do wrong.
translation_verse: Gomesese le ɖusi me na nunyala, ke bometsila ƒe gɔmesese le mia me nɛ.

english_verse: Fools show their stupidity by the way they live; it's easy to see they have no sense.
translation_verse: Ne bometsila le mɔa ɖe dzi le nunya menɔa tagbɔ nɛ o, eye sii wo baa amewo katã bometsilawoe.

english_verse: Don't give up your job when your boss gets angry. If you stay calm, you'll be forgiven.
translation_verse: Ne dziɖula ƒe ɖɔmedzoe bi ɖe ŋuwò la, megaɖe afa le tewòƒe o, elabena tufafa tsia nuvɔ gãwo nu.

english_verse: Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair:
translation_verse: Mekpɔ nu vɔ̃ɖia ɖe le ɣea te, esɔ kple dziɖula ƒe ɖaɖaƒu

english_verse: They honor fools, but dishonor the rich;
translation_verse: Wotsɔ bometsitsi ɖo kɔkɔƒe ʋi ke, eye kesinɔtɔwo bɔbɔ nɔ anyi me.

english_verse: they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
translation_verse: Mekpɔ kluviwo le sɔ dzi, eye amegãwo le afa zɔm ahe kluviwo ene.

english_verse: If you dig a pit, you might fall in; if you break down a wall, a snake might bite you.
translation_verse: Amesi le ne ɖem la, eyae gena dzea eme, eye amesi la gli gbãm la, eyae da ɖuna.

english_verse: You could even get hurt by chiseling a stone or chopping a log.
translation_verse: Amesi le kpe ɖem la, eyae wɔa nu vevi eɖokui, eye amesi le nake dzem la, eyae xɔa abi.

english_verse: If you don't sharpen your ax, it will be harder to use; if you are wise, you'll know what to do.
translation_verse: Ne lãnu tsi kpo, eye womenyire enu o la, ele be, woahe alɔkame; ke nuwɔwɔ, ne wòadze edzi, enye nunya ƒe viɖe.

english_verse: The power to charm a snake does you no good if it bites you anyway.
translation_verse: Ne da ɖu ame, hafi wosa gbe ɖoe la, ekema gbesala mekpɔ viɖea ɖeke tso eme o.

english_verse: If you talk sensibly, you will have friends; if you talk foolishly, you will destroy yourself.
translation_verse: Nyia, si tso nunyala nu la, nyo; ke bometsila ƒe nuyi gblẽa eya ŋutɔ ɖokui dome.

english_verse: Fools begin with nonsense, and their stupid chatter ends with disaster.
translation_verse: Eƒe nu me nyia ƒe gɔmedzedze enye bometsitsi, eye eƒe nuƒoƒo ƒe nuwuwu enye aɖaʋadzedze vɔ̃ɖi.

english_verse: They never tire of talking, but none of us really know what the future will bring.
translation_verse: Bometsila ƒoa nu kpoloe; amegbetɔ menya nusi gbɔna dzɔdzɔ ge o, eye ameka agblɔ nusi ava dzɔ le emegbe la nɛ?

english_verse: Fools wear themselves out— they don't know enough to find their way home.
translation_verse: Bometsilawo ƒe agbagbadzedze nana ɖeɖi tea amesi menye du me mɔ o la ŋu.

english_verse: A country is in for trouble when its ruler is childish, and its leaders party all day long.
translation_verse: Anyigba, si ƒe fia nye ɖevi, eye eƒe amegãwo ma ŋdi ɖe nuɖuɖu ŋu la, baba nɛ!

english_verse: But a nation will prosper when its ruler is mature, and its leaders don't party too much.
translation_verse: Woayra anyigba, siƒe fia nyee bubume, eye ete amegãwo ɖua nu ɖe eɖuɣi hena ŋusẽɖoɖo, eye menye hena nutsuɖuɖu o!

english_verse: Some people are too lazy to fix a leaky roof— then the house collapses.
translation_verse: Kuviawɔwɔ nana ɖaɖedziwo nyẽna ɖe eme, alɔ gblɔlɔ wɔwɔ nana xɔ ɖuɖuna.

english_verse: Eating and drinking make you feel happy, and money can buy everything you need.
translation_verse: Ɖe woɖaa nuɖuɖu hena dzidzɔkpɔkpɔ, wein doa dzidzɔ na agbe, eye gae wotsɔna kpɔa nuwo katãe.

english_verse: Don't let yourself think about cursing the king; don't curse the rich, not even in secret. A little bird might hear and tell everything.
translation_verse: Megado ɖiŋu na fia le wò tamesusuwo me o, eye megado ɖiŋu na kesinɔtɔ le wò xɔgã me o, elabena dziƒoxeviwo atso gbeɖiɖi la ayii, eye xewo aɖato nya la.

english_verse: Be generous, and someday you will be rewarded.
translation_verse: Na wò abolo nato tɔ dzi yii, elabena àgakpɔe le ŋkeke geɖewo megbe.

english_verse: Share what you have with seven or eight others, because you never know when disaster may strike.
translation_verse: Ma nu ɖe akpa adre, ɖe akpa enyi, elabena menya dzɔgbevɔ̃e ka le anyigba dzi va ge o.

english_verse: If you worry about the weather and don't plant seeds, you won't harvest a crop.
translation_verse: Amesi le to lém ɖe ya ŋu la, maƒã nuku o, eye amesi le ŋku lém ɖe alilikpo ŋu la, maŋe nu o.

english_verse: No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
translation_verse: Alesi menya ya toƒe kple alesi ƒuwo va wona ɖe dɔ me na funɔ o la, nenema mèdze si Mawu, amesi wɔ nuwo katã la ƒe dɔwɔwɔwo o.

english_verse: Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce. Youth and Old Age
translation_verse: Ƒã wò nukuwo le ŋdi, eye megadzudzɔ le ɣetrɔ me o; elabena mènya kae le wɔwɔ ge o, eɖanye asi alo ekeme alo woa kple eve lae le nyonyo ge o.

english_verse: Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun.
translation_verse: Kekeli nyo, eye ɣe kpɔkpɔ vivia ŋku nu.

english_verse: Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
translation_verse: Elabena ne amegbetɔ nɔ agbe ƒe geɖe la, nekpɔ dzidzɔ le wo katã me, eye wòanɔ ŋku ɖom vivitidogbe dzi be, wole agbɔ sɔ ge; nusiwo katã le vavam la, toflokowoe.

english_verse: Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
translation_verse: Ɖekakpui, kpɔ dzidzɔ le wò ɖekakpuime, na wò dzi naɖu agbe le wò ɖekakpui ŋkekewo me, eye nazɔ ɖe wò dzi ƒe toƒewo kple nusi wò ŋku kpɔ la nu; ke nyae be, Mawu le kplɔwò ge ava ʋɔnui le nusiawo katã ta.

english_verse: Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_verse: Ɖe dziku da le wò dzi ŋu, eye vɔ̃ neƒo asa na wò ŋutilã; elabena ɖekakpui me nɔnɔ kple ŋutsu me nónɔ toflokowoe.

english_verse: Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
translation_verse: Ɖo ŋku wɔwòla dzi le wò ɖekakpuiŋkekewo me, hafi ne ŋkeke vɔ̃wo nava, eye ƒe, siwo ŋu nele gbɔgblɔ ge le be, womedze ye ŋu o la, nagogo;

english_verse: Someday the light of the sun and the moon and the stars will all seem dim to you. Rain clouds will remain over your head.
translation_verse: hafi ne ɣe, ɣleti kple ɣletiviwo naɖo viviti, eye alilikpo nagatrɔ ava le tsidzadza megbe;

english_verse: Your body will grow feeble, your teeth will decay, and your eyesight fail.
translation_verse: esime aƒe ŋu dzalawo dzona nyanyanya, eye ŋutsu kakowo xana gobaa, nyɔnu wɔtulawo dzudzɔa dɔwɔwɔ, elabena womegasɔ gbɔ o; esime fesrenukpɔlawo ƒe mo ɖoa viviti,

english_verse: The noisy grinding of grain and the voices of singers will be shut out by your deaf ears, but even the song of a bird will keep you awake.
translation_verse: eye wodoa ʋɔtru, siwo lrɔ ɖe abla me, elabena wɔtutu megale ɖiɖim sesĩe o, eye wofɔna, ne xevi ƒe gbe tete ɖi, eye nyɔnu hadzilawo ƒe gbeme xena;

english_verse: You will be afraid to climb up a hill or walk down a road. Your hair will turn as white as almond blossoms. You will feel lifeless and drag along like an old grasshopper. We each go to our eternal home, and the streets here are filled with those who mourn.
translation_verse: togbɛwo hã dzia ŋɔ na ame, eye ŋɔdzi nɔa mawo dzi; wotsria azi, eye ʋetsuviwo tea texlolo, eye nuɖuɖu medzroa ame o; elabena amegbetɔ yia eƒe aƒe mavɔ me, eye konyifalawo nɔa yiyim le kpɔɖome;

english_verse: The silver cord snaps, the golden bowl breaks; the water pitcher is smashed, and the pulley at the well is shattered.
translation_verse: hafi ne klosaloka natso, eye sikagba nagbã, trekpezi nafli le vudo to, eye tsidumɔ̃ nakaka;

english_verse: So our bodies return to the earth, and the life-giving breath returns to God.
translation_verse: hafi ne ekewɔ nagatrɔ yi anyigba, si wònye tsã la gbɔ, eye gbɔgbɔ la nagbugbɔ ayi Mawu, amesi tsɔe na la gbɔ. Mawuvɔvɔ̃ enye nufiafiawo katã ƒe blibotɔ.

english_verse: Nothing makes sense. I have seen it all— nothing makes sense. Respect and Obey God
translation_verse: Toflokowo ƒe tofloko! Nyagblɔla be: Nuwo kalã toflokowoe!

english_verse: I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied.
translation_verse: Nyagblɔla sia la menye nunyala ko o, ke boŋ eda sidzedze dukɔ la, edo nu kpɔ, edi nu gɔme, eye wòdo lo geɖewo.

english_verse: Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
translation_verse: Nyagblɔla la di nya viviwo be, yeakpɔ, eye nyateƒenya, siwo woŋlɔ ɖi la, wole eteƒe.

english_verse: Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together.
translation_verse: Nunyalawo ƒe nyawo le abe ŋu kple gatagbadza, si woƒo ɖe nu ene. Kplɔla ɖekae ɖo amewo woƒo wo nu ƒu.

english_verse: My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these. There is no end to books, and too much study will wear you out.
translation_verse: Hekpe ɖe esia ŋu la, vinye, na woaxlɔ̃ nu wò! Agbalẽ geɖe wɔwɔ mekpɔa seƒeɖo o, eye nusɔsrɔ̃ geɖe ɖe wòtea ɖeɖi ŋufilã ŋu.

english_verse: Everything you were taught can be put into a few words: Respect and obey God! This is what life is all about.
translation_verse: Mina míase nyaawo kalã ƒe taƒonya be: Vɔ̃ Mawu, eye nalé eƒe seawo me ɖe asi; elabena esia nye amegbetɔtvo katã tɔ!

english_verse: God will judge everything we do, even what is done in secret, whether good or bad.
translation_verse: Elabena Mawu le nuwɔwɔwo katã, siwo ɣla la, he ge ava ʋɔnui, eɖanye nyui alo vɔ̃ o.

english_verse: This is Solomon's most beautiful song. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Salomo hawo ƒe ha.

english_verse: Kiss me tenderly! Your love is better than wine,
translation_verse: Etsɔ wo nu gbugbɔ nu nam, elabena wo lɔlɔ̃ nyo wu wein.

english_verse: and you smell so sweet. All the young women adore you; the very mention of your name is like spreading perfume. *
translation_verse: Wò ami le ya ɖem nyuie; wo ŋkɔ le abe ami, si wowu ene, eyata ɖetugbiwo lɔ̃a wo nya ɖo.

english_verse: Hurry, my king! Let's hurry. Take me to your home. The Young Women Speak: We are happy for you! And we praise your love even more than wine. She Speaks: Young women of Jerusalem, it is only right that you should adore him.
translation_verse: Kplɔm yii, na míaɖe abla! Fia la kplɔm yi eƒe xɔ me. Míatso aseye, eye míakpɔ dzidzɔ, eye míakafu wò lɔlɔ̃ wu wein; amewo lɔ̃a wò ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: My skin is dark and beautiful, like a tent in the desert or like Solomon's curtains.
translation_verse: Yerusalem-nyɔnuviwo, menye ame yi, gake menye abe Kedar ƒe agbadɔwo kple Salomo ƒe kuntruwo ene.

english_verse: Don't stare at me just because the sun has darkened my skin. My brothers were angry with me; they made me work in the vineyard, and so I neglected my complexion.
translation_verse: Migamɔ kpɔyem be, menya alea o, elabena ɣee ɖum. Danye viŋutsuwo ɖo dɔmedzoe ɖe ŋunye; wotsɔm ɖo weingbledzɔlae, ke nyemedzɔ nye ŋutɔ nye weingble ŋu o.

english_verse: My darling, I love you! Where do you feed your sheep and let them rest at noon? Don't let the other shepherds think badly of me. I'm not one of those women who shamelessly follow after shepherds. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Wò, amesi nye lunɔ lɔ̃na, gblɔe nam dzro: Afikanènyia lãwo le, eye afika wotsyɔa akɔ ɖo le ŋɖɔ me? Nukaŋuti manɔ tsa glãla tsam le hawòviwo ƒe lãhawo gbɔ?

english_verse: My dearest, if you don't know, just follow the path of the sheep. Then feed your young goats near the shepherds' tents.
translation_verse: Wò tugbedzɛ le nyɔnuwo dome, ne mènyae o la, ekema do go, eye naɖo lãhawo ƒe afɔ, eye nanyi wò gbɔ̃viwo le lãkplɔlawo ƒe agbadɔwo gbɔ!

english_verse: You move as gracefully as the pony that leads the chariot of the king.
translation_verse: Xɔ̃nye, èle abe nye sɔnɔ le Farao ƒe tasiaɖam ŋu ene.

english_verse: Earrings add to your beauty, and you wear a necklace of precious stones.
translation_verse: Dzonu le tonu na wò nyuie, eye adzagba le kɔ na wò.

english_verse: Let's make you some jewelry of gold, woven with silver. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Míatu sikakɔsɔkɔsɔ kple klosalokpeviwo na wò.

english_verse: My king, while you were on your couch, my aroma was a magic charm.
translation_verse: Esime fia la bɔbɔ nɔ eƒe ablegɔ me la, nye gbe ʋeʋẽewo ɖe ya.

english_verse: My darling, you are perfume between my breasts;
translation_verse: Nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ le ahe miregoe le akɔnu nam ene.

english_verse: you are flower blossoms from the gardens of En-Gedi. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ nye koferseƒoƒo nam le Engedi-weingblewo me.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— your eyes are those of a dove. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Edze tugbe, xɔ̃nye, èdze tugbe loo! Wò ŋkuwo le abe ahɔne ƒe ŋkuwo ene.

english_verse: My love, you are handsome, truly handsome— the fresh green grass will be our wedding bed
translation_verse: Nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ, èdze ɖeka, eye nènyo; mía dɔƒe ɖe ama.

english_verse: in the shade of cedar and cypress trees.
translation_verse: Míaƒe xɔ ƒe daɖedziwo nye sedertiwo, eye míaƒe xɔmeɖoʋuƒowo nye fɔfɔlĩ.

english_verse: I am merely a rose from the land of Sharon, a lily from the valley. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Nyee nye seƒoƒo le Saron kple dzogbenya le baliwo me.

english_verse: My darling, when compared with other young women, you are a lily among thorns. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Alesi dzogbenya noa aŋɔka mea le nenema xɔ̃nye le nyɔnuviwo domee.

english_verse: And you, my love, are an apple tree among trees of the forest. Your shade brought me pleasure; your fruit was sweet.
translation_verse: Alesi atɔlɔŋutiti le avemetiwo domee la, nenema nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ le ɖekakpuiwo domee. Melɔ̃a eƒe vɔvɔli te nɔnɔ, eye eƒe kutsetsewo vivina le nye nu me.

english_verse: You led me to your banquet room and showered me with love.
translation_verse: Ekplɔm yi weinxɔ me, eye lɔlɔ̃ enye eƒe aflaga le dzinye.

english_verse: Refresh and strengthen me with raisins and apples. I am hungry for love!
translation_verse: Mi tso weintsetsebolo de agbe ŋunye, eye mitsɔ atɔtɔŋuti fa dzi nam, ale bena lɔlɔ̃ de dɔ la me nam.

english_verse: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
translation_verse: Etsɔ eƒe mía de nye ta te, eye wòtsɔ eƒe nuɖusi kple kɔ nam.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles never to awaken love before it is ready. Winter Is Past She Speaks:
translation_verse: Yerusalem-nyɔnuviwo, meta sãde alo zinɔ le gbe me ne mi: Miganyɔ lɔlɔ̃ o, migaʋuʋui o, vaseɖe esime wòadze eya ŋutɔ ŋu hafi!

english_verse: I hear the voice of the one I love, as he comes leaping over mountains and hills
translation_verse: Nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ ŋkɔ le ɖiɖim! Kpɔ ɖa, eya nye ekem gbɔna; ele kpo dzom flɔ towo, eye wòle kpo tim flɔ togbɛwo.

english_verse: like a deer or a gazelle. Now he stands outside our wall, looking through the window
translation_verse: Nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ le abe sãde alo zivi ene, ele tsitre ɖe míaƒe gli te xoxo. Ele nu kpɔm to fesre nu, eye wòɖo ŋku ɖe adzrala nu.

english_verse: and speaking to me. He Speaks: My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
translation_verse: Nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ xɔ edzi gblɔ nam bena: Xɔ̃nye, tso; nye tugbedzɛ, va!

english_verse: Winter is past, the rain has stopped;
translation_verse: Elabena vuvɔŋɔli yi aƒe, tsidzadza ke, eye enu yi.

english_verse: flowers cover the earth, it's time to sing. The cooing of doves is heard in our land.
translation_verse: Seƒoƒowo ɖo ɖe anyigba dzi, weinkawo ŋu ɖeɣi ɖo, eye wole akpakpa ƒe xɔxlɔ sem le míaƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: Fig trees are bearing fruit, while blossoms on grapevines fill the air with perfume. My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
translation_verse: Gboti ƒe tsetsewo ɖe asi ɖiɖi me, eye weinka ƒe seƒoƒowo le ya ɖem nyuie. Tso, xɔnye, nye tugbedzɛ, va!

english_verse: You are my dove hiding among the rocks on the side of a cliff. Let me see how lovely you are! Let me hear the sound of your melodious voice.
translation_verse: Nye ahɔne le kpetowo me, le agawo ƒe globoeaƒe; na makpɔ ŋkuwò me, na mase wò gbe! Elabena wò gbe vivina, eye ŋkuwò me nyo.

english_verse: Our vineyards are in blossom; we must catch the little foxes that destroy the vineyards. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Milé abeiwo na mi, abeiviwo, siwo gblẽa weingblewo; elabena míaƒe weingblewo ƒo se.

english_verse: My darling, I am yours, and you are mine, as you feed your sheep among the lilies.
translation_verse: Tɔnyee nye nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ la, eye nye hã menye etɔ, eya amesi nyia lãwo le dzogbenyawo me.

english_verse: Pretend to be a young deer dancing on mountain slopes until daylight comes and shadows fade away.
translation_verse: Nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ, trɔ gbɔ, hafi anyinu nafa, eye vɔvɔli nu nayi, eye nanɔ abe sãde alo zivi le atike ʋeʋẽe towo dzi ene!

english_verse: While in bed at night, I reached for the one I love with heart and soul. I looked for him, but he wasn't there.
translation_verse: Meɖi amesi nye luʋɔ lɔna la, le nye aha dzi le zã me, medii nyemekpɔe o.

english_verse: So I searched through the town for the one I love. I looked on every street, but he wasn't there.
translation_verse: Eyata mafa aɖatsa le dua me le ablɔ me kple kpɔdomewo, ne madi amesi nye luʋɔ lɔ̃na la! Medii, ke nyemekpɔe o.

english_verse: I even asked the guards patrolling the town, “Have you seen the one I love so much?”
translation_verse: Dzɔla, siwo le tsatsam le dua me la, do gom. „Míekpɔ amesi nye luʋɔ lɔ̃na la oa?“

english_verse: Right after that, I found him. I held him and would not let go until I had taken him to the home of my mother.
translation_verse: Nyemekpɔ to wo ŋu yi o, tete mekpɔ amesi nye luʋɔ lɔ̃na la. Melée, eye megbe asiɖeɖe le eŋu, vaseɖe esime mekplɔe va danye ƒe me, va nɔnye ƒe xɔ mee.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles, never to awaken love before it is ready. The Groom and the Wedding Party Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Yerusalem-nyɔnuviwo, meta sàde alo zinɔ le gbe me na mi: Miganyɔ lɔlɔ̃ o, mígaʋuʋui o, vaseɖe esime wòadze eya ŋutɔ ŋu hafi! Xɔlɔ̃ ƒe atsyɔ̃ɖoɖo.

english_verse: What do we see approaching from the desert like a cloud of smoke? With it comes the sweet smell of spices, including myrrh and frankincense.
translation_verse: Amekae nye ekem tso gbe me gbɔna abe dzudzɔ babla ene, eye atike ʋeʋẽe, dzudzɔ ʋeʋée donu kple nudzralawo ƒe atike vovovowo le ya ɖem le eŋu?

english_verse: It is King Solomon carried on a throne, surrounded by sixty of Israel's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Kpo da, Salomo ƒe apakae! Kalẽtɔ blaade tso Israel ƒe kalẽtɔwo dome ƒo xlãe.

english_verse: Each of them wears a sword. They are experts at fighting, even in the dark.
translation_verse: Wo katã wobi de aʋawɔwɔ me, eye woƒe asi le yi dzi; amesiame ta yi de aklito le zã me ŋɔdzi la.

english_verse: The throne is made of trees from Lebanon.
translation_verse: Fia Salomo na wotso Libanon-ti kpa atiklãe.

english_verse: Its posts are silver, the back is gold, and the seat is covered with purple cloth. You women of Jerusalem have taken great care to furnish the inside.
translation_verse: Ele alɔwo nye klosalo, eye medeƒe nye sika, anyinɔƒe nye aɖabɛ, eye Yerusalem nyɔnuviwo ƒe lɔlɔ̃ do atsiã ne ɖe eme gome.

english_verse: Now come and see the crown given to Solomon by his mother on his happy wedding day.
translation_verse: Mi Zion-nyɔnuviwo, mido va, ne míakpɔ fia Salomo le fiakuku, si dadaa ɖɔ nɛ la me le eƒe srɔ̃ɖegbe, le eƒe dzi ƒe dzidzɔkpɔgbe!

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— as you look through your veil, your eyes are those of a dove. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
translation_verse: Èdze tugbe, xɔ̃nye, èdze tugbe ŋutɔ. Wò ŋkuwo nye ahɔne ƒe ŋkuwo le moxevɔ la me. Wò ɖa le abe gbɔ̃hawoe tsyɔ akɔ anyi de Gilead-to kɔgo ene.

english_verse: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
translation_verse: Wò aɖuwo le abe alẽha, si woke tu na tete, eye wodo tso tsileƒe la ene; wo katã wonye venɔwo, eye wo dometɔa ɖeke metsi ko o.

english_verse: Your lips are crimson cords, your mouth is shapely; behind your veil are hidden beautiful rosy cheeks.
translation_verse: Wò nuyiwo le abe ka dzẽ ene, eye wò nu dze ani; wò tonuƒuiwo le dzedzem le moxevɔ me abe yevuboɖa, si me wole ene.

english_verse: Your neck is more graceful than the tower of David, decorated with thousands of warriors' shields.
translation_verse: Wò ka le abe Dawid ƒe xɔ tsrala, si wotu bena gbetakpɔkpɔ ene Woku akpoxɔnu gagã akpe de eŋu, siwo katã nye kalẽtɔwo ƒe akpoxɔnuwo.

english_verse: Your breasts are perfect; they are twin deer feeding among lilies.
translation_verse: Wò nowo le abe sãdevi eve, zi venɔvi, siwo le gbe ɖum le dzogbenyawo me ene.

english_verse: I will hasten to those hills sprinkled with sweet perfume and stay there till sunrise.
translation_verse: Mayi atike ʋeʋẽe towo kple dzudzɔ ʋeʋẽe donu togbɛwo dzi, hafi anyinu nafa, eye vɔvɔli nu nayi.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely in every way.
translation_verse: Xɔ̃nye, nusianu nyo le ŋuwò, dzuƒea ɖeke mele ŋuwò o.

english_verse: My bride, together we will leave Lebanon! We will say goodbye to the peaks of Mount Amana, Senir, and Hermon, where lions and leopards live in the caves.
translation_verse: Ɖi kplim tso Libanon dzi, ŋugbetɔ, ɖi kplim tso Libanon dzi! Zɔ tso Amana ta me, tso Senir kple Xermon ta me, tso dzatawo nɔƒe kple lãkletowo dzi.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, you have stolen my heart! With one glance from your eyes and the glow of your necklace, you have stolen my heart.
translation_verse: Nɔvinyenyɔnu, nye ŋugbetɔ, ègblẽ tame nam, ètsɔ wò nukpɔkpɔ kple kɔsɔkɔsɔ, si le wò kɔdzonuwo me, gblẽ tame nam.

english_verse: Your love is sweeter than wine; the smell of your perfume is more fragrant than spices.
translation_verse: Nɔyinyenyɔnu, nye ŋugbetɔ, wò lɔlɔ̃ vivina loo! Wò lɔlɔ̃ nyo wu wein, eye wo ami ƒe ʋeʋẽ ƒo atike ʋeʋẽewo la.

english_verse: Your lips are a honeycomb; milk and honey flow from your tongue. Your dress has the aroma of cedar trees from Lebanon.
translation_verse: Ŋugbetɔ, anyitsi le tsyɔtsyɔm le nuyi ŋu na wò; anyitsi kple notsi le wò aɖe te; wò avɔwo me ƒe ʋeʋẽ le abe Libanon ƒe ʋeʋẽ ene.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, you are a garden, a fountain closed off to all others.
translation_verse: Nɔvinyenyɔnu, nye ŋugbetɔ enye abɔ, si ƒe ʋɔ wodo, vudo, si nu wotu nu do, kple tsidzɔƒe, si nu wotre.

english_verse: Your arms are vines, covered with delicious fruits and all sorts of spices— henna, nard,
translation_verse: Wò numiemiewo nye yevuboɖabɔ, si me kutsetse nyuiwo, koferseƒoƒo kple gbe ʋeʋẽewo,

english_verse: saffron, calamus, cinnamon, frankincense, myrrh, and aloes —all the finest spices.
translation_verse: gbe ʋeʋẽewo kple agumetaku, gbekee, botsyo kple dzudzɔ ʋeʋẽe dogbewo katã, mire kple aloe kpakple atike veviwo katã te.

english_verse: You are a spring in the garden, a fountain of pure water, and a refreshing stream from Mount Lebanon. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Abɔ me tsidzidzi, tsi gbagbe vudo kple tɔʋu, si si tso Libanon dzi la nènye.

english_verse: Let the north wind blow, the south wind too! Let them spread the aroma of my garden, so the one I love may enter and taste its delicious fruits.
translation_verse: Anyieheya, tso, eye dzieheya, va, naƒo ato nye abɔ me, ne eƒe ʋeʋẽ nagbagba di.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, I come to my garden and enjoy its spices. I eat my honeycomb and honey; I drink my wine and milk. Their Friends Speak: Eat and drink until you are drunk with love. Another Dream She Speaks:
translation_verse: Nɔvinyenyɔnu, nye ŋugbetɔ, meva nye abɔ me, meke nye mire kple atike ʋeʋẽewo, menyi nye anyixe kple anyitsi, meno nye wein kple nye notsi. Xɔ̃nyewo, miɖu nu, miano nu, nye lɔlɔ̃tɔwo, mino aha mu!

english_verse: I was asleep, but dreaming: The one I love was at the door, knocking and saying, “My darling, my very own, my flawless dove, open the door for me! My head is drenched with evening dew.”
translation_verse: Mele alɔ̃ dɔm, ke nye dzi le ŋute. Mido to, nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ le ʋɔ ƒom! Nɔvinyenyɔnu, xɔnye, nye ahɔne, nye ame dzadzɛ, ʋu ʋɔ nam! Elabena zãmu ƒo tame nam ƒũ, eye nye ɖa me yɔ fu kple dzadza.

english_verse: But I had already undressed and bathed my feet. Should I dress again and get my feet dirty?
translation_verse: Meɖe nye avɔwo ɖi, ɖe magatsɔ wo ataa? Meklɔ nye afɔwo, ɖe magaƒo ɖi woa?

english_verse: Then my darling's hand reached to open the latch, and my heart stood still.
translation_verse: Nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ do asi ɖe fesre nu, tete nye lãme gbagba yi ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: When I rose to open the door, my hands and my fingers dripped with perfume.
translation_verse: Mefa, be maʋu ʋɔa na nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ, eye ami ʋeʋẽe le tsyɔtsyɔm le asi ŋu nam, ami nenẽe tsrolo le ɖuɖum le nye asibide ŋu ɖe gameti ƒe asiléƒe ŋu.

english_verse: And I yearned for him while he spoke to me, but when I opened the door, my darling had disappeared. I searched and shouted, but I could not find him— there was no answer.
translation_verse: Meʋu ʋɔa na nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ, ke nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ trɔ dzo, ebu. Luʋɔ dzo le tanye, esime wòƒo nu. Medii, nyemekpɔe o; meyɔe, gake metɔ nam o.

english_verse: Then I was found by the guards patrolling the town and guarding the wall. They beat me up and stripped off my robe.
translation_verse: Dzɔla, siwo le tsatsam le dua me la do gom, woƒom de abi ŋunye; gli ŋu dzɔlawo ɖe taɖedzi le ŋunye.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, if you find the one I love, please say to him, “She is weak with desire.” Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Yerusalem-nyɔnuviwo, mele mi: Ne miekpɔ nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ la, mito nɛ be, lɔlɔ̃ de dɔ lã me nam!

english_verse: Most beautiful of women, why is the one you love more special than others? Why do you ask us to tell him how you feel? She Speaks:
translation_verse: Nyɔnuwo ƒe tughedzɛ, nuka wo lɔlɔ̃tɔ tso ƒo lɔlɔ̃tɔ bubuwo tae? Nuka wo lɔlɔ̃tɔ tsa ƒo lɔlɔ̃tɔ bubuwo tae, hafi nèta nu na mí alea?

english_verse: He is handsome and healthy, the most outstanding among ten thousand.
translation_verse: Nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ fu, eye wòbiã, eye wòƒo ame akpe nanewo la;

english_verse: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy, black as a raven.
translation_verse: eƒe ta enye sika nyuitɔ, eƒe ɖa le abe ɖeʋala, siwo dza ɖe anyi me ene, eye wònyɔ abe akpaviã ene;

english_verse: His eyes are a pair of doves bathing in a stream flowing with milk.
translation_verse: eƒe ŋkuwo le abe ahɔne le tɔʋu to ene, wole notsi, eye wosɔ ɖe ŋku to me;

english_verse: His face is a garden of sweet-smelling spices; his lips are lilies dripping with perfume.
translation_verse: eƒe alɔgo enye atike ʋeʋẽe kpo, si dzi atike ʋeʋẽe mie ɖo; eƒe nuyiwo nye dzogbenya, siwo le mire tsrolo tsyɔm;

english_verse: His arms are branches of gold covered with jewels; his body is ivory decorated with sapphires.
translation_verse: eƒe alɔwo nye sikati mlimɔwo, siwo ŋu woɖo Tarsis-kpewoe; eƒe ƒoɖo enye aɖaŋudɔ, si wotsɔ nyiɖu wɔe, eye wotsɔ safir ɖo atsyɔ̃ ɖe eŋu;

english_verse: His legs are columns of marble on feet of gold. He stands there majestic like Mount Lebanon and its choice cedar trees.
translation_verse: eƒe atawo nye kpe ɣi sɔti, siwo woɖo sikafɔ dzi; eƒe dzedzeme le abe Libanon ene, eye wonye nu vevi abe sederti ene;

english_verse: His kisses are sweet. I desire him so much! Young women of Jerusalem, he is my lover and friend.
translation_verse: vivi le eƒe nu me, eye eyama ɖze ani. Yerusalem-nyɔnuviwo, nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ lae nye esia: amesiae nye xɔ̃nye la!

english_verse: His kisses are sweet. I desire him so much! Young women of Jerusalem, he is my lover and friend.

english_verse: I was asleep, but dreaming: The one I love was at the door, knocking and saying, “My darling, my very own, my flawless dove, open the door for me! My head is drenched with evening dew.”
translation_verse: Mele alɔ̃ dɔm, ke nye dzi le ŋute. Mido to, nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ le ʋɔ ƒom! Nɔvinyenyɔnu, xɔnye, nye ahɔne, nye ame dzadzɛ, ʋu ʋɔ nam! Elabena zãmu ƒo tame nam ƒũ, eye nye ɖa me yɔ fu kple dzadza.

english_verse: But I had already undressed and bathed my feet. Should I dress again and get my feet dirty?
translation_verse: Meɖe nye avɔwo ɖi, ɖe magatsɔ wo ataa? Meklɔ nye afɔwo, ɖe magaƒo ɖi woa?

english_verse: Then my darling's hand reached to open the latch, and my heart stood still.
translation_verse: Nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ do asi ɖe fesre nu, tete nye lãme gbagba yi ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: When I rose to open the door, my hands and my fingers dripped with perfume.
translation_verse: Mefa, be maʋu ʋɔa na nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ, eye ami ʋeʋẽe le tsyɔtsyɔm le asi ŋu nam, ami nenẽe tsrolo le ɖuɖum le nye asibide ŋu ɖe gameti ƒe asiléƒe ŋu.

english_verse: My dearest, the cities of Tirzah and Jerusalem are not as lovely as you. Your charms are more powerful than all of the stars in the heavens.
translation_verse: Xɔ̃nye, èdze tugbe abe Tirza ene, ènye abe Yerusalem ene, eye nèdzia ŋɔ abe aʋakɔ ene.

english_verse: Turn away your eyes— they make me melt. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
translation_verse: Ɖe ŋku ɖa le ŋunye, elabena wole ŋɔ dzim nam! Wo ɖa le abe gbɔ̃hawoe tsyɔ akɔ anyi de Gilead kɔgo ene.

english_verse: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
translation_verse: Wo aɖuwo le abe alẽha, siwo do tso tsileƒe ene, wo katã wonye venɔwo, eye wo dometɔa ɖeke metsi ko o.

english_verse: Behind your veil are hidden beautiful rosy cheeks.
translation_verse: Wo tonuƒui le dzedzem le moxevɔ me abe yevuboɖa, si me wole ene.

english_verse: What if I could have sixty queens, eighty wives, and thousands of others!
translation_verse: Fiasrɔ̃wo le blaade, ahiãwo le blanyi, hekpe ɖe ɖetugbiwo ŋu kpaŋkpaŋ.

english_verse: You would be my only choice, my flawless dove, the favorite child of your mother. The young women, the queens, and all the others tell how excited you are as they sing your praises:
translation_verse: Ke ɖeka koe nye nye; ahɔne, nye ame dzadzɛ, eya nye dadaa ƒe tenu, nɔa ƒe nu vevi. Nyɔnuviwo kpɔe, eye woyrae, fiasrɔ̃wo kple ahiãwo kafui.

english_verse: “You are as majestic as the morning sky— glorious as the moon— blinding as the sun! Your charms are more powerful than all the stars above.” She Speaks:
translation_verse: Amekae le anyi me kpɔmahe agudzedze ene, nyo ahe ɣleti ene, dza abe ɣe ene, eye wòdzia ŋɔ ahe aoakɔwo ene?

english_verse: I went down to see if blossoms were on the walnut trees, grapevines, and fruit trees.
translation_verse: Meyi ɖe azibɔ me, ne makpɔ gbe fewo le bali me ɖa, eye maɖakpɔ be, weinkawo dze, eye yevuboɖatiwo ƒo se hã?

translation_verse: Trɔ, trɔ, Sulamit, trɔ, trɔ, ne míaɖe ŋku ɖe ŋuwò! Nuka míebe, yiewoakpɔ le Sulamit ŋu? Aʋaɣeɖuɖue loo?

english_verse: your navel is a wine glass filled to overflowing. Your body is full and slender like a bundle of wheat bound together by lilies.
translation_verse: Wo bubume vinyɔnu, aleke wò azɔlime nyo le atokota me ale? Wò kpenyenyẽ le ahe kɔdzonu, si nye aɖaŋua ƒe asinudɔwɔwɔ ene;

english_verse: Your head is held high like Mount Carmel; your hair is so lovely it holds a king prisoner.
translation_verse: wò kɔ enye nyiɖuxɔ tsrala; wò ŋkuwo le abe ta, si le Xesbon le Batrabim-gbo nu ene; wò ŋɔti le ahe Libanon ƒe xɔ tsrala, si ɖo ta Damasko ene.

english_verse: You are tall and slender like a palm tree, and your breasts are full.
translation_verse: Edze tugbe, eye nenyo loo, wò lɔlɔ̃, si nye vivisesego!

english_verse: Kissing you is more delicious than drinking the finest wine. How wonderful and tasty! She Speaks:
translation_verse: Mebe, made deti la dzi, eye malé eƒe alɔwo. Wò nowo nenye weinkpo le weinka ŋu, eye wò ŋɔli ƒe ʋeʋẽ neɖi atɔtɔŋuti tɔ!

english_verse: My darling, I am yours, and you desire me.
translation_verse: Wò nu me nenye wen nyuitɔ, si ato nuyi kple aɖu dzi na nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ wɔli.

english_verse: Let's stroll through the fields and sleep in the villages.
translation_verse: Nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ tɔ menye, eye yonyeme mɔ dim wòle.

english_verse: Perfume from the magic flower fills the air, my darling. Right at our doorstep I have stored up for you all kinds of tasty fruits.
translation_verse: Míafɔ ŋdi kanya ayi weingblewo me, ne míakpɔ be, weinkaawo dze, seƒoƒoawo ke, eye yevuboɖatiawo ƒo se hã? Afima matsɔ nye lɔlɔ̃ na wò le.

english_verse: If you were my brother, I could kiss you whenever we happen to meet, and no one would say I did wrong.
translation_verse: Oo, esi nahanɔ nam abe nɔvinyeŋutsu, si no danye ƒe no ene ɖe! Anye ne mekpɔ wo le kpɔdome la, magbugbɔ nu na wò, eye amea ɖeke maɖo vlom o;

english_verse: I could take you to the home of my mother, who taught me all I know. I would give you delicious wine and fruit juice as well.
translation_verse: anye ne makplɔ wò ayi danye ƒe me, ayi nɔnye ƒe xɔ mee. Mana atike ʋeʋẽe ƒe wein kple yevuboɖaha wò nano.

english_verse: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
translation_verse: Etsɔ eƒe mía de nye ta te, eye wòtsɔ eƒe nuɖusi kple kɔ nam.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me never to awaken love before it is ready. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Yerusalem-nyɔnuviwo, meta mi: Miganyɔ lɔlɔ̃ o, migaʋuʋui o, vaseɖe esime wòadze eya ŋutɔ ŋu hafi!

english_verse: Who is this young woman coming in from the desert and leaning on the shoulder of the one she loves? She Speaks: I stirred up your passions under the apple tree where you were born.
translation_verse: Ameka nye ekem tso gbe me gbɔna heziɔ ɖe eƒe lɔlɔ̃tɔ ŋu? Atɔtɔŋutiti le menyɔ wò le; afima dawò se veve dzi wò ɖo, afima nɔwò lé ku dzi wò ɖo.

english_verse: Always keep me in your heart and wear this bracelet to remember me by. The passion of love bursting into flame is more powerful than death, stronger than the grave.
translation_verse: Tsɔm wɔ ŋkɔslgɛ ɖe wò dzi ŋu kple ŋkɔsigɛ de wò asi! Elabena lɔlɔ̃ tri akɔ wu ku, eye ŋuʋaʋã se wu tsleƒe, eƒe bibi le abe dzo ƒe bibi ene, Yehowa ƒe dzoƒade wònye!

english_verse: Love cannot be drowned by oceans or floods. It cannot be bought— any offer would be scorned no matter how great. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Tsi geɖe mate ŋu atsi lɔlɔ̃ o, eye tɔsisi gãwo mate ŋu akplɔe adzoe o. Ne amea ɖe be, yeatsɔ eƒe aƒe me kesinɔnuwo katã ana ɖe lɔlɔ̃ ta la, ɖeko woade alɔme te eŋu.

english_verse: We have a little sister whose breasts are not yet formed. If someone asks to marry her, what should we do?
translation_verse: Nɔvinyɔnu suea ɖe le mia si, mekpɔ te no haɖe o. Aleke míawɔ na mía nɔvmyɔnu la, le gbesigbe woabia eta?

english_verse: She isn't a wall that we can defend behind a silver shield. Neither is she a room that we can protect behind a wooden door. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Nenye gbe wonye la, míatsɔ klosalo atɔ kpɔ ɖe edzi, eye nenye agboe wònye la, míatsɔ sederʋuƒowo aklãe.

english_verse: I am a wall around a city, my breasts are towers, and just looking at me brings him great pleasure.
translation_verse: Gli menye, eye nye nowo le ahe xɔ tsralawo ene; eye mekpɔ ŋutifafa le eŋku me.

english_verse: Solomon has a vineyard at Baal-Hamon, which he rents to others for a thousand pieces of silver each.
translation_verse: Weingble le Salomo si le Baal-Hamon; etsɔ weingble la ɖe asi na dzikpɔlawo be, wo dome amesiame nana klosalo sekel akpe ɖeka ɖe kutsetseawo ta.

english_verse: My vineyard is mine alone! Solomon can keep his silver and the others can keep their share of the profits. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Nye weingble le nye ŋutɔ asinye me, Salomo, tɔwòe nye sekel akpe ɖeka, eye alafa eve enye kutsetse dzikpɔlawo tɔ!

english_verse: You are in the garden with friends all around. Let me hear your voice! She Speaks:
translation_verse: Wò nyɔnu, si nɔa abɔ me, xɔlɔwo ƒu to anyi ɖe wò gbe ŋu; na masee!

english_verse: Hurry to me, my darling! Run faster than a deer to mountains of spices.
translation_verse: Nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ, ɖe afɔ mi me, eye nanɔ abe sãde alo zivi, si le atike ʋeʋẽe towo dzi ene!

english_verse: I am Isaiah, the son of Amoz. And this is the message that I was given about Judah and Jerusalem when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah: A Guilty Nation
translation_verse: Esia nye ŋutega, si Yesaya, Amoz vi la, kpo le Yuda kple Yerusalem ŋu le Yuda-fiawo Uziya, Yotam, Axaz kple Xizkiya ŋɔli.

english_verse: The Lord has said, “Listen, heaven and earth! The children I raised have turned against me.
translation_verse: Mi dziƒowo, misee, eye anyigba, ƒu to anyi; elabena Yehowa le nu ƒom bena: Menyi viwo wotsi, eye medo wo ɖe dzi, ke wodze aglã ɖe ŋunye.

english_verse: Oxen and donkeys know who owns and feeds them, but my people won't ever learn.”
translation_verse: Nyitsu nyaa etoa, eye tedzi nyaa eƒe aƒetɔ ƒe lãto; ke Israel menyae o, eye nye dukɔ melé ŋku ɖe eŋu o.

english_verse: Israel, you are a sinful nation loaded down with guilt. You are wicked and corrupt and have turned from the Lord, the holy God of Israel.
translation_verse: Baba na mi anyigba dzi nɔlawo, dukɔ, si dzi fɔɖiɖi li kɔ ɖo, vodalawo ƒe viwo, vi gbegblẽ wo! Wogblẽ Yehowa ɖi, wodo ɖiŋu na Israel ƒe kɔkɔeto la, eye wogbugbɔ ɖe megbe.

english_verse: Why be punished more? Why not give up your sin? Your head is badly bruised, and you are weak all over.
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti woanɔ mia ƒoƒo dzi, esi miele godzedze dzi ɖaa? Ta blibo la xɔ abi, eye nu te dzi blibo la ŋu belibeli.

english_verse: From your head to your toes there isn't a healthy spot. Bruises, cuts, and open sores go without care or oil to ease the pain. A Country in Ruins
translation_verse: Teƒe nyuia ɖeke mele eŋu o, tso afɔƒo me vaseɖe dzodome: abi kple dodro kpakple ƒoƒo yeye; womeyɔ tsi le eme o, womeblae o, eye womeɖe ami ɖee wobɔbɔ o.
