translation_verse: Eye woanye dzidzɔ ŋkɔ kafukafu kple adegbeƒoƒo nam le anyigba dzi dukɔwo katã dome, amesiwo ne wose nu nyui, siwo katã mawɔ na wo ŋkɔ la, ŋɔdzi alẽ wo, eye woadzo nyanyanya le nu nyui kple ŋutifafa, siwo katã mena wo la ŋuti.

english_verse: Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Teƒe sia, si ŋu miele gbɔgblɔm le be, ezu aƒedo, amegbetɔwo kple lãwo megali o, Yuda-duwo kple Yerusalem-kpɔdomeewo tsi ƒuƒlu, eye amegbetɔwo kple lãwo megali o la,

english_verse: happy voices and the sounds of parties and wedding celebrations. And when people come to my temple to offer sacrifices to thank me, you will hear them say: “We praise you, Lord All-Powerful! You are good to us, and your love never fails.” The land will once again be productive.
translation_verse: afima wòase aseyetsogbe kple dzidzɔgbe, ŋugbetɔsrɔ̃ ƒe gbe kple ŋugbetɔ ƒe gbe, amesiwo le gbɔgblɔm be: Mikafu Yehowa Zebaot, elabena Yehowa ƒe dome nyo, eye eƒe amenuveve li tegbee“ la ƒe gbe le; elabena magaɖo anyigba la te abe tsã ene, Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Now it is empty, without people or animals. But when that time comes, shepherds will take care of their flocks in pastures near every town in the hill country, in the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert, in the land of the Benjamin tribe, and around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord's Wonderful Promise
translation_verse: eye alẽwo agato wo xlẽla ƒe asi te ayi le to dzi duwo, bali me duwo kple dzieheduwo me le Benyamin-nyigba dzi kple Yerusalem-nutowo kple Yuda-duwo me, Yehowa ye gblɔe. Nyagblɔɖi le Mesia ŋuti.

english_verse: The Lord said: I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Kpɔ ɖa, ŋkeke li gbɔna, eye mawo nya nyui, si megblɔ ɖe Israel ƒe aƒe kple Yuda ƒe aƒe ŋu la dzi.

english_verse: I promise that the time will come when I will appoint a king from the family of David, a king who will be honest and rule with justice.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke mawo me le ɣemaɣi la mana atidzedze dzɔdzɔe nadze na Dawid, eye woawo nu dzɔdzɔe, si le eteƒe le anyigba dzi.

english_verse: In those days, Judah will be safe; Jerusalem will have peace and will be named, “The Lord Gives Justice.”
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke mawo me la woaɖe Yuda, eye Yerusalem anɔ anyi bɔkɔɔ, eye ŋkɔ, si woayɔ nɛ la, anye „Yehowa míaƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye.“

english_verse: The king of Israel will be one of David's descendants,
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Dawid ƒe amesi abɔbɔ nɔ Israel ƒe fiazikpui dzi la, mave gbeɖe o;

english_verse: and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
translation_verse: eye amesi asa numevɔ, atɔ dzo nuɖuvɔ, eye wòasa akpedavɔ le ŋkunye me ɣesiaɣi la, mave le nunɔla, siwo nye Lewi-viwo dome gbeɖe o. Nyagblɔɖi le Mawu ƒe nubabla mavɔ la ŋu.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va na Yeremya bena:

english_verse: I, the Lord, have an agreement with day and night, so they always come at the right time. You can't break the agreement I made with them,
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Ne miate ŋu atu nye nusi mebia kple ŋkeke kple zã, ale be ŋkeke kple zã maganɔ anyi le wo ŋɔli o la,

english_verse: and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel,
translation_verse: ekema nye nusi mebia kple nye dɔla Dawid la atu, ale be via ɖeke mana esi, si anye fia ɖe eƒe fiazikpui dzi o; nenema ke nye nusi mebia kple nunɔla, siwo nye Lewi-viwo, amesiwo le subɔyem la, hã atui.

english_verse: and there will be more descendants of David and of the priests from the Levi tribe than stars in the sky or grains of sand on the beach.
translation_verse: Alesi dziƒo ŋu nuwo mele xexlẽ me o, eye ƒutake mele dzidze me o la, nenema ke madzi nye dɔla Dawid kple nye subɔla Lewi-viwo ƒe ƒome ɖe dzii.

english_verse: The Lord also said:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va na Yeremya bena:

english_verse: You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
translation_verse: Mèdze si nya, si gblɔm dukɔ sia le bena: „Yehowa gbe ƒome eve, si wòda“ la oa? Ale wole alɔme ɖem le nye dukɔ ŋu, eye megaɖi dukɔ le wo ŋku me o.

english_verse: Jeremiah, I will never break my agreement with the day and the night or let the sky and the earth stop obeying my commands.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Ɖe nye nusi mebia kple ŋkeke kple zã meli ke, eye meɖo dziƒo kple anyigba ƒe ɖoɖowo o la,

english_verse: In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
translation_verse: anye ne magbe Yakob kple nye dɔla Dawid ƒe ƒome, ale be nyemaɖe dziɖula tso eƒe ƒome aɖo Abraham, Isak kple Yakob ƒe ƒome la nu o. Elabena megale wo ɖo ge te, eye makpɔ nublanui na wo.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar had a large army made up of people from every kingdom in his empire. He and his army were attacking Jerusalem and all the nearby towns, when the Lord told me
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe gbe, si va na Yeremya, esime Babel-fia Nebukadnezar kple eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la, anyigba dzi fiaɖuƒe, siwo katã nye eteviwo, kple dukɔwo katã lé aʋa wɔm kple Yerusalem kpakple eƒe duwo katã la, enye si:

english_verse: to say to King Zedekiah: I am the Lord, and I am going to let Nebuchadnezzar capture this city and burn it down.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Yi ɖagblɔ na Yuda-fia Zedekiya bena: Yehowa be: Kpɔ da, matsɔ du sia ade asi na Babel-fia, ne wòatɔ dzoe.

english_verse: You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Màge le esi me o, ke boŋ woalé wò atsɔ ade asi nɛ kokoko, wò ŋkuwo akpa Babel-fia ƒe ŋkuwo, miaƒo nu kple mia nɔewo, eye ayi Babel.

english_verse: Zedekiah, I promise that you won't die in battle.
translation_verse: Ke Yuda-fia Zedekiya se Yehowa ƒe nya. Ale Yehowa gblɔ ɖe ŋuwò enye si: Yi mawu wò o;

english_verse: You will die a peaceful death. People will mourn when you die, and they will light bonfires in your honor, just as they did for your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you.
translation_verse: ke boŋ àku le ŋutifafa me, eye woaɖo dzo na wò abe fofowò, fia xoxoawo, amesiwo do ŋgɔ na wò la ƒe ame kuku dzo ene, eye wòafa na wò be „ao, aƒetɔ“; nyee gblɔ nya sia, Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: I went to Zedekiah and told him what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Eye nyagblɔɖila Yeremya gblɔ nya siawo katã na Yuda-fia Zedekiya le Yerusalem,

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king of Babylonia was trying to break through the walls of Lachish, Azekah, and Jerusalem, the only three towns of Judah that had not been captured. The People Break a Promise
translation_verse: esime Babel-fia ƒe aʋakɔ le aʋa wɔm kple Yerusalem kple Yuda-du, siwo katã kpɔtɔ ɖi, siwo nye Laxis kple Aseka; elabena woawo nye du sesẽwo kpɔtɔ le Yuda-duwo dome.

english_verse: King Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Jerusalem made an agreement to free all Hebrew men and women who were slaves. No Jew would keep another as a slave. And so, all the Jewish slaves were given their freedom.
translation_verse: Amegãwo katã kple dukɔ blibo la ɖo to, eye woɖo nubabla me be, yewo dome amesiame naɖe asi le eƒe kluvi kple kosivi ŋu, ne womagawɔ kluvidɔ na yewo azɔ o; eye woɖo to heɖe asi le wo ŋu.

english_verse: But those slave owners changed their minds and forced their former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Ke emegbe la wogakplɔ kluviawo kple kosiviawo, siwo ŋu woɖe asi le la vɛ, eye wozi wo dzi be, woanye kluviwo kple kosiviwo.

english_verse: That's when the Lord told me to say to the people:
translation_verse: Tete Yehowa ƒe gbe va na Yeremya bena:

english_verse: I am the Lord God of Israel, and I made an agreement with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, where they had been slaves.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Mebia nu kple mia fofowo le gbesigbe mekplɔ wo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi tso kluvinyenye ƒe me la gblɔ bena:

english_verse: As part of this agreement, you must let a Hebrew slave go free after six years of service. Your ancestors did not obey me,
translation_verse: Le ƒe adre megbe la mia dome amesiame naɖe asi le nɔvia Hebritɔ, si tso eɖokui ƒle nɛ la ŋuti; nesubɔ wò ƒe ade, emegbe nade asi le eŋu wòadzo le gbɔwò. Ke mia fofowo meɖo tom o, eye womeƒu to anyi o.

english_verse: but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Emegbe miegatrɔ, eye miegblẽ ko ɖo na nye ŋkɔ, mia dome amesiame gakplɔ eƒe kluvi kple kosivi, siwo ŋu miede asi le, abe alesi wodi ene la vɛ, eye miezi wo dzi, be woanye kluviwo kple kosiviwo na mi.

english_verse: You have disobeyed me by not giving your slaves their freedom. So I will give you freedom—the freedom to die in battle or from disease or hunger. I will make you disgusting to all other nations on earth.
translation_verse: Eyata ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Mieɖo tom, be mia dome amesiame naɖe gbe ƒã ablɔɖe na nɔvia kple ehavi o, eyata ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Maɖe gbe ƒã ablɔɖe na mi hena yi, dɔvɔ̃ kple dɔwuame, eye matsɔ mi awɔ ŋɔdzidonu na anyigba dzi fiaɖuƒewo katã.

english_verse: You asked me to be a witness when you made the agreement to set your slaves free. And as part of the ceremony you cut a calf into two parts, then walked between the parts. But you people of Jerusalem have broken that agreement as well as my agreement with Israel. So I will do to you what you did to that calf.
translation_verse: Eye mawo ŋutsu, siwo tu nye nubabla la, amesiwo mewo nusi wobla le ŋkunye me ƒe nyawo dzi o la, abe nyivi, si me wote ɖe eve, eye woto eƒe akpaawo dome yi la ene.

english_verse: When Jehoiakim was king of Judah, the Lord told me,
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe gbe, si va na Yeremya le Yuda-fia Yoyakim, Yosiya vi ŋɔli la, enye si:

english_verse: “Go to the Rechabite clan and invite them to meet you in one of the side rooms of the temple. When they arrive, offer them a drink of wine.”
translation_verse: Yi Rexab viwo ƒe me, ƒo nu kpli wo, eye nakplɔ wo ayi Yehowa ƒe me xɔwo dometɔ ɖeka me, eye nana wein wo woano.

english_verse: So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan.
translation_verse: Tete meɖakplɔ Xabazinya vi Yeremya ƒe vi Yaasanya kple nɔviawo kple viawo katã kpakple Rexab viwo ƒe aƒe blibo la

english_verse: I brought them into the temple courtyard and took them upstairs to a room belonging to the prophets who were followers of Hanan son of Igdaliah. It was next to a room belonging to some of the officials, and that room was over the one belonging to Maaseiah, a priest who was one of the high officials in the temple.
translation_verse: yi Yehowa ƒe me ɖe Mawu ƒe ame Yigdalya vi Xanan viwo ƒe xa, si xe ɖe amegãwo ƒe xɔ ŋu le kpuinudzɔla Salum ƒe vi Maaseya ƒe xɔ ƒe dzigbe gome la me.

english_verse: I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
translation_verse: Eye metsɔ weingo, si yɔ taŋ, kple kpluwo ɖo Rexab viwo ƒe aƒe la kɔme gblɔ na wo bena: Mino wein!

english_verse: But they answered: No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine
translation_verse: Ke woɖo ŋu bena: Miele wein no ge o, elabena mía fofo Yonadab, Rexab vi, de se na mi bena: Mia kple mia viwo migano wein gbeɖe o;

english_verse: or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
translation_verse: migatu xɔ o, migaƒã nuku o, eye migade weingble alo ɖe nanye mia to o; ke boŋ minɔ agbadɔwo me le miaƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me, ne mianɔ agbe eteƒe nadidi le anyigba, si dzi míenye amedzro le la dzi.

english_verse: Our clan has always obeyed Jonadab's command. To this very day, we and our wives and sons and daughters don't drink wine or build houses or plant vineyards or crops. And we have lived in tents,
translation_verse: ke boŋ míele agbadɔwo me, mieɖo to, eye míewɔ nusiwo katã ŋu mía fofo Yonadab de se na mí le la.

english_verse: except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
translation_verse: Ke esi Babel-fia Nebukadnezar ho va anyigba dzi la, miegblɔ bena: Mina míayi Yerusalem le Kaldeatɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ kple Aramtɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ ta; ale mieva le Yerusalem.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, want you to learn a lesson
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi. Yi ɖagblɔ na Yuda-ŋutsuwo kple Yerusalemtɔwo bena: Yehowa be: Ɖe miagbe toɖoɖo tohehe kple nye nyawo sesea?

english_verse: from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me!
translation_verse: Wowɔ Yonadab, Rexab vi ƒe se, si wòde na viawo be, womegano wein o la dzi, eye womenoe o vaseɖe egbe, elabena woɖo to wo fofo ƒe sedede. Nye la meƒo nu kpli mi ɖaa atraɖi, gake miegbe toɖoɖom.

english_verse: You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
translation_verse: Meɖo nye dɔla nyagblɔɖilawo katã ɖe mi ɖaa atraɖii gblɔ bena: Mia dome amesiame netrɔ tso eƒe mɔ vɔwo dzi, miɖɔ miaƒe nuwɔnawo ɖo, eye migadze mawu tutɔwo yome, ne miasubɔ wo o; ekema mianɔ anyigba, si metsɔ na mia kple mia fofowo la dzi; ke mieƒu to anyi o, eye miegbe toɖoɖom.

english_verse: The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me,
translation_verse: Rexab vi Yonadab ƒe viwo wɔ wo fofo ƒe se, si wòɖe na wo la dzi, ke dukɔ sia meɖo tom o!

english_verse: your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
translation_verse: Eyata ale Yehowa, Mawu Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi; Kpɔ ɖa, mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e, siwo katã megblɔ ɖe Yuda kple Yerusalemtɔwo katã ŋu la, ava wo dzi, elabena meƒo nu kpli wo, ke womesee o, meyɔ wo, ke womete o.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan: “I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab,
translation_verse: Eye Yeremya gblɔ na Rexab viwo ƒe aƒe la bena: Ale Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Esi mieɖo to mia fofo Yonadab ƒe se la, mielé eƒe seawo katã me ɖe asi, eye miewɔ, abe alesi wòɖe se na mi ene la,

english_verse: so I promise that your clan will be my servants and will never die out.”
translation_verse: eyata ale Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Rexab vi Yonadab ƒe amesi atsi tre ɖe ŋkunye me la, mave akpɔ o.

english_verse: During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va na Yeremya le Yuda-fia Yoyakim, Yosiya vi ƒe ƒe enelia me bena:

english_verse: since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you,
translation_verse: Tsɔ agbalẽ naŋlɔ nya, siwo katã megblɔ na wò ɖe Israel kple Yuda kpakple dukɔwo katã ŋu tso esime mede asi nuƒoƒo me kpli wò tso Yosiya ŋɔli vaseɖe egbe la, ɖe eme.

english_verse: then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
translation_verse: Amea ɖe menya nu o Yuda ƒe aƒe la ase vɔ̃, siwo katã meɖo be, mawɔ wo la, eye amesiame atrɔ tso eƒe mɔ vɔwo dzi, eye matsɔ woƒe vodadawo kple woƒe nuvɔ̃wo ake wo.

english_verse: I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll.
translation_verse: Tete Yeremya yɔ Barux, Neriya vi, eye Barux ŋlɔ Yehowa ƒe nya, siwo katã wògblɔ nɛ la, tso Yeremya nu ɖe agbalẽ me.

english_verse: Then I said, Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple,
translation_verse: Eye Yeremya de se na Barux bena: Mele ga me, nyemate ŋu ayi Yehowa ƒe me o.

english_verse: so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud.
translation_verse: Eyata yi naɖaxlẽ agbalẽ sia, Yehowa ƒe nya, siwo neŋlɔ tso nunye me la, ɖe dukɔ la ƒe to me le Yehowa ƒe me le nutsidɔgbe, eye naxlẽe ɖe Yuda blibo, si tso woƒe duwo me va la hã ƒe to me.

english_verse: The Lord is furious, and if the people hear how he is going to punish them, maybe they will ask to be forgiven.
translation_verse: Amea ɖe menya nu o woatsɔ kokoƒoƒo abɔbɔ wo ɖokui ɖe anyi le Yehowa ŋku me, eye amesiame atrɔ tso eƒe mɔ vɔ̃wo dzi, elabena dɔmedzoe kple dziku, si ŋu Yehowa ƒo nu le na dukɔ sia la teƒe mekɔ o.

english_verse: Gemariah's son Micaiah was there and heard Baruch read what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Eye Safan vi Gemarya ƒe vi Mixaya se Yehowa ƒe nyawo katã tso agbalẽ la me.

english_verse: When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah.
translation_verse: Tete wòyi agbalẽŋlɔla ƒe xɔ me le fia ƒe me, eye kpɔ ɖa, amegãwo katã bɔbɔ nɔ afima: agbalẽŋlɔla Elisama, Delaya, Semaya vi, Elnatan, Axbor vi, Gemarya, Safan vi, kple Zedekiya, Xananya vi, hekpe ɖe amegãwo katã ŋu.

english_verse: Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people.
translation_verse: Eye Mixaya gblɔ nya, siwo katã wose, esime Barux xlẽ agbalẽ la ɖe dukɔa ƒe to me la na wo.

english_verse: the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did.
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ nɛ bena: Bɔbɔ nɔ anyi naxlẽe ɖe to me na mí! Eye Barux xlẽe ɖe to me na wo.

english_verse: After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked,
translation_verse: Esi wose nya siawo katã la, dzidzi ƒo wo, wode asi wo nɔewo ƒe ŋku me kpɔkpɔ me, eye wogblɔ na Barux bena: Miɖato nya siawo katã na fia la kokoko.

english_verse: “Did someone tell you what to write on this scroll?”
translation_verse: Eye wòbia Barux bena: Gblɔ alesi nèwɔ hafi ŋlɔ nya siawo katã tso enu me la na mí.

english_verse: “Yes, Jeremiah did,” Baruch replied. “I wrote down just what he told me.”
translation_verse: Barux ɖo ŋu na wo bena: Etsɔ eƒe nu gblɔ nya siawo katã nam, eye metsɔ agbalẽŋlɔtsi ŋlɔe ɖe agbalẽ lãme.

english_verse: The officials said, “You and Jeremiah must go into hiding, and don't tell anyone where you are going.”
translation_verse: Eye amegãwo gblɔ na Barux bena: Yi, ne mia kple Yeremya miaɣla mia ɖokui, be amea ɖeke maganya afisi miele o.

english_verse: The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us. Jeremiah's Second Scroll
translation_verse: Eye fia la de se na fiavi Yeraxmeel kple Seraya, Azriel vi, kpakple Selemya, Abdiel vi, be woaɖakplɔ agbalẽŋlɔla Barux kple nyagblɔɖila Yeremya vɛ; ke Yehowa tsɔ wo ɣla.

english_verse: I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me
translation_verse: Eye esi fia la tɔ dzo agbalẽ, si me Barux ŋlɔ Yeremya ƒe nu me nyawo ɖo megbe la, Yehowa ƒe gbe va na Yeremya bena:

english_verse: to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one.
translation_verse: Gatsɔ agbalẽ bubu, eye naŋlɔ nya tsãtɔwo katã, siwo nɔ agbalẽ gbãtɔ, si Yuda-fia Yoyakim tɔ dzoe me la, ɖe eme.

english_verse: Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim: Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals.
translation_verse: Eye nagblɔ ɖe Yuda-fia Yoyakim ŋu be: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esi nètɔ dzo agbalẽ sia hegblɔ be: Nukaŋuti nèŋlɔ ɖe eme be, Babel-fia ava gblẽ anyigba sia, eye wòatsrɔ̃ amegbetɔwo kple lãwo le edzi hã la,

english_verse: So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah.
translation_verse: eyata ale Yehowa gblɔ ɖe Yuda-fia Yoyakim ŋu enye si: Amea ɖeke manɔ esi abɔbɔ nɔ Dawid ƒe fiazikpui dzi o, eye woatsɔ eƒe kukua aƒu gbe ɖe ŋdɔkutsu nu le ŋkeke me kple vuvɔ nu le zã me.

english_verse: You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
translation_verse: Mahe to na eya kple viawo kple eƒe dɔlawo le woƒe vodadawo ta, eye mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e, siwo katã megblɔ ɖe wo ŋu wogbe esese la, ava woa kple Yerusalemtɔwo kpakple Yuda-ŋutsuwo dzii.

english_verse: After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
translation_verse: Eye Yeremya tsɔ agbalẽ bubu na agbalẽŋlɔla Barux, Neriya vi, eye wòŋlɔ agbalẽ kemea, si Yuda-fia Yoyakim tɔ dzoe la me nyawo katã tso Yeremya nu ɖe eme, eye wogakpe nya mawo tɔgbe geɖe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead.
translation_verse: Eye Zedekiya, Yosiya vi, zu fia ɖe Xonya, Yoyakim vi teƒe; elabena Babel-fia Nebukadnezar tsɔe ɖo fia ɖe Yuda-nyigba dzii.

english_verse: But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: Ke eya kple eƒe dɔlawo kple anyigba dzi dukɔ la meɖo to Yehowa ƒe nya, si wògblɔ to nyagblɔɖila Yeremya dzi la o.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message: Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Miɖagblɔ na Yuda-fia, si dɔ mi ɖe gbɔnye be, miabia gbem ase la bena: Kpɔ ɖa, Farao ƒe aʋakɔ, si ho, be yeaxɔ na mi la, agagbugbɔ ayi wo de Egipte,

english_verse: Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire.
translation_verse: eye Kaldeatɔwo agbugbɔ ava wɔ aʋa kple du sia, woaxɔe, eye woatɔ dzoe.

english_verse: Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Migano mia ɖokui ɖum anɔ gbɔgblɔm be: Kaldeatɔwo adzo le mía ŋu kokoko o; elabena womelé tutu ge adzo o.

english_verse: Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire. Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
translation_verse: Elabena ne miasi Kaldeatɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ blibo, si le aʋa wɔm kpli mi la, eye abixɔlawo ko akpɔtɔ ɖe wo dome hã la, wo dome amesiame atso le eƒe agbadɔ me ato dzo du sia.

english_verse: The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me be, esime Kaldeatɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ dzo le Yerusalem ŋu le Farao ƒe aʋakɔa ta la,

english_verse: So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land.
translation_verse: Yeremya do tso Yerusalem, be yeayi Benyamin-nyigba dzi, ne yeaxɔ yeƒe gome ɖe yeƒe dukɔ dome.

english_verse: I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
translation_verse: Eye esi wòɖo Benyamin-gbo nu la, Xananya vi Selemya ƒe vi Yiriya, amesi nye dzɔlawo ƒe amegã la, le afima, eye wòlé nyagblɔɖila Yeremya gblɔ bena: Kaldeatɔwo dzi nèbe, yeayi.

english_verse: “I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials.
translation_verse: Yeremya ɖo ŋu be: Aʋatsoe, nyemebe, mayi Kaldeatɔwo dzi o! Ke Yiriya medo toe o, eye wòlé Yeremya hekplɔe yi amegãwo gbɔe.

english_verse: King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?” “Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
translation_verse: Eye fia Zedekiya dɔ ame woɖakplɔe vɛ, eye fia la biae le adza me le eƒe me gblɔ bena: Yehowa ƒe gbea ɖe lia? Yeremya ɖo ŋu be: Ẽ! Eye wògblɔ bena: Wole tsɔ wò ge ade asi na Babel-fia!

english_verse: Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation?
translation_verse: Eye Yeremya gblɔ na fia Zedekiya bena: Nuvɔ̃ ka mewo ɖe mia kple wò dɔlawo kple dukɔ sia ŋu, hafi mietsɔm ɖe ga me?

english_verse: Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem?
translation_verse: Eye afika miaƒe nyagblɔɖila, siwo gblɔ nya ɖi na mi bena, Babel-fia mava ƒo ɖe mia kple anyigba sia dzi o la le?

english_verse: Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
translation_verse: Azɔ nye aƒetɔ fia nesee, metsɔ kokoƒoƒo baba ɖokuinye ɖe anyi le ŋkuwò me be, megagbugbɔm yi agbalẽŋlɔla Yonatan ƒe xa me, ne maku ɖe afima o.

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_verse: Tete fia Zedekiya de se be, woadzɔ Yeremya ŋu le dzɔlawo ƒe xɔxɔnu, eye wotsɔa abolo ɖeka nɛ gbesiagbe tso aboloƒolawo ƒe ablɔ me, vaseɖe esime woɖu abolowo katã wòvɔ le dua me. Eye Yeremya tsi dzɔlawo ƒe xɔxɔnu.

english_verse: One day, Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jehucal, and Pashhur heard me tell the people of Judah
translation_verse: Eye Sefatya, Matan vi, Gedalya, Pasxur vi, kple Yuxal, Selemya vi, kpakple Pasxur, Malxiya vi, wose nya, siwo Yeremya gblɔ na dukɔ blibo la bena:

english_verse: So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
translation_verse: Tete amegãwo gblɔ na fia la bena: Woawu ŋutsu sia, elabena ele alɔgblɔlɔ dom aʋawɔla, siwo kpɔtɔ ɖe du sia me kple dukɔ blibo la, esi wòle nya siawo tɔgbe gblɔm na wo la; elabena ŋutsu sia mele dukɔ la ƒe nyui dim o, negbe woƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ko.

english_verse: Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
translation_verse: Fia Zedekiya ɖo ŋu bena: Kpɔ ɖa, ele mia si me, elabena fia la mate ŋu awɔ naneke atsi tre ɖe mia ŋu o.

english_verse: Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
translation_verse: Tete wotsɔ Yeremya ɖe fiavi Malxiya ƒe vudo, si le dzɔlawo ƒe xɔxɔnu la me, eye wotsɔ atagbi ɖiɖi Yeremya ɖe eme; ke tsi mele vudoa me o, negbe ba ko, eye Yeremya ɖo to ɖe ba la me.

english_verse: Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
translation_verse: Nye aƒetɔ fia, ŋutsu siawo wɔ nu manyomanyo ɖe nyagblɔɖila Yeremya ŋu, be wotsɔe de do me, ne dɔ nawui woaku ɖe afima; elabena abolo vɔ le dua me.

english_verse: Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well.
translation_verse: Eye Ebed-Melex ɖe ŋutsuawo kpe ɖe eɖokui ŋu; ege ɖe fia ƒe aƒe la me, eye wòyi ɖe xɔ, si le nudzraɖoƒea te lãme hetsɔ ɖovuwo kple avɔ nyunyɔwo le afima, eye wòtsɔ atagbi ɖiɖi wo ɖe Yeremya le do la me.

english_verse: Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did,
translation_verse: Tete Kusitɔ Ebed-Melex gblɔ na Yeremya bena: Tsɔ ɖovu kple ava nyunyɔwo de atagbiawo te le wò axato eveawo me, eye Yeremya wo nenema.

english_verse: the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards. King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ atagbi he Yeremya tso do la me, eye Yeremya tsi dzɔlawo ƒe xɔxɔnu.

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
translation_verse: Emegbe fia Zedekiya do ame woɖakplɔ nyagblɔɖila Yeremya va Yehowa ƒe aƒe ƒe mɔnu etɔ̃lia me. Eye fia la gblɔ na Yeremya bena: Mele nya bia ge wò, megana naneke ɖem o.

english_verse: He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
translation_verse: Tete fia, Zedekiya ka atam na Yeremya le adza me bena: Metà Yehowa, amesi na agbe sia mi la ƒe agbe: Ne mawu wò alo atso wò ade asi na ŋutsu, siwo le wò ku dim la fi!

english_verse: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
translation_verse: Tete Yeremya gblɔ na Zedekiya bena: Ale Yehowa, Mawu Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Ne edo yi Babel-fia ƒe amegãwo gbɔ la, ekema atsi agbe, womatɔ dzo du sia o, eye mia kple wò aƒe míatsi agbe.

english_verse: But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
translation_verse: Ke ne medo yi Babel-fia ƒe amegãwo gbɔ o la, ekema woatsɔ du sia ade asi na Kaldeatɔwo, be wòatɔ dzoe, eye màsi le wo si me o.

english_verse: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
translation_verse: Eye fia Zedekiya gblɔ na Yeremya bena: Mele vɔvɔ̃m le Yudatɔ, siwo yi Kaldeatɔwo dzi la la, be woava tsɔm ade asi na wo, ne woawɔ funyafunyam.

english_verse: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.
translation_verse: Yeremya ɖo ŋu bena: Womelé tsɔ wò ge ade asi o. Ɖo to Yehowa ƒe gbe ko, abe alesi megblɔ na wò ene, ne eme nanyo na wò, eye natsi agbe.

english_verse: But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey,
translation_verse: Ke ne egbe dodo yi la, ekema nya, si Yehowa ɖe fiãm la, enye si:

english_verse: then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you: Friends you trusted led you astray. Now you're trapped in mud, and those friends you trusted have all turned away.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, woakplɔ nyɔnu, siwo katã kpɔtɔ ɖe Yuda-fia ƒe me la, ayi Babel-fia ƒe amegãwo gbɔe, eye woanɔ gbɔgblɔm bena: Xɔ̃wòwo flu wò, eye wokpe le dziwò, eye esi wò afɔ ɖo ba la, woka le ŋuwò.“

english_verse: The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
translation_verse: Woakplɔ srɔ̃wòwo katã kple viwòwo ayi na Kaldeatɔwo, eye womaɖe wò le wo si me o, ke boŋ Babel-fia ƒe asi axe wò, eye wòatɔ dzo du sia.

english_verse: Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life.
translation_verse: Tete Zedekiya gblɔ na Yeremya bena: Amea ɖeke megase nya sia, ne nava ku o!

english_verse: And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them.
translation_verse: Eye ne amegãwo se be, meƒo nu kpli wò, eye woava gbɔwò gblɔ na wò bena, to nya, si nègblɔ na fia la na mi, megaɣlae ɖe mi o, ekema míawu wò o, eye aleke fia la gblɔ na wò hã la,

english_verse: So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
translation_verse: ekema naɖo ŋu na wo bena: Ɖe metsɔ kokoƒoƒo bɔbɔ ɖokuinye ɖe anyi le fia la ŋku me be, megagbugbɔm ɖo de Yonatan ƒe xɔ me, ne maku ɖe afima o.

english_verse: The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
translation_verse: Tete amegãwo katã va bia Yeremya se, eye wòɖo ŋu na wo, abe alesi fia la de se nɛ pɛpɛpɛ ene, eye wona gbɔdzɔe, elabena nya la meɖi wose o.

english_verse: I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_verse: Ke Yeremya tsi dzɔlawo ƒe xɔxɔnu, vaseɖe gbesigbe wòxɔ Yerusalem.

english_verse: When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Eye esi Yuda-fia Zedekiya kple aʋawɔlawo katã kpɔ wo la, wosi dzo le dua me le zã to fia ƒe abɔ me mɔ heto agbo, si le gli ŋukplaba eve dome la nu heɖo ta gbegbe.

english_verse: to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen.
translation_verse: Yi nagblɔ na Kusitɔ Ebed-Melex bena: Ale Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, mana nye nyawo nava me ɖe du sia ŋu hena vɔ̃, eye menye hena nyui o, eye woava me le ŋkuwò me le ɣemaɣi.

english_verse: “Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
translation_verse: Kplɔe, eye wò ŋku nanɔ eŋu, eye megawɔ vɔ̃a ɖekee o, ke boŋ alesi wòagblɔ na wò la, nenema nawɔ nɛ.

english_verse: But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty,
translation_verse: Ke Kaldeatɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ la li wo yome, eye wotu Zedekiya le Yerixo-tagba, eye wolée hekplɔe vɛ na Babel-fia Nebukadnezar le Ribla le Xamat-nyigba dzi, eye wobu fɔe le afima.

english_verse: and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families.
translation_verse: Babel-fia wu Zedekiya viwo le eya ŋuta ŋku me le Ribla eye Babel-fia wu Yuda ƒe bubumewo katã.

english_verse: Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Egbã ŋku na Zedekiya, eye wòde kɔsɔkɔsoe, be wòakplɔe ayi Babel.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls.
translation_verse: Eye Kaldeatɔwo tɔ dzo fia ƒe aƒe kple dukɔ la ƒe aƒewo, eye wogbã Yerusalem ƒe gliwo ƒu anyi.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Eye fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã Nebuzaradan de aboyo dukɔa ƒe ame susɔea, si kpɔtɔ ɖe dua me, kpakple amesiwo de edzi la, yi Babel.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar had given the following orders to Nebuzaradan:
translation_verse: Eye Babel-fia Nebukadnezar de se na fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã Nebuzaradan le Yeremya ŋu bena:

english_verse: sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah. The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
translation_verse: woɖakplɔ Yeremya tso dzɔlawo ƒe xɔxɔnu vɛ, eye wotsɔe de asi na Gedalya, Safan vi Axikam ƒe vi, ne wòakplɔe ayi aƒe mee, eye wònɔ dukɔ la dome.

english_verse: While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say
translation_verse: Esi Yeremya le ga me le dzɔlawo ƒe xɔxɔnu la, Yehowa ƒe gbe va nɛ bena:

english_verse: But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: ke boŋ mana nasi, eye màtsi yi nu o, eye wò agbe anye aboyonu na wò, elabena èɖo dzi ɖe ŋunye, Yehowa ye gblɔe!

english_verse: I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free.
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe gbe va na Yeremya, esime fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã Nebuzaradan ɖee tso Yerusalem kple Yuda ƒe aboyome, siwo wokplɔ yina Babel la dome; eɖe ga le eŋu, eye wòɖe asi le eŋu le Rama la.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan said: Jeremiah, the Lord your God warned your people that he would bring disaster on this land.
translation_verse: Eye fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã na wokplɔ Yeremya vɛ, eye wògblɔ ne bena: Yehowa, wò Mawu, gblɔ dzɔgbevɔ̃e sia ɖe teƒe sia ŋu.

english_verse: But they continued to rebel against him, and now he has punished them just as he threatened.
translation_verse: Yehowa na wòva me, eye wòwɔ abe alesi wògblɔ ene, elabena miewɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Yehowa ŋu, eye mieɖo to eƒe gbe o, eyata nusia dzɔ ɖe mia dzi ɖo.

english_verse: Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish.
translation_verse: Azɔ kpɔ ɖa, meɖe ga le wò alɔ ŋu egbe; ne edze ŋuwò nèbe, yeayi Babel kplim la, va miyi, eye nye ŋku anɔ ŋuwò; ke ne medze ŋuwò be, nayi Babel kplim o la, ekema nɔ anyi; kpɔ ɖa, anyigba blibo la le ŋkuwò me, afisi nyo ŋuwò nebe, yeayi la, yi gama.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar has chosen Gedaliah to rule Judah. You can live near Gedaliah, and he will provide for you, or you can live anywhere else you choose. Nebuzaradan gave me a supply of food, then let me leave.
translation_verse: Ke esi tɔtrɔ mele lãme sẽm nɛ o la, egblɔ nɛ bena: Gbugbɔ yi Gedalya, Safan vi Axikam ƒe vi, amesi Babel-fia tsɔ ɖo Yuda-duwo nu la gbɔ, eye nanɔ egbɔ le dukɔ la dome, alo yi afisiafi, si dze ŋuwò nèbe, yeayi. Eye fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã la tsɔ mɔ dzi nuɖuɖu kple nunana nɛ, eye wòdo mɔe wòdzo.

english_verse: I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah. The Harvest Is Brought In
translation_verse: Ale Yeremya va Gedalya, Axikam vi la gbɔ le Mizpa, eye wònɔ dukɔ, si kpɔtɔ ɖe anyigba dzi la dome. Gedalya melɔ̃ be, yeaxɔe ko bena, wole ye wu ge o.

english_verse: Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Eye Gedalya, Safan vi Axikam ƒe vi, ka atam na wo kple woƒe amehawo gblɔ bena: Kaldeatɔwo subɔsubɔ megadzi ŋɔ na mi o; mitsi anyigba la dzi, eye misubɔ Babel-fia, ekema eme anyo na mi.

english_verse: I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
translation_verse: Ke nye la manɔ Mizpa, ne matsi tre de Kaldeatɔ, siwo ava mía gbɔ la ŋku me. Miawo la miƒo wein, kutsetse kple ami nu ƒu tsɔ ɖe miaƒe nuwo me, eye minɔ miaƒe du, siwo miexɔ la me.

english_verse: One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Eye Yoxanan, Kareax vi, kple aʋafia, siwo katã nɔ aʋagbe me la, va Gedalya gbɔ le Mizpa

english_verse: They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!” Gedaliah refused to believe them,
translation_verse: hegblɔ nɛ bena: Mènyae be, ɖe Amonitɔwo ƒe fia Baalis dɔ Ismael, Netanya vi la ɖa be, woawu wò oa? Ke Gedalya, Axikam vi la, mexɔ wo dzi se o.

english_verse: so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
translation_verse: Eye Yoxanan, Kareax vi la, gblɔ na Gedalya le adza me le Mizpa bena: Mayi, ne maɖawu Ismael, Netanya vi la, eye amea ɖeke manyae o. Nukaŋuti woawu wò, ne Yudatɔ, siwo katã ƒo ƒu ɖe ŋuwò la, naka ahlẽ, eye Yuda ƒe ame susɔeawo natsrɔ̃?

english_verse: Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_verse: Gedalya, Axikam vi la, ɖo ŋu na Yoxanan, Kareax vi bena: Megawɔ nusia o, elabena alakpa dam nèle ɖe Ismael si.

english_verse: But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me le dzinu adrelia me be, Ismael, Elisama vi Netanya ƒe vi, amesi nye fia ƒe amegãwo dometɔ ɖeka tso fia ƒome la me la, va Gedalya, Axikam vi la gbɔ le Mizpa, eye ŋutsu ewo kpe ɖe eŋu, eye woɖu nu kple wo nɔewo le Mizpa.

english_verse: During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Tete Ismael, Netanya vi, kple ŋutsu ewo, siwo kpe ɖe eŋu la, wotso, heda yi Gedalya, Safan vi Axikam ƒe vi la, eye wowu eya, amesi Babel-fia tsɔ ɖo anyigba la nu.

english_verse: Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
translation_verse: Eye Ismael wu Yudatɔ, siwo katã le Gedalya gbɔ le Mizpa la, hekpe ɖe Kaldeatɔ, siwo le afima, amesiwo nye aʋawɔlawo la ŋu.

english_verse: The next day, the murders had still not been discovered,
translation_verse: Ke le ŋkeke eve megbe, esi amea ɖeke mekpɔ see be, wowu; Gedalya o la,

english_verse: Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah.
translation_verse: Tete Ismael, Netanya vi la, do tso Mizpa le avi dzi yi ɖakpe wo, eye esi wòdo go wo la, egblɔ na wo bena: Miva miyi Gedalya, Axikam vi la gbɔ.

english_verse: But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well.
translation_verse: Ke esi woɖo dua titina la, Ismael, Netanya vi la, kple ŋutsu, siwo kpe ɖe eŋu la, wu wo ɖe vudo la me.

english_verse: He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field.
translation_verse: Ke wo dome ŋutsu ewo gblɔ na Ismael bena: Megawu mí o, elabena míeɖi nuwo ɖe gbe me: lu, ƒo, ami kple anyitsi. Tete wòdzudzɔ, eye mewu wo kpe ɖe wo nɔviwo ŋu o.

english_verse: The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
translation_verse: Vudo, si me Ismael tsɔ ŋutsu, siwo katã wòwu kpe ɖe Gedalya ŋu ƒe kukuawo ƒu gbe ɖo la, fia Asa ye ɖee le Israel-fia Baesa ta; vudo sia mee Ismael, Netanya vi la, tsɔ ame kukuawo ɖee fũ.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Emegbe Ismael kplɔ dukɔ la ƒe ame susɔea, siwo katã le Mizpa, fia vinyɔnuwo kple dukɔ blibo, si kpɔtɔ ɖe Mizpa, amesiwo nu fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã Nebuzaradan tso Gedalya, Axikam vi la ɖo; woawo Ismael, Netanya vi la, ɖe aboyoe, eye wòdzo, be yeayi Amon-viwo gbɔ. Yoxanan ti Ismael yome. Yudatɔwo di bena, yewoayi Egipte.

english_verse: Johanan and the other army officers heard what Ishmael had done.
translation_verse: Ke esi Yoxanan, Kareax vi, kple aʋafia, siwo katã kpe ɖe eŋu la, se vɔ̃, siwo katã Ismael, Netanya vi, wɔ la,

english_verse: So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon.
translation_verse: woɖe woƒe aʋawɔlawo katã, eye woho, be yewoaɖawɔ aʋa kple Ismael, Netanya vi la, eye woɖatui le tɔ gã, si le Gibeon la to.

english_verse: But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon. Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
translation_verse: Ke Ismael, Netanya vi la, kple ŋutsu enyi wosi le Yoxanan nu yi Amon-viwo gbɔ.

english_verse: Johanan and the officers had rescued the women, children, and royal officials that Ishmael had taken prisoner after killing Gedaliah. Johanan led the people from Gibeon
translation_verse: Tete Yoxanan, Kareax vi la, kple aʋafia, siwo katã kpe ɖe eŋu la, kplɔ dukɔa ƒe ame susɔeawo katã, ŋutsu, siwo nye aʋamewo, nyɔnuwo kple ɖeviwo kpakple aƒedzikpɔlawo, amesiwo Ismael, Netanya vi la, ɖe aboyo tso Mizpa, esime wòwu Gedalya, Axikam vi la megbe; woawo wòkplɔ tso Gibeon,

english_verse: Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me
translation_verse: Eye aʋafiawo katã, Yoxanan, Kareax vi, kple Yezanya, Hosaya vi, kpakple dukɔ blibo la, tso tsitsiawo dzi vaseɖe ɖeviawo dzi, va

english_verse: and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left.
translation_verse: gblɔ na nyagblɔɖila Yeremya bena: Míetsɔ míaƒe kokoƒoƒo bɔbɔ mía ɖokui ɖe anyi le ŋkuwò me: Ɖe kuku na Yehowa, wò Mawu la, ɖe mía ta le ame susɔeawo katã ŋuti, elabena mí ame ʋee siawoe kpɔtɔ tso ame gbogboawo dome, abe alesi wò ŋku le mía kpɔmi ene;

english_verse: Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
translation_verse: ne Yehowa, wò Mawu la, nafia mɔ, si dzi míato kple nusi míawɔ la mí.

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord himself will be our witness that we promise to do whatever he says,
translation_verse: Eye wogblɔ na Yeremya bena: Yehowa nenye ɖasefo anukwaretɔ kple nuteƒewɔla na mí, nenye be, míewɔ ɖe nya, siwo katã Yehowa, wò Mawu, aɖo ɖe mí la nu o.

english_verse: even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
translation_verse: Eɖanye nyui alo vɔ̃ o, Yehowa, mia Mawu la ƒe gbe kokoko míase, amesi gbɔ míele ɖowòm ɖo, be eme nanyo na mí, le esi míeɖo to Yehowa, mía Mawu ƒe gbe ta.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for
translation_verse: Eye wòva me le ŋkeke ewo megbe be, Yehowa ƒe gbe va na Yeremya,

english_verse: Johanan, the officers, and the other people. So I called them together
translation_verse: eye wòyɔ Yoxanan, Kareax vi, kple aʋafia, siwo katã le eŋu, kpakple dukɔ blibo la tso ɖeviwo dzi vaseɖe tsitsiawo dzi

english_verse: and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said: You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do.
translation_verse: hegblɔ na wo bena: Ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, amesi gbɔ miedɔm ɖo, be mahe miaƒe kokoƒoƒowo ayi eŋku mee la, gblɔ esi;

english_verse: I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you.
translation_verse: Ne mienɔ anyigba sia dzi la, ekema matu mi, eye nyemagbã mi o, mado mi, eye nyemaho mi o; elabena vɔ̃, si mewo mi la, vem.

english_verse: Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him,
translation_verse: Babel-fia, si vɔ̃m miele la, megadzi ŋɔ na mi o; Yehowa be: Migavɔ̃e o, elabena maxɔ na mi, eye maɖe mi atso esi me;

english_verse: and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
translation_verse: mana nublanuikpɔkpɔ nasu mia si, eye wòakpɔ nublanui na mi ahakplɔ mi agbo va miaƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Ke ne miebe, yewomele anyigba sia dzi nɔ ge o, ale be miegbe toɖoɖo Yehowa, mia Mawu la ƒe gbe

english_verse: We are going to Egypt, where there is plenty of food and no danger of war.”
translation_verse: hele gbɔgblɔm be: Kpao, ke boŋ mina míayi Egipte, afisi míakpɔ aʋawɔwɔ ŋku me, eye míase kpẽ ƒe ɖiɖi le o, afisi abolodɔ mawu mí le o, afima miaɖanɔ la,

english_verse: People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen.
translation_verse: ekema mi Yuda ƒe ame susɔeawo, mise Yehowa ƒe gbe: Ale Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Ne mietsɔ miaƒe ŋku ɖo Egipte-yiyi ŋu, eye mĩeyi, be mianye amedzro le afima la,

english_verse: You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsu, siwo katã tso woƒe ŋku ɖo Egipte ŋu, be yewoayi aɖanye amedzro le afima la, aku ɖe yi, dɔwuame kple dɔvɔ̃ si me, eye woƒe amea ɖeke makpɔtɔ asi le dzɔgbevɔ̃e, si mahe va wo dzi la nu o.

english_verse: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word. Jeremiah Gives a Warning
translation_verse: Elabena ale Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Alesi metrɔ nye dɔmedzoe kple nye dziku ko ɖe Yerusalemtɔwo dzii la, nenema ke matrɔ nye dziku akɔ ɖe mia dzii, nenye be, mieyi Egipte; miazu atamkanu, ŋɔdzinu, ɖiŋudonu kple alɔmeɖenu, eye miagakpɔ teƒe sia kple ŋku o.

english_verse: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.
translation_verse: Mi Yuda ƒe ame susɔeawo, Yehowa gblɔ ɖe mia ŋu be: Migayi Egipte o. Minyae be, megbe na mi egbea!

english_verse: You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake,
translation_verse: Elabena mia ŋutɔwoe ɖu mia ɖokui be, mieɖom ɖe Yehowa, mia Mawu la gbɔ gblɔ bena: Ɖe kuku na Yehowa, mía Mawu la, na mí, eye alesi tututu Yehowa, mía Mawu la, agblɔ la, nenema nagblɔ na mi, ne miawo.

english_verse: because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him.
translation_verse: Megblɔe na mi egbea, ke mieɖo to Yehowa, mia Mawu la ƒe gbe le nusiwo katã ŋuti wòɖom ɖe mia gbɔ ɖo la me o.

english_verse: And so, you will die in Egypt from war, hunger, and disease.
translation_verse: Eyata minyae kokoko be, miaku ɖe yi, dɔwuame kple dɔvɔ̃ si me, le teƒe, si le mia dzrom miebe, yewoaɖanye amedzro le la.

english_verse: But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt.
translation_verse: Azarya, Hosaya vi, kple Yoxanan, Kareax vi kpakple ŋutsu vlowo katã gblɔ na Yeremya bena: Alakpa dam nèle; menye Yehowa, mía Mawu, ye ɖo wò ɖa gblɔ bena: Migayi Egipte ɖanye amedzro le afima o;

english_verse: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
translation_verse: ke boŋ Barux, Neriya vi la le ʋu yɔm ɖe tewò ɖe mía ŋu, ne woatso mí ade asi na Kaldeatɔwo, ne woawu mí, eye woaɖe aboyo mí ayi Babel.

english_verse: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
translation_verse: Eye Yoxanan, Kareax vi, kple aʋafiawo katã kpakple dukɔ blibo la meɖo to Yehowa ƒe gbe, be woatsi Yuda-nyigba dzi o.

english_verse: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
translation_verse: Tete Yoxanan, Kareax vi, kple aʋafiawo katã kplɔ Yuda ƒe ame susɔea, siwo katã trɔ gbã tso dukɔwo katã dome, afisi wokaka hlẽ ɖo, be yewoava ana Yuda-nyigba dzi,

english_verse: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
translation_verse: ŋutsuwo, nyɔnuwo kple ɖeviwo, fia vinyɔnuwo kple amesiwo katã fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã Nebuzaradan gblẽ ɖi ɖe Gedalya, Safan vi Axikam ƒe vi si me la, hekpe ɖe nyagblɔɖila Yeremya kple Barux, Neriya vi la ŋu,

english_verse: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
translation_verse: eye wodzo yi Egipte-nyigba dzi, elabena wogbe toɖoɖo Yehowa ƒe gbe, eye wova Taxpanxes.

english_verse: when the Lord told me:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va na Yeremya le Taxpanxes bena:

english_verse: Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
translation_verse: Tso kpe gãwo naɖi ɖe Farao ƒe aƒe, si le Taxpanxes la ƒe mo nu le anyikpe, siwo woɖo anyigba la te le Yuda-ŋutsuwo ŋku me,

english_verse: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
translation_verse: eye nagblɔ na wo bena: Ale Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Mado woaɖakplɔ nye dɔla Babel-fia Nebukadnezar vɛ, ali eƒe fiazikpui ɖe kpe, siwo meɖi la dzi, eye wòakeke eƒe fiakuntruwo ɖe wo dzi.

english_verse: He will attack Egypt and kill many of its people; others will die of disease or be dragged away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Ava si Egipte-nyigba, eye wòatsɔ nusi nye ku tɔ la, ade asi na ku, nusi nye aboyo tɔ la, ade asi na aboyo, eye nusi nye yi tɔ la, ade asi na yi.

english_verse: The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe gbe, si va na Yeremya hena Yudatɔ, siwo katã le Egipte-nyigba dzi, amesiwo le Migdol, Taxpanxes, Nof kple Patros-nyigba dzi la, enye si:

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today,
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi. Miekpɔ dzɔgbevɔ̃e, siwo katã mehe va Yerusalem kple Yuda-duwo katã dzi, eye kpɔ ɖa, wòzu aƒedowo egbe siawo, eye amea ɖeke mele wo me o,

english_verse: because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
translation_verse: le woƒe vɔ̃, siwo wowɔ hetsɔ do dziku nam, eye woyi ɖasubɔ mawu tutu, siwo woawo loo alo miawo kple mia fofowo mienyã o, eye wodo dzudzɔ na wo la la.

english_verse: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
translation_verse: Eye meɖo nye dɔla nyagblɔɖilawo katã de mi ɖaa atraɖii gblɔ bena: Migawɔ ŋunyɔnu sia, si melé fui la o.

english_verse: but they refused to listen and would not stop worshiping other gods.
translation_verse: Ke wogbe toɖoɖom, eye womeƒu to anyi, be woatrɔ tso woƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔwo me, eye womagaɖo dzudzɔ na mawu tutɔwo azɔ o.

english_verse: Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
translation_verse: Eyata nye dziku trɔ ƒo ɖe anyi, eye nye dɔmedzoe fiã Yuda-duwo kple Yerusalem-kpɔdomeewo, ale be wòzu aƒedo kple gbegbe, abe alesi wòle egbe siawo ene.

english_verse: Why do you now insist on heading for another disaster? A disaster that will destroy not only you, but also your children and babies.
translation_verse: Azɔ ale Yehowa, Mawu Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Nukaŋuti miahe vɔ̃ gã sia ava mia ɖokui dzi, be ŋutsu kple nyɔnu, ɖevi kple vidzie natsrɔ̃ le Yuda, ale be miana be, amea ɖeke makpɔtɔ na mi o,

english_verse: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: mietsɔ miaƒe asinudɔwɔwɔwo ɖo dziku nam, eye miedo dzudzɔ na mawu tutɔwo le Egipte-nyigba dzi, afisi mieyi, be miaɖanye amedzro le, ne miatsrɔ̃ mia ɖokui, eye miazu ɖiŋudonu kple alɔmeɖenu le anyigba dzi dukɔwo katã domea?

english_verse: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
translation_verse: Ɖe mieŋlɔ mia fofowo ƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔwo, Yuda-fiawo kple woƒe amegãwo ƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔwo, miawo kple mia srɔ̃wo ƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔwo, siwo wowɔ le Yuda-nyigba kple Yerusalem-kpɔdomeewo la bea?

english_verse: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Womebɔbɔ wo ɖokui ɖe anyi vaseɖe egbe o, vɔvɔ̃ meɖo wo o, eye womezɔ ɖe nye sewo kple nye ɖoɖowo, siwo mede asi na woawo kple wo fofowo la nu o.

english_verse: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Makplɔ Yuda ƒe ame susɔea, siwo tsɔ ŋku ɖo Egipte-nyigba dzi yiyi ŋu, be woaɖanye amedzro le afima la, eye wo katã woatsrɔ̃; woatsi Egipte-nyigba dzi, eye woatsrɔ̃ ɖe yi kple dɔwuame si me: ɖeviwo kple tsitsiawo siaa aku ɖe yi kple dɔwuame si me, eye woazu atamkanu, ŋɔdzinu, ɖiŋudonu kple alɔmeɖenu.

english_verse: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
translation_verse: Mahe to na amesiwo le Egipte-nyigba dzi ta, abe alesi metsɔ yi, dɔwuame kple dɔvɔ̃ he to na Yerusalem ene.

english_verse: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
translation_verse: Amea ɖeke masi alo asusɔ le Yuda ƒe ame mamlea, siwo yi, be woaɖanye amedzro le Egipte-nyigba dzi la dome agbugbɔ ayi Yuda-nyigba, si le wo dzrom be, yewoagbugbɔ aɖanɔ afima la dzi o; elabena womelé gbugbɔ ge ayi o, negbe ame sisia ɖewo ko.

english_verse: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu, siwo katã nyae be, yewo srɔ̃wo do dzudzɔ na mawu tutɔwo, kple nyɔnu, siwo katã le tsitre le ha gã me, kpakple dukɔ blibo, si le Egipte-nyigba dzi kple Patros la, ɖo ŋu na Yeremya bena:

english_verse: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
translation_verse: Nya, si negblɔ na mí le Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ me la, miele to ɖo ge wò o;

english_verse: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
translation_verse: ke boŋ miawɔ ɖe nya sia nya, si do tso mía nu la nu, míado dzudzɔ na dziƒo fianyɔnu, eye miaƒo tsi ɖe anyi nɛ, abe alesi mia kple mía fofowo, míaƒe fiawo kple míaƒe amegãwo míenɔa wɔwɔm le Yuda-duwo kple Yerusalem-kpɔdomeewo, eye míekpɔa nu ɖuna ɖia ƒo, eme nyona na mí, eye míekpɔa dzɔgbevɔ̃ea ɖeke kple ŋku o la ene.

english_verse: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
translation_verse: Ke esi míedzudzɔ dzudzɔdodo na dziƒo fianyɔnu kple tsi ƒoƒoɖeanyi nɛ la, nusianu ƒe hiã tu mí, eye yi kple dɔwuame tsrɔ̃ mí.

english_verse: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
translation_verse: Eye ne míedo dzudzɔ na dziƒo fianyɔnu heƒo tsi ɖe anyi nɛ la, ɖe mía srɔ̃wo megbe míetona tɔa tatali ɖe eƒe nɔnɔme, eye míeƒoa tsi ɖe anyi nɛa?

english_verse: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
translation_verse: Ɖe menye miaƒe dzudzɔ, siwo mia kple mia fofowo, miaƒe fiawo kple miaƒe amegãwo kpakple dukɔ hahoo la miedo le Yuda-duwo me kple Yerusalem-kpɔdomeewo la dzi Yehowa ɖo ŋkui, eye wova ta me nɛ oa?

english_verse: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
translation_verse: Eye esi etsɔtsɔ ti Yehowa, le miaƒe nuwɔna vɔ̃ɖiwo kple miaƒe ŋunyɔnu, siwo miewɔ ta la, eyata miaƒe anyigba zu aƒedo, gbegbe kple ɖiŋudonu, eye ame vɔ le edzi, abe alesi wòle egbe siawo ene!

english_verse: This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Esi miedo dzudzɔ, eye miewɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Yehowa ŋu, miese Yehowa ƒe gbe o, eye miezɔ ɖe eƒe seawo, ɖoɖoawo kple ɖaseɖiɖiawo nu o la, eyata dzɔgbevɔ̃e sia va mia dzi ɖo, abe alesi wòle egbe siawo ene.

english_verse: Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Mia kple mía srɔ̃wo mieƒo nu kple miaƒe nu, eye mietsɔ miaƒe asiwo wɔ edzi gblɔ bena: Mina míawɔ míaƒe adzɔgbe, si míeɖe la dzi, ne míado dzudzɔ na dziƒo fianyɔnu, eye miaƒo tsi ɖe anyi nɛ. Mili ɖe miaƒe adzɔgbeɖeɖewo dzi, eye nuwo miaƒe ŋugbedodowo dzi ko!

english_verse: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
translation_verse: Eyata mi Yuda blibo, si le Egipte-nyigba dzi, mise Yehowa ƒe gbe! Yehowa be: Metà nye ŋkɔ gã la: Ne Yuda-ŋutsua ɖe ƒe nu ayɔ nye ŋkɔ le Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi agblɔ be, yetà Aƒetɔ Yehowa ƒe agbe fĩ!

english_verse: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, mele ŋu te ɖe mia ŋu hena vɔ̃wɔwɔ, menye hena nyui o, eye yi kple dɔwuame atsrɔ̃ Yuda-ŋutsu, siwo katã le Egipte-nyigba dzi la, vaseɖe esime wo nu ayi.

english_verse: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
translation_verse: Eye amesiwo si le yi nu la, agbugbɔ tso Egipte-nyigba dzi ayi Yuda-nyigba dzi, eye woanye ame xexlẽewo; eye Yuda ƒe ame susɔeawo katã, amesiwo yi Egipte, be woanye amedzro le afima la, adze si amesi ƒe nya le eme, tɔnye loo alo wo ta.

english_verse: And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Esia anye dzesi na mi be, mele to he ge na mi le teƒe sia, ne miadze sii be, nye nyawo ava me ɖe mia ŋu hena vɔ̃wɔwɔ:

english_verse: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Matso Egipte-fia Farao Xofra ade asi na eƒe futɔwo kple eƒe kudilawo, abe alesi metsɔ Yuda-fia Zedekiya de asi na eƒe futɔ kple eƒe kudila Babel-fia Nebukadnezar ene.

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him.
translation_verse: Nyagblɔɖila Yeremya ƒe nya, si wògblɔ na Barux, Neria vi la, esime wòŋlɔ nya siawo tso Yeremya nu ɖe agbalẽ me le Yuda-fia Yoyakim, Yosiya vi ƒe ƒe enelia me la, enye si:

english_verse: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
translation_verse: Barux, ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ ɖe ŋuwò enye si.

english_verse: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: „Baba nam, elabena Yehowa tsɔ nuxaxa kpe ɖe nye vevesese ŋu, nye hũɖeɖe ti kɔ nam, eye nyemekpɔ gbɔdzɔea ɖeke o.“

english_verse: But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted.
translation_verse: Ale nagblɔ nɛ enye si: Yehowa be: Nusi nye ŋutɔ metu la, magbãe aƒu anyi, eye nusi medo la, mahoe ɖa, anyigba blibo la dzi wòava;

english_verse: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: hafi wòa nèbe, yeadi nu gãwoa? Megadi wo o; elabena Yehowa be: Mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ava ŋutilãwo katã dzi; ke mana wò agbe nazu aboyonu na wò le teƒe, siwo katã nayi.

english_verse: The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world. What the Lord Says about Egypt
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe gbe, si va na nyagblɔɖila Yeremya ɖe dukɔwo ŋu enye si:

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
translation_verse: Hena Egipte, ɖe Egipte-fia Farao Nexo ƒe aʋakɔ, si le Frat-tɔsisi nu le Karkemis gbɔ, eye Babel-fia Nebukadnezar sii le Yuda-fia Yoyakim, Yosiya vi ƒe ƒe enelia me la ŋu:

english_verse: It's time to go into battle! So grab your shields,
translation_verse: Mitsɔ akpoxɔnu gã kple via bia akpae, eye mido ɖe aʋa nu!

english_verse: saddle your horses, and polish your spears. Put on your helmets and armor, then take your positions.
translation_verse: Mitsi sɔtsuwo ɖe tasiaɖam ŋu, eye miɖe sɔwo dzi, miɖo gakukuwo miado, minyre akplɔwo, eye mido gawuwo!

english_verse: I can see the battle now— you are defeated and running away, never once looking back. Terror is all around.
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti mele wo kpɔm dzidzi ƒo wo, eye wogbugbɔ ɖe megbe, wogbã woƒe kalẽtɔwo gudugudu, eye wòsi womegale megbe kpɔm o? Yehowa be: Ŋɔdzi li godoo.

english_verse: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Ame ɖeablɛ masi o, eye kalẽtɔ maɖe eɖokui o! Wotsra ɖe anyiehe le Frat-tɔsisi la to hetsi afima.

english_verse: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
translation_verse: Ameka nye esi gbɔna abe Nil ene, eye eƒe tsiwo le tsotsom abe tɔsisiwo ene?

english_verse: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
translation_verse: Egipte ye gbɔna abe Nil ene, eye eƒe tsiwo le tsotsom abe tɔsisiwo ene, eye wògblɔ be: Mayi aɖaɖe anyigba la, eye matsrɔ̃ duwo kple wo me nɔlawo.

english_verse: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Mi sɔwo, miɖe ta eme, mi tasiaɖamwo, minyẽ zi ɖe eme! Kalẽtɔwo neho, Kusi-viwo kple Put-viwo, amesiwo si me akpoxɔnu le, kpakple Libiatɔwo, amesiwo nye aŋutrɔdala, siwo hea da me!

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
translation_verse: Gbemagbe enye hlɔ̃biagbe na Aƒetɔ, Yehowa Zebaot, ne wòabia hlɔ̃ eƒe futɔwo. Yi aɖu nu aɖi ƒo, eye wòamu woƒe ʋu; elabena Aƒetɔ, Yehowa Zebaot, le vɔsaŋkekenyuie ɖum le anyiehe-nyigba dzi, le Frat-tɔsisi la nu.

english_verse: Egypt, no medicine can heal you, not even the soothing lotion from Gilead.
translation_verse: Egipte-ɖetugbi, yi naɖatsɔ atike tso Gilead; yakatsyɔe nèle atike geɖe wɔm, mahaya akpɔ o.

english_verse: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
translation_verse: Dukɔwo se wò ŋukpe ŋkɔ, eye wò ɣlikpɛdodo yɔ anyigba dzi fũ; elabena kalẽtɔ dze anyi ɖe kalẽtɔ dzi, eye wo kple eve la siaa wotsi.

english_verse: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
translation_verse: Mido kpo le Egipte, miɖe gbe ƒã le Migdol, eye miɖe gbe ƒã le Nof kple Taxpanxes! Migblɔ bena: Tso nadzra ɖokuiwò ɖo, elabena yi le nu ɖum le ŋuwò godoo.

english_verse: I have struck down your mighty god Apis and chased him away.
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti wò ŋusẽtɔwo ɖo baba ɖe anyi? Womenɔ te o, elabena Yehowa ye tutu wo ƒu anyi.

english_verse: Your soldiers stumble over each other and say, “Get up! The enemy will kill us, unless we can escape to our own land.”
translation_verse: Ena ame geɖewo kli nu, eye wodze anyi ɖe wo nɔewo dzi hegblɔ bena: Mina míagbugbɔ ayi míaƒe dukɔ gbɔ kple anyigba, si dzi wodzi mí ɖo la dzi, tso yi wuame la nu!

english_verse: Give the king of Egypt this new name, “Talks-Big-Does-Nothing.”
translation_verse: Miyɔ Egipte-fia Farao be „hohohodola, si ɖea ŋu ɖi le ɣeyiɣi nyuitɔ ŋu.“

english_verse: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
translation_verse: Ale fia, si ŋkɔ nye Yehowa Zebaot la, gblɔ esi: Metà ɖokuinye ƒe agbe: Ava abe alesi Tabor le towo dome, eye Karmel le atsiaƒu nu ene.

english_verse: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
translation_verse: Egipte-nyɔnuvi, do mɔzɔgba na ɖokuiwò; elabena Nof azu aƒedo, eye woagblẽe, ame navɔ le eme.

english_verse: The foreign soldiers you hired will turn and run. But they are doomed, like well-fed calves being led to the butcher. *
translation_verse: Amedzro, siwo nye asrafowo le wo dome, hã le abe nyivi dami ene; wo katã trɔ megbe hesi, eye womenɔ te o; elabena woƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃egbe, woƒe toheɣi va wo dzi.

english_verse: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
translation_verse: Woƒe zinyenyẽ le abe da, si le sisim la tɔ ene; elabena wogbɔna kple aʋakɔ, eye wole fiavi ɖe asi ƒo ɖe edzi abe atilãla ene.

english_verse: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Woaƒo eƒe ave, si ɖo kpekpekpe, elabena wosɔ gbɔ wu ʋetsuviwo, eye womelé xexlẽ me o.

english_verse: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
translation_verse: Ŋukpe lé Egipte-nyɔnuvi, elabena wotsɔe de asi na anyiehe dukɔ.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
translation_verse: Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Mahe to na Amon le No, na Farao, na Egipte kple eƒe mawuwo kple eƒe fiawo kpakple amesiwo le dzi ɖom ɖe Farao ŋu la.

english_verse: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
translation_verse: Matsɔ ade asi na eƒe kudilawo kple Babel-fia Nebukadnezar kpakple eƒe dɔlawo; ke emegbe la ame aganɔ edzi abe tsã ene. Yehowa ye gblɔe. Akɔfafa na Israel.

english_verse: Israel, don't be afraid. Someday I will bring you home from foreign lands. You and your descendants will live in peace and safety, with nothing to fear.
translation_verse: Ke wò, nye dɔla Yakob, megavɔ̃ o, eye Israel, dzi megaɖe le ƒowò o; elabena maɖe wò atso didiƒe kple viwòwo atso woƒe aboyonyigba dzi; Yakob atrɔ agbɔ, ava no anyi aɖe dzi ɖi bɔkɔɔ, eye amea ɖeke mado voɖi nɛ o.

english_verse: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Wò, nye dɔla Yakob, megavɔ̃ o; elabena meli kpli wò, eye matsrɔ̃ dukɔ, siwo katã dome menyã wò ɖo ɖo la gbidigbidi; ke wò la, nyematsrɔ̃ wò keŋ o; nyemagbe tohehe na wò o, ke boŋ mahe to na wò ɖe ɖoɖo la nu.

english_verse: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe gbe, si va na nyagblɔɖila Yeremya ɖe Filistitɔwo ŋu, hafi Farao nava si Gaza, enye si;

english_verse: I, the Lord, tell you that your land will be flooded with an army from the north. It will destroy your towns and sweep you away, moaning and screaming.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, tsi tso anyiehe gbɔna, eye wòazu tɔɖɔɖɔ aɖe anyigba kple edzi nuwo, duwo kple wò me nɔlawo; amegbetɔwo ado ɣli, eye anyigbadzitɔwo afa avi

english_verse: When you hear the thunder of horses and chariots, your courage will vanish, and parents will even abandon their own children.
translation_verse: le sɔtsuwo ƒe afɔtutu anyi kpitikpiti, le tasiaɖamwo ƒe zinyenyẽ kple tasiaɖamfɔwo ƒe hoowɔwɔ ta; fofowo matrɔ ɖe wo viwo ŋu o, elabena woƒe asi ado agblɔ

english_verse: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
translation_verse: le ŋkeke, si gbɔna la ta, be woagblẽ Filistitowo katã, eye woatsrɔ̃ Tiro kple Sidon ƒe xɔnametɔ susɔeawo; elabena Yehowa le Filistitɔ, siwo kpɔtɔ ɖe Kaftor-ƒukpo dzi la gblẽ ge.

english_verse: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
translation_verse: Gaza atsi ƒuƒlu, eye woatsrɔ̃ Askalon; ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe susɔeawo, ɣekaɣi miasi blini na mia ɖokui ase ɖo?

english_verse: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
translation_verse: Ao, Yehowa ƒe yi, ɣekaɣi hafi nagbɔ ɖe eme? Trɔ va ɖo wò aku, wò akɔ nefa, eye nanɔ anyi kpoo!

english_verse: But how can my sword rest, when I have commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the seacoast?
translation_verse: Nukaŋuti nagbɔ ɖe eme, esi wònye Yehowa ye de se na wò ɖe Askalon ŋu, eye wòda wò ɖe ƒutawo ŋu ɖe?

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
translation_verse: Ɖe Moab ŋu Ale Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Baba na Neho, elabena wogblẽe! Wòxɔ Kiryatayim, eye ŋukpe lée, wogbã mɔ̃ sesẽ la wòzu ŋukpe!

english_verse: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
translation_verse: Moab ƒe adegbeƒoƒo nu tso, wodo tame vɔ̃ ɖe eŋu le Xesbon be: Mina míatsrɔ̃e, ne womaganye dukɔ azɔ o! Woatsrɔ̃ wò Madmen hã, eye yi anɔ yowóme.

english_verse: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
translation_verse: Ɣli ɖi le Xoronayim be Gbegblẽ kple mumũ gã!

english_verse: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
translation_verse: Moab mũ dze anyi, eye wo viwo le ɣlikpɛ dom.

english_verse: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
translation_verse: Wole avi fam lia Luxit ƒe to dzi mɔ la, eye konyifaɣli le ɖiɖim le wo nu le Xoronayim ƒe abu nu le gbegblẽ la ta.

english_verse: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
translation_verse: Misi, miɖe miaƒe agbe, eye minɔ abe ame ɖeƒeƒle le gbegbe ene.

english_verse: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
translation_verse: Esi nèle dzi ɖom ɖe wò dɔwɔwɔwo kple wò kesinɔnuwo ŋu la, eyata woaxɔ wò hã, eye Kamos ayi aboyo me hekpe ɖe eƒe trɔ̃nuawo kple amegãwo ŋu.

english_verse: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
translation_verse: Nugblẽla ava du sia du me, eye dua ɖeke masi o, bali me nu ayi, eye tagba atsrɔ̃, abe alesi Yehowa gblɔ ene.

english_verse: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
translation_verse: Mina aʋala Moab, ne wòadzò adzo; eƒe duwo le aƒedo zu ge, amea ɖeke manɔ wo me o.

english_verse: I want you to kill the Moabites, and if you let them escape, I will put a curse on you.”
