translation_verse: Aɖi amesi le alɔgblɔlɔ wɔm le Yehowa ƒe dɔ ŋu la ŋuti, eye aɖi amesi he eƒe yi ɖe megbe tso ʋukɔkɔɖi me la ŋu kpekpekpe.

english_verse: Moab, you are like wine left to settle undisturbed, never poured from jar to jar. And so, your nation continues to prosper and improve.
translation_verse: Moab li bɔkɔɔ tso eƒe ɖevime ke, eɖo ƒã ɖi kpoo, eye wometrɔe tso goe me ko ɖe goe bubu me o, eye meyi aboyo me o, eyata eƒe vivi gale eŋu, eye eƒe ʋeʋẽ metrɔ o.

english_verse: But now, I will send enemies to pour out the wine and smash the jars!
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Eyata kpɔ ɖa, ŋkeke li gbɔna, eye madɔ goeviãlawo ɖa, ne woaviãe, woaɖi ƒuƒlu eƒe goewo, eye woagbã eƒe zewo.

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ŋu akpe Moab ɖe Kamos ŋu, abe alesi ŋu kpe Israel ƒe aƒe la ɖe Betel, si ŋu woɖo dzi ɖo la ŋu ene.

english_verse: You claim that your soldiers are strong and brave.
translation_verse: Aleke mianɔ gbɔgblɔm be: Kalẽtɔwo míenye, eye ŋutsu aʋamewo míenye?

english_verse: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
translation_verse: Fia, si ŋkɔ nye Yehowa Zebaot la be: Moab kple eƒe duwo gblẽla gbɔna xoxo, eye eƒe ɖekakpui tiatiawo yina ɖe amewuƒe.

english_verse: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
translation_verse: Moab ƒe gbegblẽ tu aƒe, ne woava eme, eye eƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃e le du dzi ŋutɔ.

english_verse: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
translation_verse: Mi eƒe aƒelikawo katã kple amesiwo katã nya eƒe ŋkɔ la, mifa nɛ! Migblɔ be: Aleke ati tɔɖeŋu sesẽ la, atikplɔ nyo la ŋe?

english_verse: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
translation_verse: Dibon-nyɔnuvi, ɖi tso wò ŋutikɔkɔe me, nabɔbɔ nɔ ke me; elabena Moab-gblẽla le ƒoƒo ge ɖe dziwò, eye wòagblẽ wò mɔ sesẽwo.

english_verse: You people of Aroer, go wait beside the road, and when refugees run by, ask them, “What happened?”
translation_verse: Aroer-nyɔnu, va tsi tre ɖe mɔ to nanɔ ŋu tsam, bia amesiwo si, eye wokplɔ la bena: Nya kae dzɔ?

english_verse: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Ŋukpe lé Moab, elabena wogbãe. Mifa avi, eye mido ɣli, mido boblo le Arnon nu be: Wogblẽ Moab!

english_verse: I will punish every town that belongs to Moab, but especially Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,
translation_verse: Ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ va gbadzaƒe nyigba, Xolon, Yaza kple Mefaat dzi,

english_verse: Dibon, Nebo, Beth-Diblathaim,
translation_verse: Dibon, Neho kple Bet-Diblatayim dzi.

english_verse: Kiriathaim, Beth-Gamul, Beth-Meon,
translation_verse: Kiryatayim, Bet-Gamul kple Bet-Meon dzi,

english_verse: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Wòŋe Moab ƒe dzo, eye wolã eƒe alɔ.

english_verse: People of Moab, you claim to be stronger than I am. Now I will tell other nations to make you drunk and to laugh while you collapse in your own vomit.
translation_verse: Mina aha Moab, ne wòano amu, be wòadze anyi ɖe eƒe xeɖeɖe me, ne eya hã nazu alɔmeɖenu, elabena Yehowa ŋu wòtɔ asi akɔ ɖo.

english_verse: You made fun of my people and treated them like criminals caught in the act.
translation_verse: Ɖe Israel mezu alɔmeɖenu na wò oa? Fiafiwo domee wolée le, hafi ne ènya ƒo nu le eŋu ko la, nènɔa ta ʋu ʋuma?

english_verse: Now you must leave your towns and live like doves in the shelter of cliffs and canyons.
translation_verse: Mi Moabitɔwo, migblẽ miaƒe duwo ɖi, ne miaɖanɔ agatowo me, minɔ abe akpakpa, si wɔ atɔ ɖe agakpewo toga ene.

english_verse: I know about your pride, and how you strut and boast.
translation_verse: Míese Moab dadala ŋkɔ be, edoa eɖokui ɖe dzi ŋutɔ, eƒoa adegbe, edana, edzraa eɖokui, eye eƒe dzi doa eɖokui ɖe dzi.

english_verse: But I also know bragging will never save you.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Menya eƒe dɔmedzoe dodo kple eƒe numeɖiɖi, eƒe nu wɔwɔ mele ɖeke me o.

english_verse: So I will cry and mourn for Moab and its town of Kir-Heres.
translation_verse: Eyata mafa avi ɖe Moab ŋu, mado ɣli ɖe Moab blibo la ŋu, eye maɖe hã ɖe Kir-Xeres-ŋutsuwo ŋu.

english_verse: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
translation_verse: Sibna ƒe weinka, mafa avi na wò, wu alesi mefa avi na Yaezer, wò kawo to atsiaƒu dzi vaseɖe ƒu nu le Yaezer, nugblẽla va ƒo ɖi le wò kutsetsegbeɣi kple wò weinxaɣi.

english_verse: Harvest celebrations are gone from the orchards and farms of Moab. I have silenced the shouts of people making wine.
translation_verse: Dzidzɔ kple aseyetsotso nu tso le agblewo me le Moab-nyigba dzi; metsi wein nu le weinfiãnu me, eye womagafiã wein kple aseyetsotso azɔ o; aseyetsotso maganye aseyetsotso o!

english_verse: Weeping from Heshbon can be heard as far as Elealeh and Jahaz; cries from Zoar are heard in Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
translation_verse: Le Xesbon ƒe aƒadodo, si ɖi vaseɖe Eleale kple Yahaz ta wodo ɣli tso Zoar va ke ɖe Xoronayim vaseɖe Eglat etɔ̃lia ke, elabena Nimrim ƒe tsiwo hã amie.

english_verse: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Matsrɔ̃ amesiwo dea nuxeƒe, eye woɖoa dzudzɔ na woƒe mawuwo la ɖa le Moab.

english_verse: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
translation_verse: Eyata nye dzi axa nu ɖe Moab ŋu abe dzekuku ene, eye nye dzi axa nu ɖe Kir-Xeres-ŋutsuwo ŋu abe dzekuku ene, elabena nusiwo wotu ɖo la ƒe mlɔea dɔ̃.

english_verse: Moab lies broken! Listen to its people cry as they turn away in shame. Other nations are horrified at what happened, but still they mock her.
translation_verse: Aleke wòhegbãe ale? Mifa avi! Aleke Moab trɔ megbe kple ŋukpee? Moab zu alɔmeɖenu kple bibi na eƒe aƒelikawo katã.

english_verse: Moab, an enemy swoops down like an eagle spreading its wings over your land.
translation_verse: Elabena ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Futɔ la adzo abe hɔ̃ ene, eye wòake aʋala ɖe Moab dzi!

english_verse: Your cities and fortresses will be captured, and your warriors as fearful as women giving birth.
translation_verse: Wòxɔ duwo, eye wòxɔ mɔ̃ sesẽwo. Moab-kalẽtɔwo ƒe dzi le ɣemaɣi abe nyɔnu, si le ku lém ƒe dzi ene.

english_verse: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Wotsrɔ̃ Moab, eye meganye dukɔ azɔ o, elabena etɔ asi akɔ ɖe Yehowa ŋu.

english_verse: Terror, pits, and traps are waiting for you.
translation_verse: Mi Moabitɔwo, Yehowa be: Ŋɔdzi, ʋe kple mɔ̃ka le mia ŋu.

english_verse: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Amesi si le ŋɔdzi nu la, age adze ʋe me, eye amesi do le ʋe me la, mɔ̃ka aɖee. Elabena Yehowa be: Mahe toheɣi avae na Moab.

english_verse: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
translation_verse: Amesisiawo tsra wɔɔ ɖe vɔvɔli te le Xesbon; elabena dzo tso Xesbon, eye dzoƒaɖe tso Sixon, efiã Moab ƒe tonuƒui kple ʋunyaʋunyaviwo ƒe dzodzome.

english_verse: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
translation_verse: Moab, baba na wò! Kamos-dukɔ tsrɔ̃, elabena wokplɔ wò ŋutsuviwo ɖade gaxɔ me, eye wokplɔ wò nyɔnuviwo yi aboyo mee.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Ke magaɖo Moab te le ŋkeke mlɔeawo me. Moab ƒe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ seƒe enye si.

english_verse: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
translation_verse: Ɖe Amon-viwo ŋu: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: ɖe ŋutsuvia ɖeke mele Israel si, alo domenyilaa ɖeke mele esi oa? Nukaŋuti Malkam xɔ Gad wɔ etɔe, eye eƒe dukɔ le eƒe duwo me?

english_verse: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
translation_verse: Eyata Yehowa be: Kpɔ ɖa, ŋkeke li gbɔna, eye mana aʋaɣli naɖi ɖe Amon-viwo ƒe Raba ŋu, be woazu anyiglãgo, woatɔ dzo eŋu duwo, eye Israel agaxɔ eƒe domenyinu, Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
translation_verse: Xesbon, fa avi, elabena wogblẽ Ai! Mi Raba-nyɔnuviwo mido ɣli, eye mita akpanya ɖe ali, mixa nu, eye mina tsa glãla tsam le lãkpɔwo me, elabena Malkam ayi aboyo me hekpe ɖe eƒe trɔ̃nuawo kple amegãwo ŋu.

english_verse: You rebellious Ammonites trust your wealth and ask, “Who could attack us?” But I warn you not to boast when your strength is fading.
translation_verse: Wò nyɔnuvi dzeaglã, si le dzi ɖom ɖe wò kesinɔnuwo ŋu, nukaŋuti nètso wò balime le adegbe ƒomee be, balime wɔnu wònye hele gbɔgblɔm be: Amekae ava gbɔnye?

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, Aƒetɔ, Yehowa Zebaot, be: Mana miaƒe aƒelikawo katã nahe ŋɔdzi ava mia dzi, woaka mi ahlẽ, eye amesiame aɖo ta eŋgɔ tẽ, ale be womaƒo sisilawo nu ƒu o.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
translation_verse: Ke emegbe la magaɖo Amon-viwo te, Yehowa ye gblɔe. Le Edom ŋuti.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says about Edom: Wisdom and common sense have vanished from Teman.
translation_verse: Ɖe Edom ŋu: Ale Yehowa Zebaot gblɔ esi: Ɖe nunyaa ɖeke megale Teman o, adaŋudede bu ɖe nunyalawo, eye wotrɔ nunya ƒo ɖe anyia?

english_verse: I will send disaster to punish you descendants of Esau, so anyone from Dedan had better turn around and run back home.
translation_verse: Mi Dedantɔwo, misi, mitrɔ dzo, eye miɣla mia ɖokui ɖe agu me; elabena mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ava Esau dzi le gbesigbe mahe to nɛ.

english_verse: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
translation_verse: Ne weintsetsexalawo ƒo ɖe dziwò la, womasusɔ mamlea ɖeke ɖi o; ne fiafitɔwo va le zã me la, woagblẽ nu, vaseɖe esime wòati kɔ na wo.

english_verse: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
translation_verse: Elabena maɖe ama Esau, maklo nu le eƒe bebeƒe dzi, be magatsi ɣaɣlaƒe o. Woatsrɔ̃ viawo, nɔviawo kple eƒe aƒelikawo, eye eya ŋutɔ nu ayi.

english_verse: But I can be trusted to care for your orphans and widows.
translation_verse: Gblẽ wò tsyɔ̃eviwo ɖi nam, maxɔ wo ɖe agbe, eye wò ahosiwo neɖo dzi ɖe ŋunye!

english_verse: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, amesiwo kplu la nono medze o hã, wononɛ kokoko, eye ɖe woagbe tohehe na wò ya? Matsi tomahemahe o, ke boŋ ànoe kokoko!

english_verse: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
translation_verse: Elabena ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Metà ɖokuinye ƒe agbe: Ne Bozra mazu ŋɔdzinu, alɔmeɖenu, aƒedo kple ɖiŋudonu, eye eƒe duwo katã nazu gbegbe mavɔ o fi!

english_verse: I have sent a messenger to command the nations to prepare for war against you people of Edom.
translation_verse: Mese nya tso Yehowa nu, eye woɖo ame ɖe dukɔwo dome be: Miƒo takpli miava ɖe wo ŋu, eye mitso miakpe aʋa!

english_verse: Your nation will be small, yet hated by other nations.
translation_verse: Elabena mewɔ wò sue le dukɔwo dome, eye medo vlo wò le amegbetɔwo dome.

english_verse: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
translation_verse: Ŋɔdzi lé wò; wò dzi ƒe dàda ble wò, wò amesi le agatowo me, eye nètso aƒe ɖe towo ƒe tsutsuẽƒe! Ne èwɔ atɔ ɖe kɔkɔƒe abe hɔ̃ ene hã la, matutu wò aƒu anyi tso afima, Yehowa ye gblɔe!

english_verse: People passing by your country will be shocked and horrified to see a disaster
translation_verse: Edom azu gbegbe, eye amesiame, si to eŋu yina la ƒe nu aku wòado tsia ɖe woƒe abixɔxɔwo katã ŋu.

english_verse: as bad as the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and towns nearby. The towns of Edom will be empty.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Amea ɖeke magatso aƒe ɖe afima o, eye amegbetɔvia ɖeke manɔ afima o, abe alesi wotrɔ Sodom kple Gomora kple woƒe aƒelikawo bu anyii ene.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ado tso Yordan ƒe aƒlawo me abe dzata ene ahayi lãnyiƒe, si de ama ɖaa la; elabena manyãe ɖa le eŋu le aɖabaƒoƒo ɖeka me, eye amesi metia la, eya matsɔ aɖo enu. Elabena ameka de nunye, ameka akplɔm ayi ʋɔnui, eye ameka nye lãkplɔvi anɔ te ɖe nunye?

english_verse: Listen to my plans for you, people of Edom. Your children will be dragged off and your country destroyed.
translation_verse: Eyata mise Yehowa ƒe adaŋu, si wòde ɖe Edom ŋu kple eƒe tame, si wòɖo ɖe Temantɔwo ŋu la: Vavã woakplɔ lã kudɔewo adzoe, eye woƒe lãnyiƒe ƒe nu aku ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will reach the Red Sea and cause the earth to shake.
translation_verse: Anyigba ʋuʋu le eƒe anyidzedze ƒe ɖiɖi ta, wose konyifaɣli le Avaƒu la nu ke.

english_verse: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, egbɔna abe hɔ̃ ene, eye wòadze akeke eƒe aʋala ɖe Bozra dzi, eye Edom-kalẽtɔwo ƒe dzi anɔ le ɣemaɣi abe nyɔnu, si le ku lém ƒe dzi ene. Le Damasko ŋuti.

english_verse: The Lord says about Damascus: The towns of Hamath and Arpad have heard your bad news. They have lost hope, and worries roll over them like ocean waves.
translation_verse: Ɖe Damasko ŋu: Ŋu kpe Xamat kple Arpad; elabena wose nya vɔ̃, eye dzi ɖe le wo ƒo; ŋɔdzi le atsiaƒu nu, womate ŋu agbɔ ɖe eme o.

english_verse: You people of Damascus have lost your courage, and in panic you turn to run, gripped by fear and pain.
translation_verse: Damasko ƒe lãme tu, etrɔ hesi, eye dzidzi ƒoe; ŋɔdzi kple vevesese va edzi abe nyɔnu léku ene.

english_verse: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
translation_verse: Aleke wogblẽ du nyɔnyɔ la, nye dzidzɔkpɔkpɔ ƒe mɔ̃ sesẽ la ɖi?

english_verse: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
translation_verse: Eyata woƒe ɖekakpuiwo atsi woƒe kpɔdomeewo, eye woƒe aʋawɔlawo katã atsrɔ̃ gbemagbe, Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
translation_verse: Eye matɔ dzo Damasko ƒe gliwo, ne wòafiã Ben-Hadad ƒe fiasãwo. Le Kedar kple Hazor fiaɖuƒe, siwo Nebukadnezar, Babel-fia, si la ŋuti.

english_verse: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
translation_verse: Ɖe Kedar kple Xazor-fiaɖuƒe, siwo Babel-fia Nebukadnezar si la ŋu: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Mitso, ne miaho ɖe Kedar ŋu, eye mitsrɔ̃ ɣedzeƒeviwo.

english_verse: His fearsome army will surround you, taking your tents and possessions, your sheep and camels.
translation_verse: Woaxɔ woƒe agbadɔwo kple alẽwo, woƒe agbadɔvɔwo kple woƒe nuwo katã, eye woakplɔ woƒe kposɔwo adzoe, woaɖo ɣli ɖe wo ŋu be: Ŋɔdzi li godoo!

english_verse: Run and hide, you people of the desert who live in villages! Nebuchadnezzar has big plans for you.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Mi Xazortɔwo, misi, afɔ nètsɔ na mi, eye miɣla mía ɖokui ɖe agu me; elabena Babel-fia de adaŋu ɖe mia ŋu, eye wòɖo ta me ɖe mia ŋu.

english_verse: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Mitso, míaho ɖe dukɔ, si ɖe dzi ɖi bɔkɔɔ la ŋu, agbo kple gameti mele wo si o, eye wole aga.

english_verse: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Woƒe kposɔwo kple woƒe lã gbogboawo azu nuhaha, eye makaka akotsolawo ahlẽ ɖe yawo katã me, eye mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e tso goawo katã me ava wo dzi, Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Only jackals will live where your villages once stood. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Elam
translation_verse: Xazor azu amegãxiwo nɔƒe, eye woazu gbegbe ɖaa, amea ɖeke matso aƒe ɖe afima o, eye amegbetɔvia ɖeke mana eme o. Le Elam ŋuti.

english_verse: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa Zebaot gblɔ esi: Maŋe Elam ƒe dati, si nye woƒe ŋusẽ vevietɔ la.

english_verse: Their armies will crush and kill you, and you will face the disaster that my anger brings.
translation_verse: Mana dzi naɖe le Elam ƒo le eƒe futɔwo kple eƒe kudilawo nu, mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e, nye dɔmedzoe heliheli, ava wo dzi, eye maɖo yi ɖe wo yome, vaseɖe esime woatsrɔ̃ avɔ, Yehowa ye gblɔe!

english_verse: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Mali nye fiazikpui ɖe Elam, eye matsrɔ̃ fia kple amegãwo siaa.

english_verse: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
translation_verse: Ke magaɖo Elam te le ŋkeke mlɔeawo me, Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe nya, si wògblɔ fe Babel kple Kaldea-nyigba ŋu to nyagblɔɖila Yeremya dzi la, enye si.

english_verse: Raise the signal flags; shout so all nations can hear— Babylon will be captured! Marduk, Babylon's god, will be ashamed and terrified, and his idols broken.
translation_verse: Mido kpo le dukɔwo dome, miɖe gbe ƒã, eye mido aflaga ɖe dzi! Miɖe gbe ƒã, migaɣlae o! Migblɔ be: Woxɔ Babel, ŋukpe lé Bel, eye wogbã Merodax ƒu anyi! Ŋukpe lé woƒe legbawo, eye wogbã woƒe mawuwo!

english_verse: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
translation_verse: Elabena dukɔa ɖe ho ɖe wo ŋu tso anyiehe, ne wòado aƒedo woƒe anyigba, be amea ɖeke naganɔ edzi o; amegbetɔwo kple lãwo siaa si, eye wobu dzo.

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Le ŋkeke mawo me, le ɣemaɣi la Israel-viwo kple Yuda-viwo siaa atrɔ agbɔ, eye woano avi dzi ava ɖi Yehowa, woƒe Mawu la.

english_verse: You will ask the way to Zion and then come and join with me in making an agreement you won't break or forget.
translation_verse: Woabia Zion ta ase, eye afima ma anɔ ŋku dzi na wo be: „Mina míaku ɖe Yehowa ŋu, eye míabla nu mava, si womaŋlɔ be akpɔ o!“

english_verse: My people, you are lost sheep abandoned in the mountains by their shepherds. You don't even remember your resting place.
translation_verse: Alẽ tatrawoe nye nye dukɔ; wo kplɔviwo flu wo, eye wokplɔ wo tra yi towo dzii, wole tsatsam tso to dzi yi togbɛ dzi, eye woŋlɔ wo miaƒe be.

english_verse: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
translation_verse: Amesiwo katã kpɔ wo la, ɖu wo, eye woƒe futɔwo gblɔ bena; Míeɖi to o, elabena ɖe wowɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Yehowa, woƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe lãnyiƒe, kple Yehowa, wo fofowo ƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ la ŋu.

english_verse: Escape from Babylonia, my people. Get out of that country! Don't wait for anyone else.
translation_verse: Misi tso Babel, miʋu tso Kaldea-nyigba dzi, eye minɔ abe agbowo le alẽhawo ŋgɔ ene!

english_verse: In the north I am bringing great nations together. They will attack Babylon and capture it. The arrows they shoot are like the best soldiers, always finding their target.
translation_verse: Elabena manyɔ dukɔ gãa ɖe tso anyiehe-nyigba dzi, eye makplɔ wo avɛ ɖe Babel ŋu, ne wòadze aʋa ɖe eŋu ahaxɔe; woƒe aŋukawo le abe kalẽtɔ dzeaɖaŋu tɔ ene, womedaa dadagbo o.

english_verse: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ale Kaldea azu nuhaha; amesiwo katã hãe la, aɖi ƒo, Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
translation_verse: Nye domenyinu halawo, minɔ dzidzɔ kpɔm, eye minɔ aseye tsom ko, miɖi adzrɔ abe nyinɔvi, si le lu tugum la ene, eye mixlɔ̃ abe sɔtsu ene.

english_verse: The city of Babylon was like a mother to you. But it will be disgraced and become nothing but a barren desert.
translation_verse: Ŋu akpe mia dada, mia no ƒe mo atsi dã; kpo ɖa, dukɔwo ƒe nuwuwu anye gbegbe, kuɖiɖi kple tagba!

english_verse: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
translation_verse: Le Yehowa ƒe dɔmedzoe ta azu aƒedo kple gbegbe ɖikaa, ale be amesiame, si to Babel ŋu yina la ƒe nu aku, eye wòado tsiã le woƒe abixɔxɔwo katã ta.

english_verse: Babylon has rebelled against me. Archers, take your places. Shoot all your arrows at Babylon.
translation_verse: Mi aŋutrɔdalawo katã, midze aʋa ɖe Babel ŋu godoo va kpe; mitee, eye migave nu le aŋutrɔ gbɔ o, elabena Yehowa ŋu wòwɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖo.

english_verse: Attack from every side! Babylon surrenders! The enemy tears down its walls and towers. I am taking my revenge by doing to Babylon what it did to other cities.
translation_verse: Mitso ayiboopɛɛ ɖe eŋu godoo; ena ta, eƒe sɔtiwo ŋe dze eme, eye eƒe gliwo mũ, elabena Yehowa ƒe hlɔ̃biabia nye esia; mibia hlɔ̃e, eye miwɔ nɛ, abe alesi wòwɔ ene!

english_verse: There is no one in Babylonia to plant or harvest crops. Even foreigners who lived there have left for their homelands, afraid of the enemy armies.
translation_verse: Mitsrɔ̃ nuƒãla kple nuŋela le nuŋeɣi ɖa le Babel! Amesiame trɔ yi eƒe dukɔ gbɔ, eye amesiame si yi eƒe anyigba dzi le yi wuame la ta.

english_verse: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
translation_verse: Israel la, alẽ, si wonyã de gbe, eye dzatawo yɔ ɖe nu la wònye; gbã la Asur-fia ɖui, emegbe Babel-fia Nebukadnezar kuko eƒe ƒuwo.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Eyata ale Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, mahe to na Babel-fia kple eƒe anyigba, abe alesi mehe to na Asur-fia ene.

english_verse: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
translation_verse: Magakplɔ Israel agbɔ va eƒe gbeɖuƒe, ne woaɖu gbe le Karmel dzi kple Basan, eye woaɖu nu aɖi ƒo le Efrayim-towo dzi kple Gilead.

english_verse: I will rescue a few people from Israel and Judah. I will forgive them so completely that their sin and guilt will disappear, never to be found. The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Le ŋkeke mawo me, le ɣemaɣi la woadi Israel ƒe vodada, ke manɔ anyi o, eye womagakpɔ Yuda ƒe nuvɔ̃wo o, elabena matsɔe ake amesiwo makpɔtɔ ɖi.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Ho ɖe aglãdzela vivivowo ƒe anyigba kple toheheviwo ŋu, wu ame, eye natsrɔ̃ woƒe susɔeawo gbidigbidi, eye nawɔ nusiwo katã ŋu mede se na wò le la.

english_verse: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Aʋaɣli kple gbegblẽ gã le anyigba dzi!

english_verse: Babylonia was a hammer pounding every country, but now it lies broken. What a shock to the nations of the world!
translation_verse: Aleke anyigba blibo la ƒe zũ gbã, eye wòkaka ale? Aleke Babel zu ŋɔdzinu le dukɔwo dome ale?

english_verse: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
translation_verse: Babel, meɖo mɔ̃ na wò, ke mèdze sii o, eye wòɖe wò; asi tu wò, eye wòlé; wò, elabena Yehowa ye nèwɔ avu kple.

english_verse: I've brought out my weapons, and with them I will put a curse on Babylonia.
translation_verse: Yehowa ʋu eƒe nudzraɖoƒe, eye wòɖe eƒe dziku ƒe aʋawɔnuwo do goe; elabena dɔ le; Aƒetɔ, Yehowa Zebaot ŋu le Kaldea-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Come from far away, you enemies of Babylon! Pile up the grain from its storehouses, and destroy it completely, along with everything else.
translation_verse: Mitso goawo katã me va ƒo ɖe edzi, miʋu nu le eƒe avawo nu, mihe trɔ ɖe anyi abe lubabla ene, eye mitsrɔ̃e gbidigbidi; migakpɔtɔ naneke ɖi nɛ o.

english_verse: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
translation_verse: Miwu woƒe nyitsuwo katã, mikplɔ wo yi wuƒee. Baba na wo, elabena woƒe toheɣi ɖo.

english_verse: The Babylonian army destroyed my temple, but soon I will take revenge. Then refugees from Babylon will tell about it in Zion.
translation_verse: Miƒu to anyi! Sisilawo kple amesiwo kpɔtɔ tso Babel-nyigba dzi va, be woaɖe gbe ƒã Yehowa, mía Mawu ƒe hlɔ̃biabia, eƒe hlɔ̃biabia ɖe eƒe gbedoxɔ nu le Zion!

english_verse: Attack Babylon, enemy archers; set up camp around the city, and don't let anyone escape. It challenged me, the holy God, so do to it what it did to other cities. Proud Babylon Will Fall
translation_verse: Miyɔ aŋutrɔdalawo ɖe Babel ŋu! Mi amesiwo katã hea da me, miɖe to ɖee godoo va kpe, amea ɖeke megakpɔtɔ o! Miɖo eƒe nuwɔna teƒe nɛ, miwɔ nɛ pɛpɛpɛ, abe alesi wòwɔ ene, elabena Yehowa, Israel ƒe kɔkɔetɔ la ŋu wòwɔ nu tovo ɖo.

english_verse: People of Babylon, I, the Lord, promise that even your best soldiers will lie dead in the streets.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Eyata woƒe ɖekakpuiwo atsi woƒe kpɔdomeewo, eye woƒe aʋawɔlawo katã atsrɔ̃ gbemagbe.

english_verse: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Yehowa Zebaot, be: Kpɔ ɖa, mado ɖe dziwò, wò ame tovo; elabena: wò ŋkeke ɖe, wò toheɣi ɖo.

english_verse: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
translation_verse: Ame tovo la akli nu adze anyi, eye amea ɖeke mafɔe ɖe tsitrenu o, matɔ dzo eƒe duwo, ne wòabi eƒe nutowo katã me.

english_verse: You Babylonians were cruel to Israel and Judah. You took them captive, and now you refuse to let them go.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa Zebaot gblɔ esi: Wote Israel-viwo kple Yuda-viwo siaa ɖe anyi, eye amesiwo katã ɖe aboyo wo la, va wo goŋgoŋ, gbe be, yewomaɖe asi le wo ŋu o.

english_verse: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, will rescue and protect them. I will bring peace to their land and trouble to yours.
translation_verse: Ke wo ɖela sesẽ, eŋkɔ nye Yehowa Zebaot. Adrɔ̃ woƒe nya ade goe, ne wòana gbɔdzɔe anyigba, eye wòaɖe zi Babeltɔwo me.

english_verse: I have declared war on you, your officials, and advisors.
translation_verse: Yehowa be, yi neva Kaldeatɔwo, Babeltɔwo kple woƒe amegãwo kple woƒe nunyalawo dzi!

english_verse: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
translation_verse: Yi neva woƒe afakalawo dzi, ne woazu bometsilawo! Yi neva woƒe kalẽtɔwo dzi, ne dzi naɖe le wo ƒo!

english_verse: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
translation_verse: Yi neva woƒe sɔwo kple woƒe tasiaɖamwo kpakple amedzro, siwo katã le wo dome la dzi, ne woazu nyɔnugbɔmewo! Yi neva woƒe kesinɔnuwo dzi, ne woaha wo!

english_verse: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
translation_verse: Kuɖiɖi neva na woƒe tsiwo, ne woamie! Elabena legbawo ƒe anyigba wònye, eye wotsɔ ŋɔdzinuwo le adegbe ƒomee.

english_verse: Never again will people live in your land— only desert animals, jackals, and unclean birds.
translation_verse: Eyata gbedadiwo kple amegãxiwo atso aƒe ɖi, eye golowo anɔ afima; ame magatso aƒe ɖi akpɔ o, eye ame manɔ eme o, tso dzidzime yi dzidzime.

english_verse: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Ame matso aƒe ɖe afima alo amegbetɔvia ɖe nanɔ eme o, abe alesi Mawu trɔ Sodom kple Gomora kpakple woƒe aƒelikawo bu anyii ene.

english_verse: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, dukɔa ɖe tso anyiehe gbɔna, eye dukɔ gãa ɖe kple fia geɖewo ho tso anyigba ƒe mlɔenu.

english_verse: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
translation_verse: Da kple akplɔ le wo si, ŋutasẽlawo wonye, eye womekpɔa nublanui o; woƒe ɣli le abe atsiaƒu ƒe gbeɖeɖe ene, wole sɔ dzi, eye wòbia akpa abe aʋawɔla ene ɖe wò Babel-nyɔnuvi ŋu.

english_verse: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
translation_verse: Esi Babel-fia se nya le wo ŋu la, eƒe asiwò ɖo agblɔ, vɔvɔ̃ ɖoe, eye wose veve abe nyɔnu léku ene.

english_verse: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ado tso Yordan ƒe aƒlawo me abe dzata ene ayi ɖe lãnyiƒe, si de ama ɖaa la; elabena manyãe ɖa le eŋu le aɖabaƒoƒo ɖeka me, eye amesi metia la, eya matsɔ ado enu. Elabena amekae so kplim, amekae akplɔm ayi ʋɔnui, eye amekae nye lãkplɔvi, si anɔ te ɖe nunye?

english_verse: Listen to my plans for you, people of Babylonia. Your children will be dragged off, and your country destroyed.
translation_verse: Eyata mise Yehowa ƒe adaŋu, si wòde ɖe Babel ŋu, kple eƒe tame, si wòɖo ɖe Kaldea-nyigba ŋu: Vavã woakplɔ lã kudɔewo adzoe, eye woƒe lãnyiƒe ƒe nu aku ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will be heard among the nations, and the earth will shake.
translation_verse: Anyigba ʋuʋu, eye wose konyifaɣli le dukɔwo dome le ɣli, si ɖi be, woxɔ Babel la ta.

english_verse: I, the Lord, am sending a wind to destroy the people of Babylonia and Babylon, its capital.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Manyɔ nugblẽla ƒe gbɔgbɔ ɖe Babel kple amesiwo le nye futɔwo ƒe domedomee la ŋu.

english_verse: Foreign soldiers will come from every direction, and when the disaster is over, Babylonia will be empty and worthless.
translation_verse: Madɔ amedzrowo ɖe Babel ŋu, ne woagbɔe, eye woadi gbolo eƒe anyigba, elabena woaƒo ɖe edzi le dzɔgbevɔ̃egbe tso goawo katã me.

english_verse: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
translation_verse: Aŋutrɔdalawo nehe da me ɖe amesi he da me kple amesi le gawu me la ŋu! Migakpɔ woƒe ɖekakpuiwo ta o, eye mitsrɔ̃ woƒe aʋakɔ blibo la;

english_verse: Their troops will fall wounded in the streets of Babylon.
translation_verse: ne ame tsiaʋawo nanɔ Kaldea-nyigba dzi, eye amesiwo woda nui lã, nanɔ woƒe ablɔwo me.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel and Judah is guilty. But I, the Lord All-Powerful, their holy God, have not abandoned them.
translation_verse: Ke woƒe Mawu, Yehowa Zebaot, megblẽ Israel kple Yuda ɖi wonye ahosi o; elabena anyigba ma ɖi to geɖe ɖe Israel ƒe kɔkɔetɔ la ŋu.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon! Run for your lives! If you stay, you will be killed when I take revenge on the city and punish it for its sins.
translation_verse: Misi dzo le Babel, eye amesiame neɖe eƒe agbe, ne míagatsrɔ̃ ɖe woƒe vodadawo me o, elabena Yehowa ƒe hlɔ̃biaɣi enye esia; nusi wòwɔ la, eya teƒe woaɖo nɛ.

english_verse: Babylon was my golden cup, filled with the wine of my anger. The nations of the world got drunk on this wine and went insane.
translation_verse: Sikakplu enye Babel le Yehowa si me, si na anyigba blibo la mũ aha; dukɔwo no eƒe wein, eyata dukɔwo le ya mum sagãsagã ɖo.

english_verse: But suddenly, Babylon will fall and be destroyed. I, the Lord, told the foreigners who lived there, “Weep for the city! Get medicine for its wounds; maybe they will heal.”
translation_verse: Zi ɖeka kasia Babel ge dze anyi hegbã. Mifa avi ɖe eŋu, miɖatsɔ atike vɛ hena eƒe veveseseawo, ɖewohĩ eƒe lãme ahaya.

english_verse: The foreigners answered, “We have already tried to treat Babylon's wounds, but they would not heal. Come on, let's all go home to our own countries. Nothing is left in Babylonia; everything is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Miehe, míada gbe le Babel ŋu, ke hayahaya mele eŋu o; eyata migblẽè ɖi, eye mia dome amesiame neyi eƒe anyigba dzi, elabena eƒe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ de dziƒo ke, eye wòɖatɔ alilikpowo.

english_verse: I, the Lord, want Babylon destroyed, because its army destroyed my temple. So, you kings of Media, sharpen your arrows and pick up your shields.
translation_verse: Minyre aŋutrɔwo, mikpla akpoxɔnuwo! Yehowa nyɔ Media-fiawo ƒe gbɔgbɔ, eye wode adaŋu ɖe Babel ŋu, be woagblẽe; elabena Yehowa ƒe hlɔ̃biabiae, hlɔ̃biabia ɖe eƒe gbedoxɔ nue.

english_verse: People of Babylon, you live along the Euphrates River and are surrounded by canals. You are rich, but now the time has come for you to die.
translation_verse: Wò amesi le lɔ gãwo to, eye kesinɔnu ɖo agbogbo ɖe asiwò, wò nuwuwu ɖo, eye dzidze, si nu woalã wò ɖo la ɖe!

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, swear by my own life that enemy soldiers will fill your streets like a swarm of locusts. They will shout and celebrate their victory. A Hymn of Praise (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Yehowa Zebaot la eƒe agbe be: Ne metsɔ amewo yɔ wò taŋ abe ʋetsuviwo ene hã la, woatso ayiboopɛɛ ɖe ŋuwò!

english_verse: The waters in the heavens roar at his command. He makes clouds appear; he sends the wind from his storehouse and makes lightning flash in the rain.
translation_verse: Eƒe gbeɖeɖe nana tsiwo ɖina hoo le dziƒo, eye wònana atu hona yia dzi tso anyigba ƒe mlɔenu; ewɔa dzikedzo kpena ɖe tsidzadza ŋu, eye wòɖea ya donae tsoa eƒe nudzraɖoƒe.

english_verse: God used his wisdom and power to create the earth and spread out the heavens.
translation_verse: Eya amesi tsɔ eƒe ŋusẽ wɔ anyigba, tsɔ eƒe nunya ɖo xexeame anyi, eye wòtsɔ eƒe gɔmesese keke dziƒo mee.

english_verse: People who make idols are stupid! They will be disappointed, because their false gods cannot breathe.
translation_verse: Amegbetɔwo katã dzɔa lã le woƒe nunya me, eye ŋukpe léa legbakɔlawo katã, elabena alakpa enye nusi wokɔna, eye gbɔgbɔa ɖeke menɔa eme o.

english_verse: Idols are merely a joke, and when the time is right, they will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Nu dzodzroawo wonye, dɔwɔwɔ, si ŋu woaɖe alɔme le la wonye; woatsrɔ̃ le gbesigbe woahe to na wo.

english_verse: But the Lord, Israel's God, is all-powerful. He created everything, and he chose Israel to be his very own. God's Hammer The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ke Yakob ƒe gome mele abe woamawo ene o, elabena eyama nye nuwo katã wɔla, eye Israel enye eya ŋutɔ ƒe ƒome; Yehowa Zebaot enye eƒe ŋkɔ.

english_verse: Babylonia, you were my hammer; I used you to pound nations and break kingdoms,
translation_verse: Zũ kple aʋawɔnu nènye nam, wòe matsɔ agbã dukɔwoe gudugudu, eye wòe matsɔ atsrɔ̃ fiaɖuƒewoe.

english_verse: shepherds and their flocks, farmers and their oxen, and governors and leaders.
translation_verse: wòe matso agba lãkplɔvi kple lãha, wòe matsɔ agbã agbledela kple eƒe lãwo, eye wòe matsɔ agba anyigbanunɔla kple amegãwo.

english_verse: But now, my people will watch, while I repay you for what you did to Zion.
translation_verse: Ke mahe to na Babel kple Kaldeatɔwo katã le mia ŋku me le woƒe vɔ̃, siwo katã wowɔ ɖe Zion ŋu la ta, Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: You destroyed the nations and seem strong as a mountain, but I am your enemy. I might even grab you and roll you off a cliff. When I am finished, you'll only be a pile of scorched bricks.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Kpɔ ɖa, maƒo ɖe dziwò, wò togblẽnu, si tsrɔ̃ anyigba blibo la, maɖo nye asi ɖa ɖe ŋuwò ahamli wò tso agakpe dzi aƒu anyi, eye matsɔ wò awɔ to fiafiãe,

english_verse: Your stone blocks won't be reused for cornerstones or foundations, and I promise that forever you will be a desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Nations Will Attack Babylon The Lord said:
translation_verse: ale be womagatsɔ wò kpea ɖeke awɔ dzogoekpe alo gɔmeɖokpee o, elabena azu gbegbe tegbee, Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Signal the nations to get ready to attack. Raise a flag and blow a trumpet. Send for the armies of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Choose a commander; let the cavalry attack like a swarm of locusts.
translation_verse: Mitu aflaga ɖe anyigba dzi, miku kpẽ le dukɔwo dome, mikɔ dukɔwo ŋu ɖe eŋuti, miyɔ fiaɖuƒewo ɖe eŋuti tso Ararat, Mini kple Askenas, miɖo aʋafiawo ɖe eŋuti, eye mikplɔ sɔwo vɛ abe ʋetsuvi tofuwo ene!

english_verse: Tell the kings and governors, the leaders and the people of the kingdoms of the Medes to prepare for war!
translation_verse: Mikɔ dukɔwo ŋu ɖe eŋuti, Media-fiawo, woƒe anyigbanunɔlawo kple woƒe amegãwo katã kpakple woƒe fiaɖuƒe ƒe anyigba blibo la!

english_verse: The earth twists and turns in torment, because I have decided to make Babylonia a desert where no one can live, and I won't change my mind.
translation_verse: Tete anyigba ʋuʋu, eye dzidzi ƒoe, elabena Yehowa wo eƒe tame, si wòɖo ɖe Babel ŋu, be yeana Babel-nyigba nazu gbegbe, eye ame navɔ le edzi la dzi.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers have lost their strength and courage. They stay in their fortresses, unable to fight, while the enemy breaks through the city gates, then sets their homes on fire.
translation_verse: Babel-kalẽtɔwo dzudzɔ aʋawɔwɔ, wobɔbɔ no woƒe mɔ̃wo me, eye ŋusẽ vɔ le wo ŋu wozu nyɔnugbɔmewo; wotɔ dzo woƒe nɔƒewo, eye wòŋe woƒe gametiwo.

english_verse: One messenger after another announces to the king, “Babylon has been captured!
translation_verse: Duƒula yi ɖakpe duƒula, eye duxɔla yi ɖakpe duxɔla, ne woagblɔ na Babel-fia be, wòxɔ eƒe du la le goawo katã me,

english_verse: The enemy now controls the river crossings! The marshes are on fire! Your army has panicked!”
translation_verse: wòxɔ tɔtsoƒewo, wòtɔ dzo tɔʋuwo, eye dzi ɖe le aʋawɔlawo ƒo.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I make this promise— “Soon Babylon will be leveled and packed down like a threshing place at harvest time.” Babylonia Will Pay!
translation_verse: Elabena ale Yehowa Zebaot, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ esi: Babel-nyɔnuvi le abe lugbɔƒe le ɣeyiɣi, si me woƒoa eme dana ɖi la ene; esusɔ vie ko, ne nuŋeɣi naɖo nɛ.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem say, “King Nebuchadnezzar made us panic. That monster stuffed himself with us and our treasures, leaving us empty— he gobbled up what he wanted and spit out the rest.
translation_verse: Babel-fia Nebukadnezar ɖu mí, etsrɔ̃ mi, eye wòtsɔ mí wɔ goe ƒuƒlui, emi mi abe ʋɔ ene, etsɔ míaƒe nu viviwo yɔ eƒe ƒodoe, eye wònyã mí de gbe.

english_verse: The people of Babylonia harmed some of us and killed others. Now, Lord, make them pay!” The Lord Will Take Revenge on Babylon
translation_verse: Zion-nyɔnu negblɔ be: Ŋuta, si wosẽ le ŋunye, kple nye ŋutilã neva Babel dzi! Yerusalem negblɔ be: Nye ʋu neva Kaldeatɔwo dzi!

english_verse: My people, I am on your side, and I will take revenge on Babylon. I will cut off its water supply, and its stream will dry up.
translation_verse: Eyata ale Yehowa gblɔ esi: Madrɔ̃ wò nya, eye mabia hlɔ̃ na wò, mana woƒe atsiaƒu naƒu kplakplakpla, eye woƒe vudo namie.

english_verse: Babylon will be a pile of rubble where only jackals live, and everyone will be afraid to walk among the ruins.
translation_verse: Babel azu anyiglãgo kple amegãxiwo nɔƒe, azu gbegbe kple tsiãdonu, eye ame avɔ le eme.

english_verse: The Babylonians roar and growl like young lions.
translation_verse: Wo katã le xɔxlɔ̃m abe dzatawo ene, eye wole gbe tem abe dzataviwo ene.

english_verse: And since they are hungry, I will give them a banquet. They will celebrate, get drunk, then fall asleep, never to wake up!
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Ne woƒe lãme tɔ dzo la, matu aglo na wo, eye mana woamu aha, ne woada alɔ̃ tegbetegbe, eye womaganyɔ akpɔ o.

english_verse: I will lead them away to die, like sheep, lambs, and goats being led to the butcher.
translation_verse: Mana woakplɔ wo ayi wuƒe abe alẽviwo, agbowo kple gbɔ̃tsuwo ene.

english_verse: All nations now praise Babylon, but when it is captured, those same nations will be horrified.
translation_verse: Aleke asi su Sesax dzi, eye woxɔ anyigba blibo la ƒe adegbeƒonu, aleke Babel zu ŋɔdzidonu le dukɔwo dome ale?

english_verse: Babylon's enemies will rise like ocean waves and flood the city.
translation_verse: Atsiaƒu ƒo ɖe Babel dzi, eye eƒe tsotsoewo ƒe nyanyrã nyẽ tsyɔ edzi.

english_verse: Horrible destruction will strike the nearby towns. The land will become a barren desert, where no one can live or even travel.
translation_verse: Eƒe duwo zu gbegbe, kuɖiɖinyigba kple tagba, anyigba, si dzi amea ɖeke mele o, eye amegbetɔvia ɖeke metona yina o.

english_verse: I will punish Marduk, the god of Babylon, and make him vomit out everything he gobbled up. Then nations will no longer bring him gifts, and Babylon's walls will crumble. The Lord Offers Hope to His People
translation_verse: Mahe to na Babel ƒe Bel, maɖe nusi wòmi la le nu me ne, eye dukɔwo magaƒo zi ɖe eŋu azɔ o; Babel ƒe gliwo hã amũ.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon, my people, and run for your lives, before I strike the city in my anger!
translation_verse: Nye dukɔ, midzo le egbɔ, eye amesiame neɖe eƒe agbe tso Yehowa ƒe dɔmedzoe heliheli la nu!

english_verse: The time will come when I will punish Babylon's false gods. Everyone there will die, and the whole nation will be disgraced,
translation_verse: Eyata kpɔ ɖa, ŋkeke li gbɔna, eye mahe to na Babel ƒe legbawo, ŋukpe alé eƒe anyigba blibo la, eye eƒe ame tsiaʋawo katã atsi eme.

english_verse: when an army attacks from the north and brings destruction. Then the earth and the heavens and everything in them will celebrate.
translation_verse: Dziƒo kple anyigba kple edzi nuwo katã atso aseye ɖe Babel ŋu; elabena nugblẽla atso anyiehe ava ƒo ɖe edzi, Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Babylon must be overthrown, because it slaughtered the people of Israel and of many other nations.
translation_verse: Israel ƒe ame tsiaʋawo, ele na Babel hã be, woatsi aʋa, abe alesi anyigba blibo la ƒe amewo tsi aʋa le Babel ta ene.

english_verse: My people, you escaped death when Jerusalem fell. Now you live far from home, but you should trust me and think about Jerusalem. Leave Babylon! Don't stay!
translation_verse: Mi amesiwo si le yi nu, midzo, eye migatɔ ɖi o! Miɖo ŋu Yehowa le adzɔge, eye Yerusalem nenɔ ta me na mi!

english_verse: Soon I will send a war to punish Babylon's idols and leave its wounded people moaning everywhere.
translation_verse: Yehowa be: Kpɔ ɖa, ŋkeke li gbɔna, eye mahe to na woƒe legbawo, eye ame tsiaʋawo anɔ ŋeŋem le anyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: Although Babylon's walls reach to the sky, the army I send will destroy that city. I, the Lord, have spoken. Babylon Will Be Destroyed The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ne Babel lia dziŋgɔli me, eye eƒe mɔ̃ sesẽwo mele lialia o hã la, nugblẽla atso gbɔnye ava ƒo ɖe edzi, Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Listen to the cries for help coming from Babylon. Everywhere in the country the sounds of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Miƒu to anyi, ɣli ɖi tso Babel, eye mumũ gãa ɖe tso Kaldea-nyigba dzi!

english_verse: The shouts of the enemy, like crashing ocean waves, will drown out Babylon's cries as I level the city.
translation_verse: Elabena Yehowa atsrɔ̃ Babel, eye wòatsi eƒe hoowɔwɔ nu, eƒe tsitsotsoewo adze agbo abe lɔ gãwo tɔ ene, eye woƒe gbeɖeɖe nu asẽ.

english_verse: An enemy will attack and destroy Babylon. Its soldiers will be captured and their weapons broken, because I am a God who takes revenge against nations for what they do.
translation_verse: Elabena nugblẽla aƒo ɖe Babel dzi, eye wòaɖe aboyo eƒe kalẽtɔwo, eye woƒe dawo aŋe, elabena Mawu nuteƒeɖola enye Yehowa, eye ahe to kokoko.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the true King, promise that the officials and advisors, the governors and leaders, and the soldiers of Babylon will get drunk, fall asleep, and never wake up.
translation_verse: Eye mana aha woƒe tatɔwo kple woƒe nunyalawo, woƒe anyigbanunɔlawo kple woƒe amegãwo kpakple woƒe kalẽtɔwo woano amu, eye woadɔ alɔ̃ tegbetegbe, womaganyɔ o; fia, si ŋkɔ nye Yehowa Zebaot lae gblɔe.

english_verse: The thick walls of that city will be torn down, and its huge gates burned. Everything that nation worked so hard to gain will go up in smoke. Jeremiah Gives Seraiah a Scroll
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa Zebaot gblɔ esi: Woagbã Babel ƒe gli kekeawo vaseɖe agunu ke, eye woatɔ dzo eƒe agbo kɔkɔwo, ale be wòanye ɖeko dukɔwo wɔ dɔ ɖe ya me, eye anyigbadzitɔwo ku kutri hena dze.

english_verse: During Zedekiah's fourth year as king of Judah, he went to Babylon. And Baruch's brother Seraiah went along as the officer in charge of arranging for places to stay overnight.
translation_verse: Nyagblɔɖila Yeremya ƒe nya, si wòtsɔ de se na Seraya, Maxseya vi, Neriya ƒe vi, esime woa kple Yuda-fia Zedekiya woyina Babel le eƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒe enelia me, eye Seraya nye mɔzɔmegã la, enye si.

english_verse: Before they left, I wrote on a scroll all the terrible things that would happen to Babylon.
translation_verse: Tete Yeremya ŋlɔ dzɔgbevɔ̃e, siwo katã le Babel dzi va ge la, ɖe agbalẽ me; eya nye nya, siwo katã woŋlɔ ɖe Babel ŋu.

english_verse: I gave the scroll to Seraiah and said: When you get to Babylon, read this scroll aloud,
translation_verse: Eye Yeremya gblɔ na Seraya bena; Ne èva Babel la, ekema ɖo ŋu anyi, eye naxlẽ nya siawo katã

english_verse: then pray, “Our Lord, you promised to destroy this place and make it into a desert where no people or animals will ever live.”
translation_verse: gblɔ bena: Yehowa, wòe gblɔ ɖe teƒe sia ŋu be, yeatsrɔ̃e, ne amea ɖeke maganɔ anyi o, amegbetɔwo kple lãwo siaa, eye wòanye gbegbe tegbee.

english_verse: When you finish praying, tie the scroll to a rock and throw it in the Euphrates River. Then say,
translation_verse: Eye ne èxlẽ agbalẽ sia vɔ la, ekema bia kpe ɖe eŋu, natsɔe aƒu gbe ɖe Frat me

english_verse: “This is how Babylon will sink when the Lord destroys it. Everyone in the city will die, and it won't have the strength to rise again.” The End of Jeremiah's Writing Jeremiah's writing ends here.
translation_verse: agblɔ bena: Ale dzɔgbevɔ̃e, si mahe va wo dzi la, anyrɔ Babel ɖe toe, magaɖo ɖe dzi akpɔ o, eye enu ayi. Yeremya ƒe nyawo seƒe enye si.

english_verse: Next, Nebuzaradan arrested Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah his assistant, and three temple officials.
translation_verse: Eye fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã kplɔ nunɔlagã Seraya kple nunɔlagã yometɔ Zefanya kpakple kpuinudzɔla etɔ̃

english_verse: then his eyes were poked out. He was put in chains, then dragged off to Babylon and kept in prison until he died.
translation_verse: Egbã ŋku na Zedekiya, eye wòde kɔsɔkɔsɔe, eye Babel-fia kplɔe yi Babel hetsɔe ɖe gaxɔ me vaseɖe eƒe kugbe.

english_verse: meters around. They were hollow, but the bronze was about
translation_verse: Woɖe to ɖe dua, vaseɖe Zedekiya ƒe ƒe wuiɖekɛlia me.

english_verse: After a year and a half, all the food in Jerusalem was gone. Then on the ninth day of the fourth month,
translation_verse: Le dzinu enelia ƒe ŋkeke asiekelia dzi la dɔwuame nu sẽ le dua me, ale be aboloa ɖeke megali na dukɔ hahoo la o.

english_verse: the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the Jordan River valley,
translation_verse: Woŋɔ mɔ ɖe dua ŋu, eye aʋawɔlawo ka tã si to fia ƒe abɔ me mɔ, to agbo, si le gli ŋukplaba eve dome la nu hegblẽ du la ɖi le zã me, eye wòto gbegbemɔ; ke Kaldeatɔwo le glia ŋu godoo.

english_verse: Zedekiah was taken to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty.
translation_verse: Tete wòlé fia la hekplɔe yina Babel-fia le Ribla le Xamat-nyigba dzi, eye wòbu fɔe.

english_verse: Zedekiah's sons and the officials of Judah were killed while he watched,
translation_verse: Eye Babel-fia wu Zedekiya viwo le eya ŋutɔ ŋku me, eye wowu Yuda-amegãwo katã hã le Ribla.

english_verse: Jerusalem was captured during Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king of Babylonia. About a month later, Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guards arrived in Jerusalem. His name was Nebuzaradan,
translation_verse: Le dzinu atɔ̃lia ƒe ŋkeke ewolia dzi, si nye fia Nebukadnezar, Babel-fia ƒe ƒe wuiasiekelia dzi la, fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã Nebuzaradan, amesi nɔa tsitre ɖe Babel-fia ŋku me la, va Yerusalem,

english_verse: and he burned down the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and every important building in the city, as well as all the houses.
translation_verse: eye wòtɔ dzo Yehowa ƒe aƒe kple fia ƒe aƒe, Yerusalem-xɔwo katã kple bubumewo ƒe xɔwo katã.

english_verse: Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Eye Kaldeatɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ blibo, si le fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã ŋu la, gbã Yerusalem ƒe gliwo katã ƒu anyi.

english_verse: He led away the people left in the city, including everyone who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar, the rest of the skilled workers, and even some of the poor people of Judah.
translation_verse: Fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã Nebuzaradan ɖe aboyo dukɔ la ƒe ame dahewo dometɔa ɖewo, dukɔ la ƒe ame mamlea, siwo kpɔtɔ ɖe dua me, kple amesiwo yi ɖe Babel-fia dzi, kpakple aɖaŋudɔwɔlawo ƒe susɔeawo dzoe.

english_verse: Only the very poorest were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
translation_verse: Eye fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã Nebuzaradan gblẽ anyigba dzi ame dahea ɖewo ɖi, be woanye weingbledelawo kple agbledelawo.

english_verse: Evil Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
translation_verse: eƒo nu fafɛ kplii, eye wòtsɔ eƒe zikpui ɖo fia, siwo kpe ɖe eŋu le Babel la ƒe zikpui ŋgɔ.

english_verse: Jehoiachin was allowed to wear regular clothes instead of a prison uniform, and he even ate at the king's table every day.
translation_verse: Eɖɔ li eƒe gaxɔmewuwo, eye woɖu nu le egbɔ ɖaa le eƒe agbenɔɣi katã.

english_verse: As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Eye Babel-fia na eƒe nuɖuɖui ɖaa, alesi nu wòbiã gbesiagbe le eƒe agbenɔɣi katã, vaseɖe esime woku.

english_verse: Jerusalem, once so crowded, lies deserted and lonely. This city that was known all over the world is now like a widow. This queen of the nations has been made a slave.
translation_verse: Ao, du, si ame yɔ, tsi akogo! Du ga le dukɔwo dome zu ahosi; duwo ƒe fia zu yakadɔwɔla.

english_verse: Each night, bitter tears flood her cheeks. None of her former lovers are there to offer comfort; her friends have betrayed her and are now her enemies.
translation_verse: Ele avi fam le zã me hehehe, eye aɖatsi tsi alɔgo dzi nɛ. Eƒe ahiãvlwo dometɔa ɖeke mefa akɔ nɛ o. Xɔlɔ̃wo katã trɔ ʋu le eye me hezu eƒe fulɔwo.

english_verse: The people of Judah are slaves, suffering in a foreign land, with no rest from sorrow. Their enemies captured them and were terribly cruel.
translation_verse: Yuda ʋu dzo le teteɖeanyi kple dɔ sesẽ ta; ele dukɔwo dome, ke mekpɔ gbɔdzɔe o. Eyometilawo katã ɖatui le xaxɛƒe.

english_verse: The roads to Zion mourn because no one travels there to celebrate the festivals. The city gates are deserted; priests are weeping. Young women are raped; Zion is in sorrow!
translation_verse: Zion-mɔwo to gbe, elabena amea ɖeke megava ŋkekenyuieɖuƒe o. Eƒe agbowo kam esi ƒuƒlu, eye eƒe nunɔlawo le hũ ɖem. Eƒe ɖetugbiwo le ŋeŋem, eye eya ŋutɔ le veve sem.

english_verse: Enemies now rule the city and live as they please. The Lord has punished Jerusalem because of her awful sins; he has let her people be dragged away.
translation_verse: Eƒe ketɔwo ƒe alɔ ɖe dzi, eye eme nyo na eƒe futɔwo, elabena Yehowa ye ɖo hiã nɛ le eƒe vodada sɔgbɔawo ta. Viawo dze ketɔwo ŋgɔ yi aboyo me.

english_verse: Zion's glory has disappeared. Her leaders are like deer that cannot find pasture; they are hunted down till their strength is gone.
translation_verse: Zion-nyɔnuvi ƒe atsyɔ̃wo katã dzo le eŋu. Eƒe amegãwo le abe agbo, siwo mekpɔ gbeɖuƒea ɖeke o la ene, eye wole te klolo tem le wo yometilawo ŋgɔ.

english_verse: Her people recall the good life that once was theirs; now they suffer and are scattered. No one was there to protect them from their enemies who sneered when their city was taken.
translation_verse: Yerusalem le ŋu ɖom eƒe atsyɔ, siwo katã nɔ eŋu le blema ŋkekewo me la, le eƒe hiãɣi kple anyidzeɣi, elabena eƒe amewo tsi futɔ la si me, eye xɔnametɔ meli o. Ketɔ la kpɔe, eye woke eƒe toyiyi.

english_verse: Jerusalem's horrible sins have made the city a joke. Those who once admired her now hate her instead— she has been disgraced; she groans and turns away.
translation_verse: Nuvɔ̃e Yerusalem wɔ, eyata wòzu ŋunyɔnu. Amesiwo katã bui tsa la, la vlo domi, le esi wokpɔ eƒe ama ta. Ke eya ŋutɔ le hũ ɖem eye wòɖe eɖokui ɖe aga.

english_verse: Her sins had made her filthy, but she wasn't worried about what could happen. And when Jerusalem fell, it was so tragic. No one gave her comfort when she cried out, “Help! I'm in trouble, Lord! The enemy has won.”
translation_verse: Ɖiƒoƒo le eƒe avɔ toga, meɖo ŋu eƒe nuwuwu o. Tete wòyi to vevie, eye akɔfalaa ɖeke meli o. Yehowa, lé ŋku ɖe nye hiã ŋu, elabena futɔ la le asi tɔm akɔ!

english_verse: Zion's treasures were stolen. Jerusalem saw foreigners enter her place of worship, though the Lord had forbidden them to belong to his people.
translation_verse: Futɔ la do asi ɖe eƒe nu veviwo katã ŋu; elabena ekpɔ ɖukɔ, siwo nèɖe se na be, womegava wò amehawo ɖome o la, woge ɖe eƒe kɔkɔeƒe la.

english_verse: Everyone in the city groans while searching for food; they trade their valuables for barely enough scraps to stay alive. Jerusalem Speaks: Jerusalem shouts to the Lord, “Please look and see how miserable I am!”
translation_verse: Eƒe amewo katã le hũ ɖem hele abolo dim. Wotsɔ woƒe nu veviwo na ɖe nuɖuɖu la, ne woalé agbe ɖe te. Yehowa, ɖo ŋku anyi nakpɔ alesi woɖo vlom ɖa!

english_verse: No passerby even cares. Why doesn't someone notice my terrible sufferings? You were fiercely angry, Lord, and you punished me worst of all.
translation_verse: Eyata mi amesiwo katã va to mɔ dzi yina, miɖo ŋku anyi, ne miakpɔ nu be, vevea ɖe ɖe vevesese, si va dzinye, kple nuxaxa, si Yehowa ɖo nam le eƒe dɔmedzɔe heliheli ɖogbe la nu mahã?

english_verse: From heaven you sent a fire that burned in my bones; you set a trap for my feet and made me turn back. All day long you leave me in shock from constant pain.
translation_verse: Eɖo dzo ɖa tso dzi me ɖe nye ƒuwo me, eye wòɖi hã ɖe dzinye. Eɖo ɖɔ na nye afɔwo, wògbugbɔm ɖe megbe, ana mezu gbegbe, eye mele nuxaxa dzi ɖaa.

english_verse: You have tied my sins around my neck, and they weigh so heavily that my strength is gone. You have put me in the power of enemies too strong for me.
translation_verse: Eƒe asi na nye vodadawo ƒe kɔkuti nu sẽ, eblae ɖe nye kɔʋume, eye wona ŋusẽ va le ŋunye. Aƒelɔ la tsɔm ɖe asi na amesiwo nu nyemate ŋu ana te ɖo o.

english_verse: You, Lord, have turned back my warriors and crushed my young heroes. Judah was a woman untouched, but you let her be trampled like grapes in a wine pit.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ la tsa nye kalẽtɔwo katã ƒu gbe le donyeme, eɖe gbe ƒã ŋkekenyuie ɖe ŋunye, ne woagbã nye ɖekakpuiwo nyanyanya. Aƒetɔ la fiã wein na Yuɖa-ɖetugbi.

english_verse: Because of this, I mourn, and tears flood my eyes. No one is here to comfort or to encourage me; we have lost the war— my people are suffering. The Prophet Speaks:
translation_verse: Esia ta mele avi fam, eye nye ŋkuwo le aɖatsi kplɔm yoyoyo ɖo; akɔfala, si afa dzi nam la, le adzɔge nam. Wotsrɔ̃ vinyewo, elabena futɔ la ƒe alo ɖe dzi.

english_verse: Zion reaches out her hands, but no one offers comfort. The Lord has turned the neighboring nations against Jacob's descendants. Jerusalem is merely a filthy rag to her neighbors. Jerusalem Speaks:
translation_verse: Zion ke eƒe abɔwo me, ke akɔfalaa ɖeke meli nɛ o. Yehowa ɖɔ ketɔwo ɖe Yakob ŋu goɖoo va kpe, eye Yerusalem zu ŋunyɔnu le wo dome.

english_verse: The Lord was right, but I refused to obey him. Now I ask all of you to look at my sufferings— even my young people have been dragged away.
translation_verse: Yehowa ta dzɔ, elabena mesẽ to ɖe eƒe nyawo ŋu. Mi dukɔwo katã, misee, eye milé ŋku ɖe nye vevesese ŋu! Nye ɖetugbiwo kple nye ɖekãkpuiwo yi aboyo me.

english_verse: I called out to my lovers, but they betrayed me. My priests and my leaders died while searching the city for scraps of food.
translation_verse: Meyɔ nye ahiãviwo, ke woblem. Nu te nye nunɔlawo kple ame tsitsiwo ŋu le dua me, elabena wole nuɖuɖu dim, ne woatsɔ lé woƒe agbe ɖe te.

english_verse: Won't you look and see how upset I am, our Lord? My stomach is in knots, and my heart is broken because I betrayed you. In the streets and at home, my people are slaughtered.
translation_verse: Yehowa, kpo alesi vɔvɔ̃ ɖom ɖa! Nye dɔkaviwo ʋu dzo hẽ, eye nye dzi le togotogoe ƒom le menye, le esi mese to ta. Yi le nu gblẽm le xexe abe ku le aƒe me ene.

english_verse: Everyone heard my groaning, but no one offered comfort. My enemies know of the trouble that you have brought on me, and it makes them glad. Hurry and punish them, as you have promised.
translation_verse: Wose alesi mele hũ ɖemee, ke xɔnametɔa ɖeke meli o. Nye futɔwo katã se nye dzɔgbevɔ̃e ŋkɔ, eye wole dzidzɔ kpɔm, elabena wòe wɔe. Ne éhe ŋkeke, si ŋu nèɖe gbe ƒã le vɛ la, ekema woawo hã woanɔ abe nye ene.

english_verse: Don't let their evil deeds escape your sight. Punish them as much as you have punished me because of my sins. I never stop groaning— I've lost all hope!
translation_verse: Woƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔwo katã neva ŋkuwò me, eye nawɔ na wo, abe alesi nèwɔm le nye vodadawo katã ta ene; elabena nye hũɖeɖewo sɔ gbɔ, eye nye dzi le nu xam.

english_verse: The Lord was angry! So he disgraced Zion though it was Israel's pride and his own place of rest. In his anger he threw Zion down from heaven to earth.
translation_verse: Aleke Aƒetɔ la na Zion-nyɔnuvi ɖo tsizi le eƒe dɔmedzoe me! Exlã Israel ƒe atsyɔ̃ ɖe anyi tso dziƒo, eye meɖo ŋu eƒe afɔɖodzinu le dɔmedzoedogbe o.

english_verse: The Lord had no mercy! He destroyed the homes of Jacob's descendants. In his anger he tore down every walled city in Judah; he toppled the nation together with its leaders, leaving them in shame.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ la gblẽ Yakob ƒe lãnyiƒewo katã, mekpɔ wo ta o, eghã Yuɖa-nyɔnuvi ƒe mɔ̃ sesẽwo wosɔ kple anyigba le eƒe dziku me, eye wogblẽ ka ɖo na fiaɖuƒe la kple eƒe amegãwo.

english_verse: The Lord was so furiously angry that he wiped out the whole army of Israel by not supporting them when the enemy attacked. He was like a raging fire that swallowed up the descendants of Jacob.
translation_verse: Eŋe dzowo katã na Israel le eƒe dɔmedzoe heliheli me; ehe eƒe nuɖusi ɖe megbe le futɔ nu, eye wodo dzo ɖe Yakob wòbi nu goɖoo va kpe.

english_verse: He attacked like an enemy with a bow and arrows, killing our loved ones. He has burned to the ground the homes on Mount Zion.
translation_verse: Ehe eƒe ɖa me abe futɔ ene, eye wòtsi tre ɖi kple eƒe nuɖusi abe ketɔ ene hetsrɔ̃ nusiwo katã dze na kpɔkpɔ; etrɔ eƒe dziku ƒo ɖe Zion-nyɔnuvi ƒe agbadɔ me abe dzo ene.

english_verse: The Lord was like an enemy! He left Israel in ruins with its palaces and fortresses destroyed, and with everyone in Judah moaning and weeping.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ la trɔ zu futɔ, etsrɔ̃ Israel, eye wòtsrɔ̃ eƒe fiasãwo katã, egblẽ eƒe mɔ̃ sesẽwo, eye wòli kɔ nuxaxa ɖe nuxaxa dzi na Yuda-nyɔnuvi.

english_verse: He shattered his temple like a hut in a garden; he completely wiped out his meeting place, and did away with festivals and Sabbaths in the city of Zion. In his fierce anger he rejected our king and priests.
translation_verse: Eka kpɔ le eŋu abe le abɔ ŋu ene, eye wògblẽ eƒe takpeƒe. Yehowa na woŋlɔ ŋkekenyuie kple dzudzɔgbe be le Zion, eye wòdo vlo fia kple nunɔla le eƒe dɔmedzoe heliheli me.

english_verse: The Lord abandoned his altar and his temple; he let Zion's enemies capture her fortresses. Noisy shouts were heard from the temple, as if it were a time of celebration.
translation_verse: Yehowa gbe eƒe vɔsamlekpui, eɖi gbɔ eƒe kɔkɔeƒe la, eye wòtsɔ eƒe fiasãwo ƒe gliwo ɖe asi na futɔ la; woƒe ɣli le ɖiɖim le Yehowa ƒe me abe le ŋkekenyuieɖugbe ene.

english_verse: The Lord had decided to tear down the walls of Zion stone by stone. So he started destroying and did not stop until walls and fortresses mourned and trembled.
translation_verse: Yehowa ɖo be, yeatsrɔ̃ Zion-nyɔnuvi ƒe gli; eda ka, mehe eƒe asi ɖe megbe tso nugbegblẽ me o, eye wona kpoƒuƒu kple gli le nu xam; nu le woa kple eve la siaa ŋu.

english_verse: Zion's gates have fallen facedown on the ground; the bars that locked the gates are smashed to pieces. Her king and royal family are prisoners in foreign lands. Her priests don't teach, and her prophets don't have a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Eƒe agbowo ɖo agu, eye wogblẽ eƒe gametiwo heŋe wo; eƒe fia kple eƒe amegãwo le dukɔwo dome, se mele wo si o, woƒe nyagblɔɖilawo hã mekpɔa ŋutega tso Yehowa gbɔ o.

english_verse: Zion's leaders are silent. They just sit on the ground, tossing dirt on their heads and wearing sackcloth. Her young women can do nothing but stare at the ground.
translation_verse: Zion-nyɔnuvi ƒe amegã ɖeɖiwo bɔbɔ nɔ anyigba, eye woƒe nu ɖe ga, wolɔ afi kɔ ɖe ta me, eye wota akpanya; Yerusalem-ɖetugbi de kɔ to.

english_verse: My eyes are red from crying, my stomach is in knots, and I feel sick all over. My people are being wiped out, and children lie helpless in the streets of the city.
translation_verse: Nye ŋkuwo la aɖatsi wòti kɔ na wo, nye dɔkaviwo ʋu dzo hẽ, eye nye aklã wó ɖe dɔ me nam le nye dukɔ ƒe nyɔnu ƒe anyidzedze la, esime nu te ɖeviwo kple vidziewo ŋu le ɖua ƒe kpɔdomeewo.

english_verse: A child begs its mother for food and drink, then blacks out like a wounded soldier lying in the street. The child slowly dies in its mother's arms.
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na wo ɖadawo be: Bli kple wein ɖe? Eye nu le wo ŋu le ɖua ƒe kpɔɖonieewo abe ame xɔabi ene, eye woƒe gbɔgbɔ do le wo me le wo dadawo ƒe akɔ nu.

english_verse: Zion, how can I comfort you? How great is your pain? Lovely city of Jerusalem, how can I heal your wounds, gaping as wide as the sea?
translation_verse: Yerusalem-nyɔnuvi, ameka matsɔ asa kpli wò, ne wòaɖi wò? Zion-ɖetugbi ameka matsɔ aɖo ŋuwò, ne mafa akɔ na wò? Elabena wò abi lolo abe atsiaƒu ene, amekae ada gbe le ŋuwò ma?

english_verse: Your prophets deceived you with false visions and lying messages— they should have warned you to leave your sins and be saved from disaster.
translation_verse: Wò nyagblɔdilawo gblɔ alakpanya kple nya mastatsa ɖi na wò, eye womeklo nu le wò vodadawo dzi, ne woagaɖo wò te o, ke boŋ wogblɔ alakpanya kple ameflunya ɖi na wò.

english_verse: Those who pass by shake their heads and sneer as they make fun and shout, “What a lovely city you were, the happiest on earth, but look at you now!”
translation_verse: Amesiwo katã va tso eme yi la, si akpe ɖe ŋuwò, woɖe tsiã heʋuʋu ta ɖe Yerusalem-nyɔnuvi ŋu be: Du, si ŋu wogblɔ le be, enye nyonyowo seƒe kple anyigba blibo la ƒe dzidzɔ la, enye esia?

english_verse: Zion, your enemies curse you and snarl like wild animals, while shouting, “This is the day we've waited for! At last, we've got you!”
translation_verse: Wò fulɔwo katã ke nu ɖe ŋuwò baa, wodo tsia heɖu aɖukli gblɔ bena: Míetsrɔ̃e! Ehɛ̃, ŋkeke, si míele mɔ kpɔm na la, enye esia, míaƒe asi su edzi, míekpɔ eteƒe kple ŋku!

english_verse: The Lord has done everything that he had planned and threatened long ago. He destroyed you without mercy and let your enemies boast about their powerful forces.
translation_verse: Yehowa wɔ eƒe tame, si wòɖo la, de goe, eye wòwɔ eƒe nya, si ŋugbe wòdo tso blema ka la dzi; egbã nu ƒu anyi, mekpɔ eta o, ena wò futɔwo kpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe ŋuwò, eye wòdo wò ketɔwo ƒe dzo ɖe dzi.

english_verse: Zion, deep in your heart you cried out to the Lord. Now let your tears overflow your walls day and night. Don't ever lose hope or let your tears stop.
translation_verse: Eƒe dzi do ɣli na Aƒetɔ la. Zion-nyɔnuvi ƒe gli, na wò aɖatsi nasi abe tɔʋu ene zã kple keli; megagbɔ ɖe eme o, eye megana wò ŋkuvi nakpɔ gbɔdzɔe o.

english_verse: Get up and pray for help all through the night. Pour out your feelings to the Lord, as you would pour water out of a jug. Beg him to save your people, who are starving to death at every street crossing. Jerusalem Speaks:
translation_verse: Fɔ nado ɣli le zã le ŋudzɔɣi ƒe gɔmedzedze! Trɔ wò dzi ƒo ɖe Aƒetɔ la ŋku me abe esi ene! Wu wò asiwo dzi nɛ le viwò, siwo dɔwuame na no te wo ŋu ɖe kpɔdomeewo ƒe dzogoewo katã dzi la ƒe agbe ta!

english_verse: Think about it, Lord! Have you ever been this cruel to anyone before? Is it right for mothers to eat their children, or for priests and prophets to be killed in your temple?
translation_verse: Yehowa ɖo ŋku anyi, ne nakpɔ nu, ameka newɔ esiae? Ɖe nyɔnuwo aɖu woƒe dɔmevi, ɖevi, siwo dzi wokpɔa? Ɖe woawu nunɔla kple nyagblɔɖila ɖe Aƒetɔ la ƒe kɔkɔeƒe laa?

english_verse: My people, both young and old, lie dead in the streets. Because you were angry, my young men and women were brutally slaughtered.
translation_verse: Ɖeviwo kple amegã ɖeɖiwo ɖo baba ɖe anyigba le kpɔdomeewo, eye nye ɖetugbiwo kple nye ɖekakpuiwo tsi yi nu. Eda nu eme le wò dɔmedzoedogbe, eye nèwu ame, mèkpɔ eta o.

english_verse: When you were angry, Lord, you invited my enemies like guests for a party. No one survived that day; enemies killed my children, my own little ones.
translation_verse: Eyɔ ŋɔdzi ɖe ŋunye godoo abe le ŋkekenyuieɖugbe ene, eye amea ɖeke mesi alo susɔ le Yehowa ƒe dɔmedzoedogbe o. Amesiwo dzi mekpɔ, eye menyi wotsi la, nye futɔ tsrɔ̃ wo.

english_verse: I have suffered much because God was angry.
translation_verse: Nyee nye ŋutsu, si kpɔ hiã teƒe le eƒe ameƒoti le.

english_verse: He chased me into a dark place, where no light could enter.
translation_verse: Ekplɔm, eye wòna mezɔ viviti me, menye kekeli me o.

english_verse: I am the only one he punishes over and over again, without ever stopping.
translation_verse: Ŋunyee wòle eƒe asi trɔm ɖo ɖaa atraɖi le ŋkeke blibo la me.

english_verse: God caused my skin and flesh to waste away, and he crushed my bones.
translation_verse: Edze lã kple agbalẽ le ŋunye yaʋayaʋa, eye wògbã nye ƒuwo.

english_verse: He attacked and surrounded me with hardships and trouble;
translation_verse: Etsɔ aɖi kple fukpekpe tɔ kpɔ ɖe ŋunye godoo va kpe.

english_verse: he forced me to sit in the dark like someone long dead.
translation_verse: Ena menɔ blukɔ me abe emesiwo ku gbaɖegbe ke ene.

english_verse: God built a fence around me that I cannot climb over, and he chained me down.
translation_verse: Eɖo gli ɖe ŋunye, toƒe meli o, eye wòna nye kɔsɔkɔsɔwo nu sẽ ɖe dzi.

english_verse: Even when I shouted and prayed for help, he refused to listen.
translation_verse: Ne mele ɣli dom le eyɔm hã le, etua nu ɖe nye gbedodoɖa nu.

english_verse: God put big rocks in my way and made me follow a crooked path.
translation_verse: Etsɔ kpe gãwo ɖo amli ɖe nye mɔ dzi, eye wògɔdɔ̃ nye toƒe.

english_verse: God was like a bear or a lion waiting in ambush for me;
translation_verse: Sisiblisi, si ɖe xa ɖi, kple dzata, si le xa me, wònye nam.

english_verse: he dragged me from the road, then tore me to shreds.
translation_verse: Ekplɔm trae, eye wòvuvum hetsɔ wɔ nu dziŋɔe.

english_verse: God took careful aim and shot his arrows
translation_verse: Ehe eƒe ɖa me, eye wòtsɔm ɖo nudzidzea ne eƒe aŋutrɔwo.

english_verse: straight through my heart.
translation_verse: Eɖo eƒe dakumeviwo ɖe nye ayikuwo me.

english_verse: I am a joke to everyone— no one ever stops making fun of me.
translation_verse: Metrɔ zu nu ɖikokoea na nye dukɔ kple woƒe hamelo ŋkeke blibo la.

english_verse: God has turned my life sour.
translation_verse: Etsɔ ama veve ɖi ƒo nam, eye wòkpe atsa nam meno.

english_verse: He made me eat gravel and rubbed me in the dirt.
translation_verse: Ena ahliha ŋe aɖu nam, eye wòtigim ɖe dzowɔ me.

english_verse: I cannot find peace or remember happiness.
translation_verse: Woxɔ ŋutifafa le nye luʋɔ si, eye meŋlɔ dzɔgbenyuie be.

english_verse: I tell myself, “I am finished! I can't count on the Lord to do anything for me.”
translation_verse: Mebe, nye ŋusẽ nu yi, eye mebu mɔkpɔkpɔ na Yehowa.

english_verse: Just thinking of my troubles and my lonely wandering makes me miserable.
translation_verse: Ɖo ŋu nye hiã kple nye fukpekpe, atsa kple aɖi.

english_verse: That's all I ever think about, and I am depressed.
translation_verse: Ɖo ŋui, nagaɖo ŋui ɖe dzi be, nye luʋɔ xa gobaa le menye.

english_verse: Then I remember something that fills me with hope.
translation_verse: Mene esia nade dzigbɔ nam, eyata mele mɔ kpɔm be:

english_verse: The Lord's kindness never fails! If he had not been merciful, we would have been destroyed.
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe amenuveve nu metso o, eye eƒe nubianuikpɔkpɔ mese ɖo o;

english_verse: The Lord can always be trusted to show mercy each morning.
translation_verse: ke boŋ ete yeye ŋɖi sia ŋɖi, eye wò amenuveve tri akɔ!

english_verse: Deep in my heart I say, “The Lord is all I need; I can depend on him!”
translation_verse: Nye luʋɔ be: Nye gome enye Yehowa, eyata mele esinu kpɔm ɖo.

english_verse: The Lord is kind to everyone who trusts and obeys him.
translation_verse: Yehowa ƒe ɖɔme nyo ɖe amesi le dzi ɖom ɖe eŋu, kple luʋɔ si le edim la ŋu.

english_verse: It is good to wait patiently for the Lord to save us.
translation_verse: Enyo be, woanɔ anyi kpoo anɔ Yehowa ƒe xɔname sinu kpɔm.

english_verse: When we are young, it is good to struggle hard
translation_verse: Enye na ŋutsu be, wòatsɔ kɔkuti le eƒe ɖevime.

english_verse: and to sit silently alone, if this is what the Lord intends.
translation_verse: Nebɔbɔ nɔ aga, eye wòazi ɖoɖoe, elabena eyamae tsoe ɖo edzi;

english_verse: Being rubbed in the dirt can teach us a lesson;
translation_verse: netsɔ eƒe nu ƒo ɖe ke me, ɖewohi mɔkpɔkpɔ gali;

english_verse: we can also learn from insults and hard knocks.
translation_verse: neɖo to me anyi na amesi le eƒom, eye netsɔ ŋukpe ɖi ƒoe.

english_verse: The Lord won't always reject us!
translation_verse: Elabena Aƒetɔ la megbea ame ɖikaa o;

english_verse: He causes a lot of suffering, but he also has pity because of his great love.
translation_verse: ke boŋ ne edo nuxaxa na ame la, egakpɔa nublanui le eƒe amenuveve geɖe la nu.

english_verse: The Lord doesn't enjoy sending grief or pain.
translation_verse: Elabena mewɔa fu ame, eye medoa nuxaxa na amegbetɔviwo le dzidzɔ teƒe o.

english_verse: Don't trample prisoners under your feet
translation_verse: Ne wofanya anyigba dza gatɔwo katã kple afɔ,

english_verse: or cheat anyone out of what is rightfully theirs. God Most High sees everything,
translation_verse: ne wote ame ƒe nya de to le dziƒoʋitɔ la ŋku me,

english_verse: and he knows when you refuse to give someone a fair trial.
translation_verse: eye wotrɔ gbo ame ƒe dzrenya la, ɖe Aƒetɔ la makpɔe oa?

english_verse: No one can do anything without the Lord's approval.
translation_verse: Amekae gblɔ nya wòva me, ne Aƒetɔ la meɖe se hafi o?

english_verse: Good and bad each happen at the command of God Most High.
translation_verse: Ɖe vɔ̃ kple nyui metsoa dziƒoʋitɔ la nu me oa?

english_verse: We're still alive! We shouldn't complain when we are being punished for our sins.
translation_verse: Nuka ta amegbetɔ le nu xam le eƒe agbe me? Amesiame nexa nu le eƒe nuvɔ̃ ŋu boŋ.

english_verse: Instead, we should think about the way we are living, and turn back to the Lord.
translation_verse: Mina míaɖo míaƒe zɔzɔme a pɔ, míadzro eme akpɔ, eye míatrɔ ɖe Yehowa ŋu!

english_verse: When we lift our hands in prayer to God in heaven, we should offer him our hearts and say,
translation_verse: Mina míakɔ míaƒe dzi kple míaƒe asiwo dzi ɖo ɖe Mawu le dziƒo.

english_verse: “We've sinned! We've rebelled against you, and you haven't forgiven us!
translation_verse: Míawo míedze aglã, eye míesẽ to, eye wo la mètsɔe ke o.

english_verse: Anger is written all over you, as you pursue and slaughter us without showing pity.
translation_verse: Eɣla ɖokuiwò le dziku me, eye neti mía yome hewu mí, mèkpɔ mía ta o.

english_verse: You are behind a wall of clouds that blocks out our prayers.
translation_verse: Eɣla ɖokuiwò ɖe alilikpo me, ale be gbedodoɖaa ɖeke meɖi go ɖe egoɖo o.

english_verse: You allowed nations to treat us like garbage;
translation_verse: Etsɔ mi wɔ gbeɖuɖɔ kple ŋunyɔnui le dukɔwo dome.

english_verse: We are terrified and trapped, caught and crushed.”
translation_verse: Mía tɔ gome enye ŋɔdzi kple ʋe, tsɔtsrɔ̃ kple gbegblẽ.

english_verse: My people are destroyed! Tears flood my eyes,
translation_verse: Nye ŋku le esi kplɔm yoyoyo le nye dukɔ ƒe nyɔnuvi ƒe gbegblẽ ta.

english_verse: until the Lord looks down from heaven and helps.
translation_verse: vaseɖe esime Yehowa naɖo ŋku anyi akpɔe tso dziƒo.

english_verse: I am horrified when I see what enemies have done to the young women of our city.
translation_verse: Nye ŋku le veyem ɖe luʋɔ me ke nam le nye ɖu ƒe nyɔnuviwo katã ta.

english_verse: No one had reason to hate me, but I was hunted down like a bird.
translation_verse: Nye futɔwo yɔm ɖe nu yakatsyɔ abe xevi ene.

english_verse: Then they tried to kill me by tossing me into a pit and throwing stones at me.
translation_verse: Wotigi nye agbe ɖe do me, eye wofɔ kpe ɖo dzinye.

english_verse: Water covered my head— I thought I was gone.
translation_verse: Tsi fiẽ tanye, eye mebe: Evɔ nam!

english_verse: From the bottom of the pit, I prayed to you, Lord.
translation_verse: Yehowa, wò ŋkɔe meva le do me ʋi ke.

english_verse: I begged you to listen. “Help!” I shouted. “Save me!” You answered my prayer
translation_verse: Ese nya ɣli, megaɖe wò to da te nye kokoƒoƒo ŋu nagbe akɔfata nam o.

english_verse: and came when I was in need. You told me, “Don't worry!”
translation_verse: Etsɔ kpuie le gbesigbe meyɔ wo, eye nẽgblɔ be: Megavɔ̃ o!

english_verse: You rescued me and saved my life.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, asiwò me nye nya le, eye nèɖe nye agbe

english_verse: You saw them abuse me, Lord, so make things right.
translation_verse: Yehowa, èkpɔ nye tetedeanyi, drɔ̃ nye nya nam.

english_verse: You know every plot they have made against me.
translation_verse: Ekpɔ woƒe hlɔ̃biabiawo katã kple tame, si wodo ɖe ŋunye la.

english_verse: Yes, you know their insults and their evil plans.
translation_verse: Yehowa èse woƒe alɔmeɖeɖe kple tame, si woɖo ɖe ŋunye,

english_verse: All day long they attack with words and whispers.
translation_verse: nye futɔwo ƒe nuƒoƒo kple woƒe susuwo ɖe ŋunye gbesiagbe.

english_verse: No matter what they are doing, they keep on mocking me.
translation_verse: De ŋku ɖe woƒe anyinɔnɔ kple tsitrenɔnɔ ŋu, hamelo menye na wo.

english_verse: Pay them back for everything they have done, Lord!
translation_verse: Yehowa, ɖo eteƒe na wo le woƒe asinudɔwɔwɔwo nu.

english_verse: Put your curse on them and make them suffer.
translation_verse: Tso tamesesẽ na wo, wo fiƒoɖe neva wo dzi!

english_verse: Get angry and go after them until not a trace is left under the heavens.
translation_verse: Ti wo yome le dziku me, eye natsrɔ̃ wo ɖa le Yehowa ƒe dziƒoa te!

english_verse: The purest gold is ruined and has lost its shine; jewels from the temple lie scattered in the streets.
translation_verse: Aleke sika nya tsiɖitsiɖi, eye sika nyui ƒe nɔnɔme trɔ? Aleke wolɔ kpe kókɔewo kɔ ɖe kpɔɖomee ƒe dzogoewo katã dzi?

english_verse: These are Zion's people, worth more than purest gold; yet they are counted worthless like dishes of clay.
translation_verse: Aleke Zion ƒe vi vevi, siwo wobuna abe sika ene la, sɔ kple sonugaglɛ, si nye zemela ƒe asinudɔwɔwɔ?

english_verse: Even jackals nurse their young, but my people are like ostriches that abandon their own.
translation_verse: Keke amegãxi ke hã nua no viawo wonona, ke nye dukɔ ƒe nyɔnuvi le ŋlɔmie wɔm abe golo le gbe dzi ene.

english_verse: Babies are so thirsty that their tongues are stuck to the roof of the mouth. Children go begging for food, but no one gives them any.
