translation_verse: Ŋutsu dzɔdzɔewo adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wo ɖe gbolowo kple nyɔnu dohlɔ̃wo ƒe se nu; elabena gbolowo wonye, eye ʋu le asi ŋu na wo.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, now say to these sisters: I will call together an angry mob that will abuse and rob you.
translation_verse: Elabena ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Woakplɔ amehawo ava ƒu wo, eye woatso wo ade asi na ŋutasesẽ kple nuhaha.

english_verse: They will stone you to death and cut you to pieces; they will kill your children and burn down your houses.
translation_verse: Amehawo nexlã kpe ɖe wo, eye woadza wo kple woƒe yiwo, woawu woƒe ŋutsuviwo kple nyɔnuviwo, eye woata dzo woƒe xɔwo.

english_verse: I will get rid of sinful prostitution in this country, so that women everywhere will be warned not to act as you have.
translation_verse: Matsi ŋukpenanuwɔwɔ nu le anyigba dzi, eye anye nuxlɔ̃me na nyɔnuwo katã, ne womagawɔ ŋukpenanu abe woawo ene o.

english_verse: You will be punished for becoming prostitutes and for worshiping idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Woahe miaƒe ŋukpenanuwɔwɔ ava mia dzi, eye nuvɔ̃, siwo miewɔ to miaƒe legbawo dzi la, anɔ mia dzi, ne miadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ Yehowa.

english_verse: Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam le ƒe asiekelia me, le dzinu ewolia ƒe ŋkeke ewolia dzi bena.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amevi, ŋlɔ ŋkeke sia tututu ƒe ŋkɔ ɖi; elabena ŋkeke sia dzi Babel-fia ɖe to ɖe Yerusalem.

english_verse: Then tell my rebellious people: “Pour water in a cooking pot and set it over a fire. *
translation_verse: Do lo na ƒome sẽto la, eye nagblɔ na wo bena: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Tsɔ gaze ɖo dzoe, tsɔe ɖo dzoe, eye naku tsi ɖe eme!

english_verse: Throw in the legs and shoulders of your finest sheep and put in the juicy bones.
translation_verse: Fɔ lãkɔwo de eme, lãkɔ nyuiwo katã, alime kple abɔgba; tso ƒu nyuiawo de eme fũ.

english_verse: Pile wood underneath the pot, and let the meat and bones boil until they are done.”
translation_verse: Tsa alé nyuitɔwo, eye nade nake ete! Na lãkɔwo nafie, eye ƒuawo hã nabi ɖewo me.

english_verse: These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it.
translation_verse: Eyata ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Baba na hlɔ̃dodu la, gaze, si lé ɣebia, eye eƒe ɣebia meɖe le eŋu o! Ɖe lãwo le eme kokoko, eye megadzidze nu ɖe edzi hafi o.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground.
translation_verse: Elabena eƒe ʋu le eme, agakpe ƒeƒle dzi wòkɔe ɖo, menye anyigba dzi wòwɔe ɖo, ne ke natsyɔ edzi o.

english_verse: But I have seen that blood, and it cries out for me to take revenge.
translation_verse: Meka eƒe ʋu dze agakpe ƒeƒle dzi, be nu magatsyɔ ɖee o, ne mahe dziku ava edzi, eye mabia hlɔ̃.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will punish that city of violence! I will make a huge pile of firewood,
translation_verse: Eyata ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Baba na hlɔ̃dodu la! Nye hã matu nake ɖo gleglegle.

english_verse: so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch.
translation_verse: Ɖe nake geɖe ve, eye nado dzoa, na lãwo nabi, detsia neto, eye ƒuawo nalé ze.

english_verse: Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust.
translation_verse: Na zea natsi dzoa dzi, ne wò axɔ dzo, eye eƒe akɔbli nabiã hẽ, nu makomako, si le eme, nalólo, eye eƒe ɣebia nafiã.

english_verse: I've tried everything else. Now the rust must be burned away.
translation_verse: Woku kutri, ke eƒe ɣebia gbogboawo gbe dodo le eŋu.

english_verse: Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it.
translation_verse: Esi meklɔ ŋuwò, ke wò nu makɔmakɔawo gbe ɖiɖi le ŋuwò le wò ŋukpenanuwɔwɔ makɔmakɔawo ta la, eyata ŋuwò maɖi akpa o, vaseɖe esime nye dziku nu nafa ɖe ŋuwò.

english_verse: That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Ezekiel's Wife Dies
translation_verse: Nye Yehowa ye ƒo nu, egbɔna, eye mawɔ edzi, nyemadzudzɔ o, nyemakpɔ ame ta o, eye nyemakpɔ nublanui o, ke boŋ woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wò ɖe wò zɔzɔme kple wò nuwɔnawo nu, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry.
translation_verse: Amevi, mele ku kpatakpata tsɔ ge aɖe nusi vivia wò ŋku nu la ɖa; megaxa nu o, megata avi o, eye wò aɖatsi megado o.

english_verse: Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
translation_verse: Ɖe hũ le adza me, eye megawɔ kunu o; bia ta, eye nado atokota ɖe afɔ, megabla nu ɖe wò ge o, eye megaɖu konyifabolo o.

english_verse: One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me,
translation_verse: Eye esi meƒo nu kple dukɔa le ŋdi la, srɔ̃nye ku le fiẽ, eye mewo le ŋdi, abe alesi woɖe se nam ene.

english_verse: and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la gblɔ nam bena: Màgblɔ nusi wɔm nèle la gɔme na mi oa?

english_verse: I answered: The Lord God says
translation_verse: Eye meɖo ŋu na wo bena: Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam be:

english_verse: he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na Israel ƒe aƒe la bena: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, magblẽ kɔ ɖo na nye kɔkɔeƒe la, miaƒe sitsoƒe, si nye miaƒe aɖegbeƒonu, nusi vivia miaƒe ŋkuwo nu kple nusi nye miaƒe luʋɔwo ƒe didi; miaƒe ŋutsuviwo kple miaƒe nyɔnuviwo, siwo miegblẽ ɖe megbe la, atsi yi nu.

english_verse: Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat.
translation_verse: Eye miawɔ pɛpɛpɛ abe nye ene: miabla nu ɖe ge o, eye miaɖu konyifabolo o,

english_verse: You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
translation_verse: miaƒe tablanu anɔ ta na mi, eye miaƒe atokotawo atsi afɔ na mi, miaxa nu o, eye miafa avi o, miatsrɔ̃ ɖe miaƒe vodadawo me, eye miaɖe hũ le mia nɔewo dome.

english_verse: I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
translation_verse: Xezekiel anye kpɔdzidze na mi, eye ne eva me la, miawɔ pɛpɛpɛ, abe alesi wòwɔ ene, eye miadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ Yehowa.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well.
translation_verse: Wò amevi, gbesigbe maɖe woƒe sitsoƒe, woƒe dzidzɔ vevi, nusi vivia woƒe ŋkuwo nu, kple woƒe luʋɔwo ƒe didi, woƒe ŋutsuviwo kple woƒe nyɔnuviwo ɖa la,

english_verse: On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened.
translation_verse: gbemagbe ame asi ava gbɔwò, be yeava to nya na wò.

english_verse: Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Gbemagbe woaʋu nu na mia kple ame sisi la siaa, àƒo nu, eye màzi kpi o. Ale nanye kpɔdzidze na wo, ne wòadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa.

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam bena:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon
translation_verse: Amevi, trɔ mo ɖe Amon-viwo ŋu, eye nagblɔ nya ɖi ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: and tell them: You celebrated when my temple was destroyed, when Israel was defeated, and when my people were taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na Amon-viwo bena: Mise Aƒetɔ Yehowa ƒe nya! Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esi miele ehẽ dom ɖe nye kɔkɔeƒe la ŋu be, wodo gui, ɖe Israel-nyigba ŋu be, ezu gbegbe, eye ele Yuda ƒe aƒe la ŋu be, eyi aboyo me ŋuti la,

english_verse: Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk.
translation_verse: eyata kpɔ ɖa, matsɔ wò ana ɣedzeƒeviwo nanye wo tɔ, ne woatu woƒe agbadɔ ɖe gbɔwò, eye woatso aƒe ɖe gbɔwò, woaɖu wò kutsetsewo, eye woano wò notsi.

english_verse: Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Mana Raba nazu kposɔwo ƒe gbeɖuƒe, eye Amon-viwo ƒe anyigba nazu akɔtsyɔƒe na alẽwo; eye miadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa.

english_verse: And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things. Judgment on Moab
translation_verse: eyata kpɔ ɖa, mado nye asi ɖa ɖe mia ŋu, eye matsɔ mi awɔ nuhaha na dukɔwo, matsrɔ̃ mi ɖa le dukɔwo dome, miabu le anyigbawo dzi gbidii, eye magblẽ mi, ne miadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa. Nyagblɔɖi le Moabitɔwo ŋuti.

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esi Moab kple Seir wole gbɔgblɔm be, Yuda ƒe aƒe la zu abe dukɔ bubuwo katã ene la,

english_verse: So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: eyata kpɔ ɖa, maʋu Moab ƒe abɔta, si nye eƒe duwo, eƒe duwo le goawo katã me, Bet-Yesimot-nyigba ƒe nu vevi, Baal-Meon kple Kiryatayim,

english_verse: The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever,
translation_verse: eye màtsɔe ana ɣedzeƒeviwo akpe ɖe Amon-viwo ƒe anyigba ŋu, ne wòanye wo tɔ, eye ŋku magadze Amon-viwo dzi le dukɔwo dome azɔ o.

english_verse: Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.” Judgment on Edom
translation_verse: Mahe to na Moab, ne wòadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa. Nyagblɔɖi le Edomtɔwo ŋuti.

english_verse: The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esi Edom bia hlɔ̃ Yuda ƒe aƒe la, eye wòɖi fɔ vevie, le esi wòbia hlɔ̃ wo ŋuti la,

english_verse: So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan.
translation_verse: eyata ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Mado nye asi ɖa ɖe Edom ŋu, eye matsrɔ̃ amegbetɔwo kple lãwo siaa ɖa le edzi, mana woazu gbegbe, eye woatsi yi nu, tso Teman vaseɖe Deɖan.

english_verse: I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.” Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: Matsɔ nye hlɔ̃biabia Edom ade asi na nye dukɔ Israel, eye woawo Edom ɖe nye dɔmedzoe kple nye dziku nu, eye wòadze si nye hlɔ̃biabia, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe. Nyagblɔɖi le Filistitɔwo ŋuti.

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esi Filistitɔwo wɔ nu ɖe hlɔ̃biabia me, eye wotsɔ fuléle makumaku ɖe dzi me bia hlɔ̃e le fewuɖuɖu me, be woatsrɔ̃ ame la,

english_verse: Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast.
translation_verse: eyata ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, mado nye asi ɖa ɖe Filistitɔwo ŋu, matsrɔ̃ Kretatɔwo, eye mana amesiwo kpɔtɔ ɖe atsiaƒu nu la, nabu gbidii.

english_verse: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Mabia hlɔ̃ gã wo, eye mahe to na wo le dziku me, ne wòadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa, nenye be, mebia hlɔ̃ wo.

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam le ƒe wuiɖekɛlia me le dzinu gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi bena:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
translation_verse: Amevi, esi Tiro le ehẽ dom de Yerusalem ŋu be: Dukɔwo ƒe agbo gbã, eyi de dzinye, eye nu abɔ de asinye, le esi wòzu gbegbe ŋuti la,

english_verse: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
translation_verse: eyata ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Tiro, maƒo de dziwò, eye mana dukɔ geɖewo naho de ŋuwò, abe alesi atsiaƒu nana eƒe tsotsoewo honae ene.

english_verse: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
translation_verse: Magblẽ Tiro ƒe gliwo, eye mamũ eƒe xɔ tsralawo aƒu anyi, makplɔ eƒe anyiglãgowo ɖa, eye mawɔe woazu agakpe ƒeƒle.

english_verse: where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed
translation_verse: Azu ɖɔsiaƒe le atsiaƒu titina, Aƒetɔ Yehowa be, nyee gblɔe, eye azu nuhaha na dukɔwo;

english_verse: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: eye woatsɔ yi awu eƒe du, siwo le anyigba dzi la me tɔwo, ne wòadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: Elabena ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, makplɔ Babel-fia Nebukadnezar, amesi nye fiawo dzi fia, atso anyiehe akpe ɖe sɔwo, tasiaɖamwo kple sɔdolawo, amehawo kple dukɔ geɖe ŋu ava ƒo ɖe Tiro dzi.

english_verse: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
translation_verse: Atsɔ yi awu wò du, siwo le anyigba dzi la me tɔwo, eye woatu dzɔlawo ƒe xɔ tsralawo ɖe ŋuwò, aƒu kpo ɖe ŋuwò, eye wòakɔ akpoxɔnu dzi ɖe ŋuwò.

english_verse: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
translation_verse: Atsɔ eƒe gligbãnuwo atu wò gli, eye wòatsɔ eƒe fiawo agba wò xɔ tsralawo aƒu anyi.

english_verse: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
translation_verse: Eƒe sɔ gbogboawo ƒe ʋuʋudedi abla wò kɔtɔɔ, eye sɔdolawo, tasiaɖamfɔwo kple tasiaɖamwo ƒe hoowɔwɔ ana be, wò gliwo nadzo kpekpekpe, ne ege de wò agbowo me, abe alesi wogena de du gbagbã me ene.

english_verse: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
translation_verse: Eƒe sɔwo ƒe afɔ anyã avuzi le wò kpɔdomeewo katã, awu wò dukɔ kple yi, eye wò ŋusẽ ƒe sɔtiawo amũ adze anyi.

english_verse: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
translation_verse: Woaha wò kesinɔnuwo, eye woada adzo wò adzɔnuwo, woamũ wò gliwo, woagbã wò dzidzɔkpɔxɔwo, eye woalɔ wò kpewo, atiwo kple anyiglãgowo aƒu gbe ɖe atsiaƒu me.

english_verse: You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps,
translation_verse: Matsi wò hadzidziwo ƒe ɖiɖi nu, eye womagase wò kasaŋkuwo ƒe ɖiɖi azɔ o.

english_verse: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
translation_verse: Mawɔ wò nazu agakpe ƒeƒle, ɖɔsiaƒe nazu, eye womagatso wò akpɔ o; Aƒetɔ Yehowa be, nye Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ ɖe Tiro ŋu enye si: Ne amesiwo woda nui, le ŋeŋem, eye wowu amewo le mewo la, wò anyidzedze ƒe didi ana ƒukpowo nadzo kpekpekpe.

english_verse: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
translation_verse: Ƒuta amegãwo katã aɖi le woƒe fiazikpuiwo dzi ɖe anyi, woaɖe woƒe awu ʋlayawo ɖi, eye woaɖe woƒe avɔ ŋɔŋɔewo ɖi; ŋɔdzi anyẽ atsyɔ wo, woabɔbɔ nɔ anyigba, woanɔ dzodzom nyanyanya ɖaa, eye woƒe nu aku de ŋuwò.

english_verse: and sing this funeral song: “The great city beside the sea is destroyed! Its people once ruled the coast and terrified everyone there.
translation_verse: Eye woato konyifaha ɖe ŋuwò agblɔ ɖe ŋuwò bena: Aleke du, si ŋkɔ nya la, tsrɔ̃ hebu le atsiaƒu nu, wò, si mia kple mewo nɔlawo miekpɔ ŋusẽ le atsiaƒu dzi, eye wò ŋɔdzi kaka ɖe ŋuwò nɔlawo katã dome la!

english_verse: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
translation_verse: Azɔ ƒukpowo le dzodzom kpekpekpe le wò anyidzegbe, eye dzidzi ƒo ƒukpowo le atsiaƒu me le wò nuwuwu la.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you
translation_verse: Elabena ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Ne mena nèzu aƒedo abe du, si me amea ɖeke mele o ene, ne mehe tɔɖɔɖɔ va dziwò, eye tsi gãwo nye tsyɔ wò la,

english_verse: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
translation_verse: mana nayi aʋlimetɔ, siwo nye blematɔwo gbɔ; mana nanɔ tsieƒe le blemaƒedo me akpe de amesiwo le aʋli me la ŋu, ale be womagatso aƒe de mewo o, eye magadze le agbagbeawo ƒe anyigba dzi akpɔ o.

english_verse: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Matsɔ wò awɔ ŋɔdzinui, eye nuwò ayi, woadi wò, ke womagakpɔ wò gbeɖegbeɖe akpɔ o, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe!

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
translation_verse: Amevi, to konyifaha ɖe Tiro ŋu,

english_verse: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
translation_verse: eye nagblɔ na Tiro bena: Wò, si le atsiaƒu to, eye nèle asi tsam kple dukɔwo yi ƒukpo geɖewo dzi, ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Tiro, ele gbɔgblɔm be: „Menyo eteƒe mekɔ o.“

english_verse: and your control of the sea. You are a ship built to perfection.
translation_verse: Wò anyigba le atsiaƒu titina; tsowòlawo na nènyo eteƒe mekɔ o.

english_verse: Builders used cypress trees from Mount Hermon to make your planks and a cedar tree from Lebanon for your tall mast.
translation_verse: Senirtɔwo ƒe sesewu wotsɔ kpa wòe, eye Libanon ƒe sederti wotsɔ wɔ abalati ɖe mewòe.

english_verse: Oak trees from Bashan were shaped into oars; pine trees from Cyprus were cut for your deck, which was then decorated with strips of ivory.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ Basantɔwo ƒe fɔfɔli kpa wò akɔfawoe, eye wofa nyiɖu ɖe mewò hetsakae kple kpomi, si tso Kititɔwo ƒe ƒukpowo dzi.

english_verse: The builders used fancy linen from Egypt for your sails, so everyone could see you. Blue and purple cloth from Cyprus was used to shade your deck.
translation_verse: Egiptetɔwo ƒe aklala, si wolɔ̃ ŋɔŋɔe la, nye wò abala, ne wòanye aflaga na wò, aɖabɛ blɔtɔ kple dzĩtɔ tso Elisa-ƒukpowo dzi nye wò agbadɔ.

english_verse: Men from Sidon and Arvad did the rowing, and your own skilled workers were the captains.
translation_verse: Zidonitɔwo kple Arwadtɔwo nye wo ʋukulawo; Tiro, wò ame nyanu, siwo nɔ mewo la, nye wò kuɖɔɖolawo.

english_verse: Experienced men from Byblos repaired any damages. Sailors from all over shopped at the stores in your port.
translation_verse: Gebal-ame tsitsiwo kple woƒe aɖaŋuawo nɔ mewo, ne woatre wò ɖuɖuƒewo; atsiaƒu dzi ʋuwo kple wo kulawo nɔ mewo, ne woaɖɔ li adzɔnu na wò.

english_verse: Brave soldiers from Persia, Lydia, and Libya served in your navy, protecting you with shields and helmets, and making you famous.
translation_verse: Amewo tso Persia, Lud kple Put nye aʋawɔlawo nɔ wò aʋakɔwo dome; wotsɔ akpoxɔnu kple gakuku ku nu ɖe mewò, woawoe ɖo atsyɔ na wò.

english_verse: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
translation_verse: Arwad-viwo kple wò aʋakɔwo le wò gliwo dzi godoo va kpe, eye Gamaditɔwo le wò xɔ tsralawo me; wotsɔ woƒe akpoxɔnuwo ku wò gliwo ŋu godoo va kpe, woawoe na wò nyonyo teƒe mekɔ o.

english_verse: Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products.
translation_verse: Tarsis tsa asi kpli wò le kesinɔnu gbogboawo katã ta; etsɔ klosalo, gayibɔ, gaɣi kple tsumi ƒle wò adzɔnuwoe.

english_verse: The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze,
translation_verse: Yawan, Tubal kple Mesex tsa asi kpli wò, amegbetɔwo kple akɔblinuwo wotsɔ ƒle wò adzɔnuwoe.

english_verse: and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules.
translation_verse: Amesiwo tso Togarma ƒe me la, tsɔ sɔwo, aʋawɔsɔwo kple tedzisɔwo ƒle wò adzɔnuwoe.

english_verse: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
translation_verse: Dedantɔwo tsa asi kpli wò, ƒukpo geɖewo ƒe asitsatsa le asiwò me, eye wodzra nyiɖuwo kple keyi na wò.

english_verse: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
translation_verse: Yuda kple Israel tsa asi kpli wò; wotsɔ Minitɔwo ƒe lu, ƒo, anyitsi, ami kple lili ƒle wò adzɔnuwoe.

english_verse: The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
translation_verse: Damasko tsɔ Xelbontɔwo ƒe wein kple alẽfu ɣi ƒle wò aɖanudɔ gbogboawo kple wò kesinɔnu gbogboawo katãe.

english_verse: Vedan and Javan near Uzal traded you iron and spices.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ Usaltɔwo ƒe wein ƒle wò adzɔnuwoe, wotsɔ gayibɔ tete, kotoklobo kple gbekee ɖɔ li wò adzɔnuwoe.

english_verse: The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets,
translation_verse: Dedan tsɔ sɔkpa kuntru, siwo wotsɔna doa sɔe, tsa asi kpli wò.

english_verse: while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats.
translation_verse: Arabiatɔwo kple Kedar-amegãwo katã nye asitsalawo nɔ asiwò me, wotsɔ alẽviwo, agbowo kple gbɔ̃tsuwo tsa asi kpli wò.

english_verse: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
translation_verse: Asitsalawo tso Saba kple Ragma tsa asi kpli wò; wotsɔ atike nyuitɔ vovovowo, kpe xɔasi vovovowo kple sika ƒle wò adzɔnuwoe.

english_verse: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
translation_verse: Xaran, Kane, Eden kple asitsalawo tso Saba, Asur kple Media blibo la tsa asi kpli wò.

english_verse: and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ atsyɔ̃vɔwo, aɖabɛ blɔtɔ ƒe awu ʋlayawo, avɔ ŋɔŋɔewo, kuntru ŋɔŋɔewo kple atagbi, siwo woƒo fefekae kple asiwo wogbe mligoe la, va tsa asi kpli wò le wò asiwo me.

english_verse: Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go. You were like a ship loaded with heavy cargo
translation_verse: Tarsis-ʋuwo he wò adzɔnuwo vɛ na wò, ale be nu bɔ ɖe asiwò, eye nèkpɔ ho fũ le atsiaƒu titina.

english_verse: and sailing across the sea, but you were wrecked by strong eastern winds.
translation_verse: Kuwòlawo ku wò to tɔ gãwo dzi; ɣedzeƒeya gbã wò ɖe atsiaƒu titina!

english_verse: The shouts of your drowning crew were heard on the shore.
translation_verse: Kuɖɔɖolawo ƒe ɣli ana ƒutawo nadzo kpekpekpe,

english_verse: Every ship is deserted; rowers and sailors and captains all stand on shore,
translation_verse: atablukulawo katã ado le woƒe ʋuwo me; ʋukulawo kple kuɖɔɖola, siwo katã le atsiaƒu dzi la, aɖi go ɖe gota.

english_verse: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
translation_verse: Wòado aƒa ɖe ŋuwò, eye woaxa nu vevie, wòala kewɔ akɔ ɖe ta me, eye woanɔ togotogoe ƒom le dzowo me.

english_verse: they shave their heads and dress in sackcloth as they cry in despair.
translation_verse: Woalũ ta kokoe le tawo, eye woata akpanya, woafa avi ɖe ŋuwò vevie tso dzi me, eye woaxa nu.

english_verse: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
translation_verse: Woato konyifaha ɖe ŋuwò le woƒe nuxaxa me adzi ha ade wò bena: „Ameka le abe Tiro ene? Ɖoɖoe zi le eŋu abe aƒedo ene le atsiaƒu titina.

english_verse: “Nations that received your merchandise were always pleased; kings everywhere got rich from your costly goods.
translation_verse: Esi wò adzɔnuwo to atsiaƒu dzi va la, eɖi ƒo na dukɔ geɖewo, etso wò kesinɔnu gbogboawo kple wò adzɔnuwo na anyigba dzi fiawo kpɔ hoe.

english_verse: But now you are wrecked in the deep sea, with your cargo and crew scattered everywhere.
translation_verse: Azɔ ègbã gudugudu ɖe tɔ gɔme, eye nete ɖa tso atsiaƒu nu; wò adzɔnuwo kple wò ameha, siwo katã na mewo la nyro!“

english_verse: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
translation_verse: Ƒukpo dzinɔlawo katã ƒe nu ku ɖe ŋuwò, woƒe fiawo ƒe lãme ble fu, eye woɖo adã lilili.

english_verse: The merchants of the world can't believe what happened. Your death was gruesome, and you are gone forever.”
translation_verse: Dukɔwo ƒe asitsalawo le tsiã dom ɖe ŋuwò; nuwo yi ŋɔdzitɔe, eye maganɔ anyi akpɔ gbeɖegbeɖe o.

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam bena:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
translation_verse: Amevi, gblɔna Tiro-amegã be: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esi wò dzi le dadam, eye nele gbɔgblɔm be, Mawu yenye, eye Mawu ƒe nɔƒe yele le atsiaƒu titina, eye nèwɔ wò dzi abe Mawu to ene, evɔ wònye amegbetɔ nènye, eye menye Mawu o la, —

english_verse: You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
translation_verse: kpɔ ɖa, ènya nu wu Daniel, nya ɣaɣlaa ɖeke mele vivi me ɖe wò o;

english_verse: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
translation_verse: wò nunya kple wò gɔmesese netsɔ kpɔ kesinɔnui, eye nède sika kple klosalo wò nudzraɖoƒewo;

english_verse: You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
translation_verse: wò nunya geɖe kple wò asitsatsa nètso kpo kesinɔnui kpaŋkpaŋ, eye wò dzi de asi dàda me le wò kesinɔnuawo ta —

english_verse: You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God,
translation_verse: eyata ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi. Esi newɔ wò dzi abe Mawu to ene la,

english_verse: will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get.
translation_verse: eyata kpɔ ɖa, makplɔ du bubu me to, siwo nye ŋutasẽlawo aƒu wò dukɔ, woadi yi ɖe wò nunya ƒe nyonyo ŋu, eye woado gu wò atsyɔ̃.

english_verse: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
translation_verse: Woatutu wò ade aʋli me, eye àku abe ame tsiaʋa ene ɖe atsiaƒu titina.

english_verse: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
translation_verse: Ɖe àgblɔ emegbe le wuwòlawo ŋku me be, Mawu yenyea? Amegbetɔ nènye le amesiwo da nu wò la si me, eye menye Mawu o.

english_verse: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
translation_verse: Àku abe bolotɔwo ene ɖe du bubu me towo si me; Aƒetɔ Yehowa be: Nyee gblɔe!

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying: At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking.
translation_verse: Amevi, to konyifaha ɖe Tiro-fia ŋu, eye nagblɔ nɛ bena: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Ŋkɔsigɛ, si wodzidze wòsɔ, nènye, nunya ba ɖe asiwò, eye wò nyonyo teƒe mekɔ o.

english_verse: You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born.
translation_verse: Ena Mawu ƒe abɔ Eden me, eye wotsɔ kpe xɔasi vovovowo ɖo ŋuwò. Karneol, topas kple yaspis, krisolit, soham kple oniks, safir, ametist kple smaragd; sika wotsɔ ɖo to na wò, eyae wotso do atsiã na wò le gbesigbe wowɔ wò.

english_verse: I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
translation_verse: Enye Kerubi keke aʋala me, metsɔ wò ɖo Mawu ƒe to kɔkɔe la dzi, eye nèzɔ dzokpewo dome.

english_verse: You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things.
translation_verse: Dzuƒe menɔ wò zɔzɔme ŋu tso gbesigbe wowɔ wò, vaseɖe esime wokpɔ nu madzɔmadzɔ le ŋuwò o.

english_verse: You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
translation_verse: Le wò asitsatsa gbogboawo ta nètso nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ yɔ ɖokuiwò mee, eye nezu nuvɔ̃wɔla; eyata menya wò ɖa le Mawu ƒe to kokoe la dzi, eye metsrɔ̃ wò le dzokpeawo dome, wò Kerubi, si keke aʋala me.

english_verse: It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you.
translation_verse: Wò dzi de asi dada me le wò nyonyo ta, ètsɔ wò nunya de aka le wò atsyɔ̃ ta; eyata matsɔ wò aƒu anyi, eye matsɔ wò ade asi na fiawo, ne woakpɔ wò ʋuu keke wòati wo.

english_verse: You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood,
translation_verse: Etsɔ wò vodada gbogboawo kple wò asitsatsa madzɔmadzɔ gblẽ ko ɖo na wò kɔkɔeƒe la; eyata mena dzo do tso mewo hefiã wò, eye metso wò wo dzowɔe ɖe anyigba dzi le amesiwo katã kpo wò la ŋku me.

english_verse: and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever. Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
translation_verse: Wò ame nyanyɛwo katã le dukɔwo dome ƒe nu ku ɖe ŋuwò; nuwo yi ŋɔdzitɔe, eye màganɔ anyi akpɔ gbeɖegbeɖe o. Zidon gbagbã.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon
translation_verse: Amevi, trɔ ŋgɔ de Zidon, eye nagblɔ nya ɖi ɖe eŋu

english_verse: and tell its people: I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy.
translation_verse: gblɔ bena: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Zidon, mele ƒoƒo ge ɖe dziwò, eye makɔ ɖokuinye ŋu le mewo, eye wòadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa, nenye be, medrɔ̃ ʋɔnui, eye mekɔ ɖokuinye ŋu ɖe eŋuti.

english_verse: I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Maɖo dɔvɔ̃ ɖe eŋu, eye ʋu ano eƒe kpɔdomeewo, amesiwo woda nui la, atsi yi, si tso goawo katã me va ɖe eŋu la nu le eme, eye woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ Yehowa.

english_verse: When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. A Blessing for Israel
translation_verse: Eye ŋu tɔame kple aŋɔka wɔnuveviame maganɔe na Israel ƒe aƒe la tso amesiwo ƒo xlã wo godoo, eye wole vlo dom wo la si me o, ne woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ Yehowa.

english_verse: The Lord God said: Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Ne meƒo Israel ƒe aƒe la nu ƒu tso dukɔ, siwo katã dome wokaka ɖo dome la, ekema makɔ ɖokuinye ŋu ɖe wo ŋuti le dukɔwo ŋku me, eye woano woƒe anyigba, si metsɔ na nye dɔla Yakob la dzi.

english_verse: They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Woanɔ edzi bɔkɔɔ, eye woatu xɔwo ahade weingblewo; ne medrɔ̃ ʋɔnu amesiwo katã le vlo dom wo le goawo katã me la, woawo ano anyi bɔkɔɔ, eye wòadze sii be, nye Yehowa ye nye woƒe Mawu.

english_verse: Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: Le ƒe ewolia me, le dzinu ewolia ƒe ŋkeke wuievelia dzi la Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam bena:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people
translation_verse: Amevi, trɔ ŋgɔ de Egipte-fia Farao, eye nagblɔ nya ɖi ɖe eya kple Egipte blibo la ŋu.

english_verse: that I am saying: King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy!
translation_verse: Ƒo nu gblɔ bena: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Egipte-fia Farao, mele ƒoƒo ge ɖe dziwò, wò lo gã, si tsyɔ akɔ ɖe Nil-tɔsisi titina hele gbɔgblɔm be: „Tɔnyee nye tɔsisi la, eye nyee wɔe.“

english_verse: I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body.
translation_verse: Matso ƒu aƒo ɖe alɔxatsa me na wò, eye mana wò tɔwo me lãwo nalé ɖe wò tsrokpa ŋu, mahe wò ado goe tso wò to me, eye wò tɔwo me lãwo katã alé ɖe wò tsrokpa ŋu.

english_verse: I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh.
translation_verse: Matsɔ wò aƒu gbe ɖe gbegbe, eye nadze dogba dzi le gbe me, womafɔ wò aƒo ƒu o, eye womaɖi wò o, matsɔ wò awɔ nuɖuɖui na gbemelãwo kple dziƒoxewo.

english_verse: Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord. You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick.
translation_verse: Eye Egiptetɔwo katã adze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa, elabena wonye aƒlati na Israel ƒe aƒe la;

english_verse: When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
translation_verse: ne wolé wò kple asi la, aŋe avuvu woƒe asi blibo la, eye ne woziɔ ɖe ŋuwò la, àŋe aƒo ɖe woƒe ali me blibo la.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock,
translation_verse: Eyata ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, mahe yi ava dziwò, eye matsrɔ̃ amegbetɔ kple lã le dziwò.

english_verse: until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things. You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it.
translation_verse: Eye Egipte-nyigba azu aƒedo kple gbegbe, ne wòadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa. Esi nègblɔ be, ye toe nye Nil-tɔsisi la, eye yee wɔe ŋuti la,

english_verse: Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia.
translation_verse: eyata kpɔ ɖa, maƒo ɖe mia kple wò tɔsisiwo dzi, eye mana Egipte-nyigba nazu gbegbe kple aƒedo, tso Migdol va ke ɖe Siene ɖaseɖe Kus ƒe liƒo dzi.

english_verse: No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for
translation_verse: Amegbetɔ ƒe afɔ kple lã ƒe afɔ mato edzi o, eye ame manɔ edzi o ƒe blane.

english_verse: It will be the most barren place on earth. Every city in Egypt will lie in ruins during those
translation_verse: Mana Egipte-nyigba nazu aƒedo abe anyigba, siwo wogblẽ ene, eye eƒe duwo atsi anyi aƒedoe abe du gbagbã wo ene ƒe blane; makaka Egiptetɔwo ɖe dukɔwo dome, eye mahlẽ wo ɖe anyigbawo dzi.

english_verse: They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom
translation_verse: magaɖo Egiptetɔwo te, eye mana woatrɔ agbɔ va Patros-nyigba, si nye wo denyigba la dzi, eye woanye fiaɖuƒe suea ɖe le afima.

english_verse: and won't ever be strong enough to rule nations, as they did in the past.
translation_verse: Ano sue le fiaɖuƒewo dome, eye magakɔ ta dzi ɖe dukɔwo ŋu azɔ o, mana woanɔ ʋee, ne womagafanya dukɔwo o.

english_verse: My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
translation_verse: Israel ƒe aƒe la magaɖo ŋu ɖe wo ŋu azɔ, ne woaɖo ŋku vodada dzi na wo, nenye be, woku ɖe wo ŋu la o; eye wòadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ Yehowa.

english_verse: Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: Le ƒe blave vɔ adrelia me le dzinu gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam bena:

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city.
translation_verse: Amevi, Babel-fia Nebukadnezar na eƒe aʋakɔ wɔ dɔ sesẽ ɖe Tiro ŋu, tawo katã bebe, eye abɔtawo ɖe bo, ke eya kple eƒe aʋakɔ la mekpɔ fetua ɖeke tso Tiro gbɔ ɖe dɔ, si wòwɔ ɖe eŋu la la o.

english_verse: So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops.
translation_verse: Eyata ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, matsɔ Egipte-nyigba ade asi na Babel-fia Nebukadnezar, eye woatɔ eƒe kesinɔnuwo adzoe, aɖe aboyonu, eye wòaha nu; esia anye fetu na eƒe aʋakɔ.

english_verse: Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Matsɔ Egipte-nyigba nɛ wòanye eƒe fetu, si ta wòwɔ dɔ ɖo, elabena nyee wòwɔ dɔ na, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: Ɣemaɣi la mana Israel ƒe aƒe la nato dzo, eye maʋu nu na wò le wo dome, ne wòadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying: Cry out in despair,
translation_verse: Amevi, gblɔ nya ɖi gblɔ bena: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Mixa nu be: Baba na ŋkeke la!

english_verse: because you will soon be punished! That will be a time of darkness and doom for all nations.
translation_verse: Elabena ŋkeke la gogo, Yehowa ƒe ŋkeke la tu aƒe, blukɔdogbe anye dukɔwo ƒe azã la.

english_verse: Your own nation of Egypt will be attacked, and Ethiopia will suffer. You will be killed in battle, and your land will be robbed and left in ruins.
translation_verse: Yi age ɖe Egipte, eye ŋɔdzi alé Kus, nenye be, amewo tsi aʋa le Egipte, wolɔ eƒe kesinɔnuwo dzoe, eye wogbã eƒe agunuwo.

english_verse: Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle.
translation_verse: Kus, Put, Lud kple dukɔ tsakatsakawo katã, Lub kple dzoɖuxɔlɔ̃wo ƒe viwo atsi yi nu akpe ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi; Egipte ƒe ziɔɖeŋu amũ, eye eƒe ŋusẽ ƒe adegbeƒoƒo ayi to; woatsi yi nu tso Migdol vaseɖe Siene, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin.
translation_verse: Woatsi gbegbe le anyigba, siwo wogblẽ la dome, eye eƒe duwo anɔ du gbagbãwo dome.

english_verse: I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Eye wòadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa, ne medo dzo ɖe Egipte, eye megbã eƒe xɔnametɔwo katã nyanyanya.

english_verse: On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
translation_verse: Gbemagbe la ame dɔdɔwo atso gbɔnye aɖo ʋuwo, ne woaɖado vɔ̃ɖi na Kus, si li bɔkɔɔ la, eye ŋɔdzi alé wo le Egipte ƒe ŋkeke la ta; elabena kpɔ ɖa, ele vava ge.

english_verse: Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Matsi Egipte ƒe hoowɔwɔ nu to Babel-fia Nebukadnezar dzi.

english_verse: He and his cruel troops will invade and destroy your land and leave your dead bodies piled everywhere.
translation_verse: Woakplɔ eya kple eƒe dukɔ, si nye dukɔ sẽŋuta la vɛ, ne woagblẽ anyigba la, woadi woƒe yiwo ɖe Egipte ŋu, eye woatsɔ ame tsiaʋawo ayɔ anyigba dzi fũ.

english_verse: I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
translation_verse: Mana tɔsisiwo naƒu kplakplakpla; matsɔ anyigba la adzra na ame vɔ̃ɖiwo, eye mana ame tutɔwo nagblẽ anyigba la kple edzi nuwo. Nye Yehowa ye ƒo nu!

english_verse: All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Matsrɔ̃ legbawo, eye mana trɔ̃wo nu natso le Nof, amegãa ɖeke maganɔ Egipte-nyigba nu azɔ o, eye makaka ŋɔdzi ɖe Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
translation_verse: matrɔ nye dziku akɔ ɖe Sin, si nye Egipte ƒe mɔ̃ sesẽ la dzi, eye matsi hoowɔwɔ nu le No.

english_verse: I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear.
translation_verse: Matɔ dzo Egipte: Sin alé ku ŋɔdzitɔe, woagbã No, eye woaxaxa Nof ɖo le ŋdɔkutsu dzatsɛ.

english_verse: The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner.
translation_verse: On kple Pibeset ƒe ɖekakpuiwo atsi yi nu, eye nyɔnuwo ayi aboyo me.

english_verse: You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke ado viviti le Taxpanxes, ne meŋe Egipte ƒe atikplɔ, eye mena eƒe ŋusẽ ƒe adegbeƒoƒo nu tso; blukɔ atsyɔ eya ŋutɔ, eye woade aboyo eƒe duwo.

english_verse: When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord. Egypt's King Is Powerless
translation_verse: Eye mahe to na Egipte, ne wòadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa.

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: Le ƒe wuiɖekɛlia me, le dzinu gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke adrelia dzi la Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam bena:

english_verse: So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever,
translation_verse: Eyata ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, maƒo ɖe Egipte-fia Farao dzi, eye míaŋe eƒe alɔwo, nyuitɔ kple ŋeŋea, eye mana yi nage le esi.

english_verse: and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
translation_verse: Makaka Egiptetɔwo ɖe dukɔwo dome, eye mahlẽ wo ɖe anyigbawo dzi.

english_verse: I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mado ŋusẽ Babel-fia ƒe alɔ, ke Farao ƒe alɔ aɖiɖi ɖe anyi, ne wòadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa, ne metsɔ nye yi de asi na Babel-fia, be wòado ɖe Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_verse: Makaka Egiptetɔwo ɖe dukɔwo dome, eye mahlẽ wo ɖe anyigbawo dzi, ne woadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa.

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
translation_verse: Le ƒe wuiɖekɛlia me, le dzinu etɔ̃lia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam bena:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying: You are more powerful than anyone on earth. Now listen to this.
translation_verse: Amevi, gblɔ na Egipte-fia Farao kple eƒe ame gbogboawo bena: Amekae nẽsɔ kplii le wò gãnyenye me?

english_verse: There was once a cedar tree in Lebanon with large, strong branches reaching to the sky.
translation_verse: Sederti nɔ Libanon ta me, eƒe alɔwo nyo, eye wòdo kpekpekpe, ekɔ, eye eƒe ɖɔmee ɖatɔ alilikpowo.

english_verse: This tree had plenty of water to help it grow tall, and nearby streams watered the other trees in the forest.
translation_verse: Tsiwo na wòtsi, eye agu me tsiwo na wòkɔ, woƒe tɔsisiwo si ƒo xlã ati dodo la, eye woɖe tɔʋuwo ɖo ɖe gbemetiwo katã.

english_verse: But this tree towered over those other trees, and its branches grew long and thick.
translation_verse: Eyata wòkɔ wu gbemetiwo katã, eƒe alɔwo sɔ gbɔ, eye wodidi, elabena ekpɔ tsi geɖe, ne wòavu eɖokui.

english_verse: Birds built nests in its branches, and animals were born beneath it. People from all nations lived in the shade of this strong tree.
translation_verse: Dziƒoxewo katã wɔ atɔ ɖe eƒe alɔwo me, gbemelãwo katã dzi vi ɖe eƒe alɔwo te, eye dukɔ geɖewo le eƒe vɔvɔli te.

english_verse: It had beautiful, long branches, and its roots found water deep in the soil.
translation_verse: Eƒe lolome nyo, eye eƒe alɔwo didi, elabena eƒe kewo le tsi geɖewo ŋu.

english_verse: None of the cedar trees in my garden of Eden were as beautiful as this tree; no tree of any kind had such long branches.
translation_verse: Sedertiwo medo vɔvɔli ɖe edzi le Mawu ƒe abɔ me o; sesewu mede eƒe alɔwo nu o, eye xetiwo meɖe alɔ abe eya ene o; ati, siwo katã le Mawu ƒe abɔ me la, menyo de enu o.

english_verse: I, the Lord, gave this tree its beauty, and I helped the branches grow strong. All other trees in Eden wanted to be just like it.
translation_verse: Mewɔe wònyo le eƒe alɔ gbogboawo la, ale be Eden-ti, siwo katã le Mawu ƒe abɔ me la, le ŋu ʋãmi.

english_verse: King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree: The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant.
translation_verse: Eyata ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Esi wòkɔ alea, eƒe ɖɔmee ɖatɔ alilikpowo, eye wòle dadam le eƒe kɔkɔ ta la,

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness.
translation_verse: eyata màtsɔe ade asi na dukɔwo ƒe ŋusẽtɔ, eye wòawɔ nu kplii; le eƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ta la manyãe ɖa.

english_verse: Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else.
translation_verse: Du bubu me tɔ, siwo nye dukɔ sẽŋutawo la, lae, eye wotsɔe ƒu anyi; eƒe alɔwo dze towo dzi kple baliwo katã me, eye eƒe alɔwo fli ɖe anyigba ƒe gbadza ƒe wo katã; anyigba dzi dukɔwo katã dzo le eƒe vɔvɔli te hegblẽe ɖi.

english_verse: Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
translation_verse: Dziƒoxewo katã dze ɖe eƒe zekpẽ, si wolã la dzi, eye gbemelãwo katã mlɔ eƒe alɔwo dzi;

english_verse: Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
translation_verse: ne ati, siwo katã le tɔ to, magaƒo adegbe le woƒe koko ta, woƒe ɖɔmee magato alilikpo, eye woƒe ŋusẽtɔ, siwo katã nye tsinolawo la, magaɖo dzi ɖe wo ɖokui ŋu le woƒe gãnyenye me o! Elabena kuviwo wo katã wonye, eye wòayi tsieƒe abe amegbetɔvi, siwo yi aʋli me la ene.

english_verse: On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Gbesigbe wòyi tsieƒe la, mena agu me tsiwo xa nu le eta, wogbugbɔ woƒe tɔsisiwo ɖe megbe, be woƒe tsiwo nu tso; Libanon ta ahovɔ le eta, eye gbemetiwo katã yrɔ le eta.

english_verse: This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble. The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls.
translation_verse: Eƒe anyidzedze ƒe ɖiɖi na dukɔwo dzo nyanyanya esi mena wòyi tsieƒe kpe ɖe aʋli me yilawo ŋu; eye Eden-tiwo katã, Libanon ƒe ati tiatia nyuitɔwo, siwo katã nye tsinolawo, fa akɔ na wo ɖokui le tsieƒe.

english_verse: Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
translation_verse: Woawo hã yi amesiwo woda yii la gbɔ le tsieƒe, amesiwo nye eƒe alɔ nɔ eƒe vɔvɔli te le dukɔwo dome.

english_verse: King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Azɔ Eden-tiwo dometɔ ka nèsɔ kpli le atsyɔ̃ kple lolo gome? Ke woatsɔ wò aƒu tsieƒe akpe ɖe Eden-tiwo ŋu; bolotɔwo dome namlɔ le amesiwo woda yii la gbɔ. Farao kple eƒe ame gbogboawo katã nye esia, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe!

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
translation_verse: Le ƒe wuievelia me, le dzinu wuievelia fe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam bena:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying: You act like a lion roaming the earth; but you are nothing more than a crocodile in a river, churning up muddy water with your feet.
translation_verse: Amevi, to konyifaha ɖe Egipte-fia Farao ŋu nagblɔ nɛ bena: Wò amesi nye dzata le dukɔwo dome la, nuwò yi! Lo nènye nɔ tɔ me, ètu tsi to ŋɔti me, ètsɔ wò afɔ blu tɔe, eye nènyã avuzi le tɔsisi me.

english_verse: King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore.
translation_verse: Eyata ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Mana dukɔ, siwo kpe ta, nada ɖɔ na wò, eye woatsɔ nye ɖɔ ahe wò ɖe go.

english_verse: I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh.
translation_verse: Matsɔ wò axlã ɖe anyi, matsɔ wò aƒu gbe ɖe dogba dzi, eye mana dziƒoxewo katã nadze ɖe dziwò, eye anyigba blibo la dzi lãwo naɖu wò aɖi ƒo.

english_verse: I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys,
translation_verse: Matsɔ wò lã ada ɖe towo dzi, eye matsɔ wò kukua ayɔ baliwo me fũ.

english_verse: and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams.
translation_verse: Mana anyigba, si dzi wò tsi gbagba ɖo la, nanɔ wò ʋu vaseɖe towo gbɔ ke, eye nayɔ baliwo me taŋ.

english_verse: I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining.
translation_verse: Ne mena nuwò yi la, matsyɔ nu na dziŋgɔli, eye eƒe ɣletiviwo ata ahovɔ; alilikpo atsyɔ ɣe dzi, eye dzinu magaɖi o.

english_verse: The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mata ahovɔ na dziƒo ƒe nu keklẽwo katã le tawò, eye mana blukɔ nado ɖe wò anyigba dzi, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you.
translation_verse: Mado nuxaxa na dukɔ geɖewo ƒe dzi, ne mehe wò anyidzedze yi dukɔwo dome le anyigba, siwo menya o la dzi.

english_verse: They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
translation_verse: Mana dzidzi naƒo dukɔ geɖewo le tawo, eye woƒe fiawo ƒe lãme able fu le tawò, ne menyẽ nye yi le wo ŋku me, eye wo dome amesiame anɔ dzodzom nyanyanya ɣeawokatãɣi le woƒe agbe ta le wò anyidzegbe.

english_verse: The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt!
translation_verse: Elabena ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Babel-fia ƒe yi aƒo ɖe dziwò.

english_verse: Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed.
translation_verse: Matsɔ kalẽtɔwo ƒe yi adza wò ame gbogboawo, amesiwo katã nye dukɔ sẽŋutawo; woagblẽ Egipte ƒe atsyɔ̃ dome, eye woatsrɔ̃ eƒe ame gbogboawo katã.

english_verse: I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water.
translation_verse: Matsrɔ̃ eƒe lãwo katã ɖa le tɔ gãwo to, amegbetɔ ƒe afɔ magablu wo azɔ o, eye lãwo ƒe afɔ magablu wo azɔ o.

english_verse: The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Emegbe mana eƒe tsiwo nadze anyi, eye eƒe tɔsisiwo nasi abe ami ene, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe,

english_verse: Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: ne medo gbegbe Egipte-nyigba, miegblẽ nusi wo katã le anyigba dzi, eye mewu ame; siwo katã le edzi, ne wòadze sii be, nyee nye Yehowa.

english_verse: This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. A Sad Ending for Egypt
translation_verse: Konyifahae nye esia woadzii; dukɔwo ƒe nyɔnuviwo nedzi konyifaha sia; wòadzi konyifaha sia ɖe Egipte kple eƒe ame gbogboawo katã ŋu, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of that same month, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Le ƒe wuievelia me le dzinu la ƒe ŋkeke wuiatɔ̃lia dzi la Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam bena:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations.
translation_verse: Amevi, fa na Egipte ƒe ame gbogboawo, eye mia kple dukɔwo ƒe ŋusẽtɔwo ƒe nyɔnuviwo mido wo de tsieƒe ɖe amesiwo yi aʋli me la gbɔ!

english_verse: You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you.
translation_verse: Woatsi amesiwo woda yii la dome. Wotso yi la ɖe asi; mikplɔ eyama kple eƒe ame gbogboawo katã yii!

english_verse: Brave military leaders killed in battle will gladly welcome you and your allies into the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Kalẽtɔwo ƒe ame sesẽwo kple woƒe dzoɖuxɔlɔ̃wo agblɔ le tsieƒe ɖe wo ŋu be: Bolotɔwo, amesiwo woda yii la, va be, woamlɔ afi.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Woɖe yɔdo nɛ ɖe aʋli me ƒe dzogoe dzi ke, eye eƒe amehawo ɖe to ɖe eƒe yɔdo; ame tsiaʋawo sɔŋ wonye, eye wotsi yi nu, woawo nye amesiwo de ŋɔdzi agbagbeawo ƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ eya kple eƒe amehawo katã mlɔ ame tsiaʋawo dome, woƒe yɔdowo de to ɖee, bolotɔwo sɔŋ wonye, eye woda yi wo, elabena wode ŋɔdzi agbagbeawo ƒe anyigba dzi; azɔ ŋu akpe wo akpe ɖe aʋli me yilawo ŋu; ame tsiaʋawo dome wotsɔ wo mlɔe.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle.
translation_verse: Mesex kple Tubal kpakple woƒe amehawo katã le afima, eye woƒe yɔdowo ɖe to ɖe wo, bolotɔwo sɔŋ wonye, eye woda yi wo, elabena wode ŋɔdzi agbagbeawo ƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
translation_verse: Womemlɔ kalẽtɔ, siwo tsi aʋa gbadegbe ke, amesiwo tsɔ woƒe aʋawɔnuwo yi tsieƒe, wotsɔ woƒe yi ziɔ tae, eye woƒe vodadawo lé de woƒe ƒuwo ŋu la gbɔ o, evɔ wònye kalẽtɔawo de ŋɔdzi agbagbeawo ƒe anyigba dzi hafi.

english_verse: You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
translation_verse: Woagbã wò hã nyanyanya le bolotɔwo dome, eye àmlɔ amesiwo woda yii la gbɔ.

english_verse: The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: Edom kple eƒe fiawo kpakple eƒe amegãwo katã le afima, wotsɔ wo mlɔ amesiwo woda yii la gbɔ, evɔ wònye ŋusẽ le wo ŋu hafi; womlɔ bolotɔwo kple aʋli me yilawo gbɔ.

english_verse: The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: Anyiehe amegãwo katã kple Zidonitɔwo katã le afima, woyi ame tsiaʋawo gbɔ, eye ŋukpe lé wo, evɔ wònye woƒe ŋusẽ dzi ŋɔ hafi; azɔ wonye bolotɔwo mlɔ amesiwo woda yii la gbɔ, eye ŋu akpe wo akpe de aʋli me yilawo ŋu.

english_verse: The Lord God says: When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering.
translation_verse: Farao akpɔ amesiawo, eye wòafa akɔ na eɖokui le eƒe ame gbogboawo katã ta; amesiwo woda yii enye Farao kple eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mena wòde ŋɔdzi agbagbeawo ƒe anyigba dzi; ke Farao kple eƒe ame gbogboawo katã woamlɔ bolotɔwo dome le amesiwo woda yii la gbɔ, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming.
translation_verse: ekpɔ yi gbɔna ɖe anyigba la ŋu, eye woku kpẽ xlã nu dukɔ la,

english_verse: Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
translation_verse: Womagaɖo ŋu eƒe nuvɔ̃, siwo katã wòwɔ la nɛ o; nu dzodzoe kple nusi le eteƒe lae wòwɔ, eyata anɔ agbe kokoko!

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
translation_verse: Le aboyoɖeɖe mi ƒe ƒe wuiɖekɛlia me, le dzinu ewolia ƒe ŋkeke atɔ̃lia dzi la amea ɖe si tso Yerusalem va gbɔnye gblɔ bena: „Wosi du la!“

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying: Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch
translation_verse: Amevi, ƒo nu kple mia deviwo nagblɔ na wo bena: Ne mena yi va anyigbaa ɖe dzi, eye anyigba dzi tɔwo ɖe ame tso wo ɖokui dome tsɔ ɖo gbetakpɔlae,

english_verse: If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
translation_verse: Ne ese kpẽa ƒe didi, eye mena woxlɔ̃ nui o la, eƒe ʋu anɔ eya ŋutɔ dzi; ke ne ame ma na woxlɔ̃ nui la, ade eƒe agbe.

english_verse: But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Ne gbetakpɔla kpɔ yi gbɔna, ke meku kpẽ o, eye mexlɔ̃ nu dukɔ la o, eye yi va heɖe ame ɖeka ɖa le wo dome la, ame ma ƒe vodada tae woɖee ɖa ɖo, ke mabia eƒe ʋu tso gbetakpɔla la si me.

english_verse: Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me.
translation_verse: Amevi, wòe metsɔ ɖo gbetakpɔla na Israel ƒe aƒe la be, ne èse nyaa ɖe tso nunye me la, naxlɔ̃ nu wo nam.

english_verse: When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Ne megblɔ na ame vɔ̃ɖi be: „Ame vɔ̃ɖi, èle kuku ge,“ ke meƒo nu hexlɔ̃ nu ame vɔ̃ɖi la le eƒe zɔzɔme ŋuti o la, ekema ame vɔ̃ɖi la aku le eƒe vodada ta, ke mabia eƒe ʋu tso asiwò me.

english_verse: If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent. The Lord Is Always Fair (Ezekiel
translation_verse: Ke ne èxlɔ̃ nu ame vɔ̃ɖi la le eƒe zɔzɔme ŋuti, be wòaɖe asi le eŋu, eye wogbe asiɖeɖe le eƒe zɔzɔme ŋu la, ekema aku le eƒe vodada ta, ke wò la èɖe wò agbe. Mawu ƒe dɔmenyo kple dzɔdzɔenyenye.

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Ne ame dzɔdzɔe ɖe asi le eƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye ŋu hewɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi la, esia tae wòaku ɖo.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.”
translation_verse: Amevi, mia ɖeviwo le nu ƒom le ŋuwò le gliwo ŋu kple xɔwo ƒe ʋɔtruwo nu, eye wole gbɔgblɔm le wo nɔewo dome bena: Miva, ne míase gbe, si tso Yehowa gbɔ!

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me.
translation_verse: Amevi, gblɔ na Israel ƒe aƒe la bena: Aleke miele gbɔgblɔm be: „Míaƒe dzidadawo kple míaƒe nuvɔ̃wo do agba ɖe mía dzi, eye wona mia nu le yiyim, ɖe míano agbea?“

english_verse: Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na wo bena: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Metà ɖokuinye ƒe agbe be: Ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe ku mevivia nunye o, negbe be, ame vɔ̃ɖi naɖe asi le eƒe zɔzɔme ŋu, ne wòanɔ agbe boŋ ye. Israel ƒe aƒe, miɖe asi le miaƒe zɔzɔme vɔ̃ɖiwo ŋu, miɖe asi le wo ŋu, nukaŋuti miehe, yewoaku ɖo?

english_verse: Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
translation_verse: Amevi, gblɔ na mia ɖeviwo bena: Ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye maɖee le gbesigbe wòda ƒu o, eye ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wowu mana wòadze anyi le gbesigbe wòɖe asi le eƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ŋu o; eye ame dzɔdzɔe mate ŋu atsi agbe le gbesigbe wòwɔ nuvɔ̃ o.

english_verse: Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
translation_verse: Ne megblɔ na ame dzɔdzɔe be, anɔ agbe kokoko, gake wòɖe asi dziɖoɖo me ɖe eƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye ŋu, eye wòwɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi la, ekema womagaɖo ŋu eƒe dzɔdzɔenyenyewo katã o, ke boŋ eƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi, si wòwɔ la, eyae ana wòaku.

english_verse: Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right.
translation_verse: Ne megblɔ na ame vɔ̃ɖi be, aku kokoko, gake wòɖe asi le eƒe nuvɔ̃ ŋu, eye wòwɔ nu dzɔdzɔe kple nusi le eteƒe,

english_verse: For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live.
translation_verse: ame vɔ̃ɖi la gbugbɔ awɔbanu na, eɖo nusi wòda adzoe la teƒe, eye wòzɔ ɖe ɖoɖo agbetɔwo nu, be megawɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi azɔ o la, ekema ano agbe kokoko, maku o.

english_verse: Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair.
translation_verse: Ke mia ɖeviwo le gbɔgblɔm be: Aƒetɔ la ƒe nuwɔna mele eteƒe o; evɔ wònye woawo ŋutɔ ƒe nuwɔnae mele eteƒe o hafi.

english_verse: And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Eye ne ame vɔ̃ɖi ɖe asi le eƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ŋu hewɔ nu dzɔdzɔe kple nusi le eteƒe la, esia tae wòana agbe ɖo.

english_verse: But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done. The News of Jerusalem's Fall
translation_verse: Eye ne miele gbɔgblɔm be: Aƒetɔ la ƒe nuwɔna mele eteƒe o hã la, Israel ƒe aƒe, madrɔ̃ ʋɔnu mi ɖe amesiame ƒe zɔzɔme nu! Nyawo le Yerusalem ƒe gbegblẽ ŋuti.

english_verse: The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak. What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe asi va dzinye le fiẽ, hafi ame sisi la nava, eye wòʋu nu nam, hafi wòva le ŋdi; ale nye nu ʋu, eye nyemegazi kpi azɔ o.

english_verse: Then the Lord said:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam bena:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
translation_verse: Amevi, glikpo dzi vi, siwo le Israel-nyigba dzi la, le gbɔgblɔm be: Abraham la eya ɖeka koliae nɔ anyi, ke exɔ anyigba la wònye etɔ, miawo la míesɔ gbɔ, míawoe wotsɔ anyigba la na, be wòanye mia ta.

english_verse: So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying: How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder
translation_verse: Eyata gblɔ na wo bena: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Miele lã kple ʋu ɖum, mieto mo te ɖe miaƒe legbawo ŋu, eye miele ʋu kɔm ɖi tso, hafi miehe, anyigba la nanye yewo taa?

english_verse: and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
translation_verse: Miele dzi ɖom ɖe miaƒe yiwo ŋu, miewɔ ŋunyɔnu, eye amesiame gblẽ kɔ ɖo na ehavi srɔ̃ tso, hafi miebe, anyigba la nanye yewo tɔa?

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases.
translation_verse: Eyata gblɔ na wo bena: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Meta ɖokuinye ƒe agbe: Amesiwo le glikpo dzi la, atsi yi nu, matsɔ amesiwo le gbe me la, ana gbemelãwo woaɖu, eye amesiwo le mɔ̃ sesẽwo kple agatowo me la, aku ɖe dɔvɔ̃ si me.

english_verse: I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them.
translation_verse: Mana anyigba la nazu aƒedo kple gbegbe, matsi eƒe ŋusẽ, si ŋu wòle adegbe ƒom ɖo la nu, eye Israel-towo atsi ƒeƒle, ale be amea ɖeke magato wo dzi ayi o.

english_verse: I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord. The People Listen, but Don't Change The Lord said:
translation_verse: Eye woadze sii bena, nyee nye Yehowa, ne mena anyigba la zu aƒedo kple gbegbe le woƒe ŋunyɔnu, siwo katã wowɔ la ta. Tohehe nyagblɔɖi yeye.

english_verse: So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money.
translation_verse: Woava akpe ta ɖe gbɔwò, eye woabɔbɔ nɔ ŋkuwò me abe nye dukɔ ene ahase wò nyawo, ke womawɔ wo dzi o, hafi boŋ anɔ ŋɔnɔe le nu me na wo, eye woƒe dzi adze viɖe yome.

english_verse: They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, èle na wo abe ha vivi kple amesi gbe vivi li na, eye wònya kasaŋku ƒoƒo la ene, wòase wò nyawo, ke womawɔ wo dzi o.

english_verse: Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ele eme va ge, ne eva me la, wòadze sii be, nyagblɔɖilaa ɖe nɔ yewo dome kpɔ.

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam bena:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them: I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep.
translation_verse: Amevi, gblɔ nya ɖi ɖe Israel ƒe lãkplɔviwo ŋu, lãkplɔviawo ŋue nagblɔ nya ɖo bena: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Baba na Israel ƒe lãkplɔviwo, amesi nyi woawo ŋutɔ ɖokui; ɖe menye lãhawoe lãkplɔviwo nanyi oa?

english_verse: You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock!
translation_verse: Mieno notsi, mietsɔ lãfu wɔ avɔe ta, eye miewu lã damiwo, ke mienyi alẽawo o.

english_verse: You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep.
translation_verse: Miedo ŋusẽ lã kudɔewo o, eye mieyɔ do esiwo ƒe lãme gblẽ o, miebla abi na esiwo ŋe ata o, miegbugbɔ esiwo ka hlẽ la gbɔe o, eye miedi esiwo bu la o, ke boŋ mieɖu amegã ɖe wo dzi kple sesẽ, eye miesẽ ŋuta le wo ŋu.

english_verse: They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals.
translation_verse: Woka hlẽ, elabena kplɔla mele wo nu o, wòzu nuɖuɖu na gbemelãwo katã, eye woka hlẽ.

english_verse: So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
translation_verse: Nye alẽwo le tsa glãla tsam le towo katã kple togbɛ kɔkɔwo katã dzi, eye nye alẽwo ka hlẽ ɖe anyigba blibo la dzi; amea ɖeke meli abla wo ta ase alo adi wo o.

english_verse: Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Metà ɖokuinye ƒe agbe: Esi nye alẽwo zu nuhaha, eye nye alẽwo zu nuɖuɖu na gbemelãwo katã, elabena kplɔlaa ɖeke meli o, eye nye lãkplɔviwo mebiaa nye alẽwo ta sena o, lãkplɔviawo nyi woawo ŋutɔ ɖokui, eye wogbe nye alẽwo nyinyi la,

english_verse: So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, maƒo ɖe lãkplɔviawo dzi, eye mabia nye alẽwo tso wo si me, mana be, womagakpɔ nye alẽwo dzi azɔ o, eye lãkplɔviawo maganyi woawo ŋutɔ ɖokui azɔ o, maɖe nye alẽwo le ve me na wo, be womaganye nuɖuɖu na wo azɔ o. Aƒetɔ la ŋutɔ akpɔ eƒe alẽha la dzi.

english_verse: The Lord God then said: I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself,
translation_verse: Elabena ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, meli maɖi nye alẽwo, eye malé ŋku ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them
translation_verse: Alesi lãkplɔvi ɖea ŋku ɖe eƒe lãhawo le gbesigbe wòle eƒe alé, siwo ka hlẽ dome la, nenema maɖe ŋku ɖe nye alẽwo, eye maɖi wo aƒo ƒu tso teƒe, siwo katã woka hlẽ ɖo le blukɔ kple tsizidogbe la.

english_verse: and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields.
translation_verse: Makplɔ wo tso dukɔwo dome, eye maƒo wo nu ƒu tso anyigbawo dzi, makplɔ wo ava woƒe anyigba dzi, eye manyi wo le Israel ƒe towo dzi kple bali wo me kpakple anyigba la ƒe amenɔƒewo katã.

english_verse: I promise to take care of them and keep them safe,
translation_verse: Nye ŋutɔ manyi nye alẽwo, eye mana woatsyɔ akɔ anyi ɖi, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right. Judgment on the Strong Sheep
translation_verse: Madi esiwo bu, eye makplɔ tsiwo ka hlẽ la agbɔe, mabia abi na esiwo ŋe ala, eye maɖo ŋusẽ esiwo ƒe lãme gblẽ, makpɔ esiwo da ami, kple esiwo ƒe lãme sẽ la ta, eye manyi wo, abe alesi dze ene.

english_verse: The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel: I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak.
translation_verse: Mi, nye lãhawo, ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, madrɔ̃ ʋɔnu le alẽ kple alẽ dome, le agbo kple gbɔ̃tsu dome.

english_verse: Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy.
translation_verse: Esi miele gbe ɖum le lãnyiƒe nyui la, nu tsɛ ko wònye na mi, hafi mienyã avuzi le miaƒe gbe mamlea dzia? Eye esi miele tsi zɔzrɔ̃e nom la, nu tsɛ ko wònye na nu, hafi mietsɔ afɔ blu mamlea,

english_verse: That means my other sheep have nothing fit to eat or drink.
translation_verse: ne nye alẽwo naɖu nusi dzi mienyã avuzi le, eye woano nusi mieblu kple afɔa?

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will separate you strong sheep from the weak.
translation_verse: Eyata ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Kpɔ ɖa, meli, eye madrɔ̃ ʋɔnu le alẽ dami kple alẽ ɖiku dome.

english_verse: You strong ones have used your powerful horns to chase off those that are weak,
translation_verse: Esi mietsɔ axadame kple abɔgba mimi lã kudɔeawo katã ɖo, eye mietu dzo wo, vaseɖe esime mienyã wo do goe la,

english_verse: but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
translation_verse: eyata maxɔ na nye alẽwo, eye womaganye nuhaha azɔ o, eye madrɔ̃ ʋɔnu le alẽ kple alẽ dome. Kplɔla, si ado go tso Dawid ƒe me ŋugbedodo.

english_verse: After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you.
translation_verse: Maɖo kplɔla ɖeka kolia, si nye nye dɔla Dawid la, wo nu, ne wòanyi wo; eya anyi wo, eye wòanye kplɔla ha wo.

english_verse: He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Nye Yehowa manye Mawu na wo, eye nye dɔla Dawid anye amegã le wo dome; nye Yehowa ye gblɔe.

english_verse: The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid.
translation_verse: Mabia ŋutifafa ƒe nu kpli wo, eye matsrɔ̃ lã vɔ̃ɖiwo ɖa le anyigba dzi, ne woanɔ gbegbe aɖe dzi ɖi, eye woatsi avewo me adɔ.

english_verse: They will live around my holy mountain, and I will bless them by sending more than enough rain
translation_verse: Mayra woawo kple nye togbɛ ƒe nutowo me, eye mana tsi nadza ɖe edzaɣi, yayra ƒe tsi wòanye.

english_verse: to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
