The worshipers can offer as much grain as they want with each lamb. Three liters of olive oil must be offered with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Le ŋkekenyuiewo dzi kple ŋkekenyuiewo ƒe takpegbewo la nuɖuvɔsa efa ɖeka nakpe ɖe nyitsu ɖeka ŋu eye efa ɖeka nakpe ɖe agbo ɖeka ŋu, ke wòakpe alesi nu woate ŋu la, ɖe alẽviawo ŋu, eye ami hin ɖeka nanɔ efa ɖeka ŋu.

english_verse: If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
translation_verse: Eyi ne amegã la be, yeasa numevɔ alo akpedavɔ na Yehowa le eɖo kui si la, ekema woaʋu agbo, si ɖe ta ɣedzeƒe gome la nɛ, eye wòase eƒe numevɔ kple akpedavɔ, abe alesi wòwɔna le dzudzɔgbe ene, emegbe wòado go, eye ne edzo la, ekema woatu agbo la.

english_verse: Each morning a year-old lamb that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to please me.
translation_verse: Eye wòatsɔ alẽvi, si xɔ ƒe ɖeka, eye wòsɔ blibo la, asa numevɔe na Yehowa gbesiagbe; ŋdi sia ŋdi woatsɔe asa vɔe.

english_verse: Along with it, two kilograms of fine flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. This law will never change—
translation_verse: Wòatsɔ nuɖuvɔsa efa ƒe adeliawo ɖeka akpe ɖe eŋu asa vɔe ŋdi sia ŋdi hekpe de ami hin ƒe etɔ̃liawo ɖeka ŋu, ne woatsɔ adzaba wɔ memee wòanye nuɖuvɔsa na Yehowa; ɖoɖo anye esia ɖaa.

english_verse: The Lord God said: If the ruler of Israel gives some of his land to one of his children, it will belong to the ruler's child as part of the family property.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ Yehowa gblɔ esi: Ne amegã la na eƒe anyigbaa de viawo dometɔ ɖeka la, netsi viawo si me ahanye woƒe domenyinu.

english_verse: But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
translation_verse: Eye ne ena eƒe anyigbaa ɖe eƒe kluviwo dometɔ ɖeka la, ekema nenye etɔ, vaseɖe esime ablɔɖeƒe naɖo, emegbe wòagayi ɖe amegã la si me; negbe viawo ƒe domenyinu koe atsi wo si me.

english_verse: The ruler must never abuse my people by taking land from them. Any land he gives his children must already belong to him. The Sacred Kitchens
translation_verse: Ke amegã la megaka dukɔ la ƒe anyigba, ne wòaxɔ woƒe anyigba le wo si sesẽ o, ke boŋ netsɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba na viawo, ne wòanye wo tɔ, ne nye dukɔ la dometɔa ɖeke magaka hlẽ tso eƒe anyigba dzi o. Nuɖaxɔwo.

english_verse: The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard
translation_verse: Eye wòkplɔm to mɔnu, si le agbo la ƒe axa dzi la, heyi nunɔlawo ƒe xɔvi kɔkɔe, siwo le anyiehe gome la me; eye kpɔ ɖa, teƒea ɖe le axa dzi le ɣetoɖoƒe gome.

english_verse: We went back to the outer courtyard and walked past the four corners.
translation_verse: Emegbe wòkplɔm yi xɔxɔnu kɔtoetɔ, eye wòkplɔm to xɔxɔnu la ƒe dzogoe eneawo dzi, kpo ɖa, xɔxɔnu suesuewo le xɔxɔnu la ƒe dzogoewo dzi.

english_verse: Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires.
translation_verse: Woɖo glikpoe ƒo xlã wo ame eneawo katã me, eye woɖi mlekpui ɖe glikpoeawo ŋu godoo va kpe.

english_verse: The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nam bena: Esia nye nuɖaxɔ, afisi aƒe la ƒe subɔlawo aɖa dukɔ la ƒe akpedavɔsalã le.

english_verse: The man took me back to the temple, where I saw a stream flowing from under the entrance. It began in the south part of the temple, where it ran past the altar and continued east through the courtyard.
translation_verse: Eye wòkplɔm gbugbɔ yi xɔ la nu, eye kpɔ ɖa, tsi le dzidzim le xɔ la ƒe kpui te ɖo ta ɣedzeƒe gome; elabena xɔ la trɔ ŋgɔ dze ɣedzeƒe gome; eye tsi la si to xɔ la ƒe ɖusikpa dzi ɖo ta vɔsamlekpui la ƒe dzigbe gome.

english_verse: We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
translation_verse: Emegbe wòkplɔm to anyiehegbo nu, eye megado mo va agbo kɔtoetɔ, si dze ŋgɔ ɣedzeƒe gome la nu; eye kpɔ ɖa, tsi la le dzidzim le ɖusikpa dzi.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.” We walked to the riverbank,
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nam bena: Amevi, èkpɔea? Tete wòkplɔm gbugbɔ to tɔsisi la ŋu.

english_verse: where I saw dozens of trees on each side.
translation_verse: Eye esi metrɔ la, kpɔ ɖa, ati geɖewo mie ɖe tɔsisi la ƒe goawo kple eve dzi fũ.

english_verse: The man said: This water flows eastward to the Jordan River valley and empties into the Dead Sea, where it turns the salt water into fresh water.
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ nam bena: Tsi sia si to ɣedzeƒe nutowo me, esi to tagba heɖade nu atsiaƒu, si nye Dzeƒu la me, eye eƒe tsi atrɔ zu tsi nyui.

english_verse: Wherever this water flows, there will be all kinds of animals and fish, because it will bring life and fresh water to the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Afisiafi, si to la de la, nu gbagbe, siwo katã ʋãna, agba agbe, eye tɔmelãwo asɔ gbɔ fũ; afisiafi, si to la va la, tsi la atrɔ zu tsi nyui, eye nusianu, si gbɔ tɔ la de la, agbɔ agbe.

english_verse: From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ɖɔkplɔlawo anɔ eto tso En-Gedi vaseɖe En-Eglayim, eye ɖɔkplɔƒe wòazu; eme lãwo asa gbɔ kpaŋkpaŋ abe atsiaƒu gã me lãwo ene.

english_verse: But the marshes along the shore will remain salty, so that people can use the salt from them.
translation_verse: Ke eƒe siiwo kple tawo matrɔ o, ke boŋ dze anɔ wo me.

english_verse: Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people. The Borders of the Land
translation_verse: Ati tseku vovovowo amie ɖe tɔsisi la ƒe goawo kple eve dzi, woƒe aŋgbawo mayrɔ o, eye woƒe tsetsewo nu matso o; woatse ku yeye ɣleti sia ɣleti, elabena kɔkɔeƒe la woƒe tsi dzo tso; woƒe tsetse anye nuɖuɖu, eye woƒe aŋgbawo anye dɔyɔgbe. Anyigba la ƒe liƒowo.

english_verse: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean Sea, then continue eastward to Hethlon, to Lebo-Hamath, then across to Zedad,
translation_verse: Anyigba la ƒe liƒo le anyiehe gome ènye si: Tso atsiaƒu gã la nu to Xetlon vaseɖe Zedad,

english_verse: Berothah, and Sibraim, which is on the border between the two kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The border will end at Hazer-Hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
translation_verse: Xamat, Berota, Sibrayim, si le Damasko ƒe liƒo kple Xamat ƒe liƒo dome, Xazer-Enon, si le Xauran ƒe liƒo dzi.

english_verse: So the northern border will run between the Mediterranean Sea and Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath.
translation_verse: Ale liƒo la natso atsiaƒu nu vaseɖe Xazer-Enon le Damasko ƒe liƒo dzi, eye wòato anyiehe gome vaseɖe Xamat ƒe liƒo dzi; esia nye anyieheliƒo.

english_verse: The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
translation_verse: Ɣedzeƒe gome enye si: Yordan nanye liƒo le Xauran kple Damasko, Gilead kple Israel-nyigba dome; midzidzee tso liƒo kemea ŋu vaseɖe atsiaƒu la nu le ɣedzeƒe gome; esia nye ɣedzeƒekpa.

english_verse: The southern border will begin at Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and will end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Dzieheliƒo natso Tamar vaseɖe dzrewɔtsi la nu le Kades, eye wòato tɔʋu la ŋu vaseɖe atsiaƒu gã la nu; esia nye dzieheliƒo.

english_verse: The western border will run north along the Mediterranean Sea to a point just west of Lebo-Hamath.
translation_verse: Atsiaƒu gã la nanye liƒo le ɣetoɖoƒe gome tso liƒo sia gbɔ vaseɖe Xamat kasa; esia nye ɣetoɖoƒeliƒo.

english_verse: That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Eye mimã anyigba sia ɖe mia nɔeawo dome ɖe Israel ƒe toawo nu.

english_verse: It will belong to the Israelites and to any foreigners living among them whose children were born in Israel. These foreigners must be treated like any other Israelite citizen, and they will receive
translation_verse: Ne miedzidze nu ɖe edzi, be wòanye miaƒe domenyinu la, mibu amedzro, siwo le mia dome, eye wodzi viwo ɖe mia dome la abe Israel-viwo ƒe aƒeviwo ene; woaxɔ domenyinu kpe ɖe mia ŋu ɖe Israel ƒe toawo dome.

english_verse: a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Eye to, si me amedzroa le la, afimae miana eƒe domenyinu: ɖo, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe!

english_verse: South of Judah's territory will be a special section of land. Its length will be twelve and a half kilometers, and its width will run from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. My temple will be located in this section of land.
translation_verse: Adzo, si na ge miala la, nanɔ Yuda ƒe liƒo ŋu tso ɣedzeƒe vaseɖe ɣetoɖoƒe, woakeke abɔklugui akpe blave vɔ atɔ̃, eye wòadidi abe gomeawo dometɔ ɖeka ene tso ɣedzeƒe vaseɖe ɣetoɖoƒe, eye kɔkɔeƒe la nanɔ etitina.

english_verse: An area in the center of this land will belong to me. It will be twelve and a half kilometers long and ten kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Adzɔ, si miana Yehowa, nadidi abɔklugui akpe blave vɔ atɔ̃, eye wòakeke abɔklugui akpe blave.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will give half of my sacred land to the priests. Their share will be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide, and my temple will be right in the middle.
translation_verse: Adzɔ kɔkɔe la nanye nunɔlawo to, wòadidi le anyiehe gome abɔklugui akpe blave vɔ atɔ̃, eye woakeke le ɣetoɖoƒe gome abɔklugui akpe ewo, wòakeke le ɣedzeƒe gome abɔklugui akpe ewo, eye wòadidi le dziehe gome abɔklugui akpe blave vo alɔ̃, eye Yehowa ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la nanɔ etitina;

english_verse: Only priests who are descendants of Zadok will receive a share of this sacred land, because they remained faithful to me when the Levites and the rest of the Israelites started sinning.
translation_verse: nunɔla, siwo ŋu woka, amesiwo nye Zadok-viwo, eye wowɔ nye subɔsubɔdɔwo, wometrɔ le yonyeme abe Lewi-viwo ene, esime Israel-viwo tra mɔ o la tɔ wòanye.

english_verse: The land belonging to the priests will be the most sacred area and will lie south of the area that belongs to the Levites.
translation_verse: Eye wòanye adzo, si woɖe le anyigba la ŋu na wo ɖe Lewi-viwo ƒe liƒo dzi ahanye nu kɔkɔetɔ.

english_verse: I will give the other half of my sacred land to the Levites. Their share will also be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide,
translation_verse: Lewi-viwo mexɔe ɖe nunɔlawo ƒe liƒo ŋu wòadidi abɔklugui akpe blave vɔ atɔ̃, eye wòakeke abɔklugui akpe ewo. Didime blibo la nanye abɔklugui akpe blave vo atɔ̃, eye kekeme nanye abɔklugui akpe blave.

english_verse: and they must never sell or trade any of this land—it is the best land and belongs to me.
translation_verse: Womekpɔ mɔ atsɔ ɖe adzra o, womaɖɔ lii o, eye anyigba la ƒe nyuitɔ mayi ɖe ame bubu si me o; elabena nu kɔkɔe wònye na Yehowa.

english_verse: South of my sacred land will be a section twelve and a half kilometers long and three kilometers wide. It will not be sacred, but will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem, together with its houses and pastureland.
translation_verse: Ke teƒe mamlea, si keke abɔklugui akpe atɔ̃ mlo ɖe didime abɔklugui akpe blave vɔ atɔ̃ ŋu la, nanye hahoo ƒe anyigba hena du la, wòanye nɔƒe kple lãnyiƒe, eye du la nano titina.

english_verse: The land on the east and west sides of the city limits will be farmland for the people of Jerusalem; both sections will be five kilometers long and three kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Didime la ƒe susɔea, si mlo ɖe adzo kɔkɔea ŋu hele abɔklugui akpe ewo le ɣedzeƒe gome kple abɔklugui akpe ewo le ɣetoɖoƒe gome la ƒe agble me nuwo nanye nuɖuɖu na dua ƒe agbledelawo.

english_verse: People from the city will farm the land, no matter which tribe they belong to.
translation_verse: Eye agbledela, siwo tso Israel ƒe toawo katã me le dua me la, nade agble ɖe edzi

english_verse: And so the center of this special section of land will be for my sacred land, as well as for the city and its property. The land will be a square, twelve and a half kilometers on each side.
translation_verse: Adzo blibo, si miana, kpakple du la ƒe anyigba nanye abɔklugui akpe blave vɔ alɔ̃ le dzogoe eneawo me, eye adzɔ kɔkɔe wòanye.

english_verse: The regions east and west of this square of land will belong to the ruler of Israel. His property will run east to the Jordan River and west to the Mediterranean Sea. In the very center of his property will be my sacred land, as well as the temple,
translation_verse: Ke mamlea, si le adzɔ kɔkɔe la kple du la ƒe anyigba ƒe goawo kple eve dzi la, nanye amegã la tɔ; amegã la tɔ nanɔ abɔklugui akpe blave vɔ atɔ̃ la xa le ɣedzeƒe gome vaseɖe ɣedzeƒe-liƒo dzi, eye wòanɔ abɔklugui akpe blave vɔ atɔ̃ la xa le ɣetodoƒe gome vaseɖe ɣetoɖoƒe-liƒo dzi ahasɔ kple toawo ƒe gomeawo; adzo kɔkɔe la kple xɔ kɔkɔe la nanɔ titina.

english_verse: Gad's southern border is also the southern border of Israel. It will begin at the town of Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Eye Gad ƒe liƒo le dziehe gome nanye liƒo, si tso Tamar vaseɖe dzrewɔtsi la nu le Kades heto tɔʋu la ŋu va ke ɖe atsiaƒu gã la nu.

english_verse: That's how the land of Israel will be divided among the twelve tribes. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Gates of Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: Esia nye anyigba, si dzi miadzidze nu ɖo wòanye domenyinu na Israel ƒe toawo, eye esia nye woƒe gomewo, Aƒetɔ Yehowa ye gblɔe. Du kɔkɔe la ƒe nɔnɔme kple eƒe agbowo ŋkɔ.

english_verse: and so the total length of the wall will be ten kilometers. The new name of the city will be “The-Lord-Is-Here!”
translation_verse: Eƒe lolome le abɔklugui akpe wuienyi, eye woayɔ dua tso gbemagbe dzi be: „Yehowa le afima“.

english_verse: In the third year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Yoyakim ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒe etɔ̃lia me la Babel-fia Nehukadnezar ho ɖe Yerusalem ŋu, eye wòɖe to ɖee.

english_verse: The Lord let Nebuchadnezzar capture Jehoiakim and take away some of the things used in God's temple. And when the king returned to Babylonia, he put these things in the temple of his own god.
translation_verse: Eye Aƒetɔ la tsɔ Yuda-fia Yoyakim kple Mawu ƒe aƒe me nua ɖewo de asi nɛ; ekplɔ woyi eƒe mawu ƒe nɔƒe le Sinear-nyigba dzi, eye wòtsɔ nuawo de eƒe mawu ƒe nudzraɖoƒe.

english_verse: One day the king ordered Ashpenaz, his highest palace official, to choose some young men from the royal family of Judah and from other leading Jewish families.
translation_verse: Eye fia la de se na aƒedzikpɔlawo ƒe amegã Aspenaz be, wòaɖe ŋutsuviwo tso Israel-viwo dome, amesiwo tso fiaƒome kple bubumewo dome,

english_verse: The king said, “They must be healthy, handsome, smart, wise, educated, and fit to serve in the royal palace. Teach them how to speak and write our language
translation_verse: ŋutsuvi, siwo nu mewɔ afiaa ɖeke na o, eye wodze ɖeka, adaŋu le mo na wo, wodze si nu, nunya le tagbɔ na wo, eye wozã la, he woasuhɔ le fiasã me, eye woafia Kaldeatɔwo le nuŋɔŋlɔ kple gbe wo.

english_verse: and give them the same food and wine that I am served. Train them for three years, and then they can become court officials.”
translation_verse: Eye fia la do woƒe gbesiagbe nuɖuɖu na wo tso fia ƒe nuɖudu kple wein me, ne woatsɔ anyi woe ƒe eta; emegbe woasubɔ fia la.

english_verse: Four of the young Jews chosen were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, all from the tribe of Judah.
translation_verse: Yuda-vi, siwo le wo dome la, wonye: Daniel, Xananya, Misael kple Azarya.

english_verse: But the king's chief official gave them Babylonian names: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abednego.
translation_verse: Eye aƒedzikpɔlawo ƒe amegã tsɔ ŋkɔ na wo; Daniel tɔe nye Beltsazar, Xananya tɔe nye Sadrax, Misael tɔe nye Mesax, eye Azarya tɔe nye Aded-Nego.

english_verse: Daniel made up his mind to eat and drink only what God had approved for his people to eat. And he asked the king's chief official for permission not to eat the food and wine served in the royal palace.
translation_verse: Ke Daniel do de ta me be, yemele fia ƒe nuɖuɖu kple wein tsɔ ge agblẽ kɔ ɖo na ye ɖokui o, eye wòɖe kuku na aƒedzikpɔlawo ƒe amegã, ne yemagagblẽ kɔ ɖo na ye ɖokui o.

english_verse: God had made the official friendly and kind to Daniel.
translation_verse: Eye Mawu na aƒedzikpɔlawo ƒe amegã nyo dɔme na Daniel, eye wòve enu.

english_verse: But the man still told him, “The king has decided what you must eat and drink. And I am afraid he will kill me, if you eat something else and end up looking worse than the other young men.”
translation_verse: Eye aƒedzikpɔlawo ƒe amegã gblɔ na Daniel bena: Mele nye aƒetɔ fia, amesi ɖo nuɖuɖu kple nunono na mi la vɔ̃m; elabena ne ekpɔ be, míaƒe mo ɖi ku wu mía hatiwo tɔ la, ekema nye tae nye ekem mietsa na fia la.

english_verse: The king's official had put a guard in charge of Daniel and his three friends. So Daniel said to the guard,
translation_verse: Tete Daniel gblɔ na dzikpɔla, si aƒedzikpɔlawo ƒe amegã ɖo Danlel, Xananya, Misael kple Azarya nu la bena:

english_verse: “For the next ten days, let us have only vegetables and water at mealtime.
translation_verse: Tee kpɔ kple wò dɔlawo ŋkeke ewo, ne woatsɔ amã na mí míaɖu kple tsi na mí míano.

english_verse: When the ten days are up, compare how we look with the other young men, and decide what to do with us.”
translation_verse: Emegbe naɖe ŋku ɖe míaƒe nɔnɔme kple ŋutsuvi, siwo ɖua fia ƒe nuɖuɖu la ƒe nɔnɔme, eye alesi nakpɔ la, nenema nu nawɔ na wo ɖɔlawo ɖo.

english_verse: The guard agreed to do what Daniel had asked.
translation_verse: Eye wòɖo to wo le nya sia me hetee kpɔ kpli wo ŋkeke ewo.

english_verse: Ten days later, Daniel and his friends looked healthier and better than the young men who had been served food from the royal palace.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke ewo megbe la woƒe nɔnɔme nyo, eye woklã wu ŋutsuvl, siwo katã ɖua fia ƒe nuɖuɖu.

english_verse: After this, the guard let them eat vegetables instead of the rich food and wine.
translation_verse: Tso gbemagbe dzi dzikpɔla la ɖe woƒe nuɖuɖu kple wein, si woɖo na wo la ɖa, eye wòna ama wo.

english_verse: God made the four young men smart and wise. They read a lot of books and became well educated. Daniel could also tell the meaning of dreams and visions.
translation_verse: Eye Mawu na nunya kple gɔmesese ŋutsuvi ene siawo le nuŋɔŋlɔ vovovowo kple nunya gome; ke Daniel ya nya ŋutegawo katã kple drɔ̃ewo gɔme.

english_verse: At the end of the three-year period set by King Nebuchadnezzar, his chief palace official brought all the young men to him.
translation_verse: Esi ɣeyiɣi, si fia la de se be, woakplɔ wo vɛ, de la, aƒedzikpɔlawo ƒe amegã kplɔ wo va Nehukadnezar ŋku me.

english_verse: The king interviewed them and discovered that none of the others were as outstanding as Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they were given positions in the royal court.
translation_verse: Eye esi fia la ƒo nu kpli wo la, womekpɔ amea ɖeke le wo katã dome, si de Daniel, Xananya, Misael kple Azarya nu o; eye wosubɔ le fia le ŋku me.

english_verse: From then on, whenever the king asked for advice, he found their wisdom was ten times better than that of any of his other advisors and magicians.
translation_verse: Eye nya sia nya, si fia la bia wo le nunya kple gɔmesese gome la, ekpɔ be, woƒo eƒe fiaɖuƒe blibo la ƒe dzotɔwo kple bokɔnɔwo katã ta zi gbɔ zi ewo.

english_verse: Daniel served there until the first year of King Cyrus.
translation_verse: Eye Daniel tsi anyi vaseɖe fia Kores ƒe ƒe gbãtɔ me.

english_verse: During the second year that Nebuchadnezzar was king, he had such horrible nightmares that he could not sleep.
translation_verse: Le Nehukadnezar ƒe fiaɖudu ƒe ƒe evelia me la Nehukadnezar ku drɔ̃e, eye wòdzo haha, ale be alɔ̃ bu ɖee.

english_verse: and said, “I am disturbed by a dream that I don't understand, and I want you to explain it.”
translation_verse: Eye fia la gblɔ na wo bena: Meku drɔ̃e, eye drɔ̃e la gɔmesese na medzo haha.

english_verse: They answered in Aramaic, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever! We are your servants. Please tell us your dream, and we will explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Tete Kaldeatɔwo ƒo nu kple fia la ɖe Aram-gbe me bena; Fia la nenɔ agbe tegbee! Li ɖrɔ̃e la na wo dɔlawo, ekema míaɖe egɔme na wò.

english_verse: But the king replied, “No! I have made up my mind. If you don't tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be chopped to pieces and your houses will be torn down.
translation_verse: Fia la ɖo ŋu na Kaldeatɔwo gblɔ bena. Tame, si meɖo, enye si: Ne mieli drɔ̃e le eye mieɖe egɔme nam o la, ekema woafli mi kakɛkakɛ, eye miaƒe aƒewo azu aɖukpo.

english_verse: However, if you do tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be greatly rewarded and highly honored. Now tell me the dream and explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Ke ne mieli drɔ̃e la, eye mieɖe egɔme la, ekema miaxɔ nunana vovovowo kple bubu geɖe tso gbɔnye, eyata mili ɖrɔ̃e la, eye miɖe egɔme.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” they said, “if you will only tell us your dream, we will interpret it for you.”
translation_verse: Woɖo ŋu zi evelia gblɔ bena: Fia la neli ɖrɔ̃e la na eƒe ɖɔlawo, ekema míaɖe egɔme.

english_verse: because you know what's going to happen if you don't come up with the answer. You've decided to make up a bunch of lies, hoping I might change my mind. Now tell me the dream, and that will prove that you can interpret it.”
translation_verse: Ke ne mieli drɔ̃e la nam o la, ekema afiatsotso ɖeka koe le mia ŋu; elabena de mieɖo gbe ɖi, be miagblɔ alakpanyawo kple nya gbegblẽwo le ŋkunye me, vaseɖe esime ɣeyiɣi la nu nayi. Eyata mili drɔ̃e la nam, ekema madza sii be, miate ŋu aɖe egɔme hã nam.

english_verse: His advisors explained, “Your Majesty, you are demanding the impossible! No king, not even the most famous and powerful, has ever ordered his advisors, magicians, or wise men to do such a thing.
translation_verse: Kaldeatɔwo ɖo ŋu na fia la gblɔ bena: Amegbetɔa ɖeke mele anyigba dzi, si ate ŋu aɖe nusi fia di la gɔme o; eye fia gã sẽŋua ɖeke meli, si bia nusiawo tɔgbe tso dzotɔwo, bokɔnɔwo kple Kaldeatɔwo si me kpɔ o.

english_verse: It can't be done, except by the gods, and they don't live here on earth.”
translation_verse: Nusi dim fia le la sesẽ, eye amea ɖeke meli ale ŋu aɖe egɔme na fia la o, negbe mawuwo ko, amesiwo ƒe nɔƒe mele kodzogbeawo dome o.

english_verse: Arioch was the king's official in charge of putting the wise men to death. He was on his way to have it done, when Daniel very wisely went to him
translation_verse: Tete Daniel tsɔ nunya kple gɔmesese ƒo nu kple fia ŋu srafowo ƒe amegã Aryox, amesi ho be, yeawu Babel-nunyalawo la.

english_verse: and asked, “Why did the king give such cruel orders?” After Arioch explained what had happened,
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ na fia ƒe aʋafia Aryox bena: Nukatae fia la de se sesẽ sia ɖo? Tete Aryox to nye la na Daniel.

english_verse: Daniel rushed off and said to the king, “If you will just give me some time, I'll explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Eye Daniel yi fia la gbɔ ɖaɖe kuku nɛ be, woana azã ye, ne yeaɖe drɔ̃e la gɔme na fia la.

english_verse: Daniel returned home and told his three friends.
translation_verse: Emegbe Daniel yi aƒe me, eye wòto nya la na eƒe hatiwo Xananya, Misael kple Azarya;

english_verse: Then he said, “Pray that the God who rules from heaven will be merciful and explain this mystery, so that we and the others won't be put to death.”
translation_verse: ne woabia amenuveve le dziƒo ƒe Mawu la si le nya ɣaɣla sia la, ne womagawu Daniel kple eƒe hatiwo akpe ɖe Babel-nunyala mamleawo ŋu o.

english_verse: In a vision one night, Daniel was shown the dream and its meaning. Then he praised the God who rules from heaven:
translation_verse: Tete woɖe nya ɣaɣla la fia Daniel le ŋutega me le zã. Eye Daniel kafu dziƒo Mawu la.

english_verse: “Our God, your name will be praised forever and forever. You are all-powerful, and you know everything.
translation_verse: Eye Daniel xɔ edzi gblɔ bena; Woakafu Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ tso mavɔ me yi ɖe mavɔ me, elabena etɔe nye nunya kple ŋusẽ.

english_verse: You control human events— you give rulers their power and take it away, and you are the source of wisdom and knowledge.
translation_verse: Eyae ɖɔa li ɣeyiɣiwo kple azãgbewo, eɖea fiawo le zi dzi, eye wòɖoa fiawo zi dzi, enaa nunya nunyalawo kple sidzedze nugɔmeselawo;

english_verse: “You explain deep mysteries, because even the dark is light to you.
translation_verse: eɖea nusi me goglo, kple nu ɣaɣla fiana, enya nusi le viviti me, elabena kekeli le egbɔ.

english_verse: You are the God who was worshiped by my ancestors. Now I thank you and praise you for making me wise and telling me the king's dream, together with its meaning.” Daniel Interprets the Dream
translation_verse: Fofonyewo ƒe Mawu, meɖa akpe na wo, eye mekafu wo, be nẽna nunya kple ŋusẽm, eye néɖe nusi míebia wò la fiam; elabena fia ƒe nyae nèɖe fia mí!

english_verse: Daniel went back to Arioch, the official in charge of executing the wise men. Daniel said, “Don't kill those men! Take me to the king, and I will explain the meaning of his dream.”
translation_verse: Tete Daniel yi Aryox, amesi fia la ɖɔ, be wòawo Babel-nunyalawo la gbɔ, eye wògblɔ nɛ bena; Megawu Babel-nunyalawo o; ke hoŋ kplɔm yi fia la gbɔe, eye maɖe drɔ̃e la gɔme na fia la.

english_verse: Arioch rushed Daniel to the king and announced, “Your Majesty, I have found out that one of the men brought here from Judah can explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Eye Aryox kplɔ Daniel yi fia la gbɔ enumake hegblɔ nɛ bena; Mekpɔ ŋutsua ɖe le Yuda-viwo ƒe aboyomewo dome, amesi be, yeaɖe drɔ̃ea gɔme na fia.

english_verse: The king asked Daniel, “Can you tell me my dream and what it means?”
translation_verse: Fia la xɔ edzi gblɔ na Daniel, amesi ŋkɔ nye Beltsazar le, bena; Ate ŋu alĩ drɔ̃e, si meku la, eye naɖe egɔme nam vavãa?

english_verse: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, not even the smartest person in all the world can do what you are demanding.
translation_verse: Daniel do ŋn na fia la gblɔ bena; Nya ɣaɣla, si dim fia le la, nunyalawo, hokɔnɔwo, dzotɔwo kple dzinuvi me nyalawo mate ŋu aɖe egɔme na fia la o.

english_verse: But the God who rules from heaven can explain mysteries. And while you were sleeping, he showed you what will happen in the future.
translation_verse: Wò fia, èle tame bum le nusi gbɔna dzɔdzɔ ge le ɣeyiɣi siawo megbe la ŋu le wò aba dzi, eye amesi ɖea nya ɣaɣlawo ɖe go la, ɖe nusi gbɔna dzɔdzɔ ge la fia wò.

english_verse: However, you must realize that these mysteries weren't explained to me because I am smarter than everyone else. Instead, it was done so that you would understand what you have seen.
translation_verse: Ke nye la, menye esi nunya le asinye wu agbagbeawo katã ta, wode nya ɣaɣla sia fiam ɖo o, ke boŋ, be woaɖe egɔme na fia la, eye nadze si wò dzimesusuwo.

english_verse: Your Majesty, what you saw standing in front of you was a huge and terrifying statue, shining brightly.
translation_verse: Wò fia, éɖo ŋku anyi, eye nèkpɔ legba gãa ɖe; legba la lolo, eye eƒe dzodada teƒe mekɔ o, ele tsitrenu de ŋkuwò me, eye eƒe nɔnɔme dzi ŋɔ.

english_verse: Its head was made of gold, its chest and arms were silver, and from its waist down to its knees, it was bronze.
translation_verse: Legba sia ƒe la nye sika nyuitɔ, eƒe akɔta kple eƒe abɔwo nye klosalo, eye eƒe ƒodo kple ali nye akɔbli;

english_verse: From there to its ankles it was iron, and its feet were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: eƒe ata wo nye gɔyibɔ, eƒe afɔwo ƒe akpaa ɖewo nye gayibɔ, eye akpaa ɖewo nye tsu.

english_verse: As you watched, a stone was cut from a mountain—but not by human hands. The stone struck the feet, completely shattering the iron and clay.
translation_verse: Eye esi néle ekpɔm la, kpea ɖe, si menye ame ƒe asie ɖae o la, ge va dze legbɔ la ƒe afɔ, si nye gayibɔ kple tsu la dzi, eye wògbae guduguɖu.

english_verse: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed and blown away without a trace, like husks of wheat at threshing time. But the stone became a tremendous mountain that covered the entire earth.
translation_verse: Ale gayibɔ kple tsu, akɔbli, klosalo kple sika wogbã gudugudu, eye wozu abe tsro le lugbɔƒe le dzomeŋɔli ene, ya kplɔ wo dzoe, eye womegakpɔ wo teƒe o; ke kpe, si dze legbaa dzi la, zu to gãa de hexɔ anyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: That was the dream, and now I'll tell you what it means.
translation_verse: Drɔe la nye esia, Azɔ miaɖe egɔme na fia la.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you are the greatest of kings, and God has highly honored you with power
translation_verse: Wò fia, si nye etiɔwo ƒe fia, amesi dziƒo ƒe Mawu la tsɔ fiaɖuɖu, ŋusẽ, kamesesẽ kple bubu na,

english_verse: After you are gone, another kingdom will rule, but it won't be as strong. Then it will be followed by a kingdom of bronze that will rule the whole world.
translation_verse: Ke fiaɖuƒe bubu ava ɖe yowòme, si anɔ ʋee wu tɔwò; emegbe fiaɖuƒe etɔ̃lia ava, si nye akɔblitɔ, eye wòaɖu anyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: This fourth kingdom will be divided—it will be both strong and brittle, just as you saw that the feet and toes were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: Alesi afɔbideawo ƒe akpaa ɖewo nye gayibɔ, eye akpaa ɖewo nye tsu la: nenema fiaɖuƒe la ƒe akpaa ɖe asesẽ, eye akpaa ɖe masesẽ o.

english_verse: This kingdom will be the result of a marriage between kingdoms, but it will crumble, just as iron and clay don't stick together.
translation_verse: Eye alesi nèkpɔ gayibɔ kple tsu wotsaka la, nenema woatsaka kple amegbetɔwo ƒe ƒomeawo, ke womalé ɖe wo nɔewo ŋu o, abe alesi gayibɔ kple tsu menye tsakana o ene.

english_verse: During the time of those kings, the God who rules from heaven will set up an eternal kingdom that will never fall. It will be like the stone that was cut from the mountain, but not by human hands—the stone that crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. Your Majesty, in your dream the great God has told you what is going to happen, and you can trust this interpretation. Daniel Is Promoted
translation_verse: Elabena ékpɔ kpea ɖe, si ame ƒe asi meɖa o la, ge tso to dzi va gbã gayibɔ, akɔbli kple tsu, klosalo kple sika la. Mawu gã lae ɖe nusi gbɔna gbaɖegbe la fia fia la. Drɔ̃e la le eme, eye eƒe gɔmeɖeɖe le eteƒe.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar bowed low to the ground and worshiped Daniel. Then he gave orders for incense to be burned and a sacrifice of grain to be offered in honor of Daniel.
translation_verse: Tete fia Nehukadnezar tsyɔ mo anyi hede ta agu ɖe Daniel ŋku me, eye wòɖe se be, woasa va, eye woado dzudzɔ ʋeʋèe nɛ.

english_verse: The king said, “Now I know that your God is above all other gods and kings, because he gave you the power to explain this mystery.”
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ na Daniel bena; Nyateƒee, miaƒe Mawu la enye mawuwo dzi Mawu kple fiawo dzi Aƒetɔ kpakple nya ɣaɣlawo defiala; elabena èle ŋu ɖe nya ɣaɣla sia fia.

english_verse: The king then presented Daniel with a lot of gifts; he promoted him to governor of Babylon Province and put him in charge of the other wise men.
translation_verse: Eye fia la de bubu Daniel ŋu, eye wòtsɔ nunana gã geɖewo nɛ, etsɔe ɖo Babel-nyigba blibo la nu, eye wòtsɔe ɖo Babel-nunyalawo katã ƒe tatɔe.

english_verse: At Daniel's request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to high positions in Babylon Province, and he let Daniel stay on as a palace official.
translation_verse: Eye Daniel ɖe kuku na fia la wòtsɔ Babel-nyigba ƒe dziɖuɖudɔwo de asi na Sadrax, Mesax kple Abed-Nego. Ke Daniel ŋutɔ ya nɔ fiaƒe me.

english_verse: and the king's high officials, governors, and advisors all crowded around them. The men were not burned, their hair wasn't scorched, and their clothes didn't even smell like smoke.
translation_verse: Eye amegãwo, anyigba dzi nunɔlawo, aʋafiawo kple fia ƒe adaŋudelawo ƒo wo ɖokui nu ƒu, eye wode ŋku ɖe ŋutsuawo hekpɔ be, dzo mewɔ naneke ŋuli na wo o, eye woƒe taɖa mefiã o, naneke mewɔ woƒe awuwo o, eye dzo meʋẽ le wo ŋu o.

english_verse: and he commanded his governors, advisors, treasurers, judges, and his other officials to come from everywhere in his kingdom to the dedication of the statue.
translation_verse: Eye fia Nebukadnezar dɔ amewo ɖo ɖa, be woaɖaƒo amegãwo, anyigba dzi nunɔlawo, aʋafiawo, ʋɔnuɖrɔ̃lawo ƒe amegãwo, nudzikpɔlawo, sefialawo, ʋɔnuɖrɔ̃lawo kple anyigbawo ƒe dziɖuɖu dɔwɔlawo katã nu ƒu, ne woava akɔ legba, si fia Nebukadnezar li anyi la ŋu.

english_verse: Then an official stood up and announced: People of every nation and race, now listen to the king's command!
translation_verse: Eye gbeƒãɖela ɖo ɣli sesie bena: Mi dukɔwo, anyigba dzi dukɔwo kple gbegbɔgblɔwo, wole se dem na nu be:

english_verse: Trumpets, flutes, harps, and all other kinds of musical instruments will soon start playing. When you hear the music, you must bow down and worship the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
translation_verse: Ne miese kpẽwo, dzewo, ga kasaŋkuwo, kasaŋkuwo, saŋkuwo, venɔwo ƒe dzewo kpakple saŋku ƒomevi vovovowo ƒe ɖiɖi la, miadze klo ado gbe ɖa na sikalegba, si fia Nebukadnezar li anyi la!

english_verse: Anyone who refuses will at once be thrown into a flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Ke amesi medze klo do gbe ɖa o la, wotsɔe aƒu gbe ɖe kpo, si me dzo le bibim le la me enumake!

english_verse: As soon as the people heard the music, they bowed down and worshiped the gold statue that the king had set up.
translation_verse: Eyata esi dukɔwo katã, anyigbɔ dzi dukɔwo kple gbegbɔgblɔwo nya se kpẽwo, dzewo, ga kasaŋkuwo, kasaŋkuwo kple saŋkuwo kpakple saŋku ƒomevi vovovowo ƒe ɖiɖi ko la, wo katã wodze klo hedo gbe ɖa na sikalegba, si fia Nebukadnezar li anyi la.

english_verse: They said, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever!
translation_verse: Eye woxɔ edzi gblɔ na fia Nebukadnezar bena: Fia nenɔ agbe tegbee!

english_verse: And you said that anyone who did not bow down and worship it would be thrown into a flaming furnace.
translation_verse: ke amesi medze klo hedo gbe ɖa o la, woatsɔe aƒu gbe ɖe kpodzo, si le bibim la me.

english_verse: Sir, you appointed three men to high positions in Babylon Province, but they have disobeyed you. Those Jews, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, refuse to worship your gods and the statue you have set up.”
translation_verse: Yuda-ŋutsu, siwo netsɔ ɖo Babel-nyigba ƒe dziɖuɖu ɖɔ nu: Saɖrax, Mesax kple Abed-Nego la, fia ƒe se la metsɔ fu lã me na wo o, womesubɔ wò mawuwo o, eye womedo gbe ɖa na sikalegba, si nèli anyi la o.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar was furious. So he sent for the three young men and said,
translation_verse: Enumake Nehukadnezar ɖe se le dɔmedzoe kple dziku me be, woaɖakplɔ Sadrax, Mesax kple Abed-Nego vɛ; eye wokplɔ ŋutsu siawo vɛ na fia la.

english_verse: “I hear that you refuse to worship my gods and the gold statue I have set up.
translation_verse: Tete Nebukadnezar xɔ edzi gblɔ na wo bena: Saɖrax, Mesax kple Abeɖ-Nego, yavãe miegbe be, yewomasubɔ nye mawu, eye míado gbe ɖa na sikalegba, si meli anyi la oa?

english_verse: Now I am going to give you one more chance. If you bow down and worship the statue when you hear the music, everything will be all right. But if you don't, you will at once be thrown into a flaming furnace. No god can save you from me.”
translation_verse: Eyata miɖɔ ɖo! Ne miese kpẽwo, dzewo, ga kasaŋkuwo, seŋkuwo, venɔwo ƒe dzewo kple saŋku ƒomevi vovovowo ƒe ɖiɖi la, ekema miadze klo ado gbe ɖa na legba, si mewɔ la; ke ne mieɖo gbe ɖa nɛ o le ekema woatsɔ nu aƒu gbe ɖe kpodzo bibi la me enumake. Mawu kae ate ŋu aɖe mi tso asinye me?

english_verse: The three men replied, “Your Majesty, we don't need to defend ourselves.
translation_verse: Tete Sadrax, Mesax kple Abed-Nego woɖo ŋu gblɔ ne fia la bena: Nebukadnezar, nya sia ŋuɖoɖo meve mi o.

english_verse: But even if he doesn't, we still won't worship your gods and the gold statue you have set up.”
translation_verse: Ke ne menɔ alea o hã la, fia, nyae be, míele wò mawuwo subɔ ge akpɔ gbeɖe o, eye mlaɖo gbe ɖa na sikalegba, si nèli anyi la o.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar's face twisted with anger at the three men. And he ordered the furnace to be heated seven times hotter than usual.
translation_verse: Tete dzi ku Nehukadnezar vevie, eye eƒe mo trɔ ɖe Sadrax, Mesax kple Abed-Nego ŋu; eye wòde se be, woado dzo ɖe kpoa me zi gbɔ zi adre wu alesi wodoe tsã.

english_verse: Next, he commanded some of his strongest soldiers to tie up the men and throw them into the flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Eye wòɖe se na ŋutsu sesẽ, siwo le eƒe aʋakɔa me la be, woabla Sadrax, Mesax kple Abed-Nego atsɔ aƒu gbe ɖe kpodzo bibi la me.

english_verse: Suddenly the king jumped up and shouted, “Weren't only three men tied up and thrown into the fire?” “Yes, Your Majesty,” his officers answered.
translation_verse: Tete fia Nehukadnezar ƒe nu ku, eye wòtso zi ɖeka kplà gblɔ na eƒe adaŋudelawo bena: Ɖe menye ŋutsu etɔ̃e míebla tsɔ ƒu gbe de dzoa me oa? Woɖo ŋu gblɔ na fia la bena: Ẽ, fia!

english_verse: “But I see four men walking around in the fire,” the king replied. “None of them is tied up or harmed, and the fourth one looks like a god.”
translation_verse: Exɔ edzi gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, mele ŋutsu ene kpɔm, ka tu le wo ŋu, eye wole tsatsam le dzoa me, eye womexɔ abi o; enelia ƒe nɔnɔme le abe mawuwo vi la ene.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar went closer to the flaming furnace and said to the three young men, “You servants of the Most High God, come out at once!” They came out,
translation_verse: Tete Nehukadnezar te ɖe kpodzo bibi la ŋu hexɔ edzi gblɔ bena: Sadrax, Mesax kple Abed-Nego, mi dziƒoʋĩtɔ la viwo, mido va! Enumake Sadrax, Mesax kple Abed-Nego wodo tso dzoa me.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar said: Praise their God for sending an angel to rescue his servants! They trusted their God and refused to obey my commands. Yes, they chose to die rather than to worship or serve any god except their own.
translation_verse: Tete Nehukadnezar xɔ edzi gblɔ bena: Woakafu Sadrax, Mesax kple Abed-Nego ƒe Mawu la, amesi dɔ eƒe dɔla ɖa, be wòade eƒe subɔla, siwo ɖoa ŋu ɖe eŋu, wo amesiwo da fia ƒe nya dzi, eye wotsɔ wo ɖokui na, be yewomagasuhɔ mawu bubua ɖeke alo aɖo gbe ɖa nɛ akpe ɖe yewoƒe Mawu la ŋu o.

english_verse: And I won't allow people of any nation or race to say anything against their God. Anyone who does will be chopped up and their houses will be torn down, because no other god has such great power to save.
translation_verse: Eyata se, si dem mele, enye si: Ne amea ɖe gblɔ nya tovoa ɖe ɖe Sadrax, Mesax kple Abed-Nego ƒe Mawu ŋu le dukɔwo, anyigba dzi dukɔwo kple gbegbɔglɔwo katã dome la, woaflii kakɛkakɛ, eye eƒe eƒe azu aɖukpo; elabena mawu bubua ɖeke meli ate ŋu aɖe ame abe eya ene o.

english_verse: After this happened, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to even higher positions in Babylon Province.
translation_verse: Emegbe fia la na ame nyo na Sadrax, Mesax kple Abed-Nego le Babel-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar sent the following letter to the people of all nations and races on the earth: Greetings to all of you!
translation_verse: Nye Nehukadnezar menɔ aƒenye me bɔkɔɔ, eye meɖu agbe le nye fiasã me.

english_verse: I am glad to tell about the wonderful miracles God Most High has done for me.
translation_verse: Meku drɔ̃e, eye wòna medze haha, nye tamesusuwo le nye aba dzi kple nye ŋutegawo na dzidzi ƒom.

english_verse: His miracles are mighty and marvelous. He will rule forever, and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: Eye mede se be, woakplɔ Babel-nunyalawo katã vɛ nam, ne woaɖe drɔ̃e la gɔme nam.

english_verse: I was enjoying a time of peace and prosperity,
translation_verse: Tete dzotɔwo, bokɔnɔwo, Kaldeatɔwo kple gbesalawo va, eye meli drɔ̃e la na wo, ke womeɖe egɔme nam o.

english_verse: Then I commanded every wise man in Babylonia to appear in my court, so they could explain the meaning of my dream.
translation_verse: Wò Beltsazar, dzotɔwo ƒe tatɔ, wò amesi me mawu kɔkɔewo ƒe gbɔgbɔ le menye, eye nya ɣaɣlaa ɖeke mele vivi me de wo o, gblɔ nye ŋutega, si mekpɔ le drɔ̃e me la, eye naɖe egɔme.

english_verse: After they arrived, I told them my dream, but they were not able to say what it meant.
translation_verse: Ŋutega, si mekpɔ le nye aba dzi, enye si: Mede ŋku anyi, eye kpɔ da, atia de le anyigba titina, si kɔ ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Finally, a young man named Daniel came in, and I told him the dream. The holy gods had given him special powers, and I had renamed him Belteshazzar after my own god.
translation_verse: Ati la lolo, eye wòsesẽ, ekɔ ɖatɔ dziŋgɔli ke, eye wòvu vaseɖe anyigba blibo la ƒe mlɔenu.

english_verse: I said, “Belteshazzar, not only are you the wisest of all advisors and counselors, but the holy gods have given you special powers to solve the most difficult mysteries. So listen to what I dreamed and tell me what it means:
translation_verse: Eƒe aŋgbawe nyo, eƒe tsetsewo sɔ gbɔ, eye wonye nuɖuɖu ne nuwo katã; gbemelãwo nɔ eƒe vɔvɔli te, dziƒoxewo wɔ atɔ ɖe eƒe alɔwo me, eye wonye ŋutilãwo katã.

english_verse: In my sleep I saw a very tall tree in the center of the world.
translation_verse: Eye meɖo ŋku anyi le ŋutega, si mekpɔ le nye aba dzi la me, kpɔ ɖa, dzɔla kɔkɔea ɖe ɖi tso dziƒo

english_verse: It grew stronger and higher, until it reached to heaven and could be seen from anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: hedo ɣli sesĩe gblɔ bena: Milã ati la, eye mitso eƒe alɔwo, mido dzodzo eƒe aŋgbawo, eye mikaka eƒe tsetsewo hlẽ, minyiã gbemelãwo ɖa le ete kple dziƒoxewo ɖa le eƒe alɔwo me!

english_verse: It was covered with leaves and heavy with fruit— enough for all nations. Wild animals enjoyed its shade, birds nested in its branches, and all creatures on earth lived on its fruit.
translation_verse: Ke migblẽ eƒe takpoea ɖe to me, eye mide gayibɔ kple akɔbli kɔsɔkɔsɔe ɖe gbe dama me, dziƒo zãmu naƒo, eye eya kple gbemelãwo naɖu anyigba dzi gbe.

english_verse: “While I was in bed, having this vision, a holy angel came down from heaven
translation_verse: Woaɖe amegbetɔ ƒe dzi le eme ahatsɔ la ƒe dzi nɛ, vaseɖe esime azã adre nu nava yi nɛ.

english_verse: and shouted: ‘Chop down the tree and cut off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Make the animals leave its shade and send the birds flying from its branches.
translation_verse: Esia nyee dzɔlawo ƒe tameɖodo, eye kɔkɔetɔ la ƒe se enye nya sia, ne agbagbeawo nadze si be, dziƒoʋĩtɔ la kpɔ ŋusẽ ɖu amegbetɔwo ƒe fiaɖuƒewo dzi, amesi dze eŋu la, wòtsɔa wo nana, eye ate ŋu atsɔ ame tsɛwo ado wo nu.

english_verse: But leave its stump and roots in the ground, surrounded by grass and held by chains of iron and bronze. ‘Make sure that this ruler lives like the animals out in the open fields, unprotected from the dew.
translation_verse: Esia nye drɔ̃e, si nye fia Nebukadnezar meku; Beltsazar, ɖe egɔme nam, elabena nunyala, siwo katã le nye fiaɖuƒe me la, mete ŋu ɖe egɔme nam o; ke wò la ale ŋu aɖe egɔme, elabena mawu kɔkɔewo ƒe gbɔgbɔ le mewò.

english_verse: “Daniel, that was the dream that none of the wise men in my kingdom were able to understand. But I am sure that you will understand what it means, because the holy gods have given you some special powers.”
translation_verse: eƒe aŋgbawo nyo, eƒe tsetsewo sɔ gbɔ, eye wònye nuɖudu na nuwo katã, gbemelãwo nɔ ete, eye dziƒoxewo wɔ atɔ ɖe eƒe alɔwo me la,

english_verse: For a while, Daniel was terribly confused and worried by what he was thinking. But I said, “Don't be bothered either by the dream or by what it means.” Daniel replied: Your Majesty, I wish the dream had been against your enemies.
translation_verse: enye wò fia, amesi tri akɔ, eye ŋusẽ le ŋuwò, wò gãnyenye ɖatɔ dziŋgɔli, eye wò ŋusẽ ɖe anyigba ƒe mlɔenu ke.

english_verse: Its leaves were beautiful, and it produced enough fruit for all living creatures; animals lived in its shade, and birds nested in its branches.
translation_verse: fia, egɔmeɖeɖe enye si, eye dziƒoʋĩtɔ ƒe tameɖoɖo, si le nye aƒetɔ fia dzi va ge la, enye si:

english_verse: Then you saw a holy angel come down from heaven and say, “Chop down the tree and destroy it! But leave its stump and roots in the ground, fastened there by a chain of iron and bronze. Let it stay for seven years out in the field with the wild animals, unprotected from the dew.”
translation_verse: Eye esi wode se be, ati la ƒe takpoea nesusɔ la, eya nye be, wò fiaɖuƒe la atsi anyi na wò, ne nadze sii be, dziƒo si me ŋusẽ le.

english_verse: Your Majesty, please be willing to do what I say. Turn from your sins and start living right; have mercy on those who are mistreated. Then all will go well with you for a long time. The Rest of Nebuchadnezzar's Letter about His Second Dream
translation_verse: exɔ edzi gblɔ bena: Ɖe menye esia nye Babel ga, si metsɔ nye ŋusẽ triakɔ la tsoe, ne wòanye fia nɔƒe kple nye atsyɔ̃ ƒe bubu oa?

english_verse: About twelve months later, I was walking on the flat roof of my royal palace and admiring the beautiful city of Babylon, when these things started happening to me. I was saying to myself, “Just look at this wonderful capital city that I have built by my own power and for my own glory!”
translation_verse: Enumake nya la va me na Nehukadnezar; wonyãe ɖa le amegbetɔwo dome, eɖu gbe abe nyitsu ene, eye dziƒo zãmu ƒoe, vaseɖe esime eƒe ɖa to abe hɔ̃wo ƒe fu ene, eye eƒe fe to abe xewo tɔ ene.

english_verse: You will be forced to live with the wild animals, away from people. For seven years you will eat grass, as though you were an ox, until you learn that God Most High is in control of all earthly kingdoms and that he is the one who chooses their rulers.
translation_verse: Anyigbadzitɔwo katã meɖi naneke nɛ o, eye wòwɔa dziƒo ŋu nuwo kple anyigbadzitɔwo alesi dze eŋu, eye amea ɖeke meli alé eƒe asi agblɔ be, nuka nye esi wɔm nèle hã o.

english_verse: This was no sooner said than done—I was forced to live like a wild animal; I ate grass and was unprotected from the dew. As time went by, my hair grew longer than eagle feathers, and my fingernails looked like the claws of a bird.
translation_verse: Nye mo gakɔ le ɣemaɣi, eye nye fiaɖuƒe ƒe bubu, nye ŋutikɔkɔe kple nye atsyɔ̃ gasu asinye; nye adaŋuɖelawo kple nye amegãwo di yonyeme mɔ, wogatsɔm ɖo nye fiaɖuƒe la nu, eye nye gãnyenye sɔ gbɔ ɖe dzi.

english_verse: Finally, I prayed to God in heaven, and my mind was healed. Then I said: “I praise and honor God Most High. God lives forever, and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: Eyata nye Nehukadnezar makafu dziƒo fia la, made bubu eŋu, eye mada akpe nɛ; elabena eƒe nuwɔwɔwo katã le eteƒe, eƒe mɔwo dza, eye wòbɔbɔa dadalawo ɖe anyi.

english_verse: One evening, King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand of his highest officials, and he drank wine with them.
translation_verse: Fia Belsazar tu aglo gãa ɖe na eƒe amegã akpewo, eye wòno wein le ame akpeawo ŋku me.

english_verse: He got drunk and ordered his servants to bring in the gold and silver cups his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem. Belshazzar wanted the cups, so that he and all his wives and officials could drink from them.
translation_verse: Eye esi Belsazar mu aha la, eɖe se be, woaɖatsɔ sikanu kple klosalonu, siwo fofoa Nebukadnezar fɔ tso gbedoxɔ me le Yerusalem la va, ne fia la kple eƒe amegãwo, srɔ̃awo kple eƒe ahiãwo nano nu le wo me.

english_verse: When the gold cups were brought in, everyone at the banquet drank from them and praised their idols made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
translation_verse: Wono wein, eye wokafu mawu, siwo nye sika, klosalo, akɔbli, gayibɔ, ati kple kpe.

english_verse: Suddenly a human hand was seen writing on the plaster wall of the palace. The hand was just behind the lampstand, and the king could see it writing.
translation_verse: Enumake kasia amegbetɔ ƒe asibiɖe va ŋlɔ nu ɖe fiasã la ƒe gli, si wosi akalo na la ŋu le akaɖitia ŋgɔdze. Eye esi fia la kpɔ asi, si ŋlɔ nua la,

english_verse: He was so frightened that his face turned pale, his knees started shaking, and his legs became weak.
translation_verse: fia la ƒe mo fu tititi, eye eƒe tamesusuwo ɖo ŋɔdzi nɛ, eƒe ali me ka tso, eye eƒe klowo le wo nɔewo ƒom kpakpakpa.

english_verse: The king called in his advisors, who claimed they could talk with the spirits of the dead and understand the meanings found in the stars. He told them, “The man who can read this writing and tell me what it means will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. He will wear robes of royal purple and a gold chain around his neck.”
translation_verse: Tete fia la do ɣli sesĩe be, woayɔ bokɔnɔwo, Kaldeatɔwo kple dzotɔwo vɛ. Eye fia la xɔ edzi gblɔ na Babel-nunyalawo bena: Amesi axlẽ nuŋɔŋlɔ sia, eye wòaɖe egɔme nam la, woata aɖabɛ nɛ, woade sika kɔsɔkɔsɔ kɔ nɛ, eye wòanye etɔ̃lia aɖu dzi le nye fiaɖuƒe la me.

english_verse: All of King Belshazzar's highest officials came in, but not one of them could read the writing or tell what it meant,
translation_verse: Enumake fia ƒe nunyalawo katã va, ke womete ŋu xlẽ nuŋɔŋlɔ la, ne woahayi egɔme ɖe ge na fia la o.

english_verse: and they were completely puzzled. Now the king was more afraid than ever before, and his face turned white as a ghost.
translation_verse: Tete vɔvɔ ɖo fia Belsazar, eye eƒe mo fu tititi, eye dzidzi ƒo eƒe amegãwo.

english_verse: When the queen heard the king and his officials talking, she came in and said: Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! Don't be afraid or look so pale.
translation_verse: Eye fia dada yi aglotuƒe la le fia la kple eƒe amegãwo ƒe nya la ta. Tete fia dada xɔ edzi gblɔ bena: Fia nenɔ agbe tegbee! Wò tamesusuwo megaɖo ŋɔdzi na wò o, eye wò mo megafu tititi o!

english_verse: In your kingdom there is a man who has been given special powers by the holy gods. When your father Nebuchadnezzar was king, this man was known to be as smart, intelligent, and wise as the gods themselves. Your father put him in charge of all who claimed they could talk with the spirits or understand the meanings in the stars or tell about the future.
translation_verse: Ŋutsua ɖe le wò flaɖuƒe la me, amesi me mawu kɔkɔewo ƒe gbɔgbɔ le. Le fofowò ŋɔli la wokpɔ sidzedze gɔmesese kple nunya le esi abe mawuwo ƒe nunya ene, eye fofowò, fia Nebukadnezar, tsɔe ɖo dzotɔwo, bokɔnɔwo, Kaldeatɔwo kple gbesalawo ƒe tatɔe,

english_verse: He also changed the man's name from Daniel to Belteshazzar. Not only is he wise and intelligent, but he can explain dreams and riddles and solve difficult problems. Send for Daniel, and he will tell you what the writing means.
translation_verse: elabena gbɔgbɔ triakɔ, sidzedze kple nunya le esi, eye wòdea drɔ̃ewo, adzowo kple nya manyatanuwo gɔme; eyama nye Daniel, amesi fia la tsa ŋkɔ na be Beltsazar. Eyata woayɔ Daniel va, ekema aɖe egɔme.

english_verse: When Daniel was brought in, the king said: So you are Daniel, one of the captives my father brought back from Judah!
translation_verse: Tete wokplɔ Daniel vɛ na fia la. Eye fia la xɔ edzi gblɔ na Daniel bena: Wòe nye Daniel tso Yuda ƒe aboyovi, siwo fofonye fia kplɔ tso Yuda vɛ la domea?

english_verse: I was told that the gods have given you special powers and that you are intelligent and very wise.
translation_verse: Mese le ŋuwò be, mawuwo ƒe gbɔgbɔ le mewò, eye sidzedze, gɔmesese kple nunya triakɔ le asiwò wokpɔ.

english_verse: Neither my advisors nor the men who talk with the spirits of the dead could read this writing or tell me what it means.
translation_verse: Azɔ wokplɔ nunyalawo kple bokɔnɔwo vɛ nam, be woaxlẽ nuŋɔŋlɔ sia, eye woaɖe egɔme nam, ke womete ŋu de nu sia gɔme nam o.

english_verse: But I have been told that you understand everything and that you can solve difficult problems. Now then, if you can read this writing and tell me what it means, you will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. You will wear royal purple robes and have a gold chain around your neck.
translation_verse: Mese le ŋuwò be, èɖea nu gɔme, eye nèdea nya manyatanuwo gɔme. Ne ete bu xlẽ nuŋɔŋlɔ sia, eye nède egɔme nam la, àta aɖabɛ, àdo sika kɔsɔkɔsɔ ɖe kɔ, eye ànye etɔ̃lia aɖu dzi le nye fiaɖuƒe la me.

english_verse: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, I will read the writing and tell you what it means. But you may keep your gifts or give them to someone else.
translation_verse: Daniel ɖo ŋu gblɔ na fia la bena: Wò nunanawo nenɔ anyi na wò, eye natsɔ wo na ame bubu! Ke maxlẽ nuŋɔŋlɔ la na fia la, eye maɖe egɔme nɛ.

english_verse: Sir, the Most High God made your father a great and powerful man and brought him much honor and glory.
translation_verse: Fia, Mawu dziƒoʋĩtɔ tsa fiaɖuƒe, gãnyenye, bubu kple ŋutikɔkɔe na fofowò Nebukadnezar.

english_verse: God did such great things for him that people of all nations and races shook with fear. Your father had the power of life or death over everyone, and he could honor or ruin anyone he chose.
translation_verse: Vɔvɔ̃ do dukɔwo katã, anyigba dzi dukɔwo kple gbegbɔgblɔwo, eye wodzo nyanyanya le ŋusẽ, si wonae la ta; ne elɔ̃ la, ewua ame, ne elɔ̃ la, exɔa ame ɖe agbe; ne elɔ̃ la, edoa ame ɖe dzi, eye ne elɔ̃ la, ebɔbɔa ame de anyi.

english_verse: His mind became like that of an animal, and he was forced to stay away from people and live with wild donkeys. Your father ate grass like an ox, and he slept outside where his body was soaked with dew. He was forced to do this until he learned that the Most High God rules all kingdoms on earth and chooses their kings.
translation_verse: Wonyãe le amegbetɔwo dome, eye eƒe dzi zu abe la tɔ ene, enɔ gbetedziwo gbɔ, wona gbee wòɖu abe nyitsu ene, eye dziƒo zãmu ƒoe, vaseɖe esime wòdze sii be, Mawu dziƒoʋĩtɔ la kpo ŋusẽ ɖe amegbetɔwo ƒe fiaɖuƒewo dzi, eye amesi dze eŋu la, eyae wòtsɔnɛ na.

english_verse: King Belshazzar, you knew all of this, but you still refused to honor the Lord who rules from heaven.
translation_verse: Ke wò, via Belsazar, mèbɔbɔ wò dzi ɖe anyi o, evɔ wònye ènya nusiawo katã hafi.

english_verse: Instead, you turned against him and ordered the cups from his temple to be brought here, so that you and your wives and officials could drink wine from them. You praised idols made of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, even though they cannot see or hear or think. You refused to worship the God who gives you breath and controls everything you do.
translation_verse: Eɖo ɖokuiwò ɖe dzi ɖe dziƒo ƒe Aƒetɔ la ŋu, eye wofɔ eƒe aƒe me nuwo vɛ na wò, mia kple wò amegãwo, srɔ̃wòwo kple wò ahiãwo mieno wein le wo me, eye nèkafu mawu, siwo nye klosalo, sika, akɔbli, gayibɔ, ati kple kpe, siwo mekpɔa du o, womesea nu o, eye womedzea si nu o; ke Mawu, amesi si me wò agbe kple wò mɔwo katã le la, mede bubu eya ŋu o.

english_verse: That's why he sent the hand to write this message on the wall.
translation_verse: Eyata wòdɔ asi sia ɖa, wova ŋlɔ nusia ɖo.

english_verse: Belshazzar gave a command for Daniel to be made the third most powerful man in his kingdom and to be given a purple robe and a gold chain.
translation_verse: Tete Belsazar de se be, woata aɖahɛ na Daniel, woatsɔ sika kɔsɔkɔsɔ ade kɔ nɛ, eye woado kpo le eŋgɔ be, eyae nye dziɖula etɔ̃lia le fiaɖuƒe la me.

english_verse: That same night, the king was killed.
translation_verse: Zã ma me ke wowu Kaldeatɔwo ƒe fia Belsazar.

english_verse: In order to make sure that his government was run properly, Darius put three other officials in charge of the governors. One of these officials was Daniel.
translation_verse: Eye Dario kpɔ be, enye, ne yeaɖo amegã alafa ɖeka kple blave fiaɖuƒe la nu, amesiwo anɔ fiaɖuƒe blibo la me.

english_verse: And he did his work so much better than the other governors and officials that the king decided to let him govern the whole kingdom.
translation_verse: Eɖo tatɔ etɔ̃ wo nu, amesiwo dome Daniel le; woawoe amegãwo nabu akɔnta na, ne fia la magaŋe ɖe eme o.

english_verse: The other men tried to find something wrong with the way Daniel did his work for the king. But they could not accuse him of anything wrong, because he was honest and faithful and did everything he was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Eye Daniel ƒo tatɔawo kple amegãawo ta, elabena gbɔgbɔ triakɔ le eme; eye fia la ɖo be, yeatsɔe aɖo fiaɖuƒe blibo la nu.

english_verse: Finally, they said to one another, “We will never be able to bring any charge against Daniel, unless it has to do with his religion.”
translation_verse: Tete tatɔawo kple amegãawo di nya le Daniel ŋu le dziɖunya gome, ke womete ŋu kpɔ nya alo nu gbegblẽ wɔwɔa ɖeke o, elabena eɖi anukware, eye womekpɔ vototo alo nu gbegblẽ wɔwɔ le eŋu o.

english_verse: They all went to the king and said: “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever!
translation_verse: Eye ŋutsuawo gblɔ bena: Míele nyaa ɖeke kpɔ ge le Daniel sia ŋu o, negbe ɖe eƒe mawusubɔsubɔ ŋu ko.

english_verse: All of your officials, leaders, advisors, and governors agree that you should make a law forbidding anyone to pray to any god or human except you for the next
translation_verse: Tete tatɔwo kple amegãwo va fia la gbɔ bibibi, eye wogblɔ nɛ bena: Fia Dario nenɔ agbe tegbee!

english_verse: Order this to be written and then sign it, so it cannot be changed, just as no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed.”
translation_verse: Fiaɖuƒe la ƒe tatɔwokatã, anyigbanunɔlawo, amegãwo, aɖaŋudelawo kple dzikpɔlawo de adaŋu be, fia la naɖo ɖoɖo, eye wòade se sesẽa de be, amesiame, si abia nu mawu alo amegbelɔ bubua ɖe le ŋkeke blaetɔ̃ me, eye menye tso wò fia si ko o la, wotsɔe aƒu gbe ɖe dzatawo ƒe ɖo me.

english_verse: They went back to the king and said, “Didn't you make a law that forbids anyone to pray to any god or human except you for the next
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu mawo ge ɖe eme, eye wokpɔ Daniel wole gbe dom ɖa hele koko ƒom le eƒe Mawu ŋku me.

english_verse: The men then told the king, “That Jew named Daniel, who was brought here as a captive, refuses to obey you or the law that you ordered to be written. And he still prays to his god three times a day.”
translation_verse: Tete wova fia la gbɔ ƒo nu kplii le fia ƒe se la ŋu bena: Ɖe mèŋlɔ ŋkɔ ɖe sea te be, amesiame, si abia nu mawu alo amegbetɔ bubua ɖe le ŋkeke blaetɔ̃ me, eye menye tso wò fia si ko o la, woatsɔe aƒu gbe ɖe dzatawo ƒe ɖo me oa? Fia la ɖo ŋu gblɔ bena: Nya la le eme ɖe Mediatɔwo kple Persiatɔwo ƒe se, si metrɔna o la nu.

english_verse: The king was really upset to hear about this, and for the rest of the day he tried to think how he could save Daniel.
translation_verse: Emegbe woɖo ŋu gblɔ na fia la bena: Ke Daniel, amesi nye Yuda ƒe aboyoviawo dometɔ ɖeka la, meléa afɔ ɖe fia la kple se, si te wòŋlɔ ŋkɔ ɖo la ŋu o, eye wòdoa gbe ɖa gbe ɖeka zi etɔ̃.

english_verse: At sunset the men returned and said, “Your Majesty, remember that no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed, not even by the king.”
translation_verse: Esi fia la se nya sia la, evee ŋutɔ, eye wòɖo be, yeaɖe Daniel; edze agbagba, vaseɖe esime ɣe ɖo to be, yeaɖee.

english_verse: So Darius ordered Daniel to be brought out and thrown into a pit of lions. But he said to Daniel, “You have been faithful to your God, and I pray that he will rescue you.”
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu mawo va fia la gbɔ bibibi gblɔ na fia la bena: Fia, nyae be, se wònye na Mediatɔwo kple Persiatɔwo be, se sia se kple ɖoɖo sia ɖoɖo, si dzi fia ɖo kpee la, tɔtrɔ megale eŋu o.

english_verse: A stone was rolled over the pit, and it was sealed. Then Darius and his officials stamped the seal to show that no one should let Daniel out.
translation_verse: Tete fia la de se wokplɔ Daniel ɖaƒu gbe ɖe dzatawo ƒe do me. Eye fia la xɔ edzi gblɔ na Daniel bena: Wò Mawu, si nesubɔna atraɖi la, neɖe wò!

english_verse: All night long the king could not sleep. He did not eat anything, and he would not let anyone come in to entertain him.
translation_verse: Womli kpe va ɖo do la nu, eye fia la tsɔ eƒe ŋkɔsigɛ kple eƒe amegãwo ƒe ŋkɔsigɛ tre enu, be nya bubua ɖeke magadzɔ ɖe Daniel dzi o.

english_verse: At daybreak the king got up and ran to the pit.
translation_verse: Emegbe fia la yi eƒe fiasã me, eye wotsi nu dɔ, womekplɔ nyɔnu vɛ nɛ o, eye wòtsi zãdomadɔlɔ̃e.

english_verse: He was anxious and shouted, “Daniel, you were faithful and served your God. Was he able to save you from the lions?”
translation_verse: Eye fia la fɔ ŋdi kanya, esime agu dze, eye wòɖe abla yi dzatawo ƒe do la gbɔ.

english_verse: The king was relieved to hear Daniel's voice, and he gave orders for him to be taken out of the pit. Daniel's faith in his God had kept him from being harmed.
translation_verse: Nye Mawu dɔ eƒe dɔla ɖa wòde ga nu na dzatawo, be womewɔ nanekem o, elabena nyemeɖi fɔ le eŋku me o, eye nyemeɖi fɔ le wò fia ŋku me hã o.

english_verse: And the king ordered the men who had brought charges against Daniel to be thrown into the pit, together with their wives and children. But before they even reached the bottom, the lions ripped them to pieces.
translation_verse: Tete fia la kpɔ dzidzɔ ŋutɔ, eye wòɖe se be, woaɖe Daniel le do la me. Eye woɖe Daniel le ɖo la me, ke naneke mewɔe o, elabena eɖo ŋu ɖe eƒe Mawu la ŋu.

english_verse: King Darius then sent this message to all people of every nation and race in the world: “Greetings to all of you!
translation_verse: Eye fia la ɖe se be, woatsɔ ŋutsu, siwo tso Daniel nu, wo viwo kple wo srɔ̃wo aƒu gbe ɖe dzatawo ƒe do la me; ke womekpɔ ɖo do la gɔme hafi dzatawo tso wo xɔ, eye wogbã woƒe ƒuwo katã o.

english_verse: I command everyone in my kingdom to worship and honor the God of Daniel. He is the living God, the one who lives forever. His power and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: Emegbe fia Dario ŋlɔ agbalẽ ɖo ɖe dukɔwo katã, anyigba dzi dukɔwo kple gbegbɔgblɔ, siwo le anyigba blibo la dzi bena: Eme nenyo na mi!

english_verse: He rescues people and sets them free by working great miracles. Daniel's God has rescued him from the power of the lions.”
translation_verse: Nyee de se be, Daniel ƒe Mawu nadzi ŋɔ, eye woavɔ̃e le nye dziɖuɖu ƒe fiaɖuƒe blibo la me, elabena Mawu gbagbe wònye, eye wòli tegbee, eƒe fiaɖuƒe nu meyina o, eye eƒe dziɖuɖu li vaseɖe nuwuwu.

english_verse: All went well for Daniel while Darius was king, and even when Cyrus the Persian ruled.
translation_verse: Eɖea ame, eye wòxɔna na ame, ewɔa dzesiwo kple nukunuwo le dziƒo kple anyigba dzi, eyae nye amesi ɖe Daniel tso dzatawo si me.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: In the first year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had some dreams and visions while I was asleep one night, and I wrote them down. The four winds were stirring up the mighty sea,
translation_verse: Daniel xlẽe fia gblɔ bena: Mekpɔ le nye ŋutega me le zã me be, dziƒo ƒe ya eneawo lɔ atsiaƒu gã la ɖe nu.

english_verse: when suddenly four powerful beasts came out of the sea. Each beast was different.
translation_verse: Lã gã ene do tso atsiaƒu la me, eye woto vovo tso wo nɔewo gbɔ.

english_verse: The first was like a lion with the wings of an eagle. As I watched, its wings were pulled off. Then it was lifted to an upright position and made to stand on two feet, just like a human, and it was given a human mind.
translation_verse: Gbãtɔ ɖi dzata, eye wòto aʋala abe hɔ̃ ene; meɖe ŋku ɖee, vaseɖe esime wotu aʋala te eŋu, eye wokɔe dzi tso anyigba hetsɔe ɖo afɔ dzi abe amegbetɔ ene, eye wona ame ƒe dzii.

english_verse: The second beast looked like a bear standing on its hind legs. It held three ribs in its teeth, and it was told, “Attack! Eat all the flesh you want.”
translation_verse: Lã evelia ɖi sisiblisi, eye wotsɔe ɖo go ɖeka me; agbaƒuti etɔ̃ le nu me nɛ le eƒe aɖuwo dome, eye wogblɔ nɛ bena. Tso naɖu lã geɖe!

english_verse: The third beast was like a leopard—except that it had four wings and four heads. It was given authority to rule.
translation_verse: Eyome meɖo ŋku anyi hekpɔ lã bubu wòɖi lãkle, eye wòto aʋala ene ɖe mẽdome abe xevi ene; lã la to ta ene, eye wona ŋusẽe.

english_verse: The fourth beast was stronger and more terrifying than the others. Its huge teeth were made of iron, and what it didn't grind with its teeth, it smashed with its feet. It was different from the others, and it had horns on its head—ten of them.
translation_verse: Emegbe mekpɔ lã enelia le ŋutega me le zã, ŋɔdzi kple vɔvɔ̃ le eŋu, eye wòsesẽ ŋutɔ, eto gaɖu kakowo, eɖu nu gbã nu, eye wòtanya mamlea kple afɔ, eto vovo tso lã, siwo katã do ŋgɔ nɛ la gbɔ, eye wòto dzo ewo.

english_verse: Just as I was thinking about these horns, a smaller horn appeared, and three of the other horns were pulled up by the roots to make room for it. This horn had the eyes of a human and a mouth that spoke with great arrogance. Judgment Daniel wrote:
translation_verse: Meɖe ŋku ɖe dzoawo, eye kpɔ ɖa, dzo suea ɖe to ɖe wo domee, dzo sia to ŋku abe amegbetɔ ƒe ŋku ene, eye nu, si gblɔa nya gãwo la, li nɛ; eye wotu eƒe dzo gbãtɔwo dometɔ etɔ̃.

english_verse: Thrones were set up while I was watching, and the Eternal God took his place. His clothing and his hair were white as snow. His throne was a blazing fire with fiery wheels,
translation_verse: Meɖe ŋku ɖee, vaseɖe esime wotsɔ fiazikpui li anyi eye amegã ɖeɖia ɖe bɔbɔ nɔ edzi, eƒe avɔ fu tititi, eye eƒe taɖa le abe ɖetifu, si me dza la ene, eƒe fiazikpui la nye dzoƒaɖe, eye tasiaɖamfɔ, siwo le eŋu la, nye dzobibi.

english_verse: and flames were dashing out from all around him. Countless thousands were standing there to serve him. The time of judgment began, and the books were opened.
translation_verse: Dzotɔsisi tso egbɔ gbagba ɖi bababa; ame akpe teƒe akpe le esubɔm, eye eme akpe ewo teƒe akpe ewo tsi tre ɖe egbɔ; woɖi ʋɔnu, eye woke agbalẽwo.

english_verse: I watched closely to see what would happen to this smaller horn because of the arrogant things it was saying. Then before my very eyes, the fourth beast was killed and its body destroyed by fire.
translation_verse: Meɖo ŋku anyi le nu kpɔm le nya gãgã, siwo gblɔm lãdzoa le la ta; mede ŋku ɖee, vaseɖe esime wowu lã la, wogblẽ eƒe kukua, eye wotɔ dzoe.

english_verse: The other three beasts had their authority taken from them, but they were allowed to live a while longer.
translation_verse: Woxɔ ŋusẽ le lã mamleawo hã si, eye woɖo agbenɔɣi na wo vaseɖe ɣeyiɣi kple gaƒoƒo dzi.

english_verse: As I continued to watch the vision that night, I saw what looked like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven, and he was presented to the Eternal God.
translation_verse: Meɖo ŋku anyi le ŋutega me le zã, kpɔ ɖa, nane zɔ kple alilikpowo le abe amegbetɔ ene heva ke ɖe amegã ɖeɖi la gbɔ, eye wokplɔe yi egbɔe.

english_verse: He was crowned king and given power and glory, so that all people of every nation and race would serve him. He will rule forever, and his kingdom is eternal, never to be destroyed. The Meaning of Daniel's Vision
translation_verse: Wotsɔ ŋusẽ, bubu kple dziɖuɖu nɛ, eye dukɔwo katã, anyigba dzi dukɔwo kple gbegbɔgblɔwo subɔe; eƒe dziɖuɖu li tegbee, eye enu mayi o, eye eƒe fiaɖuƒe magbã o.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: I was terrified by these visions, and I didn't know what to think.
translation_verse: Nye Daniel, nye gbɔgbɔ tsi dzi le menye, eye ŋutega, si mekpɔ la, do ŋɔdzi nam.

english_verse: “The four beasts are four earthly kingdoms.
translation_verse: Lã gã eneawo nye fia ene, siwo le anyigba dzi va ge.

english_verse: But God Most High will give his kingdom to his chosen ones, and it will be theirs forever and ever.”
translation_verse: Fiaɖuƒe la asu dziƒoʋĩtɔ la ƒe ame kɔkɔewo si, eye fiaɖuƒe la anɔ wo si me ɖaa tegbetegbe.

english_verse: I wanted to know more about the fourth beast, because it was so different and much more terrifying than the others. What was the meaning of its iron teeth and bronze claws and of its feet that smashed what the teeth and claws had not ground and crushed?
translation_verse: Emegbe mebia nyee tsitoo le lã enelia, si to vovo tso bubuawo katã gbɔ, ŋɔdzi kple vɔvɔ le eŋu, eƒe aɖuwo nye gayibɔ, eye eƒe fewo nye akɔbli, eɖu nu gbã nu hefãnya mamlea kple afɔ;

english_verse: I also wanted to know more about all ten of those horns on its head. I especially wanted to know more about the one that took the place of three of the others—the horn that had eyes and spoke with arrogance and seemed greater than the others.
translation_verse: dzo ewo, siwo le eta, eye wo ame etɔ̃ tu le wo ŋu, kple dzo bubu, si to, eye ŋkuwo le eŋu, eto nu, si gblɔa nya gãgãwo, eye wòlolo wu bubuawo la ŋu.

english_verse: While I was looking, this horn attacked God's chosen ones and was winning the battle.
translation_verse: Maɖo ŋku anyi kpɔ be, dzo keme awɔ aʋa kple ame kɔkɔewo, eye wòɖu wo dzi.

english_verse: Then God Most High, the Eternal God, came and judged in favor of his chosen ones, because the time had arrived for them to be given the kingdom.
translation_verse: Mlɔeba la amegã ɖeɖi la va, eye wòtso afia na dziƒoʋĩtɔ la ƒe ame kɔkɔeawo, eye azã ɖe be, ame kɔkɔeawo naxɔ fiaɖuƒe la.

english_verse: Then I was told by the one standing there: “The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom to appear on earth. It will be different from all the others— it will trample the earth and crush it to pieces.
translation_verse: Ale wògblɔ esi: Lã enelia le fiaɖuƒe enelia nye ge le anyigba dzi, eye wòato vovo tso fiaɖuƒewo katã gbɔ, aɖu anyigba blibo la, eye wòafanyae ahagbãe gudugudu.

english_verse: All ten of those horns are kings who will come from this kingdom, and one more will follow. This horn will be different from the others, and it will conquer three other kings.
translation_verse: Dzo ewoawo gɔme enye si: Fia ewo adzɔ le fiaɖuƒe ma me, eye bubu adzɔ ɖe wo yome ato vovo atso gbãtɔwo gbɔ, eye wòabɔbɔ fia etɔ̃ ɖe anyi.

english_verse: “This king will speak evil of God Most High, and he will be cruel to God's chosen ones. He will try to change God's Law and the sacred seasons. And he will be able to do this for a time, two times, and half a time.
translation_verse: Agblɔ nya tovowo ɖe dziƒoʋĩtɔ la ŋu, eye wòatsrɔ̃ dziƒoʋĩtɔ la ƒe ame kɔkɔewo; aɖo ɖe ta me be, yeatrɔ ɣeyiɣiwo kple sewo, eye woatsɔ wo aɖe asi nɛ ɣeyiɣi ɖeka kple ɣeyiɣi eve kpakple ɣeyiɣi afã.

english_verse: But he will finally be judged, and his kingdom completely destroyed.
translation_verse: Eye woaɖi ʋɔnu axɔ dziɖuɖu la le esi, eye woagblẽe ahatsrɔ̃e gbiɖigbiɖi.

english_verse: “Then the greatest kingdom of all will be given to the chosen ones of God Most High. His kingdom will be eternal, and all others will serve and obey him.”
translation_verse: Woatsɔ fiaɖuƒe la, dziɖuɖu kple fiaɖuƒewo ƒe ŋusẽ le dziƒo blibo la te ana dziƒoʋĩtɔ la ƒe ame kɔkɔewo ƒe dukɔ: eƒe fiaɖuƒe anye fiaɖuƒe mavɔ, eye dziɖulawo katã àsubɔe ahaɖo toe.

english_verse: That was what I saw and heard. I turned pale with fear and kept it all to myself.
translation_verse: Nyaawo seƒe enye si. Ke nye Daniel, nye tamesusuwo do ŋɔdzi nam, eye nye mo fu tititi; eye medzra nyaawo ɖo ɖe nye dzi me.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: In the third year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had a second vision
translation_verse: Le fia Belsazar ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒe etɔ̃lia me la nye Daniel mekpɔ ŋutega, abe esi mekpɔ tsa ene.

english_verse: when I looked up and saw a ram standing there with two horns on its head—both of them were long, but the second one was longer than the first.
translation_verse: Eye mefɔ kɔ dzi kpɔ agboa ɖe le tɔsisi la to, si to dzo legbee eve, ke ɖeka didi wu nɔvia, eye legbeetɔ enye mamletɔ, si to.

english_verse: The ram went charging toward the west, the north, and the south. No other animals were strong enough to oppose him, and nothing could save them from his power. So he did as he pleased and became even more powerful.
translation_verse: Mekpɔ agbo la wòle dzo dam ɖo ta ɣetoɖoƒe, anyiehe kple dziehe gome, eye lãa ɖeke menɔ te ɖe enu o, amea ɖeke mete ŋu xɔ ame le esi me o, ewɔ alesi dze eŋu, eye wòkpɔ ŋusẽ eteƒe mekɔ o.

english_verse: I kept on watching and saw a goat come from the west and charge across the entire earth, without even touching the ground. Between his eyes was a powerful horn,
translation_verse: Esi meɖo ŋku anyi la, gbɔisua ɖe tso ɣetoɖoƒe gome va anyigba blibo la dzi, eƒe afɔ mele anyi kam o, eye gbɔ̃tsu la to dzo sesẽa ɖe ɖe ŋugbladome.

english_verse: and with tremendous anger the goat started toward the ram that I had seen beside the river.
translation_verse: Eva agbo dzoevee, si mekpɔ wòtsi tre ɖe tɔsisia to la gbɔ, eye wòlũ ɖe edzi kple ŋusẽ le dziku me.

english_verse: The goat was so fierce that its attack broke both horns of the ram, leaving him powerless. Then the goat trampled on the ram, and no one could do anything to help.
translation_verse: Mekpɔe wòɖo agbo la gbɔ, dzi kui ɖe eŋu, eye wòtu dzo agbo la heŋe eƒe dzo eveawo, eye ŋusẽ mele agbo la ŋu, ne wòanɔ te ɖe enu o; etutui ƒu anyi henyã avuzi le edzi, eye amea ɖeke mexɔ agbo la le esi me o.

english_verse: After this, the goat became even more powerful. But at the peak of his power, his mighty horn was broken, and four other mighty horns took its place—one pointing to the north and one to the east, one to the south and one to the west.
translation_verse: Gbɔ̃tsu la kpɔ ŋusẽ eteƒe mekɔ o; eye esi ŋusẽ ɖo eŋu la, dzo gã la ŋe, eye dzo kako ene to de eteƒe ɖo ta dziƒo ƒe ya eneawo dzi.

english_verse: A little horn came from one of these, and its power reached to the south, the east, and even to the holy land.
translation_verse: Dzo suea ɖe to tso wo dometɔ ɖeka me, eye wòlolo ŋutɔ ɖo la dziehe kple ɣedzeƒe gome kpakple anyigba nyo la gbɔ.

english_verse: It became so strong that it attacked the stars in the sky, which were heaven's army. Then it threw some of them down to the earth and trampled on them.
translation_verse: Edo eɖokui ɖe dzi ɖe dziƒo ŋu nuwo ŋuti, eye wòdudu dziƒo ŋu nua ɖewo kple dzinuviwo ƒo ɖe anyi henyã avuzi lewo dzi.

english_verse: Then one of the holy angels asked another, “When will the daily sacrifices be offered again? What about this horrible rebellion? When will the temple and heaven's army no longer be trampled in the dust?”
translation_verse: Eye mese ame kɔkɔea ɖe le nu ƒom; ame kɔkɔe la bia amea ɖe gblɔ bena: Ɣekaɣle gbesiagbe vɔsa kple nugblẽla ƒe nu vɔ̃di wɔwɔ, si va me le ŋutega me, be wotsɔ kɔkɔeƒe la kple aʋakɔwo na wofanya la, ava se ɖo?

english_verse: Daniel wrote: I was trying to figure out the meaning of the vision, when someone suddenly appeared there beside me.
translation_verse: Esi nye Daniel mekpɔ ŋutega sia la, medi be, mase egɔme, eye kpɔ ɖa, amea ɖe le tsitre ɖe ŋgɔnye le abe ŋutsu ene.

english_verse: And from beside the Ulai River, a voice like that of a human said, “Gabriel, help him understand the vision.”
translation_verse: Eye mese amegbetɔ ƒe gbe le Ulai titina wògblɔ bena: Gabriel, ɖe ŋutega la gɔme na ame sia!

english_verse: Gabriel came over, and I fell to the ground in fear. Then he said, “You are merely a human, but you need to understand that this vision is about the end of time.”
translation_verse: Eva afisi metsi tre ɖo, eye esi wova la, dzidzi ƒom metsyɔ mo anyi. Tete wògblɔ nam bena: Amevi, ƒu to anyi, ŋutega sia la, nuwuɣi ŋu wòle ɖo.

english_verse: While he was speaking, I fell facedown in a deep sleep. But he lifted me to my feet
translation_verse: Eye esi wole nu ƒom kplim la, ŋuzi tsɔm metsyɔ mo anyi. Tete wòka asi ŋunye hefɔm ɖe tsitrenu ɖe nɔnyeƒe.

english_verse: and said: Listen, and I will tell you what will happen at the end of time, when God has chosen to show his anger.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nam be: Kpɔ ɖa, maɖe nusi le dzɔdzɔ ge, ne dɔmedzoe wu enu la, afia wò; elabena nuwuɣi ŋu wòle ɖo.

english_verse: The two horns of the ram are the kings of Media and Persia,
translation_verse: Agbo dzoevee, si nèkpɔ la, enye Media-kple Persia-fiawo.

english_verse: the goat is the kingdom of Greece, and the powerful horn between his eyes is the first of its kings.
translation_verse: Gbɔ̃tsu la nye Hela-nyigba ƒe fia, eye dzo ga, si le ŋugbladome nɛ la, enye fia gbãtɔ.

english_verse: After this horn is broken, four other kingdoms will appear, but they won't be as strong.
translation_verse: Eye esi dzo ene to ɖe ŋeŋea teƒe la, egɔme enye; Fiaɖuƒe ene atso dukɔ la me, ke womasesẽ aɖe eya nu o.

english_verse: When these rulers have become as evil as possible, their power will end, and then a king who is dangerous and cannot be trusted will appear.
translation_verse: Ne woƒe dziɖuɖu wu nu, eye nu vlo wɔwɔwo nu flɔ la, fia vlo, si dze aɖaŋu la, ado.

english_verse: He will gain strength, but not on his own, and he will cause terrible destruction. He will wipe out powerful leaders and God's people as well.
translation_verse: Ŋusẽ anɔ eŋu, ke menye to eya ŋutɔ ƒe ŋusẽ me o, agblẽ nu eteƒe makɔ o, eye eƒe nuwɔwɔ adze edzi nɛ, eye wòatsrɔ ame geɖewo kple ame kɔkɔewo ƒe dukɔ la.

english_verse: His deceitful lies will make him so successful, that he will think he is really great. Suddenly he will kill many people, and he will even attack God, the Supreme Ruler. But God will crush him!
translation_verse: Eƒe asi ana alakpadada nadze edzi nɛ le eƒe ayedzedze ta, aɖo eɖokui ɖe dzi le dzi me, eye wòatsrɔ̃ ame geɖewo le vo me; aɖo eɖo kui ɖe dzi ɖe aƒetɔwo ƒe Aƒetɔ la ŋu, ke woagbãe gudugudu, ame ƒe asi manɔmee.

english_verse: This vision about the evenings and mornings is true, but these things won't happen for a long time, so don't tell it to others.
translation_verse: Fiẽ kple ŋdi ƒe ŋutega, si ŋu woƒo nu le na wò la, nyateƒee; dzra ŋutega la ɖo ɖe ta me, elabena eteƒe le didi ge.

english_verse: After this, I was so worn out and weak that it was several days before I could get out of bed and go about my duties for the king. I was disturbed by this vision that made no sense to me.
translation_verse: Nu le nye Daniel ŋu, eye melé dɔ ŋkekea ɖewo; emegbe mefɔ hewɔ fia ƒe dɔwo; eye esi ŋutega la ɖe ga nu nam la, amea ɖeke medze sii o.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: Some years later, Darius the Mede, who was the son of Xerxes, had become king of Babylonia. And during his first year as king, I found out from studying the writings of the prophets that the Lord had said to Jeremiah, “Jerusalem will lie in ruins for
translation_verse: le eƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒe gbãtɔ me la nye Daniel melé ŋku ɖe agbalẽwo me ɖe ƒe, siwo ŋu Yehowa ƒe gbe va na nyagblɔɖila Yeremya ɖo be, woanye ƒe blaadre ayi ɖe Yerusalem ƒe aƒedo ŋu la ƒe xexlẽme ŋu.
