translation_verse: amesi mekpɔ bena, wole enu tsom le woƒe se la ƒe anukutsyɔtsyɔwo ŋuti; gake nutsotsoa ɖeke mele eŋu, si dze ku alo bablawo o.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: Ke esi wova fi tofi nam bena, Yudatɔwo le xa de ge ɖe ŋutsua ŋuti la, meɖoe ɖe gbɔwò le gaƒoƒo ma ke dzi, eye mede se na enutsolawo hã bena, woava gblɔ nusiwo wokpɔ le eŋuti la le gbɔwò. Nɔ anyi sesĩe!

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Tete asrafoawo kplɔ Paulo yi Amipatre le zã me, sigbe alesi wòde se na wo la ene.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: Eye esi ŋu ke la, wona sɔtɔwo yi kpakple eye afɔtɔwo gbugbɔ va mɔ̃ la me,

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: eye esi woawo va Kaisarea la, wotsɔ agbalẽ la na mɔ̃mefia la, eye wotsɔ Paulo hã de esi;

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: eye esi woxlẽe la, ebia bena, dziɖuƒe ka me wòtsoa? Eye esi wose bena, etso Kilikia la, egblɔ bena:

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: Mabia wò numegbe ase nyuie, ne nuwòtsolawo hã va. Eye wòde se be, woakpe edzi le Herodes ƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe la me.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
translation_verse: Eye ŋkeke atɔ̃ megbe la nunɔlagã Anania kple amegãa ɖewo kpakple nyanuɖela Tertulo, va afima, eye woawo ƒo nu na mɔ̃mefia la ɖe Paulo ŋuti.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: Gake bena nyemagasika wò ɖi akpa o la, meɖe kuku na wò, naɖo to mí ʋee le wò dɔmefafa la nu.

english_verse: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
translation_verse: Elabena miekpɔ ŋutsu sia bena, enye dɔvɔ̃ kple amesi ɖea zi Yudatɔwo katã dome le xexeame godoo, eye wònye Nazaretɔwo ƒe kɔmamã ƒe amegã,

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: Eye wòde se na enutsolawo bena, woava gbɔwò. Azɔ, ne èdrɔ̃ ʋɔnui la, wò ŋutɔ ate ŋu ase nu siwo ŋuti míele enu tsom ɖo la tso eya ŋutɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Eye Yudatɔwo hã de edzi, eye woka ɖe edzi bena, nusiawo le eme nenema.

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Eye esi mɔ̃mefia la mia asii bena, wòaƒo nu la, Paulo ɖo ŋu bena: Esi menyae bena, ƒe geɖee nye esi nènye ʋɔnudrɔ̃la na dukɔ sia la, dzi le ƒonye be, ma ɖe ɖokuinye nu;

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: elabena wò hã ate ŋu àse bena, mewu ŋkeke wuieve o, esime meyi ɖe Yerusalem subɔsubɔ ge;

english_verse: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
translation_verse: eye womekpɔm hã mele dze ɖom kple amea ɖe le gbedoxɔ me alo mede zi ameawo me le ƒuƒoƒeawo alo dua me hã kpɔ o.

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: Eye womate ŋu afia kpɔɖeŋu hã le nusi wotsɔ le nunye tsom la ŋu o.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Ke mele esia me ʋum na wò bena, mele mía fofowo ƒe Mawu la subɔm le mo, si woyɔna be kɔmamã la nu, ale bena mexɔ nusiwo katã woŋlɔ ɖe se la kple nyagblɔɖilawo me la dzi se,

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: eye mɔkpɔkpɔ, si le asinye na Mawu la, le woa ŋutɔwo hã si bena, tsitretsitsi li na ame dzɔdzɔewo kple ame madzɔmadzɔwo siaa.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Le esia me nye hã meɖoa vevie, bena dzitsinya, si ŋu abia ɖeke mele o la, nanɔ asinye ɖaa le Mawu kple amewo ŋku me.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Azɔ le ƒe geɖe megbe la meva be, matsɔ nunanawo na nye dukɔ la, eye masa vɔ.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: Le eya me wokpɔm le gbedoxɔ la me, mele ŋutinye kɔm, menye kple ameha alo kple hoowɔwɔa ɖeke o; woawo nye Yudatɔa ɖewo tso Asia,

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: amesiwo wòdze be, woava ŋkuwò me hafi, bena ne nyaa ɖe le wo si ɖe ŋutinye la, ne woatso nunye.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Alo na amesiawo ŋutɔ nagblɔ nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔ, si ke wokpɔ le ŋunye, esime mele tsitre ɖe ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ƒe ŋku me;

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: negbe nya ɖeka sia koe meɖo ɣli gblɔ, esime mele tsitre le wo dome bena; ame kukuwo ƒe tsitretsitsi ŋuti miele ʋɔnu drɔ̃mem egbe sia ɖoa?

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Ke Felike, esi wonyã nu le mɔ sia ŋuti kɔte la, ehe woƒe nya ɖe megbe hegblɔ bena: Ne aʋafia gã Lisia va la, mabia miaƒe nya la gɔme ase.

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: Eye wòde se na aʋafia la bena, Paulo nanɔ eƒe dzikpɔkpɔ te, eye wòana woagbɔ ɖe eme, eye megaxe mɔ na etɔwo dometɔa ɖeke be, megasubɔe o.

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Ke ŋkekea ɖewo megbe la Felike kple srɔ̃a Drusila, si nye Yudatɔ la, wova, eye wodɔ woyi ɖayɔ Paulo vɛ, eye wose Kristo Yesu dzixɔse nya tso egbɔ.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Ke esi wòle dzɔdzɔenyenye kple ɖokuidziɖuɖu nyui kpakple ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃, si le vava ge la, ŋutinya gblɔm la, dzidzi ƒo Felike, eye wòɖo ŋu bena: Azɔ la heyi egbɔ: ne mekpɔ asinu nyui la, mana woayɔ wò vɛ.

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: Eye wòle mɔ hã kpɔm bena, Paulo ana ga ye: eyaŋuti wòdɔna woɖayɔnɛ vɛ edziedzi, eye woɖoa dze kplii.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Ke le ƒe eve megbe la Porkio Festo va nɔ Felike teƒe; eye esi Felike le didim be, yeave Yudatɔwo nu la, egblẽ Paulo ɖe ga me.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi Festo va dziɖuƒea la, etso Kaisarea yi Yerusalem le ŋkeke etɔ̃ megbe.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Tete nunɔlagãwo kple Yudatɔwo ƒe amegãwo va do ɖe eƒe ŋku me ɖe Paulo ŋuti, eye woɖe kuku nɛ

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: hebia amenuveve tso egbɔ bena, wòana woakplɔe ava Yerusalem, elabena wole xa me be, yewoawui le mɔ dzi.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Ke Festo ɖo ŋu bena, woadzra Paulo ɖo ɖe Kaisarea, eye bena eya ŋutɔ gale afima yi ge kpuie.

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ bena: Eyata mia dome amesiwo ate ŋui la, nayi kplim, eye ne vodadaa ɖe le ŋutsu la ŋu la, ne woatso enu.

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Eye esi wònɔ wo dome mewu ŋkeke enyi alo ewo o la, edzo yi Kaisarea, eye esi ŋu ke la, ebɔbɔ nɔ ʋɔnudrɔ̃zikpui la dzi, eye wòde se bena, woakplɔ Paulo vɛ.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Eye esi wòva la, Yudatɔ, siwo tso Yerusalem va la, le tsitre ƒo xlãe, eye wotsɔ nutsotso vevi geɖewo vɛ ɖe Paulo ŋuti, esiwo ŋu womete ŋu fia kpɔɖeŋua ɖeke le o,

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: elabena Paulo ɖe eɖokui nu gblɔ bena: Nyemewɔ nuvɔ̃a ɖeke ɖe Yudatɔwo ƒe se la alo ɖe gbeɖoxɔ la alo ɖe kaisaro ŋu o.

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Ke esi Festo le didim bena, yeave Yudatɔwo nu la, exɔ dzi na Paulo gblɔ bena: Elɔ̃ bena, nayi Yerusalem, ne woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wò le afima le nusiawo ŋuti le ŋkunye me mahã?

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Ke Paulo gblɔ bena: Kaisaro ƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃zikpui la ŋgɔe nye esi mele tsitre ɖo, afisi wòle be, woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnum le; nyemewɔ vɔ̃a ɖeke Yudatɔwo o, abe alesi wò ŋuta hã nenyae nyuie ene.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: Ne tɔnye medzɔ o, eye mewo nane, si dze ku la, nyemegbe ku o; ke ne nusiwo amesiawo tsɔ le nunye tsom la, ƒe ɖeke mele eme o la, amea ɖeke mate ŋu atsɔm ade asi na wo o. Kaisaro si me metsɔ nye nya dee!

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Tete esi Festo kple adaŋudelawo ɖe adaŋu la, eɖo ŋu bena: Kaisaro si me nètsɔ wò nya dee, kaisaro gbɔ kee nayi. Wokplɔ Paulo va Yudatɔwo ƒe fia Agripa ŋku me.

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Eye ŋkekea ɖewo megbe la fia Agripa kple Bernike wova Kaisarea bena, yewoaɖo gbe na Festo.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Eye esi wonɔ afima ŋkekea ɖewo la, Festo tsɔ Paulo ƒe nyawo katã ɖo fia la ŋku me gblɔ bena: Ŋutsua ɖe le afisia, si Felike gblẽ ɖe ga me:

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: amesia ŋuti, esime meva Yerusalem la, nunɔlagãwo kple Yudatɔwo ƒe amegãwo gblɔ nya ɖo hebia afiatsotso le.

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: Meɖo ŋu na amesiawo bena, menye Romatɔwo ƒe kɔ bena, woatsɔ amea ɖe aɖe asi, hafi amesi nu wotso kple nutsolawo nakpe ŋku me kple ŋku me, eye wòakpɔ mɔ aɖe eɖokui nu le nutsotso la ŋuti o.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: Eyata esi wova afisia la, nyemelala kura o; ke esi ŋu ke la, mebɔbɔ nɔ ʋɔnudrɔ̃zikpui la dzi, eye mede se be, woakplɔ ŋutsu lã vɛ.

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: Esi nutsolawo tsi tre ɖe eŋuti la, wometsɔ nya vɔ̃, siwo mesusu le eŋu la ƒe ɖeke vɛ o;

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: ke wotso biabiaa ɖewo le woa ŋutɔwo ƒe mawusubɔsubɔ ŋuti kple Yesua ɖe, si ku, amesi Paulo ka ɖe dzi be, ele agbe la ƒe nya vɛ.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: Eye nye la, esi nyemenya alesi madzro nya siawo mee o la, mebiae be, ne elɔ̃ bena, yeayi Yerusalem, ne woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnui le nya siawo ŋuti.

english_verse: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
translation_verse: Ke esi Paulo bia bena, woadzra ye ɖo na kaisaro ƒe afiatsotso la, meɖo bena, woadzrae ɖo, vaseɖe esime maɖoe ɖe kaisaro gbɔ.

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Eye Agripa gblɔ na Festo bena: Nye ŋuta hã mele didim bena, mase ame la ƒe numegbe. Egblɔ bena: Etsɔ àsee.

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: Eye esi ŋu ke la, Agripa kple Bernike wova kple atsyɔ̃ɖoɖo geɖe, eye woyi ɖe ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe la kple aʋafia gãwo kple ame ŋkuta, siwo le dua me; eye le Festo ƒe sedede nu la wokplɔ Paulo vɛ.

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: Eye Festo gblɔ bena: Fia Agripa kple mi ŋutsu, siwo katã li kpli mi fi fia, mikpɔ amesia, si ŋuti Yudatɔwo ƒe ha blibo la katã, siwo le Yerusalem kple afisia la, va do ɖe dzinye hele ɣli dom bena, medze be, wòaganɔ agbe didia ɖeke o la ɖa.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Ke esi nye la medze sii bena, mewo naneke, si dze ku o, eye eya ŋutɔ hã tsɔ eƒe nya de kaisaro si me la, meɖo bena, maɖoe ɖa.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Eye nya vavãa ɖeke mele asinye le eŋuti be, maŋlɔ na aƒetɔ la o. Eyaŋuti mekplɔe va mia ŋku me, vevietɔ wò fia Agripa ŋku me, bena ne miese eƒe numegbe vɔ la, ne makpɔ nane aŋlɔ.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: Elabena mebu bena, enye nu manyatanu be, woaɖo gatɔ ɖa eye womafia eŋuti nutsotso o.

english_verse: Agrippa told Paul, “You may now speak for yourself.” Paul stretched out his hand and said:
translation_verse: Eye Agripa gblɔ na Paulo bena: Woɖe mɔ na wò be, naƒo nu le ɖokuiwò ŋuti. Tete Paulo do asi ɖa, eye wòɖe eɖokui nu bena:

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: Mebui dzidzɔ, fia Agripa, bena maɖe ɖokuinye nu egbe sia le ŋkuwò me le nusiwo katã Yudatɔwo tsɔ le nunye tsom la ŋuti,

english_verse: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
translation_verse: vevietɔ elabena ènya kɔnuwɔwɔwo kple anukutsyɔtsyɔ, siwo katã le Yudatɔwo dome; eyata meɖe kuku na wò be, naɖo tom le dzigbɔɖeanyi me.

english_verse: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
translation_verse: wonyam tsã, ne wolɔ̃ be, yewoaɖi ɖase, alesi menɔ agbe le miaƒe subɔsubɔ ƒe kɔmamã, si nu sẽ wu wo katã la nu abe farisitɔ ene.

english_verse: Now I am on trial because I believe the promise God made to our people long ago.
translation_verse: Eye azɔ la mele tsitre be, woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnum le mɔkpɔkpɔ na ŋugbedodo, si Mawu ɖo na mía fofowo la ŋuti;

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: esi míaƒe ƒome wuieve la le mɔ kpɔm na hele Mawu subɔm vevie zã kple keli, bena woasu wo si. Le mɔkpɔkpɔ sia la, fia Agripa, Yudatɔwo le nunye tsom ɖo esi.

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Ne Mawu fɔ ame kukuwo ɖe tsitre la, aleke wɔ miebu bena, enye nusi womate ŋu axɔ ase oa?

english_verse: I once thought that I should do everything I could to oppose Jesus from Nazareth.
translation_verse: Nye la mebu le ɖokuinye me bena, ele nam be, mawɔ nu geɖe, siwo atsi tre ɖe Yesu, Nazaretetɔ la, ƒe ŋkɔ la ŋuti.

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
translation_verse: Nusi mewo hã le Yerusalem; eye mede ame kɔkɔewo dometɔ geɖewo gaxɔ me le ŋusẽ, si mexɔ tso nunɔlagãwo gbɔ la nu; eye ne wole wo wu ge la, melɔ̃na de edzi.

english_verse: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
translation_verse: Eye mese ŋuta le wo ŋu enuenu le ƒuƒoƒeawo katã, eye mezia wo dzi, bena woagblɔ busunya, eye esi meku tsu gɔ̃ hã ɖe wo ŋuti la, metia wo yome yia du bubuwo ke hã me.

english_verse: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
translation_verse: Esia dzi mele heyi Damasko, eye ŋusẽ kpakple mɔnana le asinye tso nunɔlagãwo gbɔ.

english_verse: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
translation_verse: Ɣeɖota, esime mele mɔ dzi la, fia, mekpɔ kekeli, si wu ɣe ƒe keklẽ la, tso dziƒo heklẽ ƒo xlã mia kple amesiwo le mɔ zɔm kpakplim la.

english_verse: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
translation_verse: Eye esi mi katã miedze anyi la, mese gbea ɖe ƒo nu nam le Hebri-gbe me bena: „Saul, Saul! Nuka wo nèle yonyeme tim? Esẽ na wò be, nada afɔkpo nutonu.“

english_verse: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
translation_verse: Eye nye la megblɔ bena: Wò amekae, Aƒetɔ? Eye Aƒetɔ la gblɔ bena: „Nyee nye Yesu, amesi yome tim nèle.

english_verse: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
translation_verse: Gake la fɔ, eye natsi tre ɖe wò afɔwo dzi, elabena esia ta meɖe ɖokuinye fia wò ɖo, bena maɖo wò nanye dɔla kple ɖaseɖila le nusiwo nèkpɔ kple nusiwo magaɖe afia wò la ŋuti;

english_verse: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
translation_verse: eye maɖe wò atso dukɔ la kple trɔ̃subɔla, siwo gbɔ mele dɔwòm ɖo la, si me,

english_verse: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
translation_verse: be naʋu woƒe ŋkuwo, bena woatrɔ atso viviti me ava kekeli me, eye tso Satana ƒe ŋusẽ me ava Mawu gbɔ, bena woakpɔ nuvɔ̃wo ƒe keke kple domenyinyi le amesiwo ŋu wokɔ to dzinye xɔxɔse me la dome.

english_verse: King Agrippa, I obeyed this vision from heaven.
translation_verse: Eyata, fia Agripa, nyemesẽ to ɖe dziƒoɖeɖefia la ŋuti o;

english_verse: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
translation_verse: ke boŋ megblɔe fia Damaskotɔwo gbã, kple amesiwo le Yerusalem kple Yudea nutometɔwo katã kpakple trɔ̃subɔlawo hã, bena woatrɔ le woƒe dzi me, eye ne woagbugbɔ ava Mawu gbɔ, ne woawɔ dɔ, siwo dze dzimetɔtrɔ.

english_verse: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
translation_verse: Le esia ŋuti Yudatɔwo lém le mawuxɔ la me, eye wode wu ye ge kloe.

english_verse: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
translation_verse: Ke esi mekpɔ xɔxɔ tso Mawu gbɔ vaseɖe egbe ŋkeke sia dzi la, mele tsitre hele ɖase ɖim na suewo kple gãwo, eye nyemele nu bubua ɖeke gblɔm o, nègbe nusiwo nyagblɔɖilawo kple Mose wogblɔ ɖi bena, ava ve me la koe,

english_verse: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: bena Kristo lakpe fu, eye bena wòanye gbãtɔ le lãme kukuwo ƒe tsitretsitsi la me, eye wòaɖe gbe ƒã kekeli afia dukɔ la kple trɔ̃subɔlawo siaa.

english_verse: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
translation_verse: Eye esi wòɖe eɖokui nu alea la, Festo gblɔ kple gbe sesẽ bena: Ele tsu kum, Paulo, agbalẽsɔsrɔ̃ geɖe wɔ wò nèzu tsukuno!

english_verse: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
translation_verse: Ke Paulo gblɔ bena: Nyemele tsu kum o, amegã nyui Festo; hafi boŋ nyateƒe kple tamebubunyawo gblɔm mele.

english_verse: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
translation_verse: Elabena fia hã nya nusiawo, amesi mele nu ƒom na kple dzideƒo; elabena mexɔe se bena, nusiawo dometɔa ɖeke mele ɣaɣla ɖee o, elabena menye ɣaɣlaƒe wowɔ nusia le o.

english_verse: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
translation_verse: Fia Agripa, èxɔa, nyagblɔɖilawo dzi sena? Menyae bena, èxɔnɛ sena.

english_verse: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
translation_verse: Tete Agripa gblɔ na Paulo bena: Esusɔ ʋee, naƒoe ɖe nunye be, nawɔm mazu kristotɔ.

english_verse: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
translation_verse: Ke Paulo gblɔ bena: Medi bena, Mawu nana be, ne esusɔ ʋee alo geɖe la, menye wò ɖeɖeko o, hafi boŋ amesiwo katã le to ɖomem egbe la, natrɔ zu esia tɔgbe abe nye ene, negbe babla siawo ko.

english_verse: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
translation_verse: Tete fia la kple mɔ̃mefia la kple Bernike kpakple amesiwo bɔbɔ nɔ anyi kpli wo la, tsi tre,

english_verse: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
translation_verse: eye esi, wote yi megbe la, wogblɔ na wo nɔewo bena, amesia mewɔ naneke, si dze ku alo bablawo o.

english_verse: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_verse: Eye Agripa gblɔ na Festo bena: Ɖe amesia metsɔ eƒe nya de kaisaro si me o la, ne woate ŋu aɖe asi le eŋu.

english_verse: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
translation_verse: Eye esi woɖoe bena, miaɖo nu ayi Italia la, wotsɔ Paulo kple gatɔ bubua ɖewo de aʋafiaa ɖe, si ŋkɔ enye Yulio tso, kaisaro ƒe asrafoha dome la si.

english_verse: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
translation_verse: Eye esi mieɖo Adramitio-ʋua ɖe, si le didim be, yeadze ɖe Asia ƒe ʋudzeƒewo la, míeho yi; eye Makedoniatɔ Aristarxo, si tso Tesalonika la, kpe ɖe mía ŋu.

english_verse: The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, míedze ɖe Sidon, eye Yulio nyo dome na Paulo, eye wòɖe mɔ nɛ bena, wòayi xɔlɔ̃awo gbɔ, be woagbã ɖe eme.

english_verse: When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind.
translation_verse: Eye esi mieho tso afima la, mieɖo abala to Kipro ƒe anyiehe; elabena ya ƒo le mia kpem.

english_verse: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
translation_verse: Eye esi mieto Kilikia-kple Pamfilia-ƒu me yi vɔ la mieva Mira le Likia.

english_verse: There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
translation_verse: Eye afima aʋafia la kpɔ Aleksandria-ʋua ɖe, si yina ɖe Italia, eye wòna mieɖoe.

english_verse: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
translation_verse: Eye esi miezɔ blewu ŋkeke geɖe, eye bebli hafi mieva ɖo Knido kasa la, ya la mena mɔ mí o, eye mieto Kreta ƒe anyiehe va ɖo Salmone kasa,

english_verse: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
translation_verse: eye bebli hafi mieto ƒuta la ŋu heva afia ɖe, si woyɔna be ʋudzeƒenyuie, si te ɖe Lasea-du la ŋu.

english_verse: By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past.
translation_verse: Eye esi ŋkeke geɖe va yi, eye ƒudzizɔzɔ zu ŋɔdzi azɔ, elabena nutsitsidɔ-ŋkekewo va yi xoxo la,

english_verse: Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.”
translation_verse: Paulo de dzi ƒo na wo gblɔ, bena: Mia tɔwo, mekpɔ bena, ƒudzidzɔzɔ la le dzi yi ge kple fuɖeɖe kpakple nugbegblẽ geɖe, si menye ʋuamenuwo kple ʋua ɖeɖeko dzi wòava o, ke boŋ mia ŋutɔwo ƒe agbe hã dzie.

english_verse: But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
translation_verse: Gake aʋafia la xɔ kuɖɔɖola kple ʋutɔ la dzi se wu nusiwo Paulo gblɔ la.

english_verse: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
translation_verse: Eye esi ʋudzeƒe la menyo bena, woanɔ le vuvɔŋɔli ta o la, wo dome ame geɖeawo ɖo aɖaŋu bena, woaho tso afima hã, bena ɖewohĩ yewoate ŋu ade Foinike, si nye Kreta ƒe ʋudzeƒe, si le dzieheɣetoɖoƒe kple anyieheɣetoɖoƒe, be yewoanɔ afima le vuvɔŋɔlia me.

english_verse: When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete.
translation_verse: Eye esi dzieheya ƒo bɔbɔe la, wobu xa bena, yewoƒe tameɖoɖo la le eme va ge, eye woho seke heho to Kreta ŋku me kekeake.

english_verse: days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing.
translation_verse: Eye medidia ɖeke o, tete ahom, si woyɔna be anyieheɣetoɖoƒeya la, ƒo kpe mí,

english_verse: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
translation_verse: eye esi wòle ʋu la hem yinae, eye mete ŋu le ya kpem o la, miena mɔe, eye wotsɔ mí.

english_verse: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
translation_verse: Eye esi ʋu la ɖi du to ƒukpo suea ɖe, si woyɔna be Klauda, ƒe anyiehe la, miedze agbagba ŋutɔ hafi te ŋu lé batala la;

english_verse: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
translation_verse: eye esi wohee ɖe dzi la, wotsɔ ka to ʋua te heblae, be woalée ɖe asi. Esi wole vɔvɔ̃m, bena, ɖewohĩ yewoava ge ɖe Sirte, afisi libla le la, woklo abala la, eye ale ya le mía kplɔm.

english_verse: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
translation_verse: Eye esi ahom la nyama mi ŋutɔ la, wòfɔ ʋuamenuwo ƒu gbe le ŋu, si ke la dzi;

english_verse: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
translation_verse: eye ŋkeke etɔ̃agbe la mietsɔ miaƒe asiwò fɔ ʋuamedɔwɔnuwo ƒu gbe.

english_verse: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
translation_verse: Ke esi ɣe alo ɣletivia ɖeke medo kpɔ le ŋkeke geɖewo me o, eye menye ahom via ɖee tu le nua kpem o la, mlɔeba la nukpɔkpɔ katã na miaƒe agbenɔnɔ la bu ɖe mi keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
translation_verse: Eye esi wonɔ anyi eteƒe didi naneke maɖumaɖui la, Paulo tsi tre ɖe wo titina gblɔ bena: O, mía tɔwo, ɖe mieɖo tom, eye mieho tso Kreta o la, ne fuɖeɖe kple gbegblẽ sia meva mia dzi o.

english_verse: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la mele nu xlɔ̃m mi bena, miaƒe dzi nadze eme, elabena mia dome amea ɖeke ƒe agbe mele bubu ge o, negbe ʋua ko.

english_verse: I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel
translation_verse: Elabena zã sia me la Mawu, si tɔ menye, amesi mesubɔna hã la, ƒe dɔla va tsi tre ɖe gbɔnye gblɔ bena:

english_verse: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
translation_verse: Paulo, megavɔ̃ o, ele na wò be, natsi tre ɖe kaisaro ƒe ŋku me, eye kpɔ ɖa, Mawu tsɔ amesiwo katã ɖo ʋua kpli wò la ke wò.

english_verse: Cheer up! I am sure that God will do exactly what he promised.
translation_verse: Eyaŋuti, mía; tɔwo, miaƒe dzi nèdze me, elabena mexɔ Mawu dzi se bena, ava me nenema, abe alesi wògblɔ; nam ene.

english_verse: But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
translation_verse: Gake la ele na mi be, miadze go ɖe ƒukpoa ɖe dzi.

english_verse: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
translation_verse: Eye wotso sekeawo hegblẽ ɖe ƒua me, eye wolũ kuɖɔkawo hã zi ɖeka, eye esi wodo abala la hekpe yae la, woɖo ta ƒuta.

english_verse: The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship.
translation_verse: Eye esi kahelawo le didim bena, yewoasi tso ʋua me, eye woɖiɖi batala ɖe ƒua me, eye woɖa alakpa, abe ɖe wole sekewo da ge ato ʋua ta hã ene la,

english_verse: The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
translation_verse: Eye esi wova bena, míava dze go ɖe kpe gbadzawo dzi la, woda seke ene to ʋua gɔme hele didim be, ŋu nake.

english_verse: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
translation_verse: Paulo gblɔ na aʋafia la kple asrafoawo bena: Ne amesiawo menɔ ʋua me o la, miate ŋu akpɔ ɖeɖe o.

english_verse: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
translation_verse: Tete asrafoawo tso batala ŋu tagbiawo, eye wona wòdze tɔa me.

english_verse: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
translation_verse: Eyata meɖe kuku na mi bena, miatsɔ nu aɖu, elabena esia nyo na miaƒe xɔxɔ: elabena mia dometɔa ɖeke ƒe taɖa ɖeka mabu atso eta o.

english_verse: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
translation_verse: Eye esi wògblɔ esiawo, eye wotsɔ abolo la, eda akpe na Mawu le wo katã ƒe ŋku me, eye wòŋe eme hede asi eɖuɖu me.

english_verse: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
translation_verse: Tete wo katã ƒe dzi dze eme, eye woa ŋutɔwo hã tsɔ nu ɖu.

english_verse: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
translation_verse: Eye esi woɖu nu ɖi ƒo la, wotsɔ nuɖuɖuawo ƒu gbe ɖe ƒu me, bena ʋua nazu wodzoe.

english_verse: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
translation_verse: Eye esi ŋu ke la, womedze si anyigba la o, ke wokpɔ adɔ̃a ɖe, si ŋu ƒuta le, eye wode adaŋu bena, ne yewoate ŋui la, ne yewoawɔ ʋu la ayi afima.

english_verse: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
translation_verse: Eye esi wodze ɖe teƒe lebiia ɖe, si yi ɖe ƒu me la, wona ʋu la si ké, eye ʋua ta xa hetsi maʋãmaʋã, eye egɔme gbã le ƒutsotsoe sesẽawo nu.

english_verse: The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
translation_verse: Ke asrafoawo ɖe adaŋu be, woawu gatɔwo, bena amea ɖeke nagaƒu tsi asi o.

english_verse: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
translation_verse: Gake esi aʋafia la le didim bena, yeaɖe Paulo la, exe mɔ na woƒe tameɖoɖo la, eye wòde se bena, amesiwo ate ŋu aƒu tsi la, nadzo kpo gbã adze ƒua me, ne wòayi gota,

english_verse: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
translation_verse: eye ame mamleawo lã ɖewo nanɔ ʋuƒowo dzi, eye ɖewo nanɔ ʋua ƒe kakɛa ɖewo dzi. Eye ale wòva me bena, wo katã wòde gota dedie.

english_verse: When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
translation_verse: Eye miekpɔ ɖeɖe, hafi nyae bena, Melite woyɔna na ƒukpo la.

english_verse: The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
translation_verse: Eye menye dɔmenyonyo via ɖe afimatɔwo wo na nu o; elabena wodo dzo, eye woxɔ mi katã ɖe egbɔ le tsidzadza kple vuvɔ ŋuti.

english_verse: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
translation_verse: Ke esi Paulo fɔ nake wuwluiwo ƒo ƒu heɖe dzo me la, da do tso wo me le dzoxɔxɔ la ŋuti, eye wòlé ɖe eƒe asi ŋu.

english_verse: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
translation_verse: Ke esi afimatɔwo kpɔ lã la xatsa ɖe eƒe asi ŋu la, wogblɔ na wo nɔewo bena: Ɖikekea ɖeke mele eme o bena, amesia nye hlɔ̃dola, eye esi wòkpɔ ɖeɖe tso ƒu me hã la, Mawu ƒe hlɔ̃biabia meɖe mɔ ne be, wòanɔ agbe o.

english_verse: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
translation_verse: Gake eya ʋuʋu lã la ɖe dzo la me, eye nu vevia ɖeke mewɔe o.

english_verse: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
translation_verse: Ke woawo le mɔ kpɔm nɛ bena, ate alo adze anyi aku enumake; eye esi wolala ʋuu, eye wokpɔ bena, naneke mewɔe o la, wotrɔ woƒe tamesusu hegblɔ be, mawua ɖee. Paulo fe nukunuwɔwɔwo.

english_verse: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
translation_verse: Eye le afima nuto me la anyigbae ɖe li, si nye ƒukpo la ƒe amegã, si ŋkɔ nye Publio la tɔ; eya xɔ mí nyuie hewɔ amedzro na mí ŋkeke etɔ̃ sɔŋ.

english_verse: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
translation_verse: Eye wòva me bena, Publio fofo mlɔ anyi le ŋudza lém, eye wòle sisi ɖem, eye Paulo yi ɖe egbɔ, eye wòdo gbe ɖa hetsɔ eƒe asi ɖa ɖe edzi, eye wòyɔ dɔe.

english_verse: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi esia va me la, ame mamlɛ, siwo le dɔwo lém le ƒukpoa dzi la, hã va egbɔ, eye wòyɔ dɔ wo,

english_verse: The people were very respectful to us, and when we sailed, they gave us everything we needed. From Malta to Rome
translation_verse: amesiwo hã bu mí geɖe ŋutɔ, eye esi miele dzodzo ge la, wotso nusiwo le mia hiãm la na mí. Paulo ƒe Roma vava kple eƒe dɔwɔwɔ le afima.

english_verse: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
translation_verse: Eye le ɣleti etɔ̃ megbe la mieɖo Aleksandria-ʋua ɖe, si nɔ afima le vuvɔŋɔli me, eye eƒe dzesie nye Venɔviwo, eye mieho.

english_verse: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
translation_verse: Eye esi miedze ɖe Sirakusa la, mieno afima ŋkeke etɔ̃.

english_verse: From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli.
translation_verse: Eye tso afima miegbɔ mɔ heva Regio, eye le ŋkeke ɖeka megbe la dzieheya ƒo, eye le ŋkeke evelia dzi la mieva Puteoli.

english_verse: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
translation_verse: Afisi miekpɔ nɔviwo le, eye woɖe kuku na mí bena, mianɔ yewo gbɔ ŋkeke adre; eye ale mieva Roma.

english_verse: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
translation_verse: Eye esi nɔvi, siwo le afima la, se mia ŋkɔ la, wova kpe mi le keke Apiforo kple Tretaberne ke; esi Paulo kpɔ wo la, eda akpe na Mawu, eye wòlé dzi ɖe ƒo.

english_verse: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
translation_verse: Eye esi mieva Roma la, aʋafia la tsɔ gatɔwo de aʋafia gã la si; ke woɖe mɔ na Paulo bena, woanɔ etɔwo gbɔ kple asrafo, si dzaa eŋu.

english_verse: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
translation_verse: Eye le ŋkeke etɔ̃ megbe la eva me bena, Paulo yɔ amesiwo nye amegãwo le Yudatɔwo dome la ƒo ƒu: eye esi wova ƒo ƒu la, egblɔ na wo bena: Nɔviŋutsuwo, nye la nyemewɔ naneke ɖe dukɔ la alo ɖe mía fofowo ƒe kɔnuwɔwɔawo ŋuti, hafi wodo gatɔm tso Yerusalem hede Romatɔwo si o.

english_verse: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
translation_verse: Eye woawo la, esi wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnum la, wodi bena, yewoaɖe asi le ŋunye, elabena womekpɔ naneke, si dze ku le ŋunye o.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor. But I don't have anything to say against my own nation.
translation_verse: Ke esi Yudatɔwo le nya gblɔm ɖe eŋuti la, ele nam ko be, matsɔ nye nya la ade kaisaro si me; menye bena, ɖe nyaa ɖee le asinye be, matsɔ atso nye dukɔ la nu o.

english_verse: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
translation_verse: Le nya sia ta meyɔ mi vɛ, bena makpɔ mi, eye ne maƒo nu kpli mi; elabena Israel ƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ ta wòbiam kple kɔsɔkɔsɔ sia ɖo.

english_verse: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
translation_verse: Eye woawo gblɔ nɛ bena: Miawo ta miexɔ agbalẽwo tso Yudea le ŋutiwò o; eye nɔviwo dometɔa ɖeke hã meva gblɔ nya vɔ̃ alo ƒo nu le ŋutiwò le afisia o.

english_verse: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
translation_verse: Ke miele didim bena, miase nusi susum nèle la, atso nuwò; elabena miese bena, wogblɔ nya ɖe kɔmamã sia ŋuti le afisiafi.

english_verse: They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
translation_verse: Eye esi woɖo ŋkeke nɛ la, ame geɖewo va egbɔ le eƒe dzeƒe la, amesiwo wògblɔ nya la na hele ɖase ɖim le mawufiaɖuƒe la ŋuti, eye wòle eƒom ɖe wo nu le Yesu ŋuti tso Mose ƒe se la kple nyagblɔɖilawo me tso ŋdikanya vaseɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not.
translation_verse: Eye amea ɖewo xɔ nusiwo wògblɔ la dzi se, eye amea ɖewo mexɔe se o.

english_verse: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Eye esi woƒe gbe mesɔ o la, wodzo le nya ɖeka, si Paulo gblɔ la ta bena, Gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la gblɔe nyuie na nua fofowo to nyagblɔɖila Yesaya dzi bena:

english_verse: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
translation_verse: „Yi dukɔ sia gbɔ, eye nagblɔ bena: To tsɔ ge miala ase nui, ke miele egɔme se ge o, eye ŋkuwo tso ge miala akpa nui, ke miele si dze gee o.

english_verse: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
translation_verse: Elabena nenem dukɔ sia ƒe dzi ku atri, eye woƒe towo sẽ, eye womesea nu o, eye womiã woƒe ŋkuwo, be woagakpɔ nu kple woƒe ŋkuwo, eye woase nu kple woƒe towo, eye woase nu gɔme kple woƒe dzi, ne woatrɔ, eye mada gbe le wo ŋu o.“

english_verse: Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
translation_verse: Eye esi wògblɔ esiawo la, Yudatɔwo dzo, eye nusesẽ geɖe ɖo wo dome.

english_verse: For two years Paul stayed in a rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him.
translation_verse: Ke Paulo nɔ anyi ƒe blibo eve sɔŋ le ye ŋuta ƒe xɔ, si wòɣe la me; eye wòxɔa amesiwo katã va egbɔ,

english_verse: He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
translation_verse: eye wòle mawufiaɖuƒe la ƒe gbe ƒã ɖem; eye wòle nu fiãm le Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo ŋuti kple dzideƒo ŋutɔ, eye amea ɖeke mexea mɔ nɛ o.

english_verse: From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus. God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news
translation_verse: Paulo, Yesu Kristo ƒe dɔla kple apostolo, si woyɔ, eye wotia hena Mawu ƒe nyanyuie,

english_verse: that he promised long ago by what his prophets said in the holy Scriptures.
translation_verse: si wòdo ŋugbe ɖi to eƒe nyagblɔɖilawo dzi le ŋɔŋlɔ kɔkɔewo me

english_verse: This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
translation_verse: si woɖo Mawuvi kple ŋusẽ le kɔkɔenyenye ƒe Gbɔgbɔ la nu to tsitretsitsi tso ame kukuwo dome la me, amesi nye Yesu Kristo, mia Aƒetɔ,

english_verse: Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith.
translation_verse: amesi me miekpɔ amenuveve kple apostolonyenye le na xɔse ƒe toɖoɖo le dukɔwo katã dome le eƒe ŋkɔ ŋuti,

english_verse: You are some of those people chosen by Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: amesiwo dome miawo hã míenye Yesu Kristo ƒe ame yɔyɔwo le la,

english_verse: This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people. I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! A Prayer of Thanks
translation_verse: ŋlɔ ɖo ɖe mi, amesiwo katã le Roma, siwo nye Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃tɔwo kple ame kɔkɔe, siwo woyɔ la: Amenuveve kple ŋutifafa, si tso Mawu, mia Fofo, kple Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo gbɔ la, woana mi! Nyanyuie la enye Mawu ƒe ŋusẽ eye wonaa agbexɔxɔ trɔ̃subɔlawo hã.

english_verse: First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith.
translation_verse: Gbã la mele akpe dam na Mawunye to Yesu Kristo dzi le mi katã ta bena, wogblɔa miaƒe xɔsenya fiana le xexeme blibo la katã.

english_verse: God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
translation_verse: Elabena nye ɖaseɖilae nye Mawu, si mesubɔna le nye gbɔgbɔ me le Via ƒe nyanyuie la me, alesi nyemedzudzɔa ŋkuɖoɖo mia dzi o,

english_verse: In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you.
translation_verse: eye meɖea kuku le nye gbedodoɖawo me ɖaasi, abe ɖe wòadze edzi nam nyuie azɔ le Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu la nu bena, mava mia gbɔ gbaɖegbe mahĩ?

english_verse: I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith.
translation_verse: Elabena ele dzroyem vevie bena, makpɔ mi ɖa, bene matsɔ gbɔgbɔ me nunanaa ɖe ana mi, ne wòado ŋusẽ mi;

english_verse: What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
translation_verse: eya nye bene, woafa akɔ nam le mia dome le xɔse, si nye mia kple mia tɔ siaa la me.

english_verse: My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places.
translation_verse: Nɔviwo, nyemele didim be, miaganyae o bena, meɖo tame edziedzi be, mava mia gbɔ, ke woxe mɔ nam vaseɖe fifi, bene makpɔ kutsetse le mia dome hã, abe alesi mekpɔ le dukɔ bubuwo dome ene.

english_verse: I am proud of the good news! It is God's powerful way of saving all people who have faith, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Elabena nyanyuie la mekpea ŋu nam o, elabena enye Mawu ƒe ŋusẽ, si naa agbexɔxɔ amesiame, si xɔna sena la, Yudatɔwo gbã kple Helatɔwo hã.

english_verse: The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.” Everyone Is Guilty
translation_verse: Elabena woɖea Mawu ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye ɖe go le eya me tso xɔse me yina xɔse me, abe alesi woŋlɔ ɖi ene bena: „Ame dzɔdzɔe la anɔ agbe atso xɔse me.“

english_verse: From heaven God shows how angry he is with all the wicked and evil things that sinful people do to crush the truth.
translation_verse: Elabena woɖe Mawu ƒe dziku ɖe go tso dziƒo ɖe amegbetɔwo ƒe mawumavɔ̃mavɔ̃ kple madzɔmadzɔnyenye katã dzi, amesiwo xea mɔ na nyateƒe le madzɔmadzɔnyenye me.

english_verse: They know everything that can be known about God, because God has shown it all to them.
translation_verse: Eyata esi woɖe nusi woate ŋu anya le Mawu ŋuti la, fia le wo me la; elabena Mawu ɖee fia wo.

english_verse: God's eternal power and character cannot be seen. But from the beginning of creation, God has shown what these are like by all he has made. That's why those people don't have any excuse.
translation_verse: Elabena tso xexemewɔwɔ dzi la, ne wobua tame le eŋuti la, wokpɔa eƒe numanyakpɔ, si nye eƒe ŋusẽ mavɔmavɔ kple mawunyenye la kɔte le eƒe dɔwɔwɔwo me, bena taflatsedodoa ɖeke naganɔ wo si o.

english_verse: They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark.
translation_verse: Eyata esi wònye wonya Mawu hafi, gake womekafunɛ abe Mawu ene o, ke boŋ woƒe tamesusuwo zu yaka, eye woƒe dzi masenugɔmewo do viviti la.

english_verse: They claim to be wise, but they are fools.
translation_verse: Esime wole edzi bena, nunyalawo yewonye la, wozu bometsilawo,

english_verse: They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
translation_verse: eye woɖɔ li Mawu magblẽmagblẽ la ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe la, bene wòaɖi ame gbegblẽ kple xeviwo kple lãfɔnewo kple nutatawo ƒe nɔnɔme.

english_verse: So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies.
translation_verse: Eyata le woƒe dziwo ƒe nudzodzrowo me la Mawu tsɔ wo de asi na makɔmakɔnyenye, bene woado ŋunyɔ woƒe ŋutilãwo le wo nɔewo dome;

english_verse: They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
translation_verse: amesiwo tso Mawu ƒe nyateƒe la ɖɔ li aʋatsokaka, eye wovɔ̃, eye wosubɔ nuwɔwɔ wu wɔla, si wokafuna yi ɖe mavɔmavɔ me! Amen.

english_verse: God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural.
translation_verse: Eyaŋuti Mawu tsɔ wo de asi na ahɔhlɔ̃bɔbɔ yomenɔnɔ; elabena woƒe nyɔnuwo tsɔ dzɔdzɔme ƒe kɔnu wɔ nusi mele dzɔdzɔme nu o;

english_verse: Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
translation_verse: nenema ke woƒe ŋutsuwo hã gblẽ nyɔnuwo ƒe dzɔdzɔmekɔnu ɖi, eye wofiã le woƒe fiẽŋufiẽŋui me ɖe wo nɔewo ŋu, eye ŋutsu kple ŋutsu wɔ ŋukpenanuwo, eye wokpɔ woƒe vodada ŋuti fetu, si dze wo la, le wo ɖokui ŋu.

english_verse: Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things.
translation_verse: Eye alesi womebu eŋu bena, woalé Mawu ƒe sidzedze ɖe asi o la, nenema Mawu hã tsɔ wo de asi na tamebubu, si medze o, bene woawɔ nusiwo medze o;

english_verse: They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip,
translation_verse: amesiwo yɔ taŋ kple madzɔmadzɔnyenye katã: Ahasiwɔwɔ, vɔ̃ɖiwɔwɔ, nu tovo wɔwɔ, ŋubiabiã; eye woyɔ fũ kpakple ŋuʋaʋã, amewuwu, dzrewɔwɔ, beble, apasa;

english_verse: say cruel things about others, and hate God. They are proud, conceited, and boastful, always thinking up new ways to do evil. These people don't respect their parents.
translation_verse: sakplisalawo, ameŋuzɔlawo, amesiwo léa Mawu ɖe lu me, vlodolawo, dadalawo, adegbe ƒuƒlu ƒolawo, amesiwo toa nu vɔ̃ɖi vɛ, amesiwo meɖoa to woƒe dzilawo o,

english_verse: They are stupid, unreliable, and don't have any love or pity for others.
translation_verse: ame masenugɔmewo, nubabladzidalawo, amesiwo melɔ̃a ame ƒe nya o, amesiwo gbea avuléle kple ame makpɔnublanuiwo;

english_verse: They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
translation_verse: amesiwo nya Mawu ƒe nuɖoanyi dzɔdzɔe la kɔte bena, amesiwo wɔa nusiawo la, wodze ku; eye womewɔa nusiawo ɖeɖeko o, hafi boŋ wokpɔa dzidzɔ le amesiwo wɔne la hã ŋuti.

english_verse: Some of you accuse others of doing wrong. But there is no excuse for what you do. When you judge others, you condemn yourselves, because you are guilty of doing the very same things.
translation_verse: Eyata taflatsedodoa ɖeke mele asiwò o, oo ame, amesi ke ƒomevi nènye le ʋɔnu drɔ̃m la! Elabena nusi ke netsɔna drɔ̃a ʋɔnu ame bubu la, eya ke netsɔna bua fɔ ɖokuiwò; elabena wò amesi le ʋɔnu drɔ̃m la, wò ŋutɔ èwɔa nu mawo ke.

english_verse: We know that God is right to judge everyone who behaves in this way.
translation_verse: Ke mienyae bena, Mawu ƒe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ le nyateƒe la nu va amesiwo wɔ nenem nusiawo la dzi.

english_verse: Do you really think God won't punish you, when you behave exactly like the people you accuse?
translation_verse: Ke, oo ame, si le ʋɔnu drɔ̃m amesiwo woa nenem nusiawo, eye wò ŋutɔ nèwɔa nu mawo ke la, ɖe nèsusuna bena, yeate ŋu asi le Mawu ƒe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ la nu mahã?

english_verse: You surely don't think much of God's wonderful goodness or of his patience and willingness to put up with you. Don't you know that the reason God is good to you is because he wants you to turn to him?
translation_verse: Alo ɖe nèdoa vlo Mawu ƒe dɔmenyonyo kple dzidodo kple dzigbɔgbɔ blewu ƒe agbɔsɔsɔ la, eye menyae bena, Mawu ƒe dɔmenyonyo kplɔa wò yina ɖe dzimetɔtrɔ me o mahã?

english_verse: But you are stubborn and refuse to turn to God. So you are making things even worse for yourselves on that day when he will show how angry he is and will judge the world with fairness.
translation_verse: Ke wò la, le wò dzi sesẽ, si metrɔ o la nu, nèƒo dziku nu ƒu ɖi na ɖokuiwò hena dziku ƒe ŋkeke kpakple Mawu ƒe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ dzɔdzɔe ƒe ɖeɖefia la,

english_verse: God will reward each of us for what we have done.
translation_verse: amesi aɖo teƒe na amesiame le eƒe dɔwɔwɔwo nu:

english_verse: He will give eternal life to everyone who has patiently done what is good in the hope of receiving glory, honor, and life that lasts forever.
translation_verse: Amesiwo tsɔa dzidodo le dɔ nyui wɔwɔ me dia ŋutikɔkɔe kple bubu kple nu magblẽmagblẽ la, woana agbe mavɔ wo;

english_verse: But he will show how angry and furious he can be with every selfish person who rejects the truth and wants to do evil.
translation_verse: ke amesiwo lɔ̃a dzrehehe, eye womeɖoa to nyateƒe la o, hafi woɖoa to madzɔmadzɔnyenye boŋ la, wo tɔ anye dziku kple dɔmedzoe:

english_verse: All who are wicked will be punished with trouble and suffering. It doesn't matter if they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Xaxa kple momenuveve ava amesiame, si le vɔ̃ wɔm la ƒe luʋɔ dzi, Yudatɔwo gbã kple Helatɔwo hã;

english_verse: But all who do right will be rewarded with glory, honor, and peace, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: hafi ŋutikɔkɔe kple bubu kple ŋutifafa woana amesiame, si le nu nyui wɔm la, Yudatɔwo gbã kple Helatɔwo hã.

english_verse: God doesn't have any favorites!
translation_verse: Elabena ameŋkumekpɔkpɔa ɖeke mele Mawu gbɔ o.

english_verse: Those people who don't know about God's Law will still be punished for what they do wrong. And the Law will be used to judge everyone who knows what it says.
translation_verse: Elabena ame alesi nu wɔ nuvɔ̃ se manɔ wo sii la, woatsrɔ̃ se manɔ wo sii; eye ame alesi nu wɔ nuvɔ̃, eye se le wo si la, woatsɔ se la adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wo.

english_verse: God accepts those who obey his Law, but not those who simply hear it.
translation_verse: Elabena menye amesiwo sea se la, wonye ame dzɔdzɔewo le Mawu ƒe ŋku me o, hafi boŋ woatso afia na amesiwo wɔa se la dzi.

english_verse: This proves that the conscience is like a law written in the human heart. And it will show whether we are forgiven or condemned,
translation_verse: abe amesiwo fia bene, woŋlɔ se la ƒe dɔwɔwɔ ɖe woƒe dziwo me la ene, eye woƒe dzitsinya hã ɖia ɖase hekpena ɖe eŋu, eye woƒe tamebubuwo nɔa wo nɔewo nu tsom, alo wonɔa wo nɔewo nu ɖem hã,

english_verse: when God appoints Jesus Christ to judge everyone's secret thoughts, just as my message says. The Jews and the Law
translation_verse: le ŋkeke, si dzi Mawu adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu amewo ƒe nu ɣaɣlawo le nye nyanyuie la nu to Yesu Kristo dzi la dzi.

english_verse: Some of you call yourselves Jews. You trust in the Law and take pride in God.
translation_verse: Ke wò la, ne woyɔ wò be Yudatɔ, eye nèɖoa ŋu ɖe se la ŋu, eye nèƒo adegbe le Mawu me,

english_verse: By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right.
translation_verse: eye nènya eƒe lɔlɔ̃nu, eye nèbu nusi dzɔ kple esi medzɔ o me kpɔ, esi wotia nu wò le sea me la,

english_verse: You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark.
translation_verse: eye neɖo ŋu ɖe ɖokuiwò ŋu bena, yee nye ŋkuagbãtɔwo ƒe mɔfiala kple amesiwo le viviti me la ƒe kekeli

english_verse: And since there is knowledge and truth in God's Law, you think you can instruct fools and teach young people.
translation_verse: kple ame manyanuwo ƒe hela kple ɖeviwo ƒe nufiala, amesi si sidzedze kple nyateƒe ƒe nɔnɔme, si le sea me la, le la,

english_verse: But how can you teach others when you refuse to learn? You preach it is wrong to steal. But do you steal?
translation_verse: ekem wò amesi fia nu ame bubuwo la, ɖe mèfia nu ɖokuiwò oa? Wò amesi ɖe gbe ƒã bena, womegati fi o la, wòe fi fia?

english_verse: You say people should be faithful in marriage. But are you faithful? You hate idols, yet you rob their temples.
translation_verse: Wò amesi gblɔ bena, womegawɔ ahasi o la, wòe wɔ ahasia? Wò amesi nyɔ ŋu trɔ̃wo la, wòe ha trɔ̃subɔƒenuwo mahã?

english_verse: You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God.
translation_verse: Wò amesi ƒo adegbe le se la ŋuti la, wòe doa vlo Mawu to seadzidada mea?

english_verse: It is just as the Scriptures tell us, “You have made foreigners say insulting things about God.”
translation_verse: Elabena le miawo ŋuti la wogblɔa busunya ɖe Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ ŋuti le trɔ̃subɔlawo dome, abe alesi woŋlɔ ɖi ene.

english_verse: Being circumcised is worthwhile, if you obey the Law. But if you don't obey the Law, you are no better off than people who are not circumcised.
translation_verse: Elabena ne èwɔ sea dzi la, aʋatsotso enye viɖe; hafi nenye seadzidala nènye la, ekema wò aʋatsotso zu aʋamatsomatso.

english_verse: In fact, if they obey the Law, they are as good as anyone who is circumcised.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, ne aʋamatsomatsotɔ dzra se la ƒe nuɖoanyi dzɔdzɔewo ɖo la, womabu eƒe aʋamatsomatso la aʋatsotso nɛ o mahã?

english_verse: So everyone who obeys the Law, but has never been circumcised, will condemn you. Even though you are circumcised and have the Law, you still don't obey its teachings.
translation_verse: Eye amesi nye aʋamatsomatsotɔ tso dzɔdzɔ me, gake wowu sea nu la, adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wò amesi wònye agbalẽŋlɔdzesi kple aʋatsotso li na wò hafi, gake nèda se la dzi.

english_verse: Just because you live like a Jew and are circumcised doesn't make you a real Jew.
translation_verse: Elabena menye amesi ke nye Yudatɔ le gota la, enye Yudatɔ o, eye menye nusi ke le gota le ŋutilã ŋu la, enye aʋatsotso o;

english_verse: To be a real Jew you must obey the Law. True circumcision is something that happens deep in your heart, not something done to your body. And besides, you should want praise from God and not from humans.
translation_verse: hafi amesi nye Yudatɔ le ɣaɣla me la, eya boŋ enye Yudatɔ, eye dzimeʋatsotso le gbɔgbɔ me, menye le agbalẽŋlɔdzesi nu o la, eyae nye aʋatsotso; amesi ƒe kafukafu metso amewo gbɔ o, ke tso Mawu gbɔ boŋ.

english_verse: What good is it to be a Jew? What good is it to be circumcised?
translation_verse: Azɔ la, nukae nye Yudatɔ ƒe nu nyui, si ƒo ta la, alo nu kae nye aʋatsotso ƒe viɖea?

english_verse: It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews.
translation_verse: Nu geɖe le go sia go me; gbã wotsɔ Mawu ƒe nyawo ɖewo si.

english_verse: It is true that some of them did not believe the message. But does this mean that God cannot be trusted, just because they did not have faith?
translation_verse: Elabena ne amea ɖewo mewɔ nuteƒe o la, nukae? Alo ɖe woƒe nuteƒemawɔmawɔ aɖe Mawu ƒe nuteƒetɔnyenye ɖa mahã?

english_verse: No, indeed! God tells the truth, even if everyone else is a liar. The Scriptures say about God, “Your words will be proven true, and in court you will win your case.”
translation_verse: Gbeɖe! Hafi nenɔ ale: Mawu nye nyateƒetɔ, ke amesiame aʋatsokalae, abe alesi woŋlɔ ɖi ene bena: „Bene woatso afia na wò le wò nyawo me, eye bene naɖu dzi, ne wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wò.“

english_verse: If our evil deeds show how right God is, then what can we say? Is it wrong for God to become angry and punish us? What a foolish thing to ask.
translation_verse: Ke ne miaƒe madzɔmadzɔnyenye ɖe Mawu ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye ɖe go fia la, nuka gblɔ ge mialã? Ne Mawu fia dziku la, ɖe etɔ medzɔ oa? Meƒo nu abe ame ene.

english_verse: But the answer is, “No.” Otherwise, how could God judge the world?
translation_verse: Gbeɖe! Elabena ekema aleke Mawu ladrɔ̃ ʋɔnu xexeamee ma?

english_verse: Since your lies bring great honor to God by showing how truthful he is, you may ask why God still says you are a sinner.
translation_verse: Ke ne Mawu ƒe nyateƒea zu gã wu to nye aʋatsokaka me hena eƒe ŋutikɔkɔe la, nukaŋuti woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu nye hã abe nuvɔ̃wɔla ene mahã?

english_verse: You might as well say, “Let's do something evil, so that something good will come of it!” Some people even claim that we are saying this. But God is fair and will judge them as well. No One Is Good
translation_verse: Eye nukaŋuti miawo, abe alesi woɖoa vlo mi, eye abe alesi amea ɖewo ɖea aɖe nu me na mí be, miegblɔna bena: „Mina míawɔ nuvɔ̃, bena nu nyui nava“ ene o boŋ mahã? Amesiawo ƒe fɔbubu edzɔ.

english_verse: What does all this mean? Does it mean that we Jews are better off than the Gentiles? No, it doesn't! Jews, as well as Gentiles, are ruled by sin, just as I have said.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, aleke wòle? Ɖe mia tɔ ƒo ame bubuwo tɔ ta mahã? O, mele nenema kura o; elabena mietso Yudatɔwo kple Helatɔwo nu da ɖi bena, wo katã wole nuvɔ̃a te,

english_verse: The Scriptures tell us, “No one is acceptable to God!
translation_verse: alesi woŋlɔ ɖi bena: „Ame dzɔdzɔea ɖeke meli o, ɖeka hɔ̃ meli o.

english_verse: Not one of them understands or even searches for God.
translation_verse: Amea ɖeke meli, si nya nu o, amea ɖeke meli, si biaa Mawu ta sena o!

english_verse: They have all turned away and are worthless. There isn't one person who does right.
translation_verse: Wo keŋ wote ɖe aga, wo katã tim wogblẽ. Amea ɖeke meli, si wɔa nu nyui o, ɖeka hɔ̃ hã meli o.

english_verse: Their words are like an open pit, and their tongues are good only for telling lies. Each word is as deadly as the fangs of a snake,
translation_verse: Yɔdo, si le nuvo la, enye woƒe ve me, woƒe aɖewo gblɔa nya vivi ŋanɛŋanɛ; ƒliwo ƒe aɖi le woƒe nuyiwo me;

english_verse: and they say nothing but bitter curses.
translation_verse: fiƒode kple veve helĩhelĩ yɔ woƒe nu me fũ.

english_verse: These people quickly become violent.
translation_verse: Woƒe afɔwo ɖe abla, be woakɔ ʋu ɖe anyi,

english_verse: Wherever they go, they leave ruin and destruction.
translation_verse: gbegblẽ kple dzɔgbevɔ̃e le woƒe mɔwo dzi;

english_verse: They don't know how to live in peace.
translation_verse: eye womenya ŋutifafamɔ la o.

english_verse: They don't even fear God.”
translation_verse: Mawuvɔvɔ̃a ɖeke metso ga ɖe ŋku me na wo o.“

english_verse: We know that everything in the Law was written for those who are under its power. The Law says these things to stop anyone from making excuses and to let God show that the whole world is guilty.
translation_verse: Ke míenyae bena, nusianu, si se la le gbɔgblɔm la, etonɛ na amesiwo le se la me, bene amesiame ƒe nu natsi te, eye xexeme blibo la katã nazu fɔɖila na Mawu.

english_verse: God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin. God's Way of Accepting People
translation_verse: Elabena to se la ƒe dɔwɔwɔwo me la womatso afia na ŋutilãa ɖeke le eƒe ŋku me o; elabena se la me nuvɔ̃ ƒe sidzedze dzɔ tso.

english_verse: Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la se la manɔmee woɖe Mawu ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye hefiã, esi ŋuti se la kple nyagblɔɖilawo ɖi ɖase le,

english_verse: God treats everyone alike. He accepts people only because they have faith in Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: esi nye Mawu ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye, si toa Yesu Kristo dzixɔxɔse me vana na amesiwo katã xɔna sena la. Elabena vovototoa ɖeke meli o;

english_verse: All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory.
translation_verse: elabena wo katã wɔ nuvɔ̃, eye Mawu ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe hiã wo tim,

english_verse: But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins.
translation_verse: eye wotso afia na wo faa le eƒe amenuveve me to fexexeɖeta, si nye Kristo Yesu ta la me,

english_verse: What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, afika adegbeƒoƒo le mahã? Woɖee ɖe aga. To se ka ƒomevi mea? Ɖe dɔwɔwɔwo toe loo? Gbeɖe! Hafi to xɔse ƒe se la me boŋ.

english_verse: We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law.
translation_verse: Eyata míebuna bena, wotsoa afia na ame to xɔse me, se la ƒe dɔwɔwɔwo manɔmee.

english_verse: Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is!
translation_verse: Alo ɖe Mawu nye Yudatɔwo ɖeɖeko tɔ, eye menye trɔ̃subɔlawo to hã oa? Ẽ, trɔ̃subɔlawo to hã wònye:

english_verse: There is only one God, and he accepts Gentiles as well as Jews, simply because of their faith.
translation_verse: elabena Mawu ɖekae nye amesi tso afia na aʋatsotsotɔwo tso xɔse me kple aʋamatsomatsotɔwo tso xɔse me.

english_verse: Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
translation_verse: Ekem ɖe mietsɔ xɔse la tu se la mahã? Gbeɖe! Ke mietsɔ se la tu tsitre boŋ.

english_verse: Well then, what can we say about our ancestor Abraham?
translation_verse: Azɔ nuka gblɔ ge míala be, mía tɔgbui Abraham kpɔ le ŋutilã nua?

english_verse: If he became acceptable to God because of what he did, then he would have something to brag about. But he would never be able to brag about it to God.
translation_verse: Elabena nenye wotso afia na Abraham tso dɔwɔwɔwo me la, nane le esi, si ŋuti wòaƒo adegbe le, gake menye le Mawu gbɔ o.

english_verse: The Scriptures say, “God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.”
translation_verse: Elabena nuka ŋɔŋlɔa gblɔna? „Abraham xɔ Mawu dzi se, eye wobui dzɔdzɔenyenye nɛ.“

english_verse: Money paid to workers isn't a gift. It is something they earn by working.
translation_verse: Ke amesi le dɔ wɔm la, womebua fetua nɛ abe amenuvevenu ene o, ke boŋ abe nusi dzee ene.

english_verse: But you cannot make God accept you because of something you do. God accepts sinners only because they have faith in him.
translation_verse: Ke amesi mele dɔ wɔm o, hafi wòxɔa amesi tso afia na ame mavɔ̃mawu la dzi sena la, wobua eƒe xɔse dzɔdzɔenyenye nɛ;

english_verse: In the Scriptures David talks about the blessings that come to people who are acceptable to God, even though they don't do anything to deserve these blessings. David says,
translation_verse: abe alesi Dawid hã gblɔ yayranya na amesi Mawu bua dzɔdzɔenyenye na dɔwɔwɔwo manɔsii la ene bena:

english_verse: Are these blessings meant for circumcised people or for those who are not circumcised? Well, the Scriptures say that God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.
translation_verse: Azɔ la de yayranyagbɔgblɔ sia va aʋatsotsoa dzi loo, alo aʋamatsomatso hã dzi mahã? Elabena míegblɔna bena: Xɔse la wotso bu dzodzoenyenye na Abraham.

english_verse: But when did this happen? Was it before or after Abraham was circumcised? Of course, it was before.
translation_verse: Azɔ la aleke wobui nɛ? Ɖe esime wotso aʋa nɛ loo, alo esime wometso aʋa nɛ haɖe o mahã? Menye esime wotso aʋa nɛ o, ke esime wometso aʋa ne haɖe o boŋ.

english_verse: Abraham let himself be circumcised to show he had been accepted because of his faith even before he was circumcised. This makes Abraham the father of all who are acceptable to God because of their faith, even though they are not circumcised.
translation_verse: Eye wòxɔ aʋatsotso ƒe dzesi, si nye xɔse, si le esi le aʋamatsomatso me la, ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe nutrenu, bene wòanye fofo na amesiwo katã xɔna sena le aʋamatsomatso me la, bene woabui dzɔdzɔenyenye na woawo hã,

english_verse: This also makes Abraham the father of everyone who is circumcised and has faith in God, as Abraham did before he was circumcised. The Promise Is for All Who Have Faith
translation_verse: bene wòanye fofo na aʋatsotsotɔwo hã, amesiwo metso aʋatsotso me ɖeɖeko o, hafi amesiwo zɔna le mía fofo Abraham ƒe xɔse, si le esi le aʋamatsomatso me la ƒe afɔtoƒewo me la boŋ.

english_verse: God promised Abraham and his descendants that he would give them the world. This promise wasn't made because Abraham had obeyed a law, but because his faith in God made him acceptable.
translation_verse: Elabena menye se la me ŋugbedodo, si wodo na Abraham alo eƒe ƒome bena, wòanye xexeme ƒe domenyila la, to va o, ke boŋ eto xɔse ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye me va.

english_verse: If Abraham and his descendants were given this promise because they had obeyed a law, then faith would mean nothing, and the promise would be worthless.
translation_verse: Elabena nenye amesiwo tso sea me la, wonye domenyilawo la, ekema xɔse la zu gbolo, eye wode ŋugbedodo la da.

english_verse: God becomes angry when his Law is broken. But where there isn't a law, it cannot be broken.
translation_verse: Elabena se la hea dziku vɛ; gake afisi se mele o la, dzidada hã meli o.

english_verse: Everything depends on having faith in God, so that God's promise is assured by his gift of undeserved grace. This promise isn't only for Abraham's descendants who have the Law. It is for all who are Abraham's descendants because they have faith, just as he did. Abraham is the ancestor of us all.
translation_verse: Eyata xɔse me wòtso, bene wòanye le amenuveve nu, bene ŋugbedodo nali zã na ƒome sia ƒome, menye amesiwo tso sea me ɖeɖeko o, hafi amesiwo tso Abraham ƒe xɔse me hã, amesi nye mí katã mia fofo la,

english_verse: The Scriptures say that Abraham would become the ancestor of many nations. This promise was made to Abraham because he had faith in God, who raises the dead to life and creates new things.
translation_verse: abe alesi woŋlɔ ɖi ene bena: „Meɖo wò dukɔ geɖewo fofo“ le Mawu, si dzi nèxɔ se ƒe ŋku me, amesi gagbɔa agbe ame kukuwo, eye wòyɔa nusiwo meli o, abe nusiwo li la ene;

english_verse: God promised Abraham a lot of descendants. And when it all seemed hopeless, Abraham still had faith in God and became the ancestor of many nations.
translation_verse: amesi le esime mɔkpɔkpɔa ɖeke megali o la, wòkpɔ mɔ le xɔse me, bene wòatro zu dukɔ geɖewo fofo, abe alesi wogblɔ ne ene bena: „Nenema lanye wò ƒome.“

english_verse: But Abraham never doubted or questioned God's promise. His faith made him strong, and he gave all the credit to God.
translation_verse: eye meke ɖi le Mawu ƒe ŋugbedodo la ŋuti le dzimaxɔse me hã o, hafi esẽ ŋu le xɔse me boŋ, eye wòtso bubu na Mawu,

english_verse: Abraham was certain that God could do what he had promised.
translation_verse: eye wòkpɔ kakaɖedzi blibo bena, nusi ke ŋugbe wòdo la, ate ŋu awɔe hã.

english_verse: So God accepted him,
translation_verse: Eyata wobui dzɔdzɔenyenye nɛ.

english_verse: just as we read in the Scriptures. But these words were not written only for Abraham.
translation_verse: Gake menye eya ɖeɖeko ta woŋlɔe ɖi ɖo bena, wobui nɛ o;

english_verse: They were written for us, since we will also be accepted because of our faith in God, who raised our Lord Jesus to life.
translation_verse: ke miawo hã tae, mí amesiwo woava abui na, mi amesiwo xɔa amesi fɔ Yesu, mía Aƒetɔ, ɖe tsi tre tso ame kukuwo dome la dzi sena,

english_verse: God gave Jesus to die for our sins, and he raised him to life, so that we would be made acceptable to God.
translation_verse: amesi wotsɔ hena le míaƒe vodadawo ŋuti, eye wofɔe ɖe tsitre le afiatsotso na mí ta.

english_verse: By faith we have been made acceptable to God. And now, thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, we have peace with God.
translation_verse: Azɔ la esi wotso afia na mí tso xɔse me la, ŋutifafa le mia kple Mawu dome to mía Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo dzi,

english_verse: Christ has also introduced us to God's gift of undeserved grace on which we now take our stand. So we are happy, as we look forward to sharing in the glory of God.
translation_verse: amesi me miekpɔe mɔnu hã le le xɔse me heyina ɖe amenuveve sia gbɔ, si me míetsia tre ɖo la, eye mieƒoa adegbe le Mawu ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe ƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ la ŋuti.

english_verse: But that's not all! We gladly suffer, because we know that suffering helps us to endure.
translation_verse: Ke menye esia ɖeɖekoe o, hafi míeƒoa adegbe le xaxawo me hã, esi mienyae bena, xaxa dzia dzidodo;

english_verse: And endurance builds character, which gives us a hope
translation_verse: ke dzidodo dzia kelili, ke kelili dzia mɔkpɔkpɔ;

english_verse: that will never disappoint us. All of this happens because God has given us the Holy Spirit, who fills our hearts with his love.
translation_verse: ke mɔkpɔkpɔ menana ŋu kpea ame o, elabena wotrɔ Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃ la kɔ ɖe míaƒe dziwo me to Gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe, si wona mí la dzi.

english_verse: Christ died for us at a time when we were helpless and sinful.
translation_verse: Elabena Kristo gɔ̃ hã, esime míeganye gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔtɔwo la, eku ɖe ame mavɔ̃mawuwo ta le azãgbe, si woɖo ɖi la me.

english_verse: No one is really willing to die for an honest person, though someone might be willing to die for a truly good person.
translation_verse: Elabena bebli hafi amea ɖe aku ɖe ame dzɔdzɔea ɖe ta; ame nyui la, ɖewohĩ amea ɖe ado dzi aku ɖe eta.

english_verse: But God showed how much he loved us by having Christ die for us, even though we were sinful.
translation_verse: Ke Mawu ɖe ye ŋutɔ ƒe lɔlɔ̃, si wotsɔ lɔ̃ mí la fia bena, esime míeganye nuvɔ̃wɔlawo la, Kristo ku ɖe mía ta.

english_verse: But there is more! Now that God has accepted us because Christ sacrificed his life's blood, we will also be kept safe from God's anger.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, esi wotso afia na mí to eƒe ʋu me ŋuti la, woaxɔ mí geɖe awu tso dziku la me to eyama me.

english_verse: Even when we were God's enemies, he made peace with us, because his Son died for us. Yet something even greater than friendship is ours. Now that we are at peace with God, we will be saved by the life of his Son.
translation_verse: Elabena ne wolé avu le mia kple Mawu dome to Via ƒe ku me, esime míenye ketɔwo la, woaxɔ mi geɖe awu to eƒe agbe me, esime wolé avu na mi megbe la.

english_verse: And in addition to everything else, we are happy because God sent our Lord Jesus Christ to make peace with us. Adam and Christ
translation_verse: Ke menye esia ɖeɖekoe o, hafi míele adegbe ƒom le Mawu me hã to mia Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo dzi, amesi me miekpɔ avuléle le azɔ.

english_verse: Adam sinned, and that sin brought death into the world. Now everyone has sinned, and so everyone must die.
translation_verse: Esiaŋuti alesi to ame ɖeka dzi nuvɔ̃ la va xexeame, eye to nuvɔ̃ me ku la va, eye nenema ku la va to amewo katã dzi yi, esi wo katã wɔ nuvɔ̃ ŋuti la;

english_verse: Sin was in the world before the Law came. But no record of sin was kept, because there was no Law.
translation_verse: elabena vaseɖe sededeŋɔli ke nuvɔ̃ le xexeame, gake ne se meli o la, womebua nuvɔ̃ o;

english_verse: Yet death still had power over all who lived from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. This happened, though not everyone disobeyed a direct command from God, as Adam did. In some ways Adam is like Christ who came later.
translation_verse: gake ku la ɖu fia tso Adam dzi vaseɖe Mose dzi ɖe amesiwo mewɔ nuvɔ̃, si sɔ kple Adam ƒe dzidada o la dzi, amesi nye amesi gbɔna la ƒe kpɔɖeŋu la.

english_verse: But the gift of God's undeserved grace was very different from Adam's sin. That one sin brought death to many others. Yet in an even greater way, Jesus Christ alone brought God's gift of undeserved grace to many people.
