english_verse: Then the crowd shouted, “Praise the Lord! Smoke will never stop rising from her burning body.”
translation_verse: Eye wogagblɔ zi evelia bena: Mikafu Yehowa! Eye eƒe dzudzɔ le tutum le dziƒo yim tso mavɔ me yi ɖe mavɔ me.

english_verse: From the throne a voice said, “If you worship and fear our God, give praise to him, no matter who you are.”
translation_verse: Eye gbe ɖi tso fiazikpui la me le gbɔgblɔm bena: Mikafu mía Mawu, mi eƒe dɔlawo katã kple mi amesiwo vɔ̃nɛ, mí ɖeviwo kple ame tsitsiwo! Alẽvi la ƒe srɔ̃ɖeŋkekenyuieɖuɖu.

english_verse: Then I heard what seemed to be a large crowd that sounded like a roaring flood and loud thunder all mixed together. They were saying, “Praise the Lord! Our Lord God All-Powerful now rules as king.
translation_verse: Eye mese gbea ɖe le abe ameha gãa ɖe ƒe gbeɖiɖi ene, eye wòle abe tsi geɖewo ƒe gbeɖiɖi ene, eye wòle abe dziɖegbe sesẽwo ƒe gbeɖiɖi ene le gbɔgblɔm bena: Mikafu Yehowa! Elabena Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu, ŋusẽkatãtɔ la, le fia ɖum!

english_verse: So we will be glad and happy and give him praise. The wedding day of the Lamb is here, and his bride is ready.
translation_verse: Mina dzi nadzɔ mí, eye míatso aseye, eye mina miatsɔ ŋutikɔkɔe nɛ; elabena Alẽvi la ƒe srɔ̃ɖeŋkekenyuie la ɖo, eye srɔ̃a dzra eɖokui ɖo xoxo.

english_verse: She will be given a wedding dress made of pure and shining linen. This linen stands for the good things God's people have done.”
translation_verse: Eye wona ŋusẽe be, wòado aklalabiɖibiɖiwu dzadzɛ, si le dzo sim; elabena aklala biɖibiɖi la enye ame kɔkɔewo ƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔwo.

english_verse: Then the angel told me, “Put this in writing. God will bless everyone who is invited to the wedding feast of the Lamb.” The angel also said, “These things God has said are true.”
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nam bena: Ŋlɔ bena: Woayra amesiwo wokpe va Alẽvi la ƒe srɔ̃ɖenuɖuɖu la gbɔ! Eye wògagblɔ nam bena: Esiawo nye Mawu ƒe nya vavãwo.

english_verse: I knelt at the feet of the angel and began to worship him. But the angel said, “Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you and everyone else who tells about Jesus. Don't worship anyone but God. Everyone who tells about Jesus does it by the power of the Spirit.” The Rider on the White Horse
translation_verse: Eye medze klo ɖe eƒe afɔ nu, be made ta agu ne. Eye wògblɔ nam be: Kpɔ ɖa, megawɔe o, wò hadɔla kple nɔviwò, siwo lé Yesu ƒe ɖaseɖiɖi ɖe asi la, ƒe hadɔla menye; de ta agu na Mawu ko! Elabena Yesu ƒe ɖaseɖiɖi la enye nyagblɔɖigbɔgbɔ. Kristo ƒe dodo.

english_verse: I looked and saw heaven was open, and a white horse was there. Its rider was called Faithful and True, and he is always fair when he judges or goes to war.
translation_verse: Eye mekpɔ dziƒo le nuvo; eye kpɔ ɖa, mekpɔ sɔ ɣia ɖe, eye woyɔ amesi doe la be nuteƒewɔla kple nyateƒea, eye wòdrɔ̃a ʋɔnu, eye wòwɔa aʋa le dzɔdzɔenyenye me;

english_verse: He had eyes like flames of fire, and he was wearing a lot of crowns. His name was written on him, but he was the only one who knew what the name meant.
translation_verse: eye eƒe ŋkuwo le abe dzo ƒe aɖe ene, eye fiakuku geɖewo le eta, eye ŋkɔŋɔŋlɔ, si amea leke menya o, negbe eya ŋutɔ koe la, le eŋu;

english_verse: The rider wore a robe that was covered with blood, and he was known as “The Word of God.”
translation_verse: eye wòdo awua de, si ŋu wohlẽ ʋu do, eye woyɔ eƒe ŋkɔ be Mawu ƒe nya.

english_verse: He was followed by armies from heaven that rode on white horses and were dressed in pure white linen.
translation_verse: Eye aʋakɔ, siwo le dziƒo la, do sɔ ɣiwo dze eyome, eye wodo aklalabiɖibiɖiwu ɣi dzadzɛ, siwo le dzo sim.

english_verse: From his mouth a sharp sword went out to attack the nations. He will rule them with an iron rod and will show the fierce anger of God All-Powerful by trampling the grapes in the pit where wine is made.
translation_verse: Eye yi ɖaɖɛ do tso eƒe nu me, bena wòatsrɔ̃e adza dukɔwo, eye woatso gatikplɔ akplɔ wo, eye wòafanya weintsetsewo le Mawu, ŋusẽkatãtɔ la, ƒe dɔmedzoedziku ƒe weinfiãnu la me.

english_verse: On the part of the robe that covered his thigh was written, “KING OF KINGS AND Lord OF LordS.”
translation_verse: Eye ŋkɔŋɔŋlɔ le eƒe awu kple eƒe aligo dzi bena: Fiawo dzi Fia kple aƒetɔwo dzi Aƒetɔ! Lã la kple aʋatsonyagblɔlawo tsɔtsɔ ƒu gbe ɖe dzota la me.

english_verse: I then saw an angel standing on the sun, and he shouted to all the birds flying in the sky, “Come and join in God's great feast!
translation_verse: Eye mekpɔ mawudɔla ɖekaa ɖe le tsitre le ɣe me, eye wòdo ɣli kple gbe sesẽa ɖe le gbɔgblɔm na xevi, siwo katã dzona le dziƒo titina la bena: Miva ƒo mia ɖokui nu ƒu ɖe Mawu ƒe nuɖuɖu gã la gbɔ,

english_verse: You can eat the flesh of kings, rulers, leaders, horses, riders, free people, slaves, important people, and everyone else.”
translation_verse: bena miaɖu fiawo ƒe lã kple aʋafiawo ƒe lã kple ame sesẽwo ƒe lã kple sɔwo kple wo dzinɔlawo ƒe lã kple ablɔɖeviwo kple kluviwo kple ɖeviwo kpakple ame tsitsiwo katã ƒe lã.

english_verse: I also saw the beast and all kings of the earth come together. They fought against the rider on the white horse and against his army.
translation_verse: Eye mekpɔ lã la kple anyigba dzi fiawo kple woƒe aʋakɔwo ƒo wo ɖokui nu ƒu, be yewoawɔ aʋa kple amesi le sɔ dzi la kple eƒe aʋakɔ la.

english_verse: But the beast was captured and so was the false prophet. This is the same prophet who had worked miracles for the beast, so he could fool everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol. The beast and the false prophet were thrown alive into a lake of burning sulfur.
translation_verse: Eye wolé lã la kple aʋatsonyagblɔɖila, si wɔ dzesiwo le eƒe ŋku me, esiwo wotsɔ ble amesiwo xɔ lã la ƒe dzesi kple amesiwo de ta agu na eƒe legba; wotsɔ wo ame eve la siaa ƒu gbe ɖe dzota, si le bibim kple dzokpe la me agbagbe.

english_verse: But the rest of their army was killed by the sword that came from the mouth of the rider on the horse. Then birds stuffed themselves on the dead bodies.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ yi, si do tso amesi le sɔ dzi la ƒe nu me la, wu ame susɔeawo.

english_verse: I saw thrones, and sitting on those thrones were the ones who had been given the right to judge. I also saw the souls of the people who had their heads cut off because they had told about Jesus and preached God's message. They were the same ones who had not worshiped the beast or the idol, and they had refused to let its mark be put on their foreheads or hands. They will come to life and rule with Christ for
translation_verse: Eye mekpɔ fiazikpuiwo, eye wobɔbɔ no wo dzi, eye wotsɔ ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ de asi na wo; eye amesiwo nu wotso ta le le Yesu ƒe ɖaseɖiɖi kple Mawu ƒe nya la la la, ƒe luʋɔwo kple amesiwo mede ta agu na lã la alo eƒe legba o, eye womexɔ dzesi ɖe woƒe ŋgowonu alo ɖe woƒe asiwo ŋu o la, gbɔ agbe, eye woɖu fia kple Kristo ƒe akpe ɖeka.

english_verse: These people are the first to be raised to life, and they are especially blessed and holy. The second death has no power over them. They will be priests for God and Christ and will rule with them for
translation_verse: Yayratɔ kple kɔkɔetɔ enye amesi kpɔ gome le tsitretsitsi gbãtɔ la me; amesiawo dzi ku evelia mekpɔ ŋusẽa ɖeke ɖo o, ke woanye Mawu kple Kristo ƒe nunɔlawo, eye woaɖu fia kplii ƒe akpe ɖeka. Gog kple Magog.

english_verse: He will fool the countries of Gog and Magog, which are at the far ends of the earth, and their people will follow him into battle. They will have as many followers as there are grains of sand along the beach,
translation_verse: eye wòado go, be wòable dukɔ, siwo le anyigba ƒe dzogoe eneawo dzi, esiwo nye Gog kple Magog, be wòaƒo amesiwo ƒe xexlẽme nu le abe ƒutake ene la, nu ƒu hena aʋawɔwɔ.

english_verse: and they will march all the way across the earth. They will surround the camp of God's people and the city God loves. But fire will come down from heaven and destroy the whole army.
translation_verse: Eye woyi anyigba la ƒe gbadzaƒe, eye woɖe to ɖe ame kɔkɔewo ƒe asaɖa kple du lolo la ŋu, eye dzo hlẽ tso dziƒo va fiã wo.

english_verse: Then the devil who fooled them will be thrown into the lake of fire and burning sulfur. He will be there with the beast and the false prophet, and they will be in pain day and night forever and ever. The Judgment at the Great White Throne
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ Abosam, si ble wo la, ƒu gbe ɖe dzo- kple dzokpeta la me, afisi hã lã la kple aʋatsonyagblɔɖila la le, eye woawɔ fu wo zã kple keli tso mavɔ me yi ɖe mavɔ me. Nuwuwu ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃.

english_verse: I saw a great white throne with someone sitting on it. Earth and heaven tried to run away, but there was no place for them to go.
translation_verse: Eye mekpɔ fiazikpui ɣi gãa ɖe kple amesi bɔbɔ nɔ edzi, amesi ƒe ŋku me anyigba kple dziƒo si tso, eye womegakpɔ teƒea ɖeke na wo o.

english_verse: I also saw all the dead people standing in front of that throne. Every one of them was there, no matter who they had once been. Several books were opened, and then the book of life was opened. The dead were judged by what those books said they had done.
translation_verse: Eye mekpɔ ame kukuwo, ame tsitsiwo kple ɖeviwo, le tsitre ɖe fiazikpui la ŋgɔ, eye woʋu agbalẽwo; eye woʋu agbalẽ bubua ɖe, si nye agbegbalẽ; eye wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnu ame kukuawo ɖe nusiwo woŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽawo me le woƒe dɔwɔwɔwo ŋuti la nu.

english_verse: The sea gave up the dead people who were in it, and death and its kingdom also gave up their dead. Then everyone was judged by what they had done.
translation_verse: Eye atsiaƒu ɖe ame kuku, siwo le eme la, hena, eye ku kple tsieƒe woɖe ame kuku, siwo le wo si la, hena, eye wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnu amesiame ɖe eƒe dɔwɔwɔwo nu.

english_verse: Afterwards, death and its kingdom were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death.
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ ku kple tsiẽƒe ƒu gbe ɖe dzota la me. Dzota sia enye ku evelia.

english_verse: Anyone whose name wasn't written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.
translation_verse: Eye ne womekpɔ amea ɖe ƒe ŋkɔŋɔŋlɔ le agbegbalẽa me o la, wotsɔnɛ ƒua gbe ɖe dzota la me.

english_verse: I saw a new heaven and a new earth. The first heaven and the first earth had disappeared, and so had the sea.
translation_verse: Eye mekpɔ dziƒo yeye kple anyigba yeye; elabena gbã dziƒo kple gbã nyigba la nu va yi, eye atsiaƒu megali o.

english_verse: I heard a loud voice shout from the throne: God's home is now with his people. He will live with them, and they will be his own. Yes, God will make his home among his people.
translation_verse: Eye mese gbe gãa ɖe tso fiazikpui la gbɔ le gbɔgblɔm bena: Kpɔ ɖa, Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la le amewo gbɔ, eye wòanɔ anyi kpli wo, eye woawo hã woanye eƒe dukɔ, eye Mawu ŋutɔ anɔ anyi kpli wo, eye wòanye woƒe Mawu.

english_verse: He will wipe all tears from their eyes, and there will be no more death, suffering, crying, or pain. These things of the past are gone forever.
translation_verse: Eye Mawu latutu aɖatsi sia aɖatsi ɖa le woƒe ŋku mè, eye ku maganɔ anyi akpɔ o, eye konyifafa kple ɣlidodo kple vevea ɖeke maganɔ anyi o; elabena nu gbãtɔwo nu va yi.

english_verse: Then the one sitting on the throne said: I am making everything new. Write down what I have said. My words are true and can be trusted.
translation_verse: Eye amesi bɔbɔ nɔ fiazikpui dzi la, gblɔ bena: Kpɔ ɖa, mewɔ nuwo katã yeye! Eye wògblɔ be: Ŋlɔe, elabena nya siawo nye nya vavãwo kple nyateƒenyawo.

english_verse: Everything is finished! I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will freely give water from the life-giving fountain to everyone who is thirsty.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nam bena: Eva ve me! Nyee nye Alfa kple Omega, gɔmedzedze kple nuwuwu. Amesi ke tsikɔ le ewum la, mana agbetsidzidzi la ƒe ɖee faa.

english_verse: All who win the victory will be given these blessings. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
translation_verse: Amesi ke ɖu dzi la, anyi nusiawo ƒe dome, eye manye eƒe Mawu, eye eya hã anye vinye.

english_verse: But I will tell you what will happen to cowards and to everyone who is unfaithful or dirty-minded or who murders or is sexually immoral or uses witchcraft or worships idols or tells lies. They will be thrown into that lake of fire and burning sulfur. This is the second death. The New Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ke vɔvɔ̃nɔtɔwo kple dzimaxɔsetɔwo kple fewɔlawo kple hlɔ̃dolawo kple matrewɔlawo kple afakalawo kple trɔ̃subɔlawo kple aʋatsokalawo katã la woakpɔ wo tɔ gome le ta, si le bibim kple dzo kpakple dzokpe la me Esia enye ku evelia.

english_verse: I saw one of the seven angels who had the bowls filled with the seven last terrible troubles. The angel came to me and said, “Come on! I will show you the one who will be the bride and wife of the Lamb.”
translation_verse: Eye mawudɔla adre, siwo si kplu adre, siwo yɔ fũ kple fuwɔame mamletɔ adreawo nɔ la, dometɔ ɖeka va, eye wòƒo nu kplim gblɔ bena: Va abi, ne mafia ŋugbetɔ, si nye Alẽvi la srɔ̃ la wò!

english_verse: Then with the help of the Spirit, he took me to the top of a very high mountain. There he showed me the holy city of Jerusalem coming down from God in heaven.
translation_verse: Eye wòkplɔm yi to kɔkɔ gãa ɖe dzi le gbɔgbɔ me, eye woɖe du kɔkɔe, Yerusalem, si le ɖiɖim tso dziƒo tso Mawu gbɔ la liam,

english_verse: The glory of God made the city bright. It was dazzling and crystal clear like a precious jasper stone.
translation_verse: esi ŋu Mawu ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe le; eƒe keklẽ le abe kpe xɔasi ŋutɔa ɖe ene, hele abe yaspis-kpe, si me kɔ abe kristalo ene;

english_verse: The city had a high and thick wall with twelve gates, and each one of them was guarded by an angel. On each of the gates was written the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: gli kɔkɔ gãa ɖe le eŋu; agbo wuieve le eŋu, eye mawudɔla wuieve le agboawo tame, eye woŋlɔ ŋkɔ, siwo nye Israel-viwo ƒe to wuieveawo ƒe ŋkɔwo la, ɖe wo ŋuti.

english_verse: Three of these gates were on the east, three were on the north, three more were on the south, and the other three were on the west.
translation_verse: Ɣedzeƒe gome la agbo etɔ̃ li, eye anyiehe gome la agbo etɔ̃ li, dziehe gome la agbo etɔ̃ li, eye ɣetoɖoƒe gome la agbo etɔ̃ li.

english_verse: The city was built on twelve foundation stones. On each of the stones was written the name of one of the Lamb's twelve apostles.
translation_verse: Gɔmeɖoɖo wuieve li na dua ƒe gli la, eye Alẽvi la ƒe apostolo wuieveawo ƒe ŋkɔwo le wo ŋu.

english_verse: The angel who spoke to me had a gold measuring stick to measure the city and its gates and its walls.
translation_verse: Eye amesi le nu ƒom kplim la, lé sikadzidzeti ɖe asi, be yeadzidze du le kple eƒe agboawo kpakple eƒe gli la.

english_verse: The city was shaped like a cube, because it was just as high as it was wide. When the angel measured the city, it was about
translation_verse: Eye du la le dzogoe ene me, eye eƒe didime le abe eƒe kekeme ene; eye wòdzidze du la kple dzidzeti la, wòle stadio akpe wuieve: eƒe didime kple kekeme kple kɔkɔme wosɔ.

english_verse: Then the angel measured the wall, and by our measurements it was about
translation_verse: Eye wodzidze du la wòle abɔklugui alafa ɖeka kple blane vɔ ene le amewo ƒe dzidzenu, si le mawudɔla si la nu.

english_verse: The wall was built of jasper, and the city was made of pure gold, clear as crystal.
translation_verse: Eye nusi wotsɔ ɖo glia la, enye yaspis-kpe, eye du la nye sika dzadzɛ hele abe ahũhɔ̃e dzadzɛ ene.

english_verse: Each of the twelve foundations was a precious stone. The first was jasper, the second was sapphire, the third was agate, the fourth was emerald,
translation_verse: Eye wotsɔ kpe xɔasi bubu ƒomeviwo katã wɔ leke na dua ƒe gli la ƒe gɔmeɖoɖoawo. Gɔmeɖokpe gbãtɔ nye yaspis, evelia nye safir, etɔ̃lia nye xalkedon, enelia nye smaragd,

english_verse: the fifth was onyx, the sixth was carnelian, the seventh was chrysolite, the eighth was beryl, the ninth was topaz, the tenth was chrysoprase, the eleventh was jacinth, and the twelfth was amethyst.
translation_verse: atɔ̃lia nye sardonik, adelia nye sardis, adrelia nye krisolit, enyilia nye beril, asiekelia nye topas, ewolia nye krisopras, wuiɖekɛlia nye hiakint, wuievelia nye ametist.

english_verse: Each of the twelve gates was a solid pearl. The streets of the city were made of pure gold, clear as crystal.
translation_verse: Eye agbo wuieveawo nye adzagba wuieve, agboawo dome ɖesiaɖe nye adzagba ɖeka; eye dua ƒe ablɔ nye sika dzadzɛ abe ahũhɔ̃e, si me wokpɔa nu tonɛ la ene.

english_verse: I did not see a temple there. The Lord God All-Powerful and the Lamb were its temple.
translation_verse: Eye nyemekpo gbedoxɔa ɖeke le eme o; elabena Aƒetɔ, Mawu ŋusẽkatãtɔ, kple Alẽvi la wonye eƒe gbedoxɔ.

english_verse: And the city did not need the sun or the moon. The glory of God was shining on it, and the Lamb was its light.
translation_verse: Eye dua mehiã ɣe alo ɣleti, bene woaklẽ nɛ o; elabena Mawu ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe klẽna nɛ, eye Alẽvi la enye eƒe akaɖi.

english_verse: Nations will walk by the light of that city, and kings will bring their riches there.
translation_verse: Eye dukɔwo azɔ eƒe kekeli me, eye anyigba dzi fiawo atsɔ woƒe atsyɔ̃ ava emee.

english_verse: Its gates are always open during the day, and night never comes.
translation_verse: Eye womatu eƒe agbowo le ŋkeke me o; elabena zã mado le afima o,

english_verse: The glorious treasures of nations will be brought into the city.
translation_verse: eye woatsɔ dukɔwo ƒe atsyɔ̃ kple bubu ava emee.

english_verse: But nothing unworthy will be allowed to enter. No one who is dirty-minded or who tells lies will be there. Only those whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life will be in the city.
translation_verse: Eye nusianu, si nye nu makɔmakɔ kple amesiwo wɔa ŋunyɔnuwo, eye wokaa aʋatso la, womele yiyi ge ɖe eme o, negbe amesiwo woŋlɔ ɖe Alẽvi la ƒe agbegbalẽa me la koe.

english_verse: The angel showed me a river that was crystal clear, and its waters gave life. The river came from the throne where God and the Lamb were seated.
translation_verse: Eye wòfia agbetsitɔsisia ɖe, si le dzo sim abe kristalo ene, hele dodom tso Mawu kple Alẽvi la ƒe fiazikpui me le eƒe ablɔ la titina lam.

english_verse: Then it flowed down the middle of the city's main street. On each side of the river are trees that grow a different kind of fruit each month of the year. The fruit gives life, and the leaves are used as medicine to heal the nations.
translation_verse: Eye ɖe tɔsisi la ƒe goawo kple eve dzi la agbeti ti, si tsea ku wuieve, eye wotsena le ɣleti sia ɣleti, eye atiawo ƒe aŋgbawo nye dɔyɔgbe na dukɔwo.

english_verse: God's curse will no longer be on the people of that city. He and the Lamb will be seated there on their thrones, and its people will worship God
translation_verse: Eye busunua ɖeke megale anyi nɔ ge o, eye Mawu kple Alẽvi la ƒe fiazikpui la anɔ me, eye woƒe dɔlawo asubɔe,

english_verse: and will see him face to face. God's name will be written on the foreheads of the people.
translation_verse: eye woakpɔ eƒe ŋku me, eye eƒe ŋkɔ anɔ woƒe ŋgowonu.

english_verse: Never again will night appear, and no one who lives there will ever need a lamp or the sun. The Lord God will be their light, and they will rule forever. The Coming of Christ
translation_verse: Eye zã megale dodo ge o; eye womele akaɖi alo ɣe ƒe keklẽ hiã ge o; elabena Aƒetɔ Mawu ana keklẽ wo, eye woaɖu fia tso mavɔ me yi ɖe mavɔ me. Nuxɔxlɔ̃.

english_verse: Then I was told: These words are true and can be trusted. The Lord God controls the spirits of his prophets, and he is the one who sent his angel to show his servants what must happen very soon.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nam bena: Nya siawo nye nya vavãwo kple nyateƒenyawo, eye nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe gbɔgbɔwo ƒe Aƒetɔ, Mawu la, dɔ eƒe dɔla, bene wòaɖe nusiwo le eme va ge kpuie la, afia eƒe dɔlawo.

english_verse: Remember, I am coming soon! God will bless everyone who pays attention to the message of this book.
translation_verse: Eye kpɔ ɖa, megbɔna kpuie: Woayra amesiwo lé agbalẽ sia me nyagblɔɖinyawo me ɖe asi la.

english_verse: My name is John, and I am the one who heard and saw these things. Then after I had heard and seen all this, I knelt down and began to worship at the feet of the angel who had shown it to me.
translation_verse: Eye nye Yohanes ye nye amesi se nusiawo, eye mekpɔ wo. Eye esi mese wo, eye mekpɔ wo la, medze klo, be made ta agu ɖe mawudɔla, si ɖe nusiawo fiam la, ƒe afɔ nu.

english_verse: But the angel said, Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you. I am the same as a follower or a prophet or anyone else who obeys what is written in this book. God is the one you should worship.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nam bena: Kpɔ ɖa, megawɔe o, wò hadɔla kple nɔviwò, siwo nye nyagblɔɖilawo kple amesiwo lé agbalẽ sia me nyawo me ɖe asi la, ƒe hadɔla menye; de ta agu na Mawu ko!

english_verse: Don't keep the prophecies in this book a secret. These things will happen soon.
translation_verse: Eye wògblɔ nam bena Megade agbalẽ sia me nyagblɔɖinyawo nu o; elabena ɣeyiɣi la tu aƒe.

english_verse: Evil people will keep on being evil, and everyone who is dirty-minded will still be dirty-minded. But good people will keep on doing right, and God's people will always be holy.
translation_verse: Amesi ke wɔa vɔ̃ la, neno vɔ̃wɔwɔ dzi ko, eye amesi ke nye ɖime la, nenɔ ɖinuwɔwɔ la dzi ko; eye amesi ke nye ame dzɔdzɔe la, nena nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ la dzi ko, eye amesi ke le kɔkɔe la, nenɔ kɔkɔenyenye la dzi ko.

english_verse: Then I was told: I am coming soon! And when I come, I will reward everyone for what they have done.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, megbɔna kpuie, eye nye fetu kpe ɖe ŋutinye gbɔna, bene maɖo teƒe na amesiame ɖe alesi eƒe dɔwɔwɔ le la nu.

english_verse: I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
translation_verse: Nyee nye Alfa kple Omega, gbãtɔ kple mlɔetɔ, gɔmedzedze kple nuwuwu:

english_verse: God will bless all who have washed their robes. They will each have the right to eat fruit from the tree that gives life, and they can enter the gates of the city.
translation_verse: Woayra amesiwo nyẽ woƒe awuwo, bene woana ŋusẽ wo woava agbeti la gbɔ, eye ne woato agboawo nu ayi ɖe du la me.

english_verse: But outside the city will be dogs, witches, immoral people, murderers, idol worshipers, and everyone who loves to tell lies and do wrong.
translation_verse: Ke avũwo kple afakalawo kple matrewɔlawo kple hlɔ̃dolawo kple trɔ̃subɔlawo kpakple amesiame, si lɔ̃a aʋatsokaka, eye wòkanɛ la, woatsi agbo la godo.

english_verse: I am Jesus! And I am the one who sent my angel to tell all of you these things for the churches. I am David's Great Descendant, and I am also the bright morning star.
translation_verse: Nye Yesu ye nye amesi dɔ nye mawudɔla lã, bene wòaɖi ɖase le nusiawo ŋuti na mi hena hameawo. Nyee nye Dawid ƒe ke kple eƒe ƒome, ŋukeɣletivi keklẽ la.

english_verse: The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” Everyone who hears this should say, “Come!” If you are thirsty, come! If you want life-giving water, come and take it. It's free!
translation_verse: Eye Gbɔgbɔ la kple ŋugbetɔ la le gbɔgblɔm bena: Va! Eye amesi le esem la, negblɔ be: Va! Eye amesi tsikɔ le ewum la, neva; amesi lɔ̃ la, nèxɔ agbetsi la no faa. Nuwunyawo.

english_verse: Here is my warning for everyone who hears the prophecies in this book: If you add anything to them, God will make you suffer all the terrible troubles written in this book.
translation_verse: Mele ɖase ɖim na amesiame, si le agbalẽ sia me nyagblɔɖilawo sem la bena, ne amea ɖe tso nane kpe ɖe nya siawo ŋuti la, ekema Mawu atsɔ fuwɔame, siwo woŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽ sia me la akpe ɖe eŋuti nɛ,

english_verse: If you take anything away from these prophecies, God will not let you have part in the life-giving tree and in the holy city described in this book.
translation_verse: eye ne amea ɖe aɖe nane le agbalẽ sia me nyagblɔɖinyawo me la, ekema Mawu aɖe eƒe gome atso agbeti la kple du kɔkɔe, siwo woŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽ sia me la me.

english_verse: The one who has spoken these things says, “I am coming soon!” So, Lord Jesus, please come soon!
translation_verse: Amesi le nusiawo ƒe ɖase ɖim la gblɔ be: Ẽ, megbɔna kpuie! Amen, Aƒetɔ Yesu va!

english_verse: I pray that the Lord Jesus will be kind to all of you.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo ƒe amenuveve nanɔ anyi kple ame kɔkɔeawo katã! Amen.

english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Le gɔmedzedzea me, Mawu wɔ dziƒo kple anyigba.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: Anyigba nɔ nyama, nɔnɔme menɔe nɛ o; edzi ɖi gbɔlo, eye viviti do ɖe aʋli gã la dzi. Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ nɔ agba sam le tsi gbana la dzi.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Mawu gblɔ be: “Kekeli nedo!”, eye kekeli do.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: Mawu kpɔ be kekelia nyo, eye wòma kekeli kple viviti la dome.

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: Mawu yɔ kekelia be Ŋkeke, eye wòyɔ viviti la be Zã. Zã do, eye ŋu ke; eyae nye ŋkeke gbãtɔ.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Mawu gblɔ be: “Dziŋgɔli nedo ɖe tsia titina ne wòama tsia me, atso wo dome, eye wòva eme.”

english_verse: And that's what happened. God made the dome
translation_verse: Mawu wɔ dziŋgɔli la, eye wòma tsi si le dziŋgɔlia kple esi le etame la dome.

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Mawu yɔ dziŋgɔlia be Dziƒo. Zã do, eye ŋu ke; eyae nye ŋkeke evelia.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Mawu gblɔ be: “Tsi si le dziƒoa te la neƒo ƒu ɖe teƒe ɖeka ale be ƒuƒuiƒe nadze!” Esia va eme.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Mawu yɔ ƒuƒuiƒe la be Anyigba, ke tsi si ƒo ƒu la, eyɔe be Atsiaƒu. Mawu kpɔ be enyo.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to produce all kinds of plants, including fruit trees and grain.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Mawu gblɔ be: “Anyigba nemie nu miemie vovovowo: gbe siwo tsea ku kple ati tseku hamehame siwo ƒe kuwo nɔa tsetsea me la, ɖe sia ɖe kple etɔ le anyigba dzi”, eye wòva eme nenema.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Anyigba mie gbe fɛ̃wo: nu miemie siwo doa ku vovovowo tɔgbe kple ati siwo ƒe tsetsea me ku le wotɔxɛwotɔxɛe, eye Mawu kpɔ be enyo.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Ale zã do, eye ŋu ke; eyae nye ŋkeke etɔ̃lia.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Azɔ Mawu gblɔ be: “Nu keklẽwo nedo ɖe dziŋgɔlia ŋu le dziƒo ne woade vovototo ŋkeke kple zã dome. Woanye dzesiwo, eye woafia ɣeyiɣiwo, ŋkekewo kple ƒwo.

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Woanye nu keklẽwo le dziŋgɔlia ŋu be woana kekeli anyigba. Esia va eme.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Ale Mawu wɔ nu keklẽ gã eve. Ewɔ lolotɔ be eya naɖu ŋkeke dzi, eye wòwɔ suetɔ be wòaɖu zã dzi. Ewɔ ɣletiviwo hã.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: Mawu tsɔ wo ɖo dziŋgɔlia ŋu be woaklẽ ɖe anyigba dzi;

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: woaɖu ŋkeke kple zã dzi, eye woama kekeli kple viviti dome. Mawu kpɔ be enyo.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Zã do, eye ŋu ke; eyae nye ŋkeke enelia.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Mawu gblɔ be: “Tsia nedzi nu gbagbewo fũu, eye xewo nedzo le anyigba ƒe ya me to dziŋgɔli la ŋkume.

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Ale Mawu wɔ ƒumelã dziŋɔ lolowo kple nu gbagbe siwo katã tana, eye woʋãna le tsi me hamehame kpakple xe dzodzoewo katã. Mawu kpɔ be esia nyo.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Tete Mawu yra wo gblɔ be: “Ƒumelãwo nedzi, wonesɔ gbɔ, woneyɔ atsiaƒu la. Xewo nedzi asɔ gbɔ ɖe anyigba dzi!”

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Zã do, eye ŋu ke; eyae nye ŋkeke atɔ̃lia.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Azɔ Mawu gblɔ be: “Lãwo nedo hamehame tso anyigba me: aƒemelãwo, nu tatawo kple gbemelãwo.”

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Ale Mawu wɔ gbemelãwo, aƒemelãwo kple lã siwo katã tana le anyigba wotɔxɛwotɔxɛe. Mawu kpɔ be enyo.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Emegbe Mawu gblɔ be: “Mina ne míawɔ ame ɖe míaƒe nɔnɔme, eye wòaɖi mí, ne wòaɖu ƒumelãwo, xe dzodzoewo, aƒemelãwo kple gbemelãwo kpakple lã siwo katã tana le anyigba la dzi.”

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Ale Mawu wɔ ame ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe nɔnɔme. Mawu ƒe nɔnɔme nue wòwɔe ɖo. Ŋutsu kple nyɔnu wòwɔ.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: Mawu yra wo. Egblɔ na wo be: “Midzi ne miasɔ gbɔ ayɔ anyigba la dzi, eye miakpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe edzi. Miɖu ƒumelãwo kple xe dzodzoewo kpakple lã siwo katã zɔna le anyigba dzi la dzi.”

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: Ke gbewo kple amagbewo katã nanye nuɖuɖu na anyigba dzi lãwo, xe dzodzoewo kple nu gbagbe siwo katã tana le anyigba la.” Ale wòva eme nenema.

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Tete Mawu kpɔ nu siwo katã wòwɔ la, eye wòkpɔ be wonyo ŋutɔ. Zã do, eye ŋu ke; eyae nye ŋkeke adelia.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: Ale Mawu wɔ dziƒo kple anyigba kpakple nu gbogbo siwo katã le wo me la wu nu.

english_verse: By the seventh day God had finished his work, and so he rested.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke adrẽlia gbe la, Mawu wɔ eƒe dɔ wu nu, eye wòdzudzɔ eɖokui tso dɔ siwo katã wòwɔ la me.

english_verse: God blessed the seventh day and made it special, because on that day he rested from his work.
translation_verse: Ale Mawu yra ŋkeke adrẽlia, eye wòkɔ eŋuti, elabe esime wòwɔ eƒe dɔwo katã wu nu vɔ la, eya dzie wòdzudzɔ le. Eden-bɔ la

english_verse: That's how God created the heavens and the earth. The Garden of Eden When the Lord God made the heavens and the earth,
translation_verse: Dziƒo kple anyigba ƒe dzɔdzɔmenyawoe nye esiawo: Esi Aƒetɔ Mawu wɔ dziƒo kple anyigba la,

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: gbe alo ati aɖeke menɔ anyigba dzi o, eye nuku aɖeke hã memie ɖi o, elabe Aƒetɔ Mawu mena tsi dza o, eye gawu la, ame aɖeke mele anyigba dzi ade agble ɖe edzi o.

english_verse: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
translation_verse: Gake adzadza do tso anyigba la me, eye wònyɔ́ ɖe anyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ Mawu tsɔ anyi mè amegbetɔe. Egbɔ gbɔgbɔ si naa agbe la ɖe eƒe ŋɔti me, eye ame la zu ame gbagbe.

english_verse: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ Mawu tso abɔ ɖe Eden le ɣedzeƒe, eye wòtsɔ ame si wòmè la da ɖe eme.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ Mawu na ati vovovo siwo nyakpɔna kple esiwo ƒe kutsetse nyo na ɖuɖu la mie tso anyigba me. Ati si naa agbe kple ati si nana be wodzea si nyui kple vɔ̃ la le abɔ la titina.

english_verse: From Eden a river flowed out to water the garden, then it divided into four rivers.
translation_verse: Tɔsisi aɖe sí tso Eden va de tsi abɔ la. Esi wòto abɔa me vɔ la, edze ɖe ene.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: Alɔdze gbãtɔ ŋkɔe nye Pison. Esí to Xavila-nyigba blibo la dzi, afi si sika le.

english_verse: where pure gold, rare perfumes, and precious stones are found.
translation_verse: Sika si le anyigba ma dzi la nyo ŋutɔ; belodax kple oniks kpewo le afi ma.

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Alɔdze evelia ŋkɔe nye Gixon. Eyae tsa to Nubia-nyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Tɔsisia ƒe alɔdze etɔ̃lia ŋkɔe nye Xidekel. Eya sí to Asiria ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome. Tɔsisia ƒe alɔdze enelia ŋkɔe nye Frat.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Aƒetɔ Mawu tsɔ ame la ɖo Eden-bɔa me be wòaŋlɔ eme, akpɔ edzi.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Àte ŋu aɖu ati siwo le abɔa me la dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ƒe tsetsea faa.

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: Ke mègaɖu ati si nana be wodzea si nyui kple vɔ̃ ƒe tsetse la ya gbeɖe o; gbe si gbe nàɖui la, àku godoo.” Mawu mè lãwo, eye wòwɔ nyɔnu

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Aƒetɔ Mawu gblɔ be: “Menyo be ame la ɖeɖe nanɔ anyi o; mawɔ kpeɖeŋutɔ si asɔ nɛ la nɛ.”

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ Mawu na ŋutsu la dɔ alɔ̃ yi eme ʋĩi. Eɖe eƒe agbaƒuti ɖeka, eye wòtsɔ lã ɖo eteƒe.

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ tsɔ agbaƒuti la wɔ nyɔnu, eye wòkplɔe va ŋutsu la gbɔe.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu la gblɔ be: “Ehɛ̃, azɔ ko! Ame sia ƒe ƒu tso nye ŋutɔ nye ƒu me, eƒe lã tso nye ŋutɔ nye lã me. Woayɔ eya be nyɔnu, elabe ŋutsu mee woɖee tsoe.”

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: Esia tae ŋutsu gblẽa tɔ́a kple nɔa ɖi, léna ɖe srɔ̃a ŋu, eye wo kple evea wozua ame ɖeka.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Ŋutsua kple srɔ̃a le amama, ke ŋu mekpea wo o.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Azɔ la, da dze aye wu gbemelã siwo katã Aƒetɔ Mawu wɔ la. Ebia nyɔnua be: “Nyateƒe wònye be Mawu gblɔ be: ‘Migaɖu abɔmetiawo ƒe ɖeke o’ a?”

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Nyɔnua ɖo eŋu na da la be: “Woɖe mɔ be míɖu ati siwo le abɔa me la dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ƒe tsetse.

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: Ke ati si le abɔa titina ya la, Mawu de se be: ‘Migaɖu eƒe tsetsea gbeɖegbeɖe o; migaka asi eŋu gɔ̃ hã o. Ne miewɔe la, miaku.’ ”

english_verse: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
translation_verse: Ke da ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Miele kuku ge o.

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: Elabe Mawu nya be ne mieɖui la, miaƒe ŋkuwo aʋu, eye mianɔ abe ye Mawu ene, anya nyui kple vɔ̃.”

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Esi nyɔnua kpɔ be atia nyo na ɖuɖu, eƒe tsetsea nyakpɔ na ŋku, eye wòdzroa ame be wòaɖui adze nunya la, egbe eƒe tsetsea ƒe ɖe ɖu, eye wòtsɔ ɖe na srɔ̃a si nɔ egbɔ la hã wòɖu.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: Tete wo kple evea ƒe ŋkuwo ʋu, eye wokpɔ be yewole amama. Ale wotɔ aŋgbawo hesa ɖe ali.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Esi anyinu fa miaa la, ŋutsua kple srɔ̃a wose Aƒetɔ Mawu ŋkɔ wòle zɔzɔm le abɔa me. Ale wosí le Aƒetɔ Mawu nu ɖabè ɖe atiwo dome le abɔa me.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ Mawu yɔ Adam, eye wòbiae be: “Afi ka nèle?”

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu be: “Mese ŋkɔwò le abɔa me, eye mevɔ̃, elabe mele amama ale meyi ɖabè.”

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Mawu biae be: “Ame kae gblɔ na wò be amama nèle? Alo ɖe nèɖu ati si ƒe tsetsea mede se na wò be mègaɖu o laa?”

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Adam ɖo eŋu be: “Nyɔnu si nèda ɖe gbɔnye lae tsɔ atia ƒe tsetsea nam meɖu.”

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu bia nyɔnua be: “Nu kae nye esi nèwɔ?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Dae blem meɖui.” Mawu ƒe tohehe

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu gblɔ na da la be: “Le nu si nèwɔ ta la, woƒo fi de wò le aƒemelãwo kple gbemelãwo katã dome. Ƒodo dzi nàta le, eye ʋuʋudedie nàɖu le wò agbe me ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Made adika wò kple nyɔnua dome, eye eƒe dzidzimeviwo kple wò dzidzimeviwo hã anɔ kè me. Agbã ta na wò, eye wò hã àɖu afɔkpodzi nɛ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ na nyɔnua be: “Madzi wò fufɔfɔ me fukpekpewo ɖe edzi, eye àse veve helihelĩ le wò kuléle me hafi adzi vi. Ke wò didi anɔ srɔ̃wò ŋu, eye eya aɖu gã ɖe dziwò.”

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Adam be: “Esi nèse srɔ̃wò ƒe gbe, eye nèɖu ati si ƒe tsetsea mede se na wò be mègaɖu o ta la, woaƒo fi ade anyigba le tawò. Àkpe fu hafi akpɔ nu aɖu tso edzi le wò agbenɔɣi blibo la katã.

english_verse: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
translation_verse: Anyigba amie ŋu kple aŋɔka na wò, eye agble me amagbewo nàɖu.

english_verse: You will sweat all your life to earn a living; you were made out of soil, and you will once again turn into soil.”
translation_verse: Fifia ate wò hafi nàkpɔ nu aɖu. Ànɔ esia dzi ʋuu va se ɖe esime nàgatrɔ yi anyigba me elabe eya me woɖe wò tsoe. Anyie nènye, eye anyi ke nàgatrɔ azu!”

english_verse: The man Adam named his wife Eve because she would become the mother of all who live.
translation_verse: Adam yɔ srɔ̃a be Xawa elabe eyae nye amegbetɔwo katã nɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu tsɔ lãgbalẽ tɔ awu do na Adam kple srɔ̃a. Mawu nyà Adam kple Xawa do go le abɔ la me

english_verse: The Lord said, “They now know the difference between right and wrong, just as we do. But they must not be allowed to eat fruit from the tree that lets them live forever.”
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Aƒetɔ Mawu gblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, azɔ ame la zu abe míawo ke ene, eye wònya nyui kple vɔ̃. Ɖewohĩ ava do asi ɖa agbe ati si naa agbe la ƒe tsetsea hã aɖu ava tsi agbe tegbee.”

english_verse: So the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden, where they would have to work the ground from which the man had been made.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ Mawu nyà ame la do goe le Eden-bɔ la me be wòayi aɖaŋlɔ anyigba si ƒe anyi wotsɔ mee la.

english_verse: Then God put winged creatures at the entrance to the garden and a flaming, flashing sword to guard the way to the life-giving tree.
translation_verse: Esi wònyà ame la do goe la, etsɔ kerubiwo kple yi si le dzo dam mlamlamla, eye wòtroa eɖokui ɖo ɖe akpa sia akpa la, da ɖe Eden-bɔ la ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome. Ewɔ esia be woadzɔ mɔ si yi agbetia gbɔ la nu.

english_verse: Adam and Eve had a son. Then Eve said, “I'll name him Cain because I got him with the help of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Adam dɔ kple srɔ̃a Xawa, eye wòfɔ fu dzi Kain. Xawa gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ ɖi nam be medzi ŋutsu.”

english_verse: Later she had another son and named him Abel. Abel became a sheep farmer, but Cain farmed the land.
translation_verse: Emegbe edzi Abel, nɔvia ŋutsu. Abel va zu lãnyila, eye Kain ya zu agbledela.

english_verse: One day, Cain gave part of his harvest to the Lord,
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la, Kain tsɔ nuku si wòŋe tso eƒe agble me la ƒe ɖe va sa vɔe na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: and Abel also gave an offering to the Lord. He killed the first-born lamb from one of his sheep and gave the Lord the best parts of it. The Lord was pleased with Abel and his offering,
translation_verse: Abel hã tsɔ eƒe lãwo ƒe ŋgɔgbevi siwo da ami la va sa vɔe na Aƒetɔ. Aƒetɔ kpɔ ŋudzedze le Abel kple eƒe nunana la ŋu,

english_verse: but not with Cain and his offering. This made Cain so angry that he could not hide his feelings.
translation_verse: ke Kain kple eƒe nunanaa ya medze eŋu o. Ale Kain bi dzi ŋutɔ, eye wòɖo adã.

english_verse: The Lord said to Cain: What's wrong with you? Why do you look so angry?
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Kain be: “Nu ka ta nèbi dzi, heɖo adã nenema?

english_verse: If you had done the right thing, you would be smiling. But you did the wrong thing, and now sin is waiting to attack you like a lion. Sin wants to destroy you, but don't let it!
translation_verse: Ne èwɔ nyui la, ɖe womakpɔ ŋudzedze le ŋuwò oa? Evɔ ne mèwɔ nyui o la, nuvɔ̃ de xa ɖe wò ʋɔtru nu. Edi be yeaɖu dziwò, ke wò la, ele be nàɖu edzi.”

english_verse: Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let's go for a walk.” And when they were out in a field, Cain attacked and killed him.
translation_verse: Ke Kain gblɔ na nɔvia Abel be: “Va míyi agble.” Esi woyi la, Kain trɔ ɖe nɔvia ŋu, eye wòwui.

english_verse: Afterwards the Lord asked Cain, “Where is Abel?” “How should I know?” he answered. “Am I supposed to look after my brother?”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ bia Kain be: “Nɔviwò Abel ɖe?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Nyemenya o. Nɔvinye dzikpɔla menyea?”

english_verse: Then the Lord said: Why have you done this terrible thing? You killed your own brother, and his blood flowed onto the ground. Now his blood is calling out for me to punish you.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Nu kae nye esi nèwɔ? Kpɔ ɖa, nɔviwò ƒe ʋu le ɣli dom le anyigba dzi le yɔyem.

english_verse: And so, I'll put you under a curse. Because you killed Abel and made his blood run out on the ground, you will never be able to farm it again.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la, woƒo fi de wò wu anyigba si ke nu, no nɔviwò ƒe ʋu si nèkɔ ɖe edzi la.

english_verse: When you try to farm the land, it won't produce anything for you. From now on, you'll be without a home, and you'll spend the rest of your life wandering from place to place.
translation_verse: Ne ède agble ɖe anyigba dzi la, magawɔ nu na wò nyuie o. Tsatsala kple sitsoƒedila ko nye ge nàla le anyigba dzi.”

english_verse: “This punishment is too hard!” Cain said.
translation_verse: Kain gblɔ na Aƒetɔ be: “Nye tohehe la wu tsɔtsɔ nam.

english_verse: “You're making me leave my home and live far from you. I will have to wander about without a home, and just anyone could kill me.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ènyàm ɖa tso agbledenyigba dzi egbe, eye wòle nam be mabu ɖa le ŋkuta na wò. Mazu sisíla kple tsatsala le anyigba dzi, eye ame sia ame si do gom ko la, awum.”

english_verse: “No!” the Lord answered. “Anyone who kills you will be punished seven times worse than I am punishing you.” So the Lord put a mark on Cain to warn everyone not to kill him.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Mele nenema o. Ame sia ame si wu Kain la, woabia hlɔ̃e zigbɔzi adrẽ.” Ale Aƒetɔ de dzesi tɔxɛ Kain ŋu be, ne ame aɖe kpɔe la, mawui o.

english_verse: But Cain had to go far from the Lord and live in the Land of Wandering, which is east of Eden. More and More People
translation_verse: Kain dzo le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, eye wòyi ɖanɔ Nod-nyigba dzi le Eden ƒe ɣedzeƒe. Kain ƒe dzidzimeviwo

english_verse: Later, Cain and his wife had a son named Enoch. At the time Cain was building a town, and so he named it Enoch after his son.
translation_verse: Esia megbe Kain dɔ kple srɔ̃a, eye wòfɔ fu dzi Henox. Etso du, eye wòtsɔ via ƒe ŋkɔ, Henox, na dua hã.

english_verse: Then Enoch had a son named Irad, who had a son named Mehujael, who had a son named Methushael, who had a son named Lamech.
translation_verse: Henox dzi viŋutsu si ŋkɔe nye Irad. Eya dzi Mehuyael. Mehuyael dzi Metusael, eye Metusael dzi Lamex.

english_verse: Lamech and Zillah had a son named Tubal Cain who made tools out of bronze and iron. They also had a daughter, whose name was Naamah.
translation_verse: Lamex srɔ̃ evelia, Zila, dzi Tubalkain, si tsɔa akɔbli kple ga yibɔ tua nu vovovowoe. Tubalkain nɔvinyɔnu ŋkɔe nye Naama.

english_verse: One day, Lamech said to his two wives, “A young man wounded me, and I killed him.
translation_verse: Lamex gblɔ na srɔ̃awo be: “Ada kple Zila, mise ɖa, mi Lamex srɔ̃wo, miɖo to miase nya si gblɔ ge mele. Mewu ŋutsu aɖe elabe ede abi ŋunye. Mewu ɖekakpui aɖe elabe eƒom.

english_verse: Anyone who tries to get even with me will be punished ten times more than anyone who tries to get even with Cain.”
translation_verse: Ne wobia hlɔ̃ Kain wula, zigbɔzi adrẽ la, le nyateƒe me la, woabia hlɔ̃ Lamex zi bla adrẽ vɔ adrẽ.” Set kple Enos dzidzi

english_verse: Adam and his wife had another son. They named him Seth, because they said, “God has given us a son to take the place of Abel, who was killed by his brother Cain.”
translation_verse: Adam gadɔ kple srɔ̃a, eye wòdzi viŋutsu. Srɔ̃a gblɔ be: “Mawu na medzi vi bubu ɖe Abel, ame si Kain wu la, teƒe.” Ale wòtsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Set.

english_verse: Later, Seth had a son and named him Enosh. About this time people started worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Wodzi viŋutsu na Set hã, eye wòtsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Enos. Ɣe ma ɣi mee amewo dze gbedodoɖa gɔme na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Ale Adam nɔ agbe ƒe alafa asieke bla etɔ̃ hafi ku.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Enɔ agbe ƒe alafa asieke kple wui eve hafi ku.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Ale Enos nɔ agbe ƒe alafa asieke kple atɔ̃ hafi ku.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Ale Kenan nɔ agbe ƒe alafa asieke kple ewo hafi ku.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Ale Yared xɔ ƒe alafa enyi bla asieke vɔ atɔ̃ hafi ku.

english_verse: and God took him away at the age of
translation_verse: Henox nɔ hadede me kple Mawu le eƒe agbenɔɣi, ale be ɖeko wòbu vĩ elabe Mawu kplɔe dzoe.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Metusala nɔ agbe ƒe alafa asieke bla ade vɔ asieke hafi ku.

english_verse: Lamech said, “I'll name him Noah because he will give us comfort, as we struggle hard to make a living on this land that the Lord has put under a curse.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: “Ɖevi sia ana gbɔdzɔe mí tso míaƒe dɔwɔwɔ kple dagbadagba si Aƒetɔ ƒe fi si wòƒo de anyigba la he vɛ me.” Ale wòtsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Noa.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Lamex nɔ agbe ƒe alafa adrẽ bla adrẽ vɔ adrẽ hafi ku.

english_verse: More and more people were born, until finally they spread all over the earth. Some of their daughters were so beautiful that supernatural beings came down and married the ones they wanted.
translation_verse: amegbetɔ vinyɔnuawo nyakpɔ na Mawu viŋutsuwo ŋutɔ, eya ta wova ɖe wo dometɔ siwo dze wo ŋu la.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “I won't let my life-giving breath remain in anyone forever. No one will live for more than
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ be: “Esi amegbetɔ nye ŋutilã kple vodala ta la, nyemagana nye gbɔgbɔ nanɔ eme ɖaa o. Mana wòanɔ agbe ƒe alafa ɖeka bla eve ko.”

english_verse: The children of the supernatural beings who had married these women became famous heroes and warriors. They were called Nephilim and lived on the earth at that time and even later.
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi me kple emegbe gɔ̃ hã la, ame dzɔtsu kakowo nɔ anyigba dzi. Mawu viŋutsuwo ɖe amegbetɔ vinyɔnuwo, eye wodzi viwo na wo. Woawoe nye aʋawɔla xɔŋkɔ siwo nɔ anyi le blema la.

english_verse: The Lord saw how bad the people on earth were and that everything they thought and planned was evil.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ kpɔ be amegbetɔ va vɔ̃ɖi ŋutɔ le anyigba dzi, eye eƒe tamesusu kple dzimedidiwo nye vɔ̃ ɖaa.

english_verse: He was sorry that he had made them,
translation_verse: Eve Aƒetɔ, eye wòɖu dzi nɛ be yewɔ ame ɖe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: and he said, “I'm going to destroy every person on earth! I'll even wipe out animals, birds, and reptiles. I'm sorry I ever made them.”
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ gblɔ be: “Evem be mewɔ amegbetɔ ɖe anyigba dzi. Matsrɔ̃ ame ɖa. Matsrɔ̃ lã, nu tata kple xe ɖe sia ɖe hã ɖa.”

english_verse: But the Lord was pleased with Noah,
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ ve Noa nu. Noa

english_verse: and this is the story about him. Noah was the only person who lived right and obeyed God.
translation_verse: Noa ƒe dzidzimeviwo ŋu nya nye esi: Noa nye ame dzɔdzɔe kple ame maɖifɔ le eŋɔli me tɔwo dome. Kadodo nyui nɔ eya kple Mawu dome.

english_verse: He had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
translation_verse: Viŋutsu etɔ̃ nɔ Noa si. Woawoe nye Sem, Xam kple Yafet.

english_verse: God knew that everyone was terribly cruel and violent.
translation_verse: Mawu kpɔ be xexea me gblẽ keŋ, elabe ame sia ame nɔ nu vlo wɔm le anyigba dzi.

english_verse: Get some good lumber and build a boat. Put rooms in it and cover it with tar inside and out.
translation_verse: Tsɔ ati sesẽ nàkpa aɖakaʋu na ɖokuiwò. Nàma eme ɖe akpa vovovo me, eye nàtsɔ aŋɔ atre eme kple egodo nyuie.

english_verse: Noah did everything God told him to do.
translation_verse: Noa wɔ nu sia nu abe ale si Mawu gblɔ nɛ be newɔ la ene pɛpɛpɛ.

english_verse: I'm going to send a flood that will destroy everything that breathes! Nothing will be left alive.
translation_verse: Wɔ esia elabe mele nana ge tsi naɖɔ, aɖe anyigba keŋ, ne nu sia nu si me agbegbɔgbɔ le le xexe blibo la katã me la natsrɔ̃. Mana anyigbadzinuwo katã naku.

english_verse: But I solemnly promise that you, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law will be kept safe in the boat.
translation_verse: Ke mabla nu kple wò ya. Mana nàyi aɖakaʋu la me kple viwò ŋutsuwo, srɔ̃wò kpakple viwò ŋutsuawo srɔ̃wo hã.

english_verse: Take into the boat with you a male and a female of every kind of animal and bird, as well as a male and a female of every reptile. I don't want them to be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ɖe xewo ɖe woƒe ƒomewo nu, lãwo ɖe woƒe ƒomewo nu kple nu ɖe sia ɖe si tana le anyigba la, ɖe eƒe ƒome nu eveveve, woava gbɔwò ne woatsi agbe.

english_verse: Store up enough food both for yourself and for them.
translation_verse: Tsɔ nuɖuɖu ɖe sia ɖe ɖe asi, nàdzra ɖo ɖe gbɔwò na wò ŋutɔ kple lãawo.”

english_verse: The Lord told Noah: Take your whole family with you into the boat, because you are the only one on this earth who pleases me.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Noa be: “Wò kple aƒewòmetɔwo katã miyi ɖe aɖakaʋu la me, elabe mekpɔ be ame dzɔdzɔe nènye le dzidzime sia me.

english_verse: Take seven pairs of every kind of animal that can be used for sacrifice and one pair of all others.
translation_verse: Kplɔ lã siwo katã woɖuna la, atsu kple asi, adrẽadrẽ kple lã siwo womeɖuna o la, atsu kple asi eveveve, de aɖakaʋu la me.

english_verse: Also take seven pairs of every kind of bird with you. Do this so there will always be animals and birds on the earth.
translation_verse: Kplɔ xe ƒomevi vovovo ɖe sia ɖe, atsua kple nɔea, adrẽadrẽ hã de eme. Wɔ esia bene lã kple xe ƒomevi ɖe sia ɖe natsi agbe le anyigba dzi, agadzi.

english_verse: He obeyed God and took a male and a female of each kind of animal and bird into the boat with him.
translation_verse: eveveve atsua kple nɔea, woge ɖe aɖakaʋu la me kple Noa.

english_verse: Seven days later a flood began to cover the earth.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke adrẽ megbe la, tsiɖɔɖɔ la dze egɔme le anyigba dzi.

english_verse: The water under the earth started gushing out everywhere, the sky opened like windows, and rain poured down for
translation_verse: Ale tsi de asi dzadza me madzudzɔmadzudzɔe, ŋkeke bla ene zã bla ene sɔŋ.

english_verse: On that day Noah and his wife went into the boat with their three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe tututue Noa kple srɔ̃a kpakple wo viŋutsu etɔ̃awo: Sem, Xam kple Yafet, kpakple woawo hã wo srɔ̃ etɔ̃awo ge ɖe aɖakaʋu la me.

english_verse: They took along every kind of animal, tame and wild, including the birds.
translation_verse: Gbemelã, aƒemelã, nu tata kple xe ƒomevi vovovowo kpakple nu siwo dzona la katã hã kpe ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: Noah took a male and a female of every living creature with him,
translation_verse: Woge ɖe aɖakaʋu la me eveveve kple Noa, nu gbagbe siwo katã me agbe le la.

english_verse: just as God had told him to do. And when they were all in the boat, the Lord closed the door.
translation_verse: Lã siawo katã, atsua kple nɔea, woge ɖe aɖakaʋu la me kple Noa, abe ale si Mawu gblɔ nɛ ene, eye Aƒetɔ tu ʋɔa ɖe enu.

english_verse: Finally, the mighty flood was so deep that even the highest mountain peaks were about seven meters below the surface of the water.
translation_verse: Ke ɖɔɖɔ dzi ko wògale va se ɖe esime wògbɔ to kɔkɔwo tame, wobu ɖe eme meta adrẽ sɔŋ.

english_verse: Not a bird, animal, reptile, or human was left alive anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Nu gbagbe ɖe sia ɖe, eɖanye xe o, aƒemelã o, gbemelã o, nu tata o, amegbetɔ o, wo katã wotsrɔ̃ keŋ.

english_verse: The Lord destroyed everything that breathed. Nothing was left alive except Noah and the others in the boat.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ tsrɔ̃ nu gbagbewo katã le anyigba dzi; amegbetɔ, lã kple xe, ɖeke medo le eme o, negbe Noa kple aɖakaʋua me nɔlawo ɖeɖe ko.

english_verse: A hundred fifty days later, the water started going down.
translation_verse: Tsi la ɖɔ ɖe anyigba dzi ŋkeke alafa ɖeka bla atɔ̃.

english_verse: God did not forget about Noah and the animals with him in the boat. So God made a wind blow, and the water started going down.
translation_verse: Mawu meŋlɔ Noa kple gbemelã kpakple aƒemelã siwo katã le egbɔ le aɖakaʋua me la be o. Ena ya ƒo to anyigba dzi, eye tsia de asi miemie me.

english_verse: God stopped up the places where the water had been gushing out from under the earth. He also closed up the sky, and the rain stopped.
translation_verse: Tsi siwo nɔ dzidzim tso anyigba tume la nu tso, dziƒo nu tu, eye tsi la ke.

english_verse: Then on the seventeenth day of the seventh month of the year, the boat came to rest somewhere in the Ararat mountains.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti adrẽlia ƒe ŋkeke wui adrẽa gbe la, aɖakaʋu la va tɔ ɖe to aɖe tame le Ararat-to tame.

english_verse: The water kept going down, and the mountain tops could be seen on the first day of the tenth month.
translation_verse: Tsia nɔ miemiem vivivi va se ɖe ɣleti ewolia me. Le ɣleti ewolia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ gbe la, towo tame dzé.

english_verse: Forty days later Noah opened a window to send out a raven, but it kept flying around until the water had dried up.
translation_verse: eye wòna akpavia aɖe do yi. Eɖanɔ tsatsam va se ɖe esime tsia mie vɔ le anyigba dzi keŋ.

english_verse: Noah wanted to find out if the water had gone down, so he sent out a dove.
translation_verse: Noa ʋu nu le ahɔnɛ aɖe hã nu do ɖa be yeakpɔ ɖa be tsia mie vɔ le anyigba dzi mahã.

english_verse: Deep water was still everywhere, and when the dove could not find a place to land, it flew back to the boat. Then Noah held out his hand and helped it back in.
translation_verse: Akpakpa la mekpɔ teƒe aɖeke adze ɖo o, elabe tsi gale anyigba blibo la dzi ko, eye wòtrɔ va ʋua gbɔ. Noa do asi ɖa lée va eme.

english_verse: Seven days later Noah sent the dove out again.
translation_verse: Elala ŋkeke adrẽ, eye wògaɖo ahɔnɛ la ɖa.

english_verse: It returned in the evening, holding in its beak a green leaf from an olive tree. Noah knew the water was finally going down.
translation_verse: Tete ahɔnɛ la trɔ va egbɔ le fiẽ me, eye kpɔ ɖa, elé amitiŋgba fɛ̃ si wògbe la ɖe nu. Ale Noa dze sii be tsia mie le anyigba dzi azɔ.

english_verse: He waited seven more days before sending the dove out again, and this time it did not return.
translation_verse: Egalala ŋkeke adrẽ bubu, eye wògaɖo ahɔnɛ la ɖa; ke esi wòyi la, megatrɔ gbɔ o.

english_verse: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was completely dry.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti evelia ƒe ŋkeke bla eve vɔ adrẽlia gbe la, anyigba ƒu keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: God said to Noah,
translation_verse: Mawu gblɔ na Noa be:

english_verse: “You, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law may now leave the boat.
translation_verse: “Wò ŋutɔ, srɔ̃wò, viwò ŋutsuawo kple wo srɔ̃wo, mi katã mido le aɖakaʋua me.

english_verse: Let out the birds, animals, and reptiles, so they can mate and live all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Ɖe nu gbagbe siwo katã le gbɔwò: xewo, lãwo kple nu sia nu si tana le anyigba, do goe; be woadzi asɔ gbɔ ɖe anyigba la dzi.”

english_verse: After Noah and his family had left the boat,
translation_verse: Ale Noa kple srɔ̃a kple via ŋutsuawo kpakple wo srɔ̃awo do le ʋua me.

english_verse: the living creatures left in groups of their own kind. The Lord's Promise for the Earth
translation_verse: Nenema ke nu vovovo siwo katã ʋãna le anyigba dzi: lãwo, nu tatawo kple xewo katã hã do, wo ƒome wo ƒome, tso aɖakaʋua me. Noa sa vɔ na Mawu

english_verse: Noah built an altar where he could offer sacrifices to the Lord. Then he offered on the altar one of each kind of animal and bird that could be used for a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Tete Noa ɖi vɔsamlekpui na Aƒetɔ. Eɖe lã ɖuɖua ɖe sia ɖe kple xe ɖuɖua ɖe sia ɖe ƒe ɖe tsɔ wɔ numemevɔsa le vɔsamlekpui la dzi.

english_verse: The smell of the burning offering pleased the Lord, and he said: Never again will I punish the earth for the sinful things its people do. All of them have evil thoughts from the time they are young, but I will never destroy everything that breathes, as I did this time.
translation_verse: Esi Aƒetɔ se numeme la ƒe ʋeʋẽ lílili la, edze eŋu. Egblɔ le eɖokui me be: “Nyemagaxa ɖe amegbetɔ ƒe nuwɔna ta aƒo fi ade anyigba gbeɖe o. Menya be tso eƒe ɖevime ke la, vɔ̃ ko wòsusuna le eɖokui me. Nyemagatsrɔ̃ nu gbagbewo katã, abe ale si mewɔ ene akpɔ gbeɖe o.

english_verse: As long as the earth remains, there will be planting and harvest, cold and heat; winter and summer, day and night.
translation_verse: Zi ale si anyigba li ko la, nuƒãɣi kple nuŋeɣi, fafa kple dzoxɔxɔ, dzomeŋɔli kple vuvɔŋɔli, ŋkeke kple zã, nu matsi akpɔ gbeɖe o.”

english_verse: God said to Noah and his sons: I am giving you my blessing. Have a lot of children and grandchildren, so people will live everywhere on this earth.
translation_verse: Mawu yra Noa kple via ŋutsuawo gblɔ na wo be: “Midzi ne miasɔ gbɔ ayɔ anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: All animals, birds, reptiles, and fish will be afraid of you. I have placed them under your control,
translation_verse: Gbemelãwo, xewo, nu tatawo kple ƒumelãwo katã avɔ̃ mi, eye miadzi ŋɔ na wo. Metsɔ wo de asi na mi.

english_verse: and I have given them to you for food. From now on, you may eat them, as well as the green plants that you have always eaten.
translation_verse: Nu sia nu si le agbe ʋãna la nanye nuɖuɖu na mi; abe ale si metsɔ amagbewo na mi ene la, nenemae metsɔ nu sia nu na mii.

english_verse: But life is in the blood, and you must not eat any meat that still has blood in it.
translation_verse: Ɖeko migaɖu lã si me ʋu, si nye eƒe agbe la, tsi o.

english_verse: I want you and your descendants to have many children, so people will live everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: “Ke miawo la, midzi ne miasɔ gbɔ akpe xexea me ɖo.”

english_verse: Again, God said to Noah and his sons:
translation_verse: Mawu yi edzi gblɔ na Noa kple via ŋutsuawo be:

english_verse: I am going to make a solemn promise to you and to everyone who will live after you.
translation_verse: “Mikpɔ ɖa, nye la, mele nu blam kple miawo kple miaƒe dzidzimeviwo,

english_verse: This includes the birds and the animals that came out of the boat.
translation_verse: kpakple nu gbagbewo katã; eɖanye xe dzodzoe o, lãe o, nu gbagbe ɖe sia ɖe si nya do le aɖakaʋua me kpli mi ko la,

english_verse: I promise every living creature that the earth and those living on it will never again be destroyed by a flood.
translation_verse: mele nu blam kple mi katã be nyemagatsrɔ̃ nu gbagbewo katã kple tsiɖɔɖɔ akpɔ o. Nenema ke tsiɖɔɖɔ magagblẽ xexeme blibo la gbeɖe o.”

english_verse: The rainbow that I have put in the sky will be my sign to you and to every living creature on earth. It will remind you that I will keep this promise forever.
translation_verse: Metsɔ nye anyieʋɔ ɖo alilikpowo ŋu. Eyae anye nubabla si anɔ nye kple xexea me dome la ƒe dzesi.

english_verse: When I send clouds over the earth, and a rainbow appears in the sky,
translation_verse: Ne meƒo ƒu alilikpowo ɖe dziŋgɔli ŋu, eye anyieʋɔ do ɖe alilikpoawo ŋu la,

english_verse: I will remember my promise to you and to all other living creatures. Never again will I let floodwaters destroy all life.
translation_verse: ekema maɖo ŋku nu, si mebla kpli wò kpakple nu gbagbe ɖe sia ɖe, be tsiɖɔɖɔ magaɖe anyigba kple nu gbagbewo katã gbeɖe o, la dzi.

english_verse: When I see the rainbow in the sky, I will always remember the promise that I have made to every living creature.
translation_verse: Ne anyieʋɔ do ɖe alilikpowo ŋu la, makpɔe, eye maɖo ŋku nubabla si le nye kple nu gbagbe siwo katã le xexea me dome la dzi.”

english_verse: The rainbow will be the sign of that solemn promise. Noah and His Family
translation_verse: Mawu gagblɔ na Noa be: “Esia nye nubabla le nye kple nu gbagbe siwo katã le xexea me dome la ƒe dzesi.” Noa kple via ŋutsuwo ƒe ŋutinya

english_verse: Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, left the boat. Ham later had a son named Canaan.
translation_verse: Noa viŋutsu siwo do go le aɖakaʋua me la woe nye: Sem, Xam kple Yafet. Xam siae nye Kanaan tɔgbui.

english_verse: All people on earth are descendants of Noah's three sons.
translation_verse: Noa viŋutsu etɔ̃ siawo me amegbetɔwo katã va dzɔ tso hekaka ɖe xexea me katã.

english_verse: Noah farmed the land and was the first to plant a vineyard.
translation_verse: Noa nye agbledela gbãtɔ. Ede waingble.

english_verse: One day he got drunk and was lying naked in his tent.
translation_verse: Esi wòno wain mu gbe ɖeka la, eyi ɖamlɔ anyi ɖe eƒe agbadɔme amama.

english_verse: Ham entered the tent and saw him naked, then went back outside and told his brothers.
translation_verse: Xam, Kanaan tɔgbui, kpɔ eƒe ama me, eye wòyi ɖagblɔe na nɔvia eveawo le xexe.

english_verse: Shem and Japheth put a robe over their shoulders and walked backwards into the tent. Without looking at their father, they placed it over his body.
translation_verse: Tete Sem kple Yafet ke avɔ me lé ɖe abɔta, zɔ megbemegbe, eye woyi ɖatsyɔe na wo tɔ́a. Wometrɔ kɔ kpɔ wo tɔ́ ƒe ama me o.

english_verse: When Noah sobered up and learned what his youngest son had done,
translation_verse: Esi aha la kɔ le mo na Noa, eye wòse nu si via ŋutsu ɖevitɔ wɔ ɖe eŋu la,

english_verse: he said, “I now put a curse on Canaan! He will be the lowest slave of his brothers.
translation_verse: egblɔ be: “Aɖi Kanaan ŋu kpékpekpe! Azu kluviwo ƒe kluvi na nɔviawo.”

english_verse: I ask the Lord my God to bless Shem and make Canaan his slave.
translation_verse: Noa gagblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu neyra Sem! Nena Kanaan nanye eƒe kluvi.

english_verse: I pray God will give Japheth more and more land and let him take over the territory of Shem. May Canaan be his slave.”
translation_verse: Mawu nena Yafet nadzi ɖe dzi. Nena eƒe dzidzimeviwo nanɔ Sem tɔwo gbɔ faa, eye Kanaan nanye Yafet ƒe kluvi.”

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Ale enɔ agbe ƒe alafa asieke bla atɔ̃ hafi ku.

english_verse: After the flood Shem, Ham, and Japheth had many descendants. The Descendants of Japheth
translation_verse: Noa viŋutsuwoe nye Sem, Xam kple Yafet. Woƒe dzidzimeviwo ŋunyae nye esi: Le tsiɖɔɖɔ la megbe la, wodzi viŋutsuwo na wo.

english_verse: Japheth's descendants had their own languages, tribes, and land. They were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras. Gomer was the ancestor of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah. Javan was the ancestor of Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim, who settled along the coast. The Descendants of Ham
translation_verse: Ame siawo me ƒuta kple ƒukpowo dzi dukɔwo dzɔ tso. Esiawo nye Yafet viŋutsuwo le woƒe anyigbawo, woƒe gbegbɔgblɔ vovovowo, woƒe ƒomewo kple woƒe dukɔwo nu.

english_verse: This completes the list of Noah's descendants. After the flood their descendants became nations and spread all over the world.
translation_verse: Esiawoe nye Noa viŋutsuwo ƒe ƒomewo ɖe woƒe dzidzimewo kple dukɔwo nu. Woawo mee anyigba dzi dukɔwo dzɔ tso le tsiɖɔɖɔ la megbe.

english_verse: but after some of them moved from the east and settled in Babylonia,
translation_verse: Esi woʋu le ɣedzeƒe la, wova ɖo gbadzaƒe aɖe le Sinear, eye wonɔ afi ma.

english_verse: they said: Let's build a city with a tower that reaches to the sky! We'll use hard bricks and tar instead of stone and mortar. We'll become famous, and we won't be scattered all over the world.
translation_verse: Tete wogblɔ be: “Mina míatso du, eye míatu mɔ́ wòakɔ, eye etame natɔ dziƒo ke, ne míaƒe ŋkɔ nade du, ne míagava kaka ɖe xexe blibo la me o.”

english_verse: But when the Lord came down to look at the city and the tower,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖi va be yeakpɔ du kple mɔ́ kɔkɔ si amegbetɔ viwo tu la ɖa.

english_verse: he said: These people are working together because they all speak the same language. This is just the beginning. Soon they will be able to do anything they want.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, dukɔ ɖeka ame siawo nye, eye gbegbɔgblɔ ɖekae le wo katã nu. Nu si wogbɔna wɔwɔ ge la ƒe gɔmedzedze koe nye esi. Azɔ nu sia nu si woɖo be yewoawɔ la, maglo wo o.

english_verse: Let's go down and confuse them! We'll make them speak different languages, and they won't be able to understand each other.
translation_verse: Miva, mina míɖi yi ɖatɔtɔ woƒe gbe bene ame aɖeke nagase nɔvia ƒe nuƒo me o.”

english_verse: So the people had to stop building the city, because the Lord confused their language and scattered them all over the earth. That's how the city of Babel got its name. The Descendants of Shem
translation_verse: Eya ta woyɔ woƒe dua be Babel elabe afi mae Aƒetɔ tɔtɔ gbe na dukɔwo katã le, eye wòna wokaka ɖe anyigba blibo la katã dzi tso afi ma. Sem ƒe dzidzimeviwo (Kron I,

english_verse: Arpachshad had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Le Selax dzidzi megbe la, Arpaxsad ganɔ agbe ƒe alafa ene kple etɔ̃, eye wòdzi viŋutsu bubuwo kple vinyɔnuwo.

english_verse: Shelah had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Le Eber dzidzi megbe la, Selax ganɔ agbe ƒe alafa ene kple etɔ̃, eye wòdzi viŋutsu bubuwo kple vinyɔnuwo.

english_verse: Eber had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Le Peleg dzidzi megbe la, Eber ganɔ agbe ƒe alafa ene bla etɔ̃, eye wòdzi viŋutsu bubuwo kple vinyɔnuwo.

english_verse: Peleg had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Le Reu dzidzi megbe la, Peleg ganɔ agbe ƒe alafa eve kple asieke, eye wòdzi viŋutsu bubuwo kple vinyɔnuwo.

english_verse: Reu had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Le Serug dzidzi megbe la, Reu ganɔ agbe ƒe alafa eve kple adrẽ, eye wòdzi viŋutsu bubuwo kple vinyɔnuwo.

english_verse: Serug had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Le Naxor dzidzi megbe la, Serug ganɔ agbe ƒe alafa eve, eye wòdzi viŋutsu bubuwo kple vinyɔnuwo.

english_verse: Nahor had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Le Terax dzidzi megbe la, Naxor ganɔ agbe ƒe alafa ɖeka kple wui asieke, eye wòdzi viŋutsu bubuwo kple vinyɔnuwo.

english_verse: Terah decided to move from Ur to the land of Canaan. He took along Abram and Sarai and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran. But when they came to the city of Haran, they settled there instead.
translation_verse: Terax ʋu kple via Abram kple tɔgbuiyɔvia Lot, ame si nye Xaran vi kple toyɔvia Sarai, via Abram srɔ̃ la, tso Ur le Kaldea, be woayi Kanaan-nyigba dzi. Ke esi woɖo Xaran la, wotsi afi ma.

english_verse: The Lord said to Abram: Leave your country, your family, and your relatives and go to the land that I will show you.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Abram be: “Ʋu le wò anyigba dzi, tso ƒowòmeawo gbɔ kple tɔ́wò ƒeme, ne nàyi anyigba si mafia wò la dzi.

english_verse: I will bless you and make your descendants into a great nation. You will become famous and be a blessing to others.
translation_verse: Mana dukɔ gã aɖe nado tso mewò. Mayra wò, eye mana wò ŋkɔ nade du; àzu yayra.

english_verse: I will bless those who bless you, but I will put a curse on anyone who puts a curse on you. Everyone on earth will be blessed because of you.
translation_verse: Mayra ame siwo yra wò, ke ame si ƒo fi de wò la, maƒo fi adee. Mewò anyigba dzi ƒomeawo katã ato axɔ yayra.”

english_verse: Abram went as far as the sacred tree of Moreh in a place called Shechem. The Canaanites were still living in the land at that time,
translation_verse: Abram tsa le anyigba la dzi ʋuu va ɖo More-logoti la gbɔ le Sixem. Ɣe ma ɣi la, Kanaantɔwo le anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: but the Lord appeared to Abram and promised, “I will give this land to your family forever.” Abram then built an altar there for the Lord.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖe eɖokui fia Abram gblɔ nɛ be: “Wò dzidzimeviwo matsɔ anyigba sia ana.” Ale Abram ɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afi ma na Aƒetɔ ame si ɖe eɖokui fiae.

english_verse: Abram traveled to the hill country east of Bethel and camped between Bethel and Ai, where he built another altar and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Tso ɣe ma ɣi la, Abram ʋu tso afi ma yi ɖe tonyigba dzi, le Betel ƒe ɣedzeƒe, eye wòtu eƒe agbadɔ ɖi. Eɖe Betel ɖe ɣetoɖoƒe, eye Ai le ɣedzeƒe. Eɖi vɔsamlekpui na Aƒetɔ, eye wòsubɔe le afi ma.

english_verse: Later, Abram started out toward the Southern Desert. Abram in Egypt
translation_verse: Esia megbe la, Abram gaʋu tso teƒe yi teƒe ɖo ta Kanaan-nyigba ƒe anyigbemekegbegbe lɔƒo. Abram yi Egipte

english_verse: When the Egyptians see you, they will murder me because I am your husband. But they won't kill you.
translation_verse: Ne Egiptetɔwo kpɔ wò la, wòagblɔ be: ‘Srɔ̃ae nye esia.’ Ale woawum, ke woana nàtsi agbe.

english_verse: Please save my life by saying you are my sister.”
translation_verse: Eya ta meɖe kuku, gblɔ na wo ko be nɔvinye nyɔnue yenye ale woana matsi agbe anɔ dedie le tawò.”

english_verse: As soon as Abram and Sarai arrived in Egypt, the Egyptians noticed how beautiful she was.
translation_verse: Esi Abram ɖo Egipte la, Egiptetɔwo kpɔ be nyɔnua dze tugbe ŋutɔ.

english_verse: The king's officials told him about her, and she was taken to his house.
translation_verse: Esi Egipte Fiagã ƒe amegãwo kpɔ nyɔnua la, wokafui na Egipte Fiagã la, eye wokplɔ nyɔnu la va Egipte Fiagã la ƒeme.

english_verse: The king was good to Abram because of Sarai, and Abram was given sheep, cattle, donkeys, slaves, and camels.
translation_verse: Le Sarai ta la, fia la lé be na Abram nyuie. Alẽ, nyi, tedzi, kluvi, kosi, tedzinɔ kple kposɔwo nɔ esi.

english_verse: Because of Sarai, the Lord struck the king and everyone in his palace with terrible diseases.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ na dɔléle dziŋɔ aɖewo dze Egipte Fiagã la kple eƒemetɔwo dzi le Sarai, Abram srɔ̃ ta.

english_verse: Finally, the king sent for Abram and said to him, “What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me Sarai was your wife?
translation_verse: Ale Egipte Fiagã la yɔ Abram vɛ hebiae be: “Nu ka nye esi nèwɔ ɖe ŋunye? Nu ka ta mègblɔ nam be ye srɔ̃e wònye o?

english_verse: Why did you make me believe she was your sister? Now I've married her. Take her and go! She's your wife.”
translation_verse: Nu ka ta nègblɔ be ye nɔvinyɔnue wònye, eye mena wòzu srɔ̃nye? Kpɔ ɖa, srɔ̃wòe nye esi. Kplɔe dzoe! Netsɔ na mi ne miadzo!”

english_verse: So the king told his men to let Abram and Sarai take their possessions and leave.
translation_verse: Egipte Fiagã la ɖe gbe na eƒe amewo, eye wonyà Abram kple srɔ̃a kpakple wo ŋumewo katã.

english_verse: Abram and Sarai took everything they owned and went to the Southern Desert. Lot went with them.
translation_verse: Ale Abram ʋu le Egipte kple srɔ̃a kple eƒe nunɔamesiwo katã hekpe ɖe Lot ŋuti, gatrɔ va anyigbemekegbegbe la.

english_verse: Abram was very rich. He owned many cattle, sheep, and goats, and had a lot of silver and gold.
translation_verse: Abram nye kesinɔtɔ gã aɖe, eye lãwo, klosalo kple sika nɔ esi fũu.

english_verse: Abram moved from place to place in the Southern Desert. And finally, he went north and set up his tents between Bethel and Ai,
translation_verse: Azɔ edzo le teƒe si wòle le anyigbemekegbegbe la ɖo ta Betel, eye wòɖaɖo afi si wòtu agbadɔ ɖo tsã le Betel kple Ai dome.

english_verse: where he had earlier camped and built an altar. There he worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Afi siae wòɖi vɔsamlekpui hã ɖo va yi. Abram do gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ le afi ma.

english_verse: Lot, who was traveling with him, also had sheep, goats, and cattle, as well as his own family and slaves.
translation_verse: Lãhawo kple agbadɔwo nɔ Lot, ame si nɔ Abram gbɔ la hã si.

english_verse: Abram said to Lot, “We are close relatives. We shouldn't argue, and our men shouldn't be fighting one another.
translation_verse: Tete Abram gblɔ na Lot be: “Mègana dzre nanɔ nye kple wò loo, alo nye lãkplɔlawo kple wò lãkplɔlawo dome o, elabe ƒometɔ míenye.

english_verse: There is plenty of land for you to choose from. Let's separate. If you go north, I'll go south; if you go south, I'll go north.”
translation_verse: Fifia la, na miama ɖa tso mía nɔewo gbɔ. Menye anyigbae nye esi gbao le ŋkuwò me, le miame kple ɖusime oa? Tia akpa si dze ŋuwò. Ne ètsɔ miame la, maxɔ ɖusime, eye ne ètsɔ ɖusime la, maxɔ miame.”

english_verse: This happened before the Lord had destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. And when Lot looked around, he saw there was plenty of water in the Jordan Valley. All the way to Zoar the valley was as green as the garden of the Lord or the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: Lot tsa ŋku godoo, eye wòkpɔ be tsi sɔ gbɔ le Yordan-balia me ʋuu heyi keke Zoar ke, eye teƒea le abe Aƒetɔ ƒe abɔ me ene, abe Egipte-nyigba ene. Ɣe ma ɣi la, Aƒetɔ metsrɔ̃ Sodom kple Gomora duwo haɖe o.

english_verse: So Lot chose the whole Jordan Valley for himself, and as he started out toward the east, he and Abram separated.
translation_verse: Lot tia Yordan-balia me katã na eɖokui, eye wòʋu ɖo ta ɣedzeƒe lɔƒo. Aleae nɔvi eveawo ma ɖa tso wo nɔewo gbɔ nye esi.

english_verse: Abram stayed in the land of Canaan. But Lot settled near the cities of the valley and put up his tents not far from Sodom,
translation_verse: Abram nɔ Kanaan-nyigba dzi; ke Lot ya nɔ balia me, duawo me. Enɔ eƒe agbadɔ tum tso teƒe yi teƒe ʋuu va ɖo keke Sodom.

english_verse: where the people were evil and sinned terribly against the Lord. Abram Moves to Hebron
translation_verse: Ke Sodomtɔwo vɔ̃ɖi ŋutɔ, eye wowɔ nu tovo geɖe ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu. Abram ʋu yi Xebron

english_verse: After Abram and Lot had gone their separate ways, the Lord said to Abram: Look around to the north, south, east, and west.
translation_verse: Esi Lot dzo le Abram gbɔ megbe la, Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Abram be: “Fɔ mo dzi, eye nàtsa ŋku godoo tso afi si nèle tso dzigbeme va yi anyigbeme, tso ɣedzeƒe va yi ɣetoɖoƒe,

english_verse: I will give you and your family all the land you can see. It will be theirs forever!
