translation_verse: elabe mele anyigba si kpɔm nèle la katã tsɔ ge ana wò kple wò dzidzimeviwo tegbee.

english_verse: I will give you more descendants than there are specks of dust on the earth, and someday it will be easier to count those specks of dust than to count your descendants.
translation_verse: Mana wò dzidzimeviwo nasɔ gbɔ abe kewɔ ene ale be ame si ate ŋu axlẽ kewɔ la, koe ate ŋu xlẽ wò dzidzimeviwo hã.

english_verse: Now walk back and forth across the land, because I am going to give it to you.
translation_verse: Tso nàɖatsa le anyigba la katã dzi nàkpɔ eƒe lolome ɖa, elabe wòe matsɔe ana.”

english_verse: Abram took down his tents and went to live near the sacred trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ale Abram ʋu kple eƒe agbadɔ, eye wòyi ɖanɔ Mamre-logoti siwo le Xebron-nutome me la gbɔ. Eɖi vɔsamlekpui na Aƒetɔ ɖe afi ma.

english_verse: About this time, King Amraphel of Babylonia, King Arioch of Ellasar, King Chedorlaomer of Elam, and King Tidal of Goiim
translation_verse: Le Amrafel, Sinear-fia, Ariok, Elasar-fia, Kedorlaomer, Elam-fia kple Tideal, Goyim-fia ŋɔli la,

english_verse: attacked King Bera of Sodom, King Birsha of Gomorrah, King Shinab of Admah, King Shemeber of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, a city also known as Zoar.
translation_verse: aʋa dzɔ ɖe woawo kple Bera, Sodom-fia, Birsa, Gomora-fia, Sineab, Adma-fia, Semeber, Zeboyim-fia kple Bela alo Zoar-fia dome.

english_verse: A year later King Chedorlaomer and his allies attacked and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth-Karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, and the Emites in Shaveh-Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: Le ƒè wui enelia me la, Kedorlaomer kple fia siwo wɔ ɖeka kplii la va si Refaimtɔwo le Astarot-Karnaim, Zuzitɔwo le Ham kple Emitɔwo le Kiryataim-gbadzaƒe.

english_verse: They also defeated the Horites in the hill country of Edom, as far as El-Paran, near the desert.
translation_verse: Wosi Xoritɔwo hã le woƒe to Seir dzi, eye wonyà wo ɖe nu ʋuu va se ɖe Elparan si te ɖe gbedadaƒo la ŋu.

english_verse: They went back to the city of Enmishpat, better known as Kadesh. Then they captured all the land that belonged to the Amalekites, and they defeated the Amorites who were living in Hazazon-Tamar.
translation_verse: Emegbe wotrɔ va Enmisapat si nye Kades fifia, eye wosi Amalekitɔwo katã kple Amoritɔ siwo nɔ Xazazon-Tamar la hã.

english_verse: was full of tar pits, and when the troops from Sodom and Gomorrah started running away, some of them fell into the pits. Others escaped to the hill country.
translation_verse: Azɔ aŋɔʋewo le Sidim-bali la me fũu. Esi Sodom kple Gomora fia sí yina la, ɖewo ge dze aŋɔʋeawo me, ke mamlɛawo sí yi toa dzi.

english_verse: Their enemies took everything of value from Sodom and Gomorrah, including their food supplies.
translation_verse: Ale futɔawo ha Sodom kple Gomoratɔwo ƒe nunɔamesiwo kple nuɖuɖuwo katã dzoe.

english_verse: They also captured Abram's nephew Lot, who lived in Sodom. They took him and his possessions and then left.
translation_verse: Lot, Abram tɔgãyɔvi hã nɔ Sodom ɣe ma ɣi, ale wolé eya hã, eye woha eƒe nuwo dzoe.

english_verse: At this time Abram the Hebrew was living near the oaks that belonged to Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner were Abram's friends. Someone who had escaped from the battle told Abram
translation_verse: Ke ame aɖe sí va gblɔ nya si dzɔ la na Abram, Hebritɔ la. Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, Abram le Amoritɔ, Mamre ƒe ati gã kɔkɔeawo gbɔ. Mamre kple nɔvia ŋutsuwo, Eskol kple Aner, nye Abram ƒe dzoɖuxɔlɔ̃wo.

english_verse: that his nephew Lot had been taken away. Three hundred and eighteen of Abram's servants were fighting men, so he took them and followed the enemy as far north as the city of Dan.
translation_verse: Esi Abram se be woɖe aboyo ye tɔgãyɔvia la, eɖe aʋawɔla alafa etɔ̃ wui enyi tso eya ŋutɔ ƒe asaɖa me, eye woti fia eneawo yome ʋuu va ɖo Dan.

english_verse: That night, Abram divided up his troops, attacked from all sides, and won a great victory. But some of the enemy escaped to the town of Hobah north of Damascus,
translation_verse: Abram ma eƒe amewo ɖe hatsotsowo me le zã me, eye wodze futɔawo dzi hefiti wo. Wonyà wo ɖe nu va ɖo Xoba le Damasko ƒe dzigbeme.

english_verse: and Abram went after them. He brought back his nephew Lot, together with Lot's possessions and the women and everyone else who had been captured. Abram Is Blessed by Melchizedek
translation_verse: Abram xɔ nunɔamesi siwo katã futɔawo ha dzo yinae la. Exɔ tɔgãyɔvia Lot, eƒe nunɔamesiwo, nyɔnuawo kple aboyome bubuawo katã hã gbɔe. Melxizedek yra Abram

english_verse: Abram returned after he had defeated King Chedorlaomer and the other kings. Then the king of Sodom went to meet Abram in Shaveh Valley, which is also known as King's Valley.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi Abram ɖu Kedorlaomer kple fia siwo kpe ɖe eŋuti dzi hetrɔ gbɔna ɖe aƒe la, Sodom fia do yi ɖakpee le Save-bali me. Wogayɔa bali sia be Fia ƒe Bali me.

english_verse: King Melchizedek of Salem was a priest of God Most High. He brought out some bread and wine
translation_verse: Melxizedek, ame si nye Salem-fia, eye wòganye Mawu Dziƒoʋĩtɔ la ƒe nunɔla la tsɔ abolo kple wain vɛ na Abram.

english_verse: and said to Abram: “I bless you in the name of God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.
translation_verse: Eyrae gblɔ be: “Mawu Dziƒoʋĩtɔ, si wɔ dziƒo kple anyigba la, neyra Abram!

english_verse: All praise belongs to God Most High for helping you defeat your enemies.” Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
translation_verse: Woakafu Mawu Dziƒoʋĩtɔ, si tsɔ wò futɔwo de asi na wò la.” Abram tsɔ aboyonuawo katã ƒe akpa ewolia na Melxizedek.

english_verse: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “All I want are my people. You can keep everything else.”
translation_verse: Tete Sodom-fia gblɔ na Abram be: “Tsɔ ameawo nam, kesinɔnuawo ya nezu tɔwò.”

english_verse: Abram answered: The Lord God Most High made the heavens and the earth. And I have promised him
translation_verse: Abram ɖo eŋu be: “Metà Aƒetɔ, Mawu Dziƒoʋĩtɔ, dziƒo kple anyigba Wɔla!

english_verse: that I won't keep anything of yours, not even a sandal strap or a piece of thread. Then you can never say that you are the one who made me rich.
translation_verse: Ne maxɔ nane tso nu siwo katã nye tɔwò la me fĩi! Ɖetika loo, alo afɔkpaka teti hã nyemaxɔ le wò nuawo me, ne nàva gblɔ be, ‘Nyee wɔ Abram wòzu kesinɔtɔ’ o.

english_verse: Let my share be the food that my men have eaten. But Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre went with me, so give them their share of what we brought back.
translation_verse: Nye ŋutɔ nyemele naneke dim o, negbe nu si ɖekakpuiawo ɖu la ko. Ke medi be nàna Aner, Eskol kple Mamre, ame siwo va kpe ɖe ŋunye la, naxɔ woawo tɔ gome.”

english_verse: Later the Lord spoke to Abram in a vision, “Abram, don't be afraid! I will protect you and reward you greatly.”
translation_verse: Esiawo megbe la, Aƒetɔ va Abram gbɔ le ŋutega me, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Abram, mègavɔ̃ o. Nyee nye wò akpoxɔnu. Wò fetu sɔ gbɔ ŋutɔ.”

english_verse: But Abram answered, “Lord All-Powerful, you have given me everything I could ask for, except children. And when I die, Eliezer of Damascus will get all I own.
translation_verse: Ke Abram ɖo eŋu be: “Aƒetɔ Mawu, fetu ka gɔ̃ nànam? Va se ɖe egbe la, ɖeko megali, vi mele asinye o. Eliezer, Damaskotɔ la koe le nye dome nyi ge.”

english_verse: You have not given me any children, and this servant of mine will inherit everything.”
translation_verse: Abram gblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, mèna vim o; kluvi si wodzi le nye aƒeme lae anyi nye dome.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “No, he won't! You will have a son of your own, and everything you have will be his.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, Aƒetɔ xɔ edzi be: “Ŋutsu sia mele wò dome nyi ge o; ke boŋ wò ŋutɔ viwò ŋutsue anye wò domenyila.”

english_verse: Then the Lord took Abram outside and said, “Look at the sky and see if you can count the stars. That's how many descendants you will have.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ kplɔe yi xexe, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Wu mo dzi nàkpɔ dziŋgɔli me ɖa. Xlẽ ɣletiviwo kpɔ be àte ŋui mahã. Aleae wò dzidzimeviwo asɔ gbɔe.”

english_verse: Abram believed the Lord, so the Lord was pleased with him and accepted him. The Lord Makes Another Promise to Abram
translation_verse: Abram xɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nyaa dzi se. Le esia ta, ebui nɛ be ewɔ nu dzɔdzɔe.

english_verse: The Lord said to Abram, “I brought you here from Ur in Chaldea, and I gave you this land.”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ nɛ be: “Nyee nye Aƒetɔ, si kplɔ wò tso Ur le Kaldea, be matsɔ anyigba sia na wò, wòazu tɔwò.”

english_verse: Abram asked, “Lord God, how can I know the land will be mine?”
translation_verse: Ke Abram bia be: “Aƒetɔ Mawu, ale ke mawɔ anya be ava zu tɔnye?”

english_verse: Then the Lord told him, “Bring me a three-year-old cow, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a dove, and a young pigeon.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ nɛ be: “Lé nyinɔ ɖeka, gbɔ̃nɔ ɖeka kple agbo ɖeka, siwo xɔ ƒe etɔ̃etɔ̃ kple ahɔnɛ ɖeka kple ahɔnɛ ɖeka vɛ nam.”

english_verse: Abram obeyed the Lord. Then he cut the animals in half and laid the two halves of each animal opposite each other on the ground. But he did not cut the doves and pigeons in half.
translation_verse: Esi Abram tsɔ nu siawo katã vɛ nɛ la, efe ɖe sia ɖe me ɖe eve, eye wòɖo wo ɖe agbaka eve me, afã ɖe sia ɖe le nɔvia kasa; ke mefe xeawo ya me o.

english_verse: And when birds came down to eat the animals, Abram chased them away.
translation_verse: Tete xe ƒonuwo va dze ɖe lã kukuawo gbɔ, eye Abram nyà wo ɖa.

english_verse: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and everything became dark and frightening.
translation_verse: Esi ɣe le to ɖom la, Abram dɔ alɔ̃ yi eme ʋĩi. Kasia viviti dziŋɔ aɖe do ɖee, eye vɔvɔ̃ lée.

english_verse: Four generations later, your descendants will return here and take this land, because only then will the people who live here be so sinful that they deserve to be punished.
translation_verse: Dzidzime enelia me hafi tɔwòwo agatrɔ va afii, elabe Amoritɔwo ƒe nuvɔ̃ meva glo haɖe o.”

english_verse: Sometime after sunset, when it was very dark, a smoking cooking pot and a flaming fire passed between the two halves of each animal.
translation_verse: Ɣe ɖo to, eye viviti do. Kpɔ ɖa, ze si le dzudzɔ tum kɔlikɔli kple akakati si le bibim flaflafla la va to lã siwo me wofe da ɖi la dome.

english_verse: At that time the Lord made an agreement with Abram and told him: I will give your descendants the land east of the Shihor River on the border of Egypt as far as the Euphrates River.

translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla kpɔ Hagar, wòle vudo aɖe si le gbedadaƒo le Sur-mɔ dzi la to.

translation_verse: Ke esi Lot le tɔtrɔm to eme ko la, Aƒetɔ ve enu, eye ŋutsuawo lé eya, srɔ̃a kple via nyɔnu eveawo ƒe alɔnu, kplɔ wo va dua godo.

english_verse: When they were outside, one of the angels said, “Run for your lives! Don't even look back. And don't stop in the valley. Run to the hills, where you'll be safe.”
translation_verse: Esi wokplɔ wo do goe vɔ la, wogblɔ na Lot be: “Ekpo ɖe dziwò azɔ. Sí dzo, ne nàtsi agbe! Mègakpɔ megbe o; mègatɔ ɖe afi aɖeke hã le balia me o. Sí yi toawo dzi be nàgatsrɔ̃ o.”

english_verse: Lot answered, “You have done us a great favor, sir. You have saved our lives, but please don't make us go to the hills. That's too far away. The city will be destroyed before we can get there, and we will be killed when it happens.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ènyo dɔme na nye, wò dɔla ŋutɔ, eye nèkpɔ nublanui nam, xɔm ɖe agbe; ke toawo gbɔ didi akpa. Ɖewohĩ ne wode asi dua tsɔtsrɔ̃ me la, nyemele toawo gbɔ ɖo ge hafi atsrɔ̃ o.

english_verse: There's a town near here. It's only a small place, but my family and I will be safe, if you let us go there.”
translation_verse: Taflatsɛ, du sue aɖee nye ekem ɖa. Eya tsɔ ɖe mía gbɔ. Melolo o; eya ta na masí yi afi ma bene matsi agbe.”

english_verse: “All right, go there,” he answered. “I won't destroy that town.
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Enyo, melɔ̃ ɖe wò nya sia hã dzi; nyemagbã du si nèwɔnɛ la o.

english_verse: Hurry! Run! I can't do anything until you are safely there.” The town was later called Zoar because Lot had said it was small. Sodom and Gomorrah Are Destroyed
translation_verse: Ke netsɔ! Sí yi afi ma kaba! Nyemate ŋu awɔ naneke o, va se ɖe esime nèɖo afi ma hafi.” Esia ta woyɔa du la be Zoar. Wotsrɔ̃ Sodom kple Gomora

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Lot reached the town of Zoar,
translation_verse: Ɣe dze hafi Lot ɖo Zoar.

english_verse: and the Lord sent burning sulfur down like rain on Sodom and Gomorrah.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ na aŋɔkpe kple dzo dza tso dziƒo ɖe Sodom kple Gomora dzi,

english_verse: He destroyed those cities and everyone who lived in them, as well as their land and the trees and grass that grew there.
translation_verse: wofiã eye wòtsrɔ̃ nu siwo katã le balia me la keŋkeŋ. Dua me nɔlawo katã ku, eye numiemiewo tsrɔ̃ gbidii.

english_verse: On the way, Lot's wife looked back and was turned into a block of salt.
translation_verse: Ke Lot srɔ̃ si le eyome la trɔ kɔ kpɔ megbe, eye wòtrɔ zu dzekɔ.

english_verse: That same morning Abraham got up and went to the place where he had stood and spoken with the Lord.
translation_verse: Evea gbe ƒe ŋdi kanya la, Abraham fɔ kaba yi teƒe si wòtsi tsitre ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋkume le va yi la.

english_verse: He looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and saw smoke rising from all over the land—it was like a flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Ekpɔ Sodom kple Gomora kple teƒe siwo katã le balia me la ɖa, eye dzudzɔ le dzi dem tso anyigba la dzi, abe aŋɔɖaƒe ene.

english_verse: When God destroyed the cities of the valley where Lot lived, he remembered his promise to Abraham and saved Lot from the terrible destruction. Moab and Ammon
translation_verse: Esi Mawu le du siwo le bali si me Lot nɔ tsrɔ̃ ge la, eƒe ŋku nɔ Abraham dzi eye wòɖe Lot tso tsɔtsrɔ̃ gã si va du siwo me wònɔ dzi la me. Lot vinyɔnuwo dɔ kple wo tɔ́: Moab kple Amon ƒe dzɔtsoƒe

english_verse: Lot was afraid to stay on in Zoar. So he took his two daughters and moved to a cave in the hill country.
translation_verse: Azɔ Lot va le Zoar nɔnɔ vɔ̃m, eya ta eya kple via nyɔnu eveawo ʋu le afi ma ɖanɔ agado me le tonyigba la dzi.

english_verse: One day his older daughter said to her sister, “Our father is old, and there are no men anywhere for us to marry.
translation_verse: Vinyɔnu tsitsitɔa gblɔ na ɖevitɔ be: “Mía tɔ́ tsi vɔ, eye ŋutsu aɖeke megale anyigba la dzi adɔ kpli mí abe ale si amegbetɔwo wɔnɛ la ene o.

english_verse: Let's get our father drunk! Then we can sleep with him and have children.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, na míana wain mía tɔ́ wòano amu, ale be míana wòado fu mí ne míadzi vi bene mía tɔ́ ƒe dzidzime nayi edzi.”

english_verse: That night they got their father drunk, and the older daughter got in bed with him, but he was too drunk even to know she was there.
translation_verse: Ale gbe ma gbe ƒe zã me la, wona wain wo tɔ́ wòno, eye tsitsitɔ yi ɖamlɔ egbɔ. Ke wo tɔ́ menya be eva mlɔ ye gbɔ fɔ dzo o.

english_verse: The next day the older daughter said to her sister, “I slept with my father last night. We'll get him drunk again tonight, so you can sleep with him, and we can each have a child.”
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, tsitsitɔ gblɔ na ɖevitɔ be: “Étò ƒe zã me la, memlɔ tɔ́nye gbɔ. Míagana wòano wain egbe ƒe zã hã, ale be wò hã nàyi aɖamlɔ egbɔ bene míana eƒe dzidzime nayi edzi.”

english_verse: That night they got their father drunk, and this time the younger sister slept with him. But once again he was too drunk even to know she was there.
translation_verse: Ale esi zã gado la, wogana wain wo tɔ́ wòno mu, eye ɖevitɔ hã yi ɖamlɔ egbɔ. Ke wo tɔ́ menya be eva mlɔ ye gbɔ fɔ dzo o.

english_verse: That's how Lot's two daughters had children.
translation_verse: Ale wɔ Lot do fu eya ŋutɔ via nyɔnu eveawo.

english_verse: The older daughter named her son Moab, and he is the ancestor of the Moabites.
translation_verse: Tsitsitɔ dzi ŋutsuvi, eye wòtsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Moab. Eya ƒe dzidzimeviwoe nye Moabitɔ siwo li egbegbe.

english_verse: The younger daughter named her son Benammi, and he is the ancestor of the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Ɖevitɔ hã dzi ŋutsuvi, eye wòtsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Ben-Ami. Eya ƒe dzidzimeviwoe nye Amontɔ siwo li egbegbe.

english_verse: he told everyone that his wife Sarah was his sister. So King Abimelech of Gerar had Sarah brought to him.
translation_verse: egblɔ be ye nɔvinyɔnue nye Sara. Ale Abimelex, Gerar-fia, na wokplɔ Sara vɛ nɛ.

english_verse: But God came to Abimelech in a dream and said, “You have taken a married woman into your home, and for this you will die!”
translation_verse: Ke gbe ɖeka, le zã me la, Mawu ɖe eɖokui fia Abimelex le drɔ̃eƒe gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, èle kuku ge le nyɔnu si nèxɔ la ta. Ame srɔ̃e!”

english_verse: Abimelech said to the Lord, “Don't kill me! I haven't slept with Sarah. Didn't they say they were brother and sister? I am completely innocent.”
translation_verse: Menye eya ŋutɔe gblɔ nam be ye nɔvinyɔnu ye oa? Sara ŋutɔ gɔ̃ hã gblɔ be ye nɔviŋutsu ye. Nye dzi mebu fɔm o, eye nyemeda vo o ɖe.”

english_verse: Then God continued: I know you are innocent. That's why I kept you from sleeping with Sarah and doing anything wrong.
translation_verse: Mawu ɖo eŋu nɛ le drɔ̃eƒe be: “Nyateƒe, nye hã menyae be wò dzime kɔ le nu si nèwɔ la me, eya ta meɖo asi dziwò be nàgade asi eŋu ava wɔ vɔ̃ ɖe ŋunye o.”

english_verse: Her husband is a prophet. Let her go back to him, and his prayers will save you from death. But if you don't return her, you and all your people will die.
translation_verse: Azɔ gbugbɔ nyɔnua na srɔ̃a, elabe nye gbeƒãɖela ŋutsua nye, ne wòaɖe kuku ɖe tawò nàtsi agbe. Ke ne ègbe mètrɔe nɛ o la, ekema nànyae nyuie be wò kple aƒewò me tɔwo katã miele kuku ge.”

english_verse: Early the next morning Abimelech sent for his officials, and when he told them what had happened, they were frightened.
translation_verse: Abimelex fɔ ŋdi kanya, eye wòyɔ eƒe dɔlawo katã vɛ heto nya si dzɔ la na wo. Vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo ale gbegbe.

english_verse: Abimelech then called in Abraham and said: Look what you've done to us! What have I ever done to you? Why did you make me and my nation guilty of such a terrible sin?
translation_verse: Tete Abimelex yɔ Abraham eye wòbiae be: “Nu kae nye esi nèwɔ ɖe mía ŋu? Nu vɔ̃ ka gɔ̃ mewɔ ɖe ŋuwò hafi nèhe dzɔgbevɔ̃e gã sia va nye kple nye fiaɖuƒe dzi? Womewɔa nu sia, si nèwɔ ɖe ŋunye la, gbeɖegbeɖe o.

english_verse: What were you thinking when you did this?
translation_verse: Ale ke nèbu hafi wɔe?”

english_verse: Abraham answered: I did it because I didn't think any of you respected God, and I was sure that someone would kill me to get my wife.
translation_verse: Abraham ɖo eŋu be: “Nye ya metsɔe be mawuvɔ̃la aɖeke mele afi sia o, ale woawum axɔ srɔ̃nye.

english_verse: Besides, she is my half sister. We have the same father, but different mothers.
translation_verse: Ke hã, le nyateƒe me la, nɔvinye nyɔnue, elabe tɔ́viwo míenye, ke menye dadaviwo o, eye meɖee.

english_verse: When God made us leave my father's home and start wandering, I told her, “If you really love me, then tell everyone that I am your brother.”
translation_verse: Esi Mawu be maʋu le tɔ́nye ƒeme ayi dzronyigba dzi la, megblɔ na Sara be: ‘Medi be nàve nunye. Afi sia afi si míaɖo la, gblɔ na ame sia ame be ye nɔviŋutsue menye.’ ”

english_verse: After Abimelech had given Abraham some sheep, cattle, and slaves, he sent Sarah back
translation_verse: Tete Abimelex gbugbɔ Sara na Abraham, eye wòna alẽwo, nyiwo kple kluviwo hãe.

english_verse: and told Abraham he could settle anywhere in his country.
translation_verse: Egblɔ na Abraham be: “Tɔnyee nye anyigba sia katã. Nɔ afi sia afi si nyo ŋuwò la.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, God had kept Abimelech's wife and slaves from having children. But Abraham prayed, and God let them start having children again.
translation_verse: Elabe le Sara, Abraham srɔ̃, ta la, Aƒetɔ xe nyɔnu siwo katã le Abimelex ƒeme la ƒe vidzidɔ nu.

english_verse: The Lord was good to Sarah and kept his promise.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ve Sara nu abe ale si wògblɔ ene, eye wòwɔ eƒe ŋugbedodo la dzi nɛ.

english_verse: Although Abraham was very old, Sarah had a son exactly at the time God had said.
translation_verse: Ale Sara fɔ fu, eye wòdzi viŋutsu na Abraham le eƒe amegãkuku me le ɣeyiɣi, si Mawu gblɔ ɖi xoxo la dzi.

english_verse: and when the boy was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, just as God had commanded.
translation_verse: Esi ɖevia xɔ ŋkeke enyi la, Abraham tso aʋa nɛ abe ale si Mawu ɖo nɛ ene.

english_verse: and Sarah said, “God has made me laugh. And now everyone will laugh with me.
translation_verse: Sara gblɔ be: “Mawu do nukokoe nam. Ame sia ame si ase nya sia la, aɖi kokoe nɛ.”

english_verse: Who would have dared to tell Abraham that someday I would have a child? But in his old age, I have given him a son.”
translation_verse: Azɔ egblɔ yi edzi be: “Ame kae bui kpɔ be yeagblɔ na Abraham be, ‘Sara hã ava na no vi?’ Ke, togbɔ be wòtsi, ku amegã hã la, nyee nye esi dzi vi nɛ.”

english_verse: The time came when Sarah no longer had to nurse Isaac, and on that day Abraham gave a big feast. Hagar and Ishmael Are Sent Away
translation_verse: Isak va tsi. Gbe si gbe woɖee le no nu la, Abraham ɖo kplɔ̃ gã aɖe na amewo. Abraham nyà Hagar kple Ismael ɖa

english_verse: One day, Sarah noticed Hagar's son Ishmael playing, and she said to Abraham, “Get rid of that Egyptian slave woman and her son! I don't want him to inherit anything. It should all go to my son.”
translation_verse: Ale Sara gblɔ na Abraham be: “Nyà kosi sia kple via. Elabe vinye mele dome nyi ge kple kosi sia ƒe vi o.”

english_verse: But God said, “Abraham, don't worry about your slave woman and the boy. Just do what Sarah tells you. Isaac will inherit your family name,
translation_verse: Tete Mawu gblɔ na Abraham be: “Mègana nya sia naɖe fu na wò le ɖevia kple wò kosi la ta o. Ke boŋ nya sia nya si Sara gblɔ na wò la nàɖo toe, elabe Isak me wò dzidzimeviwo ado tso.

english_verse: but the son of the slave woman is also your son, and I will make his descendants into a great nation.”
translation_verse: Mana dukɔ nado tso kosi vi la hã me, elabe eya hã viwòe.”

english_verse: Early the next morning Abraham gave Hagar an animal skin full of water and some bread. Then he put the boy on her shoulder and sent them away. They wandered around in the desert near Beersheba,
translation_verse: Ale esi Abraham fɔ ŋdi kanya la, edi nuɖuɖu na Hagar. Eku tsi ɖe lãgbalẽgolo me wòyɔ, eye wòkɔ ɖevia kple nuawo ɖo abɔta nɛ hedo mɔe. Hagar dzo, eye wòyi ɖatsa le Beer-Seba gbegbe.

english_verse: and after they had run out of water, Hagar put her son under a bush.
translation_verse: Esi tsia vɔ la, Hagar tsɔ ɖevia mlɔ ati dodoe aɖe te,

english_verse: Then she sat down a long way off, because she could not bear to watch him die. And she cried bitterly.
translation_verse: elabe egblɔ na eɖokui be: “Nyemate ŋu ado dzi akpɔ ɖevia kuƒe o.” Ale wòdzo yi ɖabɔbɔ nɔ adzɔge abe kpedada ɖeka ƒe didime ene tso egbɔ. Azɔ ɖevia wó avi kple ɣli.

english_verse: When God heard the boy crying, the angel of God called out to Hagar from heaven and said, “Hagar, why are you worried? Don't be afraid. I have heard your son crying.
translation_verse: Ke Mawu se ŋutsuvia ƒe gbe, eye mawudɔla yɔ Hagar tso dziƒo gblɔ nɛ be: “Hagar, nu kae le wɔwòm? Mègavɔ̃ o. Mawu se ŋutsuvia ƒe gbe le afi si wòle.

english_verse: Help him up and hold his hand, because I will make him the father of a great nation.”
translation_verse: Tso nàyi ɖakɔe, eye nàlée ɖe asi, elabe mana eƒe dzidzimeviwo nazu dukɔ gã aɖe.”

english_verse: Then God let her see a well. So she went to the well and filled the skin with water, then gave some to her son.
translation_verse: Tete Mawu ʋu Hagar ƒe ŋkuwo, eye wòkpɔ tsivudo aɖe le afi ma. Eyi ɖaku tsia ɖe lãgbalẽgolo la me wòyɔ. Ekɔe vɛ, eye wòna ɖe ɖevia wòno.

english_verse: About this time Abimelech and his army commander Phicol said to Abraham, “God blesses everything you do!
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, Abimelex kple eƒe aʋakplɔla Pixol yi ɖagblɔ na Abraham be: “Mawu li kpli wò le nu sia nu si nèwɔna la me.

english_verse: Now I want you to promise in the name of God that you will always be loyal to me and my descendants, just as I have always been loyal to you in this land where you have lived as a foreigner.”
translation_verse: Eya ta ka atam nam le Mawu ŋkume afii, fifi laa be yemable nye ŋutɔ loo, vinyewo loo, alo nye dzidzimeviwo akpɔ o. Mewɔ nuteƒe na wò va yi, eya ta ka atam nam be ye hã yeawɔ nuteƒe nam kple anyigba si dzi yeva le fifia la hã.”

english_verse: And so, Abraham promised he would.
translation_verse: Abraham gblɔ be: “Meka atam be mawɔ nuteƒe na mi.”

english_verse: One day, Abraham told Abimelech, “Some of your servants have taken over one of my wells.”
translation_verse: Tete Abraham ƒo nu kple Abimelex le tsivudo si Abimelex ƒe dɔlawo xɔ le esi sesẽe la ŋuti.

english_verse: “This is the first I've heard about it,” Abimelech replied. “Why haven't you said something before? I don't have any idea who did it.”
translation_verse: Abimelex gblɔ be: “Nyemenya ame si wɔ nu sia o, mègblɔe nam kpɔ o, eye nyemese naneke tso eŋu kpɔ wu egbe o.”

english_verse: Abraham gave Abimelech some sheep and cattle, then the two men made a peace treaty.
translation_verse: Azɔ Abraham na alẽwo kple nyiwo Abimelex, eye wo kple evea wobla nu.

english_verse: Abraham separated seven female lambs from his flock of sheep,
translation_verse: Ke Abraham ɖe alẽnɔe adrẽ ɖe vovo.

english_verse: and Abimelech asked, “Why have you done this?”
translation_verse: Abimelex biae be: “Alẽnɔe adrẽ siawo, siwo nèɖe ɖe vovo la gɔme ɖe?”

english_verse: Abraham replied, “I want you to accept these seven lambs as proof that I dug this well.”
translation_verse: Abraham ɖo eŋu be: “Xɔ alẽnɔe adrẽ siawo. Woawoe nye kpeɖodzinu be wòe nye nye ɖasefo be nyee ɖe vudo sia.”

english_verse: So they called the place Beersheba, because they made a treaty there.
translation_verse: Esia tae woyɔa teƒe ma be Beer-Seba, elabe afi mae wo kple evea wobla nu le.

english_verse: When the treaty was completed, Abimelech and his army commander Phicol went back to the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Esi wobla nu vɔ alea le Beer-Seba la, Abimelex kple eƒe aʋakplɔla Pixol dze mɔ gatrɔ yi ɖe Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba and worshiped the eternal Lord God.
translation_verse: Abraham do atiwo ɖe Beer-Seba, eye wòsubɔ Aƒetɔ, Mawu Mavɔtɔ la le afi ma.

english_verse: Then Abraham lived a long time as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Abraham nɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi abe amedzro ene eteƒe didi.

english_verse: Some years later God decided to test Abraham, so he spoke to him. Abraham answered, “Here I am, Lord.”
translation_verse: Esiawo megbe la, Mawu do Abraham kpɔ. Eyɔe be: “Abraham!”, eye wòtɔ be: “Nyee nye esi!”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Go get Isaac, your only son, the one you dearly love! Take him to the land of Moriah, and I will show you a mountain where you must sacrifice him to me on the fires of an altar.”
translation_verse: Mawu gblɔ nɛ be: “Kplɔ Isak, viwò ɖeka hɔ̃ la, si gbɔ melɔ̃a nu le o la, yi ɖe Moria-nyigba dzi, eye nàtsɔe mè nu le to aɖe si mafia wò la dzi.

english_verse: So Abraham got up early the next morning and chopped wood for the fire. He put a saddle on his donkey and set out with Isaac and two servants for the place where God had told him to go.
translation_verse: Abraham fɔ ŋdi kanya, eye wòbla akpa na eƒe tedzi. Eyɔ eƒe dɔla eve kple Isak, eye wòdze nake ɖe numemevɔsa ŋu. Azɔ edze mɔ ɖo ta teƒe si Mawu fiae la.

english_verse: Three days later Abraham looked off in the distance and saw the place.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe la, Abraham kpɔ teƒe la ɖa ʋĩi.

english_verse: He told his servants, “Stay here with the donkey, while my son and I go over there to worship. We will come back.”
translation_verse: Tete Abraham gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo be: “Miawo minɔ afii kple tedzia ne nye kple vinyea míayi ŋgɔ aɖasubɔ Mawu agbɔ.”

english_verse: Abraham put the wood on Isaac's shoulder, but he carried the hot coals and the knife. As the two of them walked along,
translation_verse: Abraham lé nake la ɖe ta na via Isak, eye eya ŋutɔ ɖe dzo, tsɔ hɛ ɖe asi, eye wo kple evea dze mɔ.

english_verse: Isaac said, “Father, we have the coals and the wood, but where is the lamb for the sacrifice?” “My son,” Abraham answered, “God will provide the lamb.” The two of them walked on, and
translation_verse: Abraham ɖo eŋu be: “Vinye, Mawu ŋutɔ ana alẽvi si míatsɔ amè nui.” Ale wo kple eve la gaɖo ta ŋgɔ.

english_verse: when they reached the place that God had told him about, Abraham built an altar and placed the wood on it. Next, he tied up his son and put him on the wood.
translation_verse: Esi woɖo teƒe si Mawu fiae la, Abraham ɖi vɔsamlekpui, eye wòɖo nake la ɖe edzi. Ebla Isak, kɔe da ɖe nakea dzi le mlekpuia dzi.

english_verse: He then took the knife and got ready to kill his son.
translation_verse: Azɔ Abraham do asi ɖa, tsɔ hɛ be yeawu ye viŋutsu la.

english_verse: But the Lord's angel shouted from heaven, “Abraham! Abraham!” “Here I am!” he answered.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla yɔe tso dziƒo be: “Abraham! Abraham!” Etɔ be: “Nyee nye esi!”

english_verse: “Don't hurt the boy or harm him in any way!” the angel said. “Now I know that you truly obey God, because you were willing to offer him your only son.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ nɛ be: “Mègaka asi ɖevia ŋu o; mègawɔ nu vevi aɖeke hãe o. Menyae azɔ be mawuvɔ̃la nènye, elabe mète viwò ɖeka hɔ̃ lam o.”

english_verse: Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in the bushes. So he took the ram and sacrificed it instead of his son.
translation_verse: Abraham trɔ kɔ. Kasia agbo aɖee nye ekem le emegbe, eƒe dzowo ku aveka. Eyi ɖalée, eye wòtsɔe sa vɔ lae ɖe via teƒe.

english_verse: Abraham named that place “The Lord Will Provide.” And even now people say, “On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.”
translation_verse: Ale Abraham na ŋkɔ teƒe ma be: “Aƒetɔ ye naa nu.” Eya ta wogblɔna va se ɖe egbegbe be: “To dzie Aƒetɔ naa nu le.”

english_verse: The Lord's angel called out from heaven a second time:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla yɔ Abraham zi evelia tso dziƒo,

english_verse: You were willing to offer your only son to the Lord, and so he makes you this solemn promise,
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ be: “Metà ɖokuinye, esi nèwɔ nu sia, eye mète viwò ɖeka hɔ̃ lam o ta la,

english_verse: You have obeyed me, and so you and your descendants will be a blessing to all nations on earth.”
translation_verse: Esi nèwɔ nye gbe dzi ta la, woayra anyigba dzi dukɔwo katã to wò dzidzimeviwo dzi.”

english_verse: Abraham and Isaac went back to the servants who had come with him, and they returned to Abraham's home in Beersheba. The Children of Nahor
translation_verse: Ale Abraham trɔ va eƒe dɔlawo gbɔ, eye wodze mɔ yi Beer-Seba, afi si Abraham ɖanɔ. Naxor ƒe dzidzimeviwo

english_verse: Nahor also had another wife. Her name was Reumah, and she had four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
translation_verse: Eƒe ahiãvi, si ŋkɔe nye Rehuma la, hã dzi Tebax, Gaham, Tahas kple Maxa nɛ.

english_verse: “I live as a foreigner in your land, and I don't own any property where I can bury my wife. Please let me buy a piece of land.”
translation_verse: “Amedzroe menye le mia dome. Mina anyigbam ɖe mia dome ne maɖi nye ame kuku la ɖe edzi.”

english_verse: “Sir,” they answered, “you are an important man. Choose the best place to bury your wife. None of us would refuse you a resting place for your dead.”
translation_verse: “Amegã, see ɖa na mí. Mawu ƒe amee nènye le mía dome. Àte ŋu aɖi wò ame kukua ɖe míaƒe ame veviwo ɖiƒe nyuitɔ faa. Mía dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe alɔ̃ faa be nàɖi wò amea ɖe yeƒe ameɖiƒe.”

english_verse: and replied, “If you are willing to let me bury my wife here, please ask Zohar's son Ephron
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Ne mielɔ̃ be maɖi nye amea ɖe afii la, ekema taflatsɛ, miɖe kuku na Efron, Zoxar vi nam.

english_verse: to sell me Machpelah Cave at the end of his field. I'll pay what it's worth, and all of you can be witnesses.”
translation_verse: Medi be wòadzra eƒe Maxpela-kpeto si le eƒe agble to la nam, le mia ŋkume afii, ale si wòdi be yeadzrae ko la, ne maƒlee atsɔ wɔ nye ameɖiƒee koŋ le mia dome.”

english_verse: “Sir, the whole field, including the cave, is yours. With my own people as witnesses, I freely give it to you as a burial place for your dead.”
translation_verse: “Nye amegã, taflatsɛ see ɖa! Metsɔ nye agble la kple kpeto si le eme la na wò faa. Mele etsɔm na wò le mía detɔ siwo katã le afii la ŋkume. Ɖi wò ame la ɖe afi ma faa.”

english_verse: Once again, Abraham bowed down
translation_verse: Abraham bɔbɔ ta le Xitiviawo ŋkume,

english_verse: and said to Ephron, “In front of these witnesses, I offer you the full price, so I can bury my wife. Please accept my offer.”
translation_verse: eye wòƒo nu na Efron, dua me tɔwo katã see be: “Taflatsɛ, see ɖa nam. Na maxe fe ɖe anyigba la ta. Ga lae nye esi; xɔe, ne maɖi nye ame kukua ɖe edzi.”

english_verse: So Abraham buried his wife Sarah in Machpelah Cave that was in the field
translation_verse: Esia megbe la, Abraham ɖi srɔ̃a Sara ɖe kpeto la me le Maxpela, le Mamre ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome , le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Abraham was now a very old man. The Lord had made him rich, and he was successful in everything he did.
translation_verse: Azɔ Abraham tsi xɔ ƒè geɖee, eye Aƒetɔ yrae le nu sia nu me.

english_verse: One day, Abraham called in his most trusted servant and said to him, “Solemnly promise me
translation_verse: Abraham gblɔ na eƒe dɔla tsitsitɔ si kpɔa eƒe nunɔamesiwo katã dzi la be: “Tsɔ asi de nye atame,

english_verse: in the name of the Lord, who rules heaven and earth, that you won't choose a wife for my son Isaac from the people here in the land of Canaan.
translation_verse: ne natà Aƒetɔ, dziƒo kple anyigba ƒe Mawu la nam, be yemaɖe srɔ̃ na vinye tso Kanaantɔ siwo dome mele la vinyɔnuwo dome o,

english_verse: Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for him from among my relatives.”
translation_verse: ke boŋ yeayi mía denyigba dzi, aɖaɖe srɔ̃ na vinye Isak tso nye ƒometɔwo dome.”

english_verse: But the servant asked, “What if the young woman I choose refuses to leave home and come here with me? Should I send Isaac there to look for a wife?”
translation_verse: Ke dɔla la gblɔ nɛ be: “Ɖewohĩ nyɔnua malɔ̃ be yeakplɔm ɖo ava anyigba sia dzi o. Ekema makplɔ viwò la gbugbɔ yi anyigba si dzi nèʋu tso la dzia?”

english_verse: “No!” Abraham answered. “Don't ever do that, no matter what.
translation_verse: Abraham ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Kpɔ nyuie be màgagbugbɔ vinye la ayi afi mae o!

english_verse: The Lord who rules heaven brought me here from the land where I was born and promised that he would give this land to my descendants forever. When you go back there, the Lord will send his angel ahead of you to help you find a wife for my son.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, dziƒo ƒe Mawu la, ame si ɖem ɖa tso tɔ́nye ƒeme kple mía denyigba dzi, eye wòdo anyigba sia ŋugbe nam be: ‘Wò dzidzimeviwo matsɔ anyigba sia ana’ la, adɔ eƒe dɔla wòanɔ ŋgɔwò, nàɖaɖe srɔ̃ na vinye ŋutsu tso afi ma.

english_verse: If the woman refuses to come along, you don't have to keep this promise. But don't ever take my son back there.”
translation_verse: Ke ne nyɔnua melɔ̃ be yeakplɔ wò ɖo ava o la, ekema menye wòe tu atam sia o; ɖeko mègakplɔ vinye la va yi afi mae gbeɖe o!”

english_verse: So the servant gave Abraham his word that he would do everything he had been told to do.
translation_verse: Ale dɔla la tsɔ asi de Abraham, eƒe aƒetɔ la, ƒe atame, eye wòka atam nɛ ɖe nya la dzi.

english_verse: Soon after that, the servant loaded ten of Abraham's camels with valuable gifts. Then he set out for the city in northern Syria, where Abraham's brother Nahor lived.
translation_verse: Dɔla la tia eƒe aƒetɔ la ƒe kposɔ ewo, tsɔ eƒe nu nyui vovovo aɖewo hã ɖe asi, eye wòdze mɔ yi ɖe du si me Naxor nɔ le Mesopotamia ƒe dzigbeme la me.

english_verse: When he got there, he let the camels rest near the well outside the city. It was late afternoon, the time when the women came out for water.
translation_verse: Ena eƒe kposɔawo tsyɔ akɔ anyi ɖe vudo aɖe to le dua godo le fiẽ, le nyɔnuwo ƒe tɔmedeɣi.

english_verse: The servant prayed: You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships. Please keep your promise to him and let me find a wife for Isaac today.
translation_verse: Dɔla la do gbe ɖa be: “Aƒetɔ, nye aƒetɔ Abraham ƒe Mawu! Meɖe kuku, na nu si gbe meva la, nadze dzi nam egbe, eye nànyo dɔme na nye aƒetɔ Abraham.

english_verse: The young women of the city will soon come to this well for water,
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, mele tsitre ɖe vudoa to fifia, eye dua me ɖetugbiwo gbɔna tsi du ge le afii.

english_verse: and I'll ask one of them for a drink. If she gives me a drink and then offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen and that you have kept your promise to my master.
translation_verse: Na ɖetugbi si magblɔ na be: ‘Meɖe kuku, dro wò tsize ɖi ne mano tsi’, eye wòagblɔ be: ‘Noe, eye mana wò kposɔwo hã woano’ la, nenye ame si dzi nètɔ asii na wò dɔla Isak. To esia me madze sii be ève nye aƒetɔ nu.”

english_verse: Abraham's servant ran to her and said, “Please let me have a drink of water.”
translation_verse: Tete dɔla la ƒu du yi ɖakpee gblɔ nɛ be: “Meɖe kuku, na tsi vi aɖem mano!”

english_verse: “I'll be glad to,” she answered. Then she quickly took the jar from her shoulder and held it while he drank.
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: “Amegã, va no faa.” Edro ze la ɖi enumake, eye wòna tsi lae wòno.

english_verse: After he had finished, she said, “Now I'll give your camels all the water they want.” She quickly poured out water for them, and she kept going back for more, until his camels had drunk all they wanted.
translation_verse: Ewɔ kaba, trɔ tsia kɔ ɖe lãwo ƒe tsinonu me, eye wògaƒu du ɖi ɖe vudoa me ɖadu tsia gava trɔ ɖi na kposɔawo va se ɖe esime wo katã no tsi, wòɖi kɔ na wo.

english_verse: Abraham's servant did not say a word, but he watched everything Rebekah did, because he wanted to know for certain if this was the woman the Lord had chosen.
translation_verse: Ŋutsu la li kpoo nɔ ekpɔm dũu, ne yeakpɔ ɖa be Aƒetɔ ana nu si gbe yeva la nadze edzi na ye mahã.

english_verse: The servant had brought along an expensive gold ring and two large gold bracelets. When Rebekah had finished bringing the water, he gave her the ring for her nose and the bracelets for her arms.
translation_verse: Esi kposɔawo no tsia vɔ la, ŋutsua ɖe sikasigɛ si ƒe kpekpeme anɔ gram ade kple sikalɔnuga eve siwo ƒe kpekpeme anɔ sika gram alafa ɖeka wui ene la, do na ɖetugbi la.

english_verse: Then he said, “Please tell me who your father is. Does he have room in his house for me and my men to spend the night?”
translation_verse: Azɔ ebiae be: “Ame ka vi nènye? Míate ŋu akpɔ dzeƒe le tɔ́wò ƒemea?”

english_verse: She answered, “My father is Bethuel, the son of Nahor and Milcah.
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Betuel, Milka vi, si wòdzi na Naxor la vinyɔnu menye.”

english_verse: We have a place where you and your men can stay, and we also have enough straw and feed for your camels.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ yi edzi be: “Aƒla kple gbe le mía si fũu, eye dzeƒe hã li.”

english_verse: Then the servant bowed his head and prayed,
translation_verse: Ŋutsua dze klo, eye wòdo gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ

english_verse: “I thank you, Lord God of my master Abraham! You have led me to his relatives and kept your promise to him.”
translation_verse: be: “Woakafu Aƒetɔ, nye aƒetɔ Abraham ƒe Mawu la. Ekpɔa eta, vea enu, eye wòwɔa nuteƒe nɛ ɖaa. Le gonye me la, Aƒetɔ fia mɔm, eye wòkplɔm tẽe va nye aƒetɔ ƒomeawo gbɔe.”

english_verse: Rebekah ran straight home and told her family everything.
translation_verse: Ɖetugbia ƒu du yi aƒeme ɖagblɔ nya siawo na nɔa ƒemetɔwo.

english_verse: Her brother Laban heard her tell what the servant had said, and he saw the ring and the bracelets she was wearing. So Laban ran out to Abraham's servant, who was standing by his camels at the well.
translation_verse: Do ŋgɔ la, Laban kpɔ ŋɔtigɛ kple alɔnuga le nɔvia nyɔnu ŋu, eye wòse nya siwo wòbe ŋutsua gblɔ na ye la hã. Eyi ɖatu ŋutsua wòle tsitre ɖe kposɔawo gbɔ le vudoa to.

english_verse: Then Laban said, “The Lord has brought you safely here. Come home with me. There's no need for you to keep on standing outside. I have a room ready for you in our house, and there's also a place for your camels.”
translation_verse: Laban gblɔ nɛ be: “Wò ame si Aƒetɔ yra, va míyi aƒeme. Nu ka ta nètsi tsitre ɖe gbɔto le afii? Medzra xɔ me ɖo ɖi na wò. Teƒe li na wò kposɔawo hã.”

english_verse: Abraham's servant went home with Laban, where Laban's servants unloaded his camels and gave them straw and feed. Then they brought water into the house, so Abraham's servant and his men could wash their feet.
translation_verse: Esi wòkplɔ ŋutsua va aƒeme la, etu agbaawo le kposɔawo dzi, eye wòna gbe wo woɖu. Eku tsi vɛ na ŋutsua kple ame siwo katã kpe ɖe eŋuti la be woaklɔ afɔ.

english_verse: After that, they brought in food. But the servant said, “Before I eat, I must tell you why I have come.” “Go ahead and tell us,” Laban answered.
translation_verse: Ke esi wotsɔ nuɖuɖu va ɖo ŋutsua kɔme la, egblɔ be: “Nyemaɖu nu o, va se ɖe esime megblɔ afɔ si dzi mele la na mi gbã.” Laban ɖo eŋu be: “Ƒo nu faa!”

english_verse: The servant explained: I am Abraham's servant.
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: “Abraham ƒe dɔlae menye.

english_verse: The Lord has been good to my master and has made him very rich. He has given him many sheep, goats, cattle, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of silver and gold, and many slaves.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ yra nye aƒetɔ ŋutɔ, eye wòzu nunɔamesitɔ gã ale gbegbe. Ena alẽha kple nyiha, klosalo kple sika, kluviwo kple kosiwo, kposɔwo kple tedziwoe fũu.

english_verse: Sarah, my master's wife, didn't have any children until she was very old. Then she had a son, and my master has given him everything.
translation_verse: Nye aƒetɔ srɔ̃, Sara, togbɔ be eku nyagã hã, edzi viŋutsu nɛ, eye nye aƒetɔ tsɔ eƒe nunɔamesiwo katã na via.

english_verse: I solemnly promised my master that I would do what he said. And he told me, “Don't choose a wife for my son from the women in this land of Canaan.
translation_verse: Nye aƒetɔ na meka atam nɛ be mawɔ ŋugbe si medo nɛ la dzi. Egblɔ nam be, ‘Mègaɖe srɔ̃ na vinye tso Kanaantɔ siwo dome mele la vinyɔnuwo dome o;

english_verse: Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for my son from among my relatives.”
translation_verse: ke boŋ yi ɖe ƒonyemeawo gbɔ, le tɔ́nye ƒeme, eye nàɖe srɔ̃ na vinye tso afi ma.

english_verse: I asked my master, “What if the young woman refuses to come with me?”
translation_verse: Azɔ mebia nye aƒetɔ be: ‘Ke ne nyɔnua melɔ̃ be yeakplɔm ɖo ava o ɖe, nu ka mawɔ?’

english_verse: My master answered, “I have always obeyed the Lord, and he will send his angel to help you find my son a wife from among my own relatives.
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu nam be: ‘Aƒetɔ, ame si meɖoa toe ɣe sia ɣi la, adɔ eƒe dɔla wòayi kpli wò, eye wòana nu si gbe nèyi la nadze dzi na wò, ale be nàɖe srɔ̃ na vinye tso ƒonyemeawo gbɔ le tɔ́nye ƒeme.

english_verse: But if they refuse to let her come back with you, then you are freed from your promise.”
translation_verse: Evɔ ne èyi ƒonyemeawo gbɔ, eye womelɔ̃ tsɔ ɖetugbi aɖeke na wò o la, ekema menye wòe tu nye atam la o.’

english_verse: When I came to the well today, I silently prayed, “You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships, so please lead me to a wife for his son
translation_verse: “Esi meva ɖo vudoa to egbea la, medo gbe ɖa be: ‘Aƒetɔ, nye aƒetɔ Abraham ƒe Mawu! Meɖe kuku, na be nu si wɔ ge meva la, nadze dzi nam.

english_verse: while I am here at the well. When a young woman comes out to get water, I'll ask her to give me a drink.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, mele tsitre ɖe vudoa to. Nenye be ɖetugbi aɖe va tsi du ge la, mele ebia ge be wòana tsi vi aɖem mano.

english_verse: If she gives me a drink and offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen.”
translation_verse: Ne eɖo eŋu nam be: ‘Noe faa, eye mana wò kposɔawo hã woano’ la, ekema na be eya nanye nyɔnu si nètia da ɖi na nye aƒetɔ viŋutsu la be wòaɖe.’

english_verse: Even before I had finished praying, Rebekah came by with a water jar on her shoulder. When she had filled the jar, I asked her for a drink.
translation_verse: Nyemekpɔ do gbea ɖa le tame vɔ o, kasia Rebeka va do. Elé ze ɖe abɔta, eye wòɖi ɖe vudoa me ɖaku tsia do va. Megblɔ nɛ be: ‘Meɖe kuku, na tsim mano!’

english_verse: She quickly lowered the jar from her shoulder and said, “Have a drink. Then I'll get water for your camels.” So I drank, and after that she got some water for my camels.
translation_verse: Edro ze la ɖi enumake hegblɔ be: ‘Noe; mana wò kposɔawo hã.’ Esi meno tsia vɔ la, ena kposɔawo hã wono.

english_verse: I asked her who her father was, and she answered, “My father is Bethuel the son of Nahor and Milcah.” At once I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
translation_verse: Azɔ mebiae be: ‘Ame ka vi nènye?’ Eɖo eŋu nam be: ‘Betuel viŋutsu si Milka dzi na Naxor la vinyɔnue menye.’ Ale metsɔ ŋɔtigɛ la do nɛ hetsɔ alɔnuga la hã do ɖe alɔnu nɛ.

english_verse: Then I bowed my head and gave thanks to the God my master Abraham worships. The Lord had led me straight to my master's relatives, and I had found a wife for his son.
translation_verse: Tete mebɔbɔ tsyɔ mo anyi hedo gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ. Mekafu Aƒetɔ, nye aƒetɔ Abraham ƒe Mawu la, ame si kplɔm tẽe va nye aƒetɔ nɔviwo gbɔ tututu be maɖe srɔ̃ na via tso wo dome.

english_verse: Now please tell me if you are willing to do the right thing for my master. Will you treat him fairly, or do I have to look for another young woman?
translation_verse: Azɔ ne mielɔ̃ be yewoave nye aƒetɔ la nu, awɔ nuteƒe nɛ la, taflatsɛ, migblɔe nam. Ke ne mielɔ̃ o hã la, migblɔe nam bene manya nu si mawɔ.”

english_verse: Laban and Bethuel answered, “The Lord has done this. We have no choice in the matter.
translation_verse: Tete Laban kple Betuel woɖo eŋu be: “Esi wònye Aƒetɔ gbɔe nya sia tso ta la, míawo míate ŋu alɔ̃ alo agbe o.

english_verse: Take Rebekah with you; she can marry your master's son, just as the Lord has said.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, Rebekae nye esi; kplɔe yii faa, ne wòazu wò aƒetɔ ƒe vi la srɔ̃ abe ale si Aƒetɔ la gblɔe ene.”

english_verse: Then he gave clothing, as well as silver and gold jewelry, to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and her mother.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, dɔla la ɖe klosalo kple sika nuwo kple avɔ xɔasiwo ɖe go tsɔ na Rebeka. Etsɔ nunana xɔasi geɖewo hã na nɔvia ŋutsua kple nɔa.

english_verse: Abraham's servant and the men with him ate and drank, then spent the night there. The next morning they got up, and the servant told Rebekah's mother and brother, “I would like to go back to my master now.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Abraham ƒe dɔla la kple ame siwo kpe ɖe eŋu la ɖu nu, no nu, eye wotsi afi ma dɔ. Esi wofɔ ŋdi la, ŋutsua gblɔ be: “Mido mɔm ne matrɔ yi nye aƒetɔ gbɔ.”

english_verse: “Let Rebekah stay with us for a week or ten days,” they answered. “Then she may go.”
translation_verse: Ke Rebeka nɔviŋutsua kple nɔa gblɔ na ŋutsua be: “Na ɖetugbi la nanɔ mía gbɔ ʋɛ abe ŋkeke ewo ene, ema megbe la, ate ŋu ayi faa.”

english_verse: But he said, “Don't make me stay any longer. The Lord has already helped me find a wife for my master's son. Now let us return.”
translation_verse: Ke eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Migazi mía dzi be míatsi anyi o. Esi Aƒetɔ na nu si wɔ ge meva la dze dzi nam ta la, mido mɔm ne matrɔ yi nye aƒetɔ gbɔ.”

english_verse: They answered, “Let's ask Rebekah what she wants to do.”
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Míayɔ ɖetugbi la ŋutɔ vɛ abiae se.”

english_verse: They called her and asked, “Are you willing to leave with this man at once?” “Yes,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ale woyɔ Rebeka vɛ hebiae be: “Àyi kple ŋutsu siaa?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Ẽ, mayi.”

english_verse: So they agreed to let Rebekah and an old family servant woman leave immediately with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Ale wodo mɔ wo nɔvi Rebeka kple nyɔnu si tsɔe wòtsi la, wodzo yi kple Abraham ƒe dɔla la kple eŋumewo.

english_verse: They gave Rebekah their blessing and said, “We pray that God will give you many children and grandchildren and that he will help them defeat their enemies.”
translation_verse: Woyra Rebeka gblɔ nɛ be: “Wò, mía nɔvinyɔnu, nàva zu ame akpe nanewo nɔ. Wò dzidzimeviwo neɖu woƒe futɔwo dzi; wonexɔ woƒe duwo woazu wo tɔ!”

english_verse: Afterwards, Rebekah and the young women who were to travel with her prepared to leave. Then they got on camels and left with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Rebeka kple eƒe nyɔnudɔlawo dzra ɖo, de kposɔwo dzi, eye wodze ŋutsua yome dzo. Ale ŋutsua kplɔ Rebeka dzoe.

english_verse: One evening he was walking out in the fields, when suddenly he saw a group of people approaching on camels. So he started toward them. Rebekah saw him coming; she got down from her camel, and asked, “Who is that man?” “He is my master Isaac,” the servant answered. Then Rebekah covered her face with her veil.
translation_verse: Ebia dɔla la be: “Ŋutsu kae nye ekem le gbea dzi, zɔ gbɔna ɖe mía gbɔ?” Dɔla la ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Nye aƒetɔe.” Tete wòtsɔ motsyɔnu tsyɔ mo.

english_verse: The servant told Isaac everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Le esia megbe la, dɔla la gblɔ ale si wòde nua gbee la na Isak tsitotsito.

english_verse: Isaac took Rebekah into the tent where his mother had lived before she died, and Rebekah became his wife. He loved her and was comforted over the loss of his mother.
translation_verse: Azɔ Isak kplɔ Rebeka yi ɖe nɔa, Sara, ƒe agbadɔme. Eɖee wòzu srɔ̃a, eye wòlɔ̃e vevie. Ale Isak ƒe ŋku va ɖe ɖa le nɔa ƒe ku ŋu, eye eƒe dzi dze eme.

english_verse: and they had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
translation_verse: Eya dzi Simran, Yoksan, Medan, Midian, Yisbak kple Suax nɛ.

english_verse: Later, Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan, and when Dedan grew up, he had three sons: Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
translation_verse: Yoksan dzi Seba kple Dedan. Dedan ƒe dzidzimeviwoe nye: Asuritɔwo, Letusitɔwo kple Leumitɔwo.

english_verse: Midian also had five sons: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah.
translation_verse: Midian viŋutsuwoe nye Efa, Efer, Henox, Abida kple Edaa. Ame siawo katã nye Ketura ƒe dzidzimeviwo.

english_verse: While Abraham was still alive, he gave gifts to the sons of Hagar and Keturah. He also sent their sons to live in the east far from his son Isaac, and when Abraham died, he left everything to Isaac. The Death of Abraham
translation_verse: ke le eƒe agbenɔɣi la, Abraham na nu viŋutsu siwo eƒe ahiãviwo dzi nɛ la, eye wòdo mɔ wo ɖo ɖe anyigba si le ɣedzeƒe gome la dzi bene woaɖe ɖa le Isak ŋu. Abraham ku, eye woɖii

english_verse: Abraham died at the ripe old age of
translation_verse: Abraham ku esime wòtsi xɔ ƒè geɖee, eye wòzu amegãɖeɖi belibeli hafi yi tɔgbuiawo gbɔ.

english_verse: God blessed Isaac after this, and Isaac moved to a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.” Ishmael's Descendants
translation_verse: Mawu yra Isak le tɔ́a Abraham ƒe ku megbe, eye wònɔ afi si woyɔna be “Agbe tɔ si le kpɔyem la ƒe Vudo.” Ismael ƒe dzidzimeviwo

english_verse: Ishmael was the son of Abraham and Hagar, the slave woman of Sarah.
translation_verse: Ismael, ame si Egipte-nyɔnu Hagar, Sara ƒe kosi, dzi na Abraham la,

english_verse: Ishmael had twelve sons, in this order: Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
translation_verse: viwo ŋkɔwoe nye esiwo gbɔna ɖe woƒe tsitsime nu: Nebayot, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

english_verse: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
translation_verse: Misma, Duma, Masa,

english_verse: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
translation_verse: Xadad, Tema, Yetur, Nafis kple Kedma.

english_verse: Each of Ishmael's sons was a tribal chief, and a village was named after each of them.
translation_verse: Ame siawoe nye Ismael viŋutsuwo, eye esiawoe nye woƒe ŋkɔwo ɖe woƒe du suewo kple woƒe asaɖawo nu; amegã wui eve ɖe woƒe towo nu.

english_verse: Ishmael had settled in the land east of his brothers, and his sons settled everywhere from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt on the way to Asshur. Ishmael was
translation_verse: Eƒe dzidzimeviwoe nɔ Xavila kple Sur dome le Egipte ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome ɖo ta Asiria. Woawo sa wo ɖokui ɖe aga tso Abraham ƒe dzidzimevi bubuawo gbɔ. Wodzi Esau kple Yakob

english_verse: Isaac was the son of Abraham,
translation_verse: Abraham vi Isak hã ƒe dzidzimeŋutinyae nye esi:

english_verse: Rebekah still had no children. So Isaac asked the Lord to let her have a child, and the Lord answered his prayer.
translation_verse: Rebeka tsi ko eya ta Isak do gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ vevie ɖe eta. Aƒetɔ se eƒe kukuɖeɖe la, eye Rebeka fɔ fu.

english_verse: Before Rebekah gave birth, she knew she was going to have twins, because she could feel them inside her, fighting each other. She thought, “Why is this happening to me?” Finally, she asked the Lord why her twins were fighting,
translation_verse: Ɖeviawo nɔ ʋiʋlim le eƒe dɔme. Ale ebia eɖokui be: “Nu ka tae nu sia ƒomevi le wɔyem?” eye wòyi ɖabia Aƒetɔ se.

english_verse: and he told her: “Your two sons will become two separate nations. The younger of the two will be stronger, and the older son will be his servant.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Dukɔ evee le wò dɔ me. Àdzi dukɔ eve siwo aʋli nu kple wo nɔewo. Ɖeka asesẽ wu nɔvia; tsitsitɔ asubɔ ɖevitɔ.”

english_verse: the first baby was covered with red hair, so he was named Esau.
translation_verse: Gbãtɔ do. Ebiã hẽe, eye fu le eŋu kedzekedze, eya ta wona ŋkɔe be Esau.

english_verse: The second baby grabbed on to his brother's heel, so they named him Jacob. Isaac was
translation_verse: Evelia hã va do, eye wòlé Esau ƒe afɔkpodzi ɖe asi, eya ta wona ŋkɔe be Yakob. Isak xɔ ƒe bla ade esime wodzi ɖeviawo. Esau ɖɔli eƒe ŋgɔgbevinyenye

english_verse: As Jacob and Esau grew older, Esau liked the outdoors and became a good hunter, while Jacob lived the quiet life of a shepherd.
translation_verse: Esi ɖeviawo va tsi la, Esau zu adela, eye wòlɔ̃a adegbedede. Ke Yakob ya nye ame fafa, eye wòlɔ̃a aƒeme nɔnɔ.

english_verse: Esau would take the meat of wild animals to his father Isaac, so Isaac loved him more, but Jacob was his mother's favorite son.
translation_verse: Isak lɔ̃ Esau ƒe nya elabe adelã vivia enu; ke Rebeka ya lɔ̃ Yakob.

english_verse: One day, when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came home hungry
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la, Yakob nɔ nu ɖam. Esau tso adegbe gbɔ, eye dɔ nɔ ewum kutɔkutɔe.

english_verse: and said, “I'm starving to death! Here and now give me some of that red stew!” That's how Esau got the name “Edom.”
translation_verse: Esau gblɔ na Yakob be: “Dɔ le wuyem, mebe maku. Na nuɖuɖu dzĩ ma ƒe ɖem maɖu.” Eya ta wotsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Edom.

english_verse: Jacob replied, “Sell me your rights as the first-born son.”
translation_verse: Yakob ɖo eŋu be: “Dzra wò ŋgɔgbevinyenye nam gbã gbɔ.”

english_verse: “I'm about to die,” Esau answered. “What good will those rights do me?”
translation_verse: Esau gblɔ be: “Dɔ le wuyem, mebe makua, nu ka koŋ ŋgɔgbevinyenye awɔ nam?”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “Promise me your birthrights, here and now!” And that's what Esau did.
translation_verse: Yakob be: “Ka atam nam gbã gbɔ.” Tete Esau ka atam na Yakob, eye wòtsɔ eƒe ŋgɔgbevinyenye dzra nɛ.

english_verse: Jacob then gave Esau some bread and some of the bean stew, and when Esau had finished eating and drinking, he just got up and left, showing how little he thought of his rights as the first-born.
translation_verse: Azɔ Yakob na abolo kple ayidetsi la Esau. Eɖu nua, no tsi ɖe edzi, eye wòtso dzo. Aleae Esau wɔ, do vlo eƒe ŋgɔgbevinyenye nye esi.

english_verse: Once during Abraham's lifetime, the fields had not produced enough grain, and now the same thing happened. So Isaac went to King Abimelech of the Philistines in the land of Gerar,
translation_verse: Dɔ gato le anyigba la dzi, abe ale si wòto le Abraham ŋɔli ene. Ale Isak ʋu yi ɖe Filistitɔwo ƒe fia Abimelex gbɔ le Gerar.

english_verse: because the Lord had appeared to Isaac and said: Isaac, stay away from Egypt! I will show you where I want you to go.
translation_verse: Do ŋgɔ la, Aƒetɔ ɖe eɖokui fiae, gblɔ nɛ be: “Mègayi Egipte o; ke boŋ nɔ anyigba si mafia wò la dzi.

english_verse: You will live there as a foreigner, but I will be with you and bless you. I will keep my promise to your father Abraham by giving this land to you and your descendants.
translation_verse: Nɔ afi ma, eye manɔ kpli wò, ayra wò, elabe matsɔ anyigba blibo sia katã ana wò kple wò dzidzimeviwo. Mawɔ atam si meka na tɔ́wò Abraham la dzi godoo.

english_verse: I will give you as many descendants as there are stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all of this land. They will be a blessing to every nation on earth,
translation_verse: Mana wò dzidzimeviwo nasɔ gbɔ abe ɣletiviwo le dziƒo ene, eye matsɔ anyigba sia katã ana wò. Wò dzidzimeviwo dzi woato ayra anyigba dzi dukɔwo katã.

english_verse: because Abraham did everything I told him to do.
translation_verse: Mayra wò elabe Abraham ɖo tom, eye wòwɔ nye sededewo kple ɖoɖowo kpakple mɔnu siwo mefiae la dzi.”

english_verse: Isaac moved to Gerar
translation_verse: Ale Isak nɔ Gerar.

english_verse: with his beautiful wife Rebekah. He was afraid that someone might kill him to get her, and so he told everyone that Rebekah was his sister.
translation_verse: Esi afi ma ŋutsuwo bia be ame kae nye srɔ̃a hã la, egblɔ na wo be ye nɔvinyɔnue. Egblɔ alea, elabe evɔ̃ be ne yegblɔ be ye srɔ̃e la, woawu ye le Rebeka ta, elabe edze tugbe ŋutɔ.

english_verse: After Isaac had been there a long time, King Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac hugging and kissing Rebekah.
translation_verse: Esi wonɔ afi ma eteƒe didi la, gbe ɖeka Abimelex kpɔ Isak to fesre nu wònɔ fefem kple Rebeka srɔ̃tɔe.

english_verse: Abimelech called him in and said, “Rebekah must be your wife! Why did you say she is your sister?” “Because I thought someone would kill me,” Isaac answered.
translation_verse: Ale Abimelex yɔ Isak vɛ, eye wòbiae be: “Srɔ̃wòe nye nyɔnuae! Nu ka ta nègblɔ be ye nɔvinyɔnue?” Isak ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Mebu be ne megblɔ be srɔ̃nye wònye la, woawum.”

english_verse: “Don't you know what you've done?” Abimelech exclaimed. “If someone had slept with her, you would have made our whole nation guilty!”
translation_verse: Abimelex gblɔ nɛ be: “Nu kae nye esi nèwɔ mí kloe? Esusɔ vie ŋunyemewo dometɔ ɖeka dɔ kple srɔ̃wò kloe, ne nàhe fɔbubu va mía dzi.”

english_verse: Then Abimelech warned his people that anyone who even touched Isaac or Rebekah would be put to death.
translation_verse: Ale Abimelex de se na eteviwo katã be: “Ame aɖeke megawɔ naneke ŋutsu sia kple srɔ̃a o. Ne ame aɖe ka asi ŋutsu sia kple srɔ̃a ŋu la, woawui kokoko.”

english_verse: Isaac planted grain and had a good harvest that same year. The Lord blessed him,
translation_verse: Isak de agble ɖe anyigba la dzi, eye nu si wòŋe le ƒè ma me la de esi wòƒã la ƒe teƒe alafa ɖeka sɔŋ elabe Aƒetɔ yrae.

english_verse: and Isaac was so successful that he became very rich.
translation_verse: Eva zu kesinɔtɔ gã ale gbegbe. Ɖeko eƒe nukpɔkpɔwo nɔ dzidzim ɖe dzi, ganɔ dzidzim ɖe dzi.

english_verse: In fact, the Philistines were jealous of the large number of sheep, goats, and slaves that Isaac owned,
translation_verse: Alẽhawo kple nyihawo sɔ gbɔ ɖe esi ale gbegbe, eye kluviwo hã nɔ esi fũu. Ale Filistitɔwo va ʋã ŋui.

english_verse: and they stopped up the wells that Abraham's servants had dug before his death.
translation_verse: Woku anyi xe vudo siwo katã tɔ́a Abraham ƒe dɔlawo ɖe esime wònɔ agbe la keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: Finally, Abimelech said, “Isaac, I want you to leave our country. You have become too powerful to stay here.”
translation_verse: Abimelex gblɔ na Isak be: “Dzo le mía dome, elabe èva kpɔ ŋusẽ wu mí.”

english_verse: where he cleaned out those wells that the Philistines had stopped up. Isaac also gave each of the wells the same name that Abraham had given to them.
translation_verse: Egbugbɔ vudo siwo woɖe le tɔ́a Abraham ŋɔli la ɖe, eye wògatsɔ ŋkɔ siwo tɔ́a Abraham na wo tsã la na wo. Vudo siawoe Filistitɔwo xe tsã le Abraham ƒe ku megbe.

english_verse: While his servants were digging in the valley, they found a spring-fed well.
translation_verse: Isak ƒe dɔlawo ɖe vudo ɖe balia me, eye woke ɖe tsidzidzi ŋu.

english_verse: But the shepherds of Gerar Valley quarreled with Isaac's shepherds and claimed the water belonged to them. So this well was named “Quarrel,” because they had quarreled with Isaac.
translation_verse: Ke Gerartɔwo ƒe lãnyilawo wɔ dzre kple Isak ƒe lãnyilawo gblɔ be: “Míaƒe tsie.” Eya ta Isak na ŋkɔ vudoa be Esek elabe wowɔ dzre kplii ɖe vudoa ta.

english_verse: Isaac's servants dug another well, and the shepherds also quarreled about it. So that well was named “Jealous.”
translation_verse: Wogaɖe vudo bubu ɖe ema yome, eye wogawɔ dzre ɖe eya hã ta, eya ta wòna ŋkɔe be Fuléle.

english_verse: Finally, they dug one more well. There was no quarreling this time, and the well was named “Lots of Room,” because the Lord had given them room and would make them very successful.
translation_verse: Eʋu le afi ma ɖo ta ŋgɔ, eye wògaɖe vudo bubu. Womewɔ dzre ɖe esia ya ta o, ale wòna ŋkɔe be “Vovoƒe.” Egblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ na vovoƒe mí azɔ be míanɔ anyigba sia dzi, adzi ɖe dzi, akeke ta.”

english_verse: Isaac went on to Beersheba,
translation_verse: Emegbe Isak ʋu le afi ma yi Beer-Seba.

english_verse: where the Lord appeared to him that night and told him, “Don't be afraid! I am the God who was worshiped by your father Abraham, my servant. I will be with you and bless you, and because of Abraham I will give you many descendants.”
translation_verse: Gbe si gbe wòʋu yi ƒe zã me la, Aƒetɔ ɖe eɖokui fiae gblɔ nɛ be: “Nyee nye tɔ́wò Abraham ƒe Mawu. Mègavɔ̃ o; meli kpli wò. Le nye dɔla Abraham ta la, mayra wò, eye mana wò dzidzimeviwo nasɔ gbɔ ɖe dzi.”

english_verse: Isaac built an altar there and worshiped the Lord. Then he set up camp, and his servants started digging a well.
translation_verse: Ale wòɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afi ma, eye wòsubɔ Aƒetɔ. Etu agbadɔ ɖi, eye eƒe dɔlawo gaɖe vudo bubu. Isak kple Abimelex wɔ ŋutifafa

english_verse: Meanwhile, Abimelech had left Gerar and was taking his advisor Ahuzzath and his army commander Phicol to see Isaac.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la, Abimelex kple eƒe aɖaŋuɖola, Ahusat kpakple eƒe aʋakplɔla, Pixol, wova Isak gbɔ be yewoakpɔe.

english_verse: When they arrived, Isaac asked, “Why are you here? Didn't you send me away because you hated me?”
translation_verse: Isak bia wo be: “Nu ka tae mieva gbɔnye? Menye miawoe lé fum, nyàm le mia dome oa?”

english_verse: They answered, “We now know for certain that the Lord is with you, and we have decided there needs to be a peace treaty between you and us. So let's make a solemn agreement
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Fifia míekpɔ dze sii kɔtɛe be Aƒetɔ li kpli wò eya ta míebu be ele be mía kpli wò míaka atam na mía nɔewo. Míabla nu kpli wò,

english_verse: not to harm each other. Remember, we have never hurt you, and when we sent you away, we let you go in peace. The Lord has truly blessed you.”
translation_verse: bene nàgawɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke mí o, abe ale si míawo hã míewɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke wò va yi o la ene. Nu nyui wònye míewɔ na wò, be míena nèdzo le ŋutifafa me ale be Aƒetɔ yra wò.”

english_verse: Isaac gave a big feast for them, and everyone ate and drank.
translation_verse: Ale wòɖo kplɔ̃ na wo, eye woɖu nu, no nu nyuie.

english_verse: Early the next morning Isaac and the others made a solemn agreement, then he let them go in peace.
translation_verse: Le ŋufɔke la, wofɔ ŋdi kanya, eye wobla nu kple wo nɔewo heka atam ƒu edzi. Isak do mɔ wo, wotrɔ dzo le ŋutifafa me.

english_verse: Later that same day Isaac's servants came and said, “We've struck water!”
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe ke la, Isak ƒe dɔlawo va gblɔ vudo si woɖe la ŋu nya nɛ. Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Míeke ɖe tsi ŋu!”

english_verse: So Isaac named the well Shibah, and the town is still called Beersheba. Esau's Foreign Wives
translation_verse: Ena ŋkɔ vudoa be Siba. Eya tae woyɔa du si wotso ɖe afi ma la be “Beer-Seba” va se ɖe egbe. Esau ɖe srɔ̃ siwo menye Hebritɔwo o

english_verse: But these two women brought a lot of grief to Esau's parents Isaac and Rebekah.
translation_verse: Wona agbenɔnɔ zu veve na Isak kple Rebeka.

english_verse: Isaac was old and almost blind, when he called in his first-born son Esau, who asked him, “Father, what can I do for you?”
translation_verse: Azɔ esi Isak tsi zu amegãɖeɖi, eƒe ŋkuwo dzi tsyɔ, eye megate ŋu le nu kpɔm o la, eyɔ via tsitsitɔ, Esau, vɛ hegblɔ nɛ be: “Vinye!” Etɔ be: “Nyee nye esi.”

english_verse: Isaac replied, “I am old and might die at any time.
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, metsi, eye nyemenya nye kugbe o.

english_verse: So go hunting with your bow and arrows and kill a wild animal.
translation_verse: Tsɔ wò adedanuwo, da kple dati, eye nàyi gbe me nàɖawu lã aɖe vɛ nam.

english_verse: Cook some of that tasty food that I love so much and bring it to me. I want to eat it once more and give you my blessing before I die.”
translation_verse: Nàtsɔ lã la wɔ nuɖuɖu si vivia nunye ŋutɔ la vɛ nam maɖu, ne mayra wò hafi maku.”

english_verse: Rebekah had been listening, and as soon as Esau left to go hunting,
translation_verse: Rebeka se nya si Isak gblɔ na Esau la. Ale esi Esau dzo yi adegbe be yeaɖawu lã vɛ la,

english_verse: she said to Jacob, “I heard your father tell Esau
translation_verse: Rebeka gblɔ na via Yakob be: “Mese tɔ́wò gblɔ na nɔviwò be:

english_verse: to kill a wild animal and cook some tasty food for him before he dies. Your father said this because he wants to bless your brother with the Lord as his witness.
translation_verse: ‘Di adelã aɖe nàwɔ nuɖuɖu si vivia nunye vevie la vɛ nam maɖu ne mayra wò, le Aƒetɔ ŋkume hafi maku.’

english_verse: Now, my son, listen carefully to what I want you to do.
translation_verse: Azɔ vinye, se nya si gblɔ ge mala na wò la, eye nàwɔ edzi.

english_verse: Go and kill two of your best young goats and bring them to me. I'll cook the tasty food that your father loves so much.
translation_verse: Yi lãhawo dome nàlé gbɔ̃vi eve vɛ ne matsɔ wɔ nuɖuɖu si vivia tɔ́wò nu la nɛ,

english_verse: Then you can take it to him, so he can eat it and give you his blessing before he dies.”
translation_verse: eye nàtsɔe ayi na tɔ́wò wòaɖu ne wòayra wò hafi aku.”

english_verse: “My brother Esau is a hairy man,” Jacob reminded her. “And I am not.
translation_verse: Ke Yakob gblɔ na nɔa Rebeka be: “Kpɔ ɖa, fu mele ŋunye o, evɔ nɔvinye Esau ya la, fúme wònye.

english_verse: If my father touches me and realizes I am trying to trick him, he will put a curse on me instead of giving me a blessing.”
translation_verse: Ɖewohĩ tɔ́nye ali asi ŋunye kpɔ, ale wòadze sim. Ekema abum ameflulae, eye mayram o, ke aƒo fi boŋ adem.”

english_verse: Rebekah insisted, “Let his curse fall on me! Just do what I say and bring me the meat.”
translation_verse: Nɔa ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Vinye, ne eƒo fi de wò la, neɖi ŋunye. Wò ya ɖo tom; yi nàlé lãawo vɛ ko!”

english_verse: So Jacob brought the meat to his mother, and she cooked the tasty food that his father liked.
translation_verse: Ale Yakob yi ɖalé gbɔ̃viawo vɛ na nɔa, eye wòtsɔ wo ɖa nu si vivia wo tɔ́ nu ŋutɔ la.

english_verse: Then she took Esau's best clothes and put them on Jacob.
translation_verse: Tete Rebeka tsɔ via tsitsitɔ, Esau, ƒe atsyɔ̃ɖowu siwo le egbɔ le aƒea me la do na via ɖevitɔ Yakob.

english_verse: She also covered the smooth part of his hands and neck with goatskins
translation_verse: Etsɔ gbɔ̃viawo ƒe agbalẽ bla ɖe eƒe abɔ kple kɔme siwo zrɔ̃ tsinitsini la.

english_verse: and gave him some bread and the tasty food she had cooked.
translation_verse: Etsɔ nuɖuɖu vivi si wòwɔ kple abolo si wòƒo la de Yakob si.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father and said, “Father, here I am.” “Which one of my sons are you?” his father asked.
translation_verse: Tete Yakob yi tɔ́a gbɔ yɔe be: “Tɔ́nye”. Tɔ́a tɔ hebia be: “Metɔ! Wò vinye kae?”

english_verse: Jacob replied, “I am Esau, your first-born, and I have done what you told me. Please sit up and eat the meat I have brought. Then you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Yakob ɖo eŋu be: “Nye viwò ŋgɔgbea, Esau ye. Mewɔ nu si nèbe mawɔ la. Fɔ nàɖu adelã la, ne nàyram.”

english_verse: Isaac asked, “My son, how did you find an animal so quickly?” “The Lord your God was kind to me,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Ke Isak gblɔ na via be: “Vinye, ale ke wɔ nèke ɖe eŋu kaba ale?” Yakob ɖo eŋu be: “Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu lae na lã la va kpem.”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac said, “come closer, where I can touch you and find out if you really are Esau.”
translation_verse: Tete Isak gblɔ na Yakob be: “Te ɖe ŋunye ne mali asi ŋuwò kpɔ be vinye Esau tututue nènye mahã.”

english_verse: Jacob went closer. His father touched him and said, “You sound like Jacob, but your hands feel hairy like Esau's.”
translation_verse: Yakob te ɖe tɔ́a ŋu, eye esi wòle asi lim eŋu la, egblɔ be: “Gbea nye Yakob ƒe gbe; ke asiawo ya Esau ƒe asiwoe.”

english_verse: Isaac asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” “Yes, I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: ke egabiae be: “Vinye Esau, wò tututu yea?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Ẽ, nyee!”

english_verse: So Isaac told him, “Serve me the wild meat, and I can give you my blessing.” Jacob gave him some meat, and he ate it. He also gave him some wine, and he drank it.
translation_verse: Tete Isak gblɔ be: “Tsɔ vinye ƒe adelã la vɛ maɖu ne mayra wò.” Yakob tsɔe vɛ nɛ wòɖu, eye wòna wain hãe wòno.

english_verse: Then Isaac said, “Son, come over here and kiss me.”
translation_verse: Azɔ tɔ́a gblɔ nɛ be: “Te ɖe ŋunye azɔ, vinye, ne nàgbugbɔ nu nam!”

english_verse: While Jacob was kissing him, Isaac caught the smell of his clothes and said: “The smell of my son is like a field the Lord has blessed.
translation_verse: Esi wòte ɖe eŋu gbugbɔ nu nɛ la, eʋẽ eƒe awu me se, ale wòyrae. Egblɔ be: “Ehɛ̃, vinye le ʋeʋẽm lílilĩ abe anyigba si Aƒetɔ yra la ene.

english_verse: God will bless you, my son, with dew from heaven and with fertile fields, rich with grain and grapes.
translation_verse: Mawu nena zãmu nadza tso dzi, nena wò anyigba nenyo. Nena bli kple wain nawɔ na wò fũu.

english_verse: Nations will be your servants and bow down to you. You will rule over your brothers, and they will kneel at your feet. Anyone who curses you will be cursed; anyone who blesses you will be blessed.”
translation_verse: Dukɔwo nesubɔ wò, eye ƒomewo nede ta agu na wò! Ɖu aƒetɔ ɖe nɔviwò ŋutsuwo dzi, eye dawò viwo nebɔbɔ ɖe tewò. Ame si ƒo fi de wò la, woaƒo fi adee, eye ame si yra wò la, woayra eyama.” Esau ɖe kuku na Isak be neyra ye

english_verse: Right after Isaac had given Jacob his blessing and Jacob had gone, Esau came back from hunting.
translation_verse: Esi Isak yra Yakob vɔ, eye Yakob do dzo le egbɔ teti ko la, nɔvia Esau nye esi tso adegbe gbɔ va.

english_verse: He cooked the tasty food, brought it to his father, and said, “Father, please sit up and eat the meat I have brought you, so you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Eya hã ɖa nu nyui aɖe vɛ na tɔ́a. Egblɔ nɛ be: “Tɔ́nye, meɖe kuku, fɔ nàɖu viwò ŋutsu ƒe adelã la ne nàyram.”

english_verse: “Who are you?” Isaac asked. “I am Esau, your first-born son.”
translation_verse: Isak bia be: “Wò ame kae?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Nye viwò ŋgɔgbea, Esau ye.”

english_verse: Isaac started trembling and said, “Then who brought me some wild meat right before you came in? I ate it and gave him a blessing that cannot be taken back.”
translation_verse: Vɔvɔ̃ lé Isak eye wònɔ dzodzom nyànyanya hebia be: “Ke ame kae de adegbe gbɔ tsɔ adelã vɛ nam? Ɖeko meɖu nua katã vɔ heyra amea ko nye esi nèva do. Eya tɔ ko yayra la nye. Ẽ, evɔ.”

english_verse: Esau cried out in great distress, “Father, give me a blessing too!”
translation_verse: Esi Esau se nya sia la, edo ɣli sesĩe kple vevesese be: “Oo! Tɔ́nye, yra nye hã!”

english_verse: Isaac answered, “Your brother tricked me and stole your blessing.”
translation_verse: Isak ɖo eŋu be: “Nɔviwò wɔ aye va xɔ wò yayra la dzoe xoxo.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “My brother deserves the name Jacob, because he has already cheated me twice. The first time he cheated me out of my rights as the first-born son, and now he has cheated me out of my blessing.” Then Esau asked his father, “Don't you have any blessing left for me?”
translation_verse: Esau gblɔ be: “Yakob ko woayɔ nɛ vavã! Zi eveliae nye esi wòlé afɔkpodzi nam hebam. Exɔ nye ŋgɔgbevinyenye va yi, azɔ egaxɔ nye yayra hã.” Eyi edzi bia tɔ́a be: “Mèsusɔ yayra aɖeke ɖi nam oa?”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac answered, “I have made Jacob the ruler over you and your brothers, and all of you will be his servants. I have also promised him all the grain and grapes that he needs. There's nothing left that I can do for you.”
translation_verse: Isak ɖo eŋu be: “Kpɔ ɖa, meɖoe amegã ɖe dziwò, eye metsɔ nɔvia ŋutsuwo wɔ eƒe dɔlawoe. Metsɔ bli kple wain hã nɛ. Evɔ. Vinye, nu ka gɔ̃e li magawɔ na wò?”

english_verse: “Father,” Esau asked, “don't you have more than one blessing? You can surely give me a blessing too!” Then Esau started crying again.
translation_verse: Esau ɖe kuku na tɔ́a vevie be: “Tɔ́nye, meɖe kuku, yayra ɖeka ma koe le asiwòa? Tɔ́nye, yra nye hã dzro!” Esau wó avi doo.

english_verse: So his father said: “Your home will be far from that fertile land, where dew comes down from the heavens.
translation_verse: Tete tɔ́a Isak gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, wò nɔƒe adidi tso anyigba wɔnu gbɔ, eye ànɔ adzɔge tso zãmu gbɔ.

english_verse: You will live by the power of your sword and be your brother's slave. But when you decide to be free, you will break loose.”
translation_verse: Wò aʋawɔyi dzi nànɔ agbe ɖo. Àsubɔ nɔviwò; evɔ ne èdze aglã ɖe eŋu la, àdo le eƒe ŋusẽ te.”

english_verse: Esau hated his brother Jacob because he had stolen the blessing that was supposed to be his. So he said to himself, “Just as soon as my father dies, I'll kill Jacob.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Esau lé fu Yakob elabe wo tɔ́ yra eya. Eɖo nugbe ɖe eŋu gblɔ le eɖokui me be: “Mía tɔ́ ƒe kuɣi le kpuie. Ne wole fu nyim nɛ ko la, mawu nɔvinye Yakob godoo.”

english_verse: When Rebekah found out what Esau planned to do, she sent for Jacob and told him, “Son, your brother Esau is just waiting for a chance to kill you.
translation_verse: Wogblɔ Esau ƒe nugbeɖoɖoa na Rebeka. Ale wòna woyɔ Yakob, via ɖevitɔ vɛ nɛ. Egblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, nɔviwò Esau ɖo nugbe ɖe ŋuwò be yeabia hlɔ̃ awu wò.

english_verse: Now listen carefully and do what I say. Go to the home of my brother Laban in Haran
translation_verse: Eya ta, vinye, ɖo to nàwɔ nu si gblɔ ge mala na wò la. Netsɔ na wò nàsí yi ɖe nɔvinye Laban gbɔ le Xaran.

english_verse: and stay with him for a while. When Esau stops being angry
translation_verse: Nɔ egbɔ va se ɖe esime nɔviwò ƒe dzi nafa.

english_verse: and forgets what you have done to him, I'll send for you to come home. Why should I lose both of my sons on the same day?”
translation_verse: Ne edzudzɔ dzikudodo ɖe ŋuwò, eye wòŋlɔ nu si nèwɔ ɖe eŋu la be la, madɔ ame ɖa woava kplɔ wò tso afi ma vɛ. Nu ka ta mi ame evea miaku nam le ŋkeke ɖeka dzi?” Isak ɖo Yakob ɖe Laban

english_verse: Rebekah later told Isaac, “Those Hittite wives of Esau are making my life miserable! If Jacob marries a Hittite woman, I'd be better off dead.”
translation_verse: Rebeka gblɔ na Isak be: “Xiti-nyɔnu siwo Esau ɖe la na agbenɔnɔ ti kɔ nam. Ne Yakob hã aɖe Xiti-nyɔnuvi siawo ƒe ɖe la, ɖeko maku.”

english_verse: Isaac called in Jacob, then gave him a blessing, and said: Don't marry any of those Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Isak yɔ Yakob vɛ, yrae, eye wòde se nɛ be: “Mègaɖe Kanaan-nyɔnuvi aɖeke o.

english_verse: Go at once to your mother's father Bethuel in northern Syria and choose a wife from one of the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
translation_verse: Tso nàyi nɔwò tɔ́, Betuel, ƒeme le Padan-Aram ne nàɖe nyruiwò Laban vinyɔnuviwo dometɔ ɖeka.

english_verse: I pray that God All-Powerful will bless you with many descendants and let you become a great nation.
translation_verse: Mawu Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la neyra wò, eye wòana nàdzi fũu ale be nàva zu dukɔ geɖewo tɔ́.

english_verse: May he bless you with the land he promised Abraham, so that you will take over this land where we now live as foreigners.
translation_verse: Neyra wò kple wò dzidzimeviwo abe ale si wòyra Abraham ene, eye wòatsɔ anyigba si dzi nènye amedzro le fifia, anyigba si wòtsɔ na Abraham la, ana wò.”

english_verse: Isaac then sent Jacob to stay with Rebekah's brother Laban, the son of Bethuel the Aramean. Esau Marries the Daughter of Ishmael
translation_verse: Ale Isak do mɔ Yakob ɖo ɖe Padan-Aram ɖe Aramtɔ Betuel vi Laban, ame si nye Yakob kple Esau dada nɔviŋutsu la gbɔ. Esau gaɖe srɔ̃ bubu

english_verse: Esau found out that his father Isaac had blessed Jacob and had warned him not to marry any of the Canaanite women. He also learned that Jacob had been sent to find a wife in northern Syria
translation_verse: Esau va nya be Isak yra Yakob, eye wòɖoe ɖe Padan-Aram be wòayi aɖaɖe srɔ̃ le afi ma. Enya hã be Isak de se na Yakob vevie le eyraɣi be megaɖe Kanaan-vinyɔnu aɖeke o.

english_verse: and that he had obeyed his father and mother.
translation_verse: Hekpe ɖe esia ŋu la, ede dzesii be Yakob ɖo to yewo dzilawo, eye wòdzo yi Padan-Aram.

english_verse: Esau already had several wives, but he now realized how much his father hated the Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Esi wòkpɔ dzesii be Kanaan-nyɔnuwo medze yewo tɔ́ Isak ŋu o la,

english_verse: So he married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath, who was the sister of Nebaioth and the granddaughter of Abraham. Jacob's Dream at Bethel
translation_verse: eyi ɖe Abraham vi, Ismael gbɔ ɖaɖe via Mahalat si nye Nebayot nɔvinyɔnu kpe ɖe srɔ̃a bubuawo ŋu. Yakob ku drɔ̃e le Betel

english_verse: Jacob left the town of Beersheba and started out for Haran.
translation_verse: Yakob dze mɔ tso Beer-Seba ɖo ta Xaran.

english_verse: At sunset he stopped for the night and went to sleep, resting his head on a large rock.
translation_verse: Eva ɖo teƒe aɖe si zã do ɖee le, eye wòtsi afi ma dɔ. Etsɔ kpe aɖe le afi ma ziɔ, eye wòmlɔ anyi dɔ alɔ̃.

english_verse: In a dream he saw a ladder that reached from earth to heaven, and God's angels were going up and down on it.
translation_verse: Eku drɔ̃e kpɔ atsrɔe aɖe. Egɔme tɔ anyigba, ke eƒe nu gbɔ ɖatɔ dziƒo. Kpɔ ɖa, mawudɔlawo le eliam le dzi yim le ɖiɖim.

english_verse: The Lord was standing beside the ladder and said: I am the Lord God who was worshiped by Abraham and Isaac. I will give to you and your family the land on which you are now sleeping.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ le tsitre ɖe eŋgɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Nyee nye Aƒetɔ, tɔgbuiwò Abraham kple tɔ́wò Isak ƒe Mawu la! Matsɔ anyigba si dzi nèmlɔ la ana wò kple wò dzidzimeviwo.

english_verse: Your descendants will spread over the earth in all directions and will become as numerous as the specks of dust. Your family will be a blessing to all people.
