translation_verse: Wò dzidzimeviwo asɔ gbɔ abe ʋuʋudedi ene, eye miakaka ɖe xexeme ƒe ɣedzeƒe, ɣetoɖoƒe, dzigbeme kple anyigbeme katã. Wò kple wò dzidzimeviwo dzi mato ayra anyigba dzi dukɔwo katã.

english_verse: Wherever you go, I will watch over you, then later I will bring you back to this land. I won't leave you—I will do all I have promised.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, manɔ kpli wò; makpɔ tawò le afi sia afi si nàyi, eye makplɔ wò agbugbɔ va anyigba sia dzi. Nyemagblẽ wò ɖi akpɔ o, ke boŋ mawɔ ŋugbe si medo na wò la dzi godoo.”

english_verse: Jacob woke up suddenly and thought, “The Lord is in this place, and I didn't even know it.”
translation_verse: Esi Yakob nyɔ la, egblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ la le afi sia pɛ! Eli gake nyemenya o.”

english_verse: Then Jacob became frightened and said, “What a frightening place! It must be the house of God and the gateway to heaven.”
translation_verse: Vɔvɔ̃ ɖoe wògblɔ be: “Afi sia dzi ŋɔ loo! Mawu ƒe aƒe kokoko wònye, eye teƒe sia la dziƒogboe.”

english_verse: When Jacob got up early the next morning, he took the rock that he had used for a pillow and stood it up as a place of worship. Then he poured olive oil on the rock to dedicate it to God,
translation_verse: Esi Yakob fɔ ŋdi kanya la, etsɔ kpe si wòziɔ la ɖo anyi abe dzesikpe ene, eye wòkɔ ami ɖe edzi.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Before that it had been named Luz.
translation_verse: Azɔ ena ŋkɔ teƒe la be Betel. Woyɔa teƒe ma tsã be Luz.

english_verse: Jacob solemnly promised God, “If you go with me and watch over me as I travel, and if you give me food and clothes
translation_verse: Tete Yakob ɖe adzɔgbe na Aƒetɔ be: “Ne Mawu anɔ kplim, akpɔ tanye le afi si yim mele, eye wòana nuɖuɖu kple nudodom,

english_verse: and bring me safely home again, you will be my God.
translation_verse: ana magatrɔ gbɔ va tɔ́nye ƒeme dedie la, ekema Aƒetɔ anye nye Mawu.

english_verse: This rock will be your house, and I will give back to you a tenth of everything you give me.”
translation_verse: Metu kpe sia ɖe afii abe dzesi ene. Anye Mawu ƒe aƒe, eye matsɔ nu sia nu si nànam la, ƒe akpa ewolia ana wò.”

english_verse: As Jacob continued on his way to the east,
translation_verse: Yakob yi eƒe mɔzɔzɔ dzi, eye wòva ɖo ɣedzeƒenyigba dzi.

english_verse: he looked out in a field and saw a well where shepherds took their sheep for water. Three flocks of sheep were lying around the well, which was covered with a large rock.
translation_verse: Kasia eva ke ɖe vudo aɖe ŋu le agbledeƒe aɖe. Alẽha etɔ̃ tsyɔ akɔ anyi ɖe vudoa gbɔ. Eya mee wokua tsi le naa alẽhaawo wonona. Kpe gã aɖe le vudoa nu.

english_verse: Shepherds would roll the rock away when all their sheep had gathered there. Then after the sheep had been watered, the shepherds would roll the rock back over the mouth of the well.
translation_verse: Nenye be alẽhaawo katã va ƒo ƒu la, womlia kpea ɖa, eye wonaa tsi alẽawo. Emegbe la, wogamlia kpea tua enu.

english_verse: Jacob asked the shepherds, “Where are you from?” “We're from Haran,” they answered.
translation_verse: Yakob bia alẽkplɔlaawo be: “Nɔvinyewo, afi ka mietso?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Míetso Xaran.”

english_verse: Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?” “Yes we do,” they replied.
translation_verse: Ebia wo be: “Mienya Naxor vi, Labana?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Ẽ, míenyae.”

english_verse: “How is he?” Jacob asked. “He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
translation_verse: Egabia wo be: “Eli nyuiea?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Eli nyuie. Kpɔ ɖa, via Raxel gɔ̃ hãe nye ema kplɔ alẽwo gbɔna.”

english_verse: Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
translation_verse: Yakob gblɔ na wo be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ɣe gale dzi; migaƒo alẽawo nu ƒu haɖe o. Mina tsi wo woano ne miana woagayi aɖaɖu gbe.”

english_verse: But they replied, “We can't do that until they all get here, and the rock has been rolled away from the well.”
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Míate ŋu awɔ nenema o, va se ɖe esime alẽhaawo katã naƒo ƒu, ekema míamli kpe la ɖa le vudoa nu, eye míana tsi wo woano.”

english_verse: While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep.
translation_verse: Yakob mekpɔ ɖe nu le eme hafi Raxel si nye alẽkplɔla la va ɖo kple tɔ́a ƒe alẽwo o.

english_verse: When Jacob saw her and his uncle's sheep, he rolled the rock away and watered the sheep.
translation_verse: Esi Yakob kpɔ Raxel, nyruia Laban vinyɔnu kple nyruia Laban ƒe alẽha la, eyi vudoa gbɔ, mli kpea ɖa, eye wòna tsi alẽawo.

english_verse: He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy.
translation_verse: Azɔ egbugbɔ nu na Raxel, eye wòwó avi sesĩe.

english_verse: He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
translation_verse: Egblɔ na Raxel be tɔ́a ƒe ƒometɔe yenye. Yee nye Rebeka viŋutsu. Tete Raxel ƒu du yi ɖagblɔe na tɔ́a.

english_verse: As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Esi Laban se nyruiayɔvi Yakob ŋkɔ la, eƒu du yi ɖakpee, kpla asi kɔ nɛ, gbugbɔ nu nɛ, eye wòkplɔe va aƒemee. Yakob gblɔ nya siwo katã va dzɔ la nɛ.

english_verse: Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had been there for a month,
translation_verse: Laban gblɔ nɛ be: “Nyateƒe, nɔvinye kpamkpam nènye.” Yakob nɔ egbɔ ɣleti ɖeka. Yakob subɔ Laban, eye wòɖe Raxel kple Lea

english_verse: Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
translation_verse: Azɔ Laban gblɔ na Yakob be: “Togbɔ be nɔviwo míenye hã la, nyemadi be nàwɔ dɔ nam dzodzro o. Nenie maxe na wò? Gblɔe nam.”

english_verse: Laban had two daughters. Leah was older than Rachel, but her eyes didn't sparkle, while Rachel was beautiful and had a good figure.
translation_verse: Lea ƒe ŋkuwo le dɔ̃ɔ, ke Raxel ya dze tugbe, eye wònyakpɔ ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he answered, “If you will let me marry Rachel, I'll work seven years for you.”
translation_verse: Raxel ƒe nu nyo Yakob ŋu, eya ta egblɔ na Laban be: “Medi be mawɔ dɔ na wò ƒe adrẽ ne nàtsɔ Raxel, viwò nyɔnu ɖevitɔ nam maɖe.”

english_verse: Laban replied, “It's better for me to let you marry Rachel than for someone else to have her. So stay and work for me.”
translation_verse: Laban ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Enyo nam be matsɔe na wò wu be matsɔe na ŋutsu bubu. Nɔ gbɔnye.”

english_verse: Jacob worked seven years for Laban, but the time seemed like only a few days, because he loved Rachel so much.
translation_verse: Ale Yakob subɔ nyruia ƒè adrẽ, ɖe Raxel ta; ke ɣeyiɣi la nɔ nɛ abe ŋkeke ʋɛ aɖe ko ene, elabe Raxel ƒe nu lé dzi nɛ ale gbegbe.

english_verse: Jacob said to Laban, “The time is up, and I want to marry Rachel now!”
translation_verse: Ƒeawo va yi eye Yakob gblɔ na Laban be: “Nye ɣeyiɣia de, eya ta tsɔ srɔ̃nyea nam maɖe.”

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Ale Laban ɖo srɔ̃ɖekplɔ̃ eye wòkpe dua me ŋutsuwo katã vɛ.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Ke esi zã do la, ekplɔ via Lea de xɔ na Yakob, eye wòdɔ kplii.

english_verse: Laban also gave Zilpah to Leah as her servant woman.
translation_verse: Laban tsɔ eƒe kosi Silpa na Lea be wòanye eƒe subɔvi.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Ŋu ke, kasia wòbe yeakpɔ la, Lea boŋ ye. Yakob yi ɖabia Laban be: “Nu kae nye esi nèwɔ ɖe ŋunye? Menye Raxel tae mesubɔ wò ɖo oa? Nu ka ta nèblem ale?”

english_verse: Laban replied, “In our country the older daughter must get married first.
translation_verse: Laban ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Le mía de kɔnu nu la, vinyɔnu ɖevitɔ meɖea srɔ̃ hafi tsitsitɔ ɖenɛ o.

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Fifia na srɔ̃ɖekwasiɖa ɖeka sia nava yi, eye míatsɔ ɖevitɔ hã na wò nàɖe, nenye be nègawɔ dɔ nam ƒe adrẽ bubu ko.”

english_verse: At the end of the week of celebration, Laban let Jacob marry Rachel, and he gave her his servant woman Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, but he had to work another seven years for Laban.
translation_verse: Azɔ Yakob dɔ kple Raxel hã, eye wòlɔ̃ eya sãa wu Lea. Tete wògawɔ dɔ na Laban ƒe adrẽ bubu. Vi siwo wodzi na Yakob

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: Esi Aƒetɔ kpɔ be Yakob lɔ̃ Raxel sãa wu Lea la, eʋu Lea ƒe vidzidɔ, ke exe Raxel ya tɔ.

english_verse: Leah gave birth to a son and named him Reuben. Then she said, “The Lord has taken away my sorrow. Now my husband will love me more than he does Rachel.”
translation_verse: Lea dzi ŋutsuvi. Egblɔ be Aƒetɔ kpɔ nye nublanui eya ta srɔ̃nye alɔ̃m azɔ. Ale wòna ŋkɔ ɖevia be Ruben.

english_verse: She had a second son and named him Simeon, because she said, “The Lord has heard that my husband doesn't love me.”
translation_verse: Eyome egafɔ fu, eye wòdzi ŋutsuvi. Egblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ se be wolé fum eya ta wòna megadzi ŋutsuvi.” Le esia ta ena ŋkɔe be Simeon.

english_verse: When Leah's third son was born, she said, “Now my husband will hold me close.” So this son was named Levi.
translation_verse: Emegbe egafɔ fu dzi ŋutsuvi. Egblɔ be: “Azɔ ko srɔ̃nye alé ɖe ŋunye goŋgoŋ, elabe medzi ŋutsuvi etɔ̃ sɔŋ nɛ.” Ale wòna ŋkɔe be Levi.

english_verse: She had one more son and named him Judah, because she said, “I'll praise the Lord!”
translation_verse: Lea gafɔ fu gadzi ŋutsuvi, eye wògblɔ be: “Azɔ la, makafu Aƒetɔ!” Ale wòna ŋkɔe be Yuda. Tete Lea tsò vi.

english_verse: Rachel was very jealous of Leah for having children, and she said to Jacob, “I'll die if you don't give me some children!”
translation_verse: Esi Raxel kpɔ be yemedzi vi aɖeke na Yakob o la, eʋã ŋu nɔvia Lea, eye wògblɔ na Yakob be: “Na madzi vi, ne menye nenem o la, maku.”

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Yakob do dɔmedzoe ɖe eŋu gblɔ be: “Mawue menye, axe wò vidzidɔ nua?”

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Tete Raxel gblɔ be: “Nye subɔvi Bilha nye esi. Dɔ kplii ne wòadzi vi ɖe akɔ̀ nam, ne nye hã mazu vi nɔ to edzi.”

english_verse: Then Rachel let Jacob marry Bilhah,
translation_verse: Ale Raxel tsɔ eƒe kosi, Bilha, na Yakob wòɖe, eye wòdɔ kplii.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Bilha fɔ fu, eye wòdzi ŋutsuvi na Yakob.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Tete Raxel gblɔ be: “Mawu tso afia nam; ese nye gbedodoɖa, eye wòna viŋutsum. Ale wòna ŋkɔe be Dan.

english_verse: When Bilhah and Jacob had a second son,
translation_verse: Eyome Bilha gafɔ fu, eye wòdzi ŋutsuvi evelia na Yakob.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Raxel gblɔ be: “Meƒo koko na Mawu, te kame kple nɔvinye, eye meɖu dzi.” Ale wòtsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Naftali.

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Esi Lea kpɔ be yemegale vi dzim o la, etsɔ eƒe subɔvi Silpa na Yakob wòɖe.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Silpa dzi ŋutsuvi na Yakob.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Lea gblɔ be: “Nye Mawu ɖi nam!” Ale wòna ŋkɔe be Gad.

english_verse: When they had another son,
translation_verse: Eyome Silpa gadzi ŋutsuvi evelia na Yakob.

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: Tete Lea gblɔ be: “Dzi dzɔm! Azɔ mia tɔ nyɔnuwo akafum ayɔm be ‘Dzidzɔkpɔla.” Ale wòtsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Aser.

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la, Ruben yi agble le luŋeɣi, eye wòtsɔ lɔlɔ̃gbitsa vɛ na nɔa Lea. Raxel gblɔ na Lea be: “Meɖe kuku, na viwò ƒe lɔlɔ̃gbitsa la ƒe ɖem.”

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Lea ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Esi nèxɔ srɔ̃nye le asinye ɖe, mesɔ gbɔ na wò oa? Vinye ƒe agbitsa hãe nèbe yeagaxɔ le asinyea?” Raxel gblɔ be: “Ekema tsɔ viwò ƒe agbitsa la nam ne srɔ̃nyea nadɔ gbɔwò ɖe enu egbe ƒe zã.”

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: Esi Yakob gbɔ tso agble le fiẽ me la, Lea yi ɖakpee gblɔ nɛ be: “Egbe ya gbɔnye dɔ ge nàla, elabe metsɔ vinye ƒe agbitsa xe fe ɖe tawò.” Ale wòdɔ kplii gbe ma gbe ƒe zã.

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: Mawu se Lea ƒe gbedodoɖa, eye wòfɔ fu dzi ŋutsuvi atɔ̃lia na Yakob.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Lea gblɔ be: “Mawu xe fe nam elabe metsɔ nye subɔvi na srɔ̃nye wòɖe.” Ale wòna ŋkɔe be Isaxar.

english_verse: When Leah had another son,
translation_verse: Eyome Lea gafɔ fu, eye wòdzi viŋutsu adelia na Yakob.

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: Fifia Lea gblɔ be: “Mawu tsɔ nɔƒe xɔasi nam. Srɔ̃nye ade bubu ŋunye azɔ elabe medzi viŋutsu ade sɔŋ nɛ.” Ale wòna ŋkɔe be Zebulon.

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Emegbe la, edzi nyɔnuvi, eye wòna ŋkɔe be Dina.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: Efɔ fu, eye wòdzi ŋutsuvi. Egblɔ be: “Mawu ɖe nye ŋukpe ɖa azɔ.

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ nena magadzi ŋutsuvi ɖeka akpee.” Eya ta ena ŋkɔe be Yosef. Yakob ƒo nu kple Laban tso egbɔnɔnɔ ŋuti

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Le Yosef dzidzi megbe la, Yakob gblɔ na Laban be: “Medi be nàdo mɔm mayi aƒe.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Ɖe asi le srɔ̃nye kple vinye siwo ta mewɔ dɔ na wò ɖo la ŋu nam, ne madzo. Wò ŋutɔ ènya ale si mesubɔ wòe.”

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Yakob ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Wò ŋutɔ ènya vi si meɖe na wò kple ale si wò lãha la va dzi ɖe edzi, esime mele edzi kpɔm la.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: Lãha sue aɖe koe nɔ asiwò hafi meva; ke azɔ la, edzi ɖe edzi fũu, eye Aƒetɔ yra wò to nye vava eme. Gbe ka gbe nye hã mava wɔ dɔ akpɔ nye aƒe dzi?”

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Laban biae be: “Nu ka nèdi be matsɔ xe fe na ye?” Yakob ɖo eŋu be: “Nyemaxɔ naneke le asiwò o. Ke nya aɖe le asinye medi be magblɔ na wò. Ne àlɔ̃ awɔ esia nam ko la, manɔ anyi aganyi wò alẽawo, akpɔ wo dzi.

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Eyae nye be egbe la, na matsa le wò lãha la katã me. Maɖe alẽ ɖe sia ɖe si ƒe agbalẽ me fli to kple esi le ŋɔtaŋɔta kple alẽvi yibɔwo kpakple gbɔ̃ siwo le ŋɔtaŋɔta kple esiwo ƒe agbalẽ me fli to la ɖe vovo. Woawoe maxɔ abe nye fetu ene.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: Azɔ tso fifia heyina ne èva be yeakpɔ nye nuteƒewɔwɔ la, ekema eme akɔ na wò ƒãa. Ne àkpɔ gbɔ̃ aɖe si mele ŋɔtaŋɔta o, alo esi ƒe agbalẽ me fli meto o, alo alẽvi aɖe si mele yibɔ o le tɔnyeawo dome ko la, ke ɖe mefii.”

english_verse: “I agree to that,” was Laban's response.
translation_verse: Laban ɖo eŋu be: “Melɔ̃ ɖe edzi. Míawɔe nenema.”

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe ke la, Laban ɖe gbɔ̃tsu siwo ƒe agbalẽ me fli to, alo nu yibɔyibɔwo le la ɖe vovo. Nenema ke eɖe gbɔ̃nɔ siwo katã le ŋɔtaŋɔta alo esiwo ƒe agbalẽ me fli ɣi to la ɖe vovo. Azɔ egaɖe alẽvi yibɔwo hã ɖe vovo eye wòtsɔ lã siawo katã de asi na viawo.

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: Azɔ ena wokplɔ alẽha yeye sia dzoe, ŋkeke etɔ̃ mɔzɔzɔ ƒe didime, tso Yakob gbɔ. Ke Yakob nɔ Laban ƒe lãha mamlɛa dzi kpɔm.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Yakob tsɔ logo, xe kple nyati mumuwo, eye wòfo tsro le akpa aɖewo ŋu, teƒe mawo fu ɣie, wòsusɔ tsro ɖe teƒe bubuawo.

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: Azɔ etsɔ ati siawo ɖo lãawo ƒe tsinonu ŋgɔ. Ewɔ esia bene lãawo nanɔ ati siawo kpɔm ne wova le tsi nom, eye wole asi yɔm la.

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Yakob ma alẽviawo ɖa tso lãha la gbɔ, eye wòna lãha la dzea ŋgɔ Laban ƒe lã siwo le ŋɔtaŋɔta kple esiwo le yibɔ la. Mena eƒe lãwo tsaka kple Laban tɔwo o.

english_verse: When the stronger sheep were mating near the drinking place, Jacob made sure that the spotted branches were there.
translation_verse: Azɔ nenye be lã sesẽtɔwo le asi yɔm la, Yakob tsɔa ati siwo ŋu wòfo tsro le la ɖoa wo ŋgɔ le tsinonua gbɔ bene woafɔ fu adzi vi siwo ƒe agbalẽ me anɔ abe atiawo ene.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Ke meɖoa atiawo lã beliwo ya ŋgɔ o, eya ta lã beliawo ƒe viwo zua Laban tɔ, eye sesẽawo ƒe viwo zua Yakob tɔ.

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Ale Yakob va zu kesinɔtɔ gã aɖe. Alẽhawo, gbɔ̃wo, kluviwo, kosiwo, kposɔwo kple tedziwo ɖo esi fũu.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Yakob se Laban viŋutsuwo le gbɔgblɔm be: “Yakob xɔ mía tɔ́ ƒe nuwo katã. Kesinɔnu siwo katã le esi la, mía tɔ́ tɔ me wotso.”

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Yakob kpɔ be Laban megakɔa ŋkume ɖe ye abe tsã ene o.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Yakob be: “Trɔ yi tɔgbuiwòwo ƒe anyigba dzi kple ƒowòmeawo gbɔ. Manɔ kpli wò.”

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Ale Yakob dɔ woɖayɔ Raxel kple Lea vɛ nɛ le gbe dzi, afi si wòle eƒe lãhawo gbɔ le, eye wògblɔ na wo be:

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: “Mekpɔ be mia tɔ́ megakɔa ŋkume ɖem fifia abe tsã ene o; gake tɔ́nye ƒe Mawu la li kplim.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: Mi ame evea mienya nyuie be nye ŋusẽ katã metsɔ wɔ dɔ na mia tɔ́.

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: Gake ebam, eye wòtrɔ nye fetu zigbɔzi ewo; ke Mawu meɖe mɔ nɛ wòwɔ nu vevim ya o.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: Ne mia tɔ́ gblɔ be: ‘Lã ŋɔtaŋɔtawo nanye wò fetu’ la, ekema lãha blibo la katã dzia vi ŋɔtaŋɔtawo sɔŋ. Ne egagblɔ be: ‘Lã siwo ƒe agbalẽ me fli to nanye wò fetu la, ekema lãha blibo la katã dzia vi siwo ƒe agbalẽ me fli to la.

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Ale Mawu xɔ lãha blibo la katã le mia tɔ́ si hetsɔ nam.

english_verse: Then God's angel called me by name. I answered,
translation_verse: Mawudɔla aɖe yɔm le drɔ̃eƒea be: ‘Yakob!’ Metɔ be: ‘Nyee nye esi!’

english_verse: and he said, “Notice that all the rams are either spotted or speckled. I know everything Laban is doing to you,
translation_verse: Egblɔ nam be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa, lãtsu siwo katã le asi yɔm la nye esiwo ƒe agbalẽ me fli to, alo wole ŋɔtaŋɔta alo esiwo ƒe agbalẽ me ɣi kple yibɔ le la. Mekpɔ nu siwo katã wɔm Laban le ɖe ŋuwò.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Nyee nye Mawu si ɖe eɖokui fia wò le Betel, afi si nètu ŋkuɖodzikpe ɖo, kɔ ami ɖe edzi, eye nèɖe adzɔgbe nam le la. Azɔ tso, ʋu le anyigba sia dzi, eye nàgatrɔ yi mia de.’ ”

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: Menye ɖeko wòbua mí amedzrowoe oa? Etsɔ mí dzra, eye wòle ga si wòxɔ ɖe mía ta la ɖum va se ɖe fifi.

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: Kesinɔnu siwo katã Mawu xɔ le mía tɔ́ si la nye mía kple mía viwo tɔ, eya ta nu sia nu si Mawu gblɔ na wò be nàwɔ la, wɔe.”

english_verse: Then Jacob, his wives, and his children got on camels and left
translation_verse: Ale Yakob tso, eye wòtsɔ viawo kple srɔ̃awo ɖo kposɔwo dzi.

english_verse: northern Syria for the home of his father Isaac in Canaan. Jacob took along all his flocks, herds, and other property.
translation_verse: Azɔ ekplɔ eƒe lãhawo katã, eƒe lãha siwo katã su esi kple nyiha siwo katã wòwɔ dɔ kpɔ le Padan-Aram la, eye wòdze mɔ be yeayi ye tɔ́ Isak gbɔ le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Esi Laban yi fu ko ge na eƒe alẽwo la, Raxel fi tɔ́a ƒe aklama kpakpɛwo.

english_verse: long years to earn your two daughters and another
translation_verse: Yakob flu Laban Aramtɔ la elabe meklãe be yele dzodzo ge o.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: Ɖeko wòlɔ eƒe nuwo katã, sí dzo. Etso Frat-tɔsisia, eye wòɖo ta Gilead-tonyigba dzi. Laban ti Yakob yome

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke etɔ̃ megbe la, wova gblɔ na Laban be Yakob sí dzo.

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: Laban kplɔ nɔviawo kpe ɖe eɖokui ŋu, eye woti Yakob kple etɔwo yome ŋkeke adrẽ sɔŋ hafi va tu wo le Gilead-tonyigba la dzi.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe ƒe zã me la, Mawu va Laban gbɔ le drɔ̃eƒe, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ nyuie ne nàgagblɔ nya aɖeke ado ŋɔdzi na Yakob ne nàgblẽ nu ɖe edzi wu o.”

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Laban kple etɔwo va tu Yakob wòtu eƒe agbadɔ ɖe to dzi. Laban kple nɔviawo hã tu wo tɔ ɖe tonyigba la dzi le Gilead.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Laban bia Yakob be: “Nu ka nye esi nèwɔ, flum, hekplɔ vinye nyɔnuwo dzoe abe aboyomewoe wonye ene?

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Nu ka ta nèsí dzo xɛɛ le megbenye? Ne ɖe nèklãm la, anye ne aseyetsotso, hadzidzi, kasaŋku kple ʋuƒoƒo matsɔ ɖo wò ɖae.

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: Mèna megbugbɔ nu na tɔgbuiyɔvinyewo kple vinye nyɔnuawo tsɔ do hedenyuie na wo teti hã o. Ewɔ bometsinu!

english_verse: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
translation_verse: Ŋusẽ le asinye be mawɔ nu vevi mi, gake le étò ƒe zã me la, tɔ́wò ƒe Mawu la ƒo nu nam be: ‘Kpɔ nyuie be magblɔ nya vɔ̃ alo nya nyui aɖeke na Yakob o.’

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: Menya nyuie be aƒe le dzrowòm eya tae nèdzo ɖo. Ke nu ka ta nèfi nye mawuwo?”

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
translation_verse: Yakob ɖo eŋu be: “Ɖe menɔ vɔvɔ̃m elabe mebu be ɖewohĩ àxɔ viwò nyɔnuawo le asinye.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Ame si ƒe nuwo me nàkpɔ wò mawuawo le la, matsi agbe o. Ka nye nuwo me faa, nàtɔ asi nu si nye tɔwò la dzi le mía nɔviwo ŋkume afii, ne nàɖee dzoe.” Yakob menya be Raxel ye fi mawuawo o.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Ale Laban yi ɖaka nuwo me le Yakob, Lea kple kosi eveawo ƒe agbadɔ me, gake mekpɔ eƒe mawuawo o. Edo le Lea ƒe agbadɔ me ge ɖe Raxel tɔ me.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Azɔ Raxel fi mawuawo tsɔ ɣla ɖe kposɔ ƒe akpa te hebɔbɔ nɔ edzi. Laban ka nu sia nu me le agbadɔa me, gake mekpɔ mawuawo o.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Raxel gblɔ na tɔ́a be: “Tɔ́nye, mègakpɔ dziku be nyemetso ɖe tsitrenu na wò o, elabe meɖo asi anyi.” Laban di mawuawo, gadi wo ʋuu, gake mekpɔ wo o.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Tete Yakob do dziku vevie ɖe Laban ŋuti. Ebia be: “Vo kae meda? Nu vɔ̃ ka gɔ̃e mewɔ si na be nèɖem ɖe nu alea gbegbe?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be nèka nye nuwo katã me hã, wò aƒemenu kae nèkpɔ? Tsɔe va da ɖe mí kple nɔviwòawo katã ŋkume, ne woabu fɔ, atso afia.

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Ne lã lénu lé ɖe la, nye agbae; ɖe medinɛ ɖoa eteƒe. Ne wofi ɖe, ŋdɔ o, zã o, ɖe nènana media bubu ɖoa eteƒe na wò.

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: Ale ŋdɔ ɖuam le ŋkeke me, vuvɔ wɔam le zã me, eye nyemekpɔa alɔ̃ dɔna gɔ̃ hã o.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Ne menye Mawu si tɔgbuinye Abraham subɔna, Mawu si tɔ́nye Isak hã vɔ̃na la ɖe wòli kplim o la, anye ne asi ƒuƒlu ko nèdo mɔm. Ke Mawu kpɔ ale si mekpe fu, wɔ dɔ kple kutrikuku, eye wòtso afia nam étò ƒe zã me.” Yakob kple Laban wɔ ɖoɖo

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Tete Laban ɖo eŋu na Yakob be: “Nyɔnu siawo la, vinyewoe, wo viwo hã nye tɔnye, eye lãhawo hã tɔnyewoe. Le nyateƒe me la, nu sia nu si le afii la, tɔnyee. Nu ka mate ŋu awɔ ɖe nye ŋutɔ vinye nyɔnuwo kple vi siwo wodzi la ŋu?

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: Na nye kple wò míabla nu, ne wòanye ɖaseɖiɖi le nye kple wò dome.”

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Ale Yakob tsɔ kpe tu anyi be wòanye ŋkuɖodzinu.

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: Egblɔ na eƒe amewo be woafɔ kpe vɛ, eye wofɔ wo va li kɔ ɖi. Emegbe la, woɖu nu le kpekɔ la dzi.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Laban tsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Yegar Saxaduta, ke Yakob ya tsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Galed.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Laban gblɔ be: “Kpekɔ sia nanye ŋkuɖodzikpe na nye kple wò tso egbe dzi,” eya ta wòna ŋkɔe be Galed.

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: Laban gagblɔ be: “Ne míeklã ɖa tso mía nɔewo gbɔ hã la, Aƒetɔ nenɔ mía ŋu dzɔm.” Ale wòna ŋkɔ teƒe ma be Mizpa.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Laban yi edzi be: “Ne èyi ɖale fu fiam vinye nyɔnuawo, alo yi ɖaɖe srɔ̃ kpe wo la, ɖo ŋku edzi be togbɔ be ame aɖeke meli o hã la, Mawu nye ɖasefo le nye kple wò dome.”

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Kpekɔ kple ŋkuɖodzikpe siawo zu ŋkuɖodzinu na mí ɖaa. Nyemadze to kpekɔ sia ŋu ava wɔ nu vevi wò o. Nenema ke wò hã màdze to kpekɔ sia kple ŋkuɖodzikpe sia ŋu ava wɔ nu vevim o.

english_verse: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Mawu si Abraham kple Naxor kple wo tɔgbuiwo subɔna la nanye ʋɔnudrɔ̃la le nye kpli wò dome.” Tete Yakob ka atam le tɔ́a Isak ƒe Mawu la ŋkɔ me, tsɔ ɖo kpe nubabla la dzi.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: Emegbe Yakob wu lã sa vɔe le to la dzi, eye wòyɔ etɔwo wova ɖu nu. Esi woɖu nua vɔ la, wotsi toa dzi dɔ.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
translation_verse: Le ŋufɔke ƒe ŋdi kanya la, Laban gbugbɔ nu na tɔgbuiyɔviawo kple via nyɔnuawo, eye wòyra wo. Emegbe etrɔ yi aƒe.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Yakob dzo yina, eye Mawu ƒe dɔlawo va do goe.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Esi wòkpɔ wo la, egblɔ be: “Mawu ƒe asaɖae nye esia!” Ale wòna ŋkɔ teƒea be Maxanaim.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: Yakob dɔ dɔlawo ɖo ɖe nɔvia Esau gbɔ le Seir-nyigba dzi le Edom-gbegbe.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: Egblɔ na wo be: “Migblɔ na nye aƒetɔ Esau be: ‘Nye, wò dɔla Yakob mebe medzo ɖanɔ Laban gbɔ abe amedzro ene ʋuu va se ɖe fifi.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Nyiwo, tedziwo, alẽwo, kluviwo kple kosiwo va ɖo asinye fũu, eya ta mele ame dɔm ɖe wò, nye aƒetɔ, be nàve nunye.’ ”

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Amedɔdɔawo trɔ va Yakob gbɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Míede ɖakpɔ nɔviwò Esau, eye eya hã gbɔna be yeava kpe wò. Ekplɔ ame alafa ene ɖe ŋuti gbɔnae.”

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.
translation_verse: Tete dzika tso Yakob ƒo, eye wòvɔ̃ ŋutɔŋutɔ. Ema eƒe amewo ɖe hatsotso eve me, eye wòma alẽawo, nyiawo kple kposɔawo hã ɖe akpa eve me.

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ na eɖokui be: “Ne eva eme be Esau va dze hatsotso ɖeka dzi, ɖu edzi la, ekema hatsotso evelia ya así dzo.”

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: Yakob gblɔ be: “Tɔgbuinye Abraham ƒe Mawu kple tɔ́nye Isak ƒe Mawu, Aƒetɔ, wòe gblɔ nam be: ‘Trɔ yi mia denyigba dzi kple ƒowòmeawo gbɔ, eye mawɔ nyui na wò.’

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: Meɖe kuku na wò, ɖem tso nɔvinye Esau si me. Mele evɔ̃m ŋutɔ. Ne menye nenema o la, ava sim, atsrɔ̃ vi nɔwo kple wo viwo gɔ̃ hã.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.

english_verse: After Jacob had spent the night there, he chose some animals as gifts for Esau:
translation_verse: Wotsi afi ma dɔ ŋu ke, eye Yakob tsɔ nu siwo le esi la ƒe ɖe ɖo ɖe nɔvia Esau.

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.

translation_verse: Ale nunanaawo dze ŋgɔ, ke eya ŋutɔ tsi asaɖa la me dɔ zã ma me. Yakob te kame kple ŋutsu aɖe le Peniel

translation_verse: Ena wokplɔ wo tsò tɔ lae, eye nu siwo katã le esi la ɖo tɔa godo vɔ.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”

translation_verse: Nyiwo, tedziwo, alẽwo, kluviwo kple kosiwo va ɖo asinye fũu, eya ta mele ame dɔm ɖe wò, nye aƒetɔ, be nàve nunye.’ ”

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Amedɔdɔawo trɔ va Yakob gbɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Míede ɖakpɔ nɔviwò Esau, eye eya hã gbɔna be yeava kpe wò. Ekplɔ ame alafa ene ɖe ŋuti gbɔnae.”

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.
translation_verse: Tete dzika tso Yakob ƒo, eye wòvɔ̃ ŋutɔŋutɔ. Ema eƒe amewo ɖe hatsotso eve me, eye wòma alẽawo, nyiawo kple kposɔawo hã ɖe akpa eve me.

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ na eɖokui be: “Ne eva eme be Esau va dze hatsotso ɖeka dzi, ɖu edzi la, ekema hatsotso evelia ya así dzo.”

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: Yakob gblɔ be: “Tɔgbuinye Abraham ƒe Mawu kple tɔ́nye Isak ƒe Mawu, Aƒetɔ, wòe gblɔ nam be: ‘Trɔ yi mia denyigba dzi kple ƒowòmeawo gbɔ, eye mawɔ nyui na wò.’

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: Meɖe kuku na wò, ɖem tso nɔvinye Esau si me. Mele evɔ̃m ŋutɔ. Ne menye nenema o la, ava sim, atsrɔ̃ vi nɔwo kple wo viwo gɔ̃ hã.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Evɔ wònye wòe gblɔ nam be: ‘Mana nu sia nu nadze edzi na wò nyuie; wò dzidzimeviwo asɔ gbɔ abe ƒutake si womate ŋu axlẽ o la ene.’ ”

english_verse: After Jacob had spent the night there, he chose some animals as gifts for Esau:
translation_verse: Wotsi afi ma dɔ ŋu ke, eye Yakob tsɔ nu siwo le esi la ƒe ɖe ɖo ɖe nɔvia Esau.

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.
translation_verse: Migblɔ be: ‘Wò dɔla Yakob ŋutɔ hã le megbe gbɔna.’ ” Elabe egblɔ le eɖokui me be: “Nunana siwo dze ŋgɔ la afa dzi nɛ gbã hafi nye ŋutɔ mava do ɖe eŋkume. Ɖewohĩ alɔ̃ axɔm.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Yakob gblɔ be: “Mekpɔ Mawu ŋkume kple ŋkume, gake metsi agbe.” Ale wòtsɔ ŋkɔ na teƒe ma be Peniel.

english_verse: Jacob put servants in charge of each herd and told them, “Go ahead of me and keep a space between each herd.”
translation_verse: Ena dɔlaawo ma lã vovovoawo ɖa tso wo nɔewo gbɔ, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Miva dze ŋgɔ nam, eye mina dometsotso nanɔ lãha vovovoawo dome.”

english_verse: Then he said to the servant in charge of the first herd, “When Esau meets you, he will ask whose servant you are. He will want to know where you are going and who owns those animals in front of you.
translation_verse: Egblɔ na dɔla ŋgɔgbetɔ be: “Ne nɔvinye Esau va do go wò, eye wòbia wò be: ‘Ame ka vie nènye? Afi ka nèyina? Ame ka ƒe lãhawoe nye esiawo le ŋgɔwò?’ mahã la,

english_verse: So tell him, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob, who is coming this way. He is sending them as a gift to his master Esau.’ ”
translation_verse: ɖo eŋu nɛ be: ‘Wò dɔla Yakob tɔwoe. Nunana wònye wòɖo ɖe eƒe aƒetɔ Esau. Eya ŋutɔ le megbe gbɔna.’ ”

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.
translation_verse: Egblɔ nya ma ke na ame evelia, etɔ̃lia kple bubu siwo katã le lãhaawo nu la be: “Ne miedo go Esau la, migblɔ nya si megblɔ la tututu.

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Ale nunanaawo dze ŋgɔ, ke eya ŋutɔ tsi asaɖa la me dɔ zã ma me. Yakob te kame kple ŋutsu aɖe le Peniel

english_verse: Jacob got up in the middle of the night and took his wives, his eleven children, and everything he owned across to the other side of the Jabbok River for safety.
translation_verse: Ena wokplɔ wo tsò tɔ lae, eye nu siwo katã le esi la ɖo tɔa godo vɔ.

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.
translation_verse: Ke eya ɖeɖe tsi megbe. Tete ŋutsu aɖe va te kame kplii ʋuu va se ɖe fɔŋli.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Esi ŋutsua kpɔ be yemete ŋu ɖu Yakob dzi o la, etɔ asi eƒe aligo, eye eƒe aligokpeƒe ɖɔli.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Ŋutsua gblɔ be: “Ɖe asi le ŋunye madzo; ŋu le kekem!” Ke Yakob ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Nyemele asi ɖe ge le ŋuwò o; negbe ɖeko nàyram hafi.”

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ŋutsua biae be: “Ŋkɔwò ɖe?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Yakob.”

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Ŋutsua gblɔ nɛ be: “Womagayɔ wò be Yakob azɔ o; ke boŋ woayɔ wò be Israel elabe ète kame kple Mawu gate kame kple ame hã eye nèɖu dzi.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Yakob xɔ edzi be: “Meɖe kuku, yɔ wò ŋkɔ nam.” Ke ŋutsua ɖo eŋu be: “Nu ka ta nèdi be yeanya nye ŋkɔ?” Tete wòyra Yakob.

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Ɣe dze esime wòdzo le afi ma yina. Enɔ tɔ̀tɔm ɖe ata ɖeka dzi.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.
translation_verse: Esi wònye lãkusi sesẽ si le aligokpeƒee ame la tɔ asii na Yakob ta la, va se ɖe egbe Israelviwo meɖua lã ƒe akpa ma o.

english_verse: The two servant women, Zilpah and Bilhah, together with their children went first, followed by Leah and her children, then by Rachel and Joseph.
translation_verse: Etsɔ kosi eveawo kple wo viwo ɖo ŋgɔ, eyome la, Lea kple viawo va, eye Raxel kple Yosef wonɔ megbea.

english_verse: Jacob himself walked in front of them all, bowing to the ground seven times as he came near his brother.
translation_verse: Eya ŋutɔ va le ŋgɔ na wo, eye wòle ta dem agu ʋuu zi adrẽ va se ɖe esime wògogo nɔvia.

english_verse: But Esau ran toward Jacob and hugged and kissed him. Then the two brothers started crying.
translation_verse: Ke Esau ƒu du va kpee, kpla asi kɔ nɛ, eye wògbugbɔ nu nɛ, eye wofa avi.

english_verse: When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?” Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”
translation_verse: Esi Esau fɔ kɔ dzi kpɔ nyɔnuawo kple ɖeviawo la, ebia be: “Ame kawoe nye esiawo le ŋuwò?” Yakob ɖo eŋu be: “Vi siwo Mawu nyo dɔme, na nye wò dɔla woe.”

english_verse: Then the two servant women and their children came and bowed down to Esau.
translation_verse: Tete kosiawo te va kple wo viwo, eye wode ta agu nɛ.

english_verse: Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down; finally, Joseph and Rachel also came and bowed down.
translation_verse: Lea kple viawo hã te va, va de ta agu. Emegbe Raxel kple Yosef hã te va, eye wode ta agu nɛ.

english_verse: Esau asked Jacob, “Why did you send those herds I met along the road?” “Master,” Jacob answered, “I sent them so you would be friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Esau biae be: “Lãha kawoe nye gbogbo siwo va kpem le mɔ dzi?” Yakob ɖo eŋu be: “Ɖe mebe matsɔ wo afa dzi na nye aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
translation_verse: Ke Esau ɖo eŋu be: “Nɔvinye, nu le asinye sɔ gbɔ. Wò nuwo nenɔ asiwò ko.”

english_verse: “No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God.
translation_verse: Yakob ɖo eŋu be: “Gbeɖe! Meɖe kuku, ne èdi be nye dzi nadze eme tututu la, ekema xɔ nye nunana la! Elabe esi mele kpɔwòm fifi laa la, ɖeko wòwɔ nam abe Mawu kpɔm mele ene. Ale si nève nunye wɔ dɔ ɖe dzinye ale gbegbe.

english_verse: Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
translation_verse: Meɖe kuku, xɔ nye nunana la nam ko, elabe Mawu yram mekpɔ nu geɖe.” Ale wòƒo nya ɖe Esau nu va se ɖe esime wòxɔ nunanaawo.

english_verse: “Let's get ready to travel,” Esau said. “I'll go along with you.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Esau gblɔ be: “Na míadze mɔ; manɔ ŋgɔ, ne miakplɔm ɖo.”

english_verse: But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die.
translation_verse: Yakob ɖo eŋu be: “Nye aƒetɔ, wò ŋutɔ ènya be ɖevi suewo, lã vi nɔwo kple wo vi nonowo hã le ŋunye. Ne míekplɔ wo kple du ŋkeke ɖeka teti hã la, wo katã atsrɔ̃.

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
translation_verse: Meɖe kuku, do ŋgɔ nam ne manɔ yowòme blewuu ale si lãha la kple ɖeviawo ate ŋu azɔe, va se ɖe esime matu wò le Seir.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.” “You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Ale Esau xɔ edzi be: “Ekema magblẽ ŋunyeme aɖewo ɖe gbɔwò.” Gake Yakob gagblɔ be: “Ɖe wòhiã? Na makpɔ amenuveve le nye aƒetɔ ŋkume koe!”

english_verse: But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth. Jacob Arrives at Shechem
translation_verse: Ke Yakob ɖo ta Sukot. Etso aƒe ɖe afi ma eye wòtu lãkpɔ na eƒe lãhawo hã ɖe afi ma. Eya tae wotsɔ ŋkɔ na afi ma be Sukot.

english_verse: After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city.
translation_verse: Esi Yakob trɔ gbɔ tso Padan-Aram la, eva ɖo Sixem-dua me le Kanaan-nyigba dzi dedie, eye wònɔ dua xa.

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: Eƒle anyigba si dzi wòtu eƒe agbadɔ ɖo la le Hemor, ame si tso Sixem-dua la viwo si klosaloga alafa ɖeka.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Eɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afi ma, eye wòna ŋkɔe be: El-Elohe-Israel

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la, Dina, ame si nye Lea kple Yakob vinyɔnu la, ɖi tsa yi nyɔnu aɖewo gbɔ le nuto ma me.

english_verse: She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her.
translation_verse: Esi Sixem, nuto ma me fia Xamor, Xivitɔ la ƒe viŋutsu kpɔe la, elée sesẽe, de asi eŋu, eye wògblẽe.

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.
translation_verse: Dina, Yakob vinyɔnua, ƒe nu lé dzi na Sixem vevie. Elɔ̃ ɖetugbi la ŋutɔ, ale wòde asi enubeble me.

english_verse: Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
translation_verse: Tete Sixem gblɔ na tɔ́a Xamor be: “Medi be nàɖe ɖetugbi sia nam.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time.
translation_verse: Yakob se be egblẽ Dina, ye vinyɔnuvia. Ke esi via ŋutsuwo nɔ gbe dzi le lãhawo gbɔ le ɣe ma ɣi ta la, ezi kpi va se ɖe esime wogbɔ.

english_verse: just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
translation_verse: Esi Yakob viŋutsuawo gbɔ tso gbea dzi va se nyaa la, dzi ku wo vevie. Wodo dɔmedzoe helihelĩ be Sixem ɖi gbɔ Israel, elabe ede asi Yakob vinyɔnu ŋuti; elabe medze be wòawɔ nu ma ƒomevi kura o.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Xamor gblɔ na wo be: “Mia vi Dina ƒe nu lé dzi na vinye Sixem ŋutɔ, eya ta meɖe kuku, mitsɔe nɛ ne wòaɖe,

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: ne srɔ̃ɖeɖe nanɔ mía dome: Mitsɔ miaƒe nyɔnuviwo na mí míaɖe, eye míawo hã míatsɔ mía tɔwo na mi miaɖe.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Ekema mianɔ mía gbɔ; mianɔ anyigba la ƒe afi si dze mia ŋu, eye miatsa asi le mía dome aɖo nunɔamesiwo na mia ɖokui faa.”

english_verse: Shechem added, “Do this favor for me, and I'll give whatever you want.
translation_verse: Sixem hã gblɔ na Dina tɔ́a kple nɔvia ŋutsuawo be: “Minyo dɔme nam ko eye nu sia nu si miabia la, mana faa.

english_verse: Ask anything, no matter how expensive. I'll do anything, just let me marry Dinah.”
translation_verse: Nyɔnutabianu kple srɔ̃ɖenu ale sinu hiã ko la, migblɔe nam. Mele klalo be mana ale si miedi, ne mianyatsɔ ɖetugbia nam maɖe ko.”

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Yakob viŋutsuawo ɖo eŋu na Sixem kple tɔ́a Xamor ayetɔe elabe woɖi gbɔ wo nɔvi Dina.

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Míate ŋu aɖe asi le mía nɔvinyɔnu ŋuti be wòaɖaɖe bolobolotɔ o, elabe enye ŋukpenanu na mí.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Ne mielɔ̃ be yewoazu abe míawo ene, eye ŋutsu sia ŋutsu le mia dome natso aʋa la, eya ko míalɔ̃ ɖe nya sia dzi.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: Míatsɔ mía vinyɔnuwo na mi miaɖe, eye míawo hã míaɖe mia tɔwo. Míanɔ mia gbɔ, eye míazu dukɔ ɖeka.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Ke ne miexɔ míaƒe nya la hetso aʋa o la, ekema míaxɔ mía vinyɔnu la le mia si adzoe.”

english_verse: Hamor and Shechem liked what was said.
translation_verse: Nya la dze Xamor kple via Sixem ŋu.

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: Ɖekakpui la mehe nyaa kura o, elabe Yakob vinyɔnu la ƒe nu nyo eŋu ŋutɔ. Gawu la, ɖekakpui la nye ame si tɔ́a ƒometɔwo buna wu le ƒomea me.

english_verse: The two men met with the other leaders of their city and told them:
translation_verse: Xamor kple via Sixem va dua ƒe takpeƒe le du la ƒe agbo nu, eye woƒo nu na wo detɔwo. Wogblɔ be:

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: “Ame siawo la, ame fafawo wonye. Mina woanɔ mía dome, atso aƒe ɖe anyigba la dzi, eye woatsa asi le edzi faa. Mikpɔ anyigba la ɖa. Elolo le go sia go me; asu na mí kple wo siaa. Mina míaɖe wo vinyɔnuwo, eye míawo hã míatsɔ mía tɔwo ana wo woaɖe faa.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Ke wobe hafi yewoalɔ̃ anɔ mía gbɔ, eye míazu dukɔ ɖeka la, ele be mía dome ŋutsu sia ŋutsu natso aʋa abe yewo ene.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: Menye ɖeko woƒe lãhawo, nunɔamesiwo kple dɔwɔlãwo katã azu mía tɔ oa? Eya ta mina míalɔ̃ ɖe woƒe nya la dzi ko ne woanɔ mía gbɔ.”

english_verse: Every grown man followed this advice and got circumcised. Dinah's Brothers Take Revenge
translation_verse: Ame siwo katã va takpeƒea la lɔ̃ ɖe Xamor kple via Sixem ƒe nya la dzi, eye dua me ŋutsuwo katã tso aʋa.

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Tete le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe, esime abia nɔ wo vem vevie, eye woɖe ŋu ɖi la, Yakob viŋutsu eve, Simeon kple Levi, siwo nye Dina dadaviwo la, tsɔ yi, dze dua dzi hewu eme ŋutsuwo katã.

english_verse: including Hamor and Shechem. Then they took Dinah and left.
translation_verse: Wowu Xamor kple via Sixem hã kple yi, eye wokplɔ Dina tso Sixem ƒeme dzoe.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Yakob vi mamlɛawo hã va ɖe nu xɔasi siwo katã le ame kukuawo ŋu, eye woha dua le ale si wodo vlo wo nɔvinyɔnu la ta.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: Wokplɔ woƒe alẽwo, nyiwo kple tedziwo, eye wotsɔ nu sia nu si wokpɔ le dua me kple agblewo me la dzoe.

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: Woha woƒe kesinɔnuwo katã, ɖe aboyo ɖeviwo kple nyɔnuwo siaa eye wotsɔ nu sia nu si wokpɔ le aƒeawo me la dzoe.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Tete Yakob gblɔ na Simeon kple Levi be: “Miedem dzɔgbevɔ̃e me. Fifia Kanaantɔwo kple Perizitɔwo kpakple ame bubu siwo katã le anyigba sia dzi la além ɖe fu me. Mikpɔ ɖa, míesɔ gbɔ kura o. Ne woƒo ƒu, tso ɖe ŋunye la, woatsrɔ̃ nye kple ŋunyemewo katã.”

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Ke woɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Eya kpɔ mɔ awɔ mía nɔvinyɔnu abe gbolo enea?”

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: Mina míaʋu ayi Betel ne maɖaɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afi ma na Mawu si kpe ɖe ŋunye le nye xaxa me, eye wònɔ kplim le afi sia afi si mede la.”

english_verse: So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
translation_verse: Ale wotsɔ mawu bubu siwo katã le wo si kple woƒe togɛ siwo le woƒe to me la na Yakob, eye Yakob ɖi wo ɖe ati gã si le Sixem gbɔ la te.

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Esime wodze mɔ yina la, Mawu na vɔvɔ̃ ɖo du siwo ƒo xlã wo la ale gbegbe be wometi Yakob viawo yome o.

english_verse: Finally, they reached Bethel, also known as Luz.
translation_verse: Yakob kple eŋumewo katã va ɖo Luz, si nye Betel, le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Eɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afi ma, eye wòyɔ teƒea be ‘Betel ƒe Mawu’ elabe afi mae Mawu ɖe eɖokui fiae le, esime wòsí le nɔvia Esau nu yina.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Azɔ Debora, ame si kpɔ Rebeka dzi le ɖevime la, ku, eye woɖii ɖe logoti gã aɖe te le Betel ƒe anyigbeme. Ale wòna ŋkɔ afi ma be “Konyifalogoti.”

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: Anyigba si metsɔ na Abraham kple Isak la, matsɔe ana wò, eye matsɔe ana wò dzidzimevi siwo ava ɖe yowòme la hã.”

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Tete Yakob tu ŋkuɖodzikpe ɖe afi si Mawu ƒo nu kplii le la tsɔ de dzesi teƒea. Ekɔ wain ɖe edzi, eye wòkɔ ami hã ɖe dzi.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: Yakob na ŋkɔ teƒe ma si Mawu ƒo nu nɛ le la be Betel. Raxel ƒe ku

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Azɔ Yakob kple etɔwo dze mɔ tso Betel yina. Esi wogogo Efrat la, Raxel de asi kuléle me, ke via dzidzi sesẽ nɛ.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
translation_verse: Esi via dzidzi nye dɔ nɛ la, vixela la gblɔ nɛ be: “Mègavɔ̃ o; ŋutsuvi dzi ge nègale.”

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Nu té Raxel ŋu vɔ, eye wòkpɔ be yemele agbe tsi ge o. Ale wòna ŋkɔ ɖevia be Benoni Ke tɔ́a ya yɔe be Benyamin.

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Esi Raxel ku la, woɖii ɖe mɔ si ɖo ta Efrat, si woyɔna be Betlehem, la to.

english_verse: Jacob set up a tombstone over her grave, and it is still there.
translation_verse: Yakob tu ŋkuɖodzikpe ɖe eƒe yɔdo dzi si woyɔna be Raxel ƒe yɔdodzikpe va se ɖe egbe.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Emegbe Israel yi eƒe mɔzɔzɔ dzi, eye wòva tu agbadɔ ɖe Eder gbetakpɔmɔ́ godo. Yakob viŋutsuwo (Kron I,

english_verse: During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it. Jacob's Twelve Sons
translation_verse: Esime Israel le nuto ma me la, Ruben de asi Bilha si nye tɔ́a ƒe ahiãvi ŋu, eye Israel see. Azɔ viŋutsuvi wui evee nɔ Yakob si.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Yakob va tɔ́a Isak gbɔ le Mamre le Kiryat-Arba si yɔm wole egbe be Xebron, afi si Abraham kple Isak nɔ kpɔ la.

english_verse: He married three Canaanite women: The first was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; the second was Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
translation_verse: Nyɔnu siwo Esau ɖe la nye Kanaantɔwo. Woawoe nye: Ada, Xititɔ Elon vinyɔnu; Oholibama, Ana vinyɔnu, ame si nye Xititɔ Zibeon tɔgbuiyɔvi,

english_verse: the third was Basemath, who was Ishmael's daughter and Nebaioth's sister.
translation_verse: kple Basmat, Ismael vinyɔnu, ame si nye Bebayot nɔvinyɔnu.

english_verse: Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Oholibama dzi Yehus, Yalam kple Korax. Ŋutsuvi siawoe wodzi na Esau le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Esau took his children and wives, his relatives and servants, his animals and possessions he had acquired while in Canaan, and moved far from Jacob.
translation_verse: Esau kplɔ srɔ̃awo, via ŋutsuwo, via nyɔnuwo, eƒe kluvi siwo katã le eƒeme, eƒe lãhawo kple dɔwɔlãwo katã, eye wòƒo ƒu kesinɔnu siwo katã wòkpɔ le Kanaan-nyigba dzi la, eye wòʋu le nɔvia Yakob gbɔ yi Seir-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: He did this because the land was too crowded and could not support him and his brother with their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: Eʋu elabe woƒe nunɔamesiwo sɔ gbɔ ale gbegbe be womagate ŋu anɔ wo nɔewo gbɔ o. Gawu la, woƒe lãhawo dzi ɖe edzi ale gbegbe be anyigba si dzi wonye amedzro le la megalolo na wo o.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Ale Esau yi ɖanɔ Seir-tonyigba dzi. Esau kee nye Edom.

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: To siwo dzɔ tso Esau me la woe nye esiwo gbɔna: Esau ƒe ŋgɔgbevi Elifaz ƒe dzidzimeviwoe nye: Teman, Omar, Zefo, Kenaz,

english_verse: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These and Esau's other descendants lived in the land of Edom.
translation_verse: Korax, Gaetam kple Amalek. To siawo katã nye Esau srɔ̃ Ada ƒe dzidzimeviwo.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Basemath's son Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
translation_verse: Esau vi Reguel ƒe dzidzimeviwoe nye: Naxat, Serax, Sama kple Misa. To siawo katã nye Esau srɔ̃ Basmat viwo.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Vi siwo Esau srɔ̃ Oholibama dzi nɛ la woe nye: Yehus, Yaelam kple Korax.

english_verse: All of these clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom.
translation_verse: To siawo katã dzɔ tso Esau si wogayɔna hã be Edom la me. Seir ƒe dzidzimeviwo

english_verse: Seir was from the Horite tribe that had lived in Edom before the time of Esau. The clans that had descended from him were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Seir, Xoritɔ, ame si nye Edom-nyigba la dzi nɔla tsã la ƒe dzidzimeviwoe nye esi: Lotan, Sobal, Zibeon, Ana,

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Lotan viŋutsuwoe nye: Xori kple Heman. Nɔvia nyɔnue nye Timna.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Sobal viŋutsuwoe nye: Alvan, Manaxat, Ebal Sefo kple Onam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Zibeon viŋutsuwoe nye: Aya kple Ana. Ana siae fɔ tsi dzodzoe vudo esime wònɔ tɔ́a ƒe tedziwo gbɔ le gbedzi.

english_verse: Anah's children were Dishon and Oholibamah.
translation_verse: Ana viwoe nye esiawo: Dison kple Ana vinyɔnu, Oholibama.

english_verse: Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
translation_verse: Dison viŋutsuwoe nye esiawo: Xemdan, Esban, Yitran kple Keran.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Ezer viŋutsuwoe nye: Bilhan, Savan kple Akan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Disan viŋutsuwoe nye: Uz kple Aran.

english_verse: The clans of the Horites were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Xoritɔwo ƒe amegãwoe nye esiawo: Lotan, Sobal, Zibeon, Ana,

english_verse: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan, and they lived in the land of Seir.
translation_verse: Dison, Ezer kple Disan. Esiawoe nye amegãwo le Seir-nyigba dzi le woƒe duawo nu. Edom-fiawo (Kron I,

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau took their names from their families and the places where they lived. They are Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
translation_verse: Esiawo nye amegã siwo dzɔ tso Esau me la ƒe ŋkɔwo le woƒe ƒomewo, nɔƒewo kple ŋkɔwo nu: Timna, Alva, Yetet,

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: Oholibama, Ela, Pinon,

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,

english_verse: Magdiel, and Iram. These clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom, the father of the Edomites. They took their names from the places where they settled.
translation_verse: Magdiel kple Iram. Ame siawoe nye Edom-megãwo le woƒe nɔƒewo kple woawo ŋutɔ ƒe anyigbawo nu. Esau ye nye Edomtɔwo tɔgbui.

english_verse: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father Isaac had lived,
translation_verse: Yakob nɔ Kanaan-nyigba si dzi tɔ́a nye amedzro le la dzi.

english_verse: “They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.” Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan.
translation_verse: Ŋutsua gblɔ nɛ be: “Wodzo, elabe mese wogblɔ be: ‘Mina míayi Dotan.’ ” Ale Yosef ti nɔviawo yome, eye wòva ke ɖe wo ŋu le Dotan.

english_verse: Jacob loved Joseph more than he did any of his other sons, because Joseph was born when Jacob was very old. Jacob had even given Joseph a fancy coat
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Israel lɔ̃ Yosef wu via bubuawo katã, elabe enye eƒe tsitsime vi. Etɔ awu ʋlaya abɔ legbe nɛ.

english_verse: which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
translation_verse: Esi Yosef nɔviŋutsuawo kpɔ be yewo tɔ́ lɔ̃ Yosef wu yewo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe la, wolé fui, eye womegaƒoa nu nɛ lɔlɔ̃tɔe azɔ o.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka Yosef ku drɔ̃e aɖe, eye esi wòlĩi na nɔviawo la, wogalé fui wu tsã.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream.
translation_verse: Egblɔ na wo be: “Mise drɔ̃e si meku la ɖa.

english_verse: We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, míele lu blam le agble me. Tete nye lu babla tsi tsitre hedzɔ ka. Kasia mia tɔwo va ƒo xlãe hele ta dem agu nɛ.”

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: Nɔviawo biae be: “Ɖe nègbɔna fia zu ge aɖu mía dzi nyateƒea?” Ale wogalé fui ɖe edzi wu tsã le eƒe drɔ̃eawo kple nyaawo ta.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: Tete wògaku drɔ̃e bubu, eye wòlĩ eya hã na nɔviawo gblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, megaku drɔ̃e bubu be ɣe, ɣleti kple ɣletivi wuiɖekɛ wode ta agu nam.”

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: Yosef lĩ drɔ̃e la na tɔ́a kple nɔviawo. Ke tɔ́a ka mo nɛ gblɔ be: “Drɔ̃e ka ƒomevie nye esia nèku? Ɖe nye kple nɔwò, kpakple nɔviwòwo míava dze klo ade ta agu na wòa?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept wondering about the dream. Joseph Is Sold and Taken to Egypt
translation_verse: Tso esia dzi la, nɔviawo de asi ŋuʋaʋãe me, ke tɔ́a lé nya la ɖe tame. Wodzra Yosef; wokplɔe yi Egipte

english_verse: One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem,
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka Yosef nɔviwo yi wo tɔ́ ƒe alẽha kplɔƒe le Sixem.

english_verse: his father Jacob said to him, “I want you to go to your brothers. They are with the sheep near Shechem.” “Yes, sir,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Israel gblɔ na Yosef be: “Nɔviwòwo le alẽawo kplɔm le Sixem. Va madɔ wò ɖe wo gbɔ.” Yosef ɖo eŋu be: “Yoo, nyee nye esi.”

english_verse: His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley. Joseph was near Shechem
translation_verse: Tɔ́a gblɔ nɛ be: “Yi nàɖakpɔ ɖa be nɔviwòwo kple lãhaawo li nyuie hã, ne nàva gblɔ nam.” Ale tɔ́a dɔe tso Xebron-bali me ɖo ɖe Sixem. Esi wòyi la,

english_verse: and wandering through the fields, when a man asked, “What are you looking for?”
translation_verse: eɖanɔ tsatsam le gbea dzi nɔ nɔviawo dim, eye ŋutsu aɖe kpɔe. Ŋutsua biae be: “Nu ka dim nèle?”

english_verse: Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu be: “Nɔvinyewo dim mele. Meɖe kuku, fia afi si wole lãawo kplɔm le lam.”

english_verse: But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him.
translation_verse: Wokpɔe le adzɔge ɖaa, eye hafi wòava ɖo wo gbɔ la, woɖo nugbe ɖe eŋu be yewoawui.

english_verse: They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams!
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na wo nɔewo be: “Drɔ̃ekula lae nye esi gbɔna!

english_verse: pieces of silver they sold him to the Ishmaelites who took him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Mina míawui atsɔ ƒu gbe ɖe do me. Ɖeko míagblɔ be lã wɔadã aɖe lée. Ekema nu si eƒe drɔ̃eawo ava zu hã míakpɔe.”

english_verse: Reuben heard this and tried to protect Joseph from them. “Let's not kill him,” he said.
translation_verse: Ke esi Ruben se nyaa la, eɖoe be yeaxɔ nɛ. Ale egblɔ be: “Migana míaɖe eƒe agbe ɖa o!”

english_verse: “Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
translation_verse: Egagblɔ be: “Migakɔ ʋu ɖi o. Mitsɔe da ɖe do sia me le gbedadaƒo afii boŋ. Migawɔ nu vevi aɖekee o.” Egblɔ esia bene yeate ŋu aɖee tso wo si me atsɔe aɖo ɖe wo tɔ́.

english_verse: As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt.
translation_verse: Azɔ wobɔbɔ nɔ anyi be yewoaɖu nu, kasia Ismael asitsahawoe nye ekem tso Gilead gbɔna. Wodo agba na woƒe kposɔwo kple aŋe, atikemi kple kotoklobo yina Egipte.

english_verse: So Judah said, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and hide his body?
translation_verse: Tete Yuda gblɔ na nɔviawo be: “Ne míewu míawo ŋutɔ nɔvi le bebeme ko hemia nu ɖe edzi ɖe, viɖe kae le eme na mí?

english_verse: Let's sell him to the Ishmaelites and not harm him. After all, he is our brother.” And the others agreed.
translation_verse: Mina míadzrae na Ismael asitsala siawo boŋ. Ame aɖeke megawɔ nu vevii o, elabe mía nɔvi kpamkpam wònye; ʋu ɖeka me mí katã míedzɔ tso.” Nɔviawo lɔ̃ ɖe edzi.

english_verse: When the Midianite merchants came by, Joseph's brothers took him out of the well, and for
translation_verse: Ale esi Midian-sitsala aɖewo va yina la, woɖee le doa me hetsɔe dzra, klosaloga bla eve, na Ismaeltɔwo. Tete asitsalaawo kplɔe yi Egipte.

english_verse: When Reuben returned to the well and did not find Joseph there, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Esi Ruben trɔ va doa gbɔ, eye wòkpɔ be Yosef mele eme o la, edze awu le eɖokui ŋu.

english_verse: Then he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
translation_verse: Etrɔ va nɔviawo gbɔ eye wògblɔ be: “Ɖevia megali o! Nu ka wɔ ge mala?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood.
translation_verse: Emegbe wowu gbɔ̃tsu tsɔ Yosef ƒe awu la nyrɔ ɖe eƒe ʋu me.

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: Wotsɔ awu ʋlaya la ɖo ɖe wo tɔ́, eye wogblɔ be: “Míefɔ awu ʋlaya sia. Lé ŋku ɖe eŋu be viwò tɔe hã.”

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Tɔ́a kpɔ awua dze sii eye wògblɔ be: “Ẽ, vinye ƒe awu ʋlaya ye! Lã wɔadã aɖe lée ɖu! Ɖikeke aɖeke mele eme o; evuvu Yosef keŋkeŋ!”

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Tete Yakob dze awu le eɖokui ŋu, sa akpanya ɖe ali, eye wòfa via ŋkeke geɖe.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: Via ŋutsuwo kple via nyɔnuwo fa akɔ nɛ do kpoe. Egblɔ na wo be: “Matsɔ konyifafa ayi vinye gbɔe le tsiẽƒe boŋ.” Ale Yosef tɔ́ fae vevie.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Ke Midiantɔwo ɖadzra Yosef le Egipte na Potifar, Egipte Fiagã ƒe aƒedzikpɔla kple eŋutimewo ƒe amegã.

english_verse: About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam.
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, Yuda ʋu le nɔviawo gbɔ yi ɖanɔ Adulam-ŋutsu aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Xira, la gbɔ.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Yuda kpɔ Kanaan-ŋutsu aɖe si woyɔna be Sua la ƒe vinyɔnu, eye wòɖee hedɔ kplii.

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;
translation_verse: Nyɔnua fɔ fu dzi viŋutsu, eye Yuda na ŋkɔe be Er.

english_verse: she named the next one Onan.
translation_verse: Eyome egafɔ fu dzi viŋutsu, eye nyɔnua tsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Onan.

english_verse: The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
translation_verse: Emegbe egadzi viŋutsu bubu, eye nyɔnua na ŋkɔe be Sela. Nyɔnua nɔ Kesib hafi dzi ɖevi sia.

english_verse: Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son.
translation_verse: Yuda ɖe srɔ̃ na eƒe ŋgɔgbevi Er. Nyɔnua ŋkɔe nye Tamar.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Ke Er, Yuda ƒe ŋgɔgbevi, nye ame vɔ̃ɖi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, eya ta Aƒetɔ wui.

english_verse: So Judah told Onan, “It's your duty to marry Tamar and have a child for your brother.”
translation_verse: Tete Yuda gblɔ na Onan be: “Ɖe nɔviwò ƒe ahosi la, ne nàdo ƒome ɖi na nɔviwò la.”

english_verse: Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant.
translation_verse: Ke esi Onan nya be ɖeviawo manye ye tɔ o ta la, ne eya kple nɔvia srɔ̃ wole dɔdɔm, eye ŋutsunu gbɔna la, enana be wòkɔna ɖe anyigba, be nyɔnua magafɔ fu adzi vi ado ƒome ɖi na nɔvia o.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: Eƒe nuwɔna la medze Aƒetɔ ŋu kura o, eya ta ewu eya hã.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Azɔ Yuda gblɔ na toyɔvia Tamar be: “Trɔ yi tɔ́wò ƒeme, eye nànɔ anyi abe ahosi ene va se ɖe esime vinye Sela natsi.” Egblɔ esia elabe evɔ̃ be Sela hã ava ku abe nɔviawo ke ene. Ale Tamar trɔ yi ɖale tɔ́a ƒeme.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: Le ɣeyiɣi didi aɖe megbe la, Yuda srɔ̃, si nye Sua vinyɔnu la ku. Esi Yuda fae vɔ la, eya kple xɔlɔ̃a Xira, Adulamtɔ la, woyi ɖe Timnat be yewoaɖakpɔ ame siwo le fu kom na yeƒe alẽwo la ɖa.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Ame aɖe na nyanya Tamar be: “Kpɔ ɖa, towò gbɔna ɖe Timnat, fu ko ge na eƒe alẽwo.”

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: Ale eɖe eƒe ahovɔ ɖi, tsɔ motsyɔnu tsyɔ ŋkume, eye wòbla eɖokui bubui va bɔbɔ nɔ anyi ɖe Enaim-gbo nu, le Timnat-mɔ dzi. Tamar wɔ esia elabe ekpɔ be Sela tsi aɖe ye, gake wometsɔ ye nɛ be wòaɖe o.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Esi Tamar tsyɔ nu ŋkume ta la, Yuda bu xaa be gbolo aɖe ye.

english_verse: and asked her to sleep with him. She asked, “What will you give me if I do?”
translation_verse: Tete wòdze yi egbɔ le mɔa to hegblɔ nɛ be: “Va míyi, maɖamlɔ gbɔwò.” Menya be yeƒe toyɔvi lae o. Nyɔnua biae be: “Nu ka nànam hafi amlɔ gbɔnye?”

english_verse: “One of my young goats,” he answered. “What will you give me to keep until you send the goat?” she asked.
translation_verse: Yuda ɖo eŋu be: “Malé gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka le nye lãha me aɖo ɖe wò.” Nyɔnua gblɔ be: “Enyo, ekema tsɔ wò nane ɖo awɔba nam, va se ɖe esime nàɖoe ɖem.”

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Yuda biae be: “Nu ka matsɔ ɖo awɔba na wò?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Wò ŋkɔsigɛ kple eŋuka kpakple atizɔti si le asiwò la.” Yuda tsɔ wo nɛ, eye wòmlɔ egbɔ, eye nyɔnua fɔ fu nɛ.

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Tamar yi aƒeme, ɖe motsyɔnu la da ɖi, eye wògatsɔ eƒe ahovɔ ta.
