english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Emegbe Yuda tsɔ gbɔ̃tsu la de xɔlɔ̃a Adulamtɔ la si be netsɔ yi na nyɔnua ne wòaxɔ awɔbanuawo vɛ na ye, gake Xira mekpɔ nyɔnua o.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ebia dua me ŋutsuwo be: “Afi ka gbolo si nɔ mɔ to le Enaim le afii la le?” Ke woɖo eŋu be: “Gbolo aɖeke menɔ afi sia o.”

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Tete wòtrɔ yi Yuda gbɔ ɖagblɔ nɛ be: “Nyemekpɔe o. Dua me ŋutsuwo hã be gbolo aɖeke menɔ afi ma o.”

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Yuda ɖo eŋu be: “Nuawo ate ŋu atsi esi faa, ne menye nenem o la, woava ko mí. Kpɔ ɖa, nye ya, meɖo gbɔ̃tsu la ɖee, ke mèkpɔe atsɔe nɛ o.”

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti etɔ̃ lɔƒo megbe la, wova gblɔ na Yuda be: “Toyɔviwò Tamar wɔ ahasi hefɔ fu ɖe eme.” Tete Yuda ɖe gbe be: “Mikplɔe do goe ne miatɔ dzoe!”

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Ke esi wokplɔ Tamar yinae la, edɔ ame ɖe toa gbɔ be: “Ŋutsu si do fum la ƒe nuwoe nye esiawo. Taflatsɛ, lé ŋku ɖe ŋkɔsigɛa, eŋukaa kple atizɔti la ŋu nyuie be ame ka tɔwoe mahã.”

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Tete Yuda kpɔ nuawo, eye wògblɔ be: “Eƒe nya dzɔ wu tɔnye elabe nyee metsɔe na vinye Sela wòɖe o.” Tso ema dzi la, megade asi eŋu kpɔ o.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: Esime wòle ku lém la, ɖeviawo dometɔ ɖeka do asi ɖa. Tete vixela la sa ka dzĩ ɖe asi ŋu nɛ hegblɔ be: “Esiae tre dodo.”

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: Gake ɖevi sia he asi yi eme, eye wodzi nɔvia gbã. Vixela la gblɔ na esi wodzi gbã la be: “E! Ale ke nèdze mɔ na ɖokuiwò ale?” Eya ta wòna ŋkɔe be Perez.

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: Emegbe nɔvia si ŋu ka dzĩ le la hã va do; eya ta wòna ŋkɔe be Serax.

english_verse: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Esi wokplɔ Yosef yi Egipte la, Egiptetɔ Potifar, si nye Egipte Fiagã ƒe aƒedzikpɔlawo kple eŋumewo ƒe amegã la ƒlee le Ismaeltɔawo si.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: Esi eƒe aƒetɔ la kpɔ be Aƒetɔ li kple Yosef, eye nu sia nu si wòwɔna dzea dzi nɛ la,

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: ekpɔ ŋudzedze le eŋu. Potifar wɔe eƒe subɔla kple eƒemenuwo dzikpɔlae, eye wòtsɔ eƒe nunɔamesiwo katã de esi.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: Potifar tsɔ eƒe nunɔamesiwo katã de Yosef si, eye megatsi dzi le eƒe nunɔamesi aɖeke ŋu o, negbe nu si wòaɖu la ko. Azɔ Yosef dze ɖeka ŋutɔ, eye wònyakpɔ.

english_verse: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
translation_verse: Le ɣeyiɣi aɖewo megbe la, eƒe aƒetɔ srɔ̃ va nɔ ahiãmoe ɖom ɖee, eye wògblɔ na Yosef be: “Va dɔ kplim.”

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Yosef gbe hegblɔ na eƒe aƒetɔ srɔ̃ la be: “Kpɔ ɖa, nye aƒetɔ meganya aƒe sia me nu siwo le asinye me la o; etsɔ eƒe nunɔamesiwo katã de asi nam gɔ̃.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: Mete nanekem le aƒe sia me o, negbe wò dzaa ko, esi nènye srɔ̃a ta. Ale ke mawɔ nu vlo sia gbegbe awɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Mawu ŋuti?”

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be nyɔnua nɔ fu ɖem na Yosef kple nya sia gbe sia gbe hã la, Yosef melɔ̃ kpɔ be yeamlɔ egbɔ, ade asi eŋu o.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka Yosef gava aƒea me, eƒe dɔ wɔ ge. Aƒea me tɔ bubu aɖeke meli o.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: Tete nyɔnua lé Yosef ƒe awu, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Va mímlɔ anyi!” Ke Yosef gblẽ awua ɖe nyɔnua si me, hesí do go le aƒea me.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: eyɔ aƒea me tɔwo vɛ, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Mikpɔ ɖa ko. Srɔ̃nye kplɔ Hebri-ŋutsu sia va de mía dome be wòaɖi gbɔ mí. Eva gbɔnye be yeadɔ kplim, ke medo ɣli sesĩe!

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: Esi wòkpɔ be mele ɣli dom le avi fam sesĩe la, egblẽ eƒe awu ɖe gbɔnye, eye wòsí do go le aƒea me.”

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Etsɔ awu la da ɖe eɖokui gbɔ va se ɖe esime Yosef ƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: Then she said, “That Hebrew slave of yours tried to rape me!
translation_verse: Egblɔ nya mawo ke nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, Hebrivi kluvi ma, si nèkplɔ va mía dome la va gbɔnye be yeaɖi gbɔm.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: Esi medo ɣli ɖe eta la, esí do go le aƒea me gblẽ eƒe awu ɖe gbɔnye!”

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: Ale elé Yosef de gaxɔ si me fia ƒe gamenɔlawo nɔna la me.

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ nɔ kple Yosef, eye wòve enu hena be gaxɔdzikpɔla la kpɔ ŋudzedze le eŋu.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Etsɔ Yosef ɖo gaxɔmenɔlawo katã nu, eye eyae wɔa ɖoɖo ɖe nu sia nu si wowɔna le gaxɔa me la ŋu.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Gaxɔdzikpɔla la megatsia dzi le nu siwo le Yosef ƒe dzikpɔkpɔ te la ŋu o, elabe Aƒetɔ li kple Yosef, eye wòna nu sia nu si Yosef wɔna la dzea edzi.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: eye wòtsɔ wo de gaxɔ me le fiaŋumewo ƒe amegã ƒe aƒeme; Yosef hã le gaxɔ me le afi ma.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Fiaŋumewo ƒe amegã la tsɔ wo de Yosef si, be wòakpɔ wo dzi. Wonɔ gaxɔa me eteƒe didi.

english_verse: One night each of the two men had a dream, but their dreams had different meanings.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka ƒe zã me la, ahakula la kple aboloƒola la ku drɔ̃e wotɔxɛwotɔxɛe, eye ɖe sia ɖe tɔ ƒe gɔmeɖeɖe to vovo.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Esi Yosef va wo gbɔ le ŋdi me la, ekpɔ be woli kpoo, nɔ nu xam.

english_verse: and he asked, “Why are you so worried today?”
translation_verse: Ebia wo be: “Ale ke wɔ egbe mielé blanui li kpoo ale?”

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Míeku drɔ̃e, gake ame meli aɖe egɔme na mí o.” Tete Yosef gblɔ be: “Menye Mawue naa drɔ̃e gɔmeɖeɖe oa? Milĩi nam.”

english_verse: The king's personal servant told Joseph, “In my dream I saw a vine
translation_verse: Ale ahakulawo ƒe amegã lĩ eƒe drɔ̃e na Yosef be: “Le nye drɔ̃ea me la, mekpɔ wainka aɖe le ŋkunye me,

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: alɔ etɔ̃ le eŋu. Kaka aŋgbawo nado ko la, eƒo se, eye wòtse heɖi.

english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: Fia ƒe kplu la nɔ asinye. Ale megbe kutsetseawo, fiãe ɖe kplu la me, hetsɔe de fia si.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Tete Yosef gblɔ nɛ be: “Drɔ̃e la gɔmee nye esi. Alɔ etɔ̃awo nye ŋkeke etɔ̃.

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: Etsɔ manɔmee la, fia la ana nàdo le gaxɔa me, eye wòagatsɔ wò aɖo wò dɔ nu, nàgaku aha nɛ abe tsã ene.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Ke ne eme va nyo na wò la, nàɖo ŋku dzinye. Meɖe kuku, ve nunye nàɖo ŋku dzinye na Egipte Fiagã la be wòaɖem le afi sia.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Le nyateƒe me la, ɖe wofim dzoe le Hebritɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, eye le afii gɔ̃ hã la, nyemewɔ naneke hafi wolém de gaxɔ me o.”

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Esi aboloƒolawo ƒe amegã kpɔ be drɔ̃e la gɔme nyo la, egblɔ na Yosef be: “Nye hã meku drɔ̃e: metsɔ abolo kusi etɔ̃ ɖe ta.

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: Egipte Fiagã la ƒe abolo mème vovovowo le kusi edzitɔ me, ke xeviwo va nɔ wo ɖum le kusia me le tanye.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Yosef ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Wò drɔ̃e la gɔmee nye esi. Kusi etɔ̃awo nye ŋkeke etɔ̃.

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: Etsɔ manɔmee la, fia ana woatso ta le nuwò, ahe wò kukua ɖe ati ŋu, eye xeviwo ava ɖu wò ŋutilã.”

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe la, fia la ɖu eƒe dzigbe. Ekpe eƒe dɔwɔlawo katã va nuɖuƒe, eye wòna woɖe ahakulawo ƒe amegã kple aboloƒolawo ƒe amegã le gaxɔa me. Wokplɔ wo va eya kple eƒe dɔwɔlawo gbɔe.

english_verse: He put the personal servant back in his old job
translation_verse: Egatsɔ ahakulawo ƒe amegã la ɖo eƒe dɔ nu wògakua aha nɛ,

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: ke ena wode ka ve na aboloƒolawo ƒe amegã ya, abe ale si Yosef ɖe drɔ̃eawo gɔme na wo la ene.

english_verse: but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_verse: Azɔ ahakulawo ƒe amegã la meɖo ŋku Yosef dzi o; eŋlɔe be.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Le ƒe eve megbe la, Egipte Fiagã ku drɔ̃e be yenɔ tsitre ɖe Nil-tɔsisi to,

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: eye yekpɔ nyinɔ dami adrẽ siwo nyakpɔ ŋutɔ la wodo go tso tɔsisia me va le gbe ɖum le avawo me.

english_verse: Then seven ugly, skinny cows came up out of the river and
translation_verse: Emegbe nyinɔ adrẽ bubuwo hã do va; woawo ya ɖi ku glàŋuu. Wova le tsitre ɖe nyinɔ kemɛawo gbɔ le tɔsisia to.

english_verse: ate the fat, healthy cows. When this happened, the king woke up.
translation_verse: Kasia ɖeko nyinɔ ɖikuawo lé damitɔwo mi! Tete fia la nyɔ.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: Egayi alɔ̃ me, eye wòku drɔ̃e zi evelia. Ekpɔ lutsetse adrẽ siwo ʋã nyuie, eye wonyakpɔ la le luti ɖeka ŋu.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Emegbe lutsetse adrẽ siwo ɣedzeƒeya lé, eye wodze heteku la hã do.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Kasia lutsetse míamiawo lé ʋaʋãtɔwo mi. Enyɔ, eye wòkpɔ be drɔ̃e kum yenɔ.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, Egipte Fiagã la tɔtɔ, ale wòdɔ woyi ɖayɔ afakalawo kple nunyala siwo katã le Egipte-dukɔa me la vɛ. Elĩ drɔ̃eawo na wo, ke wo dometɔ aɖeke mete ŋu ɖe ɖeke gɔme nɛ o.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Tete ahakulawo ƒe amegã la gblɔ na fia la be: “Meɖo ŋku vodada aɖe si mewɔ la dzi egbe.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: Esi nèdo dɔmedzoe ɖe nye kple aboloƒolawo ƒe amegã ŋu, eye nèna wolé mí de gaxɔ me le fiaŋumewo ƒe amegã ƒeme la,

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: nye kplii míeku drɔ̃e vovovo le zã ɖeka ma me. Drɔ̃eawo gɔmeɖeɖe le vovovo.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Hebri-ɖekakpui aɖe si nye fiaŋumewo ƒe amegã ƒe kluvi la nɔ mía gbɔ le afi ma. Míelĩ míaƒe drɔ̃eawo nɛ, eye wòɖe wo gɔme na mí.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Ale si wòɖe drɔ̃eawo gɔme na mí la, nenema tututu wova emee. Ègatsɔm ɖo nye dɔ nu, ke èna wode ka ve na aboloƒolawo ƒe amegã ya.”

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Tete Egipte Fiagã la dɔ be woayɔ Yosef vɛ, eye woɖee le gaxɔa me enumake. Elũ ge, ɖɔli eƒe awuwo, eye wòva Fiagã la gbɔ.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Egipte Fiagã la gblɔ nɛ be: “Meku drɔ̃e, ame aɖeke mete ŋu ɖe egɔme nam o. Ke mese le ŋuwò be ne wolĩ drɔ̃e na wò la, ètea ŋu ɖea egɔme.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Yosef ɖo eŋu be: “Mawu aɖe drɔ̃ea gɔme na fia wòadze eŋu; menye nye o.”

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Fiagã la lĩ drɔ̃ea be: “Meku drɔ̃e be mele tsitre ɖe Nil-tɔsisi to.

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: Kasia mekpɔ nyinɔ dami adrẽ siwo nyakpɔ ŋutɔ la do tso tɔsisi la me va le gbe ɖum.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Woawo yome la, nyinɔ bubu adrẽ siwo ɖi ku glàŋuu la hã do. Nyemekpɔ nyinɔ siwo vlo abe emawo tɔgbe ene le Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi kpɔ o.

english_verse: The skinny cows ate the fat ones.
translation_verse: Enumake nyinɔ ɖiku vloawo lé nyinɔ dami gbãtɔ adrẽawo mi.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: Gake esi womi wo hã la, ɖeko wogale abe ɖe womemi naneke o ene; woƒe dzedzeme gavlo abe tsã ene. Kasia menyɔ.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: Emegbe megaku drɔ̃e bubu. Mekpɔ lutsetse adrẽ siwo ʋã nyuie, eye wonyakpɔ la le luti ɖeka ŋu.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Le woawo yome la, lutsetse adrẽ siwo ɣedzeƒeya lé womía, eye wotsi to nu la do.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: Kasia lutsetse míamiawo lé ʋaʋãtɔwo mi. Melĩ drɔ̃e siawo na afakalawo, gake wo dometɔ aɖeke mete ŋu ɖe egɔme nam o.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Tete Yosef gblɔ na Fiagã la be: “Fiagã bubutɔ, gɔmeɖeɖe ɖekae li na wò drɔ̃e eveawo. Nu si Mawu ɖo be yeawɔ la, eyae wòɖe fia wò.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Nyinɔ dami adrẽawo nye adrẽ, eye lutsetse ʋaʋã adrẽawo hã nye ƒè adrẽ. Drɔ̃e eveawo sɔ.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Nyinɔ ɖiku vlo adrẽ siwo do evelia la nye ƒè adrẽ. Lutsetse adrẽ siwo ɣedzeƒeya lé wotsi to nu la hã nye ƒè adrẽ, siwo me dɔ ato le.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Abe ale si megblɔ na wò va yi ene la, nu si wɔ ge Mawu le lae wòɖe fia wò.

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Ƒè adrẽ gbɔna, eye nuɖuɖu abɔ ŋutɔ ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Dɔ la nu asẽ ale gbegbe be amewo maganya kura be nuɖuɖu bɔ ɖe anyigba la dzi kpɔ o.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Mawu na nèku drɔ̃e la zi eve elabe eɖo nu si wɔ ge wòle la kplikpaa; ele nàna ge wòava eme kaba.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Di dɔdzikpɔlawo hã ɖo anyigba la dzi kaba, ale be ne nuɖuɖu bɔ fũu le ƒè adrẽ me la, woadzɔ nuawo ƒe akpa atɔ̃lia le dukɔa me.

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: Azɔ na ŋusẽ dɔdzikpɔla siawo be woaƒo ƒu nuɖuɖu le ƒè nyui siwo me nuɖuɖu le bɔbɔ ge la me, woatu nuɖuɖudzraɖoƒewo ɖe duwo me, eye woanɔ wo dzi kpɔm na wò.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: Nuɖuɖua ava zu megbedenu na dukɔ la, ale be ne dɔ to le Egipte-nyigba la dzi ƒè adrẽ la, woava wɔ eŋudɔ, bene dɔwuame nagatsrɔ̃ ame le dukɔa me o.” Wotsɔ Yosef ɖo mɔ́mefia ɖe Egipte-dukɔ nu

english_verse: The king and his officials liked this plan.
translation_verse: Nya sia dze fia la kple eŋumewo katã ŋu.

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Tete fia la bia eŋumeawo be: “Ɖe míate ŋu akpɔ ame aɖe si me Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ la le abe ame sia enea?”

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Ale Fiagã la gblɔ na Yosef be: “Esi Mawu ɖe nu siawo katã fia wò ta la, efia be ame nyanu aɖaŋudzela aɖeke meli abe wò ene o.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Eya ta wò koe matsɔ ɖo nye dukɔ nu. Dukɔ blibo la aɖo to wò. Nye, ame si le fiazikpui la dzi, koe anye ta na wò.”

english_verse: You are now governor of all Egypt!”
translation_verse: Fia la gagblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, metsɔ wò ɖo Egipte-nyigba blibo la nu.”

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Tete Egipte Fiagã la ɖe eƒe ŋkɔsigɛ le asi do na Yosef, do aklala biɖibiɖi wu nɛ, eye wòtsɔ sikakɔsɔkɔsɔ de kɔ nɛ.

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ena wotsɔ eƒe tasiaɖam evelia kɔ Yosef hetsae, eye gbeƒãɖelawo le eŋgɔ le ɣli dom be: “Mide ta agu nɛ! Mide ta agu nɛ!” Ale wòtsɔ Yosef ɖo Egipte-nyigba la katã nu.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Fiagã la gblɔ na Yosef be: “Nyee nye Egipte Fiagã; gake ne wò, mèɖe mɔ o la, ame aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ aɖe afɔ alo anye abɔ le Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi o.”

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Etsɔ Egipte ŋkɔ na Yosef be Zefnat Paneax. Etsɔ Asnat, Potifera si nye On nunɔla vinyɔnu nɛ wòɖe. Yosef yi ɖatsa le Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, agble me nuku ʋã le anyigba la dzi ŋutɔ ƒè adrẽ.

english_verse: Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested.
translation_verse: Ale Yosef na woƒo ƒè adrẽ nuawo nu ƒu ɖe duawo me. Ena wodzra agble ɖe sia ɖe me tɔ ɖo ɖe du si te ɖe eŋu la me.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Bli si woƒo ƒui la sɔ gbɔ abe ƒutake ene. Wodzidzee ʋuu wòglo, ale womegadzidzee yi dzi o.

english_verse: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
translation_verse: Hafi dɔa nava to la, Asnat, Potifera si nye On nunɔla vinyɔnu la, dzi viŋutsu eve na Yosef.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Yosef gblɔ be: “Mawu na meŋlɔ nye fukpekpewo kple nye ƒometɔwo be,” eya ta wòna ŋkɔ eƒe ŋgɔgbevia be Manase.

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: Egagblɔ hã be: “Mawu na medzi viwo le anyigba si dzi mekpe fu le la dzi,” eya ta wòna ŋkɔ via evelia be Efrayim.

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Ƒè adrẽ siwo me nuku ʋã le le Egipte-nyigba dzi la va yi,

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: eye ƒè adrẽ siwo me dɔ to le la dze egɔme, abe ale si Yosef gblɔe ene. Dɔ to le dukɔwo katã me, gake nuɖuɖu nɔ Egipte-nyigba ya dzi.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Mlɔeba dɔwuame la va Egipte-nyigba hã dzi, eye dukɔa me tɔwo bia fia la be wòana nuɖuɖu yewo. Eɖo wo ɖe Yosef gbɔ, gblɔ na wo be: “Nu sia nu si wògblɔ na mi la, miwɔe.”

english_verse: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Dɔwuame la nu sẽ ɖe edzi le afi sia afi le dukɔa me. Tete Yosef ʋu nuɖuɖudzraɖoƒewo katã nu, eye wòdzra bli na Egiptetɔwo.

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Amewo tso xexeme ƒe afi sia afi va Egipte be yewoaƒle bli le Yosef gbɔ, elabe dɔwuame la nu sẽ ŋutɔ le xexe blibo la me.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Esi Yakob se be bli le Egipte la, egblɔ na viawo be: “Ale ke wɔ miele afii le mia nɔewo ƒe mo kpɔm?

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: Mese be bli le Egipte, eya ta miyi ɖaƒle ɖe vɛ ne dɔ nagawu mí míaku o!”

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Ale Yosef nɔviwo dometɔ ewo dzra ɖo be yewoayi Egipte aɖaƒle blia.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Gake Yakob meɖe mɔ na Benyamin, Yosef dadavi, ya be neyi kple wo o, elabe evɔ̃ be nu vevi ava wɔe.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Tete Israelviwo va Egipte bli ƒle ge, abe ame bubuwo ene, elabe dɔ to le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, Yosef nye mɔ́mefia le dukɔa me, eye eyae dzraa bli na ame siwo katã tso xexea me godoo va la. Yosef nɔviwo va, eye wodze klo de ta agu nɛ.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋku drɔ̃e si wòku le wo ŋu la dzi, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Ŋkutsalawo mienye. Ɖe mieva be yewoadi mɔnu le míaƒe anyigba la ŋu.”

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Gbeɖe, amegã, wò dɔlawo míenye; nuɖuɖu ko ƒle ge míeva.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Ŋutsu ɖeka viwo mí katã míenye. Menye ŋkutsalawo míenye o, amegã, ke boŋ nuteƒewɔlawo míenye.”

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Yosef ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Kpao, mɔnu di ge mieva le míaƒe anyigba la ŋu!”

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Woxɔ edzi be: “Nɔvi wui eve míenye henye ŋutsu ɖeka viwo le Kanaan-nyigba dzi. Mía nɔvi ɖeka megali o, eye mía nɔvi ɖevitɔ ya tsi mía tɔ́a gbɔ.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: It's like I said. You're spies,
translation_verse: Yosef ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Eya ko megblɔ be ŋkutsalawo mienye la!

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Mele mia do ge kpɔ ale: Metà Egipte Fiagã la! Miele dzodzo ge le afii akpɔ o, negbe ɖeko mia nɔvi ɖevitɔ la va afii hafi!

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Midɔ mia dometɔ ɖeka ɖa ne wòaɖakplɔe vɛ. Ke mi ame mamlɛawo ya la, mianɔ ga me va se ɖe esime manya kɔtɛe be nyateƒe tom miele. Evɔ ne menye nenem o la, metà fia, ŋkutsalawo mienye.”

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Yosef lé wo de ga me ŋkeke etɔ̃.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe la, Yosef gblɔ na wo be: “Mawuvɔ̃la menye, eya ta ne miedi be yewoatsi agbe la, miwɔ nya si gblɔ ge mala na mi la dzi.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Nenye nyateƒe tom miele la, ekema mina mia nɔvi ɖeka natsi ga me le afii ne miadzo. Mi ame mamlɛawo mitsɔ blia yi na mia tɔwo le aƒea ne woatsɔ lé dɔwuame la nu.

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: Ne mieyi la, mikplɔ mia nɔvi ɖevitɔ la vɛ nam bene manya be nyateƒe tom miele, ne nyemagawu mi o.” Wolɔ̃ ɖe nya sia dzi,

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: eye wogblɔ na wo nɔewo be: “Le nyateƒe me la, nu si míewɔ mía nɔvia tae míeɖo xaxa sia me ɖo. Togbɔ be míekpɔ be dzidzi ƒo mía nɔvia, eye wòɖe kuku na mí vevie ʋuu hã la, ɖeko míedo tokui! Eya tae míeɖo xaxa sia me fifia.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Ruben gblɔ na wo be: “Megblɔ na mi be migawɔ vɔ̃ aɖekee o, gake miegbe. Azɔ la, wole to hem na mí ɖe eƒe ku ta.”

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Ke womenya be Yosef se nyaawo o, elabe gbesela dzie woƒo nu toe.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Tete Yosef dzo le wo gbɔ ɖafa avi. Egatrɔ va wo gbɔ, eye wòƒo nu kple wo. Eɖe Simeon le wo dome, eye wòna woblae le wo katã ŋkume. Yosef nɔviwo gatrɔ yi Kanaan

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Emegbe la, Yosef ɖe gbe be woade bli nɔviawo ƒe kotokuawo me woayɔ, woatsɔ ame sia ame ƒe ga ade eƒe kotokua me, eye woana nuɖuɖu wo hena mɔzɔzɔ. Ameawo wɔ ɖe edzi.

english_verse: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
translation_verse: Wodo bligba na woƒe tedziwo, eye wodze mɔ.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Esi woɖo afi si woatsi dɔ la, wo dometɔ ɖeka ʋu eƒe kotokua nu be yeana nuɖuɖu yeƒe tedzi. Kasia ekpɔ ga si wòtsɔ xe fee la le blia dzi.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Eyɔ nɔviawo gblɔ na wo be: “Wogbugbɔ nye ga nam! Eyae nye esi le nye kotokua me!” Tete dzika tso wo ƒo, eye wodzo nyànyanya hebia wo nɔewo be: “Nu kae nye esi Mawu wɔ mí?”

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Esi wogbɔ va wo tɔ́ Yakob gbɔ le Kanaan-nyigba dzi la, wogblɔ nya siwo katã dzɔ ɖe wo dzi la nɛ. Wogblɔ be:

english_verse: The governor of Egypt was rude and treated us like spies.
translation_verse: “Anyigba la dziɖula he nya ɖe mía ŋu vevie. Ebu mí ŋkutsalawoe.

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Ke míegblɔ nɛ be menye ŋkutsalawo míenye o; ke boŋ nuteƒewɔlawo míenye.

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Nɔvi wui eve siwo nye ŋutsu ɖeka viwo míenye. Mía nɔvi ɖeka megali o, eye mía nɔvi ɖevitɔ ya le mía tɔ́ gbɔ ɖa le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Tete dziɖula la gblɔ na mí be: ‘Nu si matsɔ ado mi kpɔ be nyateƒetolawo mienye lae nye esi: Migblẽ mia nɔvi ɖeka ɖe gbɔnye, eye mi ame mamlɛawo miatsɔ blia ayi na miaƒe ƒomeawo bene woatsɔ alé dɔwuame la nu.

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: Mikplɔ mia nɔvi ɖevitɔ la vɛ nam, ne manya be menye ŋkutsalawo mienye o, ke boŋ nyateƒe tom miele; ekema maɖe asi le mia nɔvi si le asinye me la ŋu na mi, eye miate ŋu anɔ anyigba sia dzi awɔ dɔ.’ ”

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Azɔ esi wotrɔ blia le kotokuawo me la, wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe kpɔ be yeƒe ga le kotokua me. Esi woawo kple wo tɔ́ kpɔ gaa la, vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo ŋutɔ.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Tete wo tɔ́ Yakob gblɔ na wo be: “Miena vinyewo ku nam vɔ! Yosef megali o; Simeon hã megali o. Azɔ miedi be yewoagaxɔ Benyamin hã. Nye ɖeka ko dzie nya siawo katã le dzɔdzɔm ɖo.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Ruben gblɔ na tɔ́a be: “Ne nyemekplɔ Benyamin gbɔe na wò o la, àte ŋu awu vinye ŋutsuvi eveawo faa. Wò ya tsɔe de asi nam ko; makplɔe agbɔe na wò.”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Ke Yakob ɖo eŋu be: “Vinye la mayi kpli mi gbeɖe o; dadavia ku, eye eya ɖeka koe susɔ ɖi. Ne dzɔgbevɔ̃e aɖe dzɔ ɖe edzi le mɔa dzi la, miana matsɔ ta ɣi ayi tsiẽƒe kple nuxaxa.”

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,
translation_verse: Dɔwuame la nu va sẽ ɖe dzi ŋutɔ le anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Yakob kple eƒe ƒomea ɖu bli si woƒle tso Egipte vɛ la vɔ, ale Yakob gblɔ na viawo be: “Migayi ne miaɖaƒle nuɖuɖu vi aɖe vɛ na mí.”

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: Ke ne mèlɔ̃ be neyi kpli mí o la, míayi o. Elabe ŋutsua te gbe ɖe edzi na mí be, ne míekplɔ mía nɔvia vɛ o la, mígado ɖe ye ŋkume o.”

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Israel gblɔ na wo be: “Miewɔ nu vevim. Nu ka ta mieʋu nya me na ŋutsua be nɔvi gale yewo si?”

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Ŋutsua bia gbe mí tsitotsito tso míawo ŋutɔ kple míaƒe ƒome la ŋu. Ebia be, ‘Mia tɔ́ gale agbea? Nɔvi bubu gale mia sia?’ Biabia siawo ŋue míeɖo nɛ. Ale ke míawɔ anya be agblɔ na mí be míkplɔ mía nɔvia vɛ?”

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Yuda gblɔ na tɔ́a be: “Ɖe asi le ɖevia ŋu nam ne makplɔe yii ne wò ŋutɔ, míawo kple mía viwo nagaku o.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Eƒe nya ɖe sia ɖe kpɔ ŋkunye me; ele asinye me. Ne nyemete ŋu kplɔe gbɔe na wò o la, bu fɔm tegbee.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Ne menye ɖe míele hehem ɖe megbe o la, anye ne míede gbɔ zi eve xoxo.”

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Tete wo tɔ́a, Israel, gblɔ na wo be: “Ekema mitsɔ mía de nu nyui aɖewo ɖe asi yi ɖana ŋutsua. Mitsɔ atikemi, anyitsi vi aɖe, aŋe, kotoklobo, ayedee kple yevuzi.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Mitsɔ nuƒlega ƒe teƒe eve kple ga si wogbugbɔ de kotokuawo me la hã ɖe asi. Ɖewohĩ anye vodadae wowɔ.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Azɔ mikplɔ mia nɔvia ne miayi.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Mawu Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la neve mia nu le ŋutsua gbɔ ale be wòaɖe asi le mia nɔvia kple Benyamin ŋuti na mi. Ke nye ya la, ne vi gaku nam la, eku nam.”

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Ale nɔviŋutsuawo tsɔ nunanaawo kple ga homea ƒe teƒe eve ɖe asi, kplɔ Benyamin hedze mɔ yi Egipte. Wova ɖo Yosef gbɔ.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Esi Yosef kpɔ be Benyamin le wo dome la, egblɔ na eƒe aƒedzikpɔla be: “Kplɔ ŋutsu siawo yi nye aƒemee. Wole nu ɖu ge kplim egbe ŋdɔ, eya ta wu lã nàɖa nu na mí.”

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Aƒedzikpɔla la wɔ Yosef ƒe gbe dzi, eye wòkplɔ ŋutsuawo yi Yosef ƒemee.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo elabe wokplɔ wo yi Yosef ƒeme, eye wogblɔ be: “Ga si wogbugbɔ de míaƒe kotokuawo me esi míeva zi gbãtɔ la tae wokplɔ mí vɛ ɖo. Wole mía dzi dze ge, axɔ míaƒe tedziwo le mía si sesẽe, eye woawɔ mí kluviwoe.”

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Wote ɖe Yosef ƒe aƒedzikpɔla la ŋu le xɔa ƒe ʋɔtru nu, eye wogblɔ nɛ be:

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: “Taflatsɛ, amegã, míeva afii zi gbãtɔ va ƒle bli.

english_verse: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
translation_verse: Esi míeɖo agbadroƒe, eye míetu míaƒe kotokuawo la, ame sia ame kpɔ eƒe ga si wòtsɔ xe fee la le eƒe bli dzi le kotokua me. Kpɔ ɖa, eyae nye esi míetrɔ vɛ.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Míetsɔ ga bubu ɖe asi vɛ be míatsɔ agaƒle bli. Míenya ame si trɔ míaƒe ga de míaƒe kotokuwo me o.”

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Ŋutsua ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Miaƒe dzi nedze eme. Migavɔ̃ o. Mia Mawu la, mia tɔ́ ƒe Mawu lae tsɔ ga la de miaƒe kotokuwo me. Wotsɔ miaƒe ga si miexe la nam.” Tete wòkplɔ Simeon vɛ na wo.

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, aƒedzikpɔla la kplɔ ŋutsuawo ge ɖe Yosef ƒe aƒeme. Eku tsi na wo woklɔ afɔ, eye wòna nuɖuɖu woƒe tedziwo.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Woɖo nunanaawo ɖi be ne Yosef va le ŋdɔ me la, yewoatsɔ wo nɛ elabe wose be yewole nu ɖu ge kplii le afi ma.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Esi Yosef va aƒea me la, wotsɔ nunanaawo nɛ, eye wode ta agu nɛ.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Le gbelɔlɔ̃ kplii me la, ebia wo be: “Mia tɔ́ amegãɖeɖi, si ŋu mieƒo nu le nam la ɖe, egale agbea? Eli sesĩea?”

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Mía tɔ́, wò subɔla, gale agbe, eye wòli sesĩe.” Tete wodze klo tsyɔ mo anyi ɖe eŋgɔ.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Yosef fɔ ta dzi eye wòkpɔ Benyamin, dadavia. Ebia be: “Mia nɔvi ɖevitɔ si ŋu mieƒo nu le nam lae nye esia? Vinye, Mawu neve nuwò.”

english_verse: Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried.
translation_verse: Tete Yosef dzudzɔ eƒe nuƒoa elabe eƒe dɔme trɔ ɖe nɔvia ŋu, eye wòdi be yeafa avi. Ale wòyi ɖe eƒe xɔgãme ɖafa avi le afi ma.

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: Efu mo, lé eɖokui nyuie, eye wòdo go va. Egblɔ be: “Mima nuɖuɖua!”

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ Yosef tɔ nɛ vovo, eye wotsɔ nɔviawo hã tɔ na wo vovo. Nenema ke wotsɔ Egiptetɔ siwo ɖua nu kplii la hã tɔ na wo vovo. Egiptetɔwo meɖua nu kple Hebritɔwo o, elabe wobunɛ be enye ŋunyɔnu.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: Wona wonɔ anyi dze ŋgɔ Yosef le nua ɖuƒe. Woɖo wo ɖe tsitsi nu, tso tsitsitɔ dzi va se ɖe ɖevitɔ dzi. Esi nɔviawo de dzesi ale si wòna wonɔ anyii la, woƒe nu ku, eye wole wo nɔewo kpɔm dũu.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Yosef na woka nuɖuɖu si le ekɔme la na nɔviawo, eye wòna Benyamin tɔ sɔ gbɔ wu nɔviawo katã tɔ zigbɔzi atɔ̃. Woɖu nu, no nu, eye wokpɔ dzidzɔ kplii.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: Tsɔ nye klosalokplu de ɖevitɔ ƒe kotoku me kpe ɖe ga si wòtsɔ va nu ƒle ge la ŋu.” Ewɔ ɖe nya si Yosef gblɔ nɛ la dzi.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Le ŋufɔke ŋdi kanya la, wodo mɔ ŋutsuawo wodzo kple woƒe tedziwo.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Esi wodo go le dua me yina sẽe la, Yosef gblɔ na eƒe aƒedzikpɔla be: “Tso nàti ŋutsuawo yome nàɖatu wo. Bia wo se be: ‘Nu ka ta mietsɔ vɔ̃ ɖo nyui teƒe? Nu ka ta miefi nye aƒetɔ ƒe klosalokplu ɖo?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Eyae wòtsɔna noa nui. Eya mee wokpɔa nu ɣaɣlawo le gblɔna. Miewɔ busunu!’ ”

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Esi aƒedzikpɔla la va tu wo la, egblɔ nya siawo na wo tututu.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Nu ka, amegã, nya kae nye esi gblɔm nèle? Gbeɖe, míate ŋu awɔ nu sia tɔgbe akpɔ o!

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, esi míeɖo Kanaan-nyigba dzi, kpɔ ga le blia dzi le miaƒe kotokuawo me la, míetrɔe vɛ na wòe. Ale ke wɔ míafi klosalo alo sika le wò aƒetɔ ƒeme adzoe azɔ?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Amegã, mía dometɔ si gbɔ nàkpɔe le la dze na ku, eye mí ame mamlɛawo la míazu wò kluviwo.”

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: “Melɔ̃ ɖe edzi. Ɖeko ame si gbɔ woakpɔe le la lazu nye kluvi, mi ame mamlɛawo ya miadzo ayi faa.”

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Enumake ame sia ame ɖiɖi eƒe kotoku ɖe anyigba, eye wòtui.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Aƒedzikpɔla la de asi kplua didi me. Edze egɔme tso tsitsitɔ dzi va wu nu ɖe ɖevitɔ dzi. Kasia wokpɔ kplu la le Benyamin ƒe agba me.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Nɔviŋutsuawo dze woƒe awuwo kple veve. Wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe gado agba na eƒe tedzi, eye wogbugbɔ yi dua me.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Esi Yuda kple nɔviawo va Yosef ƒeme la, Yosef gale afi ma. Wodze klo de ta agu nɛ,

english_verse: who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
translation_verse: eye Yosef bia wo se be: “Nu ka nye esi miewɔ? Ɖe mienyae be, ame abe nye ene, mekaa nu oa?”

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Yuda ɖo eŋu be: “Amegã, nya kae le mía si míate ŋu agblɔ na wò? Ale ke míaʋli nya siae? Ale ke míaɖe mía ɖokui nui? Mawu klo nu le wò dɔlawo ƒe nuvɔ̃ dzi. Kpɔ ɖa, menye ame si gbɔ wokpɔ wò kplua le la koe lanye wò kluvi o; mí katã tim míezu wò kluviwo.”

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Yosef ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Gbeɖe! Nyemawɔ nenema akpɔ o. Ame si gbɔ wokpɔ nye kplua le la, eya koe anye nye kluvi. Mi ame mamlɛawo mitrɔ yi mia tɔ́a gbɔ le ŋutifafa me.” Yuda ɖe kuku ɖe Benyamin ta

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Tete Yuda te ɖe Yosef ŋu gblɔ be: “Amegã, taflatsɛ, na maƒo nu na wò faa. Dzi megaku wò ɖe ŋunye o; èle abe Fiagã ŋutɔ ene.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Amegã, èbia mí se be, ‘Ɖe tɔ́ alo nɔviŋutsu aɖe gale mia sia?’

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Míeɖo eŋu be: ‘Mía tɔ́ amegãɖeɖi li, eye míaƒe dɔmlɔea ŋutsuvi hã li. Wodzi eya na mía tɔ́ le eƒe tsitsime. Ke dadavia ku, dadavi aɖeke megale esi o; tɔ́a lɔ̃nɛ vevie.’

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: Azɔ ègblɔ na mí be míkplɔe vɛ na ye ne yeakpɔ.

english_verse: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
translation_verse: Ke míeɖo eŋu be ɖevia mate ŋu adzo le tɔ́a gbɔ o; ne edzo la, tɔ́a aku.

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Tete nègblɔ na mí be, ne míekplɔ mía nɔvi ɖevitɔ la vɛ o la, mígado ɖe ye ŋkume o.

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: Esi míetrɔ yi mía tɔ́a gbɔ la, míegblɔ wò nya la nɛ.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: Emegbe mía tɔ́a gblɔ na mí be migatrɔ va ƒle nuɖuɖu vɛ.

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: Míeɖo eŋu be: ‘Míate ŋu ayi o. Ne míawo ɖeɖe míeyi, eye mía nɔvi ɖevitɔ la mekpe ɖe mía ŋu o la, ŋutsua maɖe mɔ míado ɖe eŋkume o. Ne mía nɔvi ɖevitɔ la le mía dome ko hafi míawo hã míayi.’

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Tete mía tɔ́a gblɔ na mí be: ‘Mienyae be viŋutsu eve ko srɔ̃nye Raxel dzi nam.

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: Ɖeka ku le gbɔnye. Megblɔ be lã wɔadã aɖe kokokoe vuvui, elabe va se ɖe fifi la, nyemekpɔe kpɔ o.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Ne miekplɔ evelia sia hã yii, eye nane dzɔ ɖe edzi la, mafa konyi ʋuu ayi yɔ me kple nye ta ɣia.’

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: Azɔ ne meɖaɖo wò dɔla, tɔ́nye gbɔ, eye ɖevi si wòlɔ̃ vevie la mele mía dome o la,

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Gawu la, metsɔ ɖokuinye dè megbe na ɖevia le tɔ́nye gbɔ. Medo ŋugbe nɛ be, ne nyemekplɔ ɖevia gbɔe o la, meɖi fɔ le egbɔ tegbee.

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Eya ta amegã, meɖe kuku, nye la, matsi afii azu wò kluvi ɖe ɖevia teƒe, ne eya nagbugbɔ ayi aƒe kple nɔviawo.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Ale ke mate ŋu atrɔ ayi tɔ́nye gbɔ, ɖevia manɔmee? Kpao! Nyemate ŋu akpɔ dzɔgbevɔ̃e gã si ava edzi la teƒe kple ŋku o.”

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Yosef magate ŋu alé eɖokui le ame siwo le egbɔ la ŋkume o. Eɖe gbe be: “Ame sia ame nedo go!” Ame bubu aɖeke menɔ wo gbɔ hafi wòɖe eɖokui fia nɔviawo o.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Yosef wó avi doo, do ɣli ale be Egiptetɔawo kple fiaƒemetɔwo hã see.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: Yosef gblɔ na nɔviawo be: “Nyee nye Yosef! Tɔ́nye gale agbea?” Ke esi nɔviawo se nyaa la, wolulu, eye gbɔgblɔ bu ɖe wo.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Yosef gblɔ na wo be: “Kpɔ ɖa, mite va gbɔnye.” Esi wote ɖe eŋu la, egblɔ na wo be: “Nyee nye mia nɔvi Yosef. Nyee miedzra ɖo ɖe Egipte.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Gake migaxa nu o, eye megave mi kura be yewoe dzram, wokplɔ va afii o, elabe Mawu ɖe wòɖom ɖe mia ŋgɔ be mava xɔ amewo ɖe agbe.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, ƒè eve koe nye esi dɔ to le anyigba dzi; egasusɔ ƒè atɔ̃ sɔŋ si me amewo mate ŋu agade agble alo aŋe nu o.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Ke Mawu dɔm ɖe mia ŋgɔ, be ame ʋɛ aɖe natsi agbe le anyigba sia dzi na mi, eye ame geɖe natsi agbe na mi.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Menye miawoe dɔm ɖe afii o; ke boŋ Mawue. Eyae tsɔm wɔ fia la ƒe adaŋudela vevi, eye nyee kpɔa eƒe aƒe dzi, ganye Egipte-nyigba blibo la dziɖula.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: Eya ta netsɔ miayi tɔ́nye gbɔ aɖagblɔ nɛ be nye via Yosef mebe: ‘Mawu wɔm mezu Egipte-nyigba la katã dziɖula. Va gbɔnye kaba; mègahe ɖe megbe o.

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Wò ŋutɔ, viwò ŋutsuwo kple wò tɔgbuiyɔviwo, wò alẽwo kple nyiwo kpakple nu siwo katã le asiwò la, mianɔ Gosen-nutome ale be miate ɖe ŋunye.

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Makpɔ dziwò le afi ma elabe esusɔ ƒè atɔ̃ sɔŋ ne dɔa nake. Ne menye nenem o la, hiã atu wò kple wò aƒekɔ kple nu siwo katã le asiwò la.’

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: Yosef yi eƒe nuƒoa dzi be: Azɔ la, miawo ŋutɔ miele ekpɔm kple ŋku; nɔvinye Benyamin hã le ekpɔm be nye ŋutɔe le nu ƒom na mi.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Miɖagblɔ bubu si gbegbe wotsɔ nam le Egipte kple nu siwo katã miekpɔ la na tɔ́nye. Miwɔ kaba ne miakplɔe va afii.”

english_verse: Joseph and Benjamin hugged each other and started crying.
translation_verse: Tete wòkpla asi kɔ na nɔvia Benyamin, eye wòwó avi; Benyamin hã kpla asi kɔ nɛ kple avi.

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Yosef gbugbɔ nu na nɔviawo katã kple avi. Esia yome la, nɔviawo de asi dzeɖoɖo me kplii.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Esi Egipte Fiagã la se be “Yosef nɔviwo va” la, dzi dzɔ eya kple eƒe dɔlawo ŋutɔ.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Fiagã la gblɔ na Yosef be: “Gblɔ na nɔviwòawo be: ‘Mido agba na miaƒe lãwo ne miagbugbɔ yi Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: Mikplɔ mia tɔ́a kple miaƒe ƒometɔwo ne miatrɔ va gbɔnye. Mana anyigba nyuitɔ mi le Egipte eye miaɖu anyigba la dzi nu nyuiwo aɖi ƒo.’

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: De se na wo be: ‘Miwɔ ale: mitsɔ tasiaɖamwo tso Egipte yii, ne mia viwo kple mia srɔ̃wo kpakple mia tɔ́a naɖo ava.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Miɖe susu ɖa le miaƒe nunɔamesiwo ŋu, elabe nu nyuitɔwo katã le Egipte-nyigba dzi lanye mia tɔ.”

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Yakob viwo wɔ nu si wogblɔ na wo la dzi. Yosef na tasiaɖamwo wo abe ale si fia la ɖe gbe ene, eye wòna nuɖuɖu hã wo na mɔzɔzɔa.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: Ena awu wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe; ke ena klosaloga alafa etɔ̃ kple awu dodo atɔ̃ Benyamin ya.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Edo agba na tedzi ewo kple Egipte nu nyuiwo, eye wògado agba na tedzinɔ ewo hã kple bli, abolo kpakple nuɖuɖu bubu siwo woaɖu le mɔ dzi, ne wotrɔ gbɔna la, ɖo ɖe tɔ́a.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Azɔ edo mɔ nɔviawo. Esi wole mɔ dzem la, exlɔ̃ nu wo be: “Migawɔ dzre le mɔ dzi o lo.”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Ale wodzo le Egipte, va ɖo wo tɔ́, Yakob, gbɔ le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Yosef gale agbe! Eyae le Egipte-nyigba katã dzi ɖum!” Yakob lulu, eye mexɔ nya la dzi se o.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Ke esi woto nya siwo katã Yosef gblɔ ɖo ɖee la nɛ, eye wòkpɔ tasiaɖam siwo Yosef ɖo ɖa be wòaɖo ava la, egaɖo eɖokui me.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Israel gblɔ be: “Esia sɔ gbɔ nam. Vinye Yosef gale agbe! Mayi aɖakpɔe hafi aku!”

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Ale Yakob ƒo ƒu eƒe nuwo katã eye wòdze mɔ yi Beer-Seba. Esa vɔ na tɔ́a Isak ƒe Mawu la le afi ma.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Mawu ƒo nu nɛ le ŋutega me le zã me. Eyɔe be: “Yakob, Yakob!” Etɔ be: “Nyee nye esi!”

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Tete Mawu gblɔ nɛ be: “Nyee nye Mawu, tɔ́wò ƒe Mawu la. Mègavɔ̃ Egipte yiyi o, elabe mawɔ wò nàzu dukɔ gã aɖe le afi ma.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: Nye ŋutɔ mayi Egipte kpli wò, eye nye ŋutɔ magakplɔ wò agbɔe. Yosef akpɔ wò kuƒe eye wòalé wò ŋkuyiwo akpe.”

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
translation_verse: Viŋutsuvi siwo Lea dzi na Yakob le Padan-Aram hekpe ɖe via nyɔnu Dina ŋu lae nye esiawo. Via ŋutsuwo kple via nyɔnuwo katã le ame bla etɔ̃ vɔ etɔ̃.

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Ne fia la yɔ mi, eye wòbia be: ‘Dɔ ka wɔlawo mienye?’ hã la,

english_verse: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
translation_verse: Silpa, kosi si Laban na via nyɔnu Lea viŋutsu siwo wòdzi na Yakob lae nye esiawo. Wo katã le ame wui ade.

english_verse: Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren. Their son Dan took his son Hushim. Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
translation_verse: Bilha, kosi si Laban na via nyɔnu Raxel la ƒe viŋutsu siwo wòdzi na Yakob lae nye esiawo. Wo katã le ame adrẽ.

english_verse: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
translation_verse: Yakob ƒe dzidzimevi ŋutɔŋutɔ siwo ʋu yi Egipte kplii la le ame bla ade vɔ ade; via ŋutsuawo srɔ̃wo mele eme o.

english_verse: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
translation_verse: Yakob dɔ Yuda ɖe Yosef gbɔ do ŋgɔ be wòava kpe yewo le Gosen. Esi wòɖaɖo la,

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Yosef dzra ɖo, eye wòɖo eƒe tasiaɖam la yi tɔ́a Israel kpe ge le Gosen. Esi wòdo go tɔ́a la, ekpla asi kɔ nɛ, eye wòfa avi ɖe edzi ʋuu.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Israel gblɔ na Yosef be: “Mate ŋu aku azɔ faa, elabe mekpɔ wò nègale agbe.”

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Tete Yosef gblɔ na nɔviawo kple tɔ́a ƒemetɔwo be: “Mayi aɖagblɔe na fia la be: ‘Nɔvinye kple tɔ́nye ƒometɔ siwo le Kanaan-nyigba dzi la va.

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Lãnyilawo wonye, eye wova kple woƒe lãhawo: alẽ, nyi kple woƒe nunɔamesiwo katã.’

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: miɖo eŋu nɛ be: ‘Lãnyilawo wò dɔlawo nye tso ɖevime ke abe mía tɔgbuiwo ene.’ Ne miegblɔ nenema la, aɖe mɔ na mi mianɔ Gosen-nutome.” Elabe alẽkplɔlawo nye ŋunyɔnu na Egiptetɔwo.

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Fia la bia Yosef nɔviwo be: “Dɔ ka wɔlawo mienye?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Lãnyilawo míenye abe mía tɔgbuiwo ke ene.”

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Woyi dzi gblɔ nɛ be: “Taflatsɛ, míeva be míanɔ anyigba sia dzi elabe míaƒe lãhawo megakpɔ gbe aɖu o eye dɔwuame la nu sẽ le Kanaan-nyigba dzi ale gbegbe. Eya ta míeɖe kuku na wò, ɖe mɔ na mí, wò dɔlawo, ne míanɔ Gosen-nutoa me.”

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Tete Fiagã la gblɔ na Yosef be: “Tɔ́wò kple nɔviwòwo va ɖo.

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Egipte-nyigba la le asiwò me. Àte ŋu ada wo ɖe Gosen-nutome elabe anyigba nyo le afi ma ŋutɔ. Ne ènya kutrikula aɖewo le wo dome la, tsɔ nye lãhawo de wo si ne woakpɔ wo dzi.”

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Tete Yosef kplɔ tɔ́a va Fiagã la gbɔe, eye Yakob yra fia la.

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: Fiagã la biae be: “Ƒe nenie nèxɔ?”

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Emegbe Yakob gayra Fiagã la, eye wòtrɔ dzo.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Azɔ Yosef fia teƒe si tɔ́a kple nɔviawo anɔ le Egipte-nyigba dzi la wo. Ena anyigba nyuitɔ wo ɖe Ramses-nutome, abe ale si Fiagã la gblɔ nɛ ene.

english_verse: The famine was bad everywhere in Egypt and Canaan, and the people were suffering terribly.
translation_verse: Dɔwuame la nu va sẽ ale gbegbe; nuɖuɖu aɖeke megale afi aɖeke o. Nu té amewo ŋu eye Egipte kple Kanaan-nyigba dzi ƒu kplákplakpla.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Yosef ƒo ƒu ga si Egiptetɔwo kple Kanaantɔwo tsɔ va ƒle bli le egbɔ la nu ƒu hetsɔ yi Egipte Fiagã ƒemee.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Esi ga vɔ le Egipte kple Kanaan-nyigba dzi la, Egiptetɔwo katã va Yosef gbɔ be: “Na nuɖuɖu mí! Ga vɔ le mía si keŋkeŋ. Ànɔ mía kpɔm ale, míaku le ŋkuwò mea?”

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Yosef ɖo eŋu be: “Ne ga vɔ le mia si la, mikplɔ miaƒe lãhawo vɛ. Maxɔ wo ana nuɖuɖu mi ɖe wo teƒe.”

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Esi ƒè trɔ la, wogava egbɔ be: “Amegã, míate ŋu aɣla nya aɖeke ɖe wò o. Nya lae nye be ga vɔ le mía si keŋkeŋ eye míaƒe lãhawo hã va zu tɔwò. Naneke megale mía si míatsɔ na wò wu míawo ŋutɔ kple míaƒe anyigbawo o.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Ànɔ mí kple anyigba kpɔm ale, míatsrɔ̃ le ŋkuwò mea? Mègana míaƒe agbledeƒewo natsi anyi o. Xɔ mí kple míaƒe agbledenyigbawo, ne nàna nuɖuɖu mí ɖe eteƒe. Míelɔ̃ be míanye fia la ƒe kluviwo, eye míaƒe anyigbawo nazu etɔ. Na nuku mí míaƒã, ne míaƒe agblewo nagazu afuti o.”

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: Ale Yosef ƒle agbledeƒe siwo katã le Egipte-nyigba dzi la na fia la. Egiptetɔ ɖe sia ɖe dzra eƒe agbledeƒe elabe dɔwuame la nu sẽ ŋutɔ. Agbledeƒewo katã va zu fia tɔ.

english_verse: and made everyone the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Azɔ dukɔmetɔwo va zu kluviwo le Egipte-nyigba bliboa dzi.

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: Ke Yosef meƒle nunɔlawo ƒe anyigba ya o, elabe fia la naa dzikpɔga wo, eye wokpɔa woƒe nuɖuɖu tso egbɔ. Eya ta nunɔlawo medzra woƒe anyigba o.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Tete Yosef gblɔ na dukɔmetɔwo be: “Mikpɔ ɖa, tso egbe dzi la, meƒle mi kple miaƒe agbledeƒewo siaa na fia. Nukuwo nye esi; mixɔ wo yi ɖaƒã.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: Ne mieŋe nu la, mima nua ɖe akpa atɔ̃ me: Akpa ɖeka nanye fia tɔ, eye akpa ene mamlɛawo nanye miawo ŋutɔ tɔ. Miaƒã ɖe, eye esi susɔ nanye nuɖuɖu na miawo ŋutɔ, mia viwo kple mia ƒemetɔwo.”

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Wòe xɔ mí ɖe agbe! Ne edze nye aƒetɔ ŋu la, míanye Egipte Fiagã ƒe kluviwo.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Ale Yosef de se le Egipte-nyigba dzi be, ne woŋe nu la, nukuawo ƒe akpa atɔ̃lia nanye fia tɔ. Se sia gali va se ɖe egbe. Nunɔlawo ƒe anyigbawo koe menye fia tɔ o. Nu mamlɛtɔ si Yakob bia be woawɔ na ye

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Israel nɔ Gosen-nutome le Egipte-nyigba dzi. Wokpɔ kesinɔnu geɖe, eye wodzi, gadzi fũu ŋutɔ.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: Esi Israel ƒe kuɣi ɖo la, ena woyɔ via Yosef vɛ, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Taflatsɛ, ne nye nya dze ŋuwò la, tsɔ asi de nye atame, eye nàdo ŋugbe be yeawɔ nuteƒe, ato nyateƒe nam. Mègaɖim ɖe Egipte-nyigba dzi gbeɖe o.

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Medi be nàɖim ɖe tɔ́nyewo gbɔ. Kɔm dzoe le Egipte, eye nàɖaɖim ɖe woƒe ɖiƒe.” Yosef ɖo eŋu be: “Mawɔ nu si nègblɔ la.”

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Egblɔ nɛ be: “Ka atam ɖe edzi nam!” Yosef ka atam nɛ. Israel bɔbɔ ta gbedoɖatɔe ɖe eƒe abati ƒe tade.

english_verse: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Esiawo megbe la, wogblɔ na Yosef be: “Kpɔ ɖa, tɔ́wò le dɔ lém.” Ale wòkplɔ via ŋutsu eveawo, Manase kple Efrayim, woyi egbɔ.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Esi wogblɔ na Yakob be: “Viwò Yosef va be yeakpɔ wò ɖa” la, Israel do ŋusẽ eɖokui fɔ, henɔ aba la dzi.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: Yakob gblɔ na Yosef be: “Mawu Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ɖe eɖokui fiam le Luz le Kanaan-nyigba dzi eye wòyram.

english_verse: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ nam be: ‘Mana nàdzi fũu, eye wò dzidzimeviwo asɔ gbɔ zã, eye mana woazu dukɔ geɖewo. Matsɔ anyigba sia ana wò dzidzimeviwo be wòanye wo tɔ tegbee.’

english_verse: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
translation_verse: Azɔ viŋutsu eve siwo wodzi na wò le Egipte hafi meva gbɔwò la zu vinyewo. Efrayim kple Manase le nam pɛ abe Ruben kple Simeon ene. Woazu tɔnye.

english_verse: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ke vi siwo nèdzi ɖe wo yome la nanye tɔwò. Woawo akpɔ woƒe domenyinuwo tso wo nɔvi Efrayim kple Manase ƒe domenyinuwo me.

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: Esi metrɔ tso Padan-Aram gbɔna ɖe Kanaan, eye wòsusɔ vie maɖo Efrat la, nɔwò Raxel ku le mɔ dzi. Meɖii ɖe mɔ to le Efrat.” Woyɔa Efrat fifia be Betlehem.

english_verse: Jacob was very old and almost blind. He did not recognize the two boys, and so he asked Joseph, “Who are these boys?” Joseph answered, “They are my sons. God has given them to me here in Egypt.” “Bring them to me,” Jacob said. “I want to give them my blessing.” Joseph brought the boys to him, and he hugged and kissed them.
translation_verse: Israel tsi, eye eƒe ŋku le tsitsim ale be megate ŋu le nu kpɔm nyuie o. Esi Yosef kplɔ via eveawo te ɖe eŋu la, Yakob kpla asi kɔ na wo hegbugbɔ nu na wo.

english_verse: Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.”
translation_verse: Tete Israel gblɔ na Yosef be: “Nyemebui be magakpɔ wò ŋkume gbeɖe o, ke azɔ Mawu wɔe meva kpɔ viwòwo gɔ̃ hã.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
translation_verse: Emegbe Yosef kɔ ɖeviawo ɖa le tɔ́a ƒe ata ta, eye wòdze klo, de ta agu ɖe tɔ́a ŋkume.

english_verse: After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right.
translation_verse: Azɔ Yosef lé via eveawo ɖe asi. Efrayim le eƒe ɖusime, si nye Israel ƒe miame, eye Manase le eƒe miame, si nye Israel ƒe ɖusime. Ekplɔ wo te ɖe tɔ́a ŋu.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ke Israel tso ga eƒe abɔwo, eye wòda eƒe nuɖusi ɖe Efrayim ƒe tame, togbɔ be eyae nye ɖevitɔ hã. Eda eƒe miasi ɖe Manase si nye tsitsitɔ la ƒe tame.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: Tete wòyra Yosef gblɔ be: “Mawu si ƒe ŋkume tɔ́nyewo Abraham kple Isak zɔ le, Mawu si kplɔm le nye agbe me ŋkekewo katã me va ɖo egbe,

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: mawudɔla si ɖem tso vɔ̃wo katã me la, neyra ɖevi siawo! Nye ŋkɔ, tɔ́nyewo Abraham kple Isak ŋkɔ, nenɔ ɖevi siawo ŋu ɖaa. Wonedzi ɖe edzi le anyigba la dzi.”

english_verse: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
translation_verse: Esi Yosef kpɔ be ye tɔ́ da eƒe nuɖusi ɖe Efrayim ƒe tame la, medze eŋu o, eya ta elé tɔ́a ƒe asi be yeaɖee ɖa le Efrayim ƒe tame ada ɖe Manase tɔ.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: Yosef gblɔ na tɔ́a be: “Tɔ́nye, menye nenemae o. Ŋgɔgbetɔe nye esi; tsɔ wò nuɖusi da ɖe eya ƒe tame.”

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: Ke tɔ́a gbe hegblɔ be: “Menya, vinye, menya! Eya hã ƒe dzidzimeviwo hã ava zu dukɔ gã aɖe. Gake nɔvia ɖevitɔ ade ŋgɔ wui, eye eƒe dzidzimeviwo ava zu dukɔ gãwo.”

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ale wòyra wo gbe ma gbe gblɔ be: “Miaƒe ŋkɔ Israelviwo atsɔ ayra amee, agblɔ be: ‘Mawu neɖi na wò abe Efrayim kple Manase ene!’ ” To esia me la, Yakob trɔ Efrayim wòzu tsitsia na Manase.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Azɔ Yakob gblɔ na Yosef be: “Kpɔ ɖa, nye kuɣi ɖo. Mawu anɔ kpli mi, eye wòagbugbɔ mi ayi mia tɔgbuiwo ƒe anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
translation_verse: Yakob yɔ viawo vɛ, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Miƒo ƒu, ne magblɔ nu si le dzɔdzɔ ge ɖe mia dzi le ɣeyiɣi siwo gbɔna me la na mi.

english_verse: Come, gather around, as I tell your future.
translation_verse: “Yakob viwo, mite va ƒo ƒu, eye miɖo to. Mise nye, mia tɔ́, Israel, ƒe nya.”

english_verse: Reuben, you are my oldest, born at the peak of my powers; you were an honored leader.
translation_verse: “Ruben, nye ŋgɔgbevi, wòe nye nye ŋusẽ kple nye ɖekakpuimevi gbãtɔ. Èdze bubu, eye èsesẽ wu vinyewo katã.
