english_verse: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
translation_verse: Ke èle abe tsi fiefie si gbagba la ene; màganye vi vevitɔ nam akpɔ o. Elabe ède tɔ́wò ƒe aba dzi, eye nèdo gu aba la. Ẽ, nye ŋutɔ nye aba dzi nède gbe ma gbe!”

english_verse: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
translation_verse: “Simeon kple Levi: nɔviŋutsuwo, wotsɔ woƒe lãnuwo do hlɔ̃e.

english_verse: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
translation_verse: Nye luʋɔ, megade adaŋu kpli wo o. Nye gbɔgbɔ, megade ha kpli wo hã o, elabe wowua ame le dziku me, eye le woƒe movidzɔdzɔ me la, wotso drika na nyitsuwo.

english_verse: Now I place a curse on you because of your fierce anger. Your descendants will be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Woƒe dziku neɖi wo ŋu, elabe ŋɔdzi le eŋu. Woƒe dɔmedzoe neɖi wo ŋu, elabe evɔ̃ɖi. Mama wo me ɖe Yakob ƒe anyigba dzi, eye maka wo ahlẽ ɖe Israel-nyigba dzi.”

english_verse: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
translation_verse: “Yuda, nɔviwò ŋutsuwo akafu wò. Àlé vehlo na wò futɔwo; tɔ́viwòwo abɔbɔ ta na wò.

english_verse: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
translation_verse: Dzatavie nye Yuda. Le nuléle ta, vinye, ànɔ to dzi. Emlɔ anyi tsyɔ akɔ abe dzatatsu ene, eye abe dzatanɔ ene; ame ka ate ŋu aʋuʋui?

english_verse: You will have power and rule until nations obey you and come bringing gifts.
translation_verse: Atamkayi mavɔ le Yuda si o, eye sewɔtikplɔ maɖe ɖa le ekɔme akpɔ o, va se ɖe esime woava xe adzɔ nɛ, eye dukɔwo aɖo toe.

english_verse: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
translation_verse: Ade ka eƒe tedzivi ɖe wainka ŋu, eye wòade ka eƒe tedzinɔ ƒe vi ɖe wainka nyui ƒe alɔdzewo ŋu. Anya eƒe avɔ le wain me, eye wòanya eƒe awu le waintsetse me tsi me.

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: Wain ana eƒe ŋku nabiã hẽe; notsi ana eƒe aɖu nafu tititi.”

english_verse: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
translation_verse: “Zebulon anɔ ƒutanyigba dzi. Ʋudzeƒewo anɔ eƒe ƒu nu, eye eƒe anyigba akeke ade keke Sidon ke.”

english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: “Isaxar nye tedzi sesẽ. Etsyɔ akɔ anyi ɖe lãkpɔwo dome.

english_verse: You found them so pleasant that you worked too hard and became a slave.
translation_verse: Ekpɔ be dzudzɔƒe la dze eme na ye, eye anyigba la nyo. Ale wòbi abɔta be yeatsɔ agba, eye wozi edzi wòzu kluvi agbatsɔla.”

english_verse: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
translation_verse: “Dan akplɔ eƒe dukɔ abe Israel-to bubuwo ke ene.

english_verse: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
translation_verse: Dan anye da tsomɔ, dzakpata le afɔmɔ dzi. Eɖua sɔ ƒe afɔkpodzi, eye sɔdola dzea anyi megbemegbee.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: O Aƒetɔ, wò xɔname la ko lalam mele!”

english_verse: Gad, you will be attacked, then attack your attackers.
translation_verse: “Adzohawo ava dze Gad dzi; ke ayɔ̀ wo ɖe nu, aha wo.”

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: “Aser ƒe nuɖuɖu ada mi, eye fia ƒe nuɖuɖu viviwo atso egbɔ.”

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: “Naftali nye zinɔ le eɖokui si. Edzia vi nyakpɔwo.”

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: “Yosef nye atilɔ tseku le tsidzɔƒe. Eɖe alɔ flɔ gli ta.

english_verse: Enemies attacked with arrows, refusing to show mercy.
translation_verse: Eƒe futɔ aŋutrɔdalawo dze edzi, tee, eye woɖe fu nɛ vevie.

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: Ke eƒe dati meʋã o. Yakob ƒe Mawu ŋusẽtɔ la, wɔ eƒe asi wòle tsɔtsɔm to Alẽkplɔla, Israel ƒe Agakpe la ŋkɔ me.

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: To tɔ́wò ƒe Mawu, ame si akpe ɖe ŋuwò, to Mawu Ŋusẽkatãtɔ, ame si ayra wò kple yayra tso dziƒo, yayra tso agume ke, yayra tso no nu kple vidzidɔ me, la dzi.

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: Tɔ́wò ƒe yayra gbɔ to mavɔwo tɔ kple togbɛ mavɔwo ƒe nu gbogboawo ŋu. Na nenɔ Yosef ƒe ta dzi, eye wòanɔ ame si wosa ɖe aga la ƒe ŋgonu.”

english_verse: Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf, destroying your enemies morning and evening.
translation_verse: “Benyamin nye amegãxi nuvuvula. Le ŋdi la, eɖua nu si wòlé la; fiẽ la, emaa aboyonuwo.”

english_verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings. Jacob's Death
translation_verse: Israel-to wui eveawoe nye esiawo, eye nya mamlɛtɔ siwo wo tɔ́a gblɔ na wo dome ɖe sia ɖe tsɔ yrae abe ale si dze nɛ ene lae nye esiawo. Yakob ƒe ku kple eɖiɖi

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: Ɖe woƒle agblea kple kpeto si le eme la le Xiti viwo si. Miɖi nye hã ɖe afi ma.”

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Esi Yakob gblɔ nya siawo na viawo vɔ la, eƒo ƒu ata ɖe aba dzi, mia nu, eye wòyi tɔgbuiawo gbɔ.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Tete Yosef dze tɔ́a dzi kple avi, eye wògbugbɔ nu nɛ.

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Le konyifaɣi la megbe la, Yosef gblɔ na Egipte Fiagã la ŋutimewo be: “Meɖe kuku, mive nunye ne miayi ɖagblɔ na fia be

english_verse: Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
translation_verse: hafi tɔ́nye naku la, ena meka atam nɛ be ne yeku la, maɖi ye ɖe Kanaan-nyigba dzi, ɖe yɔdo si ye ŋutɔ yeɖe da ɖi la me. Eya ta meɖe kuku, miɖe mɔ nam ne mayi aɖaɖii ɖe afi ma agatrɔ agbɔ.”

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Egipte Fiagã ɖo eŋu be: “Yi ɖaɖi tɔ́wò abe ale si wòna nèka atam nɛ la ene.”

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Esi wova ɖo lugbɔƒe le Atad le Yordan ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome la, wofa Yakob vevie kple ɣli. Wofa na tɔ́a ŋkeke adrẽ.

english_verse: The Canaanites saw this and said, “The Egyptians are in great sorrow.” Then they named the place “Egypt in Sorrow.”
translation_verse: Kanaantɔ siwo nye anyigba la dzi tɔwo la kpɔ kunua teƒe le Atad, eye wogblɔ be: “Egiptetɔwo va le kunu tɔxɛ aɖe wɔm.” Eya ta woyɔa teƒe ma be Abel-Mizraim.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Ale Yakob viŋutsuawo wɔ nu si wògblɔ be wonewɔ na ye la nɛ.

english_verse: They took him to Mamre in Canaan and buried him in Machpelah Cave, the burial place Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite.
translation_verse: Esi woɖo Kanaan la, woɖii ɖe kpeto si le Maxpela, le Mamre ƒe ɣedzeƒe lɔƒo la me. Kpeto sia le agble si Abraham ƒle le Efron, Xititɔ la si be wòanye yeƒe ameɖiƒe la me.

english_verse: After the funeral, Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else returned to Egypt. Joseph's Promise to His Brothers
translation_verse: Esi Yosef ɖi tɔ́a vɔ la, eya kple nɔviawo kpakple ame siwo katã kpe ɖe eŋu yi amea ɖiƒe la trɔ gbɔ va Egipte. Yosef de dzi ƒo na nɔviawo

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Esi Yosef nɔviwo kpɔ be yewo tɔ́ ku la, wogblɔ be: “Ɖewohĩ Yosef alé fu mí, eye wòaɖo nu vlo siwo katã míewɔ ɖe eŋu la teƒe na mí.”

english_verse: So they sent this message to Joseph: Before our father died,
translation_verse: Ale wodɔ ame ɖo ɖe Yosef gbɔ be: “Tɔ́wò gblɔ nya sia na mi hafi ku:

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: ‘Migblɔ na Yosef be: Taflatsɛ, tsɔ nɔviwòwo ƒe vodada kple nuvɔ̃ ke wo, elabe wowɔ vɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò.’ Azɔ míeɖe kuku na wò, tsɔ tɔ́wò ƒe Mawu la ƒe dɔlawo ƒe vodada ke wo.” Yosef fa avi esi woƒo nu kplii.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Azɔ nɔviawo ŋutɔ yi egbɔ. Wodze klo, de ta agu nɛ, eye wogblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, míawoe nye esi. Wò kluviwo míenye.”

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Ke Yosef gblɔ na wo be: “Migavɔ̃ o. Mawu teƒe melea?

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Miawo mieɖoe be yewoawɔ vɔ̃m, ke Mawu trɔe wòzu nyui, be wòaxɔ ame geɖe ɖe agbe abe ale si wòdzɔ miele kpɔkpɔm egbe ene.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Eya ta migavɔ̃ o. Malé be na mi kple mia viwo siaa.” Ale Yosef fa akɔ na wo, eye wòde dzi ƒo na wo. Yosef ƒe ku

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Yosef ganɔ Egipte kple tɔ́a ƒemetɔwo. Exɔ ƒe alafa ɖeka kple ewo.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: Enɔ agbe tsò Efrayim ƒe tɔgbuitɔgbuiyɔviwo ɖo, eye wònɔ anyi xɔ Maxir, Manase vi, hã viwo ɖe ata ta.

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka Yosef gblɔ na nɔviawo be: “Nye kuɣi ɖo; Mawu aɖo ŋku mia dzi, eye wòakplɔ mi tso anyigba sia dzi ayi anyigba si ŋugbe wòdo na Abraham, Isak kple Yakob la dzi.”

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Tete Yosef na Israelviwo ka atam nɛ be: “Ne Mawu va mia kplɔ ge la, mitsɔ nye ƒuwo tso afii yii.”

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Yosef kple nɔvia ŋutsuawo kpakple dzidzime ma katã va ku.

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Ke Israelviwo va dzi fũu. Wova sɔ gbɔ hekpɔ ŋusẽ ale gbegbe, eye wokaka ɖe anyigba la ƒe afi sia afi.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Eva eme be fia yeye aɖe si menya naneke le Yosef ŋu o la va zi dzi le Egipte.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Eya gblɔ na eƒe dukɔ la be: “Mikpɔ ɖa, Israelviwo va sɔ gbɔ wu mí. Wole ŋusẽ hã kpɔm wu mí.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Mina míadze aye ɖe wo ŋu, be womagadzi fũu ɖe edzi o. Ne menye nenema o, ne aʋa dzɔ la, woava de míaƒe futɔwo dzi ɖe mía ŋu, akpɔ mɔnu así dzo le míaƒe anyigba la dzi.”

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Ale Egiptetɔwo tia dɔdzikpɔlawo ɖo Israelviwo nu be woawɔ funyafunya wo, aɖo dɔ sesẽ na wo. Wona Israelviwo tsò nudzraɖodu na Egipte Fiagã la. Du siawoe nye Pitom kple Ramses.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Gake zi geɖe ale si Egiptetɔwo le Israelviwo tem ɖe anyi la, nenema ke wole dzidzim ɖe edzi, le ta kekem wu. Ale Egiptetɔwo de asi vɔvɔ̃ me na Israelviawo.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Wote wo ɖe anyi kple dɔ sesẽ wɔwɔ ale gbegbe be agbenɔnɔ ve helihelĩ le woƒe ve me. Egiptetɔwo na Israelviwo nya anyi tsɔ me anyikpee. Wo zi wo dzi wowɔ agbledɔ vovovowo hã. Wona wowɔ dɔ siawo nublanuimakpɔmakpɔtɔe.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Tete Egipte Fiagã la gblɔ na Hebri-vixela siwo ƒe ŋkɔwoe nye Sifra kple Pua la be:

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: Ne miele vi xem na Hebri-nyɔnu aɖe, eye miekpɔ be ŋutsu dzim wòle la, miwu ɖevia; ke nenye nyɔnu dzim wòle la, mina ɖevia natsi agbe.”

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Gake vixelaawo vɔ̃a Mawu, eya ta womewɔa fia la ƒe sea dzi o; ke boŋ wonana be ŋutsuviawo tsia agbe.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Ale Egipte Fiagã yɔ vixelaawo, eye wòbia wo be: “Nu ka ta miena ŋutsuviawo le agbe tsim?”

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Vixelaawo ɖo eŋu na Egipte Fiagã be: “Hebri-nyɔnuwo mele abe Egipte-nyɔnuwo ene o. Ŋusẽ le wo ŋu ŋutɔ, ale be kasia vixela naɖo Hebri-nyɔnu si le ku lém la gbɔ la, eya ŋutɔ dzi via xoxo.”

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Tete Egipte Fiagã de se na eƒe dukɔ blibo la be: “Ne Hebri-nyɔnu dzi ŋutsuvi la, mitsɔ ɖevia ƒu gbe ɖe Nil-tɔsisi me; ke ne edzi nyɔnuvi la, mina ɖevia natsi agbe.”

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Eva eme be ŋutsu aɖe tso Levi-to la me ɖaɖe Levi-nyɔnu aɖe.

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Nyɔnua fɔ fu eye wòdzi ŋutsuvi. Ekpɔ be ɖevia dze ɖeka ŋutɔ. Ale wòɣlae ɣleti etɔ̃ sɔŋ.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Esi megate ŋu le ɖevia ɣlam o la, edi kusi si wolɔ̃ kple aɖa eye wotree kple aŋɔ la, tsɔ ɖevi la de eme, eye wòtsɔe yi ɖada ɖe aƒlawo dome le tɔsisia to.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Ɖevia nɔvinyɔnu bè ɖe adzɔge be yeakpɔ ɖa be nu kae adzɔ ɖe edzi mahã.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Egipte Fiagã vinyɔnu va tsi le ge le tɔsisia me. Enɔ tsia lem eye eƒe subɔlawo nɔ tsa ɖim le tɔa to. Kasia eƒe ŋku kle kusia le aƒlaawo me ɖaa, eye wòna eƒe dɔlanyɔnu yi ɖatsɔe vɛ.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Esi wòʋui la, ekpɔ vidzĩ le eme. Ŋutsuvi ye; enɔ avi fam. Eƒe nu wɔ nublanui nɛ eye wògblɔ be: “Hebritɔwo ƒe viwo dometɔ ɖekae nye esia.”

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Tete nɔvia nyɔnu la te va. Ebia fiavinyɔnua be: “Mayi ɖadi Hebri-nyɔnu vi nɔ aɖe vɛ, ne wòana no ɖevia na wòa?”

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Egipte Fiagã vinyɔnua ɖo eŋu be: “Yi.” Nyɔnuvia yi ɖayɔ vidzĩ la dada vɛ.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Fiavinyɔnua gblɔ nɛ be: “Xɔ ɖevi sia nàna noe nam. Maxe fe na wò.” Nyɔnua kɔ vidzĩa dzoe, eye

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: wòɖakpɔ edzi. Esi ɖevia tsi la, ekplɔe vɛ na Egipte Fiagã vinyɔnu la. Exɔe wɔ viae, eye wòtsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Mose hegblɔ be: “Elabe tɔ mee meɖee tsoe. Mose sí yi Midian-nyigba dzi

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Esi Mose va tsi la, eɖi tsa yi nɔvia Hebritɔwo gbɔ gbe ɖeka, eye wòkpɔ wo wole woƒe dzizizidɔawo wɔm. Tete wòkpɔ Egiptetɔ aɖe wòle Hebritɔ aɖe ƒom.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Mose tsa ŋku, tsa ŋku, eye esi mekpɔ ame aɖeke o la, eƒo Egiptetɔ la wu, eye wòlɔ ke ƒo ɖe edzi.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Evea gbe la, Mose gayi nɔviawo gbɔ. Kasia Hebritɔ evee nye esiwo le avu wɔm. Ebia ame si tɔ medzɔ o la be: “Nu ka ŋuti nèle nɔviwò ƒom?”

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu na Mose be: “Ame kae ɖo wò amegã kple ʋɔnudrɔ̃la ɖe mía nu? Ɖe nèbe yeawu nye hã abe ale si nèwu Egiptetɔ ma enea?” Mose gblɔ be: “Nya la ɖi; amewo see!” Ale vɔvɔ̃ ɖoe.

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Esi Egipte Fiagã va se nyaa la, edi Mose be yeawu. Tete Mose sí le enu yi Midian-nyigba dzi. Eɖanɔ vudo aɖe to.

english_verse: the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Midian nunɔla vinyɔnu adrẽ wova tsi du ge akɔ ɖe lãwo ƒe tsinonuwo me na wo tɔ́ ƒe lãwo.

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Lãkplɔla aɖewo va nyà wo ɖa. Mose tso ʋli wo ta eye wòku tsi na wo tɔ́ ƒe lãawo wono.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Esi wotrɔ yi aƒeme la, wo tɔ́ si ŋkɔe nye Reguel la, bia wo be: “Ale ke wɔ miegbɔ kaba egbe ya ale?”

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Egipte-ŋutsu aɖee ʋli mía ta le lãkplɔlawo gbɔ, eye wòdu tsi na míaƒe alẽwo wono gɔ̃ hã.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Ebia via nyɔnuawo be: “Ŋutsua ɖe? Ale ke wɔ miegblẽe ɖe afi ma? Miyi ɖayɔe ne wòava ɖu nu.”

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Mose lɔ̃ be yeatsi ŋutsua gbɔ koŋ, eye ŋutsua tsɔ via nyɔnu Zipora nɛ wòɖe.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Zipora dzi viŋutsuvi nɛ. Mose na ŋkɔe be Gersom hegblɔ be: “Amedzro menye le dzronyigba dzi”

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Le ƒè geɖee megbe la, Egipte-fia va ku. Israelviwo nɔ ŋèŋem le woƒe kluvikɔkuti sesẽ la te. Wodo ɣli, eye Mawu se woƒe ɣlidodo la.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Mawu se woƒe ŋèŋe eye wòɖo ŋku nu, si wòbla kple Abraham, Isak kple Yakob la dzi.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Mawu trɔ kɔ kpɔ Israelviwo eye wònya nu si nɔ dzɔdzɔm ɖe wo dzi.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Mose nɔ toa Yetro si nye Midiantɔwo ƒe nunɔla la ƒe lãwo dzi kpɔm. Gbe ɖeka esi wòkplɔ lãawo yi gbedzi la, eva do ɖe Xoreb, Mawu ƒe to la gbɔ.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla ɖe eɖokui fiae le dzobibi me le ŋugbe aɖe me. Esi wòɖe ŋku ɖe eŋu la, ekpɔ be dzoa le bibim gake gbea mele fiafiãm o.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ be: “Mayi aɖakpɔ nu dziŋɔ sia ɖa: nu si ta gbea mele fiafiãm o!”

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Esi Aƒetɔ kpɔ be edze be yeakpɔ nua ɖa la, eyɔe tso ŋugbea me be: “Mose, Mose!” Mose tɔ be: “Nyee nye esi.”

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Mègate va afii o. Ɖe wò atokota le afɔ, elabe anyigba si dzi nètsi tsitre ɖo la, anyigba kɔkɔe ye.”

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Egagblɔ be: “Nyee nye tɔgbuiwòwo ƒe Mawu, Abraham ƒe Mawu, Isak ƒe Mawu kple Yakob ƒe Mawu.” Tete Mose tsyɔ nu ŋkume elabe enɔ vɔvɔ̃m be yeakpɔ Mawu.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Mekpɔ ale si wole funyafunya wɔm nye dukɔ le Egipte. Mese ɣli si dom wole be woaɖe yewo tso dɔdzikpɔla siwo te wo ɖe anyi la si me.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Ẽ, menya woƒe fukpekpewo eya ta meɖi va be maɖe wo tso Egiptetɔwo si me, eye makplɔ wo ayi anyigba nyui aɖe dzi. Anyigba sia keke, eye notsi kple anyitsi bɔ ɖe edzi. Afi ma Kanaanitɔwo, Xititɔwo, Amoritɔwo Perizitɔwo, Xivitɔwo kple Yebusitɔwo le.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Israelviwo ƒe ɣli ɖi mese eye mekpɔ ale si Egiptetɔwo le wo tem ɖe anyii.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Eya ta va, madɔ wò ɖe Egipte Fiagã gbɔ be nàɖe nye dukɔ Israelviwo tso esi me, eye nàkplɔ wo dzoe le Egipte.”

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Ke Mose gblɔ na Mawu be: “Ame ka menye be maɖado ɖe Egipte Fiagã ŋkume eye be makplɔ Israelviwo adzoe le Egipte?”

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Mawu ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Manɔ kpli wò; eye dzesi si nàkpɔ anya be nyee dɔ ye ɖa lae nye be: ne èkplɔ dukɔ la do goe tso Egipte la, miasubɔm le to sia dzi.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Mose bia Mawu be: “Ne meyi Israelviwo gbɔ, eye megblɔ na wo be: ‘Mia tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu lae dɔm ɖe mia gbɔ,’ eye wobiam be: ‘Eŋkɔ ɖe?’ hã la, ale ke maɖo eŋu na wo?”

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Mawu gagblɔ na Mose be: “Gblɔ na Israelviwo be: “Aƒetɔ, mia tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu: Abraham ƒe Mawu, Isak ƒe Mawu kple Yakob ƒe Mawue dɔm ɖe mia gbɔ. Esiae nye nye ŋkɔ tegbee. Ŋkɔ sia nye nye ŋkɔ tso dzidzime yi dzidzime.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Yi nàƒo Israelviwo ƒe ame tsitsiwo nu ƒu, eye nàgblɔ be nye Aƒetɔ, mia tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu, Abraham ƒe Mawu, Isak ƒe Mawu kple Yakob ƒe Mawu, ɖe eɖokui fiam, gblɔ be, ‘Nye ŋku le mia ŋu, eye menya nu si wole mia wɔm le Egipte.

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Eya ta medo ŋugbe be maɖe mi tso Egiptetɔwo ƒe fuwɔame la me, eye makplɔ mi ayi Kanaanitɔwo, Xititɔwo, Amoritɔwo, Xivitɔwo kple Yebusitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi; anyigba si dzi notsi kple anyitsi bɔ ɖo la.’

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: Dukɔ la aɖo to wò. Ekema wò kple Israelviwo ƒe ame tsitsiwo miayi Egipte-fia la gbɔ, eye miagblɔ nɛ be: ‘Aƒetɔ, Hebritɔwo ƒe Mawu la ɖe eɖokui fia mí; eya ta ɖe mɔ na mí míazɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃ ƒe mɔ ayi gbedzi, aɖasa vɔ na Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la.’

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Menyae be Egipte-fia la maɖe mɔ na mi miayi o, negbe ɖeko woazi edzi hafi.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Ale matsɔ nye ŋusẽ kple nukunu siwo katã mawɔ le wo dome la, atu nu kple Egipte, eye eya megbe la, ana miadzo.

english_verse: After I punish the Egyptians, they will be so afraid of you that they will give you anything you want. You are my people, and I will let you take many things with you when you leave the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: Mana gɔ̃ hã be Egiptetɔwo ƒe dɔme atrɔ ɖe dukɔ sia ŋu ale be ne miele dzodzom la, miayi asi ƒuƒlu o.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Israel-nyɔnu ɖe sia ɖe nabia klosalotsyɔ̃ɖonu, sikanuwo kple nudodowo le eƒe aƒelika kple amedzro si le eƒeme la si. Miado nu siawo na mia viŋutsuwo kple mia vinyɔnuwo adzoe. To esia me, miaha Egiptetɔwo.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Tete Mose ɖo eŋu be: “Ke ne womexɔ dzinye se o, alo womese nye gbe hã o, ke wogblɔ be: ‘Aƒetɔ meɖe eɖokui fia wò fɔ̃e o ɖe.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ biae be: “Nu kae nye ema le asiwò?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Atizɔti ye.”

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Dae ɖe anyigba.” Edae ɖe anyigba eye atia trɔ zu da. Mose sí le enu.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Do asi ɖa nàlé eƒe asikɛ.” Mose do asi ɖa lée. Tete daa gazu atizɔti ɖe esi.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Wɔ nu sia ekema Israelviwo axɔe se be nye Aƒetɔ, wo tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu: Abraham ƒe Mawu, Isak ƒe Mawu kple Yakob ƒe Mawu la, meɖe ɖokuinye fia wò vavã.”

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gagblɔ nɛ be: “Ƒo asi ɖe wò awu ƒe akɔta.” Eƒoe ɖee. Esi wohee ɖe go la, dɔ ƒo ɖe asia ŋu wòfu kpii abe tsikpe ene.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Tete Mawu be: “Gaƒo asi ɖe awua me.” Egaƒoe ɖee, eye esi wògaɖee la, asia ŋu gakɔ keŋkeŋ abe ale si wònɔ tsã ene.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Ne womexɔ dzesi eveawo dzi se o, eye womexɔ wò hã dzi se o la, ekema ku tsi le Nil-tɔsisia me nàkɔ ɖe anyigba ƒuƒui; tsia atrɔ zu ʋu ɖe anyigba.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Gake Mose gagblɔ na Aƒetɔ be: “Taflatsɛ, nye Aƒetɔ, nu menya ƒona nam o; menye egbe o, menye etsɔ o, eye menye tso esime nèdze nuƒoƒo gɔme nam hã o. Nye aɖe metrɔna ɖe nya ŋu o.”

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ biae be: “Ame kae wɔ nu na ame? Ame kae nana be ame ƒe to kuna alo ame ƒe aɖe tuna? Ame kae nana be ame kpɔa nu alo nyea ŋkuagbãtɔ? Ɖe menye nye, Aƒetɔ ye oa?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Eya ta heyi ko; makpe ɖe ŋuwò nàƒo nu eye mafia nya si nàgblɔ la wò.”

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Tete Mose gabe: “Gake, ao, nye Aƒetɔ, meɖe kuku, di ame bubu nàdɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ do dziku ɖe eŋu azɔ, eye wògblɔ be: “Nɔviwò Aron Levitɔ la meli oa? Menya be eƒoa nu nyuie. Egbɔna gɔ̃ be yeava kpe wò. Ne eva ke ɖe ŋuwò la, dzi adzɔe ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Nàlé atizɔti sia ɖe asi elabe eyae nèle tsɔtsɔ ge awɔ dzesiawoe.” Mose trɔ yi Egipte

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Tete Mose trɔ gbɔ va toa Yetro gbɔ va gblɔ nɛ be: “Taflatsɛ, ɖe mɔ nam ne matrɔ yi nɔvinyewo gbɔ le Egipte aɖakpɔ ɖa be wogale agbe mahã.” Yetro ɖo eŋu be: “Heyi le ŋutifafa me.”

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose le Midian be: “Gbugbɔ yi Egipte, elabe ame siwo katã nɔ didim be yewoawu wò la ku.”

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Mose kɔ srɔ̃a kple via ŋutsuwo ɖo tedzi dzi, eye wòtrɔ yi Egipte. Etsɔ Mawu ƒe atizɔti la ɖe asi.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Ne èɖo Egipte la, ɖo ŋku edzi nàwɔ nukunu siwo katã metsɔ de asi na wò la le Egipte Fiagã la ŋkume. Mana eƒe dzime nasẽ ale be maɖe asi le dukɔ la ŋu woadzo o.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Ekema nàgblɔ na Egipte Fiagã la be: ‘Ale Aƒetɔ gblɔ nye esi: Israel la vinye ŋutsu ye; nye ŋgɔgbevi wònye.

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: Megblɔ na wò be: ‘Ɖe asi le vinye ŋu ne woaɖasubɔm.’ Gake ègbe mèɖe mɔnɛ o; eya ta mawu wò ŋgɔgbeviŋutsu.’ ”

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Esi wole mɔa dzi va ɖo dzeƒe aɖe la, Aƒetɔ va, eye wòdi be yeawu Mose.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Tete Zipora tsɔ kpe ɖaɖɛ lã via ŋutsu ƒe aʋanuyi. Etsɔ aʋanuyi la tɔ eƒe afɔ, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Ʋusrɔ̃ nènye nam baa!”

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ megawɔ nu vevi Mose o. Le aʋatsotso la ta, Zipora da ŋkɔ ɖe srɔ̃a dzi be, “Ʋuŋugbetɔsrɔ̃.”

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Aron be: “Yi gbedzi nàɖakpe Mose.” Aron yi eye wòɖakpe Mose le Mawu ƒe to la gbɔ. Egbugbɔ nu nɛ,

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: eye Mose gblɔ dɔ si gbe Aƒetɔ dɔe ɖo, nya siwo katã wòto nɛ kple dzesi siwo keŋ wòna ŋusẽe be wòawɔ la na Aron.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Tete Mose kple Aron woyi Egipte, eye woyɔ Israelviwo ƒe ame tsitsiwo katã ƒo ƒu.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Aron gblɔ nya siwo katã Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose la na wo, eye Mose wɔ dzesiawo hã wokpɔ.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Ameawo xɔ Mose kple Aron dzi se, eye esi wose be Aƒetɔ va Israelviwo gbɔ, eye wòkpɔ ale si Egiptetɔwo le fu wɔm wo la, wode ta agu hesubɔe.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Emegbe Mose kple Aron woyi Egipte Fiagã la gbɔ ɖagblɔ nɛ be: “Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu be: “Ɖe asi le nye dukɔ ŋu ne woaɖaɖu ŋkekenyui nam le gbedadaƒo.”

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Ke Egipte Fiagã la ɖo eŋu be: “Ame kae nye Aƒetɔ ta maɖo toe, aɖe asi le Israelviwo ŋu woayi? Nyemenya Aƒetɔ la o, eye nyemaɖe asi le Israelviwo ŋu woayi o.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Mose kple Aron gagblɔ nɛ be: “Hebritɔwo ƒe Mawu la ɖe eɖokui fia mí. Ɖe mɔ na mí ne míazɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃ ƒe mɔ ayi gbedadaƒo aɖasa vɔ na Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la, ne menye nenema o la, adze mía dzi kple dɔ vɔ̃ loo, alo awu mí kple yi.”

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Egipte Fiagã la gblɔ be: “Azɔ esi ameawo sɔ gbɔ ɖe edzi le anyigbaa dzi ale hafi miebe woadzudzɔ woƒe dɔ sesẽa wɔwɔa?”

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe ke la, fia la de se na kluviwo dzikpɔlawo kple wo nunɔlawo be:

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: “Tso azɔ heyi, migana gbe Israelviwo woade anyi me amè anyikpeawoe o. Woawo ŋutɔ naɖadi gbe amè anyikpe lae.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Ke kpe ale sinu womèna tsã la ke koe wòle be woamè. Migaɖe le edzi kura o. Kuvia wɔm wole ta wole ɣli dzi be: ‘Na míayi aɖasa vɔ na mía Mawu.’

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Mizi wo dzi eye mite wo ɖe anyi ne woagawɔ dɔ sesĩe, ekema womaɖo to alakpanya mawo o.”

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Tete kluviwo dzikpɔlaawo kple woƒe dɔnunɔlawo do yi ɖagblɔ na Israelviwo be: “Egipte Fiagã la be yemegale gbe na ge mi miatsɔ amè anyikpe la azɔ o.

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: Miawo ŋutɔ miyi ɖadi gbe le afi sia afi si miakpɔe le la amèe. Ke kpe ale sinu miemèna tsã la ke koe miagamè. Womaɖe ɖeke le dzi o.”

english_verse: The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw.
translation_verse: Ale Israel-dukɔ blibo la kaka ɖe Egipte-nyigba la katã dzi hele gbe dim.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Ke kluviwo dzikpɔlaawo yɔa ʋu ɖe wo te gblɔna be: “Dɔa netsɔ! Gbe sia gbe ƒe dɔ si miewɔna tsã, esi wonaa gbe mi la kee wòle be miawɔ.”

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Ne anyikpeawo mede o la, Egipte Fiagã ƒe dɔdzikpɔlawo ƒoa Israelvi siwo nye dɔnunɔlawo eye wobiaa wo be: “Nu ka ta anyikpeawo mede xexlẽme xoxoa nu egbe o?”

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Azɔ Israelvi dɔnunɔlawo yi ɖafa konyi na Egipte Fiagã gblɔ be: “Nu ka ta nèle mí, wò dɔlawo wɔm ale?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Womegale gbe na mí o, gake ɣe sia ɣi ko wole gbɔgblɔm nam mí be ‘Mimè anyikpe! Mimè anyikpe’ eye woƒoa mí gɔ̃, evɔ wò amewo gbɔ boŋue vodada la tso.”

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Ke fia la ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Kuviatɔwo! Alɔgblɔdɔwɔlawo mienye, eya ta miele biabiam be: ‘Ɖe mɔ na mí ne míayi aɖasa vɔ na Aƒetɔ.’

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Midzo yi kaba miaɖawɔ dɔ! Womana gbe aɖeke mi o. Ke ele be miamè anyikpe xexlẽme si woɖo na mi la kokoko.”

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Esesẽ ŋutɔ na Israelvi dɔdzikpɔlawo be woaɖagblɔ na wo tɔwo be womekpɔ mɔ aɖe le anyikpe xexlẽme si woɖo na wo be woamè gbe sia gbe la dzi o.

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Esime wodzo le Egipte Fiagã la gbɔ la, wodo go Mose kple Aron siwo nɔ wo lalam.

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na wo be: “Aƒetɔ nelé ŋku ɖe mia ŋu ne wòadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu kpli mi, elabe miena Egipte Fiagã la kple eŋumewo lé fu mí vevie. Miede yi asi na wo be woawu mí.”

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Tete Mose gatrɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu eye wò gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, nu ka ta nèhe vɔ̃ va dukɔ sia dzi? Nu ka koŋ ta nèdɔm ɖa ya?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Elabe tso esime meva Egipte Fiagã la gbɔ va ƒo nu le wò ŋkɔ me la, ɖeko wògale ŋuta sẽm le wò dukɔ la ŋu wu. Ke wò la, mèɖe wò dukɔ la kura o.”

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Gake Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Azɔ àkpɔ nu si mele Egipte Fiagã la wɔ ge. Elabe alɔ sesẽe wòatsɔ nyà wo do goe, ẽ atsɔ alɔ sesẽ anyà wo ɖa le eƒe anyigba dzii.” Mawu yɔ Mose

english_verse: My name is the Lord.
translation_verse: Mawu gblɔ na Mose be: “Nyee nye Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: Nyee ɖe ɖokuinye fia Abraham, Isak kple Yakob abe Mawu Ŋusẽkatãtɔ ene. Gake nyemena wonya be ŋkɔnyee nye Aƒetɔ o.

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: Mebla nu kpli wo hã be matsɔ Kanaan-nyigba, anyigba si dzi wonɔ abe amedzrowo ene la ana wo wòazu wo tɔ.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Gawu la, mese konyi si fam Israelviwo, ame siwo Egiptetɔwo te ɖe anyi la, eye meɖo ŋku nu, si mebla kpli wo la dzi.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: Eya ta gblɔ na Israel-dukɔ be: ‘Nyee nye Aƒetɔ. Maɖe mi le Egiptetɔwo ƒe kɔkuti te. Maɖe mi le woƒe kluvinyenye me, eye maɖe mi tso wo si me ale be miaganye kluviwo na wo o. Mamlo nye abɔ me atsɔ nye ŋusẽ triakɔ la atu nu kpli wo.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Mawɔ mi mianye nye ŋutɔ nye dukɔ, eye manye miaƒe Mawu. Mianyae be nyee nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu, si ɖe mi le Egiptetɔwo ƒe agba kpekpe la te.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: Makplɔ mi ayi anyigba si meka atam be matsɔ na Abraham, Isak kple Yakob la dzi, eye matsɔe ana mi wòanye miawo ŋutɔ tɔ. Nyee nye Aƒetɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: “Yi ɖagblɔ na Egipte Fiagã la, be neɖe asi le Israelviwo ŋu ne woadzo le eƒe anyigba dzi.”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Ke Mose gblɔ na Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, esi Israelviwo gɔ̃ hã meɖo tom o ɖe, ale ke wɔ Egipte Fiagã ya boŋ laɖo to nye, ame si nu menyaƒona na kura o la?”

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ ƒo nu na Mose kple Aron, eye wòdɔ wo ɖe Israel-dukɔ la kple Egipte Fiagã la gbɔ be woakplɔ Israelviwo dzoe le Egipte-nyigba dzi. Mose kple Aron ƒe ƒomegbalẽ

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Wo tɔgbuiwo ƒe aƒekɔtatɔwoe nye esiawo: Ruben, Israel ƒe ŋgɔgbeviŋutsu viŋutsuwoe nye: Henox, Palu, Xezron kple Karmi. Woawo mee Ruben-to la dzɔ tso.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Simeon viŋutsuwoe nye: Yemuel, Yamin, Ohad, Yaxin, Zoxar kple Saul, ame si nye Kanaan-nyɔnu ƒe vi. Woawo mee Simeon-to la dzɔ tso.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Gerson viŋutsuwoe nye Libni kple Simei. Dzidzimeviwo nɔ ɖe sia ɖe si.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Merari viŋtsuwoe nye Maxeli kple Masi. Ame siawo mee Levi ƒome la dzɔ tso.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Yizhar viŋtsuwoe nye: Korax, Nefeg kple Sixri.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Uziel viŋutsuwoe nye: Misael, Elzafan kple Sitri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Aron ɖe Eliseba, Aminadab vinyɔnu, si nye Naxason nɔvinyɔnu eye wòdzi Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar kple Itamar nɛ.

english_verse: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph.
translation_verse: Korax viŋutsuwoe nye: Asir, Elkana kple Abiasaf. Woawoe nye Korax ƒome la ƒe tɔgbuitɔgbuiwo.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Eleazar, Aron vi ɖe Putiel vinyɔnuwo dometɔ ɖeka, ame si dzi Pinehas nɛ. Ame siawo nye Levi-to la ƒe tɔgbuitɔgbuiwo kple woƒe ƒomeawo.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Aron kple Mosee Aƒetɔ gblɔ na be: “Mikplɔ Israelviwo ƒe toawo dzoe le Egipte-nyigba dzi.”

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Woawoe yi ɖagblɔ na Egipte Fiagã, Egipte-fia la be neɖe mɔ ne Israelviwo nadzo le eƒe anyigba dzi. Mose sia kple Aron sia ye. Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedeasi na Mose kple Aron

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Esi Aƒetɔ ƒo nu kple Mose le Egipte-nyigba dzi la,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: egblɔ nɛ be: “Nyee nye Aƒetɔ. Yi ɖagblɔ nya siwo katã megblɔ na wò la na Egipte Fiagã, Egipte-fia la.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Ke Mose gblɔ na Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, wò ŋutɔ ènya be nu menyaƒona nam o. Ale ke wɔ Egipte Fiagã la aɖo tomee?”

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Kpɔ ɖa, mewɔ wò abe Mawu ene ɖe Egipte Fiagã dzi, eye mana nɔviwò Aron nanye wò gbeƒãɖela.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Gblɔ gbe siwo katã mede asiwò la na Aron, eye eya negblɔ na Egipte Fiagã be nena mɔ Israelviwo be woadzo le eƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: ke Fiagã la maɖo to mi o. Maɖo asi Egipte dzi akplɔ nye aʋakɔ, nye dukɔ Israelviwo, ado goe tso Egipte-nyigba dzi to nu gã siwo mawɔ atsɔ ahe toe na wo la me.

english_verse: When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ne meho kple ŋusẽ ɖe Egipte ŋu, eye mekplɔ Israelviwo dzoe la, ekema Egiptetɔwo adze sii be nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: “Ne Egipte Fiagã la gblɔ na mi be: ‘Miwɔ nukunu aɖe míakpɔ’ la, ekema nàgblɔ na Aron be: ‘Tsɔ wò atizɔti da ɖe anyigba le Egipte Fiagã la ŋkume ne wòazu da.’ ”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Ale Mose kple Aron woyi Egipte Fiagã la gbɔ, eye wowɔ nu si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na wo be woawɔ la: Aron ɖe asi le eƒe atizɔti la ŋu da ɖe anyigba le Fiagã la kple eŋumewo ŋkume, eye wòtrɔ zu da.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Tete fiagã la yɔ Egiptetɔwo ƒe nunyalawo kple dzosalawo vɛ, eye wotsɔ woƒe vivimeŋusẽwo wɔ nukunu ma tututu:

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe tsɔ eƒe atizɔti da ɖe anyigba eye wotrɔ zu da, ke Aron ƒe atizɔti la lé wo tɔwo mi.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Gake Egipte Fiagã la ƒe dzime gasẽ ko, eye abe ale si Aƒetɔ la gblɔe ene la, egbe be yemaɖo to wo o. Fukpekpewo va Egipte dzi Fukpekpe gbãtɔ: Tsi trɔ zu ʋu

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Egipte Fiagã la ƒe dzime sẽ ŋutɔ; egbe be yemaɖe asi le dukɔa ŋu woadzo o.

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Eya ta etsɔ ŋdi kanya la, yi nàɖado goe le Nil-tɔsisi la to. Ne èyina la, tsɔ wò atizɔti si trɔ zu da la ɖe asi.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: Gblɔ nɛ be: ‘Aƒetɔ, Hebritɔwo ƒe Mawu la dɔm ɖe gbɔwò be magblɔ na wò be: Ɖe asi le nye dukɔ ŋu ne woayi aɖasubɔm le gbedadaƒo. Gake ègbe va se ɖe fifi.

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Esia nàtsɔ anyae be nyee nye Aƒetɔ nye esi: Kpɔ ɖa, mele atizɔti si le asinye la tsɔ ge aƒo Nil-tɔsisi la dzi, eye tsia atrɔ zu ʋu.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Lã siwo le eme la aku, eye tɔsisia anɔ ʋeʋẽm ale gbegbe be Egiptetɔwo mate ŋu ano emetsi o.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Gblɔ na Aron be: ‘Tsɔ wò atizɔti eye nàdoe ɖe Egipte-nyigba dzi tsiwo, tɔsisiwo, tɔʋuwo, táwo kple tsiteƒewo katã dzi bene woatrɔ zu ʋu, eye ʋu nanɔ Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi; atigowo kple kpezewo gɔ̃ hã ʋu anɔ wo me.’ ”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Mose kple Aron wɔ nu si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na wo la. Ekɔ atizɔti la dzi le Egipte Fiagã kple eŋumewo ŋkume, eye wòƒo tsia dzi. Tete Nil-tɔsisi me tsi la katã trɔ zu ʋu.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Lã siwo le eme la katã ku. Tɔa de asi ʋeʋẽ me ale gbegbe be Egiptetɔwo megate ŋu no emetsi o. Ʋu xɔ afi sia afi le Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Ke Egiptetɔwo ƒe nukunuwɔlawo hã to woƒe ayemɔwo dzi wɔ nukunu siawo ke. Ale abe ale si Aƒetɔ la gblɔe ɖi ene la, Egipte Fiagã la ƒe dzime gasẽ ko, eye wògbe be yemaɖo to Mose kple Aron ƒe gbe o.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Fiagã la trɔ dzo yi aƒeme, eye esia meʋã dzi nɛ vie gɔ̃ hã o.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Egiptetɔwo ku do ɖe Nil-tɔsisi la to be tsi nadzi ɖe wo me yewoano elabe Nil-tɔsisi me tsi la meganyo ne woano o.

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblẽ Nil me tsi la ŋkeke adrẽ sɔŋ.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Yi Egipte Fiagã la gbɔ nàɖagblɔ nɛ be Aƒetɔ be: ‘Ɖe asi le nye dukɔ ŋu ne woayi aɖasubɔm.

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Ne ègbe la, mana akpɔkplɔ nadzi ɖe anyigba la katã dzi abe dɔléle ene.

english_verse: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
translation_verse: Nil-tɔsisi azu akpɔkplɔ ɖeɖe, eye woaté bìbibi ava wò fiasã me, woage ɖe wò xɔdɔme me, adzo ɖe wò abati dzi. Woabɔ ɖe wò subɔlawo kple ŋuwòmewo ƒe aƒewo me. Woage ɖe wò abolokpowo kple abolodugugbawo me.

english_verse: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
translation_verse: Akpɔkplɔawo adzo ɖe wò ŋutɔ dziwò, wò dumeviwo kple wò subɔlawo katã dzi, ado kplamatsɛ na mi atraɖii.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Gblɔ na Aron be: ‘Tsɔ wò atikplɔ la nado asi ɖe tɔsisiwo, tɔʋuwo kple táwo dzi, ne akpɔkplɔwo nava Egipte-nyigba la dzi.”

english_verse: Aaron obeyed, and suddenly frogs were everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Aron do atizɔtia ɖe Egipte-nyigba dzi tsiwo dzi, eye akpɔkplɔwo do va kɔ ɖe anyigba bliboa dzi fũu.

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Ke Egipte-dzotɔwo hã tsɔ woƒe vivimeŋusẽwo he akpɔkplɔwo va Egipte-nyigba la dzii.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Tete Egipte Fiagã la yɔ Mose kple Aron, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Mido gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ ne wòaɖe akpɔkplɔawo ɖa le nye kple nye dukɔmetɔwo gbɔ, ekema maɖe asi le miaƒe dukɔ la ŋu woayi aɖasa vɔ na Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Mose ɖo eŋu be: “Ele asiwò me. Ɣe ka ɣie maɖe kukua ɖe wò ŋutɔ, ŋuwòmewo kple wò dukɔ la ta, ne akpɔkplɔawo nadzo le ŋuwò kple miaƒe aƒewo me, eye woanɔ Nil-tɔsisia ɖeɖe ko me ya?”

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Fiagã la xɔ edzi be: “Doe ɖa etsɔ.” Mose lɔ̃ be: “Yoo. Mawɔ wò gbe dzi ne nànyae be ame aɖeke meli abe Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la ene o.

english_verse: and frogs will no longer be found anywhere, except in the Nile.”
translation_verse: Wò ŋutɔ kple wò aƒe, ŋuwòmewo kple wò dukɔmeviwo siaa miakpɔ gbɔdzɔe tso akpɔkplɔawo si me. Nil me ko woasusɔ ɖo.”

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Mose kple Aron dzo le Fiagã la gbɔ. Mose yi ɖado gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ le akpɔkplɔ siwo va bɔ̀ ɖee la ŋuti.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Moses, and the frogs died everywhere—in houses, yards, and fields.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ se eƒe gbedodoɖa. Akpɔkplɔawo ku le aƒewo me, xɔxɔnuwo kple agblewo me.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Woli kɔ wo fũu ɖi, eye anyigba la katã dzi nɔ ʋeʋẽm kũu.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Gake esi Egipte Fiagã la kpɔ be yekpɔ gbɔdzɔe tso akpɔkplɔawo si me la, egasẽ dzime eye abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ ene la, egbe toɖoɖo Mose kple Aron. Fukpekpe etɔ̃lia: Muwo va kɔ ɖi

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gagblɔ na Mose be: “Gblɔ na Aron be: ‘Tsɔ wò atizɔti ƒo ke me le anyigba ne wòatrɔ zu muwo le Egipte-nyigba la katã dzi.’ ”

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Aron tsɔ atizɔtia ƒo anyigba. Tete ke trɔ zu mu sɔŋ bɔ̀ ɖe amewo kple lãwo siaa yome le Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Muawo nye tsyɔ amegbetɔ kple lãwo dzi. Woƒe dzotɔwo hã to vivimemɔwo dzi be yewoawɔ muwo gake womete ŋui o.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na fia la be: “Esia ya la, Mawu ƒe nuwɔwɔ ye.” Ke Egipte Fiagã la ƒe dzime gasẽ ko eye abe ale si Aƒetɔ la gblɔe ene la, egbe toɖoɖo. Fukpekpe enelia: Togbatowo ƒe ha gã aɖe va

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Fɔ etsɔ ŋdi kanya naɖalala Egipte Fiagã la. Egbɔna tɔsisi la to. Nàgblɔ nɛ be Aƒetɔ be: ‘Ɖe asi le nye dukɔ la ŋu ne woayi aɖasubɔm.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Ne ègbe la, mana togbatowo nava ɖe fu na wò ŋutɔ, ŋuwòmewo kple wò dukɔ la katã. Togbatowo age ɖe miaƒe aƒewo me, eye Egiptetɔwo ƒe aƒewo me ayɔ fũu kple togbato ale be ame makpɔ afɔɖoƒe teti hã o.

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ wɔ esia. Togbatowo ƒe ha gãwo va kɔ ɖi. Wogba ɖe Egipte Fiagã la ƒe fiasã me, eŋumewo ƒe aƒewo me, woƒe xɔwo me kple Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi, eye togbatowo gblẽ anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Tete Egipte Fiagã la yɔ Mose kple Aron, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Enyo, miyi ɖasa vɔ na mia Mawu la le anyigba sia dzi.”

english_verse: “That's impossible!” Moses replied. “Any sacrifices we offer to the Lord our God would disgust the Egyptians, and they would stone us to death.
translation_verse: Mose ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Manyo be míawɔ nenema o, elabe nu siwo míele tsɔtsɔ ge asa vɔ na Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la nye busunu na Egiptetɔwo. Ne míetsɔ nu siwo nye busunu na Egiptetɔwo va le vɔ sam le wo ŋkume ɖe, womaƒu kpe mí oa?

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Ehiã be míazɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃ ƒe mɔ ayi gbedadaƒo aɖasa vɔ na Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la, abe ale si wòafia mí lae ene.”

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Ale Egipte Fiagã la be: “Maɖe asi le mia ŋu miayi aɖasa vɔ na Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la le gbedadaƒo. Ke migayi didiƒe akpa o. Miado gbe ɖa ɖe tanye.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Woxɔ edzi nɛ be: “Ne metrɔ le gbɔwò ko maɖe kuku na Aƒetɔ be wòana togbatoawo nadzo etsɔ ɖeka bene Egipte Fiagã la kple eŋumewo kpakple dukɔa me tɔwo navo tso wo si me. Ɖeko Fiagã la negablem eye wòagagbe be yemaɖe asi le dukɔ la ŋu ne woaɖasa wɔ na Aƒetɔ o.”

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ wɔ Mose ƒe nya dzi, eye wòɖe togbatoawo ɖa le fiagã la kple eŋumewo kpakple dukɔa dome. Ɖeka pɛ hã mesusɔ o.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Gake Egipte Fiagã la gasẽ dzime fifia hã, egbe meɖe asi le dukɔ la ŋu wodzo o.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Yi Egipte Fiagã la gbɔ, ne nàgblɔ nɛ be Aƒetɔ, Hebritɔwo ƒe Mawu la be: ‘Ɖe asi le nye dukɔ la ŋu, ne woaɖasubɔm.

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: kpɔ ɖa, nye Aƒetɔ, matsrɔ̃ wò lãhawo le gbedzi. Mana dɔléle dziŋɔ nadze wò lãwo katã dzi. Adze sɔwo, tedziwo, kposɔwo, nyihawo, gbɔ̃ kple alẽwo dzi.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Ke made vovototo Israelviwo ƒe lãwo kple Egiptetɔwo tɔwo dome ale be Israelviwo ƒe lã aɖeke maku o.’ ”

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖo ɣeyiɣi gblɔ be: “Etsɔ nye, Aƒetɔ mawɔ nu sia le anyigba sia dzi.”

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, Aƒetɔ wɔ nu si wòbe yeawɔ la. Egiptetɔwo ƒe lãwo katã ku gake Israelviwo tɔ ya ƒe ɖeka gɔ̃ hã meku o.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose kple Aron be: “Miɖe kpomedzɔble ɖe asiƒome eye mina Mose nahlẽe ɖe ya me le Egipte Fiagã la ŋkume.

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: Azu abe ʋuʋudedi ene akaka ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi, eye wòana ƒoƒoe si me dɔ vɔ̃ le la nate amewo kple lãwo siaa le Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi.”

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Woku kpomedzɔble ɖe asiƒome tsɔ va tsi tsitre ɖe Egipte Fiagã la ŋkume. Mose hlẽe ɖe ya me eye wòtrɔ zu ƒoƒoedɔ vɔ̃ te amewo kple lãwo siaa le Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Ƒoƒoea te Egiptetɔwo ƒe dzotɔwo hã abe Egiptetɔ bubuawo ke ene, eye le esia ta la, womete ŋu nɔ te ɖe Mose nu o.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ na Egipte Fiagã la ƒe dzime gasẽ kokoko, eye abe ale si wògblɔ na Mose ene la, Fiagã la meɖo to wo o. Fukpekpe adrẽlia: Tsikpe titri dza ɖe Egipte-nyigba dzi

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gagblɔ na Mose be: “Fɔ yi Fiagã la gbɔ etsɔ ŋdi kanya nàɖatsi tsitre ɖe eŋkume agblɔ nɛ be: ‘Aƒetɔ, Hebritɔwo ƒe Mawu la be: Ɖe asi le nye dukɔ ŋu ne woayi aɖasubɔm.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: Ne ègasẽ to azɔ ya la, mawɔ fu wò ŋutɔ, ŋuwòmewo kple wò dukɔ la vevie bene nànyae be ame aɖeke meli abe nye ene le anyigba blibo la dzi o.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Elabe mate ŋu atsɔ dɔ vɔ̃ atsrɔ̃ wò ŋutɔ kple wò dukɔ la ɖa le anyigba dzi xoxoxo hafi.

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: Ke mena nètsi agbe be maɖe nye ŋusẽ afia wò, eye nye ŋkɔ naɖi le anyigba ƒe afi sia afi.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Ke ègale dàdam hegbe be yemaɖe asi le nye dukɔ ŋu woadzo o.

english_verse: All right. At this time tomorrow, he will bring on Egypt the worst hailstorm in its history.
translation_verse: Eya ta etsɔ ɣe alewo ɣi la, mana tsikpe sesẽ nadza vevie. Tsikpe sia tɔgbe medza kpɔ le Egipte-nyigba dzi tso esime woɖo dukɔa gɔme anyi o.

english_verse: You had better give orders for every person and every animal in Egypt to take shelter. If they don't, they will die.
translation_verse: Eya ta na woadi beɖoƒe na wò lãhawo kple wò nu siwo katã le agbleta la. Ame kple lã si tsi gbedzi, eye womele beɖoƒe o la, tsikpe aƒo wo, eye wòaku.’ ”

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Egipte Fiagã la ŋume siwo Aƒetɔ ƒe nya la tso dzika ƒo na la na woƒe kluviwo kple woƒe lãhawo yi ɖe bebeƒe.

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: Ke esiwo nya la metso dzika ƒo na o la gblẽ wo tɔwo ɖe gbedzi.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Do asi ɖe dziƒo, ne kpetsi nadza ɖe Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi. Nedza ɖe amewo, lãwo kple agblemenuku siwo katã le Egipte-nyigba dzi la dzi.”

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: Dzi le gbe ɖem ɖe tsikpe la me atraɖii. Esia tɔgbe medzɔ kpɔ tso esime woɖo Egipte-dukɔ la gɔme anyi o.

english_verse: People, animals, and crops were pounded by the hailstones, and bark was stripped from trees.
translation_verse: Kpetsi la gblẽ nu le Egipte-nyigba blibo la katã dzi. Egblẽ nu sia nu le gbedzi, eye wòwu ame kple lãwo siaa. Egblẽ agblemenukuwo eye wòfe gbemetiwo katã.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Gake le Gosen-nutome, afi si Israelviwo le ya la, kpetsi aɖeke medza ɖee o.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Tete Egipte Fiagã la na woɖayɔ Mose kple Aron vɛ, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Azɔ ya la, meda vo. Aƒetɔ tɔ dzɔ. Ke nye kple nye dukɔ la tɔ medzɔ o.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Miɖaɖe kuku na Aƒetɔ ne wòana dziɖegbe kple kpetsia nu natso, ekema maɖe asi le mia ŋu miadzo; miaganɔ afi sia o.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Mose ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Ne menyado le dua me ko la, make nye abɔwo me, aƒo koko na Aƒetɔ. Ekema dziɖegbe la nu atso, eye kpetsia hã ake, ne nàtsɔ nya be Aƒetɔ tɔe nye xexea me.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Ke wò ŋutɔ kple ŋuwòmewo ya la, menyae be miele Aƒetɔ Mawu la vɔ̃m haɖe o.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: (Ɖeti kple mɔli gblẽ le agble dzi elabe mɔli do ku eye ɖeti ƒo se ɣe ma ɣi.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Ke naneke mewɔ lu ŋutɔ kple bli ya o, elabe woawo do megbe.)

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Mose dzo le Egipte Fiagã la gbɔ. Esi wòdo go le dua me la, eke eƒe abɔ me, do gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ. Tete dziɖegbe la dzudzɔ, kpetsia hã nu tso, eye tsidzadza la megakɔ ɖi o.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Esi Egipte Fiagã la kpɔ be tsidzadzaa, kpetsia kple dziɖegbe la dzudzɔ la, egayi nuvɔ̃ wɔwɔ dzi. Eya kple eŋumewo gasẽ dzime.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Ale abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ to Mose dzi ene la, egagbe be yemaɖe asi le Israelviwo ŋu woadzo o.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Eyome Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Yi Egipte Fiagã la gbɔ. Nyee na eya ŋutɔ kple eŋumewo ƒe dzime sẽ, bene mawɔ dzesi siawo le Egipte-dukɔ la me.

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: To esia me nàva xlẽ nu siwo mewɔ Egiptetɔwo le woƒe anyigba dzi la afia viwòwo kple wò tɔgbuiyɔviwo, eye mi katã mianyae be nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Ale Mose kple Aron yi Egipte Fiagã la gbɔ ɖagblɔ nɛ be: “Aƒetɔ, Hebritɔwo ƒe Mawu la be: ‘Ɣe ka ɣi nàgbe ɖokuiwò bɔbɔ ɖi nam aɖase ɖo? Ɖe mɔ na nye dukɔ la ne woayi aɖasubɔm.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: Ne ègagbe la, mahe ʋetsuviwo ava wò anyigba dzi etsɔ.

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: Woanyè tsyɔ anyigba blibo la katã dzi ale gbegbe be anyigba magadze ame nakpɔ o. Woaɖu nu si susɔ si kpetsia megblẽ o la, eye woaɖu ati siwo gato gbɔna la hã keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: Woage ɖe wò xɔwo me, atra ɖe ŋuwòmewo kple Egiptetɔwo katã ƒe xɔwo me, ayɔ wo taŋtaŋ. Tso esime tɔ́wòwo kple tɔgbuiwòwo va anyigba sia dzi va se ɖe egbe kpa, womekpɔ esia tɔgbe kpɔ o.’ ” Tete wotrɔ dzo le Egipte Fiagã la gbɔ.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Egipte Fiagã la ŋumewo gblɔ nɛ be: “Va se ɖe ɣe ka ɣi koŋ ame sia anye mɔ̀ anɔ mía ɖem? Esi Egipte-dukɔ la gbã vɔ alea ɖe, mèkpɔe haɖe oa? Ɖe asi le wo ŋu bene woayi aɖasubɔ Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la. Wò ŋutɔ kpɔ ale si Egipte dome gblẽ vɔ keŋkeŋ lae ɖa!”

translation_verse: Tete wogayɔ Mose kple Aron va Egipte Fiagã la gbɔ, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Miyi ɖasubɔ Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la. Evɔ ɖe, ame ka kple ame kawoe le yiyim?”

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Mose ɖo eŋu be: “Mí katã tim ye le yiyi ge: ɖeviwo, ame tsitsiwo, mía viŋutsuwo, mia vinyɔnuwo, míaƒe alẽwo, gbɔ̃wo kple nyiwo, elabe ele na mí be míayi ɖaɖu ŋkekenyui na Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Mose do eƒe atizɔti la ɖe Egipte-nyigba la dzi, eye Aƒetɔ na ya ƒo tso ɣedzeƒe va anyigba la dzi ŋkeke blibo kple zã blibo. Kaka ŋu nake la, ya la lɔ ʋetsuviwo va kɔ ɖi.

translation_verse: Tete Egipte Fiagã la na woyɔ Mose kple Aron vɛ kaba, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Meda vo ɖe Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la ŋu, eye meda vo ɖe miawo hã mia ŋu.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: Eya ta, meɖe kuku na mi, mitsɔ nye vodada la kem fifia hã, eye miɖe kuku na Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la, be wòaɖe ku sia ɖa le dzinye.”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ na ya sesẽ aɖe tso ɣetoɖoƒe lɔ ʋetsuviawo ɖe nu yi ɖakɔ ɖe Aƒlaƒu la me. Ɖeka pɛ gɔ̃ ha metsi Egipte-nyigba la ƒe afi aɖeke o.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ na Egipte Fiagã la ƒe dzime gasẽ ale be wògbe meɖe asi le Israelviwo ŋu wodzo o. Fukpekpe asiekelia: Viviti tsiɖitsiɖi do ɖe Egipte-nyigba dzi

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.

translation_verse: Mose ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Ele be nàɖe asi le lã siwo míatsɔ asa vɔe kple esiwo miame na Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la ŋu na mí.

english_verse: and we won't know which animals we will need until we get there. That's why we can't leave even one of them here.”
translation_verse: Ele be míakplɔ míaƒe lãwo hã ayii; ɖeke ƒe afɔkli teti hã matsi anyi o. Woawo dometɔ aɖewo tia ge míala atsɔ sa vɔe na Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la, eye ɖe kokoko míaɖo afi ma hafi anya esiwo nyo míatsɔ awɔ vɔsaawoe.”

english_verse: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
