english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Mose ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Yoo, mesee! Nyemagava do ɖe ŋkuwò me azɔ gbeɖe o!”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Esusɔ fukpekpe ɖeka mahe va Egipte Fiagã la kple Egipte dzi. Emegbe la, Fiagã la aɖe mɔ na mi miadzo le afi sia. Ke menye asi ko wòaɖe le mia ŋu o; mia nyà ge wòala miadzo le afi sia.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na dukɔ la be ŋutsu sia ŋutsu kple nyɔnu sia nyɔnu nebia klosalo kple sika nuwo le eƒe aƒelika Egiptetɔ gbɔ.”

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ na Egiptetɔwo ve Israelviwo nu, eye Mose ŋutɔ hã nye bubume gã le Egipte Fiagã la ŋumewo kple dukɔ la ŋkume.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ na Egipte Fiagã la be: “Aƒetɔ be: ‘Le zã titina la, mele Egipte-nyigba me to ge ava yi.

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: Ŋgɔgbevi ɖe sia ɖe le anyigba la dzi aku; tso Egipte Fiagã la vi gbãtɔ si ava zi dzi ɖe tɔ́a yome dzi va se ɖe kosi si le teƒo la ƒe ŋgɔgbevi dzi. Nenema ke lãwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo katã hã aku.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Aviɣli aɖi le Egipte-nyigba blibo la dzi. Ɣli sia tɔgbe meɖi kpɔ o, eye magaɖi akpɔ hã o.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Ke le Israelviwo gbɔ la, ame o alo lã o, avu gɔ̃ hã mate gbe ɖe wo ŋu o. To esia me miadze sii be Aƒetɔ dea vovototo Egiptetɔwo kple Israelviwo dome.

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: Ekema ŋuwòme siawo katã ava gbɔnye, ade ta agu nam, agblɔ be: ‘Wò ŋutɔ kple wò ameawo katã midzo yi!’ Emegbe madzo.” Mose dzo le Egipte Fiagã la ŋkume kple dziku gã ŋutɔ.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Egipte Fiagã la gale to sẽ ge kokoko, ale be to ema me la, magawɔ nukunu geɖe wu le Egipte.”

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Mose kple Aron wɔ nukunu siawo katã le Egipte Fiagã ŋkume. Ke Aƒetɔ na fiagã la ƒe dzime gasẽ ale be wògbe meɖe asi le Israelviwo ŋu wodzo le eƒe anyigba dzi o.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose kple Aron le Egipte-nyigba dzi be:

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: “Ɣleti sia nanye ɣleti vevitɔ na mi le ƒèa me. Nezu ɣleti gbãtɔ na mi le ƒèa me.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Migblɔ na Israel-dukɔ blibo la be le ɣleti sia ƒe ŋkeke ewolia dzi la, ŋutsu sia ŋutsu nalé alẽvi ɖeka; aƒe ɖeka, alẽvi ɖeka.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Woaɖee ɖe aga va se ɖe ɣletia ƒe ŋkeke wui enelia gbe, eye le gbe ma gbe fiẽ la, Israelviwo ƒe ha bliboa katã le afi sia afi nawui.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Woatsɔ eƒe ʋu asisi ɖe ʋɔtrutiawo kple eve kple wo tametɔ la ŋu.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Woamè lã la, eye woaɖui le zã ma me kple amɔwɔ maʋamaʋã bolo kpakple ama veve.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Migaɖui mumu alo aɖae le tsi me o, ke boŋ mimèe le dzo me. Ele be wòanɔ blibo nenema, ta, afɔ kple dɔmenuawo nanɔ eŋu hafi miame aɖu.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: Migasusɔ ɖeke ɖi ŋu nake ɖe edzi o. Ne ɖe tsi anyi ŋu ke la, miatɔ dzoe.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Ale mianɔ aɖui nye esi: Mibla ali dzi, eye mido afɔkpawo ɖe afɔ. Milé atizɔti ɖe asi, eye miaɖui kabakaba. Aƒetɔ ƒe Paska wònye.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: Elabe mele Egipte-nyigba la me to ge ava yi le zã ma me, eye mawu ŋgɔgbevi ɖe sia ɖe le Egipte-nyigba la dzi, eɖanye ame o, eɖanye aƒemelã o. Matso nya me na Egipte-mawuwo katã. Nyee nye Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: “Miaɖu amɔwɔ maʋamaʋã bolo la ŋkeke adrẽ. Tso ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la, ele be miaɖe amɔwɔʋãnu ɖe sia ɖe ado goe le miaƒe aƒewo katã me. Ame sia ame si aɖu nane si me amɔwɔʋãnu le tso ŋkeke gbãtɔ yi ɖase ŋkeke adrẽlia dzi la, woaɖee ɖa le Israelviwo dome.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: Miɖo ŋku amɔ maʋamaʋã bolo ŋkeke sia dzi ɖaa, elabe ŋkeke ma dzie mekplɔ miaƒe dukɔ la ƒe amehawo dzoe le Egipte-nyigba la dzi. Anye ŋkekenyui na mi, mianɔ ɖuɖum ƒe sia ƒe tso dzidzime yi dzidzime.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Mele be amɔwɔ ʋaʋã aɖeke nanɔ miaƒe aƒewo me le ŋkeke adrẽ mawo me o. Ne ame aɖe ɖu amɔwɔ ʋaʋã le ŋkeke mawo me la, woaɖee ɖa le Israelviwo dome. Eɖanye amedzro o, eɖanye Israelvi o, woaɖee ɖa.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.

translation_verse: ekema miaɖo eŋu be: ‘Esiae nye ŋutitotovɔsa na Aƒetɔ, ame si to Israelviwo ƒe aƒewo ŋu yi le Egipte, eye wòɖawu Egiptetɔwo hetso míaƒe aƒewo ɖi la.’ ” Tete dukɔ blibo la de ta agu, eye wodo gbe ɖa.

translation_verse: Tete Israelviwo ɖawɔ nu siwo Aƒetɔ ɖo na wo to Mose kple Aron dzi la dzi tututu. Ŋgɔgbeviwo ku

translation_verse: Le zã titina la, Aƒetɔ wu ŋgɔgbeviwo katã le Egipte-nyigba dzi. Ewu ŋgɔgbevi ɖe sia ɖe, tso Egipte Fiagã si le Egipte fiazikpui dzi la ƒe ŋgɔgbevi kple gaxɔmenɔla ƒe ŋgɔgbevi kpakple lãwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo katã dzi.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Tete Egipte Fiagã la, eŋumewo kple Egiptetɔwo katã fɔ le zã titina, eye aviɣli de dzi hoo le dukɔ bliboa me elabe Egiptetɔwo ƒe aƒe aɖeke meli si me ame meku le o.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.

translation_verse: Mikplɔ miaƒe alẽ kple gbɔ̃hawo kpakple miaƒe nyihawo, abe ale si miedi ene, ne miadzo! Miabia yayra na nye hã!”

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Egiptetɔwo ƒo du ɖe Israelviwo nu be woadzo le anyigba la dzi kabakaba. Wole ɣli dzi be: “Mí katã míele kuku ge!”

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo lɔ woƒe nuwo: amɔwɔ si mekpɔ ʋã haɖe o kple akpaku si me woblua nuɖuɖu le la hebla ɖe avɔ kple awu ʋlayawo me lé ɖe abɔta.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Abe ale si Mose ɖo aɖaŋu na wo va yii ene la, wobia klosalo kple sika nuwo kpakple nudodowo Egiptetɔwo hexɔ le wo si.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ na Egiptetɔwo ve Israelviwo nu tsɔ nuawo na wo faa. Esia wɔ be Israelviwo ha Egiptetɔwo tsɔ dzoe.

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo ho tso Ramses ɖo ta Sukot. Ŋutsu siwo le afɔ dzi dze mɔ la ƒe xexlẽme anɔ ame akpe alafa ade, ɖeviwo mele eme o.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Amedzro geɖewo hã ho kple wo, eye wokplɔ lãha gã ŋutɔ ɖe asi: gbɔ̃wo, alẽwo kple nyiwo.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ amɔwɔ maʋamaʋã si wotsɔ tso Egipte la me aboloe, ke amɔwɔ la meʋã o, elabe Egiptetɔwo nyà wo dzoe kpata, eye womete ŋu wɔ amɔwɔ ɖi wòʋã wotsɔ ɖe asi o. Nenema ke womekpɔ ɣeyiɣi di nuɖuɖu ɖe asi hafi tso o.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ nɔ ŋu zã blibo ma be yeakplɔ wo dzoe le Egipte-nyigba dzi. Zã ma va zu ŋudɔzã tɔxɛ si me Israelviwo katã dɔa ŋu tsɔna dea bubu Aƒetɔ ŋu, tso dzidzime yi dzidzime. Paskalẽvi la ɖuɖu ŋu ɖoɖowo

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose kple Aron be: Paska la ŋu ɖoɖowoe nye esiawo: ame si menye Israelvi o la mekpɔ mɔ aɖui o.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Ke kluvi si woƒle vɛ la, ele be woatso aʋa nɛ hafi wòaɖui.

english_verse: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
translation_verse: Amedzro alo apaɖila aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ aɖui o.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: Aƒe ɖeka me ko woaɖui le; womatsɔ lã la ƒe ɖeke adoe le aƒea me o, eye womagbã eƒe ƒu aɖeke hã o.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Israelviwo ƒe ha blibo la neɖu ŋkekenyuia.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Ke ne amedzro aɖe le gbɔwò, si di be yeaɖu Paska la la, ele be woatso aʋa na ŋutsu ɖe sia ɖe si le esi la hafi wòava ɖui. Ekema woabui abe Israel vidzidzia ene. Ke bolobolotɔ aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ aɖu Paska la o.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Sedede ɖeka mae anɔ ŋkekea ŋu na aƒevi kple amedzro siwo le mia dome la siaa.

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo katã wɔ se si Aƒetɔ de na Mose kple Aron la dzi pɛpɛpɛ.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe ye Aƒetɔ kplɔ Israelviwo ƒe hatsotsoawo do goe le Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: “Ɖe ŋgɔgbeviwo katã ɖe aga nam. Nu sia nu si aʋu dɔ nu na nɔa le Israelviwo dome la, tɔnye ye. Eɖanye ame alo lã o, tɔnyee.” Amɔwɔ Maʋamaʋã Bolo Ŋkeke Nyui

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ka atam na mia tɔgbuiwo be yeatsɔ Kanaanitɔwo, Xititɔwo, Amoritɔwo, Xivitɔwo kple Yebusitɔwo ƒe anyigba si dzi notsi kple anyitsi bɔ ɖo la ana mi. Ne wòkplɔ mi va anyigba sia dzi la, miaɖu ŋkekenyui sia le ɣleti sia me.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Miaɖu amɔwɔ maʋamaʋã bolo ŋkeke adrẽ, eye le ŋkeke adrẽa gbe la, miaɖu ŋkekenyui na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke adrẽ siawo me la, miaɖu amɔwɔ maʋamaʋã bolo ko. Womakpɔ amɔwɔ ʋaʋã bolo alo amɔwɔʋãnu aɖeke le mia si le miaƒe anyigba blibo la dzi o.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe la, miagblɔ na mia viŋutsuwo be: ‘Nu si Aƒetɔ wɔ na mí esime míeʋu tso Egipte la tae míele ŋkeke sia ɖum ɖo.’

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke nyui sia nanye ŋkuɖodzinu le miaƒe ŋgo nu, bene Aƒetɔ ƒe se la nanɔ mia nu elabe ŋusẽ triakɔ ŋutɔe wòtsɔ kplɔ mi dzoe le Egipte.

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: “Ne Aƒetɔ kplɔ mi va Kanaanitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi abe ale si wòka atam na mi kple mia tɔgbuiwoe ene, eye wòtsɔe na mi la,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: ekema miaɖe nu sia nu si ʋu dɔ nu na nɔa la ɖe aga na Aƒetɔ; miaƒe lãwo ƒe ŋgɔgbevi siwo nye atsu la katã nanye Aƒetɔ tɔ.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Ke tedzinɔ ƒe ŋgɔgbevi ya la, miatsɔ alẽ aɖɔlii. Ne mieɖɔlii o la, ekema miŋe kɔ nɛ. Ke miɖɔli amewo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo katã.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ne etsɔ megbe mia viŋutsuwo va bia mi be: ‘Nuwɔna sia gɔme ɖe?’ mahã la, miaɖo eŋu be: ‘Aƒetɔ tsɔ ŋusẽ triakɔ ŋutɔ kplɔ mí dzoe le Egipte, afi si míenye kluviwo le tsã la.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Esi Egipte Fiagã la sẽ tame, gbe be yemaɖe asi le mía ŋu míadzo o la, Aƒetɔ wu ŋgɔgbeviwo katã le Egipte-nyigba dzi, amegbetɔwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo kple lãwo tɔwo siaa. Eya ta míetsɔa atsu sia atsu si ʋu dɔ nu na nɔa la saa vɔe na Aƒetɔ, eye míeɖɔlia mía viŋutsuviwo ya kple alẽ.

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Esia nye dzesi anɔ míaƒe asi ta kple ŋgoblanu anɔ míaƒe ŋgo nu, be Aƒetɔ ye tsɔ eƒe ŋusẽ triakɔ la kplɔ mí dzoe le Egipte.’ ” Alilikpo kple dzobibi tsrala la

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Esi Egipte Fiagã la ɖe asi le Israelviwo ŋu wodzo la, Mawu mekplɔ wo to Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi mɔ o, togbɔ be eyae tsɔ kpuie hafi. Elabe Mawu gblɔ be: “Ne woho aʋa ɖe wo ŋu la, woƒe susu ava trɔ, eye woagbugbɔ ayi Egipte.”

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: Eya ta ena woto gbedadaƒomɔ si ɖo ta Aƒlaƒu la gbɔ la dzi. Ke Israelviwo bla akpa ɖe aʋawɔwɔ ŋu hafi dze mɔ tso Egipte.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Mose tsɔ Yosef ƒe ƒuwo ɖe asi elabe Yosef gblɔ na Israelviwo be: “Mika atam nam be, ne Mawu ve mia nu eye miedzo le afii yina la, miatsɔ nye ƒuwo ɖe asi ayii.”

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Israelviwo dze mɔ tso Sukot, eye woɖaƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Etam le gbedadaƒo la to.

english_verse: During the day the Lord went ahead of his people in a thick cloud, and during the night he went ahead of them in a flaming fire. That way the Lord could lead them at all times, whether day or night.
translation_verse: Alilikpo tsrala la medzona le dukɔ la gbɔ le ŋkeke me o, eye dzobibi tsrala la hã medzona le dukɔ la ŋgɔ le zã me o.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na Israelviwo be woatrɔ va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Pi-Haxirot gbɔ le Migdol kple ƒu la dome le Baal-Zefon kasa ɖe ƒua nu.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Ekema Egipte Fiagã la agblɔ le mi, Israelviwo ŋu be, ‘Wobu mɔ eye woble ɖe gbedadaƒo.’

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Mana Egipte Fiagã la ƒe dzime nasẽ, eye wòakplɔ wo ɖo. Ekema maɖe nye ŋusẽ afia ɖe Egipte Fiagã la kple eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la ŋuti be Egiptetɔwo nadze sii be nyee nye Aƒetɔ” eye wowɔ nenema.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Esi wogblɔ na Egipte-fia be Israel-dukɔ la sí dzo la, eya ŋutɔ kple eŋumewo ƒe susu trɔ eye wobia wo ɖokui be: “Nu kae nye esi míewɔ? Míeɖe asi le Israelvi siwo subɔa mí la ŋu wodzo!”

english_verse: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
translation_verse: Fia la ɖe gbe wobla akpa na eƒe aʋatasiaɖam, eye wòkplɔ eƒe aʋakɔwo yii.

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ na Egipte Fiagã la ƒe dzime sẽ ale be wokplɔ Israelviawo ɖo, esime wodzo yina aglãdzetɔe.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Egiptetɔwo kple Egipte Fiagã la ƒe sɔwo, tasiaɖamwo, sɔdolawo kpakple aʋakɔawo katã ti Israelviwo yome va tu wo le woƒe asaɖa me le ƒua nu le Pi-Haxirot gbɔ le Baal-Zefon kasa.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Egipte Fiagã la gogo wo, eye Israelviwo fɔ mo dzi. Kasia Egiptetɔwo nye esi zɔ ɖe wo dzi gbɔna. Dzidzi ƒo wo eye wodo ɣli yɔ Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: Wobia Mose be: “Yɔdoe mele Egipte o ta nèkplɔ mí dzo le afi ma be míava ku ɖe gbedadaƒoa? Nu kae nye esi nèkplɔ mí dzo le Egipte va wɔ mí?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Esia ko gblɔm míenɔ na wò le Egipte be: ‘Ɖe asi le mía ŋu, ne míasubɔ Egiptetɔwo.’ Elabe ne míele Egiptetɔwo subɔm eye míele agbe la, enyo wu be míayi aɖaku ɖe gbedadaƒo.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Ke Mose gblɔ na dukɔ la be: “Migavɔ̃ o. Milé dzi ɖe ƒo ko ne miakpɔ ale si Aƒetɔ le xɔxɔ ge na mi egbe sia la ɖa; Egiptetɔ siwo kpɔm miele egbe la, miegale wo kpɔ ge akpɔ gbeɖe o.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: Miawo mizi kpi ko, Aƒetɔ le aʋa wɔ ge ɖe mia nu.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ bia Mose be: “Nu ka ta nèle ɣli dom le yɔyem? Gblɔ na Israelviwo be woaho aɖo ta ŋgɔ ko.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Wò la, tsɔ wò atizɔti, nàdoe ɖe ƒu la dzi ne nàma tsia ɖe eve bene Israelviwo nazɔ ƒuƒuiƒe ato ƒu la me ayi.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Mana Egiptetɔwo ƒe dzime nasẽ, eye woakplɔ wo ɖo bene maɖe nye ŋusẽ afia ɖe Egipte Fiagã la kple eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la, eƒe tasiaɖamwo kple sɔdolawo katã ŋu.

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Tete mawudɔla si le Israel ƒe aʋakɔ la ŋgɔ la dzo yi emegbe. Nenema ke alilikpo tsrala si le wo ŋgɔ la hã dzo yi wo megbe,

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: heɖale Egiptetɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ kple Israelviwo ƒe aʋakɔ dome, eye alilikpo tsrala la do viviti ɖe Egiptetɔwo le zã la me, ke eklẽ na Israelviwo ya ale be wo dometɔ aɖeke mete ɖe nɔvia ŋu zã blibo la katã o.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Azɔ Mose do asi ɖe ƒua dzi. Tete Aƒetɔ na ɣedzeƒeya sesẽ ƒo zã blibo la katã, hetutu atsiaƒua ɖe megbe. Ƒuƒuiƒe do, eye tsia me ma.

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo zɔ ƒuƒuiƒe to ƒua me. Tsi la zu abe gli ene na wo le ɖusime kple miame.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Le fɔŋli me la, Aƒetɔ le dzobibi kple alilikpo tsrala me kpɔ Egiptetɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ la dzi ɖa, eye wòtɔtɔ wo.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: Ena woƒe tasiaɖamfɔtiwo gli, ŋgɔyiyi zu dɔ. Tete Egiptetɔwo gblɔ be: “Mina míasí dzo, elabe Aƒetɔ le Israel dzi tsi tre ɖe mía ŋu le aʋa wɔm na wo!”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Fifia Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Do asi ɖe ƒu la dzi ne ƒua nagbugbɔ yi enɔƒe aɖaŋe ɖe Egiptetɔawo, woƒe tasiaɖamwo kple woƒe sɔdolawo dzi.”

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Mose do asi ɖe ƒua dzi, eye kaka ŋu nake la, ƒua gaɖɔ, goglo abe tsã ene. Esi Egiptetɔwo sí yina la, Aƒetɔ nyà wo de ƒu la me.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Tsia trɔ va tsyɔ tasiaɖamuawo, sɔdolaawo kple Egipte Fiagã la ƒe aʋakɔ si kplɔ Israelviwo ɖo yi ƒua me la katã dzi. Wo dometɔ ɖeka pɛ hã metsi agbe o.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Ke Israelviwo ya zɔ ƒuƒuiƒe to ƒua me, eye tsia zu abe gli ene ɖe woƒe ɖusime kple miame.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Aleae Aƒetɔ ɖe Israelviwo tso Egiptetɔwo si me gbe ma gbe, eye Israelviwo kpɔ Egiptetɔwo ƒe kukuawo le ƒua nu.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Esi Israel kpɔ ŋusẽ triakɔ si Aƒetɔ tsɔ tu nu kple Egiptetɔwo la, dukɔ la vɔ̃ Aƒetɔ, eye woxɔ eyama kple eƒe dɔla Mose dzi se.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Ale Mose kple Israelviwo dzi ha sia na Aƒetɔ be: “Madzi ha na Aƒetɔ elabe ewɔ nu dzɔtsuwo; enyrɔ sɔ kple sɔdola ɖe ƒu me.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ nye nye ŋusẽ kple nye ha; eya va zu xɔname nam. Nye Mawue, eya ta makafui. Tɔ́nye ƒe Mawue, eya ta madoe ɖe dzi.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: Aʋawɔlae nye Aƒetɔ; Aƒetɔ nye eŋkɔ.

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: Etsɔ Egipte Fiagã la ƒe tasiaɖam kple aʋakɔ la ƒu gbe ɖe ƒu me, eye aʋakalẽtɔwo nyrɔ ɖe Aƒlaƒu la me.

english_verse: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
translation_verse: Tsiɖɔɖɔ gbagba tsyɔ wo dzi eye woyi to abe kpe ene.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: O Aƒetɔ, wò nuɖusibɔ ƒe ŋusẽ triakɔ la ɖua dzi. O Aƒetɔ, wò nuɖusibɔ sia nètsɔna gbãa futɔwoe gudugudu.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: Wò gãnyenye manyagblɔ nètsɔna hea ame siwo tsi tre ɖe ŋuwò la ƒua anyi. Èdɔ wò dɔmedzoe helihelĩ la ɖa wòfiã wo abe gbe ƒuƒu ene.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Wò ŋɔti me gbɔgbɔ na tsia ƒo kɔ. Tsi tsatsa dzɔ ɖi abe gli ene; ƒu gɔme tsi bla zu kpe.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: Futɔ ya be: “Mati wo aɖatu wo; mafiti wo, maha aboyonu hafi nye dzi nadze me. Malũ nye yi le aku me eye matsrɔ̃ wo!”

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Ke wò la, ƒuƒu ko nèɖo; tete ƒu la gbagba tsyɔ wo dzi; woyi to abe tsumi ene ɖe gogloƒe.

english_verse: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
translation_verse: O Aƒetɔ, ame kae de nuwò le mawuwo dome? Ame kae le abe wò ene, si wotsɔ gãnyenye ɖo atsyɔ̃ na, wòɖi vɔvɔ̃, dze kafukafu eye wòwɔa nukunuwo?

english_verse: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
translation_verse: Ɖusi ko nèdo ɖa, tete anyigba mi wo.

english_verse: The people you rescued were led by your powerful love to your holy place.
translation_verse: Ève wò dukɔ la nu; nèkplɔ wo eye nèɖe wo. Etsɔ wò ŋusẽ kplɔ wo va ɖo teƒe kɔkɔe la.

english_verse: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
translation_verse: Dukɔwo see eye dzidzi ƒo wo; Filistitɔwo le ƒoƒom tititi.

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Edom-fiawo ɖi vo; Moab-megãwo dzo nyànyanya; Kanaanitɔwo katã lulu.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Vɔvɔ̃ kple ŋɔdzi lé wo. Wò ŋusẽ triakɔ la na wodze ti abe kpe ene, va se ɖe esime wò dukɔ si nèxɔ ƒle la to wo dome yi!

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Àkplɔ wò dukɔ vɛ eye àtsɔ wo aɖo to si nye wò ŋutɔ tɔwò la dzi; O Aƒetɔ, teƒe si nèdzra ɖo be yeanɔ, O Aƒetɔ, kɔkɔeƒe si wò ŋutɔ nètsɔ wò asi ɖo anyii.

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ aɖu fia tegbetegbee.” Miryam ƒe ha

english_verse: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Elabe esi Egipte Fiagã ƒe sɔwo, eƒe tasiaɖamwo kple sɔdolawo ɖo ƒua me la, Aƒetɔ na tsi la tsyɔ wo dzi. Ke Israelviwo ya zɔ ƒuƒuiƒe to ƒua me do.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Tete Aron nɔvinyɔnu Miryam, Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela tsɔ axatsɛ eye nyɔnuwo katã hã tsɔ axatsɛwo kplɔe ɖo le ɣe ɖum.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Miryam do ha ɖa be: “Midzi ha na Aƒetɔ elabe eɖu dzi nukutɔe; ede sɔ kple sɔdola ƒu.” Tsi veve

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Emegbe Mose na Israel zɔ mɔ tso Aƒlaƒu la nu yi Sur-gbedadaƒo. Wozɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃ ƒe mɔ le gbedadaƒo gake womekpɔ tsi aɖeke o.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Wova ɖo Mara; ke tsi si le afi ma la vena, eya ta womete ŋu noe o. Eya ta woyɔa teƒea be “Mara”.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Dukɔ la lĩ Mose ŋu be: “Afi ka míakpɔ tsi le ano?”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Mose do ɣli yɔ Aƒetɔ, eye Aƒetɔ fia ati aɖee. Esi wòtsɔ ati la da ɖe tsia me la, tsia trɔ zu tsi nyui. Afi mae Aƒetɔ na se kple ɖoɖo Israelviwo le. Afi mae wòdo wo kpɔ le.

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: “Ne èɖo to Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la, eye nèwɔ nu si dzea Mawu ŋu, ne èlea fɔ ɖe eƒe sewo ŋu eye nèwɔa eƒe ɖoɖowo katã dzi la, nyemahe fukpekpe siwo katã mehe va Egiptetɔwo dzi la ƒe ɖeke ava dziwò o, elabe nyee nye Aƒetɔ, wò dɔyɔla.”

english_verse: Later the Israelites came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and
translation_verse: Emegbe wova ɖo Elim, teƒe si tsidzɔƒe wui eve kple deti bla adrẽ le, eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe afi ma, le tsia gbɔ.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Eyome Israelviwo ƒe ha blibo la ho tso Elim va ɖo Sin-gbedadaƒo le Elim kple Sinai dome. Gbe ma gbee nye ɣleti evelia ƒe ŋkeke wui atɔ̃lia gbe tututu esi woʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Tete ameha blibo la de asi liʋiliʋĩlilĩ me le Mose kple Aron ŋu.

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: Wobe: “Ne Aƒetɔ ɖe wòwu mí le míaƒe lãzewo gɔme le Egipte, afi si míeɖua nu ɖia ƒo nyuie le la, ne menyo wu esia be miekplɔ mí ameha gã sia va gbedadaƒo afii, be dɔ newu mí, míaku oa?”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Kpɔ ɖa, mana abolo nadza tso dziƒo na mi ne ameawo ayi aɖafɔ gbe sia gbe. Gake abolo agbɔsɔsɔ sinu ame ɖeka ate ŋu aɖu gbe ɖeka la ko ame sia ame kpɔ mɔ afɔ le ŋkeke ɖeka dzi. Mawɔ esia atsɔ do wo kpɔ be woawɔ nye sewo dzi loo, alo womawɔ wo dzi o mahã.

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke adelia dzi, kaka woaɖu nu si wofɔ vɛ vɔ la, adzi ɖe edzi ade agbɔsɔsɔ sinu wofɔna gbe sia gbe la ƒe teƒe eve.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Ale Mose kple Aron gblɔ na Israelviwo katã be: “Egbe fiẽ mianyae be Aƒetɔ ye kplɔ mi dzoe le Egipte vavã.

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: Etsɔ ŋdi la, miele Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe kpɔ ge elabe Aƒetɔ se liʋiliʋĩ si lĩm miele le eŋu?”

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Mose yi edzi be: “Ne Aƒetɔ na lã mi mieɖu le fiẽ, eye mieɖu abolo ɖi ƒo le ŋdi, elabe Aƒetɔ se miaƒe liʋiliʋĩ si mielĩ le eŋu la, nu ka míawo míenye? Menye míawo ŋu mielĩ o, ke boŋ Aƒetɔ ŋue mielĩ.

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ na Aron be: “Gblɔ na Israel ƒe ameha blibo la be: ‘Mite va Aƒetɔ ŋkume elabe ese miaƒe liʋiliʋĩlilĩ la.’ ”

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Esi Aron nɔ nu ƒom na Israel ƒe ameha bliboa la, wonɔ gbedadaƒo la lɔƒo kpɔm eye kpɔ ɖa, Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe do ɖe alilikpo me le wo ŋkume.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: “Mese Israelviwo ƒe liʋiliʋĩlilĩ la. Gblɔ na wo be: ‘Le fiẽ me la, lã si miaɖu la ava na mi, eye etsɔ ŋdi la, miakpɔ abolo aɖu wòasu mi nyuie ne mianyae be nyee nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la.’ ”

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Esi fiẽ ɖo la, tegliwo va dze ɖe asaɖa la me hetsyɔ eƒe afi sia afi. Ŋufɔke ŋdi la, edzé be zãmu dza fũu ƒo xlã asaɖa la.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Kasia zãmu la naƒu vɔ la, nu suesue, gbabɛ, gotoe aɖewo le gbedadaƒo la le anyigba fũu abe kpetsi ene.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Esi Israelviwo kpɔ wo la, wobia wo nɔewo be: “Nu kae nye esi?” Mose gblɔ na wo be: “Nu sia nye abolo si Aƒetɔ na mi be miaɖu.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Se si Aƒetɔ de lae nye esi: ‘Ame sia ame nalɔ agbɔsɔsɔ si ade na eya ŋutɔ kple eƒe agbadɔmetɔwo le ŋkeke ɖeka me la ko, eye dzidzeme si wòaku ɖe ame ɖeka nu la nanye lita ene.’ ”

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Israelviwo yi ɖalɔ nuɖuɖu la. Ame aɖewo lɔe wòsɔ gbɔ wu ale si dze; ke ame aɖewo tɔ mede o.

english_verse: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ na wo be: “Migana ame aɖeke nagblẽ ɖeke ɖi ŋu nake ɖe edzi o.”

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Gake womeɖo to Mose o, eye ame aɖewo gblẽe ɖi ŋu ke ɖe edzi; ke edze nyé eye wòƒaƒã. Mose do dɔmedzoe ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Ŋdi sia ŋdi la, woyina ɖalɔnɛ; ame sia ame ɖe ale si wòate ŋu aɖu gbe ma gbe ko nu. Ne ŋdɔ ʋu la, esi tsi anyi la lólona.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke adea gbe la, wolɔ ŋkeke eve ƒe ɖuɖu, ame ɖeka lita ene. Ameha la ƒe amegãwo va gblɔe na Mose.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Aƒetɔ be: ‘Etsɔ nye dzudzɔgbe, ŋkeke kɔkɔe na Aƒetɔ. Nuɖuɖua ƒe akpa si miatsɔ ƒo aboloe la, mitsɔe ƒoe, eye esi miaɖa la, miɖae. Ke midzra esi asusɔ la ɖo na etsɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
translation_verse: Wodae ɖi ŋu ke ɖe edzi abe ale si Mose gblɔ na wo la ene, gake meƒaƒã o, eye medze nyé hã o.

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ na wo be: Miɖu eya egbe, elabe egbe nye dzudzɔgbe na Aƒetɔ; miele ɖeke kpɔ ge le gbe me alɔ o.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke ade me la, nuɖuɖu sia anɔ anyi miayi aɖalɔ; ke le ŋkeke adrẽa gbe, si nye dzudzɔgbe la, miele ɖeke kpɔ ge o.”

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Ke le ŋkeke adrẽa gbe la, ame aɖewo ya gayi be yewoaɖalɔ ɖe; womekpɔ ɖeke o.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ bia Mose be: “Ɣe ka ɣi gɔ̃ miagbe toɖoɖo nye sewo kple ɖoɖowo ase ɖo?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, Aƒetɔ na dzudzɔgbe mi, eya tae wònaa ŋkeke eve ƒe nuɖuɖu mi le ŋkeke adelia dzi ɖo. Ame sia ame nenɔ aƒeme le ŋkeke adrẽa gbe. Ame aɖeke megado go o.”

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ale dukɔ la dzudzɔ eɖokui le ŋkeke adrẽa gbe.

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Azɔ Israelviwo tsɔ ŋkɔ na nuɖuɖu la be mana. Ele abe xé ƒe tsetse ene gake efu ɣie, eye wòvivina abe tatali si me wode anyitsii ene.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ de se be: ‘Miku gomer ɖeka dzra ɖo ɖi, ne wòanɔ anyi tso dzidzime yi dzidzime be mia viwo nava nya nuɖuɖu si metsɔ nyi mi le gbedadaƒo esime mekplɔ mi tso Egipte-nyigba dzi gbɔna.’ ”

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ na Aron be: “Tsɔ zevi nalɔ mana lita eve kɔ ɖe eme, eye nàtsɔe ɖaɖo Aƒetɔ ŋkume bene wòanɔ afi ma tso dzidzime yi dzidzime.”

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Ale Aron tsɔe da ɖe seawo gbɔ abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be woawɔe ene.

english_verse: The Israelites ate manna for
translation_verse: Omer ɖeka nye efa ƒe memama ewolia.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Israelviwo ƒe ameha blibo la ho tso Sin-gbedadaƒo ɖo ta ŋgɔ. Wotɔ ɖe teƒeteƒewo le Aƒetɔ ƒe gbeɖeɖe nu. Wova ɖo Refidim mlɔeba eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe afi ma. Ke tsi aɖeke mele afi ma woano o.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: Eya ta wokpe dzre kple Mose gblɔ be: “Di tsi na mí ne míano.” Mose bia wo be: “Nu ka ta miele dzre wɔm kplim? Nu ka ta miele Aƒetɔ tem kpɔ?”

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Gake esi tsikɔ wu ameawo vevie le afi ma la, woƒo nu le Mose ŋu be: “Nu ka ta nèkplɔ mí dzoe le Egipte? Ɖe nèbe tsikɔ nawu míawo ŋutɔ kple mía viwo kpakple míaƒe lãwo ne míakua?”

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: Ale Mose do ɣli na Aƒetɔ be: “Nu ka mawɔ na dukɔ sia? Wole klalo be yewoaƒu kpem.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Dze ŋgɔ na dukɔ la, eye nàtia Israel-me tsitsi aɖewo akpe ɖe ɖokuiwò ŋu. Tsɔ atizɔti si nètsɔ ƒo Nil dzi la ɖe asi yii.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, matsi tsitre ɖe ŋkuwò me ɖe Xoreb-kpe la dzi. Ƒo kpe la ekema tsi ado tso eme be dukɔ la nano.” Mose wɔ nenema le Israel-me tsitsiawo ŋkume.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: “Dzrewɔwɔ” Mose tsɔ ŋkɔ na teƒe ma be Masa kple Meriba elabe Israelviwo wɔ dzre eye wote Aƒetɔ kpɔ le afi ma bia be: “Ɖe Aƒetɔ le mía dome loo, alo meli o?” Amalekitɔwo wɔ aʋa kple Israelviwo

english_verse: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Esia megbe Amalekitɔwo wɔ aʋa kple Israelviwo le Refidim.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Tete Mose gblɔ na Yosua be: “Tia ŋutsu aɖewo na mí ne miayi aɖakpe aʋa kple Amalek etsɔ. Nye la, maɖatsi tsitre ɖe togbɛ la tame alé Mawu ƒe atizɔti la ɖe asi.”

english_verse: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
translation_verse: Ale Yosua wɔ abe ale si Mose gblɔ nɛ la ene eye wowɔ aʋa kple Amalek. Ke Mose, Aron kple Xur ya yi ɖe togbɛ la tame.

english_verse: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
translation_verse: Ne Mose kɔ asi dzi la, Israelviwo ƒe alɔ yia dzi, ne eɖiɖi asi ɖe anyi la, ekema Amalekitɔwo ƒe alɔ yia dzi.

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: Ke abɔ va ku ɖe Mose ŋu, ale wotsɔ kpe va de ete, eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ anyi ɖe edzi. Aron kple Xur lé eƒe asiwo ɖe dzi; ame ɖeka le axa ɖeka dzi eye ame evelia le axa kemɛ dzi. Ale wolé eƒe asiwo ɖe te, va se ɖe esime ɣe ɖo to.

english_verse: That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Yosua fiti Amalek kple eƒe aʋakɔ la kple yi keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Ŋlɔ nu sia ɖe agbalẽ me hena ŋkuɖoɖo edzi, eye nàkui ɖe to me na Yosua, elabe matsrɔ̃ Amalek ŋkɔ ɖa le xexea me keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Mose ɖi vɔsamlekpui eye wòna ŋkɔe be “Aƒetɔ nye nye aflaga,

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: hegblɔ be, “Asi le Aƒetɔ ƒe aflaga dzi! Aƒetɔ awɔ aʋa kple Amalek tso dzidzime yi dzidzime.”

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: Ke ame aɖe ɖagblɔ na Mose be: “Kpɔ ɖa, towò Yetro kple srɔ̃wò kpakple viwò ŋutsu eveawo gbɔna ɖe gbɔwò”

english_verse: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
translation_verse: Tete Mose do yi ɖakpe toa. Ede ta agu na toa eye wògbugbɔ nu nɛ. Wobia wo nɔewo ƒe dɔdɔ ta se, eye woge ɖe agbadɔ me.

english_verse: where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ nu si katã Aƒetɔ wɔ Egipte Fiagã la kple Egiptetɔwo ɖe Israel ta la na toa. Nenema ke wòxlẽ nukpekeame siwo katã ɖe fu na wo le woƒe mɔzɔzɔa me kple ale si Aƒetɔ ɖe wo tso wo me la hã fia toa.

english_verse: Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.”
translation_verse: Fifi ko menyae be Aƒetɔ lolo wu mawuwo katã elabe eɖe dukɔ la tso Egiptetɔwo si me, esime Egiptetɔwo te wo ɖe anyi dàdatɔe la.”

english_verse: Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship. Judges Are Appointed (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Yetro, Mose to, sa numemevɔ kple vɔsa bubuwo na Mawu. Aron kple Israel-me tsitsiwo katã hã va be woaɖu nu kple Mose to le Mawu ŋkume. Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ɖoɖo (Mos V,

english_verse: You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone.
translation_verse: Ɖeɖi ate wò ŋutɔ kple ame siwo vaa gbɔwò la siaa ŋu. Dɔ la sesẽ na wò akpa; wò ɖeka màte ŋu awɔe o.

english_verse: The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, Mose bɔbɔ nɔ anyi be yeadrɔ̃ nya na dukɔ la, eye dukɔ la tsi tsitre ɖe egbɔ tso ŋdi va se ɖe fiẽ.”

english_verse: Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
translation_verse: Esi toa kpɔ dɔ gbogbo siwo le edzi na dukɔa la, ebiae be: “Nu kae nye esi wɔm nèle? Nu ka ta nèlɔ dɔ gbogbo siawo kɔ ɖe ɖokuiwò dzi? Nu ka ta wòle be wò ɖeka nàbɔbɔ nɔ anyi eye dukɔ blibo la nava tsi tsitre anɔ lalawòm tso ŋdi va se ɖe fiẽ?”

english_verse: Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do.
translation_verse: Mose ɖo eŋu na toa be: “Dukɔ la va gbɔnye be yewoabia nu Mawu.

english_verse: They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
translation_verse: Ne ʋiʋli ɖo ame aɖe kple ehavi dome hã la, wotsɔa nya la vanɛ medrɔ̃na na wo, eye meɖea Mawu ƒe seawo kple ɖoɖowo me na wo.”

english_verse: Jethro replied: That isn't the best way to do it.
translation_verse: Tete Mose to gblɔ nɛ be: “Nu si wɔm nèle la menyo o.

english_verse: God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people,
translation_verse: Azɔ ɖo tom, ne maɖo aɖaŋu na wò, eye Mawu anɔ kpli wò hã: Nye dukɔa ŋgɔnɔla le Mawu gbɔ, eye nàtsɔ woƒe nyawo anɔ Mawu ŋkume ɖom.

english_verse: and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
translation_verse: Ɖe seawo kple ɖoɖoawo me na wo, nàfia ale si wòle be woanɔ agbee kple nu siwo wòle be woawɔ la wo.

english_verse: These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier.
translation_verse: Na ame siawo nanye dukɔa ƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo koŋ. Woate ŋu atsɔ nya sesẽwo ava wò ŋutɔ gbɔwòe, ke woawo nanɔ nya kpotokpotoewo katã drɔ̃m. Ale nàɖe agba le ɖokuiwò dzi, eye woawo axɔ agba la ƒe ɖe atsɔ.

english_verse: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
translation_verse: Ne èwɔ esia abe ale si Mawu di tso asiwò ene la, wò agba la azu wodzoe, eye dukɔ blibo la adzo yi aƒeme le ŋutifafa me.”

english_verse: He chose some competent leaders from every tribe in Israel and put them over groups of
translation_verse: Etia ŋutsu zazɛ̃wo tso Israel-dukɔ blibo la dome tsɔ ɖo tatɔwo, ɖewo ɖe ame akpe nu, ɖewo ɖe alafa nu, ɖewo ɖe bla atɔ̃ nu, eye ɖewo ɖe ame ewo nu.

english_verse: They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
translation_verse: Ame siawo katã drɔ̃a ʋɔnu na dukɔ la ɣe sia ɣi, negbe nya sesẽwo ko wogatsɔna vaa Mose ŋutɔ gbɔe.

english_verse: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_verse: Emegbe Mose do mɔ toa wòtrɔ yi wo denyigba dzi.

english_verse: The Israelites left Rephidim and arrived at the desert. Then two months after leaving Egypt, they arrived at the desert near Mount Sinai, where they set up camp at the foot of the mountain. This was two months after they had left Egypt.
translation_verse: Esi woho tso Refidim la, wova Sinai-gbedadaƒo eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe gbedadaƒo la, afi mae Israel ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖo le to la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
translation_verse: Tete Mose lia to la yi Mawu gbɔ eye Aƒetɔ yɔe tso to la dzi gblɔ be: “Gblɔ na Yakob ƒe aƒe la eye nàɖe gbeƒãe na Israel-dukɔ la be:

english_verse: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
translation_verse: Miawo ŋutɔ miekpɔ nu si mewɔ Egiptetɔwo eye mekplɔ mi abe ale si hɔ̃ kɔa viawo ɖe eƒe aʋalawo dzi ene la va gbɔnyee.

english_verse: Now if you will faithfully obey me, you will be my very own people. The whole world is mine,
translation_verse: Eya ta tso azɔ heyina, ne miase nye gbe eye mialé nye nubabla me ɖe asi la, ekema mianye tɔnye koŋ le dukɔwo katã dome elabe tɔnyee nye anyigba blibo la katã.

english_verse: but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests. Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ke miawo mianye nunɔlawo ƒe fiaɖuƒe kple dukɔ kɔkɔe nam. Nya si nàgblɔ na Israelviwo la nye esia.”

english_verse: After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said,
translation_verse: Ale Mose va eye woyɔ dukɔ la ƒe ame tsitsiwo, eye wògblɔ nya siwo katã Aƒetɔ de esi la na wo.

english_verse: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
translation_verse: Dukɔ blibo la ɖo eŋu hoo be: “Nu sia nu si Aƒetɔ gblɔ ko la, míawɔe.” Mose yi ɖagblɔ woƒe ŋuɖoɖo sia na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Kpɔ ɖa, megbɔna gbɔwò le alilikpo dodo aɖe me, be ne mele nu ƒom kpli wò la, dukɔ la nasee, eye woawo hã naxɔ dziwò ase tegbee.” Ale Mose gblɔ dukɔ la ƒe nyawo na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: Once more the Lord spoke to Moses: Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Gbugbɔ yi dukɔ la gbɔ, eye nàgblɔ na wo be woatsɔ egbe kple etsɔ anya woƒe nuwo, awɔ wo ɖokui dzadzɛ.

english_verse: and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
translation_verse: Na woanɔ klalo le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe, elabe gbe ma gbe la, maɖi va Sinai-to dzi le wo katã ŋkume.

english_verse: Warn the people that they are forbidden to touch any part of the mountain. Anyone who does will be put to death,
translation_verse: Ɖo seƒe na wo godoo ƒo xlã to la, eye nàgblɔ na wo be: ‘Ame aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ aflɔ liƒo ma o. Ame aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ alia to la alo agogoe gɔ̃ hã o. Ame sia ame si ka toa ŋu la, woawui.

english_verse: either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Asi aɖeke negaka nenem me ma ŋu o; ne wòkae la, woaƒu kpee alo adae; eɖanye ame alo lã o, maganɔ agbe o.’ Ne woku lãdzokpẽ he eme didie la, eya ko hafi woalia to la.”

english_verse: After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God.
translation_verse: Ale Mose ɖi tso toa dzi va dukɔ la gbɔ, eye wòna ameawo nya woƒe awuwo, dzra ɖo, eye wowɔ wo ɖokui dzadzɛ.

english_verse: He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime. The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Egblɔ na dukɔ la be: “Kaka ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe naɖo la, ame sia ame nesu te; ame aɖeke megate ɖe nyɔnu ŋu o.”

english_verse: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke etɔ̃lia ƒe ŋdi la, dzi de asi gbeɖeɖe me, le dzo kem. Alilikpo dodo aɖe ɖiɖi ɖe to la dzi, eye kpẽ aɖe ɖi sesĩe ale gbegbe be ame siwo katã le asaɖa la me la dzo nyanyanya.

english_verse: Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Tete Mose kplɔ dukɔ la tso asaɖa la me yi Mawu kpe ge, eye wotsi tsitre ɖe toa gɔme.

english_verse: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook.
translation_verse: Dzudzɔ bla Sinai-to blibo la elabe Aƒetɔ le dzo me ɖi va toa tame. Dzudzɔ de dzi ʋĩi abe dzudzɔti me wòle dodom tso ene; to blibo la le ʋuʋum sesĩe ŋutɔ.

english_verse: The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
translation_verse: Kpẽkuku la ƒe ɖiɖi le sesẽm ɖe edzi wu. Tete Mose ƒo nu, eye Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu nɛ le dziɖegbe me.

english_verse: The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖi va Sinai-to la tame. Eyɔ Mose be neva eye Mose yi.

english_verse: Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Ɖi yi toa gɔme, ne nàxlɔ̃ nu dukɔ la be womegagbɔ liƒo la dzi, ava gbɔnye be yewoakpɔ nu o, elabe wo dometɔ geɖewo aku.

english_verse: Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
translation_verse: Na nunɔla siwo ate ɖe ŋunye hã nawɔ wo ɖokui dzadzɛ, ne Aƒetɔ magaɖe gbe ɖe wo dzi o.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
translation_verse: Mose xɔ edzi na Aƒetɔ be: “Dukɔ la mate ŋu alia Sinai-to la o, elabe wò ŋutɔ ède se na mí be: ‘Miɖe liƒo ɖe to la ŋu, eye mibui kɔkɔe.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Ɖi yi nakplɔ Aron vɛ. Gake kpɔ egbɔ be nunɔlaawo kple ameawo nagaflɔ liƒo la, alia to la, ava Aƒetɔ gbɔ o; ne menye nenema o la, aɖe gbe ɖe wo dzi.”

english_verse: After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Ale Mose ɖi yi dukɔ la gbɔ ɖagblɔ nyaawo na wo.

english_verse: God said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Mawu gblɔ nya siawo katã be:

english_verse: But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off. Idols and Altars
translation_verse: Dukɔ la tsitre ɖe adzɔge ke, esime Mose te ɖe viviti tsiɖitsiɖi si me Mawu nɔ la ŋu. Vɔsamlekpuiwo ŋuti sewo

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
translation_verse: “Nyee nye Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu, si kplɔ wò dzoe le Egipte-nyigba dzi, afi si nènye kluvi le kpɔ la.

english_verse: Do not worship any god except me.
translation_verse: “Mawu bubu aɖeke meganɔ asiwò le ŋkunye me o.

english_verse: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
translation_verse: “Mègawɔ legba aɖeke na ɖokuiwò o. Mègawɔ nu siwo le dziƒo, alo nu siwo le anyigba dzi, alo nu siwo le tsi me le anyigba te la dometɔ aɖeke ƒe nɔnɔme o.

english_verse: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
translation_verse: Gake mevea ame akpe nane siwo lɔ̃am, eye wowɔa nye sewo dzi ya nu.

english_verse: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
translation_verse: “Mègayɔ Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu ŋkɔ dzodzro o, elabe Aƒetɔ magbe tohehe na ame si yɔa eŋkɔ dzodzro la o.

english_verse: Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me.
translation_verse: “Ɖo ŋku dzudzɔgbe la dzi, ne nàwɔe kɔkɔe.

english_verse: You have six days when you can do your work,
translation_verse: Ŋkeke ade nàwɔ dɔ, eye nàwɔ ŋuwò dɔwo katã.

english_verse: but the seventh day of each week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your slaves, your animals, or the foreigners who live in your towns.
translation_verse: Ke ŋkeke adrẽlia nye dzudzɔgbe na Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la. Gbe ma gbe la, mègawɔ dɔ aɖeke o. Eɖanye wò ŋutɔ o, viwò ŋutsu o, viwò nyɔnu o; eɖanye wò dɔlaŋutsu, wò dɔlanyɔnu, lã siwo wɔa dɔ na wò alo amedzro si va dze wò du me la o.

english_verse: In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
translation_verse: Elabe ŋkeke ade mee Aƒetɔ wɔ dziƒo kple anyigba, atsiaƒu kple nu siwo katã le eme, eye wòdzudzɔ eɖokui le ŋkeke adrẽa gbe. Eya ta Aƒetɔ yra dzudzɔgbe la, eye wòwɔe kɔkɔe.

english_verse: Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
translation_verse: “Bu tɔ́wò kple nɔwò, be nànɔ agbe wòadidi le anyigba si Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu na wò la dzi.

english_verse: Do not murder.
translation_verse: “Mègawu ame o.

english_verse: Be faithful in marriage.
translation_verse: “Mègawɔ ahasi o.

english_verse: Do not steal.
translation_verse: “Mègafi fi o.

english_verse: Do not tell lies about others.
translation_verse: “Mègaɖi aʋatsoɖase ɖe hawòvi ŋuti o.

english_verse: Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else. The People Are Afraid (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: “Mègabiã ŋu ɖe hawòvi ƒe aƒe ŋu o. Mègabiã ŋu ɖe hawòvi srɔ̃, eƒe dɔlaŋutsu, eƒe dɔlanyɔnu, eƒe nyitsu alo eƒe tedzi alo nu sia nu si nye hawòvi tɔ la ƒe ɖeke ŋu o.” Vɔvɔ̃ lé amewo (Mos V,

english_verse: So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
translation_verse: Migawɔ klosalo mawuwo kpe ɖe ŋunye loo, alo miawɔ sika mawuwo na mia ɖokui o.

english_verse: The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off
translation_verse: Esi ameawo se dzi ƒe gbeɖeɖeawo kple kpẽa ƒe ɖiɖi, eye wokpɔ dzi ƒe dzokeke kple ale si to la le dzudzɔ tumee la, wovɔ̃, dzo nyànyanya eye wole tsitre ɖe adzɔge ke.

english_verse: and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na Mose be: “Wò, ƒo nu kpli mí, eye míasee; ke mègana Mawu naƒo nu kpli mí o; míava ku.”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.”
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ na wo be: “Migavɔ̃ o. Mawu ɖeko wòva be yeado mi kpɔ eye yeana vɔvɔ̃ nanɔ ye ŋu le mia dome be miagawɔ nuvɔ̃ o.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel: With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Gblɔ na Israelviwo be: ‘Miawo ŋutɔ miekpɔe! Dziƒo ke meƒo nu kpli mi tso.

english_verse: Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you.
translation_verse: Tsɔ anyi ɖi vɔsamlekpui nam, eya dzie nàtsɔ wò alẽwo kple nyitsuwo asa numemevɔ, wò ŋutifafavɔ, atsɔ alẽwo, nyitsuwo le afi sia afi si mena be woaɖo ŋku nye ŋkɔ dzi le la. Mava gbɔwò eye mayra wò.

english_verse: If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship.
translation_verse: Ne èbe yeatsɔ kpe aɖi vɔsamlekpui nam la, mègatsɔ kpe si wofú la o, elabe ne ètsɔ wò dɔwɔnu aɖe ka kpe la ŋu ko, ègblẽ kɔ ɖo nɛ.

english_verse: And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
translation_verse: Mègalia atrakpui yi nye vɔsamlekpui dzi, be wò ama me nadze le edzi o.’

english_verse: Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
translation_verse: “Ame si ke ƒo tɔ́a alo nɔa la, woawui.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for murder.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe ƒo ame wòku la, woawu eya hã.

english_verse: Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed,
translation_verse: “Ne ŋutsuwo le dzre wɔm, eye ɖeka xlã kpe ɖe evelia vevie alo tu kɔe gake meku o, ke ehavia tsi aba dzi,

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses the following laws for his people:
translation_verse: “Azɔ la, esiawo nye se siwo nàtsɔ ɖo wo ŋkume:

english_verse: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him.
translation_verse: Ne èƒle Hebritɔa aɖe kluvii la, awɔ dɔ ƒe ade. Le ƒè adrẽlia me la, adzo fe aɖeke maxee.

english_verse: If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom.
translation_verse: Nenye eya ɖekae va la, ekema eya ɖeɖe nadzo. Nenye eya kple srɔ̃ae va la, ekema eya kple srɔ̃a nadzo.

english_verse: If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
translation_verse: Nenye eƒe aƒetɔe ɖe srɔ̃ nɛ, eye srɔ̃a dzi viwo nɛ la, ekema nyɔnua kple viawo azu eƒe aƒetɔ tɔ, eye wòagblẽ wo ɖi adzo.

english_verse: But suppose the slave loves his wife and children and his owner so much that he won't leave them.
translation_verse: Ke ne kluvia gblɔ faa be: ‘Melɔ̃ nye aƒetɔ, srɔ̃nye kple vinyewo. Nyemagblẽ wo ɖi adzo o’ la,

english_verse: Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
translation_verse: ekema eƒe aƒetɔ nakplɔe va Mawu ŋkume, eye wòaŋɔ to nɛ kple nuŋɔnu le ʋɔtru alo ʋɔtruti ŋu be woasubɔe va se ɖe eƒe kugbe.

english_verse: A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does.
translation_verse: “Ne ŋutsu aɖe tsɔ via nyɔnu dzra kosii la, eya madzo abe ŋutsuwo ene o.

english_verse: If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her.
translation_verse: Nenye be eƒe nu meganyo eƒe aƒetɔ ŋu o, eye medi be yeaɖee o la, ekema ana kosia ƒe amewo nava gbugbɔe aƒle le eƒe aƒetɔ si. Aƒetɔ la mekpɔ mɔ adzrae na anyigba bubu dzi tɔ aɖeke o, elabe eble kosi la gbe eɖeɖe.

english_verse: If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
translation_verse: Ne eɖoe be yeatsɔe na ye viŋutsu ne wòaɖe la, ekema awɔ nɛ abe eya ŋutɔ via nyɔnu ene.

english_verse: If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife.
translation_verse: Ke ne egaɖe nyɔnu bubu la, megaɖe eƒe nuɖuɖu, avɔ, kple nu si wòwɔna nɛ abe srɔ̃ŋutsu ene la dzi o.

english_verse: If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it. Murder and Other Violent Crimes The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ne ŋutsua mele nu etɔ̃ siawo wɔm nɛ o la, ekema kosi la ate ŋu adzo le egbɔ faa fe aɖeke maxee. Sewo le ŋutasesẽ nuwɔwɔ ŋu

english_verse: But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside.
translation_verse: Gake ne amea meɖoe tsã be yeawu ame la o, ke wònye nu si Mawu na wòva eme to edzi la, ekema maɖo teƒe aɖe na wò afi si amewula la nate ŋu así ayi.

english_verse: If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
translation_verse: Ke ne ame aɖe ɖoe koŋ wu nɔvia to ayemɔ dzi alo le dziku me la, woahee tso nye vɔsamlekpui la gɔ̃ hã gbɔ, aɖawu.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
translation_verse: “Ame si ke ƒo fi de tɔ́a alo nɔa la, woawui.

english_verse: and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
translation_verse: eye ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe wòtea ŋu tsona tɔna ɖe ati ŋu la, ekema ameƒola la meɖi fɔ o, ke hã axe ehavia ƒe afi ɖeka tsife kple dɔyɔfewo. Anɔ edzi kpɔm va se ɖe esime eƒe lã me nasẽ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for beating to death any of your slaves.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe ƒo eƒe kluvi alo kosivi kple ati wòku ɖe esi me la, woabia hlɔ̃e.

english_verse: However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
translation_verse: Gake ne kluvia nɔ anyi ŋkeke ɖeka alo eve hafi ku la, womabia hlɔ̃ aƒetɔa o, elabe kluvia nye eƒe ga.

english_verse: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
translation_verse: “Ne ŋutsu aɖewo le avu wɔm, eye wowɔ nu vevi funɔ aɖe, eye to ema me fua ge gake naneke mewɔ nyɔnua ŋutɔ o la, nyɔnua srɔ̃ abla fe na ame si na fua ge, eye wòaxe fea abe ale si ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo kpɔ be edze la ene.

english_verse: But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life,
translation_verse: Gake ne nu vevi wɔ nyɔnua ŋutɔ la, ekema àna agbe ɖe agbe teƒe,

english_verse: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
translation_verse: ŋku ɖe ŋku teƒe, aɖu ɖe aɖu teƒe, asi ɖe asi teƒe, afɔ ɖe afɔ teƒe,

english_verse: burn for burn, cut for cut, and bruise for bruise.
translation_verse: dzobi ɖe dzobi teƒe, abi ɖe abi teƒe, kple dodro ɖe dodro teƒe.

english_verse: If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe ƒo ŋku na eƒe kluvi alo kosi eye ŋkua gbã la, ele nɛ be wòaɖe asi le eŋu ne wòazu ablɔɖeme, elabe egbã ŋku nɛ.

english_verse: The same law applies if you knock out a slave's tooth—the slave goes free.
translation_verse: Nenema ke ne eŋe aɖu na eƒe kluvi alo kosi la, ele nɛ be wòaɖe asi le eŋu wòazu ablɔɖeme ɖe aɖu la ta. Lãnyilawo ƒe dɔdeasiwo

english_verse: A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
translation_verse: “Ne nyitsu aɖe tu dzo ŋutsu aɖe alo nyɔnu aɖe wòku la, woaƒu kpe nyitsu la, eye womaɖu eƒe lã o; ke womahe to na nyi tɔ la ya o.

english_verse: Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning.
translation_verse: Ke ne nyia dina tsã be yeatu dzo ame, eye wogblɔe na nyia tɔ gake metui ɖe kpo me o, eye nyia va wu ŋutsu alo nyɔnu aɖe mlɔeba la, woaƒu kpe nyia wòaku, eye woawu nyia tɔ hã.

english_verse: pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
translation_verse: Ke ne wodo hlɔ̃fe na nyia tɔ ɖe esi woawui teƒe la, ekema ele be wòaxe fea wòade tututu abe ale si wobla nɛ ene.

english_verse: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
translation_verse: Nenye ŋutsuvi alo nyɔnuvie nyia tu dzoe wòku la, woazɔ ɖe ɖoɖo sia nu.

english_verse: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe ʋu do aɖe nu da ɖi, alo ku do aɖe, metu nu ɖe enu o, eye nyitsu alo tedzi aɖe va ge dze eme la,

english_verse: You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
translation_verse: doa tɔ naɖo eteƒe. Axe nyia alo tedzia ƒe fe na nua tɔ, eye lã kukua azu etɔ.

english_verse: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe ƒe nyitsu tu dzo ame bubu ƒe nyitsu wòku la, nyi tɔ eveawo adzra nyi si tsi agbe la, eye woama ga la; woama nyi tsu kuku la hã.

english_verse: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_verse: Ke ne nyitsua dia dzotutu ame tsã, gake nyitɔa metui ɖe kpo me o la, adi nyitsu gbagbe aɖo nyitsu kuku la teƒe, eye lã kukua azu etɔ.

english_verse: If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe fi nyitsu alo alẽ eye wòwui alo dzrae la, ele nɛ be wòaɖo nyitsu atɔ̃ nyi ɖeka la teƒe, eye alẽ ene aɖo alẽ ɖeka teƒe. Ele be wòaɖo nu si wòfi la ƒe home eteƒe. Ne naneke mele esi o la, ekema woadzrae ɖe nu si wòfi la teƒe.

english_verse: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe kplɔ eƒe lãwo yi gbeɖuƒe le eƒe anyigba dzi, alo eƒe waingble me, eye eƒe lãa yi ɖaɖu nu le ame bubu ƒe anyigba dzi alo agble me la, ele be wòadi nuku siwo eƒe lãa ɖu la ƒe nyuitɔ kekeake le eya ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi alo waingble me aɖo nu siwo eƒe lãa ɖu la teƒe.

english_verse: If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe tɔ dzo nu, eye dzoa bi yi ɖagblẽ ame bubu ƒe nuku siwo le do nu alo esiwo woxa ƒo ƒui ɖi la, ele na dzoa tɔla la be wòaxe nu siwo dzoa gblẽ la ƒe fe.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe dzra ga alo nu bubu aɖe ɖo ɖe ame gbɔ ko wova fii, eye wolé fiafitɔa la, ele na fiafitɔa be wòaxe nuawo ƒe fe ƒe teƒe eve.

english_verse: But if the thief isn't caught, some judges will decide if you are the guilty one.
translation_verse: Ne womenya ame si fi nuawo o la, ekema ame si nye aƒea tɔ la ate ɖe Mawu ŋu ava ɖee afia be eya ŋutɔe fi nuawo loo, alo menye eyae o.

english_verse: Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
translation_verse: “Ne ame eve le nane abe nyi, tedzi, alẽ, nudodo aɖe alo nane ene si bu eye wofɔe tsɔ vɛ la ʋlim la, woahe ame eveawo ayi Mawu ŋkume. Ame si Mawu bu fɔ la axe nua ƒe teƒe eve na ehavia.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe tsɔ tedzi, nyitsu, alẽ alo lã bubu aɖe ɖo ehavi gbɔ eye lãa ku, alo nu vevi aɖe wɔe, alo wokplɔe dzoe eye ame aɖeke mekpɔe o la,

english_verse: If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough.
translation_verse: ekema atà Aƒetɔ na nɔvia atsɔ fia be menya nu le lã la ƒe bubu ŋu o; ame si tɔe nye lãa la axɔ nutàta sia, eye ame si gbɔ wòtsɔ lãa ɖo hafi la maxe fe aɖeke o.

english_verse: But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it.
translation_verse: Ke nenye ɖe wofi lãa la, axee na ame si tɔe nye lã la.

english_verse: If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
translation_verse: Nenye lã wɔadã aɖee vuvui la, mina wòatsɔe ava fia wòanye ɖaseɖiɖi, eye maxe fe aɖeke ɖe lãa ta o.

english_verse: Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe ɣe ehavi ƒe nane, eye nu vevi wɔe alo wòku, esime lã tɔ meli o la, ele be wòaɖo eteƒe wòade tututu.

english_verse: But if something happens to the animal while the owner is present, you do not have to replace it. If you had leased the animal, the money you paid the owner will cover any harm done to it. Laws for Everyday Life The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ke ne nua tɔ li hafi nua dzɔ la, ekema lãɣela la maxe naneke ɖe lãa ta o. Nenye ɖe wodae na dɔwɔwɔ la, womaxɔ naneke le esi o, elabe ɖe wodae xe fe ɖe eta. Agbe nyui nɔnɔ kple mawusubɔsubɔ ŋuti sewo

english_verse: Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
translation_verse: “Ne ŋutsu aɖe ble ɖetugbi si ta womebia o, eye wòde asi eŋu la, ele nɛ be wòawɔ srɔ̃ɖenu ɖe eta eye wòaɖee.

english_verse: But if her father refuses to let her marry the man, the bride price must still be paid.
translation_verse: Ne ɖetugbia tɔ́ gbe be yematsɔe nɛ wòaɖe o la, ele na ŋutsua be wòaxe srɔ̃ɖenu siwo wowɔna ɖe ɖetugbi ta la ƒe fe na tɔ́a la.
