english_verse: so future generations will know that I made their ancestors live in shelters when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
translation_verse: ne miaƒe dzidzimeviwo natsɔ nya be esi Aƒetɔ kplɔ yewo tɔgbuiwo tso Egipte gbɔnae la, mena wonɔ agbadɔwo me. Eyae nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu.”

english_verse: This is how Moses instructed the people of Israel to celebrate the Lord's festivals.
translation_verse: Aleae Mose xlẽ ŋkekenyui siwo wòle be Israelviwo nanɔ ɖuɖum na Aƒetɔ la ŋu ɖoɖowo fia Israel-dukɔ la.

english_verse: It's possible to pay the owner for an animal that has been killed, but death is the penalty for murder.
translation_verse: Ame si wu ame aɖe ƒe lã la, ele be wòadi lã ma ƒomevi tututu aɖo eteƒe; gake ame si wu ame la, ele be woawu eya hã.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: You must supply the purest olive oil for the lamps in the sacred tent, so they will keep burning.
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na Israelviwo be woanɔ ami dzadzɛtɔ si tso amiti me la tsɔm vɛ na akaɖiawo ale be akaɖi nanɔ bibim ɣe sia ɣi.

english_verse: Use your finest flour to bake twelve loaves of bread about two kilograms each,
translation_verse: “Tsɔ wɔ memee me abolo wui eve. Ɖe sia ɖe ƒe kpekpeme nanɔ abe kilo eve ene.

english_verse: then take them into the sacred tent and lay them on the gold table in two rows of six loaves.
translation_verse: Fɔ wo ɖo kplɔ̃ si le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, kplɔ̃ si ŋu wofa sika adodoe ɖo la, dzi. Ma wo ɖe akpa eve me le kplɔ̃a dzi ale be ade nanɔ akpa ɖeka, eye ade hã nanɔ akpa ɖeka.

english_verse: Alongside each row put some pure incense that will be sent up by fire in place of the bread as an offering to me.
translation_verse: Tsɔ lifi nyuitɔ ɖo mama ɖe sia ɖe dzi. Tɔ dzo lifia ɖeɖe ne eya nanye ŋkuɖodzidzovɔsa na Aƒetɔ ɖe aboloawo teƒe.

english_verse: Aaron must lay fresh loaves on the table each Sabbath, and priests in all generations must continue this practice as part of Israel's agreement with me.
translation_verse: Dzudzɔgbe sia dzudzɔgbe la, ele be woatsɔ abolo ava ɖo Aƒetɔ ŋkume alea ɖe Israel-dukɔa nu. Israelviwo nelé nubabla sia me ɖe asi tegbee.

english_verse: This bread will always belong to Aaron and his family; it is very holy because it was offered to me, and it must be eaten in a holy place. Punishment for Cursing the Lord
translation_verse: Aboloawo nezu Aron kple via ŋutsuawo tɔ emegbe, eye teƒe kɔkɔe koe wokpɔ mɔ aɖu wo le elabe dzovɔsa si wowɔ na Aƒetɔ la ƒe akpa si le kɔkɔe ŋutɔ lae wonye. Akpa sia nenye nunɔlawo tɔ ɖaa.” Woƒu kpe ame aɖe si gblɔ busunya

english_verse: Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri from the tribe of Dan, had married an Egyptian, and they had a son. One day their son got into a fight with an Israelite man in camp and cursed the name of the Lord. So the young man was dragged off to Moses,
translation_verse: Israel-nyɔnu la viŋutsu la gblɔ busunya ɖe Ŋkɔ la ŋu eye wòdo ɖiŋu nɛ. Tete wokplɔe va Mose gbɔe. Nɔa ŋkɔ nye Selomit, ame si nye Debri vinyɔnu tso Dan-to la me.

english_verse: who had him guarded while everyone waited for the Lord to tell them what to do.
translation_verse: Wolée da ɖi va se ɖe esime woanya nu si Aƒetɔ adi be wonewɔe.

english_verse: Finally, the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: This man has cursed me! Take him outside the camp and tell the witnesses to lay their hands on his head. Then command the whole community of Israel to stone him to death.
translation_verse: “Mikplɔ busunyagblɔla la yi asaɖa la godo. Mina ame siwo katã nɔ anyi hafi wògblɔ vlodonyaawo la natsɔ asi aɖo eƒe tame, eye ameha bliboa naƒu kpee wòaku.

english_verse: And warn the others that everyone else who curses me will die in the same way, whether they are Israelites by birth or foreigners living among you.
translation_verse: Ame si gblɔ busunya ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋkɔ ŋu la, ele be woawui: Eɖanye amedzro o, eɖanye Israel vidzidzi o, ele be Israelviwo ƒe ha bliboa naƒu kpee wòaku.

english_verse: Death is also the penalty for murder,
translation_verse: Ame si wu ame la, ele be woawu eya hã.

english_verse: but the killing of an animal that belongs to someone else requires only that the animal be replaced.
translation_verse: Ame si wu ame aɖe ƒe lã la, ele be wòadi lã bubu aɖo eteƒe na amea. Agbe ɖe agbe teƒe ƒe nyae.

english_verse: Personal injuries to others must be dealt with in keeping with the crime—
translation_verse: Ne ame aɖe wɔ nu vevi aɖe ehavi la, ele be woawɔ nu vevi ma ke eya hã.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, and I demand equal justice both for you Israelites and for those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Se ɖeka ko nenɔ anyi na amedzrowo kple dumeviwo siaa, elabe nyee nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu.”

english_verse: When Moses finished speaking, the people did what the Lord had told Moses, and they stoned to death the man who had cursed the Lord.
translation_verse: Esi Mose gblɔ nya siawo na Israelviwo vɔ la, wokplɔ busunyagblɔla la yi asaɖa la godo, eye woƒu kpee wòku. Ale to esia me la, Israelviwo wɔ gbe si Aƒetɔ de asi na Mose la dzi.

english_verse: So when you buy or sell farmland, the price is to be determined by the number of crops it can produce before the next Year of Celebration. Don't try to cheat.
translation_verse: Ƒe ale sinu susɔ woagaŋe nuku le anyigbaa dzi hafi aseyetsoƒe nagaɖo lae miabu, eye miado anyigbaa ƒe asi ɖe ƒeawo ƒe agbɔsɔsɔ ŋu.

english_verse: When Moses was on Mount Sinai, the Lord told him
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose le Sinai-to dzi be: “Gblɔ na Israelviwo be:

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: After you enter the land that I am giving you, it must be allowed to rest one year out of every seven.
translation_verse: Ne mieva ɖo anyigba si metsɔ na mi dzi la, mina anyigbaa nagbɔ ɖe eme na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: You may raise grain and grapes for six years,
translation_verse: Le ƒe ade me la, miƒã nuku ɖe anyigbaa dzi, miɖe miaƒe wainkawo me, eye mixa nuku.

english_verse: but the seventh year you must let your fields and vineyards rest in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Ke ƒè adrẽlia nenye gbɔɖemeɣi blibo na anyigba la, gbɔɖemeɣi si ado kɔkɔ Aƒetɔ. Migawɔ agbledɔ aɖeke le anyigbaa dzi o. Migaɖe miaƒe wainkawo me o.

english_verse: This is to be a time of complete rest for your fields and vineyards, so don't harvest anything they produce.
translation_verse: Migaŋe nuku siwo mie le wo ɖokui si la o. Migagbe waintsetse siwo ƒe alɔwo mieké o la o. Ele be anyigbaa nagbɔ ɖe eme le ƒe ma me.

english_verse: However, you and your slaves and your hired workers, as well as any domestic or wild animals, may eat whatever grows on its own. The Year of Celebration The Lord said to his people:
translation_verse: Miaƒe aƒemelãwo kple gbemelã siwo le miaƒe gbedzi la siaa akpɔ nuɖuɖu tso eme.” Nuwo tɔtrɔ na nutɔ ƒe ƒè

english_verse: or uncle or cousin, or some other family member. In fact, if you ever get enough money, you may buy your own freedom
translation_verse: alo tɔ́a nɔvi, alo tɔ́a nɔvi ƒe vi, alo eƒe ƒometɔ kekeake aɖe kpɔ mɔ ava ɖee. Eya ŋutɔ hã kpɔ mɔ aɖe eɖokui ne ŋutete va ɖo eŋu.

english_verse: on the tenth day of the seventh month, which is also the Great Day of Forgiveness, trumpets are to be blown everywhere in the land.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti adrẽlia ƒe avuléŋkeke ewolia si nye ŋkeke gã la dzi la, woaku kpẽ atsa le anyigba blibo la katã dzi.

english_verse: This fiftieth year is sacred—it is a time of freedom and of celebration when everyone will receive back their original property, and slaves will return home to their families.
translation_verse: Woakɔ ƒe bla atɔ̃lia ŋu, eye woaɖe gbeƒã ablɔɖe na anyigba la dzi nɔlawo katã. Aseyetsoƒe wòanye na mi. Ame sia ame natrɔ axɔ eƒe nunɔamesiwo, eye ame sia ame nagatrɔ yi eƒe ƒometɔwo gbɔ.

english_verse: In this time of sacred celebration you may eat only what grows on its own.
translation_verse: Elabe aseyetsoƒe ye; mibui kɔkɔe. Miɖu nu siwo do go tso anyigba me la ko.

english_verse: During this year, all property must go back to its original owner.
translation_verse: “Le aseyetsoƒe sia me la, ame sia ame nagaxɔ eƒe nunɔamesiwo.

english_verse: If it is a long time before the next Year of Celebration, the price will be higher, because what is really being sold are the crops that the land can produce.
translation_verse: Ne ƒeawo sɔ gbɔ la, asia nekɔ; ne ƒeawo mesɔ gbɔ o la, asia nebɔbɔ; elabe le nyateƒe me la, zi ale sinu anyigbaƒlelaa le nuku ŋe ge hafi aseyetsoƒe nagaɖo la dzram wole nɛ.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, so obey me and don't cheat anyone.
translation_verse: Migaba mia nɔewo o, vɔ̃ wò Mawu la; elabe nyee nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu. Nuɖuɖukpɔkpɔ le ƒè adrẽlia me

english_verse: If you obey my laws and teachings, you will live safely in the land and enjoy its abundant crops.
translation_verse: Anyigba la anyo nu, miakpɔ nuɖuɖu fũu aɖu, eye mianɔ dedie le edzi.

english_verse: Don't ever worry about what you will eat during the seventh year when you are forbidden to plant or harvest.
translation_verse: Ɖewohĩ miabia be: ‘Ne míekpɔ mɔ aƒã nu alo aŋe nu le ƒè adrẽlia me o ɖe, nu ka ɖu ge míala le ƒe ma me?’

english_verse: I will see to it that you harvest enough in the sixth year to last for three years.
translation_verse: Mayra anyigbaa le ƒè adelia me ale gbegbe be nuɖuɖu si wòana le ƒè ma me la ade ƒè etɔ̃ tɔ nu.

english_verse: In the eighth year you will live on what you harvested in the sixth year, but in the ninth year you will eat what you plant and harvest in the eighth year.
translation_verse: Ne mieƒã nu le ƒè enyilia me la, nu si mieŋe le ƒè adelia me ƒe ɖe aganɔ anyi mianɔ ɖuɖum va se ɖe esime miaxa ƒè enyilia me nukuwo hã, anɔ eɖum va ke ɖe ƒè asieke hã me. Anyigbatɔtrɔ na anyigbaa tɔ.

english_verse: No land may be permanently bought or sold. It all belongs to me—it isn't your land, and you only live there for a little while.
translation_verse: “Miekpɔ mɔ adzra anyigba aɖeke na ame be nezu etɔ gbidii o, elabe menye miawo tɔe nye anyigba o; tɔnyee. Miawo la, amedzrowo kple gbɔnyedzelawo mienye.

english_verse: When property is being sold, the original owner must be given the first chance to buy it.
translation_verse: Eya ta woagagbugbɔ anyigbawo axɔ le miaƒe anyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: If any of you Israelites become so poor that you are forced to sell your property, your closest relative must buy it back,
translation_verse: “Ne nya wu Israelvi aɖe, eye wòdzra eƒe anyigba la, ele na ame si do ƒome kplii wu keŋkeŋ la be wòayi aɖaxɔ anyigba la aƒle le ame si wodzrae na la si.

english_verse: if that relative has the money. Later, if you can afford to buy it,
translation_verse: Ne eva eme be eƒe ƒometɔ aɖeke meli si ava xɔ anyigbaa ƒle nɛ o, ko dzɔgbenyuitɔe eya ŋutɔ va kpɔ ga ate ŋu aƒlee la,

english_verse: you must pay enough to make up for what the present owner will lose on it before the next Year of Celebration, when the property would become yours again.
translation_verse: ƒe ale sinu susɔ ne gbɔɖemeƒe nagaɖo la ƒe agbɔsɔsɔe woatsɔ abu ga home si wòle be wòaxe hafi agaxɔ anyigbaa, eye ne exee ko, anyigbaa gazu etɔ.

english_verse: But if you don't have the money to pay the present owner a fair price, you will have to wait until the Year of Celebration, when the property will once again become yours.
translation_verse: Ne ga mele esi de home si wòle be wòaxe nu o la, anyigbaa anɔ ame si ƒlee la si me va se ɖe esime gbɔɖemeƒe nagaɖo, ekema anyigbaa agatrɔ zu anyigbatɔ la tɔ.

english_verse: If you sell a house in a walled city, you have only one year in which to buy it back.
translation_verse: “Ne aƒe le ame aɖe si le du aɖe si woɖo gli ƒo xlã la me, eye wòdzrae la, ekpɔ mɔ agagbugbɔe axɔ ƒle le ame si wòdzrae na la si hafi ƒe ɖeka nava yi.

english_verse: If you don't buy it back before that year is up, it becomes the permanent property of the one who bought it, and it will not be returned to you in the Year of Celebration.
translation_verse: Ne megbugbɔe xɔ ƒle o kaka ƒe ɖeka va yi la, ekema mekpɔ mɔ agaxɔ aƒe si le du si me ŋu woɖo gli ɖo la ƒle emegbe o. Aƒea azu ame si wòdzrae na la kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo tɔ ɖikaa. Ne aseyetsoƒe gaɖo hã, womazi wo dzi be woaɖe asi le eŋu o.

english_verse: But a house out in a village may be bought back at any time just like a field. And it must be returned to its original owner in the Year of Celebration.
translation_verse: Gake nenye du aɖe si womeɖo gli ƒo xlã o la me aƒea le la, ekema eya hã ŋunya sɔ kple agblenyigba tɔ: Aƒea tɔ xoxoa kpɔ mɔ agbugbɔe axɔ ƒle le ame si wòdzrae na la si. Ne magbugbɔe axɔ ƒle o la, ele be woatrɔe nɛ ne aseyetsoƒe bubu gaɖo.

english_verse: If any Levites own houses inside a walled city, they will always have the right to buy them back.
translation_verse: Gake Levitɔ ya kpɔ mɔ agbugbɔ axɔ eƒe nu si wòdzra le Levi-du me la aƒle ɣe sia ɣi si wòlɔ̃.

english_verse: And any houses that they do not buy back will be returned to them in the Year of Celebration, because these homes are their permanent property among the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Nenye Levitɔe dzra aƒea le Levi-du aɖe me, eye meva gbugbɔ xɔe ƒle o hã, ne aseyetsoƒe ɖo ko, ele be woatrɔe nɛ. Ele be woawɔ esia elabe, le Israel-dukɔ me, ne aƒe aɖe nye Levitɔ tɔ le Levi-du me ko, ele be wòanye etɔ ɖikaa.

english_verse: No pastureland owned by the Levi tribe can ever be sold; it is their permanent possession. Help for the Poor The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ame aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ adzra Levi-du ƒe tonyigba aɖeke o; ele be anyigba mawo nanye Levi viwo tɔ tegbee.” Kpekpeɖeŋunana hiãtɔwo

english_verse: If any of your people become poor and unable to support themselves, you must help them, just as you are supposed to help foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: “Ne nɔviwò aɖe zu ame dahe ale gbegbe be megate ŋu le eɖokui nyim o la, xɔe nàkpɔ edzi abe amedzro ene ne wòanɔ gbɔwò.

english_verse: Don't take advantage of them by charging any kind of interest or selling them food for profit. Instead, honor me by letting them stay where they now live.
translation_verse: Ne èdo ga nɛ la, mègaxɔ deme ɖe edzi o. Ne èdo nuɖuɖu nɛ la, mègaxɔ xɔɖedzi le esi o.

english_verse: Remember—I am the Lord your God! I rescued you from Egypt and gave you the land of Canaan, so that I would be your God.
translation_verse: Nyee nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu; nyee kplɔ mi tso Egipte-nyigba dzi vɛ, be matsɔ Kanaan-nyigba ana mi, eye manye mia Mawu. Ablɔɖenana kluviwo

english_verse: Suppose some of your people become so poor that they have to sell themselves and become your slaves.
translation_verse: Ne nya wu nɔviwò Israelvi aɖe ale gbegbe be wòtsɔ eɖokui va de awɔba me na wò la, mègana eƒe agbenɔnɔ le tewò nanye kluvigbenɔnɔ o.

english_verse: Then you must treat them as servants, rather than as slaves. And in the Year of Celebration they are to be set free,
translation_verse: Na wòanɔ gbɔwò abe apadɔ ko wɔm wòva le na wò, alo amedzro ko wònye va dze wò ene, eye wòanɔ anyi va se ɖe esime aseyetsoƒe nagaɖo.

english_verse: I brought them out of Egypt to be my servants, not to be sold as slaves.
translation_verse: Elabe Israelviwo la, Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔlawo wonye wòkplɔ tso Egipte vɛ; eya ta ame aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ adzra wo o.

english_verse: So obey me, and don't be cruel to the poor.
translation_verse: Migasẽ ŋuta le wo ŋu o; ke boŋ vɔ̃ wò Mawu la.

english_verse: If you want slaves, buy them from other nations
translation_verse: Ne miehiã kluviwo kple kosiwo la, miate ŋu aƒle wo tso dukɔ siwo ƒo xlã mi la me.

english_verse: or from the foreigners who live in your own country, and make them your property.
translation_verse: Miekpɔ mɔ aƒle amedzro siwo le mia dome la hã. Nenema ke miekpɔ mɔ aƒle wo vi siwo wodzi le miaƒe anyigba dzi la be woanye mia tɔ.

english_verse: You can own them, and even leave them to your children when you die, but do not make slaves of your own people or be cruel to them.
translation_verse: Ne èku la, woate ŋu azu domenyinu na viwò ŋutsuwo anɔ wo subɔm va se ɖe ku me. Israelvi aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ awɔ funyafunya nɔvia Israelvi o.

english_verse: Even if some of you Israelites become so much in debt that you must sell yourselves to foreigners in your country,
translation_verse: “Ne amedzro alo gbɔwò nɔla aɖe va zu kesinɔtɔ, eye nɔviwò si le egbɔ va da ahe hedzra eɖokui na amedzroa alo gbɔwò nɔla la alo amedzro la ƒe ƒometɔ aɖe la,

english_verse: you still have the right to be set free by a relative, such as a brother
translation_verse: ekema ne wodzrae vɔ la, nɔviawo dometɔ ɖeka ate ŋu ava ɖee loo,

english_verse: And even while you are the slaves of foreigners in your own country, your people must make sure that you are not mistreated.
translation_verse: Ne egatsi eƒe aƒetɔa gbɔ la, ele be aƒetɔa nabui ko abe ame aɖe si va le ƒedɔ wɔm le ye gbɔ ene, eye aƒetɔa mekpɔ mɔ asẽ ŋuta le eŋu o.

english_verse: If you cannot gain your freedom in any of these ways, both you and your children will still be set free in the Year of Celebration.
translation_verse: Ne womeva ɖee le awɔbaa me to mɔ siawo ƒe ɖeke dzi o la, ekema ne aseyetsoƒe gaɖo ko ele na eƒe aƒetɔ be wòana ablɔɖe eya ŋutɔ kple viawo siaa.

english_verse: People of Israel, I am the Lord your God, and I brought you out of Egypt to be my own servants.
translation_verse: Elabe le gonyeme la, Israelviwo la, nye dɔlawo wonye; nye dɔlawo wonye mekplɔ dzoe le Egipte-nyigba dzi. Nyee nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu.

english_verse: Respect the Sabbath and honor the place where I am worshiped, because I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Milé nye dzudzɔgbewo ŋu ɖoɖowo me ɖe asi pɛpɛpɛ, eye sosroɖa nenɔ mia me ɖe nye kɔkɔeƒe la ŋu. Nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: and I will send rain to make your crops grow and your trees produce fruit.
translation_verse: mana tsi nadza na mi nyuie le edzaɣiwo ale be anyigbaa awɔ nu, eye kutsetsetiwo atse.

english_verse: I will bless your country with peace, and you will rest without fear. I will wipe out the dangerous animals and protect you from enemy attacks.
translation_verse: Mana mia ŋu nafa le anyigbaa dzi ale be miamlɔ anyi bɔkɔɔ eye naneke mado vɔvɔ̃ na mi o. Maɖe gbemelã vɔ̃ɖiwo ɖa le anyigbaa dzi eye yi mato miaƒe anyigba dzi o.

english_verse: You will chase and destroy your enemies,
translation_verse: Mianyà miaƒe futɔwo ɖe du nu, eye woatsi miaƒe yi nu.

english_verse: I will treat you with such kindness that your nation will grow strong, and I will also keep my promises to you.
translation_verse: Matrɔ ɖe mia ŋu, ana miadzi fũu. Mawɔ nubabla si mewɔ kpli mi la dzi.

english_verse: I will live among you and never again look on you with disgust.
translation_verse: Mia domee nye agbadɔ si nye nye nɔƒe koŋ la lanɔ; nyemasa ɖokuinye ɖe aga tso mia gbɔ o.

english_verse: I will walk with you—I will be your God, and you will be my people.
translation_verse: Mazɔ mia dome. Manye mia Mawu, eye mianye nye dukɔ.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, and I rescued you from Egypt, so that you would never again be slaves. I have set you free; now walk with your heads held high. Punishment for Disobeying the Lord The Lord said:
translation_verse: Nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawue kplɔ mi dzoe le Egipte be miado le kluvinyenye la me. Meŋe kɔkuti si nɔ kɔ na mi la ale be miete ŋu dzɔ ka azɔ hafi le yiyim. Tomaɖomaɖo ŋu tohehewo

english_verse: I will punish you terribly, and you will be ruined. You will be struck with incurable diseases and with fever that leads to blindness and depression. Your enemies will eat the crops you plant,
translation_verse: mawɔ nu siawo mi: matsɔ dɔléle agblẽ mia dome. Kpedɔ kple asrã ana miaƒe ŋkutomewo anyè ɖe eme. Mianɔ ku ɖim vivivi, anɔ zuzum belii va se ɖe esime miaku. Miaƒã nuku baa gake dɔ vlo ko wòanye miawɔ elabe futɔwo ava ɖu mia dzi, eye woawo koe laɖu miaƒe nukuawo.

english_verse: and I will turn from you and let you be destroyed by your attackers. You will even run at the very rumor of attack.
translation_verse: Maɖe ŋku atɔ mi. Ne miekpe aʋa kple futɔwo la, woafiti mi. Ame siwo lé fu mi helihelĩ lae lava zu miaƒe aƒetɔwo. Nu ate mia ŋu ale gbegbe be ne ame aɖeke meƒu du kplɔ mi ɖo o hã, sisím ko mianɔ.

english_verse: Then, if you still refuse to obey me, I will punish you seven times for each of your sins,
translation_verse: Ne nu siawo katã va mia dzi gake miegagbe godoo be yewomaɖo tom o la, ekema magafiã nu ɖe eme na mi wu zigbɔzi adrẽ le miaƒe nuvɔ̃wo ta.

english_verse: until your pride is completely crushed. I will hold back the rain, so the sky above you will be like iron, and the ground beneath your feet will be like copper.
translation_verse: Be matu afɔ miaƒe ŋusẽ ma si ta miele dàdam ɖo la dzi, mana tsi magadza na mi o; dziƒo si le mia tame la asesẽ abe ga yibɔ ene, eye miaƒe anyigba hã alia abe akɔbli ene.

english_verse: All of your hard work will be for nothing—and there will be no harvest of grain or fruit.
translation_verse: Miawɔ dɔ sesĩe gake naneke mado tso miaƒe kutrikuku la me o, elabe miaƒe anyigba magawɔ nu o, eye miaƒe atiwo magatse ku o.

english_verse: If you keep rebelling against me, I'll punish you seven times worse, just as your sins deserve!
translation_verse: “Ne miaƒe azɔli gatsi tre ɖe ŋunye ko, eye miegagbe godoo be yewomaɖo tom o la, magadzi miaƒe tohehe ɖe edzi zigbɔzi adrẽ.

english_verse: I'll send wild animals to attack you, and they will gobble up your children and livestock. So few of you will be left that your roads will be deserted.
translation_verse: Mana lã wɔadãwo ava ɖo mia dome awu mia viwo, atsrɔ̃ miaƒe aƒemelãwo. Woana miaƒe agbɔsɔsɔ dzi aɖe kpɔtɔ ale gbegbe be ame siwo anɔ miaƒe mɔwo dzi zɔm la magade naneke o, eye miaƒe mɔwo ato gbe.

english_verse: I'll remain your enemy and punish you even worse.
translation_verse: ekema nye hã magabla ali dzi ɖe mia ŋu, eye mana miaƒe tohehe nagasesẽ ɖe edzi zigbɔzi adrẽ.

english_verse: War will break out because you broke our agreement, and if you escape to your walled cities, I'll punish you with horrible diseases, and you will be captured by your enemies.
translation_verse: Mahe aʋa ava miaƒe dukɔa dzi atsɔ bia hlɔ̃ mi, le esi mietu nu si nye kpli mi míebla la ta. Ne miesí aʋa gidigidi yi ɖabè ɖe miaƒe duwo me la, mahe dɔ vɔ̃ si wua ame geɖe fũu gbe sia gbe la ava ƒu mia dome kpoyi eye miaƒe futɔwo ƒe asi asu mia dzi.

english_verse: You will have such a shortage of bread, that ten women will be able to bake their bread in the same oven. Each of you will get only a few crumbs, and you will go hungry.
translation_verse: Ne mena nuɖuɖu le vevem la, nyɔnu ewo amè abolo le abolokpo ɖeka me. Woaxlẽ aboloa ɖe dɔme na mi, made afi aɖeke na mi o.

english_verse: I'll really get furious and punish you terribly for your sins!
translation_verse: nye ŋku abiã ɖe mia ŋu vevie, eye nye ŋutɔ mana miaƒe tohehe agasesẽ ɖe edzi zigbɔzi adrẽ le miaƒe nuvɔ̃wo ta.

english_verse: In fact, you will be so desperate for food that you will eat your own children.
translation_verse: Dɔ ato le mia gbɔ ale gbegbe be mialé miawo ŋutɔ mia viŋutsuwo kple vinyɔnuwo aɖa ɖu.

english_verse: I'll destroy your shrines and tear down your incense altars, leaving your dead bodies piled on top of your idols. And you will be disgusting to me.
translation_verse: Magbã miaƒe trɔ̃xɔ mawo mietu ɖe towo dzi, akaka miaƒe lifivɔsamlekpuiawo, alɔ miaƒe ame kukuwo ali kɔ ɖe miaƒe legba gbagbãwo dzi, eye matsri mi keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: I'll wipe out your towns and your places of worship and will no longer be pleased with the smell of your sacrifices.
translation_verse: Magbã miaƒe duwo ale be woazu glikpowo. Mana miaƒe teƒe kɔkɔewo aɖi gbɔlo, eye magbe nyemagase miaƒe numemevɔsawo ƒe ʋeʋẽ lílilĩ o.

english_verse: Your land will become so desolate that even your enemies who settle there will be shocked when they see it.
translation_verse: Magblẽ miaƒe anyigba kple edzinuwo keŋkeŋ ale gbegbe be ne miaƒe futɔwo, ame siwo ava zu edzinɔlawo, va ke ɖe eŋu la, woƒe nu aku.

english_verse: After I destroy your towns and ruin your land with war, I'll scatter you among the nations.
translation_verse: Mana futɔwo ava dze mia dzi, afiti mi, eye maka mi ahlẽ ɖe dzronyigba vovovowo dzi. Miaƒe anyigba dzi aɖi ƒuƒlu, eye miaƒe duwo agbã gudugudu.

english_verse: While you are prisoners in foreign lands, your own land will enjoy years of rest and refreshment, as it should have done each seventh year when you lived there.
translation_verse: Agbɔ ɖe eme le ɣeyiɣi siwo katã me wònye gbegbe, elabe tso esime miele edzi la, megbɔ ɖe eme le miaƒe dzudzɔɣiwo me alea kpɔ o.

english_verse: In the land of your enemies, you will tremble at the rustle of a leaf, as though it were a sword. And you will become so weak that you will stumble and fall over each other, even when no one is chasing you.
translation_verse: Woalɔ wo nɔewo aƒu anyi abe yi nu wole sisím le ene, togbɔ be ame aɖeke mekplɔ woɖo o hã. Miagate ŋu anɔ te ɖe miaƒe futɔwo nu o.

english_verse: Many of you will die in foreign lands,
translation_verse: Miatsrɔ̃ ɖe dzrowo de, eye miaƒe futɔwo ƒe anyigbae ami mi.

english_verse: and others of you will waste away in sorrow as the result of your sins and the sins of your ancestors.
translation_verse: Mia dometɔ ʋɛ siwo atsi agbe le miaƒe futɔwo de la axa nu aɖiku glãlɛɛ le afi ma le woawo ŋutɔ ƒe nuvɔ̃wo kple wo tɔgbuiwo tɔwo siaa ta.” Ke hã, mɔkpɔkpɔ li.

english_verse: Then suppose you realize that I turned against you and brought you to the land of your enemies because both you and your ancestors had stubbornly sinned against me. If you humbly confess what you have done and start living right,
translation_verse: ale be nye hã metsi tre ɖe wo ŋu hekplɔ wo va woƒe futɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi la, ne woƒe bolodziwo bɔbɔ wo ɖokui eye woɖɔ woƒe vodadawo ɖo la,

english_verse: I'll keep the promise I made to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will bless your land
translation_verse: ekema magaɖo ŋku nu, si mebla kple Yakob, Isak kple Abraham la dzi, eye maɖo ŋku anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: and let it rest during the time that you are in a foreign country, paying for your rebellion against me and my laws.
translation_verse: Ke, ele be woagblẽ anyigba la ɖi be wòakpɔ gbɔdzɔe esime wòle ƒuƒlu eye womele edzi o la. Ele be woaɖɔ woƒe vodadawo ɖo elabe wogbe nye ɖoɖowo eye woƒe luʋɔwo nyɔ ŋu nye seawo.

english_verse: No matter what you have done, I am still the Lord your God, and I will never completely reject you or become absolutely disgusted with you there in the land of your enemies.
translation_verse: Gake le ɣeyiɣi ma si me wole woƒe futɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi hã la, nyemaɖe nu le woƒe nya me keŋkeŋ o, eye nyemanyɔ ŋu wo be matsrɔ̃ wo keŋkeŋ ahatu nye nu, si mebla kpli wo la o, elabe nyee nye Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu.

english_verse: While nations watched, I rescued your ancestors from Egypt so that I would be their God. Yes, I am your Lord, and I will never forget our agreement.
translation_verse: Ke boŋ maxa ɖe wo ta aɖo ŋku nu si mebla kple wo tɔgbuiwo la dzi, wo tɔgbui siwo mekplɔ dzoe le Egipte, dukɔwo katã kpɔ, be nye Aƒetɔ, manye woƒe Mawu la.”

english_verse: Moses was on Mount Sinai when the Lord gave him these laws and teachings for the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Esiawoe nye ɖoɖowo, sewo kple mɔnufiame siwo Aƒetɔ ɖo anyi ɖe eya kple Israelviwo dome to Mose dzi le Sinai-to la dzi.

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If you ever want to free someone who has been promised to me,
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na Israelviwo be, ne ŋutsu aɖe tsɔ ame ɖe adzɔgbe tɔxɛ na Aƒetɔ la, le wò akɔntabubu nu la,

english_verse: you may do so by paying the following amounts, weighed according to the official standards:
translation_verse: Ne amea xɔ ƒe bla ade heyi la, ŋutsu ƒe asi nanye klosaloga wui atɔ̃, eye nyɔnu naxɔ klosaloga ewo.

english_verse: Ten percent of everything you harvest is holy and belongs to me, whether it grows in your fields or on your fruit trees.
translation_verse: “Nu siwo katã dona tsoa anyigba me la katã ƒe ewoliawo ɖeka nye Aƒetɔ tɔ: agblemenuwo kple kutsetsewo siaa. Wonye nu kɔkɔe na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: If you try to substitute any other animal, no matter how good, for the one you promised, they will both become holy and must be sacrificed.
translation_verse: ame aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ atsɔ bubu aɖeke aɖɔlii o. Ne lã bubu sia nyo wui alo menyo de enu o hã, womekpɔ mɔ atsɔe ɖɔlii o. Ne ehiã kokoko be woaɖɔlii le nane ta, eye woɖɔlii la, ekema woabu lã eveawo be wozu nu kɔkɔewo.

english_verse: If you have promised to give someone to me and can't afford to pay the full amount for that person's release, you will be taken to a priest, and he will decide how much you can afford.
translation_verse: Ne ame si ɖe adzɔgbea nye numanɔsitɔ ale be mate ŋu akpɔ ga home si hiã axe o la, ekema ele nɛ be wòakplɔ ame si wòtsɔ ɖe adzɔgbea la ayi nunɔla gbɔ, eye nunɔlaa ado asi aɖe si bɔbɔ wu ale be adzɔgbeɖelaa ate ŋu axee la ɖe eŋu.”

english_verse: If you promise to sacrifice an animal to me, it becomes holy, and there is no way you can set it free.
translation_verse: Nenye lã siwo wotsɔna saa vɔ na Aƒetɔ la ƒe ɖee wòtsɔ ɖe adzɔgbea la, ekema lãa zu lã kɔkɔe;

english_verse: Donkeys are unfit for sacrifice, so if you promise me a donkey, you must bring it to the priest,
translation_verse: Nenye lã makɔmakɔ aɖee nye lã si wotsɔ ɖe adzɔgbea ale be womate ŋu atsɔe sa vɔ na Aƒetɔ o la, ekema ele na adzɔgbeɖelaa be wòatsɔe va nunɔla gbɔ.

english_verse: But if you want to buy it back, you must pay an additional
translation_verse: Ne ame si tsɔe vɛ di be yeagbugbɔ xɔe ƒle la, ele nɛ be wòaxe eƒe asi ƒe atɔ̃liawo ɖeka akpe ɖe asia ŋu.

english_verse: If you promise part of your family's land to me, its value must be determined by the amount of seed needed to plant the land, and the rate will be ten pieces of silver for every
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe kɔ eƒe anyigba si ƒe dome wònyi ƒe akpa aɖe ŋu na Aƒetɔ la, nuku ale sinu woate ŋu aƒã ɖe edzi la dzie woakpɔ hafi ado asi ɖe eŋu. Nenye lu kilo bla eve woate ŋu aƒã ɖe edzi la, ekema ele be eƒe home nanye klosaloga ewo; nenye lu kilo alafa etɔ̃ woate ŋu aƒã ɖe edzi la, ekema ele be eƒe home nanye klosaloga bla atɔ̃.

english_verse: If this promise is made in the Year of Celebration, the land will be valued at the full price.
translation_verse: Nenye ƒe si va ɖe aseyetsoƒe yome teti mee wòkɔ anyigbaa ŋu la, ekema asi si nunɔlaa yɔ la kokoko wòle be wòaxe.

english_verse: But any time after that, the price will be figured according to the number of years before the next Year of Celebration.
translation_verse: Ne aseyetsoƒe va yi hafi wòkɔ eƒe agblea ŋu na Aƒetɔ la, ekema ƒe ale sinu susɔ hafi aseyetsoƒe bubu nagaɖo la dzie nunɔlaa lakpɔ hafi anya afi si wòaɖe agblea ƒe asi dzi ava se.

english_verse: If you decide to buy back the land, you must pay the price plus an additional
translation_verse: Ne agblea tɔ di be yeagbugbɔ agblea ƒle la, ele nɛ be wòaxe home si nunɔla do ɖe eŋu, agaxe home ma ƒe atɔ̃liawo ɖeka akpee eye wòaxɔe wòanye etɔ.

english_verse: When the Year of Celebration comes, the land becomes holy because it belongs to me, and it will be given to the priests.
translation_verse: Ke ne aseyetsoƒe gaɖo ko, agblea trɔ zu Aƒetɔ tɔ keŋkeŋ, eye to ema me la, ezu nunɔlawo katã tɔ gbidii.

english_verse: its value will be decided by a priest, according to the number of years before the next Year of Celebration, and the money you pay will be mine.
translation_verse: nunɔla akpɔ ƒe ale sinu susɔ ne aseyetsoƒe nagaɖo la dzi ɖa hafi ado asi ɖe eŋu, eye ele na agblea tɔ be wòaxe fea gbe ma gbe ke; ekema gaa zu Aƒetɔ ƒe ga.

english_verse: However, on the next Year of Celebration, the land will go back to the family of its original owner.
translation_verse: Gake ne aseyetsoƒe gaɖo ko, ele be woatrɔ agblea na ame si si woƒlee le gbã, ame si ƒe domenyinu wònye la,

english_verse: Every price will be set by the official standards. Various Offerings The Lord said:
translation_verse: woabu asi ɖe sia ɖe ɖe kɔkɔeƒe la ƒe klosalogakɔnta nu; gera bla eve nanye klosaloga ɖeka.

english_verse: All first-born animals of your flocks and herds are already mine, and so you cannot promise any of them to me.
translation_verse: “Ke lãwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo nye Aƒetɔ tɔ tsã xoxo eya ta ame aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ akɔ lã aɖeke ƒe ŋgɔgbevi ŋu na Aƒetɔ o.

english_verse: In fact, any humans who have been promised to me in this way must be put to death.
translation_verse: Nenye amegbetɔ ŋutɔ kura gɔ̃e hã, ame aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ agbugbɔe ƒle o; ɖeko woawui.

english_verse: If you want to buy back this part of your harvest, you may do so by paying what it is worth plus an additional
translation_verse: Ne ame aɖe di be yeagbugbɔ eƒe akpa aɖe aƒle la, ele be wòaxe akpa si wòdi be yeaƒle la ƒe home kple home ma ƒe atɔ̃liawo ɖeka.

english_verse: When you count your flocks and herds, one out of ten of every newborn animal is holy and belongs to me,
translation_verse: Ne èle wò lãwo – le kpɔɖeŋu me – nyiwo, alẽwo kple gbɔ̃wo xlẽm la, de dzesi lã ewolia sia ewolia si dzi nàɖo la; ele kɔkɔe na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: Moses was on Mount Sinai when the Lord gave him these laws for the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Esiawoe nye se siwo Aƒetɔ wɔ na Mose le Sinai-to dzi be wòayi aɖade na Israelviwo.

english_verse: The people of Israel had left Egypt and were living in the Sinai Desert. Then on the first day of the second month of the second year, when Moses was in the sacred tent the Lord said:
translation_verse: Esi Israelviwo ʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi le ƒe eve megbe la, Aƒetɔ ƒo nu kple Mose le ɣleti evelia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi le godoƒegbadɔ me le Sinai-gbedadaƒo. Egblɔ nɛ be:

english_verse: I want you and Aaron to find out how many people are in each of Israel's clans and families. And make a list of all the men
translation_verse: Mitia ame siwo xɔ ƒe bla eve kple vɔ, eye woate ŋu ade aʋa la miaxlẽ hamehame.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron, together with these twelve tribal leaders,
translation_verse: Mose kple Aron tsɔ ŋutsu siawo, siwo woyɔ la,

english_verse: called together the people that same day. They were counted according to their clans and families. Then Moses and the others listed the names of the men twenty years and older,
translation_verse: eye le ɣleti evelia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la, woƒo ƒu ameha blibo la ɖekae. Wode ame siwo xɔ ƒe bla ene kple vɔ la ŋkɔwo dzidzimegbalẽ me ɖekaɖeka le woƒe ƒomewo kple woƒe aƒekɔwo nu,

english_verse: The people of Israel did everything the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo wɔ nu sia nu pɛpɛpɛ abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose ene.

english_verse: But the Levites will camp around the sacred tent to make sure that no one goes near it and makes me furious with the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ke Levi viwo ya naƒu asaɖa anyi aƒo xlã agbadɔ si me se la le la godoo, eye woadzɔ eŋu le ɖoɖoawo nu, ale be ame aɖeke nagate ɖe eŋu, eye mado dɔmedzoe ɖe Israel-ha blibo la ŋu o.”

english_verse: But those from the Levi tribe were not included
translation_verse: Ke womexlẽ Levi viwo ya ŋlɔ kpe ɖe Israel-to bubuawo ŋu o,

english_verse: because the Lord had said to Moses:
translation_verse: elabe Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: When you count the Israelites, do not include those from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: “Ne èle ameawo xlẽm la, mègaxlẽ Levi viwo ya de to bubuawo ƒe xexlẽme me o.

english_verse: Instead, give them the job of caring for the sacred tent, its furnishings, and the objects used for worship. They will camp around the tent, and whenever you move, they will take it down, carry it to the new camp, and set it up again. Anyone else who tries to go near it must be put to death.
translation_verse: Ne miele hoho ge le teƒe aɖe la, Levi viwo nakaka agbadɔ la atsɔ, eye ne mieɖo nɔƒe si mianɔ la, woawo natui. Evɔ ne ame bubu aɖe te ɖe agbadɔa ŋu la, wonewui.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites will camp in their own groups and under their own banners.
translation_verse: Israelvi bubuawo naƒu asaɖa anyi hamehame ɖe woƒe nɔƒewo le woƒe aflagawo gbɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose kple Aron be:

english_verse: how the Israelites should arrange their camp: Each tribe must set up camp under its own banner and under the flags of its ancestral families. These camps will be arranged around the sacred tent, but not close to it.
translation_verse: “Ne Israelviwo ƒu asaɖa anyi la, to sia to nanɔ aflaga si nye wo tɔ́wo ƒe to ƒe dzesi la gbɔ, eye woaƒo xlã adze ŋgɔ godoƒegbadɔ la godoo.

english_verse: Judah and the tribes that march with it must set up camp on the east side of the sacred tent, under their own banner. The
translation_verse: ame si ƒe aʋawɔlawo le ame akpe bla adrẽ vɔ ene alafa ade.

english_verse: On one side of Judah will be the tribe of Issachar, with Nethanel son of Zuar as the leader of its
translation_verse: ame si ƒe aʋawɔlawo le ame akpe bla atɔ̃ vɔ ene alafa ene.

english_verse: On the other side will be the tribe of Zebulun, with Eliab son of Helon as the leader of its
translation_verse: ame si ƒe aʋawɔlawo le ame akpe bla atɔ̃ vɔ adrẽ alafa ene.

english_verse: Reuben and the tribes that march with it must set up camp on the south side of the sacred tent, under their own banner. The
translation_verse: ame si ƒe aʋawɔlawo le ame akpe bla ene vɔ ade alafa atɔ̃.

english_verse: On one side of Reuben will be the tribe of Simeon, with Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai as the leader of its
translation_verse: ame si ƒe aʋawɔlawo le ame akpe bla atɔ̃ vɔ asieke alafa etɔ̃.

english_verse: On the other side will be the tribe of Gad, with Eliasaph son of Deuel as the leader of its
translation_verse: ame si ƒe aʋawɔlawo le ame akpe bla ene vɔ atɔ̃ alafa ade bla atɔ̃.

english_verse: Marching behind Reuben will be the Levites, arranged in groups, just as they are camped. They will carry the sacred tent and their own banners.
translation_verse: “Azɔ la, Levi viwo natsɔ godoƒegbadɔ la anɔ hatsotso gbãtɔ eveawo kple mlɔetɔ eveawo titina. Hatsotso ɖe sia ɖe naho le ɖoɖo sinu woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖo me, eye ame sia ame nanɔ eteƒe le eƒe aflaga gbɔ.

english_verse: On one side of Ephraim will be the tribe of Manasseh, with Gamaliel son of Pedahzur as the leader of its
translation_verse: ame si ƒe aʋawɔlawo le ame akpe bla etɔ̃ vɔ eve alafa eve.

english_verse: So all the Israelites in the camp were counted according to their ancestral families. The troops were arranged by divisions and totaled
translation_verse: Ame siwo katã woxlẽ le asaɖaawo me le Israelviwo dome, hatsotso hatsotso la, ƒe xexlẽme nye akpe alafa ade kple etɔ̃ alafa atɔ̃ bla atɔ̃.

english_verse: On the other side will be the tribe of Benjamin, with Abidan son of Gideoni as the leader of its
translation_verse: ame si ƒe aʋawɔlawo le ame akpe bla etɔ̃ vɔ atɔ̃ alafa ene.

english_verse: Dan and the tribes that march with it must set up camp on the north side of the sacred tent, under their own banner. The
translation_verse: ame si ƒe aʋawɔlawo le ame akpe bla ade vɔ eve alafa adrẽ.

english_verse: On one side of Dan will be the tribe of Asher, with Pagiel son of Ochran as the leader of its
translation_verse: ame si ƒe aʋawɔlawo le ame akpe bla ene vɔ ɖekɛ alafa atɔ̃.

english_verse: On the other side will be the tribe of Naphtali with Ahira son of Enan as the leader of its
translation_verse: ame si ƒe aʋawɔlawo le ame akpe bla atɔ̃ vɔ etɔ̃ alafa ene.

english_verse: The only Israelites not included were the Levites, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: Ke womexlẽ Levi viwo ya ɖe eme o, elabe Aƒetɔ gblɔ be womegaxlẽ wo o.

english_verse: Israel did everything the Lord had told Moses. They arranged their camp according to clans and families, with each tribe under its own banner. And that was the order by which they marched into battle.
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo wɔ nu sia nu pɛpɛpɛ abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose ene. Woƒu asaɖa anyi eye ame sia ame le eya ŋutɔ ƒe aflaga gbɔ. Ne woho la, wohona le ɖoɖo la nu, eye ame sia ame kple eƒe ƒome zɔna le woƒe aƒekɔwo nu.

english_verse: Aaron's four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar,
translation_verse: Viŋutsu ene nɔ Aron si siwo ŋkɔwoe nye: Nadab, eƒe ŋgɔgbevi, Abihu, Eleazar kple Itamar.

english_verse: were the ones to be ordained as priests.
translation_verse: Wosi ami na wo heɖo wo nunɔlawoe,

english_verse: But the Lord killed Nadab and Abihu in the Sinai Desert when they used fire that was unacceptable in their offering to the Lord. And because Nadab and Abihu had no sons, only Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests with their father Aaron. The Duties of the Levites
translation_verse: ke Nadab kple Abihu ku esime wotsɔ dzo makɔmakɔ va sa vɔe na Aƒetɔ le Sinai-gbedadaƒo. Vi menɔ wo si o, ale Eleazar kple Itamar va zu nunɔlawo le wo tɔ́ Aron ƒe agbenɔɣi. Wotia Levi viwo be woanye nunɔlawo ƒe kpeɖeŋutɔwo

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: They are assigned to help Aaron and his sons,
translation_verse: Tsɔ wo de Aron kple viawo si be woawo nanye wo subɔlawo koŋ le Israelviwo dome.

english_verse: who have been appointed to be priests. Anyone else who tries to perform the duties of a priest must be put to death.
translation_verse: Nàɖo Aron kple viawo be woawo ko nanye nunɔlawo; ke ne ame bubu aɖe va be yeawɔ woƒe dɔ la, wonewu amea.”

english_verse: Moses, I have chosen these Levites from all Israel, and they will belong to me in a special way. When I killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, I decided that the first-born sons in every Israelite family and the first-born males of their flocks and herds would be mine. But now I accept these Levites in place of the first-born sons of the Israelites. The Levites Are Counted
translation_verse: elabe ŋgɔgbeviwo katã la tɔnyewoe. Gbe si gbe mewu ŋgɔgbeviwo katã le Egipte-nyigba dzi la, mekɔ ŋgɔgbeviwo katã le Israel ŋu la na ɖokuinye; amewo kple lãwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo siaa, be woanye tɔnye. Nyee nye Aƒetɔ.” Levi viwo xexlẽ

english_verse: In the Sinai Desert the Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose le Sinai-gbedadaƒo la be:

english_verse: “Now I want you to count the men and boys in the Levi tribe by families and by clans. Include every one at least a month old.”
translation_verse: “Tia Levi viŋutsu siwo xɔ ɣleti ɖeka alo wu nenema la nàxlẽ ɖe aƒekɔaƒekɔ kple ƒomeƒome nu.”

english_verse: Levi's three sons, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, had become the heads of their own clans.
translation_verse: Levi viwo ŋkɔwoe nye: Gerson, Kehat kple Merari.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Gerson viwo ŋkɔwo le woƒe ƒomewo nu nye esi: Libni kple Simei.

english_verse: Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
translation_verse: Kehat viwo nye esi le woƒe ƒomewo nu: Amram, Yizhar, Xebron kple Uziel.

english_verse: And Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. These were the sons and grandsons of Levi, and they had become the leaders of the Levite clans.
translation_verse: Merari viwo nye esi le woƒe ƒomewo nu: Maxeli kple Musi. Esiawo nye Levi viwo ƒe ƒomewo le wo tɔ́wo ƒe aƒewo nu.

english_verse: The two Gershon clans were the Libnites and Shimeites,
translation_verse: Gerson ƒomeawo nye: Libni viwo kple Simei viwo.

english_verse: Their duties at the tent included taking care of the tent itself, along with its outer covering, the curtain for the entrance,
translation_verse: Woƒe dɔdeasie nye be woakpɔ agbadɔ la dzi. Agbadɔ la me vɔ, egodotɔ kple mɔnuvɔwo le woƒe dzikpɔkpɔ te.

english_verse: the curtains hanging inside the courtyard around the tent, as well as the curtain and ropes for the entrance to the courtyard and its altar. The Gershonites were responsible for setting these things up and taking them down.
translation_verse: Azɔ kpɔ si ƒo xlã agbadɔa kple vɔsamlekpui la godoo kple agbadɔ la ŋu kawo hã le eme. Subɔsubɔdɔ bubu siwo katã ku ɖe nu siawo ŋu la kpɔ wo ŋkume.

english_verse: The four Kohath clans were the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and the Uzzielites,
translation_verse: Kehat ƒomeawo nye: Amram viwo, Xebron viwo kple Uziel viwo.

english_verse: Their duties at the tent included taking care of the sacred chest, the table for the sacred bread, the lampstand, the altars, the objects used for worship, and the curtain in front of the most holy place. The Kohathites were responsible for setting these things up and taking them down.
translation_verse: Woƒe dɔdeasie nye be woakpɔ nu siwo gbɔna la dzi: Nubablaɖaka la, kplɔ̃ la, akaɖiti la, vɔsamlekpuiawo, tsikunu siwo ŋudɔ nunɔlawo wɔna le kɔkɔeƒe la me kple xɔmetsovɔ la. Subɔsubɔdɔ bubu siwo katã ku ɖe nu siawo ŋu la kpɔ wo ŋkume.

english_verse: Eleazar son of Aaron was the head of the Levite leaders, and he made sure that the work at the sacred tent was done.
translation_verse: Levi viwo ƒe tatɔe nye Eleazar, nunɔla Aron vi. Eyae nye tatɔ na Levi vi siwo katã kpɔa kɔkɔeƒe la dzi.

english_verse: The two Merari clans were the Mahlites and the Mushites,
translation_verse: Merari ƒomeawo nye: Maxeli viwo kple Musi viwo.

english_verse: The Merarites, under the leadership of Zuriel son of Abihail, were to camp on the north side of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Woawo naƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe agbadɔ la ƒe dzigbeme lɔƒo, eye woƒe tatɔe nye Zuriel, Abixail vi.

english_verse: Moses, Aaron, and his sons were to camp in front of the sacred tent, on the east side, and to make sure that the Israelites worshiped in the proper way. Anyone else who tried to do the work of Moses and Aaron was to be put to death.
translation_verse: Mose kple Aron kpakple Aron viŋutsuawo naƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe agbadɔ la ŋgɔ le ɣedzeƒe lɔƒo. Woƒe dɔdeasie nye be woawɔ dɔ le kɔkɔeƒe la na Israelviwo. Ke ne ame bubu aɖe va be yeawɔ woƒe dɔ la, wonewui.

english_verse: So Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord and counted the Levites by their clans. The total number of Levites at least one month old was
translation_verse: Ŋutsu siwo katã xɔ ɣleti ɖeka alo wu nenema le Levi viwo dome siwo Mose kple Aron xlẽ le woƒe ƒomewo nu, abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na wo ene la, ƒe xexlẽme nye akpe bla eve vɔ eve. Levi viwo va xɔ ɖe ŋgɔgbeviwo teƒe

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Make a list and count the first-born sons at least one month old in each of the Israelite families.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Tia ŋutsu ŋgɔgbevi siwo katã xɔ ɣleti ɖeka alo wu nenema la le Israelviwo dome, eye nàŋlɔ woƒe ŋkɔwo axlẽ.

english_verse: They belong to me, but I will accept the Levites as substitutes for them, and I will accept the Levites' livestock as substitutes for the Israelites' first-born livestock.”
translation_verse: Eyome, tia Levi viwo ɖe Israelviwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo katã teƒe. Nyee nye Aƒetɔ. Nenema ke le lãhawo gome hã la, Levi viwo ƒe lã ŋgɔgbeviwo katã hã nye tɔnye axɔ ɖe Israel ƒe lã ŋgɔgbeviwo teƒe.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord and counted the first-born sons;
translation_verse: Ale Mose xlẽ ŋgɔgbeviwo katã le Israelviwo dome le Aƒetɔ ƒe sedede nu.

english_verse: Then the Lord said,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: “The Levites will belong to me and will take the place of the first-born sons; their livestock will take the place of the Israelites' first-born livestock.
translation_verse: “Kɔ Levi viwo ŋu nam be woanye tɔnye ɖe ŋutsu ŋgɔgbevi siwo katã le Israel la teƒe. Nenema ke kɔ Levi viwo ƒe lãhawo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo ŋu nam ɖe Israelviwo tɔ teƒe.

english_verse: For each one, you are to collect five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Xe klosaloga atɔ̃ ɖe ame ɖeka ta, le gaɖɔliɖɔli ƒe ɖoɖo si li la nu,

english_verse: This money must then be given to Aaron and his sons.”
translation_verse: eye nàtsɔ ame tsidziawo ƒe ga la na Aron kple via ŋutsuwo.”

english_verse: Moses collected the silver from the extra
translation_verse: Mose wɔ ɖe nya la dzi, eye wòtsɔ

english_verse: Then he gave it to Aaron and his sons, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: na Aron kple via ŋutsuwo abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ ene.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose kple Aron be:

english_verse: The Kohathites will be responsible for carrying the sacred objects used in worship at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Kehat viwo ƒe dɔe wònye be woakpɔ nu kɔkɔe vevitɔwo dzi le godoƒegbadɔ la me.

english_verse: When the Israelites are ready to move their camp, Aaron and his sons will enter the tent and take down the curtain that separates the sacred chest from the rest of the tent. They will cover the chest with this curtain,
translation_verse: Ne ameha la le hoho ge la, Aron kple via ŋutsuwo nayi ɖe agbadɔ la me, eye woaɖe xɔmetsovɔ la atsyɔ na nubablaɖaka la.

english_verse: Next, Aaron and his sons will use another blue cloth to cover the table for the sacred bread. On the cloth they will place the dishes, the bowls for incense, the cups, the jugs for wine, as well as the bread itself.
translation_verse: Azɔ woakeke blɔvɔ ɖe vɔsabolokplɔ̃ la dzi, emegbe woafɔ agbaawo, lifigbaawo, treawo kple goe siwo me wokua nunonovɔsa ɖo kple abolo siwo ŋudɔ wowɔna gbe sia gbe la ada ɖe edzi.

english_verse: With another blue cloth they will cover the lampstand, along with the lamps, the lamp snuffers, the fire pans, and the jars of oil for the lamps.
translation_verse: Emegbe woatsɔ blɔvɔ atsyɔ akaɖiti la kple eŋu kaɖiawo, ɖovulãnuawo, ganuviawo kple amigoe siwo kpe ɖe eŋu la.

english_verse: All of this will then be covered with a piece of fine leather and placed on a carrying frame.
translation_verse: Woabla nuawo ɖe gbɔ̃gbalẽ me, eye woatsɔe aɖo nukɔgbati dzi.

english_verse: The gold incense altar is to be covered with a blue cloth, and then with a piece of fine leather, before its carrying poles are put in place.
translation_verse: Azɔ la woakeke blɔvɔ ɖe sikavɔsamlekpui la dzi, atsɔ gbɔ̃gbalẽ abu edzi, eye woade nukɔkpoawo eŋu.

english_verse: Next, Aaron and his sons will take blue cloth and wrap all the objects used in worship at the sacred tent. These will need to be covered with a piece of fine leather, then placed on a carrying frame.
translation_verse: Emegbe woabla nu siwo katã ŋudɔ wowɔna le kɔkɔeƒe la ɖe blɔvɔ me, axatsa gbɔ̃gbalẽ la ɖe wo ŋu, eye woatsɔ wo aɖo nukɔgbati dzi.

english_verse: They are to remove the ashes from the bronze altar and cover it with a purple cloth.
translation_verse: Woalɔ dzowɔ le vɔsamlekpui la me, eye woakeke avɔ hẽtɔ ɖe edzi.

english_verse: On that cloth will be placed the utensils used at the altar, including the fire pans, the meat forks, the shovels, and the sprinkling bowls. All of this will then be covered with a piece of fine leather, before the carrying poles are put in place.
translation_verse: Eyome woafɔ eŋu nu siwo ŋudɔ wowɔna la ada ɖe edzi. Nuawoe nye: Dzowɔlɔnuawo, gafloawo, sofiawo, gagbaawo kple vɔsamlekpui la ŋu nuwo katã. Emegbe woatsɔ gbɔ̃gbalẽ abu wo dzi, eye woade nukɔkpoawo eŋu.

english_verse: When the camp is ready to be moved, the Kohathites will be responsible for carrying the sacred objects and the furnishings of the sacred tent. But Aaron and his sons must have already covered those things so the Kohathites won't touch them and die.
translation_verse: Ne ameha la le hoho ge, eye Aron kple via ŋutsuwo bla nu ɖe nu kɔkɔeawo kple wo ŋu nuawo katã ŋu vɔ la, eya ko hafi Kehat viwo nava tsɔ nuawo. Ne wokatsa ka nuawo ŋu do ŋgɔ la, woaku. Dɔdeasi siawoe Kehat viwo awɔ, ne godoƒegbadɔ la le hoho ge.”

english_verse: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest will be in charge of the oil for the lamps, the sweet-smelling incense, the grain for the sacrifices, and the olive oil used for dedications and ordinations. Eleazar is responsible for seeing that the sacred tent, its furnishings, and the sacred objects are taken care of.
translation_verse: “Eleazar, nunɔla Aron viŋutsu, akpɔ agbadɔ blibo la dzi. Eƒe dɔe nye be wòakpɔ ami si woade akaɖiawo me, dzudzɔ ʋeʋẽe donu, gbe sia gbe nuɖuɖuvɔsa, amisinanu la kple nu bubu siwo katã ŋuti wokɔ le eme kple eŋu la dzi.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: The Gershonites will be responsible
translation_verse: Woawoe anye nutsɔ siwo gbɔna la tsɔlawo:

english_verse: for carrying the curtains of the sacred tent, its two outer coverings, the curtain for the entrance to the tent,
translation_verse: Agbadɔ la, agbadɔ la ƒe kuntru emetɔ kple egodotɔ, gbɔ̃gbalẽ si wotsɔ tsyɔ edzi, mɔnutsovɔ,

english_verse: the curtains hanging around the courtyard of the tent, and the curtain and ropes for the entrance to the courtyard. The Gershonites are to do whatever needs to be done to take care of these things,
translation_verse: kpɔ si ƒo xlã agbadɔ la kple vɔsamlekpui la godoo va kpe la ŋu vɔwo kple agbonuvɔ la, agbadɔ la ŋu kawo kple nu bubu siwo katã ŋudɔ wowɔna le agbadɔ la tutu me. Gerson viwoe awɔ dɔ siawo katã.

english_verse: These are the duties of the Gershonites at the sacred tent, and Ithamar son of Aaron will make sure they do their work. The Duties of the Merarite Clans
translation_verse: Gerson viwo ƒe ƒome la ƒe dɔdeasiwo nye esiawo le agbadɔ la ŋu eye Itamar, nunɔla Aron viŋutsu, nanye wo dzikpɔla.” Merari vi siwo le Levitɔwo dome la ƒe dɔdeasiwo

english_verse: The Merarites will be responsible for carrying the frames of the tent and its other pieces, including the bars, the posts, and the stands,
translation_verse: Merari viwo ƒe dɔe nye be woatsɔ agbadɔ la ƒe ʋuƒoawo, gametiawo, sɔtiawo kple eƒe afɔawo.

english_verse: as well as the posts that support the courtyard, together with their stands, tent pegs, and ropes. The Merarites are to be told exactly what objects they are to carry,
translation_verse: Woawo kee atsɔ kpɔtiawo katã kple woƒe afɔawo, wo ŋu tsyotiawo, kaawo kple nu siwo katã ŋudɔ wowɔna le agbadɔa tutu me. Miafia ame sia ame ƒe agba si wòatsɔ lae ɖekaɖeka.

english_verse: and Ithamar son of Aaron will make sure they do their work. The Levites Are Counted Again
translation_verse: Merari viwo ƒe ƒome la ƒe dɔdeasiwo le agbadɔa ŋu lae nye esiawo, eye Itamar, nunɔla Aron viŋutsu la nanye wo dzikpɔla.” Levitɔwo xexlẽ

english_verse: Moses, Aaron, and the other Israelite leaders obeyed the Lord and counted the Levi tribe by families and clans, to find out how many men there were between the ages of
translation_verse: Mose na wofia ame sia ame ƒe dɔ kple agba si wòatsɔ lae abe ale si Aƒetɔ de se ene, eye wotia wo xlẽ abe ale si Aƒetɔ de se to Mose dzi ene.

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel, “Put out of the camp everyone who has leprosy or a bodily discharge or who has touched a dead body. Now that I live among my people, their camp must be kept clean.”
translation_verse: Woaɖo wo ɖe asaɖa la godo, ŋutsuwo kple nyɔnuwo siaa, be womagagblẽ kɔ ɖo na woƒe asaɖa la o, elabe afi mae mele wo dome le.”

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed the Lord's instructions. The Penalty for Committing a Crime (Leviticus
translation_verse: Israelviwo wɔ nu si Mose gblɔ na wo la pɛpɛpɛ, eye woɖo ameawo ɖe asaɖa la godo. Fexexe ɖe vodada ta

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you commit a crime against someone, you have sinned against me.
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na Israelviwo be, ne ŋutsu alo nyɔnu aɖe mewɔ nuteƒe na Aƒetɔ o, eye wòda vo ɖe ame aɖe ŋu la, eɖi fɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: If the victim has no relative who can accept this money, it belongs to me and will be paid to the priest. In addition to that payment, you must take a ram for the priest to sacrifice so your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Ke ne amea ku, eye ƒometɔ si te ɖe eŋu aɖu eƒe dome meli wòaxe fe la na o la, ekema fe si wòxe la zu Aƒetɔ tɔ woatsɔ na nunɔla. Agbo si woatsɔ awɔ avuléle kɔnu la hã nakpe ɖe eŋuti.

english_verse: When you make a donation to the sacred tent, that money belongs only to the priest, and each priest will keep what is given to him. A Suspicious Husband
translation_verse: Ame sia ame ƒe nu kɔkɔe si wòava na la anye nunɔla tɔ, eye nu sia nu si ame aɖe va na nunɔla la, nye eya ŋutɔ tɔ.” Ŋutsu srɔ̃tɔ anukluiwɔlawo ƒe nya

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Suppose a man becomes jealous and suspects that his wife has been unfaithful, but he has no proof.
translation_verse: Ke ava eme be ŋutsua abu nazã, ŋuʋaʋã naɖo eme, eye wòade asi anukluiwɔwɔ me le srɔ̃a ŋuti. Azɔ la, ava eme hã be ŋutsua abu nazã anɔ anuklui wɔm le srɔ̃a ŋuti, evɔ wònye nyɔnua megblẽ kɔ ɖo hafi o.

english_verse: He must take his wife to the priest, together with one kilogram of ground barley as an offering to find out if she is guilty. No olive oil or incense is to be put on that offering.
translation_verse: Ne eva eme le go eveawo me alea la, srɔ̃ŋutsua nekplɔ srɔ̃a yi nunɔla gbɔ, eye wòatsɔ luwɔ kilo ɖeka si nye vɔsanunana la akpe ɖe eŋuti. Makɔ ami ɖe edzi alo ada dzudzɔdonu hã ɖe edzi o, elabe vɔsanunana si srɔ̃ŋutsu nazãbula tsɔ vɛ be nyateƒe nadze la wònye.

english_verse: The priest will lead the woman to my altar and make her stand there.
translation_verse: Nunɔla la nana nyɔnua nate va, eye wòatsi tsitre ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: He will then pour sacred water into a clay jar and stir in some dust from the floor of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Nunɔla la neku tsi kɔkɔe ɖe agba me, eye wòalɔ ke le anyigba le agbadɔ la me akɔ ɖe tsia me.

english_verse: The priest will write these curses on special paper and wash them off into the bitter water,
translation_verse: Emegbe nunɔla aŋlɔ fiƒodenya siawo ɖe agbalẽ me, eye wòakpalae ɖe fiƒodetsi si hea fukpekpe vaa ame dzi la me.

english_verse: so that when the woman drinks this water, the curses will enter her body.
translation_verse: Hafi wòana nyɔnua nano tsi veve la wòaɖo lã me nɛ la,

english_verse: He will take the barley offering from her and lift it up in dedication to me, the Lord. Then he will place it on my altar
translation_verse: nunɔla la axɔ luvɔsanunana la le esi, eye wòanyèe le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, emegbe wòatsɔe ayi vɔsamlekpui la gbɔe.

english_verse: and burn part of it as a sacrifice. After that, the woman must drink the bitter water.
translation_verse: Nunɔla la aku luvɔsanunana la asiʋlo ɖeka, abe ŋkuɖoɖo nu dzi ƒe dzesi ene, eye wòatɔ dzoe le vɔsamlekpui la dzi. Esiawo megbe hafi wòana nyɔnua nano tsi la.

english_verse: If the woman has been unfaithful, the water will immediately make her unable to have children, and she will be a curse among her people.
translation_verse: Nenye be ewɔ ahasi, eye wògblẽ kɔ ɖo vavã hafi no fiƒodetsia la, tsia aɖo lã me nɛ, eye wòase veve vevie. Ƒodo adzi ɖe enu, eƒe ali aklẽ, eye wòatrɔ zu ɖiŋudonu le eƒe dukɔ me.

english_verse: But if she is innocent, her body will not be harmed, and she will still be able to have children.
translation_verse: Ke ne nyɔnu la megblẽ kɔ ɖo o, eye eƒe nya dzɔ la, naneke mawɔe o, eye wòagate ŋu afɔ fu adzi vi.

english_verse: This is the ceremony that must take place at my altar when a husband suspects that his wife has been unfaithful. The priest must tell the woman to stand in my presence and carefully follow these instructions.
translation_verse: ŋuʋaʋã gbɔgbɔ ɖo ŋutsu aɖe me, eye wode asi anukluiwɔwɔ me ɖe srɔ̃a ŋu la, ekema nekplɔ nyɔnu la va Aƒetɔ ŋkume, eye nunɔla nawɔ nu siawo katã nɛ ɖe se la nu.

english_verse: If the husband is wrong, he will not be punished; but if his wife is guilty, she will be punished.
translation_verse: Ŋutsu la avo tso nuvɔ̃ me, ke nuvɔ̃ ƒe agba anɔ nyɔnua dzi.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: If any of you want to dedicate yourself to me by vowing to become a Nazirite,
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na Israelviwo be: ‘Ne ŋutsu alo nyɔnu aɖe ɖe adzɔgbe hekɔ eɖokui ŋu na Aƒetɔ be yeazu Mawu ƒe Klu la,

english_verse: you must no longer drink any wine or beer or use any kind of vinegar. Don't drink grape juice or eat grapes or raisins—
translation_verse: ele be wòatsri wain alo aha sesẽ ɖe sia ɖe. Mano waintsetse me tsi alo anyi waintsetse alo aɖu waintsetse ƒuƒu hã o.

english_verse: The hair of a Nazirite is sacred to me, and as long as you are a Nazirite, you must never cut your hair.
translation_verse: “Ɣeyiɣi si me wònye Mawu ƒe Klu la, ezu ame kɔkɔe na Aƒetɔ eya ta talũhɛ maka ta nɛ le ɣeyiɣi mawo katã me o, ke boŋ ele nɛ be wòagblẽ eƒe taɖa ɖi wòato asa ɖe eme.

english_verse: During the time that you are a Nazirite, you must never go close to a dead body,
translation_verse: “Le ŋkeke siwo katã me wòkɔ eɖokui ŋu na Aƒetɔ la, mele be wòate ɖe ame kuku ŋu o.

english_verse: not even that of your father, mother, brother, or sister. That would make you unclean. Your hair is the sign that you are dedicated to me, so remain holy.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke siwo katã wònye Mawu ƒe Klu la, ezu ame si ŋu kɔ na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: If someone suddenly dies near you, your hair is no longer sacred, and you must shave it seven days later during the ceremony to make you clean.
translation_verse: “Ke ne ame aɖe ku kpata le egbɔ la, amea gblẽ kɔ ɖo na eƒe ɖa la. Anɔ anyi ŋkeke adrẽ, eye le gbe ma gbe la alũ ta, ekema eŋu gakɔ.

english_verse: Then on the next day, bring two doves or two pigeons to the priest at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke enyia gbe la, atsɔ akpakpa eve alo ahɔnɛvi eve vɛ na nunɔla le godoƒegbadɔ la nu.

english_verse: He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. You will then be forgiven for being too near a dead body, and your hair will again become sacred.
translation_verse: Nunɔla la natsɔ ɖeka asa nuvɔ̃vɔe, eye wòatsɔ evelia asa numemevɔe. Esia anye ŋutikɔkɔ kɔnu si wòawɔ nɛ elabe ete ɖe ame kuku ŋu hegblẽ kɔ ɖo. Agbugbɔ eƒe taɖa hã ŋu agakɔ gbe ma gbe ke.

english_verse: But the dead body made you unacceptable, so you must make another vow to become a Nazirite and be dedicated once more. Finally, a year-old ram must be offered as the sacrifice to make things right.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Mawu ƒe Klu la agbugbɔ adzɔgbe aɖe na Aƒetɔ hena ɣeyiɣi bubu elabe ɣeyiɣi si va yi la ŋu mekɔ o, esi wògblẽ kɔ ɖo na eɖokui ta. Ale ana alẽvi si xɔ ƒe ɖeka woatsɔ asa fɔɖivɔe nɛ.”

english_verse: When you have completed your promised time of being a Nazirite, go to the sacred tent
translation_verse: Mawu ƒe Klu ƒe se nye esi: “Ne ŋkeke siwo wòkɔ eɖokui ŋu la de la, woakplɔe ava godoƒegbadɔ la nu,

english_verse: and offer three animals that have nothing wrong with them: a year-old ram as a sacrifice to please me, a year-old female lamb as a sacrifice for sin, and a full-grown ram as a sacrifice to ask my blessing.
translation_verse: eye wòatsɔ lã etɔ̃ siwo naneke mewɔ afi aɖeke na o la ava na Aƒetɔ: alẽvi si xɔ ƒe ɖeka woawɔ numemevɔsae, alẽnɔ si xɔ ƒe ɖeka woawɔ nuvɔ̃vɔsae kple agbo ɖeka woawɔ ŋutifafavɔsae.

english_verse: Wine offerings and grain sacrifices must also be brought with these animals. Finally, you are to bring a basket of bread made with your finest flour and olive oil, but without yeast. Also bring some thin wafers brushed with oil.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, atsɔ kusi si me abolo ƒomevi siawo le la hã ɖe asi: abolo maʋamaʋã, wɔ memee bolo, abolo si wode amii kple abolo maʋamaʋã si dzi wokɔ ami ɖo. Emegbe atsɔ nu siwo woawɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsa kple nunonovɔsa hã akpe ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: The priest will take these gifts to my altar and offer them, so that I will be pleased and will forgive you.
translation_verse: Nunɔla atsɔ nu siawo ava Aƒetɔ gbɔe, eye wòasa nuvɔ̃vɔ kple numemevɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Then he will sacrifice the ram and offer the wine, grain, and bread.
translation_verse: Atsɔ agbo la kple kusimenuawo asa ŋutifafavɔ na Aƒetɔ. Eyome nunɔla la asa nuɖuɖuvɔ kple nunonovɔ nɛ.

english_verse: After that, you will stand at the entrance to the sacred tent, shave your head, and put the hair in the fire where the priest has offered the sacrifice to ask my blessing.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Mawu ƒe Klu la alũ ta le godoƒegbadɔ la nu, eye wòatsɔ taɖa la ade dzo si dzi wole ŋutifafavɔsa wɔm le la me.

english_verse: Once the meat from the ram's shoulder has been boiled, the priest will take it, along with one loaf of bread and one wafer brushed with oil, and give them to you.
translation_verse: Ne woɖa agboa ƒe abɔ la, nunɔla la natsɔ wɔ memee bolo ɖeka kple abolo si wode amii la ɖeka le kusia me ade asi na Klu la.

english_verse: You will hand them back to the priest, who will lift them up in dedication to me. Then he can eat the meat from the ram's shoulder, its choice ribs, and its hind leg, because this is his share of the sacrifice. After this, you will no longer be a Nazirite, and you will be free to drink wine.
translation_verse: Esia yome nunɔla la anyè nuawo atsɔ na Aƒetɔ. Nunana kɔkɔe wonye na nunɔla la hekpe ɖe agboa ƒe akɔ kple ata siwo nye etɔ la ŋu. Ne wowɔ kɔnu sia vɔ la, Mawu ƒe Klu la kpɔ mɔ ano wain.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be

english_verse: “When Aaron and his sons bless the people of Israel, they must say:
translation_verse: wòagblɔ na Aron kple via ŋutsuawo be: “Ne miele Israelviwo yra ge la, migblɔ na wo be:

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will bless and protect you,
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ neyra mi ne wòakpɔ mia dzi!

english_verse: and that he will show you mercy and kindness.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ nekɔ ŋkume ɖe mi ne wòave mia nu!

english_verse: May the Lord be good to you and give you peace.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ netrɔ mo ɖe mia gbɔ ne wòana ŋutifafa mi!

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If Aaron and his sons ask me to bless the Israelites, I will give them my blessing.”
translation_verse: “Ne woyɔ nye ŋkɔ tɔ ɖe Israelviwo ŋu alea la, mayra wo.”

english_verse: When Moses had finished setting up the sacred tent, he dedicated it to the Lord, together with its furnishings, the altar, and its equipment.
translation_verse: Gbe si gbe Mose tu godoƒegbadɔ la vɔ la, esi ami nɛ, eye wòkɔ eya kple eŋu nuwo katã ŋu. Esi ami na vɔsamlekpui la, eye wòkɔ eya hã kple eŋu nuwo katã ŋu.

english_verse: Then the twelve tribal leaders of Israel, the same men who had been in charge of counting the people, came to the tent
translation_verse: Azɔ Israel kplɔla siwo nye tatɔwo le woƒe aƒekɔwo nu, eye wonye toawo ƒe amegãwo ame siwo kpɔ amexexlẽ si wowɔ dzi la,

english_verse: with gifts for the Lord. They brought six strong carts and twelve oxen—one ox from each leader and a cart from every two.
translation_verse: tsɔ woƒe nunanawo vɛ na Aƒetɔ. Nunanaawoe nye: Tasiaɖam ade kple nyitsu wui eve. Wowɔe alea be kplɔla eve naxɔ tasiaɖam ɖeka, eye kplɔla ɖe sia ɖe naxɔ nyitsu ɖeka. Wona nuawo le agbadɔ la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: “Accept these gifts, so the Levites can use them here at the sacred tent for carrying the sacred things.”
translation_verse: “Xɔ nunanaawo le wo si hena godoƒegbadɔ la ŋudɔwo wɔwɔ. Ma wo na Levitɔwo ɖe ale si woƒe dɔwo le la nu.”

english_verse: Then Moses took the carts and oxen and gave them to the Levites,
translation_verse: Ale Mose xɔ tasiaɖamawo kple nyitsuawo tsɔ na Levitɔwo.

english_verse: who were under the leadership of Ithamar son of Aaron. Moses gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites for their work, and four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites for their work.
translation_verse: eye wòtsɔ tasiaɖam ene kple nyitsu enyi na Merari viwo le ale si woƒe dɔ le la nu. Woƒe dɔdzikpɔlae nye Itamar, Aron viŋutsu.

english_verse: But Moses did not give any to the Kohathites, because they were in charge of the sacred objects that had to be carried on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Ke Mose metsɔ tasiaɖam alo nyitsu aɖeke na Kehat viwo ya o, elabe nu kɔkɔe siwo dzi kpɔm wole la, abɔtae woléa wo ɖo.

english_verse: On the day the altar was dedicated, the twelve leaders brought offerings for its dedication.
translation_verse: Gbe si gbe wonɔ ami sim na vɔsamlekpui la, kplɔlaawo dzɔ nu bene woatsɔ akɔ eŋui. Wotsɔ woƒe nunanaawo va vɔsamlekpui la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Each day one leader is to give his offering for the dedication.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Gblɔ na wo be gbe sia gbe la, kplɔla ɖeka ko natsɔ eƒe nunanawo vɛ be woatsɔ akɔ vɔsamlekpuia ŋui.”

english_verse: kilograms, according to the official standards;
translation_verse: gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka ne woawɔ nuvɔ̃vɔsae;

english_verse: rams a year old as sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke asiekea gbe la, Abidan, Gideoni vi, Benyamin viwo kplɔlae na nu.

english_verse: Whenever Moses needed to talk with the Lord, he went into the sacred tent, where he heard the Lord's voice coming from between the two winged creatures above the lid of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Ne Mose yi ɖe godoƒegbadɔ la me be yeaƒo nu kple Mawu la, esea gbe aɖe tso kerubi eveawo dome le nutsyɔnu si le nubablaɖakaa tame la dzi, eye wòƒoa nu kplii le afi ma.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: “Tell Aaron to put the seven lamps on the lampstand so they shine toward the front.”
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na Aron be ne eda akaɖi adrẽawo ɖe akaɖitia dzi la, neda wo ɖi ale be woaklẽ ayi ŋgɔ.”

english_verse: Aaron obeyed and placed the lamps as he was told.
translation_verse: Ale Aron wɔ ɖe nya la dzi eye wòda akaɖiawo ɖe atia dzi le ŋgɔgbe lɔƒo.

english_verse: The lampstand was made of hammered gold from its base to the decorative flowers on top, exactly like the pattern the Lord had described to Moses. Instructions for Ordaining the Levites
translation_verse: Wotsɔ sika tu akaɖiti blibo lae tso etame va se ɖe egɔme abe ale si Aƒetɔ fia Mose be newɔe ene. Levitɔwo ŋuti kɔkɔ kple wo tsɔtsɔ na be woawɔ subɔsubɔdɔ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: and sprinkle them with the water that washes away their sins. Then have them shave their entire bodies and wash their clothes.
translation_verse: ale: Wu tsi si ɖea nuvɔ̃ ɖa le ame ŋu la ɖe wo ŋu, eye nàna woalũ fu le ŋuti katã, emegbe woanya woƒe awuwo. Ne wowɔ esia la, wo ŋuti akɔ.

english_verse: They are to bring a bull and its proper grain sacrifice of flour mixed with olive oil. And they must bring a second bull as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Azɔ nà woatsɔ nyitsuvi ɖeka kple wɔ memee si wodzaba kple ami akpe ɖe eŋu ne woawɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsae. Wò ŋutɔ nàtsɔ nyitsuvi ne woawɔ nuvɔ̃vɔsae.

english_verse: Then you, Moses, will call together all the people of Israel and send the Levites to my sacred tent,
translation_verse: Emegbe nàƒo Israelviwo ƒe ha blibo la nu ƒu, eye nàna Levitɔwo nava tsi tsitre ɖe nye agbadɔ la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: where the people will place their hands on them.
translation_verse: Na Israelviwo natsɔ woƒe asiwo ada ɖe Levitɔwo dzi,

english_verse: Aaron will present the Levites to me as a gift from the people, so that the Levites will do my work.
translation_verse: eye Aron anyè asi akɔ̀ Levitɔwo ŋu nam abe Israelviwo ƒe nunana ene bene woanɔ subɔsubɔdɔ wɔm nam.

english_verse: After this, the Levites are to place their hands on the heads of the bulls. Sacrifice one of the bulls for the forgiveness of sin, and the other to make sure that I am pleased. Then the Levites will be acceptable to me.
translation_verse: Azɔ na Levitɔwo natsɔ woƒe asiwo aɖo nyitsuawo ƒe tame; tsɔ ɖeka sa nuvɔ̃vɔe, eye nàtsɔ evelia sa numemevɔ nam be nalé avu na Levitɔwo.

english_verse: They will stand at my altar in front of Aaron and his sons, who will dedicate the Levites to me.
translation_verse: Kɔ̀ Levitɔwo ŋu be woanye nunana tɔxɛ nam, eye nàna Aron kple via ŋutsuwo nanɔ wo nu.”

english_verse: After they have been made acceptable and have been dedicated, they will be allowed to work at my sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ne èkɔ Levitɔwo ŋu alea eye nètsɔ wo nam vɔ la, ekema woava wɔ subɔsubɔdɔ le nye agbadɔ la me.

english_verse: They are mine and will take the place of the first-born Israelite sons.
translation_verse: Nye ŋutɔe xɔ wo ɖe Israelviwo ƒe ŋgɔgbevi siwo ʋu dɔ nu na wo nɔwo la teƒe, eye wova zu tɔnye blibo.

english_verse: When I killed the oldest sons of the Egyptians, I decided that the first-born sons in each Israelite family would be mine, as well as every first-born male from their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: Gbe si gbe mewu Egiptetɔwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo katã la, mekɔ Israelviwo katã ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo ŋu hekpe ɖe lã ɖe sia ɖe ƒe ŋgɔgbevi gɔ̃ hã ŋu na ɖokuinye.

english_verse: But now I have chosen these Levites as substitutes for the first-born sons,
translation_verse: Azɔ la, mexɔ Levitɔwo ɖe Israelviwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo katã teƒe.

english_verse: and I have given them as gifts to Aaron and his sons to serve at the sacred tent. I will hold them responsible for what happens to anyone who gets too close to the sacred tent. The Levites Are Dedicated to the Lord
translation_verse: Meɖe Levitɔwo abe Israelviwo ƒe nunana ene tsɔ na Aron kple via ŋutsuwo, bene woanɔ subɔsubɔdɔ wɔm le agbadɔ la me ɖe Israelviwo nu, ale be ne Israelviwo te ɖe kɔkɔeƒe la ŋu la, woawoe alé avu na Israelviwo be dɔléle vɔ̃ɖi aɖeke nagaɖo wo dome o.”

english_verse: Moses, Aaron, and the other Israelites made sure that the Levites did everything the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Ale Mose, Aron kple Israelviwo ƒe ha blibo la kɔ Levitɔwo ŋu abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be woawɔ ene.

english_verse: The Levites sprinkled themselves with the water of forgiveness and washed their clothes. Then Aaron brought them to the altar and offered sacrifices to forgive their sins and make them acceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Levitɔwo ɖe nuvɔ̃ ɖa le wo ɖokui ŋu, nya woƒe awuwo, eye Aron kɔ wo ŋu wozu nunana tɔxɛ na Aƒetɔ. Aron wɔ avuléle kɔnu la hã na wo tsɔ kɔ wo ŋutii.

english_verse: After this, the Levites worked at the sacred tent as assistants to Aaron and his sons, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Emegbe Levitɔwo yi agbadɔ la me, eye Aron kple via ŋutsuwo kpɔ wo dzi wowɔ subɔsubɔdɔ le afi ma. Ameawo wɔ nu sia nu pɛpɛpɛ abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be wòana woawɔe ene.

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: They may help the other Levites in their duties, but they must no longer be responsible for any work themselves. Remember this when you assign their duties.”
translation_verse: Ema megbe ate ŋu akpe ɖe etɔwo ŋu awɔ subɔsubɔdɔ le agbadɔa me faa, ke magawɔ dɔ aɖeke le eɖokui si o. Aleae wòle be nàna Levitɔwo nawɔ woƒe dɔdeasiwoe.”

english_verse: During the first month of Israel's second year in the Sinai Desert, the Lord had told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒo nu kple Mose le Sinai-gbedadaƒo le ƒè evelia ƒe ɣleti gbãtɔ me esime woʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi be,

english_verse: to say to the people, “Celebrate Passover
translation_verse: “Mina Israelviwo naɖu Paska la ɖe eƒe ɣeyiɣi dzi.

english_verse: in the evening of the fourteenth day of this month and do it by following all the regulations.”
translation_verse: Le ɣletia ƒe ŋkeke wui enelia ƒe fiẽ me la miaɖui ɖe ɣeyiɣia dzi ɖe ɖoɖo kple se siwo katã le eŋu la nu.”

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had said, and they celebrated Passover there in the desert in the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
translation_verse: eye le ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke wui enelia gbe ƒe fiẽ la, woɖu Paska la le Sinai-gbedadaƒo la. Wowɔ nu sia nu pɛpɛpɛ abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be woawɔe ene.

english_verse: Some people in Israel's camp had touched a dead body and had become unfit to worship the Lord, and they could not celebrate Passover. But they asked Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Ke ŋutsu aɖewo gblẽ kɔ ɖo elabe woka asi ame kuku ŋu ale be womete ŋu ɖu Paska la gbe ma gbe o. Wova Mose kple Aron gbɔ,

english_verse: “Even though we have touched a dead body, why can't we celebrate Passover and offer sacrifices to the Lord at the same time as everyone else?”
translation_verse: eye wogblɔ na wo be: “Míegblẽ kɔ ɖo elabe míeka asi ame kuku ŋu, ke nu ka tae womaɖe mɔ na mí míanɔ Israelvi bubuawo dome atsɔ vɔsanuwo vɛ na Aƒetɔ le ɣeyiɣi la dzi o?”

english_verse: Moses said, “Wait here while I go into the sacred tent and find out what the Lord says about this.”
translation_verse: Mose ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Milala va se ɖe esime mase nu si Aƒetɔ adi be mawɔ la.”

english_verse: The Lord then told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you or your descendants touch a dead body and become unfit to worship me, or if you are away on a long journey, you may still celebrate Passover.
translation_verse: be negblɔ na Israelviwo be: “Ne miawo ŋutɔ alo miaƒe dzidzimevi aɖe ka asi ame kuku ŋu, eye wògblẽ kɔ ɖo alo wòyi nugbe la, ekpɔ mɔ aɖu Paska la na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: But it must be done in the second month, in the evening of the fourteenth day. Eat the Passover lamb with thin bread and bitter herbs,
translation_verse: Ke woawo ya naɖui le ɣleti evelia ƒe ŋkeke wui enelia gbe ƒe fiẽ me, eye woatsɔ abolo maʋamaʋã aɖu ama vevee.

english_verse: and don't leave any of it until morning or break any of the animal's bones. Be sure to follow these regulations.
translation_verse: Womagblẽ nuɖuɖu aɖeke ɖi ŋu nake ɖe edzi o, eye womagbã ƒu aɖeke hã o. Woawɔ ɖe ɖoɖo siwo katã le Paska la ɖuɖu ŋu la dzi pɛpɛpɛ.

english_verse: But if any of you are fit to worship me, and yet refuse to celebrate Passover when you are not away on a journey, you will no longer belong to my people. You will be punished because you did not offer sacrifices to me at the proper time.
translation_verse: Evɔ ne ame aɖe megblẽ kɔ ɖo o, eye meyi nugbe hã o, gake wògbe Paska la ɖuɖu la, ekema woaɖe amea ɖa le eƒe amewo dome elabe mesa vɔ na Aƒetɔ ɖe ɣeyiɣi dzi o; ewɔ nuvɔ̃, eye woahe to nɛ kokoko.

english_verse: Anyone, including foreigners who live among you, can celebrate Passover, if they follow all the regulations. The Cloud over the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Ne amedzro aɖe le mia dome si di be yeaɖu Paskaa la ate ŋu aɖui, ke neɖui ɖe ɖoɖo kple se siwo le Paska ŋu la nu. Ɖoɖo ɖeka nanɔ eŋu na amedzrovi kple devi siaa.” Alilikpo si le abe dzo ene (Mos II,

english_verse: As soon as the sacred tent was set up, a thick cloud appeared and covered it. The cloud was there each day, and during the night, a fire could be seen in it.
translation_verse: Enɔ nenema ɣe sia ɣi: le ŋkeke me la, alilikpo nɔa teƒea dzi, eye le zã me la, edzena abe dzo ene.

english_verse: whether it was only one night, a few days, a month, or even a year. As long as the cloud remained over the tent, the Israelites stayed where they were. But when the cloud moved, so did the Israelites.
translation_verse: Alilikpo la ɖe wòtsi anyi ŋkeke eve o, ɣleti ɖeka o, alo wu nenema o, Israelviwo hã tsia asaɖa la me, womehona o; ke ne eho ko la, woawo hã hona dzona.

english_verse: They obeyed the Lord's commands and went wherever he directed Moses.
translation_verse: Israelviwo kpɔa Aƒetɔ sinu godoo wòɖea gbe na wo to Mose dzi hafi woƒua asaɖa anyi loo, alo hona dzona.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: Have someone make two trumpets out of hammered silver. These will be used to call the people together and to give the signal for moving your camp.
translation_verse: “Tsɔ klosalo tu kpẽ eve. Woawoe nàku ayɔ ameha la aƒo ƒu, eye woawo kee nàgaku ana asaɖaawo naho adzo.

english_verse: If both trumpets are blown, everyone is to meet with you at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ne woku kpẽ eveawo, eye wohe wo me la, ha blibo la nava ƒo ƒu ɖe gbɔwò le agbadɔ la nu.
