english_verse: But if just one is blown, only the twelve tribal leaders need to come together.
translation_verse: Ke ne woku kpẽ ɖeka ko la, Israel-ha la ƒe kplɔlawo kple toawo ƒe tatɔwo nava ƒo ƒu ɖe gbɔwò.

english_verse: Give a signal on a trumpet when it is time to break camp. The first blast will be the signal for the tribes camped on the east side, and the second blast will be the signal for those on the south.
translation_verse: Ne wogaku wo zi evelia eye wogatso wo kpukpukpui la, asaɖa si le anyigbeme gome la naho adzo. Ale woaku kpẽawo kpukpukpui ne èdi be ha la naho adzo,

english_verse: But when you want everyone to come together, sound a different signal on the trumpet.
translation_verse: ke woaku wo ahe wo me ne èdi be ha la nava kpe ta.

english_verse: The priests of Aaron's family will be the ones to blow the trumpets, and this law will never change.
translation_verse: Kpẽawo kulawo nanye Aron viŋutsu siwo nye nunɔlawo. Mia viwo nawɔ ɖoɖo si gbɔna le kpẽawo ŋu la dzi tso dzidzime yi dzidzime.

english_verse: Whenever you go into battle against an enemy attacking your land, give a warning signal on the trumpets. Then I, the Lord, will hear it and rescue you.
translation_verse: Ne miekpe aʋa kple futɔ aɖe le miaƒe anyigba dzi la, miku kpẽawo kpukpukpui, eye nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu, maɖo ŋku mia dzi, aɖe mi tso miaƒe futɔwo si me.

english_verse: During the celebration of the New Moon Festival and other religious festivals, sound the trumpets while you offer sacrifices. This will be a reminder that I am the Lord your God. The Israelites Begin Their Journey
translation_verse: Azɔ le miaƒe dzidzɔkpɔɣiwo, le kpɔɖeŋu me le ŋkekenyui ɖuɣiwo kple dzinu yeye ŋkekenyui ɖuɣiwo la, miku kpẽawo ne miele numemevɔ kple ŋutifafavɔ sam, eye wòana maɖo ŋku mia dzi. Nyee nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu.” Israelviwo ho dzo

english_verse: On the twentieth day of the second month of that same year, the cloud over the sacred tent moved on.
translation_verse: Le ƒè evelia ƒe ɣleti evelia ƒe ŋkeke bla evelia gbe la, alilikpo la ho le agbadɔ si me nubabla le la tame,

english_verse: So the Israelites broke camp and left the Sinai Desert. And some time later, the cloud stopped in the Paran Desert.
translation_verse: eye Israelviwo ho ɖe wo nɔewo yome tso Sinai-gbedadaƒo la dzo. Alilikpo la zɔ va tɔ ɖe Paran-gbedadaƒo.

english_verse: This was the first time the Lord had told Moses to command the people of Israel to move on.
translation_verse: Zi gbãtɔ nye esi woho esi Aƒetɔ de se na wo to Mose dzi.

english_verse: Judah and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out first, carrying their banner. Nahshon son of Amminadab was the leader of the Judah tribe,
translation_verse: Yuda viwo ƒe asaɖa lae hona gbã kple woƒe aflaga hamehame. Wo kplɔlae nye Naheson, Aminadab vi.

english_verse: Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the Issachar tribe,
translation_verse: Netaneel, Zuar vi, nye Isaxar-to ƒe aʋakɔkplɔla,

english_verse: and Eliab son of Helon was the leader of the Zebulun tribe.
translation_verse: eye Eliab, Xelon vi le Zebulon-to ƒe aʋakɔ nu.

english_verse: The sacred tent had been taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites carried it, marching behind the Judah camp.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, wokakaa agbadɔa, eye Gerson viwo kple Merari viwo tsɔa nuawo, eye wohona dzona.

english_verse: Reuben and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out second, carrying their banner. Elizur son of Shedeur was the leader of the Reuben tribe,
translation_verse: Eyome Ruben ƒe asaɖa la hona kple woƒe aflaga le ha vovovowo me eye woƒe aʋakɔ la kplɔlae nye Elizur, Sedeur vi.

english_verse: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was the leader of the Simeon tribe,
translation_verse: Simeon-to ƒe aʋakɔkplɔlae nye Selumiel, Zurisadai vi,

english_verse: and Eliasaph son of Deuel was the leader of the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: eye Elyasaf, Deguel vi, le Gad-to ƒe aʋakɔ nu.

english_verse: Next were the Kohathites, carrying the objects for the sacred tent, which was to be set up before they arrived at the new camp.
translation_verse: Emegbe Kehat viwo, siwo nye nu kɔkɔeawo tsɔlawo hona kple nuawo, eye kaka woawo naɖo afi si ameha nagaƒu asaɖa anyi le la, wotua agbadɔa ɖi xoxo.

english_verse: Ephraim and the tribes that camped alongside it marched next, carrying their banner. Elishama son of Ammihud was the leader of the Ephraim tribe,
translation_verse: Eyome Efrayim hona kple woƒe aflaga le ha vovovowo me, eye woƒe aʋakɔkplɔlae nye Elisama, Amihud vi.

english_verse: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was the leader of the Manasseh tribe,
translation_verse: Manase-to ƒe aʋakɔkplɔlae nye Gamaliel, Pedazur vi,

english_verse: and Abidan son of Gideoni was the leader of the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: eye Abidan, Gideon vie le Benyamin-to ƒe aʋakɔ nu.

english_verse: Dan and the tribes that camped alongside it were to protect the Israelites against an attack from behind, and so they marched last, carrying their banner. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was the leader of the tribe of Dan,
translation_verse: Dan-toe nye mamlɛtɔ si hona kple woƒe aflaga le hatsotso vovovowo me eye woawoe xea megbe na aʋakɔawo katã. Wo kplɔlae nye Axiezer, Amisadai vi.

english_verse: Pagiel son of Ochran was the leader of the Asher tribe,
translation_verse: Aser-to ƒe aʋakɔkplɔlae nye Pegiel, Oxran vi,

english_verse: and Ahira son of Enan was the leader of the Naphtali tribe.
translation_verse: eye Axira, Enan vie nye Naftali-to ƒe aʋakɔkplɔla.

english_verse: This was the order in which the Israelites marched each time they moved their camp.
translation_verse: Nenye be Israelviwo le ʋuʋum be yewoadzo ayi ɖaƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe teƒe bubu la, alea wohonae.

english_verse: Hobab the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses, was there. And Moses said to him, “We're leaving for the place the Lord has promised us. He has said that all will go well for us. So come along, and we will make sure that all goes well for you.”
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ na nyoa Hobab, Yetro, Midiantɔ la ƒe vi be: “Míeho yina ɖe teƒe si ŋugbe Aƒetɔ do be yeana mí la dzi. Edo ŋugbe na Israel be yeana nu nanyo nɛ, eya ta wò hã va míyi. Ne nu nyo na mí ko, enyo na wò hã.”

english_verse: “No, I won't go,” Hobab answered. “I'm returning home to be with my own people.”
translation_verse: Hobab ɖo eŋu be: “Gbeɖe, nyemayi o. Magbugbɔ ayi aƒe boŋ.”

english_verse: “Please go with us!” Moses said. “You can be our guide because you know the places to camp in the desert.
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ nɛ be: “Taflatsɛ, mègagblẽ mí ɖi nàdzo o. Ènya gbedadaƒo la, eye afi siwo míaƒu asaɖa anyi ɖo la le nyanya na wò, eya ta nɔ mía ŋu nàfia afɔɖoƒe mí.

english_verse: Besides that, if you go, we will give you a share of the good things the Lord gives us.”
translation_verse: Ne èyi kpli mí la, wò hã àkpɔ gome le nu nyui ɖe sia ɖe si Aƒetɔ ana mí la, me.” Dukɔa ho

english_verse: The people of Israel began their journey from Mount Sinai. They traveled three days, and the Levites who carried the sacred chest led the way, so the Lord could show them where to camp.
translation_verse: Ale dukɔ la ho tso Aƒetɔ ƒe to la gbɔ, eye wozɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃ ƒe mɔ. Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la dze wo ŋgɔ be wòatia teƒe si woaƒu asaɖa anyi ɖo la na wo.

english_verse: Each day as the Israelites began their journey, Moses would pray, “Our Lord, defeat your enemies and make them run!”
translation_verse: Ne aɖaka la ho ɣe sia ɣi la, Mose gblɔna be: “Aƒetɔ, tso ɖe wò futɔwo ŋu! Na woaka ahlẽ! Na woasí!”

english_verse: And when they stopped to set up camp, he would pray, “Our Lord, stay close to Israel's thousands and thousands of people.”
translation_verse: Ne aɖakaa tɔ la, egblɔna be: “O Aƒetɔ, gbugbɔ va Israelvi akpe ewo ƒe akpeawo dome!”

english_verse: One day the Israelites started complaining about their troubles. The Lord heard them and became so angry that he destroyed the outer edges of their camp with fire.
translation_verse: Dukɔ la gade asi liʋiliʋĩlilĩ me le Aƒetɔ ŋu be yewole fu kpem. Esi Aƒetɔ see la, edo dɔmedzoe, eye wòna dzo dze aƒe le wo dome, hebi nu le asaɖa la ƒe akpa aɖewo le eƒe gbɔto.

english_verse: When the people begged Moses to help, he prayed, and the fire went out.
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la do ɣli yɔ Mose. Edo gbe ɖa ɖe kuku na Aƒetɔ, eye dzoa tsi.

english_verse: They named the place “Burning,” because in his anger the Lord had set their camp on fire. The People Grumble about Being Hungry
translation_verse: Ale wona ŋkɔ teƒe ma be: “Dzobiƒe” elabe Aƒetɔ na dzo fiã nu le wo dome le afi ma. Mose tia kplɔla bla adrẽ

english_verse: One day some foreigners among the Israelites became greedy for food, and even the Israelites themselves began moaning, “We don't have any meat!
translation_verse: Amedzro aɖewo hã nɔ zɔzɔm kple Israelviwo. Lã nɔ ame siawo dzrom vevie eye woawo kple Israelviwo siaa galĩ liʋiliʋĩ be: “Ne ɖe míakpɔ lã aɖu la, anyo ŋutɔ.

english_verse: In Egypt we could eat all the fish we wanted, and there were cucumbers, melons, all kinds of onions, and garlic.
translation_verse: Esi míenɔ Egipte la, tɔmelã bɔ míeɖu wòti mí. Nenema kee nye adzamatre, aŋanyi, sabala vovovowo kple ayo hã.

english_verse: But we're starving out here, and the only food we have is this manna.”
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la, nyaa va glo! Naneke meli gbetɔ naɖu o, mana sia koe gbe sia gbe.”

english_verse: He prayed: I am your servant, Lord, so why are you doing this to me? What have I done to deserve this? You've made me responsible for all these people,
translation_verse: Egblɔ na Aƒetɔ be: “Nu ka ta nèlé dukɔ blibo sia ƒe agba ɖo ta nam be matsɔ?

english_verse: but they're not my children. You told me to nurse them along and to carry them to the land you promised their ancestors.
translation_verse: Nyee fɔ wo katã ƒe fu hedzia? Nu ka ta nèdi be matsɔ wo ɖe akɔ, abe ale si vitsɔla tsɔa vidzĩ ene, ayi anyigba si ŋu nèka atam le be yeatsɔ ana wo tɔgbuiwo la dzi?

english_verse: They keep whining for meat, but where can I get meat for them?
translation_verse: Afi ka makpɔ lã atsoe wòade ame siawo katã nu? Wole avi dzi le ŋkunye me le gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Na lã mí míaɖu!’

english_verse: This job is too much for me. How can I take care of all these people by myself?
translation_verse: Nye ɖeka nyemate ŋu atsɔ dukɔ blibo sia ƒe agba o. Ewu tsɔtsɔ nam.

english_verse: If this is the way you're going to treat me, just kill me now and end my miserable life! Seventy Leaders Are Chosen To Help Moses
translation_verse: Nenye alea nèbe yeawɔm la, ekem ve nunye nàwum zi ɖeka boŋ. Nyemanɔ anyi akpɔ nye gbɔɖiƒe o.”

english_verse: While I am talking with you there, I will give them some of your authority, so they can share responsibility for my people. You will no longer have to care for them by yourself.
translation_verse: Maɖi ava ƒo nu kpli wò le afi ma, eye maɖe gbɔgbɔ si le dziwò la ƒe ɖe ada ɖe wo dzi, bene woatsɔ dukɔa ƒe agba la ƒe ɖe na wò ti, ale be wò ɖeka magatsɔe o.

english_verse: As for the Israelites, I have heard them complaining about not having meat and about being better off in Egypt. So tell them to make themselves acceptable to me, because tomorrow they will have meat.
translation_verse: Ke gblɔ na dukɔ la be: ‘Mikɔ mia ɖokui ŋu hena etsɔ si gbɔna; miakpɔ lã aɖu elabe esi miefa avi gblɔ be ame kae ana lã yewo yewoaɖu mahã, eye miegblɔ hã be agbenɔnɔ dze dzi na yewo le Egipte wu la, Aƒetɔ see. Eya ta azɔ la, Aƒetɔ ana lã mi miaɖu.

english_verse: . They turned against me and wanted to go back to Egypt. Now they will eat meat until they get sick of it.
translation_verse: ke boŋ ɣleti ɖeka sɔŋ miaɖui va se ɖe esime woado to ŋɔti me na mi, anɔ ŋu nyɔm na mi. Elabe togbɔ be Aƒetɔ le mia dome hã la, miegbee, eye miefa avi be: ‘Nu ka ta gɔ̃ míedzo le Egipte ɖo?’ ”

english_verse: Even if we butchered all our sheep and cattle, or caught every fish in the sea, we wouldn't have enough to feed them.”
translation_verse: Alẽ alo nyi nenie woawu hafi wòade wo nu? Ɖe ƒumelãwo katã gɔ̃ hã ade wo nua?”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “I can do anything! Watch and you'll see my words come true.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu na Mose be: “Ɖe nèbu be nye ŋusẽ dzi ɖe kpɔtɔa? Ne nye nya la ava eme alo mava eme o hã la, èle ekpɔ ge.”

english_verse: Eldad and Medad were two leaders who had not gone to the tent. But when the Spirit took control of them, they began shouting like prophets right there in camp.
translation_verse: Ke ame tsitsi bla adrẽawo dometɔ eve tsi asaɖa la me. Wo ŋkɔwoe nye Eldad kple Medad. Woawo medo yi agbadɔ la gbɔ o. Gbɔgbɔ la va woawo hã dzi, eye wode asi gbeƒãɖeɖe ɖi me abe gbeƒãɖelawo ene.

english_verse: A boy ran to Moses and told him about Eldad and Medad.
translation_verse: Tete ɖekakpui aɖe ƒu du yi ɖagblɔ na Mose be: “Eldad kple Medad le gbeƒã ɖem abe Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo ene.”

english_verse: Joshua was there helping Moses, as he had done since he was young. And he said to Moses, “Sir, you must stop them!”
translation_verse: Yosua, Nun vi, ame si nye Mose ƒe kpeɖeŋutɔ tso ɖekakpuime ke la, gblɔ na Mose be: “Nye Aƒetɔ Mose, gbe na wo!”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “Are you concerned what this might do to me? I wish the Lord would give his Spirit to all his people so everyone could be a prophet.”
translation_verse: Mose ɖo eŋu be: “Wòe le ŋu ʋã ge ɖe nunyea? Ne Aƒetɔ ɖe wòana eƒe gbɔgbɔ la nava dukɔmetɔwo dzi, eye wo katã atrɔ zu eƒe gbeƒãɖelawo la, anyo ta.”

english_verse: Some time later the Lord sent a strong wind that blew quails in from the sea until Israel's camp was completely surrounded with birds, piled up about a meter high for many kilometers in every direction.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ na ya aɖe ƒo tso ƒu gome, eye wòlɔ tegliwo vɛ. Wodzo le ya me tso anyigba gbɔ kpuie abe meta ɖeka ko ene. Wodze ɖe anyigba ƒo xlã asaɖa la godoo va kpe le goawo katã me, va se ɖe esime wokɔ tso anyigba abe meta ɖeka ene, zɔzɔ aɖo wo gbɔ nye ŋkeke ɖeka ƒe azɔli.

english_verse: But before the meat could be eaten, the Lord became angry and sent a deadly disease through the camp.
translation_verse: Womekpɔ ɖu lã la vɔ hafi Aƒetɔ do dziku ɖe wo ŋu, eye wòna dɔléle vɔ̃ɖi aɖe ɖo wo dome o.

english_verse: After they had buried the people who had been so greedy for meat, they called the place “Graves for the Greedy.”
translation_verse: Eya ta wona ŋkɔ teƒe la be: “Nudzrolawo ɖiƒe” elabe afi mae woɖi ame siwo lã dzro vevie la ɖo.

english_verse: Israel then broke camp and traveled to Hazeroth.
translation_verse: Emegbe dukɔ la ho tso afi ma va Xazerot, eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe afi ma.

english_verse: and told Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to come to the entrance of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Enumake Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose, Aron kple Miryam be: “Mi ame etɔ̃a mido va nye agbadɔ gbɔ.” Wodo yi.

english_verse: There the Lord appeared in a cloud and told Aaron and Miriam to come closer.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖi va agbadɔ la nu le alilikpo dodo aɖe me heyɔ Aron kple Miryam. Wo kple evea do yi ŋgɔ,

english_verse: Then after commanding them to listen carefully, he said: “I, the Lord, speak to prophets in visions and dreams.
translation_verse: eye Aƒetɔ gblɔ be: “Mise nya si gblɔ ge mala na mi. Meɖea ɖokuinye fiaa ame si nye nye gbeƒãɖela le mia dome la le ŋutega me, eye meƒoa nu kplii le drɔ̃e me.

english_verse: But my servant Moses is the leader of my people.
translation_verse: Ke nyemewɔa alea na nye dɔla Mose ya o. Metsɔ nye dukɔ bliboa dzikpɔkpɔ de esi.

english_verse: He sees me face to face, and everything I say to him is perfectly clear. You have no right to criticize my servant Moses.”
translation_verse: Nye ŋutɔ meƒoa nu kplii ŋkume kple ŋkume, eye nyemeɣlaa nya aɖeke ɖee o; menana be nu sia nu me kɔna nɛ nyuie. Medzena nɛ kura gɔ̃ wòkpɔa Aƒetɔ ƒe nɔnɔme. Nu ka ta mievɔ̃a nuƒoƒo le nye dɔla Mose ŋu o?”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Aaron and Miriam. And after the Lord left
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ do dɔmedzoe ɖe wo ŋu hedzo.

english_verse: and the cloud disappeared from over the sacred tent, Miriam's skin turned white with leprosy. When Aaron saw what had happened to her,
translation_verse: Kasia esi alilikpo la nakɔ ɖa le agbadɔa dzi la, ŋutigbalẽdɔ vɔ̃ɖi aɖe si amewo vɔ̃na ŋutɔ la dze Miryam dzi enumake, eye eƒe ŋutigbalẽ fu kpii abe ɖetifu ene. Esi Aron trɔ kpɔe, eye wòkpɔ be edze ŋutigbalẽdɔ vɔ̃ɖi sia la,

english_verse: he said to Moses, “Sir, please don't punish us for doing such a foolish thing.
translation_verse: egblɔ na Mose be: “Meɖe kuku, bometsitsie na míewɔ nuvɔ̃ eya ta mègana woahe to na mí ɖe eta o.

english_verse: Don't let Miriam's flesh rot away like a child born dead!”
translation_verse: Mègana wòanɔ abe vidzĩ si ku ɖe dɔme na nɔa, eye eƒe akpa ɖeka ƒaƒã hafi wodzii la ene o.”

english_verse: Moses prayed, “Lord God, please heal her.”
translation_verse: Ale Mose do ɣli na Aƒetɔ be: “O, Mawu, meɖe kuku, yɔ dɔe dzro!”

english_verse: But the Lord replied, “Miriam would be disgraced for seven days if her father had punished her by spitting in her face. So make her stay outside the camp for seven days, before coming back.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu be: “Ɖe wònye tɔ́ae ɖe ta ɖe mo nɛ la, ŋu makpee ŋkeke adrẽ oa? Eya ta mina woasae ɖe aga wòanɔ asaɖa la godo ŋkeke adrẽ. Ema megbe la, woagakplɔe ava emee.”

english_verse: The people of Israel did not move their camp until Miriam returned seven days later.
translation_verse: Ale wode Miryam xɔ ɖe asaɖa la godo ŋkeke adrẽ, eye dukɔ la meho o, va se ɖe esime wogakplɔe va asaɖa la me.

english_verse: Then they left Hazeroth and set up camp in the Paran Desert.
translation_verse: Emegbe woho tso Xazerot, eye wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Paran-gbedadaƒo.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: In fact, we saw the Nephilim who are the ancestors of the Anakim. They were so big that we felt as small as grasshoppers.”
translation_verse: Míekpɔ Nefilim Anak viŋutsuwo, ame siwo dzɔ tso Nefilimwo me hã le afi ma; wonye ame dzɔtsu kakowo sɔŋ. Míawo ya ɖeko míedze sue abe abɔ ene le wo gbɔ, eye nenema tututu woawo hã kpɔ míi.”

english_verse: “Choose a leader from each tribe and send them into Canaan to explore the land I am giving you.”
translation_verse: “Tia ŋutsu ɖekaɖeka siwo nye kplɔlawo la tso toawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe me, eye nàdɔ wo ɖa ne woayi aɖatsa ŋku le Kanaan-nyigba si tsɔm mele na Israelviwo la dzi.”

english_verse: So Moses sent twelve tribal leaders from Israel's camp in the Paran Desert
translation_verse: Ale Mose dɔ wo ɖa tso Paran-gbedadaƒo, le Aƒetɔ ƒe gbeɖeɖe nu. Ŋutsuawo katã nye tatɔwo le Israelviwo dome.

english_verse: Before Moses sent them into Canaan, he said: After you go through the Southern Desert of Canaan, continue north into the hill country
translation_verse: Esi Mose dɔ wo la, egblɔ na wo be: “Miyi ɖe dzigbeme gome, eye miaɖo ta anyigbeme ahayi tonyigba la dzi.

english_verse: and find out what those regions are like. Be sure to remember how many people live there, how strong they are,
translation_verse: Milé ŋku ɖe anyigba la ƒe nɔnɔme kple edzinɔlawo ŋu. Mikpɔ ɖa be ame kakowoe le edzi loo, alo ame beliwoea? Wosɔ gbɔ loo, alo womesɔ gbɔ oa?

english_verse: and if they live in open towns or walled cities. See if the land is good for growing crops and find out what kinds of trees grow there. It's time for grapes to ripen, so try to bring back some of the fruit that grows there.

english_verse: But the people who live there are strong, and their cities are large and walled. We even saw the three Anakim clans.

translation_verse: Amalekitɔwo le anyigba la ƒe anyigbeme; Xititɔwo, Yebusitɔwo kple Amoritɔwo le towo dzi, eye Kanaantɔwo le Domeƒu la ŋu kple Yordan ƒe go ɖeka ŋu.”

english_verse: Caleb calmed down the crowd and said, “Let's go and take the land. I know we can do it!”
translation_verse: Ke Kaleb tsi nya ɖe ameawo nu heƒo nu de Mose dzi be: “Mina míayi fifi laa aɖaxɔ anyigba la. Ŋusẽ le mía ŋu míaɖu wo dzi.”

english_verse: But the other men replied, “Those people are much too strong for us.”

translation_verse: Nu ka ta gɔ̃ Aƒetɔ kplɔ mí va anyigba sia dzi ne míatsi aʋa? Woakplɔ mía srɔ̃wo kple mía viwo ayi aboyome. Ne míagbugbɔ ayi Egipte la, ɖe manyo na mí wu oa?”

english_verse: Then they said to one another, “Let's choose our own leader and go back.”

translation_verse: eye wogblɔ na ha blibo la be: “Anyigba si dzi míede ɖatsa ŋku la nyo ŋutɔŋutɔ.

english_verse: If we obey the Lord, he will surely give us that land rich with milk and honey.
translation_verse: Ne míaƒe nu dze Aƒetɔ ŋu ko la, akplɔ mí ayi afi mae, eye wòatsɔ anyigba si dzi notsi kple anyitsi bɔ ɖo na mí.

english_verse: So don't rebel. We have no reason to be afraid of the people who live there. The Lord is on our side, and they won't stand a chance against us!
translation_verse: Migadze aglã ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu o, eye migavɔ̃ ame siwo le afi ma la o. Míele wo dzi ɖu ge bɔbɔe. Aƒetɔ le mía dzi, eye wòɖu mawu siwo kpɔa wo ta la dzi xoxo, eya ta migavɔ̃ o.”

english_verse: Show us your great power, Lord. You promised
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ, ɖe wò ŋusẽ fia abe ale si nègblɔ ene be:

translation_verse: ‘Nye Aƒetɔ, nyemedoa dziku kabakaba o, eye nye lɔlɔ̃ metrɔna gbeɖe o. Metsɔa ame ƒe vodada kple dzidada kena, evɔ la nyemegbea tohehe na ame o, elabe ne tɔ́wo wɔ nuvɔ̃ la, mehea to na wo viwo tso dzidzime etɔ̃lia dzi va se ɖe enelia dzi.’

english_verse: You are merciful, and you treat people better than they deserve. So please forgive these people, just as you have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Eya ta, Aƒetɔ, meɖe kuku na wò, xa ɖe wò lɔlɔ̃ si metrɔna gbeɖe o la ta, nàtsɔ dukɔ sia ƒe vodada ake, abe ale si nèle ewɔm tso Egipte ke ene.”

english_verse: But as surely as I live and my power has no limit,
translation_verse: Gake le nyateƒe me, zi ale si mele agbe, eye nye ŋutikɔkɔe ayɔ xexeme bliboa la,

english_verse: I swear that not one of these Israelites will enter the land I promised to give their ancestors. These people have seen my power in Egypt and in the desert, but they will never see Canaan. They have disobeyed and tested me too many times.
translation_verse: Womade anyigba si ŋu meka atam le be mana wo tɔ́wo la dzi gbeɖe o. Wo dome ame siwo katã do vlom la made o.

english_verse: But my servant Caleb isn't like the others. So because he has faith in me, I will allow him to cross into Canaan, and his descendants will settle there.

translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose kple Aron be:

english_verse: to give this message to the people of Israel: You sinful people have complained against me too many times! Now I swear by my own life that I will give you exactly what you wanted.
translation_verse: Azɔ gblɔ na wo be, ‘Nye Aƒetɔ meta ɖokuinye be zi ale si mele agbe la, mawɔ nu si miegblɔ mese la na mi.

english_verse: You will die right here in the desert, and your dead bodies will cover the ground. You have insulted me, and none of you men who are over
translation_verse: Miaku, eye miaƒe ŋutilã akaka atsi gbedadaƒo afii. Esi mielĩ ŋunye ta la, mia dometɔ siwo katã xɔ ƒe bla eve kple vɔ, eye woxlẽ wo la, made anyigba la dzi o.

english_verse: You were worried that your own children would be captured. But I, the Lord, will let them enter the land you have rejected.
translation_verse: Miegblɔ be wole yewo viwo lé ge ayi aboyo mee, ke woawoe makplɔ ayi anyigba si miedo vlo la dzi.

english_verse: You will die here in the desert!
translation_verse: Ke miawo ya la, miaku, eye miaƒe ŋutilã aƒaƒã atsi gbedadaƒo le afii kokoko.

english_verse: So they got up early the next morning and got ready to head toward the hill country of Canaan. They said, “We were wrong to complain about the Lord. Let's go into the land that he promised us.”
translation_verse: Ŋdi kanya la, wodze mɔ. Wolia to la hegblɔ be: “Míele ŋudzɔ azɔ be míayi teƒe si ŋugbe Aƒetɔ do na mí la, elabe míewɔ nuvɔ̃.”

english_verse: You sinful people who ganged up against me will die here in the desert.

translation_verse: Yosua kple Kaleb koe tsi agbe le ame wui eve siwo de la dome. Israelviwo te kpɔ zi gbãtɔ be yewoaxɔ anyigba la (Mos V,

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: to give the Israelites the following laws about offering sacrifices:
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na Israelviwo be: Ne mieɖo anyigba si tsɔm mele na mi la dzi la, miwɔ ɖoɖo siawo dzi:

english_verse: Bulls or rams or goats are the animals that you may burn on the altar as sacrifices to please me. english_verse: If you are a native Israelite, you must obey these rules each time you offer a bull, a ram, or a goat as a sacrifice.

english_verse: When you eat food in the land that I am giving you, remember to set aside some of it as an offering to me.

english_verse: From the first batch of bread dough that you make after each new grain harvest, make a loaf of bread and offer it to me, just as you offer grain.

translation_verse: Gawu la, migatsɔe be le ɣeyiɣi si gbɔna me la, mia kple miaƒe dzidzimeviwo katã miewɔ se siwo katã Aƒetɔ de na mi to Mose dzi la dzi o.

english_verse: If all of you disobey one of my laws without knowing it, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice, a wine offering, and a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Ne ha blibo lae da vo le numanyamanya me la, ekema ha blibo la nana nyitsui ɖeka be woatsɔ asa numemevɔ si ʋẽna ɖe Aƒetɔ lílilĩ la. Le ɖoɖoa nu la, woawɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsa kple nunonovɔsa akpe ɖe eŋu. Gawu la, woana gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka be woatsɔ awɔ nuvɔ̃vɔsae.

english_verse: Then the priest will pray and ask me to forgive you. And since you did not mean to do wrong, and you offered sacrifices,

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong without knowing it, you must sacrifice a year-old female goat as a sacrifice for sin.

english_verse: The priest will then ask me to forgive you, and your sin will be forgiven.

translation_verse: Ame sia gbe Aƒetɔ ƒe nya si wògblɔ, eye wòda eƒe se dzi eya ta ele be woawui kokoko. Eya ŋutɔe na wowui; ame aɖeke meɖi fɔ le ewuwu me o.” Ŋutsu si da dzudzɔgbese la dzi

english_verse: Once, while the Israelites were traveling through the desert, a man was caught gathering firewood on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Esime Israelviwo nɔ gbedadaƒo la, wokpɔ ŋutsu aɖe si nɔ nake fɔm le dzudzɔgbe.

english_verse: He was taken to Moses, Aaron, and the rest of the community.
translation_verse: Ame siwo kpɔ ŋutsua la, kplɔe va Mose, Aron kple ha blibo la gbɔe.

english_verse: Korah, here is what you and your followers must do: Get some fire pans, fill them with coals and incense, and place them near the sacred tent. And the man the Lord chooses will be his priest. Korah, this time you Levites have gone too far!
translation_verse: miɖe dzo kɔ ɖe wo me, eye miatsɔ lifi ada ɖe edzi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume etsɔ. Ame si Aƒetɔ atia la, eyae anye ame kɔkɔe la. Mia tɔ va glo, Levi viwo!”

english_verse: You know that the God of Israel has chosen you Levites from all Israel to serve him by being in charge of the sacred tent and by helping the community to worship in the proper way. What more do you want?
translation_verse: Esi Israel ƒe Mawu la tia mi tso Israel-ha la me, be miate ɖe eŋu, awɔ dɔ le eƒe agbadɔ la me, anɔ ha la nu, eye miasubɔ wo ɖe, mesɔ gbɔ na mi oa?

english_verse: The Lord has given you a special responsibility, and now, Korah, you think you should also be his priest.
translation_verse: Gawu la, ena wò kple nɔviwò Levi viwo katã hã mietsɔ ɖe egbɔ. Nunɔladɔ hãe miagadia?

english_verse: You and your followers have rebelled against the Lord, not against Aaron.
translation_verse: Ame kae nye Aron mianɔ eŋu lĩm? Eya ta Aƒetɔ ŋue wò kple yowòmedzelawo katã miedze aglã ɖo.”

english_verse: Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, but they sent back this message: “We won't come!
translation_verse: Mose dɔ ame be woayɔ Datan kple Abiram vɛ, ke wogblɔ be: “Míegbɔna o.

english_verse: It's bad enough that you took us from our rich farmland in Egypt to let us die here in the desert. Now you also want to boss us around!
translation_verse: Esi nèkplɔ mí tso anyigba vavã, si dzi nu bɔ ɖo la dzi, be yeava wu le gbedadaƒo le afii ɖe, mesɔ gbɔ na wò oa? Amegã hã ɖu ge nàla ɖe mía dzi!

english_verse: Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Don't listen to these men! I haven't done anything wrong to them. I haven't taken as much as a donkey.”
translation_verse: Tete Mose do dɔmedzoe vevie, eye wògblɔ na Aƒetɔ be: “Mègaxɔ woƒe vɔsa o. Nyemewɔ vɔ̃ ɖe wo dometɔ aɖeke ŋu o; nyemexɔ tedzi ɖeka gɔ̃ hã le wo dometɔ aɖeke si o.”

english_verse: Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ na Korax be: “Etsɔ la, wò kple tɔwòawo katã miva Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Aron hã le vava ge.

english_verse: Each of you take along your fire pan with incense in it and offer the incense to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na mia dome ame sia ame natsɔ eƒe dzudzɔdosonu, ada dzudzɔdonu ɖe eme eye woava Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Dzudzɔdosonu alafa eve bla atɔ̃ wòanye, ame sia ame kple etɔ. Wò kple Aron hã miatsɔ mia tɔwo vɛ.”

english_verse: The next day the men placed incense and coals in their fire pans and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ale ame sia ame tsɔ eƒe dzudzɔdosonu, ɖe dzo ɖe eme, eye wòtsɔ dzudzɔdonu da ɖe edzi heva tsi tsitre ɖe godoƒegbadɔ la ƒe mɔnu le Mose kple Aron gbɔ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders. When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory
translation_verse: Korax ƒo ha blibo la nu ƒu, eye wotsi tsitre dze ŋgɔ Mose kple Aron le agbadɔ la ƒe mɔnu. Kasia Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe do ɖe ha blibo la ŋkume zi ɖeka,

english_verse: and said to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: eye Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose kple Aron be:

english_verse: “Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
translation_verse: “Mite yi adzɔge le ha sia gbɔ! Matsrɔ̃ wo fifi laa!”

english_verse: But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
translation_verse: Ke Mose kple Aron tsyɔ mo anyi hegblɔ be: “Oo, Mawu, wò si nye gbɔgbɔ le amegbetɔwo katã me, ɖe ame ɖeka awɔ nuvɔ̃, eye nàdo dɔmedzoe ɖe ha blibo la ŋua?”

english_verse: The Lord answered Moses,
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: “Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na ha la be woahe yi megbe tso Korax, Datan kple Abiram ƒe agbadɔwo gbɔ.”

english_verse: Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed.
translation_verse: Mose tso, Israel-me tsitsiwo kplɔe ɖo, eye wòyi Datan kple Abiram gbɔ.

english_verse: Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ na ha la be: “Mite yi adzɔge tso ame vɔ̃ɖi siawo ƒe agbadɔ gbɔ. Migaka asi woƒe naneke ŋu o, ne menye nenem o la, mi kpli wo siaa miatsrɔ̃ le woƒe nuvɔ̃wo ta.”

english_verse: So everyone moved away from those tents, except Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and their families.
translation_verse: Ale wote yi adzɔge le Korax, Datan kple Abiram ƒe agbadɔwo ŋu. Datan kple Abiram do go ɖe woƒe agbadɔwo nu, eye wo viwo kpe ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know:
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ na ameawo be: “Miadze sii to nu sia wɔwɔ me be Aƒetɔ ye dɔm be mawɔ dɔ siawo katã, eye menye nye ŋutɔ ko tso wɔ wo o.

english_verse: But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ke ne Aƒetɔ awɔ nu masekpɔ aɖe ale be anyigba nake nu ami ame siawo kple woƒe nunɔamesiwo katã, eye woayi tsiẽƒe agbagbee la, ekema mianyae be woawoe do vlo Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up
translation_verse: Kaka wòawu nya la nu la, anyigba wó le Datan kple Abiram te

english_verse: and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
translation_verse: Ale woawo kple woƒe nunɔamesiwo katã yi tsiẽƒe agbagbee. Anyigba tu ɖe wo nu, eye wotsrɔ̃ gbidii le ha la dome.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
translation_verse: Israelvi siwo katã ƒo xlã wo le afi ma la sí kple du, esi wose woƒe ɣlidodo. Wogblɔ be: “Netsɔ! Anyigba ava mi míawo hã!”

english_verse: Suddenly the Lord sent a fire that burned up the
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ na dzo va fiã ŋutsu alafa eve bla atɔ̃ siwo tsɔ dzudzɔdonu vɛ la. Nutɔgbawo

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Emegbe Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: “Tell Aaron's son Eleazar to take the fire pans from the smoldering fire and scatter the coals. The pans are now sacred,
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na Eleazar, nunɔla Aron vi la be nefɔ dzudzɔdosonuawo le teƒe si dzoa bi ameawo le la, eye wòakaka dzoka siwo le wo me la ɖe adzɔge, elabe sonuawo zu kɔkɔe.

english_verse: because they were used for offering incense to me. Have them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar. Those men died because of their sin, and now their fire pans will become a warning for the rest of the community.”
translation_verse: Nu vɔ̃ wɔla mawo ƒe ku na be sonu siwo wotsɔ va Aƒetɔ ŋkume la ŋu va kɔ. Eya ta ƒo wo gbadzaa nàfa ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ŋu be wòanɔ afi ma anye ŋkuɖodzinu na Israelviwo.”

english_verse: Eleazar collected the pans and had them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar,
translation_verse: Ale nunɔla Eleazar fɔ akɔblidzudzɔdosonuawo, eye woƒo wo gbadzaa tsɔ fa ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ŋu.

english_verse: just as the Lord had told Moses. The pans were a warning to the Israelites that only Aaron's descendants would be allowed to offer incense to the Lord. Anyone else who tried to would be punished like Korah and his followers. The Israelites Rebel and Are Punished
translation_verse: Wowɔ esia be wòana Israelviwo nanɔ ŋku ɖom edzi be ame si menye nunɔla tso Aron ƒe dzidzime o la, nagate ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ŋu be yeatɔ dzo lifi na Aƒetɔ o. Ne ewɔe la, eya hã atsrɔ̃ abe Korax kple eyomedzelawo ene. Ale wowɔ nu siawo katã abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Eleazar to Mose dzi be woawɔ wo ene. Aron xɔ dukɔa ɖe agbe

english_verse: The next day the people of Israel again complained against Moses and Aaron, “The two of you killed some of the Lord's people!”
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, Israelviwo ƒe ha blibo la lĩ liʋiliʋĩ le Mose kple Aron ŋu gblɔ be: “Miawoe wu Aƒetɔ ƒe ame aɖewo.”

english_verse: As the people crowded around them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the sacred tent, and the Lord appeared in his glory in the cloud covering the tent.
translation_verse: Wokpe ta tsi tre ɖe Mose kple Aron ŋu, eye wotrɔ ɖo ta godoƒegbadɔ la gbɔ. Kasia woakpɔ la, alilikpo tsyɔ agbadɔ la dzi eye Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe do ɖe afi ma.

english_verse: So Moses and Aaron walked to the front of the tent,
translation_verse: Tete Mose kple Aron do va agbadɔ la ŋgɔ,

english_verse: where the Lord said to them,
translation_verse: eye Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: “Stand back! I am going to wipe out these Israelites once and for all.” They immediately bowed down and prayed.
translation_verse: “Mite yi megbe le ha sia ŋu! Matsrɔ̃ wo fifi laa!” Wo ame eve la tsyɔ mo anyi,

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Grab your fire pan and fill it with hot coals from the altar. Put incense in it, then quickly take it to where the people are and offer it to the Lord, so they can be forgiven. The Lord is very angry, and people have already started dying!”
translation_verse: eye Mose gblɔ na Aron be: “Tsɔ wò dzudzɔdosonu la nàɖe dzo ɖe eme le vɔsamlekpui la dzi, eye nàtsɔ lifi da ɖe edzi. Netsɔ! Wɔ kaba nàtsɔe yi ha la gbɔ ɖakɔ wo ŋuti alé avu. Aƒetɔ do dɔmedzoe, eye dɔ vɔ̃ de asi nugbegblẽ me xoxo.”

english_verse: Aaron walked back and stood with Moses at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Esi dɔ vɔ̃ la nu tso la, Aron gatrɔ va Mose gbɔ le godoƒegbadɔ la nu.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you.
translation_verse: Emegbe tsɔ wo da ɖe nye agbadɔ la me le nubablaɖaka la ŋgɔ, afi si medoa go mi le.

english_verse: I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
translation_verse: Ame si ke matia la ƒe atizɔti adzè. To esia me mana Israelviwo adzudzɔ liʋiliʋĩlilĩ le mia ŋu.”

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Ale Mose gblɔ nya la na Israelviwo, eye woƒe tatɔwo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe tsɔ atizɔti ɖeka nɛ. Atizɔti wui evee wotsɔ vɛ; Aron tɔ hã le wo dome.

english_verse: Moses took them and placed them in the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mose lɔ atizɔtiawo katã va kɔ ɖe agbadɔ la me le nubablaɖaka la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: The next day when Moses went into the tent, flowers and almonds were already growing on Aaron's stick.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke, eye Mose yi ɖe agbadɔa me la, ekpɔ be Aron ƒe atizɔti si nye Levi viwo tɔ la dzè. Edo loto, ƒo se, tse yevuzi, eye kutsetseawo ɖi.

english_verse: Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
translation_verse: Tete Mose fɔ atizɔtiawo katã tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ va Israelviwo katã gbɔe. Wokpɔ wo, eye to ɖe sia ɖe ƒe tatɔ tsɔ eya ŋutɔ tɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Gbugbɔ Aron ƒe atizɔti la ya yi ɖada ɖe nubablaɖaka la ŋgɔ. Wonedzrae ɖo ɖe afi ma ne wòanye dzesi na Israelvi aglãdzelawo, woatsɔ anɔ ŋku ɖom edzi be, ne womedzudzɔ liʋiliʋĩlilĩ le ŋunye o la, woaku.”

english_verse: Moses did what he was told.
translation_verse: Mose wɔ nu si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites cried out to Moses, “We're done for
translation_verse: Israelviwo gblɔ na Mose be: “Kpɔ ɖa, míetsrɔ̃ vɔ! Evɔ na mí! Evɔ na mí katã!

english_verse: and doomed if we even go near the sacred tent!”
translation_verse: Ne ame te ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe agbadɔ ŋu ko wòazu nu kuku la, ekema míetsrɔ̃ vɔ keŋ ɖe!”

english_verse: The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent.
translation_verse: Ne wò kple viwò ŋutsuwo miele subɔsubɔdɔ wɔm le agbadɔ la ŋgɔ la, kplɔ Levi-to la me tɔwo, ame siwo nye nɔviwòwo la vɛ be woava kpe ɖe ŋuwò miawɔ subɔsubɔdɔ la.

english_verse: You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die.
translation_verse: Woawɔ dɔ siwo katã le ŋuwò kple esiwo ku ɖe agbadɔ la ŋu la ko. Womegate ɖe nu kɔkɔe siwo le kɔkɔeƒe la ŋu loo, alo ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ŋu o. Ne wote ɖe wo ŋu la, wò kple woawo siaa miaku.

english_verse: No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it.
translation_verse: Woawo ko nanɔ ŋuwò anɔ dɔ siwo katã ku ɖe agbadɔ la ŋu wɔm eye ame bubu aɖeke megate ɖe mia ŋu o.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: Miawo koe awɔ subɔsubɔdɔ siwo ku ɖe kɔkɔeƒe la kple vɔsamlekpuia ŋu, ale be nyemagado dɔmedzoe ɖe Israelviwo ŋu azɔ o.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Nye ŋutɔe tia mia nɔvi Levi viwo tso Israelviwo dome tsɔ na wò. Mekɔ wo ŋu da ɖi be woawɔ subɔsubɔdɔ le nye agbadɔ la ŋu.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ke wò kple viwò ŋutsuwo koe awɔ nunɔladɔ siwo katã ku ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ŋu kple esiwo le Kɔkɔeƒe ƒe Kɔkɔeƒe la. Miaƒe dɔdeasie nye esia koŋ elabe nunɔladɔ la, nunana wònye na mi. Ne ame bubu aɖe te va nu kɔkɔeawo gbɔ la, wonewui.” Nunɔlawo ƒe gome

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Gake woƒe lã ya tɔwòe, abe ale si akɔa kple ɖusita siwo nye teƒe tɔxɛwo la nye tɔwò ene.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Ele be miaɖu nu siawo le teƒe kɔkɔe, eye ŋutsuwo koe kpɔ mɔ aɖui. Nu kɔkɔe wònye na wò.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: Hekpe ɖe esiawo ŋu la, nunana bubu siwo katã Israelviwo ana be woanyè la nye tɔwò. Enye wò ŋutɔ, viwò ŋutsuwo kple viwò nyɔnuwo siaa ƒe gome. Ame sia ame si ŋu kɔ le kɔa nu le aƒewò me la kpɔ mɔ aɖui, eye esia nanye ɖoɖo si anɔ anyi ɖaa.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: Mele ami, wain kple bli nyuitɔ siwo katã Israelviwo kpɔna tso woƒe dɔwɔwɔ me vana nam la tsɔm na wò.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: Nu sia nu si Israelviwo tsɔ ɖe adzɔgbe be wòanye tɔnye tegbee la nanye tɔwò.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: Nu sia nu si aʋu dɔ nu na nɔa, ame wòɖanye o, lã wòɖanye o, eye wotsɔe nam la nye tɔwò. Togbɔ be wòle alea hã, ele be nàtsɔ ga axɔ amewo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo kple lã makɔmakɔwo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwoe.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Woaxɔ ɖevi siwo xɔ ɣleti ɖeka la kple klosaloga atɔ̃, le gagbagba si li la ƒe ɖoɖo nu. Gera bla eve nanye klosaloga ɖeka.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: Ke mègatsɔ ga xɔ nyiwo, alẽwo kple gbɔ̃wo ƒe ŋgɔgbeviwoe o, elabe wo ŋu kɔ. Nàhlẽ woƒe ʋu ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ŋu, eye nàtɔ dzo woƒe ami wòanye dzovɔsa si ƒe ʋeʋẽ lílilĩ dzea Aƒetɔ ŋu.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: “Metsɔ adzɔ siwo katã Israelviwo ɖena nam abe nunana kɔkɔe ene la na wò, viwò ŋutsuwo kple viwò nyɔnuwo, eye esia nanye ɖoɖo si anɔ anyi ɖaa. Nubabla matrɔmatrɔ wònye mewɔ kple wò kple wò dzidzimeviwo tegbee.”

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Aron be: “Naneke manye tɔwò si anye domenyinu le woƒe anyigba dzi o, eye anyigba aɖeke hã manye tɔwò gome le wo dome o. Nye Aƒetɔ e nye wò nu sia nu.” Levi viwo ƒe gome

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ be: “Metsɔ nuwo katã ƒe akpa ewolia si Israelviwo ɖena nam la na Levi viwo be wòanye wo tɔ. Esia nye subɔsubɔdɔ si wɔm wole le nye agbadɔ ŋu la ƒe fetu.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la, Levi viwo ko nawɔ subɔsubɔdɔ le nye agbadɔ la ŋu, eye ne vodada aɖe va la, enye woƒe nya. Esia nanye ɖoɖo si anɔ anyi ɖaa tso dzidzime yi dzidzime le mia dome. Domenyinu aɖeke manɔ Levi vi, siwo le Israelviwo dome la si o;

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na Levi viwo be: Ne miexɔ nuwo ƒe akpa ewolia si mexɔ le Israelviwo si na mi, be wòanye miaƒe domenyinu le wo si la, miɖe akpa ewolia le eŋu na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Woabu adzɔ tɔxɛ si miana la abe miawo ŋutɔe ɖe bli alo fiã wain va na ene.

english_verse: so the best of what you receive will be mine.
translation_verse: Miɖe nu siwo katã woana mi la ƒe nyuitɔwo tsɔ na adzɔ Aƒetɔ abe nunana kɔkɔe ene.

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: Ne mieɖe nyuitɔwo le wo ŋu na adzɔe la, ekema woabu susɔea abe Levi viwo ŋutɔe xa nu le agble me alo fiã wain, eye woɖe nyuitɔ va na adzɔe ene.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mia kple miaƒe ƒometɔwo miekpɔ mɔ aɖu susɔea le afi sia afi faa, elabe eyae nye subɔsubɔdɔ si wɔm miele le agbadɔa ŋu la ƒe fetu.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Ne mienyaɖe nyuitɔ le wo ŋu na adzɔe ko la, vɔ̃ aɖeke manɔ mia dzi o. Ke mikpɔ nyuie ne miagagblẽ kɔ ɖo na Israelviwo ƒe nunana kɔkɔewo hafi aɖe nyuitɔwo ana o. Ne miewɔe la, miaku.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: “Se si Aƒetɔ de lae nye esi: “Milé nyinɔ dzẽ si sɔ keŋ, nu mewɔ afi aɖeke nɛ o, eye womede kɔkuti kɔ nɛ wòwɔ dɔ kpɔ o la vɛ.

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: Mitsɔe na nunɔla Eleazar, ne wòana woakplɔe ayi asaɖa la godo, eye woawui le eŋkume.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Nunɔla Eleazar nede asi eƒe ʋu me hlẽ ɖo ɖe afi si nye agbadɔ la dze ŋgɔe lɔƒo zi adrẽ.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: Azɔ woatɔ dzo nyinɔ blibo la; eƒe agbalẽ, lã, ʋu kple dɔmenuwo katã nafiã.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Nunɔla la natsɔ sederti ƒe akpa aɖe, hisɔp kple ka dzẽ aƒu gbe ɖe dzo si le nyinɔa fiãm la me.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Emegbe nunɔla la nanya eƒe awuwo eye wòale tsi. Ekpɔ mɔ azɔ atrɔ yi ɖe asaɖa la me; ke eŋu mekɔ o, le kɔa nu, va se ɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Ame si tɔ dzo nyinɔa hã nanya eƒe awuwo, eye wòale tsi; ke eya hã ŋu mekɔ o, le kɔa nu, va se ɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Azɔ ŋutsu si ŋu kɔ le kɔa nu la nalɔ nyinɔ la ƒe afi la atsɔ yi teƒe kɔkɔe aɖe le asaɖa la godo, eye wòadzrae ɖo ɖe afi ma na Israelviwo ƒe ha la. Dzofi sia ŋudɔe woawɔ ne wole ameŋukɔtsi wɔm be woasa vɔ atsɔ ɖe nuvɔ̃ ɖa.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ame si lɔ nyinɔ ƒe afia nanya eƒe awuwo, eye eŋu mekɔ o, le kɔa nu, va se ɖe fiẽ. Esia nanye ɖoɖo si anɔ anyi ɖaa na Israelviwo kple amedzro siwo le wo gbɔ la. Tete ɖe ame kuku ŋu

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe ka asi ame kuku ŋu la, eŋu mekɔ o, le kɔa nu, va se ɖe esime ŋkeke adrẽ nava yi.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: Atsɔ tsi la akɔ eɖokui ŋu le ŋkeke etɔ̃lia kple adrẽlia gbe, eye eŋuti akɔ. Evɔ ne mekɔ eɖokui ŋu le ŋkeke etɔ̃lia kple adrẽlia gbe o la, eŋu makɔ o.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ne ame aɖe ka asi ame kuku ŋu, eye mekɔ eɖokui ŋu o la, ede busu eɖokui ŋu eye eŋu mekɔ o, elabe womewú ameŋukɔtsi ɖe eŋu o. Ame sia do gu Aƒetɔ ƒe nɔƒe la eya ta ele be woaɖee ɖa le Israelviwo dome.”

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: “Se bubue nye be ne ame ku le agbadɔ aɖe me la, ame si le agbadɔa me kplii hafi wòku kple ame si va ge ɖe agbadɔa me la siaa ŋu mekɔ o, le kɔa nu, va se ɖe esime ŋkeke adrẽ nava yi.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Ame sia ame si yi gbe me, eye wòka asi ame si wowu kple yi ŋu, alo ame kuku aɖe ŋu, alo ameƒu ŋu alo yɔdo ŋu la ŋu mekɔ o, ŋkeke adrẽ.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Gbã la, ŋutsu si ŋu kɔ la natsɔ hisɔp ade tsi la me awu ɖe agbadɔ la, emenuwo katã kple ame siwo katã le afi ma la ŋu. Nenema ke woawui ɖe ame si ka asi ameƒu, ame si wowu, ame kuku alo yɔdo ŋu la hã ŋui.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke etɔ̃a kple adrẽa gbe la, ame si ŋu kɔ le kɔa nu la nawu tsia ɖe ame si ŋu mekɔ o la ŋu. Emegbe ame la anya eƒe awuwo, eye wòale tsi ekema le fiẽ me la, eŋu kɔ.”

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: “Ke ame si ŋu mekɔ o, eye mekɔ eɖokui ŋu o la, de busu eɖokui ŋu eye eŋu mekɔ o elabe womewú ameŋukɔtsi la ɖe eŋu o. Ame sia do gu Aƒetɔ ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la eya ta ele be woaɖee ɖa le ha la me.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Esia nanye ɖoɖo si anɔ anyi ɖaa na mi. Ame si wú ameŋukɔtsia la nanya eƒe awuwo, eye ne ame aɖe ka asi ameŋukɔtsia ŋu la, eŋu makɔ o va se ɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Nenema ke nu sia nu si ŋu ame si ŋu mekɔ o la ka asii la ŋu mekɔ o, eye ne ame aɖe ka asi nu ma ŋu la, eya hã ŋu mekɔ o va se ɖe fiẽ.”

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti gbãtɔ me la, Israelviwo ƒe ha blibo la va Zin-gbedadaƒo, eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Kades. Miryam ku le afi ma eye woɖii ɖe afi ma.

english_verse: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Tsi aɖeke menɔ afi si woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖo o, eya ta wokpe ta eye wotsi tre ɖe Mose kple Aron ŋu.

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Wowɔ dzre kple Mose be: “Ne míawo hã ɖe míeku le Aƒetɔ ƒe agbadɔa ŋgɔ kple mía nɔvi Israelvi mawo la, ne enyo wu!

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Nu ka ta gɔ̃ miekplɔ mí va gbedadaƒo le afii? Menye esi mí kple míaƒe lãhawo míava ku ɖi tae oa?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Nu ka ta miekplɔ mí dzoe le Egipte va teƒe vlo sia, afi si nuku aɖeke mawɔ le o? Bli, gboti, wain kple yevuboɖati aɖeke mele afi sia o. Tsi teti hã meli ame nano o!”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Tete Mose kple Aron dzo le ha la gbɔ heyi ɖe godoƒegbadɔ la ƒe mɔnu. Wotsyɔ mo anyi, eye Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe klẽ ɖe wo dzi.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: “Tsɔ atikplɔ si le nubablaɖaka la ŋgɔ, eye wò kple Aron miaƒo ha blibo la nu ƒu. Ƒo nu kple agakpe la le wo ŋkume be nena tsi nado tso eme. Aleae miawɔ ana tsi nado tso agakpe la me ne ha la kple woƒe lãwo nano.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mose yi ɖatsɔ atikplɔ la abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ ene.

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: Eya kple Aron ƒo ha la nu ƒu ɖe agakpe la ŋgɔ, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Mi aglãdzela siawo! Misee! Ɖe míate ŋu ana tsi nado tso agakpe sia me na mia?”

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Tete Mose kɔ atikplɔ la dzi, ƒo agakpe la zi eve, eye tsi do bababa tso eme na ha la kple woƒe lãwo wono.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose kple Aron be: “Esi miexɔ dzinye se bliboe o, eye miekɔ ŋunye le Israelviwo ŋkume o ta la, nyemana miakplɔ ha sia ade anyigba si metsɔ na wo la dzi o.”

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Esia nye Meriba-tsi. Afi siae Israelviwo wɔ dzre kple Aƒetɔ le, eye wòɖe eɖokui fia wo le be ɖe yele kɔkɔe. Edom-fia gbe mɔnana Israelviwo

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Mose dɔ dɔlawo le Kades ɖo ɖe Edom-fia gbɔ. Amedɔdɔawo gblɔ nɛ be: “Wò ŋutɔ ènya nu sesẽ siwo dzɔ ɖe mía dzi.

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: Ènya be mía tɔgbuiwo ʋu va Egipte, eye míenɔ afi ma eteƒe didi. Egiptetɔwo sẽ tame le mí kple mía tɔgbuiwo ŋu,

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: eye míedo ɣli yɔ Aƒetɔ be nexɔ na mí. Ese míaƒe ɣlidodo, eye wòdɔ mawudɔla aɖe ɖa wòva kplɔ mí tso Egipte. Azɔ míeva ɖo Kades si nye du si le wò liƒo dzi la me.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Míeɖe kuku, nà míato wò anyigba me ayi. Míele agble alo wainbɔwo me to ge o. Míele vudo aɖeke me tsi hã no ge o. Míato fia ƒe mɔ gã dzi tẽe, eye míadze ɖe afi aɖeke o, va se ɖe esime míato wò anyigba me ayi.”

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Ke Edom ɖo eŋu be: “Míana miato afii ava yi o. Ne mietee kpɔ la, matso ɖe mia ŋu awɔ aʋa kpli mi.”

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Tete Israelviwo gblɔ nɛ be: “Mɔ gã dzi ko míedi be míato ayi. Ne míawo loo, alo míaƒe lãwo no miaƒe tsi la, míaxe fe ɖe eta. Ɖeko míedi be míazɔ edzi ayi; evɔ. Míedi naneke wu esia o.”

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Ke woawo gaɖo eŋu be: “Míegbe. Miele edzi to ge ayi akpɔ o!” Ale Edomtɔwo tso ɖe wo ŋu kple aʋakɔ sesẽ aɖe be ne wokatsa la, yewoawɔ aʋa kpli wo.

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Esi Edomtɔwo gbe be Israelviwo mato yewoƒe anyigba dzi ayi o ta la, wodze to mɔ bubu to wo ŋu yi. Aron ƒe ku

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Israel ƒe ha blibo la ho tso Kades, eye wova Hor-to gbɔ.

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: “Aron made anyigba si ŋugbe medo na Israelviwo la dzi o. Aku, elabe mi ame evea miesẽ to gbe nye gbe dzi wɔwɔ le Meriba.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Kplɔ Aron kple via ŋutsu Eleazar yi Hor-to la dzi.”

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: Ɖe eƒe awuwo le eŋu nàdo na via Eleazar; ke Aron aku ɖe afi ma.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Mose wɔ abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ ene. Wolia to la le ha blibo la ŋkume,

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: eye Mose ɖe awuawo le Aron ŋu hedo na via Eleazar. Ale Aron ku le toa tame le afi ma, eye Mose kple Eleazar ɖi tso toa dzi.

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Esi ha blibo la kpɔ be Aron megali o la, wofae ŋkeke bla etɔ̃ sɔŋ.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Esi woho tso Hor-to la gbɔ la, woɖo ta Aƒlaƒu la nu be woaɖe Edom-nyigba ɖe axadzi. Ke dukɔ la de dzi do ge le mɔa dzi do kpoe,

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: eye wogblɔ nyawo ɖe Mawu kple Mose ŋu. Wogblɔ be: “Nu ka ta miekplɔ mí tso Egipte va gbedadaƒo le afii be míava ku ɖi? Nuɖuɖu kple tsi aɖeke meli o. Gawu la, nuɖuɖu vlo sia le ŋu nyɔm na mí!”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ ɖo da vɔ̃ɖiwo ɖe wo dome siwo ɖu wo ale be ame geɖe ku le Israel.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Dukɔ la va Mose gbɔ va gblɔ nɛ be: “Míewɔ nuvɔ̃ be míegblɔ nya ɖe wò kple Aƒetɔ ŋu. Ɖe kuku na Aƒetɔ na mí ne wòana daawo nadzo le mía dome.” Ale Mose do gbe ɖa ɖe dukɔa ta.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Wɔ da vɔ̃ɖi la ƒe dzedzeme, eye nàtsɔe ku ɖe ati ŋu, ale be ne da ɖu ame aɖe wòkpɔe ko wòatsi agbe.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Ale Mose tsɔ akɔbli wɔ da heku ɖe ati ŋu, eye ne da ɖu ame aɖe wòkpɔ akɔblida la ko la, etsia agbe. Israelviwo ho tso Hor-to la gbɔ yi Moabtɔwo ƒe bali me

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Israelviwo ho va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Obot.

english_verse: and then in the Zered Gorge.
translation_verse: Woho tso afi ma heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Zered-bali me.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Esi wotso le afi ma la, wova gbedadaƒo le Arnon-tɔsisi si dzɔ tso Amoritɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi la nu. Arnon-tɔsisi nye liƒo le Moabtɔwo kple Amoritɔwo dome.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Esia tae woŋlɔ ɖe “Aƒetɔ ƒe aʋawɔwɔwo ŋutinyagbalẽ” me be: “Waheb-du le Sufa-nutome kple Arnon-baliwo

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: kple tɔʋu la ƒe go si ɖo ta Ar-nutowo me, eye wòdo liƒo na Moab.”

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Emegbe woho tso afi ma, eye wova vudo aɖe gbɔ. Vudo sia ŋue Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose le be: “Ƒo dukɔ la nu ƒu ne mana tsi wo.”

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, Israelviwo dzi ha sia be: “Vudo, dzi! Midzi ha nɛ!

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Vudo si fiaviwo ɖe. Vudo si bubumewo ɖe. Woƒe atikplɔ kple woƒe atizɔtiwoe wotsɔ ɖee.” Esi wotso le gbedadaƒo sia la, wova Matana.

english_verse: then at Nahaliel, and then at Bamoth.
translation_verse: Wotso le Matana va Naxaliel, eye tso Naxaliel wova Bamot.

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Tso Bamot wova bali la me le Moab-nyigba dzi le Pisga-to si dze ŋgɔ gbedadaƒoa la gbɔ. Israelviwo ɖu fia Sixon kple fia Og dzi (Mos V,

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: Xesbon nye Amoritɔwo ƒe fia Sixon ƒe du gã. Sixon wɔ aʋa kple Moab-fia si nɔ anyi tsã, eye wòxɔ eƒe anyigba katã le esi va se ɖe Arnon nu.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Tete Israelviwo dɔ amewo ɖe Sixon, Amori-fia gbɔ be wonegblɔ nɛ be:

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: “Na mato wò anyigba me ayi. Míadze ato agblewo alo wainbɔwo me o, eye míano vudo aɖeke me tsi hã o. Ke boŋ míato fia ƒe mɔ gã dzi ko tẽe va se ɖe esime míato wò anyigba me ayi.”

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Ke Sixon gbe be yemaɖe mɔ na Israelviwo be woato yeƒe anyigba me ayi o. Eƒo eƒe dukɔ blibo la nu ƒu, eye woho tso gbedadaƒo le Yaza ɖakpe aʋa kple Israelviwo.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Israelviwo wu wo dometɔ geɖe le aʋa la me, eye woxɔ Sixon ƒe anyigba tso Arnon-tɔʋu la gbɔ va se ɖe Yabok nu heva ke ɖe Amon viwo ŋu, elabe Amon viwo nɔ woƒe liƒo ŋu dzɔm sesĩe.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo xɔ Amoritɔwo ƒe duwo katã. Woxɔ Xesbon kple eŋu duwo katã hã, eye wonɔ wo me.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Eya ta hɛnɔwo sia ahama gblɔna be: “Miva Xesbon. Mina woagbugbɔe atso. Mina woagbugbɔ Sixon ƒe du la atso, wòasesẽ.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Dzo do tso Xesbon. Dzo ƒe aɖe tso Sixon ƒe du la me, eye wòfiã Moabtɔwo ƒe Ar kple Arnon ŋu nɔlawo.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Baba na mi, Moabtɔwo! Evɔ na mi, mi Kemostɔwo! Mia mawu na via ŋutsuwo zu aʋasilawo, eye via nyɔnuwo zu Amori-fia, Sixon ƒe aboyomewo.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: Ale woƒe dzidzimeviwo tsrɔ̃ tso Xesbon va se ɖe Dibon. Míetsrɔ̃ wo tso Nasim va do ɖe Nofa le Medeba gbɔ.”

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo nɔ Amoritɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi,

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: eye Mose dɔ amewo be woayi aɖatsa ŋku le Yazer. Woxɔ eŋu duwo eye wonya Amoritɔ siwo le afi ma la ɖa.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Emegbe Israelviwo trɔ dze Basan-mɔ dzi. Tete Og, Basan-fia kple eƒe aʋakɔ ho va kpe wo le Edrei.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Mègavɔ̃e o. Mana nàɖu eya ŋutɔ, dukɔa kple anyigba bliboa dzi. Nu si nètu kple Sixon, Amori-fia si nɔ Xesbon la, tui kple eya hã.”

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo wu Og kple via ŋutsuwo kpakple eƒe dukɔmetɔwo katã; ame aɖeke metsi agbe ahayi sisi ge o, eye woxɔ woƒe anyigba la.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Israelviwo ho, eye wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Moab-gbegbe le Yordan godo le Yerixo kasa.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Moabtɔwo gblɔ na Midiantɔwo ƒe ame tsitsiwo be: “Ameha si ɖe to ɖe mí la le mí kple nu siwo katã ƒo xlã mí la tsrɔ̃ ge, abe ale si nyi ɖua gbe le gbeɖuƒe ene.” Ale Balak, Zipor vi, si nye Moab-fia le ɣe ma ɣi me la,

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: dɔ amewo ɖe Bileam, Beor vi, gbɔ be woayɔe vɛ. Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, ele Petor le Frat-tɔsisi la nu le Ama ƒe anyigba dzi. Amedɔdɔawo gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, dukɔ aɖe ʋu tso Egipte va yina. Wosɔ gbɔ ŋutɔ, eye woxɔ míaƒe anyigba la katã vɔ. Woƒu asaɖa anyi dze ŋgɔm.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Wosɔ gbɔ wu mí, eya ta meɖe kuku, va ƒo fi de ame siawo nam elabe wosesẽ wum. Ɖewohĩ mate ŋu aɖu wo dzi, eye anyà wo ɖa le anyigba la dzi. Menya be ne èyra ame la, yayra nɔa edzi, eye ne èƒo fi de ame la, fiƒode nɔa edzi.”

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Ale Moab kple Midian ame tsitsiwo xɔ afakaho la, eye wodze mɔ va Bileam gbɔ hegblɔ Balak ƒe nyaawo nɛ.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Bileam gblɔ na wo be: “Mitsi afii dɔ. Ne ŋu ke la, magblɔ nya si Aƒetɔ agblɔ nam la na mi.” Ale Moab-me tsitsiawo tsi Bileam gbɔ dɔ.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Mawu va Bileam gbɔ hebiae be: “Ŋutsu kawo nye esiawo le gbɔwò?”

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Bileam ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Balak, Moab-fiae dɔ wo ɖe gbɔnye. Wobe ebe

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: dukɔ aɖe ʋu tso Egipte va kaka ɖe yeƒe anyigba bliboa dzi, eya ta mava ƒo fi de wo na ye, ɖewohĩ yeate ŋu awɔ aʋa kpli wo, anyà wo ɖa.”

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Mawu gblɔ na Bileam be: “Mègayi kpli wo o, eye mègaƒo fi de dukɔ la o, elabe meyrae xoxo.”

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Le ŋdi me la, Bileam fɔ, eye wògblɔ na amedɔdɔawo be: “Migbugbɔ yi mia de. Aƒetɔ gbe be magayi kpli mi o.”

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Ale wogbugbɔ yi Balak gbɔ ɖagblɔ nɛ be: “Bileam gbe be yemava kpli mí o.”

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Ke Balak dɔ amegã bubu siwo sɔ gbɔ, eye bubu le wo ŋu wu gbãtɔwo la ɖa.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Woyi Bileam gbɔ eye wogblɔ Balak ƒe gbedeasia nɛ be: “Mègana naneke naxe mɔ na wò gbɔnye vava o.

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: Mele bubu de ge ŋuwò ale si mate ŋui, eye mawɔ nu sia nu si nègblɔ nam. Meɖe kuku, va ƒo fi de dukɔ sia nam!”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Ke Bileam ɖo eŋu be: “Ne klosalo kple sika ayɔ Balak ƒe aƒe taŋ wòatsɔ nam gɔ̃ hã la, nyemaxɔe o. Nyemawɔ nu bubu sue aɖeke gɔ̃ hã ahada Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu ƒe gbe dzi o.

english_verse: That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
translation_verse: Le zã me la, Mawu va Bileam gbɔ hegblɔ nɛ be: “Nenye wò yɔ ge ŋutsu siawo va la, fɔ nàyi kpli wo; ke wɔ nu si magblɔ na wò be nàwɔ la ko.” Bileam kple eƒe tedzi

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Le ŋdi me la, Bileam fɔ, bla akpa na eƒe tedzi, eye wòdze mɔ kple amedɔdɔ siwo tso Moab va la.

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Ke Mawu do dɔmedzoe be eyina afi ma. Bileam nɔ eƒe tedzi dom, eye eƒe subɔla eve kpe ɖe eŋuti. Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla va tso mɔ me nɛ hetsi tsitre ɖe mɔa dzi.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Esi tedzia kpɔ mawudɔla la wòle tsitre ɖe mɔa dzi, lé yi ɖe asi la, edze le mɔa dzi to gbe me. Bileam ƒo tedzi la, eye wòtrɔe va mɔa dzi.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Emegbe mawudɔla la va tsi tsitre ɖe wainbɔwo ƒe kpɔdomeemɔ si ƒe akpawo kple eve nye gli la dzi.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Tedzia gakpɔ mawudɔla la, eye wòdze ɖe gli ŋu, hemimi Bileam ƒe afɔ ɖe glia ŋu. Bileam gaƒoe ake.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Mawudɔla la gayi ŋgɔ ɖatsi tsitre ɖe teƒe xaxɛ aɖe. Mɔ aɖeke mele afi sia be woadze ato ayi ŋgɔ o.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Esi tedzia gakpɔ mawudɔlaa la, etsyɔ akɔ anyi. Bileam do dɔmedzoe ɖe eŋuti, eye wòƒoe kple ati.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ na ŋusẽ tedzia be wòaƒo nu, eye wòbia Bileam be: “Nu ka mewɔ wò? Nu ka ta nèƒom zi etɔ̃ sɔŋ?”

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Bileam ɖo eŋu be: “Esi nèdo tsukunɔm tae! Ne ɖe wònye yie le asinye la, ne mewu wò gɔ̃!”

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Tedzi la gblɔ na Bileam be: “Menye nye koe nye wò tedzi si nèdo le wò agbe me ŋkekewo katã me va se ɖe egbe oa? Ɖe mewɔ nu sia tɔgbe ɖe ŋuwò kpɔa?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Gbeɖe!”

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ na Bileam kpɔ mawudɔla la wòle tsitre ɖe mɔa dzi, lé yi ɖe asi. Ede ta agu, eye wòtsyɔ mo anyi.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Mawudɔla la gblɔ nɛ be: “Nu ka tae nèƒo wò tedzia zi etɔ̃ sɔŋ nenema? Nyee va xe mɔ na wò elabe nu si gbe yim nèle la medze ŋunye o.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Ke wò tedzi la kpɔm, eye wòdze ɖe aga zi etɔ̃ sɔŋ. Ɖe mewɔ nenema o la, ne mewu wò, eye eya atsi agbe.”

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Bileam ɖo eŋu be: “Mewɔ nuvɔ̃. Nyemenya be wòe tsi tre ɖe ŋunye tso mɔ me nam o. Azɔ ne nye yiyi nye vɔ̃ le gbɔwò la, magbugbɔ ayi aƒeme.”

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Mawudɔla la gblɔ nɛ be: “Yi kpli wo ko, ke gblɔ nya si magblɔ na wò la ɖeɖe ko.” Ale Bileam yi kple amedɔdɔawo. Balak xɔ Bileam

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Esi Balak se be Bileam gbɔna la, eyi ɖakpee le Ir, si nye Moab-du le keke liƒo dzi ke le Arnon-tɔʋu nu.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: Balak biae be: “Nu ka ta medɔ ame ɖa be neyɔ wò vɛ, mèva kaba o? Ɖe nèbu be nyemate ŋu ade bubu ŋuwò oa?”

english_verse: “I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
translation_verse: Bileam ɖo eŋu be: “Meva ɖe! Gake ɖe mate ŋu agblɔ nya aɖea? Nu si Mawu gblɔ nam be magblɔ la, eya ko make nu agblɔ.”

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
