translation_verse: Ale Bileam zɔ kple Balak yi ɖe Kiryat-Xuzot.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Balak wu nyiwo kple alẽwo sa vɔe, eye wòɖo ɖe ɖe Bileam kple amegã siwo le egbɔ la. Bileam ƒe gbeƒãɖeɖe gbãtɔ

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, Balak kplɔ Bileam yi Bamot-Baal, afi si wòte ŋu kpɔ Israelviwo ƒe akpa si tsɔ ɖe wo gbɔ la le nyuie.

english_verse: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Bileam gblɔ na Balak be: “Na woaɖi vɔsamlekpui adrẽ ɖe afi sia nam, eye woakplɔ nyitsu adrẽ kple agbo adrẽ vɛ nam.”

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Balak wɔ nu si Bileam gblɔ nɛ la, eye wo amea evea tsɔ nyitsu ɖeka kple agbo ɖeka sa vɔ le vɔsamlekpui adrẽawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe dzi.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
translation_verse: Emegbe Bileam gblɔ na Balak be: “Va tsi tsitre ɖe wò numemevɔsa la gbɔ, ne madzo le afii vie aɖakpɔ ɖa be Aƒetɔ aɖe eɖokui afiam mahã. Ne eɖe nane fiam la, mava gblɔe na wò.” Ale eya ɖeka yi togbɛ aɖe si dzi naneke mele o la dzi,

english_verse: When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
translation_verse: eye Mawu ɖe eɖokui fiae. Bileam gblɔ nɛ be: “Meɖi vɔsamlekpui adrẽawo, eye metsɔ nyitsu ɖeka kple agbo ɖeka sa vɔ le vɔsamlekpuiawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe dzi.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nya si wòdi be Bileam nagblɔ na Balak la nɛ, eye wòɖoe ɖe egbɔ be wòayi aɖagblɔe nɛ tututu.

english_verse: When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
translation_verse: Ale Bileam gbugbɔ yi, eye wòkpɔ Balak kple Moab-megãwo le tsitre ɖe eƒe numemevɔsa la gbɔ.

english_verse: Balaam said: “King Balak of Moab brought me from the hills of Syria to curse Israel and announce its doom.
translation_verse: Bileam ɖe gbeƒã Mawu ƒe gbedeasi la be: “Balak, Moab-fia, kplɔm tso Aram, ɣedzeƒetowo dzi vɛ. Egblɔ nam be: ‘Va ƒo fi de Yakob nam! Va do ɖiŋu na Israel nam!’

english_verse: But I can't go against God! He did not curse or condemn Israel. *
translation_verse: Ale ke maƒo fi ade ame si Mawu meƒo fi de o? Ale ke mado ɖiŋu na ame si Mawu medo ɖiŋu na o?

english_verse: “From the mountain peaks, I look down and see Israel, the obedient people of God.
translation_verse: Mele towo tame le wo kpɔm ɖa! Mele togbɛwo dzi le wo kpɔm ɖa! Wonye dukɔ si ɖe ɖe aga; womebua wo ɖokui ɖe dukɔ bubuwo dome o.

english_verse: They are living alone in peace. And though they are many, they don't bother the other nations. “I hope to obey God for as long as I live and to die in such peace.”
translation_verse: Wosɔ gbɔ abe ke ene. Ame ka ate ŋu axlẽ wo? Woƒe eneliawo ɖeka pɛ hã, manyaxlẽ na ame aɖeke o. Na maku ame dzɔdzɔe. Nye nuwuwu nenɔ abe wo tɔ ene.”

english_verse: Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
translation_verse: Tete Balak gblɔ na Bileam be: “Nu ka nye esia nèwɔ ɖe ŋunye? Meyɔ wò vɛ be nàƒo fi ade nye futɔwo ko, ɖeko nètsɔ wo yra!”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “I can say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Second Message
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu be: “Nu si Aƒetɔ be magblɔ ko magblɔ.” Bileam ƒe gbeƒãɖeɖe evelia

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.”
translation_verse: Balak gblɔ na Bileam be: “Va míyi teƒe bubu, afi si nàte ŋu akpɔ wo dometɔ aɖewo ko le; ke menye wo katã o, negbe esiwo tsɔ ɖe mía gbɔ la ko. Madi be nàƒo fi de wo nam tso afi ma.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
translation_verse: Ekplɔe yi Zofim gbe dzi le Pisga-to tame. Egaɖi vɔsamlekpui adrẽ ɖe afi ma hã, eye wòtsɔ nyitsu ɖeka kple agbo ɖeka sa vɔ le vɔsamlekpuiawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe dzi.

english_verse: “Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
translation_verse: Bileam gblɔ na Balak be: “Tsi tre ɖe wò numemevɔsa la gbɔ le afii, ne mayi aɖado go Aƒetɔ le afim.”

english_verse: The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ do go Bileam, eye wògblɔ nya si Bileam agblɔ la nɛ. Egblɔ nɛ be negbugbɔ yi Balak gbɔ, eye wòagblɔ nya si tututu yegblɔ nɛ la nɛ.

english_verse: Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings. Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
translation_verse: Esi wògbugbɔ va la, Balak gale tsitre ɖe eƒe numemevɔsa la gbɔ, eye Moab-megãwo le egbɔ. Balak biae be: “Ale ke Aƒetɔ gblɔ?”

english_verse: God is no mere human! He doesn't tell lies or change his mind. God always keeps his promises.
translation_verse: Mawu menye amegbetɔ aka aʋatso o. Menye amegbetɔ dzidzia wònye ne wòado ŋugbe ko agbe edziwɔwɔ o. Ne egblɔ nya la, ewɔa edzi. Ne egblɔ nya ɖi la, nyaa vaa me.

english_verse: “My command from God was to bless these people, and there's nothing I can do to change what he has done.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, Mawu ɖe wòbe mava yra ame. Ne Mawu yra ame la, nyemate ŋu atrɔe o.

english_verse: Israel's king is the Lord God. He lives there with them and intends them no harm.
translation_verse: Nyemekpɔ dzɔgbevɔ̃e aɖeke le Yakob ŋu o; nyemekpɔ fuwɔame aɖeke le Israel ŋu o. Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu li kplii, eye dzidzɔɣli le ɖiɖim le wo dome be eyae nye yewoƒe fia.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led Israel out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Mawue kplɔ wo tso Egipte, eye wòle na wo abe to ƒe dzo ene.

english_verse: No magic charms can work against them— just look what God has done for his people.
translation_verse: Dzotɔwo ƒe dzo maɖi Yakob ŋu o. Nenema ke afatɔwo ƒe afa maɖi le Israel o. Ɖeko amewo agblɔ be: ‘Mikpɔ nu si gbegbe Mawu wɔ na Israel la ɖa!’

english_verse: They are like angry lions ready to attack; and they won't rest until their victim is gobbled up.”
translation_verse: Mikpɔ Israel-dukɔ ɖa! Etso abe dzatanɔ ene, eye wòfɔ abe dzatatsu ene. Matsyɔ akɔ anyi akpɔ o, negbe ɖeko wòaɖu nu si wòlé, eye wòano nu siwo wòwu la ƒe ʋu hafi.”

english_verse: Balak shouted, “If you're not going to curse Israel, then at least don't bless them.”
translation_verse: Tete Balak gblɔ na Bileam be: “Esi nègbe fiƒoƒo de wo ko la, mègayra wo hã o!”

english_verse: “I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Third Message
translation_verse: Bileam ɖo eŋu be: “Nyemegblɔ na wò be ele nam be mawɔ nya sia nya si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nam la dzi oa?” Bileam ƒe gbeƒãɖeɖe etɔ̃lia

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.”
translation_verse: Emegbe Balak gblɔ be: “Va makplɔ wò yi teƒe bubu. Ɖewohĩ Aƒetɔ adi be nànɔ afi ma aƒo fi ade wo nam.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ale Balak kplɔ Bileam yi Peor-to tame, eye wole kegbegbe si dze ŋgɔ wo la kpɔm ɖa.

english_verse: Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Bileam gblɔ nɛ be: “Ɖi vɔsamlekpui adrẽ ɖe afi sia nam, eye nàkplɔ nyitsu adrẽ kple agbo adrẽ vɛ nam.”

english_verse: After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Balak wɔ nu si Bileam gblɔ nɛ la, eye wòtsɔ nyitsu ɖeka kple agbo ɖeka sa vɔ le vɔsamlekpuiawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe dzi.

english_verse: Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
translation_verse: Azɔ Bileam kpɔ be edze Aƒetɔ ŋu be wòayra Israel, eya ta megayi be yeaɖabia nu ta se abe tsã ene o. Ke boŋ etrɔ mo ɖe kegbegbe la,

english_verse: and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him,
translation_verse: eye esi wòfɔ kɔ dzi la, ekpɔ ale si Israelviwo ƒe to vovovoawo ƒu asaɖa anyi wotɔxɛwotɔxɛe. Tete Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ va Bileam dzi,

english_verse: and Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ nya si le esi la ɖi be: “Bileam, Beor vi, ame si ƒe ŋkuwo woʋu, wòle nu kpɔm nyuie la ƒe numegbee nye esi:

english_verse: It comes from the Lord, the God All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Ame si sea Mawu ƒe nyawo, eye wòkpɔa nu si Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ɖena fianɛ; ame si tsyɔa mo anyi gake eƒe ŋkuwo nɔa te ɖi la ƒe gbedeasie nye esi:

english_verse: “People of Israel, your camp is lovely.
translation_verse: Yakob, wò agbadɔwo nyakpɔ loo! Israel, wò nɔƒewo nyo ŋutɔ!

english_verse: It's like a grove of palm trees or a garden beside a river. You are like tall aloe trees that the Lord has planted, or like cedars growing near water.
translation_verse: Wole abe tɔʋu si mlo ɖe nu mii le bali me heyi ene. Woɖi abɔ le tɔsisi to. Wole abe aloeti siwo Aƒetɔ do ene, eye woɖi sedertiwo le tɔ to.

english_verse: You and your descendants will prosper like an orchard beside a stream. Your king will rule with power and be a greater king than Agag the Amalekite.
translation_verse: Tsi adza fũu ɖe eƒe anyigba dzi, eye wòaƒã nu ɖe tɔ geɖewo to. Eƒe fia axɔ ŋkɔ wu Agag, eye eƒe fiaɖuƒe akeke ɖe nu.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led you out of Egypt. You will defeat your enemies, shooting them with arrows and crushing their bones.
translation_verse: Mawu kplɔ wo tso Egipte, eye wòle na wo abe tò ƒe dzo ene. Aɖu dukɔ siwo nye eƒe futɔwo dzi, agbã woƒe ƒuwo, eye wòatsɔ woƒe aŋutrɔwo aƒo ɖe wo.

english_verse: Like a lion you lie down, resting after an attack. Who would dare disturb you? “Anyone who blesses you will be blessed; anyone who curses you will be cursed.”
translation_verse: Dukɔ la le abe dzata si tsyɔ akɔ anyi dɔ alɔ̃ ene. Ame ka le enyɔ ge wòatso? Ame sia ame si yra wò la, Mawu ayrae. Ame sia ame si ƒo fi de wò la, Mawu aƒo fi ade eya hã.”

english_verse: When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
translation_verse: Tete Balak do dɔmedzoe ɖe Bileam ŋu, si akpe sesĩe gblɔ na Bileam be: “Meyɔ wò vɛ be nàƒo fi ade nye futɔwo nam, ke ɖeko nètsɔ wo yra boŋ zigbɔzi etɔ̃ sɔŋ!

english_verse: Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
translation_verse: Azɔ netsɔ na wò! Yi mia de! Ɖe medi be made bubu ŋuwò hafi, gake Aƒetɔ na mègale ekpɔ ge o.”

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: ‘Nenye be klosalo kple sika ayɔ wò fiasã taŋ nàtsɔ nam hã la, nyemawɔ naneke le ɖokuinye si o. Nya si Aƒetɔ be magblɔ ko magblɔ.’ Bileam ƒe gbeƒãɖeɖe mamlɛtɔ

english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: Bileam gblɔ na Balak be: Kpɔ ɖa, azɔ la, mele tɔtrɔ ge ayi mía detɔwo gbɔ, gake hafi madzo la, medi be magblɔ nu si Israelviwo le wò dukɔ wɔ ge le ɣeyiɣi si gbɔna me la na wò.”

english_verse: Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Tete Bileam gblɔ nya si le esi la ɖi be: “Bileam, Beor vi, ame si ƒe ŋkuwo woʋu, wòle nu kpɔm nyuie la ƒe numegbee nye esi:

english_verse: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the Lord All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Ame si sea Mawu ƒe nyawo, eye wòdzea si Dziƒoʋĩtɔ ƒe susuwo; ame si Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ɖea nu fiana, etsyɔ mo anyi gake eƒe ŋkuwo le te ɖi la ƒe gbedeasie nye esi:

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.
translation_verse: Mele nu si le dzɔdzɔ ge la kpɔm ɖa; ke madzɔ fifia o. Mele Israel-dukɔa kpɔm ɖa, ke egbɔ metsɔ o. Ɣletivi ado tso Yakob ƒeme, eye fiatikplɔ ado tso Israel me. Awu Moab-megãwo, eye wòatsrɔ̃ Set ƒe amewo keŋ.

english_verse: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
translation_verse: Axɔ Edom ƒe anyigba. Axɔ eƒe futɔ Seir hã tɔ; Ke Israel ya anɔ dzi ɖum kalẽtɔe.

english_verse: The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.
translation_verse: Ame atso Yakob ƒe dzidzime aɖu dzi, eye wòatsrɔ̃ ame siwo tsi agbe le duwo me la keŋ.”

english_verse: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.
translation_verse: Azɔ Bileam kpɔ Amalekitɔwo le ŋutega la me, eye wògblɔ nya ɖi le wo ŋu be: “Amalek ye nye gbãtɔ le dukɔwo dome; ke ava tsrɔ̃ godoo!”

english_verse: “And this is what I saw about the Kenites: They think they're safe, living among the rocks,
translation_verse: Ekpɔ Kenitɔwo hã le ŋutega la me, eye wògblɔ nya ɖi le wo ŋu be: “Afi si nèwɔ nɔƒe ɖo la sesẽ, eye wòle abe atɔ le agakpe tame ene.

english_verse: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.
translation_verse: Ke woatsrɔ̃ wò Kain; esusɔ vie Asur naɖe aboyo wò.”

english_verse: “No one can survive if God plans destruction.
translation_verse: Bileam gagblɔ nya ɖi be: “Aléle! Ame ka atsi agbe ne Mawu wɔ nu sia?

english_verse: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
translation_verse: Amewo anɔ tɔdziʋuwo me atso Kitim ava, eye woabɔbɔ Asur kple Eber ɖe anyi. Ke woaɖu woawo hã dzi atsrɔ̃ wo gbidii.”

english_verse: After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_verse: Esia megbe la, Bileam gbugbɔ va wo de, eye Balak hã dzo.

english_verse: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men had sex with Moabite women.
translation_verse: Esi Israelviwo ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Sitim la, woƒe ŋutsuwo de asi gbolowɔwɔ me kple Moab-nyɔnu siwo le afi ma.

english_verse: These women then invited the men to ceremonies where sacrifices were offered to their gods. The men ate the meat from the sacrifices and worshiped the Moabite gods.
translation_verse: Nyɔnu siawo kpea wo yia woƒe mawuwo ƒe vɔsaƒe, eye woɖua nu hesubɔa mawuawo.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel because they had worshiped the god Baal Peor.
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo ƒe susu tsi Baal, Peortɔwo ƒe mawu la ŋu eya ta Aƒetɔ do dɔmedzoe ɖe wo ŋu,

english_verse: So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ na Mose be: “Yɔ dukɔ la ƒe amegãwo katã ƒo ƒu ɖe ŋkunye me, eye nàde ka ve na wo ɖe ŋdɔgbe eye Aƒetɔ nadzudzɔ dzikudodo ɖe Israel ŋu.”

english_verse: Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
translation_verse: Tete Mose gblɔ na dukplɔlaawo be: “Mia dome ame sia ame newu ŋutsu siwo le ete la dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe si zu Peortɔwo ƒe Baal subɔla la.”

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Esime amewo nɔ avi fam le godoƒegbadɔ la nu la, ɖeko Israel-ŋutsu aɖe kplɔ Midian-nyɔnu aɖe, le Mose kple Israelviwo ƒe ha blibo la ŋkume alea ko va yi ɖe eƒe agbadɔ me.

english_verse: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear
translation_verse: Esi Pinehas, nunɔla Eleazar viŋutsu si nye Aron tɔgbuiyɔvi kpɔe la, etsi tsitre dzo le ha la dome. Eyi ɖatsɔ akplɔ, eye

english_verse: and followed the man into his tent, where he ran the spear through the man and into the woman's stomach. The Lord immediately stopped punishing Israel with a deadly disease,
translation_verse: wòti ŋutsua yome yi ɖe eƒe xɔgãme, eye wòtu akplɔa eya kple nyɔnua siaa dzi, wòto wo kple evea ƒe dɔ me do. Tete dɔ vɔ̃ si le Israelviwo wum la nu tso.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: “In my anger, I would have wiped out the Israelites if Phinehas had not been faithful to me.
translation_verse: “Ame si na dɔmedzoe si medo ɖe Israelviwo ŋu la nu fa lae nye Pinehas. Eyae ʋã ŋu ɖe nunye le wo dome ale be nyemeʋã ŋu tsrɔ̃ Israelviwo le dɔmedzoe me o.

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
translation_verse: Eya kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo anye nunɔlawo tegbee elabe eʋã ŋu ɖe nunye, eye to esia me wòlé avum, ale be metsɔ Israelviwo ƒe nuvɔ̃wo ke wo.”

english_verse: The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe.
translation_verse: Israel-ŋutsu si wowu kple Midian-nyɔnua ŋkɔe nye Simri. Enye amegã Salu si nye Simeon ƒome ƒe tatɔ la vi.

english_verse: And the Midianite woman killed with him was Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite clan leader named Zur.
translation_verse: Midian-nyɔnua ŋkɔe nye Kosbi. Enye amegã Zur, ame si nye Midiantɔwo ƒe ƒometatɔ ɖeka la ƒe vinyɔnu.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: “The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_verse: elabe woawo hã ɖe fu na mi vevie. Wowɔ aye flu mi le Peor, eye wotre mɔ̀ na mi kple wo denyɔnu Kosbi, ame si wowu gbe si gbe dɔ vɔ̃ ɖo mia dome le Peor.”

english_verse: After the Lord had stopped the deadly disease from killing the Israelites, he said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron,
translation_verse: Esi dɔ vɔ̃ la nu tso la, Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose kple Eleazar, Aron vi be:

english_verse: “I want you to find out how many Israelites are in each family. Then make a list of every man
translation_verse: “Mixlẽ Israelvi siwo katã xɔ ƒe bla eve kple vɔ eye woate ŋu ade aʋa la le dukɔa me. Mixlẽ wo aƒekɔ, aƒekɔ.”

english_verse: Israel was now camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. Moses and Eleazar told them
translation_verse: Mose kple Eleazar, nunɔla la, ƒo nu kple wo le Moab-gbegbe le Yordan nu le Yerixo gblɔ be:

english_verse: Pallu was the father of Eliab
translation_verse: Palu ƒe dzidzimeviwoe nye: Eliab,

english_verse: and the grandfather of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram who had been chosen by the people, but who followed Korah and rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord.
translation_verse: Nemuel, Datan kple Abiram. Datan kple Abiram siawo nye Israel-dukɔ la ƒe adaŋudehamenɔlawo. Woawoe tsi tre ɖe Mose kple Aron ŋu, eye wonɔ Korax ƒe ame siwo dze aglã ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu la dome.

english_verse: That's when the Lord made the earth open up and swallow Dathan, Abiram, and Korah. At the same time, fire destroyed
translation_verse: Anyigba ke nu mi wo, eye woku kpe ɖe Korax kple eyomedzelawo ŋu, esime dzo fiã ŋutsu alafa eve bla atɔ̃ mawo. Nyadzɔdzɔ sia va zu nyagbename na dukɔ la.

english_verse: But the Korahite clan wasn't destroyed.
translation_verse: Ke Korax viwo ya meku o.

english_verse: None of the people that Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai Desert were still alive,
translation_verse: Ke Israelvi siwo Mose kple nunɔla Aron tia xlẽ zi gbãtɔ le Sinai-gbedadaƒo la dometɔ ɖeka hɔ̃ hã mele ame siwo woxlẽ zi evelia sia la dome o.

english_verse: Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Viŋutsu ene nɔ Aron si, siwoe nye: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar kple Itamar.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: “Divide the land of Canaan among these tribes, according to the number of people in each one,
translation_verse: “Ma anyigba la na toawo ɖe woƒe amewo ƒe agbɔsɔsɔ nu.

english_verse: The total number of Israelite men listed was
translation_verse: Israel-ŋutsu siwo woxlẽ la le ame akpe alafa ade kple ɖeka alafa adrẽ bla etɔ̃.

english_verse: I will show you what land to give each tribe, and they will receive as much land as they need, according to the number of people in it.”
translation_verse: Dzidze nu ɖe edzi hafi nàmae. Tsɔ lolotɔ na to si me tɔwo sɔ gbɔ wu, eye nàtsɔ suetɔ na to si me tɔwo mesɔ gbɔ o.”

english_verse: The tribe of Levi included the clans of the Gershonites, Kohathites, Merarites,
translation_verse: Aƒekɔ siwo le Levi-to mee nye: Gerson, Kehat kple Merari.

english_verse: as well as the clans of Libni, Hebron, Mahli, Mushi, and Korah. Kohath the Levite was the father of Amram,
translation_verse: Woƒe dzidzimeviwo ƒe aƒekɔwoe nye: Libni, Xebron, Maxeli, Musi kple Korax. Kehat vie nye Amram.

english_verse: the husband of Levi's daughter Jochebed, who was born in Egypt. Amram and Jochebed's three children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
translation_verse: Eya ɖe Levi-nyɔnu si ŋkɔe nye Yoxebed, ame si wodzi le Egipte. Edzi ŋutsuvi eve kple nyɔnuvi ɖeka na Amram siwo ƒe ŋkɔwoe nye Aron kple Mose kpakple wo nɔvinyɔnu Miryam.

english_verse: But Nadab and Abihu had died when they offered fire that was unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke Nadab kple Abihu ku, elabe wotsɔ dzo makɔmakɔ va Aƒetɔ gbɔe.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar counted the Israelites while they were camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Mose kple Eleazar tia aƒekɔ siawo katã le Israel-toawo me xlẽ le Moab-gbegbe le Yordan godo le Yerixo kasa.

english_verse: except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. The Lord had said that everyone else would die there in the desert.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ gblɔ le wo ŋu be: “Wo katã aku le gbedadaƒo la.” Ale wo dometɔ ɖeka pɛ hã mesusɔ o, negbe Kaleb, Yefune vi kple Yosua, Nun vi ko.

english_verse: One day his daughters went to the sacred tent, where they met with Moses, Eleazar, and some other leaders of Israel, as well as a large crowd of Israelites. The young women said:
translation_verse: Wotsi tsitre ɖe Mose, nunɔla Eleazar, amegãwo kple ha blibo la ŋkume le godoƒegbadɔ la nu hegblɔ be:

english_verse: You know that our father died in the desert. But it was for something he did wrong, not for joining with Korah in rebelling against the Lord. Our father left no sons
translation_verse: “Mía tɔ́ ku le gbedadaƒo, eye viŋutsu aɖeke menɔ esi o. Eya menɔ Korax kple eyomedzela siwo dze aglã ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu la dome o, ke boŋ eya ŋutɔ ƒe nuvɔ̃ bubu si wòwɔ la tae wòku ɖo.

english_verse: to carry on his family name. But why should his name die out for that reason? Give us some land like the rest of his relatives in our clan, so our father's name can live on.
translation_verse: Ɖe wòle be mía tɔ́ ŋkɔ natsrɔ̃ le eƒe ƒome la me, esi viŋutsu menɔ esi o ta? Míedi be nàna anyigba mí ɖe mía tɔ́ nɔviwo dome.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord what should be done,
translation_verse: Mose tsɔ woƒe nya la yi Aƒetɔ gbɔe,

english_verse: and the Lord answered:
translation_verse: eye Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be:

english_verse: Zelophehad's daughters are right. They should each be given part of the land their father would have received.
translation_verse: “Zelofxad vinyɔnuawo ƒe nyaa le me, eya ta na domenyinu wo ɖe wo tɔ́ nɔviwo dome. Na wo tɔ́ ƒe domenyinu la nage ɖe wo si me.

english_verse: If he has no daughter, his brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Ne vinyɔnu aɖeke mele esi o la, woatsɔ eƒe domenyinu na nɔvia ŋutsuwo.

english_verse: But if he has no brothers, his father's brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Ne nɔviŋutsu aɖeke mele esi o la, wonetsɔ eƒe domenyinu na tɔ́a nɔviŋutsuwo.

english_verse: And if his father has no brothers, the land must be given to his nearest relative in the clan. This is my law, and the Israelites must obey it. Joshua Is Appointed Israel's Leader (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ke ne nɔviŋutsu aɖeke mele tɔ́a si o la, wonetsɔ eƒe domenyinu na eƒe ƒometɔ si tsɔ ɖe egbɔ le ƒomea me la, eye eya nanyi doa me. Esia nanye se kple ɖoɖo na Israelviwo abe ale si Aƒetɔ la gblɔe na wò ene.’ ” Aƒetɔ tia Yosua be wòanye Mose teƒenɔla (Mos V,

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “One day you will go up into the Abarim Mountains, and from there you will see the land I am giving the Israelites.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Yi Abarim-to dzi ne nàkpɔ anyigba si metsɔ na Israelviwo la ɖa.

english_verse: After you have seen it, you will die, just like your brother Aaron,
translation_verse: Ne èkpɔe vɔ la wò hã àku abe nɔviwò Aron ene,

english_verse: because both of you disobeyed me at Meribah near the town of Kadesh in the Zin Desert. When the Israelites insulted me there, you didn't believe in my holy power.”
translation_verse: elabe mi ame evea miesẽ to, gbe nye nya dzi wɔwɔ le Zin-gbedadaƒo. Esime ha blibo la nɔ nyawo gblɔm ɖe ŋunye abe dzre wɔm wole ene la, miena ŋunye kɔ le tsi la gbɔ le wo ŋkume o.” Esia nye dzrewɔtsi la le Kades le Zin-gbedadaƒo.

english_verse: “You are the Lord God, and you know what is in everyone's heart. So I ask you to appoint a leader for Israel.
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, Mawu, gbɔgbɔe nènye, eye nèle amegbetɔwo katã me. Meɖe kuku, tia ame ɖo ha la nu.

english_verse: Your people need someone to lead them into battle, or else they will be like sheep wandering around without a shepherd.”
translation_verse: Amea anye wo kplɔla si akplɔ wo ayi nugbe, eye wòagakplɔ wo agbɔe, ale be wò ha la naganɔ abe alẽ siwo nu kplɔla mele o la ene o.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Joshua son of Nun can do the job. Place your hands on him to show that he is the one to take your place.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be: “Tsɔ Yosua, Nun vi, elabe gbɔgbɔ la le eme. Yɔe, eye nàda asi ɖe edzi.

english_verse: Then go with him and tell him to stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the Israelites. Appoint Joshua as their new leader
translation_verse: Kplɔe wòava tsi tsitre ɖe nunɔla Eleazar kple ha blibo ŋkume, eye nàɖee fia le wo katã ŋkume be eyae anɔ ye teƒe.

english_verse: and tell them they must now obey him, just as they obey you.
translation_verse: Tsɔ ŋusẽ si le asiwò la ƒe ɖe nɛ be Israelviwo ƒe ha blibo la naɖo toe.

english_verse: But Joshua must depend on Eleazar to find out from me what I want him to do as he leads Israel into battle.”
translation_verse: Eya anɔ tsitre ɖe nunɔla Eleazar gbɔ eye wòatsɔ Urim abia nu nɛ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Eƒe nya nue woado ayi afi aɖe, eye eƒe nya nu kee woagagbɔ ava ɖo; eya kple Israel-dukɔ si le egbɔ la, ameha blibo la.”

english_verse: Moses followed the Lord's instructions and took Joshua to Eleazar and the people,
translation_verse: Mose wɔ abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ la ene pɛpɛpɛ. Ekplɔ Yosua vɛ, eye wòna wòtsi tsitre ɖe nunɔla Eleazar kple ha blibo la ŋkume.

english_verse: then he placed his hands on Joshua and appointed him Israel's leader.
translation_verse: Mose da eƒe asiwo ɖe edzi, eye abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ ene la, eɖe gbeƒã be eyae anye ye teƒenɔla.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: eye kilo ɖeka nakpe ɖe alẽviawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu.

english_verse: This sacrifice to please me was first offered at Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Enye numemevɔsa si wowɔna edziedzi tso Sinai-to la gbɔ ke, eye wònye dzovɔsa si ƒe ʋeʋẽ lílili dzea ŋunye.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices will please me.
translation_verse: Mitsɔ wɔ memee kilo ɖeka si wodzaba kple ami la wɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsa kpe ɖe alẽviawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu. Numemevɔsa siawo nye nuɖuɖuvɔsa siwo ƒe ʋeʋẽ lílili dzea Aƒetɔ ŋu.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Offer sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, so that I will smell the smoke and be pleased.
translation_verse: “Milé ŋku ɖe nye dzovɔsa ŋu, eye miatsɔe asa vɔe nam le ɣeyiɣi si woɖo ɖi la dzi. Nye nuɖuɖue wònye, eye eƒe ʋeʋẽ lílili dzea ŋunye.

english_verse: Each day offer two rams a year old as sacrifices to please me. The animals must have nothing wrong with them;
translation_verse: Nuɖuɖu si miatsɔ asa vɔe nam lae nye esi: Alẽvi eve siwo sɔ keŋ, eye woxɔ ƒe ɖekaɖeka lae woame asa vɔe gbe sia gbe.

english_verse: Finally, along with each of these two sacrifices, a liter of wine must be poured on the altar as a drink offering.
translation_verse: Mitsɔ nunonovɔsa lita ɖeka kpe ɖe alẽvia ɖe sia ɖe ŋu, eye miakɔ wain la ɖe kɔkɔeƒe la le Aƒetɔ ŋkume.

english_verse: On the first day of each month, bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: “Gbe si gbe dzinu dze dzi la, mimè nu sa vɔe nam. Vɔsanuawo nanye: Nyitsuvi eve, agbo ɖeka kple alẽvi adrẽ siwo naneke mewɔ afi aɖe na o, eye wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe xɔ ƒe ɖeka la.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Le nuɖuɖuvɔsa gome la, mitsɔ wɔ memee kilo etɔ̃ si wodzaba kple ami la wɔe kpe ɖe nyitsuawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu. Mitsɔ wɔ memee kilo eve si wodzaba kple ami la wɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsa kpe ɖe agbo ɖeka ŋu.

english_verse: Celebrate Passover in honor of me on the fourteenth day of the first month of each year.
translation_verse: “Ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke wui enelia nye Paska na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: The following day will begin the Festival of Thin Bread, which will last for a week. During this time you must honor me by eating bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke Nyuia ɖuɖu nadze egɔme tso ŋkeke wui atɔ̃lia gbe, eye woaɖui ŋkeke adrẽ sɔŋ. Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, miaɖu abolo si me womede aboloʋãnui o.

english_verse: On the first day of this festival, you must rest from your work and come together for worship.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke gbãtɔ nye takpegbe si le kɔkɔe; migawɔ dɔ aɖeke gbe ma gbe o.

english_verse: Bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. And then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Misa nuɖuɖuvɔ si nye numemevɔsa nam. Nu siwo ŋudɔ miawɔ lae nye: Nyitsuvi eve, agbo ɖeka kple alẽvi adrẽ siwo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe axɔ ƒe ɖeka.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Mitsɔ wɔ memee kilo etɔ̃ si wodzaba kple ami la wɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsa kpe ɖe nyitsuawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu. Wɔ memee kilo eve nakpe ɖe agbo ɖeka ŋu,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: eye wɔ memee kilo ɖeka nakpe ɖe alẽviawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu.

english_verse: All of these are to be offered each day of the festival in additional to the regular sacrifices, and the smoke from them will please me.
translation_verse: Hekpe ɖe numemevɔsa kple nunonovɔsa si miesana gbe sia gbe ŋu la, aleae miasa vɔe gbe sia gbe ŋkeke adrẽ sɔŋ. Nuɖuɖuvɔsa kple numemevɔsa siawo dzea ŋunye elabe woʋẽna ɖem lílili.

english_verse: Then on the last day of the festival, you must once again rest from work and come together for worship. The Sacrifices during the Harvest Festival (Leviticus
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke adrẽa gbe la, mikpe ta miasubɔ Mawu, eye migawɔ dɔ aɖeke gbe ma gbe o. Vɔsasa le Nuŋeŋkeke Nyui ɖuɣi (Mos III,

english_verse: On the first day of the Harvest Festival, you must rest from your work, come together for worship, and bring a sacrifice of new grain.
translation_verse: “Le Nuŋeŋkeke Nyui ɖuɣi ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ gbe la, mitsɔ bli yeye va sa vɔ nam. Gbe ma gbe nanye takpegbe tɔxɛ na mi, eye migawɔ dɔ aɖeke o.

english_verse: Offer two young bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Mitsɔ nyitsuvi eve, agbo ɖeka kple agbovi adrẽ siwo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe xɔ ƒè ɖeka la sa numemevɔ nam. Vɔsa siawo dzea Aƒetɔ ŋu elabe woʋẽna ɖee lílili.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Mitsɔ wɔ memee kilo etɔ̃ si wodzaba kple ami wɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsa kpe ɖe nyitsuawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu, kilo eve nakpe ɖe agbo ɖeka ŋu,

english_verse: Also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Emegbe woatsɔ gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka asa nuvɔ̃vɔ atsɔ alé avu na dukɔ lae.

english_verse: The animals must have nothing wrong with them and are to be sacrificed along with the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: Hekpe ɖe numemevɔsa kple eƒe nuɖuɖuvɔsa si miewɔna edziedzi ŋu la, ele be miana nu siawo kple nunonovɔsa. Mikpɔ egbɔ be lãawo sɔ keŋkeŋ; ɖeke meganye lã nuwɔe o.

english_verse: On the first day of the seventh month, you must rest from your work and come together to celebrate at the sound of the trumpets.
translation_verse: “Ɣleti adrẽlia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ nanye takpegbe tɔxɛ si le kɔkɔe. Migawɔ dɔ aɖeke gbe ma gbe o. Miku kpẽwo gbe ma gbe.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with the bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Mitsɔ wɔ memee kilo etɔ̃ si wodzaba kple ami wɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsa kpe ɖe nyitsu ɖeka la ŋu. Mitsɔ wɔ memee kilo eve kpe ɖe agbo la ŋu,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: eye mitsɔ wɔ memee kilo ɖeka kpe ɖe agbovi adrẽawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu.

english_verse: You must also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Mitsɔ gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka sa nuvɔ̃vɔ ne miatsɔ alé avu na dukɔ la.

english_verse: These sacrifices will be made in addition to the regular daily sacrifices and the sacrifices for the first day of the month. The smoke from these sacrifices will please me. The Sacrifices on the Great Day of Forgiveness (Leviticus
translation_verse: Mitsɔ nu siawo sa vɔe kpe ɖe numemevɔsa kple eŋu nuɖuɖuvɔsa si miewɔna ne dzinu dze dzi la ŋuti. Nenema ke mitsɔ numemevɔsa kple eŋu nuɖuɖuvɔsa kpakple nunonovɔsa si miewɔna gbe sia gbe la kpe ɖe eŋuti. Vɔsasa le Avuléŋkeke Nyui dzi (Mos III,

english_verse: The tenth day of the seventh month is the Great Day of Forgiveness. On that day you must rest from all work and come together for worship. Show sorrow for your sins by going without food,
translation_verse: “Ɣleti adrẽlia ƒe ŋkeke ewoa gbe nye takpegbe si le kɔkɔe na mi. Mitsi nu dɔ gbe ma gbe, eye ame aɖeke megawɔ dɔ o.

english_verse: and bring to the altar one young bull, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Mitsɔ nyitsuvi ɖeka, agbo ɖeka kple agbovi adrẽ siwo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe xɔ ƒe ɖeka, eye menye lã nuwɔe o la sa numemevɔ si ʋẽna ɖem lílili la nam.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with the bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Mitsɔ wɔ memee kilo etɔ̃ si wodzaba kple ami la wɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsa kpe ɖe nyitsu la ŋu. Nenema ke mitsɔ wɔ kilo eve kpe ɖe agbo ɖeka la ŋu,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: eye mitsɔ wɔ kilo ɖeka kpe ɖe agbovi adrẽawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu.

english_verse: A goat must also be sacrificed for the sins of the people. You will offer these sacrifices in addition to the sacrifice to ask forgiveness and the regular daily sacrifices. The Sacrifices during the Festival of Shelters (Leviticus
translation_verse: Emegbe mitsɔ gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka sa nuvɔ̃vɔe kpe ɖe nuvɔ̃vɔsa si wotsɔ lé avui kple numemevɔsa kple eŋu nuɖuɖuvɔsa kpakple nunonovɔsa si miewɔna gbe sia gbe la ŋuti. Vɔsasa le Agbadɔ Me Nɔnɔ Ŋkeke Nyui ɖuɣi (Mos III,

english_verse: Beginning on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and continuing for seven days, everyone must celebrate the Festival of Shelters in honor of me.
translation_verse: “Ɣleti adrẽlia ƒe ŋkeke wui atɔ̃lia nye takpegbe si le kɔkɔe. Miɖu ŋkekenyui sia ŋkeke adrẽ sɔŋ tsɔ de bubu ŋunye. Ame aɖeke megawɔ dɔ aɖeke le ɣeyiɣi sia me o.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the rams,
translation_verse: Mitsɔ wɔ memee kilo etɔ̃ si wodzaba kple ami la wɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsa kpe ɖe nyitsu wui eneawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu, wɔ kilo eve nakpe ɖe agbo eveawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: eye wɔ kilo ɖeka nakpe ɖe agbovi wui eneawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋuti.

english_verse: You must also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These are to be offered in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: Emegbe mitsɔ gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka sa nuvɔ̃vɔe kpe ɖe numemevɔsa kple eŋu nuɖuɖuvɔsa kpakple nunonovɔsa si miewɔna gbe sia gbe la ŋuti.

english_verse: On the eighth day, you must once again rest from your work and come together for worship.
translation_verse: “Ŋkeke enyilia gbe nye takpegbe na mi, eye ame aɖeke megawɔ dɔ aɖeke gbe ma gbe o.

english_verse: Bring to the altar one bull, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Mitsɔ nyitsu ɖeka, agbo ɖeka kple agbovi adrẽ siwo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe xɔ ƒe ɖeka, eye ɖeke menye lã nuwɔe o la, sa numemevɔ abe dzovɔsa ene, ne wòaʋẽ ɖem lílili.

english_verse: You must also offer the proper grain sacrifices and drink offerings of wine with each animal.
translation_verse: Miwɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsa kple nunonovɔsa ɖe nyitsuawo, agboawo kple alẽviawo ƒe agbɔsɔsɔme ŋu ɖe ɖoɖo la nu.

english_verse: And offer a goat as the sacrifice to ask forgiveness for the people. These sacrifices are made in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: Emegbe mitsɔ gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka sa nuvɔ̃vɔe kpe ɖe numemevɔsa kple eŋu nuɖuɖuvɔsa kpakple nunonovɔsa siwo miewɔna gbe sia gbe la ŋuti.

english_verse: You must offer all these sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, together with any offerings that are voluntarily given or given because of a promise.
translation_verse: “Esiawoe nye ɖoɖo siwo ku ɖe numemevɔsa, nuɖuɖuvɔsa, nunonovɔsa kple ŋutifafavɔsa siwo miawɔ nam le miaƒe ŋkekenyuiwo ɖuɣi la ŋuti. Vɔsasa siawo kpe ɖe esiwo mieɖe adzɔgbe be yewoana alo esiwo miena le mia ɖokui si faa la ŋuti.”

english_verse: Moses told the people of Israel everything the Lord had told him about the sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ale Mose gblɔ nya siwo katã Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be negblɔ na Israelviwo la na wo pɛpɛpɛ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to Israel's tribal leaders:
translation_verse: Mose gblɔ na Israelviwo ƒe toawo ƒe tatɔwo be Aƒetɔ de se be:

english_verse: Suppose a young woman who is still living with her parents makes a promise to the Lord.
translation_verse: “Ne ɖetugbi aɖe gale tɔ́a ƒe dzikpɔkpɔ te le eƒeme, eye wòɖe adzɔgbe na Aƒetɔ alo ka atam tsri nane na eɖokui la,

english_verse: If her father hears about it and says nothing, she must keep her promise.
translation_verse: ele be wòawɔ adzɔgbe si wòɖe alo atam si wòka la dzi, negbe ne tɔ́a se nya la, eye wògbe nɛ la ko.

english_verse: But if he hears about it and objects, then she no longer has to keep her promise. The Lord will forgive her, because her father did not agree with the promise.
translation_verse: Gake ne tɔ́a see, eye wògbe nɛ gbe ma gbe ke la, megawɔ adzɔgbe si wòɖe alo nu si wòka atam tsri la dzi o. Aƒetɔ atsɔe akee, le esi tɔ́a gbe nɛ ta.

english_verse: Suppose a woman makes a promise to the Lord and then gets married. If her husband later hears about the promise but says nothing, she must do what she said, whether she meant it or not.
translation_verse: eye gbe si gbe srɔ̃a se nyaa wòzi kpi kpɔe la, ekema newɔ eƒe adzɔgbe si wòɖe alo nu si wòka atam tsri la dzi.

english_verse: But if her husband hears about the promise and objects, she no longer has to keep it, and the Lord will forgive her.
translation_verse: Gake gbe si gbe srɔ̃a se nyaa hegbe nɛ ko la, ekema srɔ̃ae gblẽ eƒe adzɔgbeɖeɖe la kple atam si wòka tsri nu na eɖokui la me nɛ. Aƒetɔ atsɔe akee.

english_verse: Widows and divorced women must keep every promise they make to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ele be ahosi alo nyɔnu srɔ̃tɔ si wogbe la nawɔ eƒe adzɔgbeɖeɖe kple nu si wòtsri na eɖokui la dzi.

english_verse: Suppose a married woman makes a promise to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ne nyɔnu srɔ̃tɔ aɖe ɖe adzɔgbe alo ka atam hetsri nu na eɖokui,

english_verse: If her husband hears about the promise and says nothing, she must do what she said.
translation_verse: eye srɔ̃a see gake zi kpi eye megbe nɛ o la, ele be wòawɔ adzɔgbe siwo katã wòɖe kple nu siwo wòtsri na eɖokui la dzi.

english_verse: But if he hears about the promise and does object, she no longer has to keep it. The Lord will forgive her, because her husband would not allow her to keep the promise.
translation_verse: Ke ne gbe si gbe srɔ̃a se nyaa eye wògbe nɛ la, ekema magawɔ adzɔgbe si wòke nu ɖe la, alo nu si wòtsri la dzi o. Aƒetɔ atsɔe akee elabe srɔ̃ae xe mɔ nɛ be megawɔ wo dzi o.

english_verse: Her husband has the final say about any promises she makes to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ne nyɔnu srɔ̃tɔ aɖe ɖe adzɔgbe alo ka atam tsri nu na eɖokui la, srɔ̃a kpɔ mɔ ana wòawɔ edzi loo, alo agblẽ eme nɛ.

english_verse: If her husband hears about a promise and says nothing about it for a whole day, she must do what she said—since he did not object, the promise must be kept.
translation_verse: Ke ne gbe si gbe srɔ̃a se nya la wòzi kpi, eye megblɔ nya aɖeke o la, ekema nyɔnua awɔ adzɔgbe siwo katã wòɖe alo nu si wòtsri na eɖokui la dzi. Srɔ̃a lɔ̃ ɖe edzi, elabe gbe si gbe wòsee la, megblɔ nya aɖeke o.

english_verse: But if he waits until the next day to stop her from keeping her promise, he is the one who must be punished.
translation_verse: Gake ne srɔ̃ŋutsua se nyaa, zi kpi, eye emegbe hafi wòva gbe na nyɔnua be megawɔ edzi o la, vodada la zu ŋutsua tɔ, eye menye nyɔnua tɔ o.”

english_verse: These are the laws that the Lord gave Moses about husbands and wives, and about young daughters who still live at home.
translation_verse: Esiawoe nye ɖoɖo siwo ku ɖe adzɔgbeɖeɖe ŋu na ɖetugbi si meɖe srɔ̃ haɖe o, eye wògale tɔ́a ƒeme ko kple nyɔnu si le atsuƒe la.

english_verse: “Before you die, make sure that the Midianites are punished for what they did to Israel.”
translation_verse: “Bia hlɔ̃ Midiantɔwo le nu si wowɔ Israelviwo la ta. Ne èwɔ esia vɔ la, àku.”

english_verse: Then Moses told the people, “The Lord wants to punish the Midianites. So tell our men to prepare for battle.
translation_verse: Ale Mose gblɔ na dukɔ la be: “Mina miaƒe ŋutsuwo nadzra ɖo ne miaho aʋa ɖe Midiantɔwo ŋu, eye miahe to na wo le nu si wowɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu la ta.

english_verse: Twelve thousand men were picked from the tribes of Israel, and after they were prepared for battle,
translation_verse: Ale Israel-toawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ɖe ame akpe ɖeka ɖo ɖa, ale ame siwo dzra ɖo na aʋaa yiyi la le ame akpe wui eve.

english_verse: Moses sent them off to war. Phinehas the son of Eleazar went with them and took along some things from the sacred tent and the trumpets for sounding the battle signal.
translation_verse: Mose na Pinehas, nunɔla Eleazar vi, kplɔ wo yi aʋa lae. Nu kɔkɔeawo kple kpẽ siwo woaku be aʋawɔlawo nanya nu si woawɔ la le Pinehas ƒe dzikpɔkpɔ te.

english_verse: The Israelites fought against the Midianites, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. They killed all the men,
translation_verse: Woho aʋa ɖe Midiantɔwo ŋu abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose ene, eye wowu Midian-ŋutsuwo katã.

english_verse: including Balaam son of Beor and the five Midianite kings, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
translation_verse: Wowu Midian-fia atɔ̃awo hã. Woawoe nye: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Xur kple Reba. Wowu Bileam, Beor vi, hã.

english_verse: The Israelites captured every woman and child, then led away the Midianites' cattle and sheep, and took everything else that belonged to them.
translation_verse: Israelviwo ɖe aboyo Midian-nyɔnuwo kple ɖeviwo, ha woƒe nyihawo kple alẽhawo katã, lɔ woƒe kesinɔnuwo dzoe,

english_verse: They also burned down the Midianite towns and villages.
translation_verse: eye wotɔ dzo woƒe duwo katã kple woƒe asaɖawo.

english_verse: Israel's soldiers gathered together everything they had taken from the Midianites, including the captives and the animals.
translation_verse: Wokplɔ aboyomeawo kple lãawo, eye wolɔ nu siwo woha kpe ɖe wo ŋu la dzoe.

english_verse: and said, “I can't believe you let the women live!
translation_verse: Ebia wo be: “Nu ka ta miena nyɔnuawo katã tsi agbe?

english_verse: You must put to death every boy and all the women who have ever had sex.
translation_verse: Eya ta miwu ameawo dome ŋutsuvi siwo katã de asi nyɔnu ŋu kpɔ. Nenema ke miwu nyɔnuvi siwo katã de ŋutsu gbɔ kpɔ la hã.

english_verse: But do not kill the young women who have never had sex. You may keep them for yourselves.”
translation_verse: Ke nyɔnuvi siwo katã mede ŋutsu gbɔ kpɔ o le wo dome la natsi anyi na mi.

english_verse: Then Moses said to the soldiers, “If you killed anyone or touched a dead body, you are unclean and have to stay outside the camp for seven days. On the third and seventh days, you must go through a ceremony to make yourselves and your captives clean.
translation_verse: Azɔ mia dometɔ si wu ame alo ka asi ame kuku ŋu la netsi asaɖa la godo ŋkeke adrẽ. Le ŋkeke etɔ̃lia kple adrẽlia gbe la, miɖe nuvɔ̃ ɖa le mia ɖokui kple nyɔnu siwo mieɖe aboyoe la ŋu.

english_verse: Then wash your clothes and anything made from animal skin, goat's hair, or wood.”
translation_verse: Nenema ke miɖe nuvɔ̃ ɖa le avɔwo katã kple nu siwo katã wotsɔ lãgbalẽ, gbɔ̃fu alo ati wɔ la ŋu.”

english_verse: Eleazar then explained, “If you need to purify something that won't burn, such as gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, or lead, you must first place it in a hot fire. After you take it out, sprinkle it with the water that purifies. Everything else should only be sprinkled with the water. Do all of this, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
translation_verse: kpakple nu sia nu si ate ŋu ade dzo me la haha dzoe, ekema wo ŋu akɔ. Gake ele be woatsɔ ameŋukɔtsi aɖe nuvɔ̃ ɖa le wo ŋu. Ke woatsɔ tsi aklɔ nu siwo katã mate ŋu ade dzo me o lae.

english_verse: Wash your clothes on the seventh day, and after that, you will be clean and may return to the camp.” Everything Taken from the Midianites Is Divided
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke adrẽa gbe la, minya miaƒe avɔwo. Ekema mia ŋu kɔ, eye miekpɔ mɔ ayi asaɖa la me.” Nu siwo woha la mama

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: From the half that belongs to the soldiers, set aside for the Lord one out of every
translation_verse: Tsɔ wo na nunɔla Eleazar, abe nunana tɔxɛ ene, na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: So we want to give the Lord all the gold jewelry we took from the Midianites. It's our gift to him for watching over us and our troops.”
translation_verse: Eya ta míetsɔ sikanu siwo mía dome ame sia ame ha la vɛ be míana Aƒetɔ. Nuawoe nye: Sikanuwo, alɔnugawo, asigɛwo, togɛwo kple kɔdzonuwo. Míetsɔ nu siawo le Aƒetɔ nam abe fexexe ɖe míaƒe agbe ta ene ale be wòakpɔ mía ta.”

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar followed the Lord's instructions
translation_verse: Mose kple nunɔla Eleazar wɔ abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose ene.

english_verse: women and gave them to Eleazar to be dedicated to the Lord. Then from the half that belonged to the people, Moses set aside one out of every
translation_verse: Aboyonu siwo aʋawɔlawo ha la ƒe susɔea le: alẽ akpe alafa ade bla adrẽ vɔ atɔ̃;

english_verse: and listed everything that had been taken from the Midianites. The list included
translation_verse: nyɔnuvi siwo mede ŋutsu gbɔ kpɔ o la le akpe bla etɔ̃ vɔ eve.

english_verse: The army commanders went to Moses
translation_verse: Aʋakplɔla siwo kplɔ aʋakɔ la de aʋa lae la va Mose gbɔ,

english_verse: and said, “Sir, we have counted our troops, and not one soldier is missing.
translation_verse: eye wogblɔ nɛ be: “Amegã, míexlẽ aʋawɔla siwo nède asi na mí míekplɔ de aʋa lae, eye woƒe xexlẽme de; ɖeke metsi aʋa o.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar accepted the jewelry from the commanders,
translation_verse: Ale Mose kple nunɔla Eleazar xɔ sika la. Sika sia nye sikatsyɔ̃ɖonu ƒomevi vovovowo.

english_verse: This did not include the things that the soldiers had kept for themselves.
translation_verse: Nu siwo aʋawɔla siwo menye aʋakplɔlawo o ya ha la tsi wo si; wometsɔ wo na o.

english_verse: So Moses and Eleazar placed the gold in the Lord's sacred tent to remind Israel of what had happened.
translation_verse: Mose kple Eleazar tsɔ sikanuawo yi godoƒegbadɔ la me ale be woanye ŋkuɖodzinu na Aƒetɔ be wòakpɔ Israelviwo ta.

english_verse: then after the Lord helps Israel capture the land, you can return to your own land. You will no longer have to stay with the others.
translation_verse: eye wòaxɔ anyigba la. Emegbe miatrɔ agbɔ, eye Aƒetɔ magabu fɔ mi o, elabe miewɔ nu si wòle be miawɔ na eya kple mia nɔvi Israelvi bubuawo siaa. Ale Aƒetɔ ana anyigba sia azu mia tɔ.

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben and Gad owned a lot of cattle and sheep, and they saw that the regions of Jazer and Gilead had good pastureland.
translation_verse: Lãha geɖe le Ruben viwo kple Gad viwo si. Esi wokpɔ be anyigba si le Yazer kple Gilead nyo na lãnyinyi la,

english_verse: So they went to Moses, Eleazar, and the other leaders of Israel and said,
translation_verse: woyi Mose kple nunɔla Eleazar kpakple ha la ƒe amegãwo gbɔ, eye wogblɔ na wo be:

english_verse: “The Lord has helped us capture the land around the towns of Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon. That's good pastureland, and since we own cattle and sheep,
translation_verse: anyigba siwo Aƒetɔ xɔ le Israel ŋkume la nyo na lãnyinyi, eye lãwo le wò dɔlawo si.”

english_verse: would you let us stay here east of the Jordan River and have this land as our own?”
translation_verse: Eya ta míeɖe kuku, mitsɔ anyigba sia na mí, wòazu mía tɔ, ne míawo míatsi afii, eye míatso Yordan aɖanɔ egodo o.”

english_verse: Moses answered: You mean you'd stay here while the rest of the Israelites go into battle?
translation_verse: Mose ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Nu ka! Ɖe miedi be miawo miatsi afii, ne mia nɔviwo ya nayi aɖanɔ aʋa wɔma?

english_verse: If you did that, it would discourage the others from crossing over into the land the Lord promised them.
translation_verse: Nu ka ta miedi be yewoaɖe dzi le Israelviwo ƒo, be womagayi tɔa godo aɖanɔ anyigba si Aƒetɔ na wo la dzi o?

english_verse: This is exactly what happened when I sent your ancestors from Kadesh-Barnea to explore the land.
translation_verse: Alea tututu mia tɔ́wo wɔ, esi medɔ wo le Kades-Barnea be woayi ɖatsa ŋku le anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: They went as far as Eshcol Valley, then returned and told the people that we should not enter it.
translation_verse: Amedɔdɔawo zɔ ʋuu va ɖo Eskol Bali me, eye wokpɔ anyigba la. Esi wotrɔ gbɔ la, woɖe dzi le Israelviwo ƒo be womegayi anyigba si Aƒetɔ na wo la dzi o.

english_verse: Moses said: You promised that you would be ready to fight for the Lord.
translation_verse: Mose ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Nenye aleae nye miaƒe susu la, ekema mibla akpa le Aƒetɔ ŋkume be miayi aɖawɔ aʋa.

english_verse: but he was so angry with the others that he forced them to wander around in the desert for
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ do dɔmedzoe ɖe Israel-dukɔ la ŋu elabe wowɔ nuvɔ̃ eya ta wòna wotsa le gbedadaƒo ƒe bla ene sɔŋ va se ɖe esime dzidzime ma katã tsrɔ̃ vɔ keŋ.

english_verse: So Moses gave the Machirites the region of Gilead, and they settled there.
translation_verse: Ale Mose tsɔ Gilead na Manase vi, Maxir dzidzimeviwo.

english_verse: Now you people of Reuben and Gad are doing the same thing and making the Lord even angrier.
translation_verse: Azɔ mi nuvɔ̃wɔlawo ƒe dzidzime yeye, xɔxɔm miele ɖe mia tɔ́wo teƒe be miana Aƒetɔ nagado dziku ɖe Israel ŋu wu tsã?

english_verse: If you reject the Lord, he will once again abandon his people and leave them here in the desert. And you will be to blame!
translation_verse: Ne mi, Ruben kple Gad viwo, mietrɔ le eyome la, Aƒetɔ agaɖe nu le ame gbogbo siawo ƒe nya me le gbedadaƒo. Ne esia va eme la, eme nekɔ na mi be yewoe na ameawo tsrɔ̃.”

english_verse: The men from Reuben and Gad replied: Let us build places to keep our sheep and goats, and towns for our wives and children,
translation_verse: Tete wote ɖe Mose ŋu gblɔ nɛ be: “Fifia la, na míatɔ abɔ na míaƒe lãwo ɖe afii, eye míatso du sesẽ na mía viwo hã ɖe afii.

english_verse: We will stay with them until they have settled in their own tribal lands.
translation_verse: Míatrɔ agbɔ va mía nɔƒewo o, negbe Israelviwo dome ame sia ame ɖe wòxɔ anyigba si nye etɔ gome.

english_verse: The land on this side of the Jordan River will be ours, so we won't expect to receive any on the other side.
translation_verse: Míawo míegale anyigba aɖeke xɔ ge ɖe wo dome le Yordan godo o, elabe míexɔ anyigba xoxo ɖe afii le Yordan ɣedzeƒe gome.”

english_verse: You also agreed to cross the Jordan and stay with the rest of the Israelites, until the Lord forces our enemies out of the land. If you do these things,
translation_verse: Mina mia dome aʋawɔlawo katã nabla akpa atso Yordan-tɔsisi la, eye Aƒetɔ adze ŋgɔ na wo va se ɖe esime wòɖu miaƒe futɔwo dzi,

english_verse: But if you don't keep your promise, you will sin against the Lord and be punished.
translation_verse: Ke ne miewɔ miaƒe ŋugbedodoa dzi o la, miewɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu, eye wòahe to na mi le eta.

english_verse: Go ahead and build towns for your wives and children, and places for your sheep and goats. Just be sure to do what you have promised.
translation_verse: Eya ta mitso duwo na mia viwo, eye mitɔ abɔ na miaƒe lãwo, ke miwɔ nya si miawo ŋutɔ mieke nu gblɔ la dzi.”

english_verse: The men from Reuben and Gad answered: Sir, we will do just what you have said.
translation_verse: Gad viwo kple Ruben viwo gblɔ na Mose be: “Amegã, míawɔ nu si nègblɔ na mi la.

english_verse: Our wives and children and sheep and cattle will stay here in the towns in Gilead.
translation_verse: Míana mía viwo, mía srɔ̃wo, míaƒe alẽhawo kple nyihawo katã atsi Gilead-duwo me.

english_verse: But those of us who are prepared for battle will cross the Jordan and fight for the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke mí ame mamlɛawo katã míabla akpa le Aƒetɔ ƒe kpɔkplɔ te ayi aʋa le tɔa godo le wò gbeɖeɖe nu.”

english_verse: Then Moses said to Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders,
translation_verse: Ale Mose ɖe gbe na nunɔla Eleazar, Yosua kple Israel-toawo ƒe amegãwo be:

english_verse: “Make sure that the tribes of Gad and Reuben prepare for battle and cross the Jordan River with you. If they do, then after the land is in your control, give them the region of Gilead as their tribal land.
translation_verse: “Ne Gad viwo kple Ruben viwo katã bla akpa le Aƒetɔ ƒe kpɔkplɔ te yi aʋa kpli mi le Yordan godo, eye mieɖu dzi la, mitsɔ Gilead-nyigba na wo, wòazu wo tɔ.

english_verse: But if they break their promise, they will receive land on the other side of the Jordan, like the rest of the tribes.”
translation_verse: Evɔ ne womebla akpa yi tɔa godo kpli mi ɖakpe ɖe mia ŋu le aʋa me o la, ekema wonexɔ anyigba ɖe mia dome le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.”

english_verse: The tribes of Gad and Reuben replied, “We are your servants and will do whatever the Lord has commanded.
translation_verse: Tete Gad viwo kple Ruben viwo ɖo eŋu be: “Míawɔ nu si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo la pɛpɛpɛ.

english_verse: We will cross the Jordan River, ready to fight for the Lord in Canaan. But the land we will inherit as our own will be on this side of the river.”
translation_verse: Míabla akpa le Aƒetɔ ƒe kpɔkplɔ te ayi Kanaan-nyigba dzi aɖawɔ aʋa be anyigba si su mía si le Yordan ƒe ɣedzeƒe afii la natsi mía si.”

english_verse: So Moses gave the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh the territory and towns that King Sihon the Amorite had ruled, as well as the territory and towns that King Og of Bashan had ruled.
translation_verse: Ale Mose tsɔ Sixon, Amori-fia kple Og, Basan-fia ƒe dziɖuƒewo kple du siwo le nutoawo me la katã na Gad viwo kple Ruben viwo kpakple Manase, Yosef vi ƒe to afã.

english_verse: The tribe of Gad rebuilt the towns of Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
translation_verse: Du sesẽ siwo Gad viwo tso la woe nye: Dibon, Atarot, Aroer,

english_verse: Atroth-Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
translation_verse: Aterot-Sofan, Yazer, Yogbeha,

english_verse: Beth-Nimrah, and Beth-Haran. They built walls around them and also built places to keep their sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Bet-Nimra kple Bet-Xaran. Wotɔ alẽkpɔwo ɖe du siawo ŋu.

english_verse: The tribe of Reuben rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
translation_verse: Du siwo Ruben viwo tso la woe nye: Xesbon, Eleale, Kiryataim

english_verse: Sibmah, as well as the towns that used to be known as Nebo and Baal-Meon. They renamed all those places.
translation_verse: Nebo, Baal-Meon kple Sibma. Wotsɔ ŋkɔ yeyewo na du siwo wotso la.

english_verse: The clan of Machir from the tribe of East Manasseh went to the region of Gilead, captured its towns, and forced out the Amorites.
translation_verse: Manase vi, Maxir viwo yi ɖaxɔ Gilead, eye wonyà Amoritɔ siwo le eme la wodzo.

english_verse: Jair from the Manasseh tribe captured villages and renamed them “Villages of Jair.”
translation_verse: Yair, Manase vi, yi ɖaxɔ woƒe kɔƒe aɖewo, eye wòna ŋkɔ wo be “Yair ƒe kɔƒewo.”

english_verse: Nobah captured the town of Kenath with its villages and renamed it Nobah.
translation_verse: Nobax yi ɖaxɔ Kenat kple eŋu kɔƒewo, eye wòtsɔ eƒe ŋkɔ nɛ be Nobax.

english_verse: As Israel traveled from Egypt under the command of Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Esime Israelviwo ʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi yina le Mose kple Aron ƒe kpɔkplɔ te la, woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe teƒeteƒewo le hatsotso hatsotso me.

english_verse: Moses kept a list of the places they camped, just as the Lord had instructed. Here is the record of their journey:
translation_verse: Ne woɖo teƒe aɖe heƒu asaɖa anyi ɖi la, Aƒetɔ nana Mose ŋlɔa teƒea ŋkɔ ɖi. Teƒe siwo wotɔ ɖo le mɔzɔzɔa me la woe nye:

english_verse: After the Israelites left Rameses, they camped at Succoth,
translation_verse: Israelviwo ho tso Ramses va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Sukot.

english_verse: and from there, they moved their camp to Etham on the edge of the desert.
translation_verse: Wogaho tso Sukot va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Etam le kegbegbe la nu.

english_verse: Then they turned back toward Pi-Hahiroth, east of Baal-Zephon, and camped near Migdol.
translation_verse: Esi woho tso afi ma la, wotrɔ ɖo ta Pi-Haxirot le Baal-Zefon ŋgɔ, eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Migdol ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome.

english_verse: They left Pi-Hahiroth, crossed the Red Sea, then walked three days into the Etham Desert and camped at Marah.
translation_verse: Woho tso Pihaxirot eye wotso ƒu la va Sur-gbedadaƒo. Wozɔ Etam-gbedadaƒo ŋkeke etɔ̃, eye wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Mara.

english_verse: They left Elim and camped near the Red Sea,
translation_verse: Woho tso Elim va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Aƒlaƒu la nu.

english_verse: then turned east and camped along the western edge of the Sinai Desert.
translation_verse: Esi wotso le afi sia la, wova nɔ Zin-gbedadaƒo la.

english_verse: From there they went to Dophkah, Alush, and Rephidim, where they had no water.
translation_verse: Esi wotso le Alus la, wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Refidim, afi si womekpɔ tsi aɖeke le ano o.

english_verse: They left Rephidim and finally reached the Sinai Desert.
translation_verse: Esi woho tso Refidim la, wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Sinai-gbedadaƒo.

english_verse: When they left Kadesh, they came to Mount Hor, on the border of Edom.
translation_verse: Woho tso Kades heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Hor-to la gbɔ le Edom ƒe liƒo dzi.

english_verse: That's where the Lord commanded Aaron the priest to go to the top of the mountain. Aaron died there on the first day of the fifth month,
translation_verse: Nunɔla Aron lia Hor-to la, abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ ene, eye wòku le afi ma, le esime Israelviwo ʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi ƒe bla ene megbe le ɣleti atɔ̃lia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi.

english_verse: It was then that the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Southern Desert of Canaan, heard that Israel was headed that way.
translation_verse: Arad-fia si le Kanaan ƒe anyigbeme gome la se be Israelviwo gbɔna.

english_verse: and finally in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Woho tso Abarim-towo gbɔ heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Moab-gbegbe le Yordan nu le Yerixo kasa.

english_verse: Their camp stretched from Beth-Jeshimoth to Acacia. The Lord's Command To Conquer Canaan
translation_verse: Woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Yordan nu tso Bet-Yesimot va se ɖe Abel-Sitim le Moab-gbegbe. Ɖoɖo si wowɔ na Israelviwo hafi wotso Yordan-tɔsisi la

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose le Moab-gbegbe le Yordan nu le Yerixo kasa be:

english_verse: to give the people of Israel this message: When you cross the Jordan River and enter Canaan,
translation_verse: Gblɔ na Israelviwo be: “Ne mietso Yordan-tɔsisia va Kanaan-nyigba dzi la,

english_verse: you must force out the people living there. Destroy their idols and tear down their altars.
translation_verse: minyà anyigbaa dzi nɔlawo katã ɖa le anyigba la dzi. Migbã woƒe aklama kpakpɛwo katã, legbawo katã kple woƒe mawusubɔƒewo keŋ.

english_verse: Then settle in the land—I have given it to you as your own.
translation_verse: Mixɔ anyigba la le wo si mianɔ edzi, elabe ɖe metsɔe na mi be wòazu mia tɔ.

english_verse: I will show you how to divide the land among the tribes, according to the number of clans in each one, so that the larger tribes will have more land than the smaller ones.
translation_verse: Midzidze nu ɖe anyigba la dzi, eye miamae ɖe miaƒe toawo kple ƒomeawo nu. Teƒe si dzi nudzidze la dze la, mitsɔ lolotɔwo na ƒome siwo sɔ gbɔ eye mitsɔ suetɔwo na ƒome siwo mesɔ gbɔ o.

english_verse: If you don't force out all the people there, they will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your back. They will always be trouble for you,
translation_verse: Ke ne mienyà anyigba la dzi nɔlawo ɖa o la, ame siwo susɔ la azu abe ŋu ene anɔ miaƒe ŋku ta kple abe aŋɔka ene anɔ mia xa, eye woaɖe fu na mi le anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: and I will treat you as severely as I planned on treating them.
translation_verse: Eya ta ne mienyà wo ɖa o la, mawɔ nu si meɖo be mawɔ wo la miawo boŋ vevie.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: to tell the people of Israel that their land in Canaan would have the following borders:
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na Israelviwo be: “Ne mieɖo Kanaan-nyigba, si tsɔm mele na mi be nenye mia tɔ dzi la, eƒe liƒowo anye esiwo gbɔna:

english_verse: The southern border will be the Zin Desert and the northwest part of Edom. This border will begin at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Miaƒe anyigbemeliƒo natso Zin-gbedadaƒo amlo ato Edom ŋu. Adze egɔme tso Ƒukuku la ƒe mlɔenu le ɣedzeƒe gome, eye

english_verse: It will go west from there, but will turn southward to include Scorpion Pass, the village of Zin, and the town of Kadesh-Barnea. From there, the border will continue to Hazar-Addar and on to Azmon.
translation_verse: wòaɖo ta Akrabim-todzimɔ ƒe anyigbeme gome. Ato Zin ŋu ayi ɖe Kades Barnea ƒe anyigbeme lɔƒo, eye wòaɖo ta Xazar-Adar ava ke ɖe Azmon.

english_verse: It will run along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Liƒo la anyè kpo tso Azmon afii ayi ɖe Egipte-tɔʋu la ŋu, eye wòava wu nu ɖe Domeƒu nu.”

english_verse: The western border will be the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: “Miaƒe ɣetoɖoƒeliƒo nanye Domeƒu la.

english_verse: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean, then continue eastward to Mount Hor.
translation_verse: “Miaƒe dzigbemeliƒo la natso Domeƒu la nu, eye wòato Hor-to la ŋu.

english_verse: After that, it will run to Lebo-Hamath and across to Zedad, which is the northern edge of your land.
translation_verse: Atso le Hor-to la gbɔ aɖo ta Xamat, eye wòava do ɖe Zedad.

english_verse: From Zedad, the border will continue east to Ziphron and end at Hazar-Enan.
translation_verse: Liƒo la nato Zifron ava wu nu ɖe Xazar-Enan. Miaƒe dzigbemeliƒo la nanye esi.

english_verse: and on down to Riblah on the east side of Ain. From there, it will go south to the eastern hills of Lake Galilee,
translation_verse: ato Ribla le Ain ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome, eye wòazɔ Kineret-ƒu ƒe ɣedzeƒekpa ŋu.

english_verse: then follow the Jordan River down to the north end of the Dead Sea. The land within those four borders will belong to you.
translation_verse: Nezɔ Yordan ŋu, eye wòava wu nu ɖe Ƒukuku la nu. “Liƒo siawo naƒo xlã miaƒe anyigba la.”

english_verse: Then Moses told the people, “You will receive the land inside these borders. It will be yours, but the Lord has commanded you to divide it among the nine and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Ale Mose gblɔ na Israelviwo be: “Esiae nye anyigba si Aƒetɔ gblɔ be woatsɔ na to asieke kple afã. Ɖe woadzidze nu ɖe edzi hafi amae na mi.

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh have already been given their land
translation_verse: Ruben viwo ƒe to kple Gad viwo hã tɔ kpakple Manase ƒe to afã xɔ woƒe anyigba xoxo ɖe woƒe aƒekɔwo nu.

english_verse: across from Jericho, east of the Jordan River.” The Leaders Who Will Divide the Land
translation_verse: Woxɔ anyigba le Yordan ƒe go kemɛ dzi le Yerixo kasa.” Tatɔ siwo le anyigba la mama nu

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be:

english_verse: “Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun will divide the land for the Israelites.
translation_verse: “Nunɔla Eleazar kple Yosua, Nun vi, nama anyigba la na dukɔ la.

english_verse: These are the men the Lord commanded to help Eleazar and Joshua divide the land for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ame siawoe Aƒetɔ ɖo be woama anyigba la na Israelviwo le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: to say to them: When you receive your tribal lands, you must give towns and pastures to the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na Israelviwo be woana duwo Levitɔwo ɖe woƒe anyigba dzi, ne woanɔ wo me, eye woana lãnyiƒewo hã wo. Lãnyiƒeawo naƒo xlã duawo akpe ɖo.

english_verse: That way, the Levites will have towns to live in and pastures for their animals.
translation_verse: Levi viawo nanɔ duawo me, eye woƒe nyihawo, aƒemelãwo kple lã bubuawo nanɔ lãnyiƒeawo.

english_verse: The pasture around each of these towns must be in the shape of a square, with the town itself in the center. The pasture is to measure
translation_verse: ale be lãnyiƒe si le dua ƒe akpa eneawo ƒe didime kple kekeme nasɔ; woanye meta alafa asieke le goawo katã me, eye dua ŋutɔ nanɔ titina.

english_verse: Six of the towns you give them will be Safe Towns where a person who has accidentally killed someone can run for protection. But you will also give the Levites
translation_verse: Mitsɔ sitsoƒedu ade siwo me hlɔ̃dola si meɖo wu ame o la, nasí ayi la na wo. Azɔ la, mitsɔ du bla ene vɔ eve kpe ɖe wo ŋu na wo.

english_verse: Since the towns for the Levites must come from Israel's own tribal lands, the larger tribes will give more towns than the smaller ones. The Safe Towns (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Anyigba si to aɖe xɔ la ƒe lolome ŋue wòle be wòana duawo ɖo. To siwo ƒe anyigba lolo la, nana du geɖe, ke esiwo tɔ melolo o la, nana du ʋɛ aɖewo ko.” Sitsoƒeduwo (Mos V,

english_verse: by one of the victim's relatives. He will take revengefor his relative's death as soon as he finds you.
translation_verse: Ame si dze abia hlɔ̃ le ƒomea me la kpɔ mɔ abia hlɔ̃e. Ne edo goe le afi aɖe la, ekpɔ mɔ awui faa.

english_verse: The Lord then told Moses
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose

english_verse: to tell the people of Israel: After you have crossed the Jordan River and are settled in Canaan,
translation_verse: be: Gblɔ na Israelviwo be: ‘Ne mietso Yordan-tɔsisi la ge ɖe Kanaan-nyigba dzi la,

english_verse: choose Safe Towns, where a person who has accidentally killed someone can run for protection.
translation_verse: mitia duwo ne woanye sitsoƒe na mi. Du siawo mee ame si meɖo wu ame o la lasí ayi.

english_verse: If the victim's relatives think it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of these Safe Towns for protection and not be killed before a trial is held.
translation_verse: Woanye sitsoƒe na mi le hlɔ̃bialawo ta. Hafi woawu hlɔ̃dola aɖe la, ele be woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnui le ameha la ŋkume.

english_verse: three on each side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Etɔ̃ nanɔ Yordan ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome, eye etɔ̃ nanɔ Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: They will be places of protection for anyone who lives in Israel and accidentally kills someone. Laws about Murder and Accidental Killing The Lord said:
translation_verse: Du ade siawo nanye sitsoƒe na Israelviwo, amedzrowo kple ame siwo le wo gbɔ la siaa. Ame si meɖo wu ame o la ate ŋu así ayi du siawo dometɔ aɖe me.”

english_verse: Suppose you hit someone with a piece of iron or a large stone or a dangerous wooden tool. If that person dies, then you are a murderer and must be put to death
translation_verse: Alo ne etsɔ kpo si adze ame wòaku la ƒoe wòku la, enye amewula; ele be woawu amewula la.

english_verse: Or suppose you get angry and kill someone by pushing or hitting or by throwing something. You are a murderer and must be put to death by one of the victim's relatives.
translation_verse: alo ƒoe kple kɔ wòku la, ewu ame, eya ta ele be woawu eya hã. Ame kukua ƒe ƒometɔ ɖe sia ɖe kpɔ mɔ abia hlɔ̃e. Ne edo goe le afi aɖe la, ekpɔ mɔ awui faa.”

english_verse: But if you are not angry and accidentally kill someone in any of these ways, the townspeople must hold a trial and decide if you are guilty.
translation_verse: Ne eva eme alea la, ameha la nadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu le amewula la kple ƒometɔ si di be yeabia hlɔ̃ la dome ale:

english_verse: If they decide that you are innocent, you will be protected from the victim's relative and sent to stay in one of the Safe Towns until the high priest dies.
translation_verse: Ha la naɖe amewula la tso ƒometɔ si di be yeabia hlɔ̃ la si me. Woana woakplɔe agbugbɔ yi sitsoƒedu si me wòsí yi la me, eye wòanɔ afi ma va se ɖe esime nunɔlagã si li hafi wòde la naku.

english_verse: But if you ever leave the Safe Town
translation_verse: Ke nenye be amewula la do le sitsoƒedu si me wòsí yi ɖo la me,

english_verse: and are killed by the victim's relative, he cannot be punished for killing you.
translation_verse: eye ƒometɔ si di be yeabia hlɔ̃e do goe le afi aɖe hewui la, womabu ƒometɔ hlɔ̃biala sia amewulae o.

english_verse: You must stay inside the town until the high priest dies; only then can you go back home.
translation_verse: Ele be amewula la nanɔ sitsoƒedua me va se ɖe esime nunɔlagã la naku. Le nunɔlagã la ƒe ku megbe la, amewula la kpɔ mɔ agbugbɔ yi aƒe.

english_verse: The community of Israel must always obey these laws.
translation_verse: Mina miaƒe dzidzimeviwo nawɔ ɖoɖo siawo dzi le afi sia afi si miayi la.

english_verse: Death is the penalty for murder. But no one accused of murder can be put to death unless there are at least two witnesses to the crime.
translation_verse: “Ne wobe ame aɖe wu ame la, ɖasefo ɖeka nagaɖi ɖase le eŋu ko woabui fɔɖila, awui o. Ele be ɖasefoawo nade eve alo wu nenema godoo.

english_verse: You cannot give someone money to escape the death penalty; you must pay with your own life!
translation_verse: Ne ame aɖe wu ame la, ele be woawu eya hã. Megaxe ga aɖe ko woagblẽe ɖi o.

english_verse: And if you have been proven innocent of murder and are living in a Safe Town, you cannot pay to go back home; you must stay there until the high priest dies.
translation_verse: Ne amewula aɖe sí yi sitsoƒedu aɖe me la, migaɖe mɔ nɛ wòaxe ga ko atrɔ adzo ayi aƒe, esime nunɔlagãa meku haɖe o.

english_verse: One day the family leaders from the Gilead clan of the Manasseh tribe went to Moses and the other family leaders of Israel
translation_verse: Gilead nye Maxir vi. Gilead tɔgbuie nye Manase, Yosef vi. Ƒome siwo le Gilead ƒe aƒekɔ me la ƒe tatɔwo va Mose kple Israelviwo ƒe toawo ƒe amegãwo gbɔ.

english_verse: and said, “Sir, the Lord has said that he will show what land each tribe will receive as their own. And the Lord has commanded you to give the daughters of our relative Zelophehad the land that he would have received.
translation_verse: Wogblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ gblɔ na nye aƒetɔ be woadzidze nu ama anyigba la na Israelviwo. Egagblɔ hã be míatsɔ mía nɔvi Zelofxad ƒe anyigba na via nyɔnuwo.

english_verse: But if they marry men from other tribes of Israel, the land they receive will become part of that tribe's inheritance and will no longer belong to us.
translation_verse: Ke nenye be woɖe srɔ̃ le to bubu me la, woƒe anyigba azu to ma tɔ, eye míaƒe to la ƒe anyigba ava zu sue.

english_verse: Even when land is returned to its original owner in the Year of Celebration, we will not get back Zelophehad's land—it will belong to the tribe into which his daughters married.”
translation_verse: Ne Nugbugbɔxɔ ƒe ƒè ɖo na Israel la, ekema woatsɔ woƒe domenyinu akpe ɖe to si me woɖe srɔ̃ ɖo la tɔ ŋu, woaɖe woƒe domenyinu tso mía tɔgbuiwo ƒe domenyinu ŋu akpe wo tɔ.”

english_verse: So Moses told the people that the Lord had said: These men from the Manasseh tribe are right.
translation_verse: Tete Mose gblɔ nya si Aƒetɔ de esi be negblɔ na wo la na wo. Ebe Aƒetɔ be: “Yosef viwo ƒe to la gblɔe ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: I will allow Zelophehad's daughters to marry anyone, as long as those men belong to one of the clans of the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Zelofxad vinyɔnuwo kpɔ mɔ aɖe ame sia ame si dze wo ŋu la, ke ele be ŋutsua natso woawo ŋutɔ ƒe to la me.

english_verse: Tribal land must not be given to another tribe—it will remain the property of the tribe that received it.
translation_verse: Mele be to aɖeke ƒe anyigba nayi ɖe to bubu me o. Ame sia ame neku ɖe eya ŋutɔ tɔ́a ƒe anyigba ŋu.

english_verse: In the future, any daughter who inherits land must marry someone from her own tribe. Israel's tribal land is never to be passed from one tribe to another.
translation_verse: eye anyigba matso to ɖeka si me ayi ɖe bubu si me o. Toawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ƒe anyigba anye eya ko tɔ tegbee.”

english_verse: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah the daughters of Zelophehad obeyed the Lord and married their uncles' sons
translation_verse: elabe Zelofxad vinyɔnu siwo ŋkɔwo nye Maxla, Tirza, Xogla, Milka kple Noa la, ɖe wo tɔ́ nɔviŋutsuwo ƒe viwo.

english_verse: and remained part of the Manasseh tribe. So their land stayed in their father's clan.
translation_verse: Woɖe srɔ̃ le Yosef vi Manase ƒe ƒomeawo me, eye woƒe anyigba tsi wo tɔ́ ƒe ƒome la si me.

english_verse: These are the laws that the Lord gave to Moses and the Israelites while they were camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Esia nye se kple ɖoɖo siwo Aƒetɔ na Mose gblɔ na Israelviwo le Moab-gbegbe le Yordan nu le Yerixo kasa.

english_verse: Now, turn around and go back into the desert by way of Red Sea Road.
translation_verse: Ke mi ame siawo ya la, mitrɔ ne miaho ato Aƒlaƒu la gbɔ mɔ aɖo ta gbedadaƒo la.

english_verse: People of Israel, when we were in our camp at Mount Sinai, the Lord our God told us: You have stayed here long enough.
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la gblɔ na mí le Xoreb be: ‘Mienɔ to sia gbɔ eteƒe didi.

english_verse: Leave this place and go into the land that belongs to the Amorites and their neighbors the Canaanites. This land includes the Jordan River valley, the hill country, the western foothills, the Southern Desert, the Mediterranean seacoast, the Lebanon Mountains, and all the territory as far as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Mitrɔ ne miaho adzo. Miyi Amoritɔwo ƒe tonyigba kple anyigba siwo katã ƒo xlã wo le nuto ma me la dzi. Teƒe siawoe nye: Yordan-bali me, toawo dzi, gbadzaƒeawo, anyigba si le anyigbemekegbegbe ɖo ta Domeƒu ŋu. Miyi Kanaantɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi eye miato wo ŋu aɖo ta Lebanon ava se Frat-tɔsisi gã la nu.

english_verse: I give you this land, just as I promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Now you must go and take the land. Leaders Were Appointed (Exodus
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, metsɔ anyigba la ɖo mia ŋkume. Miyi ne miaxɔ anyigba si ŋu, Aƒetɔ, ka atam ɖo na mia tɔgbuiwo Abraham, Isak kple Yakob, be yeatsɔ na woawo kple woƒe dzidzimeviwo la.’ Mose tia ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo (Mos II,

english_verse: After I gave these instructions to the judges, I taught you the Lord's commands. Men Were Sent To Explore the Hill Country (Numbers
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, megblɔ nu bubu siwo katã hã wòle be miawɔ la na mi. Ŋkutsalawo dɔdɔ tso Kades-Barnea (Mos IV,

english_verse: You stayed in your tents and grumbled, “The Lord must hate us—he brought us out of Egypt, just so he could hand us over to the Amorites and get rid of us.
translation_verse: Mielĩ liʋiliʋĩ le miaƒe agbadɔwo me be: ‘Aƒetɔ lé fu mí. Eya tae wòkplɔ mí tso Egipte be yeatsɔ de asi na Amoritɔwo ne woatsrɔ̃ ɖo.

english_verse: Right after the Lord commanded us to leave Mount Sinai, I told you: Israel, being your leader is too big a job for one person.
translation_verse: “Ɣe ma ɣi la, megblɔ na mi be: ‘Nye ɖeka nyemate ŋu anɔ mia nu akplɔ mi o.

english_verse: God has even promised to bless us a thousand times more, and I pray that he will.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, mia tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu la nena miasɔ gbɔ ɖe edzi zi akpe nane, eye wòayra mi abe ale si wòdo ŋugbe na mii ene.

english_verse: But I cannot take care of all your problems and settle all your arguments alone.
translation_verse: Ke ale ke nye ɖeka mate ŋu atsɔ miaƒe fuɖenamewo ƒe agba, eye makpɔ miaƒe dzrewɔnyawo gbɔe?
