translation_verse: Tete Yosua ka atam be: “Ame si ke atso be yeagbugbɔ Yerixo-du sia agatso la, Aƒetɔ nena wòaɖi eŋu kpékpekpe. Ame si ɖo dua gɔme anyi la, eƒe ŋgɔgbeviŋutsuvi aku; ame si ade agbo dua nu la, woaɖi eƒe dɔmlɔea ŋutsu.”

english_verse: The Lord helped Joshua in everything he did, and Joshua was famous everywhere in Canaan.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ nɔ kple Yosua, eye amewo ƒo nu nyui le eŋu le dukɔa me godoo.

english_verse: The Lord had said that everything in Jericho belonged to him. But Achan from the Judah tribe took some of the things from Jericho for himself. And so the Lord was angry with the Israelites, because one of them had disobeyed him.
translation_verse: Ke Israel-dukɔ la mewɔ nuteƒe na Mawu le busunu siwo wòbe ame aɖeke megatsɔ o la ƒe nya me o. Ŋutsu aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Axan la tsɔ busunuawo ƒe ɖewo ɣla na eɖokui ale be Aƒetɔ do dɔmedzoe vevie ɖe Israel-dukɔ la ŋu. Axan sia tso Zerax ƒe ƒome me le Yuda-to la me. Tɔ́a ŋkɔe nye Karmi, eye tɔgbuia ŋkɔe nye Sabdi.

english_verse: Joshua and the leaders of Israel tore their clothes and put dirt on their heads to show their sorrow. They lay facedown on the ground in front of the sacred chest until sunset.
translation_verse: Yosua kple dumegãwo dze woƒe awuwo, xlã wo ɖokui ɖi, lɔ ke kɔ ɖe tame, eye wotsyɔ mo anyi ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la ŋgɔ va se ɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: Then Joshua said: Our Lord, did you bring us across the Jordan River just so the Amorites could destroy us? This wouldn't have happened if we had agreed to stay on the other side of the Jordan.
translation_verse: Tete Yosua gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ Mawu, nu ka ta nèhekplɔ dukɔa tsò Yordan-tɔsisi lae? Ðe nèkplɔ mí vɛ be yeade asi na Amoritɔwo ne woatsrɔ̃a? Ne ɖe míetsi Yordan godo la, ne enyo na mí wu!

english_verse: I don't even know what to say to you, since Israel's army has turned and run from the enemy.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, taflatsɛ, esi Israel-dukɔ la sí le woƒe futɔwo nu fifia ɖe, ale ke gblɔ ge mala?

english_verse: Everyone will think you weren't strong enough to protect your people. Now the Canaanites and everyone else who lives in the land will surround us and wipe us out.
translation_verse: Gawu la, Kanaanitɔwo kple ame bubuawo le nutoa me godoo le nya sia se ge tsã. Ekema woaɖe to ɖe mí, eye woawu mía dome ame sia ame. Ekema ɖe, ale ke wɔ ge nàla be bubu naganɔ ŋuwò?”

english_verse: The Lord answered: Stop lying there on the ground! Get up!
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Yosua be: “Tsi tre! Nu ka ta nètsyɔ mo anyi?

english_verse: I said everything in Jericho belonged to me and had to be destroyed. But the Israelites have kept some of the things for themselves. They stole from me and hid what they took. Then they lied about it.
translation_verse: Nu vɔ̃e Israel wɔ! Wotu nu, si mebla kpli wo la. Wotsɔ busunuawo ƒe ɖewo. Wofi wo wɔ alakpanu. Gawu la, wotsɔ busunuawo ɣla ɖe woƒe nuwo dome.

english_verse: What they stole was supposed to be destroyed, and now Israel itself must be destroyed. I cannot help you anymore until you do exactly what I have said. That's why Israel turns and runs from its enemies instead of standing up to them.
translation_verse: Esia tae Israelviwo megate ŋu le te nɔm ɖe woƒe futɔwo nu o ɖo. Woasí le futɔwo nu elabe fiƒode le wo dzi be woatsrɔ̃ godoo. Nyemaganɔ kpli mi azɔ o, negbe ɖe mieɖe busunuawo ɖa le mia dome.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel, “Tomorrow you will meet with the Lord your God, so make yourselves acceptable to worship him. The Lord says that you have taken things that should have been destroyed. You won't be able to stand up to your enemies until you get rid of those things.
translation_verse: Tsi tre nàkɔ dukɔ la ŋuti! Gblɔ na wo be woakɔ wo ɖokui ŋuti hena etsɔ si gbɔna la. Elabe nya si gblɔm Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu la, le nye esi: ‘Israel, mebe busunuawo le mia dome! Miagate ŋu anɔ te ɖe miaƒe futɔwo nu azɔ o, negbe ɖe mieɖe nuawo ɖa le mia dome hafi!’

english_verse: “Tomorrow morning everyone must gather near the place of worship. You will come forward tribe by tribe, and the Lord will show which tribe is guilty. Next, the clans in that tribe must come forward, and the Lord will show which clan is guilty. The families in that clan must come, and the Lord will point out the guilty family. Finally, the men in that family must come,
translation_verse: Eya ta le ŋdi me la, miava ŋkunye me, ame sia ame nanɔ to si me wòtso la me. To si dzi matɔ asii la, nado va ŋgɔgbe, eye ame sia ame nanɔ ƒome si me wòtso la me. Ƒome si dzi matɔ asii la, nado va ŋgɔ, eye ame sia ame nanɔ aƒe si me wòtso la me. Aƒe si dzi matɔ asii la, nado va ŋkunye me, eye ŋutsuwo nado va ɖekaɖeka.

english_verse: and the Lord will show who stole what should have been destroyed. That man must be put to death, his body burned, and his possessions thrown into the fire. He has done a terrible thing by breaking the sacred agreement that the Lord made with Israel.”
translation_verse: Ŋutsu si dzi metɔ asii, eye busunuawo le esi la, woatɔ dzo eya kple eƒe nuwo katã, elabe etu Aƒetɔ ƒe nubabla, eye wòwɔ ŋukpenanu le Israel.”

english_verse: Joshua got up early the next morning and brought each tribe to the place of worship, where the Lord showed that the Judah tribe was guilty.
translation_verse: Le ŋufɔke ŋdi kanya la, Yosua kplɔ Israel-dukɔ la vɛ, le woƒe toawo me. Tete wotɔ asi Yuda-to dzi.

english_verse: Then Joshua brought the clans of Judah to the Lord, and the Lord showed that the Zerah clan was guilty. One by one he brought the leader of each family in the Zerah clan to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Zabdi's family was guilty.
translation_verse: Ena ƒome siwo le Yuda-to la me la te va ɖekaɖeka, eye wotɔ asi Zerax ƒome dzi. Ena Zerax ƒome la me tɔwo te va ɖekaɖeka, eye wotɔ asi Zabdi ƒe aƒe dzi.

english_verse: Finally, Joshua brought each man in Zabdi's family to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Achan was the guilty one.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Yosua na Zabdi ƒemeŋutsuwo te va ɖekaɖeka. Tete asi su Axan, Karmi vi la dzi. Axan nye Zabdi tɔgbuiyɔvi, eye Zabdi tɔ́e nye Zerax.

english_verse: “Achan,” Joshua said, “the Lord God of Israel has decided that you are guilty. So tell me what you did, and don't try to hide anything.”
translation_verse: Yosua gblɔ na Axan be: “Vinye, le Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu la ŋkume, to nyateƒe, eye nàʋu ɖokuiwò me. Fifia, gblɔ nu si nèwɔ la nam; mègaɣlae ɖem o.”

english_verse: “It's true,” Achan answered. “I sinned and disobeyed the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Axan ɖo eŋu be: “Nyateƒee, mewɔ vɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu la ŋu. Nu si mewɔ lae nye be

english_verse: They brought them back and put them in front of the sacred chest, so Joshua and the rest of the Israelites could see them.
translation_verse: Wofɔ nuawo le agbadɔ la me vɛ na Yosua kple Israel-dukɔ blibo la, eye wotsɔ wo ɖo Aƒetɔ ŋkume.

english_verse: Then everyone took Achan and the things he had stolen to Trouble Valley. They also took along his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and everything else that belonged to him.
translation_verse: Tete Yosua kple Israelviwo katã lé Axan, Zerax vi la. Wotsɔ klosalo la, awu ʋlaya la kple sika la, via ŋutsuwo kple via nyɔnuwo, nyi, tedzi kple alẽwo kple eƒe agbadɔ kpakple nu siwo katã le esi la kpe ɖe eŋu va Axor-bali me.

english_verse: Joshua said, “Achan, you caused us a lot of trouble. Now the Lord is paying you back with the same kind of trouble.” The people of Israel then stoned to death Achan and his family. They made a fire and burned the bodies, together with what Achan had stolen, and all his possessions.
translation_verse: Yosua biae be: “Nu ka ta nèhe fukpekpe sia va mía dzi? Aƒetɔ ana wò hã nakpe fu egbe!” Tete Israelviwo katã ƒu kpe Axan wòku. Woƒu kpe srɔ̃a kple viawo hã, eye wotɔ dzo wo kple woƒe nunɔamesiwo wofiã keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: They covered the remains with a big pile of rocks, which is still there. Then the Lord stopped being angry with Israel. That's how the place came to be called Trouble Valley.
translation_verse: Wofɔ kpewo li kɔ gã aɖe ɖe wo dzi. Kpekɔ la gali va se ɖe egbe. Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe dzi fa. Eya ta woyɔa teƒe ma be Axor-bali.

english_verse: The rest of the army will come with me and attack near the gate. When the people of Ai come out to fight, we'll run away and let them chase us. They will think we are running from them just like the first time. But when we've let them chase us far enough away,
translation_verse: Wole mía nya ge ɖe nu va se ɖe esime míana woahe ɖa le dua gbɔ. Wole bubu ge be sisím míegale le yewo nu. Ale míasí le wo gbɔ.

english_verse: you come out of hiding. The Lord our God will help you capture the town.
translation_verse: Ekema miawo miado le xadeƒe la axɔ dua, elabe Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la atsɔe ade mia si.

english_verse: Then set it on fire, as the Lord has told us to do. Those are your orders,
translation_verse: Ne miexɔ dua vɔ la, mitɔ dzoe abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ ene. Kpɔ ɖa, nyee gblɔe na mi.”

english_verse: Early the next morning he got his troops ready to move out, and he and the other leaders of Israel led them to Ai.
translation_verse: Le ŋdi kanya la, Yosua fɔ, eye wòyɔ aʋawɔlaawo ƒo ƒui. Azɔ eya kple Israel-me tsitsiwo dze aʋawɔlaawo ŋgɔ ɖo ta Ai.

english_verse: They set up camp in full view of the town, across the valley to the north.
translation_verse: Aʋawɔla siwo katã le eŋu la zɔ yi ŋgɔ te ɖe dua ŋu. Woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe bali si le woawo kple Ai-dua dome la me le dua ƒe dzigbeme lɔƒo.

english_verse: Now all his troops were in place. Part of the army was in the camp to the north of Ai, and the others were hiding to the west, ready to make a surprise attack. That night, Joshua went into the valley.
translation_verse: Ale wona aʋawɔlaawo dze aʋa ɖi; akpa gãtɔ le dua ƒe dzigbe gome, eye mamlɛawo le dua godo le ɣetoɖoƒe gome. Ke Yosua ŋutɔ tsi bali la me dɔ.

english_verse: Finally, the Lord told Joshua, “Point your sword at the town of Ai, because now I am going to help you defeat it!” As soon as Joshua pointed his sword at the town,
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Yosua be: “Kɔ wò akplɔ dzi do ɖe Ai-dua gbɔ lɔƒo, elabe matsɔe ade asi na wò!” Ekɔe dzi do ɖa.

english_verse: the soldiers who had been hiding jumped up and ran into the town. They captured it and set it on fire.
translation_verse: Kaka wòado asi ɖe dzi la, xadelaawo do go tso woƒe beɖoƒe, ƒu du ge ɖe dua me, xɔe eye wotɔ dzoe enumake.

english_verse: Joshua made sure every building in Ai was burned to the ground. He told his men to kill the king of Ai and hang his body on a tree. Then at sunset he told the Israelites to take down the body, throw it in the gateway of the town, and cover it with a big pile of rocks. Those rocks are still there, and the town itself has never been rebuilt. Joshua Reads the Blessings and Curses (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ede ka ve na Ai-fia ɖe ati aɖe me, eye wòna eƒe kukua nɔ afi ma va se ɖe fiẽ. Esi ɣe yina to ɖo ge la, ena woɖe ame kukua le afi ma, eye wotsɔe ƒu gbe ɖe dua ƒe agbo nu. Wofɔ kpewo li kɔ gã aɖe ɖe edzi. Kpekɔa gale afi ma va se ɖe egbe. Yosua xlẽ Mawu ƒe se la na Israelviwo le Ebal-to dzi

english_verse: The people of Gibeon had also heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
translation_verse: Ke Gibeontɔwo ya se nu si Yosua tu kple Yerixotɔwo kple Aitɔwo.

english_verse: So they decided that some of their men should pretend to be messengers to Israel from a faraway country. The men put worn-out bags on their donkeys and found some old wineskins that had cracked and had been sewn back together.
translation_verse: Ale woawo ya wɔ aye aɖe. Wodi nuɖuɖu na mɔzɔzɔ, di kotoku xoxowo do agbae na woƒe tedziwo, eye wotsɔ waingolo xoxo, vuvu, siwo woka la.

english_verse: Their sandals were old and patched, and their clothes were worn out. They even took along some dry and crumbly bread.
translation_verse: Wodo afɔkpa xoxo, vuvu, siwo woka la. Woƒe awuwo do xoxo, eye abolo si wotsɔ ɖe asi la ƒu kplákplakpla hefli keŋ.

english_verse: Then they went to the Israelite camp at Gilgal, where they said to Joshua and the men of Israel, “We have come from a country that is far from here. Please make a peace treaty with us.”
translation_verse: Tete woyi Yosua gbɔ le asaɖa la me le Gilgal eye wògblɔ na eya kple Israel-ŋutsuwo be: “Anyigba si dzi míetso va la metsɔ o. Ale míedi be miabla nu kpli mí.”

english_verse: We are your servants, and we live far from here. We came because the Lord your God is so famous. We heard what the Lord did in Egypt
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Amegã, anyigba si dzi míetso va la didi ŋutɔ, elabe míese Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la ŋkɔ. Míese nu siwo katã wòwɔ le Egipte

english_verse: and what he did to those two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan: King Og of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, and King Sihon of Heshbon.
translation_verse: kple nu si wòtu kple Amoritɔwo ƒe fia eveawo, Sixon, Xesbon-fia kple Og, Basan-fia si nɔ Astarot, le Yordan godo la hã.

english_verse: Our leaders and everyone who lives in our country told us to meet with you and tell you that all of us are your servants. They said to ask you to make a peace treaty with our people. They told us to be sure and take along enough food for our journey.
translation_verse: Míaƒe ame tsitsiwo kple dukɔmetɔwo katã gblɔ na mí be míadi nuɖuɖu ɖe asi ne míadze mɔ ava do go mi. Wobe miaƒe dɔlawo yewonye eya ta míava bla nu kpli mi.

english_verse: See this dry, crumbly bread of ours? It was hot out of the oven when we packed the food on the day we left our homes.
translation_verse: Abolo si míetsɔ ɖe asi lae nye esi. Gbe si gbe míedze mɔ tso mía de la, abolo dzodzoe wònye nɔ mía si; ke fifia la, kpɔ ɖa, eƒu, hefli keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: These cracked wineskins were new when we filled them, and our clothes and sandals are worn out because we have traveled so far.
translation_verse: Waingolo siawo la, golo yeyewoe wonye míekɔ wain ɖe wo me woyɔ, ke fifia la, kpɔ ɖa, wowó. Azɔ la, mɔ didi si míezɔ lae wɔe be míaƒe awuwo kple afɔkpawo hã vuvu alea.”

english_verse: The Israelites tried some of the food, but they did not ask the Lord if he wanted them to make a treaty.
translation_verse: Ale Israel-ŋutsuwo xɔ Gibeontɔwo ƒe nuɖuɖua ƒe ɖe. Evɔ la, ɖe wòle be woabia gbe Aƒetɔ gbɔ hafi.

english_verse: So Joshua made a peace treaty with the messengers and promised that Israel would not kill their people. Israel's leaders swore that Israel would keep this promise.
translation_verse: Tete Yosua wɔ ŋutifafa kple Gibeontɔwo, eye wòbla nu kpli wo be yeana woatsi agbe. Ameha la ƒe amegãwo ka atam ɖo kpe nubabla la dzi na wo.

english_verse: But they did not attack the towns, because the Israelite leaders had sworn in the name of the Lord that they would let these people live. The Israelites complained about their leaders' decision not to attack,
translation_verse: Ke Israelviwo mewu wo o, elabe ameha la ƒe amegãwo tà Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu la, na wo. Ale ameha blibo la lĩ liʋiliʋĩ le nu si woƒe amegãwo wɔ la ta.

english_verse: Joshua told some of his soldiers, “I want to meet with the Gibeonite leaders. Bring them here.” When the Gibeonites came, Joshua said, “You live close to us. Why did you lie by claiming you lived far away?
translation_verse: Azɔ Yosua na woyɔ Gibeontɔwo va egbɔ eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Nu ka ta mieble mí gblɔ be didiƒe kee yewotso, evɔ wònye mietsɔ ɖe mía gbɔ kpuie hafi?

english_verse: So now you are under a curse, and from now on your people will have to send workers to cut wood and carry water for the place of worship.”
translation_verse: Azɔ aɖi mia ŋu. Kluviwo, nakefɔlawo kple tɔmedelawo ko nye ge miala anɔ nye Mawu la ƒeme tegbee.”

english_verse: The Gibeonites answered, “The Lord your God told his servant Moses that you were to kill everyone who lives here and take their land for yourselves. We were afraid you would kill us, and so we tricked you into making a peace treaty. But we agreed to be your servants,
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu na Yosua be: “Nu si ta míetre aye sia lae nye be míese be Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la gblɔ na eƒe dɔla Mose be yeatsɔ anyigba sia katã ana mi, eye yeawu edzinɔlawo katã le mia ŋgɔ. Míevɔ̃ be miava tsrɔ̃ mí, eya ta míeɖe afɔ sia ɖo.

english_verse: and you are strong enough to do anything to us that you want. We just ask you to do what seems right.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, azɔ míele asiwò me. Nu si wò ya nèbu be eyae nyo, eye wòdze be yeawɔ mí la, wɔ mí.”

english_verse: Joshua did not let the Israelites kill the Gibeonites,
translation_verse: Ale Yosua xɔ na wo, eye meɖe mɔ le wo ŋu na Israelviwo be woawu wo o.

english_verse: but he did tell the Gibeonites that they would have to be servants of the nation of Israel. They would have to cut firewood and bring it for the priests to use for burning sacrifices on the Lord's altar, wherever the Lord decided the altar would be. The Gibeonites would also have to carry water for the priests. And that is still the work of the Gibeonites.
translation_verse: Ke tso gbe ma gbe dzi la, Yosua na Gibeontɔwo zu nakefɔlawo kple tɔmedelawo na ameha la kple Aƒetɔ ƒe vɔsamlekpui la. Wogale dɔ siawo wɔwɔ dzi va se ɖe egbe eye woayi wo wɔwɔ dzi le teƒe si Aƒetɔ atia be woasubɔ ye le la.

english_verse: King Adonizedek of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured and destroyed the town of Ai, and then killed its king as he had done at Jericho. He also learned that the Gibeonites had signed a peace treaty with Israel.
translation_verse: Yerusalem-fia, Adoni-zedek se ale si Yosua xɔ Ai, eye wòtsrɔ̃ dua gbidii, eye wòwu woƒe fia abe ale si wòwɔ na Yerixo-du kple eƒe fia la ene. Ese hã be Gibeontɔwo wɔ ŋutifafa kple Israelviwo, eye Israelviwo xɔ wo ɖe wo dome.

english_verse: This frightened Adonizedek and his people. They knew that Gibeon was a large town, as big as the towns that had kings, and even bigger than the town of Ai had been. And all of the men of Gibeon were warriors.
translation_verse: Nya sia sese do ŋɔdzi na fia la ŋutɔŋutɔ, elabe Gibeon nye du lolo abe fiadu bubuawo ene. Gawu la, elolo wu Ai, eye dua me ŋutsuwo katã nye kalẽtɔwo.

english_verse: So Adonizedek sent messages to the kings of four other towns: King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon. The messages said,
translation_verse: Ale Yerusalem-fia, Adoni-zedek dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Xebron-fia Hoham, Yarmut-fia Piram, Laxis-fia Yafia kple Eglon-fia Debir be:

english_verse: “The Gibeonites have signed a peace treaty with Joshua and the Israelites. Come and help me attack Gibeon!”
translation_verse: “Miva kpe ɖe ŋunye ne míaho aʋa ɖe Gibeontɔwo ŋu elabe woyi ɖawɔ ŋutifafa kple Yosua kpakple Israelviwo.”

english_verse: the Gibeonites sent a message to the Israelite camp at Gilgal: “Joshua, please come and rescue us! The Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together and are attacking us. We are your servants, so don't let us down. Please hurry!”
translation_verse: Gibeontɔwo dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Yosua le asaɖa la me le Gilgal be: “Amegã, mègagblẽ mí wò subɔlawo ɖi o. Netsɔ nàva kpe ɖe mía ŋu. Va xɔ na mí! Amoritɔwo ƒe fia siwo katã le towo dzi la ho aʋa ɖe mía ŋu.”

english_verse: Joshua and his army, including his best warriors, left Gilgal.
translation_verse: Ale Yosua kple eƒe aʋakɔ kpakple kalẽtɔwo katã ho tso Gilgal.

english_verse: “Joshua,” the Lord said, “don't be afraid of the Amorites. They will run away when you attack, and I will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Yosua be: “Mègavɔ̃ wo o, elabe mana miaɖu wo dzi. Wo dometɔ ɖeka hɔ̃ hã manɔ te ɖe nuwò o.”

english_verse: Joshua marched all night from Gilgal to Gibeon and made a surprise attack on the Amorite camp.
translation_verse: Yosua kple eƒe aʋakɔ la zɔ zã tso Gilgal va Gibeon eye wova ƒo ɖe Amoritɔwo dzi kpoyi.

english_verse: The Lord made the enemy panic, and the Israelites started killing them right and left. They chased the Amorite troops up the road to Beth-Horon and kept on killing them, until they reached the towns of Azekah and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ na wolulu esime wokpɔ Israelviwo. Israelviwo wu wo nyamanyama le Gibeon, eye wonyà wo ɖe nu tso toawo dzi ɖi abu do ɖe Bet-Xoron. Wokplɔ wo ɖo nɔ wo wum va se ɖe keke Azeka kple Makeda ke.

english_verse: And while these troops were going down through Beth-Horon Pass, the Lord made huge hailstones fall on them all the way to Azekah. More of the enemy soldiers died from the hail than from the Israelite weapons.
translation_verse: Esi wonɔ sisím le Israel nu tso Bet-Xoron nɔ abu ɖim yina la, Aƒetɔ na kpe gãwo nɔ dzadzam tso dziƒo abe tsi ene henɔ wo ƒom va se ɖe keke Azeka ke hewu wo fũu ŋutɔ. Ame siwo tsi kpeawo nu la sɔ gbɔ wu esiwo tsi Israelviwo ƒe yi nu.

english_verse: The Lord was helping the Israelites defeat the Amorites that day. So about noon, Joshua prayed to the Lord loud enough for the Israelites to hear: “Our Lord, make the sun stop in the sky over Gibeon, and the moon stand still over Aijalon Valley.” So the sun and the moon stopped and stood still until Israel defeated its enemies. This poem can be found in The Book of Jashar. The sun stood still and didn't go down for about a whole day.
translation_verse: Tete ɣe nɔ te ɖi, eye ɣleti tɔ te ɖi, va se ɖe esime dukɔa bia hlɔ̃ woƒe futɔwo. Ðe womeŋlɔ nya sia ɖe Ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe Agbalẽ la me oa? Esi ɣe ɖo ta la, etɔ te eye mezɔ yi ɖaɖo to o. Enɔ afi ma abe ŋkeke blibo ene.

english_verse: Never before and never since has the Lord done anything like that for someone who prayed. The Lord was really fighting for Israel.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ wɔ ɖe amegbetɔ ƒe gbe dzi gbe ma gbe. Ŋkeke aɖeke menɔ nenema kpɔ o, eye ɖeke hã maganɔ nenema akpɔ o, elabe Aƒetɔ nɔ Israelviwo dzi wɔ aʋa na wo.

english_verse: After the battle, Joshua and the Israelites went back to their camp at Gilgal. Joshua Kills the Five Enemy Kings
translation_verse: Le esia megbe la, Yosua kple eƒe aʋakɔwo katã gbugbɔ va asaɖa la me le Gilgal. Yosua lé Amoritɔwo ƒe fia atɔ̃awo

english_verse: While the enemy soldiers were running from the Israelites, the five enemy kings ran away and hid in a cave near Makkedah.
translation_verse: Ke fia atɔ̃awo ya sí yi ɖabè ɖe agado me le Makeda.

english_verse: Joshua's soldiers told him, “The five kings have been found in a cave near Makkedah.”
translation_verse: Ame aɖe yi ɖagblɔ na Yosua be wokpɔ fia atɔ̃awo, wobè ɖe agado me le Makeda.

english_verse: Joshua answered, “Roll some big stones over the mouth of the cave and leave a few soldiers to guard it.
translation_verse: Yosua gblɔ be: “Mimli kpe gãwo tu agadoa nu, eye miɖo amewo afi ma ne woanɔ eŋu dzɔm,

english_verse: But you and everyone else must keep going after the enemy troops, because they will be safe if they reach their walled towns. Don't let them get away! The Lord our God is helping us get rid of them.”
translation_verse: ke miawo ŋutɔ miganɔ afi ma o. Miawo miti futɔawo yome, eye minɔ wo wum tso megbe. Migana woage ɖe woƒe duwo me o, elabe Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la tsɔ wo de asi na mi.”

english_verse: So Joshua and the Israelites almost wiped out the enemy soldiers. Only a few safely reached their walled towns.
translation_verse: Yosua kple Israel-ʋakɔwo wu futɔawo nyamanyama hetsrɔ̃ wo katã kloe. Ke wo dome ame ʋɛ aɖewo sí yi ɖabè ɖe woƒe sitsoƒedu sesẽwo me.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp at Makkedah, where Joshua was waiting for them. No one around there dared say anything bad about the Israelites.
translation_verse: Aʋawɔlaawo katã gbugbɔ va Yosua gbɔ le asaɖa la me le Makeda dedie. Ema megbe la, ame aɖeke megado dzi ke nu gblɔ nya aɖeke ɖe Israelviwo ŋu kpɔ o.

english_verse: Joshua told his soldiers, “Now, move the rocks from the entrance to the cave and bring those five kings to me.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Yosua gblɔ be: “Miɖe nu le agadoa nu ne miakplɔ fia atɔ̃ mawo do goe vɛ nam.”

english_verse: The soldiers opened the entrance to the cave and brought out the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
translation_verse: Wokplɔ fia atɔ̃awo, siwo nye Yerusalem, Xebron, Yarmut, Laxis kple Eglon fiawo la, va egbɔe.

english_verse: After Joshua had called the army together, he forced the five kings to lie down on the ground. Then he called his officers forward and told them, “You fought these kings along with me, so put your feet on their necks.” The officers did this,
translation_verse: Esi wokplɔ wo va Yosua gbɔe la, eyɔ Israel-ŋutsuwo katã vɛ, eye wògblɔ na aʋakplɔla siwo kplɔe de aʋagbedzi la be: “Mite va. Miɖo afɔ ve dzi na fia siawo!” Ale wote va heɖo afɔ ve dzi na wo.

english_verse: and Joshua continued, “Don't ever be afraid or discouraged. Be brave and strong. This is what the Lord will do to all your enemies.”
translation_verse: Yosua gblɔ na wo be: “Migavɔ̃ o, eye dzika megatso mia ƒo hã o. Milé dzi ɖe ƒo eye misẽ ŋu, elabe alea ye Aƒetɔ awɔ miaƒe futɔ siwo awɔ aʋa kpli mi lae.

english_verse: Joshua killed the five kings and told his men to hang each body on a tree. Then at sunset
translation_verse: Emegbe Yosua wu fiaawo. Ede ka ve na wo ɖe ati atɔ̃ ŋu, eye wonɔ atiawo ŋu va se ɖe fiẽ me.

english_verse: he told some of his troops, “Take the bodies down and throw them into the cave where the kings were found. Cover the entrance to the cave with big rocks.” Joshua's troops obeyed his orders, and those rocks are still there. Joshua Continues the Fighting
translation_verse: Esi ɣe yina to ɖo ge la, eɖe gbe be woaɖe woƒe kukuawo le atiawo ŋu. Woɖe wo, eye wotsɔ wo yi ɖaƒu gbe ɖe agado siwo me wobè ɖo va yi la me. Tete amewo mli kpe gãwo tsɔ tu agadoawo nu. Wogale afi ma va se ɖe egbe. Yosua xɔ Amoritɔwo ƒe anyigba bubuwo hã

english_verse: Later that day, Joshua captured Makkedah and killed its king and everyone else in the town, just as he had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Yosua xɔ Makeda-du gbe ma gbe, eye wòwu dufia la kple ame sia ame le dua me; ɖeke mekpɔ mɔ sí o. Nu si wòwɔ Yerixo-fia la, eya kee wòwɔ Makeda-fia hã.

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Makkedah and attacked the town of Libnah.
translation_verse: Eyome eya kple eƒe aʋakɔ la katã ho tso Makeda yi Libna, eye wokpe aʋa kple afi ma tɔwo.

english_verse: The Lord let them capture the town and its king, and they killed the king and everyone else, just as they had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ tsɔ dua kple emefia siaa de asi na Israelviwo, eye wowu ame sia ame le dua me; ɖeke mesusɔ o. Nu si Yosua wɔ Yerixo-fia la, eya kee wòwɔ Libna-fia la hã.

english_verse: Joshua then led his army to Lachish, and they set up camp around the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Yosua kple eƒe aʋakɔ la katã ho tso Libna yi Laxis. Woɖe to ɖe dua, eye wowɔ aʋa kplii.

english_verse: and the next day the Lord let them capture the town. They killed everyone, as they had done at Libnah.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ na Israelviwo ɖu Laxistɔwo dzi le ŋkeke evea gbe. Wowu dua me tɔwo katã abe ale si wowɔ le Libna ene; womegblẽ ɖeke ɖi o.

english_verse: King Horam of Gezer arrived to help Lachish, but Joshua and his troops attacked and destroyed him and his army.
translation_verse: Gezer-fia Horam ho va be yeava xɔ na Laxistɔwo. Ke Yosua ɖu eya kple eƒe aʋakɔwo hã dzi keŋkeŋ ale be wo dometɔ aɖeke metsi agbe o.

english_verse: From Lachish, Joshua took his troops to Eglon, where they set up camp surrounding the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Yosua ho kple eƒe aʋakɔ la tso Laxis yi Eglon. Woɖe to ɖe dua, eye wowɔ aʋa kplii.

english_verse: captured it that same day, then killed everyone, as they had done at Lachish.
translation_verse: Woɖu dua me tɔwo dzi gbe ma gbe ke, eye wowu wo katã. Wotsrɔ̃ wo abe ale si wowɔ le Laxis ene.

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Eglon and attacked Hebron.
translation_verse: Emegbe la, Yosua ho kple eƒe aʋakɔ la tso Eglon yi Xebron, eye wòwɔ aʋa kpli wo.

english_verse: They captured the town and the nearby villages, then killed everyone, including the king. They destroyed Hebron in the same way they had destroyed Eglon.
translation_verse: Woɖu Xebrontɔwo dzi. Wowu woƒe fia kple ame sia ame le woƒe duwo me. Yosua gbã dua gbidigbidi abe ale si wòwɔ Eglon-du la ene. Ame ɖeka hɔ̃ hã metsi agbe le eme o.

english_verse: Joshua and the Israelite army turned and attacked Debir.
translation_verse: Eyome eya kple eƒe aʋakɔ la trɔ ɖe Debir-du ŋu, eye wowɔ aʋa kplii.

english_verse: They captured the town, and its nearby villages. Then they destroyed Debir and killed its king, together with everyone else, just as they had done with Hebron and Libnah.
translation_verse: Woɖu Debirtɔwo dzi. Asi su woƒe fia dzi, eye woxɔ woƒe duwo. Wowu ame sia ame kple yi le dua me; ame ɖeka hɔ̃ hã metsi agbe le eme o. Ale si Yosua wɔ Xebron kple Libna kpakple Libna-fiae la, nenemae wòwɔ Debir kple eƒe fia hãe.

english_verse: Joshua captured towns everywhere in the land: In the central hill country and the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert and the region that slopes down toward the Dead Sea. Whenever he captured a town, he would kill the king and everyone else, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
translation_verse: Ale Yosua ɖu anyigba la katã dzi. Eɖu fia siwo katã le tonyigbawo dzi, esiwo le dzogbenyigba si le anyigbeme, esiwo le gbadzaƒe siwo le toawo gɔme le ɣetoɖoƒe kple esiwo le toawo ƒe abuɖiƒewo la hã dzi. Mesusɔ ame aɖeke ɖi o; ewu wo katã keŋkeŋ, abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ ene.

english_verse: Joshua wiped out towns from Kadesh-Barnea to Gaza, everywhere in the region of Goshen, and as far north as Gibeon.
translation_verse: Ale Yosua ɖu wo dzi tso Kades-Barnea va se ɖe Gaza, eye wòxɔ Gosen-nyigbawo katã va se ɖe Gibeon.

english_verse: King Jabin of Hazor heard about Joshua's victories, so he sent messages to many nearby kings and asked them to join him in fighting Israel. He sent these messages to King Jobab of Madon, the kings of Shimron and Achshaph,
translation_verse: Esi Xazor-fia, Yabin se ale si Israelviwo le duwo dzi ɖumee la, edɔ ame ɖo ɖe Madon-fia, Yobab kple Simron-fia kpakple Axsaf-fia.

english_verse: the kings in the northern hill country and in the Jordan River valley south of Lake Galilee, and the kings in the foothills and in Naphath-Dor to the west.
translation_verse: Eɖo ame ɖe fia siwo le tonyigbawo dzi le dzigbeme, esiwo le tagba si le Kinerot le anyigbeme, esiwo le gbadzaƒe kple esiwo le bali me le ƒuta si te ɖe Dor ŋu la.

english_verse: He sent messages to the Canaanite kings in the east and the west, to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite kings in the hill country, and to the Hivite kings in the region of Mizpah, near the foot of Mount Hermon.
translation_verse: Nenema ke wòɖo ame ɖe Kanaanitɔ siwo le ɣedzeƒe kple ɣetoɖoƒe, ɖe Amoritɔwo, Xititɔwo, Perizitɔwo kple Yebusitɔwo le tonyigbawo dzi kpakple Xivitɔ siwo le Xermon-to la ƒe bali me kple esiwo le Mizpa-nyigba dzi la hã.

english_verse: The kings and their armies went to Merom Pond, where they set up camp, and got ready to fight Israel. It seemed as though there were more soldiers and horses and chariots than there are grains of sand on a beach.
translation_verse: Fia siawo katã ƒo ƒu woƒe aʋakɔwo ɖekae eye wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Merom-tɔʋu la nu be woawɔ aʋa kple Israelviwo.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua: Don't let them frighten you! I'll help you defeat them, and by this time tomorrow they will be dead. When you attack, the first thing you have to do is to cripple their horses. Then after the battle is over, burn their chariots.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Yosua be: “Mègavɔ̃ wo o. Hafi etsɔ ɣe alewo ɣi naɖo la, mawu wo katã na Israel. Miana woƒe sɔwo ƒe ata natu, eye miatɔ dzo woƒe tasiaɖamwo.”

english_verse: Joshua and his army made a surprise attack against the enemy camp at Merom Pond
translation_verse: Ale Yosua kple eƒe aʋakɔwo va ƒo ɖe wo dzi kpoyi le Merom-tɔʋu la nu, eye wokpe aʋa kpli wo.

english_verse: Up to this time, the king of Hazor had controlled the kingdoms that had joined together to attack Israel, so Joshua led his army back and captured Hazor. They killed its king
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Yosua gbugbɔ yi ɖaxɔ Xazor eye wòwu dufia la kple yi. Ɣe ma ɣi la, Xazor nye fiaɖuƒe mawo katã ƒe ta.

english_verse: and everyone else, then they set the town on fire.
translation_verse: Wowu ame sia ame le dua me, womegblẽ ame aɖeke ɖi o, eye wotɔ dzo dua.

english_verse: Joshua captured all the towns where the enemy kings had ruled. These towns were built on small hills, and Joshua did not set fire to any of these towns, except Hazor. The Israelites kept the animals and everything of value from these towns, but they killed everyone who lived in them, including their kings. That's what the Lord had told his servant Moses to do, that's what Moses had told Joshua to do, and that's exactly what Joshua did.
translation_verse: Nu si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na eƒe dɔla Mose be newɔ la, eyae Mose hã gblɔ na Yosua be newɔ, eye Yosua wɔ ɖe edzi. Ewɔ nu siwo katã Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be newɔ la pɛpɛpɛ; meɖe ɖeke le eme o. Yosua xɔ anyigba la katã

english_verse: Joshua and his army took control of the northern and southern hill country, the foothills to the west, the Southern Desert, the whole region of Goshen, and the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Ale Yosua xɔ anyigba la katã. Anyigba la tso tonyigbawo kple woƒe balimewo, Gosen-nyigba blibo la kple gbegbe gbadza si le anyigbeme nɛ, tagba la, Israel-tonyigba la kpakple wo ŋu baliwo.

english_verse: During this same time, Joshua and his army killed the Anakim from the northern and southern hill country. They also destroyed the towns where the Anakim had lived, including Hebron, Debir, and Anab.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, Yosua yi ɖatsrɔ̃ ame dzɔtsu siwo woyɔna be Anakitɔwo la le tonyigbawo dzi le Xebron, Debir, Anab kple esiwo katã le tonyigbawo dzi le Yuda kple Israel. Yosua tsrɔ̃ wo kpakple woƒe duwo keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: There were not any Anakim left in the regions where the Israelites lived, although there were still some in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
translation_verse: Anakitɔ aɖeke megasusɔ ɖe Israel-nyigba dzi o, negbe Gaza, Gat kple Asdod koe ʋɛ aɖewo ganɔ.

english_verse: That's how Joshua captured the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua divided it up among the tribes. Finally, there was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Ale Yosua xɔ anyigba la katã abe ale si tututu Aƒetɔ la gblɔe na Mose ene. Tete Yosua tsɔ anyigba la na Israelviwo abe woƒe domenyinu ene, eye wòmae na toawo katã, to ɖe sia ɖe kple etɔ. Tete anyigba la kpɔ gbɔdzɔe tso aʋawɔwɔ me.

english_verse: Before Moses died, he and the people of Israel had defeated two kings east of the Jordan River. These kings had ruled the region from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, including the eastern side of the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Israelviwo ɖu fia eve dzi, eye woxɔ woƒe anyigba le wo si. Anyigba la tso Yordan-tɔsisi la ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome to Arnon-tɔʋu nu va se ɖe Xermon-to kple gbadzaƒe si le ɣedzeƒe gome la gbɔ. Fia siwo dzi woɖu la dometɔ ɖekae nye

english_verse: The first king that Moses and the Israelites defeated was an Amorite, King Sihon of Heshbon. The southern border of his kingdom ran down the middle of the Arnon River gorge, taking in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the gorge. The Jabbok River separated Sihon's kingdom from the Ammonites on the east. Then the Jabbok turned west and became his northern border, so his kingdom included the southern half of the region of Gilead.
translation_verse: Sixon. Eyae nye Amoritɔwo ƒe fia. Enɔ Xesbon. Eƒe dziɖuƒe tso Aroer gbɔ le Arnon-tɔʋu nu to tɔʋu la ƒe go ɖeka dzi, hetsɔ Gilead ƒe afã ɖe eme va se ɖe Yabok-tɔʋu si nye Amonviwo ƒe liƒo la nu.

english_verse: Sihon also controlled the eastern side of the Jordan River valley from Lake Galilee south to Beth-Jeshimoth and the Dead Sea. In addition to these regions, he ruled the town called Slopes of Mount Pisgah and the land south of there at the foot of the hill.
translation_verse: Eƒe dziɖuƒe la gatso gbadzaƒe la yi Kinerot-ƒu nu le ɣedzeƒe, eye wòva Dzeƒu si le tagba nu le ɣedzeƒe, ɖo ta Bet-Yesimot va se ɖe Pisga-to ƒe aga nu le anyigbeme.

english_verse: His kingdom stretched north to Mount Hermon, east to the town of Salecah, and included the land of Bashan as far west as the borders of the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. He also ruled the northern half of Gilead.
translation_verse: Eƒe dziɖuƒee nye Xermon-to, Salxa kple Basan blibo la, eye wòkeke va se ɖe keke Gesuritɔwo kple Maaxatitɔwo ƒe liƒo ŋu ke. Gilead ƒe afã kple Sixon, Xesbon-fia ƒe anyigba hã le eme.

english_verse: Moses, the Lord's servant, had led the people of Israel in defeating Sihon and Og. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
translation_verse: Mose kple Israelviwo ɖu fia eve siawo dzi, eye Mose, Mawu ƒe dɔla tsɔ woƒe anyigbawo na Ruben kple Gad viwo kpakple Manase ƒe to afã wozu wo tɔ. Fia siwo dzi Yosua ɖu la ŋkɔwo

english_verse: Many years later, the Lord told Joshua: Now you are very old, but there is still a lot of land that Israel has not yet taken.
translation_verse: Yosua tsi eye wòxɔ ƒè geɖee. Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Fifia la ètsi, eye nèxɔ ƒè geɖee, evɔ la anyigba gasusɔ fũu si wòle be woaxɔ.

english_verse: Moses had already given land east of the Jordan River to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ruben-to kple Gad-to kpakple Manase-to afã ya la, Mose, Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla la tsɔ woƒe anyigbawo na wo xoxo. Anyigba sia le Yordan-tɔsisi la godo le ɣedzeƒe kpa dzi.

english_verse: This region stretched north from the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, and included the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley. It covered the flatlands of Medeba north of Dibon,
translation_verse: Woƒe anyigba la tso Aroer si le Arnon-tɔʋu la to kple du si le balia titina la gbɔ helɔ Medeba-tonyigba gbadza la katã ɖe eme va se ɖe Dibon.

english_verse: and took in the towns that had belonged to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon. Some of these towns were as far east as the Ammonite border.
translation_verse: Anyigba la se ɖe keke Amonviwo ƒe liƒo dzi ke, eye wòtsɔ du siwo katã dzi Sixon, Amori-fia si nɔ Xesbon, ɖu la ɖe eme.

english_verse: However, the Israelites did not force the people of Geshur and Maacah to leave, and they still live there among the Israelites. Why Moses Did Not Give Land to the Levi Tribe
translation_verse: Ke Israelviwo menyà Gesuritɔwo kple Maaxatitɔwo ya ɖa o. Woawo gale Israel-nyigba dzi va se ɖe egbe.

english_verse: Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.” The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
translation_verse: Mose mena anyigba aɖeke Levi viwo ya o, elabe Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be, ne dukɔ la me nu sa vɔe na ye Israel Mawu la la, wonena vɔsanumeme la ƒe ɖe Levi viwo abe woƒe domenyinu ene. Anyigba si woka na Ruben-to la

english_verse: Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Mose ka anyigba na Ruben viwo abe woƒe domenyinu ene, ƒome ɖe sia ɖe kple etɔ.

english_verse: Their land started in the south at the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, took in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley, and went as far north as the flatlands around Medeba.
translation_verse: Woƒe anyigba la tso Aroer si le Arnon-bali la, to kple du si le balia titina kple tonyigba gbadza si ƒo xlã Medeba la katã.

english_verse: The Amorite King Sihon had lived in Heshbon and had ruled the towns in the flatlands. Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth. Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
translation_verse: Anyigba la gatsɔ du siwo katã le tonyigba gbadza la dzi kple Amoritɔwo ƒe fia Sixon, ame si ɖu dzi le Xesbon la ƒe fiaɖuƒe ɖe eme. Fia atɔ̃ aɖewo, siwo ŋkɔwo nye Evi, Rekem, Zur, Xur kple Reba la ɖu anyigba sia ƒe akpa aɖewo dzi na fia Sixon. Gake Mose ɖu fia Sixon kple fia bubu siawo katã dzi hexɔ woƒe anyigba.

english_verse: The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
translation_verse: Ame siwo Israelviwo wu la dometɔ ɖeka nye bokɔ. Eŋkɔe nye Bileam, eye wònye Beor vi.

english_verse: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
translation_verse: Ale Yordan-tɔsisi la do liƒo na Ruben viwo le ɣetoɖoƒe gome. Wotsɔ du kple kɔƒe siawo na Ruben viwo, ƒome ɖe sia ɖe kple etɔ abe woƒe domenyinu ene. Anyigba si woka na Gad-to la

english_verse: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Mose ka anyigba na Gad viwo hã, ƒome ɖe sia ɖe kple etɔ.

english_verse: It included the town of Jazer, and in the Gilead region their territory took in the land and towns as far east as the town of Aroer just west of Rabbah. This was about half of the land that had once belonged to the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Woƒe anyigba la tsɔ Yazer kple Gilead duwo katã, Amonviwo ƒe anyigba afã va se ɖe Aroer si le Raba ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome la ɖe eme.

english_verse: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
translation_verse: Anyigba la gatso Xesbon va se ɖe Ramat-Mizpa kple Betonim, eye wògatso Maxanaim va se ɖe Lo-Debar ƒe liƒo dzi.

english_verse: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
translation_verse: Du siwo nye wo tɔ le Yordan-balia me la woe nye: Bet-Haram, Bet-Nimra, Sukot kple Zafon. Wonye Xesbon-fia, Sixon, ƒe fiaɖuƒe ƒe akpa si susɔ la. Yordan-tɔsisi lae nye woƒe liƒo le ɣetoɖoƒe gome. Anyigba la yi ɖase ɖe Kinerot-ta nu le dzigbeme ke.

english_verse: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
translation_verse: Wotsɔ du kple kɔƒe siawo na Gad viwo, ƒome ɖe sia ɖe kple etɔ, abe woƒe domenyinu ene. Anyigba si woka na Manase-to afã le ɣedzeƒe gome

english_verse: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Mose ka anyigba la ƒe akpa aɖe na Manase-to afã, eye ƒome ɖe sia ɖe si le to afã ma me la xɔ etɔ.

english_verse: Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had
translation_verse: Nenema ke Gilead-nyigba ƒe afã, Astarot kple Edrei, siwo nye duwo le Basan-fia, Og ƒe dziɖuƒe me la hã le eme. Wotsɔ anyigba sia na ƒome siwo nye Manase vi, Maxir ƒe dzidzimeviwo la ƒe afã abe woƒe ƒomea tɔ ene.

english_verse: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
translation_verse: Ke Mose meka anyigba aɖeke na Levi viwo ƒe to la ya o, elabe Aƒetɔ gblɔ be ne dukɔ la me nu sa vɔe na ye la, vɔsanu la ƒe akpa aɖe nanye Levi viwo tɔ.

english_verse: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la, Yuda vi aɖewo tso Yuda-to la me va Yosua gbɔ le Gilgal. Kaleb, Yefune vi, si nye Kenizitɔ la hã le wo dome. Eya gblɔ na Yosua be: “Ènya nya si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose, Mawu ƒe ame la, le nye kpli wò ŋuti le Kades-Barnea.

english_verse: The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God.
translation_verse: Ke nɔvinye siwo de kplim la va ɖe dzi le dukɔ la ƒo gake nye ya meɖo dzi ɖe Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu la ŋu bliboe.

english_verse: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
translation_verse: Tete Mose do ŋugbe nam gbe ma gbe gblɔ be: ‘Anyigba si dzi nède la, anye wò kple viwòwo ƒe domenyinu tegbee, elabe èɖo dzi ɖe Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu la ŋu bliboe.’

english_verse: I'm just as strong today as I was then, and I can still fight as well in battle.
translation_verse: Ŋusẽ gale ŋunye egbe abe ale si wònɔ ŋunye esime Mose dɔm ene. Mele te, agate ŋu awɔ aʋa, ate ŋu awɔ nu sia nu gɔ̃ hã abe tsã ene.

english_verse: So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, tsɔ tonyigba sia, si ŋugbe Aƒetɔ do nam gbe ma gbe la nam. Wò ŋutɔ èsee le mía nu gbe ma gbe be ame dzɔtsu siwo woyɔna be Anakitɔwo la le du lolo triakɔwo me le afi ma. Ðewohĩ Aƒetɔ anɔ kplim be manyà wo ɖa abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ ene.”

english_verse: Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants.
translation_verse: Tete Yosua bia yayra na Kaleb, Yefune vi la, eye wòtsɔ Xebron-du nɛ abe eƒe domenyinu ene.

english_verse: And Hebron still belongs to Caleb's descendants, because he was faithful to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ale Xebron va zu Yefune Kenizitɔ vi, Kaleb tɔ va se ɖe egbe, le ale si wòwɔ Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu la ƒe gbe dzi tututu la ta.

english_verse: Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim. There was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Tsã la, woyɔa Xebron be Arba ƒe du. Arba nye ame si xɔ ŋkɔ wu le Anakimtɔwo dome. Tete anyigba la kpɔ gbɔdzɔe tso aʋawɔwɔ me.

english_verse: Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Anyigbemeliƒo sia to Dzeƒu la ƒe mlɔenu tso adɔ̃ si dze ŋgɔ anyigbeme lɔƒo la gbɔ, eye

english_verse: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
translation_verse: wòɖo ta anyime tso Akrabim-to la gbɔ va ɖo Zin. Emlo to Kades-Barnea ƒe anyigbeme to Xezron ŋu, fɔ dzi va ɖo Adar eye wòglɔ̃ mɔ ɖo ta Karka.

english_verse: and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
translation_verse: Eyi edzi va ɖo Azmon eye wòzɔ Egipte-tɔʋu la ŋu va wu nu ɖe Domeƒu la nu. Yuda-to la ƒe anyigba la ƒe anyigbemeliƒo lae nye esi.

english_verse: Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea. The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ɣedzeƒeliƒo lae nye Dzeƒu la va se ɖe afi si Yordan-tɔsisi la de nu ƒu la me le. Dzigbemeliƒo la dze egɔme tso afi si Yordan-tɔsisi la ge ɖe Dzeƒu me le.

english_verse: From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Liƒo la zɔ yi dzi va ɖo Bet-Xogla, eye wòto Bet-Araba ƒe dzigbeme. Azɔ eyi ŋgɔ va ɖo Bohan, Ruben viŋutsu ƒe kpe la gbɔ.

english_verse: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
translation_verse: Liƒo la zɔ to Axor-bali la me va se ɖe Debir, eye wòtrɔ to Gilgal si le Adumim-todzimɔ kasa la ƒe dzigbeme le tɔʋu la ƒe anyigbeme gome. Emegbe eva to En-Semes-tɔʋu la ŋu va ke ɖe Rogel ƒe vudo la gbɔ.

english_verse: and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites. Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Liƒo la to Hinom vi ƒe bali la me va to Yebusitɔwo ƒe to la ŋu le anyigbeme afi si Yerusalem le la. Eyome liƒo la to to si le Hinom-bali la nu le ɣetoɖoƒe gome la tame le Refaim-bali la ƒe mlɔenu le dzigbeme.

english_verse: At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
translation_verse: Tso to sia tame la, liƒo la va to Neftoax ƒe vudo la gbɔ heɖo ta du siwo le Efran-to dzi la gbɔ va se ɖe Baala alo Kiryat-Yearim.

english_verse: From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah.
translation_verse: Etrɔ tso Baala ɖo ta Seir-to la gbɔ le ɣetoɖoƒe va zɔ Yearim-to la alo Kesalon ŋu le dzigbeme, eye wòmlo to Bet-Semes va se ɖe Timna.

english_verse: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Emegbe la, eho aʋa ɖe Debirtɔwo ŋu. Tsã la, woyɔa Debir be Kiryat-Sefer.

english_verse: Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
translation_verse: Yosua tsɔ Yuda viwo ƒe anyigba la ƒe akpa aɖe na Yefune vi, Kaleb, abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ ene. Xebron si nye Anakitɔwo tɔ́, Arba, ƒe du lae wòtsɔ nɛ.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
translation_verse: Anak viŋutsu etɔ̃ siwo nye Sesai, Aximan kple Talmai ƒe dzidzimeviwo la le du sia me. Kaleb nyà wo katã ɖa le dua me.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Kaleb do ŋugbe be: “Ame si ke aɖu Kiryat-Sefer dzi ahaxɔe la, matsɔ vinye nyɔnu Axsa nɛ wòaɖe.”

english_verse: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, and Caleb let him marry Achsah.
translation_verse: Tete Otniel, Kaleb nɔvi Kenaz viŋutsu xɔ dua, ale Kaleb tsɔ via nyɔnu Axsa nɛ wòɖe.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Le srɔ̃ɖegbea la, Axsa ƒoe ɖe srɔ̃a Otniel nu be wòabia ye tɔ́a ne wòana anyigbae. Esi Axsa ɖi le eƒe tedzi dzi la, tɔ́a Kaleb biae be: “Nane hiã wòa?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond. Towns in Judah's Land
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Nyo dɔme nam. Anyigba si nènam la nye dzogbe; tsiteƒe aɖeke meli o. Eya ta medi be nàna tsivudo aɖewo hãm.” Ale Kaleb tsɔ tsivudo siwo le to dzi kple bali me la na Axsa. Du siwo Yosua tsɔ na Yuda-to la

english_verse: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
translation_verse: Anyigba si Yosua tsɔ na Yuda-to la ɖe woƒe ƒomeawo nu abe domenyinu na wo ene la woe nye esi:

english_verse: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
translation_verse: Lebaot, Silxim, Ain kple Rimon. Du siawo kple woƒe kɔƒewo le bla eve vɔ asieke.

english_verse: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: Saarayim, Aditayim, Gedera kple Gederotayim. Wole du wui ene hekpe ɖe woƒe kɔƒewo ŋu.

english_verse: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: Gederot, Bet-Dagon, Naama kple Makeda. Du siawo le wui ade hekpe ɖe woƒe kɔƒewo ŋu.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_verse: Ke Yuda viwo mete ŋu nyà Yebusitɔ siwo le Yerusalem la ɖa o. Ale Yebusitɔwo tsi Yerusalem, eye wogale Yuda viwo dome va se ɖe egbe.

english_verse: The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon
translation_verse: Anyigba si Efrayim viwo xɔ ɖe woƒe ƒomeawo nu lae nye esi: Eƒe ɣedzeƒeliƒo tso Aterot-Adar va se ɖe Bet-Xoron ƒe dzigbeme,

english_verse: Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ke Efrayim viwo menyà Kanaanitɔ siwo le Gezer la ɖa le woƒe anyigba dzi o, eya ta Kanaanitɔwo tsi Efrayim viwo dome va se ɖe egbe. Ke wonana wowɔa dɔ na wo abe woƒe kluviwo ene.

english_verse: The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
translation_verse: Tapuax-nyigba nye Manase tɔ, ke Tapuax-du si le Manase ƒe liƒo dzi la nye Efrayim ƒe dzidzimeviwo tɔ.

english_verse: Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands: Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
translation_verse: Le Isaxar kple Aser nyigbawo dzi la, du aɖewo kple wo ŋu duwo li siwo nye Manase tɔ. Woawoe nye Bet-Sean, Yibleam, Dor, esi le ƒugo ŋu, En-Dor, Tanax, Megido kple du siwo ƒo xlã wo.

english_verse: But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be du siawo nye Manase tɔ hã la, womete ŋu xɔ wo le Kanaanitɔ siwo le wo me la si o. Kanaanitɔawo tsi wo me ɖikaa.

english_verse: When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave. Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
translation_verse: Emegbe esi ŋusẽ va ɖo Israelviwo ŋu la, wozi duawo me nɔlawo dzi be woawɔ dɔ na yewo abe kluviwo ene, eye womenyà wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ɖa o. Efrayim-to la kple Manase-to si le ɣetoɖoƒe gome la bia Yosua be wòagana anyigba yewo

english_verse: One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
translation_verse: Tete Yosef ƒe dzidzimeviwo gblɔ na Yosua be: “Ale ke wɔ nèna anyigba la ƒe memama teƒe ɖeka pɛ ko mí be wòanye mía tɔ? Evɔ la, tso ɣe aɖe ɣi va se ɖe fifia la, Aƒetɔ yra mí, eye míedzi sɔ gbɔ ŋutɔ.”

english_verse: Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
translation_verse: Yosua ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Nenye be miesɔ gbɔ, eye miexaxa le tonyigba si le Efrayim la dzi la, ekema miyi ɖaƒo ave siwo le Perizitɔwo kple Refaimtɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi kpe ɖe miaƒe anyigba la ŋu.”

english_verse: “Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Tonyigba la made mía nu o. Gawu la, gatasiaɖamwo le Kanaanitɔ siwo katã le gbadzaƒe la kple esiwo le Bet-Sean kple eƒe duwo me kpakple esiwo le Yezreel-bali me la, si.”

english_verse: so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_verse: Tonyigba la anye mia tɔ. Togbɔ be teƒea nye ave hã la, miƒoe va se ɖe keke eƒe mlɔenu ke ale be teƒea katã nazu mia tɔ. Le Kanaanitɔwo gome la, togbɔ be gatasiaɖamwo le wo si, eye wonye ame sesẽwo hã la, miele wo nyà ge ɖa le afi ma.”

english_verse: After Israel had captured the land, they met at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Esi Israelviwo ɖu anyigba la dzi vɔ keŋ la, woƒe ha blibo la katã va kpe ta ɖe Silo eye wotu agbadɔ si me woasubɔ Mawu le la ɖe afi ma.

english_verse: Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
translation_verse: Ale ŋutsuawo dzo yi. Hafi woadzo la, Yosua gblɔ na wo be woata anyigba la ɖe agbalẽ dzi. Egblɔ na wo be: “Miyi ɖatsa le anyigba la katã dzi. Mitae ɖe agbalẽ dzi eye miagbugbɔ ava. Emegbe madzidze nu ɖe edzi na mi le Silo afii le Aƒetɔ ŋkume.”

english_verse: The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Ale ŋutsuawo yi ɖatsa le anyigba la katã dzi. Woɖɔ ale si womae ɖe akpa adrẽ me ɖe woƒe duwo nu la ɖe agbalẽ me. Azɔ wogbugbɔ va Yosua gbɔ le asaɖa la me le Silo.

english_verse: Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided. Benjamin's Land
translation_verse: Tete Yosua dzidze nu ɖe anyigba la dzi na wo le Aƒetɔ ŋkume le Silo, eye wòmae na Israel-to siwo susɔ la, ɖe sia ɖe kple etɔ. Anyigba si woka na Benyamin viwo ƒe to la

english_verse: Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north.
translation_verse: Anyigba la ƒe memama akpa gbãtɔ ƒe nudzidze dze Benyamin viwo ƒe to la dzi ɖe woƒe ƒomeawo nu. Woƒe anyigba la le Yuda-to la kple Yosef-to la dome.

english_verse: Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert.
translation_verse: Woƒe dzigbeliƒo tso Yordan-tɔsisi la nu eye wòyi dzi to Yerixo-to la ƒe dzigbeme, va zɔ toawo dzi le ɣetoɖoƒe gome heva wu nu ɖe Bet-Aven gbedadaƒo.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town. These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Le ɣetoɖoƒe gome la, liƒo la trɔ ɖo ta anyigbeme tso to siwo le Bet-Xoron kasa ƒe anyigbeme heva wu nu ɖe Kiryat-Baal alo Kiryat-Yearim si nye Yuda viwo ƒe du la.

english_verse: Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring.
translation_verse: Anyigbemeliƒo la dze egɔme tso Kiryat-Yearim godo, ɖo ta ɣetoɖoƒe gome, va se Neftoax ƒe tsivudo gbɔ.

english_verse: From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
translation_verse: Liƒo la trɔ zɔ va to, si le Efrayim-tagba ƒe dzigbeme le Hinom vi ƒe bali la kasa la ƒe mlɔenu, eye wòzɔ Hinom-bali la me heto Yebusitɔwo ƒe to la ŋu va se ɖe Rogel ƒe vudo la gbɔ.

english_verse: At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Azɔ liƒo la trɔ ɖo ta dzigbeme va to En-Semes, hezɔ Gelilot ŋu le Adumim-todzimɔ la kasa, eye wòva to Bohan, Ruben vi la, ƒe kpe la gbɔ.

english_verse: The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Eyi edzi zɔ to la ŋu le gbadzaƒe la ƒe dzigbeme va se ɖe Araba.

english_verse: Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Tso afi sia la, eto Bet-Xogla-to la ŋu le dzigbeme heva wu nu ɖe adɔ̃ la nu le Dzeƒu la ƒe dzigbeme le Yordan-tɔsisi la ƒe anyigbeme ƒe mlɔenu ke.

english_verse: The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border. These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
translation_verse: Yordan-tɔsisi lae nye liƒo le ɣedzeƒe gome. Liƒo siawoe ƒo xlã Benyamin viwo ƒe anyigba godoo va kpe le woƒe ƒomeawo nu.

english_verse: Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders.
translation_verse: Nudzidze evelia dze Simeon viwo ƒe to dzi, le woƒe ƒomeawo nu. Woƒe anyigba la ge ɖe Yuda viwo ƒe anyigba me.

english_verse: In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following
translation_verse: Bet-Lebaot kple Saruxen. Wole du wui ene hekpe ɖe woƒe kɔƒewo ŋu.

english_verse: and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah
translation_verse: Esi wòtso le afi sia la, eɖo ta ɣedzeƒe gome va to Gat-Xefer kple Et-Kazin hemlo to Rimon va ke ɖe Nea.

english_verse: In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages: Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
translation_verse: Du bubuwo hã nye Ayin Rimon, Eter kple Asan. Wole du ene kple woƒe kɔƒewo.

english_verse: Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
translation_verse: Kɔƒe siwo katã le du siawo gbɔ va se ɖe Baalat-Beer alo Ramat le anyigbeme la hã le eme. Esiae nye anyigba si Simeon viwo ƒe to la xɔ le woƒe ƒomeawo nu abe woƒe domenyinu ene.

english_verse: Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon. Zebulun's Land
translation_verse: Anyigba si Yuda viwo ƒe to la xɔ la lolo na wo akpa eya ta woka ɖe le eŋu tsɔ na Simeon viwo ƒe to la, be wòanye woƒe domenyinu. Anyigba si woka na Zebulon viwo ƒe to la

english_verse: and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
translation_verse: Le dzigbeme la, liƒo la glɔ̃ mɔ ɖo ta megbe va do ɖe Xanaton va wu nu ɖe Yiftax-El-bali me.

english_verse: Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Woƒe duwoe nye: Katat, Nahalal, Simron, Yidala kple Betlehem. Wole du wui eve hekpe ɖe woƒe kɔƒewo ŋu.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh. Asher's Land
translation_verse: Esiae nye anyigba si Zebulon viwo xɔ hekpe ɖe woƒe duwo kple kɔƒewo ŋu, le woƒe ƒomeawo nu. Anyigba si woka na Isaxar viwo ƒe to la

english_verse: Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following
translation_verse: Esiae nye anyigba si Isaxar viwo xɔ hekpe ɖe woƒe duwo kple kɔƒewo ŋu, le woƒe ƒomeawo nu abe woƒe domenyinu ene. Anyigba si woka na Aser viwo ƒe to la

english_verse: then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel,
translation_verse: Azɔ etrɔ ɖo ta ɣedzeƒe gome va ke ɖe Bet-Dagon, eye wòzɔ to Zebulon kple Yiftax-El-bali la ƒe dzigbeme lɔƒo va ɖo Bet-Emek kple Negiel. Eyi ŋgɔ to dzigbeme va ɖo Kabul,

english_verse: Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon.
translation_verse: Ebron, Rexob, Xamon kple Kana va se ɖe Sidon, du xɔŋkɔ la, gbɔ.

english_verse: Then it turned west to become the northern border and went to Ramah and the fortress-city of Tyre. Near Tyre it turned toward Hosah and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. Asher had a total of
translation_verse: Esiae nye anyigba si Aser viwo ƒe to la xɔ hekpe ɖe woƒe duwo kple kɔƒewo ŋu, le woƒe ƒomeawo nu abe woƒe domenyinu ene. Anyigba si woka na Naftali viwo ƒe to la

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages, including Mahalab, Achzib, Acco, Aphek, and Rehob. Naphtali's Land
translation_verse: Liƒo la va ke ɖe Tabor, Saxazima kple Bet-Semes ŋu, eye wòva wu nu ɖe Yordan-tɔsisi la nu. Wole du wui ade hekpe ɖe woƒe kɔƒewo ŋu.

english_verse: Its clans received this land and these towns with their surrounding villages. Later, when enemies forced them to leave their tribal land, they went to the town of Leshem. They attacked the town, captured it, and killed the people who lived there. Then they settled there themselves and renamed the town Dan after their ancestor. Joshua's Land
translation_verse: Esiae nye anyigba si Dan viwo ƒe to la xɔ hekpe ɖe woƒe duwo kple kɔƒewo ŋu, le woƒe ƒomeawo nu abe woƒe domenyinu ene. Anyigba si Israelviwo tsɔ na Yosua

english_verse: The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
translation_verse: Anyigba siae nunɔla Eleazar kple Yosua, Nun vi kpakple Israelviwo ƒe ƒomemetsitsiwo ma eye wodzidze nu ɖe wo dzi le Silo le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Wowɔ esia le godoƒegbadɔ ƒe mɔnu. Ale wowu anyigba si le Yordan-tɔsisi la ƒe ɣetoɖoƒe gome la mama nu.

english_verse: These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_verse: Du siawoe woɖo ɖi na Israelviwo katã kple amedzro siwo katã le wo dome la. Amewula si meɖo amewuwu hafi wu ame o la, ate ŋu así ayi du siawo dometɔ aɖe me, ale be hlɔ̃biala aɖeke nagawui o, va se ɖe esime wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnui le ameha la ŋkume.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Joshua:
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Yosua be: “Gblɔ na Israelviwo be:

english_verse: When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns.
translation_verse: ‘Mitia sitsoƒedu siwo ŋu meƒo nu le na mi va yi to Mose dzi la.

english_verse: If a person accidentally kills someone and the victim's relatives say it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of the Safe Towns and be safe from the victim's relatives. The one needing protection will stand at the entrance to the town gate and explain to the town leaders what happened. Then the leaders will bring that person in and provide a place to live in their town.
translation_verse: Ne amewula la sí yina du siawo dometɔ aɖe me, eye wòɖo eƒe agbo nu la, ele be wòatɔ ɖe afi ma. Aɖe eɖokui nu na dumegãwo woase. Emegbe woaxɔe ɖe dua me, eye woana teƒee wòanɔ wo gbɔ.

english_verse: One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies.
translation_verse: Nenye be hlɔ̃biala la ti eyome va afi ma la, dua me tɔwo megaɖe asi le eŋu nɛ o, elabe eya kple ame si wòwu la, womele ke me hafi wòwui o.

english_verse: The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder. Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
translation_verse: Amewula sia anɔ dua me va se ɖe esime woakplɔe va ameha la ŋkume, eye woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnui. Gawu la, ele be wòanɔ anyi va se ɖe esime nunɔlagã si li hafi wòva la laku. Ekema ekpɔ mɔ azɔ ate ŋu agbugbɔ ayi du si me wòsí tso va la me, eye wòaganɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe aƒeme.’ ”

english_verse: The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns: Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
translation_verse: Ale, le Yordan-tɔsisi la ƒe ɣetoɖoƒe gome la, wotɔ asi du siwo gbɔna la dzi: Kedes, le Galilea le Naftali-nyigba la dzi; Sixem, le Efrayim-tonyigba dzi kple Kiryat-Arba, si wogayɔna be Xebron le Yuda-tonyigba dzi.

english_verse: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
translation_verse: Le Yordan-tɔsisi la ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome le Yerixo ƒe ɣedzeƒe lɔƒo la, wotɔ asi du siwo gbɔna la dzi: Bezer, si le gbedadaƒo kple tonyigba gbadza dzi la le Ruben-to la me, Ramot, le Gilead le Gad-to la me kple Golan, le Basan le Manase-to la me.

english_verse: While the Israelites were still camped at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, the family leaders of the Levi tribe went to speak to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders of the other Israelite tribes. The leaders of Levi said, “The Lord told Moses that you have to give us towns and provide pastures for our animals.”
translation_verse: le Silo le Kanaan-nyigba dzi. Wogblɔ na wo le afi ma be: “Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Mose be wòana duwo mí míanɔ wo me eye lãnyiƒewo nakpe ɖe wo ŋu na míaƒe lãhawo.”

english_verse: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo wɔ nu si Aƒetɔ di be wonewɔ: wotsɔ woƒe du aɖewo kple wo ŋu nyigbawo na Levitɔwo.

english_verse: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
translation_verse: Ðe wodzidze nu hafi ƒome ɖe sia ɖe xɔ eƒe du. Kehat ƒome si tso nunɔla Aron ƒe dzidzimeviwo dome lae xɔ eƒe duwo gbã. Exɔ du wui ene tso Yuda, Simeon kple Benyamin towo me.

english_verse: towns from the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and West Manasseh.
translation_verse: Kehat ƒome si tso Aron ƒe dzidzimeviwo dome, elabe woawo dzie nudzidze la dze gbã. Duawoe nye:

english_verse: towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Ke wotsɔ agbledeƒe siwo le dua gbɔ kple dua ƒe kɔƒewo na Kaleb, Yefune vi, xoxo wozu etɔ.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did. Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
translation_verse: Ale wɔ Israelviwo dzidze nu eye to ewɔwɔ me la, wotsɔ du siwo woyɔ va yi kple esiwo gbɔna la kple wo ŋu nyigbawo na Levitɔwo, abe ale si Aƒetɔ di tso wo si to Mose dzi ene.

english_verse: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
translation_verse: Du siwo katã wotsɔ na nunɔla Aron ƒe dzidzimeviwo la le du wui ene hekpe ɖe wo ŋu lãnyiƒewo ŋu.

english_verse: The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received
translation_verse: Ale Gerson viwo ƒe ƒomeawo ƒe duwo hekpe ɖe wo ŋu lãnyiƒewo katã ŋu va le du wui ene.

english_verse: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ tsɔ anyigba si wòka atam be yele tsɔtsɔ ge ana Israelviwo tɔgbuiwo la katã na Israel-dukɔ la. Esi woxɔ anyigba la le edzinɔlawo si vɔ keŋ la, wotso aƒewo ɖe edzi eye wonɔ afi ma.

english_verse: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ na woƒe dzi dze eme le anyigba blibo la dzi, abe ale si wòdo ŋugbe na wo tɔgbuiwo ene. Woƒe futɔwo dometɔ ɖeka hɔ̃ hã mete ŋu nɔ te ɖe wo nu kpɔ o, elabe Aƒetɔ na woɖu wo katã dzi.

english_verse: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_verse: Nu nyui siwo katã ŋugbe Aƒetɔ do na Israel-dukɔa la su wo si keŋ; ɖeke mesusɔ o.

english_verse: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
translation_verse: Tete Yosua yɔ Ruben kple Gad towo me tɔwo kpakple Manase-to afã ɣedzeƒetɔ la me tɔwo ƒo ƒu.

english_verse: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
translation_verse: Le ɣeyiɣi siwo katã va yi me va se ɖe egbe la, miegblẽ mia nɔviwo ɖi kpɔ o; mieɖɔ ŋu ɖo hewɔ Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la ƒe gbe dzi.

english_verse: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la, abe ale si Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la do ŋugbee ene la, ena mia nɔviwo ƒe dzi dze eme. Eya ta fifia la, migbugbɔ yi mia nɔƒe le anyigba si Mose, Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla la na mi le ɣedzeƒe gome le Yordan-tɔsisi la godo la dzi.

english_verse: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
translation_verse: Ke mikpɔ egbɔ be yewolé ɖoɖo kple se siwo katã Mose, Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla gblɔ na mi la me ɖe asi. Ebe milɔ̃ Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la, miwɔ eƒe lɔlɔ̃nu le nuwo katã me, miwɔ eƒe ɖoɖowo dzi, miwɔ nuteƒe nɛ ɖaa, eye misubɔe tso dzi blibo kple luʋɔ blibo me.”

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
translation_verse: Tete wogblɔ na wo nɔvi Israelvi bubuawo be: “Mía tɔwo! Ruben viwo kple Gad viwo kpakple Manase viwo ƒe to afã va ɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe Yordan-tɔsisi to le míaƒe akpa dzi.”

english_verse: the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Esi Israelviwo se nya sia la, wo katã wova kpe ta ɖe Silo be yewoaho aʋa ɖe to siwo le ɣedzeƒe gome la ŋu.

english_verse: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Tete Israelviwo dɔ Pinehas, nunɔla Eleazar vi, ɖo ɖe Ruben viwo kple Gad viwo kpakple Manase-to afã ɣedzeƒetɔ si le Gilead-nyigba dzi la gbɔ.

english_verse: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
translation_verse: Woɖe ame ŋkuta ewo hã kpe ɖe Pinehas ŋu. Ame siawo tso toawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe me, eye wonye ƒometatɔwo le ƒomeawo me.

english_verse: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
translation_verse: Wova Ruben viwo kple Gad viwo kpakple Manase-to afã ɣedzeƒetɔ la gbɔ le Gilead-nyigba dzi, eye wogblɔ na wo be:

english_verse: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
translation_verse: “Ale ke wɔ miedze aglã ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu, ɖi vɔsamlekpui na mia ɖokui hetrɔ le eyome egbe? Nu ka ta miewɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi sia ɖe Israel Mawu la ŋu?

english_verse: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
translation_verse: Mele be míaŋlɔ nuvɔ̃ si míewɔ le Peor la ƒe yomedzenu be o. Ðe menye dɔ vɔ̃e va ɖo Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ ƒe ameha la dome oa? Míeklɔ mía ɖokui ŋuti gɔ̃ hã vɔ o ɖe! Tohehe sia mesu mí oa?

english_verse: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
translation_verse: Ale ke wɔ miebe yewoagbugbɔ le Aƒetɔ yome azɔ? Ne miawo ɖeɖe miegbugbɔ le Aƒetɔ yome egbe la, Israel-dukɔ blibo la ŋue wòle dɔmedzoe do ge ɖo etsɔ si gbɔna.

english_verse: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la, nenye be miaƒe anyigba la ŋu mekɔ o la, ekema mitrɔ va Aƒetɔ ƒe anyigba me le afii, afi si eƒe nɔƒe la le, ne miadi anyigba ɖe mía dome. Ke ne miedze aglã ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu heɖi vɔsamlekpui bubu na mia ɖokui kpe ɖe Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la tɔ ŋu la, woabu míawo hã aglãdzelawoe akpe ɖe mia ŋu.

english_verse: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
translation_verse: Esi Axan, Serax vi la, meto nyateƒe le busunuawo ƒe nya la me o la, nu kae dzɔ? Aƒetɔ he to na Israel- dukɔ blibo la. Menye Axan ɖeɖe koe ku le nuvɔ̃ si wòwɔ la ta o, ke boŋ Israelvi bubu geɖewo hã ku, le nuvɔ̃ si eya ɖeka wɔ la ta.”

english_verse: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
translation_verse: “Mawu ŋusẽtɔ ɖeka la! Eyae nye Aƒetɔ! Ŋusẽtɔ ɖeka lae nye Mawu! Eyae nye Aƒetɔ! Eya ŋutɔ nya nu si ta míewɔ nu sia ɖo. Israel-dukɔ hã nenyae! Nenye aglãe míebe míadze alo atu nu, si míebla kple Aƒetɔ la, ekema mitsrɔ̃ mí fifi laa!

english_verse: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Nenye ɖe míeɖi vɔsamlekpui la be míagbugbɔ le Aƒetɔ yome, alo ɖe míeɖii be míanɔ numemevɔ, nuɖuɖuvɔ alo ŋutifafavɔ sam le edzi la, Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ nehe to na mí vevie.
