english_verse: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Esia tae míeɖi vɔsamlekpui la ɖo, ke menye ɖe míeɖii be míanɔ numemevɔ alo ŋutifafavɔ sam le edzi o.

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
translation_verse: Ale Pinehas, nunɔla Eleazar vi la gblɔ na wo be: “Míenya azɔ be Aƒetɔ le mía dome elabe miedze aglã ɖe eŋu o, ale miexɔ Israel-dukɔ la ɖe agbe tso Aƒetɔ si me.”

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
translation_verse: Tete Pinehas kple ame ŋkuta siwo kpe ɖe eŋu la trɔ tso Ruben viwo kple Gad viwo gbɔ le Gilead-nyigba dzi heva Israelviwo gbɔ le Kanaan-nyigba dzi, eye wogblɔ dɔgbedenya la na wo.

english_verse: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
translation_verse: Nya si wova gblɔ la dze Israelviwo ŋu eye wokafu Mawu. Ale womegadi be yewoaho aʋa ɖe Ruben viwo kple Gad viwo ŋu ahagblẽ anyigba si dzi wole la o.

english_verse: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_verse: Ruben viwo kple Gad viwo gblɔ be: “Vɔsamlekpui sia le ɖase ɖim na mí katã be Aƒetɔ nye Mawu.” Ale wona ŋkɔe be “Ðaseɖiɖi.”

english_verse: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
translation_verse: Le esiawo megbe la, Aƒetɔ na Israelviwo kpɔ gbɔdzɔe tso woƒe futɔ siwo ƒo xlã wo godoo la si me. Wonɔ anyi alea ɣeyiɣi didi aɖe. Ke Yosua va tsi zu amegãɖeɖi.

english_verse: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
translation_verse: Eya ta eyɔ Israelviwo katã, woƒe ame tsitsiwo, tatɔwo, ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo kple dzikpɔlawo eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Fifia la, metsi: mexɔ ƒè geɖee.

english_verse: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
translation_verse: Miawo ŋutɔ miekpɔ nu siwo katã Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la xa ɖe mia ta tu kple dukɔ siwo katã ƒo xlã mi la. Elabe Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la ŋutɔ xɔ aʋa ɖe sia ɖe wɔ na mi.

english_verse: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la, ana futɔawo agbugbɔ ayi megbe le mia ŋgɔ, eye wòanyà wo ɖa keŋkeŋ. Miegale wo kpɔ ge o. Ale miaxɔ woƒe anyigba abe ale si Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la do ŋugbe na mi ene.

english_verse: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
translation_verse: Eya ta minɔ te sesĩe eye milé nu siwo katã woŋlɔ ɖe Mose ƒe segbalẽa me la me ɖe asi, eye mizɔ ɖe wo nu. Migagblẽ akpa aɖeke ɖi o.

english_verse: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
translation_verse: Migatsaka kple dukɔ siwo susɔ ɖe mia dome la me tɔwo o. Migayɔ woƒe mawuwo ŋkɔ, tsɔ wo ata nui, subɔ wo alo ade ta agu na wo o.

english_verse: Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
translation_verse: Ke boŋ miku ɖe Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la ŋu abe ale si mieku ɖe eŋu va se ɖe egbe ene.

english_verse: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ nyà dukɔ gã triakɔwo ɖa le mia ŋgɔ, eye va se ɖe fifi la, ame aɖeke mete ŋu nɔ te ɖe mia nu kpɔ o.

english_verse: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Mia dome ame ɖeka te ŋu nyàa ame akpe ɖeka ɖe du nu, elabe Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu lae wɔa aʋa na mi, abe ale si wòdo ŋugbe na mii ene.

english_verse: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Eya ta milé be na mia ɖokui nyuie ne mialɔ̃ Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la.

english_verse: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
translation_verse: ekema evɔ na mi. Minya nyuie be Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la, maganyà dukɔ siawo ɖa le mia ŋgɔ azɔ o. Woazu mɔ̀ tetre ƒomevi vovovowo anɔ mia dome; woanɔ abe ameƒotie wotsɔ le axadame ƒom na mi alo ŋue ge ɖe ŋkume na mi ene. Anɔ alea va se ɖe esime miatsrɔ̃ keŋkeŋ le anyigba sia, si Aƒetɔ, Mawu la na mi la dzi.

english_verse: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
translation_verse: “Azɔ la, nye kuɣi ɖo. Mia dome ame sia ame kpɔe dze sii kɔtɛe le eƒe dzi kple luʋɔ me, be miaƒe asi su nu nyui siwo katã ŋugbe Aƒetɔ do na mi la dzi, eye mete ɖeka pɛ hã mi o.

english_verse: Yes, when the Lord makes a promise, he does what he has promised. But when he makes a threat, he will also do what he has threatened. The Lord is our God. He gave us this wonderful land and made an agreement with us that we would worship only him. But if you worship other gods, it will make the Lord furious. He will start getting rid of you, and soon not one of you will be left in this good land that he has given you.
translation_verse: Ne mietu Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la ƒe nu, si wòbla kpli mi, eye mieyi ɖasubɔ mawu bubu hede ta agu nɛ la, baba na mi! Aƒetɔ ado dɔmedzoe ɖe mia ŋu vevie, atsrɔ̃ mi alɔ tsɔtsɔe, miavɔ keŋ le anyigba si wòna mi la dzi.”

english_verse: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Tete Yosua na Israel-toawo katã va kpe ta ɖe Sixem. Eyɔ ame tsitsiwo, tatɔwo, ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo kple dzikpɔlawo wova le tsitre ɖe Mawu ŋkume.

english_verse: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
translation_verse: Tete wòƒo nu na ameha la katã gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu la be: ‘Le blema la, mia tɔgbuiwo nɔ Frat-tɔsisi godo afi si wosubɔ mawu bubu le. Mia tɔgbuiawo dometɔ ɖeka ŋkɔe nye Tarax si nye Abraham kple Naxor tɔ́.

english_verse: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
translation_verse: Tete mekplɔ mia tɔgbui Abraham tso Frat-tɔsisia godo va afii, eye mena wòtsa le Kanaan-nyigba blibo la dzi. Mena eƒe dzidzimeviwo dzi ɖe edzi. Metsɔ Isak nɛ,

english_verse: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
translation_verse: eye metsɔ Yakob kple Esau na Isak hã. Metsɔ Seir- tonyigba na Esau, ke mia tɔgbui Yakob kple viawo ya ʋu yi Egipte.

english_verse: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
translation_verse: Tete wodo ɣli yɔm. Ale mena viviti do hema mi kple Egiptetɔwo dome. Mena ƒu la ŋe gbagba ɖe Egiptetɔwo dzi, eye wotsi eme ku. Nu si metu kple Egiptetɔwo la, miawo ŋutɔ miekpɔe kple ŋku. Azɔ la, mieva nɔ gbedadaƒo ɣeyiɣi didi aɖe.

english_verse: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
translation_verse: Tete mekplɔ mi va Amoritɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi le Yordan-tɔsisi ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome. Wowɔ aʋa kpli mi, ke mena mieɖu wo dzi hexɔ woƒe anyigba le wo si, eye metsrɔ̃ wo ɖa le mia ŋgɔ.

english_verse: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
translation_verse: Azɔ Moab-fia Balak, Zipor vi, ho va wɔ aʋa kpli mi. Edɔ woyi ɖayɔ Bileam, Beor vi, vɛ be wòaƒo fi ade mi.

english_verse: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
translation_verse: Ke megbe toɖoɖo Bileam eye wòyra mi boŋ. Ale meɖe mi tso esime.

english_verse: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
translation_verse: Eyome mietso Yordan-tɔsisi la va Yerixo, eye Yerixotɔwo wɔ aʋa kpli mi. Nenema ke Amoritɔwo, Perizitɔwo, Kanaanitɔwo, Xititɔwo, Girgasitɔwo, Xivitɔwo kple Yebusitɔwo hã va wɔ aʋa kpli mi eye mena mieɖu wo katã dzi.

english_verse: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Menyà Amoritɔwo ƒe fia eveawo ɖa le mia ŋgɔ. Wotɔtɔ le du dzi abe nutéame aɖewoe kplɔ wo ɖo ene. Menye miaƒe yi alo dae ye wɔe o.

english_verse: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
translation_verse: Metsɔ anyigba si ta miekpe fu aɖeke ɖo kpɔ o la na mi. Nenema ke metsɔ du siwo mietso o la hã na mi be mianɔ wo me. Azɔ metsɔ wainbɔ kple amitibɔ siwo mietso o la na mi be miaɖu wo me kutsetsewo.”

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
translation_verse: “Eya ta azɔ la, mivɔ̃ Aƒetɔ. Mixɔ edzi se blibo eye misubɔe le nyateƒe me. Mawu si mia tɔgbuiwo subɔ le Mesopotamia kple Egipte la, miɖee ɖa le mia dome, eye misubɔ Aƒetɔ ɖeɖe ko.

english_verse: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
translation_verse: Ke ne Aƒetɔ subɔsubɔ medze mia ŋu o la, ekema mitia mawu si miedi be yewoasubɔ azɔ, egbe ɖeka. Mawu si mia tɔgbuiwo subɔ le Mesopotamia lae loo, alo mawu si Amoritɔ siwo ƒe anyigba dzi miele fifia la subɔna la yea? Ke nye kple nye aƒemetɔwo ya la, Aƒetɔ ko míasubɔ.”

english_verse: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Tete ameha la ɖo eŋu be: “Míagblẽ Aƒetɔ ɖi aɖasubɔ mawu bubua? Madzɔ akpɔ o!

english_verse: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
translation_verse: Esime míenye kluviwo le Egipte la, Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu lae kplɔ mía kple mía tɔgbuiwo tso afi mae, eye wòwɔ nukunu gãwo míekpɔ. Eyae kpɔ mía ta míenɔ dedie le míaƒe mɔzɔzɔ blibo la me le dukɔ siwo katã me míeto la me.

english_verse: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
translation_verse: Esi míegbɔna anyigba sia dzi la, Aƒetɔ nyà Amoritɔ siwo katã le anyigba la dzi la ɖa le mía ŋgɔ. Eya ta míawo hã Aƒetɔ ko míasubɔ, elabe eyae nye mía Mawu.”

english_verse: Joshua said: The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it.
translation_verse: Ke Yosua gblɔ na ameha la be: “Miate ŋu asubɔ Aƒetɔ o, elabe Mawu kɔkɔe wònye; Mawu ʋãŋue. Matsɔ miaƒe vodadawo alo miaƒe nuvɔ̃wo ake mi o.

english_verse: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be Aƒetɔ wɔ nyui na mi kpɔ va yi hã la, ne miegbe esubɔsubɔ, eye miesubɔ mawu bubu aɖe la, ekema aɖe kɔ ɖa le mia ŋu, ahe vɔ̃ ava mia dzi, eye wòatsrɔ̃ mi.”

english_verse: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ameha la gblɔ na Yosua be: “Gbeɖe! Aƒetɔ ko míasubɔ.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
translation_verse: Yosua gblɔ na wo be: “Yoo, miawo ŋutɔe nye ɖasefo na mia ɖokui be yewotia Aƒetɔ be yewoasubɔ.” Woɖo eŋu be: “Ẽ, miawo ŋutɔe nye ɖasefoa.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ na wo be: “Ekema miɖe mawu bubu siwo le mia dome la ɖa, eye mitsɔ miaƒe dzi na Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu la.”

english_verse: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
translation_verse: Tete ameha la gblɔ na Yosua be: “Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la ko míasubɔ. Eya ƒe gbe dzi ko míawɔ.”

english_verse: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
translation_verse: Ale Yosua bla nu kple dukɔ la gbe ma gbe le Sixem, eye wòwɔ sewo kple ɖoɖowo na wo.

english_verse: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
translation_verse: Yosua ŋlɔ nya siawo ɖe Mawu ƒe segbalẽ la me. Azɔ eɖi kpe gã aɖe ɖe afi ma ɖe logoti si le Aƒetɔ ƒe kɔkɔeƒea gbɔ la te.

english_verse: and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ na ameha blibo la be: “Mikpɔ ɖa, kpe sia anye míaƒe ɖasefo. Ese nya siwo katã Aƒetɔ gblɔ na mí la. Eya ta anye ɖasefo ɖe mia ŋu ale be miagasẽ nu ɖe mia Mawu la ŋu o.”

english_verse: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
translation_verse: Emegbe Yosua ɖe asi le ameha la ŋu, eye ame sia ame trɔ yi eƒe anyigba dzi. Yosua kple Eleazar ku

english_verse: Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Le ɣeyiɣi aɖewo megbe la, Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla Yosua, Nun vi la ku, esime wòxɔ ƒe alafa ɖeka kple ewo.

english_verse: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Woɖii ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi le Timnat-Serax, si le Efrayim-tonyigba dzi le Gaas-to ƒe dzigbeme.

english_verse: As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Le Yosua ƒe agbenɔɣi blibo la me la, Israelviwo subɔ Aƒetɔ. Le eƒe ku megbe hã la, woyi dzi subɔ Aƒetɔ le woƒe ame tsitsiwo ƒe kpɔkplɔ te. Ame tsitsi siawo nɔ agbe le Yosua ŋɔli eye woawo ŋutɔ kpɔ nu siwo katã Aƒetɔ wɔ na dukɔ la.

english_verse: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
translation_verse: Azɔ Israelviwo ɖi Yosef ƒe ƒu siwo wotsɔ tso Egipte vɛ la ɖe Yakob ƒe anyigba dzi le Sixem. Yakob ƒle anyigba sia le Xamor, Sixem tɔ́a viwo si klosaloga alafa ɖeka. Emegbe anyigba la va zu Yosef ƒe dzidzimeviwo ƒe domenyinu.

english_verse: When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_verse: Eleazar, Aron vi, hã va ku, eye woɖii ɖe Gibea. Wotsɔ Gibea-du sia, si le tonyigba dzi le Efrayim la na via Pinehas tsã.

english_verse: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the Lord, “Which of our tribes should attack the Canaanites first?”
translation_verse: Le Yosua ƒe ku megbe la, Israelviwo bia Aƒetɔ be: “Míaƒe toawo dometɔ kae le hoho ge aɖawɔ aʋa kple Kanaanitɔwo gbã?”

english_verse: “Judah!” the Lord answered. “I'll help them take the land.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu be: “Yuda-to la neho yi. Kpɔ ɖa, metsɔ anyigba la de asi nɛ.”

english_verse: The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.” Troops from Simeon came to help Judah.
translation_verse: Tete Yuda gblɔ na nɔvia Simeon be: “Va kplɔm yi anyigba si wotsɔ nam la dzi ne maɖawɔ aʋa kple Kanaanitɔwo. Emegbe la, nye hã makplɔ wò ayi teƒe si wotsɔ na wò la dzi aɖakpe ɖe mia ŋu.” Ale Simeon yi kplii.

english_verse: Together they attacked an army of
translation_verse: Wodo go Adoni-Bezek le afi ma, eye wowɔ aʋa kplii.

english_verse: After that, they attacked the Canaanites who lived at Hebron, defeating the three clans called Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. At that time, Hebron was called Kiriath-Arba.
translation_verse: Wozɔ ɖe Kanaanitɔ siwo le Xebron-du me la dzi. Woyɔa du sia tsã be Kiryat-Arba. Woɖu Sesai, Aximan kple Talmai dzi le afi ma. Otniel ɖu Debir-du dzi (Yos

english_verse: The king tried to escape, but soldiers from Judah caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes,
translation_verse: Esí, eye woti eyome ɖalée. Wolã eƒe asi kple afɔ degblefetsuwo katã.

english_verse: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
translation_verse: Yuda-to la me tɔwo wɔ aʋa kple Yerusalem-dua, eye woxɔe. Wowu dua me tɔwo kple yi hetɔ dzo dua.

english_verse: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.
translation_verse: Emegbe la, Yuda-to la me tɔwo yi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Kanaanitɔ siwo le tonyigba dzi, esiwo le bali me le toawo gɔme kpakple esiwo le gbegbe si le anyigbeme la.

english_verse: From Hebron, Judah's army went to attack Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Esi Yuda-to la me tɔwo tso le afi ma la, woho aʋa ɖe Debirtɔwo ŋu. Woyɔa Debir-dua tsã be Kiryat-Sefer.

english_verse: Caleb told his troops, “The man who captures Kiriath-Sepher can marry my daughter Achsah.”
translation_verse: Tete wo dometɔ ɖeka si ŋkɔe nye Kaleb la gblɔ be: “Ame si ke aɖu Debir-dua dzi ahaxɔe la, matsɔ vinye nyɔnu Axsa nɛ wòaɖe.”

english_verse: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, so Caleb let him marry Achsah. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Kaleb ƒe tsɛ ŋutsu Kenaz vi si ŋkɔe nye Otniel lae va xɔ dua. Ale Kaleb tsɔ via Axsa nɛ wòɖe.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Le srɔ̃ɖegbea la, Otniel ƒo nu kple srɔ̃a be nebia agble tɔ́a. Tete nyɔnua ɖi le tedzi si dom wònɔ la dzi. Kaleb biae be: “Nu kae hiã wò?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so please give me some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
translation_verse: Nyɔnua ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Na nanem. Esi nèdam ɖe anyigbemekegbegbe la, na tsivudo hãm. “Ale Kaleb tsɔ vudo siwo le toawo dzi kple baliawo me la nɛ. Teƒe siwo dzi Yuda kple Benyamin toawo ɖu

english_verse: The people who belonged to the Kenite clan were the descendants of the father-in-law of Moses. They left Jericho with the people of Judah and settled near Arad in the Southern Desert of Judah not far from the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Ke Mose to, Keni, ƒe dzidzimeviwo, ʋu tso Yerixo, devedu la me, yi gbedadaƒo si le Arad ƒe anyigbeme le Yuda, eye woɖanɔ dukɔ la dome.

english_verse: Judah's army helped Simeon's army attack the Canaanites who lived at Zephath. They completely destroyed the town and renamed it Hormah.
translation_verse: Yuda-to la me tɔwo ho aʋa kpe ɖe wo nɔvi Simeon-to la me tɔwo ŋu, eye woɖu Kanaanitɔ siwo nɔ Zefat la dzi. Wotsrɔ̃ ameawo keŋkeŋ, eye wona ŋkɔ dua be Xorma.

english_verse: The Lord helped the army of Judah capture Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the land near those towns. They also took the hill country. But the people who lived in the valleys had iron chariots, so Judah was not able to make them leave or to take their land.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ nɔ kple Yuda-to la, ale be wote ŋu xɔ tonyigba la, ke womete ŋu nyà ame siwo nɔ balia me la ɖa o, elabe gatasiaɖamwo nɔ wo si.

english_verse: The tribe of Judah gave the town of Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had told them to do. Caleb defeated the three Anakim clans and took over the town. The Benjamin Tribe Does Not Capture Jerusalem
translation_verse: Wotsɔ Xebron na Kaleb, abe ale si Mose gblɔ ene, eye wònyà Anak ƒe dzidzimevi etɔ̃awo ɖa le afi ma.

english_verse: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
translation_verse: Ke Benyamin-to la me tɔwo menyà Yebusitɔ siwo nɔ Yerusalem la ɖa o, ale wɔ Yebusitɔwo kple Benyamin-to la me tɔwo tsaka le Yerusalem va se ɖe egbe. Efrayim kple Manase toawo ɖu Betel-du dzi

english_verse: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
translation_verse: Tete ŋkutsalaawo kpɔ ŋutsu aɖe si do tso dua me. Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Fia mɔ si míato age ɖe dua me la mí, eye míave nuwò.”

english_verse: The man showed them, and the two Israelite tribes attacked Bethel, killing everyone except the man and his family. The two tribes made the man and his family leave,
translation_verse: Ale ŋutsua fia mɔ wo. Efrayim kple Manase toawo me tɔwo wu ame sia ame le dua me, negbe ŋutsua kple srɔ̃a kpakple viawo ko.

english_verse: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
translation_verse: Azɔ ŋutsua yi ɖatso du ɖe Xititɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, eye wòna ŋkɔe be Luz. Ŋkɔ sia tsi dua ŋu va se ɖe egbe. Ame siwo Israelviwo menyà ɖa le wo dome o.

english_verse: Canaanites lived in the towns of Beth-Shan, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and all the villages nearby. The Canaanites were determined to stay, and the Manasseh tribe never did get rid of them. But later on, when the Israelites grew more powerful, they made slaves of the Canaanites.
translation_verse: Ke esi ŋusẽ va ɖo Israelviwo ŋu la, wozia Kanaantɔ siawo dzi wowɔa dɔ na wo dzodzroe, eye womenyà wo ɖa le afi mawo o.

english_verse: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
translation_verse: Efrayim-to la me tɔwo hã menyà Kanaantɔ siwo nɔ Gezer la ɖa o, eya ta woawo hã wotsi afi ma henɔ wo dome.

english_verse: The Zebulun tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Kitron and Nahalol, and the Canaanites stayed there with Israelites around them. But the people of Zebulun did force the Canaanites into slave labor.
translation_verse: Zebulon-to la me tɔwo menyà Kitrontɔwo kple Nahaloltɔwo ɖa o, eya ta Kanaantɔwo tsi wo dome eye wozia wo dzi wowɔa dɔ na wo dzodzroe.

english_verse: The Asher tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob, and the Asher tribe lived with Canaanites all around them.
translation_verse: Esi Aser-to la me tɔwo menyà Kanaantɔ siwo nye anyigba la dzi nɔlawo ɖa o ta la, wotsi wo dome.

english_verse: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
translation_verse: Naftali-to la me tɔwo menyà Bet-Semestɔwo kple Bet-Anatetɔwo ɖa o, eya ta wonɔ Kanaantɔ siwo nye anyigba la dzi nɔlawo la dome. Ke wozia wo dzi wowɔa dɔ na wo dzodzroe.

english_verse: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
translation_verse: Amoritɔwo nyà Dan-to la me tɔwo ɖo ɖe tonyigba dzi, eye womeɖe mɔ na wo be woava gbadzaƒe si le balia me o.

english_verse: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
translation_verse: Ke Amoritɔwo ɖoe kplikpaa be yewomadzo le Ayalon, Saalbim kple Xeres towo dzi akpɔ o. Emegbe la, Efrayim kple Manase toawo me tɔwo ƒe asi va sẽ ɖe wo dzi, eye wozia wo dzi wowɔa dɔ na wo dzodzroe.

english_verse: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
translation_verse: Amoritɔwo ƒe liƒo tso Akrabim todomemɔ si le Sela gbɔ, eye wòmlo ɖe nu ɖo ta dzi.

english_verse: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla tso Gilgal va Boxim eye wògblɔ be: “Mena mieʋu tso Egipte, eye mekplɔ mi va anyigba si ŋu meka atam ɖo be mele tsɔtsɔ ge ana mia tɔgbuiwo la dzi. Megblɔ na wo be, ‘Nyematu nu, si mebla kpli mi la akpɔ gbeɖe o,

english_verse: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
translation_verse: eye migabla nu kple anyigba sia dzi tɔwo o. Migbã woƒe vɔsamlekpuiwo gudugudu.’ Gake miegbe nye gbe dzi wɔwɔ. Menye nu si tututu mebe migawɔ o lae nye esi miewɔ oa?

english_verse: And so, I'll stop helping you defeat your enemies. Instead, they will be there to trap you into worshiping their idols.
translation_verse: Eya ta nye hã mele egblɔm na mi azɔ be nyemanyà ameawo ɖa le mia ŋgɔ o, bene woanɔ mia ŋu anɔ fu ɖem na mi. Woƒe mawuwo subɔsubɔ zu mɔ̀ si wotre ɖi na mi.”

english_verse: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
translation_verse: Wona ŋkɔ teƒe ma be Boxim, eye wosa vɔ le afi ma na Aƒetɔ. Yosua ku

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Woɖii ɖe anyigba si dome wònyi la dzi le Timnat-Xeres si le Efrayim-to dzi le Gaas-to ƒe dzigbeme lɔƒo.

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Esi dzidzime ma katã ku vɔ la, dzidzime bubu va ɖe wo yome. Woawo ya womedze si Aƒetɔ o, eye womenya naneke le nu siwo katã wòwɔ na Israelviwo la ŋu o. Israelviwo dzudzɔ Aƒetɔ subɔsubɔ

english_verse: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
translation_verse: Afi sia afi si woyi la, dzɔgbevɔ̃e kplɔ wo ɖo elabe Aƒetɔ ɖe asi le wo ŋu abe ale si wòka atam na wo la ene. Ale wɔ woɖo xaxa me ŋutɔ.

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: Ke Israelviwo mese ɖelawo ƒe gbe o. Wodzo le woƒe Mawu gbɔ, eye wode ta agu na mawu bubuwo. Togbɔ be wo tɔgbuiwo zɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe mɔ dzi hewɔ eƒe seawo dzi hã la, woawo ya wotrɔ megbe de mɔ sia kaba ŋutɔ, eye womenɔ agbe nyuie abe wo tɔgbuiwo ene o.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Nenye be Aƒetɔ ɖo ɖela na wo la, enɔna kple ɖela la, eye wòxɔna na wo tso woƒe futɔwo si me le eƒe agbenɔɣi. Ne fuɖenamelawo kple ŋutasẽlawo te wo ɖi, eye wole hũɖeɖe dzi la, Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔme trɔna ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
translation_verse: Evɔ kasia ɖela la naku ko la, wotrɔna hewɔa nu tovo wu dzidzime si yome wova ɖo la tɔ. Wodzea mawu bubuwo yome, subɔa wo hedea ta agu na wo. Wogbea asiɖeɖe le woƒe nuwɔnawo ŋu, eye woƒe to gasẽna ɖe edzi wu tsã.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ do dziku ɖe Israelviwo ŋu vevie, eye wògblɔ be: “Esi dukɔ sia mese nye gbe o, eye wotu nu, si mebla kple wo tɔgbuiwo

english_verse: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
translation_verse: ta la, nye hã nyemaganyà dukɔ siwo Yosua susɔ ɖi hafi ku la ɖa le wo ŋgɔ o.

english_verse: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: Matsɔ dukɔ siawo ado Israelviwo akpɔ be woalé ŋku ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe mɔ la ŋu abe wo tɔgbuiwo ene loo, alo womalé ŋku ɖe eŋu o mahã.”

english_verse: That's why the Lord had not let Joshua get rid of those enemy nations all at once.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ na dukɔ siawo susɔ, eye menyà wo ɖa enumake loo, alo na Yosua ɖu wo dzi o.

english_verse: And the Lord had another reason for letting these enemies stay. The Israelites needed to learn how to fight in war, just as their ancestors had done. Each new generation would have to learn by fighting
translation_verse: Ewɔ esia bene yeatsɔ afia aʋawɔwɔ Israelviwo ƒe dzidzime siwo mekpɔ aʋawɔƒe kpɔ o la, ale be woawo hã nadze aʋawɔwɔ.

english_verse: the Philistines and their five rulers, as well as the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived in the Lebanon Mountains from Mount Baal-Hermon to Hamath Pass.
translation_verse: Dukɔawoe nye: Filistitɔwo ƒe amegã atɔ̃awo ƒe duwo, Kanaanitɔwo katã, Sidontɔ kple Xivitɔ siwo nɔ Lebanon-to dzi tso Baal-Xermon va se ɖe Xamat.

english_verse: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
translation_verse: Wotsi anyi bene Aƒetɔ natsɔ wo ado Israelviwo kpɔ be woawɔ yeƒe se siwo yede na wo tɔgbuiwo to Mose dzi la dzi mahã.

english_verse: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
translation_verse: Israelviwo ɖe dukɔ siawo me nyɔnuwo, eye wotsɔ woƒe nyɔnuwo na dukɔ siawo me ŋutsuwo woɖe, eye wosubɔ woƒe mawuwo. Otniel

english_verse: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
translation_verse: Israelviwo wɔ nuvɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, elabe woŋlɔ Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la be, eye woɖale Baalwo kple nyɔnumawu Aserawo subɔm.

english_verse: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ do dziku ɖe Israelviwo ŋu. Ena Mesopotamia-fia, Kusan-Risataim, ɖu wo dzi eye wonɔ ete hesubɔe ƒè enyi.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Tete Israelviwo do ɣli yɔ Aƒetɔ, eye wòdɔ ŋutsu aɖe ɖa wòva ɖe wo. Eŋkɔe nye Otniel, Kaleb yometɔ ŋutsu Kenaz, vi.

english_verse: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
translation_verse: Tete Israelviwo gawɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu. Eya ta Aƒetɔ na ŋusẽ gaɖo Moab-fia, Eglon, ŋu ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
translation_verse: Eglon ƒo ƒu Amontɔwo kple Amalekitɔwo kpe ɖe eɖokui ŋu, eye woho aʋa ɖe Israelviwo ŋu. Woɖu Israelviwo dzi, eye woxɔ Yerixo, devedu la.

english_verse: Ehud and some other Israelites took the taxes to Eglon, who was a very fat man. As soon as they gave the taxes to Eglon, Ehud said it was time to go home.
translation_verse: Esi Ehud tsɔ nunanaawo nɛ vɔ la, ekplɔ ame siwo kpe ɖe eŋu yi la ɖaɖo ɖa.

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: Enumake Ehud do miasi ɖa, eye wòhe adekpui la le eƒe ɖusikpa dzi heƒo ɖe dɔme nɛ.

english_verse: and left. When the king's officials came back and saw that the doors were locked, they said, “The king is probably inside relieving himself.”
translation_verse: Esi wòdo go dzo la, fia la ƒe subɔlawo va eye wokpɔ be xɔtaxɔe la ƒe ʋɔawo le dodo, eya ta wobu be: “Anyanɔ afɔdzi le yaxɔƒe la.

english_verse: They stood there waiting until they felt foolish, but Eglon still didn't open the doors. Finally, they unlocked the doors and found King Eglon lying dead on the floor.
translation_verse: Ke esi wolala ʋuu meʋu ʋɔa o la, wotsɔ safui va ʋu ʋɔ lae. Va kpɔ! Woƒe aƒetɔ nye esi ku ɖe anyigba!

english_verse: But by that time, Ehud had already escaped past the statues. Ehud went to the town of Seirah
translation_verse: Esime wohe ɖe megbe la, Ehud sí gbɔ kpe kpakpaawo ŋu, eye wòva do ɖe Seira.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: Egblɔ na wo be: “Mikplɔm ɖo. Aƒetɔ na míeɖu dzi! Míeɖu míaƒe futɔ, Moabtɔwo dzi!” Enumake wodze eyome, eye wova xe Yordan-tɔsisi la tsoƒemɔ na Moabtɔwo. Womena ame aɖeke tso tɔ la o.

english_verse: and before the fighting was over, they killed about
translation_verse: Wowu Moabtɔ kalẽtɔ kako abe akpe ewo sɔŋ ene; ɖeka hɔ̃ hã mesí o.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Ale Moabtɔwo ge ɖe Israelviwo si me tso ɣe ma ɣi dzi, eye anyigba la dzi fa ƒe bla enyi sɔŋ. Samgar ƒe dukpɔkplɔ

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Ðela bubu si gado lae nye Samgar, Anat vi. Eya hã ɖe Israelviwo esime wòwu Filistitɔ alafa ade kple lãkplɔti nu tsuẽ.

english_verse: After the death of Ehud, the Israelites again started disobeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Le Ehud ƒe ku megbe la, Israelviwo gawɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu.

english_verse: So the Lord let the Canaanite King Jabin of Hazor conquer Israel. Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-Ha-Goiim.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ na Kanaan-fia, Yabin ɖu wo dzi. Enɔ Xazor hafi nɔ dzi ɖum, eye eƒe aʋakplɔla, Sisera, ya nɔ Xaroset-Goyim.

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Azɔ la, egblɔ na Yael be: “Yi nàtsi tsitre ɖe agbadɔa ƒe mɔnu. Ne ame aɖe va bia wò be ame aɖe le afii hã la, ɖo eŋu nɛ be o.”

english_verse: Deborah the wife of Lappidoth was a prophet and a leader of Israel during those days.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, nyɔnu mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela, Debora, si nye Lapidot srɔ̃ la nye ɖela nɔ Israel-dukɔ me.

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: Ebɔbɔ nɔa anyi ɖe deti aɖe te le Rama kple Betel dome le Efrayim-to dzi, eye Israelviwo yia egbɔ wòdrɔ̃a ʋɔnu na wo.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: Edɔ ame woyi ɖayɔ Barak, Abinoam vi, tso Kedes-Naftali vɛ. Egblɔ nɛ be: “Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu la be woagblɔ na wò be, ‘Tso nàɖe ame akpe ewo tso Naftali kple Zebulon towo me, eye nàkplɔ wo ayi Tabor-to dzi.

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: Makplɔ Sisera, Yabin ƒe aʋakplɔla, eƒe tasiaɖamwo kple eƒe aʋakɔ ava Kison-tɔʋu nu be wòava kpe aʋa kpli wò, ke mana nàɖu edzi.’ ”

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: Debora ɖo eŋu be: “Yoo, mayi kpli wò baa! Gake nu si gbe yim miele la, womade bubu ŋuwò o elabe Aƒetɔ adzra Sisera na nyɔnu aɖe.” Ale Debora tso yi Kedes kple Barak.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, Xeber, Kenitɔ la va tu eƒe agbadɔ ɖe logotiwo gbɔ le Zaananim le Kedes gbɔ. Do ŋgɔ la, eya ʋu tso Kenitɔ bubu siwo nye Xobab, Mose nyo, la ƒe dzidzimeviwo la gbɔ.

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Esi Sisera se be Barak yi Tabor-to dzi la,

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Tete Debora gblɔ na Barak be: “Tso kpla! Egbee nye egbe! Mènya be Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ dze ŋgɔ xoxo oa? Ele nana ge miaɖu Sisera dzi keŋkeŋ.” Ale Barak ɖi tso Tabor-to la dzi, ame akpe ewoawo dze eyome.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Kasia Barak nado la, Aƒetɔ de zi Sisera kple eƒe tasiaɖamwo kpakple eƒe aʋakɔwo dome, eye wotɔtɔ. Tete Sisera ɖi le eƒe tasiaɖam me, eye wòɖo afɔ eŋu hesí.

english_verse: Barak's forces went after Sisera's chariots and army as far as Harosheth-Ha-Goiim. Sisera's entire army was wiped out.
translation_verse: Barak ti tasiaɖamawo kple aʋakɔ la yome va do ɖe Xaroset-Goyim, eye wotsrɔ̃ wo kple yi keŋkeŋ; ame ɖeka hɔ̃ hã mesusɔ o.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: Ke Sisera to afɔ ʋuu va nyɔnu aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Yael, Kenitɔ Xeber srɔ̃, la ƒe agbadɔ gbɔ. Eva afi sia elabe ŋutifafa le Xazor-fia, Yabin kple Kenitɔ, Xeber ƒe ƒomeawo dome.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Tete Yael yi ɖakpe Sisera hegblɔ nɛ be: “Va, nye amegã! Ge ɖe nye agbadɔ me. Mègavɔ̃ o.” Enumake Sisera ge ɖe eme, eye wòtsyɔ avɔ nɛ.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Sisera gblɔ nɛ be: “Meɖe kuku, na tsi vi aɖem mano; tsikɔ le wuyem.” Enumake Yael ʋu lãgbalẽgolo si me notsi le la, eye wòna ɖee wòno. Emegbe la, egatsyɔ avɔa nɛ.

english_verse: Sisera was exhausted and soon fell fast asleep. Jael took a hammer and drove a tent-peg through his head into the ground, and he died.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, ɖeɖi te Sisera ŋu ŋutɔ ale be wòdɔ alɔ̃ yi eme ʋĩi. Tete Yael tsɔ agbadɔtsyoti kple zu, eye wòyi egbɔ dzaa. Eƒo tsyoti la ɖe tonu na Sisera, mimii ɖe anyigba sesĩe, eye wòku.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Kasia Barak, ame si le Sisera yome tim la nye esi va do. Yael do va kpee hegblɔ nɛ be: “Va ne mafia ame si dim nèle la wò!” Esi wòge ɖe eme la, Sisera nye ekem woƒo tsyoti ɖe tonu na, to eƒe tame do hemimi ɖe anyigba, wòku.

english_verse: That same day God defeated the Canaanite King Jabin while the Israelites looked on, and his army was no longer powerful enough to attack the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ale Mawu bɔbɔ Kanaan-fia, Yabin ɖe anyi gbe ma gbe le Israelviwo ŋkume.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Tso ɣe ma ɣi la, Israelviwo ƒe asi va sẽ ɖe fia la dzi wu tsã va se ɖe esime ŋusẽ va vɔ le eŋu keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: After the battle was over that day, Deborah and Barak sang this song:
translation_verse: Tete gbe ma gbe la, Debora kple Barak, Abinoam vi, dzi ha sia be:

english_verse: We praise you, Lord! Our soldiers volunteered, ready to follow you.
translation_verse: “Mikafu Aƒetɔ! Elabe esi dukɔa ƒe aʋakplɔlawo dze ŋgɔ la, dukɔmeviwo tsɔ wo ɖokui ke faa.

english_verse: Listen, kings and rulers, while I sing for the Lord, the God of Israel.
translation_verse: “Mi fiawo, miɖo to! Mi amegãwo, mike to nyuie! Mele ha dzi ge na Aƒetɔ. Mele ha dzi ge atsɔ akafu Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu lae.

english_verse: Our Lord, God of Israel, when you came from Seir, where the Edomites live,
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, esi nèho tso Seir-towo dzi, eye nèzɔ to Edom-nutome la, anyigba ʋuʋu, tsi kɔ ɖi bababa tso dziŋgɔli me, eye alilikpowo hã dza tsi.

english_verse: rain poured from the sky, the earth trembled, and mountains shook.
translation_verse: Towo ʋuʋu nyànyanya le Aƒetɔ ŋkume; Sinai-to ma ʋuʋu le Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu la ŋkume.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: “Le Samgar, Anat vi kple Yael ŋɔli la, mɔzɔlawo ƒe hawo nu tso; mɔzɔlawo va le gbedzemɔ tom.

english_verse: and villagers couldn't work in their fields. Then Deborah took command, protecting Israel as a mother protects her children.
translation_verse: Aʋakplɔlawo nu tso le Israel; wo nu tso keŋkeŋ, va se ɖe esime nètso, Debora, tso abe vi nɔ ene le Israel.

english_verse: The Israelites worshiped other gods, and the gates of their towns were then attacked. But they had no shields or spears to fight with.
translation_verse: Esi Israelviwo tia mawu yeyewo la, aʋawɔwɔ do mo ɖe anyigba la dzi, woakpɔ akpoxɔnu kple akplɔ le Israelviwo ƒe ame akpe bla eneawo domea?

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: Nye dzi ku ɖe Israelviwo kplɔlawo kple ame siwo lɔ̃ faa, tsɔ wo ɖokui ke, ɖe dukɔa ta la ŋu. Mikafu Aƒetɔ!

english_verse: Listen, everyone! Whether you ride a donkey with a padded saddle or have to walk.
translation_verse: “Miƒo nu le eŋu, mi ame siwo do tedzinɔ ɣiwo yina, mi ame siwo bɔbɔ nɔ afɔɖodzivɔ bɔbɔe xɔasiwo dzi, mi ame siwo le mɔ ta yina.

english_verse: Even those who carry water to the animals will tell you, “The Lord has won victories, and so has Israel.” Then the Lord's people marched down to the town gates
translation_verse: Miɖo to miase ɖa! Tsikulawo ƒe ha le ɖiɖim le vudowo to, afi mae wole Aƒetɔ ƒe dziɖuɖu ŋutinya gblɔm, gale gblɔm, le agbledelawo ƒe dziɖuɖu le Israel ŋu gblɔm le. “Emegbe Aƒetɔ ƒe dukɔ la zɔ ɖi abu ɖo ta woƒe agbowo nu.

english_verse: and said, “Deborah, let's go! Let's sing as we march. Barak, capture our enemies.”
translation_verse: “Nyɔ, Debora, nyɔ! Nyɔ nàdzi ha, nyɔ! Tso kpla, Barak, Abinoam vi. Kplɔ wò aboyomeawo dzoe.

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la ƒe bubume mamlɛawo ɖi abu va; Aƒetɔ ƒe amewo ɖi va egbɔ ɖe kalẽawo ŋu.

english_verse: Troops came from Ephraim, where Amalekites once lived. Others came from Benjamin; officers and leaders came from Machir and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Tso Efrayim woho ɖo ta bali la me, kplɔ wò, Benyamin kple wò ƒometɔwo ɖo. Gbeɖelawo ɖi abu tso Maxir, eye tsiamititsɔlawo tso Zebulon.

english_verse: The rulers of Issachar came along with Deborah, and Issachar followed Barak into the valley. But the tribe of Reuben was no help at all!
translation_verse: Isaxar-megãwo le Debora ŋu va do. Isaxar wɔ nuteƒe na Barak. Wole eyome kpledukpledu ɖo ta balia me. Ruben tokɔmetɔwo ya yi adaŋu me; womenya ne ɖe woayi loo, alo ɖe woatsi anyi o.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Nu ka ta nètsi alẽhawo gbɔ? Be nànɔ alẽkplɔlawo ƒe alẽwo yɔyɔ sem ta loo? Ruben tokɔmetɔwo ya yi adaŋu me.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Gilead ya tsi Yordan ƒe go kemɛ dzi. Nu ka ta Dan ya le tɔdziʋuwo gbɔ? Aser-to la me tɔwo bɔbɔ nɔ ƒuta, eye wotsyɔ akɔ anyi ɖe afi ma.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Zebulon nye ame siwo tsɔ woƒe agbe ke ku faa; Naftali hã nenema, le gbadzaƒe si le toawo dzi.”

english_verse: Canaanite kings fought us at Taanach by the stream near Megiddo— but they couldn't rob us of our silver.
translation_verse: “Fiawo va wɔ aʋa, Kanaan-fiawo va wɔ aʋa ɣe ma ɣi le Tanax le Megido-tɔʋuwo nu; ke womekpɔ klosalo aɖeke ha dzoe o.

english_verse: From their pathways in the sky the stars fought Sisera,
translation_verse: Ɣletiviwoe nɔ dziƒo wɔ aʋa la, wonɔ woƒe mɔwo dzi le ya me, eye wowɔ aʋa kple Sisera.

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Kison-tsisisi lae si kplɔ wo yii, tsi si le sisím kplakplakpla lae, Kison-tsisisi lae. Nye luʋɔ, zɔ yi ŋgɔ kple ŋusẽ!

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: “Tete sɔwo le du dzi, woƒe afɔziwo le ɖiɖim sesĩe kplàkplakpla.”

english_verse: The Lord's angel said, “Put a curse on Meroz Town! Its people refused to help the Lord fight his powerful enemies.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla be: “Neɖi Meros ŋu! Neɖi emenɔlawo ŋu kpékpekpe! Elabe womeva kpe ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu o; kpe ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu akpe akɔ kple ŋusẽtɔ la o.

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Tsie Sisera bia, ke notsie wònae; woku notsi babla kpekẽ, wòkui ɖe bubumewo ƒe tsinonu me vɛ.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: Yael do asi ɖa tsɔ tsyoti, elé gbede ƒe zu la ɖe ɖusi. Eda zua ɖe Sisera dzi, tsyotia ŋɔ eƒe tonu to eƒe tame do.

english_verse: Sisera's mother looked out through her window. “Why is he taking so long?” she asked. “Why haven't we heard his chariots coming?”
translation_verse: “Edo mo ɖe fesre nu; Sisera nɔ do mo ɖa to adzrala me: edo ɣli to adzrala me be: “Ale ke wɔ eƒe tasiaɖamwo meva do kpɔ o? Ale ke wɔ eƒe tasiaɖamfɔwo ƒe ɖiɖi tsi megbe ale?”

english_verse: She and her wisest women gave the same answer:
translation_verse: Eƒe nyɔnu nunyalawo ɖo eŋu, gbeɖe, eya ŋutɔ ɖo eŋu na eɖokui be:

english_verse: “Sisera and his troops are finding treasures to bring back— a woman, or maybe two, for each man, and beautiful dresses for those women to wear.”
translation_verse: ‘Ðe womele kekem ɖe aboyonuwo ŋu le mamam oa? Nyɔnuvi ɖeka alo eve na ŋutsu ɖe sia ɖe. Sisera naxɔ awu ŋɔŋɔewo, kɔmevɔ ŋɔŋɔe eve kple aboyonu na nye kɔ.’

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, tsrɔ̃ wò futɔwo katã alea! Ke xɔ̃wòwo, nenɔ abe ale si ɣe dzena kple eƒe ŋusẽ ene.” Emegbe anyigba la gbɔ ɖe eme ƒe bla ene sɔŋ.

english_verse: Then once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord, so he let the nation of Midian control Israel for seven years.
translation_verse: Israelviwo gawɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu, eya ta wòna Midiantɔwo ɖu wo dzi ƒe adrẽ.

english_verse: The Midianites were so cruel that many Israelites ran to the mountains and hid in caves.
translation_verse: Midiantɔwo sesẽ wu Israelviwo. Ale be le wo ta la, wowɔ beɖoƒewo ɖe towo dzi kple agadowo me eye wotu dedienɔƒe sesẽwo, afi siwo woɣlana ɖo.

english_verse: Every time the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites invaded Israel together with the Amalekites and other eastern nations.
translation_verse: Nenye be Israelviwo ƒã nu la, Midiantɔwo kple Amalekitɔwo kpakple ɣedzeƒeviwo ɖea fu na wo vevie.

english_verse: They rode in on their camels, set up their tents, and then let their livestock eat the crops as far as the town of Gaza. The Midianites stole food, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. Like a swarm of locusts, they could not be counted, and they ruined the land wherever they went.
translation_verse: Wova dona bibibi kple woƒe lãhawo kple avɔgbadɔwo abe ʋetsuviwo ene. Woawo ŋutɔ kple woƒe kposɔwo mele xexlẽme o. Ðeko wovana gblẽa nu sia nu le anyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: The Midianites took almost everything that belonged to the Israelites, and the Israelites begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Esi Israelviwo do ɣli yɔ Aƒetɔ la be neɖe yewo tso Midiantɔwo si me ta la,

english_verse: I am your God, and I told you not to worship Amorite gods, even though you are living in the land of the Amorites. But you refused to listen. The Lord Chooses Gideon
translation_verse: Megblɔ na mi be nyee nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la. Migasubɔ Amoritɔ siwo ƒe anyigba dzi miele la ƒe mawuwo o.’ Ke miegbe be yewomaɖo tom o.”

english_verse: One day an angel from the Lord went to the town of Ophrah and sat down under the big tree that belonged to Joash, a member of the Abiezer clan. Joash's son Gideon was nearby, threshing grain in a shallow pit, where he could not be seen by the Midianites.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla va kɔƒe aɖe si woyɔna be Ofra la me, eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ anyi ɖe logoti aɖe te. Ati sia nye Yoas, ame si nye Abiezer ƒe dzidzimevi la tɔ. Ɣe ma ɣi la, via ŋutsuvi Gideon nɔ lu ƒom le wainfiãƒe bene Midiantɔwo nagakpɔe o.

english_verse: The angel appeared and spoke to Gideon, “The Lord is helping you, and you are a strong warrior.”
translation_verse: Kasia Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla do ɖe edzi gblɔ nɛ be: “Ŋutsuwɔla kalẽtɔ, Aƒetɔ li kpli wò!”

english_verse: Gideon answered, “Please don't take this wrong, but if the Lord is helping us, then why have all of these awful things happened? We've heard how the Lord performed miracles and rescued our ancestors from Egypt. But those things happened long ago. Now the Lord has abandoned us to the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Gideon biae be: “Nye amegã, èbe ale ke? Ne Aƒetɔ ɖe wòli kpli mí tututu ɖe, nu ka tae nu siawo katã dzɔ ɖe mía dzi? Nukunu siwo katã ŋu mía tɔgbuiwo ƒoa nu le na mí, be woawoe Aƒetɔ wɔ esime wòkplɔ mí tso Egipte la hã ɖe, afi ka wole? Azɔ Aƒetɔ tsɔ mí ƒu gbe na Midiantɔwo.”

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Tso kple ŋusẽ si le asiwò la, eye nàyi aɖaɖe Israel-dukɔ tso Midiantɔwo si me. Nye ŋutɔŋutɔe le dɔwòm!”

english_verse: Gideon replied, “But how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in Manasseh, and everyone else in my family is more important than I am.”
translation_verse: Ke Gideon ɖo eŋu be: “Taflatsɛ, nye amegã, nu ka tsɔ ge mala aɖe Israel-dukɔ lae? Kpɔ ɖa, míaƒe ƒome lae nye ŋusẽmanɔŋutɔ kekeake le Manase-toa me, eye gawu la, nyee nye ɖevitɔ le tɔ́nye ƒeme.”

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord answered, “you can rescue Israel because I am going to help you! Defeating the Midianites will be as easy as beating up one man.”
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Nyee be meli kpli wò. Àɖu Midiantɔwo dzi abe ŋutsu ɖeka ene.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Gideon ɖo eŋu be: “Ne èkpɔ ŋudzedze le ŋunye la, ekema wɔ dzesi aɖe tsɔ ɖo kpe edzi nam be wò, Aƒetɔ ŋutɔe le nu ƒom kplim.

english_verse: And wait here until I bring you an offering.” “All right, I'll wait,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Meɖe kuku, mègadzo haɖe o, va se ɖe esime matsɔ nunana aɖe vɛ na wò gbɔ hafi.” Eɖo eŋu be: “Manɔ lalawòm va se ɖe esime nàyi ava.”

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: Ale Gideon yi aƒeme. Ewu gbɔ̃tsui ɖeka ƒo detsii, eye wòtsɔ wɔ kilo ewo wɔ abolo maʋamaʋã kpe ɖe eŋu. Azɔ la, eɖe gbɔ̃lã la ɖe kusi me, eye wòku detsi ƒuƒlua ɖe kutu me tsɔ va ɖo dɔla la kɔme le logotia te.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Mawudɔla la gblɔ nɛ be: “Tsɔ lã la kple abolo la da ɖe kpe sia dzi, eye nàkɔ detsia ɖe wo dzi.” Gideon wɔ nenema.

english_verse: The angel was holding a walking stick, and he touched the meat and the bread with the end of the stick. Flames jumped from the rock and burned up the meat and the bread. When Gideon looked, the angel was gone.
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla la tsɔ atizɔti si le esi la nu tɔ lã la kple abolo la dzi. Enumake dzo do tso agakpe la me hefiã lã la kple abolo la katã. Tete mawudɔla la bu vĩi le egbɔ.

english_verse: Gideon realized that he had seen one of the Lord's angels. “Oh!” he moaned. “Now I'm going to die.”
translation_verse: Tete Gideon kpɔ dze sii azɔ be Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔlae yekpɔ eya ta edo ɣli gblɔ be: “Aléle! Aƒetɔ Mawu! Mekpɔ wò dɔla ŋkume kple ŋkume!”

english_verse: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Wò dzi nedze eme. Mègavɔ̃ o. Mèle kuku ge o.”

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Gideon ɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afi ma na Aƒetɔ, eye wòna ŋkɔe be: “Aƒetɔ ye nye ŋutifafa.” Vɔsamlekpui sia gale Ofra va se ɖe egbe, eye wònye Abiezer ƒomeawo tɔ.

english_verse: That night the Lord spoke to Gideon again: Get your father's second-best bull, the one that's seven years old. Use it to pull down the altar where your father worships Baal and cut down the sacred pole next to the altar.
translation_verse: Zã ma me ke la, Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Lé tɔ́wò ƒe nyitsu ɖeka kple nyitsu bubu si xɔ ƒe adrẽ. Yi nàgbã tɔ́wò ƒe vɔsamlekpui si wòɖi na Baal, eye nàlã atikpo si nye Asera la ɖa le egbɔ.

english_verse: Then build an altar for worshiping me on the highest part of the hill where your town is built. Use layers of stones for my altar, not just a pile of rocks. Cut up the wood from the pole, make a fire, kill the bull, and burn it as a sacrifice to me.
translation_verse: Emegbe la, fɔ kpewo nàɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe ɖoɖo nyui me na Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la, ɖe agakpe sia tame. Azɔ lé nyitsu evelia nàmè kple atikpo si nàlã la atsɔ asa vɔe.

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: Ale Gideon ɖe ŋutsu ewo le eƒe dɔlawo dome, eye wòwɔ abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ ene. Ewɔe le zã me, ke menye le ŋkeke me o, elabe enɔ tɔ́a ƒometɔwo kple dua me ŋutsuwo vɔ̃m ŋutɔ.

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Dua me ŋutsuwo fɔ ŋdi kanya, eye wokpɔ be wogbã vɔsamlekpui si woɖi na Baal, lã nyɔnumawu Asera la hã ɖa, eye wotsɔ nyitsu sa vɔe le vɔsamlekpui si woɖi la dzi.

english_verse: “Who could have done such a thing?” they asked. And they kept on asking, until finally someone told them, “Gideon the son of Joash did it.”
translation_verse: Wobia wo nɔewo se be: “Ame kae wɔ nu sia?” Le nua wɔla didi tsitotsito vɔ megbe la, wova nya be Gideon, Yoas vi lae wɔe.

english_verse: The men of the town went to Joash and said, “Your son Gideon knocked over Baal's altar and cut down the sacred pole next to it. Hand him over, so we can kill him!”
translation_verse: Tete wogblɔ na Yoas be: “Kplɔ viwò ŋutsuvia do go va afii. Edze na ku elabe egbã vɔsamlekpui si míeɖi na Baal, eye wòlã nyɔnumawu Asera si le egbɔ la hã ɖa.”

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Ke Yoas gblɔ na ame siwo katã tsi tre ɖe eŋu la be: “Dzree miebe yewoawɔ ɖe Baal nua? Etae miebe yewoaʋlia? Ne ame aɖe ʋli eta la, woawui hafi ŋu nake. Eƒe vɔsamlekpuie wogbã. Nenye Mawue wònye la, neʋli eɖokui ta.”

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: Tso gbe ma gbe la, wona ŋkɔ Gideon be Yerub-Baal elabe Yoas gblɔ be: “Mina Baal naʋli eɖokui ta, elabe eƒe vɔsamlekpuie wogbã.”

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Tete Midiantɔwo, Amalekitɔwo kple ɣedzeƒeviwo katã va kpe ta. Wotso Yordan-tɔsisi la, eye wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Yezreel-bali la me.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe Gbɔgbɔ dze Gideon dzi, eye wòku kpẽ yɔ Abiezer ƒomeawo be woadze ye yome.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Edɔ dɔlawo ɖo ɖe Manase-to eveawo me tɔwo hã be woadze ye yome. Azɔ la, egadɔ dɔlawo ɖo ɖe Aser, Zebulon kple Naftali toawo me tɔwo, eye wova kpe wo.

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: ekema mele alẽgbalẽ tsɔ ge ada ɖe lugbɔƒe. Ne ŋu ke ŋdi, eye zãmu ƒo alẽgbalẽa ɖeɖe ko, eye anyigba le ƒuƒuie la, ekema madze sii be dzinye to ge nàla aɖe Israel-dukɔ la vavã.

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Eva eme nenema tututu. Esi Gideon fɔ ŋdi la, efiã alẽgbalẽ la, eye zãmu si do le eme la yɔ tre banaa.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Tete Gideon gblɔ na Mawu be: “Meɖe kuku, dzi megaku wò o. Medi be magagblɔ nya aɖe. Na magatsɔ alẽgbalẽ la agado wò kpɔ zi evelia. Fifia la, meɖe kuku, na alẽgbalẽa nanɔ ƒuƒuie, ke zãmu naƒo anyigba si ƒo xlãe godoo la ya.

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Mawu wɔ nenema le zã ma me. Zãmu ƒo anyigba la katã, ke alẽgbalẽ la ya le ƒuƒuie.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Gideon and his army got up and moved their camp to Fear Spring. The Midianite camp was to the north, in the valley at the foot of Moreh Hill.
translation_verse: Tete Yerub-Baal si nye Gideon kple eƒe amewo katã fɔ ŋdi kanya, eye woyi ɖaƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Xarod tsidzidzi la gbɔ. Midiantɔwo hã ƒu asaɖa anyi le dzigbeme lɔƒo ɖe bali si le More-togbɛ la gbɔ la me.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Gideon be: “Medi be mana miaɖu Midiantɔwo dzi, evɔ la, ame siwo nèkplɔ ɖe asi la sɔ gbɔ akpa. Ne mieɖu dzi la, Israel magado eɖokui ɖe dzi agblɔ be: Nye ŋutɔ nye asie ɖem’ o.

english_verse: So call your troops together and tell them that anyone who is really afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home.” Twenty-two thousand men returned home, leaving Gideon with only
translation_verse: Eya ta azɔ la, ɖe gbeƒã ne amewo katã nase be: ‘Ame si ke le vɔvɔ̃m, eye dzi mele eƒo o la, negbugbɔ yi aƒe.’ ” Tete Gideon do wo kpɔ eye ame akpe bla eve vɔ eve trɔ dzo, eye ame akpe ewo susɔ.

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Ke ne èvɔ̃ be yeayi la, ekema kplɔ wò dɔla Puva ɖe asi miayi afi ma.

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord said, “you still have too many soldiers. Take them down to the spring and I'll test them. I'll tell you which ones can go along with you and which ones must go back home.”
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Gideon be: “Ameawo gasɔ gbɔ akpa kokoko. Kplɔ wo yi ɖe tɔ la nu bene mado wo kpɔ na wò le afi ma. Ne megblɔ be ame aɖe neyi kpli wò la, eya neyi kpli wò. Ne megblɔ be ame aɖe ya megayi kpli wò o la, megayi kpli wò o.”

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Esi Gideon kplɔ ameawo va tɔa nu la, Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Tia ame siwo no tsi la kple aɖe abe avu ene la ɖe aga tso ame siwo dze klo tsyɔ nu eme noe la gbɔ.”

english_verse: Three hundred men scooped up water in their hands and lapped it, and the rest knelt to get a drink.
translation_verse: Ame siwo ku tsia ɖe asiƒome no kple aɖe la le ame alafa etɔ̃, ke ame mamlɛawo katã ya dze klo tsyɔ nu ɖe tsia me hafi noe.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army will be made up of everyone who lapped the water from their hands. Send the others home. I'm going to rescue Israel by helping you and your army of
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Gideon be: “Matsɔ ame alafa etɔ̃ siwo ku tsia no kple aɖe abe avu ene la aɖe mi, eye mana miaɖu Midiantɔwo dzi. Ke na ame mamlɛawo katã nagbugbɔ ayi wo nɔƒe.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord said to Gideon. “Get up! Attack the Midianite camp. I am going to let you defeat them,
translation_verse: Le zã ma me ke la, Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Gideon be: “Tso nàlũ ɖe wo dzi le woƒe asaɖa la me, elabe mana nàɖu wo dzi godoo.

english_verse: When you hear what the Midianites are saying, you'll be brave enough to attack.” Gideon and Purah worked their way to the edge of the enemy camp, where soldiers were on guard duty.
translation_verse: Ne mieyi la, miase nya si gblɔm wole la eye dzi aɖo ƒowò miatso ɖe wo ŋu.” Ale Gideon kple eƒe dɔla Pura woyi ɖate ɖe woƒe futɔwo ƒe asaɖa la ŋu kpuie.

english_verse: The camp was huge. The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. And it would be easier to count the grains of sand on a beach than to count their camels.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, Midiantɔwo kple Amalekitɔwo kpakple ɣedzeƒeviwo ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe bali la me kpaŋkpaŋkpaŋ; wosɔ gbɔ abe ʋetsuviwo ene. Woƒe kposɔwo ya le abe ƒutake ene.

english_verse: Gideon overheard one enemy guard telling another, “I had a dream about a flat loaf of barley bread that came tumbling into our camp. It hit the headquarters tent, and the tent flipped over and fell to the ground.”
translation_verse: Esi Gideon va ɖo la, ŋutsu aɖe nɔ drɔ̃e lĩm na xɔlɔ̃a wòse. Egblɔ be: “Meku drɔ̃e, eye mekpɔ abolo aɖe si wome kple lu. Aboloa mli togotogo va míaƒe ƒe asaɖa me. Elɔ agbadɔ ɖeka, eye agbadɔa mu gbloo tsyɔ anyigba.”

english_verse: The other soldier answered, “Your dream must have been about Gideon, the Israelite commander. It means God will let him and his army defeat the Midianite army and everyone else in our camp.”
translation_verse: Ke xɔlɔ̃a ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Israeltɔ Gideon, Yoas vi la ƒe yie nèkpɔ; menye nu bubu aɖekee o. Mawu na ŋusẽe be wòaɖu mí Midiantɔwo kple aʋakɔ sia katã dzi.”

english_verse: As soon as Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to praise God. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, “Let's go! The Lord is going to let us defeat the Midianite army.”
translation_verse: Esi Gideon se drɔ̃e la kple eƒe gɔmeɖeɖe la, edze klo do gbe ɖa. Emegbe la, egbugbɔ va Israelviwo ƒe asaɖa me, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Mía tɔwo, mitso, elabe Aƒetɔ tsɔ Midiantɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ la de mía si.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “When we get to the enemy camp, spread out and surround it. Then wait for me to blow a signal on my trumpet. As soon as you hear it, blow your trumpets and shout, ‘Fight for the Lord! Fight for Gideon!’ ”
translation_verse: Ne nye kple nye aʋalɔgo la míeku míaƒe kpẽawo la, ekema miawo hã miku mia tɔ ƒo xlã woƒe asaɖa la godoo. Mido ɣli gblɔ be: ‘Aƒetɔ kple Gideon tɔe!’ ”

english_verse: Gideon and his group reached the edge of the enemy camp a few hours after dark, just after the new guards had come on duty. Gideon and his soldiers blew their trumpets and smashed the clay jars that were hiding the torches.
translation_verse: Ale Gideon kple ame alafa ɖeka si le eŋu la zɔ tu futɔwo ƒe asaɖa la kpuie hafi zã titina ɖo. Ŋudzɔnɔlawo ɖɔli wo nɔewo teti ko wova ɖo. Tete Gideon kple etɔwo ku kpẽawo, eye wogbã ze siwo le wo si la.

english_verse: The rest of Gideon's soldiers blew the trumpets they were holding in their right hands. Then they smashed the jars and held the burning torches in their left hands. Everyone shouted, “Fight with your swords for the Lord and for Gideon!”
translation_verse: Enumake aʋalɔgo eve mamlɛawo hã wɔ nenema ke. Wolé kpẽawo ɖe ɖusi helé akakatiawo ɖe mia, eye wonɔ ɣli dom be: “Aƒetɔ kple Gideon tɔe nye yi la!”

english_verse: The enemy soldiers started yelling and tried to run away. Gideon's troops stayed in their positions surrounding the camp
translation_verse: Wo dome ame sia ame tɔ te ɖe eteƒe le futɔawo ƒe asaɖa la ŋu godoo. Zi tɔ le asaɖa la me eye wode asi dusisi me kple ɣli nɔ sísim.

english_verse: and blew their trumpets again. As they did, the Lord made the enemy soldiers pull out their swords and start fighting each other. The enemy army tried to escape from the camp. They ran to Acacia Tree Town, toward Zeredah, and as far as the edge of the land that belonged to the town of Abel-Meholah near Tabbath.
translation_verse: Esime Gideon ƒe amewo nɔ kpẽawo kum la, Aƒetɔ na futɔawo nɔ nu vevi wɔm wo nɔewo kple woawo ŋutɔ ƒe yi. Wosí ɖo ta Zereda va do ɖe Bet-Sita. Wogbɔ afi ma ŋu va ke ɖe Abel-Mexola ƒe liƒo ŋu heto Tabat ŋu dzo.

english_verse: Gideon sent word for more Israelite soldiers to come from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher, and both halves of Manasseh to help fight the Midianites.
translation_verse: Woyɔ Israel-ŋutsuwo tso Naftali kple Aser kpakple Manase-to eveawo me, eye wonyà Midiantɔwo ɖe nu.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to tell all the men who lived in the hill country of Ephraim, “Come and help us fight the Midianites! Put guards at every spring, stream, and well, as far as Beth-Barah before the Midianites can get to them. And guard the Jordan River.” Troops from Ephraim did exactly what Gideon had asked,
translation_verse: Gideon dɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Efrayim-tonyigba blibo la dzi be woaɖagblɔ be: “Miɖi va kpe Midiantɔwo. Mixe tɔʋuawo kple Yordan-tɔsisi la nu va se ɖe keke Bet Bara ke!” Ale woyɔ Efrayim-ŋutsuwo katã ƒo ƒu, eye woxe tɔawo kple Yordan nu va se ɖe Bet Bara.

english_verse: and they even helped chase the Midianites on the east side of the Jordan River. These troops captured Raven and Wolf, the two Midianite leaders. They killed Raven at a large rock that has come to be known as Raven Rock, and they killed Wolf near a wine-pit that has come to be called Wolf Wine-Pit. The men of Ephraim brought the heads of the two Midianite leaders to Gideon.
translation_verse: Tete woƒe asi su Midian-fia eveawo, Oreb kple Zeeb dzi. Wowu Oreb ɖe Oreb-kpe la gbɔ, eye wowu Zeeb ya ɖe Zeeb ƒe wainfiãƒe. Azɔ wogakplɔ Midiantɔwo ɖo ʋuu hafi trɔ. Wogbɔ va kple Oreb kple Zeeb ƒe tawo, eye wotsɔ wo na Gideon, ame si le Yordan-tɔsisi la ƒe ɣedzeƒe go ŋu ɣe ma ɣi.

english_verse: But the men were really upset with Gideon and complained, “When you went to war with Midian, you didn't ask us to help! Why did you treat us like that?”
translation_verse: Tete Efrayimtɔwo bia Gideon be: “Nu ka ta nègbe mía yɔyɔ esime nèho aʋa ɖe Midiantɔwo ŋu? Nu ka ta nèwɔ nu sia ɖe mía ŋu?”

english_verse: Gideon answered: Don't be upset! Even though you came later, you were able to do much more than I did. It's just like the grape harvest: The grapes your tribe doesn't even bother to pick are better than the best grapes my family can grow.
translation_verse: Ke eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Nu si mete ŋu wɔ la, mede nu si miawo boŋ miewɔ la nu o. Gawu la, nu si nye tokɔmetɔ gbogbo siawo te ŋu wɔ la, mede nu sue si mi Efrayimtɔwo miete ŋu wɔ la nu gɔ̃ hã o.

english_verse: Besides, God chose you to capture Raven and Wolf. I didn't do a thing compared to you. By the time Gideon had finished talking, the men of Ephraim had calmed down and were no longer angry with him. Gideon Finishes Destroying the Midianite Army
translation_verse: Mawu na miawo miewu Midian-fia eveawo, Oreb kple Zeeb. Ðe nye boŋ mete ŋu wɔ nane si sɔ kple mia tɔa?” Esi wògblɔ nya sia la, woƒe dzi fa.

english_verse: The town of Succoth was nearby, so he went there and asked, “Please give my troops some food. They are worn out, but we have to keep chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the two Midianite kings.”
translation_verse: Esi wova ɖo Sukot la, egblɔ na dua me tɔwo be: “Meɖe kuku, midi nuɖuɖu aɖe na ame siwo le zɔzɔm kplim la ne woaɖu, elabe ɖeɖi te wo ŋu ŋutɔ. Evɔ la mele Midian-fia eveawo, Zebax kple Zalmuna, yome tim.”

english_verse: The town leaders of Succoth answered, “Why should we feed your army? We don't know if you really will defeat Zebah and Zalmunna.”
translation_verse: Ke Sukot-dumegãwo ɖo eŋu be: “Ðe wò asi su Zebax kple Zalmuna dzi xoxo hafi nèbe míadi nuɖuɖu na wò aʋakɔ la?”

english_verse: “Just wait!” Gideon said. “After the Lord helps me defeat them, I'm coming back here. I'll make a whip out of thorns and rip the flesh from your bones.”
translation_verse: Gideon ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Yoo, enyo. Ne Aƒetɔ na nye asi su Zebax kple Zalmuna dzi la, matsɔ aŋɔka kple ŋu si le gbedadaƒo la akuko mia ŋui.”

english_verse: After leaving Succoth, Gideon went to Penuel and asked the leaders there for some food. But he got the same answer as he did at Succoth.
translation_verse: Esi woho tso afi ma la, wova Penuel. Gideon gabia nuɖuɖu woawo hã, ke afi ma tɔwo hã ɖo nya la ŋu nɛ abe ale si Sukotetɔwo ɖo eŋu nɛ ene.

english_verse: “I'll come back safe and sound,” Gideon said, “but when I do, I'm going to tear down your tower!”
translation_verse: Ale wògblɔ na Penueltɔwo be: “Ne metrɔ gbɔ dedie la, magbã mɔ́ sia gudugudu.”

english_verse: Gideon went to the town officials and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. Remember how you made fun of me? You said, ‘We don't know if you really will defeat those two Midianite kings. So why should we feed your worn-out army?’ ”
translation_verse: Esi Gideon va ɖo Sukotetɔwo gbɔ la, egblɔ na wo be: “Mikpɔ Zebax kple Zalmuna ɖa. Esi míeva to afii yina eye ɖeɖi te nye amewo ŋu vevie la, mebia nuɖuɖu mi be matsɔ na wo, ke ɖeko mieɖu fewu le ŋunye. Miebiam be nye asi ɖe wòsu Zebax kple Zalmuna dzi xoxo hafi le nuɖuɖu biam mahã.”

english_verse: Gideon reached the enemy camp by going east along Nomad Road past Nobah and Jogbehah. He made a surprise attack,
translation_verse: Gideon to asimɔ gã dzi le Nobax kple Yogbeha ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome, eye wova do ɖe aʋakɔ la dzi kpoyi, esime woɖe ŋu ɖi, eye wòsi wo.

english_verse: and the enemy panicked. Zebah and Zalmunna tried to escape, but Gideon chased and captured them.
translation_verse: Tete Midian-fia eveawo, Zebax kple Zalmuna sí, ke Gideon ti wo yome va se ɖe esime eƒe asi su wo dzi. Zi tɔ le Midiantɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ la dome, eye wotɔtɔ ŋutɔŋutɔ.

english_verse: After the battle, Gideon set out for home. As he was going through Heres Pass,
translation_verse: Esi Gideon trɔ tso aʋagbea dzi gbɔna la, eto Heres todzimɔ la.

english_verse: he caught a young man who lived in Succoth. Gideon asked him who the town officials of Succoth were, and the young man wrote down
translation_verse: Ekpɔ ɖekakpui aɖe si nye Sukotetɔ, eye wòlée hebia gbee. Ena wòŋlɔ dumegã siwo katã le Sukot la ƒe ŋkɔwo nɛ. Eŋlɔ ame bla adrẽ vɔ adrẽ.

english_verse: Gideon made a whip from thorn plants and used it to beat the town officials.
translation_verse: Ale wòtsɔ ŋu kple aŋuka siwo wòwɔ le gbedadaƒo la he to na Sukotetɔwo vevie.

english_verse: Afterwards he went to Penuel, where he tore down the tower and killed all the town officials.
translation_verse: Emegbe egbã mɔ́ si le Penuel-du me, eye wòwu ŋutsu siwo katã le afi ma.

english_verse: Then Gideon said, “Zebah and Zalmunna, tell me about the men you killed at Tabor.” “They were a lot like you,” the two kings answered. “They were dignified, almost like royalty.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Gideon bia Zebax kple Zalmuna be: “Ale ke ŋutsu siwo miewu le Tabor-to gbɔ la le?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Woɖi wò ŋutɔ. Wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ɖi fia vi.”

english_verse: “They were my very own brothers!” Gideon said. “I swear by the living Lord that if you had let them live, I would let you live.”
translation_verse: Ke Gideon gblɔ na wo be: “Nɔvinye ŋutsuwoe. Dadaviwo míenye! Metà Mawu na mi, ne ɖe miewu wo o la, anye ne nye hã nyemawu mi o.

english_verse: kilograms. In addition, there was the gold from the camels' ornaments and from the beautiful jewelry worn by the Midianite kings. Gideon also took their purple robes.
translation_verse: Enumake wògblɔ na eƒe ŋgɔgbevi Yeter be: “Tso nàwu wo!” Ke eya vɔ̃, eye mehe eƒe yi la ɖe go o, elabe ɖekakpuivi ko wònye.

english_verse: “What's the matter, Gideon?” Zebah and Zalmunna asked. “Do it yourself, if you're not too much of a coward!” Gideon jumped up and killed them both. Then he took the gold ornaments from the necks of their camels. The Israelites Ask Gideon To Be Their King
translation_verse: Tete Zebax kple Zalmuna gblɔ na Gideon be: “Wò ŋutɔ tso nàdza mí wu. Ŋutsu ŋutɔe ɖea eƒe ŋusẽ fiana.” Ale Gideon tso hewu wo, eye wòɖe kɔga si le kɔ na woƒe kposɔwo.

english_verse: After the battle with the Midianites, the Israelites said, “Gideon, you rescued us! Now we want you to be our king. Then after your death, your son and then your grandson will rule.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Israeltɔwo gblɔ na Gideon be: “Míedi be wò ŋutɔ kple wò dzidzimeviwo nazu mía dziɖula, elabe èɖe mí tso Midiantɔwo si me.”

english_verse: “No,” Gideon replied, “I won't be your king, and my son won't be king either. Only the Lord is your ruler.
translation_verse: Gideon ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Nye ŋutɔ loo, alo vinye ŋutsu aɖeke maɖu fia ɖe mia dzi o. Aƒetɔ ye aɖu fia ɖe mia dzi.”

english_verse: But I will ask you to do one thing: Give me all the earrings you took from the enemy.” The enemy soldiers had been Ishmaelites, and they wore gold earrings.
translation_verse: Eyi edzi gblɔ na wo be: “Medi be mabia nane mi. Ame sia ame netsɔ togɛ si wòha tso gbea dzi la nam.” Midiantɔwo dea sikatogɛ vevie abe Ismaeltɔ bubuawo ene.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers replied, “Of course we will give you the earrings.” Then they spread out a robe on the ground and tossed the earrings on it.
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Míana wò faa.” Ale wokeke awu aɖe ɖi, eye ame sia ame tsɔ togɛ si wòha tso gbea dzi la da ɖe edzi.

english_verse: He even had a wife who lived at Shechem. They had a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
