translation_verse: Ahiãvi hã nɔ esi le Sixem. Eya dzi ŋutsuvi ɖeka nɛ, eye wòna ŋkɔe be Abimelex.

english_verse: Gideon lived to be an old man. And when he died, he was buried in the family tomb in his hometown of Ophrah, which belonged to the Abiezer clan.
translation_verse: Gideon tsi ŋutɔ hafi ku, eye woɖii ɖe tɔ́a Yoas ƒe ameɖiƒe le Ofra si nye Abiezer ƒomeawo ƒe du.

english_verse: Soon after Gideon's death, the Israelites turned their backs on God again. They set up idols of Baal and worshiped Baal Berith as their god.
translation_verse: Esi Gideon nyaku ko la, Israel-dukɔ la dzudzɔ woƒe Mawu la subɔsubɔ. Wode asi Baalwo subɔsubɔ me, eye wotsɔ Baal-Berit wɔ woƒe mawui.

english_verse: The Israelites forgot that the Lord was their God, and that he had rescued them from the enemies who lived around them.
translation_verse: Mlɔeba la, Israelviwo ƒe ŋku va bu le Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la dzi keŋ, evɔ wònye eyae ɖe wo tso futɔ siwo ƒo xlã wo godoo va yi la si me hafi.

english_verse: Besides all that, the Israelites were unkind to Gideon's family, even though Gideon had done so much for Israel.
translation_verse: Gawu la, togbɔ be Gideon-ƒomeawo wɔ nyui geɖe na Israelviwo kpɔ hã la, woawo ya menyo dɔme na wo tsɔ ɖo eteƒe o.

english_verse: and told them to say to the leaders of Shechem, “Do you think it would be good to have all
translation_verse: woabia Sixemtɔwo be: “Ne Gideon viŋutsu bla adrẽa katã naɖu mia dzi, alo ame ɖeka ko naɖu mia dzi la, kae dze mia ŋu wu? Miɖo ŋku edzi be nye la, miawo ŋutɔ miaƒe ʋu kple ŋutilãe menye.”

english_verse: Abimelech's uncles talked it over with the leaders of Shechem who agreed, “Yes, it would be better for one of our relatives to be king.”
translation_verse: Ale wɔ Abimelex nɔ nɔviwo yi ɖagblɔ nya siawo katã na Sixem-dumegãwo tso Abimelex ŋu ɖe enu. Woƒe dzi trɔ ɖe Abimelex ŋu, be yewoadze eyome, elabe wogblɔ be: ‘Mía nɔviŋutsu ye.’

english_verse: Abimelech and his soldiers went to his father's home in Ophrah and brought out Gideon's other sons to a large rock, where they murdered all
translation_verse: Eyi tɔ́a ƒeme le Ofra, eye wòwu nɔvia ŋutsu bla adrẽ siwo nye Gideon viwo ɖe kpe ɖeka dzi. Ke Yotam, Gideon ƒe dɔmlɔea ya sí ɖaɣla eɖokui ale be eya tsi agbe.

english_verse: The leaders of Shechem, including the priests and the military officers, met at the tree next to the sacred rock in Shechem to crown Abimelech king.
translation_verse: Azɔ Sixemtɔwo kple Bet-milonɔlawo katã va kpe ta le Sixem ɖe logoti si nye ŋkuɖodziti le afi ma la gbɔ, eye woɖo Abimelex fiae. Yotam ƒe lododo le atiwo ŋu

english_verse: Jotham heard what they were doing. So he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted down to the people who were there at the meeting: Leaders of Shechem, listen to me, and maybe God will listen to you.
translation_verse: Esi Yotam se nu si dzɔ la, eyi ɖatsi tsitre ɖe Gerizim-to dzi. Edo ɣli sesĩe gblɔ na wo be: “Sixemtɔwo lee, miɖo tom, ne Mawu naɖo to miawo hã!

english_verse: Once the trees searched for someone to be king; they asked the olive tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la, atiwo kpe ta be yewoatia yewo dometɔ ɖeka asi ami nɛ wòanye fia ɖe yewo nu. Wogblɔ na amiti be: “Ðu fia ɖe mía dzi!’

english_verse: But the olive tree replied, “My oil brings honor to people and gods. I won't stop making oil, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Ke amiti gblɔ na wo be: ‘Ðe madzudzɔ nye ami si wotsɔna dea bubu mawuwo kple amegbetɔwo ŋu la wɔwɔ ava nɔ ya ƒom le atiwo tamea?’

english_verse: Then they asked the fig tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Atiawo gblɔ na gboti be: ‘Wò, va ɖu fia ɖe mía dzi!’

english_verse: But the fig tree replied, “I won't stop growing my delicious fruit, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Ke gboti gblɔ na wo be: ‘Ðe magblẽ nye tsi vivi kple kutsetse nyuiwo ɖi ava nɔ ya ƒom le atiwo tamea?’

english_verse: Next they asked the grape vine, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Atiwo gblɔ na wainti be: ‘Wò, va ɖu fia ɖe mía dzi.’

english_verse: But the grape vine replied, “My wine brings cheer to people and gods. I won't stop making wine, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Ke wainti gblɔ na wo be: ‘Ðe magblẽ nye kutsetsemetsi si doa dzidzɔ na mawuwo kple amegbetɔwo ɖi ava ɖu fia ɖe mi atiwo dzia?’

english_verse: Finally, they went to the thornbush and asked, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Tete atiwo katã gblɔ na aŋɔka be: ‘Wò, va ɖu fia ɖe mía dzi.’

english_verse: The thornbush replied, “If you really want me to be your king, then come into my shade and I will protect you. But if you're deceiving me, I'll start a fire that will spread out and destroy the cedars of Lebanon.” After Jotham had finished telling this story, he said:
translation_verse: Ke aŋɔka gblɔ na wo be: ‘Nenye nyateƒe gblɔm miele be miasi ami nam ne manye fia ɖe mia dzi la, ekema miva bè ɖe nye vɔvɔli te. Ne menye nenem o la, dzo ado tso nye alɔwo me afiã sedertiwo le Lebanon.’ ”

english_verse: My father Gideon risked his life for you when he fought to rescue you from the Midianites. Did you reward Gideon by being kind to his family? No, you did not! You attacked his family and killed all
translation_verse: Ke egbe la, miawoe tso ɖe tɔ́nye ƒe aƒe ŋuti. Miewu via ŋutsu bla adrẽ sɔŋ le kpe dzi, ale be eƒe dɔlanyɔnu ƒe vi, Abimelex, nye mia nɔvi, eye mitsɔe ɖo fiae ɖe Sixem.

english_verse: So, you leaders of Shechem, if you treated Gideon and his family the way you should have, then I hope you and Abimelech will make each other very happy.
translation_verse: Azɔ nenye be nu si miewɔ egbe ɖe Gideon kple eƒe ƒomea ŋu tso miaƒe dzime, eye miewɔe le nyateƒe me la, ekema mikpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe Abimelex ŋu, eye eya hã nekpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe mia ŋu.

english_verse: But if it was wrong to treat Gideon and his family the way you did, then I pray that Abimelech will destroy you with fire, and I pray that you will do the same to him.
translation_verse: Evɔ ne menye nenema o la, dzo nedo tso Abimelex me ne wòafiã Sixemtɔwo kple Milonɔlawo. Nenema ke dzo nedo tso Sixemtɔwo kple Milonɔlawo hã me ne wòafiã Abimelex.”

english_verse: Jotham ran off and went to live in the town of Beer, where he could be safe from his brother Abimelech. Abimelech Destroys Shechem
translation_verse: Yotam nɔ vɔvɔ̃m na nɔvia Abimelex eya ta esí yi ɖanɔ Beer.

english_verse: Abimelech had been a military commander of Israel for three years,
translation_verse: Abimelex ɖu Israel-dukɔ dzi ƒe etɔ̃.

english_verse: when God decided to punish him and the leaders of Shechem for killing Gideon's
translation_verse: Nu sia dzɔ bene woahe to na Abimelex kple Sixemtɔwo kutɔkutɔe, elabe woawoe de dzi ƒo na Abimelex wòwu nɔvia bla adrẽ siwo nye Gideon viwo.

english_verse: Then they sent some men to hide on the hilltops and watch for Abimelech and his troops, while they sent others to rob everyone that went by on the road. But Abimelech found out what they were doing.
translation_verse: Sixemtɔwo ɖe amewo woyi ɖade xa ɖe towo dzi ɖe Abimelex ŋuti, ale be ame sia ame si to mɔa dzi va yina la, wodaa adzo eƒe nuwo le esi.

english_verse: One day, Gaal son of Ebed went to live in Shechem. His brothers moved there too, and soon the leaders of Shechem started trusting him.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Gaal, Ebed vi, ʋu va Sixem kple nɔviawo, eye Sixemtɔwo ɖo ŋu ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: Gaal said: Hamor was the founder of Shechem, and one of his descendants should be our ruler. But Abimelech's father was Gideon, so Abimelech isn't really one of us. He shouldn't be our king, and we shouldn't have to obey him or Zebul, who rules Shechem for him.
translation_verse: Gaal gblɔ be: “Ame ka tɔgbewoe míenye le Sixem? Nu ka ta míele Abimelex subɔm ɖo? Evɔ ɖe, ame ka gɔ̃ wònye? Gideon vie wònyee. Etsɔ Zebul ɖo dumegãe. Nu ka ta koŋ wòle be míasubɔ eya ɖo? Misubɔ mía tɔgbuigã Hemor, ame si tso du sia na mí boŋ.

english_verse: If I were the ruler of Shechem, I'd get rid of that Abimelech. I'd tell him, “Get yourself an even bigger army, and we will still defeat you.”
translation_verse: Ame aɖee tsɔm wɔ dukɔ sia kplɔlae! Anye ne meɖe Abimelex ɖa xoxo! Ɖeko magblɔ nɛ be: ‘Di amewo kpe wò aʋakɔ, eye nàdo va kpem!’ ”

english_verse: Zebul was angry when he found out what Gaal had said.
translation_verse: Esi Zebul, dua dziɖula la, se Gaal ƒe nyaawo la, dzi kui vevie.

english_verse: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
translation_verse: Eya ta mia kple wò amewo mifɔ zã miaɖade xa ɖe gbe me.

english_verse: Get up the next morning at sunrise and rush out of your hiding places to attack the town. Gaal and his followers will come out to fight you, but you will easily defeat them.
translation_verse: Ne ŋu ke ɣe dze la, miwɔ kaba miava dze dua dzi kpata. Ne Gaal kple eƒe amewo do va kpe mi la, mitu nu kpli wo ale si miate ŋui.”

english_verse: So one night, Abimelech led his soldiers to Shechem. He divided them into four groups, and they all hid near the town.
translation_verse: Tete Abimelex kple eƒe aʋakɔ la fɔ zã, eye wova de xa ɖe Sixem gbɔ, le aʋalɔgo ene me.

english_verse: The next morning, Gaal went out and stood in the opening of the town gate. Abimelech and his soldiers left their hiding places,
translation_verse: Esi Gaal do yi ɖatsi tsitre ɖe dua ƒe agbo nu la, Abimelex kple eƒe aʋakɔ la do tso afi si wode xa ɖo la.

english_verse: and Gaal saw them. Zebul was standing there with Gaal, and Gaal remarked, “Zebul, that looks like a crowd of people coming down from the mountaintops.” “No,” Zebul answered, “it's just the shadows of the mountains. It only looks like people moving.”
translation_verse: Gaal kpɔ aʋakɔ la, eye wògblɔ na Zebul be: “Kpɔ ɖa, aʋakɔ aɖe nye ekem le ɖiɖim tso to la dzi gbɔna!” Ke Zebul ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Towo ƒe vɔvɔli kpɔm nèle, menye amewoe o.”

english_verse: “But Zebul, look over there,” Gaal said. “There's a crowd coming down from the sacred mountain, and another group is coming along the road from the tree where people talk with the spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Ke Gaal gagblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, amewoe. Wole ɖiɖim tso toa tame, eye aʋalɔgo ɖeka to afatɔwo ƒe logoti gbɔ mɔ!”

english_verse: Then Zebul replied, “What good is all of your bragging now? You were the one who said Abimelech shouldn't be the ruler of Shechem. Out there is the army that you made fun of. So go out and fight them!”
translation_verse: Tete Zebul gblɔ nɛ be: “Menye wòe le nu me ɖim le gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Ame kae nye Abimelex be míasubɔe’ o mahã? Aʋakɔ si ŋu nèle alɔ me ɖem le lae nye esi. Ho azɔ nàyi ɖakpe aʋa kpli wo.”

english_verse: Gaal and the leaders of Shechem went out and fought Abimelech.
translation_verse: Tete Gaal ho dze ŋgɔ na Sixemtɔwo, eye wowɔ aʋa kple Abimelex.

english_verse: Soon the people of Shechem turned and ran back into the town. However, Abimelech and his troops were close behind and killed many of them along the way.
translation_verse: Ke Gaal sí, eye Abimelex nyàe ɖe nu va se ɖe agboa nu. Ame geɖe xɔ abi.

english_verse: Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
translation_verse: Abimelex tsi Aruma, eye wònɔ afi ma, ke Zebul nyà Gaal kple nɔviawo ale be womegate ŋu nɔ Sixem o.

english_verse: The next morning, the people of Shechem were getting ready to work in their fields as usual, but someone told Abimelech about it.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, amewo yi agble, eye ame aɖewo yi ɖagblɔe na Abimelex.

english_verse: Abimelech divided his army into three groups and set up an ambush in the fields near Shechem. When the people came out of the town, he and his army rushed out from their hiding places and attacked.
translation_verse: Ekplɔ eƒe aʋakɔ la, eye wòma wo ɖe aʋalɔgo etɔ̃ me. Azɔ la, woyi ɖade xa ɖe gbe me. Esi wòkpɔ amewo do tso dua me gbɔna la, edo ɖe wo ŋu, eye wòwu wo.

english_verse: Abimelech and the troops with him ran to the town gate and took control of it, while two other groups attacked and killed the people who were in the fields.
translation_verse: Abimelex kple eƒe aʋalɔgo la va xe dua ƒe agbo nu, eye aʋalɔgo eve yi ɖadze ame siwo le agble la dzi, eye wowu wo.

english_verse: He and his troops fought in Shechem all day, until they had killed everyone in town. Then he and his men tore down the houses and buildings and scattered salt everywhere.
translation_verse: Emegbe Abimelex wɔ aʋa kple dua ŋkeke blibo la. Exɔ du la, eye wòwu emenɔlawo katã. Egbã dua nyànyanya, eye wòwu dze ɖe edzi.

english_verse: Earlier that day, the leaders of the temple of El Berith at Shechem had heard about the attack. So they went into the temple fortress,
translation_verse: Esi ame siwo le mɔ́ sesẽ si le Sixem me la se nu si dzɔ la, woyi ɖage ɖe mɔ́ si le mawu Berit ƒeme la me.

english_verse: but Abimelech found out where they were.
translation_verse: Amewo yi ɖagblɔe na Abimelex be ameawo ƒo ƒu ɖe afi ma,

english_verse: He led his troops to Mount Zalmon, where he took an ax and chopped off a tree branch. He lifted the branch onto his shoulder and shouted, “Hurry! Cut off a branch just as I did.”
translation_verse: ale wòkplɔ eƒe aʋakɔ la yi ɖe Zalmon-to dzi. Azɔ etsɔ fia lã atilɔ da ɖe abɔ. Egblɔ na eƒe amewo be: “Nu si mewɔ miekpɔ la, miawo hã miwɔe enumake.”

english_verse: When they all had branches, they followed Abimelech back to Shechem. They piled the branches against the fortress and set them on fire, burning down the fortress and killing about
translation_verse: Tete ame sia ame le aʋakɔ blibo la me lã atilɔ ɖe asi, eye wodze Abimelex yome. Wova kɔ wo ɖe mɔ́ la ŋu, eye wotɔ dzo mɔ́ la. Ale ame siwo katã le Sixem-mɔ́ la me la hã ku; woade ame akpe ɖeka, ŋutsuwo kple nyɔnuwo siaa.

english_verse: After destroying Shechem, Abimelech went to Thebez. He surrounded the town and captured it.
translation_verse: Emegbe Abimelex ho yi ɖatu Tebez. Eƒo xlã dua, eye wòxɔe.

english_verse: But there was a tall fortress in the middle of the town, and the town leaders and everyone else went inside. Then they barred the gates and went up to the flat roof.
translation_verse: Mɔ́ sesẽ aɖe le dua titina eye dua me tɔwo katã, ŋutsuwo kple nyɔnuwo siaa, sí yi afi ma. Wodo ʋɔ ɖe wo ɖokui nu, eye wode mɔ́ la tame.

english_verse: Abimelech and his army rushed to the fortress and tried to force their way inside. Abimelech himself was about to set the heavy wooden doors on fire,
translation_verse: Abimelex te ɖe mɔ́ la ŋu be yeawɔ aʋa kple emenɔlawo, eye wòva kekeke mɔ́ la ƒe agbo nu be yeatɔ dzoe.

english_verse: when a woman on the roof dropped a large rock on his head and cracked his skull.
translation_verse: Tete nyɔnu aɖe da tevi tso dzi wova dze ta na Abimelex hegbã ta nɛ.

english_verse: The soldier who carried his weapons was nearby, and Abimelech told him, “Take out your sword and kill me. I don't want people to say that I was killed by a woman!” So the soldier ran his sword through Abimelech.
translation_verse: Eyɔ eƒe adekplɔvi enumake gblɔ nɛ be: “He wò yi ɖe go nàwumee, ne womagagblɔ le ŋunye be nyɔnue wum o!” Tete eƒe adekplɔvi la tɔ hɛe wòku.

english_verse: And when the Israelite soldiers saw that their leader was dead, they went back home.
translation_verse: Esi Israeltɔwo kpɔ be Abimelex ku la, ame sia ame gbugbɔ yi eƒeme.

english_verse: That's how God punished Abimelech for killing his brothers and bringing shame on his father's family.
translation_verse: Aleae Mawu ɖo Abimelex ƒe nu vlo si wòwɔ ɖe tɔ́a ŋu hewu nɔvia bla adrẽ la teƒe nɛ.

english_verse: God also punished the people of Shechem for helping Abimelech. Everything happened just as Jotham's curse said it would.
translation_verse: Mawu na Sixemtɔwo kpe fu vevie le woƒe ŋutasesẽ ta. Ale Yotam, Gideon vi, ƒe fiƒode la ɖi wo ŋu.

english_verse: Tola was the next person to rescue Israel. He belonged to the Issachar tribe, but he lived in Shamir, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His father was Puah, and his grandfather was Dodo.
translation_verse: Le Abimelex ƒe ku megbe la, Tola, Pua vi, ame si nye Dodo tɔgbuiyɔvi la do va xɔ na Israel. Etso Isaxar-to la me, eye wònɔ Samir le Efrayim-tonyigba la dzi.

english_verse: The next leader of Israel was Jair, who lived in Gilead. He was a leader for
translation_verse: Le Tola megbe la, Yair si tso Gilead do. Eya kplɔ Israel-dukɔ ƒe bla eve vɔ eve.

english_verse: Before long, the Israelites began disobeying the Lord by worshiping Baal, Astarte, and gods from Syria, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, and Philistia.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Israelviwo gawɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi si medze Aƒetɔ ŋu o. Wosubɔ Baalwo kple Astarot. Hekpe ɖe mawu siawo ŋu la, wosubɔ Siriatɔwo, Sidontɔwo, Moabtɔwo, Amon viwo kple Filistitɔwo ƒe mawuwo. Ale wogblẽ Aƒetɔ ɖi, eye womegasubɔnɛ kura o.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and decided to let Philistia and Ammon conquer them.
translation_verse: Ðe esia ta, Aƒetɔ do dziku ɖe wo ŋu, eye wòna Filistitɔwo kple Amon viwo ɖu wo dzi.

english_verse: So the same year that Jair died, Israel's army was crushed by these two nations. For
translation_verse: Wote Israelvi siwo katã nɔ Yordan-tɔsisi la ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome, le Gilead le Amoritɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi la ɖe anyi, eye wosẽ ŋuta le wo ŋu ƒe wui enyi sɔŋ.

english_verse: The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Tete Gileadtɔwo kple woƒe kplɔlawo bia wo nɔewo be: “Ame kae adze ŋgɔ akpe aʋa kple Amon viwo? Ame si dze ŋgɔ la, eyae lava zu tatɔ na ame sia ame le Gilead.”

english_verse: Then the Ammonites began crossing the Jordan and attacking the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Life was miserable for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Amon viwo ya tso Yordan-tɔsisi la kura gɔ̃, eye wova wɔ aʋa kple Yuda, Benyamin kple Efrayim toawo me tɔwo. Ale wɔ Israel ɖo xaxa dziŋɔ aɖe me.

english_verse: They begged the Lord for help and confessed, “We were unfaithful to you, our Lord. We stopped worshiping you and started worshiping idols of Baal.”
translation_verse: Tete Israelviwo do ɣli yɔ Aƒetɔ. Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Míewɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò; míegblẽ wò, míaƒe Mawu la ɖi hesubɔ Baalwo.”

english_verse: But I'm not going to rescue you any more! You've left me and gone off to worship other gods. If you're in such big trouble, go and cry to them for help!
translation_verse: Mawu siwo mietia la, miyi ɖado ɣli miayɔ wo. Miyɔ wo ne woava xɔ na mi le miaƒe xaxaɣi.”

english_verse: “We have been unfaithful to you,” the Israelites admitted. “If we must be punished, do it yourself, but please rescue us from the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Ke Israelviwo gblɔ na Aƒetɔ be: “Míewɔ nuvɔ̃. Nu si dze ŋuwò la, wɔ mí faa. Míeɖe kuku, xɔ na mí egbe godoo.”

english_verse: Then the Israelites got rid of the idols of the foreign gods, and they began worshiping only the Lord. Finally, there came a time when the Lord could no longer stand to see them suffer. The Ammonites Invade Gilead
translation_verse: Ale woɖe mawu bubuawo ɖa le wo dome, eye wosubɔ Aƒetɔ. Esia ta fu siwo kpem Israelviwo le la mena Aƒetɔ ɖe dzi ɖi o.

english_verse: The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp. The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there.
translation_verse: Azɔ Amon viwo kpe ta, eye wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Gilead. Nenema ke Israelviwo hã kpe ta, eye wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Mizpa le Gilead-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: “Please come back to Gilead! If you lead our army, we will be able to fight off the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na Yefta be: “Va nye míaƒe aʋakplɔla, ne míawɔ aʋa kple Amon viwo.”

english_verse: “Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
translation_verse: Ke Yefta ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Mielé fum vevie henyàm do goe tso tɔ́nye ƒeme. Nu ka ta miava nɔ diyem esime mieɖo xaxa me?”

english_verse: “But we do want you to come back,” the leaders said. “And if you lead us in battle against the Ammonites, we will make you the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Ame tsitsiawo gblɔ na Yefta be: “Esia ta tututue míeva be míakpɔ wò ɖo. Míedi be nàyi kpli mí, míaɖawɔ aʋa kple Amon viwo. Emegbe la, nàzu Gileadtɔwo katã kplɔla.”

english_verse: “All right,” Jephthah said. “If I go back with you and the Lord lets me defeat the Ammonites, will you really make me your ruler?”
translation_verse: Yefta gblɔ na wo be: “Ne miekplɔm meyi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Amon viwo, eye Aƒetɔ na meɖu dzi la, ekema manye miaƒe tatɔ.”

english_verse: “You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
translation_verse: Ame tsitsiawo ɖo eŋu be: “Míelɔ̃ ɖe wò nya la dzi. Míaƒe ɖasefoe nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
translation_verse: Ale Yefta yi kple ame tsitsiawo, eye wona wòzu woƒe tatɔ kple wo kplɔla. Yefta gblɔ eƒe nyawo katã le Aƒetɔ ŋkume le Mizpa.

english_verse: After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
translation_verse: Yefta dɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Amon viwo ƒe fia gbɔ be woabia be: “Dzre ka le mía dome? Nu ka ta nètso ɖe ŋunye be yeawɔ aʋa kple nye dukɔ?”

english_verse: The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
translation_verse: Amon viwo ƒe fia gblɔ na Yefta ƒe amedɔdɔawo be: “Esime Israel-dukɔ tso Egipte va la, exɔ nye anyigba. Anyigba si wòxɔ la tso Arnon-tɔsisi la nu va se ɖe Yabok-tɔsisi kple Yordan-tɔsisi nu. Eya ta azɔ la, gbugbɔe nam kpoo!”

english_verse: Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon,
translation_verse: Yefta gadɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Amon viwo ƒe fia gbɔ ake.

english_verse: and they told him that Jephthah had said: Israel hasn't taken any territory from Moab or Ammon.
translation_verse: Egblɔ ɖo ɖee be: “Nye Yefta ŋutɔe le nya sia gblɔm: Israel-dukɔ la mexɔ anyigba aɖeke le Moabtɔwo kple Amonviwo si o.

english_verse: When the Israelites came from Egypt, they traveled across the desert to the Red Sea and then to Kadesh.
translation_verse: Nya lae nye be esi Israel-dukɔ tso Egipte gbɔna la, woto gbedadaƒo va Aƒlaƒu la nu va ɖo Kades.

english_verse: They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
translation_verse: Wodɔ ame ɖo ɖe Edom-fia be wòaɖe mɔ yewoato eƒe anyigba dzi ayi. Ke egbe. Wodɔ ame ɖo ɖe Moab-fia hã gbɔ; ke eya hã gbe. Ale wɔ Israel-dukɔ la tsi Kades.

english_verse: A little later, the Israelites set out into the desert, going east of Edom and Moab, and camping on the eastern side of the Arnon River gorge. The Arnon is the eastern border of Moab, and since the Israelites didn't cross it, they didn't even set foot in Moab.
translation_verse: Emegbe la, woto gbedadaƒo heƒo xlã Edom-nyigba kple Moab-nyigba va se ɖe esime wova ɖo Moab-nyigba ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome le Arnon-tɔsisi ƒe go kemɛ dzi. Woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe afi ma, ke womeva Moab-nyigba dzi o, elabe Arnon-tɔsisi lae do liƒo na Moab-nyigba.

english_verse: The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Israelviwo dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Amoritɔwo ƒe fia Sixon si nɔ Xesbon la gbɔ, be wòaɖe mɔ na yewo ne yewoato eƒe anyigba dzi ayi va se ɖe esime yewode afi si yewoyina.

english_verse: towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more. Jephthah's Daughter
translation_verse: Ke Sixon meka ɖe Israelviwo dzi ne wòana woato eƒe anyigba dzi ayi o. Ale Sixon ƒo eƒe aʋakɔwo katã nu ƒu, eye wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Yoza heho aʋa ɖe Israelviwo ŋu.

english_verse: But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived,
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu la na Israelviwo ɖu Sixon kple eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la dzi, eye woxɔ Amoritɔ siwo nye anyigbadzitɔwo la ƒe anyigba blibo la wòzu wo tɔ.

english_verse: from the Arnon River in the south to the Jabbok River in the north, and from the desert in the east to the Jordan River in the west.
translation_verse: Woxɔ Amoritɔwo ƒe anyigba blibo la tso Arnon-tɔsisi la nu le anyigbeme va se ɖe Yabok-tɔsisi la nu le dzigbeme, eye wògatso gbedadaƒo le ɣedzeƒe gome va se ɖe Yordan-tɔsisi la nu le ɣetoɖoƒe gome.

english_verse: The messengers also told the king of Ammon that Jephthah had said: The Lord God of Israel helped his nation get rid of the Amorites and take their land. Now do you think you're going to take over that same territory?
translation_verse: Ale wɔ Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu la nyà Amoritɔwo ɖa le eƒe dukɔ la ŋgɔ, hexɔ woƒe anyigba la le wo si. Nu ka ta wò ya nèbe yeaxɔe azɔ?

english_verse: If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
translation_verse: Nu si wò mawu Kemos tsɔ na wò la, malée ɖe asi oa? Ke dukɔ siwo katã Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la nyà ɖa le mía ŋgɔ la ƒe anyigba ya mía tɔe.

english_verse: Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
translation_verse: Wòe de ŋgɔ wu Moab-fia Balak, Zipor vi la? Etsi tre ɖe Israel-dukɔ la ŋu kpɔa? Ewɔ aʋa kplii kpɔa?

english_verse: I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
translation_verse: Nyemewɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke ɖe ŋuwò o. Nu ka ta wò ya nèwɔ vɔ̃ ɖe ŋunye heho aʋa ɖe ŋunye? Aƒetɔ ye nye ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la. Adrɔ̃e na Israelviwo kple Amon viwo egbe ɖeka.”

english_verse: But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
translation_verse: Ke Amon viwo ƒe fia metsɔ ɖeke le Yefta ƒe nya la me o.

english_verse: Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe Gbɔgbɔ va Yefta dzi. Eto Gilead kple Manase va do ɖe Mizpa le Gilead, eye wòho tso afi ma va ɖo Amon viwo gbɔ.

english_verse: he promised the Lord, “If you will let me defeat the Ammonites
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Yefta ɖe adzɔgbe na Aƒetɔ gblɔ be: “Ne èna meɖu Amon viwo dzi nyateƒe,

english_verse: and come home safely, I will sacrifice to you whoever comes out to meet me first.”
translation_verse: eye metrɔ gbɔ tso wo dziɖuƒe dedie la, nu sia nu si ado tso nye aƒeme ava kpem gbã la, anye tɔwò. Mamèe atsɔ asa vɔe na wò.”

english_verse: From Mizpah, Jephthah attacked the Ammonites, and the Lord helped him defeat them.
translation_verse: Ale Yefta tso tɔsisi la hekpe aʋa kple Amon viwo, eye Aƒetɔ na wòɖu wo dzi.

english_verse: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
translation_verse: Esi Yefta gbɔ va wo de Mizpa la, via nyɔnuvi le axatsɛ ƒom le ɣe ɖum va kpee. Eya koe nye vi ɖeka hɔ̃ si le esi, vi bubu aɖeke megale esi o.

english_verse: “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
translation_verse: Esi Yefta kpɔe la, edze awu le eɖokui ŋu gblɔ be: “Ao, vinye! Èdo nublanuitɔm. Èdem xaxa gã aɖe me. Nye ŋutɔe ke nu ɖe adzɔgbe na Aƒetɔ; nyemagate ŋu atrɔe o.”

english_verse: “Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die.
translation_verse: Egblɔ na tɔ́a be: “Tɔ́nye, ne ènyake nu ɖe adzɔgbe na Aƒetɔ ko la, ekema ale si nègblɔ nɛ be yeawɔm la, wɔm faa, elabe Aƒetɔ bia hlɔ̃ wò futɔ siwo nye Amon viwo la na wò.”

english_verse: But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
translation_verse: Eyi edzi gblɔ na tɔ́a be: “Medi be nàwɔ nu ɖeka ko nam: ‘Ðe mɔ nam ɣleti eve manɔ ɖokuinye si, ne nye kple xɔ̃nyewo míayi towo dzi aɖatsa, afa nye ɖetugbi leaƒe nyenye.’ ”

english_verse: “Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said. She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children.
translation_verse: Tɔ́a ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Yi!” Ale wòɖe mɔ nɛ ɣleti eve, eye eya kple xɔlɔ̃awo yi towo dzi ɖatsa hefa ale si wònye ɖetugbi leaƒe hafi le kuku ge lae.

english_verse: Then she went back to her father. He did what he had promised, and she never got married. That's why
translation_verse: Esi ɣleti evea wu enu la, egbugbɔ va tɔ́a gbɔ. Ale si wòɖe adzɔgbe be yeawɔe la, ewɔe nenema pɛpɛpɛ. Ke ŋutsu aɖeke mede asi eŋu kpɔ hafi wòku o. Nuwɔna sia trɔ zu kɔnu le Israel-dukɔ me,

english_verse: every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_verse: be Israel vinyɔnuviwo yina ɖafaa konyi na Gileadtɔ, Yefta vinyɔnu la ŋkeke ene ƒè sia ƒè.

english_verse: The men of the Ephraim tribe got together an army and went across the Jordan River to Zaphon to meet with Jephthah. They said, “Why did you go to war with the Ammonites without asking us to help? Just for that, we're going to burn down your house with you inside!”
translation_verse: Efrayimtɔwo ho aʋa. Wotso Yordan-tɔsisi la va Zafon, eye wogblɔ na Yefta be: “Nu ka ta nèho aʋa ɖe Amon viwo ŋu, eye mèyɔ mí ne míakplɔ wò ayi o? Míele dzo tɔ ge wò xɔ ɖe dziwò!”

english_verse: “But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us.
translation_verse: Yefta gblɔ na wo be: “Mía kple nye dukɔ míewɔ aʋa dziŋɔ aɖe kple Amon viwo, medo gbe mi baa, gake mieva xɔ nam o.

english_verse: So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
translation_verse: Esi mekpɔ be miele xɔxɔ ge nam o la, metsɔ nye agbe ke heho ge ɖe woƒe anyigba me, eye Aƒetɔ na meɖu wo dzi. Ale ke wɔ mietso ɖe ŋunye egbea be yewoawɔ aʋa kplim?”

english_verse: But the men from Ephraim said, “You people of Gilead are nothing more than refugees from Ephraim. You even live on land that belongs to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.” So Jephthah called together the army of Gilead, then they attacked and defeated the army from Ephraim.
translation_verse: Tete Yefta ƒo Gileadtɔwo katã nu ƒu, eye wòyi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Efrayimtɔwo heɖu wo dzi elabe Efrayimtɔwo gblɔna be: “Gileadtɔwo, ame dzegowo mienye le Efrayim kple Manase dome.”

english_verse: The army of Gilead also posted guards at all the places where the soldiers from Ephraim could cross the Jordan River to return to their own land. Whenever one of the men from Ephraim would try to cross the river, the guards would say, “Are you from Ephraim?” “No,” the man would answer, “I'm not from Ephraim.”
translation_verse: Gileadtɔwo yi ɖaxe Yordan-tɔsisi la tsoƒewo na Efrayimtɔwo. Ne Efrayimtɔ aɖe le sísim va ɖo tɔtsoƒea la, ebiaa mɔ be yeatso tɔ la. Gileadtɔwo bianɛ be: “Efrayimtɔwo nènyea?” Eɖoa eŋu be: “Gbeɖe!”

english_verse: The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.” If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether,
translation_verse: Wogblɔna nɛ be: “Gblɔ be Sibolet!” Ke eya gblɔna be Zibolet, elabe menyà eyɔyɔ nyuie o. Enumake wolénɛ, eye wowunɛ ɖe tɔtsoƒe la le Yordan-tɔsisi la nu. Ale wowu Efrayimtɔ ame akpe bla ene vɔ eve le ɣe ma ɣi me.

english_verse: Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead. Ibzan
translation_verse: Yefta kplɔ Israel-dukɔ la ƒe ade. Emegbe la, eku, eye woɖii ɖe wo dedu me le Gilead. Ibzan, Elon kple Abdon

english_verse: Ibzan, the next leader of Israel, came from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Le Yefta yome la, Ibzan ame si tso Betlehem la kplɔ Israel-dukɔ la.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Bethlehem. Elon
translation_verse: Emegbe la, eku, eye woɖii ɖe Betlehem.

english_verse: Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years,
translation_verse: Le Ibzan yome la, Elon, ame si tso Zebulon la va kplɔ Israel-dukɔ la ƒè ewo.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe. Abdon
translation_verse: Emegbe la, eku, eye woɖii ɖe Ayalon le Zebulon-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Abdon the son of Hillel was the next leader of Israel. He had
translation_verse: Emegbe la, Abdon ku, eye woɖii ɖe Piraton le Efrayim-nyigba dzi le Amalekitɔwo ƒe to dzi.

english_verse: Once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let the Philistines take control of Israel for
translation_verse: Azɔ Israelviwo gawɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu, eya ta wòna Filistitɔwo ɖu wo dzi ƒe bla ene.

english_verse: Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children,
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, ŋutsu aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Manoax la tso Zora, eye wòle Dan ƒomea me. Srɔ̃a nye konɔ.

english_verse: She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name,
translation_verse: Tete nyɔnu la yi ɖagblɔ na srɔ̃a be: “Mawu ƒe ame aɖe va gbɔnye. Ele abe mawudɔla ene, eye ŋɔdzi le eŋu ŋutɔ. Ke nyemebia afi si wòtso o, eye meyɔ eŋkɔ hã nam o,

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: Ke egblɔ nam be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa èle fu fɔ ge adzi ŋutsuvi, eya ta mègano wain alo aha sesẽ aɖeke o; mègaɖu nu makɔmakɔ aɖeke hã o, elabe ŋutsuvi la anye vi si ŋu Mawu kɔ̀ tso nɔa ƒe dɔme ke va se ɖe eƒe kugbe.’ ”

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Tete Manoax do gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, meɖe kuku, na Mawu ƒe ame si nèdɔ ɖa la, nagava mía gbɔ zi ɖeka, bene wòava fia nu si míawɔ na ɖevi si woadzi na mí la, mí.”

english_verse: God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time,
translation_verse: Mawu se Manoax ƒe gbedodoɖa la. Esi Manoax srɔ̃ bɔbɔ nɔ anyi ɖe agble me la, mawudɔla la gava egbɔ, ke srɔ̃a Manoax menɔ egbɔ hafi o.

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Ale nyɔnua ƒu du enumake yi ɖagblɔ na srɔ̃a be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsu si va gbɔnye gbe ma gbe la gava!”

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Manoax tso dze nyɔnua yome. Esi wova ŋutsua gbɔ la, ebiae be: “Wòe nye ame si ƒo nu kple nyɔnu sia?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Ẽ, nyee.”

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Azɔ Manoax biae be: “Ne wò nya la va eme la, ale ke ɖevia ava nɔ agbee? Nu ka wòava wɔ?”

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: Mawudɔla la ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Nu siwo katã megblɔ na srɔ̃wò be newɔ la, nekpɔ egbɔ be yewɔ wo pɛpɛpɛ.

english_verse: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
translation_verse: Megaɖu wainkanu aɖeke o. Megano wain alo aha muame aɖeke o. Nenema ke megaɖu nu makɔmakɔ aɖeke hã o. Newɔ se siwo katã mede nɛ la dzi.”

english_verse: “Please,” Manoah said, “stay here with us for just a little while, and we'll fix a young goat for you to eat.”
translation_verse: Tete Manoax gblɔ na Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla la be: “Taflatsɛ, na míasika wò ɖi vie. Míedi be míawu gbɔ̃vi aɖe na wò.”

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla la ɖo eŋu na Manoax be: “Ne èsikam ɖi hã la, nyemaɖu miaƒe nuɖuɖua o. Evɔ nenye be numemevɔ nèdi be yeasa la, ekema mèe nàtsɔ sa vɔe na Aƒetɔ.” Ke Manoax medze sii be Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla wònye o.

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Manoax biae be: “Ŋkɔwò ɖe? Míedi be ne wò nya la va eme la, míade bubu ŋuwò.”

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Mawudɔla la bia be: “Nu ka ta nèle nye ŋkɔ biam? Mènya be ŋkɔ wɔnuku wònye oa?”

english_verse: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
translation_verse: Esi dzo ƒe aɖewo de dzi le vɔsamlekpuia dzi la, Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla to vɔsamlekpui la ƒe dzo ƒe aɖeawo me yi dzi le Manoax kple srɔ̃a ŋkume wokpɔ. Tete wotsyɔ mo anyi.

english_verse: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla megaɖe eɖokui fia Manoax kple srɔ̃a kpɔ o. Azɔ Manoax dze sii be Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla wònye.

english_verse: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
translation_verse: Manoax gblɔ na srɔ̃a be: “Míele kuku ge, elabe míekpɔ Mawu!”

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: Ke srɔ̃a ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Ne Aƒetɔ ɖe wòdi be yeawu mí la, anye ne mexɔ míaƒe numemevɔsa kple nuɖuɖuvɔsa la o. Gawu la, anye ne mena míekpɔ nu siawo alo gblɔ nu siwo míese la fifia o.”

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Emegbe nyɔnu la dzi ŋutsuvi, eye wòna ŋkɔe be Simson. Ðevia va tsi, eye Aƒetɔ yrae.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe Gbɔgbɔ de asi dɔwɔwɔ me le eme le Dan ƒe asaɖa si le Zora kple Estaol dome la me.

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Simson yi Timna gbe ɖeka, eye wòkpɔ Filisti-nyɔnua aɖe le afi ma.

english_verse: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Esi wògbɔ va aƒe la, egblɔ na tɔ́a kple nɔa be: “Mekpɔ nyɔnu aɖe le Filisti-nyɔnuwo dome le Timna. Medi be mia bia eta nam.”

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Ke tɔ́a kple nɔa biae be: “Nu ka ta nèdi be yeayi aɖaɖe srɔ̃ tso Filistitɔ bolobolotɔwo dome? Ðe mèkpɔ nyɔnu aɖeke aɖe le nɔviwòwo vinyɔnuwo dome alo tso dukɔ blibo la dome o taea?” Ke Simson gblɔ na tɔ́a be: “Bia eta nam maɖe; eya ƒe nue lé dzi nam.”

english_verse: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
translation_verse: Ke tɔ́a kple nɔa medze sii be Aƒetɔ ye de susua tame nɛ o, elabe Aƒetɔ nɔ mɔnu dim le Filistitɔwo ŋu be yeaho aʋa ɖe wo ŋu. Ɣe ma ɣi la, Filistitɔwoe nɔ Israelviwo dzi ɖum.

english_verse: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
translation_verse: Ale Simson kple tɔ́a kpakple nɔa yi ɖe Timna. Esime wonɔ Timnatitɔwo ƒe waingblewo me tom yina la, dzatavi aɖe nɔ xɔxlɔ̃m va do goe.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe Gbɔgbɔ ɖo Simson me kple ŋusẽ, eye wòfé dzatavi la kple asi ɖeɖe abe ale si woféa gbɔ̃vi ene. Ke megblɔ nu si wòwɔ la na tɔ́a kple nɔa o.

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, eyi ɖaƒo nu kple nyɔnua, eye eƒe nu nyo Simson ŋu.

english_verse: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke aɖewo megbe la, eyi be yeakplɔ nyɔnua. Le mɔa dzi la, edze to afi si wòwu dzata la le be yeakpɔe ɖa. Kpɔ ɖa, anyi ɖa ɖe dɔme na dzata kuku la.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: Eɖee ɖe asi nɔ nyinyim va tɔ́a kple nɔa gbɔ. Ena ɖe woawo hã wonyi, ke Simson megblɔ na wo be dzata kuku ƒe dɔmee yeɖe anyitsi la tsoe o.

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: Simson tɔ́ yi nyɔnuvia ƒeme, eye Simson ɖo nuɖukplɔ̃ na ɖekakpui siwo le dua me, elabe nenemae ɖekakpuiwo wɔna le woƒe kɔnu nu le afi ma.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Esi Filistitɔwo kpɔe la, woɖe ɖekakpuivi bla etɔ̃ siwo nye ehatiwo la be woanɔ eŋu.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: Evɔ ne miete ŋu ɖe egɔme nam o la, ekema miawo miatsɔ awutewui bla etɔ̃ kple atsyɔ̃ɖowu bla etɔ̃ nam.” Wogblɔ be: “To wò adzo la! Toe míase!”

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: Simson gblɔ be: “Nuɖuɖu do tso nuɖula la me; nu vivi aɖe do tso ŋusẽtɔ la me.” Ŋkeke etɔ̃ sɔŋ va yi wode adzo la gɔme ɖe ge do kpo.

english_verse: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke enea gbe la, ɖekakpuiawo gblɔ na Simson srɔ̃ be: “Ble srɔ̃wò nu ne wòaɖe adzo la gɔme na mí. Ne menye nenema o la, míatɔ dzo wò kple tɔ́wò ƒe aƒe. Alo ɖe miekpe mí vɛ be yewoawɔ mí míazu ame dahewoa?”

english_verse: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
translation_verse: Tete Simson srɔ̃ fa avi nɛ gblɔ be: “Èlém ɖe dɔme! Mèlɔ̃m kura o! Èto adzo na mía deviwo, ke ègbe egɔmeɖeɖe nam.” Egblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, nyemeɖe egɔme na tɔ́nye kple nɔnye kura gɔ̃ hã o. Nu ka ta wòle be maɖe egɔme na wò ɖo?”

english_verse: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
translation_verse: Ke ele avia fafa dzi le srɔ̃ɖeŋkeke adrẽawo katã ɖuɖu me. Mlɔeba le ŋkeke adrẽa gbe la, eva ɖe egɔme nɛ elabe fuɖeɖe la va gloe. Ale nyɔnua yi ɖagblɔe na wo deviawo.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke adrẽa gbe hafi ɣe naɖo to la, dua me ŋutsuwo va gblɔ na Simson be: “Nu ka ate ŋu avivi wu anyitsi? Nu ka ate ŋu asesẽ wu dzata?” Simson ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Ne ɖe menye nye nyinɔe lae mietsɔ ŋlɔ agblee o la, anye ne miete ŋu ɖe nye adzo la gɔme o.”

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Azɔ wotsɔ Simson srɔ̃ la na exɔlɔ̃ si wòdi wònɔ eŋu kplíkplikpli le srɔ̃ɖeŋkekea ɖuɖu me la, wòɖe.

english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ na Simson be: “Nye ya mebu be mègadi eƒe nya aɖeke kura o, eya ta metsɔe na xɔ̃wò la. Eƒe tsɛ dze tugbe wui. Taflatsɛ, xɔ eya ɖe eteƒe boŋ.”

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Simson gblɔ be: “Fifia ya la, ne mehe dzɔgbevɔ̃e va Filistitɔwo dzi la, tɔnye dzɔ.”

english_verse: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
translation_verse: Etɔ dzo akakatiawo nu eye wòɖe asi le abeiawo ŋu ɖo ɖe Filistitɔwo ƒe agblewo me. To mɔ sia nu la, Simson tɔ dzo lu siwo woxa kple esiwo womexa o kpakple amiti siwo le abɔwo me.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Esi Filistitɔwo bia ame si wɔ nua la ta se la, wose be Simson ye wɔe, elabe toa xɔ srɔ̃a le esi tsɔ na Simson ŋutɔ xɔlɔ̃. Tete Filistitɔwo tɔ dzo nyɔnua kple tɔ́a siaa.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Simson gblɔ na wo be: “Ne miewɔ alea hã la, mabia hlɔ̃ mi kokoko hafi adzo!”

english_verse: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
translation_verse: Elũ ɖe wo dzi eye wòwu wo dometɔ geɖe nyamanyama. Emegbe la, edzo yi ɖanɔ agado aɖe me le to aɖe me le Etam. Simson ɖu Filistitɔwo dzi

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Azɔ Filistitɔwo ho va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Yuda, eye woxa Lexi-dua.

english_verse: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?” The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
translation_verse: Tete Yuda-ŋutsuwo bia wo be: “Nu ka ta mieva xa mí?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Simson lé ge míeva abla, ne míawɔe abe ale si wòwɔ mí ene.”

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Ale Yuda-ŋutsu akpe etɔ̃ yi ɖe agado la me le Etam, eye wogblɔ na Simson be: “Mènyae be Filistitɔwoe le mía dzi ɖum oa? Nu ka nye esi nèwɔ ɖe mía ŋu?” Eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Nu si wowɔ nam la, eya tututu nye hã mewɔ na wo.”

english_verse: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Ðe míeva be míalé wò abla aɖade Filistitɔwo si.” Simson gblɔ na wo be: “Mika atam tsɔ ɖo kpe edzi nam be menye miawo ŋutɔe be yewoawum o.”

english_verse: After the fighting was over, he made up this poem about what he had done to the Philistines: I used a donkey's jawbone to kill a thousand men; I beat them with this jawbone over and over again.
translation_verse: Ale Simson dzi ha be: “Tedzi ƒe glã metsɔ wu ame akpee! Tedzi ƒe glãe metsɔ li kɔ woe gleglegle!”

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: Esi wòdzi ha la vɔ la, etsɔ tedziglã la ƒu gbe. Wona ŋkɔ teƒe ma be Glãtogbɛ si woyɔna le Hebri-gbe me be: Ramat-Lexi.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Tete tsikɔ wui vevie, ale wòdo ɣli yɔ Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Èto nye, wò dɔla dzi na meɖu dzi nukutɔe. Azɔ la, tsikɔe lawum maku, eye mage ɖe Filistitɔ bolobolotɔ siawo si mea?”

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Tete Mawu fé teƒe globo aɖe si le Lexi eye tsi do le eme wòno. Esi agbe gaɖo eme la, eƒe lã me kɔ. Esia ta wona ŋkɔ teƒe ma be En-Hakore. Egale Lexi-du me va se ɖe egbe.

english_verse: years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_verse: Simson kplɔ Israel-dukɔ la le Filistitɔwo ƒe dziɖuɣi ƒe bla eve sɔŋ.

english_verse: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
translation_verse: Wofi tofi na Gazatɔwo be Simson le dua me, eya ta woɖe to ɖe teƒea, eye wode xa ɖe dua ƒe agbo nu nɛ zã blibo la katã. Wozi ɖoɖoe toŋ zã blibo la nɔ gbɔgblɔm be: “Mina míalala va se ɖe esime ŋu nake ne míawui.”

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: Emegbe la, Simson dze ahiã nyɔnu aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Delila, ame si nɔ Sorek-bali la me.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo va nyɔnua gbɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Ble enu, ne wòagblɔ nu si me eƒe ŋusẽ triakɔ la le, ale si míawɔ aɖu edzi ahablae, eye míabɔbɔe ɖe anyi keŋ la, na wò. Mía dome ame sia ame ana klosaloga akpe ɖeka alafa ɖeka wò.”

english_verse: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
translation_verse: Ale Delila gblɔ na Simson be: “Taflatsɛ, nu kae na nèsesẽ alea? Nu ka woatsɔ abla wò ahabɔbɔ wò ɖe anyi? Gblɔe nam.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Simson ɖo eŋu be: “Ne wotsɔ atagbi mumu ka adrẽ blam la, magbɔdzɔ azu abe ame bubu ɖe sia ɖe ene.”

english_verse: The Philistine rulers gave seven new bowstrings to Delilah. They also told some of their soldiers to go to Delilah's house and hide in the room where Samson and Delilah were. If the bowstrings made Samson weak, they would be able to capture him. Delilah tied up Samson with the bowstrings and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the bowstrings, as though they were pieces of scorched string. The Philistines had not found out why Samson was so strong.
translation_verse: Ameawo dometɔ aɖewo de xa ɖe xɔ bubu si le wo gbɔ la me. Nyɔnua do ɣli gblɔ nɛ be: “Simson, Filistitɔwo gbɔna!” Ke etso kaawo zi ɖeka abe ale si dzo gbɔna ɖe ɖetika ɖekɛ wòtsona ene. Ale wɔ womekpɔ eƒe ŋusẽ triakɔ la tsoƒe o.

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Delila gblɔ na Simson be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ɖeko nèflum heka aʋatso nam! Meɖe kuku, gblɔ nu si woatsɔ abla wòe la nam dzro!”

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Simson ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Ne wotsɔ ka yeye si wometsɔ bla naneke kpɔ o la blam la, ekema magbɔdzɔ azu abe ame bubu ɖe sia ɖe ene.’

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Tete Delila tsɔ ka yeyewo blae, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Simson, Filistitɔwo gbɔna!” Ke amewo de xa ɖe xɔ bubu si tsɔ ɖe wo gbɔ la me. Tete Simson tso kaawo abe ɖetika ɖeka hɔ̃ ene.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Delila gblɔ na Simson be: “Movitɔ ko nèdom va se ɖe fifi, hele aʋatso kam nam. Gblɔ nu si woatsɔ abla wòe la nam!” Eɖo eŋu be: “Ne èlɔ̃ nye ɖakɔ adrẽawo abe avɔe wotsi ene, eye nèbla wo sesĩe kple ɖablanu la, ekema magbɔdzɔ azu abe ame bubu ɖe sia ɖe ene.”

english_verse: While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
translation_verse: Ale esi Simson dɔ alɔ̃ la, Delila lɔ̃ eƒe ɖakɔ adrẽawo abe avɔe wotsi ene. Ebla wo sesĩe kple ɖablanu, eye wòdo ɣli be: “Simson, Filistitɔwo gbɔna!” Ke Simson nyɔ, eye wòho eƒe ɖa le agbati la me.

english_verse: “Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.”
translation_verse: Nyɔnua gblɔ nɛ be: “Wò nu ko nètsɔ lɔ̃mee; nye nu melé dzi na wò kura o. Zigbɔzi etɔ̃ sɔŋ nye esi nèdo movitɔm, eye mègblɔ nu si me wò ŋusẽ triakɔ la le la nam o.”

english_verse: Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
translation_verse: Nyɔnu la nɔ fu ɖem nɛ nɔ ebiabia dzi gbe sia gbe. Mlɔeba fuɖename la va glo Simson abe wòaku boŋ gɔ̃ hã ene,

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ eƒe dzimenyawo katã na Delila. Ebe: “Talũhɛ mede ta ŋu nam kpɔ o, elabe vi si ŋu wokɔ̀ na Mawu menye tso keke danye ƒe dɔme ke. Ne wolũ ta nam la, ekema ŋusẽ avɔ le ŋunye, eye magbɔdzɔ azu abe ame bubu ɖe sia ɖe ene.”

english_verse: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
translation_verse: Esi Delila kpɔ be egblɔ eƒe dzimenyawo katã na ye azɔ la, edɔ ame ɖo ɖa be woayɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo vɛ. Egblɔ ɖo ɖa be: “Miva azɔ, elabe egblɔ eƒe dzimenyawo katã nam!” Tete Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo va, eye wotsɔ ga la ɖe asi vɛ.

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: Ena Simson dɔ alɔ̃ ɖe eƒe ata dzi, eye wòyɔ ŋutsu aɖe wòva lũ ɖakɔ adrẽawo le eta. Delila de asi nu vevi wɔwɔ Simson me azɔ, elabe ŋusẽ vɔ le eŋu.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo lée, ho eƒe ŋkuwo le tome, eye wokplɔe yi Gaza. Wode akɔblikɔsɔkɔsɔe, eye wona wònɔ wɔ tum le gaxɔ me.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Ke eƒe ɖa gade asi toto me. Simson ƒe ku

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo va kpe ta be yewoasa vɔ na yewoƒe mawu Dagon. Wokpɔ dzidzɔ gbe ma gbe gblɔ be: “Mía mawu na míeɖu míaƒe futɔ Simson dzi!”

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: Simson gblɔ na ŋutsuvi si lé eƒe asi nɔ ekplɔm la be: “Na malé sɔti siwo dzi xɔa nɔ, ne maziɔ ɖe wo ŋu.”

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Tete Simson do gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ be: “Aƒetɔ Mawu, ɖo ŋku dzinye. Gana ŋusẽm zi ɖeka pɛ ko fifia; Mawu, meɖe kuku, ne mabia hlɔ̃ Filistitɔwo ɖe nye ŋku eveawo nu!”

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Ale Simson do asi ɖa lé titinasɔti eve siwo dzi xɔa nɔ la goŋgoŋ; ɖeka ɖe ɖusi, eye evelia ɖe mia, eye wòtutu wo

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: hegblɔ kple ɣli be: “Na maku kple Filistitɔwo!” Ebi eɖokui ŋusẽtɔe tutu sɔtiawo, eye xɔ la mu dze amegãawo kple ame bubuwo katã dzi. Ale ame siwo wòwu le eƒe kuɣi la, sɔ gbɔ wu esiwo wòwu le eƒe agbenɔɣi.

english_verse: His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Azɔ la, nɔviawo kple tɔ́a ƒemetɔwo katã va kɔe dzoe. Woyi ɖaɖii ɖe tɔ́a Manoax ƒe yɔdo me le Zora kple Estaol dome. Ekplɔ Israel-dukɔ la ƒe bla eve.

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: Azɔ la egbugbɔ ga la na nɔa. Ke nɔa ɖe klosaloga alafa eve le eŋu tsɔ yi na klosalonutula, ame si tsɔe tu aklama kpakpɛ kple legbae. Wotsɔ wo yi ɖada ɖe Mixa ƒeme.

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, fia aɖeke menɔ Israel-dukɔ me o; ame sia ame wɔa nu si dze eŋu.

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: Eʋu tso Betlehem le Yuda nɔ afi si wòanɔ la dim. Ezɔ mɔ ʋuu va ɖo Efrayim-tonyigba la dzi, eye wòge ɖe Mixa ƒeme.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Mixa biae be: “Afi ka nètso va?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Levitɔ menye tso Betlehem le Yuda. Ðeko mele tsatsam le afi aɖe dim manɔ.”

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Mixa gblɔ be: “Tsi gbɔnye ne nànye tɔ́ kple nunɔla nam. Maxe klosaloga ewo na wò ƒe sia ƒe. Madi avɔ na wò, eye mana nuɖuɖu wò.”

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Tete Mixa gblɔ be: “Menya azɔ be Aƒetɔ le nana ge be agbenɔnɔ nadze edzi nam, elabe mekpɔ Levitɔ wònye nunɔla nam.”

english_verse: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.
translation_verse: Ɣeyiɣi sia me la, fia aɖeke menɔ Israel-dukɔ la si o. Dan viwo ƒe to la nɔ anyigba dim le ɣeyiɣi sia me be yewoanɔ edzi, elabe anyigba aɖeke mesu wo si abe domenyinu ene le Israel-toawo dome va se ɖe ɣe ma ɣi o.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Ale Dan-to la me tɔwo tia ŋutsu kalẽtɔ atɔ̃ tso woƒe ƒomeawo dome, eye wodɔ wo tso Zora kple Estaol ɖo ɖa be woayi aɖatsa ŋku le anyigba la dzi alé ŋku ɖe eŋu. Wogblɔ na amedɔdɔawo be: “Miyi ɖatsa le anyigba la dzi nyuie.” Esi wova ɖo Efrayim-tonyigba la dzi la, woyi ɖe Mixa ƒeme ɖadze egbɔ.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Esi woɖo Mixa ƒe aƒea gbɔ la, wodze si Levi ɖekakpuia ƒe gbe. Ale wote ɖe eŋu biae be: “Ame ka kplɔ wò va afi siae? Nu ka wɔm nèle le afii? Dɔ ka wɔm nèle?”

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Mixa wɔ nu geɖe nam. Etsɔm meva zu nunɔla nɛ.”

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Míeɖe kuku, bia Mawu se na mí kpɔ be míaƒe mɔzɔzɔ la adze edzi na mí hã?”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Nunɔla la ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Miyi le ŋutifafa me. Aƒetɔ le mia ta kpɔm le mɔzɔzɔ la me.”

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, ŋutsu atɔ̃awo dze mɔ, eye wova Lais-du me. Wokpɔ be ame siwo le afi ma la le tomefafa me eye woɖe dzi ɖi abe Sidontɔwo ene. Ame aɖeke meɖea fu na wo o. Nuwo bɔ ɖe afi ma fũu, kesinɔnuwo le wo si zã, eye naneke mehiãa wo o. Gawu la, wole didiƒe tso Sidontɔwo gbɔ, eye kadodo aɖeke mele woawo kpakple du bubu aɖeke me tɔwo dome o.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Esi amedɔdɔawo gbɔ va wo nɔviwo gbɔ le Zora kple Estaol la, wo nɔviawo bia ale si wode nua gbe la ta se.

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Ne mieyi afi ma la, miakpɔ be ameawo ɖe dzi ɖi. Anyigba la lolo, eye nu sia nu si hiãa ame la le wo gbɔ. Mawu tsɔ anyigba la na mi.”

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Ale ŋutsu alafa ade bla akpa tso Dan-to la me, eye wodze mɔ tso Zora kple Estaol.

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: Woho va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Kiryat-Yearim ƒe ɣetoɖoƒe gome le Yuda. Eya tae woyɔa teƒe ma be Maxanexdan va se ɖe egbe.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Esi woho tso afi ma la, wova Efrayim-tonyigba la dzi, eye woyi ɖe Mixa ƒe aƒe gbɔ.

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu atɔ̃ siwo de ɖatsa ŋku le Lais-nyigba dzi la gblɔ na wo nɔviwo be: “Miawo hã mienya be kɔmewu, aƒeli, aklama kpakpɛ kple legba le aƒe sia mea? Azɔ nu ka miebu be míawɔ?”

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Zi ɖoɖoe! Tsyɔ asi nu! Va mídzo ne nànye mía tɔ́ kple míaƒe nunɔla. Ðe wònyo na wò be nànye nunɔla ɖe ame ɖeka kple eƒe aƒe ɖeɖe ko nu wu, be nànye nunɔla ɖe ƒomewo nu le to aɖe me le Israel-dukɔ mea?”

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Nya la dzɔ dzi na nunɔla la, ale wòxɔ eƒe kɔmewua, aƒelia kple aklama kpakpɛawo, eye wòge ɖe ameawo dome.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Wotrɔ hedze mɔ. Wona ɖeviwo, lãwo kple nu vevitɔwo do ŋgɔ na wo.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Wodzo le Mixa ƒe aƒe gbɔ yi sãa. Tete Mixa yɔ ŋutsu siwo ƒe aƒe te ɖe eƒe aƒe ŋu la ƒo ƒu eye woti Dan viwo yome.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Ŋutsuawo yɔ Dan viawo. Wotrɔ hebia Mixa be: “Nya kae dzɔ hafi nèkplɔ ame siawo gbegbe ɖe asi?”

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Mibiam be nya kae dzɔ hã. Mietsɔ nye mawu si mewɔ hekplɔ nye nunɔla hã kpe ɖe eŋu dzo yinae. Nu kae gasusɔ hafi miebiam be nya ka dzɔ mahã?”

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Ke Dan viwo gblɔ nɛ be: “Ne mèdi be dɔmedzoetɔwo nadze yewo dzi atsrɔ̃ wò kple wò aƒemetɔwo keŋkeŋ o la, ekema zi ɖoɖoe kpoo.”

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Ale Dan viwo gayi woƒe mɔzɔzɔ dzi. Esi Mixa kpɔ be wosẽ wu ye la, etrɔ gbɔ va aƒeme.

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: Wotrɔ ŋkɔ na dua be Dan ɖe Lais teƒe. Dan nye wo tɔ́ si wodzi na Israel la ŋkɔ.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, fia aɖeke menɔ Israel-dukɔ la si o. Levi-ŋutsu aɖe si nye amedzro va nɔ Efrayim-tonyigba la ƒe mlɔenu ke. Azɔ la ŋutsu sia tsɔ nyɔnu aɖe si tso Betlehem le Yuda-nutome la ɖo ahiãvie.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: Ke eƒe ahiãvia do dziku ɖe eŋu, eye wòdzo yi tɔ́a ƒeme le Betlehem ɖanɔ afi ma ɣleti ene.

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: Azɔ ŋutsua ɖoe be yeadze nyɔnua yome aɖable enu ne wòatrɔ agbɔ va ye gbɔ. Ekplɔ eƒe ŋutsudɔla ɖeka kple tedzi eve ɖe asi. Nyɔnua kplɔ ŋutsua ge ɖe tɔ́a ƒeme eye esi tɔ́a kpɔe la, exɔe kple dzidzɔ.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: Ðetugbia tɔ́ si nye toa la na wòtsi egbɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃. Woɖu nu, no nu, eye eya kple nyɔnua wotsi afi ma dɔ.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Esi wofɔ le ŋkeke enea gbe be yewoadze mɔ la, ɖetugbia tɔ́a gblɔ nɛ be: “Wonedi nuɖuɖu aɖe na wò nàɖu hafi miadze mɔ.”

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Ale wo kple evea nɔ anyi eye woɖu nu, no nu ɖekae. Ɖetugbia tɔ́a gblɔ na Levitɔ la be: “Tsi mía gbɔ dɔ nàgbɔ ɖe eme ʋɛ.”

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Ŋutsua tso be yeadzo, ke ɖetugbia tɔ́a ƒoe ɖe enu, eye wòtsi anyi dɔ.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke atɔ̃lia ƒe ŋdi kanya la, ebe yeadze mɔ, ke ɖetugbia tɔ́ gblɔ nɛ be: “Meɖe kuku, ɖu nane gbɔ, eye mialala ɣetrɔ me hafi miadze mɔ.” Ale ŋutsuawo kple eve ɖu nu ɖekae.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Ke esi ŋutsu la kple eƒe ahiãvia kpakple eƒe dɔla la tso be yewoadze mɔ la, ɖetugbia tɔ́a gblɔ na Levitɔ la be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ɣe yina to ɖo ge, eye anyinu le fafam; mitsi dɔ. Zã do vɔ xoxo, mitsi anyi miagbɔ ɖe eme. Etsɔ ŋdi la miafɔ kaba adze mɔ ayi aƒe.

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Gake ŋutsu la melɔ̃ be yeagatsi afi ma adɔ o, eye wòdze mɔ heva Yebus eyae nye Yerusalem. Tedzi eve siwo wòdo agba na kple eƒe ahiãvi la hã kpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Esi wogogo Yebus la, zã do vɔ ale eƒe dɔla la gblɔ nɛ be: “Na míatsi Yebusitɔwo ƒe du sia me, adɔ.”

english_verse: “No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah,
translation_verse: Ke eƒe aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Míayi aɖadze ame manyamanyawo gbɔ le du aɖeke me, afi si Israelvi aɖeke mele o la me o; ke boŋ míaɖo ta Gibea.”

english_verse: or maybe we can even reach Ramah before dark.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ na dɔla la be: “Netsɔ mina míayi duawo dometɔ ɖeka me, eye míatsi Gibea alo Rama adɔ.”

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Ale woyi woƒe mɔzɔzɔ dzi ɖo ta ŋgɔ. Ɣe va ɖo to ɖe wo le Gibea si le Benyamin-to la ƒe anyigba dzi la gbɔ.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: Tete wodze le mɔa dzi ge ɖe Gibea-dua me be yewoatsi afi ma adɔ. Woyi ɖadro ɖe dua ƒe ablɔ me elabe ame aɖeke mena dzeƒe wo ɖe eƒeme o.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Esime wole afi ma la, ame tsitsi aɖe gbɔ tso agble va yina ɖe aƒeme fiẽ ma. Efrayim-tonyigba la dzi tɔwoe nye ŋutsu sia, eye wòva le Gibea abe amedzro ene. Ame bubu siwo le afi ma la, Benyamin-to la me tɔwo wonye.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Ame tsitsi la kpɔ mɔzɔla la le ablɔa me, eye wòbiae be: “Afi ka nèyina, eye afi ka nètso?”

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Levitɔ la ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Míetso Betlehem le Yuda heyina ɖe Efrayim-tonyigba la ƒe mlɔenu ke. Afi mae metso va yi Betlehem le Yuda. Meyina Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒeme, ke ame aɖeke mexɔm ɖe eƒeme o.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Evɔ la, nuhiahiã ɖe sia ɖe le mía si hafi. Gbe kple nuɖuɖu li na míaƒe tedziawo, eye abolo kple wain li na nye ŋutɔ, nyɔnudɔla la kple nye dɔla sia hã.

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Ame tsitsi la gblɔ nɛ be: “Ŋutifafa na wò. Nu sia nu si le hiãwòm la, madii na wò. Mèle ablɔ me afi sia ya tsi ge adɔ gbeɖe o.”

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Ale wòkplɔ wo yi eƒemee, eye wòna nuɖuɖu tedziawo. Ena amedzroawo klɔ afɔ eye wòna woɖu nu, no nu.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Esi wonɔ nua ɖum la, kpɔ ɖa, yakamewo tso dua me va ƒo xlã aƒea. Wonɔ ʋɔa ƒom sesĩe henɔ gbɔgblɔm na aƒea tɔ be: “Kplɔ ŋutsu si va dze gbɔwò la doe, ne míade asi eŋu!”

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Tete aƒea tɔ la do yi wo gbɔ ɖagblɔ na wo be: “Nu ka! Nɔvinyewo, meɖe kuku na mi; migawɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi sia o. Gbɔnyee wòva dze; nye amedzroe! Migawɔ nu vlo sia o.

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Mikpɔ ɖa, vinye nyɔnu ɖetugbi kple ŋutsua ƒe ahiãvi li. Makplɔ wo vɛ ne miade asi woawo ŋu. Nu sia nu si dze mia ŋu la, miwɔe ɖe wo ŋu. Ke migawɔ nu vlo ma ɖe ŋutsu sia ŋu o.”

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Ke ŋutsuawo gbe toɖoɖoe. Ale Levi-ŋutsu la kplɔ eƒe ahiãvi la do ɖe wo gbɔ. Wode asi nyɔnua ŋu hewɔ funyafunyae zã blibo la va se ɖe esime ŋu ke. Esi ŋu le kekem la, woɖe asi le eŋu.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Fɔŋli la nyɔnua va dze anyi ɖe ŋutsua ƒe xɔ si me eƒe aƒetɔ le la ƒe ʋɔtru nu va se ɖe esime ŋua ke nyuie.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Esi Levitɔ la fɔ ŋdi eye wòʋu ʋɔa do go be yeayi yeƒe mɔzɔzɔ dzi la, ekpɔ eƒe ahiãvi la wòtsra ɖe xɔa ƒe mɔnu, eye eƒe asiwo le kpuia dzi.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Ŋutsua gblɔ nɛ be: “Tsi tre ne míadzo.” Ke meɖo eŋu nɛ o. Tete wòkɔe ɖo eƒe tedzi dzi, eye wòdze mɔ yi enɔƒe.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: Esi wòva ɖo la, ege ɖe eƒe xɔ me eye wòtsɔ hɛ. Elé eƒe ahiãvi la, eye wòflii ƒunuɖeƒe ƒunuɖeƒe. Eɖoe teƒe wui eve, eye wòɖo kɔ ɖeka ɖe toawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe le Israel-nyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
