translation_verse: Ame siwo katã kpɔe la gblɔ be: “Nu sia tɔgbe medzɔ kpɔ o. Womekpɔe kpɔ hã o. Tso gbe si gbe Israelviwo ʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi va se ɖe egbe la, nu sia medzɔ kpɔ o. Mibu eŋu kpɔ. Mide adaŋu ne miagblɔ nya aɖe.”

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Ale Levitɔ si srɔ̃ wowu la ɖo eŋu gblɔ be: “Nye kple srɔ̃nyee va Gibea si nye Benyamin-to la ƒe du me be míatsi afi ma adɔ.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Mekɔ nye ahiãvi la, eye meflii ɖo ɖe nutowo katã me le Israel-nyigba blibo la dzi, elabe wowɔ busunu kple nuvɔ̃ɖi le Israel-dukɔ me.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Mikpɔ ɖa, mí ame siwo katã le afii la, Israelviwo míenye. Nu ka wɔ ge míala? Miɖo aɖaŋu.”

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Tete ameawo katã tsi tsitre gblɔ abe ame ɖeka ene be: “Ame aɖeke matrɔ ayi eƒe agbadɔ me o, ɖeke matrɔ ayi eƒe xɔ me o.”

english_verse: Everyone agreed that Gibeah had to be punished.
translation_verse: Tete Israel-ŋutsuwo katã ƒo ƒu, eye wobla ɖekae ɖe Gibea-du la ŋu.

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Azɔ Israel-toawo dɔ amewo ɖe Benyamin ƒomeawo gbɔ bia wo be: “Nu vlo kae nye esi wowɔ le mia dome?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: Fifia la, mihe nu vlo wɔlaawo ɖe go le Gibea ne míawu wo ale be míaɖe nuvɔ̃ɖi la ɖa le Israel-dukɔ me.” Ke Benyamin viwo meɖo to wo nɔvi Israelviwo ƒe nya la o.

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: Tete Benyamin viwo tso duwo me va ƒo ƒu ɖe Gibea be woakpe aʋa kple Israelviwo.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo fɔ ŋdi kanya va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Gibea-dua gbɔ.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Woho aʋa ɖe Benyamin viwo ƒe aʋakɔ ŋu, eye wona woƒe aʋawɔlawo dze ŋgɔ dua.

english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Benyamin viwo ƒe aʋakɔ do go tso Gibea-dua me, eye wotsrɔ̃ ame akpe bla eve vɔ eve le Israel-ʋakɔ ŋu gbe ma gbe.

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Ale Israelviwo ɖe amewo woyi ɖade xa ɖe Gibea-dua ŋu kpe ɖo.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Wosí le Israel-ŋutsuwo nu to gbedzimɔ, ke aʋa la yɔ wo ɖe nu. Amewo do tso duwo me, eye wotsɔ wo ɖe to me hetsrɔ̃ wo.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: Woɖe to ɖe Benyamin viwo eye wonyà wo ɖe nu. Wotsrɔ̃ wo tso afi si wodro ɖo va se ɖe Gibea-dua kasa le ɣedzeƒe gome.

english_verse: Some other warriors of Benjamin turned and ran down the road toward Rimmon Rock in the desert. The Israelites killed
translation_verse: Tete wotrɔ hesí ɖo ta gbedzi va se ɖe Rimon-kpe la gbɔ. Wowu ame akpe atɔ̃ le woƒe megbexelawo ŋu le mɔ dzi. Woti wo yome va se ɖe Gidom, eye wogawu ame akpe eve le wo ŋu.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Aʋawɔla kalẽtɔ siwo katã kpla yi, eye wotsi aʋa le Benyamin viwo dome gbe ma gbe la le ame akpe bla eve vɔ atɔ̃.

english_verse: The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_verse: Israel-ŋutsuwo trɔ ɖe Benyamin vi mamlɛawo ŋu, eye wowu wo kple yi. Wowu lãhawo kple nu sia nu si wokpɔ la le dua me. Eyome wotɔ dzo du siwo katã le nutoa me la.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Israel-ŋutsuwo ƒo ƒu ɖe Mizpa eye woka atam be: “Ne mía dometɔ aɖe tsɔ via nyɔnu na Benyamintɔ aɖe wòɖe fĩi!”

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Esi dukɔ la va Betel la, wotsi Mawu ŋkume le afi ma, eye wofa avi vevie kple ɣli va se ɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ be: “O Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu, nu ka ta nu sia dzɔ le Israel ɖo? Nu ka ta to ɖeka nabu le míaƒe toawo dome?”

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Ŋufɔke ŋdi kanya la, dukɔ la ɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afi ma, eye wosa numemevɔ kple ŋutifafavɔ.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Wobia be: “Ame ka le Israel-toawo katã me si meva takpeƒe le Aƒetɔ gbɔ le Mizpa o?” Do ŋgɔ la, woka atam be ame si mava Aƒetɔ gbɔ le Mizpa o la, ele be woawui godoo.

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Benyamin viwo siwo nye Israelviwo nɔviwo la ƒe nu wɔ nublanui na wo ŋutɔ, eye wogblɔ be, “To ɖeka ɖe ɖa le Israel-toawo dome egbe.

english_verse: Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
translation_verse: Ale ke míawɔ ana nyɔnu ame siwo susɔ laa? Elabe míeka atam gblɔ na Aƒetɔ be míana mía vinyɔnu aɖeke wo woaɖe o.”

english_verse: Again the Israelites asked, “Did any of the tribes stay away from the meeting at Mizpah?” After asking around, they discovered that no one had come from Jabesh in Gilead.
translation_verse: Esi woƒo ameawo katã nu ƒu le dukɔa me la, Yabes Gileadtɔ aɖeke meva o.

english_verse: The warriors attacked Jabesh in Gilead, and returned to their camp at Shiloh in Canaan with
translation_verse: Wokpɔ ɖetugbi alafa ene siwo menya ŋutsu o le Yabes Gileadtɔwo dome, eye wokplɔ wo va asaɖa la me le Silo le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Tete ameha blibo la dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Benyamin viwo gbɔ le Rimon-kpe la gbɔ, eye wodo ŋugbe na wo be yewoawɔ ŋutifafa.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Ale Benyamin viwo trɔ gbɔ ɣe ma ɣi, eye wotsɔ nyɔnu siwo woxɔ ɖe agbe tso Yabes Gilead-nyɔnuwo dome la na wo woɖe, ke mede wo nu o.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Benyamin viwo ƒe nu wɔ nublanui na dukɔ la ŋutɔ elabe Aƒetɔ ɖe ɖekawɔwɔ si nɔ toawo dome le Israel-dukɔa me tsã la ɖa.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Tete ameha la ƒe amegãwo gblɔ be: “Ale ke míawɔ hafi akpɔ nyɔnu na ame siwo susɔ laa? Elabe nyɔnuwo vɔ le Benyamin viwo dome keŋkeŋ.”

english_verse: If they don't have children, one of the Israelite tribes will die out.
translation_verse: Wogblɔ be: “Benyamin viwo ƒe anyigba nye woƒe ame siwo susɔ la tɔ. To aɖeke matsrɔ̃ keŋkeŋ le Israel-dukɔ me o.

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Evɔ la, míawo míate ŋu atsɔ mía vinyɔnuwo na wo woaɖe o, elabe míeka atam be aɖi ame si ana nyɔnu Benyamintɔ aɖe ŋu.”

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ be, “Kpɔ ɖa, woɖua Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋkekenyui la ƒe sia ƒe le Silo.” Silo le Betel ƒe dzigbeme kple mɔ si tso Betel ɖo ta Sixem la ƒe ɣedzeƒe kpakple Lebona ƒe anyigbeme.

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: eye minɔ ŋudzɔ. Ne miekpɔ be Silo-nyɔnuviwo do va ɣe ɖu ge la, ekema mido tso waingbleawo me. Mia dome ame sia ame nelé nyɔnu na eɖokui, eye míakɔe ayi ɖe Benyamin-to la ƒe anyigba dzii.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Ke ne wo tɔ́wo kple wo nɔviŋutsuwo va dzre wɔ ge kpli mí la, ekema míagblɔ na wo be: “Miɖe asi le wo ŋu na mí, elabe míekpɔ nyɔnu le aʋa me na ame sia ame o. Ðe wònye miawo ŋutɔe tsɔ wo na wo la, eya ko miaɖi fɔ.”

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Tete Benyamin viwo wɔ nenema, eye wokpɔ nyɔnu wòde wo nu tso ɣeɖula siwo wolé sesẽe la dome. Emegbe wotrɔ yi woƒe anyigba dzi. Wogbugbɔ duawo tso henɔ wo me.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Israelvi mamlɛawo hã dzo yi woƒe to si me wotso kple woƒe ƒomeawo gbɔ, eye woyi woƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, fia aɖeke menɔ Israel-dukɔ la si o. Ale ame sia ame wɔa nu sia nu si dze eŋu.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Ŋutsua ŋkɔe nye Elimelex, eye srɔ̃a ŋkɔe nye Naomi. Via ŋutsuvi eveawo ŋkɔwoe nye Maxlon kple Xilion. Wotso Efrata-ƒome me le Betlehem le Yuda, eye woʋu yi ɖanɔ Moab-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: Ke Elimelex, Naomi srɔ̃, ku, eye wògblẽ srɔ̃a kple via ŋutsuvi eveawo ɖi.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Ŋutsuvi eve siawo ɖe Moab-nyɔnuwo; ɖeka ŋkɔe nye Orpa, eye evelia ŋkɔe nye Rut. Wonɔ afi ma abe ƒè ewo ene,

english_verse: Mahlon and Chilion also died. Now Naomi had no husband or sons.
translation_verse: eye Maxlon kple Xilion va ku. Ale Naomi tsi anyi, eye wòzu vimanɔsitɔ kple ahosi. Naomi trɔ gbɔ va Betlehem kple Rut

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Ke Naomi gblɔ na lɔ̃xoyɔvi eveawo be: “Mitrɔ, mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe negbugbɔ yi nɔa ƒeme. Aƒetɔ nenyo dɔme na mi abe ale si miawo hã mienyo dɔme na nye kple ameyinugbeawo ene.

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ neve mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe nu be miakpɔ atsuƒe anɔ.” Tete wògbugbɔ nu na wo, eye wode asi avifafa me sesĩe,

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: eye wogblɔ nɛ be: “Gbeɖe, míatrɔ ayi mia de kpli wò.”

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Ke Naomi gblɔ be: “Vinyewo, mitrɔ. Nu ka tae miebe yewoayi kplim? Ɖe vi gale dɔme nam, magadzi ŋutsuviwo miava ɖea?

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Vinyewo, mitrɔ; migbugbɔ yi ko elabe metsi to srɔ̃ɖeɖe me yi xoxo. Azɔ nenye be mɔkpɔkpɔ ɖe wògali nam gɔ̃ hã ɖe, ne meɖe srɔ̃ zã sia me dzi ŋutsuviwo hã la,

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: ɖe miaxa ɖe wo ta anɔ lalam ʋuu, va se ɖe esime woatsi miaɖea? Ðe miatsi srɔ̃maɖemaɖe le wo taa? Kpao, vinyewo! Mia tɔ koe le veyem be Aƒetɔ wɔ num vevie alea.”

english_verse: They cried again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
translation_verse: Tete wogafa avi sesĩe. Emegbe Orpa gbugbɔ nu na lɔ̃xoa, hetrɔ, ke Rut ya ku ɖe eŋu goŋgoŋ.

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: Naomi gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ nɔviwò ɖa! Etrɔ yina wo detɔwo kple eƒe mawuwo gbɔ. Wò hã trɔ nàdze eyome.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Ke Rut ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Mègaƒoe ɖe nunye be magblẽ wò ɖi alo agbugbɔ le yowòme o. Elabe afi si nàyi la, afi ma ko nye hã mayi; afi si nànɔ la, afi ma ko nye hã manɔ; wò dukɔ anye nye dukɔ; wò Mawu anye nye Mawu;

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: afi si nàku ɖo ko nye hã maku ɖo, eye afi mae woaɖim ɖo. Aƒetɔ nena wòaɖi ŋunye, agaɖi ŋunye ake, ne menye ku koe aklã nye kple wò dome o fĩi!”

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi Naomi kpɔ be Rut ɖoe kplikpaa be yeayi kple ye kokoko la, edzudzɔ eƒoƒo ɖe enu.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Ale wo ame eve la zɔ ʋuu va ɖo Betlehem. Esi wova ɖo Betlehem la, du bliboa ƒo zi ɖe wo ŋu. Nyɔnuwo nɔ gbɔgblɔm be: “Ao, Naomie nye esia?”

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Ke eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Migayɔm be Naomi o; miyɔm be Mara boŋ, elabe Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la do nublanuitɔm vevie.

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: Nunɔamesitɔ menye yi nua gbe, ke Aƒetɔ kplɔm gbɔe asi ƒuƒlu. Nu ka tae miegale yɔyem be Naomi esime Aƒetɔ wɔ nu vevim, eye Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la na dzɔgbevɔ̃e va dzinye?”

english_verse: The barley harvest was just beginning when Naomi and Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law, arrived in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ale Naomi trɔ gbɔ kple lɔ̃xoyɔvia Rut, si nye Moabtɔ tso Moab-nyigba dzi la, nye esi. Wova ɖo Betlehem esime luŋeɣi dze egɔme.

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Tete Boaz tso Betlehem va ɖo. Edo gbe na luxalawo be: “Aƒetɔ la nenɔ kpli mi!” Woɖo eŋu be: “Aƒetɔ la neyra wò!”

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Azɔ Boaz bia eƒe dɔla si le dɔwɔlawo dzi kpɔm la be: “Ame ka ƒe nyɔnuvie nye ema?”

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Dɔdzikpɔla la ɖo eŋu be: “Moab-nyɔnuvi si gbɔ kple Naomi tso Moab-nyigba dzi lae.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: Eva bia be yeanɔ luxalaawo yome anɔ lu si ge ɖi la fɔm. Tso ŋdi kanya, esi wòva la, dɔ dzi ko wòle; megbɔ ɖe eme vie hã kpɔ o.”

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Tete Boaz gblɔ na Rut be: “Vinye, see ɖa. Mègadzo le agble sia me yi lufɔƒe le bubu me o, ke nɔ nye dɔlanyɔnuwo yome.

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Lé ŋku ɖe agble si me wole lua xam le la ŋu, eye nànɔ wo yome. Megblɔ na dɔwɔlaawo be wo dometɔ aɖeke nagaɖe fu na wò o. Ne tsikɔ le wuwòm la, yi ɖe ze siwo me dɔwɔlaawo du tsi ɖo la gbɔ, nàno tsi.”

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Tete Rut de ta agu tsyɔ mo anyi, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Ale ke wɔ wò dɔme trɔ ɖe nye amedzro ŋu, eye nèlé ŋku ɖe ŋunye ale?”

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Ke Boaz ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Wogblɔ nu siwo katã nèwɔ na lɔ̃xowò tso esime srɔ̃wò ku la nam keŋ. Wobe ègblẽ nɔwò kple tɔ́wò kpakple mia denyigba ɖi, eye nèva dukɔ si me tɔwo mènya tsã kura o la me.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ neɖo nu si nèwɔ la teƒe na wò. Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu si nèva sí tso la nexe fetu dedee na wò.”

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Tete Rut gblɔ nɛ be: “Nye Aƒetɔ, ève nunye ŋutɔ elabe èfa akɔ nam, eye nèƒo nu dɔmenyotɔe na wò dɔlanyɔnu; togbɔ be nyemenye wò dɔlanyɔnuwo dometɔ aɖeke o hã.”

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Esi nuɖuɣi ɖo la, Boaz gblɔ nɛ be: “Va ɖu nu le afii. Tsɔ abolo nàtɔ ataditsia me nàɖu.” Ale Rut nɔ anyi ɖe luxalaawo xa, eye Boaz tsɔ bli memee nɛ. Eɖu nua ɖi ƒo nyuie, eye ɖe gasusɔ.

english_verse: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
translation_verse: Esi Rut tsi tsitre be yeayi lua fɔfɔ dzi la, Boaz gblɔ na dɔwɔlaawo be: “Mina ne wòafɔe le esi wobla da ɖi la dome, eye miganyra ɖee o.

english_verse: Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
translation_verse: Hekpe ɖe esia ŋu la, milũ ɖewo le bablaawo me da ɖi nɛ wòava fɔ. Miganyra ɖee o.”

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Ale Rut fɔ lu le agblea me ʋuu va se ɖe fiẽ. Azɔ la, eƒo esi wòfɔ la ƒu, eye wòkpɔ lu abe kilo ewo ene.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: Etsɔe yi aƒeme ɖafia lɔ̃xoa. Eɖe nu si wòɖu susɔ la hã nɛ.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Lɔ̃xoa biae be: “Afi ka nèyi ɖafɔ lua le egbe? Afi ka nèwɔ dɔ le? Mawu neyra ame si tsɔ le eme na wò.” Ale Rut gblɔ ame si gbɔ wòde ɖawɔ dɔ la na lɔ̃xoa. Ebe: “Ŋutsu si gbɔ mede ɖawɔ dɔ egbe la ŋkɔe nye Boaz.”

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Naomi gblɔ na lɔ̃xoyɔvia be: “Aƒetɔ, ame si nyoa dɔme na agbagbeawo kple kukuawo siaa la, neyrae.” Naomi yi edzi gblɔ nɛ be: “Míaƒe ƒometɔ kpamkpam ye nye ŋutsua. Ame siwo wòle be woaxɔ na mí la dometɔ ɖekae.”

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Rut gblɔ nɛ be: “Gawu la, ŋutsua gblɔ be manɔ yeƒe dɔlawo ŋu va se ɖe esime woaŋe nu le agble bliboa me vɔ.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Tete Naomi gblɔ na lɔ̃xoyɔvia Rut be: “Vinye, enyo ŋutɔ be nànɔ eƒe dɔlanyɔnuwo ŋu, ne ame aɖeke nava wɔ fu wò le agble bubu me o.”

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Ale Rut nɔ Boaz ƒe dɔlanyɔnuawo ŋu nɔ lu kple ƒo fɔm va se ɖe esime nuŋeɣi la wu nu. Enɔ lɔ̃xoa gbɔ.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka Rut lɔ̃xo, Naomi, gblɔ nɛ be: “Vinye, nyemadi atsuƒe na wò nànɔ, wò dzi nadze eme oa?

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Míaƒe ƒometɔe nye Boaz, ame si ƒe dɔlanyɔnuwo kple wò miewɔ dɔ. Kpɔ ɖa, egbe zã la, ele lu gbɔ ge le lugbɔƒe.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Eya ta yi ɖale tsi nàsi ami ʋeʋẽe, eye nàdo awu nyuie ne nàyi lugbɔƒe la. Ke mègana wòanya be nèva o, va se ɖe esime wòɖu nu, no nu vɔ.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: Nenye be wòyi ɖamlɔ anyi la, de dzesi afi si wòmlɔ la nyuie. Azɔ yi nàklo avɔ le eƒe afɔ, eye nàmlɔ afi ma, ekema agblɔ nu si nàwɔ la na wò.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Rut ɖo eŋu be: “Mawɔ nu siwo katã nègblɔ nam la.”

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Ale wòyi lugbɔƒe la, eye wòwɔ nu sia nu si lɔ̃xoa gblɔ nɛ la.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Ke esi Boaz ɖu nu, no nu vɔ, eye dzi nɔ edzɔm la, eyi ɖamlɔ anyi ɖe afi si woƒo ƒu lua ɖo la ƒe mlɔenu. Rut va dzaa, eye wòklo avɔ le afɔgbɔ nɛ hemlɔ afi ma.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Le zã titina la, Boaz ɖi vo eye wòtrɔ. Kasia wòakpɔ la, nyɔnue nye esi mlɔ anyi ɖe eƒe afɔnu!

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: Ebia be: “Wò ame kae?” Rut ɖo eŋu be: “Nye Rut, wò dɔlanyɔnue. Medi be nàtsyɔ avɔ nam elabe wòe nye srɔ̃nyeɖia.”

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Egblɔ nɛ be: “Vinye, Aƒetɔ neyra wò. Nuteƒe si nèwɔ fifia la le ɖase ɖim le ŋuwò wu esi nèwɔ va yi, elabe mèdze ɖekakpui kesinɔtɔwo alo esiwo da ahe la yome o.

english_verse: Don't worry, I'll do what you have asked. You are respected by everyone in town.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, vinye, mègavɔ̃ o. Mawɔ nu siwo katã nèbia la na wò, elabe mía detɔwo katã nya be nyɔnu ɖɔʋu nènye.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Ele eme baa be menye ƒometɔ si ate ŋu axɔ na wò, gake ame bubu li te ɖe ŋuwò wum.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Tsi afii dɔ. Ne ŋu ke, eye ame sia axɔ na wò abe ƒometɔ si te ɖe ŋuwò wum ene la, enyo. Evɔ ne medi be yeaxɔ na wò o la, ekema metà Aƒetɔ gbagbe la be maxɔ na wò. Azɔ la, mlɔ afii va se ɖe fɔŋli.”

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Ale wòmlɔ Boaz ƒe afɔnu va se ɖe fɔŋli. Efɔ hafi xexeme kɔ, woayi ame kpɔ ge adze sii, elabe Boaz gblɔ nɛ be megana ame aɖeke nanya be nyɔnu va lugbɔƒe la o.

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Boaz gblɔ nɛ be: “Ðe wò taɖedzia ɖo ɖi.” Esi Rut ɖoe ɖi la, Boaz ku lu abe kilo bla eve ene kɔ ɖe edzi nɛ. Elée ɖo abɔta nɛ eye wòdzo yi aƒeme.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: Ebe: “Etsɔ lu nudzidzenu ade sia nam hegblɔ be: ‘Mele be nàgbugbɔ ayi lɔ̃xowò gbɔ asi ƒuƒlu o.’ ”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Tete Naomi gblɔ nɛ be: “Vinye, wò ya gbɔ dzi blewuu ko; ànya ale si nya la ava yii godoo, elabe ne ŋutsua mekpɔ ta na nya la egbe o la, maɖe dzi ɖi akpɔ o.”

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Azɔ Boaz yi takpeƒe le dua ƒe agbo nu ɖanɔ anyi ɖe afi ma. Kasia ƒometɔ si ŋu Boaz ƒo nu le lae nye esi va yina. Tete Boaz yɔe hegblɔ nɛ be: “Xɔ̃nye, te va nàva nɔ anyi.” Ale wòva nɔ anyi.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Boaz di dumemetsitsi ewo hã vɛ, gblɔ na wo be woanɔ anyi. Woawo hã nɔ anyi.

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: Azɔ edoe ɖe eƒe ƒometɔ la gbɔ be: “Naomi, ame si trɔ gbɔ tso Moab-nyigba dzi la le mía nɔvi, Elimelex, ƒe anyigba dzram.

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: Eya ta mebui be mana nyanya wò tso eŋuti. Nye susue nye be nàƒlee le ame siwo le afi sia kple míaƒe dumemetsitsi siwo nɔ anyi la ŋkume. Ne èdi be yeaxɔe la, xɔe, gake ne màxɔe o la, gblɔe ne mase elabe ame bubu aɖeke megali si axɔe wu wò o; nye koe gakplɔ wò ɖo.” Ŋutsua ɖo eŋu be: “Maxɔe.”

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Boaz gblɔ nɛ be: “Ne èƒle anyigba sia le Naomi si la, nyae be yeaxɔ Rut, Moab-nyɔnu, ahosi la hã bene ameyinugbea ƒe ŋkɔ natsi domenyinuawo ŋu.”

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Tete eƒe ƒometɔ la gblɔ be: “Togbɔ be nyee wòle be maxɔ nuawo hafi hã la, nyemate ŋu axɔ wo o, elabe nye ŋutɔ nye domenyinu dome ava gblẽ. Xɔ nuawo ɖe tenyeƒe faa; nyemate ŋu axɔ wo o.”

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: Eya ta esi ƒometɔ la gblɔ na Boaz be: “Wò boŋ xɔ nuawo” la, eɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe afɔkpa tsɔ na Boaz.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Azɔ Boaz gblɔ na dumemetsitsiawo kple dua me tɔwo katã be: “Miawoe nye nye ɖasefowo egbe, be meƒle domenyinu siwo katã nye Elimelex kple Xilion kpakple Maxlon tɔ la le Naomi si.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: Nenema ke mexɔ Rut, Maxlon ƒe ahosi la hã ɖe, wòzu srɔ̃nye, ale be ameyinugbea ƒe ŋkɔ natsi domenyinua ŋu, eye magabu le nɔviawo dome alo wo de o. Miawoe nye nye ɖasefowo tso egbe.”

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Takpeƒea valawo kple dumemetsitsiawo katã lɔ̃ ɖe edzi be: “Míenye wò ɖasefowo vavã. Aƒetɔ neyra nyɔnu si gbɔna aƒewò me la. Nena wòadzi abe ale si Raxel kple Lea dzii ene. Ame eve siawoe tso Israel ƒe aƒe la, eye wona wòkeke ta. Nu nedze edzi na wò le Efrata-ƒomea me, eye wò nu nyui wɔwɔ nade du le Betlehem.

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: Vi siwo Aƒetɔ ana nyɔnu sia nadzi na wò la, nana wò aƒe nanɔ abe Perez, ame si Tamar dzi na Yuda la, tɔ ene.” Boaz kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo

english_verse: Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son.
translation_verse: Ale wɔ Boaz ɖe Rut wòzu srɔ̃a. Enɔ anyi kplii, eye Aƒetɔ na nyɔnua fɔ fu hedzi ŋutsuvi.

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Nyɔnuwo gblɔ na Naomi be: “Woakafu Aƒetɔ, be mete domenyila wò o. Ðevi sia ŋkɔ nede du le Israel-dukɔa me!

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: Ana agbe yeye nagaɖo mewò, eye wòakpɔ dziwò ne èku nyagã, elabe wò lɔ̃xoyɔvi si dzii na wò la, lɔ̃ wò ŋutɔ; ewú viŋutsuvi adrẽ gɔ̃ hã na wò.”

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Naomi xɔ ɖevi la ɖe akɔ, eye wòzu enyila.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Eƒe aƒelikawo tsɔ ŋkɔ na ɖevia be Obed. Wogblɔ na amewo be: “Wodzi ŋutsuvi na Naomi.” Obed ye va zu Yese tɔ́, ame si dzi David.

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Ŋutsu aɖe nɔ Ramataim-Zofim si nye du aɖe le Efrayim-tonyigba dzi. Eŋkɔe nye Elkana eye wònye Yeroxam vi. Yeroxam tɔ́e nye Elihu, eye tɔgbuia ŋkɔe nye Tohu, ame si nye Zuf vi tso Efrayim-to la me.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: Srɔ̃ eve nɔ Elkana si. Ðeka ŋkɔe nye Xana, eye evelia ŋkɔe nye Penina. Penina dzi vi, ke Xana ya medzi vi aɖeke o.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Azɔ ƒè sia ƒè la, Elkana tsoa wo dedu me yia Silo ɖasubɔna eye wòsaa vɔ na Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la. Silo, afi siae Eli viŋutsuvi eveawo, Hofni kple Pinehas, nye Aƒetɔ ƒe nunɔlawo le.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Gbe si gbe Elkana sa vɔ la, enaa vɔsalã ƒe akpa aɖe srɔ̃a Penina, eye wòganaa via ŋutsuwo kple via nyɔnuwo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be elɔ̃ Xana ŋutɔ hã la, vɔsalãa ƒe akpa ɖeka ko wònanɛ elabe Aƒetɔ na medzi vi o.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: Atsusia, Penina, ɖiaa enu eye wòdoa dziku nɛ vevie ɖe ale asi Aƒetɔ na medzi vi o la ta.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Aleae nuwo nɔ edzi yimee ƒè sia ƒè. Ne wonyayina vɔ sa ge na Aƒetɔ ko la, Penina doa dziku na Xana godoo. Le esia ta Xana faa avi eye wògbea nuɖuɖu.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: Ale srɔ̃a Elkana bianɛ be: “Xana, nu ka ta nèle avi fam? Nu ka ta nègbe nuɖuɖu? Nu ka ta wò dzi le nu xam? Ðe nyemewú viŋutsuvi ewo na wò oa?” Xana kple Eli

english_verse: When the sacrifice had been offered, and they had eaten the meal, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli was sitting in his chair near the door to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Esi woɖu nu eye wono nu vɔ le Silo la, Xana tso. Ɣe ma ɣi la Eli, nunɔla la, bɔbɔ nɔ zikpui dzi le Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔ ƒe ʋɔtru nu.

english_verse: Hannah was heartbroken and was crying as she prayed,
translation_verse: Xana nɔ nu xam vevie, eye wòdo gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ henɔ avi fam hehehe.

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: Xana ɖe adzɔgbe gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, ne àkpɔ wò nyɔnudɔla ƒe fukpekpe ɖa, eye àɖo ŋku dzinye, eye màŋlɔ wò nyɔnudɔla be o, eye àna viŋutsuvi wò nyɔnudɔla la, ekem matsɔe ana wò le eƒe agbenɔɣi katã. Talũhɛ aɖeke maka eƒe ta ŋu o.”

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Xana nɔ nu ƒom le eƒe dzime, eƒe nu koe nɔ ʋaʋãm, ke eƒe gbe meɖi woase o, eya ta Eli bui nyɔnu ahamula aɖee.

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: Egblɔ na Xana be: “Ɣe ka ɣi gɔ̃ aha akɔ le wò ŋkume? Dzudzɔ ahanono dzro!”

english_verse: “Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
translation_verse: Mègabu wò nyɔnudɔla nyɔnu maɖɔʋui o, elabe va se ɖe fifi la, dzimaɖi gã kple dziɖunya ko gblɔm mele.”

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Tete Eli gblɔ nɛ be: “Heyi le ŋutifafa me. Israel ƒe Mawu ana nu si nèbiae la wòasu asiwò.”

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: “Ne ànya ve wò nyɔnudɔla la nu ko.” Emegbe nyɔnua dzo, eye wòyi ɖaɖu nu. Eƒe dzedzeme trɔ, eye megaɖi ame si le veve sem la o. Samuel dzidzi kple etsɔtsɔ na Mawu

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Ŋdi kanya la, Elkana kple eƒe ƒomea fɔ yi ɖado gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ. Emegbe wotrɔ yi wo de Rama. Elkana dɔ kple srɔ̃a Xana, eye Aƒetɔ se eƒe gbedodoɖa.

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: Ale Xana fɔ fu le ɣe ma ɣi me eye wòdzi viŋutsuvi. Etsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Samuel eye wòɖe eme be: “Ðe mebia Aƒetɔ wònam.”

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Esi ƒe trɔ la, Elkana kple eƒemetɔwo katã yi Silo be woaɖasa ƒetatrɔvɔ si wosana la, eye wòaxe eƒe adzɔgbeɖefe na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Ke Xana ya meyi o. Egblɔ na srɔ̃a be: “Ne ɖevia ɖe asi le no ŋu la, makplɔe ayi Aƒetɔ ƒeme be wòaɖanɔ afi ma koŋ.”

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Elkana ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Wɔ nu si nèkpɔ be enyo la. Lala va se ɖe esime ɖevia ɖe asi le no ŋu. Aƒetɔ nena eƒe ŋugbedodo la nava eme.” Ale Xana tsi aƒe kpɔ ɖevia dzi va se ɖe esime wòɖee le no nu.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: Xana gblɔ nɛ be: “Amegã, taflatsɛ, èkpɔm dze sia? Nyee nye ame si va tsi tsitre ɖe ŋkuwò me afii kpɔ, nɔ gbe dom ɖa na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: Ðevi siae mebia be wòanam. Aƒetɔ se nye kokoƒoƒo eye wòna nu si mebiae lam.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Eya ta metsɔe na Aƒetɔ. Ezu Aƒetɔ tɔ koŋ, eƒe agbenɔɣi katã.” Emegbe wodo gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ le afi ma.

english_verse: Hannah prayed: You make me strong and happy, Lord. You rescued me. Now I can be glad and laugh at my enemies.
translation_verse: Xana hã do gbe ɖa gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ na nye dzi vu gblotoo le aseye tsom. Aƒetɔ ɖe nye ŋusẽ fia eye dzidzɔ yɔ menye. Meko nye futɔwo; elabe èxɔ nam eye dzi le dzɔyem.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: “Ame aɖeke mele kɔkɔe abe Aƒetɔ ene o. Ame aɖeke meli abe wò ene o. Agakpe aɖeke meli abe mía Mawu la ene o.

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Midzudzɔ adegbeƒoƒo dàdatɔe eye nya vlowo meganɔ dodom le mia nu o. Elabe Aƒetɔ nye Mawu si nya nu sia nu. Eyae tsoa nya me le amegbetɔwo ƒe nuwɔnawo ŋu.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: Kalẽtɔwo ƒe datiwo ŋe klíklikli, ke ame beliwo kpɔ ŋusẽ.

english_verse: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
translation_verse: Ame siwo ɖua nu ɖia ƒo tsã la, tsɔ wo ɖokui de awɔba be yewoakpɔ nu aɖu. Ke ame siwo mekpɔa nu ɖuna tsã o la, dɔ megawua wo azɔ o. Konɔ va dzi vi zi adrẽ, ke vi geɖe dzila va zu abe ame madzivikpɔ ene.

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ wua ame, eye eya ke gbɔa agbe ame. Eɖoa ame ɖe tsiẽƒe, eye wògahea ame doa goe.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ wɔa ame dahe, eye wògawɔa kesinɔtɔ hã. Eyae bɔbɔa ame aɖewo ɖe anyi, eye wòdoa bubuwo ya ɖe dzi.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: Eyae ɖea ame dahewo tso ké me, eye wòkɔa hiãtɔwo ɖe dzi tso dzowɔ me. Ewɔ esia be woanɔ anyi ɖe amegãwo dome, eye woabɔbɔ nɔ bubuteƒewo. Anyigba ƒe gɔmeɖoɖowo nye Aƒetɔ tɔ, eye woawo dzie wòtu xexea me godoo ɖo.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: Ekpɔa eƒe ame wɔnuteƒewo ta be woanya zɔzɔ; ke ame vɔ̃ɖiwo atsrɔ̃ ɖe viviti me, elabe menye ame ƒe ŋusẽe naa wòɖua dzi o.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: Woatsrɔ̃ Aƒetɔ ƒe futɔwo; aɖe gbe ɖe wo dzi tso dziƒo. Aƒetɔ adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu xexea me katã, ana ŋusẽ eƒe fia la eye wòana eƒe amesiamina la aɖu dzi.”

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Emegbe Elkana trɔ yi wo de Rama, ke via ya tsi nunɔla Eli gbɔ hesubɔ Aƒetɔ. Nunɔla Eli viŋutsuwo

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: eye wometsɔ ɖeke le kɔnu si le nunɔlawo si na dukɔa la hã me o. Ne ame aɖe va le vɔ sam la, nunɔla ƒe dɔla léa gaflo nuetɔ̃ ɖe asi vanɛ. Esime vɔsala la le lã la ɖam la,

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: nunɔla ƒe dɔla tɔa lãwo le gaze alo ze, kutu alo agba me, eye nu sia nu si gaflo la he ɖi goe la zua nunɔla la tɔ. Aleae wowɔna ɖe Israelvi ɖe sia ɖe si va vɔ sa ge le Silo la ŋu.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Gawu la, hafi woaɖe amia atɔ dzoe la, nunɔla ƒe dɔla yina ɖe ame si va le vɔ sam la gbɔ ɖagblɔna nɛ be: “Nà lã aɖem ne nunɔla name; mele ɖaɖaa dim o, mumua dim wòle.”

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Ne vɔsala la ɖo eŋu be: “Nà woatɔ dzo amia gbã, emegbe àte ŋu atsɔ lã ale sinu dze ŋuwò” la, egblɔna be: “Gbeɖe! Tsɔe nam fifi laa! Ne menye nenema o la, matsɔe kple sesẽ!”

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Eli viawo ƒe nuvɔ̃ sia vɔ̃ɖi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume ŋutɔ, elabe womede bubu aɖeke Aƒetɔ ƒe vɔsa la ŋu o. Samuel le Silo

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment
translation_verse: Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, Samuel nɔ subɔsubɔdɔ wɔm le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Enye ɖevi dzaa si doa aklalawu si tɔgbe subɔlawo dona.

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Nɔa tɔa dziwui ɖagbee aɖe ɖananɛ ƒè sia ƒè, ne eya kple srɔ̃a Elkana va ƒètatrɔvɔ sa ge.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Emegbe Eli biaa yayra na Elkana kple srɔ̃a gblɔna be: “Aƒetɔ negana nyɔnu sia nadzi viwo na wò nàtsɔ ɖo esi nètsɔ nɛ la teƒe.” Emegbe wotrɔna yia wo de.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ve Xana nu, wòdzi ŋutsuvi etɔ̃ kple nyɔnuvi eve. Samuel ɖevi la hã tsi le Aƒetɔ gbɔ. Eli kple via ŋutsuwo

english_verse: Eli was now very old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Azɔ Eli tsi ku amegã. Enɔ nu siwo katã via ŋutsuwo nɔa wɔwɔm ɖe Israel-dukɔmeviwo ŋu la sem. Ese hã be viawo dɔna kple nyɔnu siwo subɔna le godoƒegbadɔ nu la gɔ̃ hã.

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Vinyewo, mesɔ o hee! Aƒetɔ ƒe dukɔmetɔwo mele nya nyui aɖeke gblɔm le mia ŋu o.

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Ne ame wɔ vɔ̃ ɖe ehavi ŋu la, Mawu axɔ nya ɖe vɔ̃wɔla la nu. Gake ne ame wɔ vɔ̃ ɖe Mawu ŋu la, ame kae aʋli eta?” Ke wogbe wo tɔ́a ƒe gbesese elabe Aƒetɔ ɖo be yeawu wo.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Samuel ɖevi la tsi ɖe edzi, eye eƒe nu dze Aƒetɔ kple amegbetɔwo siaa ŋu. Mawu ƒe gbedeasi ɖe Eli ƒomea ŋu

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Azɔ Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela aɖe va Eli gbɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Aƒetɔ be: ‘Meɖe ɖokuinye fia tɔ́wò ƒe ƒome esime wonye kluviwo na Egipte Fiagã le Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: Le esia ta Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la gblɔ be: ‘Medo ŋugbe va yi be wò ƒome kple tɔ́wò ƒe ƒome anye nye nunɔlawo anɔ gbɔnye asubɔm tegbee.’ Ke azɔ la, Aƒetɔ le gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Evɔ, magava eme gbeɖe o. Ame siwo buam la, nye hã mabu wo eye ame siwo doa vlom la, nye hã mado vlo wo.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ɣeyiɣi aɖe gbɔna esime mawu ɖekakpuiwo le wò ƒome me kple tɔ́wò tɔ me, ale be ame tsitsi aɖeke maganɔ wò ƒomea me loo, alo tɔ́wò tɔ me o.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: Ne esia va eme la, àxa nu eye àʋã ŋu Israel-dukɔmevi bubuwo le ale si mana nu nanyo na woawo la ta. Ke le wò ya gome la, ame tsitsi aɖeke maganɔ wò ƒome me akpɔ o.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Gake magblẽ wò dzidzimevi ɖeka aɖe ɖi si anye nunɔla asubɔm. Ke mana eƒe ŋkuwo agbã eye agbenɔnɔ azu dɔ nɛ. Aƒewòmeviwo ya la, woaku ku kpata le ɖekakpuime.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: Ne viwòawo kple evea, Xofni kple Pinehas, ku gbe ɖeka la, aɖee afia wò nànya be nya siwo katã megblɔ la le me va ge godoo.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Maɖo nunɔla nuteƒewɔla, ame si awɔ nu ɖe nye didi nu la na ɖokuinye. Mana eƒe dzidzimeviwo nasubɔm le nye amesiamina gbɔ tegbee.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Wò dzidzimevi siwo asusɔ la ayi nunɔla la gbɔ aɖabia ga kple nuɖuɖui, eye woaɖe kuku nɛ be: “Míeɖe kuku, ɖe mɔ na mí ne míakpe ɖe nunɔlawo ŋu ale be míakpɔ nane aɖu.’ ”

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: Samuel ya mlɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔ me, afi si Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la le. Womekpɔ tsi akaɖiawo haɖe o.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ yɔe be: “Samuel! Samuel!” Etɔ be: “Nyee nye esi!”

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: eye wòƒu du yi Eli gbɔ hegblɔ nɛ be: “Nyee nye esi, elabe èyɔm.” Ke Eli ɖo eŋu be: “Nyemeyɔ wò o; yi ɖamlɔ anyi.” Ale Samuel yi ɖamlɔ anyi.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ gayɔ Samuel ake. Efɔ gayi Eli gbɔ gblɔ be: “Nyee nye esi, elabe èyɔm.” Eli gblɔ be: “Vinye, nyemeyɔ wò o; gbugbɔ ɖamlɔ anyi.”

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Samuel menya Aƒetɔ haɖe o, eye Aƒetɔ meɖe eƒe nya fiae haɖe o.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gayɔ Samuel zi etɔ̃lia. Efɔ yi Eli gbɔ ɖagblɔ nɛ be: “Nyee nye esi, elabe èyɔm.” Tete Eli dze sii azɔ be Aƒetɔ ye le ɖevia yɔm,

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: ale wògblɔ na Samuel be: “Yi ɖamlɔ anyi. Ne egayɔ wò la, gblɔ nɛ: ‘Aƒetɔ, ƒo nu, elabe wò dɔla le to ɖom.’ ” Ale Samuel yi ɖamlɔ emlɔƒe.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gava eye wòle tsitre yɔe abe tsã ene be: “Samuel! Samuel!” Samuel ɖo eŋu be: “Ƒo nu, elabe wò dɔla le to ɖom.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, mele nane wɔ ge le Israel-dukɔa me. Ame sia ame si asee la ƒe to eveawo me aɖi yeŋ.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: Megblɔ nɛ va yi be nyemadzudzɔ tohehe na eƒe aƒe akpɔ o. Elabe enya nu tso viawo ƒe vodada kple busunya siwo wogblɔna ɖe Mawu ŋu la ŋu, gake wòzi kpi megbena na wo o.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: Eya ta meka atam be Eli ƒe aƒe la matsɔ vɔsa alo nunana aɖeke alé avu eƒe vodada la akpɔ o.”

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Samuel gamlɔ anyi va se ɖe esime ŋu ke. Efɔ eye wòʋu gbedoxɔa ƒe ʋɔwo. Ke evɔ̃ ŋutega si wòkpɔ la gbɔgblɔ na Eli.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Gake Eli yɔe be: “Vinye Samuel!” Samuel ɖo eŋu be: “Nyee nye esi!”

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Eli biae be: “Nya ka Mawu gblɔ na wò? Gblɔ wo katã nam; mègaɣla ɖeke ɖem o. Ne mègblɔ wo katã nam o la, Mawu ahe to na wò agahee na wò ake.”

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Ale Samuel gblɔ nya la katã nɛ; ɖeke mesusɔ o. Eli gblɔ be: “Eyae nye Aƒetɔ. Newɔ nu si dze eŋu la faa.”

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Samuel va tsi. Aƒetɔ nɔ kplii eye wòna nya sia nya si Samuel gblɔ la va eme.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Israel-dukɔ blibo la, tso Dan va se ɖe Beer-Seba, va nya be woɖo Samuel abe eƒe gbeƒãɖela ene.

english_verse: The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gaɖe eɖokui fia le Silo. Aƒetɔ ɖe eɖokui fia Samuel le afi sia to nya si wògblɔ nɛ la me.

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: Samuel ƒe nya siwo wòɖea gbeƒãe la dea afi sia afi le Israel-dukɔa me. Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, Israel-dukɔ ho aʋa ɖe Filistitɔwo ŋu. Woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Eben-Ezer gbɔ eye Filistitɔwo ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Afek.

english_verse: The Philistines made a fierce attack. They defeated the Israelites and killed about
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo ho yi ɖakpe aʋa kple Israelviwo; aʋa la nu sẽ ŋutɔ. Filistitɔwo ɖu Israelviwo dzi eye wowu ame akpe ene le gbea dzi.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Ale wodɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Silo woyi ɖatsɔ Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, si le kerubiwo tame la ƒe nubablaɖaka tso afi ma vɛ. Eli viŋutsu eveawo, Xofni kple Pinehas, hã zɔ kple nubablaɖaka la va.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Esi ame siwo susɔ la gbɔ va asaɖa la me la, Israel-me tsitsiwo gblɔ be: “Nu ka ta Aƒetɔ na Filistitɔwo ɖu mía dzi egbea? Mina míayi aɖatsɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka tso Silo vɛ, ne wòava nɔ mía dome, eye wòaɖe mí tso míaƒe futɔwo si me.”

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Esi nubablaɖaka la va ɖo asaɖa la me la, Israelviwo katã do dzidzɔɣli sesĩe hoo ale be anyigba ʋuʋu.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo se ɣlidodoa eye wobia be: “Nu ka ta ɣli sesẽ sia le ɖiɖim le Hebritɔwo ƒe asaɖa me?” Esi wova nya be Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka lae wotsɔ va asaɖa la me la,

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo ŋutɔ. Tete wogblɔ be: “Mawu aɖe va ɖo woƒe asaɖa la me. Baba na mí! Nu sia tɔgbe medzɔ kpɔ o.

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: Nane wɔ mí pɛ! Ame kae ate ŋu aɖe mí tso mawu triakɔ mawo si me? Mawu siawoe he dɔ vɔ̃ vovovowo de Egiptetɔwo dome, wotsrɔ̃ le gbedadaƒo ɖe.

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo, milé dzi ɖe ƒo eye miwɔ ŋutsu. Ne menye nenema o la, míazu Hebritɔwo ƒe kluviwo abe ale si woawo hã wonye míaƒe kluviwo kpɔ ene. Eya ta mitso abe ŋutsuwo ene ne miawɔ aʋa.”

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Woxɔ Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la eye wowu Eli vi eveawo, Xofni kple Pinehas hã. Eli ƒe ku

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe ke la, ŋutsu aɖe, tso Benyamin-to la me, sí tso aʋagbea dzi kple du gbɔ va Silo. Awu vuvu le eŋu eye ke le tame nɛ.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, Eli bɔbɔ nɔ zikpui dzi le agbo nu nɔ mɔ dzi kpɔm, esi wòva, elabe Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la na meɖe dzi ɖi o. Esi ŋutsua ge ɖe dua me gblɔ nu si dzɔ la, ɣli ɖi le du bliboa me hoo.

english_verse: “I escaped from the fighting today and ran here.” “Young man, what happened?” Eli asked.
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsua gblɔ nɛ be: “Ðe mesí le aʋagbea dzi, le du dzi ʋuu va do egbe.” Eli biae be: “Vinye, nya ka dzɔ?”

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Dɔla la ɖo eŋu be: “Israelviwo sí le Filistitɔwo nu. Wowu ame geɖe le mía dome. Viwò ŋutsuvi eveawo, Xofni kple Pinehas, gɔ̃ hã ku, eye woxɔ Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la dzoe.”

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Esi ŋutsua nyayɔ Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la Eli se ko la, edze anyi megbemegbee le zikpuia dzi ɖe agboa nu. Etɔ kɔ anyi, ŋe kɔ eye wòku, elabe ame tsitsi wònye eye kpekpe le eŋu. Ekplɔ Israel-dukɔa ƒe bla ene sɔŋ. Pinehas srɔ̃ ƒe ku

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, fu tsi ɖe Eli toyɔvi, Pinehas srɔ̃, ƒo eye eƒe vidziɣi ɖo. Esi wòse be woxɔ Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la, eye toa kple srɔ̃a ku la, fua de asi eɖuɖu me enumake, eye wòdzi vi.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: Esi wòle kudɔ ƒom la, nyɔnu siwo xe ɖevia nɛ la gblɔ nɛ be: “Mègavɔ̃ o; ŋutsuvie nèdzi.” Ke meɖo nyaa ŋu alo wɔ dzesi aɖeke o.

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Esi Filistitɔwo xɔ Mawu ƒe nubablaɖakaa dzoe la, wokɔe tso Eben-Ezer yi ɖada ɖe Asdod.

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: Wokɔe yi woƒe mawu Dagon ƒe xɔ me, eye wodae ɖe eƒe legba si le afi ma la gbɔ.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Ŋdi kanya la, Asdodtɔwo kpɔ be Dagon mu, tsyɔ mo anyi ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la ŋgɔ. Ale wofɔe dzi gakɔe ɖo eteƒe.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu gake ŋdi kanya la, wokpɔ be Dagon ƒe legba la gamu hetsyɔ mo anyi ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka ŋgɔ. Ta kple abɔ eveawo flí le eŋu, eye wòtsi mɔnu afi ma, takpo kple abɔkpo nogoo ɖi.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: Le esia ta, tso ɣe ma ɣi va se ɖe egbegbe Dagon ƒe trɔ̃nuawo kple ame siwo katã subɔnɛ le trɔ̃ƒe sia le Asdod la daa ata teƒea eye womeɖoa afɔe gbeɖe o.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ he to na Asdodtɔwo vevie, eye wòna vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo ale gbegbe. Ena ƒoƒoe te dua me tɔwo kple ame siwo le woƒe nutowo me.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Esi Asdodtɔwo kpɔ nu si nɔ dzɔdzɔm la, wogblɔ be: “Israel ƒe Mawu la le to hem na mía kple míaƒe mawu Dagon. Mele be eƒe nubablaɖaka la naganɔ mía gbɔ azɔ o.”

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Ale wodɔ ame woyi ɖaƒo Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo katã nu ƒu eye wobia wo be: “Ale ke míele Israel ƒe Mawu la ƒe nubablaɖaka la wɔ gee?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Mitsɔe ɖo ɖe Gat.” Ale wokɔe yi Gat si nye Filistitɔwo ƒe du bubu aɖe.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Ale woawo hã woɖo Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la ɖe Ekron, Filistitɔwo ƒe du bubu. Ke esi Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la va Ekron la, dua me tɔwo do ɣli gblɔ be: “Wotsɔ Israel ƒe Mawu la ƒe nubablaɖaka la ɖo ɖe mí be wòawu mí katã le dua me.”

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Tete wodɔ ame woyi ɖaƒo Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo katã nu ƒu. Wogblɔ be: “Migbugbɔ Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la ɖo ɖe eteƒe, bene magawu mí katã le dua me o.” Elabe vɔvɔ̃ ɖo ame sia ame le dua me kutɔkutɔe elabe Mawu ƒe asi sẽ ɖe wo dzi.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Ame siwo meku o la, ƒoƒoe te woawo hã, eye dua ƒe ɣli de dziƒo.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: Esi Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la tsi Filistitɔwo gbɔ ɣleti adrẽ la,

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo yɔ nunɔlawo kple afakalawo hebia wo be: “Ale ke míele Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la wɔ gee? Migblɔ nu si míatsɔ akpe ɖe eŋu hafi atrɔe yi eteƒe la na mí.”

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Ne miele Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la trɔ ge aɖo ɖa la, migatrɔ eya ɖeɖe ɖo ɖa o. Ele vevie be vɔsanu aɖe si aɖe miaƒe nuvɔ̃ ɖa la nakpe ɖe eŋu godoo. To esia me miaƒe lã me asẽ, eye miadze sii be eya tae Mawu le to hem na mi ɖo.”

english_verse: “What should we send?” the Philistines asked. The priests and fortunetellers answered: There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have.
translation_verse: Wobia be: “Vɔsanu ka míatsɔ akpe ɖe eŋu be wòalé avu le mía kplii dome?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Sikaƒoƒoe atɔ̃ siwo wome kple sikafi atɔ̃ siwo wome ɖe Filistitɔwo ƒe amegã atɔ̃awo nu, elabe dɔ vɔ̃ ɖeka ma tɔgbee dze mi katã kple miaƒe amegãawo dzi.

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: Eya ta ele be miame ƒoƒoeawo kple afi siwo le nuwo gblẽm le anyigbaa dzi la ƒe nɔnɔme, eye miade bubu Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋu. Ðewohĩ ana ale si wòle to hem na miawo ŋutɔ kple miaƒe anyigbaa la dzi naka aɖe.

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Nu ka ta miasẽ to abe Egipte Fiagã kple Egiptetɔwo ene? Esi Mawu do vlo wo vɔ megbe la, womeɖe asi le Israelviwo ŋu wodzo oa?

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: Fifia la, miwɔ tasiaɖam yeye eye midi nyinɔ dzaa eve siwo womede kɔkuti kɔ na kpɔ o. Miɖe wo viwo le wo ŋu de kpɔ me, eye miatsi nyinɔawo ɖe tasiaɖam la ŋu.

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: Mikɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la da ɖe tasiaɖam la me. Mitsɔ nu siwo mieme kple sika be woatsɔ alé avu le mia dome la de aɖaka me da ɖe exa. Ale miado mɔe be wòayi le eɖokui si.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Minɔ ekpɔm; ne èɖo ta wo de, Bet-Semes la, ekema Mawue he dzɔgbevɔ̃e gã siawo va mía dzi. Ne meva eme nenema o la, ekema míanyae be menye Mawue le to hem na mí o, ke boŋ nu dogoɖenunue.”

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Wowɔ nenema; wolé nyinɔ dzaa eve, tsi wo ɖe tasiaɖam la ŋu, eye wolé wo viwo de lãkpɔ me.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la de tasiaɖam la me, eye wotsɔ aɖaka si me afi kple ƒoƒoe siwo wome kple sika la hã ɖo exa.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Enumake nyinɔawo ɖo ta mɔ gã si yi Bet-Semes la dzi tututu; womedze ɖe ɖusime alo miame o. Nyiawo nɔ xɔxlɔ̃m le mɔa dzi. Filisti-fiaawo le wo yome ʋuu va se ɖe Bet-Semes ƒe liƒo dzi.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, Bet-Semestɔwo nɔ bali me nɔ lu ŋem. Kasia woafɔ kɔ dzi la, nubablaɖaka la nye esi do. Esi wokpɔe la, dzi dzɔ wo ŋutɔ.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo ƒe fia atɔ̃awo kpɔ nu si wowɔ la teƒe, eye wotrɔ yi Ekron gbe ma gbe ke.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Sikaƒoƒoe siwo Filistitɔwo ɖo ɖe Aƒetɔ be woalé avu le wo dome la, wowɔ wo ɖe Asdod, Gaza, Askalon, Gat kple Ekron duwo nu.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Nenema ke wotsɔ sikafi ɖekaɖeka ɖe Filisti fiadu atɔ̃awo, du gã siwo woɖo gli ƒo xlã kple kɔƒe siwo ŋu womeɖo gli ɖo o la nu ɖo ɖa. Kpe gã si dzi wokɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka da ɖo le Bet-Semestɔ, Yosua ƒe agble me la gali abe ŋkuɖodzikpe ene va se ɖe egbe.

english_verse: Some of the men of Beth-Shemesh looked inside the sacred chest, and the Lord God killed
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ wu Bet-Semestɔ bla adrẽ elabe wokpɔ eƒe nubablaɖaka la me. Dua me tɔwo fa konyi vevie le ame siwo ku le wo dome la ta. Woɖo nubablaɖaka la ɖe Kiriat-Yearim

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Bet-Semestɔwo bia be: “Ame ka ate ŋu anɔ te ɖe Aƒetɔ, Mawu kɔkɔe la nu? Tso mía gbɔ la, ame ka gbɔ míaɖoe ɖo?”

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Ale wodɔ dɔlawo ɖo ɖe Kiriat-Yearimtɔwo be: “Filistitɔwo gbugbɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la ɖo ɖa. Miva kɔe yi mia gbɔe.”

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Tete Kiriat-Yearimtɔwo va kɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la yi ɖada ɖe Abinadab ƒeme le togbɛ dzi. Wokɔ̀ via Eleazar ŋu be wòakpɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖakaa dzi. Samuel zu Israel-dukɔ la kplɔla

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Samuel gblɔ na Israel-dukɔ blibo la be: “Nenye Aƒetɔ ŋue miele tɔtrɔm ɖo kple miaƒe dzi blibo la, ele be miaɖe mawu ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi ɖa le mia dome. Miɖe asi le nyɔnumawu Astarte ƒe legbawo gɔ̃ hã ŋu. Mina miaƒe dzi nalé ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu, eye miasubɔ eya ɖeka ko, ekema aɖe mi tso Filistitɔwo si me.”

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Ale Israeltɔwo ɖe Baal ƒe legbawo kple nyɔnumawu Astarte ƒe legbawo ɖa le wo dome eye wosubɔ Aƒetɔ ɖeka ko.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Emegbe Samuel ɖo gbe ɖe Israeltɔwo katã be: “Miva ƒo ƒu ɖe Mizpa ne mado gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ ɖe mia ta.”

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Ale wo katã va ƒo ƒu ɖe Mizpa. Woku tsi, ƒoe ɖe anyi na Aƒetɔ, tsi nu dɔ gbe ma gbe hegblɔ be: “Míewɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu.” Mizpa, afi siae Samuel drɔ̃ Israeltɔwo ƒe nyawo le.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Esi Filistitɔwo se be Israelviwo kpe ta le Mizpa la, woƒe fiawo ho ɖe wo ŋu. Israelviwo vɔ̃ Filistitɔwo ŋutɔ, esi wose nya sia.

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na Samuel be: “Mègadzudzɔ kokoƒoƒo na Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la, ɖe mía ta o, be wòaxɔ na mí tso Filistitɔwo si me.”

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Esime Samuel le numemevɔsa la wɔm la, Filistitɔwo ho va gogo Israeltɔwo be yewoawɔ aʋa kpli wo. Tete Aƒetɔ ɖe gbe ɖe Filistitɔwo dzi sesĩe, eye wotɔtɔ hesí le Israeltɔwo nu.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Israeltɔwo kplɔ wo ɖo tso Mizpa ʋuu va se ɖe esime wogogo Bet-Kar. Wowu wo dometɔ geɖe le mɔ dzi.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Wogbugbɔ du siwo woxɔ le Israelviwo si tso Ekron va ɖo Gat la na wo. Ale woƒe anyigba si Filistitɔwo xɔ la gaɖo wo si. Ŋutifafa nɔ Israeltɔwo kple Amoritɔwo dome azɔ.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Samuel kplɔ Israel-dukɔ le eƒe agbenɔɣi katã.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Ƒe sia ƒe la, Samuel yia Betel, Gilgal kple Mizpa siwo nye duwo le eƒe dziɖuɖu te la ɖadrɔ̃a ʋɔnu le afi mawo.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: Emegbe egatrɔna vaa Rama, afi si eƒe xɔnu le, eye wòdrɔ̃a ʋɔnu na Israelviwo le afi ma. Eɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afi ma na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: Via ŋutsu ŋgɔgbea ŋkɔ nye Yoel, eye eyometɔ ŋkɔ nye Abiya. Wonye ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo nɔ Beer-Seba.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Ke viawo meto eƒe ʋe me o. Woti ga yome, xɔ zãnu eye womedrɔ̃a ʋɔnu dzɔdzɔe o.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Ale Israel-megãwo katã kpe ta eye woyi Samuel gbɔ le Rama

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: ɖagblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, fifia ètsi eye viwòwo meto wò ʋe me o. Ðo fia na mí be wòaɖu mía dzi abe ale si wòle le dukɔ bubuwo me ene.”

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Esi wogblɔ na Samuel be neɖo fia na yewo be wòaɖu yewo dzi la, medze eŋu o. Ale Samuel do gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Ðo to nya sia nya si dukɔa agblɔ na wò eye nàwɔ edzi, elabe menye wòe wogbe o, ke boŋ nyee wogbe be magaɖu fia ɖe yewo dzi o.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Ale si wowɔ ɖe ŋunye, gbem, hele mawu bubuwo subɔm tso gbe si gbe mekplɔ wo tso Egipte va se ɖe fifi la, nenema tututu wɔm wole ɖe wò hã ŋuwò.

english_verse: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
translation_verse: Eya ta ɖo to wo. Ke ɖe nya me na wo nyuie do ŋgɔ le ale si fia si biam wole la le wo dzi ɖu gee la ŋu.”

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Ale Samuel gblɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nyawo katã na dukɔ si le ebiam be wòaɖo fia na yewo la.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: “Nu siwo wɔ ge fia si le mia dzi ɖu ge la le lae nye ana miaƒe ŋutsuviwo azu asrafowo. Ðewo anɔ tasiaɖamwo me, ɖewo anye sɔdolawo eye bubuwo anɔ du ƒum le tasiaɖamwo ŋgɔ.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
