translation_verse: Fia la axɔ mia vinyɔnuwo. Ðewo anɔ ami ʋeʋẽe sim nɛ, ɖewo anye eƒe nuɖalawo eye bubuwo anye eƒe aboloƒolawo.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: Axɔ miaƒe agble nyuitɔwo, waingblewo kple amitibɔwo le mia si atsɔ na eƒe subɔlawo.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: Axɔ nuku siwo mieŋe kple miaƒe wain ƒe akpa ewolia atsɔ na eƒe dumegãwo kple dɔlawo.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: Azi miaƒe ŋutsu kple nyɔnu apatɔwo, ɖekakpui zazɛ̃wo kple tedziwo dzi be woawɔ dɔ nɛ.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Axɔ miaƒe lãha ƒe akpa ewolia hã eye miazu eƒe kluviwo.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, miaxa nu ayɔ Mawu le fia si miawo ŋutɔ mietia la ta, ke Aƒetɔ maɖo to mi o.”

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: ale be míawo hã míanɔ abe dukɔ bubuwo ene. Aɖu mía dzi eye wòanɔ ŋgɔ akplɔ mí ayi aʋa aɖawɔ aʋa na mí.”

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Samuel ɖo to se woƒe nyawo katã eye wòyi ɖagblɔ wo na Aƒetɔ ake.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Samuel be: “Wɔ ɖe woƒe didi dzi. Ðo fia na wo.” Ale Samuel gblɔ na Israelviwo be ame sia ame negbugbɔ yi eƒe du me.

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Kesinɔtɔ aɖe nɔ Benyamin-to la me. Eŋkɔe nye Kis, tɔ́ae nye Abiel eye tɔgbuiae nye Zeror. Zeror tɔ́e nye Bexorat, ame si nye Afia vi.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: Viŋutsuvi dzeɖekɛ aɖe si ɖo ɖekakpuime la le esi. Eŋkɔe nye Saul. Enyakpɔ ale gbegbe be ame aɖeke medze ɖeka wui le Israelviwo dome o. Saul kɔ ŋutɔ; ame kɔkɔtɔ kekeake le Israel-dukɔ me se abɔta ko nɛ.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Eva ve me gbe ɖeka be Kis ƒe tedzinɔ aɖewo bu. Ale wògblɔ na via Saul be: “Yɔ dɔlawo dometɔ ɖeka kpe ɖe ɖokuiwò ŋu, ne miayi aɖadi tedzinɔawo vɛ.”

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Woyi ɖatsa le Efrayim-tonyigba dzi kple Salisa-nutome, ke womekpɔ wo o. Woyi dzi ɖadi wo le Benyamin-nutome hã, gake womekpɔ wo le afi ma hã o.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Esi woɖo Zuf-nyigba dzi la, Saul gblɔ na dɔla si kpe ɖe eŋu la be: “Na míatrɔ ayi aƒe, ne menye nenem o la, tɔ́nye ava tsi dzi ɖe míawo boŋ ŋu, eye maganye ɖe tedzinɔawo ŋu o.”

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Tete dɔla la gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, mawunua aɖe, si xɔ ŋkɔ ŋutɔ la le du sia me. Nya sia nya si wògblɔ la vaa me. Na míayi egbɔ le afi ma. Ðewohĩ ate ŋu agblɔ nu si ƒe afɔ dzi míele la na mí.”

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Saul bia eƒe dɔlaa be: “Ne míeyi ɖe, nu ka míatsɔ ɖe asi aɖanae? Elabe nuɖuɖu si míetsɔ ɖe asi la vɔ, eye naneke meli míatsɔ ana mawunua la o. Nu kae le mia sí?”

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Dɔlaa ɖo eŋu be: “Klosaloga memama akpa enelia le asinye. Matsɔe na mawunua la be wòafia afi si míaɖo tae la mí.”

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Esi wolia togbɛa yina la, wodo go ɖetugbi aɖewo siwo yina tsi du ge. Wobia ɖetugbiawo se be: “Nukpɔla le dua mea?”

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Ẽ, eli. Eyae nye ekem le mia ŋgɔ. Afɔ netsɔ na mi. Fifi laa ko wòva dua me elabe dua me tɔwo le vɔ sa ge egbe le toa dzi.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Ne mieɖo kaba la, miakpɔe hafi wòayi aɖaɖu nu le vɔsaƒea, elabe dua me tɔwo maɖu nu o, va se ɖe esime wòɖo afi ma. Eyae yraa vɔsanua hafi woɖunɛ. Emegbe la, ame kpekpeawo ɖua nua. Eya ta miheyi elabe miele go do gee le afi ma fifia.”

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Ale woɖo ta dua me. Esi woɖo la, wodo go Samuel le mɔ dzi woyina vɔsaƒea.

english_verse: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
translation_verse: Azɔ hafi ŋu nake ne Saul nava la, Aƒetɔ ɖe nu fia Samuel be:

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: “Etsɔ ɣe alewo ɣi la, madɔ ŋutsu aɖe tso Benyamin-to la me ɖe wò. Si ami nɛ be wòazu amegã ɖe nye dukɔ Israel nu. Eyae axɔ na dukɔ la tso Filistitɔwo si me, elabe menya woƒe fukpekpewo eye woƒe ɣlidodo ɖi mese.”

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Esi Samuel kpɔ Saul la, Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Samuel be: “Ame si ŋu meƒo nu le na wò lae nye esi. Eyae aɖu fia ɖe nye dukɔa dzi.”

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Tete Saul te ɖe Samuel ŋu le agboa nu hebiae be: “Meɖe kuku, afi kae nye nukpɔla ƒe aƒeme?”

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Samuel ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Nyee nye nukpɔla la. Midze ŋgɔnye yi vɔsaƒea. Egbea miaɖu nu kplim. Etsɔ ŋdi la, mado mɔ wò eye magblɔ nya siwo katã le wò tame la na wò, eyome mado mɔ wò.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Azɔ mègatsi dzi ɖe tedzinɔ siwo bu egbe ŋkeke etɔ̃ sɔŋ nye esi la ŋu o, elabe wokpɔ wo xoxo. Evɔ ɖe, ame ka gɔ̃ Israelviwo katã tsi dzi le didim vevie alea? Ðe menye wò kple tɔ́wò ƒe aƒe lae oa?”

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Saul ɖo eŋu be: “Benyamin-to si nye suetɔ kekeake le Israel-dukɔa me la mee metso. Nye ƒome la hãe nye gblɔetɔ wu le Benyamin-to ƒe ƒomeawo dome. Nya ka nye esi gblɔm nèle nam?”

english_verse: Samuel took Saul and his servant into the dining room at the place of worship. About
translation_verse: Tete Samuel kplɔ Saul kple eƒe dɔlaa yi ɖe xɔa me, eye wòna nɔƒe wo le kplɔ̃a ta, le ame kpekpe siwo anɔ bla etɔ̃ la dome.

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Ale nuɖalaa tsɔ lã ƒe ata kple nu siwo kpe ɖe eŋu la va ɖo Saul kɔme. Samuel gblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, lã si wodzra ɖo na wò la nye esi. Tsɔe ɖu. Wòe wodzrae ɖo ɖi na va se ɖe fifi be nàɖu kple ame kpekpeawo.” Ale Saul ɖu nu kple Samuel gbe ma gbe.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Esi wotrɔ tso vɔsaƒea va ɖo dua me la, Samuel ƒo nu kple Saul le xɔta, eye wòtsi afi ma dɔ. Samuel si ami na Saul wòzu fia

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Fɔŋli la, Samuel yɔ Saul le xɔta la hegblɔ nɛ be: “Fɔ ne mado mɔ wò.” Saul fɔ eye eya kple Samuel do ɖe mɔ dzi.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Esi woɖo dua ƒe gbɔto la, Samuel gblɔ na Saul be: “Gblɔe na dɔla la be nedo ŋgɔ na mí.” Dɔlaa dze ŋgɔ. “Wò ŋutɔ tɔ vie, ne magblɔ nya si Mawu be magblɔ la na wò.”

english_verse: Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him: The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people.
translation_verse: Tete Samuel tsɔ amigoe eye wòkɔ ami ɖe tame na Saul. Egbugbɔ nu nɛ hegblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ si ami na wò be nàzu amegã ɖe yeƒe dukɔ Israel dzi. Àɖu dukɔa dzi eye àʋli wo ta tso woƒe futɔwo katã si me. Dzesi si le kpe ɖom esia dzi be Aƒetɔ si ami na wò be nànye amegã ɖe yeƒe domenyinu dzi lae nye be:

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: Ne èdzo le gbɔnye egbe la, àkpɔ ame eve le Raxel ƒe yɔdo gbɔ le Zelzax le Benyamin-nyigba dzi. Woagblɔ na wo be: ‘Wokpɔ tedzinɔ siwo di ge nèyi la. Fifia la tɔ́wò megatsi dzi ɖe wo ta o, ke boŋ etsi dzimaɖi ɖe tawò le gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Nya ka dzɔ ɖe vinye dzi?’

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: Ne ètso le afi ma la, àva ɖo logotia gbɔ le Tabor. Ŋutsu etɔ̃ siwo yina vɔ sa ge na Mawu le Betel la ava do go wò le afi ma. Ðeka alé gbɔ̃vi etɔ̃ ɖe ta, evelia atsɔ abolo etɔ̃ eye lãgbalẽgolo si me wain le la anɔ etɔ̃lia si.

english_verse: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
translation_verse: Woado gbe na wò ahana abolo eve wò. Xɔ wo le wo si.

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: Emegbe àva Gibea-Elohim, afi si Filistitɔwo da dzɔlawo ɖo. Ne èle gegem ɖe dua me la, àdo go Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo ƒe ha aɖe si ɖi tso vɔsaƒea la gbɔna. Kasaŋku, axatsɛ, dze kple saŋkuwo anɔ ɖiɖim le wo ŋgɔ eye woanɔ gbeƒã ɖem.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Enumake eƒe gbɔgbɔ adze dziwò, àtrɔ zu ame bubu sãa eye wò hã àde asi gbeƒãɖeɖe me kpli wo.

english_verse: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
translation_verse: Azɔ ne dzesi siawo le me vam la, wɔ nu sia nu si nèlɔ̃ elabe Mawu li kpli wò.

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: Ekem do ŋgɔ nànɔ Gilgal yim. Megbɔna gbɔwò ava eme nu, eye masa ŋutifafavɔ na Mawu. Lalam ŋkeke adrẽ va se ɖe esime mava gblɔ nu si nàwɔ la na wò.”

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Esi Saul trɔ be yeadzo le Samuel gbɔ la, Mawu na Saul ƒe nɔnɔme trɔ, eye dzesi siwo ŋu Samuel ƒo nu le la va eme gbe ma gbe.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi wòva toa dzi la, kpɔ ɖa, Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo ƒe ha aɖe va do goe. Enumake Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ dze edzi kple ŋusẽ eye wòɖe gbeƒã le wo dome.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Ke esi ame siwo katã dze sii tsã la kpɔe wòle gbeƒã ɖem le Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo dome la, wobia wo nɔewo be: “Nu kae le Kis vi la wɔm? Saul hã ye le Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo domea?”

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Ŋutsu aɖe si tso dua me la bia be: “Ame ka gɔ̃e nye ame siawo tɔ́?” Esia va zu lo wodona le wo dome ɖaa be: “Saul hã ye le Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo domea?”

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Esi wòɖe gbeƒãa vɔ la, eyi vɔsaƒea.

english_verse: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
translation_verse: Saul nyrui kpɔ eya kple eƒe dɔla la eye wòbia wo be: “Afi ka mietso?” Saul ɖo eŋu be: “Míetso tedzinɔawo di ge. Esi míele wo kpɔm o la, míeyi Samuel gbɔ.”

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Saul nyruia bia be: “Nya ka wògblɔ na mi?”

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ nɛ be: “Egblɔ na mí kɔtɛe be wokpɔ tedziawo xoxo.” Gake megblɔ nya siwo Samuel gblɔ nɛ tso eya ŋutɔ ƒe fiaɖuɖu ŋu ya la, ƒe ɖeke nɛ o. Woɖe gbeƒã be woɖo Saul fiae

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Azɔ Samuel yɔ Israel-dukɔ la ƒo ƒu hena ŋkekenyui ɖuɖu le Mizpa,

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: ‘Mekplɔ mi do go tso Egipte-nyigba dzi, eye meɖe mi tso Egiptetɔwo si me. Nye kee ɖe mi tso dziɖula siwo nɔ mia tem ɖe anyi la hã si me.

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: Ke egbe la, miegbe nye, miaƒe Mawu, si ɖe mi tso miaƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃ewo kple hiãwo katã me la, eye miebiam be maɖo fia na yewo. Eya ta miva ɖo ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋkume ɖe miaƒe towo kple ame akpeakpeawo nu.’ ”

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Ale Samuel na Israel-toawo katã te va ŋgɔ, eye wodzidze nu. Nudzidze la dze Benyamin-to la dzi.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Ena Benyamin-to la me tɔwo do va ŋgɔ ɖe woƒe ƒomeawo nu, eye wodzidze nu wòdze Matri ƒe ƒome la dzi. Esi wodzidze nu ɖe ƒomea me nɔlawo dzi la, nudzidze la dze Saul, Kis vi dzi. Wodii, ke womekpɔe o.

english_verse: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
translation_verse: Ale wogabia nu Aƒetɔ be: “Ɖe ame la va afi siaa?” Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu be: “Kpɔ ɖa, Saul bè ɖe agbaawo totro me.”

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Ale woƒu du yi ɖakplɔe tso afi ma vɛ. Esi wòtsi tsitre ɖe ameawo dome la, ame kɔkɔtɔwo se abɔta nɛ.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Azɔ Samuel gblɔ na dukɔ la be: “Ame si Aƒetɔ tia lae nye esi! Ame aɖeke mesɔ kplii le dukɔa me o.” Tete ameawo katã do ɣli hoo be: “Fia nenɔ agbe tegbee!”

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Azɔ Samuel xlẽ fiaɖuɖu ŋuti kɔnuwo katã fia dukɔ la. Eŋlɔ wo ɖe agbalẽ me hetsɔ da ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Emegbe Samuel ɖe asi le ame sia ame ŋu wòtrɔ yi eƒeme.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Saul hã trɔ yi enɔƒe le Gibea. Kalẽtɔ aɖewo, siwo ƒe dzi Mawu ʋã la yi kplii.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Ke ame vlo aɖewo gblɔ be: “Ale ke ame sia ate ŋu axɔ na mí?” Wodo vloe eye wometsɔ nunana aɖeke vɛ nɛ o. Ke elé eɖokui kpoo abe ɖe mesee o ene.

english_verse: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
translation_verse: Emegbe ʋɛ la, Nahas, Amon-fia ho aʋa ɖe Yabes-du le Gilead-nutome ŋu eye eƒe asrafowo ɖe to ɖe dua. Tete Yabes-ŋutsuwo katã gblɔ na Nahas be: “Bla nu kpli mí ekema míana nàzu mía dziɖula.”

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Ke Nahas ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Hafi mabla nu kpli mi la, ele be miana maŋɔ mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ƒe ɖusimeŋku ale be mado ŋukpe Israel-dukɔ blibo la.”

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Tete Yabes-me tsitsiwo gblɔ nɛ be: “Taflatsɛ, kpɔ mía sinu ŋkeke adrẽ ne míadɔ ame ɖe afi sia afi le Israel-nyigba bliboa dzi. Ne míekpɔ ame aɖeke wòava xɔ na mí o la, ekem míana ta.”

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Amedɔdɔawo ɖo Gibea, afi si Saul le. Esi wogblɔ nya la dua me tɔwo se la, wowó avi hoo.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, Saul kplɔ nyiwo tso gbedzi gbɔna dua mee. Ebia be: “Nya ka dzɔ amewo le avi fam ale?” Wogblɔ nya si Yabestɔwo tsɔ vɛ la nɛ.

english_verse: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
translation_verse: Esi wòse nyaa la, Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ dze edzi, eye dzi kui vevie ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: Enumake wòlé nyi eve, fli wo kakɛkakɛe, eye wòtsɔ wo de amewo si be woatsɔ ayi Israel-nyigba ƒe akpa sia akpa. Egblɔ kpe ɖe eŋu be: “Ame si metso va dze Saul kple Samuel yome yi aʋa o la, alea tututu woawɔ eya hã ƒe nyiwoe.” Israel-dukɔa vɔ̃ nu si Aƒetɔ awɔ, eya ta wo katã wodo bibibi.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Azɔ wogblɔ na amedɔdɔ siwo tso Yabes va la be: “Miyi ɖagblɔ na Yabestɔwo be hafi ɣe naɖo ta etsɔ la, woava xɔ na wo!” Esi amedɔdɔawo va gblɔ nya la na Yabestɔwo la, dzi dzɔ wo ŋutɔ,

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: eye wogblɔ na Nahas be: “Etsɔ la, míatsɔ mía ɖokui ade asi na wò be nàwɔ nu sia nu si dze ŋuwò la mí.”

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke ŋdi la, Saul ma ameawo ɖe aʋalɔgo etɔ̃ me. Wolũ ɖe Amontɔwo dzi le asaɖaa me le fɔŋli, eye wode asi wo wuwu me va se ɖe ŋdɔ me. Ame siwo susɔ la ka hlẽ ɖekaɖeka dzo: ame eve mekpɔtɔ ɖe teƒe ɖeka o.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Emegbe Israelviwo bia Samuel be: “Ame kawoe gblɔ be Saul maɖu fia ɖe mía dzi o? Kplɔ wo vɛ míawu.”

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Ke Saul gblɔ be: “Womawu ame aɖeke egbe o, elabe egbeae Aƒetɔ ɖe Israel-dukɔ la.”

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Tete Samuel gblɔ na dukɔ la be: “Miva míyi Gilgal ne míagbugbɔ fiaɖoɖo kɔnuawo agawɔ ake.”

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Ale dukɔ blibo la yi Gilgal, eye woɖo fia Saul le afi ma le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Wosa ŋutifafavɔ le afi ma, eye Saul kple Israel-dukɔ blibo la kpɔ dzidzɔ ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Samuel told the Israelites: I have given you a king, just as you asked.
translation_verse: Azɔ Samuel gblɔ na Israel-dukɔ blibo la be: “Mikpɔ ɖa, mewɔ nu siwo katã miedi be mawɔ na mi la na mi, eye meɖo fia na mi;

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: eya akplɔ mi azɔ. Nye la metsi, ƒo wɔ. Vinyewo le mia dome. Mekplɔ mi abe miaƒe nunɔla ene tso keke nye ɖekakpuime ke va se ɖe fifi.

english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: Nyee nye esi. Ne mewɔ vɔ̃ aɖe la, migblɔe le Aƒetɔ kple fia si nye eƒe amesiamina la ŋkume. Mexɔ ame aɖe ƒe nyitsu alo eƒe tedzia? Ame kae meba alo te ɖe to? Ame ka si mexɔ zãnu le be nyemakpɔ nya dzɔdzɔe o? Migblɔe ne maɖo eteƒe na amea.”

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord and his chosen king are witnesses to what you have said.” “That's true,” they replied.
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ na wo be: “Aƒetɔ kple fia, eƒe amesiamina la, nye miaƒe ɖasefowo egbe be miekpɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke le ŋunye o.” Wogblɔ be: “Nyateƒee. Aƒetɔ e nye míaƒe ɖasefo.”

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ na wo yi edzi be: “Aƒetɔ lae nye ame si tia Mose kple Aron, eye wokplɔ mia tɔgbuiwo do go tso Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: Eya ta miva ɖo ɖe afii ne maxlẽ dɔ siwo Aƒetɔ wɔ xɔ na mi kple mia tɔgbuiwo la afia mi le eŋkume.

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: Esi Yakob kple eƒe ƒomea yi ɖe Egipte, eye Egiptetɔwo te wo ɖe anyi la, wodo ɣli yɔ Aƒetɔ. Tete Aƒetɔ dɔ Mose kple Aron ɖa woyi ɖakplɔ wo tso Egipte va teƒe sia.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: Ke woŋlɔ Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la be. Ale wòɖe asi le wo ŋu, eye wòna Filistitɔwo kple Moab-fia kpakple Sisera, Xazor-du ƒe aʋakplɔla wɔ aʋa kpli wo.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Wodo ɣli yɔ Aƒetɔ gblɔ be: ‘Míewɔ nuvɔ̃ elabe míegblẽ Aƒetɔ ɖi, eye míesubɔ Baal kple nyɔnumawu Astarte ƒe legbawo. Ke azɔ la, ɖe mí tso míaƒe futɔwo si me eye míasubɔ wò.’

english_verse: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ dɔ Yerub-Baal, Bedan, Yefta kple Samuel ɖa, wova ɖe mi tso miaƒe futɔ siwo ƒo xlã mi godoo la si me, eye mienɔ anyi le dziɖeɖi me.

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Ke esi miekpɔ be Amontɔwo ƒe fia Nahas ɖo be yeawɔ aʋa kple mi la, miegbe Aƒetɔ, miaƒe fia eye miegblɔ nam be: ‘Ðo fia na mí wòaɖu mía dzi.’

english_verse: You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king.
translation_verse: “Mikpɔ ɖa, fia si mietia lae nye esi. Eyae miebia eye azɔ la, Aƒetɔ tsɔe na mi.

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Ne mi kple fia si le mia dzi ɖum la mianɔ Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la yome, avɔ̃e, asubɔe, ase eƒe gbe eye miadze aglã ɖe eƒe seawo ŋu o la, nu sia nu adze edzi na mi.

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Gake ne miase Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe o, ke boŋ miadze aglã ɖe eƒe seawo ŋu la, ekem Aƒetɔ ahe to na mi kple miaƒe fia la.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: Azɔ minɔ te ne miakpɔ nu gã si wɔ ge Aƒetɔ ala le mia ŋkume teƒe la ɖa.

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: Dzomeŋɔli nye esia eye miele lu ŋem egbe. Gake mele egblɔ ge na Aƒetɔ wòana dzi naɖe gbe, tsi nadza. Ne eva eme la, ekem miadze sii be enye nuvɔ̃ɖi ŋutɔ miewɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu be miebiae be wòaɖo fia na mi.”

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Ale Samuel do gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ. Tete dzi ɖe gbe eye tsi dza gbe ma gbe. Ameawo katã vɔ̃ Aƒetɔ kple Samuel.

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la katã gblɔ na Samuel be: “Ðe kuku na Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la, ɖe mí wò dɔlawo ta be míagaku o. Míekpɔe dze sii azɔ be míewɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi kpe míaƒe nuvɔ̃wo le esi míebia be woaɖo fia na mí ta.”

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Samuel ɖo eŋu na dukɔ la be: “Migavɔ̃ o. Togbɔ be miewɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi sia gbegbe hã la, migagbugbɔ le Aƒetɔ yome o, ke boŋ misubɔe kple dzi blibo.

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Migatrɔ dze nu dzodzro siwo me viɖe aɖeke mele o, eye womate ŋu aɖe mi hã o la yome o, elabe nu dzodzrowo ko wonye.

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Le Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ ŋkɔ ta la, mate ŋu aɖe asi le eƒe dukɔ ŋu o elabe eya ŋutɔe ɖoe be yeawɔ mi mianye eƒe dukɔ.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: Ke le gonyeme ya la, megava eme gbeɖe be mawɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu, be magbe kukuɖeɖe ɖe mia ta o; ke boŋ mafia mɔ nyui dzɔdzɔetɔ la ɖeɖe ko mi.

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Miawo ya miɖo ŋui miavɔ̃ Aƒetɔ, eye miasubɔe nyateƒetɔe kple dzi blibo, elabe miekpɔ nu gã siwo wòwɔ na mi la.

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Gake ne miegawɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi la, mia kple miaƒe fia la siaa miatsrɔ̃.”

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Israelviwo katã see be Saul wu Filistitɔwo ƒe asrafo siwo nye dzɔlawo, eye wose hã be yewoƒe nu le dzi kum na Filistitɔwo. Tete woyɔ ameawo wova ƒo ƒu ɖe Saul gbɔ le Gilgal.

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: Wodze Israelviwo dzi hemimi wo, eye esi wokpɔ be nu le yewo glom la, wo dometɔ aɖewo sí yi ɖabè ɖe agadowo kple kpetowo me. Ðewo bè ɖe kpewo dome le ʋewo kple vudowo me.

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: Ame bubuwo tso Yordan-tɔsisi la yi Gad kple Gilead nutowo me. Ke Saul ya ganɔ Gilgal ko, eye ame siwo le eyome nɔ vɔvɔ̃m ale gbegbe.

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: Elala ŋkeke adrẽ sɔŋ abe ale si Samuel ɖo nɛ la ene, ke Samuel meva ɖo Gilgal kpɔ o. Tete eyomedzelawo de asi dzodzo me le egbɔ.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Ale Saul gblɔ be: “Mitsɔ lã si woame asa vɔe kple esiwo woatsɔ ada akpee la vɛ nam.” Eme lã la tsɔ va sa vɔe.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: Esa vɔa vɔ teti ko Samuel nye esi va do. Saul do go yi ɖakpee hedo gbe nɛ.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Ke Samuel biae be: “Nu ka nèwɔ?” Saul ɖo eŋu be: “Ameawo nɔ dzodzom le gbɔnye, eye mèva ɖo abe ale si nègblɔ nam la ene o. Hekpe ɖe esia ŋu la, Filistitɔwo va ƒo ƒu ɖe Mixmas.

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: Ale mebu be wogbɔna mía dzi dze ge le Gilgal; evɔ la, nyemebia Aƒetɔ ƒe kpekpeɖeŋu o. Eya ta mezi ɖokuinye dzi hesa numemevɔ na Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Samuel ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Èwɔ movinu. Mèwɔ ɖe se si Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la de na wò la dzi o. Ðe nèwɔ edzi la, anye ne Aƒetɔ ana wò fiaɖuɖu nali ke le Israel-nyigba dzi tegbee.

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la, wò fiaɖuɖu manɔ anyi ɖaa o. Aƒetɔ tia ame bubu si ƒe nu dze eŋu eye wòɖoe fiae ɖe eƒe dukɔ la nu, elabe mèlé nu si wòɖo na wò la me ɖe asi o.”

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Tete Samuel trɔ tso Gilgal yi Gibea le Benyamin-nutome. Saul xlẽ ame siwo susɔ ɖe egbɔ la, eye wole asrafo alafa ade ko.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Saul kple via Yonatan kpakple asrafo siwo tsi eŋu la ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Geba le Benyamin-nutome. Ke Filistitɔwo ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Mixmas.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Filisti-srafowo ma ɖe aʋalɔgo etɔ̃ me, eye woyi ɖanɔ nu gblẽm le Israelviwo ŋu. Aʋalɔgo ɖeka ɖo ta Ofra le Sual-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: Evelia yi Bet-Xoron-nutome eye etɔ̃lia ɖo ta liƒo si dzi nànɔ akpɔ Zeboim-bali me kple gbedadaƒo la.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Azɔ nutula aɖeke menɔ Israel-nyigba blibo la dzi o. Ale Filistitɔwo bu be, ne ɖe woli la, anye ne Israelviwo atu yi kple akplɔ na wo ɖokui.

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Ale gbe si gbe wokpe aʋa la, yi alo akplɔ menɔa Israel-srafo aɖeke si o, negbe Saul kple via Yonatan si ko wonɔna.

english_verse: The Philistines moved their camp to the pass at Michmash,
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo dɔ asrafoha aɖe ɖa be woaɖadzɔ Mixmas todomemɔ ŋu.

english_verse: Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
translation_verse: Esi le dzigbeme lɔƒo la dze ŋgɔ Mixmas, eye esi le anyigbeme la dze ŋgɔ Geba.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Yonatan gblɔ na eƒe adekplɔvi la be: “Va míyi bolobolotɔ siawo ƒe asaɖa la me. Ðewohĩ Aƒetɔ awɔ aʋa ɖe mía nu elabe naneke mexe mɔ nɛ be wòato ame geɖe alo ame ʋɛ aɖe dzi aɖe ame o.”

english_verse: “Do whatever you want,” the soldier answered. “I'll be right there with you.”
translation_verse: Eƒe adekplɔvi la gblɔ nɛ be: “Wɔ nu si wò susu gblɔ na wò. Nye la meli kpli wò be mawɔ nu si nèdi la.”

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Yonatan gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, míeyina ɖe ameawo gbɔ eye míana woakpɔ mí.

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: Ne wogblɔ be mítɔ ne yewoava mía gbɔ la, ekema míatɔ te ɖe afi si míele, eye míayi wo gbɔ o.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Evɔ ne woyɔ mí be míava yewo gbɔ la, ekem míayi elabe ema anye dzesi na mí afia be Aƒetɔ tsɔ wo de mía si.”

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier stood at the bottom of the hill where the Philistines could see them. The Philistines said, “Look! Those worthless Israelites have crawled out of the holes where they've been hiding.” Then they yelled down to Jonathan and the soldier, “Come up here, and we will teach you a thing or two!” Jonathan turned to the soldier and said, “Follow me! The Lord is going to let us win.”
translation_verse: Tete dzɔlawo gblɔ sesĩe ɖo ɖe Yonatan kple adekplɔvi la be: “Miva mía gbɔ ne míagblɔ nya aɖe na mi.” Ale Yonatan gblɔ na eƒe adekplɔvi la be: “Dze yonyeme, elabe Aƒetɔ tsɔ wo de Israel si me.”

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Tete Yonatan ta, asi kple afɔ, lia to la eye eƒe adekplɔvi la kplɔe ɖo. Yonatan ƒo dzɔlawo ƒu anyi eye eƒe adekplɔvi la wu wo le eyome.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: Ðe aʋakɔ la ɖu aboyonu si woxɔ le woƒe futɔwo si egbea faa la, ne enyo wu ɖe! Anye ne wotsrɔ̃ Filistitɔ geɖe ɖe!”

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Tete Saul kple aʋakɔ blibo la lũ ɖe wo dzi hekpe aʋa kpli wo. Va kpɔ, Filistitɔwo tɔtɔ nyamanyama eye wo dome ame sia ame tsɔ yi ɖe nɔvia ŋu.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Ŋɔdzi ɖo asaɖa la kple nutoa me eye dzidzi ƒo ameawo. Dzidzi ƒo dzɔlawo kple aʋamenuhalawo gɔ̃ hã wodzo nyànyanya. Anyigba ʋuʋu eye wòzu zitɔtɔ gã aɖe ŋutɔ. Woɖu Filistitɔwo dzi

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Kasia Saul ƒe gbetakpɔla siwo le Gibea le Benyamin-nutome nakpɔ la, ameha la ka hlẽ kple du. Ne ame si to afii, ame kem nato afi mɛ.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Saul ɖe gbe na eŋunɔlawo be: “Mixlẽ asrafoawo ne miakpɔ ɖa be ame aɖe bu le mía dome hã.” Esi woxlẽ ameawo la, wokpɔ be Yonatan kple eƒe adekplɔvi meli o.

english_verse: At that time, Ahijah was serving as priest for the army of Israel, and Saul told him, “Come over here! Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Ale Saul gblɔ na Axiya be: “Tsɔ Mawu ƒe aɖaka la va afii” elabe Mawu ƒe aɖaka la nɔ Israelviwo gbɔ le ɣe ma ɣi me.

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: Esime Saul nɔ nu ƒom na nunɔla la, hoowɔwɔ la nu ganɔ sesẽm ɖe edzi wu tsã le Filistitɔwo ƒe asaɖa la me. Ale Saul gblɔ na nunɔla la be: “Nenɔ anyi ko. He asi ɖa.”

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Hebritɔ aɖewo nɔ Filistitɔwo gbɔ tsã, eye wonɔ asaɖa me kpli wo. Ame siawo gɔ̃ hã trɔ ɖe wo ŋu hede Israelvi siwo le Saul kple Yonatan gbɔ la dzi.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Nenema ke esi Israelvi siwo katã bè ɖe togbɛwo dzi le Efrayim-nutome la se be Filistitɔwo le sísim la, woawo hã do go va ti wo yome le gbea dzi

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe la, ɖeɖi te Israelviwo ŋu ale gbegbe elabe Saul ka atam na wo be: “Ne ame aɖe aɖu nu egbe hafi fiẽ aɖo, esime nyemebia hlɔ̃ nye futɔwo vɔ haɖe o la, aɖi amea ŋu kpékpekpe.” Ale aʋakɔ blibo la mede naneke nu me o.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Esi woge ɖe avea me la, wokpɔ be anyitsi la nɔ sísim, ke ame aɖeke metɔ asi eme de nu me o, elabe wovɔ̃ atam si woka na wo la.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Ke Yonatan ya mese be ye tɔ́ ka atam na dukɔ la o. Ale wòtsɔ atikplɔ si le esi la nu tɔ anyiɖaɖa la me hede asi eme de nu me. Enumake eƒe mo kɔ.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Tete ameawo dometɔ ɖeka gblɔ be: “Tɔ́wò ka atam na dukɔ la be: ‘Aɖi ame si ɖu nu egbea la ŋu kpékpekpe!’ ” Evɔ nu te dukɔ la ŋu hafi.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Ale Yonatan ɖo eŋu be: “Tɔ́nye he dzɔgbevɔ̃e va anyigba la dzi. Kpɔ ɖa, esi meɖɔ anyitsi sia ƒe ɖe ko kpɔ la, nye lã me ɖeko wòkɔ.

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Israelviwo si Filistitɔwo gbe ma gbe tso Mixmas ʋuu va se ɖe Ayalon, eye nu te wo ŋu ŋutɔ.

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Ale aʋakɔ la dze aboyonuawo dzi, lé alẽwo, nyiwo kple nyiviwo hetso ʋu wo ɖe anyigba, eye ameawo ɖu lã si ƒo ʋu.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Tete wova gblɔ na Saul be: “Kpɔ ɖa, aʋakɔ la le nuvɔ̃ wɔm ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu! Wole lã si me ʋu le la ɖum!” Saul gblɔ be: “Mieda ƒu! Miewɔ nuvɔ̃! Mimli kpe gã aɖe va afii nam fifi laa.”

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: Saul ɖe gbe be: “Mikaka ɖe aʋakɔ la dome eye migblɔ na wo be: ‘Ame sia ame nekplɔ eƒe nyi alo alẽ vɛ. Newu wo le afii ne wòaɖu. Ke migawɔ vɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu ahaɖu lã si ƒo ʋu la o.’ ” Ale ameawo dome ame sia ame kplɔ eƒe nyi vɛ zã ma me, eye wowu wo le afi ma.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Saul ɖi vɔsamlekpui na Aƒetɔ; esiae nye vɔsamlekpui gbãtɔ si wòɖi na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Saul gblɔ be: “Mina míalũ ɖe Filistitɔwo dzi, zã kple zã, eye míaha woƒe nuwo va se ɖe esime ŋu nake, eye míawu wo; ame aɖeke masusɔ o.” Woɖo eŋu be: “Wɔ nu sia nu si nèkpɔ be enyo.” Ke nunɔla la gblɔ be: “Mina míabia gbe Mawu hafi.”

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Ale Saul bia Mawu se be: “Maho aʋa ɖe Filistitɔwo ŋua? Àna Israelviwo naɖu wo dzia?” Ke Mawu meɖo nyaa ŋu gbe ma gbe o.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Tete Saul gblɔ be: “Mi dukɔa ƒe kplɔlawo katã, mite va afii. Mina míakpɔ ɖa be nuvɔ̃ ka wowɔ egbe hã.

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: Metà Aƒetɔ gbagbe si xɔna na Israel, be nenye vinye Yonatan gɔ̃e wɔ esia hã la, edze na ku.” Ke ame ɖeka hɔ̃ hã megblɔ nya aɖeke le dukɔ la dome o.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Azɔ egblɔ na Israel-dukɔ blibo la be: “Mi katã miɖo ɖe akpa ɖeka eye nye kple vinye Yonatan hã míanɔ akpa evelia.” Ameawo gblɔ na Saul be: “Wɔ nu sia nu si nèkpɔ be enyo.”

english_verse: Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?” The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army.
translation_verse: Eya ta Saul gblɔ be: “O Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu, nu ka ta mèɖo nya aɖeke ŋu na wò dɔla egbe o? Nenye nye alo vinye Yonatan ye wɔ nuvɔ̃ la, Urim neɖee fia. Ke nenye Israel-dukɔ gbɔ wòtso la, ekema Tumim neɖee fia.” Tete nudzidze la lé Yonatan kple Saul; ke dukɔ la do le eme.

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Azɔ Saul gblɔ be: “Midzidze nu ɖe nye kple vinye Yonatan dzi.” Wodzidzee eye wòdze Yonatan dzi.

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Ale Saul bia Yonatan be: “Nu ka nèwɔ? Gblɔe nam.” Yonatan ʋu eme nɛ be: “Metsɔ atikplɔ si le asinye la nu tɔ anyitsi me heɖɔ kpɔ. Nyee nye esi. Mele klalo be maku.”

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ be: “Yonatan, ne womewu wò o fĩi! Mawu nefiam, ne wòagafiam ɖe dzi!”

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Ke dukɔ la bia Saul be: “Ðe Yonatan, ame si he dziɖuɖu gã sia vɛ na Israel la dze na kua? Gbeɖe! Míetà Mawu gbagbe la be eƒe taɖa ɖeka hã mage ɖe anyigba o, elabe Mawu ƒe kpekpeɖeŋu mee wòto te ŋu wɔ nu sia egbea.” Ale dukɔ la xɔ nya ɖe Yonatan nu be womewui o.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Esia megbe la, Saul megati Filistitɔwo yome o, eye wotrɔ yi wo nɔƒe. Saul kple eƒe ƒometɔwo le eƒe fiaɖuɣi

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Saul wɔ aʋa vevie kple Filistitɔwo le eƒe agbenɔɣi katã. Ne ekpɔ ŋutsu dzɔtsu alo kalẽtɔ ɖe sia ɖe ko la, ekplɔnɛ dea eƒe aʋakɔ me.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ na Saul be: “Aƒetɔ dɔm be masi ami na wò nànye fia ɖe Israel-dukɔ nu. Eya ta fifia la ɖo to nàse Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedeasi.

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la, be yele to he ge na Amalekitɔwo ɖe woƒe nuwɔna ta. Elabe wotsi tre ɖe Israelviwo ŋu le mɔzɔzɔ me esime wodo go tso Egipte.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Azɔ yi ɖasì Amalekitɔwo eye nàtsrɔ̃ woƒe nu sia nu keŋkeŋ. Mègagblẽ woƒe naneke ɖi o; tsrɔ̃ ŋutsu kple nyɔnu, ɖevi kple vi nono, nyi kple alẽ, kposɔ kple tedzi siaa.”

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: Tete Saul ƒo asrafoawo nu ƒu ɖe Telaim, eye wòxlẽ wo. Asrafo afɔzɔlawo le ame akpe alafa eve, eye asrafo siwo tso Yuda le ame akpe ewo.

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Samuel be:

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Saul kplɔ asrafoawo va Amalek-du ƒe bali me eye wode xa ɖe afi ma.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: Azɔ Saul ɖo du ɖe Kenitɔwo be: “Netsɔ na mi, ne miado adzo le Amalekitɔwo dome, ne magatsrɔ̃ mi akpe ɖe wo ŋu o. Elabe mieve Israelviwo katã nu esime wodo go tso Egipte gbɔna.” Ale Kenitɔwo do le Amalekitɔwo dome dzo.

english_verse: and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt.
translation_verse: Saul si Amalekitɔwo tso Xavila va se ɖe Sur le Egipte ƒe ɣedzeƒe lɔƒo.

english_verse: Every Amalekite was killed except King Agag.
translation_verse: Elé Agag, Amalek-fia, agbagbee eye wòtsrɔ̃ dukɔ blibo la keŋkeŋ kple yi.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Ke Saul kple eƒe asrafowo ɖe asi le fia Agag ŋu. Wona alẽ nyuitɔwo, nyitsuwo, nyivi damiwo, alẽviwo kple nu sia nu si nyakpɔ na wo ko la tsi agbe; wometsrɔ̃ woawo ya o. Ke nu siwo wotsri kple esiwo ŋu viɖe aɖeke mele o ya la, wotsrɔ̃ wo keŋkeŋ. Aƒetɔ gbe nu le Saul gbɔ abe fia ene

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: “Evem be meɖo Saul fiae elabe etrɔ le yonyeme, eye mewɔ nye gbe dzi o.” Tete Samuel do dziku eye wòƒo koko na Aƒetɔ zã blibo la katã.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Efɔ ŋdi kanya be yeaɖado go Saul. Wogblɔ na Samuel be: “Saul va Karmel. Kpɔ ɖa, eli ŋkuɖodzikpe na eɖokui ɖi eye wòtrɔ yi Gilgal.”

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Esi Samuel va Saul gbɔ la, Saul gblɔ nɛ be: “Aƒetɔ neyra wò! Mewɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe dzi.”

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Samuel biae be: “Alẽ kple nyi kawo ƒe xɔxlɔ̃ nye esi sem mele?”

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Saul ɖo eŋu be: “Nye asrafoawoe kplɔ wo tso Amalekitɔwo gbɔ vɛ. Wotsɔ alẽ kple nyitsu nyuitɔwo vɛ be yewoatsɔ asa vɔ na Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la. Ke nu bubuawo ya la, wotsrɔ̃ wo katã gbidigbidi.”

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Tete Samuel gblɔ na Saul be: “Zi ɖoɖoe, ne magblɔ nya si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nam étò ƒe zã me la na wò.” Saul xɔ edzi be: “Gblɔe mase.”

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ nɛ be: “Togbɔ be wò ŋutɔ mèbu ɖokuiwò ɖe naneke me o hã, ɖe menye wòe zu tatɔ na Israel-toawo oa? Aƒetɔ si ami na wò heɖo wò fiae ɖe Israel nu,

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: eye wòdɔ wò ɖe dɔgbe gblɔ na wò be: ‘Yi nàɖatsrɔ̃ Amalekitɔ nuvɔ̃wɔlawo keŋkeŋ. Wɔ aʋa kpli wo va se ɖe esime wo dometɔ aɖeke mesusɔ o.’

english_verse: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
translation_verse: Nu ka ta mèɖo to Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe o? Nu ka ta nèdze aboyonuawo dzi lɔ vɛ, eye nèwɔ nu si nye nuvɔ̃ɖi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume?”

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ na Samuel be: “Mewɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe dzi ɖe. Mede dɔ si gbe Aƒetɔ ɖom ɖa lae. Mesi Agag, Amalek-fia hekplɔe gbɔe eye metsrɔ̃ Amalekitɔwo gbidigbidi.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Negbe asrafoawo koe ha aboyonuawo ƒe ɖe: alẽwo, nyitsuwo kple nu nyuitɔwo, siwo dze na tsɔtsrɔ̃ hafi la, be yewoatsɔ asa vɔ na Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la le Gilgal.”

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Tete Samuel gblɔ be: “Ɖe Aƒetɔ kpɔa ŋudzedze le numemevɔsawo kple vɔsawo ŋu abe toɖoɖo Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe enea? Kpɔ ɖa, toɖoɖo nyo wu vɔsa, eye nusese nyo wu agbo ƒe ami.

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: Elabe aglãdzedze le abe afakaka ƒe nuvɔ̃ ene, eye tosesẽ le abe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ kple trɔ̃subɔsubɔ ene. Esi nègbe Aƒetɔ ƒe nya dzi wɔwɔ ta la, eya hã gbe wò be magaɖu fia o.”

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Tete Saul gblɔ na Samuel be: “Mewɔ nuvɔ̃. Meda Aƒetɔ ƒe se dzi eye nyemewɔ wò nya dzi o. Mesi dukɔ la ɖa, eye meɖo to woƒe gbe boŋ.

english_verse: Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
translation_verse: Eya ta azɔ la, meɖe kuku, tsɔ nye nuvɔ̃ kem. Va mígbugbɔ yi Gilgal ne maɖasubɔ Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Samuel ɖo eŋu be: “Nyemagbugbɔ ayi kpli wò o, elabe ègbe Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe dzi wɔwɔ eye Aƒetɔ hã gbe wò be màgaɖu fia ɖe Israel-dukɔ dzi o.”

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Ke esi Samuel trɔ be yeadzo la, Saul lé eƒe awu ʋlaya toga eye awua dze.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ nɛ be: “Aƒetɔ dze Israel-fiaɖuƒe la le asiwò egbe, eye wòtsɔe na hawòvi aɖe si nyo wu wò.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Israel ƒe Ŋutikɔkɔetɔ la mekaa aʋatso alo trɔa susu o, elabe menye ame wònye ne wòatrɔ susu o.”

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Ale Saul gagblɔ be: “Mewɔ nuvɔ̃; ke hã la de bubu ŋunye le dukɔmemetsitsiwo kple Israelviwo katã ŋkume. Gbugbɔ kplim yi ko be maɖasubɔ Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la.”

english_verse: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Ale Samuel gbugbɔ kple Saul yi wòɖasubɔ Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Samuel ɖe gbe be: “Mikplɔ Agag, Amalek-fia va gbɔnye afii.” Agag zɔ kakaka yi egbɔ dzidzɔtɔe. Agag gblɔ be: “Le nyateƒe me la, vɔvɔ̃ si ɖom mebe maku la nu yi.”

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ be: “Ale si wò yi wɔ vi nɔwo wòzu vi manɔsitɔwo la, nenema ke nɔwò hã azu vi manɔsitɔ le nyɔnuwo dome.” Ale Samuel fli Agag kakɛkakɛe le vɔsaƒe la ŋgɔ le Gilgal.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Emegbe Samuel dzo yi Rama, eye Saul hã yi eƒeme le Gibea.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Samuel megakpɔ Saul kpɔ o va se ɖe eƒe kugbe; ke exa nu ɖe Saul ŋu. Eve Aƒetɔ be eɖo Saul fiae ɖe Israel nu.

english_verse: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Samuel be: “Va se ɖe ɣe ka ɣi nàfa konyi le Saul ŋu? Megbe be magaɖu fia ɖe Israel dzi o. Kpɔ ɖa, ku ami ɖe wò lãdzo me eye nàdze mɔ ayi Betlehem. Mele dɔwòm ɖe Isai gbɔ le afi ma elabe mekpɔ fia ɖi na ɖokuinye le viawo dome.”

english_verse: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
translation_verse: Samuel bia be: “Ale ke mawɔ ayi? Ne Saul see la, awum.” Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: Kplɔ nyivi ɖeka ɖe asi yii, eye nàgblɔ be: ‘Meva vɔ sa ge na Aƒetɔ’.

english_verse: then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Kpe Yese va vɔsaƒea eye mafia nu si nàwɔ la wò. Ame si ŋkɔ mayɔ na wò la, si ami nɛ nam wòazu fia.”

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Samuel wɔ nu si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ eye wòyi Betlehem. Dumemegãwo va do goe. Vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo eye wobia be: “Ehe nya nyui aɖe vɛ na mía?”

english_verse: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
translation_verse: Samuel ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Ẽ, nya nyui mehe vɛ. Meva be masa vɔ na Aƒetɔ eya ta mikɔ mia ɖokui ŋu ne miava vɔsaƒea.” Ekɔ Yese kple viawo ŋu eye wòkpe wo va vɔsaƒe lae.

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: Esi wova kpe ta eye wòkpɔ Eliab la, ebu tame gblɔ na eɖokui be: “Ðikeke aɖeke meli o, Aƒetɔ ƒe ame si tututu wòbe masi ami na lae nye esi do ɖe eŋkume.”

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
translation_verse: Gake Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Samuel be: “Mègakpɔ eƒe dzedzeme kple eƒe atsudzɔdzɔ o, elabe megbee. Aƒetɔ mekpɔa nu abe ale si amegbetɔ kpɔnɛ la ene o; gota gome ƒe dzedzeme ko amegbetɔ kpɔna, ke ame ƒe dzime ke Aƒetɔ ya kpɔna.”

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Ale Yese yɔ via Abinadab vɛ wòtsi tsitre ɖe Samuel ŋkume. Samuel gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ metia eya hã o.”

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: Yese kplɔ Sama va to Samuel ŋkume. Samuel gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ metia eya hã o.”

english_verse: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
translation_verse: Ale Yese kplɔ via adrẽawo dome ame sia ame va to Samuel ŋkume yi, ke Samuel gblɔ nɛ be: “Aƒetɔ metia wo dometɔ aɖeke o.”

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: “Viwòawo katãe nye esi le afi sia?” Yese ɖo eŋu be: “Ðevitɔ koe susɔ. Eya kplɔ alẽwo yi gbedzi.” Samuel gblɔ na Isai be: “Dɔ ame ɖa ne woaɖakplɔe vɛ, elabe míate ŋu anɔ afii anɔ lalam ʋuu va se ɖe esime eya ŋutɔ agbɔ o.”

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Tete Yese dɔ ame ɖa woyi ɖakplɔe vɛ. Ebiã, dze ɖeka eye eƒe ŋkuwo nyakpɔna. Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Samuel be: “Tso, nàsi ami nɛ, elabe eyae.”

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Samuel tsɔ lãdzo si me ami le, eye wòsi ami nɛ le nɔviawo katã ŋkume. Tso gbe ma gbe dzi la, Aƒetɔ ƒe Gbɔgbɔ ge ɖe David me kple ŋusẽ. Samuel tso, trɔ yi Rama. David va nɔ Saul ƒe fiasã me

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe Gbɔgbɔ do le Saul me, eye gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ va wɔa funyafunyae.

english_verse: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
translation_verse: Ale Saul ƒe subɔlawo gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, Mawue na mɔ gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ wòva le fu wɔm wò.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Míaƒe aƒetɔ, dɔ mí ne míayi aɖadi ŋutsu aɖe si nya kasaŋkuƒoƒo aɖaŋutɔe la vɛ na wò. Ale be ne gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ la dze dziwò la, wòaƒo kasaŋkua ne nàhaya.”

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Tete Saul gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo be: “Miyi ɖadi ŋutsu si nya saŋkuƒoƒo nyuie la, miakplɔ vɛ nam.”

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Subɔlawo dometɔ ɖeka gblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, menya ŋutsuvi aɖe si nya kasaŋkuƒoƒo nyuie. Tɔ́a ŋkɔe nye Isai eye wòtso Betlehem. Ŋutsuvia nye aʋawɔla kalẽtɔ si nya nuƒoƒo eye wòdze ɖeka. Aƒetɔ li kplii.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: Ale Saul dɔ dɔlawo ɖe Yese gbɔ be woagblɔ nɛ be: “Ðo viwò David, alẽkplɔla la ɖem.”

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Tete Yese kplɔ tedzi ɖeka, eye wòtsɔ abolo kple wain lãgbalẽgolo ɖeka kpakple gbɔ̃vi ɖeka de David si ɖo ɖe Saul.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: Ale David va Saul gbɔ va zu eƒe subɔla. Saul lɔ̃ David ƒe nya ŋutɔ eye wòwɔe wòzu eƒe adekplɔvi.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Emegbe Saul dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Yese be woagblɔnɛ be: “Medi be nàɖe mɔ na David wòatsi gbɔnye asubɔm, elabe eƒe nu nyo ŋunye.”

english_verse: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_verse: Ale ɣe si ɣi gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ la nyadze Saul dzi ko la, David tsɔa kasaŋkua ƒona eye Saul gaɖoa ame me, hayana eye gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃a dzona le edzi.

english_verse: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
translation_verse: Azɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe asrafowo va ƒo ƒu ɖe Soko le Yuda-nutome, dzra ɖo na aʋawɔwɔ. Woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Soko kple Azaka dome le Efes-Damim.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo ɖo ɖe toa ƒe abu ɖeka nu, eye Israeltɔwo hã ɖo ɖe abu kemɛ me eye bali la tso wo dome.

english_verse: The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall.
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu dzɔtsu aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Goliat la do tso Filistitɔwo ƒe asaɖa la me. Etso Gat-du me eye wòkɔ abe meta etɔ̃ ene.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: Azɔ esi David trɔ gbɔ, le Filistitɔ la wuwu vɔ megbe la, Abner kplɔe va Saul gbɔ; Filistitɔ la ƒe ta ganɔ esi.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: Eƒe akplɔti tri abe abaladoti ene, eye ga yibɔ kplɔ la ŋutɔ ƒe kpekpeme ade kilo adrẽ. Eƒe akpoxɔnutsɔla le eŋgɔ.

english_verse: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
translation_verse: Etsi tsitre dzɔ ka do ɣli ɖo ɖe Israel-ʋakɔ la be: “Nu ka ta mieva dze aʋa ɖo? Menye miawoe nye Saul ƒe dɔlawo oa? Filistitɔwo nye ya menye. Mitia ŋutsu ɖeka le mia dome ne wòava do gom.

english_verse: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
translation_verse: Ne wòwɔ aʋa kplim wum la, ekema míanye miaƒe subɔlawo. Ke ne menɔ te ɖe enu, wui la, ekem miazu míaƒe kluviwo asubɔ mí.”

english_verse: Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
translation_verse: Azɔ Filistitɔ la yi edzi gblɔ be: “Israeltɔwo, ne ele mia ŋu la, miɖe ame ɖeka be nye kplii míawɔ aʋa.”

english_verse: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
translation_verse: Esi Saul kple Israelviwo se Filistitɔ la ƒe nya siawo la, dzi ɖe le wo ƒo eye wovɔ̃ ŋutɔ. David yi ɖe Saul ƒe asaɖa me

english_verse: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
translation_verse: Azɔ David ye nye Yese vi. Etso Efrat-ƒome me le Betlehem le Yuda-nyigba dzi. Ŋutsuvi enyi le Yese si. Le Saul ŋɔli la, enye ame tsitsi le ehatiwo dome eye wòxɔ ƒè geɖee.

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: David dzona le Saul gbɔ enuenu ɖakplɔa tɔ́a ƒe alẽwo yia Betlehem nuɖuƒee.

english_verse: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke bla ene sɔŋ me la, Filistitɔ la dona vana ŋdi kple fiẽ, kea ɖi kple Israelviwo.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: Tete wòtsɔ eƒe lãkplɔti ɖe asi, fɔ kpe zɔzrɔ̃e atɔ̃ le tɔʋu la me, eye wòtsɔ wo de golo si alẽkplɔlawo kplana la me. Etsɔ eƒe akafo ɖe asi eye wòzɔ ɖe Filistitɔ la dzi. David ɖu Goliat dzi

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la, Yese gblɔ na David be: “Afɔ netsɔ, tsɔ bli tɔtɔe kilo ewo sia kple abolo ewo yi na nɔviwòwo le asaɖa la me.

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: Tsɔ notsi babla lalɛ ewo siawo hã yi na woƒe aʋakplɔla si kpɔa asrafo akpe ɖeka dzi la. Bia nɔviwòwo ƒe dɔdɔ ta se eye nàxɔ ŋkuɖodzinu aɖe tso wo gbɔ vɛ.

english_verse: They're with Saul's army, fighting the Philistines in Elah Valley.”
translation_verse: Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, Saul, nɔviwòwo kple Israel-srafoawo le Ela-bali me, le aʋa wɔm kple Filistitɔwo.”

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: Ale David fɔ ŋdi kanya, gblẽ alẽawo ɖe alẽkplɔla aɖe si me, tsɔ nuɖuɖua eye wòdze mɔ abe ale si tɔ́a Isai gblɔ nɛ la ene. Eva ɖo asaɖa la me esime aʋakɔ la de asi dzadzraɖo me be yewoadze aʋa eye aʋaɣli nɔ ɖiɖim.

english_verse: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
translation_verse: Israeltɔwo kple Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakɔwo dze ŋgɔ wo nɔewo be woakpe aʋa.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: Tete David gblẽ nu si wòtsɔ vɛ la ɖe ame si kpɔa aʋawɔnuwo dzi la si me, eye wòƒu du yi asrafoawo gbɔ. Ete ɖe wo ŋu do gbe na nɔviawo, bia woƒe dɔdɔ ta se.

english_verse: While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
translation_verse: Esime wòle nu ƒom kpli wo la, Goliat, Filistitɔ, si va aʋaŋgɔgbea si tso Gat la, do tso Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ la dome eye wògagblɔ nya siwo wògblɔna godoo la. David se eƒe nyawo.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Ke esi Israel-ŋutsuwo katã nyakpɔ ŋutsua ko la, wovɔ̃ ŋutɔ eye wosí dzo.

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Israel-srafoawo gblɔ le wo nɔewo dome be: “Miekpɔ ŋutsu sia si do go vaa? Ðe koŋ wòva be yeaɖe alɔ me le Israelviwo ŋu. Ame si awui la, fia la ana kesinɔnu geɖee eye wòatsɔ via nyɔnuvi hã nɛ wòaɖe. Hekpe ɖe eŋu la, tɔ́a ƒe ƒome blibo la avo tso nudzɔdzɔ kple dɔdeasiwo katã me le Israel-dukɔa me.”

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
translation_verse: Tete David bia ame siwo le egbɔ la se be: “Nu ka woawɔ na ame si awu Filistitɔ sia, eye wòaɖe ŋukpe ɖa le Israel-dukɔa ŋu? Azɔ ame ka gɔ̃e nye Filistitɔ, bolobolotɔ sia, be wòanɔ alɔ me ɖem ɖe Mawu gbagbe la ƒe aʋakɔwo ŋu?”

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Ameawo ɖo eŋu nɛ abe ale si wogblɔe va yi ene be: “Ale kple ale woawɔ na ame si wui lae nye esi.”

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: Azɔ esi David le nu ƒom kple ameawo la, nɔvia tsitsitɔ Eliab see. Eƒe dzi ho ɖe David ŋu eye wòbia be: “Nu ka di ge nèva le afii? Ame ka si mee nègblẽ alẽ ʋɛ mawo ɖo le gbea dzi? Menya dàdagbɔgbɔ kple susu vlo si le mewò. Menye aʋawɔƒe kpɔ ge nèva oa?”

english_verse: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
translation_verse: David ɖo eŋu bia be: “Nu ka mewɔ fifia? Menye nya ta koe mebia oa?”

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: Ale wòtrɔ le egbɔ, trɔ ɖe ame bubu ŋu hebia nya mawo ke, eye ameawo ɖo eŋu nɛ abe tsã ene.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: Esi wose David ƒe nyaawo la, woyi ɖagblɔ wo na Saul eye Saul na wokplɔe vɛ.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
translation_verse: David gblɔ na Saul be: “Dzika megatso ame aɖeke ƒo le ŋutsua ƒe nyawo ta o. Wò dɔla ayi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔ sia.”

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ na David be: “Màte ŋu ayi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔ sia o, elabe ɖekakpui ko nènye, evɔ la, eya de asi aʋawɔwɔ me tso eƒe ɖekakpuime ke.”

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Ke David gblɔ na Saul be: “Wò dɔla la, tɔ́a ƒe alẽwo wòkplɔna. Ne dzata alo sisiblisi aɖe va lé alẽvi aɖe le lãha la dome la,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: mekplɔnɛ ɖo ɖaƒonɛ ƒua anyi eye meɖea lã la le eƒe nu me. Nenye be lã la ho ɖe ŋunye be yeawɔ nu vevim la, meléa eƒe ge, ƒonɛ ƒua anyi eye mewunɛ.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: Wò dɔla wu dzata kple sisiblisiwo siaa kpɔ. Nenema ke wòanɔ na Filistitɔ bolobolotɔ sia hã, elabe eɖe alɔ me le Mawu gbagbe la ƒe aʋakɔwo ŋu.”

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: David gayi edzi gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, ame si ɖem tso dzata kple sisiblisiwo si me la, aɖem tso Filistitɔ sia hã si me.” Ale Saul gblɔ na David be: “Heyi eye Aƒetɔ nenɔ kpli wò.”

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Tete Saul tsɔ eƒe aʋawɔnuwo do na David. Eɖɔ akɔbligakuku nɛ, eye wòdo gawu nɛ.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: David kpla eƒe yi ɖe gawua dzi eye wòdze agbagba be yeazɔ, ke mete ŋui o, elabe medo wo womae o. Eya ta David gblɔ na Saul be: “Nyemate ŋu anɔ nu siawo me ayi o. Womemam o.” Ale David ɖe wo ɖi.

english_verse: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
translation_verse: Tete Filistitɔ la zɔ ɖe ŋgɔ nɔ tetem ɖe David ŋu. Eƒe akpoxɔnutsɔla le eŋgɔ.
