english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: Esi Filistitɔ la kpɔ David la, edo vloe elabe ɖevi ko wònye. Ebiã eye wòdze ɖeka.

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: Ebia David be: “Avue menye be nètsɔ kpo ɖe ŋunyea?” Ale Filistitɔ la ƒo fi de David le eƒe mawuwo ŋkɔ me.

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: Egblɔ na David be: “Katse nàva afii eye woana wò ŋutilã azu nuɖuɖu na dziƒoxeviwo kple gbemelãwo.”

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: David ɖo eŋu na Filistitɔ la be: “Wò la, ètsɔ yi, akplɔ kple aŋutrɔ ɖe ŋunye. Ke nye la, megbɔna gbɔwò le Aƒetɔ, Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la, Israel ƒe aʋakɔwo ƒe Mawu, si ŋu nèɖe alɔ me le la ŋkɔ me.

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ atsɔ wò de asi nam egbea, eye mawu wò, atso ta le nuwò. Matsɔ Filisti-srafowo ƒe kukuawo na dziƒoxeviwo kple lã wɔadãwo woaɖu egbea, ale be anyigbadzitɔwo katã nanya be Mawu aɖe le Israel-dukɔ me.

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: Nenema ke ameha blibo sia adze sii be Aƒetɔ metsɔa yi alo akplɔ xɔna na ame o. Aƒetɔ ye ɖua dzi le aʋa me, eye eyae atsɔ mi ade asi na mí.”

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: Tete David de asi eƒe golo me tsɔ kpe ɖeka, dae kple eƒe akafo eye wòva dze Filistitɔ la ƒe ŋgonu. Kpe la ŋɔ eƒe ŋgonu henyrɔ ɖe eme, eye Filistitɔ la mu tsyɔ mo anyi.

english_verse: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
translation_verse: Ale David ɖu Filistitɔ la dzi kple akafo kpakple kpe ko. Eƒoe ƒu anyi hewui, togbɔ be yi menɔ David si o hã.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: Tete David ƒu du ɖe Filistitɔ la dzi, lũ eƒe yi le aku me hewui, tso ta le enu. Esi Filistitɔwo kpɔ be yewoƒe aʋaŋgɔgbea ku la, woka hlẽ.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Aʋaɣli ɖi eye Israelviwo kple Yudatɔwo ƒe asrafowo ho, ti Filistitɔwo yome yi balia me, kplɔ wo ɖo va se ɖe keke Ekron-gbo nu, ale be wo dometɔ siwo xɔ abi la tsi mɔ dzi tso Saraim va se ɖe keke Gat kple Ekron.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Esi Israelviwo trɔ le Filistitɔwo yome la, wova ha woƒe asaɖa la.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: David tsɔ Filistitɔ la ƒe ta yi Yerusalem, ke etsɔ eƒe aʋawɔnuwo da ɖe eƒe agbadɔ me. Woɖe David fia Saul

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Esi Saul kpɔ David wòyina aʋa kpe ge kple Filistitɔ la la, ebia eƒe aʋakplɔlagã Abner be: “Abner, ame ka viŋutsuvie nye ɖevi sia?” Abner ɖo eŋu be: “Fia nenɔ agbe tegbee. Nyemate ŋu agblɔe o.”

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Ale Saul biae se be: Ðekakpui, ame ka vi nènye?” David ɖo eŋu be: “Wò dɔla, Isai, ame si tso Betlehem vie menye.”

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Tso gbe ma gbe dzi la, Saul xɔe eye meɖe mɔ nɛ wògbugbɔ yi tɔ́a ƒeme o.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Azɔ Yonatan bla nu kple David elabe elɔ̃e vevie.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Eɖe awu ʋlaya si le eŋu la tsɔ na David. Nenema ke wòtsɔ eƒe aʋawu, yi, dati kple eƒe alidziblanu hã nɛ.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: Afi sia afi si Saul dɔe ɖo ɖa la, eɖua dzi. Esia ta Saul tsɔe ɖo aʋakplɔlae. Nu sia dze asrafoawo katã kple Saul ƒe dɔlawo keŋ ŋu. Saul ʋã ŋu David

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Esi David trɔ gbɔ va aƒe, le Filistitɔa wuwu vɔ megbe eye asrafoawo hã gbugbɔ gbɔna la, nyɔnuwo tso Israel-duwo katã me va do go fia Saul nɔ ha dzim nɔ ɣe ɖum. Wole aseyetsoha dzim, le axatsɛ kple ʋu ƒomevi vovovowo ƒom.

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: Nyɔnuawo nɔ aseye tsom nɔ ha dzim be: “Saul wu akpewo eye David wu akpe ewowo.”

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Nya la medze Saul ŋu o eye wòkpɔ dziku vevie. Egblɔ be: “Wobe David wu ame akpeakpewo eye nye la, mewu ame akpewo ko. Nu kae gasusɔ, ne menye be ava zu fia o?”

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: Evea gbe la, gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ aɖe tso Mawu gbɔ va Saul dzi, eye wònɔ nu wɔm abe tsu kum wòle le fiasã la me ene, esime David nɔ saŋku ƒom abe ale si wòwɔna gbe sia gbe ene. Saul lé eƒe akplɔ ɖe asi.

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: Eda akplɔ la, elabe ebu be: “Matɔe amimi ɖe gli ŋu.” Ke, David do axa na akplɔ la zi eve sɔŋ.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Azɔ Saul de asi vɔvɔ̃ me na David, elabe Aƒetɔ la li kple David, ke egbugbɔ le Saul ya yome.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: Nu sia nu si wòwɔna la dzea edzi, elabe Aƒetɔ la li kplii.

english_verse: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
translation_verse: Ke ame siwo katã le Israel kple Yuda ya lɔ̃a eƒe nya gbɔ, elabe enɔa wo ŋgɔ kplɔa wo yia aʋa gakplɔa wo gbɔnae dedie. David ɖe Saul vinyɔnuvi

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Saul gblɔ na David be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ne èwɔ kalẽnu eye nèwɔ aʋa, ʋli Aƒetɔ ta la, matsɔ vinye nyɔnuvi tsitsitɔ Merab na wò nàɖe.” Saul bu be le go sia me la, Filistitɔwo awui eye manye yee awui o.

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: Ale David gblɔ na Saul be: “Ame ka menye eye ame kawoe nye ƒonyemetɔwo kple tɔ́nye ƒomeawo le Israel-nyigba dzi, keke mahayi fia ƒe to nye ge?”

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Ke ɣeyiɣi si wòle be Saul natsɔ via nyɔnuvi Merab na David wòaɖe la, etsɔe na Mexolatitɔ Adriel boŋ.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Eva dzɔ be David ƒe nu va lé dzi na Saul vinyɔnuvi Mixal boŋ. Esi wogblɔ nya sia na Saul la, edze eŋu.

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ le eɖokui me be: “Matsɔe nɛ wòaɖe; ekem atrɔ zu mɔ̀ nɛ ale be Filistitɔwo ƒe asi asu edzi.” Eya ta Saul gblɔ na David zi evelia be: “Àzu tonye azɔ.”

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Ale Saul ƒe dɔlawo na nya siawo va ɖo David ƒe to me. Azɔ David gblɔ be: “Nu tsɛ ko miawo miebui be ame nanye fia toa? Nye la, ame dahe menye eye nyemele naneke me o.”

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Tete Saul ƒe dɔlawo va gblɔ nɛ be ale kple ale David gblɔ enye si.

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: Eya ta Saul gagblɔ be: “Mina David nase egɔme nyuie be fia la mehiã srɔ̃ɖenu aɖeke o, negbe Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋanuyi alafa ɖeka ko, atsɔ bia hlɔ̃ eƒe futɔwo.’ ” Saul bu be yeana David natsi Filistitɔwo si me to mɔ sia dzi.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Esi fia la ƒe dɔlawo gblɔ nya sia na David la, edze eŋu blibo be yeazu fia to. Hafi ɣe si ɣi woɖo la nade la,

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Gake esi Saul kpɔ dze sii be Aƒetɔ li kple David, eye Mixal lɔ̃ eƒe nya la,

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: Saul gavɔ̃ David wu. Esia ta David zu Saul ƒe futɔ ɖikaa.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Enuenu la, Filisti-fiawo hoa aʋa ɖe Israelviwo ŋu. Zi ale si woho aʋae la, zi nenema ke David sia wo wú Saul ƒe dɔla bubuawo. Eya ta David ŋkɔ va de du.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Azɔ Saul de gbe to me na via Yonatan kple eƒe dɔlawo katã be woawu David. Ke David ƒe nu lé dzi na Saul vi, Yonatan ŋutɔ.

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: Ke nye la, mayi tɔ́nye gbɔ le gbea dzi afi si lɔƒo nèbe ɖo la, eye maƒo nu le ŋuwò nɛ. Nu si mese le enu la, mana nànya.”

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: Etsɔ eƒe agbe ke faa yi ɖawu Filistitɔ la, eye Aƒetɔ na Israel-dukɔ ɖu dzi nukutɔe. Wò ŋutɔ èkpɔe eye dzi dzɔ wò. Nu ka ta nàwɔ vɔ̃ ɖe ame maɖifɔ ŋu awu David dzodzro?”

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Saul se Yonatan ƒe gbe eye wòka atam be: “Metà Aƒetɔ gbagbe la! Ne mewu David fĩi!”

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Tete Yonatan yɔ David eye wògblɔ nya siawo katã nɛ. Ekplɔ David yi Saul gbɔ eye wòganɔ egbɔ abe ale si wònɔe tsã la ene.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Eva eme be aʋa gava dzɔ. David yi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo eye wòwu wo dometɔ geɖe. Bubuawo sí le enu.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe ƒe zã me la, Saul dɔ amewo ɖo ɖe David ƒeme be woaɖanɔ ŋudzɔ le eŋu, eye woawui le ŋufɔke. Ke David srɔ̃ Mixal va gblɔ nɛ be: “Ne mèsí zã kple zã o la, woawu wò etsɔ ŋdi.”

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: Ale Mixal na David ɖiɖi to fesre hesí dzo.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Mixal tsɔ aklama kpakpɛ da ɖe eƒe aba dzi, tsɔ suɖui si wotsɔ gbɔ̃fu wɔ la ɖo eƒe tagbɔ eye wòtsyɔ avɔ nɛ.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Esi Saul ɖo amewo ɖa be woava kplɔ David vɛ la, srɔ̃a gblɔ be: “Ele dɔ lém.”

english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: Azɔ Saul dɔ dɔlawo ɖa be woaɖasra David kpɔ. Egblɔ na wo be: “Miyi ɖakɔe kple aba la vɛ nam ne mawu.”

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Esi amedɔdɔawo ge ɖe eme la, wokpɔ aklama kpakpɛ la le abaa dzi eye suɖui si wowɔ kple gbɔ̃fu la le eƒe tade.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Saul bia Mixal be: “Nu ka ta nèflum alea eye nèna nye futɔ sí dzo?” Mixal ɖo eŋu be: “Egblɔ nam be, ‘Na mɔm mayi, ne menye nenema o la, mawu wò.’ ”

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi David sí la, eyi Samuel gbɔ le Rama ɖagblɔ nu siwo katã Saul wɔ ɖe eŋu la nɛ. Tete eya kple Samuel yi ɖanɔ Nayot.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Emegbe wova gblɔ na Saul be: “Kpɔ ɖa, David le Nayot le Rama-nutome.”

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: Eya ta Saul dɔ amewo ɖa be woaɖakplɔ David vɛ. Esi wova ɖo la, wokpɔ Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo ƒe ha aɖe si nɔ mawunya gblɔm. Samuel nɔ ŋgɔ na wo. Tete Mawu ƒe Gbɔgbɔ dze amedɔdɔawo dzi eye woawo hã gblɔ mawunya.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Esi wova gblɔ nya sia na Saul la, edɔ ame bubuwo ɖa. Ke woawo hã de asi gbeƒãɖeɖe me. Saul gadɔ amewo ɖa zi etɔ̃lia eye woawo hã wɔ nenema ke.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Azɔ Saul ŋutɔ ɖo ta Rama. Eva ɖo vudo gã aɖe si le Sexu la gbɔ eye wòbia be: “Afi ka Samuel kple David le?” Ame aɖe ɖo eŋu be: “Kpɔ ɖa, wole Nayot le Rama-nutome.”

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Edze mɔ ɖo ta afi ma. Tete Mawu ƒe Gbɔgbɔ va dze eya hã dzi esi wole mɔa dzi yina. Enɔ gbeƒã ɖem va se ɖe esime wova ɖo Nayot le Rama-nutome.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: Eya hã ɖe eƒe awu ɖi eye wòɖe gbeƒã le Samuel gbɔ. Enɔ amama ŋkeke blibo ma kple zã katã. Afi sia nyagbɔgblɔ sia dzɔ tso amewo gblɔna be: “Ðe Saul hã le Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo domea?”

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: Azɔ David sí le Nayot le Rama. Eva Yonatan gbɔ va bia be: “Nu ka gɔ̃ mewɔ? Vo ka meda? Nu vɔ̃ ka mewɔ ɖe tɔ́wò ŋu hafi wòdi be yeawum?”

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Yonatan ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Gbeɖe! Mèle kuku ge o. Kpɔ ɖa, eɖanye nu gã aɖe alo nu sue aɖe wònye o, tɔ́nye mewɔa ɖeke ne megblɔe nam o. Nu ka ta tɔ́nye aɣla nya siam? Mele eme o.”

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: Ke David gblɔ nɛ be: “Tɔ́wò nya nyuie be mèlɔ̃a nu le gbɔnye o. Eƒe susu anye be, ‘Mele be Yonatan nase nya sia o. Ne menye nenema o la, ava xa nu.’ Gake, le nyateƒe me la, metà Aƒetɔ gbagbe la be, nye kple ku dome megadidi o.”

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Esia ta Yonatan do ŋugbe na David be: “Nu sia nu si nàbia la mawɔe na wò.”

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: Ale David gblɔ na Yonatan be: “Kpɔ ɖa, etsɔ anye dzinu yeye eye nyemate ŋu agbe nuɖuɖu kple fia la o. Gake na masí yi ɖabè ɖe gbedzi va se ɖe etɔ̃a gbe ƒe fiẽ.

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Ne tɔ́wò de dzesii be nyemeli o la, ekema gblɔ nɛ be: ‘David bia mɔ be yeayi wo de Betlehem, ale be yeanɔ ƒome blibo la ƒe ƒè sia ƒe vɔsa teƒe.

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: Ne egblɔ be: ‘Enyo, mesee’ la, ekema wò dɔla ŋu fa. Gake ne edo dziku la, ekema nànyae be eɖo tame vɔ̃ aɖe ɖe ŋunye.’

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: Eya ta meɖe kuku, ve wò dɔla nu, elabe mí kpakple eve la míebla nu le Mawu ŋkume. Gake ne mewɔ vɔ̃ aɖe la, ekema wò ŋutɔ wum. Nu ka ta wòahiã be nàkplɔm ayi ɖade asi na tɔ́wò?”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Yonatan gblɔ nɛ be: “Gbeɖe, esia mava eme o. Ne menyae be tɔ́nye ɖo nugbe ɖe ŋuwò la, ɖe nyemagblɔe na wò oa?”

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: David gblɔ na Yonatan be: “Va míyi gbedzi.” Ale wo kple eve la yi gbedzi.

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Eyi edzi gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu nenye ɖasefo na mí! Etsɔ alo nyitsɔ ɣe alewo ɣi ne meté tɔ́nye ƒe nu me se, eye mekpɔ be eƒe dɔme trɔ ɖe ŋuwò la, madɔ ame ɖa wòava gblɔe na wò.

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: Evɔ ne wònye vɔ̃ tɔ́nye ɖo be yeawɔ wò la, ekema Aƒetɔ nefia Yonatan eye wòagafiam ɖe edzi, ne nyemegblɔe na wò eye mena nèsí yi le ŋutifafa me o fĩi. Aƒetɔ nenɔ kpli wò abe ale si wònɔ kple tɔ́nye tsã ene.

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: Mègana ŋugbe si nèdo na nye aƒe be yeawɔ nyui nɛ la nabu gbeɖe o. Ne Aƒetɔ tsrɔ̃ David ƒe futɔwo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe le anyigba dzi hã la,

english_verse: Jonathan and David made an agreement that even David's descendants would have to keep. Then Jonathan said, “I pray that the Lord will take revenge on your descendants if they break our promise.”
translation_verse: megagblẽ nubabla si le Yonatan kple David ƒe aƒe la ya dome o. Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ nebia hlɔ̃ David ƒe futɔwo.”

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Ale Yonatan na David gaka atam ɖe lɔlɔ̃ si wòtsɔ nɛ la dzi, elabe elɔ̃e abe eya ŋutɔ ɖokui ene.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Tete Yonatan gblɔ nɛ be: “Etsɔ anye Dzinu Yeye Ŋkeke Nyui. Woabia tawò le nua ɖuƒe elabe wò nɔƒe aɖi gbɔlo.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Le etɔ̃a gbe la, nàɖe abla ayi afi si nèbè ɖo tsã ma, eye nànɔ kpe siwo, wofɔ li kɔe le afi ma la godo.

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: Mele aŋutrɔ etɔ̃ da ge ɖo ɖe kpekɔ la gbɔ lɔƒo, abe nane medzidze da ene.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: Emegbe madɔ ɖekakpui aɖe ɖa agblɔ nɛ be: ‘Heyi, ɖadi aŋutrɔawo.’ Ne megblɔ na ɖekakpuia be, ‘Kpɔ ɖa, aŋutrɔawo le megbewò afii. Fɔ wo vɛ’ la, ekema nàdo va, elabe ŋuwò fa eye vɔ̃ aɖeke madzɔ ɖe dziwò o. Metà Aƒetɔ gbagbe la na wò.’

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Gake ne megblɔ na ɖekakpuia be, ‘Kpɔ ɖa, aŋutrɔawo le ŋgɔwò afi mɛ’ la, ekema dzo, elabe Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ do mɔ wò.

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: Ke le nya si nye kpli wò míegblɔ ɖo kpe edzi gome ya la, kpɔ ɖa, Aƒetɔ ana míalé eme ɖe asi ɖaa.”

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: Eya ta David yi ɖabè ɖe gbea dzi. Esi Dzinu Yeye Ŋkeke Nyui la ɖo la, fia Saul va nuɖuƒea

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ teƒe si wònɔna edziedzi le glia ŋu la. Yonatan tsi tsitre eye Abner bɔbɔ nɔ Saul xa. Ke David nɔƒe ɖi gbɔlo.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Gake Saul megblɔ nya aɖeke gbe ma gbe o. Eƒe susu koe nye be: “Nane dzɔ ɖe David dzi ale be eŋu mekɔ o. Ẽ, anye eŋutie mekɔ o.”

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: Le Dzinu Yeye Ŋkeke Nyui ƒe evea gbe ŋdi hã la, David nɔƒe gaɖi gbɔlo. Ale Saul bia via Yonatan se be: “Nu ka ta Isai vi la meva nuɖuƒea etsɔ kple egbe siaa o?”

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: Ebe, ‘Meɖe kuku, ɖe mɔ nam mayi elabe míaƒe ƒomea le vɔ sa ge le dua me, eye nɔvinyewo di vevie tso asinye be manɔ eteƒe. Azɔ, ne nye nu ve le ŋuwò tututu la, ekema nà mɔm mayi aɖakpɔ ƒonyemeawo.’ Esia tae mele kplɔ̃a ŋu kple fia la o.”

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Tete Saul do dziku helihelĩ ɖe Yonatan ŋu, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Wò nyɔnu gbegblẽ dzeaglã ƒe vi! Ðe nèbu be nyemenya be nètia Isai vi la tsɔ do ŋukpe ɖokuiwò kple nɔwò ƒe ama me oa?

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Eme nekɔ na wò be, zi ale si Isai vi la le agbe la, wò ŋutɔ kple wò fiaɖuƒe la miali ke o. Eya ta dɔ ame ɖa woaɖakplɔe vɛ nam, elabe edze be wòaku godoo.

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Ale Yonatan bia tɔ́a Saul se be: “Nu ka ta wòle be wòaku? Nu ka wòwɔ?”

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Enumake Saul da akplɔ Yonatan be yeawui. Tete Yonatan dze sii be ye tɔ́ ɖoe kplikpaa be yeawu David.

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Yonatan do dziku, tso le kplɔ̃ la ŋu numaɖumaɖui le ŋkekenyuia ƒe evea gbe. Exa nu ɖe David ta elabe tɔ́a do ŋukpee.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: Le ŋufɔke la, Yonatan kplɔ ŋutsuvi sue aɖe kpe ɖe eɖokui ŋu woyi gbea dzi afi si eya kple David woɖo ɖi be yewoakpe le.

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: Egblɔ na ŋutsuvia be: “Ƒu du yi ɖadi aŋutrɔ siwo da ge mala.” Esi ŋutsuvia de asi duƒuƒu me yina la, Yonatan da aŋutrɔ ɖo ɖe eŋgɔ.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Ke esi ŋutsuvia ɖo afi si Yonatan da aŋutrɔ wòva dze la, Yonatan do ɣli ɖe eyome biae be: “Menye aŋutrɔ lae nye ekem le ŋgɔwò afi mɛ ɖa oa?”

english_verse: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
translation_verse: Eyi dzi gado ɣli ɖe eyome be: “Netsɔ, ɖe abla! Mègatɔ ɖe afi ma o!” Ale ŋutsuvia fɔ aŋutrɔawo eye wòtrɔ va eƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Ke ŋutsuvia menya nu si le edzi yim o, negbe Yonatan kple David koe nya.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Tete Yonatan tsɔ eƒe aʋawɔnua de ŋutsuvia si eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Trɔ nàtsɔ wo yi dua mee.”

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Kasia ŋutsuvia nadzo la, David do go tso anyigbeme lɔƒo, de ta agu nɛ bɔbɔ zi etɔ̃. Wogbugbɔ nu na wo nɔewo hefa avi ɖe wo nɔewo ŋu vevie. Ke David ƒe avifafa nu sẽ wu.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Tete Yonatan gblɔ na David be: “Heyi le ŋutifafa me, elabe mí ame eve la míeka atam na mía nɔewo le Aƒetɔ ŋkɔ me be, ‘Aƒetɔ ƒe nubabla anɔ nye kple wò, nye dzidzimeviwo kple tɔwòawo dome tegbee.’ ” Ale David tso dze mɔ eye Yonatan gbugbɔ yi dua me.

english_verse: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
translation_verse: Azɔ David zɔ mɔ va ɖo nunɔla Aximelex gbɔ le Nob. Aximelex do go va kpe David kple vɔvɔ̃ gã aɖe eye wòbiae be: “Nu ka ta wò ɖeka nèva eye ame aɖeke mekpe ɖe ŋutiwò o?”

english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: David gblɔ na nunɔla Aximelex be: “Fia lae de gbe asi nam be, ‘Mègana ame aɖeke nase aflui le nu si gbe medɔ wò ɖo la ŋu o.’ Azɔ megblẽ ɖekakpui aɖewo ɖe teƒe aɖe.

english_verse: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
translation_verse: Nuɖuɖu aɖe le asiwò fifia? Nà abolo atɔ̃ alo nuɖuɖu ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi si le asiwò lam.”

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Nunɔla la gblɔ na David be: “Abolo dzodzro aɖeke mele asinye o, negbe abolo si ŋu wokɔ̀ la koe li. Àte ŋu axɔ wo na ɖekakpuiawo ne womenya dɔ nyɔnu gbɔ o ko.”

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: David gblɔ na nunɔla la be: “Nye ŋutimewo metena ɖe nyɔnu ŋu ɣeaɖekeɣi ne míedo go dzro yi gbedzi hã o, kaka wòahanye egbe boŋ esi míedo go va afii le nya tɔxɛ aɖe ta? Le nyateƒe me la, woawo ŋutɔ kple wo ŋutinuwo siaa ŋuti kɔ.”

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: Ale wɔ nunɔla la tsɔ abolo si ŋuti kɔ la na David elabe abolo bubu aɖeke meli wu ema o, negbe vɔsabolo la ko. Gbe si gbe wotsɔ abolo sia le Aƒetɔ ƒe kplɔ̃ dzi la, wotsɔa abolo dzodzoe si wome gbe ma gbe ke la dana ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Ke Saul ƒe lãkplɔlawo ƒe amegã si ŋkɔe nye Doeg, tso Edom, la le afi ma. Wozi ŋutsu sia dzi ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋkume gbe ma gbe.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: David gblɔ na Aximelex be: “Akplɔ alo yi aɖeke mele asiwò le afii nàtsɔ nam oa? Fia ƒe nya la na metsi dzi ale gbegbe be nyemetsɔ nye yi alo aʋawɔnu bubu aɖeke ɖe asi hafi dze mɔ o.”

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Aximelex ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Goliat, Filistitɔ si nèwu le logotibali me la ƒe yi koe li. Ele kɔmewu la megbe, wobla avɔ ɖe eŋu. Ne èdi be yeaxɔe la, tsɔe. Eya ɖeka koe le afii.” David gblɔ nɛ be: “Tsɔe nam. Etɔgbe meli o!”

english_verse: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
translation_verse: Ale David dze mɔ gbe ma gbe hesí le Saul nu eye wòva fia Axis gbɔ le Gat.

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: Tete fia Axis ŋutimewo va gblɔ nɛ be: “Menye David, anyigba sia ƒe fia lae nye esi oa? Ðe menye eya ŋue wodzi ha, ɖu ɣe ɖo be, ‘Saul wu akpe, eye David ya wu akpe ewowo’ oa?”

english_verse: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
translation_verse: Nya siawo wɔ dɔ ɖe David dzi ale gbegbe be wòde asi fia Axis vɔvɔ̃ me.

english_verse: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
translation_verse: Ale David trɔ eƒe nɔnɔme le wo ŋkume hele nu wɔm abe tsukunɔ ene. Enɔ fli tem ɖe agbo la ŋu nyamanyama eye ade nɔ tsyɔtsyɔm le enu ɖe ge me nɛ.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: Tete Axis gblɔ na eŋumewo be: “Mikpɔ ɖa! Tsukunɔe! Nu ka ta miekplɔe vɛ nam?

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: Tsukunɔwoe le hiãyem ta miekplɔ ame sia vɛ be woava nɔ aɖaʋanu wɔm le gbɔnyea? Ðe wòle be ame sia tɔgbe nage ɖe nye aƒemea?”

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: David sí le Gat-dua me eye wòyi ɖe agado si te ɖe Adulam-du ŋu la me. Esi nɔvia ŋutsuwo kple eƒe ƒometɔ mamlɛawo se be ele afi ma la, woyi ɖakpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
translation_verse: Ame siwo le xaxa me, fenyilawo kple ame siwo mekpɔ dzidzeme le agbe me o la hã yi ɖale egbɔ le afi ma, eye wòzu woƒe tatɔ. Wo katã ƒe xexlẽme ade alafa ene.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: David dzo le afi ma eye wòyi Mizpa le Moab-nyigba dzi eye wòɖagblɔ na Moab-fia be: “Meɖe kuku, medi be nàna tɔ́nye kple nɔnye naʋu ava nɔ mia gbɔ va se ɖe esime manya nu si Aƒetɔ le wɔwɔ ge nam.”

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: Ale David gblẽ edzilawo ɖe Moab-fia la gbɔ, eye wonɔ afi ma ŋkeke siwo katã David yi ɖanɔ agadoa me.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Tete Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela Gad va David gbɔ eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Mègatsi agado sia me o; ʋu nàyi Moab-nyigba dzi.” Ale David dzo le afi ma eye wòyi ɖe ave me le Xaret.

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Saul se be wokpɔ David kple ŋutsu siwo le eŋu la. Saul bɔbɔ nɔ ati aɖe te le togbɛ aɖe dzi, le Gibea lé eƒe akplɔ ɖe asi, eye eƒe subɔlawo katã le tsitre ƒo xlãe.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ na eƒe subɔla siwo le tsitre ƒo xlãe la be: “Mi Benyamin viwo, miɖo to miase. Ðe miebu be Isai vi la atsɔ agble kple wainbɔwo na mi katã? Ðe miebu be aɖo mi katã amegãwoe, amewo ɖe ame akpe nu, eye amewo hã ɖe ame alafa nua?

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: Esiawoe miebu tae mi katã miewɔ ɖeka heɖo nugbe ɖe ŋunyea? Esime vinye wɔ ɖeka kple Isai vi la la, mia dometɔ aɖeke mefi tofi nam o. Nye nya meka mia dometɔ aɖeke wòahayi tofi fi ge nam, be nye ŋutɔ vinye, na nye dɔla tso ɖe ŋunye eye wòde xa ɖi nam kpɔ o va se ɖe egbe.”

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Doeg tsi tsitre ɖe Saul ƒe dɔlawo gbɔ eye wòɖo nyaa ŋu be: “Isai vi la va Aximelex, Axitub vi la gbɔ le Nob, mekpɔ.

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: Aximelex bia nu ta na David le Aƒetɔ gbɔ. Emegbe la, ena nuɖuɖu aɖewo David eye wòtsɔ Goliat, Filistitɔ la ƒe yia nɛ.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Tete Saul dɔ ame ɖa be woayi aɖayɔ nunɔla Aximelex kple eƒe ƒometɔwo katã, siwo hã nye nunɔlawo le Nob la vɛ, eye wo katã wova egbɔ.

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ na Aximelex be: “Axitub vi, ɖo to nàse nya sia!” Eɖo eŋu be: “Mele to dzi, nye amegã!”

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Saul biae be: “Nu ka ta wò kple David miewɔ ɖeka heɖo nugbe ɖe ŋunye? Nu ka ta nètsɔ nuɖuɖu kple yi nɛ eye nèbia nu Mawu nɛ? Èkpɔea? Azɔ la, etso ɖe ŋunye eye wòle ŋudzɔ le mɔnu dim le ŋunye fifi laa be yeawum.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
translation_verse: Aximelex ɖo eŋu be: “Ame aɖeke mele wò ŋutimewo dome si wɔa nuteƒe abe David ene o. Azɔ wò ŋutɔ towòe eye wòganye wò ŋutimewo ƒe amegã. Gawu la, ame sia ame bunɛ ŋutɔ le aƒewò me.

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: Ele eme baa be mebia nu Mawu nɛ, gake menye egbee nye zi gbãtɔ o. Fia bubutɔ, mègada nya ɖe nye loo, alo nye ƒometɔ aɖeke dzi be míeɖo nugbe ɖe ye ŋu o. Nyemenya naneke le nya blibo la ŋuti o.”

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ be: “Aximelex, wò kple wò ƒometɔwo katã miaku!”

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ na eŋudzɔla siwo le tsitre ɖe egbɔ la be: “Miwu Aƒetɔ ƒe nunɔlaawo! Wowɔ ɖeka kple David ɖo nugbe ɖe ŋunye. Wonya be ɖe wòsí gake womeva fi tofi nam o.” Ke eŋudzɔlaawo gbe be yewomawu Aƒetɔ ƒe nunɔlaawo o.

english_verse: Saul turned to Doeg, who was from Edom, and said, “Kill the priests!” On that same day, Doeg killed
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ na Doeg be: “Wòa te yi nàwu wo!” Enumake Doeg wu wo katã. Ewu nunɔla bla enyi vɔ atɔ̃ siwo do aklalakɔmewu la gbe ma gbe.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: Azɔ Saul ɖe gbe be woawu nunɔlawo katã le Nob-du me. Ale wowu ame sia ame le dua me: ŋutsuwo kple nyɔnuwo, ɖeviwo kple vidzĩwo, nyiwo, tedziwo kple alẽwo.

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Ke Abyatar, Aximelex viwo dometɔ ɖeka ya sí yi David gbɔ.

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: Egblɔ ale si Saul wu Aƒetɔ ƒe nunɔlaawoe la na David.

english_verse: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
translation_verse: David gblɔ nɛ be: “Esi mekpɔ Doeg le afi ma gbe ma gbe la, menya be eyina nya aɖe gblɔ ge na Saul godoo. Eya ta nye nuwɔnae na wowu wò ƒometɔwo katã.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: Nɔ gbɔnye eye mègavɔ̃ o, elabe ame si le diyem be yeawu la, eya kee di wò hã be yeawu. Ne èle gbɔnye la, ànɔ dedie.”

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: David se be Filistitɔwo le aʋa wɔm kple Kegila-dua, eye wole bli si le ava dzi la ham.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
translation_verse: Eya ta David bia Aƒetɔ be: “Mayi ɖawɔ aʋa kpli woa?” Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu be: “Yi nàɖawɔ aʋa kpli wo eye nàxɔ na Kegila-dua.”

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Ke David ƒe amewo gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, míele vɔvɔ̃m le Yuda afii xoxo. Ne míeho yi Kegila ɖakpe aʋa kple Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakɔwo la, ɖe mavɔ̃ɖi na mí wu oa?”

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Ale David gabia nu Aƒetɔ ake eye wòɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Tso nàyi Kegila elabe mana nàɖu Filistitɔwo dzi.”

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: Ale David kple amewo yi Kegila, eye wowɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo. Wowu wo dome ame geɖewo eye wokplɔ woƒe lãhawo dzoe. Aleae David xɔ Kegilatɔwo ɖe agbe nye esi.

english_verse: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Esi David nya be Saul le vɔ̃ ɖom ɖe ye ŋu la, egblɔ na nunɔla Abyatar be: “Tsɔ kɔmewu la va afii!”

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Tete David gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu, mese be Saul le dzadzram ɖo be yeava Kegila ava gbã dua le nye, wò dɔla, ta.

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Ðe Kegilatɔwo le asi ɖe ge le ŋunye nɛa? Ðe Saul le vava ge vavã abe ale si mesee enea? Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu, meɖe kuku ɖo eŋu nam.” Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu be: “Saul le vava ge.”

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: David gabia be: “Ekema ɖe Kegilatɔwo le asi ɖe ge le nye kple nye amewo ŋu na Saul mahã?” Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu be: “Woaɖe asi le mia ŋu nɛ.”

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: David nɔ teƒe sesẽ siwo wòabè ɖo le tonyigba dzi le gbedadaƒo si te ɖe Sif ŋu. Saul dii vevie gbe sia gbe gake Mawu meɖe asi le eŋu nɛ o.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: David kpɔ be Saul ɖoe kplikpaa be yeawu ye. Ale David dzo yi Xores le gbedadaƒo si te ɖe Sif ŋu.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Yonatan, Saul vi, yi ɖe David gbɔ le afi ma eye wòde dzi ƒo nɛ be neɖo dzi ɖe Mawu ŋu.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ nɛ be: “Mègavɔ̃ o. Tɔ́nye mate nu awɔ nu vevi aɖeke wò o. Eya ŋutɔ nya nyuie be wòe gbɔna Israel-fia nye ge, eye nyee gbɔna ŋuwò nɔ ge kplíkplikpli aɖu dzi kpli wò.”

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: Wo ame evea wobla nu le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. David tsi Xores eye Yonatan yi aƒe.

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Siftɔ aɖewo va Saul gbɔ le Gibea eye wogblɔ nɛ be: “David va bè ɖe tonyigba dzi le Xores. Ele Xaxila-togbɛ si le Yesimon ƒe anyigbeme la dzi.

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ na wo be: “Aƒetɔ neyra mi elabe mienyo dɔme nam.

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Migbugbɔ yi miaka ɖe edzi. Mikpɔ afi si tututu wòle kple ame si kpɔe le afi ma, elabe mese be ɖe wòdze aye ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Miyi ɖadii le teƒe siwo katã wobè ɖo la, eye miagbugbɔ ava gblɔe nam kaba, ekema nye ŋutɔ mayi kpli mi. Ne enyale nutoa me ko la, madii vevie. Ne ehiã be matsa le ame akpe nane siwo le Yuda-nyigba bliboa dzi la dome hã la, mawɔe.”

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Ale wotrɔ do ŋgɔ na Saul gbugbɔ yi Sif. David kple eƒe amewo le gbedadaƒo si le Maon. Teƒe sia nye gbadzaƒe si le anyigbeme le gbedadaƒo si le Yuda.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Saul kple eƒe amewo yi David di ge, ke esee eye wòɖi abu yi togbɛ si le agakpewo dome le gbedadaƒo si le Maon gbɔ la gbɔ henɔ afi ma. Esi Saul se be ele afi ma la, eti David yome yi.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Togbɛ la le wo dome; Saul kple eƒe amewo le akpa ɖeka eye David kple eƒe amewo hã le akpa kemɛ. David nɔ ʋaʋãm be yeasí le Saul nu adzo, ke Saul kple eƒe amewo ɖe to ɖe wo be yewoalé wo.

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi me tututu la, amedɔdɔ aɖe va ɖo eye wògblɔ na Saul be: “Netsɔ nàgbugbɔ va kaba! Filistitɔwo ho va le dukɔ la sim!”

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Ale wɔ Saul gbugbɔ le David yome, eye wòyi ɖakpe aʋa kple Filistitɔwo. Eya ta wona ŋkɔ teƒe ma be “Kaklãgakpe.”

english_verse: David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
translation_verse: David dzo le afi ma eye wòyi ɖanɔ totamemɔ́ me le En-Gedi.

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Esi Saul yi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo gbɔ la, wogblɔ nɛ be David le gbedadaƒo si le En-Gedi.

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: Eva ɖo agado aɖe si te ɖe alẽkpo aɖe ŋu le mɔ to la gbɔ, eye wòge ɖe eme be yeade afɔdzi. Nukutɔe la, agado sia mee David kple eƒe amewo va bè ɖo eye wole egɔme ke.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: David ƒe amewo gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, egbee nye egbe! Aƒetɔ gblɔ na wò be gbe ɖeka la yeatsɔ wò futɔ ade asi na wò, eye nàwɔ nu sia nu si dze ŋuwò lae.” Ale David yi ɖalã Saul ƒe awu ʋlaya si wòdo la nu dzaa; Saul menya o.

english_verse: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
translation_verse: Emegbe la, David ƒe dzitsinya de asi fuɖeɖe me nɛ, le esi wòlã Saul ƒe awu ʋlaya to ta.

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: David ƒe nya la dze eƒe ameawo ŋu eye mena wowɔ nu vevi aɖeke Saul o. Saul tsi tsitre eye wòdzo le agadoa me heyi eƒe mɔzɔzɔ dzi.

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: Azɔ la David do go le agadoa me kplɔe ɖo eye wòyɔe sesĩe be, “Nye aƒetɔ fia!” Saul nyè kɔ kpɔ megbe, eye David bɔbɔ de ta agu.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: David gblɔ na Saul be: “Nu ka ta nèle ame siwo le gbɔgblɔm be nye David, meɖo be mawɔ nu vevi wò la ƒe gbe sem?

english_verse: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Wò ŋutɔ kpɔ ɖa, Aƒetɔ tsɔ wò de asi nam le agadoa me egbe hafi. Nye amewo dometɔ aɖewo ƒoe ɖe nunye be mawu wò, ke megbe hegblɔ na wo be nyemawɔ nu vevi aɖeke wò gbeɖe o, elabe ame si Aƒetɔ si ami na heɖoe fia la nènye.

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, tɔ́nye, kpɔ wò awu ʋlaya kakɛ si le asinye la ɖa! Esi mekpɔ wò la, mate ŋu awu wò hafi, ke wò awu ʋlaya to sue sia ko melã dzoe. Kpɔ esia nàdze sii ƒãa be nyemeɖo be madze aglã ɖe ŋuwò loo, alo awɔ nu vevi aɖeke wò o. Wò la, èle yonyeme tim vevie be yeawum, togbɔ be nyemewɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke ɖe ŋuwò o hã.

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ nedrɔ̃ nye kple wò domenya ne wòahe to na wò nam; ke nyemawɔ nu vevi aɖeke wò akpɔ gbeɖe o.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Ame tsitsiwo doa lo be: ‘Ame vɔ̃ɖi koe wɔa nuvɔ̃ɖi’, ke nye ya nyemawɔ nu vevi aɖeke wò akpɔ gbeɖe o.

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Mikpɔ ame si Israel-fia kplɔ ɖo la ɖa! Mikpɔ ame si yome tim wòle la ɖa! Avu kuku aɖee! Dosu aɖee!

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ nedrɔ̃ nye kple wò domenya eye wòatso afia na ame si tɔ dzɔ. Eya ŋutɔ nekpɔ nya la me ne wòaʋli tanye eye wòaɖem tso asiwò me.”

english_verse: “David, my son—is that you?” Saul asked. Then he started crying
translation_verse: Esi David ƒo nu na Saul vɔ la, Saul bia be: “Vinye David, wò ŋutɔŋutɔe nye esia?” Tete wòwó avi kple ɣli.

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: Azɔ la egblɔ na David be: “Tɔwò dzɔ, ke tɔnye medzɔ o, elabe èwɔ nyui nam, ke nye la, mewɔ vɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò.

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Èɖe nyui si nèwɔ nam la fia egbe elabe togbɔ be Aƒetɔ tsɔm de asi na wò hã la, mèwum o.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Ame ƒe asi ɖe wòsua eƒe futɔ dzi vɔ tso, wògaɖea asi le eŋu wòdzona dediea? Eya ta Aƒetɔ netsɔ nyui ɖo nu si nèwɔ nam egbe la teƒe na wò.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: Azɔ meka ɖe edzi be ègbɔna Israel-fia zu ge, eye fiaɖuƒe la ali ke to dziwò.

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: Eya ta tà Aƒetɔ nam be yematsrɔ̃ nye dzidzimeviwo bene woaŋlɔm be le tɔ́nye ƒeme o.”

english_verse: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_verse: Tete David ka atam ɖe nya sia dzi na Saul. Emegbe Saul trɔ yi aƒe, eye David kple eƒe amewo gbugbɔ yi afi si wobè ɖo la.

english_verse: One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it.
translation_verse: David se le gbedadaƒoa be Nabal va le fu kom na eƒe alẽwo.

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: Egblɔ na wo be woaɖagblɔ na Nabal be: “Xɔ̃wò David be yedo gbe na wò. Èdɔa? Aƒewòmetɔwo dɔa? Wò nuwo katã li nyuiea?

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: Ese be èle fu kom na wò alẽwo, eye wòdi be nànya be esime wò lãkplɔlawo va le mía gbɔ la, míewɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke wo o. Woƒe naneke hã mebu o va se ɖe fifi.

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: Wò ya bia wo ko, wole egblɔ ge na wò. Eya ta ve wò ɖekakpuiawo nu elabe ŋkekenyui dzie míeva. Meɖe kuku, nà nu si nàte ŋui la wò dɔlawo kple xɔ̃wò David.”

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: David ƒe dɔlaawo yi ɖagblɔ nya la na Nabal le David ŋkɔ me, eye wole esi nu kpɔm.

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Ke Nabal ɖo nyaa ŋu azɔ na amedɔdɔawo be: “David hã? Ame ka wònye? Isai vi? Nyemese eŋkɔ kpɔ o! Kluvi geɖe le sísim le woƒe aƒetɔwo gbɔ le ŋkeke siawo me.

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Nu ka tae matsɔ nye nuɖuɖu kple tsi kpakple lã si mewu na ame siwo le fu kom na nye alẽwo la ana ame siwo tso afi si nyemenya o?”

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: David ƒe amewo trɔ yi egbɔ eye wogblɔ nya si Nabal gblɔ na wo la nɛ.

english_verse: “Everybody get your swords!” David ordered. They all strapped on their swords. Two hundred men stayed behind to guard the camp, but the other
translation_verse: Tete David ɖe gbe na wo be: “Ame sia ame nekpla eƒe yi!” Wo katã wowɔ ɖe edzi; David ŋutɔ hã kpla etɔ eye wòdze mɔ kple ame alafa ene. Ame alafa eve tsi woƒe nuwo gbɔ.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Eya ta azɔ la, bu tame le nu si nàwɔ la ŋuti, elabe woɖo nugbe ɖe míaƒe aƒetɔ kple eƒe ƒomea katã ŋuti. Míaƒe aƒetɔ la, ame vɔ̃ɖi wònye eya ta ame aɖeke mate ŋu ate ɖe eŋuti agblɔ nya aɖeke nɛ wòasee o.”

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: Egblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo be: “Mido ŋgɔ nam. Mele mia yome dze ge.” Ke megblɔ nya aɖeke na srɔ̃a Nabal o.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: Esi wòdo tedzi ɖi abu ɖo toa xa yina la, edo go David kple eƒe amewo wogbɔna ekpe ge.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: David gblɔ be: “Menye dɔ vlo nye esi mewɔ oa? Mekpɔ ŋutsu sia ƒe nuwo dzi nɛ le gbea dzi, eye eƒe nu suetɔ kekeake hã mebu o. Ke azɔ la, etsɔ vɔ̃ le nyui si mewɔ nɛ la teƒe ɖom nam.

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: Nenye be ŋu ke ŋdi, eye megblẽ eƒe amewo dometɔ ɖeka ɖi nyemewu o la, Mawu netsrɔ̃ nye amewo keŋkeŋ; ɖeka hɔ̃ hã megasusɔ o.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Esi Abigail kpɔ David la, ewɔ kaba ɖi le tedzi la dzi eye wòbɔbɔ de ta agu.

english_verse: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
translation_verse: Nye amegã, meɖe kuku, mègade nu eme na Nabal o tɔɔ. Ame vɔ̃ɖi wònye; eƒe ŋkɔ ɖe wòɖi eŋu. Ŋkɔa gɔmee nye movitɔ. Esi wò dɔlaawo va la, nyemekpɔ wo o.

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: Taflatsɛ, ne meda vo aɖe ɖe ŋuwò la, tsɔe kem. Aƒetɔ le nana ge naɖu fia godoo, eye wò dzidzimeviwo hã ava nɔ wò zi dzi elabe eya ŋutɔ ƒe aʋa wɔm nèle. Dzɔgbevɔ̃e aɖeke madzɔ ɖe dziwò le wò agbe me ŋkekewo katã me o.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Ne ame aɖe tso ɖe ŋuwò le yowòme tim be yeawu wò la, Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la, aʋli tawò, abe ale si woʋlia ame ƒe kesinɔnu ta ene, eye ànɔ dedie. Ke wò futɔwo la, ada wo abe ale si wodea kpe aŋetu me dana ene.

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: Ne Aƒetɔ na nu nyui siwo katã ŋugbe wòdo na wò la wò pɛpɛpɛ, eye wòtsɔ wò ɖo fiae ɖe Israel nu la,

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: megave wò be yewu ame madzemadzee alo yebia hlɔ̃ na ye ɖokui o. Ne Aƒetɔ na nu nyo na wò la, meɖe kuku, ɖo ŋku dzinye.”

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: David gblɔ nɛ be: “Mikafu Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu si dɔ wò ɖa nèva do gom egbe.

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: Akpe na Mawu be wòna nunya wò le nu si nèwɔ nam egbe la ta. Elabe èva xe mɔ nam ale be nyemewu ame alo bia hlɔ̃ na ɖokuinye o.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ xe mɔ nam be magawɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke wò o. Evɔ la metà Israel ƒe Mawu gbagbe la be, ne ɖe mèɖe abla va kpem o la, anye ne Nabal ƒe ame aɖeke masusɔ o; mawu wo katã hafi ŋu nake.”

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: David xɔ nu siwo keŋ wòtsɔ vɛ la eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Yi aƒe le ŋutifafa me. Kpɔ ɖa, mese wò nyaawo. Mawɔ nu si nèdi la.”

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Esi Abigail gbɔ va aƒe la, Nabal ɖo nuɖukplɔ̃ gã aɖe abe fia ene henɔ dzidzɔ kpɔm ale si wòate ŋui. Emu aha nɔ dzidzɔ kpɔm ale gbegbe be Abigail mete ŋu gblɔ nya aɖeke nɛ gbe ma gbe o.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke ŋdi la, Nabal ƒe mo kɔ eye Abigail gblɔ nya sia nya nɛ. Tete Nabal ƒe dzika tso enumake eye eƒe lã me tu.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Anɔ abe ŋkeke ewo megbe ene la, Aƒetɔ ƒo Nabal eye wòku.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: Abigail bɔbɔ tsyɔ mo anyi gblɔ be: “Eƒe nyɔnudɔla menye. Mele klalo be maklɔ eƒe dɔlawo ƒe afɔ.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Etso enumake eye wòde eƒe tedzi dzi. Nyɔnu subɔla atɔ̃ kpe ɖe eŋu eye wòdze mɔ kple David ƒe dɔlaawo eye wòyi ɖazu David srɔ̃.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: Do ŋgɔ la, David ɖe Axinoam tso Yezreel, eye Abigail hã va zu srɔ̃a kpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, Saul tsɔ via nyɔnu Mixal, ame si nye David srɔ̃ tsã la na Palti wòɖe. Palti nye Lais vi tso Galim.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Siftɔwo va Saul gbɔ le Gibea biae be: “David meva ɣla eɖokui ɖe Xavila-togbɛ si le Yesimon ƒe ɣedzeƒe la dzi oa?”

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Saul ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Xavila-togbɛ si le mɔ si le Yesimon ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome la xa; ke David ya tsi gbedadaƒo la. Esi wòkpɔ be Saul ti ye yome va gbedadaƒoa la,

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: edɔ ŋkutsalawo ɖa eye wode gbɔ va gblɔ nɛ be Saul le gbea dzi nyateƒe.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: David yi enumake ɖakpɔ afi si tututu Saul kple eƒe aʋakplɔla Abner, Ner vi la mlɔ anyi ɖo. Saul mlɔ anyi ɖe asaɖa la me eye eƒe amewo ƒo xlãe godoo.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
translation_verse: Tete David bia Xititɔ Aximelex kple Abisai, Yoab nɔvi, Zeruya vi la be: “Mia dometɔ kae ayi Saul ƒe asaɖa me kplim?” Abisai ɖo eŋu be: “Mayi kpli wò.”

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: Ale le gbe ma gbe ƒe zã me la, David kple Abisai ge ɖe Saul ƒe asaɖa la me. Wokpɔe wòdɔ alɔ̃ klenee ɖe asaɖa la titina; etsɔ eƒe akplɔ tu anyi ɖe eƒe tade. Abner kple aʋawɔlaawo ƒo xlãe.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Tete Abisai gblɔ na David be: “Mawu tsɔ wò futɔ de asi na wò egbe ƒe zã. Eya ta nà matsɔ akplɔ la tu edzi, zi ɖeka pɛ ko, amimii ɖe anyigba; nyemele eda ge zi eve o.”

english_verse: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
translation_verse: Ke David gblɔ nɛ be: “Mègawui o! Elabe ame ka aka asi Aƒetɔ ƒe amesiamina ŋu eye maɖi fɔ o?”

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: David gblɔ yi edzi be: “Metà Aƒetɔ gbagbe la: Ne Aƒetɔ mewui o la, eƒe ŋkeke ade wòaku loo, alo ayi aʋa woawui.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ megana maka asi Aƒetɔ ƒe amesiamina ŋu o. Ke tsɔ akplɔ si le eƒe tade kple tsizea ne míadzo.”

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: Ale David tsɔ akplɔa kple tsizea le Saul ƒe tade eye wodzo. Ame aɖeke mekpɔe loo, alo nya nu si dzɔ o. Ame aɖeke menyɔ gɔ̃ hã o; wo katã wodɔ alɔ̃ yi eme ʋĩi, elabe Aƒetɔ na wodɔ alɔ̃ yi eme ʋĩi.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: Azɔ David yi ɖe balia ƒe go kemɛ dzi tsi tsitre le adzɔge le togbɛ la dzi eye wo dome didi.

english_verse: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
translation_verse: Tete wòyɔ aʋakɔ la kple Abner, Ner vi ɖa be: “Abner! Mèle tɔtɔ ge oa?” Abner bia be: “Ame ka nye ekem le ɣli dom lelele ɖe fia ta?”

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: David ɖo eŋu be: “Abner, ɖe menye wòe nye kalẽtɔ gãtɔ le Israel oa? Nu ka ta màte ŋu adzɔ wò aƒetɔ, fia la ŋu o? Kpɔ ɖa, ame aɖe tso dukɔ la me ge ɖe asaɖa la me be yeawu wò aƒetɔ.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: Abner, mèwɔ wò dɔ o. Metà Aƒetɔ gbagbe la: Mi ame siawo katã miedze na ku, elabe miedzɔ miaƒe aƒetɔ, Aƒetɔ ƒe amesiamina la ŋu o. Kpɔ ɖa! Fia ƒe akplɔ la ɖe? Tsize si le eƒe tade la hã ɖe?”

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Saul dze sii be David ƒe nuƒoe eye wòbia be: “Vinye David, wòea?” David ɖo eŋu be: “Ẽ, nye aƒetɔ fia.”

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: Egblɔ yi edzi be: “Nye aƒetɔ, nu ka ta nègale, wò dɔla yome tim kokoko? Nu kae mewɔ? Vɔ̃ kae le ŋunye?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Azɔ fia bubutɔ, se nya si medi be magblɔ. Ne Aƒetɔ na nètsi tre ɖe ŋunye la, vɔsasa nɛ ana magawɔ nu si wòɖo be yeawɔ la o. Evɔ nenye amewoe wɔe la, Aƒetɔ ƒe fiƒode neɖi wo ŋu. Elabe wonyàm ɖa egbe tso Aƒetɔ ƒe anyigba dzi be mayi aɖasubɔ mawu bubuwo le dzronyigba dzi.

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Eya ta azɔ la, mègana woawum le dzronyigba dzi afi si Aƒetɔ mele o. Nu ka ta wòle be Israel-fia nado va be yeawu nye, si le abe dosu ene? Nu ka ta wòanɔ yonyeme tim abe tegli ene le towo dzi?”

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Saul ɖo eŋu be: “Mewɔ nuvɔ̃. Gbugbɔ, vinye David, nyemagawɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke wò azɔ o, elabe àte ŋu awum egbe hafi, ke esi nye agbe le vevie na wò ta, mèwum o. Kpɔ ɖa, mewɔ lãnu! Meda vo ŋutɔ!”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: David ɖo eŋu be: “Kpɔ ɖa, wò akplɔe nye esi. Nà ɖekakpuiawo dometɔ ɖeka nava afii ava xɔe.

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖoa eteƒe na nu dzɔdzɔe wɔlawo kple nuteƒewɔlawo. Aƒetɔ tsɔ wò de asi nam egbe, gake nyemaka asi Aƒetɔ ƒe amesiamina ŋu o.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, abe ale si wò agbe le vevie nam nyemewu wò o egbe ene la, nye hã tɔnye nenɔ vevie na Aƒetɔ nenema ale be wòaɖem le nye fukpekpewo katã me.”

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Saul gblɔ na David be: “Mawu neyra wò, vinye David! Àwɔ nu geɖewo eye àkpɔ dzidzedze le wo me.” Ale David gayi eƒe mɔzɔzɔ dzi, eye Saul trɔ yi aƒe.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: David gblɔ na eɖokui be: “Saul awum gbe ɖeka. Nu nyuitɔ si wòle be mawɔ azɔ la koe nye be masí ayi Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, ekema magadim le Israel azɔ o, eye mado le esi me.”

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Esi Saul se be David sí yi Gat la, edzudzɔ edidi.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: David gblɔ na Axis be: “Ne èdze xɔlɔ̃m vavã la, nà nɔƒem ɖe du suewo dometɔ ɖeka me ne maɖanɔ afi ma. Mehiã be manɔ fiadua me kpli wò o.”

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Ale Axis tsɔ Ziklag nɛ gbe ma gbe. Le esia ta Ziklag va zu Yuda-fiawo ƒe du va se ɖe egbe.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: David nɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi ƒe ɖeka ɣleti ene.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, eya kple eƒe amewo yina ɖadzea Gesuritɔwo, Girzitɔwo kple Amalekitɔwo, siwo le nutoa me tso gbe aɖe gbe ke la dzi. Egblẽa woƒe nuwo tso Sur ɖadona ɖe keke Egipte ke.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: Ewua ŋutsuwo kple nyɔnuwo katã eye wòtsɔa alẽwo, nyiwo, tedziwo, kposɔwo kple awuwo gbɔnae, eye wòyia Axis gbɔ.

english_verse: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
translation_verse: Ne Axis biae be: “Afi ka nède egbe ɖadze amewo dzi gblẽ nuwo?” mahã la, David ɖoa eŋu be yede Yuda ƒe anyigbeme loo, alo Yerameelitɔwo ƒe nutome le anyigbeme loo, alo Kenitɔwo ƒe nutome le anyigbeme.

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: David wua ame sia ame, ŋutsuwo kple nyɔnuwo siaa, bene ame aɖeke nagayi Gat aɖagblɔ nu si tututu wɔm wòle la o. Ŋkeke siwo katã wònɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi la, alea ko wòwɔna.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: Ke Axis xɔ David dzi se ŋutɔ, eye wòbu be: “Ewɔ eɖokui wo de Israeltɔwo lé fui keŋkeŋ; eya ta anye nye subɔla ɣe sia ɣi.”

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo kpe ta va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Sunem; Saul hã ƒo Israel blibo la nu ƒu, eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Gilboa.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Esi Saul kpɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakɔa la, evɔ̃, eye dzika tso eƒo ŋutɔ.

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
translation_verse: Ale Saul bia Aƒetɔ be wòagblɔ nu si wòle be yeawɔ la na ye. Gake Aƒetɔ meɖo eŋu nɛ le drɔ̃e me loo, alo to Urim kple Tumim dzi loo, alo to Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo dzi o.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Tete Saul gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo be: “Midi nyɔnu ŋɔliyɔla aɖe nam, ne mayi egbɔ aɖabia nui ase.” Eƒe dɔlawo gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ŋɔliyɔla aɖe le En-Dor.”

english_verse: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
translation_verse: Tete Saul do awu bubuwo be womagadze sii o, eye esi zã do la, eya kple ŋutsu eve woyi nyɔnu la gbɔ. Egblɔ na nyɔnua be: “Ka nu, ne nàyɔ ŋɔli nam. Kplɔ ame si ŋkɔ mayɔ na wò la vɛ nam.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Nyɔnua gblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, nu si fia Saul wɔ la le nyanya na wò nyuie. Ena ŋɔliyɔla kple afakala aɖeke megale Israel-nyigba dzi o. Nu ka ta nèle mɔ̀ trem nam be yealé awu?”

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Tete Saul tà nu gblɔ be: “Metà Aƒetɔ gbagbe la be, ne mena wohe to na wò fĩi!”

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Nyɔnua biae be: “Ame ka yɔ ge mala na wò?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Yɔ Samuel nam.”

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Esi nyɔnua kpɔ Samuel la, edo ɣli sesĩe eye wògblɔ na Saul be: “Nu ka ta nèblem? Ke wòe nye Saul hafi!”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Ke fia la gblɔ nɛ be: “Mègavɔ̃ o. Nu kae nèkpɔ?” Nyɔnua ɖo eŋu be: “Mekpɔ mawu aɖe si le dodom tso anyigba tu me.”

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
