translation_verse: Saul biae be: “Ale ke wòle?” Nyɔnua ɖo eŋu be: “Ame tsitsi aɖee do gbɔna. Edo awu ʋlaya.” Saul nya be Samuel ye, eya ta ede ta agu eye wòbɔbɔ.

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ na Saul be: “Nu ka ta nèɖe fu nam? Nu ka ta nèna wokplɔm vɛ?” Saul ɖo eŋu be: “Meɖo xaxa me ŋutɔ. Filistitɔwo le aʋa wɔm kplim, ke Mawu trɔ le yonyeme. Megale nya ŋu ɖom nam to eƒe gbeƒãɖelawo dzi loo, alo to drɔ̃e me azɔ o. Esia ta mena woyɔ wò vɛ, ne nàgblɔ nu si wòle be mawɔ la nam.”

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Samuel gblɔ be: “Ne Aƒetɔ trɔ le yowòme hezu wò futɔ la, nu ka ta nàva nɔ gbe biamem?

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Nya si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nam be magblɔ na wò la dzie wòwɔ. Exɔ fiaɖuƒe la le asiwò hetsɔ na David.

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: Nu si ta Aƒetɔ le nu sia wɔm egbe ɖoe nye be ègbe eƒe gbe dzi wɔwɔ. Esi wòdo dziku ɖe Amalekitɔwo ŋu, eye wògblɔ na wò be nàtsrɔ̃ wo keŋkeŋ la, mèɖo toe o.

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Azɔ atsɔ wò kple Israel-dukɔa ade Filistitɔwo si. Etsɔ la, wò kple viwò ŋutsuwo miava gbɔnye, eye woatsɔ Israel ƒe aʋakɔ la ade asi na Filistitɔwo.”

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Enumake Saul dze anyi dra legbee ɖe anyigba, elabe Samuel ƒe nyawo na vɔvɔ̃ ɖoe ŋutɔ. Egbɔdzɔ elabe meɖu naneke gbe ma gbe kple zã blibo la o.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Esi nyɔnua va egbɔ la, ekpɔ be dzidzi ƒoe ŋutɔ. Tete wògblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, mewɔ wò nya dzi wu ɖokuinye kloe.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: Azɔ wɔ nu si gblɔ ge mala na wò. Nà mawɔ nuɖuɖu aɖe na wò. Ehiã be nàɖu nu ŋusẽ nagaɖo ŋuwò hafi nàdzo.”

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: Ke Saul gbe gblɔ be yemele naneke ɖu ge o. Eŋumeawo kple nyɔnua ƒoe ɖe enu ʋuu hafi wòlɔ̃. Etso le anyigba eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ aba dzi.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Nyɔnua wɔ kaba wu nyivi dami si le esi le aƒea me. Eku wɔ tsɔ wɔ abolo maʋamaʋãe.

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: Eɖo nuɖuɖua Saul kple eŋumeawo kɔme woɖu. Esi woɖu nua vɔ la, wodzo le zã ma ke me.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Ke Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakplɔlaawo do dziku ɖe eŋu gblɔ nɛ be: “Gbugbɔe ɖo ɖe du si nètsɔ nɛ la me. Mele be wòayi aʋa la kpli mí o, elabe ate ŋu atrɔ ɖe mía ŋu le aʋaa me. Nu ka wòadi be yeawɔ adze yeƒe aƒetɔ ŋu? Ðe menye esi wòatso míaƒe ta atsɔ ayi nɛ lae oa?

english_verse: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
translation_verse: Evɔ la, ɖe menye David si nyɔnuwo dzi ha kafu be: ‘Saul wu akpe, eye David wu akpe ewowo’ lae nye esia oa?”

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Tete Axis yɔ David tà nu gblɔ be: “Metà Aƒetɔ gbagbe la be le nye gome la, ènye nuteƒewɔla eye àte ŋu aho aʋa kplim, míayi agbɔ, elabe tso gbe si gbe nèva gbɔnye va se ɖe egbe la, mèwɔ nu masɔmasɔ aɖeke mekpɔ kpɔ o. Ke aʋakplɔlaawo medi be nàyi kpli mí o.

english_verse: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
translation_verse: Eya ta gbugbɔ yi aƒe le ŋutifafa me, eye mègawɔ naneke si aɖia wo nu o.”

english_verse: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
translation_verse: David ɖo eŋu be: “Nu ka mewɔ? Nu ka nèkpɔ le ŋunye tso gbe si gbe meva gbɔwò va se ɖe fifia si wɔe be nyemate ŋu ayi kpli wò, nye aƒetɔ kple nye fia, aɖawɔ aʋa kple wò futɔwo na wò o?”

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Axis ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Le gbɔnye la, ɖe nèle nam abe mawudɔla ene; mokaka aɖeke mele ŋuwò o, ke fia bubuawo le gbɔgblɔm be medze be nàyi aʋa la kpli mí o.

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Tete David kple eƒe ameawo fɔ ŋdi kanya eye wodze mɔ hegbugbɔ yi Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi; ke Filistitɔwo ho yi Yezreel.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: Esi David kple eƒe amewo gbɔ va Ziklag le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe la, wokpɔ be Amalekitɔwo va dze anyigbemenyigba dzi le Yuda, si Ziklag-dua, tɔ dzoe,

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi David kple eƒe amewo va ɖo la, wokpɔ be wotɔ dzo dua eye wokplɔ yewo srɔ̃wo, yewo viŋutsuwo kple yewo vinyɔnuwo dzoe.

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: Tete David kple eƒe ameawo fa avi kple ɣli ʋuu va se ɖe esime ɖeɖi te wo ŋu, avi meganya le fafam na wo o.

english_verse: David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
translation_verse: Wokplɔ David srɔ̃ eveawo, Axinoam kple Abigail, hã dzoe.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: David xaxa ŋutɔ elabe eƒe ameawo le veve sem vevie le wo vi siwo bu la ta, eye wodi be yewoaƒu kpee gɔ̃. Ke David ɖo dzi ɖe Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu la ŋu eye wòna wòlé dzi ɖe ƒo.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: David gblɔ na nunɔla Abyatar, Aximelex vi be: “Tsɔ kɔmewu la vɛ nam!” eye Abyatar tsɔe yi nɛ.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: David bia nu Aƒetɔ be: “Mati adzoha la yomea? Matu woa?” Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Ti wo yome. Èle wo tu ge axɔ ameawo le wo si.”

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: David ŋumewo kpɔ Egipte-ŋutsu aɖe le gbe me, eye wokplɔe va David gbɔe. Wona aboloe wòɖu eye woku tsi nɛ wòno.

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: Woka gbotsetsebolo eye wotsɔ waintsetse ƒuƒu kpe ɖe eŋu nɛ wòɖu. Esi wòɖu nua vɔ la, ŋusẽ gaɖo eŋu, elabe ŋkeke etɔ̃ sɔŋ nye ekem megano tsi alo ɖu naneke kpɔ o.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: David biae be: “Ame kae nye wò aƒetɔ, eye afi ka nètso?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Egiptetɔe menye, henye Amalekitɔ aɖe ƒe dɔla. Medze dɔ eya ta nye aƒetɔ gblẽm ɖi dzo, egbee nye ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: Míeyi ɖadze Kretitɔwo dzi le Yuda ƒe anyigbeme kple Kaleb to ƒe anyigba dzi eye míetɔ dzo Ziklag-du.”

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: David biae be: “Màkplɔm ayi adzohaawo gbɔe oa?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Ne àtà Aƒetɔ nam be yemawum o, eye yematsɔm ade asi na nye aƒetɔ hã o la, ekema makplɔ wò ayii.”

english_verse: He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah.
translation_verse: Ale wòkplɔ David yi wo gbɔe. Ameawo kaka ɖe teƒea katã le nu ɖum, le nu nom eye wole ɣe ɖum le dzidzɔ kpɔm le aboyonu geɖe si woha tso Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi kple Yuda la ŋuti.

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: Tete David dze wo dzi, wɔ avu kpli wo tso esime anyigba nɔ tsyɔtsyɔm gbe ma gbe va se ɖe evea gbe fiẽ. Ewu wo keŋkeŋ negbe ɖekakpuivi alafa ene siwo do sɔ sí dzo la ko.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: David xɔ nu siwo katã Amalekitɔwo ha dzoe la, eye wòxɔ srɔ̃a eveawo hã.

english_verse: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
translation_verse: Naneke mebu o. Exɔ eƒe ameawo ƒe viŋutsuwo kple vinyɔnuwo kple nu siwo katã Amalekitɔwo ha dzoe la hã gbɔe.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: David xɔ alẽwo kple nyiwo hã. Eƒe ameawo kplɔ wo dze lãha bubuawo ŋgɔ gblɔ be: “David ƒe aboyonue nye esia!”

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Ke ame vlo kple yakame siwo le ame siwo David kplɔ de nua gbee dome la gblɔ na David be: “Womede kpli mí o, eya ta míana aboyonuawo ƒe ɖeke wo o; wonekplɔ wo srɔ̃wo kple wo viwo ko ne woayi.”

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Ke David gblɔ be: “Nɔvinyewo, mele be míawɔ nu si Aƒetɔ tsɔ na mí la nenema o. Ekpɔ mía ta míele dedie eye wòna míeɖu adzoha siwo va dze mía dzi heha míaƒe nuwo la dzi.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Ame aɖeke malɔ̃ ɖe nya sia dzi na mi akpɔ o. Ele be mí katã míama aboyonuawo sɔsɔe: ele be nu si aʋadela axɔ la nasɔ kple esi ame si tsi nuawo gbɔ la axɔ.”

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: David na nya sia va zu ɖoɖo kple se na Israel-dukɔ tso gbe ma gbe dzi va se ɖe egbe.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Esi David gbɔ va Ziklag la, eɖo aboyonuawo ƒe ɖewo ɖe xɔlɔ̃awo, siwo nye Yuda-me tsitsiwo. Egblɔ kpe ɖe nuawo ŋu be: “Nunana sia la, tɔwòe. Etso aboyonu siwo mexɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe futɔwo si la me.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo wɔ aʋa kple Israel eye Israel-ŋutsuwo sí le Filistitɔwo nu; amewo tsi aʋa le Gilboa-to dzi.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo ɖe wo ɖe nu eye wova tu Saul kple viawo, Yonatan, Abinadab kple Malkisua hewu wo.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Aʋa la nu sẽ ŋutɔ ɖe Saul dzi eye aŋutrɔdalawo dze sii eye wode abi eŋu vevie.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ na eƒe agbadzatsɔvi be: “Ðe wò adekpui nàƒo ɖem, ne Filistitɔ bolobolotɔ siawo magava ƒo nu ɖem ahado kokoem o!” Ke agbadzatsɔvi la gbe elabe vɔvɔ̃ ɖoe ŋutɔ. Ale Saul dze eya ŋutɔ ƒe adekpui nu.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Esi ɖekakpui la kpɔ be eku la, eya hã dze eya ŋutɔ ƒe adekpui nu, eye wòku kplii.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Ale Saul kple via ŋutsu etɔ̃awo, eƒe agbadzatsɔvi la kple eƒe amewo katã ku gbe ɖeka.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Esi Israelvi siwo le bali la ƒe go kemɛ dzi kple esiwo le Yordan ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome se be aʋa si Israelviwo ƒe aʋakɔ, wosí, eye Saul kple viawo ku la, woawo hã wosí hegblẽ woƒe duwo ɖi. Ale Filistitɔwo va xɔ duawo eye wonɔ wo me.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: Le ŋufɔke, esi Filistitɔwo yi be yewoaɖaɖe nu le ame tsiaʋaawo ŋu la, wokpɔ be Saul kple via ŋutsu etɔ̃awo ku tsi Gilboa-to dzi.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Ke esi Yabestɔ siwo le Gilead se nu si Filistitɔwo wɔ Saul la,

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: woƒe ŋutsu kalẽtɔwo katã tso, eye wozɔ zã yi Bet-San. Woɖe Saul kple via ŋutsuawo ƒe kukuawo le gliawo ŋu, eye wotsɔ wo va Yabes hetɔ dzo wo le afi ma.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Azɔ wotsɔ woƒe ƒuwo yi ɖaɖi ɖe ati aɖe te le Yabes, eye wotsi nu dɔ ŋkeke adrẽ.

english_verse: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
translation_verse: Le Saul ƒe ku megbe la, David gbɔ tso aʋa si wòde ɖawɔ le Amalek, eye wòtsi Ziklag ŋkeke eve.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe la, kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsu aɖe tso Saul ƒe asaɖa me va do. Eƒe awu vuvu, eye ke le tame nɛ. Esi wòva David gbɔ la, ebɔbɔ eye wòde ta agu.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: David biae be: “Afi ka nètso?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Israel ƒe asaɖa mee mesí tso.”

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: David biae be: “Afi ma maniɛ ɖe? Bɔe nam.” Eɖo eŋu be: “Míaƒe aʋakɔ la sí le futɔawo nu, eye ame geɖewo tsi aʋa le wo dome. Wowu Saul kple via Yonatan.”

english_verse: David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
translation_verse: David bia ɖekakpui si va to nya la be: “Ale ke nèwɔ nya be Saul kple via Yonatan ku?”

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu be: “Menɔ Gilboa-to dzi; nu do go ɖe nu nu ko wònye be menɔ afi ma le ɣe ma ɣi me. Tete mekpɔ Saul wòziɔ ɖe eƒe akplɔ ŋu, eye tasiaɖam kple sɔdolawo tu ta egbɔ nɔ tetem ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: Esi wònye kɔ kpɔm la, eyɔm, eye metɔ be, ‘Nyee nye esi!’

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: Ebiam be ame kae menye mahã, eye megblɔ nɛ be Amalekitɔ menye.

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ nam be, ‘Te ɖe ŋunye ne nàwum! Mese veve ʋuu de kuku ge hã do kpoe.’

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: Ale mete ɖe eŋu hewui elabe mekpɔe dze sii kɔtɛe be, ne edze anyi la, aku godoo. Azɔ meɖe fiakuku la le eta, ɖe alɔnuga si le eƒe alɔnu la hã, eye metsɔ wo va afii na wò, nye aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Tete David dze awu le eɖokui ŋu, eye eƒe amewo hã dze wo tɔ.

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: Wofa konyi, fa avi hetsi nu dɔ va se ɖe fiẽ. Wowɔ esia na Saul kple Yonatan kple Israel-dukɔ kpakple Aƒetɔ ƒe ame siwo katã tsi aʋa la.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: David bia ɖekakpui si va to nya la nɛ la be: “Du ka me tɔ nènye?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Amedzro aɖe, si nye Amalekitɔ la vie menye.”

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: David gblɔ na Amalekitɔ la be: “Wò ʋu anɔ wò ŋutɔ wò ta dzi elabe èbu fɔ ɖokuiwò esime nèke nu gblɔ be: ‘Nyee wu Aƒetɔ ƒe amesiamina la.’ ” David dzi konyifaha na Saul kple Yonatan

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: Tete David kpa konyifaha sia le Saul kple Yonatan ŋu,

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: “Aléle! Israel, kplɔwòla bubutɔwoe nye ekem wowu le wò togbɛwo dzi! Ale ke wɔ ŋusẽtɔwo tsi aʋa alea!

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Migagblɔe le Gat o; migaɖe gbeƒãe le Askalon ƒe ablɔwo dzi, ne Filisti vinyɔnuwo nava kpɔ dzidzɔ o; ne bolobolotɔ vinyɔnuwo nava tso aseye o.

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: “Mi Gilboa-towo, migana zãmu alo tsi nagadza ɖe mia dzi o; tomenuwo megaho ɖe dzi o! Elabe afi mae wogblẽ kɔ ɖo na ŋusẽtɔwo ƒe akpoxɔnuwo le. Saul ƒe akpoxɔnu, womesi ami nɛ o!

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Yonatan ƒe dati megbea aʋatsiawo ƒe ʋu, kple ŋusẽtɔwo ƒe ami me dede o. Saul ƒe yi megbɔna ƒuƒlu o.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: “Saul kple Yonatan nyakpɔna, amewo lɔ̃ woƒe nya vevie. Tsi meto wo dome le agbe me o, eye le ku me ke hã wo dome mema o. Woɖea abla wu hɔ̃; wosesẽ wu dzata.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: “Mi Israel vinyɔnuwo, mifa avi na Saul. Eyae na miedo avɔ dzĩ biɖibiɖi wu, eye wòna miekpla sikanuwo ɖe wo dzi, tsɔ ɖo atsyɔ̃e.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: “Ale ke wɔ ŋusẽtɔwo dze anyi le aʋa domedome ale? Wowu Yonatan da ɖe togbɛ dzi wòmlɔ anyigba!

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: “Nɔvinye Yonatan, tɔwò le veyem lo! Wò ame bliboa esɔe nam ale gbegbe! Wò lɔlɔ̃ nam nye nuku; eƒo nyɔnu ƒe lɔlɔ̃ ta.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: “Ale ke wɔ ŋusẽtɔwo dze anyi alea! Woƒe aʋawɔnuwo vɔ ɖe ya me!”

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Le nyadzɔdzɔ sia megbe la, David bia Aƒetɔ be: “Mayi ɖanɔ Yuda-duawo dometɔ ɖeka mea?” Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Yi.” David bia be: “Ka mee mayi?” Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Yi Xebron.”

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: Ale David yi Xebron kple srɔ̃a eveawo, Axinoam Yezreeltɔ kple Abigail, Nabal ƒe ahosia, tso Karmel.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: Ekplɔ ame siwo le eŋu la hã yii, ɖe sia ɖe kple eƒemetɔwo, eye woɖanɔ du siwo le Xebron gbɔ la me.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Tete Yuda-ŋutsuwo va David gbɔ le Xebron, eye wosi ami nɛ wòzu fia le Yuda. Esi wogblɔ na David be: “Yabestɔ siwo le Gilead lae ɖi Saul” la,

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: edɔ ame ɖo ɖe wo be wòaɖagblɔ na wo be: “Aƒetɔ neyra mi le esi miewɔ nuteƒe na miaƒe aƒetɔ Saul be mieɖii la ta.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Le nu si miewɔ ta, Aƒetɔ nenyo dɔme eye wòaɖi anukware na mi. Nye hã mawɔ nyui na mi le nu si miewɔ ta.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Azɔ mido ŋusẽ nu, eye miwɔ kalẽ! Elabe miaƒe aƒetɔ Saul ku, eye Yudatɔwo si ami nam be manye yewoƒe fia.” Woɖo Isboset fiae le Israel

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Ke Saul ƒe aʋakplɔla Abner, Ner vi, sí kple Saul vi, Isboset yi Maxanaim le Yordan godo.

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: Abner ɖoe fiae le afi ma ɖe Gileadtɔwo, Asertɔwo, Yezreeltɔwo, Efrayimtɔwo, Benyamintɔwo kple Israel blibo la dzi.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: eye wònɔ Xebron ɖu wo dzi ƒe adrẽ kple afã. Israel kple Yuda wɔ aʋa

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Abner kple Isboset ƒe dɔlawo ho tso Maxanaim yi Gibeon-du me.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Yoab, ame si nɔ nye Zeruya kple David ƒe dɔlawo hã ho, eye akpa eveawo va do go le tá la nu, eye wo katã nɔ anyi ɖe afi ma. Akpa ɖeka nɔ tá la ƒe go ɖeka dzi, eye evelia hã nɔ go kemɛ dzi.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Abner gblɔ na Yoab be: “Mína ɖekakpuiawo dometɔ aɖewo natsi tsitre ate kame ne míakpɔ.” Yoab lɔ̃ ɖe edzi.

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Ale ɖekakpui wui eve tso Isboset ƒe akpa dzi va kpe kple ɖekakpui wui eve tso David ƒe akpa dzi.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Wo dome ame sia ame lé nɔvia ƒe ta, eye wòƒo adekpui ɖe axadame nɛ. Ale wo katã wodze anyi zi ɖeka heku. Eya ta wona ŋkɔ teƒe la be “Helkat-hazurim” le Gibeon.

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Tete aʋa dziŋɔ aɖe dzɔ gbe ma gbe, ɖe akpa eveawo dome eye David ƒe amewo ɖu Abner kple Israeltɔwo dzi.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Yoab, Abisai kple Asahel siwo nye Zeruya viŋutsuwo la nɔ David ƒe ameawo dome. Asahel, ame si ƒua du abe zi ene la,

english_verse: missing besides Asahel.
translation_verse: ɖe Abner ɖe nu tẽe.

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Abner nye kɔ kpɔ megbe eye wògblɔ be: “Asahel, wòea?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Ẽ, nyee!”

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Abner gblɔ be: “Gbugbɔ le yonyeme. Ti ɖekakpuiawo dometɔ ɖeka yome ne nàlée axɔ eƒe nuwo le esi.” Gake Sahel gakplɔe ɖo ko.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Abner gagblɔ nɛ be: “Mebe trɔ le yonyeme! Nu ka ta nèle teyem kpɔ be mada nu wò aƒu anyi nàku? Ale ke mate ŋu akpɔ nɔviwò Yoab ŋkumee?”

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Ke egbe tɔtrɔ. Ale Abner da akplɔe to megbe. Akplɔa tɔ dɔme nɛ, ɖi go ɖe egodo. Asahel dze anyi ɖe afi ma heku eye ame sia ame si va to afi si wòdze anyi ku ɖo la tɔna ɖi.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Yoab kple Abisai kplɔ Abner ɖo kple du. Esi ɣe nɔ to ɖom la, wova Ama-togbɛ si le Giax ƒe ɣetoɖoƒe gome, le mɔ, si ɖo ta Gibeon-gbedadaƒo, to la gbɔ.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Tete Benyamin viwo ƒo wo ɖokui nu ƒu ɖe Abner ŋu, wɔ aʋakɔ ɖeka, eye wotsi tsitre ɖe togbɛ aɖe tame.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Abner yɔ Yoab ɖa gblɔ nɛ be: “Ɖe míanɔ aʋawɔwɔ dzi madzudzɔea? Mènyae be veve helihelĩ koe ava xɔ mía me ɖe mía nɔewo ŋu emegbe oa? Nɔviwo míenyee! Ɣe ka ɣi nàna be wò amewo adzudzɔ mía yometiti?”

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Yoab ɖo eŋu be: “Metà Mawu gbagbe la. Ɖe menye wòe ƒo nu o la, anye ne nye amewo anɔ mia yome tim ʋuu va se ɖe etsɔ ŋdi.”

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Tete Yoab ku kpẽ na eƒe ameawo be woadzudzɔ Israelviwo yometiti. Ale avua ke le wo dome.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Abner kple eƒe amewo zɔ to Yordan-bali la me zã blibo la. Wotso Yordan-tɔsisi la, eye woto ʋe la me va Maxanaim.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Esi Yoab dzudzɔ Abner yometiti la, eƒo eƒe ameawo katã nu ƒu eye wòkpɔ be ame wui asieke meli o, hekpe ɖe Asahel ŋu.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Yoab kple eƒe amewo kɔ Asahel ƒe kukua yi ɖaɖi ɖe tɔ́a ƒe ameɖiƒe le Betlehem. Emegbe wozɔ zã blibo la va ɖo Xebron le fɔŋli me.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Esime Saul ƒe amewo kple ame siwo kpe ɖe David ŋu, nɔ aʋa wɔm la, ŋusẽ va nɔ Abner ŋu ɖom ɖe edzi le Saul ƒe amewo dome.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la, Isboset, Saul viŋutsu tso ɖe Abner ŋu be edɔ kple ye tɔ́ ƒe ahiãvi Rizpa, Aya vinyɔnu.

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Tete Abner do dɔmedzoe vevie ɖe Isboset ŋu le nya sia ta. Egblɔ be: “Ɖe nèbu be metrɔ le Saul yome hele kpekpem ɖe Yuda ŋu azɔa? Tɔ́wò Saul ƒe akpa dzi ko megale va se ɖe egbe. Mewɔ nuteƒe na nɔvia ŋutsuwo kple xɔlɔ̃awo, eye gawu la, mexɔ na wò ŋutɔ hã ale be mège ɖe David si me o. Ale ke wɔ nàtso ɖe ŋunye azɔ le nyɔnu ta?

english_verse: I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him!
translation_verse: Mawu nefia nu Abner, negafiae ɖe edzi, ne nyemekpɔ egbɔ be David ƒe asi su nu si ŋugbe Aƒetɔ do nɛ la dzi,

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: be fiaɖuƒe la nadzo le Saul ƒe aƒeme, eye wòaɖo fiazikpui anyi na David ɖe Israel kple Yuda dzi, tso Dan va se ɖe Beer-Seba o fĩi!

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Isboset megate ŋu ɖo nya la ŋu na Abner o, elabe enɔ evɔ̃m.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Abner dɔ amewo ɖo ɖe David gbɔ le Xebron, be woaɖagblɔ nɛ be: “Ame kae le anyigba sia dzi ɖu ge? Bla nu kplim eye makpe ɖe ŋuwò akplɔ Israel blibo la vɛ na wò.”

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: David ɖo eŋu ɖo ɖee be: “Enyo, mabla nu kpli wò; ke nu ɖeka si mabia tso asiwòe nye be màkpɔ nye ŋkume o, negbe ɖeko nàkplɔ Saul vinyɔnu Mixal vɛ gbã hafi nàva kpɔm.”

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: Tete David dɔ amewo ɖe Saul viŋutsu, Isboset hã, be woagblɔ nɛ be: “Gbugbɔ srɔ̃nye Mixal ɖo ɖem. Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋanuyi alafa ɖeka mena ɖe eta hafi ɖee.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
translation_verse: Ale Isboset dɔ amewo woyi ɖaxɔe le srɔ̃a Paltiel, Lais vi si.

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Paltiel dze srɔ̃a yome kple avi ʋuu va ɖo Baxurim. Abner gblɔ nɛ le afi sia be: “Trɔ yi aƒe.” Ale wòtrɔ yi.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Azɔ Abner kpe ta kple Israel-me tsitsiwo gblɔ na wo be: “Enye miaƒe didi xoxo be David naɖu fia ɖe mia dzi.

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Mina wòava eme azɔ elabe Aƒetɔ do ŋugbe na David be: ‘Nye dɔla David ƒe asi dzie mato aɖe nye dukɔ Israel tso Filistitɔwo kple woƒe futɔ bubuwo katã si me.’ ”

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Abner yi ɖaƒo nu na Benyamin-to la me tɔwo hã, eye wòyi Xebron be yeaɖagblɔ nu siwo katã Israel kple Benyamin toawo me tɔwo bu be enyo yewoawɔ la na David.

english_verse: soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
translation_verse: Esi Abner kple ŋutsu bla eveawo va David gbɔ le Xebron la, David wɔ amedzro na wo nyuie.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Abner gblɔ na David be: “Fifia la, mayi aɖaƒo Israel-dukɔ blibo la nu ƒu be woanɔ tewò, nye aƒetɔ fia. Woabla nu kpli wò, eye nàɖu wo dzi abe ale si nèdi ene.” Ale David na Abner dzo yi le ŋutifafa me. Wowu Abner

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: Emegbe ʋɛ la, Yoab kple David ƒe dɔlawo gbɔ tso adzogbe, eye wotsɔ nu siwo woha la geɖe gbɔe. Abner dzo le David gbɔ le Xebron hafi wogbɔ, elabe David do mɔe wòdzo yi le ŋutifafa me.

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Esi Yoab kple eƒe amewo va ɖo la, wogblɔ na Yoab be Abner va fia la gbɔ, eye wòdo mɔe wòdzo yi le ŋutifafa me.

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Ale Yoab yi fia la gbɔ ɖabiae be: “Nu ka nye esi nèwɔ? Abner va gbɔwò ko nèɖe asi le eŋu wòdzo yi. Nu ka tae?

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: Mènya be Abner, Ner vi lae oa? Ɖe wòva afii be yeable wò, anya ɣeyiɣi si nèdona gagbɔna kple nu siwo katã nèwɔna.”

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Esi Yoab dzo le David gbɔ la, edɔ amewo ɖe Abner yome be woaɖatrɔe vɛ. Wotui le Sira-vudo la gbɔ eye wotrɔe gbɔe. Ke David menya naneke le nu si nɔ edzi yim la ŋu o.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Azɔ esi Abner va ɖo Xebron la, Yoab ɖe kpɔe yi agbo la nu abe ɖe wòdi be yeagblɔ nya aɖe nɛ ene, eye wòtɔ hɛ dɔme nɛ wòku ɖe afi ma. Ale Yoab wu Abner le esi eya hã wu nɔvia Asahel ta.

english_verse: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
translation_verse: Esi David va se nyaa la, egblɔ be: “Nye kple tenye viwo míeɖi fɔ kura le Abner wuwu me le Aƒetɔ gbɔ o.

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: Tohehe si adze amewuwu sia yome la nenɔ Yoab kple eƒe ƒomeawo katã dzi! Le dzidzime ɖe sia ɖe me le eƒe ƒome me la, nulɔdɔléla kple ŋutigbalẽdɔ vɔ̃ɖi léla mavɔ akpɔ o; nyɔnugbɔmewo anɔ anyi ɖaa; ame atsi yi nu eye ame anɔ anyi anye ɖunumaɖiƒoewo.”

english_verse: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Ale Yoab kple nɔvia Abisai wu Abner, elabe ewu wo nɔvi Asahel le aʋa me le Gibeon. Woɖi Abner

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: David gblɔ na Yoab kple ame siwo katã le eŋu la be: “Midze miaƒe awuwo, mita akpanya eye mifa Abner le egbɔ.” Esi woyina eɖi ge la, fia David ŋutɔ dze amekukugba la yome.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Woɖi Abner ɖe Xebron. Fia la fa avi kple ɣli le yɔdoa to, eye ameha blibo la hã fae.

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: David dzi konyifaha sia na Abner be: “Abner, ɖe wòle be nàku abe yakame enea?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: Womebla asi na wò o, womede ga afɔ na wò o; ke èku, abe hlɔ̃dola aɖee wu wò ene.” Tete ameha blibo la gafa avi ɖe dzi wu.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Ameha la ƒoe ɖe David nu ŋkeke bliboa be wòaɖu nu, ke eka atam be: “Mawu neƒom ƒu anyi, ne maku agaku, ne made nane nu me hafi ɣe naɖo to fĩi.”

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Ame sia ame de dzesi esia, eye wòdze wo ŋu. Le nyateƒe me la, nu sia nu si fia la wɔ la dze ameha blibo la ŋu.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: David ƒe amewo katã kple Israel-dukɔ blibo se egɔme gbe ma gbe be fia la menya naneke le Abner wuwu ŋu kura o.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo be: “Miekpɔe dze sii be amegã kple bubume vevi aɖee ku le Israel-dukɔ me egbe oa?

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Togbɔ be nyee nye fia si wosi ami na hã la, egbe la, megbɔdzɔ keŋ. Zeruya vi siawo ƒe nya sesẽ nam akpa. Ame si wɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi sia la Aƒetɔ newɔe ɖe nu nɛ abe ale si dze ene!”

english_verse: Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
translation_verse: Esi Isboset, Saul vi, se be Abner ku le Xebron la, vɔvɔ̃ ɖoe ŋutɔ eye dzidzi ƒo Israel-dukɔ blibo la.

english_verse: Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Adzohakplɔla eve le Isboset si siwo ƒe ŋkɔwoe nye Baana kple Rexab. Wonye Rimon, Beerotetɔ viwo tso Benyamin-to la me. Wobua Beerot hã kpena ɖe Benyamin ŋu.

english_verse: The people who used to live in Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they still live there.
translation_verse: Beerotetɔ ŋutɔŋutɔwo sí yi Gitaim, eye wotsi afi ma va se ɖe egbe.

english_verse: Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
translation_verse: Saul ƒe dzidzimevi bubu hãe nye Mefiboset, Yonatan vi. Exɔ ƒe atɔ̃ esime wowu Saul kple Yonatan. Esi du tso Yezreel va be woku la, ame si nɔ enyim la kɔe kpa hesí kplii. Etsi dzi ŋutɔ esime wònɔ sísim. Ale ɖevia ge eye eƒe atawo tu.

english_verse: One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting
translation_verse: Rexab kple Baana tso dze mɔ eye wova Isboset ƒeme le ŋdɔ me, esime wònɔ ŋdɔlɔ̃ dɔm.

english_verse: in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them. Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long.
translation_verse: Esi woge ɖe aƒea me la, woyi ɖe Isboset ƒe xɔgãme, afi si wòmlɔ anyi ɖo dɔ alɔ̃ klenee. Wowui, tso eƒe ta tsɔ dzoe eye wozɔ mɔ zã blibo la to Yordan-bali me.

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: Wova ɖo Xebron eye wotsɔ ta la vɛ na fia David gblɔ nɛ be: “Isboset, Saul vi, wò futɔ si le wò ku dim ƒe tae nye esi. Míaƒe fia bubutɔ, egbe la Aƒetɔ bia hlɔ̃ Saul kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo na wò.”

english_verse: David answered: I swear that only the Lord rescues me when I'm in trouble!
translation_verse: David ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Metà Aƒetɔ si le agbe eye wòɖem tso ŋɔdzinuwo katã me!

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: Esime aɖe va gblɔ nam be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa, Saul ku!’ eye wòbu be du nyui aɖee yexɔ vɛ nam la, melée hewui le Ziklag, wònye fetu nɛ ɖe du si wòxɔ vɛ la ta.

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: Ale ke wɔ ne ame vɔ̃ɖiwo wu ame dzɔdzɔe le eya ŋutɔ ƒe aƒeme, le aƒe aba dzi la, nyemabia eƒe ʋu tso mia si me eye matsrɔ̃ mi ɖa le anyigba dzi wu o?”

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_verse: Tete David ɖe gbe na ɖekakpuiawo eye wowu wo. Wolã woƒe asi kple afɔ le wo ŋu ɖaku nu ɖe tá to le Xebron. Ke wotsɔ Isboset ƒe ta yi ɖaɖi ɖe Abner ƒe yɔdo me le Xebron.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
translation_verse: Fia Xiram tso Tiro ɖo amewo kple sedertiwo ɖe David, eye wòna atikpalawo kple xɔtulawo hã le wo dome be woatu fiasã na David.

english_verse: He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for
translation_verse: Enɔ Xebron ɖu fia ɖe Yuda dzi ƒe adrẽ ɣleti ade, eye wòva nɔ Yerusalem ɖu fia ɖe Israel blibo la kple Yuda dzi ƒe bla etɔ̃ vɔ etɔ̃.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
translation_verse: Fia David kple eƒe amewo tso ɖe Yebusitɔwo ŋu, eye woho yi Yerusalem be yewoaɖaxɔ dua le Yebusitɔwo si. Yebusitɔwo bu be David mate ŋu axɔe o. Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Màte ŋu aɖo afɔ afi sia akpɔ o; ŋkuagbãtɔwo kple tekunɔwo koe axe mɔ na wò.”

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: David nɔ ŋusẽ kpɔm ɖe edzi elabe Aƒetɔ, Mawu Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la li kplii.

english_verse: David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people. David's Sons Born in Jerusalem (
translation_verse: David dze sii azɔ be Aƒetɔ ye ɖo ye, be yeaɖu Israel dzi eya tae wòna yeƒe fiaɖuɖu la le dzidzedze kpɔm, le eƒe dukɔ Israel ta.

english_verse: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children.
translation_verse: Esi David tso Xebron va Yerusalem la, egaɖo ahiãviwo eye wògaɖe srɔ̃ bubuwo hã. Woawo hã gadzi ŋutsuviwo kple nyɔnuviwo nɛ.

english_verse: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
translation_verse: Yibxar, Elisua, Nefeg, Yafia,

english_verse: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. David Fights the Philistines (
translation_verse: Elisama, Elyada kple Elifelet. David ɖu Filistitɔwo dzi (Kron I,

english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo se be woɖo David fia ɖe Israel nu, ale wo katã woho yi be yewoaɖadii alé. Esi David see la, eyi ɖe mɔ́ la me.

english_verse: So the Philistines camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Filistitɔwo va Refaim-bali la me, eye wokaka ɖe teƒea.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?” The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
translation_verse: David bia Aƒetɔ be: “Maho yi ɖawɔ aʋa kpli woa? Àna maɖu wo dzia?” Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Ho nàyi! Mana nàɖu wo dzi godoo.”

english_verse: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Ale David yi Baal Perazim eye wòɖu Filistitɔwo dzi le afi ma. Egblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ dze nye futɔwo le ŋgɔnye abe tsiɖɔɖɔe ŋɔ agbo ene.” Eya ta wona ŋkɔ teƒe ma be Baal Perazim.

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Esi Filistitɔwo sí dzo la, wogblẽ woƒe legbaawo ɖe afi ma eye David kple eƒe amewo yi ɖafɔ wo dzoe.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Ke Filistitɔwo gaho trɔ yi ɖe Refaim-bali la me, eye wokaka ɖe teƒea.

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: David gabia gbe Aƒetɔ, eye wòɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Mègakpe wo o, ke boŋ to wo megbe nàyi ɖatu wo le klẽtiawo gbɔ lɔƒo.

english_verse: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
translation_verse: Ne èse zinyenye to klẽtiawo dome la, ekema wɔ kaba elabe madze ŋgɔwò be masi Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ la.”

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: David zɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aɖaŋu la nu, eye wòɖu Filistitɔwo dzi, nyà wo tso Geba ʋuu va se ɖe Gezer.

english_verse: The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow.
translation_verse: Ne aɖakaa tsɔlawo ɖe afɔ zi ade la, David nana be wotɔna ɖi eye wòtsɔa nyitsu kple nyivi dami saa vɔe.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
translation_verse: David sa aklala ko ɖe ali eye wònɔ ɣe ɖum kple ŋusẽ katã be yeatsɔ de bubu Aƒetɔ ŋu.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: Ale eya kple Israelviwo katã le aseye tsom, le kpẽ kum dzidzɔtɔe hetsɔ aɖaka la va Yerusalem.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Esi wotsɔ aɖaka la ge ɖe Yerusalem-dua me la, Mixal, Saul vinyɔnu nɔ fesre nu kpɔ David wònɔ kpo tim, nɔ ɣe ɖum le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, eye wòɖu fewu le eŋu le dzime.

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
translation_verse: Wokɔe tso Abinadab ƒeme le togbɛ aɖe dzi, eye wodae ɖe keke yeye dzi. Usa kple Axio, Abinadab viwoe nɔ kekea ŋu.

english_verse: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
translation_verse: Eya kple dukɔ blibo la dze mɔ yi Baal-Yuda bene woatsɔ Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la vɛ. Aƒetɔ, Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ŋkɔ le aɖaka la ŋu, eye eƒe fiazikpui le kerubiawo tame.

english_verse: with Ahio walking in front of it.
translation_verse: Axio nɔ eŋgɔ, nɔ ehem eye Abinadab nɔ emegbe.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
translation_verse: David kple Israelviwo katã nɔ ha dzim, nɔ ɣe ɖum eye wonɔ dzidzɔ kpɔm ɖe saŋku kple kasaŋku, axatsɛ, nyawowoe kple gakogoe ƒe ɖiɖi dzi kple ŋusẽ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume.

english_verse: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Esi wova ɖo Naxon ƒe lugbɔƒe la, nyiawo kli nu eye nubablaɖaka la de gege ge, eya ta Usa do asi ɖa lée.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ Mawu la do dziku ɖe Usa ŋu, eye Mawu ƒoe ƒu anyi ɖe aɖaka la xa wòku.

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: Eve David be Aƒetɔ he to na Usa nenema, eya ta wòna ŋkɔ teƒe ma be Perez Usa. Ŋkɔ sia tsi eŋu va se ɖe egbe.

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: Tete David nɔ Aƒetɔ vɔ̃m eye wògblɔ be: “Ale ke mawɔ atsɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe aɖaka ayi gbɔnyee?”

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: David megadi be woatsɔe ava ye gbɔ le Yerusalem o, eya ta ena wokɔe yi ɖada ɖe Obed-Edom gbɔ. Ŋutsu sia tso Gat-du me.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Fia David se be Aƒetɔ yra Obed-Edom ƒe aƒe kple eƒe nuwo katã le aɖaka la ta, eya ta eyi ɖakɔ aɖaka la tso Obed-Edom ƒeme va Yerusalem kple aseyetsotso.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: Wotsɔ aɖaka la va da ɖe agbadɔ si David tu nɛ be wòanye enɔƒe la me. Eyome David sa numemevɔ kple ŋutifafavɔ na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Esi wòsa vɔawo vɔ la, eyra dukɔ la le Aƒetɔ, Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la, ŋkɔ me

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: eye wòma nuɖuɖu na ame sia ame. Ŋutsu ɖe sia ɖe kple nyɔnu ɖe sia ɖe le Israel xɔ abolo ɖeka, lã memee kɔ ɖeka kple waintsetse ƒuƒu bolo ɖeka. Eyome ame sia ame yi eƒeme.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: Emegbe, esi David yi aƒeme be yeado gbe na ye ƒemetɔwo la, Mixal do va kpee gblɔ be: “Egbe Israel-fia ɖe bubu eɖokui ŋu menye fefe o. Ɖeko wònɔ nu klom le eɖokui ŋu le eteviwo ƒe nyɔnudɔlawo ŋkume, abe ale si yakamewo wɔna ŋukpe manɔmee ene.”

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: David ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Ɖe meɖu ɣea be made bubu Aƒetɔ ŋu. Eyae tiam be manye eƒe dukɔ Israel ƒe amegã elabe nye nu nyo eŋu wu tɔ́wò kple eƒe ƒomea katã tɔ. Nyemadzudzɔ dzidzɔkpɔkpɔ le eŋkume akpɔ o,

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: ke boŋ magaɖi gbɔ ɖokuinye ɖe dzi wu esia, eye nyemaɖi naneke le ŋkuwò me o; gake le dɔlanyɔnu siwo ƒe nya nègblɔ gome la, woade bubu ŋunye!”

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Gake nyemaxɔ nye lɔlɔ̃ mavɔ la le esi abe ale si mexɔe le Saul, ame si menyà ɖa le eŋgɔ la si ene o.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ na Natan be: “Kpɔ xɔ si me mele la ɖa. Sederti wotsɔ tui, gake Mawu ƒe nubablaɖaka la ya le avɔgbadɔ me.”

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Natan gblɔ na fia la be: “Wɔ nu si va wò susu me elabe Aƒetɔ li kpli wò.”

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: “Yi nàɖagblɔ na nye dɔla David be, ‘Menye wòe le xɔ tu ge nam manɔ eme o.

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Tso gbe si gbe mekplɔ Israelviwo dzoe le Egipte la, nyemenɔ xɔ aɖeke me va se ɖe egbe kpɔ o; agbadɔ me ko mele hele tsatsam.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Le teƒe siwo katã mekplɔ Israelviwo nɔ tsatsam toe ɖe, ɖe mehe nya ɖe wo kplɔlawo dometɔ aɖe ŋu kpɔ, biae be, nu ka ta mètu sedertixɔ nam o mahã?’

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: “Eya ta gblɔ na nye dɔla David be: ‘Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be, Mekplɔ wò le alẽwo yome tso lãnyiƒe be nàva nye amegã ɖe nye dukɔ Israel dzi.

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Menɔ kpli wò le afi sia afi si nèto eye meɖu wò futɔwo katã dzi le ŋgɔwò. Azɔ la, mana wò ŋkɔ nade du abe ame xɔŋkɔ bubu siwo le xexea me la tɔ ene.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: Mana nɔƒe nye dukɔ Israel eye mana woali ke, aɖe dzi ɖi le afi si wole fifia la, ale be ame aɖeke magate wo ɖe anyi azɔ abe tsã ene o.

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: Tso esime wova anyigba sia dzi eye meɖo kplɔlawo na wo la, ame vlowo ɖe fu na wo zi geɖe, ke maganɔ nenema o. Mana woakpɔ gbɔdzɔe tso woƒe futɔwo katã si me. Gawu la, Aƒetɔ gblɔ be yele xɔ tu ge na wò.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Ne wò ŋkeke de nèku yi tɔgbuiawo gbɔ la, mana wò ŋutɔŋutɔ viwò aɖe ava nɔ wò zi dzi, eye mana eƒe fiaɖuɖu ali ke.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Eyae nye ame si lava tu xɔ nam eye mana eƒe dzidzimeviwo anɔ eƒe zi dzi ɖaa.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Manye tɔ́a, eye eya anye vinye. Ne eda vo la, mazã amegbetɔ ahe to nɛ, eye mahe to nɛ kple amegbetɔviwo ƒe ameƒoti.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu, èɖe nu sia fia wò dɔla gblɔ be, ‘Matu xɔ na wò’ eya ta dzi ɖo wò dɔla ƒo wòle gbe sia dom ɖa na wò.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Tete fia David yi agbadɔ la me le Aƒetɔ ŋkume eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ anyi do gbe ɖa be: “Aƒetɔ Mawu, nye kple nye aƒe la míenye naneke o; míedze kura o, gake nèkplɔm ʋuu va se ɖe fifi.

english_verse: and yet you have promised to do even more. Is this the way you usually treat people?
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu, esia mesɔ gbɔ na wò o, eya ta nègado nu bubu ŋugbe na nye dzidzimeviwo be woava xɔ gbe aɖe gbe, eye nèɖe esia fiam mekpɔ, Aƒetɔ Mawu.

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Nya ka gale David si wòagblɔ na wò, Aƒetɔ Mawu, elabe ènya wò dɔla nyuie.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: Wò ŋutɔ wò didi kple ɖoɖo wònye be nèwɔ nu gã siawo katã be wò dɔla nanyae.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Eya ta, ètri akɔ, Aƒetɔ Mawu elabe naneke mede nuwò o, eye Mawu bubu aɖeke meli kpe ɖe ŋuwò o, le nu siwo katã míese kple miaƒe towo ta.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Dukɔ aɖeke mele anyigba dzi si nètsɔ wɔ wò dukɔe abe Israel ene o. Nu dziŋɔ gã siwo nèwɔ na wo la na wò ŋkɔ de du le xexea me katã. Esime wò dukɔ si nèɖe tso kluvinyenye me le Egipte gbɔna la, ènyà dukɔ bubuwo kple woƒe mawuwo ɖa le wo ŋgɔ.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Èwɔ Israel wònye wò ŋutɔ wò dukɔ tegbee, eye wò Aƒetɔ, nèzu woƒe Mawu.

english_verse: And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants.
translation_verse: “Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu, wɔ ŋugbe si nèdo nam kple nye aƒe la dzi tegbee, eye nàwɔ nya si nègblɔ la hã dzi.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: Ekema wò ŋkɔ ade du tegbee, woagblɔ be, ‘Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla ye nye Israel ƒe Mawu!’ Nà nye dzidzimeviwo nanɔ nye zi dzi tegbee.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: Eya ta azɔ la, Aƒetɔ Mawu, wòe nye Mawu, wò nyawo nye nyateƒe, eye nèdo nu nyui siawo ŋugbe na wò dɔla.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: Eya ta azɔ la, nedze ŋuwò nayra wò dɔla ƒe aƒe be wòanɔ anyi tegbee le ŋkuwò me. Elabe wò Aƒetɔ Mawu ye ƒo nu, eye wò yayra awɔe be wò dɔla ƒe aƒe anɔ yayra me tegbee.”

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Benaya, Yehoyada vi, le Kretitɔwo kple Pletitɔwo nu eye David viŋutsuwo nye nunɔlawo.

english_verse: David fought the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed
translation_verse: David ŋkɔ de du wu tsã esi wòyi ɖawu Siriatɔ akpe wui enyi le Dze Bali me trɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: Eyome la, eɖu Moabtɔwo hã dzi. Ena ame siwo wòlé le aʋa la me la mlɔ anyigba ɖe fli me. Ne exlẽ fli eve la, ewua wo eye wogblẽa fli blibo ɖeka ɖi. Ale Moabtɔwo va zu David teviwo eye wodzɔa nu nɛ.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Eyome, David ɖu Zoba-fia Hadadezer, Rexob vi, hã dzi, esime Hadadezer yina eƒe dziɖuɖu ɖo ge anyi ɖe Frat-tɔsisi la nu.

english_verse: When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
translation_verse: Esi Siriatɔ siwo le Damasko va be yewoaxɔ na fia Hadadezer la, David wu wo dome ame akpe bla eve vɔ eve.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Azɔ David ɖo asrafowo nɔƒe ɖe woƒe nutome me, da eƒe amewo ɖi, eye Siriatɔwo zu eteviwo hedzɔa nu nɛ. Aƒetɔ kpe ɖe David ŋu wòɖu dzi le afi sia afi si wòyi la.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: David xɔ sikakpoxɔnu siwo le Hadadezer ƒe amewo si la tsɔ va Yerusalem.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: Elɔ akɔbli geɖe hã le Beta kple Berotai, siwo nye du nɔ Hadadezer ƒe ŋusẽ te la hã.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: edɔ via Yoram ɖe David gbɔ kple klosalo, sika kple akɔblinuwo be woaɖado gbe nɛ, eye wòakafui le ale si wòwɔ aʋa kple Hadadezer heɖu edzi ta, elabe Toi wɔ aʋa kple Hadadezer zi geɖe.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: Fia David kɔ̀ nu siawo ŋuti, hekpe ɖe klosalo kple sika siwo wòxɔ le dukɔ siwo katã dzi wòɖu si la hã ŋu hena subɔsubɔ.

english_verse: Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, Amalek, and from King Hadadezer of Zobah.
translation_verse: Dukɔawoe nye: Edom, Moab, Amon, Filistia kple Amalek. Nu siwo wòha le Zoba-fia Hadadezer gbɔ la hã kpe ɖe wo ŋuti.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: Zadok, Axitub vi kple Aximelex, Abyatar vi, nye nunɔlawo; Seraya nye agbalẽŋlɔla;

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Yoab, ame si nɔ nye Zeruya la, le dukɔa ƒe agbalẽwo nu;

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la, David bia be: “Ɖe ame aɖeke mesusɔ ɖe Saul ƒeme, ne maxa ɖe Yonatan ta anyo dɔme nɛ oa?”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
translation_verse: Dɔla aɖe le Saul ƒeme si ŋkɔe nye Ziba. Woyɔe va David gbɔ eye fia la biae be: “Wòe nye Zibaa?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Meɖe kuku, nyee.”

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Fia la biae be: “Ɖe ame aɖeke megale Saul ƒeme si manyo dɔme na abe Mawu ene oa?” Ziba ɖo eŋu be: “Yonatan viŋutsuvi ɖeka susɔ li. Enye atatututɔ.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Fia la bia be: “Afi ka wòle?” Ziba ɖo eŋu be: “Ele Amiel vi, Maxir ƒeme le Lo-Debar.”

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Eŋkɔe nye Mefiboset. Enye Yonatan vi, eye wònye Saul ƒe tɔgbuiyɔvi. Esi wòva la, ebɔbɔ tsyɔ mo anyi. Tete David yɔe be: “Mefiboset!” Etɔ be: “Nyee nye esi.”

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: David gblɔ nɛ be: “Mègavɔ̃ o. Maxa ɖe tɔ́wò Yonatan ta anyo dɔme na wò. Magbugbɔ tɔgbuiwò Saul ƒe agblewo katã na wò, eye mana nàɖu nu le nye agba nu ɖaa.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
translation_verse: Mefiboset gade ta agu eye wògblɔ be: “Ame kae nye wò dɔla, be nàlé fɔ ɖe nye avu kuku sia hã ŋu?”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Emegbe fia la yɔ Saul ƒe dɔla Ziba eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Metsɔ nu siwo katã nye Saul kple eƒe ƒome blibo la tɔ la de asi na wò aƒetɔ viŋutsua.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.

translation_verse: Ale David ƒo aʋakɔ blibo la nu ƒu yi Raba, wɔ aʋa kple dua hexɔe.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: Ekplɔ ame siwo le dua me la gbɔe, eye wova nɔa ati dzem, nɔa kpe kpam, nɔa nake fɔm nɔa anyikpe mem. Aleae wòwɔ Amonviwo ƒe duwo katã me nɔlawoe. Emegbe la, David kple aʋakɔ blibo la trɔ va Yerusalem.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: Nɔvinyɔnu ɖetugbi aɖe nɔ David vi Absalom si, si ŋkɔe nye Tamar. Edze tugbe, nyakpɔ ŋutɔ eye eƒe nu lé dzi na David viŋutsu bubu si woyɔna be Amnon la ŋutɔ.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Tamar ƒe nu lé dzi nɛ ale gbegbe be lɔlɔ̃ na nyɔnuvia va zu dɔ dze edzi. Menya ale si wòawɔ eƒe asi nasu edzi ne wòawɔ naneke kplii o.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Ke xɔlɔ̃ aɖe le Amnon si, si nya aye ŋutɔ. Eŋkɔe nye Yonadab eye wònye David nɔviŋutsu Simea vi.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Yonadab bia Amnon be: “Nu ka ta wò fiavi nèle ku ɖim gbe sia gbe ale? Màgblɔe nam oa?” Amnon ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Tamar, Absalom nɔvinyɔnu ƒe nue lé dzi nam.”

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Yonadab gblɔ nɛ be: “Wɔ abe dɔ lém nèle ene eye nàyi ɖamlɔ wò aba dzi. Ne tɔ́wò va be yeakpɔ wò ɖa la, gblɔ nɛ be: ‘Na nɔvinye Tamar nava na nuɖuɖum. Medi be wòava ɖa nua le gbɔnye ne makpɔ, eye eya ŋutɔ natsɔe nam maɖu.’ ”

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Ale Amnon wɔ abe dɔ lém wòle ene eye wòyi ɖamlɔ anyi. Esi fia va be yeakpɔe ɖa la, egblɔ nɛ be: “Na nɔvinye Tamar nava tɔ tatali eve nam le gbɔnye, ne maɖu.”

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: Ale David ɖo ame ɖe Tamar le fiasã la me be woagblɔ nɛ be: “Yi nɔviwò Amnon ƒeme nàɖaɖa nu nɛ!”

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Tamar yi nɔvia Amnon ƒeme eye wòkpɔe wòmlɔ anyi ɖi. Eka amɔwɔ, blui, mlii hetɔ tatalia le egbɔ.

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: Eɖee le amia me tsɔ nɛ, ke egbe be yemaɖui o. Amnon gblɔ nɛ be: “Na ame sia ame nado” eye ameawo katã do.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Azɔ egblɔ na Tamar be: “Tsɔ nuɖuɖua va xɔgãme nàlé ɖe asi maɖu!” Etsɔ nuɖuɖua yi nɛ le afi ma.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Esi wòtsɔ nuɖuɖua nɛ be neɖu la, elée gblɔ nɛ be: “Va mlɔ gbɔnye, nɔvinye!”

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Ke Tamar ɖo eŋu be: “Oo, nɔvinye! Mègazi dzinye o! Womewɔa nu sia tɔgbe le Israel o. Ŋukpenanue, mègawɔe o.

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Ke nye ɖe, afi ka mada mo ɖo anɔ yiyim? Ke wò ya azu movitɔ ŋukpenanuwɔlawo dometɔ ɖeka le Israel. Eya ta azɔ la, taflatsɛ yi nàƒo nu kple fia la, elabe meka ɖe edzi be aɖe asi le ŋunye na wò.”

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Ke melɔ̃ ɖe eƒe nya la dzi o. Ale wòlée, zi edzi hede asi eŋu sesẽtɔe.

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Tete Amnon lé fu Tamar vevie ŋutɔ enumake. Elé fui wu ale si wòlɔ̃e tsã gɔ̃. Egblɔ nɛ be: “Tsi tre nàdzo!”

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Tamar ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Ao, nɔvinye. Ne ènyam alea be madzo la, eya boŋ vɔ̃ɖi wu nu si nèwɔ ɖe ŋunye fifi laa.” Ke Amnon mesee nɛ o.

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: Eyɔ ɖekakpui si subɔnɛ la ɖa gblɔ nɛ be: “He nyɔnu sia do goe le gbɔnye. Nyae do ɖa nàdo ʋɔa!”

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Subɔla la hee do goe eye wòdo ʋɔa. Tamar do awu ʋlaya abɔ legbe abe ale si fiavinyɔnu ɖetugbiwo donɛ tso blema ke ene.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Eku afi kɔ ɖe tame, dze awu ʋlaya la eye wòkpla asi ta le boboe dom le yiyim.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Esi nɔvia Absalom kpɔe la, egblɔ nɛ be: “Ɖe nɔviwò Amnon wɔ nane kpli wòa? Nɔvinye, zi ɖoɖoe; nɔviwòe wònye. Mègana nya sia naɖe fu na wò o.” Ale Tamar tsi nɔvia Absalom ƒeme eye meganɔa ame dome o.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Absalom lé fu Amnon vevie eye megaƒoa nu nɛ gɔ̃ hã o, elabe elé nɔvia Tamar sesẽe de asi eŋu. Absalom bia hlɔ̃

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Le ƒe eve megbe la, Absalom yi Baal Xazor si te ɖe Efrayim-du ŋu be yeako fu na yeƒe alẽwo, eye wòkpe fia viŋutsuwo katã va afi ma.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Eyi fia David gbɔ ɖagblɔ nɛ be: “Fia Bubutɔ, mele fu kom na nye alẽwo. Meɖe kuku, mele wò kple wò dɔlawo kpem be miava afi ma.”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Fia la ɖo eŋu na Absalom be: “Gbeɖe, vinye! Ne mí katã míeyi la, ava nye agba na wò akpa.” Absalom ƒoe ɖe fia nu, gake egbe yiyi; dzɔgbe nyui ko wòdi nɛ.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Ke Absalom gblɔ nɛ be: “Ne mèdi be woayi o la, màna nɔvinye Amnon ya nayi kpli mí oa?” Fia la biae be: “Nu ka ta nèdi be eya nayi kpli wò?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Ke Absalom nɔ eƒom ɖe enu ʋuu va se ɖe esime fia ɖe asi le Amnon kple via ŋutsu bubuawo katã ŋu be woayi. Absalom ɖo nuɖukplɔ̃ si tɔgbe woɖona na fiawo ko la,

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo be: “Minɔ ŋku lém ɖe Amnon ŋu. Ne wain sui wòle dzidzɔ kpɔm la, mele gbe ɖe ge na mi be miwui. Miwui, migavɔ̃ o. Nyee be miwui. Dzi nenɔ mia ƒo; miwɔ ŋutsu.”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Ale dɔlaawo wɔ Absalom ƒe gbe dzi pɛpɛpɛ eye wowu Amnon. Tete fia viŋutsuawo katã de woƒe tedziwo dzi sí dzo.
