translation_verse: Èna nye futɔwo sí le nunye, eye metsrɔ̃ ame siwo lé fum la keŋ.

english_verse: They cried out for help, but no one saved them; they called out to you, but there was no answer.
translation_verse: Wodi xɔnametɔ; ke ɖeke meli axɔ na wo o. Wodo ɣli yɔ Aƒetɔ, ke metɔ na wo o.

english_verse: I ground them to dust, and I squashed them like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: Metu wo, wozu abe ʋuʋudedi ene. Metu afɔ wo dzi, henyama wo abe ba le ablɔwo dzi ene.

english_verse: You rescued me from my stubborn people and made me the leader of foreign nations, who are now my slaves.
translation_verse: Èɖem tso nye dukɔ si le dzrewɔwɔ dzi la si me. Elém ɖe asi hetsɔm ɖo tatɔe na dukɔwo, eye dukɔ si nyemenya o la subɔm.

english_verse: They have lost all courage and from their fortresses they come trembling.
translation_verse: Vɔvɔ̃ ɖo amedzro siawo, eye wole dzodzom nyànyanya do tso woƒe mɔwo me va.

english_verse: You are the living Lord! I will praise you! You are a mighty rock. I will honor you for keeping me safe.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ le agbe! Woakafu nye xɔnametɔ la! Woado nye Mawu la ɖe dzi! Eyae xɔna nam abe agakpe ene.

english_verse: You took revenge for me, and you put nations in my power.
translation_verse: Mawu bia hlɔ̃ nam, eye wòtsɔ dukɔwo de tenye.

english_verse: You protected me from violent enemies, and you made me much greater than all of them.
translation_verse: Ekplɔm to nye futɔwo dome do, eye wòna meɖu wo dzi. Eɖem tso ŋutasẽlawo si me.

english_verse: You give glorious victories to your chosen king. Your faithful love for David and for his descendants will never end.
translation_verse: Mawu na eƒe fia la kpɔ dziɖuɖu. Eɖe eƒe lɔlɔ̃ mavɔ la fia eƒe amesiamina David kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo tegbee.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord has told me what to say.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe Gbɔgbɔ ƒo nu to dzinye, eye eƒe gbedeasia le nunye.

english_verse: Our Mighty Rock, the God of Jacob, told me, “A ruler who obeys God and does right
translation_verse: Israel ƒe Mawu la ƒo nu; Israel ƒe xɔnametɔ la gblɔ nam be: “Dziɖula, nu dzɔdzɔe wɔla si vɔ̃a Mawu la,

english_verse: I have ruled this way, and God will never break his promise to me. God's promise is complete and unchanging; he will always help me and give me what I hope for.
translation_verse: Alea Mawu ayra nye dzidzimeviwoe, elabe ebla nu mavɔ kplim. Enye ɖoɖo si wòwɔ ɖo kpe edzi, eye matrɔ o. Nu si ko dim mele lae nye maɖu dzi.

english_verse: But evil people are pulled up like thornbushes. They are not dug up by hand,
translation_verse: Ke yakamewo katã le abe ŋu si wotsɔna ƒua gbe ene. Ame aɖeke maka asi wo ŋu o.

english_verse: except Eleazar. He killed Philistines until his hand was cramped, and he couldn't let go of his sword. When Eleazar finished, all the Israelite troops had to do was come back and take the enemies' weapons and armor. The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
translation_verse: Enɔ te wɔ avu kple Filistitɔwo eye wowu wo ʋuu va se ɖe esime eƒe asi ku le yi la ŋu eye wòtsi asi me nɛ. Aƒetɔ na woɖu dzi gã ŋutɔ gbe ma gbe. Emegbe Israelviwo gbugbɔ yi Eleazar gbɔ be yewoaɖaha ame tsiaʋaawo ƒe nuwo le wo ŋu.

english_verse: and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was the commander of the Thirty Warriors, but he still did not become one of the Three Warriors.
translation_verse: Eyae xɔ ŋkɔ wu le “Kalẽtɔ Blaetɔ̃awo” dome, eye wònye woƒe tatɔ, gake mexɔ ŋkɔ de “Kalẽtɔ Etɔ̃awo” nu o.

english_verse: These are the names of David's warriors: Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed
translation_verse: David ƒe aʋawɔla vevitɔwo ƒe ŋkɔwoe nye: Gbãtɔe nye Isbaal, Xaxmoni vi. Eya nye kalẽtɔ etɔ̃awo ƒe tatɔ. Etsɔ akplɔ wɔ aʋa kple ame alafa enyi eye wòwu wo katã le aʋawɔwɔ zi ɖeka me.

english_verse: The next one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. One time when the Philistines were at war with Israel, he and David dared the Philistines to fight them. Every one of the Israelite soldiers turned and ran,
translation_verse: Eleazar, Dodo vi tso Axoxi ƒomea me nye ame evelia le kalẽtɔ etɔ̃awo dome. Gbe ɖeka la, Filistitɔwo ƒo ƒu, ho va aʋa wɔ ge kple Israelviwo. David kple Eleazar tso ɖe wo ŋu, ke Israelviwo sí le ameawo nu eye Eleazar ɖeka ko tsi David gbɔ.

english_verse: but Shammah stood in the middle of the field and killed the Philistines. The crops were saved, and the Lord gave Israel a great victory.
translation_verse: ke Sama ya nɔ te ɖe wo nu, tsi tsitre ɖe ayigblea titina, ʋli agblea ta eye wòwu Filistitɔawo. Aƒetɔ na woɖu dzi gã aɖe.

english_verse: One year at harvest time, the Three Warriors went to meet David at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
translation_verse: Le nuŋeŋɔli ƒe gɔmedzeɣi lɔƒo la, ame etɔ̃ tso “Kalẽtɔ Blaetɔ̃awo” dome yi ɖe David gbɔ le Adulam Agado la me. Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, Filistitɔwo ƒe adzohawo ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Refaim-bali la me.

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress,
translation_verse: David nɔ mɔ́ sesẽ me le to dzi, eye Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ le Betlehem-dua me ɣe ma ɣi.

english_verse: and he was very thirsty. He said, “I wish I had a drink from the well by the gate at Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Aƒenuwo dzro David eye wògblɔ be: “Manɔ anyi ko ame aɖe naku tsi tso vudo me le agbo nu le Betlehem vɛ nam mano!”

english_verse: The Three Warriors sneaked into the Philistine camp and got some water from the well near Bethlehem's gate. But after they brought the water back to David, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as a sacrifice
translation_verse: Tete kalẽtɔ etɔ̃awo yi ɖage ɖe Filistitɔwo ƒe asaɖa me, eye woku tsia le vudoa me tsɔ vɛ na David. Ke egbe be yemanoe o, eye wòkɔe ɖe anyi na Aƒetɔ,

english_verse: and said to the Lord, “I can't drink this water! It's like the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
translation_verse: hegblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, ne mano tsi sia fĩi! Ɖe mano ame etɔ̃ siwo tsɔ woƒe agbe ke, yi ɖaku tsia vɛ la ƒe ʋua?” Ale wògbe enono. Kalẽtɔ etɔ̃awoe wɔ esia.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
translation_verse: Benaya, Yehoyada vi tso Kabzeel nye asrafo kalẽtɔ bubu si wɔ kalẽnu geɖe. Ewu kalẽtɔ eve tso Moab. Eyi ɖawu dzata le do me le gbe si gbe tsikpe dza.

english_verse: Another time, he killed an Egyptian, as big as a giant. The Egyptian was armed with a spear, but Benaiah only had a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
translation_verse: Eya kee wu Egipte-ŋutsu kako aɖe si si akplɔ le la hã. Eyi Egiptetɔ la gbɔ kple atizɔti, xɔ akplɔ la le esi tsɔ wui.

english_verse: Benaiah did these things. He never became one of the Three Warriors, but he was just as famous as they were and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. David made him the leader of his bodyguard.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be exɔ ŋkɔ le “Kalẽtɔ Blaetɔ̃awo” dome hã, eƒe kalẽwɔwɔ mede “Kalẽtɔ Etɔ̃awo” tɔ nu o. David tsɔe ɖo eƒe asrafo siwo dzɔa eŋu la nu.

english_verse: and said, “Your Majesty! Why have you come to see me?” David answered, “I've come to buy your threshing place. I have to build the Lord an altar here, so this disease will stop killing the people.”
translation_verse: hegblɔ be: “Nu ka ta nye aƒetɔ fia va eƒe dɔla gbɔ?” David ɖo eŋu be: “Ɖe meva be maƒle lugbɔƒe la ne maɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afii na Aƒetɔ, ale be dɔ vɔ̃ la nu natso.”

english_verse: They went to Gilead and to Kadesh in Syria. Then they went to Dan, Ijon, and on toward Sidon.
translation_verse: Woto Gilead va Kades le Xititɔwo ƒe nutome, eye wova Dan hetrɔ ɖo ta Sidon.

english_verse: So David told Joab and the army officers, “Go to every tribe in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north all the way south to Beersheba, and count everyone who can serve in the army. I want to know how many there are.”
translation_verse: Ale David gblɔ na aʋakɔ la ƒe tatɔ Yoab be: “Yi nàɖatsa le Israel-toawo katã me tso Dan va se ɖe Beer-Seba, eye nàxlẽ dukɔa me tɔwo. Medi be manya woƒe xexlẽme.”

english_verse: But when David refused to change his mind, Joab and the army officers went out and started counting the people.
translation_verse: Ke fia la zi Yoab kple eƒe aʋakplɔlawo dzi be woawɔ yeƒe nya la dzi. Ale wodzo yi be yewoaɖaxlẽ Israel-dukɔa me tɔwo.

english_verse: They crossed the Jordan River and began with Aroer and the town in the middle of the river valley. From there they went toward Gad and on as far as Jazer.
translation_verse: Wotso Yordan-tɔsisi la dze egɔme tso Aroer kple du si le balia titina ɖo ta Gad le Yazer gbɔ.

english_verse: After they had gone through the whole land, they went back to Jerusalem. It had taken them
translation_verse: Wotsa le dukɔ bliboa me ɣleti asieke kple ŋkeke bla eve, eye wogbugbɔ va Yerusalem.

english_verse: Araunah looked and saw David and his soldiers coming up toward him. He went over to David, bowed down low,
translation_verse: Esi Arawna fɔ kɔ dzi la, ekpɔ fia la kple eƒe dɔlawo gbɔna ɖe egbɔ. Arawna zɔ ɖe wo dzi eye wòbɔbɔ de ta agu na David,

english_verse: David saw the angel killing everyone and told the Lord, “These people are like sheep with me as their shepherd. I have sinned terribly, but they have done nothing wrong. Please, punish me and my family instead of them!” David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place (
translation_verse: Esi David kpɔ mawudɔla si le ame wum la, egblɔ na Aƒetɔ be: “Nyee wɔ nuvɔ̃. Nyee da vo. Nu ka ame gblɔe siawo, siwo le abe alẽ ene la wɔ? Meɖe kuku, he to na nye kple tɔ́nye ƒe aƒe ko.”

english_verse: After everyone had been counted, David realized he had done wrong. He told the Lord, “What I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Lord, please forgive me.”
translation_verse: Esi David xlẽ dukɔmetɔawo vɔ la, eƒe dzitsinya de asi fuɖeɖe me nɛ, eye wògblɔ na Aƒetɔ be: “Mewɔ nuvɔ̃ gã aɖe be mewɔ nu sia, eya ta meɖe kuku, tsɔe kem. Mewɔ lãnu ŋutɔ.”

english_verse: Before David even got up the next morning, the Lord had told David's prophet Gad
translation_verse: Esi David fɔ le ŋdi me la, Aƒetɔ ƒo nu kple gbeƒãɖela Gad, David ƒe nukpɔla be:

english_verse: to take a message to David. Gad went to David and told him: You must choose one of three ways for the Lord to punish you: Will there be seven years when the land won't grow enough food for your people? Or will your enemies chase you and make you run from them for three months? Or will there be three days of horrible disease in your land? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God, who sent me.
translation_verse: Gad yi egbɔ eye wògblɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nya la nɛ hebiae be: “Ka nàtsɔ? Dɔwuame neva wò anyigba dzi ƒe etɔ̃ loo, alo ànɔ sísim le wò futɔwo nu, woaɖe wò ɖe nu ɣleti etɔ̃ loo, alo dɔ vɔ̃ neva wò anyigba dzi ŋkeke etɔ̃a? Azɔ bu eŋu ne nàgblɔ nya aɖe nam mayi ɖagblɔ na ame si dɔm ɖa!”

english_verse: David was really frightened and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
translation_verse: David ɖo eŋu be: “Mexaxa ŋutɔ. Nyemedi be amegbetɔ nahe to nam o. Medi be Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ nahe to na mí elabe amenuvela wònye.”

english_verse: So that morning, the Lord sent an angel to spread a horrible disease everywhere in Israel, from Dan to Beersheba. And before it was over,
translation_verse: Esi Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla yi be yeagblẽ nu le Yerusalem la, Aƒetɔ gbugbɔ le tohehe si wòdi be yeana wo la yome, eye wògblɔ na mawudɔla si le wo wum la be: “Esɔ gbɔ! Mègagblẽ nu yi edzi o.” Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla la le Yebusitɔ Arawna ƒe lugbɔƒe gbɔ.

english_verse: Araunah said, “Take whatever you want and offer your sacrifice. Here are some oxen for the sacrifice. You can use the threshing-boards and the wooden yokes for the fire.
translation_verse: Arawna gblɔ na David be: “Na nye aƒetɔ fia naxɔe tsɔ sa vɔ lae faa ale si dze ŋuwò. Lé nyitsu siawo nàsa numemevɔe. Woƒe kɔkutiwo kple luƒoʋuƒowo nye esiawo; tsɔ wo nàdo dzo lae.”

english_verse: Take them—they're yours! I hope the Lord your God will be pleased with you.”
translation_verse: Arawna tsɔ nuawo katã na fia la eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la, nèxɔ wò nunana la.”

english_verse: But David answered, “No! I have to pay you what they're worth. I can't offer the Lord my God a sacrifice that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing place and the oxen for
translation_verse: Ke fia la ɖo eŋu na Arawna be: “Gbeɖe, ɖe mele wo ƒle ge axe fea. Nyemasa numemevɔ na Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu la femaxee o.” Ale David ƒle lugbɔƒe la kple nyitsuawo klosaloga bla atɔ̃.

english_verse: Then he built an altar for the Lord. He offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. The Lord answered the prayers of the people, and no one else died from the terrible disease.
translation_verse: Tete wòɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afi ma na Aƒetɔ, eye wosa numemevɔ kple ŋutifafavɔ. Aƒetɔ se eƒe gbedodoɖa ɖe dukɔa ta, eye dɔ vɔ̃ la nu tso le Israel.

english_verse: King David was now an old man, and he always felt cold, even under a lot of blankets.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, fia David va tsi eye wòxɔ ƒè geɖee; eye togbɔ be wotsyɔa avɔwo nɛ fũu hã la, dzo meɖoa lã me nɛ o.

english_verse: His officials said, “Your Majesty, we will look for a young woman to take care of you. She can lie down beside you and keep you warm.”
translation_verse: Eya ta eƒe subɔlawo gblɔ nɛ be: “Na woadi ɖetugbi dzaa aɖe na nye aƒetɔ fia wòava nɔ gbɔwò anɔ dzrawòm ɖo, anɔ wò akɔme mlɔm ne aƒetɔnye fia la ƒe lã me nate ŋu axɔ dzo.”

english_verse: They looked everywhere in Israel until they found a very beautiful young woman named Abishag, who lived in the town of Shunem. They brought her to David, and she took care of him. But David did not have sex with her. Adonijah Tries To Become King
translation_verse: Ɖetugbi la dze tugbe ŋutɔ. Ezu fiaa dzikpɔla koŋ henɔa esubɔm ɣe sia ɣi. Ke fia la medɔ kplii o. Adoniya di be yeaxɔ fiaa aɖu

english_verse: Adonijah was the son of David and Haggith. He was Absalom's younger brother and was very handsome. One day, Adonijah started bragging, “I'm going to make myself king!” So he got some chariots and horses, and he hired
translation_verse: Tso esime wodzii kpa tɔ́a meka mo nɛ kpɔ o be: “Nu ka ta nèwɔ esi kple ekemɛ?” Edze ɖeka hã ŋutɔ, eye eyae dzɔ ɖe Absalom yome tẽe.

english_verse: Adonijah met with Joab the son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest and asked them if they would help him become king. Both of them agreed to help.
translation_verse: Eƒo nu kple Yoab, Zeruya vi, kple nunɔla Abyatar. Wodze Adoniya yome eye wokpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's bodyguards all refused.
translation_verse: Ke nunɔla Zadok, Benaya si nye Yehoyada vi, gbeƒãɖela Natan, Simei, Rei kple eƒe kalẽtɔwo menɔ Adoniya dzi o.

english_verse: Adonijah invited his brothers and David's officials from Judah to go with him to Crawling Rock near Rogel Spring, where he sacrificed some sheep, cattle, and fat calves.
translation_verse: Adoniya wu alẽwo, nyitsuwo kple nyivi damiwo le Soxelet-kpe gbɔ le Rogel-vudo xa tsɔ sa vɔe eye wòkpe nɔvia ŋutsuwo, fiaviŋutsuwo katã kple fiaŋume siwo katã le Yuda,

english_verse: But he did not invite Nathan, Benaiah, David's bodyguards, or his own brother Solomon.
translation_verse: gake mekpe gbeƒãɖela Natan loo, Benaya loo, alo kalẽtɔwo loo, alo Salomo, nɔvia ŋutsu la o. Woɖo Salomo fia

english_verse: When Nathan heard what had happened, he asked Bathsheba, Solomon's mother: Have you heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has made himself king? But David doesn't know a thing about it.
translation_verse: Tete Natan gblɔ na Salomo nɔ Batseba be: “Èse be Adoniya, Xagit vi, zu fia eye mía aƒetɔ David menyae oa?

english_verse: You and your son Solomon will be killed, unless you do what I tell you.
translation_verse: Eya ta azɔ la, va ne maɖo aɖaŋu na wò ne nàxɔ wò ŋutɔ ɖokuiwò kple viwò Salomo ɖe agbe.

english_verse: While you are still talking to David, I'll come in and tell him that everything you said is true.
translation_verse: Màɖe nu le nyaa me o ko mava do, eye nye hã maƒoe ɖe tɔwò dzi.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was in his bedroom where Abishag was taking care of him because he was so old. Bathsheba went in
translation_verse: Ale Batseba yi fia la gbɔ le xɔgãme elabe fiaa tsi ŋutɔ hetsi xɔ me, eye Abisag Sunamitɔ lae va le esubɔm.

english_verse: and bowed down. “What can I do for you?” David asked.
translation_verse: Batseba bɔbɔ, de ta agu ɖe fia la ŋkume eye fiaa biae be: “Nu ka dim nèle?”

english_verse: Bathsheba answered: Your Majesty, you promised me in the name of the Lord your God that my son Solomon would be the next king.
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu be: “Nye Aƒetɔ, èta Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu nam kpɔ be: ‘Viwò Salomo aɖu fia ɖe yonyeme; eye eyae anɔ nye fiazikpui dzi.’

english_verse: But Adonijah has already been made king, and you didn't know anything about it.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ kpɔ ɖa, Adoniya zu fia eye wò, nye aƒetɔ fia mènyae o!

english_verse: He sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. And he invited Abiathar the priest, Joab your army commander, and all your sons to be there, except Solomon, your loyal servant.
translation_verse: Ewu nyitsuwo, nyi damiwo kple alẽwo kpaŋkpaŋkpaŋ, eye wòkpe fiaviŋutsuwo katã kple nunɔla Abyatar kpakple aʋakplɔla Yoab, gake wò dɔla Salomo ya la, mekpee o.

english_verse: Your Majesty, everyone in Israel is waiting for you to announce who will be the next king.
translation_verse: Fifia la, nye aƒetɔ fia, Israel blibo la ƒe ŋku le ŋuwò be nàgblɔ ame si le fiazikpuia dzi va ge ɖe yowòme la na yewo.

english_verse: If you don't, they will say that Solomon and I have rebelled. They will treat us like criminals and kill us as soon as you die.
translation_verse: Ne menye nenema o la, ava eme be ne èyi tɔgbuiawo gbɔ la amewo abu nye kple vinye Salomo vɔ̃wɔlawoe.”

english_verse: Just then, Nathan the prophet arrived.
translation_verse: Mekpɔ ɖe nu le nyaa me hafi gbeƒãɖela Natan va do o.

english_verse: Someone told David that he was there, and Nathan came in. He bowed with his face to the ground
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na fia la be: “Gbeƒãɖela Natan nye esi.” Esi gbeƒãɖelaa va ɖo fiaa ŋkume la, ede ta agu nɛ.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, did you say that Adonijah would be king?
translation_verse: Natan gblɔ be: “Nye aƒetɔ fia, ɖe nègblɔ be: ‘Adoniya nazu fia ɖe yonyeme eye eya abɔbɔ nɔ nye fiazikpui dzi’ a?

english_verse: Earlier today, he sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. He invited the army commanders, Abiathar, and all your sons to be there. They are already eating and drinking and shouting, “Long live King Adonijah!”
translation_verse: Elabe egbe la, etso yi ɖawu nyitsuwo, nyivi damiwo kple alẽwo fũu tsɔ sa vɔ, eye wòkpe fiaviŋutsuwo katã, aʋakɔ la ƒe tatɔwo kple nunɔla Abyatar eye kpɔ ɖa, wole nu ɖum le no num, le eŋkume le gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Fia Adoniya nenɔ agbe tegbee!’

english_verse: But he didn't invite me or Zadok the priest or Benaiah or Solomon.
translation_verse: Ke nye wò dɔla kple nunɔla Zadok, Benaya, Yehoyada vi kple wò dɔla Salomo ya, mekpe mí o.

english_verse: Did you say they could do this without telling the rest of us who would be the next king? Solomon Becomes King
translation_verse: Nye aƒetɔ fia, wò ŋutɔe ɖe gbe be woawɔ nu siawo le esime mèyɔ ame si anɔ zikpuia dzi ɖe yowòme la na wò dɔlawo oa?”

english_verse: David said, “Tell Bathsheba to come here.” She came and stood in front of him.
translation_verse: Fia David xɔ edzi be: “Miyɔ Batseba nam.” Batseba ge ɖe eme, eye wòtsi tsitre ɖe fia la ŋkume.

english_verse: Then he said, “The living Lord God of Israel has kept me safe. And so today, I will keep the promise I made to you in his name: Solomon will be the next king!”
translation_verse: egbe la, mawɔ ŋugbe si medo na wò le Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu ŋkɔ me, be viwò Salomo ye aɖu fia ɖe yonyeme, eye wòanɔ nye fiazikpui dzi ɖe tenyeƒe la dzi na wò.”

english_verse: Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and said, “Your Majesty, I pray that you will live a long time!”
translation_verse: Batseba dze klo ɖe fia la ŋkume, de ta agu eye wògblɔ be: “Nye aƒetɔ fia David nenɔ agbe tegbee!”

english_verse: Then David said, “Tell Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to come here.” When they arrived,
translation_verse: Tete fia David gblɔ be: “Miɖayɔ nunɔla Zadok, gbeƒãɖela Natan kple Benaya, Yehoyada vi vɛ nam.” Ale wova fia la ŋkume.

english_verse: he told them: Take along some of my officials and let Solomon ride my own mule to Gihon Spring.
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ na wo be: “Miyɔ subɔla siwo le nye fiasã me la kpe ɖe mia ɖokui ŋu, miana Salomo nado nye tedzisɔ, eye miakplɔe yi Gixon,

english_verse: When you get there, Zadok and Nathan will pour olive oil over Solomon's head to show that he is the new king of Israel. Then order someone to blow a trumpet and tell everyone to shout, “Long live King Solomon!”
translation_verse: ne nunɔla Zadok kple gbeƒãɖela Natan nasi ami nɛ le afi ma atsɔe ɖo fiae ɖe Israel nu; eyome miaku kpẽ, agblɔ be: ‘Fia Salomo nenɔ agbe tegbee!’

english_verse: Bring him back here, and he will take my place as king. He is the one I have chosen to rule Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Mikplɔe da ɖe ŋgɔ anɔ eyome ʋuu wòava nɔ nye fiazikpui dzi elabe eyae aɖu fia ɖe tenyeƒe; eya dzie metɔ asii be wòazu Israel kple Yuda siaa dziɖula.”

english_verse: Benaiah answered, “We will do it, Your Majesty. I pray that the Lord your God will let it happen.
translation_verse: Tete Benaya, Yehoyada vi xɔ edzi be: “Neva eme! Aƒetɔ, nye aƒetɔ fia ƒe Mawu negblɔ nenema.

english_verse: The Lord has always watched over you, and I pray that he will now watch over Solomon. May the Lord help Solomon to be an even greater king than you.”
translation_verse: Ale si Aƒetɔ nɔ kple nye aƒetɔ fia la, nenɔ kple Salomo hã nenema, eye wòana eƒe fiazikpui nakpɔ ŋusẽ, wu nye aƒetɔ fia David tɔ.”

english_verse: Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah left and took along the two groups of David's special bodyguards. Solomon rode on David's mule as they led him to Gihon Spring.
translation_verse: Ale nunɔla Zadok, gbeƒãɖela Natan, Yehoyada vi, Benaya kple Kretitɔwo kpakple Pletitɔwo yi eye Salomo de fia David ƒe tedzisɔ dzi, eye wokplɔe yi Gixon.

english_verse: Zadok the priest brought some olive oil from the sacred tent and poured it on Solomon's head to show that he was now king. A trumpet was blown and everyone shouted, “Long live King Solomon!”
translation_verse: Nunɔla Zadok tsɔ lãdzo si me ami le tso Mawu ƒe agbadɔ la me va si na Salomo. Tete woku kpẽ la, eye ameha la katã gblɔ be: “Fia Salomo nenɔ agbe tegbee!”

english_verse: Then they played flutes and celebrated as they followed Solomon back to Jerusalem. They made so much noise that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Tete ameha la katã kplɔe ɖo le dze kum hele dzidzɔseye tsom kple ɣli ale gbegbe be woƒe ɣli na anyigba ʋuʋu.

english_verse: Adonijah and his guests had almost finished eating when they heard the noise. Joab also heard the trumpet and asked, “What's all that noise about in the city?”
translation_verse: Adoniya kple eƒe ame kpekpeawo ɖu nua vɔ teti ko, se ɣli la. Esi Yoab se kpẽ la ƒe ɖiɖi la, ebia be: “Ɣli kae nye gbogbo ma le ɖiɖim le dua me ɖa?”

english_verse: Just then, Jonathan son of Abiathar came running up. “Come in,” Adonijah said. “An important man like you must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Mekpɔ ɖe nu le nyaa me hafi Yonatan, nunɔla Abyatar vi, va do o. Adoniya gblɔ be: “Ge ɖe eme elabe ame akuakua nènye; he nya nyui aɖe vɛ.”

english_verse: Jonathan answered: No, I don't! David has just announced that Solomon will be king.
translation_verse: Yonatan ɖo eŋu na Adoniya be: “Kura o lo! Míaƒe aƒetɔ fia David tsɔ Salomo ɖo fiae!

english_verse: Solomon rode David's own mule to Gihon Spring, and Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and David's special bodyguards went with him. When they got there, Zadok and Nathan made Solomon king. Then everyone celebrated all the way back to Jerusalem. That's the noise you hear in the city.
translation_verse: eye nunɔla Zadok kple gbeƒãɖela Natan si ami nɛ heɖoe fia le Gixon. Eya ƒe dzidzɔ kpɔm wole tso afi ma gbɔ va. Nu mae na dua me tɔ zi; eyae nye ɣli gã ma si miese.

english_verse: Solomon is now king.
translation_verse: Ale Salomo bɔbɔ nɔ fiazikpui la dzi sea!

english_verse: And listen to this! David's officials told him, “We pray that your God will help Solomon to be an even greater king!” David was in his bed at the time, but he bowed
translation_verse: Gawu la, fia ƒe dɔlawo kura gɔ̃ hã de mía aƒetɔ fia David gbɔ ɖado vivi ɖe eŋu be: ‘Wò Mawu na Salomo ŋkɔ de du wu tɔwò, eye eƒe fiazikpui lolo wu wò fiazikpui.’ ” Tete fia la lɔ̃ ta le eƒe aba dzi.

english_verse: and prayed, “I praise you, Lord God of Israel. You have made my son Solomon king and have let me live to see it.”
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ hã be: “Woakafu Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu be wòɖe mɔ vinyewo dometɔ ɖeka bɔbɔ nɔ nye fiazikpui dzi egbe sia, eye nye ŋutɔ nye ŋkuwo le ekpɔm.”

english_verse: Adonijah's guests shook with fear when they heard this news, and they left as fast as they could.
translation_verse: Tete ame siwo katã Adoniya kpe va eƒe kplɔ̃a ŋu la dzo nyanyanya. Ɖe sia ɖe tso eye wòdi eƒe mɔ to.

english_verse: Someone told Solomon, “Adonijah is afraid of you and is holding onto the corners of the altar. He wants you to promise that you won't kill him.”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na Salomo be: “Kpɔ ɖa, Adoniya le Salomo vɔ̃m, elabe kpɔ ɖa, eyi ɖalé vɔsamlekpuia ƒe dzowo hele gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Mina fia Salomo nàta nu nam gbã be yemana woawu eƒe dɔla kple yi o.’ ”

english_verse: Solomon answered, “If Adonijah doesn't cause any trouble, I won't hurt him. But if he does, I'll have him killed.”
translation_verse: Salomo xɔ edzi be: “Ne efia eɖokui nyateƒetɔ kple ame ɖoŋuɖeŋua la, eƒe taɖa ɖeka pɛ gɔ̃ hã mage ɖe anyigba o. Gake ne vɔɖivɔ̃ɖinyenye gadze le eƒe azɔli me la, ku ke wòaku.”

english_verse: Then he sent someone to the altar to get Adonijah. After Adonijah came and bowed down, Solomon said, “Adonijah, go home.”
translation_verse: Ale fia Salomo dɔ ame ɖa woyi ɖakplɔe tso vɔsamlekpuia gbɔ vɛ. Eva eye wòde ta agu le Salomo ŋkume. Salomo gblɔ nɛ be: “Heyi aƒewò me.”

english_verse: Not long before David died, he told Solomon:
translation_verse: Esi David ƒe kuɣi ɖo vɔ la, exlɔ̃ nu via Salomo be:

english_verse: My son, I will soon die, as everyone must. But I want you to be strong and brave.
translation_verse: “Mele demagbɔnugbe si le amewo katã lalam la yim. Kpɔ ɖa, sẽ ŋu, eye nàwɔ ŋutsu.

english_verse: Do what the Lord your God commands and follow his teachings. Obey everything written in the Law of Moses. Then you will be a success, no matter what you do or where you go.
translation_verse: Wɔ nu siwo Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu bia tso asiwò la. Zɔ eƒe mɔwo dzi; lé eƒe ɖoɖowo, kɔnuwo kple ɖaseɖiɖiwo me ɖe asi abe ale si woŋlɔ wo ɖe Mose ƒe Se la me tututu la ene be nu sia nu si nàwɔ le afi sia afi si nàyi la nadze edzi na wò.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always faithfully obey the Lord. If you do, he will keep the solemn promise he made to me that someone from our family will always be king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ekema Aƒetɔ awɔ ŋugbe si wòdo nam la dzi be: ‘Ne wò dzidzimeviwo ɖɔ ŋu ɖo, wɔ nye sededewo dzi pɛpɛpɛ kple woƒe dzi kpakple woƒe luʋɔ blibo la, ɣeyiɣi aɖeke mava si wò dzidzimevi manɔ Israel ƒe fiazikpui dzi o.’

english_verse: Solomon, don't forget what Joab did to me by killing Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of Israel's army. He killed them as if they were his enemies in a war, but he did it when there was no war. He is guilty, and now it's up to you to punish him
translation_verse: “Nya ɖeka gali: èɖo ŋku nu si Yoab, Zeruya vi wɔm to Israel ƒe aʋakplɔla eve, Abner, Ner vi kple Amasa, Yeter vi, wuwu me dzie! Èɖo ŋku ale si wòwu wo le ŋutifafaɣi be hlɔ̃ yebia wo, le ale si woawo wu amewo le aʋagbedzi ta la, dzie? Ewu ame maɖifɔ mawo; ena ʋu maɖifɔ ƒo alidziblanu si le nye ali kple afɔkpa si le nye afɔ.

english_verse: in the way you think best. Whatever you do, don't let him die peacefully in his old age.
translation_verse: Ale sia ale si wò ŋutɔ èkpɔ be yeatrɔ asi le nya ma ŋu ko la, wɔe. Gake ale ke kee hã, mègana eƒe ta ɣi nayi tsiẽƒe le ŋutifafa me o.

english_verse: Be sure to do something about Shimei son of Gera from Bahurim in the territory of Benjamin. He cursed and insulted me the day I went to Mahanaim. But later, when he came to meet me at the Jordan River, I promised that I wouldn't kill him.
translation_verse: Ame ɖeka hã gali: eyae nye Simei, Gera vi, tso Baxurim le Benyamin-nyigba me. Gbe si gbe meyina ɖe Maxanaim la, eva dzum, do vlom vevie. Gake esi metrɔ gbɔna la, eva kpem le Yordan-tɔsisi nu eye metà Aƒetɔ nɛ be: ‘Nyemawu wò kple yi o.’

english_verse: Now you must punish him. He's an old man, but you're wise enough to know that you must have him killed. David Dies
translation_verse: Gake mègana wòatsi anyi tohehemaxɔ o. Ame nyanu nènye. Wò ŋutɔ ànya ale si nàwɔe. Na eƒe ta ɣi la naƒo ʋu wòatsɔ yi tsiẽ.” David ƒe ku

english_verse: he saddled his donkey and went after them. He found them and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Simei tso, bla akpa na eƒe tedzi, eye wòyi eƒe kluviawo di ge le Axis gbɔ le Gat. Ekpɔ wo, eye wòkplɔ wo gbɔe tso Gat.

english_verse: Joab's family will always suffer because of what he did, but the Lord will always bless David's family and his kingdom with peace.
translation_verse: Yoab kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo akpɔ tohehe tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ tegbee le ame eve siawo ƒe ku ta. Ke Aƒetɔ ana ŋutifafa David, David ƒe dzidzimeviwo, eƒe ƒome kple eƒe fiazikpui heyi ɖe mavɔ me.”

english_verse: His son Solomon became king and took control of David's kingdom. Adonijah Is Killed
translation_verse: Ale Salomo nɔ tɔ́a David ƒe fiazikpui dzi, eye eƒe fiaɖuƒe la li ke sesĩe. Adoniya ƒe ku

english_verse: One day, Adonijah went to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she asked, “Is this a friendly visit?” “Yes.
translation_verse: Eva eme be Adoniya, Xagit vi va Salomo nɔ Batseba gbɔ. Batseba biae be: “Ɖagbeea?” Eɖo ŋu be: “Ẽ, ɖagbee.”

english_verse: I just want to talk with you.” “All right,” she told him, “go ahead.”
translation_verse: Ke egblɔ be: “Nya aɖe le asinye mebe magblɔ na wò.” Batseba xɔ edzi be: “Gblɔe.”

english_verse: “You know that I was king for a little while,” Adonijah replied. “And everyone in Israel accepted me as their ruler. But the Lord wanted my brother to be king, so now things have changed.
translation_verse: Adoniya yi edzi be: “Wò ŋutɔ ènya be fiaɖuƒea la tɔnye wòle be wòanye, eye Israel bliboa nɔ mɔ kpɔm be nyee le fia ɖu ge hafi. Gake nuawo va trɔ bubui; fiaɖuƒea va zu nɔvinye tɔ elabe Aƒetɔ ŋutɔe ɖoe nenema.

english_verse: Would you do me a favor?” “What do you want?” Bathsheba asked.
translation_verse: Ke nu ɖeka aɖe pɛ ko li medi be mabia wò. Mègatem o!” Batseba gblɔ nɛ be: “Yi dzi nàƒo nu.”

english_verse: “Please ask Solomon to let me marry Abishag. He won't say no to you.”
translation_verse: Adoniya yi edzi be: “Meɖe kuku na wò, ƒo nu kple fia Salomo nam ne wòatsɔ Abisag, Sunam-nyɔnu la, nam maɖe. Menya be màbia nui wòagbe o.”

english_verse: “All right,” she said. “I'll ask him.”
translation_verse: Batseba gblɔ be: “Enyo, mayi aɖaƒo nu kple fia la na wò.”

english_verse: When Bathsheba went to see Solomon, he stood up to meet her, then bowed low. He sat back down and had another throne brought in, so his mother could sit at his right side.
translation_verse: Ale Batseba yi fia Salomo gbɔ be yeatsɔ Adoniya ƒe biabiaa aɖo eŋkume. Esi fia la kpɔe wògbɔna ɖa la, etso yi ɖakpee, eye wòde ta agu nɛ hã. Tete wòtrɔ va bɔbɔ nɔ eƒe fiazikpui dzi. Ena wotsɔ zikpui vɛ na fia nɔ, eye nɔa bɔbɔ nɔ eƒe ɖusime.

english_verse: Bathsheba sat down and then asked, “Would you do me a small favor?” Solomon replied, “Mother, just tell me what you want, and I will do it.”
translation_verse: Batseba gblɔ be: “Medi be maɖe kuku na wò nàwɔ nu vi aɖe nam. Mègagbe o!” Fia la gblɔ nɛ be: “Nɔnye, nu ka nèdi be mawɔ na ye? Nyemagbe o ɖe!”

english_verse: “Allow your brother Adonijah to marry Abishag,” she answered.
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: “Na woatsɔ Abisag, Sunam-nyɔnu la na nɔviwò Adoniya ne wòaɖe.”

english_verse: Solomon said: What? Let my older brother marry Abishag? You may as well ask me to let him rule the kingdom! And why don't you ask such favors for Abiathar and Joab?
translation_verse: Fia Salomo ɖo nyaa ŋu na nɔa be: “Nu ka ta nèle Abisag ko biam na Adoniya? Bia fiaɖuƒea hã nɛ! Fonye wònye, eye kura gɔ̃ la, nunɔla Abyatar kple aʋakplɔla Yoab, Zeruya vi la, le edzi xoxo.”

english_verse: I swear in the name of the Lord that Adonijah will die because he asked for this! If he doesn't, I pray that God will severely punish me.
translation_verse: Tete fia Salomo tà Aƒetɔ be: “Mawu nefiam wòagafiam ɖe edzi, ne Adoniya metsɔ eƒe agbe xe fe ɖe nya sia ta o fĩi!

english_verse: The Lord made me king in my father's place and promised that the kings of Israel would come from my family. Yes, I swear by the living Lord that Adonijah will die today.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ nye ame si li kem, tsɔm ɖo tɔ́nye David ƒe fiazikpui dzi, eye wòna nye dzidzime zu fiaƒome abe ale si wòdo ŋugbe ene. Metà Aƒetɔ be mana woawu Adoniya egbe sia ke.”

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “go kill Adonijah.” So Adonijah died. Abiathar Is Sent Back Home
translation_verse: Ale fia Salomo dɔ Benaya, Yahoyada vi ɖa wòyi ɖaxlã nu ɖee ƒu anyi wòku. Abyatar nyànya; Yoab ƒe ku

english_verse: Solomon sent for Abiathar the priest and said: Abiathar, go back home to Anathoth! You ought to be killed too, but I won't do it now. When my father David was king, you were in charge of the sacred chest, and you went through a lot of hard times with my father.
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ na nunɔla Abyatar be: “Yi ɖanɔ wò anyigba me le Anatot. Èdze na ku gake nyemana woawu wò fifia o, elabe wòe tsɔ Aƒetɔ Mawu ƒe aɖaka la le tɔ́nye David ŋgɔ; gawu la, ènɔ tɔ́nye ŋu kplíkplikpli heto eƒe fukpekpewo katã me kplii.”

english_verse: But I won't let you be a priest of the Lord anymore. And so the promise that the Lord had made at Shiloh about the family of Eli came true. Joab Is Killed
translation_verse: Ale Salomo nyà Abyatar ɖa be maganye Aƒetɔ ƒe nunɔla azɔ o. Abyatar nyànya siae nye nya si Aƒetɔ gblɔ ɖi le Silo ɖe Eli ƒe ƒome ŋu la ƒe mevava.

english_verse: Joab had not helped Absalom try to become king, but he had helped Adonijah. So when Joab learned that Adonijah had been killed, he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
translation_verse: Esi Yoab se nu si dzɔ ɖe Adoniya kple Abyatar dzi la, esí yi Aƒetɔ ƒe agbadɔ me ɖalé vɔsamlekpui la ƒe dzowo ɖe asi. Esí alea elabe eya hã nɔ Adoniya dzi, togbɔ be mede Absalom ya dzi o hã.

english_verse: When Solomon heard about this, he sent someone to ask Joab, “Why did you run to the altar?” Joab sent back his answer, “I was afraid of you, and I ran to the Lord for protection.” Then Solomon shouted, “Benaiah, go kill Joab!”
translation_verse: Esi wova gblɔ na fia Salomo be: “Yoab sí yi Aƒetɔ ƒe agbadɔ me ɖale vɔsamlekpuia gbɔ” la, Salomo dɔ Benaya, Yehoyada vi ɖa be: “Yi ɖawui.”

english_verse: Benaiah went to the sacred tent and yelled, “Joab, the king orders you to come out!” “No!” Joab answered. “Kill me right here.” Benaiah went back and told Solomon what Joab had said.
translation_verse: Ale Benaya va Aƒetɔ ƒe agbadɔ la me, eye wògblɔ be: “Fia ɖe gbe be: ‘Do go va.’ ” Yoab ɖo eŋu be: “Gbeɖe, maku le afi sia.” Benaya gatrɔ yi fia la gbɔ ɖagblɔ Yoab ƒe ŋuɖoɖoa nɛ.

english_verse: Solomon replied: Do what Joab said. Kill him and bury him! Then my family and I won't be responsible for what he did to Abner the commander of Israel's army and to Amasa the commander of Judah's army. He killed those innocent men without my father knowing about it. Both of them were better men than Joab. Now the Lord will make him pay for those murders.
translation_verse: Yoab wu Israel ƒe aʋakplɔla Abner, Ner vi kple Yuda ƒe aʋakplɔla, Amasa, Yeter vi. Ame siwo nyo wui, eye woxɔ asi wui hã, gake ɖeko wòtso ko wu wo le tɔ́nye ƒe manyamanya me, evɔ wònye ameawo mewɔ naneke si ta wòdze be woawu wo ɖo hafi o. Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ agahe to nɛ le eƒe nuwɔna vɔ̃ɖiawo ta.

english_verse: Benaiah went back and killed Joab. His body was taken away and buried near his home in the desert.
translation_verse: Tete Benaya, Yehoyada vi ɖaƒo Yoab ƒu anyi hewui. Woɖii ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe aƒeme le gbedadaƒo.

english_verse: Solomon put Benaiah in Joab's place as army commander, and he put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest. Shimei Is Killed
translation_verse: Eyome fia tsɔ Benaya, Yehoyada vi ɖo aʋakɔ la nu, ɖe Yoab teƒe eye wòtsɔ nunɔla Zadok ɖo Abyatar teƒe. Simei ƒe ku

english_verse: Solomon sent for Shimei and said, “Build a house here in Jerusalem and live in it. But whatever you do, don't leave the city!
translation_verse: Azɔ fia na woɖayɔ Simei vɛ nɛ, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Tso aƒe na ɖokuiwò ɖe Yerusalem, eye nànɔ afi ma, eye wò afɔ eve megado yi afi aɖeke o.

english_verse: If you ever cross Kidron Valley and leave Jerusalem, you will be killed. And it will be your own fault.”
translation_verse: Elabe gbe si gbe nàdo go atsò Kidron-tɔʋua la, nyae be yeku, wò ʋu anɔ wò ŋutɔ wò ta dzi.”

english_verse: “That's fair, Your Majesty,” Shimei answered. “I'll do that.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem from then on.
translation_verse: Simei gblɔ na fia la be: “Nu si nègblɔ la nyo, abe ale si nye aƒetɔ fia gblɔ ene la, nenemae wò dɔla awɔ.” Ale Simei nɔ Yerusalem-du me ŋkeke geɖewo.

english_verse: About three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to King Achish in Gath. When Shimei found out where they were,
translation_verse: Le ƒe etɔ̃ megbe la, eva va eme be eƒe kluvi eve sí yi Gat-fia Axis, Maaxa vi gbɔ. Esi amewo va gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, wò kluviwo le Gat” la,

english_verse: Someone told Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath and was back.
translation_verse: Ke esi wogblɔ na Salomo be Simei tso Yerusalem yi Gat gbɔ la,

english_verse: Solomon sent for him and said: Shimei, you promised in the name of the Lord that you would never leave Jerusalem. I warned you that you would die if you did. You agreed that this was fair, didn't you?
translation_verse: fia na woyɔ Simei vɛ, eye wòbiae be: “Ɖe nyemena nètà Aƒetɔ, eye mexlɔ̃ nu wò be: ‘Nyae nyuie be gbe si gbe nèdo le afi sia yi afi aɖe la, àku’ oa? eye nègblɔ nam be: ‘Nu si nègblɔ la, enyo, maɖo toe’ oa?

english_verse: You have disobeyed me and have broken the promise you made to the Lord.
translation_verse: Nu ka ta mèwɔ adzɔgbe si nèɖe na Aƒetɔ dzi o, eye nu ka ta nèda se si mede na wò la dzi?”

english_verse: I know you remember all the cruel things you did to my father David. Now the Lord is going to punish you for what you did.
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ hã na Simei be: “Ènya le wò dzime, vɔ̃ siwo katã nèwɔ ɖe tɔ́nye David ŋu, eya ta Aƒetɔ atrɔ wò vɔ̃ la akɔ ɖe wò ŋutɔ wò ta dzi.

english_verse: But the Lord will bless me and make my father's kingdom strong forever.
translation_verse: Ke woayra fia Salomo ya, eye David ƒe fiazikpui ali ke le Aƒetɔ ŋkume tegbee.”

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “kill Shimei.” So Shimei died. Solomon was now in complete control of his kingdom.
translation_verse: Tete fia ɖe gbe na Benaya, Yehoyada vi, eye wòkplɔ Simei do goe ɖaƒoe ƒu anyi wòku. Ale fiaɖuƒe la li ke keŋkeŋ ɖe Salomo ƒe asi me.

english_verse: At that time, there was no temple for worshiping the Lord, and everyone offered sacrifices at the local shrines.
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣiwo me la, dukɔa me tɔwo nɔa vɔsawo wɔm le nuxeƒewo ko le dukɔa me, elabe wometu xɔ aɖeke na Aƒetɔ ŋkɔ haɖe o.

english_verse: I'll also give you what you didn't ask for. You'll be rich and respected as long as you live, and you'll be greater than any other king.
translation_verse: Mena nu si mèbia o la hã wò, kesinɔnu kple bubu siaa, ale be fia bubu aɖeke masɔ kpli wò le wò ŋkekewo katã me o.

english_verse: Solomon loved the Lord and followed his father David's instructions, but Solomon also offered sacrifices and burned incense at the shrines.
translation_verse: Salomo lɔ̃ Aƒetɔ, eye wòzɔna ɖe tɔ́a David ƒe ɖoɖowo nu pɛpɛpɛ; negbe nuxeƒeawo ko wòdena ɖasaa vɔ, eye wòtɔa dzo lifi le afi mawo.

english_verse: One night while Solomon was in Gibeon, the Lord God appeared to him in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖe eɖokui fia Salomo le drɔ̃e me le zã me le Gibeon. Mawu gblɔ be: “Bia nu si mana wò la wò.”

english_verse: Solomon answered: My father David, your servant, was honest and did what you commanded. You were always loyal to him, and you gave him a son who is now king.
translation_verse: Salomo ɖo eŋu be: “Èɖe lɔlɔ̃ kple amenuveve gã ŋutɔ fia wò dɔla tɔ́nye David elabe eƒe agbenɔnɔ ɖe ŋuwò fia be enye nyateƒetɔ, elɔ̃a nya dzɔdzɔe, eye wòdza le eƒe dzime hã. Eya ta ève enu kple wò lɔlɔ̃ gã be nèna viŋutsui, si bɔbɔ nɔ eƒe fiazikpui dzi egbe.

english_verse: Lord God, I'm your servant, and you've made me king in my father's place. But I'm very young and know so little about being a leader.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu, wòe ɖo wò dɔla fia ɖe tɔ́nye David teƒe. Ɖevi sue ko menye, nyemenya ale si madoe, agagbɔ o.

english_verse: And now I must rule your chosen people, even though there are too many of them to count.
translation_verse: Evɔ wò dɔla nye esi va le wò dukɔ si nètia la dome, dukɔ gã sia si me viwo sɔ gbɔ ale gbegbe be womate ŋu axlẽ wo o.

english_verse: Please make me wise and teach me the difference between right and wrong. Then I will know how to rule your people. If you don't, there is no way I could rule this great nation of yours.
translation_verse: Eya ta na susu si sea nu gɔme la wò dɔla be wòatsɔ kplɔ wò dukɔ lae, ne mate ŋu ade vovototo nyui kpe vɔ̃ dome, elabe ame kae ate ŋu anɔ dukɔ sia nu anye ekplɔla?”

english_verse: God said: Solomon, I'm pleased that you asked for this. You could have asked to live a long time or to be rich. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom to make right decisions.
translation_verse: Mawu gblɔ nɛ be: “Be nèbia nu sia, eye mèbia agbe didi alo kesinɔnuwo, alo be yeƒe futɔwo neku o, ke boŋ nèbia nugɔmesese be yeate ŋu adze si nu si nyo ta la,

english_verse: If you obey me and follow my commands, as your father David did, I'll let you live a long time.
translation_verse: Azɔ ne àwɔ nye lɔlɔ̃nu le nu sia nu me, alé nye ɖoɖowo kple nye sededewo me ɖe asi abe tɔ́wò David ene la, ekema mana wò agbenɔŋkekewo adzi ɖe edzi.”

english_verse: Solomon woke up and realized that God had spoken to him in the dream. He went back to Jerusalem and stood in front of the sacred chest, where he offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. Then Solomon gave a feast for his officials. Solomon Makes a Difficult Decision
translation_verse: Tete Salomo nyɔ, ke kpɔ ɖa, drɔ̃ ye wòku. Etrɔ va Yerusalem, eye wòva tsi tsitre ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la ŋgɔ, eye wòsa numemevɔwo kple ŋutifafavɔwo. Eɖo kplɔ̃ gã aɖe na eƒe dɔlawo katã. Salomo tso afia nunyatɔe

english_verse: One day two women came to King Solomon,
translation_verse: Azɔ, gbolo eve aɖewo va, eye wotsi tsitre ɖe fia la ŋkume.

english_verse: and one of them said: Your Majesty, this woman and I live in the same house. Not long ago my baby was born at home,
translation_verse: Nyɔnua ɖeka gblɔ be: “Fia bubutɔ, nye kple nyɔnu sia la aƒe aɖeka me míele, eye medzi vi, esime eya hã nɔ aƒea me.

english_verse: One night while we were all asleep, she rolled over on her baby, and he died.
translation_verse: Etsɔ zã me la, nyɔnu sia viŋutsuvi ku, elabe emlɔ edzi.

english_verse: Then while I was still asleep, she got up and took my son out of my bed. She put him in her bed, then she put her dead baby next to me.
translation_verse: Ke efɔ zã gã dome esime meyi alɔ̃ me ʋĩi, va kɔ vinye le akɔnyenu yi ɖamlɔ eɖokui gbɔ, tsɔ via kukua va mlɔ nye akɔnu.

english_verse: In the morning when I got up to feed my son, I saw that he was dead. But when I looked at him in the light, I knew he wasn't my son.
translation_verse: Esi menyɔ fɔŋli be mana no vinye la, kpɔ ɖa, eku; ke esi ŋu ke, eye meɖe ŋku ɖee nyuie la, mekpɔ be menye vi si medzi lae nye ema o.”

english_verse: “No!” the other woman shouted. “He was your son. My baby is alive!” “The dead baby is yours,” the first woman yelled. “Mine is alive!” They argued back and forth in front of Solomon,
translation_verse: Ke nyɔnu evelia gblɔ be: “Kpao! Vinyee nye vi gbagbea; tɔwòe nye kukua.” Nyɔnu gbãtɔ gblɔ be: “Ao! Viwòe nye kukua, tɔnyee nye agbagbea.” Aleae nyaa va zu le fia la ŋkume.

english_verse: until finally he said, “Both of you say this live baby is yours.
translation_verse: Fia la be: “Ame ɖeka be: ‘Vinyee le agbe, tɔwòe ku.’ Evelia be: ‘Ao; viwòe ku, tɔnyee nye agbagbea’ ”

english_verse: Someone bring me a sword.” A sword was brought, and Solomon ordered,
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ be: “Mitsɔ yi vɛ nam.” Wotsɔ yi vɛ na fia la.

english_verse: “Cut the baby in half! That way each of you can have part of him.”
translation_verse: Tete fia la gblɔ be: “Mife ɖevi gbagbe la me ɖe eve ne miatsɔ ɖeka na nyɔnu ɖeka, eye miatsɔ evelia na nyɔnu evelia.”

english_verse: “Please don't kill my son,” the baby's mother screamed. “Your Majesty, I love him very much, but give him to her. Just don't kill him.” The other woman shouted, “Go ahead and cut him in half. Then neither of us will have the baby.”
translation_verse: Tete nyɔnu si tɔ nye ɖevi gbagbea la gblɔ na fia la, le lɔlɔ̃ si le eme ɖe via ŋu ta, be: “O nye aƒetɔ! Mitsɔ ɖevi gbagbe la nɛ ko, migawui kura o.” Ke nyɔnu evelia ya be: “Manye tɔnye o, manye wò hã tɔwò o; mife eme.”

english_verse: Solomon said, “Don't kill the baby.” Then he pointed to the first woman, “She is his real mother. Give the baby to her.”
translation_verse: Tete fia la ɖo eŋu gblɔ be: “Mitsɔ vi gbagbe la na nyɔnu gbãtɔ; eye migawui kura o, eya nye nɔa.”

english_verse: Everyone in Israel was amazed when they heard how Solomon had made his decision. They realized that God had given him wisdom to judge fairly.
translation_verse: Esi Israelviwo katã se fia ƒe nyametsotso la, dukɔ blibo la ƒe nu ku. Vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo le fia la ŋu, elabe wokpɔe be Mawu ƒe nunya le eyama me, be wòatsɔ adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu dzɔdzɔe.

english_verse: Solomon chose twelve regional officers, who took turns bringing food for him and his household. Each officer provided food from his region for one month of the year.
translation_verse: Salomo ɖo nutomedzikpɔla wui eve Israel-dukɔa nu; ame siawo dia nuɖuɖu na fia la kple eƒemetɔwo. Ɖe sia ɖe kpɔa fiasã la dzi alea le nuɖuɖu gome ɣleti ɖeka le ƒe ɖeka me.

english_verse: The son of Deker was in charge of the towns of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-Shemesh, and Elon-Beth-Hanan.
translation_verse: Ben-Deker le Makaz, Saalbim, Bet-Semes, Elon kple Bet-Xanan.

english_verse: The son of Abinadab was in charge of Naphath-Dor and was married to Solomon's daughter Taphath.
translation_verse: Ben-Abinadab le Dor-nyigba blibo la nu eyae ɖe Salomo ƒe vinyɔnu Tafat,

english_verse: The son of Geber was in charge of the town of Ramoth in Gilead and the villages in Gilead belonging to the family of Jair, a descendant of Manasseh. He was also in charge of the region of Argob in Bashan, which had
translation_verse: Bengeber le Ramot-du le Gilead nu, eyae xɔ Manase vi Yair ƒe kɔƒe siwo le Gilead kple Argob-nutowo me le Basan. Argob-nutome duawo de bla ade, eye wo katã nye du gãwo siwo woɖo gli ƒo xlã, eye akɔbligameti le woƒe agbowo ŋu.

english_verse: Ahinadab son of Iddo was in charge of the territory of Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Axinadab, Ido vi le Maxanaim-nutome nu.

english_verse: Ahimaaz was in charge of the territory of Naphtali and was married to Solomon's daughter Basemath.
translation_verse: Aximaaz le Naftali-nutome. Eyae ɖe Salomo vinyɔnu Basmat,

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was in charge of the territory of Issachar.
translation_verse: Yehosafat, Paruah vi le Isaxar-nyigba nu.

english_verse: Shimei son of Ela was in charge of the territory of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Simei, Ela vi le Benyamin-nyigba nu.

english_verse: Geber son of Uri was in charge of Gilead, where King Sihon of the Amorites and King Og of Bashan had lived. And one officer was in charge of the territory of Judah. The Size of Solomon's Kingdom
translation_verse: Geber, Uri vi le Gilead-nyigba si nye Amoritɔwo ƒe fia Sixon kple Basan-fia Og ƒe anyigba tsã la nu. Nutomedzikpɔla ɖeka nɔ Yuda-nyigba nu. Salomo ƒe fiaɖuɖu dze dzi nɛ

english_verse: Solomon ruled every kingdom between the Euphrates River and the land of the Philistines down to Egypt. These kingdoms paid him taxes as long as he lived.
translation_verse: Salomo ƒe dziɖuƒe keke tso Frat-tɔsisi ŋu yi Filistitɔwo ƒe liƒo kple Egipte-nyigba ƒe liƒo dzi ke. Elɔ fiaɖuƒe sue siwo katã nɔ afi mawo la ɖe me. Le Salomo ƒe agbenɔɣi la, fiaɖuƒe mawo katã nɔ ete; wodzɔa nu nɛ, eye wonɔ ete le eƒe agbenɔɣi katã.

english_verse: Everyone living in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, was safe as long as Solomon lived. Each family sat undisturbed beneath its own grape vines and fig trees.
translation_verse: Ale Yuda-nyigba dzi tɔwo kple Israel-nyigba dzi tɔwo nɔ agbe le dziɖeɖi me bɔkɔɔ, tso Dan va se ɖe Beer-Seba gɔ̃ hã. Ame sia ame le eƒe wainkawo kple gbotiwo te le ŋutifafa me le Salomo ƒe agbenɔɣi katã.

english_verse: Each of the twelve regional officers brought food to Solomon and his household for one month of the year. They provided everything he needed,
translation_verse: Ne nutomedzikpɔlaawo dometɔ aɖe ƒe ɣleti si woɖo nɛ ɖo ko la, edia nuɖuɖu si ahiã na fia Salomo kple ame siwo va ɖua nu le eƒe kplɔ̃ ŋu la katã vanɛ; womenana be nuɖuɖu vɔna ɣeaɖekeɣi o.

english_verse: He was wiser than anyone else in the world, including the wisest people of the east and of Egypt. He was even wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Mahol's three sons, Heman, Calcol, and Darda. Solomon became famous in every country around Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Enya nu wu amegbetɔ ɖe sia ɖe. Enya nu wu Etan, Ezraxitɔ la, nya nu wu Maxol viwo Yeman, Xalkol kple Darda. Eŋkɔ ɖi hoo le dukɔ siwo le xexeme ƒe akpa mawo la me godoo va kpe.

english_verse: He could talk about all kinds of plants, from large trees to small bushes, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
translation_verse: Egblɔ nya detowo le atiwo kple gbewo ŋu, tso sederti si wɔna le Lebanon va ɖo hisɔp si miena ɖe gli ŋu la dzi; nenema ke wòhe nyateƒe vovovowo ɖe go le lãfɔnewo, xewo, nutatawo kple tɔmelãwo ŋu.

english_verse: Kings all over the world heard about Solomon's wisdom and sent people to listen to him teach.
translation_verse: Amewo tsoa dukɔ geɖewo me vana koŋ ko be yewoava se Salomo ƒe nunya. Fia siwo katã se eƒe nunya ŋkɔ la va be yewoase eƒe nunya.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre had always been friends with Solomon's father David. When Hiram learned that Solomon was king, he sent some of his officials to meet with Solomon.
translation_verse: Azɔ Tiro-fia Xiram dɔ eƒe dɔlawo ɖo ɖe Salomo, esi wòse be wosi ami nɛ ɖo fiae ɖe tɔ́a teƒe, elabe Xiram lɔ̃ David ɣe sia ɣi.

english_verse: The Lord God promised my father that when his son became king, he would build a temple for worshiping the Lord. So I've decided to do that.
translation_verse: Eya ta meɖo be matu xɔ na Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu. Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ gɔ̃ gblɔ na tɔ́nye kpɔ be: ‘Viwò si matsɔ ɖo wò fiazikpui dzi ɖe tewòƒe lae latu gbedoxɔ si me woanɔ subɔyem le.’

english_verse: I'd like you to send your workers to cut down cedar trees in Lebanon for me. I will pay them whatever you say and will even have my workers help them. We both know that your workers are more experienced than anyone else at cutting lumber.
translation_verse: Eya ta na woatso sedertiwo nam le Lebanon. Wò ŋutɔ ènya be ame aɖeke mele mía gbɔ le afii si nya nu le atitsotso ŋu abe Sidontɔwo ene o. Madɔ amewo ɖa woava kpe ɖe wò ameawo ŋu le dɔa wɔwɔ me, eye maxe home si nàdi be wonexe na wò ameawo la na wo.”

english_verse: Hiram was so happy when he heard Solomon's request that he said, “I am grateful that the Lord gave David such a wise son to be king of that great nation!”
translation_verse: Esi Xiram se Salomo ƒe nyaawo la, dzi dzɔe ŋutɔ, eye wògblɔ be: “Kafukafu woana Aƒetɔ egbe sia be wòna vi nyanu David be wòava nɔ dukɔ gã sia nu.”

english_verse: Then he sent back his answer: I received your message and will give you all the cedar and pine logs you need.
translation_verse: Xiram ɖo ame ɖe Salomo be: “Du si nèɖo ɖem la va tum. Mana woatso sedertiawo kple sesewutiawo na wò abe ale si nèdi ene.

english_verse: My workers will carry them down from Lebanon to the Mediterranean Sea. They will tie the logs together and float them along the coast to wherever you want them. Then they will untie the logs, and your workers can take them from there. To pay for the logs, you can provide the grain I need for my household.
translation_verse: Nye dɔlawo alɔ wo aɖi abu tso Lebanon va ƒu nu. Mabla wo ɖe babla vovovowo me; ekema ne wò ya ènyagbe gblɔ teƒe si nèdi be woalɔ wo va kɔ ɖo na ye ko la, matsɔ bablaawo ato ƒu dzi ava afi ma. Tete mana woatu ka atiawo le afi ma, eye wò amewo alɔ wo vɛ na wò. Nu si ko mabia tso asiwò lae nye be nàɖo nuɖuɖu ɖem na nye aƒemetɔwo.”

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise and made Solomon wise. Hiram and Solomon signed a treaty and never went to war against each other. Solomon's Workers
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ na nunya Salomo abe ale si wòdo ŋugbe nɛ ene. Gbe dze gbe dzi na Xiram kple Salomo, eye wo kple eve la bla nu.

english_verse: and he put Adoniram in charge of these workers. Solomon divided them into three groups of
translation_verse: Eɖoa wo ɖa akpe ewo, akpe ewo ɣleti sia ɣleti. Wotsɔa ɣleti ɖeka nɔa Lebanon eye wonɔa aƒe ɣleti eve. Adoniram ye le dɔwɔlawo nu.

english_verse: He ordered the workers to cut and shape large blocks of good stone for the foundation of the temple.
translation_verse: Le fia ƒe gbeɖeɖe nu la, woɖe kpe gã xɔasiwo do goe kpe ɖe esiwo wokpa la ŋu ne woatsɔ ɖo xɔa gɔme anyii.

english_verse: Solomon's and Hiram's men worked with men from the city of Gebal, and together they got the stones and logs ready for the temple.
translation_verse: Ale Salomo ƒe xɔtulawo kple Xiram ƒe xɔtulawo kpakple Gibli-du me tɔwo trɔ asi le kpewo kple atiwo ŋu na xɔ la tutu.

english_verse: The windows were narrow on the outside but wide on the inside.
translation_verse: Woɖe fesre aɖewo ƒomevi ɖe xɔawo ŋu. Fesreawo nu mia le gota gome wu le xɔa me, eye wode adzralawo wo nu.

english_verse: The roof of the temple was made out of beams and cedar boards. The workers finished building the outside of the temple.
translation_verse: Esi wòtu xɔa wu nu vɔ keŋ la, etsɔ daɖedziwo, siwo wotsɔ sederti kpa la kple sederʋuƒowo wɔ dzisasrã ɖe eme.

english_verse: Along the sides and back of the temple, there were three levels of storage rooms. The rooms on the bottom level were just over two meters wide, the rooms on the middle level were over two and a half meters wide, and those on the top level were just over three meters wide. There were ledges on the outside of the temple that supported the beams of the storage rooms, so that nothing was built into the temple walls.
translation_verse: Xɔŋuxɔeawo ƒe anyigbaxɔ me keke meta eve kple afã. Woƒe dziƒoxɔ gbãtɔ me keke meta etɔ̃, eye woƒe dziƒoxɔ evelia me keke meta etɔ̃ kple afã. Xɔa tulawo ɖo glia kple aɖaŋu tɔxɛ aɖe si wɔe be zi ale si glia ƒe kɔkɔme le dzi yim ko la, eƒe titrime dzi nɔ ɖeɖem kpɔtɔ. Aɖaŋu sia wɔe be xɔa ƒe gli ŋutɔ koe kɔ xɔŋuxɔea ƒe dzisasrãwo ɖe abɔta ale be megahiã be woaŋɔ glia atsɔ dzisasrãawo ƒe atiwo aƒo ɖe doawo me o.

english_verse: Solomon did not want the noise of hammers and axes to be heard at the place where the temple was being built. So he gave orders for the workers to shape the blocks of stone at the quarry.
translation_verse: Wotrɔ asi le kpe siwo wotsɔ tu xɔae la ŋu le keke kpeawo kuƒe ke. Eya ta esime wonɔ xɔa tum la, màse zu, alo fía alo gakpodɔwɔnu bubu aɖeke ƒe ɖiɖi le xɔa gbɔ o.

english_verse: Storage rooms just over two meters high were all around the temple, and they were attached to the temple by cedar beams.
translation_verse: Etu xɔŋuxɔewo ɖe gbedoxɔ la ŋu katã. Xɔŋuxɔeawo nye tuɖedzi-eve-dziƒoxɔwo. Tuɖedzi ɖe sia ɖe kɔ meta eve kple afã. Ɖe sia ɖe ƒe sederti siwo woda ɖe edzi la ƒe nugbɔ va le xɔa ƒe gli dzi.

english_verse: The Lord told Solomon:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va na Salomo be:

english_verse: The floor of the temple was made out of pine, and the walls were lined with cedar from floor to ceiling.
translation_verse: Woklã sederʋuƒowo ɖe xɔa me ƒe gliwo ŋu tso anyigba yi ɖatɔ gliawo ƒe daɖedziwo, eye woklã sesewuʋuƒowo ɖe xɔa me ƒe anyigba.

english_verse: The most holy place was in the back of the temple, and it was nine meters square. Cedar boards standing from floor to ceiling separated it from the rest of the temple.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ sederʋuƒowo tso xɔa me le eƒe megbe kpa dzi ale be afi ma zu xɔmexɔe aɖe. Sederʋuƒoawo kɔ yi ɖatɔ xɔa ƒe daɖedziwo ke. Xɔmexɔe sia didi meta asieke. Woyɔe be Kɔkɔeƒe ƒe kɔkɔeƒe.

english_verse: The inside walls were lined with cedar to hide the stones, and the cedar was decorated with carvings of gourds and flowers.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ hɛ ɖaɖɛ ta gotsetsewo kple seƒoƒo aɖe ƒomevi si kè nyuie la ɖe sederʋuƒoawo ŋu. Sederʋuƒowo xɔ gliawo ŋu ƒe afi sia afi ale gbegbe be màkpɔ kpe siwo wotsɔ ɖo glia la ƒe afi aɖeke o.

english_verse: Solomon had two statues of winged creatures made from olive wood to put in the most holy place. Each creature was four and a half meters tall
translation_verse: Etsɔ amiti wɔ kerubi eve ɖe kɔkɔeƒe si le ememe la me. Wo dome ɖe sia ɖe kɔ meta ene kple afã.

english_verse: and four and a half meters across. They had two wings, and the wings were just over two meters long.
translation_verse: Kerubi ɖeka kɔ meta ene sentimeta ene; evelia hã nenema ke.

english_verse: The creatures were also covered with gold.
translation_verse: Wofa sika ɖe kerubi eveawo hã ŋu.

english_verse: The walls of the two rooms were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ ga ɖaɖɛ ɖè kerubiwo, detiwo kple seƒoƒo siwo kè nyuie la ƒe tatawo ɖe gli ŋu le xɔa me katã kple Kɔkɔeƒe ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la hã.

english_verse: Even the floor was covered with gold.
translation_verse: Wofa sika ɖe anyigba gɔ̃ hã le xɔa me ƒe afi sia afi.

english_verse: The two doors to the most holy place were made out of olive wood and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures. The doors and the carvings were covered with gold. The door frame came to a point at the top.
translation_verse: Woɖè kerubiwo, detiwo kple seƒoƒo aɖe si kè nyuie la ƒe tatawo ɖe ʋɔtruawo ŋu be ʋɔtruawo nanyakpɔ, eye wofa sika ɖe ʋɔtruawo ŋutɔ kple atsyɔ̃ɖonu siawo ŋu.

english_verse: The two doors to the main room of the temple were made out of pine, and each one had two sections so they could fold open. The door frame was shaped like a rectangle and was made out of olive wood.
translation_verse: Wode ʋɔtru eve enu. Ʋɔtru eveawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe hã ma ɖe akpa eve me, eye àte ŋu aʋu akpa ɖeka ko ne èlɔ̃. Sesewuʋuƒoe wotsɔ kpa ʋɔtruawoe.

english_verse: The doors were covered with gold and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: Woɖè kerubiwo, detiwo kple seƒoƒo aɖe si kè nyuie la ƒe tatawo ɖe wo ŋu be woanyakpɔ, eye wofa sika ɖe nutataawo hã me.

english_verse: The inner courtyard of the temple had walls made out of three layers of cut stones with one layer of cedar beams.
translation_verse: Etɔ kpɔ emetɔ. Etsɔ kpe fúfu ɖo amli etɔ̃ eye wòtu sederti ɖe wo dzi.

english_verse: Work began on the temple during Ziv, the second month of the year, four years after Solomon became king of Israel.
translation_verse: Woɖo Aƒetɔ ƒe xɔa gɔme anyi le Salomo ƒe fiaɖuɣi ƒe ƒè enelia me, le ɣleti Ziv me.

english_verse: Seven years later the workers finished building it during Bul, the eighth month of the year. It was built exactly as it had been planned.
translation_verse: Wowu etutu nu le Salomo ƒe fiaɖuɣi ƒe ƒè wui ɖekɛlia me, le ƒea ƒe ɣleti enyilia, Bul, me. Wotui wòle abe ale si woɖo be yewoatui ene la tututu. Xɔa tutu xɔ ƒe adrẽ sɔŋ.

english_verse: a large bowl; twelve bulls that held up the bowl;
translation_verse: gazɔ ɖeka, nyitsu wui eve siwo le gazɔa te,

english_verse: -centimeter strip, and there were four braces attached to the corners of each stand. The panels and the supports were attached to the stands,
translation_verse: Sɔtiawo ƒe ta le abe dzogbenya ene. Nu siawoe Xiram wɔ tsɔ wu sɔtiawo ŋudɔwo nui. Akɔblizɔ gã la (Kron II,

english_verse: pans for hot ashes, and also shovels and sprinkling bowls. Hiram made these bronze things for Solomon
translation_verse: gazewo, sofiwo kple ametagbɛwo. Akɔbli si ŋu wozrɔ̃ lae Xiram tsɔ wɔ nu siawo katã na fia Salomo hena Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la.

english_verse: Solomon's throne was in Justice Hall, where he judged cases. This hall was completely lined with cedar.
translation_verse: Wogatu xɔ bubu aɖe si wòyɔ be Fiazikpui Xɔgã, afi si wòadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu le. Afi mae nye kodzoɖiƒe. Woklã sederʋuƒowo ɖe xɔ sia me ƒe gliwo ŋu tso egɔme ke yi ɖatɔ dzisasrãa.

english_verse: The section of the palace where Solomon lived was behind Justice Hall and looked exactly like it. He had a similar place built for his wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt.
translation_verse: Xɔ si nye Salomo ŋutɔ ƒe nɔƒe koŋ la le xɔxɔnu bubu le ʋɔnudrɔ̃xɔa megbe. Wotui wòle abe Lebanon-ve xɔa ene tututu. Salomo tu xɔ ma ƒomevi ke na srɔ̃a si nye Egipte Fiagã vinyɔnu la hã.

english_verse: From the foundation all the way to the top, these buildings and the courtyard were made out of the best stones carefully cut to size, then smoothed on every side with saws.
translation_verse: Kpe xɔasi siwo wofú ɖe dzidzeme nu eye wotsɔ laxalaxa sẽ wo me kple wo kɔgo la wotsɔ tu wo katã, tso egɔme va se ɖe daɖedziwo gbɔ, tso gota va se ɖe xɔxɔnu gãtɔ la gbɔ.

english_verse: The caps were decorated with seven rows of designs that looked like chains,
translation_verse: Etsɔ akɔbli lɔ̃ gaɖɔ ƒomevi aɖewo ɖe taawo ŋu, gatsɔ akɔbli wɔ kɔsɔkɔsɔ suesue aɖewo siwo wolɔ̃ to wo nɔewo me la hã ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: Hiram was a skilled bronze worker from the city of Tyre. His father was now dead, but he also had been a bronze worker from Tyre, and his mother was from the tribe of Naphtali. King Solomon asked Hiram to come to Jerusalem and make the bronze furnishings to use for worship in the Lord's temple, and he agreed to do it.
translation_verse: Enye ahosi aɖe si tso Naftali-toa me la viŋutsu. Tɔ́a nye Tirotɔ, ame si nye akɔblinutula. Nunya, nugɔmesese kple aɖaŋu geɖe le tagbɔ nɛ, eye wòbi ɖe akɔbliɖaŋudɔ vovovowo wɔwɔ me. Eva fia Salomo gbɔ eye wòwɔ eƒe dɔwo katã nɛ. Akɔblisɔti dzɔtsu eveawo (Kron II,

english_verse: For the top of each column, he also made a bronze cap just over two meters high.
translation_verse: Xiram tsɔ akɔbli wɔ nane si de nɔnɔ ge mligo abe ta ene la na sɔti ɖe sia ɖe hetsɔ ɖo atsyɔ̃ nɛ. Ta sia kɔ meta eve kple afã.

english_verse: with two rows of designs that looked like pomegranates.
translation_verse: Egawɔ yevuboɖa gbaka eve ɖe gaɖɔawo ŋu kpe ɖo le sɔtiawo tame.

english_verse: The caps for the columns of the porch were almost two meters high and were shaped like lilies.
translation_verse: Ewɔ sɔti siwo le akpataa me ya ƒe tawo ɖe dzogbenya ƒe nɔnɔme me, eye le afi sia ya la, ta ɖe sia ɖe kɔ meta eve ko.

english_verse: The chain designs on the caps were right above the rounded tops of the two columns, and there were
translation_verse: Ta ɖeka le sɔti ɖe sia ɖe nu, le sɔtia ƒe afi aɖe si wowɔ wòdo gɔ̃ɔ kpe ɖo la tame. Wowɔ yevuboɖa ƒe tata alafa eve ɖe gbaka eve me ƒo xlã ta ɖe sia ɖe.

english_verse: Hiram placed the two columns on each side of the main door of the temple. The column on the south side was called Jachin, and the one on the north was called Boaz.
translation_verse: Xiram tu sɔti eveawo ɖe wo nɔƒewo le akpata si me nàto hafi age ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒeme la ŋkume. Ɖeka le ɖusime, eye evelia le miame. Eyɔ ɖusimetɔ be Yarin, eye wòyɔ miametɔ be Boaz.

english_verse: The bowl itself sat on top of twelve bronze bulls with three bulls facing outward in each of four directions.
translation_verse: Gazɔ la le nyitsu wui eve ƒe dzime. Etɔ̃ dze ŋgɔ dzigbeme, etɔ̃ dze ŋgɔ ɣetoɖoƒe, etɔ̃ dze ŋgɔ anyigbeme, eye etɔ̃ dze ŋgɔ ɣedzeƒe. Ale nyitsuawo wɔ to, wo katã trɔ agɔnugbɔ ɖo ɖe toa me.

english_verse: Hiram made pans for hot ashes, and also shovels and sprinkling bowls. A List of Everything inside the Temple (
translation_verse: Xiram wɔ gazewo, sofiwo kple ametagbɛwo hã tsɔ wu dɔ siwo fia Salomo dɔe be wòawɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ŋu la nu siwo nye:

english_verse: Hiram made ten movable bronze stands, each one over a meter high, almost two meters long, and almost two meters wide.
translation_verse: Eyome Xiram tsɔ akɔbli wɔ anyinɔ ewo siwo dome ɖe sia ɖe didi meta ɖeka sentimeta enyi, keke meta ɖeka sentimeta enyi, kɔ meta ɖeka sentimeta etɔ̃.

english_verse: The sides were made with panels attached to frames decorated with flower designs. The panels themselves were decorated with figures of lions, bulls, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: Woɖe dzatawo, nyitsuwo kple kerubiwo ɖe ga gbadzɛawo dzi, eye woɖe seƒoƒokawo ƒe tatawo ɖe dzataawo kple nyitsuawo tame kple wo te hã.

english_verse: and looked like chariot wheels. The axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were made out of bronze.
translation_verse: Wowɔ afɔtiawo abe ale si ko tasiaɖam ŋutɔ ƒe afɔti nɔna ene. Hekpe ɖe esia ŋuti la, ɖe wokɔ̀ woƒe afɔtitrogakpowo, afɔtimetsogawo kple afɔtimetsogakpeƒewo katã.

english_verse: and the stands were decorated with flower designs and figures of lions, palm trees, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: Wogaɖe kerubiwo, dzatawo kple detiwo ɖe afi siwo keŋ nu siawo ate ŋu akpɔ teƒe le ko la, eye wowɔ seƒoƒokawo ƒo xlã wo.

english_verse: Hiram made the ten bronze stands from the same mold, so they were exactly the same size and shape.
translation_verse: Aleae wowɔ anyinɔ ewoawoe. Wo katã la: nɔnɔme ɖeka, dzidzeme ɖeka kple dzedzeme ɖekae li na wo.

english_verse: Hiram also made ten small bronze bowls, one for each stand. The bowls were almost two meters across and could hold about
translation_verse: Xiram wɔ akɔbligago gã ewo na anyinɔ ewoawo eye wòtsɔ ɖeka de ɖe sia ɖe me. Gagoa nu keke meta ɖeka sentimeta enyi, tsi lita alafa enyi ayɔe.

english_verse: He put five stands on the south side of the temple, five stands on the north side, and the large bowl at the southeast corner of the temple.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ atɔ̃ ɖo anyinɔ atɔ̃ siwo le xɔa ƒe anyigbeme la me, tsɔ atɔ̃ mamlɛawo ɖo anyinɔ atɔ̃ siwo le dzigbeme la hã me, eye wotsɔ zɔ gã tegblẽ la ya ɖo dzogoe me le anyigbeme ɣedzeƒe gome. Nu siwo katã Xiram wɔ (Kron II,
