translation_verse: Esia nye nya le dzizizidɔ si fia Salomo ɖo amewo dzi tsɔ tu Aƒetɔ ƒe xɔ la, eya ŋutɔ ƒe xɔ kple Milo la eye wòɖo gli ɖe Yerusalem, Xazor, Megido kple Gezer ŋu la nye esi:

english_verse: Earlier, the king of Egypt had captured the town of Gezer; he burned it to the ground and killed the Canaanite people living there. Then he gave it to his daughter as a wedding present when she married Solomon.
translation_verse: Tsã la, Gezer nye Kanaantɔwo ƒe du; ke Egipte Fiagã va dze edzi, wu emenɔlawo katã eye wotɔ dzoe. Emegbe, esi Egipte Fiagã vinyɔnu va ɖe fia Salomo la, tɔ́a tsɔ Gezer-du la nae abe eƒe srɔ̃ɖegbe ƒe nunana ene.

english_verse: So Solomon had the town rebuilt. Solomon ordered his workers to rebuild Lower Beth-Horon,
translation_verse: Ale Salomo gbugbɔ Gezer-dua tso. Egbugbɔ Anyigbe Bet-Xoron

english_verse: They also built towns where he could keep his supplies and his chariots and horses. Solomon ordered them to build whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and anywhere in his kingdom.
translation_verse: Salomo tso nudzraɖoƒedu siwo katã nɔ esi la; etso duwo na eƒe tasiaɖamwo, duwo na eƒe sɔwo kple nu sia nu si wòdi be yeatu le Yerusalem, Lebanon kple anyigba siwo katã le eƒe dziɖuƒe me la.

english_verse: Solomon's wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt, moved from the older part of Jerusalem to her new palace. Then Solomon had the land on the east side of Jerusalem filled in.
translation_verse: Ke Egipte Fiagã vinyɔnu la dzo le David ƒe du la me, eye wòyi eya ŋutɔ ƒe aƒe si Salomo tso nɛ la me. Salomo ye tu Milo la.

english_verse: Three times a year, Solomon burned incense and offered sacrifices to the Lord on the altar he had built. Solomon had now finished building the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Ƒe sia ƒe la, Salomo saa numemevɔ kple ŋutifafavɔ na Aƒetɔ zi etɔ̃, le vɔsamlekpui si wòɖi na Aƒetɔ la dzi, eye wòtɔa dzo lifi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Ale Salomo wu xɔ la nu.

english_verse: He also had a lot of ships at Ezion-Geber, a town in Edom near Eloth on the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Tɔdziʋuwo hã nɔ Salomo si le Ezeon-Geber le Aƒlaƒu-ƒuta si te ɖe Elon ŋu le Edomtɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: King Hiram let some of his experienced sailors go to the country of Ophir with Solomon's own sailors, and they brought back about
translation_verse: Woku ʋuawo yi Ofir ɖalɔ sika si wu kilo akpe wui ene la tso afi ma vɛ na Salomo.

english_verse: The Queen was amazed at Solomon's wisdom. She was breathless when she saw his palace, the food on his table, his officials, his servants in their uniforms, the people who served his food, and the sacrifices he offered at the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: nuɖuɖu siwo tɔgbe vaa eƒe kplɔ̃ dzi, eƒe dɔlawo ƒe nɔƒewo, eƒe dɔlawo ƒe subɔsubɔ, awu siwo tɔgbe eƒe subɔlawo do, eƒe ahakulawo kple numemevɔsa siwo wòwɔna le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me la, gbɔgblɔ bu ɖee.

english_verse: She said: Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done.
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ na fia Salomo be: “Nya siwo mese le mía de le wò nunya kple nu siwo keŋ nèwɔ ŋu la nye nyateƒe.

english_verse: But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are wiser and richer than I was told.
translation_verse: Ke nyemexɔ wo dzi se o va se ɖe esime meva afi sia va kpɔ nuawo kple ŋku. Le nyateƒe me la, womegblɔ woƒe afã gɔ̃ nam o. Wò nunya kple kesinɔnuwo gbɔ ale si woƒo nu tso wo ŋu nam la ta sãa.

english_verse: Your wives and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
translation_verse: A! Srɔ̃wòwo tɔ me nyo loo! Wò subɔla siwo nɔa tsitre ɖe gbɔwò enuenu eye wosea wò nunya la tɔ me nyo loo!

english_verse: He was the richest and wisest king in the world.
translation_verse: Fia Salomo ƒo anyigba dzi fiawo katã ta le nunɔamesi kple nunya gome.

english_verse: The merchants and traders, as well as the kings of Arabia and rulers from Israel, also gave him gold.
translation_verse: Ke womebu nudzralawo, asitsala gãwo, Arabia-fiawo katã kple anyigbadzikpɔlawo tɔ ɖe eme o.

english_verse: His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold.
translation_verse: Salomo na wokpa nyiɖufiazikpui gã aɖe hã nɛ, eye wofa sika nyuitɔ ɖe eŋu katã kloe.

english_verse: Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
translation_verse: Tɔdziʋuwo nɔ fia Salomo si. Ʋu siawo kple Xiram tɔwo dea didiƒenyigbawo dzi. Le ƒe etɔ̃ sia ƒe etɔ̃ megbe la, wokua sika, klosalo, nyiɖu, kesewo kple yevutsaxewo gbɔnɛ.

english_verse: People from every nation wanted to hear the wisdom God had given him.
translation_verse: Le xexea me ƒe afi sia afi la, amewo dina be yewoayi egbɔ aɖase eƒe nunya si Mawu de susu me nɛ la ɖa.

english_verse: Year after year people came and brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, or mules.
translation_verse: Ƒè sia ƒè la, amewo tsɔa nunanawo abe klosalonuwo, sikanuwo, awuwo, kotoklobo, atike ʋeʋẽewo, sɔwo kple tedzisɔwo ene ɖe asi vanɛ nɛ.

english_verse: While he was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as ordinary sycamore trees in the foothills.
translation_verse: Fia Salomo na klosalo bɔ ɖe Yerusalem abe kpe ene, eye wòna sedertiwo xɔ afi sia afi abe ale si sikamortiwo bɔ ɖe bali me ene.

english_verse: Solomon also worshiped Astarte the goddess of Sidon, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Elabe Salomo de asi Sidontɔwo ƒe nyɔnumawu Astarte kple Amontɔwo ƒe ŋunyɔnu Milkom subɔsubɔ me.

english_verse: Solomon's father had obeyed the Lord with all his heart, but Solomon disobeyed and did what the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Ale Salomo wɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume; melé Aƒetɔ ƒe se la me ɖe asi kplikpaa abe ale si tɔ́a David wɔ ene o.

english_verse: Solomon built shrines on a hill east of Jerusalem to worship Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Molech the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Tete Salomo tu nuxeƒe na Kemos, si nye Moabtɔwo ƒe ŋunyɔnu kple Molex si nye Amon viwo ƒe ŋunyɔnu ɖe to dzi le Yerusalem ƒe ɣedzeƒe.

english_verse: In fact, he built a shrine for each of his foreign wives, so all of them could burn incense and offer sacrifices to their own gods.
translation_verse: Ewɔ esia na srɔ̃a siwo katã nye dzronyɔnuwo, ame siwo tɔa dzo lifi eye wosaa vɔ na wo demawuwo la.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel had appeared to Solomon two times and warned him not to worship foreign gods. But Solomon disobeyed and did it anyway. This made the Lord very angry,
translation_verse: Togbɔ be Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la de se nɛ be negasubɔ mawu bubuwo o hã la, mewɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe sedede la dzi o.

english_verse: and he said to Solomon: You did what you wanted and not what I told you to do. Now I'm going to take your kingdom from you and give it to one of your officials.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Salomo be: “Esi nu sia tɔgbe le tame na wò, eye mèlé nye nubabla kple nye ɖoɖo siwo megblɔ na wò la me ɖe asi o la, eya ta madu fiaɖuƒe la ɖa le asiwò atsɔ na wò dɔla.

english_verse: But because David was your father, you will remain king as long as you live. I will wait until your son becomes king, then I will take the kingdom from him.
translation_verse: Ɖe mebe mawɔe le wò ŋutɔ ŋkuwò me hafi, gake le tɔ́wò David ta nyemawɔe le wò agbenɔɣi o. Ke boŋ madui le viwò ŋutsu ƒe asi me.

english_verse: When I do, I will still let him rule one tribe, because I have not forgotten that David was my servant and Jerusalem is my chosen city. Hadad Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: Nyemadu fiaɖuƒe la katã le esi o. Le nye dɔla David kple Yerusalem, du si metia tsɔ wɔ nye ŋutɔ nye du ta la, magblẽ Israel ƒe to ɖeka ɖe esi me.” Salomo ƒe futɔwo

english_verse: Hadad was from the royal family of Edom, and here is how the Lord made him Solomon's enemy:
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ na Edomtɔ aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Hadad la zu futɔ helihelĩ na Salomo. Etso Edom fiaƒome me.

english_verse: Hadad and his wife had a son named Genubath, and the queen let the boy grow up in the palace with her own children.
translation_verse: Nyɔnu sia dzi ŋutsuvi na Hadad. Wotsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Genubat. Taxpenes na wonyii le Egipte Fiagã la ƒe fiasã me le fia ŋutɔ viwo dome.

english_verse: When Hadad heard that David and Joab were dead, he said to the king, “Your Majesty, please let me go back to my own country.”
translation_verse: Ke esi Hadad va se be fia David ku, eye David ƒe aʋakplɔla Yoab hã ku la, eyi ɖagblɔ na Egipte Fiagã la be: “Fia, ɖe mɔ nam ne matrɔ yi aƒe.”

english_verse: Here is how God made Rezon son of Eliada an enemy of Solomon: Rezon had run away from his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah.
translation_verse: Mawu gaɖo futɔ gã bubu aɖe na Salomo. Eyae nye Rezon, Elyada vi, ame si sí tso eƒe aƒetɔ Zoba-fia Hadadezer gbɔ,

english_verse: He formed his own small army and became its leader after David had defeated Hadadezer's troops. Then Rezon and his army went to Damascus, where he became the ruler of Syria and an enemy of Israel. Both Hadad and Rezon were enemies of Israel while Solomon was king, and they caused him a lot of trouble. The Lord Makes a Promise to Jeroboam
translation_verse: Enye Israel ƒe futɔ le Salomo ƒe ŋkekewo katã me henɔ nu vlo wɔm abe Hadad ene. Elé fu Israel, eye wòɖu fia ɖe Siria dzi. Ŋugbe si Mawu do na Yerobeam

english_verse: Jeroboam was from the town of Zeredah in Ephraim. His father Nebat had died, but his mother Zeruah was still alive. Jeroboam was one of Solomon's officials, but even he rebelled against Solomon.
translation_verse: Fia Salomo ƒe futɔ helihelĩ ɖeka hãe nye Yerobeam, Nebat vi, ame si nye Salomo ŋumewo dometɔ ɖeka tsã hafi. Etso Efrayim-du aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Zerada la me. Nɔa nye ahosi, eŋkɔe nye Zerua.

english_verse: Here is how it happened: While Solomon's workers were filling in the land on the east side of Jerusalem and repairing the city walls,
translation_verse: Nu si he masɔmasɔ va eya kple Salomo dome nye be: Salomo tu Milo la, eye wòxe tɔ́a David ƒe du la ƒe ʋe.

english_verse: Solomon noticed that Jeroboam was a hard worker. So he put Jeroboam in charge of the work force from Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Yerobeam hã nye ŋutsu si ŋu ŋutete le, eye esi Salomo kpɔ be ɖekakpui la doa vevie dɔ ta la, etsɔe ɖo dzizizidɔwo katã nu le Yosef ƒe aƒe la me.

english_verse: One day when Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem, he met Ahijah, a prophet from Shiloh. No one else was anywhere around. Suddenly, Ahijah took off his new coat and ripped it into twelve pieces.
translation_verse: Tete Axiya lé awu ʋlaya yeye si le eŋu la, dzee kakɛkakɛ ɖe akpa wui eve me,

english_verse: But Solomon will still rule one tribe, since he is the son of David my servant, and Jerusalem is my chosen city.
translation_verse: Le nye dɔla David kple le Yerusalem-du si metia le Israel-nyigba blibo la dzi be wòanye nye ŋutɔ nye du ta, to ɖeka asusɔ nɛ.

english_verse: “Solomon and the Israelites are not like their ancestor David. They will not listen to me, obey me, or do what is right. They have turned from me to worship Astarte the goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Nu si ta mawɔ esia lae nye be Israelviwo gblẽm ɖi, yi ɖale ta dem agu na Sidontɔwo ƒe nyɔnumawu Astarte, Moabtɔwo ƒe mawu Kemos kple Amontɔwo ƒe mawu Milkom. Salomo gbe toɖoɖom; ewɔ nuvɔ̃. Mezɔ ɖe nye sewo kple ɖoɖowo nu abe tɔ́a David ene o.

english_verse: “Solomon is David's son, and David was my chosen leader, who did what I commanded. So I will let Solomon be king until he dies.
translation_verse: Ke nyemaxɔ fiaɖuƒea katã le esi o. Ŋkeke ale si wòle agbe la, mana wòanɔ fiazikpuia dzi. Mawɔ esia le nye dɔla David, ame si metia, eye wòwɔ nye sewo dzi, zɔ ɖe nye ɖoɖowo nu la ta.

english_verse: Then I will give you ten tribes to rule,
translation_verse: Gake maxɔ fiaɖuƒea le via si, eye matsɔ eme to ewo na wò.

english_verse: but Solomon's son will still rule one tribe. This way, my servant David will always have a descendant ruling in Jerusalem, the city where I have chosen to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Matsɔ to ɖeka ana via be akaɖi nasusɔ ɖi na David le ŋkunye me ŋkekeawo katã le Yerusalem, du si metia na ɖokuinye be matsɔ nye ŋkɔ aɖo eme la ta.

english_verse: “You will be king of Israel and will rule every nation you want.
translation_verse: Eya ta, meɖo wò be nàɖu fia ɖe nu sia nu si dze ŋuwò la dzi eye nàɖui ɖe Israel dzi.

english_verse: I'll help you if you obey me. And if you do what I say, as my servant David did, I will always let someone from your family rule in Israel, just as someone from David's family will always rule in Judah. The nation of Israel will be yours.
translation_verse: Ne èɖo tom le nu sia nu me, zɔ ɖe nye sewo nu, eye nèwɔ nye ɖoɖowo katã dzi heto ema me na mekpɔ ŋudzedze le ŋuwò, abe ale si mekpɔ ŋudzedze le nye dɔla David ŋu ene la, manɔ kpli wò ɣeawo katã ɣi. Maɖo fia wò ɖe Israel nu, eye makpɔ gbɔ be wò dzidzimeviwo ɖu fia ɖe yowòme abe ale si mewɔe na David ene.

english_verse: “I will punish the descendants of David, but not forever.”
translation_verse: Mahe to na David ƒe dzidzimeviwo le esia ta, ke manye tegbee o.’ ”

english_verse: Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the book about him and his wisdom.
translation_verse: Salomo ŋutinya susɔea, nu siwo katã wòwɔ kple eƒe nunya ŋu nya la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Salomo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: he died and was buried there in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_verse: Salomo ku eye woɖii ɖe tɔ́a David ƒe du la me. Via Rexabeam ɖu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: But the people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said,
translation_verse: Tete wodɔ ame ɖo ɖee woɖayɔe vɛ. Tete Yerobeam kple Israel ƒe ameha la katã va eye wogblɔ na Rexabeam be:

english_verse: “Give me three days to think about it,” Rehoboam replied, “then come back for my answer.” So the people left.
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Miyi ne miatrɔ va le ŋkeke etɔ̃ megbe.” Ale wodzo.

english_verse: Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
translation_verse: Tete Rexabeam yɔ tɔ́a Salomo ƒe adaŋudelawo ƒo ƒu, eye wòbia wo be: “Aɖaŋu kae miaɖo nam ne matsɔ aɖo nya ŋu na dukɔ sia?”

english_verse: They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should do what they ask today. Tell them you will make their work easier.”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Ne ànye subɔla na dukɔ sia egbe, asubɔ wo, eye nèƒo nu na wo nyuie tsɔ ɖo nya ŋu na wo la, ekema woasubɔ wò tegbee.”

english_verse: But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials.
translation_verse: Gake fiaa gbe ame tsitsiawo ƒe aɖaŋu si woɖo nɛ la, eye wòde adaŋu kple ɖekakpui siwo tsi kplii hele eŋu azɔ la.

english_verse: He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
translation_verse: Ebia wo be: “Ŋuɖoɖo ka miadi be míana dukɔ sia si va tum gblɔ be: ‘Ka kɔkuti si tɔ́wò ɖo mía dzi la dzi ɖe na mí?’ ”

english_verse: He spoke bluntly and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: abe ale si eƒe ɖekakpuimezɔhɛawo gblɔ nɛ ene. Egblɔ na wo be: “Tɔ́nye na miaƒe kɔkuti kpe; nye la, mana miaƒe kɔkuti la nakpe ɖe edzi. Tɔ́nye la, atam wòtsɔ ƒo mi; nye la, nye ameƒoti anɔ abe dziɖegbetéame ene!”

english_verse: When the Israelites heard that Jeroboam was back, they called everyone together. Then they sent for Jeroboam and made him king of Israel. Only the people from the tribe of Judah remained loyal to David's family. Shemaiah Warns Rehoboam (
translation_verse: Esi Israelviawo se be Yerobeam trɔ gbɔ la, wogava ƒo ƒu, eye wodɔ ame ɖee. Eva, eye wolée ɖo fia ɖe Israel-dukɔ blibo la nu. Aleae Israelviwo gbe be David ƒe ƒome la megaɖu fia ɖe yewo dzi o; negbe Yuda-to dzaa koe. Semaya ƒe nyagblɔɖi (Kron II,

english_verse: After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and take control of the whole country. So he called together
translation_verse: Esi Rexabeam trɔ va ɖo Yerusalem la, eƒo eƒe aʋawɔla tiatia akpe alafa ɖeka bla enyi nu ƒu tso Yuda-to kple Benyamin-to me, be yeayi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Israel-fiaɖuƒea ƒe dzigbemetɔwo agbugbɔ wo va yeƒe ŋusẽ te.

english_verse: Meanwhile, God told Shemaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Gake Mawu dɔ gbeƒãɖela Semaya

english_verse: to give Rehoboam and everyone from Judah and Benjamin this warning:
translation_verse: be neyi ɖagblɔ na Rexabeam kple Yuda-to la me tɔwo kpakple Benyamin-to la me tɔwo katã be:

english_verse: “Don't go to war against the people from Israel—they are your relatives. Go home! I am the Lord, and I made these things happen.” Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord and went home. Jeroboam Makes Religious Changes
translation_verse: “Migaho yi ɖawɔ aʋa kple mia nɔvi Israelviwo o. Nye ŋutɔe na nu siawo le me vam. Ame sia ame negbugbɔ yi eƒeme.” Wo katã wose Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe, eye wotrɔ yi aƒe abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ ene. Yerobeam de megbe tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ

english_verse: Jeroboam rebuilt Shechem in Ephraim and made it a stronger town, then he moved there. He also fortified the town of Penuel.
translation_verse: Emegbe la, Yerobeam gbugbɔ Sixem-du la tso wòzu du sesẽ. Egbugbɔe tso ɖe enɔƒe xoxoa le Efrayim-to dzi eye wònɔ afi ma. Etso le afi ma, yi ɖatsò Penuel.

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam started thinking, “Everyone in Israel still goes to the temple in Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the Lord. What if they become loyal to David's family again? They will kill me and accept Rehoboam as their king.”
translation_verse: Ne dukɔ sia le Yerusalem yim ɖale vɔ sam le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒeme la, ekema dukɔ sia ƒe dzi agatrɔ ɖe woƒe aƒetɔ Rexabeam Yuda-fia ŋu, eye woawum agbugbɔ ayi Rexabeam Yuda-fia gbɔ.”

english_verse: Jeroboam asked for advice and then made two gold statues of calves. He showed them to the people and said, “Listen everyone! You won't have to go to Jerusalem to worship anymore. Here are your gods who rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Esi wòbu nya sia ŋu ʋuu la, susu aɖe va nɛ: ewɔ sikanyivi eve, eye wògblɔ na eteviawo be: “Miaƒe Yerusalem dede la va glo azɔ. Israelviwo, miaƒe mawu siwo kplɔ mi dzoe le Egipte tsɔ va afi sia la woe nye esiawo!”

english_verse: The people sinned because they started going to these places to worship.
translation_verse: To esia me la, ena ameawo wɔ nuvɔ̃, be ɖewo yina ɖasubɔna le Betel, eye ɖewo hã yina ɖasubɔna le keke Dan ke.

english_verse: Jeroboam built small places of worship at the shrines and appointed men who were not from the tribe of Levi to serve as priests.
translation_verse: Yerobeam tu nuxeƒexɔwo eye wòtia amewo tso ƒome ɖe sia ɖe me, menye tso Levi ƒomewo ɖeɖe ko me o, tsɔ ɖo nunɔlawoe. Subɔsubɔ le Betel medze o

english_verse: He also decided to start a new festival for the Israelites on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, just like the one in Judah. On that day, Jeroboam went to Bethel and offered sacrifices on the altar to the gold calf he had put there. Then he assigned the priests their duties.
translation_verse: Ede vɔsamlekpui si wòɖi ɖe Betel le dzinu enyilia ƒe ŋkeke wui atɔ̃a gbe la dzi. Eɖo ŋkeke sia le eya ŋutɔ ɖokui si eye wòɖoe wònye ŋkekenyui na Israel-dukɔ la; ede vɔsamlekpuia dzi be yeatɔ dzo lifi.

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam was standing at the altar in Bethel, ready to make an offering. Suddenly one of God's prophets arrived from Judah and shouted: The Lord sent me with a message about this altar. A child named Josiah will be born into David's family. He will sacrifice on this altar the priests who make offerings here, and human bones will be burned on it.
translation_verse: Ŋutsua do ɣli ɖe vɔsamlekpuia ta le Aƒetɔ ƒe nya nu be: “O vɔsamlekpui, vɔsamlekpui! Aƒetɔ be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa, wole ŋutsuvi aɖe dzi ge le David ƒe ƒome la me; eŋkɔ anye Yosiya. Eya atsɔ nuxeƒe sia ƒe nunɔla siwo tɔa dzo lifi le dziwò la asa vɔe le dziwò. Woatɔ dzo ameƒuwo gɔ̃ hã le dziwò.’ ”

english_verse: You will know that the Lord has said these things when the altar splits in half, and the ashes on it fall to the ground.
translation_verse: Egblɔ dzesi ɖi gbe ma gbe ke be: “Dzesi si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nye esi: ‘Kpɔ ɖa, woagbã vɔsamlekpui la eye dzofi si le edzi la woakɔe ɖe anyi.”

english_verse: “Come home with me and eat something,” Jeroboam said. “I want to give you a gift for what you have done.”

english_verse: “No, I wouldn't go with you, even if you offered me half of your kingdom. I won't eat or drink here either.
translation_verse: Mawu ƒe ame la gblɔ be: “Ne ètsɔ wò aƒe la ƒe afã nam hã la, nyemayi kpli wò o. Nyemaɖu nu alo ano tsi le afi sia o.

translation_verse: Egblɔ na viawo be: “Mibla akpa na tedzia nam.” Wobla akpa na tedzia eye wòde edzi.

translation_verse: Egblɔ nɛ be: “Va míyi aƒeme ne nade asi nu me.”

translation_verse: Yuda gbeƒãɖela la xɔ edzi be: “Ao, nyemate ŋu atrɔ yi megbe o; nyemayi wò aƒeme o, eye nyemaɖu nu alo ano tsi le gbɔwò o,

english_verse: The old prophet said, “I'm a prophet too. One of the Lord's angels told me to take you to my house and give you something to eat and drink.” The prophet from Judah did not know that the old prophet was lying,
translation_verse: Gake gbeƒãɖela tsitsi la xɔ edzi nɛ be: “Nye hã gbeƒãɖela menye abe wò ke ene. Aƒetɔ na mawudɔla aɖe gblɔ nam be: ‘Yi ɖagbugbɔe va wò aƒeme ne wòaɖu nu eye wòano tsi. Evɔ wònye alakpae gbeƒãɖela tsitsi la da nɛ.

english_verse: a message for the prophet from Judah: Listen to the Lord's message. You have disobeyed the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Tete wòdo ɣli gblɔ na Mawu ƒe ame si tso Yuda va la be: “Aƒetɔ be: ‘Esi nègbe toɖoɖo Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe, eye mèlé se si Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu de na wò la me ɖe asi o,

english_verse: He told you not to eat or drink anything here, but you came home and ate with me. And so, when you die, your body won't be buried in your family tomb.
translation_verse: ke boŋ ètrɔ gbɔ eye nèɖu nu, no tsi le afi si ŋu wòde se na wò le be: Mègaɖu nu o, eye mègano tsi le o la, womaɖi wò kukua ɖe tɔgbuiwòwo ƒe ɖiƒe o.’ ”

translation_verse: Esime wòɖu nu no nu vɔ la, gbeƒãɖela tsitsi la bla akpa na gbeƒãɖela si wòtrɔ gbɔe la ƒe tedzi,

english_verse: and the prophet from Judah left. Along the way, a lion attacked and killed him, and the donkey and the lion stood there beside his dead body.

english_verse: Some people walked by and saw the body with the lion standing there. They ran into Bethel, telling everyone what they had seen.
translation_verse: Ŋutsu aɖewo va yina kasia, ame kukue nye esi le mɔƒo me, dzata le tsitre ɖe egbɔ. Woyi ɖaka nya sia ta le du si me gbeƒãɖela tsitsia le la.

english_verse: When the old prophet heard the news, he said, “That must be the prophet from Judah. The Lord warned him, but he disobeyed. So the Lord sent a lion to kill him.”
translation_verse: Esi gbeƒãɖela, si ɖagbugbɔe tso mɔta vɛ la se nyaa la, egblɔ be: “Eya nye Mawu ƒe ame si gbe Aƒetɔ ƒe nya dzi wɔwɔ, eye Aƒetɔ tsɔe de asi na dzata wòvuvu hewu le Aƒetɔ ƒe nya si wogblɔ nɛ la nu.”

english_verse: The old prophet picked up the body, put it on his own donkey, and took it back to Bethel, so he could bury it and mourn for the prophet from Judah.
translation_verse: Gbeƒãɖela tsitsi la kɔ ame kukua ɖo tedzia dzi tsɔ va dua me be wòafa nɛ, eye wòaɖii.

translation_verse: Eɖii ɖe yɔdo si wòɖe ɖi na eɖokui hafi la me, eye wofae gblɔ be: “Ao, nɔvinye!”
