english_verse: But Jeroboam kept on doing evil things. He appointed men to be priests at the local shrines, even if they were not Levites. In fact, anyone who wanted to be a priest could be one.
translation_verse: Le nya siawo katã megbe hã, Yerobeam metrɔ tso eƒe mɔ vɔ̃wo dzi o, ke boŋ egaɖo dukɔ la ƒe ame sia ame ƒomevi nuxeƒe nunɔlae. Ame sia ame ƒomevi si be yeazu nunɔla ko, eɖonɛ nuxeƒe nunɔlae.

english_verse: This sinful thing led to the downfall of his kingdom.
translation_verse: Nu sia zu nuvɔ̃ na Yerobeam ƒe aƒe, esi na be woɖee ɖa eye wotsrɔ̃e ɖa le anyigba dzi.

english_verse: About the same time, Abijah son of Jeroboam got sick.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, Yerobeam vi, Abiya, dze dɔ.

english_verse: But when Ahijah heard her walking up to the door, he said: Come in! I know you're Jeroboam's wife—why are you pretending to be someone else? I have some bad news for you.
translation_verse: Gake esi Axiya se eƒe afɔzi le mɔa nu ko la, egblɔ be: “Ge ɖe eme, Yerobeam srɔ̃. Nu ka ta nètrɔ ɖokuiwò ame bubui? Elabe nye la, wode nya vɔ̃ nu nam be magblɔ na wò.

english_verse: Give your husband this message from the Lord God of Israel: “Jeroboam, you know that I, the Lord, chose you over anyone else to be the leader of my people Israel.
translation_verse: Yi ɖagblɔ na Yerobeam be: ‘Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: ‘Metia wò tso dukɔa me tɔwo dome hetsɔ wò ɖo fia ɖe nye dukɔ Israel nu.

english_verse: I even took David's kingdom away from his family and gave it to you. But you are not like my servant David. He always obeyed me and did what was right.
translation_verse: Medu fiaɖuƒe la le David ƒe dzidzimeviwo si tsɔ na wò. Gake wò ya mèto nye dɔla David ƒe ʋe me o. Mèɖi anukware nam tututu, zɔ ɖe nye sewo nu pɛpɛpɛ kple wò dzi blibo, wɔ nu si nyo le ŋkunye me la ɖeɖe ko abe nye dɔla David ene o;

english_verse: “You have made me very angry by rejecting me and making idols out of gold. Jeroboam, you have done more evil things than any king before you.
translation_verse: ke boŋ èwɔ nu vlowo wu fia siwo katã do ŋgɔ na wò la sãa. Èɖo mawu bubuwo na ɖokuiwò, kɔ̀ legbawo tsɔ do dziku nam, eye nètsɔm ƒu gbe ɖe megbewò.

english_verse: “Because of this, I will destroy your family by killing every man and boy in it, whether slave or free. I will wipe out your family, just as fire burns up trash.
translation_verse: Eya ta kpɔ ɖa, mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ava Yerobeam ƒe aƒe dzi. Mawu ŋutsuwo katã le Yerobeam ƒe ƒomea me, kluviwo kple aƒeviwo siaa le Israel. Matsrɔ̃ Yerobeam ƒe aƒe ɖa keŋkeŋ abe ale si wotɔa dzo gbeɖuɖɔ wòfiãna keŋkeŋ ene.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel will mourn at his funeral. But he will be the last one from Jeroboam's family to receive a proper burial, because he's the only one the Lord God of Israel is pleased with.
translation_verse: Israel blibo la afae, eye woaɖii. Eya ɖeka koe lanye ame tso Yerobeam ƒe ƒome me si woaɖi ɖe yɔdo me, elabe eya ɖeka dzaa ko ŋu Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu, kpɔ ŋudzedze le.

english_verse: The Lord will soon choose a new king of Israel, who will destroy Jeroboam's family. And I mean very soon.
translation_verse: Gawu la, Aƒetɔ aɖo fia aɖe na eɖokui ɖe Israel dzi, ame si aɖe Yerobeam ƒe aƒe ɖa gbidii egbe.

english_verse: years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon.
translation_verse: Tete Yerobeam srɔ̃ tso, eye wòdzo, trɔ va Tirza. Esi wòɖo aƒea ƒe agbalinu teti ko la, ɖevia ku.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel came and mourned at his funeral, just as the Lord's servant Ahijah had said. Jeroboam Dies
translation_verse: Israel-dukɔ blibo la ɖii, eye wofae abe ale si Aƒetɔ la gblɔe to eƒe dɔla Axiya, gbeƒãɖela la dzi ene. Yerobeam ƒe ku

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including the battles he won, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Yerobeam ŋutinya susɔea, aʋa siwo wòwɔ kple ale si wòɖu fiae la, kpɔ ɖa, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: The people of Judah disobeyed the Lord and made him even angrier than their ancestors had.
translation_verse: Yuda wɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, eye wotsɔ woƒe nuvɔ̃ tsɔ do dziku na Aƒetɔ wu esi wo tɔgbuiwo wɔ tsɔ do dziku nɛ gɔ̃.

english_verse: They also built their own local shrines and stone images of foreign gods, and they set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Elabe woawo hã tu nuxeƒewo na woƒe mawuwo, wɔ aƒeliwo, eye wowɔ nyɔnumawu Asera ƒe nɔnɔme ɖe towo dzi kple ati dama ɖe sia ɖe te.

english_verse: Even worse, they allowed prostitutes at the shrines, and followed the disgusting customs of the foreign nations that the Lord had forced out of Canaan.
translation_verse: Ŋutsu nuxeƒe gbolowɔlawo hã ƒe nɔƒe le anyigba la dzi. Wokpɔ dukɔ siwo katã Aƒetɔ nyà ɖa le Israelviwo ŋgɔ la ƒe nuwɔna wɔ.

english_verse: After Rehoboam had been king for four years, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Le Rexabeam ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè atɔ̃lia me la, Egipte-fia Sisak va dze Yerusalem dzi.

english_verse: He took everything of value from the temple and the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
translation_verse: Elɔ kesinɔnu siwo katã nɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me kple fiasã la me kpakple sikakpoxɔnu siwo Salomo wɔ da ɖi la tsɔ dzoe.

english_verse: Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe.
translation_verse: Fia Rexabeam wɔ akɔblikpoxɔnuwo ɖe sikakpoxɔnuawo teƒe, eye wòtsɔ wo de asrafo siwo dzɔa fiasãa ƒe agbowo nu la ƒe amegãwo si me.

english_verse: Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he was finished.
translation_verse: Ɣe sia ɣi si fiaa gbɔna ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me la, ele be fia ŋu srafowo natsɔ akpoxɔnuawo eye wogbugbɔa wo va dana ɖe wo dzraɖoƒe.

english_verse: Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Yerobeam ƒe ŋutinya susɔea kple nu siwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Yuda-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: He and Jeroboam were constantly at war.
translation_verse: Aʋa dzi ko Rexabeam kple Yerobeam nɔ kple wo nɔewo.

english_verse: Rehoboam's mother Naamah was from Ammon, but when Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Abijam then became king.
translation_verse: Rexabeam va ku, eye woɖii ɖe tɔgbuiawo gbɔ le David ƒe du la me. Nɔa ŋkɔ nye Naama, Amon-nyɔnu. Via Abiyam zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: His own grandmother Maacah had made an idol of Asherah, and Asa took it and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
translation_verse: Eɖe nɔa Maaxa, nyɔnufia la, ɖa le zi dzi, elabe Maaxa wɔ nyɔnumawu Asera ƒe legba si nye ŋunyɔnu wòle esi la. Asa mu legba la ƒu anyi, eye wòkɔe yi ɖatɔ dzoe le Kidron-tɔʋu nu.

english_verse: Abijam became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel,
translation_verse: Le Yerobeam, Nebat vi ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè wui enyilia me la, Abiyam zu fia le Yuda.

english_verse: Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to strengthen the town of Ramah. Then he used these same stones and wood to fortify the town of Geba in the territory of Benjamin and the town of Mizpah.
translation_verse: Tete fia Asa na woyɔ Yuda-nyigba dzi tɔwo katã va Rama, eye wòna wofɔ ati kple kpe siwo Baesa lɔ va le Rama-du la tsomee la dzoe. Baesa ƒe xɔtunu siawoe Asa tsɔ tsò Geba-du, si le Benyamin kple Mizpa.

english_verse: Abijam did not truly obey the Lord his God as his ancestor David had done. Instead, he was sinful just like his father Rehoboam.
translation_verse: Enɔ agbe le nuvɔ̃ siwo katã tɔ́a wɔ va yi la me eye eƒe dzi menɔ Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu la ŋu le nyateƒe me bliboe abe tɔ́a David ƒe dzi ene o.

english_verse: David had always obeyed the Lord's commands by doing right, except in the case of Uriah. And since Abijam was David's great-grandson, the Lord kept Jerusalem safe and let Abijam have a son who would be the next king.
translation_verse: Elabe David wɔ nu si nyo le Aƒetɔ ŋkume eye meda Aƒetɔ ƒe sewo dometɔ aɖeke dzi le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo me o, negbe le Uriya, Xititɔ la ƒe nya me ko.

english_verse: Abijam died and was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Asa became king. King Asa of Judah (
translation_verse: Abiyam ku, eye woɖii ɖe David ƒe du la me. Via Asa zu fia ɖe eyome. Yuda-fia Asa (Kron II,

english_verse: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Elɔ tɔ́a ƒe nunana kɔkɔewo kple eya ŋutɔ tɔ siwo nye klosalo, sika kple ŋudɔwɔnuwo yi Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me.

english_verse: Asa was always at war with King Baasha of Israel.
translation_verse: Aʋa nɔ Yuda-fia Asa kple Israel-fia Baesa dome le woƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: Asa obeyed the Lord, as David had done.
translation_verse: Asa wɔ nu si dzè, le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, abe ale si tɔ́a David wɔ ene.

english_verse: Asa became king of Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's rule in Israel,
translation_verse: Le Israel-fia Yerobeam ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè bla evelia me la, Asa zu fia ɖe Yuda-dukɔ nu.

english_verse: He forced the prostitutes at the shrines to leave the country, and he got rid of the idols his ancestors had made.
translation_verse: Enyà ŋutsu nuxeƒe gbolowɔlawo ɖa le anyigba la dzi eye wòlɔ legba siwo katã tɔgbuiawo wɔ la ƒu gbe.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was completely faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines.
translation_verse: Ke womeɖe nuxeƒeawo ɖa o. Gake hã, Asa ƒe dzi lé ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu goŋgoŋ le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
translation_verse: Eva eme be Israel-fia Baesa ho ɖe Yuda ŋu, eye wòtsò Rama-dua ale be meɖe mɔ be ame aɖeke nagado alo ayi Yuda-fia Asa gbɔ o.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Tete Asa lɔ klosalo kple sika siwo katã susɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me gadzraɖoƒe kple esiwo susɔ ɖe fia ƒe aƒeme tsɔ de asi na eƒe dɔlawo be woatsɔ wo ayi na fia Ben-Hadad le Damasko. Fia Ben-Hadad sia nye Xesion vi, Tabrimon vi. Fia Asa gblɔ na dɔlaawo be woaɖagblɔ nɛ be:

english_verse: “Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
translation_verse: “Na nye kpli wò míabla nu abe ale si tɔ́nye kple tɔ́wò blae va yi ene. Xɔ klosalo kple sika sia; metsɔ wo na wò. Tu nu si nèbla kple Israel-fia Baesa, ne wòaho adzo le nye anyigba me.”

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, and Abel-Bethmaacah, and the territories of Chinneroth and Naphtali.
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad lɔ̃ ɖe Asa ƒe biabia la dzi, eye wòdɔ eƒe aʋakɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo ɖa woyi ɖadze Israel-duwo dzi. Woxɔ Iyon, Dan, Abel-Bet-Maaxa, Kinerot kple Naftali-nyigba la katã.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
translation_verse: Esi Baesa se esia la, edzudzɔ Rama-du la tsotso eye woɖanɔ Tirza.

english_verse: Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease.
translation_verse: Azɔ Asa ŋutinya susɔeawo katã, eƒe kalẽwɔwɔ le teƒe teƒewo kple du siwo wògbugbɔ tsò la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Yuda-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me. Esi Asa va tsi zu amegãɖeɖi la, afɔdɔléle aɖe va ɖe fu nɛ.

english_verse: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years.
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Asa ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè evelia me la, fia Yerobeam vi Nadab zu fia le Israel eye wòɖu Israel dzi ƒe eve.

english_verse: Nadab disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of his father, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, eye wòto tɔ́a ƒe ʋe me, eye wòwɔ nuvɔ̃ tsɔ kplɔ Israel de nuvɔ̃ mee.

english_verse: The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family,
translation_verse: Esi wònyazu fia teti ko la, ewu Rexabeam ƒe ƒometɔwo katã, eye mena nugbagbe aɖeke susɔ na Yerobeam o, ke boŋ etsrɔ̃ wo keŋ le Aƒetɔ ƒe nya si wògblɔ to eƒe dɔla Axiya, Silotɔ dzi la nu.

english_verse: because Jeroboam had made the Lord God of Israel angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Elabe Yerobeam ŋutɔ wɔ nuvɔ̃ geɖe, hena Israel-dukɔ la hã wɔ nuvɔ̃, eye wòwɔ nu bubuwo hã tsɔ do dziku na Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la.

english_verse: Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Nadab ŋutinya susɔea kple nu siwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war. King Baasha of Israel
translation_verse: Aʋa nɔ Yuda-fia Asa kple Israel-fia Baesa dome le woƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me. Israel-fia Baesa

english_verse: Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Asa ƒe fiaɖuɣi ƒe ƒè etɔ̃lia me la, Baesa, Axiya vi, zu fia ɖe Israel-dukɔ bliboa nu le Tirza. Enɔ zia dzi ƒe bla eve vɔ ene.

english_verse: Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Eya hã wɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Ewɔ vɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu eye wòkplɔ Israel hã de nuvɔ̃ me.

english_verse: The Lord sent Jehu son of Hanani to say to Baasha:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe va Yehu, Xanani vi, gbɔ na Baesa be:

english_verse: Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry
translation_verse: “Wò la, ʋuʋudedi me mekɔ wò tso tsɔ ɖo kplɔla ɖe nye dukɔ Israel nu, gake nèto Yerobeam ƒe ʋe me eye nèkplɔ nye dukɔ Israel de nuvɔ̃ me, ale be woƒe nuvɔ̃wo do dziku nam,

english_verse: that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam.
translation_verse: eya ta kpɔ ɖa, makplɔ Baesa kple eƒe ƒome la katã aƒu gbe abe ale si mewɔ Yerobeam, Nebat vi la, kple eƒe ƒome lae ene.

english_verse: Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Eƒe ame ɖe sia ɖe si ku la, avuwo aɖui, eye eƒe ame ɖe sia ɖe si ku le gbedzi la, dziƒoxeviwo aɖui.

english_verse: Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family! Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king. King Elah of Israel
translation_verse: Nu vɔ̃ siwo Baesa wɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu tae Aƒetɔ gblɔ ŋɔdzinya mawo na gbeƒãɖela Yehu be neyi ɖagblɔ nɛ ɖo. Menye agbe baɖa si wònɔ abe Yerobeam ene la ɖeɖe ta koe Aƒetɔ do dɔmedzoe ɖe eŋu o, ke boŋ ale si wòwu Yerobeam ƒe dzidzimeviwo katã la hã tae. Israel-fia Ela

english_verse: Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel after Asa had been king of Judah for
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Asa ƒe fiaɖuɣi ƒe ƒè bla eve vɔ adelia me la, Ela, Baesa vi, zu fia le Israel, ƒe eve le Tirza.

english_verse: Omri did more evil things than any king before him.
translation_verse: Omri wɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume wu fia siwo katã do ŋgɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah. One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister,
translation_verse: Ke eƒe dɔla Zimri si nye eƒe tasiaɖamwo ƒe afã ƒe aʋakplɔla la wɔ babla ɖe eŋu, esime wòno aha mu le eƒe fiasãdzikpɔla Arza ƒeme le Tirza.

english_verse: when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Tete Zimri ƒoe wu le aƒea me, eye wòtsɔ eɖokui ɖo fiae ɖe eteƒe, le Yuda-fia Asa ƒe fiaɖuɣi ƒe ƒè bla eve vɔ adrẽlia me.

english_verse: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed.
translation_verse: Esi Zimri yi zia dzi tetee ko la, ewu Baesa ƒe ƒometɔ, xɔlɔ̃ kple yomedzela siwo katã nye ŋutsuwo la.

english_verse: Baasha's family was completely wiped out, just as the Lord's prophet Jehu had warned.
translation_verse: Ale, abe ale si Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ gblɔe ɖi to gbeƒãɖela Yehu dzi ene la, Zimri tsrɔ̃ Baesa ƒe ƒome blibo la katã.

english_verse: Baasha and Elah sinned and caused the Israelites to sin, and they made the Lord angry by worshiping idols.
translation_verse: Nu sia va eme le esi Baesa kple via, Ela wɔ nuvɔ̃, ble Israel-dukɔ la de nuvɔ̃ me, eye wo ame eve la to ema me do dziku na Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la ta.

english_verse: Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Zimri of Israel
translation_verse: Ela ŋutinya susɔea kple nu siwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me. Israel-fia Zimri

english_verse: Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah. Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day.
translation_verse: Esi asrafoawo nɔ asaɖaa me la, wose be: “Zimri wɔ babla eye wòwu fia la.” Asrafoawo tsɔ woƒe aʋakplɔla Omri, si nɔ wo nu le asaɖaa me la ɖo fiae ɖe Israel-dukɔa nu le asaɖa la me gbe ma gbe ke.

english_verse: When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire.
translation_verse: Esi Zimri kpɔ be Omri kple etɔwo xɔ dua vɔ la, etɔ dzo fiasã la. Eyome eyi ɖale mɔ́ si wotu ɖe fiasãa titina ke la me. Dzoa bi va afi ma hã, eye wòku ɖe mɔ́a me.

english_verse: Zimri had disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Nyaawo va yi alea elabe Zimri wɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu: eya ŋutɔ nɔ agbe vlo le Aƒetɔ ŋkume abe fia Yerobeam ene, eye wòkplɔ Israel-dukɔa de nuvɔ̃ me hã.

english_verse: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
translation_verse: Zimri ŋutinya susɔea kple ale si wòwɔ babla ɖe Ela ŋu hewui la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me. Israel-fia Omri

english_verse: After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri.
translation_verse: Israel-dukɔ la ma ɖe akpa eve me: afã be yewoatsɔ Tibni, Ginat vi, aɖo fiae; akpa evelia le Omri yome.

english_verse: in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah. Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah,
translation_verse: Ƒe si me Omri zu Israel-fia aleae nye Asa, Yuda-fia ƒe ƒè bla etɔ̃ vɔ ɖekɛlia le Yuda-fiazikpui dzi. Omri ɖu fia ƒe wui eve. Le eƒe fiaɖuƒe ade gbãtɔawo me la, enɔ Tirza.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
translation_verse: Abe Yerobeam, Nebat vi, si hã ɖu fia do ŋgɔ nɛ ene la, etsɔ eƒe nuvɔ̃ wɔwɔ vivivo kple ale si wòna legbawo subɔsubɔ xɔ aƒe le dukɔa me la do dziku na Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la.

english_verse: Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Omri ŋutinya susɔea, nu siwo wòwɔ kple kalẽ si wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king. King Ahab of Israel
translation_verse: Esi wòku la, woɖii ɖe Samaria. Via ŋutsu Axab nye ame si ɖu fia ɖe eteƒe. Israel-fia Axab

english_verse: Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Asa ƒe fiaɖuƒe bla etɔ̃ vɔ enyilia me la, Axab, Omri viŋutsu zu fia ɖe Israel-dukɔ nu. Eƒe fiadue nye Samaria, eye wòɖu fia le afi ma ƒe bla eve vɔ eve.

english_verse: Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him.
translation_verse: Eƒe agbenɔnɔ vɔ̃ɖi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume wu fia siwo katã do ŋgɔ nɛ la tɔ.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nuvɔ̃ siwo katã Yerobeam, Nebat vi wɔ va yi la dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe, eye nu tsɛ ko woɖi nɛ. Etso yi ɖaɖe Sidon-fia Etbaal vinyɔnu Izebel, eye wòyi ɖasubɔ Baal, de ta agu nɛ.

english_verse: Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria
translation_verse: Etu xɔ ɖe Samaria na Baal eye wòɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe eme.

english_verse: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
translation_verse: Axab wɔ nyɔnumawu Asera hã. Ewɔ nu geɖe tsɔ do dziku na Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la wu Israel-fia siwo do ŋgɔ nɛ la dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe.

english_verse: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_verse: Axab ŋɔlie Betel-ŋutsu aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Xiel la gbugbɔ Yerixo-du tso. Abe ale si Aƒetɔ la gblɔe ɖi xoxo to Yosua, Nun vi, dzi ene la, Xiel viŋutsu tsitsitɔ, Abiram ƒe ku, wotsɔ ɖo Yerixo-dua gɔme anyii, eye esi wòtui vɔ la, via ŋutsu dɔmlɔea, Segub ƒe ku, wotsɔ de agbowo enui.

english_verse: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
translation_verse: Eliya, Tisbitɔ, si tso Tisbe le Gilead la gblɔ na Axab be: “Metà Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu ame si ŋkume mele tsitre ɖo la ƒe agbe: Zãmu alo tsi madza le ƒe siawo me o, negbe ɖe meɖe gbe na wo hafi.”

english_verse: Later, the Lord said to Elijah,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe va nɛ be:

english_verse: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: “Dzo le afi sia yi ɣedzeƒe gome, eye nàyi ɖabè ɖe Krit-tɔʋu si le Yordan ƒe ɣedzeƒe la to.

english_verse: You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
translation_verse: Nànɔ tɔʋua me tsi nom; medɔ akpaviawo be woanyi wò le afi ma.”

english_verse: Elijah obeyed the Lord and went to live near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: Ale Eliya wɔ nu si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be newɔ. Eyi ɖale Krit-tɔʋua to le Yordan ƒe ɣedzeƒe.

english_verse: Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek.
translation_verse: Akpaviawo tsɔa abolo kple lã vanɛ nɛ ŋdi kple fiẽ, eye wòyina ɖanoa tsi le tɔʋu la me.

english_verse: But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain. Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
translation_verse: Ke le ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe la, tɔʋua mie elabe tsi megale dzadzam le anyigba la dzi o. Eliya kple ahosi aɖe le Zarefat

english_verse: The Lord told Elijah,
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe va nɛ be:

english_verse: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
translation_verse: “Dzo le afii nàyi Zarefat, si nye Sidontɔwo ƒe du, ne nàɖanɔ afi ma. Kpɔ ɖa, megblɔ na ahosi aɖe si le afi ma la be nenyi wò.”

english_verse: When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked.
translation_verse: Ale Eliya dze mɔ ɖo ta Zarefat. Esi wòɖo dua ƒe agbo nu la, kpɔ ɖa, ahosi aɖe le afi ma le nake fɔm. Eyɔe gblɔ nɛ be: “Ku tsi vi aɖe ɖe nane me vɛ nam mano.”

english_verse: As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
translation_verse: Esi wòyina tsia ku ge la, eyɔe gagblɔ nɛ be: “Tsɔ abolo kakɛ aɖe hã ɖe asi vɛ.”

english_verse: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu be: “Metà Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu ƒe agbe be naneke mele mía si o, negbe wɔ asiʋlo ɖeka koe le ze me kple ami vi aɖe le goe me. Azɔ hafi mele nake wuwlui aɖewo fɔm ne mayi ɖaɖae, ne nye kple vinye míaɖu ko ne míaku.”

english_verse: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
translation_verse: Eliya xɔ edzi nɛ be: “Mègavɔ̃ o. Yi ɖawɔ nu si nèbe yeawɔ, gake tsɔ wɔa tɔ tatali vi aɖe vɛ nam gbã, emegbe hafi nàdi nane awɔ na wò ŋutɔ kple viwò.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu be: ‘Wɔzea maɖi gbɔlo o, eye ami si le goea me la hã mavɔ o, va se ɖe gbe si gbe Aƒetɔ ana tsi agadza ɖe anyigbaa dzi.’ ”

english_verse: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
translation_verse: Ahosi la yi ɖawɔ nu si Eliya gblɔ nɛ. Ale eya ŋutɔ kple ŋutsua kpakple ahosia vi wokpɔ nu ɖu ŋkeke geɖe.

english_verse: The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil. Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
translation_verse: Wɔ mevɔ le wɔzea me o, eye ami si le goea me la hã mevɔ o, le Aƒetɔ ƒe nya si wògblɔ to Eliya dzi la nu.

english_verse: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
translation_verse: Le esia megbe la, nyɔnu si nye aƒenɔa la vi va dze dɔ. Dɔa nu sesẽ ale gbegbe be gbɔgbɔ megale dɔnɔa me o.

english_verse: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
translation_verse: Tete nyɔnua bia Eliya be: “Mawu ƒe ame! Nya kae le nye kpli wò dome? Ɖe nèva be yeana woaɖo ŋku nye nuvɔ̃ dzi ne vinye nakua?”

english_verse: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Kɔ ɖevia do ɖem.” Exɔ ɖevia le nyɔnua si, kɔe yi xɔtamexɔ si wonae wòle eme mlɔm la me, eye wòtsɔe mlɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe aba dzi.

english_verse: and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.”
translation_verse: Tete wòdo ɣli gblɔ na Aƒetɔ be: “O Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu, ahosi si gbɔ meva dze la hã dzie nèhe dzɔgbevɔ̃e vɛ ale, to via wuwu mea?”

english_verse: Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
translation_verse: Tete wòdra eɖokui ɖe ɖevi la dzi zigbɔzi etɔ̃, eye wòdo ɣli gblɔ na Aƒetɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu, nà ɖevi sia ƒe agbe nagbugbɔ va eyama me.”

english_verse: The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ se Eliya ƒe gbe; ɖevi la ƒe agbe gbugbɔ va eme, eye wògbɔ agbe.

english_verse: Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
translation_verse: Eliya ɖi tso xɔtamexɔ la me kple ɖevia, eye wòtsɔe de asi na nɔa hegblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa! Viwòa gbɔ agbe!”

english_verse: “You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ale nyɔnu la gblɔ na Eliya be: “Azɔ la, medze sii be Mawu ƒe ame nènye, eye Aƒetɔ ƒe nya si le nuwò la nye nyateƒe.”

english_verse: At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid
translation_verse: Esime Izebel nɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo wum la, Obadya kplɔ wo ame alafa ɖeka yi ɖaɣla ɖe agado eve me blatɔ̃bla atɔ̃, eye wòtsɔ abolo kple tsi nyi woe.

english_verse: and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass.
translation_verse: Tete Axab gblɔ na Obadya be: “Yi ɖatsa to anyigba blibo la katã me ne nalé ŋku ɖe tsidzɔƒewo kple balimewo katã ŋu kpɔ; ɖewohĩ míakpɔ gbe le afi mawo atsɔ axɔ sɔawo kple tedziawo ɖe agbe, be ɖeke nagaku o.”

english_verse: As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”
translation_verse: Esi Obadya nɔ yiyim la kpɔ ɖa, Eliya va do goe. Obadya kpɔe dze sii, eye wòtsyɔ mo anyi gblɔ be: “Wòea, nye aƒetɔ Eliya?”

english_verse: Obadiah replied: King Ahab would kill me if I told him that. And I haven't even done anything wrong.
translation_verse: Obadya xɔ edzi nɛ be: “Nu vɔ̃ ka mewɔ hafi nèbe yeatsɔ wò dɔla ade asi na Axab ne wòawu?

english_verse: I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country.
translation_verse: Metà Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu ƒe agbe be dukɔ alo fiaɖuƒe aɖeke meli, si me nye aƒetɔ medɔ ame ɖo, be wòayi ɖadi wò le o, eye ne dukɔ aɖe me tɔwo be: ‘Mele mía gbɔ o’ la, ebiana tso wo si be woaka atam na ye be yewomekpɔ wò o.

english_verse: Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
translation_verse: Ke azɔ nèbe: ‘Yi ɖagblɔ na wò aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, Eliya le afii?’

english_verse: What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me. I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy.
translation_verse: Ko ne medzo le gbɔwò vɔ tetee ko Aƒetɔ ƒe gbɔgbɔ nakɔ wò ayi afi aɖe, le nye manyamanya me ale be ne meva gblɔ na Axab be èle afi ma, eye wòdɔ ame ɖa kasia womeva ke ɖe ŋuwò o ɖe, mawum oa? Evɔ wònye nye, wò dɔla, mevɔ̃a Aƒetɔ tso nye ɖevime ke hafi.

english_verse: Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”
translation_verse: Eliya xɔ edzi nɛ be: “Metà Aƒetɔ Aʋakɔwokplɔla la, ame si ŋkume mele tsitre ɖo la ƒe agbe be mayi aɖatsɔ ɖokuinye fiae egbe godoo.”

english_verse: Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah. Ahab went to meet Elijah,
translation_verse: Tete Obadya yi ɖagblɔe na Axab, eye Axab yi ɖado go Eliya.

english_verse: and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
translation_verse: Esi Axab kpɔ Eliya la, Axab biae be: “Wò ŋkumee nye esia? Wò Israel ƒe fuɖenametɔ la!”

english_verse: Elijah answered: You're the troublemaker—not me! You and your family have disobeyed the Lord's commands by worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Eliya ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Nyemegblẽ Israel-dukɔ dome o. Wò boŋue nye ame si gblẽ edome. Wò kple tɔgbuiwò ƒe ƒomee ɖe fu nɛ elabe miawoe ɖe asi le Aƒetɔ ƒe sededewo ŋu hedze Baalwo yome.

english_verse: Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel.
translation_verse: Ale Axab dɔ ame ɖe Israelviwo katã, eye wòƒo gbeƒãɖelaawo nu ƒu ɖe Karmel-to gbɔ.

english_verse: Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!” The people did not say a word.
translation_verse: Eliya te ɖe ameawo katã ŋu, eye wògblɔ be: “Ɣe ka ɣi koŋ miaƒe susu anɔ evedomesi ase ɖo? Nenye Aƒetɔ e nye Mawu la, midze eyome; ke nenye Baal ye la, ekema midze eyome.” Ame aɖeke meke nu o.

english_verse: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
translation_verse: Mina woatsɔ nyitsu eve vɛ na mí; mina Baal ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo natia ɖeka afli atsɔ ɖo nake dzi, gake womegade dzo nakea me o. Nye hã mafli ɖeka atsɔ aɖo nake dzi, gake nyemade dzo nakea me o.

english_verse: The prophets of Baal will pray to their god, and I will pray to the Lord. The one who answers by starting the fire is God. “That's a good idea,” everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Eyome, woado gbe ɖa na woƒe mawu, eye nye hã mado gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ. Mawu si ase gbedodoɖaa la ade dzo nakea me lae nye Mawu.” Ƒuƒoƒea katã lɔ̃ ɖe edzi be: “Nya lae nye ema.”

english_verse: Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”
translation_verse: Tete Eliya gblɔ na Baal ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo be: “Mitia nyitsuawo dometɔ ɖeka. Miesɔ gbɔ, eya ta miawo miwɔ mia tɔ gbã. Mido gbe ɖa na miaƒe mawu, ke migade dzo nakea me o!”

english_verse: They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
translation_verse: Ale wolé nyitsu si wotsɔ na wo la, trɔ asi le eŋu, eye wode asi gbedodoɖa me na Baal tso ŋdi va ɖo ŋdɔ me le gbɔgblɔm be: “O, Baal, tɔ na mí!” Ke gbe aɖeke meɖi o; ame aɖeke metɔ o. Woti kpo ƒo xlã vɔsamlekpui si woɖi.

english_verse: At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
translation_verse: Le ŋdɔ me la, Eliya de asi wo koko me. Ebe: “Mido ɣli sesĩe elabe mawu wònye! Ɖewohĩ anyale modzaka ɖem, alo eyi nugodo, alo eyi nugbe, alo edɔ alɔ̃ eye wòle be woanyɔe!”

english_verse: The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped,
translation_verse: Woƒe ɣlia gade dzi wu bobobo; wosi wo ɖokui kple yi kple akplɔ le woƒe kɔnu la nu, va se ɖe esime ʋu le ɖuɖum le wo ŋu.

english_verse: and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
translation_verse: Ɣe trɔ, gake kpao! Wole edzi, le edzi, de asi nugbenugbeewo wɔwɔ me va se ɖe esime nuɖuɖuvɔsaɣi ɖo; ke gbe aɖeke meɖi o, ame aɖeke metɔ o, eye ŋuɖoɖo aɖeke meva o.

english_verse: Elijah told everyone to gather around him while he repaired the Lord's altar.
translation_verse: Tete Eliya gblɔ na ameawo katã be: “Mite ɖe ŋunye;” eye ameawo katã te ɖe eŋu. Egbugbɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe vɔsamlekpui si wogbã la wɔ nyuie.

english_verse: He placed the wood on the altar, then they cut the bull into pieces and laid the meat on the wood. He told the people, “Fill four large jars with water and pour it over the meat and the wood.” After they did this,
translation_verse: Eɖo nake ɖe vɔsamlekpuia dzi, eye wòfli nyitsua ɖo nakea dzi. Egblɔ na ameawo azɔ be: “Miku tsi tɔmedeze ene kɔ ɖe numemevɔsalã la kple nakea dzi.”

english_verse: he told them to do it two more times. They did exactly as he said
translation_verse: Egblɔ na wo be: “Migakui zi evelia” eye wogakui zi evelia. Egblɔ be: “Migakui zi etɔ̃lia”, eye wogakui zi etɔ̃lia.

english_verse: until finally, the water ran down the altar and filled the ditch.
translation_verse: Tsia gbagba ƒo xlã vɔsamlekpuia, tsa yi ʋea me va se ɖe esime ʋea hã yɔ banaa.

english_verse: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah prayed: Our Lord, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Now, prove that you are the God of this nation, and that I, your servant, have done this at your command.
translation_verse: Esime nuɖuɖuvɔsaɣi ɖo la, gbeƒãɖela Eliya te va, eye wògblɔ be: “O Aƒetɔ, Abraham, Isak kple Israel ƒe Mawu, na eme nakɔ na amewo be wòe nye Mawu le Israel, eye menye wò dɔla, eye mewɔ nu siawo katã le wò nya nu.

english_verse: Please answer me, so these people will know that you are the Lord God, and that you will turn their hearts back to you.
translation_verse: Tɔ nam, Aƒetɔ, tɔ nam ne dukɔ sia nanya be wò Aƒetɔ ye nye Mawu, eye ègagbugbɔ woƒe dziwo vɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord immediately sent fire, and it burned up the sacrifice, the wood, and the stones. It scorched the ground everywhere around the altar and dried up every drop of water in the ditch.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe dzo ge va fiã numemevɔsa la, nakeawo, kpeawo kple ke si le afi ma eye wòno tsi si le ʋea me la hã vɔ ƒiaƒiaƒia.

english_verse: When the crowd saw what had happened, they all bowed down and shouted, “The Lord is God! The Lord is God!”
translation_verse: Esi ameawo katã kpɔ nu sia la, wotsyɔ mo anyi eye wògblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ ye nye Mawu, Aƒetɔ ye nye Mawu.”

english_verse: Just then, Elijah said, “Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let any of them get away.” So the people captured the prophets and took them to Kishon River, where Elijah killed every one of them. It Starts To Rain
translation_verse: Eliya gblɔ na wo be: “Milé Baal ƒe gbeƒãɖelaawo; migana ɖeka pɛ hã nasí o.” Tete wolé wo. Eliya kplɔ wo va Kison-tɔʋu nu, eye wòwu wo le afi ma. Kuɖiɖi la nu tso

english_verse: Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
translation_verse: Eyome Eliya gblɔ na Axab be: “Yi ɖaɖu nu, nàno nu, elabe tsidzadza le ɖiɖim hoo mele sesem.”

english_verse: Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground
translation_verse: Tete Axab dzo be yeayi ɖaɖu nu, ano nu hã. Eliya yi Karmel-to la tame, eye wòbɔbɔ ɖe anyigba eye wòtsɔ mo de ata me.

english_verse: and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.” The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
translation_verse: Egblɔ na eƒe dɔla be: “Lia toa azɔ nàkpɔ ƒu gome ɖa.” Elia toa hekpɔ ɖa, eye wògblɔ be: “Naneke meli o.” Eliya gblɔ nɛ be: “Ga yi zigbɔzi adrẽ.”

english_verse: After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.” Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
translation_verse: Esi wòyi zi adrẽlia la, egblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, alilikpo sue aɖe si le abe ame ƒe asi ene la le dodom tso ƒu gome gbɔna.” Tete Eliya gblɔ nɛ be: “Yi ɖagblɔ na Axab be: ‘Tsi lãawo ɖe tasiaɖam ŋu ne nàɖi toa adzo kaba ne tsi magasika wò o.’ ”

english_verse: A few minutes later, it got very cloudy and windy, and rain started pouring down. So Elijah wrapped his coat around himself, and the Lord gave him strength to run all the way to Jezreel. Ahab followed in his chariot.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe asi va Eliya dzi, eye wòbla ali dzi, de afɔ du me nɔ Axab eŋgɔ va se ɖe esime woɖo Yezreel mɔnu.

english_verse: Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done and that he had killed the prophets.
translation_verse: Axab gblɔ nu siwo katã Eliya wɔ kple ale si wòwu gbeƒãɖelawo katã kple yi la na Izebel.

english_verse: She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Tete Izebel dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Eliya be: “Mawuawo nefiam, woagafiam, ne nyemewɔ wò agbe etsɔ ɣe alewo ɣi abe ale si nèwɔ ame siawo dometɔ ɖeka ƒe agbe ene o fĩi!”

english_verse: Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there,
translation_verse: Tete Eliya vɔ̃, eye wòtso dze mɔ, le eƒe agbe ta, eye wòva Beer-Seba si nye Yuda tɔ eye wògblẽ eƒe subɔvia ɖe afi ma.

english_verse: then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.”
translation_verse: Ke eya ŋutɔ ya gazɔ ŋkeke ɖeka ƒe azɔli yi gbedadaƒo eye wò ɖabɔbɔ nɔ dzoŋgbalẽti aɖe te. Edi ku be yeaku hegblɔ be: “Esɔ gbɔ; azɔ la, Aƒetɔ, ɖe nye agbe ɖa, elabe nyemenyo wu tɔgbuinyewo o.”

english_verse: Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.”
translation_verse: Emlɔ anyi, eye wòdɔ alɔ̃ ɖe dzoŋgbalẽtia te. Kpɔ ɖa, mawudɔla aɖe ka asi eŋu, gblɔ nɛ be: “Tso nàɖu nu!”

english_verse: Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
translation_verse: Yeakpɔ kasia, abolo si wome le kpe xɔdzo dzi kple tsigoe nye esi le eƒe tagbe. Eɖu nu, no tsi, eye wògamlɔ anyi.

english_verse: So Elijah sat up and ate and drank. The food and water made him strong enough to walk
translation_verse: Etso, ɖu nu, no tsi. Nuɖuɖu sia do ŋusẽe wòte ŋu nɔ anyi numaɖumaɖui ŋkeke bla ene, zã bla ene va se ɖe esime wòɖaɖo, Xoreb, Mawu ƒe to la gbɔ.

english_verse: and he spent the night there in a cave. The Lord Appears to Elijah While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Eva agado aɖe gbɔ le afi ma, eye wòtsi anyi dɔ. Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe va nɛ be: “Eliya, nu ka wɔm nèle le afi sia?”

english_verse: He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu be: “Ɖe meʋã ŋu ɖe Aƒetɔ, aʋakɔwo ƒe Mawu la nu, elabe Israelviwo gblẽ wò nubabla la ɖi, gbã wò vɔsamlekpuiwo, eye wowu wò gbeƒãɖelawo kple yi. Nye, nye ɖeka kolia gɔ̃ koe susɔ, eye wole nye agbe dim be yewoaɖe ɖa.”

english_verse: “Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.” All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
translation_verse: Egblɔ nɛ be: “Do go nàɖatsi tsitre ɖe to la dzi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume.” Kpɔ ɖa, Aƒetɔ tso eme va yi, eye ya sesẽ gã aɖe ƒo, fe towo, gbã agakpewo gudugudu le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, gake Aƒetɔ menɔ yaƒoƒo la me o. Le yaƒoƒoa yome la, anyigba ʋuʋu, gake Aƒetɔ menɔ anyigbaʋuʋu la me o.

english_verse: Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. Finally, there was a gentle breeze,
translation_verse: Le anyigbaʋuʋua yome la, dzobibi va, gake Aƒetɔ menɔ dzoa me o. Le dzoa yome gbe sue aɖe ɖi dzaa.

english_verse: and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave. A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Esi Eliya see la, ehe eƒe awu ʋlaya tsyɔ mo, eye wòva le tsitre ɖe agado la nu. Tete gbe aɖe ɖi va egbɔ bia be: “Eliya, nu ka wɔm nèle le afi sia?”

english_verse: Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu be: “Ɖe meʋã ŋu ɖe Aƒetɔ, aʋakɔwo ƒe Mawu nu, elabe Israelviwo gblẽ wò nubabla, gbã wò vɔsamlekpuiwo eye wowu wò gbeƒãɖelawo kple yi. Nye, nye ɖeka kolia gɔ̃ koe susɔ, eye wole nye agbe dim be yewoaɖe ɖa.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Heyi; gbugbɔ dze wò mɔ dzi nàɖo ta Damasko-gbedadaƒo. Ne èɖo la, si ami na Xazael ne wòazu Siria-fia.

english_verse: Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
translation_verse: Si ami na Yehu, Nimsi vi, hã ne wòazu Israel- fia, eye nàsi ami na Elisa, Safat vi, si tso Abel-Mexola ne wòanye gbeƒãɖela ɖe tewòƒe.

english_verse: Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
translation_verse: Ne ame aɖe así le Xazael ƒe yi nu la, Yehu nawui, eye ame si ke así le Yehu ƒe yi nu la, Elisa nawui.

english_verse: Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
translation_verse: Ale wòdzo le afi ma yina, eye wòkpɔ Elisa, Safat vi, wòtsɔ nyitsuwo le agble me ŋlɔm. Elisa bla kɔkuti ɖe nyiawo ŋu eveveve teƒe wui eve eye eya ŋutɔ le zɔzɔm kple wui evelia. Eliya to eŋu yina eye wòda eƒe awu ʋlaya ɖa wòɖadze Elisa dzi.

english_verse: Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said. “You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
translation_verse: Tete Elisa dzo le nyitsuawo gbɔ, ƒu du kplɔ Eliya ɖo, gblɔ nɛ be: “Na maɖagbugbɔ nu na tɔ́nye kple nɔnye, emegbe mava nɔ yowòme.” Eliya gblɔ nɛ be: “Gbugbɔ yi elabe nu ka mawɔ na wò?”

english_verse: Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_verse: Elisa gbugbɔ le eyome. Elisa ɖe kɔkutiawo le eƒe nyiawo ŋu eye wòwu wo. Etsɔ kɔkutiawo do dzo tsɔ ɖa nyilã lae hema na amewo woɖu. Tete wòtso kplɔ Eliya ɖo eye wòsubɔe.

english_verse: They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.” “Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”
translation_verse: Ale wosa akpanya ɖe ali, sa ka ɖe ta, eye woyi Israel-fia gbɔ ɖagblɔ nɛ be: “Wò dɔla Ben-Hadad be yeɖe kuku, na ne yeatsi agbe.” Axab gblɔ be: “Egale agbea? Nɔvinye ŋutsue ɖe!”

english_verse: Benhadad sent a messenger to tell King Ahab of Israel,
translation_verse: Edɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Israel-fia Axab gbɔ be woagblɔ nɛ be: “Ben-Hadad be:

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Ahab replied, “everything I have is yours, including me.”
translation_verse: Israel-fia ɖo eŋu be: “Ale si nègblɔ la, nye aƒetɔ fia, tɔwòe menye, nu siwo katã nye tɔnye hã, tɔwòwoe.”

english_verse: Later, Benhadad sent another messenger to say to Ahab, “I already told you to give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your children.
translation_verse: Emegbe amedɔdɔawo gatrɔ va be: “Ben-Hadad be: ‘Medɔ ame ɖe wò va yi be: Ɖe asi le wò klosalo kple sika, srɔ̃wòwo kple viwòwo ŋu nam. Enyo.

english_verse: But tomorrow at this time, I will send my officials into your city to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take everything else that you own.”
translation_verse: Etsɔ ɣe alewo ɣi la, madɔ nye dɔlawo ɖa woava tsa wò kple wò dɔlawo ƒe aƒewo kple xɔwo me, atsɔ nu sia nu si dze wo ŋu la adzoe.’ ”

english_verse: “Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Tete ame tsitsiawo kple ame bubuawo katã gblɔ nɛ be: “Mègalɔ̃ o; gbe.”

english_verse: So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.” When Benhadad got his answer,
translation_verse: Ale wògblɔ na Ben-Hadad ƒe amedɔdɔawo be: “Migblɔ na nye aƒetɔ fia be nu siwo katã wòbia tso asinye zi gbãtɔ be mawɔ la, melɔ̃ be mawɔ wo, ke evelia sia ya la, nyemate ŋu alɔ̃ ɖe edzi o.” Amedɔdɔawo trɔ dzo. Ke wogaxɔ gbe tso Ben-Hadad gbɔ vɛ nɛ.

english_verse: he replied, “I'll completely destroy Samaria! There won't even be enough of it left for my soldiers to carry back in their hands. If I don't do it, I pray that the gods will punish me terribly.”
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad dɔ be woneyi ɖagblɔ nɛ be: “Mawuawo nefiam, ne woagafiam ɖe edzi wu, ne Samaria ƒe ke asɔ gbɔ ayɔ ame siwo katã dze yonyeme la ƒe asiʋlo me fĩi!”

english_verse: Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
translation_verse: Israel-fia ɖo eŋu be: “Migblɔ nɛ be: ‘Ame si le agbadza blam la meƒoa adegbe o, ke boŋ ame si gbɔ tso nugbe va tu agbadza lae kpɔ mɔ aƒo adegbe.’ ”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad kple etɔ fiawo nɔ aha nom le agbadɔ me hafi wova gblɔ Israel-fia ƒe ŋuɖoɖoa nɛ. Eɖe gbe na eƒe aʋawɔlawo enumake be: “Midze aʋa!” eye wodze aʋa ɖe dua ŋu.

english_verse: At that very moment, a prophet ran up to Ahab and said, “You can see that Benhadad's army is very strong. But the Lord has promised to help you defeat them today. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Ke kpɔ ɖa, gbeƒãɖela aɖe va Israel-fia Axab gbɔ va gblɔ nɛ be: “Aƒetɔ be: ‘Èle ameha gbogbo sia kpɔma? Kpɔ ɖa, matsɔe de asi na wò egbe, ne nàdze sii be nyee nye Aƒetɔ.’ ”

english_verse: “Who will fight the battle?” Ahab asked. The prophet answered, “The young bodyguards who serve the district officials.” “But who will lead them into battle?” Ahab asked. “You will!” the prophet replied.
translation_verse: Axab biae be: “Ame ka dzi wòato?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Aƒetɔ be ato anyigbaa dzikpɔlawo ƒe ɖekakpui siwo nɔa wo ŋu, nɔa wo subɔm la dzi.” Tete wògabia be: “Ame kae le aʋaa gɔme dze ge?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Wòe.”

english_verse: At noon, King Ahab and his Israelite army marched out of Samaria, with the young soldiers in front. King Benhadad of Syria and the
translation_verse: Anyigbadzikpɔlawo ƒe ɖekakpuiawo ƒe aʋalɔgoe ho gbã. Do ŋgɔ la, Ben-Hadad dɔ ŋkutsalawo ɖe teƒe mawo. Ŋkutsalaawo kpɔ ɖekakpuiawo ƒe aʋalɔgoa, eye wova gblɔ na Ben-Hadad be: “Ŋutsu aɖewo tso Samaria gbɔna.”

english_verse: “Take them alive!” Benhadad ordered. “I don't care if they have come out to fight or to surrender.”
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad gblɔ na wo be: “Nenye ŋutifafa bia ge wova hã, milé wo agbagbee. Nenye aʋa wɔ ge wova hã, milé wo agbagbee.”

english_verse: The young soldiers led Israel's troops into battle,
translation_verse: Ke esi nutomedzikpɔlawo ƒe ɖekakpuiawo do le dua me la, aʋakɔ la dze wo yome.

english_verse: and each of them attacked and killed an enemy soldier. The rest of the Syrian army turned and ran, and the Israelites went after them. Benhadad and some others escaped on horses,
translation_verse: Wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe wu ame si kpe akɔ kplii. Tete Siriatɔwo de afɔ du me, eye Israelviwo kplɔ wo ɖo. Siria-fia Ben-Hadad de sɔ dzi sí kple eƒe sɔdolawo dzo.

english_verse: but Ahab and his soldiers followed them and captured their horses and chariots. Ahab and Israel's army crushed the Syrians.
translation_verse: Azɔ Israel-fia ƒe amewo kaka ɖe gbea dzi, wu sɔwo, gblẽ tasiaɖamwo dome, eye woɖu Siria-ʋakɔawo dzi keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: Later, the prophet went back and warned Ahab, “Benhadad will attack you again next spring. Build up your troops and make sure you have some good plans.” Syria Attacks Israel Again
translation_verse: Tete gbeƒãɖela la va Israel-fia gbɔ va gblɔ nɛ be: “Va dzra ɖokuiwò ɖo, nàbla akpa sesĩe, eye ne èbe yeawɔ nane la, nàbu eŋu kpɔ nyuie hafi awɔe elabe ne ƒe trɔ dzomeŋɔli ɖo la, Siria-fia gale hoho ge ɖe ŋuwò.” Aʋawɔwɔ kple Siria zi evelia

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad's officials went to him and explained: Israel's gods are mountain gods. We fought Israel's army in the hills, and that's why they defeated us. But if we fight them on flat land, there's no way we can lose.
translation_verse: Siria-fia ƒe dɔlawo gblɔ nɛ be: “Woƒe mawuwo la, todzimawuwo wonye eya ta Israelviwo sesẽ wu mí ɖo. Ke na míawɔ aʋa kpli wo le gbegbe gbadza eye míasesẽ wu wo godoo.

english_verse: Here's what you should do. First, get rid of those
translation_verse: Fifia ɖe, ɖe fia ɖa le wo nɔƒe ne nàtsɔ aʋakplɔlawo aɖo wo teƒe.

english_verse: Then get more soldiers, horses, and chariots, so your army will be as strong as it was before. We'll fight Israel's army on flat land and wipe them out. Benhadad agreed and did what they suggested.
translation_verse: Gbugbɔ aʋakɔ bubu ɖo ne wòanɔ abe xoxotɔ ene tututu, eƒe sɔwo kple tasiaɖamwo nesɔ gbɔ abe aʋakɔ xoxotɔwo ene tututu, ne míayi ɖakpe kpli wo le gbegbe gbadza! Womate ŋu anɔ te ɖe mía nu kura o.” Ese eƒe gbe eye wòwɔ nenema.

english_verse: In the spring, Benhadad got his army together, and they marched to the town of Aphek to attack Israel.
translation_verse: Esi ƒe trɔ la, Ben-Hadad gaƒo Siria-ʋakɔ nu ƒu, eye wòho va Afek be yeava wɔ aʋa kple Israel.

english_verse: The prophet went to Ahab and said, “The Syrians think the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys. So he has promised to help you defeat their powerful army. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Tete Mawu ƒe ame aɖe va afi ma. Ete ɖe Israel-fia ŋu, eye wògblɔ na fiaa be: “Aƒetɔ Mawu be: ‘Esi Siriatɔwo be nye, Aƒetɔ la towo dome Mawu menye, nyemenye gbadzaƒe Mawu o ta la, mahe ameha gbogbo sia ade asiwò me, eye eme akɔ na mi be nyee nye Aƒetɔ.’ ”

english_verse: For seven days the two armies stayed in their camps, facing each other. Then on the seventh day the fighting broke out, and before sunset the Israelites had killed
translation_verse: Aʋakɔ eveawo ƒu asaɖa anyi dze ŋgɔ wo nɔewo ŋkeke ade, nya aɖeke medzɔ o. Ke le ŋkeke adrẽa gbe la, aʋaa fe ati. Israelviwo wu Siriatɔ akpe alafa ɖeka gbe ma gbe ɖeɖe.

english_verse: His officials said, “Your Majesty, we've heard that Israel's kings keep their agreements. We will wrap sackcloth around our waists, put ropes around our heads, and ask Ahab to let you live.”
translation_verse: Eƒe dɔlawo va gblɔ nɛ be: “Míese be Israel-fiawo la, ɖe wokpɔa nublanui na ame. Na míasa akpanya ɖe ali, asa ka ɖe ta, eye míayi Israel-fia gbɔ; ɖewohĩ agblɔ be womegawu wò o.”

english_verse: Benhadad's officials were trying to figure out what Ahab was thinking, and when he said “brother,” they quickly replied, “You're right! You and Benhadad are like brothers.” “Go get him,” Ahab said. When Benhadad came out, Ahab had him climb up into his chariot.
translation_verse: Ameawo menya be yewoase o. Woxee le enu kaba be: “Nyateƒee! Ben-Hadad la, nɔviwòe.” Tete fia la be: “Miyi ɖakplɔe vɛ.” Esi Ben-Hadad va ɖo la, Axab na wòva egbɔ le tasiaɖam la me.

english_verse: Benhadad said, “I'll give back the towns my father took from your father. And you can have shops in Damascus, just as my father had in Samaria.” Ahab replied, “If you do these things, I'll let you go free.” Then they signed a peace treaty, and Ahab let Benhadad go. A Prophet Condemns Ahab
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad gblɔ na Axab be: “Matrɔ du siwo tɔ́nye xɔ le tɔ́wò si la na wò. Hekpe ɖe ema ŋu la, àte ŋu ava ʋu fiasewo ɖe Damasko faa ne èlɔ̃, abe ale si tɔ́nye ɖo fiasewo ɖe Samaria ene.” Axab ɖo eŋu be: “Maɖe asi le ŋuwò nayi le nya siawo nu.” Ale wobla nu, eye Axab ɖe asi le Ben-Hadad ŋu wòdzo. Gbeƒãɖela aɖe bu fɔ Axab

english_verse: About this time the Lord commanded a prophet to say to a friend, “Hit me!” But the friend refused,
translation_verse: Ŋutsu ade tso gbeƒãɖelawo viwo dome gblɔ na ehavi le Aƒetɔ ƒe nya nu be: “Meɖe kuku, ƒom.”

english_verse: and the prophet told him, “You disobeyed the Lord, and as soon as you walk away, a lion will kill you.” The friend left, and suddenly a lion killed him.
translation_verse: Amea gbe eƒoƒo. Tete wògblɔ na amea be: “Esi nègbe Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe dzi wɔwɔ ta, ne èdzo le gbɔnye yina tetee ko, dzata awu wò.” Ale esi wòdzo le egbɔ yina la, dzata va do goe hewui.

english_verse: The prophet found someone else and said, “Hit me!” So this man beat him up.
translation_verse: Tete wògado go ame bubu gblɔ be: “Meɖe kuku, ƒom.” Amea ƒoe vevie, de abi eŋu.

english_verse: The prophet left and put a bandage over his face to disguise himself. Then he went and stood beside the road, waiting for Ahab to pass by.
translation_verse: Tete wòdzo. Eyi ɖadi nu bla mo, ne amewo nagakpɔe dze sii o. Eyome eyi ɖatsi tsitre ɖe mɔ to nɔ fia lalam.

english_verse: When Ahab went by, the prophet shouted, “Your Majesty, right in the heat of battle, someone brought a prisoner to me and told me to guard him. He said if the prisoner got away, I would either be killed or forced to pay
translation_verse: Esi fia va yina la, edo ɣli gblɔ na fia be: “Menɔ aʋagbea dzi le akpa si aʋaa nu sẽ ŋutɔ le la. Kasia, aʋawɔla aɖe kplɔ ŋutsu aɖe vɛ nam, gblɔ kpe ɖe eŋu be: ‘Dzɔ ame sia ŋu. Ne wova dii do kpo la, woatsɔ wò agbe aɖo etɔ teƒe, alo woaxɔ klosaloga akpe etɔ̃ le asiwò.’

english_verse: But I got busy doing other things, and the prisoner escaped.” Ahab answered, “You will be punished just as you have said.”
translation_verse: Esi meva nɔ nanewo wɔm, eye wòhiã be matso afii, ayi afii, atso afii, ayi afii la, amea sí.” Israel-fia gblɔ nɛ be: “Èbu fɔ ɖokuiwò xoxo; ele be nàxɔ tohehea.”

english_verse: The man quickly tore the bandage off his face, and Ahab saw that he was one of the prophets.
translation_verse: Amea ɖe nu si wòtsɔ bla mo la ɖa enumake, eye fiaa kpɔe dze sii be gbeƒãɖelawo dometɔ ɖekae.

english_verse: The prophet said, “The Lord told you to kill Benhadad, but you let him go. Now you will die in his place, and your people will die in place of his people.”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ na fiaa be: “Aƒetɔ be: ‘Esi nèɖe asi le ŋutsu ma, si nye ya metso kufia na xoxo ŋu wòdzo ta la, wò agbe anɔ eƒe agbe teƒe, eye wò dukɔ anɔ eƒe dukɔ teƒe.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab went back to Samaria, angry and depressed.
translation_verse: Tete dzi ku Israel-fia la wòɖo adã, dzo yi aƒe, eye wòva Samaria.

english_verse: One day, Ahab said, “Naboth, your vineyard is near my palace. Give it to me so I can turn it into a vegetable garden. I'll give you a better vineyard or pay whatever you want for yours.”
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la, Axab gblɔ na Nabot be: “Tsɔ wò waingble la nam ne manɔ amagbewo kple detsiƒonu bubuwo dom ɖe eme, elabe ete ɖe nye aƒe ŋu nyuie ŋutɔ. Matsɔ waingble bubu si nyo wu esia la na wò ɖe eteƒe. Alo ne enyo na wò la, do asi ɖe eŋu nam ne maxe fea na wò.”

english_verse: Naboth answered, “This vineyard has always been in my family. I won't let you have it.”
translation_verse: Ke Nabot ɖo eŋu na Axab be: “Matsɔ tɔgbuinyewo ƒe domenyinu na wò! Aƒetɔ nete esia ɖa xaa tso gbɔnye.”

english_verse: So Ahab went home, angry and depressed because of what Naboth had told him. He lay on his bed, just staring at the wall and refusing to eat a thing.
translation_verse: Tete Axab yi aƒeme. Eɖo adã eye dzi kui le nya si Yezreeltɔ Nabot gblɔ nɛ be: “Nyemate ŋu atsɔ tɔgbuinyewo ƒe domenyinu na wò o” ta. Eyi ɖamlɔ anyi, trɔ mo ɖe aga, eye wògbe be yemaɖu nu o.

english_verse: Jezebel his wife came in and asked, “What's wrong? Why won't you eat?”
translation_verse: Srɔ̃a Izebel va egbɔ biae be: “Nu ka ta nèlé blanui ale gbegbe be nègbe nuɖuɖu?”

english_verse: “I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard or to let me give him a better one,” Ahab replied. “And he told me I couldn't have it.”
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Elabe meƒo nu kple Nabot, Yezreeltɔ la gblɔ nɛ be: ‘Tsɔ wò waingble nam maƒle, alo ne èlɔ̃ la, nàtsɔe nam ne mana bubu wò ɖe eteƒe.’ Ke eɖo eŋu be: “Nyematsɔ nye waingble na wò o.”

english_verse: “Aren't you the king of Israel?” Jezebel asked. “Get out of bed and eat something! Don't worry, I'll get Naboth's vineyard for you.”
translation_verse: Ke srɔ̃a Izebel gblɔ nɛ be: “Èle fia ɖum ɖe Israel dzi fifiaa? Fɔ nàɖu nu, nana wò dzi nadze me. Matsɔ Yezreeltɔ Nabot ƒe waingble la na wò.”

english_verse: They told the people that it was a day to go without eating, and when they all came together, they seated Naboth at the front.
translation_verse: woɖe gbeƒã be woatsi nu adɔ, eye wokplɔ Nabot da ɖe dukɔa ŋgɔ.

english_verse: The two liars came in and sat across from Naboth. Then they accused him of cursing God and the king, so the people dragged Naboth outside and stoned him to death.
translation_verse: Tete yakame eve va nɔ anyi dze ŋgɔe. Woɖi ɖase tso enu le dukɔa ŋkume gblɔ be: “Nabot do ɖiŋu na Mawu kple fia la.” Ale wokplɔe yi dua godo, eye woƒu kpee wòku.

english_verse: The leaders of Jezreel sent a message back to Jezebel that said, “Naboth is dead.”
translation_verse: Tete wodɔ ame ɖe Izebel be: “Woƒu kpe Nabot; eku.”

english_verse: As soon as Jezebel got their message, she told Ahab, “Now you can have the vineyard Naboth refused to sell. He's dead.”
translation_verse: Enumake esi Izebel se be woƒu kpe Nabot wòku la, Izebel gblɔ na Axab be: “Tso nàyi ɖaxɔ Nabot, Yezreeltɔ la ƒe waingble si wògbe be yematsɔ na wò nàƒle o la. Nabot megale agbe o; eku.”

english_verse: Ahab got up and went to take over the vineyard. Elijah Condemns Ahab
translation_verse: Enumake esi Axab se be Nabot ku la, edze mɔ be yeayi Nabot, Yezreeltɔ la ƒe waingble la me aɖaxɔe wòazu ye tɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Elijah the prophet,
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Eliya, Tisbitɔ la be:

english_verse: “King Ahab of Israel is in Naboth's vineyard right now, taking it over.
translation_verse: “Tso nàɖakpe Israel-fia Axab ame si le Samaria. Kpɔ ɖa, ele Nabot ƒe waingble me be yeaɖaxɔ agblea atsɔ wɔ ye tɔe.

english_verse: Go tell him that I say, ‘Ahab, you murdered Naboth and took his property. And so, in the very spot where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they will lick up your blood.’ ” When Elijah found him,
translation_verse: Gblɔ nɛ be: ‘Aƒetɔ be: Afi si avuwo ɖuɖɔ Nabot ƒe ʋu le la, afi ma ke woaɖuɖɔ wò hã tɔwò le.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab said, “So, my enemy, you found me at last.” Elijah answered: Yes, I did! Ahab, you have managed to do everything the Lord hates.
translation_verse: Axab gblɔ na Eliya be: “O! Nye futɔ, èva ke ɖe ŋunyea?” Eliya ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Megava ke ɖe ŋuwò, elabe ètsɔ ɖokuiwò dzra be yeawɔ nu si nye nuvɔ̃ɖi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume.

english_verse: Now you will be punished. You and every man and boy in your family will die, whether slave or free.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ava dziwò. Mana navɔ ɖa keŋkeŋ; matsrɔ̃ wò ƒomea me ŋutsuwo katã, kluviwo kple aƒeviwo siaa le Israel.

english_verse: Your whole family will be wiped out, just like the families of King Jeroboam and King Baasha. You've made the Lord very angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Mawɔ wò ƒome abe Yerobeam, Nebat vi ƒe ƒome kple Baesa, Axiya vi ƒe ƒome ene, elabe èdo dziku nam eye nèna Israel wɔ nuvɔ̃.

english_verse: And as for Jezebel, dogs will eat her body there in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Le Izebel hã gome la, Aƒetɔ be: ‘Avuwo aɖu Izebel ƒe kukua le Yezreel-du me.’

english_verse: Dogs will also eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Ne Axab ƒe ame aɖe ku le Yezreel-du me la, avuwo aɖu eƒe kukua, eye ne Axab ƒe ame aɖe ku le gbedzi la, dziƒoxeviwo aɖu eƒe kukua.”

english_verse: Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
translation_verse: Migblɔ na wo be, fia be: ‘Mide ame sia gaxɔ me, eye minɔ abolo vi aɖe kple tsi vi aɖe ɖeɖe ko nam eyama va se ɖe esime metrɔ gbɔ le ŋutifafa me.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab asked his officials, “Why haven't we tried to get Ramoth in Gilead back from the Syrians? It belongs to us.”
translation_verse: Israel-fia gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo be: “Mienya be Ramot, si le Gilead la, mía tɔe gake míexɔe le Siria-fia si oa?”

english_verse: Then he asked Jehoshaphat, “Would you go to Ramoth with me and attack the Syrians?” “Just tell me what to do,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Tete wòbia Yosafat be: “Àyi aʋa kplim le Ramot-Gilead mahã?” Yosafat ɖo eŋu na Israel-fia be: “Nye kple wòe; nye amewo nye wò amewo, eye nye sɔwo nye wò sɔwo.”

english_verse: But first, let's ask the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ke Yosafat gagblɔ na Israel-fia be: “Bia gbe Aƒetɔ se gbã.”

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Gake Yosafat gabia be: “Aƒetɔ ƒe gbeƒãɖela bubu aɖeke megale afi sia, ne míayi ɖabia nu le eya hã gbɔ kpɔ oa?”

english_verse: “We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.” “Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied.
translation_verse: Israel-fia ɖo eŋu na Yosafat be: “Ɖeka aɖe gali, ame si gbɔ wobiaa nu Aƒetɔ le, eyae nye Mixa, Yimla vi. Gake melé fui elabe megblɔa nya nyui aɖeke ɖi le ŋunye gbeɖe o; vɔ̃ ko.” Yosafat xɔ edzi nɛ be: “Fia megagblɔ nenema o.”

english_verse: Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
translation_verse: Tete Israel-fia dɔ aƒedzikpɔla aɖe be: “Yi ɖakplɔ Mixa, Yimla vi, vɛ fifi laa.”

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria. They were listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Fia eveawo, Israel-fia kple Yosafat, Yuda-fia, dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe do fiawu, bɔbɔ nɔ eƒe fiazikpui dzi. Wole teƒe aɖe le lugbɔƒe le Samaria-du ƒe agbo nu eye gbeƒãɖelaawo katã le wo ŋkume le gbeƒã ɖem.

english_verse: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
translation_verse: Zedekiya, Kenaana vi, tsɔ ga wɔ lã ƒe dzowo ɖe asi, eye wògblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ be: ‘Esiawoe nàtsɔ tu Siriatɔwo va se ɖe esime woatsrɔ̃ avɔ ɖa.’ ”

english_verse: All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth, and they promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
translation_verse: Gbeƒãɖelaawo katã ɖe gbeƒã nenema be: “Ho yi Ramot-Gilead. Àɖu dzi; Aƒetɔ atsɔe ade asi na fia la.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
translation_verse: Amedɔdɔ si yi Mixa yɔ ge la gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, gbeƒãɖelaawo ƒe gbe sɔ: wo katã wogblɔ nya nyui na fia la; nà wò nya nanɔ abe wo dometɔ ɖeka tɔ ene eye nàgblɔ nya nyui.”

english_verse: “I'll say whatever the living Lord tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
translation_verse: Gake Mixa gblɔ be: “Metà Aƒetɔ ƒe agbe, be nya si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nam la, eyae magblɔ.”

english_verse: Then Micaiah went to Ahab, and Ahab asked, “Micaiah, should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?” “Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Esi wòva ɖo fiaa gbɔ la, fiaa biae be: “Mixa, mího aʋa yi Ramot-Gilead loo, alo mímegayi oa?” Eɖo eŋu na fiaa be: “Miho yi; miaɖu dzi; Aƒetɔ atsɔe ade asi na fia la.”

english_verse: “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth!” Ahab shouted. “What does the Lord really say?”
translation_verse: Gake fia la gblɔ nɛ be: “Zi nenie matà wò, be nàgblɔ nyateƒe nam le Aƒetɔ ŋkɔ me?”

english_verse: He answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers walking around in the hills like sheep without a shepherd to guide them. The Lord said, ‘This army has no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
translation_verse: Mixa gblɔ be: “Mekpɔ Israelviwo katã wokaka ɖe towo dzi abe alẽ siwo nu kplɔla mele o la ene, eye Aƒetɔ gblɔ be: ‘Aƒetɔ aɖeke mele ame siawo nu o; wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe negbugbɔ yi eƒeme le ŋutifafa me.’ ”

english_verse: Micaiah replied: Listen to this! I also saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him.
translation_verse: Mixa gblɔ be: “Eya ta se Aƒetɔ ƒe nya. Mekpɔ Aƒetɔ wòbɔbɔ nɔ eƒe fiazikpui dzi eye dziƒoʋakɔ la katã le tsitre ɖe eƒe ɖusime kple miame,
