translation_verse: Ale dɔlaa tsɔ nuɖuɖua na wo, woɖui wòtsi anyi abe ale si Aƒetɔ la gblɔe ene.

english_verse: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
translation_verse: Naeman nye Siria-fia ƒe aʋakplɔla. Enye fiaa ƒe ame vevi, eye wòbunɛ ŋutɔ elabe eya dzie Aƒetɔ to na Siria-ʋakɔwo ɖu dzi. Enye asrafo kalẽtɔ, gake ŋutigbalẽdɔ aɖe le eŋu.

english_verse: One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife.
translation_verse: Esi Siriatɔwo yi adzogbe le Israel-nyigba dzi la, woɖe aboyo nyɔnuvi sue aɖe si va le Naeman srɔ̃ subɔm.

english_verse: When Naaman told the king what the girl had said,
translation_verse: Naeman yi Siria-fia la gbɔ ɖagblɔ nu si nyɔnuvia gblɔ la nɛ.

english_verse: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
translation_verse: Fia la be: “Ekema heyi; maɖo agbalẽ ɖee.” Ale Naeman dze mɔ. Etsɔ klosaloga akpe bla etɔ̃, sikaga akpe ade kple atsyɔ̃ɖowu, dodo ewo ɖe asi.

english_verse: He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
translation_verse: Lɛta si wòtsɔ na Israel-fia la me nyawo nye esi: “Mele nye dɔla Naeman ɖom ɖe wò kple lɛta sia be nàda ŋutigbalẽdɔ si le eŋu la nɛ.”

english_verse: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
translation_verse: Elisa dɔ ame ɖo ɖee be: “Yi ɖado ɖi ɖe Yordan me zi adrẽ ekema wò ŋutigbalẽ aɖɔ ɖo, eye ŋuwò akɔ.”

english_verse: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
translation_verse: Esi Israel-fia xlẽ agbalẽa la, edze eƒe awuwo gblɔ be: “Mawue menye wua ame gagbɔa agbeea? Ale ke wɔ wòɖo ŋutsu sia ɖe gbɔnye be mada ŋutigbalẽdɔ sia nɛ mahã? Mikpɔ ale si wòle ge dim le ŋunye la ɖa!”

english_verse: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
translation_verse: Ke esi Elisa, Mawu ƒe ame la, se be Israel-fia dze eƒe awuwo la, edɔ ame ɖe egbɔ be: “Nu ka ta nèdze wò awuwo? Ðo ŋutsua ɖem ne maɖee fiae be Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela aɖe le Israel.”

english_verse: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
translation_verse: Ale Naeman kple eƒe sɔwo kpakple tasiaɖam va tɔ ɖe Elisa ƒe agbo nu.

english_verse: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
translation_verse: Tete Naeman do dziku, dzo yina be: “Mikpɔ ɖa, nyea mebu be eya ŋutɔ ava tsi tsitre ɖe gbɔnye, ayɔ Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu la ŋkɔ, anyè asi dɔteƒeawo dzi eye wòada gbe le ŋunye.

english_verse: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
translation_verse: Ðe Abana kple Farpar, Damasko-tɔsisiwo, menyo wu Israeltɔwo katã oa? Ɖe nyemate ŋu ale tsi le wo me ŋunye nakɔ oa?” Ale wòtrɔ dzo yina kple dziku.

english_verse: His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
translation_verse: Tete eƒe dɔlawo te ɖe eŋu gblɔ nɛ be: “Tɔ́nye, ne Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela la ɖe wògblɔ na wò be nàwɔ nu sesẽ aɖe ɖe, màwɔe oa? Fifia, ɖeko wògblɔ na wò be: ‘Yi ɖale tsi; ŋuwò akɔ’; ko màwɔe oa?”

english_verse: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
translation_verse: Ale Naeman ɖi abu ɖado ɖi ɖe Yordan me, zi adrẽ, abe ale si Mawu ƒe ame la gblɔ ene. Eƒe ŋutigbalẽ ɖɔ ɖo abe ŋutsuvi dzaa tɔ ene, eye eŋu kɔ.

english_verse: Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
translation_verse: Tete eya kple ame siwo katã le eŋu la gbugbɔ yi Mawu ƒe ame la gbɔ, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Medze sii azɔ be Mawu aɖeke mele xexeme ƒe afi aɖeke o; negbe le Israel ko. Azɔ taflatsɛ, nunana aɖe nye esi tso wò dɔla gbɔ.”

english_verse: “I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.” Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing.
translation_verse: Ke Elisa ɖo eŋu be: “Metà Aƒetɔ gbagbe, si mesubɔna la, nyemaxɔ naneke o.” Naeman ƒoe ɖe enu, gake egbe.

english_verse: Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ale Naeman gblɔ be: “Ekema meɖe kuku, nà woaku anyi tedzisɔ eve ƒe tsɔtsɔ nu na wò dɔla elabe tso azɔ dzi la, nyemagasa vɔ alo ame nu na mawu bubu aɖeke o, negbe Aƒetɔ ko.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will forgive me when I go into the temple of the god Rimmon and bow down there with the king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Ðeko nàtsɔ nu ɖeka sia ke wò dɔla: ne nye aƒetɔ fia la ziɔ ɖe nye abɔ ŋu yi Rimon subɔƒe, eye mede ta agu na Rimon la, Aƒetɔ netsɔ kem.”

english_verse: “Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left. Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi After Naaman had gone only a short distance,
translation_verse: Elisa gblɔ nɛ be: “Heyi le ŋutifafa me!” Ke esi Naeman dzo yina ʋɛ ko la,

english_verse: Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.”
translation_verse: Gexazi, si nye Mawu ƒe ame Elisa, ƒe dɔla la, gblɔ le eɖokui me be: “Kpɔ ɖa, nye aƒetɔ nyo dɔme na Naeman, Siriatɔ sia akpa. Mexɔ nu si wòtsɔ vɛ la ƒe ɖeke o. Metà Aƒetɔ ƒe agbe; madze eyome aɖaxɔ nane le esi godoo!”

english_verse: So he hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
translation_verse: Ale Gexazi dze Naeman yome. Esi Naeman kpɔ be ame aɖe kplɔ ye ɖo le du dzi gbɔna la, eɖi le tasiaɖam la me ɖakpee. Ebiae be: “Eme faa?”

english_verse: “Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu be: “Eme fa; ke nye aƒetɔ dɔm ɖa be magblɔ na wò be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa, ɖekakpui eve siwo nye gbeƒãɖelawo ƒe nusrɔ̃lawo la tso Efrayim-tonyigba dzi, va dzem fifi laa. Meɖe kuku, na klosaloga akpe etɔ̃ kple atsyɔ̃ɖowu, dodo eve wo.”

english_verse: “Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
translation_verse: Naeman ɖo eŋu be: “Taflatsɛ, xɔ akpe ade dzro!” Eƒoe ɖe enu, eye wòbla klosaloga la ɖe kotoku eve me hetsɔ atsyɔ̃ɖowu, dodo eve kpe ɖe eŋu nɛ. Naeman tsɔ nuawo na eƒe dɔla eve wotsɔ dze Gexazi ŋgɔe.

english_verse: When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone,
translation_verse: Esi wova ɖo togbɛa dzi la, Gexazi xɔ nuawo le ŋutsuawo si dzra ɖo ɖe eƒeme, eye wòdo mɔ wo, wotrɔ dzo.

english_verse: Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
translation_verse: Gexazi yi eme ɖatsi tsitre ɖe eƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ. Elisa biae be: “Gexazi afi ka nètso?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Nye aƒetɔ, wò dɔla medo yi afi aɖeke o.”

english_verse: Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants.
translation_verse: Ke Elisa gblɔ nɛ be: “Ðe nye gbɔgbɔ meyi kpli wò, esime ŋutsua trɔ heɖi le eƒe tasiaɖam me va kpe wò oa? Klosalo kple awu xɔɣi nye esia? Amitiwo kple waingble xɔɣie nye esia? Alẽ kple nyihawo xɔɣie nye esia? Kluvi kple kosiwo xɔɣie nye esia?

english_verse: Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!” Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
translation_verse: Le esia ta Naeman ƒe ŋutigbalẽdɔ la adre ɖe wò kple wò dzidzimeviwo ŋu tegbee!” Tete Gexazi dzo le egbɔ, eye ŋutigbalẽdɔ la ƒo ɖe eŋu wòfu kpii abe tsikpe ene.

english_verse: One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka la, Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo ƒe nusrɔ̃lawo gblɔ na Elisa be: “Teƒe si míele le gbɔwò la, xaxa na mí akpa.

english_verse: Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.” “That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
translation_verse: Taflatsɛ, míedi be míayi Yordan nu aɖadi ati le afi ma. Mía dome ame sia ame atso ɖeka ne míatu nɔƒe si míanɔ la ɖe afi ma.” Elisa ɖo eŋu be: “Miheyi!”

english_verse: “Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked. “Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered,
translation_verse: Ke wo dometɔ ɖeka gblɔ nɛ be: “Meɖe kuku, va míyi.” Eɖo eŋu be: “Mayi baa.”

english_verse: and he left with them. They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees.
translation_verse: Ale wòyi kpli wo. Wova ɖo Yordan nu, eye wode asi atiawo tsotso me.

english_verse: “Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
translation_verse: Ke Mawu ƒe ame la biae be: “Afi ka wòge dze?” Efia teƒe lae. Elisa tso ati aɖe, eye wòdae ɖe afi ma. Tete fía la ho ɖe tsia dzi.

english_verse: “Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it. Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
translation_verse: Elisa gblɔ nɛ be: “Ðee!” Ale wòdo asi ɖa ɖee. Israelviwo ɖu Siria-ʋakɔ dzi

english_verse: Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
translation_verse: Eva eme be Siria-fia ho aʋa ɖe Israel ŋu. Ede adaŋu kple eƒe aʋakplɔlawo, eye wotia teƒe si woaƒu asaɖa anyi ɖo la.

english_verse: Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.”
translation_verse: Ke Mawu ƒe ame la dɔ ame ɖe Israel-fia be: “Kpɔ nyuie, mègato afi sia o elabe Siriatɔwo gbɔna afi ma.”

english_verse: The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
translation_verse: Nu sia na Siria-fia tɔtɔ ŋutɔ, eye wòyɔ eŋumewo, bia wo be: “Mimagblɔ mía dome ame si le Israel-fia dzi la nam oa?”

english_verse: “None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
translation_verse: Wo dometɔ ɖeka ɖo eŋu be: “Nye aƒetɔ fia, menye mía dometɔ aɖeke ye o. Ke boŋ Elisa, Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela si le Israel lae. Eyae gblɔa wò xɔgãmenya na Israel-fia la.”

english_verse: “Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.” They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king.
translation_verse: Fia la gblɔ be: “Miyi ɖadi teƒe si wòle la, ne madɔ ame woaɖalée vɛ.” Wogblɔ nɛ be ele Dotan.

english_verse: He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
translation_verse: Ale edɔ aʋakɔ gã aɖe ɖa. Wotsɔ sɔwo kple tasiaɖamwo yi ɖaɖe to ɖe dua le zã me.

english_verse: When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
translation_verse: Esi Mawu ƒe ame la ƒe dɔla fɔ ŋdi kanya, eye wòdo ɖe xexe la, kpɔ ɖa, aʋakɔ kple sɔwo kpakple tasiaɖamwo ƒo xlã dua. Dɔla la biae be: “Ao, nye aƒetɔ! Nu ka wɔ ge míala?”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.”
translation_verse: Elisa ɖo eŋu be: “Mègavɔ̃ o, elabe ame siwo le mía dzi la sɔ gbɔ wu ame siwo le wo dzi.”

english_verse: Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
translation_verse: Ale Elisa do gbe ɖa be: “Aƒetɔ ʋu eƒe ŋkuwo, ne wòakpɔ nu!” Tete Aƒetɔ ʋu dɔlaa ƒe ŋkuwo, eye wòkpɔ dzosɔwo kple dzotasiaɖamwo fũu le toa ŋu, woƒo xlã Elisa.

english_verse: As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
translation_verse: Esi Siria-ʋakɔ la ɖi abu, lũ ɖe Elisa dzi la, Elisa do gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ be: “Meɖe kuku, nà ameha sia ƒe ŋku nagbã!” Ale Aƒetɔ na ameawo ƒe ŋku gbã abe ale si Elisa biae ene.

english_verse: Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Tete Elisa gblɔ na wo be: “Menye mɔ lae nye esia o, eye menye du la hãe nye esia o. Mikplɔm ɖo, ne míayi ŋutsu si dim miele la gbɔ”, eye wòkplɔ wo yi Samaria.

english_verse: When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
translation_verse: Esi woɖo la, Elisa gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, ʋu ame siawo ƒe ŋkuwo, ne woakpɔ nu!” Ale Aƒetɔ ʋu woƒe ŋkuwo, kasia wokpɔ be yewole Samaria-dua titina.

english_verse: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
translation_verse: Esi Israel-fia kpɔ ameawo la, ebia Elisa be: “Tɔ́nye, mawu woa? Mawu wo hã?”

english_verse: “No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu be: “Gbeɖe! Ɖe nàwu ame siwo nètsɔ wò yi kple dati, ɖe aboyoe laa? Na abolo kple tsi wo, ne woaɖu nu, ano nu, eye woagbugbɔ ayi woƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ.”

english_verse: The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go. For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory. King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
translation_verse: Ale Israel-fia ɖo kplɔ̃ gã aɖe na wo; woɖu nu, no nu, eye wòdo mɔ wo woyi woƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ. Tso esia dzi la, Siriatɔwo ƒe adzohawo megava Israel-nyigba dzi o. Siria ho aʋa ɖe Samaria ŋu. Dɔ to le afi ma

english_verse: Some time later, King Benhadad of Syria called his entire army together, then they marched to Samaria and attacked.
translation_verse: Esiawo megbe la, Siria-fia Ben-Hadad ƒo eƒe aʋakɔwo katã nu ƒu, eye wòva ɖe to ɖe Samaria-dua.

english_verse: They kept up the attack until there was nothing to eat in the city. In fact, a donkey's head cost
translation_verse: Dɔ gã aɖe to le Samaria. Kpɔ ɖa, futɔwo ɖe to ɖee ale gbegbe be tedzita ɖeka xɔ klosaloga bla enyi, eye ahɔnɛmi kpekpeme gram alafa eve xɔ klosaloga atɔ̃.

english_verse: One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
translation_verse: Eva eme be Israel-fia nɔ tsa ɖim le dua ƒe gli dzi, eye nyɔnu aɖe do ɣli yɔe be: “Nye aƒetɔ fia, xɔ nam!”

english_verse: “Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?”
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu be: “Esi Aƒetɔ mexɔ na wò o la, ale ke mawɔ axɔ na wò? Mato lugbɔƒea loo, alo wainfiãƒea?”

english_verse: Then he asked, “What's the matter anyway?” The woman answered, “Another woman and I were so hungry that we agreed to eat our sons. She said if we ate my son one day, we could eat hers the next day.
translation_verse: Fia la yi edzi biae be: “Nu kae le wɔwòm?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Nyɔnu sia gblɔ nam be: ‘Na míaɖu viwò ŋutsu egbe, eye etsɔ la, míaɖu tɔnye.’

english_verse: So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
translation_verse: Ale míeɖa tɔnyea ɖu. Esi ŋu ke la, megblɔ nɛ be: ‘Tsɔ viwò ŋutsua vɛ ne míaɖu, ke eya tsɔ via ŋutsua ɣla.’ ”

english_verse: The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath.
translation_verse: Esi fia la se nyɔnua ƒe nyaawo la, edze eƒe awuwo. Azɔ esi wònɔ dua ƒe glia dzi zɔm ta la, amewo kpɔ be eta akpanya ɖe awu gɔme.

english_verse: He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Edo ɣli gblɔ be: “Mawu newum maku, agaku! Ne Elisa, Safat vi, ƒe ta aganɔ enu egbe fĩi!”

english_verse: Before Elisha finished talking, the messenger came up and said, “The Lord has made all these terrible things happen to us. Why should I think he will help us now?”
translation_verse: Mekpɔ ɖe nu le nyaa me o, kasia fia la nye esi va do. Egblɔ be: “Dzɔgbevɔ̃e sia tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ. Nu ka ta maganɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe asi nu kpɔm?”

english_verse: Elisha answered, “I have a message for you. The Lord promises that tomorrow here in Samaria, you will be able to buy a large sack of flour or two large sacks of barley for almost nothing.”
translation_verse: Elisa ɖo eŋu be: “Se Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe. Aƒetɔ be: ‘Etsɔ ɣealeawoɣi la, wɔ memee kilo etɔ̃ loo, alo lu kilo ade axɔ klosaloga ɖeka le Samaria ƒe agbo nu.’ ”

english_verse: The chief officer there with the king replied, “I don't believe it! Even if the Lord sent a rainstorm, it couldn't produce that much grain by tomorrow.” “You will see it happen, but you won't eat any of the food,” Elisha warned him. The Syrian Army Stops Its Attack
translation_verse: Gake fia ƒe aʋakplɔla si ƒe abɔ ŋu fia la ziɔ ɖo la gblɔ na Mawu ƒe ame la be: “Ne Aƒetɔ aɖe fesre ɖe dziŋgɔli ŋu gɔ̃ hã la, ɖe esia ava emea?” Elisa ɖo eŋu be: “Kpɔ ɖa, àkpɔ eteƒe kple wò ŋku, gake màɖu ɖeke o.” Siria-ʋakɔ la dzo

english_verse: About the same time, four men with leprosy were just outside the gate of Samaria. They said to each other, “Why should we sit here, waiting to die?
translation_verse: Azɔ ŋutsu ene siwo le ŋutigbalẽdɔ si amewo vɔ̃na la lém la le dua ƒe agbo nu. Wogblɔ na wo nɔewo be: “Nu ka ta míabɔbɔ nɔ afii, aku?

english_verse: There's nothing to eat in the city, so we would starve if we went inside. But if we stay out here, we will die for sure. Let's sneak over to the Syrian army camp and surrender. They might kill us, but they might not.”
translation_verse: Ne míegblɔ be míage ɖe dua me la, dɔwuame le afi ma, míaku ɖi. Ke ne míebɔbɔ nɔ afi sia hã, míele kuku ge, eya ta mina míagblẽ mía tɔwo ɖi ayi Siriatɔwo ƒe asaɖa me. Ne wona míetsi agbe la, ekema míetsi agbe. Ne wowu mí la, ekema míeku ko evɔ.”

english_verse: They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
translation_verse: Ke wogblɔ na wo nɔewo be: “Nu si wɔm míele la menyo o. Nya nyui aɖee va na mí egbea. Ne míalala va se ɖe ŋu nake la, woabu fɔ mí. Eya ta mina míaɖagblɔe le fiaƒeme.”

english_verse: They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
translation_verse: Ale woyi ɖayɔ agbonudzɔlawo gblɔ na wo be: “Míede Siriatɔwo ƒe asaɖa me, ke ame aɖeke meli o; míese nuƒo aɖeke hã o. Wode ka sɔwo kple tedziwo ɖi, eye agbadɔwo hã li. Nuawo li alea míekpɔ.”

english_verse: The guards reported the news to the king's palace.
translation_verse: Agbonudzɔlaawo ɖe gbeƒã nya la, eye fiaƒemetɔwo see.

english_verse: The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
translation_verse: Fia la fɔ le zã ma me gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo be: “Magblɔ nu si Siriatɔwo ɖo ɖe mía ŋu la na mi. Wonya be dɔ le mía wum, eya ta wodzo le asaɖa la me ɖabè ɖe gbe me kple susu be míele go do ge le dua me, ekema yewoalé mí agbagbee age ɖe dua me.”

english_verse: One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.”
translation_verse: Eƒe dɔlawo dometɔ ɖeka xɔ edzi gblɔ be: “Na míadɔ ame, woatsɔ sɔ atɔ̃ siwo susɔ la be woaɖakpɔ nu si tututu dzɔ la ava gblɔ na mí, elabe ame siwo susɔ le dua me la, kuku ge ko woala abe ame siwo ku xoxo la ene.”

english_verse: They found two chariots, and the king commanded the men to find out what had happened to the Syrian troops.
translation_verse: Ale woɖe ame kple tasiaɖam eve kpakple sɔwo dɔ ɖe Siriatɔwo ƒe asaɖa la me, ne woaɖakpɔ nu si dzɔ la.

english_verse: The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
translation_verse: Woti wo yome va ɖo keke Yordan nu ke. Awu kple aʋawɔnu siwo Siriatɔwo tsɔ ƒu gbe esime wole sisím la ko wokpɔ le mɔa dzi fũu. Ale amedɔdɔawo gbɔ va gblɔe na fia.

english_verse: At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Tete dukɔ la do go yi ɖaha nuwo le Siriatɔwo ƒe asaɖa la me. Ale wɔ memee kilo etɔ̃ alo lu kilo ade xɔ klosaloga ɖeka le Aƒetɔ ƒe nya la nu.

english_verse: The king of Israel had put his chief officer in charge of the gate, but he died when the people trampled him as they rushed out of the city.
translation_verse: Ke fia la ɖe aʋakplɔla si ƒe abɔ ŋu wòziɔna ɖo la ɖo agboa nu. Tete dukɔ la zɔ edzi, fanyae ɖe agboa nu wòku, abe ale si Mawu ƒe ame la gblɔ esime fia la va egbɔ ene.

english_verse: Earlier, when the king was at Elisha's house, Elisha had told him that flour or barley would sell for almost nothing.
translation_verse: Esi Mawu ƒe ame la gblɔ na fia la be: “Lu kilo ade alo wɔ kilo etɔ̃ axɔ klosaloga ɖeka pɛ ko le Samaria-dua ƒe agbo nu etsɔ ɣealeawoɣi” la,

english_verse: But the officer refused to believe that even the Lord could do that. So Elisha warned him that he would see it happen, but would not eat any of the food.
translation_verse: aʋakplɔla sia, si ƒe abɔ ŋu fia ziɔna ɖo la xɔ edzi gblɔ na Mawu ƒe ame la be: “Ne Aƒetɔ aɖe fesre ɖe dziŋgɔli ŋu gɔ̃ hã la, ɖe esia ava emea?” Elisa gblɔ nɛ be: “Àkpɔ eteƒe kple wò ŋkuwo, gake màɖu ɖeke o.”

english_verse: And that's exactly what happened—the officer was trampled to death.
translation_verse: Edzɔ ɖe edzi nenema; dukɔ la zɔ edzi, fanyae ɖe agboa nu, wòku.

english_verse: Then she returned to Israel and immediately begged the king to give back her house and property.
translation_verse: Le ƒe adrẽa megbe la, nyɔnua gbɔ tso Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba la dzi. Eyi fia la gbɔ be yeaɖe kuku nɛ ne wòatrɔ yeƒe aƒe kple agble na ye.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king was asking Gehazi the servant of Elisha about the amazing things Elisha had been doing.
translation_verse: Fia la nɔ nu ƒom kple Gexazi, Mawu ƒe ame ƒe dɔla, esime nyɔnua va ɖo. Fia la gblɔ na Gexazi be: “Gblɔ nu gã nu gã siwo katã Elisa wɔ la nam.”

english_verse: While Gehazi was telling him that Elisha had brought a dead boy back to life, the woman and her son arrived. “Here's the boy, Your Majesty,” Gehazi said. “And this is his mother.”
translation_verse: Esime Gexazi le ale si Elisa gbɔ agbe ame kuku la gblɔm na fiaa la, nyɔnua va ɖe kuku na fiaa be wòatrɔ yeƒe aƒe kple agble na ye. Gexazi gblɔ na fiaa be: “Nye aƒetɔ fia, nyɔnua nye esi; via si Elisa gbɔ agbee la hã nye esi.”

english_verse: Some time later Elisha went to the capital city of Damascus to visit King Benhadad of Syria, who was sick. And when Benhadad was told he was there,
translation_verse: Elisa va Damasko esime Siria-fia Ben-Hadad le dɔ lém. Wogblɔ na fia la be: “Mawu ƒe ame va afi sia!”

english_verse: Hazael left with forty camel loads of the best things made in Damascus as a gift for Elisha. He found the prophet and said, “Your servant, King Benhadad, wants to know if he will get well.”
translation_verse: Ale Xazael yi ɖakpɔe kple nunana nyuitɔ vovovo siwo le Damasko la; wole kposɔ bla ene ƒe agbatsɔtsɔ. Esi wòva ɖo la, etsi tsitre ɖe Elisa gbɔ, gblɔ nɛ be: “Viwò Siria-fia Ben-Hadad ye dɔm ɖe gbɔwò. Ebe mabia wò be: ‘Mahaya le dɔ sia mea?’ ”

english_verse: “Tell him he will,” Elisha said to Hazael. “But the Lord has already told me that Benhadad will definitely die.”
translation_verse: Elisa ɖo eŋu be: “Yi ɖagblɔ nɛ be: ‘Àhaya godoo’ gake Aƒetɔ ɖee fiam be èle kuku ge kokoko.”

english_verse: Elisha stared at him until Hazael was embarrassed, then Elisha began crying.
translation_verse: Elisa lé ŋku ɖe Xazael dzi gãa aɖabamaƒomaƒoe va se ɖe esime ŋukpe Xazael. Mawu ƒe ame la de asi avifafa me.

english_verse: “Sir, why are you crying?” Hazael asked. Elisha answered, “Because I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn down their walled cities and slaughter their young men. You will even crush the heads of their babies and rip open their pregnant women.”
translation_verse: Tete Xazael biae be: “Nye aƒetɔ, nu ka ta nèle avi fam?” Elisa ɖo eŋu be: “Elabe menya nuvɔ̃ɖi si wɔ ge nèle ɖe Israelviwo ŋu: Àtɔ dzo woƒe mɔ́wo, àwu woƒe ɖekakpuiwo kple yi, àxlã woƒe vidzĩwo ɖe nu, eye àdze ƒo le woƒe funɔwo nu.”

english_verse: “How could I ever do anything like that?” Hazael replied. “I'm only a servant and don't have that kind of power.” “Hazael, the Lord has told me that you will be the next king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Xazael bia be: “Nu ka nye, wò dɔla menye? Nye avu, afi ka makpɔ ŋusẽ tsoe awɔ nu sia gbegbee?” Elisa ɖo eŋu be: “Aƒetɔ ɖee fiam be wòe gbɔna fia ɖu ge ɖe Siria dzi.”

english_verse: Hazael went back to Benhadad and told him, “Elisha said that you will get well.”
translation_verse: Tete wòdzo le Elisa gbɔ yi eƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ. Eƒe aƒetɔa biae be: “Nya ka Elisa gblɔ na wò?” Xazael ɖo eŋu be: “Ebe èle hayahaya ge.”

english_verse: But the very next day, Hazael got a thick blanket; he soaked it in water and held it over Benhadad's face until he died. Hazael then became king. King Jehoram of Judah (
translation_verse: Gake esi ŋu ke la, etsɔ abadzivɔ de tsi me hetsyɔ mo na fia la wòku. Ale Xazael zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Yuda-fia Yoram

english_verse: So Jehoram and his cavalry marched to Zair, where the Edomite army surrounded him and his commanders. During the night he attacked the Edomites, but he was defeated, and his troops escaped to their homes.
translation_verse: Tete Yoram ho kple eƒe tasiaɖamwo katã yi Zair, afi si Edomtɔwo ɖe to ɖe eƒe aʋakɔwo le. Esi wòfɔ le zã me la, ekpɔ be Edomtɔwo ɖe to ɖe ye kple woƒe tasiaɖam-megãwo, ke edze wo, eye dukɔ la sí yi yi woƒe nɔƒewo.

english_verse: While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king.
translation_verse: Le Yehoram ƒe fiaɖuɣi la, Edom dze aglã ɖe Yuda-dukɔa ƒe dziɖuɖu ŋu, eye wòɖo fia na eɖokui.

english_verse: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah in Joram's fifth year as king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was still king of Judah.
translation_verse: Le Israel-fia Yoram, Axab vi, ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè atɔ̃lia me la, Yehoram, Yosafat vi zu fia.

english_verse: Jehoram disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He married Ahab's daughter and was as sinful as Ahab's family and the kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Eto Israel-fiawo ƒe ʋe me, eye wòwɔ nu abe Axab fiaƒome la ene elabe eɖe Axab vinyɔnu. Ewɔ nuvɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume.

english_verse: But the Lord refused to destroy Judah, because he had promised his servant David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Gake Aƒetɔ medi be yeatsrɔ̃ Yuda o, elabe edo ŋugbe na David be yeana akaɖi aɖe eya kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo tegbee.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoram did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Yoram ƒe ŋutinya mamlɛa kple nu bubu siwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Yuda-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: Jehoram died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Ahaziah then became king. King Ahaziah of Judah (
translation_verse: Yoram ku eye woɖii ɖe tɔgbuiawo gbɔ le David ƒe du la me, eye via Axazya zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Axazya zu fia le Yuda (Kron II,

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah in the twelfth year of Joram's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Le Israel-fia Yoram, Axab vi ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè wui evelia me la, Axazya, Yuda-fia Yoram vi zu fia.

english_verse: Since Ahaziah was related to Ahab's family, he acted just like them and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong.
translation_verse: Axazya tsɔ Axab fiaɖuƒomea ƒe afɔ, eye wòwɔ nuvɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume elabe enye Axab ƒome la to.

english_verse: Ahaziah went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
translation_verse: Axazya kpe ɖe Yoram, Axab vi ŋu woho aʋa ɖe Siria-fia Xazael ŋu le Ramot-Gilead, eye Siriatɔwo de abi Yoram ŋu.

english_verse: One day, Elisha called for one of the other prophets and said: Take this bottle of olive oil and get ready to go to the town of Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Tete gbeƒãɖela Elisa yɔ gbeƒãɖelawo ƒe nusrɔ̃lawo dometɔ ɖeka gblɔ nɛ be: “Bla ali dzi. Tsɔ amigoe sia ɖe asi ne nàyi Ramot-Gilead.

english_verse: When you get there, find Jehu son of Jehoshaphat and grandson of Nimshi. Take him to a place where the two of you can be alone,
translation_verse: Ne èɖo afi ma la, di Yehu, Yosafat vi, si nye Nimsi vi nàkpɔ. Ðe kpɔe tso nɔviawo dome nàkplɔe yi xɔgãme.

english_verse: then pour olive oil on his head to show that he is the new king. Say to him, “The Lord has chosen you to be king of Israel.” Then leave quickly—don't wait around for anything!
translation_verse: Tsɔ amigoe la eye nàkɔ ami ɖe tame nɛ agblɔ be: ‘Aƒetɔ be: Mesi ami na wò heɖo wò fiae ɖe Israel-dukɔ nu.’ Emegbe ʋu ʋɔa nàsí; mègalala o.”

english_verse: The young prophet left for Ramoth.
translation_verse: Ale ɖekakpui nusrɔ̃la la yi Ramot-Gilead.

english_verse: When he arrived, the army officers were meeting together. “Sir, I have a message for you,” he said. “For which one of us?” Jehu asked. “You, sir,” the prophet answered.
translation_verse: Esi wòge ɖe dua me la, aʋakɔ la ƒe amegãwo ɖi anyi. Egblɔ be: “Amegã, mexɔ gbedeasi aɖe vɛ na wò!” Yehu bia be: “Na mía dometɔ ka?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Amegã, na wò.”

english_verse: So Jehu got up and went inside. The prophet poured olive oil on Jehu's head and told him: The Lord God of Israel has this message for you: “I am the Lord, and I have chosen you to be king of my people Israel.
translation_verse: Ale Yehu tsi tsitre eye wòge ɖe xɔa me. Ðekakpuia kɔ ami la ɖe tame nɛ gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: ‘Mesi ami na wò, eye meɖo wò fiae ɖe nye dukɔ, Israel nu.

english_verse: Every man and boy in Ahab's family must die, whether slave or free.
translation_verse: Axab ƒe ƒome blibo la atsrɔ̃ gbidii. Matsrɔ̃ ŋutsuwo katã, kluviwo kple ablɔɖeviwo siaa le Israel.

english_verse: Jehu went back to his officers, and one of them asked, “What did that crazy prophet want? Is everything all right?” “You know him and how he talks,” Jehu answered.
translation_verse: Esi Yehu do va eƒe aƒetɔ ƒe dɔlawo gbɔ la, wobiae be: “Eme faa? Nu ka ta aɖaʋatɔ ma va gbɔwò ɖo?” Eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Mienya amea nyuie kple eƒe nuwɔnawo ɖe!”

english_verse: “No, we don't. What did he say?” they asked. “He had a message from the Lord,” Jehu replied. “He said that the Lord has chosen me to be the next king of Israel.”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ be: “Mele eme o, gblɔ nyaa na mí!” Ale wògblɔ na wo be: “Nya si ko wògblɔ nam lae nye esi: ‘Aƒetɔ be: Mesi ami na wò heɖo wò fiae ɖe Israel nu.’ ”

english_verse: They quickly grabbed their coats and spread them out on the steps where Jehu was standing. Someone blew a trumpet, and everyone shouted, “Jehu is king!” Jehu Kills Joram and Ahaziah
translation_verse: Enumake ame sia ame ɖe eƒe awu ɖo ɖe atrakpuiawo dzi nɛ, eye woku kpẽ ɖe gbeƒã be: “Yehu zu fia!” Wowu Israel-fia Yoram

english_verse: When the guard in the watchtower at Jezreel saw Jehu and his men riding up, he shouted to the king, “I see a large group of men coming this way.” Joram ordered, “Send someone out to ask them if this is a friendly visit.”
translation_verse: Dzɔla nɔ gbetakpɔxɔ me le Yezreel kpɔ Yehu kple eƒe amehawo gbɔna ɖa, eye wògblɔ be: “Ameha aɖe nye ekem gbɔna ɖa!” Yoram gblɔ be: “Ðe sɔdola ɖeka ɖo ɖa wòaɖabiae be: ‘Ŋutifafa yea?”

english_verse: One of the soldiers rode out and said to Jehu, “King Joram wants to know if this is a friendly visit.” “What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just stay behind me with the rest of my troops!” About the same time the guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back.”
translation_verse: Ale sɔdola la yi ɖakpe Yehu biae be: “Fia be: ‘Ŋutifafa yea?’ ” Yehu ɖo eŋu be: “Ŋutifafanya ka tsɔ gbɔwò? Dze nava nɔ megbenye.” Dzɔla la na wonya be: “Amedɔdɔ la ɖo ameawo gbɔ, gake metrɔ gbɔ kpɔ o.”

english_verse: So Joram sent out another rider, who rode up to Jehu and said, “The king wants to know if this is a friendly visit.” “What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just get behind me with the rest of my troops!”
translation_verse: Wogadɔ ame bubu ɖa wòyi wo gbɔ ɖabia be: “Fia be ‘Ŋutifafa yea?’ ” Yehu ɖo eŋu be: “Ŋutifafanya ka tsɔ gbɔwò? Dze nam mayi.”

english_verse: The guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back either. Wait a minute! That one man is a reckless chariot driver—it must be Jehu!”
translation_verse: Dzɔla la gana wonya be: “Amedɔdɔ la ɖo wo gbɔ, gake metrɔ gbɔ kpɔ o. Amea ƒe nuwɔna ɖi Yehu, Nimsi vi tɔ; ele nu wɔm abe aɖaʋatɔ ene.”

english_verse: Joram commanded, “Get my chariot ready.” Then he and Ahaziah got in their chariots and rode out to meet Jehu. They all met on the land that had belonged to Naboth.
translation_verse: Yoram gblɔ be: “Midzra ɖo.” Tete wodzra eƒe tasiaɖam ɖo. Israel-fia Yoram kple Yuda-fia Axazya dze mɔ. Wo dome ame sia ame le eya ŋutɔ ƒe tasiaɖam me yina Yehu kpe ge. Wokpee le Nabot, Yezreeltɔ ƒe agble me.

english_verse: “Ahaziah, let's get out of here!” Joram yelled. “It's a trap!” As Joram tried to escape,
translation_verse: Tete Yoram trɔ sí yina, gblɔ na Axazya be: “Axazya, dugbãnugbeɖoɖo!”

english_verse: Jehu shot an arrow. It hit Joram between his shoulders, then it went through his heart and came out his chest. He fell over dead in his chariot.
translation_verse: Yehu vu eƒe da me kple ŋusẽ katã, eye wòté abɔgbakpeƒe na Yoram. Aŋutrɔ la ƒo ɖe eƒe dzi, eye wòmu dze eƒe tasiaɖam me.

english_verse: Jehu commanded his assistant Bidkar, “Get Joram's body and throw it in the field that Naboth once owned. Do you remember when you and I used to ride side by side behind Joram's father Ahab? It was then that the Lord swore to Ahab that he would be punished in the same field where he had killed Naboth and his sons. So throw Joram's body there, just as the Lord said.”
translation_verse: ‘Le Nabot ƒe ʋu kple viawo ƒe ʋu si mekpɔ etsɔ ta la, meka atam be maɖo eteƒe na wò le teƒe sia tututu le agble sia me.’ Eya ta azɔ la, kɔe nàƒu gbe ɖe teƒe sia le agble sia me le Aƒetɔ ƒe nya la nu.” Wowu Yuda-fia Axazya (Kron II,

english_verse: Ahaziah saw all of this happen and tried to escape to the town of Beth-Haggan, but Jehu caught up with him and shouted, “Kill him too!” So his troops shot Ahaziah with an arrow while he was on the road to Gur near Ibleam. He went as far as Megiddo, where he died.
translation_verse: Esi Yuda-fia Axazya kpɔ nu si dzɔ la, esí ɖo ta Bet-Xagan lɔƒo. Yehu kplɔe ɖo le gbɔgblɔm be: “Mité eya hã!”, eye woté eya hã le tasiaɖam la me le togbɛ si le Gur le Yibleam gbɔ la dzi. Gake Axazya te kpɔ sí yi Megido, eye wòɖaku ɖe afi ma.

english_verse: Ahaziah's officers put his body in a chariot and took it back to Jerusalem, where they buried him beside his ancestors.
translation_verse: Eŋumewo kɔe ɖe tasiaɖam me yi Yerusalem ɖaɖi ɖe eƒe yɔdo me le tɔgbuiawo gbɔ le David ƒe dua me.

english_verse: Ahaziah had become king of Judah in the eleventh year of the rule of Ahab's son Joram. Jehu Kills Jezebel
translation_verse: Axazya zu fia le Yuda esime fia Yoram, Axab vi le eƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè wui ɖekɛlia me. Wowu fianyɔnu Izebel

english_verse: Jehu headed toward Jezreel, and when Jezebel heard he was coming, she put on eye shadow and brushed her hair. Then she stood at the window, waiting for him to arrive.
translation_verse: Emegbe Yehu va Yezreel. Esi Izebel see la, ede ɖuŋkui ŋku, ɖo atsyɔ̃ na eƒe ta, eye wòdo mo ɖe fesre nu.

english_verse: As he walked through the city gate, she shouted down to him, “Why did you come here, you murderer? To kill the king? You're no better than Zimri!”
translation_verse: Esi Yehu to agboa nu le gegem ɖe eme la, Izebel gblɔ be: “Zimri, wò, wò aƒetɔ wula, ŋutifafa yea?”

english_verse: He looked up toward the window and asked, “Is anyone up there on my side?” A few palace workers stuck their heads out of a window,
