english_verse: The priests agreed that they would not collect any more money or be in charge of the temple repairs.
translation_verse: Ale nunɔlaawo lɔ̃ be yewomagaxɔ ga aɖeke azɔ o, eye yewomaɖɔ xɔa ƒe gbagbãƒeawo hã ɖo o.

english_verse: Jehoiada found a wooden box; he cut a hole in the top of it and set it on the right side of the altar where people went into the temple. Whenever someone gave money to the temple, the priests guarding the entrance would put it into this box.
translation_verse: Tete nunɔla Yehoyada tsɔ aɖaka aɖe, ŋɔ do ɖe nutuvia ŋu, eye wòtsɔe ɖo vɔsamlekpui la xa, le ɖusime gome, ne ame ge ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe xɔ la me. Nunɔla siwo le mɔnu dzɔm la tsɔa ga siwo katã amewo va na la dea aɖaka la me.

english_verse: When the box was full of money, the king's secretary and the chief priest would count the money and put it in bags.
translation_verse: Ne wokpɔ be ga si le aɖakaa me la sɔ gbɔ la, ekema fiaa ƒe agbalẽŋlɔla kple nunɔlagã la vana eye woblaa ga si wokpɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒeme la xlẽna.

english_verse: Then they would give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. Some of the money was used to pay the builders, the woodworkers,
translation_verse: Wodaa ga la, eye wotsɔnɛ dea asi na Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe ƒe dɔdzikpɔlawo. Woawo tsɔnɛ xea fee na atikpalawo kple xɔtulawo.

english_verse: the stonecutters, and the men who built the walls. And some was used to buy wood and stone and to pay any other costs for repairing the temple.
translation_verse: Woxea fe na gliɖolawo kple kpefúlawo hã, eye woƒle ati kple kpe kpakple nu siwo katã hiã na xɔ la ɖɔɖɔɖo la.

english_verse: While the repairs were being made, the money that was given to the temple was not used to make silver bowls, lamp snuffers, small sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or anything gold or silver for the temple.
translation_verse: Ke wometsɔ ga si wokpɔ tso Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me la wɔ klosalogbawo, akaɖitsinuwo, agbawo, kpẽwo, sikanuwo kple klosalonuwo ya o.

english_verse: It went only to pay for repairs.
translation_verse: Ke boŋ wotsɔe na dɔwɔlawo wotsɔ dzra Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ɖoe.

english_verse: The men in charge were honest, so no one had to keep track of the money.
translation_verse: Womebia akɔnta tso ame siwo si me wotsɔ ga la dee o, elabe woka ɖe wo dzi.

english_verse: About the same time, King Hazael of Syria attacked the town of Gath and captured it. Next, he decided to attack Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, Siria-fia Xazael ho aʋa ɖe Gat ŋu, eye wòɖu edzi. Xazael ɖoe be yeawɔ aʋa kple Yerusalem hã.

english_verse: So Joash collected everything he and his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah had dedicated to the Lord, as well as the gold in the storage rooms in the temple and palace. He sent it all to Hazael as a gift, and when Hazael received it, he ordered his troops to leave Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Tete Yuda-fia Yoas tsɔ tɔgbuiawo, Yuda-fiawo: Yosafat, Yoram kple Axazya, ƒe nu tɔxɛ siwo katã wotsɔ na Aƒetɔ kple eya ŋutɔ tɔ kpakple sika siwo katã le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ƒe nudzraɖoƒe la ɖo ɖe Siria-fia Xazael. Ale wòtrɔ dzo le Yerusalem ŋu. Fia Yoas ƒe ku

english_verse: Everything else Joash did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Fia Yoas ƒe ŋutinya mamlɛa kple nu siwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Yuda-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: At the end of his rule, some of his officers rebelled against him. Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer murdered him in a building where the land was filled in on the east side of Jerusalem, near the road to Silla. Joash was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Amaziah became king.
translation_verse: Yozaxar, Simeat vi kple Yozabad, Somer vi, ame siwo nye eƒe dɔlawo lae wui. Woɖii ɖe tɔgbuiawo gbɔ le David ƒe du la me, eye via Amazya zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king of Israel in the twenty-third year of Joash's rule in Judah. Jehoahaz ruled
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Yoas, Axazya vi ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè bla eve vɔ etɔ̃lia me la, Yoaxaz, Yehu vi zu fia ɖe Israel nu. Eɖu fia le Samaria ƒe wui adrẽ.

english_verse: and said, “Open the window facing east.” When it was open, Elisha shouted, “Now shoot!” Jehoash shot an arrow and Elisha said, “That arrow is a sign that the Lord will help you completely defeat the Syrian army at Aphek.”
translation_verse: Elisa gblɔ nɛ be: “Ʋu fesre si le ɣedzeƒe gome!” Eʋui. Elisa gblɔ nɛ be: “Dae!” Edae. Tete Elisa gblɔ nɛ be: “Dziɖuɖu ƒe aŋutrɔ tso Aƒetɔ gbɔe. Aŋutrɔ si aɖu Siria-dukɔ dzi! Àwɔ aʋa kple Siriatɔwo le Afek va se ɖe esime nàtsrɔ̃ wo.”

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He never stopped following the example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nuvɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Ekplɔ Yerobeam, Nebat vi, ame si na Israel wɔ nuvɔ̃ la ƒe nuvɔ̃ ɖo, eye meɖe asi le eŋu o.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with the Israelites, so he let King Hazael of Syria and his son Benhadad rule over them for a long time.
translation_verse: Esia na Aƒetɔ do dɔmedzoe ɖe eŋu, eye wòtsɔ wo de asi na Siria-fia Xazael kple via Ben-Hadad, zi geɖe.

english_verse: Jehoahaz prayed to the Lord for help, and the Lord saw how terribly Hazael was treating the Israelites. He answered Jehoahaz
translation_verse: Gake Yoaxaz ɖe kuku na Aƒetɔ, eye Aƒetɔ see nɛ, elabe eya ŋutɔ hã kpɔ ale si Siria-fia te Israel ɖe anyii.

english_verse: by sending Israel a leader who rescued them from the Syrians, and the Israelites lived in peace as they had before.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ na xɔnametɔ Israel, eye wodo le Siriatɔwo si me. Ale Israelviwo nɔ anyi le ŋutifafa me abe tsã ene.

english_verse: Jehoash became king of Israel in the thirty-seventh year of Joash's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Yoas ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè bla etɔ̃ vɔ adrẽlia me la, Yoas, Yoaxaz vi zu fia ɖe Israel nu. Eɖu fia le Samaria ƒe wui ade.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoahaz did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Yoaxaz ƒe ŋutinya mamlɛa, nu siwo katã wòwɔ kple eƒe kalẽwɔwɔwo la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: Jehoahaz died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoash became king. King Jehoash of Israel
translation_verse: Yoaxaz ku, eye woɖii ɖe Samaria, eye via Yoas va zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Yoas zu fia le Israel

english_verse: “Grab a bow and some arrows,” Elisha told him, “and hold them in your hand.” Jehoash grabbed the bow and arrows and held them. Elisha placed his hand on the king's hand
translation_verse: Egblɔ na Israel-fia be: “He da la me.” Ehe eme, eye Elisa tsɔ asi ɖo fia la ƒe asi dzi.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord by doing just like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nuvɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Meɖe asi le Yerobeam, Nebat vi ƒe nuvɔ̃ siwo katã wòwɔ, siwo me wòkplɔ Israel dee la ŋu o; ke boŋ ewɔ wo.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his war against King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Yoas ƒe ŋutinya mamlɛa, nu siwo katã wòwɔ kple ale si wòwɔ aʋa kple Yuda-fia Amazya la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria beside the other Israelite kings. His son Jeroboam then became king. Elisha the Prophet Dies
translation_verse: Yoas ku eye Yerobeam zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Woɖi Yoas ɖe Israel-fiawo gbɔ le Samaria. Elisa ƒe ku

english_verse: Some time before the death of King Jehoash, Elisha the prophet was very sick and about to die. Jehoash went in and stood beside him, crying. He said, “Master, what will Israel's chariots and cavalry be able to do without you?”
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, Elisa dze kudɔ. Gbe ɖeka Israel-fia Yoas yi egbɔ be yeaɖakpɔe ɖa. Esi wòɖo la, Yoas fa avi be: “Tɔ́nyee! Tɔ́nyee! Israel ƒe tasiaɖam kple sɔdolawo loo!”

english_verse: Elisha said, “Pick up the arrows and hit the ground with them.” Jehoash grabbed the arrows and hit the ground three times, then stopped.
translation_verse: Elisa gagblɔ be: “Fɔ aŋutrɔawo!” Efɔ wo. Egblɔ na Israel-fia be: “Tsɔ wo ƒo anyigbae.” Etsɔ wo ƒo anyigba zi etɔ̃, eye wòtɔ.

english_verse: Elisha became angry with the king and exclaimed, “If you had struck it five or six times, you would completely wipe out the Syrians. Now you will defeat them only three times.”
translation_verse: Tete Mawu ƒe ame la do dziku ɖe eŋu gblɔ be: “Zi atɔ̃ alo zi adee nàƒoe hafi, anye ne àɖu Siriatɔwo dzi va se ɖe esime woatsrɔ̃ avɔ. Ke azɔ la, zi etɔ̃ ko nàsi Siriatɔwo.”

english_verse: Elisha died and was buried. Every year in the spring, Moab's leaders sent raiding parties into Israel.
translation_verse: Emegbe Elisa ku, eye woɖii. Ƒè sia ƒè la, Moabitɔwo ƒe adzohawo vaa Israel-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Once, while some Israelites were burying a man's body, they saw a group of Moabites. The Israelites quickly threw the body into Elisha's tomb and ran away. As soon as the man's body touched the bones of Elisha, the man came back to life and stood up. Israel Defeats Syria
translation_verse: Eva eme be amewo le ŋutsu aɖe ɖim, kasia wokpɔ adzoha aɖe gbɔna. Ale wotsɔ ŋutsu la ƒu gbe ɖe Elisa ƒe yɔdo me. Esi ame kukua ka Elisa ƒe ƒuwo ŋu ko la, egbɔ agbe, eye wòtso ɖe afɔ dzi. Aʋa dzɔ ɖe Israel kple Siria dome

english_verse: Israel was under the power of King Hazael of Syria during the entire rule of Jehoahaz.
translation_verse: Siria-fia Xazael te Israel ɖe anyi le Yoaxaz ƒe ŋkekewo katã me.

english_verse: But the Lord was kind to the Israelites and showed them mercy because of his solemn agreement with their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. In fact, he has never turned his back on them or let them be completely destroyed.
translation_verse: Gake Aƒetɔ va ve wo nu, eye wòkpɔ nublanui na wo. Etrɔ ɖe wo ŋu le nu si Aƒetɔ bla kple Abraham, Isak kple Yakob la ta. Medi be yeatsrɔ̃ wo o, eye meɖe wo ɖa le eŋkume va se ɖe fifi o.

english_verse: Hazael died, and his son Benhadad then became king of Syria.
translation_verse: Siria-fia Xazael ku, eye via Ben-Hadad zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: King Jehoash of Israel attacked and defeated the Syrian army three times. He took back from Benhadad all the towns Hazael had captured in battle from his father Jehoahaz.
translation_verse: Tete Yoas, Yoaxaz vi gaxɔ du siwo Xazael xɔ le tɔ́a Yoaxaz si le aʋa me la le via Ben-Hadad si. Yoas sii zi etɔ̃, eye wògbugbɔ Israel-duwo xɔ.

english_verse: Jeroboam extended the boundaries of Israel from Lebo-Hamath in the north to the Dead Sea in the south, just as the Lord had promised his servant Jonah son of Amittai, who was a prophet from Gath-Hepher.
translation_verse: Egbugbɔ Israel ƒe liƒowo ɖo te tso Xamat-mɔnu va se ɖe tagbaƒu la nu, abe ale si Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la gblɔ to eƒe dɔla Yona, Amitai, gbeƒãɖela la si tso Gat-Xefer ƒe vi dzi ene.

english_verse: Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah in the second year of Jehoash's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Le Yoas Yoaxaz vi si nye Israel-fia ƒe ƒè evelia me la, Yuda-fia, Amazya, Yoas vi la dze fiaɖuɖu gɔme.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nu si nye nuvɔ̃ɖi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume; metrɔ tso nuvɔ̃ siwo katã Yerobeam, Nebat vi la wɔ tsɔ kplɔ Israel de nuvɔ̃ me la gbɔ o.

english_verse: Jeroboam died and was buried, and his son Zechariah became king.
translation_verse: Yerobeam trɔ megbe hemlɔ tɔgbuia Israel-fiawo gbɔ. Via Zaxarya zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Amaziah followed the example of his father Joash by obeying the Lord and doing right. But he was not as faithful as his ancestor David.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nu si dzɔ la le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, ke mewɔe abe tɔgbuia David ene o. Ewɔ nuwo katã abe ale si tɔ́a Yoas wɔe ene.

english_verse: Amaziah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ke womeɖe nuxeƒewo ɖa o, dukɔ la ganɔ vɔ sam le nuxeƒewo.

english_verse: As soon as Amaziah had control of Judah, he arrested and killed the officers who had murdered his father.
translation_verse: Esi fiaɖuɖu ŋusẽ nyagbe su esi teti ko la, ewu eƒe dɔla siwo wu tɔ́a si nye fia la.

english_verse: But the children of those officers were not killed. The Lord had commanded in the Law of Moses that only the people who sinned were to be punished, not their parents or children.
translation_verse: Ke abe ale si Aƒetɔ de se woŋlɔ ɖe Mose ƒe segbalẽa me ene be: “Womawu tɔ́ ɖe vi teƒe loo, alo vi ɖe tɔ́a teƒe o, ke ame sia ame aku ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe nuvɔ̃ ta” la, mewu ame siwo do hlɔ̃ la viwo o.

english_verse: Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. Go ahead and celebrate—but stay at home. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ele eme baa be nèƒo Edom eye wò dzi do wò ɖe dzi. Wò bubu neɖi ƒo na wò, eye nànɔ aƒe, elabe nu ka tae nàdɔ avu be xaxa naxlã wò kple Yuda siaa ɖe anyi?”

english_verse: One day, Amaziah sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
translation_verse: Amazya dɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Israel-fia Yoas, Yoaxaz vi, si nye Yehu vi be: “Va ne miado go ŋkume kple ŋkume.”

english_verse: Jehoash sent back this reply: Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon announced that his son was going to marry the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
translation_verse: Israel-fia, Yoas ɖo gbe ɖe Amazya, Yuda-fia be: “Ŋuve le Lebanon dzi dɔ sederti le Lebanon dzi be, ‘Tsɔ viwò nyɔnu na vinye ŋutsu ne wòaɖe.’ Gbemelã aɖe tso Lebanon tso eme va yi, eye wònya avuzi le ŋuve la dzi.

english_verse: But Amaziah refused to listen. So Jehoash and his troops marched to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops.
translation_verse: Ke Amazya gbe toɖoɖo. Ale Israel-fia, Yoas ho yi eya kple Amazya kpe akɔ kple wo nɔewo le aʋa me le Bet-Semes si nye Yuda tɔ la.

english_verse: During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home,
translation_verse: Israel ɖu Yuda dzi eye ame sia ame sí yi eƒe aƒeme.

english_verse: and Jehoash captured Amaziah. Jehoash then marched to Jerusalem and broke down the city wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a section nearly
translation_verse: Israel-fia lé Amazya Yuda-fia, Axazya vi, si nye Yoas vi le Bet-Semes. Ekplɔe va Yerusalem. Egbã Yerusalem-gli la tso Efrayim-gbo nu va se ɖe Dzogoedzigbo la gbɔ. Glia ƒe didime nye meta alafa eve.

english_verse: He took the gold and silver, as well as everything of value from the Lord's temple and the king's treasury. He took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Eɖo asi sika kple klosalo kple kplu siwo katã wòkpɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me kple fia ƒe nudzraɖoƒe la dzi, lɔ wo kpe ɖe aʋalélewo ŋu hekplɔ va Samaria.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he defeated King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Azɔ Yoas ƒe nuwɔna mamlɛa siwo wòwɔ, eƒe kalẽwɔwɔ, kple ale si wòwɔ aʋa kple Yuda-fia Amazya la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: After his death the people of Judah made his son Azariah king, even though he was only
translation_verse: Yuda-dukɔ blibo la lé Azarya, ame si xɔ ƒe wui ade la ɖo fiae ɖe tɔ́a Amazya teƒe.

english_verse: Azariah was the one who later recaptured and rebuilt the town of Elath. King Jeroboam the Second of Israel
translation_verse: Eyae tsò Elat gatsɔ na Yuda esime fia la trɔ megbe yi tɔgbuiawo gbɔ. Israel-fia Yerobeam evelia

english_verse: Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel in the fifteenth year of Amaziah's rule in Judah. Jeroboam ruled
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Amazya, Yoas vi ƒe ƒè wui atɔ̃lia me la, Yerobeam, Israel-fia Yoas vi dze fiaɖuɖu gɔme le Samaria. Eɖu fia ƒe bla ene vɔ ɖekɛ.

english_verse: The Lord helped Jeroboam do this because he had seen how terribly the Israelites were suffering, whether slave or free, and no one was left to help them.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ kpɔ be Israel ƒe fukpekpe sesẽ ŋutɔ, elabe ame aɖeke megasusɔ o. Ame aɖeke megali si nye kluvi loo, alo ablɔɖevi akpe ɖe Israel ŋu o.

english_verse: And since the Lord had promised that he would not let Israel be completely destroyed, he helped Jeroboam rescue them.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ megblɔ be yeatutu Israel ƒe ŋkɔ ɖa le dziƒoa te o, ale wòɖe wo to Yerobeam, Yoas vi ƒe asi dzi.

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he recaptured the towns of Damascus and Hamath, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Azɔ Yerobeam ƒe ŋutinya mamlɛa, nu siwo katã wòwɔ, eƒe kalẽwɔwɔ, ale si wòwɔ aʋa kple ale si wògaxɔ Damasko kple Xamat siwo nye Yuda tɔ tsã na Israel la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: Everything else Pekahiah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Pekah of Israel
translation_verse: Azɔ, Pekax ƒe nuwɔna mamlɛawo kple nu siwo katã wòwɔ la, kpɔ ɖa, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me. Israel-fia Pekax

english_verse: Pekahiah became king of Israel in the fiftieth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Azarya ƒe ƒè bla etɔ̃lia me la, Pekaxya, Menaxem vi dze fiaɖuɖu gɔme ɖe Israel dzi le Samaria. Eɖu fia ƒe eve.

english_verse: Azariah obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nu si dze la le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, abe ale si tɔ́a Amazya wɔ pɛpɛpɛ la ene.

english_verse: But Azariah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Negbe ɖeko womeɖe nuxeƒewo ɖa o; dukɔ la ganɔa vɔ sam, eye wotɔa dzo lifi le nuxeƒeawo.

english_verse: The Lord punished Azariah with leprosy for the rest of his life. He wasn't allowed to live in the royal palace, so his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
translation_verse: Ewɔ esia elabe David wɔ nu si dzɔ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, eye le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me la, megbe nu si wòwɔ nɛ la dzi wɔwɔ o, negbe le Uriya, Xititɔ la, ƒe nya me ko.

english_verse: Everything else Azariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Aʋa si gɔme Rexabeam kple Yerobeam dze la yi edzi le Abiyam ƒe fiaɖuɣi la katã.

english_verse: Azariah died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Jotham then became king. King Zechariah of Israel
translation_verse: Azarya trɔ megbe eye woɖii ɖe tɔgbuiawo gbɔ le David ƒe du la me. Via Yotam zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Israel-fia Zaxarya

english_verse: Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, but he ruled only six months from Samaria.
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Azarya ƒe ƒè bla etɔ̃ vɔ enyilia me la, Zaxarya, Yerobeam vi ɖu fia ɖe Israel dzi ɣleti ade.

english_verse: Shallum son of Jabesh plotted against Zechariah and killed him in public. Shallum then became king.
translation_verse: Salum, Yaabes vi ɖo nugbe ɖe eŋu. Exlã nu ɖee ƒu anyi hewui le Yibleam, eye wòzu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: So the Lord had kept his promise to Jehu that the next four kings of Israel would come from his family. Everything else Zechariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Shallum of Israel
translation_verse: Esia nye ŋugbe si Aƒetɔ do na Yehu be: “Viwòwo anɔ Israel-fiazikpui la dzi va se ɖe dzidzime enelia dzi.” Eva eme nenema pɛ. Israel-fia Salum

english_verse: Shallum became king of Israel in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's rule in Judah. But only one month after Shallum became king,
translation_verse: Salum, Yabes vi ɖu fia le Samaria, le Yuda-fia Uziya ƒe ƒè bla etɔ̃ vɔ asiekelia me. Ɣleti ɖekae wòɖu fia.

english_verse: Menahem became king of Israel in Azariah's thirty-ninth year as king of Judah, and he ruled Israel ten years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Azarya ƒe ƒè bla etɔ̃ vɔ asiekelia me la, Menaxem, Gad vi dze fiaɖuɖu ɖe Israel dzi gɔme. Eɖu fia ƒè ewo le Samaria.

english_verse: He constantly disobeyed the Lord by following the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nu si nye nuvɔ̃ɖi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me la, meɖe asi le Yerobeam, Nebat vi la ƒe nuvɔ̃ siwo wòwɔ tsɔ kplɔ Israel de nuvɔ̃ me la ŋu o.

english_verse: During Menahem's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria invaded Israel. He agreed to help Menahem keep control of his kingdom, if Menahem would pay him over
translation_verse: Asiria-fia Pul va dze anyigba la dzi. Menaxem tsɔ klosalo kilo akpe bla etɔ̃ vɔ ene na Pul be wòade ye dzi ne fiaɖuɖu la nali ke ɖe ye si me.

english_verse: Jotham followed the example of his father by obeying the Lord and doing right.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nu si dzɔ la le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, abe ale si tɔ́a Uziya wɔ pɛpɛpɛ la ene.

english_verse: Everything else Menahem did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Azɔ Menaxem ƒe nuwɔna mamlɛawo kple nu siwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king. King Pekahiah of Israel
translation_verse: Menaxem trɔ megbe yi tɔgbuiawo gbɔ, eye via Pekaxya zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Israel-fia Pekaxya

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and caused the Israelites to sin, just as Jeroboam son of Nebat had done.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nu si nye nuvɔ̃ɖi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Metrɔ tso Yerobeam, Nebat vi la ƒe nuvɔ̃ si wòna Israel wɔ la gbɔ o.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and followed the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nu si nye nuvɔ̃ɖi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Metrɔ tso Yerobeam, Nebat vi la ƒe nuvɔ̃ si wòna Israel wɔ la gbɔ o.

english_verse: During Pekah's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria marched into Israel. He captured the territories of Gilead and Galilee, including the towns of Ijon, Abel-Bethmaacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, as well as the entire territory of Naphtali. Then he took Israelites from those regions to Assyria as prisoners.
translation_verse: Le Israel-fia Pekax ƒe ɣeyiɣi me la, Asiria-fia Tiglat-Pileser va si Yion, Abel-Bet-Maaxa, Yanoax, Kedes, Xazor, Gilead kple Galilea, Naftali-nyigba bliboa, eye wòɖe aboyo ameawo yi Asiria.

english_verse: In the twentieth year of Jotham's rule in Judah, Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah and murdered him. Hoshea then became king of Israel.
translation_verse: Tete Xosea, Ela vi ɖo nugbe ɖe Pekax, Remalya vi la ŋu. Exlã nu ɖee ƒu anyi hewui, eye wòzu fia ɖe eteƒe le Yotam, Uziya vi ƒe ƒè bla evelia me.

english_verse: Everything else Pekah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Jotham of Judah (
translation_verse: Azɔ Pekax ƒe nuwɔna mamlɛawo kple nu siwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me. Yuda-fia Yotam

english_verse: Jotham son of Azariah became king of Judah in the second year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Le Israel-fia Pekax, Remalya vi ƒe ƒè evelia me la, Yuda-fia Yotam, Uziya vi la dze fiaɖuɖu gɔme.

english_verse: It was Jotham who rebuilt the Upper Gate that led into the court around the Lord's temple. But the local shrines were not destroyed, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Negbe ɖeko womeɖe nuxeƒewo ɖa o; dukɔ la gasaa vɔ, eye wotɔa dzo lifi le nuxeƒeawo. Eyae de Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ƒe dzigbegbo la.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Azɔ Yotam ƒe nuwɔna mamlɛawo kple nu siwo katã wòwɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Yuda-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: During his rule, the Lord let King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel start attacking Judah.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke mawo me la, Aƒetɔ de asi Siria-fia, Rezin kple Pekax, Remalya vi la dɔdɔ me ɖe Yuda ŋu.

english_verse: Jotham died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Yotam trɔ megbe, woɖii ɖe tɔgbuiawo gbɔ ɖe tɔgbuia David ƒe du la me. Via Axaz zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah in the seventeenth year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Le Pekax, Remalya vi ƒe ƒè wui adrẽlia me la, Yuda-fia Axaz, Yotam vi la dze fiaɖuɖu gɔme.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Hezekiah became king.
translation_verse: Axaz trɔ megbe yi tɔgbuiawo gbɔ, eye woɖii ɖe tɔgbuiawo gbɔ le David ƒe du la me. Via Xizkiya zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: and was even more sinful than the kings of Israel. He sacrificed his own son, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
translation_verse: Ke eto Israel-fiawo ƒe afɔtoƒe. Etɔ dzo via ŋutsu gɔ̃ abe vɔsa ene, ɖe ŋunyɔnu siwo dukɔ siwo Aƒetɔ nyà ɖa le Israel dukɔ la ŋgɔ la, ƒe kɔnuwo nu.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Esa vɔ eye wotɔ dzo lifi le nuxeƒewo, le togbɛwo dzi kple le ati dama ɖe sia ɖe te.

english_verse: Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria that said, “Your Majesty, King Rezin and King Pekah are attacking me, your loyal servant. Please come and rescue me.”
translation_verse: Ale Axaz dɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Asiria-fia Tiglat-Pileser be: “Wò dɔla kple viwò ŋutsue menye. Va, ne nàɖem tso Siria-fia kple Israel-fia ame siwo ho aʋa ɖe ŋunye la si me.”

english_verse: Along with the message, Ahaz sent silver and gold from the Lord's temple and from the palace treasury as a gift for the Assyrian king.
translation_verse: Axaz gatsɔ klosalo kple sika siwo wokpɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me kple esi le fia ƒe nudzraɖoƒe hã wɔ nunanae ɖo ɖe Asiria-fia.

english_verse: As soon as Tiglath Pileser received the message, he and his troops marched to Syria. He captured the capital city of Damascus, then he took the people living there to the town of Kir as prisoners and killed King Rezin.
translation_verse: Asiria-fia ɖo toe; Asiria-fia ho aʋa ɖe Damasko ŋu, eye wòxɔe. Eɖe aboyo eƒe amewo kplɔ yi Kir, eye wòwu Rezin.

english_verse: Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one.
translation_verse: Esi fia Axaz yi Damasko be yeaɖado go Asiria-fia, Tiglat-Pileser la, ekpɔ vɔsamlekpui si le Damasko la. Fia Axaz tsɔ vɔsamlekpui la ƒe nɔnɔmetata kple ɖoɖo si nu tututu wowɔe ɖo la ɖo ɖe nunɔla Uriya, wòde le go sia go me.

english_verse: Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
translation_verse: Nunɔla Uriya ɖi vɔsamlekpui la pɛpɛpɛ abe ale si fia Axaz ɖoe ɖa tso Damasko la ene. Ale nunɔla Uriya wɔe hafi fia Axaz gbɔ tso Damasko.

english_verse: When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar
translation_verse: Esi fia la gbɔ tso Damasko la, fia la lé ŋku ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ŋu. Tete fia la te ɖe eŋu eye wòde edzi.

english_verse: and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings.
translation_verse: Eme eƒe numemevɔsa kple nuɖuɖuvɔsa le edzi; ekɔ eƒe nunonovɔsa ɖe edzi, hehlẽ eƒe ŋutifafavɔsa ƒe ʋu ɖe vɔsamlekpui la dzi.

english_verse: After that, he had the bronze altar moved aside, so his new altar would be right in front of the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Ete akɔblivɔsamlekpui si nɔ Aƒetɔ ŋkume, si dze ŋgɔ xɔa la ɖa tso eƒe vɔsamlekpui la kple Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la dome, eye wòtsɔe da ɖe eƒe vɔsamlekpui la ƒe dzigbeme lɔƒo.

english_verse: He told Uriah the priest: From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
translation_verse: Fia Axaz de se na nunɔla Uriya be: “Vɔsamlekpui gã la dzie nàsa ŋdi numemevɔsa kple fiẽ nuɖuɖuvɔsa fia ƒe numemevɔsa kple nuɖuɖuvɔsa, kpakple dukɔ hahoo la le anyigba la dzi ƒe numemevɔsa, nuɖuɖuvɔsa, kple nunonovɔsa le. Eya dzie nàkɔ woƒe numemevɔsa kple vɔsawo katã ƒe ʋuwo ɖo. Ke akɔblivɔsamlekpui la nanɔ anyi nam manɔ nu biam le egbɔ.”

english_verse: He took down the special tent that was used for worship on the Sabbath and closed up the private entrance that the kings of Judah used for going into the temple. He did all these things to please Tiglath Pileser.
translation_verse: Eɖe dzudzɔgbe kpata si wotu ɖe fiasã la me kple fia ƒe toƒe si le gota gome la ɖa le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ŋu le Asiria-fia ta.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Azɔ Axaz ƒe nuwɔna mamlɛ siwo wòwɔ la woŋlɔ wo ɖe “Yuda-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ” la me.

english_verse: Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz's rule in Judah, and he ruled nine years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Axaz ƒe ƒè wui evelia me la, Hosea, Ela vi, dze fiaɖuɖu gɔme le Samaria ɖe Israel dzi, eye wòɖu fia ƒè asieke.

english_verse: Hoshea disobeyed the Lord and sinned, but not as much as the earlier Israelite kings had done.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, ke menye abe Israel-fia siwo do ŋgɔ nɛ la ene o.

english_verse: During Hoshea's rule, King Shalmaneser of Assyria invaded Israel; he took control of the country and made Hoshea pay taxes.
translation_verse: Asiria-fia Salmanaser tso ɖe eŋu, eye Hosea zu eƒe dɔla hedzɔ nu nɛ.

english_verse: But later, Hoshea refused to pay the taxes and asked King So of Egypt to help him rebel. When Shalmaneser found out, he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison. Samaria Is Destroyed and the Israelites Are Taken to Assyria
translation_verse: Ke Asiria-fia kpɔ be Hosea ɖo nugbe ɖe ye ŋu, elabe edɔ ame ɖo ɖe Egipte-fia So, eye megadzɔa nu na Asiria-fia ƒe sia ƒe abe tsã ene o. Eya ta Asiria-fia lée, eye wòblae tsɔ de gaxɔ me. Woɖe aboyo Samaria

english_verse: Shalmaneser invaded Israel and attacked the city of Samaria for three years,
translation_verse: Tete Asiria-fia ho va anyigba blibo la dzi, eye wòho ɖe Samaria ŋu heɖe to ɖee ƒe etɔ̃.

english_verse: All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods,
translation_verse: Enɔ alea elabe Israel-dukɔ wɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu si kplɔ wo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi ɖe wo tso Egipte Fiagã si me eye wovɔ̃ mawu bubuwo.

english_verse: followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel, and were just as sinful as the Israelite kings.
translation_verse: Wozɔ le dukɔ siwo Aƒetɔ nyà ɖa le wo ŋgɔ la ƒe kɔnuwo nu kple kɔnu siwo Israel-fiawo to vɛ la nu.

english_verse: Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Israel-dukɔ wɔ nuwo le bebeme ɖe Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la ŋu siwo medze o. Wotu nuxeƒewo na wo ɖokui ɖe duwo katã me tso gbetakpɔxɔ gbɔ va ɖo du sesẽ la gbɔ.

english_verse: They also built stone images of foreign gods and set up sacred poles for the worship of Asherah on every hill and under every shady tree.
translation_verse: Woli aƒeliwo kple nyɔnumawu Aserawo ɖe togbɛ kɔkɔwo katã dzi kple ati damawo katã te,

english_verse: They offered sacrifices at the shrines, just as the foreign nations had done before the Lord forced them out of Israel. They did sinful things that made the Lord very angry.
translation_verse: eye wotɔ dzo lifi le nuxeƒeawo katã abe dukɔ siwo Aƒetɔ nyà ɖa le wo ŋgɔ ene. Wowɔ nuvɔ̃ɖiwo tsɔ do dziku na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: Even though the Lord had commanded the Israelites not to worship idols, they did it anyway.
translation_verse: Wosubɔ legbawo, siwo ŋu Aƒetɔ gblɔ le na wo be: “Migawɔ nu sia o.”

english_verse: So the Lord made sure that every prophet warned Israel and Judah with these words: “I, the Lord, command you to stop doing sinful things and start obeying my laws and teachings! I gave them to your ancestors, and I told my servants the prophets to repeat them to you.”
translation_verse: Evɔ la Aƒetɔ gbe nya na Israel kple Yuda to eƒe gbeƒãɖelawo kple nukpɔla ɖe sia ɖe dzi be: “Mitrɔ tso miaƒe mɔ vɔ̃wo dzi, eye milé nye sededewo kple ɖoɖowo me ɖe asi, abe ale si mede se na na mia tɔgbuiwo ene kple esi meɖo ɖe mi to nye dɔla gbeƒãɖelawo dzi.”

english_verse: But the Israelites would not listen; they were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to worship the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Ke womeɖo to o hafi boŋ wosẽ tame abe wo tɔgbui siwo mexɔ Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu dzi se o la ene.

english_verse: They ignored the Lord's warnings and commands, and they rejected the solemn agreement he had made with their ancestors. They worshiped worthless idols and became worthless themselves. The Lord had told the Israelites not to do the things that the foreign nations around them were doing, but Israel became just like them.
translation_verse: Wodo vlo eƒe ɖoɖowo kple nu, si wòbla kple wo tɔgbuiwo kple eƒe nyagbenamewo. Wodze alakpalegbawo yome eye wozu alakpanuwɔlawo ale be wodze dukɔ siwo ƒo xlã wo la yome, evɔ wònye Aƒetɔ de se na wo be womegawɔ abe woawo ene o hafi.

english_verse: The people of Israel disobeyed all the commands of the Lord their God. They made two gold statues of calves and set up a sacred pole for Asherah; they also worshiped the stars and the god Baal.
translation_verse: Wogblẽ Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la ƒe sededewo katã ɖi, eye wokɔ legbawo siwo nye nyivi eve. Wowɔ nyɔnumawu Aserawo, eye wode ta agu na dziƒo ŋu nuwo katã, eye wosubɔ Baal.

english_verse: They used magic and witchcraft and even sacrificed their own children. The Israelites were determined to do whatever the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Wome wo viŋutsuwo kple wo vinyɔnuwo le dzo me sa vɔe, woka afa, sa dzo. Wotsɔ wo ɖokui ƒle na nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume tsɔ do dziku nɛ.

english_verse: The Lord became so furious with the people of Israel that he allowed them to be carried away as prisoners. Only the people living in Judah were left,
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ do dziku ɖe Israel ŋu vevie, eye wòɖe wo ɖa le eƒe ŋku ta; wo dometɔ aɖeke mesusɔ o, negbe Yuda-to la ko.

english_verse: but they also disobeyed the Lord's commands and acted like the Israelites.
translation_verse: Yuda hã melé Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu la ƒe sededewo me ɖe asi o, ke boŋ wozɔ le kɔnu siwo Israel to vɛ la nu.

english_verse: So the Lord turned his back on everyone in Israel and let them be punished and defeated until no one was left.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ gbe Israel ƒe dzidzimeviwo katã eye wòwɔ fu wo hetsɔ wo de asi na nugblẽlawo va se ɖe esime wòɖe wo ɖa le eƒe ŋku ta.

english_verse: Earlier, when the Lord took the northern tribes away from David's family, the people living in northern Israel chose Jeroboam son of Nebat as their king. Jeroboam caused the Israelites to sin and to stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Esi wòfe Israel ɖa tso David ƒe aƒeme ŋu la, wotsɔ Yerobeam, Nebat vi la, ɖo fiae. Yerobeam ɖe Israel ɖa le Aƒetɔ yome eye wòna wowɔ nuvɔ̃ gã aɖe.

english_verse: The people kept on sinning like Jeroboam,
translation_verse: Israel-dukɔ wɔ nuvɔ̃ siwo katã Yerobeam wɔ la, womeɖe asi le wo ŋu o,

english_verse: until the Lord got rid of them, just as he had warned his servants the prophets. That's why the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners to Assyria, and that's where they remained. Foreigners Are Resettled in Israel
translation_verse: va se ɖe esime Aƒetɔ ɖe Israel ɖa le eƒe ŋku ta, abe ale si wògblɔ to eƒe dɔla gbeƒãɖelawo katã dzi la ene. Ale woɖe aboyo Israel tso woawo ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi yi Asiria va se ɖe egbe.

english_verse: The king of Assyria took people who were living in the cities of Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and forced them to move to Israel. They took over the towns where the Israelites had lived, including the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Asiria-fia kplɔ amewo tso Babilon, Kuta, Ava, Xamat kple Sefarvayim, eye wòda wo ɖe Samaria-duwo me ɖe Israel-dukɔ teƒe. Woxɔ Samaria eye wonɔ eƒe duwo me.

english_verse: At first these people did not worship the Lord, so he sent lions to attack them, and the lions killed some of them.
translation_verse: Le woƒe afi ma nɔnɔ me le gɔmedzedzea la, womesubɔ Aƒetɔ o, eya ta Aƒetɔ ɖo dzatawo ɖe wo dome, eye wowu wo dometɔ aɖewo.

english_verse: A messenger told the king of Assyria, “The people you moved to Israel don't know how to worship the god of that country. So he sent lions that have attacked and killed some of them.”
translation_verse: Ale wogblɔ na Asiria-fia be: “Dukɔ siwo nèkplɔ yi ɖada ɖe Samaria-duwo me la menya anyigba la ƒe mawu ƒe se o, eya ta eɖo dzatawo ɖe wo dome, eye kpɔ ɖa, wole wo wum, elabe womenya anyigba la ƒe mawu ƒe se o.”

english_verse: The king replied, “Get one of the Israelite priests we brought here and send him back to Israel. He can live there and teach them about the god of that country.”
translation_verse: Tete Asiria-fia ɖe gbe be: “Miɖo nunɔla siwo mieɖakplɔ tso afi ma vɛ la dometɔ ɖeka ɖa. Mina wòaɖanɔ afi ma be wòafia anyigba la ƒe mawu ƒe se la wo.”

english_verse: One of the Israelite priests was chosen to go back to Israel. He lived in Bethel and taught the people how to worship the Lord.
translation_verse: Ale nunɔla siwo wokplɔ tso Samaria dzoe la dometɔ ɖeka va eye wònɔ Betel hefia ale si wòle be woavɔ̃ Aƒetɔ la woe.

english_verse: But in towns all over Israel, the different groups of people made statues of their own gods, then they placed these idols in local Israelite shrines.
translation_verse: Ke hã dukɔ sia dukɔ wɔ mawuwo na eɖokui, eye wotsɔ wo ɖo nuxeƒexɔ siwo Samariatɔwo wɔ la me. Dukɔ sia dukɔ wɔe ɖe du si me wòle la me.

english_verse: The people from Babylonia made the god Succoth-Benoth; those from Cuthah made the god Nergal; those from Hamath made Ashima;
translation_verse: Babilontɔwo wɔ Sukot-Benot; Kuttɔwo wɔ Nergal, eye Xamat tɔwo wɔ Asima;

english_verse: those from Avva made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the people from Sepharvaim sacrificed their children to their own gods Adrammelech and Anammelech.
translation_verse: Avitɔwo wɔ Nibxaz kple Tartak, eye Sefarvayimtɔwo me wo viwo le dzo me na Adramelex kple Anamelex siwo nye Sefarvayimtɔwo ƒe mawuwo.

english_verse: They worshiped their own gods, just as they had before they were taken away to Israel. They also worshiped the Lord, but they chose their own people to be priests at the shrines.
translation_verse: Ale wovɔ̃ Aƒetɔ, ke wogasubɔa woawo ŋutɔ ƒe mawuwo hã le dukɔ siwo dome wokplɔ wo tsoe la ƒe kɔnuwo nu.

english_verse: Everyone followed their old customs. None of them worshiped only the Lord, and they refused to obey the laws and commands that the Lord had given to the descendants of Jacob, the man he named Israel.
translation_verse: Egbegbe la, wogazɔna ɖe kɔnu xoxoawo nu ko. Womevɔ̃a Aƒetɔ o, eye womezɔna ɖe kɔnuawo alo ɖoɖoawo alo se la alo sedede si Aƒetɔ na Yakob viwo, ame si wòna ŋkɔ be Israel la nu o.

english_verse: At the time when the Lord had made his solemn agreement with the people of Israel, he told them: Do not worship any other gods! Do not bow down to them or offer them a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ bla nu kpli wo, eye wode se na wo be: “Migavɔ̃ mawu bubuwo loo, alo ade ta agu na wo loo, alo asubɔ wo loo, alo asa vɔ na wo o;

english_verse: Worship only me! I am the one who rescued you from Egypt with my mighty power. Bow down to me and offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: ke boŋ mivɔ̃ Aƒetɔ ame si kplɔ mi tso Egipte-nyigba dzi kple ŋusẽ triakɔ kple abɔ si wòdo ɖe dzi; mide ta agu na eya, eye eyae miasa vɔ na.

english_verse: and remember the solemn agreement between us. I will say it again: Do not worship any god
translation_verse: Migaŋlɔ nu si mebla kpli mi la be o. Migavɔ̃ mawu bubuwo o,

english_verse: except me. I am the Lord your God, and I will rescue you from all your enemies.
translation_verse: ke boŋ mivɔ̃ Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la, eye wòaɖe mi tso miaƒe futɔwo katã si me.”

english_verse: But the people living in Israel ignored that command and kept on following their old customs.
translation_verse: Ke hã la, womeɖo to o, ke boŋ wozɔ ɖe kɔnu xoxoa nu.

english_verse: They did worship the Lord, but they also worshiped their own idols. Their descendants did the same thing.
translation_verse: Ale dukɔ siawo vɔ̃ Aƒetɔ, eye wosubɔ woƒe legbawo hã; wo viwo wɔ nenema eye wo viwo ƒe viwo hã wɔ nenema ke; ale si wo tɔ́wo wɔ la, nenema woawo hã wɔ va ɖo egbe.

english_verse: Don't be fooled by Hezekiah. He can't save you.
translation_verse: Fia la be: ‘Migana Xizkiya nable mi o, elabe mate ŋu aɖe mi tso nye asi me o.

english_verse: Stop listening to Hezekiah! Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns
translation_verse: Migaɖo to Xizkiya o, elabe Asiria-fia be: “Miwɔ ŋutifafa kplim, mido va gbɔnye; ekema mia dome ame sia ame aɖu eƒe waintsetse, ame sia ame aɖu eƒe gbotitsetse, eye ame sia ame ano eya ŋutɔ ƒe vudo me tsi;

english_verse: Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
translation_verse: Gawu la, Aƒetɔ manɔme ye metso ɖe teƒe sia ŋu be matsrɔ̃ea? Aƒetɔ ye gblɔ nam be: “Ho ɖe anyigba sia ŋu eye nàtsrɔ̃e.’ ”

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nu si dze la le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, abe ale si tɔgbuia David wɔ pɛpɛpɛ la ene.

english_verse: He destroyed the local shrines, then tore down the images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. He also smashed the bronze snake Moses had made. The people had named it Nehushtan and had been offering sacrifices to it.
translation_verse: Eɖe nuxeƒewo ɖa, gbã aƒeliwo eye wolã nyɔnumawu Asera la ɖa. Egbã akɔblida si Mose wɔ la gudugudu, elabe va se ɖe ŋkeke mawo me la, Israelviwo nɔa dzo tɔm lifi nɛ; wona ŋkɔe be Nexustan.

english_verse: Hezekiah trusted the Lord God of Israel. No other king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before or after him.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋu ɖe Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋu ale be etɔgbe aɖeke menɔ Yuda-fia siwo dze eyome alo do ŋgɔ nɛ la dome o.

english_verse: He was completely faithful to the Lord and obeyed the laws the Lord had given to Moses for the people.
translation_verse: Elabe eku ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu vevie; mete ɖa le eyome o, ke boŋ elé se siwo Aƒetɔ de na Mose la me ɖe asi.

english_verse: The Lord helped Hezekiah, so he was successful in everything he did. He even rebelled against the king of Assyria, refusing to be his servant.
translation_verse: Afi sia afi si wòyi la, Aƒetɔ nɔ kplii, eye nu dze edzi nɛ. Edze aglã ɖe Asiria - fia ŋuti, eye megasubɔe o.

english_verse: Hezekiah defeated the Philistine towns as far away as Gaza—from the smallest towns to the large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Esi Filistitɔwo va se ɖe keke Gaza kple eƒe nutowo me ke, tso gbetakpɔxɔ gbɔ va se ɖe du sesẽ la gbɔ.

english_verse: During the fourth year of Hezekiah's rule, which was the seventh year of Hoshea's rule in Israel, King Shalmaneser of Assyria led his troops to Samaria, the capital city of Israel. They attacked
translation_verse: Le fia Xizkiya ƒe ƒè enelia, si nye Israel-fia Hosea, Ela vi ƒe ƒè adrẽlia me la, Asiria-fia Salmanaser ho ɖe Samaria ŋu heɖe to ɖee.

english_verse: and captured it three years later, in the sixth year of Hezekiah's rule and the ninth year of Hoshea's rule.
translation_verse: Woxɔ Samaria le Xizkiya ƒe ƒè adelia, si nye Hosea, Israel-fia ƒe ƒè asiekelia me.

english_verse: All of that happened because the people of Israel had not obeyed the Lord their God. They rejected the solemn agreement he had made with them, and they ignored everything that the Lord's servant Moses had told them. King Sennacherib of Assyria Invades Judah (
translation_verse: Elabe womeɖo to Aƒetɔ woƒe Mawu la ƒe gbe o, ke boŋ woda eƒe nubabla dzi. Se siwo katã Mose, Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla de na wo gɔ̃ hã la, womeɖo to wo loo, alo wɔ wo dzi o. Asiria do vɔvɔ̃ na Yerusalem

english_verse: for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards, raise your own grain, and have plenty of olive oil and honey. Believe me, you won't starve there. Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him.
translation_verse: va se ɖe esime mava, akplɔ mi adzoe ayi anyigba, si le abe mia tɔ ene la dzi. Anyigba si dzi bli kple wain, abolo kple waingblewo, amitiwo kple anyitsi le, ne mianɔ agbe, eye miaku o.

english_verse: One of the Assyrian commanders told them: I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself.
translation_verse: Rabsake gblɔ na wo be, “Gblɔ na Xizkiya be: ‘Asiria-fia, fia gã la be, nu ka ŋu koŋ nèle dzi ɖom ɖo?

english_verse: Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
translation_verse: Ke ne ègblɔ nam be: “Mieɖo ŋu ɖe Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la ŋu” la, ɖe menye eya ƒe nuxeƒewo kple vɔsamlekpuiwoe Xizkiya ɖe ɖa, hegblɔ na Yuda kple Yerusalem be, “Ele be miasubɔ le vɔsamlekpui sia ŋgɔ le Yerusalem” oa?

english_verse: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's rule in Judah, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city, except Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Le fia Xizkiya ƒe ƒè wui enelia me la, Asiria-fia Sanxerib ho ɖe Yuda-du sesẽwo katã ŋu hexɔ wo.

english_verse: Hezekiah sent this message to Sennacherib, who was in the town of Lachish: “I know I am guilty of rebellion. But I will pay you whatever you want, if you stop your attack.” Sennacherib told Hezekiah to pay ten tons of silver and one ton of gold.
translation_verse: Yuda-fia Xizkiya dɔ ame ɖe Asiria-fia le Laxis ne woagblɔ nɛ be: “Mewɔ nuvɔ̃; gbugbɔ ɖe megbe tso gbɔnye, nu sia nu si nàɖo dzinye la matsɔe.” Asiria-fia bia tso Yuda-fia Xizkiya si be wòaɖo klosalo kilo akpe ewo kple sika kilo akpe ɖeka ɖa.

english_verse: So Hezekiah collected all the silver from the Lord's temple and the royal treasury.
translation_verse: Xizkiya tsɔ klosalo siwo katã wòkpɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒeme kple fia ƒe nudzraɖoƒe nɛ.

english_verse: He even stripped the gold that he had used to cover the doors and doorposts in the temple. He gave it all to Sennacherib.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, Xizkiya fo sika si Yuda-fia Xizkiya fa ɖe gbedoxɔa ƒe ʋɔtruwo ŋu hetsɔ na Asiria-fia.

english_verse: The king of Assyria ordered his three highest military officers to leave Lachish and take a large army to Jerusalem. When they arrived, the officers stood on the road near the cloth makers' shops along the canal from the upper pool.
translation_verse: Asiria-fia dɔ Tartan, Rabsaris kple Rabsake kpakple aʋakɔ gã aɖe tso Laxis ɖo ɖe fia Xizkiya ŋu le Yerusalem. Woho va Yerusalem. Esime woɖo la, wotɔ ɖe dzigbetá, si le avɔnyala ƒe agblemɔ dzi la ƒe tɔʋu nu.

english_verse: They called out to Hezekiah, and three of his highest officials came out to meet them. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
translation_verse: Esime woyɔ fia la la, Eliyakim, Xilkiya vi, ame si le aƒekɔ la nu, agbalẽŋlɔla Sebna, kple Yoax, Asaf vi, si nye fia ƒe tsiami la do va wo gbɔ.

english_verse: Does he think he can plan and win a war with nothing but words? Who is going to help him, now that he has turned against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Ɖe nèbu be numenya ƒuƒlu ye nye aɖaŋu kple ŋusẽ si wɔa aʋaa? Ame ka ŋue nèle gogom ɖo fifia hafi dze aglã ɖe ŋunye?

english_verse: Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, nèle gogom ɖe Egipte, aƒla ŋeŋe ma, si ne ame aɖe ziɔ ɖe eŋu la wòaŋɔ asi nɛ la ŋu. Nenemae Egipte Fiagã le, na ame siwo katã aziɔ ɖe eŋu la.

english_verse: The king of Assyria wants to make a bet with you people. He will give you
translation_verse: Azɔ, va ne mia kple nye aƒetɔ Asiria-fia miatso gbe ɖe edzi: Mana sɔ akpe eve wò, ne àte ŋu akpɔ sɔdolawo aɖo wo dzi.

english_verse: How could you even defeat our lowest ranking officer, when you have to depend on Egypt for chariots and cavalry?
translation_verse: Ale ke nàte ŋu atutu aʋakplɔla ɖeka pɛ si nye nye aƒetɔ ƒe dɔlawo dome suetɔ hã ado ɖe megbe le esime wònye Egipte ŋue nèle dzi ɖom ɖo hena tasiaɖamwo kple sɔwo?

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Sir, we don't want the people listening from the city wall to understand what you are saying. So please speak to us in Aramaic instead of Hebrew.”
translation_verse: Tete Elyakim, Xilkiya vi, kple Sebna kpakple Yoax gblɔ na Rabsake be, “Míeɖe kuku, ƒo nu na wò dɔlawo le Aram-gbe me, elabe miesenɛ, mègado Yuda-gbe na mí ne dukɔ si le glia dzi la nasee o.”

english_verse: The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you.”
translation_verse: Ke Rabsake ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Ɖe nye aƒetɔ dɔm ɖa be magblɔ nya siawo na mia kple wò aƒetɔ, eye medɔm ɖo ɖe ŋutsu siwo bɔbɔ nɔ glia dzi siwo tɔ koe nye be woava ɖu woawo ŋutɔ ƒe mí, eye woano woawo ŋutɔ ƒe aɖuɖɔ gbɔ oa?”

english_verse: Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted in Hebrew: Listen to what the great king of Assyria says!
translation_verse: Tete Rabsake tsi tsitre hedo ɣli sesĩe ɖo ɖa le Yuda-gbe me be: “Mise fia gã, Asiria-fia ƒe gbe!

english_verse: Don't trust him when he tells you that the Lord will protect you from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Migana Xizkiya nawɔe be mianɔ gogom ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu anɔ gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Aƒetɔ aɖe mí godoo, eye womatsɔ du sia ade asi na Asiria-fia o.

english_verse: Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Ɖe dukɔ aɖewo ƒe mawuwo te ŋu ɖe woƒe anyigba kpɔ tso Asiria-fia si mea?

english_verse: What happened to the gods of Hamath and Arpad? What about the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces?
translation_verse: Afi ka Xamat kple Arpad ƒe mawuwo le? Sefarvayim, Hena kple Iva ƒe mawuwo ɖe? Ɖe wote ŋu ɖe Samaria tso asinye mea?

english_verse: None of these gods kept their people safe from the king of Assyria. Do you think the Lord your God can do any better?
translation_verse: Mawu kae le mawuwo katã dome, le anyigbawo dzi, te ŋu ɖe eƒe anyigba tso asinye me kpɔ, hafi Aƒetɔ ya nava ɖe Yerusalem tso asinye me?’ ”

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.
translation_verse: Tete Elyakim, Xilkiya vi, aƒea dzikpɔla, kple agbalẽŋlɔla Sebna kpakple Yoax, Asaf vi, si nye fia ƒe tsiami dze woƒe awuwo va Xizkiya gbɔ, eye wogblɔ Rabsake ƒe nyawo nɛ.

english_verse: One day he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, when his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with their swords. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king.
translation_verse: Esi wònɔ gbe dom ɖa le Nisrox, eƒe mawu ƒeme la, via ŋutsuwo, Adramelex kple Sarezer, wova wui kple yi, eye wosí yi Ararat-nyigba dzi. Via ŋutsu, Esar-Xadon zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah heard the news, he tore off his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he went into the temple of the Lord.
translation_verse: Esi fia Xizkiya see la, edze eƒe awuwo; eta akpanya heyi Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me.

english_verse: The kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah have all disappeared. Hezekiah Prays (Isaiah
translation_verse: Afi ka Xamat-fia, Arpad-fia, Sefarvayim du, Hena-fia kple Iva-fia wole?

english_verse: He told Prime Minister Eliakim, Assistant Prime Minister Shebna, and the senior priests to dress in sackcloth and tell the prophet Isaiah:
translation_verse: Edɔ aƒedzikpɔla Elyakim, agbalẽŋlɔla Sebna kple nunɔlawo ƒe ame tsitsi siwo ta akpanya la ɖo ɖe gbeƒãɖela Yesaya Amoz vi la gbɔ.

english_verse: These are difficult and disgraceful times. Our nation is like a woman too weak to give birth, when it's time for her baby to be born.
translation_verse: Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Xizkiya be: ‘Egbe nye xaxa, mokaname kple vlodoamegbe, elabe vi ɖo ata me gake ŋusẽ meli woasii adzi o.

english_verse: Please pray for those of us who are left alive. The king of Assyria sent his army commander to insult the living God. Perhaps the Lord heard what he said and will do something, if you will pray.
translation_verse: Ɖewohĩ Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la se Rabsake, ame si eƒe aƒetɔ Asiria-fia dɔ, be wòava ɖe alɔ me le Mawu gbagbe la ŋu la ƒe nyawo katã, eye wò Mawu la see. Eya ta, do gbe ɖa ɖe ame mamlɛa siwo li la ta.”

english_verse: When these leaders went to Isaiah,
translation_verse: Esime fia Xizkiya ƒe dɔlawo va Yesaya gbɔ la,

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had this message for Hezekiah: I am the Lord. Don't worry about the insulting things that have been said about me by these messengers from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Yesaya gblɔ na wo be: “Migblɔ na miaƒe aƒetɔ be, ‘Aƒetɔ be: Mègavɔ̃ le nya siwo Asiria-fia ƒe dɔlawo tsɔ ɖe alɔ me le ŋunye nèse la ta o.

english_verse: I will upset him with rumors about what's happening in his own country. He will go back, and there I will make him die a violent death.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, matsɔ gbɔgbɔ aɖe ade eme, ase segblɔ aɖe, eye wòagbugbɔ ayi eya ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi; mana wòatsi yi nu le eya ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi. Asiriatɔwo gado vɔvɔ̃ na wo

english_verse: Meanwhile, the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.
translation_verse: Rabsake gbugbɔ dzo, eye wòkpɔ be Asiria-fia la nɔ aʋa wɔm kple Libna, elabe ese be fia la dzo le Laxis.

english_verse: About this same time the king of Assyria learned that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia was on his way to attack him. Then the king of Assyria sent some messengers with this note for Hezekiah:
translation_verse: Esi fia la se nu tso Tirhaka, Etiopia-fia ŋu be: “Kpɔ ɖa, eho be yeaɖawɔ aʋa kpli wò la,” egaɖo dɔlawo ɖe Xizkiya be,

english_verse: Don't trust your God or be fooled by his promise to defend Jerusalem against me.
translation_verse: Migblɔ na Yuda-fia, Xizkiya be: “Mègana wò Mawu si ŋu nèle dzi ɖom ɖo la nable wò be womatsɔ Yerusalem ade asi na Asiria-fia o.

english_verse: You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe?
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ese nu siwo Asiria-fia wɔ wò anyigbawo katã, hetsrɔ̃ wo keŋkeŋ. Ɖe woaɖe wò ya?

english_verse: The Assyrian kings before me destroyed the towns of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and everyone from Eden who lived in Telassar. What good did their gods do them?
translation_verse: Ɖe dukɔ siwo tɔgbuinyewo tsrɔ̃: Gozan, Xaran, Rezek kple Eden vi siwo nɔ Telasar la ƒe mawuwo ɖe woa?

english_verse: After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see.
translation_verse: Xizkiya xɔ agbalẽ la le amedɔdɔawo si, eye wòxlẽe. Xizkiya yi Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me, eye wòkee ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋkume.

english_verse: Isaiah went to Hezekiah and told him that the Lord God of Israel had said: Hezekiah, I heard your prayer about King Sennacherib of Assyria.
translation_verse: Tete Yesaya, Amoz vi, dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Xizkiya be: “Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: ‘Mese gbe si nèdo ɖa nam le Asiria-fia Sanxerib ŋuti.

english_verse: He prayed: Lord God of Israel, your throne is above the winged creatures. You created the heavens and the earth, and you alone rule the kingdoms of this world.
translation_verse: Xizkiya do gbe ɖa le Aƒetɔ ŋkume gblɔ be: “O Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu, wò si nye fia le kerubiwo dzi, wò ɖeka koe nye Mawu na fiaɖuƒewo katã le anyigba dzi; wòe wɔ dziƒo kple anyigba.

english_verse: It is true, our Lord, that Assyrian kings have turned nations into deserts.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, le nyateƒe me la, Asiria-fiawo nyatsrɔ̃ dukɔwo kple woƒe anyigbawo.

english_verse: They destroyed the idols of wood and stone that the people of those nations had made and worshiped.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ woƒe mawuwo de dzo me, elabe menye mawuwo wonye o, ke boŋ amegbetɔwo ƒe asinudɔwɔwɔwoe, ati kple kpe wonye; eya ta wotsrɔ̃ wo.

english_verse: But you are our Lord and our God! We ask you to keep us safe from the Assyrian king. Then everyone in every kingdom on earth will know that you are the only God. The Lord's Answer to Hezekiah (Isaiah
translation_verse: Eya ta, azɔ, Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu, meɖe kuku na wò, ɖe mí tso eƒe asi me, ne anyigba dzi fiaɖuƒewo katã nadze sii, be wò Aƒetɔ ɖeka koe nye Mawu!” Yesaya ƒe gbedeasi na fia la

english_verse: Now this is what I say to that king: The people of Jerusalem hate and make fun of you; they laugh behind your back.
translation_verse: Nya si Aƒetɔ gblɔ tso eŋuti lae nye esi: Ɖetugbi, Zion vinyɔnu, ɖe alɔ me le ŋuwò, heko wò; Yerusalem vinyɔnu, ʋuʋu ta ɖe yowòme.

english_verse: Sennacherib, you cursed, shouted, and sneered at me, the holy God of Israel.
translation_verse: “Ame ka ŋu nèɖu fewu le hedo vloe? Ame ka tae nèdo ɣli ɖo eye ame kae nèkpɔ ŋkume na dàdatɔe? Israel ƒe Kɔkɔetɔ la ŋue!

english_verse: You let your officials insult me, the Lord. And this is how you bragged about yourself: “I led my chariots to the highest heights of Lebanon's mountains. I went deep into its forest, cutting down the best cedar and cypress trees.
translation_verse: Eɖo hehe ɖe Aƒetɔ ta to wò dɔlawo dzi, eye nègblɔ be, ‘Metsɔ nye tasiaɖam gbogboawo lia to kɔkɔwo tame, de keke Lebanon ƒe tsutsɔẽƒewo ke. Memu eƒe sederti kɔkɔwo kple eƒe sesewu nyuiwo. Mege ɖe eƒe nɔƒe kɔkɔwo kple aƒe ave dodowo me.

english_verse: I dried up every stream in the land of Egypt, and I drank water from wells I had dug.”
translation_verse: Meɖe vudowo eye meno dzronyigba dzi tsiwo nye afɔƒome ka Egipte tɔʋuwo katã me womie.’

english_verse: Sennacherib, now listen to me, the Lord. I planned all this long ago. And you don't even realize that I alone am the one who decided that you would do these things. I let you make ruins of fortified cities.
translation_verse: “Mèsee kpɔ be meɖo kpe edzi tso blema ke oa? Nu si mena wòdzɔ fifia la, mewɔ ɖoɖo ɖe eŋu xoxoxo be nàtrɔ du sesẽwo woazu glikpo,

english_verse: Their people became weak, terribly confused. They were like wild flowers or tender young grass growing on a flat roof, scorched before it matures.
translation_verse: esime wo me nɔlawo ƒe lã me tu, dzi ɖe le wo ƒo eye gbɔgblɔ bu ɖe wo. Wozu abe amagbe le agble me kple gbe fɛ̃ ene; wole abe xɔtagbe si tsi to nu gbe tsitsi ene.

english_verse: I know all about you, even how fiercely angry you are with me.
translation_verse: Menya wò anyinɔnɔ, wò gododo, wò gbɔgbɔ kple wò nyanyra ɖe ŋunye.

translation_verse: Ke nunɔla siwo le nuxeƒewo la mevaa Aƒetɔ ƒe vɔsamlekpui si le Yerusalem la gbɔ o, ke boŋ woɖua abolo maʋamaʋã kple wo nɔviwo ya.

english_verse: Josiah sent some men to Hinnom Valley just outside Jerusalem with orders to make the altar there unfit for worship. That way, people could no longer use it for sacrificing their children to the god Molech.
translation_verse: Fia la do gu Tofet-nuxeƒe si le Ben-Him-balia me ale be ame aɖeke magatsɔ via ŋutsu alo via nyɔnu asa vɔ le dzo me na Molex azɔ o.

english_verse: Some of the kings of Judah, especially Manasseh, had built altars in the two courts of the temple and in the room that Ahaz had built on the palace roof. Josiah had these altars torn down and smashed to pieces, and he had the pieces thrown into Kidron Valley, just outside Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Fia la ɖe vɔsamlekpui siwo le Axaz ƒe xɔta siwo Yuda-fiawo ɖi la kple esiwo Manase hã ɖi ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ƒe xɔxɔnu eveawo la hã ɖa. Egbã wo gudugudu lɔ ɖaƒu gbe ɖe Kidron-tɔʋu me.

english_verse: After that, he closed down the shrines that Solomon had built east of Jerusalem and south of Spoil Hill to honor Astarte the disgusting goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Fia Yosiya do gu nuxeƒe siwo le Yerusalem ƒe ɣedzeƒe le Amito la ƒe anyigbeme. Vɔsamlekpui siawo nye ŋunyɔnu siwo Israel-fia Salomo ɖi na Astarte, Kemos Sidontɔwo ƒe ŋunyɔnu, Moabitɔwo ƒe ŋunyɔnu kple Milkom, Amontɔwo ƒe ŋunyɔnu.

english_verse: He tore down the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole used in the worship of Asherah. Then he had the whole area covered with human bones.
translation_verse: Yosiya gbã aƒeliwo, mu nyɔnumawu Asera ŋu nuwo ƒu anyi, eye wòlɔ ameƒuwo kɔ ɖe wo teƒewo.

english_verse: But Josiah was not finished yet. At Bethel he destroyed the shrine and the altar that Jeroboam son of Nebat had built and that had caused the Israelites to sin. Josiah had the shrine and the Asherah pole burned and ground into dust.
translation_verse: Nenema ke wòɖe vɔsamlekpui si le Betel kple nuxeƒe si Yerobeam, Nebat vi ɖi tsɔ na Israel wɔ nuvɔ̃ la ɖa. Egbã vɔsamlekpui la kple nuxeƒe la, tɔ dzo nuxeƒea, eye wòtui memie. Etɔ dzo Asera la hã.

english_verse: As he looked around, he saw graves on the hillside. He had the bones in them dug up and burned on the altar, so that it could no longer be used. This happened just as God's prophet had said when Jeroboam was standing at the altar, celebrating a festival. Then Josiah saw the grave of the prophet who had said this would happen
translation_verse: Yosiya tsa ŋku, eye wòkpɔ yɔdo aɖewo le to dzi ɖa. Ena woyi ɖalɔ ƒuwo le wo me vɛ nɛ, eye wòtɔ dzo wo le vɔsamlekpui la dzi. Ale wòdo gu vɔsamlekpui la le Aƒetɔ ƒe nya si gbeƒãɖela gblɔ ɖi la nu gbe aɖe gbe le ŋkekenyui ɖuƒe, esime fia Yerobeam le tsitre ɖe vɔsamlekpui gbɔ. Yosiya nye kɔ kpɔ Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela si gblɔ nya siawo ɖi la ƒe yɔdo.

english_verse: and he asked, “Whose grave is that?” Some people who lived nearby answered, “It belongs to the prophet from Judah who told what would happen to this altar.”
translation_verse: Tete wò bia be: “Ŋkuɖodzikpe kae nye ekema kpɔm mele?” Dua me tɔwo ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela si tso Yuda va ɖe gbeƒã nu si nèwɔ ɖe vɔsamlekpuia ŋu le Betel la ƒe yɔdoe.”

english_verse: Josiah replied, “Then leave it alone. Don't dig up his bones.” So they did not disturb his bones or the bones of the old prophet from Israel who had also been buried there.
translation_verse: Azɔ egblɔ be: “Miɖe asi le eŋu; ame aɖeke megaka asi eƒe ƒuwo ŋu o.” Ale womeka asi eya kple Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela si tso Samaria la ƒe ƒuwo ŋu o.

english_verse: Josiah told the people of Judah, “Celebrate Passover in honor of the Lord your God, just as it says in The Book of God's Law.”
translation_verse: Fia la bia tso dukɔ blibo la si be: “Miɖu Paska la na Aƒetɔ, miaƒe Mawu la abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖe nubabla ƒe agbalẽ sia me la ene.”

english_verse: This festival had not been celebrated in this way since the time that tribal leaders ruled Israel or the kings ruled Israel and Judah.

english_verse: Josiah got rid of every disgusting person and thing in Judah and Jerusalem—including magicians, fortunetellers, and idols. He did his best to obey every law written in the book that the priest Hilkiah found in the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Gawu la, Yosiya di be dukɔa nawɔ nya siwo woŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽ si nunɔla Xilkiya fɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me la dzi, eya ta eɖe ŋɔliyɔlawo, adzetɔwo aklama kpakpɛwo, legbawo kple ŋunyɔnu siwo katã wòkpɔ le Yuda-nyigba dzi kple Yerusalem la ɖa.

english_verse: But the Lord was still furious with the people of Judah because Manasseh had done so many things to make him angry.
translation_verse: Gake dɔmedzoe gã si fia Manase do na Aƒetɔ la gale dɔ me nɛ kokoko ɖe Yuda ŋuti.

english_verse: A few of Josiah's servants put his body in a chariot and took it back to Jerusalem, where they buried it in his own tomb. Then the people of Judah found his son Jehoahaz and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. King Jehoahaz of Judah (

translation_verse: Ewɔ nuvɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume abe ale si tɔgbuiawo wɔ ene.

translation_verse: Ewɔ nuvɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume abe ale si tɔgbuiawo katã wɔ ene.

translation_verse: Yehoyakim ku, eye via Yehoyakin zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

translation_verse: Ewɔ nuvɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume abe ale si tɔ́a wɔ ene.

english_verse: The Lord had warned that someday the treasures would be taken from the royal palace and from the temple, including the gold objects that Solomon had made for the temple. And that's exactly what Nebuchadnezzar ordered his soldiers to do.
translation_verse: Elɔ kesinɔnu siwo katã le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me kple fiasã la me la dzoe, eye wògbã sikanu siwo katã Israel-fia Salomo wɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me la. Nebukadnezar wɔ esiawo katã le Aƒetɔ ƒe nya si wògblɔ ɖi la nu.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar took Jehoiachin to Babylon, along with his mother, his wives, his officials, and the most important leaders of Judah.
translation_verse: Yehoyakin yi Babilonia. Fia nɔ, fia srɔ̃wo, fiasãmenuwo dzikpɔlawo kple bubumewo katã tso Yerusalem kpe ɖe eŋu yi.

english_verse: the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the desert,
translation_verse: Togbɔ be Babiloniatɔwo ƒo xlã dua hã la, woŋɔ dugli la, eye fia la kple eƒe aʋawɔlawo katã sí le zã me to agbo si le gli eveawo dome le fia ƒe abɔ gbɔ lɔƒo la heɖo ta Yordan-gbegbe la.

english_verse: Zedekiah was taken to Riblah, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty.
translation_verse: Ale wolé fia la, kplɔe va Babilonia-fia gbɔ le Ribla, eye wòdrɔ̃ ʋɔnui.

english_verse: About a month later, in Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king, Nebuzaradan, who was his official in charge of the guards, arrived in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti etɔ̃lia ƒe ŋkeke adrẽlia gbe, si nye Babilonia-fia Nebukadnezar ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè wui asiekelia me la, Nebuzaradan, fia ŋu srafowo ƒe tatɔ si nye Babilonia-fia ƒe dɔla la va Yerusalem.

english_verse: Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Babilonia-srafo siwo katã le woƒe tatɔa ŋu la gbã dugli siwo katã ƒo xlã Yerusalem va kpe ɖo la.

english_verse: He led away as prisoners the people left in the city, including those who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradan, fia ŋu srafowo ƒe tatɔ kplɔ ame mamlɛ siawo yi aboyo mee: ame siwo tsi dua me, ame siwo na ta Babilonia-fia kple ame haho la.

english_verse: Only some of the poorest people were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
translation_verse: Gake egblẽ ame siwo da ahe ŋutɔŋutɔ la ya ɖi be woade waingble kple agble bubuwo.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers took the two bronze columns that stood in front of the temple, the ten movable bronze stands, and the large bronze bowl called the Sea. They broke them into pieces so they could take the bronze to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Babiloniatɔwo mu akɔblisɔti siwo le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me, eye wògbã anyinɔawo kple akɔbligazɔ si le afi ma la hã, eye wolɔ akɔblia yi Babilonia.

english_verse: They carried off the bronze things used for worship at the temple, including the pans for hot ashes, and the shovels, snuffers, and also the dishes for incense,
translation_verse: Wotsɔ zeawo, sofiawo, akaɖitsinuawo kple agba siwo me wotɔa dzo lifi le la kpakple akɔblinuawo, siwo katã ŋudɔ wowɔna le subɔsubɔ me la hã dzoe.

english_verse: as well as the fire pans and the sprinkling bowls. Nebuzaradan ordered his soldiers to take everything made of gold or silver.
translation_verse: Fia ŋu srafowo ƒe tatɔ la tsɔ dzoɖenuawo kple agba bubuawo kpakple nu sia nu si wotsɔ sika alo klosalo wɔ la siaa dzoe.

english_verse: Before kings ruled in Israel, Bela son of Beor ruled the country of Edom from its capital of Dinhabah.
translation_verse: Fia siwo ɖu Edom-nyigba dzi hafi fia aɖe naɖu fia le Israel la woe nye: Bela, Beor vi, ame si ƒe fiadue nye Dinhaba.

english_verse: Seir was the father of Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
translation_verse: Seir viŋutsuwoe nye: Lotan, Sobal, Zibeon, Ana, Dison, Ezer kple Disan.

english_verse: Lotan was the father of Hori and Homam; Lotan's sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Lotan viŋutsuwoe nye Xori kple Homan ƒe towo. Lotan nɔvinyɔnu nye Timna.

english_verse: Shobal was the father of Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. Zibeon was the father of Aiah and Anah.
translation_verse: Sobal viŋutsuwoe nye: Alyan, Manaxat, Ebal, Sefi kple Onam. Zibeon viŋutsuwoe nye Aya kple Ana ƒe towo.

english_verse: Anah was the father of Dishon and the grandfather of Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
translation_verse: Ana vie nye Dison, eye Dison viŋutsuwoe nye: Xamran, Esban, Yitran kple Xeran ƒe towo.

english_verse: Ezer was the father of Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. Dishan was the father of Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Ezer viŋutsuwoe nye: Bilhan, Zaavan kple Yaakan. Disan viŋutsuwoe nye Uz kple Aran. Edom-fiawo (Mos I,

english_verse: After Bela's death, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah became king.
translation_verse: Esi Bela ku la, Yobab, Zerax vi, tso Bozra ɖu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: After Jobab's death, Husham from the land of Teman became king.
translation_verse: Esi Yobab ku la, Xusam si tso Temantɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi la zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: After Husham's death, Hadad son of Bedad became king and ruled from Avith. Earlier, Bedad had defeated the Midianites in the territory of Moab.
translation_verse: Esi Xusam ku la, Hadad, Bedad vi, zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Eyae ɖu Midiantɔwo dzi le Moab-tagba. Eƒe fiadue nye Avit.

english_verse: After Hadad's death, Samlah from Masrekah became king;
translation_verse: Esi Hadad ku la, Samla tso Masreka ɖu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: after Samlah's death, Shaul from the town of Rehoboth on the Euphrates River became king;
translation_verse: Esi Samla ku la, Saul tso Rexobot le tɔsisi la nu zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: and after Shaul's death, Baal Hanan son of Achbor became king.
translation_verse: Esi Saul ku la, Baal-Xanan, si nye Axbor vi, zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: After Baal Hanan's death, Hadad ruled from Pai. His wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Mezahab.
translation_verse: Esi Baal-Xanan ku la, Hadad zu fia ɖe eteƒe. Eƒe fiadue nye Pagi. Srɔ̃a Mahatabeel nye Matred vinyɔnu kple Masaxab ƒe mamayɔvi.

english_verse: The Edomite clans were Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
translation_verse: Le Hadad ƒe ku megbe la, Edom-fiawoe nye: Timna, Alva, Yetet,

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: Oholibama, Ela, Pinon,

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,

english_verse: Judah and his Canaanite wife Bathshua had three sons: Er, Onan, and Shelah. But the Lord had Er put to death, because he disobeyed and did what the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Yuda viŋutsuwoe nye: Ger, Onan kple Sela; Sua vinyɔnu si tso Kanaan lae dzi wo nɛ. Ger, Yuda ƒe ŋgɔgbevi wɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, ale wòwui.

english_verse: Judah and his daughter-in-law Tamar also had two sons: Perez and Zerah.
translation_verse: Tamar, ame si nye Yuda toyɔvi la hã dzi Perez kple Zerax nɛ. Ale Yuda viŋutsuwoe katã le atɔ̃.

english_verse: Perez was the father of Hezron and Hamul.
translation_verse: Perez viŋutsuwoe nye: Xezron kple Xamul.

english_verse: Zerah was the father of Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Darda.
translation_verse: Zerax viŋutsuwoe nye: Zimri, Etan, Heman, Xalkol kple Dara; wo katã le atɔ̃.

english_verse: Achan, who was a descendant of Zerah and the son of Carmi, caused trouble for Israel, because he kept for himself things that belonged only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Karmi viŋutsuwoe nye Axan, ame si he dzɔgbevɔ̃e va Israel-dukɔ la dzi, le esi wòtsɔ busunuawo ƒe ɖe ta.

english_verse: Ethan's son was Azariah. The Ancestors of King David
translation_verse: Etan viŋutsue nye Azarya. David ƒe ƒome

english_verse: Hezron was the father of Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb.
translation_verse: Xezron viŋutsu siwo wodzi nɛ la woe nye: Yeraxmeel, Ram kple Kalubai.

english_verse: Ram was the father of Amminadab and the grandfather of Nahshon, a tribal leader of Judah.
translation_verse: Ram nye Aminadab tɔ́a eye Aminadab nye Naxeson tɔ́a, ame si nye Yuda viwo ƒe ƒometatɔ.

english_verse: Nahshon's descendants included Salma, Boaz,
translation_verse: Naxeson nye Salma tɔ́a eye Salma nye Boaz tɔ́a.

english_verse: Jesse also had two daughters: Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah was the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.
translation_verse: Wo nɔvinyɔnuwoe nye Zeruya kple Abigail. Zeruya viŋutsuwoe nye: Abisai, Yoab kple Asahel, wole ame etɔ̃.

english_verse: Abigail's husband was Jether, who was a descendant of Ishmael, and their son was Amasa. The Descendants of Hezron
translation_verse: Abigail dzi Amasa, eye Amasa tɔ́a nye Yeter, Ismaeltɔ la. Xezron ƒe dzidzimeviwo

english_verse: Hezron's son Caleb married Azubah, and their daughter was Jerioth, the mother of Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
translation_verse: Kaleb, Xezron vi, dzi vi kple srɔ̃a Azuba kpakple Yeriot. Via ŋutsuwoe nye: Yeser, Sobab kple Ardon.

english_verse: After the death of Azubah, Caleb married Ephrath. Their son Hur
translation_verse: Esi Azuba ku la, Kaleb ɖe Efrat eye wòdzi Xur nɛ.

english_verse: was the father of Uri and the grandfather of Bezalel.
translation_verse: Xur nye Uri tɔ́a, eye Uri nye Bezaleel tɔ́a.

english_verse: After the death of Hezron, Caleb married Ephrath, his father's wife. Their son was Ashhur, who later settled the town of Tekoa. The Descendants of Jerahmeel
translation_verse: Le Xezron ƒe ku megbe la, Kaleb de Efrata, Xezron tɔ́ srɔ̃ gbɔ, eye wòdzi Asur si va nye Tekoa tɔ́ la nɛ. Yeraxmeel ƒe dzidzimeviwo

english_verse: Jerahmeel, Hezron's oldest son, was the father of Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
translation_verse: Yeraxmeel, ame si nye Xezron ƒe ŋgɔgbevi la viŋutsuwoe nye esiawo: Ram, ŋgɔgbevi la kple eyometɔwo Buna, Oren, Ozem kple Axiya,

english_verse: Jerahmeel had a second wife, Atarah, who gave birth to Onam.
translation_verse: Yerax srɔ̃ bubu nye Atara, eyae nye Onam nɔ.

english_verse: Ram was the father of Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
translation_verse: Ram, Yerameel ƒe ŋgɔgbevi viŋutsuwoe nye: Maaz, Yamin kple Eker.

english_verse: Onam was the father of Shammai and Jada. Shammai was the father of Nadab and Abishur.
translation_verse: Onam viŋutsuwoe nye Samai kple Yada. Samai viŋutsuwoe nye Nadab kple Abisur.

english_verse: Abishur married Abihail, and their two sons were Ahban and Molid.
translation_verse: Abisur srɔ̃ ŋkɔe nye Abixail, eye eyae dzi Axban kple Molid nɛ.

english_verse: Nadab was the father of Seled and Appaim. Seled had no children;
translation_verse: Nadab viŋutsuwoe nye Seled kple Apayim, ke Seled medzi vi hafi ku o.

english_verse: Appaim's son was Ishi, the father of Sheshan and the grandfather of Ahlai.
translation_verse: Apayim viŋutsue nye Yisi; Yisi viŋutsue nye Sesan, eye Sesan viŋutsue nye Axelai.

english_verse: Jada was the father of Jether and Jonathan. Jether had no children,
translation_verse: Yada Semai nɔvi viŋutsuwoe nye: Yeter kple Yonatan. Yeter medzi vi hafi ku o.

english_verse: but Jonathan had two sons: Peleth and Zaza.
translation_verse: Yonatan viŋutsuwoe nye Pelet kple Zaza. Ame siawoe nye Yeraxmeel ƒe dzidzimeviwo.

english_verse: Sheshan had no sons, and so he let one of his daughters marry Jarha, his Egyptian slave. Their son was Attai,
translation_verse: Ale Sesan tsɔ via nyɔnu na eƒe kluvi Yarxa wòɖe eye wòdzi Atai nɛ.

english_verse: the father of Nathan and the grandfather of Zabad.
translation_verse: Atai nye Natan tɔ́a, eye Natan nye Zabad tɔ́a.

english_verse: Zabad's descendants included Ephlal, Obed, Jehu, Azariah, Helez, Eleasah, Sismai, Shallum, Jekamiah, and Elishama. The Descendants of Caleb
translation_verse: Salum nye Yekamya tɔ́a, eye Yekamya nye Elisama tɔ́a. Kaleb ƒe dzidzimevi bubuwo

english_verse: Caleb, Jerahmeel's brother, had the following descendants: Mesha, Ziph, Mareshah, Hebron,
translation_verse: Kaleb nye Yeraxmeel nɔviŋutsu. Kaleb viŋutsuwoe nye: Mesa, eƒe ŋgɔgbevi, ame si nye Sif tɔ́a, eyometɔe nye Maresa, eyae nye Xebron tɔ́a.

english_verse: and Hebron's four sons, Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
translation_verse: Xebron viŋutsuwoe nye: Korax, Tapuax, Rekem kple Sema.

english_verse: Shema was the father of Raham and the grandfather of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai,
translation_verse: Sema nye Raxam tɔ́a, eye Raxam nye Yorkeam tɔ́a. Rekem nye Samai tɔ́a.

english_verse: the grandfather of Maon, and the great-grandfather of Bethzur.
translation_verse: Samai viŋutsue nye Maon, eye Maon nye Bet-Zur tɔ́a.

english_verse: Ephah was one of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran named his son after his brother Gazez.
translation_verse: Efa, Kaleb ƒe ahiãvi dzi Xaran, Moza kple Gazez; ke Xaran hã dzi vi hetsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Gazez.

english_verse: Ephah was the daughter of Jahdai, who was also the father of Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, and Shaaph.
translation_verse: Yadai viwoe nye: Regem, Yotam, Gesan, Pelet, Efa kple Saaf.

english_verse: Maacah was another of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Sheber and Tirhanah.
translation_verse: Maaxa, Kaleb ƒe ahiãvi bubu, dzi Seber kple Tirxana.

english_verse: Later, they had two more sons: Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.
translation_verse: Eya kee dzi Saaf, ame si nye Madmana kple Seva tɔ́a; Seva va nye Maxbena kple Gibea tɔ́a. Kaleb vinyɔnu ŋkɔe nye Axsa.

english_verse: Shobal, who settled the town of Kiriath-Jearim, was the ancestor of Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth clan,
translation_verse: Sobal, ame si tsò Kiryat-Yearim la ƒe dzidzimeviwoe nye Haroetɔwo kple Menuxotitɔwo ƒe afã.

english_verse: and the clans that lived near Kiriath-Jearim; they were the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. The Zorathites and the Eshtaolites were descendants of the Mishraites.
translation_verse: Kiryat-Yearim ƒomeawo nye Yitritɔwo, Putitɔwo. Sumatitɔwo kple Misraitɔwo. Ƒome siawo mee Zoreatitɔwo kple Estaolitɔwo dzɔ tso.

english_verse: Salma settled the town of Bethlehem and was the ancestor of the Netophathites, the people of Atroth-Bethjoab, half of the Manahathite clan, and the Zorites.
translation_verse: Salma ƒe dzidzimeviwoe nye Betlehemtɔwo, Netofatitɔwo, Atarot, Bet-Yoab kple Manafitɔwo ƒe afã siwo nye Zoreatitɔwo.

english_verse: more sons. His wife Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel gave birth to Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon.
