english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. He sat there and prayed: Lord God, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Tete David fia la, va bɔbɔ nɔ Aƒetɔ ŋkume, eye wògblɔ be: “O Aƒetɔ Mawu, ame kae menye eye nu kae nye nye ƒome la hafi nèkplɔm va ɖo teƒe sia gbegbe?

english_verse: It was your choice to do these wonderful things for me and to make these promises.
translation_verse: O Aƒetɔ, wò dzimedidi na nye, wò dɔla tae nèwɔ nu gã siawo ɖo, be nàtsɔ ɖe wò nu triakɔ wɔwɔwo katã afia.

english_verse: No other god is like you, Lord—you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, le nu siwo katã míese kple míaƒe towo nu la, ame aɖeke mele abe wò ene o; wò ɖeka koe nye Mawu.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so that your people could live here.
translation_verse: Dukɔ bubu kae gale anyigba dzi abe wò dukɔ Israel, si wò Mawu nèɖaɖe tso Egipte be wòanye ye ŋutɔ ye tɔ la ene? To nu dziŋɔwo wɔwɔ me, èxɔ ŋkɔ le esime nènyà dukɔwo ɖa le wò dukɔ Israel ŋgɔ.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Èwɔ Israel wòzu wò dukɔ tegbee, eye wò, o Aƒetɔ, nèzu eƒe Mawu.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord All-Powerful rules Israel and is their God.” My kingdom will be strong,
translation_verse: Ekema wò ŋkɔ ade du tegbee eye dukɔwo agblɔ be: ‘Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae nye Israel-dukɔ ƒe Mawu,’ eye wò dɔla David ƒe aƒe ali ke le ŋkuwò me.

english_verse: because you are my God, and you have promised that my descendants will be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Elabe wò, nye Mawu, eɖee fia wò dɔla be yeatu xɔ nɛ; esia tae dzi ɖo ƒonye mele gbe sia dom ɖa le ŋkuwò me.

english_verse: You are the Lord God, and you have made this good promise to me.
translation_verse: Azɔ wò Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu ŋutɔe gblɔ nya nyui sia le wò dɔla ŋu.

english_verse: Now please bless my descendants forever, and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already blessed my family, and I know you will bless us forever.
translation_verse: Eya ta azɔ la, edze ŋuwò be nèyra wò dɔla ƒe aƒe be wòanɔ ŋkuwò me tegbee elabe nu si wò Aƒetɔ nèyra la, woyrae tegbee.”

english_verse: While King Hadadezer of Zobah was trying to gain control of the territory near the Euphrates River, David met him in battle at Hamath and defeated him.
translation_verse: David ɖu Zoba-fia Hadadezer dzi le Xamat gbɔ esime Hadadezer be yeakeke yeƒe fiaɖuƒe ɖe enu ava ɖo Frat-tɔsisi la nu.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried gold shields, but David took these shields and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: David tsɔ sikakpoxɔnu siwo le Hadadezer ƒe asrafowo si la va Yerusalem.

english_verse: When troops from the Syrian kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
translation_verse: Esi Siriatɔwo tso Damasko va be yewoakpe ɖe Zoba-fia Hadadezer ŋu la, David wu wo dome ame akpe bla eve vɔ eve.

english_verse: Then David stationed some of his troops in Damascus, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Emegbe David ɖe asrafowo da ɖe Siria ƒe du gã Damasko me, eye Siriatɔwo zu David teviwo hedzɔ nu nɛ. Ale Aƒetɔ na David ɖu dzi le afi sia afi si wòyi la.

english_verse: King Tou of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Tou heard that David had defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Hadoram to congratulate David on his victory. Hadoram also brought him gifts made of gold, silver, and bronze.
translation_verse: etsɔ sika, klosalo kple akɔblinu vovovowo de via Hadoram si ɖo ɖe fia David, ado gbe nɛ, eye wòadi nyui nɛ be eɖu Hadadezer dzi. Tou wɔ esia elabe eya kple Hadadezer wowɔa aʋa edziedzi.

english_verse: David gave these gifts to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold he had captured from Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, and Amalek.
translation_verse: David kɔ̀ nu siawo hã ŋu na Aƒetɔ kpe ɖe klosalo kple sika siwo katã wòxɔ tso Edomtɔwo, Moabtɔwo, Amontɔwo, Filistitɔwo kple Amalekitɔwo si la ŋu.

english_verse: Abishai the son of Zeruiah defeated the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed
translation_verse: Abisai, Zeruya vi si Edomtɔ akpe wui enyi le Dze Bali la me.

english_verse: Then he stationed troops in Edom, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler. Everywhere David went, the Lord gave him victory in war. A List of David's Officials (
translation_verse: Eɖe asrafowo da ɖe Edom eye Edomtɔwo katã zu David subɔlawo. Aƒetɔ na David ɖu dzi le afi sia afi si wòyi la.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Yoab, Zeruya vi, le aʋakɔa nu. Yosafat, Axilud vi nye dziɖuɖunyawo léɖila.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were the priests. Shavsha was the secretary.
translation_verse: Zadok, Axitub vi kple Abimelex, Abyatar vi wonye nunɔlawo, eye Savsa nye agbalẽŋlɔla.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were his highest-ranking officials.
translation_verse: Benaya, Yehoyada vi, le Kretitɔwo kple Pletitɔwo, nu. David viŋutsuwo xɔ ɖoƒe kɔkɔtɔwo le fiaŋunɔlawo dome.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, so I will be kind to his son.” He sent some officials to Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died. But when David's officials arrived at Ammon,
translation_verse: David gblɔ be: “Manyo dɔme na Xanun, Naxas vi elabe tɔ́a nyo dɔme nam.” Ale David dɔ amewo ɖa be woaɖafa akɔ nɛ le tɔ́a ƒe ku ta. David ƒe amedɔdɔawo va Xanun gbɔ le Amontɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi be yewoafa akɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Joab saw that the enemy troops were lined up on both sides of him. So he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Syrians.
translation_verse: Esi Yoab kpɔ be futɔwo ƒe aʋakɔa dze aʋa ɖe ye ŋu le ŋgɔ kple megbe la, etia Israel aʋakalẽtɔ tɔxɛwo be yeakpe aʋa kple Siria.

english_verse: Some time later, King Nahash of Ammon died, and his son Hanun became king.
translation_verse: Esia megbe la, Amon-fia Naxas ku, eye via zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and accepted him as their new ruler. The Syrians never helped the Ammonites again.
translation_verse: Esi Hadadezer teviwo kpɔ be Israelviwo ɖu yewo dzi la, wowɔ ŋutifafa kple David, trɔ zu eteviwo. Ale Siriatɔwo megalɔ̃na kpena ɖe Amontɔwo ŋu azɔ o.

english_verse: the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, “Do you really believe King David is honoring your father by sending these men to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our country, so he can come and destroy it.”
translation_verse: Ke Amon dumegãwo gblɔ na Xanun be: “Ðe nèbu be bubudede tɔ́wò ŋu tae David dɔ amewo ɖa be woava fa akɔ na yea? Ðe wòdɔ wo ɖa be woava tsa ŋku le anyigba la dzi boŋ ne wòakpɔ mɔnu ava ɖu mía dzi.”

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off and their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Tete Xanun lé David ƒe amedɔdɔawo. Wolũ ge na wo, lã woƒe awu ʋlaya ɖe domedomee, ɖe agɔnu, eye wotrɔ wo ɖo ɖa.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message that told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Wodo ŋukpe ŋutsuawo ŋutɔ. Esi wova gblɔ ŋutsuawo ŋu nya na David la, edɔ woɖakpe wo. Fia la gblɔ be: “Minɔ Yerixo ne miaƒe ge nato hafi miagbɔ.”

english_verse: David heard what was happening, and he sent out Joab with his army.
translation_verse: Esi David see la, edɔ Yoab kple aʋakalẽawo ƒe aʋakɔ bliboa ɖa.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops marched to the entrance of the city and prepared for battle, while the Syrian troops took their positions in the open fields.
translation_verse: Amontɔwo ho va dze aʋa ɖe dua ƒe agbo nu, eye fia siwo va la dze aʋa ɖe gbe dzi, wo tɔ, wo tɔ.

english_verse: Then he put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and told them to fight against the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Etsɔ aʋakɔ mamlɛa de nɔvia Abisai si ne woakpe aʋa kple Amontɔwo.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Syrians are too much for me to handle, come and help me. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: “Ne èkpɔ be Siriatɔwo sesẽ wum la, ekem nàva kpe ɖe ŋunye. Ne nye hã mekpɔ be Amontɔwo sesẽ wu wò la, ekema mava kpe ɖe ŋuwò.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the towns of our Lord God. I pray he will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Sẽ ŋu, eye na míawɔ kalẽ ɖe míaƒe dukɔ kple mía Mawu ƒe duwo ta. Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ newɔ nu si wòkpɔ be enyo la.”

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Syrians, and the Syrians ran from them.
translation_verse: Ale Yoab kple aʋakɔ si le eŋu la lũ ɖe Siriatɔwo dzi. Siriatɔwo sí le wo nu.

english_verse: When the Ammonite troops saw that the Syrians had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab then returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Esi Amontɔwo kpɔ be Siriatɔwo le sisím la, woawo hã sí le Abisai Yoab nɔvi la nu yi dua me. Yoab trɔ va Yerusalem.

english_verse: As soon as the Syrians realized they had been defeated, they sent for their troops that were stationed on the other side of the Euphrates River. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led these troops to Ammon.
translation_verse: Esi Siriatɔwo kpɔ be Israelviwo ɖu yewo dzi la, wodɔ ame ɖe Siriatɔ siwo le Frat-tɔsisi la ƒe go kemɛ dzi be woaɖakplɔ wo vɛ. Sofax, Hadadezer ƒe aʋakplɔlae nɔ wo nu.

english_verse: David found out what the Syrians were doing, and he brought Israel's entire army together. They crossed the Jordan River, and he commanded them to take their positions facing the Syrian troops. Soon after the fighting began,
translation_verse: Wova gblɔe na David, eye wòƒo Israel ƒe aʋakɔ bliboa nu ƒu. Wotsò Yordan-tɔsisi la va dze aʋa ɖe futɔawo ŋu, eye wokpe aʋa la. David dze aʋa ɖe Siriatɔwo ŋu eye wokpe aʋa kplii.

english_verse: The next spring, the time when kings go to war, Joab marched out in command of the Israelite army and destroyed towns all over the country of Ammon. He attacked the capital city of Rabbah and left it in ruins. But David stayed in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Esi ƒe trɔ eye fiawo ƒe aʋahoɣi ɖo la, Yoab kplɔ aʋakɔ la doe kple ŋusẽ, eye woɖagblẽ nu le Amontɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi. Woɖe to ɖe Raba. Ke David ŋutɔ nɔ Yerusalem. Yoab si Raba, eye wògbãe.

english_verse: He forced the people of Rabbah to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. He also did the same thing with the people in all the other Ammonite towns. David then led Israel's army back to Jerusalem. The Descendants of the Rephaim (

translation_verse: Esia megbe aʋa gadzɔ ɖe Israelviwo kple Filistitɔwo dome le Gezer. Aʋa sia mee Sibekai, Xusatitɔ la wu Sipai, ame si nye ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe dzidzimevi la le, eye wobɔbɔ wo ɖe anyi.

english_verse: In another battle against the Philistines, Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.
translation_verse: Emegbe wogawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo, eye Elxanan Yair vi, wu Lami, Goliat nɔviŋutsu tso Gat. Lami ƒe akplɔti le abe abaladoti ene.

english_verse: Another one of the Philistine soldiers who was a descendant of the Rephaim was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. During a battle at Gath,
translation_verse: Wogawɔ aʋa bubu le Gat. Ame dzɔtsu aɖe nɔ afi ma. Eto asibidɛ ade kple afɔbidɛ ade ale be wo katã le bla eve vɔ ene. Eya hã nye ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe dzidzimevi.

english_verse: he made fun of Israel, so David's nephew Jonathan killed him.
translation_verse: Eɖe alɔ me le Israelviwo ŋu, ale David nɔvi, Yonatan, Simei vi wui.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these three men from Gath who were descendants of the Rephaim.
translation_verse: Ame siawo katã tso ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe ƒome la me le Gat. Wo katã wotsi David kple eƒe dɔlawo ƒe yi nu.

english_verse: But David replied, “No! I want to pay you what they're worth. I can't just take something from you and then offer the Lord a sacrifice that cost me nothing.”
translation_verse: Ke fia ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Kpao, maƒlee ɖe eƒe asi nu tututu, elabe nyemate ŋu axɔ wò nu atsɔ na Aƒetɔ o, eye nyemasa numemevɔ femaxee o.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Gad, one of David's prophets,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Gad, David ƒe nukpɔla be:

translation_verse: Yoab ɖo eŋu na fia la be: “Nye Aƒetɔ Fia, ne Aƒetɔ na dukɔa dzi ɖe edzi zi alafa kura hã la, ɖe menye tewòviwo ko wo katã wonye oa? Nu ka ta nèdi be wò, nye Aƒetɔ, nàwɔ esia? Nu ka ta nàhe fɔbubu va Israel dzi?”

english_verse: But David would not change his mind. And so Joab went everywhere in Israel and Judah and counted the people. He returned to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Gake fia la té nya la ɖe Yoab dzi, ale Yoab yi ɖatsa le Israel-dukɔ blibo la me gagbɔ va Yerusalem.

english_verse: Joab refused to include anyone from the tribes of Levi and Benjamin, because he still disagreed with David's orders. God Punishes Israel (
translation_verse: Ke mexlẽ Levi kple Benyamin ƒe dzidzimeviwo ya ɖe eme o, elabe fia la ƒe nya la nye busunya le Yoab gbɔ.

english_verse: “Tell David that I will punish him in one of three ways. But he will have to choose which one it will be.”
translation_verse: “Yi ɖagblɔ na David be: ‘Aƒetɔ be: Metsɔ nu etɔ̃ le ŋkuwò me ɖom; tia ɖeka ne mawɔ wò?’ ”

english_verse: and David prayed, “It's my fault! I sinned by ordering the people to be counted. They have done nothing wrong—they are innocent sheep. Lord God, please punish me and my family. Don't let the disease wipe out your people.” David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place (
translation_verse: David gblɔ na Mawu be: “Menye nyee be woaxlẽ dukɔa oa? Nyee da vo, wɔ nuvɔ̃ gã sia. Ke alẽha sia ɖe, nu ka wowɔ? O Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu, meɖe kuku na wò, nà wò tohehe nava nye kple tɔ́nye ƒe ƒome dzi, ke mègatsɔ dɔ vɔ̃ tsrɔ̃ wò amewo o.” David ɖi vɔsamlekpui na Aƒetɔ

english_verse: David's order to count the people made God angry, and he punished Israel.
translation_verse: Nu sia medze Mawu ŋu o, ale wòtsrɔ̃ Israel-dukɔa.

english_verse: David prayed, “I am your servant. But what I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Please forgive me.”
translation_verse: Tete David gblɔ na Mawu be: “Mewɔ nuvɔ̃ gã ŋutɔ be mewɔ nu sia; mewɔ lãnu, eya ta meɖe kuku na wò, tsɔ nye wò dɔla ƒe dzidada kem.”

english_verse: Gad went to David and told him: You must choose how the Lord will punish you:
translation_verse: Gad va David gbɔ, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Aƒetɔ be: ‘Tsɔ ɖeka:

english_verse: Will there be three years when the land won't grow enough food for its people? Or will your enemies constantly defeat you for three months? Or will the Lord send a horrible disease to strike your land for three days? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God who sent me.
translation_verse: Dɔwuame ƒe etɔ̃ loo, aʋasisi dzinu etɔ̃, esi me wò futɔwo naɖe wò ɖe nu kple yi loo, alo dɔ vɔ̃ ŋkeke etɔ̃, esi me Aƒetɔ atsɔ eƒe yi ɖe ŋuwò, eye eƒe dɔla agblẽ nu to anyigba blibo la me.’ Azɔ bu eŋu, nàɖo eŋu maɖagblɔ na ame si dɔm ɖa la.”

english_verse: David was miserable and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
translation_verse: David ɖo eŋu na Gad be: “Mexaxa ŋutɔ, ke azɔ la, madze Aƒetɔ si me elabe eƒe amenuveve sɔ gbɔ ŋutɔ. Megana madze amegbetɔ si me o.”

english_verse: So the Lord sent a horrible disease on Israel, and
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ na dɔ vɔ̃ va Israel-nyigba dzi, eye ame akpe bla adrẽ ku.

english_verse: Then he sent an angel to destroy the city of Jerusalem. But just as the angel was about to do that, the Lord felt sorry for all the suffering he had caused the people, and he told the angel, “Stop! They have suffered enough.” This happened at the threshing place that belonged to Araunah the Jebusite.
translation_verse: Mawu ɖo dɔla ɖe Yerusalem be wòatsrɔ̃e, gake esi dɔla la be yeadze nugbegblẽ gɔme la dzɔgbevɔ̃e la ve Mawu, eye wògblɔ na dɔla si le nu gblẽm la be: “Esɔ gbɔ! Dzudzɔ!” Ɣe ma ɣi la, Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla la le tsitre ɖe Ornan, Yebusitɔ la ƒe lugbɔƒe gbɔ.

english_verse: David saw the Lord's angel in the air, holding a sword over Jerusalem. He and the leaders of Israel, who were all wearing sackcloth, bowed with their faces to the ground,
translation_verse: Esi David fɔ kɔ dzi la, ekpɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla la wòle tsitre ɖe anyigba kple dziƒo dome, ɖe yi le aku me do ɖe Yerusalem dzi. Tete David kple eƒe dumegãwo, le akpanya me tsyɔ mo anyi.

english_verse: The Lord's angel told the prophet Gad to tell David that he must go to Araunah's threshing place and build an altar in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla gblɔ na Gad be wòaɖagblɔ na David be neyi ɖaɖi vɔsamlekpui na Aƒetɔ ɖe Ornan, Yebusitɔ la ƒe lugbɔƒe.

english_verse: Araunah and his four sons were threshing wheat at the time, and when they saw the angel, the four sons ran to hide.
translation_verse: Ornan le lu ƒom. Esi Ornan trɔ kɔ la, ekpɔ dɔla la. Via ŋutsu ene siwo le egbɔ la, sí yi ɖabè.

english_verse: Just then, David arrived, and when Araunah saw him, he stopped his work and bowed down.
translation_verse: Esi David va Ornan gbɔ, eye Ornan fɔ kɔ dzi kpɔ David la, edo tso lugbɔƒe la ɖade ta agu ɖe David ŋkume.

english_verse: David said, “Would you sell me your threshing place, so I can build an altar on it to the Lord? Then this disease will stop killing the people. I'm willing to pay whatever you say it's worth.”
translation_verse: David gblɔ na Ornan be: “Tsɔ lugbɔƒe la nam, ne maɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖi na Aƒetɔ. Tsɔe nam ɖe eƒe asi nu tututu, ne dɔ vɔ̃ la nu natso le dukɔa me.”

english_verse: Araunah answered, “Take it, Your Majesty, and do whatever you want with it. I'll even give you the oxen for the sacrifice and the wheat for the grain sacrifice. And you can use the threshing-boards for the fire. It's all yours!”
translation_verse: Tete Ornan ɖo eŋu na David be: “Nye aƒetɔ fia, tsɔe. Tsɔe faa nàtsɔ wɔ nu si dze ŋuwò la. Kpɔ ɖa, mana nyi na numemevɔsa la, tsɔ luƒotiawo wɔ nake eye nàtsɔ lu la wɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsae. Metsɔ wo katã na faa.”

english_verse: David built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. David prayed, and the Lord answered him by sending fire down on the altar.
translation_verse: David ɖi vɔsamlekpui la na Aƒetɔ ɖe afi ma, eye wòsa numemevɔ kple ŋutifafavɔ, eye wòyɔ Aƒetɔ. Etɔ nɛ, eye wòna dzo tso dziƒo va numemevɔsamlekpui la dzi.

english_verse: Then the Lord commanded the angel to put the sword away.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ ɖe gbe na eƒe dɔla be netsɔ eƒe yi la de aku.

english_verse: When David saw that the Lord had answered his prayer, he offered more sacrifices there at the threshing place,
translation_verse: Esi David kpɔ be Aƒetɔ tɔ na ye le Ornan, Yebusitɔ la ƒe lugbɔƒea la, ede asi vɔsasa me le afi ma.

english_verse: because he was afraid of the angel's sword and did not want to go all the way to Gibeon. That's where the sacred tent that Moses had made in the desert was kept, as well as the altar where sacrifices were offered to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke le vɔvɔ̃ na yi si Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla la lé ɖe asi ta la, David mete ŋu yi afi ma be yeaɖabia nu Mawu o.

english_verse: David said, “The temple of the Lord God must be built right here at this threshing place. And the altar for offering sacrifices will also be here.” David Prepares To Build the Temple
translation_verse: David gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, Mawu ƒe aƒee nye esia, eye Israel ƒe numemevɔsamlekpuie nye esia.” Dzadzraɖo na gbedoxɔa tutu

english_verse: David ordered the foreigners living in Israel to come to Jerusalem. Then he assigned some to cut blocks of stone for building the temple.
translation_verse: David ɖe gbe be woaƒo amedzro siwo katã le Israel-nyigba dzi la nu ƒu, eye wòɖe kpeɖaŋudɔwɔlawo be woafú kpe ne woatsɔ tu Mawu ƒe xɔ lae.

english_verse: He also brought an endless supply of cedar logs from the cities of Sidon and Tyre.
translation_verse: Nenema ke sedertiwo hã mele xexlẽme o, elabe Sidontɔwo kple Tirotɔwo he sederti vɛ na David ale gbegbe.

english_verse: He said, “The temple for the Lord must be great, so that everyone in the world will know about it. But since my son Solomon is young and has no experience, I will make sure that everything is ready for the temple to be built.” That's why David did all these things before he died. David Instructs Solomon To Build the Temple
translation_verse: David wɔ esia elabe egblɔ be: “Ðekakpui dzaa, makpɔnuteƒe koe nye vinye Salomo. Evɔ xɔ si wole tutu ge na Aƒetɔ la, ele be wòalolo, anyakpɔ ne eŋu ŋkɔ kple bubu nade du. Eya ta madzra ɖo ɖe eŋu nyuie.” Ale David ƒo nuwo nu ƒu ɖi fũu hafi va ku.

english_verse: David sent for his son Solomon and told him to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Eyɔ via Salomo, eye wògblɔ nɛ be wòatu xɔ na Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la.

english_verse: He said: My son, I wanted to build a temple where the Lord my God would be worshiped.
translation_verse: David gblɔ na Salomo be: “Vinye, nye la, meɖoe be matu xɔ ade bubu Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu ŋu.

english_verse: But some time ago, he told me, “David, you have killed too many people and have fought too many battles. That's why you are not the one to build my temple.
translation_verse: Gake Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe va nam be: ‘Èkɔ ʋu ɖi akpa eye èwɔ aʋa geɖe, eya ta wò la, màtu xɔ nam o, elabe èkɔ ʋu geɖe ɖe anyi le ŋkunye me le anyigba dzi.

english_verse: But when your son becomes king, I will give him peace throughout his kingdom. His name will be Solomon, because during his rule I will keep Israel safe and peaceful.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, wole viŋutsu dzi ge na wò; eya anye ŋutifafame. Mana gbɔdzɔe eyama tso eƒe futɔ siwo ƒo xlãe kpe ɖo la si me, elabe Salomo anye eŋkɔ eye mana ŋutifafa kple gbɔɖeme Israel le eƒe agbe me ŋkekewo me.

english_verse: Solomon will build my temple. He will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him. In fact, one of his descendants will always rule in Israel.”
translation_verse: Eyae atu xɔ ade bubu ŋunyee. Azu vi nam, eye mazu tɔ́ nɛ, eye mana eƒe dziɖuɖu ƒe fiazikpui nali ke ɖe Israel tegbee.’

english_verse: Solomon, my son, I now pray that the Lord your God will be with you and keep his promise to help you build a temple for him.
translation_verse: Azɔ vinye, Aƒetɔ nenɔ kpli wò ne nàtu Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu ƒe xɔ la awu enu, abe ale si wògblɔ le ŋuwò la ene.

english_verse: May he give you wisdom and knowledge, so that you can rule Israel according to his Law.
translation_verse: Ðeko Aƒetɔ nena nyametsotso nyui kple nunya wò ale be ne eɖo wò Israel nu la, nàlé Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu ƒe se la me ɖe asi.

english_verse: If you obey the laws and teachings that the Lord gave Moses, you will be successful. Be strong and brave and don't get discouraged or be afraid of anything.
translation_verse: Ne èkpɔ ɖokuiwò dzi, eye nèlé ɖoɖo kple kɔnu, siwo Aƒetɔ ɖo da ɖi na Israel-dukɔ to Mose dzi la me ɖe asi la, ekema eme anyo na wò. Do ŋusẽ nu eye nalé dzi ɖe ƒo. Mègavɔ̃ o, eye dzika megatso ƒowò o!

english_verse: I have also assigned men who will cut and lay the stone. And there are carpenters and people who are experts in working with
translation_verse: Gawu la, dɔwɔlawo le asiwò zã: kpegbãlawo, gliɖolawo, atikpalawo kple aɖaŋudɔ ɖe sia ɖe wɔla siwo mele xexlẽme o la li.

english_verse: gold, silver, bronze, and iron. You have plenty of workers to do the job. Now get started, and I pray that the Lord will be with you in your work.
translation_verse: Sika, klosalo, akɔbli kple ga yibɔ ŋudɔwɔlawo mele xexlẽme o. Eya ta tso ɖe dɔ la ŋu! Aƒetɔ nenɔ kpli wò!”

english_verse: David then gave orders for the leaders of Israel to help Solomon.
translation_verse: David gblɔ na Israel-dumegãwo katã be woakpe ɖe ye vi, Salomo ŋu. Egblɔ na wo be:

english_verse: David said: The Lord our God has helped me defeat all the people who lived here before us, and he has given you peace from all your enemies. Now this land belongs to the Lord and his people.
translation_verse: “Ɖe Aƒetɔ, miaƒe Mawu la meli kpli mi oa? Ena miekpɔ gbɔdzɔe le go sia go me, elabe etsɔ anyigba la dzi tɔwo de asi nam, eye wobɔbɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ kple eƒe dukɔ la te.

english_verse: Obey the Lord your God with your heart and soul. Begin work on the temple to honor him, so that the sacred chest and the things used for worship can be kept there.
translation_verse: Eya ta miaƒe susu kple dzi naku ɖe Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu ŋu. Mitso ne miatu Aƒetɔ, Mawu ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la, bene woatsɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la kple Mawu ƒe nu kɔkɔeawo ava xɔ si tu ge woala na Aƒetɔ la me.”

english_verse: David was old when he chose his son Solomon to be king of Israel.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi David tsi, eye agbe ɖi ƒo nɛ la, etsɔ via Salomo ɖo fiae ɖe Israel nu.

english_verse: Some time later, David called together all of Israel's leaders, priests, and Levites.
translation_verse: David ƒo Israel-dumegãwo, nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo nu ƒu.

english_verse: He then counted the Levite men who were at least
translation_verse: Ena woxlẽ Levi vi siwo katã xɔ ƒe bla etɔ̃ kple vɔ, eye wode ame akpe bla etɔ̃ vɔ enyi.

english_verse: Every morning and evening, the Levites are to give thanks to the Lord and sing praises to him.
translation_verse: Woanɔ tsitrenu gbe sia gbe ŋdi kple fiẽ ada akpe na Aƒetɔ eye woakafui.

english_verse: David then divided the Levites into three groups according to the clans of Levi's sons, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
translation_verse: David ma Levi viwo ɖe hatsotso etɔ̃ me ɖe woƒe ƒomewo nu ale: Gerson, Kehat kple Merari.

english_verse: Gershon had two sons: Ladan and Shimei.
translation_verse: Gerson viŋutsuwo nye: Ladan kple Simei.

english_verse: Ladan was the father of Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel.
translation_verse: Ladan dzi viŋutsu etɔ̃ Yexiel, ame si nye tsitsitɔ kple Zetam kpakple Yoel.

english_verse: They were all family leaders among their father's descendants. Shimei was the father of Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran.
translation_verse: Simei viŋutsuwo nye: Selomot, Xaziel kple Xaran. Woawoe nye Ladan ƒe ƒometatɔwo.

english_verse: Later, Shimei had four more sons, in the following order: Jahath, Ziza, Jeush, and Beriah. But Jeush and Beriah didn't have many children, so their descendants were counted as one family.
translation_verse: Yaxat nye gbãtɔ, eye Zizae nye evelia. Esi Yeus kple Beria medzi viŋutsu geɖe o ta, wobu wo viwo ƒome ɖekae.

english_verse: Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
translation_verse: Kehat viŋutsuwo nye: Amram, Yizhar, Xebron kple Uziel. Wole ene.

english_verse: Amram was the father of Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were chosen to be in charge of all the sacred things. They served the Lord by offering sacrifices to him and by blessing the people in his name.
translation_verse: Amram viŋutsuwoe nye Aron kple Mose. Wotia Aron be wòakɔ nu siwo nye nu kɔkɔetɔwo ŋu. Eya kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo nawɔ esia tegbee. Woatɔ dzo lifi le Aƒetɔ ƒeme, asubɔ Aƒetɔ, eye woayra ame le Aƒetɔ ŋkɔ me tegbee.

english_verse: Gershom's oldest son was Shebuel.
translation_verse: Sebuel ye nye Gersom ƒe dzidzimeviwo ƒe tatɔ.

english_verse: The second son born to Kohath was Izhar, and his oldest son was Shelomith.
translation_verse: Selomot ye nye Yizhar ƒe dzidzimeviwo ƒe tatɔ.

english_verse: Hebron, the third son of Kohath, was the father of Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
translation_verse: Yeriya ye nye Xebron ƒe dzidzimeviwo ƒe tatɔ. Amarya nye evelia, Yaxaziel nye etɔ̃lia, eye Yekamam nye enelia.

english_verse: Merari had two sons: Mahli and Mushi. Mahli was the father of Eleazar and Kish.
translation_verse: Maxli kple Musi wonye Merari viŋutsuwo, eye Maxli viŋutsuwoe nye Eleazar kple Kis.

english_verse: Eleazar had no sons, only daughters, and they married their uncle's sons.
translation_verse: Eleazar medzi viŋutsu aɖeke hafi ku o; negbe nyɔnuviwo ko. Ale wo nɔvi Kis viŋutsuwo ɖe wo.

english_verse: Mushi the second son of Merari, was the father of Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.
translation_verse: Musi viŋutsuwo nye: Maxli, Eder kple Yeremot; wole etɔ̃.

english_verse: David said: The Lord God of Israel has given his people peace, and he will live in Jerusalem forever.
translation_verse: David gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la na gbɔdzɔe eƒe dukɔ, eye anɔ Yerusalem tegbee;

english_verse: And so, the Levites won't need to move the sacred tent and the things used for worship from place to place.
translation_verse: eya ta megahiã azɔ be Levi viwo naganɔ nubablaɖaka la kple nu siwo katã kpe ɖe eŋu la kɔm tso teƒe yi teƒe o.”

english_verse: will serve the Lord by helping Aaron's descendants do their work at the temple, by keeping the courtyards and rooms of the temple clean, and by making sure that everything used in worship stays pure.
translation_verse: “Ke woƒe dɔe nye be woakpe ɖe Aron ƒe dzidzimeviwo ŋu ne woawɔ dɔ siwo le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ŋu. Woakpɔ xɔxɔnuawo kple xɔawo dzi, aklɔ nu kɔkɔeawo katã ŋu, eye woawɔ dɔ bubu siwo katã hiã le Mawu ƒe aƒe la ŋu.

english_verse: They will also be in charge of the sacred loaves of bread, the flour for the grain sacrifices, the thin wafers, any offerings to be baked, and the flour mixed with olive oil. These Levites will weigh and measure these offerings.
translation_verse: Hekpe ɖe esiawo ŋu la, woakpɔ vɔsabolo kple wɔ memee si wotsɔ wɔa nuɖuɖuvɔsa, tatali si wowɔna kple abolo maʋamaʋã, nu siwo wotɔna le nutɔgba me, nu siwo katã wobakana kple ami kple nudzidzenu vovovo siwo le xɔ la me la dzi.

english_verse: They must also give thanks and sing praises when sacrifices are offered on each Sabbath, as well as during New Moon Festivals and other religious feasts. There must always be enough Levites on duty at the temple to do everything that needs to be done.
translation_verse: Ɣe sia ɣi si woasa vɔ na Aƒetɔ le Dzudzɔgbe, alo Dzinu Yeye dzi alo le ŋkekenyui bubuwo dzi la, Levi viwo ƒe xexlẽme si woɖo na ŋkekea la nasɔ ta ava.

english_verse: They were once in charge of taking care of the sacred tent; now they are responsible for the temple and for helping Aaron's descendants.
translation_verse: Woawoe awɔ dɔ siwo katã ku ɖe godoƒegbadɔa kple eƒe kɔkɔeƒea ŋu, eye woanɔ wo nɔvi Aron viwo ŋu, asubɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒea me.”

english_verse: Aaron's descendants were then divided into work groups. Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Aron ƒe dzidzimeviwo ƒe hatsotsowoe nye esi: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar kple Itamar.

english_verse: But Nadab and Abihu died long before their father, without having any sons. That's why Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
translation_verse: Ke Nadab kple Abihu tre kuku na wo tɔ́, eye viŋutsu menɔ wo si o, ale Eleazar kple Itamar zu nunɔlawo.

english_verse: David divided Aaron's descendants into groups, according to their assigned work. Zadok, one of Eleazar's descendants, and Ahimelech, one of Ithamar's descendants, helped David.
translation_verse: David ma Aron ƒe dzidzimeviwo ɖe hatsotsowo me ɖe woƒe dɔwo nu. Ame siwo kpe ɖe eŋu le dɔ sia me lawoe nye Zadok, Eleazar ƒe dzidzime vi kple Aximelex, Itamar ƒe dzidzime vi.

english_verse: groups, and Ithamar's were divided into eight groups, because Eleazar's family included more family leaders.
translation_verse: wui asiekelia dze Petaxya dzi, bla evelia dze Yexezkel dzi,

english_verse: However, both families included temple officials and priests, and so to make sure the work was divided fairly, David asked God what to do.
translation_verse: Wodzidze nu hema woawo kple eve la siaa, elabe kɔkɔeƒea dzikpɔlawo kple Mawu ƒe dɔnunɔlawo sɔ gbɔ le Eleazar kple Itamar ƒe dzidzimeviawo dome.

english_verse: As each group was assigned their duties, Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the Levite wrote down the name of the family leader in charge of that group. The witnesses were David and his officials, as well as Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the family leaders from the clans of the priests and the Levites.
translation_verse: Ne wodzidze nu ɖe Eleazar ƒe ƒome ɖeka dzi la, wodzidzea nu ɖe Itamar hã ƒe ƒome ɖeka dzi. Agbalẽŋlɔla Semaya, Netaneel vi, tso Levi viwo domee ŋlɔnɛ ɖi. Fia ŋutɔ, dumegãwo, nunɔla Zadok, Aximelex, Abyatar vi la kple nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo ƒe ƒometatɔwo le eteƒe.

english_verse: These men were assigned their duties at the temple, just as the Lord God of Israel had commanded their ancestor Aaron. The Rest of the Levites Are Assigned Their Duties
translation_verse: Ame siawo xɔ woƒe dɔdeasi si woɖo na wo le woƒe subɔsubɔdɔ me be woava Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me le ɖoɖo si wo tɔ́ Aron ɖo na wo la nu, abe ale si Aƒetɔ, Israel Mawu la ɖo nɛ la ene. Levi viwo ƒe tatɔwo

english_verse: Here is a list of the other descendants of Levi: Amram was the ancestor of Shubael and Jehdeiah.
translation_verse: Levi viŋutsu mamlɛawoe nye esi: Subael tso Amram viwo dome, Yexdeya tso Subael viwo dome.

english_verse: Rehabiah was the ancestor of Isshiah, the oldest son in his family.
translation_verse: Yisiya nye tatɔ na Rexabya viwo.

english_verse: Izhar was the father of Shelomoth and the grandfather of Jahath.
translation_verse: Selomot tso Yizhar viwo dome, Yaxat tso Selomot viwo dome.

english_verse: Hebron had four sons, in the following order: Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
translation_verse: Yeriya kple eyometɔwo: Amarya, Yaxaziel kple Yekamam, ame siwo nye Xebron viwo.

english_verse: Uzziel was the father of Micah and the grandfather of Shamir.
translation_verse: Mixa tso Uziel viwo dome, eye Samir tso Mixa viwo dome.

english_verse: Isshiah, Micah's brother, was the father of Zechariah.
translation_verse: Mixa nɔvie nye Yisiya. Zaxarya tso Yisiya viwo dome.

english_verse: Merari was the father of Mahli, Mushi, and Jaaziah.
translation_verse: Merari viwo nye Maxli kple Musi kpakple Musi vi Yaazya viwo.

english_verse: Jaaziah had three sons: Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
translation_verse: Yaazya dzi viŋutsu etɔ̃: Soham, Zakur kple Ibri.

english_verse: Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the descendants of Levi, according to their clans.
translation_verse: Musi viwoe nye Maxli, Eder kple Yerimot. Ame siawoe nye Levi ƒe dzidzimeviwo ɖe woƒe ƒomewo nu.

english_verse: Each one was assigned his duties in the same way that their relatives the priests had been assigned their duties. David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the family leaders of the priests and Levites were the witnesses.
translation_verse: Woawo hã dzidze nu abe wo nɔvi Aron ƒe dzidzimeviwo ke ene le David, fia la, Zadok, Aximelex kple nunɔlawo kpakple Levi viwo ƒe ƒometatɔwo ŋkume. Ƒometatɔ tsitsiawo kple wo tsɛwo siaa nɔ eteƒe.

english_verse: David and the temple officials chose the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to be in charge of music. They were to praise the Lord by playing cymbals, harps and other stringed instruments. Here is a list of the musicians and their duties:
translation_verse: David kple asrafowo ƒe amegãwo tia Asaf, Heman kple Yedutun viwo, ame siwo nye kasaŋku, saŋku kple gakogoe ƒolawo be Yedutun viwo naɖe gbeƒã le subɔsubɔ me.

english_verse: Asaph's four sons, Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, were under the direction of their father and played music whenever the king told them to.
translation_verse: Asaf viwoe nye: Sakur, Yosef, Netanya kple Asarela. Wonɔ Asaf ƒe kpɔkplɔ te, eye Asaf ɖea gbeƒã ɖe fia la ƒe ɖoɖo nu.

english_verse: Heman was one of the king's prophets, and God honored Heman by giving him
translation_verse: Ame siawo katã nye Heman, fia ƒe nukpɔla viwo. Woawoe kua kpẽ le Mawu ƒe nya la nu. Mawu na viŋutsu wui ene kple vinyɔnu etɔ̃ Heman.

english_verse: His sons were under his direction and played cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments during times of worship at the temple. Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman took their orders directly from the king.
translation_verse: Ame siawo katã tsɔa gakogoe, kasaŋku kple saŋku ƒoa hae le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me, le wo tɔ́ Asaf, Yedutun kple Heman ƒe kpɔkplɔ te, abe ale si fia la ɖoe na wo la ene.

english_verse: David assigned them their duties by asking the Lord what he wanted. Everyone was responsible for something, whether young or old, teacher or student.
translation_verse: Ðe wodzidzea nu ɖe ame sia ame ƒe dɔwɔɣi dzi; ɖevi o, ame tsitsi o, nusrɔ̃la o, nufiala o, wo dome ɖe sia ɖe.

english_verse: Elam, Jehohanan, and Eliehoenai.
translation_verse: Elam, atɔ̃lia; Yehohanan, adelia kple Elyoenai, adrẽlia.

english_verse: Obed-Edom had been blessed with eight sons: Shemaiah, Jehozabad, Joah, Sachar, Nethanel, Ammiel, Issachar, and Peullethai.
translation_verse: Amiel, adelia; Isaxar, adrẽlia kple Peuletai, enyilia. Mawu yra Obed-Edom ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Shemaiah was the father of Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad, Elihu, and Semachiah. They were all respected leaders in their clan.
translation_verse: Semaya viwoe nye: Otani, Rafael, Obed kple Elzabad. Wo nɔviwoe nye Elihu kple Semaxya, siwo ŋu ŋutete le.

english_verse: Eighteen descendants of Meshelemiah were chosen for this work.
translation_verse: Meselemya viwo kple nɔviawo nye kalẽtɔwo. Wole ame wui enyi.

english_verse: Hosah, from the Merari clan, was the father of Shimri, Hilkiah, Tebaliah, and Zechariah. Hosah had made Shimri the family leader, even though he was not the oldest son. Thirteen men from Hosah's family were chosen to be temple guards.
translation_verse: Xilkiyae nye vi evelia. Tebalya nye etɔ̃lia, eye Zaxarya nye enelia. Xosa viwo katã kple nɔviawo de ame wui ene.

english_verse: The guards were divided into groups, according to their family leaders, and they were assigned duties at the temple, just like the other Levites.
translation_verse: Dɔdeasi le agbonudzɔlawo ƒe hatsotso siwo wotia ɖe woƒe kplɔlawo ŋu la si abe wo nɔviwo ke ene. Wosubɔna le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me abe dzɔlawo ene.

english_verse: Each group, no matter how large or small, was assigned a gate to guard, and they let the Lord show them what he wanted done.
translation_verse: Wodzidze nu le ƒome ɖe sia ɖe me, eɖale sue, alo elolo o, ɖe agbo si ŋu woadzɔ la dzi.

english_verse: Shelemiah was chosen to guard the East Gate. Zechariah his son was a wise man and was chosen to guard the North Gate.
translation_verse: Nudzidzea dze Selemya dzi be wòadzɔ ɣedzeƒe gome ŋu, eye wòdze via Zaxarya, aɖaŋu nyui ɖola la dzi be wòadzɔ dzigbeme gome.

english_verse: Obed-Edom was then chosen to guard the South Gate, and his sons were chosen to guard the storerooms.
translation_verse: Obed-Edom xɔ anyigbeme gome, eye viawo xɔ nudzraɖoƒe la.

english_verse: Shuppim and Hosah were chosen to guard the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the upper road. The guards were assigned the following work schedule:
translation_verse: Supim kple Xosa woxɔ ɣetoɖoƒe gome kple Salexet-gbo si ʋu ɖe mɔ si lia to la dzi. Dzɔla ɖe sia ɖe sɔ ɖe nɔvia tɔ nu.

english_verse: Each day six guards were on duty on the east side of the temple, four were on duty on the north side, and four were on duty on the south side. Two guards were stationed at each of the two storerooms,
translation_verse: Gbe sia gbe la, agbonudzɔla ade nɔa ɣedzeƒe gome, ene nɔa dzigbeme gome, eye ene bubuwo hã nɔa anyigbeme gome. Ame eve dzɔa nudzraɖoƒe eveawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu gbe sia gbe.

english_verse: four were stationed along the road leading to the west courtyard, and two guards stayed in the court itself.
translation_verse: Le Parbar la gome la, ame ene le mɔ to, eye eve le Parbar la ŋutɔ.

english_verse: These were the guard duties assigned to the men from the clans of Korah and Merari. Guards Are Assigned to the Treasury
translation_verse: Esiawoe nye agbonudzɔlawo ƒe hatsotsowo tso Korax kple Merari ƒe ƒomeawo me. Gbedoxɔ me dɔ bubuwo

english_verse: The Levites who were relatives of the Korahites and the Merarites were in charge of guarding the temple treasury and the gifts that had been dedicated to God.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ Axiya si nye Levi ƒe dzidzimevi la ɖo Mawu ƒe aƒe la ƒe kesinɔnuwo kple nu kɔkɔeawo nu.

english_verse: Ladan was from the Gershon clan and was the father of Jehieli. Many of his other descendants were family leaders in the clan.
translation_verse: Ƒome geɖewo dzɔ tso Ladan, ame si nye Gerson viwo dometɔ ɖeka la me, eye viawo nye ƒomemegãwo. Wo dometɔ ɖekae nye Yexiel.

english_verse: Jehieli was the father of Zetham and Joel, and they were responsible for guarding the treasury.
translation_verse: Yexiel viwoe nye: Zetam kple nɔvia Yoel; woawoe woɖo Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒea ƒe kesinɔnuwo nu.

english_verse: Other guards at the treasury were from the Kohathite clans of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
translation_verse: Amewo tso Amram, Yizhar Xebron kple Uziel ƒomeawo me. Wo dometɔ ɖekae nye

english_verse: Shebuel was a descendant of Gershom the son of Moses. He was the chief official in charge of the temple treasury.
translation_verse: Sebuel, ame si nye Mose vi, Gersom ƒe dzidzimevi la, eyae nye dzikpɔlawo ƒe tatɔ.

english_verse: Shelomoth and his relatives were in charge of all the gifts that were dedicated to the Lord. These included the gifts that King David had dedicated, as well as those dedicated by the family leaders, army officers, and army commanders.
translation_verse: Selomot sia kple nɔviawoe le kesinɔnu kɔkɔe siwo katã fia David ŋutɔ, ƒometatɔwo, asrafo alafawo kple akpewo ƒe amegãwo kpakple aʋakplɔlawo, ɖeɖe ɖe aga la nu.

english_verse: And whenever valuable things were captured in battle, these men brought back some of them to make repairs to the temple.
translation_verse: Aboyonu siwo woxɔ le aʋa me la, wokɔ̀ wo ŋu hena Aƒetɔ ƒe xɔ la dzikpɔkpɔ.

english_verse: Shelomoth and his relatives were responsible for any gifts that had been given to the temple, including those from Samuel the prophet, King Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah. Other Officers Are Assigned Their Duties
translation_verse: Nu kɔkɔe siwo katã ŋu nukpɔla Samuel kple Saul, Kis vi la kple Abner, Ner vi kpakple Yoab, Zeruya vi, woɖe ɖe aga la hã le eme. Wotsɔa nunana kɔkɔewo katã dea asi na Selomot kple nɔviawo. Levitɔ bubuwo ƒe dɔwo

english_verse: Chenaniah from the Izhar clan and his sons were government officials and judges. They did not work at the temple.
translation_verse: Wotia Kenanya kple viawo tso Yizhar ƒe dzidzimeviwo dome ɖo dudɔwo nu le Israel. Woawoe nye dudɔdzikpɔlawo kple ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah had begun to count the people, but he stopped when the Lord began punishing Israel. So the total number was never included in David's official records. Officials in Charge of the King's Property
translation_verse: Yoab, Zeruya viŋutsue dze wo xexlẽ gɔme; ke mewu enu o, elabe esia he dɔmedzoe va Israel dzi. Ale womede xexlẽme la fia David ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽ me o. David ƒe nunɔamesiwo dzikpɔlawo

english_verse: In the first month, Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel,
translation_verse: Ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe hatsotso nɔ Yasobeam, Zabdiel vi ƒe kpɔkplɔ te.

english_verse: in the second month, Dodai the Ahohite, whose assistant was Mikloth;
translation_verse: Ɣleti evelia ƒe hatsotso nɔ Dodai si nye Axoxitɔ la ƒe kpɔkplɔ te. Dumegã Miklot hã nɔ eƒe hatsotsoa me.

english_verse: in the third month, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada the priest,
translation_verse: Ɣleti etɔ̃lia ƒe hatsotso nɔ Benaya, nunɔla Yoyada vi ƒe kpɔkplɔ te.

english_verse: who was the leader of the Thirty Warriors, and whose son Ammizabad was also an army commander;
translation_verse: Benaya nye Kalẽtɔ Blaetɔ̃awo dometɔ ɖeka, eye wònye woƒe tatɔ. Via Amizabad hã nɔ hatsotso sia me.

english_verse: in the fourth month, Asahel the brother of Joab, whose son Zebadiah took over command after him;
translation_verse: Ɣleti enelia ƒe hatsotso nɔ Asahel, Yoab nɔvi ƒe kpɔkplɔ te. Via Zabadya va ɖe eyome.

english_verse: in the fifth month, Shamhuth from the Izrah clan;
translation_verse: Ɣleti atɔ̃lia ƒe hatsotso nɔ Samhut, si tso Yizrax, ƒe dzidzimeviwo dome la ƒe kpɔkplɔ te.

english_verse: in the sixth month, Ira the son of Ikkesh from Tekoa;
translation_verse: Ɣleti adelia ƒe hatsotso nɔ Ira, si nye Ikes vi, tso Tekoa, ƒe kpɔkplɔ te.

english_verse: in the seventh month, Helez from Pelon in the territory of Ephraim;
translation_verse: Ɣleti adrẽlia ƒe hatsotso nɔ Xelez, tso Perlon le Efrayim-to la me ƒe kpɔkplɔ te.

english_verse: in the eighth month, Sibbecai from Hushah of the Zerah clan;
translation_verse: Ɣleti enyilia ƒe hatsotso nɔ Sibekai, Xusatitɔ si tso Zarxi ƒe dzidzimeviwo dome la ƒe kpɔkplɔ te.

english_verse: in the ninth month, Abiezer from Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin;
translation_verse: Ɣleti asiekelia ƒe hatsotso nɔ Abiezer, Anatotitɔ, si tso Benyamin-to la me ƒe kpɔkplɔ te.

english_verse: in the tenth month, Maharai from Netophah of the Zerah clan;
translation_verse: Ɣleti ewolia ƒe hatsotso nɔ Maharai, Netofatitɔ, si tso Zarxi ƒe dzidzimeviwo dome la ƒe kpɔkplɔ te.

english_verse: in the eleventh month, Benaiah from Pirathon in the territory of Ephraim;
translation_verse: Ɣleti wui ɖekɛlia ƒe hatsotso nɔ Benaya, Piratonitɔ si tso Efrayim-to la me ƒe kpɔkplɔ te.

english_verse: in the twelfth month, Heldai from Netophah, who was a descendant of Othniel. David Assigns Tribal Leaders
translation_verse: Ɣleti wui evelia ƒe hatsotso nɔ Xeldai, Netofatitɔ, si nye Otniel ƒe dzidzimevi la ƒe kpɔkplɔ te. Ame akpe bla eve vɔ ene nɔ hatsotso la me. Israel-toawo ƒe tatɔwo

english_verse: When David decided to count the people of Israel, he gave orders not to count anyone under
translation_verse: Ke David mexlẽ ame siwo mexɔ ƒe bla eve la ŋlɔ ɖi o, elabe Aƒetɔ do ŋugbe be yeana Israelviwo adzi asɔ gbɔ abe ɣletiviwo ene.

english_verse: years of age, because the Lord had promised long ago that Israel would have as many people as there are stars in the sky.
translation_verse: na Efrayim viwoe nye Hosea, Azazya viŋutsu; na Manase-to afã la viwoe nye Yoel, Pedaya viŋutsu;

english_verse: Azmaveth the son of Adiel was in charge of the king's personal storage rooms. Jonathan the son of Uzziah was in charge of the king's other storerooms that were in the towns, the villages, and the defense towers in Israel.
translation_verse: Fia la ƒe kesinɔnuwo dzraɖoƒe dzikpɔlae nye: Azmavet, Adiel vi. Yonatan, Uziya vie kpɔa nudzraɖoƒe siwo le agblewo, dutawo, kɔƒewo kple mɔ́ sesẽwo me la dzi.

english_verse: Shimei from Ramah was in charge of the vineyards, and Zabdi from Shepham was in charge of storing the wine.
translation_verse: Simei, Ramatitɔ lae le waingblewo nu, eye Zabdi, Sifmitɔ lae le waingble me kutsetsewo kple ahadzraɖoƒewo nu.

english_verse: Baal Hanan from Geder was in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the western foothills, and Joash was in charge of storing the olive oil.
translation_verse: Baal-Xanan, Grederitɔ lae le amiti kple sikamorti siwo le tagba la nu, eye Yoas kpɔa amidzraɖoƒewo dzi.

english_verse: Shitrai from Sharon was responsible for the cattle that were kept in Sharon Plain, and Shaphat son of Adlai was responsible for those kept in the valleys.
translation_verse: Sitrai, Saronitɔ lae le lãha siwo wonyina le Saron la nu, eye Safat, Adlai vie le nyi siwo wonyina le bali me la nu.

english_verse: These were the men in charge of David's royal property. David's Personal Advisors
translation_verse: eye via Yaziz, Hagritɔ le alẽhawo nu. Ame siawo katã nye fia David ƒe nunɔamesiwo dzikpɔlawo. David ƒe aɖaŋuɖolawo

english_verse: David's uncle Jonathan was a wise and intelligent advisor. He and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni taught David's sons.
translation_verse: David tɔɖea, Yonatan nye fia ƒe aɖaŋuɖola. Enye ame nyanu kple agbalẽnyala. Yexiel, Xaxmoni vie kpɔa fia viwo dzi.

english_verse: Ahithophel and Hushai the Archite were two of David's advisors.
translation_verse: Axitofel nye fia ƒe adaŋudela, eye Xusai Arkitɔ lae nye fia xɔlɔ̃.

english_verse: Jehoiada the son of Benaiah was the king's advisor after Ahithophel, and later, Abiathar was his advisor. Joab was commander of Israel's army.
translation_verse: Ame siwo kplɔ Axitofel ɖo lae nye: Yoyada, Benaya vi kple Abyatar, Yoab nye fia ƒe aʋakplɔla gãtɔ.

english_verse: David called a meeting in Jerusalem for all of Israel's leaders, including the tribal leaders, the government officials, the army commanders, the officials in charge of the royal property and livestock, the palace officials, and the brave warriors.
translation_verse: David ƒo Israel-dumegãwo katã nu ƒu ɖe Yerusalem. Ale toawo ƒe hatsotso siwo subɔa fia la ƒe kplɔlawo: ame akpewo kple ame alafawo ƒe tatɔwo, ame siwo katã kpɔa fia ƒe nunɔamesiwo, eƒe lãhawo kple viawo dzi, fiasã la dzikpɔlawo, aʋakalẽawo kpakple aʋawɔlawo katã va ƒo ƒu.

english_verse: After everyone was there, David stood up and said: Listen to me, my people. I wanted to build a place where the sacred chest would be kept, so we could go there and worship the Lord our God. I have prepared all the supplies for building a temple,
translation_verse: David fia la tso ɖe tsitre, eye wògblɔ be: “Nɔvinyewo kple nye dukɔmetɔwo, miɖo tom! Meɖo tame vevie be matu gbɔɖemeƒe na Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la kple afɔɖodzinu na mía Mawu la, eye medzra ɖo ɖe etutu ŋu hã.

english_verse: but the Lord has refused to let me build it, because he said I have killed too many people in battle.
translation_verse: Gake Mawu gblɔ nam be: ‘Màtu xɔ ade bubu ŋunye o, elabe aʋawɔme nènye, eye nèkɔ ʋu ɖi.’

english_verse: The Lord God chose Judah to be the leading tribe in Israel. Then from Judah, he chose my father's family, and from that family, he chose me to be the king of Israel, and he promised that my descendants will also rule as kings.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu tiam tso tɔgbuinyewo ƒe ƒome blibo la me, be maɖu fia ɖe Israel dzi tegbee, elabe Yuda-to lae wòtia be wòanye fia, eye tɔ́nye ƒe ƒome wòtia le Yuda. Nenema ke edze eŋu le tɔ́nye viwo dome be wòtsɔm ɖo fiae ɖe Israel blibo la nu.

english_verse: The Lord has blessed me with many sons, but he chose my son Solomon to be the next king of Israel.
translation_verse: Le vi geɖe siwo Aƒetɔ nam la dome la, etia vinye Salomo be wòanɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe fiaɖuƒe la ƒe fiazikpui dzi le Israel.

english_verse: The Lord said to me, “Your son Solomon will build my temple, and it will honor me. Solomon will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him.
translation_verse: Egblɔ nam be: ‘Viwò Salomo ye atu nye aƒe kple eƒe xɔxɔnuwo, elabe metiae be wòanye vinye, eye manye tɔ́a.

english_verse: My friends, you are the Lord's people. And now, with God as your witness, I want you to promise that you will do your best to obey everything the Lord God has commanded us. Then this land will always belong to you and your descendants.
translation_verse: Eya ta mele nu xlɔ̃m mi le Israel bliboa, si nye Aƒetɔ ƒe ha la ŋkume, eye Mawu hã le esem, be: miwɔ Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la ƒe sededewo katã dzi, eye midi eyome mɔ vevie bene anyigba nyui la nanɔ mia si ne miava gblẽ ɖi abe domenyinu ene na mia megbeviwo tegbee.

english_verse: Solomon, my son, worship God and obey him with all your heart and mind, just as I have done. He knows all your thoughts and your reasons for doing things, and so if you turn to him, he will hear your prayers. But if you ignore him, he will reject you forever.
translation_verse: “Azɔ wò vinye Salomo, dze si tɔ́wò ƒe Mawu la, ne nàsubɔe kple wò tamesusu kple dzimedidi ɖeka dzaa, elabe Aƒetɔ dzroa dziwo katã me kpɔna, eye wònya ame sia ame ƒe ɖoɖo kple tamesusu! Ne èdii la, ana nàkpɔe; ke ne ètrɔ le eyome la, atsɔ wò aƒu gbe tegbee.

english_verse: The Lord has chosen you to build a temple for worshiping him. Be confident and do the work you have been assigned.
translation_verse: Kpɔ nyuie, elabe Aƒetɔ tia wò be nàtu xɔ si anye eƒe kɔkɔeƒea. Do ŋusẽ nu, ne nàtso ɖe dɔa ŋu! Lé dzi ɖe ƒo eye nàwɔe ade goe.”

english_verse: After David finished speaking, he gave Solomon the plans for building the main rooms of the temple, including the porch, the storerooms, the rooms upstairs and downstairs, as well as the most holy place.
translation_verse: David tsɔ gbedoxɔa, eŋu xɔwo, nudzraɖoƒewo, eƒe dzisasrãwo, xɔa etometɔwo kple Kɔkɔeƒe afi si wotsɔa nuvɔ̃wo kena le la ƒe nɔnɔmetata de asi na Salomo.

english_verse: He gave Solomon his plans for the courtyards and the open areas around the temple, and for the rooms to store the temple treasures and gifts that had been dedicated to God.
translation_verse: Etsɔ ɖoɖo siwo katã wòwɔ ɖe xɔxɔnuawo ŋu, wo ŋu xɔwo, nudzraɖoƒewo kple nunana siwo ŋu wòkɔ na Aƒetɔ la dzraɖoƒewo la de asi nɛ.

english_verse: David also gave Solomon his plans for dividing the priests and the Levites into groups, as well as for the work that needed to be done at the temple and for taking care of the objects used for worship.
translation_verse: Hekpe ɖe eŋu la, egblɔ ɖoɖo si wòwɔ ɖe nunɔlawo, Levi viwo ƒe hatsotsoawo, ale si woasubɔe le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒeme kple subɔsubɔnuawo katã ŋu nya na Salomo.

english_verse: He told Solomon how much gold and silver was to be used in making the sacred objects,
translation_verse: Egblɔ sika kpekpeme si hiã na sikagba siwo katã wòatsɔ asubɔe kple klosalo kpekpeme si hiã na klosalogba siwo katã hiã la nɛ.

english_verse: the gold table which held the sacred loaves of bread, the tables made of silver,
translation_verse: Egblɔ sika kple klosalo kpekpeme si woatsɔ awɔ sikakplɔ̃ si dzi woada aboloawo ɖo kple klosalo si hiã na klosalokplɔ̃wo la nɛ.

english_verse: the gold incense altar, and the gold statue of a chariot for the winged creatures which were on the lid of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Woatsɔ sika kɔkɔetɔ awɔ vɔsamlekpui si dzi woanɔ dzo tɔm lifi le, eye woatsɔ sika awɔ tasiaɖam siwo dzi sika kerubiawo anɔ, akeke aʋala atsyɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nubablaɖaka la dzi.

english_verse: David then said to Solomon: The Lord showed me how his temple is to be built.
translation_verse: David gblɔ na Salomo be: “Esiawo katã nye Aƒetɔ, ame si fia dɔa ƒe ɖoɖom la ƒe asinuŋɔŋlɔ.”

english_verse: But you must see that everything is done according to these plans. Be confident, and never be afraid of anything or get discouraged. The Lord my God will help you do everything needed to finish the temple, so it can be used for worshiping him.
translation_verse: David gayi edzi gblɔ na via Salomo be: “Do ŋusẽ nu, wɔ kalẽ, nàtso ɖe dɔa ŋu wɔ. Mègavɔ̃ o, eye dzika megatso ƒowò o, elabe Aƒetɔ, Mawu, nye Mawu la li kpli wò. Maɖe asi le ŋuwò o, eye nyemagblẽ wò ɖi akpɔ o, ɖeko nàwu eƒe aƒe la kple eŋudɔwo katã nu.

english_verse: The priests and Levites have been assigned their duties, and all the skilled workers are prepared to do their work. The people and their leaders will do anything you tell them.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo ƒe hatsotsoawoe nye esi li na subɔsubɔdɔ ɖe sia ɖe le Mawu ƒe aƒe la ŋu. Aɖaŋudɔwɔla geɖe siwo nya nu vovovowo la lɔ̃ faa be yewoakpe ɖe ŋuwò, eye dumegãwo kple dukɔ blibo la le asiwò nu ko kpɔm.”

english_verse: That's why I have done my best to get everything Solomon will need to build it—gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, onyx, turquoise, colored gems, all kinds of precious stones, and marble.
translation_verse: Metsɔ nye ŋutete katã dzra ɖo ɖe nye Mawu ƒe aƒe la ŋu. Medi sika ɖe sikanuwo ŋu, klosalo ɖe klosalonuwo ŋu, akɔbli ɖe akɔblinuwo ŋu, ga yibɔ ɖe ga yibɔ nuwo ŋu kple ati ɖe atinuwo ŋu. Meƒo sohamkpe kple kpe siwo woatsɔ aɖo awuwo ŋu, kpe yibɔwo, kpe ŋɔŋɔewo, kpe xɔasi vovovowo kpakple kpe ɣiwo nu ƒu taŋtaŋ.

english_verse: and to make the gold and silver objects. Now, who else will show their dedication to the Lord by giving gifts for building his temple?
translation_verse: Woatsɔ wo awɔ sikanuawo kple klosalonuawo katã kpakple aɖaŋuwɔlawo ƒe dɔ vovovoawoe. Azɔ mia dometɔ kae lɔ̃ be yeana nu Aƒetɔ faa egbea?”

english_verse: After David finished speaking, the family leaders, the tribal leaders, the army commanders, and the government officials voluntarily gave gifts
translation_verse: Tete ƒometatɔawo, toawo ƒe tatɔwo, ame akpewo kple ame alafawo ƒe tatɔwo kpakple dumegãwo lɔ̃ na nu faa.

english_verse: Everyone who owned precious stones also donated them to the temple treasury, where Jehiel from the Levite clan of Gershon guarded them.
translation_verse: Ame si si kpe xɔasi le la tsɔe vɛ na Yexiel, Gerson vi la ne wòanye Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ƒe kesinɔnu.

english_verse: David and the people were very happy that so much had been given to the Lord, and they all celebrated. David Praises the Lord
translation_verse: Dukɔ la lɔ̃ na nu tso dzi blibo me faa, eya ta wokpɔ dzidzɔ eye fia David hã kpɔ dzidzɔ ŋutɔ. David kafu Mawu

english_verse: Then, in front of everyone, David sang praises to the Lord: I praise you forever, Lord! You are the God our ancestor Jacob worshiped.
translation_verse: Tete David kafu Aƒetɔ le ameha blibo la ŋkume gblɔ be: “Woakafu wò Aƒetɔ, mía tɔgbui Israel ƒe Mawu tso mavɔ me yi mavɔ me.

english_verse: Your power is great, and your glory is seen everywhere in heaven and on earth. You are king of the entire world,
translation_verse: O, Aƒetɔ tɔwòe nye gãnyenye, ŋusẽ, ŋutikɔkɔe, dziɖuɖu kple bubu, elabe nu sia nu si le dziƒo kple anyigba la, tɔwòe. O, Aƒetɔ, tɔwòe nye fiaɖuɖu eye wòe nye gã ɖe nuwo katã dzi.

english_verse: and you rule with strength and power. You make people rich and powerful and famous.
translation_verse: Kesinɔnu kple bubu tso gbɔwò, eye nèɖu fia ɖe nuwo keŋ dzi. Asiwò me ŋusẽ kple ŋutete le, eye gbɔwò wòtsona be ame nazu gã, eye wòakpɔ ŋusẽ.

english_verse: But why should we be happy that we have given you these gifts? They belong to you, and we have only given back what is already yours.
translation_verse: “Ke ame kae menye, eye nu ka nye dukɔ nye be míete ŋu na nu faa alea? Elabe gbɔwòe nu sia nu tso, eye asiwò me míexɔ wo le gatsɔ na wò.

english_verse: We are only foreigners living here on earth for a while, just as our ancestors were. And we will soon be gone, like a shadow that suddenly disappears.
translation_verse: Amedzrowo míenye le ŋkuwò me, eye emetsolawo míenye, abe mía tɔgbuiwo katã ene. Míaƒe agbenɔŋkekewo le abe vɔvɔli ene le anyigba dzi; wometɔna ɖi o.

english_verse: Our Lord God, we have brought all these things for building a temple to honor you. They belong to you, and you gave them to us.
translation_verse: O Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu, nu geɖe siwo míena be woatsɔ atu xɔ hena wò ŋkɔ ŋuti kɔkɔ la katã tso asiwò me, eye tɔwòe nye ɖe sia ɖe.

english_verse: But we are happy, because everyone has voluntarily given you these things. You know what is in everyone's heart, and you are pleased when people are honest.
translation_verse: Nye Mawu, menyae be edzroa dzime kpɔna, eye dzimekɔkɔ nyoa ŋuwò. Mena nu siawo katã faa kple dzimekɔkɔ, eye mekpɔ be wò dukɔ si ƒo ƒu ɖe afii hã tsɔ dzidzɔ na nu wò faa.

english_verse: Always make us eager to give, and help us be faithful to you, just as our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob faithfully worshiped you.
translation_verse: O Aƒetɔ, wò si nye mía tɔgbuiwo Abraham kple Isak kple Israel ƒe Mawu, na susu kple tameɖoɖo sia nanɔ wò dukɔ si ɖaa, eye nàtrɔ woƒe dziwo ɖe ŋuwò.

english_verse: And give Solomon the desire to completely obey your laws and teachings, and the desire to build the temple for which I have provided these gifts.
translation_verse: Na vinye Salomo nalé wò sededewo, nufiafiawo kple ɖoɖowo me ɖe asi sesĩe, awɔ wo katã dzi tso eƒe dzime ke, eye na be wòate ŋu atu xɔ sia si ŋu medzra ɖo la.”

english_verse: David then said to the people, “Now it's your turn to praise the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped!” So everyone praised the Lord, and they bowed down to honor him and David their king. Solomon Is Crowned King
translation_verse: Tete David gblɔ na ameha blibo la be: “Mikafu Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la!” Ale ameha blibo la kafu Aƒetɔ, wo tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu la. Wobɔbɔ ta tsyɔ mo anyi ɖe Aƒetɔ kple fia la ŋkume.

english_verse: The people were very happy, and they ate and drank there at the Lord's altar. That same day, Solomon was again crowned king. The people celebrated and poured olive oil on Solomon's head to show that he would be their next king. They also poured oil on Zadok's head to show that he was their priest.
translation_verse: Woɖu nu, no nu, eye wokpɔ dzidzɔ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume gbe ma gbe. Wogaɖo Salomo, David vi la fiae zi evelia; wosi ami nɛ heɖoe dziɖulae na Aƒetɔ. Wosi ami na Zadok hã wòzu nunɔla.

english_verse: So Solomon became king after David his father. Solomon was successful, and everyone in Israel obeyed him.
translation_verse: Salomo bɔbɔ nɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe fiazikpui la dzi hezu fia ɖe tɔ́a David yome. Nu dze edzi nɛ, eye Israel-dukɔ blibo la ɖo toe.

english_verse: Every official and every soldier, as well as all of David's other sons, were loyal to him.
translation_verse: Dumegãwo katã, asrafomegãwo kple David vi bubuawo katã bɔbɔ wo ɖokui na Salomo.

english_verse: The Lord made Solomon a great king, and the whole nation was amazed at how famous he was. In fact, no other king of Israel was as great as Solomon. David Dies
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ de bubu Salomo ŋu ŋutɔ le dukɔ blibo la ŋkume. Ena wòɖu fia kple atsyɔ̃ gã si tɔgbe menɔ Israel-fia siwo do ŋgɔ nɛ la ŋu o. David ƒe agbenɔŋutinya kpuie

english_verse: David the son of Jesse was king of Israel
translation_verse: Ale David, Yese vi la ɖu fia ɖe Israel blibo la dzi.

english_verse: David was rich and respected and lived to be an old man. Then he died, and his son Solomon became king.
translation_verse: Etsi, ku amegã belibeli, hafi ku. Enɔ agbe didi, kpɔ kesinɔnu, eye bubu hã nɔ eŋu. Via Salomo ye ɖu fia ɖe eyome.

english_verse: Everything David did while he was king is included in the history written by the prophets Samuel, Nathan, and Gad.
translation_verse: Woŋlɔ nu siwo katã David wɔ tso gɔmedzedzea va se ɖe nuwuwu la ɖe nukpɔla Samuel, gbeƒãɖela Natan kple nukpɔla Gad ƒe ŋutinyagbalẽwo me.

english_verse: They wrote about his powerful rule and about the things that happened not only to him, but also to Israel and the other nations.
translation_verse: Eƒe fiaɖuɖu, eƒe ŋusẽ triakɔ la, nya siwo katã dzɔ ɖe eya ŋutɔ kple Israel-dukɔ kpakple anyigba dzi fiaɖuƒewo dzi la, le agbalẽ siawo me.

english_verse: While Solomon was king of Israel, there was silver and gold everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as ordinary sycamore trees in the foothills.
translation_verse: Fia la wɔe be klosalo kple sika bɔ ɖe Yerusalem abe kpe ene, eye sederti sɔ gbɔ ɖi abe sikamorti le bali me ene.

english_verse: and there at the bronze altar, Solomon offered a thousand animals as sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Salomo te ɖe akɔblivɔsamlekpui si le Aƒetɔ ƒe agbadɔa me la ŋu, eye wòsa numemevɔ akpe ɖeka le edzi.

english_verse: God appeared to Solomon that night in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe ƒe zã me la, Mawu ɖe eɖokui fia Salomo, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Bia nu si mana wò lam.”

english_verse: Solomon answered: Lord God, you were always loyal to my father David, and now you have made me king of Israel.
translation_verse: Salomo gblɔ na Mawu be: “Ève tɔ́nye David nu ŋutɔ, eye nètsɔm ɖo fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: I am supposed to rule these people, but there are as many of them as there are specks of dust on the ground. So keep the promise you made to my father
translation_verse: O Aƒetɔ, Mawu, azɔ la, wɔ ŋugbe si nèdo na tɔ́nye David la dzi. Dukɔ si nu nètsɔm ɖo fiae la me nɔlawo sɔ gbɔ abe anyigbake ene.

english_verse: God replied: Solomon, you could have asked me to make you rich or famous or to let you live a long time. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom and knowledge to rule my people.
translation_verse: Mawu gblɔ na Salomo be: “Esi wònye nu siae le dzime na wò, eye mèbia nunɔamesi, alo kesinɔnu, alo bubu o; mèbia ame siwo lé fu wò la ƒe ku o; mèbia agbe didi o, ke boŋ nèbia nunya kple sidzedze ne nàte ŋu akplɔ nye dukɔ si nu meɖo wò fiae ɖo la,

english_verse: Solomon then left Gibeon and returned to Jerusalem, the capital city of Israel. Solomon's Wealth (
translation_verse: Salomo gbɔ tso vɔsaƒe kple godoƒegbadɔ la gbɔ le Gibeon va Yerusalem, eye wòɖu fia ɖe Israel dzi.

english_verse: Solomon's merchants bought his horses and chariots in the regions of Musri and Kue. They paid
translation_verse: Ne wotsɔ wo va Egipte la, woɖadzraa tasiaɖam ɖeka klosaloga alafa ade, sɔ ɖeka klosaloga alafa ɖeka bla atɔ̃ na Xiti-fiawo katã kple Siria-fiawo.

english_verse: This will be a great temple, because our God is greater than all other gods.
translation_verse: Xɔ lolo ŋutɔ mebe matu elabe mía Mawu la lolo wu mawu bubuwo katã.

english_verse: Praise the Lord God of Israel who made heaven and earth! He has given David a son who isn't only wise and smart, but who has the knowledge to build a temple for the Lord and a palace for himself.
translation_verse: Xuram gagblɔ be: “Woakafu Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu, dziƒo kple anyigba Wɔla, be wòna vi nyanu fia David. Ena nunya kple nugɔmesesee be wòatu gbedoxɔ na Aƒetɔ, eye wòatu fiasã na eɖokui.

english_verse: I am building a temple where the Lord my God will be worshiped. Sweet-smelling incense will be burned there, and sacred bread will be offered to him. Worshipers will offer sacrifices to the Lord every morning and evening, every Sabbath, and on the first day of each month, as well as during all our religious festivals. These things will be done for all time, just as the Lord has commanded.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, mebe matu xɔ na Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu, ne woasubɔe le eme. Makɔ eŋu nɛ, ne woatɔ dzo lifi le eŋkume, ada vɔsabolo ɖe eŋgɔ, eye woasa numemevɔ nɛ le afi ma ŋdi kple fiẽ, le dzudzɔgbewo, le Dzinu Yeye Ŋkeke Nyui ɖuɣiwo kple le Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu ƒe ŋkekenyui bubuwo dzi. Esia nye Israel ƒe dɔdeasi tegbee.

english_verse: Send me a worker who can not only carve, but who can work with gold, silver, bronze, and iron, as well as make brightly colored cloth. The person you send will work here in Judah and Jerusalem with the skilled workers that my father has already hired.
translation_verse: Eya ta ɖo aɖaŋudɔwɔla aɖe ɖem. Amea nenya sika, klosalo, akɔbli kple ga yibɔ ŋu ɖaŋu. Nenya aɖabɛ dzĩtɔ, ka dzẽ kple aɖabɛ blɔtɔ ŋudɔwɔwɔ, eye wòanya atiŋɔŋlɔ hã nyuie. Medi be wòava kpe ɖe aɖaŋudɔwɔla siwo tɔ́nye David tia, eye wole gbɔnye le Yuda kple Yerusalem la ŋu.

english_verse: I know that you have workers who are experts at cutting lumber in Lebanon. So would you please send me some cedar, pine, and juniper logs? My workers will be there to help them,
translation_verse: Menya be wò amewo nya Lebanon-ti ŋudɔwɔwɔ, eya ta ɖo sederti, sesewuti kple papawuti ɖem tso Lebanon. Nye amewo akpe ɖe wò amewo ŋu,

english_verse: because I'll need a lot of lumber to build such a large and glorious temple.
translation_verse: ne woadi atiwo nam geɖe fũu elabe xɔ si tu ge mala la alolo, eye wòanye nukpɔkpɔ tɔxɛ.

english_verse: Hiram sent his answer back to Solomon: I know that the Lord must love his people, because he has chosen you to be their king.
translation_verse: Tete Xuram Tiro-fia ŋlɔ agbalẽ ɖo ɖe Salomo be: “Aƒetɔ lɔ̃ eƒe dukɔ eya ta wòtsɔ wò ɖo fiae ɖe wo nu.”

english_verse: I am sending Huram Abi to you. He is wise and very skillful.
translation_verse: “Azɔ mele Xuram Abi ɖom ɖe wò. Enye aɖaŋudɔwɔla si nunya le tagbɔ na.

english_verse: His mother was from the Israelite tribe of Dan, and his father was from Tyre. Not only is Huram an expert at working with gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, but he can also make colored cloth and fine linen. And he can carve anything if you give him a pattern to follow. He can help your workers and those hired by your father King David.
translation_verse: Nɔa tso Dan-to la me, eye tɔ́a tso Tiro. Enya sika kple klosalo, akɔbli kple ga yibɔ, kpe kple ati ŋudɔwɔwɔ. Enya aɖabɛ dzĩtɔ kple blɔtɔ, avɔ dzĩ xɔasi kple aklala biɖibiɖi ŋudɔwɔwɔ. Enya nɔnɔme vovovowo ŋɔŋlɔ, eye wòtea ŋu ŋlɔa aɖaŋu si woɖɔ nɛ la hã. Na wòakpe ɖe wò aɖaŋudɔwɔlawo kple nye aƒetɔ David ƒe aɖaŋudɔwɔlawo ŋu.

english_verse: Go ahead and send the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine you promised to pay my workers.
translation_verse: Azɔ lu kple ƒo, ami kple wain siwo ƒe nya nègblɔ la, àte ŋu aɖo wo ɖe mí, wò dɔlawo.

english_verse: I will tell them to start cutting down trees in Lebanon. They will cut as many as you need, then tie them together into rafts, and float them down along the coast to Joppa. Your workers can take them to Jerusalem from there. Solomon's Work Force
translation_verse: Ati agbɔsɔsɔ sinu nèhiã la, míatso wo le Lebanon-toa dzi, abla wo tatata atsɔ to ƒu dzi ava Yafo na wò, eye wò la, nàva fɔ wo yi Yerusalem.” Wodze gbedoxɔ la tutu gɔme (Fia I,

english_verse: Solomon counted all the foreigners who were living in Israel, just as his father David had done when he was king, and the total was
translation_verse: Fia Salomo na woxlẽ amedzro siwo katã le Israel-nyigba dzi abe ale si tɔ́a David wɔ kpɔ ene. Ekpɔ ŋutsu akpe alafa ɖeka bla atɔ̃ vɔ etɔ̃ alafa ade.

english_verse: He used precious stones to decorate the temple, and he used gold imported from Parvaim
translation_verse: Eɖo kpe xɔasi ɖe xɔa me tsɔ ɖo atsyɔ̃ nɛ. Sika la tso Parvayim.
