translation_verse: Uziya xɔ ƒe wui ade esime woɖoe fiae, eye wòɖu fia ƒe bla atɔ̃ vɔ eve le Yerusalem. Nɔae nye Yekolya, tso Yerusalem.

english_verse: Uzziah became proud of his power, and this led to his downfall. One day, Uzziah disobeyed the Lord his God by going into the temple and burning incense as an offering to him.
translation_verse: Ke esi ŋusẽ ɖo eŋu la, ede asi dàda me, si na wòva dze anyi. Ewɔ alakpanu ɖe Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu la ŋu. Ege ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me be yeatɔ dzo lifi le lifivɔsamlekpui dzi.

english_verse: He obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
translation_verse: Uziya hã wɔ nu si dze Aƒetɔ ŋu abe tɔ́a Amazya ene pɛpɛpɛ.

english_verse: Zechariah was Uzziah's advisor and taught him to obey God. And so, as long as Zechariah was alive, Uzziah was faithful to God, and God made him successful.
translation_verse: Le Zaxarya ame si fia Mawu vɔvɔ̃e ƒe agbenɔɣi la, Uziya subɔ Mawu, eye zi ale si wòsubɔ Aƒetɔ la, Mawu na nu dze edzi nɛ.

english_verse: While Uzziah was king, he started a war against the Philistines. He smashed the walls of the cities of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, then rebuilt towns around Ashdod and in other parts of Philistia.
translation_verse: Uziya wɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo. Egbã Gat, Yabne kple Asdod-duwo ƒe gliwo, eye wòtso duwo ɖe Asdod-nutome kple teƒe bubuwo le Filistitɔwo dome.

english_verse: Even the Ammonites paid taxes to Uzziah. He became very powerful, and people who lived as far away as Egypt heard about him.
translation_verse: Amontɔwo xe adzɔ na Uziya. Eva kpɔ ŋusẽ ale gbegbe be eŋkɔ de keke Egipte-liƒo dzi ke.

english_verse: In Jerusalem, Uzziah built fortified towers at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the place where the city wall turned inward.
translation_verse: Uziya tu gbetakpɔxɔ sesẽwo ɖe Yerusalem ɖe Dzogoedzigbo, Balimegbo kple Dzogoe la dzi, eye wòwɔ wo wosesẽ.

english_verse: He also built defense towers out in the desert. He owned such a large herd of livestock in the western foothills and in the flatlands, that he had cisterns dug there to catch the rainwater. He loved farming, so he had crops and vineyards planted in the hill country wherever there was fertile soil, and he hired farmers to take care of them.
translation_verse: Etu gbetakpɔxɔwo ɖe gbedadaƒo, eye wòɖe vudo geɖewo elabe lãha geɖe nɔ esi le balia me kple gbedadaƒo. Agbledede dzɔa dzi nɛ ale ena amewo de waingble ɖe towo ŋu kple anyigba nyonuwo dzi.

english_verse: Uzziah's army was always ready for battle. Jeiel and Maaseiah were the officers who kept track of the number of soldiers, and these two men were under the command of Hananiah, one of Uzziah's officials.
translation_verse: Asrafo hatsotso vovovo siwo nɔ klalo na aʋa la nɔ esi. Uziya ƒe agbalẽŋlɔla Yeiel kple dɔdzikpɔla Maaseya tia asrafoawo xlẽ, heŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽ me le Xananya, ame si tso fia ƒe aʋakplɔlawo dome la ƒe dzikpɔkpɔ te.

english_verse: and said, “Your Majesty, this isn't right! You are not allowed to burn incense to the Lord. That must be done only by priests who are descendants of Aaron. You will have to leave! You have sinned against the Lord, and so he will no longer bless you.”
translation_verse: Wotsi tre ɖe eŋu gblɔ nɛ be: “Wò, Uziya, menye wòe atɔ dzo lifi na Aƒetɔ o. Ke boŋ nunɔlawo, Aron ƒe dzidzimeviwo ame siwo ŋu wokɔ la koe kpɔ mɔ awɔe. Do go le kɔkɔeƒe la, elabe èwɔ nu tovo. Aƒetɔ, Mawu made bubu aɖeke ŋuwò o.”

english_verse: Uzziah, who was standing next to the incense altar at the time, was holding the incense burner, ready to offer incense to the Lord. He became very angry when he heard Azariah's warning, and leprosy suddenly appeared on his forehead!
translation_verse: Ke Uziya do dziku. Ɣe ma ɣi la, elé dzidzɔdonu la ɖe asi be yeado dzudzɔ. Esi wòdo dziku ɖe nunɔlawo ŋu alea la, ŋutigbalẽdɔ dziŋɔ aɖe ƒo ɖe eƒe ŋgonu, le nunɔlawo ŋkume, le lifidzudzɔmlekpui la xa, le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me.

english_verse: Azariah and the other priests saw it and immediately told him to leave the temple. Uzziah realized that the Lord had punished him, so he hurried to get outside.
translation_verse: Nunɔlagã Azarya kple nunɔla bubuawo nye kɔ be yewoakpɔe ɖa, kasia woakpɔ la, ŋutigbalẽdɔ dziŋɔ ƒo ɖe eƒe ŋgonu! Wonyàe afɔ tsɔtsɔe, eye eya ŋutɔ hã wɔ kabakaba do le afi ma elabe Aƒetɔ ƒoe.

english_verse: Since Uzziah had leprosy, he could not be buried in the royal tombs. Instead, he was buried in a nearby cemetery that the kings owned. His son Jotham then became king.
translation_verse: Uziya ku, eye woɖii ɖe ameɖiƒe si nye tɔgbuiawo tɔ la ƒe agble me, ke womeɖii ɖe fiawo ɖiƒe o, elabe wogblɔ be: “Ŋutigbalẽdɔ le eŋu.” Via Yotam zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Jotham obeyed the Lord and did right. He followed the example of his father Uzziah, except he never burned incense in the temple as his father had done. But the people of Judah kept sinning against the Lord.
translation_verse: Yotam wɔ nu si dze Aƒetɔ ŋu abe tɔ́a Uziya ene, negbe ɖeko eya mege ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me o. Ke dukɔ la ganɔ nu gbegblẽ wɔwɔ dzi ko.

english_verse: During his rule he attacked and defeated the Ammonites. Then every year for the next three years, he forced them to pay
translation_verse: Ewɔ aʋa kple Amonviwo ƒe fia, eye wòɖu wo dzi. Ƒe ma me la, Amonviwo xe adzɔ nɛ. Woxe klosalo kilo akpe etɔ̃ alafa ene, lu ton akpe ɖeka kple ƒo ton akpe ɖeka.

english_verse: Jotham remained faithful to the Lord his God and became a very powerful king.
translation_verse: Ale Yotam kpɔ ŋusẽ elabe eɖɔ ŋu ɖo le Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu la ŋkume.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king, including the wars he fought, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Yotam ƒe nuwɔnawo, eƒe aʋa siwo katã wòwɔ kple eƒe agbenɔnɔ la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel kple Yuda-fiawo ƒe Ŋutinyagbalẽ la me.

english_verse: He was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Yotam ku eye woɖii ɖe David ƒe du la me. Via Axaz zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees. Syria and Israel Attack Judah (
translation_verse: Esa vɔ, eye wòdo lifidzudzɔ le nuxeƒewo, le togbɛwo dzi kple ati dama ɖe sia ɖe te. Israel-dukɔ kple Siria-dukɔ wɔ aʋa kple Yuda (Fia II,

english_verse: So Tiglath Pileser came to Judah, but instead of helping, he made things worse.
translation_verse: Ke Tiglat-Pileser, Asiria-fia meva kpe ɖe eŋu o, ke boŋ eho ɖe eŋu eye wòxaxae ɖo.

english_verse: and he offered sacrifices in Hinnom Valley. Worst of all, Ahaz sacrificed his own sons, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
translation_verse: Axaz do lifidzudzɔ le Hinom vi ƒe bali la me, eye wòme via ŋutsuwo tsɔ sa vɔe, ŋunyɔnu si dukɔ siwo Aƒetɔ nyà ɖa le Israelviwo ŋgɔ la wɔna la.

english_verse: Ahaz and the people of Judah sinned and turned away from the Lord, the God their ancestors had worshiped. So the Lord punished them by letting their enemies defeat them. The king of Syria attacked Judah and took many of its people to Damascus as prisoners. King Pekah of Israel later defeated Judah and killed
translation_verse: Pekax, Remalya vi la, wu ame akpe alafa ɖeka bla eve le Yuda le ŋkeke ɖeka dzi, elabe wogblẽ Aƒetɔ, wo tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu la ɖi. Ame siawo katã nye kalẽtɔwo.

english_verse: If you make slaves of the people of Judah and Jerusalem, you will be as guilty as they are of sinning against the Lord.
translation_verse: Fifia miele eɖom be yewoate Yuda kple Yerusalem vidzidziawo ɖe anyi, woazu kluviwo kple kosiwo na mi. Ðe esia menye fɔɖiɖi sɔŋ le Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu ŋkume oa?

english_verse: Send these prisoners back home—they are your own relatives. If you don't, the Lord will punish you in his anger.
translation_verse: Azɔ miɖo tom! Migbugbɔ aboyome siwo mielé le mia nɔviwo dome la yii, elabe Aƒetɔ do dɔmedzoe ɖe mia ŋu vevie.”

english_verse: About the same time, four of Israel's leaders arrived. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai. They agreed with Oded that the Israelite troops were wrong,
translation_verse: Efrayim-tatɔwo dome ame aɖewo tsi tre ɖe Israel-ʋakɔa ƒe nuwɔna ŋu. Woawoe nye: Azarya, Taxanan vi, Berexya, Mesilemot vi, Yexizkiya, Salum vi kple Amasa, Xadlai vi.

english_verse: and they said: If you bring these prisoners into Samaria, that will be one more thing we've done to sin against the Lord. And he is already angry enough with us.
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na wo be: “Migakplɔ aboyomeawo va afii o, elabe Aƒetɔ bu fɔ mi xoxo hafi miegaɖo be yewoadzi míaƒe nuvɔ̃wo kple fɔɖiɖi ɖe edzi. Míeɖi fɔ geɖe eye Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔmedzoe le bibim ɖe Israel ŋu.”

english_verse: So in front of the leaders and the crowd, the troops handed over their prisoners and the property they had taken from Judah.
translation_verse: Ale aʋakalẽawo ɖe asi le aboyomeawo kple aboyonuawo ŋu le ameha la kple dumegãwo ŋkume.

english_verse: The four leaders took some of the stolen clothes and gave them to the prisoners who needed something to wear. They later gave them all a new change of clothes and shoes, then fixed them something to eat and drink, and cleaned their wounds with olive oil. They gave donkeys to those who were too weak to walk, and led all of them back to Jericho, the city known for its palm trees. The leaders then returned to Samaria. Ahaz Asks the King of Assyria for Help (
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu siwo ŋkɔ woyɔ la tso ɖaxɔ aboyomeawo. Woɖe awu kple afɔkpa tso aboyonuawo me na ame siwo le amama la wodo. Wona woɖu nu, no nu eye wosi ami na wo. Wotsɔ ame siwo katã gbɔdzɔ la ɖo tedziwo dzi, eye wokplɔ aboyomeawo katã gbugbɔ va wo nɔviwo gbɔ le Yerixo, devedu la me. Emegbe woawo ŋutɔ gbugbɔ yi Samaria. Axaz bia kpekpeɖeŋu tso Asiria gbɔ (Fia II,

english_verse: But God was punishing Judah with these disasters, because Ahaz had disobeyed him and refused to stop Judah from sinning.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ bɔbɔ Yuda ɖe anyi le Israel-fia Axaz ta, elabe mena wolé fɔ ɖe mawusubɔsubɔ ŋu o, eye wòwɔ alakpanu ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu.

english_verse: Ahaz gave him gifts from the Lord's temple and the king's palace, as well as from the homes of Israel's other leaders. The Assyrian king still refused to help Ahaz. The Final Sin of Ahaz and His Death
translation_verse: Togbɔ be Axaz lɔ́ nuwo le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me, fiasã la me kple dumegãwo ƒe aƒewo me ɖatsɔ xe adzɔ na Asiria-fia hã la, esia mekpe ɖe eŋu o. Axaz ƒe nuvɔ̃wo

english_verse: Even after all these terrible things happened to Ahaz, he sinned against the Lord even worse than before.
translation_verse: Le fia Axaz sia ƒe xaxaɣi la, egawɔ alakpanu geɖe ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu ɖe edzi.

english_verse: He said to himself, “The Syrian gods must have helped their kings defeat me. Maybe if I offer sacrifices to those gods, they will help me.” That was the sin that finally led to the downfall of Ahaz, as well as to the destruction of Judah.
translation_verse: Esa vɔ na Damaskotɔ siwo sii la ƒe mawuwo. Egblɔ be: “Siria-mawuwo kpe ɖe Siria-fiawo ŋu, eya ta nye hã masa vɔ na wo, ne woakpe ɖe nye hã ŋunye.” Ke mawu siawo boŋ he dzɔgbevɔ̃e va eya kple Israel-dukɔ blibo la dzi.

english_verse: Ahaz collected all the furnishings of the temple and smashed them to pieces. Then he locked the doors to the temple and set up altars to foreign gods on every street corner in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Eƒo Mawu ƒe aƒe la me dɔwɔnuwo katã nu ƒu, eye wògbã wo gudugudu. Etu Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ƒe ʋɔtruwo, eye wòɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe dzogoewo katã me le Yerusalem.

english_verse: In every city and town in Judah he built local shrines to worship foreign gods. All of this made the Lord God of his ancestors very angry.
translation_verse: Gawu la, ewɔ nuxeƒewo ɖe Yuda-duwo katã me, ne woasa lifivɔ na mawu bubuwo. To esiawo wɔwɔ me la, Axaz gado dziku na Aƒetɔ, tɔgbuiawo ƒe Mawu la ɖe edzi.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Axaz ƒe nuwɔna mamlɛawo kple eƒe agbenɔnɔ katã, tso gɔmedzedzea va se ɖe nuwuwua la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Yuda kple Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ la me.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. His son Hezekiah then became king.
translation_verse: Axaz ku, eye woɖii ɖe dua me le Yerusalem, ke womeɖii ɖe Israel-fiawo ɖiƒe o. Via Xizkiya zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord by doing right, just as his ancestor David had done. The Temple Is Purified
translation_verse: Xizkiya wɔ nu si dze Aƒetɔ ŋu abe tɔgbuia David ene pɛpɛpɛ. Gbedoxɔa me kɔkɔ

english_verse: they went back to Hezekiah and said: Your Majesty, we have finished our work. The entire temple is now pure again, and so is the altar and its utensils, as well as the table for the sacred loaves of bread and its utensils.
translation_verse: Azɔ Levi viawo yi fia Xizkiya gbɔ ɖagblɔ nɛ be: “Míekɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe blibo la katã ŋu vɔ. Míekɔ numemevɔsamlekpui la, vɔsabolokplɔ̃ kple wo ŋu nuwo katã ŋuti hã vɔ.

english_verse: Next, Hezekiah assigned the Levites to their places in the temple. He gave them cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments, according to the instructions that the Lord had given King David and the two prophets, Gad and Nathan.
translation_verse: Fia la ɖo Levi viwo Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me, eye wolé gakogoewo, saŋkuwo kple kasaŋkuwo ɖe asi ɖe David kple fia ƒe nukpɔla Gad kpakple Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela Natan ƒe ɖoɖo nu, elabe Aƒetɔ ye wɔ ɖoɖo sia to eƒe gbeƒãɖelawo dzi.

english_verse: After that, Hezekiah and the crowd of worshipers bowed down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Esi wowu enu la, fia kple ame siwo katã le eŋu la dze klo do gbe ɖa.

english_verse: Then he called the priests and Levites to the east courtyard of the temple
translation_verse: Ena nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo va, eye wokpe ta ɖe gbadzaƒe si le ɣedzeƒe gome.

english_verse: and said: It's time to purify the temple of the Lord God of our ancestors. You Levites must first go through the ceremony to make yourselves clean, then go into the temple and bring out everything that is unclean and unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Egblɔ na wo be: “Mi Levi viwo, miɖo tom! Mikɔ mia ɖokui ŋu, eye mikɔ Aƒetɔ, mia tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu ƒe aƒe la hã ŋu. Miɖe nu makɔmakɔawo ɖa le kɔkɔeƒe la.

english_verse: Some of our ancestors were unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord our God. Not only did they turn their backs on the Lord, but they also completely ignored his temple.
translation_verse: Elabe mía tɔgbuiwo mewɔ nuteƒe na Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la o, eye wowɔ nu si medze eŋu o. Wogblẽe ɖi, eye woɖe kɔ ɖa le Aƒetɔ, ame si wotrɔ megbe dee la ƒe nɔƒe la ŋu.

english_verse: They locked the doors, then let the lamps go out and stopped burning incense and offering sacrifices to him.
translation_verse: Wodo akpata la ƒe ʋɔtruwo, wotsi akaɖiawo, eye womegatɔa dzo lifi alo gasaa numemevɔ le kɔkɔeƒe la na Israel ƒe Mawu la o.

english_verse: The Lord became terribly angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and everyone was shocked and horrified at what he did to punish them. Not only were
translation_verse: Le esia ta Aƒetɔ do dɔmedzoe ɖe Yuda kple Yerusalem ŋu, eye wòhe to na wo wozu, ŋɔdzinu, nukunu kple nu si ŋu woaʋuʋu ta ɖo abe ale si miawo ŋutɔ miele ekpɔm kple ŋku lae ene.

english_verse: our ancestors killed in battle, but our own children and wives were taken captive.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, mía tɔ́wo tsi yi nu, eye mía viŋutsuwo, mía vinyɔnuwo kple mía srɔ̃wo le aboyo me le esia ta.

english_verse: So I have decided to renew our agreement with the Lord God of Israel. Maybe then he will stop being so angry with us.
translation_verse: Azɔ meɖoe tso nye dzime ke be mabla nu kple Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la, ne dziku helihelĩ si wòdo ɖe mía ŋu la nu nafa.

english_verse: Let's not waste any time, my friends. You are the ones who were chosen to be the Lord's priests and to offer him sacrifices.
translation_verse: Vinyewo, azɔ migahe ɖe megbe o. Miawoe Aƒetɔ tia be mianɔ tsitre ɖe eŋkume, awɔ eƒe dɔwo, eye mianye eƒe subɔlawo asa lifivɔ nɛ.

english_verse: These leaders gathered together the rest of the Levites, and they all went through the ceremony to make themselves clean. Then they began to purify the temple according to the Law of the Lord, just as Hezekiah had commanded.
translation_verse: Ame siawo ƒo wo nɔviŋutsuwo nu ƒu, eye wokɔ wo ɖokui ŋu. Wova le fia ƒe gbeɖeɖe kple Aƒetɔ ƒe nya nu be yewoakɔ̀ Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ŋu.

english_verse: The priests went into the temple and carried out everything that was unclean. They put these things in the courtyard, and from there, the Levites carried them outside the city to Kidron Valley.
translation_verse: Nunɔlaawo ge ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe xɔ la me be yewoakɔ eŋu. Woɖe nu makɔmakɔ siwo katã wokpɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔ me la do goe ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ƒe xɔxɔnua, eye Levi viawo xɔ nuawo tsɔ yi ɖe Kidron-tɔʋu la nu.

english_verse: The priests and Levites began their work on the first day of the first month. It took them one week to purify the courtyards of the temple and another week to purify the temple. So on the sixteenth day of that same month
translation_verse: Wodze xɔa ŋu kɔkɔ gɔme le ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi, eye woɖo akpata la me le ŋkeke enyia gbe. Tso evea gbe la, wowɔ dɔ ŋkeke enyi, eye le ɣletia ƒe ŋkeke wui adelia dzi la, wowu dɔ blibo la nu. Wogbugbɔ gbedoxɔ me subɔsubɔ ɖo te

english_verse: And we have brought back all the things that King Ahaz took from the temple during the time he was unfaithful to God. We purified them and put them back in front of the altar. Worship in the Temple
translation_verse: Gawu la, míefɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me dɔwɔnu siwo ŋudɔwɔwɔ fia Axaz gbe le eƒe fiaɖuɣi, esime wògbe nuteƒewɔwɔ na Mawu la hã vɛ, eye míekɔ woawo hã ŋu. Kpɔ ɖa, wole Aƒetɔ ƒe vɔsamlekpui la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: At once, Hezekiah called together the officials of Jerusalem, and they went to the temple.
translation_verse: Tete fia Xizkiya fɔ ŋdi kanya ƒo dumegãwo nu ƒu, eye woyi Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me.

english_verse: They brought with them seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as sacrifices to take away the sins of Hezekiah's family and of the people of Judah, as well as to purify the temple. Hezekiah told the priests, who were descendants of Aaron, to sacrifice these animals on the altar.
translation_verse: Wokplɔ nyitsu adrẽ, agbo adrẽ, alẽvi adrẽ kple gbɔ̃tsu adrẽ ɖe asi yii be woatsɔ sa nuvɔ̃vɔe ɖe fiaɖuƒe la, kɔkɔeƒe la kple Yuda ta. Fia ɖe gbe na nunɔlawo, Aron ƒe dzidzimeviawo be woatsɔ lãawo asa vɔe le Aƒetɔ ƒe vɔsamlekpui la dzi.

english_verse: The priests killed the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, then splattered the blood on the altar.
translation_verse: Wowu nyitsuawo, eye nunɔlawo xɔ ʋua hlẽ ɖe vɔsamlekpuia ŋu; wowu agboawo, eye wohlẽ ʋua ɖe vɔsamlekpuia ŋu; wowu alẽviawo, eye wohlẽ ʋu la ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ŋu.

english_verse: They took the goats to Hezekiah and the worshipers, and they laid their hands on the animals.
translation_verse: Azɔ wokplɔ nuvɔ̃vɔsa gbɔ̃tsuawo va fia la kple ameha la ŋkume, eye woawo tsɔ asi da ɖe wo dzi.

english_verse: The priests then killed the goats and splattered the blood on the altar as a sacrifice to take away the sins of everyone in Israel, because Hezekiah had commanded that these sacrifices be made for all the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Tete nunɔlaawo wu wo, eye wotsɔ woƒe ʋu wɔ nuvɔ̃vɔsa le vɔsamlekpuia dzi, bene woatsɔ alé avu ɖe Israel blibo la nu, elabe fia la ɖe gbe be woasa nuvɔ̃vɔ kple numemevɔ ɖe Israel blibo la ta.

english_verse: The Levites were ready to play the instruments that had belonged to David; the priests were ready to blow the trumpets.
translation_verse: Levi viawo le tsitre, David ƒe hadzinuawo le wo si, eye nunɔlawo lé kpẽawo ɖe asi.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah gave the signal for the sacrifices to be burned on the altar, the musicians began singing praises to the Lord and playing their instruments,
translation_verse: Tete Xizkiya ɖe gbe be woasa numemevɔ le vɔsamlekpui la dzi. Esi wodze numemevɔ la sasa gɔme la, Aƒetɔ ƒe ha la kple kpẽawo kpakple Israel-fia David ƒe hadzinuawo de asi ɖiɖi me.

english_verse: and everyone worshiped the Lord. This continued until the last animal was sacrificed.
translation_verse: Ameha blibo la le gbe dom ɖa. Hadzilawo le ha dzim, kpẽkulawo le kpẽ kum va se ɖe esime wowu numemevɔsa la nu.

english_verse: Then Hezekiah and his officials ordered the Levites to sing the songs of praise that David and Asaph the prophet had written. And so they bowed down and joyfully sang praises to the Lord.
translation_verse: Azɔ fia Xizkiya kple dumegãwo gblɔ na Levi viwo be woatsɔ David kple nukpɔla Asaf ƒe nyawo adzi kafukafuhawo na Aƒetɔ. Ale wodzi kafukafuhaawo kple dzidzɔ, eye wodze klo do gbe ɖa.

english_verse: Hezekiah said to the crowd, “Now that you are once again acceptable to the Lord, bring sacrifices and offerings to give him thanks.” The people did this, and some of them voluntarily brought animals to be offered as sacrifices.
translation_verse: Emegbe fia Xizkiya gblɔ na wo be: “Azɔ miekɔ mia ɖokui ŋu na Aƒetɔ vɔ. Mite va Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me kple vɔsanuwo kple akpedanunanawo.” Ameha blibo la tsɔ vɔsanuwo kple akpedanunanawo vɛ, eye ame siwo katã ŋu wòdze la tsɔ numemevɔsawo hã vɛ.

english_verse: There were not enough priests to skin all these animals, because many of the priests had not taken the time to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. However, since all the Levites had made themselves clean, they helped the priests until the last animal was skinned.
translation_verse: Ke esi nunɔlawo megade ha ako numemevɔsalãwo katã o ta la, wo nɔvi Levi viwo kpe ɖe wo ŋu va se ɖe esime dɔ blibo la wu nu. Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, nunɔla bubuwo hã kɔ wo ɖokui ŋu. Elabe Levi viwo léa fɔ ɖe wo ɖokui ŋu kɔkɔ ŋu wu nunɔlaawo.

english_verse: Besides all the sacrifices that were burned on the altar, the fat from the other animal sacrifices was burned, and the offerings of wine were poured over the altar. So the temple was once again used for worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Hekpe ɖe numemevɔsalã gbogboa ŋu la, lãawo ƒe ami si tsɔ ge wole asa ŋutifafavɔ kple wain si wotsɔ kpe ɖe numemevɔsa ŋu vɛ la hã li. Ale wɔ wogbugbɔ Mawu subɔsubɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me gaɖo te.

english_verse: Hezekiah and the people of Judah celebrated, because God had helped them make this happen so quickly.
translation_verse: Xizkiya kple dukɔ blibo la kpɔ dzidzɔ le nu si Mawu wɔ na dukɔ la ŋuti, elabe ɖeko nua va dzɔ kpata.

english_verse: Everyone from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north was invited. This was the largest crowd of people that had ever celebrated Passover, according to the official records.
translation_verse: Ale woɖo kpe edzi be woaɖe gbeƒã na Israelviwo katã tso Beer-Seba va se ɖe Dan bene woava ɖu Paska na Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la le Yerusalem, elabe eteƒe didi womegaɖui kpɔ abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖi ene o.

english_verse: Hezekiah's messengers went everywhere in Israel and Judah with the following letter: People of Israel, now that you have survived the invasion of the Assyrian kings, it's time for you to turn back to the Lord God our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob worshiped. If you do this, he will stop being angry.
translation_verse: Dɔtsɔlawo xɔ agbalẽawo tso fia la kple eƒe dumegãwo gbɔ, eye woɖatsa le Israel bliboa kple Yuda abe ale si fia ɖe gbe na woe ene be: “Israel ƒe dzidzimeviwo, mitrɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ, Abraham, Isak kple Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋu, ne wòatrɔ ɖe miaƒe ame mamlɛa, siwo sí tso Asiria-fia si me va la ŋu.

english_verse: Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Decide now to obey the Lord our God! Come to Jerusalem and worship him in the temple that will belong to him forever. Then he will stop being angry,
translation_verse: Miawo ya migalia kɔ abe mia tɔgbuiwo ene o; ke boŋ miɖe asi le mia ɖokui ŋu na Aƒetɔ ne miava eƒe kɔkɔeƒe si ŋu wòkɔ tegbee la. Miva subɔ Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la, eye eƒe dziku helihelĩ ɖe mia ŋu nu afa.

english_verse: and the enemies that have captured your families will show pity and send them back home. The Lord God is kind and merciful, and if you turn back to him, he will no longer turn his back on you.
translation_verse: Elabe ne mietrɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu la, mia nɔviwo kple mia viwo ƒe nu awɔ nublanui na ame siwo ɖe aboyo wo la, ale be woatrɔ gbɔ va anyigba sia dzi gɔ̃. Elabe amenuvela kple nublanuikpɔla nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la. Ne mietrɔ ɖe eŋu la, maɖe kɔ ɖa le mia ŋu o.

english_verse: Only a few people from the tribes of Asher, West Manasseh, and Zebulun were humble and went to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ke ame aɖewo bɔbɔ wo ɖokui le Aser, Manase kple Zebulon toawo me, eye wova Yerusalem.

english_verse: God also made everyone in Judah eager to do what Hezekiah and his officials had commanded. Passover Is Celebrated
translation_verse: Le Yuda hã la, Mawu trɔ amewo ƒe dzi be wowɔ ɖeka hewɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nya si fia la kple amegãwo gblɔ na wo la dzi. Paska la ɖuɖu

english_verse: In the second month, a large crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti evelia le ƒè la me la, ameha gã aɖe va kpe ta ɖe Yerusalem be woaɖu Abolo Maʋamaʋã Ŋkeke Nyui la. Vavalawo sɔ gbɔ ŋutɔ.

english_verse: They took all the foreign altars and incense altars in Jerusalem and threw them into Kidron Valley.
translation_verse: Wolɔ vɔsamlekpui siwo katã le Yerusalem, esiwo dzi womea nu le kple esiwo dzi wotɔa dzo lifi le la siaa, ɖaƒu gbe ɖe Kidron-tɔʋu la me.

english_verse: Most of the people that came from Ephraim, West Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun had not made themselves clean, but they ignored God's Law and ate the Passover lambs anyway. Hezekiah found out what they had done and prayed, “Lord God, these people are unclean according to the laws of holiness. But they are worshiping you, just as their ancestors did. So, please be kind and forgive them.”
translation_verse: ƒe Mawu, tsɔ ke ame siwo katã le subɔwòm le afii tso dzi blibo me, evɔ womekɔ wo ɖokui ŋuti, abe ale si wòle be woawɔ ne kɔkɔeƒe sia nanɔ dzadzɛ ene o hã.”

english_verse: The Lord answered Hezekiah's prayer and did not punish them.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ se Xizkiya ƒe gbedodoɖa, eye mewɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke wo o.

english_verse: The worshipers in Jerusalem were very happy and celebrated the Festival for seven days. The Levites and priests sang praises to the Lord every day and played their instruments.
translation_verse: Ale Israelvi siwo va Yerusalem la ɖu Abolo Maʋamaʋã Ŋkeke Nyui la ŋkeke adrẽ kple dzidzɔ gã ŋutɔ, eye Levi viwo kple nunɔlawo tsɔ hadzinuwo kafu Aƒetɔ sesĩe ŋkekeawo katã.

english_verse: Hezekiah thanked the Levites for doing such a good job, leading the celebration. The worshipers celebrated for seven days by offering sacrifices, by eating the sacred meals, and by praising the Lord God of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Xizkiya ƒo nu de dzi ƒo na Levi vi siwo katã nya ale si woasubɔ Aƒetɔ lae la. Ale dukɔ la ɖu ŋkekenyui nuɖuɖu la ŋkeke adrẽ eye wosa ŋutifafavɔ, bia dedienɔnɔ, eye woda akpe na Aƒetɔ, wo tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu la. Wogaɖu ŋkekenyui la ake

english_verse: Everyone was so excited that they agreed to celebrate seven more days.
translation_verse: Tete ameha blibo la ɖoe be yewoagaɖui ŋkeke adrẽ bubu. Ale wogaɖui kple dzidzɔ ŋkeke adrẽ sɔŋ.

english_verse: Everyone was very happy, including those from Judah and Israel, the priests and Levites, and the foreigners living in Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Tete Yuda ƒe ameha blibo la: nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo, ameha si tso Israel va la katã, amedzro siwo tso Israel kple esiwo nɔ Yuda-nyigba dzi la katã kpɔ dzidzɔ geɖe.

english_verse: It was the biggest celebration in Jerusalem since the days of King Solomon, the son of David.
translation_verse: Dzidzɔ gã ŋutɔ xɔ Yerusalem-dua me kpe ɖo, elabe tso Israel-fia Salomo, David vi la ŋɔli va se ɖe ɣe ma ɣi me kpaa, nu sia tɔgbe megadzɔ le Yerusalem kpɔ o.

english_verse: The priests and Levites asked God to bless the people, and from his home in heaven, he did.
translation_verse: Nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo tsi tsitre, eye wobia Aƒetɔ ƒe yayra na dukɔ la. Woƒe gbedodoɖa de Mawu ƒe nɔƒe kɔkɔe la le dziƒo, eye wòse woƒe gbe.

english_verse: Hezekiah divided the priests and Levites into groups, according to their duties. Then he assigned them the responsibilities of offering sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He also appointed people to serve at the temple and to sing praises at the temple gates.
translation_verse: Xizkiya ɖo nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo ƒe hawo, hatsotsohatsotso, eye hatsotso ɖe sia ɖe le eƒe dɔ nu ɖe numemevɔsa kple ŋutifafavɔsa ŋu. Woawoe asubɔ, ada akpe, eye woakafu le Aƒetɔ ƒe agbadɔwo ƒe agbowo nu.

english_verse: The official records also included their wives and children, because they had also been faithful in keeping themselves clean and acceptable to serve the Lord.
translation_verse: Wode nunɔlawo kple woƒe vidzĩwo, wo srɔ̃wo, wo viŋutsuviwo kple wo vinyɔnuviwo katã ƒe ŋkɔ agbalẽ me elabe ele na wo be woanɔ wo ɖokui ŋu kɔm na woƒe dɔ.

english_verse: He told the people of Jerusalem to bring the offerings that were to be given to the priests and Levites, so that they would have time to serve the Lord with their work.
translation_verse: Ebia tso Yerusalemnɔlawo si be woana nu siwo nye nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo tɔ gome la wo, bene woavo alé fɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe se la ŋu.

english_verse: After the Festival, the people went to every town in Judah and smashed the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. They destroyed all the local shrines and foreign altars in Judah, as well as those in the territories of Benjamin, Ephraim, and West Manasseh. Then everyone went home. Offerings for the Priests and Levites
translation_verse: Esi wowu nu siawo katã nu la, Israelvi siwo katã va la ho yi Yuda-duwo me. Wogbã aƒeliwo, mu nyɔnumawu Aserawo, eye wogbã nuxeƒewo kple vɔsamlekpuiwo le Yuda, Benyamin, Efrayim kple Manase nutowo me va se ɖe esime wogblẽ wo katã. Emegbe Israel blibo la gbugbɔ yi woƒe duwo me, le woƒe nunɔamesiwo gbɔ.

english_verse: Hezekiah provided animals from his own herds and flocks to use for the morning and evening sacrifices, as well as for the sacrifices during the Sabbath celebrations, the New Moon Festivals, and the other religious feasts required by the Law of the Lord.
translation_verse: Fia la na nu tso eya ŋutɔ ƒe kesinɔnuwo me be woatsɔ sa numemevɔ ŋdi kple fiẽ, le dzudzɔgbewo, Dzinu Yeye Ŋkeke Nyui ɖuɣiwo kple ŋkekenyui ɖoɖi bubuwo dzi, abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe se la me ene.

english_verse: As soon as the people heard what the king wanted, they brought a tenth of everything they owned, including their best grain, wine, olive oil, honey, and other crops.
translation_verse: Esi wòse esia la, Israelviwo tsɔ bli, wain, ami kple anyitsi kpakple agblemenukuwo ƒe ŋgɔgbetɔwo va na. Woɖe woƒe nu sia nu ƒe akpa ewolia va na fũu.

english_verse: The people from the other towns of Judah brought a tenth of their herds and flocks, as well as a tenth of anything they had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Israelvi kple Yudavi siwo le Yuda-duwo me la hã tsɔ woƒe nyiwo kple alẽwo ƒe ewoliawo va na. Wogatsɔ nunana siwo ŋu wokɔ na Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la hã vɛ gleglegle.

english_verse: The people started bringing their offerings to Jerusalem in the third month, and the last ones arrived four months later.
translation_verse: Wodze ƒuƒoƒo nuawo gɔme le ɣleti etɔ̃lia me, eye wowu enu le ɣleti adrẽlia me.

english_verse: When Hezekiah and his officials saw these offerings, they thanked the Lord and the people.
translation_verse: Esi Xizkiya kple eƒe dumegãwo va kpɔ nu siwo woli kɔe ɖi la, wokafu Aƒetɔ kple eƒe dukɔ Israel.

english_verse: Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the large amount of offerings.
translation_verse: Fia bia gbe nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo le nu siwo woli kɔe ɖi la ŋu,

english_verse: The high priest at the time was Azariah, a descendant of Zadok, and he replied, “Ever since the people have been bringing us their offerings, we have had more than enough food and supplies. The Lord has certainly blessed his people. Look at how much is left over!”
translation_verse: eye nunɔlagã Azarya, si nye Zadok ƒe dzidzimevi la ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Tso esime wode asi nudzɔdzɔawo tsɔtsɔ va Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me la, míeɖu nu ɖi ƒo, wògasusɔ fũu, elabe Aƒetɔ yra eƒe dukɔ la eya ta nu gbogbo siawo susɔ ɖo.”

english_verse: So the king gave orders for storerooms to be built in the temple, and when they were completed,
translation_verse: Tete Xizkiya ɖe gbe be woawɔ xɔwo ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me, eye wowɔe.

english_verse: all the extra offerings were taken there. Hezekiah and Azariah then appointed Conaniah the Levite to be in charge of these storerooms. His brother Shimei was his assistant, and the following Levites worked with them: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah.
translation_verse: Woɖo Levi vi bubu ewo be woawɔ dɔ le Xananya kple nɔvia Simei te. Woawoe nye: Yexiel, Azarya, Naxat, Asahel, Yerimot, Yozabad, Eliel, Yismaxya, Maxat kple Benanya. Fia Xizkiya kple nunɔlagã Azarya, Mawu ƒe aƒe la dzikpɔlae wɔ ɖoɖoa alea.

english_verse: Kore son of Imnah was assigned to guard the East Gate, and he was put in charge of receiving the offerings voluntarily given to God and of dividing them among the priests and Levites.
translation_verse: Woɖo Kore, Yimna vi, ame si nye Levi vi, eye wònye agbonudzɔla le gbedoxɔa ƒe ɣedzeƒekpa dzi la be wòanɔ nu siwo amewo va naa Aƒetɔ faa la xɔm, eye wòanɔ wo mam hã.

english_verse: He had six assistants who were responsible for seeing that all the priests in the other towns of Judah also got their share of these offerings. They were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah. Every priest and every Levite over
translation_verse: Ame siwo mele eme o la woe nye: Ŋutsu siwo ŋkɔ woŋlɔ ɖe dzidzimegbalẽ la me, eye woxɔ ƒe etɔ̃ alo wu nenema, ame siwo katã vaa Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me be woawɔ woƒe subɔsubɔdɔ le woƒe ɖoɖowo nu.

english_verse: Hezekiah also appointed other men to take food and supplies to the priests and Levites whose homes were in the pastureland around the towns of Judah. But the priests had to be descendants of Aaron, and the Levites had to be listed in the official records.
translation_verse: Le nunɔla siwo le du siwo nye Aron ƒe dzidzimeviwo tɔ kple wo ŋu agbletawo gome la, woɖo ame tɔxɛwo ɖi be woama nuɖuɖua na wo. Ame siawo maa nuɖuɖu na ŋutsu siwo le nunɔlawo ƒe ƒomea me kple ame bubu siwo katã ƒe ŋkɔ le Levi viwo ƒe ƒomegbalẽa me la.

english_verse: Everything Hezekiah did while he was king of Judah, including what he did for the temple in Jerusalem, was right and good. He was a successful king, because he obeyed the Lord God with all his heart.
translation_verse: Nu sia nu si gɔme wòdze be yeawɔ, eɖanye le Mawu ƒe aƒe la me alo nufiafia alo se la ŋu, be yeatsɔ adi yeƒe Mawui la, ewɔe kple dzi blibo eye nu dze edzi nɛ.

english_verse: The officials said all these things in Hebrew, so that everyone listening from the city wall would understand and be terrified and surrender.
translation_verse: Wodo ɣli sesĩe le Yuda-gbe me be yewoatsɔ de vɔvɔ̃ lã me na ame siwo le glia dzi le Yerusalem aɖe dzi le wo ƒo, ale be woate ŋu axɔ du la.

english_verse: You've heard what my ancestors and I have done to other nations. Were the gods of those nations able to defend their land against us?
translation_verse: Nu si nye kple tɔgbuinyewo míetu kple dukɔ bubuwo la, ɖe miesee oa? Ðe dukɔ mawo ƒe mawuwo te ŋu xɔ na wo tso asinye mea?

english_verse: The Lord rescued Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from Sennacherib and also protected them from other enemies.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ xɔ na fia Xizkiya kple Yerusalemnɔlawo tso Asiria-fia Sanxerib kple futɔ bubuwo katã si me. Ena wonɔ kple dukɔ siwo katã ƒo xlã wo godoo va kpe le ŋutifafa me.

english_verse: he and his officials worked out a plan to cut off the supply of water outside the city, so that the Assyrians would have no water when they came to attack. The officials got together a large work force that stopped up the springs and streams near Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Woƒo ameha gã aɖe nu ƒu eye woxe vudowo katã kple tɔʋu si sí va to anyigba la dzi la. Wogblɔ be: “Nu ka ta tsi abɔ ɖi Asiria-fiawo nava kpɔ?”

english_verse: Hezekiah's workers also repaired the broken sections of the city wall. Then they built defense towers and an outer wall to help protect the one already there. The landfill on the east side of David's City was also strengthened. He gave orders to make a large supply of weapons and shields,
translation_verse: Fia la dzra ɖo ɖe wo ŋu. Eɖɔ glia ƒe gbagbãƒewo katã ɖo, tu gbetakpɔxɔwo ɖe wo dzi, eye wòɖo gli bubu ɖe xoxotɔ godo. Eɖo gli ɖe David ƒe du la ƒe Milo la ŋu, eye wòna wowɔ aʋawɔnuwo kple akpoxɔnuwo fũu.

english_verse: and he appointed army commanders over the troops. Then he gathered the troops together in the open area in front of the city gate and said to them:
translation_verse: Eɖo aʋakplɔlawo ɖe aʋakɔawo nu, eye wòyɔ wo va egbɔ ɖe gbadzaƒe si le dugbo la nu. Eƒo nu de dzi ƒo na wo be:

english_verse: Be brave and confident! There's no reason to be afraid of King Sennacherib and his powerful army. We are much more powerful,
translation_verse: “Misẽ ŋu eye milé dzi ɖe ƒo. Migavɔ̃ o. Asiria-fia kple ame gbogbo siwo katã le eŋu la megadzi ŋɔ na mi o, elabe ame si le mía dzi la, sesẽ wu ame si le edzi.

english_verse: When Sennacherib and his troops were camped at the town of Lachish, he sent a message to Hezekiah and the people in Jerusalem. It said:
translation_verse: Le nu siawo megbe, esime Asiria-fia Sanxerib kple eƒe aʋakɔ la katã gale Laxis kasa la, edɔ ame ɖe Yuda-fia Xizkiya kple Yudatɔ siwo katã le egbɔ le Yerusalem la be:

english_verse: I am King Sennacherib of Assyria, and I have Jerusalem surrounded. Do you think you can survive my attack?
translation_verse: “Ale nye Sanxerib, Asiria-fia, mele gbɔgblɔm nye esi: ‘Nu ka ŋu miele dzi ɖom ɖo gabɔbɔ nɔ Yerusalem si meɖe to ɖo la?

english_verse: Don't be fooled by Hezekiah! No god of any nation has ever been able to stand up to Assyria. Believe me, your God cannot keep you safe!
translation_verse: Eya ta migana Xizkiya nable mi alo akplɔ mi trae o. Migaxɔ edzi se o. Dukɔ alo fiaɖuƒe aɖeke ƒe mawu aɖeke mete ŋu ɖe eƒe dukɔ tso nye kple tɔgbuinyewo si me kpɔ o. Miaƒe mawu la mate ŋu aɖe mi tso asinye me koŋ o.’ ”

english_verse: The Assyrian officials said terrible things about the Lord God and his servant Hezekiah.
translation_verse: Asiria-fia ƒe dɔlawo hã gblɔ nya geɖe ɖe Aƒetɔ, Mawu kple eƒe dɔla Xizkiya ŋu.

english_verse: Sennacherib's letter even made fun of the Lord. It said, “The gods of other nations could not save their people from Assyria's army, and neither will the God that Hezekiah worships.”
translation_verse: Asiria-fia ŋlɔ agbalẽ hã ɖe alɔ me le Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋu gblɔ ɖe eŋu be: “Ale si dukɔ aɖeke ƒe mawu mete ŋu ɖee tso asinye me kpɔ o la, nenema ke Xizkiya ƒe mawu hã mate ŋu aɖe eƒe dukɔ tso asinye mee o.”

english_verse: People brought offerings to Jerusalem for the Lord and expensive gifts for Hezekiah, and from that day on, every nation on earth respected Hezekiah. Hezekiah Gets Sick and Almost Dies (
translation_verse: Ame geɖewo he nunanawo vɛ na Aƒetɔ le Yerusalem. Wotsɔ nunana xɔasiwo vɛ na Yuda-fia Xizkiya hã, ale be tso esia dzi la, eŋkɔ de du le dukɔwo katã dome. Xizkiya ƒe dɔléle kple eƒe dàda (Fia II,

english_verse: About this same time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. He prayed, and the Lord gave him a sign that he would recover.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke mawo me la, Xizkiya lé dɔ eye wòku kloe. Edo gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ eye Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu nɛ kple dzesi aɖe.

english_verse: But Hezekiah was so proud that he refused to thank the Lord for everything he had done for him. This made the Lord angry, and he punished Hezekiah and the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ke Xizkiya de asi dàda me, eye meɖe eƒe akpedada fia Aƒetɔ le nyui si wòwɔ nɛ la ta o, eya ta Aƒetɔ do dziku ɖe eya kple Yuda-dukɔa kpakple Yerusalem ŋu.

english_verse: Hezekiah and the people later felt sorry and asked the Lord to forgive them. So the Lord did not punish them as long as Hezekiah was king. Hezekiah's Wealth (
translation_verse: Tete Xizkiya kple Yerusalemnɔlawo bɔbɔ wo ɖokui, eye Aƒetɔ ƒe dzi fa ale be megahe to na wo le Xizkiya ƒe agbenɔɣi o. Xizkiya ƒe kesinɔnuwo kple atsyɔ̃

english_verse: Hezekiah was very rich, and everyone respected him. He built special rooms to store the silver, the gold, the precious stones and spices, the shields, and the other valuable possessions.
translation_verse: Kesinɔnu kple bubu geɖe ŋutɔ su Xizkiya si. Etu nudzraɖoƒe geɖe siwo me klosalo, sika, kpe xɔasiwo, atike ʋeʋẽewo, akpoxɔnuwo kple nu xɔasi ƒomevi vovovowo nɔ.

english_verse: Storehouses were also built for his supply of grain, wine, and olive oil; barns were built for his cattle, and pens were put up for his sheep.
translation_verse: Etu nudzraɖoƒewo na bli, wain kple ami hã. Etu lãxɔ na nyihawo, eye wotɔ kpɔ na alẽhawo.

english_verse: God made Hezekiah extremely rich, so he bought even more sheep, goats, and cattle. And he built towns where he could keep all these animals.
translation_verse: Etso duwo na eɖokui, eye alẽha kple nyiha gãwo nɔ esi elabe Mawu na kesinɔnu geɖe ŋutɔe.

english_verse: It was Hezekiah who built a tunnel that carried the water from Gihon Spring into the city of Jerusalem. In fact, everything he did was successful!

translation_verse: Xizkiya ƒe ŋutinya mamlɛa kple eƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔwo la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe gbeƒãɖela Yesaya, Amoz vi, ƒe Ŋutegagbalẽ kple Yuda kple Israel-fiawo Ŋutinyagbalẽ me.

english_verse: When Hezekiah died, he was buried in the section of the royal tombs that was reserved for the most respected kings, and everyone in Judah and Jerusalem honored him. His son Manasseh then became king.
translation_verse: Xizkiya ku, eye woɖii ɖe kɔkɔƒe le David ƒe dzidzimeviwo ƒe ɖiƒe. Yuda blibo la kple Yerusalemnɔlawo katã de bubu eŋu le eƒe ku me. Via Manase zu fia ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: But the people of Judah and Jerusalem listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
translation_verse: Ke Manase na Yuda kple Yerusalemnɔlawo wɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi wu dukɔ siwo Aƒetɔ tsrɔ̃ ɖa le Israelviwo ŋgɔ gɔ̃ hã. Manase trɔ dzime

english_verse: Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his prayer to the Lord God and the warnings from his prophets, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Manase ƒe ŋutinya mamlɛawo, eƒe gbedodoɖawo na Mawu kple nukpɔlawo ƒe nya siwo wogblɔ nɛ le Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋkɔ me la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel-fiawo ƒe Ŋutinyagbalẽ la me.

english_verse: While Manasseh was held captive there, he asked the Lord God to forgive him and to help him.
translation_verse: Esi Manase ɖo xaxa me la, eƒo koko na Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu la, eye wòbɔbɔ eɖokui ɖe anyi ŋutɔ le tɔgbuiawo ƒe Mawu la ŋkume.

english_verse: He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. And he continued to worship the stars.
translation_verse: Elabe egbugbɔ tu nuxeƒe siwo tɔ́a Xizkiya gbã la. Eɖi vɔsamlekpuiwo na Baalwo, mè legba na nyɔnumawu Asera, eye wòde ta agu na dziŋgɔli me ŋusẽwo katã hesubɔ wo.

english_verse: In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods
translation_verse: Eɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe si ŋu Aƒetɔ gblɔ le be: “Yerusalem woasubɔm le tegbee” la me.

english_verse: and the stars. He placed these altars in both courtyards of the temple
translation_verse: Eɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ƒe xɔxɔnu eveawo hã.

english_verse: and even set up a stone image of a foreign god. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own sons in Hinnom Valley. He did many other sinful things and made the Lord very angry. Years ago, God had told David and Solomon: Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there in the temple I will be worshiped forever.
translation_verse: Emè legba, eye wotsɔe ɖo mawuxɔ la me. Evɔ wònye teƒe sia ŋue Mawu gblɔ na David kple via Salomo le be: “Xɔ sia me kple Yerusalem afi siae metia le Israel-towo ƒe nɔƒewo katã be woasubɔm le tegbee.

english_verse: If my people will faithfully obey all the laws and teaching I gave to my servant Moses, I will never again force them to leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
translation_verse: Nyemate Israel ƒe afɔ ɖa le anyigba sia si metia na mia tɔgbuiwo la dzi o; ɖeko woaɖɔ ŋu ɖo awɔ se, ɖoɖo kple kɔnu siwo katã mena wo to Mose dzi la dzi.”

english_verse: The Lord tried to warn Manasseh and the people about their sins, but they ignored the warning.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be Aƒetɔ gbe nya na Manase kple eƒe dukɔa hã la, womeɖo toe o.

english_verse: So he let Assyrian army commanders invade Judah and capture Manasseh. They put a hook in his nose and tied him up in chains, and they took him to Babylon.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ na Asiria-fia ƒe aʋakplɔlawo va dze wo dzi. Wolé Manase bɔ pãe, dee akɔblikunyowu me heɖe aboyoe yi Babilonia.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Manasseh's prayer and saw how sorry he was, and so he let him go back to Jerusalem and rule as king. Manasseh knew from then on that the Lord was God.
translation_verse: Edo gbe ɖa na Mawu, eye Aƒetɔ se eƒe kokoƒoƒo nɛ, eye wogagbugbɔe va eƒe fiaɖuƒe la me le Yerusalem. To esia me Manase dze sii be Aƒetɔ ye nye Mawu.

english_verse: Later, Manasseh rebuilt the eastern section of Jerusalem's outer wall and made it taller. This section went from Gihon Valley north to Fish Gate and around the part of the city called Mount Ophel. He also assigned army officers to each of the fortified cities in Judah.
translation_verse: Esia megbe la, eɖo gli ɖe David ƒe du la ŋu le bali la me, tso Gixon ƒe ɣetoɖoƒe gome, va ƒo xlã Ofel, ɖaɖo Tɔmelãgbo la nu. Eɖo gliawo wokɔ ŋutɔ. Azɔ eɖe aʋakplɔlawo da ɖe Yuda-du sesẽ ɖe sia ɖe me.

english_verse: Manasseh also removed the idols and the stone image of the foreign god from the temple, and he gathered the altars he had built near the temple and in other parts of Jerusalem. He threw all these things outside the city.
translation_verse: Eɖe amedzrowo ƒe mawuwo kple legba la ɖa le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me, hekpe ɖe vɔsamlekpui siwo wòɖi ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe ƒe to dzi kple Yerusalem-dua me la ŋuti. Elɔ wo ɖaƒu gbe ɖe dua godo.

english_verse: Then he repaired the Lord's altar and offered sacrifices to thank him and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He gave orders that everyone in Judah must worship the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Edzra Aƒetɔ ƒe vɔsamlekpui la ɖo, eye wòsa ŋutifafavɔ kple akpedadavɔ le edzi. Eɖoe na Yuda be woasubɔ Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la ko.

english_verse: Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done, and he worshiped and offered sacrifices to the idols his father had made.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi le Aƒetɔ ŋkume abe tɔ́a Manase ene. Amon sa vɔ na legba siwo katã tɔ́a Manase wɔ la, eye wòsubɔ wo.

english_verse: Manasseh had turned back to the Lord, but Amon refused to do that. Instead, he sinned even more than his father.
translation_verse: Ke eya mede ta agu na Aƒetɔ abe ale si tɔ́a Manase bɔbɔ eɖokui la ene o, ke Amon na fɔɖiɖi dzi ɖe edzi.

english_verse: Some of Amon's officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace.
translation_verse: Eŋumewo ɖo nugbe ɖe eŋu, eye wowui le eƒeme.

english_verse: But the people of Judah killed the murderers of Amon and made his son Josiah king.
translation_verse: Ke dukɔmetɔwo hã wu ame siwo katã ɖo nugbe ɖe fia Amon ŋu la, eye wotsɔ via Yosiya ɖo fiae ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Hilkiah and the four other men left at once and went to talk with Huldah the prophet. Her husband was Shallum, who was in charge of the king's clothes. Huldah lived in the northern part of Jerusalem, and when they met in her home,

english_verse: In the eighteenth year of Josiah's rule in Judah, after he had removed all the sinful things from the land and from the Lord's temple, he sent three of his officials to repair the temple. translation_verse: Le Yosiya ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè wui enyilia me, esime wòɖe nu gbegblẽwo ɖa le anyigba la kple xɔa me vɔ la, edɔ Safan, Azalya vi kple dua dziɖula Maaseya kpakple Yoax, fia ƒe agbalẽŋlɔla Yoaxaz vi ɖa be woaɖadzra Aƒetɔ, Mawu la ƒe aƒe la ɖo.

english_verse: After Josiah had finished reading, he stood in the place reserved for the king. He promised in the Lord's name to faithfully obey the Lord and to follow his laws and teachings that were written in the book.
translation_verse: Fia la tsi tsitre ɖe enɔƒe, eye wòbla nu kple Aƒetɔ be yeanɔ eyome, alé eƒe sewo, sededewo kple ɖoɖowo me ɖe asi tso dzi blibo kple luʋɔ blibo me. Edo ŋugbe be yeawɔ nubablaa ƒe nyawo dzi abe ale si woŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽa me la ene.

english_verse: He watched as the altars for the worship of the god Baal were torn down, and as the nearby incense altars were smashed. The Asherah poles, the idols, and the stone images were also smashed, and the pieces were scattered over the graves of their worshipers.
translation_verse: Eya ŋutɔ le eteƒe wogbã Baalwo ƒe vɔsamlekpuiwo. Wokaka lifivɔsaƒe siwo le wo dzi la. Womu nyɔnumawu Asera ƒe ati kɔkɔawo ƒu anyi, eye wogbã aklama kpakpɛ kple legba siwo wolólo hekɔ la. Wotu wo memie helɔ kɔ ɖe ame siwo sa vɔ na wo tsã la ƒe yɔdowo dzi.

english_verse: Shaphan took the book to Josiah and reported, “Your officials are doing everything you wanted.
translation_verse: Sefan tsɔ agbalẽa vɛ na fia la gblɔ be: “Dɔ siwo katã nèdɔ mí, wò dɔlawo la, míele wo dzi.

english_verse: Josiah then had the bones of the pagan priests burned on the altars. And so Josiah got rid of the worship of foreign gods in Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Etɔ dzo nunɔlawo ƒe ƒuwo le woƒe vɔsamlekpui dzi, eye wòkɔ Yuda kple Yerusalem ŋu.

english_verse: He did the same things in the towns and ruined villages in the territories of West Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as the border of Naphtali.
translation_verse: Ewɔ esia le duwo kple aƒedowo me le Manase, Efrayim kple Simeon towo hã me ɖado ɖe keke Naftali ke.

english_verse: These three men went to Hilkiah the high priest. They gave him the money that the Levite guards had collected from the people of West Manasseh, Ephraim, and the rest of Israel, as well as those living in Judah, Benjamin, and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Wova Xilkiya, nunɔlagã gbɔ, eye wotsɔ ga si amewo he va Mawu ƒe aƒe la me si Levi vi siwo dzɔa agbo nu la dzɔ le Manase, Efrayim kple Israelvi mamlɛawo katã si le Yuda, Benyamin kple Yerusalem blibo la katã vɛ.

english_verse: and they gave the rest of it to the carpenters and builders, who used it to buy the stone and wood they needed to repair the other buildings that Judah's kings had not taken care of.
translation_verse: Woawo tsɔ ga la na atikpalawo kple gliɖolawo ne woatsɔ aƒle kpe fúfuwo, xɔblatiwo kple daɖedzitiwo atsɔ adzra xɔ siwo Yuda-fiawo gblẽ ɖi wogbã la ɖo.

english_verse: The workers were honest, and their supervisors were Jahath and Obadiah from the Levite clan of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the Levite clan of Kohath. Other Levites, who were all skilled musicians,
translation_verse: Ameawo wɔ dɔa anukwaretɔe. Levi vi ene kpɔ wo dzi. Wotia: Yaxat kple Obadya siwo nye Levi viwo tso Merari-ƒome la me kple Zaxarya kpakple Mesulam tso Kehat-ƒome la me ɖo dɔwɔlawo nu. Wotsɔ Levi vi bubu siwo katã nya hadzinuwo ŋudɔwɔwɔ la

english_verse: While the money was being given to these supervisors, Hilkiah found the book that contained the laws that the Lord had given to Moses.
translation_verse: Esime wotsɔ ga si amewo na Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me la do goe gbɔna la, nunɔla Xilkiya fɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe Segbalẽ si wòna to Mose dzi la.

english_verse: Hilkiah handed the book to Shaphan the official and said, “Look what I found here in the temple—The Book of God's Law.”
translation_verse: Xilkiya gblɔ na agbalẽŋlɔla Safan be: “Mefɔ Segbalẽ la le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me”, eye wòtsɔ agbalẽ la nɛ.

translation_verse: Wolɔ ga si wokpɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me la na dɔdzikpɔlaawo kple dɔwɔlaawo.”

english_verse: But there's something else, Your Majesty. The priest Hilkiah gave me this book.” Then Shaphan read it aloud.
translation_verse: Azɔ Safan, agbalẽŋlɔla gagblɔ na fia la be: “Agbalẽ aɖee nye esi nunɔla Xilkiya tsɔ nam.” Safan xlẽe na fia la.

english_verse: When Josiah heard what was in The Book of God's Law, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Esi fia la se agbalẽa me nyawo la, edze awu le eɖokui ŋu.

english_verse: “The Lord must be furious with me and everyone else in Israel and Judah, because our ancestors did not obey the laws written in this book. Go find out what the Lord wants us to do.”
translation_verse: “Miyi ɖabia nu ɖe nye kple ame siwo susɔ le Israel kple Yuda la nu, le agbalẽ si wofɔ la me nyawo ŋuti. Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔmedzoe si va mía dzi la nu sesẽ ŋutɔ elabe mía tɔgbuiwo melé eƒe nyawo me ɖe asi o, eye womewɔ ɖe nu siwo katã woŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽ sia me la dzi o.”

english_verse: “Josiah, I am the Lord! And I intend to punish this country and everyone in it, just as this book says.
translation_verse: ‘Aƒetɔ, be: Kpɔ ɖa, dzɔgbevɔ̃e kple fiƒode siwo katã woŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽ si woxlẽ na Yuda-fia me la, ava teƒe sia kple edzinɔlawo dzi.

english_verse: The people of Judah and Israel have rejected me. They have offered sacrifices to foreign gods and have worshiped their own idols. I can't stand it any longer. I am furious.
translation_verse: Elabe wogblẽm ɖi ɖasa lifivɔ na mawu tutɔwo, ale wotsɔ woƒe asinudɔwɔwɔwo do dziku nam vevie. Eya ta woakɔ nye dɔmedzoe ɖe teƒe sia dzi eye womate ŋu atsi enu o.

english_verse: “Josiah, listen to what I am going to do. I noticed how sad you were when you heard that this country and its people would be completely wiped out. You even tore your clothes in sorrow, and I heard you cry.

english_verse: So before I destroy this place, I will let you die in peace.” The men left and reported to Josiah what Huldah had said. Josiah Reads The Book of God's Law (

english_verse: King Josiah called together the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Tete fia la na woƒo Yuda kple Yerusalem ame tsitsiwo katã nu ƒu.

english_verse: Then he went to the Lord's temple, together with all the people of Judah and Jerusalem, the priests, and the Levites. Finally, when everybody was there, he read aloud The Book of God's Law that had been found in the temple.
translation_verse: Fia la, Yudatɔwo katã, Yerusalemnɔlawo keŋ, nunɔlawo, Levi viwo, dukɔ blibo la, ɖeviwo kple tsitsiawo siaa, woyi Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me. Fia la tsi tsitre xlẽ nubablagbalẽ si wofɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me la me nyawo na wo wose ɖe to me.

english_verse: Then he asked the people of Jerusalem and Benjamin to make that same promise and to obey the God their ancestors had worshiped.

english_verse: Josiah destroyed all the idols in the territories of Israel, and he commanded everyone in Israel to worship only the Lord God. The people did not turn away from the Lord God of their ancestors for the rest of Josiah's rule as king.
translation_verse: Yosiya ɖe ŋunyɔnuwo katã ɖa le Israelviwo ƒe anyigba la katã dzi, eye wòna ame sia ame si le Israel la subɔ Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la. Le eƒe agbe me ŋkekeawo me la, womete ɖa le wo tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu la ŋu o.

english_verse: During the battle an Egyptian soldier shot Josiah with an arrow. Josiah told his servants, “Get me out of here! I've been hit.”
translation_verse: Tete aŋutrɔdalawo té fia Yosiya. Fia la gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo be: “Mikplɔm dzoe; mexɔ abi vevie.”

english_verse: Neco sent the following message to Josiah: I'm not attacking you, king of Judah! We're not even at war. But God has told me to quickly attack my enemy. God is on my side, so if you try to stop me, he will punish you.
translation_verse: Ke Nexo dɔ ame ɖee be: “O, Yuda-fia, nya kae le nye kple wò dome? Menye wò ŋu meho ɖo fifia o, boŋ fiaɖuƒe si mía kplii míele aʋa dzi la ŋu ye, eye Mawu be mawɔ kaba. Megatsi tsitre ɖe Mawu, ame si li kplim la ŋu ne wòava atsrɔ̃ wò o.”

english_verse: Josiah commanded that Passover be celebrated in Jerusalem to honor the Lord. So, on the fourteenth day of the first month, the lambs were killed for the Passover celebration.
translation_verse: Fia Yosiya ɖu Paska le Yerusalem tsɔ de bubu Aƒetɔ ŋu. Wowu Ŋutitotovɔsalãwo le ƒè la ƒe ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke wui enea gbe.

english_verse: Get ready to do the work that David and Solomon assigned to you, according to your clans.
translation_verse: Miɖo ɖe hatsotsowo me ɖe mia tɔgbuiwo ƒe ƒomeawo nu, abe ale si David Israel-fia kple via Salomo ŋlɔ ɖi la ene.

english_verse: When the people bring you their Passover lamb, you must kill it and prepare it to be sacrificed to the Lord. Make sure the people celebrate according to the instructions that the Lord gave Moses, and don't do anything to make yourselves unclean and unacceptable.
translation_verse: Miwu ŋutitotovɔsalã la eye mikɔ mia ɖokui ŋu ne miadzrae ɖo na mia nɔviwo be woawɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe ɖoɖo si wòna to Mose dzi la dzi.”

english_verse: Josiah's officials also voluntarily gave some of their animals to the people, the priests, and the Levites as sacrifices. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, who were the officials in charge of the temple, gave the priests
translation_verse: Eƒe dumegãwo hã na lɔlɔ̃nununana dukɔa, nunɔlaawo kple Levi viawo faa. Xilkiya, Zaxarya kple Yexiel, ame siwo nye Mawu ƒe aƒe la dzikpɔlawo la na alẽvi kple gbɔ̃vi akpe eve kple alafa ade kple nyitsu alafa etɔ̃ nunɔlaawo.

english_verse: Conaniah, his two brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, as well as Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad were leaders of the Levites, and they gave the other Levites
translation_verse: Azɔ Xananya, Semaya, Netaneel kple nɔviawo kple Xasabya, Yeiel kpakple Yozabad, ame siwo nye Levi viwo ƒe tatɔwo la na alẽvi kple gbɔ̃vi akpe atɔ̃ kple nyitsu alafa atɔ̃ Levi viwo hena ŋutitotovɔsawo.

english_verse: When everything was ready to celebrate Passover, the priests and the Levites stood where Josiah had told them.
translation_verse: Esi wowɔ ɖoɖo ɖe subɔsubɔ la ŋu vɔ la, nunɔlawo tsi tsitre ɖe woƒe teƒe eye Levi viwo le woƒe hatsotsowo me abe ale si fia la ɖe gbe na wo la ene.

english_verse: Then the Levites killed and skinned the Passover lambs, and they handed some of the blood to the priests, who splattered it on the altar.
translation_verse: Wowu ŋutitotovɔsalãawo eye nunɔlawo xɔ ʋu la le Levi viawo si me le hehlẽm, esime Levi viawo le agbalẽ kom le lãawo ŋu.

english_verse: The Levites set aside the parts of the animal that the worshipers needed for their sacrifices to please the Lord, just as the Law of Moses required. They also did the same thing with the bulls.
translation_verse: Woɖe numemevɔsalã la ɖe aga be woama na ameawo ɖe woƒe ƒomewo nu, ne woatsɔ sa vɔ na Aƒetɔ, abe ale si wogblɔ be woawɔe le Mose ƒe sea me la ene. Wowɔ nyitsuawo hã nenema.

english_verse: They sacrificed the Passover animals on the altar and boiled the meat for the other offerings in pots, kettles, and pans. Then they quickly handed the meat to the people so they could eat it.
translation_verse: Womè ŋutitotolã la le dzo me ɖe ɖoɖoa nu, eye woɖa nunana kɔkɔeawo le ze kple gaze kpakple agbawo me ɖama kabakaba na ameha blibo la katã.

english_verse: All day long, the priests were busy offering sacrifices and burning the animals' fat on the altar. And when everyone had finished, the Levites prepared Passover animals for themselves and for the priests.
translation_verse: Emegbe wokpɔ woawo ŋutɔ kple nunɔlawo tɔ gbɔ. Nunɔlawo, ame siwo nye Aron ƒe dzidzimeviwo la nɔ dzo tɔm numemevɔsawo kple lãmiawo va se ɖe esime zã do. Eya ta Levi viwo wɔ woawo ŋutɔ kple nunɔlawo Aron ƒe dzidzimeviwo tɔ.

english_verse: During the celebration some of the Levites prepared Passover animals for the musicians and the guards, so that the Levite musicians would not have to leave their places, which had been assigned to them according to the instructions of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's prophet. Even the guards at the temple gates did not have to leave their posts.
translation_verse: Hadzilawo, ame siwo nye Asaf ƒe dzidzimeviwo la le woƒe teƒe abe ale si David, Asaf, Heman kple Yedutun, fia ƒe nukpɔla ɖo na wo lae ene. Nenema ke agbonudzɔlawo le agbo sia agbo nu. Womekpɔ mɔ adzo le woƒe dɔdeasi gbɔ o, elabe wo nɔvi Levi viwo ɖa nu na wo.

english_verse: So on that day, Passover was celebrated to honor the Lord, and sacrifices were offered on the altar to him, just as Josiah had commanded.
translation_verse: Aleae wowɔ ɖoɖo ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe subɔsubɔdɔ blibo la ŋu gbe ma gbee. Woɖu Paska la, eye wosa numemevɔ le Aƒetɔ ƒe vɔsamlekpui la dzi abe ale si fia Yosiya ɖe gbe be woaɖui la ene.

english_verse: The worshipers then celebrated the Festival of Thin Bread for the next seven days.
translation_verse: Israelvi siwo va la ɖu Paska la kple Abolo Maʋamaʋã Ŋkeke Nyui la ŋkeke adrẽ.

english_verse: People from Jerusalem and from towns all over Judah and Israel were there. Passover had not been observed like this since the days of Samuel the prophet. In fact, this was the greatest Passover celebration in Israel's history!
translation_verse: Tso Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela Samuel ŋɔli va se ɖe ɣe ma ɣi kpa womeɖu Paska aɖeke alea kpɔ o. Israel-fia siwo katã do ŋgɔ na Yosiya la dometɔ aɖeke meɖu Paska aɖeke abe esi Yosiya, nunɔlawo, Levi viwo, Yuda-dukɔ bliboa kple Israelvi siwo va kpakple Yerusalemnɔlawo ɖui la ene o.

english_verse: All these things happened in the eighteenth year of Josiah's rule in Judah. Josiah Dies in Battle (
translation_verse: Woɖu Paska sia esime Yosiya le eƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè wui enyilia me. Yosiya ƒe nuwuwu (Fia II,

english_verse: Some time later, King Neco of Egypt led his army to the city of Carchemish on the Euphrates River. And Josiah led his troops north to meet the Egyptians in battle.
translation_verse: Esi Yosiya ɖɔ aƒe la me ɖo vɔ megbe keŋ la, Nexo, Egipte-fia ho be yeaɖawɔ aʋa le Karkemis le Frat-tɔsisi nu. Yosiya ho yi be yeakpe kplii.

english_verse: But Josiah ignored Neco's warning, even though it came from God! Instead, he disguised himself and marched into battle against Neco in the valley near Megiddo.
translation_verse: Ke Yosiya metrɔ dzo o. Meɖo to Nexo ƒe nya si Mawu gblɔ nɛ la o, ke boŋ edze avu be yeaɖakpe aʋa kplii le Megido-bali la me.

english_verse: They carried Josiah out of his chariot, then put him in the other chariot he had there and took him back to Jerusalem, where he soon died. He was buried beside his ancestors, and everyone in Judah and Jerusalem mourned his death.
translation_verse: Ale eƒe dɔlawo ɖee le tasiaɖam la me de eƒe tasiaɖam evelia me, eye wòkɔe va Yerusalem. Eku, eye woɖii ɖe tɔgbuiawo ɖiƒe. Yuda kple Yerusalem katã fa na Yosiya.

english_verse: Jeremiah the prophet wrote a funeral song in honor of Josiah. And since then, anyone in Judah who mourns the death of Josiah sings that song. It is included in the collection of funeral songs.
translation_verse: Yeremya kpa konyifaha na Yosiya, eye ŋutsuhadzilawo kple nyɔnuhadzilawo siaa dzi konyifaha na Yosiya, eye esia zu kɔnu le Israel va se ɖe egbe. Woŋlɔ ha siawo ɖe Konyifahawo ƒe agbalẽ me.

english_verse: Everything else Josiah did while he was king, including how he faithfully obeyed the Lord,
translation_verse: Yosiya ƒe ŋutinya mamlɛawo, eƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe se la nu

english_verse: is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: kple eƒe ŋutinya tso gɔmedzedzea va se ɖe nuwuwua la, woŋlɔ wo ɖe Israel kple Yuda-fiawo ƒe Ŋutinyagbalẽ la me.

english_verse: The message said: I am King Cyrus of Persia. The Lord God of heaven has made me the ruler of every nation on earth. He has also chosen me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. The Lord God will watch over any of his people who want to go back to Judah.
translation_verse: “ ‘Kores, Persia-fia, be: ‘Aƒetɔ, Dziƒo Mawu la tsɔ anyigba dzi fiaɖuƒewo katã nam, eye wòɖoe nam be matu xɔ na ye ɖe Yerusalem si le Yuda la. Ame sia ame si nye eƒe dukɔmevi le mia dome la, Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu nenɔ kplii. Mina ne wòayi!’ ”

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar also carried off many of the valuable things in the Lord's temple, and he put them in his palace in Babylon.
translation_verse: Nebukadnezar lɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me ŋudɔwɔnu aɖewo ɖada ɖe eƒe fiasã me le Babilon.

english_verse: The Lord sent King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to attack Jerusalem. Nebuchadnezzar killed the young men who were in the temple, and he showed no mercy to anyone, whether man or woman, young or old. God let him kill everyone in the city.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ kplɔ Kaldea-fia vɛ wòho aʋa ɖe wo ŋu. Ewu woƒe ɖekakpuiwo kple yi le aƒe la ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la me. Mekpɔ nublanui na ɖekakpui alo ɖetugbi, ame tsitsi alo amegãɖeɖi o; etsɔ wo katã de asi nɛ.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar carried off everything that was left in the temple; he robbed the treasury and the personal storerooms of the king and his officials. He took everything back to Babylon.
translation_verse: Babilon-fia lɔ Mawu ƒe aƒe la me ŋudɔwɔnuwo katã, gãtɔwo kple suetɔwo siaa, Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me kesinɔnuwo, fia la kple dumegãwo ƒe kesinɔnuwo, eye wotsɔ wo katã yi Babilon.

english_verse: In the spring of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had Jehoiachin arrested and taken to Babylon, along with more of the valuable items in the temple. Then Nebuchadnezzar appointed Zedekiah king of Judah. King Zedekiah of Judah (
translation_verse: Esi ƒe trɔ la, Nebukadnezar dɔ woɖakplɔe, lɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me ŋudɔwɔnu veviwo kpe ɖe eŋu, va Babilon. Etsɔ nɔvia ŋutsu Zedekiya ɖo fiae ɖe Yuda kple Yerusalem nu. Yuda-fia Zedekiya (Fia II,

english_verse: The survivors were taken to Babylonia as prisoners, where they were slaves of the king and his sons, until Persia became a powerful nation.
translation_verse: Ekplɔ ame siwo metsi yi nu o la yi Babilon, eye wozu kluvi na eya kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo va se ɖe esime Persia-fiaɖuƒe la va.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord his God and refused to change his ways, even after a warning from Jeremiah, the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Ewɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi le Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu la ŋkume. Mebɔbɔ eɖokui na gbeƒãɖela Yeremya esime wòɖe gbeƒã Aƒetɔ ƒe numegbe nɛ o. Yerusalem-gbagbã (Fia II,

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had forced Zedekiah to promise in God's name that he would be loyal. Zedekiah was stubborn and refused to turn back to the Lord God of Israel, so he rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Zedekiya dze aglã ɖe Nebukadnezar, ame si na wòtà Mawu nɛ be yeawɔ nuteƒe la ŋu. Etri to, sẽ dzime, eye wògbe be yematrɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋu o.

english_verse: The people of Judah and even the priests who were their leaders became more unfaithful. They followed the disgusting example of the nations around them and made the Lord's holy temple unfit for worship.
translation_verse: Gawu la, nunɔlawo ƒe tatɔwo katã kple dukɔ la hã tra mɔ vevie, elabe woawo hã subɔ dukɔ siwo ƒo xlã wo la ƒe legba nyɔŋuawo. Woƒo ɖi Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe le Yerusalem si ŋu wòkɔ la.

english_verse: But the Lord God felt sorry for his people, and instead of destroying the temple, he sent prophets who warned the people over and over about their sins.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, wo tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu la ɖo eƒe amedɔdɔwo ɖe wo enuenu elabe eƒe dukɔ la kple eƒe nɔƒe la wɔ nublanui nɛ.

english_verse: But the people only laughed and insulted these prophets. They ignored what the Lord God was trying to tell them, until he finally became so angry that nothing could stop him from punishing Judah and Jerusalem. Jerusalem Is Destroyed (
translation_verse: Ke woɖe alɔ me le Mawu ƒe amedɔdɔawo ŋu, do vlo eƒe nyaawo, eye woɖu fewu le gbeƒãɖelaawo ŋu, va se ɖe esime Aƒetɔ va do dɔmedzoe ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe dukɔ la ŋu vevie ale gbegbe be womete ŋu tsi enu o.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar's troops burned down the temple and destroyed every important building in the city. Then they broke down the city wall.
translation_verse: Wotɔ dzo Mawu ƒe aƒe la, mu Yerusalem ŋu gliawo ƒu anyi, tɔ dzo fiasãwo katã, eye wogblẽ woƒe nu xɔasiwo katã.

english_verse: In the first year that Cyrus was king of Persia, the Lord had Cyrus send a message to all parts of his kingdom. This happened just as Jeremiah the Lord's prophet had promised.
translation_verse: Le Kores, Persia-fia ƒe ƒè gbãtɔ me la, Aƒetɔ ƒe nya si wògblɔ to eƒe gbeƒãɖela Yeremya dzi la va eme. Aƒetɔ nyɔ Kores, Persia-fia ƒe gbɔgbɔ be wòaɖe gbeƒã le eƒe fiaɖuƒe blibo la me, eye wòana woaŋlɔ agbalẽ atu edzi be:

english_verse: I am King Cyrus of Persia. The Lord God of heaven, who is also the God of Israel, has made me the ruler of all nations on earth. And he has chosen me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. The Lord God will watch over and encourage any of his people who want to go back to Jerusalem and help build the temple.
translation_verse: Eƒe dukɔmetɔ ɖe sia ɖe si le mia dome la, eƒe Mawu nenɔ kplii. Neyi Yerusalem si le Yuda la, ne wòaɖatu xɔ na Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la. Eyae nye Mawu si le Yerusalem.

english_verse: Everyone else must provide what is needed. They must give money, supplies, and animals, as well as gifts for rebuilding God's temple.
translation_verse: Na ame sia ame si susɔ ɖe teƒe si wòle la nɔlawo nakpe ɖe eŋu kple klosalo, sika, kesinɔnu vovovowo, agbatsɔlãwo kple lɔlɔ̃nununana bubuwo hena Mawu ƒe aƒe si le Yerusalem.”

english_verse: The others helped by giving silver articles, gold, personal possessions, cattle, and other valuable gifts, as well as offerings for the temple.
translation_verse: Woƒe aƒelikawo katã do alɔ wo kple klosalonuwo, sika, kesinɔnu vovovowo, agbatsɔlãwo, nunana xɔasiwo hekpe ɖe lɔlɔ̃nununanawo ŋuti.

english_verse: King Cyrus gave back the things that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the Lord's temple in Jerusalem and had put in the temple of his own gods.
translation_verse: Fia Kores hã he Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔ me nu siwo Nebukadnezar lɔ tso Yerusalem va eƒe mawuwo ƒeme la ɖe go.

english_verse: Cyrus placed Mithredath, his chief treasurer, in charge of these things. Mithredath counted them and gave a list to Sheshbazzar, the governor of Judah.
translation_verse: Etsɔ wo na kesinɔnuwo dzikpɔla, Mitredat. Mitredat xlẽ wo ŋlɔ ɖi, eye wòtsɔ wo de asi na Yuda ƒe amegã Sesbazar.

english_verse: Here is how many people returned whose ancestors had come from the following towns:
translation_verse: Senaa viŋutsuwo le ame akpe etɔ̃ alafa ade bla etɔ̃.

english_verse: Here is a list of how many returned from each family of priests:
translation_verse: Xarim viŋutsuwo le ame akpe ɖeka wui adrẽ.

english_verse: In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until we find out if you really are priests.”
translation_verse: Anyigba dzikpɔla de se na wo be womekpɔ mɔ agaɖu vɔsanu kɔkɔetɔa ƒe ɖeke o, negbe nunɔla aɖe, ɖe wòtsɔ Urim kple Tumim va tso nya me hafi.

english_verse: When the people came to where the Lord's temple had been in Jerusalem, some of the family leaders gave gifts so it could be rebuilt in the same place.
translation_verse: Esi wova ɖo Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la gbɔ le Yerusalem la, ƒomeawo ƒe tatɔ aɖewo na nu kple lɔlɔ̃nu faa ɖe Mawu ƒe aƒe la ŋu, bene woagbugbɔe atu ɖe eteƒe.

english_verse: Everyone returned to the towns from which their families had come, including the priests, the Levites, the musicians, the temple guards, and the workers.
translation_verse: Nunɔlawo, Levi viwo kple ameawo dometɔ aɖewo nɔ Yerusalem kple eŋu duwo me, eye hadzilawo, agbonudzɔlawo kple gbedoxɔ me dɔwɔlawo yi ɖanɔ wo deduwo me. Ale Israel blibo la nɔ woƒe duwo me.

english_verse: During the seventh month of the year, the Israelites who had settled in their towns went to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Azɔ Israelviwo katã le wo deduawo me. Le ƒè la ƒe ɣleti adrẽlia me la, dukɔ blibo la va ƒo ƒu ɖe Yerusalem.

english_verse: The priest Joshua son of Jozadak, together with the other priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives rebuilt the altar of Israel's God. Then they were able to offer sacrifices there by following the instructions God had given to Moses, the man of God.
translation_verse: Tete Yesua, Yozadak vi kple nɔvia nunɔlawo kpakple Zerubabel, Sealtiel vi kple nɔviawo tso, eye woɖi vɔsamlekpui na Israel ƒe Mawu la bene woasa numemevɔ nɛ le edzi abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖe Mose, Mawu ƒe ame ƒe se la me la ene.

english_verse: And they built the altar where it had stood before, even though they were afraid of the people who were already living around there. Then every morning and evening they burned sacrifices and offerings to the Lord.
translation_verse: Woda vɔsamlekpui la ɖe eƒe gɔmeɖokpeawo dzi tututu, elabe wovɔ̃ na dukɔ siwo dome wova le la, eye wosaa numemevɔ le edzi na Aƒetɔ ŋdi kple fiẽ.

english_verse: The people followed the rules for celebrating the Festival of Shelters and offered the proper sacrifices each day.
translation_verse: Woɖu Agbadɔ Me Nɔnɔ Ŋkeke Nyui la abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖi be woaɖui la ene. Wosaa numemevɔ gbe sia gbe ɖe xexlẽme si woɖo ɖi na ŋkeke la nu.

english_verse: They offered sacrifices to please the Lord, sacrifices at each New Moon Festival, and sacrifices at the rest of the Lord's festivals. Every offering the people had brought voluntarily was also presented to the Lord.
translation_verse: Emegbe la, wosaa vɔ ɖoɖeanyi vovovowo: dzinu yeye vɔsa, Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋkeke kɔkɔeawo katã ƒe vɔsawo kple amewo ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu faa ƒe numemevɔsawo na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: Although work on the temple itself had not yet begun, the people started offering sacrifices on the Lord's altar on the first day of the seventh month of that year. The Rebuilding of the Temple Begins
translation_verse: Ale, tso ɣleti adrẽlia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ gbe la, wodze numemevɔsasa gɔme na Aƒetɔ. Gake womekpɔ ɖo Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔ la gɔme anyi haɖe o. Wodze gbedoxɔa gbugbɔ tutu gɔme

english_verse: King Cyrus of Persia had said the Israelites could have cedar trees brought from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. So they sent grain, wine, and olive oil to the cities of Tyre and Sidon as payment for these trees, and they gave money to the stoneworkers and carpenters.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ ga na gliɖolawo kple atikpalawo, eye wona nuɖuɖu, nunono kple ami Sidontɔwo kple Tirotɔwo be woatsɔ sederti tso Lebanon ato ƒu dzi va Yafo, abe ale si Persia-fia Kores ɖe gbe na woe ene.

english_verse: During the second month of the second year after the people had returned from Babylonia, they started rebuilding the Lord's temple. Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jozadak, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned started working. Every Levite over
translation_verse: Esi wogbɔ va Mawu ƒe xɔ la gbɔ le Yerusalem le ƒè evelia ƒe ɣleti evelia me la, Zerubabel, Sealtiel viŋutsu, Yerusa, Yozadak viŋutsu kple wo nɔvi mamlɛawo dze dɔ gɔme. Wo kple nunɔlawo, Levi viwo kple ame siwo katã tso aboyoa me va le Yerusalem lae dze dɔa gɔme. Wotsɔ Levi vi siwo xɔ ƒe bla eve kple edzi vɔwo la ɖo Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ƒe dɔwo nu.

english_verse: The Levites in charge of the whole project were Joshua and his sons and relatives and Kadmiel and his sons from the family of Hodaviah. The family of Henadad worked along with them.
translation_verse: Ale Yesua kple via ŋutsuwo kpakple nɔviawo, Kadmiel kple via ŋutsuwo, Binui kple Hodavia, hekpe ɖe Xenadad viŋutsuwo ŋu, Levi viwo, wo viŋutsuwo kple wo nɔviwoe nye ame siwo wɔ dɔ le Mawu ƒe aƒea ŋu la dzikpɔlawo.

english_verse: When the builders had finished laying the foundation of the temple, the priests put on their robes and blew trumpets in honor of the Lord, while the Levites from the family of Asaph praised God with cymbals. All of them followed the instructions given years before by King David.
translation_verse: Esi xɔtulawo ɖo Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔa gɔme anyi vɔ la, nunɔlawo le woƒe awuwo me lé kpẽwo ɖe asi va ɖo ɖi. Levi viwo, ame siwo nye Asaf ƒe dzidzimeviwo, hã tsɔ gakogoewo ɖe asi vɛ hena Aƒetɔ kafukafu abe ale si Israel-fia David ɖoe ɖi la ene.

english_verse: They praised the Lord and gave thanks as they took turns singing: “The Lord is good! His faithful love for Israel will last forever.” Everyone started shouting and praising the Lord because work on the foundation of the temple had begun.
translation_verse: Wodzi kafukafuha kple akpedaha doɖaxetɔe na Aƒetɔ be: “Elabe enyo, eye eƒe lɔlɔ̃ mavɔ la, le Israel dzi tegbee.” Dukɔ blibo la katã xe haa kple ɣli bobobo hekafu Aƒetɔ elabe woɖo Aƒetɔ ƒe xɔ la gɔme anyi.

english_verse: Many of the older priests and Levites and the heads of families wept bitterly because they remembered seeing the first temple years before. But others were so happy that they celebrated with joyful shouts.
translation_verse: Ke nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo kpakple aƒekɔwo ƒe tatɔ dometɔ geɖe siwo tsi kpɔ gbedoxɔ gbãtɔ, wònɔ tsitre ɖe eƒe gɔmeɖoɖo dzi kpɔ la ya, fa avi hehehe esi wokpɔ gbedoxɔ yeye sia ƒe gɔmeɖoɖo. Ale, esime ame aɖewo le dzidzɔseye tsom la, ɖewo hã le avi dzi bobobo.

english_verse: Their shouting and crying were so noisy that it all sounded alike and could be heard a long way off.
translation_verse: Dzidzɔseyea tɔtɔ kple avifafa sesẽ la ale gbegbe be womeganya kae nye ka o, eye hoowɔwɔ la ɖi de didiƒe ʋĩi.

english_verse: The enemies of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin heard that the people had come back to rebuild the temple of the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi Yuda kple Benyamin ƒe ketɔwo se be aboyometsolawo le gbedoxɔ tum na Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la la,

english_verse: So they went to Zerubbabel and to the family leaders and said, “Let us help! Ever since King Esarhaddon of Assyria brought us here, we have worshiped your God and offered sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: wova Zerubabel kple ƒomeawo ƒe tatɔwo gbɔ gblɔ na wo be: “Mina míakpe ɖe mia ŋu atu xɔa elabe míawo hã míesubɔa miaƒe Mawu la abe miawo ke ene. Eya míesaa vɔ na tso esime Asiria-fia Asar-Xadon kplɔ mí va afi siae.”

english_verse: But Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the family leaders answered, “You cannot take part in building a temple for the Lord our God! We will build it ourselves, just as King Cyrus of Persia commanded us.”
translation_verse: Ke Zerubabel, Yesua kple Israel-ƒomeawo ƒe tatɔ mamlɛawo ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Mímalɔ̃, mí kpakple miawo míatu xɔ na míaƒe Mawu la o. Míawo ɖeɖe míatui na Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la abe ale si Persia-fia Kores ɖoe na mí la ene.”

english_verse: Then the neighboring people began to do everything possible to frighten the Jews and to make them stop building.
translation_verse: Tete anyigba la dzi nɔlawo ɖe dzi le Yudatɔwo ƒo, eye wodo vɔvɔ̃ na wo le xɔa tutu me.

english_verse: During the time that Cyrus was king and even until Darius became king, they kept bribing government officials to slow down the work. Trouble Rebuilding Jerusalem
translation_verse: Wona zãnu amegã siwo le Persia-fia ŋu la be woagblẽ ɖoɖo si wowɔ la me. Wowɔ esia le Persia-fia Kores ƒe dziɖuɣi katã va ɖo Persia-fia Dario ŋɔli. Amewo tsi tre ɖe gbedoxɔ la gbugbɔtudɔ ŋu le Yerusalem

english_verse: In the first year that Xerxes was king, the neighboring people brought written charges against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Esi Persia-fia Axasweros va zia dzi teti la, woŋlɔ agbalẽ tsɔ tso Yudatɔwo kple Yerusalemnɔlawo nu nɛ.

english_verse: Later, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their advisors got together and wrote a letter to Artaxerxes when he was king of Persia. It was written in Aramaic and had to be translated.
