translation_verse: Nenema ke le Artaxsasta ŋɔli hã la, Bislam, Mitredat, Tabeel kple wo tɔwo ŋlɔ agbalẽ na fia la. Woŋlɔe kple Aram ŋɔŋlɔdzesiwo, ɖe Aram-gbe me.

english_verse: This letter said: Your Majesty King Artaxerxes, we are your servants from everywhere in Western Province, and we send you our greetings.
translation_verse: agbalẽ si woɖo ɖa la nye esi: “Na Fia Artaxsasta: Wò dɔla Tɔgodo Nutometɔwo do gbe na wò. Azɔ

english_verse: You should know that the Jews who left your country have moved back to Jerusalem and are now rebuilding that rebellious city. In fact, they have almost finished rebuilding the walls and repairing the foundations.
translation_verse: míele nyanya nam wò be Yudatɔ siwo tso gbɔwò va mía gbɔ le afii la yi Yerusalem. Wogbugbɔ du vɔ̃ɖi dzeaglã ma le tsotsom. Wole gliawo nu flɔm, eye wole gɔmeɖoɖoa hã dzram ɖo.

english_verse: You should also know that if the walls are completed and the city is rebuilt, the Jews won't pay any kind of taxes, and there will be less money in your treasury.
translation_verse: Azɔ míedi be fia nanya be ne wogbugbɔ du sia tso, gaɖo gliawo woflɔ la, emenɔlawo agbe nudzɔdzɔ, adzɔ kple mɔtaho xexe eye fia ƒe gakpɔkpɔ dzi aɖe kpɔtɔ.

english_verse: We are telling you this, because you have done so much for us, and we want everyone to respect you.
translation_verse: Esi wònye fiasã la mee míaƒe nuɖuɖu tsona, eye medze be bubu naklo le fia ŋu míakpɔ o ta la, míele ame ɖom ɖa be

english_verse: If you look up the official records of your ancestors, you will find that Jerusalem has constantly rebelled and has led others to rebel against kings and provinces. That's why the city was destroyed in the first place.
translation_verse: nàna woadzro tɔ́wòwo ƒe agbalẽ siwo woŋlɔ da ɖi la me. Àke ɖe eŋu le nuŋlɔɖiawo me be du sia la, du dzeaglã si ɖea fu na fiawo kple nutomedzikpɔlawo wònye tso gbe aɖe gbe ke. Tso tititi ke ko la, du ma dzea aglã ɖe dziɖuɖu ŋu. Esia tae wogbã du sia ɖo.

english_verse: If Jerusalem is rebuilt and its walls completed, you will no longer have control over Western Province.
translation_verse: Míedi be míana fia nanya be, ne wogbugbɔ du sia tso, eye wogaɖo eƒe gliwo yi dzi woflɔ la, gome aɖeke maganɔ asiwò le Tɔgodo Nutome ƒe akpa aɖeke o.”

english_verse: King Artaxerxes answered: Greetings to Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and to your advisors in Samaria and other parts of Western Province.
translation_verse: Fia ɖo agbalẽa ŋu be: “Na Rexum, fiateƒenɔla kple Simsai, agbalẽŋlɔla, wo tɔ mamlɛa siwo le Samaria kple Tɔgodo Nutome ƒe akpa bubuwo, medo gbe na mi. Azɔ

english_verse: After your letter was translated and read to me,
translation_verse: woxlẽ agbalẽ si mieɖo ɖe mí la nam.

english_verse: I had the old records checked. It is true that for years Jerusalem has rebelled and caused trouble for other kings and nations.
translation_verse: Eya ta meɖe gbe be woadzro nuŋlɔɖiawo me tsitotsito. Wova ke ɖe eŋu be du sia tsia tre ɖe fiawo ŋu tso gbe aɖe gbe ke; emenɔlawo nye ame dzeaglã siwo hea ʋunyaʋunya kple zitɔtɔ vɛ zi geɖe.

english_verse: And powerful kings have ruled Western Province from Jerusalem and have collected all kinds of taxes.
translation_verse: Fia triakɔwo nɔ Yerusalem va yi. Woawoe ɖu Tɔgodo Nutome bliboa dzi, eye woawoe woxea nudzɔdzɔ, adzɔ kple mɔtaho na.

english_verse: I want you to command the people to stop rebuilding the city until I give further notice.
translation_verse: Eya ta mide se be ame siawo nadzudzɔ dɔa. Womagbugbɔ dua atso o va se ɖe esime mawɔ se yeye.

english_verse: Do this at once, so that no harm will come to the kingdom.
translation_verse: Gawu la, migawɔ alɔgblɔdɔ le nya sia me kura o. Ale ke nu agblẽ ʋuu ava lɔ fia la?”

english_verse: As soon as this letter was read, Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and their advisors went to Jerusalem and forced everyone to stop rebuilding the city. Work on the Temple Starts Again
translation_verse: Esi woxlẽ Fia Artaxsasta ƒe agbalẽa na Rexum kple agbalẽŋlɔla Simsai kpakple wo tɔwo la, wotso kpla ti Yudatɔwo yi Yerusalem ɖazi wo dzi kple sesẽ, eye wodzudzɔ dɔa. Wogayi Gbedoxɔa Gbugbɔtudɔ la dzi

english_verse: The Jews were forced to stop work on the temple and were not able to do any more building until the year after Darius became king of Persia.
translation_verse: Tete Mawu ƒe xɔdɔ si wɔm wole le Yerusalem la tɔ, hetsi nenema va se ɖe Persia-fia Dario ƒe fiaɖuɣi ƒe ƒè evelia me.

english_verse: Then the Lord God of Israel told the prophets Haggai and Zechariah to speak in his name to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. And they did.
translation_verse: Azɔ eva eme be gbeƒãɖelawo Xagai kple Zaxarya, Ido vi, de asi gbeƒãɖeɖe me na Yudatɔ siwo le Yuda kple Yerusalem le Israel ƒe Mawu si le wo dzi la ŋkɔ me.

english_verse: So Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the priest urged the people to start working on the temple again, and God's prophets encouraged them.
translation_verse: Tete Zerubabel, Sealtiel vi kple Yesua, Yozadak vi tso gayi Mawu ƒe aƒe la gbugbɔtudɔ dzi le Yerusalem, eye Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo hã va le kpekpem ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: Governor Tattenai of Western Province and his assistant Shethar Bozenai got together with some of their officials. Then they went to Jerusalem and said to the people, “Who told you to rebuild this temple?
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, Tatenai, ame si nye Tɔgodo Nutoa me ƒe mɔ́mefia kple Setar-Bozenai kpakple wo tɔ aɖewo va wo gbɔ be: “Ame kae na ŋusẽ mi be mitu xɔ sia, eye miadzrae ɖo?”

english_verse: Give us the names of the workers!”
translation_verse: Wobia wo hã be: “Xɔa tulawo ŋkɔwo ɖe?”

english_verse: But God was looking after the Jewish leaders. So the governor and his group decided not to make the people stop working on the temple until they could report to Darius and get his advice.
translation_verse: Ke Yudatɔwo ƒe Mawua ɖi na woƒe ame tsitsiawo be womezi wo dzi be woadzudzɔ dɔa ne yewoadɔ ame ɖe Dario, wòaŋlɔ agbalẽ aɖo biabiawo ŋu gbɔ, hafi woagayi dɔa dzi o.

english_verse: Governor Tattenai, Shethar Bozenai, and their advisors sent a report to Darius,
translation_verse: Agbalẽ si Tɔgodo Nutomedziɖula Tatenai kple Setar-Bozenai kpakple wo tɔ Tɔgodo Dziɖuɖudɔwɔlagã bubuawo ŋlɔ ɖo ɖe fia Dario nye esi:

english_verse: which said: King Darius, we wish you the best!
translation_verse: Enye nutsogbalẽ si me nyawoe nye: “Ŋutifafa blibo na fia Dario!

english_verse: We went to Judah, where the temple of the great God is being built with huge stones and wooden beams set in the walls. Everyone is working hard, and the building is going up quickly.
translation_verse: Míele nyanya nam fia be míede Yuda Nutome ɖakpɔ Mawu gã la ƒe xɔ la. Wole etum kple kpe gãwo, eye wode ati titriwo gliawo me. Wole dɔa dzi kple beléle tɔxɛ, eye wòle afɔ tsɔm ŋutɔ.

english_verse: We asked those in charge to tell us who gave them permission to rebuild the temple.
translation_verse: Míeɖo dze kple ame tsitsi siwo le dɔa nu. Míebia wo be: ‘Ame kae na ŋusẽ mi be miatu xɔ sia, eye miadzrae ɖo?’

english_verse: We also asked for the names of their leaders, so that we could write them down for you.
translation_verse: Míebia woƒe ŋkɔwo hã, be míate ŋu aŋlɔ ame siwo wonye la ŋkɔwo aɖo ɖe wò.

english_verse: They claimed to be servants of the God who rules heaven and earth. And they said they were rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago by one of Israel's greatest kings.
translation_verse: Ŋuɖoɖo si wona mí lae nye be: ‘Dziƒo kple anyigba ƒe Mawu la ƒe dɔlawo míenye, eye míele xɔ sia, si Israel-fia gã aɖe tu wu nu keŋkeŋ gbe aɖe gbe ʋĩi la gbugbɔ tum.

english_verse: We were told that their people had made God angry, and he let them be captured by Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian king who took them away as captives to Babylonia. Nebuchadnezzar tore down their temple,
translation_verse: Ke esi mía tɔgbuiwo do dɔmedzoe na dziƒo Mawu la ta la, etsɔ wo de asi na Babilonia-fia Nebukadnezar, Kaldeatɔ la, ame si gbã xɔ sia, eye wòɖe aboyo dukɔ la yi Babilonia.

english_verse: Sheshbazzar then went to Jerusalem and laid the foundation for the temple, and the work is still going on.
translation_verse: Sesbazar sia va ɖo Mawuƒe la gɔme anyi ɖe Yerusalem, eye tso ɣe ma ɣi va se ɖe fifia la, wole etutu dzi. Womewu enu haɖe o.’

english_verse: Your Majesty, please order someone to look up the old records in Babylonia and find out if King Cyrus really did give orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem. We will do whatever you think we should.
translation_verse: Eya ta ne fia lɔ̃ la, nena woadzro agbalẽ xoxo siwo le fiaƒeme le Babilonia la me akpɔ ɖa be nyateƒe fia Kores ɖe gbe be woagbugbɔ Mawu ƒe aƒe sia atu ɖe Yerusalem mahã. Fia nena míanya eƒe didi le nya sia ŋu.”

english_verse: King Darius ordered someone to go through the old records kept in Babylonia.
translation_verse: Tete Dario ɖe gbe eye wotsa agbalẽ xoxo siwo le Babel-dua ƒe nuwo dzraɖoƒe la me.

english_verse: Finally, a scroll was found in Ecbatana, the capital of Media Province, and it said: This official record will show
translation_verse: Ke Ekbatana si nye Media Nutome fiadu la ƒe fiasã mee wova ke ɖe agbalẽ aɖe ŋu le, si me woŋlɔ ɖo be: “Dzesidede:

english_verse: that in the first year Cyrus was king, he gave orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem, so that sacrifices and offerings could be presented there. It is to be built
translation_verse: Le fia Kores ƒe fiaɖuɣi ƒe ƒè gbãtɔ me la, eɖe gbe be: ‘Le Mawu ƒe aƒe si le Yerusalem ƒe nya me la, woagbugbɔ aƒe la atu wòanye teƒe si woasa vɔ le kple afi si woatsɔ numemevɔsawo vɛ la. Eƒe kɔkɔme nanye meta bla eve vɔ adrẽ, eye eƒe kekeme hã nanye meta bla eve vɔ adrẽ.

english_verse: with one row of wooden beams for each three rows of large stones. The royal treasury will pay for everything.
translation_verse: Woatsɔ kpe gãwo aɖo amli etɔ̃, eye amli ɖeka nanye ati. Ga si ŋudɔ woawɔ ɖe dɔ la ŋu la natso fia ƒe gaɖaka me.

english_verse: Then the gold and silver things that Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple and brought to Babylonia are to be returned to their proper places. King Darius Orders the Work To Continue
translation_verse: Gawu la, woagbugbɔ Mawu ƒe xɔ me sika kple klosalonu siwo Nebukadnezar lɔ tso gbedoxɔ si nɔ Yerusalem tsã me va Babilonia la ayi gbedoxɔa me le Yerusalem, eye woatsɔ ɖe sia ɖe aɖo teƒe si wònɔ le Mawu ƒe xɔa me tsã la.’ ” Fia Dario ɖe gbe be woayi dɔa dzi, eye wowu gbedoxɔa nu

english_verse: King Darius sent this message: Governor Tattenai of Western Province and Shethar Bozenai, you and your advisors must stay away from the temple.
translation_verse: Eya ta, tso azɔ dzi la, wò Tatenai Tɔgodo Nutome mɔ́mefia Setar-Bozenai kple mi wo tɔ dziɖuɖuteƒenɔla siwo le Tɔgodo Nutoa me, migayi afi ma o.

english_verse: Let the Jewish governor and leaders rebuild it where it stood before. And stop slowing them down!
translation_verse: Miɖe asi le Mawu ƒe xɔdɔ sia me. Mina Yudatɔwo ƒe mɔ́mefia kple woƒe ame tsitsiwo natu Mawu ƒe xɔ sia ɖe enɔƒe.

english_verse: And don't fail to let the priests in Jerusalem have whatever they need each day so they can offer sacrifices to the God of heaven. Give them young bulls, rams, sheep, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and olive oil.
translation_verse: Nu siwo katã hiã na numemevɔsa na dziƒo Mawu la, eɖanye nyitsuiwo, agbowo alo alẽwo o, eɖanye lu, dze, wain alo ami o, nu sia nu si nunɔla siwo le Yerusalem la hiã la, mina nu siawo naka wo si godoo gbe sia gbe.

english_verse: I want them to be able to offer pleasing sacrifices to God and to pray for me and my family.
translation_verse: Miwɔ esia ne woasa vɔ ʋeʋẽe lílili na dziƒo Mawu la, eye woado gbe ɖa ɖe fia la kple viawo ƒe agbe ta.

english_verse: If any of you don't obey this order, a wooden beam will be taken from your house and sharpened on one end. Then it will be driven through your body, and your house will be torn down and turned into a garbage dump.
translation_verse: Megale gbe ɖem hã be ne ame aɖe trɔ sedede sia la, woaɖe ati titri ɖeka le eƒe xɔ me, eye woatsɔ nenem me ma atrɔ ɖe enu. Eyome woana eƒe aƒe nazu aɖukpo.

english_verse: I ask the God who is worshiped in Jerusalem to destroy any king or nation who tries either to change what I have said or to tear down his temple. I, Darius, give these orders, and I expect them to be followed carefully. The Temple Is Dedicated
translation_verse: Mawu si ɖo eŋkɔ anyi ɖe afi ma la netu asi fia sia fia alo dukɔ sia dukɔ si ate kpɔ be yeatrɔ ɖoɖo sia, alo agbã Mawu ƒe aƒe sia si le Yerusalem la. Nye Dario ye de se sia; ame sia ame nezɔ ɖe enu pɛpɛpɛ.” Wokɔ gbedoxɔ la ŋu

english_verse: With great success the Jewish leaders continued working on the temple, while Haggai and Zechariah encouraged them by their preaching. And so, the temple was completed at the command of the God of Israel and by the orders of kings Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes of Persia.
translation_verse: Yudatɔwo ƒe ame tsitsiwo yi xɔa dzi, wòdze edzi na wo. Gbeƒãɖelawo Xagai kple Zaxarya, Ido vi, ƒe nyagblɔɖiwo do ŋusẽ wo ale be dɔa tsɔ afɔ nyuie. Wowu xɔa tutu nu abe ale si Israel ƒe Mawu ɖo na wo eye Persia-fiawo Kores, Dario kple Artaxsasta hã woɖe gbe na wo be woawɔe la ene.

english_verse: On the third day of the month of Adar in the sixth year of the rule of Darius, the temple was finished.
translation_verse: Wowu xɔ sia nu le ɣleti Adar ƒe ŋkeke etɔ̃lia dzi le fia Dario ƒe ƒè adelia me.

english_verse: The people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned from exile were happy and celebrated as they dedicated God's temple.
translation_verse: Israelviwo, nunɔlawo, Levi viwo kple aboyometsola mamlɛawo tsɔ Mawu ƒe aƒe sia de asi na Mawu kple dzidzɔ.

english_verse: One hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs were offered as sacrifices at the dedication. Also twelve goats were sacrificed as sin offerings for the twelve tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Le Mawu ƒe aƒe sia nuʋuʋu me la, wotsɔ nyitsu alafa ɖeka, agbo alafa eve kple alẽvi alafa ene sa vɔ na Mawu. Wotsɔ gbɔ̃tsu wui eve ɖe Israel ƒe to wui eveawo ƒe xexlẽme nu sa nuvɔ̃vɔe.

english_verse: Then the priests and Levites were assigned their duties in God's temple in Jerusalem, according to the instructions Moses had written. The Passover
translation_verse: Azɔ la, woɖe nunɔlawo ɖe woƒe mamawo nu, eye woma Levi viwo ɖe woƒe hatsotso me hena woƒe mawusubɔsubɔdɔwo le Yerusalem, abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖi ɖe Mose ƒe agbalẽa me ene. Woɖu Paska

english_verse: Everyone who had returned from exile celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
translation_verse: Ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke wui enelia gbe la, aboyometsolaawo ɖu Paska.

english_verse: The priests and Levites had gone through a ceremony to make themselves acceptable to lead in worship. Then some of them killed Passover lambs for those who had returned, including the other priests and themselves.
translation_verse: Nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo kɔ wo ɖokui ŋu ɖekae, eye wo katã ŋu kɔ. Ale wowu Paskalẽvi la na aboyometsolaawo katã kple wo tɔ nunɔlawo kpakple woawo ŋutɔ ɖokui.

english_verse: The sacrifices were eaten by the Israelites who had returned and by the neighboring people who had given up the sinful customs of other nations in order to worship the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ame siwo ɖu nua la woe nye: Israelvi siwo katã gbɔ tso aboyo me kple ame siwo ɖe asi le anyigba la dzi dukɔawo ƒe kɔnu makɔmakɔwo me, eye wova be yewoasubɔ Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la kple aboyometsolaawo la.

english_verse: For seven days they celebrated the Festival of Thin Bread. Everyone was happy because the Lord God of Israel had made sure that the king of Assyria would be kind to them and help them build the temple.
translation_verse: Ale woɖu Amɔwɔ Maʋamaʋã Bolo Ŋkeke Nyui la kple aseyetsotso ŋkeke adrẽ elabe Aƒetɔ do dzidzɔ na wo, eye Aƒetɔ wɔe be Asiria-fia ƒe dɔme trɔ ɖe wo ŋu, ale be wòkpe ɖe wo ŋu le Israel ƒe Mawu la ƒe aƒe la tutu me.

english_verse: Much later, when Artaxerxes was king of Persia, Ezra came to Jerusalem from Babylonia. Ezra was the son of Seraiah and the grandson of Azariah. His other ancestors were Hilkiah, Shallum, Zadok, Ahitub, Amariah, Azariah, Meraioth, Zerahiah, Uzzi, Bukki, Abishua, Phinehas, Eleazar, and Aaron, the high priest. Ezra was an expert in the Law that the Lord God of Israel had given to Moses, and the Lord made sure that the king gave Ezra everything he asked for.
translation_verse: Ezra siae ho tso Babilonia va. Enye agbalẽfiala, eye wòbi ɖe Mose ƒe se si Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la de la me. Fia la na nu siwo katã wòbia lae, elabe Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu ƒe asi le dzi.

english_verse: Other Jews, including priests, Levites, musicians, the temple guards, and servants, came to Jerusalem with Ezra. This happened during the seventh year that Artaxerxes was king.
translation_verse: Israelviwo ƒe ha aɖe, siwo dome nunɔlawo, Levi viwo, hadzilawo, agbonudzɔlawo kple gbedoxɔ me dɔwɔlawo nɔ la hã gbɔ kplii va Yerusalem

english_verse: God helped Ezra, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month of that seventh year, after leaving Babylonia on the first day of the first month.
translation_verse: Ezra dze mɔ tso Babilonia le ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi, eye le ɣleti atɔ̃lia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la, eva ɖo Yerusalem elabe eƒe Mawu ƒe amenuveve nɔ edzi.

english_verse: Ezra was a priest and an expert in the laws and commands that the Lord had given to Israel. One day King Artaxerxes gave Ezra a letter which said:
translation_verse: Agbalẽ si fia Artaxsasta ŋlɔ de asi na nunɔla Ezra ame si nye agbalẽfiala, eye wònya Aƒetɔ ƒe se kple ɖoɖowo na Israel tsitotsito lae nye esi:

english_verse: Greetings from the great King Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest and expert in the teachings of the God of heaven.
translation_verse: “Nye Artaxsasta, fiawo dzi fiae le esia ŋlɔm na nunɔla Ezra si nye dziƒo Mawu la ƒe sefiala. Ŋutifafa na wò!

english_verse: Any of the people of Israel or their priests or Levites in my kingdom may go with you to Jerusalem if they want to. My seven advisors and I agree that you may go to Jerusalem and Judah to find out if the laws of your God are being obeyed.
translation_verse: Elabe nye, fia la ŋutɔ kple nye adaŋudela adrẽawoe dɔ wò ɖa be nàtsɔ wò Mawu ƒe se si le asiwò la adzro Yuda kple Yerusalem ƒe nyawo me akpɔ.

english_verse: When you go, take the silver and gold that I and my advisors are freely giving to the God of Israel, whose temple is in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nàtsɔ klosalo kple sika siwo nye kple nye adaŋudelawo míena faa la ɖana Israel ƒe Mawu si ƒe nɔƒe le Yerusalem la.

english_verse: Take the silver and gold that you collect from everywhere in Babylonia. Also take the gifts that your own people and priests have so willingly contributed for the temple of your God in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nenema ke nàtsɔ klosalo kple sika siwo katã nàkpɔ le Babilonia ƒe nutowo katã me kple nu siwo Israelviwo ŋutɔ kple nunɔlawo ana faa ɖe woƒe Mawu ƒe aƒe si le Yerusalem ŋu la hã yii.

english_verse: Use the money carefully to buy the best bulls, rams, lambs, grain, and wine. Then sacrifice them on the altar at God's temple in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nàtsɔ ga sia ƒle nyitsuwo, agbowo, alẽviwo kple wo ŋu nuɖuɖuvɔsanuwo kple nunonovɔsanuwo kple beléle tɔxɛ, eye nàtsɔ wo sa vɔe le miaƒe Mawu ƒe aƒe si le Yerusalem la ƒe vɔsamlekpui dzi.

english_verse: If any silver or gold is left, you and your people may use it for whatever pleases your God.
translation_verse: Nu sia nu si dze mia kple nɔviwòwo ŋu miebe yewoatsɔ klosalo kple sika awɔe la, miwɔe le mia Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu nu.

english_verse: If you need to get anything else for the temple, you may have the money you need from the royal treasury.
translation_verse: Ne nane gahiã le Mawu ƒe aƒe la ŋu si wòle be nàwɔ la, nàxɔ ga tso fia ƒe gaɖaka me wɔe faa.

english_verse: Ezra, you are a priest and an expert in the laws of the God of heaven, and I order all treasurers in Western Province to do their very best to help you.
translation_verse: “Azɔ nye, fia Artaxsasta meɖe gbe na fia ƒe gadzikpɔla siwo le Tɔgodo Nutome la be nu sia nu si nunɔla Ezra, dziƒo Mawu la ƒe sefiala abia tso mia si la, minae wòade tututu;

english_verse: They must provide whatever the God of heaven demands for his temple, so that he won't be angry with me and with the kings who rule after me.
translation_verse: Nu sia nu si dziƒo Mawu la di be woawɔ le yeƒe xɔa ŋu ko la, miwɔe wòade pɛpɛpɛ. Nu ka ta eƒe dɔmedzoe ava nye fia kple vinyewo ƒe fiaɖuƒe dzi?

english_verse: We want you to know that no priests, Levites, musicians, guards, temple servants, or any other temple workers will have to pay any kind of taxes.
translation_verse: Mele nyanya nam mi hã be ame aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ axɔ nudzɔdzɔ, adzɔ alo mɔtaho le nunɔlawo, Levi viwo, gbedoxɔ me hadzilawo, agbonudzɔlawo, gbedoxɔ me dɔwɔlawo kple Mawu ƒe aƒe sia me subɔla bubu aɖeke si o.

english_verse: Ezra, use the wisdom God has given you and choose officials and leaders to govern the people of Western Province. These leaders should know God's laws and have them taught to anyone who doesn't know them.
translation_verse: “Azɔ wò Ezra, nàɖo kodzoɖilawo kple ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ɖe Mawu ƒe nunya si wòna wò la nu, ne woakplɔ ame siwo katã nya wò Mawu la ƒe seawo le Tɔgodo Nutoa me, eye nàfia sea ame siwo menya wo o la hã.

english_verse: Everyone who fails to obey God's Law or the king's law will be punished without pity. They will either be executed or put in prison or forced to leave their country, or have all they own taken away. Ezra Praises God
translation_verse: Ne ame aɖe gbe be yemawɔ wò Mawu ƒe se kple fia la ƒe se dzi o la, wonehe to si dzee la nɛ. Nenye ɖe woawui, alo anyae dzoe le dukɔa me, alo axɔ eƒe nunɔamesiwo le esi, alo adee gaxɔ me la, woawɔe ɖe eteƒe tututu.” Ezra kafu Mawu

english_verse: Because King Artaxerxes was so kind, Ezra said: Praise the Lord God of our ancestors! He made sure that the king honored the Lord's temple in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ezra gblɔ be: “Mekafu Aƒetɔ, mía tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu, ame si de susu fia ƒe tame be woade bubu Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe si le Yerusalem ŋu,

english_verse: God has told the king, his advisors, and his powerful officials to treat me with kindness. The Lord God has helped me, and I have been able to bring many Jewish leaders back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: eye wòɖe eƒe lɔlɔ̃ gã sinu metsina o la fiam le fia kple eƒe adaŋudelawo kpakple amegã ŋusẽtɔ siwo katã le eŋu la ŋkume. Azɔ dzi ɖo ƒonye elabe Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu ƒe amekplɔsi li kplim. Ale meƒo Israelviwo ƒe kplɔlawo nu ƒu, be woayi kplim.

english_verse: Artaxerxes was king of Persia when I led the following chiefs of the family groups from Babylonia to Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Aƒekɔwo ƒe tatɔ siwo gbɔ kplim tso Babilonia le fia Artaxsasta ƒe dziɖuɣi ŋkɔwo kple dzidzimeŋutinyae nye esi:

english_verse: Gershom of the Phinehas family; Daniel of the Ithamar family; Hattush son of Shecaniah of the David family; Zechariah and
translation_verse: Ame siwo tso Bigevai viŋutsuwo dome la woe nye: Utai kple Zabud, eye ŋutsu bla adrẽ kpe ɖe wo ŋu. Ezra di nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo na gbedoxɔa

english_verse: I said to the priests: You belong to the Lord, the God of your ancestors, and these things also belong to him. The silver and gold were willingly given as gifts to the Lord.
translation_verse: Megblɔ na wo be: “Miele kɔkɔe na Aƒetɔ, eye gbedoxɔ me nuawo hã le kɔkɔe. Klosaloawo kple sikaawo nye lɔlɔ̃nununana faa na Aƒetɔ, mía tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu la.

english_verse: I brought everyone together by the river that flows to the town of Ahava where we camped for three days. Not one Levite could be found among the people and priests.
translation_verse: Meƒo amewo nu ƒu ɖe tɔsisi si tsa yi Axava la nu, eye míeƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe afi ma ŋkeke etɔ̃. Esi melé ŋku ɖe ameawo kple nunɔlawo siaa dome la, nyemekpɔ Levi ƒe viŋutsu aɖeke o.

english_verse: So I sent for the leaders Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam. I also sent for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were very wise counselors.
translation_verse: Eya ta mena woyɔ Eliezer, Ariel, Semaya, Elnatan, Yarib, Elnatan, Natan, Zaxarya kple Mesulam vɛ. Ame siawo nye kplɔlawo. Megana woyɔ Yoarib kple Elnatan, ame siwo nye nugɔmeselawo la,

english_verse: Then I sent them to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia, and I told them to ask him and his temple workers to send people to serve in God's temple.
translation_verse: eye medɔ wo ɖe Ido si nye tatɔ le du si woyɔna be Kasifya me la gbɔ. Mebe woagblɔ na Ido kple nɔviawo be woaɖo gbedoxɔ me subɔlawo ɖe mí ne woawɔ dɔ le mía Mawu ƒe aƒe la me.

english_verse: God was kind to us and caused them to send a skillful man named Sherebiah, who was a Levite from the family of Mahli. Eighteen of his relatives came with him.
translation_verse: Esi mía Mawu ƒe asi nyui le mía ŋu ta la, wokplɔ ŋutsu ɖɔŋuɖo aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Serebya kple viawo kpakple eƒe ƒometɔwo vɛ na mí. Wo katã le ame wui enyi. Serebya nye Mahli, Levi vi si nye Israel viŋutsu la, ƒe dzidzimevi.

english_verse: We were also sent Hashabiah and Jeshaiah from the family of Merari along with
translation_verse: Woɖo Xasabya kple Yesaya, siwo nye Merari ƒe dzidzimevi kple eƒe ƒometɔwo kpakple wo viŋutsuwo hã ɖa. Wo katã wole ame bla eve.

english_verse: Beside the Ahava River, I asked the people to go without eating and to pray. We humbled ourselves and asked God to bring us and our children safely to Jerusalem with all of our possessions.
translation_verse: Tete meɖe gbeƒã le Ahava-tɔsisia to afi ma be míatsi nu adɔ, agbe nu le mía ɖokui gbɔ le mía Mawu ŋkume, aɖe kuku nɛ be wòakpɔ míawo ŋutɔ, mía viwo kple míaƒe nunɔamesiwo katã ta be mɔ me nakɔ na mí.

english_verse: So we went without food and asked God himself to protect us, and he answered our prayers. The Gifts for the Temple
translation_verse: Ale míetsi nu dɔ, ƒo koko, di mía Mawu le esia ta, eye wòse míaƒe kukuɖeɖe.

english_verse: I chose twelve of the leading priests—Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their relatives.
translation_verse: Azɔ meɖe kpɔ nunɔla vevi wui eve, Serebya kple Xasabya kpakple wo nɔvi bubu ewo,

english_verse: Be sure to guard them and keep them safe until you reach Jerusalem. Then weigh them inside God's temple in the presence of the chief priests, the Levites, and the heads of the Israelite families.
translation_verse: Milé be na wo ne woanɔ dedie va se ɖe esime miagada wo le nunɔlagãwo kple Levi viwo kpakple aƒekɔwo ƒe tatɔwo ŋkume le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ƒe xɔwo me le Yerusalem.”

english_verse: The priests and Levites then took charge of the gifts that had been weighed, so they could take them to the temple of our God in Jerusalem. The Return to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Tete nunɔlawo kple Levi viawo xɔ klosalo, sika kple ŋudɔwɔnu siwo woda la be woatsɔ wo ayi mía Mawu ƒe aƒe la me le Yerusalem. Aboyometsolawo gbɔ va Yerusalem

english_verse: On the twelfth day of the first month, we left the Ahava River and started for Jerusalem. Our God watched over us, and as we traveled along, he kept our enemies from ambushing us.
translation_verse: Azɔ míedze mɔ tso Ahava-tɔsisi la to le ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke wui evelia dzi ɖo ta Yerusalem. Mía Mawu kpɔ mía ta, eye wòɖe mí tso futɔwo kple ame siwo dea xa ɖe mɔ dzi la si me.

english_verse: After arriving in Jerusalem, we rested for three days.
translation_verse: Míeva ɖo Yerusalem, eye míenɔ afi ma ŋkeke etɔ̃.

english_verse: Then on the fourth day we went to God's temple, where the silver, the gold, and the other things were weighed and given to the priest Meremoth son of Uriah. With him were Eleazar son of Phinehas and the two Levites, Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke enea gbe la, woda klosalo, sika kple gbedoxɔ me nuawo le mía Mawu ƒe aƒe la me. Eyome wotsɔ wo de asi na nunɔla Meremot, Uriya vi, nunɔla Eleazar, Pinehas vi nɔ eteƒe, eye Levi vi siwo nye Yozabad, Yesua vi kple Noadya, Binui vi hã kpe ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: Those who had returned from exile offered sacrifices on the altar to the God of Israel. Twelve bulls were offered for all Israel. Ninety-six rams and
translation_verse: Tete aboyometsola siwo gbɔ la sa numemevɔ na Israel ƒe Mawu la. Wona nyitsu wui eve ɖe Israel blibo la nu. Wona agbo bla asieke vɔ ade kple alẽvi bla adrẽ vɔ adrẽ hã. Azɔ wona gbɔ̃tsu wui eve hena nuvɔ̃vɔsa. Nu siawo katã nye numemevɔsa na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: Some of those who had returned took the king's orders to the governors and officials in Western Province. Then the officials did what they could for the people and for the temple of God.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ fia la ƒe gbedeasia na fia ƒe dziɖula gã kple mɔ́mefia siwo le Tɔgodo Nutoa me, eye wodo alɔ dukɔ la kple Mawu ƒe aƒe la.

english_verse: Later the Jewish leaders came to me and said: Many Israelites, including priests and Levites, are living just like the people around them. They are even guilty of some of the horrible sins of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Esi wowɔ nu siawo vɔ megbe la, amegãwo te ɖe ŋunye va gblɔ nam be: “Israelviwo, nunɔlawo kple Levi viwo meɖe wo ɖokui ɖe aga tso anyigbaa dzi dukɔwo, Kanaantɔwo, Xititɔwo, Perizitɔwo, Yebusitɔwo, Amontɔwo, Moabitɔwo, Egiptetɔwo kple Amoritɔwo ƒe ŋunyɔnuwo gbɔ o.

english_verse: Some Israelite men have married foreign women and have let their sons do the same thing. Our own officials and leaders were the first to commit this disgusting sin, and now God's holy people are mixed with foreigners.
translation_verse: Elabe woawo ŋutɔ kple wo viŋutsuwo ɖe srɔ̃ tso dukɔ siawo ƒe nyɔnuwo dome ale be dukɔ kɔkɔe la ƒe ƒome tsaka wo ɖokui kple anyigba la dzi dukɔwo. Israelviwo ƒe amegãwo kple dukplɔlawo koŋ ye le ŋgɔ le nuteƒemawɔmawɔ sia me.”

english_verse: This news made me so angry that I ripped my clothes and tore hair from my head and beard. Then I just sat in shock
translation_verse: Esi mese nya sia la, medze nye awu kple awu ʋlaya, nyɔ nye taɖa kple ge, bɔbɔ nɔ anyi hegbɔdzɔ kple nuxaxa.

english_verse: until the time for the evening sacrifice. Many of our people were greatly concerned and gathered around me, because the God of Israel had warned us to stay away from foreigners. Ezra's Prayer
translation_verse: Tete ame siwo katã dzidzi ƒo le nya siwo Israel ƒe Mawu la gblɔ ɖe aboyometsolaawo ƒe nuteƒemawɔmawɔ ŋu la va ƒo ƒu ɖe ŋunye. Mebɔbɔ nɔ anyi hegbɔdzɔ nenema, va se ɖe fiẽvɔsaɣi.

english_verse: At the time of the evening sacrifice, I was still sitting there in sorrow with my clothes all torn. So I got down on my knees, then lifted my arms,
translation_verse: Le fiẽvɔsaɣi la, metso le nye nuxaxa la me; nye awu kple awu ʋlaya le dzedze ɖe ŋunye nenema. Tete medze klo, kè nye abɔwo me na Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu,

english_verse: and prayed: I am much too ashamed to face you, Lord God. Our sins and our guilt have swept over us like a flood that reaches up to the heavens.
translation_verse: gblɔ be: “O nye Mawu, ŋu le kpeyem ale gbegbe. Esesẽ nam ŋutɔ be mawu mo dzi na wò, nye Mawu, elabe míaƒe vodadawo li kɔ́ gbɔ mía ta ŋu yi; míaƒe fɔɖiɖiwo kɔ ɖatɔ keke dziƒo ke.

english_verse: Since the time of our ancestors, all of us have sinned. That's why we, our kings, and our priests have often been defeated by other kings. They have killed some of us and made slaves of others; they have taken our possessions and made us ashamed, just as we are today.
translation_verse: Tso mía tɔgbuiwo ŋɔli va ɖo egbe la, míeɖi fɔ geɖe, eye le míaƒe vodadawo ta wotsɔ míawo ŋutɔ, míaƒe fiawo kple nunɔlawo de asi na anyigba dzi fiawo, na yi kple aboyoɖeɖe, na haha kple gbɔɖiɖi, abe ale si wògale egbe ene.

english_verse: But for now, Lord God, you have shown great kindness to us. You made us truly happy by letting some of us settle in this sacred place and by helping us in our time of slavery.
translation_verse: Ke le ɣeyiɣi ʋɛ siawo me la, Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu ve mía nu, eye wòsusɔ ame aɖewo ɖi na mí. Ena míekpɔ gome le eƒe nɔƒe kɔkɔe la me, bene mía Mawu nana be míaƒe ŋku dzi nakɔ, eye míakpɔ gbɔdzɔe vie le míaƒe kluvinyenye la me.

english_verse: We are slaves, but you have never turned your back on us. You love us, and because of you, the kings of Persia have helped us. It's as though you have given us new life! You let us rebuild your temple and live safely in Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Elabe kluviwo míenye gake mía Mawu megblẽ mí ɖi le míaƒe kluvinyenye la me o, ke boŋ eɖe eƒe lɔlɔ̃ matrɔmatrɔ la fia mí, eye wòna Persia-fia na agbe ɖo mía me, ne míatu mía Mawu ƒe xɔ la, adzra eƒe aƒedowo ɖo, eye wòagakpɔ mía ta le Yudea kple Yerusalem.

english_verse: Our God, what can we say now? Even after all this, we have disobeyed the commands
translation_verse: “Ke fifia ɖe, mía Mawu, ale ke gblɔ ge míele le nu siawo megbe? Elabe míegblẽ wò seawo ɖi;

english_verse: that were given to us by your servants the prophets. They said the land you are giving us is full of sinful and wicked people, who never stop doing disgusting things.
translation_verse: se siwo nède to wò dɔla gbeƒãɖelawo dzi be: ‘Anyigba si dzi mieva be yewoaxɔ la, anyigba makɔmakɔ wònye le edzinɔlawo ƒe nu makɔmakɔ wɔwɔ kple woƒe ŋunyɔnuwɔwɔ ta. Wotsɔ woƒe nu makɔmakɔ wɔwɔ yɔ anyigba blibo la katã dzi.

english_verse: And we were warned not to let our daughters and sons marry their sons and daughters. Your prophets also told us never to help those foreigners or even let them live in peace. You wanted us to become strong and to enjoy the good things in the land, then someday to leave it to our children forever.
translation_verse: Eya ta migatsɔ mia vinyɔnuwo na wo viŋutsuwo woaɖe o, eye migaɖe wo vinyɔnuwo na mia viŋutsuwo o. Migadi ŋutifafa kple nyui na wo gbeɖe o, bene ŋusẽ naɖo mia ŋu, miaɖu anyigbaa dzi nu nyuitɔwo eye miagblẽ anyigba la ɖi na mia viwo, wòazu woƒe domenyinu tegbee.’

english_verse: You punished us because of our terrible sins. But you did not punish us nearly as much as we deserve, and you have brought some of us back home.
translation_verse: Le nu siwo katã dzɔ ɖe mía dzi le míaƒe nuwɔna vɔ̃ɖiwo kple míaƒe fɔɖiɖi gã la ta megbe la, míekpɔe be wò, mía Mawu, mèhe to na mí ɖe míaƒe dzidadawo nu abe ale si dze la ene o, eye nèna ame siawo susɔ na mí.

english_verse: Why should we disobey your commands again by letting our sons and daughters marry these foreigners who do such disgusting things? That would make you angry enough to destroy us all!
translation_verse: Ðe míagada wò seawo dzi ake, ade asi dukɔ siwo wɔa ŋunyɔnu siawo la me tɔwo ɖeɖe mea? Ðe màdo dziku ɖe mía ŋu ale gbegbe be nàtsrɔ̃ mí keŋkeŋ, ame aɖeke masusɔ alo atsi agbe oa?

english_verse: Lord God of Israel, you have been more than fair by letting a few of us survive. But once again, our sins have made us ashamed to face you.
translation_verse: O Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu, dzɔdzɔetɔ nènye; ke nèɖe mɔ be mí ame siawo míesusɔ fifia. Kpɔ ɖa, mí fɔɖilawo nye esi le ŋkuwò me, ame aɖeke mate ŋu anɔ te le ŋkuwò me le esia ta o.

english_verse: While Ezra was down on his knees in front of God's temple, praying with tears in his eyes and confessing the sins of the people of Israel, a large number of men, women, and children gathered around him and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Esime Ezra do gbe ɖa, ʋu nuvɔ̃ me kple avi le eɖokui xlãm ɖe anyi le Mawu ƒe aƒe la ŋgɔ la, Israel-ŋutsuwo, nyɔnuwo kple ɖeviwo ƒe ha gã aɖe ŋutɔ va ƒo ƒu ɖe eŋu tso Israel, eye woawo hã fa avi hehehe.

english_verse: Shecaniah son of Jehiel from the family of Elam said: Ezra, we have disobeyed God by marrying these foreign women. But there is still hope for the people of Israel,
translation_verse: Tete Sexanya, Yexiel vi si nye Elam ƒe dzidzimeviwo dometɔ ɖeka la ƒo nu na Ezra be: “Míewɔ nuteƒe na Mawu o, be míeɖe dukɔ bubu me nyɔnuwo. Gake fifi gɔ̃ hã la, mɔkpɔkpɔ gali na Israel.

english_verse: if we follow your advice and the advice of others who truly respect the laws of God. We must promise God that we will divorce our foreign wives and send them away, together with their children.
translation_verse: Eya ta mina míabla nu kple mía Mawu be míaɖe asi le mía srɔ̃ siawo katã kple wo viwo ŋu le mía dome. Míawɔ esia abe ale si wò, nye aƒetɔ kple ame siwo me vɔvɔ̃ le wodzona nyànyanya ɖe mía Mawu ƒe sewo ŋu la, miaɖo aɖaŋu na mí la ene. Mina míawɔe ɖe sea nu.

english_verse: Ezra, it's up to you to do something! We will support whatever you do. So be brave!
translation_verse: Tso, elabe wò dɔdeasi ye. Míele megbe na wò; lé dzi ɖe ƒo nàwɔe.”

english_verse: Ezra stood up and made the chief priests, the Levites, and everyone else in Israel swear that they would follow the advice of Shecaniah.
translation_verse: Ezra tso, eye wòna nunɔlawo ƒe amegãwo kple Levi viwo kpakple Israel blibo la katã ka atam be yewoawɔ nya la dzi. Ale woka atam la.

english_verse: Then Ezra left God's temple and went to spend the night in the living quarters of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He felt sorry because of what the people had done, and he did not eat or drink a thing.
translation_verse: Ezra dzo le Mawu ƒe aƒe la ŋgɔ yi Yehohanan, Elyasib vi ƒe xɔ me, eye wòtsi afi ma dɔ. Meɖu nu o, eye meno tsi hã o elabe ele nu xam le aboyometsolaawo ƒe nuteƒemawɔmawɔ ŋuti.

english_verse: The officials and leaders sent a message to all who had returned from Babylonia and were now living in Jerusalem and Judah. This message told them to meet in Jerusalem within three days, or else they would lose everything they owned and would no longer be considered part of the people that had returned from Babylonia.
translation_verse: eye ne ŋkeke etɔ̃ va yi, ame aɖe meva ɖo o la, amegãwo kple ame tsitsiwo naɖe gbe ne woaxɔ eƒe nunɔamesiwo katã le esi, eye woaɖe eyama le aboyometsolaawo ƒe ha me.

english_verse: Three days later, on the twentieth day of the ninth month, everyone from Judah and Benjamin came to Jerusalem and sat in the temple courtyard. It was a serious meeting, and they sat there, trembling in the rain.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke etɔ̃awo me la, ŋutsuwo katã tso Yuda kple Benyamin va kpe ta ɖe Yerusalem. Ɣleti asiekelia ƒe ŋkeke bla eveliae nye takpegbe la. Ameawo katã va bɔbɔ nɔ anyi ɖe gbadzaƒe le Mawu ƒe xɔ la ŋgɔ. Wole dzodzom nyànyanya le nya la kple tsidzadza gã ta.

english_verse: Ezra the priest stood up and said: You have broken God's Law by marrying foreign women, and you have made the whole nation guilty!
translation_verse: Tete nunɔla Ezra tsi tsitre, gblɔ na wo be: “Mieda vo be mieɖe dukɔ bubu me nyɔnuwo, ale miedzi Israel ƒe fɔɖiɖi ɖe edzi.

english_verse: Now you must confess your sins to the Lord God of your ancestors and obey him. Divorce your foreign wives and don't have anything to do with the rest of the foreigners who live around here.
translation_verse: Eya ta azɔ la miʋu miaƒe nuvɔ̃ me na Aƒetɔ, mia tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu la, eye miawɔ eƒe lɔlɔ̃nu. Miklã mia ɖokui ɖa tso anyigba la dzi tɔwo kple mia srɔ̃, dukɔ bubu me nyɔnuawo gbɔ.”

english_verse: Everyone in the crowd shouted: You're right! We will do what you say.
translation_verse: Tete ƒuƒoƒea katã xɔ edzi kple gbe sesẽ be: “Ele eme tututu; ele be míawɔ nu si nègblɔ.

english_verse: But there are so many of us, and we can't just stay out here in this downpour. A lot of us have sinned by marrying foreign women, and the matter can't be settled in only a day or two.
translation_verse: Gake ameawo sɔ gbɔ; tsidzaɣi hãe nye esia, mímate ŋu anɔ ya nu didie o, evɔ nu si wòle be míawɔ la, menye ŋkeke ɖeka alo eve ƒe nya o elabe mía dometɔ siwo nye sedzidalawo le nya sia me la sɔ gbɔ ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Why can't our officials stay on in Jerusalem and take care of this for us? Let everyone who has sinned in this way meet here at a certain time with leaders and judges from their own towns. If we take care of this problem, God will surely stop being so terribly angry with us.
translation_verse: Eya ta mina míaƒe nunɔlawo natsi Yerusalem atrɔ asi le nya sia ŋu ɖe dukɔa nu. Mina dukɔ bubu me nyɔnuɖela siwo le míaƒe duwo me la nava kpɔ nunɔlawo le ɣeyiɣi ɖoɖiwo dzi, eye ne wogbɔna la woava kple du si me wole la ƒe ame tsitsiwo kple eƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo bene dɔmedzoe helihelĩ si mía Mawu do ɖe mía ŋu le nya sia me la nu nafa.”

english_verse: Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah were the only ones who objected, except for the two Levites, Meshullam and Shabbethai.
translation_verse: Amewo katã lɔ̃ ɖe susu sia dzi, negbe Yonatan, Asahel vi kple Yaxzeya, Tikva vi, koe tsi tre ɖe eŋu, eye Mesulam kple Sabetai, ame siwo nye Levi viwo la, hã de wo dzi.

english_verse: Everyone else who had returned from exile agreed with the plan. So Ezra the priest chose men who were heads of the families, and he listed their names. They started looking into the matter on the first day of the tenth month,
translation_verse: Ale aboyometsolaawo wɔ esia. Nunɔla Ezra tia ƒometatɔwo tso aƒekɔ ɖe sia ɖe me heyɔ woƒe ŋkɔwo ɖekaɖeka. Tso ɣleti ewolia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ gbe la, wonɔ anyi be woadzro nya la me.

english_verse: and they did not finish until the first day of the first month of the next year. The Men Who Had Foreign Wives
translation_verse: Le ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔa dzi la, wowu ŋutsu siwo katã ɖe dukɔ bubuwo me nyɔnuwo la ƒe nya nu. Ŋutsu siwo ɖe srɔ̃ tso dukɔ bubuwo me

english_verse: Here is a list of the priests who had agreed to divorce their foreign wives and to sacrifice a ram as a sin offering: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah from the family of Joshua son of Jozadak and his brothers;
translation_verse: Woɖe adzɔgbe be yewoaɖe asi le yewo srɔ̃awo ŋu, eye yewoana agbo ɖeka woatsɔ sa fɔɖivɔ ɖe yewoƒe fɔɖiɖi la ta.

english_verse: Hanani and Zebadiah from the family of Immer;
translation_verse: Esiwo tso Imer viŋutsuwo dome: Xanani kple Zebadya.

english_verse: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah from the family of Harim;
translation_verse: Esiwo tso Xarim viŋutsuwo dome: Maaseya, Eliya, Semaya, Yexiel kple Uziya.

english_verse: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah from the family of Pashhur.
translation_verse: Esiwo tso Pasxur viŋutsuwo dome: Elyoenai, Maaseya, Ismael, Netaneel, Yozabad kple Eleasa.

english_verse: Those Levites who had foreign wives were: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah , Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
translation_verse: Esiwo tso Levi viŋutsuwo dome: Yozabad, Simei, Kelaya, si woyɔna hã be Kelita, Petaxya, Yuda kple Eliezer.

english_verse: Eliashib, the musician, had a foreign wife. These temple guards had foreign wives: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
translation_verse: Esi tso hadzilawo dome Elyasib. Esiwo tso agbonudzɔlawo dome: Salum, Telem kple Uri.

english_verse: Here is a list of the others from Israel who had foreign wives: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Hashabiah, and Benaiah from the family of Parosh;
translation_verse: Esiwo tso Israel: Esiwo tso Pareos viŋutsuwo dome: Ramya, Yizia, Malkiya, Miyamin, Eleazar, Malkiya kple Benaya.

english_verse: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah from the family of Elam;
translation_verse: Esiwo tso Elam viŋutsuwo dome: Matanya, Zaxarya, Yexiel. Abdi, Yeremot kple Eliya.

english_verse: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza from the family of Zattu;
translation_verse: Esiwo tso Zatu viŋutsuwo dome: Elyoenai, Elyasib, Matanya, Yeremot, Zabad kple Aziza.

english_verse: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai from the family of Bebai;
translation_verse: Esiwo tso Bebai viŋutsuwo dome: Yehohanan, Xananya, Zabai kple Atlai.

english_verse: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth from the family of Bani;
translation_verse: Esiwo tso Bani viŋutsuwo dome: Mesulam, Malux, Adaya, Yasub, Seal kple Yeramot.

english_verse: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh from the family of Pahath Moab;
translation_verse: Esiwo tso Paxat-Moab viŋutsuwo dome: Adna, Xelal, Benaya, Maaseya, Matanya, Bezaleel, Binui kple Manase.

english_verse: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei from the family of Hashum;
translation_verse: Esiwo tso Xasum viŋutsuwo dome: Matenai, Matata, Zabad, Elifelet, Yeremai, Manase kple Simei.

english_verse: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah from the family of Nebo.
translation_verse: Esiwo tso Nebo viŋutsuwo dome: Yeiel, Matitya, Zabad, Zebina, Yadai, Yoel kple Benaya.

english_verse: These men divorced their foreign wives, then sent them and their children away.
translation_verse: Ame siawo katã ɖe nyɔnuwo tso dukɔ bubuwo me, eye nyɔnuawo dometɔ aɖewo dzi viwo. Woɖe asi le nyɔnuawo kple wo viwo ŋu.

english_verse: I am Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, and in this book I tell what I have done. During the month of Chislev in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes ruled Persia, I was in his fortress city of Susa,
translation_verse: Nexemya, Haxalya vi, ƒe nyaxlẽfiae nye esi gbɔna. Nexemya tsi dzi ɖe Yerusalem ŋu Gbe ɖeka le ɣleti Kislev me le Persia-fia Artaxsasta ƒe fiaɖuɣi ƒe ƒè bla evelia me la, menɔ Susa, si nye Persia ƒe fiadu la me.

english_verse: when my brother Hanani came with some men from Judah. So I asked them about the Jews who had escaped from being captives in Babylonia. I also asked them about the city of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Tete Xanani, si nye nɔvinyewo dometɔ ɖeka kple ame bubu aɖewo tso Yuda va. Mebia gbe wo le Yudatɔ siwo womelé yi aboyo me o, ale be woawo susɔ ɖe anyigbaa dzi la ŋu eye mebia nya geɖewo le Yerusalem hã ŋu.

english_verse: They told me, “Those captives who have come back are having all kinds of troubles. They are terribly disgraced, Jerusalem's walls are broken down, and its gates have been burned.”
translation_verse: Wogblɔ nam be: “Yudatɔ siwo susɔ ɖe anyigbaa dzi la ƒe agbenɔnɔ nye fukpekpe gã aɖe kple ŋukpe sɔŋ. Wogbã gli si ƒo xlã Yerusalem ƒe akpa aɖewo eye wotɔ dzo dua ƒe agbowo.”

english_verse: When I heard this, I sat down on the ground and cried. Then for several days, I mourned; I went without eating to show my sorrow, and I prayed:
translation_verse: Esi mese nya siawo la, mebɔbɔ nɔ anyi, fa avi. Mefa konyi ŋkeke geɖe. Menɔ nutsitsidɔ kple gbedodoɖa dzi na dziƒo Mawu la be:

english_verse: Lord God of heaven, you are great and fearsome. And you faithfully keep your promises to everyone who loves you and obeys your commands.
translation_verse: “O, Aƒetɔ, dziƒo Mawu, Mawu gã si ŋu ŋɔdzi le! Wò si, ne èbla nu kple ame, eye nenem me ma lɔ̃a wò hewɔa wò sewo dzi la, èléa nu si nèbla kplii la me ɖe asi sesĩe, eye wò lɔlɔ̃ nɛ nu metsina o!

english_verse: I am your servant, so please have mercy on me and answer the prayer that I make day and night for these people of Israel who serve you. I, my family, and the rest of your people have sinned
translation_verse: Ke to ɖe ŋunye, nàʋu ŋku kpɔm, eye nàse gbe si nye, wò dɔlaŋutsu mele ŋkuwò me azɔ, zã kple keli, hele dodom ɖa na wò, ɖe wò dɔla Israelviwo ta la. Mele mí Israel-dukɔa ƒe nuvɔ̃ siwo míewɔ ɖe ŋuwò la me ʋum na wò. Ẽ, nye ŋutɔ kple tɔgbuinyewo siaa míewɔ nuvɔ̃.

english_verse: by choosing to disobey you and the laws and teachings you gave to your servant Moses.
translation_verse: Míewɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi ɖe ŋuwò; míezɔ ɖe wò se kple ɖoɖo siwo nèwɔ na mí to wò dɔla Mose dzi la nu o.

english_verse: Please remember the promise you made to Moses. You told him that if we were unfaithful, you would scatter us among foreign nations.
translation_verse: Ðo ŋku nya si nègblɔ na wò dɔla Mose la dzi. Ègblɔ nɛ be: ‘Ne miewɔ nye sewo dzi, eye miezɔ ɖe nye ɖoɖowo nu o la, maka mi ahlẽ ɖe dukɔwo dome.

english_verse: But you also said that no matter how far away we were, we could turn to you and start obeying your laws. Then you would bring us back to the place where you have chosen to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Gake ne miegatrɔ ɖe ŋunye, lé nye sewo me ɖe asi, eye miezɔ ɖe wo nu pɛpɛpɛ la, ekema nenye anyigba ƒe seƒewo ke woɖe aboyo mi yii le dziƒoa te hã, maƒo mia nu ƒu tso afi mawo katã akplɔ va teƒe si metia be nye ŋkɔ nanɔ ɖaa la’.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am praying for your servants—those you rescued by your great strength and mighty power.
translation_verse: Wò dɔlawo wonye, wò dukɔ wonye; ame siwo nèxɔ ɖe agbe kple wò ŋusẽ triakɔ la kpakple wò kalẽsi lae wonye.

english_verse: Please answer my prayer and the prayer of your other servants who gladly honor your name. When I serve the king his wine today, make him pleased with me and let him do what I ask.
translation_verse: O, Aƒetɔ, se nye gbedodoɖa sia nam dzro. Ƒu to anyi ɖe wò dɔla bubu siwo bubudede wò ŋkɔ ŋu doa dzidzɔ na la hã ƒe kokoƒoƒo ŋu. Na makpɔ dzidzedze egbe sia dzro; na ŋutsu sia nave nunye.” Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, fia ƒe ahakula menye.

english_verse: During the month of Nisan in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king, I served him his wine, as I had done before. But this was the first time I had ever looked depressed.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka le ɣleti Nisan me, le fia Artaxsasta ƒe fiaɖuɣi ƒe ƒè bla evelia me la, meku aha na fia la esime wònɔ nu ɖum. Mekpɔm melé blanui le eŋkume kpɔ o.

english_verse: So the king said, “Why do you look so sad? You're not sick. Something must be bothering you.” Even though I was frightened,
translation_verse: Fia la biam be: “Nya kae dzɔ nètsi kpoo ale? Mekpɔ be wò lã me megblẽ o ɖe! Menye nanekee o; nu xam nèle le dzime.” Tete mevɔ̃ ŋutɔ.

english_verse: I answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! I feel sad because the city where my ancestors are buried is in ruins, and its gates have been burned down.”
translation_verse: Megblɔ na fia la be: “Fia nenɔ agbe tegbee! Nye Aƒetɔ, mese be mía de, du si me woɖi tɔgbuinyewo ɖo la, zu aƒedo hetsi nuvo, elabe dzo bi eƒe agbowo. Ale ke wɔ nyemalé blanui o?”

english_verse: The king asked, “What do you want me to do?” I prayed to the God who rules from heaven.
translation_verse: Fia la biam be: “Nu ka nàdi be mawɔ na ye?” Medo gbe ɖa le tame na dziƒo Mawu la,

english_verse: Then I told the king, “Sir, if it's all right with you, please send me back to Judah, so that I can rebuild the city where my ancestors are buried.”
translation_verse: eye megblɔ na fiaa be: “Ne edze ŋuwò, Fia Bubutɔ, be yeave nye wò dɔla nu la, ekema ɖe mɔ nam ne mayi Yuda, ne magbugbɔ du si nye tɔgbuinyewo ƒe ɖiƒe, afi si woƒe yɔdowo le la, atso.”

english_verse: The queen was sitting beside the king when he asked me, “How long will it take, and when will you be back?” The king agreed to let me go, and I told him when I would return.
translation_verse: Tete fiaa lɔ̃ be mayi. Srɔ̃a nɔ exa. Ebiam be: “Ŋkeke nenie nàtsɔ zɔ mɔ lae? Ne èyi ɖe, ɣe ka ɣi nàtrɔ gbɔ?” Ale edze fia la ŋu be yeaɖom ɖa. Meɖo ŋkeke nɛ.

english_verse: Then I asked, “Your Majesty, would you be willing to give me letters to the governors of the provinces west of the Euphrates River, so that I can travel safely to Judah?
translation_verse: Megagblɔ be: “Meɖe kuku, fia, na be woaŋlɔ agbalẽ de asinye matsɔ yi na mɔ́mefia siwo le Frat-tɔsisi ƒe ɣetoɖoƒe nutome be woaɖe mɔ nam mato woƒe anyigba me ayi Yuda.

english_verse: I will need timber to rebuild the gates of the fortress near the temple and more timber to construct the city wall and to build a place for me to live. And so, I would appreciate a letter to Asaph, who is in charge of the royal forest.” God was good to me, and the king did everything I asked.
translation_verse: Megaɖe kuku be maxɔ agbalẽ yi na fia ƒe avedzikpɔla, Asaf, hã be wòana atim ne matso akpa agbowo na mɔ́ si le gbedoxɔa ŋu kple dua ƒe gliwo kpakple aƒe si me nɔ ge mala la.” Fia la lɔ̃ wɔ nye biabiaawo katã dzi nam elabe nye Mawu ƒe asi nyui nɔ dzinye.

english_verse: The king sent some army officers and cavalry troops along with me, and as I traveled through the Western Provinces, I gave the letters to the governors.
translation_verse: Fiaa ɖe asrafomegã aɖewo kple sɔdzisrafo aɖewo kpe ɖe ŋunye. Tete medze mɔ. Meva ɖo Tɔgodo Nutome mɔ́mefiawo gbɔ, eye metsɔ fia ƒe agbalẽawo na wo.

english_verse: But when Sanballat from Horon and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about what had happened, they became very angry, because they didn't want anyone to help the people of Israel. Nehemiah Inspects the Wall of Jerusalem
translation_verse: Esi Sanebalat, Xorontɔ la kple eƒe kpeɖeŋutɔ Tobiya, si nye Amontɔ, se be meva ɖo la, eku dzi na wo ŋutɔ be ame aɖe va be yeawɔ nyui na Israelviwo.

english_verse: Three days after arriving in Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Meva ɖo Yerusalem, eye menɔ anyi ŋkeke etɔ̃ sɔŋ

english_verse: I got up during the night and left my house. I took some men with me, without telling anyone what I thought God wanted me to do for the city. The only animal I took was the donkey I rode on.
translation_verse: gake nyemekɔ nu le nu si Mawu nyɔ le menye be mawɔ na Yerusalem la dzi na ame aɖeke o. Le ŋkeke etɔ̃lia ƒe zã me la, mefɔ, kplɔ ŋutsu eve aɖewo ɖe asi, eye míedo go. Tedzi si dom menɔ la koe nye lã nɔ mía ŋu.

english_verse: I went through Valley Gate on the west, then south past Dragon Spring, before coming to Garbage Gate. As I rode along, I took a good look at the crumbled walls of the city and the gates that had been torn down and burned.
translation_verse: Meto Balimegbo nu va do ɖe Lovudo gbɔ, yi dzi ɖado ɖe Akɔligbo gbɔ. Le nye tsaɖiɖia me la, melé ŋku ɖe Yerusalem-gliawo ƒe afi siwo gbã kple dua ƒe agbo siwo dzo fiã la ŋu.

english_verse: On the east side of the city, I headed north to Fountain Gate and King's Pool, but then the trail became too narrow for my donkey.
translation_verse: Meto ŋgɔ ɖado ɖe Vudogbo kple Fia ƒe tá gbɔ; ke teƒe aɖeke megale glikpoawo dome si nye tedzi la ate ŋu ato o.

english_verse: So I went down to Kidron Valley and looked at the wall from there. Then before daylight I returned to the city through Valley Gate.
translation_verse: Eya ta meto bali la me le vivitia me, ganɔ ŋku lém ɖe nuwo ŋu ko. Tete metrɔ azɔ gagbugbɔ yi ɖato Balimegbo nu eye mege ɖe dua me.

english_verse: None of the city officials knew what I had in mind. And I had not even told any of the Jews—not the priests, the leaders, the officials, or any other Jews who would be helping in the work.
translation_verse: Amegã siwo nɔ dua nu la menya kura be mede afi aɖeke o elabe va se ɖe ɣe ma ɣi la, nyemegblɔ nya aɖeke na Yudatɔwo, nunɔlawo, bubumewo, dua dzikpɔlawo kple ame bubu siwo le dɔa wɔ ge la ƒe ɖeke haɖe o.

english_verse: But when I got back, I said to them, “Jerusalem is truly in a mess! The gates have been torn down and burned, and everything is in ruins. We must rebuild the city wall so that we can again take pride in our city.”
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la, megblɔ na wo be: “Miekpɔ ale si gbegbe míele dzɔgbevɔ̃e me, be Yerusalem zu aƒedo eye dzo bi eƒe agbowo la ɖa. Mina míagbugbɔ Yerusalem-gliwo aɖo be ŋukpe gã si me míele fifia la naklo ɖa.”

english_verse: When Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem the Arab heard about our plans, they started insulting us and saying, “Just look at you! Do you plan to rebuild the walls of the city and rebel against the king?”
translation_verse: Esi Sanebalat, Xorontɔ la, Tobiya kple Arabia-ŋutsu aɖe si woyɔna be Gesem se nyaa la, woko mí, ɖu fewu le mía ŋu. Wobia mí be: “Nu ka wònye wɔm miele? Ðe miedi be yewoadze aglã ɖe fia ŋua?”

english_verse: I answered, “We are servants of the God who rules from heaven, and he will make our work succeed. So we will start rebuilding Jerusalem, but you have no right to any of its property, because you have had no part in its history.”
translation_verse: Meɖo eŋu na wo be: “Dziƒo Mawu la ana dɔa adze dzi na mí. Mí eƒe dɔlawo míatso ziã aɖo glia. Ke miawo la, naneke mele Yerusalem-du sia me fifia si miate ŋu atɔ asi akɔ be enye yewo tɔ o, eye naneke meli woatsɔ aɖo ŋku mia dzi o.”

english_verse: These are the people who helped rebuild the wall and gates of Jerusalem: The high priest Eliashib and the other priests rebuilt Sheep Gate and hung its doors. Then they dedicated Sheep Gate and the section of the wall as far as Hundred Tower and Hananel Tower.
translation_verse: Elyasib, nunɔlagã la kple wo tɔ nunɔla bubuawo tso dze dɔa dzi. Wotu Alẽgbo ƒe mɔnu la, kɔ eŋu eye wode ʋɔtruwo enu. Eyome wokɔ glia ŋu va ɖo Xɔ Tsrala Alafa gbɔ, eye woyi edzi va se ɖe Xɔ Tsrala Xananel gbɔ.

english_verse: The people of Jericho rebuilt the next section of the wall, and Zaccur son of Imri rebuilt the section after that.
translation_verse: Yerixo-ŋutsuwo ɖo glia ƒe akpa si kplɔe ɖo la, eye Sakur, Imri vi, ɖo akpa si kplɔ Yerixo-ŋutsuawo tɔ ɖo la.

english_verse: Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, completed the next section of the wall. Meshullam, son of Berechiah and grandson of Meshezabel, rebuilt the next section, and Zadok son of Baana rebuilt the section beside that.
translation_verse: Ame si dzra glia ƒe akpa si kplɔe ɖo la ŋu ɖo lae nye Meremot, Uriya vi, Hakoz ƒe tɔgbuiyɔvi. Ame si dzra akpa si va ɖe Meremot tɔ yome ɖo lae nye Mesulam, Mesezabeel vi, Berexya ƒe tɔgbuiyɔvi. Zadok, Baana vie dzra akpa si kplɔe ɖo la ɖo.

english_verse: The next section was to be repaired by the men of Tekoa, but their town leaders refused to do the hard work they were assigned.
translation_verse: Tekoatɔwo dzra glia ƒe akpa si kplɔe ɖo la. Ke Tekoatɔwo ƒe bubumewo ya gbe, womede asi woƒe aƒetɔ ƒe dɔ la me o.

english_verse: Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah restored Ancient Gate. They put the beams in place, hung the doors, and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
translation_verse: Yoyada, Peseax vi kple Mesulam, Besodya vi, nye ame siwo dzra Agbo Xoxo la ɖo: woawoe ɖi ʋɔtrutiawo, de ʋɔtruawo wo ŋu, eye wode ʋɔtruŋugawo kple ʋɔmedetiwo teƒe siwo wòle be woanɔ la.

english_verse: Melatiah from Gibeon, Jadon from Meronoth, and the men from Gibeon and Mizpah rebuilt the next section of the wall. This section reached as far as the house of the governor of West Euphrates Province.
translation_verse: Ame siwo dzra glia ƒe akpa si gakplɔe ɖo lae nye Melatya, Gibeontɔ la kple Mizpatɔ bubu siwo nɔ Tɔgodo Nutomedzikpɔla ƒe dziɖuɖu te.

english_verse: Uzziel son of Harhaiah the goldsmith rebuilt the next section. Hananiah the perfume maker rebuilt the section next after that, and it went as far as Broad Wall.
translation_verse: Uziel, Xarhaya vi, si nye sikanutula lae dzra akpa si kplɔ Melatya tɔ la ɖo. Xananya si nye ami ʋeʋẽe ɖala lae dzra akpa si va ɖe esia yome la ɖo va se ɖe Gli Gbadza la nu.

english_verse: Rephaiah son of Hur ruled half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall.
translation_verse: Refaya, Xur vi, si nye mɔ́mefia le Yerusalem-nutome ƒe afã nu lae dzra glia ƒe akpa si gava ɖe esia yome la ɖo.

english_verse: The section after that was close to the home of Jedaiah son of Harumaph, and he rebuilt it. Hattush son of Hashabneiah constructed the next section of the wall.
translation_verse: Yedaya, Harumaf vi dzra akpa si gakplɔe ɖo la ɖo. Akpa sia dze ŋgɔ eƒe aƒe. Xatus, Xasbneya vie dzra akpa si va ɖe esia yome la ɖo.

english_verse: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath Moab rebuilt the section after that, and they also built Oven Tower.
translation_verse: Milkiya, Xarim vi kple Xasub Paxat, Moab vi nye ame siwo dzra glia ƒe akpa si kplɔe ɖo la ɖo. Woawo kee dzra Dzokpowo ƒe Xɔ Tsrala la ɖo.

english_verse: Shallum son of Hallohesh ruled the other half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. Shallum's daughters also worked with him.
translation_verse: Salum, Xaloxes vi, si nye Yerusalem-nutome ƒe afã evelia dzikpɔla lae dzra glia ƒe akpa si gakplɔe ɖo la ɖo. Via nyɔnuwo kpe ɖe eŋu le dɔa wɔwɔ me.

english_verse: Hanun and the people who lived in the town of Zanoah rebuilt Valley Gate. They hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. They also rebuilt the wall for
translation_verse: Xanun kple Zanoaxtɔwoe dzra Balimegboa ɖo: wogbugbɔe ɖo, de ʋɔtruawo enu eye wode ʋɔtruŋugaawo kple ʋɔmedetiawo wo nɔƒewo. Eyome wodzra glia ɖo va se ɖe Akɔligboa gbɔ. Akpa si woawo ɖeɖe dzra ɖo la didi meta alafa ene bla ene.

english_verse: Malchijah son of Rechab ruled the district of Beth-Haccherem, and he rebuilt Garbage Gate. He hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
translation_verse: Malkiya, Rexab vi, si nye amegã le Bet Hakerem lae dzra Akɔligbo la ɖo: egbugbɔe ɖo, de agbo enu eye wòde ʋɔtruŋugawo kple ʋɔmedetiwo agboa ŋu.

english_verse: Shallum son of Colhozeh ruled the district of Mizpah, and he rebuilt Fountain Gate. He put a cover over the gateway, then hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. He also rebuilt the wall at Shelah Pool. This section was next to the king's garden and went as far as the stairs leading down from David's City.
translation_verse: Salum, Kol-Xoze vi, ame si nye amegã le Mizpa-nutowo me lae dzra Vudogbo la ɖo. Egbugbɔe tu, gbae abe xɔ ene, de ʋɔtruwo enu, eye wòde ʋɔtruŋugawo kple ʋɔmedetiwo ʋɔtruawo ŋu. Eɖo Selax tá la ƒe gli si le fia ƒe abɔ kple atrakpui si ɖiɖi tso David ƒe du me, dome la.

english_verse: Nehemiah son of Azbuk ruled half of the district of Beth-Zur, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. It went as far as the royal cemetery, the artificial pool, and the army barracks. Levites Who Worked on the Wall
translation_verse: Nexemya, Abzuk vi, si nye amegã le Bet-Zur nutome ƒe afã nu la hã dzra glia ɖo tso Salum tɔ seƒe ʋu keke va ɖo David ƒe yɔdo gbɔ, gatso le afi ma yi do si woku tsɔ wɔ tá la gbɔ, ʋuu keke va do ɖe fia ƒe asrafowo nɔƒe gbɔ. Levi vi siwo wɔ dɔ le glia ŋu

english_verse: The Levites who worked on the next sections of the wall were Rehum son of Bani; Hashabiah, who ruled half of the district of Keilah and did this work for his district;
translation_verse: Le eya yome Levi viwo hã dzra glia ƒe akpa aɖewo ɖo: Rexum, Bani vi, dzra akpa aɖe ɖo; Xosabya, si nye Keila-nutome ƒe afã dzikpɔla la dzra akpa si va ɖe Rexum tɔ yome la ɖo. Ewɔ dɔ sia ɖe eƒe nutome nu.

english_verse: Binnui son of Henadad, who ruled the other half of the district of Keilah;
translation_verse: Bavai, Xenadad vi, si nye Keila-nutome ƒe afã evelia dzikpɔla, dzra akpa si va ɖe Rexum tɔ yome la ɖo.

english_verse: Ezer son of Jeshua, who ruled Mizpah, rebuilt the section of the wall that was in front of the armory and reached to the corner of the wall;
translation_verse: Ame si dzra glia ƒe akpa si va ɖe Bavai tɔ yome ɖo lae nye Eser, Yesua vi, si nye amegã le Mizpa la. Akpa sia dze ŋgɔ togbɛ si lia yi aʋawɔnuxɔ gbɔ. Eƒe seƒee nye glia ƒe dzogoe dzi.

english_verse: Baruch son of Zabbai eagerly rebuilt the section of the wall that went all the way to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest;
translation_verse: Barux, Zabai vi, dzra akpa si va ɖe Eser tɔ yome la ɖo va se ɖe nunɔlagã Elyasib ƒe agbo nu.

english_verse: Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, built up to the far end of Eliashib's house. Priests Who Worked on the Wall
translation_verse: Eya yome Meremot, Uriya vi, Xakoz ƒe tɔgbuiyɔvi, dzra glia ɖo tso Elyasib ƒe aƒe ƒe agbo nu va se ɖe aƒea ƒe nuwuƒe. Nunɔla siwo wɔ dɔ le glia ŋu

english_verse: Here is a list of the priests who worked on the wall: Priests from the region around Jerusalem rebuilt the next section of the wall.
translation_verse: Eyome nunɔla siwo nye ŋutsuwo tso Gbegbe la la dzra akpa si kplɔ Uriya tɔ ɖo la ɖo.

english_verse: Benjamin and Hasshub rebuilt the wall in front of their own houses. Azariah, who was the son of Maaseiah and the grandson of Ananiah, rebuilt the section in front of his house.
translation_verse: Benyamin kple Xasub dzra akpa si kplɔ nunɔlaawo tɔ ɖo la ɖo. Akpa sia dze ŋgɔ Benyamin ƒe aƒe kple Xasub ƒe aƒe. Azarya si nye Maaseya vi kple Ananya ƒe tɔgbuiyɔvi lae dzra akpa si kplɔe ɖo la ɖo. Akpa sia le eƒe aƒe gbɔ.

english_verse: Binnui son of Henadad rebuilt the section of the wall from Azariah's house to the corner of the wall.
translation_verse: Benui, Xenadad vi, dzra akpa si kplɔe ɖo la ɖo. Akpa sia tso Azarya ƒe aƒe gbɔ va se glia ƒe dzogoe dzi.

english_verse: Palal son of Uzai rebuilt the next section, which began at the corner of the wall and the tower of the upper palace near the court of the guard. Pedaiah son of Parosh rebuilt the next section of the wall.
translation_verse: Palal, Uzai vie dzra glia ƒe akpa si le tɔtrɔƒea kple Xɔ Tsrala dzigbemetɔ si le fiasã ŋu le gaxɔ ƒe xɔxɔnu la kasa la ɖo.

english_verse: He stopped at a place near the Water Gate on the east and the tower guarding the temple. This was close to a section in the city called Ophel, where the temple workers lived. Other Builders Who Worked on the Wall
translation_verse: Pedaya, Paros vi kple gbedoxɔ me dɔ gblɔe wɔla siwo nɔ Ofel lae dzra glia ƒe akpa si kplɔe ɖo la ɖo va se ɖe Xɔ Tsrala si do gɔ̃ɔ le Tsigbo la ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome la kasa. Ame bubu siwo hã wɔ dɔ le glia ŋu

english_verse: The men from Tekoa rebuilt the next section of the wall, and it was their second section. It started at a place across from the large tower that guarded the Temple, and it went all the way to the wall near Ophel.
translation_verse: Tekoatɔwoe dzra akpa si va ɖe esia yome la ɖo. Wo tɔ tso Xɔ Tsrala gã si do gɔ̃ɔ la ŋkume va se ɖe Ofel ƒe gli gbɔ.

english_verse: Some priests rebuilt the next section of the wall. They began working north of Horse Gate, and each one worked on a section in front of his own house.
translation_verse: Tso Sɔgbo gbɔ heyi la, nunɔlawo ƒe ha aɖee va dzra glia ɖo. Ðe sia ɖe xɔ akpa si dze ŋgɔ eƒe aƒe la dzra ɖo.

english_verse: Zadok son of Immer rebuilt the wall in front of his house. Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, who looked after the East Gate, rebuilt the section after that.
translation_verse: Zadok, Imer vi, hã dzra akpa si dze ŋgɔ eƒe aƒe ɖo; eya yome Semaya, Sexanya vi, si nye ɣedzeƒegbo nudzɔla la hã dzra akpa aɖe ɖo.

english_verse: Hananiah and Hanun rebuilt the next section, which was the second section for them. Meshullam son of Berechiah rebuilt the next section, which happened to be in front of his house.
translation_verse: Eyome Xananya, Selemya vi, dzra akpa aɖe ɖo eye Xanun, si nye Zalaf vi adelia la dzra akpa si gava ɖe esiawo yome la ɖo. Le eya megbe Mesulam, Berexya vi, dzra akpa si dze ŋgɔ eƒe aƒe ŋkume ɖo.

english_verse: Malchijah, a goldsmith, rebuilt the next section, as far as the house used by the temple workers and merchants. This area was across from Gathering Gate, near the room on top of the wall at the northeast corner.
translation_verse: Sikaɖaŋudɔwɔla Malkiya nye ame si dzra akpa si va ɖe Mesulam tɔ yome la ɖo va se ɖe gbedoxɔ me dɔwɔlawo kple nudzralaawo ƒe aƒe gbɔ, tso Ŋudzɔnɔgbo ƒe sɔsɔme yi dziƒoxɔ si le glia ƒe dzogoe dzi la gbɔ.

english_verse: The goldsmiths and merchants rebuilt the last section of the wall, which went from the corner room all the way to Sheep Gate.
translation_verse: Sikaɖaŋudɔwɔla mamlɛawo kple nudzralawoe dzra glia ƒe akpa mamlɛtɔ ɖo. Akpa sia tso le dziƒoxɔ dzogoedzitɔ gbɔ va se ɖe Alẽgbo la gbɔ.

english_verse: When Sanballat, the governor of Samaria, heard that we were rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, he became angry and started insulting our people.
translation_verse: Esi Sanebalat se be míele glia ɖom la, eku dzi nɛ. Edo dɔmedzoe vevie, eye wòɖe alɔ me le Yudatɔwo ŋu.

english_verse: In front of his friends and the Samaritan army he said, “What is this feeble bunch of Jews trying to do? Are they going to rebuild the wall and offer sacrifices all in one day? Do they think they can make something out of this pile of scorched stones?”
translation_verse: Egblɔ le exɔlɔ̃wo kple Samaria-ʋakɔ ŋkume be: “Nu ka wɔm Yudatɔ beli siawo le? Ðe woagbugbɔ nuwo aɖo tea? Ɖe wole vɔ sa gea? Ɖe woawu enu le ŋkeke ɖeka mea? Ðe woagaho gliɖokpe ƒodzowo tso gbeɖuɖɔwo tome ko atsɔ ɖo glia ko wòanyoa?”

english_verse: Tobiah from Ammon was standing beside Sanballat and said, “Look at the wall they are building! Why, even a fox could knock over this pile of stones.”
translation_verse: Tobiya Amontɔ la hã nɔ exa hafi wònɔ nyaa gblɔm. Eya hã gbɔ ɖi ɖa be: “Tsuiã! Glie nye ema ɖom wolea? Ne abei kura gɔ̃ lia woƒe kpegli ma la, amu.”

english_verse: But I prayed, “Our God, these people hate us and have wished horrible things for us. Please answer our prayers and make their insults fall on them! Let them be the ones to be dragged away as prisoners of war.
translation_verse: O, mía Mawu, se ale si wole vlo dom mí ɖa! Na woƒe fewuɖuɖu la nazu ŋukpe ava tsyɔ woawo ŋutɔ ƒe ta dzi. Na futɔwo nava ha woƒe nuwo, eye woalé woawo ŋutɔ akplɔ ayi aboyo mee.

english_verse: Don't forgive the mean and evil way they have insulted the builders.”
translation_verse: Mègatsyɔ nu woƒe vodada dzi o, eye mègaɖe woƒe nuvɔ̃ ɖa le ŋkuwò me o, elabe wodo dziku na wò le gliɖolaawo ŋkume.

english_verse: But Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people from the city of Ashdod saw the walls going up and the holes being repaired. So they became angry
translation_verse: Esi Sanebalat, Tobiya, Arabiatɔwo, Amontɔwo kple Asdodtɔwo se be Yerusalem ŋu glidzraɖodɔ la le afɔ tsɔm nyuie, eye gbagbãƒeawo de asi xexe me vɔ la, dzi ku wo ŋutɔ.

english_verse: and decided to stir up trouble, and to fight against the people of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Eya ta wosɔ nu be yewo katã yewoaho aʋa ɖe Yerusalem ŋu aɖadze edzi, ade ʋunyaʋunya eme.

english_verse: But we kept on praying to our God, and we also stationed guards day and night.
translation_verse: Ke míawo míedo gbe ɖa na mía Mawu, eye míeɖo dzɔlawo teƒe vovovowo. Ame siawo nɔa ŋudzɔ na futɔawo zã kple keli.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Judah were singing a sorrowful song: “So much rubble for us to haul! Worn out and weary, will we ever finish this wall?”
translation_verse: Ke Yuda gblɔ be: “Míelɔ gli gbagbã ʋuu ɖeɖi te, gake gli gbagbãa gali zã wòle be míalɔ. Míete ŋu le gli sia ɖo ge o.”

english_verse: Our enemies were saying, “Before those Jews know what has happened, we will sneak up and kill them and put an end to their work.”
translation_verse: Míaƒe futɔawo gblɔ be: “Manɔ nyanya me na wo kura o; ɖeko woanɔ vo me ko míava do ɖe wo dzi, awu wo eye dɔa ase ɖe afi ma.”

english_verse: On at least ten different occasions, the Jews living near our enemies warned us against attacks from every side,
translation_verse: Ke Yudatɔ siwo kple míaƒe futɔawo le teƒe ɖeka la va kui ɖe to me na mí zi geɖe, be futɔawo katã le woƒe du vovovowo me tso ge ava dze mía dzi zi ɖeka gbe ɖeka.

english_verse: and so I sent people to guard the wall at its lowest places and where there were still holes in it. I placed them according to families, and they stood guard with swords and spears and with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Le esia ta, meɖe amewo ɖo glia godo le eƒe akpa siwo dɔ gale be míawɔ la, be woanɔ afi mawo ŋu dzɔm. Mema wo ɖe hatsotso vovovowo me ɖe woƒe aƒekɔwo nu, eye wolé woƒe yiwo, akplɔwo kple dawo ɖe asi hele teƒe mawo dzɔm.

english_verse: Then I looked things over and told the leaders, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Don't be afraid of your enemies! The Lord is great and fearsome. So think of him and fight for your relatives and children, your wives and homes!”
translation_verse: Mekpɔ be ameawo tsi dzodzodzoe eya ta megblɔ na woƒe bubumewo, amegãwo kple ame mamlɛawo be: “Migavɔ̃ futɔawo o. Miaƒe ŋku nenɔ ale si Aƒetɔ tri akɔ, eye wòdzi ŋɔ la dzi ne miaʋli mia nɔviwo, mia viŋutsuwo, mia vinyɔnuwo, mia srɔ̃wo kple miaƒe aƒewo ta.”

english_verse: Our enemies found out that we knew about their plot against us, but God kept them from doing what they had planned. So we went back to work on the wall.
translation_verse: Míaƒe futɔwo va se be míenya nugbe si ɖom wole ɖe mía ŋuti, eye wokpɔ be Mawu gblẽ yewoƒe ɖoɖoa me. Eya ta mí katã míetrɔ va gli la gbɔ, eye ame sia ame yi eƒe dɔ dzi.

english_verse: From then on, I let half of the young men work while the other half stood guard. They wore armor and had spears and shields, as well as bows and arrows. The leaders helped the workers
translation_verse: Tso gbe ma gbe dzi la, ame siwo le dɔ wɔm le glia gbɔ la mana ɖe akpa eve me, eye ne akpa ɖeka le dɔ wɔm la, akpa evelia ƒe amewo doa gawu, léa akplɔ, akpoxɔnu kple dati ɖe asi, nɔa ŋudzɔ. Dukɔa ƒe amegãwo katã nɔ megbe na Yuda ƒe aƒe la sesĩe

english_verse: who were rebuilding the wall. Everyone who hauled building materials kept one hand free to carry a weapon.
translation_verse: le nu sia nu me le glidzraɖodɔ blibo la me. Ame siwo nɔ ke, kpe kple xɔtunu bubuwo lɔm na gliɖolaawo hã tsɔa asi ɖeka nɔa dɔa wɔm, eye aʋawɔnu nɔa asi evelia na wo.

english_verse: Even the workers who were rebuilding the wall strapped on a sword. The worker who was to blow the signal trumpet stayed with me.
translation_verse: Gliɖola ɖe sia ɖe hã kplaa yi ɖe ali hafi nɔa glia ɖom. Kpẽkula nɔa ŋunye.

english_verse: I told the people and their officials and leaders, “Our work is so spread out, that we are a long way from one another.
translation_verse: Megblɔ na bubumewo, amegãwo kple ame mamlɛawo katã be: “Dɔa sɔ gbɔ, hekeke ta ale be míekaka ɖe glia dzi, eye ame sia ame le adzɔge tso ehavi gbɔ.

english_verse: If you hear the sound of the trumpet, come quickly and gather around me. Our God will help us fight.”
translation_verse: Ne miese kpẽ ƒe ɖiɖi ko la, mitu ta afi si wòɖi le la enumake ne miava ƒo ƒu ɖe mía ŋu. Mía Mawu awɔ aʋa na mí.”

english_verse: Every day from dawn to dark, half of the workers rebuilt the walls, while the rest stood guard with their spears.
translation_verse: Aleae míewɔa dɔ lae gbe sia gbe, tso ŋdi va se ɖe esime ɣletiviwo tona le fiẽ me: ameawo ƒe afã léa akplɔ ɖe asi, le esime afã mamlɛa nɔa dɔ dzi le glia dzi.

english_verse: I asked the men in charge and their workers to stay inside Jerusalem and stand guard at night. So they guarded the city at night and worked during the day.
translation_verse: Megblɔ na dukɔ la le ɣe ma ɣi me hã be wo dome ame sia ame kple eƒe dɔlawo nanɔ Yerusalem tsim dɔ, ale be mí katã míanɔ dua dzɔm le zã me, anɔ dɔa wɔm le ŋkeke me.

english_verse: I even slept in my work clothes at night; my relatives, the workers, and the guards slept in theirs as well. And we always kept our weapons close by.
translation_verse: Ale nye kple nɔvinyewo kple nye subɔlawo kpakple ŋunyedzɔlawo míeɖea míaƒe awuwo dana ɖi ɣeaɖekeɣi o, ame sia ame léa eƒe aʋawɔnu ɖe asi ɣe sia ɣi.

english_verse: Some of the men and their wives complained about the Jews in power
translation_verse: Azɔ la ɣli ɖi hoo le dukɔ la kple wo srɔ̃wo dome hetsi tre ɖe wo nɔvi Yudatɔwo ŋu.

english_verse: and said, “We have large families, and it takes a lot of grain merely to keep us alive.”
translation_verse: Ðewo be: “Mí kple mía viwo míesɔ gbɔ; ehiã godoo be míakpɔ nu aɖu, bene míatsi agbe.”

english_verse: Others said, “During the famine we even had to mortgage our fields, vineyards, and homes to them in order to buy grain.”
translation_verse: Bubuwo be: “Le ale si dɔ to ta la, ɖe míetsɔ míaƒe agblenyigbawo, míaƒe waingblewo kple míaƒe xɔwo ɖo awɔba hafi te ŋu kpɔ nu le ɖuɖum.”

english_verse: Then others said, “We had to borrow money from those in power to pay the government tax on our fields and vineyards.
translation_verse: Bubuwo hã be: “Ðe míedo ga hafi te ŋu xe duga ɖe míaƒe agblenyigbawo kple waingblewo ŋu na fia.

english_verse: We are Jews just as they are, and our children are as good as theirs. But we still have to sell our children as slaves, and some of our daughters have already been raped. We are completely helpless; our fields and vineyards have even been taken from us.”
translation_verse: Evɔ la, míawo hã ɖeko míele pɛ abe mía nɔvi Yudatɔ bubuawo ene; ŋutilã ɖeka ko míeto, eye mía viwo hã ɖeko wole abe wo viwo ke ene, gake ele na míawo ya be míatsɔ mía viwo awɔ kluviwoe; mía vinyɔnuawo dometɔ aɖewo ya zu kluviwo xoxo gɔ̃. Wɔna aɖeke meli o elabe míaƒe nuɖuɖugblewo kple waingblewo yi ɖe ame bubuwo si me.”

english_verse: When I heard their complaints and their charges, I became very angry.
translation_verse: Esi mese woƒe konyifafaawo la, dzi kum ŋutɔ.

english_verse: So I thought it over and said to the leaders and officials, “How can you charge your own people interest?” Then I called a public meeting and accused the leaders
translation_verse: Mebu tame sẽe, eye mekpɔ be dukɔa ƒe bubumewo kple amegãwo mele azɔli nyui zɔm o. Meyɔ wo ƒo ƒu hegblɔ na wo be: “Miele mia nɔviwo bam.” Eyome meyɔ dutakpekpe gã aɖe ɖe nyaa ŋu,

english_verse: by saying, “We have tried to buy back all of our people who were sold into exile. But here you are, selling more of them for us to buy back!” The officials and leaders did not say a word, because they knew this was true.
translation_verse: eye megblɔ na ƒuƒoƒea be: “Míawo míedze agbagba ale si míate ŋui hexɔ mía nɔvi Yudatɔ siwo tsɔ wo ɖokui dzra na dukɔ bubuwo la ƒe ɖewo ƒle tso kluvinyenye me. Fifi boŋ miawo ya miele miawo ŋutɔ mia nɔviwo dzi zim, wole wo ɖokui dzram na mi wo nɔvi Yudatɔwo!” Dumegãawo zi ɖoɖoe toŋ; wode nu ke ge do kpoe.

english_verse: I continued, “What you have done is wrong! We must honor our God by the way we live, so the Gentiles can't find fault with us.
translation_verse: Meyi edzi be: “Nu si wɔm miele menyo o. Ðe mele be miatsɔ bubu na mía Mawu oa? Ðe mele be miawɔ nu si dze, be dukɔ bubuwo, ame siwo nye míaƒe futɔwo la, nagakpɔ mɔnu anɔ alɔ me ɖem le mía ŋu oa?

english_verse: My relatives, my friends, and I are also lending money and grain, but we must no longer demand payment in return.
translation_verse: Nye ŋutɔ hã melɔ̃ amewo va do ga kple bli le asinye; nenema ke nɔvinyewo kple ame siwo le dɔ wɔm nam la hã do nu siawo na amewo. Mina míatsɔ feawo ake wo dzro.

english_verse: Now give back the fields, vineyards, olive orchards, and houses you have taken and also the interest you have been paid.”
translation_verse: Migbugbɔ fetɔwo ƒe nuɖuɖugblewo, waingblewo, amitigblewo kple woƒe xɔwo na wo egbe sia ke. Nenema ke mitsɔ ga, bli, aha, ami siwo miedo na wo ƒe alafa ɖekalia si miexɔna le wo si la ke wo.”

english_verse: The leaders answered, “We will do whatever you say and return their property, without asking to be repaid.” So I made the leaders promise in front of the priests to give back the property.
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Míexɔ wò aɖaŋua; míawɔ edzi. Míatrɔ nuawo na wo, eye míagalĩ fe aɖeke wo o.” Meyɔ nunɔlawo vɛ, eye mena ame siwo ŋu amewo nyi fe le la va ka atam le nunɔlaawo ŋkume be yewoawɔ ŋugbe si yewodo la dzi.

english_verse: Then I emptied my pockets and said, “If you don't keep your promise, that's what God will do to you. He will empty out everything you own, even taking away your houses.” The people answered, “We will keep our promise.” Then they praised the Lord and did as they had promised. Nehemiah Is Generous
translation_verse: Meʋuʋu nye akɔ nu hã, gblɔ kpe ɖe eŋu be: “Ne ame aɖe gbe eƒe ŋugbedodoa dzi wɔwɔ la, Mawu naʋuʋu eyama alea tso eƒe aƒeme kple eƒe dɔwɔɖua gbɔ ne wòatsi ƒuƒlu.” Ameha la katã lɔ̃ ɖe edzi be: “Neva eme”, eye wokafu Aƒetɔ. Tete wowɔ woƒe ŋugbedodo la dzi. Nexemya menye ɖokuitɔdila o

english_verse: Each governor before me had been a burden to the people by making them pay for his food and wine and by demanding forty silver coins a day. Even their officials had been a burden to the people. But I respected God, and I didn't think it was right to be so hard on them.
translation_verse: Mɔ́mefia siwo do ŋgɔ nam la zu agba kpekpe na dukɔ la. Woxɔa nuɖuɖu kple aha tsoa dukɔa gbɔ eye, gawu la, dukɔa gaxea klosaloga bla ene na wo gbe sia gbe. Woƒe subɔlawo gɔ̃ hã ɖua aƒetɔ ɖe dukɔa dzi. Nye la, nyemewɔ nu ma o, le sosroɖa si le menye na Mawu ta.

english_verse: I spent all my time getting the wall rebuilt and did not buy any property. Everyone working for me did the same thing.
translation_verse: Metsɔ nye ameti blibo la katã ƒo ɖe gligbugbɔɖodɔ la me. Nyemeƒle anyigba aɖeke na ɖokuinye o, eye mena ame siwo katã wɔa dɔ le tenye la hã va míekpe asi ɖe gliɖodɔa ŋu wɔ.
