Evɔ la, nyemedɔ wo o, eye nyemeɖe gbe na wo be woayi hafi o. Eya ta womeɖe vi aɖeke na dukɔ sia kura o.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Aƒetɔ ƒe agba si wotsɔ

english_verse: Jeremiah, when a prophet or a priest or anyone else comes to you and asks, “Does the Lord have news for us?” tell them, “You people are a nuisance to the Lord, and he will get rid of you.”
translation_verse: “Ne dukɔ sia me tɔ aɖe alo gbeƒãɖela aɖe, alo nunɔla aɖe bia wò be: ‘Nu ka nye Aƒetɔ ƒe agba?’ hã la, ɖo eŋu na wo be: Aƒetɔ be: ‘Miawoe nye agba la, eye matsɔ mi aƒu gbe.’

english_verse: If any of you say, “Here is news from the Lord,” I will punish you and your families, even if you are a prophet or a priest.
translation_verse: Ne gbeƒãɖela aɖe, alo nunɔla aɖe, alo dukɔmetɔ aɖe gblɔ be: ‘Aƒetɔ ƒe agba’ la, mahe to na eyama kple eƒe aƒe siaa.

english_verse: Instead, you must ask your friends and relatives, “What answer did the Lord give?” or “What has the Lord said?”
translation_verse: Ale mia dome ame sia ame nebia ehavi kple nɔvia be: ‘Ale ke Aƒetɔ ɖo nya la ŋui?’ alo ‘Nya kae Aƒetɔ gblɔ?’

english_verse: It seems that you each have your own news! So if you say, “Here is news from the Lord,” you are twisting my words into a lie. Remember that I am your God, the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Ke ame aɖeke megagblɔ be: ‘Aƒetɔ ƒe agba’ azɔ o, elabe ne egblɔe la, mana nye nya azu agba nɛ, esi dukɔ la trɔ gbo woƒe Mawu, Mawu gbagbe, Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la, ƒe nyawo ta.

english_verse: If you go to a prophet, it's all right to ask, “What answer did the Lord give to my question?” or “What has the Lord said?”
translation_verse: Nya si nàbia gbeƒãɖelaawo lae nye: ‘Ŋuɖoɖo kae Aƒetɔ na mi? Nya kae Aƒetɔ gblɔ?’

english_verse: I will pick you up and throw you far away. And I will abandon this city of Jerusalem that I gave to your ancestors.
translation_verse: eya ta, kpɔ ɖa, makɔ mi ɖe dzi, eye matsɔ mia kple du si metsɔ na mia kple mia tɔgbuiwo siaa la, aƒu gbe ɖa tso ŋkunye me.

english_verse: You will never be free from your shame and disgrace.
translation_verse: Mahe ŋukpe kple vlodoame mavɔ si womaŋlɔ be akpɔ o la, ava mia dzi.”

english_verse: The Lord spoke to me in a vision after King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had come to Judah and taken King Jehoiachin, his officials, and all the skilled workers back to Babylonia. In this vision I saw two baskets of figs in front of the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Esime Nebukadnezar, Babilon-fia ɖe aboyo Xonya, Yehoyakim vi, Yuda-fia tso Yerusalem yi Babilonia, eye wokplɔ Yuda-dumegãwo, aɖaŋudɔwɔlawo kple gbedewo hã yii vɔ megbe la, Aƒetɔ ɖe ŋutega sia fiam: Kpɔ ɖa, woda kusi eve siwo me gbotsetsewo le la ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔ la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: One basket was full of very good figs that ripened early, and the other was full of rotten figs that were not fit to eat.
translation_verse: Gbotsetse nyuiwo le kusi ɖeka me. Woawo le abe gbotsetse siwo ɖina gbã ene. Gake gbotsetse siwo le kusi evelia me la gblẽ ale gbegbe be womate ŋu aɖu wo o.

english_verse: “Jeremiah,” the Lord asked, “what do you see?” “Figs,” I said. “Some are very good, but the others are too rotten to eat.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ biam be: “Yeremya, nu ka kpɔm nèle?” Meɖo eŋu be: “Gbotsetsewoe. Nyuitɔwo nyakpɔ ŋutɔ, ke gbegblẽtɔwo ya gblẽ keŋkeŋ; womate ŋu aɖu wo o.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say:
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ gblɔ nam be:

english_verse: People of Judah, the good figs stand for those of you I sent away as exiles to Babylonia,
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la, be: Ale si gbotsetse siawo nyoe la, nenema mabu ame siwo menyà tso Yuda ɖo ɖe aboyo me le Kaldea-nyigba dzi la be wonyoe.

english_verse: where I am watching over them. Then someday I will bring them back to this land. I will plant them, instead of uprooting them, and I will build them up, rather than tearing them down.
translation_verse: Nye ŋku anɔ wo ŋu hena nyui, eye makplɔ wo agbugbɔ va anyigba sia dzi. Matu wo woatsi, eye nyemagbã wo o. Mado wo, eye nyemaho wo o.

english_verse: I will give them a desire to know me and to be my people. They will want me to be their God, and they will turn back to me with all their heart.
translation_verse: Mana dzi wo ne woadze sii be nyee nye Aƒetɔ. Woanye nye dukɔ, eye manye woƒe Mawu, elabe woatrɔ ava gbɔnye kple woƒe dzi blibo.”

english_verse: The rotten figs stand for King Zedekiah of Judah, his officials, and all the others who were not taken away to Babylonia, whether they stayed here in Judah or went to live in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ be: “Abe gbotsetse siwo gblẽ, eye womate ŋu aɖu wo o ene la, nenema mawɔ Zedekiya, Yuda-fia kple eƒe dumegãwo kple ame siwo susɔ ɖe Yerusalem kple ame siwo susɔ ɖe anyigba sia dzi kpakple ame siwo le Egipte-nyigba dzi lae.

english_verse: I will punish them with a terrible disaster, and everyone on earth will tremble when they hear about it. I will force the people of Judah to go to foreign countries, where they will be cursed and insulted.
translation_verse: Mana woazu ŋɔdzinu na anyigba dzi fiaɖuƒewo katã. Woado vlo wo, woazu hamelo, woako wo, eye woatsɔ wo ŋkɔ aƒo fi ade ame le teƒe siwo katã manyà wo aɖo ɖa la.

english_verse: War and hunger and disease will strike them, until they finally disappear from the land that I gave them and their ancestors.
translation_verse: Mahe aʋawɔwɔ, dɔwuame kple dɔ vɔ̃ ade wo dome, va se ɖe esime woatsrɔ̃ avɔ keŋkeŋ, le anyigba si metsɔ na woawo kple wo tɔgbuiwo la dzi.”

english_verse: The Lord has sent prophets to you time after time, but you refused to listen.
translation_verse: Miegbe toɖoɖo, gbe nusese togbɔ be Aƒetɔ nɔ eƒe dɔla siwo nye eƒe gbeƒãɖelawo ɖom ɖe mi edziedzi hã.

english_verse: They told you that the Lord had said: Change your ways! If you stop doing evil, I will let you stay forever in this land that I gave your ancestors.
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na mi be: ‘Ame sia ame netrɔ dzime, eye wòadzudzɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ, ne mianɔ anyigba si Aƒetɔ tsɔ na mia kple mia tɔgbuiwo siaa gbe aɖe gbe wòzu mia tɔ tegbee la dzi;

english_verse: I don't want to harm you. So don't make me angry by worshiping idols and other gods.
translation_verse: migadze mawu bubuwo yome be miasubɔ wo, eye miade ta agu na wo o; migatsɔ miaƒe asinudɔwɔwɔwo do dziku nam o, ekema nyemawɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke mi o.’

english_verse: and now I will let you be attacked by nations from the north, and especially by my servant, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. You and other nearby nations will be destroyed and left in ruins forever. Everyone who sees what has happened will be shocked, but they will still make fun of you.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, maɖo dukɔ siwo katã le dzigbemenyigbawo dzi la ɖa. Maɖo nye dɔla Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar hã ɖa. Makplɔ wo vɛ be woawɔ aʋa kple Yuda-nyigba sia kple edzinɔlawo kpakple dukɔ siwo katã ƒo xlãe. Matsrɔ̃ wo keŋkeŋ, awɔ wo ŋɔdzinu, nu si ŋu woaʋuʋu ta le kple alɔmeɖenu tegbee.

english_verse: I will put an end to your parties and wedding celebrations; no one will grind grain or be here to light the lamps at night.
translation_verse: Gawu la, matsi aseyetsoɣli kple dzidzɔɣli, ŋugbetɔsrɔ̃ ƒe gbe kple ŋugbetɔ ƒe gbe nu le wo dome. Womagatu wɔ le teƒo o, eye womagasi akaɖi le zã me o.

english_verse: This country will be as empty as a desert, because I will make all of you the slaves of the king of Babylonia for
translation_verse: Anyigba sia katã azu aƒedo kple gbegbe, eye dukɔ siawo asubɔ Babilon-fia ƒe bla adrẽ sɔŋ.

english_verse: When that time is up, I will punish the king of Babylonia and his people for everything they have done wrong, and I will turn that country into a wasteland forever.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: Ekema le ƒe bla adrẽ la megbe la, mahe to na Babilon-fia kple dukɔ ma, Kaldeatɔwo ƒe anyigba la, le woƒe vodada ta; le esi wogblẽ anyigba la dome, eye wòzu gbegbe tegbee la ta.

english_verse: My servant Jeremiah has told you what I said I will do to Babylonia and to the other nations, and he wrote it all down in this book. I will do everything I threatened.
translation_verse: Mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e siwo katã megblɔ ɖe anyigba ma ŋuti la ava edzi. Mana nu siwo katã gbeƒãɖela Yeremya ɖe gbeƒãe ɖe dukɔwo katã ŋu, eye woŋlɔ wo ɖe agbalẽ sia me la nava wo dzi.

english_verse: I will pay back the Babylonians for every wrong they have done. Great kings from many other nations will conquer the Babylonians and force them to be slaves. The Cup Full of God's Anger
translation_verse: Elabe dukɔ geɖewo kple fia xɔŋkɔ geɖewo awɔ wo kluviwoe, eye maɖo eteƒe na wo ɖe woƒe nuwɔnawo kple woƒe asinudɔwɔwɔwo nu.” Mawu ahe to na dukɔwo

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel showed me a vision in which he said, “Jeremiah, here is a cup filled with the wine of my anger. Take it and make every nation drink some.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la gblɔ nam be: “Xɔ wainkplu sia si dɔmedzoe yɔ la le asinye. Tsɔe yi na dukɔ siwo katã gbɔ maɖo wò ɖa la be woano.

english_verse: They will vomit and act crazy, because of the war this cup of anger will bring to them.”
translation_verse: Woanoe, anɔ mumum sagasaga, eye woƒe susu atɔtɔ le aʋawɔwɔ si maɖo ɖe wo dome la ta.”

english_verse: I took the cup from the Lord's hand, and I went to the kings of the nations and made each of them drink some.
translation_verse: Ale mexɔ kplu la le Aƒetɔ si, eye mena dukɔ siwo katã gbɔ wòɖom ɖa la no emenu.

english_verse: I started with Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and the king and his officials were removed from power in disgrace. Everyone still makes insulting jokes about them and uses their names as curse words.
translation_verse: Yerusalem kple Yuda-duwo, eƒe fiawo kple eƒe amegãwo no emenu, ne mawɔ wo woazu aƒedo kple gbegbe, nu si ŋu woaʋuʋu ta le kple fiƒode abe ale si wogale wɔwɔm va ɖo egbee ene.

english_verse: and all the foreigners who lived in the country. Next I went to the king of Uz, and then to the four kings of Philistia, who ruled from Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and what was left of Ashdod.
translation_verse: dukɔ bubu me tɔ siwo katã tsaka kple Egiptetɔwo; fia siwo katã le Uz-nyigba dzi; fia siwo katã le Askalon, Gaza, Ekron siwo nye Filisti-duwo kple ame siwo susɔ ɖe Asdod-du me;

english_verse: and to the kings of Tyre, Sidon, and their colonies across the sea.
translation_verse: fia siwo katã le Tiro kple Sidon; fia siwo katã le atsiaƒu ƒe go kemɛ dzi;

english_verse: After this, I went to the kings of Dedan, Tema, Buz, the tribes of the Arabian Desert,
translation_verse: Arabia-fiawo katã, dukɔ tsakatsaka siwo le kegbegbe ƒe fiawo katã;

english_verse: and the countries in the north, both near and far. I went to all the countries on earth, one after another, and finally to Babylonia.
translation_verse: fia siwo katã le dzigbeme, le kpuiƒe kple didiƒe siaa, anoe ɖe wo nɔewo yome; xexemefiaɖuƒe siwo katã le anyigba dzi. Le wo yome la, Sesax-fia anoe.”

english_verse: The Lord had said to tell each king, “The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, commands you to drink from this cup that is full of the wine of his anger. It will make you so drunk that you will vomit. And when the Lord sends war against the nations, you will be completely defeated.”
translation_verse: Ekema nàgblɔ na wo be: “Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la, be: ‘Mino aha miamu, mitru, midze anyi, eye migafɔ o, le aʋawɔwɔ si maɖo ɖe mia dome la ta.’

english_verse: The Lord told me that if any of them refused to drink from the cup, I must tell them that he had said, “I, the Lord All-Powerful, command you to drink.
translation_verse: “Ne wogbe be yewomaxɔ kplu la le asiwò ano emenua o la, ekema gblɔ na wo be: ‘Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: Ele be mianoe kokoko.

english_verse: Starting with my own city of Jerusalem, everyone on earth will suffer from war. So there is no way I will let you escape unharmed.”
translation_verse: Elabe kpɔ ɖa, medze nugbegblẽ gɔme tso du si ŋu woyɔ nye ŋkɔ ɖo la dzi. Ɖe magblẽ mi ɖi, nyemahe to na mi oa? Nyemagbe tohehe na mi o, elabe mana aʋa adzɔ ɖe ame siwo katã le xexea me la dome. Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe.’

english_verse: My voice will be heard everywhere on earth, accusing nations of their crimes and sentencing the guilty to death. Disaster Is Coming
translation_verse: Hoowɔwɔ ade anyigba ƒe mlɔenu ke, elabe Aƒetɔ tsɔ nya ɖe dukɔwo ŋu. Akplɔ nu gbagbewo katã ayi ʋɔnui eye wòana ame vɔ̃ɖiwo natsi yi nu.’ ” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says: You can see disaster spreading from far across the earth, from nation to nation like a horrible storm.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Kpɔ ɖa, dzɔgbevɔ̃e gbɔna tso dukɔ me yi dukɔ me, eye ahom gã de asi tutu me gbɔna tso keke anyigba ƒe mlɔenu ke!”

english_verse: When it strikes, I will kill so many people that their bodies will cover the ground like manure. No one will be left to bury them or to mourn. The Leaders of Judah Will Be Punished
translation_verse: “Ame siwo Aƒetɔ awu gbe ma gbe la, atsi anyigba tso xexeme ƒe akpa ɖeka yi akpa bubu. Womafa ame kukuwo, aƒo ƒu wo loo, alo aɖi wo gɔ̃ hã o. Woanɔ anyigba abe lãmí ene.”

english_verse: The Lord's people are his flock, and you leaders were the shepherds. But now it's your turn to be butchered like sheep. You'll shatter like fine pottery dropped on the floor. So roll on the ground, crying and mourning.
translation_verse: “Mi alẽkplɔlawo, mifa avi, mido ɣli sesĩe. Mi dukɔ la dziɖulawo mimli le dzowɔ me. Ɣeyiɣi de be woawu mi, aka mi ahlẽ; woatso mi abe agbo dami siwo woɖo ɖi na wuwu ene.

english_verse: You have nowhere to run, nowhere to hide. *
translation_verse: Sitsoƒe aɖeke manɔ anyi na alẽkplɔlaawo o, eye sisí abu ɖe dukɔa dziɖulawo.

english_verse: Listen to the cries of the shepherds, as the Lord's burning anger turns peaceful meadows into barren deserts.
translation_verse: Ame siwo le ŋutifafa me la ƒe dzidzeme dome gblẽ le Aƒetɔ ƒe dziku helihelĩ la ta.

english_verse: Like a lion leaving its den, the Lord has abandoned his people to the destruction of war.
translation_verse: Egblẽ eƒe avekɔe ɖi abe dzata ene, elabe woƒe anyigba zu gbegbe le ameteɖeanyila kple Aƒetɔ ƒe dziku helihelĩ la ta.”

english_verse: The priests, the prophets, and everyone else in the temple heard what I said,
translation_verse: Nunɔlawo kple Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo kpakple dukɔ blibo la ɖo to se nya siwo Yeremya nɔ gbɔgblɔm le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me.

english_verse: Soon after Jehoiakim became king of Judah, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Le Yehoyakim, Yosiya vi ƒe fiaɖuɖu gɔmedzedze le Yuda-dukɔ me la, Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe va be:

english_verse: But if you put me to death, you and everyone else in Jerusalem will be guilty of murdering an innocent man, because everything I preached came from the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɖeko minya nyuie be ne miewum la, miahe ʋu maɖifɔ ava mia ɖokui, du sia kple emenɔlawo dzi; elabe le nyateƒe me la, Aƒetɔ ye dɔm ɖe mia gbɔ be magblɔ nya siawo katã ɖe to me na mi.”

english_verse: Jeremiah, I have a message for everyone who comes from the towns of Judah to worship in my temple. Go to the temple courtyard and speak every word that I tell you.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Yi ɖatsi tsitre ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ƒe xɔxɔnu, eye nàgblɔ nya siwo katã megblɔ be nàgblɔ na ame siwo tsoa Yuda-duwo katã me va doa gbe ɖa le Aƒetɔ ƒeme la. Mègagblẽ nya aɖeke ɖi o.

english_verse: Maybe the people will listen this time. And if they stop doing wrong, I will change my mind and not punish them for their sins.
translation_verse: Ðewohĩ woasee, eye wo dome ame sia ame adzudzɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi si wɔm wòle la, ekema vɔ̃ si meɖo be mawɔ wo la avem, eye maɖe asi le eŋu.

english_verse: Tell them that I have said: You have refused to listen to me and to obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na wo be: ‘Aƒetɔ be: Ne miegbe toɖoɖom, eye miewɔ se siwo mede na mi la dzi o,

english_verse: Again and again I have sent my servants the prophets to preach to you, but you ignored them as well. Now I am warning you that if you don't start obeying me at once,
translation_verse: eye ne mieɖoa to nye dɔla gbeƒãɖela siwo medɔna ɖe mi enuenu la ƒe nyawo o la,

english_verse: I will destroy this temple, just as I destroyed the town of Shiloh. Then everyone on earth will use the name “Jerusalem” as a curse word. Jeremiah on Trial
translation_verse: ekema mawɔ aƒe sia wòazu abe Silo ene, eye mana anyigba dzi dukɔwo katã atsɔ du sia ƒe ŋkɔ aƒo fi ade amee.’ ”

english_verse: and as soon as I finished, they all crowded around me and started shouting, “Why did you preach that the Lord will destroy this temple, just as he destroyed Shiloh? Why did you say that Jerusalem will be empty and lie in ruins? You ought to be put to death for saying such things in the Lord's name!” Then they had me arrested.
translation_verse: Nu ka ta nèɖe gbeƒã le Aƒetɔ ŋkɔ me be: ‘Aƒe sia azu abe Silo ene, eye du sia agbã, ame aɖeke maganɔ eme o’?” Tete ameawo katã ƒo xlã Yeremya le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒea me.

english_verse: The royal officers heard what had happened, and they came from the palace to the new gate of the temple to be the judges at my trial.
translation_verse: Esi Yuda-dumegãwo se nu si le dzɔdzɔm la, wotso le fia ƒeme va Aƒetɔ ƒeme, eye wobɔbɔ nɔ teƒe si woyɔna be Agbo Yeye la nu.

english_verse: While they listened, the priests and the prophets said to the crowd, “All of you have heard Jeremiah prophesy that Jerusalem will be destroyed. He deserves the death penalty.”
translation_verse: Tete nunɔlaawo kple Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelaawo gblɔ na dumegãawo kple ameha blibo la be: “Edze be woatso kufia na ŋutsu sia elabe egblɔ nya vɔ̃ ɖe du sia ŋu. Miawo ŋutɔ miesee kple miaƒe towo.”

english_verse: Then I told the judges and everyone else: The Lord himself sent me to tell you about the terrible things he will do to you, to Jerusalem, and to the temple. But if you change your ways and start obeying the Lord, he will change his mind.
translation_verse: Eya ta azɔ la, miɖɔ miaƒe agbenɔnɔ ɖo eye midzudzɔ nu madzɔmadzɔ siwo wɔm miele la, eye miawɔ nu si Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la, di be miawɔ la. Ekema Aƒetɔ atrɔ susu, eye magawɔ vɔ̃ si wògblɔ ɖe mia ŋu la mi o.

english_verse: You must decide what to do with me. Just do whatever you think is right.
translation_verse: Ke nye ya, mele mia si me xoxo. Nu si miekpɔ be enyo, eye wòdze ko la, miwɔm faa.

english_verse: The judges and the other people told the priests and prophets, “Since Jeremiah only told us what the Lord our God had said, we don't think he deserves to die.”
translation_verse: Tete dumegãwo kple ameha blibo la gblɔ na nunɔlaawo kple Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelaawo be: “Ŋutsu sia ƒo nu na mi le Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ me eya ta medze be woatso kufia nɛ o.”

english_verse: Then some of the leaders from other towns stepped forward. They told the crowd that
translation_verse: Ametsitsi aɖewo tsi tsitre, eye wogblɔ na ame siwo katã ƒo ƒu ɖe afi ma la be:

english_verse: years ago when Hezekiah was king of Judah, a prophet named Micah from the town of Moresheth had said: “I, the Lord All-Powerful, say Jerusalem will be plowed under and left in ruins. Thorns will cover the mountain where the temple now stands.”
translation_verse: “Le Yuda-fia, Xizkiya ŋɔli la, Mixa, Morasitɔ ɖe gbeƒã na Yuda-dukɔ blibo la be Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la gblɔ be: ‘Amewo ade Zion abe agble ene Yerusalem-du azu glikpo, eye gbedoxɔ nɔƒe le toa dzi azu ave.’

english_verse: Then the leaders continued: No one put Micah to death for saying that. Instead, King Hezekiah prayed to the Lord with fear and trembling and asked him to have mercy. Then the Lord decided not to destroy Jerusalem, even though he had already said he would. People of Judah, if Jeremiah is killed, we will bring a terrible disaster on ourselves.
translation_verse: Ðe Yuda-fia Xizkiya kple Yuda-dukɔ la wuia? Ɖe fia la mevɔ̃ Aƒetɔ, eye wòƒo koko nɛ be wòakpɔ nublanui na yewo oa? Ðe Aƒetɔ meɖe asi le vɔ̃ si wògblɔ be yeawɔ la ŋu oa? Ke míawo míedi be míahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e gã sia ava mía ɖokui dzi!”

english_verse: Then send a message to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon. Some officials from these countries are in Jerusalem, meeting with Zedekiah.
translation_verse: De gbe asi na amedɔdɔ siwo va Yuda-fia Zedekiya gbɔ le Yerusalem la si, be woaxɔ yi na Edom-fia, Amon-fia kple Sidon-fia.

english_verse: So have them tell their kings that I have said: I am the All-Powerful Lord God of Israel,
translation_verse: Gblɔ ɖo ɖe woƒe aƒetɔwo be: ‘Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be:

english_verse: and with my power I created the earth, its people, and all animals. I decide who will rule the earth,
translation_verse: Nu si miagblɔ na miaƒe aƒetɔwoe nye esi: Nye ŋutɔe tsɔ nye ŋusẽ triakɔ kple alɔ si medo ɖe dzi wɔ anyigba, amegbetɔ kple lã; ame si melɔ̃ la, eyae metsɔnɛ na.

english_verse: and I have chosen my servant King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to rule all nations, including yours. I will even let him rule the wild animals. All nations will be slaves of Nebuchadnezzar, his son, and his grandson. Then many nations will join together, and their kings will make slaves of the Babylonians.
translation_verse: Dukɔwo katã asubɔ eya ŋutɔ, via kple eƒe tɔgbuiyɔvi va se ɖe esime eƒe anyigba la ƒe ɣeyiɣi nade. Ekema dukɔ geɖewo kple fia sesẽwo awɔe wòazu woƒe kluvi.”

english_verse: This yoke stands for the power of King Nebuchadnezzar, and I will destroy any nation that refuses to obey him. Nebuchadnezzar will attack, and many will die in battle or from hunger and disease.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Ke ne dukɔ aɖe alo fiaɖuƒe aɖe gbe be yemasubɔ Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar sia, eye wòatsɔ Babilon-fia ƒe kɔkuti o la, matsɔ aʋawɔwɔ, dɔwuame kple dɔ vɔ̃ ahe to na dukɔ ma, va se ɖe esime mato eƒe asi dzi atsrɔ̃e keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: You might have people in your kingdom who claim they can tell the future by magic or by talking with the dead or by dreams or messages from a god. But don't pay attention if any of them tell you not to obey Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Eya ta migaɖo to miaƒe gbeƒãɖela, bokɔ, drɔ̃ekula, afakala alo dzotɔ siwo le gbɔgblɔm na mi be: ‘Mele be miasubɔ Babilon-fia o’ la o.

english_verse: If you listen to such lies, I will have you dragged far from your country and killed.
translation_verse: Wole mia blem kple woƒe gbeƒãɖeɖeawo ale be woana woaɖe mi ɖa boo tso miaƒe anyigba dzi, eye manyà mi ɖa, miatsrɔ̃.

english_verse: But if you and your nation are willing to obey Nebuchadnezzar, I will let you stay in your country, and your people will continue to live and work on their farms.
translation_verse: Gake dukɔ si tsɔ Babilon-fia ƒe kɔkuti, eye wòsubɔe la, mana wòanɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi, ade agble ɖi ahanɔ afi ma.’ ” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: After I had spoken to the officials from the nearby kingdoms, I went to King Zedekiah and told him the same thing. Then I said: Zedekiah, if you and the people of Judah want to stay alive, you must obey Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians.
translation_verse: Megblɔ nya mawo na Yuda-fia Zedekiya nenema ke be: “Mibɔbɔ mia ɖokui ɖe Babilon-fia te, eye miasubɔ eya kple eƒe dukɔ ne mianɔ agbe.

english_verse: But if you refuse, then you and your people will die from war, hunger, and disease, just as the Lord has warned.
translation_verse: Nu ka ta wò kple wò dukɔ miaku ɖe aʋawɔwɔ, dɔwuame kple dɔ vɔ̃ si me abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ ɖe dukɔ ɖe sia ɖe si gbe be yemasubɔ Babilon-fia o la ŋu ene?

english_verse: Your prophets have told you that you don't need to obey Nebuchadnezzar, but don't listen to their lies.
translation_verse: Migaɖo to gbeƒãɖela siwo le gbɔgblɔm na mi be: ‘Mele be miasubɔ Babilon-fia o’ la o. Mia blem wole kple woƒe gbeƒãɖeɖeawo.

english_verse: Those prophets claim to be speaking for the Lord, but he didn't send them. They are lying! If you do what they say, he will have both you and them dragged off to another country and killed. The Lord has spoken.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: Menye nyee dɔ wo o; alakpanya wole gbeƒã ɖemee le nye ŋkɔ me kple susu be manyà mi, miadzo, eye woatsrɔ̃ mi akpe ɖe gbeƒãɖela siawo, siwo le mia blem la ŋuti.”

english_verse: When I finished talking to the king, I told the priests and everyone else that the Lord had said: Don't listen to the prophets when they say that very soon the Babylonians will return the things they took from my temple. Those prophets are lying!
translation_verse: Tete megblɔ na nunɔlaawo kple dukɔ blibo la be Aƒetɔ be: “Migaɖo to nya si miaƒe gbeƒãɖelawo le gbɔgblɔm na mi be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa, esusɔ vie woatrɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒemenuwo avɛ tso Babilonia’ o. Mia blem wole kple woƒe gbeƒãɖeɖe mawo.

english_verse: If you choose to obey the king of Babylonia, you will live. But if you listen to those prophets, this whole city will be nothing but a pile of rubble.
translation_verse: Migaɖo to wo o. Misubɔ Babilon-fia ne mianɔ agbe. Nu ka ta du sia azu aƒedo ɖo?

english_verse: If I really had spoken to those prophets, they would know what I am going to do. Then they would be begging me not to let everything else be taken from the temple and the king's palace and the rest of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nenye gbeƒãɖela wonye, eye Aƒetɔ ƒe nya le wo si la, ekema na woaƒo koko na Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la ɖe mia nu, ale be womagatsɔ nu siwo susɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒeme, Yuda-fia ƒeme kple Yerusalem la ayi Babilon o.

english_verse: will be taken to Babylonia, where they will remain until I decide to bring them back to Jerusalem. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: woatsɔ woawo hã ayi Babilon. Woanɔ afi ma va se ɖe gbe si gbe maɖo ŋku wo dzi, eye magbugbɔ wo agava da ɖe teƒe sia.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Later that same year, in the fifth month of the fourth year that Zedekiah was king, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur from Gibeon came up to me in the temple. And while the priests and others in the temple were listening,
translation_verse: Esime Yuda-fia Zedekiya va zi dzi, le ƒè enelia ƒe dzinu atɔ̃lia me le ƒè ma ke me la, gbeƒãɖela Xananya, Asur vi, tso Gibeon-du me va ƒo nu kplim le Aƒetɔ ƒeme. Egblɔ nam le nunɔlawo kple dukɔ blibo la ŋkume be:

english_verse: And within two years, I will bring back to Jerusalem everything that he took from my temple and carried off to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Le ƒè eve me la, magbugbɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒemenu siwo katã Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar tsɔ tso teƒe sia yi Babilon la agbɔ va afi siae.

english_verse: King Jehoiachin and the other people who were taken from Judah to Babylonia will be allowed to come back here as well. All this will happen because I will smash the power of the king of Babylonia!
translation_verse: Gawu la, makplɔ Yuda-fia Xonya, Yehoyakim vi kple ame siwo katã woɖe aboyoe kpe ɖe eŋu tso Yuda yi Babilon la agbɔ va teƒe siae elabe maŋe Babilon-fia ƒe kɔkuti la.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: The priests and the others were still standing there, so I said:
translation_verse: Tete Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela Yeremya gblɔ na gbeƒãɖela Xananya le nunɔlawo kple ameha si le tsitre ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒea ŋkume

english_verse: Hananiah, I hope the Lord will do exactly what you said. I hope he does bring back everything the Babylonians took from the temple, and that our people who were taken to Babylonia will be allowed to return home.
translation_verse: be: “Neva eme! Aƒetɔ newɔe nenema! Aƒetɔ nena nya siwo nèɖe gbeƒãe la nava eme. Netrɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒemenuawo kple ame siwo katã woɖe aboyoe la tso Babilon va teƒe sia.

english_verse: that long before we were born, prophets were saying powerful kingdoms would be struck by war, disaster, and disease.
translation_verse: Gbeƒãɖela siwo do ŋgɔ na nye kple wò le blema la, ɖe gbeƒã aʋawɔwɔ, dɔwuame kple dɔ vɔ̃ ɖe dukɔ geɖewo kple fiaɖuƒe triakɔwo ŋu ɖi.

english_verse: Now you are saying we will have peace. We will just have to wait and see if that is really what the Lord has said.
translation_verse: Ne gbeƒãɖela aɖe ɖe gbeƒã be ŋutifafa gbɔna, eye eƒe nyaa va eme la, wodzea sii be Aƒetɔ ye dɔ gbeƒãɖela ma ɖa nyateƒe.”

english_verse: Hananiah grabbed the wooden yoke from my neck and smashed it.
translation_verse: Tete gbeƒãɖela Xananya ɖe kɔkuti la le kɔ na Yeremya, eye wòŋee

english_verse: Then he said, “The Lord says this is the way he will smash the power Nebuchadnezzar has over the nations, and it will happen in less than two years.” I left the temple,
translation_verse: hegblɔ le ameawo katã ŋkume be: “Aƒetɔ be: Alea mele Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar ƒe kɔkuti si le kɔ na dukɔwo katã la ŋe gee le ƒè eve me.” Ke Yeremya, gbeƒãɖela la, dzo.

english_verse: to go back and say to Hananiah: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You smashed a wooden yoke, but I will replace it with one made of iron. I will put iron yokes on all the nations, and they will have to do what King Nebuchadnezzar commands. I will even let him rule the wild animals.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la gblɔ be: Metsɔ kɔkuga ku kɔ na dukɔ siawo katã ne woanye Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar teviwo asubɔe. Elabe metsɔ gbemelãwo gɔ̃ hã na fia Nebukadnezar be woasubɔe.’ ”

english_verse: Hananiah, I have never sent you to speak for me. And yet you have talked my people into believing your lies and rebelling against me. So now I will send you—I'll send you right off the face of the earth! You will die before this year is over.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa, maɖe wò ɖa le anyigba dzi. Àku le ƒe sia me, elabe ègblɔ aglãdzenya ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu.’ ”

english_verse: I gave the letter to Elasah and Gemariah, two men that King Zedekiah of Judah was sending to Babylon to talk with Nebuchadnezzar. In the letter, I wrote
translation_verse: Woɖo agbalẽa ɖa to Eleasa, Safan vi kple Gemarya, Xilkiya vi, ame siwo Yuda-fia Zedekiya dɔ ɖo ɖe Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar gbɔ le Babilon la dzi. Emenyawoe nye:

english_verse: that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. Now I tell you
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la le gbɔgblɔm na ame siwo katã wòɖo ɖe aboyo me tso Yerusalem yi Babilonia la be:

english_verse: to settle there and build houses. Plant gardens and eat what you grow in them.
translation_verse: Mitso aƒe mianɔ eme. Mitɔ abɔ miado nu ɖe eme aɖu.

english_verse: Get married and have children, then help your sons find wives and help your daughters find husbands, so they can have children as well. I want your numbers to grow, not to get smaller.
translation_verse: Miɖe srɔ̃ miadzi viŋutsuwo kple vinyɔnuwo. Miɖe srɔ̃ na mia viŋutsuwo, eye mitsɔ mia vinyɔnuwo na be woaɖe, ne woadzi viŋutsuviwo kple vinyɔnuviwo. Midzi ɖe edzi le afi ma, eye migazu ʋɛ o.

english_verse: Pray for peace in Babylonia and work hard to make it prosperous. The more successful that nation is, the better off you will be.
translation_verse: Ke midi du si me meɖe aboyo mi ɖo ɖa la me tɔwo ƒe nyonyo. Mido gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ ɖe wo nu, elabe ne nu nyo na dua la, anyo na miawo hã.

english_verse: I will bless you with a future filled with hope—a future of success, not of suffering.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ be: Menya ɖoɖo si mewɔ ɖe mia ŋu. Nunyoname ƒe ɖoɖoe, ke menye vɔ̃ o, mɔkpɔkpɔ li na mi le etsɔ me.

english_verse: You will turn back to me and ask for help, and I will answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Ekema miayɔm, ado gbe ɖa nam eye masee na mi.

english_verse: You will worship me with all your heart, and I will be with you
translation_verse: Miadim, eye miakpɔm. Ne miedim kple miaƒe dzi blibo la,

english_verse: and accept your worship. Then I will gather you from all the nations where I scattered you, and you will return to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: miakpɔm, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Magaɖo miaƒe nunyonamewo te, eye maƒo mia nu ƒu tso dukɔwo katã dome kple teƒe siwo katã menyà mi ɖo ɖa la, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, eye magakplɔ mi ava teƒe si menyà mi dzoe le ɖo ɖe aboyo me la.”

english_verse: You feel secure, because you think I have sent prophets to speak for me in Babylonia.
translation_verse: “Esi miegblɔ be: ‘Aƒetɔ ɖo gbeƒãɖelawo na mi le Babilon’ ta la,

english_verse: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. But you had better listen to me now.
translation_verse: Mi ame siwo katã meɖo ɖe aboyo me tso Yerusalem yi Babilon, mise Aƒetɔ ƒe nya:

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me what would happen to Shemaiah, who was one of our people in Babylonia. After my letter reached Babylonia, Shemaiah wrote letters to the people of Jerusalem, including the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and the other priests. The letter to Zephaniah said:
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Èɖo agbalẽ ɖa, le wò ŋkɔ me, ɖe ame siwo katã le Yerusalem kple nunɔla Zefanya, Maaseya vi kpakple nunɔlawo katã be:

english_verse: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the Lord chose you to be the priest in charge of the temple security force. You know that anyone who acts crazy and pretends to be a prophet should be arrested and put in chains and iron collars.
translation_verse: ‘Aƒetɔ tsɔ wò ɖo nunɔlae ɖe nunɔla Yehoyada teƒe ale be nànye dzikpɔla le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒeme ɖe tsukunɔ ɖe sia ɖe si le gbeƒã ɖem la dzi, nàdee atikpofɔblanu kpekpe me, ade ga kɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Jeremiah from the town of Anathoth is pretending to be a prophet there in Jerusalem, so why haven't you punished him?
translation_verse: Ke nu ka ta mèka mo na Yeremya, Anatotitɔ la esime wòle gbeƒã ɖem na mi o?

english_verse: He even wrote a letter to the people here in Babylonia, saying we would be here a long time. He told us to build homes and to plant gardens and grow our own food.
translation_verse: Elabe eɖo agbalẽ ɖe mí le Babilon be: Miaƒe aboyo me nɔnɔ adidi; mitso aƒe mianɔ eme, mitɔ abɔ miado nu ɖe eme aɖu.’ ”

english_verse: When Zephaniah received Shemaiah's letter, he read it to me.
translation_verse: Nunɔla Zefanya xlẽ agbalẽa na Yeremya, gbeƒãɖela la, wòse.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me what to write in a second letter
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Yeremya be:

english_verse: to the people of Judah who had been taken to Babylonia. In this letter, I wrote that the Lord had said: I, the Lord, have not chosen Shemaiah to be one of my prophets, and he has misled you by telling lies in my name.
translation_verse: “Ɖo ame ɖa, ne woagblɔ na aboyomeawo katã be: ‘Aƒetɔ gblɔ ɖe Semaya, Nexelamitɔ la ŋu be: Esi Semaya ɖe gbeƒã na mi, evɔ wònye nyemedɔe hafi o, eye wòna miele dzi ɖom ɖe alakpanya ŋu ta la,

english_verse: He has even talked you into disobeying me. So I will punish Shemaiah. He and his descendants won't live to see the good things I will do for my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: eya ta Aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, mahe to na Semaya, Nexelamitɔ la kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo. Eƒe dzidzimevi aɖeke masusɔ nɛ anɔ dukɔ sia me, akpɔ nyui si wɔ ge mala na nye dukɔ la o; Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Elabe egblɔ aglãdzenya ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel said, “Jeremiah, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: “Ŋlɔ nya siwo katã megblɔ na wò la ɖe agbalẽ me.

english_verse: Someday I will let my people from both Israel and Judah return to the land I gave their ancestors.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: Elabe kpɔ ɖa, ɣeyiɣi aɖe gbɔna, esime maɖo nye dukɔ, Israel kple Yuda, ƒe nunyonamewo te. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Makplɔ wo agbɔe ava anyigba si metsɔ na wo tɔgbuiwo la dzi, eye woaxɔe wòanye wo tɔ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to Israel and Judah: Screams of terror are heard, with no word of peace.
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ be: Míese ɣli aɖe, dzikatsoameƒo, ŋɔdzi kple ŋutifafa manɔanyi ɣlie.

english_verse: Can men give birth? Then why do I see them looking so pale and clutching their stomachs like women in labor?
translation_verse: Azɔ mibia, eye mibu eŋu kpɔ! Ðe ŋutsu ate ŋu dzi via? Ekema nu ka tae mekpɔ ŋutsu ɖe sia ɖe wòɖo asi ali abe nyɔnu si le ku lém la ene? Nu ka tae mo ɖe sia ɖe fu tititi?

english_verse: My people, soon you will suffer worse than ever before, but I will save you.
translation_verse: Aléle! Ŋkeke ma dzi ŋɔ; ŋkeke aɖeke masɔ kplii o. Xaxaɣi wònye na Yakob gake woaɖee le eme.”

english_verse: Now you are slaves of other nations, but I will break the chains and smash the yokes that keep you in slavery.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Ava eme gbe ma gbe, maŋe woƒe kɔkuti ɖa le woƒe kɔ, atso woƒe kawo, eye amedzrowo magawɔ wo subɔlawoe azɔ o.

english_verse: Then you will be my servants, and I will choose a king for you from the family of David. *
translation_verse: Ke boŋ woasubɔ Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la kple woƒe fia David, ame si meɖo na wo la.”

english_verse: Israel, you belong to me, so don't be afraid. You deserved to be punished; that's why I scattered you in distant nations. But I am with you, and someday I will destroy those nations.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ be: “Mègavɔ̃ o, nye dɔla Yakob. Israel, dzi megaɖe le ƒowò o, elabe kpɔ ɖa, maxɔ na wò tso didiƒe ʋĩi, maxɔ na wò dzidzimeviwo le anyigba si dzi wole aboyo me le. Yakob atrɔ gbɔ va aƒe, anɔ anyi bɔkɔɔ le dziɖeɖi me, eye naneke mado ŋɔdzi nɛ o.

english_verse: Then I will bring you and your descendants back to your land, where I will protect you and give you peace. Then your fears will be gone. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Heal Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Elabe meli kpli wò, ne maɖe wò, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Matsrɔ̃ dukɔ siwo katã dome mekaka mi ɖo ɖa la, ke wò ya, nyematsrɔ̃ wò gbidii o. Mahe to na wò ale si dze pɛpɛpɛ, eye nyemagbe tohehe na wò gbeɖe o.”

english_verse: The Lord said: My people, you are wounded and near death.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ be: “Nu vevi si wɔ wò la, manya da o; abi makumakue nèxɔ.

english_verse: You are accused of a crime with no one to defend you, and you are covered with sores that no medicine can cure. *
translation_verse: Wò nya meka ame aɖeke o, atike aɖeke meli na wò abiawo o; naneke meli woawɔ nàhaya o.

english_verse: Your friends have forgotten you; they don't care anymore. Even I have acted like an enemy. And because your sins are horrible and countless, I will be cruel as I punish you.
translation_verse: Wò ahiãviwo katã ŋlɔ wò be; womegatsɔ ɖeke le eme na wò o, elabe metu nu kpli wò abe futɔ ene, eye mehe to na wò nublanuimakpɔmakpɔtɔe abe ketɔ ene; elabe èɖi fɔ ŋutɔ, eye wò nuvɔ̃wo sɔ gbɔ ale gbegbe.

english_verse: But if your enemies try to rob or destroy you, I will rob and destroy them, and they will be led as captives to foreign lands.
translation_verse: Eya ta ame siwo katã vuvu wò la, woavuvu wo. Wò ketɔwo katã, wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe, ayi aboyo me. Ame siwo ha wò la, woaha woawo hã; ame siwo katã da adzo wò la, woada adzo woawo hã.

english_verse: No one wants you as a friend or cares what happens to you. But I will heal your injuries, and you will get well. The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Elabe mana nàgakpɔ lãmesẽ, eye wò abiawo aku, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, elabe woyɔ wò be amenyàdegbea: ‘Zion si ame aɖeke metsɔ ɖeke le eme na o!’ ”

english_verse: The Lord said: Israel, I will be kind to you and let you come home. Jerusalem now lies in ruins, but you will rebuild it, complete with a new palace.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, magaɖo Yakob ƒe aƒe la ƒe nunyonamewo te, eye makpɔ nublanui na enɔƒewo. Woagatso du la ɖe eƒe togbɛa dzi, eye fiasã la anɔ teƒe si wònɔ tsã la.

english_verse: Other nations will respect and honor you. Your homes will be filled with children, and you will celebrate, singing praises to me.
translation_verse: Akpedahawo aɖi tso teƒe mawo, eye dzidzɔkpɔlawo ƒe gbe aɖi atso afi ma. Mana woadzi asɔ gbɔ, eye womazu ʋɛ o. Made bubu wo ŋu, eye womaɖi gbɔ wo o.

english_verse: It will be just like old times. Your nation will worship me, and I will punish anyone who abuses you.
translation_verse: Wo viwo aganɔ abe ale si wonɔ tsã la ene. Woƒe amehawo ali ke le ŋkunye me, eye mahe to na ame siwo katã te wo ɖe anyi la.

english_verse: One of your own people will become your ruler. And when I invite him to come near me at the place of worship, he will do so. No one would dare to come near without being invited.
translation_verse: Woƒe amegã anye wo dometɔ ɖeka, eye wo dziɖula ado tso wo dome. Mana wòate va gbɔnye, eye wòate ɖe ŋunye elabe ame kae ate ŋu ado dzi ate ɖe ŋunye? Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: I am furious! And like a violent storm I will strike those who do wrong.
translation_verse: Mikpɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe ahom ɖa! Dɔmedzoe do yina. Ele totrom abe yali ene, eye wòbla ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe ta kɔtɔɔ.

english_verse: I won't calm down until I have finished what I have decided to do. Someday, you will understand what I mean.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe dziku helihelĩ la nu mafa o va se ɖe esime wòwɔ nu si wòɖo be yeawɔ wu enu vɔ keŋ hafi. Emegbe la, miase egɔme nyuie.

english_verse: The Lord said: Israel, I promise that someday all your tribes will again be my people, and I will be your God.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Ɣe ma ɣi la, manye Mawu na Israel-ƒomeawo katã, eye woawo anye nye dukɔ.”

english_verse: In the desert I was kind to those who escaped death. I gave them peace, and when the time is right, I'll do the same for you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Rebuild Israel
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Dukɔ si tsi agbe tso yi nu kpɔ amenuveve le gbedadaƒo. Esime Israel nɔ gbɔɖemeƒe dim la,

english_verse: Some time ago, the Lord appeared to me and told me to say: Israel, I will always love you; that's why I've been so patient and kind.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖe eɖokui fiae le didiƒe. Melɔ̃ wò kple lɔlɔ̃ mavɔ, eya tae meyi edzi le nuteƒe wɔm na wò ɖo.

english_verse: You are precious to me, and so I will rebuild your nation. Once again you will dance for joy and play your tambourines.
translation_verse: Israel, ɖetugbi leaƒe, matso wò, eye nànye du si wotso nyateƒe. Àgatsɔ wò asiʋuiwo age ɖe tò me anɔ dzidzɔkpɔlawo dome aɖu ɣe.

english_verse: You will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria and enjoy the grapes.
translation_verse: Àgade waingble ɖe Samaria-towo ŋu, agblea delawo ado nu, eye woaɖu eƒe kutsetse.

english_verse: Someday those who guard the hill country of Ephraim will shout, “Let's go to Zion and worship the Lord our God.” Israel Will Return to Its Own Land
translation_verse: Elabe ɣeyiɣi aɖe gbɔna esi dzi gbetakpɔlawo ado ɣli le Efrayim-towo dzi be: ‘Mitso, mina míayi Zion ɖe Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la gbɔ!’ ”

english_verse: The Lord says: Celebrate and sing for Israel, the greatest of nations. Offer praises and shout, “Come and rescue your people, Lord! Save what's left of Israel.”
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ be: “Midzi ha sesĩe kple dzidzɔ na Yakob, eye mitso aseye ɖe dukɔwo ƒe tatɔ ŋu! Miɖe gbeƒã, mikafui, eye migblɔ be: ‘Aƒetɔ xɔ eƒe dukɔ ɖe agbe! Exɔ na Israelvi siwo susɔ la!’

english_verse: I, the Lord, will bring my people back from Babylonia and everywhere else on earth. The blind and the lame will be there. Expectant mothers and women about to give birth will come and be part of that great crowd.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, makplɔ wo tso dzigbemenyigbawo dzi agbɔe. Maƒo wo nu ƒu tso keke didiƒewo ʋĩi ke le anyigba dzi vɛ. Ŋkunɔwo, xɔdrɔ̃wo, funɔwo, nyɔnu siwo le ku lém gɔ̃ hã anɔ wo dome! Wo katã anɔ hame hoo atrɔ gbɔ va afii.

english_verse: They will weep and pray as I bring them home. I will lead them to streams of water. They will walk on a level road and not stumble. I am a father to Israel, my favorite children.
translation_verse: Woanɔ avi dzi ava, eye woanɔ koko ƒom makplɔ wo vɛ. Makplɔ wo to mɔ dzɔdzɔe dzi ayi tɔʋuwo to; womakli nu o, elabe tɔ́e menye na Israel, eye Efrayim nye vinye ŋgɔgbea.”

english_verse: Listen to me, you nations nearby or across the sea. I scattered the people of Israel, but I will gather them again. I will protect them like a shepherd guarding a flock;
translation_verse: “Dukɔwo, mise Aƒetɔ ƒe nya! Miɖe gbeƒãe le ƒutanyigbawo dzi le didiƒe ʋĩi be: ‘Eya, ame si kaka Israel hlẽ la, agaƒo enu ƒu, eye wòakpɔ edzi abe ale si alẽkplɔla kpɔa eƒe alẽhawo dzii ene.’

english_verse: I will rescue them from enemies who could overpower them.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ xɔ Yakob ƒle tso aboyo me heɖee tso asi si sẽ wui la me.

english_verse: My people will come to Mount Zion and celebrate; their faces will glow because of my blessings. I'll give them grain, grapes, and olive oil, as well as sheep and cattle. Israel will be prosperous and grow like a garden with plenty of water.
translation_verse: Woava dzi ha sesĩe kple dzidzɔ le Zion-togbɛ la dzi, eye dzi adzɔ wo le nu nyui si Aƒetɔ wɔ la ŋu. Woakpɔ dzidzɔ le lu, wain kple ami, alẽviwo ƒe ha kple nyihawo ŋu. Woanɔ agbe abe abɔ si wode tsii ene, eye womagaxa nu azɔ o.

english_verse: Young women and young men, together with the elderly, will celebrate and dance, because I will comfort them and turn their sorrow into happiness.
translation_verse: Ekema ɖetugbiwo akpɔ dzidzɔ aɖu ɣe; ɖekakpuiwo kple ame tsitsiwo atso aseye. Matrɔ woƒe nuxaxa wòazu dzidzɔ. Mafa akɔ na wo, eye mana woakpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe konyifafa teƒe.

english_verse: I will bless my people with more food than they need, and the priests will enjoy the choice cuts of meat. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Offers Hope
translation_verse: Mana nuɖuɖu nasu nunɔlawo ƒe luʋɔ, eye maɖi ƒo na nye dukɔ kple nye nu nyui geɖe.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Aƒetɔ akpɔ nublanui na Israel

english_verse: In Ramah a voice is heard, crying and weeping loudly. Rachel mourns for her children and refuses to be comforted, because they are dead. *
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Gbe aɖe le ɖiɖim le Rama. Konyifafa kple avifafa kutɔkutɔ ƒe gbee. Raxel ye le fafam na viawo, eye wògbe be womegafa akɔ na ye le ɖeviawo ta o elabe womegali o.”

english_verse: But I, the Lord, say to dry your tears. Someday your children will come home from the enemy's land. Then all you have done for them will be greatly rewarded.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Dzudzɔ avia fafa, nàtutu ŋkume elabe woaxe dɔ si nèwɔ la ƒe fetu na wò, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, eye woagatrɔ gbɔ tso futɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: So don't lose hope. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mɔkpɔkpɔ li na wò le etsɔ me, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, eye viwòwo agatrɔ va woawo ŋutɔ wo de.

english_verse: The people of Israel moan and say to me, “We were like wild bulls, but you, Lord, broke us, and we learned to obey. You are our God— please let us come home.
translation_verse: Mese Efrayim xa nu be: ‘Èhe to nam, eye mebɔbɔ ɖokuinye xɔe kpoo. Mele abe nyivi si womemla o ene. Gakplɔm gbɔe, ne magatrɔ ɖe ŋuwò, elabe wòe nye Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu.

english_verse: When we were young, we strayed and sinned, but then we realized what we had done. We are ashamed and disgraced and want to return to you.”
translation_verse: Elabe esi meɖe ɖa le ŋuwò la, metrɔ dzime. Esi medze si nu si mewɔ la, meƒo aklito. Ŋu kpem, eye gbɔgblɔ bu ɖem, elabe nye ɖekakpuime ŋukpenanuwo zu ŋukpe nam.’

english_verse: People of Israel, you are my own dear children. Don't I love you best of all? Though I often make threats, I want you to be near me, so I will have mercy on you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ɖe Efrayim nye vinye ŋutsu lɔlɔ̃a? Eyae nye vinye si gbɔ nyemelɔ̃a nu le oa? Elabe zi ale si menyale nya aɖe gblɔm ɖe eŋu ko la, meɖoa ŋku edzi kokoko. Eya ta nye dzi le edim vevie; makpɔ nublanui nɛ godoo,” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: With rock piles and signposts, mark the road well, my dear people. The road by which you left by will now lead you home.
translation_verse: “Fɔ kpewo ɖo ɖe mɔ to na ɖokuiwò nàtsɔ de dzesi mɔ lae. Tu dzesidenu siwo akpe ɖe ŋuwò la ɖi. Lé ŋku ɖe mɔ gã si nèto yi la ŋu. Israel ɖetugbi leaƒe, trɔ gbɔ, trɔ gbɔ va mia dedu siawo me.

english_verse: Will you ever decide to be faithful? I will make sure that someday things will be different, as different as a woman protecting a man. The Lord Will Bring Judah Home
translation_verse: Vinyɔnu mawɔnuteƒe, ɣe ka ɣi nàtsa tsa glãla ase ɖo? Elabe Aƒetɔ wɔ nu yeye aɖe ɖe anyigba dzi: nyɔnu le ŋutsu ta ʋlim.” Nunyonamewo gbɔna na Mawu ƒe dukɔ

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, said: I promise to set the people of Judah free and to lead them back to their hometowns. And when I do, they will once again say, “We pray that the Lord will bless his home, the sacred hill in Jerusalem where his temple stands.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: “Ne megaɖo dukɔ la ƒe nunyonamewo te la, woagawɔ nyagbɔgblɔ sia ŋudɔ le Yuda-nyigba dzi kple eƒe duwo me be: ‘Aƒetɔ ayra wò, wò nu dzɔdzɔe wɔƒe! Wò togbɛ kɔkɔe!’

english_verse: The people will live in Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah. Some will be farmers, and others will be shepherds.
translation_verse: Amewo anɔ Yuda kple eƒe duwo katã me. Agbledelawo kple ame siwo ʋuna kple woƒe lãhawo tso teƒe yi teƒe la hã akpe ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: Those who feel tired and worn out will find new life and energy,
translation_verse: Elabe mana ŋusẽ naɖo ame siwo ŋu ɖeɖi te la ŋu, eye manyi ame siwo katã dɔ le wuwum la.”

english_verse: and when they sleep, they will wake up refreshed.
translation_verse: Afi mae menyɔ le, eye mekpɔ be alɔ̃ vivi nam.

english_verse: Someday, Israel and Judah will be my field where my people and their livestock will grow.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ɣeyiɣi gbɔna, esime mana amegbetɔwo kple lãwo nadzi ɖe Israel-nyigba kple Yuda-nyigba dzi fũu abe nukuwo meƒã ene.

english_verse: In the past, I took care to uproot them, to tear them down, and to destroy them. But when that day comes, I will take care to plant them and help them grow.
translation_verse: Ava eme be ale si menɔ ŋute ɖe wo ŋu be maho wo, agbã wo, aɖe wo ɖa, atsrɔ̃ wo, eye mana vɔ̃ nadzɔ ɖe wo dzi la, nenema ke maganɔ ŋudzɔ ɖe wo ŋu be matu wo, eye mado woe. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: No longer will anyone go around saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi la, womagblɔ be: ‘Vi tɔ́wo ɖu waintsetse hɔhlɔ̃e, aɖu nyɔ viwo’ o.

english_verse: When that day comes, only those who eat sour grapes will get the sour taste, and only those who sin will be put to death. The New Agreement with Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Ke ame sia ame aku ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe nuvɔ̃ si wòwɔ la ta; ame sia ame si ɖu waintsetse hɔhlɔ̃e la, eyae aɖu anyɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said: The time will surely come when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, ɣeyiɣi gbɔna, esime mabla nu yeye kple Israel ƒe aƒe kple Yuda ƒe aƒe.

english_verse: It will be different from the agreement I made with their ancestors when I led them out of Egypt. Although I was their God, they broke that agreement.
translation_verse: Eya manɔ abe esi mebla kple wo tɔgbuiwo esime melé woƒe alɔnu hekplɔ wo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi la ene o; nye nubabla si wotu togbɔ be menɔ na wo abe srɔ̃ŋutsu ene hã. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Here is the new agreement that I, the Lord, will make with the people of Israel: “I will write my laws on their hearts and minds. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ be: Nu, si mele babla ge kple Israel-dukɔ le ŋkeke mawo megbe lae nye esi: Matsɔ nye se la ade wo me, eye maŋlɔe ɖe woƒe dzi ŋu. Manye woƒe Mawu, eye woawo anye nye dukɔ.

english_verse: “No longer will they have to teach one another to obey me. I, the Lord, promise that all of them will obey me, ordinary people and rulers alike. I will forgive their sins and forget the evil things they have done.”
translation_verse: Ame aɖeke magafia nu ehavi alo agblɔ na nɔvia be: ‘Dze si Aƒetɔ’ o, elabe ame sia ame adze sim tso ame gblɔewo dzi va se ɖe ame ŋkutawo dzi; elabe matsɔ woƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ake wo, eye nyemagaɖo ŋku woƒe nuvɔ̃ dzi o.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful. I command the sun to give light each day, the moon and stars to shine at night, and ocean waves to roar.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, ame si na ŋusẽ ɣe be wòaklẽ le ŋkeke me, eye wòɖoe na ɣleti kple ɣletiviwo be woaklẽ le zã me; eya ame si blua atsiaƒu ale be eƒe tsotsoewo dzea agbo, ame si ŋkɔe nye Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la, be:

english_verse: I will never forget to give those commands, and I will never let Israel stop being a nation. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: “Ne ɖoɖo matrɔmatrɔ sia trɔ le ŋkunye me la, ekema Israel ƒe dzidzime aɖeke hã maganɔ anyi abe dukɔ ene le ŋkunye me akpɔ gbeɖe o.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Can you measure the heavens? Can you explore the depths of the earth? That's how hard it would be for me to reject Israel forever, even though they have sinned. I, the Lord, have spoken. Jerusalem Will Be Rebuilt
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Ne woate ŋu adzidze dziƒowo le dzime, eye woate ŋu atsa le anyigba ƒe gɔmeɖoɖowo ŋu le to me kpɔ la, ekema magbe Israel ƒe dzidzimeviwo katã le nu siwo katã wowɔ la ta.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: The Lord said: Someday, Jerusalem will truly belong to me. It will be rebuilt with a boundary line running from Hananel Tower to Corner Gate.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ɣeyiɣi gbɔna, esime woagbugbɔ du la atso na Aƒetɔ. Atso Xananel ƒe xɔ tsrala la gbɔ va se ɖe Dzogoegbo la nu.

english_verse: From there, the boundary will go in a straight line to Gareb Hill, then turn toward Goah.
translation_verse: Liƒoa azɔ tso afi ma le ɣetoɖoƒe ato Gareb ƒe togbɛ dzi tẽe, eye wòanye kpò aɖo ta Goa.

english_verse: Even that disgusting Hinnom Valley will be sacred to me, and so will the eastern slopes that go down from Horse Gate into Kidron Valley. Jerusalem will never again be destroyed.
translation_verse: Bali si me woɖia ame ɖo, afi si woƒoa ƒu dzowɔ hã ɖo kple agble siwo katã le afi ma yi ɖake ɖe Kidron-tɔʋu la nu va do ɖe Sɔgbo la ƒe dzogoe dzi la, anɔ kɔkɔe na Aƒetɔ. Womagagblẽ dua alo agbãe akpɔ gbeɖe o.”

english_verse: The Lord spoke to me in the tenth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Le Zedekiya, Yuda-fia, ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè ewolia me, si nye Nebukadnezar ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè wui enyilia me la, Aƒetɔ ƒo nu kple Yeremya.

english_verse: At that time, the Babylonian army had surrounded Jerusalem, and I was in the prison at the courtyard of the palace guards.
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, Babilon-fia ƒe aʋakɔ ɖe to ɖe Yerusalem. Wode Yeremya, gbeƒãɖela la, gaxɔ me ɖe dzɔlawo ƒe xɔxɔnu si le Yuda-fia ƒe fiasã me.

english_verse: Zedekiah had ordered me to be held there because I told everyone that the Lord had said: I am the Lord, and I am about to let the king of Babylonia conquer Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Elabe Yuda-fia Zedekiya dee gaxɔ me ɖe afi sia gblɔ be: “Nu ka ta nèɖe gbeƒã gblɔ ɖi be: ‘Aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, mele du sia tsɔ ge ade asi na Babilon-fia, eye wòaxɔe.

english_verse: King Zedekiah will be captured and taken to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will speak with him face to face.
translation_verse: Yuda-fia Zedekiya masí le Kaldeatɔwo si me o, ke boŋ woatsɔe ade asi na Babilon-fia, eye wo kple evea ado go ŋkume kple ŋkume akpɔ wo nɔewo.

english_verse: Then Zedekiah will be led away to Babylonia, where he will stay until I am finished with him. So, if you people of Judah fight against the Babylonians, you will lose. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Akplɔ Zedekiya ayi Babilon, eye wòanɔ afi ma va se ɖe esime mava egbɔ. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Togbɔ be nèle aʋa wɔm kple Kaldeatɔwo hã la, màɖu dzi o.’ ”

english_verse: Later, when I was in prison, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Yeremya gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ gblɔ nam be:

english_verse: Jeremiah, your cousin Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, will visit you. He must sell his field near the town of Anathoth, and because you are his nearest relative, you have the right and the responsibility to buy it and keep it in the family.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, tɔwòɖea Salum vi, Xanameel ava gbɔwò agblɔ be: ‘Xɔ nye agble si le Anatot la ƒle, elabe wòe nye ƒometɔ si dze axɔe aƒle.’

english_verse: Hanamel came, just as the Lord had promised. And he said, “Please buy my field near Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. You have the right to buy it, and if you do, it will stay in our family.” The Lord had told me to buy it
translation_verse: Ale Xanameel va gbɔnye le dzɔlawo ƒe xɔxɔnu, abe ale si Aƒetɔ gblɔ ene, eye wògblɔ nam be: ‘Xɔ nye agble si le Anatot le Benyamin-nutome la ƒle, elabe wòe nye ƒometɔ si dze axɔe wòazu tɔwò. Ƒlee na ɖokuiwò.’ Tete mekpɔe dze sii azɔ be Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ ƒe gbedeasie.”

english_verse: Lord God, you stretched out your mighty arm and made the sky and the earth. You can do anything.
translation_verse: ‘O Aƒetɔ Mawu! Wòe tsɔ wò ŋusẽ triakɔ kple wò abɔ sesẽ wɔ dziƒowo kple anyigbae. Naneke wɔwɔ megloa wò o.

english_verse: And while he, the witnesses, and all the other Jews sitting in the courtyard were still watching, I gave both copies to Baruch son of Neriah.
translation_verse: Metsɔ agbalẽ si nu wotre la de asi na Barux, Neriya vi, si nye Maxseya tɔgbuiyɔvi la. Metsɔe nɛ le Xanameel, tɔnyeɖea vi la kple ɖasefo siwo ŋlɔ woƒe ŋkɔdzesiwo ɖe nuƒlegbalẽa te la ŋkume.

english_verse: I told Baruch that the Lord had said: Take both copies of this bill of sale, one sealed shut and the other open, and put them in a clay jar so they will last a long time.
translation_verse: ‘Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la gblɔ be: Tsɔ nuƒlegbalẽ eve siawo, esi nu wotre kple eƒe gbugbɔŋlɔ si le ʋuʋu la, de ze me da ɖi, ne woate ŋu anɔ anyi wòadidi.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I promise you that people will once again buy and sell houses, farms, and vineyards in this country. Jeremiah Questions the Lord
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la gblɔ be: ‘Woagaƒle xɔwo, agblewo kple waingblewo le anyigba sia dzi.’ ” Yeremya ƒe gbedodoɖa

english_verse: You show kindness for a thousand generations, but you also punish people for the sins of their parents. You are the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Èɖe wò amenuveve fia ame akpe nanewo, ke nèhe to na viwo ɖe wo tɔgbuiwo ƒe vo siwo woda la ta. Mawu gã ŋusẽtɔ, wò ŋkɔe nye Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla.

english_verse: With great wisdom you make plans, and with your great power you do all the mighty things you planned. Nothing we do is hidden from your eyes, and you reward or punish us as we deserve.
translation_verse: Wò adaŋudede de to, eye wò nuwɔwɔwo wɔ nuku. Wò ame si ƒe ŋkuwo le nu siwo katã amegbetɔwo wɔna la ŋu, eye nèɖoa eteƒe na ame sia ame ɖe eƒe nuwɔna ƒe metsonu nu;

english_verse: You are famous because you worked miracles in Egypt, and you are still working them in Israel and in the rest of the world as well.
translation_verse: wò ame si wɔ dzesi kple nukunuwo le Egipte-nyigba dzi gbe aɖe gbe, eye nèyi edzi gale wo wɔm le Israel kple amegbetɔƒomea katã dome va ɖo fifia. Èna wò ŋkɔ de du va se ɖe egbe ŋkeke siawo me gɔ̃ hã.

english_verse: You terrified the Egyptians with your miracles, and you reached out your mighty arm and rescued your people Israel from Egypt.
translation_verse: Ètsɔ dzesiwo kple nukunuwo, wò ŋusẽsi sesẽ la kple wò abɔ kpakple ŋɔdzi gã kplɔ wò dukɔ tso Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Then you gave Israel this land rich with milk and honey, just as you had promised our ancestors.
translation_verse: Ètsɔ anyigba sia na wo, le atam si nèka na wo tɔgbuiwo be yele anyigba si dzi notsi kple anyitsi le la na ge wo la nu.

english_verse: Jerusalem is under attack, and we suffer from hunger and disease. The Babylonians have already built dirt ramps up to the walls of our city, and you can see that Jerusalem will be captured just as you said.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, futɔwo ƒo kpo ƒo xlã dua be yewoaxɔe. Dua le gege ge ɖe Kaldeatɔ siwo le aʋa wɔm kplii la si me godoo, elabe aʋawɔwɔ, dɔwuame kple dɔ vɔ̃ gbɔna. Nya si nègblɔ la va eme tututu abe ale si wò ŋutɔ nèle ekpɔm ene.

english_verse: So why did you tell me to get some witnesses and buy a field with my silver, when Jerusalem is about to be captured by the Babylonians? The Lord Explains about the Field
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu, nya la le alea vɔ tso hafi nègblɔ nam be: Ɖe ga nàtsɔ ƒle anyigba, eye ɖasefowo nanɔ asiwò ɖe eŋu! Evɔ dua ge ɖe Kaldeatɔwo si me vɔ xoxo!’ ”

english_verse: The Lord explained:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Yeremya be:

english_verse: Jeremiah, I am the Lord God. I rule the world, and I can do anything!
translation_verse: “Kpɔ ɖa, nyee nye Aƒetɔ, nu gbagbewo katã ƒe Mawu; ɖe nanewɔwɔ agloma?

english_verse: It is true that I am going to let King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia capture Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Eya ta, Aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, matsɔ du sia ade asi na Kaldeatɔwo, eye mana Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar naxɔe.

english_verse: The Babylonian army is already attacking, and they will capture the city and set it on fire. The people of Jerusalem have made me angry by going up to the flat roofs of their houses and burning incense to Baal and offering wine sacrifices to other gods. Now these houses will be burned to the ground!
translation_verse: Kaldeatɔ siwo le aʋa wɔm kple dua la age ɖe eme, eye woatɔ dzoe wòafiã; afiã kple eƒe xɔwo keŋ. Xɔ siawo tamee wotɔ dzo lifi na Baal le, eye woƒo tsi ɖi na mawu bubuwo le, be yewoatsɔ do dziku nam.

english_verse: They have set up repulsive idols in my temple, and now it isn't a fit place to worship me.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ woƒe ŋunyɔnuwo ɖo aƒe si ŋu woyɔ nye ŋkɔ ɖo la me, eye wogblẽ kɔ ɖo na teƒea.

english_verse: And they led Judah into sin by building places to worship Baal in Hinnom Valley, where they also sacrificed their sons and daughters to the god Molech. I have never even imagined they would commit such disgusting sins.
translation_verse: Wowɔ nuxeƒewo ɖe Hinom vi ƒe balia me na Baal, ne woakɔ wo viŋutsuwo kple wo vinyɔnuwo siaa aɖasa vɔ na mawu Molex le teƒe mawo, evɔ la, nyemebia tso wo si nenema o. Gawu la, meva tame nam kpɔ be woawɔ ŋunyɔnu sia ahatsɔ he Yuda-dukɔ la de nuvɔ̃ me o.” Mawu do ŋugbe be yeagaɖo dukɔ la te

english_verse: Jeremiah, what you said is true. The people of Jerusalem are suffering from hunger and disease, and so the king of Babylonia will be able to capture Jerusalem.
translation_verse: “Eya ta azɔ la, Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔ ɖe du sia, si ŋu miawo miele gbɔgblɔm le be: ‘Wotsɔe de asi na Babilon-fia to aʋawɔwɔ, dɔwuame kple dɔ vɔ̃ dzi’ la ŋu be:

english_verse: I am angry with the people of Jerusalem, and I will scatter them in foreign countries. But someday I will bring them back here and let them live in safety.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, maƒo wo nu ƒu tso anyigba siwo katã dzi menyà wo ɖo ɖa, le dziku kple dɔmedzoe me, esime menɔ nyanyram vevie la dzi. Makplɔ wo agbugbɔ va teƒe sia, eye mana woanɔ anyi le dziɖeɖi me.

english_verse: They will be my people, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Woanye nye dukɔ, eye manye woƒe Mawu.

english_verse: Even though I have brought disaster on the people, I will someday do all these good things for them.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ be: “Ale si mehe vɔ̃ gã sia va dukɔ sia dzii la, nenema ke mahe nunyoname siwo katã ŋugbe medo na wo la hã vɛ na woe.

english_verse: Jeremiah, when you bought the field, you showed that fields will someday be bought and sold again. You say that this land has been conquered by the Babylonians and has become a desert, emptied of people and animals.
translation_verse: Miele gbɔgblɔm be anyigba sia zu gbegbe, amegbetɔ alo lã megale edzi o, eye wotsɔe de Kaldeatɔwo si. Ke woaƒle agble le anyigba sia dzi.

english_verse: But someday, people will again spend their silver to buy fields everywhere—in the territory of Benjamin, the region around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and in the hill country, the foothills to the west, and the Southern Desert. Buyers and sellers and witnesses will sign and seal the bills of sale for the fields. It will happen, because I will give this land back to my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Amewo aɖe ga agaƒle agblewoe. Woade wo agbalẽ me, aŋlɔ woƒe ŋkɔdzesiwo ɖe wo te, atre wo nu, eye woaɖo ɖasefowo ɖe wo ŋu. Esia ava eme le Benyamin-nyigba dzi, le Yerusalem-nutowo me, le Yuda-duwo me, le togbɛ dzi duwo me, le baliwo kple anyigbemekegbegbe me. Elabe magaɖo dukɔa te kple nunyonamewo.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: I was still being held prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guards when the Lord told me: I am the Lord, and I created the whole world.
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, ame si wɔ xexea me, eya ame si trɔ asi le eŋu be wòanɔ te ɖaa, ame si ŋkɔ nye Aƒetɔ la be:

english_verse: Ask me, and I will tell you things that you don't know and can't find out.
translation_verse: Yɔm, ekema matɔ na wò, eye maɖe nu gã kako, siwo mènya o la, afia wò.

english_verse: Then someday, I will heal this place and my people as well, and let them enjoy unending peace.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, mahe lãmesẽ kple dɔyɔyɔ vɛ, eye mada gbe le wo ŋu. Mana nu nasu wo si fũu, eye woanɔ anyi le dziɖeɖi blibo me.

english_verse: I will give this land to Israel and Judah once again, and I will make them as strong as they were before.
translation_verse: Magbugbɔ Yuda-dukɔ kple Israel-dukɔ ƒe nu nyuiwo vɛ na wo, eye magaɖo wo te abe tsã ene.

english_verse: They sinned and rebelled against me, but I will forgive them and take away their guilt.
translation_verse: Maklɔ nuvɔ̃ siwo katã wowɔ ɖe ŋunye la ɖa le wo ŋu, eye matsɔ nuvɔ̃ si wowɔ ɖe ŋunye kple aglã si wodze ɖe ŋunye la ƒe fɔɖiɖi ake wo.

english_verse: When that happens, all nations on earth will see the good things I have done for Jerusalem, and how I have given it complete peace. The nations will celebrate and praise and honor me, but they will also tremble with fear because of the powerful things I have done.
translation_verse: Du sia anye dzidzɔŋkɔ, kafukafu kple bubu nam le dukɔwo katã ŋkume le anyigba dzi, ne wose nu nyui siwo katã mewɔ na wo la. Woavɔ̃, adzo nyànyanya le nyui kple nunyoname siwo katã menae la ta.”

english_verse: Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Miele gbɔgblɔm le teƒe sia ŋu be: ‘Ezu gbegbe, amegbetɔ alo lã aɖeke megali o’, le Yuda-duwo kple Yerusalem ƒe ablɔ siwo le ƒuƒlu, eye amegbetɔ alo lãwo megale wo me o la, afi ma miagase

english_verse: happy voices and the sounds of parties and wedding celebrations. And when people come to my temple to offer sacrifices to thank me, you will hear them say: “We praise you, Lord All-Powerful! You are good to us, and your love never fails.” The land will once again be productive.
translation_verse: ŋugbetɔsrɔ̃ ƒe gbe kple ŋugbetɔ ƒe gbe, miase amewo ƒe hadzidzi, eye woatsɔ akpedadanunanawo ava Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒeme anɔ gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Mida akpe na Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la, elabe eƒe dɔme nyo, eye eƒe amenuveve li tegbee!’ Elabe magagbugbɔ anyigba la ƒe nunyonamewo nɛ abe tsã ene.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Now it is empty, without people or animals. But when that time comes, shepherds will take care of their flocks in pastures near every town in the hill country, in the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert, in the land of the Benjamin tribe, and around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord's Wonderful Promise
translation_verse: Alẽhawo agato wo xlẽla ƒe asi te le du siwo le togbɛnyigbawo dzi, du siwo le Yuda ƒe anyigbeme, du siwo le anyigbemekegbegbe, le Benyamin-nyigba dzi, teƒe siwo ƒo xlã Yerusalem kple du siwo le Yuda.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: The Lord said: I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ɣeyiɣi gbɔna, esime mawɔ ŋugbe si medo na Israel-dukɔ kple Yuda-dukɔ la dzi.

english_verse: I promise that the time will come when I will appoint a king from the family of David, a king who will be honest and rule with justice.
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, mana Atilɔ, nu dzɔdzɔe wɔla aɖe nadze na David. Eya adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu dzɔdzɔe eye wòawɔ nu dzɔdzɔe le anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: In those days, Judah will be safe; Jerusalem will have peace and will be named, “The Lord Gives Justice.”
translation_verse: Woaxɔ Yuda ɖe agbe, eye Yerusalem anɔ anyi le tomefafa me le ɣe ma ɣi me. Ŋkɔ si woayɔ nɛ lae nye: ‘Aƒetɔ, míaƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The king of Israel will be one of David's descendants,
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ be: “David ƒe dzidzimevi si aɖu fia le eƒe fiazikpui dzi la, nu matso akpɔ o,

english_verse: and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
translation_verse: eye nunɔlawo atso Levi viwo dome ɣe sia ɣi asubɔm, asa numemevɔ, atɔ dzo nuɖuɖuvɔ, eye woasa vɔ le ŋkunye me tegbee.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Yeremya be:

english_verse: I, the Lord, have an agreement with day and night, so they always come at the right time. You can't break the agreement I made with them,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Ne àte ŋu tu nye nubabla kple ŋkeke kple nye nubabla kple zã be ŋu nake le ekeɣi, eye zã nado le edoɣi la,

english_verse: and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel,
translation_verse: ekema nye nu, si mebla kple nye dɔla David hã atu eye eƒe dzidzimevi aɖeke maganɔ eƒe fiazikpui dzi o, eye nye nu, si mebla kple Levi viwo, nye nunɔlawo hã atu.

english_verse: and there will be more descendants of David and of the priests from the Levi tribe than stars in the sky or grains of sand on the beach.
translation_verse: Ale si womate ŋu axlẽ dziƒo ŋu nuwo, eye womate ŋu adzidze ƒutake o la, nenemae madzi nye dɔla David kple Levi viwo, ame siwo subɔam la, ƒe dzidzimeviwo ɖe edzii.”

english_verse: The Lord also said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Yeremya be:

english_verse: You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
translation_verse: “Mèlé to ɖe nya si gblɔm ame siawo le la ŋu oa? Wobe: ‘Aƒetɔ gbe ƒome eve siwo wòtia la.’ Ale wole alɔ me ɖem le nye dukɔ ŋu, eye womeganye dukɔ le wo ŋkume azɔ o.

english_verse: Jeremiah, I will never break my agreement with the day and the night or let the sky and the earth stop obeying my commands.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: Ne nyemebla nu kple ŋkeke kple zã, eye nyemewɔ ɖoɖo na dziƒo kple anyigba o la,

english_verse: In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
translation_verse: ekema magbe Yakob kple nye dɔla David ƒe dzidzimeviwo. Nyematia David ƒe dzidzimevi aɖeke be wòaɖu Abraham, Isak kple Yakob ƒe dzidzimeviwo dzi o. Elabe magbugbɔ woƒe nunyonamewo na wo, eye makpɔ nublanui na wo.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar had a large army made up of people from every kingdom in his empire. He and his army were attacking Jerusalem and all the nearby towns, when the Lord told me
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒo nu kple Yeremya esime Nebukadnezar, Babilon-fia kple eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la, fiaɖuƒe siwo katã le anyigba, siwo dzi ɖum wòle kple dukɔ siwo katã le aʋa wɔm kple Yerusalem kpakple eƒe du siwo katã ƒo xlãe la.

english_verse: to say to King Zedekiah: I am the Lord, and I am going to let Nebuchadnezzar capture this city and burn it down.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: “Yi ɖagblɔ na Zedekiya, Yuda-fia be: ‘Aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, mele du sia tsɔm de asi na Babilon-fia be wòatɔ dzoe.

english_verse: You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Màsí ado le esi me o, ke boŋ woalé wò atsɔ de asi nɛ godoo. Àkpɔ Babilon-fia ŋkume kple ŋkume, eye àƒo nu kplii ŋkume kple ŋkume, eye àyi Babilon.’

english_verse: You will die a peaceful death. People will mourn when you die, and they will light bonfires in your honor, just as they did for your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you.
translation_verse: Àku le ŋutifafa me. Woado lifidzudzɔ na wò abe ale si wowɔnɛ na tɔgbuiwòwo, fia siwo ku va yi la ene. Woafa wò be: ‘Ao! Tɔgbui yi aƒe! Elabe nyee gblɔ nya la. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.’ ”

english_verse: I went to Zedekiah and told him what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Tete Yeremya, gbeƒãɖela la gblɔ nya siawo katã na Zedekiya, Yuda-fia la, le Yerusalem.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king of Babylonia was trying to break through the walls of Lachish, Azekah, and Jerusalem, the only three towns of Judah that had not been captured. The People Break a Promise
translation_verse: Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, Babilon-fia ƒe aʋakɔ le aʋa wɔm kple Yerusalem kple Laxis kpakple Aseka siwo nye Yuda-du sesẽ siwo ko susɔ ɖi la hã. Wowɔ ayemenu ɖe kluviwo ŋu

english_verse: King Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Jerusalem made an agreement to free all Hebrew men and women who were slaves. No Jew would keep another as a slave. And so, all the Jewish slaves were given their freedom.
translation_verse: Amegãwo katã kple ame bubu ɖe sia ɖe lɔ̃ ɖe nya sia dzi, eye wobla nu be ame sia ame naɖe asi le eƒe kluvi ŋu; eɖanye ŋutsu alo nyɔnu o. Ame aɖeke naganye kluvi na ame aɖeke azɔ o. Ale wowɔ ɖoɖo la dzi, ɖe asi le kluviwo ŋu.

english_verse: But those slave owners changed their minds and forced their former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Gake emegbe la, wogatrɔ kplɔ kluviawo, ŋutsuawo kple nyɔnuawo siaa, siwo ŋu woɖe asi le la vɛ, eye wozi wo dzi wogazu woƒe kluviwo.

english_verse: That's when the Lord told me to say to the people:
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedeasi va na Yeremya be:

english_verse: I am the Lord God of Israel, and I made an agreement with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, where they had been slaves.
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Mebla nu kple mia tɔgbuiwo esime mekplɔ wo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi, tso aƒe si me wonye kluviwo le la, eye megblɔ na wo be:

english_verse: As part of this agreement, you must let a Hebrew slave go free after six years of service. Your ancestors did not obey me,
translation_verse: ‘Le ƒe ade sia ƒe ade ƒe nuwuwu la, mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe neɖe asi le nɔvia Hebritɔ si wodzra nɛ, eye wòsubɔe ƒe ade la ŋuti. Miɖe asi le eŋu wòadzo.’ Ke mia tɔgbuiwo gbe toɖoɖo, gbe nusese.

english_verse: but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Tete ɖeko miegatrɔ susu hegblẽ kɔ ɖo nam! Mia dome ame sia ame gakplɔ eƒe kluvi, ŋutsu alo nyɔnu, si ŋu wòɖe asi le abe ale si wodi ene la gava eɖokui gbɔ, eye wòna wògazu eƒe kluvi.

english_verse: You have disobeyed me by not giving your slaves their freedom. So I will give you freedom—the freedom to die in battle or from disease or hunger. I will make you disgusting to all other nations on earth.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ be: Mimeɖo tom, ɖe gbeƒã ablɔɖe na mia nɔviwo kple miaƒe aƒelikawo o. Kpɔ ɖa, mele gbeƒã ɖem aʋawɔwɔ, dɔ vɔ̃ kple dɔwuame ƒe ablɔɖe na mi. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Mawɔ mi miazu ŋɔdzinu na fiaɖuƒewo katã le anyigba dzi.

english_verse: When Jehoiakim was king of Judah, the Lord told me,
translation_verse: Nya si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Yeremya, esime Yuda-fia Yehoyakim, Yosiya vi, nɔ fia ɖum lae nye:

english_verse: “Go to the Rechabite clan and invite them to meet you in one of the side rooms of the temple. When they arrive, offer them a drink of wine.”
translation_verse: “Yi ɖe Rexab ƒomeawo ƒeme ne nàƒo nu kpli wo. Kplɔ wo yi ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me, miage ɖe xɔwo dometɔ ɖeka me, eye nàna wain wo woano.”

english_verse: So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan.
translation_verse: Ale meyi ɖakplɔ Yaasanya, Yeremya vi, ame si nye Xabazinya vi kple nɔvia ŋutsuwo kple via ŋutsuwo katã kpakple Rexab ƒome blibo.

english_verse: I brought them into the temple courtyard and took them upstairs to a room belonging to the prophets who were followers of Hanan son of Igdaliah. It was next to a room belonging to some of the officials, and that room was over the one belonging to Maaseiah, a priest who was one of the high officials in the temple.
translation_verse: Mekplɔ wo yi Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me hege ɖe Mawu ƒe ame Xanan, Yigdalya vi ƒe xɔ si te ɖe amegãwo ƒe xɔ ŋu la me. Xɔ sia le Maaseya, Salum vi, ame si nye kpuinudzɔla ƒe xɔ tame.

english_verse: I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
translation_verse: Tete metsɔ waingo si yɔ banaa la kple kpluwo ɖo Rexab ƒomea kɔme hegblɔ be: “Mino wain.”

english_verse: But they answered: No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine
translation_verse: Ke woɖo eŋu be: “Míele wain no ge o, elabe mía tɔgbui Yonadab, Rexab vi, de se na mí be: ‘Miawo kple mia viwo siaa migano wain gbeɖe o;

english_verse: or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
translation_verse: migatu xɔ o; migaƒã nu o, eye migade waingble alo waingble aɖe nanɔ mia si anye mia tɔ o; ke boŋ mianɔ avɔgbadɔwo me le miaƒe agbe me ŋkekewo katã me, ale be mianɔ agbe didi le anyigba si dzi mienye amedzrowo le la dzi.’

english_verse: Our clan has always obeyed Jonadab's command. To this very day, we and our wives and sons and daughters don't drink wine or build houses or plant vineyards or crops. And we have lived in tents,
translation_verse: ke míenɔ avɔgbadɔwo me. Míeɖo to wɔ se siwo katã mía tɔgbui Yonadab de na mí la dzi.

english_verse: except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
translation_verse: Ke esi Nebukadnezar, Babilon-fia ho aʋa ɖe anyigba la ŋu la, míegblɔ be: ‘Miva, mina míayi Yerusalem le Kaldeatɔwo kple Asiriatɔwo ƒe aʋakɔwo ta.’ Eya tae míeva le Yerusalem ɖo.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, want you to learn a lesson
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Yi ɖagblɔ na Yudatɔwo kple Yerusalemnɔlawo be: Ɖe mimaxɔ nye nufiame, aɖo to nye nyawo oa? Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me!
translation_verse: Se si Yonadab, Rexab vi, de na via ŋutsuwo be womegano wain o la, wowɔ edzi, eye wo dometɔ aɖeke menoa wain o va se ɖe egbe, elabe woɖo to wo tɔgbui ƒe sededea. Nye la, meƒo nu na mi edziedzi, gake miegbe be yewomaɖo tom o.

english_verse: You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
translation_verse: Medɔ nye dɔla gbeƒãɖelawo katã ɖe mi edziedzi be: ‘Mia dome ame sia ame neɖɔ eƒe agbenɔnɔ ɖo, eye megadze mawu bubuwo yome asubɔ wo o, bene mianɔ anyigba si metsɔ na miawo kple mia tɔgbuiwo la dzi.’ Ke miegbe toɖoɖo, gbe nusese.

english_verse: The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me,
