translation_verse: Rexab vi, Yonadab, viwo wɔ wo tɔgbui ƒe se si wòde na wo la dzi, gake dukɔ sia ya gbe toɖoɖom.

english_verse: your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ, Mawu Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Kpɔ ɖa, mele dzɔgbevɔ̃e siwo katã megblɔ ɖe Yudatɔwo kple Yerusalemnɔlawo katã ŋu la, hege ava wo dzi, elabe meƒo nu na wo, womesee o; meyɔ wo, wogbe tɔtɔ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan: “I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab,
translation_verse: Tete Yeremya gblɔ na Rexab ƒomea be: “Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Esi mieɖo to mia tɔ́ Yonadab ƒe sedede, lé eƒe seawo katã me ɖe asi, eye miewɔ nu siwo katã wògblɔ na mi

english_verse: so I promise that your clan will be my servants and will never die out.”
translation_verse: dzi ta la, Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Rexab vi, Yonadab, ƒe ame magbe tsitrenɔnɔ ɖe ŋkunye me akpɔ o.”

english_verse: During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Esime Yuda-fia Yehoyakim, Yosiya vi, le eƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè enelia me la, Aƒetɔ ƒo nu kple Yeremya be:

english_verse: since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you,
translation_verse: “Tsɔ agbalẽ. Ŋlɔ nya siwo katã megblɔ na wò ɖe Israel kple Yuda kpakple dukɔwo katã ŋu la ɖe edzi. Dze egɔme tso esime mede asi nuƒoƒo me kpli wò le fia Yosiya ŋɔli va ɖo egbe.

english_verse: then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
translation_verse: Ðewohĩ Yuda-to la ase dzɔgbevɔ̃e siwo katã meɖo be mana woadzɔ ɖe wo dzi la, ale be wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe atrɔ dzime tso eƒe mɔ vɔ̃ dzi, eye matsɔ woƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ kple nuvɔ̃ ake wo.”

english_verse: I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll.
translation_verse: Ale Yeremya yɔ Barux, Neriya vi, vɛ, eye wògblɔ nya siwo katã Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ la na Barux wòŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽ me.

english_verse: Then I said, Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple,
translation_verse: Azɔ Yeremya de se na Barux be: “Womeɖe mɔ nam be mayi Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me o.

english_verse: so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud.
translation_verse: Eya ta yi nàɖaxlẽ Aƒetɔ ƒe nya si mena nèŋlɔ la, le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la me sesĩe le nutsidɔgbe ne dukɔa nase. Xlẽe na Yudatɔ siwo do tso woƒe duwo me va la hã ne woase.

english_verse: The Lord is furious, and if the people hear how he is going to punish them, maybe they will ask to be forgiven.
translation_verse: Ðewohĩ Aƒetɔ ase woƒe kokoƒoƒo, eye ame sia ame atrɔ dzime tso eƒe mɔ vɔ̃ dzi, elabe Aƒetɔ ƒe dziku kple dɔmedzoe si wòdo gblɔ ɖe dukɔa ŋu la dzi ŋɔ.”

english_verse: In the ninth month of the fifth year that Jehoiakim was king, the leaders set a day when everyone who lived in Jerusalem or who was visiting there had to pray and go without eating. So Baruch took the scroll to the upper courtyard of the temple. He went over to the side of the courtyard and stood in a covered area near New Gate, where he read the scroll aloud. This covered area belonged to Gemariah, one of the king's highest officials.
translation_verse: Tete Barux xlẽ Yeremya ƒe nya siwo katã wògblɔ nɛ wòŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽa me la sesĩe ame sia ame se, le agbalẽŋlɔla Gemarya, Sefan vi ƒe xɔ me, le xɔxɔnu dzigbetɔ si le Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ƒe Agbo Yeye la nu. Woxlẽ agbalẽa na dumegãwo

english_verse: Gemariah's son Micaiah was there and heard Baruch read what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Mixaya, Gemarya vi, ame si nye Safan ƒe tɔgbuiyɔvi la ɖo to se Aƒetɔ ƒe nyaawo katã tso agbalẽa me.

english_verse: When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah.
translation_verse: Tete wòyi fiasã la me, eye wòge ɖe agbalẽŋlɔla la ƒe xɔ me. Amegãwo katã bɔbɔ nɔ afi ma: Elisama, agbalẽŋlɔla; Delaya, Semaya vi; Elnatan, Axbor vi; Gemarya, Safan vi kple Zedekiya, Xananya vi, hekpe ɖe amegã bubuawo katã ŋu.

english_verse: Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people.
translation_verse: Mixaya gblɔ nya siwo katã Barux xlẽ tso agbalẽa me na dukɔa wòse la na wo.

english_verse: the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did.
translation_verse: Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Bɔbɔ nɔ anyi nàxlẽe!” Ale Barux xlẽe na wo.

english_verse: After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked,
translation_verse: Esi wose nyaawo katã la, wotrɔ ɖe wo nɔewo ŋu kple vɔvɔ̃, eye wogblɔ na Barux be: “Ele be míana fia nase nya siawo katã godoo!”

english_verse: “Did someone tell you what to write on this scroll?”
translation_verse: Azɔ wobia gbe Barux be: “Ale ke nèwɔ ŋlɔ nya siawo katã? Ɖe wògblɔ wo na wò nèŋlɔa? Gblɔe míse!”

english_verse: “Yes, Jeremiah did,” Baruch replied. “I wrote down just what he told me.”
translation_verse: Barux ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Egblɔ nya siawo katã nam ɖekaɖeka, eye metsɔ nuŋlɔtsi ŋlɔ woe ɖe agbalẽa me.”

english_verse: The officials said, “You and Jeremiah must go into hiding, and don't tell anyone where you are going.”
translation_verse: Tete amegãawo gblɔ na Barux be: “Yi, ne wò kple Yeremya miayi ɖabè. Ame aɖeke meganya afi si miele o.” Fia tɔ dzo agbalẽ la

english_verse: The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us. Jeremiah's Second Scroll
translation_verse: Tete fia la ɖe gbe na fia vi Yeraxmeel kple Seraya, Azriel vi kpakple Selemya, Abdiel vi, be woalé Barux, agbalẽŋlɔla kple Yeremya, Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela la, vɛ. Ke Aƒetɔ tsɔ wo ɣla. Yeremya ŋlɔ agbalẽ bubu

english_verse: I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me
translation_verse: Azɔ esi fia la tɔ dzo agbalẽ si me Barux ŋlɔ nya siwo Yeremya gblɔ nɛ wòŋlɔ vɔ la, Aƒetɔ gaƒo nu kple Yeremya be:

english_verse: to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one.
translation_verse: “Gatsɔ agbalẽ bubu nàŋlɔ nya siwo katã megblɔ na wò, siwo nɔ Agbalẽ Gbãtɔ si Yuda-fia Yehoyakim tɔ dzoe me la, ɖe eme.

english_verse: Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim: Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals.
translation_verse: Azɔ ku ɖe Yuda-fia Yehoyakim ŋu gblɔ be: ‘Aƒetɔ be: Ètɔ dzo agbalẽ sia gblɔ be: Nu ka ta nèŋlɔ ɖe eme be Babilon-fia le vava ge godoo agblẽ anyigba sia, eye wòatsrɔ̃ amegbetɔwo kple lãwo siaa le edzi?

english_verse: So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ gblɔ ɖe Yehoyakim, Yuda-fia ŋu be: Eƒe dzidzimevi aɖeke manɔ David ƒe fiazikpui dzi o. Woatsɔ eƒe ŋutilã kukua aƒu gbe; ŋdɔ aɖui le ŋkeke me eye zãmu aƒoe le zã me.

english_verse: You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
translation_verse: Mahe to na eya kple eƒe dzidzimeviwo kpakple eƒe dɔlawo le woƒe vodada ta. Mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e siwo katã megblɔ ɖe wo ŋu la ava woawo, Yerusalemnɔlawo kple Yudatɔwo dzi, elabe wodo toku nye nyawo.’ ”

english_verse: After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
translation_verse: Ale Yeremya gatsɔ agbalẽ bubu na agbalẽŋlɔla Barux, Neriya vi, eye wògaŋlɔ nya siwo katã Yeremya gblɔ nɛ wòŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽ si fia Yehoyakim tɔ dzoe la ɖe eme. Egagblɔ nya mawo tɔgbe geɖe kpe ɖe wo ŋu, wòŋlɔ.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead.
translation_verse: Zedekiya, Yosiya vi, ame si Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar tsɔ ɖo fia ɖe Yuda-nyigba dzi la ɖu fia ɖe Xonya, Yehoyakim vi, teƒe.

english_verse: But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: Ke Zedekiya loo, alo eƒe dɔlawo loo, alo anyigba la dzi nɔla aɖeke meɖo to Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedeasi to Yeremya, gbeƒãɖela la, dzi o.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message: Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt.
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Gblɔ na Yuda-fia si dɔ wò ɖo ɖem be nàva bia nyam la be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa, Egipte Fiagã ƒe aʋakɔ si va be yeakpe ɖe ŋuwò la le tɔtrɔ ge ayi Egipte, eya ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi.’

english_verse: Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire.
translation_verse: Kaldeatɔwo agbugbɔ ava wɔ aʋa kple du sia. Woaxɔe eye woatɔ dzoe.

english_verse: Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: ‘Migaflu mia ɖokui anɔ gbɔgblɔm be: Kaldeatɔwo adzo le mía gbɔ tsã o, elabe womele dzodzo ge o.

english_verse: Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire. Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
translation_verse: Elabe ne miete ŋu ɖu Kaldeatɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ bliboa si le aʋa wɔm kpli mi la dzi, eye ame siwo xɔ abi le wo dome la koe susɔ, tsi woƒe agbadɔwo me hã la, agbadɔmenɔla ɖe sia ɖe atso, atɔ dzo du sia.’ ” Wolé Yeremya de gaxɔ me

english_verse: The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi Kaldeatɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ gbugbɔ ɖe megbe le Yerusalem-dua ŋu esime Egipte Fiagã ƒe aʋakɔ la gbɔna la,

english_verse: So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land.
translation_verse: Yeremya do le Yerusalem-dua me be yeayi Benyamin-nyigba dzi be yeaɖaxɔ ye tɔ gome le yeƒe amewo dome.

english_verse: I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
translation_verse: Ke esi wòɖo Benyamin-gbo la nu la, dzɔla aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Yiriya, Selemya vi, ame si nye Xananya ƒe tɔgbuiyɔvi la lé Yeremya, gbeƒãɖela la gblɔ be: “Èsí yina Kaldeatɔwo gbɔ!”

english_verse: “I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials.
translation_verse: Yeremya xɔ edzi gblɔ be: “Gbeɖe! Nyemedzo yina Kaldeatɔwo dzi o.” Ke Yiriya mexɔ nyaa nɛ o. Elé Yeremya eye wòkplɔe va amegãwo gbɔe.

english_verse: King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?” “Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
translation_verse: fia Zedekiya dɔ ame ɖa wòva kplɔ Yeremya vɛ nɛ, eye wòxɔe. Fia la bia gbee le adzame le eƒeme be: “Gbedeasi aɖe tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ vaa?” Yeremya ɖo eŋu be: “Ẽ!” Eyi edzi be: “Woatsɔ wò ade asi na Babilon-fia!”

english_verse: Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation?
translation_verse: Yeremya bia Zedekiya be: “Nu vɔ̃ ka mewɔ ɖe ŋuwò loo, alo wò dɔlawo ŋu loo, alo dukɔ sia ŋu tae mietsɔm de gaxɔ me ɖo?

english_verse: Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem?
translation_verse: Afi ka miaƒe gbeƒãɖela siwo gblɔ na mi be: ‘Babilon-fia matso ɖe wò kple anyigba sia ŋu o’ la le?

english_verse: Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
translation_verse: Azɔ nye aƒetɔ fia, meɖe kuku, mele koko ƒom le ŋkuwò me kple ɖokuibɔbɔ. Mègatrɔm ɖo ɖe agbalẽŋlɔla Yonatan ƒeme o. Ne menye nenema o la, maku ɖe afi ma.”

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_verse: Ale fia Zedekiya ɖe gbe woda Yeremya ɖe dzɔlawo ƒe xɔxɔnu. Wotsɔa abolo ɖeka nɛ tso aboloƒolawo ƒe ablɔ me gbe sia gbe, ʋuu va se ɖe esime abolo va vɔ keŋ le dua me. Ale Yeremya tsi dzɔlawo ƒe xɔxɔnu la.

english_verse: One day, Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jehucal, and Pashhur heard me tell the people of Judah
translation_verse: Azɔ Sefatya, Matan vi, Gedalya, Pasxur vi, Yuxal, Selemya vi kple Pasxur, Malkiya vi, se nya siwo Yeremya le gbɔgblɔm na dukɔ bliboa be:

english_verse: So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
translation_verse: Tete amegãwo gblɔ na fia la be: “Na woawu ŋutsu sia elabe nya siwo gblɔm wòle la le dzi ɖem le aʋawɔla siwo susɔ ɖe dua me kple dukɔ bliboa me la ƒo. Ŋutsu sia mele dukɔa ƒe nyui dim o; eƒe vɔ̃e ko dim wòle.”

english_verse: Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
translation_verse: Fia Zedekiya gblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ele mia si me; elabe fia mate ŋu awɔ naneke atsi tre ɖe mia ŋu o.”

english_verse: Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
translation_verse: Ale wolé Yeremya, eye woɖiɖii kple ka ɖe fiavi Malkiya ƒe vudo si le dzɔlawo ƒe xɔxɔnu la me. Tsi mele vudoa me o, ba koe li, eye Yeremya yi to ɖe ba la me.

english_verse: Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
translation_verse: “Nye aƒetɔ fia, ŋutsu siawo wɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi le nu siwo katã wowɔ la me. Wotsɔ Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela Yeremya de vudo me, dɔ le wuwu ge wòaku, elabe nuɖuɖu aɖeke megale dua me o!”

english_verse: Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well.
translation_verse: Ale Ebedmelex ɖe ŋutsuawo kpe ɖe eɖokui ŋu. Ege ɖe fia ƒe aƒe la me, eye wòyi ɖe xɔ si le nudzraɖoƒea te la me. Etsɔ avɔ vuvu kple awu xoxo aɖewo le afi ma, eye wòɖiɖi wo kple ka ɖe Yeremya gbɔ le vudoa me.

english_verse: Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did,
translation_verse: Tete Ebedmelex Etiopiatɔ, la gblɔ na Yeremya be: “Tsɔ avɔ vuvuawo kple awu xoxoawo de axatome, eye nàtsɔ kaa de wo te.” Yeremya wɔ nenema.

english_verse: the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards. King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
translation_verse: Ale wolé ka la, eye wohe Yeremya do goe tso vudo la me. Yeremya tsi dzɔlaawo ƒe xɔxɔnu. Zedekiya bia tso Yeremya si be woaɖo aɖaŋu na ye

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
translation_verse: Fia Zedekiya dɔ ame ɖa woɖakplɔ Yeremya vɛ, eye wòxɔe ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la ƒe mɔnu etɔ̃lia. Fia la gblɔ na Yeremya be: “Mele nya aɖe bia ge wò; mègaɣla nya aɖeke ɖem o.”

english_verse: He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
translation_verse: Tete fia Zedekiya ka atam na Yeremya le adzame gblɔ be: “Metà Aƒetɔ, ame si na agbe mí la ƒe agbe. Ne mawu wò alo atsɔ wò ade asi na ŋutsu siwo le didim be yewoawu wò la fĩi!”

english_verse: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
translation_verse: Tete Yeremya gblɔ na Zedekiya be: “Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Ne èna ta Babilon-fia ƒe amegãwo la, woana nàtsi agbe, eye womatɔ dzo du sia o, eye wò kple wò aƒemetɔwo miatsi agbe.

english_verse: But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
translation_verse: Evɔ ne mèna ta Babilon-fia ƒe amegãawo o la, ekema woatsɔ du sia ade asi na Kaldeatɔwo. Woatɔ dzoe, eye wò ŋutɔ hã màdo le wo si me o.”

english_verse: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
translation_verse: Ke Zedekiya gblɔ na Yeremya be: “Mele Yudatɔ siwo dzo yi Kaldeatɔwo dzi la vɔ̃m. Woava tsɔm ade asi na wo, eye woawɔ funyafunyam.”

english_verse: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.
translation_verse: Yeremya gblɔ be: “Womatsɔ wò ade asi na wo o. Wò ya wɔ nya si Aƒetɔ gblɔ nam megblɔ na wò la dzi ko, eye eme anyo na wò, eye woana nàtsi agbe.

english_verse: But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey,
translation_verse: Evɔ ne ègbe godogodo be yemana ta o la, ekema nya si Aƒetɔ ɖe fiam lae nye esi:

english_verse: then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you: Friends you trusted led you astray. Now you're trapped in mud, and those friends you trusted have all turned away.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, wokplɔ nyɔnu siwo katã susɔ ɖe Yuda-fia ƒeme la yina ɖe Babilon-fia ƒe amegãwo gbɔe, eye wonɔ gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Xɔ̃wò siwo dzi nèka ɖo la flu wò, eye woɖu dziwò. Fifia esi wò afɔ yi to ɖe ba me la, woka le ŋuwò.’

english_verse: The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
translation_verse: Woakplɔ srɔ̃wòwo katã kple viwòwo ayi na Kaldeatɔwo, eye wò ŋutɔ hã mado le wo si me o. Ke Babilon-fia ƒe asi asu dziwò, eye woatɔ dzo du sia.”

english_verse: Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life.
translation_verse: Tete Zedekiya gblɔ na Yeremya be: “Mègana ame aɖeke nase nya siawo o, ekema màku o.

english_verse: And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them.
translation_verse: Ne amegãawo se be meƒo nu kpli wò, eye wova gbɔwò gblɔ na wò be: ‘Gblɔ nu si nègblɔ na fia la, eye wò hã nègblɔ nɛ la na mí. Mègaɣla nya aɖeke ɖe mí o, ekema míawu wò o’ la,

english_verse: So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
translation_verse: ekema gblɔ na wo be: ‘Meƒo koko na fia la kple ɖokuibɔbɔ be megaɖom ɖe Yonatan ƒe aƒeme, ne maɖaku ɖe afi ma o.’ ”

english_verse: The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
translation_verse: Tete amegãawo katã va bia nya la Yeremya se, eye wòɖo eŋu na wo pɛpɛpɛ abe ale si fia la de see nɛ ene. Ale wodzudzɔ nyaawo biabiae, elabe dzeɖoɖoa meɖi ame aɖeke se o.

english_verse: I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_verse: Ale Yeremya tsi dzɔlaawo ƒe xɔxɔnua va se ɖe gbe si gbe woxɔ Yerusalem-dua.

english_verse: When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Esi Yuda-fia Zedekiya kple aʋawɔlaawo katã kpɔ wo la, wosí le zã me to fia ƒe abɔ me dzo. Woto mɔ si to gli eveawo dome heɖo ta Araba me.

english_verse: to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen.
translation_verse: “Yi ɖagblɔ na Ebedmelex, Etiopiatɔ la be: ‘Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Kpɔ ɖa, mana nye nyawo nava eme ɖe du sia ŋu, hena dzɔgbevɔ̃e, menye hena dzɔgbe nyui o. Woava eme le ŋkuwò me gbe ma gbe.

english_verse: “Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
translation_verse: “Kplɔe yi nàkpɔ edzi nyuie, eye mègawɔ nu vevi aɖekee o. Ke nu si wòdi be nàwɔ na ye la, wɔe nɛ.”

english_verse: But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty,
translation_verse: Ke Kaldeatɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ ti wo yome, eye wotu Zedekiya le Yerixo-gbegbe. Esi wolée la, wokplɔe vɛ na Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar le Ribla le Xamat-nyigba dzi, eye wòdrɔ̃ ʋɔnu bu fɔe.

english_verse: and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families.
translation_verse: Babilon-fia wu Zedekiya viŋutsuwo le eŋkume le Ribla. Babilon-fia wu bubume siwo katã le Yuda la hã.

english_verse: Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Eho ŋku le to me na Zedekiya, eye wòna wode kɔsɔkɔsɔe be yeakplɔe ayi Babilonia.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls.
translation_verse: Kaldeatɔwo tɔ dzo fia ƒe aƒe kple aƒe siwo le dua me la, eye womu Yerusalem-dua ƒe gliwo ƒu anyi.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Tete fia ŋu srafowo ƒe tatɔ, Nebuzaradan, ɖe aboyo ame siwo susɔ ɖe dua me, ame siwo dzo yi egbɔ xoxo la, hekpe ɖe ame siwo tsi anyi la ŋu, eye wòkplɔ wo yi Babilon.

english_verse: Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradan gblẽ dukɔa ƒe ame dahe siwo si nunɔamesi gobi aɖeke mele o la dometɔ aɖewo ɖe Yuda-nyigba dzi, eye wòtsɔ waingblewo kple agblewo na wo. Woɖe asi le Yeremya ŋu

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar had given the following orders to Nebuzaradan:
translation_verse: Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar ɖe gbe na fia ŋu srafowo ƒe tatɔ, Nebuzaradan, tso Yeremya ŋu be:

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, Nebushazban, Nergal Sharezer, and the other officers of King Nebuchadnezzar
translation_verse: Ale Nebuzaradan, Nebusazban kple Nergal-Sarezer kpakple Babilon-fia ƒe amegãawo katã ɖo ame ɖa,

english_verse: sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah. The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
translation_verse: woɖakplɔ Yeremya tso dzɔlaawo ƒe xɔxɔnua vɛ. Wotsɔe de Gedalya, Axikam vi, ame si nye Safan ƒe tɔgbuiyɔvi la si, ne wòakplɔe yi eƒeme. Ale Yeremya nɔ ameawo dome. Mɔkpɔkpɔ su Ebedmelex si

english_verse: While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say
translation_verse: Esime Yeremya nɔ ga me le dzɔlaawo ƒe xɔxɔnua la, Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be:

english_verse: But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Elabe maxɔ wò ɖe agbe kokoko, eye màtsi yi nu o. Ke wò agbe anɔ abe nunana tso aʋagbedzi ene, elabe èɖo dzi ɖe ŋunye.’ ” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒo nu kple Yeremya esime fia ŋu srafowo ƒe tatɔ Nebuzaradan ɖe asi le eŋu le Rama. Do ŋgɔ la, wode kɔsɔkɔsɔ Yeremya kpe ɖe aboyomeawo katã ŋu tso Yerusalem kple Yuda hekplɔ yina ɖe aboyo me le Babilon.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan said: Jeremiah, the Lord your God warned your people that he would bring disaster on this land.
translation_verse: Fia ŋu srafoawo ƒe tatɔ kplɔ Yeremya yi eɖokui gbɔ, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la gblɔ be dzɔgbevɔ̃e sia adzɔ ɖe teƒe sia dzi,

english_verse: But they continued to rebel against him, and now he has punished them just as he threatened.
translation_verse: eye wòna wòdzɔ abe ale si wògblɔe ene. Nu sia dzɔ ɖe mia dzi elabe miewɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu, eye mieɖo to eƒe gbe o.

english_verse: Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish.
translation_verse: Azɔ kpɔ ɖa, meɖe ga le alɔnu na wò egbe. Ne edze ŋuwò be yeayi Babilon kplim la, va míyi; malé be na wò nyuie. Evɔ ne medze ŋuwò be yeayi Babilon kplim o la, tsi anyi faa. Kpɔ ɖa, anyigba blibo la nye esi le ŋkuwò me. Yi afi sia afi si nèbu be enyo eye wòdze ŋuwò nebe yeayi la.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar has chosen Gedaliah to rule Judah. You can live near Gedaliah, and he will provide for you, or you can live anywhere else you choose. Nebuzaradan gave me a supply of food, then let me leave.
translation_verse: Ne àtsi anyi la, ekema gbugbɔ yi Gedalya, Safan vi, Axikam vi, ame si Babilon-fia tsɔ ɖo Yuda-duwo nu la gbɔ, eye nànɔ egbɔ le dukɔa me, alo nàyi afi sia afi si nèkpɔ be edze yeayi la.” Ale asrafoawo ƒe tatɔ la tsɔ nuɖuɖu kple nunana aɖewo na Yeremya hedo mɔe wòdzo.

english_verse: I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah. The Harvest Is Brought In
translation_verse: Tete Yeremya yi Gedalya, Axikam vi, gbɔ le Mizpa, eye wònɔ ame siwo susɔ ɖe anyigbaa dzi la dome. Gedalya zu anyigbanunɔla le Yuda

english_verse: Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Gedalya, Axikam vi, Safan vi, la ka atam na wo kple woƒe asrafowo be: “Migavɔ̃ Kaldeatɔwo subɔsubɔ o. Minɔ anyigba la dzi, eye misubɔ Babilon-fia la, ekema eme anyo na mi.

english_verse: I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
translation_verse: Nye ya manɔ Mizpa, anye mia teƒenɔla, le Kaldeatɔwo siwo ava mía gbɔ la ŋkume. Ke miawo la, miƒo wain, dzomeŋɔlikutsetsewo kple ami nu ƒu, eye mitsɔ wo de miaƒe nuwo me; minɔ miaƒe du siwo miexɔ la me.”

english_verse: One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Yehohanan, Kareax vi kple aʋakplɔla siwo katã ganɔ aʋagbea dzi kokoko la va Gedalya gbɔ le Mizpa.

english_verse: They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!” Gedaliah refused to believe them,
translation_verse: Wobiae be: “Ènya be Amontɔwo ƒe fia, Baalis, dɔ Ismael, Netanya vi la, ɖa be wòaɖe wò agbe ɖaa?” Gake Gedalya, Axikam vi la, mexɔ wo dzi se o.

english_verse: so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
translation_verse: Tete Yehohanan, Kareax vi, ƒo nu kple Gedalya le adzame le Mizpa be: Na mayi ɖawu Ismael, Netanya vi la; ame aɖeke manya o. Nu ka ta eya naɖe wò agbe ɖa ale be Yudatɔ siwo katã ƒo ƒu ɖe ŋuwò la naka hlẽ, eye ame susɔeawo hã natsrɔ̃?”

english_verse: But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti adrẽlia me le ƒè ma me la, Ismael, Netanya vi, ame si nye Elisama ƒe tɔgbuiyɔvi, si tso fiaƒomea me, eye wònye fia ƒe amegãwo dometɔ ɖeka la kplɔ ŋutsu ewo kpe ɖe eɖokui ŋu va Gedalya, Axikam vi la gbɔ le Mizpa. Esi woƒo ƒu nɔ nu ɖum ɖekae le Mizpa la,

english_verse: During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Ismael, Netanya vi kple ŋutsu ewo siwo kpe ɖe eŋu la tso, he woƒe yiwo ɖe go, eye wowu Gedalya, Axikam vi, Safan vi, ame si Babilon-fia tsɔ ɖo anyigba la nu.

english_verse: Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
translation_verse: Ismael wu Yudatɔ siwo katã le Gedalya gbɔ le Mizpa la hã. Gawu la, Kaldea-srafo siwo le afi ma la hã tsi esi me.

english_verse: The next day, the murders had still not been discovered,
translation_verse: Le Gedalya wuwu ƒe ŋufɔke, esi ame aɖeke menya haɖe o la,

english_verse: Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah.
translation_verse: Tete Ismael, Netanya vi la, do tso Mizpa va kpe wo le avi fam. Esi wòdo go wo la, egblɔ na wo be: “Mige ɖe eme miakpɔ Gedalya, Axikam vi la ɖa!”

english_verse: But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well.
translation_verse: Ke esi woge ɖe dua me la, Ismael, Netanya vi la kple ŋutsu siwo kpe ɖe eŋu la wu ameawo, eye wotsɔ wo ƒu gbe ɖe vudo aɖe me.

english_verse: He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field.
translation_verse: Ke ŋutsu ewo le ameawo dome gblɔ na Ismael be: “Míeɖe kuku, mègawu mí o. Lu, ƒo, ami kple anyitsi le mía si, míeɣla ɖe gbe me.” Ale megaxa wu wo kpe ɖe wo tɔwo ŋu o.

english_verse: The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
translation_verse: Azɔ vudo si me Ismael tsɔ ŋutsu, siwo katã wòwu kpe ɖe Gedalya ŋu ƒe ŋutilã kukuawo ƒu gbe ɖo la, nye vudo gã aɖe si fia Asa ɖe, tsɔ xe mɔ na Israel-fia Baesa. Ismael, Netanya vi la, fɔ ame kukuawo kɔ ɖe eme tsɔ xee.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Azɔ Ismael ɖe aboyo ame mamlɛ siwo katã nɔ Mizpa, fiavinyɔnuwo kple ame siwo katã susɔ ɖe Mizpa siwo fia ŋu srafowo ƒe tatɔ Nebuzaradan tsɔ de Gedalya, Axikam vi la si. Ismael, Netanya vi la ɖe aboyo ame siawo katã, eye wokplɔ wo dzoe ɖo ta Amon-nutome.

english_verse: So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon.
translation_verse: wokplɔ woƒe aʋawɔlawo katã, eye woho be woaɖawɔ aʋa kple Ismael, Netanya vi la. Wotui le ta gã si le Gibeon la to.

english_verse: But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon. Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
translation_verse: Gake Ismael, Netanya vi la kple ŋutsu enyi, wosí le Yehohanan nu yi ɖe Amon-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: Johanan and the officers had rescued the women, children, and royal officials that Ishmael had taken prisoner after killing Gedaliah. Johanan led the people from Gibeon
translation_verse: Tete Yehohanan, Kareax vi la kple aʋakplɔla siwo katã kpe ɖe eŋu la, kplɔ ame susɔe siwo katã Ismael, Netanya vi la ɖe aboyoe tso Mizpa esime wòwu Gedalya, Axikam vi la megbe. Ekplɔ wo tso Gibeon vɛ. Ameawoe nye: aʋawɔlawo, nyɔnuwo, ɖeviwo kple aƒedzikpɔlawo.

english_verse: Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me
translation_verse: Tete aʋakplɔlaawo katã kple Yehohanan, Kareax vi kple Azarya, Hosaya vi, hekpe ɖe ɖeviwo kple ame tsitsiwo siaa ŋu te va

english_verse: and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left.
translation_verse: gblɔ na Yeremya, gbeƒãɖela la be: “Nyo dɔme na mí nàse míaƒe kokoƒoƒo, eye nàdo gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la na mí, ɖe ame susɔe siawo katã ta. Elabe ame geɖe ŋutɔ míenye gake mí ame ʋɛ siawo koe susɔ abe ale si nèle mía kpɔm ene.

english_verse: Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
translation_verse: Na Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la nafia mɔ si wòle be míato kple nu si wòle be míawɔ la mí.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord himself will be our witness that we promise to do whatever he says,
translation_verse: Tete wogblɔ na Yeremya be: “Aƒetɔ nenye ɖasefo anukwaretɔ kple nuteƒewɔla na mí, nenye be míewɔ ɖe nya siwo katã eya, Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la agblɔ ɖo ɖe mí la nu o.

english_verse: even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
translation_verse: Nya nyui wòɖanye o, nya vɔ̃ wòɖanye o, Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la, ame si gbɔ míele ɖowòm ɖo la ƒe gbe ko míase be eme nanyo na mí, ne míese eƒe gbe.” Aƒetɔ ɖo Yeremya ƒe gbedodoɖa ŋu

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for
translation_verse: Ŋkeke ewo megbe la, Aƒetɔ ƒo nu kple Yeremya.

english_verse: Johanan, the officers, and the other people. So I called them together
translation_verse: Ale wòyɔ Yehohanan, Kareax vi kple aʋakplɔla siwo katã le eŋu la kple ame sia ame, ɖeviwo kple ame tsitsiwo siaa,

english_verse: and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said: You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do.
translation_verse: eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la, ame si gbɔ mieɖom ɖo be maɖaƒo koko nɛ kple miaƒe nyawo la gblɔ be:

english_verse: I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you.
translation_verse: Ne mianɔ anyigba sia dzi la, ekema matu mi ɖo, eye nyemagbã mi o; mado mi eye nyemaho mi o, elabe dzɔgbevɔ̃e si mehe va mia dzi la vem.

english_verse: Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him,
translation_verse: Migavɔ̃ Babilon-fia si vɔ̃m miele la o; migavɔ̃e azɔ o, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, elabe meli kpli mi axɔ na mi, eye maɖe mi tso esi me.

english_verse: and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
translation_verse: Makpɔ nublanui na mi ale be eya hã nakpɔ nublanui na mi eye wòana mianɔ miawo ŋutɔ mia denyigba dzi.

english_verse: But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Evɔ ne miegblɔ be: ‘Míele anyigba sia dzi nɔ ge o’, eye miegbe toɖoɖo Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu ƒe gbe

english_verse: We are going to Egypt, where there is plenty of food and no danger of war.”
translation_verse: ahanɔ gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Gbeɖe, míayi Egipte-nyigba dzi, elabe afi ma, aʋa magadzɔ míakpɔ o, aʋayikpẽ maɖi míase o, eye dɔ magawu mí gbeɖe o, eye míaɖanɔ afi ma la,’

english_verse: People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen.
translation_verse: ekema mi ame siwo susɔ ɖe Yuda, mise Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la ƒe nya be: Ne mieɖoe kplikpaa be yewoagbugbɔ ayi Egipte aɖanɔ afi ma la,

english_verse: You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
translation_verse: Ame siwo katã ɖoe kplikpaa be Egipte ko yewoayi aɖanɔ la, aku le aʋa me loo, alo dɔwuame atsrɔ̃ wo loo, alo woatsi dɔ vɔ̃ si me. Wo dometɔ ɖeka hɔ̃ hã masusɔ le dzɔgbevɔ̃e si he ge mala ava wo dzi la me o.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word. Jeremiah Gives a Warning
translation_verse: “Elabe Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la le gbɔgblɔm be: Ale si metrɔ nye dɔmedzoe kple nye dziku ƒo ɖe Yerusalemnɔlawo dzii la, nenema ke matrɔ nye dziku aƒo ɖe mia dzi, ne mieyi Egipte. Miazu atamkanu, ŋɔdzinu, ɖiŋudonu kple alɔmeɖenu; miagakpɔ teƒe sia ya akpɔ o.

english_verse: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na mi, ame siwo susɔ le Yuda la be: ‘Migayi Egipte o.’ Minya nyuie be megbee na mi egbe,

english_verse: You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake,
translation_verse: be kunue mietra ɖawɔ. Elabe miawo ŋutɔe ɖom ɖe Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la gbɔ be: ‘Do gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la, na mí. Nu sia nu si Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la gblɔ la, va gblɔe na mí, eye míawɔ edzi.’

english_verse: because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him.
translation_verse: Ale megblɔe na mi egbe, gake mieɖo to Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la ƒe gbe le nu siwo wògblɔ nam meva gblɔ na mi la ƒe ɖeke me o.

english_verse: But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt.
translation_verse: Azarya, Hosaya vi kple Yehohanan, Kareax vi kpakple ŋutsu nu baɖa wɔlawo katã gblɔ na Yeremya be: “Èka aʋatso. Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la medɔ wò ɖa be nàgblɔ na mí be: ‘Migayi Egipte aɖanɔ afi ma o.’

english_verse: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
translation_verse: Ke boŋ Barux, Neriya vi lae le ʋu yɔm ɖe tewò ɖe mía ŋu, ne woatsɔ mí ade asi na Kaldeatɔwo be ne woawu mí loo, alo aɖe aboyo mí akplɔ yi Babilon.”

english_verse: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
translation_verse: Ale Yehohanan, Kareax vi kple aʋakɔwo kplɔlaawo katã kple dukɔ blibo la meɖo to Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe be woatsi Yuda-nyigba dzi o.

english_verse: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
translation_verse: Ke Yehohanan, Kareax vi kple aʋakplɔlaawo katã kplɔ ame siwo katã susɔ le Yuda, eye wotrɔ gbɔ tso dukɔ siwo me wokaka ɖo la be yewoava nɔ Yuda-nyigba dzi la, dzoe.

english_verse: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
translation_verse: Wokplɔ ŋutsuwo, nyɔnuwo, ɖeviwo, fiavinyɔnuwo kple ame bubu siwo katã fia ŋu srafowo ƒe tatɔ Nebuzaradan gblẽ ɖi ɖe Gedalya, Axikam vi, Safan vi la si me hekpe ɖe Yeremya, gbeƒãɖela la kple Barux, Neriya vi la ŋu dzoe.

english_verse: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
translation_verse: Wova ɖo Egipte-nyigba dzi elabe wogbe toɖoɖo Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe. Woge ɖe Taxpanxes-du me.

english_verse: Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
translation_verse: “Tsɔ kpe gã aɖewo nàɖi ɖe Egipte Fiagã ƒe fiasã si le Taxpanxes la ƒe mɔnu. Ði wo ɖe anyikpe siwo woɖo ɖe anyigba la te, eye na Yuda-ŋutsuwo nakpɔ eteƒe.

english_verse: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na wo be: ‘Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Kpɔ ɖa, madɔ woayi ɖakplɔ nye dɔla Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar vɛ. Malí eƒe fiazikpui ɖe kpe siwo meɖi la dzi, eye wòakeke eƒe fiaɖuƒe ɖe enu va teƒe ma.

english_verse: He will attack Egypt and kill many of its people; others will die of disease or be dragged away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Egbɔna ava ɖu Egipte-nyigba dzi. Ana ame siwo xɔ dɔléku vɛ la, alé dɔ aku; ame siwo xɔ aboyomeyiyi vɛ la, ana woayi aboyo me, eye ame siwo xɔ aʋameku vɛ la, atsi aʋa.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: “Miekpɔ dzɔgbevɔ̃e siwo katã mehe va Yerusalem kple Yuda-duwo katã dzii. Kpɔ ɖa, egbe la, wozu aƒedo; ame megale wo me o.

english_verse: because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
translation_verse: Elabe wo me nɔlawo wɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi tsɔ do dziku nam. Woyi ɖatɔ dzo lifi na mawu bubuwo, eye wosubɔ wo. Evɔ, woawo, miawo kple mia tɔgbuiwo menya mawu mawo o.

english_verse: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
translation_verse: Meɖo nye dɔla gbeƒãɖelawo katã ɖa edziedzi be woagblɔ na mi be: ‘O, migawɔ ŋunyɔnu sia si melé fui la o.’

english_verse: but they refused to listen and would not stop worshiping other gods.
translation_verse: Gake womeɖo tom, ade nye nyawo susu me ale be woadzudzɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ eye womagatɔ dzo lifi na mawu bubuwo.

english_verse: Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
translation_verse: Eya ta metrɔ nye dziku kple dɔmedzoe ƒo ɖe Yuda-duwo dzi kple ablɔwo me le Yerusalem, eye wofiã zu aƒedo kple gbegbe abe ale si wogale egbe sia ene.

english_verse: Why do you now insist on heading for another disaster? A disaster that will destroy not only you, but also your children and babies.
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ, Mawu Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la le biabiam be: Nu ka ta miele nuvɔ̃ɖi sia wɔm ɖe mia ɖokui ŋu, be mehe dzɔgbevɔ̃e vɛ hetsrɔ̃ ŋutsu kple nyɔnu, ɖevi kple vidzĩ ɖa le Yuda-nyigba dzi ale be mia dometɔ aɖeke mesusɔ o?

english_verse: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Nu ka ta miedo dziku nam kple miaƒe asinudɔwɔwɔwo, eye miele dzo tɔm lifi na mawu bubuwo le Egipte-nyigba dzi, afi si mieva le la? Ne miatsrɔ̃ mia ɖokui, eye miazu ɖiŋudonu kple alɔmeɖenu le anyigba dzi dukɔwo katã dome tae loo?

english_verse: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
translation_verse: Ðe mieŋlɔ mia tɔgbuiwo ƒe vɔɖivɔ̃ɖinyenye, Yuda-fiawo ƒe vɔɖivɔ̃ɖinyenye, wo srɔ̃wo ƒe vɔɖivɔ̃ɖinyenye, miawo ŋutɔ ƒe vɔɖivɔ̃ɖinyenye kple mia srɔ̃wo ƒe vɔɖivɔ̃ɖinyenye si wowɔ le Yuda-nyigba dzi kple ablɔwo me le Yerusalem la bea?

english_verse: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Womebɔbɔ wo ɖokui va se ɖe egbe alo avɔ̃m o. Womezɔ ɖe nye sewo kple ɖoɖo siwo mewɔ na mi kple mia tɔgbuiwo la nu o.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have decided to wipe you out with disasters.
translation_verse: Eya ta, Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Kpɔ ɖa, meɖoe be mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ava mia dzi, ne matsrɔ̃ Yuda-dukɔ blibo la ɖa.

english_verse: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Mana Yuda-dukɔa ƒe ame susɔea siwo ɖoe be yewoayi ɖanɔ Egipte-nyigba dzi la katã natsrɔ̃. Woatsrɔ̃ le Egipte-nyigba dzi le afi ma. Aʋawɔwɔ kple dɔwuame ye latsrɔ̃ wo. Ɖeviwo kple ame tsitsiwo siaa aku ɖe aʋawɔwɔ kple dɔwuame si me. Woava zu atamkanu, ŋɔdzinu, ɖiŋudonu kple alɔmeɖenu.

english_verse: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
translation_verse: Mahe to na ame siwo le Egipte-nyigba dzi abe ale si metsɔ aʋawɔwɔ, dɔwuame kple dɔ vɔ̃ he to na Yerusalemnɔlawoe ene.

english_verse: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
translation_verse: Ale Yuda-dukɔa ƒe ame susɔea siwo va Egipte-nyigba dzi nɔ ge la dometɔ aɖeke masí, alo atsi agbe, alo agbugbɔ ayi ɖe Yuda-nyigba dzi, afi si le wo dzrom be yewoatrɔ yi aɖanɔ la akpɔ o. Elabe womagatrɔ ayi o, negbe aʋasíla aɖewo ko.”

english_verse: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
translation_verse: Tete ŋutsu siwo katã nya be yewo srɔ̃wo tɔ dzo lifi na mawu bubuwo kple nyɔnu siwo katã le tsitre ɖe afi ma, ameha gã aɖe, hekpe ɖe ame siwo katã le Egipte-nyigba ƒe anyigbeme ŋu la, ɖo nyaa ŋu na Yeremya be:

english_verse: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
translation_verse: “Nya si nègblɔ na mí le Aƒetɔ ŋkɔ me la, míele edzi wɔ ge o.

english_verse: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
translation_verse: Ke míawɔ nu sia nu si míeɖe adzɔgbe be míawɔ la. Míatɔ dzo lifi na dziƒofianyɔnu la, eye míaƒo tsi ɖi nɛ. Míawɔe abe ale si mía kple mía tɔgbuiwo siaa, míaƒe fiawo kple míaƒe amegãwo míewɔnɛ le Yuda-duwo me kple le ablɔwo me le Yerusalem ene. Elabe ɣe ma ɣi la, míekpɔa nu ɖuna ɖia ƒo, agbenɔnɔ dze edzi na mí, eye dzɔgbevɔ̃e medzɔna ɖe mía dzi o.

english_verse: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
translation_verse: Gake tso esime míenya dzudzɔ dzotɔtɔ lifi na dziƒofianyɔnua eye míegale tsi ƒom ɖi nɛ o ko la, hiã tu mí le nu sia nu me eye aʋawɔwɔ kple dɔwuame tsrɔ̃ mí.”

english_verse: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
translation_verse: Tete nyɔnuawo gblɔ be: “Esi míetɔ dzo lifi na dziƒofianyɔnua eye míeƒo tsi ɖi nɛ la, ɖe mía srɔ̃wo melɔ̃na ɖe edzi na mí hafi míeƒoa abolo nɛ, taa eƒe nɔnɔme ɖe edzi, eye míeƒoa tsi ɖi nɛ oa?”

english_verse: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
translation_verse: “Ɖe miebu be Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋku mele miawo kple mia tɔgbuiwo, miaƒe fiawo kple miaƒe amegãwo kpakple dukɔ bliboa ƒe lifi si mietɔ dzo le Yuda-duwo me kple ablɔwo me le Yerusalem la dzi oa? Ɖe miebu be eŋlɔe bea?

english_verse: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ magate ŋu ado dzi atsɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi kple ŋunyɔnu siwo wɔm miele la o. Eya ta miaƒe anyigba zu aƒedo, gbegbe kple ɖiŋudonu eye ame vɔ le edzi abe ale si wòle egbe ene.

english_verse: This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Dzɔgbevɔ̃e siawo dzɔ ɖe mia dzi abe ale si wòle egbe ene elabe mietɔ dzo lifi na mawu bubuwo, eye miewɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu. Esi mimese eƒe gbe alo zɔ ɖe eƒe seawo, ɖoɖoawo kple ɖaseɖiɖiwo nu o tae.”

english_verse: Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: ‘Mi kple mia srɔ̃wo miewɔ nu si mieke nu gblɔ la dzi, eye mietsɔ asi wɔe hã hegblɔ be: Míawɔ adzɔgbe si míeɖe la dzi godoo be míatɔ dzo lifi na dziƒofianyɔnua, eye míaƒo tsi ɖi nɛ. Milé adzɔgbe si mieɖe la me ɖe asi, eye miwɔ edzi.’

english_verse: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
translation_verse: Eya ta mi Yudatɔ siwo katã le Egipte-nyigba dzi, mise Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedeasi be: Kpɔ ɖa, metà nye ŋkɔ gã la, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, be ne Yudatɔ aɖe ake nu ayɔ nye ŋkɔ le Egipte-nyigba bliboa dzi atà nui be: ‘Metà Aƒetɔ Mawu ƒe agbe’ fĩi!

english_verse: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, manɔ mo xexi akpɔ egbɔ be vɔ̃ wɔ wo, menye nyui o. Yudatɔ siwo katã le Egipte-nyigba dzi la, aʋawɔwɔ kple dɔ vɔ̃ atsrɔ̃ wo va se ɖe esime woavɔ ɖa.

english_verse: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
translation_verse: Ame siwo meku le aʋa me o la, anɔ ʋɛ agbugbɔ tso Egipte-nyigba dzi ayi Yuda-nyigba dzi. Ale Yudatɔ siwo katã susɔ yi be yewoaɖanɔ Egipte-nyigba dzi la, anya ame si ƒe nyae le eme: tɔnye alo wo tɔ.

english_verse: And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt.
translation_verse: Esia anye dzesi na mi, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, be mele to he ge na mi le teƒe sia ale be mianya be nya vɔ̃ si gblɔm mele ɖe mia ŋu la le eme va ge kokoko.

english_verse: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, matsɔ Egipte Fiagã Xofra ade asi na eƒe futɔwo kple ame siwo di be yewoaɖe eƒe agbe ɖa la, abe ale si metsɔ Yuda-fia Zedekiya de asi na Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar, ame si nye eƒe futɔ eye wòdi be yeawui la ene.”

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him.
translation_verse: Le Yuda-fia Yehoyakim, Yosiya vi, ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè enelia me la, Yeremya, gbeƒãɖela la gblɔ nya siawo na Barux, Neriya vi la wòŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽ me be:

english_verse: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu la gblɔ na wò Barux be:

english_verse: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
translation_verse: ‘Ègblɔ be: Evɔ nam elabe Aƒetɔ tsɔ nuxaxa kpe ɖe nye vevesese ŋu. Meŋè, ŋè ʋuu ɖeɖi te ŋunye, eye nyemekpɔ gbɔdzɔe aɖeke o.’

english_verse: But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted.
translation_verse: Gblɔ nɛ be: Aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, nu si metu la, mele egbãm ƒu anyi; nu si medo la, mele ehom ɖa. Anyigba blibo la gblɔm mele.

english_verse: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ɖe nèle nu gãwo dim na ɖokuiwòa? Mègadi wo o, elabe kpɔ ɖa, mele dzɔgbevɔ̃e he ge ava nu gbagbewo katã dzi. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Gake wò ya la, matsɔ wò agbe ana wò abe nunana tso aʋagbedzi ene, le teƒe siwo katã nàyi la.”

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
translation_verse: Gbedeasi ku ɖe Egipte ŋu: Gbedeasi si wògblɔ ɖe Egipte Fiagã Nexo ƒe aʋakɔ si le Frat-tɔsisi nu le Karkemis gbɔ la ŋu. Le Yehoyakim, Yosiya vi, ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè enelia me, esime Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar ɖu edzi lae nye esi:

english_verse: It's time to go into battle! So grab your shields,
translation_verse: “Mibla akpa kple akpoxɔnu gãtɔ kple suetɔ. Milũ ɖe aʋa la me.

english_verse: saddle your horses, and polish your spears. Put on your helmets and armor, then take your positions.
translation_verse: Mitsi sɔwo ɖe tasiaɖamwo ŋu. Sɔdolawo, mide wo dzi. Miɖɔ gakuku, mianɔ fli me. Minyre miaƒe akplɔwo, eye mido gawu.

english_verse: I can see the battle now— you are defeated and running away, never once looking back. Terror is all around.
translation_verse: Ke nu ka mekpɔ? Dzidzi ƒo wo wogbugbɔ ɖe megbe. Woɖu woƒe aʋakalẽawo dzi, wode afɔ du me sí yina. Megbekpɔkpɔ meli o; ŋɔdzi le afi sia afi. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Afɔtsɔtsɔetɔ mate ŋu así o; aʋakalẽa de sisí ge do kpo. Wokli nu le dzigbeme le Frat-tɔsisi nu, dze anyi.”

english_verse: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
translation_verse: “Ame kae nye esi ho abe Nil ene, abe tɔsisi siwo ɖɔ gbagba ene?

english_verse: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
translation_verse: Egipte ye tso abe Nil ene, abe tɔsisi siwo ɖɔ gbã go la ene. Egblɔ be: Maho, aɖaɖe anyigba la. Matsrɔ̃ duwo kple wo me nɔlawo.

english_verse: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Sɔwo, milũ ɖe eme! Tasiaɖamwo, minyè zi ge ɖe eme! Mina aʋakalẽawo nazɔ ɖe eme. Etiopia kple Put aʋakalẽ akpoxɔnutsɔlaawo ɖe? Ludtɔ aŋutrɔdala siwo bí le dati ŋudɔwɔwɔ me la ɖe? Mido yi!

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbee nye Aƒetɔ Mawu, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la ƒe ŋkeke, hlɔ̃biagbe wònye. Ele hlɔ̃ bia ge eƒe futɔwo na eɖokui. Yi avuvu nu, aɖi ƒo; ano woƒe ʋu amu elabe Aƒetɔ Mawu, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la le vɔ sam le dzigbemenyigba dzi le Frat-tɔsisia nu.

english_verse: Egypt, no medicine can heal you, not even the soothing lotion from Gilead.
translation_verse: Egipte-ɖetugbi leaƒe, yi Gilead nàɖadi atike aɖe kpɔ. Ne èwɔ atike geɖe hã, dzodzroe; mahaya o.

english_verse: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
translation_verse: Dukɔwo se ale si wobɔbɔ wò ɖe anyii. Wò ɣlidodo xɔ anyigba bliboa dzi, elabe aʋakalẽa dze anyi ɖe aʋakalẽa dzi, eye wo kple eve la siaa tsi.” Nebukadnezar gbɔna

english_verse: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
translation_verse: “Mido kpo le Egipte-nyigba dzi. Miɖe gbeƒã le Migdol, Memfis kple Taxpanxes duwo me. Migblɔ be: ‘Mitso, miʋli mia ɖokui ta elabe yi avuvu nu ƒo xlã mi.’

english_verse: I have struck down your mighty god Apis and chased him away.
translation_verse: Nu ka tae mawu Apis sí? Nu ka tae wò nyitsua mete ŋu nɔ te o? Elabe Aƒetɔ tɔ nui ƒu anyi.

english_verse: Your soldiers stumble over each other and say, “Get up! The enemy will kill us, unless we can escape to our own land.”
translation_verse: Wò amehaawo kli nu, dze anyi, eye wogblɔ na wo nɔewo be: ‘Mitso! Mina míagbugbɔ yi mía detɔwo gbɔ, ayi anyigba si dzi wodzi mí ɖo la dzi le ameteɖeanyila ƒe yia ta.’

english_verse: Give the king of Egypt this new name, “Talks-Big-Does-Nothing.”
translation_verse: Miyɔ megbeŋkɔ na Egipte Fiagã la be: ‘Hohoho dzodzro dola, ame si nana be ɣeyiɣi toa eŋu yina.’

english_verse: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
translation_verse: Fia la, ame si ŋkɔe nye Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: Zi ale si mele agbe la, ale si Tabor-to le, le towo katã dome, eye Karmel-to le, le atsiaƒu nu la, nenema wòavae.

english_verse: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
translation_verse: Egiptenɔlawo, mido agba na mia ɖokui na aboyo me yiyi, elabe Memfis azu aƒedo, gbegbe afi si ame maganɔ o.”

english_verse: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
translation_verse: “Egipte le abe nyinɔvi nyakpɔ ene. Ke adzɔ̃e tso dzigbeme va dze ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: The foreign soldiers you hired will turn and run. But they are doomed, like well-fed calves being led to the butcher. *
translation_verse: Eƒe asrafomedzro siwo le egbɔ gɔ̃ hã le abe nyivi damiwo ene. Woawo hã trɔ megbe de afɔ du me hesí dzo. Womenɔ te o; elabe woƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ŋkeke la tu wo, woƒe toheɣi ɖo.”

english_verse: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
translation_verse: “Eƒe nuwɔwɔ le ɖiɖim abe da si le sisím tɔ ene. Elabe eƒe futɔwo le zɔzɔm kple ŋusẽ gbɔna. Wolé fía ɖe asi abe atitsolawo ene.

english_verse: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
translation_verse: Woaƒo eƒe ave dodo la, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, togbɔ be ame mate ŋu age ɖe eme o hã. Elabe woƒe aʋawɔlawo sɔ gbɔ wu ʋetsuviwo, womele xexlẽme o.

english_verse: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
translation_verse: Woado ŋukpe Egipte vinyɔnu la elabe woatsɔe ade asi na dukɔ si tso dzigbeme.”

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: “Kpɔ ɖa, mahe to na Amon, Tebestɔwo ƒe mawua, akpe ɖe Egipte Fiagã kple Egipte-dukɔa kple eƒe mawuwo kple eƒe fiawo ŋu. Mahe to na Egipte Fiagã kple ame siwo katã ɖoa dzi ɖe eŋu la hã.

english_verse: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
translation_verse: Matsɔ wo ade asi na ame siwo le woƒe agbe dim la, Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar kple eƒe amegãwo. Emegbe la, ame aganɔ Egipte-nyigba dzi abe tsã ene.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Aƒetɔ axɔ eƒe dukɔ ɖe agbe

english_verse: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Wò Yakob, nye dɔla, mègavɔ̃ o, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, elabe meli kpli wò. Matsrɔ̃ dukɔ siwo katã dome menyà mi ɖo ɖa la keŋkeŋ. Ke wò la, nyematsrɔ̃ wò keŋ o. Nyemagbe tohehe na wò ya o, ke boŋ mahe to na wò abe ale si dze ene.”

english_verse: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
translation_verse: Hafi Egipte Fiagã naho aɖasi Gaza la, Aƒetɔ de gbe asi na Yeremya tso Filistitɔwo ŋu.

english_verse: I, the Lord, tell you that your land will be flooded with an army from the north. It will destroy your towns and sweep you away, moaning and screaming.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, tsiwo ŋɔ tso dzigbeme gbɔna; woazu tɔɖɔɖɔ ava do. Woaɖe anyigba kple edzi nuwo katã. Woaɖe dua kple eme nɔlawo; amegbetɔwo ado ɣli, eye anyigba dzi nɔla ɖe sia ɖe afa avi.

english_verse: When you hear the thunder of horses and chariots, your courage will vanish, and parents will even abandon their own children.
translation_verse: Ne sɔtsuwo le afɔ tum anyi, tasiaɖamwo le zi nyem, eye tasiaɖamfɔwo le hoo wɔm wose la, vi tɔ́wo matrɔ ɖe wo viwo ŋu o, elabe abɔ ku ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
translation_verse: Elabe ɣeyiɣi de be woatsrɔ̃ Filistitɔwo katã. Woaɖe kpekpeɖeŋu ɖe sia ɖe si atso Tiro kple Sidon ava la ɖa. Elabe Aƒetɔ le Filistitɔ siwo susɔ ɖe Kaftor-ƒukpo dzi la tsrɔ̃ ge.

english_verse: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
translation_verse: Gaza tsi ƒuƒlu. Askalon tsrɔ̃. Ame dzɔtsuwo ƒe susɔeawo, ɣe ka ɣi miade abi mia ɖokui ŋu ase ɖo?

english_verse: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
translation_verse: Ao, Aƒetɔ ƒe yi, ɣe ka ɣi ɖoɖoe azi le nuwò ase ɖo? Trɔ va ge ɖe aku me. Gbɔ ɖe eme, nànɔ anyi kpoo.

english_verse: But how can my sword rest, when I have commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the seacoast?
translation_verse: Gake ale ke wòate ŋu azi ɖoɖoe esime Aƒetɔ de dɔ asi nɛ? Edɔe be wòaɖagblẽ nu le Askalon, eye wòatsrɔ̃ amewo le ƒugowo ŋu.”

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
translation_verse: Gbedeasi ɖe Moab ŋu. Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: “Baba na Nebo elabe wowɔe wòzu aƒedo. Wodo ŋukpe Kiryataim, eye woxɔe. Wodo ŋukpe mɔ́ la, eye womui ƒu anyi.

english_verse: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
translation_verse: Womagakafu Moab azɔ o. Woɖo nugbe ɖe eŋu le Xesbon be: ‘Miva, mina míatsrɔ̃e ɖa, ne maganye dukɔ azɔ o!’ Wò, Madmen hã, woana ɖoɖoe azi le ŋuwò; aʋa ayɔ wò ɖe nu.”

english_verse: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
translation_verse: “Miɖo to! Ɣli le ɖiɖim le Xoronaim me be: ‘Gbegblẽ kple tsɔtsrɔ̃ gã ye!’

english_verse: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
translation_verse: Wotsrɔ̃ Moab! Wose ɣli si ɖi bobobo de Zoar ke!

english_verse: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
translation_verse: Elabe wole avi fam lia Luxit-to dzi mɔ la, esime wole abu ɖim tso Xoronaim, wose woƒe tsɔtsrɔ̃ɣli la.

english_verse: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
translation_verse: Misí! Mixɔ mia ɖokui ɖe agbe! Miwɔ abe gbetedzie le kegbegbe ene!

english_verse: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
translation_verse: Elabe esi nèle dzi ɖom ɖe wò xɔ sesẽwo kple wò kesinɔnuwo ŋu ta la, woaɖu wò hã dziwò. Wò mawu Kemos ayi aboyo me hekpe ɖe eƒe trɔ̃nuawo kple amegãwo ŋu.

english_verse: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
translation_verse: Nugblẽla ava gblẽ nu le du sia du me. Du aɖeke masí o, bali atsrɔ̃, eye woagblẽ gbegbewo abe ale si Aƒetɔ la gblɔe ene.”

english_verse: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
translation_verse: “Mina aʋalawo Moab elabe ele dzodzo ge adzó. Eƒe duwo le aƒedo zu ge, ame aɖeke maganɔ wo me o.”

english_verse: I want you to kill the Moabites, and if you let them escape, I will put a curse on you.”
translation_verse: “Neɖi ame si le alɔgblɔdɔ wɔm le Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔ ŋu la ŋuti. Neɖi ame si gbe eƒe yi hehe ɖe go, be yemakɔ ʋu ɖi o la ŋuti kpékpekpe!” Wotsrɔ̃ Moab-duwo

english_verse: Moab, you are like wine left to settle undisturbed, never poured from jar to jar. And so, your nation continues to prosper and improve.
translation_verse: “Moab li bɔkɔɔ tso eƒe ɖevime; eɖo ƒã ɖi kpoo abe aha ene. Wometrɔe tso eƒe goe me kɔ ɖe goe bubu me kpɔ, alo kplɔe yi aboyo me kpɔ o. Ale eƒe vivi la gale eme ko, eye eƒe ʋeʋẽ nyui la metrɔ o.”

english_verse: But now, I will send enemies to pour out the wine and smash the jars!
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Eya ta, kpɔ ɖa, ɣeyiɣi gbɔna esime madɔ goetrɔlawo ɖa woava trɔe kɔ ɖi tso eƒe goeawo me, eye woagbã goeawo kakɛkakɛe.

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ekema ŋu akpe Moab le eƒe Kemos ta, abe ale si ŋukpe lé Israel hã le Betel si ŋu woɖoa dzi ɖo la ta ene.”

english_verse: You claim that your soldiers are strong and brave.
translation_verse: “Ale ke wɔ miele gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Kalẽtɔwo míenye, aʋakalẽawo míenye!’ mahã?

english_verse: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
translation_verse: Nugblẽla si atsrɔ̃ Moab kple eƒe duwo la va ɖo vɔ. Wokplɔ eƒe ɖekakpui akuakuawo yi wuwu ge. Fia, si ŋkɔe nye Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe.

english_verse: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
translation_verse: Moab ƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃e gã la gogo, eye eƒe fukpekpe le du dzi gbɔna.

english_verse: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
translation_verse: Mi dukɔ siwo katã ƒo xlãe la, mifa nɛ. Mi ame siwo katã nya eŋkɔ la, migblɔ be: ‘Ale wɔ eƒe atizɔti sesẽ la, eƒe atikplɔ nyakpɔ la ŋe?’ ”

english_verse: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
translation_verse: “Wò Dibon-nɔla, ɖi tso wò bubunɔƒe nàva bɔbɔ nɔ anyigba! Elabe Moab-tsrɔ̃la ƒo ɖe dziwò vɔ; egbã wò mɔ́ sesẽwo gɔ̃ xoxo.

english_verse: You people of Aroer, go wait beside the road, and when refugees run by, ask them, “What happened?”
translation_verse: Wò Aroernɔla, va tsi tsitre ɖe mɔ to nànɔ nu kpɔm. Bia ŋutsu si le du dzi va yina kple nyɔnu si le sisím la be: ‘Nya kae dzɔ?’

english_verse: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Wodo ŋukpe Moab elabe wogbãe. Mifa avi; mido ɣli! Miɖe gbeƒã le Arnon-tɔsisi nu be wogbã Moab.”

english_verse: I will punish every town that belongs to Moab, but especially Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,
translation_verse: “Wobu fɔ du siwo le tonyigba gbadza la dzi: Xolon, Yaza-Mefaat,

english_verse: Dibon, Nebo, Beth-Diblathaim,
translation_verse: Dibo, Nebo kple Bet-Diblatayim,

english_verse: Kiriathaim, Beth-Gamul, Beth-Meon,
translation_verse: Kiryataim, Bet-Gamul, Bet-Meon,

english_verse: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
translation_verse: Woŋe dzo le Moab ta. Eƒe abɔ ŋe. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Woabɔbɔ Moab ɖe anyi

english_verse: People of Moab, you claim to be stronger than I am. Now I will tell other nations to make you drunk and to laugh while you collapse in your own vomit.
translation_verse: “Mina wòano amu, elabe evu eɖokui gblotoo ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu, ale be Moab namli le nu si wòtru la me, ne woaɖe alɔ me le eya hã ŋu.

english_verse: You made fun of my people and treated them like criminals caught in the act.
translation_verse: Ɖe Israel menye alɔmeɖenu na wò kpɔ oa? Ɖe wokpɔe le fiafiwo dome kpɔ, hafi ne ènya le nu ƒom le eŋu ko nènɔa ta ʋuʋuma?”

english_verse: Now you must leave your towns and live like doves in the shelter of cliffs and canyons.
translation_verse: “Mi Moabnɔlawo, miʋu le duawo me ne miaɖanɔ agatowo me! Minɔ abe ahɔnɛ si wɔ atɔ ɖe agakpewo toga la ene.

english_verse: I know about your pride, and how you strut and boast.
translation_verse: Míese Moab ƒe dàda ŋkɔ; edàna ŋutɔ. Edoa eɖokui ɖe dzi glodzoo; eƒoa adegbe; edzraa eɖokui, eye eƒe dzi blenɛ.

english_verse: But I also know bragging will never save you.
translation_verse: Menya eƒe amemabumabu. Eɖia nu me alakpatɔe, eƒe nuwɔnawo nye alakpa.

english_verse: So I will cry and mourn for Moab and its town of Kir-Heres.
translation_verse: Eya ta mele avi fam na Moab. Mele fafam na Moab bliboa, mele konyi fam na Kir-Xeres ŋutsuwo.

english_verse: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
translation_verse: Sibma ƒe wainka, mele avi fam na wò wu Yazer. Wò alɔdzewo to ƒu la dzi ɖaɖo ƒu nu le keke Yazer ke. Ke nugblẽla la va ƒo ɖi le wò kutsetsegbeɣi kple wainxaɣi.

english_verse: Harvest celebrations are gone from the orchards and farms of Moab. I have silenced the shouts of people making wine.
translation_verse: Dzidzɔkpɔkpɔ kple aseyetsotso nu tso le agble wɔnuwo me, le Moab-nyigba dzi. Mena wain nu tso le wainfiãnuwo me; ame aɖeke megafiãa wain kple aseyetsotso o. Ɣli aɖeke hã meganyea dzidzɔɣli o.”

english_verse: Weeping from Heshbon can be heard as far as Elealeh and Jahaz; cries from Zoar are heard in Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
translation_verse: “Ame siwo le Xesbon kple Eleale ƒe ɣli ɖi. Woƒe ɣlia de keke Yahaz ke, tso Zoar va ɖo Xoronaim kple Eglat Selisxiya ke hã, elabe Nimrim-tɔʋuwo gɔ̃ hã mie.

english_verse: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: Matsrɔ̃ amewo le Moab, ame si saa vɔ le nuxeƒe, eye wòtɔa dzo lifi na eƒe mawu.

english_verse: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
translation_verse: Eya ta nye dzi le nu xam le Moab ta abe dze kum wole ene, eye nye dzi le nu xam le Kir-Xerestɔwo ta abe konyifala si le dze kum la ene. Eya ta kesinɔnu si su wo si la ƒe ɖekeɖeke megali o.”

english_verse: The people of Moab mourn on the rooftops and in the streets. Men cut off their beards, people shave their heads; they make cuts on their hands and wear sackcloth. And it's all because I, the Lord, have shattered Moab like a jar that no one wants.
translation_verse: Amewo le xɔta kple ablɔwo me le afi sia afi le Moab le nu xam, elabe megbã Moab abe ze si ame aɖeke mehiã o la ene. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Moab lies broken! Listen to its people cry as they turn away in shame. Other nations are horrified at what happened, but still they mock her.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ale si wogbãe la ɖa! Kpɔ ale si wòle avi fam hehehe la ɖa! Kpɔ ale si ŋu kpe Moab, wòtrɔ megbe la ɖa! Ale Moab zu alɔmeɖenu kple ŋɔdzinu na dukɔ siwo katã ƒo xlãe godoo.” Moab mate ŋu así o

english_verse: Moab, an enemy swoops down like an eagle spreading its wings over your land.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, futɔ aɖe adzo sesĩe, abe hɔ̃e le nu ƒo ge ene, eye wòakeke eƒe aʋala ɖe Moab ŋu.

english_verse: Your cities and fortresses will be captured, and your warriors as fearful as women giving birth.
translation_verse: Aɖu duwo dzi, eye wòaxɔ mɔ́ sesẽwo. Gbe ma gbe la, Moab ƒe aʋakalẽawo ƒe dzi anɔ abe nyɔnu si le ku lém la tɔ ene.

english_verse: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Woatsrɔ̃ Moab, eye maganye dukɔ azɔ o; elabe edo eɖokui ɖe dzi glodzoo ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu.

english_verse: Terror, pits, and traps are waiting for you.
translation_verse: Moabnɔlawo, ŋɔdzi, ʋe kple mɔ̀ le mia ŋgɔ. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ame si sí le ŋɔdzi nu la, adze ʋe la me; ame si do le ʋe la me la, mɔ̀ la aɖee; elabe meɖo be mahe nu siawo ava Moab dzi le ƒè si me mahe to na wo la.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
translation_verse: “Ame síaʋa siwo ŋu wɔna vɔ le la, tɔ te ɖe Xesbon ƒe vɔvɔli me; elabe dzo le bibim tso Xesbon yina. Dzoa tso Sixon ƒe aƒeme. Dzoa fiã Moab ƒe liƒowo kple ame siwo dɔa aʋa la ƒe fiakuku.

english_verse: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
translation_verse: Moab, baba na wò! Wò, Kemos subɔla, wotsrɔ̃ wò elabe woɖe aboyo viwò ŋutsuwo, eye wokplɔ viwò nyɔnuwo yi aboyo me.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ke hã la, mana Moab ƒe nunyonamewo agava nɛ emegbe.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Afi siae wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnu Moab se ɖo.

english_verse: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
translation_verse: Gbedeasi ɖe Amonviwo ŋu. Aƒetɔ be: “Viŋutsuwo mele Israel si oa? Domenyila aɖeke mele esi oa? Ke nu ka tae Milkom xɔ Gad wòzu etɔ, eye eteviwo tso aƒe ɖe eƒe duwo me?

english_verse: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
translation_verse: Eya ta, Aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, ɣeyiɣi gbɔna, esime mana aʋaɣli naɖi ɖe Amonviwo ƒe du Raba ŋu. Azu glikpo ɖi, eye woatɔ dzo eƒe kɔƒewo, ekema Israel agaxɔ eƒe domenyinu si woxɔ le esi la.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
translation_verse: “Xesbontɔwo, mifa avi, elabe wogbã Ai-du! Raba vinyɔnuwo, mido ɣli! Mita akpanya, mifa konyi, eye mianɔ du dzi anɔ yiyim anɔ gbɔgbɔm le ati dodoe bɔwo me. Elabe miaƒe mawu Milkom ayi aboyo me kple eƒe trɔ̃nuawo kple eƒe amegãwo.

english_verse: You rebellious Ammonites trust your wealth and ask, “Who could attack us?” But I warn you not to boast when your strength is fading.
translation_verse: O, vinyɔnu maxɔse, nu ka ta nètsɔ wò baliwo le adegbe ƒomee? Wò si ɖoa dzi ɖe wò kesinɔnuwo ŋu lae le biabiam be: ‘Ame kae atso ava dze dzinye’ mahã?

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, mahe ŋɔdzi ava dziwò, Aƒetɔ Mawu, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe, atso dukɔ siwo katã ƒo xlã wò la me, eye woanyà wò ado goe, ame sia ame akpɔ eŋgɔ tẽe adzo, ame aɖeke maƒo sisílaawo nu ƒu o.”

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
translation_verse: “Gake emegbe la, magaɖo Amonviwo te, agbugbɔ woƒe nunyonamewo na wo”. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Aƒetɔ ahe to na Edom

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says about Edom: Wisdom and common sense have vanished from Teman.
translation_verse: Gbedeasi ɖe Edom ŋu. Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Ɖe nunya megale Teman oa? Ɖe adaŋudede bu ɖe nunyalawoa? Ɖe woƒe nunya bu vĩa?

english_verse: I will send disaster to punish you descendants of Esau, so anyone from Dedan had better turn around and run back home.
translation_verse: Dedantɔwo, misí! Mitrɔ dzo! Miɣla mia ɖokui ɖe agadowo me, elabe mele Esau ƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃e gã la he ge va edzi; le ɣe si ɣi mahe to nɛ.

english_verse: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
translation_verse: Ne waintsetsexalawo va xa nu le mia gbɔ la, ɖe womegblẽa ɖewo ɖe kaawo ŋu oa? Ne fiafiwo va nu fi ge le zã me la, ɖe wometsɔa nu si ko dim wole, eye wogblẽa nanewo ko oa?

english_verse: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
translation_verse: Ke nye ya, meɖe ama Esau. Meklo nu le eƒe bebeƒewo dzi, eye magate ŋu aɣla eɖokui o. Metsrɔ̃ viawo kple nɔvia ŋutsuwo kple eƒe aƒelikawo, eye megali o.

english_verse: But I can be trusted to care for your orphans and widows.
translation_verse: Migblẽ miaƒe tsyɔ̃eviwo ɖi; makpɔ wo ta woatsi agbe. Mina miaƒe ahosiwo naɖo dzi ɖe ŋunye.”

english_verse: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ be: “Ne ame siwo medze be woano kplu la me nu o, hafi wonoe godoo la, ɖe woagbe tohehe na wò yaa? Màtsi tomahe o, ele be nànoe kokoko.

english_verse: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: Elabe metà ɖokuinye be ne Bozra mezu ŋɔdzinu, alɔmeɖenu, aƒedo kple ɖiŋudonu, eye eƒe duwo katã zu gbegbe tegbee o fĩi!”

english_verse: I have sent a messenger to command the nations to prepare for war against you people of Edom.
