translation_verse: Mexɔ gbedeasi tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ, eye woɖo amedɔdɔ ɖe dukɔwo dome be: “Miƒo mia ɖokui nu ƒu ne miava kpe akɔ kplii. Ne miatso na aʋawɔwɔ.”

english_verse: Your nation will be small, yet hated by other nations.
translation_verse: Elabe, kpɔ ɖa, mawɔ wò nànɔ sue le dukɔwo dome, eye woado vlo wò le amegbetɔwo dome.

english_verse: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
translation_verse: Ŋɔdzi si le ŋuwò ble wò, eye nèdana le dzime; wò si le agatowo me, eye nètso aƒe ɖe keke towo tame ʋĩi ke lae. Togbɔ be nèwɔ atɔ ɖe kɔkɔƒe ʋĩi abe hɔ̃ ene hã la, mahe wò tso afi ma ava anyigbae. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: People passing by your country will be shocked and horrified to see a disaster
translation_verse: “Edom azu ŋɔdzinu, eye ame sia ame si to eŋu yina la ŋɔdzi alée, eye wòaʋuʋu ta le dzɔgbevɔ̃e siwo katã dzɔ ɖe edzi la ta.

english_verse: as bad as the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and towns nearby. The towns of Edom will be empty.
translation_verse: Abe ale si wònɔ na Sodom kple Gomora kpakple wo ŋu duwo esime metsrɔ̃ wo enee la, nenemae ame maganɔ afi ma o, eye womagatso aƒe ɖi o. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ale si dzata dona tso ave dodo me le Yordan ŋu, ɖe lãha siwo ƒo ƒu ŋui la, nenema mele wo wɔ ge woasí du adzo le egbɔ kpata, eye matia ame si melɔ̃ la wòaɖu edzi. Elabe ame kae sɔ kplim? Ame kae ate ŋu asamam? Alẽkplɔla kae ate ŋu anɔ te ɖe nunye?

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will reach the Red Sea and cause the earth to shake.
translation_verse: Woƒe anyidzedze ana anyigba la katã naʋuʋu, eye woƒe ɣli aɖi ade keke Aƒlaƒu la nu ke.

english_verse: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, futɔ aɖe atso ɖe Bozra ŋu, adzo sesĩe akeke eƒe aʋala me abe hɔ̃e be yeaƒo nu ene. Gbe ma gbe la, aʋawɔla siwo le Edom ƒe dziwo anɔ abe nyɔnu si le ku lém la tɔ ene.” Aƒetɔ ahe to na Damasko

english_verse: The Lord says about Damascus: The towns of Hamath and Arpad have heard your bad news. They have lost hope, and worries roll over them like ocean waves.
translation_verse: Gbedeasi ɖe Damasko ŋu. “Gbɔgblɔ bu ɖe Xamat kple Arpad elabe wose nya vɔ̃. Dzi ɖe le wo ƒo. Wotsi dzodzodzoe abe atsiaƒu si mate ŋu azi ɖoɖoe o la ene.

english_verse: You people of Damascus have lost your courage, and in panic you turn to run, gripped by fear and pain.
translation_verse: Damasko gbɔdzɔ, eye wòtrɔ be yeasí. Dzidzi ƒoe! Ŋɔdzi lée, eye wòle veve sem abe nyɔnu si le ku lém la ene.

english_verse: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
translation_verse: Kpɔ ale si wogblẽ du xɔŋkɔ la, aseyetsodu la ɖi ɖa!

english_verse: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
translation_verse: Eya ta woawu eƒe ɖekakpuiwo ɖe woƒe ablɔwo dzi, eye woatsrɔ̃ woƒe aʋawɔlawo katã gbe ma gbe. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
translation_verse: Matɔ dzo Damasko-dua ƒe gliwo, eye fia Hadad vi ƒe fiasãwo afiã.” Aƒetɔ ahe to na Kedar-to la kple Xazor-du

english_verse: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
translation_verse: Gbedeasi ku ɖe Kedar kple Xazor ƒe fiaɖuƒe siwo dzi Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar ɖu la ŋu. Aƒetɔ be: “Mitso! Milũ ɖe Kedar dzi! Mitsrɔ̃ ɣedzeƒenɔlawo!

english_verse: Run and hide, you people of the desert who live in villages! Nebuchadnezzar has big plans for you.
translation_verse: Xazornɔlawo, misí! Miɣla mia ɖokui ɖe agadowo me! Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Elabe Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar de adaŋu heɖo nugbe ɖe mia ŋu.”

english_verse: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
translation_verse: “Mitso! Mizɔ ɖe dukɔ si li bɔkɔɔ la dzi, dukɔ si me dedienɔnɔ le la dzi. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Agbo alo gameti mele woƒe duwo nu o; woawo ɖeɖe koe li.

english_verse: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Woƒe kposɔwo azu aboyonu; woƒe lãha azu nu woaha. Makaka ame siwo ƒlɔa ta kolikoli la ahlẽ ɖe afi sia afi, eye mahe dzɔgbevɔ̃e gã tso goawo katã me ava wo dzii. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Only jackals will live where your villages once stood. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Elam
translation_verse: Xazor ava zu akpatakuwo nɔƒe, azu gbegbe tegbee. Ame maganɔ afi ma o; womagatso aƒe ɖi o.” Aƒetɔ ahe to na Elam

english_verse: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Kpɔ ɖa, maŋe Elam ƒe dati si nye eƒe ŋusẽ vevitɔ la.

english_verse: Enemies will attack from all directions, and you will be led captive to every nation on earth.
translation_verse: Makplɔ ya tso dziƒo ƒe go eneawo dzi ava ƒo ɖe Elam dzi, eye maka wo ahlẽ ɖe ya mawo katã nu. Dukɔ aɖeke manɔ xexea me, esime Elamtɔwo makaka ɖo o.

english_verse: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Matsrɔ̃ Elam-fia kple eƒe amegãwo, eye malí nye fiazikpui anyi ɖe afi ma.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
translation_verse: “Gake emegbe la, magaɖo Elam te, eye magbugbɔ eƒe nunyonamewo nɛ.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedeasi na Yeremya, gbeƒãɖela la, ɖe Babilon kple Kaldea-nyigba ŋu:

english_verse: Raise the signal flags; shout so all nations can hear— Babylon will be captured! Marduk, Babylon's god, will be ashamed and terrified, and his idols broken.
translation_verse: “Mido kpo le dukɔwo dome, eye miaɖe gbeƒãe! Mido aflaga ɖe dzi, eye miaɖe gbeƒãe! Migaɣlae o! Migblɔ be: ‘Woxɔ Babilon! Wodo ŋukpe Bel! Dzi ɖe le mawu Merodax ƒo. Wodo ŋukpe eƒe legbawo, eye dzi ɖe le eƒe mawuwo ƒo.’ ”

english_verse: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
translation_verse: “Elabe dukɔ aɖe ho tso dzigbeme va esi ge. Ado aƒedo anyigba la, eye ame aɖeke maganɔ edzi o. Amegbetɔwo kple lãwo siaa así, adzo.” Israel atrɔ gbɔ

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Le ŋkeke mawo me le ɣe ma ɣi la, Israel-dukɔ kple Yuda-dukɔ siaa aƒo ƒu atrɔ gbɔ, anɔ avi fam anɔ Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la dim.

english_verse: You will ask the way to Zion and then come and join with me in making an agreement you won't break or forget.
translation_verse: Woabia Zion-mɔ ta se, eye woaɖo ta afi ma agblɔ be: ‘Miva, mina miaƒo ƒu aku ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu, abla nu mavɔ si womaŋlɔ be akpɔ o la kplii.’ ”

english_verse: My people, you are lost sheep abandoned in the mountains by their shepherds. You don't even remember your resting place.
translation_verse: “Nye dukɔ zu alẽ siwo bu. Wo kplɔlawo kplɔ wo trae yi towo dzi. Wole tsatsam tso to dzi yi togbɛ dzi, eye woŋlɔ wo nɔƒe be.

english_verse: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
translation_verse: Ame siwo katã kpɔ wo la, vuvu wo, eye woƒe futɔwo gblɔ be: ‘Míeɖi fɔ o, elabe woawo ŋutɔe wɔ vɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu. Aƒetɔ ye nye woƒe lãnyiƒe vavãtɔ, eye wònye wo tɔgbuiwo ƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Escape from Babylonia, my people. Get out of that country! Don't wait for anyone else.
translation_verse: Misí tso Babilon! Mido go le Kaldeatɔwo ƒe anyigba la dzi! Minɔ abe gbɔ̃tsuwo ene le alẽha la ŋgɔ.

english_verse: In the north I am bringing great nations together. They will attack Babylon and capture it. The arrows they shoot are like the best soldiers, always finding their target.
translation_verse: Elabe kpɔ ɖa, mele dukɔ triakɔ aɖewo ƒe ha nyɔm le dzigbemenyigba dzi ɖe Babilon ŋu. Woadze aʋa ɖe eŋu ahaxɔe. Woƒe aŋutrɔwo medaa dadagbo o; wole abe aʋawɔla asinudzɔdzɔetɔ tɔ ene.”

english_verse: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
translation_verse: Woaha Kaldea-nyigba la, eye ehalawo katã aɖi ƒo. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Wogbã Babilon-dua

english_verse: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
translation_verse: “Nye domenyinuhalawo, togbɔ be miele dzidzɔ kpɔm, togbɔ be miele aseye tsom, togbɔ be miele kpo tim movitɔe abe nyinɔvie le gbeɖuƒe ene, eye miele xɔxlɔ̃m abe sɔtsuwo ene hã la,

english_verse: The city of Babylon was like a mother to you. But it will be disgraced and become nothing but a barren desert.
translation_verse: ŋu akpe mia nɔ vevie, eye woado ŋukpe eya ame si dzi wò. Kpɔ ɖa, anye suetɔ le dukɔwo dome, anye gbedadaƒo si ƒu kple kegbegbe.

english_verse: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
translation_verse: Le dɔmedzoe si Aƒetɔ do ɖe eŋu ta la, ame maganɔ edzi o, ke boŋ azu aƒedo keŋkeŋ. Ame sia ame si ato Babilon-du ŋu ayi la, ƒe nu aku, eye wòaʋuʋu ta ɖe eŋu le abi siwo katã le eŋu ta.

english_verse: Babylon has rebelled against me. Archers, take your places. Shoot all your arrows at Babylon.
translation_verse: Mi ame siwo katã vu miaƒe dati me, midze aʋa ƒo xlã Babilon. Mitee! Migagblẽ aŋutrɔ aɖeke ɖi o! Elabe ewɔ nuvɔ̃ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu.

english_verse: Attack from every side! Babylon surrenders! The enemy tears down its walls and towers. I am taking my revenge by doing to Babylon what it did to other cities.
translation_verse: Mido aʋaɣli hoo ɖe eŋu be ena ta! Eƒe sɔtiwo ŋe dze eme! Womu eƒe gliwo! Elabe Aƒetɔ le hlɔ̃ biam. Miawo hã mibia hlɔ̃e. Miwɔe abe ale si wòwɔ amewo ene.

english_verse: There is no one in Babylonia to plant or harvest crops. Even foreigners who lived there have left for their homelands, afraid of the enemy armies.
translation_verse: Mitsrɔ̃ nuƒãla kple nuŋela ɖa le Babilon, elabe ameteɖeanyila he aʋa vɛ; ame sia ame atrɔ yi eya ŋutɔ ƒe dukɔ me, eye ame sia ame así yi eya ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi.” Israel atrɔ gbɔ

english_verse: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
translation_verse: “Israel nye alẽ si dzatawo yɔ ɖe nu. Gbã la, Asiria-fiae vuvui, eye azɔ la, Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar va kuko eƒe ƒuwo.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Eya ta, Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Kpɔ ɖa, mahe to na Babilon-fia kple eƒe anyigba abe ale si mehee na Asiria-fia ene.

english_verse: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
translation_verse: Magakplɔ Israel agbɔ va eƒe lãnyiƒe, eye wòaɖu gbe le Karmel ŋu kple Basan. Woakpɔ nu aɖu aɖi ƒo le Efrayim-togbɛwo dzi kple Gilead me.

english_verse: I will rescue a few people from Israel and Judah. I will forgive them so completely that their sin and guilt will disappear, never to be found. The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: Le ŋkeke mawo me le ɣe ma ɣi la, woadi nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ le Israel-dukɔ me, ke womakpɔe o; woadi nuvɔ̃ le Yuda-dukɔ me hã, ke womakpɔ ɖeke o, elabe matsɔ nu ake ame siwo mesusɔ ɖi la.” Mawu ahe to na Babilonia

english_verse: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
translation_verse: “Miho ɖe Meratayim-nyigba kple Pekodtɔwo ŋu. Miwu wo, mitsrɔ̃ wo katã keŋkeŋ, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, eye nàwɔ nu siwo katã meɖe gbe be nàwɔ la.

english_verse: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Aʋaɣli le ɖiɖim le anyigba la dzi, eye nuwo le tsɔtsrɔ̃m ale gbegbe.

english_verse: Babylonia was a hammer pounding every country, but now it lies broken. What a shock to the nations of the world!
translation_verse: Kpɔ ale si anyigba blibo la ƒe zu gbã hekakae la ɖa! Kpɔ ale si Babilon va zu ŋɔdzinu le dukɔwo domee la ɖa!

english_verse: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
translation_verse: Babilon, meɖo mɔ̀ ɖi na wò, eye meɖe wò, gake mènyae o. Asi tu wò, eye melé wò elabe èle avu wɔm kple Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: I've brought out my weapons, and with them I will put a curse on Babylonia.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ʋu eƒe aʋawɔnudzraɖoƒeʋɔ, eye wòhe eƒe dzikuʋawɔnuwo do goe elabe dɔ aɖe le Aƒetɔ Mawu, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la si be wòawɔ le Kaldeatɔwo ƒe anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: Come from far away, you enemies of Babylon! Pile up the grain from its storehouses, and destroy it completely, along with everything else.
translation_verse: Mizɔ ɖe edzi tso goawo katã me va tui. Miʋu nu le eƒe avawo nu! Milɔ nuawo li kɔe ɖi abe lubabla ene, eye mitsrɔ̃ dukɔa keŋkeŋ. Migasusɔ naneke ɖi nɛ o.

english_verse: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
translation_verse: Miwu eƒe nyitsuwo katã! Mikplɔ wo yi lãwuƒe lae. Baba na wo, elabe woƒe ŋkeke de, woƒe toheɣi ɖo.”

english_verse: The Babylonian army destroyed my temple, but soon I will take revenge. Then refugees from Babylon will tell about it in Zion.
translation_verse: “Miɖo to! Wosí tso Babilon-nyigba dzi va be woaɖe gbeƒã ale si Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la, le hlɔ̃ biam ɖe eƒe gbedoxɔ nui la, le Zion.”

english_verse: Attack Babylon, enemy archers; set up camp around the city, and don't let anyone escape. It challenged me, the holy God, so do to it what it did to other cities. Proud Babylon Will Fall
translation_verse: “Miyɔ aŋutrɔdalawo vɛ ɖe Babilon ŋu. Mi ame siwo katã bí le dati ŋudɔwɔwɔ me ko, miyi. Miɖe to ɖee godoo; migana ame aɖeke nasí o. Miɖo nu siwo wòwɔ la teƒe nɛ. Miwɔe nɛ tututu abe ale si eya hã wɔe ene; elabe Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu Kɔkɔe la ŋu wòle dàdam le hewɔ nu tovo ɖo.

english_verse: People of Babylon, I, the Lord, promise that even your best soldiers will lie dead in the streets.
translation_verse: Eya ta gbe ma gbe la, woawu eƒe ɖekakpuiwo le eƒe kpɔdomeewo, eye woatsrɔ̃ eƒe aʋawɔlawo katã.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
translation_verse: “Wò dàdala, kpɔ ɖa, metsi tre ɖe ŋuwò, Aƒetɔ Mawu, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe, elabe wò ŋkeke de, ɣe si ɣi mahe to na wò la ɖo.

english_verse: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
translation_verse: Dàdala la akli nu adze anyi, eye ame aɖeke mafɔe ɖe tsitrenu o. Matɔ dzo eƒe duwo, eye wòabi nu sia nu aƒo xlãe.”

english_verse: You Babylonians were cruel to Israel and Judah. You took them captive, and now you refuse to let them go.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Wote Israel-dukɔ kple Yuda-dukɔ ɖe anyi. Ame siwo ɖe aboyo wo la lé wo goŋgoŋ, eye wogbe asiɖeɖe le wo ŋu ne woadzo.

english_verse: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, will rescue and protect them. I will bring peace to their land and trouble to yours.
translation_verse: Gake wo Ɖela nye ŋusẽtɔ. Eŋkɔ nye Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla. Eya ŋutɔ axɔ woƒe nya ɖe akɔ, eye wòana gbɔdzɔe anyigba la; ke ana zitɔtɔ nanɔ Babiloniatɔwo dome.”

english_verse: I have declared war on you, your officials, and advisors.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Aʋa netsrɔ̃ Kaldeatɔwo. Netsrɔ̃ Babiloniatɔwo, eƒe amegãwo kple nunyalawo.

english_verse: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
translation_verse: Aʋa netsrɔ̃ woƒe afakalawo ne woazu bometsilawo. Netso ɖe woƒe aʋawɔlawo ŋu ne woatsrɔ̃!

english_verse: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
translation_verse: Aʋa netso ɖe woƒe sɔwo, tasiaɖamwo kple amedzrosrafo siwo katã le wo dome la ŋu ne woazu nyɔnugbɔmewo. Aʋa netso ɖe woƒe kesinɔnuwo ŋu, ne woaha wo!

english_verse: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
translation_verse: Ku neɖi ne eƒe tɔwo namie! Elabe enye anyigba si dzi legbawo le, eye wodoa tsu mawuawo subɔlawo.”

english_verse: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
translation_verse: Abe ale si wònɔ esime Mawu gbã Sodom kple Gomora kpakple du siwo ƒo xlã wo enee la, nenemae ame maganɔ afi ma o; ame aɖeke magatso aƒe ɖe afi ma o.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
translation_verse: “Kpɔ ɖa, dukɔ aɖe ho tso dzigbeme va ɖo. Dukɔ triakɔ kple fia geɖewoe le hohom tso anyigba ƒe didiƒe ʋĩi ke gbɔna.

english_verse: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
translation_verse: Dati kple akplɔ le wo si, wosẽa ŋuta, eye womekpɔa nublanui na ame o. Woƒe ɣli ɖina abe atsiaƒue le gbe ɖem ene. Wole sɔwo dzi, bla akpa abe ŋutsu ene na aʋawɔwɔ kple wò Babilon vinyɔnu.”

english_verse: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
translation_verse: “Babilon-fia se wo ŋu nya, abɔ fa ɖe eŋu. Vɔvɔ̃ ɖo eyama, eye wòse veve abe nyɔnu si le ku lém la ene.”

english_verse: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: “Kpɔ ɖa, ale si dzata dona tso ave dodo me le Yordan ŋu, ɖe lãha siwo ƒo ƒu ŋui la, nenema mele wo wɔ ge woasí du adzo le egbɔ kpata, eye matia ame si melɔ̃ la wòaɖu edzi. Elabe ame kae sɔ kplim? Ame kae ate ŋu asamam? Alẽkplɔla kae ate ŋu anɔ te ɖe nunye?

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will be heard among the nations, and the earth will shake.
translation_verse: Ne woxɔ Babilon-dua la, ɣli aɖi hoo ale be anyigba aʋuʋu, eye eƒe konyifaɣli aɖi woase le dukɔwo dome.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, am sending a wind to destroy the people of Babylonia and Babylon, its capital.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, maʋuʋu nugblẽla aɖe ƒe gbɔgbɔ wòatso ɖe Babilon ŋu, wòatso ɖe ame siwo le Kaldea la ŋu.

english_verse: Foreign soldiers will come from every direction, and when the disaster is over, Babylonia will be empty and worthless.
translation_verse: Maɖo nugbɔlawo ɖe Babilon, eye woagbɔe. Woana eƒe anyigba la naɖi ƒuƒlu, ne wova dze wo dzi tso akpa sia akpa le xaxagbe ma.

english_verse: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
translation_verse: Migana aŋutrɔdala navu eƒe da me o, eye migana wòado eƒe gawu o. Migagblẽ woƒe ɖekakpuiwo ɖi o; mitsrɔ̃ eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: Their troops will fall wounded in the streets of Babylon.
translation_verse: Woadze anyi atsi aʋa le Kaldea-nyigba dzi, eye woade abi wo ŋu ɖe eƒe ablɔwo me.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel and Judah is guilty. But I, the Lord All-Powerful, their holy God, have not abandoned them.
translation_verse: Elabe Mawu, Aƒetɔ Aʋakɔwokplɔla la, megblẽ Israel-dukɔ kple Yuda-dukɔ ɖi o, gake fɔɖiɖi ɖe Israel ƒe Kɔkɔetɔ la ŋu yɔ Kaldeatɔwo ƒe anyigba la dzi.”

english_verse: Get out of Babylon! Run for your lives! If you stay, you will be killed when I take revenge on the city and punish it for its sins.
translation_verse: “Misí dzo le Babilon! Mina ame sia ame naɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe agbe! Mele be miatsrɔ̃ ɖe eƒe fɔɖiɖi ta o, elabe Aƒetɔ ƒe hlɔ̃biaɣie nye esia. Nu si wòwɔ la teƒe ɖom wole nɛ.

english_verse: Babylon was my golden cup, filled with the wine of my anger. The nations of the world got drunk on this wine and went insane.
translation_verse: Babilon le abe sikakplu ene le Aƒetɔ ƒe asi me, eye wòna xexea me katã mu aha. Dukɔwo no eƒe wain eya ta woƒe susu tɔtɔ.

english_verse: But suddenly, Babylon will fall and be destroyed. I, the Lord, told the foreigners who lived there, “Weep for the city! Get medicine for its wounds; maybe they will heal.”
translation_verse: Kasia Babilon ge dze anyi hegbã! Mifa avi vevie ɖe eŋu. Mitsɔ atike bla abiawo nɛ kpɔ, ɖewohĩ ahaya.

english_verse: The foreigners answered, “We have already tried to treat Babylon's wounds, but they would not heal. Come on, let's all go home to our own countries. Nothing is left in Babylonia; everything is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Ɖe míedi be míada gbe le Babilon ŋu hafi, ke mete ŋu haya o. Migblẽe ɖi, eye mina ame sia ame nadzo yi eya ŋutɔ wo de. Elabe eƒe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ de dziƒo ke, eye wòyi ɖatɔ dziŋgɔli gɔ̃.

english_verse: I, the Lord, want Babylon destroyed, because its army destroyed my temple. So, you kings of Media, sharpen your arrows and pick up your shields.
translation_verse: “Minyre aŋutrɔawo! Mitsɔ akpoxɔnuawo! Aƒetɔ ʋuʋu Media-fiawo ƒe gbɔgbɔ be woatso elabe eɖo tame ɖe Babilon ŋu be woatsrɔ̃e. Aƒetɔ ƒe hlɔ̃biabia ye nye ema, hlɔ̃biabia ɖe eƒe gbedoxɔ nu wònye.

english_verse: People of Babylon, you live along the Euphrates River and are surrounded by canals. You are rich, but now the time has come for you to die.
translation_verse: Mi tɔ geɖewo to nɔlawo, mi ame siwo si kesinɔnu xɔasiwo le fũu, miaƒe nuwuwu ɖo; wotso miaƒe agbe ƒe ka.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, swear by my own life that enemy soldiers will fill your streets like a swarm of locusts. They will shout and celebrate their victory. A Hymn of Praise (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla tà eya ŋutɔ ɖokui gblɔ be: Ne nyemekplɔ aʋakɔwo vɛ kpaŋkpaŋkpaŋ, abe ʋetsuviwo ene va ƒo ɖe anyigba sia dzi taŋ, eye woƒe dziɖuɣli ɖi ɖe mia ŋu hoo o fĩi!” Kafukafuha na Mawu

english_verse: The waters in the heavens roar at his command. He makes clouds appear; he sends the wind from his storehouse and makes lightning flash in the rain.
translation_verse: Ne eɖe gbe la, dziŋgɔli me tsiwo dzea agbo. Enana be afu dona yia dzi tso anyigba ƒe mlɔenu ke. Ewɔ dzikedzo na tsidzadza, eye wònana be ya dona tso eƒe nudzraɖoƒe.

english_verse: God used his wisdom and power to create the earth and spread out the heavens.
translation_verse: “Eyae wɔ anyigba kple eƒe ŋusẽ, etsɔ nunya ɖo xexea me gɔme anyi, eye wòtsɔ eƒe nugɔmesese keke dziƒo me.

english_verse: People who make idols are stupid! They will be disappointed, because their false gods cannot breathe.
translation_verse: Ame sia ame dzɔ movi, eye medze si nu o. Sikanutula ɖe sia ɖe ƒe legbawo doa ŋukpee, elabe nu siwo wòtu la nye alakpa; agbe mele wo me o.

english_verse: Idols are merely a joke, and when the time is right, they will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Nu dzodzro siwo ɖi kokoe la wonye. Gbe si gbe woahe to na wo la, woatsrɔ̃.

english_verse: But the Lord, Israel's God, is all-powerful. He created everything, and he chose Israel to be his very own. God's Hammer The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yakob ƒe gome ya mele abe woawo ene o. Elabe eyae wɔ nuwo katã, eye Israel-to la nye eƒe domenyinu. Eŋkɔe nye Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la.” Aƒetɔ ƒe zu

english_verse: Babylonia, you were my hammer; I used you to pound nations and break kingdoms,
translation_verse: “Wòe nye nye zu, nye aʋawɔnu: Wòe metsɔna gbãa dukɔwoe gudugudu; wòe metsɔna tsrɔ̃a fiaɖuƒewoe.

english_verse: But now, my people will watch, while I repay you for what you did to Zion.
translation_verse: “Maɖo eteƒe na Babilon kple Kaldea-nyigba dzi nɔlawo katã le miawo ŋutɔ ŋkume miakpɔ, le nuvɔ̃ɖi siwo katã wowɔ le Zion la ta. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.”

english_verse: You destroyed the nations and seem strong as a mountain, but I am your enemy. I might even grab you and roll you off a cliff. When I am finished, you'll only be a pile of scorched bricks.
translation_verse: “Kpɔ ɖa, wò to si gblẽa nu, metso ɖe ŋuwò, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, wòe tsrɔ̃ xexea me katã. Mado asi ɖa ahamli wò tso agakpe dzi aƒu anyi awɔ wò nànye to si fiã la.

english_verse: Your stone blocks won't be reused for cornerstones or foundations, and I promise that forever you will be a desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Nations Will Attack Babylon The Lord said:
translation_verse: Womatsɔ wò kpe aɖeke awɔ dzogoedzikpee loo, alo atsɔ ɖe awɔ gɔmeɖokpee o. Ke boŋ ànye gbegbe tegbee.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Signal the nations to get ready to attack. Raise a flag and blow a trumpet. Send for the armies of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Choose a commander; let the cavalry attack like a swarm of locusts.
translation_verse: “Mitu aflaga ɖe anyigba la dzi! Miku kpẽ le dukɔwo dome! Midzra dukɔwo ɖo ɖe eŋu, ne woawɔ aʋa kplii. Miyɔ Ararat, Mini kple Askenaz fiaɖuƒewo vɛ ɖe eŋu. Miɖo aʋakplɔla ɖe eŋuti. Mikplɔ sɔwo vɛ fũu abe ʋetsuvi tofuwo ene.

english_verse: Tell the kings and governors, the leaders and the people of the kingdoms of the Medes to prepare for war!
translation_verse: Midzra dukɔwo ɖo ɖe eŋu ne woawɔ aʋa kplii. Miyɔ Media-fiawo kple woƒe anyigbanunɔlawo kpakple woƒe kpeɖeŋutɔwo hekpe ɖe anyigba ɖe sia ɖe si le woƒe dziɖuɖu te la vɛ.

english_verse: The earth twists and turns in torment, because I have decided to make Babylonia a desert where no one can live, and I won't change my mind.
translation_verse: Tete anyigba la dzo nyànyanya, eye wòle veve sem; elabe Aƒetɔ ƒe tame si wòɖo ɖe Babilon ŋu le te, be Babilon-nyigba nazu gbegbe, eye ame maganɔ edzi o.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers have lost their strength and courage. They stay in their fortresses, unable to fight, while the enemy breaks through the city gates, then sets their homes on fire.
translation_verse: Babilon ƒe aʋawɔlawo dzudzɔ aʋawɔwɔ, eye wonɔ anyi ɖe woƒe mɔwo me. Ŋusẽ vɔ le wo ŋu; wozu nyɔnugbɔmewo. Wotɔ dzo enɔƒewo, eye woŋe eƒe gametiwo.

english_verse: The enemy now controls the river crossings! The marshes are on fire! Your army has panicked!”
translation_verse: Woxɔ tɔtsoƒewo, eye wotɔ dzo teƒe siwo tsi xɔna; ŋɔdzi lé aʋawɔlawo.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I make this promise— “Soon Babylon will be leveled and packed down like a threshing place at harvest time.” Babylonia Will Pay!
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la be: Babilon vinyɔnu la le abe lugbɔƒe le ɣe si ɣi wole eme ƒom da ɖi ene. Esusɔ vie ko ne eƒe nuŋeɣi naɖo.”

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem say, “King Nebuchadnezzar made us panic. That monster stuffed himself with us and our treasures, leaving us empty— he gobbled up what he wanted and spit out the rest.
translation_verse: Mina Zion-nɔla nagblɔ be: “Nebukadnezar, Babilon-fia la vuvum; egbãm gudugudu. Ewɔm mezu goe ƒuƒlu; emim abe ʋɔ ene. Eɖu nye nu viviwo ɖi ƒo, eye wòtum ƒu gbe.

english_verse: The people of Babylonia harmed some of us and killed others. Now, Lord, make them pay!” The Lord Will Take Revenge on Babylon
translation_verse: Woneɖo ŋuta si wosẽ le nye kple nye ƒometɔwo ŋu la teƒe na Babilon.” Mina Yerusalem nagblɔ be: “Woneɖo nye ʋu si wokɔ ɖi la teƒe na Kaldeatɔwo.” Aƒetɔ akpe ɖe Israel-dukɔ ŋu

english_verse: My people, I am on your side, and I will take revenge on Babylon. I will cut off its water supply, and its stream will dry up.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, maxɔ miaƒe nya ɖe akɔ, eye mabia hlɔ̃ na mi. Mana eƒe atsiaƒu namie, eye eƒe tsidzɔƒe hã naƒu.

english_verse: Babylon will be a pile of rubble where only jackals live, and everyone will be afraid to walk among the ruins.
translation_verse: Babilon azu glikpo ɖi, anye akpatakuwo nɔƒe. Azu ŋɔdzinu si ŋu woaʋuʋu ta ɖo, eye ame maganɔ eme o.”

english_verse: And since they are hungry, I will give them a banquet. They will celebrate, get drunk, then fall asleep, never to wake up!
translation_verse: Ne nu tsu ɖuɖu le wo dzrom la, maɖo nuɖukplɔ̃ gã na wo, eye mana woamu aha anɔ dzidzɔ kpɔm. Eyome woadɔ alɔ̃ mavɔ; womaganyɔ akpɔ o. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: I will lead them away to die, like sheep, lambs, and goats being led to the butcher.
translation_verse: Makplɔ wo abe alẽviwo, agbowo kple gbɔ̃tsu ene ava lãwuƒee.” Nu si le dzɔdzɔ ge ɖe Babilon dzi

english_verse: All nations now praise Babylon, but when it is captured, those same nations will be horrified.
translation_verse: “Mikpɔ ale si woxɔ Sesax la ɖa! Mikpɔ ale si asi su du si xexea me katã kafuna la dzi ɖa! Babilon va zu ŋɔdzinu le dukɔwo dome!

english_verse: Babylon's enemies will rise like ocean waves and flood the city.
translation_verse: Atsiaƒu ƒo ɖe Babilon dzi, eye ƒutsotsoewo nyra, nyè tsyɔ edzi.

english_verse: Horrible destruction will strike the nearby towns. The land will become a barren desert, where no one can live or even travel.
translation_verse: Eƒe duwo zu ŋɔdzinu; eƒe anyigba zu kuɖiɖinyigba kple kegbegbe, anyigba si dzi ame aɖeke megale o, eye amegbetɔ vi aɖeke megatonɛ yina o.

english_verse: I will punish Marduk, the god of Babylon, and make him vomit out everything he gobbled up. Then nations will no longer bring him gifts, and Babylon's walls will crumble. The Lord Offers Hope to His People
translation_verse: Mahe to na Bel, le Babilon, eye maɖe nu si wòmi la tso eƒe nu me. Dukɔwo magaƒo zi ɖe eŋu azɔ o. Babilon ƒe gliwo mu.”

english_verse: Get out of Babylon, my people, and run for your lives, before I strike the city in my anger!
translation_verse: “Nye dukɔ, mido le eme. Mina ame sia ame naxɔ eɖokui ɖe agbe tso Aƒetɔ ƒe dziku helihelĩ la nu.

english_verse: Don't be afraid or lose hope, though year after year there are rumors of leaders fighting for control in the city of Babylon.
translation_verse: Wobewobe ɖina hekakana ɖe anyigba dzi ƒe sia ƒe be wole ŋutasẽnuwo wɔm, eye dziɖula tsona ɖe dziɖula ŋu. Ne miese wobewobe siawo le anyigbaa dzi la, dzi megaɖe le mia ƒo o, eye vɔvɔ̃ megaɖo mi o.

english_verse: The time will come when I will punish Babylon's false gods. Everyone there will die, and the whole nation will be disgraced,
translation_verse: “Eya ta, kpɔ ɖa, ɣeyiɣi gbɔna esime mahe to na Babilon ƒe legbawo. Ŋu akpe anyigba blibo la, eye eƒe ame siwo katã wowu atsi anyigba.

english_verse: when an army attacks from the north and brings destruction. Then the earth and the heavens and everything in them will celebrate.
translation_verse: Tete nu siwo katã le dziƒowo kple anyigba dzi atso aseye dzidzɔtɔe ɖe Babilon ŋu elabe nugblẽlawo atso dzigbeme ava ɖe wo ŋu, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Babylon must be overthrown, because it slaughtered the people of Israel and of many other nations.
translation_verse: Ele be woagbã Babilon le ame siwo wòwu le Israel ta. Babilon ye na ame geɖe tsi aʋa le anyigba bliboa dzi.” Mawu ƒe gbedeasi na Israelvi siwo le Babilonia

english_verse: My people, you escaped death when Jerusalem fell. Now you live far from home, but you should trust me and think about Jerusalem. Leave Babylon! Don't stay!
translation_verse: “Mi ame siwo tsi agbe tso aʋa me, midzo yi! Migatɔ ɖi o! Miɖo ŋku Aƒetɔ dzi le adzɔge, eye mina Yerusalem nanɔ miaƒe susu me:

english_verse: Soon I will send a war to punish Babylon's idols and leave its wounded people moaning everywhere.
translation_verse: “Eya ta, Aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, ɣeyiɣi gbɔna esime mahe to na woƒe legbawo, eye abixɔlawo anɔ ŋèŋem le anyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: Although Babylon's walls reach to the sky, the army I send will destroy that city. I, the Lord, have spoken. Babylon Will Be Destroyed The Lord said:
translation_verse: Togbɔ be Babilon alia yi dziŋgɔli me, eye wòana eƒe mɔ́ kɔkɔawo nagasẽ ɖe edzi hã la, nugblẽlawo atso gbɔnye aƒo ɖe edzi,” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Wogbã Babilon-dua ɖe edzi

english_verse: Listen to the cries for help coming from Babylon. Everywhere in the country the sounds of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: “Miɖo to! Ɣli aɖe ɖi le Babilon! Nane mu gbloo le Kaldeatɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi!

english_verse: The shouts of the enemy, like crashing ocean waves, will drown out Babylon's cries as I level the city.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ le Babilon tsrɔ̃m, eye wòle eƒe hoowɔwɔ vivivo nu tsim. Eƒe tsitsotsoewo le abe tɔ gãwo tɔ ene, eye woƒe gbeɖeɖe nu sẽ.

english_verse: An enemy will attack and destroy Babylon. Its soldiers will be captured and their weapons broken, because I am a God who takes revenge against nations for what they do.
translation_verse: Elabe nugblẽla ƒo ɖe edzi, eƒo ɖe Babilon dzi, eye wòlé eƒe aʋawɔlawo. Woŋe woƒe datiwo klíklikli, elabe Aƒetɔ la, Mawu nuteƒeɖola wònye. Ele eteƒe ɖo ge wòade go.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the true King, promise that the officials and advisors, the governors and leaders, and the soldiers of Babylon will get drunk, fall asleep, and never wake up.
translation_verse: Mana woƒe amegãwo kple nunyalawo namu aha. Woƒe anyigbanunɔlawo, aʋakplɔlawo kple aʋawɔlawo hã amui. Woadɔ alɔ̃ tegbee; womanyɔ o.” Fia si ŋkɔ nye Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe.

english_verse: The thick walls of that city will be torn down, and its huge gates burned. Everything that nation worked so hard to gain will go up in smoke. Jeremiah Gives Seraiah a Scroll
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: Woagbã Babilon-gli kekeawo woasɔ kple anyigba, eye woatɔ dzo eƒe agbo kɔkɔawo. Dukɔawo wɔ dɔ ɖe ya me, eye wodagba wo ɖokui wɔ dɔ dzo va fiã.” Woɖo Yeremya ƒe gbedeasi ɖe Babilonia

english_verse: During Zedekiah's fourth year as king of Judah, he went to Babylon. And Baruch's brother Seraiah went along as the officer in charge of arranging for places to stay overnight.
translation_verse: Esiae nye nya si gbeƒãɖela Yeremya tsɔ de se na Seraya, Neriya vi, Maxseya vi, esime eya kple Yuda-fia Zedekiya wozɔ mɔ yi Babilon, le Zedekiya ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè enelia me. Serayae nye dzeƒeŋuɖoɖowɔla la.

english_verse: Before they left, I wrote on a scroll all the terrible things that would happen to Babylon.
translation_verse: Yeremya ŋlɔ dzɔgbevɔ̃e siwo katã ava Babilon dzi la ɖe agbalẽ me kple nya siwo ku ɖe Babilon ŋu la ɖe eme.

english_verse: I gave the scroll to Seraiah and said: When you get to Babylon, read this scroll aloud,
translation_verse: Yeremya gblɔ na Seraya be: “Ne èɖo Babilon la, kpɔ egbɔ be nèxlẽ nya siawo katã.

english_verse: then pray, “Our Lord, you promised to destroy this place and make it into a desert where no people or animals will ever live.”
translation_verse: Azɔ gblɔ be: ‘Aƒetɔ, wò ŋutɔe gblɔ le teƒe sia ŋu be yeatsrɔ̃e, ne amegbetɔ alo lã aɖeke naganɔ anyi o, eye wòanye gbegbe tegbee.’

english_verse: When you finish praying, tie the scroll to a rock and throw it in the Euphrates River. Then say,
translation_verse: Ne èxlẽ agbalẽ sia vɔ la, bla kpe ɖe eŋu nàtsɔe ƒu gbe ɖe Frat-tɔsisi me,

english_verse: “This is how Babylon will sink when the Lord destroys it. Everyone in the city will die, and it won't have the strength to rise again.” The End of Jeremiah's Writing Jeremiah's writing ends here.
translation_verse: eye nàgblɔ be: ‘Babilon-du ayi to alea, eye magafɔ akpɔ o le dzɔgbevɔ̃e siwo he ge mala ava edzi la ta.’ ” Yeremya ƒe nyawo ƒe nuwuwue nye esi.

english_verse: Next, Nebuzaradan arrested Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah his assistant, and three temple officials.
translation_verse: Fia ŋu srafowo ƒe tatɔ kplɔ nunɔlagã Seraya kple Zefanya si le nunɔlagã la yome kpakple kpuinudzɔla etɔ̃.

english_verse: then his eyes were poked out. He was put in chains, then dragged off to Babylon and kept in prison until he died.
translation_verse: Azɔ egbã Zedekiya ƒe ŋkuwo, de kɔsɔkɔsɔe, eye wòkplɔe yi Babilon. Edee gaxɔ me va se ɖe eƒe kugbe. Wogbã gbedoxɔ la (Fia II,

english_verse: meters around. They were hollow, but the bronze was about
translation_verse: Woɖe to ɖe dua ʋuu va se ɖe esime Zedekiya ge ɖe eƒe ƒe wui ɖekɛlia me.

english_verse: After a year and a half, all the food in Jerusalem was gone. Then on the ninth day of the fourth month,
translation_verse: Le ɣleti enelia ƒe ŋkeke asiekea gbe la, dɔwuame nu sẽ le dua me ale gbegbe be nuɖuɖu aɖeke meli na ame siwo le anyigba la dzi la o.

english_verse: the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the Jordan River valley,
translation_verse: Tete woŋɔ mɔ ɖe duglia ŋu, togbɔ be Kaldeatɔwo le glia ŋu godoo hã la, aʋawɔlaawo katã te kpɔ sí le zã me. Woto fia ƒe abɔ me mɔ, to agbo si le gli eve dome, eye wosí ɖo ta Araba me.

english_verse: Zedekiah was taken to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty.
translation_verse: Tete wolé fia la, eye wokplɔe yi na Babilon-fia le Ribla le Xamat-nyigba dzi, eye wòbu fɔe.

english_verse: Zedekiah's sons and the officials of Judah were killed while he watched,
translation_verse: Tete Babilon-fia wu Zedekiya viŋutsuawo le eya ŋutɔ ŋkume, eye wòwu Yuda-megãwo katã hã le Ribla.

english_verse: Jerusalem was captured during Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king of Babylonia. About a month later, Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guards arrived in Jerusalem. His name was Nebuzaradan,
translation_verse: Le Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒè wui asiekelia me, le ɣleti atɔ̃lia ƒe ŋkeke ewoa gbe la, fia ŋu srafowo ƒe tatɔ Nebuzaradan, ame si subɔa Babilon-fia la ge ɖe Yerusalem-dua me.

english_verse: and he burned down the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and every important building in the city, as well as all the houses.
translation_verse: Etɔ dzo Aƒetɔ ƒe aƒe la, fiasã la, xɔ siwo katã le dua me; etɔ dzo xɔ vevi ɖe sia ɖe.

english_verse: Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Kaldeatɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ siwo katã le fia ŋu srafowo ƒe tatɔ ŋu la mu Yerusalem ŋu gliawo katã ƒu anyi.

english_verse: He led away the people left in the city, including everyone who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar, the rest of the skilled workers, and even some of the poor people of Judah.
translation_verse: Azɔ Nebuzaradan ɖe aboyo dukɔa ƒe ame dahewo dometɔ aɖewo, dukɔa ƒe ame mamlɛ siwo susɔ ɖe dua me, ame siwo sí yi ɖe Babilon-fia ƒe akpa dzi kple aɖaŋudɔwɔla mamlɛawo dzoe.

english_verse: Only the very poorest were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
translation_verse: Gake Nebuzaradan, fia ŋu srafowo ƒe tatɔ gblẽ ame dahe siwo da ahe wu la dometɔ aɖewo ɖi be woade waingble kple agble bubuwo.

english_verse: Evil Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
translation_verse: Evil-Merodax ƒo nu lɔlɔ̃tɔe kple Yehoyakin, eye wòna nɔƒee ɖe etɔ fia bubuwo ŋgɔ le Babilon.

english_verse: Jehoiachin was allowed to wear regular clothes instead of a prison uniform, and he even ate at the king's table every day.
translation_verse: Ale Yehoyakin ɖe eƒe gaxɔmewuwo ɖi, eye wòɖua nu le fiaa gbɔ le eƒe agbenɔɣi katã.

english_verse: As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Wonaa dzikpɔga aɖee edziedzi le eƒe hiahiã nu gbe sia gbe le eƒe agbenɔɣi katã va se ɖe eƒe kugbe.

english_verse: Jerusalem, once so crowded, lies deserted and lonely. This city that was known all over the world is now like a widow. This queen of the nations has been made a slave.
translation_verse: Ao, du si me gbetɔ yɔ fũu kpɔ, koŋ ye tsi akogo ale! Du triakɔ le dukɔwo domee va zu abe ahosi enea? Fiavinyɔnu le dukɔwo domee va zu kluvi fukpela!

english_verse: Each night, bitter tears flood her cheeks. None of her former lovers are there to offer comfort; her friends have betrayed her and are now her enemies.
translation_verse: Ele avi fam hehehe le zã me, aɖatsi ƒo alɔgo nɛ belee. Eƒe lɔlɔ̃tɔ aɖeke mekpɔtɔ afa akɔ nɛ o. Xɔlɔ̃awo katã trɔ ʋu le eyome zu eƒe futɔwo.

english_verse: The people of Judah are slaves, suffering in a foreign land, with no rest from sorrow. Their enemies captured them and were terribly cruel.
translation_verse: Yuda-dukɔ yi aboyo me kple fukpekpe, eye wotee ɖe anyi. Ðeko wòle dukɔwo dome mekpɔ gbɔdzɔe aɖeke o. Eyometilawo katã va mimii ɖo, toƒe aɖeke meli o.

english_verse: The roads to Zion mourn because no one travels there to celebrate the festivals. The city gates are deserted; priests are weeping. Young women are raped; Zion is in sorrow!
translation_verse: Zion-mɔwo le konyi fam, elabe ame aɖeke megavaa ŋkekenyui ɖuƒe o. Eƒe agbowo katã tsi ƒuƒlu, nunɔlawo le hũ ɖem, ɖetugbiwo le ŋeŋem, eye eya ŋutɔ le veve sem.

english_verse: Enemies now rule the city and live as they please. The Lord has punished Jerusalem because of her awful sins; he has let her people be dragged away.
translation_verse: Eƒe ketɔwo va zu eƒe aƒetɔ, eye eme nyo na eƒe futɔwo elabe Aƒetɔ na wòle fu kpem le eƒe vodada gbogboawo ta. Futɔwo kplɔ viawo ɖe ŋgɔ yi aboyo mee.

english_verse: Zion's glory has disappeared. Her leaders are like deer that cannot find pasture; they are hunted down till their strength is gone.
translation_verse: Zion vinyɔnu ƒe fianyenye katã bu. Eƒe amegãwo zu abe zi siwo mekpɔ gbeɖuƒe aɖeke o la ene. Ŋusẽ mele wo ŋu hafi wole sisím le wo yometilawo ŋgɔ o.

english_verse: Her people recall the good life that once was theirs; now they suffer and are scattered. No one was there to protect them from their enemies who sneered when their city was taken.
translation_verse: Le Yerusalem ƒe fukpeɣi kple veveseɣi la, eɖo ŋku nu xɔasi, siwo katã nɔ esi le blema la dzi. Esi eƒe amewo ge ɖe futɔwo si me, eye ame aɖeke meli axɔ nɛ o la, futɔawo kpɔ eƒe anyidzedze le kokom.

english_verse: Jerusalem's horrible sins have made the city a joke. Those who once admired her now hate her instead— she has been disgraced; she groans and turns away.
translation_verse: Nu vɔ̃e Yerusalem wɔ, eya ta wòzu ŋunyɔnu ɖo. Ame siwo katã bunɛ tsã la le vlo domee, elabe wokpɔ eƒe ama me. Eya ŋutɔ le hũ ɖem trɔ mo ɖe adzɔge.

english_verse: Her sins had made her filthy, but she wasn't worried about what could happen. And when Jerusalem fell, it was so tragic. No one gave her comfort when she cried out, “Help! I'm in trouble, Lord! The enemy has won.”
translation_verse: Eƒe ɖiƒoƒo le dzedzem le eƒe awu ŋu. Menya be ava nɔ na ye alea o. Edze anyi vevie; akɔfala aɖeke meli o. Yerusalem do ɣli be: “Ao, Aƒetɔ, kpɔm ɖa! Woɖi gbɔm; nye futɔwo ƒe alɔ de dzi!”

english_verse: Zion's treasures were stolen. Jerusalem saw foreigners enter her place of worship, though the Lord had forbidden them to belong to his people.
translation_verse: Futɔwo ha eƒe nu xɔasiwo katã. Ekpɔ dukɔ siwo Aƒetɔ meɖe mɔ na be woayi eƒe amehawo dome o la, woge ɖe eƒe kɔkɔeƒe ke gɔ̃ hã.

english_verse: Everyone in the city groans while searching for food; they trade their valuables for barely enough scraps to stay alive. Jerusalem Speaks: Jerusalem shouts to the Lord, “Please look and see how miserable I am!”
translation_verse: Eƒe amewo katã le hũ ɖem, le nuɖuɖu dim aɖu. Wotsɔ woƒe nu xɔasiwo ɖɔli nuɖuɖu, bene woatsi agbe. “Ao, Aƒetɔ, kpɔm ɖa, kpɔ nye gbɔɖiƒe ɖa!”

english_verse: No passerby even cares. Why doesn't someone notice my terrible sufferings? You were fiercely angry, Lord, and you punished me worst of all.
translation_verse: Mi ame siwo katã va le yiyim, milé ŋku ɖe ŋunye miakpɔ ɖa. Ðe ame aɖe se veve kpɔ, abe esi sem mele enea? Gbe si gbe Aƒetɔ do dziku manyagblɔ ɖe ŋunye, eye wòhe veve helihelĩ va dzinye la, mewɔ naneke mi oa?

english_verse: From heaven you sent a fire that burned in my bones; you set a trap for my feet and made me turn back. All day long you leave me in shock from constant pain.
translation_verse: Eɖo dzo ɖa tso dzi wòva ge ɖe nye ƒuto me ke. Eɖo ɖɔ na nye afɔ, ɖem, eye wòhem va emegbe. Egblẽm ɖi dzo. Ŋkeke blibo la katã, nyemegale ame me o.

english_verse: You have tied my sins around my neck, and they weigh so heavily that my strength is gone. You have put me in the power of enemies too strong for me.
translation_verse: Eƒo ƒu nye vodadawo katã, eye eya ŋutɔ bla wo sesĩe tsɔ ɖo kɔʋume nam abe kɔkuti ene. Wole kpeyem, wona ŋusẽ vɔ le ŋunye. Aƒetɔ la tsɔm de asi na ame siwo nu nyemate ŋu anɔ te ɖo o.

english_verse: You, Lord, have turned back my warriors and crushed my young heroes. Judah was a woman untouched, but you let her be trampled like grapes in a wine pit.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖe nye kalẽtɔwo katã ɖa le ŋunye. Eɖe gbeƒã ɖe ŋunye be yeatsrɔ̃ nye ɖekakpuiwo gbidii. Aƒetɔ la fanya Yuda, vinyɔnu ɖetugbi la, abe ale si wowɔa wain le wainfiãƒe ene.

english_verse: Because of this, I mourn, and tears flood my eyes. No one is here to comfort or to encourage me; we have lost the war— my people are suffering. The Prophet Speaks:
translation_verse: Esia ta mele avi fam; nye ŋkuwo le aɖatsi kplɔm yoyoyo. Akɔfala aɖeke meli ade dzi ƒo nam o. Futɔ la ƒe alɔ yi dzi; vinyewo tsrɔ̃.

english_verse: Zion reaches out her hands, but no one offers comfort. The Lord has turned the neighboring nations against Jacob's descendants. Jerusalem is merely a filthy rag to her neighbors. Jerusalem Speaks:
translation_verse: Zion ke abɔ me, ke akɔfala aɖeke meli nɛ o. Aƒetɔ ɖe gbe ɖe Yakob ŋu be eƒe aƒelikawo nava zu eƒe ketɔwo. Yerusalem va zu ŋunyɔnu le wo dome.

english_verse: The Lord was right, but I refused to obey him. Now I ask all of you to look at my sufferings— even my young people have been dragged away.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ tɔ dzɔ, elabe nyee dze aglã, gbe eƒe nya dzi wɔwɔ. Mi dukɔwo katã misee. Mikpɔm ɖa! Mele veve sem! Woɖe aboyo nye ɖetugbiwo kple ɖekakpuiwo.

english_verse: I called out to my lovers, but they betrayed me. My priests and my leaders died while searching the city for scraps of food.
translation_verse: Meyɔ nye lɔlɔ̃tɔwo, ke woblem. Nye nunɔlawo kple ame tsitsiwo tsrɔ̃ le dua me, esime wonɔ nu dim be yewoaɖu, akpɔ ŋusẽ.

english_verse: Won't you look and see how upset I am, our Lord? My stomach is in knots, and my heart is broken because I betrayed you. In the streets and at home, my people are slaughtered.
translation_verse: Ao, Aƒetɔ, kpɔm ɖa! Mele veve sem! Nye dɔme ʋu dzo hẽe, eye nye dzi le dzodzom nyànyanya; elabe mesẽ to. Le ablɔ me, yi le nu gblẽm; le aƒeme hã, ku le ame wum.

english_verse: Everyone heard my groaning, but no one offered comfort. My enemies know of the trouble that you have brought on me, and it makes them glad. Hurry and punish them, as you have promised.
translation_verse: Wose mele ŋeŋem, ke akɔfala meli o. Nye futɔwo katã se dzɔgbevɔ̃e si dzɔ ɖe dzinye, eye wole dzidzɔ kpɔm be wò, Aƒetɔ ye wɔm alea. Na ŋkeke si nèɖe gbeƒãe la nade, ne woawo hã woazu abe nye ene.

english_verse: Don't let their evil deeds escape your sight. Punish them as much as you have punished me because of my sins. I never stop groaning— I've lost all hope!
translation_verse: “Ðo ŋku woƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔwo katã dzi. He to na wo abe ale si nèhee nam le nye nuvɔ̃wo katã tae ene. Nye hũɖeɖewo sɔ gbɔ; nye dzi gbã.”

english_verse: The Lord was angry! So he disgraced Zion though it was Israel's pride and his own place of rest. In his anger he threw Zion down from heaven to earth.
translation_verse: Ale ke wɔ Aƒetɔ la do dziku na tsizi do ɖe Zion vinyɔnu la dzi ale? Etsɔ Israel ƒe atsyɔ̃ la xlã ɖe anyi tso dziƒo. Gbe si gbe wòdo dziku la, megaɖo ŋu eƒe afɔɖodzinu la o.

english_verse: The Lord had no mercy! He destroyed the homes of Jacob's descendants. In his anger he tore down every walled city in Judah; he toppled the nation together with its leaders, leaving them in shame.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ la gbã kɔƒe sia kɔƒe nublanuimakpɔmakpɔtɔe le Yakob. Ekaka Yuda ƒe mɔ́ sesẽwo le eƒe dɔmedzoe me. Ebɔbɔ fiaɖuƒe la kple edziɖulawo ɖe anyi ŋukpetɔe.

english_verse: The Lord was so furiously angry that he wiped out the whole army of Israel by not supporting them when the enemy attacked. He was like a raging fire that swallowed up the descendants of Jacob.
translation_verse: Etsɔ dziku helihelĩ, ɖe Israel ƒe ŋusẽ ɖa keŋkeŋ. Egbe xɔxɔ nɛ, esi futɔwo lũ ɖe edzi la. Etso ɖe Yakob ŋu abe dzo bibi ene, eye wòtsrɔ̃ nu sia nu si ƒo xlãe godoo la.

english_verse: He attacked like an enemy with a bow and arrows, killing our loved ones. He has burned to the ground the homes on Mount Zion.
translation_verse: Ebi eƒe dati abe futɔ ene. Ehe eme kple ɖusi abe ketɔ ene, eye wòwu ame siwo katã dzi míedàna ɖo le Zion vinyɔnu ƒe agbadɔ me. Etrɔ eƒe dɔmedzoe helihelĩ la, kɔ ɖi abe dzo ene.

english_verse: The Lord was like an enemy! He left Israel in ruins with its palaces and fortresses destroyed, and with everyone in Judah moaning and weeping.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ la va zu abe futɔ ene, eye wòtsrɔ̃ Israel. Egbã eƒe fiasãwo kple mɔ́ sesẽwo katã. Edzi vinyɔnu Yuda ƒe nuxaxa kple konyifafa ɖe edzi.

english_verse: He shattered his temple like a hut in a garden; he completely wiped out his meeting place, and did away with festivals and Sabbaths in the city of Zion. In his fierce anger he rejected our king and priests.
translation_verse: Ekaka eƒe subɔƒe la, eye wòvuvu kpɔ le eŋu. Egbã eƒe takpeƒe la. Aƒetɔ tsi ŋkekenyui kple dzudzɔgbe nu le Zion. Le eƒe dɔmedzoe helihelĩ me la, edo vlo fia kple nunɔla.

english_verse: The Lord abandoned his altar and his temple; he let Zion's enemies capture her fortresses. Noisy shouts were heard from the temple, as if it were a time of celebration.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ la gbe eƒe vɔsamlekpui, eye wògblẽ eƒe kɔkɔeƒe la ɖi. Etsɔ eƒe fiasãwo ƒe gliwo de asi na futɔwo. Woƒe ɣli ɖi le Aƒetɔ ƒeme, abe ŋkekenyui ɖum wole ene.

english_verse: The Lord had decided to tear down the walls of Zion stone by stone. So he started destroying and did not stop until walls and fortresses mourned and trembled.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖoe kplikpaa be yeana woamu Zion vinyɔnu la ƒe gliwo aƒu anyi. Eda nudzidzeka ɖe eŋu, dzidzee be yeana woagblẽe keŋkeŋ. Ena kpo si woƒu ɖe eŋu kple gli la siaa fa konyi.

english_verse: Zion's gates have fallen facedown on the ground; the bars that locked the gates are smashed to pieces. Her king and royal family are prisoners in foreign lands. Her priests don't teach, and her prophets don't have a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Eƒe agbowo yi to, eye woŋe gametiwo keŋ. Eƒe fia kple eƒe bubumewo le dzronyigbawo dzi. Se megali o, Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo hã megaxɔa ŋutega tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ o.

english_verse: Zion's leaders are silent. They just sit on the ground, tossing dirt on their heads and wearing sackcloth. Her young women can do nothing but stare at the ground.
translation_verse: Zion vinyɔnu ƒe dua ƒe amegãɖeɖiwo bɔbɔ nɔ anyi hezi ɖoɖoe kpoo. Wolɔ dzowɔ ƒo ɖe tame, eye wota akpanya. Yerusalem-ɖetugbiwo de mo to.

english_verse: My eyes are red from crying, my stomach is in knots, and I feel sick all over. My people are being wiped out, and children lie helpless in the streets of the city.
translation_verse: Nye ŋkuwo fa aɖatsi ʋuu ɖeɖi te. Nye dɔme ʋu dzo hẽe; nye veve wó ɖe dɔ me nam, elabe wotsrɔ̃ nye dukɔ vinyɔnu; ɖeviwo kple vidzĩwo ku ƒenyi le dua ƒe ablɔwo me.

english_verse: A child begs its mother for food and drink, then blacks out like a wounded soldier lying in the street. The child slowly dies in its mother's arms.
translation_verse: Wodo ɣli bia wo nɔwo be: “Abolo ɖe? Wain ɖe?” Woyi ɖi me abe ame xɔabiwo ene le dua ƒe ablɔwo me, eye woƒe gbɔgbɔ nu tsí le wo nɔwo ƒe akɔnu.

english_verse: Zion, how can I comfort you? How great is your pain? Lovely city of Jerusalem, how can I heal your wounds, gaping as wide as the sea?
translation_verse: Ao, Yerusalem-nyɔnuvi, nu ka magblɔ aɖe nuwòe? Nu ka ŋu matsɔ wò asɔ ɖo? Zion vinyɔnu, ɖetugbi leaƒe ame kae matsɔ asɔ kpli wò, wò akɔ nafa? Wò abi la lolo abe atsiaƒu ene. Ame kae ate ŋu ada gbe le ŋuwò?

english_verse: Your prophets deceived you with false visions and lying messages— they should have warned you to leave your sins and be saved from disaster.
translation_verse: Wò gbeƒãɖelawo kpɔ alakpaŋutega gblɔ na wò heble wò. Womeklo nu le wò vodadawo dzi, bene woaɖɔ wò ɖo, ne eme nanyo na wò o. Ke wokpɔ alakpa kple ameflunya ɖe gbeƒãe na wò.

english_verse: Those who pass by shake their heads and sneer as they make fun and shout, “What a lovely city you were, the happiest on earth, but look at you now!”
translation_verse: Ame siwo katã va tso eme yina la, ɖu fewu le ŋuwò. Woɖe tsiã, ʋuʋu ta ɖe Yerusalem-nyɔnuvia ŋu be: “Du si wokafuna be enyakpɔna, etɔgbe meli o, xexe blibo la ƒe dzidzɔ lae nye esia?”

english_verse: Zion, your enemies curse you and snarl like wild animals, while shouting, “This is the day we've waited for! At last, we've got you!”
translation_verse: Wò futɔwo katã ke nu le alɔ me ɖem le ŋuwò. Woʋuʋu ta, ɖu fewu le ŋuwò be: “Asi su edzi! Míetsrɔ̃e loo! Ehɛ̃, ŋkeke si míele mɔ kpɔm na lae nye egbe. Míekpɔe kple ŋku!”

english_verse: The Lord has done everything that he had planned and threatened long ago. He destroyed you without mercy and let your enemies boast about their powerful forces.
translation_verse: Nu si Aƒetɔ ɖo tso blema ke be yele wɔwɔ ge la, eyae wòwɔ. Egblẽ nu nublanuimakpɔmakpɔtɔe, eye wòna wò futɔwo dzɔ dzi. Ena ŋusẽ wò ketɔwo.

english_verse: Zion, deep in your heart you cried out to the Lord. Now let your tears overflow your walls day and night. Don't ever lose hope or let your tears stop.
translation_verse: Zion vinyɔnu, do ɣli sesĩe na Aƒetɔ la! Na wò aɖatsi nasí abe tɔsisi ene zã kple keli. Mègagbɔ ɖe eme o. Na wò ŋkuvi nanɔ aɖatsi fam madzudzɔmadzudzɔe.

english_verse: Get up and pray for help all through the night. Pour out your feelings to the Lord, as you would pour water out of a jug. Beg him to save your people, who are starving to death at every street crossing. Jerusalem Speaks:
translation_verse: Tso, nàdo ɣli le zã me. Trɔ wò dzi ƒo ɖe Aƒetɔ la ŋkume abe tsi ene le zãdzɔɣi ƒe gɔmedzedze. Wu asi dzi nàɖe kuku nɛ le viwò siwo dɔ wu ʋuu nu té wo ŋu le ablɔwo ƒe godoƒe la ta.

english_verse: Think about it, Lord! Have you ever been this cruel to anyone before? Is it right for mothers to eat their children, or for priests and prophets to be killed in your temple?
translation_verse: Ao, Aƒetɔ, kpɔ ame siwo nèle funyafunya wɔmee la ɖa! Ðe nyɔnuwo alé woawo ŋutɔ ƒe dɔmeviwo aɖua? Ðe woawu nunɔla kple gbeƒãɖela le Aƒetɔ la ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la gɔ̃ hã?

english_verse: My people, both young and old, lie dead in the streets. Because you were angry, my young men and women were brutally slaughtered.
translation_verse: Ðeviwo kple ame tsitsiwo siaa ku, tsi anyigba le ablɔ me. Nye ɖetugbiwo kple ɖekakpuiwo tsi futɔwo ƒe yi nu. Le wò dzikudogbe la, èwu wo nublanuimakpɔmakpɔtɔe.

english_verse: When you were angry, Lord, you invited my enemies like guests for a party. No one survived that day; enemies killed my children, my own little ones.
translation_verse: Èna nye futɔwo tso afi sia afi va kpe ta ɖe ŋunye, abe ŋkekenyui ɖu ge wova ene. Ame aɖeke mesí alo tsi agbe le Yerusalem le Aƒetɔ ƒe dzikudogbe o. Vi siwo medzi, kpɔ wo dzi, wotsi la, nye futɔ tsrɔ̃ wo keŋ.

english_verse: I have suffered much because God was angry.
translation_verse: Nyee nye ame si kpe fu, eye Mawu tsɔ ameƒoti ɖe ŋunye dɔmedzoetɔe.

english_verse: He chased me into a dark place, where no light could enter.
translation_verse: Enyàm kple du tege ɖe viviti me, kekeli aɖeke meli o.

english_verse: I am the only one he punishes over and over again, without ever stopping.
translation_verse: Ẽ, nye ko ŋue wòtrɔ ɖo, le ƒoƒom atraɖii ŋkeke blibo la.

english_verse: God caused my skin and flesh to waste away, and he crushed my bones.
translation_verse: Edze nye lã kple ŋutigbalẽ le ŋunye, eye wògbã nye ƒuwo.

english_verse: He attacked and surrounded me with hardships and trouble;
translation_verse: Etsɔ vevesese kple fukpekpe ɖo gli ƒo xlãm.

english_verse: he forced me to sit in the dark like someone long dead.
translation_verse: Ena menɔ viviti tsiɖitsiɖi me abe ame siwo ku gbe aɖe gbe ke ene.

english_verse: God built a fence around me that I cannot climb over, and he chained me down.
translation_verse: Eɖo gli ƒo xlãm va kpe ɖo, eye wòde kɔsɔkɔsɔ sesẽwom ale be nyemate ŋu así o.

english_verse: Even when I shouted and prayed for help, he refused to listen.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be mele ɣli dom be woaxɔ nam hã la, edo toku nye gbedodoɖa.

english_verse: God put big rocks in my way and made me follow a crooked path.
translation_verse: Etsɔ kpe gligowo xe mɔ me nam, eye wòglɔ̃ nye toƒewo katã.

english_verse: God was like a bear or a lion waiting in ambush for me;
translation_verse: Etsyɔ akɔ anyi le lalayem abe sisiblisi ene, eye wòde xa ɖi nam abe dzata ene.

english_verse: he dragged me from the road, then tore me to shreds.
translation_verse: Ehem dzoe le nye mɔ dzi, eye wòvuvum yaʋayaʋa. Egblẽ nye ɖeka ɖi dzo.

english_verse: God took careful aim and shot his arrows
translation_verse: Ehe eƒe da me, eye wòdzidze eƒe aŋutrɔ ɖe dzinye tututu.

english_verse: I am a joke to everyone— no one ever stops making fun of me.
translation_verse: Mezu nu ɖikokoe na nye dukɔ azɔ. Wodo ham le dzidzim ŋkeke blibo la.

english_verse: He made me eat gravel and rubbed me in the dirt.
translation_verse: Ena meɖu kpeku, eye wòtigim ɖe dzowɔ me.

english_verse: I cannot find peace or remember happiness.
translation_verse: Wona ŋutifafa bu ɖem, eye meŋlɔ dzidzeme be.

english_verse: I tell myself, “I am finished! I can't count on the Lord to do anything for me.”
translation_verse: Ale mebe: “Bubu vɔ le ŋunye. Nu siwo katã mekpɔ mɔ na tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ la nu tso.”

english_verse: Just thinking of my troubles and my lonely wandering makes me miserable.
translation_verse: Ɖo ŋku nye fukpekpe kple vevesese dzi, tsà kple aɖi ko wonye nam.

english_verse: That's all I ever think about, and I am depressed.
translation_verse: Mebua eŋu edziedzi, eye wòtea nye gbɔgbɔ ɖe to.

english_verse: Then I remember something that fills me with hope.
translation_verse: Ke mɔkpɔkpɔ gaɖoa menye ne meɖo ŋku edzi be:

english_verse: The Lord's kindness never fails! If he had not been merciful, we would have been destroyed.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe amenuveve tae míetsrɔ̃ o, eye eƒe nublanuikpɔkpɔ nu metsina o.

english_verse: The Lord can always be trusted to show mercy each morning.
translation_verse: Wozua yeye ŋdi sia ŋdi. Wò nuteƒewɔwɔ tri akɔ.

english_verse: Deep in my heart I say, “The Lord is all I need; I can depend on him!”
translation_verse: Nye luʋɔ be: “Nye gomee nye Aƒetɔ eya ta eya ko makpɔ mɔ na.”

english_verse: The Lord is kind to everyone who trusts and obeys him.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ nyoa dɔme na ame siwo ɖoa dzi ɖe eŋu kple ame siwo dinɛ.

english_verse: It is good to wait patiently for the Lord to save us.
translation_verse: Enyo be ame nagbɔ dzi ɖi kpoo akpɔ mɔ na Aƒetɔ ƒe xɔname.

english_verse: When we are young, it is good to struggle hard
translation_verse: Enyo be ame natsɔ kɔkuti le eƒe ɖevime.

english_verse: and to sit silently alone, if this is what the Lord intends.
translation_verse: Ne Aƒetɔ la ɖoe edzi la, nenɔ anyi ɖe aga, ne wòatsɔe le ɖoɖoezizi me.

english_verse: Being rubbed in the dirt can teach us a lesson;
translation_verse: Nebɔbɔ eɖokui keŋ; ɖewohĩ mɔkpɔkpɔ gali.

english_verse: we can also learn from insults and hard knocks.
translation_verse: Neɖe mɔ woaƒo to me nɛ, eye woado ŋukpee faa.

english_verse: The Lord won't always reject us!
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ la magbe ame ɖikaa o.

english_verse: He causes a lot of suffering, but he also has pity because of his great love.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be edoa nuxaxa na ame hã la, agakpɔ nublanui nɛ le eƒe amenuveve sɔgbɔ la nu,

english_verse: The Lord doesn't enjoy sending grief or pain.
translation_verse: elabe menye dzidzɔ nɛ be yeawɔ fu ame, alo ado nuxaxa nɛ o.

english_verse: Don't trample prisoners under your feet
translation_verse: Ne wofanya anyigba dzi gamenɔlawo katã,

english_verse: or cheat anyone out of what is rightfully theirs. God Most High sees everything,
translation_verse: ne wote ame ƒe nya dzɔdzɔe ɖe to, le Dziƒoʋĩtɔ la ŋkume,

english_verse: and he knows when you refuse to give someone a fair trial.
translation_verse: ne wotrɔ gbo nya dzɔdzɔe le ʋɔnu la, Aƒetɔ la medaa asi ɖe edzi o.

english_verse: No one can do anything without the Lord's approval.
translation_verse: Ame kae gblɔa nya wòvaa me, ne Aƒetɔ la meɖoe nenema o?

english_verse: Good and bad each happen at the command of God Most High.
translation_verse: Ðe menye Dziƒoʋĩtɔ lae ɖea gbe, eye vɔ̃ kple nyui dzɔna oa?

english_verse: We're still alive! We shouldn't complain when we are being punished for our sins.
translation_verse: Nu ka tae ame gbagbe afa konyi, gbetɔ, ne wohe to nɛ ɖe eƒe nuvɔ̃ ta?

english_verse: Instead, we should think about the way we are living, and turn back to the Lord.
translation_verse: Mina míado míaƒe nuwɔna kpɔ, adzro eme, eye míatrɔ va Aƒetɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: When we lift our hands in prayer to God in heaven, we should offer him our hearts and say,
translation_verse: Mina míakɔ dzi kple asiwo ɖe dzi na Mawu le dziƒo:

english_verse: “We've sinned! We've rebelled against you, and you haven't forgiven us!
translation_verse: “Míawo míewɔ nuvɔ̃, dze aglã, eye mètsɔe ke mí o.

english_verse: Anger is written all over you, as you pursue and slaughter us without showing pity.
translation_verse: Èɣla ɖokuiwò ɖe wò dziku me; èti mía yome va wu nublanuimakpɔmakpɔtɔe.

english_verse: You are behind a wall of clouds that blocks out our prayers.
translation_verse: Èɣla ɖokuiwò ɖe alilikpo me ale be gbedodoɖa aɖeke mate ŋu aɖo gbɔwò o.

english_verse: You allowed nations to treat us like garbage;
translation_verse: Ètsɔ mí wɔ gbeɖuɖɔ kple ŋunyɔnui le dukɔwo dome.

english_verse: our enemies curse us.
translation_verse: “Míaƒe futɔwo katã ke nu le mía dzum.

english_verse: We are terrified and trapped, caught and crushed.”
translation_verse: Ŋɔdzi zu ʋe míege dze eme. Dzɔgbevɔ̃e kple gbegblẽ ɖe to ɖe mí.

english_verse: My people are destroyed! Tears flood my eyes,
translation_verse: Aɖatsi zu tɔʋu le dodom le nye ŋkume yoyoyo elabe wotsrɔ̃ nye dukɔ vinyɔnu.

english_verse: and they won't stop
translation_verse: “Aɖatsi matso le ŋkume nam kpɔ,

english_verse: until the Lord looks down from heaven and helps.
translation_verse: va se ɖe esime Aƒetɔ naɖo ŋku anyi akpɔm tso dziƒo o.

english_verse: I am horrified when I see what enemies have done to the young women of our city.
translation_verse: Ne mekpɔ nu si dzɔ ɖe nye du me ɖetugbiwo katã dzi la, mesea veve le ememe ke.

english_verse: No one had reason to hate me, but I was hunted down like a bird.
translation_verse: “Nyemewɔ naneke nye futɔwo o, gake woyɔm ɖe nu abe xevi ene.

english_verse: Then they tried to kill me by tossing me into a pit and throwing stones at me.
translation_verse: Wotsɔm ƒu gbe ɖe do me agbagbee, eye wofɔ kpe kɔ ɖe dzinye.

english_verse: Water covered my head— I thought I was gone.
translation_verse: Tsi fie to tanye eye mebe: “Evɔ nam!”

english_verse: From the bottom of the pit, I prayed to you, Lord.
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, do la gɔme ke mele le yɔwòm.

english_verse: I begged you to listen. “Help!” I shouted. “Save me!” You answered my prayer
translation_verse: Èse nye kokoƒoƒo. Mègado tokum o; se nye xɔnameɣli, nàxɔ nam.”

english_verse: and came when I was in need. You told me, “Don't worry!”
translation_verse: Ète va gbɔnye esime meyɔ wò. Ègblɔ nam be: ‘Mègavɔ̃ o!’

english_verse: You rescued me and saved my life.
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, èxɔ nye nya ɖe akɔ, eye nèɖe nye agbe.

english_verse: You saw them abuse me, Lord, so make things right.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, èkpɔ vɔ̃ si wowɔ ɖe ŋunye; tso nya me nam.

english_verse: You know every plot they have made against me.
translation_verse: Èdze si woƒe hlɔ̃biabiawo katã kple woƒe nugbeɖoɖo ɖe ŋunyewo katã.

english_verse: Yes, you know their insults and their evil plans.
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, èse woƒe alɔmeɖeɖe kple nugbe si woɖo ɖe ŋunye la.

english_verse: All day long they attack with words and whispers.
translation_verse: Ame siwo dze dzinye ƒe nuyiwo kple susuwo le ŋunye ŋkeke blibo la.

english_verse: No matter what they are doing, they keep on mocking me.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, anyie wonɔ o, tsitre wole o, wokpa hawo dem le dzidzim.

english_verse: Pay them back for everything they have done, Lord!
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, ɖo woƒe nuwɔna teƒe na wo.

english_verse: Put your curse on them and make them suffer.
translation_verse: Na dzi kuatri wo. Wò fiƒode neva wo dzi.

english_verse: Get angry and go after them until not a trace is left under the heavens.
translation_verse: Ti wo yome kple dziku, eye nàtsrɔ̃ wo ɖa le wò, Aƒetɔ ƒe dziƒoa te.

english_verse: The purest gold is ruined and has lost its shine; jewels from the temple lie scattered in the streets.
translation_verse: Ale wɔ sika nyɔ vìi ale? Ale wɔ sika nyuitɔ trɔ ale? Ale ke wɔ kpe kɔkɔeawo kaka ɖe ablɔ ɖe sia ɖe ƒe dzogoewo dzi?

english_verse: These are Zion's people, worth more than purest gold; yet they are counted worthless like dishes of clay.
translation_verse: Zion viŋutsu xɔasi siwo nye sika nyuitɔ la, ale wɔ wobu wo abe anyizewo ene, zemela ƒe asinudɔwɔwɔwo?

english_verse: Even jackals nurse their young, but my people are like ostriches that abandon their own.
translation_verse: Akpataku kekeake hã naa no viawo, gake nye dukɔ vinyɔnu ya le ŋlɔmee wɔm le viawo ŋu, abe tsatsaboli le gbedadaƒo ene.

english_verse: Babies are so thirsty that their tongues are stuck to the roof of the mouth. Children go begging for food, but no one gives them any.
translation_verse: Tsikɔ wu vi nonowo ʋuu woƒe aɖe lé ɖe aŋɔ ŋu na wo. Ðeviwo bia nuɖuɖu, ke ame aɖeke mena na wo o.

english_verse: All who ate expensive foods lie starving in the streets; those who grew up in luxury now sit on trash heaps.
translation_verse: Ame siwo ɖua nu viviwo tsã la, tsrɔ̃ le ablɔwo me. Ame siwo wonyi le avɔ xɔasiwo me la, tsi aɖukpo dzi.

english_verse: My nation was punished worse than the people of Sodom, whose city was destroyed in a flash without the help of human hands.
translation_verse: To si wohe na nye dukɔ vinyɔnu la sẽ wu esi wohe na Sodom-du si wotsrɔ̃ le aɖabaƒoƒo ɖeka me, asi aɖeke maka eŋui.

english_verse: The leaders of Jerusalem were purer than snow and whiter than milk; their bodies were healthy and glowed like jewels.
translation_verse: Woƒe amegãwo kɔ wu tsikpe, eye wofu wu notsi. Wobiã wu soe, eye woƒe dzedzeme le abe safirkpe ene.

english_verse: Now they are blacker than tar, and no one recognizes them; their skin clings to their bones and is drier than firewood.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la, woƒe mo nyɔ wu dzɔble, eye womegakpɔ wo dze sii le ablɔ me o. Woƒe ŋutigbalẽ lé ɖe ƒu ŋu kpaɖii, eye woƒu abe nake ene.

english_verse: Life in the city is so bad that loving mothers have boiled and eaten their own children.
translation_verse: Nyɔnu siwo ame nu wɔa nublanui na la gɔ̃ hã lé woawo ŋutɔ viwo ɖa ɖu. Amelã va zu nuɖuɖu na gbetɔ le nye dukɔ vinyɔnu la gbãɣi.

english_verse: The Lord was so fiercely angry that he burned the city of Zion to the ground.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe dzi fla, eye wòtrɔ eƒe dziku kɔ ɖe Zion dzi. Etɔ dzoe, wòfiã eƒe gɔmeɖokpewo gɔ̃.

english_verse: Not a king on this earth or the people of any nation believed enemies could break through her gates.
translation_verse: Anyigba dzi fiawo kple xexemetɔ aɖeke mexɔe se kpɔ be futɔ alo ketɔ aɖe ate ŋu age ɖe Yerusalem ƒe agbowo me hafi o.

english_verse: Jerusalem was punished because her prophets and her priests had sinned and caused the death of innocent victims.
translation_verse: Nya siawo dzɔ le woƒe gbeƒãɖelawo ƒe nuvɔ̃ kple woƒe nunɔlawo ƒe hlɔ̃dodo ta; elabe wokɔ ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe ʋu ɖi le dua me.

english_verse: Yes, her prophets and priests were covered with blood; no one would come near them, as they wandered from street to street.
translation_verse: Wonɔ tsa glãla tsam abe ŋkunɔwo ene le ablɔwo me. Woƒo ʋu ale gbegbe be ame aɖeke mate ŋu aka asi woƒe awu ŋu o.

english_verse: Instead, everyone shouted, “Go away! Don't touch us! You're filthy and unfit to belong to God's people!” So they had to leave and become refugees. But foreign nations told them, “You can't stay here!”
translation_verse: Amewo le ɣli dom ɖe wo ta be: “Midzo! Ame makɔmakɔwo! Midzo! Midzo! Migaka asi mía ŋu o!” Ale wozu sisílawo kple tsa glãla tsalawo. Dukɔwo gblɔ be: “Ame siawo maganɔ mía dome o.”

english_verse: The Lord is the one who sent them scattering, and he has forgotten them. No respect or kindness will be shown to the priests or leaders.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ŋutɔe ka wo hlẽ; megatsɔ ɖeke le eme na wo o. Mede bubu nunɔlawo ŋu o, eye meve amegãɖeɖiwo nu o.

english_verse: Our eyes became weary, hopelessly looking for help from a nation that could not save us.
translation_verse: Míekpɔ mɔ ʋuu be woava xɔ na mí, wòglo! Míeɖo ŋu ɖe dukɔ si mate ŋu axɔ na ame o la ŋu.

english_verse: Enemies hunted us down on every public street. Our time was up; our doom was near.
translation_verse: Futɔwo le mía yome le afɔ xlẽm na mí, ale be mɔwo dzi toto zu dɔ. Míaƒe nuwuwu gogo, ŋkeke boo megale mía si o; míaƒe nuwuwu ɖo.

english_verse: They swooped down faster than eagles from the sky. They hunted for us in the hills and set traps to catch us out in the desert.
translation_verse: Mía yometilawo le du dzi sesĩe wu hɔ̃ le ya me. Woyɔ mí ɖe nu le towo dzi, eye wode xa na mí le gbedadaƒo.

english_verse: The Lord's chosen leader was our hope for survival! We thought he would keep us safe somewhere among the nations, but even he was caught in one of their traps.
translation_verse: Míaƒe amesiamina ame si na míegbɔna la ge ɖe woƒe mɔ̀ me! Evɔ la, eyama ŋue míegblɔ le be: “Míanɔ agbe le eƒe vɔvɔli te le dukɔwo me!” hafi.

english_verse: You people of Edom can celebrate now! But your time will come to suffer and stagger around naked.
translation_verse: Wò Edom vinyɔnu le Uz-nyigba dzi, tso aseye, nàkpɔ dzidzɔ. Ke kplu la gbɔna na wò hã. Èle eno ge amu, aɖe ama ɖokuiwò.

english_verse: The people of Zion have paid for their sins, and the Lord will soon let them return home. But, people of Edom, you will be punished, and your sins exposed.
translation_verse: O Zion vinyɔnu, wohe to na wò le wò vodadawo ta vɔ. Aƒetɔ magana nanɔ aboyo me o. Ke wò Edom ya la, ahe to na wò le wò vodada ta, eye wòaklo nu le wò nuvɔ̃wo dzi.

english_verse: Our Lord, don't forget how we have suffered and been disgraced.
translation_verse: Ao! Aƒetɔ, ɖo ŋku nu si dzɔ ɖe mía dzi la dzi. Trɔ kɔ, nàkpɔ míaƒe ŋukpe ɖa!

english_verse: Foreigners and strangers have taken our land and our homes.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ míaƒe domenyinu na amedzrowo, míaƒe aƒewo zu ame manyamanyawo tɔ.

english_verse: We are like children whose mothers are widows.
translation_verse: Míezu tsyɔ̃eviwo; tɔ́ mele mía si o, mía nɔwo le abe ahosiwo ene.

english_verse: The water we drink and the wood we burn cost far too much.
translation_verse: Ele be míadze tsi hafi ano, aƒle nake hafi ado dzo.

english_verse: We are terribly mistreated; we are worn out and can find no rest.
translation_verse: Kɔkuti le kɔ na mí, woyɔ mí ɖe nu kplìkplikpli, ɖeɖi te mía ŋu; ke womeɖe mɔ na mí be míagbɔ ɖe eme o.

english_verse: We had to surrender to Egypt and Assyria because we were hungry.
translation_verse: Míena ta Egipte kple Asiria, bene míakpɔ nu aɖu aɖi ƒo.

english_verse: Our ancestors sinned, but they are dead, and we are left to pay for their sins.
translation_verse: Mía tɔgbuiwo wɔ nuvɔ̃; womegali o. Míawo míele fu kpem le woƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔwo ta.

english_verse: Slaves are now our rulers, and there is no one to set us free.
translation_verse: Kluviwo le mía dzi ɖum, ke ame aɖeke meli aɖe mí le wo si me o.

english_verse: We are in danger from brutal desert tribes; we must risk our lives just to bring in our crops.
translation_verse: Yi le asi le gbedadaƒo; ale be ɖe míetsɔa míaƒe agbe kena hafi dia nuɖuɖu vaa aƒee.

english_verse: Our skin is scorched from fever and hunger.
translation_verse: Dɔwuame sesẽ na míaƒe ŋutigbalẽ ʋu dzo abe kpodzo me ene.

english_verse: On Zion and everywhere in Judah our wives and daughters are being raped.
translation_verse: Wode asi nyɔnuwo ŋu sesẽtɔe le Zion, eye wogblẽ ɖetugbiwo le Yuda-duwo me.

english_verse: Our rulers are strung up by their arms, and our nation's advisors are treated shamefully.
translation_verse: Wode ka dukplɔlawo ƒe abɔ tsi ɖe ya me, eye womede bubu aɖeke amegãɖeɖiwo ŋu o.

english_verse: Young men are forced to do the work of slaves; boys must carry heavy loads of wood.
translation_verse: Wozi ɖekakpuiwo dzi wole nu tum le té dzi, eye ŋutsuviwo le ƒoƒom le nakegba te.

english_verse: Our leaders are not allowed to decide cases in court, and young people no longer play music.
translation_verse: Ame tsitsiwo dzo le dutakpeƒe, eye ɖekakpuiwo dzudzɔ hadzidzi.

english_verse: Our hearts are sad; instead of dancing, we mourn.
translation_verse: Míaƒe dzidzɔkpɔkpɔ nu tso; konyifafa xɔ ɣeɖuɖu teƒe.

english_verse: Zion's glory has disappeared! And we are doomed because of our sins.
translation_verse: Fiakuku la ge le mía ta! Nu wɔ mí loo! Elabe míewɔ nuvɔ̃.

english_verse: We feel sick all over and can't even see straight;
translation_verse: Míaƒe dzi dze dɔ le esia ta, míaƒe ŋkuwo dzi wɔ flukpee le nu siawo ta,

english_verse: our city is in ruins, overrun by wild dogs.
translation_verse: elabe Zion-to zu gbegbe, afi si akpatakuwo le tsatsam le.

english_verse: You will rule forever, Lord! You are King for all time.
translation_verse: Ke wò Aƒetɔ la, èle fia ɖum tegbee, eye wò fiazikpui li tso dzidzime yi dzidzime.

english_verse: Why have you forgotten us for so long?
translation_verse: Nu ka ta nèŋlɔ mí be ɖikaa? Nu ka ta nègblẽ mí ɖi eteƒe didi ale?

english_verse: Bring us back to you! Give us a fresh start.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, gbugbɔ mía gɔme ɖo anyi ɖe gbɔwò, ne míanɔ te. Gbugbɔ egbeŋkekewo wɔ yeyee na mí abe tsãtɔwo ene.

english_verse: Or do you despise us so much that you don't want us?
translation_verse: Alo ɖe nègbe mí keŋkeŋua? Ðe nèdo dziku ɖe mía ŋu ale gbegbea?

english_verse: I saw a windstorm blowing in from the north. Lightning flashed from a huge cloud and lit up the whole sky with a dazzling brightness. The fiery center of the cloud was as shiny as polished metal,
translation_verse: Esi meda ŋku ɖi la, kpɔ ɖa, ahom tu tso dzigbeme, alilikpo gã aɖe klẽ ƒo xlãe, eye dzo nɔ bibim le eme flaflafla. Nane nɔ dzedzem le dzo la titina abe akɔbli si le dzo sim la ene.

english_verse: and in that center I saw what looked like four living creatures. They were somewhat like humans,
translation_verse: Nu ene siwo ɖi nu gbagbewo la, do tso eme. Woƒe dzedzeme nɔ ale: Woɖi amegbetɔ,

english_verse: except that each one had four faces and four wings.
translation_verse: ke mo ene kple aʋala ene le wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe si.

english_verse: Their legs were straight, but their feet looked like the hoofs of calves and sparkled like bronze.
translation_verse: Woƒe atawo dzɔ abe ati ene, eye woƒe afɔƒome le abe nyivi tɔ ene, eye wonɔ dzo dam abe akɔbligba ene.

english_verse: Each creature had the face of a human in front, the face of a lion on the right side, the face of a bull on the left, and the face of an eagle in back.
translation_verse: Woƒe mo ɖi amegbetɔ tɔ le ŋgɔ; wo ame eneawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe to dzata ƒe mo le nuɖusi kpa dzi, eye wo ame ene la to nyitsu ƒe mo le mia kpa dzi. Wo ame ene la katã to hɔ̃ ƒe mo ɖe megbe.

english_verse: Two wings of each creature were spread out and touched the wings of the creatures on either side. The other two wings of each creature were folded against its body.
translation_verse: Nenema woƒe mowo nɔ. Woklẽ woƒe aʋalawo me ɖo ɖe dzi. Ɖe sia ɖe ƒe aʋala eve ka nɔvia tɔ ŋu, eye wotsɔ eve tsyɔ wo ɖokui.

english_verse: The four living creatures went wherever the Spirit led them, and they moved together without turning their bodies, because each creature faced straight ahead.
translation_verse: Ɖe sia ɖe yia ŋgɔ tẽe; afi si gbɔgbɔ la yina la, afi mae woɖoa tae. Ne wole azɔli dzi la, wometrɔna o.

english_verse: The creatures were glowing like hot coals, and I saw something like a flaming torch moving back and forth among them. Lightning flashed from the torch every time its flame blazed up.
translation_verse: Nane le nu gbagbeawo dome abe dzoka ene. Wole bibim abe akakati si wole nyenyem la ene le wo dome. Dzoa nɔ keklẽm, eye dzi nɔ dzo kem tso dzoa me.

english_verse: The creatures themselves moved as quickly as sparks jumping from a fire.
translation_verse: Nu gbagbeawo nɔ keklẽm miamiamia abe dzikedzo ene.

english_verse: I then noticed that on the ground beside each of the four living creatures was a wheel,
translation_verse: Azɔ esi melé ŋku ɖe nu gbagbeawo ŋu la, mekpɔ tasiaɖamfɔ nɔ anyigba le nu gbagbe eneawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe gbɔ.

english_verse: shining like chrysolite. Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it,
translation_verse: Ku ɖe tasiaɖamfɔawo ƒe dzedzeme kple wɔwɔme ŋu la: Wodze abe adzagba si le keklẽm la ene. Wo ame ene la ɖi wo nɔewo; wowɔ wo abe ɖe tasiaɖamfɔ ɖeka le nɔvia me ene.

english_verse: so that they could move in any direction without turning.
translation_verse: Ne wole yiyim la, wozɔna ɖe woƒe axa eneawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe dzi, eye wometrɔna o.

english_verse: The rims of the wheels were large and frightening, and they had eyes all the way around them.
translation_verse: Toga li na afɔ eneawo, eye kekemegati lɛlɛlɛwo le wo si. Ŋkuwo le togaawo ŋu ƒo xlã godoo.

english_verse: The creatures controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the four creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels were beside them.
translation_verse: Ne woɖe zɔ la, tasiaɖamfɔawo hã ɖea zɔ. Ne wotɔ la, wotɔna. Ne wokɔ wo ɖokui dzi tso anyigba la, woawo hã kɔa wo ɖokui dzi; elabe nu gbagbeawo ƒe gbɔgbɔ le tasiaɖamfɔawo me.

english_verse: Above the living creatures, I saw something that was sparkling like ice, and it reminded me of a dome. Each creature had two of its wings stretched out toward the creatures on either side, with the other two wings folded against its body.
