translation_verse: Elabe edo vlo atam la, eye wòtu nubabla la. Esi wòna asi ame ɖe nya sia dzi vɔ hafi va wɔ nu siawo katã ta la, mate ŋu así o.

english_verse: He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Zi ale si mele agbe la, nye atam si wòdo vloe kple nye nubabla si wòtu ta la, maɖo eteƒe nɛ.

english_verse: I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me.
translation_verse: Maɖo ɖɔ nɛ, aɖee le mɔ̀ me. Makplɔe va Babilon afi si madrɔ̃ ʋɔnui le, le ale si meto nyateƒe nam o la ta.

english_verse: His best troops will be killed in battle, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Kalẽtɔ akuakua siwo le esi la atsi yi nu, eye ame siwo tsi agbe la, akaka ɖe ya nu le afi sia afi, ne miadze sii be, nye Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.” Mawu do ŋugbe be mɔkpɔkpɔ li

english_verse: Someday, I, the Lord, will cut a tender twig from the top of a cedar tree, then plant it on the peak of Israel's tallest mountain,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Nye ŋutɔ maŋe sederti kɔkɔtɔ ƒe ɖɔme aɖado. Eƒe ɖɔmeɖɔme fɛ̃ kekeake ƒe alɔ maŋe, eye nye ŋutɔ matsɔe aɖado ɖe to kɔkɔ aɖe dzi.

english_verse: where it will grow strong branches and produce large fruit. All kinds of birds will find shelter under the tree, and they will rest in the shade of its branches.
translation_verse: Israel ƒe to kɔkɔtɔ dzie madoe ɖo, ne wòaɖe alɔ, eye wòatse ku, azu sederti vavã. Gbemelã vovovowo anɔ ete, eye xevi vovovowo awɔ atɔ ɖe eƒe alɔwo ƒe vɔvɔli me.

english_verse: Every tree in the forest will know that I, the Lord, can bring down tall trees and help short ones grow. I dry up green trees and make dry ones green. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will keep my word.
translation_verse: Ati siwo katã le gbe me la adze sii be nye Aƒetɔ ye bɔbɔa ati kɔkɔwo ɖe anyi, eye menana be ati siwo le kpuie la kɔna. Menana be ati mumu kuna, eye ati kuku dzena. Nye Aƒetɔ ye ƒo nu, eye mawɔe.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya gava nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: “Nu ka tae miedoa lo sia kokoko le Israel-nyigba dzi be: ‘Vi tɔ́wo ɖu waintsetse siwo tea atse la, eye aɖu nyɔ wo viwo’?

english_verse: Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Zi ale si mele agbe la, miegale lo sia do ge le Israel akpɔ o.

english_verse: The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, tɔnyee nye luʋɔ ɖe sia ɖe; vi tɔ́ kple via ŋutsu siaa ƒe luʋɔ nye tɔnye. Luʋɔ si wɔ nuvɔ̃ la, eyae aku.”

english_verse: Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right.
translation_verse: “Ne ame aɖe nye nu dzɔdzɔe wɔla, eye wòwɔa se dzi hewɔa nu dzɔdzɔe,

english_verse: He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period.
translation_verse: ne meɖua nu le towo dzi alo subɔa Israelviwo ƒe legbawo o; ne media ame srɔ̃ alo dɔna kple nyɔnu si kpɔ dzinu la o;

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: ne metea ame ɖe to o, ke etrɔa nu si wòxɔ awɔbae la ɖoa eteƒe ɖe ɣeyiɣi dzi; ne medaa adzo o, ne enaa nu dɔwuitɔ wòɖuna, eye ne ame aɖe le amama la, wònaa avɔe wòtana;

english_verse: and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone
translation_verse: ne medoa ga be wòaɖe vi na ye alo xɔa deme o; ne wòtea asi ɖa tso nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ gbɔ; ne wòtsoa afia na ame kple ehavi ɖe eteƒe,

english_verse: and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
translation_verse: zɔna ɖe nye ɖoɖowo nu, eye wòwɔa nye seawo dzi la, ame sia nye nu dzɔdzɔe wɔla, anɔ agbe godoo.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins
translation_verse: “Ne edzi vi si nye adzodala kple ʋukɔɖila,

english_verse: his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife,
translation_verse: ame si mewɔa dɔdeasi siawo ƒe ɖeke o, ke boŋ wòɖua nu le towo dzi, dea asi ehavi srɔ̃ ŋu,

english_verse: cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things,
translation_verse: tea ame dahewo kple hiãtɔwo ɖe anyi, daa adzo, eye wòxɔa awɔbanu metrɔnɛ ɖoa eteƒe o, ne esubɔa legbawo, eye wòwɔa ŋunyɔnuwo,

english_verse: and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
translation_verse: ne edoa ga be yeakpɔ viɖe, eye wòxɔa deme la; ekema ɖe eyama anɔ agbea? Manɔ agbe o. Ame awɔ ŋunyɔnu siawo katã gbegbe anɔ agbea? Aku godoo. Eƒe ʋu anɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe ta dzi.”

english_verse: But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him.
translation_verse: “Ke ne ame sia dzi vi si kpɔ nuvɔ̃ siwo katã tɔ́a wɔ, wodzi ŋɔ nɛ, eye metsɔ tɔ́a ƒe afɔ o,

english_verse: He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife.
translation_verse: ame si meɖua nu le towo dzi loo, alo subɔa Israelviwo ƒe legbawo o; medea asi ehavi srɔ̃ ŋu o,

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: media ge le ame aɖeke ŋu o, mexɔa awɔbanu o, medaa adzo o, ke wònaa nuɖuɖu dɔwuitɔwo, eye wòtsyɔa avɔ na ame siwo tsi ama;

english_verse: and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father.
translation_verse: etea asi ɖa tso nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ gbɔ, medoa ga be yeakpɔ viɖe alo axɔ deme o; ezɔna ɖe nye ɖoɖowo nu, eye wòwɔa nye sewo dzi la, eyama maku ɖe tɔ́a ƒe nuvɔ̃ ta o; anɔ agbe godoo.

english_verse: You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws.
translation_verse: “Gake miawo ya miebe: ‘Nu ka tae vi makpe fu ɖe tɔ́a ƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ta o?’ Ne ɖevia wɔ nu si le dzɔdzɔe ɖe se nu, eye wòlé eɖokui helé nye ɖoɖowo me ɖe asi la, anɔ agbe godoo.

english_verse: Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
translation_verse: Luʋɔ si wɔa nuvɔ̃ la, eyae aku. Vi makpe fu ɖe tɔ́a ƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ta loo, alo tɔ́a hã nakpe fu ɖe via ƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ta o. Nu dzɔdzɔe wɔla ƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔe wòadro ɖe ta, eye ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe vɔɖivɔ̃ɖinyenye anye eya ŋutɔ ƒe agba.”

english_verse: Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death.
translation_verse: “Ke ne ame vɔ̃ɖi aɖe trɔ, eye megawɔa nuvɔ̃ siwo katã wòwɔna la o, eye wòlé nye ɖoɖowo katã me ɖe asi hewɔ nu si le dzɔdzɔe ɖe se nu la, anɔ agbe, maku o.

english_verse: All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right.
translation_verse: Womagaɖo ŋku se siwo katã dzi wòda va yi la dzi nɛ o. Anɔ agbe le nu dzɔdzɔe si wòwɔ la ta.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: ‘Ɖe ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe ku doa dzidzɔ nama? Ɖe nyemadi be netrɔ dzime ne wòatsi agbe boŋ oa?’

english_verse: But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
translation_verse: Gake ne nu dzɔdzɔe wɔla dzudzɔ nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ, eye wòwɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi, eye wòwɔa ŋunyɔnu mawo ƒomevi ke ame vɔ̃ɖi wɔna la, ɖe wòanɔ agbea? Womagaɖo ŋku nu dzɔdzɔe siwo katã wòwɔ va yi la ƒe ɖeke dzi o. Elabe esi wòwɔ alakpanu, ɖi fɔ, hewɔ nuvɔ̃ ta la, ɖeko wòaku.”

english_verse: You people of Israel accuse me of being unfair! But listen—I'm not unfair; you are!
translation_verse: “Ke miawo miebe: ‘Aƒetɔ la ƒe mɔwo mele dzɔdzɔe kura o.’ Israel-dukɔ, azɔ misee ɖa: Nyee le nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔm loo, alo miawo boŋ ye le nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔm?

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Ne nu dzɔdzɔe wɔla trɔ le nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ gbɔ hewɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi la, aku ɖe eta. Nu vɔ̃ɖi si wòwɔ la tae wòaku ɖo.

english_verse: And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Hekpe ɖe esia ŋu la, ne ame vɔ̃ɖi aɖe dzudzɔ eƒe vɔɖivɔ̃ɖinyenye, eye wòwɔa nu dzɔdzɔe si le se nu la, atsi agbe.

english_verse: They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death.
translation_verse: Elabe esi wòbu tame, eye megadaa se dzi o ta la, atsi agbe godoo, maku akpɔ o.

english_verse: But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
translation_verse: Ke Israel-dukɔ la be: ‘Aƒetɔ la ƒe nuwɔnawo mele eteƒe o.’ Ao, Israel-dukɔ! Nyee le nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔm loo, alo miawo boŋ ye le nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔma?”

english_verse: I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished.
translation_verse: Eya ta, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Israelviwo, madrɔ̃ ʋɔnu mia dome ame sia ame pɛpɛpɛ ɖe eƒe nuwɔnawo nu. Mitrɔ tso miaƒe dzidadawo katã gbɔ, ne miaƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ magatsrɔ̃ mi o.

english_verse: Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins?
translation_verse: Miɖe asi le se siwo katã dzi mieda le mia dome ɖe ŋunye la ŋu. Miwɔ miaƒe dziwo yeyee, eye gbɔgbɔ yeye nege ɖe mia me. O Israel-dukɔ, nu ka ta koŋ miadi be yewoaku ɖo?

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Amegbetɔ aɖeke ƒe ku medzɔa dzi nam o. Eya ta mitrɔ azɔli ne miatsi agbe.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
translation_verse: Ke wò la, kpa konyifaha de Israel ƒe amegãwo.

english_verse: Your mother was a brave lioness who raised her cubs among lions.
translation_verse: Dzi ha be: Dzatanɔ tɔxɛ aɖe nye nɔwò nɔ dzatatsuwo dome! Emlɔa dzataviwo dome, nyia viawo.

english_verse: She taught one of them to hunt, and he learned to eat people.
translation_verse: Enyi viawo dometɔ ɖeka, wòzu dzatavi; esrɔ̃ nuléle hevuvu amewo.

english_verse: When the nations heard of him, they trapped him in a pit, then they used hooks to drag him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Dukɔwo de zi eŋu, nyae ɖe nu wòge dze woƒe ʋe me wolé. Wode gae, kplɔe yi Egipte-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: His mother waited for him to return. But soon she lost all hope and raised another cub, who also became fierce.
translation_verse: Esi wòkpɔ be wotɔtɔ ye, yeƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ bu la, etia via bubu wɔe wòzu dzatavi.

english_verse: He hunted with other lions and learned to eat people.
translation_verse: Enɔa ade minyam le dzatawo dome. Ezu dzatavi; esrɔ̃ nuléle hevuvu amewo.

english_verse: He destroyed fortresses and ruined towns; his mighty roar terrified everyone.
translation_verse: Egbã woƒe mɔ́ sesẽwo, ena woƒe duwo zu aƒedo. Ne eɖe gbe la, ŋɔdzi léa anyigba la kple edzinɔlawo katã.

english_verse: Nations plotted to kill him, and people came from all over to spread out a net and catch him in a trap.
translation_verse: Tete dukɔwo tre mɔ̀ nɛ ɖe afi sia afi; woɖo ɖɔ nɛ, ege dze woƒe ʋe me, eye wolée.

english_verse: They put him in a cage and took him to Babylonia. The lion was locked away, so that his mighty roar would never again be heard on Israel's hills.
translation_verse: Wode gae, dee xadza me hekplɔe yi na Babilon-fia. Wodee gaxɔ me, be womagase eƒe gbe le Israel-towo dzi azɔ o.

english_verse: Your mother was a vine like you, growing near a stream. There was plenty of water, so she was filled with branches and with lots of fruit.
translation_verse: Nɔwò nɔ abe wainka le wainbɔ aɖe me ene. Wohoe va do ɖe tɔ to. Esi wòkpɔ tsi nyuie ta la, eɖe alɔ fũu hetse ku geɖe.

english_verse: Her strong branches became symbols of authority, and she was taller than all other trees— everyone could see how strong and healthy she was.
translation_verse: Eƒe lobome si kpɔ ŋusẽ wu la zu fiatikplɔ. Ekɔ yi dzi le alɔ siwo tri la dome. Wokpɔe be ede dzi wu alɔ geɖeawo.

english_verse: But in anger, I pulled her up by the roots and threw her to the ground, where the scorching desert wind dried out her fruit. Her strong branches wilted and burned up.
translation_verse: Gake wodo dziku ho wainka la ƒu anyi. Ɣedzeƒeya ƒo to edzi wòƒu; kutsetseawo dudu, eƒe lobome sesẽ la ƒu hebi dzo.

english_verse: Then she was planted in a hot, dry desert,
translation_verse: Azɔ wohoe ɖado ɖe gbegbe, ɖe anyigba ƒuƒu si dzi tsi vena le la dzi.

english_verse: where her stem caught fire, and flames burned her branches and fruit. Not one strong branch is left; she is stripped bare. This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_verse: Dzo bii tso eƒe lobome. Efiã alɔawo kple kutsetseawo ale be lobome sesẽ aɖeke meganɔ eŋu si anye dziɖula ƒe fiatikplɔ o. Esia nye konyifafa, eye wòzu konyifaha.

english_verse: Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti atɔ̃lia ƒe ŋkeke ewolia dzi, le ƒè adrẽlia me la, Israel-metsitsi aɖewo va nɔ ŋkunye me, be yewoabia gbe tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: Just then, the Lord God said:
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, gblɔ na Israel-metsitsiawo be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Nyee mieva gbe bia gea? Zi ale si mele agbe la, nyemana miabia gbem akpɔ o. Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Àdrɔ̃ ʋɔnu woa? Amegbetɔ vi, àdrɔ̃ ʋɔnu woa? Ekema na woanya wo tɔgbuiwo ƒe ŋunyɔnuwo.

english_verse: Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na wo be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Gbe si gbe metia Israel la, meka atam na Yakob ƒe ƒome la, meɖe ɖokuinye fia wo le Egipte-nyigba dzi. Meka atam na wo be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la.

english_verse: I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbee meka atam na wo be makplɔ wo ado go tso Egipte-nyigba la dzi ava anyigba si medi da ɖi na wo la dzi, anyigba si dzi notsi kple anyitsi bɔ ɖo, anyigba nyuitɔ kekeake wònye le anyigbawo katã dome.

english_verse: I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God,
translation_verse: Megblɔ na wo be: Mitsɔ nu siwo katã melé fui, esiwo ŋu miaƒe ŋku le la ƒu gbe. Mia dome ame aɖeke megaƒo ɖi eɖokui kple Egipte-legbawo o. Nyee nye Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la.

english_verse: but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods. In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ke wodze aglã ɖe ŋunye hegbe to ɖoɖom. Wo dome ame aɖeke metsɔ nu siwo melé fui, esiwo ŋu woƒe ŋku le la ƒu gbe loo, alo ɖe asi le Egipte-legbawo ŋu o.” “Tete mebu be matrɔ nye dɔmedzoe akɔ ɖe wo dzi, aɖe dziku ɖe wo ŋu le Egipte-nyigba la dzi.

english_verse: But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Gake melé ɖokuinye le nye ŋkɔ la ta. Nyemedi be maƒo ɖi nye ŋkɔ le dukɔ siwo dome wole la ŋkume o. Dukɔ mawo ŋkumee meɖe ɖokuinye fia le, esime meɖe wo hekplɔ wo do go tso Egipte la.

english_verse: So I brought them out and led them into the desert.
translation_verse: Ale be mekplɔ wo do goe le Egipte-nyigba dzi hekplɔ wo va gbedadaƒo.

english_verse: I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right.
translation_verse: Metsɔ nye ɖoɖowo na wo, eye mexlẽ nye sewo fia wo, mɔ siwo dzi ame ato anɔ agbe la.

english_verse: And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me.
translation_verse: Gawu la, meɖo nye dzudzɔgbewo na wo, ne woanye dzesi anɔ nye kple wo dome. Ale woadze sii be nye Aƒetɔ ye kɔ wo ŋu.

english_verse: But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day. Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all.
translation_verse: Ke Israel-dukɔ la dze aglã ɖe ŋunye le gbedadaƒo. Womezɔ nye ɖoɖowo dzi o; ke wogbe nye seawo, mɔ siwo dzi ame ato anɔ agbe la, eye woɖu kɔ na nye dzudzɔgbewo ale gbegbe.” “Tete mebu be matrɔ nye dɔmedzoe akɔ ɖe wo dzi le gbedadaƒo, ne woatsrɔ̃ keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Gake melé ɖokuinye le nye ŋkɔ la ta. Nyemedi be maƒo ɖi nye ŋkɔ le dukɔ siwo ŋkume mekplɔ wo do goe le la o.

english_verse: Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised.
translation_verse: Gawu la, meka atam na wo le gbedadaƒo be nyemakplɔ wo va anyigba si metsɔ na wo la dzi o, anyigba si dzi notsi kple anyitsi bɔ ɖo, anyigba nyuitɔ kekeake wònye le anyigbawo katã dome.

english_verse: I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
translation_verse: Elabe wogbe nye sewo, eye womezɔ nye ɖoɖowo dzi o. Woɖu kɔ na nye dzudzɔgbewo, elabe woƒe dzi le woƒe legbawo yome.

english_verse: Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert.
translation_verse: Ke hã la, meŋe aɖaba ƒu edzi. Nyemetsrɔ̃ wo le gbedadaƒo be woavɔ ɖa keŋkeŋ o.”

english_verse: So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols.
translation_verse: Megbe nya na wo viwo le gbedadaƒo be: “Migawɔ mia tɔgbuiwo ƒe ɖoɖowo dzi loo, alo miazɔ ɖe woƒe sewo nu o. Migatsɔ woƒe legbawo gblẽ kɔ ɖo na mia ɖokui o.

english_verse: I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Nye Aƒetɔ ye nye mia Mawu. Mizɔ ɖe nye ɖoɖowo nu, eye mikpɔ nyuie be miewɔ nye seawo dzi.

english_verse: I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Mikɔ nye dzudzɔgbewo ŋu nam ale be woanye dzesi le nye kple miawo dome, ne miadze sii be nye Aƒetɔ ye nye mia Mawu.

english_verse: But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day. I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert.
translation_verse: Ke wo viwo dze aglã ɖe ŋunye. Womezɔ ɖe nye ɖoɖowo nu o. Womeɖɔ ŋu ɖo wɔ nye sewo dzi o, mɔ siwo dzi ame azɔ anɔ agbe. Woɖu kɔ na nye dzudzɔgbewo.” “Tete mebu be matrɔ nye dɔmedzoe akɔ ɖe wo dzi eye maɖe nye dziku ɖe wo ŋu le gbedadaƒo la.

english_verse: But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Gake mehe nye asi ɖe megbe, eye mewɔ nu le nye ŋkɔ ta; ale be nye ŋkɔ magblẽ le dukɔ siwo ŋkume mekplɔ wo do goe le la gbɔ o.

english_verse: So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations,
translation_verse: Gawu la, meka atam na wo le gbedadaƒo la be makaka wo ahlẽ ɖe dukɔwo dome, eye makaka wo ɖe anyigbawo dzi.

english_verse: because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made.
translation_verse: Elabe womewɔ ɖe nye ɖoɖowo nu o. Ke wogbe nye sewo dzi wɔwɔ. Woɖu kɔ na nye dzudzɔgbewo, eye woƒe ŋku tsi wo tɔgbuiwo ƒe legbawo ŋu.

english_verse: I gave them laws that bring punishment instead of life,
translation_verse: Gawu la, metsɔ ɖoɖo gbegblẽ siwo nye se siwo makplɔ wo woanɔ agbe o la na wo.

english_verse: and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
translation_verse: Megblẽ kɔ ɖo na wo to woƒe vɔsawo kekeake me, esi wɔnɛ be woléa woƒe ŋgɔgbevi ŋutsuwo katã nɔa memem le dzo me abe vɔsalã ene. Mewɔe be wòadzi ŋɔ na wo, mewɔe be woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, tell the people of Israel that their ancestors also rejected and insulted me
translation_verse: Eya ta, amegbetɔ vi, ƒo nu na Israel-dukɔ la, eye nàgblɔ na wo be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Mia tɔgbuiwo gawɔ busunu ɖe ŋunye ake. Wometo nyateƒe nam o.

english_verse: by offering sacrifices, incense, and wine to gods on every hill and under every large tree. I was very angry, because they did these things in the land I had given them!
translation_verse: Elabe esi mekplɔ wo va anyigba si ŋu meka atam ɖo be matsɔ na wo dzi la, ne wokpɔ togbɛ kɔkɔ ɖe sia ɖe ko alo ati dama ɖe sia ɖe ko la, wosaa vɔ le afi ma. Wotsɔa woƒe vɔsanu siwo ado dziku na ame la nana. Wotɔa dzo lifi, ƒoa tsi hã ɖi le afi ma.

english_verse: I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
translation_verse: Mebia wo be nuxeƒe ka ƒomevie nye esi miedena? Eya ta woyɔnɛ be Bama va se ɖe egbe.

english_verse: by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer.
translation_verse: Elabe miena vɔsanuwo, heme mia viŋutsuwo le dzo me, mietsɔ miaƒe legbawo katã gblẽ kɔ ɖo na mia ɖokui va se ɖe egbe. Ao, Israel-dukɔ! Ɖe miabia gbema? Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Zi ale si mele agbe la, miabia gbem akpɔ o.”

english_verse: They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen! The Lord Promises To Restore Israel The Lord said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: “Nu si le tame na mi la mava eme akpɔ o. Miesusui be: ‘Mina mianɔ abe dukɔ bubuawo kple anyigba bubuwo ƒe towo ene, ahasubɔ ati kple kpe.’ ” Mawu hea to na ame gatsɔa nu kena

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Zi ale si mele agbe la, meka ɖe edzi be matsɔ asi sesẽ kple abɔ si medo ɖe dzi la kpakple dɔmedzoe si wotrɔ kɔ ɖi la aɖu fia ɖe mia dzi.

english_verse: and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you
translation_verse: eye makplɔ mi ayi dukɔwo ƒe gbedadaƒo. Afi mae madrɔ̃ ʋɔnu mi le ŋkume kple ŋkume.

english_verse: and punish you, just as I punished your ancestors in the desert near Egypt.
translation_verse: Ale si medrɔ̃ ʋɔnu kple mia tɔgbuiwo le gbedadaƒo le Egipte-nyigba dzi la, nenemae maɖo kodzo kpli mi. Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: Makplɔ mi ato amekplɔti la te, azi mia dzi ɖekaɖeka be mianɔ nubabla me kplim.

english_verse: I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Matsra aglãdzelawo le mia dome, eye ame siwo daa vo ɖe ŋunye la, makplɔ wo tso dzronyigba dzi. Ke womaɖo afɔ Israel-nyigba dzi o, ekema miadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me!
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Ke wò Israel-dukɔ, ne mimase nye gbe o la, mia dome ame sia ame neyi edzi azɔ ne wòasubɔ eƒe legba. Gake migagblẽ kɔ ɖo na nye ŋkɔ kɔkɔe la kple miaƒe nunanawo kpakple legbawo o.”

english_verse: When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Israel-dukɔ blibo la asubɔm le nye to kɔkɔe la, Israel ƒe to kɔkɔ la dzi. Afi mae wo katã woava subɔm le, le anyigba la dzi. Maxɔ wo atuu le afi ma. Mabia miaƒe adzɔwo, nunana tɔxɛwo kple nu siwo katã ŋu wokɔ la.

english_verse: When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy,
translation_verse: Maxɔ mi abe dzudzɔ si le ʋeʋẽm lílilĩ la ene, nenye be mekplɔ mi do goe tso dukɔwo dome, eye meƒo mia nu ƒu tso anyigba siwo dzi miekaka ɖo la, eye maɖe nye ŋutikɔkɔe afia le mia dome le dukɔwo ŋkume.

english_verse: and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors.
translation_verse: Ne mekplɔ mi va Israel-nyigba, anyigba si ŋu meka atam ɖo na mia tɔgbuiwo be matsɔ na wo dzi la, miadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me,
translation_verse: Afi mae miava ɖo ŋku miaƒe zɔzɔme kple nuwɔna siwo mietsɔ ƒo ɖi mia ɖokui la dzi le. Ekema mianɔ ŋu nyɔm na mia ɖokui le nu vloe siwo katã miewɔ va yi la ta.

english_verse: so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God. Fire from the South
translation_verse: Azɔ miava dze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ, nenye be le nye ŋkɔ ta, nyemewɔ na mi ɖe miaƒe nuvɔ̃ɖiwo kple nɔnɔme vloewo nu o, Israel-dukɔ.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe. Dzobibi le anyigbeme

english_verse: The Lord said,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, turn toward the south and warn the forests
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, trɔ dze ŋgɔ anyigbeme. Gblɔ nya ɖe anyigbemetɔwo ŋu, eye ɖe gbeƒã ɖo ɖe ave siwo le anyigbemekegbegbe la.

english_verse: that I, the Lord God, will start a fire that will burn up every tree, whether green or dry. Nothing will be able to put out the blaze of that fire as it spreads to the north and burns everything in its path.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na ave siwo le anyigbemekegbegbe la be: Mise Aƒetɔ ƒe nya, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, matɔ dzo wò, eye ati mumu kple ati ƒuƒu ɖe sia ɖe afiã le mewò. Womate ŋu atsi dzo si anɔ bibim flaflafla la o. Ame siwo katã tso anyigbeme va yi dzigbeme ƒe ŋkume aƒo dzo.

english_verse: Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
translation_verse: Ŋutilãwo katã akpɔe be nye Aƒetɔ ye tɔ dzo avea. Womate ŋu atsii o.”

english_verse: But I complained, “Lord God, I don't want to do that! People already say I confuse them with my messages.”
translation_verse: Tete megblɔ be: “Ao, Aƒetɔ Mawu! Wole gbɔgblɔm le ŋunye be: ‘Ame sia ɖe, menye abe sɔŋ ko bum wòle oa?’ ”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, dze ŋgɔ Yerusalem, nàgblɔ ɖe kɔkɔeƒewo katã ŋu; ɖe gbeƒã ɖe Israel-nyigba la ŋu.

english_verse: that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na Israel-nyigba la be, Aƒetɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, metsi tre ɖe ŋuwò, eye maɖe nye yi le aku me. Matsrɔ̃ nu dzɔdzɔe wɔlawo kple ame vɔ̃ɖiwo siaa ɖa.

english_verse: Ezekiel, groan in sorrow and despair so that everyone can hear you.
translation_verse: Eya ta, amegbetɔ vi, nɔ hũ ɖem abe ame si ƒe dzi gbã, eye wòle konyi fam la ene le wo ŋkume.

english_verse: When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise! A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
translation_verse: Ne wobia wò be: ‘Nu ka ƒe hũ ɖem nèle?’ la, gblɔ na wo be: ‘Gbedeasi la tae. Ne eɖo dzi la, ame sia ame ƒe dzi agbã, alɔwo agbɔdzɔ, ame sia ame ƒe gbɔgbɔ ayi to, eye klowo katã azu belii abe tsi ene. Kpɔ ɖa, egbɔna, eye ele eme va ge.’ ” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem: I have sharpened my sword to slaughter you; it is shiny and will flash like lightning! Don't celebrate— punishment is coming, because everyone has ignored my warnings.
translation_verse: Wonyree ɖe amewuwu ŋu, wosi ami nɛ wòle dzo dam abe dzikedzo ene. Alo ɖe mianɔ dzidzɔ kpɔma? Vinye, èdo vlo ameƒoti kple atinu ɖe sia ɖe.

english_verse: Groan in sorrow, Ezekiel; the sword is drawn against my people and their leaders. They will die! So give up all hope.
translation_verse: Amegbetɔ vi, fa avi nàƒu asi nu. Elabe etsi tre ɖe nye dukɔ la ŋu, Israel ƒe amegãwo katã ŋue wòtsi tre ɖo. Wotsɔ nye dukɔ la de asi na yi. Eya ta ƒo aklito.

english_verse: I am testing my people, and they can do nothing to stop me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Elabe menye dodokpɔ wòanye o. Nu ka ameƒoti agate ŋu awɔ ne miedo vloe?” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Ezekiel, warn my people, then celebrate my victory by clapping your hands. My vicious sword will attack again and again, killing my people with every stroke.
translation_verse: “Eya ta amegbetɔ vi, ɖe gbeƒã. Ƒo asikpoloe, eye nàna yi la nadza nu zi eve, ẽ zi etɔ̃ hã. Yi si awu ame siwo wòawu lae, yi si awu ame gbogbowo la, eyae ɖe to ɖe wo;

english_verse: They will lose all courage and stumble with fear. My slaughtering sword is waiting at every gate, flashing and ready to kill.
translation_verse: bene woƒe dzi nalólo, eye amewo adze anyi ɖe woƒe agbowo nu. Metsɔ yi si le dzo dam la na. O, wowɔe abe dzikedzo ene, wosi ami nɛ hena amewuwu.

english_verse: It will slash right and left, wherever the blade is pointed.
translation_verse: Lã nu le ɖusime kple miame afi si wò nu trɔ ɖo ko.

english_verse: Then I will stop being angry, and I will clap my hands in victory. I, the Lord, have spoken. The King of Babylonia and His Sword
translation_verse: Nye hã maƒo asikpoloe, eye nye dziku nu afa. Nye Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.” Babilon-fia ƒe yi

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions.
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, ta mɔ eve na Babilon-fia ƒe yi ne wòato edzi ava. Wo kple eve la siaa natso anyigba ɖeka dzi ava. Wɔ dzesi si afia mɔ la ɖe wo dzi. Wɔe ɖe afi si mɔawo dze egɔme tsoe ɖo ta du sia me.

english_verse: Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah.
translation_verse: Ɖe mɔ ɖeka va Amontɔwo de le Raba, ɖeka nava Yuda, eye ɖeka nava Yerusalem, du si ŋu wotɔ glikpɔ sesẽ ɖo la.

english_verse: When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal.
translation_verse: Elabe Babilon-fia le tsitre ɖe mɔ dzeve la nu le dzesi siwo le mɔawo fiam la gbɔ. Etɔ ɖe mɔ dzeveawo ƒe gɔmedzeƒe be yeaka afa. Eʋuʋu aŋutrɔawo, bia gbe aklama kpakpɛwo, eye wòlé ŋku ɖe lã ƒe aklã ŋu.

english_verse: His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people.
translation_verse: Nu si wodzidze ɖe Yerusalem ŋu la va dze eƒe ɖusime, be woatu nu siwo woatsɔ agbã gli, woaƒu asi nu ado ɣli sesĩe hoo. Woatu nu si woatsɔ gbã gli la ɖe eƒe agbowo ŋu. Woaƒu kpo ɖe dua ŋu, atu dzɔlawo ƒe xɔ kɔkɔwo.

english_verse: Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
translation_verse: Woawo woabui be afa la meɖi o; woka atam na wo nɔewo. Ke eya le ŋku ɖo ge woƒe fɔɖiɖiwo dzi ale be wòana woalé wo asiasii.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying: Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: “Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Elabe miena woɖo ŋku miaƒe fɔɖiɖi dzi, esime woklo nu le miaƒe dzidadawo dzi, ale be miaƒe nuvɔ̃wo le dzedzem le miaƒe wɔnawo keŋ me. Elabe esi miena woɖo ŋku edzi la, woalé mi le wo me.

english_verse: And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here.
translation_verse: Ke wò Israel-megã, ame vɔ̃ɖi makɔmakɔ, wo ame si ƒe ŋkeke ɖo edzi la, wò tohehe mamlɛa nye esi.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Ɖe wò tablanu, ɖe wò fiakuku. Nuwo maganɔ alea o. Mido ame gblɔe ɖe dzi, eye miaɖiɖi amegã la ɖe anyi.

english_verse: I will leave Jerusalem in complete ruins like no one has ever seen until my chosen one comes to punish this city. Judgment against Ammon
translation_verse: Aƒedo, aƒedo, aƒedoe mawɔe. Womagakpɔ enɔƒe adze sii o, va se ɖe esime ame si tɔ wònye ava, eye matsɔe nɛ.” Yi aɖe kple Amontɔwo

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying: A sword is drawn, ready to slaughter; it is polished and prepared to kill as fast as lightning.
translation_verse: Azɔ wò amegbetɔ vi, ɖe gbeƒã nàgblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ Mawu gblɔ nya ɖe Amontɔwo ŋu le woƒe alɔmeɖeɖe ŋuti be: Yi, wohe yi ɖe go na amewuwu. Wosi ami nɛ be wòaklẽ, eye wòada dzo abe dzikedzo ene.

english_verse: You wicked Ammonites see false visions and believe untrue messages. But your day of punishment is coming soon, and my sword will slaughter you!
translation_verse: Wole alakpaŋutega kpɔm na mi, wole aʋatsofa kam na mi be woatsɔ mi aɖo kɔ dzi na ame vɔ̃ɖi makɔmakɔ siwo ƒe ŋkeke de, siwo ƒe toheɣi mamlɛa ɖo.

english_verse: Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth.
translation_verse: Trɔ wò yi la de aku me. Mele ʋɔnu drɔ̃ ge wò le teƒe si wowɔ wò le, le anyigba si dzi nèdzɔ tso la.

english_verse: My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing.
translation_verse: Maɖe ale si wò nu gblẽ ŋunye la afia wò. Matrɔ nye dziku akɔ ɖe dziwò, eye maƒlɔ nye dɔmedzoe ƒe dzo ɖe ŋuwò. Matsɔ wò ade asi na ŋutasẽlawo, ame siwo gblẽa ame kple aɖaŋu.

english_verse: You will be burned and will die in your own land. Then you will be forgotten forever. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Àtrɔ zu nake le dzo me. Wò ʋu anɔ sisím le anyigba dzi. Womagaɖo ŋku dziwò akpɔ o.” Elabe nye Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Some time later, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Gawu la, Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, are you ready to condemn Jerusalem? That city is filled with murderers, so remind the people of their sins
translation_verse: “Wò amegbetɔ vi, àdrɔ̃ ʋɔnua? Àdrɔ̃ ʋɔnu hlɔ̃dodu laa? Ekema gblɔ eƒe ŋunyɔnu siwo katã wòwɔ la fiae.

english_verse: and tell them I am saying: Jerusalem, you have murdered many of your own people and have worshiped idols. You will soon be punished!
translation_verse: Gblɔ nɛ be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Du si kɔa ʋu ɖe anyigba dzi lae wònye. Eƒe ɣeyiɣi gbɔna. Ewɔ legbawo be yeatsɔ gblẽ kɔ ɖo na ye ɖokui.

english_verse: Those crimes have made you guilty, and the idols have made you unacceptable to me. So your final punishment is near. Other nations will laugh at you and make insulting remarks,
translation_verse: Le ʋu si nèkɔ ɖi ta la, èɖi fɔ, eye nègblẽ kɔ ɖo na ɖokuiwò to legba siwo nèlí la me. Nèna wò ŋkeke tsɔ kaba, eye wò ƒewo ƒe nuwuwu ɖo. Eya ta mena nèzu alɔmeɖenu na dukɔwo, eye nèɖi kokoe na anyigbawo katã.

english_verse: and people far and near will make fun of your misery.
translation_verse: Kpuiƒe kple didiƒe tɔwo katã aɖu fewu le ŋuwò. Wò ame si ƒe ŋkɔ gblẽ, eye nèyɔ fũu kple ʋunyaʋunya.”

english_verse: You show no respect for my sacred places and treat the Sabbath just like any other day.
translation_verse: Miedo vlo nye nu kɔkɔeawo, eye miegblẽ kɔ ɖo na nye dzudzɔgbewo.

english_verse: Some of your own people tell lies, so that others will be put to death. Some of you eat meat sacrificed to idols at local shrines, and others never stop doing vulgar things.
translation_verse: Amewo le mewò le ame ŋu gblẽm ne woakɔ ʋu ɖi. Amewo le nu ɖum le towo dzi. Amewo dze ha kple fieŋufieŋu le mewò.

english_verse: Men have sex with their father's wife or with women who are having their monthly period
translation_verse: Amewo ɖe ama wo tɔ́wo le mewò; amewo zia nyɔnuwo dzi dɔna kpli wo le woƒe dzinukpɔɣiwo me.

english_verse: or with someone else's wife. Some men even sleep with their own daughter-in-law or half sister.

translation_verse: Babiloniatɔwo kple Kaldeatɔwo katã, Pekod, Soa kple Koa, Asiriatɔwo katã akpe ɖe wo ŋu, ɖekakpui siwo dze ɖeka, anyigba dziɖulawo, aʋakplɔlawo katã, asrafomegãwo kple kalẽtɔwo, ame siwo katã le sɔ dzi.

translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, de dzesi egbe ŋkeke sia nàŋlɔ ŋkeke sia tututu da ɖi. Ŋkeke sia dzi tututue Babilon-fia ɖe to ɖe Yerusalem.

translation_verse: Tia alẽ nyuitɔwo, nàde nake dzoa me; na lãkɔwo nafie, ƒuawo hã nabi abɔbɔ.”

english_verse: These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Baba na du si le ʋu kɔm ɖi na gaze si lé ɣebia, eye eƒe ɣebia meɖe ɖa le eŋu o la. Ɖe lãwo le eme ɖekaɖeka, mègatia wo me o.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground.
translation_verse: Elabe ʋu si wòkɔ ɖi la gale eme ko. Agakpe si dzi ke aɖeke mele o la dzie wòkɔ ʋua ɖo. Mekɔe ɖe anyigba ne woaxe ke ɖe edzi o.

english_verse: But I have seen that blood, and it cries out for me to take revenge.
translation_verse: Be makpɔe ne dzi nakum vevie, eye mabia hlɔ̃ ta la, mena ʋu si wokɔ ɖi la tsi agakpe ƒuƒlu la dzi, ale be womaxe ke ɖe edzi o.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will punish that city of violence! I will make a huge pile of firewood,
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu gblɔ be: Baba na du si kɔa ʋu ɖi! Nye hã mali kɔ nake la gleglegle.

english_verse: so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch.
translation_verse: Tu dzotikpoawo ɖo, nàdo dzo la. Ɖa lã la ne wòabi nyuie; detsia neto; ƒua nalé ze.

english_verse: Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust.
translation_verse: Na ze ƒuƒlu la nanɔ dzoka dzi, ne wòaxɔ dzo, eye eƒe akɔbli nafiã, ne nu ƒoɖi siwo le eme la nalólo, ale be ɣebia si le eŋu la nafiã keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: I've tried everything else. Now the rust must be burned away.
translation_verse: Meɖe fu na ɖokuinye dzodzro; dzo mete ŋu fiã ɣebia si tri le eŋu la o.

english_verse: Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it.
translation_verse: Eƒe ɣebia nye wò hadzedze ƒoɖi la. Anye ne maklɔ ŋuwò gake wò ɖiƒoƒo la gbe ɖiɖi. Nyemagaklɔ ŋuwò azɔ o, va se ɖe esime nye akɔ nafa, eye madzudzɔ dɔmedzoedodo ɖe ŋuwò.

english_verse: That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Ezekiel's Wife Dies
translation_verse: Nye Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, eye ava eme hã. Mawɔe, nyemagbe ewɔwɔ o, nyemaɖe ame aɖeke le eme o, eye nyematrɔ susu o. Ale si nèzɔe kple nu siwo nèwɔ la nue madrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wò ɖo.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe. Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela srɔ̃ ƒe ku

english_verse: The Lord said,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya gava nam be:

english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry.
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, kpɔ ɖa, maɖe ame si ƒe nu nyoa ŋuwò la ɖa kpata. Mègaxa nu loo, afa avi loo, alo aɖatsi nage le mo na wò o.

english_verse: Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
translation_verse: Ɖe hũ, ke mègana woasee o. Mègawɔ kunu o. Bla ta nàdo afɔkpa; mègabla ŋkume loo, alo aɖu kuteƒe nuɖuɖu o.

english_verse: One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me,
translation_verse: Ale meƒo nu na dukɔ la le ŋdi me, eye srɔ̃nye ku le fiẽ me. Esi ŋu ke la, mewɔ abe ale si woɖo nam la ene.”

english_verse: and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
translation_verse: Dukɔ la biam be: “Maɖe nu si ta nèle nu siawo wɔm ale gɔme na mí oa?”

english_verse: I answered: The Lord God says
translation_verse: Tete megblɔ na wo be: “Aƒetɔ ƒe nyae va nam be:

english_verse: he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed.
translation_verse: ‘Gblɔ na Israel-dukɔ la be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, magblẽ kɔ ɖo na nye kɔkɔeƒe la, ŋusẽ si dzi miedàna ɖo, nu si nyoa miaƒe ŋkuwo ŋu, eye miaƒe luʋɔ dina la. Mia viŋutsu kple vinyɔnu siwo miegblẽ ɖe megbe la, woava wu wo kple yi.

english_verse: Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat.
translation_verse: Miawɔ abe ale si mewɔ ene. Migabla nu ɖe ŋkume loo, alo aɖu kuteƒe nu o.

english_verse: You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
translation_verse: Miaƒe tablanu anɔ ta na mi, eye afɔkpa anɔ miaƒe afɔ. Migafa konyi loo, alo afa avi o. Ke miaxa nu le miaƒe nuvɔ̃wo me anɔ ŋeŋem le mia nɔewo dome.

english_verse: I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
translation_verse: Ale Xezekiel atrɔ zu dzesi na mi. Nu siwo katã wòwɔ miekpɔ la, miawo hã miwɔe. Ne nu sia va eme la, ekema miadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ Mawu.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well.
translation_verse: “Ke wò, amegbetɔ vi, gbe si gbe maɖe woƒe sitsoƒe, woƒe dzidzɔ kple ŋutikɔkɔe, nu si nyakpɔna na wo, woƒe dzi ƒe didi la, akpe ɖe wo viŋutsuwo kple wo vinyɔnuwo ŋu la,

english_verse: On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened.
translation_verse: gbe ma gbee sisíla aɖe ava be yeagblɔ nyadzɔdzɔ la na wò.

english_verse: Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe la, àke nu ɖe te le sisíla la ŋkume, eye àƒo nu gbe ma gbe, eye maganye mumu o. Ale àzu dzesi na wo, eye woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, trɔ nàdze ŋgɔ Amontɔwo, eye nàɖe gbeƒã ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: and tell them: You celebrated when my temple was destroyed, when Israel was defeated, and when my people were taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na Amontɔwo be, mise Aƒetɔ Mawu ƒe nya. Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Miegblɔ ‘ehɛ̃’ ɖe nye kɔkɔeƒe la ŋu esime wogblẽ kɔ ɖo nɛ la, ɖe Israel-nyigba la ŋu esime wòzu gbegbe, eye ɖe Yuda ƒe aƒe la ŋu esime wokplɔe yi aboyo me la.

english_verse: Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk.
translation_verse: Eya ta matsɔ wò ade asi na ɣedzeƒetɔwo nàzu wo tɔ. Woatu agbadɔwo ɖe gbɔwò, eye woatso aƒe ɖe gbɔwò. Woaɖu wò kutsetsewo, eye woano wò notsi.

english_verse: Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Mawɔ Raba wòazu gbeɖuƒe na kposɔwo, eye Amontɔwo ƒe duwo azu alẽwo ƒe mlɔƒe. Ekema miadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: You hated Israel so much that you clapped and shouted and celebrated.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Esi miesi akpe, tu afɔ anyi, kpɔ dzidzɔ le vɔ̃ediname si le miaƒe dzime ɖe Israel-nyigba ŋu ta la,

english_verse: And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things. Judgment on Moab
translation_verse: eya ta kpɔ ɖa, mekɔ nye asi dzi ɖe mia ŋu, eye matsɔ mi ana dukɔwo woaha. Malã mi ɖa le dukɔwo dome, eye mana miatsrɔ̃ gbidii le anyigba dzi dukɔwo dome. Miavɔ ɖa keŋkeŋ. Ekema miadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.” Gbeƒãɖeɖe ɖe Moab ŋu

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Moab gblɔ be: Kpɔ ɖa, Yuda le ko abe dukɔ bubuawo katã ene.

english_verse: So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: Eya ta maʋu mɔ na du siwo le Moab xa, esiwo le eƒe liƒowo dzi, dukɔ la ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe, Bet-Yesimot, Baal-Meon kple Kiryataim.

english_verse: The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever,
translation_verse: Matsɔ eya kple Amontɔwo na ɣedzeƒetɔwo be woazu wo tɔ, ale be womagaɖo ŋku wo dzi le dukɔwo dome azɔ o.

english_verse: Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.” Judgment on Edom
translation_verse: Madrɔ̃ ʋɔnu Moab. Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.” Gbeƒãɖeɖe ɖe Edom ŋu

english_verse: The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Esi Edom wɔ nu be yeabia hlɔ̃ Yuda-to la, eye woɖi fɔ ŋutɔ le hlɔ̃biabia sia me ta la,

english_verse: So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Makɔ asi dzi ɖe Edom ŋu. Matsrɔ̃ amewo kple lãwo siaa, eye mana wòazu gbegbe. Woawu wo kple yi tso Teman va se ɖe Dedan.

english_verse: I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.” Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: Matsɔ Edom ade asi na nye dukɔ Israel be woabia hlɔ̃ wo nam. Woatu nu kple Edom ɖe ale si medo dziku kple dɔmedzoe ɖe wo ŋui la nu, eye woadze si nye hlɔ̃biabia.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe. Gbeƒãɖeɖe ɖe Filistia ŋu

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Esi Filistitɔwo tsɔ hlɔ̃biabia wɔ nui, eye wotsɔ tame vɔ̃e kple keléle le dzime bia hlɔ̃e ta la,

english_verse: Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast.
translation_verse: eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, makɔ nye asi dzi ɖe Filistitɔwo ŋu. Matsrɔ̃ Kretatɔwo, eye mana ƒutatɔ mamlɛawo navɔ ɖa gbidii.

english_verse: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Mabia hlɔ̃ wo vevie, atsɔ dɔmedzoe ahe to na wo. Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ, ne mebia hlɔ̃ wo.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
translation_verse: Le ɣletia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi le ƒè wui ɖekɛlia me la, Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, esi Tiro gblɔ le Yerusalem ŋu be: ‘Ehɛ̃, dukɔwo ƒe agbo la gbã, woʋu agbo la siaa nam, nuwo agbugbɔ aɖo asinye esi wòzu aƒedo ta la,’

english_verse: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
translation_verse: eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, wò Tiro, metso ɖe ŋuwò. Makplɔ dukɔ geɖe woava dze dziwò abe ale si ƒutsotsoewo ŋena ɖe nu dzi ene.

english_verse: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
translation_verse: Woagbã Tiro ƒe gliwo, agbã eƒe xɔ tsralawo ƒu anyi. Makuko eƒe anyigba, eye wòazu agakpe si le ƒeƒle.

english_verse: where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed
translation_verse: Azu ɖɔsiaƒe le atsiaƒu titina. Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Nyee gblɔe. Azu nuhaha na dukɔwo.

english_verse: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Woawu via nyɔnu siwo le anyigba la ŋutɔ dzi kple yi. Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Kpɔ ɖa, makplɔ Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar, fiawo ƒe fia la, atso dzigbeme kple sɔwo, tasiaɖamwo, sɔdolawo kple asrafowo ƒe ha gbogbo aɖe ava ƒo ɖe Tiro dzi.

english_verse: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
translation_verse: Awu du siwo le anyigba dzi la me tɔwo kple yi, atu xɔ tsrala siwo me wonɔna dzɔa duwo ŋu ɖe ŋuwò, aƒu kpo ɖe ŋuwò, eye woakɔ woƒe akpoxɔnuwo dzi ɖe ŋuwò.

english_verse: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
translation_verse: Atsɔ eƒe gligbãnuwo ɖe wò gliwo ŋu, agbã wò xɔ tsralawo ƒu anyi kple fía.

english_verse: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
translation_verse: Eƒe sɔwo asɔ gbɔ ale gbegbe be woƒe fufu si anɔ wo yome la agbã ɖe dziwò kɔtɔɔ. Wò gliwo aʋuʋu kpèkpekpe le sɔdolawo, tasiaɖamfɔwo, tasiaɖamwo ƒe afɔzi ta nenye be ege ɖe wò agbowo me abe ale si wogena ɖe du si ƒe gliwo gbã la me ene.

english_verse: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
translation_verse: Eƒe sɔwo atsɔ woƒe afɔwo anya avuzi le wò ablɔwo katã dzi. Atsɔ yi atsrɔ̃ wò dukɔ la, eye wò sɔti titriwo amu dze anyi.

english_verse: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
translation_verse: Woaha wò kesinɔnuwo, eye woada adzo wò adzɔnuwo. Woagbã wò gliwo ƒu anyi, eye woagbã wò xɔ nyuiwo keŋkeŋ. Woalɔ kpeawo, atiawo kple gli gbagbã aɖakɔ ɖe atsiaƒu me.

english_verse: You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps,
translation_verse: Matsi wò hadzidziwo nu, eye wò kasaŋkuwo magaɖi woase azɔ o.

english_verse: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Mawɔ wò agakpe si dzi ke aɖeke mele o la; ɖɔsiaƒe ko nànye. Womagagbugbɔ wò atu akpɔ o. Elabe Aƒetɔ be: Nye Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.”

english_verse: The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu gblɔ na Tiro be: “Ɖe ƒutanyigbawo madzo nyànyanya ne wose wò anyidzedze, ne ame siwo xɔ abi le mewò le ŋeŋem, ne wova wu amewo le mewò oa?

english_verse: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
translation_verse: Tete ƒutamegãwo katã aɖi le woƒe fiazikpuiwo dzi. Woaɖe woƒe awuwo da ɖi, atra nudodo siwo to wolɔ̃ atsyiã tɔxɛwo ɖo hã da ɖi. Ne wole awu dom la, woanɔ ƒoƒom tititi. Woanɔ anyinɔƒe anɔ dzodzom ɣeawo katã ɣi nyànyanya. Wò nya awɔ nuku na wo.

english_verse: and sing this funeral song: “The great city beside the sea is destroyed! Its people once ruled the coast and terrified everyone there.
translation_verse: Woakpa konyifaha ɖe ŋuwò adzi na wò be: ‘Ale ke wɔ nètsrɔ̃ ɖa le ƒuta? Ao du xɔŋkɔ la. Wò si kpɔ ŋusẽ le atsiaƒu dzi, wò kple wò dumetɔ siwo doa ŋɔdzi na anyigba blibo la katã!

english_verse: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
translation_verse: Azɔ tɔdomekpowo le dzodzom nyànyanya le gbe si gbe nèdze anyi la. Nyateƒee, enye nu si wɔ nuku na tɔdomekpowo le atsiaƒu me be nèvɔ ɖa.’ ”

english_verse: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
translation_verse: ekema mate wò ɖe to kpe ɖe aʋlimeyilawo ŋu, ɖo ɖe blematɔwo gbɔ, eye mana nàtsi yɔme. Ànɔ blemaƒedowo me kple aʋlimeyilawo, ale be ame aɖeke maganɔ mewò loo, alo woagbugbɔ wò atso abe du ene o.

english_verse: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mawɔe be wò nuwuwu nadzi ŋɔ, ale be nàvɔ ɖa keŋkeŋ. Togbɔ be amewo adi wò hã la, womagakpɔ wò gbeɖe o. Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
translation_verse: “Azɔ wò amegbetɔ vi, dzi aviha na Tiro,

english_verse: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
translation_verse: eye gblɔ na Tiro, du si le atsiaƒu nu, si tsaa asi kple ƒutadukɔ geɖewo la be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Ao Tiro, ègblɔ be: ‘Medze tugbe ŋutɔŋutɔ.’

english_verse: and your control of the sea. You are a ship built to perfection.
translation_verse: Wò liƒowo le atsiaƒu titina. Ame siwo tsò wò la na nèdze tugbe ale gbegbe.

english_verse: Builders used cypress trees from Mount Hermon to make your planks and a cedar tree from Lebanon for your tall mast.
translation_verse: Sesewuʋuƒowo tso Senir wotsɔ kpa wòe. Lebanon-sedertie wotsɔ wɔ wò abalati.

english_verse: Oak trees from Bashan were shaped into oars; pine trees from Cyprus were cut for your deck, which was then decorated with strips of ivory.
translation_verse: Wotsɔ fɔfɔlĩ tso Basan kpa wò akɔfawoe. Wodo atsyiã ɖe mewò kple kpomi tso Kipro-ƒukpowo dzi. Wotsaka kpomi la kple nyiɖu.

english_verse: The builders used fancy linen from Egypt for your sails, so everyone could see you. Blue and purple cloth from Cyprus was used to shade your deck.
translation_verse: Wò abala nye aklala si tso Egipte. Wolɔ̃ nu ɖe eto atsyiãtɔe; aɖabɛ blɔtɔ kple dzĩtɔ tso Elisa-ƒukpowo dzi, woawoe wɔ wò xɔnugbadɔ viwo.

english_verse: Men from Sidon and Arvad did the rowing, and your own skilled workers were the captains.
translation_verse: Sidontɔwo kple Arvaditɔwoe kua wò ʋu la. Wò Tiro ŋutɔ ƒe ame siwo dze aɖaŋu ŋutɔe ɖoa kuɖɔ na wò ʋu la.

english_verse: Experienced men from Byblos repaired any damages. Sailors from all over shopped at the stores in your port.
translation_verse: Ametsitsi siwo tso Gebal kple eƒe aɖaŋuwɔlawo nɔa mewò. Woawoe nɔa wò gbagbãƒewo trem. Atsiaƒudziʋuwo kple wo me nɔlawo katã gena ɖe mewò be woaɖɔli adzɔnuwo kpli wò.”

english_verse: Brave soldiers from Persia, Lydia, and Libya served in your navy, protecting you with shields and helmets, and making you famous.
translation_verse: “Persia, Lud kple Put tɔwoe nye aʋawɔla siwo nɔa wò aʋakɔwo dome. Wotsɔa akpoxɔnuwo kple gakukuwo kua nu le mewò. Woawoe na nèxɔ ŋkɔ.

english_verse: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
translation_verse: Arvad kple Helex ŋutsuwoe nɔ wò gliwo dzi va kpe ɖo, eye Gamad-ŋutsuwo de wò xɔ tsralawo dzi. Wotsɔ woƒe akpoxɔnuwo ku wò gliwo ŋu ƒo xlã. Wowɔ wò dzedzeme wònyakpɔ ŋutɔŋutɔ.”

english_verse: Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products.
translation_verse: “Tarsis tsa asi kpli wò le wò kesinɔnu vovovo siwo sɔ gbɔ la ta. Klosalo, ga yibɔ, ga ɣi kple tsumi woe wotsɔna ɖɔlia wò adzɔnuwoe.

english_verse: The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze,
translation_verse: Yavan, Tubal kple Mesex tsa asi kpli wò. Wotsɔ amewo kple akɔblinuwo va ɖɔli wò adzɔnuwo.

english_verse: and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules.
translation_verse: Bet-Togarmatɔwo va ɖɔlia wò adzɔnuwo kple sɔwo, aʋawɔsɔwo kple tedzisɔwo.

english_verse: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
translation_verse: Rodetɔwo tsa asi kpli wò. Ƒutanyigba geɖewo nye wò ŋutɔ wò asitsaƒe tɔxɛwo. Wotsɔ nyiɖu kple keyi va xe fe na wò.

english_verse: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
translation_verse: Yuda kple Israel-nyigba la tsa asi kpli wò. Wotsɔ lu, amiti tsetse, gbo tsetse gbãtɔwo, anyitsi, ami kple lifi va ɖɔlia wò adzɔnuwo.

english_verse: The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
translation_verse: Damasko tsa asi kpli wò le wò adzɔnu gbogboawo ta, le kesinɔnu vovovo siwo sɔ gbɔ la ta. Wotsɔ wain tso Xelbon kple alẽfu ɣiwo,

english_verse: Vedan and Javan near Uzal traded you iron and spices.
translation_verse: kpakple wain tso Usal, ga yibɔ si woté, kotoklobo kple gbekee va ɖɔli adzɔnuawo.

english_verse: The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets,
translation_verse: Dedan tsɔ sɔkpa kple avɔ si woɖona ɖe sɔ dzi la va tsa asi kpli wò.

english_verse: while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats.
translation_verse: Arabiatɔwo kple amegãwo katã tso Kedar nye wò asitsala siwo gbɔ melɔ̃a nu le o. Woawoe tsɔa alẽviwo, agbowo kple gbɔ̃wo va tsaa asi kpli wò.

english_verse: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
translation_verse: Asitsalawo tso Saba kple Ragma tsa asi kpli wò. Wotsɔ atike nyuitɔ vovovowo, kpe xɔasiwo kple sika va ɖɔ li wò adzɔnuwoe.

english_verse: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
translation_verse: Xaran, Kane, Eden, Asiria kple Kilmad tsa asi kpli wò.

english_verse: Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go. You were like a ship loaded with heavy cargo
translation_verse: Tarsis-ʋuwoe ku wò adzɔnuwo na wò. “Ale be nukpɔkpɔwo do agbogbo ɖe dziwò le atsiaƒu titina.

english_verse: and sailing across the sea, but you were wrecked by strong eastern winds.
translation_verse: Wò ʋukulawo ku wò yi atsiaƒu dzi ʋĩi. Ɣedzeƒeya gbã wò le atsiaƒu titina.

english_verse: The shouts of your drowning crew were heard on the shore.
translation_verse: Wò kuɖɔɖolawo ƒe ɣlidodo ana agbleta nadzo kpèkpekpe,

english_verse: Every ship is deserted; rowers and sailors and captains all stand on shore,
translation_verse: eye atablukulawo katã ado le woƒe ʋuwo me. Ʋukulawo kple kuɖɔɖola siwo katã nɔa atsiaƒu dzi la, do go va tsi tsitre ɖe ƒua ta.

english_verse: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
translation_verse: Wodo ɣli lélele le tawò, eye wofa avi hehehe. Wolɔ ke kɔ ɖe tame, eye womli le dzowɔ me.

english_verse: they shave their heads and dress in sackcloth as they cry in despair.
translation_verse: Wolũ ta kokoe le tawò, eye wota akpanya. Woƒe luʋɔ se veve fa avi, eye woxa nu vevie.

english_verse: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
translation_verse: Esi wole avia fam la, wodzi aviha na wò, eye wofa konyi le tawò be: ‘Ame ka koŋ ye tsrɔ̃ le atsiaƒu titina kpɔ abe Tiro ene?

english_verse: “Nations that received your merchandise were always pleased; kings everywhere got rich from your costly goods.
translation_verse: Esi wò adzɔnuwo ɖi go tso ƒuwo dzi la, èna dukɔ geɖewo ɖi ƒo. Ètsɔa wò kesinɔnu gbogboawo kple adzɔnuwo na anyigba dzi fiawo zu kesinɔtɔwo.

english_verse: But now you are wrecked in the deep sea, with your cargo and crew scattered everywhere.
translation_verse: Ke fifia la, atsiaƒu gbã wò gudugudu ɖe tɔ ƒe gogloƒe; wò adzɔnuwo kple ame siwo katã le mewò la, nyrɔ kpli wò.

english_verse: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
translation_verse: Wò nu wɔ nublanui na ƒutanɔlawo katã, vɔvɔ̃ ɖo woƒe fiawo ale gbegbe; wofiã ŋkume sũu.

english_verse: The merchants of the world can't believe what happened. Your death was gruesome, and you are gone forever.”
translation_verse: Asitsalawo tso dukɔwo dome fa na wò be: Wò nuwuwu dzi ŋɔ ŋutɔ, eye màganɔ anyi akpɔ o.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, gblɔ na Tiro-megã be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Elabe wò dzi yɔ kple dàda, eye nègblɔ be: ‘Mawu menye, mawuwo ƒe zikpui dzie menɔna le atsiaƒu titina’; ke amegbetɔ ko nènye, mènye mawu o, togbɔ be èbua ɖokuiwò nunyala abe mawu ene hã.

english_verse: You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
translation_verse: Le nyateƒe me la, ènya nu wu Daniɛl ; naneke mele ɣaɣla ɖe wò o.

english_verse: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
translation_verse: Etsɔ wò nunya kple gɔmesese kpɔ kesinɔnu na ɖokuiwò, eye nèƒo ƒu sika kple klosalo ɖe wò nudzraɖoƒewo.

english_verse: You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
translation_verse: Etsɔ wò aɖaŋu gã la tsa asii, wò kesinɔnuwo dzi ɖe edzi, eye wò dzi le dàdam le wò kesinɔnuwo ta.”

english_verse: You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God,
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Esi nèle ɖokuiwò kpɔm be yenya nu abe Mawu ene ta la,

english_verse: will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get.
translation_verse: kpɔ ɖa, makplɔ amedzrowo woava dze dziwò, dukɔ siwo sẽa ŋuta ŋutɔŋutɔ; woaɖe woƒe yiwo ɖe wò nunya ƒe nyonyo ŋu eye woagblẽ kɔ ɖo na wò atsyɔ̃.

english_verse: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
translation_verse: Woatu asi wò aƒu yɔme, eye àku abe ame tsiaʋa ene le atsiaƒu titina.

english_verse: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
translation_verse: Ɖe àgagblɔ le ame siwo le wuwòm la ŋkume be: ‘Mawue menye’; togbɔ be amegbetɔ ko nènye, eye mènye mawu o, le ame siwo le abi dem ŋuwò la si mea?

english_verse: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
translation_verse: Àku bolobolotɔwo ƒe ku le amedzrowo ƒe asi me. Elabe Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Nyee gblɔe.” Tiro-fia ƒe anyidzedze

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya gava nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying: At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking.
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, kpa aviha de Tiro-fia nàgblɔ nɛ be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Ŋkɔsigɛ si de blibo heyɔ fũu kple nunya lae nènye, eye nèdze ɖeka wu gbɔgblɔ.

english_verse: You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born.
translation_verse: Ènɔ Eden, Mawu ƒe abɔ la me; kpe xɔasi ɖe sia ɖe nye wò atsyɔ̃ɖonu, karneol, topas kple yaspis, krisolit, soham kple oniks, safir, ametist kple smaragd; wotsɔ sika ɖo wò togawo keŋ, eye wotsɔe do atsyiã vovovowo ɖe ŋuwò. Wowɔ nu siawo le gbe si gbe wowɔ wò.

english_verse: I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
translation_verse: Metsɔ wò ɖo Mawu ƒe to kɔkɔe la dzi le kerubi si wosi ami na wòle nuwo ŋu dzɔm la gbɔ, eye dzokpewo dome nèzɔna.

english_verse: You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things.
translation_verse: Fɔbubu aɖeke menɔ wò zɔzɔme ŋu tso gbe si gbe wowɔ wò la o, va se ɖe esime wokpɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ le mewò.

english_verse: You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
translation_verse: Le wò asitsatsa geɖe la me la ŋutasesẽ yɔ mewò, eye nèwɔ nuvɔ̃; eya tae menyà wò ɖa le Mawu ƒe to kɔkɔe la dzi, abe ame si gblẽ kɔ ɖo la ene, eye kerubi si dzɔa nuwo ŋu la nyà wò do goe tso dzokpeawo dome.

english_verse: It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you.
translation_verse: Dàdagbɔgbɔ va yɔ mewò le wò ɖekadzedze ta; èƒo ɖi wò nunya le ale si nènyakpɔnae ta. Mexlã wò ɖe anyi; mewɔ wò nèzu nukpɔkpɔ na fiawo, ne woakpɔ wò ʋuu wòati ŋku na wò.

english_verse: You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood,
translation_verse: To wò nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ gbogbo siwo nèwɔ la me, le wò asi madzɔmadzɔ tsatsa me la, nègblẽ kɔ ɖo na wò kɔkɔeƒewo. Eya tae metɔ dzo aƒe ɖe dziwò wòfiã wò, eye metrɔ wò nèzu dzowɔ le anyigba dzi le ame siwo katã kpɔ wò la ŋkume.

english_verse: and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever. Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
translation_verse: Wò nu wɔ nublanui na ame siwo katã dze si wò le dukɔwo dome; wò nuwuwu la dziŋɔ ŋutɔŋutɔ, màganɔ anyi akpɔ o.” Gbeƒãɖeɖe ɖe Sidon ŋu

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, trɔ nàdze ŋgɔ Sidon ne nàɖe gbeƒã ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: and tell its people: I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy.
translation_verse: Gblɔ be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: O Sidon, kpɔ ɖa, metso ɖe ŋuwò, eye maɖe nye ŋutikɔkɔe afia le mewò. Woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ, ne medrɔ̃ ʋɔnu le eme, eye meɖe nye ŋutikɔkɔe fia le eme.

english_verse: I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Elabe maɖo dɔ vɔ̃ ɖe eme, eye ʋu anɔ eƒe ablɔwo dzi. Ame siwo wowu la anɔ dua me le yi si wotsɔ ɖe wo ŋu tso akpa sia akpa ta. Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.” Woayra Israel

english_verse: When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. A Blessing for Israel
translation_verse: “Ke le Israel-dukɔ la gome la, ŋu si tɔa ame kple aŋɔka si wɔa nu vevi ame la maganɔ dukɔ siwo katã ƒo xlãe, eye womekpɔa wo ɖe naneke me o la dome o. Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ Mawu.”

english_verse: The Lord God said: Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Ne meƒo Israel-dukɔ la nu ƒu tso dukɔ siwo dome wokaka ɖo la dome, eye meɖe nye ŋutikɔkɔe fia le wo dome le dukɔwo ŋkume la, ekema woanɔ woawo ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba si metsɔ na nye dɔla Yakob la dzi.

english_verse: They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Woanɔ dedie le edzi, eye woatu xɔwo ade waingblewo. Ne medrɔ̃ ʋɔnu ame siwo katã ƒo xlã wo, siwo womekpɔna ɖe naneke me o la, woawo woanɔ anyi bɔkɔɔ. Ekema woadze sii be, nye Aƒetɔ ye nye woƒe Mawu.”

english_verse: Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: Le ƒè ewolia ƒe ɣleti ewolia ƒe ŋkeke wui evelia dzi la, Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, trɔ nàdze ŋgɔ Egipte Fiagã, eye nàɖe gbeƒã ɖe eya kple Egipte blibo la ŋu.

english_verse: that I am saying: King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy!
translation_verse: Ƒo nu nàgblɔ be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, metso ɖe ŋuwò, Egipte Fiagã, ƒumeʋɔdriba gã si mlɔ anyi ɖe eƒe tɔwo me, si gblɔna be: ‘Nye Nil-tɔsisi la, nye ŋutɔ tɔnyee; Nyee wɔe.’

english_verse: I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body.
translation_verse: Matsɔ ƒè aku alɔxatsa me na wò, eye mana tɔmelã siwo le wò tɔwo me la nalé ɖe wò tsrowo ŋu. Mahe wò ado goe tso wò tɔ la me kple wò tɔwo me lã siwo katã lé ɖe wò tsrowo ŋu la.

english_verse: I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh.
translation_verse: Matsɔ wò aƒu gbe ɖe gbedadaƒo, wò kple wò tɔmelãwo katã. Miage adze gbadzaƒe le gbedzi, eye womafɔ mi aƒo ƒu ɖi o. Metsɔ wò na gbemelãwo kple dziƒoxewo be woaɖu.”

english_verse: Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord. You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick.
translation_verse: “Ekema Egiptenɔlawo katã adze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ. Elabe miele abe aƒlati ene na Israel-dukɔ la.

english_verse: When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
translation_verse: Esi wolé wò kple asi la, èŋe hevuvu woƒe abɔtawo, eye esi woziɔ ɖe ŋuwò la, èŋe eye èna woƒe ali ʋuʋu.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock,
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, maɖe yi ɖe dziwò, atsrɔ̃ amegbetɔ kple lã le dziwò.

english_verse: until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things. You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it.
translation_verse: Egipte-nyigba la azu aƒedo kple gbegbe. Ekema woanyae be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.” “Elabe ègblɔ be: ‘Nil-tɔsisi la tɔnyee, eye nyee wɔe’.

english_verse: Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Eya ta kpɔ ɖa, metso ɖe wò kple wò tɔsisiwo ŋu, eye mawɔ Egipte-nyigba la wòazu gbegbe kple aƒedo keŋkeŋ, tso Migdol va se ɖe Siene ava ke ɖe keke Etiopia ƒe liƒo dzi ke.

english_verse: No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for
translation_verse: Amegbetɔ ƒe afɔ loo, alo lã ƒe afɔ mato edzi o; naneke manɔ edzi o, ƒe bla ene.

english_verse: They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom
translation_verse: Magbugbɔ Egiptetɔwo ƒe nunyonamewo aɖo te, eye makplɔ wo va Patros si nye wo denyigba la dzi. Woanye fiaɖuƒe gblɔe aɖe le afi ma.

english_verse: and won't ever be strong enough to rule nations, as they did in the past.
translation_verse: Anye fiaɖuƒe gblɔe kekeake, eye magakɔ eɖokui dzi wu fiaɖuƒewo azɔ o. Mana woanɔ sue ale gbegbe be womagakpɔ ŋusẽ aɖu dukɔwo dzi azɔ o.

english_verse: My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
translation_verse: Womaganye ame siwo ŋu Israel-dukɔ la agaɖo ŋu ɖo azɔ o. Woaɖo ŋku edzi be nuvɔ̃ɖi wònye yewowɔ be yewodi kpekpeɖeŋu tso wo gbɔ. Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ Mawu.” Fia Nebukadnezar aɖu Egipte dzi

english_verse: Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: Le ƒè bla eve vɔ adrẽlia ƒe ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la, Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city.
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar na eƒe aʋakɔ tso hloloe ɖe Tiro ŋu. Wowɔe ʋuu woƒe tawo katã bebe, eye woxɔ abi ɖe abɔta keŋkeŋ. Ke eya ŋutɔ loo, alo eƒe aʋakɔ la mekpɔ fetu aɖeke tso woƒe fukpekpe la me tso Tiro o.

english_verse: So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, matsɔ Egipte ana Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar, eye wòalɔ eƒe kesinɔnuwo adzoe. Aɖe aboyoe, aha eƒe nuwo, eye eyae anye eƒe aʋakɔ la ƒe fetu.

english_verse: Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Metsɔ Egipte-nyigba la nɛ abe eƒe fetu si ta wòwɔ dɔ ɖo la ene. Elabe wowɔ dɔ nam.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: “Gbe ma gbe la, mana Israel ƒe aƒe la nato dzo, eye maʋu nu na wò le wo dome. Ekema woanyae be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying: Cry out in despair,
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, ɖe gbeƒã nàgblɔ be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Fa avi kple ɣli be: ‘Baba na ŋkeke la!’

english_verse: because you will soon be punished! That will be a time of darkness and doom for all nations.
translation_verse: Elabe ŋkeke la gogo, Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋkeke la tu aƒe. Ŋkeke doblukɔ aɖe wòanye, anye ɣeyiɣi si dukɔwo atsrɔ̃.

english_verse: Your own nation of Egypt will be attacked, and Ethiopia will suffer. You will be killed in battle, and your land will be robbed and left in ruins.
translation_verse: Woatsɔ yi ɖe Egipte ŋu, eye veve helihelĩ sese anɔ Etiopia, ne aʋatsilawo mlɔ anyi le Egipte, eye wolɔ eƒe kesinɔnuwo dzoe hegbã eƒe gɔmeɖokpewo.

english_verse: Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle.
translation_verse: Etiopia, Put, Lud, Arabia katã kple Libia kple dukɔ siwo bla nu kpli wo la, woatsi yi nu kpli wo.”

english_verse: All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Ame siwo de megbe na Egipte la, adze anyi, eye eƒe ŋusẽ si dzi wòdàna ɖo la, ayi to tso Migdol va se ɖe Siene. Woatsi yi nu le eme, Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin.
translation_verse: Atrɔ zu aƒedo le anyigba siwo zu aƒedo la dome, eye eƒe duwo anɔ du siwo zu gbegbe la dome.
