english_verse: I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ, nenye be metɔ dzo Egipte, eye eƒe kpeɖeŋutɔwo katã ŋe.”

english_verse: On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
translation_verse: “Gbe ma gbe la, amedɔdɔ siwo anɔ du dzi sesĩe la, atso gbɔnye ayi aɖado ŋɔdzi na Etiopiatɔ siwo aɖe ŋu ɖi la, eye woase veve helihelĩ le Egipte ƒe tsɔtsrɔ̃gbe. Elabe kpɔ ɖa, egbɔna!”

english_verse: Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Mana Egipte ƒe kesinɔnuwo navɔ, to Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar ƒe asi dzi.

english_verse: He and his cruel troops will invade and destroy your land and leave your dead bodies piled everywhere.
translation_verse: Eya kple eƒe dukɔ, ame siwo doa ŋɔdzi na ame la, woakplɔ wo vɛ be woava tsrɔ̃ anyigba la. Woaɖe woƒe yiwo ɖe Egipte ŋu, eye anyigba la ayɔ fũu kple ame tsiaʋawo.

english_verse: I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
translation_verse: Mana Nil-tɔsisi la namie keŋkeŋ, eye madzra anyigba la na ame vɔ̃ɖiwo. Mana anyigba la kple nu sia nu si le edzi la nazu aƒedo, to amedzrowo ƒe asi dzi. Nye Aƒetɔ ye ƒo nu.”

english_verse: All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Magbã legbawo, eye maɖe mawu siwo miemè le Memfis la ɖa. Amegã aɖeke maganɔ Egipte-nyigba dzi azɔ o, ale mana vɔvɔ̃ nanɔ Egipte-nyigba la dzi.

english_verse: The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
translation_verse: Matrɔ nye dɔmedzoe akɔ ɖe Pelusium si nye Egipte ƒe mɔ́ sesẽ la dzi, eye malã ame gbogbo siwo le Tebes la ɖa.

english_verse: I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear.
translation_verse: Matɔ dzo Egipte; Pelusium anɔ vevesese gã ŋutɔ me. Woagbã Tebes, eye eƒe gliwo agbã.

english_verse: The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner.
translation_verse: Ɖekakpuiwo le On kple Pibeset atsi yi nu, eye woakplɔ nyɔnuwo ayi aboyo mee.

english_verse: You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity.
translation_verse: Viviti ado le ŋkeke me le Taxpanxes, ne meŋe alɔ na Egipte ƒe dziɖuɖu le afi ma, eye mena ŋusẽ si wotsɔ ƒoa adegbee la nu tso. Alilikpo ado blukɔ ɖe edzi, eye via nyɔnuviwo ayi aboyo me.

english_verse: When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord. Egypt's King Is Powerless
translation_verse: Aleae maɖo kodzo kple Egipte nye esi. Ekema woanyae be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.” Egipte-fia ƒe ŋusẽ si woŋe la

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: Le ƒè wui ɖekɛlia ƒe ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke adrẽa gbe la, Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword.
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, meŋe Egipte Fiagã ƒe alɔ, eye kpɔ ɖa, womeblae nɛ, ne woaɖo eme nɛ, ale be wòate ŋu alé yi ada o.

english_verse: So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever,
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, metso ɖe Egipte Fiagã ŋu, eye maŋe alɔ nɛ, esi sesẽ kple esi ŋe xoxo la. Mawɔe be yi nage le esi.

english_verse: and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
translation_verse: Makaka Egiptetɔwo ɖe dukɔwo dome, eye mana woaka hlẽ ɖe anyigbawo dzi.

english_verse: I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mado ŋusẽ Babilon-fia ƒe alɔ, ke Egipte Fiagã ƒe alɔ age le eŋu. Woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ. Nenye be metsɔ nye yi de asi na Babilon-fia la, aɖee ɖe Egipte-nyigba la ŋu.

english_verse: I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_verse: Makaka Egiptetɔwo ɖe dukɔwo dome, eye maka wo ahlẽ ɖe anyigbawo dzi. Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
translation_verse: Le ƒe wui ɖekɛlia me, le ɣleti etɔ̃lia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la, Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying: You are more powerful than anyone on earth. Now listen to this.
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, gblɔ na Egipte Fiagã kple etevi gbogboawo be: Wò kple ame kae sɔ le wò gãnyenye me?

english_verse: There was once a cedar tree in Lebanon with large, strong branches reaching to the sky.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, matsɔ wò asɔ ɖe sederti ŋu le Lebanon. Wò alɔwo nyo, èkɔ de dzi hewɔ ave, do vɔvɔli. Wò ɖɔme de alilikpowo me ke.

english_verse: This tree had plenty of water to help it grow tall, and nearby streams watered the other trees in the forest.
translation_verse: Tsiwo na wòtsi, kpɔ ŋusẽ, eƒe kewo ƒe toyiyi na wòkɔ. Ena eƒe tsiwo tsa ƒo xlã afi si wodoe ɖo. Ena tɔʋuwo sí de avemetiwo katã gbɔ.

english_verse: But this tree towered over those other trees, and its branches grew long and thick.
translation_verse: Ale wòkɔ de dzi wu avemetiwo katã. Eƒe alɔwo tri, eye wòɖe alɔ de didiƒe, esi tsi te eƒe ke me nyuie ta.

english_verse: Birds built nests in its branches, and animals were born beneath it. People from all nations lived in the shade of this strong tree.
translation_verse: Dziƒoxeviwo katã wɔ atɔ ɖe eƒe alɔwo me. Gbemelãwo katã dzi vi ɖe eƒe alɔwo te, eye dukɔ gãwo katã nɔ eƒe vɔvɔli te.

english_verse: It had beautiful, long branches, and its roots found water deep in the soil.
translation_verse: Eƒe lolome nyakpɔ; eɖe alɔwo yi didiƒe. Elabe eƒe kewo de to kpɔ tsi fũu ŋutɔ.

english_verse: None of the cedar trees in my garden of Eden were as beautiful as this tree; no tree of any kind had such long branches.
translation_verse: Sederti siwo le Mawu ƒe abɔ me mate ŋu ake ɖi kplii loo, alo sesewu ƒe alɔwo nate ɖe eŋu o. Xetiwo meɖe alɔ abe eya ene o; ati aɖeke medze ani le Mawu ƒe abɔ me de enu o.

english_verse: I, the Lord, gave this tree its beauty, and I helped the branches grow strong. All other trees in Eden wanted to be just like it.
translation_verse: Nyee wɔe wònyakpɔ le alɔ geɖe si wòɖe la ta, ale ati gbogbo siwo katã le Mawu ƒe abɔ me le Eden la ʋã ŋui.”

english_verse: King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree: The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Esi wòkɔ hede dzi, eye eƒe ɖɔme ɖatɔ alilikpowo, wòzu dàda nɛ le dzime ta la,

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness.
translation_verse: matsɔe ade asi na ŋusẽtɔ aɖe le dukɔwo dome. Eya atu nu kplii kokoko wòade ale si wò vɔ̃ɖii la nu. Metsɔe ƒu gbe.

english_verse: Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else.
translation_verse: Amedzro siwo dzi ŋɔ wu le dukɔwo dome lae atsoe ƒu anyi, adzo le egbɔ. Eƒe alɔwo adze towo dzi kple baliwo katã me. Eƒe alɔ gãtɔwo afli atsi tɔʋuwo katã me le anyigba la dzi, eye anyigba dzi dukɔwo katã adzo le eƒe vɔvɔli te, agblẽe ɖi.

english_verse: Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
translation_verse: Dziƒoxeviwo katã ava dze ɖe atitakpo la nu, eye gbemelãwo katã ava mlɔ alɔawo dzi.

english_verse: Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Nu siawo katã awɔe be ati siwo le tɔ to la ƒe ɖeke magakɔ ade dzi bobobo ne eƒe ɖɔme naɖatɔ alilikpowo o, eye ati siwo kpɔ tsi nyuie la ƒe ɖeke magakɔ ade enu o. Elabe wo katã wodzɔ na ku, dzɔ na agbe. Wole yɔme yi ge kple amegbetɔ siwo yi aʋlime la.”

english_verse: On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Ne eyi tsiẽƒe la, mana agume nafà nɛ. Eƒe tɔsisiwo masí o, eye tsi geɖewo nu atso. Mata avɔ yibɔ na Lebanon le eta, eye gbemetiwo katã ayrɔ le eta.

english_verse: This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble. The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls.
translation_verse: Mana dukɔwo nadzo nyànyanya le eƒe anyidzedze si ɖi la ta. Ne meɖoe ɖe tsiẽƒe kpe ɖe ame siwo yi aʋlime la ŋu, eye ati siwo le Eden kple ati tiatia nyuitɔwo kekeake le Lebanon, esiwo katã noa tsi la, woakpɔ akɔfafa le yɔme.

english_verse: Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
translation_verse: Woawo hã woayi tsiẽƒe kplii. Woayi ame siwo tsi yi nu le aʋa me la gbɔ. Ẽ, ame siwo nɔ eƒe vɔvɔli te le dukɔwo dome la atsrɔ̃.

english_verse: King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ame kae sɔ kplii le lolome kple atsyɔ̃ me le ati siwo le Eden la dome? Woatutu wò akpe ɖe ati siwo le Eden la ŋu aɖo ɖe yɔme. Mia kple bolobolotɔwoe amlɔ teƒe ɖeka kpe ɖe ame siwo tsi yi nu le aʋa me la ŋu.” “Egipte Fiagã sia kple etevi gbogboawo ƒe nyae nye esia.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
translation_verse: Le ƒe wui ɖekɛlia ƒe ɣleti wui evelia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la, Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying: You act like a lion roaming the earth; but you are nothing more than a crocodile in a river, churning up muddy water with your feet.
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, kpa aviha de Egipte Fiagã be: Èbu ɖokuiwò abe dzata ene le dukɔwo dome, ke èle abe ƒumeʋɔdriba ene le atsiaƒu me; ètua tsi to ŋɔti me, nyaa avuzi le tɔ me kple wò afɔwo, eye nèblua tsi.

english_verse: King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Maɖo nye ɖɔ na wò; dukɔ geɖewo akpe ɖe ŋunye, eye mahe wò kple nye ɖɔ ava gotae.

english_verse: I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh.
translation_verse: Maxlã wò ɖe anyi, gbadzaƒee mada wò ɖo, eye mana dziƒoxeviwo katã nadze ɖe dziwò. Mana anyigbadzilãwo katã naho wò lã.

english_verse: I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys,
translation_verse: Matsɔ wò lã kakɛwo aƒu gbe ɖe towo dzi, eye mana wò kukua nayɔ baliwo me.

english_verse: and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams.
translation_verse: Mana anyigba la kple towo kekeake, naƒo wò ʋu si le sisím la, eye wòayɔ tɔsisiwo me taŋ.

english_verse: I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining.
translation_verse: Ne meɖe wò ɖa la, matsyɔ avɔ na dziŋgɔli, eye mana woƒe ɣletiviwo nado viviti. Mana alilikpo naxe ɣe ŋkume, eye ɣleti magaɖi o.

english_verse: The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mana dziŋgɔli me nu siwo katã klẽna le ta wò me la natsi, eye mana viviti nado ɖe wò anyigba dzi.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you.
translation_verse: “Maɖe fu na dukɔ geɖewo ƒe dziwo, ne mekplɔ mi yi aboyo me le dukɔwo dome, le anyigba siwo mienya o la dzi.

english_verse: They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
translation_verse: Mana miaƒe nu nawɔ nublanui na ame geɖewo, eye woƒe fiawo nanɔ dzodzom nyànyanya le mia ta, ne menyè nye yi le wo ŋkume. Woanɔ ƒoƒom tititi ɣeawo katã ɣi, ame sia ame le eya ŋutɔ ƒe agbe ta, gbe si gbe nèdze anyi.

english_verse: The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt!
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Babilon-fia ƒe yi aƒo ɖe dziwò.

english_verse: Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed.
translation_verse: Mana ame gbogbo siwo le asiwò la natsi ŋusẽtɔwo ƒe yi nu, ame siwo katã ŋu ŋɔdzi le le dukɔwo dome.” “Woana Egipte nadzudzɔ dàda, eye eƒe ame gbogboawo atsrɔ̃.

english_verse: I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water.
translation_verse: Matsrɔ̃ eƒe gbemelãwo katã ɖa le tɔ geɖewo to; amegbetɔ aɖeke ƒe afɔ magablu wo azɔ loo, alo gbemelã aɖeke ƒe afɔ nablu wo o.

english_verse: The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Emegbe mana woƒe tsiwo nazrɔ̃, eye mana woƒe tɔsisiwo nasí abe ami ene. Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ne mena Egipte-nyigba zu aƒedo, eye megblẽ edzi nuwo katã, ne mewu edzinɔlawo katã la, ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. A Sad Ending for Egypt
translation_verse: Konyifahae nye esia woado ɖa; dukɔwo ƒe nyɔnuviwo adzii. Woadzii na Egipte kple eƒe dumevi gbogboawo, woawoe woadzii na. Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.” Ame kukuwo de

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of that same month, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Le ƒe wui evelia ƒe ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke wui atɔ̃a gbe la, Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations.
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, fa avi ɖe Egipte ƒe ame gbogboawo ŋu, eye nàkplɔ wo ɖo ɖa, eya kple fia gãwo ƒe vinyɔnuviwo miaɖo ɖe yɔme le aʋlimeyilawo gbɔ.

english_verse: You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you.
translation_verse: Woaɖamlɔ ame siwo tsi yi nu le aʋa me la dome, eye eƒe ameha gbogboawo katã amlɔ exa.

english_verse: Brave military leaders killed in battle will gladly welcome you and your allies into the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Fia siwo kpɔ ŋusẽ kple woƒe kpeɖeŋutɔwo agblɔ le tsiẽƒe tso wo ŋu be: ‘Wova ɖo yɔme, womlɔ anyi kpoo, bolobolotɔ siwo wowu kple yi la.’ ”

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Woɖe yɔdo nɛ ɖe dzogoe dzi ke le aʋlime, eye eƒe amehawo ƒo xlã eƒe yɔdo. Wo katã la, aʋatsilawo wonye, woawoe do ŋɔdzi na agbagbeawo kpɔ le anyigba dzi.”

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
translation_verse: Woɖo aba nɛ ɖe ame tsiaʋawo dome kple eƒe amehawo katã. Woƒe yɔdowo ƒo xlãe, wo katã nye bolobolotɔ siwo tsi aʋa. Woawoe do ŋɔdzi na agbagbeawo kpɔ le anyigba dzi, eye woayi aʋlime kple ŋukpe akpe ɖe kukuawo ŋu. Woatsɔ wo amlɔ aʋatsilawo dome.”

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Mesex kple Tubal le afi ma kple woƒe ameha gbogboawo. Woƒe yɔdowo ƒo xlã wo. Wo katã wonye bolobolotɔwo, ame siwo tsi yi nu elabe woƒe ŋɔdzidoname xɔ agbagbeawo ƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
translation_verse: Womemlɔ blema kalẽtɔ siwo tsi aʋa, eye woyi tsiẽƒe kple woƒe aʋawɔnu siwo wotsɔ wɔ kɔziɔe la gbɔ o, ame siwo ƒe akpoxɔnuwo mlɔ woƒe ƒuwo dzi. Elabe ŋɔdzidoname kple kalẽwɔwɔ la, agbe me ko wole.

english_verse: You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
translation_verse: Ale woagbã wò hã, eye àmlɔ bolobolotɔwo gbɔ le aʋatsilawo dome.”

english_verse: The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Edom le afi ma kple eƒe fia kpakple amegãwo, wo ame siwo sẽ ŋutɔŋutɔ la. Woawo hã mlɔ aʋatsilawo dome, le bolobolotɔwo dome kple aʋlimeyilawo.”

english_verse: The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Amegã siwo tso dzigbeme la le afi ma. Wo katã kple Sidontɔwo katã, ame siwo yi yɔme kple ŋukpe kple aʋatsilawo. Elabe le ŋɔdzi siwo katã wodo na amewo kple woƒe ŋusẽ megbe la, womlɔ anyi aʋamatsomatsoe kple aʋatsilawo, eye wolé ŋukpe ɖe ta yi kple aʋlimeyilawo.”

english_verse: The Lord God says: When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering.
translation_verse: “Nenye be Egipte Fiagã kpɔ wo la, afa akɔ na eɖokui ɖe eƒe ameha gbogboawo ta, Egipte Fiagã la kple eƒe aʋakɔwo katã, ame siwo tsi yi nu. Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Elabe edo ŋɔdzi geɖe na amegbetɔwo le agbe me ŋutɔ. Eya ta woatsɔ Egipte Fiagã la kple eƒe ame gbogboawo amlɔ bolobolotɔwo dome, le ame siwo tsi yi nu la gbɔ.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming.
translation_verse: eye nenye wòkpɔ be wotsɔ yi ɖe anyigba la ŋu, eye wòku kpẽ hena nyanya dukɔa la,

english_verse: Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
translation_verse: Womagaɖo ŋku nuvɔ̃ɖi siwo wòwɔ va yi la ƒe ɖeke dzi o; eva wɔ se dzi kple nu si le eteƒe. Eya ta atsi agbe godoo.”

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
translation_verse: Le ƒe wui evelia ƒe ɣleti ewolia ƒe ŋkeke atɔ̃a gbe la, ŋutsu aɖe si sí tso Yerusalem la va gbɔnye va gblɔ nam be: “Wogbã du la.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying: Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, ƒo nu na wò dukɔmeviwo be: Ne metsɔ yi ɖe anyigba aɖe ŋu, eye dukɔa me viwo tia wo dometɔ ɖeka be wòanye dua ŋu dzɔla,

english_verse: If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
translation_verse: Ese kpẽkuku, eye metsɔ ɖeke le eme o; eƒe ʋu anɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe ta dzi. Ke ne esee, eye wòɖe afɔ ɖe edzi la, atsi agbe.

english_verse: But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Ke ne dua ŋu dzɔla kpɔ be wotsɔ yi ɖe dukɔ la ŋu gbɔna, eye wògbe meku kpẽ be yeana amewo nanya o, ne wova dze wo dzi, eye wowu wo dometɔ aɖe la, wowui ɖe eƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ me. Ke mabia eƒe ʋu tso dua ŋu dzɔla la si me.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me.
translation_verse: “Eya ta wò amegbetɔ vi, wòe nye Israel-dukɔ la ŋu dzɔla. Ne èse nya aɖe tso nunye me la, nàgbe nya na wo nam.

english_verse: When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Ne megblɔ na ame vɔ̃ɖi be: Wò ame vɔ̃ɖi, èle kuku ge godoo. Ke mèke nu gbe nya na ame vɔ̃ɖi la be wòatrɔ agbenɔnɔ o la, ame vɔ̃ɖi ma aku ɖe eƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ me. Ke mabia eƒe ʋu tso asiwò me.

english_verse: If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent. The Lord Is Always Fair (Ezekiel
translation_verse: Gake ne ègbe nya na ame vɔ̃ɖi be netrɔ agbenɔnɔ, eye wògbe tɔtrɔ la, aku ɖe eƒe nuvɔ̃ me. Ke wò la, atsi agbe.” Ame sia ame ana akɔnta le eƒe dɔdeasi ŋu

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Ne nu dzɔdzɔe wɔla trɔ le nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ gbɔ hewɔ nuvɔ̃ la, eƒe kue wòaku.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.”
translation_verse: “Ke wò amegbetɔ vi ya la, wò dukɔmevi siwo tɔ ɖe gliwo ŋu kple xɔwo ƒe ʋɔtruwo nu la, le nu ƒom le ŋuwò. Wole gbɔgblɔm le wo nɔewo dome, ame sia be, ame kemɛ hã be: ‘Miva se nya si tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ na mí la ɖa.’

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me.
translation_verse: “Azɔ wò amegbetɔ vi, gblɔ na Israel-dukɔ la be miele gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Míaƒe dzidadawo kple nuvɔ̃wo zu agba ɖe mía dzi hele mía wum. Ale ke míawɔ atsi agbe?’

english_verse: Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na wo be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Zi ale si mele agbe la, nyemekpɔa dzidzɔ le ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe ku ŋu o, ke boŋ be ame vɔ̃ɖi natrɔ agbenɔnɔ ne wòatsi agbe. Mitrɔ, mitrɔ tso miaƒe mɔ vɔ̃wo dzi. O Israel-dukɔ, nu ka tae miele ku dim?

english_verse: Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
translation_verse: Azɔ wò amegbetɔ vi, gblɔ na wò dukɔmetɔwo be: Ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ mate ŋu aɖee, ne eda se dzi o. Ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ matsrɔ̃e, ne etrɔ tso eƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ gbɔ o. Ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ mate ŋu ana wòanɔ agbe, ne ewɔ nuvɔ̃ o.

english_verse: Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be megblɔ be nu dzɔdzɔe wɔla atsi agbe godoo hã la, ne eka ɖe eƒe nu dzɔdzɔe si wòwɔna la dzi eye wòwɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi la, womaɖo ŋku eƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ aɖeke dzi o. Ke nuvɔ̃ɖi si wòwɔ la mee wòaku ɖo.

english_verse: Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be megagblɔ na ame si wɔa nuvɔ̃ɖi be: ‘Àku godoo’ hã la, ne etrɔ tso eƒe nuvɔ̃ me hewɔ nuteƒe kple se dzi,

english_verse: For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live.
translation_verse: nenye be ame sia trɔa awɔbanu si wòxɔ la ɖoa eteƒe, ne eda adzo ame aɖe wògbugbɔ nua na nutɔ hezɔ ɖe agbemeɖoɖowo nu, gbe nu le nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ gbɔ la, atsi agbe godoo, maku o.

english_verse: Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair.
translation_verse: “Gake mia detɔwo be: ‘Aƒetɔ la mele nu dzɔdzɔe wɔm o’; evɔ wònye woawo ŋutɔe mewɔa nu dzɔdzɔe o hafi.

english_verse: And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Ne ame vɔ̃ɖi trɔ tso eƒe vɔɖivɔ̃ɖinyenye me, eye wòzɔ ɖe se nu hewɔ nuteƒe la, atsi agbe le eta.

english_verse: But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done. The News of Jerusalem's Fall
translation_verse: Ke miawo miebe: ‘Aƒetɔ la mele nu dzɔdzɔe wɔm o.’ Ao, Israel-dukɔ, madrɔ̃ ʋɔnu mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ɖe eƒe nuwɔna nu.” Woɖe gbeƒã be Yerusalem agbã

english_verse: The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak. What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe asi va dzinye le fiẽ si do ŋgɔ na ame si sí aʋa va gbɔnye la ƒe vava. Ena nye nu ʋu le esi amea va ɖo gbɔnye le ŋdi. Ale woʋu nu nam, eye nyemeganye mumu o.” Dukɔ la ƒe nuvɔ̃wo

english_verse: Then the Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, ame siwo tsi aƒedo me le glikpo siawo dzi le Israel-nyigba la dzi la le gbɔgblɔm kokoko be: ‘Abraham la, ame ɖeka ko wònye, gake exɔ anyigba la. Ke esi míawo míesɔ gbɔ la, ɖikeke aɖeke mele eme o, be wotsɔ anyigba la na mí wòzu mía tɔ.’

english_verse: So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying: How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder
translation_verse: Eya ta gblɔe na wo be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Miele lã mumu si me ʋu le la ɖum. Miaƒe ŋkuwo le miaƒe legbawo ŋu, eye miele ʋu kɔm ɖi. Ɖe anyigba la aganye mia tɔa?

english_verse: and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
translation_verse: Miele gogom ɖe miaƒe yiwo ŋu, miele ŋunyɔnuwo wɔm, eye mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe dea asi ehavi srɔ̃ ŋu. Ɖe anyigba la aganye mia tɔa?

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases.
translation_verse: Gblɔ nya sia na wo be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Zi ale si mele agbe la, ava eme godoo be ame siwo tsi aƒedo me le glikpo dzi la, atsi yi nu. Ame siwo le gbedzi la, matsɔ wo na gbemelãwo woaɖu, eye ame siwo le mɔ́ sesẽwo kple agadowo me la, dɔ vɔ̃ awu wo.

english_verse: I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them.
translation_verse: Mana anyigba la nazu aƒedo kple gbegbe, eye eƒe ŋusẽ si ta wòle dàdam ɖo la nu atsi. Israel-towo azu aƒedo ale gbegbe be ame aɖeke magato afi ma o.

english_verse: I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord. The People Listen, but Don't Change The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ, nenye be mewɔ anyigba la wòzu aƒedo kple gbegbe le woƒe ŋunyɔnu siwo katã wowɔ la ta.” Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela la ƒe gbedeasi la metsonuwo

english_verse: So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money.
translation_verse: Wova gbɔwò abe dukɔ ene. Wova nɔ ŋkuwò me abe nye dukɔ ene, eye wose nu si nègblɔ na wo; gake womele edzi wɔ ge o. Elabe wovivia nu me na wo ɖokui be yewolɔ̃a ame, ke woƒe dzi ku ɖe woƒe viɖekpɔkpɔ ŋu.

english_verse: They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, wò la, èle na wò ko abe ame si si gbe vivi le, wònya saŋkuƒoƒo, eye wòle lɔlɔ̃ha dzim na wo la ene. Elabe wose nu si nègblɔ la, gake womele edzi wɔ ge o.

english_verse: Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_verse: Ne nya sia va eme, abe ale si wòle eme va gee kokoko ene la, ekema woava dze sii be Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela aɖe nɔ wo dome kpɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them: I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep.
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, ɖe gbeƒã ɖe Israel ƒe alẽkplɔlawo ŋu. Ɖe gbeƒã, gblɔe na wo, gblɔ na alẽkplɔlawo gɔ̃ hã be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Ao, Israel ƒe alẽkplɔlawo, mia ɖokui ko nyim miele ɖe! Ɖe medze be alẽkplɔlawo nanyi woƒe alẽwo oa?

english_verse: You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock!
translation_verse: Mieɖu lãmiwo, mietsɔ lãfu tɔ awui do, miewu lã damiwo. Ke miegbe alẽawo nyinyi.

english_verse: You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep.
translation_verse: Miedo ŋusẽ lã siwo gbɔdzɔ la o. Mieda gbe le esiwo dze dɔ la ŋu o. Miebla ataŋeŋetɔwo ƒe atawo na wo o. Mietrɔ esiwo tra mɔ la va lãkpɔ me o. Miedi esiwo bu la o. Ke mietsɔ dzizizi kple ŋutasesẽ ɖu wo dzii.

english_verse: They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals.
translation_verse: Ale woka wo hlẽ, elabe kplɔla mele wo ŋu o. Wozu nuɖuɖu na gbemelãwo katã.

english_verse: So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
translation_verse: Woka nye alẽawo hlẽ; wotsa tsa glãla le towo katã kple togbɛwo keŋ dzi. Woka nye alẽawo hlẽ ɖe anyigba ɖe sia ɖe dzi. Ame aɖeke meli si abia wo ta se ahayi wo di ge o.”

english_verse: Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Zi ale si mele agbe la, esi nye alẽawo zu nuléle kple nuɖuɖu na lã wɔadãwo elabe alẽkplɔla aɖeke mele wo si o, eye esi nye alẽkplɔlawo medi nye alẽawo o, gake alẽkplɔlawo nyi wo ɖokui hegbe nye alẽawo nyinyi ta la,

english_verse: So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, metso ɖe alẽkplɔlawo ŋu, eye mabia nye alẽawo ƒe akɔnta tso wo si me, eye mana woadzudzɔ nye alẽawo nyinyi. Alẽkplɔlaawo magakpɔ wo ɖokui dzi azɔ o. Maɖe nye alẽawo le woƒe nu me, be womaganye woƒe nuɖuɖu azɔ o.” Alẽkplɔla nyui la

english_verse: The Lord God then said: I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself,
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Kpɔ ɖa, nye, nye ŋutɔ madi nye alẽwo, eye mati mɔ na wo.

english_verse: just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them
translation_verse: Abe ale si alẽkplɔla dia eƒe alẽwoe nenye be wo dometɔ aɖewo kaka ɖe gbedzi ene la, nenemae madi nye alẽwoe, eye maɖe wo tso teƒe siwo katã wokaka ɖo le blukɔ kple tsizidogbe.

english_verse: and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields.
translation_verse: Makplɔ wo tso dukɔwo dome, eye maƒo wo nu ƒu tso anyigbawo dzi. Makplɔ wo va woawo ŋutɔ denyigba dzi, anyi wo le Israel ƒe towo dzi le tsi dzidziwo gbɔ kple toƒe siwo katã nye amenɔƒewo le anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: I promise to take care of them and keep them safe,
translation_verse: Nye ŋutɔ manye nye alẽawo kplɔla. Mana woatsyɔ akɔ ɖi kpoo. Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right. Judgment on the Strong Sheep
translation_verse: Madi esiwo bu la, eye esiwo tra mɔ la, makplɔ wo va kpɔ me. Esiwo ƒe ata ŋe la, mablae na wo, eye mado ŋusẽ esiwo gbɔdzɔ la. Makpɔ esiwo da ami kple esiwo ŋu ŋusẽ le la ta. Manyi wo kple ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ dzɔdzɔe.”

english_verse: The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel: I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Kpɔ ɖa, mi ame siwo nye nye alẽha la, madrɔ̃ ʋɔnu le alẽ kple alẽ dome, le agbo kple gbɔ̃tsu dome.

english_verse: Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy.
translation_verse: Ɖe menyo na mi be mieɖu gbe le gbeɖuƒe nyui o tae, mienya avuzi le miaƒe gbe mamlɛawo dzia? Alo ɖe medze mia ŋu be mieno tsi zɔzrɔ̃e o tae, mieblu miaƒe tsi mamlɛa kple miaƒe afɔwoa?

english_verse: That means my other sheep have nothing fit to eat or drink.
translation_verse: Ɖe wòle be nye alẽwo naɖu gbe siwo mietugu kple afɔ, eye woano tsi si mieblu kple miaƒe afɔwoa?”

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will separate you strong sheep from the weak.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Kpɔ ɖa, nye, nye ŋutɔ madrɔ̃ ʋɔnu le alẽ dami kple alẽ ɖiku dome.

english_verse: You strong ones have used your powerful horns to chase off those that are weak,
translation_verse: Esi mieɖo ŋui lã kudɔewo kple abɔgba, tu dzo wo, va se ɖe esime mienya wo de gbe la,

english_verse: but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
translation_verse: eya ta maxɔ na nye alẽha la, ale be womaganye nuléle azɔ o. Madrɔ̃ ʋɔnu le alẽ kple alẽ dome.

english_verse: After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you.
translation_verse: Matsɔ alẽkplɔla ɖeka, nye dɔla David, aɖo wo nu, eye eyae anyi wo: Akpɔ wo ta, eye wòanye woƒe alẽkplɔla.

english_verse: He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Nye Aƒetɔ, manye woƒe Mawu, eye nye dɔla David anye amegã le wo dome. Nye Aƒetɔ ye ƒo nu.”

english_verse: The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid.
translation_verse: “Mabla ŋutifafa nu kpli wo, eye manyà lã wɔadãwo katã ɖa le anyigba la dzi. Ale be woanɔ dedie le gbegbe, eye woatsi avewo me adɔ.

english_verse: They will live around my holy mountain, and I will bless them by sending more than enough rain
translation_verse: Mayra wo kple teƒe siwo ƒo xlã nye togbɛ la. Mana agbafie nadza na wo ɖe ɣeyiɣi dzi. Yayragbafie wòanye adza.

english_verse: to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Gbemetiwo atse ku, eye anyigba awɔ nu, amewo anɔ dedie le woƒe anyigba dzi. Woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ, ne meŋe woƒe kɔkuti, eye meɖe wo tso ame siwo wɔ wo kluviwoe la si me.

english_verse: Foreign nations will never again rob them, and wild animals will no longer kill and eat them. They will have nothing to fear.
translation_verse: Womaganye nuléle na dukɔwo azɔ loo, alo anyigba la dzi gbemelãwo navuvu wo o. Woanɔ dedie, ame aɖeke magado vɔvɔ̃ na wo azɔ o.

english_verse: I will make their fields produce large amounts of crops, so they will never again go hungry or be laughed at by foreigners.
translation_verse: Mana agbledeƒe wɔnuwo naɖo wo si, ne dɔwuame nagatsrɔ̃ wo ɖa le anyigba la dzi azɔ o, eye dukɔwo magaɖe alɔ me le wo ŋu o.

english_verse: Then everyone will know that I protect my people Israel. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: Woadze sii be, nye Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la, meli kpli wo. Woawo Israel-dukɔ lae nye nye dukɔ. Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: They are my sheep; I am their God, and I take care of them.
translation_verse: Azɔ miawoe nye nye alẽwo, alẽ siwo le nye lãnyiƒe, eye nyee nye mia Mawu.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Edom
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, trɔ mo ɖe Seir-to ŋu, eye nàɖe gbeƒã ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: and say to them: I, the Lord God, am now your enemy! And I will turn your nation into an empty wasteland,
translation_verse: Gblɔ nɛ be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, Seir-to, metsi tre ɖe ŋuwò, eye maɖe alɔka me ɖe ŋuwò. Mawɔ wò nàzu gbegbe kple aƒedo.

english_verse: leaving your towns in ruins. Your land will be a desert, and then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mana wò duwo nazu aƒedo, eye nàtrɔ zu gbegbe, eye àdze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: People of Edom, not only have you been Israel's longtime enemy, you simply watched when disaster wiped out its people as punishment for their sins.
translation_verse: Esi fuléle ame ɖikaɖika doa dzidzɔ na wò, eye nètsɔ Israel-dukɔ la de asi na ame siwo kpɔ ŋusẽ tsɔ yi ɖe wo ŋu, esi dzɔgbevɔ̃e dzɔ ɖe wo dzi le ɣeyiɣi mamlɛ si me wohe to na wo ta la,

english_verse: And so, as surely as I am the living Lord God, you are guilty of murder and must be put to death.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Zi ale si mele agbe la, mana nànɔ mɔ kpɔm na ʋu, eye ʋue anɔ yowòme. Elabe èkɔ ʋu ɖi, eye ʋue akplɔ wò ɖo.

english_verse: I will destroy your nation and kill anyone who travels through it.
translation_verse: Mana Seir-to la nazu gbegbe kple aƒedo, eye matsrɔ̃ ame siwo vana gadzona la ɖa le edzi.

english_verse: and your land will lie in ruins forever. No one will live in your towns ever again. You will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mawɔ wò nàzu gbegbe ɖikaa, eye wò duwo azu aƒedo. Ekema miadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: You thought the nations of Judah and Israel belonged to you, and that you could take over their territory. But I am their God,
translation_verse: “Esi nègblɔ be: ‘Ye tɔe nye dukɔ eve siawo, eye anyigba eve siawo anye ye tɔ, eye míaxɔe woanye mía tɔ’, evɔ wònye Aƒetɔ nɔ afi ma kpɔ hafi la,

english_verse: and as surely as I live, I will punish you for treating my people with anger and hatred. Then they will know that I, the Lord, am punishing you!
translation_verse: eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Zi ale si mele agbe la, matu nu kpli wò le dɔmedzoe kple ŋuʋaʋã si meɖe fia le esime nèlé fu wo ta. Maɖe ɖokuinye afia le mia dome, ne meva drɔ̃ ʋɔnu mi,

english_verse: And you will finally realize that I heard you laugh at their destruction and say their land was yours to take.
translation_verse: eye mia dze sii be nye Aƒetɔ, mese nya siwo mietsɔ ɖi gbɔ Israel-towo hegblɔ be: ‘Wowɔ wo wozu gbegbe; wotsɔ wo na mí be míavuvu.’

english_verse: You even insulted me, but I heard it all.
translation_verse: Miewɔ nu me, kɔ mia ɖokui dzi ɖe ŋunye. Mieƒo nu le ŋunye kpaŋkpaŋ. Mesee.

english_verse: Everyone on earth will celebrate when I destroy you,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Mawɔ wò nàzu gbegbe be anyigba blibo la katã natso aseye.

english_verse: just as you celebrated when Israel was destroyed. Your nation of Edom will be nothing but a wasteland. Then everyone will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Abe ale si nèkpɔ dzidzɔ be yenyi Israel-dukɔ la dome, elabe ezu gbegbe ene la, nenema ke mawɔe na wòe. Àzu gbegbe; Seir-to kple Edom blibo la katã woazu gbegbe. Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the mountains of Israel
translation_verse: “Azɔ wò amegbetɔ vi, ɖe gbeƒã ɖo ɖe Israel-towo, eye nàgblɔ be: Mi Israel-towo, mise Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe.

english_verse: that I, the Lord God, am saying: Your enemies sneered and said that you mountains belonged to them.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Esi futɔ la gblɔ le ŋuwò be: ‘Ehɛ̃! Azɔ blema kɔkɔƒeawo va trɔ zu mía tɔ’

english_verse: So all you mountains and hills, streams and valleys, listen to what I will do. Your towns may now lie in ruins, and nations may laugh and insult you.
translation_verse: Eya ta mi Israel-towo, mise Aƒetɔ Mawu ƒe nya: Aƒetɔ Mawu gblɔ ɖo ɖe towo kple togbɛwo, baliwo kple agatowo, aƒedo siwo zu glikpowo, du ƒuƒlu siwo me ame sí dzo le, eye wozu nuhaha. Du siwo katã trɔ zu kokoe na dukɔ mamlɛ siwo ƒo xlã wo godoo la.

english_verse: But in my fierce anger, I will turn against those nations, and especially the Edomites, because they laughed at you the loudest and took over your pasturelands.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Maƒo nu kple ŋuʋaʋã xɔdzo la atsi tre ɖe dukɔ mamlɛawo ŋu, ɖe Edom katã ŋu, ame siwo tsɔ nye anyigba wɔ wo ɖokui tɔe kple dzidzɔ blibo, ame makpɔɖenanekemetɔe, ale be woawɔe wòazu wo tɔ, eye woahae.

english_verse: so I will now insult and disgrace them. That is my solemn promise.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Mele atam kam be dukɔ siwo ƒo xlã wò la ŋutɔe aɖu ŋukpe.”

english_verse: Trees will grow on you mountains of Israel and produce fruit for my people, because they will soon come home.
translation_verse: “Ke mi Israel-towo, miaɖe alɔwo, eye miatse ku na nye dukɔ Israel. Elabe woagbɔ va aƒe kpuie.

english_verse: I will take care of you by plowing your soil and planting crops on your fertile slopes.
translation_verse: Elabe kpɔ ɖa, meli na mi, eye matrɔ ɖe mia ŋu, eye woade agble ɖe mia dzi, aƒã nu ɖe mia dzi.

english_verse: The people of Israel will return and rebuild your ruined towns and live in them.
translation_verse: Mana Israel-dukɔ blibo la katã ƒe amewo nadzi ɖe anyigba la katã dzi. Amewo anɔ duawo me, eye woagbugbɔ aƒedowo atso.

english_verse: Children will be born, and animals will give birth to their young. You will no longer be deserted as you are now, but you will be covered with people and treated better than ever. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mana amewo kple gbemelãwo nadzi ɖe mia dzi. Woadzi akeke ta, eye mana amewo nanɔ mia dzi abe tsã ene. Mana eme nanyo na mi wu tsã gɔ̃ hã. Ekema miadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: I will bring my people Israel home, and they will live on you mountains, because you belong to them, and your fertile slopes will never again let them starve.
translation_verse: Le nyateƒe me la, mana amewo, nye dukɔ Israel gɔ̃, nazɔ mia dzi. Woaxɔ wò, eye nànye woƒe domenyinu, eye màgana wo viwo naku azɔ o.

english_verse: It's true that you have been accused of not producing enough food and of letting your people starve.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Elabe amewo gblɔ na wò be: ‘Èɖua amelã, eye nènana be ɖeviwo kuna na wò dukɔ,’

english_verse: But I, the Lord, promise that you won't hear other nations laugh and sneer at you ever again. From now on, you will always produce plenty of food for your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Lord Will Be Honored
translation_verse: Nyemagana nàgase dukɔwo ƒe alɔmeɖeɖe le ame ŋu azɔ o. Màgatsɔ dukɔwo ƒe ŋukpedoamegba azɔ o, eye màgana wò dukɔ la nakli nu azɔ o.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe. Israel ƒe agbe yeye nɔnɔ

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own country, they made the land unclean by the way they behaved, just as a woman's monthly period makes her unclean.
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, esi Israel-dukɔ la nɔ woƒe anyigba dzi la, wogblẽ kɔ ɖo nɛ kple woƒe zɔzɔme kple nuwɔnawo. Woƒe nɔnɔme nɔ le ŋkunye me abe nyɔnu ƒe makɔmakɔ le eƒe dzinukpɔɣi ene.

english_verse: They committed murders and worshiped idols, which made the land even worse. So in my anger, I punished my people
translation_verse: Eya ta metrɔ nye dɔmedzoe kɔ ɖe wo dzi, le ʋu si wokɔ ɖe anyigba la dzi kple legba siwo wotsɔ gblẽ kɔ ɖo nɛ la ta.

english_verse: and scattered them throughout the nations, just as they deserved.
translation_verse: Mekaka wo ɖe dukɔwo dome, eye wokaka ɖe anyigbawo dzi. Medrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wo ɖe woƒe nɔnɔme kple nuwɔna nu.

english_verse: Wherever they went, my name was disgraced, because foreigners insulted my people by saying I had forced them out of their own land.
translation_verse: Ke esi wova dukɔwo dome la, afi sia afi si woyi la, wogblẽ kɔ ɖo na nye ŋkɔ kɔkɔe la. Ale be amewo gblɔ le wo ŋuti be: ‘Ame siawoe nye Aƒetɔ ƒe dukɔ; ke hã la, ele na wo be woaʋu tso eƒe anyigba dzi.’

english_verse: so tell the Israelites that I am saying: You have disgraced my holy name among the nations where you now live. So you don't deserve what I'm going to do for you. I will lead you home to bring honor to my name
translation_verse: Eya ta gblɔ na Israel-dukɔ la be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Israel-dukɔ, menye miawo tae mebe mawɔ nu sia ɖo o. Ke boŋ nye ŋkɔ kɔkɔe si miegblẽ le dukɔ siwo dome mieva la tae.

english_verse: I will gather you from the foreign nations and bring you home.
translation_verse: Elabe makplɔ mi tso dukɔwo dome, eye maƒo mia nu ƒu tso anyigbawo katã dzi, eye makplɔ mi ava miawo ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: I will sprinkle you with clean water, and you will be clean and acceptable to me. I will wash away everything that makes you unclean, and I will remove your disgusting idols.
translation_verse: Mahlẽ tsi dzadzɛ ɖe mia ŋu, eye miaƒe nu makɔmakɔwo katã aɖe ɖa. Maklɔ miaƒe legbawo katã ɖa le mia ŋu.

english_verse: I will take away your stubborn heart and give you a new heart and a desire to be faithful. You will have only pure thoughts,
translation_verse: Mana dzi yeye mi, eye made gbɔgbɔ yeye mia me. Maɖe kpedzi ɖa le mia me atsɔ lãkusidzi na mi.

english_verse: because I will put my Spirit in you and make you eager to obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Matsɔ nye gbɔgbɔ ade mia me, eye mawɔe be miazɔ ɖe nye ɖoɖowo nu kple nye sewo dzi pɛpɛpɛ.

english_verse: You will once again live in the land I gave your ancestors; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
translation_verse: Mianɔ anyigba si metsɔ na mia tɔgbuiwo la dzi. Mianye nye dukɔ, eye nye la manye mia Mawu.

english_verse: I will protect you from anything that makes you unclean. Your fields will overflow with grain, and no one will starve.
translation_verse: Maɖe mi tso miaƒe makɔmakɔnyenyewo katã me. Mana bli nado, asɔ gbɔ kpaŋkpaŋ, eye nyemana dɔ nawu mi o.

english_verse: Your trees will be filled with fruit, and crops will grow in your fields, so that you will never again feel ashamed for not having enough food.
translation_verse: Mana atikutsetsewo kple agblemenukuwo nadzi ɖe edzi ale be dɔwuame magado ŋukpe mi le dukɔwo dome azɔ o.

english_verse: People of Israel, I'm not doing these things for your sake. You sinned against me, and you must suffer shame and disgrace for what you have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be menyae be menye miawo tae mele ewɔ ge ɖo o. Israel-dukɔ, ŋu nekpe mi, miaƒe mo neyi to le miaƒe zɔzɔme la ta.”

english_verse: After I have made you clean, I will let you rebuild your ruined towns and let you live in them.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Gbe si gbe makɔ mia ŋu tso miaƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔwo katã me la, mawɔe be ame nanɔ duawo me, eye woagbugbɔ aƒe gbagbãwo atu.

english_verse: Your land will be plowed again, and nobody will be able to see that it was once barren.
translation_verse: Anyigba si nye gbegbe le ame siwo tsoa eme yina la ŋkume la azu agbledeƒe ɖe gbegbe teƒe.

english_verse: Instead, they will say that it looks as beautiful as the garden of Eden. They won't see towns lying in ruins, but they will see your strong cities filled with people.
translation_verse: Woagblɔ be: ‘Anyigba si nye gbegbe kpɔ la va zu abe Eden-bɔ ene, eye aƒedo kple gbegbe kpakple du gbagbãawo va zu ame nɔƒe kple du sesẽwo.’

english_verse: Then the nearby nations that survive will know that I am the one who rebuilt the ruined places and replanted the barren fields. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: Ekema dukɔ siwo ƒo xlã wo godoo la ava dze sii be, nye Aƒetɔ ye, nyee gbugbɔ du siwo wogbã la tso, eye mede agble ɖe teƒe si nye gbegbe la. Nye Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, eye mawɔe.”

english_verse: I will once again answer your prayers, and I will let your nation grow until you are like a large flock of sheep.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Maɖe mɔ be Israel-dukɔ nabiam nu sia hã, eye mawɔe na wo; ne mana woƒe amewo nadzi asɔ gbɔ abe alẽhawo ene.

english_verse: The towns that now lie in ruins will be filled with people, just as Jerusalem was once filled with sheep to be offered as sacrifices during a festival. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Abe alẽha siwo wotsɔna saa vɔe, abe alẽhawo le Yerusalem le ŋkekenyuiwo ɖuɣi ene la, nenemae amehawo ayɔ du siwo zu aƒedo la mee. Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: Some time later, I felt the Lord's power take control of me, and his Spirit carried me to a valley full of bones.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe asi nɔ dzinye, eye wòkplɔm do goe to Aƒetɔ ƒe gbɔgbɔ dzi va da ɖe bali la me. Ƒuwo yɔ bali la fũu.

english_verse: The Lord showed me all around, and everywhere I looked I saw bones that were dried out.
translation_verse: Ekplɔm to wo dome godoo, eye kpɔ ɖa, wosɔ gbɔ ŋutɔ le balia me; kpɔ ɖa, woƒu kplakplakpla.

english_verse: He said, “Ezekiel, son of man, can these bones come back to life?” I replied, “Lord God, only you can answer that.”
translation_verse: Ebiam be: “Amegbetɔ vi, ƒu siawo ate ŋu agbɔ agbea?” Meɖo eŋu be: “Aƒetɔ Mawu, wòe nyae.”

english_verse: He then told me to say: Dry bones, listen to what the Lord is saying to you,
translation_verse: Egagblɔ nam be: “Ɖe gbeƒã na ƒu siawo. Gblɔ na wo be, mi ƒu ƒuƒuwo, mise Aƒetɔ ƒe nya.

english_verse: “I, the Lord God, will put breath in you, and once again you will live.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu le gbɔgblɔm na ƒu siawo be: Kpɔ ɖa, mana gbɔgbɔ naɖo mia me, eye miagbɔ agbe.

english_verse: I will wrap you with muscles and skin and breathe life into you. Then you will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Made lãmeka mia ŋu, mana lãkusi naɖo mia ŋu, eye mafa ŋutigbalẽ ɖe mia ŋu. Magbɔ agbegbɔgbɔ ɖe mia me, eye miagbɔ agbe. Ne miadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: I did what the Lord said, but before I finished speaking, I heard a rattling noise. The bones were coming together!
translation_verse: Ale meɖe gbeƒã abe ale si wòɖe gbe nam la ene, eye esi menɔ gbeƒã ɖem la, zi tɔ. Ƒuawo nɔ tetem kpe kplɛkplɛkplɛ, ɖe sia ɖe te kpe nɔvia.

english_verse: I saw muscles and skin cover the bones, but they had no life in them.
translation_verse: Esi meda ŋku ɖi la, mekpɔ be lãmekawo ɖo wo ŋu, lãkusi ɖo wo ŋu, eye ŋutigbalẽ fa ɖe wo ŋu. Gake gbɔgbɔ menɔ wo me o.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, now say to the wind, “The Lord God commands you to blow from every direction and to breathe life into these dead bodies, so they can live again.”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ nam be: “Amegbetɔ vi, ɖe gbeƒã ɖo ɖe gbɔgbɔ la. Ɖe gbeƒã ɖo ɖe gbɔgbɔ la be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Gbɔgbɔ, do va tso ya eneawo me, va gbɔ ɖe ame kuku siawo me ne woate ŋu agbɔ agbe.”

english_verse: As soon as I said this, the wind blew among the bodies, and they came back to life! They all stood up, and there were enough to make a large army.
translation_verse: Ale meɖe gbeƒã abe ale si wòɖe gbe nam lae ene. Gbɔgbɔ ɖo wo me, eye wogbɔ agbe. Wotso ɖe woƒe afɔwo dzi, eye wonye aʋakɔ gã drinya aɖe.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, the people of Israel are like dead bones. They complain that they are dried up and that they have no hope for the future.
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ nam be: “Amegbetɔ vi, Israel-dukɔ blibo lae nye ƒu siawo. Kpɔ ɖa, wole gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Tsi no le míaƒe ƒuwo me, eye míaƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ bu; wolã mí ɖa keŋkeŋ.’

english_verse: So tell them, “I, the Lord God, promise to open your graves and set you free. I will bring you back to Israel,
translation_verse: Eya ta ɖe gbeƒã nàgblɔ na wo be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, nye dukɔ, maʋu miaƒe yɔdowo. Mana miafɔ tso miaƒe yɔdowo me, eye makplɔ mi ava mia de le Israel-nyigba la dzi.

english_verse: and when that happens, you will realize that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Nye dukɔ, azɔ miadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ, ne meʋu miaƒe yɔdowo, eye mena miefɔ tso miaƒe yɔdowo me.

english_verse: My Spirit will give you breath, and you will live again. I will bring you home, and you will know that I have kept my promise. I, the Lord, have spoken.” Judah and Israel Together Again
translation_verse: Matsɔ nye Gbɔgbɔ ade mia me, eye miagbɔ agbe, eye matsɔ mi ada ɖe miawo ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi. Ekema miadze sii be, nye Aƒetɔ ye ƒo nu, eye mewɔe.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Yuda kple Israel le fiaɖuƒe ɖeka te

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, get a stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Judah.” Then get another stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Israel.”
translation_verse: “Amegbetɔ vi, tsɔ ati, eye nàŋlɔ nu ɖe edzi be: ‘Yuda kple Israelvi siwo wɔ ɖeka kplii la tɔe’. Ekema nàgatsɔ ati bubu, eye nàŋlɔ ɖe edzi be: ‘Yosef kple Israel-dukɔ blibo la si wɔ ɖeka kplii la tɔe.’

english_verse: Hold these two sticks end to end, so they look like one stick.
translation_verse: Tsyia wo ne woazu ati ɖeka ɖe asiwò me.

english_verse: And when your people ask you what this means,
translation_verse: Ne mia deviwo abia wò be: ‘Màɖe nu siawo gɔme na mí oa?’

english_verse: tell them that I, the Lord, will join together the stick of Israel and the stick of Judah. I will hold them in my hand, and they will become one.
translation_verse: Gblɔ na wo be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, mele Yosef ƒe ati kple Israel ƒe to siwo wɔ ɖeka kplii la, tsyia ge ɖe Yuda ƒe ati la nu, eye mawɔ wo woanye ati ɖeka le nye asi me.

english_verse: Hold these two sticks where they can be seen by everyone
translation_verse: Nenye be èlé ati siwo dzi nèŋlɔ nuawo ɖo ɖe asi le wo ŋkume la,

english_verse: and then say: I, the Lord God, will gather the people of Israel and bring them home from the foreign nations where they now live.
translation_verse: ekema gblɔ na wo be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, makplɔ Israelviwo tso dukɔ siwo dome woyi la, aƒo wo nu ƒu tso akpa sia akpa, eye makplɔ wo ava woawo ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi.

english_verse: I will make them into one nation and let them once again live in the land of Israel. Only one king will rule them, and they will never again be divided into two nations.
translation_verse: Mawɔ wo woanye dukɔ ɖeka le anyigba la dzi, le Israel-towo dzi, eye fia ɖeka aɖu fia ɖe wo katã dzi. Womaganye dukɔ eve azɔ o, eye fiaɖuƒe la hã magama ɖe eve o.

english_verse: They will no longer worship idols and do things that make them unacceptable to me. I will wash away their sin and make them clean, and I will protect them from everything that makes them unclean. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Womagatsɔ woƒe legbawo kple nu siwo metsri la, alo woƒe dzidada aɖeke agblẽ kɔ ɖo na wo ɖokui azɔ o. Ke maɖe wo tso megbedede siwo katã nana be wowɔa nuvɔ̃ la me. Makɔ wo ŋu, eye woanye nye dukɔ, eye nye la, manye woƒe Mawu.”

english_verse: Their king will always come from the family of my servant King David and will care for them like a shepherd. The people of Israel will faithfully obey my laws. They and their descendants will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, just as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: Woanɔ anyigba si dzi mia tɔgbuiwo nɔ, esi metsɔ na nye dɔla Yakob la dzi. Woawo ŋutɔ kple wo viwo kpakple wo viwo ƒe viwo anɔ afi ma tegbee, eye nye dɔla David anye amegã ɖe wo nu tegbee.

english_verse: I solemnly promise to bless the people of Israel with unending peace. I will protect them and let them become a powerful nation. My temple will stand in Israel for all time,
translation_verse: Mabla ŋutifafanu kpli wo. Anye nubabla mavɔ kpli wo; mayra wo, ana woadzi asɔ gbɔ, eye maɖo nye kɔkɔeƒe anyi ɖe wo dome tegbee.

english_verse: and I will live among my people and be their God.
translation_verse: Nye nɔƒe anɔ wo dome; manye woƒe Mawu, eye woawo anye nye dukɔ.

english_verse: Every nation on earth will know that my temple is in Israel and that I have chosen the Israelites to be my people.
translation_verse: Ekema dukɔwo adze sii be, nye Aƒetɔ ye kɔ Israel ŋu, ne meɖo nye kɔkɔeƒe la anyi ɖe wo dome tegbee.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya va nam be:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog, that wicked ruler of the kingdoms of Meshech and Tubal in the land of Magog. Tell him:
translation_verse: Amegbetɔ vi, trɔ dze ŋgɔ Gɔg le Magɔg-nyigba dzi, ame si nye amegã le Mesex kple Tubal. Ɖe gbeƒã ɖe eŋu,

english_verse: and I will make you powerless! I will put a hook in your jaw and drag away both you and your large army. You command cavalry troops that wear heavy armor and carry shields and swords.
translation_verse: Matrɔ wò to eme, eye made ga alɔgo na wò. Makplɔ wò kple wò aʋakɔ blibo la, sɔwo kple sɔdolawo, ame siwo katã do aʋawɔnuwo tsaklii, ameha gã siwo katã lé akpoxɔnu suewo kple gãwo ɖe asi, hele yi dam.

english_verse: Your army includes soldiers from Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya,
translation_verse: Persia, Nubia kple Put kpe ɖe wo ŋu, wo katã wolé akpoxɔnu ɖe asi, eye woɖɔ gakuku.

english_verse: as well as from Gomer and Beth-Togarmah in the north. Your army is enormous!
translation_verse: Gomer kple eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la, Bet-Togarma kple eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la tso keke dzigbeme ke; dukɔ geɖewo kpe ɖe ŋuwò.”

english_verse: because in a few years, I will command you to invade Israel, a country that was ruined by war. It was deserted for a long time, but its people have returned from the foreign nations where they once lived. The Israelites now live in peace in the mountains of their own land.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke geɖewo megbe la, woayɔ mi. Le ƒè siwo akplɔe ɖo me la, àho ɖe anyigba si dzi aʋa ke le la ŋu. Anyigba sia dzie wokplɔ ame tso dukɔ vovovowo me va da ɖe Israel-towo dzi, teƒe si nye gbegbe ɣeyiɣi didi aɖe. Wokplɔ eƒe amewo tso dukɔwo dome, eye azɔ la wo katã woli dedie.

english_verse: But you and your army will attack them like a fierce thunderstorm and surround them like a cloud.
translation_verse: Àho aɖe zɔ ava abe ahom ene. Ànyè, atsyɔ anyigba la dzi abe alilikpo ene, wò kple wò aʋakɔ blibo la kpakple dukɔ geɖe siwo kpe ɖe ŋuwò.”

english_verse: When that day comes, I know that you will have an evil plan
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Gbe ma gbe la, susu geɖewo ava wò tame, eye àɖo tame vɔ̃,

english_verse: to take advantage of Israel, that weak and peaceful country where people live safely inside towns that have no walls or gates or locks.
translation_verse: ahagblɔ be: ‘Matso ɖe anyigba si ƒe duwo le sue, eye womeɖo gli ɖe wo ŋu o la ŋu. Madze ame siwo ɖe dzi ɖi bɔkɔɔ la dzi; ame siwo ŋu gli, gameti alo agbo mele o la.’

english_verse: You will rob the people in towns that were once a pile of rubble. These people lived as prisoners in foreign nations, but they have returned to Israel, the most important place in the world, and they own livestock and property.
translation_verse: Maha wo, aɖe aboyo wo. Mage ɖe aƒedo si me amewo le fifia la me kple dukɔ si woƒo ƒu tso dukɔwo dome la me; ame siwo si nyiwo kple nuwo le, eye wole anyigba la titina.

english_verse: The people of Sheba and Dedan, along with merchants from villages in southern Spain, will be your allies. They will want some of the silver and gold, as well as the livestock and property that your army takes from Israel.
translation_verse: Seba, Dedan kple Tarsis ƒe asitsalawo kpakple woƒe du viwo katã abia wò be: ‘Aboyonu ha ge nèvaa? Ɖe nèƒo ƒu wò amehawo be nàva ɖe aboyo nuwo atsɔ klosalo kple sika, nyihawo kple adzɔnuwo adzoe ahaɖo asi nu geɖewo dzia?’ ”

english_verse: I, the Lord God, know that when you see my people Israel living in peace,
translation_verse: “Eya ta amegbetɔ vi, ɖe gbeƒã nàgblɔ na Gɔg be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Gbe si gbe nye dukɔ Israel li, ɖe dzi ɖi bɔkɔɔ la, àʋã ɖokuiwò.

english_verse: You will attack my people like a storm-cloud that covers their land. I will let you invade my country Israel, so that every nation on earth will know that I, the Lord, am holy. Judgment on Gog
translation_verse: Àho ɖe nye dukɔ Israel ŋu abe alilikpoe do ɖe anyigba dzi ene. Ava eme le nuwuwu ŋkekeawo me be mana wò Gɔg nàtso ɖe nye anyigba ŋu, ale be dukɔwo nadze sii be, nyee to dziwò kɔ ɖokuinye ŋu le wo ŋkume.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Gog: Long ago, I ordered my prophets to warn the people of Israel that someday I would send an enemy to attack them. You, Gog, are that enemy, and that day is coming.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Wò ŋue meƒo nu tso, le blema ŋkekewo me, to nye dɔlawo, Israel ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo dzi, ame siwo ɖe gbeƒã ƒè geɖewo le ɣe ma ɣi be makplɔ wò nàtso ɖe wo ŋutia? Mawu ahe to na Gɔg

english_verse: and in my anger I will send a terrible earthquake to shake Israel.
translation_verse: Elabe le nye ŋuʋaʋã kple dɔmedzoe si le bibim flaflafla me la, meɖe gbe. Anyigba aʋuʋu ŋutɔ le Israel-nyigba dzi gbe ma gbe.

english_verse: Every living thing on earth will tremble in fear of me—every fish and bird, every wild animal and reptile, and every human. Mountains will crumble, cliffs will fall, and cities will collapse.
translation_verse: Ƒumelãwo kple dziƒoxeviwo, gbemelãwo kple lã siwo katã tana le anyigba dzi kpakple amegbetɔ siwo katã le anyigba dzi la, adzo nyànyanya le ŋkunye me. Towo amu dze anyi, agakpewo aglí, eye gli ɖe sia ɖe amu dze anyi.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will make the mountains of Israel turn against you. Your troops will be so terrified that they will attack each other.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Mayɔ ŋɔdzidonu ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi ɖe Gɔg ŋu; ame sia ame atsɔ yi ɖe nɔvia ŋu.

english_verse: I will strike you with diseases and punish you with death. You and your army will be pounded with rainstorms, hailstones, and burning sulfur.
translation_verse: Dɔ vɔ̃ kple ʋukɔkɔɖie matsɔ drɔ̃ ʋɔnui. Mana tsi gãwo, tsikpewo, dzo kple aŋɔ nadza ɖe eya kple eƒe aʋakɔ kpakple dukɔ geɖe siwo kpe ɖe eŋu la dzi.

english_verse: I will do these things to show the world that I, the Lord, am holy.
translation_verse: Ale maɖe nye gãnyenye kple nye ŋutikɔkɔe afia le dukɔ geɖewo ŋkume, eye mana woadze sim. Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog and tell him: You are the ruler of Meshech and Tubal, but I, the Lord, am your enemy!
translation_verse: Azɔ wò amegbetɔ vi, ɖe gbeƒã ɖe Gɔg ŋu nàgblɔ nɛ be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Kpɔ ɖa, Gɔg, metso ɖe ŋuwò, wò si nye amegã le Mesex kple Tubal.

english_verse: I will turn you around and drag you from the north until you reach the mountains of Israel.
translation_verse: Matrɔ wò to eme, atutu wò do ɖe ŋgɔ, eye makplɔ wò tso keke dzigbeme ke vɛ, ɖe Israel-towo ŋu.

english_verse: I will knock the bow out of your left hand and the arrows out of your right hand,
translation_verse: Ekema maƒo wò dati le wò miasi me, eye mana wò aŋutrɔwo nage le wò nuɖusi.

english_verse: and you and your army will die on those mountains. Then birds and wild animals will eat the flesh
translation_verse: Àdze anyi ɖe Israel-towo dzi, wò kple wò aʋakɔ blibo la kple dukɔ siwo katã kpe ɖe ŋuwò la. Matsɔ wò ana xe ƒonu ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi kple gbemelãwo ne woavuvu.

english_verse: of your dead bodies left lying in open fields. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Miatsi gbadzaƒe le gbedzi, elabe nyee ƒo nu. Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: I will set fire to the land of Magog and to those nations along the seacoast that think they are so secure, and they will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mana dzo nage dze Magɔg kple ame siwo katã ɖe dzi ɖi bɔkɔɔ le ƒutanyigbawo dzi la dzi; ne woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: My people Israel will know me, and they will no longer disgrace my holy name. Everyone on earth will know that I am the holy Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: “Mana woadze si nye ŋkɔ kɔkɔe la le nye dukɔ Israel dome. Nyemagana wòaƒo ɖi nye ŋkɔ kɔkɔe la azɔ o, eye dukɔwo adze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Kɔkɔetɔ la.

english_verse: The day is coming when these things will happen, just as I have promised.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, egbɔna, woana wòava eme, Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe. Ŋkeke ma ŋutie meƒo nu le.”

english_verse: When that day comes, the people in the towns of Israel will collect the weapons of their dead enemies. They will use these shields, bows and arrows, spears, and clubs as firewood, and there will be enough to last for seven years.
translation_verse: “Ekema ame siwo le duwo me le Israel la ado aɖado dzo kple aʋawɔnuawo woafiã. Woatsɔ akpoxɔnu gãwo kple sueawo, datiwo kple aŋutrɔwo, kpowo kple akplɔwo, ado dzoe ƒè adrẽ.

english_verse: They will burn these weapons instead of gathering sticks or chopping down trees. That's how the Israelites will take revenge on those who robbed and abused them. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Burial of Gog The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ale be magahiã be woaɖafɔ nake le gbe me loo, alo atso atiwo le avewo me na nake o. Elabe aʋawɔnuawoe woatsɔ ado dzoe. Woada adzo ame siwo da adzo wo eye woaha ame siwo ha wo la.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe. Gɔg ɖiɖi

english_verse: After Gog has been destroyed, I will bury him and his army in Israel, in Travelers' Valley, east of the Dead Sea. That graveyard will be so large that it will block the way of anyone who tries to walk through the valley, which will then be known as “The Valley of Gog's Army.”
translation_verse: “Gbe ma gbe la, mana teƒe si woaɖi Gɔg ɖo le Israel, ɖe Mɔzɔlawo ƒe Bali la me, le atsiaƒu ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome. Axe mɔ na mɔzɔlawo, elabe afi mae woaɖi Gɔg kple eƒe amehawo gbogboawo ɖo. Woayɔe be Hamon-Gɔg Bali la.

english_verse: The Israelites will spend seven months burying dead bodies and cleaning up their land.
translation_verse: Israel-dukɔ la atsɔ ɣleti adrẽ aɖi woe, ale be woakɔ anyigba la ŋu.

english_verse: Everyone will help with the burial, and they will be honored for this on the day the brightness of my glory is seen.
translation_verse: Dukɔ haho lae aɖi wo, eye wòana woaxɔ ŋkɔ gbe si gbe meɖe nye ŋutikɔkɔe fia. Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: After those seven months, the people will appoint a group of men to look for any dead bodies left unburied. This must be done for seven months to make sure that the land is no longer unclean.
translation_verse: Woaɖe amewo be woatsa enuenu le anyigba la dzi, eye woaɖi ame siwo ku ɖe edzi la, ale be woakɔ anyigba la ŋu. Le ɣleti adrẽlia megbe la, woagatsa.

english_verse: Whenever they find a human bone, they will set up a marker next to it. Then the gravediggers will bury it in “The Valley of Gog's Army”
translation_verse: Ne ame siwo le tsatsam le anyigba la dzi kpɔ ameƒu aɖe la, woade dzesi egbɔ va se ɖe esime ameɖilawo ava kɔe aɖaɖi ɖe Hamon-Gɔg Bali la me.

english_verse: near the town of “Gog's Army.” After that, the land will be pure again.
translation_verse: Afi mae du si woyɔna be Hamona hã le. Alea woawɔ akɔ anyigba la ŋutii.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to hold a feast on Israel's mountains and offer sacrifices there. So invite all the birds and wild animals to come from every direction and eat the meat of sacrifices and drink the blood. The birds and animals
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Ke wò amegbetɔ vi, ƒo nu na xe ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi kple gbemelãwo katã be: Miƒo ƒu miava. Mite va tso afi sia afi ne miava ɖu vɔsa ŋkekenyui si medzra ɖo na mi la. Vɔsa ŋkekenyui gã ŋutɔ wònye le Israel ƒe towo dzi, eye miaɖu lã, ano ʋu.

english_verse: will feast on the bodies of warriors and foreign rulers that I will sacrifice like sheep, goats, and bulls.
translation_verse: Miaɖu kalẽtɔwo ƒe lã, eye miano anyigba dzi megãwo ƒe ʋu: agbowo, alẽviwo, gbɔ̃wo, nyitsuwo, wo katã wonye lã damiwo tso Basan.

english_verse: I want the birds and animals to eat until they are full and drink until they are drunk.
translation_verse: Miaɖu ami ʋuu aɖi ƒo, eye miano ʋu kakaka amu le vɔsa ŋkekenyui si medzra ɖo na mi la ɖuƒe.

english_verse: They will come to my table and stuff themselves with the flesh of horses and warriors of every kind. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Israel Will Be Restored The Lord said:
translation_verse: Miaɖu sɔ kple sɔdolawo ƒe lã, kalẽtɔwo kple aʋawɔla vovovowo le nye kplɔ̃ la ŋu aɖi ƒo.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe. Woagbugbɔ Israel aɖo te

english_verse: When I punish the nations of the earth, they will see the brightness of my glory.
translation_verse: “Matsɔ nye ŋutikɔkɔe aɖo dukɔwo dome, eye dukɔwo katã akpɔ nye ʋɔnu si medrɔ̃ kple nye asi si meɖo wo dzi la.

english_verse: The people of Israel will know from then on that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Israel-dukɔ la adze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu tso gbe ma gbe dzi heyi.

english_verse: Foreign nations will realize that the Israelites were forced to leave their own land because they sinned against me. I turned my back on my people and let enemies attack and kill them.
translation_verse: Dukɔwo adze sii be Israel-dukɔ la yi aboyo me le woƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ta. Elabe wogbugbɔ le yonyeme ale be meɣla nye ŋkume ɖe wo. Metsɔ wo de asi na woƒe futɔwo, eye wowu wo katã kple yi.

english_verse: Their lives were wicked and corrupt, and they deserved to be punished.
translation_verse: Mewɔe na wo ɖe woƒe nu makɔmakɔ wɔwɔ kple dzidadawo nu pɛ, eye meɣla nye ŋkume ɖe wo.”

english_verse: Now I will show mercy to the people of Israel and bring them back from the nations where they are living. They are Jacob's descendants, so I will bless them and show that I am holy.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Azɔ la, magbugbɔ Yakob ƒe nunyonamewo aɖo te, eye makpɔ nublanui na Israel-dukɔ blibo la. Maʋã ŋu le nye ŋkɔ kɔkɔe la ta.

english_verse: They will live safely in their own land, but will be ashamed when they remember their evil ways and how they disgraced me.
translation_verse: Woaŋlɔ woƒe ŋukpe kple alakpanuwɔna siwo katã wowɔ ɖe ŋunye la be, nenye be wogale woƒe anyigba dzi bɔkɔɔ, eye ame aɖeke medoa vɔvɔ̃ na wo o.

english_verse: Foreign nations will watch as I take the Israelites from enemy lands and bring them back home, and those nations will see that I am holy.
translation_verse: Ne megatrɔ wo gbɔe tso dukɔwo dome, eye meƒo wo nu ƒu tso woƒe futɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi la, mato eme aɖe nye kɔkɔenyenye afia le dukɔ geɖewo ŋkume.

english_verse: My people will realize that I, the Lord their God, sent them away as prisoners and now will bring them back to their own land.
translation_verse: Ekema woadze sii be, nyee nye Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu. Elabe mekplɔ wo yi aboyo me le dukɔwo dome, eye megaƒo wo nu ƒu ɖe woawo ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi. Nyemagblẽ wo dometɔ aɖeke ɖe dukɔwo dome azɔ o.

english_verse: Never again will I turn my back on the people of Israel, and my Spirit will live in them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nyemagaɣla nye ŋkume ɖe wo azɔ o, ne metrɔ nye Gbɔgbɔ la kɔ ɖe Israel-dukɔ la dzi.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Twenty-five years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, and
translation_verse: Ekplɔm le ŋutega siwo Mawu ɖe fiam la me va Israel-nyigba dzi, eye wòtsɔm da ɖe to kɔkɔ aɖe tame. Nane si ƒe dzedzeme le abe du aɖe ene la nɔ ŋgɔnye le to sia dzi.

english_verse: He measured the entrance room at the far end of the passageway, and it was ten meters wide.
translation_verse: Edzidze akpata la, enɔ meta ewo, eye akpata ƒo xlã xɔxɔnu la.

english_verse: In my vision the Lord took me closer, and I saw a man who was sparkling like polished bronze. He was standing near one of the gates and was holding a tape measure in one hand and a measuring stick in the other.
translation_verse: Esi wòkplɔm va teƒe ma la, kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsu aɖe, si ƒe nɔnɔme ɖi akɔbli la, nɔ afi ma. Elé ka si wogbi kple anazi la ɖe asi, hekpe ɖe nudzidzeti ŋu hetɔ ɖe agboa nu.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay close attention to everything I'm going to show you—that's why you've been brought here. Listen carefully, because you must tell the people of Israel what you see.” The East Gate
translation_verse: Ŋutsu la gblɔ nam be: “Amegbetɔ vi, kpɔ nu kple wò ŋku, se nu kple wò to, eye nalé nu siwo katã mafia wò la, ɖe susu me. Elabe ɖe wokplɔ wò va afi siae, be maɖe wo afia wò. Ɖe gbeƒã nu siwo katã nèkpɔ la, na Israel-dukɔ la.” Ɣedzeƒegbo la

english_verse: The three guardrooms on each side of the passageway were the same size, and the walls that separated them were the same thickness.
translation_verse: Xɔvi etɔ̃ nɔ ɣedzeƒegbo la ƒe akpa eveawo, ɖe sia ɖe ƒe lolome sɔ, eye gli si ma wo dome le akpa sia akpa la ƒe titrime le ɖeka.

english_verse: Next, the man measured the width of the passageway, and it was six and a half meters, but the two doors of the gate were only five meters wide.
translation_verse: Tete wòdzidze agbo la ƒe mɔnu. Ekeke meta atɔ̃, eye agboa ŋutɔ keke meta ade kple afã.

english_verse: The man measured the distance from the back wall of one of these rooms to the same spot in the room directly across the passageway, and it was twelve and a half meters.
translation_verse: Tete wòdzidze xɔviawo ƒe agbo tso ɖeka megbe va se ɖe evelia megbe, eye woƒe kekeme tso ʋɔtru nu va ɖo ʋɔtru nu nye meta wui eve kple afã.

english_verse: Finally, he measured the total length of the passageway, from the outer wall to the entrance room, and it was
translation_verse: Tso agboa ƒe mɔnu le xexe va se ɖe akpata emetɔ la ƒe agbo ƒe nuwuwu le meta bla eve vɔ atɔ̃.

english_verse: The three walls in the guardrooms had small windows in them, just like the ones in the entrance room. The walls along the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. The Outer Courtyard
translation_verse: Fesrewo ƒo xlã agboawo va kpe. Wonɔ miamiam ɖo ta domegliawo kple xɔ siwo le axawo dzi la gbɔ, eye fesrewo ƒo xlã akpata la hã kpe ɖo. Wota detiwo ɖe domegliawo ŋu. Xɔxɔnu si le gota la

english_verse: The man then led me through the passageway and into the outer courtyard of the temple, where I saw
translation_verse: Eyome wòkplɔm yi ɖe xɔxɔnu si le egodo la me. Kpɔ ɖa, xɔviwo le xɔxɔnu la, eye woɖo kpewo ƒo xlã anyigba. Xɔvi bla etɔ̃ dze ŋgɔ kpe siwo woɖo ƒo xlã anyigba la.

english_verse: In fact, everything along the passageway was also the same size, including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, the entrance room at the far end, and the windows. This gate, like the others, was
translation_verse: Akpatawo ƒo xlãe godoo va kpe. Wodidi meta wui eve kple afã hekeke meta eve kple afã.

english_verse: This was known as the lower sidewalk, and it was
translation_verse: Woɖo kpewo ɖe agbo la ƒe axawo dzi ɖe eƒe didime nu. Esia nye kpenyigba si le anyigbeme.

english_verse: I saw the gates that led to the inner courtyard of the temple and noticed that they were higher than those leading to the outer courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gates, and it was
translation_verse: Eyome wòdzidze kekeme si nɔ agbo si le anyigbeme ƒe eme lɔƒo va se ɖe xɔxɔnu si le egodo la nu le gota la dome wònɔ meta bla atɔ̃. Dzigbemegbo la Tete wòdzo le gbɔnye yi dzigbeme lɔƒo,

english_verse: Next, the man measured the north gate that led to the outer courtyard.
translation_verse: eye kpɔ ɖa, agbo aɖe li si dze ŋgɔ dzigbeme, eye wòle xɔxɔnu si le egodo la ŋu. Edzidze eƒe didime kple kekeme.

english_verse: This gate also had three guardrooms on each side of a passageway. The measurements of these rooms, the walls between them, and the entrance room at the far end of the passageway were exactly the same as those of the east gate. The north gate was also
translation_verse: Xɔvi etɔ̃etɔ̃ le eƒe axawo kple eve dzi. Domegliawo kple akpata la ƒe dzidzeme sɔ kple agbo gbãtɔ tɔ. Wodidi meta bla eve vɔ atɔ̃ hekeke meta wui eve kple afã.

english_verse: and the windows, the entrance room, and the carvings of palm trees were just like those in the east gate. The entrance room also faced the courtyard of the temple and had seven steps leading up to it.
translation_verse: Eƒe fesrewo, eƒe akpata kple detiwo ƒe lolome sɔ kple agbo si le ɣedzeƒe gome la tɔ. Atrakpui adrẽ woflɔna dea edzi, eye eƒe akpata le eme lɔƒo.

english_verse: Directly across the outer courtyard was a gate that led to the inner courtyard, just as there was for the east gate. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was
