translation_verse: Agbo aɖe dze ŋgɔ agbo si le dzigbeme la hege ɖe xɔxɔnu emetɔ la me abe ale si wònɔ le ɣedzeƒegbo la gome ene. Edzidze agbo nu yi agbo nu wònɔ meta bla atɔ̃. Anyigbemegbo la

english_verse: The man then took me to the south gate. He measured the walls and the entrance room of this gate, and the measurements were exactly the same as those of the other two gates.
translation_verse: Tete wòkplɔm ɖo ta anyigbeme, eye kpɔ ɖa, agbo aɖe le anyigbeme. Wodzidze eƒe domegliawo kple akpata la hã. Abe bubuawo ene la, dzidzeme ɖeka li na wo.

english_verse: Seven steps led up to the gate; the entrance room was at the far end of the passageway and faced the courtyard of the temple. Carvings of palm trees decorated the walls along the passageway.
translation_verse: Atrakpui adrẽ woflɔna dea edzi, eye eƒe akpata le eme lɔƒo. Wota detiwo ɖe eƒe domegliawo ƒe akpa eveawo; deti ɖeka ɖe akpa sia akpa.

english_verse: And directly across the outer courtyard was a gate on the south side of the inner courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was also
translation_verse: Le xɔxɔnu emetɔ ƒe anyigbeme la, agbo aɖe li. Edzidze tso agbo nu yi agbo nu ɖo ta anyigbeme, eye dzidzemea le meta bla atɔ̃. Xɔxɔnu si le ememe: Anyigbemegbo la

english_verse: We then went into the inner courtyard, through the gate on the south side of the temple. The man measured the gate, and it was the same size as the gates in the outer wall.
translation_verse: Tete wòkplɔm yi xɔxɔnu ememetɔ la me to anyigbemegbo la nu. Edzidze anyigbemegbo la; eƒe dzidzeme sɔ kple bubuawo tɔ.

english_verse: The entrance room of this gate faced the outer courtyard, and carvings of palm trees decorated the walls of the passageway. Eight steps led up to this gate.
translation_verse: Eƒe akpata dze ŋgɔ xɔxɔnu si le kɔto la. Detiwo le eƒe domegliawo ŋu, eye eƒe atrakpuiwo le enyi. Xɔxɔnu si le ememe: Ɣedzeƒegbo la

english_verse: Next, we went through the east gate to the inner courtyard. The man measured this gate, and it was the same size as the others.
translation_verse: Ekplɔm yi ɖe xɔxɔnu si le ememe le ɣedzeƒekpa dzi, eye wòdzidze agbo la. Eƒe dzidzeme le abe bubuawo tɔ ene.

english_verse: The guardrooms, the walls separating them, and its entrance room had the same measurements as the other gates. The guardrooms and the entrance room had windows, and the gate was
translation_verse: Eƒe xɔviwo, domegliawo kple akpata la ƒe dzidzeme le abe bubuawo tɔ ene. Fesrewo ƒo xlãe kpe ɖe eƒe akpata la ŋuti. Eƒe didime nye meta bla eve vɔ atɔ̃, eye eƒe kekeme le meta wui eve kple afã.

english_verse: The entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and the walls in the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate.
translation_verse: Eƒe akpata dze ŋgɔ xɔxɔnu si le kɔto la. Detiwo le eƒe domegliawo ƒe akpa eve; deti ɖeka le akpa ɖeka, atrakpui enyi le eŋu. Xɔxɔnu si le ememe: Dzigbemegbo la

english_verse: Then the man took me to the north gate. He measured it, and it was the same size as the others,
translation_verse: Ekplɔm va dzigbemegbo la nu, eye wòdzidze agbo la. Eƒe dzidzeme sɔ kple bubuawo tɔ.

english_verse: including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, and the entrance room. There were also windows in this gate. It was
translation_verse: Eƒe xɔviwo, domegliawo kple akpata la ƒe dzidzeme le abe bubuawo tɔ ene. Eƒe fesrewo ƒo xlãe godoo va kpe. Eƒe didime le meta bla eve vɔ atɔ̃, eye eƒe kekeme nye meta wui eve kple afã.

english_verse: and like the other inner gates, its entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and its walls were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate. The Rooms for Sacrificing Animals
translation_verse: Eƒe akpata dze ŋgɔ xɔxɔnu kɔtoe tɔ, eye detiwo le domegliawo ƒe akpa eve. Deti ɖeka le akpa ɖeka, atrakpui enyi le eŋu. Xɔ siwo te ɖe dzigbemegbo la ŋu

english_verse: Four more tables were in the outer courtyard, two on each side of the steps leading into the entrance room.
translation_verse: Le akpata la ƒe gota gome le dzigbemegbo la nu la, kplɔ̃ eve le afi ma hã.

english_verse: So there was a total of eight tables, four inside and four outside, where the animals were killed,
translation_verse: Le ememe gome la, kplɔ̃ ene le agbo la me, eye kplɔ̃ ene le gota gome. Kplɔ̃ enyi li na vɔsalãwo wuwu.

english_verse: and where the meat was placed until it was sacrificed on the altar. Next to the tables in the entrance room were four stone tables
translation_verse: Woɖo ga gɔdɔ̃ewo, asi ƒe kekeme ɖeka, ɖe kplɔ̃awo to, wobi ɖo ɖe eme. Nu siawo keke milimeta bla adrẽ vɔ atɔ̃. Kplɔ̃ siawo dzie woada vɔsalãwo ɖo.

english_verse: The man then took me to the inner courtyard, where I saw two buildings, one beside the inner gate on the north and the other beside the inner gate on the south.
translation_verse: Tete wòkplɔm tso gota ge ɖe xɔxɔnu emetɔ la me, eye kpɔ ɖa, xɔvi eve le xɔxɔnu emetɔ la me. Ɖeka le dzigbemegbo la xa dze ŋgɔ anyigbeme, eye evelia le anyigbemegbo la xa dze ŋgɔ dzigbeme.

english_verse: He said, “The building beside the north gate belongs to the priests who serve in the temple,
translation_verse: Egblɔ nam be: Xɔvi si dze ŋgɔ anyigbeme la nye nunɔla siwo kpɔa gbedoxɔ la dzi la tɔ,

english_verse: and the building beside the south gate belongs to those who serve at the altar. All of them are descendants of Zadok and are the only Levites allowed to serve as the Lord's priests.” The Inner Courtyard and the Temple
translation_verse: eye xɔvi si dze ŋgɔ dzigbeme la nye nunɔla siwo kpɔa vɔsamlekpui la dzi la tɔ. Ame siawoe nye Zadok viwo, woawo koe kpɔ mɔ le Levi viwo dome be woate ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu awɔ eƒe subɔsubɔ. Xɔxɔnu si le ememe gome kple gbedoxɔ la

english_verse: We walked to the porch of the temple, and the man measured the doorway of the porch: It was seven meters long, two and a half meters wide, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one and a half meters.
translation_verse: Eyome ekplɔm va gbedoxɔ la ƒe akpata me, eye wòdzidze akpata la ƒe domegliawo, eƒe akpa eveawo ɖe sia ɖe le meta eve kple afã. Agboa keke meta adrẽ, eye agboa ƒe axadzigliwo tri meta ɖeka kple afã le akpa eveawo.

english_verse: The porch itself was ten meters by six meters, with steps leading up to it. There was a column on each side of these steps.
translation_verse: Akpata la didi meta ewo, eye wòkeke meta ade. Atrakpui ewo le eŋu woflɔna dea edzi. Sɔtiwo le domegliawo ŋu le woƒe akpawo kple eve dzi.

english_verse: Next we went into the main room of the temple. The man measured the doorway of this room: It was
translation_verse: Tete wòkplɔm ge ɖe gbedoxɔ la me, eye wòdzidze domegliawo. Woƒe kekeme le akpa eveawo nɔ meta etɔ̃, etɔ̃.

english_verse: and the nearest buildings ten meters away.
translation_verse: gbedoxɔ la dome la, keke meta ewo le akpa sia akpa godoo va kpe.

english_verse: Then the man walked to the far end of the temple's main room and said, “Beyond this doorway is the most holy place.” He first measured the doorway: It was one meter wide,
translation_verse: Edzidze xɔa me ƒe didime ɖo ta gbedoxɔ la gbɔ wònɔ meta ewo, eye eƒe kekeme hã nɔ meta ewo. Egblɔ nam be: “Esia nye kɔkɔeƒewo ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la.” Xɔ siwo wotu ɖe gbedoxɔ la ƒe gliwo ŋu

english_verse: The walls of the temple were thicker at the bottom than at the top, which meant that the storage rooms on the top level were wider than those on the bottom level. Steps led from the bottom level, through the middle level, and into the top level.
translation_verse: Xɔŋuxɔe ɖe sia ɖe ƒe tuɖedziwo nɔ kekem ɖe edzi tso tuɖedzi ɖeka dzi yi bubu dzi, si wɔe be xɔ la klã le dzi me ƒo xlã gbedoxɔ la. Atrakpui si te ɖe gbedoxɔa ŋu dze egɔme tso anyigbaxɔ me to dometɔ me heyi etametɔ me.

english_verse: The temple rested on a stone base three meters high, which also served as the foundation for the storage rooms.
translation_verse: Mekpɔ hã be woƒu kpo ɖe gbedoxɔa ŋu godoo va kpe. Woawoe nye xɔŋuxɔeawo ƒe gɔmeɖoɖo siwo tri dzidzeti ɖeka alo meta eve.

english_verse: One door led into the storage rooms on the north side of the temple, and another door led to those on the south side. The stone base extended two and a half meters beyond the outside wall of the storage rooms. The West Building and the Measurements of the Temple
translation_verse: Xɔŋuxɔeawo ƒe ʋɔtruwo trɔ ɖo ɖe teƒe si wotso ɖi le kpo si woƒu ƒo xlã la gbɔ, ʋɔtru ɖeka dze ŋgɔ dzigbeme, eye bubu dze ŋgɔ anyigbeme. Teƒe si wotso ɖi la, keke meta eve kple afã ƒo xlãe. Xɔ si le ɣetoɖoƒe

english_verse: The man measured the length of the temple, and it was
translation_verse: Edzidze gbedoxɔ la, edidi meta bla atɔ̃. Teƒe si ŋu wotɔ kpɔ ɖo, xɔ la kple eƒe gli didi meta bla atɔ̃.

english_verse: The distance across the front of the temple, including the open space on either side, was also
translation_verse: Gbedoxɔ la ŋkume le ɣedzeƒe gome kple teƒe si ŋu wotɔ kpɔ ɖo la hã keke meta bla atɔ̃.

english_verse: were paneled with wood all the way from the floor to the windows, while the doorways, the small windows, and the three side rooms were trimmed in wood.
translation_verse: Wofae ɖe wo ŋu ƒo xlã wo ame etɔ̃ la godoo, eye wofa nu ɖe woƒe fesrewo hã ŋu. Wofa ʋuƒo ɖe eŋu kpe ɖo, tso anyigba va ɖo fesrewo nu. Ke fesreawo le tutu.

english_verse: The paneling stopped just above the doorway. These walls were decorated
translation_verse: Le ʋɔtrua tame, le xɔmexɔ kple dodonutɔ kekeake me la, wota nɔnɔmetatawo ɖe gliawo ŋu godoo va kpe.

english_verse: The doorframe to the temple's main room was in the shape of a rectangle. The Wooden Altar In front of the doorway to the most holy place was something that looked like
translation_verse: Gbedoxɔ la ƒe ʋɔtrutiwo le dzogoe ene me. Vɔsamlekpui si wotsɔ ati wɔe Nane le kɔkɔeƒeawo ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la si ɖi

english_verse: a wooden altar. It was one and a half meters high and one meter square, and its corners, its base, and its sides were made of wood. The man said, “This is a reminder that the Lord is constantly watching over his temple.” The Doors in the Temple
translation_verse: vɔsamlekpui si wotsɔ ati wɔe la. Ekɔ meta ɖeka kple afã, didi meta ɖeka, eye wòkeke meta ɖeka. Eƒe dzogoewo, afɔwo kple axawo katã dzi nye ati. Egblɔ nam be: “Esia nye kplɔ̃ si le Aƒetɔ ŋkume.” Ʋɔtruawo

english_verse: Both the doorway to the main room of the temple and the doorway to the most holy place had two doors,
translation_verse: Ʋɔtru siwo ʋuna ɖo ɖe akpa eveawo la, le kɔkɔeƒe la kple kɔkɔeƒewo ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la, ƒe mɔwo nu.

english_verse: and each door had two sections that could fold open.
translation_verse: Ʋɔtruawo dze eve le mɔawo nu, eye ɖe sia ɖe trona le mɔ ɖe sia ɖe nu.

english_verse: The doors to the main room were decorated with carvings of winged creatures and palm trees just like those on the walls, and there was a wooden covering over the porch just outside these doors.
translation_verse: Wowɔ kerubiwo kple detiwo ɖe wo ŋu abe ale si wowɔ wo ɖe gliawo ŋui la ene, eye wotsɔ ʋuƒo wɔ agbadɔe ɖe akpata la nu le xexe lɔƒo.

english_verse: The walls on each side of this porch had small windows and were also decorated with carvings of palm trees.
translation_verse: Fesreawo ʋu ɖo ɖe eme lɔƒo, eye detiwo le woƒe akpa eveawo kple xɔŋuxɔeawo ƒe gliawo ŋu.

english_verse: After the man and I left the temple and walked back to the outer courtyard, he showed me a set of rooms on the north side of the west building. This set of rooms was
translation_verse: Xɔ si nɔ dzigbeme la ƒe didime nɔ meta bla atɔ̃, eye wòkeke meta bla eve vɔ atɔ̃.

english_verse: and at the east end of this wall was the door leading from the courtyard to these rooms. There was also a set of rooms on the south side of the west building.
translation_verse: afi si xɔxɔnu la ƒe gliwo dze egɔme tsoe. Xɔviwo le anyigbeme gome hã. Wodze ŋgɔ gbadzaƒe si ŋu wotɔ kpɔ ɖo kple xɔ la.

english_verse: with doors that opened toward the north, and in front of them was a walkway five meters wide and
translation_verse: Teƒe aɖe le xɔviawo nu ɖo ta xɔxɔnu si le eme la gbɔ. Ekeke meta atɔ̃, eye wòdidi meta bla atɔ̃. Woƒe ʋɔtruwo ɖo ta dzigbeme lɔƒo.

english_verse: The rooms on the top level were narrower than those on the middle level, and the rooms on the middle level were narrower than those on the bottom level.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, xɔvi siwo le etame la, mekeke abe esiwo le ete kple dome la ene o. Elabe dzisasrãwo xɔ nɔƒe le wo si.

english_verse: The rooms on the bottom level supported those on the two upper levels, and so these rooms did not have columns like other buildings in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Elabe tuɖedzi etɔ̃ wonye, eye sɔtiwo menɔ wo ŋu abe ale si wonɔ xɔxɔnu siwo nɔ gota la ŋu la ene o. Eya ta xɔvi siwo le etame la, mekeke abe esiwo le ete kple dome la ene o.

english_verse: These rooms were exactly like those on the north side, and they also had a walkway in front of them.
translation_verse: Toƒe le wo ŋgɔ, eye woɖi xɔvi siwo le dzigbeme lɔƒo la. Woƒe didime kple kekeme sɔ, woƒe mɔnuwo kple ʋɔtruwo hã sɔ pɛpɛpɛ.

english_verse: The door to these rooms was at the east end of the wall that stood in front of them.
translation_verse: Le xɔvi siwo le anyigbeme gome la, ʋɔtru aɖe le ɣedzeƒe lɔƒo. Afi mae ame ato age ɖe teƒe la, eye gli si ma wo me la dze ŋgɔ wo.

english_verse: The man then said to me: These rooms on the north and south sides of the temple are the sacred rooms where the Lord's priests will eat the most holy offerings. These offerings include the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices for sin, and the sacrifices to make things right.
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ nam be: “Xɔvi siwo le dzigbeme kple anyigbeme, siwo dze ŋgɔ teƒe si ŋu wotɔ kpɔ ɖo la nye xɔvi kɔkɔewo. Afi siae nunɔla siwo tena ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu la, aɖu vɔsanu kɔkɔeawo le. Afi mae woada vɔsanu kɔkɔeawo ɖo: nuɖuɖuvɔsa, nuvɔ̃vɔsa kple fɔɖiɖivɔsa ɖo. Elabe teƒe kɔkɔe ye.

english_verse: When the priests are ready to leave the temple, they must go through these rooms before they return to the outer courtyard. They must leave their sacred clothes in these rooms and put on regular clothes before going anywhere near other people. The Size of the Temple Area
translation_verse: Nenye be nunɔlawo ge ɖe teƒe kɔkɔea la, womado go kple awu siwo wotsɔ subɔ le kɔkɔeƒe la, ayi ɖe xɔxɔnu si le kɔto la o. Elabe nu kɔkɔewo wonye. Woaɖɔli awu bubuwo ado hafi ado go age ɖe afi si nye dukɔmetɔwo tɔ.” Gbedoxɔ la nɔƒe ƒe dzidzeme

english_verse: After the man had finished measuring the buildings inside the temple area, he took me back through the east gate and measured the wall around this area.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi wòdzidze gbedoxɔ la me vɔ la, ekplɔm do goe to agbo si le ɣedzeƒe gome la nu, eye wòdzidze gbedoxɔ la ƒe nɔƒe godoo va kpe.

english_verse: He used his measuring stick to measure the east side of this wall; it was
translation_verse: Edzidze ɣedzeƒe gome kple nudzidzeti la; enɔ meta alafa eve bla atɔ̃.

english_verse: Then he measured the north side, the south side, and the west side of the wall, and they were each
translation_verse: Eyome la, etrɔ ɖe ɣetoɖoƒe gome, dzidzee kple nudzidzeti la, enɔ meta alafa eve bla atɔ̃.

english_verse: and so the temple area was a perfect square. The wall around this area separated what was sacred from what was ordinary.
translation_verse: Edzidze akpa eneawo. Gli ƒo xlãe; glia didi meta alafa eve bla atɔ̃ hekeke meta alafa eve bla atɔ̃. Wowɔe be nu siwo le kɔkɔe la ma ɖa tso esiwo mekɔ o la, gbɔ.

english_verse: The man took me back to the east gate of the temple,
translation_verse: Emegbe la, ekplɔm va agbo si dze ŋgɔ ɣedzeƒe gome la gbɔ.

english_verse: meters high, was the place where sacrifices were burned, and the four corners of the top section looked like the horns of a bull. The steps leading up to the altar were on the east side. The Dedication of the Altar
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, Israel ƒe Mawu la ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe tso ɣedzeƒe lɔƒo va. Eƒe vava ƒe ɖiɖi nɔ abe tɔ geɖewo ƒe hoowɔwɔ ene, eye eƒe ŋutikɔkɔe na anyigba klẽ.

english_verse: This vision was like the one I had seen when God came to destroy Jerusalem and like the one I had seen near the Chebar River. I immediately bowed with my face to the ground,
translation_verse: Ŋutega si mekpɔ la nɔ abe esi mekpɔ esi wòva be yeatsrɔ̃ du la ene, eye enɔ abe nɔnɔme si mekpɔ le Kebar-tɔsisi la to ene. Tete metsyɔ mo anyi.

english_verse: and the Lord's glory came through the east gate and into the temple.
translation_verse: Esi Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe la ge ɖe gbedoxɔ la me to agbo si dze ŋgɔ ɣedzeƒe me la,

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit lifted me to my feet and carried me to the inner courtyard, where I saw that the Lord's glory had filled the temple.
translation_verse: Gbɔgbɔ la kɔm ɖe dzi, eye wòkplɔm ge ɖe xɔxɔnu si le eme la me. Kpɔ ɖa, Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe yɔ gbedoxɔ la taŋ.

english_verse: But if the people and their kings stop worshiping other gods and tear down those memorials, I will live among them forever.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, na ne woate woƒe gbolowɔwɔ kple woƒe fiawo ƒe ŋutilã kukuawo ɖe adzɔge tso gbɔnye, eye manɔ wo dome tegbee.”

english_verse: The people of Israel must suffer shame for sinning against me, so tell them about my holy temple. Let them think about it,
translation_verse: “Wò amegbetɔ vi, ɖɔ gbedoxɔ la ƒe nɔnɔme kple ɖoɖo si dzi wotui ɖo la, na Israel-dukɔ la, ne woƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔawo nakpe ŋu na wo.

english_verse: then if they are truly sorry, describe for them the design and shape of the temple, the gates, the measurements, and how the buildings are arranged. Explain the regulations about worshiping there, then write down these things, so they can study and obey them.
translation_verse: Ne nu siwo katã wowɔ kpe ŋu na wo la, ɖɔ gbedoxɔ la ƒe nɔnɔme, ɖoɖo si me wòle, eƒe mɔnu siwo wotona gena ɖe eme kple esiwo wotona doa go kpakple eƒe nɔnɔme blibo la katã na wo. Na ne woanya eƒe ɖoɖowo kple sewo katã. Ŋlɔe ɖe anyi le wo ŋkume, ale be woalé ŋku ɖe wo ŋu awɔ woƒe sewo kple ɖoɖowo katã dzi.

english_verse: The temple area on my holy mountain must be kept sacred! This is the most important law about the temple. The Altar
translation_verse: Se si le gbedoxɔa ŋu lae nye esi: Teƒe si ƒo xlãe godoo va kpe ɖo le toa dzi la, nanɔ kɔkɔe ŋutɔŋutɔ. Kpɔ ɖa, esiae nye se si le gbedoxɔ la ŋu.” Vɔsamlekpui la

english_verse: According to the official standards, the altar in the temple had the following measurements: Around the bottom of the altar was a gutter
translation_verse: “Vɔsamlekpui la ƒe dzidzeti nye meta afã ” Eƒe anyinɔ kɔ sentimeta bla atɔ̃, eye wòkeke sentimeta bla atɔ̃. Etogawo keke sentimeta bla eve. Esia nye vɔsamlekpui la ƒe kɔkɔme.

english_verse: Each day for the next seven days, you must offer a goat and a bull and a ram as sacrifices for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Gbe sia gbe le ŋkeke adrẽ me la, ele na wò be nàtsɔ gbɔ̃ asa nuvɔ̃vɔe, eye nyitsu kple agbo si tso alẽhawo dome la, nakpe ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, after the altar is built, it must be dedicated by offering sacrifices on it and by splattering it with blood. Here is what you must do:
translation_verse: Egblɔ nam be: “Amegbetɔ vi, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: Vɔsamlekpui la ƒe sewoe nye esiawo: Le ŋkeke si dzi woɖii vɔ hena numemevɔsa le edzi kple ʋuhehlẽ ɖe eŋu la,

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe from the family of Zadok the priest are the only ones who may serve in my temple—this is my law. So give them a young bull to slaughter as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: àtsɔ nyitsu ɖeka na nunɔla siwo nye Levi viwo tso Zadok ƒe ƒome, siwo tena ɖe ŋunye hesubɔam la, ne woatsɔ asa nuvɔ̃vɔsae. Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: Take some of the animal's blood and smear it on the four corners of the altar, some on the corners of the middle section, and some more on the rim around its edge. That will purify the altar and make it fit for offering sacrifices to me.
translation_verse: Ele be nàtsɔ eƒe ʋu ƒe ɖe asisi ɖe vɔsamlekpui la ƒe dzo eneawo, eƒe kɔ ƒe dzogoe eneawo kple to si woɖo nɛ ƒo xlã la ŋu. Alea nàwɔ akɔ eŋuti, eye nàlé avui.

english_verse: Then take the body of the bull outside the temple area and burn it at the special place.
translation_verse: Ele na wò hã be nàtsɔ nuvɔ̃vɔsanyitsu la aɖatɔ dzoe ɖe teƒe si woɖo ɖi le gbedoxɔ la ŋu, le kɔkɔeƒe la godo.

english_verse: The next day, a goat that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice for sin. Purify the altar with its blood, just as you did with the blood of the bull.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke evea gbe la, nàtsɔ gbɔ̃tsu si sɔ blibo la awɔ nuvɔ̃vɔsae. Ale be vɔsamlekpui la ŋuti nakɔ abe ale si nyitsu la ƒe ʋu wɔe ene.

english_verse: Then choose a young bull and a young ram that have nothing wrong with them,
translation_verse: Ne èkɔ eŋuti vɔ la, ekema nàtsɔ nyitsu si sɔ blibo kple agbo si sɔ blibo tso alẽhawo dome asa vɔe.

english_verse: and bring them to my temple. The priests will sprinkle salt on them and offer them as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Ele be nàtsɔ wo aɖo Aƒetɔ ŋkume, eye nunɔlawo nawu dze ɖe wo dzi ahatsɔ wo asa numemevɔe na Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: The priests will purify the altar during those days, so that it will be acceptable to me and ready to use.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke adrẽ wòle be woatsɔ alé avu na vɔsamlekpui la, aklɔ eŋu ahakɔ eŋuti.

english_verse: From then on, the priests will use this altar to offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices to ask my blessing. Then I will be pleased with the people of Israel. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ne wowu ŋkeke siawo nu la, ekema nunɔlawo nasa numemevɔ kple akpedadavɔ, le vɔsamlekpui la dzi tso ŋkeke enyia gbe heyi, eye maxɔe na mi.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: The man took me back to the outer courtyard, near the east gate of the temple area. I saw that the doors to this gate were closed.
translation_verse: Tete wòkplɔm, trɔ va kɔkɔeƒe ƒe agbo si le kɔto, eye wòdze ŋgɔ ɣedzeƒe la nu; ke wotu agbo la.

english_verse: The Lord said: I, the Lord God of Israel, came through this gate, so it must remain closed forever! No one must ever use it.
translation_verse: Egblɔ nam be: “Ele be agbo sia nanɔ tutu. Mele be woaʋui o, eye ame aɖeke mato eme age ɖe eme o. Elabe Aƒetɔ, Israel ƒe Mawu to enu ge ɖe eme, eya ta ele be wòanɔ tutu.

english_verse: The ruler of Israel may come here to eat a sacrificial meal that has been offered to me, but he must use only the entrance room of this gate. People Who Are Not Allowed in the Temple
translation_verse: Amegã la koe ate ŋu anɔ eme aɖu abolo le Aƒetɔ ŋkume. Ele be wòato agbo la ƒe akpata la xa age ɖe eme, eye wòagado to afi ma ke.” Se siwo akplɔ gege ɖe gbedoxɔ la me

english_verse: Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the brightness of the Lord's glory had filled the temple, and I immediately bowed with my face to the ground.
translation_verse: Ekplɔm emegbe to agbo si le dzigbeme me heva gbedoxɔ la nu, eye kpɔ ɖa, esi melé ŋku ɖe eŋu la, mekpɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe wòyɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔ la taŋ. Tete metsyɔ mo anyi.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to give you the laws for my temple. So pay attention and listen carefully to what kind of people are allowed to come in the temple, and what kind are not.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nam be: “Amegbetɔ vi, lé ŋku ɖe nu siawo ŋu, nàkpɔ wo nyuie kple wò ŋku, eye nàlé to ɖe nu siwo katã gblɔ ge mala na wò tso Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔ la ƒe ɖoɖowo kple eƒe sewo ŋu la nyuie. Nàde dzesi ame siwo ƒomevi wòle be woaɖe mɔ na woage ɖe gbedoxɔ la me kple esiwo wòle be woaxe mɔ na tso kɔkɔeƒe la gbɔ.

english_verse: Tell those rebellious people of Israel: I, the Lord God, command you to stop your evil ways!
translation_verse: Gblɔ na Israel-dukɔ dzeaglã la be, Aƒetɔ Mawu be: O, Israel-dukɔ, mitsɔ miaƒe ŋunyɔnuawo katã se afi aɖe dzro,

english_verse: My temple has been disgraced, because you have let godless, stubborn foreigners come here when sacrifices are being offered to me. You have sinned and have broken our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: elabe miekplɔa amedzrowo, bolobolotɔwo kple ame siwo gbe dzimetɔtrɔ la, vaa nye kɔkɔeƒe la hegblẽa kɔ ɖo nɛ; ne mietsɔ ami kple ʋu sa vɔe hetsɔ nye nuɖuɖu nam la. Mietu nye nubabla la hekpe ɖe miaƒe ŋunyɔnuawo katã ŋu.

english_verse: Instead of following the proper ways to worship me, you have put foreigners in charge of worship at my temple.
translation_verse: Miegbe nye nu kɔkɔeawo dzi kpɔkpɔ. Ke mietsɔ amedzrowo ɖo nye nuwo nu le nye kɔkɔeƒe la.”

english_verse: And so I, the Lord God, say that no godless foreigner who disobeys me will be allowed in my temple. This includes any foreigner living in Israel. The Levites Are Punished The Lord said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Eya ta amedzrovi bolobolotɔ, esi metso aʋa le ŋutilã kple dzime o, le amedzro siwo katã le Israel-dukɔ la me la, mage ɖe nye kɔkɔeƒe la o.

english_verse: Some of the Levites turned their backs on me and joined the other people of Israel in worshiping idols. So these Levites must be punished!
translation_verse: Ke Levitɔ siwo tra yi adzɔge le gbɔnye, eye wobu mɔ dze legbawo yome esime Israel tra mɔ la, woawoe axɔ woƒe tohehe.

english_verse: They will still be allowed to serve me as temple workers by guarding the gates and by killing the animals to be sacrificed and by helping the worshipers.
translation_verse: Woawoe asubɔ le nye kɔkɔeƒe la, adzɔ gbedoxɔ la ƒe agbowo nu, eye woasubɔ le gbedoxɔ la me. Woawoe awu numemevɔsalã, asa vɔ ɖe dukɔ la nu, eye woanɔ dukɔ la ŋu asubɔ wo.

english_verse: But because these Levites served the people of Israel when they worshiped idols, I, the Lord God, promise that the Levites will be punished. They did not stop the Israelites from sinning,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be esi wosubɔ wo le woƒe legbawo gbɔ, eye wotrɔ zu nukikli na Israel-dukɔ la wòwɔ nuvɔ̃ ta la, meka atam ɖe wo ŋu be woahe to na wo.

english_verse: and now I will no longer let the Levites serve as my priests or come near anything sacred to me. They must suffer shame and disgrace for their disgusting sins.
translation_verse: Mele be woate ɖe ŋunye, asubɔm abe nunɔlawo ene loo, ate ɖe nye nu kɔkɔe aɖeke ŋu loo, alo nu kɔkɔewo ƒe kɔkɔetɔwo ƒe ɖeke ŋu o. Ke boŋ le ŋunyɔnu siwo wowɔ ta la, ele be ŋu nakpe wo.

english_verse: They will be responsible for all the hard work that must be done in the temple. Rules for Priests The Lord said:
translation_verse: Togbɔ be ele alea hã la, maɖo wo dɔ nu le gbedoxɔ la me, be woanɔ subɔsubɔdɔ siwo katã hiã be woawɔ la wɔm le eme.” Nunɔlawo

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe who are descendants of Zadok the priest were faithful to me, even when the rest of the Israelites turned away. And so, these priests will continue to serve as my priests and to offer the fat and the blood of sacrifices.
translation_verse: “Ke nunɔla siwo nye Levi viwo tso Zadok ƒe ƒome la me, ame siwo subɔ le nye kɔkɔeƒe la esime Israelviwo tra le yonyeme la, woate ɖe ŋunye asubɔm. Woatsi tsitre ɖe ŋkunye me atsɔ ami kple ʋu asa vɔe nam. Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: They will come into my temple, where they will offer sacrifices at my altar and lead others in worship.
translation_verse: Woawoe age ɖe nye kɔkɔeƒe la, ate ɖe nye kplɔ̃ ŋu, asubɔm, eye woakpɔ nye dɔwo dzi.

english_verse: When they come to the inner courtyard, they must wear their linen priestly clothes. My priests must never wear anything made of wool when they are on duty in this courtyard or in the temple.
translation_verse: Ne woge ɖe xɔxɔnu emetɔ ƒe agbowo me la, ele na wo be woado aklalawuwo; lãfuvɔwu aɖeke meganɔ wo ŋu esime wole subɔsubɔdɔ wɔm le xɔxɔnu emetɔ ƒe agbowo kple xɔ la me o.

english_verse: Even their turbans and underwear must be made of linen to keep my priests from sweating when they work.
translation_verse: Ele be aklalatablanu nanɔ wo ta, eye woado aklalagbotɛ. Womegatsɔ naneke si nana be fifia tea ame la bla ali dzi o.

english_verse: And before they leave to join the other people in the outer courtyard, they must take off their priestly clothes, then place them in the sacred rooms and put on their regular clothes. That way, no one will touch their sacred clothes and be harmed.
translation_verse: Nenye be wodo go yi ɖe dukɔ la gbɔ le xɔxɔnu si le kɔto la, ele be woaɖe awu siwo me wonɔ subɔ la da ɖe xɔvi kɔkɔeawo me, eye woado awu bubuwo; ne womagatsɔ woƒe awu awɔe be dukɔ la ŋuti nakɔ o.

english_verse: Priests must never shave their heads when they are mourning. But they must keep their hair properly trimmed and not let it grow too long.
translation_verse: Mele be woalũ ta kolikoli alo ana woƒe ɖa nato ʋluyaa o. Ke boŋ woafiã ta woasɔ dzaa ko.

english_verse: They must not drink wine before going to the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Mele be nunɔla aɖeke nano wain ne wòle gegem ɖe xɔxɔnu si le eme la me o.

english_verse: A priest must not marry a divorced woman; he can marry only a virgin from Israel or the widow of another priest.
translation_verse: Mele be woaɖe ahosi alo nyɔnu si wogbe la o. Ke boŋ woaɖe ɖetugbi leaƒe tso ƒome si tso Israel-dukɔ la me loo, alo ahosi si nye nunɔla aɖe srɔ̃ kpɔ.

english_verse: Priests must teach my people the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary, and between what is clean and what is unclean.
translation_verse: Ele na wo be woafia vovototo si le nu kɔkɔe kple nu makɔmakɔ dome, eye woafia nye dukɔ la be woade vovototo nu si medza o kple esi dza la dome.

english_verse: They will make decisions in difficult legal cases, according to my own laws. They must also observe the religious festivals my Law requires and must always respect the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Woawoe adrɔ̃ nya ne dzre dzɔ, eye woadrɔ̃e ɖe nye ɖoɖowo nu. Woakpɔ nye sewo kple ɖoɖowo dzi le ŋkekenyui siwo katã meɖo la dzi, eye ele be woawɔ nye dzudzɔgbe la wòanɔ kɔkɔe.

english_verse: Touching a dead body will make a person unclean. So a priest must not go near a dead body, unless it is one of his parents or children, or his brother or unmarried sister.
translation_verse: Mele be woate ɖe ame kuku ŋuti agblẽ kɔ ɖo na wo ɖokui o. Ke woate ŋu awɔe nenye be wo tɔ́ alo wo nɔ, wo viŋutsu alo wo vinyɔnu, wo nɔviŋutsu alo wo nɔvinyɔnu si meɖe srɔ̃ o la ku.

english_verse: If a priest touches a dead body, he is unclean and must go through a ceremony to make himself clean. Then seven days later,
translation_verse: Nenye be egblẽ kɔ ɖo alea la, ele nɛ be wòaxlẽ ŋkeke adrẽ na eɖokui, ekema eŋuti kɔ.

english_verse: he must go to the inner courtyard of the temple and offer a sacrifice for sin. After that, he may once again serve as my priest. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Gbe si gbe wòge ɖe kɔkɔeƒe la, heyi ɖe xɔxɔnu si le eme be yeasubɔ la, nesa nuvɔ̃vɔ ɖe eɖokui ta.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: I myself will provide for my priests, and so they won't receive any land of their own.
translation_verse: “Domenyinu aɖeke manɔ wo si o. Nyee nye woƒe domenyinu, eye migana gomekpɔkpɔ aɖeke wo le Israel o. Nyee nye woƒe gome.

english_verse: Instead, they will receive part of the grain sacrifices, as well as part of the sacrifices for sin and sacrifices to make things right. They will also be given everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Woawoe aɖu nuɖuɖuvɔsa, nuvɔ̃vɔsa kple fɔɖiɖivɔsa, eye nu sia nu si wotsɔ na Mawu le Israel, esi amewo mekpɔ mɔ aɖu o la, anye wo tɔ.

english_verse: Priests must not eat any bird or animal that dies a natural death or that has been killed by a wild animal.
translation_verse: Nunɔlawo mekpɔ mɔ aɖu lã alo xe kuku aɖeke o, eɖanye ɖe woku le wo ɖokui si loo, alo nue lé wo o.”

english_verse: So from now on, you must use honest weights and measures.
translation_verse: “Nudzidzenu kple nudanu siwo sɔ kple wo nɔewo la nanɔ mia si,

english_verse: The Festival of Shelters will begin on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and will continue for seven days. On each day of this festival, the ruler will provide the same number of animals that he did each day during Passover, as well as the same amount of grain and olive oil for the sacrifices.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti adrẽlia ƒe ŋkeke wui atɔ̃a gbe la, woawɔ alea ke ŋkeke adrẽ sɔŋ hena ŋkekenyui la ɖuɖu. Nuvɔ̃vɔsa, numemevɔsa kple nuɖuɖuvɔsa kpakple amiawo nanɔ abe ekemɛawo ene.”

english_verse: kilometers wide. This will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem. Land for Israel's Ruler The Lord said:
translation_verse: Le teƒe kɔkɔe sia la, woadzidze teƒe si adidi kilometa wui eve kple afã, eye wòakeke kilometa atɔ̃ hena kɔkɔeƒewo ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la tutu.

english_verse: The Lord God said: You leaders of Israel have cheated and abused my people long enough! I want you to stop sinning and start doing what is right and fair. You must never again force my people off their own land. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “O, Israel-megãwo, eva glo! Miɖe asi le ŋutasesẽ kple ameteteɖeto ŋu. Midrɔ̃ ʋɔnu dzɔdzɔe, eye miwɔ nuteƒe. Midzudzɔ nye dukɔmetɔwo nyanya de gbe.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: The ephah will be the standard dry measure, and the bath will be the standard liquid measure. Their size will be based on the homer, which will equal ten ephahs or ten baths.
translation_verse: efa kple bat ɖe akpa ewo la ne wòanye bat ɖeka alo efa ɖeka. Xomer nanye dzidzenu si atso nya me ɣe sia ɣi.

english_verse: The same ceremony must also be done on the seventh day of the month, so that anyone who sins accidentally or without knowing it will be forgiven, and so that my temple will remain holy.
translation_verse: Woawɔ nenema ke le ɣleti la ƒe ŋkeke adrẽa gbe, le ame siwo ɖe ŋu ɖi alo wɔ nu le manyamanya me la ta, ale be mialé avu na gbedoxɔ la.”

english_verse: Leaders of Israel, the people must bring you one sixtieth of their grain harvests as offerings to me.
translation_verse: “Miaƒe adzɔ si miana ayi ale: Woaɖe lu efa adeliawo ƒe ɖeka le xomer ɖe sia ɖe ŋu; ƒo hã nenema.

english_verse: The people of Israel will bring you these offerings.
translation_verse: Ele be dukɔ bliboa le anyigba la dzi nana adzɔ sia Israel-megã la.

english_verse: But during New Moon Festivals, Sabbath celebrations, and other religious feasts, you leaders will be responsible for providing animals for the sacrifices, as well as the grain and wine. All these will be used for the sacrifices for sin, the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices to please me, and those to ask my blessing. I will be pleased and will forgive the sins of my people. The Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: Enye amegã la ƒe dɔdeasi be wòana woasa numemevɔ, nuɖuɖuvɔ kple nunonovɔ le ŋkekenyuiwo dzi le dzinu yeyewo kple dzudzɔgbewo dzi le Israel ƒe takpegbe siwo katã woɖo na wo la dzi. Eyae ana woasa nuvɔ̃vɔwo, nuɖuɖuvɔwo, numemevɔwo kple akpedadavɔwo atsɔ lé avui na Israel-dukɔ la.” Ŋkeke nyuiwo

english_verse: Each day of the festival he is to bring seven bulls and seven rams as sacrifices to please me, and he must bring a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke adrẽ siwo me wole ŋkekenyui la ɖum la, ele be wòana woatsɔ nyitsuvi adrẽ kple agbo adrẽ siwo le blibo la asa numemevɔ na Aƒetɔ. Awu ɖeka gbe sia gbe, eye woasa nuvɔ̃vɔ kple gbɔ̃tsu ɖeka gbe sia gbe.

english_verse: The Lord God said: On the first day of the first month, a young bull that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to purify the temple.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Le ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la, lé nyitsuvi ɖeka si de blibo nàtsɔ ɖe nuvɔ̃ ɖae le kɔkɔeƒe la ŋu.

english_verse: The priest will take some blood from this sacrifice and smear it on the doorposts of the temple, as well as on the four corners of the altar and on the doorposts of the gates that lead into the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Nunɔla la natsɔ nuvɔ̃vɔsalã la ƒe ʋu ƒe ɖe asisi ɖe gbedoxɔ la ƒe ʋɔtrutiwo, vɔsamlekpui la ƒe kɔwo ƒe dzogoe eneawo kple xɔxɔnu si le eme la ƒe ʋɔtrutiwo ŋu.

english_verse: Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, and continuing for seven days, everyone will celebrate Passover and eat bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: “Le ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke wui enelia dzi la, miaɖu Paska, eye woaɖu abolo si meʋã o la, ŋkeke adrẽ.

english_verse: On the first day, the ruler will bring a bull to offer as a sacrifice for his sins and for the sins of the people.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe la, ele be amegã la nana woatsɔ nyitsuvi ɖeka asa nuvɔ̃vɔe ɖe eya ŋutɔ kple dukɔ blibo la ta.

english_verse: He will also provide nine kilograms of grain and three liters of olive oil to be offered with each bull and each ram.
translation_verse: Ele nɛ hã be wòatsɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsa bli efa ɖeka akpe ɖe nyitsuvi ɖeka ɖe sia ɖe ŋu, efa ɖeka na agbo ɖe sia ɖe, eye ami lita etɔ̃ nakpe ɖe bli la ŋu.

english_verse: The Lord said: The east gate of the inner courtyard must remain closed during the six working days of each week. But on the Sabbath and on the first day of the month, this gate will be opened.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Woatu xɔxɔnu si le eme, si dze ŋgɔ ɣedzeƒe la ƒe agbo le dɔwɔŋkeke adeawo dzi. Ke woaʋui le dzudzɔgbe kple dzinu yeye dzi.

english_verse: Israel's ruler will go from the outer courtyard into the entrance room of this gate and stand in the doorway while the priest offers sacrifices to ask my blessing and sacrifices to please me. The ruler will bow with his face to the ground to show that he has worshiped me. Then he will leave, and the gate will remain open until evening.
translation_verse: Amegã la nato agbo la ƒe akpata nu le gota, eye wòage ɖe eme, ava tɔ ɖe agboa ƒe ʋɔtruti ŋu anɔ tsitre. Nunɔlawo nanɔ eƒe numemevɔsa kple akpedadavɔsa wɔm, eya nanɔ gbe dom ɖa le agboa ƒe agbalinu. Emegbe la, ele nɛ be wòado go adzo, ke womatu agbo la o, va se ɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: Each Sabbath and on the first day of each month, the people of Israel must also come to the east gate and worship me.
translation_verse: Ele be dukɔ blibo la nado gbe ɖa le Aƒetɔ ŋkume le agbo sia nu le dzudzɔgbewo kple dzinu yeyewo dzi.

english_verse: On the Sabbath, the ruler will bring six lambs and one ram to be offered as sacrifices to please me. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: Numemevɔsa si amegã la nana woawɔ le dzudzɔgbe la dzi la nanye alẽvi ade siwo le blibo kple agbo ɖeka si le blibo,

english_verse: With the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: eye bli efa ɖeka nakpe ɖe agbo la ƒe nuɖuɖuvɔsa la ŋu. Nuɖuɖuvɔsa ƒe bli si akpe ɖe alẽviawo ŋu la nanɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe ŋutete nu. Hekpe ɖe esiawo ŋu la, ami lita etɔ̃ nakpe ɖe bli efa ɖeka ɖe sia ɖe ŋu.

english_verse: The ruler is to bring six lambs, a bull, and a ram to be offered as sacrifices at the New Moon Festival. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: Le dzinu yeye dzi la, ele nɛ be wòatsɔ nyitsuvi si le blibo la ana woasa vɔe akpe ɖe alẽvi ade kple agbo ɖeka siwo le blibo la ŋu.

english_verse: With the bull and the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Nuɖuɖuvɔsa efa ɖeka nakpe ɖe nyitsuvi la kple agbo la hã ŋu. Le alẽviawo gome la, newɔ eƒe ŋutete, ami lita etɔ̃ nakpe ɖe lã ɖe sia ɖe ƒe bli ŋu.

english_verse: The ruler must come through the entrance room of the east gate and leave the same way.
translation_verse: Ne amegã la be yeage ɖe eme la, neto agboa ƒe akpata nu yi ɖe eme; negato afi ma ke do go.”

english_verse: When my people come to worship me during any festival, they must always leave by the opposite gate from which they came: Those who come in the north gate must leave by the south gate, and those who come in the south gate must leave by the north gate.
translation_verse: “Ne dukɔ la va Aƒetɔ ŋkume le ŋkekenyuiwo dzi la, ame si to dzigbemegbo la nu ge ɖe eme be yeado gbe ɖa la, nato anyigbemegbo la nu ado, eye ame si to anyigbemegbo la nu ge ɖe eme la nato dzigbemegbo la nu ado. Ame aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ atrɔ do to agbo si nu wòto ge ɖe eme la o, ke boŋ ame sia ame nedze ŋgɔ tẽe ado.

english_verse: Their ruler will come in at the same time they do and leave at the same time they leave.
translation_verse: Ne woge ɖe eme la, amegã la nage ɖe eme kpli wo, eye wòado go kpli wo nenye be wodo go.”

english_verse: At all other festivals and celebrations, nine kilograms of grain will be offered with a bull, and nine kilograms will be offered with a ram. The worshipers can offer as much grain as they want with each lamb. Three liters of olive oil must be offered with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: “Le ŋkekenyuiwo dzi kple azãɖugbewo la, nuɖuɖuvɔsa si kpe ɖe nyitsuvi la ŋu la nanye efa ɖeka. Nenema ke wòanɔ le agbo la hã gome, eye alẽviawo tɔ la, woawɔe le ame ƒe ŋutete nu hekpe ɖe ami lita etɔ̃ ŋu na bli efa ɖeka ɖe sia ɖe.

english_verse: If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
translation_verse: Nenye be amegã la ɖo be yeasa vɔ faa ko, eɖanye numemevɔsa loo, alo akpedadavɔsa kple lɔlɔ̃nu faa na Aƒetɔ la, woaʋu agbo si dze ŋgɔ ɣedzeƒe la nɛ, eye wòana woasa vɔ la nɛ abe ale si wòwɔnɛ le dzudzɔgbe lae ene. Emegbe la, ele nɛ be wòado go, eye ne edo go la, woatu agbo la.” Gbe sia gbe vɔsa

english_verse: Each morning a year-old lamb that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to please me.
translation_verse: “Ele nɛ be wòana alẽvi si xɔ ƒe ɖeka, esi ŋu kpɔtsɔtsɔ mele o la, gbe sia gbe, be woatsɔ awɔ numemevɔsae na Aƒetɔ. Ele be wòanae ŋdi sia ŋdi.

english_verse: Along with it, two kilograms of fine flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. This law will never change—
translation_verse: Ele be wòatsɔ wɔ kilo eve kple ami lita ɖeka si woatsɔ ablu wɔ lae la akpe ɖe eŋu ŋdi sia ŋdi atsɔ wɔ nuɖuɖuvɔsae na Aƒetɔ. Numemevɔsa ƒe ɖoɖo mavɔe nye esia.

english_verse: The Lord God said: If the ruler of Israel gives some of his land to one of his children, it will belong to the ruler's child as part of the family property.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu be: “Nenye be amegã la wɔ nunana na viawo dometɔ aɖe tso nu si nye eƒe domenyinu me la, anye viawo tɔ, anye domenyinyi ƒe nunɔamesi na wo.

english_verse: But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
translation_verse: Ke ne ewɔ nunana na eƒe subɔlawo dometɔ aɖe la, anye etɔ va se ɖe ablɔɖeƒe la me. Ekema wòagatrɔe na amegã la. Viawo koe kpɔ mɔ axɔ eƒe nunana la wòatsi wo si me.

english_verse: The ruler must never abuse my people by taking land from them. Any land he gives his children must already belong to him. The Sacred Kitchens
translation_verse: Amegã la mekpɔ mɔ axɔ amewo ƒe domenyinu le wo si ahanyà wo ɖa sesẽtɔe le woƒe nunɔamesiwo gbɔ o. Eya ŋutɔ ƒe domenyinu ko wòkpɔ mɔ atsɔ na viawo, ale be womaxɔ nye dukɔmetɔ aɖeke ƒe nunɔamesi le esi o.” Dzodoƒe siwo anɔ gbedoxɔ la ŋu

english_verse: The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard
translation_verse: Azɔ ekplɔm to mɔnu si le agbo la xa la me, heva nunɔlawo ƒe xɔvi kɔkɔe siwo le dzigbeme la gbɔ, eye mekpɔ teƒe aɖe le xɔviawo ƒe kɔto le ɣetoɖoƒe.

english_verse: We went back to the outer courtyard and walked past the four corners.
translation_verse: Azɔ ekplɔm va xɔxɔnu si le egodo, eye wòkplɔm to eƒe dzogoe eneawo dzi. Xɔxɔnu le dzogoe ɖe sia ɖe me.

english_verse: Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires.
translation_verse: Woɖo gli ƒo xlã wo ame eneawo katã heɖi mlekpuiwo ɖe wo gɔme va kpe ɖo.

english_verse: The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ nam be: “Esiawoe nye dzodoƒe siwo anye ame siwo subɔna le gbedoxɔ la me la ƒe vɔsalãwo ɖaƒe hena dukɔ la.”

english_verse: The man took me back to the temple, where I saw a stream flowing from under the entrance. It began in the south part of the temple, where it ran past the altar and continued east through the courtyard.
translation_verse: Egbugbɔm va gbedoxɔ la ƒe ʋɔtru nu, eye kpɔ ɖa, tsi nɔ sisím tso gbedoxɔ la ƒe kpui la gɔme ɖo ta ɣedzeƒe lɔƒo . Tsi la nɔ sisím tso kpui la ƒe anyigbeme, le vɔsamlekpui la ƒe anyigbe lɔƒo.

english_verse: We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
translation_verse: Tete wòkplɔm do goe to dzigbemegbo la nu, eye wòna metrɔ va egodo va agbo si le egodo, si dze ŋgɔ ɣedzeƒe la nu, eye tsi la nɔ dzidzim le anyigbeme.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.” We walked to the riverbank,
translation_verse: Egblɔ nam be: “Amegbetɔ vi, èkpɔ nu sia?” Tete wòkplɔm gbugbɔ yi tɔa ƒe godzi.

english_verse: where I saw dozens of trees on each side.
translation_verse: Esi metrɔ yina la, mekpɔ be ati geɖewo mie ɖe tɔsisi la ƒe go eveawo dzi.

english_verse: The man said: This water flows eastward to the Jordan River valley and empties into the Dead Sea, where it turns the salt water into fresh water.
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ nam be: “Tsi sia sí ɖo ta ɣedzeƒenutowo me, to Yordan-bali la me. Ne etsa ge ɖe atsiaƒu si mele tsatsam o la me la, tsi la azu tsi nyui.

english_verse: Wherever this water flows, there will be all kinds of animals and fish, because it will bring life and fresh water to the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Afi sia afi si tsi la ɖo tae la, nu gbagbe siwo katã nɔa ha me la, agbɔ agbe, eye tɔmelãwo ado fũu. Elabe tsi ɖo ta afi ma, ale be atsiaƒu la natrɔ zu tsi nyui. Eya ta teƒe ɖe sia ɖe si tsia de la, nuwo atsi agbe.

english_verse: From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ɖɔkplɔlawo anɔ atsiaƒua to tso En-Gedi va se ɖe En-Eglayim. Anye teƒe siwo woada ɖɔ ɖo. Eƒe tɔmelã vovovowo asɔ gbɔ kpaŋkpaŋ abe Atsiaƒu Gã la me lãwo ene.

english_verse: But the marshes along the shore will remain salty, so that people can use the salt from them.
translation_verse: Ke teƒe siwo nye siiwo kple táwo la matrɔ o, dze anɔ wo me.

english_verse: Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people. The Borders of the Land
translation_verse: Le tɔsisi la ƒe go eveawo dzi la, ati vovovo siwo tsea ku woɖuna la, anɔ anyi. Woƒe aŋgbawo mayrɔ loo, alo agbe kutsetse ɣeaɖekeɣi o. Ke woatse ku yeye ɣleti sia ɣleti. Elabe woƒe tsi tsa tso kɔkɔeƒe la. Woƒe kutsetsewo anye nuɖuɖu, eye woƒe aŋgbawo ayɔ dɔ.” Anyigba la ƒe liƒowo

english_verse: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean Sea, then continue eastward to Hethlon, to Lebo-Hamath, then across to Zedad,
translation_verse: Anyigba la ƒe liƒo la anɔ ale: “Le dzigbeme lɔƒo la, atso Atsiaƒu Gã la nu ato Xetlon ava Xamat-mɔnu atɔ edzi va ɖo Zedad,

english_verse: So the northern border will run between the Mediterranean Sea and Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath.
translation_verse: Ale liƒo la atso ƒu la nu va ɖo Xazar-Enon, si le Damasko ƒe liƒo dzi le dzigbeme lɔƒo va ɖo Xamat ƒe dzigbeme liƒo dzi.”

english_verse: The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
translation_verse: “Le ɣedzeƒekpa dzi la, liƒo la alɔ ɖe enu tso Xazar-Enon ato Xauran kple Damasko dome. Azɔ Yordan-bali la ŋu ato Gilead kple Israel-nyigba la dome ayi aɖatu atsiaƒu la le ɣedzeƒe gome va se ɖe Tamar ke. Esia anye ɣedzeƒekpa dzi.”

english_verse: The southern border will begin at Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and will end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: “Le anyigbeme la, liƒo la atso Tamar ayi keke Meriba-Kades tsiwo gbɔ. Ekema atso afi ma ato Egipte-tɔʋu la ŋu ava tu Atsiaƒu Gã la. Esia anye anyigbemekpa dzi.”

english_verse: The western border will run north along the Mediterranean Sea to a point just west of Lebo-Hamath.
translation_verse: “Le ɣetoɖoƒe lɔƒo la, Atsiaƒu Gã la anye liƒo va se ɖe teƒe si dze ŋgɔ Xamat. Esia anye ɣetoɖoƒekpa dzi.”

english_verse: That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: “Ale miama anyigba sia ɖe mia nɔewo dome ɖe Israel-toawo nu.

english_verse: It will belong to the Israelites and to any foreigners living among them whose children were born in Israel. These foreigners must be treated like any other Israelite citizen, and they will receive
translation_verse: Miama anyigba la ɖe mia nɔewo dome abe domenyinu ene na mia ɖokui kple amedzrovi siwo le mia dome, eye wodzi viwo ɖe mia dome la. Woanɔ na mi abe Israelvi dzɔleaƒeawo ene. Woawo hã woaxɔ domenyinu abe miawo ke ene le Israel-toawo dome.

english_verse: a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: To si me amedzrovia le la, eya mee wòaxɔ eƒe domenyinu le.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe.

english_verse: South of Judah's territory will be a special section of land. Its length will be twelve and a half kilometers, and its width will run from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. My temple will be located in this section of land.
translation_verse: “Tso Yuda ƒe liƒo nu tso ɣedzeƒe va se ɖe ɣetoɖoƒe la, anye akpa aɖe si woaɖe ɖe aga. Nekeke kilometa wui eve kple afã, eƒe didime nesɔ kple mama ɖeka si xɔm toawo le la tso ɣedzeƒe va se ɖe ɣetoɖoƒe, kɔkɔeƒe la nanɔ eƒe titina.

english_verse: An area in the center of this land will belong to me. It will be twelve and a half kilometers long and ten kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Akpa si miaɖe ɖe aga na Aƒetɔ la nadidi kilometa wui eve kple afã, eye wòakeke kilometa ewo.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will give half of my sacred land to the priests. Their share will be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide, and my temple will be right in the middle.
translation_verse: Teƒe kɔkɔe si woaɖe ɖe aga lae nye esi: Nunɔlawo nakpɔ gome si adidi kilometa wui eve kple afã le dzigbeme lɔƒo, akeke kilometa atɔ̃ le ɣetoɖoƒekpa dzi, eye wòakeke kilometa atɔ̃ le ɣedzeƒekpa dzi, eye eƒe didime le anyigbeme la nanɔ kilometa wui eve kple afã. Aƒetɔ ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la nanɔ teƒe sia titina.

english_verse: Only priests who are descendants of Zadok will receive a share of this sacred land, because they remained faithful to me when the Levites and the rest of the Israelites started sinning.
translation_verse: Teƒe sia anye nunɔla siwo ŋuti wokɔ la tɔ. Woawoe nye Zadok vi siwo wɔa nye subɔsubɔdɔ la. Woawo metrɔ dzo le yonyeme abe Levi viwo ene esime Israel tra mɔ ʋu le yonyeme o.

english_verse: The land belonging to the priests will be the most sacred area and will lie south of the area that belongs to the Levites.
translation_verse: Anye nunana tɔxɛ na wo tso adzɔ kɔkɔe si woɖe le anyigba la ŋuti la me. Anye teƒe si kɔ̀ ŋutɔŋutɔ, eye wòaɖe liƒo kple Levi viwo ƒe anyigba.

english_verse: I will give the other half of my sacred land to the Levites. Their share will also be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide,
translation_verse: Levi viwo nexɔe ɖe nunɔlawo ƒe liƒo nu. Wo tɔ nedidi kilometa wui eve kple afã, eye wòakeke kilometa atɔ̃. Didime la katã nanɔ kilometa wui eve kple afã, eye wòakeke kilometa ewo.

english_verse: and they must never sell or trade any of this land—it is the best land and belongs to me.
translation_verse: Womadzra eƒe akpa aɖeke alo aɖɔlii o. Womana anyigba nyui tɔxɛ sia nage ɖe ame bubu aɖeke si me o. Elabe nu kɔkɔe wònye na Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: South of my sacred land will be a section twelve and a half kilometers long and three kilometers wide. It will not be sacred, but will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem, together with its houses and pastureland.
translation_verse: “Anyigba la ƒe akpa si susɔ, eye wòdidi kilometa wui eve kple afã hekeke kilometa eve kple afã la nanye dua haho ƒe anyigba. Woatso aƒewo ɖe edzi, eye wòanye lãnyiƒe. Woatso du la ɖe anyigba la titina.

english_verse: The land on the east and west sides of the city limits will be farmland for the people of Jerusalem; both sections will be five kilometers long and three kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Anyigba si susɔ, eye wòdo liƒo kple kɔkɔeƒea la ƒe didime lanɔ meta akpe atɔ̃ le ɣedzeƒe, eye wòle meta akpe atɔ̃ le ɣetoɖoƒe hã, eye wòamlɔ kɔkɔeƒe la ŋu. Eƒe nukuwo nanye nuɖuɖu na dua me dɔwɔlawo.

english_verse: People from the city will farm the land, no matter which tribe they belong to.
translation_verse: Dua me dɔwɔla siwo tso to vovovoawo me la, woawoe wòle be woade agble ɖe edzi.

english_verse: And so the center of this special section of land will be for my sacred land, as well as for the city and its property. The land will be a square, twelve and a half kilometers on each side.
translation_verse: Akpa blibo sia si miaɖe ɖe aga la ƒe dzidzeme nasɔ le akpa sia akpa. Dzidzeme la nanɔ kilometa wui eve kple afã le go ɖe sia ɖe dzi. Teƒe sia lanye teƒe kɔkɔe la, eye wòanye dukɔ la tɔ.”

english_verse: The regions east and west of this square of land will belong to the ruler of Israel. His property will run east to the Jordan River and west to the Mediterranean Sea. In the very center of his property will be my sacred land, as well as the temple,
translation_verse: “Teƒe si susɔ ɖe kɔkɔeƒe ƒe akpa eveawo, si le dukɔ la ƒe anyigba ŋu la, nanye amegã la tɔ. Nekeke ɖe enu tso anyigba kɔkɔe la gbɔ kilometa wui eve kple afã ava ɖo ɣedzeƒeliƒo dzi, eye wòakeke kilometa wui eve kple afã ava ɖo ɣetoɖoƒeliƒo dzi. Amlɔ toawo ƒe anyigba xa. Anye amegã la ƒe anyigba. Memama kɔkɔe la si ƒe titina gbedoxɔa ƒe kɔkɔeƒe la le

english_verse: together with the share belonging to the Levites and the city of Jerusalem. The northern border of the ruler's property will be the land that belongs to Judah, and the southern border will be the land that belongs to Benjamin. The Division of Land among Tribes in the South The Lord God said:
translation_verse: kple Levi viwo ƒe nunɔamesi kpakple dua ƒe nunɔamesi, nanɔ nu si nye amegã la tɔ la titina. Amegã la ƒe anyigba namlɔ Yuda kple Benyamin ƒe anyigbawo dome.” To bubuawo ƒe anyigba

english_verse: Gad's southern border is also the southern border of Israel. It will begin at the town of Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Le Gad tɔ nu le anyigbeme la, liƒo la natso Tamar ayi Meriba-Kades-tsi la nu. Atso afi ma ayi ɖe Egipte-tɔʋu la gbɔ ava tu Atsiaƒu Gã la.

english_verse: That's how the land of Israel will be divided among the twelve tribes. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Gates of Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: Esia nye anyigba si ŋu miadzidze nu ɖo ahama abe domenyinu ene ɖe Israel ƒe toawo dome, eye esiawoe nye gome vovovo siwo woakpɔ.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe. Yerusalem-gbowo

english_verse: and so the total length of the wall will be ten kilometers. The new name of the city will be “The-Lord-Is-Here!”
translation_verse: Dua ƒe lolome katã ƒo xlã adidi meta akpe asieke. Woatsɔ ŋkɔ na dua tso ɣe ma ɣi dzi be: Aƒetɔ le afi ma.”

english_verse: I am Hosea son of Beeri. When Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah, and when Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel, the Lord spoke this message to me. Hosea's Family
translation_verse: Gbedeasi sia nye nya si Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Hosea, Beer vi, be wòayi aɖagblɔ esime Uziya, Yotam, Axaz kple Xizkiya nye fiawo le Yuda, eye Yerobeam, Yoas vi, nye fia le Israel. Hosea srɔ̃ kple viawo

english_verse: The Lord said, “Hosea, Israel has betrayed me like an unfaithful wife. Marry such a woman and have children by her.”
translation_verse: Esime Aƒetɔ ƒo nu to Hosea dzi zi gbãtɔ na Israel la, egblɔ na Hosea be: “Yi nàɖe gbolo ne wòadzi ahasiviwo na wò. Elabe dukɔ la mewɔ nuteƒe nam o, eye wotrɔ le Aƒetɔ yome.”

english_verse: So I married Gomer the daughter of Diblaim, and we had a son.
translation_verse: Ale Hosea yi ɖaɖe srɔ̃. Eŋkɔe nye Gomer, Diblayim vinyɔnu. Edzi ŋutsuvi nɛ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Hosea, name your son Jezreel, because I will soon punish the descendants of King Jehu of Israel for the murders he committed in Jezreel Valley. I will destroy his kingdom,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Hosea be: “Tsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be ‘Yezreel’, elabe eteƒe madidi o mahe to na Israel-fia le ame siwo wo tɔgbui Yehu wu le Yezreel la ta. Mana Israel-fiaɖuƒe la agbã.

english_verse: and in Jezreel Valley I will break the power of Israel.”
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi me la, maxɔ aʋawɔŋusẽ le Israel-dukɔ si le Yezreel-bali me.”

english_verse: Later, Gomer had a daughter, and the Lord said, “Name her Lo-Ruhamah, because I will no longer have mercy and forgive Israel.
translation_verse: Gomer gafɔ fu, eye wòdzi nyɔnuvi. Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Hosea be: “Tsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be: ‘Amemakpɔnublanuina’ elabe nyemagakpɔ nublanui na Israel alo atsɔ nu akee azɔ kura o.

english_verse: But I am the Lord God of Judah, and I will have mercy and save Judah by my own power—not by wars and arrows or swords and cavalry.”
translation_verse: Ke makpɔ nublanui na Yudatɔwo ya. Nye Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la, maxɔ na wo gake manye to aʋawɔwɔ me ale be matsɔ da kple dati, yi, sɔ kple sɔdolawo axɔ na woe o.”

english_verse: After Gomer had stopped nursing Lo-Ruhamah, she had another son.
translation_verse: Esi Gomer tso no na Amemakpɔnublanuina la, egafɔ fu, eye wòdzi ŋutsuvi.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Name him Lo-Ammi, because these people are not mine, and I am not their God.” Hope for Israel
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Hosea be: “Tsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be ‘Amemanyenyedukɔe’ elabe mienye nye dukɔ o, eye nye hã nyemenye miaƒe Mawu o.” Mawu agaxɔ na Israel

english_verse: Someday it will be impossible to count the people of Israel, because there will be as many of them as there are grains of sand along the seashore. They are now called “Not My People,” but in the future they will be called “Children of the Living God.”
translation_verse: Israel-dukɔmetɔwo ava sɔ gbɔ fũu abe ƒutake ene; womate ŋu adzidze wo alo axlẽ wo o. Ke afi si wogblɔ na wo le be: “Mienye nye dukɔ o” la, woagblɔ na wo be: “Mawu gbagbe la viŋutsuwo.”

english_verse: Israel and Judah will unite and choose one leader. Then they will take back their land, and this will be a great day for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Woaƒo ƒu Yuda-dukɔ kple Israel-dukɔ eye woatia tatɔ ɖeka na wo ɖokui. Woaho adzo le anyigba la dzi, elabe Yezreel ŋkeke la anye ŋkeke gã aɖe.

english_verse: So let your brothers be called “My People” and your sisters be called “Shown Mercy.” The Lord Promises To Punish Israel
translation_verse: Miyɔ mia nɔviŋutsu be “Nyedukɔ”, eye miyɔ mia nɔvinyɔnu be “Nyeamekpɔnublanuina.” Gomer mawɔnuteƒe, Israel mawɔnuteƒe

english_verse: Accuse! Accuse your mother! She is no longer my wife, and now I, the Lord, am not her husband. Beg her to give up prostitution and stop being unfaithful,
translation_verse: “Miƒo koko na mia nɔ, Miƒo koko nɛ - elabe menye srɔ̃nye o, eye nyemenye srɔ̃a o - be wòaɖe gbolowɔwɔ le mo kple ahasiwɔwɔ ɖa le eƒe nowo domee.

english_verse: or I will strip her naked like the day she was born. I will make her barren like a desert, and she will die of thirst.
translation_verse: Ne menye nenema o la, maɖe amae, eye mawɔe wòanɔ abe gbe si gbe wodzii ene. Mawɔe wòanɔ abe gbedadaƒo ene, wòanɔ abe kuɖiɖinyigba ene, eye mana tsikɔ nawui wòaku.

english_verse: You children are the result of her unfaithfulness, and I'll show you no pity.
translation_verse: Nyemakpɔ nublanui na mi viawo hã o, elabe ahasiviwo wonye.

english_verse: Your mother was unfaithful. She was disgraceful and said, “I'll run after my lovers. Everything comes from them— my food and drink, my linen and wool, my olive oil and wine.”
translation_verse: Elabe wo nɔ wɔ gbɔlo; eye ame si dzi wo wɔ ŋukpenanu. Elabe egblɔ be: ‘Matrɔ ayi nye ahiãviwo gbɔ, woawoe naa nye nuɖuɖu kple tsim, nye alẽfu kple anazi, nye ami kple wain nunonom.’

english_verse: I, the Lord, will build a fence of thorns to block her path.
translation_verse: Eya ta matsɔ ŋu atɔ kpɔ ɖe eƒe mɔ dzi, maɖo gli aƒo xlã eyama ale be mate ŋu akpɔ eƒe toƒewo o.

english_verse: She will run after her lovers, but not catch them; she will search, but not find them. Then she will say, “I'll return to my first husband. Life was better then.”
translation_verse: Ati eƒe ahiãviwo yome, ke eƒe asi matu wo o; adi wo, ke make ɖe wo ŋu o. Tete agblɔ be: ‘Magbugbɔ ayi srɔ̃nye gbãtɔ gbɔ, elabe enyo nam tsã wu fifia.’

english_verse: She didn't know that her grain, wine, and olive oil were gifts from me, as were the gold and silver she used in worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Ke medze sii be nyee nye ame si naa bli, wain kple ami, ame si naa klosalo kple sika geɖe siwo ŋudɔ wowɔna le Baal gbɔ la o.

english_verse: So I'll hold back the harvest of grain and grapes. I'll take back my wool and my linen that cover her body.
translation_verse: Eya ta magbugbɔ axɔ nye bli ne ɣeyiɣia ɖo edzi, maxɔ nye wain, ne azãgbea ɖo edzi. Maxɔ nye alẽfu kple nye anazi siwo xea eƒe ama me.

english_verse: Then I'll strip her naked in the sight of her lovers. No one can rescue her.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, maklo nu le eƒe ŋukpeƒe dzi le eƒe ahiãviwo ŋkume, eye ame aɖeke maxɔe le asinye o.

english_verse: I'll stop Israel's celebrations— no more New Moon Festivals, Sabbaths, or other feasts.
translation_verse: Matsi eƒe dzidzɔkpɔkpɔwo katã nu: ƒetatrɔ ŋkekenyuiwo, ɣleti dzedzi ŋkekenyuiwo dzudzɔgbewo, kple eƒe ŋkekenyui ɖoɖiwo katã.

english_verse: She said, “My lovers gave me vineyards and fig trees as payment for sex.” Now I, the Lord, will ruin her vineyards and fig trees; they will become clumps of weeds eaten by wild animals.
translation_verse: Magblẽ eƒe wainka kple gboti siwo ŋu wògblɔ le be: ‘Esiawo nye fetu, siwo nye ahiãviwo nam’ esime yewonɔ zɔzɔm la dome. Mana woazu ave, eye gbemelãwo avuvu wo.

english_verse: I'll punish her for the days she worshiped Baal and burned incense to him. I'll punish her for the times she forgot about me and wore jewelry and rings to attract her lovers. I, the Lord, have spoken! The Lord Will Help Israel
translation_verse: Mahe to nɛ ɖe Baalwoƒe ŋkekenyuiwo ta, esime wòdo lifidzudzɔ na wo, eye wòɖo atsyɔ̃ na eɖokui kple eƒe asigɛ kpakple atsyɔ̃ɖonuwo hekplɔ eƒe ahiãviwo ɖo, eye wòŋlɔm be, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.” Aƒetɔ lɔ̃ eƒe dukɔ la

english_verse: Israel, I, the Lord, will lure you into the desert and speak gently to you.
translation_verse: “Eya ta kpɔ ɖa, mable enu akplɔe va gbedadaƒo, eye maƒo nu nɛ lɔlɔ̃tɔe.

english_verse: I will return your vineyards, and then Trouble Valley will become Hopeful Valley. You will say “Yes” to me as you did in your youth, when leaving Egypt.
translation_verse: Magatrɔ eƒe waingblewo nɛ le afi ma, eye mawɔ Azor-bali la wòazu mɔkpɔkpɔ ƒe ʋɔtru. Aɖo eŋu le afi ma abe eƒe ɖetugbimenɔɣi ene abe esime wòʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi ene.

english_verse: I promise from that day on, you will call me your husband instead of your master.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, àyɔm be ‘Srɔ̃nye’, eye màgayɔm be ‘Nye Baal’ azɔ o.

english_verse: I will no longer even let you mention the names of those pagan gods that you called “Master.”
translation_verse: Elabe maɖe Baalwo ŋkɔ ɖa le eƒe nu me, eye womagayɔ wo ŋkɔ azɔ o.

english_verse: And I will agree to let you live in peace—you will no longer be attacked by wild animals and birds or by weapons of war.
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, mabla nu kple gbemelãwo kple xewo kpakple nutatawo katã ɖe nye dukɔ nu. Maɖe dati kple yi kpakple aʋawɔwɔ ɖa le anyigba la dzi, eye mana woamlɔ anyi anɔ dedie.

english_verse: I will accept you as my wife forever, and instead of a bride price I will give you justice, fairness, love, kindness,
translation_verse: Matsɔ wò awɔ nye ŋugbetɔe tegbee. Matsɔ wò ana ɖokuinye le nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ, ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ dzɔdzɔe, amenuveve kple nublanuikpɔkpɔ me, nànye nye ŋugbetɔ.

english_verse: and faithfulness. Then you will truly know who I am.
translation_verse: Matsɔ wò ana ɖokuinye le nuteƒewɔwɔ me, eye àdze si Aƒetɔ.”

english_verse: I will command the sky to send rain on the earth,
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ be: “Ɣe ma ɣi la maɖo eŋu na dziƒowo eye woawo hã aɖo eŋu na anyigba.

english_verse: and it will produce grain, grapes, and olives in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Anyigba aɖo eŋu na bli, wain kple ami, eye woawo hã aɖo eŋu na Yezreel.

english_verse: I will scatter the seeds and show mercy to Lo-Ruhamah. I will say to Lo-Ammi, “You are my people,” and they will answer, “You are our God.”
translation_verse: Maƒãe na ɖokuinye ɖe anyigba la dzi. Makpɔ nublanui na Amemakpɔnublanuina; eye magblɔ na Amemanyenyedukɔ be, ‘Nye dukɔe nènye’, eye eya agblɔ be, ‘Wòe nye nye Mawu.’ ”

english_verse: Once again the Lord spoke to me. And this time he said, “Hosea, fall in love with an unfaithful woman who has a lover. Do this to show that I love the people of Israel, even though they worship idols and enjoy the offering cakes made with fruit.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nam be: “Gayi nàɖadi nyɔnu si le zɔzɔm kple ŋutsu bubu aɖe la. Lɔ̃e abe ale si nye hã megalɔ̃ Israel ene. Togbɔ be wogale mawu bubuwo subɔm, eye wotsɔ waintsetse le abolo ƒom na wo hã la, megalɔ̃ wo.”

english_verse: Then I said, “Now you are mine! You will have to remain faithful to me, though it will be a long time before we sleep together.”
translation_verse: Megblɔ nɛ be: “Tɔ ɖe gbɔnye koŋ azɔ; mègawɔ gbolo loo, alo nànye ŋutsu bubu tɔ o. Nye hã manɔ na wò nenema.”

english_verse: It will also be a long time before Israel has a king or before sacrifices are offered at the temple or before there is any way to get guidance from God.
translation_verse: Elabe Israelviwo hã anɔ anyi alea eteƒe adidi; fia alo kplɔla manɔ wo si o, eye womagasa vɔ o. Legba alo kɔmewu alo aklama kpakpɛ aɖeke hã manɔ wo si o.

english_verse: But later, Israel will turn back to the Lord their God and to David their king. At that time they will come to the Lord with fear and trembling, and he will be good to them.
translation_verse: Ke emegbe la, Israelviwo agatrɔ ava di Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la kple David, woƒe fia la. Woatsɔ vɔvɔ̃ ava Aƒetɔ

english_verse: Israel, listen as the Lord accuses everyone in the land! No one is faithful or loyal or truly cares about God.
translation_verse: Israel-dukɔ, mise Aƒetɔ ƒe nya, elabe Aƒetɔ tsɔ nya ɖe ame siwo le anyigba la dzi la ŋu. Nuteƒewɔwɔ alo dɔmenyowɔwɔ kple sidzedze Mawu megale anyigba la dzi o.

english_verse: And so your land is a desert. Every living creature is dying— people and wild animals, birds and fish. The Lord Warns the Priests
translation_verse: Eya ta anyigba le konyi fam, eye nu siwo katã le edzi le veve sem; wokplɔ gbemelãwo kple dziƒoxewo, kpakple ƒumelãwo kekeake hã dzoe. Aƒetɔ tsɔ nya ɖe nunɔlawo ŋu

english_verse: Don't accuse just anyone! Not everyone is at fault. My case is against you, the priests.
translation_verse: Migana ame aɖeke nahe nya kple ame aɖe alo aka mo nɛ o, elabe mi nunɔlawo ŋue metsɔ nya ɖo.

english_verse: You and the prophets will stumble day and night; I'll silence your mothers.
translation_verse: Àkli nu le ŋkeke me, eye nye gbeƒãɖelawo hã akli nu akpe ɖe ŋuwò le zã me, eye matsrɔ̃ mia nɔ.

english_verse: You priests have rejected me, and my people are destroyed by refusing to obey. Now I'll reject you and forget your children, because you have forgotten my Law.
translation_verse: Wotsrɔ̃ nye dukɔ elabe sidzedze mele esi o. Esi nègbe nu le sidzedze gbɔ ta la, nye hã megbe be màganye nunɔla nam o. Esi mieŋlɔ mia Mawu ƒe se la be ta la, nye hã maŋlɔ mia viwo be.

english_verse: By adding more of you priests, you multiply the number of people who sin. Now I'll change your pride into shame.
translation_verse: Ale si wole agbɔ sɔm ɖe edzii la, nenemae woƒe vɔ̃wɔwɔ ɖe ŋunye le agbɔ sɔm ɖe edzii. Eya ta matrɔ bubu si le wo ŋu la wòazu ŋukpe.

english_verse: You encourage others to sin, so you can stuff yourselves on their sin offerings.
translation_verse: Nye dukɔ ƒe nuvɔ̃ zu nuɖuɖu na wo; dɔ le wo wum vevie, ɖe woƒe vodada ŋu.

english_verse: That's why I will punish the people for their deeds, just as I will punish you priests.
translation_verse: Ava eme na dukɔ la abe nunɔla ene. Mahe to na wo ɖe woƒe mɔwo ta, eye maɖo woƒe nuwɔnawo teƒe na wo.

english_verse: Their food won't satisfy, and having sex at pagan shrines won't produce children. My people have rebelled
translation_verse: Woaɖu nu, ke maɖi na wo o; woawɔ gbolo, ke womadzi ɖe edzi o; elabe wogblẽ Aƒetɔ ɖi, hele dzidzɔ kpɔm le gbolowɔwɔ ŋu. Aƒetɔ tsri trɔ̃subɔsubɔ

english_verse: You expect wooden idols and other objects of wood to give you advice. Lusting for sex at pagan shrines has made you unfaithful to me, your God.
translation_verse: Nye dukɔ le gbe biam nu si wotsɔ ati wɔe la. Atizɔtie gblɔa nya na wo! Elabe gbolowɔgbɔgbɔ kplɔ wo trae, eye wodzo le woƒe Mawu gbɔ be yewoaɖawɔ gbolo.

english_verse: You offer sacrifices on mountaintops and hills, under oak trees, and wherever good shade is found. Your own daughters and daughters-in-law sell themselves for sex.
translation_verse: Wosaa vɔ le towo tame, eye wowɔa nunanawo le togbɛwo dzi le fɔfɔlĩwo, sesewuwo kple logotiwo te, elabe woƒe vɔvɔli nyo. Le esia ta mia vinyɔnuviwo zu gbolowo, eye miaƒe ŋugbetɔwo le ahasi wɔm.

english_verse: But I won't punish them. You men are to blame, because you go to prostitutes and offer sacrifices with them at pagan shrines. Your own foolishness will lead to your ruin.
translation_verse: Nyemahe to na mia vinyɔnuviwo, ne wowɔ gbɔlo o, alo miaƒe ŋugbetɔwo, ne wowɔ ahasi o, elabe ŋutsuawo ŋutɔ zɔna kple gbɔlowo le adzame eye wosaa vɔ kple mawu ƒeme gbolowo, ale dukɔ masenugɔme atsrɔ̃.

english_verse: Israel, you are unfaithful, but don't lead Judah to sin. Stop worshiping at Gilgal or at sinful Bethel. And quit making promises in my name—the name of the living Lord.
translation_verse: O Israel, togbɔ be nèle gbɔlo wɔm hã la, mègana Yuda naɖi fɔ o. Migage ɖe Gilgal loo, alo miayi Bet-Aven o, eye migatà nu be, “Esi Aƒetɔ le agbe la” o.

english_verse: You are nothing more than a stubborn cow— so stubborn that I, the Lord, cannot feed you like lambs in an open pasture.
translation_verse: Abe nyinɔ dzeaglã ene la, Israel dze aglã. Ɖe Aƒetɔ ate ŋu anyi wo azɔ abe alẽvi ene le gbeɖuƒe gbadzaa?

english_verse: You people of Israel are charmed by idols. Leave those people alone!
translation_verse: Efrayim dze xɔlɔ̃ legbawo. Mina wòawɔ nu si dze eŋu.

english_verse: You get drunk, then sleep with prostitutes; you would rather be vulgar than lead a decent life.
translation_verse: Wonoa wain geɖe, eye wowɔa ahasi. Ŋukpenanuwɔwɔ doa dzidzɔ na wo.

english_verse: And so you will be swept away in a whirlwind for sacrificing to idols.
translation_verse: Yaƒoƒo bla wo ɖe eƒe aʋalawo me, eye ŋukpe alé wo le woƒe vɔsamlekpuiwo ta.

english_verse: Listen, you priests! Pay attention, Israel! Listen, you members of the royal family. Justice was your duty. But at Mizpah and Mount Tabor you trapped the people.
translation_verse: Nunɔlawo, mise nya sia! Israel ƒe aƒe, zi ɖoɖoe! Fiaƒemetɔwo, miƒu to anyi miasee! Elabe miawoe wole ʋɔnua drɔ̃ gee. Miezu mɔ̀ le Mizpa kple ɖɔ si woɖo ɖe Tabor-to dzi,

english_verse: At the place of worship you were a treacherous pit, and I will punish you.
translation_verse: eye miaƒe aglãdzelawo ƒe nuvɔ̃wo do fievo, ke mahe to na mi katã.

english_verse: Israel, I know all about you, and because of your unfaithfulness, I find you unacceptable.
translation_verse: Menya ale si Efrayim le, eye Israel mele ɣaɣla ɖem o. Efrayim, èwɔ ahasi; Israel, ègblẽ kɔ ɖo na ɖokuiwò. Hosea tsi tre ɖe trɔ̃subɔsubɔ ŋuti

english_verse: Your evil deeds are the reason you won't return to me, your Lord God. And your constant craving for sex keeps you from knowing me.
translation_verse: Woƒe nuwɔnawo xe mɔ na wo, ale be womagatrɔ ayi woƒe Mawu la gbɔ o. Elabe ahasiwɔwɔ ƒe gbɔgbɔ le wo me eye womedze si Aƒetɔ o.

english_verse: Israel, your pride testifies to your guilt; it makes you stumble, and Judah stumbles too.
translation_verse: Israel ƒe dàda le ɖase ɖim le eƒe mo. Efrayim akli nu adze anyi, ɖe eƒe fɔɖiɖi me; eye Yuda hã akli nu akpe ɖe wo ŋu.

english_verse: You offer sheep and cattle as sacrifices to me, but I have turned away and refuse to be found.
translation_verse: Woatsɔ alẽwo kple nyiwo aɖadi Aƒetɔ, ke womakpɔe o, elabe ete ɖa le wo gbɔ.

english_verse: You have been unfaithful to me, your Lord; you have had children by prostitutes. So at the New Moon Festival, you and your crops will be destroyed. The Lord Warns Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Womewɔ nuteƒe na Aƒetɔ o, eye wodzi gbɔmeviwo. Azɔ dzinu yeye avuvu woawo kple woƒe anyigba la siaa. Aʋa dzɔ ɖe Yuda kple Israel dome

english_verse: Give a warning on the trumpet! Let it be heard in Gibeah, Ramah, and sinful Bethel. Benjamin, watch out!
translation_verse: Miku lãdzo le Gibea! Kpẽ neɖi le Rama! Miƒu asi nu le Betel! Benyamin, dzo nyànyanya!

english_verse: I, the Lord, will punish and wipe out Israel. This is my solemn promise to every tribe of Israel.
translation_verse: Efrayim azu gbegbe le tohegbe; meɖe gbeƒã nu si le eme va ge godoo le Israel-toawo dome.

english_verse: Judah's leaders are like crooks who move boundary markers; that's why I will flood them with my anger.
translation_verse: Yuda-megãwo zu abe ame siwo ŋea liƒo ɖe me ene; woawo dzie matrɔ nye dɔmedzoe akɔ ɖo abe tsi ene.

english_verse: Israel was brutally crushed. They got what they deserved for worshiping useless idols.
translation_verse: Wote Efrayim ɖe anyi, eye wohe to nɛ, bɔbɔe ɖe anyi elabe eɖoe kplikpaa dze nu maɖinuwo yome.

english_verse: Now I, the Lord, will fill Israel with maggots and make Judah rot.
translation_verse: Eya ta mele abe agbagblaʋui ene, na Efrayim, eye mele abe ŋɔ si ɖua nu ene na Yuda ƒe aƒe la.

english_verse: When Israel and Judah saw their sickness and wounds, Israel asked help from Assyria and its mighty king. But the king cannot cure them or heal their wounds.
translation_verse: Esi Efrayim kpɔ be yedze dɔ, eye Yuda kpɔ abi si le eya ŋutɔ ŋu la, Efrayim yi Asiria, eye wòdɔ ame ɖe fia gã la. Ke mete ŋu da gbe le ŋuwò alo yɔ dɔ wò abi la o.

english_verse: So I'll become a fierce lion attacking Israel and Judah. I'll snatch and carry off what I want, and no one can stop me.
translation_verse: Elabe manɔ abe dzata ene na Efrayim, abe dzata ɖekakpui ene na Yuda ƒe aƒe la. Nye, nye gɔ̃ hã, avuvu nu ahadzo; makɔe adzoe, eye ame aɖeke mate ŋu axɔe o.

english_verse: Then I'll return to my temple until they confess their guilt and worship me, until they are desperate and beg for my help.
translation_verse: Matrɔ ayi nye nɔƒe va se ɖe esime wodze sii be yewoɖi fɔ, eye wodi nye ŋkume, eye le woƒe xaxa me la, wodim gblɔ b

english_verse: Let's return to the Lord. He has torn us to shreds, but he will bandage our wounds and make us well.
translation_verse: “Miva, mina míagatrɔ ayi Aƒetɔ gbɔ; elabe eyae vuvu nu, be yeada gbe le mía ŋu; eyae de abi mía ŋu, ke ablae na mí.

english_verse: In two or three days he will heal us and restore our strength that we may live with him.
translation_verse: Agbɔ agbe mí le ŋkeke eve megbe, le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe la, afɔ mí ɖe tsitrenu, be míanɔ agbe le eŋkume.

english_verse: Let's do our best to know the Lord. His coming is as certain as the morning sun; he will refresh us like rain renewing the earth in the springtime. The Lord Speaks to Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Mina míanyae, mina míate kpɔ adze si Aƒetɔ. Ado na mí godoo abe agudzedze ene, ava mía gbɔ abe agbafie ene abe keletsi si ƒoa anyigba ene.”

english_verse: People of Israel and Judah, what can I do with you? Your love for me disappears more quickly than mist or dew at sunrise.
translation_verse: O Efrayim, nu ka mawɔ kpli wò? O Yuda, nu ka mawɔ kpli wò? Miaƒe lɔlɔ̃ le abe ŋdililikpo ene. Ele abe zãmu si nu yina kaba ene.

english_verse: That's why I slaughtered you with the words of my prophets. That's why my judgments blazed like the dawning sun.
translation_verse: Eya ta meƒo wo to gbeƒãɖelawo dzi, mewu wo kple nye numenya. Nye ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ do yi, abe kekeli ene.

english_verse: I'd rather for you to be faithful and to know me than to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Elabe lɔlɔ̃ matrɔ dim mele, ke menye vɔsa o. Mele sidzedze Mawu dim wu numemevɔsa.

english_verse: At a place named Adam, you betrayed me by breaking our agreement.
translation_verse: Ke wotu nye nu, si mebla kpli wo le Adam, eye afi mae womewɔ nuteƒe nam le o.

english_verse: Everyone in Gilead is evil; your hands are stained with the blood of victims.
translation_verse: Gilead nye nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔlawo ƒe du eye wòƒo ʋu.

english_verse: You priests are like a gang of robbers in ambush. On the road to Shechem you murder and commit other horrible crimes.
translation_verse: Abe ale si adzodalawo ƒe ha dea xa ɖi na ame ene la, nenemae nunɔlawo zu adzohae; wowua ame le Sixem-mɔ dzi gɔ̃ hã, ẽ, wowɔa ŋutasẽnu.

english_verse: I have seen a terrible thing in Israel— you are unfaithful and unfit to worship me.
translation_verse: Le Israel ƒeme la, mekpɔ ŋɔdzinu aɖe. Efrayim ƒe gbolowɔwɔ le afi ma, wogblẽ kɔ ɖo Israel.

english_verse: People of Judah, your time is coming too. The Lord Wants To Help Israel I, the Lord, would like to make my nation prosper again
translation_verse: Yuda wò hã la, woɖo nuŋeɣi ɖi na wò. Ne medi be maɖo nye dukɔ ƒe nunyonamewo te,

english_verse: and to heal its wounds. But then I see the crimes in Israel and Samaria. Everyone is deceitful; robbers roam the streets.
translation_verse: ne meɖoe be mada gbe le nye amewo ŋu la, woɖea Efrayim ƒe nu fitifiti wɔwɔ kple Samaria ƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ fiana. Wodaa alakpa, fiafiwo gbãa ʋɔ, eye adzohawo tsoa ame le mɔ ta.

english_verse: The king and his officials take great pleasure in their sin and deceit.
translation_verse: Wotsɔa woƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ doa dzidzɔ na fia la kple woƒe alakpanuwɔwɔ, doa dzidzɔ na amegãwo.

english_verse: Everyone burns with desire— they are like coals in an oven, ready to burst into flames.
translation_verse: Ahasiwɔlawo wo katã wonye. Wole abe abolokpo ene. Ne aboloƒola la blu wɔ vɔ la, megatua dzoa ɖo o, va se ɖe esime aboloa naʋã.

english_verse: On the day their king was crowned, his officials got him drunk, and he joined in their foolishness.
translation_verse: Le míaƒe fia ƒe ŋkeke dzi la, amegãwo dea dɔ lã me na wo ɖokui kple wain xɔdzo, eye wòbɔa ha kple fewuɖulawo.
