translation_verse: Tete nunɔla Amazya si le Betel la dɔ ame ɖe Israel-fia Yerobeam be: “Amos le nugbe ɖom ɖe wò kple dukɔa ŋu. Nya siwo gblɔm wòle la wu tsɔtsɔ na mí azɔ.

english_verse: Here is what he is saying: ‘Jeroboam will be put to death, and the people will be taken to a foreign country.’ ”
translation_verse: Ele gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Yerobeam atsi yi nu, eye wole aboyo ɖe ge Israel-dukɔmetɔwo akplɔ adzoe tso woƒe anyigba dzi.’ ”

english_verse: Then Amaziah told me, “Amos, take your visions and get out! Go back to Judah and earn your living there as a prophet.
translation_verse: Ale Amazya gblɔ na Amos be: “Nukpɔla, dzo, sí nàyi Yuda aɖanɔ wò gbeƒã la ɖem le afi ma boŋ. Àkpɔ nu aɖu tso eme.

english_verse: Don't do any more preaching at Bethel. The king worships here at our national temple.”
translation_verse: Ke mègaɖe gbeƒã nya le Betel azɔ o, elabe teƒe siae fia la subɔa Mawu le, eye fiaɖuƒea ƒe gbedoxɔ hã li.”

english_verse: I answered: I'm not a prophet! And I wasn't trained to be a prophet. I am a shepherd, and I take care of fig trees.
translation_verse: Tete Amos ɖo eŋu be: “Nyemenye gbeƒãɖela alo gbeƒãɖelawo ƒe hahɔbɔmenɔla o. Lãkplɔvi kple sikamortigble dzikpɔla menye tsã.

english_verse: But the Lord told me to leave my herds and preach to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ va ɖem le lãkplɔdɔ la me, eye wògblɔ nam be: ‘Yi ɖaɖe gbeƒã nye nya na nye dukɔ Israel.’

english_verse: Now, listen to what the Lord says about you: Your wife will become a prostitute in the city, your sons and daughters will be killed in war, and your land will be divided among others. You will die in a country of foreigners, and the people of Israel will be dragged from their homeland.
translation_verse: Eya ta, Amazya, Aƒetɔ be: ‘Srɔ̃wò awɔ gbolo le du sia me, eye viwòwo atsi aʋa. Woama wò anyigba na amewo, eye wò ŋutɔ àku ɖe anyigba makɔmakɔ aɖe dzi. Ke Israel-dukɔ la ya la, woaɖe aboyoe akplɔe dzoe tso eƒe anyigba dzi.’ ”

english_verse: and asked, “Amos, what do you see?” “A basket of ripe fruit,” I replied. Then he said, “This is the end for my people Israel. I won't forgive them again.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ bia be: “Amos, nu kae nye esia?” Meɖo eŋu be: “Kusie, kutsetse ɖiɖiwo le eme.” Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ nam be: “Nye dukɔ Israel gbãɣi ɖo. Nyemagaɖe asi le nu si meɖo be mawɔ la ŋu azɔ gbeɖe o.

english_verse: Instead of singing in the temple, they will cry and weep. Dead bodies will be everywhere. So keep silent! I, the Lord, have spoken!” Israel Is Doomed The Lord said:
translation_verse: Konyifahawo aɖi kple ɣli le mawuxɔ me hawo teƒe gbe ma gbe.” Aƒetɔ Mawu ye gblɔe. “Ame kukuwo asɔ gbɔ ɣe ma ɣi, eye woatsɔ wo aƒu gbe ɖe afi sia afi. Ðoɖoe azi toŋ.” Mawu ahe to na Israel-dukɔ

english_verse: You people crush those in need and wipe out the poor.
translation_verse: Mise nya sia, mi ame siwo fanyaa hiãtɔwo, eye miena ame dahewo le aya ɖum le dukɔa me.

english_verse: You say to yourselves, “How much longer before the end of the New Moon Festival? When will the Sabbath be over? Our wheat is ready, and we want to sell it now. We can't wait to cheat and charge high prices for the grain we sell. We will use dishonest scales
translation_verse: Mi ame siwo le gbɔgblɔm be: “Gbe ka gbe gɔ̃ dzinu dzedzi ŋkekenyui nu ayi ne míadzra nukuwo? Ɣe ka ɣi dzudzɔgbe nu ayi, be míaʋu míaƒe avawo ne míadze nudzadzra gɔme? Ɣe ma ɣi la, míatò nudzidzenuwo ɖe me, míadzi asi ɖe edzi, eye míaŋe nudanu ɖe me atsɔ ba míaƒe nuƒlelawoe.

english_verse: and mix dust in the grain. Those who are needy and poor don't have any money. We will make them our slaves for the price of a pair of sandals.”
translation_verse: Míadzra bli gbegblẽ asi gãe. Míaƒle ame dahe ɖe klosaloga ƒe fe nu, eye míaƒle hiãtɔ ɖe atokota dodo ɖeka ƒe asi nu.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, won't forget any of this, though you take great pride in your ancestor Jacob.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, ame si dzi Yakob dàna ɖo la, tà eɖokui gblɔ be: “Ne maŋlɔ woƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ be fĩi!

english_verse: Your country will tremble, and you will mourn. It will be like the Nile River that rises and overflows, then sinks back down.
translation_verse: Ɖe anyigba maʋuʋu le esia ta, eye ame sia ame afa konyi le anyigba dzi, eye dukɔ blibo la aʋuʋu, aho dzekee adze me abe ale si Nil-tɔsisi dzea agbo, gadzea kɔ anyi ene oa?”

english_verse: On that day, I, the Lord God, will make the sun go down at noon, and I will turn daylight into darkness.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe la, mana ɣe naɖo to le ŋdɔ me, eye zãdokeli ado. Aƒetɔ Mawu lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Your festivals and joyful singing will turn into sorrow. You will wear sackcloth and shave your heads, as you would at the death of your only son. It will be a horrible day.
translation_verse: Matrɔ miaƒe ŋkekenyuiwo woazu konyifaɣiwo, eye miaƒe dzidzɔhawo azu avihɛwo. Mana mialũ ta, ata akpanya, eye mianɔ abe dzila siwo le konyi fam na wo vi ɖeka hɔ̃ ene. Ŋkeke bliboa awu enu le vevesese gã me.

english_verse: I, the Lord, also promise you a terrible shortage, but not of food and water. You will hunger and thirst to hear my message.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ɣeyiɣi aɖe li gbɔna esime mana dɔ nato le anyigba dzi. Menye nu, ame nakpɔ aɖu alo tsi, ame nakpɔ ano ƒe dɔe ato o, ke boŋ Aƒetɔ ƒe nya, ame nakpɔ ase ƒe dɔe le toto ge.

english_verse: You will search everywhere— from north to south, from east to west. You will go all over the earth, seeking a message from me, the Lord. But you won't find one.
translation_verse: Amewo azɔ tramatrama tso atsiaƒu nu ayi atsiaƒu nu, eye woatsa tsa glãla tso dzigbeme ava yi ɣedzeƒe. Woatsa tso afii ayi afi mɛ anɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe nya ko dim be yewoase, gake womakpɔe ase o.

english_verse: Your beautiful young women and your young men will faint from thirst.
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi me la, tsikɔ awu ɖetugbi nyakpɔwo kple ɖekakpui sesẽwo gɔ̃ hã, woaku ƒenyi.

english_verse: You made promises to the goddess Ashimah at Samaria; you made vows to other gods at the shrines of Dan and Beersheba. So now you will fall and never get up.
translation_verse: Ame siwo tàa Samaria-legbawo gblɔna be: ‘Míetà Dan ƒe mawu!’ alo ‘Míetà Beer-Seba ƒe mawu!’ la, adze anyi, eye womagafɔ akpɔ gbeɖe o.”

english_verse: I saw a vision of the Lord standing by the temple altar, and he said, “Shake the columns until the tops fall loose, and the doorposts crumble. Then make the pieces fall on the people below. I will take a sword and kill anyone who escapes.
translation_verse: Mekpɔ Aƒetɔ wòle tsitre ɖe vɔsamlekpui la gbɔ. Egblɔ be: “Ƒo sɔtiwo ta sesĩe ale be wo gɔme naʋuʋu. Ŋe wo ƒu ameawo ƒe ta dzi. Mele ame mamlɛawo wu ge le aʋa me. Wo dometɔ aɖeke masí o; ɖeka hɔ̃ hã masusɔ o.

english_verse: “If they dig deep into the earth or climb to the sky, I'll reach out and get them.
translation_verse: Ne woku do ge ɖe eme yi tsiẽƒe ke gɔ̃ hã, mahe wo tso afi ma vɛ. Ne wolia va dziƒo hã, maɖiɖi wo tso afi ma ɖe anyi.

english_verse: If they escape to the peaks of Mount Carmel, I'll search and find them. And if they hide from me at the bottom of the ocean, I'll command a sea monster to bite them.
translation_verse: Ne woyi ɖabè ɖe Karmel-to tame hã, nye asi atu wo le afi ma. Ne wosí le nunye yi ɖabè ɖe atsiaƒu gɔme ke hã, maɖe gbe na da wòaɖu wo le afi ma.

english_verse: I'll send a sword to kill them, wherever their enemies drag them off as captives. I'm determined to hurt them, not to help them.” His Name Is the Lord
translation_verse: Ne woƒe futɔwo kplɔ wo ɖe ŋgɔ yi aboyo me gɔ̃ hã, mana woawu wo kple yi le afi ma. Nye ŋku anɔ wo ŋu woatsrɔ̃ kokoko; womatsi agbe gbeɖe o.”

english_verse: When the Lord God All-Powerful touches the earth, it melts, and its people mourn. God makes the earth rise and then fall, just like the Nile River.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aƒetɔ Aʋakɔwokplɔla la, ame si kaa asi anyigba ŋu wòlólona gbanaa, eye edzinɔlawo katã xaa nu, anyigba blibo la hona dzekee yia dzi dzea eme abe Nil-tɔsisi le Egipte ene;

english_verse: He built his palace in the heavens and let its foundations rest on the earth. He scoops up the ocean and empties it on the earth. His name is the Lord. The Lord Is God
translation_verse: ame si tso aƒe ɖe edzi, eye wòna dziŋgɔli tsyɔ anyigba dzi; ame si yɔ tsiwo tso atsiaƒu me, eye wòtsɔ wo kɔ ɖe anyigba dzi la, eyama ŋkɔe nye Aƒetɔ.

english_verse: Israel, I am the Lord God, and the Ethiopians are no less important to me than you are. I brought you out of Egypt, but I also brought the Philistines from Crete and the Arameans from Kir.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Aƒetɔ be: “Israelviwo, miawo hã menye ɖeko miele nam abe Etiopiatɔwo ene oa? Ɖe nyemekplɔ Filistitɔwo tso Kreta, eye mekplɔ Siriatɔwo hã tso Kir abe ale si mekplɔ Israel hã tso Egipte-nyigba dzi ene oa?

english_verse: My eyes have seen what a sinful nation you are, and I'll wipe you out. But I will leave a few of Jacob's descendants. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, Aƒetɔ Mawu ƒe ŋku le Israel-fiaɖuƒe wɔnuvɔ̃ sia ŋu, eye matsrɔ̃ mi le anyigba dzi. Ke ɖeko nyematsrɔ̃ Yakob ƒe dzidzimeviwo katã o.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: At my command, all of you will be sifted like grain. Israelites who remain faithful will be scattered among the nations. And the others will be trapped like trash in a sifter.
translation_verse: “Kpɔ ɖa, maɖe gbe, aʋuʋu Israel-dukɔ la le dukɔwo dome, abe ale si wosraa ke le nusranu me, eye kpeku aɖeke megena o ene.

english_verse: Some of you are evil, and you deny that you will ever get caught. But you will be killed. The Lord's Promise to Israel
translation_verse: Nu vɔ̃ wɔla siwo katã le nye dukɔ me la atsi yi nu. Woawo ame siwo le gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Dzɔgbevɔ̃e aɖeke natu mí loo, alo alili mí o.’ ” Woagaɖo Israel-dukɔ la te

english_verse: In the future, I will rebuild David's fallen kingdom. I will build it from its ruins and set it up again, just as it used to be.
translation_verse: “Ɣe ma ɣi la, magbugbɔ David ƒe aƒe si gbã la atso. Maɖɔ gbagbãƒeawo ɖo, eye mafɔ eƒe glikpowo ɖe tsitrenu, eye magatui abe tsã ene.

english_verse: Then you will capture Edom and the other nations that are mine. I, the Lord, have spoken, and my words will come true.
translation_verse: Israel-dukɔ la agaxɔ Edom-nyigba ƒe akpa si susɔ kple dukɔ bubu siwo katã dzi wòɖu nam va yi.” Aƒetɔ, ame si le nu siawo wɔ ge godoo lae gblɔe.

english_verse: You will have such a harvest that you won't be able to bring in all of your wheat before plowing time. You will have grapes left over from season to season; your fruitful vineyards will cover the mountains.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ŋkekewo gbɔna esime anyigba aganyo nuku vevie. Nukuwo aʋã ale gbegbe be nuŋelawo anɔ nu ŋem nuŋlɔɣi nagaɖo. Woanɔ waintsetsewo fiãm nuƒãɣi nagaɖo. Aha yeye atsyɔ tso towo ŋu, eye wòasí le togbɛwo katã ŋu.

english_verse: I'll make Israel prosper again. You will rebuild your towns and live in them. You will drink wine from your own vineyards and eat the fruit you grow.
translation_verse: Magbugbɔ nye dukɔ Israel ƒe nunyonamewo aɖo te, eye woagbugbɔ woƒe duwo atso anɔ wo me. Woade waingble ano emeha. Woatɔ abɔ ado nu ɖe eme aɖu.

english_verse: I'll plant your roots deep in the land I have given you, and you won't ever be uprooted again. I, the Lord God, have spoken!
translation_verse: Mado wo abe ati ene ɖe woƒe anyigba dzi; womagaho wo tso anyigba si mena wo la dzi akpɔ gbeɖe o.” Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu lae gblɔe.

english_verse: The Lord God gave Obadiah a message about Edom, and this is what we heard: “I, the Lord, have sent a messenger with orders for the nations to attack Edom.”
translation_verse: Obadya ƒe ŋutega. Aƒetɔ Mawu ƒo nu ku ɖe Edom-dukɔ ŋu. Aƒetɔ ahe to na Edom Míese du tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ, edɔ dɔla aɖe ɖo ɖe dukɔwo: Ebe: “Mitso! Mina míaho aʋa ɖe Edom ŋu!”

english_verse: The Lord said to Edom: I will make you the weakest and most despised nation.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, mawɔ wò nàzu sue le dukɔwo dome; maɖi gbɔ wò vevie.

english_verse: You live in a mountain fortress, because your pride makes you feel safe from attack, but you are mistaken.
translation_verse: Dàda si le wò dzime la ble wò, wò, ame si le agatowo me, eye wò nɔƒe le kɔkɔƒewo, wò, ame si le gbɔgblɔm le wò dzime be: “Ame kae atutum aƒu anyi?”

english_verse: I will still bring you down, even if you fly higher than an eagle or nest among the stars. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Togbɔ be nèyi dzi ʋĩi abe hɔ̃ ene, togbɔ be nèwɔ atɔ ɖe ɣletiviwo dome hã la, matutu wò tso afi ma aƒu anyi. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: If thieves break in at night, they steal only what they want. And people who harvest grapes always leave some unpicked. But, Edom, you are doomed!
translation_verse: Ne fiafiwo ƒo ɖe dziwò, ne adzodalawo va le zã me, ɖe womafi nu si asu wo la ko na wo ɖokui oa? Kpɔ ale si woahatsrɔ̃ wòe la ɖa! Ne wainxalawo va gbɔwò, ɖe womagblẽ ɖe ɖi oa?

english_verse: Everything you treasure most will be taken from you.
translation_verse: Ale ke womekaka Esau ƒe nuwo me, hedi eƒe kesinɔnuwoe o!

english_verse: Your allies can't be trusted. They will force you out of your own country. And your best friends will trick and trap you, even before you know it.
translation_verse: Wò dzoɖuxɔlɔ̃wo katã ble wò; wonyà wò va ɖo liƒo dzi ke. Wò kple ame siwo katã nyi dzo la, woawoe va ɖu dziwò azɔ. Xɔ̃wò siwo ŋu nèɖoa dzi ɖo la, tre mɔ̀ ɖi na wò; mèse egɔme o.

english_verse: Edom, when this happens, I, the Lord, will destroy all your marvelous wisdom.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: Gbe ma gbe la, ɖe nyematsrɔ̃ Edom ƒe nunyalawo kple nugɔmesese ɖa le Esau-to la dzi oa?

english_verse: Warriors from the city of Teman will be terrified, and you descendants of Esau will be wiped out. The Lord Condemns Edom's Cruelty
translation_verse: Teman, dzi aɖe le wò kalẽawo ƒo, eye woawu ŋutsu ɖe sia ɖe si tso Esau-to la dzi. Nu siwo ta wòle be woahe to na Edom ɖo

english_verse: You were cruel to your relatives, the descendants of Jacob. Now you will be destroyed, disgraced forever.
translation_verse: Le ŋuta si nèsẽ le nɔviwò Yakob ŋu ta la, àɖu ŋukpe, eye woatsrɔ̃ wò ɖa tegbee.

english_verse: You stood there and watched as foreigners entered Jerusalem and took what they wanted. In fact, you were no better than those foreigners.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe nètsi tsitre ɖi ɖekematsɔlemetɔe, gbe ma gbe amedzrowo tsɔ eƒe kesinɔnuwo dzoe, eye dutatɔwo ge ɖe eƒe agbowo me hedzidze nu ɖe Yerusalem dzi, nènɔ abe wo dometɔ ɖeka ene.

english_verse: Why did you celebrate when such a dreadful disaster struck your relatives? Why were you so pleased when everyone in Judah was suffering?
translation_verse: Gake mele be nàkpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe nɔviwò ƒe ŋkeke la ŋu o, ɖe eƒe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ŋkeke la ŋu o. Mele be nàkpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe Yuda-dukɔ ŋu le woƒe tsɔtsrɔ̃gbe o. Mele be nàƒo adegbe gbe si gbe nɔviwò xaxa o.

english_verse: In their time of torment, you ambushed refugees and handed them over to their attackers. The Lord Will Judge the Nations
translation_verse: Menye wòe atsi tsitre ɖe mɔ dzevee nu, anɔ eƒe ame siwo sí yina la wum o. Menye wòe atsɔ eƒe agbetsilawo ade asi le eƒe xaxagbe o. Mawu adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu dukɔwo

english_verse: The day is coming when I, the Lord, will judge the nations. And, Edom, you will pay in full for what you have done.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋkeke la tu aƒe na dukɔwo katã. Ale si nèwɔ la, nenemae woawɔ wò hã. Wò nuwɔnawo atrɔ va wò ŋutɔ wò ta dzi.

english_verse: I forced the people of Judah to drink the wine of my anger on my sacred mountain. Soon the neighboring nations must drink their fill— then vanish without a trace. Victory for Israel
translation_verse: Elabe ale si mieno aha le nye to kɔkɔe dzii la, nenemae dukɔ siwo katã ƒo xlã godoo la, anoe. Woanoe, anɔ yiyim sagasaga, eye woanɔ abe ɖe womedzɔ kpɔ o ene. Israel-dukɔ la aɖu dzi

english_verse: The Lord's people who escape will go to Mount Zion, and it will be holy. Then Jacob's descendants will capture the land of those who took their land.
translation_verse: Ke sisíla aɖewo anɔ Zion-to dzi, eye wòanɔ kɔkɔe, eye Yakob ƒe ƒome la axɔ nu siwo nye woawo ŋutɔ tɔ la.

english_verse: The people of Israel who live in the Southern Desert will take the land of Edom. Those who live in the hills will capture Philistia, Ephraim, and Samaria. And the tribe of Benjamin will conquer Gilead.
translation_verse: Anyigbemekegbegbe tsolawo axɔ Esau-to la, eye ame siwo tso togbɛ siwo le ɣetoɖoƒe balia me la, axɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba. Woaxɔ Efrayim-nyigba kple Samaria-nyigba, eye Benyamin axɔ Gilead.

english_verse: Those who return from captivity will control Phoenicia as far as Zarephath. Captives from Jerusalem who were taken to Sepharad will capture the towns of the Southern Desert.
translation_verse: Aboyome siwo le Xala, siwo tso Israelviwo dome la, axɔ Foenisiatɔwo ƒe anyigba va se ɖe keke Zarefat ke. Ame siwo woɖe aboyoe tso Yerusalem, eye wole Sefarad la, axɔ du siwo le Yuda ƒe anyigbemekegbegbe.

english_verse: Those the Lord has saved will live on Mount Zion and rule over Edom. Then the kingdom will belong to the Lord.
translation_verse: Xɔnametɔwo ayi Zion-to la dzi be woaɖu fia ɖe Esau-to la dzi, eye fiaɖuƒe la anye Aƒetɔ tɔ.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Jonah, the son of Amittai,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Yona, Amitai vi la be:

english_verse: to go to the great city of Nineveh and say to the people, “The Lord has seen your terrible sins. You are doomed!”
translation_verse: “Tso nàyi Ninive, du gã la me, eye nàhe nya ɖe emenɔlawo ŋu elabe menya nuvɔ̃ɖi si wɔm wole la.”

english_verse: Instead, Jonah ran from the Lord. He went to the seaport of Joppa and found a ship that was going to Spain. So he paid his fare, then got on the ship and sailed away to escape.
translation_verse: Ke Yona tso be yeasí boŋ le Aƒetɔ gbɔ ayi Tarsis. Eyi Yopa, eye wòkpɔ tɔdziʋu aɖe si yina Tarsis. Exe ʋuɖofe, eye wòge ɖe eme be yeadzo le Aƒetɔ gbɔ ayi Tarsis kpli wo.

english_verse: But the Lord made a strong wind blow, and such a bad storm came up that the ship was about to be broken to pieces.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ lɔ ya sesẽ aɖe ƒo le atsiaƒu la dzi, eye ahom tu sesĩe ale gbegbe be tɔdziʋua di be yeagbã.

english_verse: The sailors were frightened, and they all started praying to their gods. They even threw the ship's cargo overboard to make the ship lighter. All this time, Jonah was down below deck, sound asleep.
translation_verse: Tete vɔvɔ̃ ɖo ʋukulaawo, eye wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe yɔ mawu si wòsubɔna la. Wofɔ agba siwo le ʋua me la ƒu gbe ɖe ƒua me, be ʋua nazu wodzoe. Ke Yona ya yi ɖe ʋua gɔme, mlɔ anyi, dɔ alɔ̃ yi eme ʋĩi.

english_verse: The ship's captain went to him and said, “How can you sleep at a time like this? Get up and pray to your God! Maybe he will have pity on us and keep us from drowning.”
translation_verse: Tete ʋumefia la va egbɔ, eye wòbiae be: “Alɔ̃ dɔm wò ya nèlea? Fɔ nàyɔ wò mawu! Ðewohĩ ase wò kukuɖeɖe, be míagatsrɔ̃ o.”

english_verse: Finally, the sailors got together and said, “Let's ask our gods to show us who caused all this trouble.” It turned out to be Jonah.
translation_verse: Azɔ ʋua me nɔlawo gblɔ na wo nɔewo be: “Mía tɔwo, netsɔ; mina míadzidze nu ale be míanya ame si ta koŋ dzɔgbevɔ̃e sia va dzɔ ɖe mía dzi ɖo.” Ale wodzidze nu, eye wòdze Yona dzi.

english_verse: They started asking him, “Are you the one who brought all this trouble on us? What business are you in? Where do you come from? What is your country? Who are your people?”
translation_verse: Wobiae be: “Nu kae he dzɔgbevɔ̃e sia va mía dzii? Gblɔe na mí. Dɔ kae nèwɔna? Afi ka nètso? Afi kae nye mia de? Dukɔ ka me tɔ nènye?”

english_verse: Jonah answered, “I'm a Hebrew, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Hebritɔ menye. Mesubɔa Aƒetɔ, dziƒo Mawu si wɔ anyigba kple atsiaƒu.”

english_verse: When the sailors heard this, they were frightened, because Jonah had already told them he was running from the Lord. Then they said, “Do you know what you have done?”
translation_verse: Yona yi edzi gblɔ na ameawo be Aƒetɔ gbɔe yele sisím le. Ameawo vɔ̃ ŋutɔ, eye wobiae: “Nu kae nye esi nèwɔ?” Elabe be ameawo nya be enɔ sisím le Aƒetɔ nu; elabe egblɔe na wo do ŋgɔ.

english_verse: The storm kept getting worse, until finally the sailors asked him, “What should we do with you to make the sea calm down?”
translation_verse: Ale wobiae be: “Nu ka míawɔ wò, ne ƒu la nadze kɔ anyi na mí?” Elabe ƒu la gale nyanyram ɖe edzi wu tsã.

english_verse: Jonah told them, “Throw me into the sea, and it will calm down. I'm the cause of this terrible storm.”
translation_verse: Yona gblɔ na wo be: “Mikɔm ƒu gbe ɖe ƒua me ekema adze kɔ anyi na mi, elabe menya be nye tae ahom sesẽ sia va mia dzi ɖo.”

english_verse: The sailors tried their best to row to the shore. But they could not do it, and the storm kept getting worse every minute.
translation_verse: Gake ŋutsuawo ku ʋua kple ŋusẽ be yewoatrɔ ayi gota, ke womete ŋui o, elabe atsiaƒua gadze agbo wu tsã va le wo kpem.

english_verse: So they prayed to the Lord, “Please don't let us drown for taking this man's life. Don't hold us guilty for killing an innocent man. All of this happened because you wanted it to.”
translation_verse: Ale woyɔ Aƒetɔ sesĩe gblɔ be: “Míeɖe kuku, Aƒetɔ, mègana míatsrɔ̃ le ŋutsu sia ƒe agbe ta o, eye mègahe to na mí be míewu ame dzɔdzɔe o. Elabe Aƒetɔ, wò la, nu si dze ŋuwò lae nèwɔna.”

english_verse: Then they threw Jonah overboard, and the sea calmed down.
translation_verse: Ale wokɔ Yona ƒu gbe ɖe ƒua me. Enumake ƒua dze kɔ anyi.

english_verse: The sailors were so terrified that they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made all kinds of promises.
translation_verse: Tete ameawo vɔ̃ Aƒetɔ ŋutɔŋutɔ. Wosa vɔ na Aƒetɔ, eye woɖe adzɔgbe be yewoasubɔe.

english_verse: The Lord sent a big fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ na tɔmelã gã aɖe va mi Yona, eye wònɔ lã la ƒe dɔme ŋkeke etɔ̃, zã etɔ̃.

english_verse: From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God:
translation_verse: Tete Yona do gbe ɖa le lã la ƒe dɔme na Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu la gblɔ be:

english_verse: When I was in trouble, Lord, I prayed to you, and you listened to me. From deep in the world of the dead, I begged for your help, and you answered my prayer.
translation_verse: “Meyɔ Aƒetɔ le nye xaxa me, eye wòtɔ nam. Medo ɣli yɔ wò tso tsiẽƒe ke, eye nèse nye gbe.

english_verse: You threw me down to the bottom of the sea. The water was churning all around; I was completely covered by your mighty waves.
translation_verse: Ètsɔm ƒu gbe ɖe gogloƒe, ɖe atsiaƒu ƒe gogloƒe ke, afi si tsi sisí sesẽ ƒo xlãm kpe ɖo le, eye ƒutsotsoewo mlí to dzinye.

english_verse: I thought I was swept away from your sight, never again to see your holy temple.
translation_verse: Tete megblɔ be: ‘Wotsɔm ƒu gbe le ŋkuwò me, ale ke mawɔ agakpɔ wò gbedoxɔ kɔkɔe la?’

english_verse: I was almost drowned by the swirling waters that surrounded me. Seaweed had wrapped around my head.
translation_verse: Tsi mlí tem ɖe to, eye metsi tɔ gɔme ke, tɔgɔmegbewo xatsa ɖe ta nam,

english_verse: I had sunk down deep below the mountains beneath the sea. I knew that forever, I would be a prisoner there. But, you, Lord God, rescued me from that pit.
translation_verse: le towo ƒe bali me ke. Medo ɖe afi si anyigba ƒe ʋɔwo tu ɖe nunye tegbee le. Ke wò Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu, èxɔm ɖe agbe tso aʋlime.

english_verse: When my life was slipping away, I remembered you— and in your holy temple you heard my prayer.
translation_verse: Esi wɔna vɔ le ŋunye keŋ la, meɖo ŋku dziwò, Aƒetɔ, eye nèse nye gbedodoɖa tso wò gbedoxɔ kɔkɔe la me.

english_verse: All who worship worthless idols turn from the God who offers them mercy.
translation_verse: Ame siwo subɔa yakanuwo la, woƒe amenuvevee wogblẽ ɖi.

english_verse: But with shouts of praise, I will offer a sacrifice to you, my Lord. I will keep my promise, because you are the one with power to save.
translation_verse: Ke nye la, makɔ gbe me ada akpe na wò atsɔ asa vɔe na wò, eye mana nu si ƒe adzɔgbe meɖe la. Aƒetɔ ye ɖea ame!”

english_verse: The Lord commanded the fish to vomit up Jonah on the shore. And it did.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ na tɔmelã la yi ɖatru Yona ɖe gota.

english_verse: Once again the Lord told Jonah
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ gaƒo nu na Yona zi evelia gblɔ be:

english_verse: to go to that great city of Nineveh and preach his message of doom.
translation_verse: “Tso nàyi Ninive, du gã la me, eye nàɖe gbeƒã nya si magblɔ na wò la.”

english_verse: Jonah obeyed the Lord and went to Nineveh. The city was so big that it took three days just to walk through it.
translation_verse: Ale Yona tso, eye wòyi Ninive abe ale si Aƒetɔ bia tso esi la ene. Azɔ Ninive nye du aɖe si lolo ŋutɔ. Dua ƒe kekeme nye ŋkeke etɔ̃ ƒe azɔli.

english_verse: After walking for a day, Jonah warned the people, “Forty days from now, Nineveh will be destroyed!”
translation_verse: Yona ge ɖe dua me, zɔ ŋkeke ɖeka ƒe azɔli, eye wòɖe gbeƒã be: “Esusɔ ŋkeke bla ene pɛ ko ne woatsrɔ̃ Ninive-dua keŋ!”

english_verse: They believed God's message and set a time when they would go without eating to show their sorrow. Then everyone in the city, no matter who they were, dressed in sackcloth.
translation_verse: Tete Ninivetɔwo xɔ Mawu dzi se. Woɖe gbeƒã be dua me tɔwo katã, ame tsitsiwo kple ɖeviwo siaa, natsi nu adɔ ata akpanya.

english_verse: When the king of Nineveh heard what was happening, he also dressed in sackcloth; he left the royal palace and sat in dust.
translation_verse: Esi Ninive-fia se nya la la, etso kpla le eƒe fiazikpui dzi, ɖe eƒe awu ʋlaya ɖi, ta akpanya hebɔbɔ nɔ dzowɔ me.

english_verse: When God saw that the people had stopped doing evil things, he had pity and did not destroy them as he had planned.
translation_verse: Esi Mawu kpɔ nu si wowɔ, ale si wodzudzɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ la, eɖe asi le vɔ̃ si wòɖo be yeawɔ wo la ŋu, eye megawɔe o.

english_verse: Jonah was really upset and angry.
translation_verse: Ke esia medze Yona ŋu kura o. Dzi kui vevie.

english_verse: So he prayed: Our Lord, I knew from the very beginning that you wouldn't destroy Nineveh. That's why I left my own country and headed for Spain. You are a kind and merciful God, and you are very patient. You always show love, and you don't like to punish anyone.
translation_verse: Ale wòdo gbe ɖa na Aƒetɔ gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ, taflatsɛ, nya sia ko megblɔ esime menɔ mía dee! Aleae mebu le gɔmedzedzea eya ta mesí yina Tarsis ɖo! Elabe menyae be Mawu si vea ame nu, eye wòkpɔa nublanui na ame lae nènye. Mèkpɔa dziku kabakaba o; ènyoa dɔme tegbee, eye nètrɔa tame tso vɔ̃ wɔwɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: Now let me die! I'd be better off dead.
translation_verse: Eya ta, Aƒetɔ, fifia meɖe kuku, nà maku boŋ, enyo nam wu.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “What right do you have to be angry?”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ biae be: “Ɖe wònyo be nàdo dzikua?”

english_verse: Jonah then left through the east gate of the city and made a shelter to protect himself from the sun. He sat under the shelter, waiting to see what would happen to Nineveh.
translation_verse: Tete Yona do go le dua me, eye wòyi ɖe dua ƒe ɣedzeƒe lɔƒo. Ewɔ agbadɔ ɖe afi ma, nɔ anyi ɖe ete be yeakpɔ nu si le dzɔdzɔ ge ɖe dua dzi la ɖa.

english_verse: The Lord made a vine grow up to shade Jonah's head and protect him from the sun. Jonah was very happy to have the vine,
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ Mawu dɔ treklɔnu aɖe wòva mie ɖe afi si Yona le la heɖe alɔ ɖo vɔvɔli ɖe edzi bene eƒe dzi nafa. Yona kpɔ dzidzɔ le ka la ŋu ŋutɔ.

english_verse: but early the next morning the Lord sent a worm to chew on the vine, and the vine dried up.
translation_verse: Ke evea gbe ƒe fɔŋli la, Mawu dɔ ŋɔ aɖe wòva ɖu treklɔnu la wòyrɔ.

english_verse: During the day the Lord sent a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, making him feel faint. Jonah was ready to die, and he shouted, “I wish I were dead!”
translation_verse: Esi ɣe dze la, Mawu dɔ ɣedzeƒeya xɔdzo ɖa, eye ŋdɔ ɖu ta na Yona ale gbegbe be wòku ƒenyi. Ku gɔ̃ hã dzroe. Egblɔ be: “Ne meku boŋ la, enyo nam wu.”

english_verse: But the Lord asked, “Jonah, do you have the right to be angry about the vine?” “Yes, I do,” he answered, “and I'm angry enough to die.”
translation_verse: Ke Mawu bia Yona be: “Dziku dom nèle be treklɔnu la kua? Tɔwò dzɔ fifia?” Yona ɖo eŋu be: “Ne medo dziku la, tɔnye dzɔ. Medo dziku be maku gɔ̃ hã.”

english_verse: But the Lord said: You are concerned about a vine that you did not plant or take care of, a vine that grew up in one night and died the next.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Treklɔnu sia mie hewɔ le zã ɖeka me, eye wòku le zã ɖeka me. Mèdoe o, mèkpɔ edzi wòtsi o, eye eƒe ku wɔ nublanui na wò alea gbegbe!

english_verse: I am Micah from Moresheth. And this is the message about Samaria and Jerusalem that the Lord gave to me when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah. Judgment on Samaria
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ de gbe asi na Mixa, Moresetɔ la, le Samaria kple Yerusalem ŋu le Yuda-fia siwo nye Yotam, Axaz kple Xizkiya ƒe dziɖuɣiwo me. Konyifafa na Samaria kple Yerusalem

english_verse: Listen, all of you! Earth and everything on it, pay close attention. The Lord God accuses you from his holy temple.
translation_verse: Mi dukɔwo katã, mise nya sia! Anyigba kple edzinɔlawo katã, miɖo to miasee! Mina, Aƒetɔ Mawu nanye ɖasefo ɖe mia ŋu. Aƒetɔ la tso eƒe gbedoxɔ kɔkɔe me!

english_verse: And he will come down to crush underfoot every pagan altar.
translation_verse: Elabe kpɔ ɖa, Aƒetɔ do tso eƒe nɔƒe gbɔna. Eɖi gbɔna ava tsa le anyigba ƒe kɔkɔƒewo.

english_verse: Mountains will melt beneath his feet like wax beside a fire. Valleys will vanish like water rushing down a ravine.
translation_verse: Towo alólo le ete, eye baliwo agoglo ɖe edzi, abe anyígba ye wolólo le dzo nu ene, abe tsi wotrɔ kɔ ɖi le to trɔabu kɔgo ene.

english_verse: This will happen because of the terrible sins of Israel, the descendants of Jacob. Samaria has led Israel to sin, and pagan altars at Jerusalem have made Judah sin.
translation_verse: Nu siawo katã dzɔ le Yakob ƒe dzidada kple Israel ƒe aƒe ƒe nuvɔ̃ ta. Nu kae nye Yakob ƒe dzidada? Ðe menye Samaria ye oa? Nu kae nye Yuda ƒe aƒe ƒe nuvɔ̃? Ðe menye Yerusalem ye oa?

english_verse: So the Lord will leave Samaria in ruins— merely an empty field where vineyards are planted. He will scatter its stones and destroy its foundations.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ be: “Mana Samaria nazu glikpo ɖe gbe me, azu waingbledeƒe. Malɔ eƒe kpewo aƒu gbe ɖe bali me, eye maklo nu le gɔmeɖokpeawo dzi.

english_verse: Samaria's idols will be smashed, and the wages of temple prostitutes will be destroyed by fire. Silver and gold from those idols will then be used by foreigners as payment for prostitutes. Judah Is Doomed
translation_verse: Woagbã eƒe aklama kpakpɛwo katã gudugudu, woatɔ dzo nunana siwo katã woƒe gbolowo xɔ la, eye matsrɔ̃ woƒe legbawo keŋkeŋ. Elabe gboloe wowɔ kpɔ nu siawo katã, eya ta gbolowoe woagatsɔ wo axe fee na.”

english_verse: Because of this tragedy, I go barefoot and naked. My crying and weeping sound like howling wolves or ostriches.
translation_verse: Le esia ta, nye la mafa konyi, afa avi, eye manɔ amama anɔ yiyim. Mafa konyi abe akpataku ene, eye maxa nu abe tsatsaboli ene.

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath! Don't even cry. Instead, roll in the dust at Beth-Leaphrah.
translation_verse: Migakɔ nu le edzi woase le Gat o, migafa avi kura o. Mi Bet-Leafratɔwo, Mimli mia ɖokui le ke me, le Bet-Leafra.

english_verse: Depart naked and ashamed, you people of Shaphir. The town of Bethezel mourns because no one from Zaanan went out to help.
translation_verse: Mi Safirtɔwo, miɖe amama miaʋu adzo kple ŋukpe. Zaanantɔwo, migakatsa be yewoado go o. Ne miese Bet Haezeltɔwo le konyi fam la, ekema minyae be sitsoƒe mele afi ma na yewo o.

english_verse: Everyone in Maroth hoped for the best, but the Lord sent disaster down on Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Elabe Marotetɔwo tsi dzodzodzoe le xɔname dim, elabe vɔ̃ ɖi ɖe anyi tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ, ɖe Yerusalem-gbo nu ke.

english_verse: Get the war chariots ready, you people of Lachish. You led Jerusalem into sin, just as Israel did.
translation_verse: Laxistɔwo, mitsi tasiaɖamwo ɖe sɔwo ŋu. Miawoe to Zion vinyɔnu ƒe nuvɔ̃ vɛ, elabe mewòe wokpɔ Israel ƒe dzidadawo le.

english_verse: People of Mareshah, the Lord will send someone to capture your town. Then Israel's glorious king will be forced to hide in Adullam Cave.
translation_verse: Mi Maresanɔlawo, magana dziɖula nava dze mia dzi, eye Israel ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe ade Adulam.

english_verse: Judah, shave your head as bald as a vulture and start mourning. Your precious children will be dragged off to a foreign country.
translation_verse: Mi Yudatɔwo, milũ ta ƒiaƒiaƒia ne miafa konyi ɖe mia vi siwo miewɔ vi na la ta. Mina miaƒe ta ŋu naɖi ƒiaƒiaƒia abe akaga tɔ ene, elabe woaɖe aboyo mia viawo adzoe le mia gbɔ.

english_verse: Doomed! You're doomed! At night you lie in bed, making evil plans. And when morning comes, you do what you've planned because you have the power.
translation_verse: Baba na ame siwo, ne wole aba dzi la, woɖoa vɔ̃ ɖe tame hewɔa ɖoɖo ɖe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ŋu, eye ne agu dze la, woyina ɖawɔnɛ, elabe ŋusẽ le wo si.

english_verse: You grab any field or house that you want; you cheat families out of homes and land.
translation_verse: Agblee biã ŋu na wo o, woxɔnɛ sesẽe; xɔe biã ŋu na wo o, wotsyɔa asi edzi. Wotea ame kple eƒe ƒometɔwo ɖe anyi, eye woxɔa woƒe domenyinu le wo si.

english_verse: But here is what the Lord says: “I am planning trouble for you. Your necks will be caught in a noose, and you will be disgraced in this time of disaster.”
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, meɖo nugbe ɖe mia ŋu, eye miate ŋu aɖe kɔ ɖa le ete o. Mana miage ɖe xaxa me ale be miagate ŋu anɔ yiyim dàdatɔe azɔ o, elabe ɣeyiɣi vɔ̃ wòanye na mi.

english_verse: When that happens, this sorrowful song will be sung about you: “Ruined! Completely ruined! The Lord has taken our land and given it to traitors.”
translation_verse: Tso gbe ma gbe la, woadzi fewuɖuha ɖe mia ŋu, eye woadzi konyifaha vevie agblɔ be: Wogblẽ mía dome keŋkeŋ! Etrɔ nye dukɔ la ƒe gome, ale ke wòxɔe le asinyee? Ema míaƒe agblewo ɖe ame siwo ɖe aboyo mí la dome.”

english_verse: And so you will never again own property among the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Eya ta, ame aɖeke manɔ asiwò adzidze nu, ada ka le Aƒetɔ ƒe ameha dome o.

english_verse: “Enough of your preaching!” That's what you tell me. “We won't be disgraced, so stop preaching!”
translation_verse: Wole gbɔgblɔm be: “Dzudzɔ nyagbɔgblɔ! Ame aɖeke megagblɔ nya tso nu sia tɔgbe ŋu o! Womele gbɔ ɖi ge mí o.”

english_verse: Descendants of Jacob, is it right for you to claim that the Lord did what he did because he was angry? Doesn't he always bless those who do right?
translation_verse: Ao, Yakob ƒe ƒome, ɖe woagblɔ esia? Ðe Aƒetɔ ƒe gbɔgbɔ megbɔa dzi ɖi oa? Ðe nu siawo nye eƒe nuwɔnaa? Ðe nye nyawo mewɔa nyui na ame si zɔna le nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ me oa?

english_verse: My people, you have turned against one another! You have even stolen clothes right off the backs of innocent neighbors who pass by in peace.
translation_verse: “Ke mietso ɖe nye amewo ŋu abe futɔwo ene. Mieɖe awu ʋlaya le ame siwo ɖe dzi ɖi bɔkɔɔ va tso eme yina ƒe awuwo dzi; evɔ la, aʋawɔwɔ menɔ tame na wo o.

english_verse: You take over lovely homes that belong to the women of my nation. Then you cheat their children out of the inheritance that comes from the Lord.
translation_verse: Mienyà nye dukɔ la ƒe nyɔnuwo do goe le aƒe siwo gbɔ womelɔ̃a nu le o la me. Mieɖe nye bubu le wo viwo ŋu ɖikaa.

english_verse: Get out of here, you crooks! You'll find no rest here. You're not fit to belong to the Lord's people, and you will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Mitso miadzo! Elabe afi sia menye gbɔɖemeƒe aɖeke o, le nu makɔmakɔ si gblẽa nu keŋkeŋ la ta.

english_verse: The only prophet you want is a liar who will say, “Drink and get drunk!” A Promise of Hope
translation_verse: Ne ame aɖe akplɔ ya ɖo anɔ tsatsam anɔ alakpa dam be: “Magblɔ nya na mi tso wain kple aha sesẽ ŋu” la, eya anye nyagblɔla na dukɔ sia.

english_verse: I, the Lord, promise to bring together the people of Israel who have survived. I will gather them, just as a shepherd brings sheep together, and there will be many.
translation_verse: O Yakob, maƒo mia nu ƒu godoo; maƒo Israel ƒe ame mamlɛawo nu ƒu; maƒo ƒu wo ɖekae abe alẽwo ene ɖe alẽkpɔ ɖeka me.

english_verse: I will break down the gate and lead them out— then I will be their king.
translation_verse: Ame si agbã glia la, adze wo ŋgɔ. Woagbã dua ƒe agbo, eye woazɔ ato eme ado. Woƒe Fia, Aƒetɔ ŋutɔ, adze ŋgɔ na wo.

english_verse: Listen to me, you rulers of Israel! You know right from wrong,
translation_verse: Mi Yakob ƒe tatɔwo kple edziɖulawo, miɖo to miase. Menye miaƒe dɔ wònye be mianya nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ oa?

english_verse: but you prefer to do evil instead of what is right. You skin my people alive. You strip off their flesh,
translation_verse: Ke miawo boŋ mielé fu nyui, eye mielɔ̃ vɔ̃. Mievuvua agbalẽ le amewo ŋu agbagbee, eye miefoa lã le woƒe ƒu ŋu.

english_verse: Someday you will beg the Lord to help you, but he will turn away because of your sins.
translation_verse: Emegbe woado ɣli ayɔ Aƒetɔ, ke matɔ na wo o. Aɣla ŋkume ɖe wo ɣe ma ɣi elabe wowɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi.

english_verse: You lying prophets promise security for anyone who gives you food, but disaster for anyone who refuses to feed you. Here is what the Lord says to you prophets:
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ gblɔ na gbeƒãɖela siwo kplɔa dukɔ la tranae, ame siwo doa boblo be “Ŋutifafa” ne wokpɔ nu ɖu, ke wohoa aʋa ɖe ame siwo menaa naneke wo o la ŋu, lae nye esi:

english_verse: “You will live in the dark, far from the sight of the sun, with no message from me.
translation_verse: Eya ta zã ado ɖe mi, miakpɔ ŋutega o. Blukɔ ado ɖe mi; afa magaɖi o. Ɣe aɖo to ɖe gbeƒãɖelawo, eye ŋkeke azu viviti tsiɖitsiɖi na wo.

english_verse: You prophets and fortunetellers will all be disgraced, with no message from me.”
translation_verse: Woaɖi gbɔ nukpɔlawo, eye woado ŋukpe bokɔwo. Wo katã amia nu kpoo elabe Mawu megale nya ŋu ɖom na wo o.

english_verse: But the Lord has filled me with power and his Spirit. I have been given the courage to speak about justice and to tell you people of Israel that you have sinned.
translation_verse: Ke nye la, wotsɔ ŋusẽ, Aƒetɔ ƒe Gbɔgbɔ, ʋɔnu dzɔdzɔe dɔdrɔ̃ kple ŋutete yɔm taŋ bene magblɔ Yakob ƒe dzidada kple Israel ƒe nuvɔ̃ nɛ.

english_verse: So listen to my message, you rulers of Israel! You hate justice and twist the truth.
translation_verse: Mise esia, mi Yakob ƒe tatɔwo, kple Israel aƒe aƒe la dziɖulawo; mi ame siwo tsri ʋɔnu dzɔdzɔe dɔdrɔ̃, eye miegbe nu sɔsɔe wɔwɔ;

english_verse: You make cruelty and murder a way of life in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: mi ame siwo le Zion tum kple ʋu eye miele Yerusalem-du la tum kple nu gbegblẽ wɔwɔ.

english_verse: You leaders accept bribes for dishonest decisions. You priests and prophets teach and preach, but only for money. Then you say, “The Lord is on our side. No harm will come to us.”
translation_verse: Eƒe tatɔwo xɔa zãnu hafi tsoa nya me; eƒe nunɔlawo xɔa ga hafi fiaa se la, eye gbeƒãɖelawo xɔa ga hafi gblɔa gbedeasi. Evɔ la, woziɔna ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu gblɔna be: “Ɖe Aƒetɔ mele mía dome oa? Vɔ̃ aɖeke mava mía dzi o.”

english_verse: And so, because of you, Jerusalem will be plowed under and left in ruins. Thorns will cover the mountain where the temple now stands.
translation_verse: Eya ta woade agble ɖe Zion. Yerusalem azu glikpo, eye to si dzi gbedoxɔ la le la azu ave, le mia ta. a.

english_verse: In the future, the mountain with the Lord's temple will be the highest of all. It will reach above the hills, and every nation will rush to it.
translation_verse: Ava eme le ɣeyiɣi mamlɛawo me be to si dzi Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔ la le la, woaɖoe anyi wòanye to kɔkɔtɔ; woawɔe wòakɔ agbɔ togbɛwo ta. Dukɔwo ayi afi ma bibibi,

english_verse: People of many nations will come and say, “Let's go up to the mountain of the Lord God of Jacob and worship in his temple.” The Lord will teach us his Law from Jerusalem, and we will obey him.
translation_verse: eye anyigba dzi dukɔwo ava agblɔ be: Miva, mina míayi Aƒetɔ ƒe to la dzi; ne míayi Yakob ƒe Mawu la ƒeme bene wòafia eƒe mɔwo mí, ne míazɔ eƒe toƒewo! Elabe se la atso Zion, eye Aƒetɔ ƒe nya la atso Zion.”

english_verse: He will settle arguments between distant and powerful nations. They will pound their swords and their spears into rakes and shovels; they will never again make war or attack one another.
translation_verse: Adrɔ̃ nya na dukɔ geɖewo, eye wòatso nya me na dukɔ sesẽwo le didiƒe ke. Woatsɔ woƒe yiwo atu kodzoewoe; woƒe akplɔwo atu hɛ gobɛwoe. Dukɔ magatsɔ yi ɖe dukɔ ŋu azɔ o; womagasrɔ̃ aʋawɔwɔ hã o.

english_verse: Everyone will find rest beneath their own fig trees or grape vines, and they will live in peace. This is a solemn promise of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Wo dome ame sia ame aɖe dzi ɖi anɔ eƒe wainka kple eƒe gboti te bɔkɔɔ, ame aɖeke magado vɔvɔ̃ na wo o. Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la ŋutɔe ke nu gblɔ nya sia.

english_verse: Others may follow their gods, but we will always follow the Lord our God. The Lord Will Lead His People Home
translation_verse: Elabe dukɔwo katã le zɔzɔm, ɖe sia ɖe le eƒe mawu ŋkɔ me; ke míawo ya míazɔ le Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la ŋkɔ me ɖaa tegbee. Israel atrɔ gbɔ tso aboyo me

english_verse: The Lord said: At that time I will gather my people— the lame and the outcasts, and all others into whose lives I have brought sorrow.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Gbe ma gbe la, maƒo tekunɔwo kple ame siwo wonyà de gbe kpakple ame siwo mewɔ funyafunyae la nu ƒu.

english_verse: Then the lame and the outcasts will belong to my people and become a strong nation. I, the Lord, will rule them from Mount Zion forever.
translation_verse: Mana tekunɔwo nazu ame siwo susɔ, eye ame siwo wonyà de gbe la, nazu dukɔ sesẽ, eye Aƒetɔ anye fia ɖe wo nu le Zion-to la dzi tegbee tso fifia yi mavɔ me.”

english_verse: Mount Zion in Jerusalem, guardian of my people, you will rule again.
translation_verse: Wò, alẽha la ƒe xɔ tsrala; wò Zion vinyɔnu ƒe togbɛ, gbɔwòe wòava, dziɖuɖu tsãtɔ la ava, Yerusalem vinyɔnu ƒe dziɖuɖu la.

english_verse: Jerusalem, why are you crying? Don't you have a king? Have your advisors gone? Are you suffering like a woman in childbirth?
translation_verse: Azɔ la, nu ka ta nèle ɣli dom sesĩe ale? Ɖe fia aɖeke mele mewò oa? Ɖe wò adaŋudela tsrɔ̃ tae nèle veve sem abe nyɔnu si le ku lém la enea? Alo esi wò adaŋudelawo ku tae mahã?

english_verse: Keep on groaning with pain, you people of Jerusalem! If you escape from your city to the countryside, you will still be taken as prisoners to Babylonia. But later I will rescue you from your enemies.
translation_verse: Zion-nyɔnu, tro ɖokuiwo naŋè abe nyɔnu si le ku lém la ene, elabe ele be miaʋu le dua me aɖanɔ gbedadaƒo. Miayi ɖe Babilon. Afi mae woaɖe mi le, eye Aƒetɔ axɔ mi tso miaƒe futɔwo si me le afi ma.

english_verse: Zion, because of your sins you are surrounded by many nations who say, “We can hardly wait to see you disgraced.”
translation_verse: Azɔ la, dukɔ geɖewo va kpe ta ɖe ŋuwò. Wole gbɔgblɔm be: “Mina woagblẽ kɔ ɖo nɛ, mina míalĩ ŋku ɖe Zion dzi!”

english_verse: But they don't know that I, the Lord, have gathered them here to grind them like grain.
translation_verse: Ke womenya Aƒetɔ ƒe tame o. Womese eƒe ɖoɖo gɔme o. Womese egɔme be woƒo ƒu yewo heli kɔe ɖi abe lubabla ene ɖe lugbɔƒe o.

english_verse: Smash them to pieces, Zion! I'll let you be like a bull with iron horns and bronze hoofs. Crush those nations and bring their wealth to me, the Lord of the earth.
translation_verse: “Zion vinyɔnu tso natugu nu, elabe mawɔ wò dzo wòanye ga yibɔ, eye wò afɔkli nanye akɔbli. Miagbã dukɔ geɖewo gudugudu, eye miakɔ̀ woƒe viɖenuwo ŋu na Aƒetɔ, miatsɔ woƒe kesinɔnuwo na xexeme blibo ƒe Aƒetɔ la.

english_verse: Jerusalem, enemy troops have surrounded you; they have struck Israel's ruler in the face with a stick.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, woɖo gli ƒo xlã wò, woƒu kpo ɖe ŋuwò. Wotsɔ ati ƒo to me na Israel-kplɔla la. Mawu do ŋugbe be dziɖula aɖe atso Betlehem ava

english_verse: Bethlehem Ephrath, you are one of the smallest towns in the nation of Judah. But the Lord will choose one of your people to rule the nation— someone whose family goes back to ancient times.
translation_verse: “Ke wò Betlehem Efrata, wòe nye du suetɔ kekeake le Yuda-ƒomeawo dome, gake mewòe dziɖula si aɖu Israel dzi la adzɔ tso nam. Dziɖula sia ƒe ƒome li xoxoxo tso keke gbe aɖe gbe ke.”

english_verse: The Lord will abandon Israel only until this ruler is born, and the rest of his family returns to Israel.
translation_verse: Eya ta aɖe asi le wo ŋu va se ɖe esime nyɔnu si le ku lém la, nadzi vi. Ekema nɔvia siwo susɔ la, atrɔ gbɔ va wo nɔvi Israelviwo gbɔ.

english_verse: Like a shepherd taking care of his sheep, this ruler will lead and care for his people by the power and glorious name of the Lord his God. His people will live securely, and the whole earth will know his true greatness,
translation_verse: Anɔ te anyi eƒe alẽha, le Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋusẽ me, le Aƒetɔ, eƒe Mawu ƒe fianyenye ŋkɔ me. Woanɔ anyi dedie, elabe azɔ la, anye gã va se ɖe anyigba ƒe mlɔenuwo ke,

english_verse: because he will bring peace. Assyria Will Be Defeated Let Assyria attack our country and our palaces. We will counterattack, led by a number of rulers
translation_verse: eye esia anye ŋutifafa. Aƒetɔ aɖe etɔwo eye wòahe to na futɔwo Ne Asiriatɔ la va míaƒe anyigba dzi, eye wòɖo afɔ míaƒe anyigba dzi la, míadɔ lãkplɔvi adrẽ kple amegã enyi ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: whose strong army will defeat the nation of Assyria. Yes, our leaders will rescue us, if those Assyrians dare to invade our land. The Survivors Will Be Safe
translation_verse: Woatsɔ yi aɖu Asiria-nyigba la dzi, wòaɖu Nimrod dzi kple yi si wòɖe tso aku me la, eye woaɖe mí tso Asiriatɔ la si me ne eva míaƒe anyigba dzi, eye wòɖo afɔ míaƒe liƒo dzi.

english_verse: A few of Jacob's descendants survived and are scattered among the nations. But the Lord will let them cover the earth like dew and rain that refreshes the soil.
translation_verse: Ekema Yakob ƒe ame siwo susɔ la, anɔ dukɔ geɖewo dome abe zãmu tso Aƒetɔ gbɔ abe agbafie si nyɔna ɖe gbe dzi si medzɔa amegbetɔ alo lalaa amegbetɔ viwo o la ene.

english_verse: At present they are scattered, but later they will attack, as though they were fierce lions pouncing on sheep. Their enemies will be torn to shreds, with no one to save them;
translation_verse: Yakob ƒe ame siwo susɔ la anɔ dukɔwo dome, le anyigba dzi dukɔwo dome abe dzata le gbemelãwo dome le ave me, alo abe dzatavi le alẽhawo dome ene. Ne eto wo dome la, xɔnametɔ aɖeke meganɔa anyi o; edzea wo dzi hevuvua wo.

english_verse: they will be helpless, completely destroyed. Idols Will Be Destroyed in Israel
translation_verse: Woakɔ wò alɔ dzi ɖe wò ketɔwo ŋu, eye wòatsrɔ̃ wò futɔwo katã.

english_verse: The Lord said: At that time I will wipe out your cavalry and chariots,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Gbe ma gbe la, matsrɔ̃ miaƒe sɔwo ɖa le mia dome, eye magblẽ miaƒe tasiaɖamwo keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: as well as your cities and your fortresses.
translation_verse: Matsrɔ̃ du siwo le wò anyigba dzi, eye mamu wò mɔ́ sesẽwo katã aƒu anyi.

english_verse: I will stop you from telling fortunes and practicing witchcraft.
translation_verse: Matsrɔ̃ dzosasa ɖa le asiwò me, eye bokɔ aɖeke maganɔ asiwò o.

english_verse: You will no longer worship the idols or stone images you have made— I will destroy them,
translation_verse: Matsrɔ̃ miaƒe aklama kpakpɛwo kple aƒeliwo ɖa le dowòme eye màgade ta agu na wò asinudɔwɔwɔwo azɔ o.

english_verse: together with the sacred poles and even your towns.
translation_verse: Maho miaƒe nyɔnumawu, Aserawo ɖa le dowòme, eye magbã wò duwo keŋ.

english_verse: I will become furious and take revenge on the nations that refuse to obey me.
translation_verse: Mabia hlɔ̃ dukɔ siwo gbe be yewomaɖo tom o la, le dɔmedzoe kple dziku me.”

english_verse: The Lord said to his people: Come and present your case to the hills and mountains.
translation_verse: Mise nya si gblɔm Aƒetɔ le la ɖa. Tso ne nàto wò nya le towo ŋkume, eye nà togbɛwo nase wò gbe.

english_verse: Israel, I am bringing charges against you— I call upon the mountains and the earth's firm foundation to be my witnesses.
translation_verse: Mi towo, mise Aƒetɔ ƒe dzrenya! Mi anyigba ƒe gɔmeɖoɖo si li tegbee hã, misee. Elabe Aƒetɔ tsɔ nya ɖe eƒe dukɔ ŋu. Ele nya he ge kple Israel.

english_verse: My people, have I wronged you in any way at all? Please tell me.
translation_verse: “Ao, nye dukɔ, nu kae mewɔ ɖe ŋuwò? Nu ka mee meɖe fu na wò le? Ɖo eŋu nam.

english_verse: I rescued you from Egypt, where you were slaves. I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Elabe mekplɔ wò tso Egipte-nyigba dzi, eye meɖe wò tso kluvinyenye me. Medɔ Mose, Aron kple Miryam ɖe ŋgɔwò.

english_verse: Don't forget the evil plans of King Balak of Moab or what Balaam son of Beor said to him. Remember how I, the Lord, saved you many times on your way from Acacia to Gilgal. True Obedience
translation_verse: O, nye dukɔ, ɖo ŋku nu si Moab-fia Balak ɖo be yeawɔ wò kple ale si Bileam, Beor vi la ɖo eŋu nɛ la dzi. Ɖo ŋku nu siwo dzɔ tso Sitim va se ɖe Gilgal dzi, nàdze si Aƒetɔ ƒe xɔname.” Nu si dim Aƒetɔ le

english_verse: What offering should I bring when I bow down to worship the Lord God Most High? Should I try to please him by sacrificing calves a year old?
translation_verse: Nu kae matsɔ ɖe asi ava Aƒetɔ ŋkume, eye made ta agu ɖe Mawu Dziƒoʋĩtɔ la ŋkume? Ðe matsɔ nyivi si xɔ ƒe ɖeka la ɖe asi ayi eŋkume, be mawɔ numemevɔsa nɛa?

english_verse: Will thousands of sheep or rivers of olive oil make God satisfied with me? Should I sacrifice to the Lord my first-born child as payment for my terrible sins?
translation_verse: Ðe agbo akpe nanewo kple amitɔʋu akpeakpewo adze Aƒetɔ ŋua? Ðe matsɔ nye ŋgɔgbevi anae ɖe nye dzidada ta kple nye dɔmevi ana ɖe nye luʋɔ ƒe nuvɔ̃wo taa?

english_verse: The Lord God has told us what is right and what he demands: “See that justice is done, let mercy be your first concern, and humbly obey your God.” Cheating and Violence
translation_verse: O, amegbetɔ, egblɔ nu si nyo la na wò. Nu ka dim Aƒetɔ le be nàwɔ? Ɖe menye nàdrɔ̃ ʋɔnu dzɔdzɔe, nàlɔ̃ dɔmenyowɔwɔ, eye nàbɔbɔ ɖokuiwò ahazɔ kple wò Mawu oa? Aƒetɔ ahe to na eƒe dukɔ

english_verse: I am the Lord, and you are wise to respect my power to punish. So listen to my message for the city of Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe ɖi bobobo yɔ du la eye enye nunya deto be woavɔ̃ wò ŋkɔ. “Dua ƒe to kple ameha la misee.

english_verse: But I, the Lord, will punish you for cheating with weights and with measures.
translation_verse: Ðe mate ŋu atso afia na ame si wɔa amebanudanu ŋudɔ, eye amebanudakpe le eƒe kotoku mea?

english_verse: You rich people are violent, and everyone tells lies.
translation_verse: Miaƒe kesinɔtɔwo yɔ fũu kple ŋutasesẽ, dua me nɔlawo kaa aʋatso, eye alakpaɖe le nu me na wo.

english_verse: Because of your sins, I will wound you and leave you ruined and defenseless.
translation_verse: Eya ta nye hã medze tohehe gɔme na mi, eye megblẽ mia dome le miaƒe nuvɔ̃wo ta.

english_verse: You will eat, but still be hungry; you will store up goods, but lose everything— I, the Lord, will let it all be captured in war.
translation_verse: Miaɖu nu; ke miaɖi ƒo o, eye dɔ aganɔ mia wum boŋ. Miadzra nu ɖo, ke manɔ anyi o, eye nu si medzra ɖo la, matsɔe ade asi na yi.

english_verse: You won't harvest what you plant or use the oil from your olive trees or drink the wine from grapes you grow.
translation_verse: Miaƒã nu, ke miaŋee o. Miawɔ ami, ke miakpɔ ɖeke asi ɖe ŋuti gɔ̃ hã o. Miafiã wain, ke miakpɔ ɖeke ano o.

english_verse: Jerusalem, this will happen because you followed the sinful example of kings Omri and Ahab. Now I will destroy you and your property. Then the people of every nation will make fun and insult you.
translation_verse: Elabe miewɔ Omri ƒe ɖoɖowo dzi, miewɔ Axab ƒe nuwɔnawo katã, eye miezɔ ɖe woƒe adaŋudedewo nu, ne matsɔ wò awɔ gbegbee, eye woaʋuʋu ta, ɖe ame siwo le mewò la ŋu. Ale àtsɔ dukɔwo ƒe alɔmeɖeɖe.

english_verse: I feel so empty inside— like someone starving for grapes or figs, after the vines and trees have all been picked clean.
translation_verse: Evɔ nam! Elabe mezu abe ale si woxaa kutsetse vɔ le dzomeŋɔli, abe ale si wotsaa wain tsetsetiwo me vɔ la ene: kutsetse aɖeke meli woaɖu o, gbotitsetse ɖiɖi gbãtɔ si nye luʋɔ di la meli o;

english_verse: No one is loyal to God; no one does right. Everyone is brutal and eager to deceive everyone else.
translation_verse: mawumeme tsrɔ̃ le anyigba dzi, eye ame dzɔdzɔe aɖeke megale amegbetɔwo dome o. Wo katã wode xa be woakɔ ʋu ɖi. Ame sia ame ɖo ɖɔ ɖi na nɔvia.

english_verse: People cooperate to commit crime. Judges and leaders demand bribes, and rulers cheat in court.
translation_verse: Woda asi ɖe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ dzi, eye wowɔnɛ nyuie. Amegãwo kple ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo biaa zãnu. Dumegã gblɔa nya vɔ̃ɖi si dzroe la. Ale wosɔa nu ɖe vɔ̃wɔwɔ ŋu.

english_verse: The most honest of them is worse than a thorn patch. Your doom has come! Lookouts sound the warning, and everyone panics.
translation_verse: Wo dometɔ nyuitɔ le abe ŋu ene, eye woƒe nuteƒewɔla nyuitɔ vɔ̃ɖi wu aŋɔkakpɔtɔtɔ. Ŋkeke de be woahe to na woƒe gbetakpɔlawo. Azɔ la, wotɔtɔ keŋ.

english_verse: Don't trust anyone, not even your best friend, and be careful what you say to the one you love.
translation_verse: Mègaxɔ hawòvi dzi se o, eye mègaɖo ŋu ɖe xɔ̃wò aɖeke ŋu o. Kpɔ wò nu dzi le nyɔnu si le gbɔwò la ŋu,

english_verse: Sons refuse to respect their own fathers, daughters rebel against their own mothers, and daughters-in-law despise their mothers-in-law. Your family is now your enemy.
translation_verse: elabe viŋutsu mabu tɔ́a o, vinyɔnu atsi tre ɖe nɔa ŋuti, eye lɔ̃xoyɔvinyɔnu atso ɖe lɔ̃xoa ŋu. Ame ƒe futɔwo anye eya ŋutɔ ƒe aƒemetɔwo.

english_verse: But I trust the Lord God to save me, and I will wait for him to answer my prayer. The Nation Turns to God
translation_verse: Ke nye la, matso ŋku na Aƒetɔ. Makpɔ mɔ na Mawu, nye Xɔnametɔ, Nye Mawu aɖo tom. Aƒetɔ axɔ eƒe amewo ɖe agbe

english_verse: My enemies, don't be glad because of my troubles! I may have fallen, but I will get up; I may be sitting in the dark, but the Lord is my light.
translation_verse: Nye futɔ, mèganɔ dzidzɔ kpɔm le nye anyidzedze ŋu o. Ne medze anyi la, magafɔ. Ne menɔ anyi ɖe viviti me la, Aƒetɔ anye kekeli nam.

english_verse: I have sinned against the Lord. And so I must endure his anger, until he comes to my defense. But I know that I will see him making things right for me and leading me to the light.
translation_verse: Mado dzi atsɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe dziku, elabe mewɔ vɔ̃ ɖe eŋu, va se ɖe esime wòaʋli tanye, atso afia nam. Akplɔm ado ɖe kekeli nu, eye makpɔ eƒe ɖeɖe.

english_verse: You, my enemies, said, “The Lord God is helpless.” Now each of you will be disgraced and put to shame. I will see you trampled like mud in the street. A Bright Future
translation_verse: Ekema nye futɔ akpɔe, eye ŋukpe alée. Eya ame si le biayem be: “Afi ka Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la le?” Makpɔe kakaka, ne wole efanyam abe ba ene le ablɔ dzi.

english_verse: Towns of Judah, the day is coming when your walls will be rebuilt, and your boundaries enlarged.
translation_verse: Ɣeyiɣi si woagbugbɔ wò gliwo aɖo la, tu aƒe. Ɣe ma ɣi la, miaƒe liƒowo ate yi megbe ʋĩi.

english_verse: Those nations will suffer disaster because of what they did. Micah's Prayer and the Lord's Answer
translation_verse: Ke anyigba dzi azu gbegbe le edzinɔlawo ta, le woƒe nuwɔnawo ƒe kutsetse ta. Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔme trɔ ɖe Israel ŋu

english_verse: Lead your people, Lord! Come and be our shepherd. Grasslands surround us, but we live in a forest. So lead us to Bashan and Gilead, and let us find pasture as we did long ago.
translation_verse: Tsɔ wò atikplɔ nàkplɔ wò dukɔ, alẽha si ƒe dome nènyi, si tsò abo le ave me, le anyigba si dzi abɔ le la titina. Na woayi aɖaɖu gbe le Basan kple Gilead abe le blema ene.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will work miracles just as I did when I led you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Maɖe nukunuwo afia wò, abe gbe si gbe nèdo go tso Egipte-nyigba dzi ene.

english_verse: Nations will see this and be ashamed because of their helpless armies. They will be in shock, unable to speak or hear,
translation_verse: Dukɔwo akpɔe, eye ŋu akpe wo, togbɔ be ŋutete le wo ŋu ŋutɔ hã. Woaɖo asi nu, eye woƒe to atsí.

english_verse: because of their fear of me, your Lord and God. Then they will come trembling, crawling out of their fortresses like insects or snakes, lapping up the dust. No One Is Like God The people said:
translation_verse: Woaɖuɖɔ kewɔ abe da kple nutata bubuwo le anyigba ene. Woado tso woƒe mɔ́ sesẽwo me anɔ dzodzom nyànyanya kple vɔvɔ̃. Woalulu ava Aƒetɔ, mía Mawu la gbɔ, eye vɔvɔ̃ aɖo wo le tawò.

english_verse: Our God, no one is like you. We are all that is left of your chosen people, and you freely forgive our sin and guilt. You don't stay angry forever; you're glad to have pity
translation_verse: Ame kae nye Mawu li abe wò ene si tsɔa vodada kena, eye wòŋea aɖaba ƒua eƒe domenyinu si susɔ la ƒe dzidadawo dzi? Meléa dziku ɖi ɖikaa o, elabe ekpɔa dzidzɔ le amenuveve ŋu.

english_verse: and pleased to be merciful. You will trample on our sins and throw them in the sea.
translation_verse: Eƒe dɔme agatrɔ ɖe mía ŋu. Atiti afɔ ɖe míaƒe vodadawo dzi. Àtsɔ míaƒe nuvɔ̃wo aƒu gbe ɖe atsiaƒu ƒe gogloƒe ke!

english_verse: You will keep your word and be faithful to Jacob and to Abraham, as you promised our ancestors many years ago.
translation_verse: Àwɔ nuteƒe na Yakob, eye àve Abraham nu, abe ale si nèka atam na mía tɔgbuiwo le blema ene.

english_verse: I am Nahum from Elkosh. And this is the message that I wrote down about Nineveh. The Fierce Anger of the Lord
translation_verse: Gbedeasi ɖe Ninive ŋu. Naxum, Elkositɔ la ƒe ŋutegagbalẽ. Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔmedzoe ɖe Ninive ŋu

english_verse: The Lord God demands loyalty. In his anger, he takes revenge on his enemies.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ nye Mawu si ʋãa ŋu, eye wòbiaa hlɔ̃. Aƒetɔ biaa hlɔ̃, eye wòdoa dɔmedzoe. Aƒetɔ hea to na eƒe ketɔwo, eye wòléa dɔmedzoe ɖi na eƒe futɔwo.

english_verse: The Lord is powerful, yet patient; he makes sure that the guilty are always punished. He can be seen in storms and in whirlwinds; clouds are the dust from his feet.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ medoa dziku kabakaba o; ŋusẽ le esi ŋutɔ. Meɖea asi le fɔɖila ŋu o. Etoƒe le ahom kple yali me, Alilikpowo nye ʋuʋudedi nɔa eƒe afɔtoƒe.

english_verse: At the Lord's command, oceans and rivers dry up. Bashan, Mount Carmel, and Lebanon wither, and their flowers fade.
translation_verse: Ebluna ɖe atsiaƒu ta, wòmiena. Enana be tɔsisiwo katã miena. Gbe yrɔna le Basan kple Karmel; Lebanon seƒoƒowo yrɔna.

english_verse: At the sight of the Lord, mountains and hills tremble and melt; the earth and its people shudder and shake.
translation_verse: Towo ʋuʋuna le eŋgɔ; togbɛwo lólona. Anyigba tsi ƒeƒle le eŋkume, xexea me kple emenɔlawo katã.

english_verse: Who can stand the heat of his furious anger? It flashes out like fire and shatters stones. The Power of Assyria Will Be Broken
translation_verse: Ne Aƒetɔ do dziku la, ame kae ate ŋu anɔ te ɖe enu? Ne edo dɔmedzoe helihelĩ la, ɖe ame aɖe ate ŋu anɔ te ɖe enua? Etrɔa eƒe dɔmedzoe kɔna ɖi abe dzo ene, eye agakpewo wóna le eŋgɔ.

english_verse: The Lord is good. He protects those who trust him in times of trouble.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔme nyo; enye sitsoƒe na eƒe amewo le xaxaɣi. Enya ame siwo sínɛ tsona.

english_verse: But like a roaring flood, the Lord chases his enemies into dark places and destroys them.
translation_verse: Ke atsɔ tsiɖɔɖɔ sesẽ atsrɔ̃ eƒe futɔwo keŋkeŋ, eye wòayɔ̀ eƒe ketɔwo ɖe nu ayi viviti me.

english_verse: So don't plot against the Lord! He wipes out his enemies, and they never revive.
translation_verse: Nugbe ka ɖom miele ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu? Ele nuwo nu wu ge keŋkeŋ. Mabia hlɔ̃ eƒe futɔ zi eve o.

english_verse: They are like drunkards overcome by wine, or like twisted thornbushes burning in a fire.
translation_verse: Ne woɖo wo nɔewo me abe ŋuwo ene, alo woƒo tsi belee abe woƒe nunonowo ene hã, wole bibi ge vlavlavla abe gbe ƒuƒu ene.

english_verse: Assyria, one of your rulers has made evil plans against the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɖe ame medo tso mewò, si ɖo nugbe ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu, hede adaŋu be yeado hlɔ̃ oa?

english_verse: But the Lord says, “Assyria, no matter how strong you are, you will be cut down! My people Judah, I have troubled you before, but I won't do it again.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ be: “Togbɔ be wosesẽ, eye wosɔ gbɔ hã la, woatsrɔ̃ avɔ keŋkeŋ. Togbɔ be mena miekpe fu geɖe hã la, miagakpe fu azɔ o.

english_verse: I'll snap your chains and set you free from the Assyrians.”
translation_verse: Ke azɔ maŋe eƒe kɔkuti ɖa le mia ŋu, eye matso miaƒe kɔsɔkɔsɔwo ɖa.”

english_verse: Assyria, this is what else the Lord says to you: “Your name will be forgotten. I will destroy every idol in your temple, and I will send you to the grave, because you are worthless.”
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ de se ɖe mia ŋu be: “Womagatɔ mia ŋkɔ gbeɖe o. Matsrɔ̃ aklama kpakpɛ kple legba kɔ̀kɔwo ɖa le miaƒe mawuxɔwo me. Maɖe yɔdo na mi, elabe miegblẽ.”

english_verse: Look toward the mountains, people of Judah! Here comes a messenger with good news of peace. Celebrate your festivals. Keep your promises to God. Your evil enemies are destroyed and will never again invade your country.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, du nyui xɔla aɖee nye ekem le du dzi tso toawo dzi gbɔna. Etsɔ nya nyui aɖe gbɔnae. Ele gbeƒã ɖem ŋutifafa. Yudatɔwo, miɖu ŋkekenyuiwo azɔ! Mixe miaƒe adzɔgbeɖefewo! Elabe ame vlo la magatso ɖe mia ŋu azɔ gbeɖe o! Wotsrɔ̃e gbidii!

english_verse: Nineveh, someone is coming to attack and scatter you. Guard your fortresses! Watch the road! Be brave! Prepare for battle!
translation_verse: Nugbãla tso ɖe ŋuwò. Dzɔ wò sitsoƒexɔwo ŋu. Nɔ ŋudzɔ nànɔ mɔ dzi kpɔm. Bla ali dzi; dzra ɖo kple wò ŋusẽ katã.

english_verse: Nineveh, on this day of attack, your enemies' shields are red; their uniforms are crimson.
translation_verse: Eƒe kalẽtɔwo ƒe akpoxɔnuwo biã hẽe; eƒe asrafowo le nyagãdzĩwu me. Tasiaɖamwo le keklẽm abe dzo ƒe aɖe ene. Ne woɖo ɖe fli me la, wonyea woƒe akplɔwo.

english_verse: Their horses prance, and their armored chariots dart around like lightning or flaming torches.
translation_verse: Tasiaɖamwo le zi nyem le kpɔdomeewo kple ablɔwo dzi, le yiyim, le gbɔgbɔm. Woklẽ abe akakatiwo ene; woɖe abla abe dzikedzo ene.

english_verse: An officer gives a command. But his soldiers stumble, as they hasten to build a shelter to protect themselves against rocks thrown down from the city wall.
translation_verse: Woyɔ aʋakplɔlawo, wole nu klim le yiyim. Futɔwo ɖe abla yi duglia gbɔ, wotu akpoxɔ ɖi.

english_verse: The river gates fly open, and panic floods the palace.
translation_verse: Woʋu agbo siwo le tɔsisia gbɔ lɔƒo. Vɔvɔ̃ lé fiasã la me nɔlawo.

english_verse: Nineveh is disgraced. The queen is dragged off. Her servant women mourn; they moan like doves, and they beat their breasts in sorrow.
translation_verse: Woɖe nu le fia srɔ̃ ŋu, hekplɔe dzoe amamae. Eƒe nyɔnudɔlawo nɔ akɔta ƒom, nɔ fafam nɛ abe ahɔnɛ ene henɔ vevesese ɖem fia.

english_verse: Nineveh is like a pond with leaking water. Shouts of “Stop! Don't go!” can be heard everywhere. But everyone is leaving.
translation_verse: Ninivetɔwo do le dua me bibibi abe tsisisi tso tsikpo gbagbã me ene. Wodo ɣli be: “Mitɔ! Mitɔ!” Ke ame aɖeke menye kɔ kpɔ megbe o.

english_verse: Enemy soldiers shout, “The city is full of treasure and all kinds of wealth. Steal her silver! Grab her gold!”
translation_verse: Miha klosalo! Miha sika! Kesinɔnuwo li zã! Nu xɔasi veviwo yɔ dua! Miha wo!

english_verse: Nineveh is doomed! Destroyed! Her people tremble with fear; their faces turn pale.
translation_verse: Ninive gbã! Egbã zu du ƒuƒlu! Vɔvɔ̃ ɖo amewo, woƒe klowo le ƒoƒom kpakpakpa. Ŋusẽ vɔ le wo ŋu, wole dzodzom nyànyanya. Woƒe mo trɔ!

english_verse: What happened to this city? They were safer there than powerful lions in a den, with no one to disturb them.
translation_verse: Afi ka dzatawo ƒe do la le, afi ka dzataviwo ƒe agado la le, afi si dzata léa nu vanɛ, eye dzataviwo nɔa anyi naneke medoa ŋɔdzi na wo o?

english_verse: These are the same lions that ferociously attacked their victims, then dragged away the flesh to feed their young.
translation_verse: Dzata vuvu lã ale si nu atu viawo, eye wòwu ɖewo tsɔ vɛ na dzatanɔwo hã. Elé lã geɖe vuvu va kɔ ɖe enɔƒe fũu.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful is against you, Nineveh. God will burn your chariots and send an army to kill those young lions of yours. You will never again make victims of others or send messengers to threaten everyone on this earth.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Kpɔ ɖa, metso ɖe ŋuwò azɔ. Matɔ dzo wò tasiaɖamwo, eye wò kalẽtɔwo atsi aʋa. Matsi wò adzodada nu le anyigba dzi. Ŋusẽ avɔ le ŋuwò keŋ; ame aɖeke magase ŋkɔwò azɔ o.”

english_verse: Doom to the crime capital! Nineveh, city of murder and treachery,
translation_verse: Baba na du si ƒe asi ƒo ʋu, afi si alakpadada kple adzonuwo bɔ ɖo, nuhaha nu metsina o!

english_verse: here is your fate— cracking whips, churning wheels; galloping horses, roaring chariots;
translation_verse: Sɔƒokawo ƒe sɔwo dzidzedze; sɔwo ƒe duƒuƒu kplakplakpla; tasiaɖamfɔwo ƒe zinyenye; tasiaɖamwo ƒe hoowɔwɔ,

english_verse: You were nothing more than a prostitute using your magical charms and witchcraft to attract and trap nations.
translation_verse: Le gbolo ƒe gbolowɔwɔ vivivo kple dzosala dzetugbe la, ame si tsɔ eƒe tugbedzedze kple dzosasa flu dukɔwo heɖe aboyo wo ta la,

english_verse: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, am now your enemy. I will pull up your skirt and let nations and kingdoms stare at your nakedness.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be, kpɔ ɖa, metso ɖe ŋuwò. Maklo awu le ŋuwò akɔ tsyɔ ŋkume na wò, eye mana dukɔwo nakpɔ wò ama me, fiaɖuƒewo akpɔ wò ŋukpeƒe.

english_verse: I will cover you with garbage, treat you like trash, and rub you in the dirt.
translation_verse: Malɔ gbeɖuɖɔ akɔ ɖe dziwò, maɖi gbɔ wò, eye mawɔ wò nazu nukpɔkpɔ.

english_verse: Everyone who sees you will turn away and shout, “Nineveh is done for! Is anyone willing to mourn or to give her comfort?” Nineveh's Fate Is Sealed
translation_verse: Ame siwo katã kpɔ wò la así le nu wò agblɔ be: “Wogbã Ninive-du! Ame kae afa nɛ? Afi ka makpɔ akɔfala tsoe nɛ?”

english_verse: Nineveh, do you feel safer than the city of Thebes? The Nile River was its wall of defense.
translation_verse: Ɖe nènyo wu Tebes si wotso ɖe Nil-tɔsisi to; tsi ƒo xlãe godoo, atsiaƒu nye kpo nɔ eŋu, eye tsi nye gli nɔ eŋu laa?

english_verse: Thebes trusted the mighty power of Ethiopia and Egypt; the nations of Put and Libya were her allies.
translation_verse: Etiopia nye eƒe ŋusẽ, seɖoƒe meli na Egipte ya tɔ o; eƒe kpeɖeŋutɔwoe nye Putitɔwo kple Libiatɔwo.

english_verse: But she was captured and taken to a foreign country. Her children were murdered at every street corner. The members of her royal family were auctioned off, and her high officials were bound in chains.
translation_verse: Ke woɖe aboyoe, kplɔe dzoe. Woxlã wo viwo ɖe nu wokaka ɖe ablɔ ɖe sia ɖe dzi. Wodzidze nu ɖe woƒe bubumewo dzi, eye wode kɔsɔkɔsɔ woƒe amegãwo.

english_verse: Nineveh, now it's your turn! You will get drunk and try to hide from your enemy.
translation_verse: Wò hã àmu aha, wò mo atsyɔ, eye nàdi afi si nàsí ayi, adzo le wò futɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: Your fortresses are fig trees with ripe figs. Merely shake the trees, and fruit will fall into every open mouth.
translation_verse: Wò mɔ́wo katã le abe gboti siwo dzi kutsetse gbãtɔwo ɖi ɖo la ene. Ne woʋuʋu atia la, kutsetse ɖiɖiawo gena dzea nu me na eɖula.

english_verse: Your army is weak. Fire has destroyed the crossbars on your city gates; now they stand wide open to your enemy.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, wò aʋakɔwo le abe nyɔnuwo ene. Wò anyigba ƒe agbowo le ʋuʋu ɖi gbadzaa na wò futɔwo. Dzo fiã wò gametiwo.

english_verse: Your city is under attack. Haul in extra water! Strengthen your defenses! Start making bricks! Stir the mortar!
translation_verse: Du tsi da ɖi, elabe wole to ɖe ge ɖe wò. Na wò mɔwo nagasẽ ɖe dzi. Yi anyiʋe me nànya anyi atsɔ ame anyikpewo da ɖi.

english_verse: You will still go up in flames and be cut down by swords that will wipe you out like a field attacked by grasshoppers. So, go ahead and increase like a swarm of locusts!
translation_verse: Afi mae dzo afiã wò le, eye nàtsi yi nu le. Woavuvu wò abe ale si ʋetsuviwo ɖua nui ene. Midzi ɖe dzi abe ʋetsuviwo ene, eye midzi abe gbagblame ene.

english_verse: More merchants are in your city than there are stars in the sky— but they are like locusts that eat everything, then fly away.
translation_verse: Èna wò asitsalawo dzi ɖe edzi sɔ gbɔ wu dziƒoɣletiviwo gɔ̃ hã. Ke azɔ la, ʋetsuvi la ke aʋala me, eye wòdzo dzó.

english_verse: Your guards and your officials are swarms of locusts. On a chilly day they settle on a fence, but when the sun comes out, they take off to who-knows-where.
translation_verse: Wò amegãwo sɔ gbɔ abe gbagblamewo ene, eye wò agbalẽfialawo le abe ʋetsuviwo ƒe ha le kpɔ ŋu, le vuvɔgbe ene. Ke ne ɣe dze la, wodzona dzóna, eye ame aɖeke menyaa afi si wodzo yi o.

english_verse: King of Assyria, your officials and leaders are sound asleep, while your people are scattered in the mountains. Yes, your people are sheep without a shepherd.
translation_verse: O Asiria-fia, wò alẽkplɔlawo le alɔ̃ dɔm, wò bubumewo le akɔlɔ̃e dɔm. Wò amewo kaka ɖe towo dzi, eye ame aɖeke meli aƒo wo nu ƒu o.

english_verse: You're fatally wounded. There's no hope for you. But everyone claps when they hear this news, because your constant cruelty has caused them pain.
translation_verse: Wɔwɔ aɖeke mele nu vevi si wɔ wò la ŋu o; èxɔ abi vevie. Ame siwo katã se wò nyaa la, kpɔ dzidzɔ, si akpe. Elabe ɖe ame aɖe li si ŋu wò nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ madzudzɔmadzudzɔe la megblẽ nu le oa?

english_verse: I am Habakkuk the prophet. And this is the message that the Lord gave me. Habakkuk Complains to the Lord
translation_verse: Gbedeasi sia nye nya si Mawu ɖe fia eƒe gbeƒãɖela Xabakuk. Xabakuk fa konyi le nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔ ŋu

english_verse: Our Lord, how long must I beg for your help before you listen? How long before you save us from all this violence?
translation_verse: O Aƒetɔ, va se ɖe ɣe ka ɣi mado ɣli ayɔ wò be nàkpe ɖe ŋunye, màsee o? Va se ɖe ɣe ka ɣi manɔ ɣli dom le ŋutasesẽ ta, eye màxɔ na ame o?

english_verse: Why do you make me watch such terrible injustice? Why do you allow violence, lawlessness, crime, and cruelty to spread everywhere?
translation_verse: Nu ka ta nèna mele nu gbegblẽ wɔwɔ kple xaxa teƒe kpɔm? Amewo le nuwo gblẽm, le ŋuta sẽm mele kpɔkpɔm. Wole avuwɔwɔ kple dzrewɔwɔ dzi le afi sia afi.

english_verse: Laws cannot be enforced; justice is always the loser; criminals crowd out honest people and twist the laws around. The Lord Answers Habakkuk
translation_verse: Womegaléa fɔ ɖe sea dzi wɔwɔ ŋu o, eye nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ megadzena kura o. Ame vɔ̃ɖi te ame dzɔdzɔewo ɖe to, ale wotrɔ gbo nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ. Aƒetɔ ɖo Xabakuk ƒe nya la ŋu nɛ

english_verse: Look and be amazed at what's happening among the nations! Even if you were told, you would never believe what's taking place now.
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na eƒe dukɔ la be: Miawo mida ŋku ɖi mianɔ dukɔ siwo ƒo xlã mi la kpɔm. Nu siwo miava kpɔ la, ana miaƒe nu aku. Mele nane wɔ ge le mia ŋɔli, eye ne wogblɔe na mi la, miaxɔe ase o.

english_verse: I am sending the Babylonians. They are fierce and cruel— marching across the land, conquering cities and towns.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, manyɔ Kaldeatɔwo woagakpɔ ŋusẽ aɖu dzi. Wonye ame siwo wɔa adã; womedzea kɔ anyi o. Wole zɔzɔm to anyigbawo dzi, eye wole du siwo menye wo tɔ o la xɔm gbɔna.

english_verse: How fearsome and frightening. Their only laws and rules are the ones they make up.
translation_verse: Ŋɔdzi kple vɔvɔ̃ le wo ŋu. Se aɖeke mele wo si o; nu si woɖo la, eyae wowɔna.

english_verse: Their cavalry troops are faster than leopards, more ferocious than wolves hunting at sunset, and swifter than hungry eagles suddenly swooping down.
translation_verse: Woƒe sɔwo ƒua du wu lãkle, eye wowɔa adã wu amegãxi dɔwui le fiẽ me. Woƒe sɔdolawo tso didiƒe ke gbɔna, eye woƒe sɔwo le zi nyem. Wole dzodzom abe hɔ̃ si le adzɔge ʋĩi be yeaƒo nu ene.

english_verse: They are eager to destroy, and they gather captives like handfuls of sand.
translation_verse: Woƒe aʋakɔwo gbɔna kple ŋutasesẽ, eye wozɔ ɖo ta ŋgɔ tẽe, wole ƒu ƒom woƒe aboyomewo abe ke ene.

english_verse: They make fun of rulers and laugh at fortresses, while building dirt mounds so they can capture cities.
translation_verse: Woɖea alɔ me le fiawo ŋu, eye wotsɔa woƒe dziɖulawo wɔa fefenui. Mɔ́ ɖe sia ɖe ɖia kokoe na wo, elabe woƒoa kpo ɖe eŋu xɔnɛ.

english_verse: Then suddenly they disappear like a gust of wind— those sinful people who worship their own strength. Habakkuk Complains Again
translation_verse: Emegbe wohona dzona abe ya ene. Woƒe ŋusẽe nye woƒe mawu. Xabakuk gafa konyi le nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔ ŋu

english_verse: Holy Lord God, mighty rock, you are eternal, and we are safe from death. You are using those Babylonians to judge and punish others.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, ɖe menye wòe nye nye Mawu, Kɔkɔetɔ la, si li tegbee tso gbe aɖe gbe ke oa? Aƒetɔ, míaƒe Xɔnametɔ, wò ŋutɔe tia wo be woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu eye woahe to na amewo.

english_verse: But you can't stand sin or wrong. So don't sit by in silence while they gobble up people who are better than they are.
translation_verse: Ke ale ke wɔ nàdo dzi anɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ kpɔm? Evɔ la, wò ŋkuwo le kɔkɔe; mele be woanɔ nu tovo wɔwɔ kpɔm hafi o. Nu ka ta nàzi kpi, esime ame vɔ̃ɖi le ame si le dzɔdzɔe wui la tsrɔ̃m?

english_verse: The people you put on this earth are like fish or reptiles without a leader.
translation_verse: Èna amegbetɔ zu abe ƒumelã alo nutata, si nu aƒetɔ mele o la ene.

english_verse: Then an enemy comes along and takes them captive with hooks and nets. It makes him so happy
translation_verse: Eɖea wo katã kple ƒè abe tɔmelã ene. Eɖea wo kple ɖɔ hena vaa gotae, eye wòkpɔa dzidzɔ tsoa aseye.

english_verse: that he offers sacrifices to his fishing nets, because they make him rich and provide choice foods.
translation_verse: Esaa vɔ na eƒe ɖɔ, eye wòtɔa dzo lifi na ɖɔ la ƒe aguɖɔe elabe ɖɔawo naa dzidzemee, eye eƒe nuɖuɖu da ami.

english_verse: Will he keep hauling in his nets and destroying nations without showing mercy?
translation_verse: Ðe wòanɔ eƒe ɖɔkaka dzi ɣe sia ɣi anɔ dukɔwo tsrɔ̃m tegbee nublanuimakpɔtɔea?

english_verse: While standing guard on the watchtower, I waited for the Lord's answer, before explaining the reason for my complaint.
translation_verse: Mayi aɖatsi tsitre ɖe xɔta, alala ase nya si Aƒetɔ agblɔ nam be magblɔ, eye mase nye biabia la ƒe ŋuɖoɖo.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me: “I will give you my message in the form of a vision. Write it clearly enough to be read at a glance.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ɖo eŋu nam be: “Ŋlɔ nu si meɖe fia wò la ɖi ɖe nuŋlɔkpe dzi be wòanya xlẽ bɔbɔe kaba.

english_verse: At the time I have decided, my words will come true. You can trust what I say about the future. It may take a long time, but keep on waiting— it will happen!
translation_verse: Ŋlɔe ɖi ko, elabe ɣeyiɣi si wòava eme la meɖo haɖe o. Ke ɣeyiɣia de vɔ, menye beblee o. Evɔ ne etsi megbe la, kpɔ esi nu, elabe ele me va ge godoo; mahe ɖe megbe o.

english_verse: “I, the Lord, refuse to accept anyone who is proud. Only those who live by faith are acceptable to me.” Trouble for Evil People
translation_verse: Gbedeasi lae nye be: Dàdala mewɔa nu dzɔdzɔe o; ke ame dzɔdzɔe ya anɔ agbe to eƒe xɔse me. Baba na nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔlawo

english_verse: Wine is treacherous, and arrogant people are never satisfied. They are no less greedy than death itself— they open their mouths as wide as the world of the dead and swallow everyone.
translation_verse: Wain ɖe wòblea ame. Dàdala manɔ te o. Eƒe ve me keke abe tsiẽƒe ene. Esɔ kple ku; meɖia ƒo o. Eha dukɔwo katã na eɖokui, eye wòli kɔ anyigbadzitɔwo katã ɖe eɖokui gbɔ.”

english_verse: But without warning, those you owe will demand payment. Then you will become a frightened victim.
translation_verse: Ðe wò fetɔwo mado ɖe dziwò esime nèɖe ŋu ɖi oa? Ðe womaʋuʋu wò nànyɔ adzo nyànyanya oa? Woaha wò adzoe.

english_verse: You robbed cities and nations everywhere on earth and murdered their people. Now those who survived will be as cruel to you.
translation_verse: Esi nèha dukɔ geɖewo ta la, ame siwo katã susɔ le dukɔwo me la aha wò. Elabe èkɔ amewo ƒe ʋu ɖi, eye nèsẽ ŋuta le anyigba kple duwo kpakple wo me nɔlawo ŋuti.

english_verse: You're doomed! You made your family rich at the expense of others. You even said to yourself, “I'm above the law.”
translation_verse: Baba na ame si sẽ ŋuta tsɔ kpɔ nui na eƒe ƒometɔwo, eye wòte kpɔ wɔ eƒe nɔƒe dedie be dzɔgbevɔ̃e aɖeke nagadzɔ ɖe ye dzi o!

english_verse: But you will bring shame on your family and ruin to yourself for what you did to others.
translation_verse: Ke wò tameɖoɖo na be wò ƒome ɖu ŋukpe. Esi nètsrɔ̃ dukɔ geɖewo ta la, wò hã atsrɔ̃.

english_verse: The very stones and wood in your home will testify against you.
translation_verse: Xɔtukpewo gɔ̃ hã ado ɣli le gli me ɖe tawò, eye xɔgbatiwo axɔ ɖe edzi na wo.

english_verse: You're doomed! You built a city on crime and violence.
translation_verse: Baba na ame si tso du to amewuwu me, eye wòɖo egɔme anyi to nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ me!

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful sends up in flames what nations and people work so hard to gain.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, amewo dzea agbagba wɔa dɔ, ke dzo koe fiãnɛ, eye dukɔwo kua kutri dzodzro. Ðe menye Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la gbɔe esia tso oa?

english_verse: Just as water fills the sea, the land will be filled with people who know and honor the Lord.
translation_verse: Ke sidzedze Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe axɔ anyigba dzi keŋ abe ale si tsi yɔ atsiaƒu ene.

english_verse: You're doomed! You get your friends drunk, just to see them naked.
translation_verse: Baba na ame si na ehavi noa nu le eƒe dɔmedzoekplu nu be wòamu ne wòakpɔ eƒe ŋukpeƒe.

english_verse: Now you will be disgraced instead of praised. The Lord will make you drunk, and when others see you naked, you will lose their respect.
translation_verse: Ðe bubu teƒe la miaɖu ŋukpe. Wò hã ano nu amu, ahaɖe ama ɖokuiwò. Aƒetɔ ƒe nuɖusi akpe dɔmedzoekplu la na wò hã, eye wò bubu atrɔ zu ŋukpe.

english_verse: You destroyed trees and animals on Mount Lebanon; you were ruthless to towns and people everywhere. Now you will be terrorized. Idolatry Is Foolish
translation_verse: Ŋuta si wosẽ le Lebanon ŋu la, atrɔ va dziwò. Eƒe lãawo tsɔtsrɔ̃ ado vɔvɔ̃ na mi. Nu siawo le dzɔdzɔ ge elabe miewu ame, eye miesẽ ŋuta le anyigba kple duwo kpakple wo me nɔlawo ŋuti.

english_verse: What is an idol worth? It's merely a false god. Why trust a speechless image made from wood or metal by human hands?
translation_verse: Viɖe kae le aklama kpakpɛ ŋu na ekpala alo le legba si wòkɔ̀ la ŋu? Alakpanufiala ko wònye. Ewɔla le dzi ɖom ɖe nu si eya ŋutɔ wɔ la ŋu, evɔ la, nu maƒonu ko wònye.

english_verse: What can you learn from idols covered with silver or gold? They can't even breathe. Pity anyone who says to an idol of wood or stone, “Get up and do something!”
translation_verse: Baba na ame si gblɔ na ati be: “Nyɔ!” alo na kpe maƒonu be: “Fɔ!” Kpɔ ɖa, ele nane ɖe ge afia. Togbɔ be wofa sika kple klosalo ɖe eŋu kpe ɖo hã la, gbɔgbɔ mele eme kura o.
