english_verse: Let all the world be silent— the Lord is present in his holy temple.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ le eƒe xɔ kɔkɔe me; anyigba blibo la nezi ɖoɖoe le eŋkume. eŋkume.

english_verse: I know your reputation, Lord, and I am amazed at what you have done. Please turn from your anger and be merciful; do for us what you did for our ancestors.
translation_verse: O Aƒetɔ, esi mese nu si nèwɔ la, vɔvɔ̃ ɖom! Nu siwo nèwɔna tsã la, gawɔ wo le mía ŋɔli hã. Ne èdo dɔmedzoe hã, ɖo ŋui nàkpɔ nublanui na wò amewo.

english_verse: You are the same Holy God who came from Teman and Paran to help us. The brightness of your glory covered the heavens, and your praises were heard everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Mawu tso Teman gbɔna. Kɔkɔetɔ la ɖi tso Paran-towo dzi gbɔna. Eƒe ŋutikɔkɔe xɔ dziƒo katã kpe ɖo; wole ekafum le afi sia afi le anyigba dzi.

english_verse: Your glory shone like the sun, and light flashed from your hands, hiding your mighty power.
translation_verse: Eƒe keklẽ le abe kekeli ene, eye wòle dodom tso eƒe asi me abe ɣetotoe ene; eƒe ŋusẽ bè ɖe afi ma.

english_verse: Dreadful diseases and plagues marched in front and followed behind.
translation_verse: Dɔ vɔ̃ dze eŋgɔ, eye dzikedzo kplɔe ɖo.

english_verse: When you stopped, the earth shook; when you stared, nations trembled; when you walked along your ancient paths, eternal mountains and hills crumbled and collapsed.
translation_verse: Etɔ, eye anyigba ʋuʋu. Eda ŋku ɖi, kpɔ nu; dzidzi ƒo dukɔwo. To siwo li tso blema ke la fe kplà; togbɛ siwo li tso gbe aɖe gbe ke hã ŋe dze eme ʋlì. Evɔ wònye woawo dzie wòzɔna le blema.

english_verse: The tents of desert tribes in Cushan and Midian were ripped apart.
translation_verse: Kusatɔwo ɖo xaxa me mekpɔ, eye Midiantɔwo le dzodzom nyànyanya.

english_verse: Our Lord, were you angry with the monsters of the deep? You attacked in your chariot and wiped them out.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, tɔsisiwo ŋue nèdo dziku ɖoa? Woawo ŋue nèdo dɔmedzoe ɖo loo, alo atsiaƒu ŋue dzi le kuwòm ɖo, be nèdo wò sɔwo eye nèɖo wò tasiaɖamwo yi ɖaɖu dzia?

english_verse: Your arrows were ready and obeyed your commands. You split the earth apart with rivers and streams;
translation_verse: Èdzra wò dati ɖo be yeada, eye nètsɔ aŋutrɔ de eme. Èna tɔsisiwo ɖe mɔ to anyigba me.

english_verse: mountains trembled at the sight of you; rain poured from the clouds; ocean waves roared and rose.
translation_verse: Esi towo kpɔ wò la, wodzo nyànyanya; tɔwo ɖɔ gbagba. Anyigba gɔme tsiwo ɖe gbe, eye woƒe tsotsoewo kɔ yi dzi boo.

english_verse: The sun and moon stood still, while your arrows and spears flashed like lightning.
translation_verse: Esi wò aŋutrɔwo nye kekeli le yiyim, eye wò akplɔwo nye keklẽ le dzo kem la, ɣe kple ɣleti tɔ ɖe wo teƒewo.

english_verse: In your furious anger, you trampled on nations
translation_verse: Èzɔ to anyigba dzi kple dziku, eye nèfanya dukɔwo le dɔmedzoe me.

english_verse: to rescue your people and save your chosen one. You crushed a nation's ruler and stripped his evil kingdom of its power.
translation_verse: Ètso be yeaxɔ wò dukɔ ɖe agbe; be yeaxɔ wò amesiamina la ɖe agbe. Èwu ame vɔ̃ɖiwo kplɔla, eye nètsrɔ̃ eyomedzelawo keŋ.

english_verse: His troops had come like a storm, hoping to scatter us and glad to gobble us up. To them we were refugees in hiding— but you smashed their heads with their own weapons.
translation_verse: Ènyrɔ wò aŋutrɔ ɖe woƒe aʋakplɔla, si va abe yaƒoƒo sesẽ ene be yeaka mí ahlẽ la ƒe tame. Wole dzidzɔɣli dom, abe ame siwo tea ame dahe ɖe to le adzame ene.

english_verse: Then your chariots churned the waters of the sea. Habakkuk's Response to God's Message
translation_verse: Ètsɔ wò sɔwo to atsiaƒu kple tɔ gã dzeagbowo dzi.

english_verse: When I heard this message, I felt weak from fear, and my lips quivered. My bones seemed to melt, and I stumbled around. But I will patiently wait. Someday those vicious enemies will be struck by disaster. Trust in a Time of Trouble
translation_verse: Mesee, lulu; nye nuyiwo le ƒoƒom. Ðuɖui ɖo nye ƒuwo me. Esi metsi tsitre la, nye afɔwo nɔ ƒoƒom kpakpakpa le tenye. Manɔ anyi kpoo anɔ lalam be makpɔ ame siwo ɖe to ɖe mí la ƒe xaxagbe.

english_verse: Fig trees may no longer bloom, or vineyards produce grapes; olive trees may be fruitless, and harvest time a failure; sheep pens may be empty, and cattle stalls vacant—
translation_verse: Togbɔ be gbotiwo megatse o, eye kutsetse mele wainka aɖeke ŋu o; togbɔ be amiti meganaa ami o, eye nu megawɔna le agblewo me o, togbɔ be alẽwo tsrɔ̃ le lãkpo me, eye nyi megale nyikpo aɖeke me o hã la,

english_verse: but I will still celebrate because the Lord God is my Savior.
translation_verse: nye ya makpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu eye matso aseye ɖe Mawu, nye Xɔnametɔ ŋuti.

english_verse: The Lord gives me strength. He makes my feet as sure as those of a deer, and he helps me stand on the mountains. To the music director: Use stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ Mawu lae nye nye ŋusẽ. Ena ŋusẽ ɖo nye afɔ ŋu abe zi tɔ ene, eye wòna mezɔa nye teƒe kɔkɔwo. Na hadzihakplɔla: woadzi kple kasaŋkuwo.

english_verse: I am Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the grandson of Gedaliah, the great-grandson of Amariah, and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah. When Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah, the Lord gave me this message. Judgment on Judah
translation_verse: Gbedeasi sia nye nya si Aƒetɔ gblɔ to Zefanya dzi, esime Yosiya, Amon vi, nye fia le Yuda-nyigba dzi. Zefanya nye Kusi, Gadalya, Amarya kple fia Xizkiya ƒe dzidzimevi. Aƒetɔ ƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃gbe la

english_verse: I, the Lord, now promise to destroy everything on this earth—
translation_verse: “Mele nu sia nu tsrɔ̃ ge ɖa keŋkeŋ le anyigba dzi.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: people and animals, birds and fish. Everyone who is evil will crash to the ground, and I will wipe out the entire human race.
translation_verse: “Matsrɔ̃ amegbetɔ, lã, xe kple ƒumelãwo katã. Matsrɔ̃ ame vɔ̃ɖiwo keŋ. Maɖe amegbetɔƒomea ɖa le anyigba dzi.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: I will reach out to punish Judah and Jerusalem— nothing will remain of the god Baal; nothing will be remembered of his pagan priests.
translation_verse: “Mahe to na Yuda kple Yerusalemnɔlawo katã. Maɖe Baal ƒe mamlɛa kple nunɔla siwo subɔa trɔ̃ la ƒe ŋkɔ ɖa le teƒe sia.

english_verse: Not a trace will be found of those who worship stars from their rooftops, or bow down to the god Milcom, while claiming loyalty to me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Matsrɔ̃ ame sia ame si yia xɔta ɖasubɔa ɣe, ɣleti kple ɣletiviwo la, ame siwo subɔa Aƒetɔ, eye ne woka atam nam vɔ la, wogatsɔa mawu Milkom ŋkɔ nɔa atam kamee la hã.

english_verse: Nothing will remain of anyone who has turned away and rejected me.
translation_verse: Matsrɔ̃ ame siwo katã trɔ le Aƒetɔ yome kple ame siwo media Aƒetɔ alo biaa eta sena o.”

english_verse: Be silent! I am the Lord God, and the time is near. I am preparing to sacrifice my people and to invite my guests.
translation_verse: Mizi ɖoɖoe le Aƒetɔ Mawu ŋkume! Elabe Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋkeke la tu aƒe. Aƒetɔ dzra vɔsa ɖo, eye wòkɔ ame siwo wòkpe la ŋu.

english_verse: On that day I will punish national leaders and sons of the king, along with all who follow foreign customs.
translation_verse: Le Aƒetɔ ƒe vɔsagbe la, “Mahe to na amegãwo kple fiaviŋutsuwo kpakple ame siwo katã doa awu abe dukɔ bubu me tɔwo ene.

english_verse: I, the Lord, promise that on that day noisy crying will be heard from Fish Gate, New Town, and Upper Hills.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Gbe ma gbe asiƒunu aɖi le Tɔmelãgbo nu le Yerusalem-du me. Miase avifafa le dua ƒe To Evelia, eye nu gbagbã ƒe ɖiɖi sesĩe atso togbɛwo dzi.

english_verse: Everyone in Lower Hollow will mourn loudly, because merchants and money changers will be wiped out.
translation_verse: Mi Tomenɔlawo, mifa avi, elabe asitsalawo katã megali o, wotsrɔ̃ ame siwo katã daa klosalo.

english_verse: I'll search Jerusalem with lamps and punish those people who sit there unworried while thinking, “The Lord won't do anything, good or bad.”
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, matsɔ akaɖi atsa le Yerusalem-dua me. Mahe to na ame siwo katã ƒe dzi dze eme, woɖe dzi ɖi, eye wogblɔna na wo ɖokui be: ‘Aƒetɔ mele nyui alo vɔ̃ wɔ ge o.’

english_verse: Their possessions will be taken, their homes left in ruins. They won't get to live in the houses they build, or drink wine from the grapes in their own vineyards. A Terrible Day
translation_verse: Woaha woƒe kesinɔnuwo, eye woagbã woƒe aƒewo. Togbɔ be wotu xɔwo hã la, womanɔ wo me o. Togbɔ be wode waingblewo hã la, womano wain tso wo me o.”

english_verse: The great day of the Lord is coming soon, very soon. On that terrible day, fearsome shouts of warriors will be heard everywhere.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋkeke gã la tu aƒe; egogo vɔ, eye wòle du dzi sesĩe gbɔna. Aƒetɔ ƒe ŋkeke la le vevem helihelĩ, ŋutsu kalẽtɔwo ado aʋaɣli bobobo gbe ma gbe.

english_verse: It will be a time of anger— of trouble and torment, of disaster and destruction, of darkness and despair, of storm clouds and shadows,
translation_verse: Ŋkekea anye dɔmedzoegbe, fukpegbe kple xaxagbe. Anye aƒegbãgbe kple nugblẽgbe; anye blukɔdogbe kple vivitidogbe; anye alilikpodogbe kple tsizidogbe;

english_verse: of trumpet calls and battle cries against fortified cities and mighty fortresses.
translation_verse: anye aʋayikpẽɖigbe kple aʋaɣlidogbe ɖe du sesẽwo kple gbetakpɔxɔ kɔkɔwo ŋu.

english_verse: The Lord warns everyone who has sinned against him, “I'll strike you blind! Then your blood and your insides will gush out like vomit.
translation_verse: Mana amegbetɔwo naxaxa, ale be woazɔ abe ŋkunɔwo ene, le vɔ̃ si wowɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋuti ta. Woakɔ woƒe ʋu ɖi abe tsi ene, eye woatsɔ woƒe ŋutilã aƒu gbe abe mí ene.

english_verse: Not even your silver or gold can save you on that day when I, the Lord, am angry. My anger will flare up like a furious fire scorching the earth and everyone on it.”
translation_verse: Woƒe klosalo kple sika mate ŋu aɖe wo le Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔmedzoeŋkeke la dzi o. Le ŋkeke ma dzi la, eƒe ŋuʋaʋã si nu sẽ abe dzo ene afiã xexea me katã. Ẽ, elabe atsrɔ̃ anyigbadzinɔlawo katã zi ɖeka kpata, eye woavɔ ɖa keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: before it's too late. The Lord has set a time when his fierce anger will strike like a storm and sweep you away.
translation_verse: hafi woalɔ mi ɖe nu abe nutsro ene, hafi Aƒetɔ ƒe dziku helihelĩ la nava mia dzi, hafi Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔmedzoedogbe nava mia dzi.

english_verse: If you humbly obey the Lord, then come and worship him. If you do right and are humble, perhaps you will be safe on that day when the Lord turns loose his anger. Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: Midi Aƒetɔ, mi ame siwo katã bɔbɔa mia ɖokui le anyigba dzi, eye miewɔa eƒe sewo dzi la. Midi nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ, eye midi ɖokuibɔbɔ. Ðewohĩ woaɣla mi le Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔmedzoedogbe. Baba na dukɔ siwo ƒo xlã Israel

english_verse: Gaza and Ashkelon will be deserted and left in ruins. Ashdod will be emptied in broad daylight, and Ekron uprooted.
translation_verse: Ame aɖeke masusɔ ɖe Gaza-du me o, eye Askalon azu aƒedo. Woanyà Asdod ŋdɔ kutsu dzatsɛ, eye woanyà Ekrontɔwo hã woadzo.

english_verse: To you people of Philistia who live along the coast, the Lord has this to say: “I am now your enemy, and I'll wipe you out!”
translation_verse: Baba na mi ƒutanɔlawo, mi Kreta-dukɔmetɔwo! Aƒetɔ ƒe nya tsi tre ɖe mia ŋu. Ao, Kanaan, Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba, matsrɔ̃ mi va se ɖe esime ame aɖeke masusɔ o.

english_verse: Your seacoast will be changed into pastureland and sheep pens.
translation_verse: Ao, ƒutanyigba, ele gbeɖuƒewo zu ge, azu lãnyiƒewo na alẽkplɔlawo kple lãkpɔwo na alẽhawo.

english_verse: The Lord God hasn't forgotten those survivors in Judah, and he will help them— his people will take your land to use for pasture. And when evening comes, they will rest in houses at Ashkelon. Judgment on Moab and Ammon *
translation_verse: Ame siwo susɔ le Yuda-nyigba dzi la axɔ ƒutanyigba la. Woanyi woƒe alẽhawo le afi ma, eye le fiẽ me la, woatsi aƒe siwo le Askalon me adɔ. Elabe Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la, aɖo ŋku wo dzi, eye wòagbugbɔ woƒe nunyonamewo aɖo te.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, said: I've heard Moab and Ammon insult my people and threaten their nation.
translation_verse: “Mese ale si Moabtɔwo le alɔ me ɖem, eye Amonviwo le nya vlowo gblɔm ɖe nye dukɔ ŋu, eye wole kakam be yewole eƒe anyigba xɔ ge.

english_verse: And so, I swear by my very life that Moab and Ammon will end up like Sodom and Gomorrah— covered with thornbushes and salt pits forever. Then my people who survive will take their land.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, Israel ƒe Mawu la, be: “Zi ale si mele agbe la, Moab azu abe Sodom ene, eye Amonviwo abe Gomora ene; anyigba si ayɔ fũu kple ŋuve, dzeƒee kple gbegbe tegbee. Ame siwo susɔ le nye dukɔ me la aha wo, eye ame siwo tsi agbe le nye dukɔ me la, woaxɔ woƒe anyigba.”

english_verse: This is how Moab and Ammon will at last be repaid for their pride— and for sneering at the nation that belongs to me, the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Esia anye woƒe gome le woƒe dàda ta. Elabe woɖe alɔ me, eye woka ɖe Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la ƒe dukɔ ŋu.

english_verse: I will fiercely attack. Then every god on this earth will shrink to nothing, and everyone of every nation will bow down to me, right where they are. Judgment on Ethiopia
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ado ŋɔdzi na wo. Ẽ, ana dɔ nawu anyigba dzi legbawo katã, ekem dukɔwo katã ade ta agu nɛ, ɖe sia ɖe le enɔƒe, le dukɔwo ƒe anyigbawo katã dzi.

english_verse: People of Ethiopia, the sword of the Lord will slaughter you! Judgment on Assyria
translation_verse: Mi Etiopiatɔwo hã, nye yi awu mi.

english_verse: The Lord will reach to the north to crush Assyria and overthrow Nineveh.
translation_verse: Ado asi ɖe dzigbeme atsrɔ̃ Asiria ɖa. Ana Ninive-du nazu gbegbe, aƒu kplakplakpla abe kegbegbe ene.

english_verse: Herds of wild animals will live in its rubble; all kinds of desert owls will perch on its stones and hoot in the windows. Noisy ravens will be heard inside its buildings, stripped bare of cedar.
translation_verse: Anye teƒe si lãhawo kple gbemelã vovovowo ava tsyɔ akɔ anyi ɖo. Akaga kple hlɔ̃madewo anɔ woƒe glikpowo me. Adzexewo anɔ xɔxlɔ̃m le fesre gbagbãwo nu. Akpaviawo anɔ xɔxlɔ̃m le xɔmɔnuwo elabe sederʋuƒowo atsi go.

english_verse: This is the glorious city that felt secure and said, “I am the only one!” Now it's merely ruins, a home for wild animals. Every passerby simply sneers and makes vulgar signs.
translation_verse: Esiae nye du si wodo ɖe dzi, eye wòli bɔkɔɔ. Egblɔna le eɖokui me be: “Nye koe, ame aɖeke megali o.” Ke azɔ la, eva zu gbegbe, gbemelãwo ƒe nɔƒe! Ame sia ame si ato eŋu la, ado tsiã, aʋuʋu asi.

english_verse: Too bad for that disgusting, corrupt, and lawless city!
translation_verse: Baba na Yerusalem, du ƒoɖi, tosẽla, ŋutasẽla.

english_verse: Forever rebellious and rejecting correction, Jerusalem refuses to trust or obey the Lord God.
translation_verse: Meɖoa to Aƒetɔ o, eye medina be woahe to na ye o. Meɖoa dzi ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu alo tena ɖe eƒe Mawu ŋu o.

english_verse: Its officials are roaring lions, its judges are wolves; in the evening they attack, by morning nothing is left.
translation_verse: Eƒe amegãwo le abe dzata, siwo le gbe ɖem la ene; eƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ya le abe fiẽ amegãxi siwo womesusɔa naneke ɖi ŋu kena o la ene.

english_verse: Jerusalem's prophets are proud and not to be trusted. The priests have disgraced the place of worship and abused God's Law.
translation_verse: Eƒe gbeƒãɖelawo nye movitɔwo, womate ŋu axɔ wo dzi ase o. Eƒe nunɔlawo gblẽa kɔ ɖo na nu kɔkɔe la, eye wotrɔa se la.

english_verse: All who do evil are shameless, but the Lord does right and is always fair. With the dawn of each day, God brings about justice.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ si le eme la le dzɔdzɔe, mewɔa nu gbegblẽ aɖeke o. Ŋdi sia ŋdi la, eɖea eƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ fiana, medana ƒu le fɔŋli aɖeke o. Ke nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔla, menya ŋukpe aɖeke o.

english_verse: The Lord wiped out nations and left fortresses crumbling in the dirt. Their streets and towns were reduced to ruins and emptied of people.
translation_verse: “Metsrɔ̃ dukɔwo; eye woƒe xɔ sesẽ kɔkɔtɔwo katã zu glikpo ɖi dzoɣlii. Woƒe ablɔwo tsi ƒuƒlu, ame megatoa wo me yina o. Duawo gbã zu aƒedo, eye ame vɔ le wo me.

english_verse: God felt certain that Jerusalem would learn to respect and obey him. Then he would hold back from punishing the city and not wipe it out. But everyone there was eager to start sinning again. Nations Will Turn to the Lord
translation_verse: Megblɔ be: ‘Mebu be woavɔ̃m, eye woalɔ̃ axɔ hehe si mana wo la, ale be womaŋlɔ nu si wosrɔ̃ tso gbɔnye la be o.’ Ke wogbe be yewomatrɔ nɔnɔme o; wogale nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ dzi.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Just wait for the day when I accuse you nations. I have decided on a day, when I will bring together every nation and kingdom and punish them all in my fiery anger. I will become furious and destroy the earth.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Milala va se ɖe gbe si gbe matso abe ɖasefo ene ɖe dukɔwo ŋu. Elabe meɖoe be maƒo dukɔwo kple fiaɖuƒewo nu ƒu ale be matrɔ nye dziku akɔ ɖe wo dzi, nye dziku helihelĩ la katã. Elabe le nye dɔmedzoe ƒe ŋuʋaʋã ƒe dzo la me la, anyigba blibo la katã afiã.”

english_verse: I will purify each language and make those languages acceptable for praising me. Then, with hearts united, everyone will serve only me, the Lord.
translation_verse: “Ẽ, ɣe ma ɣi la, matrɔ dukɔwo ƒe nuƒo wòadza, be wo katã nayɔ Aƒetɔ ŋkɔ, eye woasubɔe kple nusɔsɔ.

english_verse: From across the rivers of Ethiopia, my scattered people, my true worshipers, will bring offerings to me.
translation_verse: Nye ame siwo ka hlẽ yi keke Nubia-tɔsisiwo godo ke hã ƒe viwo agbɔ va, eye woatsɔ vɔsanuwo vɛ nam.”

english_verse: When that time comes, you won't rebel against me and be put to shame. I'll do away with those who are proud and arrogant. Never will any of them strut around on my holy mountain.
translation_verse: “Gbe ma gbe la, womado ŋukpe mi le nu siwo miewɔ tsɔ dze aglãe ɖe ŋunye la ta o. Elabe ɣe ma ɣi la, maɖe miaƒe dàdala ɖokuidoɖedzilawo ɖa le mia dome, eye miagado mia ɖokui ɖe dzi, le nye to kɔkɔe la dzi o.

english_verse: But I, the Lord, won't destroy any of your people who are truly humble and turn to me for safety.
translation_verse: Elabe magblẽ ɖokuibɔbɔlawo kple ame siwo mewɔa wo ɖokui gã o la, ɖe mia dome. Woadi sitsoƒe le Aƒetɔ me.

english_verse: The people of Israel who survive will live right and refuse to tell lies. They will eat and rest with nothing to fear. A Song of Celebration
translation_verse: Israelvi siwo asusɔ ɖi la, mawɔ nu gbegblẽ o; womaka aʋatso loo, alo awɔ alakpanu o. Agbenɔnɔ adze edzi na wo. Woaɖe dzi ɖi bɔkɔɔ, eye ame aɖeke mado vɔvɔ̃ na wo gbeɖe o.” Dzidzɔha

english_verse: Everyone in Jerusalem and Judah, celebrate and shout with all your heart!
translation_verse: Zion vinyɔnu, dzi dzidzɔha; O Israel, do ɣli! Yerusalem-nyɔnuvi, kpɔ dzidzɔ, na wò dzi navu gblotoo!

english_verse: Zion, your punishment is over. The Lord has forced your enemies to turn and retreat. Your Lord is King of Israel and stands at your side; you don't have to worry about any more troubles.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ he to na wò vɔ, eye wòkplɔ wò futɔwo dzoe. Aƒetɔ, Israel Fia la, li kpli mi azɔ; miagavɔ̃ nuvɔ̃ɖi aɖeke azɔ o.

english_verse: Jerusalem, the time is coming, when it will be said to you: “Don't be discouraged or grow weak from fear!
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe la, woagblɔ na Yerusalem be: “Zion-du, mègavɔ̃ o! Abɔ megaku wò o!

english_verse: The Lord your God wins victory after victory and is always with you. He celebrates and sings because of you, and he will refresh your life with his love.” The Lord's Promise to His People
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, wò Mawu la le dowòme; kalẽtɔ si naa dziɖuɖu wònye. Aƒetɔ akpɔ dzidzɔ le ŋuwò ŋutɔ, eye wòatsɔ lɔlɔ̃ agbɔ agbe wò. Adzi dzidzɔhawo, atso aseye ɖe ŋuwò,

english_verse: The Lord has promised: Your sorrow has ended, and you can celebrate.
translation_verse: abe ŋkekenyui ɖugbe ene. Maɖe dzɔgbevɔ̃e ɖa le mia dzi ale be ŋu makpe mi o.

english_verse: I will punish those who mistreat you. I will bring together the lame and the outcasts, then they will be praised, instead of despised, in every country on earth.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, ɣe ma ɣi la, matu nu kple ame siwo katã te mi ɖe anyi la, maxɔ na tekunɔwo, maƒo ame siwo woɖe le ame dome la nu ƒu. Matrɔ woƒe ŋukpe la wòazu kafukafu, eye wo ŋkɔ ade dzi le anyigba blibo la dzi.

english_verse: I will lead you home, and with your own eyes you will see me bless you with all you once owned. Then you will be famous everywhere on this earth. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, makplɔ mi agbɔ va aƒee. Ame siwo katã ka hlẽ la, maƒo wo nu ƒu. Ẽ, mana mia ŋkɔ nanyɔ, eye woakafu mi le anyigba dzi dukɔwo katã dome, ne megbugbɔ miaƒe nunyonamewo ɖo te le mia ŋkume.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: On the first day of the sixth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak his message to the governor of Judah and to the high priest. So Haggai told Governor Zerubbabel and High Priest Joshua
translation_verse: Le fia Dario ƒe dziɖuɣi ƒe ƒè evelia me, le ɣleti adelia ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la, Aƒetɔ ƒo nu to eƒe gbeƒãɖela Xagai dzi na Zerubabel Sealtiel vi, Yuda-nyigba nunɔla kple nunɔlagã Yosua, Yehozadak vi.

english_verse: You harvest less than you plant, you never have enough to eat or drink, your clothes don't keep you warm, and your wages are stored in bags full of holes.
translation_verse: Mieƒã nu geɖe, gake nu ʋɛ aɖe ko mieŋe; mieɖu nu gake meɖi ƒo na mi o; mieno nu gake meɖi kɔ na mi o; mieta avɔ gake mede dzo lã me na ame aɖeke o; ame si xɔa fetu la, xɔnɛ kɔna ɖe kotoku ŋɔŋɔ me.’ ”

english_verse: But first, go to the hills and get wood for my temple, so I can take pride in it and be worshiped there.
translation_verse: Miyi ɖe towo dzi ne miatsɔ atiwo vɛ ava tu xɔ lae, ne wòadze ŋunye, eye mado kple nye bubu. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: You expected much, but received only a little. And when you brought it home, I made that little disappear. Why have I done this? It's because you hurry off to build your own houses, while my temple is still in ruins.
translation_verse: Miekpɔ mɔ na nu geɖe, kpɔ ɖa, nu sue aɖe koe su mia si. Esi mietsɔe va aƒee la, meɖo ƒuƒu ɖee. Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la bia be nu ka tae? Esi nye xɔ zu glikpo li, gake mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe tsi dzi ɖe etɔ ya ŋu la tae.

english_verse: That's also why the dew doesn't fall and your harvest fails.
translation_verse: Eya tae dziƒowo te zãmu mi, eye anyigba te nuwɔwɔ mi ɖo.

english_verse: And so, at my command everything will become barren—your farmland and pastures, your vineyards and olive trees, your animals and you yourselves. All your hard work will be for nothing.
translation_verse: Nyee na ku le ɖiɖim vevie ɖe anyigba kple towo ŋu, ɖe bli, wain yeye kple ami ŋu, ɖe nu siwo katã tsoa anyigba me ŋu, ɖe amegbetɔwo kple lãwo siaa ŋu, ɖe dɔ siwo katã wotsɔa asi wɔnɛ ko la ŋu.” Dukɔ la wɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe dzi

english_verse: Zerubbabel and Joshua, together with the others who had returned from exile in Babylonia, obeyed the Lord's message spoken by his prophet Haggai, and they started showing proper respect for the Lord.
translation_verse: Tete Zerubabel, Sealtiel vi kple nunɔlagã Yosua, Yehozadak vi kpakple dukɔ la ƒe ame siwo susɔ la, ɖo to Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la ƒe gbe kple Xagai, gbeƒãɖela la ƒe nyawo abe ale si Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la dɔe ene, eye dukɔ la vɔ̃ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume.

english_verse: Haggai then told them that the Lord had promised to be with them.
translation_verse: Azɔ la Xagai, Aƒetɔ ƒe amedɔdɔ la gblɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedeasi la na dukɔ la be: “Meli kpli mi.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: And the work began on the twenty-fourth day of that same month.
translation_verse: le ɣleti adelia ƒe ŋkeke bla eve vɔ enea gbe.

english_verse: On the twenty-first day of the next month, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak this message to Governor Zerubbabel, High Priest Joshua, and everyone else:
translation_verse: “Azɔ gblɔ na Zerubabel, Sealtiel vi, Yuda-nyigba la nunɔla kple nunɔlagã Yosua, Yehozadak vi kpakple dukɔa ƒe ame siwo katã susɔ la be:

english_verse: Does anyone remember how glorious this temple used to be? Now it looks like nothing.
translation_verse: ‘Ame kae susɔ le mia dome kpɔ xɔ sia ƒe atsyɔ̃ tsãtɔ la? Ale ke miekpɔe fifia? Ɖe medze numaɖinui le mia ŋkume oa?

english_verse: just as I promised your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt. Don't worry. My Spirit is right here with you.
translation_verse: abe ale si medo ŋugbee na mi esi mieʋu tso Egipte la ene. Nye Gbɔgbɔ le mia dome, migavɔ̃ o.’

english_verse: Soon I will again shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: ‘Esusɔ vie ko magaʋuʋu dziƒowo, anyigba, atsiaƒu kple anyigba ƒuƒui.

english_verse: I will shake the nations, and their treasures will be brought here. Then the brightness of my glory will fill this temple.
translation_verse: Maʋuʋu dukɔwo katã, ale be woatsɔ woƒe kesinɔnuwo ava afii, eye mana xɔ sia ayɔ taŋ kple nu xɔasiwo. Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe.

english_verse: All silver and gold belong to me,
translation_verse: Klosalo la, tɔnyee; sika hã tɔnyee. Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe.

english_verse: and I promise that this new temple will be more glorious than the first one. I will also bless this city with peace. The Past and the Future
translation_verse: Xɔ megbetɔ sia ƒe atsyɔ̃ anyakpɔ wu tsãtɔ, Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe. Mana nu nadze edzi na mi le teƒe sia.’ ” Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe. Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela la ƒo nu kple nunɔlawo

english_verse: to ask the priests for their opinion on the following matters:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Bia nunɔlawo ne woatso nya me le nya sia ŋu:

english_verse: Suppose meat ready to be sacrificed to God is being carried in the folds of someone's clothing, and the clothing rubs against some bread or stew or wine or olive oil or any other food. Would those foods that were touched then become acceptable for sacrifice? “Of course not,” the priests answered.
translation_verse: ‘Ne ame aɖe lɔ lã si ŋu kɔ la ɖe avɔ nu, eye avɔ la ka abolo, nuɖaɖa, wain, ami alo nuɖuɖu bubu aɖe ŋu la, ɖe nua ŋu kɔa?’ ” Nunɔlawo ɖo eŋu be: “Kpao.”

english_verse: Then Haggai said, “Suppose someone has touched a dead body and is considered unacceptable to worship God. If that person touches these foods, would they become unclean?” “Of course they would,” the priests answered.
translation_verse: Tete Xagai bia be: “Ekema ne ame aɖe ka asi ame kuku ŋu, eye amea ŋu mekɔ o, emegbe wòka asi nu siawo dometɔ aɖe ŋu la, ɖe nua hã zu nu makɔmakɔa?” Nunɔlawo ɖo eŋu be: “Ẽ, ezu nu makɔmakɔ.”

english_verse: So the Lord told Haggai to say: That's how it is with this entire nation. Everything you do and every sacrifice you offer is unacceptable to me.
translation_verse: Tete Xagai gblɔ be: “Alea tututue wòle na dukɔ sia me tɔwo kple dukɔ sia le ŋkunye me. Nenema ke nu sia nu si wotsɔ asi wɔe kple nu sia nu si wotsɔ sa vɔe le afi ma la ŋu mekɔ o.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe. Aƒetɔ do ŋugbe be yeayra dukɔ la

english_verse: But from now on, things will get better. Before you started laying the foundation for the temple,
translation_verse: “Taflatsɛ, mibu nya siwo ava va eme tso egbe sia heyi la ŋuti kpɔ. Hafi woatsɔ kpe aɖo kpe dzi le Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔa tutu me la,

english_verse: That same day the Lord spoke to Haggai again and said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gaƒo nu to Xagai dzi zi evelia le ɣletia ƒe ŋkeke bla eve vɔ enea gbe be:

english_verse: I made all of your hard work useless by sending mildew, mold, and hail—but you still did not return to me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Mehe to na mia kple miaƒe agbagbadzedzewo metsonuwo katã. Miaƒe bli hlɔ̃ hedze heteku, tsikpewo dza; gake mietrɔ va gbɔnye o. Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Today you have completed the foundation for my temple, so listen to what your future will be like.
translation_verse: Mibu eŋu tso egbe, ɣleti asiekelia ƒe ŋkeke bla eve vɔ enelia sia gbe, heyi. Mibu eŋu tso gbe si gbe woɖo Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔ la gɔme anyi.

english_verse: Although you have not yet harvested any grain, grapes, figs, pomegranates, or olives, I will richly bless you in the days ahead. God's Promise to Zerubbabel
translation_verse: Ɖe bli gale ava mea? Ɖe kutsetse aɖeke mele wainka, gboti, yevuboɖati kple amiti dzi oa? Tso egbe heyi la, mayra mi.” Aƒetɔ do ŋugbe na Zerubabel

english_verse: Tell Governor Zerubbabel of Judah that I am going to shake the heavens and the earth
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na Zerubabel, Yuda-nyigba la nunɔla la be, mele dziƒo kple anyigba ʋuʋu ge,

english_verse: and wipe out kings and their kingdoms. I will overturn war chariots, and then cavalry troops will start slaughtering each other.
translation_verse: eye mamu fiaɖuƒewo ƒe fiazikpuiwo aƒu anyi. Mele ŋusẽ si le dukɔwo ƒe fiaɖuƒewo si la tsrɔ̃ ge, eye matu asi tasiaɖamwo kple wo kulawo aƒu anyi; sɔwo kple wo dolawo adze anyi, eye ame sia ame atsi ehavi ƒe yi nu.

english_verse: But tell my servant Zerubbabel that I, the Lord All-Powerful, have chosen him, and he will rule in my name.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be, gbe ma gbe la, matsɔ wò, Zerubabel, nye dɔla, Sealtiel vi, awɔ abe ŋkɔsigɛ ene. Elabe wòe metia.” Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe.

english_verse: I am the prophet Zechariah, the son of Berechiah and the grandson of Iddo. In the eighth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told me to say:
translation_verse: Le Dario ƒe ƒè evelia me, le ɣleti enyilia dzi la, Aƒetɔ de gbe asi na gbeƒãɖela Zaxarya Berexya vi, ame si nye Ido ƒe tɔgbuiyɔvi be:

english_verse: Israel, I, the Lord All-Powerful, was very angry with your ancestors. But if you people will return to me, I will turn and help you.
translation_verse: Eya ta gblɔ na wo be, Aƒetɔ Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: Mitrɔ va gbɔnye, Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe, eye nye hã matrɔ ɖe mia ŋu. Aƒetɔ Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. They were warned by the earlier prophets to give up their evil and turn back to me, but they paid no attention.
translation_verse: Miganɔ abe mia tɔgbuiwo ene o. Woawo la, blema gbeƒãɖelawo ɖe gbeƒã kple ɣli na wo be: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: Mitrɔ tso miaƒe mɔ vɔ̃ɖiwo dzi kple miaƒe nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔwo me! Ke womesee loo, alo ɖo tom o.

english_verse: Where are your ancestors now? Not even prophets live forever.
translation_verse: Afi ka mia tɔgbuiwo le fifia? Gbeƒãɖelawo ɖe, wole agbe tegbetegbeea?

english_verse: But my warnings and my words spoken by the prophets caught up with your ancestors. So they turned back to me and said, “Lord All-Powerful, you have punished us for our sins, just as you had planned.” First Vision: Horses and Riders
translation_verse: Ke nye nya kple ɖoɖo siwo mede asi na nye dɔla gbeƒãɖelawo la, ɖe womewɔ dɔ ɖe mia tɔgbuiwo dzi oa? Ale wotrɔ dzime gblɔ be: Ale si Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la, ɖo be yeahe to na mí ɖe miaƒe zɔzɔme kple nuwɔna nui la, nenemae wòwɔ míi.” Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela la kpɔ sɔwo le ŋutega me

english_verse: On the twenty-fourth day of Shebat, which was the eleventh month of that same year, the Lord spoke to me in a vision during the night: In a valley among myrtle trees, I saw someone on a red horse, with riders on red, brown, and white horses behind him.
translation_verse: “Mekpɔ nane le ŋutega me le zã me. Kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsu aɖe ye; enɔ sɔ dzĩ aɖe dom. Etɔ ɖe gbemiti aɖewo dome le bali me, eye sɔ bubuwo nɔ eyome. Ðewo nɔ dzĩe, ɖewo nɔ hẽe, eye ɖewo hã nɔ ɣie.

english_verse: An angel was there to explain things to me, and I asked, “Sir, who are these riders?” “I'll tell you,” the angel answered.
translation_verse: Tete mebiae be: ‘Nye aƒetɔ, nu kawoe nye esiawo?’ Mawudɔla si ƒo nu kplim la gblɔ nam be: ‘Maɖe nu si wonye la afia wò.’

english_verse: At once, the man standing among the myrtle trees said, “These are the ones the Lord has sent to find out what's happening on earth.”
translation_verse: Ale ŋutsu si tɔ ɖe gbemitiawo dome la ɖo eŋu be: Woawoe nye ame siwo Aƒetɔ ɖo ɖa be woaɖatsa le anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: Then the riders spoke to the Lord's angel, who was standing among the myrtle trees, and they said, “We have gone everywhere and have discovered that the whole world is at peace.”
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu na Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla si tɔ ɖe gbemitiawo dome la be: ‘Míetsa le anyigba la dzi, eye kpɔ ɖa, anyigba blibo la kpɔ gbɔdzɔe.’

english_verse: The Lord's answer was kind and comforting.
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ gblɔ amenuvenya kple akɔfanyawo na mawudɔla si ƒo nu kplim la.

english_verse: So the angel told me to announce: I, the Lord All-Powerful, am very protective of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ale mawudɔla si ƒo nu kplim la gblɔ nam be: Ɖe gbeƒã sesĩe nàgblɔ be: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla be, meʋã ŋu ɖe Yerusalem kple Zion nu vevie ŋutɔ.

english_verse: For a while I was angry at the nations, but now I am furious, because they have made things worse for Jerusalem and are not the least bit concerned.
translation_verse: Dzi kum vevie ɖe dukɔ siwo li bɔkɔɔ la ŋu, elabe esi medo dziku vie ko la, woawo gblẽ nu ɖe edzi.

english_verse: And so, I will have pity on Jerusalem. The city will be completely rebuilt, and my temple will stand again.
translation_verse: Eya ta Aƒetɔ be, Metsɔ dɔmetɔtrɔ gbɔ va Yerusalem; woatso nye aƒe ɖe eme, eye woada nudzidzeka ɖe Yerusalem ŋu. Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe.

english_verse: I also promise that my towns will prosper—Jerusalem will once again be my chosen city, and I will comfort the people of Zion. Second Vision: Animal Horns
translation_verse: Gaɖe gbeƒã sesĩe ake be, Aƒetɔ Aʋakɔwokplɔla be: Nu nyui agagba go ɖe nye duwo me, eye Aƒetɔ agafa akɔ na Zion, eye woagatia Yerusalem.’ ” Gbeƒãɖela la kpɔ lãdzo ene le ŋutega me

english_verse: Next, I saw four animal horns.
translation_verse: Tete mefɔ mo dzi, eye kpɔ ɖa, mekpɔ lãdzo ene.

english_verse: The angel who was sent to explain was there, and so I asked, “What do these mean?” His answer was, “These horns are the nations that scattered the people of Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem, and took away their freedom.” Then the Lord showed me four blacksmiths, and I asked, “What are they going to do?” He replied, “They are going to terrify and crush those horns.”
translation_verse: Mebia be: “Nu ka wɔ ge ame siawo va?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Esiawoe nye dzo siwo kaka Yuda ale be ame aɖeke megafɔ ta dzi o, eye esiawo va be yewoado ŋɔdzi na wo, ale be woatutu dukɔ siwo kɔ woƒe dzowo dzi ɖe Yuda-nyigba ŋu be yewoakakae la.”

english_verse: This time I saw someone holding a measuring line,
translation_verse: Tete mefɔ mo dzi, eye kpɔ ɖa, mekpɔ ŋutsu aɖe si lé nudzidzeka ɖe asi.

english_verse: and I asked, “Where are you going?” “To measure Jerusalem,” was the answer. “To find out how wide and long it is.”
translation_verse: Mebiae be: “Afi ka yim nèle?” Eɖo eŋu nam be: “Meyina Yerusalem dzidze ge ne manya eƒe kekeme kple didime.”

english_verse: The angel who had spoken to me came toward me, when another angel came up to him
translation_verse: Tete mekpɔ be mawudɔla si nɔ nu ƒom kplim la do, zɔ yi ŋgɔ, eye mawudɔla bubu do va ŋgɔ va kpee.

english_verse: and said, “Hurry! Tell that man with the measuring line that Jerusalem won't have any boundaries. It will be too full of people and animals even to have a wall.
translation_verse: Egblɔ nɛ be: “Ƒu du yi ɖagblɔ na ɖekakpuivi ma be gli magaƒo xlã Yerusalem azɔ o, ke boŋ anɔ abe kɔƒe ene elabe dua me nɔlawo kple lãhawo asɔ gbɔ wu dua.

english_verse: The Lord himself has promised to be a protective wall of fire surrounding Jerusalem, and he will be its shining glory in the heart of the city.” A Call to Action
translation_verse: Elabe manye glikpɔ si anye dzo aƒo xlãe, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, eye manye atsyɔ̃ anɔ eme.” Aƒetɔ yɔ aboyomenɔlawo be woagbɔ va aƒe

english_verse: The Lord says to his people, “Run! Escape from the land in the north, where I scattered you to the four winds.
translation_verse: Hee! Hee! Misí tso dzigbemenyigba dzi, Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe, elabe mekaka mi ɖe gbeta abe dziƒo ƒe ya eneawo ene.

english_verse: Leave Babylonia and hurry back to Zion.”
translation_verse: Hee! Misí yi Zion, mi ame siwo le Babilon vinyɔnu gbɔ.

english_verse: Then the glorious Lord All-Powerful ordered me to say to the nations that had raided and robbed Zion: Zion is as precious to the Lord as are his eyes. Whatever you do to Zion, you do to him.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be bubu tae wodɔm ɖe dukɔ si ha mi la gbɔ, elabe ame si ka asi mia ŋu la ka asi eƒe ŋkuvi ŋu.

english_verse: And so, he will put you in the power of your slaves, and they will raid and rob you. Then you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, maʋuʋu asi ɖe wo, eye woatrɔ zu nuhaha na ame siwo subɔ wo la. Ekema mianyae be Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae dɔm ɖa.

english_verse: City of Zion, sing and celebrate! The Lord has promised to come and live with you.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Wò Zion vinyɔnu, dzi ha, eye tso aseye elabe megbɔna be manɔ dowòme!”

english_verse: When he does, many nations will turn to him and become his people. At that time you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, dukɔ geɖewo ava ku ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu azu nye dukɔ. Manɔ dowòme, eye nànya be Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae dɔm ɖe gbɔwò.

english_verse: Then Judah will be his part of the holy land, and Jerusalem will again be his chosen city.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ anyi Yuda ƒe dome le anyigba kɔkɔe la dzi, eye wòagatia Yerusalem.

english_verse: Everyone, be silent! The Lord is present and moving about in his holy place.
translation_verse: Ŋutilãwo katã nezi ɖoɖoe toŋ le Aƒetɔ ŋkume, elabe edo tso eƒe nɔƒe kɔkɔe la gbɔna.

english_verse: I was given another vision. This time Joshua the high priest was standing in front of the Lord's angel. And there was Satan, standing at Joshua's right side, ready to accuse him.
translation_verse: Tete eɖe nunɔlagã Yosua fiam, wòle tsitre ɖe Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla la ŋgɔ eye Satana le tsitre ɖe eƒe ɖusime be yeatsɔ nya ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: But the Lord said, “Satan, you are wrong. Jerusalem is my chosen city, and this man was rescued like a stick from a flaming fire.”
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ na Satana be: “Aƒetɔ neka mo na wò, Satana. Aƒetɔ, ame si tia Yerusalem la, neka mo na wò! Ɖe menye nake si woɖe tso dzo me lae nye esia oa?”

english_verse: So the angel told some of the people to remove Joshua's filthy clothes. Then he said to Joshua, “This means you are forgiven. Now I will dress you in priestly clothes.”
translation_verse: Mawudɔla la gblɔ na ame siwo tsi tsitre ɖe eŋkume la be: “Miɖe awu ƒoɖiawo le ŋutsu sia ŋu!” Egblɔ na eya ŋutɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, meɖe wò nuvɔ̃wo ɖa le ŋuwò, eya ta mado awu xɔasiwo na wò.”

english_verse: I spoke up and said, “Also put a clean priestly turban on his head.” Then they dressed him in priestly clothes and put the turban on him, while the Lord's angel stood there watching.
translation_verse: Megblɔ be: “Mitsɔ tablanu dzadzɛ bla ta nɛ!” Ale wotsɔ tablanu dzadzɛ bla ta nɛ eye wodo awu nɛ; Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla la nɔ tsitre ɖi.

english_verse: After this, the angel encouraged Joshua by telling him that the Lord All-Powerful had promised:
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla la xlɔ̃ nu Yosua be,

english_verse: If you truly obey me, I will put you in charge of my temple, including the courtyard around it, and you will be allowed to speak at any time with the angels standing beside me.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Ne èwɔ nye sewo dzi, eye nèlé nye ɖoɖowo me ɖe asi la, ànye nye aƒe la kple eƒe xɔxɔnuwo dzikpɔla. Mana nɔƒe wò ɖe ame siwo le tsitre ɖe afii la dome.

english_verse: Listen carefully, High Priest Joshua and all of you other priests. You are a sign of things to come, because I am going to bring my servant, the Chosen King.
translation_verse: Azɔ, wò nunɔlagã Yosua, ɖo to nàsee; wò kple xɔ̃wòwo siwo nɔ gbɔwò la misee. Elabe woawoe nye nu nyui siwo gbɔna la ƒe dzesi. Mana nye dɔla si woyɔna be Alɔdze la nava.

english_verse: Joshua, I have placed in front of you a stone with seven sides. I will engrave something on that stone, and in a single day I will forgive this guilty country.
translation_verse: Elabe, kpɔ ɖa, metsɔ kpe si axa adrẽ li na la da ɖe Yosua ŋgɔ. Mele nane ŋlɔ ge ɖe edzi, Aƒetɔ Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe; maɖe anyigba sia ƒe vodadawo ɖa le eŋu le ŋkeke ɖeka dzi.

english_verse: Then each of you will live at peace and entertain your friends in your own vineyard and under your own fig trees.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: Gbe ma gbe la, mia dome ame sia ame akpe ehavi ayi eƒe wainkawo kple eƒe gbotiwo te.

english_verse: The angel who explained the visions woke me from what seemed like sleep.
translation_verse: Tete mawudɔla si ƒo nu kplim la trɔ gbɔ va ʋuʋum abe ale si wonyɔa ame tso alɔ̃ me ene.

english_verse: Then he asked, “What do you see?” “A solid gold lampstand with an oil container above it,” I answered. “On the stand are seven lamps, each with seven flames.
translation_verse: Ebiam be: “Nu kae nye esi kpɔm nèle?” Meɖo eŋu be: “Akaɖiti si wotsɔ sika ɖeɖe wɔ lae. Amigba le etame. Akaɖi adrẽ le akaɖiti la dzi, eye akaɖimekadeƒe adrẽ le akaɖiawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu.

english_verse: One olive tree is on the right side and another on the left of the oil container.
translation_verse: Akaɖiti la le amiti eve dome; ɖeka le eƒe ɖusime, eye evelia le eƒe miame.”

english_verse: So the angel explained that it was the following message of the Lord to Zerubbabel: I am the Lord All-Powerful. So don't depend on your own power or strength, but on my Spirit.
translation_verse: Mawudɔla la gblɔ nam be mayi ɖagblɔ na Zerubabel be Aƒetɔ be: “Èle dzi ɖu ge, manye to aʋakɔ dzi alo to wò ŋutɔ wò ŋusẽ me o; ke boŋ to nye gbɔgbɔ dzi. Nye Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Zerubbabel, that mountain in front of you will be leveled to the ground. Then you will bring out the temple's most important stone and shout, “God has been very kind.”
translation_verse: Azɔ wò to kɔkɔ, nu ka nènye? Àzu gbadzaƒe le Zerubabel ŋgɔ. Aɖe kpe si le tawò me ke la vɛ, eye ɣli aɖi hoo be: ‘Enyakpɔ loo! Enyakpɔ loo!’ ”

english_verse: The Lord spoke to me again and said:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ gagblɔ nya bubu nam be mayi ɖagblɔ.

english_verse: Zerubbabel laid the foundation for the temple, and he will complete it. Then everyone will know that you were sent by me, the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Ebe: “Zerubabel ye ɖo gbedoxɔ sia gɔme anyi; eyae atui awu enu hã. Ne esia va eme la, nye dukɔ adze sii be nye Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae dɔ wò ɖe wo gbɔ vavã.

english_verse: Those who have made fun of this day of small beginnings will celebrate when they see Zerubbabel holding this important stone. Those seven lamps represent my eyes—the eyes of the Lord—and they see everything on this earth.
translation_verse: aEve wo be nuwo mele abe ale si wokpɔ mɔ be woanɔ la ene o, elabe dɔ sue aɖe ko wowɔ. Ke woakpɔ Zerubabel wòanɔ gbedoxɔa tum ayi edzi, eye dzi adzɔ wo.”

english_verse: Then I asked the angel, “What about the olive trees on each side of the lampstand? What do they represent?
translation_verse: Tete mebiae be: “Amiti eve siwo le akaɖiti la ƒe ɖusime kple miame la ya gɔme ɖe?”

english_verse: And what is the meaning of the two branches from which golden olive oil flows through the two gold pipes?”
translation_verse: Megabiae be: “Amiti la ƒe alɔdze eve ma siwo le sikato eveawo xa, eye ami sina toa wo me la hã gɔme ɖe?”

english_verse: “Don't you know?” he asked. “No sir, I don't,” was my answer.
translation_verse: Ebiam be: “Mèse wo gɔme oa?” Meɖo eŋu be: “Nye amegã, nyemese wo gɔme o.”

english_verse: Then he told me, “These branches are the two chosen leaders who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.”
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ nam be: “Woawoe nye ame eve siwo wotia hesi ami na, eye wole tsitre ɖe anyigba blibo la ƒe Aƒetɔ ŋkume.” Mawu do ŋugbe na Zerubabel

english_verse: When I looked the next time, I saw a flying scroll,
translation_verse: Megafɔ mo dzi, eye kpɔ ɖa, mekpɔ agbalẽ aɖe si le dzodzom le ya me.

english_verse: and the angel asked, “What do you see?” “A flying scroll,” I answered. “About nine meters long and four and a half meters wide.”
translation_verse: Tete mawudɔla la biam be: “Nu kae nye esia?” Meɖo eŋu be: “Agbalẽ aɖee. Ele dzodzom le ya me. Edidi meta asieke eye wòkeke meta ene kple afã.”

english_verse: Then he told me: This scroll puts a curse on everyone in the land who steals or tells lies. The writing on one side tells about the destruction of those who steal, while the writing on the other side tells about the destruction of those who lie.
translation_verse: Tete wògblɔ nam be: “Woŋlɔ ale si woƒo fi de anyigba bliboa la ɖe edzi, elabe fiafi ɖe sia ɖe atsrɔ̃ le anyigba la dzi le eƒe ŋɔŋlɔa nu, eye atam dzodzro kala ɖe sia ɖe atsrɔ̃ le eƒe ŋɔŋlɔa nu.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful has said, “I am sending this scroll into the house of everyone who is a robber or tells lies in my name, and it will remain there until every piece of wood and stone in that house crumbles.” Seventh Vision: A Woman in a Basket
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: Madɔ fiƒode ɖo ɖe fiafitɔ kple atam dzodzro kala ɖe sia ɖe ƒe aƒeme le nye ŋkɔ me. Anɔ aƒea me va se ɖe esime wòafiã ati kple kpewo.” Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela la kpɔ nyɔnu aɖe le kusi me

english_verse: Now the angel who was there to explain the visions came over and said, “Look up and tell me what you see coming.”
translation_verse: Mawudɔla si ƒo nu kplim la gado va eye wògblɔ nam be: “Fɔ mo dzi nàkpɔ nu si do gbɔna.”

english_verse: “I don't know what it is,” was my reply. “It's a big basket,” he said. “And it shows what everyone in the land has in mind.”
translation_verse: Mebiae be: “Nu kae nye esia?” Eɖo eŋu nam be: “Nudogbae do gbɔna. Esia nye woƒe nuvɔ̃ le anyigba blibo la dzi.”

english_verse: The lead cover of the basket was opened, and in the basket was a woman.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɖa, nutuvi si wowɔ kple tsumi la le kusia nu. Esi menɔ ekpɔm la, nutuvi la ʋu, eye mekpɔ nyɔnu aɖe wònɔ anyi ɖe nudogba la me.

english_verse: “This woman represents evil,” the angel explained. Then he threw her back into the basket and slammed the heavy cover down tight.
translation_verse: Mawudɔla la gblɔ nam be: “Nyɔnu sia nye vɔɖivɔ̃ɖi ƒe dzesi.” Azɔ la, etu asii ƒu agbaa me hehe nutuvia tu enu.

english_verse: Right after this I saw two women coming through the sky with wings outstretched like a stork in the wind. Suddenly they lifted the basket into the air,
translation_verse: Tete mefɔ mo dzi, eye kpɔ ɖa, mekpɔ nyɔnu eve siwo aʋala li na abe damixe ene; ya ɖo aʋala me na wo, eye wodzo gbɔna. Wova kɔ nudogba la hedzò yi ya me kplii.

english_verse: and I asked the angel, “Where are they taking the basket?”
translation_verse: Mebia mawudɔla la be: “Afi ka wokɔ nudogba la yinae?”

english_verse: “To Babylonia,” he answered, “where they will build a house for the basket and set it down inside.”
translation_verse: Eɖo eŋu be: “Wokɔe yina Sinear, afi si woaɖatu gbedoxɔ nɛ ɖo. Ne wotui vɔ la, woatsɔe adro ɖe enɔƒe le afi ma.

english_verse: Finally, I looked up and saw four chariots coming from between two bronze mountains.
translation_verse: Megafɔ mo dzi, eye kpɔ ɖa, mekpɔ tasiaɖam ene, siwo le go dom tso akɔblito eve dome la.

english_verse: The first chariot was pulled by red horses, and the second by black horses;
translation_verse: Sɔwo nɔ tasiaɖamawo hem. Tasiaɖam gbãtɔ ƒe sɔwo le dzĩe, evelia tɔwo le yibɔɔ,

english_verse: the third chariot was pulled by white horses, and the fourth by spotted gray horses.
translation_verse: etɔ̃lia tɔwo le ɣie eye enelia tɔwo le abe dzowɔ ene hele ŋɔtaŋɔta.

english_verse: “Sir,” I asked the angel. “What do these stand for?”
translation_verse: Tete mebia mawudɔla si ƒo nu kplim la be: “Nye Aƒetɔ, nu ka woe nye esiawo?”

english_verse: Then he explained, “These are the four winds of heaven, and now they are going out, after presenting themselves to the Lord of all the earth.
translation_verse: Mawudɔla la ɖo eŋu be: “Woawoe yina dziƒo ƒe ya eneawo nu, ne woyi ɖaɖe wo ɖokui fia le Aƒetɔ, anyigba la katã ƒe Aƒetɔ la ŋkume.”

english_verse: The chariot with black horses goes toward the north, the chariot with white horses goes toward the west, and the one with spotted horses goes toward the south.”
translation_verse: Tasiaɖam si hem sɔ yibɔawo le la ɖo ta dzigbeme, esi hem ɣitɔwo le la ɖo ta ɣetoɖoƒe, eye esi hem ŋɔtaŋɔtaawo le la ɖo ta anyigbeme.

english_verse: The horses came out eager to patrol the earth, and the angel told them, “Start patrolling the earth.” When they had gone on their way,
translation_verse: Esi sɔ dzĩawo ho la, wotsi dzi be yewoayi aɖatsa le anyigba dzi. Tete wògblɔ na wo be: “Miyi ɖatsa le anyigba la dzi!” Ale woyi ɖatsa le edzi.

english_verse: he shouted to me, “Those that have gone to the country in the north will do what the Lord's Spirit wants them to do there.” The Chosen Leader
translation_verse: Tete wodo ɣli yɔm gblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, sɔ siwo ho ɖo ta dzigbeme la na nye gbɔgbɔ dze akɔ anyi le dzigbemenyigba la dzi.” Woɖɔ fiakuku na Yosua

english_verse: The Lord said to me:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe va nam be:

english_verse: Tell him that I, the Lord All-Powerful, say, “Someone will reach out from here like a branch and build a temple for me. I will name him ‘Branch,’ and he will rule with royal honors. A priest will stand beside his throne, and the two of them will be good friends.
translation_verse: Eyae nye ame si atu gbedoxɔ la. Woade bubu eyama ŋu abe fia ene, eye wòaɖu eƒe dukɔ dzi. Nunɔla anɔ eƒe fiazikpui ŋu eye wo kple eve la ase wo nɔewo gɔme ahawɔ dɔ le ŋutifafa me.’ ”

english_verse: This crown will be kept in my temple as a reminder and will be taken care of by Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Josiah.”
translation_verse: Fiakuku la nenɔ Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔ me be woatsɔ anɔ ŋku ɖom Xeldai, Tobiya kple Yedaya kpakple Yosiya dzii.

english_verse: When people from distant lands come and help build the temple of the Lord All-Powerful, you will know that the Lord is the one who sent me. And this will happen, if you truly obey the Lord your God.
translation_verse: “Amewo atso didiƒe ʋĩi ava kpe ɖe xɔa tulawo ŋu woatu Aƒetɔ ƒe gbedoxɔ la, eye miadze sii be Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae dɔm ɖe mi. Nu siawo katã ava eme ne miewɔ Aƒetɔ, mia Mawu la ƒe gbe dzi pɛpɛpɛ.”

english_verse: On the fourth day of Chislev, the ninth month of the fourth year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord again spoke to me.
translation_verse: Esime fia Dario ƒe dziɖuɖu ɖo ƒè enelia me la, Aƒetɔ ƒe gbe va na Zaxarya le ɣleti asiekelia si woyɔna be Kislev ƒe ŋkeke enea gbe.

english_verse: It happened after the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer with Regem-Melech and his men to ask the priests in the Lord's temple and the prophets to pray for them. So they prayed, “Should we mourn and go without eating during the fifth month, as we have done for many years?”
translation_verse: Wodi be woabia nunɔla siwo le Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la, ƒeme kple Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo be: “Ðe magafa konyi, atsi nu dɔ le ɣleti atɔ̃lia me abe ale si mewɔ ƒè geɖee nye esi enea?”

english_verse: It was then that the Lord All-Powerful told me to say to everyone in the country, including the priests: For
translation_verse: “Gblɔ na dukɔ blibo la kple nunɔlawo be, le ƒè bla adrẽ siwo va yi me la, wotsia nu dɔna kple nuxaxa le ɣleti atɔ̃lia kple adrẽlia me. Ðe wobu be nyee yewonɔ ewɔm naa?

english_verse: And when you eat and drink, isn't it for your own enjoyment?
translation_verse: Azɔ ne mieɖu nu, no nu la, ɖe menye miawo ŋutɔe mieɖui na, henoe na oa?”

english_verse: My message today is the same one I commanded the earlier prophets to speak to Jerusalem and its villages when they were prosperous, and when all of Judah, including the Southern Desert and the hill country, was filled with people.
translation_verse: Le ɣe ma ɣi esime, Yerusalem kple du siwo ƒo xlãe godoo nɔ ŋutifafa me, nuwo bɔ eye agbenɔnɔ mesesẽ o ale be amewo nɔ du siawo kple esiwo le anyigbeme le toawo gɔme la me fũu la, ɖe menye nya siawoe Aƒetɔ ɖe gbeƒãe to blemagbeƒãɖelawo dzi oa? Amewo yi aboyo me elabe womeɖo to Mawu o

english_verse: So once again, I, the Lord All-Powerful, tell you, “See that justice is done and be kind and merciful to one another!
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: ‘Midrɔ̃ ʋɔnu dzɔdzɔe, mia dome ame sia ame nenyo dɔme na ehavi eye wòakpɔ nublanui nɛ.

english_verse: Don't mistreat widows or orphans or foreigners or anyone who is poor, and stop making plans to hurt each other.”
translation_verse: Migate ahosiwo kple tsyɔ̃eviwo, amedzrowo kple ame dahewo ɖe anyi o. Mia dome ame aɖeke negaɖo vɔ̃ ɖe nɔvia ŋu le eƒe dzime o.’

english_verse: But everyone who heard those prophets, stubbornly refused to obey. Instead, they turned their backs on everything my Spirit had commanded the earlier prophets to preach. So I, the Lord, became angry
translation_verse: Wona woƒe dzi ku atri ale be yewomagase se la kple Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la ƒe nya siwo wògblɔ ɖo ɖa, to eƒe gbɔgbɔ kple eƒe gbeƒãɖela siwo nɔ anyi le blema la dzi o. Le esia tae, dɔmedzoe tso Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la gbɔ va ɖo.

english_verse: and said, “You people paid no attention when I called out to you, and now I'll pay no attention when you call out to me.”
translation_verse: Esi meyɔ wo, woku to ɖe eme tae nye hã meku to ɖe eme esime woyɔm.

english_verse: That's why I came with a whirlwind and scattered them among foreign nations, leaving their lovely country empty of people and in ruins.
translation_verse: Metsɔ yali ka wo hlẽ ɖe dukɔ siwo womenya o la dome. Ale woƒe anyigba si wogblẽ ɖi la zu gbegbe, eye ame aɖeke megatoa afi ma yina o; wowɔ anyigba nyui la wòzu gbegbe.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful said to me:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la ƒe gbe va nam be:

english_verse: I love Zion so much that her enemies make me angry.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Meʋã ŋu ɖe Zion nu vevie eye meʋã ŋu ɖe enu vevie kple dɔmedzoe.

english_verse: I will return to Jerusalem and live there on Mount Zion. Then Jerusalem will be known as my faithful city, and Zion will be known as my holy mountain.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: Magatrɔ ayi Zion, eye maɖanɔ Yerusalem, eye woayɔ Yerusalem be ‘Duwɔnuteƒe’ eye woayɔ Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, ƒe to la be ‘To kɔkɔe.’ ”

english_verse: Very old people with walking sticks will once again sit around in Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Amewo agatsi axɔ ƒè geɖee, agaku amegã alo nyagã, alé atizɔti ɖe asi abɔbɔ nɔ ablɔwo dzi le Yerusalem.

english_verse: while boys and girls play in the streets.
translation_verse: Ŋutsuviwo kple nyɔnuviwo agayɔ ablɔwo dzi taŋ anɔ fefem.”

english_verse: This may seem impossible for my people who are left, but it isn't impossible for me, the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Nu sia awɔ mo yaa na dukɔa me tɔ siwo susɔ fifia, ke ɖe woawɔ nuku na nye hã?” Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe.

english_verse: I will save those who were taken to lands in the east and the west,
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Maxɔ na nye ame siwo tso ɣedzeƒe kple ɣetoɖoƒe nyigbawo dzi,

english_verse: and I will bring them to live in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, faithful to bring about justice.
translation_verse: eye makplɔ wo vɛ be woava nɔ Yerusalem. Woanye nye dukɔ eye manye woƒe Mawu le nyateƒe kple nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ me.”

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful! So don't give up. Think about the message my prophets spoke when the foundation of my temple was laid.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Alɔka me nasẽ na mi, ame siwo se nya siawo tso gbeƒãɖelawo ƒe nu me, tso gbe si gbe woɖo Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la ƒe gbedoxɔ la gɔme anyi be woatui.

english_verse: Before that time, neither people nor animals were rewarded for their work, and no one was safe anywhere, because I had turned them against each other.
translation_verse: Elabe do ŋgɔ na ɣe ma ɣi la, fetu menɔe na amegbetɔ loo, alo lã o; dedienɔnɔ menɔe na ame aɖe si le dodom alo le gbɔgbɔm la tso futɔ la si me o. Elabe mena ame sia ame tsi tre ɖe ehavi ŋu.

english_verse: My people, only a few of you are left, and I promise not to punish you as I did before.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la, nyemagawɔ ɖe dukɔa me tɔ siwo susɔ la ŋu abe ale si mewɔ ɖe wo ŋu tsã ene o.” Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Instead, I will make sure that your crops are planted in peace and your vineyards are fruitful, that your fields are fertile, and the dew falls from the sky.
translation_verse: Elabe: “Amewo ade agble le ŋutifafa me eye wain atse fũu. Dziƒo adza zãmu eye anyigba ana nu aʋã. Mana ame siwo susɔ la azu nu siawo ƒe gomekpɔlawo.

english_verse: People of Judah and Israel, you have been a curse to the nations, but I will save you and make you a blessing to them. So don't be afraid or lose courage.
translation_verse: Yudatɔwo kple Israeltɔwo! Ale si amewo ƒoa fi dea mi, doa hamelo ɖe mia ŋu tsã la, nenemae maxɔ na mii, eye mianye yayra. Migavɔ̃ o, ke boŋ alɔka me nasẽ na mi.”

english_verse: When your ancestors made me angry, I decided to punish you with disasters, and I didn't hold back.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Ale si meɖo tame be mawɔ vɔ̃ mia tɔgbuiwo esime wodo dɔmedzoe nam eye nyemetrɔ o la, Aƒetɔ Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae gblɔe,

english_verse: Now you no longer need to be afraid. I have decided to treat Jerusalem and Judah with kindness.
translation_verse: nenemae megaɖo tame le ŋkeke siawo me be mawɔ nyui na Yerusalem kple Yuda ƒe aƒe la; migavɔ̃ o.

english_verse: But you must be truthful with each other, and in court you must give fair decisions that lead to peace.
translation_verse: Nu siwo wòle be miawɔ lae nye: Mito nyateƒe na mia nɔewo. Midrɔ̃ ʋɔnu ɖe eteƒe le miaƒe agbowo me, eye midi ŋutifafa.

english_verse: Don't ever plan evil things against others or tell lies under oath. I, the Lord, hate such things. A Time of Celebration
translation_verse: Migaɖo vɔ̃ ɖe mia nɔewo ŋu o; migatà nu alakpatɔe o elabe melé fu nu siawo katã.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful told me to say:
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la ƒe gbe va nam be:

english_verse: People of Judah, I, the Lord, demand that whenever you go without food as a way of worshiping me, it should become a time of celebration. No matter if it's the fourth month, the fifth month, the seventh month, or the tenth month, you should have a joyful festival. So love truth and live at peace.
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla be: Nutsitsidɔ siwo miewɔna le ɣleti enelia, atɔ̃lia, adrẽlia kple ewolia me la azu dzidzɔ ŋkekenyuiwo na Yuda ƒe aƒe la, eya ta milɔ̃ nyateƒe kple ŋutifafa.”

english_verse: I tell you that people will come here from cities everywhere.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: “Dukɔwo gale vava ge; du bubuwo me nɔlawo ke hã.

english_verse: Those of one town will go to another and say, “We're going to ask the Lord All-Powerful to treat us with kindness. Come and join us.”
translation_verse: Du ɖeka me tɔwo ayi du bubu me tɔwo gbɔ aɖagblɔ na wo be, ‘Míawo míeyina enumake be míaɖaƒo koko na Aƒetɔ ne wòave mía nu, eye míasubɔ Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la. Mele yiyi ge.’

english_verse: Many people from strong nations will come to Jerusalem to worship me and to ask me to treat them with kindness.
translation_verse: Ameha geɖe kple dukɔ sesẽ deŋgɔ geɖewo ava subɔ Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la le Yerusalem eye woaƒo koko nɛ be neve yewo nu.

english_verse: When this happens, ten people from nations with different languages will grab a Jew by his clothes and say, “Let us go with you. We've heard that God is on your side.” I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la be: Ɣe ma ɣi la, ame ewo atso dzronyigba vovovowo dzi ava Yudatɔ ɖeka gbɔ, alé eƒe awu toga agblɔ nɛ be, ‘Nà míazɔ kpli wò yi elabe míese be Mawu li kpli mi.’ ”

english_verse: This is a message from the Lord: His eyes are on everyone, especially the tribes of Israel. So he pronounces judgment against the cities of Hadrach and Damascus.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya tsi tre ɖe Xadra-nyigba ŋu, eye wòava dzudzɔ ɖe Damasko dzi. Elabe Aram-duwo nye Aƒetɔ tɔ abe Israel-toawo katã gɔ̃ hã ene.

english_verse: Judgment will also fall on the nearby city of Hamath, as well as on Tyre and Sidon, whose people are clever.
translation_verse: Xamat hã do liƒo kplii; Tiro kple Sidon, siwo nya nu ŋutɔ hã.

english_verse: Tyre has built a fortress and piled up silver and gold, as though they were dust or mud from the streets.
translation_verse: Tiro tu mɔ́ sesẽ na eɖokui, eli kɔ klosalo ɖi gleglegle abe ʋuʋudedi ene, sika abe ba le ablɔwo me ene.

english_verse: Now the Lord will punish Tyre with poverty; he will sink its ships and send it up in flames.
translation_verse: Ke kpɔ ɖa, aƒetɔ la axɔ eƒe nunɔamesiwo le esi, atsɔ eƒe nukpɔkpɔwo aƒu gbe ɖe atsiaƒu me, eye dzo afiãe.

english_verse: Both Ashkelon and Gaza will tremble with fear; Ekron will lose all hope. Gaza's king will be killed, and Ashkelon emptied of its people.
translation_verse: Askalon akpɔe, eye vɔvɔ̃ aɖoe; Gaza hã akpɔe, eye wòatro, aɖu aɖukli. Ekron hã, eƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ bu, gbɔgblɔ bu ɖee. Fia atsrɔ̃ le Gaza; ame maganɔ Askalon o.

english_verse: A mob of half-breeds will settle in Ashdod, and the Lord himself will rob Philistia of pride.
translation_verse: Ame tsakatsakawo anɔ Asdod, eye matsi Filistitɔwo ƒe dàda nu.

english_verse: No longer will the Philistines eat meat with blood in it or any unclean food. They will become part of the people of our God from the tribe of Judah. And God will accept the people of Ekron, as he did the Jebusites.
translation_verse: Maɖe eƒe ʋu ɖa tso eƒe nu me, kple eƒe ŋunyɔnu ɖa tso eƒe aɖutame; eya hã anye nu si asusɔ na mía Mawu la anɔ abe Yuda ƒe hlɔ̃ ɖeka ene eye Ekron anɔ abe Yebusitɔwo ene.

english_verse: God says, “I will stand guard to protect my temple from those who come to attack. I know what's happening, and no one will mistreat my people ever again.” The Lord Tells about the Coming King
translation_verse: Ekema maƒu asaɖa anyi abe dzɔla ene, ɖe nye aƒe ŋu, ale be ame aɖeke manɔ yiyim anɔ gbɔgbɔm o; ameteɖeanyila aɖeke magazɔ wo dzi azɔ o. Fia si gbɔna

english_verse: Everyone in Jerusalem, celebrate and shout! Your king has won a victory, and he is coming to you. He is humble and rides on a donkey; he comes on the colt of a donkey.
translation_verse: Zion vinyɔnu, tso aseye vevie! Yerusalem vinyɔnu, do ɣli sesĩe! Kpɔ ɖa, wò fia gbɔna gbɔwò. Dziɖula si ƒe alɔ de dzi kple ɖokuibɔbɔla si do tedzi la wònye. Ele tedzinɔ ƒe vi dzi.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will take away war chariots and horses from Israel and Jerusalem. Bows that were made for battle will be broken. I will bring peace to nations, and your king will rule from sea to sea. His kingdom will reach from the Euphrates River across the earth. The Lord Promises To Rescue Captives
translation_verse: “Maɖe tasiaɖam ɖa le Efrayim; maɖe sɔwo ɖa le Yerusalem eye aʋadedatiwo atsrɔ̃. Aɖe gbe be ŋutifafa nenɔ dukɔwo dome; eƒe dziɖuɖu atso atsiaƒu nu ayi atsiaƒu nu. Atso tɔsisi la nu yi ɖase anyigba ƒe mlɔenu ke.” Mawu ƒe amewo agbugbɔ va aƒe

english_verse: When I made a sacred agreement with you, my people, we sealed it with blood. Now some of you are captives in waterless pits, but I will come to your rescue
translation_verse: “Ke wò hã, le nu, si mebla kpli wò, tsɔ ʋu ɖo kpe edzii ta la, maɖe ga wò gamenɔlawo tso tsivudo ƒuƒlu la me.

english_verse: and offer you hope. Return to your fortress, because today I will reward you with twice what you had.
translation_verse: Mitrɔ va azɔ, mi gamenɔla mɔkpɔlawo. Mitrɔ gbɔ va miaƒe mɔ́ sesẽwo me. Mele gbeƒã ɖem egbea be: Maɖo miaƒe fukpekpewo teƒe na mi, zigbɔzi eve.

english_verse: I will use Judah as my bow and Israel as my arrow. I will take the people of Zion as my sword and attack the Greeks. The Lord Will Protect His People
translation_verse: Elabe mehe Yuda abe dati ene, eye mewɔ Efrayim wònye eƒe aŋutrɔ. Zion, manyè viwò ŋutsuwo abe yi ene eye made adã tame na viwòwo ɖe Helaviwo ŋu, eye nada wò abe kalẽtɔ ƒe yi ene.

english_verse: Like a cloud, the Lord God will appear over his people, and his arrows will flash like lightning. God will sound his trumpet and attack in a whirlwind from the south.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ado ɖe wo tame eye wòada eƒe aŋutrɔwo woazɔ abe dzikedzo ene. Aƒetɔ Mawu aku kpẽ eye wòanɔ anyigbemeyali me ava yi.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful will protect his people, and they will trample down the sharpshooters and their slingshots. They will drink and get rowdy; they will be as full as a bowl at the time of sacrifice.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la akpɔ wo ta, eye wòavuvu akafodalawo, anya avuzi le wo dzi. Woano woƒe ʋu abe wain ene, woaɖi ƒo abe tre ene eye woaƒo ʋu abe vɔsamlekpui ƒe dzogoewo ene.

english_verse: The Lord God will save them on that day, because they are his people, and they will shine on his land like jewels in a crown.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe la, Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la axɔ na wo elabe wonye eƒe dukɔ la ƒe alẽha. Elabe woaklẽ le eƒe anyigba dzi abe kpe xɔasiwo le fiakuku ŋu ene.

english_verse: How lovely they will be. Young people will grow there like grain in a field or grapes in a vineyard.
translation_verse: Anyigba la anyo anyakpɔ loo! Bli ana ɖekakpuiwo akpɔ lã me, eye aha yeye ana ɖetugbiwo nanyakpɔ.

english_verse: I, the Lord, am the one who sends storm clouds and showers of rain to make fields produce. So when the crops need rain, you should pray to me.
translation_verse: Mibia tsidzadza Aƒetɔ le edzaɣi le adame; tso Aƒetɔ ame si wɔa ahomlilikpowo, ame si nana be agbafie wɔna na amegbetɔwo eye gbe wɔna na ame sia ame le gbedzi la gbɔ.

english_verse: You can't believe idols and fortunetellers, or depend on the hope you receive from witchcraft and interpreters of dreams. But you have tried all of these, and now you are like sheep without a shepherd.
translation_verse: Elabe aklama kpakpɛwo ƒoa nu susu manɔmee eye bokɔwo kpɔa alakpanu; drɔ̃ekulawo lĩa aʋatsodrɔ̃ewo eye wofaa akɔ dzodzro. Eya ta dukɔ la le tsa glãla tsam abe alẽwo ene. Wowɔa funyafunya wo elabe kplɔla mele wo si o.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, am fiercely angry with you leaders, and I will punish you. I care for my people, the nation of Judah, and I will change this flock of sheep into charging war horses.
translation_verse: Nye dziku lé dzo ɖe alẽkplɔlawo ŋu eye mahe to na kplɔlawo elabe Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla la tsɔ le eme na Yuda, eƒe alẽha eye woatsɔ wo awɔ eƒe sɔ sesẽ siwo dzi wòada ɖo le aʋa me.

english_verse: From this flock will come leaders who will be strong like cornerstones and tent pegs and weapons of war.
translation_verse: Woawo domee dzogoedzikpe, agbadɔtsyoti, aʋadedati kple dziɖula ɖe sia ɖe ado tso.

english_verse: They will join in the fighting, and together they will trample their enemies like mud. They will fight, because I, the Lord, will be on their side. And they will crush the enemy cavalry.
translation_verse: Woaƒo ƒu anɔ abe ŋusẽtɔwo ene le aʋa me; woafanya futɔwo ɖe ba me le ablɔwo dzi. Woawɔ aʋa, elabe Aƒetɔ li kpli wo, eye sɔdolawo aɖu ŋukpe.

english_verse: I will strengthen the kingdoms of Judah and Israel. And I will show mercy because I am the Lord, their God. I will answer their prayers and bring them home. Then it will seem as though I had never rejected them.
translation_verse: “Mado ŋusẽ Yuda ƒe aƒe la, eye maxɔ na Yosef ƒe aƒe. Makplɔ wo agbɔe, elabe nye dɔme trɔ ɖe wo ŋu, eye woanɔ abe ɖe nyemegbe wo o ene, elabe nyee nye Aƒetɔ, woƒe Mawu la, eye matɔ na wo.

english_verse: Israel will be like a tribe of warriors celebrating with wine. When their children see this, they will also be happy because of me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Ekema Efrayim azu abe aʋawɔla ŋusẽtɔ ene, eye woanɔ dzidzɔ kpɔm abe wainnolawo ene. Wo viwo akpɔe, eye woatso aseye, eye woakpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe Aƒetɔ ŋu.

english_verse: I will give a signal for them to come together because I have rescued them. And there will be as many as ever before.
translation_verse: “Mala aku ayɔ wo aƒo ƒui. Elabe meɖe wo, eye woagadzi asɔ gbɔ fũu abe tsã ene.

english_verse: Although I scattered my people in distant countries, they won't forget me. Once their children are raised, they will return—
translation_verse: Togbɔ be mekaka wo hlẽ ɖe dukɔwo dome hã, afi ka ke wole o, woaɖo ŋku dzinye. Woawo kple wo viwo woatsi agbe atrɔ gbɔ.

english_verse: I will bring them home from Egypt and Assyria, then let them settle as far as Gilead and Lebanon, until the land overflows with them.
translation_verse: Makplɔ wo va aƒee tso Egipte-nyigba dzi, eye maƒo wo ƒu tso Asiria. Makplɔ wo va Gilead kple Lebanon-nyigba dzi, va se ɖe esime teƒe magatu wo o.

english_verse: My people will go through an ocean of troubles, but I will overcome the waves and dry up the deepest part of the Nile. Assyria's great pride will be put down, and the power of Egypt will disappear.
translation_verse: Woato Egipte-ƒu me eye woaŋe ƒua ƒe ƒutsotsoewo, ale be Nil-tɔsisi ƒe gogloƒewo katã amie. Woabɔbɔ Asiria ƒe dàda la ɖe anyi, eye Egipte ƒe fiatikplɔ ate ɖa.

english_verse: I'll strengthen my people because of who I am, and they will follow me. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Mana woakpɔ ŋusẽ le Aƒetɔ me, eye woade bubu eŋkɔ ŋu.” Aƒetɔ lae gblɔe.

english_verse: Lebanon, open your gates! Let the fire come in to destroy your cedar trees.
translation_verse: Lebanon, ʋu wò agbowo, be dzo nafiã wò sedertiwo.

english_verse: Cry, you cypress trees! The glorious cedars have fallen and are rotting. Cry, you oak trees of Bashan! The dense forest has been chopped down.
translation_verse: Sesewuwo, mifa avi elabe sedertiwo mu eye ati nyuitɔwo tsrɔ̃. Basan-logotiwo, mifa avi elabe woƒo ave dodo la keŋ.

english_verse: Listen! Shepherds are crying. Their glorious pastures have been ruined. Listen! Lions are roaring. The forests of the Jordan Valley are no more to be found. Worthless Shepherds
translation_verse: Ðo to nàse lãkplɔviwo ƒe avi ɖa; woƒe atsyɔ̃ bu. Ðo to nàse dzataviwo ƒe gbeɖeɖe ɖa; woƒo ave dodo le Yordan ŋu la keŋ. Lãkplɔvi eveawo

english_verse: The Lord my God said to me: Tend those sheep doomed for slaughter!
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ, nye Mawu la be: “Va zu alẽ siwo woawu la kplɔla.

english_verse: The people who buy and butcher them go unpunished, while everyone who sells them says, “Praise the Lord! I'm rich.” Not even their shepherds have pity on them.
translation_verse: Wo ƒlelawo wua wo eye ame aɖeke mehea to na wo o. Wo dzralawo gblɔna be ‘Mikafu Aƒetɔ’ elabe mezu kesinɔtɔ. Alẽawo kplɔlawo ŋutɔ gɔ̃ hã mekpɔa nublanui na wo o.”

english_verse: Tend those sheep because I, the Lord, will no longer have pity on the people of this earth. I'll turn neighbor against neighbor and make them slaves of a king. They will bring disaster on the earth, and I'll do nothing to rescue any of them.
translation_verse: Elabe Aƒetɔ be: “Nyemagakpɔ nublanui na anyigba sia dzi nɔlawo azɔ o. Nye ŋutɔ matsɔ ame sia ame ade asi na ehavi kple eƒe fia. Fiaawo agbã anyigba la gudugudu, eye nyemaxɔ ame aɖeke le wo si me o.”

english_verse: So I became a shepherd of those sheep doomed to be slaughtered by the sheep dealers. And I gave names to the two sticks I used for tending the sheep: One of them was named “Mercy” and the other “Unity.”
translation_verse: Ale meva zu alẽ siwo woɖo be woawu la kplɔla na ame siwo fia alẽ dzrana la. Metsɔ atikplɔ eve. Meyɔ ɖeka be “Amenuveve” eye meyɔ evelia be “Ðekawɔwɔ.” Ale mekpɔ alẽawo dzi.

english_verse: In less than a month, I became impatient with three shepherds who didn't like me, and I got rid of them.
translation_verse: Le ɣleti ɖeka me la, metsrɔ̃ lãkplɔvi etɔ̃awo. Ke nyemegbɔ dzi ɖi na wo o, eye woawo hã lé fum.

english_verse: Then I said, “I refuse to be your shepherd. Let the sheep that are going to die, go on and die, and those that are going to be destroyed, go on and be destroyed. Then let the others eat one another alive.”
translation_verse: Ale megblɔ na alẽha la be: “Nyemaganye mia kplɔla azɔ o. Ame si be yeaku la, neku; ame si be yeatsrɔ̃ la, netsrɔ̃, eye mamlɛawo nelé wo nɔewo ɖu.”

english_verse: On that same day, I broke the stick named “Mercy” to show that the Lord had canceled his agreement with all people.
translation_verse: Azɔ metsɔ nye atikplɔ si meyɔna be “Amenuveve” la eye meŋee tsɔ tú nu, si mebla kple dukɔwo katã la.

english_verse: The sheep dealers who saw me knew at once that this was a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Ale nubabla la tu gbe ma gbe. Alẽsitsala siwo nɔ ŋku lém ɖe ŋunye la, kpɔe dze sii be Aƒetɔ ye nɔ nu ƒom to dzinye.

english_verse: I told them, “Pay me my wages, if you think you should; otherwise, forget it.” So they handed me my wages, a measly
translation_verse: Tete Aƒetɔ gblɔ nam be: “Tsɔe ƒu gbe ɖe nudzraɖoƒe si le gbedoxɔ me la me.” Ale metsɔ klosaloga bla etɔ̃ si wobu be eyae yewotsɔ de bubu ŋunye la da ɖe nudzraɖoƒe si le gbedoxɔ me la me.

english_verse: Then I broke the stick named “Unity” and canceled the ties between Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Emegbe meŋe atikplɔ evelia si meyɔna be “Ðekawɔwɔ” la, eye megblẽ nɔviwɔwɔ si le Yuda kple Israel dome la me.

english_verse: Next, the Lord said to me, “Act like a shepherd again—this time a worthless shepherd.
translation_verse: Azɔ Aƒetɔ gblɔ nam be: “Gatsɔ lãkplɔvi maɖota la ƒe lãkplɔnuwo.

english_verse: Once more I am going to let a worthless nobody rule the land—one who won't care for the strays or search for the young or heal the sick or feed the healthy. He will just dine on the fattest sheep, leaving nothing but a few bones.”
translation_verse: Elabe kpɔ ɖa, mele lãkplɔvi xɔ ge le anyigba la dzi; lãkplɔvi sia la, metsɔa ɖeke le eme na tsɔtsrɔ̃lawo loo; alo dia esiwo buna la loo, alo daa gbe le esiwo xɔ abi la ŋu loo, alo esiwo tsi agbe la o. Le ema teƒe boŋ la, eɖua damitɔwo ƒe lã eye wòtúa woƒe afɔkliwo.

english_verse: You worthless shepherd, deserting the sheep! I hope a sword will cripple your arm and blind your right eye.
translation_verse: Baba na nye lãkplɔvi, maɖota si gblẽ eƒe lãha ɖe ya me. Na yi nagblẽ eƒe abɔ kple ɖusime ŋku! Na eƒe abɔ naƒu ɖe eŋu kplakplakpla, eye eƒe ɖusime ŋku negbã keŋkeŋ!”

english_verse: This is a message from the Lord about Israel: I am the Lord! I stretched out the heavens; I put the earth on its foundations and gave breath to humans.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ ƒe nya si wògblɔ ɖe Israel ŋu lae nye esi: Aƒetɔ, ame si keke dziƒo me heɖo anyigba gɔme anyi eye wòde gbɔgbɔ amegbetɔ me la be:

english_verse: I have decided that Jerusalem will become a bowl of wine that makes the neighboring nations drunk. And when Jerusalem is attacked, Judah will also be attacked.
translation_verse: “Kpɔ ɖa, mawɔ Yerusalem wòanye ahanotre si me aha muame le na dukɔ siwo ƒo xlãe godoo la. Woanoe amu anɔ mumum sagasaga. Ne futɔwo ɖe to ɖe Yerusalem la, woaɖe to ɖe Yuda hã.

english_verse: But I will turn Jerusalem into a heavy stone that crushes anyone who tries to lift it. When all nations on earth surround Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, mawɔ Yerusalem wòanɔ abe kpe kpekpe ene na dukɔwo katã. Ame siwo katã ate kpɔ be yewoakɔe la, awɔ nu vevi wo ɖokui. Xexea me dukɔwo katã ava ƒo ƒu atso ɖe eŋu.

english_verse: I will blind every horse and make them panic, and every rider will be confused. But at the same time, I will watch over Judah.
translation_verse: Mado ŋɔdzi na sɔwo katã ɣe ma ɣi, eye mana wo dolawo nadze aɖaʋa. Makpɔ Yudatɔwo ta, ke mana dukɔwo ƒe sɔwo katã ƒe ŋku agbã.

english_verse: Then every clan in Judah will realize that I, the Lord All-Powerful, am their God, and that I am the source of their strength.
translation_verse: Tete Yuda-hlɔ̃wo agblɔ na wo ɖokui be, ‘Yerusalemnɔlawo kpɔ ŋusẽ to Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla, woƒe Mawu la dzi.’

english_verse: At that time I will let the clans of Judah be like a ball of fire in a wood pile or a fiery torch in a hay stack. Then Judah will send the surrounding nations up in smoke. And once again the city of Jerusalem will be filled with people.
translation_verse: “Ɣe ma ɣi la, mana Yuda-hlɔ̃wo anɔ abe ze si le dzo bim le ave titina, abe akakati si le bibim le gbe ƒuƒu me la ene. Woafiã dukɔ siwo katã ƒo xlã wo le ɖusime kple miame godoo va kpe la, esime ame aganɔ Yerusalem ya le enɔƒe, le Yerusalem-du me.

english_verse: But I will first give victory to Judah, so the kingdom of David and the city of Jerusalem in all of their glory won't be thought of more highly than Judah itself.
translation_verse: “Aƒetɔ ana Yuda naɖu dzi gbã ale be David ƒe aƒe kple Yerusalem ƒe bubu makɔ dzi agbɔ Yuda tɔ ta o.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will protect Jerusalem. Even the weakest person there will be as strong as David, and David's kingdom will rule as though my very own angel were its leader.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, Aƒetɔ atsɔ akpoxɔnu aƒo xlã Yerusalemnɔlawo ale be ame belitɔ kekeake le wo dome anɔ abe David ene, eye David ƒe aƒe anɔ abe Mawu ene; woanɔ abe Aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla ene, adze wo ŋgɔ.

english_verse: I am determined to wipe out every nation that attacks Jerusalem. Mourning for the One Pierced with a Spear
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe la madi dukɔ siwo katã tsi tre ɖe Yerusalem ŋu la, ahatsrɔ̃ wo.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will make the descendants of David and the people of Jerusalem feel deep sorrow and pray when they see the one they pierced with a spear. They will mourn and weep for him, as parents weep over the death of their only child or their first-born.
translation_verse: “Mana nublanuikpɔkpɔ kple gbedodoɖa ƒe gbɔgbɔ axɔ aƒe ɖe David ƒe aƒe kple Yerusalemnɔlawo me, eye woafɔ ŋku ɖe ame si wotɔ nui la dzi. Woafae abe ale si wofaa vi ɖeka hɔ̃ si ku na dzila ene. Woafae vevie abe dzila siwo ƒe ŋgɔgbevi ku na wo la ene.

english_verse: On that day the people of Jerusalem will mourn as much as everyone did for Hadad Rimmon on the flatlands near Megiddo.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, woafa konyi vevie le Yerusalem abe ale si wowɔa kunu na Hadad-Rimon le Megido gbegbe ene.

english_verse: Everyone of each family in the land will mourn, and the men will mourn separately from the women. This includes those from the family of David, and the families of Nathan,
translation_verse: Anyigba afa konyi, ƒome sia ƒome afae le eɖokui si. David ƒe aƒe afae le eɖokui si, wo srɔ̃wo afae le wo ɖokui si. Natan ƒe aƒe afae le eɖokui si, wo srɔ̃wo afae le wo ɖokui si.

english_verse: In the future there will be a fountain, where David's descendants and the people of Jerusalem can wash away their sin and guilt.
translation_verse: Aƒetɔ be: “Gbe ma gbe la, tsidzidzi nu aʋu na David ƒe aƒe kple Yerusalemnɔlawo be wòaklɔ woƒe nuvɔ̃ kple makɔmakɔnyenye ɖa le wo ŋu.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says: When that time comes, I will get rid of every idol in the country, and they will be forgotten forever. I will also do away with their prophets and those evil spirits that control them.
translation_verse: “Gbe ma gbe la, matsrɔ̃ legbawo le anyigba dzi eye ɖeke ƒe ŋkɔ magava tame na ame azɔ o. Aƒetɔ, Aʋakɔwokplɔla lae le gblɔm. Maɖe gbeƒãɖelawo kple gbɔgbɔ makɔmakɔwo ɖa le anyigba la dzi.

english_verse: If any such prophets ever appear again, their own parents must warn them that they will die for telling lies in my name—the name of the Lord. If those prophets don't stop speaking, their parents must then kill them with a sword.
