english_verse: But we believe that we will be saved by the gift of undeserved grace from our Lord Jesus Christ, just as the Gentiles are.
translation_verse: Ke míexɔ se be ale si Mawu axɔ mí ɖe agbe elabe eve mía nu le Aƒetɔ Yesu ta la, axɔ woawo hã ɖe agbe nenema ke.”

english_verse: Everyone kept quiet and listened as Barnabas and Paul told how God had given them the power to work a lot of miracles and wonders for the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ameawo katã zi ɖoɖoe. Woɖo to Barnaba kple Paulo wole dzesi kple nukunu siwo Mawu to wo dzi wɔ le ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la dome la xlẽm fia.

english_verse: After they had finished speaking, James said: My friends, listen to me!
translation_verse: Esi wowu woƒe nuƒoa nu la, Yakobo ƒo nu gblɔ be: “Nɔvinyewo, miɖo tom!

english_verse: Simon Peter has told how God first came to the Gentiles and made some of them his own people.
translation_verse: Simon xlẽ ale si Mawu do ŋgɔ, ɖee fia be yetsɔ ɖe le ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la hã ƒe nya me fia mí. Esia ta Mawu tia amewo tso wo dome be woanye eƒe dukɔ.

english_verse: “I, the Lord, will return and rebuild David's fallen house. I will build it from its ruins and set it up again.
translation_verse: ‘Le nu siawo megbe la, mele tɔtrɔ ge ava; eye magbugbɔ David ƒe agbadɔ si mu la, agatu. Magbugbɔ eƒe gbagbãƒeawo agatu, eye mawɔe wòanɔ te.

english_verse: Then other nations will turn to me and be my chosen ones. I, the Lord, say this.
translation_verse: Ale be ame mamlɛawo katã woadi Aƒetɔ la. Ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o, siwo katã meyɔ be woanye nye ŋutɔ tɔnyewo.

english_verse: And so, my friends, I don't think we should place burdens on the Gentiles who are turning to God.
translation_verse: Yakobo yi edzi gblɔ be: “Eya ta nye susue nye be mele be míaɖe fu na ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo hafi le tɔtrɔm ɖe Mawu ŋu o la o.

english_verse: We should simply write and tell them not to eat anything that has been offered to idols. They should be told not to eat the meat of any animal that has been strangled or that still has blood in it. They must also not commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Ke boŋ míaŋlɔ agbalẽ na wo be woatsri nuɖuɖu si ŋu mekɔ o elabe wotsɔe sa vɔe na trɔ̃; woatsri ahasiwɔwɔ, woatsri lã si me ʋu tsi la kple ʋuɖuɖu.

english_verse: We must remember that the Law of Moses has been preached in city after city for many years, and every Sabbath it is read in our synagogues. A Letter to Gentiles Who Had Faith in the Lord
translation_verse: Elabe tso blema ke la, woɖea gbeƒã Mose ƒe se la le du sia du me eye woxlẽnɛ le ƒuƒoƒewo Dzudzɔgbe ɖe sia ɖe.” Agbalẽ si woŋlɔ na xɔsetɔ siwo menye Yudatɔwo o

english_verse: The apostles, the leaders, and all the church members decided to send some men to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Silas and Judas Barsabbas, who were two leaders of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Tete nya la dze amedɔdɔawo, hamemetsitsiwo kple ha blibo la ŋu eye woɖo kpe edzi be yewoatia ame aɖewo tso yewo dome, akpe ɖe Paulo kple Barnaba ŋu aɖo ɖe Antioxia. Wotia hanunɔla eve tso nɔviawo dome. Woawoe nye Yuda, ame si wona ŋkɔe be Barsaba kple Sila.

english_verse: They wrote a letter that said: We apostles and leaders send friendly greetings to all of you Gentiles who are followers of the Lord in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
translation_verse: Agbalẽ si woxɔ yi la me nyawoe nye: “Mía nɔvi lɔlɔ̃tɔ, siwo menye Yudatɔwo o le Antioxia, Siria kple Kilikia; agbalẽ sia tso mí amedɔdɔwo, hamemetsitsiwo kple mia nɔviwo gbɔ. Mi katã miedɔ nyuiea?

english_verse: We have heard that some people from here have terribly upset you by what they said. But we did not send them!
translation_verse: Míese be ame aɖewo tso mía dome afii va mia gbɔ, tsɔ nya aɖewo va ɖe fui na mi hetɔtɔ miaƒe susu. Evɔ la, menye míawoe dɔ wo ɖa o.

english_verse: So we met together and decided to choose some men and to send them to you along with our good friends Barnabas and Paul.
translation_verse: Eya ta míewɔ takpekpe eye míeɖo kpe edzi be míatia amewo tso mía dome akpe ɖe Barnaba kple Paulo, ame siwo nye míaƒe lɔlɔ̃tɔwo ŋu aɖo ɖe mi,

english_verse: These men have risked their lives for our Lord Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: elabe wotsɔ woƒe agbe kè ɖe mía Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo ƒe dɔ la ta.

english_verse: We are also sending Judas and Silas, who will tell you in person the same things that we are writing.
translation_verse: Ale míetia Yuda kple Sila, ame siwo ava gblɔ nya mawo ke na mi.

english_verse: The Holy Spirit has shown us that we should not place any extra burden on you.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, míawo kpakple Gbɔgbɔ Kɔkɔe la míekpɔ be medze be míado agba kpekpe na mi wu se vevi siwo gbɔna la o.

english_verse: But you should not eat anything offered to idols. You should not eat any meat that still has the blood in it or any meat of any animal that has been strangled. You must also not commit any terrible sexual sins. If you follow these instructions, you will do well. We send our best wishes.
translation_verse: Woawoe nye: Mitsri nuɖuɖu si wotsɔ sa vɔe na trɔ̃wo. Mitsri ʋuɖuɖu. Mitsri lã si me ʋu tsi la. Migawɔ ahasi o. Ne mielé se siawo me ɖe asi la, anyo na mi. Mi katã minɔ anyi nyuie.”

english_verse: The four men left Jerusalem and went to Antioch. Then they called the church members together and gave them the letter.
translation_verse: Esi wodo mɔ amedɔdɔawo la, wova ɖo Antioxia. Woƒo ƒu hametɔawo katã, eye wotsɔ agbalẽa na wo.

english_verse: When the letter was read, everyone was pleased and greatly encouraged.
translation_verse: Esi woxlẽe la, nuxlɔ̃amenya si le eme la do dzidzɔ na wo ŋutɔ.

english_verse: Judas and Silas were prophets, and they spoke a long time, encouraging and helping the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Yuda kple Sila wonye Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo, eye woxlɔ̃ nu nɔviawo kple nya geɖe hedo ŋusẽ wo.

english_verse: The men from Jerusalem stayed on in Antioch for a while. And when they left to return to the ones who had sent them, the followers wished them well.
translation_verse: Esi wonɔ wo gbɔ ɣeyiɣi aɖe la, hametɔawo do mɔ wo, wotrɔ yi ɖe ame siwo dɔ wo ɖa la gbɔ.

english_verse: But Paul and Barnabas stayed on in Antioch, where they and many others taught and preached about the Lord. Paul and Barnabas Go Their Separate Ways
translation_verse: Ke Paulo kple Barnaba ya tsi Antioxia, eye woawo kple ame bubu geɖewo nɔ nu fiam henɔ gbeƒã ɖem Aƒetɔ ƒe nya la. Paulo kple Barnaba klã tso wo nɔewo gbɔ

english_verse: Sometime later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let's go back and visit the Lord's followers in the cities where we preached his message. Then we will know how they are doing.”
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke aɖewo megbe la, Paulo gblɔ na Barnaba be: “Nà míagbugbɔ ayi aɖakpɔ nɔvi siwo míegblɔ Aƒetɔ la ƒe nya na le du ɖe sia ɖe me la ɖa, ale be míanya ale si wole anyii.”

english_verse: Barnabas wanted to take along John, whose other name was Mark.
translation_verse: Barnaba di be yewoakplɔ Yohanes, ame si wona ŋkɔe be Marko hã ɖe asi.

english_verse: But Paul did not want to, because Mark had left them in Pamphylia and had stopped working with them.
translation_verse: Ke Paulo bu be mesɔ be yewoakplɔe ɖe asi o, elabe egbugbɔ le yewo yome tsã le Pamfilia, eye mewɔ dɔa yi edzi kple yewo o.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas argued, then each of them went his own way. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus,
translation_verse: Paulo kple Barnaba ʋli nya sia ŋutɔ, eye woma tso wo nɔewo gbɔ. Barnaba kplɔ Marko ɖe asi, eye woɖo tɔdziʋu yi ɖe Kipro.

english_verse: but Paul took Silas and left after the followers had placed them in God's care.
translation_verse: Ke Paulo tia Sila kpe ɖe eɖokui ŋu. Hametɔawo tsɔ wo de asi na Aƒetɔ la be wòave wo nu, eye wodze mɔ dzo.

english_verse: They traveled through Syria and Cilicia, encouraging the churches.
translation_verse: Ezɔ to Siria kple Kilikia hedo ŋusẽ hameawo.

english_verse: Paul and Silas went back to Derbe and Lystra, where there was a follower named Timothy. His mother was also a follower. She was Jewish, and his father was Greek.
translation_verse: Paulo zɔ mɔ va ɖo Derbe kple Listra. Nusrɔ̃la aɖe le afi ma si ŋkɔe nye Timoteo. Dadaa nye xɔsetɔ, ame si nye Yudatɔ, ke tɔ́a nye Helatɔ.

english_verse: The Lord's followers in Lystra and Iconium said good things about Timothy,
translation_verse: Nɔvi siwo le Listra kple Ikonio la ƒo nu nyui le Timoteo ŋuti.

english_verse: and Paul wanted him to go with them. But Paul first had him circumcised, because all the Jewish people around there knew that Timothy's father was Greek.
translation_verse: Paulo di be yeakplɔ Timoteo ɖe asi, ale wòtso aʋa nɛ. Ewɔ esia, elabe Yudatɔ siwo katã le nuto ma me la nya be Timoteo tɔ́ la, Helatɔ wònye.

english_verse: As Paul and the others went from city to city, they told the followers what the apostles and leaders in Jerusalem had decided, and they urged them to follow these instructions.
translation_verse: Ne wozɔ mɔ va ɖo du aɖe me la, wogblɔa ɖoɖo siwo dzi amedɔdɔawo kple hamemetsitsiwo ɖo kpee le Yerusalem la na hametɔwo, eye wobiana tso wo si be woawɔ ɖe wo dzi.

english_verse: The churches became stronger in their faith, and each day more people put their faith in the Lord. Paul's Vision in Troas
translation_verse: Ale hameawo ƒe xɔse gasẽ ŋu ɖe edzi, eye wole agbɔ sɔm ɖe edzi gbe sia gbe. Paulo kpɔ ŋutega le Troa

english_verse: Paul and his friends went through Phrygia and Galatia, but the Holy Spirit would not let them preach in Asia.
translation_verse: Esi Gbɔgbɔ Kɔkɔe la meɖe mɔ na wo be woagblɔ nya le Asia o ta la, wozɔ mɔ to Frigia kple Galatia nutowo me

english_verse: After they arrived in Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not let them.
translation_verse: va ɖo Misia ƒe liƒo dzi. Wote kpɔ be yewoayi Bitinia, gake Yesu ƒe Gbɔgbɔ la meɖe mɔ na wo o.

english_verse: So they went on through Mysia until they came to Troas.
translation_verse: Ale wotso eme to Misia yi ɖe Troa.

english_verse: During the night, Paul had a vision of someone from Macedonia who was standing there and begging him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us!”
translation_verse: Le zã me la, Paulo kpɔ ŋutega. Makedonia-ŋutsu aɖe le tsitre hele kuku ɖem nɛ be: “Tso ƒua nàva kpe ɖe mía ŋuti le Makedonia!”

english_verse: After Paul had seen the vision, we began looking for a way to go to Macedonia. We were sure that God had called us to preach the good news there. Lydia Becomes a Follower of the Lord
translation_verse: Esi Paulo kpɔ ŋutega la la, míekpɔe dze sii kɔtɛe be Mawue yɔ mí be míaɖagblɔ Nyanyui la na amewo le afi ma. Ale míeɖoe be míayi Makedonia enumake. Lidia trɔ dzime le Filipi

english_verse: We sailed straight from Troas to Samothrace, and the next day we arrived in Neapolis.
translation_verse: Míeɖo tɔdziʋu tso Troa, tso eme tẽe yi Samotrake, eye le ŋufɔke la, míeyi ɖe Neapoli.

english_verse: From there we went to Philippi, which is a Roman colony in the first district of Macedonia. We spent several days in Philippi.
translation_verse: Míetso le afi ma yi Filipi. Filipi ye nye du lolotɔ le Makedonia-nutoa me eye wònye Romatɔwo ƒe du. Míenɔ afi sia ŋkeke aɖewo.

english_verse: Then on the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to a place by the river, where we thought there would be a Jewish meeting place for prayer. We sat down and talked with the women who came.
translation_verse: Dzudzɔgbe la, míedo le dua me yi ɖe tɔsisi aɖe to, afi si míebu be enye gbedoɖaƒe. Míebɔbɔ nɔ anyi, eye míeƒo nu na nyɔnu siwo va ƒo ƒu ɖi la.

english_verse: One of them was Lydia, who was from the city of Thyatira and sold expensive purple cloth. She was a worshiper of the Lord God, and he made her willing to accept what Paul was saying.
translation_verse: Ame siwo se míaƒe nyawo la dometɔ ɖekae nye Lidia. Enye avɔ biɖibiɖi xɔasi dzrala tso Tiatira. Mawuvɔ̃la wònye, eye Aƒetɔ la ʋu eƒe susu be wòalé to ɖe nya siwo Paulo gblɔ la ŋu.

english_verse: Then after she and her family were baptized, she kept on begging us, “If you think I really do have faith in the Lord, come stay in my home.” Finally, we accepted her invitation. Paul and Silas Are Put in Jail
translation_verse: Esi wole mawutsi na eya kple eƒemetɔwo la, eɖe kuku na mí vevie gblɔ be: “Ne miebum be mexɔ Aƒetɔ la dzi se vavã la, ekema miva dze aƒenye me.” Ale míelɔ̃ heyi kplii. Paulo kple Sila le gaxɔ me le Filipi

english_verse: One day on our way to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl. She had a spirit in her that gave her the power to tell the future. By doing this she made a lot of money for her owners.
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka esi míeyina ɖe gbedoɖaƒea la, nyɔnuvi kluvi aɖe si me afakagbɔgbɔ le la va do go mí. Ewɔa ga geɖe na eƒe aƒetɔwo to afakaka me.

english_verse: The girl followed Paul and the rest of us, and she kept yelling, “These men are servants of the Most High God! They are telling you how to be saved.”
translation_verse: Nyɔnuvi sia dze míawo kple Paulo yome nɔ gbɔgblɔm kple ɣli be: “Ame siawo la, Dziƒoʋĩtɔ la ƒe dɔlawoe wonye, eye ale si woaxɔ mi ɖe agbe la ƒe gbeƒã ɖem wole na mi!”

english_verse: This went on for several days. Finally, Paul got so upset that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I order you to leave this girl alone!” At once the evil spirit left her.
translation_verse: Enɔ nu sia wɔwɔ dzi ŋkeke geɖe. Mlɔeba dzi va ku Paulo, eye wòtrɔ gblɔ na gbɔgbɔ la be: “Le Yesu Kristo ŋkɔ me, do le eme.” Tete gbɔgbɔ la do le nyɔnuvia me le ɣeyiɣi ma me tututu.

english_verse: When the girl's owners realized they had lost all chances for making more money, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into court.
translation_verse: Ke esi ame siwo tɔ kluvia nye la kpɔ be yewobu yewoƒe gakpɔmɔnu la, wolé Paulo kple Sila, eye wohe wo yi ɖe ʋɔnui le dumegãwo ŋkume.

english_verse: They are telling us to do things we Romans are not allowed to do.”
translation_verse: Wole kɔ siwo medze be míaxɔ alo anyi abe Roma-dumeviwo ene o la fiam.”

english_verse: The crowd joined in the attack on Paul and Silas. Then the officials tore the clothes off the two men and ordered them to be beaten with a whip.
translation_verse: Tete ameha blibo la lũ ɖe Paulo kple Sila dzi. Ʋɔnudrɔ̃laawo dze awu le Paulo kple Sila ŋu, eye woɖe gbe be woaƒo wo kple ati.

english_verse: After they had been badly beaten, they were put in jail, and the jailer was told to guard them carefully.
translation_verse: Esi woƒo wo vevie la, wode wo gaxɔ me, eye wogblɔ na gaxɔdzikpɔla be nekpɔ egbɔ be wole dedie.

english_verse: The jailer did as he was told. He put them deep inside the jail and chained their feet to heavy blocks of wood.
translation_verse: Esi wogblɔ esia nɛ la, etsɔ wo de gaxɔ dometɔ ke me, eye wòde woƒe afɔwo atikpofɔblanu kpekpewo me.

english_verse: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing praises to God, while the other prisoners listened.
translation_verse: Ke le zã titina lɔƒo la, Paulo kple Sila nɔ gbe dom ɖa henɔ kafukafuhawo dzim na Mawu, eye gaxɔmenɔlaawo nɔ to ɖom wo.

english_verse: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the jail to its foundations. The doors opened, and the chains fell from all the prisoners.
translation_verse: Kasia anyigba ʋuʋu sesĩe, ale be gaxɔa ƒe gɔmeɖokpewo gli le wo nɔewo dzi. Ʋɔawo katã ʋu enumake eye gamenɔla ɖe sia ɖe ƒe kɔsɔkɔsɔ ge le eŋu.

english_verse: When the jailer woke up and saw that the doors were open, he thought that the prisoners had escaped. He pulled out his sword and was about to kill himself.
translation_verse: Ke esi gaxɔdzikpɔla la nyɔ eye wòkpɔ be ʋɔawo katã le ʋuʋu la, ebu be gamenɔlaawo si. Ale wòhe yi le aku me be yeawu ye ɖokui.

english_verse: But Paul shouted, “Don't harm yourself! No one has escaped.”
translation_verse: Ke Paulo do ɣli sesĩe be: “Mègawɔ nu vevi ɖokuiwò o! Mí katã míele afii!”

english_verse: The jailer asked for a torch and went into the jail. He was shaking all over as he knelt down in front of Paul and Silas.
translation_verse: Gaxɔdzikpɔla la bia be woatsɔ akaɖi vɛ na ye, eye wòɖe abla ge ɖe xɔa me. Vɔvɔ̃ ɖoe wònɔ dzodzom nyanyanya va dze anyi ɖe Paulo kple Sila ŋgɔ.

english_verse: After he had led them out of the jail, he asked, “What must I do to be saved?”
translation_verse: Gaxɔdzikpɔla la kplɔ wo doe, hebia wo be: “Amegãwo, nu ka mawɔ be woaxɔm ɖe agbe?”

english_verse: They replied, “Have faith in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved! This is also true for everyone who lives in your home.”
translation_verse: Woɖo eŋu be: “Xɔ Aƒetɔ Yesu dzi se, eye woaxɔ wò kple wò aƒemetɔwo ɖe agbe.”

english_verse: Then Paul and Silas told him and everyone else in his house about the Lord.
translation_verse: Wogblɔ Aƒetɔ la ƒe nya la na eya kple ame siwo katã le eƒeme la.

english_verse: While it was still night, the jailer took them to a place where he could wash their cuts and bruises. Then he and everyone in his home were baptized.
translation_verse: Ale le zã ƒe gaƒoƒo ma ke me la, gaxɔdzikpɔla la kplɔ wo yi ɖaklɔ woƒe abiawo na wo, eye wole mawutsi na eya kple eƒemetɔwo katã zi ɖeka.

english_verse: They were very glad they had put their faith in God. After this, the jailer took Paul and Silas to his home and gave them something to eat.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, ekplɔ Paulo kple Sila va eƒeme, eye wòna nu wo woɖu. Dzi dzɔ eya kple eƒemetɔwo ŋutɔ, be yewoxɔ Mawu dzi se.

english_verse: The next morning the officials sent some police with orders for the jailer to let Paul and Silas go.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, ʋɔnudrɔ̃laawo dɔ kpovitɔwo ɖa, de gbe asi na wo be: “Miɖe asi le ame mawo ŋu woayi.”

english_verse: The jailer told Paul, “The officials have ordered me to set you free. Now you can leave in peace.”
translation_verse: Ale gaxɔdzikpɔla la gblɔ na Paulo be: “Ʋɔnudrɔ̃laawo gblɔ ɖo ɖa be woaɖe asi le mia ŋu miayi. Eya ta mido va yi azɔ le ŋutifafa me.”

english_verse: But Paul told the police, “We are Roman citizens, and the Roman officials had us beaten in public without giving us a trial. They threw us into jail. Now do they think they can secretly send us away? No, they cannot! They will have to come here themselves and let us out.”
translation_verse: Ke Paulo gblɔ na kpovitɔawo be: “Womedrɔ̃ ʋɔnu mí o, ke woƒo mí le dutoƒo, eye wode mí gaxɔ me; evɔ la, Roma-dumeviwo míenye. Nu ka ta wodi be yewoaɖe asi le mía ŋu dzaa fifia, ame aɖeke masee? Gbeɖe, woawo ŋutɔ koe ava kplɔ mí adoe.”

english_verse: When the police told the officials that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, the officials were afraid.
translation_verse: Kpovitɔawo yi ɖagblɔ nya la na ʋɔnudrɔ̃laawo, ke esi wose be Roma-dumeviwoe Paulo kple Sila nye la, vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo.

english_verse: So they came and apologized. They led them out of the jail and asked them to please leave town.
translation_verse: Ale woyi ɖaɖe kuku na wo. Wokplɔ wo doe, eye wobia tso wo si be woadzo le dua me.

english_verse: But Paul and Silas went straight to the home of Lydia, where they saw the Lord's followers and encouraged them. Then they left.
translation_verse: Ale Paulo kple Sila do le gaxɔ la me, eye woyi ɖe Lidia ƒeme. Esi wokpɔ nɔviawo le afi ma la, wodo ŋusẽ wo eye wodzo.

english_verse: After Paul and his friends had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they went on to Thessalonica. A synagogue was in that city.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi wozɔ to Amfipoli kple Apolonia la, wova ɖo Tesalonika, afi si Yudatɔwo ƒe ƒuƒoƒe aɖe le.

english_verse: So as usual, Paul went there to worship, and on three Sabbaths he spoke to the people. He used the Scriptures
translation_verse: Paulo yi ƒuƒoƒe la, abe ale si wòwɔnɛ ɖaa la ene. Edzro mawunya me kpli wo Dzudzɔgbe etɔ̃,

english_verse: to show them that the Messiah had to suffer, but that he would rise from death. Paul also told them that Jesus is the Messiah he was preaching about.
translation_verse: eye wòɖe nya geɖe hã me na wo kple kpeɖodzinyawo. Paulo gblɔ be ehiã be Kristo la nakpe fu, eye wòafɔ tso ame kukuwo dome. Egblɔ yi edzi be: “Yesu, ame si ƒe nya mele gbeƒã ɖemee lae nye Kristo la.”

english_verse: Some of them believed what Paul had said, and they became followers with Paul and Silas. Some Gentiles and many important women also believed the message.
translation_verse: Nya la dze wo dometɔ aɖewo ŋu, eye woxɔe se hedze Paulo kple Sila yome. Nenema kee eme kɔ na Helatɔ vɔ̃mawu geɖe kple nyɔnu ŋkuta gbogbo aɖewo hã, eye woawo hã wodze wo yome.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders were jealous and got some troublemakers who hung around the marketplace to start a riot in the city. They wanted to drag Paul and Silas out to the mob, and so they went straight to Jason's home.
translation_verse: Ke Yudatɔwo ʋã ŋu Paulo kple Sila, eye woyi ɖaƒo ƒu nu vlo wɔla aɖewo le ablɔ me kpe ɖe wo ɖokui ŋu. Amewo ƒo zi ɖe wo ŋu, eye wona zi tɔ le dua me hoo. Wozɔ ɖe ŋutsu aɖe, si ŋkɔe nye Yason la ƒe aƒe dzi henɔ Paulo kple Sila dim be yewoahe ayi ɖe ameha la gbɔe.

english_verse: But when they did not find them there, they dragged out Jason and some of the Lord's followers. They took them to the city authorities and shouted, “Paul and Silas have been upsetting things everywhere. Now they have come here,
translation_verse: Esi womekpɔ wo o la, wohe Yason kple nɔviawo dometɔ aɖewo yi ɖe dua dziɖulawo gbɔe. Wotso wo nu be: “Ame siawoe he zitɔtɔ va afi sia afi le xexea me godoo eye wova du sia me hã.

english_verse: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. All of them break the laws of the Roman Emperor by claiming that someone named Jesus is king.”
translation_verse: Yason xɔ wo ɖe eƒeme, eye nu si wɔm wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe le la, tsi tre ɖe Roma Fiagã la ƒe sewo ŋu. Wobe fia bubu aɖe hã gali, si ŋkɔe nye Yesu.”

english_verse: The officials and the people were upset when they heard this.
translation_verse: Esi ameha la kple dua dziɖulawo se esia la, wotɔtɔ.

english_verse: So they made Jason and the other followers pay bail before letting them go. People in Berea Welcome the Message
translation_verse: Wona Yason kple ame bubuawo xe ga aɖe hetsɔ de megbee na wo ɖokui, eye woɖe asi le wo ŋu. Beroeatɔwo xɔ nya la

english_verse: That same night the Lord's followers sent Paul and Silas on to Berea, and after they arrived, they went to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Gbe ma gbe ƒe zã me la, nɔviawo ɖo Paulo kple Sila ɖe Beroea enumake. Esi woɖo la, woyi Yudatɔwo ƒe ƒuƒoƒe.

english_verse: The people in Berea were much nicer than those in Thessalonica, and they gladly accepted the message. Day after day they studied the Scriptures to see if these things were true.
translation_verse: Yudatɔ siwo le du sia me la se nu gɔme wu esiwo le Tesalonika. Woxɔ nya la kple dzo ŋutɔ, eye wodzroa mawunyagbalẽwo me gbe sia gbe be yewoakpɔ ɖa be Paulo ƒe nyawo nye nyateƒe mahã.

english_verse: Many of them put their faith in the Lord, including some important Greek women and several men.
translation_verse: Nya la dze wo dometɔ aɖewo ŋu, eye woxɔe se hedze Paulo kple Sila yome. Nenema kee Hela-ŋutsu vɔ̃mawu geɖe kple nyɔnu bubume geɖe hã xɔe se.

english_verse: When the Jewish leaders in Thessalonica heard that Paul had been preaching God's message in Berea, they went there and caused trouble by turning the crowds against Paul.
translation_verse: Ke esi Yudatɔ siwo le Tesalonika la se be Paulo yi ɖaɖe gbeƒã Mawu ƒe nya la le Beroea hã la, wova afi ma hã eye wode zi ameha la dome hetɔtɔ woƒe susu.

english_verse: At once the followers sent Paul down to the coast, but Silas and Timothy stayed in Berea.
translation_verse: Enumake nɔviawo ɖo Paulo ɖe afi ma ƒugo ŋu, ke wona Sila kple Timoteo ya tsi Beroea.

english_verse: Some men went with Paul as far as Athens, and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible. Paul in Athens
translation_verse: Ame siwo kplɔ Paulo ɖo ɖa la va ɖo keke Atene ke. Hafi woatrɔ adzo la, Paulo ɖo du ɖe Sila kple Timoteo be woaɖe abla ava tu ye kaba. Paulo le Atene

english_verse: While Paul was waiting in Athens, he was upset to see all the idols in the city.
translation_verse: Esime Paulo le Atene henɔ mɔ kpɔm na Sila kple Timoteo la, ekpɔ legbawo le dua me fũu ŋutɔ. Dzi kui.

english_verse: He went to the synagogue to speak to the Jews and to anyone who worshiped with them. Day after day he also spoke to everyone he met in the market.
translation_verse: Ale Paulo dzro nya me kple Yudatɔwo kpakple Helatɔ vɔ̃mawuwo le ƒuƒoƒe la. Gbe sia gbe la, eʋlia nya le ablɔmetakpeƒe kple ame sia ame si va yina la.

english_verse: Some of them were Epicureans and some were Stoics, and they started arguing with him. People were asking, “What is this know-it-all trying to say?” Some even said, “Paul must be preaching about foreign gods! That's what he means when he talks about Jesus and about people rising from death.”
translation_verse: Nunyala deŋgɔ aɖewo tso Epikurotɔwo kple Stoatɔwo dome hã va do goe. Wo dometɔ aɖewo bia be: “Ame manyanu nu kpoloe ƒola sia hã ɖe, nya ka koŋ le esi wòdi be yeagblɔ?” Ame bubuwo ɖo eŋu be: “Ewɔ abe dukɔ aɖe me mawu ŋuti wòle nu ƒom le ene.” Wogblɔ esia, elabe Paulo ƒo nu le Yesu kple ame kukuwo ƒe tsitretsitsi ŋu.

english_verse: They brought Paul before a council called the Areopagus, and said, “Tell us what your new teaching is all about.
translation_verse: Wolé Paulo, eye wokplɔe yi ɖe dutakpeƒe, si woyɔna be Areopago la. Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Míedi be nàƒo nu le nufiafia yeye si ƒe nya gblɔm nèle la ŋuti na mí.

english_verse: We have heard you say some strange things, and we want to know what you mean.”
translation_verse: Elabe nya siwo gblɔm nèle la, nye nya yeye le mía gbɔ; míese wo kpɔ o. Eya ta míedi be nàɖe wo me na mí ne míase wo gɔme.”

english_verse: More than anything else the people of Athens and the foreigners living there loved to hear and to talk about anything new.
translation_verse: Godoo la, ne nya yeye aɖe va Atene-du me la, Atenetɔ ŋutɔŋutɔwo kple amedzrowo siaa tsia dzi, gblẽa woƒe ɣeyiɣi katã be yewoase nya la ahato na ame bubuwo.

english_verse: So Paul stood up in front of the council and said: People of Athens, I see that you are very religious.
translation_verse: Ale Paulo tsi tsitre ɖe takpelawo ŋkume le dutakpeƒe la gblɔ be: “Atenetɔwo, mede dzesii le miaƒe nuwo katã ŋu be mievɔ̃a mawu ŋutɔ.

english_verse: As I was going through your city and looking at the things you worship, I found an altar with the words, “To an Unknown God.” You worship this God, but you don't really know him. So I want to tell you about him.
translation_verse: Elabe esime mezɔ to dua me, helé ŋku ɖe nu siwo miesubɔna la dometɔ aɖewo ŋu la, meke ɖe vɔsamlekpui aɖe ŋu. Woŋlɔ ɖe edzi be, ‘Mawu si ame aɖeke menya o la tɔe.’ Eya ta nu si mienya o, evɔ miehele esubɔm la ƒe nyae mele gbeƒã ɖemee na mi.

english_verse: This God made the world and everything in it. He is Lord of heaven and earth, and he doesn't live in temples built by human hands.
translation_verse: Mawu, ame si wɔ xexea me kple nu sia nu si le eme, eye wònye Aƒetɔ le dziƒo kple anyigba siaa la, menɔa gbedoxɔ siwo amegbetɔ tu la me o.

english_verse: God has done all this, so that we will look for him and reach out and find him. He isn't far from any of us,
translation_verse: Ewɔ esia, ale be amewo natsa así adii, abe woakpɔe ene. Evɔ la, Mawu mele adzɔge tso mía dometɔ aɖeke gbɔ hafi o.

english_verse: and he gives us the power to live, to move, and to be who we are. “We are his children,” just as some of your poets have said.
translation_verse: Elabe ame aɖe gblɔ be: ‘Eya mee míele agbe le heʋãna hafi le anyi.’ Esɔ kple nya si miaƒe hakpala aɖewo gblɔ be: ‘Eƒe dzidzimeviwo míawo hã míenye.’

english_verse: Since we are God's children, we must not think that he is like an idol made out of gold or silver or stone. He isn't like anything that humans have thought up and made.
translation_verse: Esi míawo hã míenye Mawu ƒe dzidzimeviwo ta la, mele be míabu be Mawu ƒe dzedzeme ɖe wòle abe sika, klosalo alo kpe si amegbetɔ bu tame wɔ aɖaŋutɔe le eƒe susu nu la ene o.

english_verse: In the past, God forgave all this because people did not know what they were doing. But now he says that everyone everywhere must turn to him.
translation_verse: Mawu ŋe aɖaba ƒu ɣeyiɣi si me amewo menyae o la dzi. Ke azɔ la, eɖe gbe be amewo katã natrɔ dzime le afi sia afi.

english_verse: He has set a day when he will judge the world's people with fairness. And he has chosen the man Jesus to do the judging for him. God has given proof of this to all of us by raising Jesus from death.
translation_verse: Eɖo ŋkeke ɖi be yegbɔna ame aɖe, si yetia la dzi to ge adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu ame siwo le xexea me la le dzɔdzɔenyenye nu. Mawu na amewo katã nya be yele esia wɔ ge godoo, esime wòfɔ ame la ɖe tsitre tso ame kukuwo dome.”

english_verse: As soon as the people heard Paul say a man had been raised from death, some of them started laughing. Others said, “We will hear you talk about this some other time.”
translation_verse: Esi Paulo ƒo nu le ame kukuwo ƒe tsitretsitsi ŋu la, ame aɖewo koe, ke bubuwo ya gblɔ be: “Míedi be nàgava ƒo nu na mí le nu sia ŋuti.”

english_verse: When Paul left the council meeting,
translation_verse: Tete Paulo dzo le takpeƒe la.

english_verse: some of the men put their faith in the Lord and went with Paul. One of them was a council member named Dionysius. A woman named Damaris and several others also put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Ame aɖewo tsi eŋu, eye woxɔe se. Ame siawo dometɔ ɖekae nye Dionisio, si nye aɖaŋuɖoƒea me nɔla ɖeka kple nyɔnu aɖe, si ŋkɔe nye Damaris, hekpe ɖe ame bubu aɖewo ŋu.

english_verse: Paul left Athens and went to Corinth,
translation_verse: Le nu siawo megbe la, Paulo dzo le Atene, eye wòva Korinto.

english_verse: where he met Aquila, a Jewish man from Pontus. Not long before this, Aquila had come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Emperor Claudius had ordered the Jewish people to leave Rome. Paul went to see Aquila and Priscilla
translation_verse: Edo go Yudatɔ aɖe, si ŋkɔe nye Akwila. Enye Pontotɔwo. Eya kple srɔ̃a Priskila tso Italia va Korinto eteƒe medidi o. Woʋu va afi sia, elabe Roma Fiagã Klaudio ɖe gbe be Yudatɔwo katã nadzo le Roma. Paulo yi ɖakpɔ wo ɖa,

english_verse: and found out they were tent makers. Paul was also a tent maker, so he stayed with them, and they worked together.
translation_verse: eye esi eya kple ame siawo nye avɔgbadɔwɔlawo ta la, enɔ wo gbɔ hewɔ dɔa kpli wo.

english_verse: Every Sabbath, Paul went to the synagogue. He spoke to Jews and Gentiles and tried to win them over.
translation_verse: Dzudzɔgbe ɖe sia ɖe la, edzroa nya me kple amewo le ƒuƒoƒe la, eye wòto esia wɔwɔ me na Yudatɔ kple Helatɔ geɖe trɔ susu va xɔ se.

english_verse: But after Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, he spent all his time preaching to the Jews about Jesus the Messiah.
translation_verse: Esi Sila kple Timoteo tso Makedonia va ɖo la, Paulo tsɔ mawunyagbɔgblɔ ɖo dɔe koŋ, eye wòɖi ɖase gblɔ na Yudatɔwo be Yesue nye Kristo la.

english_verse: Finally, they turned against him and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes and told them, “Whatever happens to you will be your own fault! I am not to blame. From now on I am going to preach to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Ke Yudatɔwo tsi tre ɖe eŋu kple busunyawo gbɔgblɔ. Ale Paulo ʋuʋu eƒe awuwo me, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Miaƒe fiƒode nenɔ miawo ŋutɔ mia dzi. Nye la, nyemeɖi fɔ aɖeke o. Tso azɔ heyina la, mayi ɖe ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la dome.”

english_verse: Paul then moved into the house of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Ale Paulo dzo le afi ma, eye wòyi ɖe ŋutsu aɖe, si ŋkɔe nye Tito Yusto la ƒeme. Ŋutsu sia nye mawuvɔ̃la si ƒe aƒe te ɖe ƒuƒoƒe la ŋu.

english_verse: Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and everyone in his family put their faith in the Lord. Many others in Corinth also heard the message, and all the people who had faith in the Lord were baptized.
translation_verse: Ke Krispo, ƒuƒoƒemegã la kple eƒemetɔwo katã xɔ Aƒetɔ la dzi se. Nenema ke Korintotɔ geɖe, siwo va se Paulo ƒe nyawo hã xɔe se, eye wole mawutsi na wo.

english_verse: One night, Paul had a vision, and in it the Lord said, “Don't be afraid to keep on preaching. Don't stop!
translation_verse: Gbe ɖeka zã la, Aƒetɔ la gblɔ na Paulo le ŋutega me be: “Mègavɔ̃ o. Ɖe gbeƒã nya la, eye mègazi ɖoɖoe o,

english_verse: I am with you, and you won't be harmed. Many people in this city belong to me.”
translation_verse: elabe meli kpli wò. Ame aɖeke matso ɖe ŋuwò awɔ nu vevi wò o, elabe ame geɖewo le du sia me nam.”

english_verse: Paul stayed on in Corinth for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.
translation_verse: Ale Paulo nɔ afi ma ƒe ɖeka kple afã eye wònɔ nu fiam le ameawo dome.

english_verse: While Gallio was governor of Achaia, some of the Jewish leaders got together and grabbed Paul. They brought him into court
translation_verse: Ke esi Galio va zu Romatɔwo ƒe dziɖula le Axaya-nutome la, Yudatɔwo sɔ nu, lé Paulo, eye wokplɔe yi ʋɔnui.

english_verse: and said, “This man is trying to make our people worship God in a way that is against our Law!”
translation_verse: Wotsɔ nya ɖe eŋu be: “Ame sia le amewo ƒe susu trɔm bene woasubɔ Mawu le mɔ si tsi tre ɖe se ŋu la nu.”

english_verse: Even before Paul could speak, Gallio said, “If you were charging this man with a crime or some other wrong, I would have to listen to you.
translation_verse: Ke esi Paulo di be yeaƒo nu la, Galio gblɔ na Yudatɔwo be: “Yudatɔwo, ne ɖe wònye nu gbegblẽ wɔwɔ aɖe ƒe nya alo hlɔ̃nya dziŋɔ aɖee mietsɔ vɛ la, magbɔ dzi ɖi adrɔ̃e na mi.

english_verse: But since this concerns only words, names, and your own law, you will have to take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters.”
translation_verse: Ke esi wònye miaƒe nyawo la dzixɔsenufiafia, ŋkɔwo kple miawo ŋutɔ miaƒe sewo ko ŋu wotsɔ ɖo ta la, miawo ŋutɔ mikpɔ egbɔ. Abe ʋɔnudrɔ̃la ene la, nyemelɔ̃na be madrɔ̃ nya siawo tɔgbe ƒe ʋɔnu o.”

english_verse: Then he sent them out of the court.
translation_verse: Ale Galio nyà wo doe le ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒea.

english_verse: The crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the Jewish leader, and beat him up in front of the court. But none of this mattered to Gallio. Paul Returns to Antioch in Syria
translation_verse: Tete wo katã wolé Sostene, ƒuƒoƒemegã la, eye woƒoe le ʋɔnua ŋkume. Ke Galio metsɔ ɖeke le nu si wowɔ la me o. Paulo trɔ yi Antioxia

english_verse: After Paul had stayed for a while with the Lord's followers in Corinth, he told them goodbye and sailed on to Syria with Aquila and Priscilla. But before he left, he had his head shaved at Cenchreae because he had made a promise to God.
translation_verse: Paulo nɔ nɔviawo gbɔ ŋkeke geɖe. Emegbe la, eklã wo, eye eya kple Priskila kpakple Akwila ɖo tɔdziʋu yi ɖe Siria. Hafi woadze mɔ tso Kenxrea la, Paulo lũ ta le adzɔgbe aɖe, si wòɖe la ta.

english_verse: The three of them arrived in Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He then went into the synagogue to talk with the people there.
translation_verse: Esi wova ɖo Efeso la, egblẽ Priskila kple Akwila ɖe afi ma. Ke eya ŋutɔ yi ɖe ƒuƒoƒe la ɖadzro nya me kple Yudatɔwo.

english_verse: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
translation_verse: Ameawo bia tso esi be wòanɔ yewo gbɔ ʋɛ, ke melɔ̃ o.

english_verse: He told them goodbye and said, “If God lets me, I will come back.”
translation_verse: Eklã wo eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Ne Mawu lɔ̃ la, magatrɔ va mia gbɔ.” Tete wòɖo tɔdziʋu tso Efeso dzo.

english_verse: Paul sailed to Caesarea, where he greeted the church. Then he went on to Antioch.
translation_verse: Esi wòɖi go ɖe Kaisarea la, eyi Yerusalem ɖado gbe na hame la, eye wòtso eme yi Antioxia.

english_verse: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
translation_verse: Paulo nɔ afi ma ɣeyiɣi aɖe eye wòdze mɔ yi ɖato Galatia kple Frigia nutowo me hedo ŋusẽ nusrɔ̃lawo katã. Apolo va Efeso kple Korinto

english_verse: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
translation_verse: Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, Yudatɔ aɖe, si ŋkɔe nye Apolo, eye wònye Aleksandria vidzidzia la va Efeso. Enya nuƒoƒo eye wònya mawunya hã nyuie.

english_verse: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be Yohanes ƒe mawutsilele ŋu ko wònya nu le hã la, wofia mɔ sinu Aƒetɔ la di be woanɔ agbe ɖo lae. Dzo le eme ŋutɔ eye wòɖea gbeƒã hefiaa nu le Yesu ŋu ɖe eteƒe tututu.

english_verse: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
translation_verse: Eƒo nu vɔvɔ̃ manɔmee le ƒuƒoƒe la. Esi Priskila kple Akwila ɖo to se eƒe nyawo la, wokplɔe yi wo ƒeme eye woɖe agbenɔnɔ si dze Mawu ŋu la me nɛ nyuie wu.

english_verse: Apollos decided to travel through Achaia. So the Lord's followers wrote letters, encouraging the followers there to welcome him. After Apollos arrived in Achaia, he was a great help to everyone who had put their faith in the Lord Jesus because of God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Apolo di be yeayi Axaya, ale nɔviawo do ŋusẽe eye woŋlɔ agbalẽ na nusrɔ̃lawo le afi ma be woaxɔe nyuie. Esi wòɖo la, ena kpekpeɖeŋu manyagblɔ ame siwo nu Mawu ve, wozu xɔsetɔwo la.

english_verse: He got into fierce arguments with the Jewish people, and in public he used the Scriptures to prove that Jesus is the Messiah.
translation_verse: Le nya siwo wòhe kple Yudatɔwo le dutoƒo me la, eɖe nya me kple ŋusẽ tɔxɛ heɖu Yudatɔwo ƒe nya dzi. Etsɔ mawunya ɖee fia kɔtɛe be Yesue nye Kristo la.

english_verse: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled across the hill country to Ephesus, where he met some of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Esime Apolo le Korinto la, Paulo to nuto la ƒe dzigbeme va ɖo Efeso. Edo go nusrɔ̃la aɖewo le afi ma.

english_verse: He asked them, “When you put your faith in Jesus, were you given the Holy Spirit?” “No!” they answered. “We have never even heard of the Holy Spirit.”
translation_verse: Ebia wo be: “Esi miezu xɔsetɔwo ɖe, miexɔ Gbɔgbɔ Kɔkɔe laa?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Míesee kpɔ gɔ̃ hã be Gbɔgbɔ Kɔkɔe aɖe li o.”

english_verse: “Then why were you baptized?” Paul asked. They answered, “Because of what John taught.”
translation_verse: Paulo bia wo be: “Ekema mawutsi ka tɔgbe wole na mi?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Yohanes ƒe mawutsie.”

english_verse: Paul replied, “John baptized people so they would turn to God. But he also told them someone else was coming, and they should put their faith in him. Jesus is the one that John was talking about.”
translation_verse: Paulo gblɔ be: “Yohanes le mawutsi na dzimetrɔlawo eye wògblɔ na ameawo be woaxɔ ame si le ye yome gbɔna la dzi ase. Ame siae nye Yesu.”

english_verse: After the people heard Paul say this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Esi ameawo se esia la, wona wole mawutsi na wo le Aƒetɔ Yesu ŋkɔ me.

english_verse: Then Paul placed his hands on them. The Holy Spirit was given to them, and they spoke unknown languages and prophesied.
translation_verse: Esi Paulo da asi ɖe wo dzi la, woxɔ Gbɔgbɔ Kɔkɔe la, eye wogblɔ gbe bubuwo, heɖe gbeƒã Mawu ƒe nya la hã.

english_verse: There were about twelve men in this group.
translation_verse: Ame siawo ƒe xexlẽme ade ŋutsu wui eve.

english_verse: For three months Paul went to the synagogue and talked bravely with the people about God's kingdom. He tried to win them over,
translation_verse: Paulo de ƒuƒoƒe la ɣleti etɔ̃ eye wòƒo nu ɖe nya me vɔvɔ̃ manɔmee hete kpɔ be yeatrɔ woƒe susu ɖe Mawu ƒe fiaɖuɖu ŋuti.

english_verse: but some of them were stubborn and refused to believe. In front of everyone they said terrible things about God's Way. Paul left and took the followers with him to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. He spoke there every day
translation_verse: Ke ame vlo aɖewo le ameawo dome, siwo sẽ dzime, eye womexɔe se o. Wogblɔ nya vlowo ɖe mɔ sinu Aƒetɔ la di be woanɔ agbe ɖo la ŋu le ƒuƒoƒe la me. Ale Paulo kplɔ nusrɔ̃laawo eye eya kple woawo wodzo le ha ma me. Woyi ɖe Tirano ƒe sukuxɔ me, afi si wòdzro nya me kpli wo le gbe sia gbe.

english_verse: for two years, until every Jew and Gentile in Asia had heard the Lord's message. The Sons of Sceva
translation_verse: Enɔ esia wɔwɔ dzi ƒe eve sɔŋ, ale be ame siwo katã nɔ Asia-nutome, eɖanye Yudatɔ alo Helatɔ o, wose Aƒetɔ la ƒe nya la. Skeva viŋutsuwo

english_verse: God gave Paul the power to work great miracles.
translation_verse: Mawu wɔ nukunu tɔxɛwo to Paulo dzi.

english_verse: People even took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul's body, and they carried them to everyone who was sick. All of the sick people were healed, and the evil spirits went out.
translation_verse: Ale be amewo tsɔa takuviwo kple akɔtawuiwo gɔ̃ hã ɖoa eŋu yina na dɔnɔwo eye woƒe lã me sẽna; gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo hã do le amewo me.

english_verse: Some Jewish men started going around trying to force out evil spirits by using the name of the Lord Jesus. They said to the spirits, “Come out in the name of that same Jesus that Paul preaches about!”
translation_verse: Azɔ Yudatɔ aɖewo, siwo tsana tso du me yi du me, eye wonyàa gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo doa goe le amewo me la hã te kpɔ tsɔ Aƒetɔ Yesu ŋkɔ, be yewoanyà gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo adoe. Wogblɔna be: “Mebe do go, le Yesu, ame si Paulo le gbeƒã ɖemee la ŋkɔ me!”

english_verse: Seven sons of a high priest named Sceva were doing this,
translation_verse: Nɔviŋutsu adrẽ aɖewo, siwo nye Yudatɔwo ƒe nunɔlagã Skeva viwo lae nɔ nu sia wɔm.

english_verse: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
translation_verse: Ke gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ la gblɔ na wo be: “Menya Yesu, menya Paulo hã, ke ame kae miawo ya mienye?”

english_verse: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and beat them up. They ran out of the house, naked and bruised.
translation_verse: Ame si me gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ la le la ti kpo dze wo dzi, wɔ fu wo heɖu wo katã dzi. Ede abi wo ŋu; ale wosí dzo le aƒe ma me amamae.

english_verse: When the Jews and Gentiles in Ephesus heard about this, they were so frightened that they praised the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Esi Yudatɔ kple Helatɔ siwo katã nɔ Efeso se nya sia la, vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo. Ale wotsɔ bubu na Aƒetɔ Yesu.

english_verse: Many who were followers now started telling everyone about the evil things they had been doing.
translation_verse: Xɔsetɔawo dometɔ geɖe va ʋu woƒe nuvɔ̃wo me eye wogblɔ nu siwo wowɔna la.

english_verse: Some who had been practicing witchcraft even brought their books and burned them in public. These books were worth about
translation_verse: Wo dometɔ siwo nye dzosalawo la lɔ woƒe agbalẽwo va kɔ ɖi, eye wotɔ dzo wo le ameha la ŋkume. Esi wowɔ akɔnta le agbalẽawo ƒe home ŋu la, wokpɔ be axɔ klosaloga akpe bla atɔ̃ sɔŋ.

english_verse: So the Lord's message spread and became even more powerful. The Riot in Ephesus
translation_verse: Ale Aƒetɔ la ƒe nya la tsi ɖe edzi hekeke ta ŋusẽtɔe. Zitɔtɔ le Efeso

english_verse: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
translation_verse: Le nu siawo megbe la, Gbɔgbɔ la na Paulo ɖoe be yeato Makedonia kple Axaya, ayi Yerusalem. Egblɔ be: “Ne meɖo afi ma la, ele be mayi aɖakpɔ Roma hã ɖa.”

english_verse: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
translation_verse: Ale wòdɔ eƒe kpeɖeŋutɔ eve, Timoteo kple Erasto, ɖe Makedonia, eye eya ŋutɔ tsi Asia-nutome vie.

english_verse: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
translation_verse: Ɣeyiɣi sia me lɔƒoe zi dziŋɔ aɖe tɔ le Efeso tso mɔ sinu Aƒetɔ la di be woanɔ agbe ɖo la ŋu.

english_verse: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
translation_verse: Klosalonutula aɖe li si ŋkɔe nye Demetrio. Ŋutsu sia tsɔa klosalo tua nyɔnumawu si ŋkɔe nye Artemis la ƒe mawuxɔ ƒe nɔnɔme na amewo. Dɔ sia hea viɖe geɖe ŋutɔ vanɛ na eƒe aɖaŋudɔwɔlawo.

english_verse: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
translation_verse: Eyɔ ame siawo kple dɔ sia ƒomevi wɔlawo katã ƒo ƒu, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Mía tɔwo, miawo ŋutɔ mienya be dɔ sia wɔwɔ me míetona kpɔa kesinɔnu geɖe.

english_verse: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
translation_verse: Nu si wɔm Paulo le la, miele esem hele ekpɔm ɖe. Ele gbɔgblɔm na amewo be mawu si wowɔ kple asi la, menye mawu wònye o. Egblɔ nya sia le Efeso kple Asia blibo la katã kpe ɖo vɔ kloe, eye wòdze agbagba trɔ ame geɖe ƒe susu woxɔ edzi se.

english_verse: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
translation_verse: Eya ta edze ƒãa be míaƒe dɔ sia gbɔna gbegblẽ ge. Menye esia ɖeɖe ko o, ke boŋ amewo magabu nyɔnumawu Artemis bubutɔ la ƒe mawuxɔ la ɖe naneke me kura o. Gawu la, bubu gã, si wotsɔna na Artemis la hã aklo le eŋu keŋkeŋ; evɔ wònye eyae nye mawu, si amewo katã subɔna le Asia blibo la kple xexea me godoo hafi.”

english_verse: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Esi ameawo se nya sia la, wodo dɔmedzoe, eye wodo ɣli gblɔ be: “Efesotɔwo ƒe Artemis ye nye gã!”

english_verse: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
translation_verse: Ale zi tɔ le dua me katã. Ameawo lé Gayo kple Aristarxo, Makedoniatɔ siwo nye Paulo ƒe mɔzɔhatiwo la. Wohe wo kple du yi dutakpeƒe la.

english_verse: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
translation_verse: Paulo di be yeage ɖe ameha la dome ayi ɖe dutakpeƒe la kpli wo, gake nusrɔ̃laawo meɖe mɔ nɛ o.

english_verse: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
translation_verse: Asia-megã aɖewo, siwo nye Paulo xɔlɔ̃wo la hã ɖo ame ɖee kple kukuɖeɖe be megayi o.

english_verse: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
translation_verse: Hoowɔwɔ xɔ takpeƒea katã. Ne ame si to afii, wòagblɔ nya ɖeka; ne bubu to afi mɛ, wòagblɔ bubu; elabe wo dometɔ geɖe menya nu si ta wova ƒo ƒu ɖo o.

english_verse: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
translation_verse: Ameawo dometɔ aɖewo doe ɖa be Aleksandro, ame si Yudatɔwo tsɔ ɖo ŋgɔ la, neƒo nu. Aleksandro di be yeaƒo nu, aɖe ye ɖokui nu na wo ale wòwɔ asi na wo be woazi ɖoɖoe.

english_verse: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Ke esi ameha la kpɔe dze sii be Yudatɔ wònye la, wo katã wode asi ɣlidodo me, abe gaƒoƒo eve sɔŋ ene kple gbe ɖeka be: “Efesotɔwo ƒe Artemis lae nye gã!”

english_verse: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
translation_verse: Mlɔeba la, dua ƒe agbalẽŋlɔla na ameha la zi ɖoɖoe, eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Nɔvinye Efesotɔwo, ame kae le mía dome afii, si menya be Efeso-du siae nye Artemis gã la ƒe mawuxɔ nɔƒe o? Ame kae menya hã be teƒe siae nye kpe kɔkɔe, si ge tso dziƒo la nɔƒe o?

english_verse: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
translation_verse: Ɖe ame aɖe ate ŋu agblɔ nya aɖe atsi tre ɖe nya siawo ŋua? Eya ta midze kɔ anyi kpoo, eye migawɔ naneke tame mabumabutɔe o.

english_verse: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
translation_verse: Ame siwo miekplɔ va afii la, womefi naneke le mawuxɔ la me o, eye womegblɔ busunya aɖeke hã ɖe míaƒe nyɔnumawu la ŋu o.

english_verse: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
translation_verse: Eya ta nenye be nya aɖe le Demetrio kple eƒe aɖaŋudɔwɔlawo si ɖe ame aɖe ŋu la, ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒewo li, eye dua dziɖulawo hã li. Mina woatsɔ nya ɖe wo nɔewo ŋu le afi ma.

english_verse: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
translation_verse: Ke ne nya bubu aɖe le mia si la, ekema woate ŋu adrɔ̃ eya le se nu le ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒea.

english_verse: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
translation_verse: Ne míekpɔ nyuie o la, woatsɔ nya ɖe mía ŋu le ʋunyaʋunya si dzɔ la ta. Evɔ la, míate ŋu agblɔ nu si ta koŋ míena zi tɔ alea gbegbe ɖo o.”

english_verse: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
translation_verse: Esi wògblɔ nya sia la, ena ameha la ka.

english_verse: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
translation_verse: Esi zitɔtɔ la nu tso le dua me la, Paulo yɔ nusrɔ̃lawo ƒo ƒu hexlɔ̃ nu wo. Eklã wo, eye wòdze mɔ ɖo ta Makedonia.

english_verse: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
translation_verse: Eto afi ma nutowo me hedo ŋusẽ amewo hafi va ɖo Hela-nyigba dzi.

english_verse: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
translation_verse: Enɔ afi ma ɣleti etɔ̃. Esi wònɔ dzadzram ɖo be yeayi Siria la, eva nya be Yudatɔwo ɖo nugbe ɖe ye ŋu, eya ta eɖoe be yeatrɔ ato Makedonia.

english_verse: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
translation_verse: Soparte, ame si nye Piro, Beroeatɔ la vi nɔ eŋuti. Ame bubu siwo hã gakplɔe yii la woe nye: Aristarxo kple Sekundo tso Tesalonika; Gayo, Derbetɔ kple Timoteo, Tixiko kple Trofimo tso Asia.

english_verse: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
translation_verse: Ame siawo do ŋgɔ henɔ mía lalam le Troa.

english_verse: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
translation_verse: Le Amɔwɔ Maʋamaʋã Ŋkekeawo ɖuɖu vɔ megbe la, míeɖo tɔdziʋu tso Filipi. Míenɔ tɔ dzi ŋkeke atɔ̃ hafi va tu wo le Troa, afi si míenɔ ŋkeke adrẽ. Paulo ɖi tsa yi Troa zi mamlɛtɔ

english_verse: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
translation_verse: Le kwasiɖa ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la, míeƒo ƒu be míaɖu nu ɖekae, eye Paulo ƒo nu na ameawo. Eƒo nu ʋuu va se ɖe zã titina ke, elabe eɖoe be ne ŋu ke la, yeadzo.

english_verse: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
translation_verse: Wosi akaɖi geɖe ɖe xɔ si me míeƒo ƒu ɖo le dziƒoxɔ dzi la me.

english_verse: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
translation_verse: Ɖekakpui aɖe, si ŋkɔe nye Eutixo la bɔbɔ nɔ fesre nu. Esi Paulo ƒe nuƒoa va didi alea la, Eutixo de asi alɔ̃dɔdɔ me. Edɔ alɔ̃ yi eme ʋĩi ale gbegbe be wòge tso dziƒoxɔ etɔ̃lia dzi va dze anyigba. Esi woyi ɖakɔe la, wokpɔ be eku.

english_verse: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
translation_verse: Paulo ɖi yi anyigba, bɔbɔ ɖe edzi hekpla asi ɖee. Egblɔ na wo be: “Migado boboe o. Agbe gale eme.”

english_verse: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, Paulo gatrɔ yi dziƒoxɔ la dzi, eye wòɖu nua kple etɔwo. Egayi edzi ƒo nu kpli wo ʋuu va se ɖe fɔŋli hafi dzo.

english_verse: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
translation_verse: Wokplɔ ɖekakpui la yi aƒeme agbagbee eye woƒe dzi dze eme ŋutɔ. Paulo tso le Troa yi Mileto

english_verse: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
translation_verse: Míedo ŋgɔ yi ɖe tɔdziʋua me, eye míedze mɔ ɖo ta Aso. Paulo na míenya do ŋgɔ be yele afɔ to ge atso mí le afi sia hafi aɖo ʋua kpli mí.

english_verse: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
translation_verse: Esi wòva tu mí le Aso la, eɖo ʋua kpli mí va Mitilene.

english_verse: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
translation_verse: Míeho tso afi ma va ɖo Xio kasa ŋufɔke. Esi ŋu ke la, míeva Samo, eye le ŋkeke si kplɔ ema ɖo dzi la, míeva ɖo Mileto.

english_verse: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
translation_verse: Paulo medi be yeagblẽ ɣeyiɣi le Asia o, eya ta eɖoe be yeato Efeso ŋu ayi, elabe ele kplakpla dzi be, ne yeate ŋui la, yeaɖo Yerusalem hafi ŋkeke bla atɔ̃lia le Paska la yome naɖo edzi. Paulo ƒe kaklãnyawo na Efeso-hamemegãwo

english_verse: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
translation_verse: Paulo dɔ ame tso Mileto ɖo ɖe Efeso be woayɔ hamemegãwo vɛ.

english_verse: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
translation_verse: Esi wova la, egblɔ na wo be: “Mienya ale si menɔ mia gbɔ ɣeyiɣiawo katã tso ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi, esi menyaɖo afɔ Asia-nutome ko.

english_verse: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
translation_verse: Ale si mebɔbɔ ɖokuinye ɖe anyi kple aɖatsi hesubɔ Aƒetɔ la le ɣeyiɣi sesẽ siwo katã me wotem kpɔ, esime Yudatɔwo ɖo nugbe ɖe ŋunye la, le nyanya na mi.

english_verse: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
translation_verse: Mienyae be meƒo nu hefia nu le dutoƒo eye mede aƒewo me hã ɖekaɖeka. Mewɔ nu siawo esi nyemedi be maɣla naneke, si akpe ɖe mia ŋu ɖe mi o ta.

english_verse: I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Mexlɔ̃ nu Yudatɔwo kple Helatɔwo siaa be woadzudzɔ nuvɔ̃ wɔwɔ ava Mawu gbɔ, eye woaxɔ Yesu mía Aƒetɔ dzi ase.

english_verse: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
translation_verse: Azɔ meyina ɖe Yerusalem, abe ale si Gbɔgbɔ Kɔkɔe la dii ene, eye nyemenya nu si le dzɔdzɔ ge ɖe dzinye le afi ma o.

english_verse: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nu si menya koe nye be, le du ɖe sia ɖe me la, Gbɔgbɔ Kɔkɔe la ɖenɛ fiam be woadem gaxɔ me, eye makpe fu le afi ma.

english_verse: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Ke nyemebu nye agbe, be enye nu vavã alo nu xɔasi aɖeke na nye ŋutɔ o. Nu si koe le vevie nam lae nye be mawu mɔzɔzɔ kple dɔ si Aƒetɔ Yesu ɖo nam be mawɔ la nu. Dɔ siae nye be maɖi ɖase le Nyanyui, si fia ale si Mawu ve mía nui la ŋu.

english_verse: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, menya be mi ame siwo dome menɔ heɖe gbeƒã fiaɖuɖu la ŋutinya la dome ame aɖeke magakpɔm o.

english_verse: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
translation_verse: Eya ta mele ɖase ɖim na mi egbe be, ne mia dometɔ aɖe tsrɔ̃ la, nyemeɖi fɔ kura o,

english_verse: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
translation_verse: elabe megblɔ nu siwo katã Mawu di be miawɔ la na mi.

english_verse: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
translation_verse: Eya ta mikpɔ miawo ŋutɔ mia ɖokui kple alẽha blibo la katã dzi. Gbɔgbɔ Kɔkɔe lae ɖo mi be mianye edzikpɔla. Milé be na Aƒetɔ ƒe hame si eya ŋutɔ ɖo kple Via ƒe ʋu la.

english_verse: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
translation_verse: Menyae be, ne medzo la, amegãxi wɔadãwo gbɔna mia dome ɖo ge, eye womakpɔ nublanui na alẽha la o.

english_verse: Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Amewo latso miawo ŋutɔ mia dome, ada alakpa ale be nusrɔ̃lawo nadze wo yome.

english_verse: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
translation_verse: Eya ta minɔ ŋudzɔ. Miɖo ŋku edzi be ƒe etɔ̃ sɔŋ ye menɔ mia dome, zã kple keli, tsɔ aɖatsi fia nu mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe.

english_verse: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, mele mia gblẽm ɖe Mawu si me, be wòatsɔ eƒe nya la ave mia nui. Amenuvenya sia ate ŋu ana miatsi ɖe edzi, eye mianyi dome kple ame siwo katã ŋuti wokɔ la.

english_verse: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
translation_verse: Ame aɖeke ƒe klosalo, sika, alo nudodo aɖeke mebiã ŋu nam o.

english_verse: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
translation_verse: Miawo ŋutɔ mienya be nye asi siae metsɔ wɔ dɔ hedi mía kple ame siwo kpe ɖe ŋunye la ƒe nuhiahiãwoe.

english_verse: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
translation_verse: Le nu sia nu me la, mefia mi be ele be ame nawɔ dɔ sesĩe alea, ahakpe ɖe ame siwo gbɔdzɔ la ŋu. Miɖo ŋku Aƒetɔ Yesu ƒe nya, si wògblɔ la dzi. Ebe: ‘Yayra le nunana ame me wu nuxɔxɔ.’ ”

english_verse: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
translation_verse: Esi Paulo wu eƒe nuƒoa nu la, eya kple ameawo katã dze klo, eye wodo gbe ɖa.

english_verse: Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him.
translation_verse: Ameawo katã fa avi, kpla asi kɔ nɛ hegbugbɔ nu nɛ.

english_verse: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_verse: Woxa nu vevie le esi wògblɔ na wo be womegale ye kpɔ ge azɔ o la ta. Woɖoe ɖa va ɖo tɔdziʋua gbɔ.

english_verse: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
translation_verse: Míeklã wo, eye míeho zɔ tẽe va ɖo Kos. Míeɖo Rodo ŋufɔke, eye tso afi ma la, míeva ɖo Patara.

english_verse: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
translation_verse: Míekpɔ tɔdziʋu aɖe si yina ɖe Foenisia le afi sia. Míeɖoe, eye míeho dzo.

english_verse: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
translation_verse: Emegbe la, míekpɔ Kipro le adzɔge ɖa. Míeɖee da ɖe miame lɔƒo, eye míeva ɖo Siria heɖi go ɖe Tiro, afi si ʋua le agba ɖe ge ɖo.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Ke esi míaƒe ɣeyiɣia de la, míedzo le wo gbɔ, eye míeyi míaƒe mɔzɔzɔ dzi. Esi míenɔ dzodzom la, woawo ŋutɔ, wo srɔ̃wo kple wo viwo ɖo mí ɖa ʋuu do le dua me va ɖo ƒuta. Míedze klo do gbe ɖa,

english_verse: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
translation_verse: eye míeklã wo. Míege ɖe ʋua me, eye woawo hã trɔ yi aƒeme.

english_verse: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
translation_verse: Míenɔ ƒu dzi tso Tiro va ɖo Ptolemai. Míedo gbe na nɔviawo le afi ma, eye míenɔ wo gbɔ ŋkeke ɖeka.

english_verse: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
translation_verse: Ŋufɔke la, míeva ɖo Kaisarea afi si míedze Filipo, Nyanyui gblɔla la ƒeme le. Ŋutsu sia nye ame adrẽ, siwo wotia abe kpeɖeŋutɔwo ene la dometɔ ɖeka.

english_verse: and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
translation_verse: Vinyɔnu ɖetugbi ene le esi. Wonye Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo.

english_verse: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
translation_verse: Esime míenɔ afi ma xɔ ŋkeke geɖe la, Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Agabo la tso Yudea va.

english_verse: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Esi wòva mía gbɔ la, etsɔ Paulo ƒe alidziblanu bla eya ŋutɔ ƒe afɔ kple asi hegblɔ be: “Gbɔgbɔ Kɔkɔe la gblɔ be: ‘Yudatɔ siwo le Yerusalem la le alidziblanu sia tɔ bla ge alea, eye woatsɔe ade asi na ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o.’ ”

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Esi mí kple ame bubu, siwo le afi ma la míese nya sia la, míeɖe kuku na Paulo be megayi Yerusalem o.

english_verse: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
translation_verse: Tete Paulo gblɔ be: “Nu kae nye esi wɔm miele? Nu ka ƒe avi fam miele hele dzi gbãm nam? Nye la, nyemedzra ɖo be woadem gaxɔ me ɖeɖe ko le Yerusalem o, ke boŋ be maku le afi ma gɔ̃ hã, le Aƒetɔ Yesu ta.”

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: Esi wògbe be yemaxɔ míaƒe nyawo o la, míedzudzɔ fuɖeɖe nɛ hegblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ la ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu neva eme.”

english_verse: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke siawo megbe la, míedzra ɖo eye míeyi Yerusalem.

english_verse: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
translation_verse: Nusrɔ̃la aɖewo hã tso Kaisarea yi kpli mí. Wokplɔ mí yi ɖe nusrɔ̃la xoxo aɖe, si ŋkɔe nye Mnason tso Kipro la, ƒeme be míadze egbɔ. Paulo yi ɖakpɔ Yakobo ɖa

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: Esi míeɖo Yerusalem la, nɔviawo xɔ mí kple dzidzɔ.

english_verse: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
translation_verse: Ŋufɔke la, Paulo zɔ kpli mí yi be yeaɖakpɔ Yakobo ɖa. Hamemetsitsiwo katã hã va afi ma.

english_verse: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Esi wose eƒe nyawo la, wokafu Mawu. Azɔ la, wogblɔ nɛ be: “Mía nɔvi, èle esema? Yudatɔ akpe nane siwo zu xɔsetɔwo la katã lé Mose ƒe sea me ɖe asi sesĩe.

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: Wogblɔ na wo tso ŋuwò be ègblɔ na Yudatɔ, siwo le ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la dome, be woaɖe asi le Mose ƒe sea ŋuti. Gawu la, wobe ègagblɔ hã be womegatso aʋa alo nyi woƒe kɔwo o.

english_verse: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
translation_verse: Wole ese ge godoo, be nèva. Nu kae míawɔ fifia?

english_verse: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
translation_verse: Eya ta wɔ nu si gblɔ ge míala na wò la. Ŋutsu ene le mía dome, ame siwo ɖe adzɔgbe.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Kplɔ wo, ne nàyi aɖakɔ ɖokuiwò ŋu kpli wo, eye nàxe woƒe nugblẽfewo, ale be woate ŋu alũ ta. Ale ame sia ame anya be nu si wose le ŋuwò la, menye nyateƒe o, ke boŋ wò ŋutɔ hã, èle sea dzi wɔm.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Ke le xɔsetɔ siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la gome ya la, míeŋlɔ agbalẽ gblɔ ɖo ɖe wo be míeɖoe be woatsri nuɖuɖu si wotsɔ savɔe na trɔ̃wo. Woatsri ʋuɖuɖu kple lã si me ʋu tsi la ɖuɖu. Womegawɔ ahasi o.”

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Ale Paulo kplɔ ameawo dzoe. Esi ŋu ke la, eyi ɖakɔ eɖokui ŋu kpli wo. Eyi ɖe mawuxɔ la me, eye wòɖe gbeƒã ŋkeke si dzi ŋutikɔɣi la awu enu, eye woana vɔsanu ɖe wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ta la. Wolé Paulo le mawuxɔ la me

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Esi wòsusɔ ʋɛ ne ŋkeke adrẽa nawu enu la, Yudatɔ aɖewo, siwo tso Asia va la kpɔ Paulo le mawuxɔ la me. Wode zi ameha blibo la me, eye wolé Paulo.

english_verse: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Wodo ɣli be: “Israel-ŋutsuwo, minya aƒe na mí loo! Ame si le tsatsam le nu fiam le afi sia afi tsɔ le ta gblẽm le amewo katã nu lae nye esi! Eyae tsi tre ɖe dukɔ la, Mose ƒe se la kple teƒe sia ŋu! Ekplɔ Helatɔ aɖewo gɔ̃ hã va mawuxɔa me. Eƒo ɖi teƒe kɔkɔe sia!”

english_verse: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
translation_verse: Do ŋgɔ la, wokpɔ Paulo kple Trofimo, Efesotɔ la, le dua me, eye wobu be Paulo kplɔe yi ɖe mawuxɔa me.

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Zi tɔ le du blibo la katã me hoo, eye amewo katã do kple du va lé Paulo, eye wohee do go le mawuxɔa me hetu ʋɔawo enumake.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Esime ameawo di be yewoawu Paulo la, nya la ɖo Romatɔwo ƒe aʋakplɔlagã la gbɔ be zi tɔ le Yerusalem-dua katã me.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: Eɖe asrafo kple aʋakplɔla aɖewo kpe ɖe eɖokui ŋu enumake, eye woƒu du yi ɖe teƒe la. Esi ameawo kpɔ aʋakplɔlagã la kple asrafoawo la, wodzudzɔ Paulo ƒoƒo.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Aʋakplɔlagã la te ɖe Paulo ŋu eye wòlée. Eɖe gbe be woablae kple kɔsɔkɔsɔ eve. Azɔ la, ebia be: “Ame kae nye esia? Nu kae wòwɔ?”

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: Ke amehawo nɔ ɣli dom nɔ nyawo gblɔm hoo. Ne ame si gblɔ ale, ame bubu hã nagblɔ nya bubu. Ʋunyaʋunya la nu sẽ ale gbegbe be aʋakplɔlagã la mete ŋu nya nu si tutu dzɔ o. Ale wòɖe gbe be woakplɔ Paulo ayi ɖe mɔ́ la me.

english_verse: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
translation_verse: Esi wova ɖo atrakpuiawo nu la, ehiã be asrafoawo nakɔ Paulo ɖe ya me, elabe amehawo nɔ nyanyram ŋɔdzitɔe.

english_verse: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
translation_verse: Ameawo katã kplɔe ɖo hoo kple ɣli be: “Miwui!” Paulo ʋli eɖokui ta

english_verse: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi asrafoawo kplɔ Paulo yina gege ge ɖe mɔ́ la me la, ebia aʋakplɔlagã la be: “Meɖe kuku, àɖe mɔ magblɔ nya aɖe na wòa?” Aʋakplɔlagã la biae be: “Ɖe nèse Hela-gbea?

english_verse: “Aren't you that Egyptian who started a riot not long ago and led
translation_verse: Ke menye wòe nye Egiptetɔ ma, si na zi tɔ le ŋkeke siawo me, eye wòkplɔ hlɔ̃dola akpe ene sɔŋ do yi gbedzi oa?”

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Tete Paulo ɖo eŋu be: “Nye la, Yudatɔwoe menye tso Tarso le Kilikia. Du mafeleŋua me vie menye. Taflatsɛ, ɖe mɔ nam be maƒo nu na ameawo.”

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Aʋakplɔlagã la ɖe mɔ nɛ. Ale Paulo tsi tsitre ɖe atrakpuia dzi wɔ asi na ameawo be woazi ɖoɖoe. Ɖoɖoe zi, eye wòƒo nu na wo le Hebri-gbe me gblɔ be:

english_verse: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
translation_verse: Esi wose be Hebri-gbe dom wòle la, wogazi ɖoɖoe ɖe edzi wu tsã. Tete Paulo yi edzi gblɔ be:

english_verse: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
translation_verse: “Yudatɔe menye. Wodzim le Tarso le Kilikia, gake Yerusalem afii wonyim le eye menye Gamaliel ƒe nusrɔ̃vi. Wofia mía tɔgbuiwo ƒe se lam tsitotsito, eye mesubɔa Mawu kple vevidodo, abe ale si miawo hã miele esubɔmee egbe ene.

english_verse: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
translation_verse: Meti ame siwo le mɔ sia dzi tom la yome vevie, hedi ku gɔ̃ hã na wo. Melé ŋutsu kple nyɔnu geɖe bla he va de gaxɔ me.

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: Nunɔlagã la kple ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo katã ate ŋu aɖi ɖase be nyateƒe tom mele. Woawo gbɔe mexɔ agbalẽ tsoe yina na mía nɔvi Yudatɔ siwo le Damasko. Medze mɔ yina be malé ame siwo le afi ma hã abla ahakplɔ va Yerusalem bene woahe to na wo. Paulo gblɔ eƒe dzimetɔtrɔ ŋutinya (Dɔw

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: “Esi mele mɔ dzi te tu Damasko abe ŋdɔ ga wui eve me ene la, kekeli sesẽ aɖe tso dziƒo klẽ ƒo xlãm zi ɖeka.

english_verse: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: Medze anyi, eye mese gbe aɖe ɖi biam be: ‘Saulo! Saulo! Nu ka ta nèle yonyeme tim?’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
translation_verse: Mebia be: ‘Wò ame kae, Aƒetɔ?’ Eɖo eŋu nam be: ‘Nye Yesu Nazaretetɔ, ame si yome tim nèle lae.’

english_verse: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
translation_verse: Ame siwo le mɔ zɔm kplim la kpɔ keklẽ la, gake womese ame si nɔ nu ƒo nam la ƒe gbe o.

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: Mebia be: ‘Aƒetɔ, nu ka mawɔ?’ eye Aƒetɔ la gblɔ nam be: ‘Tso nàyi Damasko-dua me, eye woagblɔ nu siwo katã woɖo ɖi be nàwɔ la na wò.’

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: Le ale si ŋutikɔkɔe kekeli sia sẽ ŋui ta la, mede nu kpɔ ge do kpo. Ale ame siwo le mɔ zɔm kplim la lé nye alɔnu hekplɔm va Damasko.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: “Ŋutsu aɖe, si ŋkɔe nye Anania la le dua me. Enye mawuvɔ̃la, ame si lé míaƒe se la me ɖe asi sesĩe, eye Yudatɔ siwo katã le dua me la ƒo nu nyui le eŋu.

english_verse: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
translation_verse: Ame sia va tsi tsitre ɖe gbɔnye gblɔ be: ‘Nɔvi Saulo, gakpɔ nu!’ Enumake megakpɔ nu, eye mekpɔ eyama.

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: ‘Mía tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu la tia wò ɖi be nànya eƒe lɔlɔ̃nu, nàdze si Dzɔdzɔetɔ la, eye nàse nya tso eya ŋutɔ ƒe nu me.

english_verse: You must tell everyone what you have seen and heard.
translation_verse: Elabe àzu eƒe ɖasefo le nu si nèse kple nu si nèkpɔ la ŋuti na amewo katã.

english_verse: What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Azɔ, nu ka lalam nèle? Tsi tre, do gbe ɖa nɛ, ne woale mawutsi na wò, aklɔ wò nuvɔ̃wo ɖa.’ Woyɔ Paulo be wòagblɔ mawunya na ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la

english_verse: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
translation_verse: “Metrɔ yi Yerusalem, eye esime menɔ gbe dom ɖa le mawuxɔ la me la,

english_verse: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
translation_verse: mekpɔ Aƒetɔ la le ŋutega me wògblɔ nam be: ‘Wɔ kaba nàdo le Yerusalem-dua me, elabe du sia me nɔlawo mexɔ wò ɖaseɖiɖi le ŋutinye o.’

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: Meɖo eŋu be: ‘Aƒetɔ, woawo ŋutɔ nya nyuie be meyina ƒuƒoƒe ɖe sia ɖe ɖaléa ame siwo xɔ dziwò se la, ƒoa wo hedea wo gaxɔ me.

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: Esi wowu wò ɖaseɖila Stefano la, nye hã mele tsitre ɖe afi ma, eye melɔ̃ ɖe edzi be woawui. Nyee kpɔ ewulawo ƒe awuwo gɔ̃ hã dzi.’

english_verse: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ke Aƒetɔ la gblɔ nam be: ‘Heyi, elabe maɖo wò ɖe keke ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la dome ʋĩi ke.’ ”

english_verse: The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.”
translation_verse: Ameawo ɖo to Paulo ʋuu va se ɖe nya sia dzi, kasia wogade asi ɣlidodo me sesĩe be: “Miɖe ame sia tɔgbe ɖa le xexea me! Medze be wòanɔ agbe o!”

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: Wodo ɣli bobobo, dze woƒe awuwo eye wolɔ ke hlẽ ɖe ya me.

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: Aʋakplɔlagã la ɖe gbe be woakplɔ Paulo ayi ɖe mɔ́ la me. Egblɔ be woneƒoe ne wòato nyateƒe bene yeanya nu si ta amehawo nɔ ɣli dom ɖe eta nenema.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: Ke esi woblae be woaƒo la, Paulo bia aʋakplɔla si le tsitre ɖe egbɔ la be: “Se ɖe mɔ be miaƒo Romatɔ, si womebu fɔe o la kple atam mahã?”

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Esi aʋakplɔla la se esia la, eyi ɖe aʋakplɔlagã la gbɔ hebiae be: “Nu kae nèbe yeawɔ? Kpɔ ɖa, Romatɔe nye ame sia lo!”

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Ale aʋakplɔlagã la va Paulo gbɔ, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Gblɔe nam. Romatɔ nènyea?” Paulo ɖo eŋu be: “Ẽ.”

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Aʋakplɔlagã la gblɔ be: “Nye la, ga home gã aɖe metsɔ ƒle nye Romatɔnyenye.” Paulo gblɔ be: “Nye la, ɖe wodzim ɖe eme.”

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Tete ame siwo be yewoaƒoe abia eƒe numenya ase la dzo le egbɔ enumake. Azɔ vɔvɔ̃ ɖo aʋakplɔlagã la elabe edze sii be Paulo nye Romatɔ, hekpe ɖe esia ŋu la eblae ɖe ka me. Wokplɔ Paulo va ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ŋkume
