english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Aʋakpɔlagã la di be yeanya nu si ta Yudatɔwo tsɔ nya ɖe Paulo ŋuti godoo. Ale esi ŋu ke la, ena woɖee le gaxɔa me, eye wòɖe gbe be nunɔlagãwo kple ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo katã nakpe ta. Ekplɔe vɛ, eye wòna Paulo tsi tsitre ɖe wo ŋkume.

english_verse: Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
translation_verse: Paulo lé ŋku ɖe ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo dzi henɔ wo kpɔm tututu, eye wògblɔ be: “Nɔvinyewo, menɔ agbe kple dzitsinya nyui le Mawu ŋkume va se ɖe egbe.”

english_verse: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
translation_verse: Tete nunɔlagã Anania ɖe gbe na ame siwo te ɖe Paulo ŋu la be woaƒo nu gbɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
translation_verse: Ke Paulo gblɔ nɛ be: “Mawu aƒo wò. Wò gli si wosi akalo na! Wò la, èbɔbɔ nɔ anyi be yeadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu ɖe se nu, ke wò ŋutɔ nèda se la dzi ɖe gbe be woaƒom.”

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Ame si te ɖe Paulo ŋu la gblɔ nɛ be: “Ã, Mawu ƒe nunɔlagã dzum nèlea?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
translation_verse: Paulo ɖo eŋu be: “Nɔvinyewo, nyemenya be eyae nye nunɔlagã o elabe woŋlɔ ɖi be: ‘Mègagblɔ nya vlo ɖe wò dukɔdziɖula ŋu o.’ ”

english_verse: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
translation_verse: Esi Paulo kpɔ dze sii be ameawo dometɔ aɖewo nye Zadukitɔwo, eye bubuwo hã nye Farisitɔwo la, egblɔ sesĩe le ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe la be: “Nɔvinyewo, nye la, Farisitɔ menye henye Farisitɔ viŋutsuvi. Mɔkpɔkpɔ si le asinye be ame kukuwo latsi tsitre tae wohem va ʋɔnu afii ɖo.”

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: Esi wògblɔ nya sia ko la, nyaʋiʋli ɖo Farisitɔ kple Zadukitɔ, siwo le afi ma la dome. Ale takpekpe la ma ɖe eve,

english_verse: The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these,
translation_verse: elabe Zadukitɔwo gblɔna be ame kukuwo metsia tsitre o, eye mawudɔlawo kple gbɔgbɔwo hã meli o, ke Farisitɔwo ya xɔ nu siawo katã dzi se.

english_verse: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
translation_verse: Ale ɣlidodo la gasẽ ɖe edzi wu tsã. Agbalẽfiala siwo le Farisitɔwo ƒe akpa dzi la, tsi tsitre ʋli nya la gblɔ be: “Míekpɔ vodada aɖeke le ame sia ŋu o. Nu kae gblẽ be gbɔgbɔ alo mawudɔla aɖee ƒo nu kplii?”

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Nyaʋiʋli la nu va sesẽ ale gbegbe be aʋakplɔlagã la vɔ̃ be wole Paulo vuvu ge. Eya ta eɖe gbe na asrafoawo be woaɖi ayi ɖakplɔe sesẽtɔe le ameawo dome ava mɔ́ la me.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: Zã ma me la, Aƒetɔ la tsi tsitre ɖe Paulo gbɔ gblɔ be: “Lé dzi ɖe ƒo. Ale si nèɖi ɖase le ŋunye le Yerusalem afii la, ele be nàgawɔ nenema ke le Roma hã.” Yudatɔwo ɖo be yewoawu Paulo

english_verse: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
translation_verse: Tete woyi ɖe nunɔlagã la kple dumegãwo gbɔ gblɔ be: “Míeka atam be ne míewu Paulo o kpa, míaɖu naneke o.

english_verse: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
translation_verse: Eya ta mi kpakple ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo miɖo ame ɖe aʋakplɔlagã, be wòakplɔ Paulo vɛ na mi, abe ɖe miedi be yewoagase nya la me tsitotsito wu tsã ene. Míawo míele klalo be kaka wòaɖo afii la, míawui.”

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Ke Paulo nyruiyɔvi aɖe se ale si ameawo de xa ɖe eŋui. Ege ɖe mɔ́ la me, eye wòfi tofi na Paulo.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
translation_verse: Tete Paulo yɔ aʋakplɔlaawo dometɔ ɖeka hegblɔ nɛ be: “Kplɔ ɖekakpui sia yi ɖe aʋakplɔlagã la gbɔe elabe nya aɖe le esi wòdi be yeagblɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
translation_verse: Ale aʋakplɔla la kplɔe yi ɖe aʋakplɔlagã la gbɔ, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Paulo, gamenɔla la yɔm, eye wòbia tso asinye be makplɔ ɖekakpui sia va gbɔwòe, elabe nya aɖe le esi wòdi be yeagblɔ na wò.”

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Aʋakplɔlagã la lé ɖekakpuia ƒe alɔnu, kplɔe ɖe kpɔe hebiae be: “Nya kae le asiwò nèbe yeagblɔ nam?”

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: Egblɔ be: “Yudatɔwo ƒe amegãwo ɖoe be yewoabia wò be etsɔ la, nàkplɔ Paulo va ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe la, abe ɖe wodi be yewoagase eƒe nya la me nyuie wu ene.

english_verse: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
translation_verse: Aʋakplɔlagã la de se nɛ be: “Mègagblɔe na ame aɖeke be yegblɔ nya sia nam o.” Emegbe la, edo mɔ ɖekakpui la wòdzo. Woɖo Paulo ɖe mɔ́mefia Felike gbɔ

english_verse: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
translation_verse: Midi sɔ na Paulo hã ne wòado. Mikpɔ egbɔ be wòaɖo mɔ́mefia Felike gbɔ dedie.”

english_verse: The commander wrote a letter that said:
translation_verse: Aʋakplɔlagã la ŋlɔ agbalẽ si gbɔna la ɖo ɖe mɔ́mefia la:

english_verse: Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
translation_verse: “Bubutɔgã Mɔ́mefia Felike, nye Klaudio Lisia ye ŋlɔ agbalẽ sia ɖo ɖe wò. Medo gbe na wò nyuie.

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Yudatɔwo lé ŋutsu sia, eye wode ewu ge kloe. Ke mía kple asrafowo míeva ke ɖe wo ŋuti xɔe le wo si. Míeva nya be Romatɔ wònye.

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: Medi be manya nu si wòwɔ hafi wolée, eya ta mekplɔe yi ɖe woƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ŋkume.

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: Ke meva kpɔe dze sii be mele be woawui, alo adee gaxɔ me gɔ̃ hã o, elabe nya si wotsɔ ɖe eŋu la ku ɖe woawo ŋutɔ ƒe sewo ŋu.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: Ke esi wova fi tofi nam be Yudatɔ aɖewo ɖo nugbe ɖe eŋu la, meɖoe be maɖoe ɖe gbɔwò enumake. Megblɔ na ame siwo le enu tsom la be woava gblɔ nya si le wo si ɖe eŋu la na wò. Nɔ anyi sesĩe!”

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Asrafoawo wɔ nu si wogblɔ na wo la dzi pɛpɛpɛ, eye wokplɔ Paulo va Antipatre zã ma me ke.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, asrafo afɔzɔlawo gbugbɔ va mɔ́ la me, ke sɔdolawo ya yi kple Paulo.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: Wokplɔe va Kaisarea, eye wotsɔ agbalẽ la na mɔ́mefia la hekplɔ Paulo de esi.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: Mɔ́mefia la xlẽ agbalẽ la, eye wòbia nuto si me wòtso la ta se. Esi wòva nya be Kilikia wòtso la,

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: egblɔ be: “Ne nuwòtsolawo hã va ɖo la, mase nya si le asiwò.” Azɔ la, ena be woadzɔ Paulo ŋu le mɔ́mefia Herodes ƒe fiasã la me.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke atɔ̃ megbe la, nunɔlagã Anania kple amegã aɖewo kpakple nyanuɖela Tertulo, va Kaisarea. Wotsɔ nya si wotsɔ ɖe Paulo ŋu la ɖo mɔ́mefia Felike ŋkume.

english_verse: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
translation_verse: Tete woyɔ Paulo vɛ, eye Tertulo he woƒe nutsonya la ɖe go gblɔ be: “Míaƒe Bubutɔgã Felike! To dziwò la, tomefafa blibo le mía dome. Èna be wole nu geɖewo ɖɔm ɖo na míaƒe dukɔ sia.

english_verse: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
translation_verse: Míekpɔ ŋudzedze le nu siawo katã ŋu le afi sia afi. Eya ta tɔwòe nye akpe.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: Nyemedi be magblẽ ɣeyiɣi geɖe na wò o, eya ta meɖe kuku be nànyo dɔme ase nya kpui si le mía si la.

english_verse: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
translation_verse: Míekpɔ ŋutsu sia be enye nugblẽla vɔ̃ɖi aɖe. Eyama le ʋunyaʋunya hem de Yudatɔwo dome le xexea me godoo. Eganye Nazarete-ha tatra me nɔlawo ƒe ŋgɔnɔla vloe ɖeka.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: Nenye be wò ŋutɔ èbia gbee ko la, èle nu siwo katã ta míele enu tsom la nya ge.”

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Yudatɔwo katã lɔ̃ ɖe edzi be nutsonyaawo katã le eme tututu. Paulo ʋli eɖokui ta le Felike ŋkume

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, mɔ́mefia la wɔ asi na Paulo be wòaƒo nu. Tete Paulo gblɔ be: “Mekpɔe dze sii be ènye ʋɔnudrɔ̃la le dukɔ sia me ƒè geɖee. Eya ta mele ɖokuinye ta ʋlim dzidzɔtɔe.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: Abe ale si nànya nyuie ene la, anɔ abe ŋkeke wui evee nye esi, meyi Yerusalem be masubɔ Mawu le afi ma.

english_verse: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
translation_verse: Womekpɔm mele nya ʋlim kple ame aɖeke o. Womekpɔm mede zi ameha aɖeke me le mawuxɔa me loo, ƒuƒoƒeawo loo, alo le dua ƒe akpa aɖeke o.

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: Kpɔɖeŋu aɖeke hã mele wo si si woate ŋu atsɔ aɖo kpe woƒe nya siwo wotsɔ ɖe ŋunye la dzi na wò o.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Ke le agbenɔnɔ si wole yɔyɔm be xɔse tatra ƒe nya me ya la, mesubɔa mía tɔgbuiwo ƒe Mawu la pɛpɛpɛ, eye mexɔ nu siwo katã le sea me kple esiwo Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo ŋlɔ ɖi la dzi se.

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: Enye nye mɔkpɔkpɔ be Mawu lava fɔ nu nyui wɔla kple nu baɖa wɔla siaa ɖe tsitre. Mɔkpɔkpɔ sia kee le ame siawo hã si.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Mɔkpɔkpɔ sia tae meʋlina vevie be dzitsinya nyui nanɔ asinye le Mawu kple amegbetɔwo siaa ŋkume.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: “Azɔ le ƒe aɖewo megbe, esi medzo le Yerusalem la, megatrɔ yi afi ma be matsɔ nunanawo ayi na nye dukɔmetɔwo, eye masa vɔ hã.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: Esime menɔ ŋutikɔkɔ kɔnu la wɔm le mawuxɔa me la, wokpɔm. Ameha aɖeke menɔ gbɔnye o, eye ʋunyaʋunya aɖeke hã menɔ anyi o.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Ke Yudatɔ aɖewo tso Asia-nutome nɔ afi ma. Woawo boŋ wòle be woava gbɔwò afii, eye ne nya aɖe le wo si ɖe ŋunye la, woatsɔ ɖe ŋunye hafi.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Alo àte ŋu ana ame siawo nagblɔ fɔ si wobum, esime medo ɖe ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ŋkume va yi.

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: Nya ɖeka, si medo ɣli gblɔ esime mele tsitre ɖe wo ŋkume la koe nye be: ‘Nu si ta wole ʋɔnu drɔ̃mem le afii egbe ɖoe nye be mexɔe se be ame kukuwo latsi tsitre.’ ”

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Tete Felike, ame si nya nu tso mɔ sinu Aƒetɔ la di be woanɔ agbe ɖo ŋu nyuie la, tɔ nyadɔdrɔ̃ la ɖe afi ma gblɔ be: “Ne aʋakplɔlagã Lisia va ɖo la, matso miaƒe nya la me.”

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: Eɖe gbe na aʋakplɔla la be wòakpɔ Paulo dzi, ne wòanɔ dedie, ke nena ablɔɖe aɖe sinui. Ne nane hiãe la, neɖe mɔ xɔlɔ̃awo nawɔe nɛ faa. Paulo le Felike kple Drusila ŋkume

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke aɖewo megbe la, Felike kple srɔ̃a Drusila, si nye Yudatɔ la, va. Edɔ ame wòyi ɖayɔ Paulo vɛ, eye Paulo ƒo nu tso Kristo Yesu dzixɔse ŋu nɛ wòse.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Ke esi Paulo ƒo nu tso dzɔdzɔenyenye, ɖokuidziɖuɖu kple ʋɔnudrɔ̃gbe si lava la ŋu la, Felike vɔ̃, eye wògblɔ be: “Heyi gbɔ, ne mekpɔ vovo la, magayɔ wò.”

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: Enɔ mɔ kpɔm le ɣeyiɣi sia me hã be Paulo ana ga ye. Ale edɔa ame woɖayɔnɛ vɛ enuenu wòɖoa dze kplii.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Le ƒe eve megbe la, Felike dzo, eye Porkio Festo va zu mɔ́mefia ɖe eteƒe. Ke esi Felike di be yeadze Yudatɔwo ŋu ta la, egblẽ Paulo ɖe gaxɔa me.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Azɔ Festo va ɖo eƒe dziɖuƒe la eye le ŋkeke etɔ̃ megbe la, etso Kaisarea yi Yerusalem.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Nunɔlagãwo kple Yudatɔwo ƒe amegãwo yi ɖagblɔ nya si wotsɔ ɖe Paulo ŋuti la nɛ.

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: Woɖe kuku nɛ be wòanyo dɔme ana woakplɔ Paulo ava Yerusalem, elabe woɖo nugbe ɖe eŋu be yewoade xa ɖi awui le mɔ dzi.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Festo ɖo eŋu na wo be: “Paulo le gaxɔ me le Kaisarea fifia, eye nye ŋutɔ hã mele tɔtrɔ ge ayi afi ma kpuie.

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: Mina miaƒe amegãwo nazɔ kplim ayi Kaisarea, eye ne nya aɖe le mia si ɖe ŋutsua ŋu la, woava tso enu le afi ma.”

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Festo tsi wo gbɔ abe ŋkeke enyi va se ɖe ewo ene, eye wòtrɔ yi ɖe Kaisarea. Esi ŋu ke la, ebɔbɔ nɔ ʋɔnudrɔ̃zikpui la dzi, eye wòɖe gbe be woakplɔ Paulo vɛ.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Paulo va ɖo, eye Yudatɔ siwo tso Yerusalem va la ƒo xlãe. Wotso enu kple nya vevi geɖewo gake kpɔɖeŋu aɖeke menɔ wo si wotsɔ ɖo kpe nutsotsoawo dzi o.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: Tete Paulo ʋli eɖokui ta gblɔ be: “Nyemeda le Yudatɔwo ƒe se la dzi, alo ƒo ɖi mawuƒe la, alo wɔ vɔ̃ ɖe Roma Fiagã la ŋu o.”

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Ke Festo di be yeadé Yudatɔwo dzi eya ta ebia Paulo be: “Èdi be yeayi Yerusalem, be woadrɔ̃ nya siawo na wò le gbɔnyea?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Tete Paulo ɖo eŋu gblɔ be: “Roma Fiagã la ŋutɔ ƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒee mele tsitre ɖo, eye afi siae wòle be woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnum le. Abe ale si wò ŋutɔ nènya nyuie ene la, nyemewɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke ɖe Yudatɔwo ŋu o.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: Nenye nu baɖa wɔla menye, eye mewɔ nane si ta wòle be woawum ɖo la, nyemegbe ku o. Evɔ nenye be nyemewɔ nu siwo wobe mewɔ la ƒe ɖeke o la, ame aɖeke mekpɔ mɔ aɖe asi le ŋunye na wo o. Medi be Roma Fiagã la ŋutɔ natso nya me nam.”

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Azɔ esi Festo kple eƒe aɖaŋuɖolawo dzro nya sia me la, eɖo eŋu be: “Roma Fiagã ŋutɔ nèbe nèdrɔ̃ nya na ye; àyi Roma Fiagã gbɔ.” Festo ƒo nu le Paulo ŋu na Agripa

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke aɖewo megbe la, fia Agripa kple Bernike va Kaisarea be yewoado dzaa na Festo.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Wonɔ afi ma ŋkeke geɖe, eya ta Festo tsɔ Paulo ƒe nya la ɖo fia la ŋkume. Egblɔ nɛ be: “Felike gblẽ ŋutsu aɖe ɖe gaxɔ me le afii hafi dzo.

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: Esi meyi Yerusalem la, Yudatɔwo ƒe nunɔlagãwo kple dumegãwo tsɔ nya ɖe ŋutsua ŋu, eye wobia tso asinye be mabu fɔe.

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: Ke meɖo eŋu na wo be le Romatɔwo ƒe dekɔnu nu la, ne ame aɖe tsɔ nya ɖe ehavi ŋu la, womebua fɔ ame si ŋu wotsɔ nya ɖo la o. Negbe akpa eveawo ɖe wodo go ŋkume kple ŋkume, eye ame si ŋu wotsɔ nya ɖo la ʋli eɖokui ta gbɔ.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: Eya ta esi wova ɖo afi sia la, nyemehe ɖe megbe kura o, ke boŋ esi ŋu ke la, mebɔbɔ nɔ ʋɔnudrɔ̃zikpui la dzi eye mebia be woakplɔ ŋutsua vɛ.

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: Esi enutsolawo tsi tsitre la, wometsɔ nya vɔ̃ siwo mebu be woawoe wotsɔ ɖe eŋu la ƒe ɖeke vɛ o.

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: Nu siwo katã wogblɔ la nye nyaʋiʋli kple Paulo le woawo ŋutɔ ƒe subɔsubɔ kple ame aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Yesu, si wobe eku, ke Paulo ya ka ɖe edzi be ele agbe la ko ŋu.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: Esi nya la me yiyi tsitotsito be mate ŋu atso afia glom ta la, mebiae be elɔ̃ be yeayi Yerusalem, ne woadrɔ̃ nya siawo na ye le afi ma mahã.

english_verse: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
translation_verse: Ke Paulo gblɔ be Roma Fiagã ŋutɔ koe atso nya me na ye. Ale wòbia be yeanɔ nye dzikpɔkpɔ te, va se ɖe esime woaɖo ye ɖe Roma Fiagã gbɔ.”

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Agripa gblɔ na Festo be: “Nye ŋutɔ hã medi be mase eƒe numegbe.” Festo ɖo eŋu be: “Àsee etsɔ.” Wokplɔ Paulo va Agripa kple Bernike ŋkume

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, Agripa kple Bernike ɖo atsyɔ̃ nyuie va takpeƒe la. Aʋakplɔlagãwo kple ame ŋkuta siwo le dua me la hã kpe ɖe wo ŋuti va. Festo bia be woakplɔ Paulo vɛ.

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: Tete Festo gblɔ be: “Fia Agripa kple mi ame siwo katã le teƒe sia kpli mí, miekpɔ ŋutsu sia? Yudatɔ siwo katã le Yerusalem kple afii la tsɔ nya ɖe eŋu. Wova gbɔnye kple ɣli be mele be wòaganɔ agbe o.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Ke nye la, nyemekpɔ be ewɔ naneke, si dze na ku o. Ke eya ŋutɔ di be Roma Fiagã ŋutɔ natso nya me na ye, eya ta meɖo be maɖoe ɖe egbɔ.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Evɔ la, nya tɔxɛ aɖeke mele asinye si maŋlɔ aɖo ɖe nye amegã la le eŋu o. Eya ta mekplɔe va mia ŋkume, vevietɔ wò Fia Agripa gbɔ, be ne míese eƒe numegbe nyuie vɔ la, makpɔ nya aɖe aŋlɔ aɖo ɖa.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: Elabe nye ya mekpɔ be mele susu nu be woaɖo gamenɔla ɖe ʋɔnu, eye womaŋlɔ nya si wotsɔ ɖe eŋu la akpe ɖe eŋu o.”

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: “Fia Agripa, mekpɔ be Mawu ɖi nam ŋutɔ be wò Fia Agripa ŋkumee mele ɖokuinye ta ʋli ge le egbe, aɖe nya siwo katã Yudatɔwo tsɔ ɖe ŋunye la nu.

english_verse: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
translation_verse: Megblɔ esia, elabe ènya nu le Yudatɔwo ƒe dekɔnuwo kple nya siwo le wo dome woʋlina la ŋu koŋ. Eya ta meɖe kuku be nàgbɔ dzi blewuu ase nye nyawo nam.

english_verse: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
translation_verse: Ne woato nyateƒe la, wonya tso gbe aɖe gbe ke be menɔ agbe abe Farisitɔ ene. Míaƒe kɔnyinyi nu sẽ wu míaƒe subɔsubɔha bubuawo katã tɔ.

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: Ŋugbedodo sia tututue míaƒe ƒome wui eve la le mɔ kpɔm na be wòasu yewo si, tae wosubɔa Mawu vevie zã kple keli. Fia Bubutɔ, mɔkpɔkpɔ sia tae Yudatɔwo tsɔ nya ɖe ŋunye ɖo.

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Ne wobe Mawu fɔa ame kukuwo ɖe tsitre la, nu ka ta mia dometɔ aɖe abu be esia menye nya woaxɔ ase o mahã?

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
translation_verse: Mewɔ esia le Yerusalem. Mexɔ ŋusẽ tso nunɔlagãwo gbɔ, hede ame siwo ŋu wokɔ la dometɔ geɖe gaxɔ me. Gawu la, ne wole wo wu ge la, nye hã melɔ̃na ɖe edzi.

english_verse: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
translation_verse: Mehea to na wo zi geɖe le ƒuƒoƒewo, eye mezia wo dzi be woagblɔ busunya. Medoa dɔmedzoe ɖe wo ŋu ale gbegbe, be metia wo yome yia dzronyigbaduwo ke hã me. Paulo gblɔ eƒe dzimetɔtrɔ ŋutinya (Dɔw

english_verse: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
translation_verse: “Esia dzie mele, zɔ mɔ yina Damasko gbe ɖeka. Nunɔlagãwo na ŋusẽm, hedo mɔm.

english_verse: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
translation_verse: Fia Bubutɔ, anɔ abe ŋdɔ ga wui eve me ene la, mekpɔ kekeli, si nu sẽ wu ɣe ƒe keklẽ gɔ̃ hã la. Eklẽ tso dziƒo ƒo xlã mía kple ame siwo nɔ mɔ zɔm la.

english_verse: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
translation_verse: Mí katã míedze anyi. Tete mese gbe aɖe, si gblɔ nam le Hebri-gbe me be: ‘Saulo! Saulo! Nu ka ta nèle yonyeme tim? Afɔtɔtɔ nutɔame, nu vevi ɖe wòwɔa ame!’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
translation_verse: Mebia be: ‘Wò ame kae, Aƒetɔ?’ Aƒetɔ la ɖo eŋu be: ‘Nye Yesu, ame si yome tim nèle lae.

english_verse: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
translation_verse: Ke fɔ, nàtsi tsitre. Meɖe ɖokuinye fia wò be maɖo wò nànye nye dɔla. Àɖi ɖase le nu si nènya le ŋutinye xoxo kple nu si maɖe afia wò emegbe la ŋuti.

english_verse: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
translation_verse: Maɖe wò tso ame siwo dome mele dɔwòm ɖo ɖa la, si me. Yudatɔwo kple ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la siaa.

english_verse: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
translation_verse: Àʋu ŋku na wo, eye àtrɔ wo tso viviti me ava kekeli me. Àɖe wo tso Abosam ƒe ŋusẽ te ava Mawu gbɔ, be woatsɔ woƒe nuvɔ̃ ake wo, ale be woakpɔ nɔƒe le ame siwo xɔ dzinye se, eye wokɔ wo ŋuti la dome.’ Paulo ƒo nu tso eƒe dɔ ŋu

english_verse: King Agrippa, I obeyed this vision from heaven.
translation_verse: “Fia Agripa, ale wɔ mezu nu si woɖe fiam tso dziƒo la dziwɔla.

english_verse: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
translation_verse: Gbã la, meyi Damasko. Emegbe la, meyi Yerusalem. Metsa Yudea-nyigba blibo la katã dzi. Metɔ edzi yi ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la hã gbɔ. Meyi ɖaɖe gbeƒã na wo be woadzudzɔ nuvɔ̃ wɔwɔ atrɔ va Mawu gbɔ, eye woawɔ nu si fia be wotrɔ dzime.

english_verse: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
translation_verse: Esia tae Yudatɔwo lém le mawuxɔa me ɖo, eye wote kpɔ be yewoawum.

english_verse: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
translation_verse: Ke Mawu kpe ɖe ŋunye va se ɖe egbe, ale be mele tsitre ɖe amegãwo kple ame bubuwo siaa ŋkume le ɖase ɖim na wo katã. Nya siwo Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo kple Mose gblɔ be woava eme la koe nye hã megblɔ. Mebe

english_verse: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: ele be Kristo la nakpe fu, eye wòanye ame gbãtɔ, si afɔ tso ame kukuwo dome, eye wòaɖe gbeƒã kekeli la na Yudatɔwo kple ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la hã.”

english_verse: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
translation_verse: Esi Paulo ɖe eɖokui nu alea la, Festo gblɔ sesĩe be: “Paulo, èdze aɖaʋa! Wò agbalẽsɔsrɔ̃ vivivo la na nèdze aɖaʋa.”

english_verse: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
translation_verse: Ke Paulo ɖo eŋu be: “Bubutɔgã Festo, nyemedze aɖaʋa o. Nye susu le te; nyateƒe tom mele.

english_verse: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
translation_verse: Fia Agripa nya nu tso nu siawo ŋuti, eya ta mele nu ƒom nɛ faa. Meka ɖe edzi be enya nu tso wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ŋu, elabe womewɔ ɖeke le bebeme o.

english_verse: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
translation_verse: Fia Agripa, èxɔ Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo dzi sea? Menya be èxɔ wo dzi se.”

english_verse: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
translation_verse: Agripa gblɔ na Paulo be: “Fifi laa ko nèbu be yeawɔm mazu Kristotɔa?”

english_verse: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
translation_verse: Paulo ɖo eŋu be: “Eɖanye fifia o, eɖanye emegbe o, nye gbedodoɖa na Mawu koe nye be wò kple ame siwo katã le to ɖomem egbe la, miava zu abe nye ene, ɖeko womegade ga miawo ya alea o.”

english_verse: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
translation_verse: Tete fia la, mɔ́mefia la kple Bernike kpakple anyinɔƒea katã tsi tsitre.

english_verse: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
translation_verse: Woyi adaŋu me eye wogblɔ le wo nɔewo dome be: “Ŋutsu sia mewɔ naneke si dze na ku alo gaxɔmeyiyi o.”

english_verse: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_verse: Agripa gblɔ na Festo be: “Ne ŋutsu sia ɖe megblɔ be Roma Fiagã ŋutɔ koe atso yeƒe nya me o la, anye ne woate ŋu aɖe asi le eŋu hafi.”

english_verse: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
translation_verse: Esi wotso nya me be míato ƒudzimɔ ayi Roma la, wotsɔ Paulo kple gamenɔla bubu aɖewo de aʋakplɔla aɖe si. Eŋkɔe nye Yulio, tso Fiagã Augusto ƒe aʋakɔwo dome.

english_verse: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
translation_verse: Míeɖo Adramitio-ʋu aɖe, si ɖoe be yeadze ɖe Asia ʋudzeƒewo, eye míeho. Makedoniatɔ aɖe, si ŋkɔe nye Aristarxo, tso Tesalonika la, kpe ɖe mía ŋu.

english_verse: The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Esi ŋu ke la, míeva dze ɖe Sidon. Aʋakplɔla Yulio nyo dɔme ɖe mɔ na Paulo be wòayi aɖakpɔ xɔlɔ̃awo ɖa, bene woadi nu siwo ahiãe la nɛ.

english_verse: When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind.
translation_verse: Míeho tso afi ma, eye esi ya de asi ƒoƒo me le mía kpem ta la, míeto Kipro-ƒukpo la ƒe dzigbeme.

english_verse: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
translation_verse: Míeto Kilikia kple Pamfilia ƒu me, eye míeva Mira le Likia.

english_verse: There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
translation_verse: Aʋakplɔla la kpɔ tɔdziʋu aɖe le afi ma, si tso Aleksandria yina ɖe Italia, eye wòna míeɖoe.

english_verse: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
translation_verse: Míezɔ blewuu ŋkeke geɖe, eye bebli hafi míeva ɖo Knido kasa. Ya la meɖe mɔ na mí be míayi ŋgɔ o, eya ta míeto Kreta-ƒukpo ƒe akpa si ya meƒona le o la va ɖo Salmone kasa.

english_verse: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
translation_verse: Míeto ƒugo la ŋu, eye mlɔeba la, míeva ɖo teƒe aɖe, si wona ŋkɔe be, “Ʋudzeƒenyui” la. Teƒe sia te ɖe Lasea-du la ŋu.

english_verse: By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past.
translation_verse: Azɔ esi ŋkeke geɖe va yi xoxo, eye ƒudzimɔzɔzɔ va zu ŋɔdzi, eye gawu la, Paska ɖuɣi hã va yi ta la,

english_verse: Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.”
translation_verse: Paulo ɖo aɖaŋu na wo gblɔ be: “Mía tɔwo, mekpɔ be nu geɖe le gbegblẽ ge, eye geɖe hã abú le míaƒe mɔzɔzɔa me. Menye agbaawo, ʋua me nuwo kple ʋua ɖeɖe koe lagblẽ o, ke boŋ ame hã le eme tsi ge.”

english_verse: But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
translation_verse: Gake nya siwo kuɖɔɖola la kple ʋutɔ la gblɔ la dze aʋakplɔla la ŋu wu Paulo tɔ.

english_verse: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
translation_verse: Esi ʋudzeƒea menyo be woanɔ le vuvɔŋɔli o ta la, ame akpa gãtɔ lɔ̃ ɖe edzi be míaho adzo, ɖewohĩ míate ŋu ade Foinike, si nye ʋudzeƒe le Kreta, eye míanɔ afi ma le vuvɔŋɔli. Ʋudzeƒe sia dze ŋgɔ anyigbeme ɣedzeƒe kple dzigbemeɣedzeƒe. Ahom dziŋɔ tu le ƒu dzi

english_verse: When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete.
translation_verse: Ya nɔ ƒoƒom blewuu tso anyigbeme, ale ameawo bu be yewoƒe didi la adze edzi. Wohe seke la de ʋua me, eye woho to Kreta-ƒugo ŋu kpuie.

english_verse: days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing.
translation_verse: Ke eteƒe medidi o, ya sesẽ si woyɔna be “Dzigbeme ɣedzeƒeya” la de asi ƒoƒo me tso ƒukpo la dzi va kpe mí.

english_verse: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
translation_verse: Esi ya la kpe ʋu la wòde ŋgɔ yi ge do kpoe ta la, míena mɔe wòkɔ mí dzoe.

english_verse: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
translation_verse: Ʋu la le du dzi to akpa si ya ƒona le na ƒukpo sue aɖe, si woyɔna be Klauda la, eye bebli hafi míete ŋu lé batala la.

english_verse: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
translation_verse: Wohee ɖe dzi, tsɔ ka to ʋua te heblae be wòalée ɖe asi. Esi wovɔ̃ be míava ge ɖe libla me le Libia-ƒugo ŋu ta la, woklo abala la, ale ya kɔ ʋua ɖe nu.

english_verse: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
translation_verse: Ahomya la nyama mí ŋusẽtɔe ale gbegbe be, esi ŋu ke la, ʋua me nɔlawo de asi agbaawo fɔfɔ ƒu gbe ɖe ƒu me me.

english_verse: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
translation_verse: Le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe la, woawo ŋutɔ fɔ ʋua me dɔwɔnu kple ʋukunu siwo le ʋua me la ƒu gbe.

english_verse: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke geɖe va yi ahom la nu sẽ wu gbɔgblɔ, ɣe alo ɣletivi aɖeke kpɔkpɔ meli o. Ale míebu mɔkpɔkpɔ keŋ be míatsi agbe.

english_verse: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
translation_verse: Ameawo nɔ anyi numaɖumaɖui ŋkeke geɖe. Ale Paulo tsi tsitre, do yi ŋgɔ gblɔ na wo be: “Mía tɔwo, ne ɖe mieɖo tom, eye mímeho dzo le Kreta o la, anye ne nu vevi mewɔ mí, eye míaƒe nuwo hã mebu alea o.

english_verse: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la, meɖe kuku na mi, milé dzi ɖe ƒo. Mía dometɔ aɖeke mele eme tsi ge o, negbe ʋua ko.

english_verse: I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel
translation_verse: Elabe le zã si va yi me la, Mawu, ame si tɔ menye, ame si mesubɔna la, ƒe dɔla va gbɔnye.

english_verse: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
translation_verse: Egblɔ nam be: ‘Paulo, mègavɔ̃ o. Ele be nàdo ɖe Roma Fiagã la ŋkume. Kpɔ ɖa, Mawu tsɔ ame siwo katã ɖo ʋua kpli wò la de asi na wò.’

english_verse: Cheer up! I am sure that God will do exactly what he promised.
translation_verse: Eya ta, mía tɔwo, milé dzi ɖe ƒo ko, elabe meka ɖe Mawu dzi be ana nya si eya ŋutɔ gblɔ nam la nava eme tututu.

english_verse: But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
translation_verse: Ke ele na mí be míadze go ɖe ƒukpo aɖe dzi.”

english_verse: They measured and found that the water was about
translation_verse: Ale woda dzidzeka, eye wokpɔ abɔ bla eve. Woyi ŋgɔ vie gadae, eye wokpɔ abɔ wui atɔ̃.

english_verse: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
translation_verse: Ale wotso ka sekeawo ɖe ƒua me, eye wotu kuɖɔŋukawo hã zi ɖeka. Wodo abala hekpe ya lae, eye woɖo ta ƒuta la.

english_verse: The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship.
translation_verse: Ke ʋukulaawo ɖoe be yewoasí le ʋua me, eya ta woɖiɖi batala la ɖe ƒua me, eye woda alakpa hewɔ abe ɖe wole sekeawo da ge ato ʋua ta hã ene.

english_verse: The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
translation_verse: Esi wovɔ̃ be míava dze go ɖe kpewo dzi ta la, woda seke ene to ʋua gɔme, eye wodo gbe ɖa be Mawu neɖi ŋu nake ɖe yewo.

english_verse: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
translation_verse: Ke Paulo gblɔ na aʋakplɔla la kple asrafoawo be: “Ne ame siawo manɔ ʋua me o la, miatsrɔ̃.”

english_verse: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
translation_verse: Ale asrafoawo tso batalawo ŋu kaawo, eye ʋua ge dze tsia me.

english_verse: Just before daylight Paul begged the people to eat something. He told them, “For
translation_verse: Le fɔŋli me la, Paulo ɖe kuku na wo katã be woaɖu nu. Egblɔ be: “Ŋkeke wui ene sɔŋ nye esi, mietsi dzodzodzoe heli naneke maɖumaɖui.

english_verse: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
translation_verse: Eya ta meɖe kuku na mi be miaɖu nu, ne miakpɔ ŋusẽ. Mia dometɔ aɖeke ƒe taɖa ɖeka hɔ̃ hã mabu o.”

english_verse: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
translation_verse: Esi Paulo gblɔ esia la, etsɔ abolo, da akpe na Mawu ɖe eta, eye wòkae le wo katã ŋkume hede asi eɖuɖu me.

english_verse: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
translation_verse: Tete dzi ɖo wo katã ƒo, ale wo dome ame sia ame ɖu nu.

english_verse: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
translation_verse: Esi woɖu nu ɖi ƒo la, woɖe lugba si wodo la ƒu gbe ɖe ƒua me. Ale ʋua zu wodzoe. Ƒutsotsoe gbã ʋu la

english_verse: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
translation_verse: Ŋu ke, ke ʋukulaawo medze si anyigba la o. Wokpɔ adɔ̃ aɖe, si ŋu ƒuta le, eye woɖoe be ne yewoate ŋui la, yewoaƒo ʋua ɖe afi ma.

english_verse: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
translation_verse: Ke ʋua va lɔ kekpo aɖe eye wòsi ke. Eta xaxa hetsi kea me; megate ŋu le ʋaʋãm o, eye ƒutsotsoe sesẽawo gbã egɔme.

english_verse: The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
translation_verse: Asrafoawo ɖoe be yewoawu gamenɔlaawo, ale be wo dome ame aɖeke nagaƒu tsi así o.

english_verse: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
translation_verse: Ke esi aʋakplɔla la di be yeaxɔ na Paulo ta la, egbe be asrafoawo megawɔ ɖe nu si woɖo be yewoawɔ la dzi o. Eɖe gbe na ame siwo ate ŋu aƒu tsi la be woati kpo adze tsia me gbã, aƒu tsi ayi gota.

english_verse: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
translation_verse: Ke ame mamlɛawo adze wo yome, ɖewo naku ɖe ʋuƒowo ŋu, eye bubuwo naku ɖe ʋua ƒe akpa siwo kaka la ŋu. Ale ameawo katã to mɔ sia dzi do ɖe gota dedie.

english_verse: When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
translation_verse: Míeɖi go ɖe ƒukpo la dzi vɔ hafi va nya be eyae nye Malta.

english_verse: The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
translation_verse: Ƒukpo sia dzi nɔlawo xɔ mí kple lɔlɔ̃ manyagblɔ, elabe esi tsi de asi dzadza me eye vuvɔ nɔ wɔwɔm la, wodo dzo yɔ mí katã be míava ƒu.

english_verse: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
translation_verse: Paulo nɔ ƒu ƒom nake wuwlui aɖewo be yeade dzoa me. Le dzoxɔxɔa ta la, da do tso nake bablɛ la me va xatsa ɖe eƒe asi.

english_verse: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
translation_verse: Ke esi afi ma tɔwo kpɔ da la wòxatsa ɖe eƒe asi la, wogblɔ na wo nɔewo be: “Ɖikeke aɖeke mele eme o, amewulae nye ŋutsu sia. Elabe togbɔ be wòdo le atsiaƒu si me hã la, Mawu di be yeahe to nɛ kple ku kokoko.”

english_verse: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
translation_verse: Tete Paulo ʋuʋu da la ɖe dzoa me, eye nu vevi aɖeke mewɔe o.

english_verse: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
translation_verse: Ke ameawo kpɔ mɔ be Paulo le tete ge alo amu dze anyi enumake aku. Ke esi wolala ʋuu, eye wokpɔ be naneke mewɔe o la, wotrɔ susu gblɔ be: “Mawu aɖee wònye.”

english_verse: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
translation_verse: Anyigba aɖe te ɖe teƒe si míeɖi go ɖo la ŋu. Enye Publio, ame si nye fia le ƒukpoa dzi la, tɔ. Fia sia xɔ mí nyuie, eye wòkpɔ mía dzi hewɔ amedzro na mí ŋkeke etɔ̃.

english_verse: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
translation_verse: Ɣe ma ɣi la, asrã lé Publio tɔ́, eye wònɔ kpeta hã dem hele anyimlɔƒe. Paulo yi ɖe egbɔ, do gbe ɖa, da asi ɖe edzi, eye wòyɔ dɔe.

english_verse: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
translation_verse: Esia megbe la, dɔléla bubu siwo katã le ƒukpoa dzi la hã va egbɔ, eye wòyɔ dɔ woawo hã.

english_verse: The people were very respectful to us, and when we sailed, they gave us everything we needed. From Malta to Rome
translation_verse: Wona nunana geɖe mí, eye esi míele dzodzom la, wotsɔ nu siwo katã hiã mí la na mí. Mɔzɔzɔ tso Malta yi Roma

english_verse: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
translation_verse: Ɣleti etɔ̃ megbe la, míegadze mɔ. Míeɖo tɔdziʋu aɖe, si woyɔna be “Evenɔvimawuwo” tso Aleksandro. Tɔdziʋu sia nɔ ƒukpoa dzi le vuvɔŋɔli la.

english_verse: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
translation_verse: Míeɖi go ɖe Sirakuse-ƒuta, eye míenɔ afi ma ŋkeke etɔ̃.

english_verse: From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli.
translation_verse: Míeglɔ̃ mɔ tso afi ma va Regio. Esi ŋu ke la, anyigbemeya de asi ƒoƒo me eye le ŋkeke evea gbe la, míeva ɖo Puteoli.

english_verse: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
translation_verse: Míedo go nɔvi aɖewo le afi ma, ame siwo bia tso mía si be míanɔ yewo gbɔ ŋkeke adrẽ. Afi siae míetso le ko va ɖo Roma.

english_verse: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
translation_verse: Nɔvi siwo le Roma la se be míeva, eye wova do go mí le keke Apio-si me kple teƒe si woyɔna be “Amedzrodzeƒeetɔ̃awo” la ke. Esi Paulo kpɔ wo la, eda akpe na Mawu, eye dzi gaɖo eƒo. Paulo le Roma

english_verse: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
translation_verse: Esi míeɖo Roma la, woɖe mɔ na Paulo be wòanɔ eɖokui si, ke wòna asrafo nɔ eŋu dzɔm le afi ma.

english_verse: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
translation_verse: Ŋkeke etɔ̃ megbe la, Paulo yɔ Yudatɔ siwo le afi ma la ƒe amegãwo va takpekpe. Esi wova la, egblɔ na wo be: “Nɔvinyewo, togbɔ be nyemewɔ nu gbegblẽ aɖeke ɖe mía detɔwo ŋu, alo da le mía tɔgbuiwo ƒe kɔnu aɖeke dzi o hã, wolém de gae le Yerusalem, eye wotsɔm de Romatɔwo si.

english_verse: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
translation_verse: Esi woyi ɖe nya la me kplim tsitotsito la, wokpɔ be nyemewɔ naneke si dze na ku o, eya ta wodi be yewoaɖe asi le ŋutinye hafi.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor. But I don't have anything to say against my own nation.
translation_verse: Ke Yudatɔwo melɔ̃ kura o. Ale woƒe nuwɔna sia zi dzinye be mabia be Roma Fiagã ŋutɔ natso nya me nam, togbɔ be nyemetsɔ nya aɖeke ɖe mía dedukɔ ŋu o hã.

english_verse: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
translation_verse: Nya sia tae medi be makpɔ mi ɖo, eye maƒo nu kpli mi, elabe nu si Israel le mɔ kpɔm na tae woblam kple kɔsɔkɔsɔ sia ɖo.”

english_verse: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
translation_verse: Woawo gblɔ nɛ be: “Míawo la, míexɔ agbalẽ aɖeke tso Yudea le ŋuwò o. Gawu la, nɔviawo dometɔ aɖeke hã metso afi ma va ƒo nu, alo gblɔ nya vɔ̃ aɖeke le ŋuwò na mí o.

english_verse: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
translation_verse: Ke míedi be míase wò susu, elabe míenya be amewo ƒo nu tsi tre ɖe ha sia, si me nèle la ŋuti le afi sia afi.”

english_verse: They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
translation_verse: Ale woɖo ŋkeke na Paulo. Esi ŋkekea de la, amewo va ƒo ƒu fũu ɖe eƒe dzeƒe la. Eɖe nya me na wo tso Mose ƒe se la kple Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo ƒe agbalẽwo me le Mawu ƒe fiaɖuɖu kple ame si Yesu nye la ŋuti. Ewɔ esia tso ŋdi va se ɖe fiẽ.

english_verse: Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not.
translation_verse: Ame aɖewo xɔ nu si wògblɔ la dzi se, ke bubuwo mexɔe se o.

english_verse: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Esi memama va wo dome alea la, Paulo ƒo nu gblɔ nya ɖeka na wo hafi wokaka. Egblɔ na wo be: “Gbɔgbɔ Kɔkɔe la gblɔe ɖe eteƒe, esime wòƒo nu to Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖela Yesaya dzi na mia tɔgbuiwo!

english_verse: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
translation_verse: Ebe: ‘Yi ame siawo gbɔ nàgblɔ na wo be: Miase nu, agasee baa, gake miele egɔme se ge o. Miakpɔ nu, agakpɔe baa, gake miele si dze gee o.

english_verse: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
translation_verse: Elabe ame siawo ƒe susu le dɔ̃, woƒe towo mesea nu nyuie o, eye womia woƒe ŋkuwo. Ɖe mele nenema o la, woƒe ŋkuwo akpɔ nu, woƒe towo ase nu, woƒe susu ase nu gɔme, eye woatrɔ ɖe ŋunye, be mayɔ dɔ wo.’ ”

english_verse: For two years Paul stayed in a rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him.
translation_verse: Paulo nɔ afi ma ƒe eve le xɔ si eya ŋutɔ ɣe la me, eye wòxɔa ame siwo katã vaa egbɔ la le afi ma.

english_verse: He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
translation_verse: Egblɔ nya le Mawu ƒe fiaɖuɖu ŋu, eye wòfia nu dzideƒotɔe le Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo ŋuti; ame aɖeke mexea mɔ nɛ o.

english_verse: From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus. God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news
translation_verse: Agbalẽ sia tso nye Paulo, Yesu Kristo ƒe dɔla gbɔ. Mawue tiam, heyɔm meva zu amedɔdɔ, bene maɖe gbeƒã yeƒe Nyanyui la.

english_verse: that he promised long ago by what his prophets said in the holy Scriptures.
translation_verse: Mawu do Nyanyui sia ŋugbe xoxoxo to eƒe gbeƒãɖelawo dzi, eye wòle mawunya kɔkɔeawo me.

english_verse: This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
translation_verse: Abe ame si tso Mawu gbɔ ene la, woɖee fia ŋusẽtɔe abe Mawu Vi ene, esi wofɔe ɖe tsitre tso ku me. Eyamae nye Yesu Kristo, mía Aƒetɔ la.

english_verse: Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith.
translation_verse: Mawu to eyama dzi ve mía nu míeva zu amedɔdɔwo, ale be, to eƒe ŋkɔ me la, míakplɔ dukɔwo katã, be woava xɔ Mawu dzi ase ahaɖo toe.

english_verse: You are some of those people chosen by Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: Mi Romanɔlawo hã miele ame siwo woyɔ be woava zu Yesu Kristo tɔwo la dome.

english_verse: This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people. I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! A Prayer of Thanks
translation_verse: Esia tae mele agbalẽ sia ŋlɔm na mi, ame siwo katã le Roma; mi ame siwo Mawu lɔ̃ vevie, eye wòyɔ mi be miava zu ame siwo ŋu wokɔ la. Mawu mía Tɔ́ kple Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo neve mia nu, eye woana ŋutifafa mi! Paulo da akpe na Mawu

english_verse: First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith.
translation_verse: Gbã la, mele akpe dam na nye Mawu le mi katã mia ta, to Yesu Kristo dzi, elabe ale si miexɔ Mawu dzi see la, ɖi hoo de afi sia afi le xexea me.

english_verse: God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
translation_verse: Mawu si mesubɔna le gbɔgbɔ me to Via ƒe Nyanyui la kaka me lae nye nye ɖasefo, be ne mele gbe dom ɖa la, meɖoa ŋku mia dzi ɖaa.

english_verse: In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you.
translation_verse: Mele kuku ɖem nɛ be wòaɖe mɔ azɔ be mate ŋu ava kpɔ mi ɖa dzro.

english_verse: I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith.
translation_verse: Enye nye didi vevie be míado go ŋkume kple ŋkume, ale be mana nunana aɖe si tso Gbɔgbɔ la gbɔ la mi, bene wòado ŋusẽ mi.

english_verse: What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
translation_verse: Nu si mewɔnɛ lae nye be míado ŋusẽ mía nɔewo: nye xɔse nado ŋusẽ mi, eye miawo hã mia tɔ nado ŋusẽ nye hã.

english_verse: My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places.
translation_verse: Nɔviwo, medi be mianya be meɖoe zi geɖe ŋutɔ, be mava mia gbɔ hafi, ke medze edzi nam kpɔ va se ɖe fifi o. Medi be nye asi nasu dzimetrɔla aɖewo dzi le miawo hã mia dome, abe ale si wòsu ame bubu siwo hã menye Yudatɔwo o la, dzi la ene.

english_verse: It doesn't matter if people are civilized and educated, or if they are uncivilized and uneducated. I must tell the good news to everyone. That's why I am eager to visit all of you in Rome. The Power of the Good News
translation_verse: Ale enye nye didi vevie be magblɔ Nyanyui la na mi, ame siwo le Roma hã. Ŋusẽ le Nyanyui la si

english_verse: I am proud of the good news! It is God's powerful way of saving all people who have faith, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Nyanyui la mekpea ŋu nam o, elabe Mawu ƒe ŋusẽ wònye. Exɔa ame siwo katã xɔa edzi sena la ɖe agbe; Yudatɔwo gbã kple ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la hã.

english_verse: The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.” Everyone Is Guilty
translation_verse: Nyanyui la mee woɖe ale si Mawu bua ame be ele dzɔdzɔe la ɖe go fia le. Esia nye xɔse ƒe nya tso gɔmedzedzea va se ɖe nuwuwu. Woŋlɔ ɖe mawunya me be: “Ame si le dzɔdzɔe le eƒe xɔse ta la latsi agbe.” Ame aɖeke mele dzɔdzɔe le Mawu ŋkume o

english_verse: From heaven God shows how angry he is with all the wicked and evil things that sinful people do to crush the truth.
translation_verse: Ale si Mawu doa dziku ɖe ame siwo mevɔ̃nɛ o la ŋu, ame siwo tsɔ nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ɖo dɔe, ale be wotsɔa nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ tea nyateƒe la ɖe to la, dze ƒãa tso keke dziƒo ke.

english_verse: They know everything that can be known about God, because God has shown it all to them.
translation_verse: Nu si amegbetɔ ate ŋu anya tso Mawu ŋuti la, enyae xoxo hafi, elabe Mawu ŋutɔ ɖee fiae.

english_verse: God's eternal power and character cannot be seen. But from the beginning of creation, God has shown what these are like by all he has made. That's why those people don't have any excuse.
translation_verse: Tso esime wowɔ xexea me la, Mawu ƒe ŋusẽ si li ɖaa kple nu si wònye ƒe nɔnɔme, esiwo nye nu siwo ŋkumekpɔna le Mawu ŋu o la, dze ƒã le nu siwo wòwɔ la me. Ale amegbetɔ aɖeke mate ŋu ado taflatsɛ be yemenya nu siawo o.

english_verse: They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be wonya Mawu hã la, wometsɔa bubu si dze nɛ, alo daa akpe nɛ abe ale si wòle be woada akpe nɛ la ene o. Le esia teƒe la, nu maɖeviwo ŋu ko wobuna. Susu megale wo si o, ale woƒe tame do viviti.

english_verse: They claim to be wise, but they are fools.
translation_verse: Woawo ŋutɔ be yewole nu nyam, ke wova zu movitɔwo.

english_verse: They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
translation_verse: Eye woɖɔ li Mawu makumaku ƒe ŋutikɔkɔea kple nutata siwo ɖi amegbetɔ si nye nu kuku, alo xewo, alo lãfɔnewo, alo lã siwo tana ƒe nɔnɔme.

english_verse: So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies.
translation_verse: Ale Mawu ɖe asi le wo ŋu be woawɔ nu si dzro woƒe dzi, eye woatsɔ woƒe ŋutilã awɔ ŋunyɔnu kple ŋukpenanu kple wo nɔewo.

english_verse: They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
translation_verse: Woawoe nye ame siwo trɔ Mawu ƒe nyateƒe la wɔ aʋatsoe. Wosubɔ nu siwo Mawu wɔ la hede ta agu na wo, ɖe nuawo Wɔla, si dze na kafukafu yi ɖase mavɔ me la, ŋutɔ teƒe. Amen.

english_verse: God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural.
translation_verse: Le esia ta la, Mawu ɖe asi le wo ŋuti, eye fieŋufieŋu ɖua wo dzi ale be wowɔa ŋukpenanuwo. Woƒe nyɔnuwo dɔna kple nyɔnuwo, evɔ la, menye nenemae dzɔdzɔme ɖoe da ɖi o.

english_verse: Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
translation_verse: Nenema ke woƒe ŋutsuwo hã medɔna kple nyɔnu, abe ale si dzɔdzɔme ɖoe da ɖi la ene o, ke boŋ wofiena gudaguda le woƒe ŋutilã me ɖe wo tɔ ŋutsuwo ŋu, ale be ŋutsu dɔna kple ŋutsu ŋukpe manɔmee. Le nu gbegblẽ si wowɔ ta la, Mawu he to na wo, abe ale si dze wo la ene, eye wokpɔ esia le wo ɖokui me.

english_verse: Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things.
translation_verse: Esi medze wo ŋu be woaxɔ nunya vavãtɔ si tso Mawu ŋu ɖe wo ɖokui me o ta la, Mawu hã gblẽ wo ɖe woawo ŋutɔ ƒe susu masɔmasɔ me, be woawɔ nu siwo mesɔ kura o la.

english_verse: They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip,
translation_verse: Woyɔ taŋ kple nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔwo tsyo ƒomevi: vɔɖivɔ̃ɖi, ŋukeklẽ kple vɔ̃ediname. Bubu siwo gaxɔ aƒe ɖe wo mee nye: ŋubiabiã, amewuwu, avuwɔwɔ, amebeble, susu vɔ̃ɖiwo ŋu bubu kple ameŋunyagbɔgblɔ.

english_verse: say cruel things about others, and hate God. They are proud, conceited, and boastful, always thinking up new ways to do evil. These people don't respect their parents.
translation_verse: Wonye ameŋugblẽlawo, ame siwo lé Mawu ɖe fu me, amedzulawo, dàdalawo, adegbeƒolawo, ame siwo toa nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ vɛ, ame siwo meɖoa to wo dzilawo o,

english_verse: They are stupid, unreliable, and don't have any love or pity for others.
translation_verse: movitɔwo, ame siwo dzi menyaxɔna sena o, ame siwo mekpɔa nublanui na ame o kple ame siwo sẽa ŋuta.

english_verse: They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
translation_verse: Togbɔ be wonya nyuie be le Mawu ƒe se nu la, ame siwo wɔa nu siawo dze na ku hã la, wowɔa wo, eye gawu la, wodea ame bubu siwo hã wɔa nu siawo la dzi.

english_verse: Some of you accuse others of doing wrong. But there is no excuse for what you do. When you judge others, you condemn yourselves, because you are guilty of doing the very same things.
translation_verse: Nɔvinye, wòe le ʋɔnu drɔ̃m ame bubuwoa? Ame ka kee nènye hã la, màte ŋu agblɔ be ye ya yewɔa nu dzɔdzɔe o. Ne èbu fɔ ame bubuwo la, wò ŋutɔ ɖokuiwò ko nèbu fɔe, elabe nu mawo ke ko wò, ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la, ŋutɔ hã nèwɔna.

english_verse: We know that God is right to judge everyone who behaves in this way.
translation_verse: Míenya be Mawu tɔ ɖe wòdzɔ, ne edrɔ̃ ʋɔnu ame siwo wɔa nu siawo ƒomevi.

english_verse: Do you really think God won't punish you, when you behave exactly like the people you accuse?
translation_verse: Nɔvinye, ke wò, ame si le ʋɔnu drɔ̃m nu siawo wɔlawo, evɔ wò ŋutɔ nèwɔa nu mawo ke la, ɖe nèle bubum be yeate ŋu así le Mawu ƒe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ nua?

english_verse: You surely don't think much of God's wonderful goodness or of his patience and willingness to put up with you. Don't you know that the reason God is good to you is because he wants you to turn to him?
translation_verse: Alo ètsɔe be Mawu nyoa dɔme ŋutɔ, doa dzi ale gbegbe, hegbɔa dzi blewuu ta, mètsɔ ɖeke le eme o? Ke mènyae be Mawu ɖe wònyo dɔme na ye hele ye kplɔm be yeatrɔ dzime oa?

english_verse: But you are stubborn and refuse to turn to God. So you are making things even worse for yourselves on that day when he will show how angry he is and will judge the world with fairness.
translation_verse: Ke esi nèsẽ to gbe be yematrɔ dzime o la, wò ŋutɔ èna tohehe, si Mawu le na wò ge le ŋkeke ma dzi la, le ŋu sẽm ɖe edzi na wò ŋutɔ ɖokuiwò. Gbe ma gbee Mawu adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu dzɔdzɔe, eye wòaɖe eƒe dziku ɖe go afia.

english_verse: God will reward each of us for what we have done.
translation_verse: Aɖo eteƒe na ame sia ame ɖe nu si wòwɔ la nu.

english_verse: He will give eternal life to everyone who has patiently done what is good in the hope of receiving glory, honor, and life that lasts forever.
translation_verse: Ame siwo ku kutri hewɔ nu nyui, eye wodi ŋutikɔkɔe, bubu kple agbe nyui nɔnɔ la, Mawu ana agbe mavɔ wo.

english_verse: But he will show how angry and furious he can be with every selfish person who rejects the truth and wants to do evil.
translation_verse: Ke ame siwo dzrewɔwɔ dzɔa dzi na, eye womeɖoa to nyateƒe la o, ke boŋ wolɔ̃ nuvɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ la, Mawu ahe to na wo vevie kple dziku.

english_verse: All who are wicked will be punished with trouble and suffering. It doesn't matter if they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ame siwo katã tsɔ nuvɔ̃ wɔwɔ ɖo dɔe la, akpe fu, eye woase veve; Yudatɔwo gbã kple ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la hã.

english_verse: But all who do right will be rewarded with glory, honor, and peace, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ke ŋutikɔkɔe, bubu kple ŋutifafa anye nu nyui wɔlawo katã tɔ. Yudatɔwo gbã kple ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la hã.

english_verse: God doesn't have any favorites!
translation_verse: Elabe Mawu medea ame aɖeke dzi o.

english_verse: Those people who don't know about God's Law will still be punished for what they do wrong. And the Law will be used to judge everyone who knows what it says.
translation_verse: Ame siwo katã Mose ƒe se la mebla o, eye wowɔ nuvɔ̃ la, woahe to na wo se sia manɔmee, ke ame siwo katã le se sia te, eye wowɔ nuvɔ̃ la, se siae woatsɔ adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu woe.

english_verse: God accepts those who obey his Law, but not those who simply hear it.
translation_verse: Elabe menye ame siwo ɖoa to hesea se lae le dzɔdzɔe le Mawu ŋkume o, ke boŋ ame siwo wɔa se la dzi lae.

english_verse: when God appoints Jesus Christ to judge everyone's secret thoughts, just as my message says. The Jews and the Law
translation_verse: Nu si fiam nye Nyanyui la le lae nye be alea wòava nɔ gbe ma gbe, esime Mawu le ʋɔnu drɔ̃ ge amegbetɔwo ƒe nya ɣaɣlawo to Yesu Kristo dzi. Nu si se la gblɔ tso Yudatɔwo ŋu

english_verse: Some of you call yourselves Jews. You trust in the Law and take pride in God.
translation_verse: Wò la, eyɔa ɖokuiwò be Yudatɔ, èɖoa ŋu ɖe se la ŋu, eye nèdana be Mawu ƒe ame tɔxɛ yenye.

english_verse: By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right.
translation_verse: Ènya Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu, eye nènya nu si nye nu nyuitɔ abe ale si nèsrɔ̃e tso se la me la ene.

english_verse: You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark.
translation_verse: Èbua ɖokuiwò be yenye ŋkuagbãtɔwo kplɔla kple kekeli na ame siwo le viviti me.

english_verse: And since there is knowledge and truth in God's Law, you think you can instruct fools and teach young people.
translation_verse: Ètsɔ ɖokuiwò wɔ ame manyanuwo hela kple ame siwo metsi haɖe o la ƒe nufialae. Ènya nyuie be nunya kple nyateƒe ɖeɖe sɔŋ le se la me.

english_verse: But how can you teach others when you refuse to learn? You preach it is wrong to steal. But do you steal?
translation_verse: Ale ke wɔ wò, ame si fiaa nu ame bubuwo, màfia nu ɖokuiwò o? Èɖe gbeƒã be womegafi fi o, evɔ la, wò ŋutɔ nèle fi fim.

english_verse: You say people should be faithful in marriage. But are you faithful? You hate idols, yet you rob their temples.
translation_verse: Ègblɔ be womegawɔ ahasi o, gake wò ŋutɔ nèhele ahasi wɔm. Legba nyɔa ŋu na wò, ke èfiaa trɔ̃ƒemenuwo.

english_verse: You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God.
translation_verse: Wò, ame si ƒoa adegbe be yewɔa sea dzi la, wò kee gadaa sea dzi tsɔna ɖea bubu le Mawu ŋuti.

english_verse: It is just as the Scriptures tell us, “You have made foreigners say insulting things about God.”
translation_verse: Mawunya la gblɔe alea pɛ, be mi Yudatɔwo ƒe nuwɔnawo tae, ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la gblɔa nya vlowo ɖe Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ ŋu ɖo.

english_verse: Being circumcised is worthwhile, if you obey the Law. But if you don't obey the Law, you are no better off than people who are not circumcised.
translation_verse: Ne èwɔa sea dzi la, ekema viɖe le wò aʋatsotso abe Yudatɔ ene me; ke ne mèwɔa sea dzi o la, ekema èzu abe ame manye Yudatɔ si wometso aʋa na o la ene.

english_verse: In fact, if they obey the Law, they are as good as anyone who is circumcised.
translation_verse: Nenye be ame si menye Yudatɔ o, wɔa sea ƒe ɖoɖowo dzi la, ɖe Mawu mabui abe ame si wɔ sea dzi la ene oa?

english_verse: So everyone who obeys the Law, but has never been circumcised, will condemn you. Even though you are circumcised and have the Law, you still don't obey its teachings.
translation_verse: Azɔ ame si menye Yudatɔ o evɔ wòwɔa sea dzi la, ado ŋukpe wò, Yudatɔ si daa sea dzi, togbɔ be woŋlɔ se la de asi na wò gɔ̃ hã.

english_verse: To be a real Jew you must obey the Law. True circumcision is something that happens deep in your heart, not something done to your body. And besides, you should want praise from God and not from humans.
translation_verse: ke boŋ ame si nye Yudatɔ le eɖokui me, eye wòtso aʋa na eya ŋutɔ ƒe dzi lae. Aʋatsotso sia tɔgbe tso Mawu ƒe Gbɔgbɔ la gbɔ, eye metso se, si woŋlɔ ɖi la me o. Mawue kafua ame sia tɔgbe, ke menye amewoe o.

english_verse: What good is it to be a Jew? What good is it to be circumcised?
translation_verse: Azɔ nu ka koŋ Yudatɔ tsɔ le ŋgɔ na ame si menye Yudatɔ o la, alo viɖe kawoe le aʋatsotso me?

english_verse: It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews.
translation_verse: Viɖe siawo sɔ gbɔ ŋutɔ. Gbã la, Yudatɔwoe Mawu tsɔ eƒe nya la de asi na.

english_verse: It is true that some of them did not believe the message. But does this mean that God cannot be trusted, just because they did not have faith?
translation_verse: Ke esi wo dometɔ aɖewo mehewɔ nuteƒe o ɖe? Esia ɖe wòfia be, le esia ta Mawu hã agbe nuteƒewɔwɔa?

english_verse: No, indeed! God tells the truth, even if everyone else is a liar. The Scriptures say about God, “Your words will be proven true, and in court you will win your case.”
translation_verse: Ao! Esia madzɔ akpɔ o. Ne amegbetɔ ɖe sia ɖe zu alakpatɔ hã la, Mawu ya, nyateƒetɔ ko wòanye godoo. Woŋlɔ ɖi be: “Ne èƒo nu la, tɔwò nedzɔ. Ne wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wò la, woatso afia na wò godoo.”

english_verse: If our evil deeds show how right God is, then what can we say? Is it wrong for God to become angry and punish us? What a foolish thing to ask.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ nenye be nu madzɔmadzɔ, si mí amegbetɔwo míewɔna lae wɔnɛ be nu dzɔdzɔe, si Mawu wɔna la dzena ƒãa la, nu ka míate ŋu agblɔ le go sia me? Ɖe míagblɔ be Mawu wɔ nu madzɔmadzɔ, nenye be wòhe to na mía?

english_verse: But the answer is, “No.” Otherwise, how could God judge the world?
translation_verse: Gbeɖe! Ne Mawu nye nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔla ɖe, ale ke wòate ŋu adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu xexea mee?

english_verse: Since your lies bring great honor to God by showing how truthful he is, you may ask why God still says you are a sinner.
translation_verse: Ne ele alea be nye aʋatsokaka mee Mawu ƒe nyateƒe dzena le ƒãa, be woakafui la, ekema nu ka tae woagabum nuvɔ̃wɔlae?

english_verse: You might as well say, “Let's do something evil, so that something good will come of it!” Some people even claim that we are saying this. But God is fair and will judge them as well. No One Is Good
translation_verse: Ne ele alea ɖe, nu ka tae mímanɔ nuvɔ̃ wɔm ko, ale be nu nyui nanɔ go dom tso eme o? Ame aɖewo le aʋatso kam ɖe mía si xoxo, be eyae nye míaƒe nya míele gbɔgblɔm. Nyemegblɔ nenema o, ke ne wobu fɔ ame si agblɔ nya sia la, wo tɔ dzɔ. Ame aɖeke mele dzɔdzɔe o

english_verse: What does all this mean? Does it mean that we Jews are better off than the Gentiles? No, it doesn't! Jews, as well as Gentiles, are ruled by sin, just as I have said.
translation_verse: Ekema azɔ la, ɖe mí Yudatɔwo mía tɔ me nyo wu ame bubuwo tɔ mea? Ao, menyo wu le go aɖeke me o! Míeɖe eme do ŋgɔ va yi xoxo, be Yudatɔwo kple ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la siaa le nuvɔ̃ ƒe ŋusẽ te.

english_verse: The Scriptures tell us, “No one is acceptable to God!
translation_verse: Mawunya ɖo kpe edzi be: “Ame aɖeke meli, si le dzɔdzɔe o. Ao, ɖeka pɛ hã meli o.

english_verse: Not one of them understands or even searches for God.
translation_verse: Ame aɖeke meli, si sea nu gɔme o, eye ɖeke hã meli, si dia Mawu ƒe mɔ o.

english_verse: They have all turned away and are worthless. There isn't one person who does right.
translation_verse: Wo katã wotra mɔ; wo katã woda ƒú, eye ɖeke meli, si wɔa nu nyui o. Ɖeka pɛ hã meli o.

english_verse: Their words are like an open pit, and their tongues are good only for telling lies. Each word is as deadly as the fangs of a snake,
translation_verse: Woƒe vehlo le kèke ɖi, abe yɔdo nuvo ene. Woblea ame ŋánaŋana kple woƒe aɖe. Woƒe nyawo le abe da ƒe aɖi ene le aɖe dzi na wo.

english_verse: and they say nothing but bitter curses.
translation_verse: Fiƒode kple veve helihelĩ yɔ nu me na wo taŋ.

english_verse: These people quickly become violent.
translation_verse: Wole du dzi, yina ame wu ge.

english_verse: Wherever they go, they leave ruin and destruction.
translation_verse: Ne wodzo yina la, wogblẽ aƒedo kple vevesese ɖe megbe.

english_verse: They don't know how to live in peace.
translation_verse: Womenya ale si wonɔa agbe le ŋutifafa me o,

english_verse: They don't even fear God.”
translation_verse: eye mawuvɔvɔ̃ ya ɖekeɖeke mele ŋku dzi na wo o.”

english_verse: We know that everything in the Law was written for those who are under its power. The Law says these things to stop anyone from making excuses and to let God show that the whole world is guilty.
translation_verse: Azɔ míenya be nu siwo se la gblɔ la, ame siwo le se la tee wògblɔ wo na, be ame sia ame nadzudzɔ eɖokuinuɖeɖe, ale be Mawu nadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu xexeme blibo la.

english_verse: God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin. God's Way of Accepting People
translation_verse: Womabu amegbetɔ aɖeke be ele dzɔdzɔe le Mawu ŋkume, esi wòwɔ sea dzi ta o, elabe se la ɖeko wònana míedzea sii be nuvɔ̃ li boŋ. Nu si nana Mawu bua ame be ele dzɔdzɔe

english_verse: Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ke azɔ la, woɖe ale si Mawu bua ame be ele dzɔdzɔe la fia, eye esia meto se la dzi va o. Se la ŋutɔ kple Mawu ƒe gbeƒãɖelawo hã ɖi ɖase le esia ŋuti.

english_verse: God treats everyone alike. He accepts people only because they have faith in Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: Mawu bua ame sia ame si xɔ Kristo dzi se la be ele dzɔdzɔe. Mede vovototo aɖeke wo me o.

english_verse: All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory.
translation_verse: Elabe ame sia ame wɔ nuvɔ̃, eye mete va Mawu ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe la gbɔ kura o.

english_verse: But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins.
translation_verse: Ke Mawu ve wo nu, bu wo be wole dzɔdzɔe, abe nunana ene, esi Kristo Yesu xe fe ɖe wo nu la ta.

english_verse: God sent Christ to be our sacrifice. Christ offered his life's blood, so by faith in him we could come to God. And God did this to show that in the past he was right to be patient and forgive sinners. This also shows that God is right when he accepts people who have faith in Jesus.
translation_verse: Ewɔ esia be yeaɖee afia, le egbe ŋkeke siawo me, be ye ŋutɔ la, ɖe yele dzɔdzɔe, eye yebua ame si xɔ Yesu dzi se la hã be ele dzɔdzɔe.

english_verse: What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith.
translation_verse: Azɔ la, nu ka koŋ míate ŋu agatsɔ aƒo adegbee? Naneke megali o. Susu ka tae? Esi míewɔ sea dzi tae loo? Gbeɖe, ke esi míexɔ se tae.

english_verse: We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law.
translation_verse: Nyati si míetu tsitre lae nye be wobua ame be ele dzɔdzɔe, nenye be exɔ Kristo dzi se, ke menye esi wòwɔ sea dzi ta o.

english_verse: Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is!
translation_verse: Alo Mawu la, Yudatɔwo ɖeɖe ko ƒe Mawu wònye loo? Ɖe menye ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la hã tɔ oa? Ẽ, enye woawo hã ƒe Mawu baa!

english_verse: There is only one God, and he accepts Gentiles as well as Jews, simply because of their faith.
translation_verse: Ale Mawu ɖeka koe li. Eyae abu ame siwo nye Yudatɔwo be wole dzɔdzɔe le woƒe xɔse nu, eye wòabu ame siwo menye Yudatɔwo o la hã be wole dzɔdzɔe le woƒe xɔse nu.

english_verse: Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
translation_verse: Ekema menye ɖee míetsɔ xɔse sia le se la ɖem ɖa oa? Kpao! Ɖe boŋ míelé se la ɖe te sesĩe.

english_verse: If he became acceptable to God because of what he did, then he would have something to brag about. But he would never be able to brag about it to God.
translation_verse: Nenye be Mawu ɖe wòbu Abraham be ele dzɔdzɔe le dɔ si wòwɔ ta la, ekema nane anɔ esi wòatsɔ aƒo adegbee, ke menye le Mawu ŋkume ya o.

english_verse: The Scriptures say, “God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.”
